nodes.title: Fix an integer m>=2, a real number eta with 0<eta<1/2, and a bounded complex function W supported in [1+eta,2-eta]. Let x tend to infinity through positive real values for which N=2x is an integer, and define R_{m,N}(W)=sum_{p prime, p<N, p congruent to N modulo m} log(p) mu((N-p)/m) W(p/x). A direct specialization of Banks and Shparlinski, arXiv:2506.08787, Theorem 2.1, with the physical prime p as its first variable gives, for every fixed C>0, the bound R_{m,N}(W)<<_{C,m,W} x^2(log x)^(1-C). For every fixed C this upper bound is asymptotically larger than x/log x, so this direct specialization cannot by itself prove R_{m,N}(W)=o(x/log x). If instead the first theorem variable is compressed to the prime index k and its injective map is f(k)=p_k, where p_k is the k-th prime, then the Möbius factor supplied by the theorem is mu(kd), not mu(p_k d) and not mu(d); hence this prime-indexed expression is not a direct coefficient-preserving specialization of R_{m,N}(W). This is only a no-direct-specialization statement, not an assertion that R_{m,N}(W) cannot be estimated by another argument

Entrywise, G_{(i,a),(i,a)}=1, G_{(i,a),(i,b)}=0 for a different from b, and G_{(i,a),(j,b)}=1/r for i different from j. Moreover every row of A has absolute row sum c-1, the operator norm of A is c-1, and the Hilbert-Schmidt norm of A is sqrt(c(c-1)). nodes.title: Proposition (scoped no-go for two quadratic-form Bombieri–Vinogradov interfaces at the determinant-carrier scale). Let H tend to infinity. For each integer matrix Q=(a,c;-d,b) with |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|<=H^{3+o(1)}, define F_Q(x,y)=ad x^2-bc y^2. On any nondegenerate slice on which |disc(F_Q)|=|4abcd|=H^{12+o(1)} and |x|,|y|=H^{2+o(1)}, every represented value F_Q(x,y) has size at most H^{10+o(1)}. (1) The range hypotheses in Ditchen's arXiv:1312.1502, Theorems 1.1 and 1.2, fail on this slice, including the conditional Lindelof relaxations stated in Remark 1.6. (2) Lam's arXiv:1812.08823, Proposition 1, does not average over Q or over F_Q: it fixes one primitive positive-definite binary quadratic form and averages auxiliary congruence moduli. (3) Both cited results put primality on the represented integer F(m,n), whereas the determinant carrier requires x and y themselves to be prime and F_Q(x,y) to equal a fixed, generally composite integer. Consequently neither cited theorem, without an additional cross-form transfer theorem changing its quantifiers and primality slots, is an applicable source of a fixed-power saving for the varying det(Q)=ab+cd shell

nodes.title: CENTERED-ROW CRITICAL-FREQUENCY SATURATION NO-FIT. Let p be a prime, let N be an integer with p not dividing N, and let k_0 be a nonzero residue modulo p. There exists a row Z on Z/pZ satisfying sum_{z mod p} Z(z)=0 such that its unit-inversion Fourier response Y(k)=sum_{u mod p, u nonzero} Z(u)e_p(kNu^{-1}) obeys Y(k_0)=p-1 and Y(k)=-1 for every k not congruent to k_0 modulo p. Consequently, for every set K of residues modulo p containing k_0, sum_{k in K}|Y(k)|^2=(p-1)^2+|K|-1, while sum_{k mod p, k nonzero}|Y(k)|^2=p^2-p-1. Hence even a short critical band containing k_0 can carry asymptotically all complete nonzero-frequency energy. 0025283165f465c4.title: UNIFORM MAYNARD SIEGEL-WALFISZ PROPERTY FOR NORMALIZED LOGARITHMIC PRIME TWISTS. Let P>=3 and theta be real. Define
0025283165f465c4.author: slava chan
0025283165f465c4.statement:
UNIFORM MAYNARD SIEGEL-WALFISZ PROPERTY FOR NORMALIZED LOGARITHMIC PRIME TWISTS. Let P>=3 and theta be real. Define
alpha_theta(n)
 =1_{n prime}1_{P<n<=2P} n^(i theta)/(1+|theta|).                 (1)
Then the family {alpha_theta:theta real} satisfies Maynard's Siegel-Walfisz condition uniformly in theta: for every A>1, every d,q>=1, and every integer a with (a,q)=1,
| sum_{P<n<=2P,n congruent a (mod q),(n,d)=1}alpha_theta(n)
 -phi(q)^(-1)sum_{P<n<=2P,(n,dq)=1}alpha_theta(n) |
 <<_A P tau(d)^2 (log P)^(-A),                                  (2)
where the implied constant is independent of theta,d,q,a and P.
0025283165f465c4.proof:
We first prove a uniform prefix estimate for the unweighted prime discrepancy. For P<=u<=2P put
E(u)=sum_{P<p<=u,(p,d)=1}
 [1_{p congruent a (mod q)}-phi(q)^(-1)1_{(p,q)=1}],             (3)
where p is prime.

Fix A>1 and choose H>A+6. Suppose first that q<=(log P)^H. Theorem 2 of Liu and Wang, arXiv:2202.00635, states that for every fixed H there is C_H>0 such that, uniformly for (b,q)=1 and q<=(log x)^H,
pi(x;q,b)=li(x)/phi(q)+O_H(x exp(-C_H sqrt(log x))).             (4)
Apply (4) at x=u and x=P. Apply it also with modulus 1 to the total prime count. The primes dividing q contribute at most omega(q), which is at most log q/log 2, when the total prime count is replaced by the count of primes coprime to q. Hence the discrepancy in (3) before imposing (p,d)=1 is
O_H(P exp(-c_H sqrt(log P))+log q).                              (5)
Deleting the primes which divide d changes each of the two sums in (3) by at most omega(d); since 1/phi(q)<=1, the total change is at most 2omega(d)<=2tau(d). For sufficiently large P, (5) is therefore
O_A(P tau(d)^2(log P)^(-A-2)).                                  (6)
The finitely many smaller P are absorbed by enlarging the constant.

Suppose next that q>(log P)^H. Direct counting gives, before the d-restriction,
|E(u)|<=P/q+1+P/phi(q)+1.                                       (7)
For every integer q>=1,
q/phi(q)=product_{l|q}(1-1/l)^(-1)
 <=product_{l|q}(1+1/l)^2
 =(sum_{e|q}1/e)^2<=(1+log q)^2.                                (8)
For q beyond the threshold (log P)^H, the function (1+log q)^2/q is decreasing once q is larger than an absolute constant. Thus (7)-(8), with H>A+6, give
|E(u)|<<_A P(log P)^(-A-2)+1.                                  (9)
Deleting primes dividing d again costs at most 2tau(d), so after adjusting the constant,
sup_{P<=u<=2P}|E(u)|
 <<_A P tau(d)^2(log P)^(-A-2)                                 (10)
also in the large-q case.

Now apply Abel summation to the signed measure whose cumulative function is E(u), with
f_theta(u)=u^(i theta)/(1+|theta|).
The endpoint term has modulus at most sup|E|/(1+|theta|), while
|f'_theta(u)|=|theta|/((1+|theta|)u)<=1/u.                       (11)
Therefore the absolute value in (2) is at most
2 sup_{P<=u<=2P}|E(u)|
 +integral_P^(2P)|E(u)|du/u
 <<_A P tau(d)^2(log P)^(-A-2).                                (12)
This is stronger than (2), uniformly in theta. Equation (2) is exactly Maynard's condition (4.1) on the P-dyadic segment.

glossary.E(u): The unweighted centered prime discrepancy up to the variable endpoint u.
glossary.H: An auxiliary logarithmic-modulus exponent chosen larger than A+6.
glossary.alpha_theta(n): The prime indicator on the P-dyadic interval, twisted by n^(i theta) and normalized by 1+|theta|.
glossary.f_theta(u): The normalized logarithmic twist u^(i theta)/(1+|theta|).

0029944864b851e8.title: EXACT PRIMITIVE-DENOMINATOR AND DETERMINANT-COLLISION LEDGER FOR THE TWO-SIDED LIT-INC CARRIER
0029944864b851e8.author: slava chan
0029944864b851e8.statement:
EXACT PRIMITIVE-DENOMINATOR AND DETERMINANT-COLLISION LEDGER FOR THE TWO-SIDED LIT-INC CARRIER.

Let p be a prime and let d_1,d_2 be positive squarefree integers coprime to p. Put
 g=(d_1,d_2), d_1=gr_1, d_2=gr_2.                          (1)
Thus g,r_1,r_2 are pairwise coprime and squarefree. Let N,x_1,x_2 be coprime to pd_1d_2. Define
 cal C
 =e_{pd_1}(Nx_1^(-1))e_{pd_2}(-Nx_2^(-1)),                 (2)
and put
 Delta_car=x_1r_1-x_2r_2.                                  (3)
Then the primitive additive denominator of cal C is exactly
 q_prim=r_1r_2 {pg/(pg,Delta_car)}.                         (4)
Equivalently, every prime dividing r_1r_2 is active, while for a prime ell|pg the ell-local phase is trivial exactly when ell|Delta_car.

Apply this to the literal two-sided carrier in fact 75432ab3881c2178 by putting
 x_i=n_ik_i,
where s_1=d_1k_1 and q_2=d_2k_2. Then
 Delta_car=n_1k_1r_1-n_2k_2r_2.                            (5)
Moreover, in the literal notation of fact b9560e346963b9e0,
 A!=D if and only if p does not divide Delta_car.            (6)
Consequently every off-diagonal J_2 main subface retains p in its primitive denominator. Its complete primitive denominator is
 r_1r_2 {pg/(gcd(g,Delta_car))},                            (7)
because p does not divide Delta_car there. On the H_2 main face no A!=D restriction is present, and formula (4), including the possible p-collision, is exact.

No estimate for either collision sector, the carrier aggregate, LIT-INC-VLS, K_inc^rem, another incidence cell, C_small or Goldbach is asserted.
0029944864b851e8.proof:
Because d_i are squarefree, the two moduli in (2) have least common multiple
 pgr_1r_2.
We inspect the phase at each prime of this modulus.

Let ell|r_1. Then ell does not divide pd_2. The ell-local component of cal C comes only from the first factor in (2). Its numerator is N times units arising from x_1 and the CRT cofactor, so it is nonzero modulo ell. Hence ell is active. The same argument with the second factor proves that every ell|r_2 is active.

Now let ell|pg. Both factors contribute. Put
 H=pg/ell.
Since
 pd_1/ell=Hr_1, pd_2/ell=Hr_2,
the ell-local additive coefficient of (2) is
 N(Hr_1x_1)^(-1)-N(Hr_2x_2)^(-1)
 =NH^(-1){(x_1r_1)^(-1)-(x_2r_2)^(-1)} modulo ell.          (8)
Every factor outside the braces is a unit. The expression in braces is zero exactly when
 x_1r_1=x_2r_2 modulo ell,
which is exactly ell|Delta_car. Thus among the primes of pg, precisely those not dividing Delta_car remain active. Multiplying the always-active exclusive product r_1r_2 by the surviving shared product pg/(pg,Delta_car) proves (4).

For the literal application, fact 75432ab3881c2178 gives (2) with x_i=n_ik_i, proving (5). Put n_i=au_i. Since
 s_1=d_1k_1=gr_1k_1,
 q_2=d_2k_2=gr_2k_2,
and a,g are units modulo p, one has
 A=D
 if and only if
 u_1s_1=u_2q_2 modulo p
 if and only if
 n_1k_1r_1=n_2k_2r_2 modulo p
 if and only if
 p|Delta_car.                                               (9)
This proves (6). Under A!=D, the factor p is absent from (pg,Delta_car), so (4) becomes (7). The H_2 statement is simply (4) without imposing (6), completing the proof and all scope restrictions.

glossary.Delta_car: the determinant x_1r_1-x_2r_2 controlling cancellation on the shared carrier primes
glossary.q_prim: the primitive additive denominator of the two-sided carrier

006c61051140749b.title: Fix real numbers
006c61051140749b.author: slava chan
006c61051140749b.statement:
Fix real numbers
\[
 1/2<\alpha<\beta<1,\qquad \eta>0,\qquad \rho>0,\qquad B_{\rm src}>0.
\]
Let \(W\) and \(\Phi\) be bounded real functions supported respectively in
\([\alpha,\beta]\) and \([1/2,2]\). Let \(N=2x\) be an integer with \(x\ge3\), put
\[
 T_x=(\log x)^{6+\eta+\rho},
\]
and assume
\[
 {1\over2}x^{1/2}(\log x)^{-B_{\rm src}}\le D\le2x^{1/2},
 \qquad D>2T_x,\qquad U>0.
\]
Let \(\mu\) be the Möbius function, extend \(\Lambda\) by zero on nonpositive
integers, and define
\[
 {\cal I}_D=\{d\ge2:(d,N)=1,\ \mu(d)\ne0,\ d\le x^{1/2},\
 \Phi(d/D)\ne0\}.
\]
For positive integers \(s,m,w\), put
\[
 f_{s,m}(w)=
 {\bf1}_{sw\in{\cal I}_D}\mu(w)\Phi(sw/D)W(smw/x)
 \Phi((N-smw)/U)\Lambda(N-smw).
\]
For \(s\ge1\) and \(h\in\mathbb Z\), define the literal two-reflected-prime
correlation
\[
\begin{split}
 {\cal B}_s(h)=
 \sum_{\substack{m,w\ge1\\w-h\ge1}}
 &{\bf1}_{sw\in{\cal I}_D}{\bf1}_{s(w-h)\in{\cal I}_D}
 \mu(w)\mu(w-h)\Phi(sw/D)\Phi(s(w-h)/D)\\
 &\times W(smw/x)W(sm(w-h)/x)\\
 &\times\Phi((N-smw)/U)\Phi((N-sm(w-h))/U)\\
 &\times\Lambda(N-smw)\Lambda(N-sm(w-h)).
                                                               \tag{1}
\end{split}
\]
Define
\[
 c_{T_x}(s)=
 \sum_{\substack{gr=s\\1\le g<T_x\\1\le r<T_x}}\mu(r),
 \qquad
 \omega_s(h)=\min\left(1,{sT_x|h|\over D}\right).       \tag{2}
\]
Let \({\cal R}_{<}^{F}\) be the Fejer residual of fact
1024f6bb05c0bb49. Then the exact arithmetic expansion is
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 {\cal R}_{<}^{F}
 =
 \sum_{1\le s<T_x^2}c_{T_x}(s)
 \sum_{\substack{h\in\mathbb Z\\h\ne0}}
 \omega_s(h){\cal B}_s(h).
 \quad}                                                  \tag{3}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 c_{T_x}(1)=1,\qquad c_{T_x}(s)=0\quad(1<s<T_x),         \tag{4}
\]
so (3) consists of the \(s=1\) term and the boundary range
\(T_x\le s<T_x^2\), with the exact signed \(\mu(r)\)-sum retained inside
\(c_{T_x}(s)\).

For every nonzero summand in (1), put
\[
 d=sw,\qquad d'=s(w-h),\qquad
 p=N-dm,\qquad p'=N-d'm.                                \tag{5}
\]
Then
\[
 {D\over2}\le d,d'\le\min(2D,x^{1/2}),\qquad
 {\alpha x\over2D}\le m\le{2\beta x\over D},            \tag{6}
\]
\[
 p'=p+smh,\qquad d-d'=sh,\qquad
 \omega_s(h)=\min\left(1,{T_x|d-d'|\over D}\right),     \tag{7}
\]
and the two prime weights in (1) are exactly \(\Lambda(p)\Lambda(p')\).
Consequently the following arithmetic large-slope contract is exactly
equivalent to TB-FEJ-RES:
\[
 \sum_{1\le s<T_x^2}c_{T_x}(s)
 \sum_{h\ne0}\omega_s(h){\cal B}_s(h)
 \ll_{W,\Phi,\alpha,\beta,\eta,\rho}
 xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta}.                                  \tag{TB-AF}
\]

A literal Vaughan or Heath--Brown expansion does not by itself separate the
coefficient slots in (1). Precisely, if positive integers \(a_1,b_1\) satisfy
\[
 a_1b_1=N-smw,                                          \tag{8}
\]
then
\[
 sw\mid N-a_1b_1,\qquad
 m={N-a_1b_1\over sw},\qquad
 N-sm(w-h)=a_1b_1+smh
 ={hN+(w-h)a_1b_1\over w}.                              \tag{9}
\]
If the second prime is also represented as \(a_2b_2=N-sm(w-h)\), then
\[
 a_2b_2-a_1b_1=smh,\qquad N-a_1b_1=smw.                \tag{10}
\]
Thus the companion prime, the quotient \(m\), the Möbius factors, and the
cutoffs remain coupled to the divisor variables.

Even on the unit sector \((a_1,sw)=1\), the congruence in (8) only gives
\[
 b_1\equiv N a_1^{-1}\pmod {sw}.                        \tag{11}
\]
Completion or additive reciprocity can create a reciprocal phase from (11),
but the same summand still contains
\(\Lambda(a_1b_1+smh)\), \(m=(N-a_1b_1)/(sw)\), and all the joint cutoffs in
(1). Hence (11) alone does not produce coefficients independent of the
varying modulus.

In particular, the raw formula (3) is not a direct specialization of fact
73fb9efe1286f7e9: that fact starts with an explicit varying modulus \(q\), a
reciprocal phase \(e_q(A_qh(st)^{-1})\), and three coefficient sequences
independent of \(q\), whereas (3) has no reciprocal phase before an additional
transform and has the joint coefficient displayed in (1). It is also not a
direct application of the classical Barban--Davenport--Halberstam theorem
recorded in fact 9e1ff55fe17bc513, whose modulus range begins at
\(x(\log x)^{-A}\) for a fixed \(A>0\); the moduli in (6) are at most
\(x^{1/2}\), which is smaller than \(x(\log x)^{-A}\) for all sufficiently
large \(x\). These are scoped no-direct-fit statements. They do not exclude a
new Heath--Brown decomposition followed by a transform which separates the
joint coefficient, nor a new two-form large-sieve theorem retaining the
signed sum \(c_{T_x}(s)\mu(w)\mu(w-h)\).
006c61051140749b.proof:
Fact 1024f6bb05c0bb49 proves that
\[
 {\cal R}_{<}^{F}
 =
 \sum_{g<T_x}\sum_{r<T_x}\mu(r)
 \sum_{h\in\mathbb Z}
 \min\left(1,{grT_x|h|\over D}\right)C_{gr}(h),          \tag{12}
\]
where
\[
 C_s(h)=\sum_m\sum_{w-w'=h}f_{s,m}(w)f_{s,m}(w').       \tag{13}
\]
The coefficients are real, so no complex conjugation changes (13).
Set \(s=gr\) and \(w'=w-h\). Substitution of the displayed definition of
\(f_{s,m}\) into (13) gives exactly
\[
 C_s(h)={\cal B}_s(h).                                  \tag{14}
\]
The multiplier in (12) depends on \(g,r\) only through \(s=gr\). Grouping all
factorizations \(s=gr\) therefore gives the coefficient \(c_{T_x}(s)\) in
(2), and \(g,r<T_x\) implies \(s<T_x^2\). The multiplier at \(h=0\) is zero.
Equations (12)--(14) prove (3).

Fact 83c98e3d3a11382b proves (4). It may also be checked directly: when
\(1<s<T_x\), every divisor \(r\mid s\) satisfies \(r<T_x\) and \(s/r<T_x\),
so
\[
 c_{T_x}(s)=\sum_{r\mid s}\mu(r)=0.
\]
For \(s=1\), the only factorization is \(g=r=1\), so \(c_{T_x}(1)=1\).
This proves the asserted range decomposition without replacing the signed
coefficient by its absolute value.

If a term of (1) is nonzero, membership of \(d=sw\) and \(d'=s(w-h)\) in
\({\cal I}_D\), together with the support of \(\Phi\), gives
\[
 D/2\le d,d'\le2D,\qquad d,d'\le x^{1/2}.
\]
The two \(W\)-factors give
\[
 \alpha x\le dm\le\beta x,\qquad
 \alpha x\le d'm\le\beta x.
\]
Using \(d,d'\le2D\) for the lower bound on \(m\), and
\(d,d'\ge D/2\) for the upper bound, proves (6). The definitions (5) give
\[
 p'-p=(d-d')m=smh,\qquad d-d'=sh.
\]
Substitution into (2) proves (7). Hence the two final factors of (1) are
\(\Lambda(p)\Lambda(p')\). Equation (3) now proves the equivalence between
TB-AF and TB-FEJ-RES.

Suppose (8) holds. Rearranging it gives \(smw=N-a_1b_1\), which proves the
divisibility and quotient formula in (9). Furthermore,
\[
 N-sm(w-h)=N-smw+smh=a_1b_1+smh.
\]
Substituting \(sm=(N-a_1b_1)/w\) in the last term gives
\[
 a_1b_1+{h(N-a_1b_1)\over w}
 ={hN+(w-h)a_1b_1\over w}.
\]
This proves all of (9). If \(a_2b_2=N-sm(w-h)\), subtraction from (8) proves
the first equation in (10), and the second was already proved. Thus an
identity which expands either von Mangoldt factor leaves the other factor on
the coupled form in (9), while expanding both leaves the coupled system
(10).

On the sector \((a_1,sw)=1\), reducing (8) modulo \(sw\) and multiplying by
the inverse of \(a_1\) proves (11). The coefficient multiplying any phase
obtained from this congruence is still the literal summand (1). After (8) is
imposed, that summand contains the companion von Mangoldt factor shown in
(9), the quotient \(m\) shown in (9), and the \(s,m,w,h\)-dependent cutoffs.
Therefore the congruence does not itself separate those coefficient slots.

Fact 73fb9efe1286f7e9 requires, in its statement, a varying modulus \(q\), an
already present phase \(e_q(A_qh(st)^{-1})\), and independent coefficient
sequences in its three summation variables. Formula (3), before any further
transformation, has none of these separated data and instead has the joint
coefficient (1). This proves the stated literal no-direct-fit; it makes no
claim about the result of a future additional decomposition and transform.

Finally, fact 9e1ff55fe17bc513 records the classical
Barban--Davenport--Halberstam lower modulus condition
\(Q\ge x(\log x)^{-A}\) for fixed \(A>0\). For every fixed \(A\),
\[
 {x^{1/2}\over x(\log x)^{-A}}
 ={(\log x)^A\over x^{1/2}}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus the moduli \(d,d'\le x^{1/2}\) in (6) do not satisfy that hypothesis for
all sufficiently large \(x\). This proves the final scoped no-direct-fit
statement.

glossary.TB-AF: the exact arithmetic two-form restatement of TB-FEJ-RES
glossary.cal B_s(h): the literal grouped two-reflected-prime correlation at common divisor parameter s and quotient difference h
glossary.omega_s(h): the centered Fejer residual multiplier min(1,s*T_x*|h|/D)

01b550792363535d.title: POST-C3 SELECTED SAME-N LEDGER THROUGH THE SECOND-BUFFER AND GENERAL-MARKER INTERFACES
01b550792363535d.author: slava chan
01b550792363535d.statement:
POST-C3 SELECTED SAME-N LEDGER THROUGH THE SECOND-BUFFER AND GENERAL-MARKER INTERFACES.

Fix \(0<\kappa\le 1/100\), put
\[
 \sigma=\kappa/100,\qquad
 \beta _0=6/5-2\kappa,\qquad
 \beta _1=6/5-3\sigma,\qquad
 \beta_m=6/5-12\sigma/5,
\]
fix \(0<\eta<\sigma\) and \(\omega>0\), and put
\[
 \Gamma_{BC}(\beta)=\max\{0,(19\beta-20)/17\}.
\]
Let \(N=2x\) be the fixed selected bad even integer and let
\(T_{\rm late,sel}\) be the finite real same-selected-\(N\) aggregate of fact
\(dde1e246a629bcc4\). Thus
\[
 T_{\rm late,sel}\le
 -c_{\rm dir}\mathfrak c(N){x\over\log x}
 +o\!\left(\mathfrak c(N){x\over\log x}\right),             \tag{1}
\]
where \(c_{\rm dir}>0\), \(\mathfrak c(N)\ge C_2>0\), and every atom has
normalized exponent \(\beta>\beta_1\).

Retain on every atom its original selected source and active dyadic label, fixed
\(U\), high, smooth/projective, paired Fourier frequency, target-gcd,
rough-prime ordering, equal-cell, collision, deletion, provenance, exact
outer-gcd \(g\), orientation, parent, normalized marker and actual imbalance
\(G\) coordinates.  In the forward orientation
\[
 Q=D/g,\quad B=R/g=Q^\beta,\quad G=M/Q,
\]
and in the reverse orientation
\[
 Q=R/g,\quad B=D/g=Q^\beta,\quad G=K/Q.
\]

Let \(T_{\rm HG,sel}\) be the complete projection of
\(T_{\rm late,sel}\) onto
\[
 \beta_1<\beta<6/5,qquad
 G\ge Q^{\Gamma_{BC}(\beta)+\omega},                         \tag{2}
\]
with all other retained coordinates recombined to completion, and define
\[
 T_{\rm postC3,sel}=T_{\rm late,sel}-T_{\rm HG,sel}.           \tag{3}
\]
Then for some fixed \(\delta_{\rm HG}>0\),
\[
 |T_{\rm HG,sel}|\ll x^{1-\delta_{\rm HG}},                  \tag{4}
\]
and consequently
\[
 T_{\rm postC3,sel}\le
 -c_{\rm dir}\mathfrak c(N){x\over\log x}
 +o\!\left(\mathfrak c(N){x\over\log x}\right).             \tag{5}
\]

The aggregate in (3) is the exact disjoint union of the following three
sectors.

(i) The standard-marker second-buffer sector:
\[
 \beta_1<\beta<\beta_m,quad
 \text{orientation}\in\{\mathrm{forward},\mathrm{reverse}\},quad
 \text{parent}=U_{\rm low},
\]
\[
 \text{anatomy}\in\{A,B,C1,C2,C3\},qquad
 Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\le G<Q^{\Gamma_{BC}(\beta)+\omega}.       \tag{6}
\]
Here \(C0\) is empty.

(ii) The general-marker pre-\(6/5\) sliver:
\[
 \beta_m\le\beta<6/5,quad
 \text{orientation}\in\{\mathrm{forward},\mathrm{reverse}\},quad
 \text{parent}=U_{\rm low},
\]
\[
 \text{anatomy}\in\{C0,A,B,C1,\ldots,C_{J_\theta}\},qquad
 Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\le G<Q^{\Gamma_{BC}(\beta)+\omega},       \tag{7}
\]
where \(\theta\) is the retained frozen normalized layer and
\(J_\theta\) is its finite truncation index in the exact general marker
identity.  No standard three-rough-prime truncation is asserted in (7).

(iii) The inherited tail \(\beta\ge6/5\).  Every source, orientation,
parent, \(G\), marker and auxiliary label of this sector is retained exactly
as in \(T_{\rm late,sel}\); no parent collapse, finite standard anatomy
list, or further \(G\)-range assertion is made there.

The decomposition does not assign negativity to any one sector or cell.  It
makes no second-buffer anatomy estimate, endpoint, PMD, DCE, four-prime,
Goldbach implication, or Goldbach conclusion.
01b550792363535d.proof:
Fact \(dde1e246a629bcc4\) gives (1), the lower bound
\(\mathfrak c(N)\ge C_2\), and the exact support condition
\(\beta>\beta_1\), with every listed literal coordinate retained.

We first remove only a complete family already paid by the global coverage
theorem.  Part (D) of fact \(15425579cb248eff\) proves, at each exact outer
gcd and in both orientations, the complete fixed-g estimate
\[
 x^\epsilon\{G^{3/20}QB^{19/20}+Q^{7/8}B\}.
\]
For \(\beta<6/5\), its comparison with the fixed-g source scale pays every
parent and every normalized marker family satisfying (2), with a fixed
\(\omega\)-margin.  The same fact proves from forced high that \(Q\) is a
fixed positive power of \(x\) throughout this range, so the exact-g sum and
the polylogarithmically many retained labels preserve a fixed power saving.
The estimate retains the source masks and all the coordinates listed in the
statement.  Restricting it to the selected source and to
\(\beta>\beta_1\), and recombining the complete coordinates inside that
projection, proves (4).

Because \(\mathfrak c(N)\ge C_2>0\), (4) is
\(o(\mathfrak c(N)x/\log x)\).  The exact identity (3) and the real upper
bound (1) therefore prove (5).

It remains to identify the support of (3).  The post-low selected fact
\(7ffe3d237362a451\) proves that its remaining atoms have normalized base
larger than a fixed constant and \(\beta>\beta_0\), that \(U_{\rm sh}\)
is empty, and that for \(\beta<6/5\) the sole possible parent is
\(U_{\rm low}\).  These properties are inherited by every later
anatomy/beta subtraction, hence by \(T_{\rm late,sel}\).

For \(\beta_1<\beta<\beta_m\), fact \(cbfebc160d4bc310\) gives the
exact standard-marker Cartesian ledger
\[
 \{\mathrm{forward},\mathrm{reverse}\}\times
 \{C91,U_{\rm sh},U_{\rm low}\}\times
 \{A,B,C1,C2,C3\}
\]
after the accepted low-beta, empty-\(C0\), and large-imbalance payments,
with residual actual imbalance
\[
 Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\le G<Q^{\Gamma_{BC}(\beta)+\omega}.
\]
Intersecting with the selected parent conclusions of
\(7ffe3d237362a451\) leaves exactly (6).  The first-buffer subtractions
used to construct \(T_{\rm late,sel}\) have support
\(\beta_0<\beta\le\beta_1\), so they remove no atom in this open
second-buffer range.  Thus all five standard anatomies remain.

For \(\beta_m\le\beta<6/5\), Part (D) of
\(15425579cb248eff\), using the exact normalized identity
\(a71f777ad842c886\), gives the exhaustive layerwise list
\(C0,A,B,C1,\ldots,C_{J_\theta}\).  Its physical source lower bound for
actual \(G\) makes \(0<G<Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\) empty for sufficiently
large normalized base; the subtraction (2) removes exactly the opposite
high-\(G\) range.  The selected parent conclusion again leaves only
\(U_{\rm low}\).  This proves (7), without replacing the general marker
list by the standard list.

Finally facts \(15425579cb248eff\) and
\(7ffe3d237362a451\) explicitly stop their pre-endpoint parent/anatomy audit
at \(\beta<6/5\).  Hence the exact complement \(\beta\ge6/5\) can only
be carried forward with all inherited coordinates unchanged and no new
classification.  The three beta sectors are disjoint and exhaustive because
\(\beta_1<\beta_m<6/5\).  No sign was inferred for a proper projection,
which proves the final scope assertions.

glossary.J_theta: The finite rough-prime truncation index chosen on the frozen normalized layer in the exact general marker identity.
glossary.T_HG,sel: The complete pre-6/5 high-imbalance projection of the selected post-C3 tail.
glossary.T_postC3,sel: The selected post-C3 tail after the already-paid pre-6/5 high-imbalance sector is subtracted.
glossary.delta_HG: A fixed positive power-saving exponent for the selected high-imbalance projection.
glossary.theta: A frozen normalized layer carrying the original dyadic label, exact outer gcd, and orientation.

01ecc6fab24e57c6.title: LITERAL C4 MARKER GEOMETRY GIVES AN ALMOST-SQUARE-ROOT POINTWISE BOUND FOR EVERY PRIMITIVE-RAY K2 KERNEL. Fix the literal pre-6/5 C4 parameters of facts e58fc7c00f1683e6 and 9bee61f3627bd506:
01ecc6fab24e57c6.author: slava chan
01ecc6fab24e57c6.statement:
LITERAL C4 MARKER GEOMETRY GIVES AN ALMOST-SQUARE-ROOT POINTWISE BOUND FOR EVERY PRIMITIVE-RAY K2 KERNEL. Fix the literal pre-6/5 C4 parameters of facts e58fc7c00f1683e6 and 9bee61f3627bd506:
B=Q^beta,  Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma),  beta<6/5,
and let one C4 row have
B/2<=n<=2B,  n=Dv,  D=p_1p_2p_3p_4,
where v is a positive squarefree integer, the p_i are four distinct odd primes, every p_i>=Z, and gcd(D,v)=1. Assume the unit hypotheses of fact 34d306bcb630f9df for a primitive ray rho=(epsilon,a,b). Then its scoped six-sibling kernel satisfies
|K_{2,D,v}(rho)| <= 27/(2Z^2),                                    (1)
|K_{2,D,v}(rho)|^2 <= (729/2) B/(DZ^4)
 = (729/2) Q^(5beta-6+12sigma)/D
 <= (729/2) Q^(12sigma)/D.                                        (2)
The full kernel K_{2,D,v}^{full}(rho), including the exact small-v phase, has the same bounds. Equivalently, multiplication by the literal scoped K2 kernel on any finite primitive-ray coefficient space has l2 operator norm at most 27/(2Z^2). This is a uniform pointwise ray bound and materially limits the prime-imbalance obstruction of fact a411252e2c6ac7a7 on literal rows. It does not estimate the number of rays, the signed off-ray operator Rcal_{K2} of fact 134b03fc362a7cf1, the varying-row/common-source synthesis, C4, or Goldbach.
01ecc6fab24e57c6.proof:
Fact 34d306bcb630f9df gives, for every p dividing D,
Gamma_p(rho)=zeta_p(rho)+1/(p-1),
where |zeta_p(rho)|=1. Since p is an odd prime, p>=3 and therefore
|Gamma_p(rho)|<=1+1/(p-1)<=3/2.                                   (3)
The same fact gives the exact six-term formula
K_{2,D,v}(rho)
=sum_{S subset {p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4}, |S|=2}
 (product_{p in S}Gamma_p(rho))
 (product_{p dividing D, p notin S}(-1/p)).                        (4)
For each of the six two-element sets S, (3) bounds the active product by 9/4. The two inactive primes are each at least Z, so the inactive reciprocal product is at most Z^(-2). Applying the triangle inequality to the six terms in (4) gives
|K_{2,D,v}(rho)|<=6*(9/4)*Z^(-2)=27/(2Z^2),
which proves (1). Squaring gives
|K_{2,D,v}(rho)|^2<=729/(4Z^4).                                   (5)

By fact 9bee61f3627bd506, n=Dv with v a positive integer, so D<=n. By the literal dyadic support in fact e58fc7c00f1683e6, n<=2B. Hence D<=2B, or B/D>=1/2. It follows from (5) that
729/(4Z^4) <= (729/2) B/(DZ^4).                                   (6)
The definitions of B and Z give the exact identity
B/Z^4
=Q^[beta-4(3/2-beta-3sigma)]
=Q^(5beta-6+12sigma).                                              (7)
Since beta<6/5, the exponent in (7) is less than 12sigma, and Q>1 yields
B/Z^4<=Q^(12sigma).                                                (8)
Equations (6)-(8) prove (2).

Fact 34d306bcb630f9df also gives
K_{2,D,v}^{full}(rho)
=e_v(A epsilon b(aD)^(-1))K_{2,D,v}(rho).
The prefactor has absolute value one, so all the same bounds hold for the full kernel. Finally, a diagonal multiplication operator on l2 has operator norm equal to the supremum of the multiplier magnitudes; (1) proves the stated l2 multiplier bound. Fact a411252e2c6ac7a7 concerns unrestricted CRT ray residues and is therefore compatible with the additional literal constraints used here. No summation over distinct rays or rows has been performed.

0220ab16ae677eec.title: ACTUAL-MASK EXCEPTIONAL LEDGER FOR THE ONE-ROUGH PMD SQUARE
0220ab16ae677eec.author: slava chan
0220ab16ae677eec.statement:
ACTUAL-MASK EXCEPTIONAL LEDGER FOR THE ONE-ROUGH PMD SQUARE.

Fix C_A>=1, 0<kappa<1/10, 0<=sigma<3kappa, and 0<delta<1/10. Let Q be sufficiently large and let
  1<=H<=Q^(1/3-kappa),
  1<=V<=H^2Q^sigma,
  P=QH/V>=2.                                                (1)
Let A be a nonzero integer with |A|<=Q^C_A. Let Phi be a fixed smooth function supported in [-2,-1] union [1,2], and put
  K_{v,p}(r)=|Phihat(-Hr/(vp))|.
Restrict V<=v<2V, P<=p<2P with p prime, Q<=q_i<2Q, gcd(v,p)=1, and gcd(vp,q_1q_2)=1. For r in Z define
  F=A(q_2-q_1)-rq_1q_2.                                    (2)
For a set S of these tuples define the literal centered square ledger
  E_act(S)=QH sum_S K_{v,p}(r)1_{v|F}
                    |1_{p|F}-1/p|.                         (3)
This is the absolute exceptional-sector ledger attached to the exact actual-source identity in fact dbe03cbcb7136c4c.

Put
  R_small=Q^(1-delta)/H,
  G_large=HQ^delta.                                        (4)
Then, for every epsilon>0,

(a) E_act(0<|r|<=R_small, F nonzero)
    <<Q^(4-delta+epsilon).

(b) E_act(gcd(q_1,q_2)>=G_large, r nonzero, F nonzero)
    <<Q^(4-delta+epsilon).

(c) E_act(r nonzero, F=0)<<Q^(2+epsilon)H^2.

(d) E_act(r=0)<<Q^(3+epsilon)H(V+H).

Together with the pre-Poisson q-diagonal bound Q^(3+epsilon)H^2 from fact e68c309611367942, all these sectors total O(Q^(4-eta)) for some eta=eta(kappa,sigma,delta)>0. Hence the exceptional-zone conclusions of that separated model remain power-small for the literal coupled mask v|F. The remaining actual-mask sector has
  q_1 not equal q_2,
  |r|>Q^(1-delta)/H,
  gcd(q_1,q_2)<HQ^delta,
  F nonzero.                                                (5)
No cancellation estimate for (5) is asserted.
0220ab16ae677eec.proof:
The scale hypotheses give P/H=Q/V>2 for sufficiently large Q, so fact dbe03cbcb7136c4c applies. Smoothness gives, uniformly on p comparable to P and v comparable to V,
  K_{v,p}(r)<<_{Phi,J}(1+|r|/Q)^(-J),                       (6)
because vp/H is comparable to VP/H=Q. Thus r outside a fixed polynomial range is negligible after choosing J large. On the polynomial range, every nonzero F has polynomial size and the divisor bound gives tau(|F|)<<Q^epsilon.

For (a), fix r,q_1,q_2 with F nonzero. The conditions v|F and p|F restrict v and p to divisors of F, hence their joint indicator contribution has O(Q^epsilon) choices after adjusting epsilon. For the centered part, there are O(Q^epsilon) choices of v|F and sum_{p comparable to P}1/p=O(1). Therefore the complete v,p sum is O(Q^epsilon). There are O(R_small Q^2) choices of r,q_1,q_2, and multiplying by QH gives (a).

For (b), the number of q-pairs with gcd(q_1,q_2)>=G_large is O(Q^2/G_large). For each such pair, (6) gives total effective r-length O(Q). At F nonzero, the simultaneous divisor restrictions in v and p cost Q^epsilon, and the centered p-part again costs O(Q^epsilon). Thus
  E_act<<QH (Q^2/G_large)Q^(1+epsilon)
       =Q^(4-delta+epsilon),
proving (b).

For (c), the factorization argument in fact e68c309611367942 proves that there are O(Q^epsilon) triples (q_1,q_2,r) with r nonzero and F=0. The literal condition v|F is then automatic for every v, as is p|F for every p. There are O(VP)=O(QH) pairs (v,p), and K is bounded. Multiplication by the outer QH in (3) gives
  E_act<<QH*QH*Q^epsilon=Q^(2+epsilon)H^2.

For (d), discard the condition v|F, which only enlarges the nonnegative ledger. The r=0 proof in fact e68c309611367942 then applies verbatim: primes not dividing A force q_1 congruent q_2 modulo p, primes dividing A are divisor-many, and the result is Q^(3+epsilon)H(V+H).

Finally, H<=Q^(1/3-kappa) and V<=H^2Q^sigma imply
  Q^3HV<=Q^(4-3kappa+sigma),
  Q^3H^2<=Q^(4-(1/3+2kappa)),
  Q^2H^2<=Q^(8/3-2kappa).
Because sigma<3kappa, these bounds and (a)-(b) all save a fixed power after epsilon is chosen small. This proves the final assertion.

glossary.E_act: The absolute exceptional-sector ledger with the literal coupled condition v divides F and centered prime incidence retained.
glossary.actual-mask sector: A PMD tuple carrying the exact small-v divisibility mask from the full CRT source.

02510b4e3b1c1fc3.title: ZERO-COFACTOR HARD-SOURCE QUARTIC SECTOR IS ABSOLUTELY PAID
02510b4e3b1c1fc3.author: slava chan
02510b4e3b1c1fc3.statement:
ZERO-COFACTOR HARD-SOURCE QUARTIC SECTOR IS ABSOLUTELY PAID.

Adopt the scale, labels, height intervals, hard-source atom sets, and coefficient bound of fact 95058e339b3441a3. In particular,
  2<=H<=Q^(1/3),  2<=V<H,  P=QH/V,
and every atom x=(q,m,k) in cal X_{lambda,v,p} satisfies
  Q<=q,m<2Q,  qm+vpk=A,  gcd(qm,vp)=1,
while |a_{lambda,v,p,h}(x)|<=B. Here lambda denotes the pre-existing projective label and is unrelated to the cofactor below.

For each atom define its source cofactor
  ell(x)=vk=(A-qm)/p.
Let M_zero be any sub-sum of the complete hard-source fourth-moment expansion over projective labels lambda, integers V<=v<2V, primes P<=p<2P, heights
  h_i in I_lambda,  h_1+h_2=h_3+h_4,
and four atoms x_i in cal X_{lambda,v,p}, whose support requires ell(x_i)=0 for at least one i. The summand may retain the complete literal phases, every source/projective mask, and any further deletion of tuples; assume only that its modulus is at most
  B^4 product_{i=1}^4 1_{x_i in cal X_{lambda,v,p}}.
Then for every epsilon>0,
  |M_zero| <<_{C,epsilon} B^4 #cal L Q^(4+epsilon)H.
Moreover,
  Q^4 H <= P^2 Q^(7/3).
Thus, under the usual subpolynomial bounds on B and #cal L, every hard-source quartic subrange containing at least one zero cofactor is within the vector target
  Q^epsilon P^2 Q^(7/3).
Consequently the unproved OSC cross-Gram supplier of fact ad79e2b004abf5ec may be restricted to tuples for which all four source cofactors are nonzero. This statement estimates no part of that remaining all-nonzero sector and makes no PMD or Goldbach conclusion.
02510b4e3b1c1fc3.proof:
By fact 5a334011a0da2a70,
  ell(x)=0
is equivalent to qm=A, and the source equation then forces k=0. Hence, at fixed lambda,v,p, the number Z_{lambda,v,p} of zero-cofactor atoms is at most the number of factor pairs (q,m) with qm=A, namely
  Z_{lambda,v,p} <= tau(|A|) <<_{C,epsilon} Q^epsilon.       (1)
Fact 914048233fada05f gives for the whole hard-source atom set
  X_{lambda,v,p}:=#cal X_{lambda,v,p}
  <<_{C,epsilon} Q^epsilon Q/H.                             (2)

There are O(H^3) height quadruples satisfying h_1+h_2=h_3+h_4: choose h_1,h_2,h_3, after which h_4 is determined. Use the union bound over the four possible positions of a zero-cofactor atom. For a fixed position, (1) gives at most Z choices there and (2) gives at most X choices for each of the remaining three atoms. Since all retained phases and masks have modulus at most one, the contribution at fixed lambda,v,p is at most
  O(B^4 H^3 Z_{lambda,v,p} X_{lambda,v,p}^3)
  <<_{C,epsilon} B^4 Q^epsilon H^3 (Q/H)^3
  =B^4 Q^(3+epsilon).                                       (3)
The union over the four positions changes only the implied constant.

There are O(V) allowed integers v and O(P) primes p, so summing (3) over lambda,v,p gives
  |M_zero|
  <<_{C,epsilon} B^4 #cal L V P Q^(3+epsilon)
  =B^4 #cal L Q^(4+epsilon)H,                               (4)
because VP=QH.

Finally,
  P^2 Q^(7/3)/(Q^4H)
  =(Q^2H^2/V^2)Q^(7/3)/(Q^4H)
  =Q^(1/3)H/V^2.
Since V<H and H<=Q^(1/3), one has V^2<H^2<=Q^(1/3)H, so the last ratio exceeds one. This proves the target comparison. Removing the paid zero-cofactor sector leaves only tuples with every ell(x_i) nonzero in the remaining OSC interface.

0299d6fc830c8f33.title: FIXED-PRIME SCALAR RECIPROCAL-FRAME LARGE SIEVE WITH THE LITERAL UNIT MASK
0299d6fc830c8f33.author: slava chan
0299d6fc830c8f33.statement:
FIXED-PRIME SCALAR RECIPROCAL-FRAME LARGE SIEVE WITH THE LITERAL UNIT MASK.

Let p>2 be a prime, let A be a nonzero residue modulo p, and let I,J be integer intervals containing at most Q and S integers, respectively, where Q,S>=1. Let eta_u be arbitrary complex numbers indexed by u in J. For every integer a in I with p not dividing a, define
 T_{p,A}eta(a)
  = sum_{u in J; p not dividing u}
      eta_u {e_p(A(au)^(-1))+1/(p-1)},                    (1)
where the inverse is taken modulo p. Then
 sum_{a in I; p not dividing a}|T_{p,A}eta(a)|^2
 <=(Q/p+1)(S+p)
   sum_{u in J; p not dividing u}|eta_u|^2.               (2)
If Q,S>=p, then
 sum_{a in I; p not dividing a}|T_{p,A}eta(a)|^2
 <=4QS/p
   sum_{u in J; p not dividing u}|eta_u|^2.               (3)

This is a scalar estimate: eta_u is independent of a. No estimate with an arbitrary a-dependent complementary tensor, no ROP estimate, no CEN-MZB estimate, no C_small estimate and no Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
0299d6fc830c8f33.proof:
For each nonzero residue C modulo p put
 E_C=sum_{u in J; p not dividing u; A u^(-1)=C (mod p)} eta_u.
Then (1) becomes
 T_{p,A}eta(a)=sum_{C nonzero mod p}E_C r_C(a),
where r_C(a)=e_p(Ca^(-1))+1/(p-1) is the frame row of fact 0d1daae6c3854186.

Each nonzero residue a_0 modulo p occurs at most Q/p+1 times among the integers a in I. Therefore
 sum_{a in I;p not dividing a}|T_{p,A}eta(a)|^2
 <=(Q/p+1) sum_{a_0 mod p;a_0 nonzero}
      |sum_C E_C r_C(a_0)|^2.
The exact frame identity in fact 0d1daae6c3854186 gives
 sum_{a_0 nonzero}|sum_C E_C r_C(a_0)|^2
 =p{sum_C|E_C|^2-(p-1)^(-1)|sum_C E_C|^2}
 <=p sum_C|E_C|^2.

For a fixed C, the condition A u^(-1)=C modulo p selects one nonzero residue class of u modulo p. That residue class occurs at most S/p+1 times in J. Cauchy's inequality in each residue class, followed by summation over C, gives
 sum_C|E_C|^2
 <=(S/p+1)sum_{u in J;p not dividing u}|eta_u|^2.
Multiplying the last three estimates proves
 (Q/p+1)p(S/p+1)=(Q/p+1)(S+p),
which is (2). If Q,S>=p, then Q/p+1<=2Q/p and S+p<=2S, proving (3).

glossary.E_C: the sum of input coefficients in the unique u residue class corresponding to the frame index C
glossary.I: the integer input interval in the averaging variable a
glossary.J: the integer coefficient interval in the variable u
glossary.T_{p,A}: the fixed-prime scalar reciprocal-frame operator defined in (1)
glossary.eta_u: the scalar input coefficient attached to u

02a763eba051c761.title: Assume all hypotheses and notation of fact bc46ed5832faeade. In particular, \(N=2x\), \(D\le 2x^{1/2}\),
02a763eba051c761.author: slava chan
02a763eba051c761.statement:
Assume all hypotheses and notation of fact bc46ed5832faeade. In particular, \(N=2x\), \(D\le 2x^{1/2}\),
\[
 D\ge {1\over2}x^{1/2}(\log x)^{-B_{\rm src}},\qquad
 T_x=(\log x)^{6+\eta+\rho},
\]
\[
 {\cal I}_D=\{d\ge2:(d,N)=1,\ \mu(d)\ne0,\ d\le x^{1/2},\
                    \Phi(d/D)\ne0\},
\quad
 V_{d,m}=W(dm/x)\Phi((N-dm)/U),
\]
and
\[
 {\cal Z}_\star=\{(d_1,d_2)\in{\cal I}_D^2:
 d_1\ne d_2,\ |d_1-d_2|>D/T_x,\ (d_1,d_2)<T_x\}.
\]
Extend the von Mangoldt function by zero on nonpositive integers, and write
\[
 \Lambda_{\rm pp}(n)=\Lambda(n)-\Lambda_{\rm pr}(n),
\]
so \(\Lambda_{\rm pp}\) is supported on proper prime powers \(p^j\) with \(j\ge2\). Define
\[
 {\mathfrak C}_\star^\Lambda=
 \sum_{(d_1,d_2)\in{\cal Z}_\star}
 \mu(d_1)\mu(d_2)\Phi(d_1/D)\Phi(d_2/D)
 \sum_{m\ge1}V_{d_1,m}V_{d_2,m}
 \Lambda(N-d_1m)\Lambda(N-d_2m).                         \tag{1}
\]
Then, for every fixed \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 {\mathfrak C}_\star^\Lambda-{\mathfrak C}_\star
 \ll_{\varepsilon,W,\Phi}D x^{1/2+\varepsilon}(\log x)^2. \tag{2}
\]
Consequently, for every fixed \(A>0\),
\[
 {\mathfrak C}_\star^\Lambda-{\mathfrak C}_\star
 =o_{A,W,\Phi}\!\left(xD(\log x)^{-A}\right).             \tag{3}
\]

There is the following exact shifted-quotient reindexing. For integers
\(h\ne0\), \(m\ge1\), and \(p\), put \(d=(N-p)/m\) when \(m\mid N-p\), and define
\[
\begin{split}
 \Omega_N(h,m,p)={}&
 {\bf1}_{\substack{m\mid N-p,\ d\in{\cal I}_D,\ d+h\in{\cal I}_D\\
                    |h|>D/T_x,\ (d,h)<T_x}}
 \mu(d)\mu(d+h)\Phi(d/D)\Phi((d+h)/D)\\
 &\times W((N-p)/x)W((N-p+hm)/x)
 \Phi(p/U)\Phi((p-hm)/U)\Lambda(p)\Lambda(p-hm).
\end{split}                                                            \tag{4}
\]
Then
\[
 {\mathfrak C}_\star^\Lambda
 =\sum_{h\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}}\sum_{m\ge1}\sum_{p\in\mathbb Z}
   \Omega_N(h,m,p).                                      \tag{5}
\]
In particular, \((d,d+h)= (d,h)\), so the literal hard-core greatest-common-divisor condition is preserved exactly.

More generally, let \(\alpha,\beta\) be finitely supported complex sequences and let
\[
 (\alpha*\beta)(n)=\sum_{rs=n}\alpha(r)\beta(s)
\]
for positive integers \(n\), extended by zero otherwise. Let
\({\mathfrak C}_\star[\alpha*\beta,\Lambda]\) be the expression in (1) with the first factor
\(\Lambda(N-d_1m)\) replaced by \((\alpha*\beta)(N-d_1m)\), while the second factor remains \(\Lambda(N-d_2m)\). Then exactly
\[
\begin{split}
 {\mathfrak C}_\star[\alpha*\beta,\Lambda]
 =\sum_{\substack{h\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}\\m,r,s\ge1\\m\mid N-rs}}
 &{\bf1}_{\substack{d=(N-rs)/m\in{\cal I}_D,\ d+h\in{\cal I}_D\\
                    |h|>D/T_x,\ (d,h)<T_x}}
 \alpha(r)\beta(s)\mu(d)\mu(d+h)\\
 &\times\Phi(d/D)\Phi((d+h)/D)
 W((N-rs)/x)W((N-rs+hm)/x)\\
 &\times\Phi(rs/U)\Phi((rs-hm)/U)\Lambda(rs-hm).
\end{split}                                                            \tag{6}
\]
Thus any exact finite decomposition of the first von Mangoldt factor into convolution components inherits (6) componentwise. The two raw Möbius weights become
\[
 \mu((N-rs)/m)\mu((N-rs)/m+h),
\]
the integrality condition is \(m\mid N-rs\), and the second von Mangoldt argument is \(rs-hm\). Equations (2)--(6) are exact reductions; they assert no saving for the right side of (6) and do not prove (TB-HARD).
02a763eba051c761.proof:
We first compare the prime-only and full von Mangoldt covariances. Since
\(\Lambda=\Lambda_{\rm pr}+\Lambda_{\rm pp}\), the difference between (1) and
\({\mathfrak C}_\star\) is a sum of three terms, and every contributing triple
\((d_1,d_2,m)\) has at least one of \(N-d_1m,N-d_2m\) equal to a proper prime power.

We count triples for which \(N-d_1m=q\) is a proper prime power. The number of such \(q<N\) is
\[
 \sum_{2\le j\le\log_2N}N^{1/j}\ll N^{1/2}\log N\ll x^{1/2}\log x.       \tag{7}
\]
For a fixed \(q\), the equation \(d_1m=N-q\) gives at most
\(\tau(N-q)\) choices for \((d_1,m)\). For every fixed
\(\varepsilon>0\), the elementary divisor estimate
\[
 \tau(n)\ll_\varepsilon n^\varepsilon                                  \tag{8}
\]
holds. For completeness, choose \(P=2^{2/\varepsilon}\). If
\(n=\prod p^{a_p}\), then for \(p\ge P\), \(a_p+1\le p^{\varepsilon a_p/2}\).
For the finitely many \(p<P\), there is a constant \(C_{\varepsilon,p}\) such that
\(a+1\le C_{\varepsilon,p}p^{\varepsilon a/2}\) for all \(a\ge0\).
Multiplication gives \(\tau(n)\le C_\varepsilon n^{\varepsilon/2}\), which implies (8).

After \((q,d_1,m)\) is chosen, there are \(O(D)\) possible \(d_2\), because
\(\Phi(d_2/D)\ne0\) forces \(D/2\le d_2\le2D\). Thus the number of triples with the first argument a proper prime power is
\[
 \ll_\varepsilon D x^{1/2+\varepsilon}.                                \tag{9}
\]
The same argument applies when the second argument is a proper prime power. Every smooth weight is bounded and every von Mangoldt or prime-only weight occurring here is \(O(\log x)\). Equations (7)--(9), after absorbing their one extra logarithm into \(x^\varepsilon\), prove (2).

By the lower bound on \(D\),
\[
 xD(\log x)^{-A}\gg x^{3/2}(\log x)^{-A-B_{\rm src}},
\]
whereas the right side of (2), with \(\varepsilon=1/8\), is
\(O(x^{9/8}(\log x)^2)\) because \(D\le2x^{1/2}\). Their ratio tends to zero for every fixed \(A\), proving (3).

We prove (5). Given a triple \((d_1,d_2,m)\) in (1), put
\[
 h=d_2-d_1,\qquad p=N-d_1m.
\]
Then \(h\ne0\), \(m\mid N-p\), and \(d_1=(N-p)/m\). Moreover
\[
 N-d_2m=N-(d_1+h)m=p-hm,                                \tag{10}
\]
\[
 (d_1,d_2)=(d_1,d_2-d_1)=(d_1,h).                       \tag{11}
\]
The smooth factors transform identically:
\[
 V_{d_1,m}=W((N-p)/x)\Phi(p/U),
\]
\[
 V_{d_2,m}=W((N-p+hm)/x)\Phi((p-hm)/U).                  \tag{12}
\]
Equations (10)--(12) show that the summand in (1) is exactly (4).

Conversely, every nonzero term in (4) determines
\[
 d_1=(N-p)/m,\qquad d_2=d_1+h.
\]
Its indicator puts \((d_1,d_2)\) in \({\cal Z}_\star\), and (10)--(12) reverse. The two maps are inverse, proving the bijection and (5).

Finally replace the first \(\Lambda\) in (1) by
\[
 (\alpha*\beta)(N-d_1m)=\sum_{rs=N-d_1m}\alpha(r)\beta(s).
\]
All sums are finite on the support of the weights and of \(\alpha,\beta\), so their order may be interchanged. Put \(h=d_2-d_1\). The equation \(rs=N-d_1m\) is equivalent to
\[
 m\mid N-rs,\qquad d_1=(N-rs)/m,
\]
and the second argument is
\[
 N-d_2m=N-(d_1+h)m=rs-hm.
\]
Using (11)--(12) with \(p=rs\) gives exactly (6). Linearity proves the assertion for every finite sum of convolution components.

glossary.Lambda_pp: the higher-prime-power part of the von Mangoldt function
glossary.Omega_N(h,m,p): the exact shifted-quotient summand after setting h=d2-d1 and p=N-d1m
glossary.mathfrak C_star[alpha*beta,Lambda]: the hard-core covariance with the first von Mangoldt factor replaced by the convolution alpha*beta
glossary.mathfrak C_star^Lambda: the hard-core covariance with full von Mangoldt weights

02d47d6aa2984aae.title: PAIR NONRESONANCE DOES NOT EXCLUDE A CONSTANT EFFECTIVE PHASE IN ONE ROW. Let p be a prime, let mathscr A be an integer with p not dividing mathscr A, and let q_1,q_2 be integers with p not dividing q_1q_2. Put
02d47d6aa2984aae.author: slava chan
02d47d6aa2984aae.statement:
PAIR NONRESONANCE DOES NOT EXCLUDE A CONSTANT EFFECTIVE PHASE IN ONE ROW. Let p be a prime, let mathscr A be an integer with p not dividing mathscr A, and let q_1,q_2 be integers with p not dividing q_1q_2. Put
h_1=p,  h_2=1,
Delta=h_1q_2-h_2q_1.
Then
p does not divide mathscr A Delta,
but
p divides mathscr A h_1.                                      (1)
If the marked dilator is d_lambda=p, then p is the first nonresonant prime selected from the pair determinant in facts 4f9aec67f5be35db and ff228b0e569531f8. If the first row has squarefree reciprocal modulus n_1=p and numerator C_1=mathscr A h_1, then
n_1/gcd(C_1,n_1)=1.                                           (2)
Consequently the first-nonresonant pair mask alone cannot exclude the m_eff=1 chamber or imply nonresonance of each individual row numerator. This is an algebraic no-go for the rowwise nonresonance shortcut; it does not assert that the displayed heights belong to every physical support block.
02d47d6aa2984aae.proof:
Modulo p one has
Delta=pq_2-q_1 congruent to -q_1.
Because p does not divide q_1, the residue Delta is nonzero modulo p. Since p does not divide mathscr A, the residue mathscr A Delta is also nonzero modulo p. This proves the first assertion in (1). The equality h_1=p gives p divides mathscr A h_1, proving the second assertion.

When d_lambda=p, its only prime divisor is p. The definition of the first nonresonant prime in facts 4f9aec67f5be35db and ff228b0e569531f8 therefore selects p because p does not divide mathscr A Delta; there is no earlier divisor prime to test.

Finally n_1=p and C_1=mathscr A p give gcd(C_1,n_1)=p, so n_1/gcd(C_1,n_1)=1. The construction simultaneously satisfies pair nonresonance and constant effective phase in the first row. Hence the pair condition cannot logically imply the claimed rowwise exclusion. The final scope restriction follows because no Archimedean height-support hypothesis was imposed.

glossary.rowwise nonresonance shortcut: The invalid inference that a pair-selected nonresonant prime is nonresonant in each individual row numerator.

0418d8cd300ae161.title: Let S_H be the determinant-4 shell from fact 89b262fc9d54d792, and for j in Z let S_H(j) be the subset on which J=ab-cd=j. Then for every epsilon>0, uniformly in j, |S_H(j)|<<_epsilon H^epsilon, while the set of realized values {j:S_H(j) is nonempty} has cardinality at least H^{6-epsilon} for all sufficiently large H. Every realized j satisfies |j|<=2H^6. Hence the H^{6+o(1)} determinant shell cannot be covered by H^{6-delta} fixed-J slices for any fixed delta>0. Moreover, in every normalized unit state of fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb with K=2, one has J=4uv and abcd=4-J^2/4, so fixed J is simultaneously fixed uv and fixed quadratic-form discriminant
0418d8cd300ae161.author: slava chan
0418d8cd300ae161.statement: Let S_H be the determinant-4 shell from fact 89b262fc9d54d792, and for j in Z let S_H(j) be the subset on which J=ab-cd=j. Then for every epsilon>0, uniformly in j, |S_H(j)|<<_epsilon H^epsilon, while the set of realized values {j:S_H(j) is nonempty} has cardinality at least H^{6-epsilon} for all sufficiently large H. Every realized j satisfies |j|<=2H^6. Hence the H^{6+o(1)} determinant shell cannot be covered by H^{6-delta} fixed-J slices for any fixed delta>0. Moreover, in every normalized unit state of fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb with K=2, one has J=4uv and abcd=4-J^2/4, so fixed J is simultaneously fixed uv and fixed quadratic-form discriminant.
0418d8cd300ae161.proof:
On S_H one has ab+cd=4 and J=ab-cd. Therefore
ab=(4+J)/2 and cd=(4-J)/2.
Because a,b,c,d are nonzero, both products are nonzero, so J is not 4 or -4. If J=j is fixed and the displayed halves are not integers, the fibre is empty. Otherwise the number of ordered nonzero integer pairs (a,b) with their product fixed is twice the divisor function of |(4+j)/2|, and similarly for (c,d). Ignoring the evenness and box restrictions only enlarges the count. Since |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|<=H^3, each nonzero product has absolute value at most H^6. The elementary bound tau(n)<<_eta n^eta gives |S_H(j)|<<_eta H^{12eta}; choosing eta=epsilon/12 proves the uniform H^epsilon fibre bound.

Fact 89b262fc9d54d792 gives |S_H|>>H^6. Since S_H is the disjoint union of the fibres S_H(j), the number of nonempty fibres is at least |S_H| divided by their maximum size, and hence is >>_epsilon H^{6-epsilon}. Absorbing the constant by slightly enlarging epsilon gives the stated lower bound for sufficiently large H. Also |J|=|ab-cd|<=|ab|+|cd|<=2H^6.

If the realized J-values were contained in O(H^{6-delta}) slices for some fixed delta>0, the uniform fibre estimate with epsilon<delta/2 would give |S_H|=O(H^{6-delta/2}), contradicting fact 89b262fc9d54d792. Finally fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb states, for every normalized unit state, J=4uv and abcd=K^2-4u^2v^2. Substituting K=2 and J=4uv yields abcd=4-J^2/4. Thus fixing J fixes both uv and the discriminant 4abcd of the associated diagonal quadratic form.

glossary.S_H(j): The subset of the determinant-4 shell S_H on which ab-cd=j.

0437c7a25bf0c1c5.title: LITERAL C1 SMOOTH-COFACTOR REFINEMENT OF THE GENUINE UNBALANCED A-DIVISOR GAP. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, eta=kappa/20, and s=kappa/100, and let beta_m<=beta<6/5 in the literal strict-top C1 setting. Thus n=pv is squarefree, p is the unique rough prime, gcd(p,v)=1, every prime divisor of v is at most
0437c7a25bf0c1c5.author: slava chan
0437c7a25bf0c1c5.statement:
LITERAL C1 SMOOTH-COFACTOR REFINEMENT OF THE GENUINE UNBALANCED A-DIVISOR GAP. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, eta=kappa/20, and s=kappa/100, and let beta_m<=beta<6/5 in the literal strict-top C1 setting. Thus n=pv is squarefree, p is the unique rough prime, gcd(p,v)=1, every prime divisor of v is at most
L_0=Q^(beta-1+sigma),
C=mathscr A h, and m_eff=n/gcd(C,n). Assume Q^(1/2+kappa)<=m_eff<=Q^(6/5). In one MULTI-FREE box of fact 8eb30e55bdef6b27, with delta=rho=kappa/200, let B_* be the largest omitted coefficient-one scale and put
X_A=max{Q^(4s),m_eff Q^(2s)/B_*},
Y_A=B_*^2Q^(-4s).
Assume the box lies in the genuine divisor-gap class (R3) of fact 1c42e0c22d9a5cca, so X_A<=Y_A and [X_A,Y_A] contains no divisor of m_eff.

Then the box belongs to the following disjoint union, in the displayed order:
(G1) B_*^2<L_0Q^(8s);
(G2) B_*^2>=L_0Q^(8s) and B_*^3<L_0m_eff Q^(6s);
(G3) both reversed weak inequalities hold, p does not divide C, and, with r_eff=m_eff/p, one has r_eff<X_A.
In particular, when p divides C, every genuine divisor gap is forced by one of the two explicit width failures (G1)-(G2). When both width inequalities are favorable, the only remaining gap is the dynamic near-prime condition (G3). This is an exact necessary classification of (R3), not an estimate for its three subfamilies.
0437c7a25bf0c1c5.proof:
The MULTI-FREE omitted-factor bound and the calculation in fact 8f9c29373de3486c give
B_*>Q^(b-a-o(1)),  b-a>=8kappa/5.
Hence B_*>Q^(2s) for sufficiently large Q. Also m_eff>=Q^(1/2+kappa)>Q^(4s). Therefore
Q^(4s)<m_eff,  m_eff Q^(2s)/B_*<m_eff,
so
X_A<m_eff.                                                     (1)

Suppose neither (G1) nor (G2) holds. Then
B_*^2>=L_0Q^(8s),
B_*^3>=L_0m_eff Q^(6s).                                        (2)
Since Y_A=B_*^2Q^(-4s), the first inequality in (2) gives
Y_A>=L_0Q^(4s),
and the second gives
Y_A>=L_0m_eff Q^(2s)/B_*.
Consequently
Y_A>=L_0X_A.                                                    (3)

We use a deterministic smooth-divisor lemma. If w is a positive squarefree integer all of whose prime divisors are at most L_0 and w>=X_A, multiply its prime divisors in any fixed order until the product d first reaches X_A. The preceding product is below X_A and the last prime is at most L_0, so
X_A<=d<X_AL_0<=Y_A                                             (4)
by (3). Thus d is a divisor in the forbidden interval.

Because n is squarefree, m_eff consists of the prime divisors of n not dividing C. If p divides C, then m_eff divides v. It is therefore L_0-smooth, and (1) permits the smooth-divisor lemma with w=m_eff. Equation (4) contradicts (R3). Hence, outside (G1)-(G2), p cannot divide C.

If p does not divide C, then p divides m_eff and r_eff=m_eff/p is a squarefree divisor of v, hence L_0-smooth. If r_eff>=X_A, apply the lemma with w=r_eff; again (4) gives a divisor of m_eff in [X_A,Y_A], contradicting (R3). Therefore r_eff<X_A, which is (G3).

The alternatives are disjoint because (G2) is conditioned on failure of (G1), while (G3) is conditioned on failure of both preceding strict inequalities. The argument proves that every (R3) box enters one of them. No bound for any alternative was used.

glossary.dynamic near-prime gap: The condition that the surviving smooth complement r_eff is below the lower endpoint of the actual A-divisor interval.

047f4bc01579ce66.title: CONSTANT-SAFE SOURCE-PRESERVING RE-MARKER THROUGH \(\beta_m\)
047f4bc01579ce66.author: slava chan
047f4bc01579ce66.statement:
CONSTANT-SAFE SOURCE-PRESERVING RE-MARKER THROUGH \(\beta_m\).

Fix \(0<\kappa\le1/100\), put
\[
 \sigma=\kappa/100,\qquad
 \beta_1=6/5-3\sigma,qquad
 \beta_m=6/5-12\sigma/5,
\]
and let \(T_{\rm postC3,sel}\) be the exact selected residual of fact
\(01b550792363535d\).  Restrict it to
\[
 \beta_1<\beta\le\beta_m.                                      \tag{1}
\]
On a forward atom write \(d=ga,r=gb\), put
\[
 Q=D/g,quad B=R/g=Q^\beta,quad n_z=b,quad s_z=a,
\]
and on a reverse atom put
\[
 Q=R/g,quad B=D/g=Q^\beta,quad n_z=a,quad s_z=b.
\]
Freeze before any marker operation the selected \(N\), original source
atom and active dyadic label, fixed \(U\), high label, orientation, parent,
actual \(G\), exact outer gcd \(g\), paired Fourier frequency, target,
smooth/projective amplitude, deletion and provenance coordinates.

Within every such fixed layer, first sum every old normalized marker leaf
\(C0,A,B,C1,\ldots,C_{J_\theta}\), together with every
marker-dependent prime-order, equality, collision, target-gcd and auxiliary
descendant, back to its complete coefficient.  This restores pointwise the
literal factor \(\mu(n_z)\); it is not a re-marking of any individually
selected old anatomy.

Now put
\[
 L=H_TQ^\sigma=Q^{\beta-1+\sigma},qquad
 S_0=H_T^2Q^{3\sigma}=Q^{2\beta-2+3\sigma},
\]
\[
 Z_*=2Q^{3/2-\beta-3\sigma}.                                    \tag{2}
\]
Apply the independent-height stopping identity directly to the restored
literal \(\mu(n_z)\), using \((L,S_0,Z_*)\).  Then every atom in (1)
has the exact sign-preserving disjoint anatomy
\[
 A_*,\quad B_*,\quad C1_*,\quad C2_*,\quad C3_*,               \tag{3}
\]
where \(A_*\) uses a prime in \((L,Z_*)\), \(B_*\) is the first
\(S_0\)-crossing stopping alternative using primes at most \(L\), and
\(Cj_*\) has a small factor at most \(S_0\) followed by exactly \(j\)
distinct ordered primes at least \(Z_*\), for \(1\le j\le3\).
There is no \(C0_*\) atom.

After the new leaf in (3) is formed, its canonical target-gcd, prime-order,
equal-cell, outer-g/rough-prime collision and deletion refinements may be
introduced as exact finite partitions.  Recombining those refinements
returns the new leaf coefficient.  The re-marker changes only the displayed
factor \(\mu(n_z)\): every frozen coordinate listed above, including
orientation, \(U_{\rm low}\) parent, actual \(G\), source amplitude,
fixed \(U\), frequency/projective data, target, exact \(g\), and
provenance, is retained.

Thus the complete projection (1) has an exact source-preserving Cartesian
ledger by the two orientations, frozen parent \(U_{\rm low}\), inherited
residual \(G\)-range, and the five new anatomies (3), including at
\(\beta=\beta_m\).  This is an algebraic re-marker only.  It gives no
anatomy estimate, negative cell, \(C4\), endpoint-parent, PMD, DCE, or
Goldbach conclusion.
047f4bc01579ce66.proof:
Fact \(a71f777ad842c886\) proves at the pre-marker level that
\(g,a,b\) are pairwise coprime and
\[
 \mu(d)\mu(r)=\mu(s_z)\mu(n_z).                                \tag{4}
\]
It also proves that every old normalized marker list is a pointwise
sign-preserving expansion of \(\mu(n_z)\), with all non-marker source
coordinates unchanged.  Therefore summing all old leaves and all of their
marker-dependent descendants at a fixed pre-marker atom gives exactly
\(\mu(n_z)\).  This is why the operation must be performed before
selecting an old anatomy.  No estimate or sign inequality is used in this
recombination.

We verify the new stopping hypotheses uniformly through the closed endpoint.
The dyadic support inherited from the original normalized larger-factor
label gives
\[
 c_BB\le n_z\le2B                                                   \tag{5}
\]
for a fixed \(c_B>0\).  Since
\[
 {B\over S_0}=Q^{2-\beta-3\sigma}
 \ge Q^{,4/5-3\sigma/5},                                        \tag{6}
\]
equation (5) gives \(n_z>S_0\) for sufficiently large \(Q\).
Also \(H_T=Q^{\beta-1}\ge1\), so
\[
 {S_0\over L}=H_TQ^{2\sigma}\ge1
\]
and \(2\le L\le S_0\) for large \(Q\).  Moreover
\[
 \log_Q\!\left({Z_*/2\over L}\right)
 =5/2-2\beta-4\sigma
 \ge1/10+4\sigma/5>0,                                            \tag{7}
\]
so \(L<Z_*\).

The constant factor in (2) repairs the only closed-endpoint failure of the
old cutoff.  Indeed
\[
 Z_*^4=16Q^{6-4\beta-12\sigma}.
\]
For \(\beta\le\beta_m\),
\[
 6-4\beta-12\sigma-\beta
 =6-5\beta-12\sigma\ge0.
\]
Consequently
\[
 Z_*^4\ge16Q^\beta=16B>2B\ge n_z.                               \tag{8}
\]
The inequality is strict even when \(\beta=\beta_m\).

Every source atom is squarefree on the nonzero Möbius support.  Equations
(6)-(8) are exactly the hypotheses of fact \(6414b11506a84ff0\), with its
squarefree integer \(r\) replaced by \(n_z\) and its stopping height
\(S\) replaced by \(S_0\).  That fact gives the mutually exclusive and
exhaustive interval-prime, stopping-composite, and one-, two-, or
three-\(Z_*\)-rough-prime alternatives, with the exact Möbius signs.
Because (6) excludes the small branch, there is no \(C0_*\) atom.  This
proves (3) pointwise.

Multiply the new pointwise identity by the unchanged factor
\(\mu(s_z)q_z\), where \(q_z\) denotes the complete transformed source
amplitude carrying the frozen labels, and sum inside each fixed layer.
By (4) the left side is the original literal source coefficient.  Hence the
new decomposition neither creates nor removes an original atom and changes
no frozen coordinate.  Prime ordering, equal-cell symmetrization,
outer-g/rough-prime collision, target-gcd and deletion labels introduced
afterward are exact finite partitions of a new leaf; their complete sum is
the leaf itself.  Fact \(01b550792363535d\) supplies the inherited
selected parent \(U_{\rm low}\), orientations and residual \(G\)-range
through \(\beta<6/5\), so intersecting it with the new pointwise identity
gives the asserted selected ledger, including the endpoint
\(\beta_m<6/5\).

glossary.A_*: The interval-prime anatomy formed using the cutoff Z_*.
glossary.B_*: The raised-stopping anatomy formed using L and S_0 after restoration of the literal Möbius coefficient.
glossary.C1_*: The one-Z_*-rough-prime anatomy after source-preserving re-marking.
glossary.C2_*: The two-Z_*-rough-prime anatomy after source-preserving re-marking.
glossary.C3_*: The three-Z_*-rough-prime anatomy after source-preserving re-marking.

050efa07f87f374a.title: EXACT JOINT CONDUCTOR--COFACTOR VECTOR AND THE Q^(8/3) ENERGY SUPPLIER FOR THE VERY-LARGE-CONDUCTOR ACTUAL-Z_MID CORE
050efa07f87f374a.author: slava chan
050efa07f87f374a.statement:
EXACT JOINT CONDUCTOR--COFACTOR VECTOR AND THE Q^(8/3) ENERGY SUPPLIER FOR THE VERY-LARGE-CONDUCTOR ACTUAL-Z_MID CORE.

Assume the g=1, |h|=1 upper-boundary packet, endpoint scales and absolutely summable natural-mask Fourier tensor separation of facts 58c03698e1b077c3, c9accda871a70b43 and 3afa321a72a3612b. Write
Q=x^(1/2+o(1)),  B=x^(2/3+o(1))=Q^(4/3+o(1)),
and fix a conductor cutoff F_0>=2. On the literal support b is squarefree.

For squarefree b and (a,b)=1 define
Pi_{b,>F_0}(a)
 =1/phi(b) sum_{chi modulo b;
                 cond(chi)>F_0, (cond(chi),N)=1}
   G^+_{N,b}(chi)chi(a),                                      (1)
where G^+_{N,b} is defined in fact c9accda871a70b43. Define
tau_f(psi)=sum_{v modulo f}psi(v)e_f(v).
For (a,b)=1, grouping the characters in (1) by b=fs and primitive psi modulo f gives exactly
Pi_{b,>F_0}(a)
 =1/phi(b) sum_{f|b; f>F_0,(f,N)=1}
    c_{b/f}(N)
    sum_{psi primitive modulo f}
     overline(psi(N))psi(a b/f)tau_f(psi).                    (2)
The formula is asserted only on (a,b)=1; no extension beyond the full unit support is claimed. Uniformly on this support,
|Pi_{b,>F_0}(a)|<<_epsilon b^epsilon.                         (3)

For one Fourier tensor in the absolutely convergent expansion used in fact 3afa321a72a3612b, absorb the literal mu(a), a-only masks and the a-side smooth factor into alpha_a, and absorb mu(b), b-only masks and the b-side smooth factor into beta_b. Its high-conductor contribution is exactly
T_{>F_0}=sum_{b asymp B;b squarefree}
 beta_b sum_{a asymp Q;(a,b)=1}alpha_aPi_{b,>F_0}(a),          (4)
where
sum_b|beta_b|^2<=B x^(o(1)),  |alpha_a|<=x^(o(1)).            (5)
The tensor coefficients have total absolute mass x^(o(1)), so all rearrangements and the final tensor summation are justified by absolute convergence. All actual logarithmic, endpoint, dyadic, squarefree, coprimality and provenance factors are retained in this inventory.

Define
E_{>F_0}(alpha)
 =sum_{b asymp B;b squarefree}
   |sum_{a asymp Q;(a,b)=1}alpha_aPi_{b,>F_0}(a)|^2.           (6)
Then
|T_{>F_0}|^2<=B x^(o(1))E_{>F_0}(alpha).                      (7)
The contribution with equal a-indices after expanding (6) satisfies
E_diag<=QB x^(o(1))=Q^(7/3+o(1)).                             (8)

For any fixed omega with 0<omega<1/3, the literal uniform energy theorem
E_{>F_0}(alpha)<<Q^(8/3-omega)                                (MZB-ENERGY)
for every tensor alpha arising from the actual expansion implies
T_{>F_0}<<Q^(2-omega/2+o(1))
        =x^(1-omega/4+o(1)).                                  (9)
The bound E_{>F_0}(alpha)<<Q^(8/3+o(1)) analogously implies T_{>F_0}<<x^(1+o(1)). In the fixed-power version, (8) pays the equal-index part because omega<1/3, so the missing content is the crossed unequal-index kernel.

Fix eta with 0<eta<1/2 and put F_0=x^(1/2-eta). Fact 3afa321a72a3612b pays every omitted principal or nonprincipal conductor at most F_0 by a fixed power and restricts the unresolved core to
f>x^(1/2-eta), (f,N)=1, b=fs asymp x^(2/3),
s<x^(1/6+eta+o(1)).                                         (10)

Fact 97e496ab242dcab8 does not obstruct MZB-ENERGY: it concerns an isolated character second moment at one fixed prime f, whereas (6) retains the Gauss weights, cofactor sum and varying squarefree b. Conversely, fact 3704d40c75e8269c does not directly prove MZB-ENERGY: its Bourgain--Garaev input bounds complete fourth additive energy of reciprocals modulo one fixed prime and averages every reciprocal-difference output, whereas (6) is a fixed-target second energy over varying generally composite squarefree moduli with a primitive-conductor projection. These are theorem-interface scope statements, not impossibility claims.

No estimate for MZB-ENERGY is asserted here. No claim is made for |h|>1, g>1, the derivative-integral term, boundary strips, complete small-g reassembly, endpoint capture, C3, or Goldbach.
050efa07f87f374a.proof:
Multiplicative Fourier inversion in fact c9accda871a70b43 gives
e_b(Na^(-1))
 =1/phi(b)sum_{chi modulo b}G^+_{N,b}(chi)chi(a)
for (a,b)=1. Restricting this finite sum to the characters in (1) defines the high-conductor component exactly.

Because b is squarefree, every character modulo b is induced by a unique primitive character psi modulo a divisor f of b. Put s=b/f. Fact 5a651793cab6648b proves that its Gauss coefficient is zero if (f,N)>1, and otherwise equals
c_s(N)overline(psi(N))psi(s)tau_f(psi).                       (11)
On the asserted support (a,b)=1, the induced value chi(a) equals psi(a). Grouping (1) by f and inserting (11) gives (2). We make no claim for a outside this support.

For (3), use fact 9ef7fac8978ac244 with q=b, dilator 1, t=1 and u=a. Its common-core projector is
1/phi(b)sum_{psi;cond(psi)>F_0,(cond(psi),N)=1}
 G_{N,b}(psi)overline(psi(a)),
where G_{N,b}(psi)=sum_z^*e_b(-Nz)overline(psi(z)).
Its complex conjugate is Pi_{b,>F_0}(a), since the conjugate of G_{N,b}(psi) is G^+_{N,b}(psi). The hypotheses (a,b)=1 and squarefreeness are satisfied. That fact gives
|Pi_{b,>F_0}(a)|<=tau(b)^2<<_epsilon b^epsilon,
proving (3).

The proof of fact 3afa321a72a3612b expands the joint endpoint amplitude into an absolutely summable two-variable Fourier tensor series. Its one-variable factors are uniformly bounded and its coefficient l1 mass is x^(o(1)). For each tensor, multiplicative inversion and restriction to (1) give (4); absolute convergence permits interchange of the tensor, a, b and finite character sums. The literal coefficient and zeroth-derivative bounds give (5), and summing the final estimates over the tensor coefficients costs x^(o(1)).

Cauchy's inequality in b gives
|T_{>F_0}|^2
 <=(sum_b|beta_b|^2)
   sum_b|sum_a alpha_aPi_{b,>F_0}(a)|^2,
which is (7). Expanding (6), the equal-index part is
sum_b sum_a |alpha_a|^2|Pi_{b,>F_0}(a)|^2.
There are O(B) possible b and O(Q) possible a. Apply (3) and (5) to obtain QBx^(o(1))=Q^(7/3+o(1)), proving (8).

If 0<omega<1/3 and MZB-ENERGY holds, (7) and B=Q^(4/3+o(1)) give
|T_{>F_0}|
 <=Q^(2/3+o(1))Q^(4/3-omega/2)
 =Q^(2-omega/2+o(1)).
Since Q=x^(1/2+o(1)), this is (9). The same calculation at exponent 8/3+o(1) proves the endpoint implication. Also 7/3<8/3-omega exactly when omega<1/3, so (8) removes the equal-index part in the fixed-power formulation.

For fixed 0<eta<1/2, fact 3afa321a72a3612b proves the fixed-power deletion through F_0=x^(1/2-eta) and derives (10). Finally, the fixed-prime isolated moment in fact 97e496ab242dcab8 and the fixed-prime complete fourth reciprocal energy in fact 3704d40c75e8269c have the different scopes stated in the theorem and therefore do not assert (6). This proves the exact reduction, diagonal bound, sufficient-energy implication and scope statements.

glossary.E_diag: the equal-a-index contribution after expanding E_{>F_0}(alpha)
glossary.E_{>F_0}(alpha): the squared l2 norm over squarefree b of the actual high-conductor a-row
glossary.MZB-ENERGY: the sufficient estimate E_{>F_0}(alpha)<<Q^(8/3-omega) on every actual tensor
glossary.Pi_{b,>F_0}(a): the multiplicative Fourier projection of e_b(Na^{-1}) onto characters of primitive conductor greater than F_0 and coprime to N
glossary.T_{>F_0}: one absolutely separated literal upper-boundary tensor restricted to primitive conductors greater than F_0
glossary.tau_f(psi): the primitive Gauss sum sum_{v modulo f}psi(v)e_f(v)

052064336e86e65c.title: Fix real numbers A>0 and C>=0. There exists B_BV=B_BV(A,C)>0 with the following property. Let x tend to infinity, put Q_BV=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B_BV), and for every positive integer q<=Q_BV choose an integer a_q with gcd(a_q,q)=1 and a continuously differentiable complex function F_q on [2,x]. Assume
052064336e86e65c.author: slava chan
052064336e86e65c.statement:
Fix real numbers A>0 and C>=0. There exists B_BV=B_BV(A,C)>0 with the following property. Let x tend to infinity, put Q_BV=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B_BV), and for every positive integer q<=Q_BV choose an integer a_q with gcd(a_q,q)=1 and a continuously differentiable complex function F_q on [2,x]. Assume
2 sup_{2<=t<=x}|F_q(t)|+integral_2^x|F_q'(t)|dt <=(log x)^C
for every q. Define
R_q=sum_{2<=n<=x, n congruent a_q modulo q}Lambda(n)F_q(n) -(1/phi(q))integral_2^x F_q(t)dt.
Then for every complex sequence lambda(q) with |lambda(q)|<=1,
|sum_{q<=Q_BV}lambda(q)R_q| <<_{A,C} x(log x)^(-A).

In particular, let B_src>B_BV, put D_*=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B_src), let psi_cut be a real function with 0<=psi_cut<=1, and let Phi be the nonnegative partition function from fact 3ef233e014331fc3. For a positive dyadic D put
lambda_D(q)=mu(q)psi_cut(q/D_*)Phi(q/D).
If 2D<=Q_BV, then for every integer N, after setting a_q congruent to N modulo q on the moduli with gcd(q,N)=1,
|sum_{q<=Q_BV, gcd(q,N)=1}lambda_D(q)R_q| <<_{A,C} x(log x)^(-A),
uniformly in the possibly x-dependent integer N and in the allowed family F_q. Moreover Q_BV/D_*=(log x)^(B_src-B_BV) tends to infinity, so for sufficiently large x there are positive dyadic D with 2D_*<=D and 2D<=Q_BV. This is a classical-level initial-slice theorem only; it does not control gcd(q,N)>1 or any dyadic support with 2D>Q_BV.
052064336e86e65c.proof:
For q<=Q_BV and 2<=y<=x define
Delta_q(y)=psi_AP(y;q,a_q)-y/phi(q),
where psi_AP(y;q,a_q)=sum_{n<=y, n congruent a_q modulo q}Lambda(n). By Stieltjes integration by parts,
R_q=F_q(x)Delta_q(x)-F_q(2)Delta_q(2)-integral_2^x F_q'(t)Delta_q(t)dt,
with an immaterial endpoint convention at t=2. Consequently
|R_q|<=[2 sup_t|F_q(t)|+integral_2^x|F_q'(t)|dt] max_{2<=y<=x}|Delta_q(y)|
<=(log x)^C max_{2<=y<=x}|Delta_q(y)|.

Sedunova, arXiv:1705.06660, states the maximal Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem as follows: for every L>0 there exists B_0(L)>0 such that, whenever Q<=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B_0(L)),
sum_{q<=Q} max_{2<=y<=x} max_{gcd(a,q)=1}|psi_AP(y;q,a)-y/phi(q)| <<_L x(log x)^(-L).
Apply this theorem with L=A+C+2 and take B_BV=B_0(L). Since each a_q is a reduced residue and |lambda(q)|<=1, the triangle inequality and the preceding bound give
|sum_{q<=Q_BV}lambda(q)R_q|
<= (log x)^C sum_{q<=Q_BV}max_y max_{gcd(a,q)=1}|psi_AP(y;q,a)-y/phi(q)|
<<_{A,C}x(log x)^(-A-2),
which is stronger than the first assertion.

For the application, fact 3ef233e014331fc3 gives a nonnegative dyadic partition Phi whose translates sum to one. Hence 0<=Phi(t)<=1 for every t. Together with |mu(q)|<=1 and 0<=psi_cut<=1 this gives |lambda_D(q)|<=1. Define lambda(q)=lambda_D(q) when gcd(q,N)=1 and lambda(q)=0 otherwise, and on its support choose a_q to be the residue of N modulo q. This residue is reduced by construction. The first part therefore gives the claimed estimate uniformly in N. The support of Phi(q/D) lies in q<=2D, so 2D<=Q_BV ensures that the complete dyadic weight is inside the theorem's modulus range.

Finally,
Q_BV/D_*=(log x)^(B_src-B_BV),
which tends to infinity because B_src>B_BV. Let D be the least positive power of two at least 2D_*. Then D<4D_*, and the displayed ratio implies 2D<8D_*<=Q_BV for all sufficiently large x. This supplies the stated nonempty initial dyadic slice. The argument explicitly removed noncoprime moduli and used the inequality 2D<=Q_BV, proving the final scope sentence.

glossary.B_BV: the logarithmic exponent in the maximal Bombieri-Vinogradov level Q_BV
glossary.B_src: a source cutoff exponent strictly larger than B_BV
glossary.F_q: the continuously differentiable prime-variable test function attached to q
glossary.Q_BV: the classical maximal Bombieri-Vinogradov modulus level
glossary.a_q: a reduced residue class modulo q which may depend on q and x
glossary.psi_cut: the bounded real cutoff entering the raw modulus coefficient

0576f567200d41f1.title: FIXED-TARGET THREE-ROUGH-PRIME ENDPOINT BELOW \(\beta=6/5\)
0576f567200d41f1.author: slava chan
0576f567200d41f1.statement:
FIXED-TARGET THREE-ROUGH-PRIME ENDPOINT BELOW \(\beta=6/5\).

Fix \(0<\kappa\le1/100\) and integers \(J,C_A\ge1\), put \(\sigma=\kappa/100\), and suppose
\[
 1\le\beta\le6/5-2\kappa.
\]
For sufficiently large \(Q\), define
\[
 R=Q^\beta,\quad H=R/Q,\quad
 L=HQ^\sigma,\quad Z=Q^{3/2-\beta-3\sigma}. \tag{1}
\]
Let
\[
 V=Q^\nu,\qquad P_i=Q^{a_i}\quad(1\le i\le3),
\]
where
\[
 0\le\nu\le2\beta-2+3\sigma,\qquad
 a_i\ge\frac32-\beta-3\sigma,\qquad
 a_1+a_2+a_3+\nu=\beta. \tag{2}
\]
Let \(\xi_v\) be supported on squarefree \(V\le v<2V\), all of whose prime divisors are at most \(L\), with \(|\xi_v|\le\tau_J(v)\). Let \(A\ne0\) be fixed with \(|A|\le Q^{C_A}\), let \(|c_q|\le1\), and let \(|\nu_h|\le\tau_J(|h|)\) on \(H\le|h|<2H\).

Let \(\mathfrak F\) be a fixed uniformly scaled-smooth family on \([1,2]^6\). For \(\Psi\in\mathfrak F\), define
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 {\cal R}_{V,P_1,P_2,P_3}
 =H^{-1}\sum_{Q\le q<2Q}c_q
 \sum_{\substack{H\le|h|<2H\\v\sim V\\p_i\sim P_i\ (1\le i\le3)\\
 p_1<p_2<p_3\ {\rm primes}\\(vp_1p_2p_3,q)=1}}
 \nu_h\xi_v\Psi(q/Q,|h|/H,v/V,p_1/P_1,p_2/P_2,p_3/P_3)
 e_q\!\left(Ah(vp_1p_2p_3)^{-1}\right).
 \end{aligned} \tag{3}
\]
Assume the ordered prime cells have been refined so that order between distinct cells is automatic, while the coefficient and amplitude are symmetric under permutations of prime variables belonging to the same cell.

Then there is \(\delta=\delta(\kappa,C_A)>0\) such that
\[
 |{\cal R}_{V,P_1,P_2,P_3}|
 \ll_{\kappa,J,C_A,\mathfrak F}Q^{2-\delta}. \tag{4}
\]
The same estimate holds after summing a polylogarithmic number of refined prime cells and smooth labels. Taking \(\xi_v=-\mu(v)\) gives the exact sign of the three-rough-prime alternative in fact \(6414b11506a84ff0\). No outer-\(g\) assembly is asserted.
0576f567200d41f1.proof:
Part (D) of the slot-selection fact \(461b4af4d8047ab5\) applies to (2). It states that every \(a_i+\nu\) is below the upper correlated boundary and that at least one index \(i\) satisfies
\[
 2\beta-2+4\sigma<a_i+\nu<3-2\beta-4\sigma. \tag{5}
\]
Fix such an index and group
\[
 S=VP_i,\qquad T=P_jP_k,\qquad\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}. \tag{6}
\]
After absorbing fixed dyadic endpoint constants, (5) gives
\[
 H^2Q^{3\sigma}\le S\le\frac{Q^{1-3\sigma}}{H^2}. \tag{7}
\]
Also
\[
 ST\asymp VP_1P_2P_3=R=QH. \tag{8}
\]

Before grouping, expand the scaled-smooth amplitude in logarithmic Fourier modes. Its projective coefficient norm is uniformly summable. The coefficient on \(S\), obtained by convolving \(\xi_v\) with one prime indicator, is bounded by a fixed divisor function. The coefficient on \(T\), obtained by convolving the other two prime indicators, is also divisor-bounded. All rough primes are at least \(Z>L\), so they are automatically coprime to \(v\).

Apply the full fixed-target correlated estimate in fact \(73fb9efe1286f7e9\). Its four expanded terms after the \(H^{-1}\) prefactor are
\[
 Q^2H^{1/2}S^{-1/4},\quad
 Q^{7/4}H^{1/2}S^{1/4},\quad
 Q^2HS^{-1/2},\quad
 Q^{7/4}H.
\]
Equations (7)-(8) bound all four by \(Q^{2-\delta_0}\) for some fixed \(\delta_0\gg\sigma\). The fixed target, divisor weights, and Fourier modes cost \(Q^\epsilon\), absorbed by choosing \(\epsilon\) sufficiently small.

We now justify the distinct ordered-prime restriction. Refine the prime axes into common dyadic cells. Variables in distinct cells have automatic order. Within a cell containing \(m\) of the prime variables, symmetry gives the ordered distinct sum as \(1/m!\) times the unrestricted sum with all equality diagonals removed by inclusion-exclusion. There are only finitely many set partitions of three indices, so this creates an absolute number of collision strata.

Every nontrivial collision identifies at least two rough primes. Suppose, for instance, \(p_i=p_j=p\). The remaining free arithmetic variables have at most
\[
 O(VP_iP_k)
\]
choices, up to divisor and logarithmic factors. Since
\[
 R\asymp VP_i^2P_k
\]
on this collision cell and \(P_i\ge Z\), this number is \(O(R/Z)\). Summing \(q\), summing \(h\), and multiplying by \(H^{-1}\), every collision stratum is therefore
\[
 \ll Q^\epsilon QR/Z. \tag{9}
\]
A triple collision is no larger. From (1),
\[
 \log_Q(QR/Z)
 =2\beta-\frac12+3\sigma
 \le\frac{19}{10}-4\kappa+\frac{3\kappa}{100}<2-\kappa. \tag{10}
\]
Thus all collision strata are power-saving. The unrestricted distinct-cell pieces are controlled by the correlated estimate above, and summing the polylogarithmic refined partition proves (4).

glossary.P_i: The dyadic scale of the i-th rough prime.
glossary.cal R_{V,P_1,P_2,P_3}: The fixed-target reciprocal trace for a small factor and three ordered rough primes.

05b9d888ec18077c.title: Let Q_set be a finite set and let (X_q)_{q in Q_set} be centered real random variables with finite fourth moments on one probability space. Define the covariance matrix
05b9d888ec18077c.author: slava chan
05b9d888ec18077c.statement:
Let Q_set be a finite set and let (X_q)_{q in Q_set} be centered real random variables with finite fourth moments on one probability space. Define the covariance matrix
C(q,q')=E[X_qX_{q'}],
the centered-square covariance matrix
