A(q,q')=E[(X_q^2-E[X_q^2])(X_{q'}^2-E[X_{q'}^2])],
and the repeated-pair connected fourth-moment matrix
K(q,q')=kappa(X_q,X_q,X_{q'},X_{q'}),
where kappa is the connected partition functional defined in fact 104522049dda64e6. Let C_had2 be the entrywise square C_had2(q,q')=C(q,q')^2. Then
K=A-2C_had2.                                                   (1)
Both A and C_had2 are positive semidefinite. Consequently the following are equivalent:
(i) K is positive semidefinite;
(ii) A>=2C_had2 in the Loewner order;
(iii) for every complex coefficient vector z,
sum_{q,q'}overline(z_q)A(q,q')z_{q'}>=2sum_{q,q'}overline(z_q)C(q,q')^2z_{q'}.
Thus even in the structured repeated-pair moment setting, a PSD connected-partition factorization requires a concrete domination of the two Wick-pairing Gram contributions by the covariance of centered squares. It does not follow from the separate positivity of those constituent matrices. For a one-index Rademacher family, A=0, C_had2=1, and K=-2, recovering fact 104522049dda64e6. This is an exact abstract partition-factorization criterion; it neither proves that the actual WF-RPS connected kernel has repeated-pair form nor proves the domination, COH, or an arithmetic saving.
05b9d888ec18077c.proof:
Because every X_q is centered, the fourth connected partition formula reduces in the repeated-pair slots to
kappa(X_q,X_q,X_{q'},X_{q'})
=E[X_q^2X_{q'}^2]-E[X_q^2]E[X_{q'}^2]-2E[X_qX_{q'}]^2.
Indeed, every partition containing a singleton block vanishes, the one-block partition gives the fourth joint moment, the pairing {1,2}{3,4} gives -E[X_q^2]E[X_{q'}^2], and the other two pairings each give -E[X_qX_{q'}]^2. The first two displayed terms are exactly A(q,q'), proving (1).

The matrix A is a Gram matrix in real L^2: if Y_q=X_q^2-E[X_q^2], then A(q,q')=E[Y_qY_{q'}]. Hence A is positive semidefinite.

The covariance matrix C is the Gram matrix of the vectors X_q in real L^2. The entrywise square C_had2 is also a Gram matrix: in the Hilbert tensor square L^2 tensor L^2, set W_q=X_q tensor X_q. Then
<W_q,W_{q'}>=<X_q,X_{q'}>^2=C(q,q')^2.
Thus C_had2 is positive semidefinite.

By (1), K is positive semidefinite exactly when A-2C_had2 is positive semidefinite, which is the Loewner-order statement (ii). A finite Hermitian matrix is positive semidefinite exactly when all its complex quadratic forms are nonnegative, giving equivalence with (iii).

If Q_set has one element and X is Rademacher, then X^2=1 almost surely, so its centered square is zero and A=0. Also E[X^2]=1, so C_had2=1. Formula (1) gives K=-2, in agreement with fact 104522049dda64e6. The final scope limitations follow because no WF-RPS identification or estimate was used.

glossary.A: the covariance Gram matrix of the centered squares X_q^2-E[X_q^2]
glossary.C_had2: the entrywise square of the covariance matrix C
glossary.Loewner order: the order A>=B meaning that A-B is positive semidefinite

05cbed389411618a.title: EXACT TARGET-MINUS-A PHYSICAL TRANSLATION, COMMON-ENVELOPE SPAN, REFINEMENT TAX, AND NORMALIZED DIRECT NO-FIT
05cbed389411618a.author: slava chan
05cbed389411618a.statement:
EXACT TARGET-MINUS-A PHYSICAL TRANSLATION, COMMON-ENVELOPE SPAN, REFINEMENT TAX, AND NORMALIZED DIRECT NO-FIT.

Fix constants C_0,C_1,D_0>=1. Let Q>=2 and let real numbers H,V,P,L satisfy
  2<=H<=Q^(1/3),  2<=V<H,  P=QH/V,  L>=1.                 (1)
Let cal O be a nonempty set of pairs j=(v,p), where v is an integer in [V,2V), p is prime in [P,2P), gcd(v,p)=1, and
  p>2(D_0H+1).                                               (2)
Put n_j=vp and Y_j=n_j/H. Let A be a nonzero integer satisfying gcd(A,n_j)=1 for every j. Let cal L be a nonempty finite label set. Let Phi be one fixed smooth compactly supported complex function whose support avoids zero and has length at most D_0.

For every ell in cal L and j in cal O let cal Q_{ell,j} be a nonempty set of positive integers contained in [Q,2Q), with gcd(q,n_j)=1. For every q in cal Q_{ell,j} let F_{ell,j,q} be a smooth compactly supported complex function. Assume that, for one closed interval J^0_{ell,j},
  supp(F_{ell,j,q}) subset J^0_{ell,j},
  |J^0_{ell,j}|<=C_1Y_j,
  |F_{ell,j,q}(t)|<=L                                       (3)
for all q and all real t. Define
  G_{ell,j,q}(t)=F_{ell,j,q}(t+A/q).                         (4)
With the Fourier convention
  Fhat(xi)=integral_R F(t)e(-xi t)dt,
define the raw and normalized rows
  R_{ell,j}(theta)
   =sum_{q in cal Q_{ell,j}}n_j^(-1)sum_{h in Z}
      Phi(h/H)Fhat_{ell,j,q}(h/n_j)e(Ah/(qn_j))
      e_{n_j}(-Ahqbar)e(h theta),                            (5)
  X_{ell,j}(theta)=H R_{ell,j}(theta),                       (6)
where e(x)=exp(2 pi i x), e_n(x)=e(x/n), and qbar is the inverse of q modulo n_j.

Then
  Ghat_{ell,j,q}(h/n_j)
   =e(Ah/(qn_j))Fhat_{ell,j,q}(h/n_j),                       (7)
and consequently R_{ell,j} is exactly the row of fact 85c90a4160baba8d with physical function G_{ell,j,q} and target -A:
  R_{ell,j}(theta)
   =sum_q n_j^(-1)sum_h Phi(h/H)Ghat_{ell,j,q}(h/n_j)
      e_{n_j}(-Ahqbar)e(h theta).                            (8)
There is no reflection of h or theta in (8).

Put q_- =min cal Q_{ell,j} and q_+=max cal Q_{ell,j}. The translation set {-A/q:q in cal Q_{ell,j}} has exact diameter
  T_{ell,j}=|A|(1/q_- -1/q_+),                              (9)
with T_{ell,j}=0 when q_-=q_+. Moreover
  supp(G_{ell,j,q})=supp(F_{ell,j,q})-A/q.                  (10)
Thus all translated supports lie in one closed interval of length at most
  C_1Y_j+T_{ell,j}.                                        (11)
If a point t_{ell,j} belongs to supp(F_{ell,j,q}) for every q, every common closed interval containing all translated supports has length at least T_{ell,j}. Hence (9) is an exact obstruction to deriving a uniform O(Y_j) envelope merely from a common pre-translation interval when the source supplies no bound T_{ell,j}=O(Y_j). In particular, since q lies in [Q,2Q),
  T_{ell,j}<=|A|/Q.                                        (12)
The sufficient source-size condition |A|<=C_A QY_j, with fixed C_A, gives a common translated interval of length at most (C_1+C_A)Y_j.

Without that condition, each cal Q_{ell,j} can be partitioned into at most
  K_{ell,j}<=2+min(Q, |A|/(QY_j))                           (13)
consecutive q-pieces so that the translation diameter on every piece is at most Y_j. Put K_ref=max_{ell in cal L,j in cal O}K_{ell,j}. If R_{ell,j,a} is the restriction of (5) to its a-th piece, extended by zero when the piece is absent, then
  integral_{R/Z}|R_{ell,j}(theta)|^4dtheta
  <=K_ref^3 sum_{a=1}^{K_ref}
       integral_{R/Z}|R_{ell,j,a}(theta)|^4dtheta.           (14)
Consequently fact 85c90a4160baba8d, applied separately to every label and piece, gives for every epsilon>0
  sum_{ell in cal L}sum_{j in cal O}
    integral_{R/Z}|R_{ell,j}(theta)|^4dtheta
  <<_{Phi,C_1,epsilon}
    (#cal L)K_ref^4 L^4 Q^(5+epsilon)/H^3.                  (15)
If #cal L and K_ref are subpolynomial, they may be absorbed by renaming epsilon. A nonconstant refinement is not free: the direct fourth-power recombination carries the displayed K_ref^4 tax.

Even in the best case K_ref=1 and #cal L subpolynomial, homogeneity and (6) give
  M_4^norm
  :=sum_{ell,j}integral_{R/Z}|X_{ell,j}(theta)|^4dtheta
  <<_{Phi,C_1,epsilon}L^4Q^(5+epsilon)H.                    (16)
Relative to the normalized vector target P^2Q^(7/3), the ratio of the powers in (16) is
  [Q^5H]/[P^2Q^(7/3)]=Q^(2/3)V^2/H
  >=4Q^(1/3).                                               (17)
Thus direct insertion of fact 85c90a4160baba8d for an H-normalized row is a fixed-power no-fit throughout (1), even after the exact common-envelope match. This is a no-fit for this upper-bound insertion, not a lower bound for the literal fourth moment.

Finally, compare with the literal row of fact ddcb0baef17b6ab0. Write j=(v,p), n_j=vp, and put
  cal A_j={q in Z:Q<=q<2Q, gcd(q,n_j)=1}.                   (18)
Extend F_{ell,j,q} by the zero function for q in cal A_j outside cal Q_{ell,j}, so (5) is unchanged when its q-sum is extended to cal A_j. Extend the literal coefficient from fact ddcb0baef17b6ab0 by zero outside both its literal height interval I_ell and its exact literal q-support. Its complete q-row equals X_{ell,j} term by term if the following full coefficient identity holds for every integer h and every q in cal A_j:
  1_{(h,q) in the exact literal support}
    c_q nu_h U_ell(q,h,v,p)chi_ell(v,p,h,q)
   =H n_j^(-1)Phi(h/H)Fhat_{ell,j,q}(h/n_j).                (19)
Condition (19) includes exact q-index matching, the cutoff, every off-band zero, and every retained mask; F_{ell,j,q} is independent of h. The hypotheses of fact ddcb0baef17b6ab0 specify and bound its left side but do not assert the existence of functions satisfying (3) and (19). Therefore the current accepted literal interface does not by itself establish a common-envelope PMD sector. The exact first missing source bridge is (19) together with either T_{ell,j}=O(Y_j) or a tax-paid use of (13)-(15). No nonprincipal OSC estimate, PMD closure, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
05cbed389411618a.proof:
For a real translation a, substitution u=t+a gives
  integral_R F(t+a)e(-xi t)dt
  =e(a xi)integral_R F(u)e(-xi u)du.
Take a=A/q and xi=h/n_j. This proves (7). In fact 85c90a4160baba8d replace its target A by -A. Its modular factor is then e_{n_j}(-Ahqbar). Inserting (7) proves (8), including both signs and the Archimedean factor.

Let Z(F) be the set on which a continuous function F is nonzero. Translation gives
  Z(G_{ell,j,q})=Z(F_{ell,j,q})-A/q.
Translation is a homeomorphism, so it commutes with closure. Since support is the closure of the nonzero set, this proves (10) without asserting that F is nonzero at every point of its support.

The map q maps to -A/q is monotone on the positive real axis. Its diameter on a nonempty finite q-set is therefore the absolute difference of its values at q_- and q_+, which is (9). If J^0_{ell,j}=[a,b], all translated supports are contained in
  [a+min_q(-A/q), b+max_q(-A/q)].
This is a closed interval of length |J^0_{ell,j}|+T_{ell,j}, proving (11). If t_{ell,j} lies in every support, then the two points t_{ell,j}-A/q_- and t_{ell,j}-A/q_+ occur in the union of translated supports. Their distance is T_{ell,j}; every interval containing the union has at least that length. This proves the obstruction assertion. Since q_- >=Q and q_+<2Q, equation (12) follows, and the stated source-size condition inserted in (11) gives the fixed common envelope.

For the refinement, put lambda=|A|/(QY_j). If lambda<=1, take one piece. If 1<lambda<Q, partition the containing q-interval into at most ceil(lambda)+1 consecutive intervals of length at most Q/lambda=Q^2Y_j/|A|. On such a piece [u,u+Delta],
  |A|(1/u-1/(u+Delta))
  =|A|Delta/[u(u+Delta)]
  <=|A|Delta/Q^2<=Y_j.
If lambda>=Q, use singleton q-pieces. The number of integers in [Q,2Q) is at most ceil(Q)<=Q+1, which is at most Q+2, the right side of (13) in this case. Thus all cases prove (13).

For complex numbers z_1,...,z_K, Holder's inequality gives
  |sum_a z_a|^4<=K^3 sum_a|z_a|^4.
Apply this pointwise with z_a=R_{ell,j,a}(theta) and K=K_ref, padding with zero pieces, then integrate to prove (14). On each nonempty piece, (11) has length at most (C_1+1)Y_j. All other hypotheses of fact 85c90a4160baba8d are exactly (1)-(3), positivity of q, gcd(A,n_j)=1, and (2). For each fixed ell and a, that fact, with empty outer rows omitted, gives
  sum_j integral|R_{ell,j,a}|^4
  <<L^4Q^(5+epsilon)/H^3.
Sum first over a and ell, then use (14). This proves (15).

Equation (6) gives |X|^4=H^4|R|^4. In the case K_ref=1, multiply (15) by H^4 and absorb the subpolynomial label count to obtain (16). Since P=QH/V,
  P^2Q^(7/3)=Q^(13/3)H^2/V^2,
so division gives the equality in (17). The assumptions V>=2 and H<=Q^(1/3) give its lower bound.

It remains only to compare coefficients on the common ambient q-set cal A_j. Equations (2)-(5) of fact ddcb0baef17b6ab0 define the coefficient of e(h theta) at q as the left side of (19) multiplied by
  e(Ah/(qn_j))e_{n_j}(-Ahqbar).
Equations (5)-(6), after the zero extension just defined, give the coefficient in X_{ell,j} as the right side of (19) multiplied by the same two phases. Hence (19) gives exact termwise equality for every h and every ambient q, including equality of the q-index supports. Conversely, equality term by term in this specified ambient representation forces (19) after canceling the nonzero phase. The cited fact imposes only a boundedness hypothesis on its displayed literal amplitude and supplies no physical functions or common support assertion, so it does not imply (19) or (3). This proves the stated interface gap and every scope qualification.

glossary.G_{ell,j,q}: The translated physical function F_{ell,j,q}(t+A/q) which absorbs the Archimedean reciprocity phase.
glossary.J^0_{ell,j}: The common pre-translation physical support interval in one label and outer row.
glossary.K_ref: The maximum number of q-support pieces used to make every translation span at most Y_j.
glossary.M_4^norm: The fourth moment of the H-normalized translated rows.

062a7f6f0c58b1f2.title: TOP-UNMARKED-SURVIVING-THETA/BV AUDIT AND THE PRE-MARKER PROVENANCE OBSTRUCTION. Work in the strict top sliver
062a7f6f0c58b1f2.author: slava chan
062a7f6f0c58b1f2.statement:
TOP-UNMARKED-SURVIVING-THETA/BV AUDIT AND THE PRE-MARKER PROVENANCE OBSTRUCTION. Work in the strict top sliver
\[
 \beta_m<\beta<6/5
\]
and in one fixed unmarked source row of fact \(b0a38f5e9ae7feb6\). Thus all six new marker anatomies and every marker-dependent descendant have been recombined, but the surviving pre-marker selector
\(\Theta^\epsilon_\lambda(s,n,h)\) remains explicit. Fix the selected integer \(N\), active dyadic label, exact outer gcd \(g\), orientation \(\epsilon\), fixed-\(U\), high, \(U_{\rm low}\)-parent, actual-\(G\), smooth, source, and provenance labels.

The accepted selector information has the following exact classification.

1. The selected \(N\), active scales, high residual condition, orientation, actual \(G\), and the parent \(U_{\rm low}\) are frozen outer-label data on the fixed row. The conclusion that the parent is \(U_{\rm low}\) on this exact top sliver is supplied by fact \(e58fc7c00f1683e6\). The physical fixed-\(U\), dyadic, logarithmic, and original source dependence is contained in the specified smooth source amplitude \(F^\epsilon_{g,s,n}\), as is visible from facts \(60b26a9b6f79467a\) and \(b0a38f5e9ae7feb6\); it is not an extra sharp selector.

2. Split the paired nonzero frequencies into a sign and a dyadic block
\[
 F\le |h|<2F,\qquad F\ge1.                                    \tag{1}
\]
Its sharp selector is one-variable. On either signed block its supremum plus discrete total variation is at most \(3\).

3. The inherited pre-marker provenance selector is not eliminated by the recombination in fact \(b0a38f5e9ae7feb6\). Denote this remaining zero-one factor by
\[
 \Pi_{\rm prov}(s,n,h).
\]
None of the cited accepted facts gives a definition-level formula, a bounded-projective decomposition, or a one-variable bounded-variation description for \(\Pi_{\rm prov}\). Hence the full literal \(\Theta^\epsilon_\lambda\) is not currently licensed for the separated coefficient slots of fact \(9ea2dddfbbbd191a\). In particular, it is illegal to absorb \(\Pi_{\rm prov}\) into the smooth amplitude or into an arbitrary divisor-bounded \(h\)-coefficient.

This provenance factor is the smallest remaining coefficient-interface obstruction in the following precise sense. Remove only \(\Pi_{\rm prov}\), while retaining every arithmetic Möbius factor, coprimality gate, one-sided Vaughan/Huang threshold, and tuple-dependent zero-one occupancy mask outside the Archimedean coefficient. Let \(n=mv\), and restrict
\[
 M_1\le m<2M_1,\qquad V_1\le v<2V_1,\qquad M_1V_1\asymp B.     \tag{2}
\]
For every fixed \(A>0\), the remaining literal coefficient
\[
 {\bf1}_{F\le |h|<2F}\,{H_P\over mv}\,
 \widehat F^\epsilon_{g,s,mv}(\epsilon h/(mv))\,
 e\!\left({\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\over smv}\right)             \tag{3}
\]
has an exact absolutely convergent expansion
\[
 (3)=\sum_\rho \eta_\rho A_\rho(s)C_\rho(m)D_\rho(v)E_\rho(h) \tag{4}
\]
whose one-variable factors have supremum at most \(1\), after normalization, and whose coefficient mass satisfies
\[
 \sum_\rho|\eta_\rho|
 \ll_A(\log x)^2(1+F/H_P)^{-A}.                              \tag{5}
\]
If
\[
 {\cal V}_F(E)=\|E\|_\infty+
 \sum_{\substack{h,\ h+1\ {\rm in}\\{\rm one\ fixed\ signed\ block}}}
 |E(h+1)-E(h)|,
\]
then the normalization may be chosen so that
\[
 \sum_\rho|\eta_\rho|\,{\cal V}_F(E_\rho)
 \ll_A(\log x)^2(1+F/H_P)^{-A},\qquad
 \|D_\rho\|_\infty\le1.                                      \tag{6}
\]
Thus the nonnegative envelopes
\[
 w_\rho(k)=|E_\rho(\epsilon k)|,\qquad b_\rho(v)=|D_\rho(v)|,
 \qquad F\le k<2F,
\]
have exactly the bounded-variation numerator slot and bounded cofactor slot required by fact \(9ea2dddfbbbd191a\). For the negative block one reindexes \(h=-k\); the reciprocal-ratio balance and every zero-one occupancy mask are pulled back bijectively, since
\[
 -k_1/t_1-k_2/t_2=-k_3/t_3-k_4/t_4
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 k_1/t_1+k_2/t_2=k_3/t_3+k_4/t_4.
\]
No mixed-sign assertion is needed: the two signed rows may be separated before a fourth moment, at constant cost.

Finally, over the complete infinite dyadic frequency ledger,
\[
 \sum_{F=2^j,\ j\ge0}(\log x)^2(1+F/H_P)^{-A}
 \ll_A(\log x)^2(1+\log(2+H_P))=x^{o(1)},                    \tag{7}
\]
because the source scales make \(H_P\) polynomially bounded in \(x\). Thus there is no unaccounted Fourier tail in the coefficient audit.

This theorem proves no energy estimate, Type-I estimate, endpoint payment, tail payment, or Goldbach conclusion. Its conclusion is that the smooth coefficient and paired-frequency slots are compatible with fact \(9ea2dddfbbbd191a\), whereas the inherited pre-marker provenance selector \(\Pi_{\rm prov}\) remains the exact unverified interface.
062a7f6f0c58b1f2.proof:
Fact \(60b26a9b6f79467a\) displays the original selected source. Its physical dependence is a product of the two logarithms and the specified smooth \(W,\psi,\Phi\) factors. The bad integer \(N\), the active dyadic scales, the high residual family, and the orientation are selected as outer labels. The parameter \(U\) is a dyadic label, while its physical dependence is the smooth factor \(\Phi(rk/U)\). Fact \(e58fc7c00f1683e6\), whose statement is specifically on \(\beta_m\le\beta<6/5\), gives the sole inherited parent \(U_{\rm low}\), the actual-\(G\) interval, and the exact fixed-label ledger on the present sliver.

Fact \(b0a38f5e9ae7feb6\) is applied before the proper \(A\)-projection is subtracted: its equations (6)-(7) explicitly require estimating the complete unmarked source and only then subtracting the already paid \(A\)-projection. Thus the proper \(A\) mask is not placed in \(\Theta^\epsilon_\lambda\). That fact recombines every new anatomy and marker-dependent descendant, but its statement explicitly retains selected-source, active-scale, fixed-\(U\), high, parent, actual-\(G\), paired-frequency, and inherited-provenance selectors. The first six items have the outer/smooth status just traced. A signed dyadic frequency block is an integer interval, so its indicator has supremum one and at most two endpoint jumps.

By contrast, the statement and proof of \(b0a38f5e9ae7feb6\) do not recombine the inherited pre-marker provenance factor and explicitly disclaim projective separability of an arbitrary surviving \(\Theta^\epsilon_\lambda\). The other predecessors cited here record that provenance is retained, but do not display a formula for its dependence on \(s,n,h\). Therefore no accepted predecessor implies a projective or bounded-variation norm for \(\Pi_{\rm prov}\). This proves the no-license assertion without claiming that the factor is intrinsically nonseparable.

It remains to prove that no other coefficient obstruction is hidden in (3). We give the forward argument; the reverse one is identical after replacing the physical \(M\)-scale by \(K\) and changing the fixed sign. Put
\[
 x_1=s/Q,\qquad y_1=n/B,\qquad z_1=h/F,\qquad \tau_1=t/M.
\]
Since \(H_P=B/M\), substitution in (3F) of fact \(b0a38f5e9ae7feb6\) gives
\[
 {H_P\over n}\widehat F^+_{g,s,n}(h/n)
 ={1\over y_1}\int {\cal W}_+(x_1,y_1,\tau_1)
 e\!\left(-{F\over H_P}{z_1\tau_1\over y_1}\right)d\tau_1,    \tag{8}
\]
where \({\cal W}_+\) is compactly supported in a fixed positive box and has scaled derivatives bounded by \(O_r((\log x)^2)\) through every fixed order \(r\). The reciprocity factor is
\[
 e\!\left(\lambda {F\over H_P}{z_1\over x_1y_1}\right),
 \qquad \lambda={L_{\rm src}H_P\over QB}\asymp1,              \tag{9}
\]
using \(N\asymp DM\), \(L_{\rm src}=N/g\), \(Q=D/g\), and \(H_P=B/M\).

Fix a mixed derivative of total order at most \(r\) in \(x_1,y_1,z_1\). Differentiating (8)-(9) costs at most \(O_r((1+F/H_P)^r)\). Before taking this derivative, integrate by parts in \(\tau_1\) \(A+2r+20\) times. The phase derivative has magnitude comparable to \(F/H_P\) on the fixed positive box. Consequently every such mixed derivative of the normalized coefficient is
\[
 O_{A,r}\!\left((\log x)^2(1+F/H_P)^{-A-r-10}\right).         \tag{10}
\]
For \(F/H_P\le1\) the same bound follows directly without integration by parts. This proves the required derivative control rather than only a zeroth-order decay estimate.

Now use (2) and put
\[
 x_2=m/M_1,\qquad x_3=v/V_1.
\]
Then \(y_1=(M_1V_1/B)x_2x_3\), with the prefactor in a fixed compact positive interval. Composition of (10) therefore gives the same fixed-order derivative bounds in \(x_1,x_2,x_3,z_1\). Extend the function smoothly to a fixed four-torus. Take \(r=12\). Repeated integration by parts in its four Fourier variables gives Fourier coefficients whose absolute sum remains bounded by (5) after multiplication by \(1+|\xi_h|\), where \(\xi_h\) is the Fourier index in \(z_1\). Restriction to the integer variables yields the exact absolutely convergent expansion (4).

For one \(h\)-mode, the mean-value theorem gives discrete variation \(O(1+|\xi_h|)\) on the normalized interval; the sharp block indicator contributes at most two endpoint jumps. Absorb this factor into its Fourier coefficient. The weighted Fourier summability just proved yields (6). Since
\[
 \big||u|-|v|\big|\le |u-v|,
\]
passing from \(E_\rho\) to its absolute value does not increase total variation. The cofactor factor \(D_\rho\) already has bounded supremum. This proves the positive smooth-slot assertion.

For the negative frequency row put \(k=-h\). This is a bijection from its signed block to \(F\le k<2F\). Four ratios acquire the same minus sign, so the displayed balance equivalence holds, and any retained zero-one occupancy mask is transported by composition with the bijection. Thus the hypotheses of fact \(9ea2dddfbbbd191a\) are matched mode by mode only after this reindexing. If both signed rows are later combined, \(|X+Y|^4\le8(|X|^4+|Y|^4)\) separates them with a constant loss.

Finally, the integer frequency blocks are \(F=2^j\), \(j\ge0\). If \(F\le H_P\), their number is \(O(1+\log(2+H_P))\); if \(F>H_P\), the dyadic sum of \((F/H_P)^{-A}\) converges. The source has all scales bounded by fixed powers of \(x\), hence so is \(H_P\). This proves (7).

06485889a0b3e455.title: COMPLETE-CELL SPECTRAL TOP/PRIME-STAR DECOMPOSITION
06485889a0b3e455.author: slava chan
06485889a0b3e455.statement:
COMPLETE-CELL SPECTRAL TOP/PRIME-STAR DECOMPOSITION.

Let L>=4, let mathcal P_L be an L-element set, and let mathcal E_L be the set of all two-element subsets of mathcal P_L. Put n_L=binom(L,2) and d_L=binom(L-2,2). On C^{mathcal E_L} use the standard Hermitian inner product. Define the disjointness operator A_L and the prime-support incidence map B_L by
(A_Lx)_G=sum_{G' in mathcal E_L:G' intersect G=emptyset}x_{G'},
(B_Lx)_r=sum_{G in mathcal E_L:r in G}x_G.
Let 1_E and 1_P denote the all-one vectors on mathcal E_L and mathcal P_L. For x in C^{mathcal E_L}, put
t=sum_G x_G,  s=B_Lx,  s^0=s-(2t/L)1_P,
a=t/n_L,  y=s^0/(L-2),  z=x-a1_E-B_L^*y.                    (1)

(A) The decomposition
x=a1_E+B_L^*y+z                                               (2)
is orthogonal, with sum_r y_r=0 and B_Lz=0. The three summands are respectively the constant sector, the centered prime-star sector, and the star-null sector.

(B) The operator acts by
A_L1_E=d_L1_E,
A_L(B_L^*y)=-(L-3)B_L^*y,
A_Lz=z.                                                       (3)
The three invariant sectors in this order have dimensions
1, L-1, L(L-3)/2.                                            (4)
For L>=5 their eigenvalues are distinct, so the spectrum with multiplicities is d_L with multiplicity 1, -(L-3) with multiplicity L-1, and 1 with multiplicity L(L-3)/2. For L=4 the spectrum is 1 with total multiplicity 3 and -1 with multiplicity 3: the one-dimensional constant sector and the two-dimensional star-null sector share the eigenvalue 1.

(C) The exact Hermitian disjointness quadratic form is
sum_{G,G' disjoint}conjugate(x_G)x_{G'}
 =(d_L/n_L)|t|^2
  -((L-3)/(L-2))sum_r|s_r-2t/L|^2
  +sum_G|z_G|^2.                                              (5)
The exact algebraic form of fact 890c794f463db36a is
sum_{G,G' disjoint}x_Gx_{G'}
 =(d_L/n_L)t^2
  -((L-3)/(L-2))sum_r(s_r-2t/L)^2
  +sum_G z_G^2.                                               (6)

(D) In the actual fixed-semiprime source family of fact 890c794f463db36a, importance-sampled decoder reopening leaves the scalar coefficients x_G and hence t,s^0,z unchanged. Thus labelled l2 dilution cannot alter the three spectral sectors after the copies are summed back to the scalar common-cell kernel. If the literal source deletion is h-symmetric as in fact 0abb9119d9247de6, then every x_G is real and (5) equals (6). In that case any source-specific cancellation of the positive constant sector must occur through the negative centered prime-star sector, up to the positive star-null sector. No estimate asserting that the literal source realizes such a balance, no source lower bound, no varying-fibre estimate, no cell capture, and no Goldbach implication is asserted.
06485889a0b3e455.proof:
For G,G' in mathcal E_L, the (G,G') entry of B_L^*B_L is |G intersect G'|. Therefore, writing J_E for the all-one operator on C^{mathcal E_L},
A_L=J_E-B_L^*B_L+I_E.                                       (7)
Indeed, the right side has entry 1 when G and G' are disjoint, entry 1-1=0 when they are distinct and meet in one point, and diagonal entry 1-2+1=0.

For r,r' in mathcal P_L, the (r,r') entry of B_LB_L^* counts two-subsets containing both r and r'. It is L-1 on the diagonal and 1 off the diagonal. Hence
B_LB_L^*=(L-2)I_P+J_P.                                      (8)

Since each G has two elements,
sum_r s_r=2t.
It follows that sum_r s_r^0=0 and therefore sum_r y_r=0. Also
B_L(a1_E)=a(L-1)1_P=(2t/L)1_P,
because n_L=L(L-1)/2. By (8) and sum_r y_r=0,
B_LB_L^*y=(L-2)y=s^0.
Applying B_L to the definition of z in (1) now gives
B_Lz=s-(2t/L)1_P-s^0=0.                                    (9)
Equation (9) also gives sum_G z_G=0, since twice this last sum equals sum_r(B_Lz)_r.

The three summands in (2) are pairwise orthogonal. First,
<1_E,B_L^*y>=<B_L1_E,y>=(L-1)<1_P,y>=0.
Second, <1_E,z>=sum_G z_G=0. Third,
<B_L^*y,z>=<y,B_Lz>=0.
This proves (A).

Every fixed G is disjoint from exactly d_L two-subsets, so A_L1_E=d_L1_E. If sum_r y_r=0, then for G={i,j},
(A_LB_L^*y)_G
 =sum_{{k,l} subset mathcal P_L minus {i,j}}(y_k+y_l).
Each k outside {i,j} occurs in exactly L-3 summands. The last display is therefore
(L-3)sum_{k outside {i,j}}y_k
 =-(L-3)(y_i+y_j)
 =-(L-3)(B_L^*y)_G.                                        (10)
Finally, (7), (9), and sum_Gz_G=0 give A_Lz=z. This proves (3).

Equation (8) is positive definite for L>=4: on 1_P it has eigenvalue 2(L-1), and on the orthogonal complement it has eigenvalue L-2. Thus B_L has rank L. Its range under B_L^* splits as the one-dimensional constant sector and the (L-1)-dimensional centered prime-star sector. The kernel of B_L has dimension
n_L-L=L(L-3)/2.
This proves the sector dimensions (4). For L>=5, d_L>1, while -(L-3)<0, so the three sector eigenvalues in (3) are distinct and have the stated multiplicities. For L=4, d_L=1, the constant and star-null sectors have respective dimensions 1 and 2, and the centered prime-star sector has dimension 3 and eigenvalue -1. This proves the separate L=4 spectrum and completes (B).

By orthogonality and (3),
<A_Lx,x>=d_L||a1_E||^2-(L-3)||B_L^*y||^2+||z||^2.           (11)
Here
||a1_E||^2=|t|^2/n_L,
while (8) and sum y=0 give
||B_L^*y||^2=<B_LB_L^*y,y>
 =(L-2)||y||^2
 =(L-2)^{-1}||s^0||^2.
Substitution in (11) proves (5). The same pairwise orthogonality calculations are valid for the complex bilinear dot product without conjugation, since all matrices and the decomposition coefficients are real. Replacing Hermitian norm squares by algebraic squares in (11) proves (6), which refines the top/prime-star identity of fact 890c794f463db36a on the complete cell.

Part (D) follows from fact 890c794f463db36a: its importance-sampled copies sum pairwise back to the same scalar coefficients x_Gx_{G'}, so reopening does not change x and cannot change any linear projection of x. Under the h-symmetry hypothesis, fact 0abb9119d9247de6 gives eta_{-h}=conjugate(eta_h) inside each fixed support fibre. Since h=0 is absent, gamma_G is real, and kappa_G=phi(G)/G is real, so x_G is real. Then (5) and (6) coincide. Their signs show precisely the stated necessary structural mechanism, without supplying any estimate for the sizes of the three source sectors.

glossary.B_L: The prime-versus-support incidence map from C^{mathcal E_L} to C^{mathcal P_L}.

06a7e3e83ec7551e.title: Fix L>=1 and epsilon>0. Let H>=2, let C be a nonzero integer with |C|<=H^L, and let real numbers U_1,U_2,U_3,U_4 satisfy 1<=U_i<=H. Let P(C;U_1,U_2,U_3,U_4) be the set of ordered tuples
06a7e3e83ec7551e.author: slava chan
06a7e3e83ec7551e.statement:
Fix L>=1 and epsilon>0. Let H>=2, let C be a nonzero integer with |C|<=H^L, and let real numbers U_1,U_2,U_3,U_4 satisfy 1<=U_i<=H. Let P(C;U_1,U_2,U_3,U_4) be the set of ordered tuples
(r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4,b_1,b_2,b_3,b_4)
such that the r_i are pairwise distinct primes in [H^2,2H^2), the b_i are nonzero integers with U_i<|b_i|<=2U_i, and
C=(b_1r_2+b_2r_1)r_3r_4+(b_3r_4+b_4r_3)r_1r_2.
For s in {+1,-1} put S_{12}^s=b_1r_2+s b_2r_1 and U_min=min(U_1,U_2).

For every V>=0, the number of tuples in P(C;U_1,U_2,U_3,U_4) satisfying |S_{12}^s|<=V is
<<_{L,epsilon} H^{4+epsilon}U_min(1+V/H^2).
Without a strip restriction one has
|P(C;U_1,U_2,U_3,U_4)|<<_{L,epsilon}H^{4+epsilon}U_1U_2.
Consequently either condition
U_1U_2<=H
or
|S_{12}^s|U_min<=H^3
defines a subfamily of cardinality <<_{L,epsilon}H^{5+epsilon}.

Assume additionally that gcd(C,r_1r_2r_3r_4)=1 for every tuple under consideration. Then the subfamily satisfying
H gcd(|C|,|S_{12}^s|)>=U_1U_2
also has cardinality <<_{L,epsilon}H^{5+epsilon}. The same conclusions hold for any of the six choices of a pair of frequency-prime slots after relabeling the complementary pair.

Finally, suppose the four U_i range over dyadic values, each packet weight is at most (log(2H))^B for a fixed B>=0, and L_H(C) is a nonnegative common carrier weight supported on 0<|C|<=H^L with total mass at most H^9(log(2H))^B. Summed over all dyadic boxes, all six pairs, and both signs, each of the small-frequency, signed-small-strip, and unit large-gcd boundary aggregates weighted by L_H(C) is <<_{L,B,epsilon}H^{14+epsilon}.
06a7e3e83ec7551e.proof:
We prove the assertions for the pair (1,2); relabeling gives the other pairs. Put G=r_1r_2, T=r_3r_4, B_0=b_1r_2+b_2r_1, and D_0=b_3r_4+b_4r_3. The carrier equation is C=B_0T+GD_0.

First count the strip |S_{12}^s|<=V. There are O(H^4) choices for the ordered pair (r_1,r_2). If U_1<=U_2, choose b_1 in O(U_1) ways. The inequality
|b_1r_2+s b_2r_1|<=V
places b_2 in a real interval of length 2V/r_1, so it contains O(1+V/H^2) integers. If U_2<U_1, choose b_2 first and obtain the same bound with U_2. Thus the first pair of frequencies costs
O(U_min(1+V/H^2)).

The integer B_0 is coprime to G. Indeed modulo r_1 it is b_1r_2, which is nonzero because r_1 and r_2 are distinct and 0<|b_1|<=2H<r_1 for all sufficiently large H; the finitely many smaller H are absorbed into the implied constant. The argument modulo r_2 is identical. Reducing the carrier equation modulo G therefore gives
T congruent to C B_0^{-1} modulo G.
The interval H^4<=T<4H^4 has length 3H^4, while G>=H^4, so it contains at most four integers in this residue class. Each such nonzero T has <<_epsilon H^epsilon ordered factorizations T=r_3r_4: this follows from the elementary divisor bound tau(n)<<_delta n^delta, proved in fact 3c92603bdcab54d5, and T<4H^4. Requiring the two factors to be distinct primes in the stated interval only decreases the count.

Once r_3,r_4 are fixed, D_0=(C-B_0T)/G is fixed. The congruence D_0 congruent to b_3r_4 modulo r_3 determines b_3 modulo r_3. Since |b_3|<=2H and r_3>=H^2, it gives O(1) possible b_3, uniformly after absorbing bounded H. Then b_4=(D_0-b_3r_4)/r_3 is unique. Thus the complementary frequencies cost O(1). Multiplying the preceding choices proves
#{|S_{12}^s|<=V}<<_{L,epsilon}H^{4+epsilon}U_min(1+V/H^2).
The same argument with both b_1 and b_2 chosen freely gives the unrestricted bound H^{4+epsilon}U_1U_2.

If U_1U_2<=H, the unrestricted bound is H^{5+epsilon}. If |S_{12}^s|U_min<=H^3, take V=H^3/U_min in the strip bound. Since U_min<=H,
U_min(1+V/H^2)=U_min+H<=2H,
which gives the same conclusion.

Now impose gcd(C,r_1r_2r_3r_4)=1. If a tuple satisfies H gcd(|C|,|S_{12}^s|)>=U_1U_2, put g=gcd(|C|,|S_{12}^s|). To upper-bound all such tuples, sum over every positive divisor d of |C| satisfying d>=U_1U_2/H and impose d|S_{12}^s. The unit hypothesis gives gcd(d,r_1r_2)=1. For fixed r_1,r_2 and a choice of the frequency in the shorter window, the congruence
b_1r_2+s b_2r_1 congruent to 0 modulo d
places the other frequency in one residue class modulo d. It therefore has O(1+U_max/d) choices, where U_max=max(U_1,U_2). The first-pair frequency cost is
O(U_min+U_1U_2/d).
For every divisor being summed, this is O(H): if U_1U_2/H>=1, use d>=U_1U_2/H; if U_1U_2/H<1, then U_1U_2<H and d>=1. The remaining product and frequencies cost H^{epsilon} by the preceding product-congruence argument. The number of divisors d of C is <<_{L,epsilon}H^epsilon by the divisor bound and |C|<=H^L. Hence the large-gcd subfamily has size <<_{L,epsilon}H^{5+epsilon}, after decreasing the auxiliary epsilon parameters inside the proof.

For the final aggregate, there are O((log(2H))^4) dyadic frequency boxes and only twelve pair-sign choices. In each box the relevant pointwise boundary count is <<H^{5+epsilon/4}. Multiplication by the packet-weight bound, by the total L_H-mass H^9(log(2H))^B, and by the polylogarithmic number of boxes and choices gives
<<H^{14+epsilon/4}(log(2H))^{2B+4}.
For fixed B and epsilon the logarithmic factor is <<H^{3epsilon/4}. This proves the claimed H^{14+epsilon} weighted bounds.

glossary.D_0: the complementary plus pair carrier b_3r_4+b_4r_3
glossary.L_H(C): the common nonnegative carrier weight used in the boundary aggregate
glossary.P(C;U_1,U_2,U_3,U_4): the fixed-carrier dyadic four-prime packet family
glossary.S_{12}^s: the signed pair carrier in slots 1 and 2
glossary.U_max: the larger of the two frequency scales U_1 and U_2
glossary.U_min: the smaller of the two frequency scales U_1 and U_2

06aa6fe1a991b7b5.title: SHARP PUBLISHED-THEOREM NO-FIT FOR THE ACTUAL-\(Z_{\rm mid}\) RECIPROCAL-PLUS-SQUARE-ROOT BOUNDARY
06aa6fe1a991b7b5.author: slava chan
06aa6fe1a991b7b5.statement:
SHARP PUBLISHED-THEOREM NO-FIT FOR THE ACTUAL-\(Z_{\rm mid}\) RECIPROCAL-PLUS-SQUARE-ROOT BOUNDARY.

Use the exact selected-source moving-boundary transfer of fact \(152484e836f90c47\). Its only potentially nonzero hard Fourier face is
\[
 -\frac{F_{g,a,b}(u_{g,a,b})}{2\pi i h}
 e_a(-Lh\bar b)e\!\left(\frac{h\sqrt{gb}}a\right),       \tag{1}
\]
where \(L=N/g\), \(a\asymp Q=D/g\), \(b\asymp B=R/g\), \(B>Q\), and \(h\ne0\). The complete literal conjugate-paired sum of (1), over all exact \(g\mid N\), physical \(a,b,h\), source labels, and unchanged Möbius, logarithmic, dyadic, fixed-\(U\), high, parent, tag, and provenance masks, is denoted by \(\mathfrak B_{\sqrt{\ }}\).

The following are the full theorem slots audited here.

Banks--Shparlinski, arXiv:1411.1820, Lemma 11, fixes arbitrary integers \(A_{BS}\) and \(C_{BS}\ne0\), positive integers \(M_{BS}\le N_{BS}\), sets
\[
 \mathfrak M\subseteq(M_{BS},2M_{BS}],\qquad
 \mathfrak N\subseteq(N_{BS},2N_{BS}],
\]
and for each \(n\asymp N_{BS}\) integers \(K_n,L_n\) satisfying
\[
 M_{BS}\le K_n<K_n+L_n\le2M_{BS}.
\]
If \(|A_{BS}|M_{BS}\le N_{BS}\), then
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sum_{\substack{(m,n)\in\mathfrak M\times\mathfrak N\\
 K_n<m\le K_n+L_n\\(m,n)=1}}
 e_n(A_{BS}m+C_{BS}\bar m)
 \ll&
 |\mathfrak M|^{1/2}|\mathfrak N|^{1/2}
 \left(1+\frac{|C_{BS}|}{M_{BS}N_{BS}}\right)^{1/4}\\
 &\times
 \left(N_{BS}^{7/8}
       +M_{BS}^{3/10}N_{BS}^{13/20}\right)N_{BS}^{o(1)}
 +|A_{BS}|J_{BS}M_{BS}N_{BS}^{-1},                            \tag{2}
\end{aligned}
\]
where \(\bar m\) is the inverse of \(m\) modulo \(n\) and \(J_{BS}\) is the number of pairs satisfying the displayed interval and coprimality conditions.

Kerr--Shparlinski--Wu--Xi, arXiv:2204.05038, Theorem 2.4, fixes positive integers \(q,r\) with \(r\mid q\), an interval \(\mathcal I\) of length \(M\), \(1\le K\le r\), arbitrary coefficients \(\alpha_m,\gamma_k\), and units \(A\in\mathbb Z_q^*\), \(c\in\mathbb Z_r^*\). For
\[
 \mathcal W
 =\sum_{m\in\mathcal I}
   \sum_{\substack{k\in\mathbb Z_q^*\\
   \langle ck\rangle_r\le K}}
   \alpha_m\gamma_k e_q(Am\bar k),
\]
it proves
\[
 |\mathcal W|
 \ll \|\alpha\|_2\|\gamma\|_\infty
 M^{1/2}Kq^{1+o(1)}r^{-1}\Delta_2,                            \tag{3}
\]
where any one of
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Delta_2={}&(Mq/r)^{-1/4}+M^{-1/2}+(Kq/r)^{-1/2},\\
 \Delta_2={}&M^{-1/2}\{1+(K/r)^{-1/4}+K^{-1}r^{1/2}\}
              +(Kq/r)^{-1/2},\\
 \Delta_2={}&M^{-1/2}\{1+K^{-1/2}r^{1/4}+K^{-1}r^{3/4}\}
              +(Kq/r)^{-1/2}
\end{aligned}                                                \tag{4}
\]
may be used.

Theorems 2.5 and 2.6 of the same paper fix a prime \(p\), a fixed positive integer \(s\), an arbitrary set \(\mathcal M\subseteq\mathbb F_p\) of cardinality \(M\), an interval \(\mathcal K\subseteq\mathbb F_p^*\) of length \(K\ge p^{1/s}\), arbitrary bounded separated coefficients \(\alpha_m,\gamma_k\), and a unit \(A\in\mathbb F_p^*\). For
\[
 \mathcal W_p
 =\sum_{m\in\mathcal M}\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}
   \alpha_m\gamma_k e_p(Am\bar k),
\]
Theorem 2.5 proves
\[
 |\mathcal W_p|
 \ll \|\alpha\|_\infty\|\gamma\|_\infty
 MKp^{o(1)}
 \left(\frac1M+\frac{p^{1+1/s}}{MK^2}\right)^{7/(24s)},    \tag{5}
\]
and, assuming additionally \(M\le p^{1/2}\), Theorem 2.6 proves
\[
 |\mathcal W_p|
 \ll \|\alpha\|_\infty\|\gamma\|_\infty
 MKp^{o(1)}
 \left(\frac1{M^{2s}}+\frac1K+
       \frac{p^{1+1/s}}{M^{10/13}K^2}\right)^{1/(4s)}.       \tag{6}
\]

Theorems 2.7 and 2.8 fix a prime \(p\), a fixed positive integer \(s\), an arbitrary set \(\mathcal M\subseteq\mathbb F_p\) of cardinality \(M\), an interval \(\mathcal J\subseteq\mathbb F_p^*\) of length \(T\le p^{1-1/s}\), and coefficients \(\alpha_m\). For
\[
 \mathcal S_p
 =\sum_{m\in\mathcal M}\sum_{n\in\mathcal J}
   \alpha_m\mathcal K_p(m,n),
\]
Theorem 2.7 proves
\[
 |\mathcal S_p|
 \ll \|\alpha\|_\infty MTp^{1/2+o(1)}
 \left(
 \frac{p^{1/2}}{M^{7/(24s)}T}
 +\frac{p^{1/2-7(s-1)/(24s^2)}}
        {M^{7/(24s)}T^{1-7/(12s)}}
 \right),                                                    \tag{7}
\]
while Theorem 2.8, assuming additionally \(M\le p^{1/2}\), proves
\[
\begin{aligned}
 |\mathcal S_p|
 \ll \|\alpha\|_\infty MTp^{1/2+o(1)}
 \bigg(
 &\frac{p^{1/2}}{M^{1/2}T}
 +\frac{p^{1/2-1/(4s)}}{T^{1-1/(4s)}}\\
 &+\frac{p^{1/2-(s-1)/(4s^2)}}
         {M^{13/(40s)}T^{1-1/(2s)}}
 \bigg).                                                     \tag{8}
\end{aligned}
\]
Corollary 2.9 gives constants \(\delta,\eta>0\), for every fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), such that
\[
 |\mathcal S_p|
 \ll \|\alpha\|_\infty MTp^{1/2-\eta}                   \tag{9}
\]
when \(M>p^\varepsilon\) and \(T>p^{1/2-\delta}\).

None of (2)--(9) is a direct specialization to \(\mathfrak B_{\sqrt{\ }}\). For the lower boundary before its forced-high vanishing, the only exact Banks--Shparlinski variable map is
\[
 m_{BS}=b,\quad n_{BS}=a,\quad
 M_{BS}\asymp B,\quad N_{BS}\asymp Q,\quad
 A_{BS}=hg,\quad C_{BS}=-hL.                                \tag{10}
\]
It fails both \(M_{BS}\le N_{BS}\), because \(B>Q\), and
\[
 |A_{BS}|M_{BS}\le N_{BS},
\]
because \(|A_{BS}|M_{BS}\asymp |h|gB=|h|R>Q\). The upper phase (1) is not linear in \(b\), so it has no map even after ignoring those failed scale hypotheses.

For (3)--(6), the pure reciprocal kernel has one fixed modulus and separated one-variable coefficients. Mapping \(m=h,k=b,q=a\) leaves the joint factor
\[
 e(h\sqrt{gb}/a),
\]
which depends simultaneously on \(h\) and the actual integer lift \(b\) and cannot be absorbed into either separated coefficient. In addition, the physical modulus \(a\) varies, \(-L\) need not be a unit modulo \(a\), and \(b\asymp B>Q\asymp a\) may have several lifts of one residue with different square-root factors. Theorems 2.5 and 2.6 also require the modulus to be prime, which the physical \(a\) is not required to be. Theorems 2.7--2.9 concern complete Kloosterman sums at a fixed prime modulus, whereas (1) is an incomplete reciprocal phase with no complete Kloosterman summation variable. Thus their hypotheses do not contain (1).

This is a sharp direct-specialization no-fit, not an impossibility theorem for new arguments. The minimal natural-mask theorem slot exposed by the audit is:

\(\mathbf{MZB}\). There exists a fixed \(\delta>0\) such that the complete actual-\(Z_{\rm mid}\) moving-boundary contribution obtained from fact \(152484e836f90c47\)—including (1), its derivative-integral term, or equivalently an exact \(\Delta\)-smooth interior plus both literal boundary strips, summed over every physical varying modulus \(a\), actual lift \(b\), frequency \(h\), exact \(g\mid N\), and all unchanged natural source masks—is \(O(x^{1-\delta})\) uniformly for the selected bad \(N\).

MZB permits only the literal natural mask and does not ask for arbitrary-mask stability. It is not proved here. No endpoint capture, \(C2\) selection, terminal deficit, four-prime equivalence, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
06aa6fe1a991b7b5.proof:
Fact \(152484e836f90c47\) proves (1), including every source factor and the exact distinction between smooth amplitudes and arithmetic index masks.

We first verify the Banks--Shparlinski audit. Its Lemma 11 is reproduced in (2), with all scale, moving-interval, coefficient, coprimality, and linear-phase hypotheses. The lower boundary term in fact \(152484e836f90c47\), before its forced-high vanishing is used, has phase
\[
 e_a(hgb-Lh\bar b).
\]
Thus its inverse variable is \(b\), its modulus variable is \(a\), its linear coefficient is \(hg\), and its reciprocal coefficient is \(-hL\). This forces (10). The source scales give
\[
 B=R/g>D/g=Q,
\]
so the theorem's required ordering \(M_{BS}\le N_{BS}\) fails. Also
\[
 |A_{BS}|M_{BS}\asymp |h|gB=|h|R
 >D\ge D/g=Q\asymp N_{BS},
\]
so the small-linear-phase hypothesis fails for every nonzero \(h\). Swapping the two theorem variables is not an alternative map: it would put the modulus at \(b\), whereas the inverse in the actual phase is \(\bar b\pmod a\). Finally the upper phase replaces the linear term \(hgb/a\) by \(h\sqrt{gb}/a\), which is not \(A_{BS}b/a\) for an integer \(A_{BS}\) independent of \(b\). Hence Lemma 11 does not directly apply.

For the Kerr--Shparlinski--Wu--Xi audit, equations (3)--(9) reproduce Theorems 2.4--2.8 and Corollary 2.9 with their modulus, length, coefficient, interval, set, unit, and prime hypotheses. In the only formal incomplete-reciprocal map, the first variable is \(h\), the inverse variable is the residue of \(b\), and the modulus is \(a\). The reciprocal part of (1) is then of the form \(e_a(-Lh\bar b)\), but the remaining multiplier is
\[
 e(h\sqrt{gb}/a).
\]
For two frequencies \(h_1\ne h_2\), the ratio of these multipliers depends on \(b\), so it cannot be a coefficient depending only on \(h\); for two actual lifts \(b_1,b_2\), it depends on \(h\), so it cannot be a coefficient depending only on the inverse-variable residue. Therefore it is not among the separated arbitrary coefficients in (3), (5), or (6). This kernel mismatch is independent of exponent choices.

Theorem 2.4 also fixes one modulus \(q\) and requires its phase parameter to be a unit. The literal family sums varying \(a\), and no predecessor asserts \((L,a)=1\). Aggregating the actual \(b\)-values by residues modulo \(a\) does not repair the issue because the square-root multiplier depends on the lift. Theorems 2.5 and 2.6 require \(a\) to be prime after the proposed map, an absent hypothesis. Theorems 2.7--2.9 require the complete Kloosterman kernel \(\mathcal K_p(m,n)\), which contains an additional complete unit summation and again fixes a prime modulus. Formula (1) contains neither. Thus none is a direct specialization.

The MZB paragraph merely records the exact weakest complete natural family that must be estimated to transport the actual-\(Z_{\rm mid}\) deletion through Poisson. It retains every term from the accepted identity and requests a fixed power saving only for that literal family, not arbitrary masks. No estimate for it is claimed, completing the scoped audit.

073df17b2efc41d6.title: Let Q_lvl>1 and let ell be a prime with ell>Q_lvl^(1/3). Every sequence which is triply well-factorable of level Q_lvl in the sense reproduced in fact 3bcd070f8558ce6f has value zero at ell. Consequently every finite complex linear combination of triply well-factorable sequences of the same level Q_lvl also has value zero at ell
073df17b2efc41d6.author: slava chan
073df17b2efc41d6.statement:
Let Q_lvl>1 and let ell be a prime with ell>Q_lvl^(1/3). Every sequence which is triply well-factorable of level Q_lvl in the sense reproduced in fact 3bcd070f8558ce6f has value zero at ell. Consequently every finite complex linear combination of triply well-factorable sequences of the same level Q_lvl also has value zero at ell.

In the high-divisor construction of fact 3bcd070f8558ce6f, the raw weight lambda_D has lambda_D(ell) nonzero at such a prime ell. Therefore lambda_D cannot equal any finite complex linear combination of triply well-factorable level-Q_lvl sequences. It also admits no pointwise nonnegative majorant M which is itself triply well-factorable of level Q_lvl and satisfies M(n)>=|lambda_D(n)| for every positive integer n: at the displayed ell one would have 0=M(ell)>=|lambda_D(ell)|>0.

This obstruction is confined to exact finite linear recombination and pointwise majorization inside the same triply well-factorable class. It does not rule out a comparison after changing variables or modulus, an inequality that uses cancellation rather than pointwise domination, an infinite limiting procedure with altered levels, a different factorability class, or a new raw-weight theorem.
073df17b2efc41d6.proof:
The balanced-factorization argument in fact 3bcd070f8558ce6f proves that a triply well-factorable sequence f of level Q_lvl satisfies f(ell)=0 at every prime ell>Q_lvl^(1/3). If f_1,...,f_J are any finite family of such sequences and c_1,...,c_J are complex numbers, then
sum_{j=1}^J c_j f_j(ell)=sum_{j=1}^J c_j*0=0.
This proves the finite-linear-combination assertion.

The same predecessor supplies a high-divisor raw weight lambda_D and a prime ell>Q_lvl^(1/3) with lambda_D(ell) nonzero. Equality between lambda_D and a finite linear combination would give zero and a nonzero value at ell, a contradiction.

Finally suppose M is nonnegative, triply well-factorable of level Q_lvl, and pointwise dominates |lambda_D|. The support lemma gives M(ell)=0, while domination gives M(ell)>=|lambda_D(ell)|>0, again a contradiction. The proof uses only evaluation at one prime and therefore establishes none of the broader exclusions listed in the final scope sentence.

0747c1083be2ef08.title: Fix an integer m>=2, a real number eta with 0<eta<1/2, and a bounded complex function W supported in [1+eta,2-eta]. Let x tend to infinity through positive real values for which N=2x is an integer, and define R_{m,N}(W)=sum_{p prime, p<N, p congruent to N modulo m} log(p) mu((N-p)/m) W(p/x). A direct specialization of Banks and Shparlinski, arXiv:2506.08787, Theorem 2.1, with the physical prime p as its first variable gives, for every fixed C>0, the bound R_{m,N}(W)<<_{C,m,W} x^2(log x)^(1-C). For every fixed C this upper bound is asymptotically larger than x/log x, so this direct specialization cannot by itself prove R_{m,N}(W)=o(x/log x). If instead the first theorem variable is compressed to the prime index k and its injective map is f(k)=p_k, where p_k is the k-th prime, then the Möbius factor supplied by the theorem is mu(kd), not mu(p_k d) and not mu(d); hence this prime-indexed expression is not a direct coefficient-preserving specialization of R_{m,N}(W). This is only a no-direct-specialization statement, not an assertion that R_{m,N}(W) cannot be estimated by another argument
0747c1083be2ef08.author: slava chan
0747c1083be2ef08.statement: Fix an integer m>=2, a real number eta with 0<eta<1/2, and a bounded complex function W supported in [1+eta,2-eta]. Let x tend to infinity through positive real values for which N=2x is an integer, and define R_{m,N}(W)=sum_{p prime, p<N, p congruent to N modulo m} log(p) mu((N-p)/m) W(p/x). A direct specialization of Banks and Shparlinski, arXiv:2506.08787, Theorem 2.1, with the physical prime p as its first variable gives, for every fixed C>0, the bound R_{m,N}(W)<<_{C,m,W} x^2(log x)^(1-C). For every fixed C this upper bound is asymptotically larger than x/log x, so this direct specialization cannot by itself prove R_{m,N}(W)=o(x/log x). If instead the first theorem variable is compressed to the prime index k and its injective map is f(k)=p_k, where p_k is the k-th prime, then the Möbius factor supplied by the theorem is mu(kd), not mu(p_k d) and not mu(d); hence this prime-indexed expression is not a direct coefficient-preserving specialization of R_{m,N}(W). This is only a no-direct-specialization statement, not an assertion that R_{m,N}(W) cannot be estimated by another argument.
0747c1083be2ef08.proof:
We first state exactly the external result being used. In the notation of Banks and Shparlinski [BS25, Theorem 2.1], take three intervals Acal=[1,A_BS], Bcal=[1,B_BS], and Ncal=[1,L_BS]. Let u and v be complex weights of supremum norm at most one, let f:Acal intersect Supp(u)->Z and g:Bcal intersect Supp(v)->Z be injective, and let wp:Z->Z be a bracket polynomial of complexity delta. Their constrained sum is
S_mu(D;M)=sum_{n_1 in Acal, n_2 in Bcal, n_3 in Ncal, f(n_1)+g(n_2)+wp(n_3)=M} u_{n_1}v_{n_2} mu(n_1 n_2 n_3).
For C>0, L_BS>=10, and log L_BS >= (log max{A_BS,B_BS})^theta with a fixed theta>0, the theorem states
S_mu(D;M)<<_{C,theta,delta}(A_BS+B_BS)L_BS(log L_BS)^(-C).

We now give the physical-prime embedding, including every theorem slot. Put A_BS=N-1, B_BS=1, and L_BS=floor((N-1)/m). Put
K_x=max{1, ||W||_infinity log(N-1)}.
For 1<=n_1<=A_BS define u_{n_1}=1_{n_1 is prime} log(n_1)W(n_1/x)/K_x. Put v_1=1, f(n_1)=n_1, g(1)=0, wp(n_3)=m n_3, and M=N. Both weights have supremum norm at most one. The identity map f is injective on the support of u, g is injective on its one-point domain, and wp is an ordinary integral polynomial, hence a bracket polynomial of fixed complexity. Since m is fixed, L_BS is asymptotic to 2x/m. Consequently, for any fixed theta in (0,1), one has L_BS>=10 and log L_BS >= (log max{A_BS,B_BS})^theta once x is sufficiently large.

The constraint in the theorem is exactly p+md=N, with p prime because of the support of u and d=n_3. It parametrizes precisely the terms of R_{m,N}(W). Moreover, a term in the support of W has p>=(1+eta)x, and therefore
d=(2x-p)/m <= (1-eta)x/m < p.
Thus p does not divide d. Complete multiplicativity of the Möbius function on coprime arguments, together with mu(p)=-1, gives mu(pd)=-mu(d), including the case mu(d)=0. It follows that the specialized theorem sum is exactly
S_mu(D;N)=-R_{m,N}(W)/K_x.
Theorem 2.1 therefore gives
|R_{m,N}(W)|<<_{C,theta} K_x(A_BS+B_BS)L_BS(log L_BS)^(-C)
<<_{C,m,W} x^2(log x)^(1-C).
The ratio of the displayed right-hand side to x/log x is, up to a fixed multiplicative constant, x(log x)^(2-C), which tends to infinity for every fixed C. Hence this estimate has one full factor of x that no fixed logarithmic saving supplied by the theorem removes. It cannot by itself establish the requested o(x/log x) scale. This scale mismatch agrees with the authors' warning in [BS25, Section 7.6] that the H=1 binary-Goldbach-type case in their short-variable family remains out of reach and is a variant of the Chowla problem; that warning is used only as corroborating context, not as an impossibility theorem.

Finally consider the tempting compression n_1=k, f(k)=p_k. The defining formula of Theorem 2.1 always places the actual input variable n_1 inside mu(n_1 n_2 n_3). With n_2=1 and n_3=d, its coefficient is therefore mu(kd), even though its additive constraint is p_k+md=N. The physical-prime embedding instead has mu(pd), which on the separated support equals -mu(d). There is no general coefficient identity mu(kd)=mu(p_kd) or mu(kd)=mu(d); for example, whenever k and d share a prime factor while d is squarefree, mu(kd)=0 although mu(d) is nonzero. Thus replacing p by its index may shorten the first interval, but it changes the Möbius coefficient and does not directly specialize the target sum. The argument rules out only these two direct uses of Theorem 2.1 at the required scale and makes no claim about indirect uses or other methods.

glossary.A_BS: length of the first interval in the Banks–Shparlinski specialization
glossary.B_BS: length of the second interval in the Banks–Shparlinski specialization
glossary.L_BS: length of the third interval in the Banks–Shparlinski specialization
glossary.S_mu(D;M): the constrained three-variable Möbius sum in Banks–Shparlinski Theorem 2.1
glossary.eta: fixed positive separation of the support of W from 1 and 2
glossary.theta: fixed exponent in the logarithmic size condition of Banks–Shparlinski Theorem 2.1

076bc0ba8fc2536a.title: ACTUAL LITERAL-DIGIT OBSTRUCTION TO THE GENERIC-FIBRE TRIANGLE LEDGER
076bc0ba8fc2536a.author: slava chan
076bc0ba8fc2536a.statement:
ACTUAL LITERAL-DIGIT OBSTRUCTION TO THE GENERIC-FIBRE TRIANGLE LEDGER.

Let m>=9 be odd and put
 U_cut=floor(m/4)+1,  N=2(U_cut-1).                                 (1)
For a residue nu modulo m define the literal interval-multiplicity weight
 W_{U,m}(nu)=#{u in Z:0<|u|<U_cut and u is congruent to nu modulo m} (2)
and its centered version
 W_star(nu)=W_{U,m}(nu)-N/m.                                       (3)
Then
 sum_{nu modulo m}W_star(nu)=0,
 ||W_star||_2^2=N(1-N/m),                                          (4)
and
 ||W_star||_2>=sqrt(m/6).                                          (5)

Define the digit-only triangle ledger
 D_tri(W_star)=inf sum_j|lambda_j| ||W_j||_2,                       (6)
where the infimum is over all finite exact decompositions
 W_star=sum_jlambda_j W_j
by complex functions W_j modulo m. Then
 D_tri(W_star)=||W_star||_2>=sqrt(m/6).                             (7)

Consequently, consider the method that represents a literal centered digit weight by such a decomposition, applies the generic shared-lift estimate (12) of fact 5b9e0311f7e49ea2 separately to every digit atom while holding a common normalized first-row profile with V_F=1, common column sequences, and all other bounded gates fixed, and finally sums the atom bounds by absolute values. Its normalized IJOP digit tax is at least sqrt(m/6). In particular this method cannot satisfy the sufficient tax contract
 L_IJOP_core<=m^(1/80-delta)                                      (8)
of that fact for any fixed delta>=0 and all sufficiently large m.

The weight (2) is the literal integer normal-coordinate range weight of fact 5f60a4633e6b0b70, not an abstract matrix selector, and fact f23bad095a2e6a52 permits its centered version in the complete generic fixed-fibre carrier-first sum. The obstruction is nevertheless only to the generic ||W||_2 fibre majorant followed by digit-atom triangle assembly. It does not rule out a stronger estimate for the actual carrier-correlated coefficient C_outer that gains from correlations between W_star and the prime, carrier, source, or moving-window gates; nor does it assert a counterexample to the underlying IJOP bound.
076bc0ba8fc2536a.proof:
Since U_cut-1=floor(m/4)<m/2, the residues
 1,2,...,U_cut-1,-1,-2,...,-(U_cut-1)
are pairwise distinct modulo m. Therefore W_{U,m} is the indicator of a set E of exactly N residues. Its mean is N/m, which proves the centering assertion. Directly,
 ||W_star||_2^2
 =N(1-N/m)^2+(m-N)(N/m)^2
 =N-N^2/m=N(1-N/m),                                                (9)
proving (4).

For odd m>=9, floor(m/4)>=m/6 and in fact
 m/3<=2floor(m/4)=N<=m/2.                                         (10)
Thus N>=m/3 and 1-N/m>=1/2. Inserting these two inequalities in (9) gives ||W_star||_2^2>=m/6 and proves (5).

For every exact decomposition in (6), the triangle inequality in the Hilbert space l^2(Z/mZ) gives
 ||W_star||_2
 =||sum_jlambda_jW_j||_2
 <=sum_j|lambda_j|||W_j||_2.                                      (11)
Taking the infimum gives D_tri(W_star)>=||W_star||_2. The one-term decomposition lambda_1=1,W_1=W_star gives the reverse inequality, proving (7).

Fact 5b9e0311f7e49ea2 declares that a separately bounded shared-lift atom contributes a ledger factor ||W_j||_2, multiplied by its coefficient absolute value and by its other profile, fibre, and column factors. With a common profile normalized by V_F=1 and all other gates and columns held fixed, digit-only decomposition followed by the triangle inequality therefore contains exactly the quantity in (6), and hence at least sqrt(m/6). For fixed delta>=0,
 sqrt(m/6)>m^(1/80-delta)
for all sufficiently large m, because 1/2>1/80-delta. This contradicts the sufficient tax requirement (8) within the stated method.

Fact 5f60a4633e6b0b70 identifies (2) as the residue multiplicity induced by a literal bounded integer normal-coordinate interval. Fact f23bad095a2e6a52 accepts arbitrary centered W in the actual carrier-first generic family. Hence the example belongs to that arithmetic digit class. The proof used only the generic digit norm charged by the method and never lower-bounded the true correlated coefficient or the target sum, which proves the final scope limitations.

glossary.D_tri: the minimal digit-only triangle ledger measured by the sum of coefficient-weighted digit L2 norms
glossary.W_star: the centered literal interval-multiplicity digit weight at cutoff floor(m/4)+1

07bfa46055824600.title: SUBUNIT NATURAL-FREQUENCY RESET FOR THE FULL-FREQUENCY RECIPROCAL-ENERGY LEDGER
07bfa46055824600.author: slava chan
07bfa46055824600.statement:
SUBUNIT NATURAL-FREQUENCY RESET FOR THE FULL-FREQUENCY RECIPROCAL-ENERGY LEDGER.

Fix integers \(J,C\ge1\) and \(A_0\ge3\). Let
\[
 Q,H_T,S,T\ge1,\qquad 0<H_P<1,\qquad G=H_T/H_P,
\]
and assume
\[
 C^{-1}QH_T\le ST\le CQH_T.
\]
For each \(q\asymp Q\), choose a unit \(V_q\pmod q\), fix a nonzero integer \(A\), and let \(a_s,b_t\) be divisor-bounded coefficients supported on \(s\asymp S,t\asymp T\). Suppose
\[
 |\nu_h|\le \tau_J(|h|)\left(1+\frac{|h|}{H_P}\right)^{-A_0}
 \qquad(h\ne0).
\]
Put
\[
 W_q=\sum_{\substack{h\ne0,\ s\asymp S,\ t\asymp T\\(st,q)=1}}
 \nu_ha_sb_t e_q(AV_qh(st)^{-1}),
\]
with either no condition between \(s,t\), or with the additional condition \((s,t)=1\). Then, for every \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 H_P^{-1}\sum_{q\asymp Q}|W_q|
 \ll (|A|QST)^\epsilon\big[
 &Q^2H_T^{3/4}S^{-1/4}
 +Q^{7/4}H_T^{3/4}S^{1/4}\\
 &+Q^2H_TS^{-1/2}+Q^{7/4}H_T\big].
\end{aligned} \tag{1}
\]
The same assertion holds for the finite projective aggregate in fact \(f7b5ba9fa0d6cfc8\), with its right side multiplied by the projective \(\ell^1\)-norm.

If, in addition, for fixed \(\tau>0\),
\[
 H_T^2Q^\tau\le S\le Q^{1-\tau}/H_T^2, \tag{2}
\]
and \(|A|,H_T,S,T\le Q^{C_1}\) for a fixed \(C_1\), then there is a fixed
\(\delta=\delta(\tau,C_1)>0\) such that
\[
 H_P^{-1}\sum_{q\asymp Q}|W_q|\ll GQ^{2-\delta}. \tag{3}
\]
This is only an exact \(H_P<1\) reset and its clean-window corollary; it asserts no literal-source identification or outer-label summation.
07bfa46055824600.proof:
Define
\[
 \widetilde H_P=1,\qquad \widetilde G=H_T,\qquad
 \widetilde\nu_h=H_P^{-1}\nu_h.
\]
Since \(h\ne0\) is integral, \(|h|\ge1\). Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
 |\widetilde\nu_h|
 &\le \tau_J(|h|)H_P^{-1}
       \left(1+\frac{|h|}{H_P}\right)^{-A_0}\\
 &\le \tau_J(|h|)H_P^{A_0-1}|h|^{-A_0}
 \le 2^{A_0}\tau_J(|h|)(1+|h|)^{-A_0}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus \(\widetilde\nu_h\) satisfies the frequency hypothesis of fact
\(f7b5ba9fa0d6cfc8\) at the admissible parameter
\(\widetilde H_P=1\). All other hypotheses of that fact are unchanged:
in particular \(ST\asymp QH_T\), the possibly nonunit target \(A\) is fixed
and nonzero, \(V_q\) is a unit, and the optional cross-coprimality
\((s,t)=1\) is allowed.

Let \(\widetilde W_q\) denote the same sum as \(W_q\), but with
\(\widetilde\nu_h\) in place of \(\nu_h\). Exactly,
\[
 \widetilde W_q=H_P^{-1}W_q,
 \qquad
 \widetilde H_P^{-1}\sum_{q\asymp Q}|\widetilde W_q|
 =H_P^{-1}\sum_{q\asymp Q}|W_q|.
\]
Apply fact \(f7b5ba9fa0d6cfc8\) with parameters
\(\widetilde H_P=1\) and \(\widetilde G=H_T\). Its four terms become,
respectively,
\[
 Q^2H_T^{3/4}S^{-1/4},\quad
 Q^{7/4}H_T^{3/4}S^{1/4},\quad
 Q^2H_TS^{-1/2},\quad
 Q^{7/4}H_T,
\]
which proves (1). Its projective-family conclusion is preserved by the
same coefficient rescaling, proving the projective assertion.

Under (2), the first and second terms in (1) are at most
\[
 Q^{2-\tau/4}H_T^{1/4};
\]
indeed the first uses the lower inequality in (2), and the second uses the
upper inequality. The third and fourth terms are at most
\[
 Q^{2-\tau/2}\quad\hbox{and}\quad Q^{7/4}H_T.
\]
Since
\[
 GQ^2=Q^2H_T/H_P,
\]
the ratios of these four bounds to \(GQ^2\) are at most
\[
 H_PH_T^{-3/4}Q^{-\tau/4},\quad
 H_PH_T^{-3/4}Q^{-\tau/4},\quad
 H_PH_T^{-1}Q^{-\tau/2},\quad
 H_PQ^{-1/4}.
\]
Here \(0<H_P<1\) and \(H_T\ge1\), so these ratios are bounded by
\(Q^{-\tau/4},Q^{-\tau/4},Q^{-\tau/2},Q^{-1/4}\), respectively.
The polynomial-size hypotheses make the epsilon factor in (1) at most
\(Q^{C_2\epsilon}\) for a fixed \(C_2=C_2(C,C_1)\). Choose the internal
epsilon sufficiently small compared with \(\min(\tau/4,1/4)/C_2\).
This yields (3) with some fixed positive \(\delta\).

glossary.\\widetilde H_P: The reset natural-frequency parameter, equal to 1 when the physical H_P is below 1.

0880dc648c429047.title: Assume the hypotheses and definitions of fact 2827630745a3225b, and reproduce them as follows. Fix 1/2<a<b<1, a nonzero nonnegative continuously differentiable real function W supported in [a,b], and a continuously differentiable real cutoff ψ with 0≤ψ≤1, ψ(u)=0 for 0<u≤1, and ψ(u)=1 for u≥2. Choose B=B(W,ψ) as in fact 2827630745a3225b. For a sufficiently large even integer N=2x that is not a sum of two primes, put D_*=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B), let 𝔠(N) be the Goldbach singular factor from that fact, and set c_W=2∫_0^∞W(u)du. Let Φ be a real function supported in [1/2,2] with Σ_{j∈Z}Φ(t/2^j)=1 for t>0. For positive dyadic D,M,U define the sibling-complete coarse block
0880dc648c429047.author: slava chan
0880dc648c429047.statement:
Assume the hypotheses and definitions of fact 2827630745a3225b, and reproduce them as follows. Fix 1/2<a<b<1, a nonzero nonnegative continuously differentiable real function W supported in [a,b], and a continuously differentiable real cutoff ψ with 0≤ψ≤1, ψ(u)=0 for 0<u≤1, and ψ(u)=1 for u≥2. Choose B=B(W,ψ) as in fact 2827630745a3225b. For a sufficiently large even integer N=2x that is not a sum of two primes, put D_*=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B), let 𝔠(N) be the Goldbach singular factor from that fact, and set c_W=2∫_0^∞W(u)du. Let Φ be a real function supported in [1/2,2] with Σ_{j∈Z}Φ(t/2^j)=1 for t>0. For positive dyadic D,M,U define the sibling-complete coarse block
B_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;U)=Σ_{d,m,q≥1;dm+q=N}μ(d)log(m)W(dm/x)ψ(d/D_*)Λ(q)Φ(d/D)Φ(m/M)Φ(q/U).
Then the smooth source has the exact decomposition
H_{N,W,ψ}=Σ_{D,M,U}B_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;U),
with at most J_x^3 nonzero blocks, where J_x=ceil(log_2 x)+4. Consequently, every sufficiently large bad N has a positive dyadic triple satisfying
B_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;U)≤-c_W𝔠(N)x/(2J_x^3).

For positive dyadic R,K also define
B_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;U;R,K)=Σ_{d,m,r,k≥1;dm+rk=N}μ(d)μ(r)log(m)log(k)W(dm/x)ψ(d/D_*)Φ(d/D)Φ(m/M)Φ(rk/U)Φ(r/R)Φ(k/K).
For every fixed D,M,U one has the exact sibling recombination identity
B_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;U)=Σ_{R,K}B_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;U;R,K).
Thus the negative coarse block is genuine reflected von-Mangoldt mass and is the complete signed aggregate of all divisor siblings (r,k) in that fixed (D,M,U) block. No individual (R,K) summand is asserted to retain the negativity, and no endpoint localization follows from this fact alone.
0880dc648c429047.proof:
Fact 2827630745a3225b gives
H_{N,W,ψ}=Σ_{d,m≥1}μ(d)log(m)W(dm/x)ψ(d/D_*)Λ(N-dm)
=-c_W𝔠(N)x+o_{W,ψ}(𝔠(N)x).
Write q=N-dm. On the support of W one has ax≤dm≤bx, hence (2-b)x≤q≤(2-a)x. Insert the dyadic partition identity separately in d, m, and q. All sums are finite, and the resulting inner sum is exactly B_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;U). This proves the exact coarse decomposition.

The support also gives d,m≤x and q<2x. If Φ(t/V) is nonzero for a positive integer t<2x and a positive dyadic V, then 1/2≤t/V≤2, so 1/2≤V<4x. As in fact cdb5cefbc7333591, there are at most J_x=ceil(log_2 x)+4 possible dyadic labels per variable. Hence at most J_x^3 coarse blocks are nonzero. For sufficiently large bad N, the source asymptotic implies H_{N,W,ψ}≤-c_W𝔠(N)x/2. If every nonzero coarse block were greater than -c_W𝔠(N)x/(2J_x^3), their sum would be greater than -c_W𝔠(N)x/2, a contradiction. This proves the negative coarse block.

For the sibling identity, use the elementary divisor formula Λ(q)=Σ_{rk=q}μ(r)log k, proved in fact cdb5cefbc7333591. Substitute it into the definition of B_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;U). Then insert 1=Σ_RΦ(r/R) and 1=Σ_KΦ(k/K). Interchanging the finite sums gives exactly Σ_{R,K}B_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;U;R,K). Since the sum includes every factorization rk=q with its sign μ(r), it is sibling-complete. The final scope sentence follows logically: equality of a negative total with a signed sum does not force a specified summand to be negative or large.

glossary.B_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;U): the sibling-complete coarse dyadic block defined in the statement
glossary.B_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;U;R,K): the refined sibling block with r and k scales
glossary.D_*: the smooth divisor cutoff from fact 2827630745a3225b
glossary.J_x: the explicit label count ceil(log_2 x)+4
glossary.N: the sufficiently large bad even integer 2x
glossary.U: the dyadic scale of the unexpanded reflected integer q
glossary.W: the nonzero nonnegative smooth source weight

0895975a7f3918e9.title: EXACT SIGNED \(J_qJ_n\) DISPERSION KERNEL AND POINTWISE-WEIL NO-FIT. Retain the strict-top source, cutoffs
0895975a7f3918e9.author: slava chan
0895975a7f3918e9.statement:
EXACT SIGNED \(J_qJ_n\) DISPERSION KERNEL AND POINTWISE-WEIL NO-FIT. Retain the strict-top source, cutoffs
\[
 {1\over2}Q^{1/12}\le V_q,V_n\le Q^{1/12},
\]
and literal signed frequency block of facts a21645b0ae152b3f and 2b5e86cdf81bb711. For \(Q_0<q\le Q_1\) define the exact q-Type-II coefficient
\[
 \alpha_J(q)=
 \sum_{\substack{d\mid q\\V_q<d\le Q_1/V_q\\
                  q/d>\max\{V_q,Q_0/d\}}}
 b_{V_q}(d)\mu(q/d),                                      \tag{1}
\]
and for \(B_0<n\le B_1\) define
\[
 \gamma_J(n)=
 \sum_{\substack{e\mid n\\V_n<e\le B_1/V_n\\
                  n/e>\max\{V_n,B_0/e\}}}
 b_{V_n}(e)\mu(n/e).                                      \tag{2}
\]
Then
\[
 |\alpha_J(q)|\le2\tau_3(q),\qquad
 |\gamma_J(n)|\le2\tau_3(n),                              \tag{3}
\]
and the exact remaining DOUBLE-VAUGHAN-QN term is
\[
 {\cal J}_{q,V_q}{\cal J}_{n,V_n}\Phi_F
 =
 {1\over H_P}\sum_{F\le|h|<2F}T_h,                        \tag{4}
\]
where, with \(a_h=\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\),
\[
 T_h=
 \sum_{\substack{q\asymp Q,\ n\asymp B\\
                  (g,qn)=(q,n)=1}}
 \alpha_J(q)\gamma_J(n)
 {\cal C}^{\flat}_{g,q,n}(h)e_n(a_h\overline q).           \tag{5}
\]
Thus both long Möbius signs are present in (5) before any Cauchy inequality or absolute value.

Cauchy in the complete n-Type-II coordinate gives the exact signed q-pair dispersion inequality
\[
 |T_h|^2
 \ll BQ^{o(1)}
 \left({\cal D}_h+{\cal O}_h\right),                       \tag{6}
\]
where
\[
 {\cal D}_h\ll_A BQ^{1+o(1)}
 (\log x)^{2C}(1+F/H_P)^{-2A},                            \tag{7}
\]
and the off-diagonal is the real signed sum
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 {\cal O}_h
 =\sum_{\substack{q_1,q_2\asymp Q,\ q_1\ne q_2\\
                   (g,q_1q_2)=1}}
 &\alpha_J(q_1)\overline{\alpha_J(q_2)}
 \sum_{\substack{n\asymp B\\(n,gq_1q_2)=1}}
 {\cal C}^{\flat}_{g,q_1,n}(h)
 \overline{{\cal C}^{\flat}_{g,q_2,n}(h)}\\
 &\times
 e_n\!\left(a_h(\overline{q_1}-\overline{q_2})\right).
                                                               \tag{8}
 \end{aligned}
\]
For each off-diagonal pair, the kernel has the exact reciprocity form
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 e_n\!\left(a_h(\overline{q_1}-\overline{q_2})\right)
 =
 e\!\left({a_h(q_2-q_1)\over nq_1q_2}\right)
 e_{q_1q_2}\!\left(-a_h(q_2-q_1)\overline n\right).
 \quad}                                                       \tag{9}
\]
The ordinary factor in (9), together with the two literal source coefficients, has uniformly bounded n-variation with arbitrary-order \((1+F/H_P)^{-A}\) decay.

Even grant the favorable hypothesis
\[
 (a_h(q_2-q_1),q_1q_2)=1                                   \tag{10}
\]
for every supported off-diagonal pair. If one bounds each n-kernel in (8) separately by the incomplete reciprocal Weil estimate and then sums \(q_1,q_2\) absolutely, one obtains only
\[
 |T_h|
 \ll_A(\log x)^C(1+F/H_P)^{-A}Q^{o(1)}
 \left(BQ^{1/2}+B^{1/2}Q^{3/2}\right).                     \tag{11}
\]
After the \(H_P^{-1}\) normalized frequency sum, the second term has Q-exponent
\[
 {3\over2}+{\beta\over2}>2\qquad(\beta>1).                 \tag{12}
\]
Thus pointwise off-diagonal Weil followed by absolute q-pair summation does not furnish a fixed-power bound \(Q^{2-\delta}\) anywhere in the strict-top band, even under the unit-numerator grant (10). This is a right-hand-side no-fit, not a lower bound.

The exact remaining source-specific supplier is a signed estimate for (8). Fix
\[
 0<\delta<1/4.                                             \tag{13}
\]
A uniform bound
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 |{\cal O}_h|
 \ll_A(\log x)^{2C}(1+F/H_P)^{-2A}
 Q^{\,4-\beta-2\delta-o(1)}
 \quad}                                                       \tag{SIGNED-QPAIR-DISP}
\]
together with (6)-(7) implies
\[
 H_P^{-1}\sum_{F\le|h|<2F}|T_h|\ll Q^{2-\delta+o(1)}.
\]
Relative to the favorable pointwise-Weil envelope \(|{\cal O}_h|\ll Q^{3+o(1)}\), SIGNED-QPAIR-DISP requires a genuine signed q-pair gain of
\[
 Q^{\beta-1+2\delta}.                                      \tag{14}
\]
No such signed estimate, no \(J_qJ_n\) payment, no critical \(\beta\ge6/5\) result, and no post-A or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
0895975a7f3918e9.proof:
Regroup the exact formula (9) of fact a75ea6a8a40dd1f8 by the products \(q=dm\) and \(n=e\ell\). The coefficient of a fixed q is exactly (1), and the coefficient of a fixed n is exactly (2). Since \(|b_V(d)|\le2\tau(d)\),
\[
 |\alpha_J(q)|\le2\sum_{d\mid q}\tau(d)=2\tau_3(q),
\]
and the same proof gives the second inequality in (3). Finite regrouping proves (4)-(5). In particular the factors \(\mu(q/d)\) and \(\mu(n/e)\) in (1)-(2) are the literal long signs \(\mu(m)\) and \(\mu(\ell)\) of the unregrouped formula.

We record a self-contained second-moment bound. For a prime power \(p^k\), \(\tau_3(p^k)\) counts weak compositions of k into three parts. A pair of such compositions can be injected into weak compositions of k into nine parts: choose deterministically, for example by the northwest-corner rule, a nonnegative \(3\) by \(3\) matrix with the first composition as row sums and the second as column sums. The matrix recovers both margin vectors, so the map is injective. Hence
\[
 \tau_3(p^k)^2\le\tau_9(p^k),
\]
and multiplicativity gives \(\tau_3(r)^2\le\tau_9(r)\) for every r. If
\[
 S_j(X)=\#\{(u_1,\ldots,u_j)\in{\mathbb N}^j:u_1\cdots u_j\le X\},
\]
then \(S_1(X)\le X\), and induction using
\[
 S_j(X)=\sum_{u\le X}S_{j-1}(X/u),\qquad
 \sum_{u\le X}{1\over u}\le1+\log X
\]
gives
\[
 S_j(X)\le X(1+\log X)^{j-1}.                              \tag{15}
\]
Since \(\sum_{r\le X}\tau_9(r)=S_9(X)\), equations (3) and (15) prove
\[
 \sum_{q\asymp Q}|\alpha_J(q)|^2\ll Q(1+\log Q)^8,\qquad
 \sum_{n\asymp B}|\gamma_J(n)|^2\ll B(1+\log B)^8.          \tag{16}
\]

Put
\[
 W_h(q,n)={\cal C}^{\flat}_{g,q,n}(h)
 {\bf1}_{(g,qn)=(q,n)=1}.
\]
Cauchy's inequality in n gives
\[
 |T_h|^2
 \le\left(\sum_{n\asymp B}|\gamma_J(n)|^2\right)
 \sum_{n\asymp B}
 \left|\sum_{q\asymp Q}\alpha_J(q)W_h(q,n)
 e_n(a_h\overline q)\right|^2.                              \tag{17}
\]
Use (16) in the first factor and expand the second. The product of the two W_h gates for \(q_1,q_2\) is exactly
\[
 {\bf1}_{(g,q_1q_2)=1}{\bf1}_{(n,gq_1q_2)=1}.              \tag{18}
\]
Thus the terms \(q_1=q_2\) form \({\cal D}_h\), while the ordered terms \(q_1\ne q_2\) give exactly (8), with no gate omitted. Conjugate ordered pairs make \({\cal O}_h\) real. The normalized smooth-coefficient derivative audit in facts 062a7f6f0c58b1f2 and 544c7ba4db45c06f gives
\[
 |W_h(q,n)|\ll_A(\log x)^C(1+F/H_P)^{-A}.
\]
Together with the first estimate in (16), this proves (6)-(7).

For the phase, since n is coprime to \(q_1q_2\),
\[
 \overline{q_1}-\overline{q_2}
 \equiv(q_2-q_1)\overline{q_1q_2}\pmod n.                  \tag{19}
\]
The elementary additive-reciprocity identity used in fact ecd6325d7ef2bc37 says
\[
 e_n(C\overline R)=e(C/(nR))e_R(-C\overline n)
\]
when \((n,R)=1\). Substitute \(C=a_h(q_2-q_1)\), \(R=q_1q_2\) to prove (9).

We also justify the variation assertion. In normalized variables, the size of the ordinary phase on one h-block is
\[
 {|L_{\rm src}|F|q_2-q_1|\over BQ^2}
 \ll {|L_{\rm src}|F\over BQ}\ll F/H_P,                    \tag{20}
\]
using the strict-top source balance already used in facts ecd6325d7ef2bc37 and a21645b0ae152b3f. Every normalized n-derivative costs a fixed power of \(1+F/H_P\). The two literal coefficients have arbitrary-order Fourier decay by fact 062a7f6f0c58b1f2. Choosing that order larger than the derivative cost shows that the product in (8)-(9) has supremum plus total n-variation
\[
 \ll_A(\log x)^{2C}(1+F/H_P)^{-2A}                          \tag{21}
\]
after relabelling \(A\).

Under (10), the incomplete reciprocal estimate reproduced in fact 8138369f26f88aad, with modulus \(q_1q_2\asymp Q^2\) and interval length \(B<Q^2\), bounds each off-diagonal n-kernel by
\[
 \ll_A(\log x)^{2C}(1+F/H_P)^{-2A}Q^{1+o(1)}.              \tag{22}
\]
The gate \((n,g)=1\) is handled after partial summation by the same divisor expansion as in that fact; the outer gate in (18) guarantees that its divisors are units modulo \(q_1q_2\). Its cost is \(Q^{o(1)}\). There are \(O(Q^2)\) ordered q-pairs and (3) is divisor-bounded. Hence
\[
 |{\cal O}_h|
 \ll_A(\log x)^{2C}(1+F/H_P)^{-2A}Q^{3+o(1)}.              \tag{23}
\]
Insert (7) and (23) into (6) and take square roots. This gives (11). The dyadic frequency normalization costs
\[
 {F\over H_P}(1+F/H_P)^{-A},
\]
whose full dyadic sum is bounded for \(A>3\). Since \(B=Q^\beta\), (12) follows.

Finally assume SIGNED-QPAIR-DISP with (13). Its contribution through (6) is
\[
 B^{1/2}Q^{2-\beta/2-\delta+o(1)}=Q^{2-\delta+o(1)}.
\]
The diagonal contribution from (7) is \(BQ^{1/2+o(1)}\). Since
\[
 \delta<1/4<3/10<3/2-\beta
\]
throughout \(\beta<6/5\), this is also \(O(Q^{2-\delta+o(1)})\). Frequency summation proves the conditional consequence. Comparing exponents in (23) and SIGNED-QPAIR-DISP gives the required gain (14). All scope exclusions follow because no estimate for the signed off-diagonal has been supplied.

glossary.SIGNED-QPAIR-DISP: The exact source-specific signed q-pair dispersion estimate sufficient to pay J_qJ_n.
glossary.alpha_J: The regrouped signed q-Type-II coefficient in DOUBLE-VAUGHAN-QN.
glossary.gamma_J: The regrouped signed n-Type-II coefficient in DOUBLE-VAUGHAN-QN.
glossary.mathcal D_h: The q-pair diagonal in the n-side TT* expansion of J_qJ_n.
glossary.mathcal O_h: The signed off-diagonal q-pair kernel in the n-side TT* expansion.

09416be97c36d374.title: EXACT HILBERT-DUAL CROSS-MODULUS VAUGHAN OPERATOR AND THE Q^(7/3-omega) SHORT-SLOT SUPPLIER FOR CEN-MZB
09416be97c36d374.author: slava chan
09416be97c36d374.statement:
EXACT HILBERT-DUAL CROSS-MODULUS VAUGHAN OPERATOR AND THE Q^(7/3-omega) SHORT-SLOT SUPPLIER FOR CEN-MZB.

Assume the actual scales, squarefree moduli, high-conductor cutoff and complete centered projector of facts 050efa07f87f374a, 14fe68fdcbfd99ff and 1d28c0f84d1aad83. Thus B=Q^(4/3+o(1)), Q>8, and
  cal B={b integer:B<=b<2B, b squarefree}.
Put U=Q^(1/3). Let w_n be any actual tensor coefficient from fact 58c03698e1b077c3 after writing alpha_n=mu(n)w_n as in fact b3c1cdc5cb47ae63. For b in cal B define
 T_b(w)
  =sum_{Q<=n<2Q;(n,b)=1}mu(n)w_n P_b(n),                    (1)
where
 P_b(n)
  =sum_{f|b;f>F_0,(f,N)=1}
     c_{b/f}(N)R_{b,f}(n)/phi(b/f).                          (2)

Let gamma=(gamma_b)_{b in cal B} be an arbitrary complex vector satisfying
 sum_{b in cal B}|gamma_b|^2=1,
and define, for every positive integer n,
 P_gamma(n)
  =sum_{b in cal B;(n,b)=1}overline(gamma_b)P_b(n).          (3)
For every positive integer d<=U define the small-small short-slot fibre
 X_d^{ss}(gamma,w)
  =mu(d)sum_{m<=U,l>=1;Q<=ldm<2Q}
          mu(m)w_{ldm}P_gamma(ldm).                          (4)
For every positive integer l<2U define the long-long short-slot fibre
 X_l^{ll}(gamma,w)
  =sum_{U<d<=m;Q<=ldm<2Q}
      kappa(d,m)mu(d)mu(m)w_{ldm}P_gamma(ldm),               (5)
where kappa is the symmetry multiplicity from fact b3c1cdc5cb47ae63. Then exactly
 sum_{b in cal B}overline(gamma_b)T_b(w)
  =-sum_{d<=U}X_d^{ss}(gamma,w)
    +sum_{l<2U}X_l^{ll}(gamma,w).                            (6)

Define
 K_tri(gamma,w)
  =sum_{d<=U}|X_d^{ss}(gamma,w)|^2
    +sum_{l<2U}|X_l^{ll}(gamma,w)|^2.                        (7)
Then
 |sum_{b in cal B}overline(gamma_b)T_b(w)|^2
  <=3U K_tri(gamma,w).                                       (8)

The complete centered energy has the exact Hilbert-dual representation
 E_{>F_0}(alpha)
  =sup_{sum_b|gamma_b|^2=1}
     |sum_b overline(gamma_b)T_b(w)|^2.                      (9)
Consequently, for every fixed omega with 0<omega<1/3, CEN-MZB is equivalent to the dual estimate
 |sum_b overline(gamma_b)T_b(w)|
  <<Q^(4/3-omega/2)                                         (DUAL-CEN)
uniformly for every actual w and every unit vector gamma. A sufficient short-slot supplier is
 K_tri(gamma,w)<<Q^(7/3-omega)                               (TRI-CROSS)
uniformly for the same data; TRI-CROSS implies
 E_{>F_0}(alpha)<<Q^(8/3-omega).                             (10)
