Moreover, the factor occurring after expansion of every fibre square is exactly
 P_gamma(n_1)overline(P_gamma(n_2))
 =sum_{b_1,b_2 in cal B;(n_1,b_1)=(n_2,b_2)=1}
   overline(gamma_{b_1})gamma_{b_2}
   P_{b_1}(n_1)overline(P_{b_2}(n_2)).                       (11)
Thus TRI-CROSS pairs distinct moduli b_1,b_2 before any residue completion. Equations (2) and (11) retain both complete signed conductor/cofactor superpositions, and equations (4)-(5) retain the literal product-coupled values w_{ldm}; no one-variable separation of w is assumed.

No estimate for TRI-CROSS, DUAL-CEN, CEN-MZB, C_small or Goldbach is asserted. In particular, (8) is a sufficient short-slot reduction, not a converse to TRI-CROSS and not permission to complete either b-row separately.
09416be97c36d374.proof:
By formula (3) of fact 14fe68fdcbfd99ff, P_b is the complete signed high-conductor projector in (2). Therefore formula (1) is the b-th row whose squared l2 norm is E_{>F_0}(alpha) for alpha_n=mu(n)w_n.

Apply fact b3c1cdc5cb47ae63 to S_{b,f}(alpha) for every active f in (2), multiply by c_{b/f}(N)/phi(b/f), and sum over the active conductors f. All sums are finite. The small-small part becomes
 sum_{d<=U}mu(d)
  sum_{m<=U,l>=1;Q<=ldm<2Q;(ldm,b)=1}
   mu(m)w_{ldm}P_b(ldm),                                    (12)
because the complete conductor sum of R_{b,f}(ldm) is P_b(ldm). The long-long part becomes
 sum_{l<2U}
  sum_{U<d<=m;Q<=ldm<2Q;(ldm,b)=1}
   kappa(d,m)mu(d)mu(m)w_{ldm}P_b(ldm).                     (13)
The restriction l<2U in (13) follows from the support conclusion in fact b3c1cdc5cb47ae63. That fact gives the sign minus for (12) and plus for (13).

Multiply the resulting identity for T_b(w) by overline(gamma_b), sum over b in cal B, and interchange the finite b,l,d,m sums. Definition (3) absorbs the conditions (ldm,b)=1 and the complete P_b response. The fixed-d terms in (12) are exactly (4), and the fixed-l terms in (13) are exactly (5). This proves (6).

There are floor(U) positive integers d<=U. There are ceil(2U)-1 positive integers l<2U. Their total is strictly less than 3U. Apply Cauchy's inequality to the sum in (6), treating the small-small fibres with scalar sign minus and the long-long fibres with scalar sign plus. If the number of fibres is J, Cauchy gives the left side of (8) at most J K_tri(gamma,w). Since J<3U, this is at most 3U K_tri(gamma,w), including when K_tri(gamma,w)=0. This proves (8).

Let T=(T_b(w))_{b in cal B}. Finite-dimensional Hilbert-space duality gives
 ||T||_2
  =sup_{sum_b|gamma_b|^2=1}
    |sum_b overline(gamma_b)T_b(w)|.                         (14)
By the definition of the energy in facts 050efa07f87f374a and 14fe68fdcbfd99ff,
 ||T||_2^2=E_{>F_0}(alpha).
Squaring (14) proves (9). Taking square roots shows that
 E_{>F_0}(alpha)<<Q^(8/3-omega)
holds if and only if DUAL-CEN holds, with the implied constants changed by a square root or a square. This proves the asserted equivalence.

Assume TRI-CROSS. Thus there is a constant C_omega, uniform in the actual coefficient w and the unit vector gamma, such that
 K_tri(gamma,w)<=C_omega Q^(7/3-omega).                       (15)
Since U=Q^(1/3), equations (8) and (15) give
 |sum_b overline(gamma_b)T_b(w)|^2
 <=3C_omega Q^(8/3-omega).                                  (16)
Take the supremum over gamma in (9). The fixed factor 3C_omega is an admissible implied constant, proving (10).

Finally, expand definition (3) and its complex conjugate. Finite distributivity gives (11). Each P_b in (11) is still the full sum (2), since no conductor expansion, triangle inequality or completion has been applied. Definitions (4)-(5) contain w only as w_{ldm}, so no factorization of that coefficient has been used. This proves the exact cross-modulus and coefficient-retention assertions and all stated scope restrictions.

glossary.K_tri(gamma,w): The sum of the squared magnitudes of all small-small and long-long short-slot fibres.
glossary.P_gamma(n): The Hilbert-dual cross-modulus superposition of the complete projectors P_b(n).
glossary.T_b(w): The complete centered high-conductor row with coefficient mu(n)w_n.
glossary.X_d^{ss}(gamma,w): The small-small Vaughan fibre with the short index d fixed.
glossary.X_l^{ll}(gamma,w): The long-long Vaughan fibre with the genuinely short index l fixed.

09481c959b37db03.title: SHARP FULL-UNIT ZERO-EXTENSION ENVELOPE INFLATION FOR A SPARSE SELECTED-PRIME COFACTOR ROW
09481c959b37db03.author: slava chan
09481c959b37db03.statement:
SHARP FULL-UNIT ZERO-EXTENSION ENVELOPE INFLATION FOR A SPARSE SELECTED-PRIME COFACTOR ROW.

Let p be a prime, let S be a nonempty subset of F_p^* contained in a nonzero additive interval of cardinality R with 1<=R<p, and consider the source-envelope notation of facts a84f95a82329a894 and bbd687d016ee3ff6. Take one pole shift r_0, one nonzero height h_0, one source copy at every t in S, and vectors of norm one. Thus
A_p(r_0,h_0,t)=1 for t in S
and all other A_p(r,h,t) are zero.

Using the actual interval of length R gives
U_p(r_0)=1,qquad Y_{m actual}=R^2.                            (1)
Zero-extend the same row to the full nonzero interval F_p^* and use the full-unit length p-1 in the supplier normalization. Then
U_p^{m full}(r_0)=1,qquad Y_{m full}=(p-1)^2.              (2)
Consequently
Y_{m full}/Y_{m actual}=((p-1)/R)^2,                         (3)
and the corresponding fourth-root trivial baselines, namely
Y_{m full}^{1/2} and Y_{m actual}^{1/2}, have the exact ratio
(p-1)/R.                                                         (4)
Thus zero extension to F_p^* is not envelope-neutral: it pays a factor comparable to p/R at the fourth-root output scale. The configuration above saturates (3)-(4).

Now use the actual first-nonresonant-prime cofactor interval J_p of fact ec8a0fbdab03cda6, and put
R_p=#{t in J_p:p does not divide t}.                             (5)
Whenever this set is nonempty and the exact short-cofactor condition
#J_p<p^delta,qquad 0<delta<1,                                  (6)
holds, full-unit zero extension costs
(p-1)/R_p>=(p-1)/p^delta.                                       (7)
If also p>=Q^zeta for fixed zeta>0, then for every fixed
0<rho<zeta(1-delta)
and all sufficiently large Q, the cost in (7) is at least Q^rho. (8)
In particular, fact ec8a0fbdab03cda6 shows that (6) holds throughout its explicit large-selected-prime subrange p^(1+delta)>3B. Therefore replacing those literal short rows by all of F_p^* destroys a fixed power at the fourth-root envelope scale.

This is a sharp normalization and method no-fit. It is not a lower bound for the literal oscillatory occupancy, does not rule out cancellation from a source-specific Hilbert or common-output representation, and proves no complete top trace or Goldbach estimate.
09481c959b37db03.proof:
For the actual interval, the definition in fact a84f95a82329a894 gives
A_p(r_0,h_0,t)=1
on S. There is only one height, so
U_p(r_0)=sum_h max_{t in S}A_p(r_0,h,t)=1.
There are no other pole shifts. The same fact defines the trivial scale by
Y=L^2 sum_r U_p(r)^2.
With L=R this is Y_actual=R^2, proving (1).

Extend A_p by zero from S to F_p^*. The maximum over all nonzero t is still one because S is nonempty; hence U_p^full(r_0)=1. The full interval has length p-1, so its scale is
Y_full=(p-1)^2.
This proves (2), and division proves (3).

In facts a84f95a82329a894 and bbd687d016ee3ff6, the trivial exceptional fourth-moment baseline is Y^2 and the completion enters under a fourth root. The fourth root of Y^2 is Y^(1/2). Taking square roots in (3) proves (4). Every displayed equality is attained by the stated unit-norm row, so the comparison is sharp as an envelope calculation.

For the actual specialization, fact ec8a0fbdab03cda6 proves that every supported cofactor belongs to J_p and p does not divide it. Thus the allowable ambient support has cardinality R_p in (5). Under (6),
1<=R_p<=#J_p<p^delta.
Therefore
(p-1)/R_p>(p-1)/p^delta,
which proves (7).

Assume p>=Q^zeta and fix rho<zeta(1-delta). For sufficiently large Q, p>=3 and p-1>=p/2. Hence the right side of (7) is at least
(1/2)p^(1-delta)>=(1/2)Q^(zeta(1-delta))>=Q^rho.
This proves (8). The last implication follows from equation (9) of fact ec8a0fbdab03cda6, which states that p^(1+delta)>3B forces all of J_p to be short. The final scope paragraph distinguishes this exact envelope inflation from any lower bound for the signed or oscillatory literal sum.

glossary.R_p: The number of nonzero cofactor residues in the actual integer interval J_p.
glossary.Y_{actual}: The trivial fourth-moment source-envelope scale computed on the actual cofactor interval.
glossary.Y_{full}: The same source-envelope scale after zero extension to all nonzero residues modulo the selected prime.

09cdaef01a098185.title: ANATOMY-SPECIFIC EFFECTIVE-MODULUS AND NUMERICAL LARGE-SIEVE TRANSFER FOR THE C2, C3 AND C4 TWO-ACTIVE SIBLING FAMILIES. Let J be one of 2,3,4 and adopt the J-prime setting of fact 5ba70b46990216f1. Assume additionally that B/2<=n_lambda<=2B, n_lambda=D_lambda v_lambda, every prime dividing D_lambda is at least Z, and Dcal<=D_lambda<2Dcal. For r|D_lambda with omega(r)<=2 put
09cdaef01a098185.author: slava chan
09cdaef01a098185.statement:
ANATOMY-SPECIFIC EFFECTIVE-MODULUS AND NUMERICAL LARGE-SIEVE TRANSFER FOR THE C2, C3 AND C4 TWO-ACTIVE SIBLING FAMILIES. Let J be one of 2,3,4 and adopt the J-prime setting of fact 5ba70b46990216f1. Assume additionally that B/2<=n_lambda<=2B, n_lambda=D_lambda v_lambda, every prime dividing D_lambda is at least Z, and Dcal<=D_lambda<2Dcal. For r|D_lambda with omega(r)<=2 put
m_lambda,r=v_lambda r.                                             (1)
Then
m_lambda,r<=2B/Z^(J-omega(r)).                                     (2)
The nonzero mode coefficients, after removal of their common sign (-1)^(J-2), have the exact forms
|c_{J,D_lambda}(r)|=m_lambda,r/n_lambda
  if omega(r)=2,                                                   (3)
|c_{J,D_lambda}(p)|
=(m_lambda,p/n_lambda)
 sum_{q|D_lambda, q!=p}q/(q-1),                                   (4)
|c_{J,D_lambda}(1)|
=(m_lambda,1/n_lambda)
 sum_{S subset P_lambda, |S|=2}
 product_{p in S}p/(p-1).                                         (5)
Consequently
m_lambda,r/(2B)
<=|c_{J,D_lambda}(r)|
<=27m_lambda,r/B                                                   (6)
for every nonzero mode and every J in {2,3,4}.

Let B_lambda^{(J)}(rho;z) be the literal anatomy-specific ray-scale coefficient required in fact 5ba70b46990216f1, with no transfer between anatomies, and define
S_lambda,r^{(J)}(z)
=sum_rho B_lambda^{(J)}(rho;z)
 e_{v_lambda r}(A epsilon b[a(D_lambda/r)]^(-1)),                   (7)
E_J(z)=sum_lambda sum_{r|D_lambda, omega(r)<=2}
 |c_{J,D_lambda}(r)||S_lambda,r^{(J)}(z)|^2,                       (8)
V_J(z)=sum_lambda sum_{r|D_lambda, omega(r)<=2}
 m_lambda,r|S_lambda,r^{(J)}(z)|^2.                               (9)
Then
V_J(z)/(2B)<=E_J(z)<=27V_J(z)/B.                                  (10)

Put
M_CMD=BQF+BQ^2F^2/Dcal.                                            (11)
A sufficient anatomy-specific energy supplier for the full two-active sibling row is
E_J(z)<<_epsilon Q^epsilon Z^(J-2)M_CMD||z||_2^2.                 (12)
Equivalently up to absolute constants, its modulus-weighted form is
V_J(z)<<_epsilon Q^epsilon Z^(J-2)B M_CMD||z||_2^2.               (13)
Thus C2 requires a four-mode supplier with no Z allowance, C3 a seven-mode supplier with one factor Z, and C4 the eleven-mode supplier with two factors Z already identified in fact 4a18a6fc30232be9.

Equations (7)-(13) are formulation transfers only. Every C2, C3 and C4 coefficient retains its own terminal sign, source amplitude, masks, gates, heights, convolution or stopping slots and original support. No physical coefficient array is transferred between anatomies, and no C2, C3, C4, canonical moment, or Goldbach estimate is asserted.
09cdaef01a098185.proof:
Put D=D_lambda, v=v_lambda, n=n_lambda and m=vr. Since n=Dv,
m=n/(D/r).                                                        (14)
The complementary divisor D/r has J-omega(r) distinct prime factors, all at least Z. Therefore (14) and n<=2B prove (2).

For omega(r)=2, only the active set S equal to the support of r contributes to equation (4) of fact 5ba70b46990216f1. There are J-2 inactive factors -1/p. Removing the common sign gives
|c_{J,D}(r)|
=product_{p|D/r}1/p
=r/D
=vr/(Dv)
=m/n,
which is (3).

Let r=p be prime. The active set is {p,q}, where q runs over the other J-1 primes. After removing the common sign, the q-term is
[1/(q-1)] product_{t|D/(pq)}1/t
=(p/D)q/(q-1)
=(m/n)q/(q-1).
Summing q proves (4).

For r=1, an active pair S={p,q} contributes
[1/((p-1)(q-1))]product_{t|D/(pq)}1/t
=(1/D)[p/(p-1)][q/(q-1)]
=(m/n)[p/(p-1)][q/(q-1)].
Summing the pairs proves (5).

For every odd prime x,
1<x/(x-1)<=3/2.
The multiplier sums in (4)-(5) contain at most three and six terms respectively because J<=4. Together with B/2<=n<=2B, equations (3)-(5) imply the uniform bounds (6). Multiply (6) by the nonnegative squares in (8) and sum to prove (10).

Fact 5ba70b46990216f1 gives
sum_r|c_{J,D}(r)|
<=(9/4)binom(J,2)Z^(-(J-2)).                                     (15)
Weighted Cauchy therefore yields
|T_lambda^{(J)}(z)|^2
<=(9/4)binom(J,2)Z^(-(J-2))
 sum_r|c_{J,D_lambda}(r)||S_lambda,r^{(J)}(z)|^2.                  (16)
Sum (16) over lambda. If (12) holds, the powers Z^(J-2) and Z^(-(J-2)) cancel, leaving Q^epsilon M_CMD||z||_2^2 with only a J-dependent absolute constant. Thus (12) is sufficient.

Finally (10) shows that (12) and (13) imply one another after multiplying or dividing by B and changing absolute constants. Substituting J=2,3,4 gives powers Z^0,Z^1,Z^2 and mode counts 4,7,11 from fact 5ba70b46990216f1. The proof never identifies any B_lambda^{(J)} belonging to different anatomies, so all coefficient-transfer exclusions remain exact.

glossary.E_J: The anatomy-specific coefficient-weighted reciprocal-slope energy for J rough primes.
glossary.M_CMD: The canonical marked-dilator moment scale BQF+BQ^2F^2/Dcal.

09faa77da8d8b9a0.title: CAN-MED/ROUGH3 CLOSED-INTERVAL DICHOTOMY AND EXACT MOBIUS RESIDUAL. Fix real numbers eta and B with 0<eta<=1/4 and B>2^(1/(4eta)). Put Y_med=B^eta and Z_rough=B^(1/4+eta), and use the convention P^+(1)=1. Let n be a squarefree integer with B<n<=2B. Then n has no positive divisor in the closed interval [Y_med,Z_rough] if and only if there is a unique factorization n=s p_1...p_r such that s is positive and squarefree, s<Y_med, P^+(s)<=Z_rough, 1<=r<=3, and Z_rough<p_1<...<p_r are primes
09faa77da8d8b9a0.author: slava chan
09faa77da8d8b9a0.statement:
CAN-MED/ROUGH3 CLOSED-INTERVAL DICHOTOMY AND EXACT MOBIUS RESIDUAL. Fix real numbers eta and B with 0<eta<=1/4 and B>2^(1/(4eta)). Put Y_med=B^eta and Z_rough=B^(1/4+eta), and use the convention P^+(1)=1. Let n be a squarefree integer with B<n<=2B. Then n has no positive divisor in the closed interval [Y_med,Z_rough] if and only if there is a unique factorization n=s p_1...p_r such that s is positive and squarefree, s<Y_med, P^+(s)<=Z_rough, 1<=r<=3, and Z_rough<p_1<...<p_r are primes.

Consequently, for every complex-valued function F_test on the positive integers, one has the exact finite identity
sum_{B<n<=2B, mu(n) nonzero} mu(n)F_test(n) 1_{no d|n lies in [Y_med,Z_rough]}
= sum_{r=1}^3 (-1)^r sum mu(s)F_test(s p_1...p_r),
where the inner sum on the right is over positive squarefree s and primes p_1<...<p_r satisfying s<Y_med, P^+(s)<=Z_rough< p_1, and B<s p_1...p_r<=2B. Thus no endpoint divisor, ordering multiplicity, or Mobius sign is lost.
09faa77da8d8b9a0.proof:
Because B>1 and 0<eta<=1/4, one has 1<Y_med<B. Also eta<=1/4 gives Y_med^2=B^(2eta)<=B^(1/4+eta)=Z_rough, while B>2^(1/(4eta)) gives Z_rough^4=B^(1+4eta)>2B.

Assume first that n has no divisor in [Y_med,Z_rough]. Let s be the product of all prime divisors of n that are at most Z_rough; this product is well defined because n is squarefree. Every prime divisor p of s is in fact smaller than Y_med: otherwise Y_med<=p<=Z_rough and p itself would be a forbidden divisor of n.

Suppose for contradiction that s>=Y_med. Order the prime divisors of s arbitrarily and let d be the first prefix product that is at least Y_med. The preceding prefix d' is smaller than Y_med, and the last prime p is smaller than Y_med. Hence d=d'p<Y_med^2<=Z_rough. Thus d is a divisor of n lying in [Y_med,Z_rough], a contradiction. Therefore s<Y_med.

Write n=sw. By construction every prime divisor of w is greater than Z_rough. The number w is not 1, because otherwise n=s<Y_med<B<n. If w had at least four prime divisors, then squarefreeness and the strict lower bound on those primes would give n>=w>Z_rough^4>2B, contradicting n<=2B. Thus w is the product of r distinct primes for some 1<=r<=3; ordering them increasingly gives Z_rough<p_1<...<p_r. This proves existence.

Conversely, suppose n=s p_1...p_r has the displayed form. Every divisor of n which contains none of the p_i divides s and is therefore at most s<Y_med. Every divisor which contains some p_i is at least p_i>Z_rough. Hence n has no divisor in the closed interval [Y_med,Z_rough].

The factorization is unique: s must be exactly the product of all prime divisors of n at most Z_rough, and the p_i must be the remaining prime divisors in increasing order.

For the final identity, the equivalence and uniqueness show that each integer on the left occurs exactly once on the right. Since s and the p_i are pairwise coprime and squarefree, multiplicativity gives mu(s p_1...p_r)=mu(s)(-1)^r. Substitution proves the identity term by term, including the closed endpoints and the exact Mobius sign.

glossary.F_test: An arbitrary complex-valued test function on the positive integers.
glossary.Y_med: The real lower endpoint B^eta of the closed forbidden-divisor interval in this fact.
glossary.Z_rough: The real upper endpoint B^(1/4+eta) of the closed forbidden-divisor interval in this fact.

0a2db895d49fe29f.title: TWO-SIDED SMALL-IMBALANCE FIXED-TARGET CORRELATED-ENERGY COROLLARY
0a2db895d49fe29f.author: slava chan
0a2db895d49fe29f.statement:
TWO-SIDED SMALL-IMBALANCE FIXED-TARGET CORRELATED-ENERGY COROLLARY.

Fix integers \(J,C\ge1\), a real number \(\tau>0\), a nonzero integer \(A\), and real scales \(Q,H,S,T\ge1\). Let
\[
 0<G\le Q^{\tau/8}. \tag{1}
\]
For every integer \(q\) with \(Q\le q<2Q\), choose a unit \(V_q\) modulo \(q\). Let \(\nu_h,a_s,b_t\) be complex coefficients supported respectively on
\[
 H\le h<2H,\qquad S\le s<2S,\qquad T\le t<2T,
\]
and satisfying
\[
 |\nu_h|\le\tau_J(h),\qquad
 |a_s|\le\tau_J(s),\qquad
 |b_t|\le\tau_J(t). \tag{2}
\]
Define
\[
 W_q=\sum_{\substack{h,s,t\\(st,q)=1}}
 \nu_ha_sb_t e_q\!\left(AV_qh(st)^{-1}\right). \tag{3}
\]
Assume
\[
 C^{-1}GQH\le ST\le CGQH, \tag{4}
\]
and
\[
 H^2Q^\tau\le S\le\frac{Q^{1-\tau}}{H^2}. \tag{5}
\]
Then, for every \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
 H^{-1}\sum_{Q\le q<2Q}|W_q|
 \ll_{J,C,\tau,\epsilon}(|A|QHST)^\epsilon Q^{2-\tau/8}. \tag{6}
\]
No condition \((A,q)=1\) or \((h,q)=1\) is imposed.
0a2db895d49fe29f.proof:
The proof of fact \(51861749711881ca\) applies after one inspection. Starting from the fixed-target estimate in fact \(73fb9efe1286f7e9\) and substituting \(T\asymp_CGQH/S\), it derives exactly
\[
 G^{3/4}Q^2H^{1/2}S^{-1/4},\quad
 G^{3/4}Q^{7/4}H^{1/2}S^{1/4},\quad
 GQ^2HS^{-1/2},\quad
 GQ^{7/4}H. \tag{7}
\]
The derivation of (7) is valid for every \(G>0\). No reciprocal or negative power of \(G\) occurs.

From (5),
\[
 H^{1/2}S^{-1/4}\le Q^{-\tau/4},\quad
 H^{1/2}S^{1/4}\le Q^{(1-\tau)/4},\quad
 HS^{-1/2}\le Q^{-\tau/2},
\]
and the simultaneous inequalities imply \(H\le Q^{1/4-\tau/2}\). Using only the upper bound \(G\le Q^{\tau/8}\), the first two terms in (7) are at most
\[
 Q^{2-\tau/4+3\tau/32}=Q^{2-5\tau/32},
\]
and the last two are at most
\[
 Q^{2-\tau/2+\tau/8}=Q^{2-3\tau/8}.
\]
All four are bounded by \(Q^{2-\tau/8}\). Restoring the fixed-target epsilon factor in fact \(73fb9efe1286f7e9\) gives (6). That fact explicitly permits arbitrary common divisors of \(A\) and \(q\), the unit twist \(V_q\), and unrestricted \(h\)-gcd, proving the final sentence.

glossary.G: A positive product imbalance that may be smaller or larger than one.

0a39d6be778e7dc9.title: LARGE OUTER-GCD DELETION FOR EVERY NONZERO POISSON SUBLEAF
0a39d6be778e7dc9.author: slava chan
0a39d6be778e7dc9.statement:
LARGE OUTER-GCD DELETION FOR EVERY NONZERO POISSON SUBLEAF.

Fix positive constants c_0,C_0,c_1,C_1 and a fixed scaled-smooth compactly supported weight W as in fact df9748efe29ab475. Let x>=3, let c_0x<=N<=C_0x be an integer, and let D,M,R,K satisfy c_1x<=DM,RK<=C_1x. Write g=gcd(d,r), d=ga, r=gb, and L=N/g. For every admissible g,a,b define

F_{g,a,b}(t)=log(t)log((L-at)/b)
 W(ga/D,t/M,gb/R,(L-at)/(bK)),
extended by zero outside its compact positive support, and define
  lambda_{g,a,b,h}=mu(ga)mu(gb)b^(-1)Fhat_{g,a,b}(h/b)
for every nonzero integer h, with the Fourier convention of fact d8ba46800ba433c2.

Let Lambda_* be any restriction of this nonzero-frequency coefficient array obtained only by deleting indices. It may in particular impose a one-rough factorization b=vp, dyadic prime and small-factor cells, a frozen parent label, coprimality conditions already present in the source, and any other zero-one source mask. Then for every real G>=1,

sum_{(g,a,b,h) in Lambda_*, g>G}|lambda_{g,a,b,h}|
 <<_{W,c_i} DR G^(-1)(log x)^2.                              (1)

Consequently assume additionally that
  c_2 x^(1/2)<=D<=C_2 x^(1/2)
for fixed positive c_2,C_2, and put H_0=R/D. For every eta>0, the complete part of any nonzero Poisson subleaf with
  g>max(1,H_0 x^eta)                                       (2)
has absolute coefficient mass
  <<x^(1-eta)(log x)^2.                                    (3)
Since every source phase has modulus one, (3) also bounds the absolute value of that large-g subleaf. This pays the large outer common-gcd sector before any PMD square. It does not estimate the remaining g<=H_0x^eta layers or the centered PMD incidence there.
0a39d6be778e7dc9.proof:
Scaled smoothness and compact support give, for every fixed integer J>=2,

|Fhat_{g,a,b}(h/b)|
 <<_{J,W}M(log x)^2(1+|h|M/b)^(-J).                        (4)

Indeed F_{g,a,b} is supported on an interval of length O(M); after t is rescaled by M, every derivative is O_W((log x)^2), because all four arguments of W remain in one fixed compact set and DM,RK are comparable to x. Repeated integration by parts proves (4).

For every delta>0 and J>1,
  sum_{h nonzero}(1+|h|delta)^(-J)<<_J delta^(-1).
Using delta=M/b in (4) and multiplying by b^(-1) gives

sum_{h nonzero}b^(-1)|Fhat_{g,a,b}(h/b)|<<_W(log x)^2.      (5)

At a fixed outer gcd g, scaled support allows O(D/g) values of a and O(R/g) values of b. Therefore the complete coefficient mass at that g is
  <<DR g^(-2)(log x)^2.                                    (6)
Deleting indices cannot increase this nonnegative majorant. Summing (6) over divisors g of N with g>G, and then enlarging to all integers g>G, gives
  <<DR(log x)^2 sum_{g>G}g^(-2)
  <<DRG^(-1)(log x)^2,
which proves (1).

For (3), if G=H_0x^eta=(R/D)x^eta is at least one, then
  DR/G=D^2x^(-eta)<<x^(1-eta)
by the balanced hypothesis on D. If H_0x^eta<1, condition (2) is g>1 and (1) with G=1 gives DR; but H_0<R^? More directly H_0x^eta<1 means R<Dx^(-eta), so DR<D^2x^(-eta)<<x^(1-eta). Thus (3) holds in both cases. Finally every omitted factor multiplying lambda in the literal Poisson sum is either its unit-modulus additive phase or a deletion mask, so the triangle inequality turns the coefficient-mass bound into the same bound for the subleaf itself.

glossary.H_0: The physical high-divisor ratio R/D, equal to x^(rho-1/2) in the balanced Goldbach scale.
glossary.Lambda_*: An arbitrary deletion restriction of the literal nonzero Poisson coefficient array, including a one-rough frozen-parent leaf.

0a7dc0c20f026253.title: CORRECTED MODULAR-INVERSE WINDOW COMPLETION AND EXACT SAME-WINDOW/CROSS-WINDOW TT-STAR
0a7dc0c20f026253.author: slava chan
0a7dc0c20f026253.statement:
CORRECTED MODULAR-INVERSE WINDOW COMPLETION AND EXACT SAME-WINDOW/CROSS-WINDOW TT-STAR.

Fix Q>=8, H>=2, a positive integer n>=QH, and an integer A with gcd(A,n)=1. Let I be a finite set of integers. For every h in I let cal Q_h be a finite set of integers q satisfying
  Q<=q<2Q,  gcd(q,n)=1.                                    (1)
For q in cal Q_h assume that there is a unique integer m_n(q) in [Q,2Q) satisfying
  q m_n(q) congruent A modulo n,                            (2)
and let B_h(q) be a complex coefficient. Extend B_h by zero to every integer q in [Q,2Q) outside cal Q_h.

For a real interval W put
  cal M_W(q)={m in Z:Q<=m<2Q, m-A/q belongs to W},          (3)
and define
  Z_h(W)
   =sum_{Q<=q<2Q,(q,n)=1} B_h(q)
      sum_{m in cal M_W(q)}
       1_{qm congruent A modulo n}
       e(h[A/(nq)-m/n]).                                    (4)
For r modulo n put
  C_{h,W}(r)
   =sum_{Q<=q<2Q,(q,n)=1}
      B_h(q)e(hA/(nq))
      sum_{m in cal M_W(q)}e_n(m(rq-h)).                    (5)
Then exactly
  Z_h(W)=n^(-1)sum_{r modulo n}e_n(-rA)C_{h,W}(r).          (6)

Let W_1,...,W_K be pairwise disjoint real intervals. Put
  E_same
   =sum_{h in I}sum_{j=1}^K|Z_h(W_j)|^2,                   (7)
  E_cross
   =sum_{h in I}sum_{1<=j,t<=K,j not equal t}
       Z_h(W_j)conjugate(Z_h(W_t)).                         (8)
Then E_cross is real and the exact completed TT-star formulas are
  E_same
   =n^(-2)sum_{h in I}sum_j
      sum_{r_1,r_2 modulo n}
       e_n(A(r_2-r_1))
       C_{h,W_j}(r_1)conjugate(C_{h,W_j}(r_2)),             (9)
  E_cross
   =n^(-2)sum_{h in I}sum_{j not equal t}
      sum_{r_1,r_2 modulo n}
       e_n(A(r_2-r_1))
       C_{h,W_j}(r_1)conjugate(C_{h,W_t}(r_2)).             (10)
In particular,
  sum_{h in I}|sum_j Z_h(W_j)|^2=E_same+E_cross.            (11)
No absolute value has been inserted into either completed sector.

Now let cal X be a complete literal source row from fact 3b2d15db39ad0217 with this n, and let J_1,...,J_K be pairwise disjoint real intervals such that the sets
  cal X_j={x in cal X:lambda_x belongs to J_j}              (12)
partition cal X. Put W_j=-nJ_j. For every h define the one common global support
  cal Q_h={q: the recovered source atom
       x_q=(q,m_n(q),[A-qm_n(q)]/n)
       belongs to cal X and satisfies every literal mask},  (13)
and, on this global support, set
  B_h(q)=c_q U_ell(q,h,v,p)chi_ell(v,p,h,q),                (14)
with zero extension elsewhere. Then, for every j,
  x_q belongs to cal X_j
if and only if
  m_n(q)-A/q belongs to W_j.                                (15)
Consequently the moving interval in (3), rather than the support of B_h, selects the j-th piece. Formula (4) is exactly the height-factor-removed literal cluster sum on cal X_j, and every W_j has length at most n/(12H) when every J_j is critical.

The unequal-slope additive Gram in this row and height set is exactly
  E_same+E_cross
   -sum_{h in I}sum_lambda
      |sum_{x in cal X:lambda_x=lambda}
          B_h(q_x)e(h lambda_x)|^2.                         (16)
Thus (9)-(10) are an exact same-window/cross-window completion of the remaining literal TT-star problem, retaining c_q, U_ell, chi_ell, the moving correction A/q, and the equal-slope subtraction.

This is an identity and theorem interface only. The moving inner interval cal M_W(q) depends on q through A/q, and no coefficient or source mask is separated in (5). No estimate for (9) or (10), no PMD closure, and no Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
0a7dc0c20f026253.proof:
Because H>=2 and n>=QH, one has n>=2Q. Thus two integers m_1,m_2 in [Q,2Q) satisfying qm_i congruent A modulo n would obey
  n divides q(m_1-m_2).
Since gcd(q,n)=1, n divides m_1-m_2, while |m_1-m_2|<Q<=n/2. Hence m_1=m_2. This proves the uniqueness used in (2), consistently with fact fddede33d4205fe2.

For every integer u, additive orthogonality gives
  1_{u congruent 0 modulo n}
   =n^(-1)sum_{r modulo n}e_n(ru).                          (17)
Insert (17), with u=qm-A, into (4). The other exponential factor is
  e(h[A/(nq)-m/n])
   =e(hA/(nq))e_n(-hm).                                    (18)
All sums are finite, so interchange them. The factors depending on r outside the m-sum give e_n(-rA), while the remaining m-phase is
  e_n(rqm)e_n(-hm)=e_n(m(rq-h)).
The resulting inner expression is exactly (5), proving (6). Notice that the membership condition m-A/q in W remains inside the q-dependent inner sum; it has not been replaced by a fixed interval.

Apply (6) to W_s and take the complex conjugate of (6) for W_t. Since the conjugate of e_n(-r_2A) is e_n(r_2A), multiplication gives
  Z_h(W_s)conjugate(Z_h(W_t))
   =n^(-2)sum_{r_1,r_2 modulo n}
      e_n(A(r_2-r_1))
      C_{h,W_s}(r_1)conjugate(C_{h,W_t}(r_2)).              (19)
Sum (19) first over h and s=t to obtain (9), and then over h and the ordered pairs s not equal to t to obtain (10). Interchanging s and t conjugates each term in the ordered cross-window sum, so E_cross is real. Expanding the square of sum_j Z_h(W_j) proves (11).

We verify the literal specialization. Fact fddede33d4205fe2 proves that the complete source projection to q is injective, that the recovered atom is the one in (13), and that its exact slope is
  lambda_{x_q}=A/(nq)-m_n(q)/n.                             (20)
It also proves
  lambda_{x_q} belongs to J_j
if and only if
  m_n(q)-A/q belongs to -nJ_j=W_j.                          (21)
The global support (13) is independent of j and retains the complete literal row. Therefore, for fixed j, the unique congruent m surviving in (4) is m_n(q), and the moving condition (3) selects exactly those and only those q for which x_q belongs to cal X_j. The phase in (4) is e(h lambda_{x_q}). Fact a1b0c0ad5a923524 removes only the common height scalar. Fact 3b2d15db39ad0217 identifies the remaining literal coefficient as (14), with every zero-one source mask retained. Thus (4) is exactly the claimed literal cluster sum on cal X_j. The window-length assertion follows by multiplying the critical length 1/(12H) by n.

Finally expand the complete literal row square. Since the cal X_j partition cal X, its ordered pairs split exactly according as their source atoms lie in the same window or in different windows, giving E_same+E_cross by (7)-(11). On the equal-slope subdomain the phase is one, and grouping by the common value lambda gives the nonnegative fibre squares subtracted in (16), exactly as in fact 3b2d15db39ad0217. Removing those fibres leaves the unequal-slope additive Gram. Every condition was imposed by the one global zero extension (13)-(14) or by the inner moving interval, so no coefficient, mask, or equal-slope term was dropped. This proves all identities and scope qualifications.

glossary.C_{h,W}(r): The complete additive Fourier coefficient at residue frequency r for one corrected modular-inverse window.
glossary.E_cross: The ordered sum of literal TT-star products whose two source atoms lie in distinct corrected windows.
glossary.E_same: The sum of literal TT-star products whose two source atoms lie in the same corrected window.
glossary.cal M_W(q): The q-dependent set of dyadic integers m satisfying m-A/q in the real interval W.

0aa36f583d53cb82.title: Let m>=7 be odd, let s belong to {1,-1}, let K be coprime to m, put gamma=2sK^(-1) modulo m, and fix a nonzero residue ell modulo m. Let G be the unit group modulo m^2. There exist multiplicative characters chi and psi of G whose restriction frequencies satisfy
0aa36f583d53cb82.author: slava chan
0aa36f583d53cb82.statement:
Let m>=7 be odd, let s belong to {1,-1}, let K be coprime to m, put gamma=2sK^(-1) modulo m, and fix a nonzero residue ell modulo m. Let G be the unit group modulo m^2. There exist multiplicative characters chi and psi of G whose restriction frequencies satisfy
gamma(r_chi-r_psi)=ell modulo m.                                     (1)
Extend chi and psi to positive integers by setting them equal to zero on integers not coprime to m. The pure digit weight
W_ell(u)=e_m(ell u)                                                   (2)
has mean zero and Fourier transform supported only at ell, with W_hat_ell(ell)=m. Hence the pair chi,psi occurs with nonzero coefficient in the centered shared-digit character expansion of fact 8230d44e6677f45b.

For positive integer intervals S_1,S_2, a nonzero integer Delta, and smooth compactly supported functions f,g on the positive reals, define the formal Bettin--Chandee column main term
Z_{chi,psi}=sum_{n_1 in S_1,n_2 in S_2; gcd(n_1,n_2) divides Delta}
 [gcd(n_1,n_2)/(n_1n_2)] psi(n_1)chi(n_2)
 integral_R f((x+Delta)/n_2)g(x/n_1) dx.                              (3)
This is exactly the explicit main-term functional in fact b1398db2962d7491 for the two column sequences alpha(n_1)=psi(n_1) and beta(n_2)=chi(n_2).

Character orthogonality does not force (3) to vanish for a centered nonzero digit mode. More precisely, with X=m+1, H=X^(1/3), Delta=1, N_1=N_2=2X, and S_1=S_2=[X,2X] intersect Z, there exist nonnegative infinitely differentiable functions f,g supported respectively inside [3X/4,3X/2] and [X,2X], satisfying the Bettin--Chandee smoothness hypotheses for some finite derivative parameter, such that
Z_{chi,psi} is nonzero.                                                (4)
Thus no termwise character-orthogonality cancellation of the centered nonzero digit main term occurs before any assembly across character atoms, conductors, or outer variables. This is only a column-slot main-term audit. By fact a695dcaf05aaa83d, the same full character atom also has nontrivial row-character factors and is not a direct input to the existing Bettin--Chandee corollary. Equation (4) does not rule out cancellation after summing all character atoms of the centered mode or after summing m,r_2,r_3 and the remaining literal selectors.
0aa36f583d53cb82.proof:
The restriction map from the character group of G to the character group of H_0={1+mt modulo m^2:t modulo m} is onto, as proved in fact 8230d44e6677f45b. Take psi to be the trivial character, so r_psi=0, and choose chi with
r_chi=gamma^(-1)ell modulo m.                                        (5)
Then (1) holds. Since ell is nonzero,
sum_{u modulo m}W_ell(u)=0,                                          (6)
while direct additive orthogonality gives
sum_{u modulo m}W_ell(u)e_m(-h u)=m if h=ell modulo m and 0 otherwise. (7)
This proves the centered Fourier assertions. Formula (13) in the proof of fact 8230d44e6677f45b shows that character pairs satisfying (1) have nonzero coefficient for W_ell, proving occurrence of the chosen pair.

It remains to construct f and g. Put
n_1^*=X=m+1,  n_2^*=2X-1=2m+1.                                     (8)
Both numbers lie in [X,2X], both are coprime to m, and
gcd(n_1^*,n_2^*)=gcd(m+1,2m+1)=1.                                  (9)
For every coprime pair (n_1,n_2) in S_1 times S_2 define the affine function
L_{n_1,n_2}(t)=(n_1t+1)/n_2.                                        (10)
If L_{n_1,n_2} is identically equal to L_{n_1^*,n_2^*}, then equality of the constant terms gives n_2=n_2^*, and equality of the linear terms then gives n_1=n_1^*. Therefore, for every other coprime pair, the equation
L_{n_1,n_2}(t)=L_{n_1^*,n_2^*}(t)                                  (11)
has at most one real solution. There are finitely many pairs, so choose
t_0 in (3X/2,8X/5)                                                   (12)
avoiding all of those finitely many solutions. Put
q_0=L_{n_1^*,n_2^*}(t_0)=(Xt_0+1)/(2X-1).                           (13)
For X>=8 and t_0 in (3X/2,8X/5), one has
3X/4<q_0<3X/2.                                                       (14)
The lower bound follows from (Xt_0+1)/(2X-1)>(3X^2/2)/(2X)=3X/4. For the upper bound, Xt_0+1<8X^2/5+1 and 2X-1>X, so q_0<8X/5+1/X<3X/2 is not the correct numerical comparison; instead use 2X-1>=15X/8 for X>=8, which gives q_0<(8X^2/5+1)/(15X/8)<128X/150+8/(15X)<3X/2. Thus (14) holds.

By (11)-(13), the finitely many real numbers L_{n_1,n_2}(t_0) for other coprime pairs are all different from q_0. Continuity and finiteness therefore give open intervals J_g containing t_0 and J_f containing q_0, with closures contained respectively in (X,2X) and (3X/4,3X/2), such that
if t is in J_g and (n_1t+1)/n_2 is in J_f for a coprime pair in S_1 times S_2, then (n_1,n_2)=(n_1^*,n_2^*).                            (15)
Choose nonzero nonnegative infinitely differentiable functions g and f supported in J_g and J_f, respectively, and positive at t_0 and q_0. Their compact supports lie in the displayed dyadic row intervals. After rescaling by M_2=2X and M_1=3X/2 they are smooth profiles supported in (1/2,1), and because they are fixed smooth functions for this construction, their scaled derivatives satisfy the Bettin--Chandee hypotheses for some finite parameter.

If a summand in (3) has nonzero integral, there is a real x such that
x/n_1 is in J_g and (x+1)/n_2 is in J_f.                              (16)
Writing t=x/n_1, condition (16) and (15) force the pair to be (n_1^*,n_2^*). Conversely, for x near n_1^*t_0, both factors in the target integral are positive, so that integral is strictly positive. Since the target gcd is one, (3) reduces to the single value
Z_{chi,psi}=[psi(n_1^*)chi(n_2^*)/(n_1^*n_2^*)]
 integral_R f((x+1)/n_2^*)g(x/n_1^*) dx.                              (17)
Both target integers are units modulo m, so the two character values in (17) have absolute value one. The integral is positive. Therefore (17) is nonzero, proving (4). The final scope statements follow from fact a695dcaf05aaa83d and from the fact that this construction isolates one column-character atom rather than summing the full character expansion.

glossary.W_ell: the pure centered normal-digit Fourier weight u maps to e_m(ell u)
glossary.Z_{chi,psi}: the explicit Bettin--Chandee column main-term functional evaluated on the two column-character sequences chi and psi

0aa454c6baf243c0.title: Let L_0 be a positive integer. For j in {1,2}, let a_j,m_j,k_j,v_j be positive integers, let h_j be a nonzero integer, and let p_{j,1},p_{j,2} be distinct odd primes. Put
0aa454c6baf243c0.author: slava chan
0aa454c6baf243c0.statement:
Let L_0 be a positive integer. For j in {1,2}, let a_j,m_j,k_j,v_j be positive integers, let h_j be a nonzero integer, and let p_{j,1},p_{j,2} be distinct odd primes. Put
G_j=p_{j,1}p_{j,2}, b_j=v_jG_j,
and assume b_j is squarefree, gcd(a_j,b_j)=1, and
a_jm_j+b_jk_j=L_0.                                                (SRC)
These are the normalized arithmetic data of a C2 Poisson incidence: v_j is the small-prime factor and G_j is its two-prime rough factor. Write e_n(x)=exp(2 pi i x/n), with e_1(x)=1.

(A) Let inverses always be taken in the displayed coprime modulus. The exact source phase satisfies
e_{b_j}(L_0h_ja_j^{-1})=e_{b_j}(m_jh_j)
 =e_{v_j}(m_jh_jG_j^{-1})e_{G_j}(m_jh_jv_j^{-1}).             (PH)
Define the centered rough-prime frequency lifts
beta_{j,1}=<m_jh_jv_j^{-1}p_{j,2}^{-1}>_{p_{j,1}},
beta_{j,2}=<m_jh_jv_j^{-1}p_{j,1}^{-1}>_{p_{j,2}},
and
B_j=beta_{j,1}p_{j,2}+beta_{j,2}p_{j,1}.
Then
B_j congruent to m_jh_jv_j^{-1} modulo G_j
and the rough part of (PH) is exactly e_{G_j}(B_j).

(B) Assume the four rough primes are pairwise distinct. Put G=G_1, T=G_2, B=B_1, D=B_2, and
C=BT+GD.                                                           (CAR)
Then pairing the two source phases before absolute values gives the exact identity
e_{b_1}(L_0h_1a_1^{-1})e_{b_2}(L_0h_2a_2^{-1})
=e_{v_1}(m_1h_1G^{-1})e_{v_2}(m_2h_2T^{-1})e_{GT}(C).          (PAIR)
Any original source coefficients multiply both sides unchanged. Thus a canonical four-rough-prime carrier C does exist at the congruence level, while the two small-v phases remain separate.

The primitive additive denominator of e_G(B) is G/gcd(m_1h_1,G), and that of e_T(D) is T/gcd(m_2h_2,T). Hence the four-prime rough phase has full primitive denominator GT exactly when
gcd(m_1h_1,G)=gcd(m_2h_2,T)=1.                                  (FULL)

(C) Additive reciprocity rewrites each source phase as
e_{b_j}(L_0h_ja_j^{-1})
 =exp(2 pi i L_0h_j/(a_jb_j)) e_{a_j}(-L_0h_jb_j^{-1}).        (REC)
Therefore in the reciprocated representation the rough primes occur inside the inverse argument modulo a_j. Recovering (PAIR) from that representation requires retaining the archimedean factor in (REC) and undoing reciprocity; the reciprocal phase alone does not display the four-rough-prime carrier modulus.

(D) The short Poisson window for h_j does not imply the literal short windows for beta_{j,s}. More precisely, let H>=9 and take any four pairwise distinct primes p_{j,s} in [H^2,2H^2). For each j put
beta_{j,1}=(p_{j,1}-1)/2, beta_{j,2}=(p_{j,2}-1)/2,
B_j=G_j-(p_{j,1}+p_{j,2})/2,
and set a_j=v_j=h_j=1 and m_j=B_j. By the Chinese remainder theorem there is a common positive even L_0, arbitrarily large, such that
L_0 congruent to B_j modulo G_j for j=1,2.
Choose it large enough that k_j=(L_0-B_j)/G_j are positive integers. Then (SRC) holds for both incidences, both h_j lie in the smallest nonzero Poisson window, and (FULL) holds.

Nevertheless, for the carrier C in (CAR), the literal centered parity-and-window gate of fact 397f417416c4cb9d fails. Indeed, for the first semiprime,
G/2<B<G,
so the centered recovery gives B_C=B-G=-(p_{1,1}+p_{1,2})/2. The corresponding centered signed coordinate is
z_C=(p_{1,1}-p_{1,2})/2.
The original B and z_C have the same parity, while G is odd, so B_C and z_C have opposite parity. Thus B_C is not congruent to z_C modulo 2. In particular, for the literal windows
I_i={c in Z:0<|c|<=H},
which satisfy the strict shortness hypotheses because the primes lie in [H^2,2H^2) and H>=9, fact 397f417416c4cb9d shows that no four-frequency packet at carrier C exists. The actual source lifts also satisfy
|beta_{j,s}|=(p_{j,s}-1)/2>H.

Consequently the C2xC2 branch has an exact carrier-level map, but it does not automatically feed the literal DCE packet family. Beyond the Q_1/Q_2 collision, orientation, and projective taxes of facts c882223fd3a1511a, c9ed24359b1f5321, and 3845a81c13f5cf81, it requires a new arithmetic theorem forcing (FULL) and forcing the modular lifts beta_{j,s} into the prescribed short windows without centered wrap. This statement neither bounds the C2xC2 source nor implies an equivalence with Goldbach.
0aa454c6baf243c0.proof:
From (SRC), L_0 is congruent to a_jm_j modulo b_j. Multiplying by h_ja_j^{-1} gives
L_0h_ja_j^{-1} congruent to m_jh_j modulo b_j,
which proves the first equality in (PH). Since b_j=v_jG_j is squarefree, gcd(v_j,G_j)=1. The elementary CRT factorization
e_{vG}(x)=e_v(xG^{-1})e_G(xv^{-1})
proves the second equality.

Modulo p_{j,1}, B_j is congruent to beta_{j,1}p_{j,2}, which by definition is congruent to m_jh_jv_j^{-1}. The same argument modulo p_{j,2} and CRT proves the congruence for B_j, hence e_{G_j}(B_j)=e_{G_j}(m_jh_jv_j^{-1}). This proves (A).

For (B), divide (CAR) by GT:
C/(GT)=B/G+D/T.
Exponentiating gives e_{GT}(C)=e_G(B)e_T(D). Insert the two instances of (PH), leaving the v_j factors untouched, to obtain (PAIR). Multiplication by arbitrary coefficients preserves an equality.

For any integers x,n, the rational number x/n in lowest terms has denominator n/gcd(x,n). Since B is congruent to m_1h_1v_1^{-1} modulo G and v_1 is a unit modulo G,
gcd(B,G)=gcd(m_1h_1,G).
This proves the first denominator formula, and the second is identical. Pairwise distinctness makes G,T coprime, so the product phase has full denominator GT exactly under (FULL).

For (C), choose integer inverses A_j of a_j modulo b_j and V_j of b_j modulo a_j. The integer a_jA_j-1 is divisible by b_j; writing it as q_jb_j gives q_jb_j congruent to -1 modulo a_j, hence q_j congruent to -V_j modulo a_j. Therefore
A_j/b_j=1/(a_jb_j)+q_j/a_j
is congruent modulo one to
1/(a_jb_j)-V_j/a_j.
Multiplying by L_0h_j and exponentiating proves (REC). Its second factor has modulus a_j and inverse variable b_j; the rough-modulus factorization in (PH) is not visible unless the exact equality, including its first factor, is reversed.

For (D), each B_j is an integer because the primes are odd, and direct substitution gives
beta_{j,1}p_{j,2}+beta_{j,2}p_{j,1}
=G_j-(p_{j,1}+p_{j,2})/2.
The two moduli G_1,G_2 are coprime. CRT gives an integer residue satisfying both congruences for L_0; adding multiples of the odd product G_1G_2 makes the representative arbitrarily large and alternates its parity, so one can choose it positive, even, and large enough that both k_j are positive. This proves the two common-target source equations.

Each beta_{j,s} is nonzero modulo its prime and the other prime is a unit, so B_j is not divisible by either prime. Thus gcd(B_j,G_j)=1, proving (FULL) because m_j=B_j and h_j=1.

For distinct odd primes at least 5,
B_j>G_j/2
is equivalent to G_j>p_{j,1}+p_{j,2}, which holds because
(p_{j,1}-1)(p_{j,2}-1)>1.
Also B_j<G_j. With C=BT+GD, reducing CT^{-1} modulo G gives B, so its centered representative is B-G. Put
z=beta_{1,1}p_{1,2}-beta_{1,2}p_{1,1}
 =(p_{1,1}-p_{1,2})/2.
The CRT involution in fact 397f417416c4cb9d sends B to z modulo G. Since |z|<G/2, its centered representative z_C is z. The identities
B+z=2beta_{1,1}p_{1,2},
B-z=2beta_{1,2}p_{1,1}
show that B and z have the same parity. Subtracting odd G reverses parity, so B_C=B-G and z_C have opposite parity. The first parity gate therefore fails.

Finally, if |c_i|<=H and r_i is in [H^2,2H^2), then each first-pair sum or difference has absolute value at most 4H^3, while G/2>=H^4/2; and the second-pair difference has the same bound relative to T/2. For H>=9, 4H^3<H^4/2. Thus the strict window hypotheses of fact 397f417416c4cb9d hold. Its equivalence now shows that parity failure excludes every packet in these windows at carrier C. Meanwhile p_{j,s}>=H^2 gives (p_{j,s}-1)/2>H. This completes the counterconfiguration and all scope conclusions.

glossary.B: the first semiprime carrier coordinate B_1
glossary.B_C: the centered first semiprime coordinate recovered from C
glossary.B_j: the semiprime carrier coordinate reconstructed from the two local lifts of source j
glossary.D: the second semiprime carrier coordinate B_2
glossary.I_i: the literal short nonzero frequency window at the i-th rough prime
glossary.L_0: the common normalized fixed target N/g in the two C2 source equations
glossary.SRC: the normalized fixed-target C2 source equation
glossary.a_j: the normalized d-side coefficient of source j
glossary.b_j: the full normalized residual modulus v_jG_j
glossary.beta_{j,s}: the centered local rough-prime lift induced by the source Poisson phase
glossary.h_j: the nonzero Poisson frequency of source j
glossary.p_{j,s}: the s-th rough prime of source j
glossary.v_j: the small-prime factor of the normalized residual modulus in source j
glossary.z_C: the centered signed first-semiprime coordinate recovered from C

0aa821ade9a14b45.title: FORWARD GA-TAIL CENTERED-ACTIVE-FACE COMPLETION AND EXACT LITERAL WEIGHTED-TENSOR INTERFACE
0aa821ade9a14b45.author: slava chan
0aa821ade9a14b45.statement:
FORWARD GA-TAIL CENTERED-ACTIVE-FACE COMPLETION AND EXACT LITERAL WEIGHTED-TENSOR INTERFACE.

Work in one fixed forward-orientation fiber of fact e55b27d39c593164. Fix one exact GA-TAIL-MARK copy \(\lambda\), one signed frequency \(h\ne0\), and write
\[
 n=dv,\qquad d=d_\lambda=d_\star^{\rm tail},\qquad (d,v)=1,
\]
with \(n,d,v\) squarefree except that \(v\in\{1,2\}\) on a \(C_j\)-copy and with the precise \(A\)-copy factorization supplied by that fact. Put \(\mathscr A=N/g\ne0\). Let \(c_\lambda(q,h)\) be the exact coefficient in equation (9) of fact e55b27d39c593164. Since the orientation is forward, define
\[
 b_{\lambda,h}(q)
 =c_\lambda(q,h)e\!\left(-{\mathscr A h\over qn}\right).       \tag{1}
\]
Thus \(b_{\lambda,h}(q)\) contains the literal marker weight, \(\mu(q)\), the dimensionless physical Fourier amplitude, and every target-gcd, fixed-\(U\), high, source, parent, ordering, equality, collision, deletion and provenance mask, but it does not contain the Archimedean reciprocity phase.

Let
\[
 d^{\rm u}_{\lambda,h}
 =\prod_{\substack{p\mid d\\p\nmid \mathscr A h}}p.            \tag{2}
\]
For every prime \(p\mid d^{\rm u}_{\lambda,h}\), define on \(\mathbb F_p\)
\[
 g_{p;\lambda,h}(x)
 =\begin{cases}
 e_p\!\left(\mathscr A h(n/p)^{-1}x^{-1}\right),&x\ne0,\\
 0,&x=0,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 \phi_{p;\lambda,h}(x)=g_{p;\lambda,h}(x)+{1\over p}.             \tag{3}
\]
For a divisor \(r\mid d^{\rm u}_{\lambda,h}\), put
\[
 B_{\lambda,h,r}(q)
 =b_{\lambda,h}(q)
  e_v\!\left(\mathscr A h(qd)^{-1}\right)
  \prod_{\substack{p\mid d^{\rm u}_{\lambda,h}/r}}\left(-{1\over p}\right),  \tag{4}
\]
where \(e_1=1\). Define the exact centered active-face row
\[
 K_{\lambda,h,r}
 =\sum_{\substack{Q\le q<2Q\\(q,n)=1}}
 B_{\lambda,h,r}(q)
 \prod_{p\mid r}\phi_{p;\lambda,h}(q).                            \tag{5}
\]
Then the fixed-frequency literal row of fact e55b27d39c593164 has the exact decomposition
\[
 \sum_{\substack{Q\le q<2Q\\(q,n)=1}}
 c_\lambda(q,h)e_q(-\mathscr Ahn^{-1})
 =
 \sum_{r\mid d^{\rm u}_{\lambda,h}}K_{\lambda,h,r}.             \tag{6}
\]

For nonempty \(r\), let
\[
 \Omega_r=\prod_{p\mid r}\mathbb F_p^\times,
 \qquad
 V_{\lambda,h,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)
 =\prod_{p\mid r}\widehat g_{p;\lambda,h}(\rho_p),
 \qquad
 \chi_{\boldsymbol\rho}(q)=\prod_{p\mid r}e_p(\rho_pq),         \tag{7}
\]
where the normalized Fourier transforms are those of fact df97bf1eba0495be. Put
\[
 W_{\lambda,h,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)
 =\sum_{\substack{Q\le q<2Q\\(q,n)=1}}
 B_{\lambda,h,r}(q)\chi_{\boldsymbol\rho}(q).                    \tag{8}
\]
Then
\[
 K_{\lambda,h,r}
 =\sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r}
 V_{\lambda,h,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)
 W_{\lambda,h,r}(\boldsymbol\rho).                               \tag{9}
\]
Consequently, for any finite family \(\mathcal J_r\) of such rows with a common nonempty active product \(r\), the exact coordinatewise weighted tensor Gram is
\[
 \mathcal G_r^{\rm GA}(j,k)
 =\sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r}
 W_{j,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)\overline{W_{k,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)}
 V_{j,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)\overline{V_{k,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)}.    \tag{10}
\]
If \(W_{j,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)=a_j\) is independent of \(\boldsymbol\rho\) for every row \(j\), then
\[
 \mathcal G_r^{\rm GA}(j,k)
 =a_j\overline{a_k}\,G_r(n_j,h_j;n_k,h_k),                         \tag{11}
\]
and the square-divisor tensor identity of fact df97bf1eba0495be applies; under the interval and length hypotheses of fact d9a096ed4e597b2b its positive majorant has the stated fixed-\(r\) Schur bound. For the literal coefficient (8), however, \(W_{j,r}\) is generally mode-dependent. Fact 7b88f3f21d0836c8 excludes replacing (10) by the scalar bound uniformly for arbitrary mode-dependent transforms.

The nonresonant selector in fact e55b27d39c593164 is pair-dependent:
\[
 \Delta=h_1q_2-h_2q_1,\qquad
 d_\lambda\nmid\mathscr A\Delta.                                \tag{12}
\]
It is not a product of a condition on \((q_1,h_1)\) and a condition on \((q_2,h_2)\). Hence (9)--(10) are an exact completion of the full row before the proper \(\Delta\)-deletion, not by themselves a completion of \(\mathcal M_F^{(\rm NR)}\). A proof of GA-NR-DIL through centered active faces must therefore either recombine the full row moment and subtract the already explicit \(\Delta=0\) and fully resonant sectors, or prove a deletion-aware version of the literal weighted tensor estimate (10), together with the incomplete cross-\(r\) discrepancy left after the complete orthogonality of fact 3fde81ce051bff7b.

This is an exact algebraic and theorem-interface reduction. It proves no weighted tensor bound for (10), no deletion-aware estimate, no GA-NR-DIL estimate, no payment of the good-\(\mathscr W\) tail, no assertion for the reverse orientation, and no Goldbach conclusion.
0aa821ade9a14b45.proof:
By equation (9) of fact e55b27d39c593164 and the forward sign \(\varepsilon_{\rm or}=1\), equation (1) removes exactly the factor \(e(\mathscr Ah/(qn))\) from \(c_\lambda(q,h)\). The reciprocal phase in equation (11) of that fact therefore satisfies
\[
 c_\lambda(q,h)e_q(-\mathscr Ahn^{-1})
 =b_{\lambda,h}(q)
  e\!\left({\mathscr Ah\over qn}\right)e_q(-\mathscr Ahn^{-1}).
\]
For \((q,n)=1\), additive reciprocity gives
\[
 e\!\left({\mathscr Ah\over qn}\right)e_q(-\mathscr Ahn^{-1})
 =e_n(\mathscr Ahq^{-1}).                                          \tag{13}
\]
This is the point at which the Archimedean phase is consumed; it is not present in (4) or (8).

Since \(n=dv\) and \((d,v)=1\), the Chinese remainder theorem gives
\[
 e_n(\mathscr Ahq^{-1})
 =e_d\!\left(\mathscr Ah(qv)^{-1}\right)
  e_v\!\left(\mathscr Ah(qd)^{-1}\right).                       \tag{14}
\]
Because \(d\) is squarefree, its first factor is
\[
 e_d\!\left(\mathscr Ah(qv)^{-1}\right)
 =\prod_{p\mid d}
 e_p\!\left(\mathscr Ah(n/p)^{-1}q^{-1}\right).                 \tag{15}
\]
If \(p\mid(\mathscr Ah,d)\), its factor in (15) equals one on the supported unit \(q\). The remaining primes are exactly those in (2). For each of them, (3) gives on supported \(q\)
\[
 e_p\!\left(\mathscr Ah(n/p)^{-1}q^{-1}\right)
 =g_{p;\lambda,h}(q)
 =\phi_{p;\lambda,h}(q)-{1\over p}.                              \tag{16}
\]
Expanding the product of (16) over all primes dividing \(d^{\rm u}_{\lambda,h}\), and choosing \(r\) to be the set of factors from which the centered term \(\phi\) is taken, gives exactly (4)--(6). No source coefficient or mask is altered.

For \(p\mid r\), the slope in (3) is nonzero by (2). Fact df97bf1eba0495be uses the normalized transform
\[
 \widehat g_{p;\lambda,h}(\rho)
 ={1\over p}\sum_{x\in\mathbb F_p}
 g_{p;\lambda,h}(x)e_p(-\rho x).
\]
The zero mode is \(-1/p\), so Fourier inversion gives
\[
 \phi_{p;\lambda,h}(q)
 =\sum_{\rho\in\mathbb F_p^\times}
 \widehat g_{p;\lambda,h}(\rho)e_p(\rho q).                     \tag{17}
\]
Multiplying (17) over \(p\mid r\), inserting it in (5), and interchanging finite sums proves (7)--(9).

For a family with common \(r\), expanding the coordinate inner product of the vectors
\[
 \bigl(W_{j,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)V_{j,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)\bigr)_
 {\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r}
\]
gives (10). If every \(W_{j,r}\) is the scalar \(a_j\), it factors out of (10), and the remaining sum is exactly the simultaneous tensor Gram \(G_r\) in fact df97bf1eba0495be, proving (11). Fact d9a096ed4e597b2b gives the asserted conditional Schur specialization. Fact 7b88f3f21d0836c8 constructs arbitrary coordinatewise modulations for which the scalar off-slope reciprocal factor fails, so scalar factorization cannot be asserted for general mode-dependent \(W\).

Finally, (12) is the definition of the NR indicator in equation (15) of fact e55b27d39c593164. The integer \(\Delta\) contains one coordinate from each side of the squared row. Therefore its divisibility indicator is a condition on the ordered pair \(((q_1,h_1),(q_2,h_2))\), rather than separate one-row support conditions. Equations (5)--(10), whose coefficients are defined one row at a time, do not absorb that proper deletion. The two legal continuations stated after (12) follow from the exact trichotomy (16) of fact e55b27d39c593164 and from the complete-versus-incomplete distinction in fact 3fde81ce051bff7b. The final scope sentence introduces no further estimate.

glossary.B_{lambda,h,r}(q): The exact forward literal q-coefficient on the centered active face r after the Archimedean reciprocity phase has been consumed.
glossary.G_r^{GA}: The exact source-weighted coordinatewise tensor Gram for forward GA-tail rows sharing active product r.
glossary.K_{lambda,h,r}: One centered active-prime face of a fixed-frequency forward GA-tail row.
glossary.V_{lambda,h,r}: The tensor product of normalized nonzero local inverse-phase Fourier coefficients on the active product r.
glossary.W_{lambda,h,r}: The additive Fourier transform modulo the active product r of the exact literal face coefficient B_{lambda,h,r}.
glossary.d^{u}_{lambda,h}: The product of prime factors of the GA-tail marked dilator d_lambda that do not divide the target-frequency product mathscr A h.

0abb9119d9247de6.title: FIXED-SEMIPRIME COMMON-CELL SOURCE-ENERGY LEDGER
0abb9119d9247de6.author: slava chan
0abb9119d9247de6.statement:
FIXED-SEMIPRIME COMMON-CELL SOURCE-ENERGY LEDGER.

Fix the literal normalized nonzero-Poisson setup of fact d8ba46800ba433c2: a target N comparable to x, fixed dyadic scales D,M,R,K with DM and RK comparable to x, the smooth amplitudes F_{g,a,b}, and
lambda_{g,a,b,h}=mu(ga)mu(gb)b^{-1} Fhat_{g,a,b}(h/b)
for h in Z\{0}. Fix H>=2 and a rough-frequency cutoff Z_0 with 2<=Z_0<=H^2. Let mathcal L be any restriction by zero-one deletion of source indices to C2 labels
z=(g,a,b,h),   b=v p q,
where b is squarefree, p<q are distinct primes in [H^2,2H^2), gcd(a,b)=1, and 0<|h|<Z_0. Write G_z=pq. Let bar m_z be the residue class modulo b_z defined by
a_z bar m_z congruent to N/g_z modulo b_z,
and impose the full-rough-conductor condition
gcd(bar m_z h_z,G_z)=1.                                      (1)
The restriction may retain any inherited dyadic, parent, marker, target, coprimality, or source masks in addition to (1). Put
mathcal G_H={G_z:z in mathcal L},   mathcal L_G={z in mathcal L:G_z=G},
L_G=sum_{z in mathcal L_G}|lambda_z|.                         (2)

For z in mathcal L, choose any representative m_z of bar m_z and define B_z and the one-sided phase as in fact 0d3dbb6b3e7b8abd:
u_z=e_{v_z}(m_z h_z G_z^{-1}) e_{G_z}(B_z)
    =e_{b_z}((N/g_z)h_z a_z^{-1}).                            (3)
Define
eta_z=lambda_z u_z,   gamma_G=sum_{z in mathcal L_G}eta_z,
kappa_G=phi(G)/G.                                             (4)
Thus |eta_z|=|lambda_z|.

(A) Let G,G' in mathcal G_H be coprime, equivalently let their two-prime supports be disjoint. Suppose the retained pair selector on mathcal L_G times mathcal L_{G'} is the Cartesian product of the retained one-sided source selectors; this is the fixed-(G,G') selector occurring in the support-disjoint, short-frequency, empty-J full face of fact 707345f56faff29e. Define the actual source carrier
C_src(z,z')=B_zG'+GB_{z'}.                                    (5)
Then the exact fixed-(G,G') full-face contribution is
F_src(G,G')
 =kappa_G kappa_{G'}
   sum_{z in mathcal L_G}\sum_{z' in mathcal L_{G'}}
   lambda_z lambda_{z'}
   e_{v_z}(m_zh_zG^{-1})e_{v_{z'}}(m_{z'}h_{z'}(G')^{-1})
   e_{GG'}(C_src(z,z'))
 =kappa_G kappa_{G'} gamma_G gamma_{G'}.                       (6)
Consequently the source-label matrix in each such fixed support pair has rank at most one; it has rank one if both retained fibre vectors (eta_z)_{z in mathcal L_G} and (eta_{z'})_{z' in mathcal L_{G'}} are nonzero. Formula (6) is not asserted for an additional pair-dependent deletion, for G=G', or for a one-prime-overlap collision block.

The carrier C_src in (5) is actual source data. It is not the auxiliary decoder carrier C_dec of fact dcabcf2f566b5721. In that fact
C_dec=B_dec r_3r_4+r_1r_2D_dec
is generated by an auxiliary primitive-residue quadruple. No equality between C_src and C_dec follows from (6).

(B) Uniformly in G and in every zero-one deletion within the family above,
L_G << DR G^{-1}(log x)^2.                                    (7)
Moreover
sum_{G in mathcal G_H}|gamma_G|^2
 <<D^2R^2 H^{-4}(log x)^4.                                   (8)

All multiplicities in (7)-(8) are as follows. For fixed g and G, smooth support gives O(D/g) choices of a; the condition b=vG in the fixed R-support gives O(R/(gG)) choices of v; the complete retained h-sum at fixed (g,a,vG) costs O((log x)^2); and the sum over g|N costs sum_{g|N}g^{-2}=O(1). The unordered convention p<q makes the prime factorization of G unique. If ordered prime orientations are stored, their multiplicity is at most two and is absorbed in the implied constant. Since D,M,R,K and the prime cell [H^2,2H^2) are fixed, there is no dyadic or cell-counting tax in (7)-(8), and no factor equal to the number of semiprimes G occurs.

More generally, if at most mathfrak T separately labelled dyadic/cell copies satisfying the same D,R upper bounds are aggregated into each gamma_G, then the same proof gives
sum_G|gamma_G|^2
 <<mathfrak T^2D^2R^2H^{-4}(log x)^4.                          (9)
Thus mathfrak T<< (log x)^A costs exactly a replacement of the logarithmic fourth power by 4+2A. The literal single-dyadic, single-cell theorem (8) has mathfrak T=1.

(C) If the deletion masks are h-symmetric, reality of F_{g,a,b} gives
eta_{(g,a,b,-h)}=conjugate(eta_{(g,a,b,h)}).                  (10)
This is conjugacy only: the two retained terms add to twice the real part and need not cancel. Neither (8) nor its proof uses h-pair cancellation.

Estimate (8) is an absolute l1-fibre bound. It does not assert a contraction relative to the coefficient energy sum_z|lambda_z|^2, exact-fibre cancellation, a synthesis over varying (m,C_dec,K), common-cell capture of the total source, cross-cell control, or a Goldbach implication.
0abb9119d9247de6.proof:
Fact 0d3dbb6b3e7b8abd proves (3), including independence from the chosen representative m_z. Its label J_z is empty precisely under (1). For coprime G and G', its paired carrier identity gives
e_{GG'}(C_src(z,z'))=e_G(B_z)e_{G'}(B_{z'}),                  (11)
because
C_src(z,z')/(GG')=B_z/G+B_{z'}/G'.
Multiplying (11) by the two literal small-v phases and by lambda_zlambda_{z'} gives eta_zeta_{z'}.

On the support-disjoint empty-J block, fact 707345f56faff29e defines the full-face coefficient as the product over the four distinct rough primes of 1-1/r. Since the supports are G and G', this coefficient is
product_{r|GG'}(1-1/r)=phi(G)phi(G')/(GG')=kappa_Gkappa_{G'}.
It is constant on mathcal L_G times mathcal L_{G'}. The pair selector in (A) is a Cartesian product, so finite distributivity gives
sum_{z in mathcal L_G}\sum_{z' in mathcal L_{G'}}eta_zeta_{z'}
 =(sum_{z in mathcal L_G}eta_z)(sum_{z' in mathcal L_{G'}}eta_{z'})
 =gamma_Ggamma_{G'}.
This proves (6). The coefficient matrix is the outer product of the two displayed fibre vectors, so its rank is at most one and is one exactly when both vectors are nonzero. An extra mask depending jointly on z,z' need not factor, while G=G' and overlapping supports lie in the collision blocks excluded from the four-distinct-prime full face. These observations prove the exact scope of (A). The definition of C_dec quoted in the statement is the auxiliary construction in dcabcf2f566b5721, whereas (5) uses the actual B_z from (3); no step identifies them.

We prove (7) directly from the literal coefficient normalization. The integration-by-parts estimate in the proof of fact d8ba46800ba433c2 implies, for every fixed supported triple (g,a,b),
sum_{h nonzero}|lambda_{g,a,b,h}|<< (log x)^2.                 (12)
Deleting h-indices only decreases the left side.

Fix G and g. Compact scaled support of the first source coordinate ga/D permits O(D/g) integers a. Compact scaled support of gb/R, with b=vG, places v in an interval of length O(R/(gG)), so its integer count is initially O(1+R/(gG)). If this interval contains a positive integer v, the same compact support relation gb comparable to R gives R/(gG) comparable to v and hence bounded below by a positive constant. The additive 1 is therefore absorbed, and the number of supported v is O(R/(gG)). All squarefreeness, C2, parent, marker, target, coprimality, short-frequency, full-conductor, and other zero-one masks only delete these choices. Combining the a-count, v-count, and (12), and then summing over the necessarily admissible outer gcds g|N, gives
L_G
 <<sum_{g|N}(D/g)(R/(gG))(log x)^2
 =DRG^{-1}(log x)^2 sum_{g|N}g^{-2}
 <<DRG^{-1}(log x)^2,
which proves (7).

Since the fixed-cell family is a restriction of the C2 array, fact d8ba46800ba433c2 also gives
sum_{G in mathcal G_H}L_G=sum_{z in mathcal L}|lambda_z|
 <<DR(log x)^2.                                               (13)
Every G=pq in the cell satisfies G>=H^4. By (4), |gamma_G|<=L_G. Therefore
sum_G|gamma_G|^2
 <=sum_G L_G^2
 <=(max_G L_G)sum_G L_G
 <<(DRH^{-4}(log x)^2)(DR(log x)^2),
which is (8). This argument explains why neither a prime-counting factor nor the number of active semiprimes occurs.

For mathfrak T labelled copies, triangle inequality first gives the fixed-G absolute mass bound mathfrak T times (7), while the total absolute mass is mathfrak T times (13). Repeating the maximum-times-total argument yields (9). This is the complete dyadic/cell copy tax.

Finally F_{g,a,b} is real-valued, so its Fourier transform at -h is the complex conjugate of its transform at h. The Möbius and b^{-1} factors are real. Replacing h by -h also conjugates both additive phases in (3). The empty-J condition is unchanged under h replacing -h. Hence (10) follows whenever the source deletion retains the paired label. The identity says that the pair sum is twice a real part; it supplies no vanishing. All estimates above used absolute values, proving the scope assertions in (C).

glossary.B_dec: The first auxiliary decoder linear form in dcabcf2f566b5721.
glossary.C_dec: The auxiliary decoder carrier generated from sampled primitive-residue coordinates in dcabcf2f566b5721.
glossary.C_src: The actual paired source carrier B_zG'+GB_{z'}.
glossary.D_dec: The second auxiliary decoder linear form in dcabcf2f566b5721.
glossary.F_src(G,G'): The exact fixed-support portion of the support-disjoint full-conductor face.
glossary.L_G: The total absolute literal Poisson coefficient mass in mathcal L_G.
glossary.eta_z: The literal coefficient lambda_z multiplied by u_z.
glossary.gamma_G: The sum of eta_z over retained actual source labels in mathcal L_G.
glossary.mathcal G_H: The set of active actual rough semiprime supports p q with both primes in the fixed common cell.
glossary.mathcal L_G: The retained actual short full-conductor C2 source labels having fixed rough semiprime support G.
glossary.mathfrak T: The number of separately labelled dyadic or prime-cell copies aggregated before the grouped source energy is formed.
glossary.u_z: The complete literal one-sided small-v and rough additive unit phase of source label z.

0ac682c6483c79a8.title: Let q_0>1 be an integer, let A be coprime to q_0, and let Omega be a finite set of ordered pairs (m,n) of integers with gcd(mn,q_0)=1. Let w_{m,n} belong to {0,1}, let L be the number of pairs on which w_{m,n}=1, and assume 1<=L<=q_0. Define F=sum_{(m,n) in Omega} w_{m,n} exp(2 pi i A(mn)^(-1)/q_0), and for k modulo q_0 define widehat w(k)=sum_{(m,n) in Omega}w_{m,n}exp(2 pi i k mn/q_0). Exact completion and the degenerate singleton-by-full-dual application of Milicevic--Qin--Wu arXiv:2511.07550, Theorem 1.1 give, for every epsilon>0,
0ac682c6483c79a8.author: slava chan
0ac682c6483c79a8.statement:
Let q_0>1 be an integer, let A be coprime to q_0, and let Omega be a finite set of ordered pairs (m,n) of integers with gcd(mn,q_0)=1. Let w_{m,n} belong to {0,1}, let L be the number of pairs on which w_{m,n}=1, and assume 1<=L<=q_0. Define F=sum_{(m,n) in Omega} w_{m,n} exp(2 pi i A(mn)^(-1)/q_0), and for k modulo q_0 define widehat w(k)=sum_{(m,n) in Omega}w_{m,n}exp(2 pi i k mn/q_0). Exact completion and the degenerate singleton-by-full-dual application of Milicevic--Qin--Wu arXiv:2511.07550, Theorem 1.1 give, for every epsilon>0,
|F| <<_epsilon q_0^epsilon ||widehat w||_2 (q_0^(1/6)+q_0^(-1/10)+q_0^(-1/64)).
Here ||widehat w||_2 is the ell^2 norm over k modulo q_0. Parseval gives ||widehat w||_2^2=q_0 sum_{s modulo q_0}(sum_{(m,n) in Omega, mn congruent s modulo q_0}w_{m,n})^2, and consequently ||widehat w||_2>=(q_0L)^(1/2). Therefore, for these nonnegative weights with L<=q_0, the numerical right side furnished by this degenerate application is at least q_0^(1/6)L, up to q_0^epsilon, and is larger than the trivial bound |F|<=L. Thus combining this legal full-dual application with the trivial bound yields no fixed-power saving for such a positive outer pair marginal. To obtain a saving after this completion one needs additional information not supplied by Theorem 1.1, such as a different transform preserving two square-root-length variables or signed cancellation in the product-pushforward Fourier coefficients.
0ac682c6483c79a8.proof:
By fact b302e2cd6d611a35,
F=q_0^(-1) sum_{k modulo q_0} S(-k,A;q_0) widehat w(k),
where S is the classical Kloosterman sum. Since A is a unit modulo q_0, changing the Kloosterman summation variable x to Ax gives S(-k,A;q_0)=S(-Ak,1;q_0). With the normalized Kloosterman function K(y;q_0)=q_0^(-1/2)S(y,1;q_0), this becomes
F=q_0^(-1/2) sum_{k modulo q_0} widehat w(k)K(-Ak;q_0).

Represent the residues k modulo q_0 by the integers 1 through q_0, with q_0 representing zero. Apply Milicevic--Qin--Wu arXiv:2511.07550, Theorem 1.1 with its first length M=1, second length N=q_0, first coefficient alpha_1=1, second coefficient beta_k=widehat w(k), and fixed multiplier -A. The theorem's range conditions hold: 1<=q_0*q_0^(1/4), 1^(7/5)q_0<q_0^(3/2), and q_0<=q_0^(5/4). Its displayed bound for the normalized Kloosterman bilinear sum is
q_0^epsilon ||widehat w||_2 q_0^(1/2)(q_0^(1/6)+q_0^(-3/10)q_0^(1/5)+q_0^(-3/16)q_0^(11/64)).
The second and third terms simplify to q_0^(-1/10) and q_0^(-1/64). Multiplying by the outside factor q_0^(-1/2) gives the asserted bound for F.

For Parseval, define g(s)=sum_{(m,n) in Omega, mn congruent s modulo q_0}w_{m,n}. Then widehat w(k)=sum_{s modulo q_0}g(s)exp(2 pi i ks/q_0), so additive Fourier orthogonality gives ||widehat w||_2^2=q_0 sum_s g(s)^2. Since every w_{m,n} is zero or one, every g(s) is a nonnegative integer and sum_s g(s)=L. Hence sum_s g(s)^2>=sum_s g(s)=L, proving ||widehat w||_2>=(q_0L)^(1/2).

The leading numerical right side of the theorem application is q_0^(1/6+epsilon)||widehat w||_2, which is at least q_0^(2/3+epsilon)L^(1/2). Dividing this quantity by L and using L<=q_0 gives a ratio at least q_0^(1/6+epsilon). Thus that furnished bound is weaker than the elementary triangle inequality |F|<=L. Taking the better of the two returns only the trivial bound. This is a statement about this specific degenerate completion-and-Theorem-1.1 route; it does not preclude a different transformation or extra signed structure.

glossary.L: the support size of the pair weight
glossary.Omega: the finite set of ordered unit pairs
glossary.q_0: the fixed modulus, distinct from any matrix coefficient
glossary.widehat w: the additive Fourier transform of the product-residue pushforward of w

0b3642c89b136065.statement:
Fix B≥0, real numbers 1/2<a<b<1, a continuously differentiable real function W supported in [a,b], and a continuously differentiable real function ψ on the positive reals such that ψ(u)=0 for 0<u≤1 and ψ(u)=1 for u≥2. For every even integer N=2x with x sufficiently large, define D_*=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B), Q_N=rad(2N), let 𝔠(N)>0 be any positive real number, and define
r_N(n)=1_{gcd(n,Q_N)=1}∏_{p|n,p∤Q_N}(p-1)/(p-2), b_N(n)=2𝔠(N)r_N(n).
Define the deep comparison tail
E_{b,N}=Σ_{d,m≥1}μ(d)log(m)W(dm/x)ψ(d/D_*)b_N(dm).
Then for every A>0,
E_{b,N}≪_{A,B,W,ψ}𝔠(N)x(log x)^(-A)
uniformly in the even integer N. In particular E_{b,N}=o_{B,W,ψ}(𝔠(N)x).
0b3642c89b136065.proof:
We use the following external theorem (Carella, arXiv:2206.12956, Theorem 2.1(i)): there are absolute constants c,C>0 such that for all sufficiently large Y,
|Σ_{n≤Y}μ(n)|≤CY exp(-c sqrt(log Y)).                                      (1)
Partial summation implies the corresponding estimate, with possibly different constants, for a continuously differentiable weight supported in a fixed subinterval of [1/2,2] and having uniformly bounded supremum and total variation.

Write E_{b,N}=2𝔠(N)Σ_m log(m)r_N(m)I_{N,m}, where
I_{N,m}=Σ_d μ(d)R_{N,m}(d)W(dm/x)ψ(d/D_*),
and R_{N,m} is multiplicative in d with prime-power values
R_{N,m}(p^j)=0 if p|Q_N,
R_{N,m}(p^j)=1 if p∤Q_N and p|m,
and R_{N,m}(p^j)=(p-1)/(p-2) if p∤Q_Nm.
This factorization follows directly from the definition: r_N(dm)=r_N(m)R_{N,m}(d). If r_N(m)=0, both sides vanish; otherwise adjoining a prime already dividing m does not change the product defining r_N, while adjoining a new prime p∤Q_N multiplies it by (p-1)/(p-2).

Let f_{N,m}(d)=μ(d)R_{N,m}(d). Its Dirichlet series has the factorization
Σ_d f_{N,m}(d)d^(-s)=ζ(s)^(-1)A_{N,m}(s).
Indeed, with z=p^(-s), the local factor A_p is (1-z)^(-1) if p|Q_N, is 1 if p∤Q_N and p|m, and is
(1-[(p-1)/(p-2)]z)/(1-z)=1-[1/(p-2)](z+z^2+z^3+...)
if p∤Q_Nm. Let a_{N,m}(h) be the Dirichlet coefficients of A_{N,m}. At σ=3/4, the Euler product for their absolute values gives
Σ_h |a_{N,m}(h)|h^(-3/4)
≤∏_{p|Q_N}(1-p^(-3/4))^(-1)∏_{p∤Q_N}(1+[1/(p-2)]p^(-3/4)/(1-p^(-3/4))).       (2)
The second product is bounded absolutely because its local excess is O(p^(-7/4)). For the first product, list the k distinct prime divisors of Q_N increasingly. The j-th is at least j+1, so the logarithm of the product is O(Σ_{j≤k}j^(-3/4))=O(k^(1/4)). Since the product of the first k positive integers is at most Q_N≤2N, one has k=O(log N/log log N), and therefore the right side of (2) is exp(O((log N)^(1/4)))=N^{o(1)}, uniformly in m and N. The same argument at σ=1 gives
Σ_h |a_{N,m}(h)|/h=N^{o(1)}.                                            (3)

Put X=x/m. The weight in I_{N,m} is supported on aX≤d≤bX. If it is nonzero then d>D_*, hence X>D_*/b. Thus every relevant X satisfies
X≫_{b,B}x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B).                                             (4)
Because f_{N,m}=μ*a_{N,m},
I_{N,m}=Σ_h a_{N,m}(h)Σ_n μ(n)W(hn/X)ψ(hn/D_*).                         (5)
If the derivative of ψ is nonzero on the support of W(hn/X), then hn is simultaneously comparable to D_* and to X, so D_* is comparable to X. Consequently the inner weight in (5), viewed as a function of n at scale X/h, has uniformly bounded supremum and total variation, with constants depending only on W and ψ.

Split (5) at h=X^(1/2). For h≤X^(1/2), (1), partial summation, and X/h≥X^(1/2) give
Σ_n μ(n)W(hn/X)ψ(hn/D_*)≪_{W,ψ}(X/h)exp(-c_1 sqrt(log X))
for an absolute c_1>0. By (3), the total contribution of these h is at most
X exp(-c_1 sqrt(log X))N^{o(1)}.                                        (6)
For h>X^(1/2), the trivial bound for the inner sum is O_{W,ψ}(X/h). Since h^(-1)≤X^(-1/8)h^(-3/4) in this range, (2) gives a contribution at most
X^(7/8)N^{o(1)}.                                                         (7)
By (4), both (6) and (7) are O_{A,B,W,ψ}(X(log x)^(-A)) for every fixed A>0. Hence
I_{N,m}≪_{A,B,W,ψ}(x/m)(log x)^(-A)                                     (8)
uniformly in N and m.

Finally, r_N(m)≤2^{ω(m)}≤τ(m), because (p-1)/(p-2)≤2 for p≥3 and r_N(m)=0 when a prime divisor of m lies in Q_N. The support restriction and ψ imply m≤bx/D_*. Therefore (8) yields
|E_{b,N}|≪𝔠(N)x(log x)^(-A)Σ_{m≤bx/D_*}τ(m)log(m)/m.
Writing τ(m)=Σ_{uv=m}1 shows Σ_{m≤Y}τ(m)/m≤(1+log Y)^2; multiplying by log(m)≤log Y gives a bound O((log Y)^3). Replacing A by A+3 in (8) proves the asserted estimate.

glossary.I_{N,m}: the inner d-sum after fixing m
glossary.W: a continuously differentiable weight supported in [a,b]
glossary.r_N(n): the local-density weight defined in the statement
glossary.ψ: a continuously differentiable cutoff equal to zero up to 1 and one from 2 onward

0d1daae6c3854186.title: EXACT TIGHT FRAME IN THE COMPULSORY-PRIME RECIPROCAL COEFFICIENT
0d1daae6c3854186.author: slava chan
0d1daae6c3854186.statement:
EXACT TIGHT FRAME IN THE COMPULSORY-PRIME RECIPROCAL COEFFICIENT.

Let p be a prime with p>2. For nonzero residues C,a modulo p define
 r_C(a)=e_p(Ca^(-1))+1/(p-1).                               (1)
Then
 1/(p-1)sum_{a modulo p;a nonzero}r_C(a)=0.                 (2)
For nonzero residues C,D modulo p, the exact normalized Gram is
 1/(p-1)sum_{a modulo p;a nonzero}
   r_C(a)overline(r_D(a))
 =p/(p-1){1_{C=D}-1/(p-1)}.                                 (3)

Consequently, for arbitrary complex scalars eta_C,
 1/(p-1)sum_{a modulo p;a nonzero}
  |sum_{C nonzero}eta_C r_C(a)|^2
 =p/(p-1)
   {sum_{C nonzero}|eta_C|^2
    -1/(p-1)|sum_{C nonzero}eta_C|^2}.                      (4)
The constant C-vector is the exact kernel:
 sum_{C nonzero}r_C(a)=0                                    (5)
for every nonzero a. On the subspace sum_C eta_C=0, the squared frame norm in (4) is exactly p/(p-1)sum_C|eta_C|^2.

In the nonzero compulsory rough-prime factorization of fact bab04e002177e282,
 r_{p,pb'}(a)=r_C(a),  C=N(b')^(-1) modulo p.                (6)
Thus complementary factors b' that are distinct modulo p give distinct C-frame indices. Equations (3)-(4) apply directly only when the coefficients eta_C are independent of the averaging variable a. They do not by themselves permit replacing the actual a-dependent shifted-cutoff factor P^{(p)}_{b',>F_0/p}(a) by a scalar coefficient.

No incomplete-interval estimate, vector-valued restriction estimate, ROP estimate, CEN-MZB estimate, C_small estimate or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
0d1daae6c3854186.proof:
Because inversion permutes the p-1 nonzero residues, and C is nonzero,
 sum_{a nonzero}e_p(Ca^(-1))
 =sum_{u nonzero}e_p(Cu)
 =-1.
Adding p-1 copies of 1/(p-1) proves (2).

Put c=1/(p-1). If C=D, expansion gives
 1/(p-1)sum_a|r_C(a)|^2
 =1+c E[e_p(Ca^(-1))]
    +c E[e_p(-Ca^(-1))]+c^2
 =1-c^2,                                                    (7)
where E denotes the normalized average and both exponential averages equal -c.

If C is not equal to D, then C-D, C and -D are all nonzero modulo p. Therefore the same permutation calculation gives
 E[e_p((C-D)a^(-1))]
 =E[e_p(Ca^(-1))]
 =E[e_p(-Da^(-1))]
 =-c.
Expanding the cross product gives
 E[r_C(a)overline(r_D(a))]
 =-c-c^2-c^2+c^2
 =-c-c^2
 =-p/(p-1)^2.                                               (8)
The right side of (3) has diagonal value
 p/(p-1){1-1/(p-1)}
 =p(p-2)/(p-1)^2
 =1-1/(p-1)^2,
which is (7), and offdiagonal value -p/(p-1)^2, which is (8). This proves (3).

Multiply (3) by eta_C overline(eta_D) and sum over all nonzero C,D. Finite distributivity gives
 E|sum_C eta_Cr_C(a)|^2
 =p/(p-1)
   {sum_C|eta_C|^2
    -1/(p-1)sum_{C,D}eta_Coverline(eta_D)}.
The double sum is |sum_Ceta_C|^2, proving (4).

For fixed nonzero a, multiplication by a^(-1) permutes the nonzero C. Hence
 sum_{C nonzero}e_p(Ca^(-1))=-1.
The sum of the p-1 constants 1/(p-1) is one, proving (5). Equation (4) then gives the stated exact norm on the orthogonal complement of the constant vector.

Finally, fact bab04e002177e282 defines
 r_{p,pb'}(a)
  =e_p(N[a b']^(-1))+1/(p-1).
Since a and b' are units modulo p on its nonzero branch,
 [ab']^(-1)=a^(-1)(b')^(-1) modulo p.
Setting C=N(b')^(-1) gives (6). If b'_1 and b'_2 are distinct modulo p, inversion and multiplication by the nonzero N preserve distinctness, so their C indices are distinct. The scalar identity (4) assumes eta_C is fixed while a is averaged; the actual complementary factor in fact bab04e002177e282 is a function of a, so no direct substitution is made. This proves every identity and scope restriction.

glossary.eta_C: A complex scalar coefficient indexed by nonzero C modulo p.
glossary.r_C(a): The centered reciprocal trace e_p(Ca^{-1})+1/(p-1) on nonzero residues modulo p.

0d3dbb6b3e7b8abd.title: Fix the constants, target N, scales D,M,R,K, smooth weight, functions F_{g,a,b}, and literal coefficients lambda_{g,a,b,h} of fact d8ba46800ba433c2. Fix real numbers kappa and eta with
0d3dbb6b3e7b8abd.author: slava chan
0d3dbb6b3e7b8abd.statement:
Fix the constants, target N, scales D,M,R,K, smooth weight, functions F_{g,a,b}, and literal coefficients lambda_{g,a,b,h} of fact d8ba46800ba433c2. Fix real numbers kappa and eta with
0<kappa<1/100, 0<eta<=kappa/10,
and assume
D<=x^(1/2+eta), R<=x^(9/16-kappa).
Put
Z_0=x^(3/4-4eta)/R.
Let mathcal L be any restriction of the nonzero-Poisson coefficient array to indices
z=(g,a,b,h)
in the C2 class
b=v p q,
