where p,q are distinct rough primes at least Z_0, b is squarefree, gcd(a,b)=1, and
0<|h|<Z_0.
Retain the original coefficients and any zero-one deletion masks. For z in mathcal L put
ell_z=|lambda_{g,a,b,h}|, S_z={p,q},
and define
L_abs=sum_z ell_z,
A_r=sum_{z:r in S_z}ell_z.
Write L_z=N/g. Define bar m_z to be the unique residue class modulo b satisfying
a bar m_z congruent to L_z modulo b.
For r in S_z, the assertion r divides bar m_z h means that it divides one, equivalently every, integer representative of that residue class. Put
J_z={r in S_z:r divides bar m_z h}.

(A) Uniformly for every rough prime r at least Z_0,
A_r << DR r^(-1)(log x)^2,
and L_abs<<DR(log x)^2. Consequently the complete repeated-prime collision mass
COL=sum_{z,z' in mathcal L:S_z intersect S_{z'} nonempty}ell_z ell_{z'}
satisfies
COL<=sum_{r>=Z_0}A_r^2
 <<D^2R^2Z_0^(-1)(log x)^4.                                  (1)
Thus (1) pays, by absolute values, all Q_1 and Q_2 ordered-pair blocks.

(B) The label J_z is coefficientwise well defined after Poisson summation. Because |h|<Z_0<=r,
J_z=S_z intersect {r:r divides N/g}.
In particular every r in J_z divides N. Hence
BAD=sum_{z:J_z nonempty}ell_z
 <<DR Z_0^(-1)(log x)^3,
and the mass of all ordered pairs having at least one bad side obeys
BAD_2<=2 BAD L_abs
 <<D^2R^2Z_0^(-1)(log x)^5.                                  (2)
The rough additive phase of z has full primitive denominator G_z=pq exactly when J_z is empty.

(C) Before imposing the short-frequency restriction, let TAIL be the absolute coefficient mass with |h|>=Z_0. For every fixed positive A,
TAIL<<_A DR x^(-A).
The absolute mass of all ordered pairs having at least one long-frequency side satisfies
TAIL_2<=2 TAIL L_abs+TAIL^2<<_A D^2R^2x^(-A),                 (3)
where in the last estimate the arbitrary decay exponent in the preceding TAIL bound is increased if necessary.
Together with the full-face deletion estimate of fact d8ba46800ba433c2, (1)--(3) show that the union of
(i) every Q_1 or Q_2 collision pair,
(ii) every disjoint pair with a nonempty J-label,
(iii) every pair with a long Poisson frequency, and
(iv) the aggregate of the fifteen proper-conductor faces on the remaining good block
has absolute contribution
<<D^2R^2Z_0^(-1)(log x)^5+O_A(D^2R^2x^(-A))
<<x^(31/16-kappa)                                               (4)
for all sufficiently large x.

(D) There is an exact carrier for every ordered pair surviving (i)--(iii), even when its two outer gcds g and g' differ. For z=(g,a,vpq,h), choose any integer representative m_z of bar m_z. Put G_z=pq and define
beta_{z,p}=<m_z h v^(-1)q^(-1)>_p,
beta_{z,q}=<m_z h v^(-1)p^(-1)>_q,
B_z=beta_{z,p}q+beta_{z,q}p,
where inverses and centered representatives are taken in the displayed prime modulus. Then
e_b(L_z h a^(-1))
=e_v(m_z h G_z^(-1))e_{G_z}(B_z).                              (5)
For a disjoint pair z,z', put
C_{z,z'}=B_z G_{z'}+G_z B_{z'}.
Without requiring L_z=L_{z'}, one has the exact paired identity
e_b(L_z h a^(-1))e_{b'}(L_{z'}h'(a')^(-1))
=e_v(m_z h G_z^(-1))
 e_{v'}(m_{z'}h'G_{z'}^(-1))
 e_{G_zG_{z'}}(C_{z,z'}).                                     (6)
All original coefficients multiply (6) unchanged. If J_z=J_{z'}=emptyset, the last phase in (6) has full primitive denominator G_zG_{z'}.

Equations (4)--(6) reduce the actual buffered C2xC2 source, up to a power-small absolute remainder, to full-four-rough-prime carriers with their exact coefficients and small-v phases. They do not prove that the induced beta_{z,p} lie in any prescribed literal DCE windows. Fact 0aa454c6baf243c0 proves only that abstract normalized source equations, short h, and full conductor do not imply such localization; its counterconfiguration is not asserted to satisfy the present dyadic support. Therefore a scale-specific modular-lift localization theorem for the surviving buffered array is the remaining interface. No estimate for that localized carrier block and no Goldbach implication is asserted.
0d3dbb6b3e7b8abd.proof:
For fixed g,a,b, the Fourier decay estimate in the proof of fact d8ba46800ba433c2 gives
sum_{h nonzero}|lambda_{g,a,b,h}|<< (log x)^2.                  (7)
At fixed g the smooth support admits O(D/g) choices of a. If a rough prime r divides b and gb is in the R-dyadic support, then b is a multiple of r in an interval of length O(R/g), so there are
O(R/(gr)+1)
possible b. In the present C2 restriction, b=vrs with the other rough prime s>=Z_0. Since b is comparable to R/g, this nonempty fibre has R/(gr) comparable from below to vs>=Z_0, and the additive 1 is absorbed. Summing (7) over a,b and then over g gives
A_r<<sum_{g|N}(D/g)(R/(gr))(log x)^2
<<DR r^(-1)(log x)^2,
because sum_{g>=1}g^(-2) converges. The L_abs estimate is fact d8ba46800ba433c2.

Every colliding ordered pair is counted by A_r^2 for at least one r in its support intersection. Also each z contributes to exactly two prime fibres, whence
sum_r A_r=2L_abs.
Therefore
COL<=sum_r A_r^2
<=(max_r A_r)sum_r A_r
<<D^2R^2Z_0^(-1)(log x)^4.
By the exact support ledger in facts c9ed24359b1f5321 and 3845a81c13f5cf81, Q_1 and Q_2 consist precisely of these one-prime and equal-support collisions, proving (A).

Since gcd(a,b)=1, the congruence a m congruent to L_z modulo b has one residue class bar m_z. Divisibility of that class by r|b is independent of the representative. Because r>=Z_0>|h|,
r divides bar m_z h if and only if r divides bar m_z.
Reducing the defining congruence modulo r and using that a is a unit modulo r shows that this is equivalent to r dividing L_z=N/g. This proves the displayed formula for J_z and also proves r|N.

A union bound over possible target primes and Part (A) give
BAD<=sum_{r|N,r>=Z_0}A_r
<<DR(log x)^2 sum_{r|N,r>=Z_0}r^(-1).
The number of distinct prime divisors of N is at most log N/log 2. Since N is comparable to x, the last sum is O(Z_0^(-1)log x), proving the bound for BAD. The ordered pair mass with at least one bad side is at most 2 BAD L_abs, proving (2).

The rough part of the source phase will be shown in (5) to be e_{G_z}(B_z), where B_z is congruent to m_z h v^(-1) modulo G_z. Since v is a unit modulo G_z,
gcd(B_z,G_z)=gcd(m_z h,G_z).
Its reduced denominator is consequently G_z exactly when no rough prime lies in J_z. This also proves the final assertion of (B).

For the tail, the repeated integration-by-parts estimate from fact d8ba46800ba433c2 states, for every integer J>=2,
|lambda_{g,a,b,h}|
<<M b^(-1)(log x)^2(1+|h|M/b)^(-J).                            (8)
Summing (8) over |h|>=Z_0 gives, after increasing J if necessary,
<< (log x)^2(1+Z_0M/b)^(-(J-1))
per fixed g,a,b. On support, b<=2R and M is bounded below by a positive constant times x/D. Therefore
Z_0M/b >> x^(7/4-4eta)/(D R^2)
>=x^(1/8+2kappa-5eta).
The last exponent is positive under eta<=kappa/10. Summing over the normalized a,b choices with the convergent g^(-2) weight, and choosing J in terms of A, proves TAIL<<_A DR x^(-A). The long-short and short-long blocks have total mass at most 2 TAIL L_abs, while the long-long block has mass TAIL^2. Increasing the arbitrary decay exponent absorbs the latter and proves (3).

The collision, bad-side, and tail bounds are union bounds, so overlaps only improve the estimate. On the remaining support-disjoint, short-frequency, full-rough-conductor block, fact d8ba46800ba433c2 bounds the aggregate discrepancy from the full conductor face by
<<D^2R^2Z_0^(-1)(log x)^4.
Adding this to (1)--(3) proves the first bound in (4). Furthermore
D^2R^2/Z_0=D^2R^3x^(-3/4+4eta)
<=x^(31/16+6eta-3kappa).
Since eta<=kappa/10, the exponent is at most 31/16-(12/5)kappa. For sufficiently large x, (log x)^5<=x^kappa, yielding (4).

It remains to prove the two-target carrier identity. The definition of bar m_z gives
L_z h a^(-1) congruent to m_z h modulo b.
As b=vG_z is squarefree, the elementary Chinese-remainder factorization gives
e_b(m_z h)
=e_v(m_z h G_z^(-1))e_{G_z}(m_z h v^(-1)).
By the definitions of the two beta lifts, B_z is congruent to m_z h v^(-1) modulo each of p and q, hence modulo G_z. This proves (5), and it also shows that all displayed quantities are independent of the chosen representative m_z.

For a disjoint pair, G_z and G_{z'} are coprime. Directly from the definition of C_{z,z'},
C_{z,z'}/(G_zG_{z'})=B_z/G_z+B_{z'}/G_{z'}.
Exponentiating and inserting the two identities (5) proves (6). This calculation uses each target only in its own first congruence, so it remains valid for g different from g'. When both J-labels are empty, the two rough phases have full coprime denominators G_z and G_{z'}, so their product has full denominator G_zG_{z'}.

The final paragraph is a scope conclusion. The quantitative argument never bounds the centered beta lifts. Fact 0aa454c6baf243c0 supplies an abstract counterconfiguration to deriving localization from source equations, short h, and full conductor alone, but no step here embeds that example into the present dyadic support. Hence the only conclusion about the buffered array is that an additional localization theorem is still required.

glossary.A_r: the total absolute coefficient mass in the fixed rough-prime fibre r
glossary.BAD: the absolute coefficient mass with non-full rough frequency conductor
glossary.BAD_2: the absolute ordered-pair mass having at least one non-full rough frequency conductor
glossary.B_z: the rough semiprime carrier coordinate reconstructed from the two local prime lifts
glossary.COL: the absolute ordered-pair mass of all repeated-rough-prime collisions
glossary.C_{z,z'}: the exact four-rough-prime carrier B_z G_{z'}+G_z B_{z'}
glossary.G_z: the rough semiprime product of the two primes in S_z
glossary.J_z: the set of rough primes at which the phase of z loses primitive conductor
glossary.L_abs: the total absolute coefficient mass on mathcal L
glossary.S_z: the unordered pair of rough primes of z
glossary.TAIL: the absolute coefficient mass of frequencies with absolute value at least Z_0
glossary.TAIL_2: the absolute ordered-pair mass having at least one frequency with absolute value at least Z_0
glossary.bar m_z: the uniquely determined residue class modulo b satisfying a bar m_z congruent to N/g modulo b
glossary.beta_{z,p}: the centered local lift at rough prime p induced by bar m_z h v^{-1}
glossary.ell_z: the absolute value of the literal Poisson coefficient at z
glossary.mathcal L: the literal short-rough-C2 nonzero-Poisson coefficient index set

0d53c27d174b26ed.title: FULL-FREQUENCY CELL-\(G\) COVERAGE FOR THE LITERAL NORMALIZED \(A/B/C_1/C_2/C_3\) LEAVES AND THE NONUNIT-\(A\) RESIDUAL GAP
0d53c27d174b26ed.author: slava chan
0d53c27d174b26ed.statement:
FULL-FREQUENCY CELL-\(G\) COVERAGE FOR THE LITERAL NORMALIZED \(A/B/C_1/C_2/C_3\) LEAVES AND THE NONUNIT-\(A\) RESIDUAL GAP.

Fix \(0<\kappa\le1/100\), put \(\sigma=\kappa/100\), and work on one forward forced-high frozen layer of facts \(a71f777ad842c886\), \(5ced883d5560f772\), and \(7131a06664967733\). Thus
\[
 R>D,\quad D=x^{1/2+o(1)},\quad R>x^{9/16-\kappa_0},
\]
\(g=(d,r)\mid N\), and
\[
 Q=D/g>1,\quad B=R/g=Q^\beta,\quad
 1\le\beta\le6/5-2\kappa,
\]
\[
 G_*=M/Q,\quad H_T=B/Q,\quad H_P=B/M=H_T/G_*,
 \quad DM=gG_*Q^2\asymp x.                                  \tag{1}
\]
The fixed target is \(L_0=N/g\). Every occurrence of a literal leaf below includes all nonzero Poisson frequencies, the factor \(b^{-1}\widehat F_{g,a,b}(h/b)\), both logarithmic source weights, every smooth/dyadic/fixed-\(U\) source mask, the high-label mask, and the frozen parent.

Define, for a selected factor scale \(S=Q^s\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \Gamma_{\rm cell}(\beta,s)=\max\bigg(&0,
 \frac{2\beta-2-s}{3},
 \frac{2\beta+s-3}{3},\\
 &\beta-1-\frac s2,\ \beta-\frac54\bigg).                  \tag{2}
 \end{aligned}
\]
For every fixed \(\omega>0\), a separated marker block with total factor product \(ST\asymp B\) is power-saving relative to \(x\) whenever
\[
 G_*\ge Q^{\Gamma_{\rm cell}(\beta,s)+\omega}.               \tag{3}
\]
If
\[
 2\beta-2+\tau\le s\le3-2\beta-\tau                         \tag{4}
\]
for fixed \(\tau>0\), then every \(G_*\ge1\) is covered.

Assume \(G_*\ge1\).

(i) Every raised-stopping \(B\) leaf is power-saving.

(ii) Every \(C_3\) leaf, including \(\beta\) arbitrarily close to \(6/5-2\kappa\), is power-saving. Thus there is no \(C_3\) gap at the upper low-\(\beta\) edge.

(iii) Every \(C_2\) leaf is power-saving.

(iv) Every \(C_1\) leaf is power-saving.

(v) For an interval-prime \(A\) leaf, put
\[
 \Gamma_A(\beta)=\max\left(0,\frac{\beta-1-\sigma}{2}\right). \tag{5}
\]
If \(L_0\) is a unit modulo every supported reciprocal modulus, the complete \(A\) leaf is power-saving for every \(G_*\ge1\). For arbitrary possibly nonunit \(L_0\), it is power-saving when
\[
 G_*\ge Q^{\Gamma_A(\beta)+\omega}.                           \tag{6}
\]

(vi) With normalized marker height \(S_0=H_T^2Q^{3\sigma}\), the \(C_0\) leaf \(b\le S_0\) is
\[
 O(xQ^{-1/2}/g).                                              \tag{7}
\]

If \(H_P<1\), all aggregate anatomy leaves are power-saving by the fixed-\(g\) Bettin--Chandee estimate in fact \(7131a06664967733\).

After summing \(g\mid N\), all parents and anatomy types, and the polylogarithmically many algebraic and smooth labels, the covered sectors contribute \(O(x^{1-\delta})=o(x/\log x)\). Within the lane \(G_*\ge1\), the only range not covered by the cited facts is
\[
 H_P\ge1,\quad
 1\le G_*<Q^{\Gamma_A(\beta)+\omega},\quad
 (L_0,q)>1\ \text{for at least one supported }q.             \tag{8}
\]
This is a scoped theorem-interface no-fit, not a lower bound or impossibility result. Bounded or nonpositive logarithmic bases \(Q\) are absent on this forced-high low-\(\beta\) band for sufficiently large \(x\). No reverse-orientation, \(\beta\ge4/3\), or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
0d53c27d174b26ed.proof:
We first record the literal full-frequency separation. On the fixed \(g\)-layer, write \(a\asymp Q,b\asymp B\). Fact \(d8ba46800ba433c2\) gives
\[
 \lambda_{g,a,b,h}
 =\mu(ga)\mu(gb)b^{-1}\widehat F_{g,a,b}(h/b)
\]
and, for every integer \(A_1\ge1\),
\[
 |\widehat F_{g,a,b}(h/b)|
 \ll M(\log x)^2(1+|h|/H_P)^{-A_1}.                          \tag{9}
\]
Split \(h\ne0\) into signed blocks \(H\le|h|<2H\) and put \(V=H/H_P\). After rescaling the \(m\)-integral by \(M\), the normalized kernel depends on variables lying in a fixed compact box:
\[
 a/Q,\quad b/B,\quad |h|/H,
\]
and on the already dyadically localized marker factors. Differentiate this kernel any fixed number \(r\) of times in the logarithms of those variables. Differentiating the Fourier phase costs at most \(V^r\); applying (9) with exponent \(A_1+r\) gives
\[
 \|\partial_{\log}^r{\cal K}_H\|_\infty
 \ll_r(\log x)^2(1+V)^{-A_1}.                               \tag{10}
\]
Extend the kernel from its fixed box to a fixed torus and expand it in a Fourier series. Repeated integration by parts more times than the number of variables plus two shows that the sum of the absolute Fourier coefficients is
\[
 {\mathfrak P}_H\ll(\log x)^2(1+V)^{-A_1}.                   \tag{11}
\]
Truncating the Fourier series at polynomial height has error \(O(x^{-100})\); the discarded tail follows from the same derivative bounds. Thus (11) is an explicit projective separation of every literal smooth amplitude. The factor \(M/b\asymp H_P^{-1}\) is the literal Poisson prefactor. The 60-residual high mask and the low-\(\beta\) parent are label scalars by facts \(77d7a3419a07305c\) and \(a71f777ad842c886\), so they do not alter (11).

For a marker block with separated factor scales \(S,T\), apply fact \(f7b5ba9fa0d6cfc8\) with projective norm (11); powers of \(\log x\) are absorbed into \(x^\epsilon\). Its complete all-\(h\) bound is
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 x^\epsilon\big[
 &G_*^{1/4}Q^2H_T^{1/2}S^{-1/4}
 +G_*^{1/4}Q^{7/4}H_T^{1/2}S^{1/4}\\
 &+Q^2H_TS^{-1/2}+Q^{7/4}H_T\big].                           \tag{12}
 \end{aligned}
\]
That fact permits either unrestricted factor variables or the exact additional coprimality condition between them.

Write \(G_*=Q^\gamma\). Divide (12) by \(DM=gG_*Q^2\). The four exponents of \(Q\), apart from \(g^{-1}\), are
\[
 (2\beta-2-s)/4-3\gamma/4,\quad
 (2\beta+s-3)/4-3\gamma/4,
\]
\[
 \beta-1-s/2-\gamma,\quad \beta-5/4-\gamma.                  \tag{13}
\]
Equations (2)-(4) follow.

For \(B\), fact \(e18b670f5d48f500\) gives a stopping factor \(Y\) in
\[
 H_T^2Q^{2\sigma}\le Y\le Q^{1-2\sigma}/H_T^2
\]
and \(UY\asymp QH_T\). Fact \(533acf4056cf5bee\) gives its exact separated coefficient, including \((u,y)=1\). Apply (12) with \(S=Y\).

For \(C_3\), fact \(461b4af4d8047ab5\), Part (D), selects \(S=VP_i\) with
\[
 2\beta-2+4\sigma<\log_QS<3-2\beta-4\sigma.
\]
Fact \(0576f567200d41f1\) supplies the divisor-bounded grouping, smooth separation, and collision payment. Hence (12) proves (ii).

For \(C_2\), Cases 2 and 3 of fact \(3b1bda56ad927c5e\) select
\[
 H_T^2Q^{2\sigma}\le S\le Q^{1-3\sigma}/H_T^2.
\]
Case 1 invokes the separated-outer one-prime mechanism. Equal-prime collisions are paid in that fact.

For \(C_1\), fact \(2ff1c15aef183bac\) selects an \(S\) satisfying (4) on every Type-II and medium/large Type-I block. On a low Type-I block, its grouped coefficient factor \(L'\) and unweighted factor \(M'\) satisfy
\[
 L'\le Q^{1/2-2\sigma},\qquad L'M'\asymp B\le Q^{2-2\sigma}.
\]
Apply fact \(bbcb9f66597c667c\) on each frequency block \(H=VH_P\), restore the literal prefactor by multiplying by \(V\), and use the projective decay (11). The normalized block bound is
\[
 V(1+V)^{-A_1}Q^\epsilon(L'M'+Q^{3/2}L').
\]
Its dyadic sum is \(O(Q^{2-\sigma})\) when \(A_1\ge3\). Prime-power and collision estimates in the cited \(C_1,C_2,C_3\) facts are absolute after their frequency prefactor cancels the number of frequencies; at scale \(H\), restoring \(H_P^{-1}\) again multiplies by \(V\), so (11) makes their full-frequency sums no larger than their stated bounds. This proves (i)-(iv).

For \(A\), the exact interval-prime identity in fact \(7c1f38cfbb8d0569\) writes \(b=up\), and the prime scale \(Y=Q^y\) lies between \(H_TQ^\sigma/2\) and \(Q^{3/2-\beta-3\sigma}\). Apply the jointly coprime version of (12) with \(S=Y\). The four thresholds in (2) are bounded by
\[
 \frac{\beta-1-\sigma}{3}+O(1/\log Q),\quad
 \frac{\beta-3/2-3\sigma}{3},
\]
\[
 \frac{\beta-1-\sigma}{2}+O(1/\log Q),\quad
 \beta-\frac54.
\]
This proves the nonunit assertion (6).

Suppose now that \(L_0\) is a unit on every supported modulus. Fact \(ea623cefa72d3a76\) proves the unit \(A\) estimate on the natural block. To complete frequencies, let \(V_0=Q^{\sigma/4}\). For a block \(H=VH_P\) with \(V\le V_0\), rerun its pointwise proof with support parameter \(2H\). The conditions remain valid:
\[
 2H\le2Q^{\sigma/4}H_T\le H_TQ^\sigma/2\le Y
\]
and
\[
 8HY\le8Q^{\sigma/4}H_TY
 \le8Q^{1/2-11\sigma/4}<Q.
\]
Relative to the two terms in fact \(ea623cefa72d3a76\), restoring \(H_P^{-1}\) and (11) multiplies them by
\[
 V^{1/2}(1+V)^{-A_1},\qquad V(1+V)^{-A_1},
\]
respectively; its \(p\mid u\) diagonal gets \(V(1+V)^{-A_1}\). These dyadic sums are bounded for \(A_1\ge3\).

For \(H>V_0H_P\), apply the absolute-tail estimate of fact \(7131a06664967733\) with \(T=V_0H_P\). It is
\[
 \ll \frac{x}{g}H_PQ^{-(A_1-1)\sigma/4}(\log x)^2.
\]
Since \(H_P\le H_T\le Q^{1/5}\), choose the fixed integer \(A_1\) sufficiently large in terms of \(\sigma\). The tail is then \(O(xQ^{-\delta}/g)\). This proves the complete unit \(A\) assertion.

For \(C_0\), fact \(d8ba46800ba433c2\) gives \(O((\log x)^2)\) complete all-frequency absolute mass per \((a,b)\). There are \(O(QS_0)\) pairs, so
\[
 \ll QS_0(\log x)^2
 =\frac{x}{gG_*}Q^{2\beta-3+3\sigma}(\log x)^2.
\]
Because \(\beta\le6/5-2\kappa\), the exponent is below \(-1/2\), proving (7).

If \(H_P<1\), fact \(7131a06664967733\) applies to the complete leaf. The forced-high hypotheses imply \(\beta>20/19\): otherwise \(Q\le D=x^{1/2+o(1)}\) gives \(H_T\le x^{1/38+o(1)}\), contradicting \(H_T=R/D>x^{1/16-\kappa_0+o(1)}\). Hence
\[
 \beta-1-\frac{19\beta-20}{17}
 =\frac{3-2\beta}{17}\ge3/85,
\]
so \(G_*>H_T\) lies inside its fixed-\(g\) Bettin--Chandee sector with a uniform buffer.

Finally, fact \(5ced883d5560f772\) gives \(Q\ge x^{c_\kappa+o(1)}\). Summing the exact-\(g\) estimates costs \(\sum_{g\mid N}g^{-1}=x^{o(1)}\), and all algebraic labels cost \(x^{o(1)}\). This proves the global covered bound. In (8), the unit theorem is unavailable, and on the smallest \(A\)-prime cell the third exponent in (13) is
\[
 (\beta-1-\sigma)/2-\gamma+O(1/\log Q),
\]
which need not be negative below (6). Thus (8) is the exact remaining theorem-interface gap.

glossary.Gamma_A: The uniform imbalance threshold for a possibly nonunit interval-prime A leaf.
glossary.Gamma_cell: The least Q-exponent of imbalance forced by the four full-frequency CELL-G terms.
glossary.mathfrak P_H: The l1 projective norm of the literal smooth amplitude on a dyadic frequency block H.

0e8ef74ba484418d.title: MIXED SPARSE-SOURCE/DENSE-DENSITY FOUR-ROW PMD BOUND
0e8ef74ba484418d.author: slava chan
0e8ef74ba484418d.statement:
MIXED SPARSE-SOURCE/DENSE-DENSITY FOUR-ROW PMD BOUND.

Fix a constant C_0>=1. Let Q>=2, H>=1, let p>2Q be a prime, let A be an integer not divisible by p, and put
  I_Q={q in Z:Q<=q<2Q}.
For j in {1,2,3,4}, let c_j be one of two types of complex coefficient rows on I_Q:

(U) a sparse row supported on at most C_0Q/H integers and satisfying |c_j(q)|<=C_0;

(Z) a dense-small row satisfying |c_j(q)|<=C_0/H for every q.

For q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4 in I_Q define
  Delta=(q_2-q_1)q_3q_4-(q_4-q_3)q_1q_2,
  rho_12=A(q_2-q_1)(q_1q_2)^(-1) modulo p,
  rho_34=A(q_4-q_3)(q_3q_4)^(-1) modulo p.
Let W be a complex function on Z/pZ satisfying
  |W(r)|<=1 for every r,  sum_rW(r)=0,
and define
  Gamma_W(x,y)=sum_rW(r)[1_{r=x}-1/p][1_{r=y}-1/p],
  M_W(c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4)
   =sum_{q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4 in I_Q; Delta nonzero}
      c_1(q_1)conjugate(c_2(q_2))
      conjugate(c_3(q_3))c_4(q_4)
      Gamma_W(rho_12,rho_34).                               (1)

If all four rows have type (U), then
  |M_W(c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4)|
   <<_{C_0} Q^3/H^3+Q^4/(pH^4).                            (2)
If at least one row has type (Z), then
  |M_W(c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4)|
   <<_{C_0} Q^3/H^4+Q^4/(pH^4).                            (3)
Both estimates retain the full complex physical kernel W and the exact restriction Delta nonzero.

Consequently suppose a nonzero-Poisson row has the exact source--density form a=u-z of fact ace362082848a702 on the coprime q-domain in that fact, the U rows satisfy the actual-source hypotheses of fact 914048233fada05f, and the Z rows satisfy the pointwise type-(Z) bound above. In a dyadic family with
  2<=V<H,  P=QH/V,  p in [P,2P),
and squared (v,s)-mass at most Q^epsilon, assume p>2Q throughout. Then the sum of the fifteen terms in the expansion of fact ace362082848a702 which contain at least one Z row is
  <<_{C_0,epsilon}Q^epsilon[P Q^3/H^4+Q^4/H^4].             (4)
The all-U term is bounded by fact 914048233fada05f by
  <<_{C_0,epsilon}Q^epsilon P Q^3/H^3.                      (5)
In particular, if H>=Q^(1/9), the complete sixteen-term source--density expansion is
  <<_{C_0,epsilon}Q^epsilon P Q^(8/3).                      (6)
This consequence is conditional on the literal coefficient family meeting the displayed U/Z hypotheses; it does not assert that an arbitrary separated coefficient row has this form or these bounds.
0e8ef74ba484418d.proof:
Because p>2Q, every q in I_Q is a unit modulo p. Because W has mean zero, direct expansion gives
  Gamma_W(x,y)=1_{x=y}W(x)-[W(x)+W(y)]/p.                   (7)
Consider first the incidence term. Since p does not divide A, the equality rho_12=rho_34 is equivalent to
  q_1^(-1)-q_2^(-1)=q_3^(-1)-q_4^(-1) modulo p.             (8)
After any three of q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4 are fixed, equation (8) determines the inverse of the fourth variable modulo p. The interval I_Q has length Q<p, so reduction modulo p is injective on I_Q; hence there is at most one possible value of the fourth variable in I_Q.

If every row has type (U), choose any variable as the determined fourth variable. There are at most (C_0Q/H)^3 choices for the other three, and the product of coefficient magnitudes is at most C_0^4. Thus the absolute incidence contribution is O_{C_0}(Q^3/H^3).

Suppose at least one row has type (Z), and choose a Z-row variable as the determined fourth variable. If exactly k of the four rows have type (U), then the three free variables have k U supports and 3-k Z supports. Their number is at most
  (C_0Q/H)^k Q^(3-k),
while the product of all four coefficient magnitudes is at most C_0^4H^{-(4-k)}. Their product is O_{C_0}(Q^3/H^4). Deleting the Delta=0 tuples only decreases these absolute incidence majorants.

For either cross term in (7), discard the restriction Delta nonzero. Every U row has l1 norm at most C_0^2Q/H, and every Z row has l1 norm at most C_0Q/H. Hence the absolute value of each cross term is
  <<_{C_0}p^(-1)(Q/H)^4.                                   (9)
Combining the incidence estimates with the two bounds (9) proves (2)-(3).

For the family consequence, there are fifteen mixed terms in the exact expansion of fact ace362082848a702. Sum (3) over at most 2P primes and multiply by the assumed squared (v,s)-mass, absorbing the fixed factor fifteen and divisor losses into Q^epsilon. This gives (4). Fact 914048233fada05f gives (5) for the all-U actual-source term.

Finally H>=Q^(1/9) implies Q^(1/3)<=H^3 and also Q^(1/3)<=H^4. Therefore
  P Q^3/H^3<=P Q^(8/3),
  P Q^3/H^4<=P Q^(8/3).                                   (10)
Since V<H gives P=QH/V>Q,
  Q^4/H^4<=P Q^3/H^4<=P Q^(8/3).                           (11)
Equations (4)-(5) and (10)-(11) prove (6), with epsilon adjusted.

glossary.mixed source--density term: A four-row term containing at least one type-(Z) row.
glossary.type (U): A coefficient row supported on O(Q/H) actual-source positions and bounded pointwise.
glossary.type (Z): A coefficient row supported on the whole Q-interval but bounded pointwise by O(H^{-1}).

0e9a1691fd933c33.title: Fix real numbers 1/2<a<b<1 and a nonnegative continuously differentiable real function W supported in [a,b]. For every even integer N=2x with x≥2, let Q_N=rad(2N), let 𝔠(N)>0 be any positive real number, and define
0e9a1691fd933c33.author: slava chan
0e9a1691fd933c33.statement:
Fix real numbers 1/2<a<b<1 and a nonnegative continuously differentiable real function W supported in [a,b]. For every even integer N=2x with x≥2, let Q_N=rad(2N), let 𝔠(N)>0 be any positive real number, and define
r_N(n)=1_{gcd(n,Q_N)=1}∏_{p|n, p∤Q_N}(p-1)/(p-2)
and
b_N(n)=2𝔠(N)r_N(n)
for positive integers n. Define M_{N,W}=Σ_{n≥1}W(n/x)b_N(n)Λ(n), and c_W=2∫_0^∞W(u)du. Then, as x tends to infinity through values for which N=2x is an even integer,
M_{N,W}=c_W𝔠(N)x+o_W(𝔠(N)x),
with a relative error uniform in N and independent of the size of the positive factor 𝔠(N).
0e9a1691fd933c33.proof:
We use the following external theorem, stated in the introduction of Shao and Teräväinen, arXiv:2006.05954: for every fixed A>0 and ε>0,
Σ_{q≤y^(1/2-ε)} max_{gcd(c,q)=1}|Σ_{n≤y,n≡c (mod q)}Λ(n)-y/φ(q)| ≪_{A,ε} y/(log y)^A.
The q=1 term is nonnegative and is included in this sum, so
Σ_{n≤y}Λ(n)=y+O_{A,ε}(y/(log y)^A).
Partial summation, using that W is continuously differentiable and supported in the fixed compact interval [a,b], gives
Σ_{n≥1}W(n/x)Λ(n)=x∫_0^∞W(u)du+o_W(x).                                                   (1)

We compare the left side of (1) with S_N=Σ_{n≥1}W(n/x)r_N(n)Λ(n). First consider prime arguments n=p in the support. Then ax≤p≤bx, so p>N/4 and p<N/2 because x=N/2, a>1/2, and b<1. We claim p∤Q_N. For p>2, the condition p|Q_N implies p|N. Since N is even and p is odd, N/p is an even positive integer. The inequalities N/4<p<N/2 imply 2<N/p<4, but there is no even integer strictly between 2 and 4. The prime p=2 is outside [ax,bx] for all sufficiently large x. Thus p∤Q_N for every prime in the support when x is sufficiently large, and
r_N(p)=(p-1)/(p-2)=1+1/(p-2).
The total correction on primes is
Σ_p W(p/x)log(p)/(p-2).
For p≥ax and sufficiently large x, 1/(p-2)≤2/(ax). The q=1 consequence of the external theorem also gives Σ_{p≤x}log p≤Σ_{n≤x}Λ(n)=O(x). Hence the prime correction is O_W(1).

It remains to bound prime powers p^e with e≥2. For p≥3 one has (p-1)/(p-2)≤2, while if p|Q_N then r_N(p^e)=0. Consequently 0≤r_N(p^e)≤2. The number of pairs (p,e) with p^e≤x and e≥2 is at most Σ_{e=2}^{floor(log_2 x)}x^(1/e)≤x^(1/2)+(log_2 x)x^(1/3). Each corresponding von-Mangoldt weight is at most log x, so the total prime-power contribution to either S_N or the left side of (1) is O_W(x^(1/2)log x+x^(1/3)(log x)^2)=o_W(x), uniformly in N. Combining this with the prime correction and (1) yields
S_N=x∫_0^∞W(u)du+o_W(x),
where the relative error does not depend on N.

By definition M_{N,W}=2𝔠(N)S_N. Multiplying the last display by the positive number 2𝔠(N) gives
M_{N,W}=2𝔠(N)x∫_0^∞W(u)du+o_W(𝔠(N)x)=c_W𝔠(N)x+o_W(𝔠(N)x).
Since the error before multiplication was uniform in N and 𝔠(N) is merely a common positive factor, the stated uniformity follows.

glossary.M_{N,W}: the weighted comparison correlation defined in the statement
glossary.W: a nonnegative continuously differentiable weight supported in [a,b]
glossary.c_W: the positive constant 2 times the integral of W
glossary.r_N(n): the multiplicative local-density weight defined in the statement
glossary.𝔠(N): a positive normalization factor attached to N

0fd3b33d63081ee3.title: ONE-CAUCHY BOUND FOR A UNIQUE DILATOR STRATUM. Let \(\mathcal H\) be a complex Hilbert space with inner product linear in the first variable. Let \(X\) be a positive integer, let \(P\ge1\) be real, and let \(\mathcal P\) be a finite set of integers contained in \([P,2P]\). Let \(U_n\in\mathcal H\) for \(1\le n\le X\), with
0fd3b33d63081ee3.author: slava chan
0fd3b33d63081ee3.proof:
For \(m\le X/P\), define
\[
 Z_m=\sum_{\substack{a\in\mathcal P\\am\le X}}\lambda_{a,m}U_{am}.
\]
Since every \(a\in\mathcal P\) is at least \(P\), equation (3) gives
\[
 S=\sum_{m\le X/P}Z_m.
\]
Hilbert-space Cauchy--Schwarz yields
\[
 \|S\|_{\mathcal H}^2
 \le\left\lfloor\frac XP\right\rfloor
 \sum_{m\le X/P}\|Z_m\|_{\mathcal H}^2. \tag{7}
\]
Expand the last square. Its diagonal part is
\[
 \sum_{a\in\mathcal P}\sum_{m\le X/a}
 |\lambda_{a,m}|^2\|U_{am}\|_{\mathcal H}^2
 \le B^2X
\]
by (1) and (2). Pairing the off-diagonal terms and applying the triangle inequality bounds them by \(\mathcal C_{\rm off}\) as defined in (4). Substitution into (7) proves (5). Discarding \(\mathcal C_{\rm off}\) from the expression identifying the diagonal contribution and using \(\lfloor X/P\rfloor^{1/2}\le(X/P)^{1/2}\) gives (6).

Finally, under the uniqueness condition in the last sentence, the number of pairs \((a,m)\) with nonzero \(\lambda_{a,m}\) is at most \(X\), and each corresponding square has absolute value at most one. Hence (2) holds.

glossary.S: the Hilbert-valued sum on the unique-dilator stratum
glossary.Z_m: the sum of dilated vectors at fixed cofactor m
glossary.lambda_a,m: the coefficient selecting and weighting the representation n=am
glossary.mathcal C_off: the total absolute weighted off-diagonal two-dilate correlation
glossary.mathcal P: the finite set of dilators in the scale interval [P,2P]

1024f6bb05c0bb49.title: Fix
1024f6bb05c0bb49.author: slava chan
1024f6bb05c0bb49.statement:
Fix
\[
 1/2<\alpha<\beta<1,\quad \eta>0,\quad\rho>0,\quad
 B_{\rm src}>0.
\]
Let \(W\) and \(\Phi\) be bounded real functions supported in
\([\alpha,\beta]\) and \([1/2,2]\), respectively. Let \(N=2x\) be an integer with \(x\ge3\), put
\[
 T_x=(\log x)^{6+\eta+\rho},
\]
and assume
\[
 {1\over2}x^{1/2}(\log x)^{-B_{\rm src}}\le D\le2x^{1/2},
 \qquad D>2T_x,qquad U>0.
\]
Let \(\mu\) be the Möbius function, extend \(\Lambda\) by zero on nonpositive integers, and put
\[
 {\cal I}_D=\{d\ge2:(d,N)=1,\ \mu(d)\ne0, d\le x^{1/2},\ \Phi(d/D)\ne0\}.
\]
For positive integers \(s,m,w\), define
\[
 f_{s,m}(w)=
 {\bf1}_{sw\in{\cal I}_D}\mu(w)\Phi(sw/D)W(smw/x)
 \Phi((N-smw)/U)\Lambda(N-smw),
\]
\[
 F_s(\theta)=
 \left(\sum_w f_{s,m}(w)e(\theta w)\right)_{m\ge1},
 \qquad e(t)=\exp(2\pi it).
\]
For every real \(L>0\), define the finite trigonometric polynomial
\[
 P_L(\theta)=
 \sum_{h\in\mathbb Z}\left(1-{|h|\over L}\right)_+e(h\theta),
 \qquad y_+=\max(y,0).                                  \tag{1}
\]
It is nonnegative and
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R/\mathbb Z}P_L(\theta)d\theta=1.      \tag{2}
\]
For \(g,r\ge1\), put
\[
 L_{gr}={D\over grT_x}.                                  \tag{3}
\]
Define
\[
 {\cal A}_{<}^{F}=
 \sum_{g<T_x}\sum_{r<T_x}\mu(r)
 \int_{\mathbb R/\mathbb Z}
 P_{L_{gr}}(\theta)\|F_{gr}(\theta)\|_{ell^2_m}^{,2}d\theta,
                                                                    \tag{4}
\]
\[
 {\cal R}_{<}^{F}=
 \sum_{g<T_x}\sum_{r<T_x}\mu(r)
 \left(
 \|F_{gr}(0)\|_{ell^2_m}^{,2}
 -
 \int_{\mathbb R/\mathbb Z}
 P_{L_{gr}}(\theta)\|F_{gr}(\theta)\|_{ell^2_m}^{,2}d\theta
 \right).                                                \tag{5}
\]
Let
\[
 {\cal E}_{<}=
 \sum_{g<T_x}\sum_{r<T_x}\mu(r)
 \|F_{gr}(0)\|_{ell^2_m}^{,2}.                        \tag{6}
\]
Then exactly
\[
 {\cal E}_{<}={\cal R}_{<}^{F}+{\cal A}_{<}^{F}.       \tag{7}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 |{\cal A}_{<}^{F}|
 \ll_{W,\Phi,\alpha,\beta}
 {xD(\log x)^2\over T_x}.                               \tag{8}
\]
Thus the unproved one-sided residual estimate
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 {\cal R}_{<}^{F}
 \ll_{W,\Phi,\alpha,\beta,\eta,\rho}
 xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta}
 \quad}                                                  \tag{TB-FEJ-RES}
\]
implies
\[
 {\cal E}_{<}\ll xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta}.                \tag{9}
\]
Consequently it implies the full-von-Mangoldt hard covariance bound of fact 1f5316e61daf156d and the physical-shift estimate of fact 308c7c0d43bda909.

The residual in (5) is diagonal-free term by term in its Fourier expansion. More precisely, if
\[
 C_s(h)=\sum_m\sum_{w-w'=h}
 f_{s,m}(w)\overline{f_{s,m}(w')},
\]
then
\[
 \|F_s(0)\|_2^2-
 \int P_{D/(sT_x)}\|F_s(\theta)\|_2^2d\theta
 =
 \sum_{h\in\mathbb Z}
 \min\left(1,{sT_x|h|\over D}\right)C_s(h),           \tag{10}
\]
whose \(h=0\) coefficient is zero. Hence (TB-FEJ-RES), rather than the uncentered positive TB-VL2 of fact 6a2652fb92d86417, is the exact centered large-slope reflected-prime theorem isolated by this local-circle split. No estimate for (5) is asserted.

Fact 73fb9efe1286f7e9 remains a separate post-Heath--Brown/Poisson seam. Its coefficients are independent of its varying modulus except for a unit phase numerator, whereas the literal coefficient \(f_{s,m}(w)\) depends jointly on \(s,m,w\). The Fejér identity does not perform the decomposition or pay the projective coefficient norm needed to enter that theorem.
1024f6bb05c0bb49.proof:
The Fourier coefficient sequence
\[
 a_L(h)=\left(1-{|h|\over L}\right)_+
\]
is positive definite. One direct verification is Poisson summation applied to the nonnegative function
\[
 t\mapsto {1\over L}\left({\sin(\pi Lt)\over\pi t}\right)^2.
\]
Its periodization has Fourier coefficients \(a_L(h)\), so it equals \(P_L\) and is nonnegative. The coefficient at \(h=0\) is one, proving (2).

Equation (7) follows immediately by adding (4) and (5). We prove (8). First extend (4) to the complete projector:
\[
 {\cal A}_{\rm all}^{F}=
 \sum_{g<T_x}\sum_{r\ge1}\mu(r)
 \int P_{L_{gr}}(\theta)\|F_{gr}(\theta)\|_2^2d\theta.            \tag{11}
\]
Expand the squared norm and use the Fourier coefficients of \(P_{L_{gr}}\). Write
\[
 u=rw,\qquad u'=rw',\qquad G=gm.
\]
The kernel coefficient becomes
\[
 \left(1-{grT_x|w-w'|\over D}\right)_+
 =
 \left(1-{gT_x|u-u'|\over D}\right)_+,                \tag{12}
\]
which is independent of the projector divisor \(r\). Therefore the complete divisor identity
\[
 \sum_{r\mid u,\ r\mid u'}\mu(r)={\bf1}_{(u,u')=1}
\]
gives
\[
\begin{split}
 {\cal A}_{\rm all}^{F}
 =\sum_{g<T_x}\sum_{g\mid G}
 \sum_{\substack{u,u'\ge1\\(u,u')=1}}
 &B_{g,G}(u)B_{g,G}(u')\\
 &\times
 \left(1-{gT_x|u-u'|\over D}\right)_+,                \tag{13}
\end{split}
\]
where explicitly
\[
 B_{g,G}(u)=
 {\bf1}_{gu\in{\cal I}_D}\mu(u)\Phi(gu/D)W(uG/x)
 \Phi((N-uG)/U)\Lambda(N-uG).                          \tag{14}
\]
There is no diagonal in (13). If \(u=u'\) and \((u,u')=1\), then \(u=1\); but \(gu\in{\cal I}_D\) would give \(g\ge D/2>T_x\), contradicting \(g<T_x\). Every remaining term in (13) satisfies
\[
 0<g|u-u'|<D/T_x.                                        \tag{15}
\]
Under the bijection
\[
 d_1=gu,\qquad d_2=gu',\qquad m=G/g,
\]
condition (15) becomes
\[
 0<|d_1-d_2|<D/T_x.
\]
There are \(O(D^2/T_x)\) ordered pairs \((d_1,d_2)\), and for each pair the support of \(W(d_1m/x)\) permits \(O(x/D)\) values of \(m\). Every summand is
\(O_{W,\Phi}((\log x)^2)\). Since the triangular coefficient is at most one,
\[
 |{\cal A}_{\rm all}^{F}|
 \ll {xD(\log x)^2\over T_x}.                         \tag{16}
\]

It remains to compare the complete and truncated projectors. Since \(P_L\ge0\) and has integral one,
\[
\begin{split}
 |{\cal A}_{\rm all}^{F}-{\cal A}_{<}^{F}|
 &\le
 \sum_{g<T_x}\sum_{r\ge T_x}
 \int P_{L_{gr}}(\theta)\|F_{gr}(\theta)\|_2^2d\theta.            \tag{17}
\end{split}
\]
If the \(m\)-th coordinate of \(F_{gr}(\theta)\) is nonzero, then there are
\(O(D/(gr))\) possible \(w\), each summand is
\(O_{W,\Phi}(\log x)\), and there are \(O(x/D)\) possible \(m\). Hence, uniformly in \(\theta\),
\[
 \|F_{gr}(\theta)\|_2^2
 \ll_{W,\Phi,\alpha,\beta}
 {xD(\log x)^2\over g^2r^2}.                          \tag{18}
\]
Insert (18) into (17), use (2), and sum
\[
 \sum_{g\ge1}g^{-2}<\infty,qquad
 \sum_{r\ge T_x}r^{-2}\ll T_x^{-1}.
\]
This gives the same bound as (16), proving (8).

To prove (10), expand
\[
 \|F_s(\theta)\|_2^2=\sum_h C_s(h)e(h\theta).
\]
The integral against \(P_{D/(sT_x)}\) multiplies \(C_s(h)\) by
\[
 \left(1-{sT_x|h|\over D}\right)_+.
\]
Subtracting from the value at zero gives multiplier
\[
 1-\left(1-{sT_x|h|\over D}\right)_+
 =\min\left(1,{sT_x|h|\over D}\right),
\]
proving (10). Its value at \(h=0\) is zero.

Under TB-FEJ-RES, equations (7)--(8) and
\[
 (\log x)^2/T_x=(\log x)^{-4-\eta-\rho}
\]
prove (9). Fact 1f5316e61daf156d transfers (9) to the hard covariance, and fact 308c7c0d43bda909 gives the physical-shift identity. The last coefficient-slot statement follows directly from the hypotheses of fact 73fb9efe1286f7e9 and the displayed definition of \(f_{s,m}(w)\).

glossary.P_L: the periodic real-scale Fejer kernel with Fourier coefficient (1-|h|/L)_+
glossary.TB-FEJ-RES: the one-sided large-slope reflected-prime Fejer-residual estimate sufficient for the hard covariance
glossary.cal A_<^F: the truncated signed Fejer-average part of the coprimality-projector energy
glossary.cal R_<^F: the signed diagonal-free Fejer residual after subtracting cal A_<^F

10333483b7c7c2d5.title: TENSOR-STABLE JOINT-(h,t) REPEATED-POLE PAYMENT FOR ACTUAL C1,C2,C3,C4 ROWS, AND THE EXACT POINTWISE RESIDUAL-CRT REALIZATION
10333483b7c7c2d5.author: slava chan
10333483b7c7c2d5.statement:
TENSOR-STABLE JOINT-(h,t) REPEATED-POLE PAYMENT FOR ACTUAL C1,C2,C3,C4 ROWS, AND THE EXACT POINTWISE RESIDUAL-CRT REALIZATION.

Adopt the actual C1-C4 long natural chamber of fact f6f2a56af7b391c8. Thus p is a selected first-nonresonant prime, T<=t=n/p<2T is one natural dyadic cofactor interval, the physical nonzero heights satisfy H<=|h|<2H, and
  2H<p, 2T<p, H,T>=p^delta                                    (1)
for a fixed 0<delta<1. Let X_p be the nonzero physical q-residue set and R_{p,Q}=#X_p.

Let E be a complex normed vector space. For every x in X_p, signed h, and t, let Lambda_p(x,h,t) be a finite set of literal source copies and let
  v_{p,lambda}(x,h,t) in E.
Assume that for every fixed A>=2 and epsilon_0>0,
  sum_{lambda in Lambda_p(x,h,t)}||v_{p,lambda}(x,h,t)||_E
  <<_{A,epsilon_0}
  Q^epsilon_0(1+Q/p)(1+|h|/H_P)^(-A).                         (2)
For every ordered four-row source tuple z, allow a tuple-dependent complex four-linear functional K_{p,z}:E^4->C and a mask 0<=D_{p,z}<=1 such that
  |K_{p,z}(w_1,w_2,w_3,w_4)|
  <=D_{p,z} product_{i=1}^4||w_i||_E.                         (3)
Let V_{p,C_j}^{rep} be the sum of
  |K_{p,z}(v_{p,lambda_1},v_{p,lambda_2},
           v_{p,lambda_3},v_{p,lambda_4})|
over exactly the no-singleton physical-q-residue partitions and block balances of fact f6f2a56af7b391c8, with every source, selected-prime, pair-deletion, and tuple mask retained.

For
  0<eta<min(1,4delta),  0<rho<min(eta,2delta),                 (4)
one has, for all sufficiently large p,
  V_{p,C_j}^{rep}
  <<_{A,delta,eta,rho,epsilon_0}
  Q^(4epsilon_0)(1+Q/p)^4(1+H/H_P)^(-4A)
  R_{p,Q}^2(HT)^4p^(-rho).                                    (5)
Hence the sharper joint-(h,t) payment, including all three two-pair pole partitions and every physical-height sign sector, is stable under any exact remaining-face vectorization satisfying the per-row norm bound (2) and the norm-one four-linear contraction (3). It does not revert to the height-l1/cofactor-l-infinity envelope of fact a84f95a82329a894.

There is an unconditional pointwise residual-CRT realization of (2)-(3) for every actual canonical C1-C4 row before any additional joint-completion operator. In the notation of fact 41b56ed8e64bdba6, write
  d_lambda=pm,  n=d_lambda v_lambda,  t=n/p=mv_lambda.
The exact canonical row factors as
  ctilde_lambda(q,h)
  e_p(mathscr A h(qt)^(-1))
  e_m(mathscr A h(qv_lambda p)^(-1)).                          (6)
Put
  a_lambda(q,h)=ctilde_lambda(q,h)
                e_m(mathscr A h(qv_lambda p)^(-1)),
  E=C^2,  ||(z_1,z_2)||_E=max(|z_1|,|z_2|),
  v_{p,lambda}=(a_lambda,conjugate(a_lambda)).                 (7)
For a four-row TT-star tuple define
  K_{p,z}(w_1,w_2,w_3,w_4)
  =D_{p,z}(w_1)_1(w_2)_1(w_3)_2(w_4)_2.                       (8)
Then (3) holds with norm at most one, (8) is exactly the product of the two positive-row residual amplitudes and the conjugates of the two negative-row amplitudes, and (2) follows from the literal C1-C4 coefficient bound used in fact dbfaad4be3d523a8. Thus residual CRT phases, conjugation, and tuple masks do not obstruct the tensor lift.

The remaining open vector interface is narrower: (6)-(8) do not construct a source-preserving common-X completion on unequal q-residues, and do not show that any additional dual-frequency or joint-completion Hilbert vector has norm bounded by the scalar right side of (2). No comparison with the complete literal joint-completion Hilbert norm, cross-modulus assembly, short-block or zero-height payment, Top B estimate, complete trace estimate, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
10333483b7c7c2d5.proof:
Put
  A_{p,x}(h,t)=sum_lambda||v_{p,lambda}(x,h,t)||_E.
By (3), every summand of V_{p,C_j}^{rep} is at most
  D_{p,z} product_i||v_{p,lambda_i}(x_i,h_i,t_i)||_E.
Summing the literal source labels first replaces this product by
  D_{p,z} product_i A_{p,x_i}(h_i,t_i).                        (9)
Thus it suffices to prove the scalar nonnegative occupancy bound under (2); no coordinate of E is chosen.

Partition the physical height signs. After putting h_i^*=|h_i|, each of the sixteen sectors has one of the sixteen algebraic sign balances covered by fact ae1623e3b77d7695. The majorant (2) has the separated form
  Q^epsilon_0(1+Q/p) w(h_i^*),
  w(h)=(1+h/H_P)^(-A),
whose supremum-plus-variation on H<=h<2H is at most twice
  (1+H/H_P)^(-A)
by fact 3286b0e75a3ea94a. Facts 9ea2dddfbbbd191a and ae1623e3b77d7695 therefore give, for the all-four-equal block at one residue x,
  <<Q^(4epsilon_0)(1+Q/p)^4(1+H/H_P)^(-4A)
    (HT)^4p^(-eta).                                           (10)
Summing (10) over x gives its factor R_{p,Q}.

For a two-element block at a fixed residue x, the balance has the form
  sigma_i h_i/t_i+sigma_j h_j/t_j=0 mod p.
After h_i,h_j,t_i are fixed, t_j is uniquely determined modulo p. Reduction of [T,2T) is injective because T<p, so there is at most one supported t_j. Using (2), the block occupancy is therefore
  <<Q^(2epsilon_0)(1+Q/p)^2(1+H/H_P)^(-2A)H^2T.               (11)
Two blocks, summed over their two residue labels after dropping distinctness, contribute at most
  <<Q^(4epsilon_0)(1+Q/p)^4(1+H/H_P)^(-4A)
    R_{p,Q}^2H^4T^2.                                         (12)
There are three two-pair partitions. Equations (10)-(12) reproduce the precise bound (7) of fact f6f2a56af7b391c8. Since T>=p^delta and R_{p,Q}<=R_{p,Q}^2 when nonzero, (4) implies (5), exactly as in that fact. This proves the abstract tensor lift.

It remains to verify the actual pointwise specialization. Equation (5) of fact 41b56ed8e64bdba6 gives the row
  ctilde_lambda(q,h)e_{d_lambda}(mathscr A h(qv_lambda)^(-1)).
With d_lambda=pm and gcd(p,m)=1, the Chinese remainder identity used in that fact gives
  e_{pm}(z)=e_p(zm^(-1))e_m(zp^(-1)).
For z=mathscr A h(qv_lambda)^(-1), the p-factor is
  e_p(mathscr A h(qv_lambda m)^(-1))
  =e_p(mathscr A h(qt)^(-1)),
and the m-factor is the one displayed in (6). This proves (6).

The residual m-factor in (6) has modulus one. Therefore (7) has norm
  ||v_{p,lambda}||_E=|a_lambda|=|ctilde_lambda|.
Equation (8) is complex four-linear and satisfies
  |K_{p,z}(w_1,w_2,w_3,w_4)|
  <=D_{p,z} product_i||w_i||_E,
while direct substitution of (7) gives the claimed positive-positive-negative-negative residual product. The coefficient aggregation in the proof of fact dbfaad4be3d523a8, based on fact 3286b0e75a3ea94a, proves (2), including the physical q-lift factor 1+Q/p. This proves the pointwise realization. No additional completion vector was introduced, so the final scope paragraph follows.

glossary.K_{p,z}: The tuple-dependent norm-one four-linear contraction of the four remaining-face vectors.
glossary.V_{p,C_j}^{rep}: The vector-valued actual Cj repeated-pole occupancy evaluated by a tuple-dependent contractive four-linear functional.
glossary.a_lambda: The canonical row amplitude after removing the selected-p prime phase and retaining the residual CRT phase.

104522049dda64e6.title: Let X be a Rademacher random variable: X=1 and X=-1 each with probability one half. For random variables X_1,X_2,X_3,X_4 with finite joint moments define their connected four-point partition functional by
104522049dda64e6.author: slava chan
104522049dda64e6.statement:
Let X be a Rademacher random variable: X=1 and X=-1 each with probability one half. For random variables X_1,X_2,X_3,X_4 with finite joint moments define their connected four-point partition functional by
kappa(X_1,X_2,X_3,X_4)=sum_{pi in Part({1,2,3,4})}(-1)^{|pi|-1}(|pi|-1)! product_{B in pi} E[product_{i in B}X_i].
Then
kappa(X,X,X,X)=-2.
Consequently, even a genuine joint-moment connected/Ursell partition sum can be negative on a one-dimensional diagonal and therefore need not be a positive-semidefinite Gram kernel. This remains true after applying an identity support-disjoint pair projection. Thus moment provenance and support-projection positivity do not automatically supply the PSD connected-partition factorization required by COH in fact f077de751a5189b6. This is a finite probabilistic counterexample to automatic partition positivity, not an assertion about the sign of the actual WF-RPS connected kernel and not an arithmetic saving.
104522049dda64e6.proof:
The moments of X are E[X]=0, E[X^2]=1, E[X^3]=0, and E[X^4]=1. In the partition formula, the unique one-block partition contributes E[X^4]=1.

Among the seven two-block partitions, exactly three have two blocks of size two. Each of these contributes coefficient -1 times E[X^2]E[X^2]=-1. The remaining four two-block partitions have block sizes three and one, so their products contain E[X]=0 and vanish.

Every partition into three blocks has at least two singleton blocks, and the partition into four blocks has four singleton blocks. All of those terms vanish because E[X]=0. Therefore
kappa(X,X,X,X)=1-3=-2.

A one-dimensional positive-semidefinite Gram matrix must be a scalar [a] with a>=0. The scalar connected kernel here is [-2], so it is not positive semidefinite. If the ordered pair-coordinate space consists of one support-disjoint coordinate, the support projection of fact f077de751a5189b6 is the identity and leaves [-2] unchanged. Hence genuine moment origin plus support projection does not imply partition positivity. The scope qualifications follow because this example supplies no WF-RPS packet data.

glossary.Rademacher random variable: a random variable taking the values +1 and -1 with equal probability
glossary.kappa: the connected four-point functional defined by the partition-lattice Mobius sum

10b0cd08eacc17fa.title: UNIT-RAY-PHYS-COLLAPSE: PHYSICAL-COORDINATE REASSEMBLY, DIVISOR OCCUPANCY, AND A COMPLETE-U SECOND-MOMENT BOUND
10b0cd08eacc17fa.author: slava chan
10b0cd08eacc17fa.statement:
UNIT-RAY-PHYS-COLLAPSE: PHYSICAL-COORDINATE REASSEMBLY, DIVISOR OCCUPANCY, AND A COMPLETE-U SECOND-MOMENT BOUND.

Adopt the exact fixed-orientation, fixed-anatomy, fixed-frequency and fixed-dilator family of fact a36284a9dbec7837, with
1<=F<=x^3, Q<=q<2Q, F<=|h|<2F,
one exact copy lambda over n, and exact pre-reciprocity coefficient c_lambda(q,h) from fact e55b27d39c593164. Let
S_lambda
 =sum_{supported (epsilon,b)}
   A_lambda(epsilon,b)U_lambda(epsilon,b)
be the complete signed unit-ray aggregate used in fact 5dec521df02ef076. Then
S_lambda
 =sum_{substack{Q<=q<2Q, F<=|h|<2F, (q,n)=1, q divides h}}
   c_lambda(q,h).                                                (UNIT-RAY-PHYS)

The sum on the right retains every literal mask occurring in c_lambda. Its coordinate support N_lambda^unit satisfies
N_lambda^unit<=sum_{F<=|h|<2F} tau(|h|)<=x^{o(1)}F.              (1)
In particular S_lambda=0 if 2F<=Q. Summed over every exact copy in one anatomy and dilator block,
sum_lambda |S_lambda|^2
 <=x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 B F^2.                                  (UNIT-RAY-U2)

Consequently the complete-U supplier PRIME-rho-CONST-U of fact 5dec521df02ef076 holds whenever
Dcal<=Q^2 x^{o(1)}; more concretely, for every fixed A>0 it holds on
Dcal<=Q^2(log(2x))^A,
with the fixed logarithmic factor absorbed by x^{o(1)}. In the genuinely larger range the exact remaining loss in this argument relative to the canonical scale
x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 BQ^2F^2/Dcal
is Dcal/Q^2, rather than the Dcal/Q loss produced by raywise Cauchy and the full proportional-ray budget.

This proves only the physical-coordinate collapse and complete-U second-moment estimate. It proves no prime-rho nonconstant-mode payment outside the chamber of fact 5dec521df02ef076, no composite-rho estimate, no full P-qSRC-SUP, no tail payment, and no Goldbach conclusion.
10b0cd08eacc17fa.proof:
By RAY-MU in fact a36284a9dbec7837, on the primitive unit ray R=(epsilon,1,b),
B_lambda(epsilon,1,b)
 =A_lambda(epsilon,b)U_lambda(epsilon,b)
 =sum_{k>0: c_lambda(k,epsilon k b) nonzero}
   c_lambda(k,epsilon k b).                                    (2)
Summing (2) over every supported signed unit ray gives S_lambda.

The map
(k,epsilon,b) mapsto (q,h)=(k,epsilon k b)                     (3)
is a bijection from the summation indices in (2), after the outer signed-ray sum, to supported physical coordinates satisfying q divides h. Indeed (3) gives q divides h. Conversely, if q divides h and h is nonzero, then
k=q, epsilon=sgn(h), b=|h|/q
is the unique inverse, and (epsilon,1,b) is primitive because gcd(1,b)=1. The support conditions and every factor in c_lambda are unchanged under this relabeling. This proves UNIT-RAY-PHYS.

For a fixed nonzero h, every q counted in UNIT-RAY-PHYS is a positive divisor of |h|. Hence its number is at most tau(|h|). There are fewer than 2F signed integers h with F<=|h|<2F up to an absolute endpoint factor. Since |h|<=2x^3, the divisor estimate used throughout fact e55b27d39c593164 gives tau(|h|)=x^{o(1)} uniformly. This proves (1).

If 2F<=Q, a counted coordinate would satisfy
Q<=q<=|h|<2F<=Q,
which is impossible. Thus the aggregate is then empty.

Let N_lambda^unit denote the number of nonzero coordinates in UNIT-RAY-PHYS. Cauchy--Schwarz gives
|S_lambda|^2
 <=N_lambda^unit
   sum_{q divides h}|c_lambda(q,h)|^2
 <=x^{o(1)}F
   sum_{q divides h}|c_lambda(q,h)|^2.                          (4)
In the proof of fact e55b27d39c593164, after extracting omega_F, every dimensionless coefficient c_lambda(q,h) on one fixed projective fibre is x^{o(1)}. The same fact proves that the total number of exact copies over n asymptotic to B is Bx^{o(1)}. Applying (1) to each copy therefore gives
sum_lambda sum_{q divides h}|c_lambda(q,h)|^2
 <=x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 B F.                                    (5)
Summing (4) and using (5) proves UNIT-RAY-U2.

The target in PRIME-rho-CONST-U is
x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 BQ^2F^2/Dcal.
The quotient of the right side of UNIT-RAY-U2 by its scale without x^{o(1)} is Dcal/Q^2. Thus any fixed power of log(2x) in that quotient is absorbed into x^{o(1)}, proving the displayed near-boundary consequence and the exact loss comparison. No estimate for any excluded family was used, so the stated limitations follow.

glossary.N_lambda^unit: The number of supported physical coordinates q,h with q dividing h in one exact copy.
glossary.UNIT-RAY-PHYS: The exact reassembly of the complete signed unit-ray aggregate in the original physical coordinates q,h, characterized by q dividing h.
glossary.UNIT-RAY-U2: The complete signed unit-ray aggregate second-moment estimate obtained from physical divisor occupancy.

10fd259d904acea7.title: BOUNDED SCHUR-MULTIPLIER NORM OF A ROW-DEPENDENT ROUGH COPRIMALITY GATE. Let Pcal be a finite set of primes. Let Lambdacal and Qcal be finite nonempty sets. For every lambda in Lambdacal choose R_lambda subset Pcal, and for every q in Qcal choose T_q subset Pcal. Assume
10fd259d904acea7.author: slava chan
10fd259d904acea7.statement:
BOUNDED SCHUR-MULTIPLIER NORM OF A ROW-DEPENDENT ROUGH COPRIMALITY GATE. Let Pcal be a finite set of primes. Let Lambdacal and Qcal be finite nonempty sets. For every lambda in Lambdacal choose R_lambda subset Pcal, and for every q in Qcal choose T_q subset Pcal. Assume
|R_lambda|<=J and |T_q|<=K                                             (1)
for fixed nonnegative integers J,K. Define
U(lambda,q)=1 if R_lambda intersect T_q is empty, and U(lambda,q)=0 otherwise. (2)
For every complex matrix A=(A(lambda,q)), regarded as an operator from l2(Qcal) to l2(Lambdacal), let U circle A be its entrywise product with U. Then
||U circle A||_{op}<=2^{(J+K)/2}||A||_{op}.                         (3)
The constant is independent of |Pcal|, |Lambdacal|, |Qcal|, and the number of distinct row sets R_lambda.

Suppose now that the elements q of Qcal are positive integers. Attach to every lambda a squarefree positive integer m_lambda all of whose prime divisors lie in Pcal, and define
R_lambda={p in Pcal:p divides m_lambda},
T_q={p in Pcal:p divides q}.                                       (4)
If
omega(m_lambda)<=J and |T_q|<=K,                                   (5)
then
1_{gcd(q,m_lambda)=1}=U(lambda,q),                                  (6)
so inserting this row-dependent coprimality gate in any row-output operator matrix costs at most 2^{(J+K)/2} in operator norm.

For a literal C4 rough gate, m_lambda may be any squarefree divisor of the four-rough-prime product in that row. Thus one may take J=4. On any output interval where every q has at most K primes from the common rough-prime universe, (3) gives a fixed gate cost 2^{(4+K)/2}; it does not depend on the union of the row divisors. This is an operator-Schur transfer only. It does not prove that a proposed PFACE-VEC estimate has been formulated on the required row-output matrix, does not handle non-coprimality masks outside the bounded rough universe, varying small-v phases, signed face recombination, shared-prime collision aggregation, a C4 estimate, or Goldbach.
10fd259d904acea7.proof:
Let Hcal be the Hilbert space l2 of all subsets of Pcal. For lambda in Lambdacal and S subset Pcal define
a_lambda(S)=(-1)^{|S|}1_{S subset R_lambda},                         (7)
and for q in Qcal define
b_q(S)=1_{S subset T_q}.                                            (8)
Then
<a_lambda,b_q>
=sum_{S subset R_lambda intersect T_q}(-1)^{|S|}
=(1-1)^{|R_lambda intersect T_q|}
=U(lambda,q).                                                       (9)
Also,
||a_lambda||_2^2=2^{|R_lambda|}<=2^J,
||b_q||_2^2=2^{|T_q|}<=2^K.                                        (10)

Define
V:l2(Lambdacal)->l2(Lambdacal) tensor Hcal,
V e_lambda=e_lambda tensor a_lambda,                                (11)
and
W:l2(Qcal)->l2(Qcal) tensor Hcal,
W e_q=e_q tensor b_q.                                               (12)
Equation (10) gives ||V||<=2^{J/2} and ||W||<=2^{K/2}. Direct calculation gives
U circle A=V^*(A tensor identity_{Hcal})W,                           (13)
because its (lambda,q) entry is A(lambda,q)<b_q,a_lambda>=A(lambda,q)U(lambda,q). Therefore
||U circle A||_{op}
<=||V||||A tensor identity_{Hcal}||_{op}||W||
<=2^{(J+K)/2}||A||_{op},
proving (3).

In (4), Pcal consists only of primes and contains every prime divisor of m_lambda. Hence R_lambda is exactly the prime-divisor set of m_lambda and |R_lambda|=omega(m_lambda)<=J. Also gcd(q,m_lambda)=1 exactly when R_lambda intersect T_q is empty. This proves (6), and (5) verifies (1).

Fact 9bee61f3627bd506 states that a literal C4 marked factor is a small squarefree cofactor times four distinct rough primes. A squarefree divisor m_lambda supported on those four rough primes has at most four prime divisors, so the theorem applies with J=4 whenever the stated output bound K holds. The excluded structures do not enter (7)-(13), proving the scope assertions.

glossary.R_lambda: the set of rough primes in the row-dependent gate modulus
glossary.T_q: the set of rough primes from the common universe that divide the output q
glossary.U circle A: the entrywise product of the rough coprimality mask U with the operator matrix A

11ec605c5135a640.title: COMPLEX-L1 MIXED SOURCE--DENSITY QUARTIC PAYOFF
11ec605c5135a640.author: slava chan
11ec605c5135a640.statement:
COMPLEX-L1 MIXED SOURCE--DENSITY QUARTIC PAYOFF.

Let Q>=2, H>=1, B>=1, let p>2Q be prime, and let A be an integer not divisible by p. Put I_Q={q in Z:Q<=q<2Q}. A coefficient row of type U is supported on at most BQ/H integers of I_Q and has pointwise modulus at most B. A coefficient row of type Z is supported on I_Q and has pointwise modulus at most B/H.

Let c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4 be four such rows, with at least one row of type Z. Define Delta, rho_12, rho_34, Gamma_W, and the exact Delta-nonzero four-row form M_W(c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4) as in fact 0e8ef74ba484418d. Let W be an arbitrary complex function on Z/pZ satisfying
  sum_{r modulo p}W(r)=0,
  sum_{r modulo p}|W(r)|<=L.                                (1)
Then
 |M_W(c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4)|
 << B^8[LQ^2/H^3+(L/p)Q^3/H^3].                            (2)
The implied constant is absolute. The estimate uses no positivity of W and retains the exact Delta nonzero restriction supplied by the all-shift rational-slope subtraction.

Let P>2Q and let cal P be any set of primes in [P,2P). Suppose that for every p in cal P and every member of a (v,s)-family, the fifteen mixed terms of the exact expansion in fact ace362082848a702 satisfy the preceding U/Z conditions with the same B,H,L, and suppose the total squared (v,s)-mass is at most B. Then their complete family contribution is
 <<B^9[P LQ^2/H^3+LQ^3/H^3].                               (3)
If L<=C_LQ and H>=Q^(1/9), this is
 <<_{C_L}B^9P Q^(8/3).                                     (4)
Thus if B<=Q^epsilon, the mixed source--density terms meet the full-kernel mean-zero discrepancy scale after an adjustment of epsilon. The all-U term is not included in this assertion; it is the term assigned to fact 914048233fada05f when its hypotheses and the required pointwise normalization of W hold.
11ec605c5135a640.proof:
For two rows c_i,c_j define their fixed-output reciprocal-difference sum
 R_{ij}(r)=sum_{q_i,q_j in I_Q; rho_p(q_i,q_j)=r}
                 c_i(q_i)conjugate(c_j(q_j)).               (5)
Since p does not divide A and p>2Q, fixing r and either q_i or q_j determines the other variable modulo p, and the interval I_Q is injective modulo p. Hence the number of pairs in (5) is at most the smaller support size.

It follows that
 |R_{ij}(r)|<<
  B^3Q/H       if both rows have type U,
  B^3Q/H^2     if at least one row has type Z,               (6)
where the second bound also covers two Z rows because B>=1 and H>=1.

Since W has mean zero,
 Gamma_W(x,y)=1_{x=y}W(x)-[W(x)+W(y)]/p.                    (7)
For the incidence part, group q_1,q_2 and q_3,q_4 by their common output r. At least one of the two row pairs contains a Z row. Equations (1) and (6) therefore give
 sum_r|W(r)R_{12}(r)conjugate(R_{34}(r))|
 <<B^6LQ^2/H^3.                                             (8)
Deleting Delta=0 tuples can only decrease this absolute majorant.

For the first cross term in (7), group the q_1,q_2 pair by its output and discard the Delta restriction after taking absolute values. If this pair contains a Z row, (1) and (6) bound its W-weighted sum by B^3LQ/H^2, while the product of the l1 norms of the other two rows is at most B^4Q^2/H^2. This is at most B^7LQ^3/H^4. If the first pair consists of two U rows, then the other pair contains a Z row. The W-weighted first pair is at most B^3LQ/H, and the product of the other two l1 norms is at most B^3Q^2/H^2. This is at most B^6LQ^3/H^3. After multiplication by p^(-1), both cases are bounded by
 B^7(L/p)Q^3/H^3.                                          (9)
The second cross term is identical with the two pairs interchanged. Combining (8)-(9), and enlarging B^7 to B^8, proves (2). This argument is purely absolute after the exact three-term centered kernel has been reduced using the mean-zero identity; it never invokes positivity.

There are fifteen mixed terms. Sum (2) over at most 2P primes and multiply by the squared-family mass at most B. Absorb the fixed factor fifteen and the factor two into the absolute constant to obtain (3).

Assume L<=C_LQ and H>=Q^(1/9). Then H^3>=Q^(1/3), so
 P LQ^2/H^3<=C_LP Q^(8/3).                                 (10)
Also P>2Q gives
 LQ^3/H^3<=C_LQ^4/H^3
          <=C_LQ^(11/3)
          <=(C_L/2)P Q^(8/3).                              (11)
This proves (4). Finally B<=Q^epsilon makes B^9<=Q^(9epsilon), which is absorbed by renaming epsilon. The all-U scope statement follows from the exact sixteen-term expansion in fact ace362082848a702 and the source estimate in fact 914048233fada05f.

glossary.R_{ij}: The fixed-output reciprocal-difference sum for coefficient rows i and j.
glossary.complex-L1 mixed payoff: The estimate of a mixed U/Z quartic form using only the l1 norm of a complex mean-zero physical kernel.

1218e64e51ba3131.title: Fix L>=1 and epsilon>0. Let H>=2, let C be a nonzero integer with |C|<=H^L, and let K be an integer. For an integer matrix Q=((a,c),(-d,b)) with even entries, |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|<=L H^3, and ab+cd=2K, let N_{C,K}(Q;H) be the number of ordered pairs of distinct primes r_2,r_3 in [H^2,2H^2) for which the intrinsic conditions (II) of fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb hold (so the ordered corners r_1,r_4 and the integers u,v are then uniquely recovered)
1218e64e51ba3131.author: slava chan
1218e64e51ba3131.statement:
Fix L>=1 and epsilon>0. Let H>=2, let C be a nonzero integer with |C|<=H^L, and let K be an integer. For an integer matrix Q=((a,c),(-d,b)) with even entries, |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|<=L H^3, and ab+cd=2K, let N_{C,K}(Q;H) be the number of ordered pairs of distinct primes r_2,r_3 in [H^2,2H^2) for which the intrinsic conditions (II) of fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb hold (so the ordered corners r_1,r_4 and the integers u,v are then uniquely recovered).

Uniformly in C,K,Q,
N_{C,K}(Q;H) <<_{L,epsilon} H^epsilon.

Furthermore, if S_K(H,L) is the complete coefficient shell of all such Q, including matrices with zero entries, then
|S_K(H,L)| <<_L H^6 log(2H)
and
sum_{Q in S_K(H,L)} N_{C,K}(Q;H) <<_{L,epsilon} H^{6+epsilon}.
The same H^{6+epsilon} bound holds after inserting the four von Mangoldt prime weights, or any weights bounded by a fixed power of log H. Matrices with J=ab-cd=0, a zero coefficient, or odd K contribute no normalized unit states; K=0 otherwise needs no separate loss. Thus the complete fixed-determinant matrix-shell tax is H^{6+o(1)}, and the fixed-Q divisor-scale estimate alone leaves no fixed power saving after the shell sum.
1218e64e51ba3131.proof:
By fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb, every state counted by N_{C,K}(Q;H) has nonzero a,b,c,d and J, and if q=gcd(|A|,|B|), then q is positive and even and 2q divides J. Hence q divides |J|/2. There are at most tau(|J|/2) possible q, and two possible common signs s.

For fixed q and s, the condition D=2sqC is
(ad) r_2^2+(-bc) r_3^2=2sqC.                                            (1)
All three coefficients ad, -bc, 2sqC are nonzero. We use the following uniform binary-quadratic representation estimate: for nonzero integers alpha,beta,gamma and X>=1, the number of integer pairs (x,y) with max(|x|,|y|)<=X and alpha x^2+beta y^2=gamma is O_epsilon(|alpha beta gamma X|^epsilon). This is Proposition 3 of Baier--Haldar, arXiv:2202.06759. Its hypotheses match (1) with alpha=ad, beta=-bc, gamma=2sqC and X=2H^2; signs are unrestricted in that proposition.

For completeness, the mechanism of that estimate is as follows. Multiplication by alpha turns the equation into
(alpha x)^2+alpha beta y^2=alpha gamma.
If -alpha beta is a square, it factors into two integral linear factors, and divisor pairs of alpha gamma determine the solutions. Otherwise, in the quadratic field generated by sqrt(-alpha beta), the element alpha x+y sqrt(-alpha beta) has fixed nonzero norm alpha gamma. Its principal ideal is an ideal divisor of (alpha gamma), giving at most a divisor-power number of ideals. Generators of one such ideal differ by units. In an imaginary quadratic field there are at most six units. In a real quadratic field they are, up to sign, powers of a fundamental unit at least (1+sqrt(5))/2; the polynomial coordinate box and the fixed nonzero norm confine the exponent to an interval of length O(log|2 alpha beta gamma X|). This gives the asserted epsilon-bound.

Here |J|<=2L^2H^6, q<=|J|/2, |ad|,|bc|<=L^2H^6, |C|<=H^L, and X=2H^2. Thus every quantity in the representation estimate is bounded by a fixed power of H depending only on L. The elementary divisor estimate tau(n)<<_epsilon n^epsilon shows that summing over q and s preserves an H^epsilon bound after decreasing the epsilon used inside the two estimates. Primality, pairwise distinctness, gcd(C,P)=1, and the exact gcd and quotient conditions only remove solutions of (1). This proves the fixed-Q estimate.

It remains to count the entire shell without omitting singular coordinate planes. Put X=ceil(LH^3). First take a,c both nonzero. For fixed a,c, let g=gcd(|a|,|c|). Integer solutions of
ab+cd=2K
form either the empty set or one affine progression whose steps in (b,d) are (c/g,-a/g). Intersecting with |b|,|d|<=X gives at most
1+3Xg/max(|a|,|c|)
solutions. Summing the first term over a,c costs O(X^2). By signs and symmetry it remains to bound
X sum_{1<=c<=a<=X} gcd(a,c)/a.
For fixed a,
sum_{c<=a} gcd(a,c)
 =sum_{e|a} e #{c<=a:gcd(a,c)=e}
 =sum_{e|a} e phi(a/e)
 <=a tau(a).
Therefore the last display is at most
X sum_{a<=X} tau(a)
 <=X sum_{mn<=X}1
 <=X^2(1+log X).
So the nonzero (a,c) sector has O(X^2 log(2X)) matrices.

If a=0 and c is nonzero, the equation cd=2K fixes d when c divides 2K, while b has O(X) choices; even the crude sum over c is O(X^2). The case c=0,a nonzero is identical. If a=c=0, there are no solutions unless K=0, and when K=0 the free pair (b,d) has O(X^2) choices. Hence the complete shell, including every zero stratum and K=0, has O(X^2 log(2X))=O_L(H^6 log(2H)) matrices. The parity restriction on entries can only decrease this number; moreover it makes K even, so the shell is empty for odd K.

Multiplying the shell bound by the fixed-Q estimate and absorbing log(2H) into H^epsilon yields the total H^{6+epsilon} bound. Four von Mangoldt factors are O((log H)^4) on the dyadic prime box, and any fixed polylogarithmic weights are absorbed in the same way. Fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb makes the J=0 and zero-coefficient contributions empty on the normalized unit layer. This accounts for every shell and reconstruction factor and proves the claimed endpoint tax.

glossary.L: fixed polynomial height constant for the carrier and coefficient boxes
glossary.N_{C,K}(Q;H): number of ordered dyadic prime pairs (r_2,r_3) satisfying the intrinsic normalized-unit conditions for fixed C,K,Q
glossary.S_K(H,L): complete bounded even-entry matrix shell with ab+cd=2K
glossary.alpha: first coefficient in the auxiliary binary quadratic equation
glossary.beta: second coefficient in the auxiliary binary quadratic equation
glossary.gamma: nonzero represented integer in the auxiliary binary quadratic equation

122bdf7f46de05e6.title: GA-PRIME-LOCAL-SPEC: EXACT LOCAL SPECTRUM AND THE UNIQUE LARGE COMMON-CORE SLOPE MODE. Let p be an odd prime and let a be a unit modulo p. Define on residues ell modulo p
122bdf7f46de05e6.author: slava chan
122bdf7f46de05e6.statement:
GA-PRIME-LOCAL-SPEC: EXACT LOCAL SPECTRUM AND THE UNIQUE LARGE COMMON-CORE SLOPE MODE. Let p be an odd prime and let a be a unit modulo p. Define on residues ell modulo p
f_{p,a}(ell)
 =1_{ell not congruent 0 (mod p)}
  [e_p(-a ell)+1/(p-1)].                                        (1)
For k modulo p define its positive-sign additive Fourier transform
fhat_{p,a}(k)=sum_{ell (mod p)}f_{p,a}(ell)e_p(k ell).            (2)
Then
fhat_{p,a}(0)=0,                                                 (3)
fhat_{p,a}(a)=p-1-1/(p-1)=p(p-2)/(p-1),                         (4)
and
fhat_{p,a}(k)=-p/(p-1)                                          (5)
for every k not congruent to 0 or a modulo p. Thus the constant slope mode is annihilated exactly, there is one specified nonzero mode of size p(p-2)/(p-1), and every other nonzero mode has modulus p/(p-1)<2.

Apply this to the common-core kernel Psi^{core}_{d,v} of fact 53737f4b1646ac1c. Put
a_{d,v}=gamma(dv)^{-1} modulo p.                                 (6)
The exact common-core conductor-class condition contains p not dividing ell, so the p-local factor of Psi^{core}_{d,v} is precisely f_{p,a_{d,v}}. The remaining conductor-class factor is modulo g_0 and the hard kernel is modulo rho_d; these moduli are coprime to p. Hence under the Chinese-remainder factorization of additive characters modulo
M_core=p g_0 rho_d,
the Fourier transform of Psi^{core}_{d,v} is the product of the p-local multiplier (3)-(5), a g_0-local class-mask transform, and the rho_d-local hard-kernel transform.

More explicitly, because g_0 is squarefree, put
r_0=gcd(g_0,T), h_0=g_0/r_0.                                    (7)
The g_0-local common-core class mask is
1_{h_0 divides ell},                                             (8)
and its positive Fourier transform modulo g_0 is
r_0 1_{r_0 divides k}.                                          (9)
The rho_d-local transform is
kappa_{rho_d,L}(k)
 =sum_{e divides rho_d, e>L}c_e(k),                             (10)
where c_e is the Ramanujan sum, as in fact eb589e60e7e30a33. Therefore every common-core Fourier coefficient in equation (12) of fact 53737f4b1646ac1c is zero on the p-constant mode; on the unique p-frequency a_{d,v} it carries the large local factor p(p-2)/(p-1); and on every other nonzero p-frequency it carries only the bounded local factor -p/(p-1), multiplied in all cases by the exact class-mask and hard-kernel factors (9)-(10).

For the one-end chamber with p dividing alpha, the twist in equation (15) of fact 53737f4b1646ac1c has the following exact effect. If A is extended by zero to all residues modulo p and
Ahat(k)=sum_{x (mod p)}A(x)e_p(-kx),                             (11)
then
widehat(A^{tw})(k)
 =Ahat(k+gamma(dv)^{-1})+Ahat(k)/(p-1).                          (12)
The p dividing beta chamber has the conjugate right-end analogue. Thus a one-end twist does not supply an operator saving by itself; it samples an explicit shifted source Fourier coefficient plus a small multiple of the unshifted one.

This theorem proves the exact local spectra only. It does not estimate the specified source frequency in the common-core chamber, the shifted source transform in the one-end chamber, the g_0 or rho_d factors after summation, any additional selector, PRIME-PAIR-DISC, the prime trace, C-HILBERT-OP-SUP, tail payment, or Goldbach.
122bdf7f46de05e6.proof:
For k=0, the first part of (2) is
sum_{ell not congruent 0}e_p(-a ell)=-1,
while the constant correction contributes
(p-1)/(p-1)=1.
This proves (3).

For k=a, the exponential part is p-1. Since a is nonzero, the correction contributes
(1/(p-1))sum_{ell not congruent 0}e_p(a ell)=-1/(p-1).
This proves (4).

If k is nonzero and k is not a, both k-a and k are nonzero. Each complete sum over nonzero ell is -1. Hence
fhat_{p,a}(k)=-1-1/(p-1)=-p/(p-1),
proving (5).

In the common-core chamber, fact fd22069145f59332 gives
C_q congruent gamma ell modulo p,
and fact 53737f4b1646ac1c gives the centered factor
1_{p does not divide ell}
[e_p(-gamma ell(dv)^{-1})+1/(p-1)].
This is exactly (1) with a=a_{d,v}. The other local masks have moduli g_0 and rho_d, both coprime to p, so the Chinese remainder theorem factors the additive character group and the Fourier transform into the stated local products.

We verify (8). The exact common-core class condition is
gcd(pg_0,T ell)=g_0,
with p not dividing T. For p this is exactly p not dividing ell. For a prime q dividing g_0, the condition requires q to divide T ell. It is automatic if q divides T and requires q to divide ell otherwise. Since g_0 is squarefree, the product of the latter primes is h_0=g_0/gcd(g_0,T), proving (8).

Write ell=h_0j modulo g_0, where j ranges modulo r_0=g_0/h_0. Then
sum_{ell (mod g_0),h_0 divides ell}e_{g_0}(k ell)
 =sum_{j (mod r_0)}e_{r_0}(kj),
which equals r_0 if r_0 divides k and zero otherwise. This proves (9). Equation (10) is the hard-kernel Fourier formula already verified in fact eb589e60e7e30a33.

Finally, in the one-end left chamber equation (15) of fact 53737f4b1646ac1c reads
A^{tw}(x)
 =[e_p(-gamma x(dv)^{-1})+1/(p-1)]A(x).
Multiplying by e_p(-kx) and summing x gives (12) directly. The right chamber is its conjugate version from equation (18) of that fact. All exclusions follow.

glossary.a_{d,v}: The unique large common-core slope frequency gamma(dv)^{-1} modulo p.
glossary.f_{p,a}: The p-local centered slope-difference kernel, extended by zero at the forbidden zero difference.
glossary.fhat_{p,a}: The positive-sign additive Fourier transform of f_{p,a}.
glossary.h_0: The complementary part g_0/r_0 forced to divide the slope difference.
glossary.kappa_{rho_d,L}: The Ramanujan-sum Fourier multiplier of the hard-conductor difference kernel.
glossary.r_0: The part of g_0 dividing the target T.

12515655a5e7ed7c.title: PRINCIPAL-CHARACTER DELETION IN THE FORWARD E11 SPECTRAL TRACE. Assume the hypotheses and notation of facts fc442085ff47a053 and 75d461ea0320c1a8. Define T_E11^prin by replacing, in every signed-frequency atom of T_E11^crit, the character sum of fact 75d461ea0320c1a8 by its principal-character term, and then restoring the literal conjugate-frequency pairing and every original coefficient and mask. Uniformly on each forward E11 dyadic central-strip label,
12515655a5e7ed7c.author: slava chan
12515655a5e7ed7c.statement:
PRINCIPAL-CHARACTER DELETION IN THE FORWARD E11 SPECTRAL TRACE. Assume the hypotheses and notation of facts fc442085ff47a053 and 75d461ea0320c1a8. Define T_E11^prin by replacing, in every signed-frequency atom of T_E11^crit, the character sum of fact 75d461ea0320c1a8 by its principal-character term, and then restoring the literal conjugate-frequency pairing and every original coefficient and mask. Uniformly on each forward E11 dyadic central-strip label,
 |T_E11^prin| <<_epsilon R x^epsilon.
After summing all literal dyadic, fixed-U, high-label, parent, least-tag and normalized-marker copies, there is a fixed delta_prin>0 such that
 |T_E11^prin| << x^(1-delta_prin).
Thus the principal character is an absolutely negligible part of T_E11^crit. The complementary nonprincipal cubic-character trace is not estimated, and no E21/E22 or Goldbach assertion is made.
12515655a5e7ed7c.proof:
We use the exact coefficient notation from fact 0a39d6be778e7dc9 on the g=1 layer. Thus, before the unit-modulus additive phase is inserted,
 lambda_{1,d,r,h}=mu(d)mu(r)r^(-1)Fhat_{1,d,r}(h/r),
and for every fixed integer J at least 3,
 |lambda_{1,d,r,h}| <<_J (M/r)(log x)^2(1+|h|M/r)^(-J).    (1)
All literal source and E11 masks are deletions of these indices. Fact fc442085ff47a053 also proves that the total absolute variation of the actual normalized-marker copies is bounded by an absolute constant on r=p ell. It therefore suffices to estimate the unrestricted majorant obtained from (1).

For one atom, fact 75d461ea0320c1a8 puts c_E=(d,h), q_E=d/c_E and shows that the principal spectral multiplier is
 |G_{N,q_E}(chi_0)|/phi(q_E)=|c_{q_E}(N)|/phi(q_E).         (2)
We first sum (2) over d at fixed h. The nonzero Mobius coefficient restricts d, hence q_E, to squarefree integers.

We derive the needed Ramanujan identity from its definition. If q_1 and q_2 are coprime, the Chinese remainder parametrization of a unit u modulo q_1q_2 gives unit residues u_i modulo q_i. Writing inverses of q_2 modulo q_1 and q_1 modulo q_2 in the additive character shows that e_{q_1q_2}(Nu) is a product of one additive character in u_1 and one in u_2. The extra inverse multipliers are units and hence permute the respective unit residue systems. Therefore
 c_{q_1q_2}(N)=c_{q_1}(N)c_{q_2}(N).                        (3)
For a prime p, if p divides N then every unit summand equals one and c_p(N)=p-1. If p does not divide N, the complete sum over all residues u modulo p of e_p(Nu) is zero; removing its u=0 term gives c_p(N)=-1. Now let q be squarefree, put a=(q,N), and q=ab. Then (a,b)=1. Multiplying the prime-local values using (3) yields
 c_q(N)=mu(b)phi(a)=mu(b)phi(q)/phi(b),
so
 |c_q(N)|/phi(q)=1/phi(b).                                 (4)

Group d by c=(d,h). Dropping the exact-gcd and coprimality restrictions only enlarges the nonnegative sum. Since c divides |h| and q=d/c is comparable to D/c, (4) gives
 sum_{d comparable to D, mu(d) nonzero}|c_{d/(d,h)}(N)|/phi(d/(d,h))
 <=sum_{c divides |h|} sum_{q comparable to D/c, q squarefree}|c_q(N)|/phi(q)
 <<tau(|h|)tau(N)log(2D).                                  (5)
Here is a self-contained proof of the last bound. Group q=ab by a=(q,N). There are at most tau(N) choices for a. For each a, sum 1/phi(b) over b<=C D/c. The identity
 b/phi(b)=sum_{s divides b}mu(s)^2/phi(s)
follows prime by prime: both sides are multiplicative, and at a prime power p^j with j>=1 the right side is 1+1/(p-1)=p/(p-1). After writing b=st and summing 1/t, it follows that
 sum_{b<=X}1/phi(b)<<log(2X)sum_{s>=1}1/(s phi(s))<<log(2X).
The final series converges because 1/(s phi(s)) is multiplicative and its prime-power local tail is O(p^(-2)), so its Euler product converges. This proves (5).

Insert (5) into (1), sum both signs of h, and use the elementary divisor bound tau(n)<<_epsilon n^epsilon. On the forward E11 strip, R>D and the source relations D M comparable to x together with D>=c x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B_src) and R>=D^(4/3) imply r/M>=x^(1/6-o(1))>1. Hence
 sum_{h nonzero}tau(|h|)(1+|h|M/r)^(-J)<<_epsilon (r/M)x^epsilon.  (6)
