Equations (1), (5), and (6) show that the complete principal contribution at each fixed r is O_epsilon(x^epsilon). There are at most a constant times R possible r, and restricting them to distinct-prime products p ell can only decrease this count. Therefore
 |T_E11^prin|<<_epsilon R x^epsilon,                         (7)
uniformly on one label. The constant marker-copy variation noted above and the polylogarithmic number of literal labels are absorbed into x^epsilon.

Finally the E11 central strip has beta_E<=4/3+6 eta_t, D<=2x^(1/2), and eta_t<kappa_t/20<1/120. Thus
 R=D^(beta_E)<=D^(4/3+6 eta_t)<<x^(2/3+3 eta_t).
Choose epsilon>0 fixed and sufficiently small. Since 2/3+3 eta_t<1, (7) is O(x^(1-delta_prin)) for some fixed delta_prin>0. This proves both assertions and leaves exactly the nonprincipal character family untreated.

glossary.T_E11^prin: The complete principal-character component in the exact cubic-character reconstruction of T_E11^crit.
glossary.delta_prin: A fixed positive exponent saving for the principal E11 character component.

1334e22642cfa30f.title: K-SHIFTED-DIVISOR REINDEXING OF Aadd, ABSOLUTE EQUAL-K PAYMENT, AND THE LITERAL RESIDUAL
1334e22642cfa30f.author: slava chan
1334e22642cfa30f.statement:
K-SHIFTED-DIVISOR REINDEXING OF Aadd, ABSOLUTE EQUAL-K PAYMENT, AND THE LITERAL RESIDUAL.

Fix constants C>=1 and Q>=8. Let real numbers H,V,P,B satisfy
  2<=H<=Q^(1/3),  2<=V<H,  P=QH/V,  B>=1.                 (1)
Let A be a nonzero integer with |A|<=Q^C, and let cal L be a finite label set. For each outer row o=(ell,v,p), where ell belongs to cal L, V<=v<2V is an integer, p is prime in [P,2P), and gcd(v,p)=1, put n_o=vp. Let cal X_o be a finite set of triples x=(q,m,k) satisfying
  Q<=q,m<2Q,  qm+n_o k=A,  gcd(qm,n_o)=1.                  (2)
For each ell let I_ell be an integer interval contained either in [H,2H) or in (-2H,-H]. Let a_{o,h}(x) be complex coefficients satisfying
  |a_{o,h}(x)|<=B.                                         (3)
For x=(q,m,k) put lambda_x=k/q. Define
  Aadd
   =sum_o sum_{h in I_ell}
      sum_{x_1,x_2 in cal X_o,lambda_{x_1} not equal lambda_{x_2}}
       a_{o,h}(x_1)conjugate(a_{o,h}(x_2))
       e(h[lambda_{x_1}-lambda_{x_2}]).                     (4)
This is the same exact phase as the reduced slope t_x/r_x in fact 4b89ec4ce7a7b67a.

For every outer row and integer k define
  D_o(k)=A-n_o k,                                          (5)
  cal Q_o(k)={q in Z:Q<=q<2Q, q divides D_o(k),
       Q<=D_o(k)/q<2Q,
       (q,D_o(k)/q,k) belongs to cal X_o}.                 (6)
For q in cal Q_o(k) put
  b_{o,h}(k,q)=a_{o,h}(q,D_o(k)/q,k).                      (7)
Then there is an exact shifted-divisor expansion
  Aadd
   =sum_o sum_{h in I_ell}
      sum_{k_1,k_2 in Z}
      sum_{q_i in cal Q_o(k_i),
           k_1/q_1 not equal k_2/q_2}
       b_{o,h}(k_1,q_1)conjugate(b_{o,h}(k_2,q_2))
       e(h[k_1/q_1-k_2/q_2]).                              (8)
Every literal source, least-prime, marker, fixed-U, frequency, collision, provenance, and projective mask remains in the membership condition (6) and coefficient (7).

Split (8) as
  Aadd=Aadd^{=k}+Aadd^{not=k},                              (9)
according as k_1=k_2 or k_1 is not equal to k_2. For every epsilon>0,
  |Aadd^{=k}|
   <<_{C,epsilon}B^2(#cal L)Q^(2+epsilon)H
   <<_{C,epsilon}B^2(#cal L)P Q^(5/3+epsilon).             (10)
Consequently, under the subpolynomial coefficient and label hypotheses of fact 4b89ec4ce7a7b67a, its remaining one-sided supplier may be restricted to
  Aadd^{not=k}<<_{C,epsilon}P Q^(5/3+epsilon).             (11)
An absolute-value estimate in (11) is stronger than necessary.

There is a precise limitation of the equal-k deletion for the sufficient local interface in fact 3b2d15db39ad0217. When C>=2, the actual-source family of fact 9e63ab11cf963ef5 has a retained subset cal Y' of cardinality
  #cal Y'>>_epsilon Q^(1-epsilon)/H                        (12)
whose slopes lie in one interval of length at most 1/(12H), are pairwise distinct, and whose source frequencies k are also pairwise distinct. With constant coefficients on cal Y', the complete coherent off-diagonal cluster lies inside Aadd^{not=k}, and its critical-cluster ratio is at least 1/2. Thus deleting the equal-k sector does not imply the sufficient local estimate Theta_cl<<Gadd^(-1)Q^epsilon from source geometry and bounded coefficients alone.

This local observation is not a counterexample to the global residual estimate (11), because one coherent row is below its global target and fact 3b2d15db39ad0217 asserts no necessity or converse. A different global geometric argument for (11) is not excluded. This theorem proves the exact K-shifted-divisor reduction and pays one complete residual sector. It proves no estimate for (11), no PMD closure outside the endpoint strip, and no Goldbach conclusion.
1334e22642cfa30f.proof:
For a source atom x=(q,m,k), equation (2) is equivalent to
  qm=A-n_o k=D_o(k).                                       (13)
Since q and m are positive, D_o(k) is positive. Also q,m<2Q, so
  0<D_o(k)<4Q^2.                                           (14)
Equation (13) implies q divides D_o(k) and m=D_o(k)/q. Conversely, every q in (6) recovers exactly the source atom displayed there. Hence the map
  x=(q,m,k) maps to (k,q)
is a bijection between cal X_o and the pairs indexed by (6). Substitution into (4) proves (8), including every membership condition and coefficient. Fact 1a9cfcfe3eedd5e2 proves k/q=t_x/r_x on the source support, so (4) is exactly the Aadd phase of fact 4b89ec4ce7a7b67a.

We estimate the equal-k sector. Put
  M_o(k)=#cal Q_o(k),  X_o=#cal X_o.                       (15)
By the bijection,
  sum_k M_o(k)=X_o.                                        (16)
Equations (6) and (14) show
  M_o(k)<=tau(D_o(k)).                                     (17)
The divisor bound proved in fact e705401df9f0709e applies to every positive integer below 4Q^2. Thus, for every epsilon>0,
  max_k M_o(k)<<_epsilon Q^epsilon.                        (18)
For fixed o,h, take absolute values only on the k_1=k_2 subdomain of (8). The unequal-slope deletion can only reduce the number of ordered pairs, so (3), (16), and (18) give
  |equal-k contribution at o,h|
  <=B^2 sum_k M_o(k)^2
  <=B^2(max_k M_o(k))X_o
  <<_epsilon B^2Q^epsilon X_o.                           (19)

Here p>=P=QH/V>Q. Fact 914048233fada05f therefore applies and gives
  X_o<<_{C,epsilon}Q^(1+epsilon)/H,                        (20)
because n_o=vp>=VP=QH. Each I_ell contains at most 2H integers, and there are fewer than 4(#cal L)VP outer rows. Sum (19), insert (20), use VP=QH, and distribute a sufficiently small exponent budget:
  |Aadd^{=k}|
  <<B^2(#cal L)(VP)H[Q/H]Q^epsilon
  =B^2(#cal L)Q^(2+epsilon)H.                            (21)
This proves the first bound in (10). Its ratio to the target is
  [Q^2H]/[P Q^(5/3)]
   =[Q^2H]/[(QH/V)Q^(5/3)]
   =V/Q^(2/3)
   <H/Q^(2/3)
   <=Q^(-1/3).                                             (22)
After renaming epsilon, (22) proves the second bound in (10). Equations (9)-(10) show that the one-sided estimate (11) pays the remaining Aadd supplier in fact 4b89ec4ce7a7b67a.

We prove only the stated local limitation. Assume C>=2 and start with the set cal Y in fact 9e63ab11cf963ef5, whose target satisfies A<=Q^2<=Q^C. For fixed k, equation (13) and the divisor bound (17)-(18) show that at most Q^epsilon of its atoms have that source frequency. Choose one atom from every represented k-value and call the result cal Y'. After adjusting epsilon, the cardinality lower bound for cal Y gives (12). Deletion preserves its common critical interval and pairwise distinct slopes, while by construction the k-values are pairwise distinct.

Give cal Y' constant coefficients and use it as one source row. Fact 714f3597f5ef527c shows that its off-diagonal cluster sum is at least one half of the ordered off-diagonal count. Every off-diagonal pair has distinct k-values, so the entire sum belongs to Aadd^{not=k}. Equivalently, adding the diagonal and using fact 3b2d15db39ad0217 gives critical-cluster ratio at least 1/2. Fact 9e63ab11cf963ef5 has Gadd growing as a fixed power, so equal-k deletion does not imply the sufficient local Gadd^(-1) estimate of fact 3b2d15db39ad0217.

The contribution of this single row is not compared with the global scale P Q^(5/3), and no converse to the local interface is used. Therefore the argument proves only the local limitation stated above and leaves open every other possible proof of (11). This proves all assertions and scope qualifications.

glossary.Aadd^{=k}: The part of Aadd whose two source atoms have the same source frequency k.
glossary.Aadd^{not=k}: The part of Aadd whose two source atoms have different source frequencies.
glossary.D_o(k): The shifted source product A-n_o k in outer row o.
glossary.cal Q_o(k): The exact retained set of dyadic divisors q of D_o(k) which recover source atoms.
glossary.cal Y': A retained critical-cluster source subset with pairwise distinct slopes and pairwise distinct source frequencies.

134b03fc362a7cf1.title: EXACT OFF-RAY RAY-C4-K2 QUADRATIC OPERATOR AFTER PRIMITIVE-RAY GROUPING. Fix a finite nonempty family Lambdacal. For every lambda in Lambdacal let
134b03fc362a7cf1.author: slava chan
134b03fc362a7cf1.statement:
EXACT OFF-RAY RAY-C4-K2 QUADRATIC OPERATOR AFTER PRIMITIVE-RAY GROUPING. Fix a finite nonempty family Lambdacal. For every lambda in Lambdacal let
D_lambda=p_{lambda,1}p_{lambda,2}p_{lambda,3}p_{lambda,4}
be a product of four distinct odd primes, let v_lambda be positive and squarefree with gcd(D_lambda,v_lambda)=1, and put n_lambda=D_lambda v_lambda. Fix a common nonzero integer A. Let Zcal be a finite nonempty common row space. For every lambda and every supported pair q>0,h!=0, let c_lambda(q,h;z) be complex and linear in z in C^{Zcal}; it may include all literal amplitudes, source weights and masks. Assume it vanishes unless
gcd(q,D_lambda v_lambda)=1 and gcd(Ah,D_lambda)=1.                  (1)

For a primitive ray rho=(epsilon,a,b), where epsilon in {+1,-1}, a,b>0 and gcd(a,b)=1, define
B_lambda(rho;z)
=sum_{kappa>=1}
 c_lambda(kappa a,epsilon kappa b;z)
 mu(kappa a)^2 1_{gcd(kappa a,D_lambda v_lambda)=1},                (2)
restricted to the original finite support. Let
K_lambda(rho)=K_{2,D_lambda,v_lambda}^{full}(epsilon,a,b)           (3)
be the kernel of fact 34d306bcb630f9df, put
F_lambda(rho;z)=B_lambda(rho;z)K_lambda(rho),                       (4)
and
T_lambda(z)=sum_rho F_lambda(rho;z).                                (5)

For rho=(epsilon,a,b), rho'=(epsilon',a',b') define
delta(rho,rho')=epsilon b a'-epsilon'b'a.                           (6)
For supported scales kappa,kappa',
Delta=(epsilon kappa b)(kappa'a')-(epsilon'kappa'b')(kappa a)
=kappa kappa' delta(rho,rho').                                     (7)
The gates give gcd(kappa kappa',D_lambda)=1. Therefore
Delta=0 if and only if rho=rho',                                   (8)
D_lambda divides A Delta if and only if
D_lambda divides A delta(rho,rho').                                (9)
Thus
D_lambda^{ray}(z)=sum_rho|F_lambda(rho;z)|^2,                       (10)
R_lambda^{FR}(z)
=sum_{rho!=rho'; D_lambda divides A delta(rho,rho')}
 F_lambda(rho;z)overline{F_lambda(rho';z)},                         (11)
R_lambda^{off}(z)
=sum_{rho!=rho'; D_lambda does not divide A delta(rho,rho')}
 F_lambda(rho;z)overline{F_lambda(rho';z)}                          (12)
form the exact disjoint trichotomy
|T_lambda(z)|^2
=D_lambda^{ray}(z)+R_lambda^{FR}(z)+R_lambda^{off}(z).              (13)
The first term is the primitive-ray form of the Delta=0 sector and the second is the primitive-ray form of the nonzero fully resonant sector. These are the two sector types absolutely paid in the full literal marked-dilator moment by fact 54029717e980dcb7. Equation (12) is the scoped genuinely nonresonant cross-primitive-ray remainder.

For real weights theta_lambda define
RAY-C4-K2(z)=sum_lambda theta_lambda R_lambda^{off}(z).              (14)
For each lambda,rho let L_{lambda,rho}:C^{Zcal}->C be z mapsto F_lambda(rho;z). Then
RAY-C4-K2(z)=<z,Rcal_{K2}z>,                                       (15)
where
Rcal_{K2}
=sum_lambda theta_lambda
 sum_{rho!=rho'; D_lambda does not divide A delta(rho,rho')}
 L_{lambda,rho}^*L_{lambda,rho'}                                  (16)
is self-adjoint, and
sup_{||z||_2=1}|RAY-C4-K2(z)|=||Rcal_{K2}||_{op}.                  (17)
Equations (14)-(17), with literal c_lambda and varying v_lambda retained, are the exact scoped off-ray common-row interface and take no pairwise absolute values. Restricting to b=1 gives only the primitive-frequency-one submatrix. No bound for (16), no assertion that the six faces equal the complete centered-face synthesis, no transfer of fact 540's numerical bounds to an altered coefficient family, no shared-prime aggregation, C4 estimate, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
134b03fc362a7cf1.proof:
Fact 34d306bcb630f9df proves that on q=kappa a, h=epsilon kappa b the exact rough and small-v phases and the six primitive semiprime siblings are independent of kappa, while every amplitude, mask and the gate in (2) remain in the scale sum. Grouping the finite physical sum by its unique primitive ray proves (2)-(5).

Substitution proves (7). If rho=rho' then delta=0. Conversely, delta=0 forces epsilon=epsilon' and ba'=b'a; the two coprimality conditions give a=a', b=b'. This proves (8). Every nonzero term has gcd(kappa kappa',D_lambda)=1. Multiplication or division by this unit in (7) proves (9) without a unit hypothesis on A.

Expand (5). By (8), diagonal ray pairs give (10). Every off-diagonal pair lies in exactly one of the complementary divisibility classes (11)-(12), proving (13). Fact 54029717e980dcb7 defines the full literal sectors by Delta=0 and by Delta!=0 with D_lambda dividing A Delta; equations (8)-(9) identify their ray labels. The statement does not transfer that fact's numerical estimates to another coefficient family.

The maps L_{lambda,rho} are linear by (2)-(4). With inner products linear in the first variable,
F_lambda(rho;z)overline{F_lambda(rho';z)}
=<z,L_{lambda,rho}^*L_{lambda,rho'}z>.                              (18)
Sum (18) over (12) and lambda to obtain (15)-(16). The ordered-pair conditions are invariant under interchanging rho,rho'. Hence the adjoint of every term in (16) also occurs with the same real theta_lambda, so Rcal_{K2} is self-adjoint. The largest absolute Rayleigh quotient of a finite-dimensional self-adjoint operator is its operator norm, proving (17). Restricting b=1 deletes all other rays and is only a submatrix. This proves all assertions.

glossary.B_lambda: the exact scale sum along one primitive ray with all literal gates and coefficients retained
glossary.RAY-C4-K2: the signed off-ray common-row quadratic form for the scoped six-face kernel
glossary.Rcal_{K2}: the self-adjoint row-space operator representing RAY-C4-K2
glossary.delta(rho,rho'): the determinant of two primitive ray directions

13cb8b02b12d19bc.title: SHARP EFFECTIVE-EXPONENT LOCALIZATION OF THE LITERAL C1 R3 WIDTH FAILURES. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, eta=kappa/20, and s=kappa/100, and let beta_m<=beta<6/5. In the literal strict-top C1 setting let n=pv be squarefree, where p is the unique rough prime, gcd(p,v)=1, and every prime divisor of v is at most L_0=Q^(beta-1+sigma). Put C=mathscr A h, m_eff=n/gcd(C,n), and assume Q^(1/2+kappa)<=m_eff<=Q^(6/5). Write t=log(m_eff)/log(Q). In an applicable MULTI-FREE box of fact 8eb30e55bdef6b27 let B_* be the largest omitted coefficient-one scale and put X_A=max{Q^(4s),m_eff Q^(2s)/B_*} and Y_A=B_*^2Q^(-4s). Assume X_A<=Y_A and that [X_A,Y_A] contains no divisor of m_eff. Define the following disjoint ordered alternatives: (G1) B_*^2<L_0Q^(8s); (G2) B_*^2>=L_0Q^(8s) and B_*^3<L_0m_eff Q^(6s); (G3) B_*^2>=L_0Q^(8s), B_*^3>=L_0m_eff Q^(6s), p does not divide C, and, with r_eff=m_eff/p, one has r_eff<X_A. Fix zeta>0. For all sufficiently large Q: (i) (G1) is empty when t>=11/20+89kappa/400+zeta. (ii) (G2) is empty when 16/25+127kappa/500+zeta<=t<=28/25-97kappa/250-zeta. Consequently, throughout the latter interval every such genuine divisor-gap box belongs to (G3). Thus the two interval-width failures are confined to explicit lower and upper effective-exponent edge regions. This is a structural localization and does not estimate (G3) or the edge regions
13cb8b02b12d19bc.author: slava chan
13cb8b02b12d19bc.statement: SHARP EFFECTIVE-EXPONENT LOCALIZATION OF THE LITERAL C1 R3 WIDTH FAILURES. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, eta=kappa/20, and s=kappa/100, and let beta_m<=beta<6/5. In the literal strict-top C1 setting let n=pv be squarefree, where p is the unique rough prime, gcd(p,v)=1, and every prime divisor of v is at most L_0=Q^(beta-1+sigma). Put C=mathscr A h, m_eff=n/gcd(C,n), and assume Q^(1/2+kappa)<=m_eff<=Q^(6/5). Write t=log(m_eff)/log(Q). In an applicable MULTI-FREE box of fact 8eb30e55bdef6b27 let B_* be the largest omitted coefficient-one scale and put X_A=max{Q^(4s),m_eff Q^(2s)/B_*} and Y_A=B_*^2Q^(-4s). Assume X_A<=Y_A and that [X_A,Y_A] contains no divisor of m_eff. Define the following disjoint ordered alternatives: (G1) B_*^2<L_0Q^(8s); (G2) B_*^2>=L_0Q^(8s) and B_*^3<L_0m_eff Q^(6s); (G3) B_*^2>=L_0Q^(8s), B_*^3>=L_0m_eff Q^(6s), p does not divide C, and, with r_eff=m_eff/p, one has r_eff<X_A. Fix zeta>0. For all sufficiently large Q: (i) (G1) is empty when t>=11/20+89kappa/400+zeta. (ii) (G2) is empty when 16/25+127kappa/500+zeta<=t<=28/25-97kappa/250-zeta. Consequently, throughout the latter interval every such genuine divisor-gap box belongs to (G3). Thus the two interval-width failures are confined to explicit lower and upper effective-exponent edge regions. This is a structural localization and does not estimate (G3) or the edge regions.
13cb8b02b12d19bc.proof:
Use the routing exponents a,b of fact 8eb30e55bdef6b27 and put d=b-a. Fact 8f9c29373de3486c proves that every displayed MULTI-FREE box satisfies
B_*>Q^(d-o(1)),                                                  (1)
and
 d=2t-1-8eta                 for 1/2+kappa<=t<=2/3,
 d=t/2-8eta                  for 2/3<=t<=1+2eta,
 d=1-t/2-6eta                for 1+2eta<=t<=6/5.                (2)
Also beta<6/5 gives
L_0<Q^(1/5+sigma).                                               (3)

Alternative (G1) requires B_*^2<L_0Q^(8s). By (1)-(3), this is impossible with fixed slack whenever
2d>1/5+sigma+8s.                                                 (4)
On the first piece of (2), condition (4) is
4t-2-16eta>1/5+sigma+8s,
or
t>11/20+(16eta+sigma+8s)/4
 =11/20+89kappa/400.                                             (5)
At t=2/3 the left side of (4) already exceeds its right side for kappa<=1/100, and the second and third formulas in (2) keep 2d uniformly above the right side throughout their ranges. Therefore the extra fixed margin zeta in (5) absorbs the o(1) in (1) and proves (i).

Alternative (G2) requires B_*^3<L_0m_eff Q^(6s). By (1)-(3), it is impossible with fixed slack whenever
3d>t+1/5+sigma+6s.                                               (6)
On the first piece of (2), condition (6) becomes
5t>16/5+24eta+sigma+6s,
or
t>16/25+(24eta+sigma+6s)/5
 =16/25+127kappa/500.                                            (7)
On the second piece of (2), the difference between the two sides of (6) is
t/2-1/5-24eta-sigma-6s.
It is positive uniformly because t>=2/3 and 24eta+sigma+6s=127kappa/100<=127/10000<2/15. On the third piece, condition (6) becomes
14/5-(5/2)t-18eta-sigma-6s>0,
or
t<28/25-(18eta+sigma+6s)/(5/2)
 =28/25-97kappa/250.                                             (8)
The fixed zeta margins in (7)-(8) again absorb the o(1) in (1), proving (ii).

Fact 0437c7a25bf0c1c5 proves under the fully displayed hypotheses that the genuine divisor-gap class is the disjoint union of exactly (G1),(G2),(G3). The lower endpoint in (ii) exceeds the endpoint in (i) for the allowed kappa and any common sufficiently small positive zeta; if the interval is empty the consequence is vacuous. Hence on every nonempty part of the interval in (ii), both (G1) and (G2) are absent and only (G3) remains. No analytic estimate was used.

glossary.X_A: The lower endpoint max{Q^(4s),m_eff Q^(2s)/B_*} of the fixed-slack A-process divisor interval.
glossary.Y_A: The upper endpoint B_*^2Q^(-4s) of the fixed-slack A-process divisor interval.

14fe68fdcbfd99ff.title: EXACT PRIMEWISE-CENTERED ROW PRODUCT FOR THE COMPLETE FOUR-FACE HIGH-CONDUCTOR MZB ENERGY
14fe68fdcbfd99ff.author: slava chan
14fe68fdcbfd99ff.statement:
EXACT PRIMEWISE-CENTERED ROW PRODUCT FOR THE COMPLETE FOUR-FACE HIGH-CONDUCTOR MZB ENERGY.

Assume the actual high-conductor tensor, squarefree moduli, and notation of facts 050efa07f87f374a and 2e80012db28da736. Thus b asymp B is squarefree, a asymp Q, and F_0=x^(1/2-eta) with 0<eta<1/12.

For f|b with (f,N)=1 and (a,b)=1 define
R_{b,f}(a)=product_{p|f}[e_p(N[a(b/p)]^(-1))+1/(p-1)],       (1)
S_{b,f}(alpha)=sum_{a asymp Q;(a,b)=1}alpha_a R_{b,f}(a).    (2)
Then
Pi_{b,>F_0}(a)
 =sum_{f|b;f>F_0,(f,N)=1}
   c_{b/f}(N)R_{b,f}(a)/phi(b/f),                            (3)
and
E_{>F_0}(alpha)
 =sum_{b asymp B;b squarefree}
  |sum_{f|b;f>F_0,(f,N)=1}
    c_{b/f}(N)S_{b,f}(alpha)/phi(b/f)|^2.                   (4)

For every p|f, after fixing a unit residue class modulo b/p, the sum of R_{b,f}(a) over the p-1 unit lifts modulo p is zero.

For a conductor pair write
f_1=dr_1, f_2=dr_2, b=dr_1r_2t.
The complete row-product coefficient is
W(d,r_1,r_2,t)
 =mu(r_1)mu(r_2)c_t(N)^2/
  [phi(r_1)phi(r_2)phi(t)^2].                               (5)
Therefore
E_{>F_0}(alpha)
 =sum_{d,r_1,r_2,t}^{*}
   W(d,r_1,r_2,t)
   S_{b,dr_1}(alpha)overline(S_{b,dr_2}(alpha)),             (6)
where b=dr_1r_2t and the star retains pairwise coprime squarefree d,r_1,r_2,t, b asymp B, dr_i>F_0, and (dr_1r_2,N)=1.

The exact unequal-a crossed energy is
E_cross
 =sum_{d,r_1,r_2,t}^{*}W(d,r_1,r_2,t)
  [S_{b,dr_1}(alpha)overline(S_{b,dr_2}(alpha))
   -D_{b;dr_1,dr_2}(alpha)],                                (7)
where
D_{b;f_1,f_2}(alpha)
 =sum_{a asymp Q;(a,b)=1}
   |alpha_a|^2R_{b,f_1}(a)overline(R_{b,f_2}(a)).             (8)

For q|b define
A_{b,q}(alpha)
 =sum_{a asymp Q;(a,b)=1}
   alpha_a e_q(Na^(-1)(b/q)^(-1)),                           (9)
with inverses modulo q and A_{b,1} untwisted. For every active f in (3),
S_{b,f}(alpha)=sum_{q|f}A_{b,q}(alpha)/phi(f/q).             (10)
For q_1|dr_1 and q_2|dr_2 in this active expansion there are unique pairwise coprime squarefree factors
d=d_0d_1d_2d_{12}, u_1|r_1, u_2|r_2
such that
q_1=d_1d_{12}u_1, q_2=d_2d_{12}u_2.                         (11)
Then (q_1,q_2)=d_{12}, and
S_{b,dr_1}(alpha)overline(S_{b,dr_2}(alpha))
 =
sum_{d_0d_1d_2d_{12}=d}^{pairwise}
 sum_{u_1|r_1,u_2|r_2}
 A_{b,d_1d_{12}u_1}(alpha)
 overline(A_{b,d_2d_{12}u_2}(alpha))
 /
 [phi(d_0)^2phi(d_1)phi(d_2)
  phi(r_1/u_1)phi(r_2/u_2)].                                (12)
Thus (5) and (12) retain shared b, common selected response d_{12}, the signed Ramanujan simplification, every proper common-core face, and every residual response.

Every q occurring in (10)-(12) divides an active f with (f,N)=1, hence (q,N)=1. For p|q, the unnormalized sum of the local Fourier phase inside A_{b,q} over the p-1 unit residues is -1, equivalently its normalized mean is -1/(p-1). Hence a single active Fourier-subset phase term is not locally centered. Centering belongs to the complete recombination (10). A termwise treatment of one face or one fixed active q_1,q_2 pair is not an exact replacement for (4) unless all correction terms in (12) are restored.

The minimal complete centered estimate is
sum_{b asymp B;b squarefree}
 |sum_{f|b;f>F_0,(f,N)=1}
   c_{b/f}(N)S_{b,f}(alpha)/phi(b/f)|^2
 <<Q^(8/3-omega)                                             (CEN-MZB)
for some fixed omega>0 and every actual tensor alpha. It is exactly MZB-ENERGY. No bound for CEN-MZB, remaining off-diagonal rows, or C_small is asserted, and no closure is claimed.
14fe68fdcbfd99ff.proof:
Fact 2e80012db28da736 gives Pi as phi(b)^(-1) times the sum of c_{b/f}(N)overline(K_f(b;a)) over active f. For squarefree b,
overline(K_f(b;a))
 =product_{p|f}[1+(p-1)e_p(N[a(b/p)]^(-1))]
 =phi(f)R_{b,f}(a).                                         (13)
Since phi(b)=phi(f)phi(b/f), this proves (3), and then (4).

Fix p|f and all CRT coordinates of a modulo b/p. Since (f,N)=1, N(b/p)^(-1) is nonzero modulo p. Inversion permutes the units, so the local phase sum is -1; adding p-1 copies of 1/(p-1) gives zero. This proves local centering.

Expanding (4), use f_1=dr_1,f_2=dr_2,b=dr_1r_2t. Multiplicativity and (r_1r_2,N)=1 give
[c_{r_2t}(N)/phi(r_2t)]
[c_{r_1t}(N)/phi(r_1t)]
 =mu(r_1)mu(r_2)c_t(N)^2/
  [phi(r_1)phi(r_2)phi(t)^2].
This proves (5)-(6). The equal-a part of the row product is (8), so deleting it proves (7).

Expand (1) by choosing the exponential at primes in q and 1/(p-1) at primes in f/q. Squarefree CRT gives
product_{p|q}e_p(N[a(b/p)]^(-1))
 =e_q(Na^(-1)(b/q)^(-1)),                                   (14)
so (10) follows. Partition primes of d by membership in q_1,q_2 and put u_i=(q_i,r_i), proving unique (11). Since
dr_1/q_1=d_0d_2(r_1/u_1), dr_2/q_2=d_0d_1(r_2/u_2),
the coefficients in (10) multiply to the denominator in (12).

In (10)-(12), q divides an active f and therefore (q,N)=1. Applying the same unit calculation to the local phase in (14) gives sum -1 and normalized mean -1/(p-1), proving the scoped non-centering warning. Finally (3) identifies CEN-MZB with fact 050efa07f87f374a's energy.

glossary.CEN-MZB: The exact primewise-centered formulation of MZB-ENERGY.

152484e836f90c47.title: EXACT MOVING-ENDPOINT ACTUAL-\(Z_{\rm mid}\) POISSON TRANSFER AND BOUNDARY-OPERATOR LEDGER
152484e836f90c47.author: slava chan
152484e836f90c47.statement:
EXACT MOVING-ENDPOINT ACTUAL-\(Z_{\rm mid}\) POISSON TRANSFER AND BOUNDARY-OPERATOR LEDGER.

Fix one selected forced-high forward literal source label and one exact outer-gcd layer from facts \(60b26a9b6f79467a\), \(77d7a3419a07305c\), and \(7131a06664967733\). Thus
\[
 d=ga,\qquad r=gb,\qquad (a,b)=1,\qquad L=N/g,\qquad am+bk=L,
\]
\(R>D\), \(DM\asymp x\), \(RK\asymp x\), \(R>x^{9/16-\kappa _0}\), and every nonzero source atom has \(\mu(ga)\mu(gb)\ne0\). Put
\[
 k(t)=\frac{L-at}{b},\qquad
 \ell_{g,a,b}=\frac{L-gb^2}{a},\qquad
 u_{g,a,b}=\frac{L-b\sqrt{gb}}{a}.                         \tag{1}
\]
Let \(F_{g,a,b}\) and its Fourier convention be exactly those of fact \(d8ba46800ba433c2\). All literal smooth and logarithmic source factors are retained in \(F_{g,a,b}\); Möbius, fixed-\(U\), high, parent, tag, provenance, and other arithmetic selectors remain unchanged as coefficient factors or index restrictions and are not differentiated. Define
\[
 F^{\rm mid}_{g,a,b}(t)
 =F_{g,a,b}(t)\mathbf 1_{\ell_{g,a,b}<t<u_{g,a,b}}.
\]

For every real \(t\) with \(k(t)>0\),
\[
 k(t)<gb<k(t)^2
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \ell_{g,a,b}<t<u_{g,a,b}.                                  \tag{2}
\]
The interval in (2) is nonempty whenever it carries an actual \(Z_{\rm mid}\) incidence.

For every nonzero integer \(h\), the restricted Fourier-Poisson coefficient is
\[
 C^{\rm mid}_{g,a,b,h}
 =b^{-1}e_b(hL\bar a)
   \int_{\ell_{g,a,b}}^{u_{g,a,b}}
   F_{g,a,b}(t)e(-ht/b)\,dt,                                \tag{3}
\]
where \(\bar a\) is the inverse of \(a\) modulo \(b\). If \(\bar b\) is the inverse of \(b\) modulo \(a\), additive reciprocity and one integration by parts give the exact identity
\[
\begin{aligned}
 C^{\rm mid}_{g,a,b,h}
 =\frac{e_a(-Lh\bar b)}{2\pi i h}
 \bigg(&F_{g,a,b}(\ell_{g,a,b})e_a(hgb)\\
       &-F_{g,a,b}(u_{g,a,b})
          e\!\left(\frac{h\sqrt{gb}}a\right)\\
       &+\int_{\ell_{g,a,b}}^{u_{g,a,b}}
          F'_{g,a,b}(t)e\!\left(\frac{hk(t)}a\right)dt
 \bigg).                                                     \tag{4}
\end{aligned}
\]
On every sufficiently large selected forced-high label,
\[
 F_{g,a,b}(\ell_{g,a,b})=0.                                 \tag{5}
\]

The exact strict-open arithmetic reconstruction is understood as a Fejer, equivalently first Cesaro, limit of symmetric frequency sums. With
\[
 \widehat F^{\rm mid}(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R}F^{\rm mid}_{g,a,b}(t)e(-\xi t)dt
\]
and \(c\equiv L\bar a\pmod b\), one has
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sum_{\substack{n\in\mathbb Z\\n\equiv c\ ({\rm mod}\ b)\\
                   \ell_{g,a,b}<n<u_{g,a,b}}}F_{g,a,b}(n)
 =
 \lim_{H\to\infty}\frac1b
 \sum_{|h|\le H}\left(1-\frac{|h|}{H+1}\right)
 e_b(hc)\widehat F^{\rm mid}(h/b).                          \tag{6}
\end{aligned}
\]
There is no endpoint half-weight in (6): the lower endpoint has weight zero by (5), and the upper endpoint is not a source progression point. Hence the only potentially nonzero hard Fourier face in (4) is
\[
 -\frac{F_{g,a,b}(u_{g,a,b})}{2\pi i h}
 e_a(-Lh\bar b)
 e\!\left(\frac{h\sqrt{gb}}a\right).                     \tag{7}
\]
It may vanish when the upper endpoint lies outside the smooth support. Uniformly in all retained arithmetic masks,
\[
 |C^{\rm mid}_{g,a,b,h}|
 \ll \frac{(\log x)^2}{|h|}.                               \tag{8}
\]
Thus direct rapid-decay estimates for a complete smooth parent do not apply to the hard deletion; the universal statement furnished here is the upper bound (8), not a nonzero asymptotic \(1/|h|\) term.

There is also an exact smooth-interior/boundary-strip decomposition. Fix a smooth function \(\chi\) with \(\chi(s)=0\) for \(s\le0\) and \(\chi(s)=1\) for \(s\ge1\). For
\[
 0<\Delta\le\frac{u_{g,a,b}-\ell_{g,a,b}}2
\]
put
\[
 I_\Delta(t)
 =\chi\!\left(\frac{t-\ell_{g,a,b}}\Delta\right)
  \chi\!\left(\frac{u_{g,a,b}-t}\Delta\right),\qquad
 R_\Delta(t)=\mathbf1_{\ell_{g,a,b}<t<u_{g,a,b}}-I_\Delta(t).
                                                                    \tag{9}
\]
Then
\[
 F^{\rm mid}_{g,a,b}=F_{g,a,b}I_\Delta+F_{g,a,b}R_\Delta          \tag{10}
\]
exactly, \(R_\Delta\) is supported on two strips of total \(t\)-length at most \(2\Delta\), and
\[
 \left|b^{-1}\int F_{g,a,b}(t)R_\Delta(t)e(-ht/b)dt\right|
 \ll \frac{\Delta(\log x)^2}{b}.                              \tag{11}
\]
Writing \(T_\Delta=1+M/\Delta\), every scaled derivative of total order at most \(J\) in the three moving coordinates \(a/Q,b/B,t/M\) of the smooth interior is
\[
 \ll_J(\log x)^2T_\Delta^J.                                  \tag{12}
\]
Consequently a standard three-coordinate Fourier tensor separation using \(J>1\) integrations in each coordinate may be taken with projective coefficient \(\ell^1\)-norm
\[
 \ll_J(\log x)^2T_\Delta^{3J}.                               \tag{13}
\]
The identities (9)--(13) do not remove the literal boundary strips; decreasing \(\Delta\) makes (11) smaller while increasing the derivative/projective tax in (12)--(13).

No complete-parent \(g\)-, \(h\)-, tail-, anatomy-, or source-deletion estimate is transported through the hard mask. No endpoint capture, \(C2\) selection, terminal conclusion, four-prime equivalence, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
152484e836f90c47.proof:
Put \(r=gb\). Since \(k(t)>0\), the inequality \(r<k(t)^2\) is equivalent to \(\sqrt r<k(t)\). Thus the actual-\(Z_{\rm mid}\) condition is
\[
 \sqrt{gb}<\frac{L-at}{b}<gb.
\]
Because \(a,b>0\), the right inequality is equivalent to
\(t>(L-gb^2)/a\), and the left inequality is equivalent to
\(t<(L-b\sqrt{gb})/a\). This proves (2). Also
\[
 u_{g,a,b}-\ell_{g,a,b}
 =\frac{b\sqrt{gb}(\sqrt{gb}-1)}a>0
\]
whenever \(gb>1\), as holds on the selected forced-high support.

For fixed \(g,a,b\), the equation \(am+bk=L\) says
\(m\equiv L\bar a\pmod b\). Formula (3) is the Fourier coefficient of the literal source amplitude restricted by (2).

The reciprocity identity
\[
 e_b(hL\bar a)=e(hL/(ab))e_a(-hL\bar b)
\]
holds because \((a,b)=1\). Since \(k(t)=(L-at)/b\), it gives
\[
 e_b(hL\bar a)e(-ht/b)
 =e_a(-hL\bar b)e(hk(t)/a).                                 \tag{14}
\]
For \(h\ne0\), integration by parts gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 b^{-1}e_b(hL\bar a)
 \int_\ell^u F(t)e(-ht/b)dt
 =\frac{e_b(hL\bar a)}{2\pi ih}
 \left(F(\ell)e(-h\ell/b)-F(u)e(-hu/b)
       +\int_\ell^u F'(t)e(-ht/b)dt\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
At \(t=\ell\), \(k(t)=gb\); at \(t=u\), \(k(t)=\sqrt{gb}\). Apply (14) to the two boundary values and to the integral. This proves (4).

We prove (5). On a source dyadic support, \(r=gb\ge R/2\). The relation \(RK\asymp x\) gives \(K\ll x/R\), while
\(R>x^{9/16-\kappa _0}\) and \(\kappa _0=1/200\). Hence
\[
 \frac rK\gg\frac{R^2}{x}
 >x^{1/8-2\kappa _0}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Thus \(r>2K\) for sufficiently large \(x\). But
\(k(\ell)=r\), whereas the literal amplitude is supported where
\(k/K\in[1/2,2]\). Therefore \(F(\ell)=0\).

We justify (6) and its endpoint assertion. Periodize the bounded-variation compactly supported function
\(F^{\rm mid}\) on the progression \(c+b\mathbb Z\). Fejer's theorem says that the first Cesaro means of its symmetric Fourier series converge at every point to the average of its two one-sided limits. Summing over the finitely many progression points meeting the compact support gives the right side of (6), plus one half of \(F(\ell)\) if \(\ell\) is a progression point and one half of \(F(u)\) if \(u\) is a progression point. The first possible correction is zero by (5). If \(u\) were a progression point, the corresponding value \(k(u)=\sqrt r\) would be an integer, so \(r\) would be a perfect square. The literal source has \(\mu(r)\ne0\), hence \(r\) is squarefree, and forced high gives \(r>1\). A squarefree integer greater than one is not a square. Thus the upper correction is absent. This proves (6) and (7), with the stated possibility that its amplitude vanishes.

Scaled smoothness of \(F\) gives
\[
 \sup_t|F(t)|\ll(\log x)^2,qquad
 \int_{\mathbb R}|F'(t)|dt\ll(\log x)^2.
\]
Insert these bounds in (4) to prove (8).

The definition of \(\chi\) shows pointwise that \(I_\Delta\) vanishes outside \((\ell,u)\), equals one on
\([\ell+\Delta,u-\Delta]\), and differs from the open-interval indicator only in
\((\ell,\ell+\Delta)\cup(u-\Delta,u)\). This proves (10), the support claim, and (11).

We prove (12) separately on the two transition supports. The source scales give
\[
 L/a\asymp (N/g)/(D/g)\asymp M.                              \tag{15}
\]
On the lower transition there is a point \(t\asymp M\) with
\(0<t-\ell<\Delta\), so
\[
 |\ell|\ll M+\Delta.
\]
Every fixed-order derivative of
\(\ell=L/a-gb^2/a\) under \(a\partial_a\) and \(b\partial_b\) is a fixed linear combination of \(\ell\) and \(L/a\). By (15), its absolute value divided by \(\Delta\) is therefore
\[
 \ll 1+M/\Delta=T_\Delta.
\]
On the upper transition, \(0<u-t<\Delta\) and
\[
 0<u=L/a-\sqrt g\,b^{3/2}/a\le L/a\ll M.
\]
Every fixed-order scaled \(a,b\) derivative of \(u\) is a fixed linear combination of \(u\) and \(L/a\), so its absolute value divided by \(\Delta\) is \(\ll M/\Delta\le T_\Delta\). Derivatives in \(t/M\) have the same cost. The arithmetic masks remain coefficient factors or index restrictions and are not differentiated. Applying the product and chain rules to the two smooth transitions and the original scaled-smooth amplitude proves (12).

Finally Fourier-expand the compactly supported smooth interior in the three normalized coordinates. Integrating by parts \(J>1\) times in each coordinate makes the Fourier coefficients bounded by a constant times
\((\log x)^2T_\Delta^{3J}\) times the product of three summable sequences
\((1+|n_j|)^{-J}\). Summation proves (13). No step estimates the remaining hard strips or transports any complete-parent deletion theorem, which proves the scope statements.

glossary.C^{mid}_{g,a,b,h}: The h-th Poisson coefficient of the actual-Z_mid restricted source, including its original additive phase and Poisson prefactor.
glossary.F^{mid}_{g,a,b}: The literal one-variable source amplitude F_{g,a,b} restricted to the open moving interval (ell_{g,a,b},u_{g,a,b}).
glossary.I_Delta: A smooth interior cutoff at physical distance Delta from both moving endpoints.
glossary.Z_mid: The actual sibling cell k<r<k^2 from fact aa34b1862b993377.
glossary.e(z): The additive character exp(2 pi i z).
glossary.ell_{g,a,b}: The lower moving t-endpoint (L-gb^2)/a for the actual Z_mid selector.
glossary.u_{g,a,b}: The upper moving t-endpoint (L-b sqrt(gb))/a for the actual Z_mid selector.

15425579cb248eff.title: POST-LOW-BETA GLOBAL COVERAGE LEDGER AND FIRST OPEN CELL
15425579cb248eff.author: slava chan
15425579cb248eff.statement:
POST-LOW-BETA GLOBAL COVERAGE LEDGER AND FIRST OPEN CELL.

Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, fix 0<eta<sigma, and put
beta_0=6/5-2kappa,   beta_m=6/5-12sigma/5.
Work only with the literal paired nonzero-Poisson high-source atoms and exact parent/normalized-marker partition of facts 60b26a9b6f79467a, 77d7a3419a07305c, and a71f777ad842c886. Retain every original source, high-label, parent, fixed-U, smooth/projective, Fourier, target-gcd, prime-order, collision, deletion, and exact outer-gcd label. Assume the physical source bounds used in the forward and reverse assembly theorems: in a forward orientation R>D one has
c_1 x<=DM<=C_1 x,  c_D x^(1/2)(log x)^(-A_D)<=D<=C_D x^(1/2),
and in a reverse orientation D>R one has
c_1 x<=RK<=C_1 x,  c_R x^(1/2)(log x)^(-A_R)<=R<=C_R x^(1/2),
with fixed positive constants, while all physical scales are O(x). In both orientations impose the forced-high condition that the larger divisor scale exceeds x^(9/16-kappa_0), kappa_0=1/200.

For an exact outer gcd g=(d,r), put in the forward orientation
Q=D/g, B=R/g, beta=log B/log Q, G_f=M/Q,
and in the reverse orientation
Q=R/g, B=D/g, beta=log B/log Q, G_r=K/Q,
whenever Q>1. Then the following ledger holds.

(A) Equal-scale and bounded-base cells. Every active label with D=R is 60-controlled for sufficiently large x and therefore contributes no atom to the 60-residual high family. For every fixed Q_0, the complete paired nonzero-Poisson mass of all exact-g layers with 0<Q<=Q_0 is O(x^(1/2+epsilon)) after all such g and the polylogarithmically many source labels are summed, in either orientation. Thus bounded or nonpositive-logarithmic normalized bases are power-small before any reciprocal trace is used.

(B) Original versus normalized beta and parents. In a strict orientation with Q>1,
1<=beta_orig<=beta,
where beta_orig=log R/log D forward and beta_orig=log D/log R reverse. Hence throughout beta<4/3 the only possible frozen parents are C91,U_sh,U_low; the endpoint parents E_11,E_21,E_22,E_asym and the nonendpoint parents U_gap,U_sup are empty. This conclusion is about the original parent label, while beta is always the normalized exponent; no identification of the two exponents is made.

(C) All actual G in the proved low-beta range. On every forward physical source layer,
G_f=gM/D>=c_1/C_D^2,
and on every reverse physical source layer,
G_r=gK/R>=c_1/C_R^2.
Consequently, for sufficiently large Q the formal range
0<G<Q^(-sigma+eta)
is empty on the actual source. Every actual G<1 lies in
Q^(-sigma+eta)<=G<1<Q^(sigma-eta)
and is power-small by fc328dd4cfe6679c forward or 15a95f602f1add2d reverse. Every actual G>=1 is power-small by c6a3ee810402825f forward or 65b10e9a052e9479 reverse. Therefore every strict forward and reverse high-source atom with
Q>1, 1<=beta<=beta_0, and any actual G>0
is power-small after summing every exact g|N. This includes all three surviving parent masks C91,U_sh,U_low, all standard leaves C0,A,B,C1,C2,C3, H_P<1, all Fourier blocks, and every target-gcd layer. No outer-g layer is omitted. For large Q the standard C0 cell is empty; its bounded-base complement is already included in (A).

(D) Disjoint post-low-beta residual. Restrict for this paragraph to beta_0<beta<6/5, so endpoint parents are still empty by (B). The normalized exact identity gives a disjoint exhaustive decomposition by
orientation in {forward,reverse},
parent in {C91,U_sh,U_low},
normalized anatomy, and G.
For beta_0<beta<beta_m the standard cutoffs
L=Q^(beta-1+sigma), S_0=Q^(2beta-2+3sigma),
Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma)
satisfy the hypotheses of the five-way marker identity, so the anatomy list is exactly C0,A,B,C1,C2,C3. The C0 cell is empty for large Q because
B/S_0=Q^(2-beta-3sigma) tends to infinity. For beta_m<=beta<6/5 the exact general normalized identity of a71f777ad842c886 remains exhaustive with anatomy C0,A,B,C1,...,C_{J_max}, but the standard three-rough-prime truncation is not asserted.

For a fixed omega>0 define
Gamma_BC(beta)=max(0,(19beta-20)/17).
The fixed-g Poisson estimate of 7131a06664967733, together with forced high, pays every parent/anatomy family with
G>=Q^(Gamma_BC(beta)+omega).
Indeed its fixed-g bound is orientation-neutral after swapping the two divisor-complement pairs, and forced high with beta<6/5 gives Q>=x^c for a fixed c>0; hence exact-g summation retains a power saving. Combining this with (A)-(C), the still-unestimated standard-marker buffer is the disjoint union mathscr R_buf of cells
orientation in {forward,reverse},
parent in {C91,U_sh,U_low},
anatomy in {A,B,C1,C2,C3},
beta_0<beta<beta_m,
Q^(-sigma+eta)<=G<Q^(Gamma_BC(beta)+omega).
The later pre-6/5 sliver beta_m<=beta<6/5 is separately and exhaustively described by the general normalized anatomy list above. All beta>=6/5 atoms, and hence every possible endpoint parent, are outside this audit. No PMD, endpoint, logical bad-N, or Goldbach conclusion is made.

(E) First open cell and exact missing theorem slot. The lowest normalized-beta slab in mathscr R_buf is structurally nonempty already with parent U_low, anatomy A, and G asymptotic to one. More precisely, choose a fixed beta_* in a sufficiently short right-neighborhood of beta_0 contained in (beta_0,beta_m). There are arbitrarily large square-root-balanced arithmetic index tuples with g=1, normalized beta beta_*+o(1), G=1, 60-residual label outside C91, parent U_low, and an interval-prime factor in (L,Z), hence A anatomy. On this cell H_P=H_T>1. The hypotheses beta<=beta_0 of c6a3ee810402825f, fc328dd4cfe6679c and their reverse analogues fail; the fixed-g Bettin--Chandee condition fails because Gamma_BC(beta_*)>0 while G=1; and the absolute large-imbalance condition in 8346861a976aa604 fails because its right side contains the growing factor H_T Q^xi. Thus no accepted controlled-label or Poisson/Fourier estimate cited here pays this cell.

The exact first missing theorem slot is a complete-frequency, exact-target-gcd-descended interval-prime A estimate with fixed power saving O(GQ^(2-delta)) for beta in a fixed subinterval immediately above beta_0 and G bounded above and below by positive constants, retaining the literal source amplitude and every listed mask. The reverse slot is the same theorem after the verified coordinate swap and h-sign reindexing of 65b10e9a052e9479. This is a scoped theorem-interface no-fit, not a lower bound or an impossibility statement.
15425579cb248eff.proof:
We prove the five parts in order.

For (A), on an actual source label D=x^(1/2+o(1)). If D=R, the two 60-controlled inequalities in the R<=D branch are
D^33<=x^(17-sigma),  D^15<=x^(8-sigma).
Their left sides are x^(33/2+o(1)) and x^(15/2+o(1)); since 33/2<17-sigma and 15/2<8-sigma, both hold for sufficiently large x. Thus equality is excluded before the high residual family is formed.

For bounded Q, fact 8346861a976aa604 gives complete exact-g l1 mass O(QB(log x)^2). Forward,
QB=DR/g^2=(R/D)Q^2.
If Q<=Q_0, D>=c_Dx^(1/2)(log x)^(-A_D), and R=O(x), this is O(x^(1/2)(log x)^(A_D)). Reverse gives the same expression QB=DR/g^2=(D/R)Q^2, and the lower bound on R yields O(x^(1/2)(log x)^(A_R)). There are at most tau(N)=x^o(1) exact gcds and polylogarithmically many source labels. Arbitrary deletion only decreases the l1 mass, proving (A). This argument also covers 0<Q<1; if the positive integer normalized variable has empty support there is simply no atom.

For (B), forward write D=gQ and R=gB with B=Q^beta. Then
beta_orig=(log g+beta log Q)/(log g+log Q).
Since g>=1, Q>1, and beta>=1, this is a convex combination of 1 and beta, so 1<=beta_orig<=beta. The reverse computation is identical with D and R interchanged. If beta<4/3, the original-label exponent is below 4/3. By the parent precedence of 77d7a3419a07305c no boundary-admissible endpoint tag is possible; outside C91 the atom is U_sh or U_low according as min(D,R)<4D_* or not. This proves (B) without replacing beta_orig by beta.

For (C), forward physical balance gives
M/D=(DM)/D^2>=c_1/C_D^2.
Since g is a positive integer,
G_f=M/(D/g)=gM/D>=c_1/C_D^2.
Reverse gives K/R=(RK)/R^2>=c_1/C_R^2 and G_r=gK/R. Put c_G equal to the smaller of these fixed positive constants. As sigma-eta>0, Q^(-sigma+eta)<c_G for sufficiently large Q. If actual G<1, it therefore lies inside the complete near-balanced strip, whose upper endpoint exceeds one. The forward and reverse near-balanced facts retain all parents, all six standard anatomies, every Fourier and target-gcd layer, and exact outer gcds. If G>=1, the complete forward and reverse full-G facts retain the same inventory for every G without an upper bound. Taking the disjoint union G<1 and G>=1 and decreasing the smaller saving exponent proves the claimed all-G power saving. Fact 8bf5ca45f71b8c2c makes C0 empty at large Q and pays its bounded-base complement; (A) is a stronger complete-source bounded-base payment.

For (D), (B) gives the parent list because beta<6/5<4/3. Exact orientation, parent, anatomy, and G selectors are nested zero-one partitions of the unchanged atom family, so their Cartesian refinement is disjoint and exhaustive. For the standard cutoffs, L<=S_0 and B>S_0 follow respectively from beta>=1 and beta<2-3sigma; L<Z follows from beta<5/4-2sigma. Finally
Z^4/B=Q^(6-5beta-12sigma),
which tends to infinity precisely when beta<beta_m. Hence fact 6414b11506a84ff0 gives exactly A,B,C1,C2,C3 above C0 throughout beta<beta_m. Also B/S_0=Q^(2-beta-3sigma) tends to infinity uniformly in this range, so no integer n comparable to B can satisfy n<=S_0 at sufficiently large Q.

Fact 7131a06664967733 gives at fixed g the complete aggregate bound
x^epsilon[G^(3/20)QB^(19/20)+Q^(7/8)B].
Dividing by the fixed-g source scale gGQ^2 gives its threshold Gamma_BC(beta), uniformly in every parent/anatomy deletion. The reverse statement follows by the exact coordinate permutation used in 65b10e9a052e9479. To sum g, forced high gives in either orientation
Q^(beta-1)=B/Q=(larger physical divisor scale)/(smaller physical divisor scale)
>x^(1/16-kappa_0+o(1)).
Since beta-1<1/5, Q>=x^c for some fixed c>0. Thus a fixed omega margin yields a global fixed power saving after sum_{g|N}1/g=x^o(1). Removing this large-G part, the low-beta part (C), bounded bases (A), empty C0, and the empty actual G<Q^(-sigma+eta) interval leaves exactly mathscr R_buf and the separately stated top sliver.

For (E), we give a symbolic arithmetic support construction; it is not a lower bound for the resulting signed sum. Fix beta_* strictly between beta_0 and beta_m, sufficiently close to beta_0. Let T tend to infinity. Using the prime-in-(y,2y) theorem already recorded in accepted fact b7fcb27a091203e5, choose distinct odd primes d,p,s on scales
T, T^(beta_*-1+sigma), T^(1-sigma),
respectively, and put r=ps. Set m=d. Choose a constant c>1 such that 2/(1+c) lies where the fixed nonzero nonnegative source weight W is positive, and choose an odd integer k=c d^2/r+O(1). Put N=dm+rk and x=N/2. Then N is even,
x is comparable to d^2, dm/x=2/(1+c)+o(1),
r is comparable to d^beta_*, and k is comparable to d^(2-beta_*). The nonnegative dyadic partition supplies active labels with D and M equal, D comparable to d, R comparable to r, and K comparable to k. Thus g=(d,r)=1, G=M/D=1, and normalized beta is beta_*+o(1).

The label is forced high because beta_*/2>9/16-kappa_0. It is 60-residual: R/M is a positive power of x, while the two forward controlled monomials have x-exponents
7+19beta_*/2>17-sigma,  7/2+4beta_*>8-sigma.
The corresponding C91 UBC inequalities, including after swapping, fail with the same strict exponent margins; its balanced and Fourier-tail predicates also fail. Since beta_*<4/3 and D,R are both deep, the parent is U_low. The selected prime p has scale L, and because L<Z by a fixed power it may be chosen, after a harmless constant adjustment, strictly in (L,Z). Hence the normalized marker is A.

Here beta_*>20/19, so Gamma_BC(beta_*)>0 and G=1 does not satisfy the fixed-power threshold. Also G^2(D/M)=1, whereas H_TQ^xi=Q^(beta_*-1+xi) tends to infinity, so the absolute large-imbalance hypothesis fails. Finally all four assembly facts impose beta<=beta_0. This verifies the no-fit and isolates the stated missing theorem slot. Every assertion stops below beta=6/5 and before endpoint, PMD, logical capture, or Goldbach.

15a95f602f1add2d.title: REVERSE NEAR-BALANCED ALL-PARENT ASSEMBLY THROUGH THE FULL LOW-BETA RANGE, WITH NO TARGET-GCD DELETION. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, sigma=kappa/100, and 0<eta<sigma. Consider the literal normalized source atoms with D>R and exact outer gcd d=ga,r=gb. Use the reverse convention of fact a71f777ad842c886: Q=R/g, B=D/g, H_T=B/Q, G=K/Q, H_P=B/K, L_src=N/g, reciprocal modulus b, and marked inverse argument a. Use L=H_TQ^sigma, S_0=H_T^2Q^(3sigma), Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma), beta=log B/log Q
15a95f602f1add2d.author: slava chan
15a95f602f1add2d.statement:
REVERSE NEAR-BALANCED ALL-PARENT ASSEMBLY THROUGH THE FULL LOW-BETA RANGE, WITH NO TARGET-GCD DELETION. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, sigma=kappa/100, and 0<eta<sigma. Consider the literal normalized source atoms with D>R and exact outer gcd d=ga,r=gb. Use the reverse convention of fact a71f777ad842c886: Q=R/g, B=D/g, H_T=B/Q, G=K/Q, H_P=B/K, L_src=N/g, reciprocal modulus b, and marked inverse argument a. Use L=H_TQ^sigma, S_0=H_T^2Q^(3sigma), Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma), beta=log B/log Q.
Assume c_1x<=DM,RK<=C_1x, c_Rx^(1/2)(log x)^(-A_R)<=R<=C_Rx^(1/2), and all physical scales are at most Cx. Let mathcal G_rev_full be the exact g|N layers with Q sufficiently large, 1<=beta<=6/5-2kappa, and Q^(-sigma+eta)<=G<=Q^(sigma-eta). Let R_near_rev_full be the complete reverse literal nonzero-Poisson sum over mathcal G_rev_full, every frozen low-beta parent and every leaf C0,A,B,C1,C2,C3, retaining every source mask, amplitude, dyadic frequency, target-gcd layer, prime-order label and collision stratum; include bounded-base C0 layers.
Then |R_near_rev_full|<<x^(1-delta) for some delta=delta(kappa,eta)>0. No reverse A target-gcd incidence and no other listed sector is deleted. Outer-g layers outside the displayed G strip are outside the assertion.
15a95f602f1add2d.proof:
Fact a091dd4ea1922f73 proves this assertion for beta<=1+sigma/4. For 1+sigma/4<beta<=6/5-2kappa it proves the same complete reverse assertion after deleting only A incidences with
Q^(sigma/2)<c=gcd(b,L_src)<H_TQ^(sigma/4).                   (1)
We pay exactly (1).

Fix g and one incidence. The positive source equation is am+bk=L_src, with squarefree coprime a,b. Apply fact 1c64020b89f097c4 after interchanging (a,m) with (b,k). Write
b=cq, m=cm_1, L_src=cL_1.
Then gcd(c,q)=gcd(c,a)=gcd(q,a)=1 and gcd(q,L_1)=1. The exact reverse character constructed in a091dd4ea1922f73 is e_b(L_src h a^(-1)). Therefore
e_{cq}(cL_1 h a^(-1))=e_q(L_1 h a^(-1)).                    (2)

Under the reverse marker convention, the inverse-product variable is a=up with UY comparable to B and
H_TQ^sigma/2<=Y<=Z.
Squarefreeness gives gcd(u,p)=1, and gcd(a,b)=1 gives gcd(up,cq)=1. Also q is comparable to Q/c. Apply fact 97e9b97caca25b8d with its abstract signed target chosen as -L_src. Its displayed character then equals
e_q(-(-L_src/c)h(up)^(-1))=e_q(L_1h(up)^(-1)),
which is (2). The divisor set C_med is exactly (1).

The relabeled Fourier amplitude and every reverse source mask are already shown in a091dd4ea1922f73 to form the same uniformly scaled-smooth family with natural frequency H_P=B/K; its proof preserves all signs and reindexes only the complete h-family. Facts d26acaefc372b4d0 and 3e326f797b2e04e4 give the polynomial target bound and arbitrary dyadic Fourier decay after this relabeling. Parent, fixed-U, high-label, sign, prime-cell and collision restrictions are scalar coefficients or deletion masks, all permitted uniformly in 97e9b97caca25b8d. Hence that fact gives
sum_{c in (1)}|T_c|<<Q^(2-delta_1)                           (3)
on the exact g-layer.

Restore (3) to the deleted-band reverse assembly. Since Q=R/g,
sum_{g|N,Q large}Q^(2-delta_1)
<=R^(2-delta_1)sum_{g>=1}g^(-2+delta_1)
<<R^(2-delta_1)
<<x^(1-delta_1/2).
Polylogarithmic labels are absorbed by reducing the saving. Bounded-base C0 is already paid in a091dd4ea1922f73. Combining its two beta ranges with (3) proves the complete reverse assertion.

glossary.R_near_rev_full: The complete literal reverse all-parent sum with every target-gcd layer restored.
glossary.m_1: The quotient m/c after reverse target-gcd descent.
glossary.mathcal G_rev_full: The exact reverse outer-gcd layers in the near-balanced full low-beta strip.

15aaf8bd9c13ba39.title: EXACT LITERAL RESONANT FULL-DENOMINATOR RESIDUAL AND ITS NONPROJECTIVE SHARED-PRIME DEPENDENCE. Fix 0<eta<1/12, 0<delta<2eta, and 0<theta<1/2. Let Q tend to infinity and put U=Q^(1/3), B=Q^(4/3+o(1)), F_0=Q^(1-2eta+o(1)), and A_P=Q^(1+delta)/P^2. Let P be a dyadic shared-prime scale in the literal medium range Q^(1/3+2eta+o(1))<=P<=Q^(1/2+theta), and assume A_P>1. Let N be a fixed positive integer. Let cal B be the squarefree integers b in [B,2B), put L_b=product_{r|b,b/r<F_0}r, let cal R={b in cal B:L_b>1,(L_b,N)=1}, define pi(b) as the largest prime divisor of L_b, and put s(b)=b/pi(b). Let gamma_b be complex numbers satisfying sum_{b in cal R}|gamma_b|^2<=1. For primes p in [P,2P) put S_p={s:ps in cal R,pi(ps)=p} and Q_p={q:pq in cal R,p|s(pq)}. Let w_n be supported on Q<=n<2Q and satisfy |w_n|<=Q^epsilon for every epsilon>0. Extend by zero off Q<=au<2Q and define
15aaf8bd9c13ba39.author: slava chan
15aaf8bd9c13ba39.statement:
EXACT LITERAL RESONANT FULL-DENOMINATOR RESIDUAL AND ITS NONPROJECTIVE SHARED-PRIME DEPENDENCE. Fix 0<eta<1/12, 0<delta<2eta, and 0<theta<1/2. Let Q tend to infinity and put U=Q^(1/3), B=Q^(4/3+o(1)), F_0=Q^(1-2eta+o(1)), and A_P=Q^(1+delta)/P^2. Let P be a dyadic shared-prime scale in the literal medium range Q^(1/3+2eta+o(1))<=P<=Q^(1/2+theta), and assume A_P>1. Let N be a fixed positive integer. Let cal B be the squarefree integers b in [B,2B), put L_b=product_{r|b,b/r<F_0}r, let cal R={b in cal B:L_b>1,(L_b,N)=1}, define pi(b) as the largest prime divisor of L_b, and put s(b)=b/pi(b). Let gamma_b be complex numbers satisfying sum_{b in cal R}|gamma_b|^2<=1. For primes p in [P,2P) put S_p={s:ps in cal R,pi(ps)=p} and Q_p={q:pq in cal R,p|s(pq)}. Let w_n be supported on Q<=n<2Q and satisfy |w_n|<=Q^epsilon for every epsilon>0. Extend by zero off Q<=au<2Q and define
beta_{ss,a}(u)=mu(a)w_{au}sum_{m|u,m<=U}mu(m), 1<=a<=U,
beta_{ll,a}(u)=w_{au}sum_{dm=u,U<d<=m}varkappa(d,m)mu(d)mu(m), 1<=a<2U,
where varkappa(d,m)=1 for d=m and 2 for d<m. Put U_a={u in Z:Q<=au<2Q}. For s in S_p with (s,N)=1 define M_1 modulo s by pM_1 congruent to N modulo s. For q in Q_p with q<=F_0 and (q,N)=1 define M_12 modulo q by pM_12 congruent to N modulo q.

On an edge satisfying (a,sq)=1, for k modulo ps and l modulo pq define
hat beta_{p,tau,a,s}^{(1)}(k)=sum_{u in U_a,(au,ps)=1} beta_{tau,a}(u)e_{ps}(-ku),
hat beta_{p,tau,a,q}^{(2)}(l)=sum_{u in U_a,(au,pq)=1} conjugate(beta_{tau,a}(u))e_{pq}(-lu),
K_{p,s,a}^{(1)}(k)=sum_{z modulo s,(z,s)=1}e_s(M_1a^(-1)z^(-1)+kp^(-1)z),
K_{p,q,a}^{(2)}(l)=sum_{z modulo q,(z,q)=1}e_q(-M_12a^(-1)z^(-1)+lp^(-1)z),
where every inverse is taken in the displayed coprime modulus. Define
E_full^res(P)=sum_{p,tau,a} sum_{s in S_p,q in Q_p;(s,N)=(q,N)=1,q<=F_0,(s,q)<A_P,(a,sq)=1}
conjugate(gamma_{ps})gamma_{pq}/((p-1)sq)
times
sum_{k modulo ps,l modulo pq;p not dividing kl;kq^2+ls^2 congruent to 0 modulo p}
hat beta_{p,tau,a,s}^{(1)}(k)K_{p,s,a}^{(1)}(k)
hat beta_{p,tau,a,q}^{(2)}(l)K_{p,q,a}^{(2)}(l),
where tau ranges over ss,ll with the corresponding displayed a-range. Then every edge of the literal E_full(P) of fact f439118e1e8818a1 with (a,sq)>1 is zero, and
E_full(P)=E_full^res(P)+E_full^nr(P),
where E_full^nr(P) is the nonresonant term of fact e9ba03365d02ff89 and hence
|E_full^nr(P)| << Q^(7/3-omega_nr)
for every fixed omega_nr<6eta and all sufficiently large Q.

Choose centered integer representatives k,l in the inner sum. Put g=(s,q), s=gs', and q=gq'. Every resonant term satisfies p|R for
R=kq'^2+ls'^2,
and R is nonzero with |R|<8B^3/P^2. Therefore, for fixed s',q',k,l, only O_{eta,delta}(1) primes p in [P,2P) can occur.

Nevertheless, after this divisor-first reindexing the literal summand is not independent of p. Indeed the exact CRT identities are
hat beta_{p,tau,a,s}^{(1)}(k)=sum_{u in U_a,(au,ps)=1}beta_{tau,a}(u)e_p(-ks^(-1)u)e_s(-kp^(-1)u),
hat beta_{p,tau,a,q}^{(2)}(l)=sum_{u in U_a,(au,pq)=1}conjugate(beta_{tau,a}(u))e_p(-lq^(-1)u)e_q(-lp^(-1)u),
while
K_{p,s,a}^{(1)}(k)=sum_{z modulo s,(z,s)=1}e_s(Np^(-1)a^(-1)z^(-1)+kp^(-1)z),
K_{p,q,a}^{(2)}(l)=sum_{z modulo q,(z,q)=1}e_q(-Np^(-1)a^(-1)z^(-1)+lp^(-1)z).
The outer factors conjugate(gamma_{ps})gamma_{pq}, the unit masks, the Fourier periods ps,pq and centered frequency ranges also retain p. Thus the bounded prime incidence is an exact support statement but does not by itself estimate E_full^res(P). A fixed-power bound for this displayed weighted residual, retaining these literal coefficients, is the precise remaining supplier required to close E_full(P) by this completion route. No such bound, estimate for another additive subface, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
15aaf8bd9c13ba39.proof:
First remove the non-coprime-a edges before introducing any inverse of a. If (a,s)>1, then for every integer u one has (au,ps)>1, so the first unit-supported row in the definition of E_full(P) is empty. If (a,q)>1, the second row is empty. Thus every edge with (a,sq)>1 contributes zero. On every remaining edge, a is a unit modulo both s and q, so all displayed Kloosterman factors are defined.

Now apply the exact additive completion formula of fact 5a7bf376fe94485e edge by edge to the literal full-denominator aggregate of fact f439118e1e8818a1 with d_1=s, d_2=q, c=sq^(-1) modulo p, C_1=M_1a^(-1) modulo s, C_2=-M_12a^(-1) modulo q, and the two unit-supported literal Vaughan rows. In formula (5) of fact 5a7bf376fe94485e, the prefactor 1/(p^2sq) cancels the displayed p^2, and the factor {(p-1)1_res-1}/(p-1)^2 splits into 1_res/(p-1) and -1/(p-1)^2. The first part is exactly the displayed definition of E_full^res(P), because its resonance alpha_1+c alpha_2=0 is
ks^(-1)+sq^(-1)lq^(-1)=0 modulo p,
which is equivalent to kq^2+ls^2=0 modulo p. The second part is exactly E_full^nr(P). Its stated bound is fact e9ba03365d02ff89.

For a resonant term, write s=gs' and q=gq'. The hypotheses of fact f7bbe736fbfa275b are satisfied because ps,pq lie in [B,2B), (p,sq)=1, g<A_P, delta<2eta, and k,l are centered nonzero classes modulo p. That fact gives p|R, R nonzero, |R|<8B^3/P^2, and the bounded count of possible p for fixed s',q',k,l.

For the coefficient identities, additive CRT for coprime p and s gives
e_{ps}(-ku)=e_p(-ks^(-1)u)e_s(-kp^(-1)u);
substitution in the definition of hat beta^{(1)} proves the first identity, and the same argument with q proves the second. From pM_1=N modulo s and pM_12=N modulo q one has M_1=Np^(-1) modulo s and M_12=Np^(-1) modulo q; substitution into the definitions of K^{(1)} and K^{(2)} proves the last two identities. Each displayed occurrence of p then shows the asserted literal p-dependence. The outer gamma factors, unit masks, periods and centered representative ranges are visibly p-indexed in the exact definition. Hence the divisor-incidence conclusion controls only support multiplicity; the final paragraph states the remaining weighted interface and makes no unproved estimate.

glossary.E_full^res(P): the exact resonant indicator contribution to the literal full-denominator aggregate E_full(P)
glossary.K_{p,q,a}^{(2)}(k): the row-two cofactor Kloosterman completion factor modulo q
glossary.K_{p,s,a}^{(1)}(k): the row-one cofactor Kloosterman completion factor modulo s
glossary.R: the nonzero integer kq'^2+ls'^2 controlling resonant shared primes
glossary.g: the greatest common divisor of s and q
glossary.hat beta_{p,tau,a,q}^{(2)}(k): the additive Fourier transform modulo pq of the unit-supported second literal Vaughan row
glossary.hat beta_{p,tau,a,s}^{(1)}(k): the additive Fourier transform modulo ps of the unit-supported first literal Vaughan row
glossary.s',q': the coprime primitive cofactors defined by s=gs' and q=gq'

15dc89545ee8244b.title: Let m>1 be odd, let s belong to {1,-1}, let K be coprime to m, let Delta be a nonzero integer, and let Z_W^{ass} be the sign-adjusted complete formal Bettin--Chandee column-main assembly defined in fact a170364aba04897b. Let X>=1, let S_1 and S_2 be finite positive-integer intervals contained in [X,2X] intersect Z, and assume that the functions f and g in that definition are supported in [X/2,2X]. Then
15dc89545ee8244b.author: slava chan
15dc89545ee8244b.statement:
Let m>1 be odd, let s belong to {1,-1}, let K be coprime to m, let Delta be a nonzero integer, and let Z_W^{ass} be the sign-adjusted complete formal Bettin--Chandee column-main assembly defined in fact a170364aba04897b. Let X>=1, let S_1 and S_2 be finite positive-integer intervals contained in [X,2X] intersect Z, and assume that the functions f and g in that definition are supported in [X/2,2X]. Then
|Z_W^{ass}|
 <=3|Delta| ||f||_infinity ||g||_infinity
    (1+X/m^2)^2 sum_{u modulo m}|W(u)|.                              (1)

Consequently, fix real constants delta in (0,3/2), C_0>=1, and C_1>=1. If H>=2, X=H^3,
H^(3-delta)<=m<=C_0X,
and either W(u)=e_m(ell u) for some residue ell modulo m or W is the interval-multiplicity weight W_{U,m} of fact 5f60a4633e6b0b70 with U_cut<=C_1X, then
|Z_W^{ass}| <<_{Delta,C_0,C_1}
 H^3 ||f||_infinity||g||_infinity.                                  (2)
For the pure mode, the conclusion includes every nonzero centered frequency ell. Formula (2) is a fixed-m bound for the complete formal column-main assembly, which has only O(m) paired residue columns at near-maximal conductor. It is not an estimate for a valid two-row-character-twisted determinant main term, does not pay the outer sums over m,r_2,r_3, and does not control the remaining prime, gcd, C-coupling, mask, source, or coefficient-box selectors.
15dc89545ee8244b.proof:
Fact a170364aba04897b gives the exact formula
Z_W^{ass}
=sum_{n_1 in S_1,n_2 in S_2; gcd(n_1,n_2) divides Delta}
 [gcd(n_1,n_2)/(n_1n_2)] I(n_1,n_2)
 sum_{u modulo m}W(u)
 Delta_{m^2}(n_2-K-2smu)Delta_{m^2}(-n_1-K+2smu),                    (3)
where
I(n_1,n_2)=integral_R f((x+Delta)/n_2)g(x/n_1) dx.                   (4)

For fixed n_1 in [X,2X], the support condition on g shows that the integrand in (4) can be nonzero only when
x belongs to [n_1X/2,2n_1X].
This interval has length 3n_1X/2<=3X^2. Therefore
|I(n_1,n_2)|<=3X^2||f||_infinity||g||_infinity.                     (5)
The positive integer gcd(n_1,n_2) divides the nonzero integer Delta, so
gcd(n_1,n_2)<=|Delta|.
Also n_1n_2>=X^2. Hence the absolute value of the density kernel multiplying the digit selector in (3) is at most
3|Delta|||f||_infinity||g||_infinity.                               (6)

Fix u modulo m. Each delta in (3) restricts its corresponding column variable to one residue class modulo m^2. An interval of length at most X contains at most
1+X/m^2
integers in a fixed residue class modulo m^2. Thus the number of ordered pairs (n_1,n_2) in S_1 times S_2 satisfying both deltas for this fixed u is at most
(1+X/m^2)^2.                                                         (7)
Apply the triangle inequality to (3), then use (6) and (7), and finally sum |W(u)| over u. This proves (1).

For (2), the lower bound m>=H^(3-delta) and X=H^3 give
X/m^2<=H^(-3+2delta)<=1
because delta<3/2 and H>=2. Thus the squared factor in (1) is at most four. For a pure mode |W(u)|=1 for all m residues, so
sum_u|W(u)|=m<=C_0H^3.                                               (8)
For W_{U,m}, its definition in fact 5f60a4633e6b0b70 gives
sum_{u modulo m}|W_{U,m}(u)|
 =#{v in Z:0<|v|<U_cut}=2(U_cut-1)<=2C_1H^3.                         (9)
Insert (8) or (9) into (1) to obtain (2). If ell is nonzero, the pure mode is centered by additive orthogonality, as stated in fact a170364aba04897b. The final limitations follow because (3) is the formal column functional from that fact, while fact a695dcaf05aaa83d proves that the existing Bettin--Chandee theorem does not accept the full row-character atoms.

16c145000d211540.title: PERRON-EULER FACTORIZATION OF THE LITERAL CRITICAL PHYSICAL ROW. Assume the hypotheses and notation of fact 7264046d8776d59f. For real t, complex s with Re(s)>0, define
16c145000d211540.author: slava chan
16c145000d211540.statement:
PERRON-EULER FACTORIZATION OF THE LITERAL CRITICAL PHYSICAL ROW. Assume the hypotheses and notation of fact 7264046d8776d59f. For real t, complex s with Re(s)>0, define
cal W_t(s)=(2*pi)^{-1} integral_0^infinity W(u)Phi(x(2-u)/U)(x(2-u))^s u^{-it}du/u.                    (1)
For bold t=(t_1,t_2) and integers w,v define
omega_{bold t}(w,v)=1_{w,v in cal I_D}1_{w-v in cal H_mid}mu(w)mu(v)Phi(w/D)Phi(v/D)(w/D)^{it_1}(v/D)^{it_2}.     (2)
For a prime p, residues w,v,z, and complex s_1,s_2, put
ell_p(w,v,z;s_1,s_2)=-p^{-s_1}1_{p|w+z}-p^{-s_2}1_{p|v+z}+p^{-s_1-s_2}1_{p|w+z}1_{p|v+z}.             (3)
If S is not squarefree, H_{S,bold t}(z)=0. If S is squarefree, then for every sigma_1,sigma_2>0 one has the absolutely convergent exact representation
H_{S,bold t}(z)=(2*pi*i)^{-2} integral_{Re(s_1)=sigma_1} integral_{Re(s_2)=sigma_2} [cal W_{t_1}(s_1)cal W_{t_2}(s_2)/(s_1^2s_2^2)]
 times sum_{w,v in Z} omega_{bold t}(w,v) product_{p|S}ell_p(w,v,z;s_1,s_2) ds_2 ds_1.                    (4)
Thus the entire fixed-total-modulus q_1,q_2 shell, including both Mobius signs and both moving positive logarithms, is an exact product of local two-reflected-form factors before the physical Gram is formed. Equation (4) is an identity only; it asserts no bound for the critical Gram or for SUPPLIER_A in fact 3db20da48fdfac31.
16c145000d211540.proof:
For y>0 and sigma>0, Perron's formula gives
log(y)_+=(2*pi*i)^{-1} integral_{Re(s)=sigma} y^s ds/s^2.                    (5)
The integral is absolutely convergent because the integral of |sigma+i tau|^{-2} over tau is finite. Apply (5) with y=x(2-u)/q in the definition of tilde F_q(t) from fact ffa8f6d3f766b9f5. The support of W lies in a fixed compact subinterval of (0,1), so x(2-u) is positive and bounded by a constant times x. Absolute convergence permits interchange of the u- and s-integrals, giving
widetilde F_q(t)=(2*pi*i)^{-1} integral_{Re(s)=sigma}cal W_t(s)q^{-s}ds/s^2.                    (6)

Now start from equation (3) defining H in fact 7264046d8776d59f and put v=w-h. For a tuple with d=(q_1,q_2)|h, the congruence w congruent gamma_{q_1,q_2,h}-z modulo S=[q_1,q_2] is equivalent to the pair
q_1|w+z,qquad q_2|v+z.                                      (7)
Indeed gamma is zero modulo q_1 and h modulo q_2, while v=w-h. Conversely, the two divisibilities in (7) imply w congruent gamma-z modulo both q_1 and q_2; they also imply d|w-v=h, so no compatibility condition has been lost. The change h=w-v turns the remaining physical coefficient exactly into omega_{bold t}(w,v).

Insert (6) twice into H and use (7). All q_1,q_2 sums are finite at fixed S, and the w,v sums are finite by their supports, so the changes of order are valid. The q-shell inside the two Perron integrals is
sum_{[q_1,q_2]=S}mu(q_1)mu(q_2)q_1^{-s_1}q_2^{-s_2}1_{q_1|w+z}1_{q_2|v+z}.                         (8)
Only squarefree q_1,q_2 occur. Therefore (8) vanishes unless S is squarefree. When S is squarefree, each prime p|S occurs in q_1 only, q_2 only, or both. The contribution of these three mutually exclusive choices is respectively
-p^{-s_1}1_{p|w+z},quad -p^{-s_2}1_{p|v+z},quad p^{-s_1-s_2}1_{p|w+z}1_{p|v+z}.
The choices are independent across primes, so (8) equals product_{p|S}ell_p. Substitution into the double Perron integral proves (4). Since no estimate was used, the final scope statement follows.

glossary.cal W_t: the archimedean Perron-Mellin transform in equation (1)
glossary.ell_p: the three-state local fixed-lcm factor at p in equation (3)
glossary.omega_{bold t}: the signed two-reflected-variable physical weight in equation (2)
glossary.s_1: the first Perron variable separating the q_1 moving logarithm
glossary.s_2: the second Perron variable separating the q_2 moving logarithm
glossary.sigma_1: the positive real part of the first Perron contour
glossary.sigma_2: the positive real part of the second Perron contour

16e3378d8ed3c224.title: THREE-TIER EFFECTIVE-MODULUS NORMAL FORM AND THE EXACT MINIMAL VECTOR LARGE-SIEVE SCALE FOR THE C4 ELEVEN-MODE SUPPLIER. Adopt the literal C4 setting of facts a3132ecd1bd44382 and 4a18a6fc30232be9. Thus B/2<=n_lambda<=2B, n_lambda=D_lambda v_lambda, D_lambda is a product of four distinct odd primes at least Z, and gcd(D_lambda,v_lambda)=1. For every r|D_lambda with omega(r)<=2 put
16e3378d8ed3c224.author: slava chan
16e3378d8ed3c224.statement:
THREE-TIER EFFECTIVE-MODULUS NORMAL FORM AND THE EXACT MINIMAL VECTOR LARGE-SIEVE SCALE FOR THE C4 ELEVEN-MODE SUPPLIER. Adopt the literal C4 setting of facts a3132ecd1bd44382 and 4a18a6fc30232be9. Thus B/2<=n_lambda<=2B, n_lambda=D_lambda v_lambda, D_lambda is a product of four distinct odd primes at least Z, and gcd(D_lambda,v_lambda)=1. For every r|D_lambda with omega(r)<=2 put
m_lambda,r=v_lambda r.                                             (1)
Then
m_lambda,r<=2B/Z^(4-omega(r)).                                     (2)
In particular, with B=Q^beta, Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma), beta<6/5,
m_lambda,1<=2Q^(12sigma),
m_lambda,p<=2Q^(3/10+9sigma) when r=p is prime, and
m_lambda,r<=2Q^(3/5+6sigma) when omega(r)=2.                        (3)

The positive mode coefficients of fact a3132ecd1bd44382 satisfy the uniform two-sided estimate
m_lambda,r/(2B)<=c_lambda(r)<=27m_lambda,r/B.                       (4)
More precisely,
3m_lambda,1/B<=c_lambda(1)<=27m_lambda,1/B,
3m_lambda,p/(2B)<=c_lambda(p)<=9m_lambda,p/B,
and
m_lambda,r/(2B)<=c_lambda(r)<=2m_lambda,r/B
for omega(r)=2.                                                     (5)

The primitive-ray transform has the following exact physical-source form:
S_lambda,r(z)
=sum_{q,h} c_lambda(q,h;z)mu(q)^2 1_{gcd(q,D_lambda v_lambda)=1}
 e_{m_lambda,r}(A h [q(D_lambda/r)]^(-1)),                          (6)
where the sum is over the original finite support Q<=q<2Q, F<=|h|<2F, every literal mask and amplitude remains inside c_lambda(q,h;z), and inverses are taken in the displayed modulus. If m_lambda,r>1, additive reciprocity gives the equivalent exact phase identity
e_{m_lambda,r}(A h [q(D_lambda/r)]^(-1))
=e(Ah/(q n_lambda))
 e_{qD_lambda/r}(-Ah [m_lambda,r]^(-1)).                            (7)
For m_lambda,r=1 the left side is 1 and the right side is interpreted by the same identity with the inverse of 1 modulo qD_lambda/r.

Define the modulus-weighted common-row energy
V_11(z)=sum_lambda sum_{r|D_lambda, omega(r)<=2}
 m_lambda,r |S_lambda,r(z)|^2.                                    (8)
Then the exact eleven-mode energy E_11 of fact 4a18a6fc30232be9 obeys
V_11(z)/(2B)<=E_11(z)<=27V_11(z)/B.                                (9)
Consequently C4-11-LS is equivalent, up to absolute constants, to the single vector Bessel estimate
V_11(z)
<<_epsilon Q^epsilon Z^2
 [B^2QF+B^2Q^2F^2/Dcal]||z||_2^2.                                (C4-VLS-m)
The three disjoint pieces omega(r)=0,1,2 may be estimated separately at the three modulus ceilings in (3); summing three bounds at the scale in C4-VLS-m changes only an absolute constant. This reformulation retains common output, varying v_lambda, the complete ray-scale sums, every literal mask, and all positive coefficients. It proves no C4-VLS-m estimate, C4 closure, or Goldbach conclusion.
16e3378d8ed3c224.proof:
Put D=D_lambda, v=v_lambda, n=n_lambda and m=vr. Since n=Dv,
m=vr=n/(D/r).                                                      (10)
The integer D/r is a product of 4-omega(r) distinct rough primes, each at least Z. Therefore D/r>=Z^(4-omega(r)). Using n<=2B in (10) proves (2).

For r=1, substitute the exact formula from the proof of fact a3132ecd1bd44382:
c_lambda(1)
=(1/D) sum_{S subset P_lambda, |S|=2}
 product_{p in S} p/(p-1)
=(m/n) sum_{S subset P_lambda, |S|=2}
 product_{p in S} p/(p-1).                                       (11)
There are six terms. Since every rough prime is odd,
1<p/(p-1)<=3/2.
Hence the final sum in (11) lies between 6 and 27/2. Since B/2<=n<=2B,
3m/B<=c_lambda(1)<=27m/B.                                         (12)

For r=p prime, the exact coefficient calculation in fact a3132ecd1bd44382 gives
c_lambda(p)
=(p/D) sum_{q in P_lambda minus {p}}q/(q-1)
=(m/n) sum_{q in P_lambda minus {p}}q/(q-1).                       (13)
The three-term sum lies between 3 and 9/2. The same bounds for n give
3m/(2B)<=c_lambda(p)<=9m/B.                                       (14)

For omega(r)=2, fact a3132ecd1bd44382 gives
c_lambda(r)=r/D=vr/(Dv)=m/n.                                      (15)
Thus m/(2B)<=c_lambda(r)<=2m/B. Equations (12), (14), and (15) prove (4)-(5).

We prove (6) without changing any source coefficient. A supported physical pair has the unique primitive-ray representation
q=kappa a, h=epsilon kappa b,
where kappa>=1, epsilon is +1 or -1, a,b>0 and gcd(a,b)=1. The gate in fact 134b03fc362a7cf1 makes q a unit modulo Dv, hence modulo m. In the modulus m,
h[q(D/r)]^(-1)
=epsilon kappa b [kappa a(D/r)]^(-1)
=epsilon b[a(D/r)]^(-1).                                         (16)
The right side of (16) is exactly the argument defining Psi_lambda,r on that ray in fact a3132ecd1bd44382. Insert the definition of B_lambda, interchange the finite ray and scale sums, and use uniqueness of the primitive-ray representation. This reconstructs every original physical pair exactly once and proves (6), with mu(q)^2, the unit gate, and c_lambda(q,h;z) unchanged.

For (7), put t=D/r. Then mt=n. Moreover gcd(m,qt)=1: the support gives gcd(q,n)=1, the squarefreeness of D gives gcd(r,D/r)=1, and gcd(D,v)=1. Elementary additive reciprocity for coprime positive integers m and qt states
e_m(u[qt]^(-1))
=e(u/(mqt))e_{qt}(-u[m]^(-1)).                                   (17)
Take u=Ah and use mqt=qn. This proves (7). If m=1, its additive character is trivial and (17) reduces to the standard identity modulo qt with [1]^(-1)=1.

Finally all terms in both energies are nonnegative. Multiplying (4) by |S_lambda,r(z)|^2 and summing over lambda,r gives (9). If C4-VLS-m holds, the upper inequality in (9) gives C4-11-LS after changing the implied constant by 27. Conversely C4-11-LS and the lower inequality in (9) give C4-VLS-m after changing the implied constant by 2. This proves the asserted equivalence and the legal three-tier split. No analytic estimate has been introduced.

glossary.C4-VLS-m: The exact modulus-weighted vector Bessel estimate equivalent to C4-11-LS.
glossary.V_11: The modulus-weighted common-row energy of all eleven reciprocal-slope transforms.

16eaa93099f0bcdc.title: SOFT-SOURCE TWIST-AVERAGED EXACT-SLOPE PAYOFF AND A REDUCED POSITIVE L4 SUPPLIER
16eaa93099f0bcdc.author: slava chan
16eaa93099f0bcdc.statement:
SOFT-SOURCE TWIST-AVERAGED EXACT-SLOPE PAYOFF AND A REDUCED POSITIVE L4 SUPPLIER.

Fix Q>=2, H>1, V,P,B>=1 with VP=QH. Let cal O be a set of pairs j=(v,p), where V<=v<2V, p is prime, P<=p<2P, and gcd(v,p)=1. For each j put n_j=vp and Y_j=n_j/H. Let Phi be a fixed smooth compactly supported complex function whose support avoids zero and has length at most D_0. For every j let cal Q_j be a subset of [Q,2Q) containing at most Q integers. Assume gcd(q,n_j)=1 for q in cal Q_j. For every such j,q let F_{j,q} be smooth and compactly supported, with |F_{j,q}(x)|<=B and with support in an interval of length at most C_0Y_j. Define
 b_{j,t}(q)=n_j^(-1)sum_{h in Z}
  Phi(h/H)Fhat_{j,q}(h/n_j)e_{n_j}(hAqbar)e_p(ht)            (1)
for t modulo p. Assume
 p>max(2H,2(D_0H+1))                                       (2)
for every j. Put
 A_j(theta)=sum_q n_j^(-1)sum_h
  Phi(h/H)Fhat_{j,q}(h/n_j)e_{n_j}(hAqbar)e(htheta).         (3)
Then
 integral_{R/Z}|A_j(theta)|^4dtheta
 =p^(-1)sum_{t modulo p}|sum_qb_{j,t}(q)|^4.                (4)

For an ordered q-pair let lambda(q_1,q_2)=1/q_1-1/q_2 and
 B_{j,t,lambda}=sum_{lambda(q_1,q_2)=lambda}
 b_{j,t}(q_1)conjugate(b_{j,t}(q_2)).
Define
 cal D_{j,t}=sum_lambda|B_{j,t,lambda}|^2.                   (5)
For q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4 in cal Q_j put
 rho_{12}=A(q_2-q_1)(q_1q_2)^(-1) modulo p,
 rho_{34}=A(q_4-q_3)(q_3q_4)^(-1) modulo p,
 Delta=(q_2-q_1)q_3q_4-(q_4-q_3)q_1q_2,
 beta_{j,t}=b_{j,t}(q_1)conjugate(b_{j,t}(q_2))
             conjugate(b_{j,t}(q_3))b_{j,t}(q_4).           (6)
Define
 cal J_{j,t}=sum_{rho_{12}=rho_{34}}beta_{j,t},
 cal M_{j,t}=sum_{Delta nonzero}beta_{j,t}
                 [1_{rho_{12}=rho_{34}}-1/p].               (7)
Put
 cal J_vec=sum_{j in cal O}sum_{t modulo p}cal J_{j,t},
 cal D_vec=sum_{j in cal O}(p-1)/p sum_{t modulo p}cal D_{j,t},
 cal M_vec=sum_{j in cal O}sum_{t modulo p}cal M_{j,t},
 cal M_4=sum_{j in cal O}integral_{R/Z}|A_j(theta)|^4dtheta. (8)
Then exactly
 cal M_4=cal J_vec-cal D_vec-cal M_vec,                      (9)
where cal J_vec>=0 and cal D_vec>=0. Consequently
 cal M_4<=cal J_vec+|cal M_vec|.                            (10)
Thus the exact-slope term is favorable in this positive pre-Cauchy fourth-moment upper bound; no estimate for it is required in the sufficient implication (10).

It can also be paid absolutely. For every epsilon>0,
 cal D_vec<<_{Phi,C_0,epsilon}B^4 P Q^(3+epsilon).          (11)
In particular, if P>=Q^(2/3), then
 cal D_vec<<_{Phi,C_0,epsilon}B^4P^2Q^(7/3+epsilon).        (12)
If B is subpolynomial in the sense that for every delta>0 one has B<<_delta Q^delta, its fourth power can be absorbed by renaming epsilon in (11)-(12).

Hence, after the exact bandpass source bridge, the following is a sufficient two-term positive-moment input at the target of fact 44e700816602dd36:
 cal J_vec+|cal M_vec|<<P^2Q^(7/3+epsilon),                 (13)
with every literal outer coefficient, source mask, and smooth/projective label retained. No minimality or converse is asserted.

The bandpass has Phi(0)=0, so its soft-source amplitude G_{j,q}=F_{j,q}*psi_{Y_j} has Ghat_{j,q}(0)=0. Thus (1) is exactly the soft actual-source row of fact 84bf915e8a88d8d3 and has no additional zero-frequency density row. Facts 914048233fada05f, ace362082848a702, 0e8ef74ba484418d, and 11ec605c5135a640 do not supply (13): 914 requires an eligible fixed-interval injective hard source, ace is an exact expansion rather than an estimate, and 0e8/11ec require pointwise type-(U)/(Z) control and a mean-zero physical kernel, whereas the soft translated row has only twist-average mass control and cal M_{j,t} uses W=1. Therefore (13) still asks for a vector modular-mean estimate for cal J_vec and a twist-stable soft-source Delta-nonzero estimate for cal M_vec. No such estimate, impossibility statement, PMD closure, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
16eaa93099f0bcdc.proof:
Fact 84bf915e8a88d8d3 applies separately to every j because Q>=2, H>1, |cal Q_j|<=Q, and (2) contains both of its sampling and twist-average hypotheses. Its equations (7) and (15) identify b_{j,t}(q) with
 sum_{m:qm congruent A mod n_j}G_{j,q}(m+vt)
and prove (4).

We next derive the fourth-moment identity for the present coefficient rows without any hypothesis on A. For fixed j,t let
