 I_{j,t}=sum_{Delta nonzero; rho_{12}=rho_{34}}beta_{j,t},
 O_{j,t}=sum_{Delta nonzero}beta_{j,t}.                     (14)
Exact equality of rational slopes implies equality of their reductions rho modulo p because every q is a unit modulo p. Grouping the Delta=0 quadruples by their exact rational slope therefore gives
 cal J_{j,t}=cal D_{j,t}+I_{j,t}.                           (15)
Direct expansion of the unphased fourth power gives
 |sum_qb_{j,t}(q)|^4=cal D_{j,t}+O_{j,t}.                   (16)
Definition (7) gives
 cal M_{j,t}=I_{j,t}-O_{j,t}/p.                             (17)
Eliminate I_{j,t} and O_{j,t} from (15)-(17):
 |sum_qb_{j,t}(q)|^4
 =p cal J_{j,t}-(p-1)cal D_{j,t}-p cal M_{j,t}.             (18)
Also additive orthogonality gives
 cal J_{j,t}=p^(-1)sum_{ell modulo p}
  |sum_qb_{j,t}(q)e_p(ell A qbar)|^4>=0,                   (19)
while (5) gives cal D_{j,t}>=0. Average (18) over t with factor p^(-1), use (4), and sum over j. This proves (9). Nonnegativity and (9) give (10).

It remains to prove (11). For fixed j,t put
 Z_{j,t}=sum_{q in cal Q_j}|b_{j,t}(q)|.
The pointwise estimate in the proof of fact 84bf915e8a88d8d3 gives
 max_q|b_{j,t}(q)|<<_{Phi,C_0}B.                            (20)
Therefore
 sum_q|b_{j,t}(q)|^2
 <=max_q|b_{j,t}(q)|Z_{j,t}
 <<_{Phi,C_0}BZ_{j,t}.                                     (21)
Apply fact e7458a42217c2756:
 cal D_{j,t}
 <<_epsilon Q^epsilon(sum_q|b_{j,t}(q)|^2)^2
 <<_{Phi,C_0,epsilon}B^2Q^epsilon Z_{j,t}^2.                (22)
Because (2) includes p>2H and |cal Q_j|<=Q, the r=2 case of fact 84bf915e8a88d8d3 gives
 p^(-1)sum_{t modulo p}Z_{j,t}^2
 <<_{Phi,C_0}B^2Q^2/H.                                     (23)
Combining (22)-(23),
 (p-1)/p sum_tcal D_{j,t}
 <<_{Phi,C_0,epsilon}pB^4Q^(2+epsilon)/H.                   (24)

There are at most 2V possible integers v in [V,2V), at most 2P possible primes p in [P,2P), and every such p is less than 2P. Summing (24) over cal O gives
 cal D_vec<<B^4VP^2Q^(2+epsilon)/H.
Use VP=QH to prove (11). If P>=Q^(2/3), then P Q^3<=P^2Q^(7/3), proving (12). The stated subpolynomial absorption follows by choosing delta smaller than the requested final epsilon and then renaming epsilon.

If (13) holds, (10) gives the fourth-moment target of fact 44e700816602dd36. Since the support of Phi avoids zero, Phi(0)=0. Fact 84bf915e8a88d8d3 gives Ghat_{j,q}(0)=Fhat_{j,q}(0)Phi(0)=0, so no zero-frequency density row remains in this bandpass bridge. The final supplier audit follows by comparing the hypotheses of the four accepted facts with the present soft translated rows. This proves all scope claims.

glossary.A_j: The finite-band trigonometric polynomial attached to j.
glossary.B_{j,t,lambda}: The coefficient sum over one exact rational reciprocal-slope fibre of b_{j,t}.
glossary.F_{j,q}: The compactly supported smooth physical amplitude attached to j and q.
glossary.G_{j,q}: The bandpass-softened amplitude F_{j,q} convolved with psi_{Y_j}.
glossary.Y_j: The natural physical source width n_j/H.
glossary.Z_{j,t}: The l1 mass of the sampled soft-source q-row b_{j,t}.
glossary.b_{j,t}: The q-coefficient row obtained by sampling the finite h-band at theta=t/p.
glossary.cal D_vec: The full twist-averaged exact rational-slope contribution to the outer vector fourth moment.
glossary.cal D_{j,t}: The exact rational-slope energy of b_{j,t}.
glossary.cal J_vec: The full outer sum of modular reciprocal-phase fourth moments over twists.
glossary.cal J_{j,t}: The modular reciprocal-phase collision fourth moment of b_{j,t}.
glossary.cal M_vec: The full outer sum of soft-source Delta-nonzero centered forms with constant kernel W=1.
glossary.cal M_{j,t}: The Delta-nonzero centered constant-kernel form of b_{j,t}.
glossary.cal O: The finite outer family of pairs (v,p).
glossary.cal Q_j: The q-row attached to the outer pair j.
glossary.j: An outer pair (v,p) in cal O.
glossary.n_j: The product vp attached to j.
glossary.reduced positive L4 supplier: A sufficient two-term input controlling cal J_vec and cal M_vec after discarding the favorable exact-slope term.

174b2e718a4e4e89.title: COMMON-REDUCED-GCD ADDITIVE LARGE-SIEVE LEDGER AND ITS EMPTY-RANGE NO-FIT FOR CNP2
174b2e718a4e4e89.author: slava chan
174b2e718a4e4e89.statement:
COMMON-REDUCED-GCD ADDITIVE LARGE-SIEVE LEDGER AND ITS EMPTY-RANGE NO-FIT FOR CNP2.

Fix constants C>=1 and Q>=8. Let real numbers H,V,P,B,G satisfy
  2<=H<=Q^(1/3),  2<=V<H,  P=QH/V,  B>=1,  G>=1.          (1)
Let A be a nonzero integer with |A|<=Q^C. Let cal L be a finite label set. For every outer row o=(ell,v,p), where ell is in cal L, V<=v<2V, p is prime in [P,2P), and gcd(v,p)=1, put n=vp and let cal X_o be a finite set of triples x=(q,m,k) satisfying
  Q<=q,m<2Q,  qm+nk=A,  gcd(qm,n)=1.                       (2)
For x define
  d_x=gcd(|A|,q),  r_x=q/d_x,  t_x=k/d_x,
  beta_x=t_x/r_x modulo 1.                                 (3)
Then gcd(t_x,r_x)=1 and r_x<2Q. Let b_o(x) and z_{o,h} be complex coefficients satisfying
  |b_o(x)|<=B,  |z_{o,h}|<=1,                              (4)
where h ranges over an integer interval I_ell contained either in [H,2H) or in (-2H,-H]. Thus the source coefficient is height-separated as a_{o,h}(x)=z_{o,h}b_o(x), while every source and outer mask may remain inside b_o and z_{o,h}.

Define the gcd-threshold uncentered additive-core form
  T_G^add
   =sum_o sum_{h in I_ell}|z_{o,h}|^2
      sum_{x_1,x_2 in cal X_o,
           gcd(r_{x_1},r_{x_2})>=G}
        b_o(x_1)conjugate(b_o(x_2))
        e(h(beta_{x_1}-beta_{x_2})).                       (5)
The sum is real but need not be nonnegative.

Assume B and #cal L are subpolynomial. Then, for every epsilon>0,
  |T_G^add|
  <<_{C,epsilon}
    B^2(#cal L)Q^epsilon[Q^2H+Q^4/G].                      (6)
The first term in (6) lies under P Q^(5/3+epsilon). The second term reaches that target through this ledger only if
  G>=VQ^(4/3)/H.                                           (7)
But (1) gives VQ^(4/3)/H>=2Q, whereas every nonempty pair in (5) has gcd(r_{x_1},r_{x_2})<2Q. Therefore the common-reduced-gcd spacing furnished by the ordinary additive large sieve yields no nonempty CNP2 range at the required scale.

The additive phase in (5) is exactly the first term e_{g u_1u_2}(h delta_12) of the centered crossed kernel in fact 1a9cfcfe3eedd5e2, with g=gcd(r_1,r_2). Estimate (6) does not control the three Ramanujan-centering correction terms in that fact and does not estimate CNP2. It is a no-fit for this upper-bound insertion, not a lower bound for T_G^add or the literal source. No PMD or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
174b2e718a4e4e89.proof:
First we control multiplicity of the phase points beta_x. Choose for every x the unique integer a_x with
  0<=a_x<r_x,  a_x congruent t_x modulo r_x.
Because gcd(t_x,r_x)=1, the fraction a_x/r_x is reduced, except that r_x=1 gives the unique point zero. If beta_{x_1}=beta_{x_2}, uniqueness of reduced representatives in [0,1) gives
  r_{x_1}=r_{x_2}=r,  t_{x_1} congruent t_{x_2} modulo r.   (8)
Write q_i=d_i r. The source equation divided by d_i is
  r m_i+n t_i=A/d_i.                                       (9)
For a fixed divisor d_i of A, if two atoms have the same residue t modulo r, their t-values differ by Lr and (9) makes their m-values differ by -Ln. But n=vp>=VP=QH>Q, while both m-values lie in an interval of length less than Q. Hence L=0 and the two atoms coincide. There is therefore at most one atom for each d|A in one beta-fibre. The fixed-power divisor bound contained in fact 2359a25d9fc6dd9b gives
  max_beta #{x in cal X_o:beta_x=beta}<<_{C,epsilon}Q^epsilon. (10)
Consequently, if coefficients at identical beta are combined, Cauchy's inequality gives
  sum_beta|sum_{x:beta_x=beta}b_o(x)|^2
  <<_{C,epsilon}B^2Q^epsilon #cal X_o.                     (11)

For a positive integer D, restrict to atoms with D|r_x. Any two distinct beta-points in this restriction have reduced denominators r_1,r_2<2Q, both divisible by D. Their distance modulo one is at least
  1/lcm(r_1,r_2)
  =gcd(r_1,r_2)/(r_1r_2)
  >=D/(4Q^2).                                               (12)
Tuxanidy--Panario, arXiv:2307.16637, Lemma 1.6, states that for delta-spaced points alpha_j modulo one and coefficients c_h on an interval of N consecutive integers,
  sum_j|sum_h c_h e(alpha_j h)|^2
  <=(delta^(-1)+N-1)sum_h|c_h|^2.                          (13)
By Hilbert-space duality, the same constant bounds
  sum_h|sum_j C_j e(alpha_j h)|^2
  <=(delta^(-1)+N-1)sum_j|C_j|^2.                          (14)
Apply (14) to the distinct grouped beta-points, use (11)-(12), and use #I_ell<=2H. This gives
  sum_{h in I_ell}|z_{o,h}|^2
   |sum_{x in cal X_o,D|r_x}b_o(x)e(h beta_x)|^2
  <<_{C,epsilon}
   B^2Q^epsilon(H+Q^2/D)#cal X_o.                          (15)

We now expand the gcd threshold. For an integer D>=1 put
  lambda_D(G)=sum_{e|D,e>=G}mu(D/e).                        (16)
Möbius inversion gives, for every positive integer s,
  1_{s>=G}=sum_{D|s}lambda_D(G).                            (17)
Also lambda_D(G)=0 for D<G and |lambda_D(G)|<=tau(D). Insert (17), with s=gcd(r_{x_1},r_{x_2}), into (5). The inner form for fixed D is exactly the nonnegative quadratic form on the left of (15). Taking the triangle inequality only over D and applying (15) gives for each outer row
  |T_{G,o}^add|
  <<B^2Q^epsilon sum_{D>=G}
      tau(D)(H+Q^2/D)#{x in cal X_o:D|r_x}.                (18)
For each atom, the sum of tau(D) over D|r_x is Q^epsilon by the same fixed-power divisor estimate. Also 1/D<=1/G in the second term. Thus
  |T_{G,o}^add|
  <<_{C,epsilon}B^2Q^epsilon(H+Q^2/G)#cal X_o.             (19)

Fact 914048233fada05f gives
  #cal X_o<<_{C,epsilon}Q^epsilon(1+Q^2/n)
           <<_{C,epsilon}Q^(1+epsilon)/H,                  (20)
because n>=QH. There are O((#cal L)VP)=O((#cal L)QH) outer rows. Sum (19), insert (20), and absorb subpolynomial factors to prove (6).

Finally,
  [Q^2H]/[P Q^(5/3)]=V/Q^(2/3)<1,
while
  [Q^4/G]/[P Q^(5/3)]=VQ^(4/3)/(GH).
This proves (7). From V>=2 and H<=Q^(1/3), its right side threshold is at least 2Q. But r_x<2Q, so every gcd in a nonempty pair is less than 2Q. The phase identification and all scope statements follow from equations (10)-(11) of fact 1a9cfcfe3eedd5e2. This proves the theorem.

glossary.T_G^add: The gcd-threshold uncentered additive-core quadratic form.
glossary.beta_x: The reduced source phase t_x/r_x viewed modulo one.
glossary.lambda_D(G): The Möbius coefficient expanding the predicate n>=G over divisors D of n.

175003bf27fb8e0f.title: ABSTRACT FOUR-TERM ENDPOINT RIGHT-HAND-SIDE DIAGNOSTIC AND THE EXACT FIVE-ANATOMY COVERAGE REQUIREMENT
175003bf27fb8e0f.author: slava chan
175003bf27fb8e0f.statement:
ABSTRACT FOUR-TERM ENDPOINT RIGHT-HAND-SIDE DIAGNOSTIC AND THE EXACT FIVE-ANATOMY COVERAGE REQUIREMENT.

Let \(Q\) tend to infinity, let \(1\le\beta<6/5\), put
\[
 H_T=Q^{\beta-1},
\]
and consider a direct application at \(G=1\) of fact
\(95626318cdcc099f\), equivalently the four algebraic terms of fact
\(42720f6d803c4640\), with two factor scales \(S,T\) satisfying
\(ST\asymp QH_T\). Write
\[
 S=Q^{s+O(1/\log Q)},\qquad
 \Delta_-=s-(2\beta-2),\qquad
 \Delta_+=(3-2\beta)-s.                                      \tag{1}
\]
Relative to \(Q^2\), the four displayed terms in that theorem are,
up to \(Q^{o(1)}\),
\[
 Q^{-\Delta_-/4},\qquad Q^{-\Delta_+/4},\qquad
 Q^{-\Delta_-/2},\qquad Q^{-(5/4-\beta)}.                    \tag{2}
\]

Therefore a direct insertion with
\[
 s=\beta/2+O(1/\log Q)                                       \tag{3}
\]
has in its second right-hand-side term only the certified gain
\[
 Q^{-(6-5\beta)/8+o(1)},                                     \tag{4}
\]
while a direct insertion with
\[
 s=\beta/3+O(1/\log Q)                                       \tag{5}
\]
has in its first and third terms only the certified gains
\[
 Q^{-(6-5\beta)/12+o(1)},\qquad
 Q^{-(6-5\beta)/6+o(1)}.                                    \tag{6}
\]
Along \(\beta=6/5-C/\log Q\), with fixed \(C>0\), (4) and (6)
are nonzero constants rather than fixed negative powers of \(Q\).
Consequently the stated four-term theorem, invoked directly on blocks
with (3) or (5), does not by itself certify
\(O(Q^{2-\delta})\) for one fixed \(\delta>0\) independent of
\(\beta\). This is only a diagnostic of that theorem's nonnegative
right-hand side under the displayed substitutions. It does not assert
that (3) or (5) is a verified literal reduction of any particular
anatomy, does not give a lower bound for any trace, and does not rule out
another decomposition or estimate.

There is an independent exact anatomy-coverage conclusion. Let
\(\mathcal T_{\rm nonA,top}\) denote the complete joint projection of the
selected top sliver in fact \(e58fc7c00f1683e6\) onto
\[
 B,\quad C1,\quad C2,\quad C3,\quad C4.                       \tag{7}
\]
This definition makes no assertion that the remaining \(A\) anatomy has
already been estimated or removed. One proposed single joint interface for
(7), weaker than five separate absolute-value bounds because it permits
cross-anatomy cancellation, is
\[
 |\mathcal T_{\rm nonA,top}|
 \ll GQ^{2-\delta_*}\quad(G\ge1),                             \tag{CS-5F}
\]
and
\[
 |\mathcal T_{\rm nonA,top}|
 \ll Q^{2-\delta_*}
 \quad(Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\le G\le Q^{\sigma-\eta}),             \tag{CS-5N}
\]
uniformly for \(\beta_m\le\beta<6/5\), with one fixed
\(\delta_*>0\), after every selected-source, fixed-\(U\), exact-\(g\),
target, actual-frequency, phase, target-gcd, order/equal-cell, collision,
deletion and provenance coordinate is retained and recombined as specified
in fact \(e58fc7c00f1683e6\). CS-5 is an open interface and is not
asserted here.

From exact anatomy and total sign alone, a \(C4\)-only estimate cannot
control (7). Such a reduction requires verifier-accepted estimates for the
\(B,C1,C2,C3\) complement or a verifier-accepted sign/localization theorem.
No complete-top-sliver estimate, \(A\) estimate, endpoint conclusion or
Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
175003bf27fb8e0f.proof:
Set \(G=1\) in fact \(95626318cdcc099f\). Then
\(H_P=H_T\), and its four displayed terms are
\[
 Q^2H_T^{1/2}S^{-1/4},\quad
 Q^{7/4}H_T^{1/2}S^{1/4},\quad
 Q^2H_TS^{-1/2},\quad Q^{7/4}H_T.
\]
Substitute \(H_T=Q^{\beta-1}\) and
\(S=Q^{s+O(1/\log Q)}\). After division by \(Q^2\), their
exponents are
\[
 {2\beta-2-s\over4}=-{\Delta_-\over4},\quad
 {2\beta+s-3\over4}=-{\Delta_+\over4},\quad
 {2\beta-2-s\over2}=-{\Delta_-\over2},\quad
 \beta-{5\over4}.
\]
This proves (2); fact \(42720f6d803c4640\) has the same four
algebraic terms.

If \(s=\beta/2+O(1/\log Q)\), then
\[
 \Delta_+={6-5\beta\over2}+O(1/\log Q),
\]
so the second term in (2) is (4). If
\(s=\beta/3+O(1/\log Q)\), then
\[
 \Delta_-={6-5\beta\over3}+O(1/\log Q),
\]
so the first and third terms are (6). For
\(\beta=6/5-C/\log Q\),
\[
 Q^{-(6-5\beta)/8}=e^{-5C/8},\quad
 Q^{-(6-5\beta)/12}=e^{-5C/12},\quad
 Q^{-(6-5\beta)/6}=e^{-5C/6}.
\]
Because the accepted estimate presents a sum of nonnegative upper-bound
terms, its direct invocation cannot discard the binding displayed term.
This proves exactly the scoped right-hand-side diagnostic and no statement
about a literal anatomy reduction or trace size.

For the coverage assertion, fact \(e58fc7c00f1683e6\) gives the exact
source-preserving top-sliver list
\[
 A,B,C1,C2,C3,C4
\]
and assigns no sign to any proper cell. Removing only the \(A\) coordinate
as a matter of definition leaves exactly (7); no estimate for \(A\) is
inferred. A bound for the single joint sum in (7) is logically weaker than
five separate absolute bounds by the triangle inequality and permits
cancellation between anatomies.

Finally fact \(7c1f38cfbb8d0569\) proves that an exact
sign-preserving anatomy partition and a negative total do not localize the
negative mass into a prescribed rough class: its one-incidence signed
coefficient model may put all negative mass in any chosen non-\(C4\)
class while the \(C4\) sum is zero. Thus a \(C4\)-only estimate cannot
control the complete non-\(A\) sum (7) from anatomy and total sign alone.
An independent complement estimate or sign theorem is necessary. This
establishes the final scope statement without asserting CS-5 or any
complete-top-sliver estimate.

glossary.CS-5: The proposed single joint uniform fixed-power trace bound for T_nonA,top.
glossary.Delta_+: The upper four-term balanced-window margin (3-2 beta)-s.
glossary.Delta_-: The lower four-term balanced-window margin s-(2 beta-2).
glossary.T_nonA,top: The exact joint top-sliver aggregate of anatomies B,C1,C2,C3,C4, without any assertion that A has been removed.

17557ebe80636618.title: Let H>=2, let I_H=[H^2,2H^2) intersect Z, let C be a nonzero integer, let K be an integer, and let r_2,r_3 be distinct primes in I_H. Let m>1 be odd and assume gcd(m,2 K r_2 r_3)=1. For a residue z modulo m, let ev_m(z) be the unique even integer in the interval (-m,m] that is congruent to z modulo m
17557ebe80636618.author: slava chan
17557ebe80636618.statement:
Let H>=2, let I_H=[H^2,2H^2) intersect Z, let C be a nonzero integer, let K be an integer, and let r_2,r_3 be distinct primes in I_H. Let m>1 be odd and assume gcd(m,2 K r_2 r_3)=1. For a residue z modulo m, let ev_m(z) be the unique even integer in the interval (-m,m] that is congruent to z modulo m.

For every unit t modulo m define
a0=ev_m(t r_2^{-1}),
b0=ev_m(K r_2 t^{-1}),
c0=ev_m(t r_3^{-1}),
d0=ev_m(K r_3 t^{-1}),
and define the integer
delta_K=(2 K-a0b0-c0d0)/(2m).
Then every even integer quadruple reducing to this torus point has a unique expression
a=a0+2mx, b=b0+2my, c=c0+2mz, d=d0+2mw
with x,y,z,w integers. It satisfies the exact determinant identity ab+cd=2 K if and only if
a0 y+b0 x+c0 w+d0 z+2m(xy+zw)=delta_K.                 (1)

Define the base carries
alpha0=(b0 r_3-d0 r_2)/(2m),
beta0=(a0 r_2-c0 r_3)/(2m),
j0=(a0b0-c0d0)/(4m).
They are integers. For every lift satisfying (1), put
lambda_A=alpha0+y r_3-w r_2,
lambda_B=beta0+x r_2-z r_3,
lambda_J=j0+(a0y+b0x-c0w-d0z)/2+m(xy-zw).               (2)
Then, for
A=b r_3-d r_2, B=a r_2-c r_3, J=ab-cd,
one has
A=2m lambda_A, B=2m lambda_B, J=4m lambda_J.

The lift is a normalized unit state of fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb with q=gcd(|A|,|B|)=2m if and only if all of the following literal conditions hold:
(a) lambda_A lambda_B>0 and gcd(|lambda_A|,|lambda_B|)=1;
(b) r_1=|lambda_A| and r_4=|lambda_B| are primes in I_H and r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4 are pairwise distinct;
(c) gcd(C,r_1r_2r_3r_4)=1;
(d) lambda_J is nonzero;
(e) with s the common sign of lambda_A and lambda_B,
d r_2 lambda_B-c r_3 lambda_A=2sC.
When these conditions hold, the recovered short coordinates are v=sm and u=s lambda_J.

For every real coefficient bound X_box>=0, the additional literal box |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|<=X_box is exactly the conjunction
|a0+2mx|<=X_box, |b0+2my|<=X_box,
|c0+2mz|<=X_box, |d0+2mw|<=X_box.
Thus the generic full-conductor integer family is an affine bilinear lift hypersurface over the unit torus, with the prime quotients, normal carries, signs, distinctness, C-unit condition, and coefficient boxes retained as explicit selectors rather than inferred from reduction modulo m.
17557ebe80636618.proof:
Because m is odd, multiplication by 2 permutes the residue classes modulo m. The interval (-m,m] contains exactly m even integers, no two congruent modulo m. Hence ev_m(z) exists and is unique for every residue z.

Fact d472dd752c1eb6a8 proves that the four displayed residues parameterized by t are exactly the generic torus locus modulo m. An even integer congruent to a0 modulo m differs from a0 by a multiple of m. Since both integers are even and m is odd, the multiplier is even, so the difference is a multiple of 2m. This proves the unique expressions for a,b,c,d.

Expansion gives
ab+cd
 =a0b0+c0d0
  +2m(a0y+b0x+c0w+d0z)
  +4m^2(xy+zw).
The torus congruence gives a0b0+c0d0=2 K modulo m. The difference 2 K-a0b0-c0d0 is even and divisible by the odd integer m, hence divisible by 2m; thus delta_K is integral. Equating the expansion to 2 K and dividing by 2m proves the equivalence with (1).

The torus linear congruences imply m divides b0 r_3-d0 r_2 and a0 r_2-c0 r_3. These numerators are even, so 2m divides them and alpha0,beta0 are integers. The torus also gives a0b0-c0d0=0 modulo m. This difference is divisible by 4 because all four representatives are even. Since gcd(4,m)=1, it is divisible by 4m, proving that j0 is integral.

Substituting the lift formulas into A and B gives
A=(b0 r_3-d0 r_2)+2m(y r_3-w r_2)=2m lambda_A,
B=(a0 r_2-c0 r_3)+2m(x r_2-z r_3)=2m lambda_B.
Similarly,
J=(a0b0-c0d0)
 +2m(a0y+b0x-c0w-d0z)
 +4m^2(xy-zw)
 =4m lambda_J.
This proves every formula in (2); the half of the middle linear expression is integral because a0,b0,c0,d0 are even.

We now prove the normalized-state equivalence. Suppose first that the lift is a normalized unit state of fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb and q=2m. That fact gives AB>0, the common sign s, primes r_1=|A|/q and r_4=|B|/q in I_H with all four corners pairwise distinct, gcd(C,r_1r_2r_3r_4)=1, J a nonzero multiple of 2q, and D=2sqC, where
D=ad r_2^2-bc r_3^2.
Since A=2m lambda_A, B=2m lambda_B and q=2m, one obtains
r_1=|lambda_A|, r_4=|lambda_B|,
lambda_A lambda_B>0, and
gcd(|lambda_A|,|lambda_B|)=gcd(|A|,|B|)/(2m)=1.
Also J=4m lambda_J is nonzero. Fact d472dd752c1eb6a8 proves the exact identity
D=2m(d r_2 lambda_B-c r_3 lambda_A).
Comparing it with D=2s(2m)C proves condition (e). Thus conditions (a)-(e) are necessary.

Conversely, assume (1) and conditions (a)-(e). The formulas for A and B show AB>0. Condition (a) gives
gcd(|A|,|B|)=2m gcd(|lambda_A|,|lambda_B|)=2m,
so q=2m. Condition (b) says that the normalized quotients |A|/q and |B|/q are exactly the required pairwise-distinct dyadic primes r_1,r_4. Condition (c) is the required unit condition. Condition (d) and J=4m lambda_J show that J is a nonzero multiple of 2q. Finally, the exact D-identity from fact d472dd752c1eb6a8 and condition (e) give
D=2m(2sC)=2sqC.
All clauses (II) of fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb now hold, so its equivalence proves that the lift is a normalized unit state. Its recovery formulas give
v=sq/2=sm,
u=sJ/(2q)=s(4m lambda_J)/(4m)=s lambda_J.

The coefficient-box equivalence follows by direct substitution of the four unique lift expressions. No congruence or cancellation estimate is used. Therefore every selector listed in the final sentence is retained literally on the lift hypersurface.

glossary.X_box: a nonnegative real bound for the four integer coefficients
glossary.a0: the canonical even representative of the torus residue of a
glossary.b0: the canonical even representative of the torus residue of b
glossary.c0: the canonical even representative of the torus residue of c
glossary.d0: the canonical even representative of the torus residue of d
glossary.ev_m: the unique even representative in (-m,m] of a residue modulo odd m
glossary.w_lift: the integer lift coordinate denoted w in d=d0+2mw
glossary.x: the integer lift coordinate in a=a0+2mx
glossary.y: the integer lift coordinate in b=b0+2my
glossary.z: the integer lift coordinate in c=c0+2mz

175907af543c5308.title: For every integer q>1 define two real-valued functions by
175907af543c5308.author: slava chan
175907af543c5308.statement:
For every integer q>1 define two real-valued functions by
L_lt(q)=sum_{r k=q, r<k^2} mu(r) log(k),
L_ge(q)=sum_{r k=q, r>=k^2} mu(r) log(k),
where the sums range over positive integer factorizations q=r k. Then
L_lt(22)=log(2)>0 and L_ge(22)=-log(2)<0,
whereas
L_lt(385)=-log(35)<0 and L_ge(385)=log(35)>0.
Moreover L_lt(q)+L_ge(q)=0 for q=22 and q=385. Consequently each truncated coefficient takes both signs even on composite integers that are not prime powers; neither side of the cut r<k^2 versus r>=k^2 has a fixed pointwise sign on that class. Since for q=r k the inequality r<k^2 is equivalent to 2 log(r)/log(q)<4/3, this is exactly a two-sided sign obstruction at the nonterminal/terminal cut used in fact aa34b1862b993377.
175907af543c5308.proof:
For q=22, its positive divisors r are 1,2,11,22, with complementary factors k equal to 22,11,2,1. The pairs with r<k^2 are (1,22) and (2,11), while (11,2) and (22,1) have r>=k^2. Since mu(2)=mu(11)=-1 and log(1)=0,
L_lt(22)=log(22)-log(11)=log(2)>0,
and
L_ge(22)=-log(2)+mu(22)log(1)=-log(2)<0.
Their sum is zero.

For q=385, the positive divisors r are
1,5,7,11,35,55,77,385,
with complementary factors k respectively
385,77,55,35,11,7,5,1.
For the first five pairs one has r<k^2: the only closest comparison is 35<11^2=121. For the last three pairs one has r>=k^2, since 55>=7^2=49, 77>=5^2=25, and 385>=1^2.

Because 385 is squarefree with three prime factors, the Moebius values on the displayed divisors are determined by the parity of their number of prime factors. Therefore
L_lt(385)
=log(385)-log(77)-log(55)-log(35)+log(11).
Using 385=5*7*11, 77=7*11, 55=5*11, and 35=5*7, this simplifies to
L_lt(385)=-log(5)-log(7)=-log(35)<0.
On the complementary side, the r=55 and r=77 terms have Moebius value +1, while the r=385 term is multiplied by log(1)=0. Thus
L_ge(385)=log(7)+log(5)=log(35)>0.
Their sum is zero. Both 22 and 385 are composite and have at least two distinct prime factors, so neither is a prime power. The four displayed strict inequalities prove that each function takes both signs on the declared class.

Finally, for any factorization q=r k with q>1, positivity of log(q)=log(r)+log(k) permits cross multiplication:
2 log(r)/log(q)<4/3
if and only if 6 log(r)<4 log(r)+4 log(k),
if and only if log(r)<2 log(k),
if and only if r<k^2.
Thus the sign failures occur at exactly the stated scale cut.

glossary.L_ge: the real-valued function whose value at q is the sum of mu(r)log(k) over positive factorizations q=rk satisfying r>=k^2
glossary.L_lt: the real-valued function whose value at q is the sum of mu(r)log(k) over positive factorizations q=rk satisfying r<k^2

17bda5948d58822e.title: FIXED-POWER PAYMENT OF A CONCRETE GENUINELY UNBALANCED LITERAL C1 DYNAMIC NEAR-PRIME CHAMBER. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100 and K_0>=2. Let Q be sufficiently large. In the literal strict-top C1 setting let n=pv be squarefree, where p is the unique rough prime and gcd(p,v)=1, put C=mathscr A h and m_eff=n/gcd(C,n), and assume Q^(1/2+kappa)<=m_eff<=Q^(6/5), p does not divide C, and m_eff=p r_eff with r_eff<=Q^(1/100). Let c be squarefree with nc<=Q^K_0, and let W be extended by zero, supported on Q<=q<2Q, with V_Q(W)<=Q^epsilon for every fixed epsilon>0
17bda5948d58822e.author: slava chan
17bda5948d58822e.statement:
FIXED-POWER PAYMENT OF A CONCRETE GENUINELY UNBALANCED LITERAL C1 DYNAMIC NEAR-PRIME CHAMBER. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100 and K_0>=2. Let Q be sufficiently large. In the literal strict-top C1 setting let n=pv be squarefree, where p is the unique rough prime and gcd(p,v)=1, put C=mathscr A h and m_eff=n/gcd(C,n), and assume Q^(1/2+kappa)<=m_eff<=Q^(6/5), p does not divide C, and m_eff=p r_eff with r_eff<=Q^(1/100). Let c be squarefree with nc<=Q^K_0, and let W be extended by zero, supported on Q<=q<2Q, with V_Q(W)<=Q^epsilon for every fixed epsilon>0.

Fix one MULTI-FREE dyadic box from the exact routing of fact 8eb30e55bdef6b27. Let B_* be its deterministically selected largest omitted coefficient-one scale and write B_*=Q^(b_*+o(1)). Convolve every other factor position into a variable a of scale A, with divisor-bounded coefficient alpha_a, and retain the selected free variable b of scale B_*, so AB_* is comparable to Q. Assume
7/20<=b_*<=13/20,
Q^(7/10)<=p<=Q^(9/10).                                          (1)
Let S_box be the complete sum of this box, with its signed convolution coefficient, literal product weight W(ab), gate gcd(ab,nc)=1, and reciprocal phase e_n(C(ab)^(-1)). Then
|S_box|<=Q^(1-41/6400+o(1)).                                    (2)
In particular every genuine R3 dynamic near-prime box satisfying (1) and r_eff<=Q^(1/100) is paid. This theorem does not estimate dynamic near-prime boxes outside the displayed factor and prime ranges, nor the G1/G2 width failures.
17bda5948d58822e.proof:
Because n is squarefree and m_eff=n/gcd(C,n), writing g=gcd(C,n) and C'=C/g gives gcd(C',m_eff)=1 and, on the unit support,
e_n(C(ab)^(-1))=e_{m_eff}(C'(ab)^(-1)).                         (3)
Since p does not divide C, the unique rough prime p survives in m_eff; by hypothesis m_eff=p r_eff, where r_eff is squarefree and gcd(p,r_eff)=1.

Fact 8eb30e55bdef6b27 proves for the fixed MULTI-FREE box that the deterministic grouping has AB_* comparable to Q, the b-variable is coefficient one, alpha_a is bounded by a fixed divisor function, and the literal W, phase, and complete gate are retained. The additional primes in the gate gcd(ab,nc)=1 can be represented by a squarefree auxiliary modulus whose product with p r_eff is at most Q to a fixed power, because nc<=Q^K_0. Thus the sum after (3) is an instance of fact 183c9310b93b9005.

Put alpha=1-b_* and pi=log(p)/log(Q). The dyadic relation AB_* comparable to Q gives A=Q^(alpha+o(1)). From (1),
7/20<=alpha<=13/20,
7/10<=pi<=9/10.                                                  (4)
Therefore max(alpha,b_*)<=13/20<7/10<=pi with fixed slack. Also
b_*>=7/20>9/40>=pi/4,                                           (5)
so the interval-length hypothesis for fact 183c9310b93b9005 holds with its moment parameter R=4.

For R=4, the two exponent gains inside that fact are alpha and
1+b_*-(5/4)pi.
Equations (1),(4) give
alpha>=7/20,
1+b_*-(5/4)pi>=1+7/20-(5/4)(9/10)=9/40.                        (6)
Thus their minimum is at least 9/40. The prime-bilinear saving before the small-complement tax is therefore at least
(7/96)(9/40)=21/1280.                                           (7)
The factor r_eff<=Q^(1/100) costs at most Q^(1/100). Since
21/1280-1/100=41/6400,                                          (8)
fact 183c9310b93b9005 and equations (3)-(8) prove (2), after absorbing every divisor, variation, dyadic, and fixed-convolution loss into Q^o(1). The final R3 conclusion is immediate because it only restricts the already estimated boxes.

glossary.b_*: The exponent log(B_*)/log(Q) of the largest omitted coefficient-one scale.
glossary.pi: The exponent log(p)/log(Q) of the unique strict-top C1 rough prime.

1813c7a42cfeab55.title: OPTIMAL DIAGONAL SPLIT OF A POSITIVE COORDINATE ENVELOPE. Let \(\mathscr A\) be a finite nonempty set and let \(E_\alpha>0\) for every \(\alpha\in\mathscr A\). For arbitrary positive real numbers \(s_\alpha\), define
1813c7a42cfeab55.author: slava chan
1813c7a42cfeab55.statement:
OPTIMAL DIAGONAL SPLIT OF A POSITIVE COORDINATE ENVELOPE. Let \(\mathscr A\) be a finite nonempty set and let \(E_\alpha>0\) for every \(\alpha\in\mathscr A\). For arbitrary positive real numbers \(s_\alpha\), define
\[
 \mathcal B(s)=\left(\sum_{\alpha\in\mathscr A}s_\alpha^2E_\alpha^2\right)^{1/2},
 \qquad
 \mathcal K(s)=\left(\sum_{\alpha\in\mathscr A}s_\alpha^{-2}\right)^{1/2}. \tag{1}
\]
Then
\[
 \mathcal B(s)\mathcal K(s)\ge\sum_{\alpha\in\mathscr A}E_\alpha. \tag{2}
\]
Equality holds when \(s_\alpha=cE_\alpha^{-1/2}\) for any fixed \(c>0\). Consequently the envelope-weighted reconstruction of fact cf6e2f624d3b1a82 minimizes, among all positive diagonal coordinate rescalings, the product of the coordinatewise-envelope upper bound for the vector norm and the reconstruction-vector norm.
1813c7a42cfeab55.proof:
Apply Cauchy--Schwarz to the two finite real sequences \(s_\alpha E_\alpha\) and \(s_\alpha^{-1}\):
\[
 \left(\sum_\alpha E_\alpha\right)^2
 =\left(\sum_\alpha(s_\alpha E_\alpha)s_\alpha^{-1}\right)^2
 \le\left(\sum_\alpha s_\alpha^2E_\alpha^2\right)
    \left(\sum_\alpha s_\alpha^{-2}\right)
 =\mathcal B(s)^2\mathcal K(s)^2.
\]
All quantities are nonnegative, so taking square roots proves (2). If \(s_\alpha=cE_\alpha^{-1/2}\), then
\[
 \mathcal B(s)^2=c^2\sum_\alpha E_\alpha,\qquad
 \mathcal K(s)^2=c^{-2}\sum_\alpha E_\alpha,
\]
and their product is \(\sum_\alpha E_\alpha\), proving equality and the minimizing assertion. In the reconstruction of fact cf6e2f624d3b1a82 one takes \(c=1\), so \(s_\alpha=E_\alpha^{-1/2}\).

glossary.mathcal B(s): the envelope-derived upper-bound factor for the rescaled vector norm
glossary.mathcal K(s): the norm factor of the corresponding reconstruction vector

183c9310b93b9005.title: ASYMMETRIC PRODUCT-BV BILINEAR SUPPLIER FOR A PRIME TIMES A SMALL COMPLEMENT. Fix integers J>=1, K_0>=1, and R>=1. Let Q be sufficiently large. Let p be prime and r_0 a positive squarefree integer with gcd(p,r_0)=1. Let C be an integer with gcd(C,pr_0)=1, and let c be a positive squarefree integer with cpr_0<=Q^K_0. Let I_A=[A,2A) intersect Z and I_B=[B,2B) intersect Z, where Q/4<=AB<=4Q, 4max(A,B)<p, and B>=4p^(1/R). Let alpha_a be supported on I_A with |alpha_a|<=tau_J(a). Let W be extended by zero, supported on Q<=k<2Q, and satisfy V_Q(W)<=Q^epsilon for every fixed epsilon>0. Then
183c9310b93b9005.author: slava chan
183c9310b93b9005.statement:
ASYMMETRIC PRODUCT-BV BILINEAR SUPPLIER FOR A PRIME TIMES A SMALL COMPLEMENT. Fix integers J>=1, K_0>=1, and R>=1. Let Q be sufficiently large. Let p be prime and r_0 a positive squarefree integer with gcd(p,r_0)=1. Let C be an integer with gcd(C,pr_0)=1, and let c be a positive squarefree integer with cpr_0<=Q^K_0. Let I_A=[A,2A) intersect Z and I_B=[B,2B) intersect Z, where Q/4<=AB<=4Q, 4max(A,B)<p, and B>=4p^(1/R). Let alpha_a be supported on I_A with |alpha_a|<=tau_J(a). Let W be extended by zero, supported on Q<=k<2Q, and satisfy V_Q(W)<=Q^epsilon for every fixed epsilon>0. Then
S=sum_{a in I_A,b in I_B;gcd(ab,cpr_0)=1}alpha_a W(ab)e_{pr_0}(C(ab)^(-1))
satisfies
|S| <= r_0 AB Q^o(1)[A^(-1)+p^(1+1/R)/(AB^2)]^(7/(24R)).       (1)
The o(1) is uniform in the displayed data for fixed J,K_0,R.

In particular, suppose for fixed exponents alpha,b,pi,chi and fixed positive slack that A=Q^(alpha+o(1)), B=Q^(b+o(1)), p=Q^(pi+o(1)), r_0<=Q^(chi+o(1)), alpha+b=1, max(alpha,b)<pi, b>pi/R, and
gamma=(7/(24R))min{alpha,1+b-(1+1/R)pi}-chi>0.                 (2)
Then |S|<=Q^(1-gamma+o(1)). This theorem retains the literal BV product weight, divisor-bounded carrier, complete unit and auxiliary coprimality gates, and all CRT residue taxes. It is a conditional asymmetric supplier; no assertion that every unbalanced G3 box satisfies (2) is made.
183c9310b93b9005.proof:
Partition each real dyadic interval [A,2A) and [B,2B) into its two half-open multiplicative subintervals cut at sqrt(2) times the lower endpoint. This creates four subrectangles. Discard any subrectangle whose product set misses [Q,2Q). On a retained subrectangle, the ratio of its largest to smallest product is at most two; because it meets [Q,2Q), its whole product range lies in [Q/4,4Q]. Fact e446377f3ab5a559 therefore separates W(ab), including its zero extension, into bounded one-variable tensors with total projective mass O(V_Q(W)log Q)=Q^o(1), plus an arbitrarily power-small aggregate remainder. The divisor-bounded alpha_a costs Q^o(1), while the gate gcd(ab,cpr_0)=1 factors into two bounded one-variable gates. It suffices to bound one separated tensor on one subrectangle. We record the external input. Kerr--Shparlinski--Wu--Xi, arXiv:2204.05038, Theorem 2.5 states: if p is prime, R is a fixed positive integer, mathcal M is an arbitrary subset of F_p of cardinality M, mathcal K is an interval in F_p^* of length K>=p^(1/R), alpha_m and gamma_k are arbitrary bounded separated coefficients, and A_0 is a unit modulo p, then |sum_{m in mathcal M}sum_{k in mathcal K}alpha_m gamma_k e_p(A_0 m k^(-1))| <=MKp^o(1)[1/M+p^(1+1/R)/(MK^2)]^(7/(24R)). (3) The definitions here match the paper: mathcal M has no interval or additive-structure assumption, mathcal K is a genuine interval, and the coefficients are separated and bounded. Split the CRT phase. For r_0>1, choose the standard inverses and write e_{pr_0}(C(ab)^(-1)) =e_p(C r_0^(-1)(ab)^(-1)) e_{r_0}(C p^(-1)(ab)^(-1)). (4) Split b according to its unit residue modulo r_0, using at most r_0 classes. On one such class the second factor in (4) is a bounded one-variable function of a, while the class indicator is a bounded one-variable coefficient in b. For r_0=1 there is one class and the second factor is absent. On a fixed class and subrectangle, map a to m=a^(-1) modulo p and put k=b. The condition 4max(A,B)

=4p^(1/R) ensures K>=p^(1/R). The p-phase in (4) is exactly e_p(A_0 m k^(-1)) with the unit A_0=C r_0^(-1) modulo p. After dividing the divisor-bounded a-coefficient by its Q^o(1) supremum, all hypotheses of (3) hold. Therefore one class is bounded by ABQ^o(1)[A^(-1)+p^(1+1/R)/(AB^2)]^(7/(24R)). (5) Summing at most r_0 classes, the four subrectangles, and the Q^o(1) tensor mass proves (1). For the exponent corollary, the hypotheses max(alpha,b)pi/R, with fixed slack, imply 4max(A,B)

=4p^(1/R) for large Q. The two terms in the bracket of (1) are Q^(-alpha+o(1)) and Q^(-[1+b-(1+1/R)pi]+o(1)), respectively. Equation (2) and r_0<=Q^(chi+o(1)) therefore turn (1) into Q^(1-gamma+o(1)). This proves every assertion.

glossary.R: The fixed positive integer moment parameter in Kerr--Shparlinski--Wu--Xi Theorem 2.5.
glossary.r_0: The squarefree complementary factor to the prime p in the effective modulus p r_0.

18a0de57eaf35171.title: ABSTRACT DISJOINT PMLS CRT/OPERATOR NORMAL FORM AND MULTIPLICATIVE-CHARACTER DIAGONAL. For a positive integer m put G_m=(Z/mZ)^*, let e_m(a)=exp(2pi i a/m), and define
18a0de57eaf35171.author: slava chan
18a0de57eaf35171.statement:
ABSTRACT DISJOINT PMLS CRT/OPERATOR NORMAL FORM AND MULTIPLICATIVE-CHARACTER DIAGONAL. For a positive integer m put G_m=(Z/mZ)^*, let e_m(a)=exp(2pi i a/m), and define
 S_m(a,b)=sum_{u in G_m}e_m(au+bu^{-1}).                            (1)
Let r,r'>1 be coprime squarefree integers, put L=rr', and let A,k,h satisfy gcd(Akh,L)=1. Put c=Ak^{-2} modulo r and c'=Ak^{-2} modulo r'. For functions f on G_r and g on G_{r'}, and a finitely supported function w on Z, define
 what_L(t)=sum_{j,gcd(j,L)=1}w(j)e_L(-tj),                          (2)
 B_{r,r'}(f,g;w,h,k)=sum_{j,gcd(j,L)=1}w(j)
 [sum_{x in G_r}f(x)e_r(chxj^{-1})]
 conjugate([sum_{y in G_{r'}}g(y)e_{r'}(c'hyj^{-1})]).              (3)
For a modulo r put
 Kcal_{r,c,h}f(a)=sum_{x in G_r}f(x)r^{-1}S_r(a,chx),               (4)
and define the analogous r' expression. Then exactly
 B_{r,r'}(f,g;w,h,k)=sum_{t mod L}what_L(t)
 Kcal_{r,c,h}f(t(r')^{-1})
 conjugate(Kcal_{r',c',h}g(-tr^{-1})).                              (5)
Thus each partner enters the other local transform through its modular inverse.

For the unit-completion block gcd(t,L)=1 define, on G_r,
 K_{r,c}(u)=r^{-1}S_r(1,cu),
 (T_{r,c}f)(y)=sum_{x in G_r}f(x)K_{r,c}(xy).                       (6)
The t-summand in (5) is then
 what_L(t)(T_{r,c}f)(ht(r')^{-1})
 conjugate((T_{r',c'}g)(-htr^{-1})).                               (7)
For a character chi modulo r define
 fhat(chi)=phi(r)^{-1}sum_{x in G_r}f(x)conjugate(chi(x)),
 tau_r(chi)=sum_{u in G_r}chi(u)e_r(u),                             (8)
and
 m_{r,c}(chi)=chi(c)tau_r(conjugate chi)^2/r.                       (9)
Then
 widehat(T_{r,c}f)(chi)=m_{r,c}(chi)fhat(conjugate chi).            (10)
If chi is induced by a primitive character of conductor d_chi|r, then
 |m_{r,c}(chi)|=d_chi/r.                                           (11)
Thus the principal multiplier is exactly 1/r and primitive multipliers have absolute value one. Fourier inversion gives

 (T_{r,c}f)(ht(r')^{-1})conjugate((T_{r',c'}g)(-htr^{-1}))
 =sum_{chi mod r}sum_{psi mod r'}
 m_{r,c}(chi)conjugate(m_{r',c'}(psi))
 fhat(conjugate chi)conjugate(ghat(conjugate psi))
 chi(ht)conjugate(chi(r'))conjugate(psi(-ht))psi(r).                (12)

There is also a completely defined quadratic-form interface. Let Rcal be a finite family of squarefree integers greater than one, Hcal a finite set of nonzero integers, and Zcal a finite row-label set. For each r in Rcal let Zcal_r be a subset of Zcal, let x_{r,rho} belong to G_r and alpha_{r,rho} be complex for rho in Zcal_r, and define
 (I_rz)(x)=sum_{rho in Zcal_r:x_{r,rho}=x}alpha_{r,rho}z_rho.       (13)
Fix k coprime to every r in Rcal and, for each h in Hcal, a finitely supported common integer weight w_{k,h}. Define
 Q_k(z)=sum_{h in Hcal}sum_{r,r' in Rcal;r!=r',gcd(r,r')=1}
 B_{r,r'}(I_rz,I_{r'}z;w_{k,h},h,k).                               (14)
On the finite Hilbert direct sum Xcal=direct_sum_{r in Rcal}l2(G_r), let A_k be the unique block operator whose (r,r') sesquilinear block is the sum over h of B_{r,r'} with the displayed common weights, and whose diagonal and noncoprime blocks are zero. Then, with Iz=(I_rz)_r,
 Q_k(z)=<Iz,A_kIz>_Xcal.                                           (15)
If every w_{k,h} is real, the ordered-pair sum makes Q_k real. Equations (5), (12), and (15) are exact. They do not estimate A_k, identify these abstract data with a literal source, pay nonunit t, handle shared moduli, prove a C4 estimate, or imply Goldbach.
18a0de57eaf35171.proof:
Group w by residues modulo L. If W(a)=sum_{j congruent a mod L}w(j)1_{gcd(j,L)=1}, finite Fourier inversion gives
 W(a)=L^{-1}sum_{t mod L}what_L(t)e_L(ta).                          (16)
Insert this in (3). CRT factors the complete unit-residue sum, for fixed x,y,t, as
 sum_{a in G_L}e_L(ta)e_r(chxa^{-1})e_{r'}(-c'hya^{-1})
 =S_r(t(r')^{-1},chx)S_{r'}(tr^{-1},-c'hy).                        (17)
After division by L=rr', the first factor summed against f is (4). Since conjugate(S_{r'}(-a,b))=S_{r'}(a,-b), the second factor summed against conjugate(g) is the conjugate of Kcal_{r',c',h}g(-tr^{-1}). This proves (5).

For unit a, substitution u=a^{-1}v in (1) gives S_m(a,b)=S_m(1,ab). Apply this to both local factors in (5) when gcd(t,L)=1 to obtain (7).

For (10), substitute u=xy in the multiplicative Fourier transform of (6):
 widehat(T_{r,c}f)(chi)=fhat(conjugate chi)
 sum_{u in G_r}K_{r,c}(u)conjugate(chi(u)).                         (18)
Expanding K and, in the inner sum, putting a=cuv^{-1}, gives
 sum_{u in G_r}K_{r,c}(u)conjugate(chi(u))
 =chi(c)tau_r(conjugate chi)^2/r.                                  (19)
This is (9)-(10).

We prove (11) without an external citation. Let chi be induced by a primitive chi_star modulo d=d_chi and write r=dm. Since r is squarefree, gcd(d,m)=1. Direct CRT summation gives
 tau_r(chi)=mu(m)chi_star(m)tau_d(chi_star).                        (20)
It remains to find the primitive magnitude. Extend chi_star by zero to Z/dZ and put
 T(n)=sum_{a mod d}chi_star(a)e_d(an).                              (21)
If gcd(n,d)=1, substitution b=an gives T(n)=conjugate(chi_star(n))tau_d(chi_star). If gcd(n,d)>1 and d>1, primitivity supplies a unit u congruent to 1 modulo d/gcd(n,d) with chi_star(u)!=1; otherwise chi_star would factor through the proper divisor d/gcd(n,d). Multiplication a by u leaves e_d(an) unchanged and multiplies (21) by chi_star(u), so T(n)=0. Finite additive Parseval therefore gives
 d phi(d)=sum_{n mod d}|T(n)|^2=phi(d)|tau_d(chi_star)|^2,          (22)
whence |tau_d(chi_star)|=sqrt(d). For d=1 the unique character has tau_1=1, so the same formula holds. Equations (20)-(22) imply |tau_r(chi)|=sqrt(d), and (11) follows from (9).

Apply multiplicative Fourier inversion to (7). The first evaluation is chi(ht(r')^{-1})=chi(ht)conjugate(chi(r')); after conjugating the second it is conjugate(psi(-htr^{-1}))=conjugate(psi(-ht))psi(r). Together with (10), these give (12).

Finally, all sets and maps in (13)-(15) are finite. Each B is sesquilinear in its two incidence vectors, so the displayed blocks define a unique linear operator A_k on Xcal. Expanding the direct-sum inner product gives exactly the ordered sums in (14), proving (15). Interchanging r,r' conjugates the summand when w is real, proving reality.

glossary.A_k: The explicitly defined disjoint-modulus block operator on the direct sum of incidence spaces.
glossary.I_r: A defined row-linear incidence map from one common finite row space to functions on G_r.
glossary.K_{r,c}: The normalized Kloosterman convolution kernel u mapsto r^{-1}S_r(1,cu;r).

18a3123756aef746.title: PRE-CAUCHY SOURCE-ALIGNED SHARPNESS, NO REVERSE INEQUALITY FROM THE DELTA-NONZERO FORM, AND THE MINIMAL MEAN/SLOPE LEDGER
18a3123756aef746.author: slava chan
18a3123756aef746.statement:
PRE-CAUCHY SOURCE-ALIGNED SHARPNESS, NO REVERSE INEQUALITY FROM THE DELTA-NONZERO FORM, AND THE MINIMAL MEAN/SLOPE LEDGER.

Let n be a positive integer divisible by a prime p>2. Let A,q_0,m_0,k_0 be integers satisfying
  q_0>0,  gcd(q_0,n)=1,  q_0m_0+nk_0=A.                    (1)
Fix a positive real scale Y and put H_0=n/Y. Assume H_0 is sufficiently large and that a fixed source interval contains
  [m_0-delta Y,m_0+delta Y]                                 (2)
for some fixed sufficiently small delta>0.

There exists a fixed nonnegative smooth compactly supported function phi on [-delta,delta] such that
  phihat(xi)>=c_0>0 for 1<=xi<=2.                           (3)
Define
  F(t)=phi((t-m_0)/Y)
and
  lambda_h=n^(-1)Fhat(h/n)e_n(hA q_0^(-1)).                 (4)
For cal H={h in Z:H_0<=h<2H_0},
  lambda_h=H_0^(-1)phihat(h/H_0)>=c_0/H_0                  (5)
and
  |sum_{h in cal H}lambda_h|^2
   >>H_0 sum_{h in cal H}|lambda_h|^2.                     (6)
Thus the factor H_0 in Cauchy over the natural Poisson-frequency block is sharp for one fixed A, one actual source triple, one fixed pair (v,p) with n=vp, and one fixed scaled-smooth source amplitude. Any zero-one source mask which is one on (q_0,m_0,k_0) and is independent of h may be retained.

The complete nonzero-Poisson coefficient on the single q-row is
  a_{q_0}=n^(-1)sum_{h in Z;h nonzero}
       Fhat(h/n)e_n(hA q_0^(-1))
          =F(m_0)-n^(-1)Fhat(0),                            (7)
and is nonzero for sufficiently large H_0. Set a_q=0 for q not equal to q_0. For every complex physical kernel W, the exact Delta-nonzero form M_W(a,a,a,a) of facts ace362082848a702 and 0e8ef74ba484418d is zero, because every supported quadruple has Delta=0. Hence no uniform inequality can bound the nonzero pre-Cauchy mass in (7), or the sharp block mass in (6), solely by M_W(a,a,a,a).

Define a mean/slope-respecting PMD ledger to be an exact additive ledger which:
(a) splits W=alpha+W^circ, where alpha=p^(-1)sum_rW(r);
(b) partitions the W^circ four-q covariance by exact rational-slope equality Delta=0 and inequality Delta nonzero;
(c) controls the outer (v,p,h) pairing uniformly for arbitrary outer coefficients by a Hilbert-space inequality.
Within this stipulated class, the minimal exact data are:
  the squared outer coefficient norm,
  alpha cal F_p(1;a),
  E_{p,0}(W^circ;a),
  M_{W^circ}(a,a,a,a),                                     (8)
where cal F_p is the full centered four-q covariance before deleting Delta=0. Indeed, exactly
 cal F_p(W;a)
  =alpha cal F_p(1;a)+E_{p,0}(W^circ;a)
       +M_{W^circ}(a,a,a,a).                               (9)

Each entry in (8) is non-omissible within this exact ledger. The outer norm is forced by (6). For the single-q row, W=1 gives
  cal F_p(1;a)=(1-1/p)|a_{q_0}|^4>0,                        (10)
while W^circ=0. For the mean-zero kernel
  W(0)=1,quad W(1)=-1,quad W(r)=0 otherwise,              (11)
the same row gives
  E_{p,0}(W;a)=(1-2/p)|a_{q_0}|^4>0,quad M_W(a,a,a,a)=0.  (12)
Finally, consider a row supported with coefficient one on two q-values q_0,q_1 which are units modulo p and satisfy
  q_0 not congruent to q_1 modulo p,
and assume A is a unit modulo p. Put
  r=A(q_1-q_0)(q_0q_1)^(-1) modulo p.
Then r is nonzero. For the mean-zero kernel W(0)=1,W(r)=-1, zero elsewhere,
  M_W(a,a,a,a)=-2/p
e0.                                   (13)
If the two q-values arise from retained triples q_i m_i+nk_i=A, this last example preserves the fixed A and those source masks. In the injective PMD range p>2Q with both q-values in [Q,2Q), the displayed noncongruence is automatic. No unconditional existence of two such retained source triples is asserted.

Thus a pre-Cauchy PMD consumer may use already-proved estimates for the density and exact-slope pieces, but it cannot replace the full vector ledger (8) by the Delta-nonzero mean-zero form alone. This is a sharp theorem-interface no-fit, not a lower bound for the complete literal Goldbach source.
18a3123756aef746.proof:
Choose a nonnegative smooth function psi supported in [-delta/2,delta/2] with integral one, and put phi=psi*tilde psi, where tilde psi(t)=psi(-t). Then phi is nonnegative, smooth, supported in [-delta,delta], and
  phihat(xi)=|psihat(xi)|^2.                                (14)
Choose delta small enough that cos(2 pi xi t)>=3/4 whenever |t|<=delta/2 and 1<=xi<=2. Then Re psihat(xi)>=3/4 and phihat(xi)>=9/16 on that interval, proving (3).

Fourier scaling and translation give
  Fhat(xi)=Y exp(-2 pi i m_0xi)phihat(Yxi).                 (15)
Equation (1) implies A q_0^(-1) congruent m_0 modulo n. Substitution of xi=h/n in (15) cancels the translation phase in (4), and Y/n=H_0^(-1), proving (5). The set cal H has cardinality comparable to H_0. Hence the left side of (6) is bounded below by a positive constant, while |phihat|<=integral phi=1 gives
  sum_{h in cal H}|lambda_h|^2<<H_0^(-1).
This proves (6) and the sharpness of the outer squared l2 norm, since the all-one coefficient vector on cal H has squared norm comparable to H_0. The function F is one fixed scaled-smooth atom, so no projective decomposition tax occurs.

The interval (2) has length less than n for large H_0, and it contains only the source integer m_0 in its residue class modulo n. Progression Poisson summation, equivalently fact ace362082848a702, gives (7). Since F(m_0)=phi(0)>0 and n^(-1)Fhat(0)=H_0^(-1)integral phi=H_0^(-1), this coefficient is nonzero for large H_0. A one-q row has only Delta=0 quadruples, proving the no-reverse assertion.

Equation (9) follows first by complex linearity in W and then by the exact all-shift partition into Delta=0 and Delta nonzero in fact 27540b4094f677f4. This also proves that (8) is the complete exact datum under conditions (a)-(c).

For W=1, the one-q centered punctual kernel at the sole output zero is Gamma_1(0,0)=1-1/p, proving (10). For (11), the physical mean is zero, and equation (11) of fact 27540b4094f677f4 gives (12).

It remains to verify (13). For the two-q row the exact slopes are zero, lambda, and -lambda, where lambda=1/q_0-1/q_1. Their fibre coefficients are respectively 2,1,1, and their output residues are 0,r,-r. The explicit noncongruence hypothesis and the fact that A,q_0,q_1 are units make r nonzero. Since p>2, the three residues 0,r,-r are distinct. Apply the output-profile identity in fact 35ff1e5855450319. Its quantities are
 F_p(0)=2,quad F_p(r)=F_p(-r)=1,
 D_p(0)=4,quad D_p(r)=D_p(-r)=1,quad S_0=4.
Therefore
 G_p(0)=-8/p,qquad G_p(r)=G_p(-r)=-6/p.
The kernel used in (13) pairs with this profile as
  M_W=G_p(0)-G_p(r)=-2/p,
proving (13). If two actual source triples are present, assigning coefficient one to their two q-projections gives exactly this row; the fixed A and the declared source masks remain unchanged.

The examples (10), (12), and (13) show that deleting respectively the density, diagonal, or remainder term changes the exact covariance inside the stipulated mean/slope-respecting ledger. Equation (6) independently shows that replacing the outer direct-sum coefficient norm by a smaller uniform factor is impossible. This proves the claimed minimality within the explicitly defined class and the final no-fit.

glossary.cal F_p: The full centered four-q covariance before deleting the exact rational-slope diagonal.
glossary.mean/slope-respecting PMD ledger: The exact outer-Hilbert, physical-mean, rational-slope-diagonal, and Delta-nonzero decomposition specified in (8).
glossary.source-aligned Fourier family: A translated smooth amplitude centered at an actual solution, whose Fourier translation phase cancels the progression character.

18b6a72f43ed47b2.title: Assume the hypotheses and notation of facts 54f71c4dcc1bc9bb, bc46ed5832faeade, 02a763eba051c761, and 308c7c0d43bda909. Thus \(N=2x\) is fixed,
18b6a72f43ed47b2.author: slava chan
18b6a72f43ed47b2.statement:
Assume the hypotheses and notation of facts 54f71c4dcc1bc9bb, bc46ed5832faeade, 02a763eba051c761, and 308c7c0d43bda909. Thus \(N=2x\) is fixed,
\[
 {1\over2}x^{1/2}(\log x)^{-B_{\rm src}}\le D\le2x^{1/2},
 \qquad T_x=(\log x)^{6+\eta+\rho},
\]
and every hard physical shift satisfies
\[
 |H|>{ax\over2T_x}.                                      \tag{1}
\]
Put \(e(t)=\exp(2\pi i t)\).

Matomäki--Radziwiłł--Tao, arXiv:1707.01315, Theorem 1.3(i), does not directly apply to any shift in (1). Indeed, for fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), its hypotheses require
\[
 x^{8/33+\varepsilon}\le L\le x^{1-\varepsilon},
 \qquad 0\le h_0\le x^{1-\varepsilon},
 \qquad |h-h_0|\le L,                                  \tag{2}
\]
and hence \(|h|\le2x^{1-\varepsilon}\). For sufficiently large \(x\), (1) is larger than \(2x^{1-\varepsilon}\).

There are two further quantitative losses even if one counterfactually extends the center range in (2) to the macroscopic physical-shift region. Every nonzero lattice incidence has
\[
 {ax\over2D}\le m\le {2bx\over D},                    \tag{3}
\]
so \(m\gg x^{1/2}\). In an interval of length \(L\), the progression \(H\in m\mathbb Z\) has at most \(2L/m+1\) points. For every fixed \(A>0\) and every \(L\ge x^{8/33+\varepsilon}\),
\[
 {2L\over m}+1\le L(\log x)^{-A}                       \tag{4}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(x\). Therefore the exceptional allowance
\(O_{A,\varepsilon}(L(\log x)^{-A})\) in MRT Theorem 1.3(i) is large enough to contain the entire prescribed progression in such a hypothetical macroscopic-center extension.

For the second loss, define
\[
 F(\theta)=\sum_{x<n\le2x}\Lambda(n)e(n\theta),\qquad
 F_{m,N}(\theta)=
 \sum_{\substack{x<n\le2x\\n\equiv N\ ({\rm mod}\ m)}}\Lambda(n)e(n\theta).
\]
Then
\[
 F_{m,N}(\theta)={1\over m}\sum_{c\ ({\rm mod}\ m)}
 e(-cN/m)F(\theta+c/m),                                  \tag{5}
\]
and for every interval \(I\) in the circle,
\[
 \int_I|F_{m,N}(\theta)|^2d\theta
 \le {1\over m}\sum_{c\ ({\rm mod}\ m)}
       \int_{I+c/m}|F(\theta)|^2d\theta.                \tag{6}
\]
Applying the scalar short-frequency estimate of MRT Proposition 3.4 separately to all translates yields at best
\[
 \int_I|F_{m,N}|^2\ll_A x(\log x)^{-A},                 \tag{7}
\]
not the density-normalized size \((x/m)(\log x)^{-A}\).

Equivalently, let \(R\ge1\) be a real number, let \(\Psi\) be even and Schwartz, define
\[
 \widehat\Psi(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Psi(u)e(-u\xi)\,du,
\]
and assume \(\widehat\Psi\) is supported in \([-1/2,1/2]\). Then
\[
 \sum_{h\in\mathbb Z}e(m(\alpha-\beta)h)\Psi(h/R)
 =R\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}
   \widehat\Psi(R(j-m(\alpha-\beta))).                 \tag{8}
\]
On the circle this is supported on \(m\) translated intervals of width \(1/(mR)\), rather than the single interval in MRT Proposition 3.1. These are scoped no-direct-import statements, not impossibility results for a new vector theorem.

The first sufficient exact vector extension is as follows. For \(m\ge1\), define
\[
\begin{split}
 {\cal C}_m={}&
 \sum_{\substack{d_1,d_2\in{\cal I}_D\\d_1\ne d_2}}
 \mu(d_1)\mu(d_2)\Phi(d_1/D)\Phi(d_2/D)
 V_{d_1,m}V_{d_2,m}
 \Lambda_{\rm pr}(N-d_1m)\Lambda_{\rm pr}(N-d_2m),                  \tag{9}\\
 {\cal M}_m={}&
 \sum_{\substack{d_1,d_2\in{\cal I}_D\\d_1\ne d_2}}
 \mu(d_1)\mu(d_2)\Phi(d_1/D)\Phi(d_2/D)
 V_{d_1,m}V_{d_2,m}\mathfrak S_N(d_1,d_2),                            \tag{10}\\
 {\cal E}_m={}&{\cal C}_m-{\cal M}_m.                               \tag{11}
\end{split}
\]
The estimate
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \sum_{m\ge1}|{\cal E}_m|
 \ll_{W,\Phi,a,b,\eta,\rho}
 xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta}
 \quad}                                                \tag{SL-MRT-m1}
\]
implies
\[
 \sum_{H\ne0}\sum_p{\cal A}_N(H,p)\Lambda(p)\Lambda(p-H)
 \ll xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta}.                             \tag{12}
\]
Thus (SL-MRT-m1) implies TB-PHYS and all consequences in fact bc46ed5832faeade. It preserves the same fixed \(N\), the equations \(H=m(d_2-d_1)\), \(p=N-md_1\), the exact signs \(\mu(d_1)\mu(d_2)\), and every source selector. It is not asserted to be proved.
18b6a72f43ed47b2.proof:
If a term in (9) or (10) is nonzero, then
\[
 D/2\le d_i\le2D,qquad ax\le d_im\le bx.
\]
This proves (3). Since \(D\le2x^{1/2}\), it also gives
\(m\ge ax^{1/2}/4\). Equation (1), on the other hand, is equation (3) of fact 308c7c0d43bda909.

Under (2), \(|h|\le h_0+L\le2x^{1-\varepsilon}\). Since
\[
 {ax/(2T_x)\over2x^{1-\varepsilon}}
 ={a\over4}{x^\varepsilon\over(\log x)^{6+\eta+\rho}}\longrightarrow\infty,
\]
(1) and (2) are disjoint for sufficiently large \(x\). This proves the first no-fit.

The number of multiples of \(m\) in an interval of length comparable to \(L\) is at most \(2L/m+1\). For fixed \(A\), (3) implies
\[
 2L/m\le {1\over2}L(\log x)^{-A}
\]
eventually, while \(L\ge x^{8/33+\varepsilon}\) implies
\[
 1\le {1\over2}L(\log x)^{-A}.
\]
This proves (4). We use (4) only as the stated counterfactual cardinality comparison; MRT Theorem 1.3(i) itself does not reach the physical centers.

For (5), insert
\[
 { f1}_{n\equiv N\ ({\rm mod}\ m)}
 ={1\over m}\sum_{c\ ({\rm mod}\ m)}e(c(n-N)/m)
\]
into \(F_{m,N}\). Cauchy--Schwarz then gives
\[
 |F_{m,N}(\theta)|^2
 \le {1\over m}\sum_{c\ ({\rm mod}\ m)}
 |F(\theta+c/m)|^2.
\]
Integration proves (6). If every translated scalar energy is bounded by
\(x(\log x)^{-A}\), their number \(m\) cancels the factor \(1/m\), proving only (7). The missing density factor is \(m\).

For (8), apply Poisson summation to
\(t\mapsto\Psi(t/R)e(m(\alpha-\beta)t)\). With the stated convention its Fourier transform at the integer \(j\) is
\[
 R\widehat\Psi(R(j-m(\alpha-\beta))).
\]
The support of \(\widehat\Psi\) forces
\[
 |j-m(\alpha-\beta)|\le1/(2R).
\]
The residues \(j\pmod m\) give exactly \(m\) intervals modulo one, each of width \(1/(mR)\). MRT Proposition 3.4 applies only to the unrestricted functions \(\Lambda 1_{(x,2x]}\) and \(d_k1_{(x,2x]}\); it supplies neither density-normalized progression energy nor the exact quotient Möbius signs.

It remains to prove the sufficiency of (SL-MRT-m1). Summing (9) over \(m\) gives the prime-only full off-diagonal covariance of fact 54f71c4dcc1bc9bb:
\[
 \mathfrak C_{\rm off}=\sum_m{\cal C}_m
 =\sum_m{\cal E}_m+\sum_m{\cal M}_m.                  \tag{13}
\]
For fixed \(m\), define
\[
 G_m(u)={\bf1}_{Du\le x^{1/2}}\Phi(u)
 W(Dum/x)\Phi((N-Dum)/U).
\]
It is supported in \([1/2,2]\). When nonzero, (3) gives \(Dm/x\asymp1\), so its supremum and total variation are bounded uniformly in \(m\); the cutoff has one jump. Equation (10) is equation (1) of fact 5b7b0955c5efaa1b with both test functions equal to \(G_m\). The top-band lower bound gives \(N\le D^3\) eventually. Therefore, for every fixed \(A_1>0\),
\[
 |{\cal M}_m|\ll_{A_1,W,\Phi}
 \mathfrak c(N)D^2(\log x)^{-A_1}.                     \tag{14}
\]
Only \(O(x/D)\) moduli occur by (3), so
\[
 \sum_m|{\cal M}_m|
 \ll_{A_1,W,\Phi}\mathfrak c(N)xD(\log x)^{-A_1}.     \tag{15}
\]
Fact 54f71c4dcc1bc9bb gives \(\mathfrak c(N)\ll(\log x)^3\). Choose \(A_1>8+\eta+\rho\). From (13), (15), and (SL-MRT-m1),
\[
 |\mathfrak C_{\rm off}|\ll xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta}.   \tag{16}
\]

Fact bc46ed5832faeade bounds the prime-only complement of the hard core by
\[
 O(xD(\log x)^2/T_x)
 =O(xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta-\rho}).                       \tag{17}
\]
Subtracting that complement from (16) proves prime-only TB-HARD. Fact 02a763eba051c761 replaces prime-only weights by full von Mangoldt weights with
\(o_A(xD(\log x)^{-A})\) error for every fixed \(A\). Fact 308c7c0d43bda909 then identifies the resulting hard core exactly with the left side of (12). This proves the implication.

No estimate for \({\cal E}_m\) is claimed here. The fact isolates the exact vector-valued progression theorem needed after the scalar MRT interfaces fail.

glossary.cal E_m: the fixed-m covariance error cal C_m minus cal M_m
glossary.cal M_m: the fixed-m local singular-series model for cal C_m

18c3a93006507edb.title: GA-GOODW-GENEALOGY: COMPLETE GOOD-W REFINEMENT RECOMBINATION AND MASK-FREE PRE-COPY COEFFICIENT. Fix tau>0 and the complete Good-W projection mathcal T_{good,sel}(tau) of fact e55b27d39c593164, namely the inherited beta>=6/5 post-low family restricted by the outer-scale condition mathscr W>=Q^tau. Fix the selected N, one active dyadic label, exact outer gcd g, orientation, normalized layer, actual-G layer, fixed-U/high layer, one allowed parent, and one smooth/projective physical source fibre. Before choosing a proper old refinement leaf, before the terminal marker, and before imposing any terminal-child-dependent dilator, hard, principal or centered projection, retain the complete family of auxiliary source, target-gcd, order/equality, collision, deletion and provenance siblings over this outer row
18c3a93006507edb.author: slava chan
18c3a93006507edb.proof:
The original selected source is the literal smooth double-Mobius source displayed and audited in fact 328503a935cabe60. Its dependence on the integer solutions consists of logarithms and the specified smooth W, psi and Phi factors. In particular, it contains no independent zero-one deletion, collision or provenance predicate.

Fact 7ffe3d237362a451 forms the post-low remainder by subtracting the complete C91 aggregate and complete bounded-base and low-beta families. As recorded in fact 328503a935cabe60, these are complete label/normalized-layer projections and no actual-(r,k) deletion is inserted. Fact 3f2f255ea6845a50 acts only on beta<6/5, so the beta>=6/5 family used here is inherited unchanged. Restricting further by mathscr W>=Q^tau is an outer-scale projection, because mathscr W=G^2Q^(2-beta) on the fixed normalized layer by fact e55b27d39c593164. Hence this restriction does not select a proper solution-dependent refinement sibling.

Fact a71f777ad842c886 recombines every old marker leaf and marker-dependent descendant pointwise to the literal normalized factor mu(n). Fact 328503a935cabe60 proves the underlying finite-partition principle in this same beta>=6/5 inherited source: target-gcd, order/equal-cell, collision, deletion and provenance coordinates introduced in marker/anatomy refinements are auxiliary finite sibling partitions, and retaining their full coordinate makes their complementary zero-one selectors sum pointwise to one. The proof there uses only the unchanged beta>=6/5 inheritance and the absence of a physical deletion in the post-low source, not the later inequality mathscr W<Q^tau. The complementary outer-scale inequality mathscr W>=Q^tau therefore leaves the same complete sibling fibres intact. Summing their selectors proves (1). The terminal anatomy identity is itself an exact finite refinement of mu(n); its canonical descendants have the same partition property, proving the second assertion.

At fixed outer data, the selected scales, beta and mathscr W ranges, actual G, orientation, fixed-U/high layer, allowed parent and physical projective fibre are scalars. The remaining physical dependence is precisely the literal smooth Fourier transform in equation (9) of fact e55b27d39c593164. Replacing the product Xi_lambda there by the complete sum (1) gives (2)-(3). The coprimality and frequency restrictions occur outside Xi_lambda in equations (10)-(11) of that fact, so they remain explicit.

Finally, fact 2223056b02c29f78 proves that, before a terminal-child-dependent projection and after reuniting all marked-dilator blocks, the flat physical row is common to every terminal child and the terminal coefficients sum to mu(n). Applying that identity to (2)-(3) gives (4) and the stated squared-modulus conclusion. The same fact supplies the noncommutation boundary, so none of the excluded projected conclusions follows.

19544eedf19b375b.title: INACTIVE-FACE-WEIGHTED \(C\)-TYPE TENSOR BESSEL BOUND
19544eedf19b375b.author: slava chan
19544eedf19b375b.statement:
INACTIVE-FACE-WEIGHTED \(C\)-TYPE TENSOR BESSEL BOUND.

Let \(X,D\ge2\), let \(A\ne0\) be an integer, let \(r\) be a nonempty squarefree positive integer, and let \(J\) be a finite integer interval of cardinality \(V\) not containing \(0\). Assume that \(A,r,D\), and the endpoints of \(J\) are bounded by a fixed power of \(X\). Let \(\mathcal R\) be a finite set of distinct triples
\[
 j=(d_j,v_j,h_j)
\]
such that
\[
 D\le d_j<2D,\quad v_j\in\{1,2\},\quad h_j\in J,\quad
 d_j\ \hbox{and}\ n_j=d_jv_j\ \hbox{are squarefree}.                 \tag{1}
\]
Put
\[
 d_j^{\rm u}=\prod_{\substack{p\mid d_j\\p\nmid Ah_j}}p,
 \qquad r\mid d_j^{\rm u},\qquad
 a_j={d_j^{\rm u}\over r},\qquad
 \alpha_j={\mu(a_j)\over a_j}e_{v_j}(Ah_j).                         \tag{2}
\]
For every \(p\mid r\), define \(g_{p;j}\), its normalized Fourier transform \(\widehat g_{p;j}\), the product frequency set \(\Omega_r\), and
\[
 V_j(\boldsymbol\rho)=\prod_{p\mid r}\widehat g_{p;j}(\rho_p)
\]
exactly as in fact df97bf1eba0495be with \((n,h)=(n_j,h_j)\).

Then, for every complex coefficient array \((c_j)_{j\in\mathcal R}\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 \sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r}
 \left|\sum_{j\in\mathcal R}c_j\alpha_jV_j(\boldsymbol\rho)\right|^2
 \ll_\varepsilon X^\varepsilon V\sum_{j\in\mathcal R}|c_j|^2.      \tag{3}
\]
The implied constant may depend on the fixed polynomial envelope in \(X\).

More generally, suppose
\[
 Y_j(\boldsymbol\rho)=\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}
 \beta_{j,t}Z_t(\boldsymbol\rho),                                  \tag{4}
\]
where \(\mathcal T\) is finite, \(\beta_{j,t}\in\mathbb C\), and the functions \(Z_t:\Omega_r\to\mathbb C\) are common to all rows. Define
\[
 \mathfrak P_C(Y)=\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}
 \left(\sup_{j\in\mathcal R}|\beta_{j,t}|\right)
 \left(\sup_{\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r}|Z_t(\boldsymbol\rho)|\right).
                                                                         \tag{5}
\]
Then
\[
 \sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r}
 \left|\sum_{j\in\mathcal R}
 c_j\alpha_jY_j(\boldsymbol\rho)V_j(\boldsymbol\rho)\right|^2
 \ll_\varepsilon X^\varepsilon V\,\mathfrak P_C(Y)^2
 \sum_{j\in\mathcal R}|c_j|^2.                                    \tag{6}
\]

In the forward GA-tail completion of fact 0aa821ade9a14b45, restrict to one fixed \(C_\ell\)-anatomy, one fixed source/projective fiber, and rows with common nonempty active product \(r\). For such a row \(n=dv\) with \(v\in\{1,2\}\). If
\[
 Y_{\lambda,h,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)
 =\sum_{\substack{Q\le q<2Q\\(q,n)=1}}
 b_{\lambda,h}(q)\chi_{\boldsymbol\rho}(q),                        \tag{7}
\]
then its literal transform satisfies the exact identity
\[
 W_{\lambda,h,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)
 =\alpha_{\lambda,h,r}Y_{\lambda,h,r}(\boldsymbol\rho),            \tag{8}
\]
where \(\alpha_{\lambda,h,r}\) is (2). Hence (6) controls the exact common-\(r\) \(C_\ell\) weighted tensor Gram once a common-spectrum decomposition of the stripped transforms (7) is supplied, with operator scale \(V\) rather than \(B/r\).

This result proves no bound for \(\mathfrak P_C(Y)\), no pair-dependent nonresonance deletion, no distinct-\(r\) discrepancy, no \(A\)-anatomy estimate, no GA-NR-DIL estimate, no tail payment, and no Goldbach conclusion.
19544eedf19b375b.proof:
For a row \(j\), every prime divisor of \(r\) divides \(d_j^{\rm u}\). Hence
\[
 (Ah_j,r)=1,\qquad r\mid d_j,\qquad
 \left(r,{n_j\over r}\right)=1.
\]
Thus all hypotheses of fact df97bf1eba0495be hold for every pair of rows. Put
\[
 m_j={d_j\over r},\qquad s_j=(d_j,Ah_j).
\]
Because \(d_j\) is squarefree and \((r,Ah_j)=1\), definition (2) gives
\[
 d_j^{\rm u}={d_j\over s_j},\qquad
 a_j={m_j\over s_j},\qquad |\alpha_j|={s_j\over m_j}.             \tag{9}
\]
Also \(n_j/r=m_jv_j\).

For two rows \(j,k\), fact df97bf1eba0495be gives their exact tensor Gram and the bound
\[
 \left|\sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r}
 V_j(\boldsymbol\rho)\overline{V_k(\boldsymbol\rho)}\right|
 \le 2^{\omega(r)}{\gcd(r,T_{jk})\over r},                         \tag{10}
\]
where
\[
 T_{jk}=h_jm_kv_k-h_km_jv_j.
\]
Indeed, the exceptional product in that fact is
\[
 \prod_{\substack{p\mid r\\p^2\mid h_jn_k-h_kn_j}}p
 =\prod_{\substack{p\mid r\\p\mid T_{jk}}}p
 =\gcd(r,T_{jk}),                                                  \tag{11}
\]
because \(r\) is squarefree.

We bound the positive Schur row sum after inserting the exact inactive-face weights. Fix \(j\). The divisor identity
\[
 \gcd(r,T)=\sum_{\substack{t\mid r\\t\mid T}}\varphi(t)            \tag{12}
\]
reduces the row sum to weighted congruence counts. Fix \(t\mid r\), \(h_k\in J\), and \(v_k\in\{1,2\}\). The congruence \(t\mid T_{jk}\) is
\[
 h_jv_km_k\equiv h_kv_jm_j\pmod t.                                \tag{13}
\]
The coefficient of \(m_k\) is a unit modulo \(t\): \((h_j,r)=1\), while squarefreeness of \(n_k=d_kv_k\) and \(r\mid d_k\) give \((v_k,r)=1\). Hence (13) restricts \(m_k\) to one residue class modulo \(t\).

Let \(M=D/r\), so \(M\ge1/2\) on a nonempty row family, and let \(L=|Ah_k|>0\). After dropping the squarefree and other row restrictions, the weighted mass in that residue class is at most
\[
 \sum_{\substack{M\le m<2M\\m\equiv c\ ({\rm mod}\ t)}}
 {\gcd(m,L)\over m}.                                               \tag{14}
\]
Since
\[
 \gcd(m,L)=\sum_{\substack{s\mid L\\s\mid m}}\varphi(s),           \tag{15}
\]
and \((L,t)=1\) for every retained row \(k\), the conditions \(s\mid m\) and \(m\equiv c\pmod t\) occupy one residue class modulo \(st\). Using \(m^{-1}\ll M^{-1}\), (14) is at most a constant times
\[
 {1\over M}\sum_{\substack{s\mid L\\s\le2M}}\varphi(s)
 \left({M\over st}+1\right)
 \le {\tau(L)\over t}+2\tau(L).                                   \tag{16}
\]
Here the first term uses \(\varphi(s)/s\le1\), and the second uses
\(\varphi(s)\le s\le2M\). Fact e705401df9f0709e and the polynomial envelope give
\[
 \tau(L)+\tau(r)+2^{\omega(r)}\ll_\varepsilon X^\varepsilon.       \tag{17}
\]

There are \(V\) choices for \(h_k\) and at most two for \(v_k\). Combining (9)--(17),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_{k\in\mathcal R}|\alpha_j\alpha_k|
 \left|\sum_{\boldsymbol\rho}V_j(\boldsymbol\rho)
        \overline{V_k(\boldsymbol\rho)}\right|
 &\ll_\varepsilon
 X^\varepsilon {|\alpha_j|V\over r}
 \sum_{t\mid r}\varphi(t)\left(1+{1\over t}\right)\\
 &\ll_\varepsilon X^\varepsilon V,
 \end{aligned}                                                     \tag{18}
\]
because \(|\alpha_j|\le1\), \(\sum_{t\mid r}\varphi(t)=r\), and
\(\sum_{t\mid r}\varphi(t)/t\le\tau(r)\). The same estimate holds for column sums. Schur's test applied to the exact positive majorant (10) proves (3).

For (6), substitute (4), use Minkowski's inequality in \(\ell^2(\Omega_r)\), and apply (3) to the coefficient array \((c_j\beta_{j,t})_j\) for each \(t\):
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \left\|\sum_jc_j\alpha_jY_jV_j\right\|_2
 &\le\sum_t\left\|Z_t\sum_jc_j\alpha_j\beta_{j,t}V_j\right\|_2\\
 &\ll_\varepsilon X^{\varepsilon/2}V^{1/2}
 \sum_t\|Z_t\|_\infty\sup_j|\beta_{j,t}|
 \left(\sum_j|c_j|^2\right)^{1/2}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Squaring and replacing \(\varepsilon\) by \(\varepsilon/2\) proves (6).

Finally consider a \(C_\ell\)-row in fact 0aa821ade9a14b45. There \(v\in\{1,2\}\), \((qd,v)=1\), and every unit modulo \(v\) is congruent to \(1\). Therefore
\[
 e_v\!\left(Ah(qd)^{-1}\right)=e_v(Ah),                            \tag{19}
\]
independently of \(q\). The inactive product in equation (4) of that fact is
\[
 \prod_{p\mid d^{\rm u}/r}\left(-{1\over p}\right)
 ={\mu(a)\over a}.                                                 \tag{20}
\]
Equations (19)--(20) pull out of the \(q\)-transform and give (8). Applying (6) proves the stated specialization and all scope limitations are explicit.

glossary.inactive-face-weighted C-type tensor Bes: The fixed-active-product tensor estimate after retaining the exact inactive-prime coefficient on a C-type marker row.
glossary.stripped C-type transform: The transform Y obtained from the literal C-type coefficient after removing its row-scalar inactive-prime factor and its q-independent v-phase.

1a4654c1b828f1f6.title: EXACT CENTERED PRIME-MODULUS DIVISIBILITY TRANSFORM
1a4654c1b828f1f6.author: slava chan
1a4654c1b828f1f6.statement:
EXACT CENTERED PRIME-MODULUS DIVISIBILITY TRANSFORM.

Let p be a prime, let v,q_1,q_2 be positive integers with p not dividing vq_1q_2, let A be an integer, and let H>0. Write e_p(t)=exp(2 pi i t/p), and let bars denote inverses modulo p. Let Phi be a smooth compactly supported function on R whose support is contained in [-2,-1] union [1,2], and define
  Phihat(y)=integral_R Phi(t) exp(-2 pi i y t) dt.
Then the exact Poisson identity is

sum_{h in Z} Phi(h/H) e_p(A h vbar(q_1bar-q_2bar))
 = H sum_{r in Z, v|r} Phihat(-Hr/(vp))
       1_{p | A(q_2-q_1)-r q_1q_2}.                       (1)

If p>2H, then the dual kernel has exact total mass zero:

sum_{r in Z, v|r} Phihat(-Hr/(vp))=0.                       (2)

Consequently (1) has the exactly centered form

sum_{h in Z} Phi(h/H) e_p(A h vbar(q_1bar-q_2bar))
 = H sum_{r in Z, v|r} Phihat(-Hr/(vp))
   [1_{p | A(q_2-q_1)-r q_1q_2}-1/p].                     (3)

Thus the subtraction 1/p is an identity, not an estimate: it is licensed by exclusion of the original h=0 mode through Phi(0)=0 and the inequality p/H>2. The small factor v is retained as the source mask v|r. For every integer J>=2 and every Y>=1,

sum_{r in Z, v|r, |r|>Yvp/H}|Phihat(-Hr/(vp))|
 <<_{Phi,J} (p/H)Y^(1-J).                                  (4)

Hence the natural rescaled dual length is vp/H. In particular, on a frozen product scale vp=R with H=R/Q, it is Q. If Phi is real and even, then both sides of (1) and (3) are real. No estimate for the centered incidence sum over p,q_1,q_2 is asserted.
1a4654c1b828f1f6.proof:
Put B=A vbar(q_1bar-q_2bar) modulo p. With the Fourier-transform convention in the statement, ordinary Poisson summation applied to x maps to Phi(x/H)e(Bx/p) gives

sum_h Phi(h/H)e_p(Bh)
 =H sum_{k in Z} Phihat(H(k-B/p))
 =H sum_{ell in Z, ell congruent -B mod p} Phihat(Hell/p). (5)

For every ell in the last sum set r=-vell. This is a bijection from Z onto the integers divisible by v, and the Fourier weight becomes Phihat(-Hr/(vp)). Moreover ell congruent -B modulo p is equivalent to r congruent vB modulo p. Since

vB congruent A(q_1bar-q_2bar)
     congruent A(q_2-q_1)(q_1q_2)bar modulo p,

and q_1q_2 is a unit modulo p, this congruence is exactly

p | A(q_2-q_1)-r q_1q_2.

This proves (1).

For (2), write r=vk and apply Poisson summation once more, now to Phihat at spacing H/p:

sum_{r:v|r} Phihat(-Hr/(vp))
 =sum_{k in Z}Phihat(-Hk/p)
 =(p/H)sum_{n in Z}Phi(np/H).                               (6)

The n=0 term is zero because Phi(0)=0. If n is nonzero, then |np/H|>=p/H>2, outside the support of Phi. Hence every term on the right of (6) vanishes, proving (2). Multiplying (2) by 1/p and subtracting it from the right side of (1) proves (3). This also explains precisely why the absent original zero frequency, rather than a heuristic expectation over residues, permits centering.

Smooth compact support gives |Phihat(y)|<<_{Phi,J}(1+|y|)^(-J). Writing r=vk and summing this estimate over |k|>Yp/H gives

sum_{|k|>Yp/H}|Phihat(-Hk/p)|
 <<_{Phi,J} sum_{|k|>Yp/H}(H|k|/p)^(-J)
 <<_{Phi,J}(p/H)Y^(1-J),

which is (4). The scale assertions follow by substitution. Finally, if Phi is real and even, its Fourier transform is real and even; the h and -h summands on the left are conjugate pairs, so the stated reality follows.

glossary.PMD centered incidence: The bracket 1_{p divides A(q_2-q_1)-r q_1q_2}-1/p produced exactly by the zero-mass Poisson kernel.
glossary.rescaled dual variable r: The original integer Poisson frequency multiplied by the frozen small factor v, so that v divides r and its natural length is vp/H.

1a9ce3acae020cb8.title: EXACT FIXED-BLOCK OPERATOR NORM AND THE ARBITRARY-VAUGHAN PERIODIZATION LEDGER. Let p>2 be prime. For i=1,2 let d_i be positive squarefree integers coprime to p, and let \((C_i,d_i)=1\). Let c be a nonzero residue modulo p. On the unit residue groups modulo \(pd_1\) and \(pd_2\), define the matrix
1a9ce3acae020cb8.author: slava chan
1a9ce3acae020cb8.statement:
EXACT FIXED-BLOCK OPERATOR NORM AND THE ARBITRARY-VAUGHAN PERIODIZATION LEDGER. Let p>2 be prime. For i=1,2 let d_i be positive squarefree integers coprime to p, and let \((C_i,d_i)=1\). Let c be a nonzero residue modulo p. On the unit residue groups modulo \(pd_1\) and \(pd_2\), define the matrix
\[
\mathscr K_{c;d_1,d_2}(x,y)
=G_c(x\bmod p,y\bmod p)
 e_{d_1}(C_1x^{-1})e_{d_2}(C_2y^{-1}), \tag{1}
\]
where
\[
G_c(f,g)={p\over p-1}\left({\bf1}_{g=cf}-{1\over p-1}\right).
\]
As an operator from \(\ell^2((\mathbb Z/pd_2\mathbb Z)^\times)\) to \(\ell^2((\mathbb Z/pd_1\mathbb Z)^\times)\), it has the exact norm
\[
\boxed{\ \|\mathscr K_{c;d_1,d_2}\|_{\rm op}
={p\over p-1}\sqrt{\phi(d_1)\phi(d_2)}.\ } \tag{2}
\]

Let alpha_i be arbitrary finitely supported complex sequences, with support contained in an integer interval of cardinality L_i. Periodize them on unit residues by
\[
\widetilde\alpha_i(z)
=\sum_{\substack{n\in\mathbb Z\\n\equiv z\ ({\rm mod}\ pd_i)}}\alpha_i(n),
\qquad z\in(\mathbb Z/pd_i\mathbb Z)^\times. \tag{3}
\]
Then
\[
\|\widetilde\alpha_i\|_2^2
\le\left(1+{L_i\over pd_i}\right)\|\alpha_i\|_2^2, \tag{4}
\]
and the incomplete bilinear block
\[
\mathscr B(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)
=\sum_{x,y\in\mathbb Z}
\alpha_1(x)\alpha_2(y)
{\bf1}_{(x,pd_1)=(y,pd_2)=1}
\mathscr K_{c;d_1,d_2}(x,y) \tag{5}
\]
satisfies
\[
|\mathscr B(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)|
\le {p\over p-1}\sqrt{\phi(d_1)\phi(d_2)}
\prod_{i=1}^2
\left(1+{L_i\over pd_i}\right)^{1/2}\|\alpha_i\|_2. \tag{6}
\]
In particular, if \(L_1,L_2\ll Q/a+1\) and \(|\alpha_i(n)|\le Q^\varepsilon\), then
\[
|\mathscr B(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)|
\ll Q^{2\varepsilon}(Q/a+1)\sqrt{d_1d_2}
\prod_{i=1}^2
\left(1+{Q/a+1\over pd_i}\right)^{1/2}. \tag{7}
\]

For every fixed additive subface of the literal J_2 Gram term in fact b9560e346963b9e0, fact ce5de84556b212d9 identifies its kernel with (1), with c=s_1q_2^{-1} modulo p and the signed coefficients C_i stated there. On actual tensors, the literal Vaughan coefficients satisfy the support and pointwise hypotheses used in (7), by fact 55c6f91ec7fd414f. Thus (7) is the exact fixed-block simultaneous-completion/Cauchy scale available for arbitrary literal Vaughan values.

The primitive denominator in fact 0029944864b851e8 does not improve (2): after p,d_i,c are frozen, both inverse phases in (1) are coordinatewise unitary multipliers and their primitive conductors do not change the singular values. Any primitive-denominator saving for the arbitrary literal vector must therefore come from aggregation across distinct outer blocks before the operator norm is taken. No such cross-block estimate, no sum over subfaces, no K_inc estimate, and no Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
1a9ce3acae020cb8.proof:
Use the Chinese remainder theorem to identify
\[
(\mathbb Z/pd_i\mathbb Z)^\times
\simeq \mathbb F_p^\times\times(\mathbb Z/d_i\mathbb Z)^\times.
\]
Under this identification the inverse phase \(e_{d_i}(C_iz^{-1})\) depends only on the second coordinate. Let v_i be the vector on \((\mathbb Z/d_i\mathbb Z)^\times\) with entries
\[
v_i(z)=e_{d_i}(C_iz^{-1}).
\]
Every entry has absolute value one, so \(\|v_i\|_2=\sqrt{\phi(d_i)}\). The matrix in (1) is the tensor product of the p-coordinate matrix G_c and the rank-one matrix \(v_1v_2^{\mathsf T}\). Fact 6ab529accdede090 proves
\[
\|G_c\|_{\rm op}={p\over p-1}.
\]
The rank-one matrix \(v_1v_2^{\mathsf T}\) has operator norm \(\|v_1\|_2\|v_2\|_2\), and operator norms multiply under finite Hilbert tensor products. This proves (2). It also proves directly that changing the unit-modulus entries v_i, including changing their primitive additive conductors, does not change the fixed-block norm.

For (4), a residue class modulo pd_i contains at most \(1+L_i/(pd_i)\) integers from an interval of cardinality L_i. Cauchy--Schwarz within each residue class gives
\[
