|\widetilde\alpha_i(z)|^2
\le\left(1+{L_i\over pd_i}\right)
\sum_{n\equiv z\ ({\rm mod}\ pd_i)}|\alpha_i(n)|^2.
\]
Sum this inequality over the unit residue classes. They are disjoint, so the right side is at most the displayed factor times \(\|\alpha_i\|_2^2\). This proves (4).

Because the kernel in (1) is periodic in x modulo pd_1 and in y modulo pd_2, equation (5) is exactly the bilinear pairing of the two periodized vectors in (3) through the matrix \(\mathscr K_{c;d_1,d_2}\). Apply (2), Cauchy--Schwarz, and (4) to obtain (6). Under the hypotheses of (7),
\[
\|\alpha_i\|_2\le Q^\varepsilon L_i^{1/2}
\ll Q^\varepsilon(Q/a+1)^{1/2}.
\]
Also \(\phi(d_i)\le d_i\). Inserting these inequalities into (6) proves (7).

The literal identification follows from fact ce5de84556b212d9, including the row-two conjugation sign. Fact 55c6f91ec7fd414f supplies the actual-tensor pointwise Vaughan bound and interval support. Finally, fact 0029944864b851e8 identifies the primitive carrier denominator across blocks, but the first paragraph proves that within one frozen block the phase vectors remain unit vectors of the same norms. Hence that denominator can affect only a cross-block comparison, as claimed.

glossary.\\mathscr B(\\alpha_1,\\alpha_2): The incomplete bilinear form through one fixed block.
glossary.\\mathscr K_{c;d_1,d_2}: The complete fixed-slope two-row Gram/inverse-phase block.
glossary.\\widetilde\\alpha_i: The periodization of the i-th integer coefficient sequence modulo pd_i on unit residues.

1a9cfcfe3eedd5e2.title: TWO RECIPROCITY CHARTS, PAID EQUAL REDUCED-PHASE SECTOR, AND THE EXACT CENTERED CROSSED L2 SUPPLIER
1a9cfcfe3eedd5e2.author: slava chan
1a9cfcfe3eedd5e2.statement:
TWO RECIPROCITY CHARTS, PAID EQUAL REDUCED-PHASE SECTOR, AND THE EXACT CENTERED CROSSED L2 SUPPLIER.

Fix constants C,J>=1 and Q>=8. Let real numbers H,V,P,B satisfy
  2<=H<=Q^(1/3),  2<=V<H,  P=QH/V,  B>=1.                 (1)
Let A be a nonzero integer with |A|<=Q^C. Let cal L be a finite label set. For every ell in cal L, integer v in [V,2V), and prime p in [P,2P) with gcd(v,p)=1, put n=vp and let cal X_{ell,v,p} be a finite set of triples x=(q,m,k) satisfying
  Q<=q,m<2Q,  qm+nk=A,  gcd(qm,n)=1.                       (2)
For h in an integer interval I_ell contained either in [H,2H) or in (-2H,-H], let a_{ell,v,p,h}(x) be a complex coefficient with
  |a_{ell,v,p,h}(x)|<=B.                                   (3)
It may retain every literal source, least-prime, marker, fixed-U, frequency, collision, provenance, and projective mask, but does not include the reciprocal/source phase. Assume B and #cal L are subpolynomial.

For x=(q,m,k), define
  d_x=gcd(|A|,q),  r_x=q/d_x,  t_x=k/d_x,                  (4)
  pi_{x,h}=c_{r_x}(h)/phi(r_x),
  eta_{x,h}=e_{r_x}(ht_x)-pi_{x,h}.                        (5)
Then d_x divides k, gcd(t_x,r_x)=1, and the two exact reciprocity charts agree:
  e(Ah/(qn))e_n(-Ahqbar)
   =e_q(Ah nbar)
   =e_q(hk)
   =e_{r_x}(ht_x).                                         (6)
Thus eta_{x,h} is exactly the same-gauge nonprincipal remainder of fact c5f49ab9e8bd2c60, with every factor in (3) unchanged.

Define the complete q-off-diagonal nonprincipal L2 sum
  O_2^np
   =sum_{ell,v,p}sum_{h in I_ell}
      sum_{x_1,x_2 in cal X_{ell,v,p}, q_1 not equal q_2}
       a_{ell,v,p,h}(x_1)
       conjugate(a_{ell,v,p,h}(x_2))
       eta_{x_1,h}conjugate(eta_{x_2,h}).                   (7)
Split it exactly as
  O_2^np=O_2^eq+O_2^cross,                                  (8)
where O_2^eq has t_1/r_1=t_2/r_2 and O_2^cross has t_1/r_1 not equal to t_2/r_2.

For every epsilon>0, the equal reduced-phase part is paid absolutely:
  |O_2^eq|<<_{C,epsilon}B^2(#cal L)Q^(2+epsilon)H
  <<_{C,epsilon}P Q^(5/3+epsilon).                         (9)
This includes q_1 not equal to q_2: equality of reduced phases does not force q_1=q_2 because the divisors d_1,d_2 of A may differ.

For a term of O_2^cross put
  g=gcd(r_1,r_2),  r_1=gu_1,  r_2=gu_2,
  gcd(u_1,u_2)=1,
  delta_12=u_2t_1-u_1t_2.                                 (10)
Then delta_12 is nonzero, and the exact centered kernel is
  eta_{x_1,h}conjugate(eta_{x_2,h})
   =e_{g u_1u_2}(h delta_12)
    -pi_{x_1,h}e_{r_2}(-ht_2)
    -pi_{x_2,h}e_{r_1}(ht_1)
    +pi_{x_1,h}pi_{x_2,h}.                                 (11)
All common-gcd strata g, both source divisors d_i, both reduced conductors r_i, the source coordinates t_i, and every coefficient and mask in (3) remain in (11).

For the following sufficiency conclusion, assume explicitly the normalized principal-row factorization used in fact c5f49ab9e8bd2c60. Namely, by the injective q-projection write the unique coefficient at q as
  a_{ell,v,p,h}(x_q)=alpha_{q,h}w_{q,h},                   (12)
where
  |alpha_{q,h}|<=tau(r_x),
  |w_{q,h}|<=C_J(L_pr/H)(1+|h|/H)^(-J),
  L_pr<=BH,                                                 (13)
and extend it by zero outside the displayed finite band. Then, after the q-diagonal and principal row paid in facts 294ac3b02b065aec and c5f49ab9e8bd2c60 and the equal-phase payment (9), the precise remaining sufficient source theorem is
  CNP2:
  |O_2^cross|<<_{C,J,epsilon}P Q^(5/3+epsilon).             (14)
This is an absolute sufficient form; a one-sided upper bound would suffice for the original positive L2 moment. Without (12)-(13), equations (6)-(11) and the payment (9) remain valid, but no principal-row payment is asserted for the general bounded coefficient class.

Fact c5f49ab9e8bd2c60 proves that the ordinary character large sieve does not supply (14), even on a favorable prime-conductor separated slice. Thus a proof of CNP2 must use source-specific crossed dispersion in the joint variables d_i,r_i,t_i,v,p, or another mechanism stronger than direct height-character orthogonality.

No estimate for CNP2, no PMD closure, and no Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
1a9cfcfe3eedd5e2.proof:
The first equality in (6) is the additive reciprocity identity in fact ddcb0baef17b6ab0. The second is the actual-source phase collapse in fact db067f4633c13fed. Facts 7670948dedd78714 and c5f49ab9e8bd2c60 prove d_x|k, gcd(t_x,r_x)=1, and e_q(hk)=e_{r_x}(ht_x). This proves (4)-(6), with no change to the coefficient array.

We estimate the equal-phase sector. Since t_i/r_i are reduced fractions, the equality
  t_1/r_1=t_2/r_2
implies r_1=r_2 and t_1=t_2. Equivalently k_1/q_1=k_2/q_2. Fact 2359a25d9fc6dd9b proves that every fixed rational source phase k/q has at most tau(|A|) preimages in a source set of the form (2). Also
  |pi_{x,h}|=|c_{r_x}(h)|/phi(r_x)<=1,
because c_{r_x}(h) is a sum of phi(r_x) complex numbers of modulus one. Hence
  |eta_{x,h}|<=2.                                          (15)

Fix ell,v,p,h and group cal X_{ell,v,p} by the reduced phase alpha=t/r. On one fibre cal F_alpha, eta_{x,h} has the same value eta_{alpha,h}. Taking absolute values only within this equal-phase sector gives
  |sum_alpha |eta_{alpha,h}|^2
       sum_{x_1,x_2 in cal F_alpha,q_1 not equal q_2}
         a_h(x_1)conjugate(a_h(x_2))|
  <=4 tau(|A|)B^2 #cal X_{ell,v,p}.                        (16)
Indeed, for a fibre of size M, the ordered off-diagonal absolute sum is at most M(M-1)B^2<=M tau(|A|)B^2.

Fact 914048233fada05f applies because p>P>Q and gives
  #cal X_{ell,v,p}
  <<_{C,epsilon}Q^epsilon(1+Q^2/(vp))
  <<_{C,epsilon}Q^(1+epsilon)/H.                           (17)
There are at most 2H heights, O((#cal L)VP) outer rows, and VP=QH. Sum (16), use (17), and use the fixed-power divisor estimate for tau(|A|) already contained in fact 2359a25d9fc6dd9b. This proves the first bound in (9). Its ratio to P Q^(5/3) is
  [Q^2H]/[Q^(8/3)H/V]=V/Q^(2/3)
  <H/Q^(2/3)<=Q^(-1/3),                                   (18)
so the second bound follows after renaming epsilon.

We derive the crossed kernel. From (10),
  t_1/r_1-t_2/r_2
   =(u_2t_1-u_1t_2)/(g u_1u_2)
   =delta_12/(g u_1u_2).                                  (19)
The unequal-phase condition makes delta_12 nonzero. Ramanujan sums are real, so both pi_{x_i,h} are real. Expand
  (e_{r_1}(ht_1)-pi_{x_1,h})
  (e_{r_2}(-ht_2)-pi_{x_2,h})
and use (19). This gives (11) exactly.

Under (12)-(13), the principal row satisfies exactly the normalized decay/provenance hypotheses in fact c5f49ab9e8bd2c60, with L_pr<=BH. That fact therefore pays the principal L2 mass. Fact 294ac3b02b065aec pays the original q-diagonal. Equation (8) is an exhaustive partition of the remaining nonprincipal q-off-diagonal, and (9) pays its equal-phase part. Hence (14) is sufficient under the explicitly stated factorization. If it is absent, the proof has established only the unconditional identities and equal-phase estimate, as stated. The large-sieve and scope assertions are precisely those proved in fact c5f49ab9e8bd2c60. This proves every claim.

glossary.CNP2: The exact centered unequal-phase nonprincipal L2 supplier.
glossary.O_2^cross: The q-off-diagonal nonprincipal L2 sector with unequal reduced rational source phases.
glossary.O_2^eq: The q-off-diagonal nonprincipal L2 sector with equal reduced rational source phases.
glossary.delta_12: The crossed numerator u_2t_1-u_1t_2 after extracting gcd(r_1,r_2).

1acbe88cc741c6f1.title: GA-HARD-dBV: DIVISOR-SPARSE LOW-d-CONDUCTOR SET, REDUNDANT NONRESONANCE DELETION, AND HARD-SELECTOR VARIATION
1acbe88cc741c6f1.author: slava chan
1acbe88cc741c6f1.statement:
GA-HARD-dBV: DIVISOR-SPARSE LOW-d-CONDUCTOR SET, REDUNDANT NONRESONANCE DELETION, AND HARD-SELECTOR VARIATION.

Let T and Delta be nonzero integers, let L>=1 and D>=1 be real numbers, and for every positive integer d put
rho(d)=d/gcd(d,T),
m_d=rho(d)/gcd(rho(d),Delta).                                   (1)
Then
d divides T Delta if and only if m_d=1.                          (2)
In particular, when L>1, the condition m_d>L implies d does not divide T Delta, so the explicit nonresonance deletion is redundant on that hard branch.

Let
E(D;T,Delta,L)={d in Z:D<=d<2D and m_d<=L}.                     (3)
Then
|E(D;T,Delta,L)|
 <=floor(L) tau(|T|)tau(|Delta|).                               (4)
Define H(d)=1_{D<=d<2D}1_{m_d>L} for d in Z, with H(d)=0 for d<=0. Its complete discrete variation satisfies
sum_{d in Z}|H(d+1)-H(d)|
 <=2+2 floor(L)tau(|T|)tau(|Delta|).                            (5)
Consequently, for every complex sequence f(d) supported on D<=d<2D,
Var(Hf)
 <=Var(f)+[2+2 floor(L)tau(|T|)tau(|Delta|)] sup_d|f(d)|,        (6)
where both variations are endpoint-inclusive after zero-extension.

Applied to one fixed primitive-ray pair in the hard Good-W form of fact cff9d29efb555b8e, take T=mathscr A and Delta=Delta_0. Distinct primitive signed rays have Delta_0 nonzero. With L=(log(2x))^C and polynomially bounded physical parameters, the hard d-selector has x^{o(1)} total variation per fixed ray pair. Thus this particular selector cannot by itself be the source of linear mask variation in the conditional ledger C-qSRC-BV-SUP of fact eb01e7b374521a0c. Equations (4)-(6) are only a rowwise selector audit: summing their supremum term over every literal ray, source, copy, and provenance row is not estimated here. The theorem does not bound the fully aggregated profile A_{m,c,chi}(d), does not estimate the F>Q principal source or the small-dilator projected-incidence branch, and proves no C-qSRC-BV-SUP, tail payment, or Goldbach conclusion.
1acbe88cc741c6f1.proof:
Put
g=gcd(d,T),  e=gcd(rho(d),Delta),  s=m_d.                        (7)
Then
d=g rho(d)=g e s.                                                (8)
The integer g is a positive divisor of |T|, the integer e is a positive divisor of |Delta|, and s is a positive integer. If m_d<=L, then 1<=s<=floor(L). Therefore the map d to the triple (g,e,s) in (7) places every d in E(D;T,Delta,L) among at most
tau(|T|)tau(|Delta|)floor(L)
triples. Distinctness of the map is not required for this upper bound. This proves (4).

Because g=gcd(d,T), the integers rho(d)=d/g and T/g are coprime. Hence
d divides T Delta
if and only if
g rho(d) divides g(T/g)Delta
if and only if
rho(d) divides Delta.
By definition (1), rho(d) divides Delta if and only if gcd(rho(d),Delta)=rho(d), which is equivalent to m_d=1. This proves (2), and the redundancy statement follows from L>1.

On the interval [D,2D), H equals one except at the integers in E(D;T,Delta,L). Starting from the constant interval indicator, whose endpoint-inclusive variation is at most two, changing its value from one to zero at one integer changes the total variation by at most two. Therefore
Var(H)<=2+2|E(D;T,Delta,L)|.
Insert (4) to obtain (5).

For every d,
|H(d+1)f(d+1)-H(d)f(d)|
 <=H(d+1)|f(d+1)-f(d)|
   +|f(d)| |H(d+1)-H(d)|.
Summing over d, using 0<=H<=1, and then using (5) proves (6).

In the primitive signed-ray notation of fact cff9d29efb555b8e,
Delta_0=epsilon b a'-epsilon' b'a.
If Delta_0=0, the two positive coprime pairs (a,b) and (a',b') have the same sign and the same reduced positive slope, so primitiveness forces a=a', b=b', and epsilon=epsilon'; hence the rays are equal. Therefore distinct rays have Delta_0 nonzero. All physical integers are polynomially bounded in x, so fixed divisor functions are x^{o(1)}, and L is a fixed power of log(2x). Equation (5) then gives the stated rowwise x^{o(1)} variation. The final exclusions are explicit because no sum over row-pair supremum terms was estimated.

glossary.E(D;T,Delta,L): The low-reduced-conductor exceptional set inside one marked-dilator interval.
glossary.GA-HARD-dBV: The divisor-sparse variation bound for the hard reduced-dilator selector.
glossary.H(d): The zero-extended hard marked-dilator selector on one interval.

1b35788590b2a000.title: EXACT CENTERED-MELLIN SUBTRACTION, TWO-FIBRE GRAM FORMULA, AND NONORTHOGONALITY
1b35788590b2a000.author: slava chan
1b35788590b2a000.statement:
EXACT CENTERED-MELLIN SUBTRACTION, TWO-FIBRE GRAM FORMULA, AND NONORTHOGONALITY.

Assume the notation of fact 2d6fadb9f8bc513b. Thus b is squarefree, (a,b)=1, and for real t the conductor-generating tensor is
 G_{b,t}(a)
  =product_{p|b;p does not divide N}
    {p^(it)e_p(N[a(b/p)]^(-1))
      +(p^(it)-1)/(p-1)}.                                   (1)
Put
 m_b=c_b(N)/phi(b),                                         (2)
 Gtilde_{b,t}(a)=G_{b,t}(a)-m_b.                            (3)
Then for every real t,
 1/phi(b)sum_{a modulo b;(a,b)=1}Gtilde_{b,t}(a)=0.          (4)

Let W be infinitely differentiable and compactly supported in the positive reals, let F>0, and assume W(1/F)=0. For the smooth conductor block H_{b,W,F} and Mellin transform W_hat from fact 2d6fadb9f8bc513b, one has exactly
 H_{b,W,F}(a)
  =1/(2pi)integral_R W_hat(t)F^(-it)Gtilde_{b,t}(a)dt.       (5)
The integral is absolutely convergent.

For real t,s, the exact normalized complete-unit Gram is
 1/phi(b)sum_{a modulo b;(a,b)=1}
   Gtilde_{b,t}(a)overline(Gtilde_{b,s}(a))
 =
 product_{p|b;p does not divide N}
  {(p-1)^(-2)+[1-(p-1)^(-2)]p^(i(t-s))}
 -|m_b|^2.                                                   (6)

In particular, if b=p is prime and p does not divide N, then
 Gtilde_{p,t}(a)
  =p^(it){e_p(Na^(-1))+1/(p-1)},                             (7)
and
 1/(p-1)sum_{a modulo p;a nonzero}
  Gtilde_{p,t}(a)overline(Gtilde_{p,s}(a))
  =[1-(p-1)^(-2)]p^(i(t-s)).                                (8)
Thus distinct real t-fibres are not orthogonal on this prime slice; they are scalar multiples of the same centered inverse-trace row. Centering in (3) is global on the complete unit group. It does not assert primewise centering of each Gtilde fibre for composite b.

No incomplete-a estimate, cross-b estimate, CEN-MZB estimate, C_small estimate or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
1b35788590b2a000.proof:
Fact 2d6fadb9f8bc513b proves that the normalized complete-unit mean of G_{b,t} is m_b=c_b(N)/phi(b), independently of t. Subtracting this constant gives (4).

The same fact gives
 H_{b,W,F}(a)
  =1/(2pi)integral_R W_hat(t)F^(-it)G_{b,t}(a)dt.            (9)
Insert G_{b,t}=Gtilde_{b,t}+m_b. The contribution of the constant m_b equals
 m_b/(2pi) integral_R W_hat(t)F^(-it)dt
 =m_b W(1/F)                                                 (10)
by Mellin inversion. The hypothesis W(1/F)=0 makes (10) vanish, proving (5). The rapid decay of W_hat proved in the predecessor and the pointwise bound for G_{b,t} there show absolute convergence; subtracting the fixed constant m_b preserves it.

It remains to prove (6). Fix a prime p|b with p not dividing N and put
 c=1/(p-1), z=p^(it), y=p^(is).
Let e(a) denote the p-local phase
 e_p(N[a(b/p)]^(-1)).
As the p-coordinate of a ranges over the units, fact 2d6fadb9f8bc513b proves
 E_p e(a)=E_p overline(e(a))=-c,                             (11)
where E_p denotes the normalized unit average. Also E_p|e(a)|^2=1. The p-local factors in G_{b,t} and G_{b,s} are
 g_z(a)=z e(a)+(z-1)c,
 g_y(a)=y e(a)+(y-1)c.                                      (12)
Using (11), expand their local cross moment:
 E_p[g_z(a)overline(g_y(a))]
 =z overline(y)
  -z(overline(y)-1)c^2
  -(z-1)overline(y)c^2
  +(z-1)(overline(y)-1)c^2
 =c^2+(1-c^2)z overline(y).                                 (13)
Since z overline(y)=p^(i(t-s)), (13) is the p-factor in the product in (6).

If p|b and p|N, formula (1) has no p-factor; equivalently that coordinate contributes one to the normalized cross moment. Squarefreeness and the Chinese remainder theorem therefore multiply (13) over exactly the primes p|b with p not dividing N. This gives
 1/phi(b)sum_a^*G_{b,t}(a)overline(G_{b,s}(a))
 =
 product_{p|b;p does not divide N}
  {c_p^2+(1-c_p^2)p^(i(t-s))},                              (14)
where c_p=1/(p-1).

Both G_{b,t} and G_{b,s} have mean m_b. Expanding
 (G_{b,t}-m_b)overline(G_{b,s}-m_b)
and averaging subtracts |m_b|^2 from (14). This proves (6).

Finally take b=p prime with p not dividing N. Formula (1) becomes
 G_{p,t}(a)=p^(it)e_p(Na^(-1))+(p^(it)-1)/(p-1).
Here m_p=c_p(N)/phi(p)=-1/(p-1). Subtracting m_p gives (7). Formula (8) follows either from (6) or by multiplying (7) and using the normalized second moment
 1/(p-1)sum_{a nonzero}|e_p(Na^(-1))+1/(p-1)|^2
 =1-(p-1)^(-2),
which is the local calculation in fact 2d6fadb9f8bc513b. Equation (7) shows directly that changing t multiplies the same row by p^(it), proving nonorthogonality and all stated scope restrictions.

glossary.Gtilde_{b,t}(a): The globally centered Mellin conductor fibre G_{b,t}(a)-m_b.
glossary.m_b: The t-independent complete-unit mean c_b(N)/phi(b) of G_{b,t}.

1b4627a257cc9c00.title: GA-ETA-TENSOR: EXACT PRIME-LOCAL PROJECTOR DECOMPOSITION, LITERAL SOURCE-INCIDENCE ENERGIES, AND THE PRIME-CONDUCTOR MEAN-ZERO NO-FIT
1b4627a257cc9c00.author: slava chan
1b4627a257cc9c00.statement:
GA-ETA-TENSOR: EXACT PRIME-LOCAL PROJECTOR DECOMPOSITION, LITERAL SOURCE-INCIDENCE ENERGIES, AND THE PRIME-CONDUCTOR MEAN-ZERO NO-FIT.

Adopt the fixed positive squarefree additive conductor t, the normalized Kloosterman columns V_{t;eta}, the Gram matrix M_t, and the literal source profiles G_{t,eta}^{agg}, G_{t,eta}^{perp}, Z_{t,eta}^{agg}(n) from facts f0fa4ee49bb23934 and 3207666028864f95. Let
Omega_t=product_{p|t}(Z/pZ)^*
be the Chinese-remainder coordinate set for the unit inverse arguments eta.

For every prime p|t and every Hilbert-valued profile X=(X_eta)_{eta in Omega_t}, define the local constant and centered projections
(C_p X)(eta)=1/(p-1) sum_{u in (Z/pZ)^*} X(eta with its p-coordinate replaced by u),
D_p=I-C_p.                                                         (1)
The operators belonging to distinct primes commute. Let P_o(t) be the set of odd prime divisors of t. For S contained in P_o(t), put
Pi_{t,S}
 = product_{p in S}D_p product_{p in P_o(t)\S}C_p,                 (2)
and include the factor C_2 in (2) when 2|t. Then the nonzero Pi_{t,S} are mutually orthogonal projections and
I=sum_{S contained in P_o(t)}Pi_{t,S}.                              (3)
Their dimensions on the scalar eta space are
d_{t,S}=product_{p in S}(p-2).                                     (4)

The complete Kloosterman-column Gram has the exact spectral resolution
M_t=sum_{S contained in P_o(t)} lambda_{t,S}Pi_{t,S},
lambda_{t,S}=1/t product_{p in S}p^2.                              (5)
Consequently, for any finite-dimensional Hilbert space K, any K-valued eta profile X, and the Hilbert-valued synthesis A_t tensor I_K,
||(A_t tensor I_K)X||_2^2
 =sum_{S contained in P_o(t)}lambda_{t,S}||Pi_{t,S}X||_2^2.         (6)

Apply these projectors to the literal coefficient profiles by defining
Z_{t,S}(eta;n)
 =Pi_{t,S}(Z_{t,bullet}^{agg}(n))(eta).                             (7)
For every nonempty S,
Pi_{t,S}(G_{t,bullet}^{perp})
 =Pi_{t,S}(G_{t,bullet}^{agg})
 =sum_n conjugate(Z_{t,S}(bullet;n))E_{t;n},                        (8)
and the exact projected source energy is
||Pi_{t,S}(G_{t,bullet}^{perp})||_2^2
 =1/t sum_eta sum_{n,n'}
   conjugate(Z_{t,S}(eta;n))Z_{t,S}(eta;n')c_t(n-n').              (9)
Here every sum defining Z_{t,eta}^{agg} is still the literal sum from fact f0fa4ee49bb23934, so (7) is an alternating combination of exact retained-pair incidence classes eta=-C_q s^{-1} modulo t; every source coefficient and pair-dependent deletion remains inside those incidence classes.

Put
Vbold_t=(V_{t;eta})_eta,
Gbold_t^{perp}=(G_{t,eta}^{perp})_eta.
The fixed-t mean-zero residual has the exact direct-pairing decomposition
sum_eta <V_{t;eta},G_{t,eta}^{perp}>
 =sum_{nonempty S contained in P_o(t)}
   <Pi_{t,S}Vbold_t,Pi_{t,S}Gbold_t^{perp}>.                        (10)
Moreover
||Pi_{t,S}Vbold_t||_2^2=lambda_{t,S}d_{t,S},                       (11)
so every sector has the exact source-specific Cauchy interface
|<Pi_{t,S}Vbold_t,Pi_{t,S}Gbold_t^{perp}>|
 <=(lambda_{t,S}d_{t,S})^(1/2)
   [1/t sum_eta sum_{n,n'}
    conjugate(Z_{t,S}(eta;n))Z_{t,S}(eta;n')c_t(n-n')]^(1/2).      (12)
Equation (12) is an interface, not an asserted canonical estimate.

The global mean-zero condition of fact 3207666028864f95 removes exactly the sector S=empty:
Pi_{t,empty}Gbold_t^{perp}=0.                                      (13)
It forces no other sector to vanish. In particular, if t=p is an odd prime, then
Pi_{p,{p}}Gbold_p^{perp}=Gbold_p^{perp},
(M_p tensor I)Gbold_p^{perp}=p Gbold_p^{perp}.                     (14)
Thus the complete prime-conductor residual lies in the top eigenvalue p sector. More generally, the fully locally centered sector S=P_o(t) has eigenvalue
lambda_{t,P_o(t)}=t when t is odd, and t/4 when 2|t.                (15)

Equations (7)-(12) identify the first literal coefficient-incidence quantities that a tensor-spectral proof of GA-ETA-PERP-SUP must estimate. Global eta mean zero and the bare spectrum alone cannot provide a fixed-power saving: for an odd prime p, any nonzero Hilbert vector W and distinct eta_1,eta_2 give the mean-zero abstract profile X_{eta_1}=W, X_{eta_2}=-W, X_eta=0 otherwise, and (M_p tensor I)X=pX. This is a formal method no-fit, not an assertion that this abstract profile is realized by the Good-W source.

This theorem proves the tensor projector ledger and exact literal incidence interfaces only. It proves no bound for any nonempty projected source energy in (9), no GA-ETA-PERP-SUP estimate, no full GA-qCENT estimate, no tail payment, and no Goldbach conclusion.
1b4627a257cc9c00.proof:
For each odd prime p, fact f0fa4ee49bb23934 gives
M_p=pI-(1+1/p)J,
where J is the all-ones matrix on the p-1 unit eta coordinates. The local constant projection is C_p=J/(p-1), and D_p=I-C_p. Hence
M_p=pD_p+p^{-1}C_p.                                                (16)
For p=2, the eta space is one-dimensional, C_2=I, D_2=0, and M_2=2^{-1}C_2, so (16) remains valid after discarding the zero centered sector.

The averaging operators C_p are self-adjoint idempotents, D_p are their orthogonal complements, and operators in distinct CRT coordinates commute. Expanding
product_{p|t}(C_p+D_p)
and omitting D_2 proves (2)-(3). A centered local coordinate has dimension p-2, while a constant coordinate has dimension one, proving (4).

Fact f0fa4ee49bb23934 identifies M_t, after CRT and harmless local unit permutations, with the tensor product of the M_p. Local unit permutations preserve both the constant line and its orthogonal complement. Tensoring (16) over p|t gives (5): choosing D_p instead of C_p changes the local eigenvalue from p^{-1} to p and therefore multiplies the base eigenvalue product_{p|t}p^{-1}=t^{-1} by p^2. Orthogonality of the projectors gives (6), first for scalar profiles and then componentwise for K-valued profiles.

For (8), fact f0fa4ee49bb23934 gives
G_{t,eta}^{agg}=sum_n conjugate(Z_{t,eta}^{agg}(n))E_{t;n}.
The projections in (1)-(2) have real coefficients and act only in eta, so applying Pi_{t,S} commutes with conjugation and the finite n-sum, giving the second equality in (8). Fact 3207666028864f95 gives
G_{t,eta}^{perp}=G_{t,eta}^{agg}-Gbar_t,
where Gbar_t is independent of eta. Every nonempty Pi_{t,S} contains at least one factor D_p, which kills an eta-independent profile. This proves the first equality in (8).

Expand the squared norm in (8). Fact 7ee795d9bff04bb2 gives
<E_{t;n},E_{t;n'}>=c_t(n-n')/t.
Substitution proves (9). Definition (7) applies only finite conditional averages and differences after the exact aggregates have been formed. Since each aggregate is literally the sum of all retained gamma=(t,s,C_q) with eta=-C_qs^{-1}, this changes no term or selector and proves the incidence interpretation.

View Vbold_t and Gbold_t^{perp} as vectors in the Hilbert direct sum over eta. Insert the orthogonal resolution (3) in both slots. Cross terms between different S vanish, proving (10). If A_t is the synthesis map with columns V_{t;eta}, then
||Pi_{t,S}Vbold_t||_2^2
 =trace(Pi_{t,S}A_t^*A_t)
 =trace(Pi_{t,S}M_t)
 =lambda_{t,S}d_{t,S},
which is (11). Cauchy in the eta-direct-sum Hilbert space, followed by (9) and (11), proves (12).

The global average projection is precisely
Pi_{t,empty}=product_{p|t}C_p.
Equation (3) of fact 3207666028864f95 says the global eta sum of G_{t,eta}^{perp} is zero, which is equivalent to (13). If t=p is an odd prime, the only sectors are empty and {p}; equations (3), (5), and (13) give (14). Formula (15) follows from (5): for odd t the product over all p|t is t^{-1}t^2=t, while for t=2u with u odd it is (2u)^{-1}u^2=u/2=t/4.

Finally, the displayed two-point profile has global sum zero. At an odd prime, JX=0, so (16) gives (M_p tensor I)X=pX. Therefore global mean zero alone is compatible with the exact top spectral scale. This proves the stated formal no-fit without making any claim about realization by the literal source. All exclusions follow because no bound on the nonempty incidence energies (9) has been assumed or proved.

glossary.C_p: Conditional averaging in the p-component of the inverse-argument eta.
glossary.Omega_t: The Chinese-remainder product of the unit inverse-argument coordinate sets modulo the primes dividing t.
glossary.P_o(t): The set of odd prime divisors of t.
glossary.Pi_{t,S}: The tensor projector centered exactly in the prime coordinates in S and constant in the remaining coordinates.
glossary.Z_{t,S}(eta;n): The literal aggregate coefficient profile after applying the tensor projector Pi_{t,S} in eta.
glossary.d_{t,S}: The dimension of the eta tensor sector Pi_{t,S}.

1c0f8ee6ed71cd50.title: EXACT COLLAPSE OF THE ALL-NONZERO NONRESONANT FOURIER-KLOOSTERMAN TENSOR. Let p>2 be prime. For i=1,2 let d_i>1 be squarefree with (p,d_i)=1, let C_i be a unit modulo d_i, and let a_i be a finitely supported complex sequence. Define its unit periodization and additive Fourier transform by
1c0f8ee6ed71cd50.author: slava chan
1c0f8ee6ed71cd50.statement:
EXACT COLLAPSE OF THE ALL-NONZERO NONRESONANT FOURIER-KLOOSTERMAN TENSOR. Let p>2 be prime. For i=1,2 let d_i>1 be squarefree with (p,d_i)=1, let C_i be a unit modulo d_i, and let a_i be a finitely supported complex sequence. Define its unit periodization and additive Fourier transform by
tilde a_i(z)=sum_{n congruent to z modulo pd_i}a_i(n) for (z,pd_i)=1, with tilde a_i(z)=0 otherwise,
hat a_i(k)=sum_{z modulo pd_i}tilde a_i(z)e_{pd_i}(-kz). (1)
Let bar p_i be the inverse of p modulo d_i and define
K_i(k)=sum_{z modulo d_i,(z,d_i)=1}e_{d_i}(C_i z^(-1)+k bar p_i z), (2)
A_i=sum_{k modulo pd_i,p not dividing k}hat a_i(k)K_i(k),
R_i=sum_{n in Z}a_i(n)1_{(n,pd_i)=1}e_{d_i}(C_i n^(-1)). (3)
Then exactly
A_i=-d_iR_i. (4)
Consequently the scalar
N_nr=-1/(p^2d_1d_2) times p^2/(p-1)^2 times A_1A_2 (5)
is exactly
N_nr=-R_1R_2/(p-1)^2. (6)
The scalar (5) is the all-nonzero nonresonant minus-one part of the completion tensor in fact 5a7bf376fe94485e, but equations (1)--(6) are self-contained. No estimate is asserted.
1c0f8ee6ed71cd50.proof:
Parametrize k modulo pd_i by its CRT coordinates r=k d_i^(-1) modulo p and t=k p^(-1) modulo d_i. The condition p not dividing k is exactly r nonzero. The CRT additive-character identity gives
hat a_i(k)=sum_n a_i(n)1_{(n,pd_i)=1}e_p(-rn)e_{d_i}(-tn). (7)
Also K_i(k) depends only on t and is
K_i(t)=sum_{z modulo d_i,(z,d_i)=1}e_{d_i}(C_i z^(-1)+tz). (8)
For every n with (n,p)=1,
sum_{r in F_p^times}e_p(-rn)=-1. (9)
Sum (7) over r nonzero, multiply by (8), and then sum t modulo d_i. This gives
A_i=-sum_n a_i(n)1_{(n,pd_i)=1}sum_{t modulo d_i}e_{d_i}(-tn)sum_{z unit modulo d_i}e_{d_i}(C_i z^(-1)+tz). (10)
Additive orthogonality in t forces z congruent to n modulo d_i and contributes d_i. Since n is a unit modulo d_i, the surviving term is d_i e_{d_i}(C_i n^(-1)). Hence (10) is -d_iR_i, proving (4). Substitute (4) twice into (5). The product A_1A_2 equals d_1d_2R_1R_2, so all d_i and p^2 factors cancel and (6) follows.

glossary.A_i: The i-th Fourier-Kloosterman row summed over frequencies nonzero modulo p.
glossary.N_nr: The all-nonzero nonresonant minus-one scalar contribution.
glossary.R_i: The original incomplete cofactor inverse-phase row.

1c42e0c22d9a5cca.title: EXACT DISJOINT CLASSIFICATION OF THE CONDITION-(6) A-ROUTING RESIDUAL. Fix Q>1, delta>0, rho>0, a positive squarefree integer m_eff, and a positive real B_*. Put s=delta+rho and define
1c42e0c22d9a5cca.author: slava chan
1c42e0c22d9a5cca.statement:
EXACT DISJOINT CLASSIFICATION OF THE CONDITION-(6) A-ROUTING RESIDUAL. Fix Q>1, delta>0, rho>0, a positive squarefree integer m_eff, and a positive real B_*. Put s=delta+rho and define
L_A=max{Q^(4s),m_eff Q^(2s)/B_*},
U_A=B_*^2Q^(-4s).
Then the existence of a factorization m_eff=m_0m_1 satisfying
m_1<=B_*Q^(-2s),
Q^(4s)<=m_0<=B_*^2Q^(-4s)
is equivalent to the existence of a divisor d of m_eff in the closed A-divisor interval [L_A,U_A]. Consequently the A-ROUTING RESIDUAL of fact 8eb30e55bdef6b27 is the disjoint union, in the displayed order, of
(R1) B_*<Q^(4s);
(R2) B_*>=Q^(4s) and B_*^3<m_eff Q^(6s);
(R3) B_*>=Q^(4s), B_*^3>=m_eff Q^(6s), and [L_A,U_A] contains no divisor of m_eff.
In (R3) the interval is nonempty. Thus unbalanced residual boxes split without overlap into two pure scale failures and one genuine effective-modulus divisor gap. This theorem classifies the routing condition only and estimates none of the three classes.
1c42e0c22d9a5cca.proof:
Suppose m_eff=m_0m_1 and put d=m_0. The upper bound on m_1 is equivalent to
m_eff/d<=B_*Q^(-2s),
which is equivalent to
d>=m_eff Q^(2s)/B_*.
The two bounds on m_0 are exactly
Q^(4s)<=d<=B_*^2Q^(-4s).
Thus all three factorization inequalities hold exactly when d divides m_eff and L_A<=d<=U_A. Conversely any divisor d in this interval gives the required factorization by taking m_0=d and m_1=m_eff/d. Since m_eff is squarefree, m_0 and m_1 are automatically coprime, as required in fact 8eb30e55bdef6b27.

It remains to classify when the interval can be nonempty. The inequality
Q^(4s)<=B_*^2Q^(-4s)
is equivalent to B_*>=Q^(4s). The inequality
m_eff Q^(2s)/B_*<=B_*^2Q^(-4s)
is equivalent to B_*^3>=m_eff Q^(6s). Hence L_A<=U_A exactly when both scale inequalities hold. If the first fails, the box belongs to (R1). If the first holds and the second fails, it belongs to (R2). If both hold, the interval is nonempty, and failure of eligibility is exactly the absence of a divisor in it, which is (R3). The ordered alternatives are visibly disjoint and exhaustive. By the definition of A-ROUTING RESIDUAL in fact 8eb30e55bdef6b27 as the logical complement of eligibility, this proves every assertion.

glossary.A-divisor interval: The exact interval of complementary effective-modulus divisors whose occupancy is equivalent to fixed-slack A-process eligibility.

1c64020b89f097c4.title: EXACT TARGET-GCD DESCENT FOR A NORMALIZED LINEAR INCIDENCE. Let a,b,m,k,L be positive integers with am+bk=L, gcd(a,b)=1, and a squarefree. Put c=gcd(a,L). Then c divides k. Writing a=cq, k=ck_1, and L=cL_1 gives qm+bk_1=L_1, with gcd(c,q)=1, gcd(c,b)=1, gcd(q,b)=1, and gcd(q,L_1)=1. Conversely, if positive integers c,q,b,m,k_1,L_1 satisfy qm+bk_1=L_1 and gcd(cq,b)=1, then a=cq,k=ck_1,L=cL_1 satisfy am+bk=L and gcd(a,b)=1. One always has gcd(a,L)=c gcd(q,L_1); hence gcd(q,L_1)=1 implies gcd(a,L)=c
1c64020b89f097c4.author: slava chan
1c64020b89f097c4.statement: EXACT TARGET-GCD DESCENT FOR A NORMALIZED LINEAR INCIDENCE. Let a,b,m,k,L be positive integers with am+bk=L, gcd(a,b)=1, and a squarefree. Put c=gcd(a,L). Then c divides k. Writing a=cq, k=ck_1, and L=cL_1 gives qm+bk_1=L_1, with gcd(c,q)=1, gcd(c,b)=1, gcd(q,b)=1, and gcd(q,L_1)=1. Conversely, if positive integers c,q,b,m,k_1,L_1 satisfy qm+bk_1=L_1 and gcd(cq,b)=1, then a=cq,k=ck_1,L=cL_1 satisfy am+bk=L and gcd(a,b)=1. One always has gcd(a,L)=c gcd(q,L_1); hence gcd(q,L_1)=1 implies gcd(a,L)=c.
1c64020b89f097c4.proof:
Because c divides both a and L, the equation am+bk=L implies c divides bk. Since c divides a and gcd(a,b)=1, one has gcd(c,b)=1, hence c divides k. Substituting a=cq,k=ck_1,L=cL_1 and dividing by c yields qm+bk_1=L_1. Squarefreeness of a=cq gives gcd(c,q)=1. The original gcd(a,b)=1 gives gcd(c,b)=gcd(q,b)=1. Finally gcd(a,L)=c and a=cq,L=cL_1 imply c gcd(q,L_1)=c, hence gcd(q,L_1)=1.
Conversely, multiplying qm+bk_1=L_1 by c gives (cq)m+b(ck_1)=cL_1, which is am+bk=L. The hypothesis gcd(cq,b)=1 is exactly gcd(a,b)=1. Finally gcd(a,L)=gcd(cq,cL_1)=c gcd(q,L_1), proving the last assertion.

1cdf7ff6cd4588d4.title: Let I be a finite set. For each s∈I let H_s be a complex Hilbert space and let a_s,f_s∈H_s. Let R and Q be real numbers satisfying Q=R+Re(∑_{s∈I}⟨a_s,f_s⟩). Define E=∑_{s∈I}||f_s||^2 and define the nonnegative number A=(∑_{s∈I}||a_s||^2)^{1/2}. Then
1cdf7ff6cd4588d4.author: slava chan
1cdf7ff6cd4588d4.statement:
Let I be a finite set. For each s∈I let H_s be a complex Hilbert space and let a_s,f_s∈H_s. Let R and Q be real numbers satisfying Q=R+Re(∑_{s∈I}⟨a_s,f_s⟩). Define E=∑_{s∈I}||f_s||^2 and define the nonnegative number A=(∑_{s∈I}||a_s||^2)^{1/2}. Then
(-Q)_+≤A E^{1/2}+|R|.
Moreover A is the least nonnegative constant C for which |Re(∑_{s∈I}⟨a_s,f_s⟩)|≤C(∑_{s∈I}||f_s||^2)^{1/2} holds for every tuple (f_s)_{s∈I} in the Hilbert direct sum. Consequently, if P≥1 and ε≥0 are real numbers and A^2≤P^{6+2ε}, then (-Q)_+≤P^{3+ε}E^{1/2}+|R|. Conversely, if R=0 and (-Q)_+≤P^{3+ε}E^{1/2} holds for every tuple (f_s)_{s∈I}, with Q=Re(∑_{s∈I}⟨a_s,f_s⟩), then A≤P^{3+ε}. Thus, on the full Hilbert direct sum, the sharp exponent factor multiplying E^{1/2} is determined by the squared norm of the coefficient vectors.
1cdf7ff6cd4588d4.proof:
Since Q is real,
(-Q)_+=max(-Q,0)≤|Q-R|+|R|.
The defining identity for Q gives
|Q-R|≤|∑_{s∈I}⟨a_s,f_s⟩|.
Apply Cauchy–Schwarz in the Hilbert direct sum ⊕_{s∈I}H_s:
|∑_{s∈I}⟨a_s,f_s⟩|
≤(∑_{s∈I}||a_s||^2)^{1/2}(∑_{s∈I}||f_s||^2)^{1/2}
=A E^{1/2}.
This proves the first bound.

The same argument shows that C=A is admissible in the asserted operator inequality. If A=0, every a_s is zero and the least constant is 0. Suppose A>0. In the direct-sum Hilbert space choose f_s=a_s/A for every s, with a harmless common unit scalar if required by the convention for which argument of the inner product is complex-linear. Then ∑_s||f_s||^2=1 and the absolute value of the real part of the summed inner products can be made equal to A. Hence no C<A can work for every tuple. Therefore the least constant is exactly A.

If P≥1, ε≥0, and A^2≤P^{6+2ε}, then A≤P^{3+ε}; substitution into the first bound proves the forward consequence. For the converse, the hypothesis is asserted for every tuple. Apply it first to (f_s) and then to (-f_s). Since Q changes sign and E does not, the two inequalities imply
|Re(∑_s⟨a_s,f_s⟩)|≤P^{3+ε}E^{1/2}
for every tuple. By the sharp least-constant result, A≤P^{3+ε}.

glossary.(-Q)_+: The positive part max(-Q,0) of the negative of Q.
glossary.H_s: The complex Hilbert space attached to state s.
glossary.I: The finite set of state labels.
glossary.P: A real scale parameter satisfying P≥1.
glossary.Q: The real signed quantity represented by the state pairing plus a remainder.
glossary.R: The real remainder term outside the state pairing.
glossary.a_s: The coefficient vector in state s.
glossary.f_s: An arbitrary test vector in state s.

1d28c0f84d1aad83.title: COMPLETE-UNIT ORTHOGONALITY OF THE CENTERED CONDUCTOR TENSOR AND A MODULUS-BY-MODULUS COMPLETION NO-FIT FOR CEN-MZB
1d28c0f84d1aad83.author: slava chan
1d28c0f84d1aad83.statement:
COMPLETE-UNIT ORTHOGONALITY OF THE CENTERED CONDUCTOR TENSOR AND A MODULUS-BY-MODULUS COMPLETION NO-FIT FOR CEN-MZB.

Assume the notation and actual scales of facts 050efa07f87f374a and 14fe68fdcbfd99ff. Thus b is squarefree, B=Q^(4/3+o(1)), and for all sufficiently large Q every b in [B,2B) satisfies b>Q. For f|b with (f,N)=1 put
  nu(f)=product_{p|f}[1-1/(p-1)^2].                          (1)

If f_1,f_2|b and (f_1f_2,N)=1, then
  1/phi(b) sum_{a modulo b;(a,b)=1}
    R_{b,f_1}(a)overline(R_{b,f_2}(a))
  =1_{f_1=f_2} nu(f_1).                                     (2)

Define the complete signed high-conductor centered projector
  P_b(a)
   =sum_{f|b;f>F_0,(f,N)=1}
      c_{b/f}(N)R_{b,f}(a)/phi(b/f)
   =Pi_{b,>F_0}(a).                                         (3)
Then exactly
  1/phi(b) sum_{a modulo b;(a,b)=1}|P_b(a)|^2
   =sum_{f|b;f>F_0,(f,N)=1}
      |c_{b/f}(N)/phi(b/f)|^2 nu(f)
   <=1.                                                      (4)
Without the cutoff f>F_0, the last conductor sum is exactly one:
  sum_{f|b;(f,N)=1}
      |c_{b/f}(N)/phi(b/f)|^2 nu(f)=1.                       (5)

Let alpha be supported on Q<=a<2Q and satisfy
  sum_a|alpha_a|^2<=Q^(1+o(1)).
For the complete CEN-MZB energy
  E_{>F_0}(alpha)
   =sum_{B<=b<2B;b squarefree}
      |sum_{Q<=a<2Q;(a,b)=1}alpha_aP_b(a)|^2,
separate complete-residue completion modulo each b followed by Cauchy's inequality gives only
  E_{>F_0}(alpha)
   <=4B^2 sum_a|alpha_a|^2
   <<Q^(11/3+o(1)).                                         (6)
The direct right side in (6) exceeds Q^(8/3-omega) by Q^(1+omega+o(1)) for every fixed omega>0. Hence complete-unit tensor orthogonality removes every divisor-count loss but modulus-by-modulus completion of the a-interval still does not supply CEN-MZB.

This is a no-fit for that direct completion upper bound, not a lower bound for the literal energy. It does not permit separating conductors before the b-square, does not estimate the exact unequal-a crossed bracket after its equal-a subtraction, and does not rule out cancellation from incompleteness, the signed conductor/cofactor superposition, the Möbius tri-factor structure of fact b3c1cdc5cb47ae63, or averaging different b before completion. No estimate for C_small or Goldbach is asserted.
1d28c0f84d1aad83.proof:
For p|f define the local centered factor
  r_p(a)=e_p(N[a(b/p)]^(-1))+1/(p-1).
Because (f,N)=1, the coefficient N(b/p)^(-1) is nonzero modulo p. As a ranges over the units modulo p, inversion followed by multiplication by that coefficient permutes the units. Hence
  1/(p-1) sum_{a modulo p;a nonzero}
      e_p(N[a(b/p)]^(-1))
  =-1/(p-1).                                                (7)
Writing c=1/(p-1), equation (7) gives
  1/(p-1)sum_{a modulo p;a nonzero}|r_p(a)|^2
   =1+c^2+2c Re(-c)
   =1-1/(p-1)^2.                                            (8)
It also gives the normalized mean of r_p as zero, as already recorded in fact 14fe68fdcbfd99ff.

For squarefree b, CRT makes the unit group modulo b the product of its local unit groups. If f_1 is not equal to f_2, choose p dividing exactly one of them. At p the local inner product in (2) contains the mean of r_p or its conjugate, hence is zero. If f_1=f_2=f, the local inner product is (8) for p|f and one for p|b/f. Multiplying the local factors proves (2).

Insert (3) into its complete unit squared norm and expand. Equation (2) kills every pair f_1 not equal to f_2 and gives the equality in (4). All remaining terms are nonnegative. It remains to prove (5), after which deleting the terms with f<=F_0 proves the inequality in (4).

The sum in (5) factors prime by prime because b is squarefree. Let p|b. If p does not divide N, there are two choices. When p|f, the local factor is
  1-1/(p-1)^2.
When p|b/f, squarefreeness and p not dividing N give c_p(N)=-1, so the squared cofactor factor is
  |c_p(N)/phi(p)|^2=1/(p-1)^2.
Their sum is one. If p|N, the condition (f,N)=1 forces p|b/f, and c_p(N)=phi(p)=p-1, so the only local squared cofactor factor is one. Thus every prime dividing b contributes one, proving (5).

Now fix b in [B,2B). Since b>Q and the interval [Q,2Q) contains fewer than b integers, its supported unit residues are distinct modulo b. Therefore the nonnegative interval sum is bounded by the complete unit sum:
 sum_{Q<=a<2Q;(a,b)=1}|P_b(a)|^2
 <=sum_{a modulo b;(a,b)=1}|P_b(a)|^2
 <=phi(b)                                                     (9)
by (4). Cauchy's inequality and (9) give
 |sum_{Q<=a<2Q;(a,b)=1}alpha_aP_b(a)|^2
 <=(sum_a|alpha_a|^2)phi(b).                                 (10)
There are fewer than 2B integers b in [B,2B), and phi(b)<=b<2B. Summing (10) gives
 E_{>F_0}(alpha)
 <=(sum_a|alpha_a|^2)sum_{B<=b<2B}phi(b)
 <=4B^2 sum_a|alpha_a|^2,
which is (6). Finally B=Q^(4/3+o(1)) and the assumed coefficient energy give Q^(11/3+o(1)). The exponent difference from 8/3-omega is 1+omega. Because the proof completed each b-row before using any cross-b or incomplete-sum structure, it establishes exactly the scoped no-fit and none of the excluded conclusions.

glossary.P_b(a): The complete signed high-conductor centered projector row, equal to Pi_{b,>F_0}(a).
glossary.nu(f): The normalized complete-unit squared norm of R_{b,f}.

1dc19800a1e52b3c.title: LITERAL GENERIC-WINDOW EMBEDDING INTO ONE SHARED-LIFT CORE, WITH THE EVEN LIFT HYPOTHESIS
1dc19800a1e52b3c.author: slava chan
1dc19800a1e52b3c.statement:
LITERAL GENERIC-WINDOW EMBEDDING INTO ONE SHARED-LIFT CORE, WITH THE EVEN LIFT HYPOTHESIS.

Fix real constants L>=1 and A>=1. Let m>4L+1 be odd, let H>=2 satisfy H<=m^A, let r_2,r_3 be distinct primes in [H^2,2H^2), and let C,K be integers with C nonzero and
 gcd(m,2Kr_2r_3)=1.                                                 (1)
Let 1<=X_box<=Lm. Fix s in {1,-1}. Put q=m^2 and define
 I_a=I_c=I_1=I_2=[1,X_box] intersect Z.                             (2)

For integers a in I_a, c in I_c, n_1 in I_1, n_2 in I_2 put
 b=n_2, d=-n_1.                                                     (3)
When the following quotients are integers, put
 lambda_A=(b r_3-d r_2)/(2m),
 lambda_B=(a r_2-c r_3)/(2m),
 lambda_J=(ab-cd)/(4m).                                             (4)
Let E_lit_even be the tuples
 (a,c,n_1,n_2,u,k) in I_a times I_c times I_1 times I_2 times {0,...,m-1} times Z
satisfying all of the following:
 a,c,n_1,n_2 are even;                                              (5)
 a n_2=K+2smu+kq,
 c n_1=a n_2-2K;                                                    (6)
 the three quotients in (4) are integers;
 lambda_A and lambda_B have common sign s and
 gcd(|lambda_A|,|lambda_B|)=1;                                     (7)
 r_1=|lambda_A| and r_4=|lambda_B| are primes in [H^2,2H^2), and
 r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4 are pairwise distinct;                             (8)
 gcd(C,r_1r_2r_3r_4)=1, lambda_J is nonzero, and
 d r_2 lambda_B-c r_3 lambda_A=2sC;                                (9)
 lambda_J is congruent to su modulo m and
 k=2(lambda_J-su)/m.                                               (10)
The integer in (10) is the same k as in (6), and
 -c n_1=K-2smu-kq.                                                 (11)

Let F be supported on I_a, let W be a centered complex function modulo m, let alpha,beta be supported on I_1,I_2, and let Gamma_extra be any complex function on E_lit_even with |Gamma_extra|<=1 and independent of all Fourier characters. Define
 T_lit_even=sum_{E_lit_even}F(a)W(u)alpha(n_1)beta(n_2)
                  Gamma_extra(a,c,n_1,n_2,u,k),                    (12)
and
 V_F=||F||_infinity+sum_{z in Z}|F(z+1)-F(z)|.                      (13)
Then, for every epsilon>0,
 |T_lit_even|
 <=C_{A,L,epsilon}m^(15/16+epsilon)
 V_F||W||_2||alpha||_2||beta||_2.                                 (14)

Under the identification (3), E_lit_even is exactly the fixed-sign, fixed-(m,r_2,r_3,C,K), positive-box portion of the normalized generic unit states characterized in fact 17557ebe80636618, together with the displayed canonical shared-lift coordinates u,k. Thus Gamma_extra may contain any further zero-one moving window or source mask that is explicitly a function of the displayed tuple and independent of Fourier characters.

Both recovered-prime lines are retained inside E_lit_even. Therefore their possible partial-matching length of order H creates no separate H projective factor in (14). Such a factor occurs only if one chooses to decompose a recovered-prime incidence into one-variable atoms before applying (14). If each tuple is weighted by the four von Mangoldt prime weights, (14) remains valid with an explicit factor (log(2H))^4, which is absorbed into m^epsilon because H<=m^A.

The theorem fixes m,s,r_2,r_3,C,K. It does not pay their outer aggregation, does not improve ||W||_2, and does not cover even m, failure of (1), a different sign convention, or non-generic conductor layers.
1dc19800a1e52b3c.proof:
First verify every hypothesis needed for the literal normalization chart. For a tuple in E_lit_even, all four integers a,b,c,d are even by (3) and (5). Equations (3) and (6) give
 ab=K+2smu+km^2,  cd=-c n_1=2K-ab,
so
 ab+cd=2K                                                        (15)
and ab is congruent to K modulo m. Hence gcd(ab,m)=1 by (1), so a and b are units modulo m. Equation (15) gives cd congruent to K modulo m, so c and d are also units modulo m.

The integrality of lambda_A and lambda_B gives the two torus congruences
 b r_3 is congruent to d r_2 modulo m,
 a r_2 is congruent to c r_3 modulo m.                            (16)
Put t congruent to a r_2 modulo m. This is a unit. From (16) and ab congruent to K modulo m one obtains
 a congruent to t r_2^(-1),
 c congruent to t r_3^(-1),
 b congruent to K r_2 t^(-1),
 d congruent to K r_3 t^(-1)                                    (17)
modulo m. These are exactly the generic torus residues used in fact 17557ebe80636618. Since a,b,c,d are even, that fact supplies their unique lifts from the canonical even representatives; equation (15) is precisely its affine lift hypersurface.

The three quantities in (4) are exactly the carries of fact 17557ebe80636618. Conditions (7)-(9) are word for word its normalized-state conditions (a)-(e), with the common sign fixed to s. Therefore that fact proves the claimed exact equivalence with the normalized generic unit states and gives the recovered short coordinate s lambda_J.

It remains to verify the shared k-coordinate. From (15),
 4m lambda_J=ab-cd=2ab-2K.
Using the first equation of (6),
 lambda_J=(ab-K)/(2m)=su+km/2.                                  (18)
Thus (10) is equivalent to the same k occurring in (6), and subtracting 2K from that equation proves (11). Notice also that (10), when imposed, forces k to be even because m is odd; no division ambiguity remains.

We now prove (14). Every admitted n_2=b and n_1=-d is a unit modulo m, hence modulo q=m^2 is not automatic from unitness modulo m alone; but gcd(n_i,m)=1 implies gcd(n_i,m^2)=1, so gcd(n_1n_2,q)=1. The four ambient intervals have cardinality at most Lm and the column intervals are positive. Furthermore
 1<=|a n_2-2K|=c n_1<=X_box^2<=L^2m^2<=q^2,                     (19)
where the last inequality follows from m>4L+1. Thus E_lit_even, with Gamma_extra and the zero-one indicators of (5), (7)-(10), is an admissible incidence set and bounded gate in fact b40e31c2127d327d with its exponent B=2. That fact gives
 ||C_lift_hat||_2
 <=C_{L,epsilon}q^(1/2+epsilon)
 ||W||_2||alpha||_2||beta||_2.                                  (20)
All literal prime, distinctness, carrier, parity, and shared-lift conditions remain inside the single bounded gate; none is expanded into one-variable atoms.

Apply fact 5b9e0311f7e49ea2 to the exact one-column transform furnished by b40e31c2127d327d. It gives
 |T_lit_even|<=C_epsilon q^(-1/32+epsilon)
 V_F||C_lift_hat||_2.                                             (21)
Combining (20)-(21) and q=m^2 yields (14), after changing epsilon.

The estimate depends only on the modulus-scale intervals and the absolute bound one for the combined gate. It therefore has no factor measuring the number of possible recovered primes. Multiplying by the four von Mangoldt weights costs at most (log(2H))^4 pointwise. Since H<=m^A, this is O_{A,epsilon}(m^epsilon). The final scope limitations follow because none of the cited estimates sums the fixed outer parameters or improves the three displayed coefficient norms.

glossary.E_lit_even: the literal fixed-parameter generic sign-sector shared-lift incidence set with all four coefficient variables even
glossary.Gamma_extra: an additional bounded tuple selector independent of Fourier characters

1de7f7c45ccfee10.title: Fix real numbers \(1/2<a<b<1\). Let \(W\) be a nonzero nonnegative continuously differentiable real function supported in \([a,b]\), let \(\psi\) be continuously differentiable with \(0\leq\psi\leq1\), \(\psi(u)=0\) for \(0<u\leq1\), and \(\psi(u)=1\) for \(u\geq2\), and choose the nonnegative smooth dyadic partition \(\Phi\) of fact 3ef233e014331fc3
1de7f7c45ccfee10.author: slava chan
1de7f7c45ccfee10.statement:
Fix real numbers \(1/2<a<b<1\). Let \(W\) be a nonzero nonnegative continuously differentiable real function supported in \([a,b]\), let \(\psi\) be continuously differentiable with \(0\leq\psi\leq1\), \(\psi(u)=0\) for \(0<u\leq1\), and \(\psi(u)=1\) for \(u\geq2\), and choose the nonnegative smooth dyadic partition \(\Phi\) of fact 3ef233e014331fc3.

Apply the maximal Bombieri--Vinogradov fact 052064336e86e65c with large parameter \(X=2x\), target exponent \(A_{\rm init}=8\), and variation exponent \(C_{\rm var}=5\). Denote its fixed exponent by \(B_{\rm init}\) and put
\[
 Q_{\rm init}=(2x)^{1/2}(\log(2x))^{-B_{\rm init}}.
\]
Apply the cofinal-cutoff fact 5084a731a9f78a09 with requested source accuracy \(L=8\) and prescribed floor \(B_{\rm floor}=B_{\rm init}+1\). Let \(B_{\rm src}>B_{\rm init}+1\) be the resulting single fixed exponent, and put
\[
 D_*=x^{1/2}(\log x)^{-B_{\rm src}}.
\]
Let \(x\) tend to infinity through values for which \(N=2x\) is an even integer not representable as a sum of two primes.

For positive dyadic \(D,M,U\), define
\[
 F_d(t)=\log\!\left({N-t\over d}\right)W\!\left({N-t\over x}\right)
 \Phi\!\left({N-t\over dM}\right)\Phi(t/U),
\]
with value zero off the region \(N-t>0\), and define
\[
 \Delta_d^F(N)=
 \sum_{\substack{p<N\\p\ {\rm prime}\\p\equiv N\ ({\rm mod}\ d)}}\log p\,F_d(p)
 -{1\over\phi(d)}\sum_{\substack{p<N\\p\ {\rm prime}}}\log p\,F_d(p).
\]
Then every sufficiently large such bad \(N\) has one and the same dyadic triple \((D,M,U)\) for which
\[
 {\cal E}_N(D,M;U):=
 \sum_{\substack{d\ge2\\(d,N)=1}}\mu(d)\psi(d/D_*)\Phi(d/D)\Delta_d^F(N)
 \leq-c_{\rm dir}{\mathfrak c(N)x\over\log x},                         \tag{1}
\]
where
\[
 c_{\rm dir}={c_W\over12L_{DM}L_U}>0,\qquad
 c_W=2\int_0^\infty W(u)\,du,
\]
and \(L_{DM},L_U\) are the fixed block-count constants in fact 5084a731a9f78a09. The same block satisfies
\[
 2D>Q_{\rm init}.                                                       \tag{2}
\]
Thus (1) is a same-\(N\), negative, genuine-prime fixed-residue discrepancy block of magnitude at least a fixed positive multiple of \(\mathfrak c(N)x/\log x\), and its modulus label lies beyond the complete classical initial range. The exponent \(B_{\rm src}>B_{\rm init}\) is the same fixed exponent in the bad-\(N\) source, in the block, and in (1); it is chosen only after the initial BV accuracy and its exponent \(B_{\rm init}\) have been fixed.
1de7f7c45ccfee10.proof:
Write
\[
 \lambda_D(d)=\mu(d)\psi(d/D_*)\Phi(d/D).
\]
Fact 5084a731a9f78a09, invoked in the quantifier order stated above, gives for every sufficiently large bad \(N\) a genuine-prime block
\[
 P_N(D,M;U)=
 \sum_{\substack{dm+p=N\\p\ {\rm prime}}}
 \mu(d)\log m\log p\,W(dm/x)\psi(d/D_*)
 \Phi(d/D)\Phi(m/M)\Phi(p/U)
\]
such that
\[
 P_N(D,M;U)\leq-{c_W\mathfrak c(N)x\over2J_xL_{DM}L_U},\qquad
 J_x=\lceil\log_2x\rceil+4.                                             \tag{3}
\]
All its incidences have \(d\ge2\), \(p>x>d\), and \((d,N)=1\). In particular, the selected block is nonempty, and \(\psi(d/D_*)\Phi(d/D)\ne0\) implies \(d>D_*\) and \(d\le2D\), hence
\[
 D>D_*/2.                                                              \tag{4}
\]
For sufficiently large \(x\), \(J_x\le3\log x\), so (3) gives
\[
 P_N(D,M;U)\leq-{c_W\over6L_{DM}L_U}{\mathfrak c(N)x\over\log x}.        \tag{5}
\]

We first prove that this very block cannot lie in the classical initial range. Suppose for contradiction that \(2D\le Q_{\rm init}\). Replace the prime \(p\) in \(P_N(D,M;U)\) by a von Mangoldt variable and put
\[
 {\cal R}_N(D,M;U)=
 \sum_{d\ge1}\lambda_D(d)
 \sum_{\substack{2\le n\le2x\\n\equiv N\ ({\rm mod}\ d)}}\Lambda(n)F_d(n).
                                                                            \tag{6}
\]
The support of \(\Phi(d/D)\) makes \(d\le2D\le Q_{\rm init}\).

Here is the required \(C^1\) check. On the support of \(F_d\), one has
\(ax\le N-t\le bx\), \(dM\asymp x\), and \(U\asymp x\), with implied constants depending only on \(a,b\) and the fixed supports. Consequently
\[
 2\sup_{2\le t\le2x}|F_d(t)|+
 \int_2^{2x}|F_d'(t)|\,dt
 \ll_{W,\Phi}\log x\le(\log(2x))^5                                    \tag{7}
\]
for sufficiently large \(x\). Indeed, the logarithm is \(O(\log x)\); differentiating it costs \(O(x^{-1})\), differentiating \(W((N-t)/x)\) costs \(O(x^{-1})\), differentiating \(\Phi(t/U)\) costs \(O(U^{-1})\), and differentiating \(\Phi((N-t)/(dM))\) costs \(O((dM)^{-1})\). Each derivative is integrated over an interval of its natural support length, leaving \(O(\log x)\). The zero extension is continuously differentiable because the fixed compactly supported \(C^1\) factors vanish with their first derivatives at the support boundary.

Apply fact 052064336e86e65c at the large parameter \(2x\), using the reduced residue \(N\bmod d\) on \((d,N)=1\), the bounded coefficient \(\lambda_D(d)\), (7), and target exponent \(8\). This gives
\[
 \sum_{\substack{d\ge1\\(d,N)=1}}\lambda_D(d)
 \sum_{n\equiv N\ ({\rm mod}\ d)}\Lambda(n)F_d(n)
 =
 \sum_{\substack{d\ge1\\(d,N)=1}}{\lambda_D(d)\over\phi(d)}
 \int_2^{2x}F_d(t)\,dt+O(x(\log x)^{-8}).                              \tag{8}
\]

For completeness, the noncoprime tax omitted from (8) is negligible by the exact mechanism of fact f6871c593f8f6f35, with the harmless resizing forced by the present prime interval. If \(\mu(d)\ne0\), \((d,N)>1\), \(\Lambda(n)\ne0\), and \(n\equiv N\pmod d\), write \(n=q^j\). A prime divisor of \((d,N)\) must equal \(q\), hence \(q\mid N\), and \(d\mid N-q^j\). The support of \(W((N-n)/x)\) gives \(ax\le N-q^j\le bx\), so this difference is nonzero. There are \(O(\log N)\) possible prime divisors \(q\mid N\), \(O(\log x)\) exponents, and \(O_\varepsilon(x^\varepsilon)\) possible squarefree divisors \(d\) of each difference, by the self-contained divisor estimate in f6871c593f8f6f35. Since \(\Lambda(n)F_d(n)\ll(\log x)^2\),
\[
 {\cal R}_{N,\mathrm{nc}}\ll_{\varepsilon,W,\Phi}x^\varepsilon(\log x)^4
 =o(x(\log x)^{-8}).                                                    \tag{9}
\]

The density main in (8) is also negligible. Exchange \(t\) and \(d\). For fixed \(t\), after putting \(d=Ds\), its \(d\)-profile is
\[
 G_t(s)=\psi(Ds/D_*)\Phi(s)\log((N-t)/(Ds))
 W((N-t)/x)\Phi((N-t)/(DMs)).
\]
The family \((\log(2x))^{-1}G_t\) has uniformly bounded supremum and total variation. The only extra derivative is that of \(\psi(Ds/D_*)\); when it is nonzero, \(1\le Ds/D_*\le2\), so \(D/D_*\) is bounded on that support after multiplication by the compact \(s\)-range. The last \(\Phi\)-argument is likewise bounded on its derivative support. Now (4) permits the inverse-zeta estimate in the first assertion of fact 415fa7afad9006c5 with \(B=B_{\rm src}\). Taking logarithmic exponent \(10\) and integrating over \(2\le t\le2x\) yields
\[
 \sum_{\substack{d\ge1\\(d,N)=1}}{\lambda_D(d)\over\phi(d)}
 \int_2^{2x}F_d(t)\,dt
 \ll x(\log x)^{-9}.                                                     \tag{10}
\]
Equations (8)--(10) give \({\cal R}_N(D,M;U)\ll x(\log x)^{-8}\).

Returning from \(\Lambda(n)\) to genuine primes costs only higher prime powers. For \(n=q^j\), \(j\ge2\), the equation \(dm=N-n\) gives at most \(\tau(N-n)\ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon\) pairs, and there are \(O_\varepsilon(x^{1/2+\varepsilon})\) such powers up to \(2x\). Including the logarithmic weights,
\[
 {\cal R}_N(D,M;U)-P_N(D,M;U)
 \ll_{\varepsilon,W,\psi,\Phi}x^{1/2+2\varepsilon}(\log x)^2
 =o(x(\log x)^{-8})                                                     \tag{11}
\]
on choosing a fixed sufficiently small \(\varepsilon>0\). Hence \(P_N(D,M;U)\ll x(\log x)^{-8}\), contradicting (5) because \(\mathfrak c(N)\ge C_2>0\) by fact f41f5f91b52e0d13. This proves (2), for the same selected block and the same \(N\).

It remains to transfer negativity to the discrepancy rather than merely to the prime sum. Define the unrestricted-prime comparison
\[
 {\cal M}_N(D,M;U)=
 \sum_{\substack{d\ge1\\(d,N)=1}}{\lambda_D(d)\over\phi(d)}
 \sum_{\substack{p<N\\p\ {\rm prime}}}\log p\,F_d(p).
\]
Adding and subtracting this expression gives the exact identity
\[
 P_N(D,M;U)={\cal M}_N(D,M;U)+{\cal E}_N(D,M;U).                         \tag{12}
\]
There is no \(d=1\) discrepancy: \(D_*>1\) for large \(x\), so \(\psi(1/D_*)=0\).

Exchange the \(p\)- and \(d\)-sums in \({\cal M}_N\). For each fixed \(p\), the normalized \(d\)-profile is exactly of the bounded-\(C^1\) type checked above and in fact 415fa7afad9006c5. By (4), its inverse-zeta estimate applies for the fixed exponent \(B_{\rm src}\), with arbitrary logarithmic saving. The elementary Chebyshev bound \(\sum_{p\le2x}\log p\ll x\), reproduced in fact 415fa7afad9006c5, therefore gives
\[
 {\cal M}_N(D,M;U)\ll_{W,\psi,\Phi}x(\log x)^{-4}.                       \tag{13}
\]
Since \(\mathfrak c(N)\ge C_2>0\), (13) is at most
\[
 {c_W\over12L_{DM}L_U}{\mathfrak c(N)x\over\log x}
\]
for sufficiently large \(x\). Combining this with (5) and (12) proves (1), with
\(c_{\rm dir}=c_W/(12L_{DM}L_U)\). Every choice—first the BV accuracy and \(B_{\rm init}\), then \(B_{\rm src}>B_{\rm init}\), then the same-\(N\) block—is made in the displayed order, so neither (1) nor (2) uses the invalid inference that an existential source exponent may be enlarged.

glossary.A_init: the logarithmic accuracy requested from maximal Bombieri--Vinogradov before choosing the source cutoff
glossary.B_init: the fixed exponent defining the complete classical initial modulus range
glossary.C_var: the exponent allowed in the C1 norm of the prime-variable profiles
glossary.Delta_d^F(N): the F_d-weighted prime progression discrepancy at residue N modulo d
glossary.F_d: the prime-variable test profile of the selected genuine-prime block
glossary.c_dir: the fixed positive constant c_W/(12 L_DM L_U)

1e2d635f6691e832.title: Fix real numbers 1/2<a<b<1 and 0<sigma<1/100. Choose W, psi and Phi to be infinitely differentiable functions satisfying all hypotheses of fact 1de7f7c45ccfee10, with Phi the nonnegative partition supplied by fact 3ef233e014331fc3. Use the quantifier order and the single fixed source exponent B_src of fact 1de7f7c45ccfee10. Thus, for every sufficiently large even integer N=2x which is not a sum of two primes, there is a positive dyadic triple (D,M,U) for which the genuine-prime block P_N(D,M;U) of that fact satisfies
1e2d635f6691e832.author: slava chan
1e2d635f6691e832.statement:
Fix real numbers 1/2<a<b<1 and 0<sigma<1/100. Choose W, psi and Phi to be infinitely differentiable functions satisfying all hypotheses of fact 1de7f7c45ccfee10, with Phi the nonnegative partition supplied by fact 3ef233e014331fc3. Use the quantifier order and the single fixed source exponent B_src of fact 1de7f7c45ccfee10. Thus, for every sufficiently large even integer N=2x which is not a sum of two primes, there is a positive dyadic triple (D,M,U) for which the genuine-prime block P_N(D,M;U) of that fact satisfies
P_N(D,M;U) <= -c_dir mathfrak c(N)x/log x
and D>D_*/2, where D_*=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B_src) and c_dir>0 is the fixed constant in that fact.

For this same N,D,M,U define
B_N(D,M;U)
= sum_{d,m,q>=1, dm+q=N} mu(d)log(m)W(dm/x)psi(d/D_*)Lambda(q)
  Phi(d/D)Phi(m/M)Phi(q/U)
and put
PP_N(D,M;U)=B_N(D,M;U)-P_N(D,M;U).
For positive dyadic R,K define
Q_N(D,M;U;R,K)
= sum_{d,m,r,k>=1, dm+rk=N} mu(d)mu(r)log(m)log(k)W(dm/x)psi(d/D_*)
  Phi(d/D)Phi(m/M)Phi(rk/U)Phi(r/R)Phi(k/K).

Call an active label (R,K) controlled, and write (R,K) in cal C_sigma, when at least one of the following three conditions holds:
FT: R/M <= x^(-sigma);
BC-minus: R<=D, D^19 R^14 <= x^(17-sigma), and D^8 R^7 <= x^(8-sigma);
BC-plus: R>D, D^14 R^19 <= x^(17-sigma), and D^7 R^8 <= x^(8-sigma).
Define
C_dir,N=sum_{(R,K) in cal C_sigma} Q_N(D,M;U;R,K)
and
T_res,N=sum_{(R,K) not in cal C_sigma} Q_N(D,M;U;R,K),
where only active dyadic labels are included. Then, for every fixed epsilon>0,
B_N(D,M;U)=P_N(D,M;U)+PP_N(D,M;U),
B_N(D,M;U)=C_dir,N+T_res,N,
and
PP_N(D,M;U)=O_epsilon(x^(1/2+epsilon)).
Consequently,
P_N(D,M;U)=C_dir,N+T_res,N-PP_N(D,M;U).                 (1)

For every residual label use the Poisson decomposition of fact df9748efe29ab475, and let Z_res,N^(0) and R_res,N^(nonzero) be respectively the sums of its zero and nonzero Poisson-frequency pieces. Then
P_N(D,M;U)=C_dir,N+Z_res,N^(0)+R_res,N^(nonzero)-PP_N(D,M;U),           (2)
C_dir,N=o(x/log x), Z_res,N^(0)=o(x/log x), and PP_N(D,M;U)=o(x/log x).
It follows that
R_res,N^(nonzero)
<=-c_dir mathfrak c(N)x/log x+o(mathfrak c(N)x/log x).                  (3)
No bound or saving for R_res,N^(nonzero) is asserted.

There is a precise composite-orbit interpretation in the top logarithmic divisor case. If in addition D<=2x^(1/2), then every nonzero divisor sibling belonging to a q with Lambda(q) nonzero lies in cal C_sigma. Therefore every nonzero incidence contributing to T_res,N, Z_res,N^(0), or R_res,N^(nonzero) has q=rk composite and not a prime power, and its complete fixed-(d,m,q) sibling orbit has total coefficient
sum_{r'k'=q}mu(r')log(k')=0.
Thus the residual is a selected redistribution of composite zero-total sibling orbits, not direct von Mangoldt support. The selected residual sum itself need not be zero. This composite-only assertion is not made when D>2x^(1/2). Independently of all regions, the r=1 sibling equals log q for every integer q>=1; it is not an indicator that q is prime.

Finally put
delta=log(D)/log(x), nu=log(M)/log(x), rho=log(R)/log(x),
and define
theta_sigma^-(delta,nu)
=max(nu-sigma,
     min((17-sigma-19delta)/14,(8-sigma-8delta)/7)),
theta_sigma^+(delta,nu)
=max(nu-sigma,
     min((17-sigma-14delta)/19,(8-sigma-7delta)/8)).
For an active label with R<=D, membership in cal C_sigma is equivalent to
rho<=theta_sigma^-(delta,nu); for an active label with R>D, it is equivalent to
rho<=theta_sigma^+(delta,nu). Hence the residual conditions are the corresponding strict reverse inequalities.

The source support gives nu=1-delta+O(1/log x), and D>D_*/2 gives delta>=1/2-o(1). In this range the exact max-min formulas have the following buffered piecewise form, with an O(1/log x) error arising only from DM being a fixed constant multiple of x:
theta_sigma^-(delta,nu)
= (17-sigma-19delta)/14+O(1/log x)
  when delta<=(3+13sigma)/5,
and
theta_sigma^-(delta,nu)
=1-delta-sigma+O(1/log x)
  when delta>=(3+13sigma)/5;
theta_sigma^+(delta,nu)
=(17-sigma-14delta)/19+O(1/log x)
  when delta<=(16-11sigma)/21,
and
theta_sigma^+(delta,nu)
=(8-sigma-7delta)/8+O(1/log x)
  when delta>=(16-11sigma)/21.
At either transition the two displayed values agree up to O(1/log x). In particular, when delta=1/2+o(1),
theta_sigma^+(delta,nu)=(10-sigma)/19+o(1).
Thus on the R>D side there is an uncontrolled near-diagonal wedge
(10-sigma)/19+o(1)<rho<2/3-o(1)
below the natural forward endpoint boundary rho=2/3+o(1) determined by r=k^2 and rk comparable to x. This is only a rigorous location of the remaining nonzero-frequency residual; no cancellation on the wedge and no identification with any terminal-anatomy mask are asserted.
1e2d635f6691e832.proof:
The exact first identity is a same-block prime versus higher-prime-power split. In B_N the factor Lambda(q) is nonzero exactly when q is a prime power. Its q=p part is precisely P_N because both sums use the same N,D,M,U and every same-block weight is identical. The remaining q=p^j, j>=2 terms form PP_N. This proves B_N=P_N+PP_N.

We bound PP_N without cancellation. For a fixed q=p^j in its support, put n=N-q. The support of W gives ax<=n<=bx. The sum over dm=n of the absolute value of the d,m weight is at most a constant times tau(n)log n, because 0<=Phi<=1, 0<=psi<=1, and W is bounded. Also Lambda(q)<=log(2x). The elementary proof in fact d6fd2c2cf8b5d0f0 gives tau(n)<<_epsilon x^epsilon and shows that the number of prime powers p^j<=2x with j>=2 is O_epsilon(x^(1/2+epsilon)). Shrinking epsilon by a fixed factor before applying those estimates gives
|PP_N(D,M;U)|<<_epsilon x^(1/2+epsilon).
This is uniform in the selected block.

Fact 0880dc648c429047 proves the exact sibling identity after inserting
Lambda(q)=sum_{rk=q}mu(r)log k
and the two dyadic partitions in r and k. Its proof is purely algebraic and applies with the present cofinally chosen fixed B_src. The factor Phi(q/U) becomes Phi(rk/U). Therefore
B_N(D,M;U)=sum_{R,K}Q_N(D,M;U;R,K).
The indicator of cal C_sigma and its complement partition this finite label set, so
B_N=C_dir,N+T_res,N.
Combining with B_N=P_N+PP_N proves (1).

We next justify applying fact df9748efe29ab475 uniformly. Every active source label satisfies DM comparable to x and RK comparable to x, with constants depending only on the fixed supports; this is the same support calculation as in facts d6fd2c2cf8b5d0f0 and 0880dc648c429047. In scaled variables d/D,m/M,r/R,k/K, the factors W(dm/x), Phi(rk/U), and all one-variable dyadic factors form a compactly supported smooth joint weight with uniformly bounded scaled derivatives. The only possible concern is psi(d/D_*). If a derivative of psi is nonzero, then d/D_* lies in its fixed transition interval while d/D lies in [1/2,2], forcing D/D_* into a fixed compact interval. Outside that case psi is constant on the relevant support. Thus this factor also has uniformly bounded scaled derivatives. Hence the general Q_N theorem of df9748efe29ab475 applies to every active label.

Take eta_0=2/5 in that fact. Since
D>D_*/2=(1/2)x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B_src),
one has D>=x^(2/5) for all sufficiently large x. Thus max(D,R)>=x^(eta_0) for every active label, including every residual label. The zero-frequency assertion of df9748efe29ab475 therefore gives an arbitrary logarithmic saving
Q_N^(0)(D,M;U;R,K)<<_A x(log x)^(-A)
for every label.

For a controlled label satisfying FT, consequence (2) of that fact gives the same arbitrary logarithmic saving for the whole Q_N. For a controlled label satisfying BC-minus or BC-plus, consequence (1) gives
Q_N<<_sigma x^(1-3sigma/80)+x(log x)^(-A)
in absolute value. There are O((log x)^2) possible pairs (R,K), because r,k<=2x on every nonzero incidence and each variable has O(log x) possible dyadic labels. Summing the displayed bounds and taking A>5 gives
C_dir,N=o(x/log x).
Applying the zero-frequency bound to the residual labels and summing gives
Z_res,N^(0)=o(x/log x).
By definition T_res,N=Z_res,N^(0)+R_res,N^(nonzero), which proves (2). The prime-power estimate gives PP_N=o(x/log x). Rearranging (2) now gives
R_res,N^(nonzero)=P_N-C_dir,N-Z_res,N^(0)+PP_N.
Insert the certified upper bound for P_N. Fact f41f5f91b52e0d13 gives mathfrak c(N)>=C_2>0, so every o(x/log x) term is also o(mathfrak c(N)x/log x). This proves (3).

Assume now D<=2x^(1/2). Suppose Lambda(q) is nonzero and a sibling mu(r)log k with rk=q is nonzero. Fact b7fcb27a091203e5 proves r<=sqrt(q). Since q=N-dm<N=2x, one has r<sqrt(2x). If Phi(r/R) is nonzero, its support gives R<=2r<2sqrt(2x). Thus D and R are both at most a fixed constant times x^(1/2). If R<=D, then
D^19R^14<<x^(33/2), D^8R^7<<x^(15/2).
Because sigma<1/100<1/2, for sufficiently large x these are respectively at most x^(17-sigma) and x^(8-sigma), so BC-minus holds. If R>D, the same calculation with the exchanged exponents gives
D^14R^19<<x^(33/2), D^7R^8<<x^(15/2),
so BC-plus holds. Hence every live prime-power sibling label is controlled.

It follows that every nonzero residual incidence has Lambda(q)=0. The incidence has k>1 because log k is nonzero, and r>=1, while q lies in a fixed positive-proportion interval comparable to x and hence q>1. Fact b7fcb27a091203e5 then says q is a composite non-prime-power and that its complete sibling sum is zero. All other factors attached to fixed d,m,q before the R,K partition are common to the complete sibling orbit; the residual label indicator merely selects some of its siblings. This proves the stated composite zero-orbit interpretation and also explains why the selected residual need not vanish. The restriction D<=2sqrt(x) was used essentially to force the two BC inequalities and is not removed. Finally, setting r=1 and k=q in the sibling coefficient gives mu(1)log q=log q for every q, including composite q; this proves the r=1 warning.

It remains to verify the geometry. Since x>1, the FT inequality is exactly
rho-nu<=-sigma, or rho<=nu-sigma.
On R<=D, the two BC-minus inequalities are exactly
rho<=(17-sigma-19delta)/14
and
rho<=(8-sigma-8delta)/7.
Their conjunction is the condition that rho is at most their minimum. Taking the union with FT is therefore exactly
rho<=theta_sigma^-(delta,nu).
The R>D calculation is identical and gives theta_sigma^+ with denominators 19 and 8. Complements give the strict reverse inequalities.

The source support gives ax/4<=DM<=4bx by fact d6fd2c2cf8b5d0f0, hence
nu=1-delta+O(1/log x).
Also D>D_*/2 gives
delta>=1/2-B_src log(log x)/log x+O(1/log x)=1/2-o(1).
For such delta, the first BC-minus boundary is the smaller one, because their difference is (1+sigma-3delta)/14<0 for sufficiently large x. Comparing it with 1-delta-sigma gives the crossing
delta=(3+13sigma)/5.
This proves the stated theta-minus pieces, including the O(1/log x) perturbation from nu.

For BC-plus, the two BC boundaries cross when
delta=(16-11sigma)/21.
Below this value the denominator-19 boundary is smaller, and above it the denominator-8 boundary is smaller. Each is greater than 1-delta-sigma throughout delta>=1/2-o(1): the respective differences are
(-2+18sigma+5delta)/19
and
(delta+7sigma)/8,
which are positive for sufficiently large x. This proves the theta-plus pieces. At delta=1/2+o(1), the first plus piece gives
theta_sigma^+=(17-sigma-7)/19+o(1)=(10-sigma)/19+o(1).
Finally active labels have rk comparable to x. The relation r=k^2 together with rk comparable to x gives r comparable to x^(2/3), hence rho=2/3+o(1). Therefore residual plus-orientation labels with rho between the displayed theta-plus boundary and 2/3 form the asserted near-diagonal wedge. No estimate beyond the already separated zero-frequency bound has been used on it, and no terminal-anatomy mask was inserted.

glossary.B_N(D,M;U): the same-block sibling-complete von Mangoldt sum defined in the statement
glossary.C_dir,N: the sum of Q_N over the controlled label union cal C_sigma
glossary.P_N(D,M;U): the forced negative genuine-prime block supplied by fact 1de7f7c45ccfee10
glossary.Q_N(D,M;U;R,K): the refined divisor-sibling block defined in the statement
glossary.R_res,N^(nonzero): the sum of the nonzero Poisson-frequency pieces of the residual labels
glossary.T_res,N: the sum of Q_N over the complementary refined labels
glossary.Z_res,N^(0): the sum of the zero Poisson-frequency pieces of the residual labels
glossary.cal C_sigma: the union of the FT, BC-minus and BC-plus refined label sets
glossary.theta_sigma^+(delta,nu): the exact controlled radial boundary for labels with R greater than D
glossary.theta_sigma^-(delta,nu): the exact controlled radial boundary for labels with R at most D

1e357f0a9f079ca2.title: GA-GOODW-ONECOEFF-NREG: UNIFORM SCALED n-VARIATION OF ONE MASK-FREE GOOD-W FOURIER COEFFICIENT. Adopt fact 18c3a93006507edb and fix one of its complete Good-W outer rows, one integer q with Q<=q<2Q, and one h in a signed frequency block F<=|h|<2F. Exclude the explicit arithmetic gate (q,n)=1 and the terminal incidence. Extend n continuously as n=By on the fixed compact dyadic y-support and define
1e357f0a9f079ca2.author: slava chan
1e357f0a9f079ca2.proof:
We use the literal source formula. In the forward orientation, after outer-gcd normalization, the physical progression variable t has scale M and its complementary variable u=(mathscr A-qt)/n has scale K. The source amplitude is a product of log t, log u, and the fixed scaled-smooth compactly supported W, psi and Phi factors evaluated at q/Q, t/M, n/B and u/K. The reverse orientation interchanges the two divisor-complement pairs and has the identical scaled form. Fact d8ba46800ba433c2 records this literal one-variable amplitude and proves arbitrary Fourier decay on the scale |h|M/n, which is comparable to |h|/H_P, by repeated integration by parts in t.

Set n=By. On the fixed dyadic support, y lies in a compact subset of the positive reals. Differentiating any smooth source factor with respect to y has bounded cost: n/B=y, while
[
 partial_y(u/K)=-{Bmathscr Aover K(By)^2}
                 +{Bqtover K(By)^2}.
]
On physical support qM and nK are both comparable to mathscr A, because the active scales satisfy DM and RK comparable to x and q=D/g, n=R/g in the forward orientation. The reverse orientation gives the same comparison. Hence B times the n-derivative of u/K is bounded. Differentiating log u has a logarithmic-size bound. Thus every fixed number of mixed y- and scaled-t derivatives of the physical amplitude is bounded by a fixed power of log x on a compact scaled support.

Differentiating the Fourier phase e(-epsilon_or h t/(By)) costs at most a constant times |h|M/B, which is bounded by a constant times F/H_P. Differentiating the Archimedean phase costs at most a constant times |h|mathscr A/(qB), also bounded by a constant times F/H_P because mathscr A is comparable to qM and BK, so M/B and K/q are comparable to 1/H_P. Differentiating H_P/(By) costs only a bounded scalar multiple of the same prefactor.

Apply repeated integration by parts in t before and after one y-derivative. With J integrations, the undifferentiated term is bounded by
[
 (log x)^{C_0}(1+F/H_P)^{-J},
]
and the differentiated term by
[
 (log x)^{C_0}(1+F/H_P)(1+F/H_P)^{-J}.
]
Choose J>A+2. Since the y-support has bounded length, the supremum and derivative integral satisfy (2).

Fact 18c3a93006507edb proves that auxiliary source, deletion and provenance selectors disappear on the complete sibling union, while coprimality and terminal incidence remain explicit. Hence no unlisted sharp factor is hidden in (1). The proof is termwise in the fixed pair (q,h), and no summation over a primitive ray is taken.

glossary.C_{q,h}(y): The continuously interpolated mask-free Good-W Fourier coefficient for one fixed pair (q,h), with n=By.
glossary.cal V_y: The supremum plus continuous total-variation norm on the fixed compact y-support.

1ea36d543252d94d.title: P-qSRC-OSF-SLOPE: EXACT REDUCED-SLOPE REASSEMBLY OF THE OUTER-SIGN-FREE SOURCE, COMPLETE U_lambda WEIGHTS, AND THE COPRIMALITY/HARD-DELETION NO-FIT
1ea36d543252d94d.author: slava chan
1ea36d543252d94d.statement:
P-qSRC-OSF-SLOPE: EXACT REDUCED-SLOPE REASSEMBLY OF THE OUTER-SIGN-FREE SOURCE, COMPLETE U_lambda WEIGHTS, AND THE COPRIMALITY/HARD-DELETION NO-FIT.

Adopt P-qSRC-DUALMU from fact 7a9257c915a47f6b in the range Dcal>Q^2. Put T=mathscr A and L=(log(2x))^C, and assume L>1. For one exact retained pair
R=(epsilon,a,b), R'=(epsilon',a',b'),
write
g=gcd(a,a'), alpha=a/g, beta=a'/g,
L_0=epsilon b beta-epsilon'b'alpha.                                (1)
For every squarefree g put
c_g=gcd(g,T), r_g=g/c_g, T_g=T/c_g.                                (2)
For a supported ray R with g|a and alpha_g(R)=a/g coprime to T, define the reduced slope
x_g(R)=epsilon b alpha_g(R)^{-1} (mod r_g),                         (3)
with the unique residue class used when r_g=1, and define the complete normalized ray weight
W_{lambda,g}(R)
 =A^0_lambda(R)U_lambda(R)/phi(alpha_g(R)).                         (4)
Here U_lambda(R) is exactly the complete signed scaling Möbius transform of facts a36284a9dbec7837 and 7a9257c915a47f6b, with every Fourier, source, deletion, and provenance factor retained.

For a pair whose exact common divisor is g, the outer-sign-free condition m_P=1 is equivalent to
gcd(alpha beta,T)=1,
x_g(R)=x_g(R').                                                     (5)
On this class m_q=alpha beta and
1/phi(m_q)=1/[phi(alpha)phi(beta)].                                 (6)

There is also an exact hard-deletion quotient. If the slopes in (5) are equal, put
ell_g(R,R')=L_0/r_g.                                                (7)
Let
rho_lambda=d_lambda/gcd(d_lambda,T).                               (8)
Then
Delta_0=gL_0=g r_g ell_g(R,R'),
m_d=rho_lambda/gcd(rho_lambda,g r_g ell_g(R,R')).                  (9)
Moreover
d_lambda divides T Delta_0 if and only if m_d=1.                    (10)
Thus on L>1 the condition m_d>L already implies both R!=R' and the nonresonance deletion d_lambda not dividing T Delta_0.

Let Theta_lambda(R,R') be the product of every remaining literal retained-pair selector in P-qSRC-DUALMU after the displayed conditions are separated. The complete m_P=1 restriction of P-qSRC is exactly
P-qSRC_{m_P=1}
 =sum_lambda sum_g
  sum_{R,R'}
   1_{gcd(a,a')=g}
   1_{gcd(alpha beta,T)=1}
   1_{x_g(R)=x_g(R')}
   1_{m_d>L}
   Theta_lambda(R,R')
   W_{lambda,g}(R)conjugate(W_{lambda,g}(R')).                     (OSF-SLOPE)
All rays in this formula are exact supported rays, alpha=a/g and beta=a'/g, and no U_lambda transform or selector is replaced.

The equal-slope arithmetic parent before the hard pair deletion has an exact signed-Gram expansion. Let R_{lambda,g} be the finite set of exact supported rays R with g|a and gcd(alpha_g(R),T)=1, and define
Q_{lambda,g}^{par}
 =sum_{R,R' in R_{lambda,g}}
   1_{gcd(alpha_g(R),alpha_g(R'))=1}
   1_{x_g(R)=x_g(R')}
   W_{lambda,g}(R)conjugate(W_{lambda,g}(R')).                     (11)
Then
Q_{lambda,g}^{par}
 =sum_{h>=1}mu(h) sum_{z (mod r_g)}
  |sum_{R in R_{lambda,g}, h|alpha_g(R), x_g(R)=z}
    W_{lambda,g}(R)|^2.                                            (12)
Every sum is finite.

Equation (12) is a signed sum of positive slope-class norms, not a positive Gram. The coprimality kernel itself can be indefinite: with two abstract same-slope rows whose reduced denominators are 1 and a prime q, its matrix is
