[[1,1],[1,0]],
which has a negative eigenvalue. The actual form OSF-SLOPE has in addition the quotient deletion m_d>L and Theta_lambda. Therefore neither the positive outer coefficient in fact 7a9257c915a47f6b nor equal reduced slopes permits positivity or a generic row-norm domination. This is a formal method no-fit; it does not assert that the two-row abstract profile occurs in the literal source.

This theorem proves the exact outer-sign-free reduced-slope and complete-source reassembly only. It proves no estimate for OSF-SLOPE, no P-qSRC-SUP, no C-qSRC-SUP, no tail payment, and no Goldbach conclusion.
1ea36d543252d94d.proof:
Fact 7a9257c915a47f6b proves that g,alpha,beta are pairwise coprime and squarefree and that
m_P=1 if and only if g|T L_0 and gcd(alpha beta,T)=1.               (13)
Write g=c_g r_g and T=c_g T_g. The definition c_g=gcd(g,T) gives
gcd(r_g,T_g)=1.
Hence
g|T L_0
 if and only if c_g r_g|c_g T_g L_0
 if and only if r_g|L_0.                                           (14)
Because alpha and beta are coprime to g, they are units modulo r_g. Multiplying the congruence L_0=0 modulo r_g by (alpha beta)^{-1} gives
epsilon b alpha^{-1}
 =epsilon'b' beta^{-1} (mod r_g).                                  (15)
The two sides are precisely x_g(R) and x_g(R'), proving (5).

On m_P=1, fact 7a9257c915a47f6b gives m_q=alpha beta. Since alpha and beta are coprime,
phi(alpha beta)=phi(alpha)phi(beta),
which proves (6). Substituting the complete weights (4) in the m_P=1 restriction of P-qSRC-DUALMU therefore produces the factorized product
W_{lambda,g}(R)conjugate(W_{lambda,g}(R')).
No term inside U_lambda is altered.

Under equal slopes, equation (14) makes ell_g in (7) an integer and
Delta_0=gL_0=g r_g ell_g.                                         (16)
Fact cff9d29efb555b8e defines
m_d=
 [d_lambda/gcd(d_lambda,T)]/
 gcd(d_lambda/gcd(d_lambda,T),Delta_0).
Insert (8) and (16) to obtain (9).

We prove (10). Write h=gcd(d_lambda,T),
d_lambda=h rho_lambda, T=h T_1.
Then gcd(rho_lambda,T_1)=1. Therefore
d_lambda|T Delta_0
 if and only if h rho_lambda|h T_1 Delta_0
 if and only if rho_lambda|Delta_0
 if and only if m_d=1.                                             (17)
If R=R', then Delta_0=0, so (9) gives m_d=1. Since L>1, m_d>L excludes both this case and, by (17), every resonant pair. This proves the hard-deletion assertions.

Now restrict P-qSRC-DUALMU termwise to m_P=1. Use the exact common divisor g, equivalence (5), factorization (6), the complete weights (4), and the hard quotient (9). Place all other inherited pair predicates in Theta_lambda without changing them. This gives OSF-SLOPE exactly.

For the parent identity, use the elementary coprimality formula
1_{gcd(alpha,beta)=1}
 =sum_{h|alpha,h|beta}mu(h).                                       (18)
Insert (18) in (11) and interchange the finite sums. For fixed h and fixed slope z, the remaining double sum factors as
[sum_{R: h|alpha_g(R), x_g(R)=z}W_{lambda,g}(R)]
conjugate(
 [sum_{R': h|alpha_g(R'), x_g(R')=z}W_{lambda,g}(R')]).
This is the squared modulus in (12). Summing over h and z proves the signed-Gram expansion.

Finally, for reduced denominators 1 and q, the pairwise coprimality values are
gcd(1,1)=1, gcd(1,q)=gcd(q,1)=1, gcd(q,q)=q>1,
which gives the displayed matrix. Its determinant is -1, so it has one negative eigenvalue. This proves the scoped nonpositivity no-fit. No estimate for the actual complete weights or the hard deleted form has been made, proving every stated exclusion.

glossary.Q_{lambda,g}^{par}: The undeleted equal-slope arithmetic parent of the outer-sign-free source.
glossary.W_{lambda,g}(R): The complete U_lambda ray weight divided by phi(a/g).
glossary.c_g: The greatest common divisor of the exact common ray denominator g and the target T.
glossary.ell_g(R,R'): The integer quotient L_0/r_g on an equal reduced-slope pair.
glossary.x_g(R): The reduced projective slope epsilon b alpha^{-1} modulo r_g for alpha=a/g.

1f5316e61daf156d.title: Fix real numbers \(1/2<\alpha<\beta<1\), \(\eta>0\), and \(\rho\ge0\). Let \(W\) be a bounded real function supported in \([\alpha,\beta]\), and let \(\Phi\) be a bounded real function supported in \([1/2,2]\). Let \(x\ge3\), \(N=2x\) be an integer, and let \(D,U>0\) satisfy
1f5316e61daf156d.author: slava chan
1f5316e61daf156d.statement:
Fix real numbers \(1/2<\alpha<\beta<1\), \(\eta>0\), and \(\rho\ge0\). Let \(W\) be a bounded real function supported in \([\alpha,\beta]\), and let \(\Phi\) be a bounded real function supported in \([1/2,2]\). Let \(x\ge3\), \(N=2x\) be an integer, and let \(D,U>0\) satisfy
\[
 D\le2x^{1/2},\qquad D>2T_x,\qquad
 T_x=(\log x)^{6+\eta+\rho}.
\]
Define
\[
 {\cal I}_D=\{d\ge2:(d,N)=1,\ \mu(d)\ne0,\ d\le x^{1/2},\
                    \Phi(d/D)\ne0\},
\]
and extend \(\Lambda\) by zero on nonpositive integers. Define the full-von-Mangoldt hard covariance
\[
\begin{split}
 {\mathfrak C}_\star^\Lambda
 =\sum_{\substack{d_1,d_2\in{\cal I}_D\\
                  |d_1-d_2|>D/T_x\\(d_1,d_2)<T_x}}
 &\mu(d_1)\mu(d_2)\Phi(d_1/D)\Phi(d_2/D)\\
 &\times\sum_{m\ge1}
 W(d_1m/x)W(d_2m/x)
 \Phi((N-d_1m)/U)\Phi((N-d_2m)/U)\\
 &\times\Lambda(N-d_1m)\Lambda(N-d_2m).                  \tag{1}
\end{split}
\]
For positive integers \(g,G,u\), define
\[
 B_{g,G}(u)=
 {\bf1}_{\substack{g<T_x,\ g\mid G,\ gu\in{\cal I}_D}}
 \mu(u)\Phi(gu/D)W(uG/x)\Phi((N-uG)/U)\Lambda(N-uG),      \tag{2}
\]
and
\[
 S_{g,G,r}=\sum_{\substack{u\ge1\\r\mid u}}B_{g,G}(u).    \tag{3}
\]
Put
\[
 {\cal E}_{<}=
 \sum_{1\le g<T_x}\ \sum_{\substack{G\ge1\\g\mid G}}\
 \sum_{1\le r<T_x}\mu(r)|S_{g,G,r}|^2.                   \tag{4}
\]
Then
\[
 {\mathfrak C}_\star^\Lambda
 ={\cal E}_{<}
 +O_{W,\Phi,\alpha,\beta}\!\left({xD(\log x)^2\over T_x}\right).
                                                                    \tag{5}
\]
More precisely, define
\[
 {\cal P}_\Delta^\Lambda=
 \sum_{1\le g<T_x}\sum_{\substack{G\ge1\\g\mid G}}
 \sum_{\substack{u,u'\ge1\\(u,u')=1\\
                 0<g|u-u'|\le D/T_x}}
 B_{g,G}(u)B_{g,G}(u').                                  \tag{6}
\]
Then the exact identity
\[
 {\mathfrak C}_\star^\Lambda
 =\sum_{1\le g<T_x}\sum_{\substack{G\ge1\\g\mid G}}
   \sum_{r\ge1}\mu(r)|S_{g,G,r}|^2
  -{\cal P}_\Delta^\Lambda                                \tag{7}
\]
holds, while
\[
 |{\cal P}_\Delta^\Lambda|
 \ll_{W,\Phi,\alpha,\beta}{xD(\log x)^2\over T_x},         \tag{8}
\]
and
\[
 \sum_{1\le g<T_x}\sum_{\substack{G\ge1\\g\mid G}}
 \sum_{r\ge T_x}|S_{g,G,r}|^2
 \ll_{W,\Phi,\alpha,\beta}{xD(\log x)^2\over T_x}.         \tag{9}
\]
Therefore the following one-sided estimate is sufficient:
\[
 {\cal E}_{<}\ll_{W,\Phi,\alpha,\beta,\eta,\rho}
 xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta}.                                   \tag{TB-COP-CORE}
\]
It implies the full-von-Mangoldt hard-core bound and, by the prime-power removal in fact 02a763eba051c761, (TB-HARD) of fact bc46ed5832faeade.

The remaining sum (4) has two and only two auxiliary Möbius divisors at this stage: the exact common gcd \(g<T_x\) and the coprimality-projector divisor \(r<T_x\). For fixed \(g,G,r\), (3) is a single fixed-\(G\) reflected-prime sum. No estimate for \({\cal E}_{<}\) is asserted.
1f5316e61daf156d.proof:
We first reindex (1). For each ordered pair put
\[
 g=(d_1,d_2),\qquad d_1=gu,\qquad d_2=gu'.
\]
Then \(g<T_x\), \((u,u')=1\), and, because \(d_1,d_2\) are squarefree,
\[
 \mu(d_1)\mu(d_2)=\mu(u)\mu(u').
\]
Put
\[
 G=gm.
\]
Then \(g\mid G\), \(m=G/g\), and
\[
 d_1m=uG,\qquad d_2m=u'G.                               \tag{10}
\]
The transformation
\[
 (d_1,d_2,m)\longleftrightarrow(g,u,u',G)
\]
is bijective under the displayed conditions. Substitution into (1) gives
\[
 {\mathfrak C}_\star^\Lambda
 =\sum_{g<T_x}\sum_{g\mid G}
 \sum_{\substack{u,u'\ge1\\(u,u')=1\\
                 g|u-u'|>D/T_x}}
 B_{g,G}(u)B_{g,G}(u').                                  \tag{11}
\]

Let
\[
 {\cal E}=
 \sum_{g<T_x}\sum_{g\mid G}
 \sum_{\substack{u,u'\ge1\\(u,u')=1}}
 B_{g,G}(u)B_{g,G}(u').
\]
There is no diagonal term in this sum. Indeed, if \(u=u'\) and
\((u,u')=1\), then \(u=1\). But \(gu\in{\cal I}_D\) implies
\(g\ge D/2>T_x\), contradicting \(g<T_x\). Hence (11) gives the exact identity
\[
 {\mathfrak C}_\star^\Lambda={\cal E}-{\cal P}_\Delta^\Lambda.          \tag{12}
\]

Use the finite coprimality identity
\[
 {\bf1}_{(u,u')=1}=\sum_{r\mid u,\ r\mid u'}\mu(r).
\]
All sums are finite because of the supports. Interchanging them and using that the coefficients are real gives
\[
 {\cal E}
 =\sum_{g<T_x}\sum_{g\mid G}\sum_{r\ge1}
 \mu(r)\left|\sum_{r\mid u}B_{g,G}(u)\right|^2,
\]
which is (7).

We prove (8) directly. Returning through the bijection (10), the pairs in
\({\cal P}_\Delta^\Lambda\) correspond to ordered
\(d_1,d_2\in[D/2,2D]\) with
\(0<|d_1-d_2|\le D/T_x\). There are \(O(D^2/T_x)\) such ordered pairs.
For each pair, the support of \(W(d_1m/x)\) gives \(m\ll_{\alpha,\beta}x/D\).
Every smooth factor is bounded and both von Mangoldt factors are
\(O(\log x)\). Thus
\[
 |{\cal P}_\Delta^\Lambda|
 \ll {D^2\over T_x}{x\over D}(\log x)^2
 ={xD(\log x)^2\over T_x},
\]
proving (8).

It remains to prove (9). If \(B_{g,G}(u)\ne0\), then
\[
 D/2\le gu\le2D,\qquad \alpha x\le uG\le\beta x.          \tag{13}
\]
For fixed \(g,G,r\), the number of \(u\) divisible by \(r\) in (13) is
\[
 O\!\left({D\over gr}+1\right).
\]
If it is nonzero, then \(r\le2D/g\), so the preceding quantity is
\(O(D/(gr))\). Therefore
\[
 |S_{g,G,r}|\ll_{W,\Phi}{D\log x\over gr}.                \tag{14}
\]
Also, for fixed \(g\), the existence of a \(u\) satisfying (13) forces
\[
 {\alpha xg\over2D}\le G\le{2\beta xg\over D}.
\]
Since \(g\mid G\), the number of possible \(G\) is \(O_{\alpha,\beta}(x/D)\).
Using (14),
\[
\begin{split}
 \sum_{g<T_x}\sum_{g\mid G}\sum_{r\ge T_x}|S_{g,G,r}|^2
 &\ll {x\over D}
 \sum_{g<T_x}\sum_{r\ge T_x}
 {D^2(\log x)^2\over g^2r^2}\\
 &\ll {xD(\log x)^2\over T_x},
\end{split}
\]
because \(\sum_g g^{-2}\) is bounded and
\(\sum_{r\ge T_x}r^{-2}\ll T_x^{-1}\). This proves (9).

Split the \(r\)-sum in (7) at \(T_x\). Equations (8)--(9) prove (5).
Finally
\[
 {(\log x)^2\over T_x}
 =(\log x)^{-4-\eta-\rho}.
\]
Thus (TB-COP-CORE) gives the required one-sided full-von-Mangoldt upper bound with an error no larger than
\(xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta-\rho}\). Fact 02a763eba051c761 transfers this to the prime-only hard core, and fact bc46ed5832faeade supplies the stated consequences.

glossary.B_{g,G}(u): the reduced fixed-G reflected-prime coefficient at residual common gcd g
glossary.S_{g,G,r}: the restriction of the reduced reflected-prime sum to r dividing u
glossary.TB-COP-CORE: the one-sided double-polylogarithmic signed-energy estimate sufficient for TB-HARD
glossary.cal E_<: the signed coprime-projector energy with both g and r below T_x

1fd55b934f638328.title: POWER PAYMENT OF THE RESIDUE DIAGONAL IN THE FULL-DOUBLE CROSSED MZB FACE
1fd55b934f638328.author: slava chan
1fd55b934f638328.statement:
POWER PAYMENT OF THE RESIDUE DIAGONAL IN THE FULL-DOUBLE CROSSED MZB FACE.

Assume facts 050efa07f87f374a and f71c0564150cb532, with
0<eta<1/12,
F_0=x^(1/2-eta)=Q^(1-2eta+o(1)),
B=Q^(4/3+o(1)).
Let E_res^{dbl} be the sub-sum of E_cross^{dbl} in equation (6) of fact f71c0564150cb532 on which
a_1 congruent a_2 (mod d).                                  (1)
Thus the composite d-phase equals one, but every literal coefficient, Ramanujan weight, one-sided r_i Euler response, squarefree condition, coprimality condition, conductor threshold dr_i>F_0, and dyadic condition dr_1r_2t asymp B is retained. Then
|E_res^{dbl}|<<Q^(7/3+4eta+o(1)).                            (2)
Consequently, for every fixed omega satisfying
0<omega<1/3-4eta,                                            (3)
the residue diagonal satisfies
|E_res^{dbl}|<<Q^(8/3-omega).                                (4)

Therefore the residue diagonal of the full-double face is paid at the fixed-power MZB-ENERGY scale. This theorem does not estimate the off-residue-diagonal part of the full-double face, any proper common-core face in equation (3) of fact f71c0564150cb532, or C_small, and it asserts no actual-Z_mid or Goldbach closure.
1fd55b934f638328.proof:
Fact 050efa07f87f374a gives |alpha_a|<=Q^o(1) on every literal tensor. We first bound the arithmetic coefficient in (5) of fact f71c0564150cb532.

Because r_1,r_2,t are pairwise coprime and (r_1r_2,N)=1, multiplicativity of Ramanujan sums gives
c_{r_2t}(N)c_{r_1t}(N)
 =c_{r_2}(N)c_{r_1}(N)c_t(N)^2.                             (5)
The squarefree integers r_i are coprime to N, so
c_{r_i}(N)=mu(r_i).
Also |c_t(N)|<=phi(t), directly from the defining sum of phi(t) unit complex numbers. Hence
|c_{r_2t}(N)c_{r_1t}(N)|<=phi(t)^2.                         (6)

For every squarefree r and every admissible a,b,
|K_r(b;a)|
 <=product_{p|r}(1+p-1)=r.                                  (7)
Using multiplicativity of phi and (6)-(7), the absolute value of the coefficient in (5) of fact f71c0564150cb532, apart from the d-phase, is at most
r_1r_2 phi(t)^2/
 [phi(r_1)^2phi(r_2)^2phi(t)^2]
 =r_1/phi(r_1)^2 times r_2/phi(r_2)^2
 <<Q^o(1)/(r_1r_2),                                         (8)
because all variables are of polynomial size and n/phi(n)=n^o(1).

Split d into dyadic ranges d asymp D. For fixed d put
V=B/d and R_0=max(1,F_0/d).
The conductor conditions dr_i>F_0 imply r_i>R_0 up to harmless endpoint constants. Discarding squarefreeness and coprimality only enlarges the following positive sum. For fixed r_1,r_2, the number of positive t with
r_1r_2t asymp V
is O(V/(r_1r_2)+1). Therefore
sum_{r_1,r_2,t; r_i>R_0, r_1r_2t asymp V}1/(r_1r_2)
 << V(sum_{r>R_0}r^(-2))^2
    +(sum_{R_0<r<O(V)}r^(-1))^2
 << V/R_0^2+(log(2V))^2.                                    (9)
If d<=F_0, then V/R_0^2=Bd/F_0^2. If d>F_0, then
V/R_0^2=B/d<=Bd/F_0^2.
Moreover fact 2e80012db28da736 gives d>F_0^2/b, and b asymp B, so Bd/F_0^2 is bounded below by a positive constant up to endpoint constants. The logarithmic term in (9) is therefore absorbed into Q^o(1), giving uniformly
sum_{r_1,r_2,t}^{*}1/(r_1r_2)
 <<Q^o(1)BD/F_0^2.                                          (10)

For each d asymp D, the number of ordered a_1!=a_2 in an interval of length O(Q) satisfying (1) is
O(Q^2/D+Q),
as proved in fact f71c0564150cb532. If d exceeds a sufficiently large constant multiple of Q, the interval diameter is smaller than d and there is no unequal pair satisfying (1). Hence only D<<Q occurs.

Combine the Q^o(1) alpha bound, (8), (10), the residue-pair count, and O(D) possible integers d asymp D. The contribution of one dyadic D is
<<Q^o(1) D(Q^2/D+Q) BD/F_0^2
 =Q^o(1)(Q^2+QD)BD/F_0^2
 <<Q^o(1)Q^2BD/F_0^2,                                      (11)
since D<<Q. Summing the logarithmically many D-ranges and using D<<Q gives
|E_res^{dbl}|
 <<Q^o(1)Q^3B/F_0^2
 =Q^(3+4/3-2+4eta+o(1))
 =Q^(7/3+4eta+o(1)),
which proves (2).

Condition (3) is equivalent to
7/3+4eta<8/3-omega.
Thus the o(1) term in (2) is absorbed into the strict exponent margin, proving (4). All estimates were restricted to the full-double residue diagonal, so the scope clauses follow.

glossary.E_res^{dbl}: The a_1 congruent a_2 modulo d sub-sum of the literal full-double crossed MZB energy.

1feb8a751976e771.title: TOP-B RECOMBINED POLYLOGARITHMIC CROSS-\(y\) NEAR-RESONANCE PAYMENT. Use the fixed \(k,U,Y,F\) recombined singleton top-\(B\) pre-Cauchy energy of fact \(d63101722d12c88c\). Thus
1feb8a751976e771.author: slava chan
1feb8a751976e771.statement:
TOP-B RECOMBINED POLYLOGARITHMIC CROSS-\(y\) NEAR-RESONANCE PAYMENT. Use the fixed \(k,U,Y,F\) recombined singleton top-\(B\) pre-Cauchy energy of fact \(d63101722d12c88c\). Thus
\[
 U\le u<2U,\qquad Y\le y<2Y,\qquad
 Q\le q<2Q,\qquad F\le|h|<2F,
\]
every supported \(y\) is squarefree, the nonzero integer target
\(\mathscr A\) and all displayed scales have fixed polynomial size in
\(Q\), and the singleton coefficient satisfies a fixed divisor envelope.
For an ordered pair of row coordinates put
\[
 \Omega=h_1q_2u_2-h_2q_1u_1.
\]
On the sector \(\Omega\ne0\), define
\[
 r_y={y\over(y,\mathscr A\Omega)}.
\]
Fix a real constant \(A_0\ge0\), and let
\(V_{\rm rec}^{(\mathrm{near\text{-}FR},A_0)}\) be the exact restriction of the expanded recombined energy to
\[
 \Omega\ne0,\qquad
 1<r_y\le(\log(2Q))^{A_0}.                                    \tag{1}
\]
Then, for every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 |V_{\rm rec}^{(\mathrm{near\text{-}FR},A_0)}|
 \ll_{\varepsilon,A_0}Q^\varepsilon U^2Q^2F^2.
 \quad}                                                        \tag{2}
\]
Every source, marker, Fourier, target-gcd, fixed-\(U\), parent, sign,
order/equal-cell, collision, deletion, coprimality and provenance
coordinate already recombined in the singleton remains present.
The sector \(r_y=1\) is exactly the fully resonant sector already paid in
fact \(d63101722d12c88c\). Equation (2) pays only a fixed
polylogarithmic effective-conductor neighborhood and leaves
\[
 r_y>(\log(2Q))^{A_0}
\]
inside the literal nonresonant specified-spectrum problem. Summing over all
supported stopping lengths \(k\) changes (2) only by a polylogarithmic
factor.
1feb8a751976e771.proof:
Expand the recombined energy exactly as in fact
d63101722d12c88c. For fixed
\[
 (u_1,q_1,h_1,u_2,q_2,h_2)
\]
with \(\Omega\ne0\), the integer
\[
 M=\mathscr A\Omega
\]
is nonzero and has fixed polynomial size in \(Q\).

For a supported \(y\), put
\[
 d=(y,M),\qquad r={y\over d}.
\]
Then
\[
 d\mid |M|,\qquad y=dr,\qquad r=r_y.
\]
The squarefreeness of \(y\), supplied by the explicit stopping-weight
support in facts 6414b11506a84ff0 and d63101722d12c88c, also gives
\((d,r)=1\), although this extra coprimality is not needed for the upper
bound.

Let
\[
 L_0=(\log(2Q))^{A_0}.
\]
For each positive integer \(r\le L_0\) and each positive divisor
\(d\mid|M|\), the equation \(y=dr\) determines at most one integer \(y\).
Consequently the number of supported \(y\in[Y,2Y)\) satisfying (1) is at
most
\[
 \lfloor L_0\rfloor\tau(|M|)
 \ll_{\varepsilon,A_0}Q^\varepsilon.                          \tag{3}
\]
All dyadic, coprimality and inherited literal selectors only reduce this
count.

There are \(O(U^2Q^2F^2)\) ordered coordinate sextuples. The two
singleton coefficient factors have modulus at most
\[
 \tau_J(u_1u_2y^2q_1q_2|h_1h_2|)
 (\log(2Q))^C
 \ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon
\]
after enlarging the fixed divisor order and renaming \(\varepsilon\).
The reciprocity phases have modulus one. Absolute summation using (3)
therefore gives (2).

Finally,
\[
 r_y=1
 \Longleftrightarrow y=(y,\mathscr A\Omega)
 \Longleftrightarrow y\mid\mathscr A\Omega,
\]
so this is exactly the fully resonant sector when \(\Omega\ne0\).
If \(r_y>1\), then \(y\nmid\mathscr A\Omega\), so every term in (1)
belongs to the nonresonant sector. Fact d63101722d12c88c proves that a
fixed \(y\) occurs for at most one \(k\), and that the number of supported
\(k\)'s is \(O(\log Q)\); this proves the final multiplicity and scope
statements.

glossary.V_rec^(near-FR,A_0): The recombined pre-Cauchy energy sector with nonzero cross-u determinant and cross-y effective conductor strictly between one and a fixed power of log(2Q).
glossary.r_y: The cross-y effective conductor y divided by gcd(y, the target times the cross-u determinant).

2015f67a9c3aca53.title: PRE-CAUCHY-B: EXACT FIXED-y CROSS-u MOMENT, RANDOMIZATION, AND SPECIFIED-SPECTRUM DETERMINANT. Fix one orientation, exact outer-gcd layer, normalized scales Q,B, a nonzero integer target A, one dyadic frequency block F<=|h|<2F, and one smooth/projective fiber of the literal top-B source. Fix an integer k>=2 and a dyadic scale Y. Restrict to exact first-crossing B-copies for which the marked integer is
2015f67a9c3aca53.author: slava chan
2015f67a9c3aca53.statement:
PRE-CAUCHY-B: EXACT FIXED-y CROSS-u MOMENT, RANDOMIZATION, AND SPECIFIED-SPECTRUM DETERMINANT. Fix one orientation, exact outer-gcd layer, normalized scales Q,B, a nonzero integer target A, one dyadic frequency block F<=|h|<2F, and one smooth/projective fiber of the literal top-B source. Fix an integer k>=2 and a dyadic scale Y. Restrict to exact first-crossing B-copies for which the marked integer is
n=uy,  Y<=y<2Y,
the canonical marked dilator is y, the complementary factor is u, and (u,y)=1. Every other source, parent, fixed-U, target-gcd, order, equal-cell, collision, deletion and provenance coordinate is denoted collectively by zeta and retained.

Put
alpha_k(u)=(-1)^k mu(u)1_{j_I(u)=0}/binom(k+omega_L(u),k),
and let Gamma_k(y)=Gamma_{k;L,S}(y) be the nonnegative first-crossing weight. On every nonzero exact B-copy, write its literal coefficient uniquely as
c_{u,y,zeta}(q,h)=alpha_k(u)Gamma_k(y)b_{u,y,zeta}(q,h),
where b retains every remaining literal coefficient and mask and is extended by zero unless
Q<=q<2Q, F<=|h|<2F, (q,uy)=1.
Let H_P>0 be the literal Poisson normalization and define
S_{k,y}=sum_{u,zeta,q,h}alpha_k(u)b_{u,y,zeta}(q,h)e_q(-Ah(uy)^(-1)),
T_{k,Y}^B=H_P^(-1)sum_{Y<=y<2Y}Gamma_k(y)S_{k,y},
W_{k,Y}=sum_{Y<=y<2Y}Gamma_k(y),
M_{k,Y}^pre=sum_{Y<=y<2Y}Gamma_k(y)|S_{k,y}|^2.             (1)
All sums are finite and all inverses are taken on the displayed coprime support. Then
|T_{k,Y}^B|^2<=H_P^(-2)W_{k,Y}M_{k,Y}^pre,
0<=W_{k,Y}<=Y+1.                                             (2)
If epsilon_y are independent random signs with values plus or minus one, then exactly
M_{k,Y}^pre=E_epsilon |sum_{Y<=y<2Y}epsilon_y Gamma_k(y)^(1/2)S_{k,y}|^2.   (3)

There is an exact common-y reciprocal normal form. Define
tilde b_{u,y,zeta}(q,h)=b_{u,y,zeta}(q,h)
 e(-Ah/(quy)) e_u(Ah(qy)^(-1)).
Then
S_{k,y}=sum_{u,zeta,q,h}alpha_k(u)tilde b_{u,y,zeta}(q,h)
 e_y(Ah(qu)^(-1)),                                           (4)
and
M_{k,Y}^pre=sum_y Gamma_k(y)
 sum_{u_1,zeta_1,q_1,h_1,u_2,zeta_2,q_2,h_2}
 alpha_k(u_1)conjugate(alpha_k(u_2))
 tilde b_{u_1,y,zeta_1}(q_1,h_1)
 conjugate(tilde b_{u_2,y,zeta_2}(q_2,h_2))
 e_y(A Delta_B (q_1q_2u_1u_2)^(-1)),                         (5)
where
Delta_B=h_1q_2u_2-h_2q_1u_1.                                (6)
Thus (5) partitions identically into
Delta_B=0;
Delta_B nonzero and y divides A Delta_B;
Delta_B nonzero and y does not divide A Delta_B.             (7)
No u-copy has been squared separately before (5), and every literal coefficient remains inside the two tilde-b factors.

At the endpoint G=1, where H_P=B/Q and the desired fixed-block trace scale is Q^(2-delta_B) for a fixed delta_B>0, the explicit sufficient pre-Cauchy supplier is
M_{k,Y}^pre << H_P^2 Q^(4-2delta_B)/Y,                       (8)
up to subpolynomial block and label losses. On the critical k=3 slice of fact 7d26c3f3b82d9b71, Y=Q^(beta/2+o(1)) and H_P=Q^(beta-1), so the right side of (8) is
Q^(2+3beta/2-2delta_B+o(1)).                                 (9)
Equations (1)-(7) are exact, and (8) is an open sufficient estimate. This fact proves no bound for (8), no payment of any proper sector in (7), no complete top-B or TOP-BC123-CMD-RED estimate, and no Goldbach conclusion.
2015f67a9c3aca53.proof:
The exact first-crossing identity in fact 6414b11506a84ff0 gives the B-marker coefficient
alpha_k(u)Gamma_k(y)
on every copy n=uy. Fact f0f6807663d3ef3c identifies y as the canonical marked dilator and u as its coprime complement. The literal source identity of fact 41b56ed8e64bdba6 retains the marker coefficient multiplicatively inside c_lambda(q,h), together with all other masks and coefficients. On a nonzero copy, division by the nonzero marker coefficient therefore defines b uniquely; zero copies are absent and the zero extension is harmless. Substitution gives the first two definitions in (1) and the exact formula for T_{k,Y}^B.

Because Gamma_k(y)>=0, weighted Cauchy--Schwarz yields
|sum_y Gamma_k(y)S_{k,y}|^2
 <=(sum_y Gamma_k(y))(sum_y Gamma_k(y)|S_{k,y}|^2),
which proves the first assertion in (2). From its definition, Gamma_k(y) is an indicator times k^(-1) times a count of at most k primes, so 0<=Gamma_k(y)<=1. There are at most Y+1 integers in [Y,2Y), proving the second assertion. Expanding the expectation in (3), independence gives E(epsilon_y epsilon_{y'})=1 when y=y' and zero otherwise, proving (3).

For a supported summand, (q,uy)=1 and (u,y)=1. Additive reciprocity followed by CRT gives
e_q(-Ah(uy)^(-1))
 =e(-Ah/(quy)) e_{uy}(Ahq^(-1))
 =e(-Ah/(quy)) e_u(Ah(qy)^(-1)) e_y(Ah(qu)^(-1)).
Absorbing the first two factors into b proves (4). Multiply (4) by its conjugate. Modulo y,
h_1(q_1u_1)^(-1)-h_2(q_2u_2)^(-1)
is congruent to
(h_1q_2u_2-h_2q_1u_1)(q_1q_2u_1u_2)^(-1).
This proves (5)-(6). The alternatives in (7) are disjoint and exhaustive.

Finally (2) and W_{k,Y}<=Y+1 show that (8), with a harmless constant and subpolynomial taxes, implies |T_{k,Y}^B|<=Q^(2-delta_B). At G=1, fact 41b56ed8e64bdba6 gives H_P=B/Q. On the critical k=3 block, fact 7d26c3f3b82d9b71 and its predecessor 6edc174d83447911 give Y=Q^(beta/2+o(1)) and B=Q^beta. Hence
H_P^2 Q^(4-2delta_B)/Y
=Q^(2beta-2)Q^(4-2delta_B)Q^(-beta/2+o(1))
=Q^(2+3beta/2-2delta_B+o(1)),
which is (9). No estimate of that moment has been inserted.

glossary.M_{k,Y}^pre: the Gamma-weighted fixed-y pre-Cauchy moment of the assembled rows S_{k,y}
glossary.S_{k,y}: the complete literal top-B row obtained by summing all complementary u copies before squaring, at fixed stopping variable y
glossary.W_{k,Y}: the total first-crossing weight sum over the fixed dyadic y-block
glossary.alpha_k(u): the u-dependent factor in the exact k-prime first-crossing coefficient

20609f1342ff4558.title: LITERAL SHORT-CONDUCTOR MASK AUDIT, EXACT DELETION REMAINDER, AND q-PRINCIPAL/OSC RECONCILIATION
20609f1342ff4558.author: slava chan
20609f1342ff4558.statement:
LITERAL SHORT-CONDUCTOR MASK AUDIT, EXACT DELETION REMAINDER, AND q-PRINCIPAL/OSC RECONCILIATION.

Let a,b,m,k,L_0 be positive integers satisfying
  gcd(a,b)=1,  am+bk=L_0.                                    (1)
Let S be a nonempty finite set of prime divisors of b, let h be an integer satisfying
  |h|<min_{r in S} r,
and define
  J(h)={r in S:r divides mh}.                                (2)
Then
  J(h)=S intersect {r:r is prime and r divides L_0}          (3)
for h nonzero, while
  J(0)=S.                                                     (4)
Consequently the short full-rough-conductor mask is
  1_{J(h)=emptyset}
  =1_{gcd(L_0,product_{r in S}r)=1}1_{h nonzero}.            (5)
It is constant on the short nonzero band. If gcd(L_0,product_{r in S}r)=1, it equals one there and differs from its zero-alias value zero. If that greatest common divisor is greater than one, the mask is identically zero on the full short family including h=0.

Now adopt the assumptions and notation of fact 7670948dedd78714. Thus n=vp, gcd(A,n)=gcd(q,n)=1, F is smooth and compactly supported,
  z_q=n^(-1)Fhat(0),                                         (6)
and completion of the reduced source progression gives z_q plus the original nonzero h-row. Let S be a nonempty finite set of prime divisors of n and restrict to |h|<min_{r in S}r. On every source solution qm+nk=A, equation (5), with a=q, b=n, and L_0=A, reduces to
  1_{J(h)=emptyset}=1_{h nonzero},                            (7)
because gcd(A,n)=1. Hence multiplying the completed alias family by the literal short full-conductor mask leaves every nonzero alias unchanged but changes its zero alias from z_q to zero. The exact facewise principal discrepancy is therefore
  z_q=n^(-1)Fhat(0),                                         (8)
not a new oscillatory term. If |F(y)|<=L and the support of F has length at most C_0 M, then, with H_0=n/M,
  |z_q|<=C_0 L/H_0.                                          (9)

Let cal O be a finite outer family of triples (q,v,p) with at most C_1 Q possible q-values, at most C_1 V possible v-values, and at most C_1 P possible prime p-values. Assume n=vp, all outer coefficients have modulus at most one, H_0>=c_H H uniformly, and VP=QH, where C_0,C_1>=1 and c_H>0. Then the total absolute discrepancy from imposing the short full-conductor face before principal cancellation is at most
  C_0 C_1^3 c_H^(-1) L QVP/H
  =C_0 C_1^3 c_H^(-1) L Q^2.                               (10)
This is only a density ledger.

There is also an exact formula for an arbitrary unrecombined source deletion. Let E(m,k) be any zero-one function on integer solutions of qm+nk=A and put
  u_q=sum_{qm+nk=A}F(m),
  u_{q,E}=sum_{qm+nk=A}E(m,k)F(m),
  r_{q,E}=sum_{qm+nk=A}(1-E(m,k))F(m).                       (11)
For the unmasked and deleted rows
  a_q=u_q-z_q,  a_{q,E}=u_{q,E}-z_q,
one has exactly
  a_{q,E}=a_q-r_{q,E}.                                       (12)
If the support of F has length less than n, then
  |r_{q,E}|<=||F||_infinity,                                 (13)
because the source progression contains at most one supported integer m. Thus an arbitrary discrete m- or kappa-deletion does not inherit the old principal cancellation: its exact residual is (11), or, after choosing a smooth extension, it has the new zero alias stated in fact 7670948dedd78714.

For the literal source of facts 77d7a3419a07305c and 7131a06664967733, the logarithmic, fixed-U, smooth, dyadic, and physical source weights are absorbed into the smooth function F before Poisson summation; the high mask and frozen parent are outer label predicates; and the marker class, prime ordering, outer-gcd provenance, and rough-support collision labels depend only on outer factorization data. Those masks commute with the pointwise row identity. In the unit hard-source specialization, the first named mask in that literal refinement which is not constant across the completed alias family is the short full-conductor mask (7). The legal order is therefore: complete the unmasked reduced progression and cancel (6) pointwise by fact 7670948dedd78714; only then impose the nonzero-band conductor and collision refinements. In this order every surviving nonzero alias is the original h-coefficient. Consequently the all-nonzero OSC term remains exactly T_OSC^nz of fact 670a97b5f2366250, and the still-required estimate is
  |T_OSC^nz|<<Q^epsilon P^2Q^(7/3).                          (14)
No saving toward (14), PMD closure, or Goldbach follows from this mask audit.
20609f1342ff4558.proof:
For r in S, the divisibility r|b implies r|bk. Reducing (1) modulo r gives
  am congruent L_0 modulo r.
Because gcd(a,b)=1 and r|b, a is invertible modulo r. Hence
  r|m if and only if r|L_0.                                  (15)
If h is nonzero and |h|<r, then r does not divide h. Therefore
  r|mh if and only if r|m if and only if r|L_0.              (16)
Applying (16) to every r in S proves (3). When h=0, every r divides mh=0, proving (4). Because S is nonempty, (4) gives a nonempty J(0). The empty-set condition in (3)-(4) is exactly (5), and its two greatest-common-divisor cases give the stated dichotomy.

In the specialization a=q, b=n, and L_0=A, every r in S divides n. The hypothesis gcd(A,n)=1 gives r does not divide A. Thus the first factor on the right side of (5) equals one, proving (7). Fact 7670948dedd78714 proves that the zero alias of the completed reduced progression is z_q and that all nonzero aliases are exactly the original nonzero h-row. Multiplication by (7) retains all of those nonzero aliases and deletes h=0. Therefore the difference between the unmasked and full-conductor zero aliases is exactly z_q, proving (8).

By definition of the Fourier transform,
  |Fhat(0)|=|integral_R F(y)dy|
  <=integral_R|F(y)|dy
  <=C_0 M L.
Divide by n and use H_0=n/M to prove (9). Under the outer-family assumptions, the number of triples is at most C_1^3 QVP and every one contributes at most C_0 L/(c_H H). Multiplication and VP=QH prove (10).

Definitions (11) give
  u_{q,E}=u_q-r_{q,E}.
Subtracting the same z_q from both sides proves (12). The congruence qm congruent A modulo n places m in one residue class modulo n because gcd(q,n)=1. An interval of length less than n contains at most one integer in that residue class. Therefore the sum defining r_{q,E} has at most one nonzero term, and (13) follows.

It remains to justify the literal-mask and OSC statements. Fact 7131a06664967733 states and proves that, on the literal forward source, the logarithms and every remaining physical source factor, including the fixed-U and dyadic smooth weights, are contained in the smooth Poisson function, while the high mask and frozen parent are label predicates. Fact 77d7a3419a07305c defines the marker class from the factorization of the normalized modulus, orders the two C2 rough primes, defines outer-gcd provenance from those prime factors, and defines pair collisions from intersections of the rough supports. None of those operations changes the completed source progression at fixed outer data. Equations (3)-(5) give the exact audit for the apparently m-dependent short conductor mask. In the unit specialization, (7) shows that it alone among these listed masks distinguishes h=0 from the nonzero short band.

Thus fact 7670948dedd78714 may be applied before the conductor refinement, when its complete-progression hypothesis is satisfied. After its pointwise zero-alias cancellation, applying any of the listed outer masks and then (7) only deletes or groups surviving nonzero aliases; it does not alter their coefficients or phases. Fact 670a97b5f2366250 identifies the all-nonzero surviving hard-source OSC term with T_OSC^nz and states (14) as the remaining sufficient estimate. Since the present proof has established only identities and absolute density bounds, it supplies no estimate for T_OSC^nz. This proves every assertion and the scope statements.

glossary.J(h): The set of rough primes in S that divide the physical product mh at alias h.
glossary.S: The nonempty finite set of rough prime divisors whose primitive conductor is audited.
glossary.T_OSC^nz: The all-nonzero source-transmuted OSC term defined in fact 670a97b5f2366250.
glossary.cal O: The finite family of outer triples in the density ledger.
glossary.r_{q,E}: The exact sum of source terms removed by the zero-one deletion E.
glossary.u_{q,E}: The source progression sum after the zero-one deletion E.

212d1415bf03c2a7.title: SHARED INTEGER LIFT, EXACT ONE-COLUMN DOUBLE DFT, AND FIBRE L2 BOUND
212d1415bf03c2a7.author: slava chan
212d1415bf03c2a7.statement:
SHARED INTEGER LIFT, EXACT ONE-COLUMN DOUBLE DFT, AND FIBRE L2 BOUND.

Fix positive constants L and B. Let m>2L+1 be odd, put q=m^2, let s belong to {1,-1}, and let K be an integer coprime to m. Every residue u modulo m is represented below by its unique integer in {0,1,...,m-1}, and
 A_u=K+2smu.                                                         (1)
Let I_a,I_c,I_1,I_2 be integer intervals of cardinality at most Lm. Assume I_1 and I_2 contain only positive integers coprime to q. Let F be a complex function supported on I_a, let W be a complex function modulo m, and let alpha and beta be complex sequences supported respectively on I_1 and I_2.

Let E_lift be any subset of the tuples
 (a,c,n_1,n_2,u,k) in I_a times I_c times I_1 times I_2 times {0,...,m-1} times Z
satisfying
 a n_2=A_u+kq,  c n_1=a n_2-2K,                                    (2)
and assume
 1<=|a n_2-2K|<=q^B                                                  (3)
on E_lift. Let Gamma be any complex function on E_lift with |Gamma|<=1. Define
 T_lift=sum_{E_lift}F(a)W(u)alpha(n_1)beta(n_2)
                         Gamma(a,c,n_1,n_2,u,k).                     (4)
The integer k in (2) is a common lift relative to the fixed representative convention: the same equations give exactly
 -c n_1=K-2smu-kq.                                                   (5)

For a unit residue x modulo q define
 C_lift(x)=sum_{E_lift; ax congruent 1 modulo q}
 W(u)alpha(n_1)beta(n_2)Gamma(a,c,n_1,n_2,u,k),                      (6)
and define C_lift(x)=0 when gcd(x,q)>1. For a residue y modulo q define
 F_per(y)=sum_{a congruent y modulo q}F(a).                          (7)
Define
 C_hat_lift(p)=sum_{x modulo q}C_lift(x)e_q(-px),
 F_hat(h)=sum_{y modulo q}F_per(y)e_q(-hy),                          (8)
where e_q(z)=exp(2 pi i z/q). Then
 T_lift=sum_{x modulo q;gcd(x,q)=1}C_lift(x)F_per(x^(-1))            (9)
and
 T_lift=q^(-2)sum_{p modulo q}sum_{h modulo q}
 C_hat_lift(p)F_hat(h)S(p,h;q),                                    (10)
where
 S(p,h;q)=sum_{x modulo q;gcd(x,q)=1}e_q(px+h x^(-1)).               (11)

For every epsilon>0,
 ||C_lift||_2
 <=C_{B,L,epsilon}q^epsilon||W||_2||alpha||_2||beta||_2,             (12)
and
 ||C_hat_lift||_2=q^(1/2)||C_lift||_2
 <=C_{B,L,epsilon}q^(1/2+epsilon)
   ||W||_2||alpha||_2||beta||_2.                                   (13)
All norms in (12)-(13) are counting-measure norms on the displayed finite residue sets or supports.

The set E_lift and Gamma may retain the second row window, signs, masks, primality conditions, the literal value of k, and other zero-one selectors. If W is centered, then a specialization of fact 8592875ae5046498 reaches (4) whenever its row weight has the separated form F(a) times a bounded literal gate: for every admitted row and column tuple, u is the unique residue determined by a n_2 congruent K+2smu modulo q, k is then fixed by (2), and the indicator of E_lift times Gamma defines a character-independent row gate. No estimate for (10) is asserted here.
212d1415bf03c2a7.proof:
Equation (5) follows from (2):
 -c n_1=2K-a n_2=K-2smu-kq.
The fixed representative convention makes both A_u and k unambiguous.

Every A_u is a unit modulo q because it is congruent to K modulo m. In E_lift, n_2 is a unit and a n_2 is congruent to A_u modulo q, so a is a unit.

Since |I_a|<=Lm<q, each residue modulo q has at most one representative in I_a. Thus, for each unit x, all tuples in (6) have the same a, namely the unique integer in I_a congruent to x^(-1). Hence F(a)=F_per(x^(-1)). Every tuple has exactly one x congruent to a^(-1), proving (9).

Fourier inversion on Z/qZ gives
 C_lift(x)=q^(-1)sum_p C_hat_lift(p)e_q(px),
 F_per(x^(-1))=q^(-1)sum_h F_hat(h)e_q(hx^(-1)).
Insert these in (9), interchange the finite sums, and use (11). This proves (10).

Fix a unit x. There is at most one a. Reducing the first equation of (2) modulo m and using a congruent to x^(-1) gives
 n_2 congruent Kx modulo m.                                         (14)
An interval of cardinality at most Lm contains at most L+1 integers in one residue class modulo m. Thus there are at most L+1 possible n_2. For fixed x,a,n_2, the congruence
 (a n_2-K)/m congruent 2su modulo m
determines u uniquely because 2s is a unit modulo odd m. For fixed x,a,n_2, the second equation in (2) says that positive n_1 divides the nonzero integer a n_2-2K and determines c.

We now prove the needed divisor estimate. For every delta>0 there is C_delta such that tau(N)<=C_delta N^delta for every positive integer N. Write N=product_p p^{v_p}. For p>=2^(1/delta), one has v_p+1<=2^{v_p}<=p^{delta v_p}. For the finitely many primes p<2^(1/delta), the supremum over v>=0 of (v+1)p^{-delta v} is finite. Multiplying these finitely many suprema gives C_delta and proves the claim. Apply it with delta=epsilon/B to 1<=|a n_2-2K|<=q^B. After renaming epsilon,
 tau(|a n_2-2K|)<=C_{B,epsilon}q^epsilon.                            (15)
Thus every fibre of E_lift -> x has cardinality at most C_{B,L,epsilon}q^epsilon.

Cauchy--Schwarz in each x-fibre gives
 sum_x|C_lift(x)|^2
 <=C_{B,L,epsilon}q^epsilon
   sum_{E_lift}|W(u)|^2|alpha(n_1)|^2|beta(n_2)|^2.                 (16)
For fixed u,n_1,n_2, the congruence a n_2 congruent A_u modulo q fixes one residue class of a because n_2 is a unit. Since |I_a|<q, there is at most one a; it fixes k, and n_1 fixes c. Hence E_lift -> (u,n_1,n_2) has fibres of size at most one. The last sum in (16) is at most
 ||W||_2^2||alpha||_2^2||beta||_2^2.
Renaming epsilon proves (12).

Because C_lift was explicitly extended to all residues, additive Parseval applies and gives
 sum_p|C_hat_lift(p)|^2=q sum_x|C_lift(x)|^2,
which proves (13).

For the final specialization, assume W is centered. Formula (6) of fact 8592875ae5046498 is the sum over exact determinant rows and the unique u satisfying the first digit congruence. On every admitted tuple this u is exactly the canonical residue in (2), k=(a n_2-A_u)/q is an integer, and the determinant gives the second equation of (2). Define the row gate to vanish off E_lift and on E_lift to equal Gamma at these uniquely determined u,k, multiplied by the indicators of I_c,I_1,I_2 and all retained literal selectors. This gate depends on rows and columns but not on the characters. Multiplication by the separated F(a) gives (4).

glossary.C_hat_lift(p): the additive Fourier transform of C_lift modulo q
glossary.C_lift(x): the coefficient on the residue x retaining the second row window, both columns, the digit, the common lift, and the literal gate
glossary.E_lift: the finite shared-lift incidence set in the one-column IJOP core
glossary.F_per: the periodization modulo q of the separated first-row profile F

21a5411eeb4d6b76.title: SEMIPRIME CROSS-TOTAL-MODULUS CANCELLATION TAX IN THE LITERAL QUAD SOURCE. Assume the hypotheses and notation of fact 2d839168a73eedfa, and put M_0=x/D as in fact a0a35db8dccc10c0. Fix one literal unit-m source tuple (h,m,w) for which v=w-h is positive, the coefficient
21a5411eeb4d6b76.author: slava chan
21a5411eeb4d6b76.statement:
SEMIPRIME CROSS-TOTAL-MODULUS CANCELLATION TAX IN THE LITERAL QUAD SOURCE. Assume the hypotheses and notation of fact 2d839168a73eedfa, and put M_0=x/D as in fact a0a35db8dccc10c0. Fix one literal unit-m source tuple (h,m,w) for which v=w-h is positive, the coefficient
C_src=1_{(m,N)=1} mu(w)mu(v) Omega(m,w,h)
is nonzero, and
P_1=N-mw=pi_crit lambda_sub,   P_2=N-mv=varpi,                         (1)
where pi_crit, lambda_sub, and varpi are primes, pi_crit and lambda_sub are distinct, and
pi_crit>=M_0,   pi_crit>2D.                                           (2)
For divisors q_1|P_1 and q_2|P_2 define the exact two-reflected Mobius-log coefficient
c(q_1,q_2)=C_src mu(q_1)mu(q_2)log(P_1/q_1)log(P_2/q_2),               (3)
and, for each positive integer S, define its total-modulus shell coefficient
C_S=sum_{q_1|P_1,q_2|P_2,[q_1,q_2]=S}c(q_1,q_2).                      (4)
Then
lambda_sub < ((2-alpha)/2)M_0 < M_0,                                  (5)
and the only nonzero shell coefficients are
C_1=C_src log(pi_crit lambda_sub)log(varpi),
C_{pi_crit}=-C_src log(lambda_sub)log(varpi),
C_{lambda_sub}=-C_src log(pi_crit)log(varpi).                          (6)
Consequently
sum_{S>=1}C_S=0= C_src Lambda(P_1)Lambda(P_2),                         (7)
whereas the fixed-total-modulus critical shell square satisfies
sum_{S>=M_0}|C_S|^2 >= |C_src|^2(log lambda_sub)^2(log varpi)^2>0.     (8)
Thus complete von-Mangoldt sibling recombination across total moduli does not pass through the nonnegative fixed-S shell square underlying QUAD-SUPPLIER_A: on the displayed literal source tuple, its cancellation uses S=1, the subcritical shell S=lambda_sub<M_0, and the critical shell S=pi_crit>=M_0. This does not assert that such tuples are abundant, does not give a lower bound for the transformed Gram cal Q_crit, and does not disprove QUAD-SUPPLIER_A. It proves only that any proof of QUAD-SUPPLIER_A must obtain cancellation within the fixed-S transformed rows (or reassemble before the shell square), rather than import the complete cross-S identity Lambda(P_1)=0.
21a5411eeb4d6b76.proof:
Because C_src is nonzero, the factor W(mw/x) inside Omega(m,w,h) is nonzero. The support hypothesis on W in fact 2d839168a73eedfa gives alpha<=mw/x<=beta. Since N=2x,
P_1=N-mw=x(2-mw/x)<=(2-alpha)x.                                      (9)
Equations (1) and (2) therefore give
lambda_sub=P_1/pi_crit < (2-alpha)x/(2D)=((2-alpha)/2)M_0.
The standing hypothesis alpha>1/2 implies (2-alpha)/2<3/4<1, proving (5).

The positive divisors of the prime P_2=varpi are 1 and varpi. If q_2=varpi, then log(P_2/q_2)=log 1=0. Hence every nonzero term in (3) has q_2=1, mu(q_2)=1, and its second logarithmic factor is log(varpi).

The positive divisors of P_1=pi_crit lambda_sub are 1, pi_crit, lambda_sub, and pi_crit lambda_sub. Their Mobius values are respectively 1,-1,-1,1. With q_2=1, their total moduli [q_1,q_2] equal q_1, and their first logarithmic factors are respectively
log(pi_crit lambda_sub), log(lambda_sub), log(pi_crit), log 1.
Multiplication by their Mobius signs, by C_src, and by log(varpi) gives exactly (6); the last divisor gives zero. Terms with q_2=varpi were already shown to vanish, so there are no other nonzero C_S.

Adding the three values in (6) gives
C_src log(varpi)[log(pi_crit lambda_sub)-log(lambda_sub)-log(pi_crit)]=0,
which proves the first equality in (7). The second equality follows directly because P_1 is a product of two distinct primes and hence Lambda(P_1)=0, while P_2 is prime. This is also the semiprime sibling calculation of fact d9eb8f470bce53ac with the unchanged second reflected factor included.

By (2), S=pi_crit occurs in the sum on the left of (8). Every summand there is nonnegative, so retaining that one shell and using (6) gives
sum_{S>=M_0}|C_S|^2 >= |C_{pi_crit}|^2
=|C_src|^2(log lambda_sub)^2(log varpi)^2.
The three displayed numbers are nonzero: C_src is nonzero by assumption and lambda_sub,varpi are primes greater than one. This proves the strict inequality in (8).

Equation (7) is a cancellation between different total moduli, while equation (8) is formed after the coefficients have been separated by total modulus and squared. Such a nonnegative shell square has no cross term between S=1, S=lambda_sub, and S=pi_crit, so (7) cannot imply its smallness. Fact a0a35db8dccc10c0 defines QUAD-SUPPLIER_A by a sum of nonnegative fixed-S transformed Gram quantities after precisely this total-modulus separation. The present calculation occurs before the later transforms and therefore does not lower-bound cal Q_crit; within each transformed fixed-S row further arithmetic cancellation may occur. These observations prove exactly the final scoped conclusion and no stronger claim.

glossary.C_S: the aggregate Mobius-log coefficient of that fixed source tuple over divisor pairs having total modulus S
glossary.C_src: the unchanged nonzero scalar coefficient of one literal unit-m source tuple, including both reflected Mobius signs and every source mask
glossary.lambda_sub: the other, subcritical prime factor of P_1
glossary.pi_crit: the critical large prime factor of the squarefree semiprime reflected value P_1

2223056b02c29f78.title: GA-PRECOPY-COLLAPSE: EXACT RESTORATION OF THE SINGLE PRE-MARKER PHYSICAL ROW AND THE PROJECTED-COMMUTATION BOUNDARY
2223056b02c29f78.author: slava chan
2223056b02c29f78.statement:
GA-PRECOPY-COLLAPSE: EXACT RESTORATION OF THE SINGLE PRE-MARKER PHYSICAL ROW AND THE PROJECTED-COMMUTATION BOUNDARY.

Adopt the complete physical Good-W pre-copy family of fact 5ce54dcef3d61da1. Fix one marked integer n and all the outer data frozen in that fact, and reunite all half-open marked-dilator blocks. Let K_F^base(n) be the physical row obtained from K_F(n,lambda) after removing the scalar terminal-marker coefficient a_lambda(n). Then K_F^base(n) is independent of the terminal child lambda, and
K_F(n,lambda)=a_lambda(n)K_F^base(n).                            (1)
Consequently
K_F^agg(n)=mu(n)K_F^base(n),                                    (2)
|K_F^agg(n)|^2=|K_F^base(n)|^2,                                 (3)
and
M_F^precopy=sum_{B/2<=n<=2B}|K_F^base(n)|^2.                    (4)

More explicitly, every source, target-gcd, fixed-U, high, actual-G, parent, order, equality, collision, deletion, provenance, coprimality, smooth, and projective coordinate named in fact 5ce54dcef3d61da1 is fixed before the terminal marker and is inherited unchanged by every child. The physical reciprocal phase and Fourier amplitude in the row depend on the common n, q, and h, not on the terminal factorization n=d_lambda v_lambda. The only new localization is the marked-dilator block, and its disjoint union has been completely reunited. Thus every one of the named inherited selectors either deletes the whole fixed family or survives on every terminal child; none creates a cross-copy mismatch in (1)-(4).

The scope is exactly the complete physical pre-copy square. A projection that depends on d_lambda or v_lambda need not commute with (2). For example, take L=S=2, Z>5, and n=15. The two A-copies indexed by p=3 and p=5 have coefficients 1/2 and dilators 5 and 3. If their common flat row is X and one inserts the formal selector 1_{d_lambda=5}, the projected terminal sum is X/2 rather than X. Therefore (2)-(4) do not authorize inserting the terminal identity after a copy-dependent hard, principal, centered, or single-dilator projection.

In particular, the aligned physical rows have no relative terminal-marker cancellation: the exact marker restores mu(n), whose modulus disappears in (3). This theorem proves the literal selector classification and the exact physical collapse only. It does not estimate M_F^precopy, does not estimate the F>Q principal source, does not estimate the small-dilator projected-incidence branch, and proves no C-qSRC-BV-SUP, GA-NR-DIL, tail payment, or Goldbach conclusion.
2223056b02c29f78.proof:
Equation (9) of fact e55b27d39c593164 writes the exact physical coefficient as
c_lambda(q,h)=a_lambda(n) mu(q)(H_P/n) Fhat_{q,n}(epsilon_or h/n)
 e(epsilon_or mathscr A h/(qn)) Xi_lambda(q,h,n).                (5)
Fact 5ce54dcef3d61da1 fixes the selected integer, orientation, outer gcd, normalized layer, original source atom, active dyadic label, fixed-U, high, actual-G, parent, target-gcd, source, smooth/projective, ordering, equality, collision, deletion, provenance, and every other frozen coordinate before taking the union over terminal dilator blocks. Fact e55b27d39c593164 states that the terminal re-marker changes none of those data. Hence, at fixed n,q,h, the factor in (5) after a_lambda(n) is removed is common to every terminal child. The physical phase e_q(-mathscr A h n^{-1}) in equation (11) of that fact also depends only on n,q,h. Summing (5) over q,h therefore proves (1), once all dilator blocks are reunited as in fact 5ce54dcef3d61da1.

The terminal marker is an exact pointwise identity. Equivalently, fact f234dbd4fdda994e classifies its fixed-n children and proves that their scalar coefficients sum to mu(n): in the A alternative there are r(n) coefficients each equal to mu(n)/r(n), and in the unique C_j alternative the sole coefficient is mu(n). Summing (1) over lambda therefore proves (2).

The supported n is squarefree, so |mu(n)|=1. Taking squared absolute values in (2) proves (3), and summing (3) over n gives (4) by the definition of M_F^precopy in fact 5ce54dcef3d61da1.

For the scope example, n=15 is squarefree and, when Z>5, its two interval primes are 3 and 5. Fact f234dbd4fdda994e gives coefficient mu(15)/2=1/2 on both A-copies. Their dilators n/3=5 and n/5=3 are distinct. The selector 1_{d_lambda=5} retains exactly one copy, so its selected sum is X/2. This proves that arbitrary copy-dependent projections do not commute with the unprojected identity. No such projection was used in (1)-(4), and all exclusions follow.

glossary.GA-PRECOPY-COLLAPSE: The exact restoration of the pre-marker physical row inside the complete unprojected pre-copy moment.
glossary.K_F^base(n): The common complete physical row at fixed n after removing the terminal scalar and reuniting all dilator blocks.

2234aaf28e165b88.title: EXACT PRIME FACE FUSION AND THE CROSS-INCIDENCE CUTOFF BOUNDARY CORRECTION
2234aaf28e165b88.author: slava chan
2234aaf28e165b88.statement:
EXACT PRIME FACE FUSION AND THE CROSS-INCIDENCE CUTOFF BOUNDARY CORRECTION.

Assume the full actual high-conductor hypotheses and notation of fact 14fe68fdcbfd99ff. Thus b is one of its squarefree moduli, F_0 is its actual cutoff, a is in its actual range, and (a,b)=1. Let b=pq, where p is prime and p does not divide N.

If q>1, let M be the unique integer satisfying
 1<=M<=q,  pM congruent N (mod q).                           (1)
For h|q define
 R^M_{q,h}(a)
  =product_{r|h}
    [e_r(M[a(q/r)]^(-1))+1/(r-1)].                          (2)
For a real cutoff Y>0 define
 P^M_{q,>Y}(a)
  =sum_{h|q;h>Y;(h,M)=1}
    c_{q/h}(M)R^M_{q,h}(a)/phi(q/h),                        (3)
and
 B^M_{q;(F_0/p,F_0]}(a)
  =sum_{h|q;F_0/p<h<=F_0;(h,M)=1}
    c_{q/h}(M)R^M_{q,h}(a)/phi(q/h).                        (4)

If q=1, set M=1 and define
 P^1_{1,>Y}(a)=1_{Y<1},
 B^1_{1;(F_0/p,F_0]}(a)=1_{F_0/p<1<=F_0}.                   (5)
These conventions are the literal h=1 empty-product divisor sums.

Put
 r_{p,b}(a)
  =e_p(N[aq]^(-1))+1/(p-1).                                 (6)
Then the complete high-conductor projector P_b(a) has the exact two-face decomposition
 P_b(a)
  =-1/(p-1)P^M_{q,>F_0}(a)
    +r_{p,b}(a)P^M_{q,>F_0/p}(a).                           (7)
Equivalently,
 P_b(a)
  =e_p(N[aq]^(-1))P^M_{q,>F_0}(a)
    +r_{p,b}(a)B^M_{q;(F_0/p,F_0]}(a).                      (8)
Thus the only correction to pure face fusion is the literal conductor boundary F_0/p<h<=F_0.

For the cross-incidence specialization, let b_1,b_2 be two actual squarefree moduli from fact 14fe68fdcbfd99ff and let a_i be in the actual a-range with (a_i,b_i)=1. Write
 b_1=p_1s_1, b_2=p_2s_2,
where p_i are prime, s_i<F_0, and p_i does not divide N. Assume p_1|s_2 and put
 q_2=b_2/p_1=p_2(s_2/p_1).                                  (9)
If s_1>1, let M_1 satisfy p_1M_1 congruent N modulo s_1; if s_1=1, put M_1=1 and use convention (5). Let M_{12} satisfy p_1M_{12} congruent N modulo q_2. Then
 P_{b_1}(a_1)overline(P_{b_2}(a_2))
 =
 r_{p_1,b_1}(a_1)P^{M_1}_{s_1,>F_0/p_1}(a_1)
 times the complex conjugate of
 {e_{p_1}(N[a_2q_2]^(-1))P^{M_{12}}_{q_2,>F_0}(a_2)
  +r_{p_1,b_2}(a_2)
   B^{M_{12}}_{q_2;(F_0/p_1,F_0]}(a_2)}.                    (10)
Equation (10) retains the full shifted complementary tensor of row one, the full transported high and boundary tensors of row two, and the exact p_1-local factors before any triangle inequality.

No estimate for the fused leading term or boundary correction, no TRI-CROSS or ROP estimate, no CEN-MZB estimate, no C_small estimate and no Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
2234aaf28e165b88.proof:
First assume q>1. Start from the exact projector formula in fact 14fe68fdcbfd99ff:
 P_b(a)
  =sum_{f|b;f>F_0;(f,N)=1}
    c_{b/f}(N)R_{b,f}(a)/phi(b/f).                          (11)
Split its active divisors into those not containing p and those containing p.

If p does not divide f, write f=h with h|q. The conditions are h>F_0 and (h,N)=1. The cofactor is p(q/h). Since p does not divide N,
 c_{p(q/h)}(N)/phi(p(q/h))
 =-1/(p-1) times c_{q/h}(N)/phi(q/h).                       (12)
Target transport by (1), exactly as in fact 9ef4a136053bd1e1, identifies every q-local response with (2), gives (h,N)=1 iff (h,M)=1, and gives c_{q/h}(N)=c_{q/h}(M). Hence the p-out face is
 -1/(p-1)P^M_{q,>F_0}(a).                                  (13)

If p|f, write f=ph with h|q. The conditions become ph>F_0 and (h,N)=1. The p-local response is r_{p,b}(a); target transport gives the same q-response and cofactor as above. Hence the p-in face is
 r_{p,b}(a)P^M_{q,>F_0/p}(a).                              (14)
Adding (13)-(14) proves (7) for q>1.

If q=1, the actual scale has b=p>F_0. The only active conductor is f=p; its cofactor and empty complementary response are one, so P_p(a)=r_{p,p}(a). In convention (5), P^1_{1,>F_0}=0 because F_0>1, while P^1_{1,>F_0/p}=1 because p>F_0. Thus (7) also gives r_{p,p}(a).

For either q, the exact divisor-range partition is
 P^M_{q,>F_0/p}
  =P^M_{q,>F_0}+B^M_{q;(F_0/p,F_0]}.                        (15)
For q=1 this is checked directly from (5); for q>1 it is the disjoint partition of the h-divisors. Definition (6) gives
 r_{p,b}(a)-1/(p-1)=e_p(N[aq]^(-1)).                        (16)
Insert (15) into (7) and use (16), proving (8).

Now consider the cross incidence. Since p_1|s_2 and b_2 is squarefree, b_2=p_1q_2 with q_2 as in (9), q_2>1 and (p_1,q_2)=1. The unit condition (a_2,b_2)=1 makes every inverse in (8) legal. Apply (8) to b_2,p_1,q_2 and M_{12}.

For row one, if s_1>1, facts bab04e002177e282 and 9ef4a136053bd1e1 give
 P_{b_1}(a_1)
  =r_{p_1,b_1}(a_1)P^{M_1}_{s_1,>F_0/p_1}(a_1).             (17)
If s_1=1, then b_1=p_1>F_0, the preceding q=1 argument gives P_{b_1}(a_1)=r_{p_1,b_1}(a_1), and convention (5) gives P^1_{1,>F_0/p_1}=1, so (17) remains true. Multiply (17) by the complex conjugate of (8) for row two. This is exactly (10). All variables satisfy the unit and ambient hypotheses, and no factor has been estimated, proving every retention and scope statement.

glossary.B^M_{q;(F_0/p,F_0]}(a): The exact centered conductor boundary block with F_0/p<h<=F_0.
glossary.P^M_{q,>Y}(a): The complete centered conductor projector on squarefree modulus q, target M, and conductor cutoff Y, with an explicit modulus-one convention.
glossary.prime face fusion: The recombination of the p-out cofactor face and p-in centered-response face.

225b1500e4d495e6.title: Let p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4 be distinct primes greater than 3 and put P=p_1p_2p_3p_4. Use the centered interval-weighted companion definitions M_q,C_q,E_q and Gamma from fact be4e5ad5378f0122. For each i choose an arbitrary integer L_i with 1<=L_i<=p_i-1 and an arbitrary cyclic interval B_i in Z/p_iZ of cardinality L_i. Put X_2=0 and X_3=2^{-1}-3^{-1} modulo P, and for q=2,3 define I_{i,q}=B_i+(X_q modulo p_i). Thus the q=2 and q=3 windows have the same prescribed length and shape in each local coordinate and differ only by one global CRT translation
225b1500e4d495e6.author: slava chan
225b1500e4d495e6.statement:
Let p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4 be distinct primes greater than 3 and put P=p_1p_2p_3p_4. Use the centered interval-weighted companion definitions M_q,C_q,E_q and Gamma from fact be4e5ad5378f0122. For each i choose an arbitrary integer L_i with 1<=L_i<=p_i-1 and an arbitrary cyclic interval B_i in Z/p_iZ of cardinality L_i. Put X_2=0 and X_3=2^{-1}-3^{-1} modulo P, and for q=2,3 define I_{i,q}=B_i+(X_q modulo p_i). Thus the q=2 and q=3 windows have the same prescribed length and shape in each local coordinate and differ only by one global CRT translation.

For a cyclic interval B in Z/pZ define its centered autocorrelation
A_B(t)=|B intersect (B+t)|-|B|^2/p.
Then for every prime p>3 and every nonempty proper cyclic interval B one has
A_B(3^{-1})<0,                                                 (1)
where 3^{-1} is taken modulo p. Define
R=product_{i=1}^4 A_{B_i}(3^{-1} modulo p_i)/A_{B_i}(0).
Then R>0, and the explicit q=2,3 windows above satisfy
||Gamma-I||_op=sqrt((1+R)/2)>1/sqrt(2).                       (2)
Consequently no hypotheses involving only the four local interval lengths or densities, however restrictive inside 1<=L_i<=p_i-1, can imply an o(1) centered companion-flatness estimate if q-dependent translations remain unrestricted. A literal positive theorem must use the arithmetic relation governing q-dependent window locations or an equivalent hypothesis excluding the displayed alignment. This is a universal translated-interval companion countermodel, not an arithmetic PAVG27 counterexample and not a counterexample to a fully specified WF-RPS window family.
225b1500e4d495e6.proof:
First prove the local sign assertion. Translation of B does not change its autocorrelation, so write B={0,1,...,L-1} modulo p, where 1<=L<=p-1. Every prime p>3 is congruent to 1 or -1 modulo 6. Let a=3^{-1} modulo p and let d=min(a,p-a), using representatives between 1 and p-1. If p=6k+1 then a=4k+1 and d=2k=(p-1)/3. If p=6k-1 then a=2k and d=2k=(p+1)/3. In either case
p/4<d<p/2.                                                   (3)
The overlap of two length-L cyclic intervals separated by cyclic distance d is
|B intersect (B+a)|=max(0,L-d)+max(0,L-(p-d)).               (4)
There are three ranges.

If L<=d, (4) is zero, so A_B(a)=-L^2/p<0.
If d<L<=p-d, (4) is L-d, so
A_B(a)=L-d-L^2/p=L(p-L)/p-d<=p/4-d<0,
where L(p-L)<=p^2/4 and (3) were used.
If p-d<L<p, (4) is 2L-p, so
A_B(a)=2L-p-L^2/p=-(p-L)^2/p<0.
This proves (1). Also A_B(0)=L-L^2/p=L(p-L)/p>0.

Now let f_i be the centered indicator of B_i, let fhat_i be its additive Fourier transform, and define
M_0(h)=product_{i=1}^4 fhat_i(rho_i(h)),
with rho_i as in fact be4e5ad5378f0122. Translating B_i by X_q modulo p_i multiplies fhat_i(rho_i(h)) by e_{p_i}(-rho_i(h)X_q), so CRT gives
M_q(h)=M_0(h)e_P(-hX_q).                                    (5)
The number S=sum_h|M_0(h)|^2 is positive. Indeed, CRT supplies an h with rho_i(h)=1 for all i, and at this h every factor
fhat_i(1)=sum_{x in B_i}e_{p_i}(-x)
is nonzero: after translating B_i this is a nonzero phase times a geometric sum of length L_i strictly between zero and p_i.

Using X_2=0 and X_3=2^{-1}-3^{-1}, the q=2 and q=3 columns can be written
C_2=x,
C_3=x+y,
where
x(h)=M_0(h)e_P(-h2^{-1}),
y(h)=M_0(h)e_P(-h(2^{-1}+3^{-1})).                           (6)
Thus ||x||^2=||y||^2=S and
<x,y>=sum_h|M_0(h)|^2e_P(-h3^{-1}).                         (7)
The exact CRT collision factorization in fact be4e5ad5378f0122, applied to the same base interval in both local slots, gives
S=P product_i A_{B_i}(0)
and
<x,y>=P product_i A_{B_i}(-3^{-1} modulo p_i).
Autocorrelation is even, so (1) shows that all four factors in the second product are negative. Therefore
<x,y>/S=product_i A_{B_i}(3^{-1})/A_{B_i}(0)=R>0.           (8)

It follows from (6)-(8) that
E_2=S,
E_3=2S(1+R),
<C_2,C_3>=S(1+R).
The normalized off-diagonal Gram entry consequently has modulus sqrt((1+R)/2), which is strictly larger than 1/sqrt(2). Since a two-by-two normalized Hermitian Gram has diagonal entries one, this modulus equals ||Gamma-I||_op. This proves (2), the universal failure of length-only hypotheses, and all stated scope limitations.

glossary.A_B: the centered cyclic autocorrelation of the interval B
glossary.B_i: an arbitrary nonempty proper base cyclic interval at the prime p_i
glossary.universal translated-interval companion: the aligned q=2,3 construction valid for every nontrivial choice of local interval lengths

2290690807ca8ff2.title: SCALAR SQUAREFREE-q COMPLETION FOR DISTINCT CENTERED ACTIVE PRODUCTS, WITH AUXILIARY COPRIMALITY AND SHARED-PRIME COLLISIONS. Fix positive integers J and A_0 and a continuously differentiable function psi supported in [1,2]. Let Q>=2. Let M divide N, where N is squarefree, 2<=M<=N<=Q^{A_0}, and omega(N)<=J. If gcd(C,M)=1, then
2290690807ca8ff2.author: slava chan
2290690807ca8ff2.statement:
SCALAR SQUAREFREE-q COMPLETION FOR DISTINCT CENTERED ACTIVE PRODUCTS, WITH AUXILIARY COPRIMALITY AND SHARED-PRIME COLLISIONS. Fix positive integers J and A_0 and a continuously differentiable function psi supported in [1,2]. Let Q>=2. Let M divide N, where N is squarefree, 2<=M<=N<=Q^{A_0}, and omega(N)<=J. If gcd(C,M)=1, then

 |sum_{q>=1,gcd(q,N)=1}mu(q)^2psi(q/Q)e_M(Cq^{-1})|
 <<_{J,A_0,psi,epsilon}Q^epsilon[Q/M+Q^{1/2}M^{1/4}].               (1)

The Q/M term records the complete-period contribution in the proof; no lower bound or sharpness assertion is made. If M=N>=Q^{2/5}, this term is dominated by the second term.

Let r and r' be distinct nonempty squarefree integers, with omega(r),omega(r')<=2, and put L_0=lcm(r,r'). For every p|r choose C_p nonzero modulo p, and for every p|r' choose C'_p nonzero modulo p. On integers q define

 Phi_r(q)=product_{p|r}[1_{p does not divide q}e_p(C_pq^{-1})+1/p],
 Phi'_{r'}(q)=product_{p|r'}[1_{p does not divide q}e_p(C'_pq^{-1})+1/p].  (2)

Assume C_p is not congruent to C'_p modulo p for every p|gcd(r,r'). Then, whenever L_0<=Q^{A_0},

 |sum_{q>=1,gcd(q,L_0)=1}mu(q)^2psi(q/Q)Phi_r(q)conjugate(Phi'_{r'}(q))|
 <<_{A_0,psi,epsilon}Q^epsilon[Q/L_0+Q^{1/2}L_0^{1/4}].             (3)

In the literal same-target C4 specialization of facts 3330e83b6d253b69 and df97bf1eba0495be, the excluded equality C_p=C'_p at a shared active prime p is exactly the accepted square-divisor collision p^2|hn'-h'n. Hence (3) applies uniformly off every shared-prime collision. Because r and r' are distinct and nonempty, their union contains at least two primes. In the natural C4 range of fact 67d49768ecdc058e these primes are at least Z=Q^{3/2-beta-3sigma}, beta<6/5, so L_0>=Z^2>Q^{2/5} for sufficiently large Q under its fixed small sigma; consequently (3) is then

 <<Q^epsilon Q^{1/2}L_0^{1/4}.                                     (4)

Equations (1)-(4) are scalar common-output estimates. They retain the common mu(q)^2 weight, the full auxiliary coprimality gcd(q,L_0)=1, and every local centered constant. They do not permit summing literal row pairs absolutely, remove the exact row-dependent small-v phases or source masks, or prove the vector partner-multiplier inequality, C4-VEC, another anatomy bound, or Goldbach.
2290690807ca8ff2.proof:
First consider a squarefree modulus M with omega(M)<=J and a unit C modulo M. Put
 g_{M,C}(x)=1_{gcd(x,M)=1}e_M(Cx^{-1})
for residues x modulo M. For t modulo M, its unnormalized complete additive transform is
 K_{M,C}(t)=sum_{x mod M,gcd(x,M)=1}e_M(Cx^{-1}+tx).                  (5)
Chinese remaindering factors (5) into one prime-local sum for each p|M, after multiplication of C and t by CRT units. The local inverse coefficient remains nonzero. If the local additive coefficient is zero, inversion gives -1. If it is nonzero, fact 4f9aec67f5be35db, after undoing its normalization, bounds the local Kloosterman sum by 2sqrt(p). Therefore
 |K_{M,C}(t)|<=2^{omega(M)}sqrt(M)<=2^Jsqrt(M).                      (6)

Let I be any interval of at most M consecutive residues. Fourier inversion of its indicator gives
 sum_{x in I mod M}g_{M,C}(x)
 =M^{-1}sum_{t mod M}widehat{1_I}(t)K_{M,C}(-t).                     (7)
The geometric-series formula gives
 sum_{t mod M}|widehat{1_I}(t)|<<M log(2M):                          (8)
the zero term is at most M, and for centered representatives 1<=|t|<=M/2 each other term is at most min(|I|,M/(2|t|)). Thus every incomplete period is O_J(sqrt(M)log(2M)). A complete period is K_{M,C}(0)=mu(M). Hence a prefix of length Y has absolute sum
 <<_J Y/M+sqrt(M)log(2M),                                           (9)
and also the trivial bound O(Y+1). Partial summation, using the support of psi, gives, for X>0 whenever the summation range is nonempty,
 |sum_{m>=1,gcd(m,M)=1}psi(m/X)e_M(Cm^{-1})|
 <<_{J,psi}X/M+min(X,sqrt(M)log(2M)).                               (10)
If the range is empty the same assertion is immediate.

We now retain the stronger auxiliary coprimality by N. Use
 mu(q)^2=sum_{k^2|q}mu(k).                                          (11)
After q=k^2m, gcd(q,N)=1 implies gcd(k,N)=1 and gcd(m,N)=1. Since N is squarefree and M|N, M and N/M are coprime and
 1_{gcd(m,N)=1}=1_{gcd(m,M)=1}
   sum_{ell|N/M, ell|m}mu(ell).                                     (12)
For one ell in (12), write m=ell n. Both k and ell are units modulo M, the phase becomes
 e_M(Ck^{-2}ell^{-1}n^{-1}),                                       (13)
and the smooth length is X=Q/(k^2ell). Apply (10). Since N has at most J prime factors, the number of ell is at most 2^J. Taking absolute values over k and ell gives the left side of (1) at most
 <<_{J,psi} sum_{ell|N/M}sum_{k<=sqrt(2Q/ell)}
 [Q/(k^2ell M)+min(Q/(k^2ell),sqrt(M)log(2M))].                      (14)
The first part is O_J(Q/M). For fixed ell put R=sqrt(M)log(2M) and split the second k-sum at (Q/(ell R))^{1/2}. The two ranges contribute O(sqrt(QR/ell)); summing the at most 2^J divisors ell gives O_J(sqrt(QR)). Because N<=Q^{A_0}, logarithms are absorbed by Q^epsilon, yielding Q^epsilon Q^{1/2}M^{1/4}. This proves (1). For M=N, Q/M<=Q^{1/2}M^{1/4} exactly when M>=Q^{2/5}.

On the imposed unit support in (3), every p-local factor of Phi_r is e_p(C_pq^{-1})+1/p and every conjugated p-local factor of Phi'_{r'} is e_p(-C'_pq^{-1})+1/p. Expand their product. At p in the symmetric difference, the two choices are one unit inverse phase with coefficient one or the constant 1/p. At a shared p the four choices are
 e_p((C_p-C'_p)q^{-1}),
 p^{-1}e_p(C_pq^{-1}),
 p^{-1}e_p(-C'_pq^{-1}),
 p^{-2}.                                                            (15)
Every displayed phase numerator is nonzero by the hypotheses. Hence every global expansion term is either constant or has the form
 c_Te_{L_T}(C_Tq^{-1}),                                             (16)
where L_T|L_0 is squarefree, gcd(C_T,L_T)=1, and
 |c_T|<=L_T/L_0.                                                    (17)
Indeed every prime of L_0 absent from L_T contributes at least one factor 1/p; coefficients 1/p attached to a still-active shared-prime phase only strengthen (17).

If L_T=1, the retained restriction gcd(q,L_0)=1 and a trivial count give
 |c_T sum_q mu(q)^2psi(q/Q)1_{gcd(q,L_0)=1}|<<Q/L_0.                (18)
If L_T>1, apply the auxiliary-coprimality form (1) with M=L_T and N=L_0, and then (17):
 |c_T|[Q/L_T+Q^{1/2}L_T^{1/4}]
 <=Q/L_0+Q^{1/2}L_0^{1/4}.                                        (19)
There are only an absolute number of local choices, so (18)-(19) prove (3).

Fact df97bf1eba0495be identifies equality of the two literal shared-prime slopes with p^2|hn'-h'n; these slopes are the parameters in the centered factors of fact 3330e83b6d253b69. Finally, distinct nonempty r,r' have at least two primes in their union. Fact 67d49768ecdc058e gives their natural lower bound. Since beta<6/5 and sigma is fixed sufficiently small there, 3-2beta-6sigma>2/5. Thus L_0>=Z^2>Q^{2/5}, and (4) follows. The final limitations are operations absent from the scalar argument.

glossary.BV(psi): The fixed bounded-variation norm sup|psi| plus the integral of |psi'|.
glossary.L_T: The effective reciprocal modulus of one term in the centered-face product expansion.
glossary.c_T: The coefficient of one term in the centered-face product expansion.

22ee06fc82829016.title: COMPLETE LITERAL STRICT-TOP SHORT-\(A_X\) TYPE-I PAYMENT BY THE VARIABLE-AMPLITUDE CONSUMER. Retain the notation and complete strict-top unmarked source of facts \(f26c5b12eea4a623\) and \(391896a807980083\). Thus
22ee06fc82829016.author: slava chan
22ee06fc82829016.statement:
COMPLETE LITERAL STRICT-TOP SHORT-\(A_X\) TYPE-I PAYMENT BY THE VARIABLE-AMPLITUDE CONSUMER. Retain the notation and complete strict-top unmarked source of facts \(f26c5b12eea4a623\) and \(391896a807980083\). Thus
\[
 \beta_m<\beta<6/5,\qquad B=Q^\beta,\qquad
 a=2\beta-2+\tau,\qquad 0<\tau<1/100,
\]
and the remaining \(A_X\) Type-I rows are
\[
 -\sum_{\substack{rw=n\\r<Q^a}}\mu(r).                         \tag{1}
\]
Let \({\cal T}_{A_X,\rm short}\) be their complete contribution to the selected strict-top unmarked source, over both orientations, all active source rows, all nonzero frequencies and both signs, and all exact outer gcds \(g\mid N\), with every provenance sibling recombined before estimation.

There exists a fixed \(\delta_I>0\) such that
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 |{\cal T}_{A_X,\rm short}|\ll x^{1-\delta_I}.
 \qquad}                                                       \tag{2}
\]

The literal match to fact \(8138369f26f88aad\) is as follows. Fix a dyadic short-factor box
\[
 L\le r<2L,\qquad L<Q^a,
\]
and a dyadic long-factor box
\[
 M_1\le w<2M_1,\qquad LM_1\asymp B.                            \tag{3}
\]
The reciprocal modulus in that fact is the original \(s\asymp Q\); its short variable is \(l=r\), its long variable is \(m=w\), its fixed target is
\[
 A_0=-\epsilon L_{\rm src},\qquad L_{\rm src}=N/g,             \tag{4}
\]
and its auxiliary core is the exact outer gcd \(g\). The arithmetic conditions are exactly
\[
 (rw,s)=1,\qquad(rw,g)=1,                                      \tag{5}
\]
which are the two conditions \((lm,q)=1,(lm,g)=1\) in fact \(8138369f26f88aad\). The short coefficient is \(-\mu(r)\), both frequency signs are retained, and no coprimality of \(A_0h\) with \(s\) is imposed.

For a dyadic frequency block \(F\le |h|<2F\), the literal long-variable amplitude, including the physical Fourier coefficient and the Archimedean reciprocity phase but not the reciprocal phase modulo \(s\), has a continuously differentiable extension
\[
 {\cal W}_{s,r,h}(y)
 =\chi_{M_1}(y)\,{H_P\over ry}\,
 \widehat F^\epsilon_{g,s,ry}(\epsilon h/(ry))
 e\!\left({\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\over sry}\right),             \tag{6}
\]
where \(\chi_{M_1}\) is one member of a fixed smooth dyadic partition supported in \([M_1,2M_1]\). For every fixed \(A>0\), uniformly in the row,
\[
 \|{\cal W}_{s,r,h}\|_\infty+
 \int_{M_1}^{2M_1}|{\cal W}'_{s,r,h}(y)|\,dy
 \ll_A(\log x)^C(1+F/H_P)^{-A}                                \tag{7}
\]
for a fixed \(C\). Thus (7) is the variation parameter \({\cal V}\) required by fact \(8138369f26f88aad\); it may depend on \(s,r,h\) exactly as that theorem permits.

After converting its \(F^{-1}\) frequency average to the literal \(H_P^{-1}\) normalization, fact \(8138369f26f88aad\) gives the block bound
\[
 {F\over H_P}(\log x)^C(1+F/H_P)^{-A}Q^{o(1)}
 \left(B+Q^{3/2}L\right).                                      \tag{8}
\]
The short-factor exponent is load-bearing:
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 Q^{3/2}L
 \le Q^{3/2+a}
 =Q^{\,2\beta-1/2+\tau}
 <Q^{\,19/10+\tau}
 <Q^{\,2-\delta_*},
 \quad}                                                        \tag{9}
\]
where one may take any fixed \(0<\delta_*<1/10-\tau\). Also \(LM_1\asymp B=Q^\beta\ll Q^{2-\delta_*}\). The dyadic \(F\)-sum of the prefactor in (8) is bounded for \(A>2\), including \(H_P<1\). Frequencies beyond a sufficiently large fixed power of \(Q\) are paid absolutely by the same arbitrary-order decay in (7). Therefore every fixed outer-\(g\) row has size
\[
 O(Q^{2-\delta_0})
\]
for a fixed \(\delta_0>0\), after all factor boxes and source labels are summed.

This theorem applies, rather than reproves, the Type-I estimate \(8138369f26f88aad\). It pays no ULTRA-LONG-MU-\(N\), no ENDPOINT-DIAGONAL-\(N\), no critical \(\beta\ge6/5\) source, and no Goldbach conclusion.
22ee06fc82829016.proof:
We first prove the long-variable variation assertion (7). Let \(T_\epsilon\) denote the physical complementary scale: \(T_\epsilon=M_{\rm phys}\) in the forward orientation and \(T_\epsilon=K_{\rm phys}\) in the reverse orientation. Then
\[
 H_P=B/T_\epsilon.
\]
In the Fourier integral defining (6), write
\[
 t=T_\epsilon u,\qquad ry=Bv,\qquad s=Qq,\qquad z=h/H_P.
\]
On the literal source support, \(q,v,u\) range in fixed compact sets with \(v\) bounded away from zero. The exact formula in fact \(b0a38f5e9ae7feb6\) turns the coefficient in (6), apart from the fixed smooth dyadic cutoff, into
\[
 {1\over v}\int {\mathfrak W}_\epsilon(q,v,u)
 e(-\epsilon zu/v)\,du\,
 e\!\left({\epsilon\lambda_\epsilon z\over qv}\right),          \tag{10}
\]
where \({\mathfrak W}_\epsilon\) is a fixed-complexity compactly supported smooth function carrying the two source logarithms and the literal \(W,\psi,\Phi\) factors, and
\[
 \lambda_+=N/(DM_{\rm phys}),\qquad
 \lambda_-=N/(R K_{\rm phys}).                                 \tag{11}
\]
The physical balances \(DM_{\rm phys}\asymp N\) and
\(RK_{\rm phys}\asymp N\) make (11) bounded above and away from infinity uniformly. Every fixed derivative of \({\mathfrak W}_\epsilon\) is bounded by a fixed power of \(\log x\).

Differentiate (10) zero or one time by \(v\partial_v\). For \(|z|\le1\), direct differentiation gives \(O((\log x)^C)\). For \(|z|>1\), integrate by parts in \(u\) an arbitrary fixed number of times, after the \(v\)-derivative is taken. Compact support removes boundary terms; each integration supplies \(|z|^{-1}\), while the derivative of the phase contributes only a fixed polynomial in \(|z|\). Choosing sufficiently many integrations proves
\[
 |{\cal W}_{s,r,h}(y)|+
 |y{\cal W}'_{s,r,h}(y)|
 \ll_A(\log x)^C(1+|h|/H_P)^{-A}.                              \tag{12}
\]
On \(M_1\le y<2M_1\), integration of the second term in (12) against \(dy/y\), together with the fixed smooth cutoff derivative, proves (7). This is the literal physical amplitude; fact \(544c7ba4db45c06f\) ensures that no unrecombined provenance selector multiplies it.

We now match fact \(8138369f26f88aad\). Substitute (1) in the exact row of fact \(b0a38f5e9ae7feb6\), and fix the boxes (3). The modulus coefficient \(\mu(s){\bf1}_{(s,g)=1}\) has absolute value at most one and may be discarded only after the theorem's \(s\)-wise absolute value. Put
\[
 \alpha_r=-\mu(r){\bf1}_{(r,g)=1},\qquad \nu_h=1
\]
on the fixed signed frequency block. The remaining core gate is
\({\bf1}_{(w,g)=1}\), so together they give \((rw,g)=1\). The source gate \((s,rw)=1\) is (5). The reciprocal phase is
\[
 e_s\!\left(-\epsilon L_{\rm src}h(rw)^{-1}\right),
\]
which is (4) in the notation of fact \(8138369f26f88aad\). That theorem explicitly allows a nonunit \(A_0\), both signs, and arbitrary \(s,r,h\)-dependence of the amplitude (6).

Its normalized form is
\[
 {1\over F}\sum_{F\le|h|<2F}\sum_{s\asymp Q}
 \left|\sum_{r,w}\cdots\right|.
\]
Triangle inequality in \(h\) converts the literal prefactor \(H_P^{-1}\) to \(F/H_P\) times this expression. Apply its bound (4) with the variation (7) and \(LM_1\asymp B\). This proves (8).

For completeness, the scale hypotheses of its power-saving corollary also hold with a fixed margin. Since \(\beta<6/5\),
\[
 LM_1\asymp Q^\beta\le Q^{2-\tau_I}
\]
for some fixed \(\tau_I>0\). Moreover
\[
 L<Q^a,\qquad
 a=2\beta-2+\tau<2/5+\tau<1/2-\tau_I
\]
after choosing, for example, a sufficiently small fixed
\(\tau_I<1/20-\tau\). Finally (7) is polylogarithmic on natural blocks and hence at most \(Q^{\tau_I/4}\) for large \(Q\). The sharper exponent obtained directly from the general bound is (9).

For dyadic \(F\), put \(u_F=F/H_P\). If \(H_P\ge1\), the dyadic sum over \(F\le H_P\) of \(u_F\) is a bounded geometric series, and the sum over \(F>H_P\) of
\(u_F(1+u_F)^{-A}\) converges for \(A>2\). If \(H_P<1\), every \(u_F>1\) and the same tail series is bounded. The theorem requires \(F\) to be bounded by a fixed power of \(Q\). Facts \(be94f5e014ad4d3d\) and \(f26c5b12eea4a623\) give \(Q\ge x^{c_0}\) and polynomial bounds for \(g,L_{\rm src},H_P\) and the source scales, so all blocks \(F\le Q^{C_F}\) fit its size hypothesis for a fixed \(C_F\). For \(F>Q^{C_F}\), use (7), triangle inequality, and the trivial counts \(O(Q)\) for \(s\) and \(O(Bx^{o(1)})\) for the factor pairs. Choosing \(A\) and then \(C_F\) sufficiently large makes the complete far tail \(O(x^{-10})\). This proves the fixed-row \(Q^{2-\delta_0}\) bound after the polylogarithmically many factor boxes.

Finally sum exact outer gcds. In either orientation write \(D_{\rm sm}\) for the smaller physical divisor scale. Then
\[
 Q=D_{\rm sm}/g,\qquad D_{\rm sm}\ll x^{1/2}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \sum_{g\mid N}Q^{2-\delta_0}
 \le D_{\rm sm}^{\,2-\delta_0}
 \sum_{g\mid N}g^{-2+\delta_0}
 \ll x^{1-\delta_0/2+o(1)}.                                    \tag{13}
\]
The two orientations and active source labels cost only \(x^{o(1)}\). Decreasing the exponent proves (2).

glossary.T_epsilon: The physical complementary scale M_phys forward and K_phys reverse.
glossary.cal T_{A_X,short}: The complete strict-top unmarked contribution of the A_X rows whose original coefficient-bearing factor r is smaller than Q^a.
glossary.cal W_{s,r,h}: The literal long-variable physical amplitude used in the variable-amplitude Type-I theorem, including the Fourier and Archimedean factors.
glossary.delta_*: A fixed local exponent margin smaller than 1/10-tau.
glossary.delta_I: A fixed positive saving exponent for the complete literal short-A_X contribution.

2301d9c5068afddd.title: FULL DYADIC AND FACTOR-BOX AGGREGATION TAX FOR THE ZHANG-ELIGIBLE GIANT1 HC-MED ROW. Fix A_0>0 and epsilon>0, and assume the hypotheses and notation of facts edabb9a0d2959b41, 52e1736c39e88aee and 487a65cdbb7ab2fc for one fixed literal h-row and one complete frozen source block. In particular
2301d9c5068afddd.author: slava chan
2301d9c5068afddd.statement:
