FULL DYADIC AND FACTOR-BOX AGGREGATION TAX FOR THE ZHANG-ELIGIBLE GIANT1 HC-MED ROW. Fix A_0>0 and epsilon>0, and assume the hypotheses and notation of facts edabb9a0d2959b41, 52e1736c39e88aee and 487a65cdbb7ab2fc for one fixed literal h-row and one complete frozen source block. In particular
Q_c=X^(1/2+delta_h),  delta_h>=0,  0<eta<=1/4,
X^eta<=d<=X^(1/4+eta),  d<=m,  X<=dm<2X,
and on GIANT1
m=ap,  P^+(a)<P_-,  p>=H.
Let log_2^+(y)=max(0,log y/log 2). Let cal D, cal M and cal P be the sets of powers of two D_0,M_m,P for which respectively an inherited cutoff Psi_{D_0}(d), an inherited cutoff Psi_{M_m}(m), or a giant-prime interval P<p<=2P is nonzero on at least one retained GIANT1 tuple. For each P let cal V(P) be the set of powers of two M_v for which M_v<v=da<=2M_v occurs. Put
N_D=#cal D,  N_M=#cal M,  N_P=#cal P,  N_V(P)=#cal V(P).
Then
N_D<=3+(1/4)log_2 X,                                           (1)
N_M<=4+(1/2-eta)log_2 X,                                       (2)
N_P<=2+log_2^+(2X^(1-eta)/H),                                  (3)
N_V(P)<=3.                                                       (4)

For the canonical Zhang boxes of fact 487a65cdbb7ab2fc,
N_Z(P)<=3(1+log_2 Q_c).                                        (5)
Let
N_Z^*=3(1+log_2 Q_c),
L_proj^*=max L_proj,G1,
L_W^*=max L_W,G1,
where the maxima run over the nonempty cells
(P,D_0,M_m,M_v) in cal P times cal D times cal M times cal V(P);
an empty maximum is zero. Define
Omega_H(c_*)=#{r:r is prime, r|c_*, r>=H},
L_log=1+log(2XQ_c).
For each literal modulus s, let
U_s^{G1,Z}
 =sum_{P in cal P:s in cal S_Z(P)}
   sum_{D_0 in cal D, M_m in cal M, M_v in cal V(P)}
 U_s^{G1}(P;D_0,M_m,M_v),                                      (6)
where an absent cell contributes zero. Then
sum_s |U_s^{G1,Z}|
 <<_{A_0,epsilon}
 3N_DN_M N_PN_Z^* L_proj^* X(log X)^(-A_0)
 +3N_DN_M N_Z^* L_W^* Omega_H(c_*)
 [XH^(-1)L_log^3+Q_c sqrt(X/H)L_log^2].                         (7)
Equation (6) is exactly the complete Zhang-eligible GIANT1 projection of this fixed h-row and frozen source block: the smooth D_0,M_m partitions sum to one, while the P and M_v intervals are disjoint. Thus (7) is a complete consumer-level aggregation of all eligible GIANT1 cells, not a single-cell statement.

The compatible-window definition of H in fact 52e1736c39e88aee gives
H>X^(1/2-3delta_h)(log X)^(-C),                                 (8)
and hence the deletion bracket in (7) is at most
X^(1/2+3delta_h)(log X)^(C+3)
 +X^(3/4+(5/2)delta_h)(log X)^(C/2+2),                          (9)
up to the harmless replacement of powers of log X by the displayed L_log powers. The compatible-window nonemptiness also implies
X^(1/10-9delta_h)>=(log X)^(3C),                                (10)
so both powers in (9) are strictly smaller than X by a fixed power whenever delta_h stays in a fixed closed subinterval of [0,1/90). Therefore the entire explicit prime-unit deletion remains a fixed-power-saving error after the O((log X)^3) cell tax and the O(log Q_c) box tax, provided Omega_H(c_*) and L_W^* have at most fixed polylogarithmic size.

More precisely, the main term in (7) has only the explicit tax
O(N_DN_MN_PN_Z^* L_proj^*)=O((log X)^4 L_proj^*).               (11)
Consequently, if on a family of such rows log x<<log X and
L_proj^*<<(log x)^(C_G1), then choosing A_0>A+C_G1+4 times the fixed comparison constant yields
sum_s|U_s^{G1,Z}|<<X(log X)^(-A)
plus the fixed-power deletion in (7), for every prescribed A>0.

The exact complementary GIANT1 projection consists of the same dyadic cells with s not in cal S_Z(P), equivalently no ordered factorization of s lies in any (P,epsilon)-admissible Zhang box. It is not estimated here. The boundary eta-6delta_h=o(1), SMOOTH, MS-FIRST-NOSCALE, every noneligible GIANT1 row, other HC sectors, the complete critical tail and Goldbach are not asserted.
2301d9c5068afddd.proof:
The cutoff Psi_D(d)=Psi(d/D) in fact edabb9a0d2959b41 is supported only when D/2<d<2D. On HC-MED, X^eta<=d<=X^(1/4+eta), so every active D_0 satisfies
X^eta/2<D_0<2X^(1/4+eta).
The ratio of the endpoints is 4X^(1/4), and the number of powers of two in such an interval is at most 3+(1/4)log_2 X. This proves (1).

Because d<=m and dm>=X, one has m>=sqrt X. Since d>=X^eta and dm<2X, one has m<2X^(1-eta). An active inherited m-cutoff therefore satisfies
sqrt X/2<M_m<4X^(1-eta).
The endpoint ratio is 8X^(1/2-eta), which proves (2).

On GIANT1, p<=m<2X^(1-eta). The number H is a power of two, because H=2P_+ and P_+ is a power of two. Since a prime p>=H cannot equal H for sufficiently large X, the disjoint half-open dyadic intervals P<p<=2P with powers of two P>=H cover every possible giant prime uniquely. Nonemptiness forces H<=P<2X^(1-eta), giving (3).

For a fixed P, dm=pv with P<p<=2P and X<=dm<2X gives
X/(2P)<=v<2X/P.
The ratio of these endpoints is four. A half-open dyadic v-block M_v<v<=2M_v can meet this range only if X/(4P)<=M_v<2X/P. This power-of-two interval has endpoint ratio eight, so it contains at most three powers of two. This proves (4).

Fix a nonempty Zhang box alpha=(Q_1,Q_2). It contains a selected modulus
s=q_1q_2 in [Q_c,2Q_c), with Q_i<q_i<=2Q_i. Hence
Q_c/4<=Q_1Q_2<2Q_c.                                            (12)
For fixed Q_1, equation (12) confines Q_2 to an interval of endpoint ratio eight, containing at most three powers of two. Also Q_2>=2 and Q_1Q_2<2Q_c imply Q_1<Q_c. There are at most 1+log_2 Q_c possible powers Q_1>=2. This proves (5). Notice that admissibility can only decrease the count.

Insert both exact smooth partitions of unity from fact edabb9a0d2959b41. On GIANT1, additionally insert the disjoint dyadic partition of the unique giant prime p and the disjoint half-open dyadic partition of v=da. Therefore (6) restores exactly every Zhang-eligible GIANT1 tuple, with its original smooth weights, and restores no ineligible tuple. Smooth cutoff supports can overlap, but their weighted sums equal one; the triangle inequality over their finitely many labels costs N_DN_M and does not change any coefficient identity.

Apply equation (17) of fact 487a65cdbb7ab2fc to every nonempty cell and sum. Its main contribution is at most the first term of (7), using N_V(P)<=3, N_Z(P)<=N_Z^*, and the definitions of the two maxima.

For the prime-unit deletion, the P-intervals are disjoint. Thus
sum_{P in cal P} omega_P(c_*)<=Omega_H(c_*).                    (13)
Since P>=H,
sum_P omega_P(c_*)/P<=Omega_H(c_*)/H,
sum_P omega_P(c_*)/sqrt(P)<=Omega_H(c_*)/sqrt(H).               (14)
Using (4), (5), (13)-(14) in the deletion part of the fixed-cell bound gives the second term of (7). This proves the aggregation estimate.

Fact 52e1736c39e88aee gives H>U_P with
U_P=X^(1/2-3delta_h)(log X)^(-C),
which is (8). Substitution in X/H and Q_c sqrt(X/H), using Q_c=X^(1/2+delta_h), gives the two powers and logarithmic factors in (9). The same fact proves (10). In particular delta_h<1/90 for all sufficiently large X, and on a fixed closed subinterval of [0,1/90) the gaps
1-(1/2+3delta_h) and 1-(3/4+(5/2)delta_h)
are positive constants. Multiplication by fixed powers of logarithms preserves a fixed power saving. Equations (1)-(5) prove (11), and the stated arbitrary-logarithmic-saving corollary follows by choosing the input exponent A_0 after the fixed tax.

Finally, by definition cal S_Z(P) contains exactly the moduli admitting at least one admissible factorization at P. Its set-theoretic complement is therefore exactly the asserted no-box projection. No estimate for that complement was used.

glossary.L_W^*: The maximum fixed-cell GIANT1 pointwise divisor-bound constant over the active eligible aggregation.
glossary.L_proj^*: The maximum fixed-cell GIANT1 projective norm over the active eligible aggregation.
glossary.N_Z^*: The uniform upper bound 3(1+log_2 Q_c) for the number of nonempty Zhang boxes.
glossary.Omega_H(c_*): The number of distinct prime divisors of c_* that are at least H.
glossary.U_s^{G1,Z}: The fully aggregated Zhang-eligible GIANT1 centered row for one fixed h-row and frozen source block.
glossary.cal D: The active inherited smooth dyadic labels D_0 for the HC smaller factor d.
glossary.cal M: The active inherited smooth dyadic labels M_m for the original HC larger factor m.
glossary.cal P: The active dyadic giant-prime scales P.
glossary.cal V(P): The active folded-cofactor dyadic labels M_v at prime scale P.

2359a25d9fc6dd9b.title: DIVISOR COMPRESSION OF EQUAL RATIONAL SOURCE PHASES
2359a25d9fc6dd9b.author: slava chan
2359a25d9fc6dd9b.statement:
DIVISOR COMPRESSION OF EQUAL RATIONAL SOURCE PHASES.

Fix a constant C>=1 and Q>=2. Let A be a nonzero integer with |A|<=Q^C. Let v,p be positive integers, and let cal X be any finite set of triples x=(q,m,k) of integers satisfying
  Q<=q<2Q,  Q<=m<2Q,  qm+vpk=A.                            (1)
Define the rational source phase
  alpha(x)=k/q.                                             (2)
Then every rational number alpha has at most tau(|A|) preimages in cal X. Consequently, for every epsilon>0,
  max_{alpha in Q} #{x in cal X:alpha(x)=alpha}
  <<_{C,epsilon}Q^epsilon.                                  (3)

More precisely, write alpha=r/t in lowest terms with t>0 and gcd(|r|,t)=1, using r=0,t=1 for alpha=0. Every x in the alpha-fibre is uniquely determined by a positive divisor d of |A| through
  q=td,  k=rd,  m=(A/d-vpr)/t,                              (4)
provided the displayed quantities are integral and satisfy the support conditions. Conversely every positive divisor d producing admissible quantities in (4) gives one source triple in the fibre.

If c_x are arbitrary complex coefficients on cal X and
  C_alpha=sum_{x in cal X:alpha(x)=alpha}c_x,               (5)
then
  sum_alpha|C_alpha|^2
  <=tau(|A|)sum_{x in cal X}|c_x|^2
  <<_{C,epsilon}Q^epsilon sum_x|c_x|^2.                     (6)
Thus exact phase collisions in the source-restored representation e_q(hk)=e(h alpha(x)) are divisor-compressible. This statement gives no estimate for unequal or near-equal rational phases, no finite-band fourth-moment saving, and no PMD or Goldbach conclusion.
2359a25d9fc6dd9b.proof:
Fix alpha=r/t in the stated reduced form. The equality k/q=r/t is equivalent to
  kt=rq.
Since gcd(|r|,t)=1, this implies t divides q. Write q=td. Substitution into kt=rtd gives k=rd. The source equation (1) becomes
  td m+vp rd=d(tm+vpr)=A.                                  (7)
Hence d is a positive divisor of |A|, and once d is fixed equation (7) determines
  m=(A/d-vpr)/t.
This proves the injective parametrization (4). Conversely, direct substitution of any admissible divisor choice in (4) proves (1) and alpha(x)=r/t. The fibre cardinality is therefore at most tau(|A|). Fact e705401df9f0709e gives tau(|A|)<<_{C,epsilon}Q^epsilon on |A|<=Q^C, proving (3).

For (6), Cauchy's inequality in each alpha-fibre gives
  |C_alpha|^2
  <=#{x:alpha(x)=alpha} sum_{x:alpha(x)=alpha}|c_x|^2.
Apply the fibre bound tau(|A|) and sum the disjoint fibres. The final scope statement follows because no comparison between distinct rational values has been used.

glossary.C_alpha: The aggregate coefficient on one exact rational source phase.
glossary.cal X: A finite actual-source set of triples (q,m,k).

247a783bb607d741.title: SMALL OUTER-\(g\) PARAMETER STABILITY BELOW \(3/5\)
247a783bb607d741.author: slava chan
247a783bb607d741.statement:
SMALL OUTER-\(g\) PARAMETER STABILITY BELOW \(3/5\).

Fix \(0<\kappa\le1/100\), and let
\[
 0<\eta,\eta_g\le\kappa/100000.
\]
Let \(x\) be sufficiently large, and let positive real scales \(D,M,R\) satisfy
\[
 x^{1/2-\eta}\le D,M\le x^{1/2+\eta},\qquad
 x^{9/16}\le R\le x^{3/5-\kappa}. \tag{1}
\]
Let \(g\) be a positive integer satisfying
\[
 g\le x^{\eta_g},\qquad g\le R/M. \tag{2}
\]
Define
\[
 Q_0=D/g,\qquad B_0=R/g,\qquad
 H_g=R/(gM),\qquad G_g=gM/D. \tag{3}
\]
Then
\[
 Q_0,H_g\ge1,\qquad B_0=G_gQ_0H_g. \tag{4}
\]
Writing
\[
 \beta_g=\frac{\log B_0}{\log Q_0}, \tag{5}
\]
one has
\[
 1\le\beta_g\le\frac65-\frac\kappa2. \tag{6}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 0<G_g\le Q_0^{\kappa/10000}. \tag{7}
\]
If a positive integer target \(N\) satisfies
\[
 g\mid N,\qquad N\le C_Nx
\]
for a fixed \(C_N\), then
\[
 1\le N/g\le Q_0^3 \tag{8}
\]
for sufficiently large \(x\).

Consequently, putting
\[
 \kappa_*=\kappa/4,\qquad \sigma_*=\kappa_*/100,
\]
the local scales \(Q_0,B_0\) lie in the buffered range
\[
 \beta_g\le6/5-2\kappa_*,
\]
and the imbalance satisfies
\[
 G_g\le Q_0^{(2\sigma_*)/8}. \tag{9}
\]
Thus every use of the two-sided imbalance corollary \(0a2db895d49fe29f\) with window margin at least \(2\sigma_*\) is numerically admissible on these small-\(g\) layers. This theorem is only a parameter-stability result; it does not itself assemble a Poisson block or estimate large \(g\).
247a783bb607d741.proof:
The identities in (4) are direct:
\[
 G_gQ_0H_g
 =\frac{gM}{D}\frac Dg\frac{R}{gM}
 =\frac Rg=B_0.
\]
The lower bound \(H_g\ge1\) is exactly the second inequality in (2). Also
\[
 Q_0\ge x^{1/2-\eta-\eta_g}>1
\]
for large \(x\).

Put \(t=\log g/\log x\), so \(0\le t\le\eta_g\). From (1),
\[
 \frac{\log B_0}{\log x}\ge\frac9{16}-\eta_g,\qquad
 \frac{\log Q_0}{\log x}\le\frac12+\eta.
\]
Hence
\[
 \beta_g\ge
 \frac{9/16-\eta_g}{1/2+\eta}>1. \tag{10}
\]
For the upper bound,
\[
 \frac{\log B_0}{\log x}\le\frac35-\kappa,
 \qquad
 \frac{\log Q_0}{\log x}\ge\frac12-\eta-\eta_g.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \beta_g\le
 \frac{3/5-\kappa}{1/2-\eta-\eta_g}. \tag{11}
\]
The difference
\[
 \left(\frac65-\frac\kappa2\right)
 \left(\frac12-\eta-\eta_g\right)
 -\left(\frac35-\kappa\right)
 =\frac{3\kappa}{4}
 -\left(\frac65-\frac\kappa2\right)(\eta+\eta_g)>0, \tag{12}
\]
because \(\eta+\eta_g\le2\kappa/100000\). This proves (6).

Next,
\[
 G_g=\frac{gM}{D}
 \le x^{\eta_g+2\eta}
 \le x^{3\kappa/100000}. \tag{13}
\]
Since
\[
 Q_0\ge x^{1/2-\eta-\eta_g}
 \ge x^{1/2-2\kappa/100000},
\]
one has
\[
 Q_0^{\kappa/10000}
 \ge x^{(\kappa/10000)(1/2-2\kappa/100000)}
 >x^{3\kappa/100000}, \tag{14}
\]
which proves (7).

If \(g\mid N\) and \(N\) is positive, then \(N/g\) is a positive integer, so \(N/g\ge1\). Also
\[
 N/g\le N\le C_Nx.
\]
But
\[
 Q_0^3\ge x^{3/2-3\eta-3\eta_g},
\]
whose exponent is greater than \(1\). Thus \(C_Nx\le Q_0^3\) for large \(x\), proving (8).

Finally,
\[
 \frac65-\frac\kappa2=\frac65-2\kappa_*.
\]
Also \(2\sigma_*=\kappa/200\), hence
\[
 (2\sigma_*)/8=\kappa/1600>\kappa/10000.
\]
Together with (7), this proves (9) and the stated compatibility with fact \(0a2db895d49fe29f\).

24a573ab44a5fb68.title: GENERALIZED STOPPING IDENTITY AND FIVE-WAY ROUGH COVERAGE
24a573ab44a5fb68.author: slava chan
24a573ab44a5fb68.proof:
We prove each identity directly.

First suppose (j=j_I(r)>0). Because (r) is squarefree, for every prime (pmid r) with (L<p<Z), the complementary factor (u=r/p) satisfies
[
 j_I(u)=j-1,qquad 1+j_I(u)=j,qquad mu(u)=-mu(r).
]
There are exactly (j) such primes. Therefore the right side of (4) is
[
 -sum_{substack{pmid r\L<p<Z}} rac{mu(r/p)}j
 =- rac{j(-mu(r))}{j}=mu(r).
]
This proves (4) without invoking any predecessor.

Now suppose (j_I(r)=0) and (v_L(r)>S). Let the (n=omega_L(r)) prime divisors of (v_L(r)) be put in a uniformly random order. Starting with the empty product (1), reveal primes in this order and stop at the first prefix whose product exceeds (S). Such a stopping prefix exists because the product of all (n) primes is (v_L(r)>S). It contains some (kge2) primes: a one-prime prefix cannot exceed (S), since every revealed prime is at most (Lle S).

Fix a squarefree divisor (ymid v_L(r)) having (k) prime factors. It can be the stopping prefix precisely when (y>S) and the last revealed prime (pmid y) satisfies (y/ple S). The probability that the set of the first (k) revealed primes is exactly the prime-divisor set of (y) is ( inom nk^{-1}). Conditional on that event, each of its (k) primes is equally likely to be last. Hence
[
 {mathbb P}(yhbox{ is the stopping prefix})
 = rac{Gamma_{k;L,S}(y)}{ inom nk}. 	ag{9}
]
Every ordering has exactly one stopping prefix, so summing (9) over all (k) and all (ymid v_L(r)) gives
[
 sum_{kge2}sum_{substack{ymid v_L(r)\omega(y)=k}}
  rac{Gamma_{k;L,S}(y)}{ inom nk}=1. 	ag{10}
]

For such a divisor (y), put (u=r/y). Then ((u,y)=1),
[
 n=k+omega_L(u),qquad j_I(u)=0,
]
and squarefreeness gives
[
 (-1)^kmu(u)=mu(y)mu(u)=mu(r). 	ag{11}
]
Conversely, every nonzero term on the right side of (5) arises from exactly one such stopping candidate (y). Substituting (11) into (5) and using (10) proves (5).

If (y) is an actual stopping prefix, then (y>S). If (p) is its last revealed prime, its preceding prefix is (y/ple S) and (ple L). Thus (yle SL), proving (6).

It remains to consider (j_I(r)=0) and (v=v_L(r)le S). Set (w=r/v). This factorization is unique. Since (r>Sge v), one has (w>1). A prime divisor of (w) is not at most (L), by the definition of (v), and it is not strictly between (L) and (Z), because (j_I(r)=0). Hence every prime divisor of (w) is at least (Z).

The integer (w) is squarefree. If it had four or more prime divisors, then (wge Z^4), hence (r=vwge Z^4), contradicting (Z^4>r). Therefore (w) has exactly one, two, or three distinct prime divisors, yielding the three mutually exclusive forms in (7), after ordering them increasingly. Finally, multiplicativity of (mu), together with ((v,w)=1), gives the three signs in (8).

The tests (j_I(r)>0), and when (j_I(r)=0), (v_L(r)>S) versus (v_L(r)le S), are mutually exclusive and exhaustive. The three possible numbers of rough prime factors in alternative (C) are also mutually exclusive. Hence the five classes give exact exhaustive coverage.

glossary.Gamma_{k;L,S}(y): The stopping-prefix probability numerator for a k-prime squarefree y crossing S with all primes at most L.
glossary.j_I(u): The number of prime divisors of u lying strictly between L and Z.
glossary.omega_L(u): The number of prime divisors of u that are at most L.
glossary.v_L(r): The product of the prime divisors of the squarefree integer r that are at most L.

24e13ac742ddd3c1.title: Let p be an odd prime, let K be an integer not divisible by p, and put U_p={1,...,p-1}. Let chi_p be the Legendre character modulo p and define the matrix
24e13ac742ddd3c1.author: slava chan
24e13ac742ddd3c1.statement:
Let p be an odd prime, let K be an integer not divisible by p, and put U_p={1,...,p-1}. Let chi_p be the Legendre character modulo p and define the matrix
P_K(a,b)=Delta_p(ab-K),  a,b in U_p.                                  (1)
Suppose I is a finite set and P_K has an exact decomposition
P_K(a,b)=sum_{j in I}F_j(a)beta_j(b),                                 (2)
where each beta_j is a complex-valued function on U_p, each F_j is the restriction to U_p of a continuously differentiable complex-valued function on the real interval [1,p-1], and there is a real number eta_j>=0 such that
sup_{1<=x<=p-1}|F_j'(x)|<=eta_j/p.                                   (3)
Define
Q_smooth=sum_{j in I}eta_j||beta_j||_2.                              (4)
Then
Q_smooth>=sqrt(p-1).                                                   (5)
If additionally eta_j>=1 for every j, then also
sum_{j in I}eta_j^(3/2)||beta_j||_2>=sqrt(p-1).                       (6)

For m=p, the full unweighted normal-digit union in fact 4f2052945785b331 collapses to the product selector Delta_p(ab-K), whose restriction to unit representatives is P_K. Thus (5) is a scoped prime-conductor smooth-row obstruction to replacing that collapsed selector by exact smooth profiles at negligible derivative-weighted cost. It is not by itself a lower bound for the literal Pi_BC of fact b1398db2962d7491: that quantity has two arbitrary sequence slots, two row profiles, dyadic subintervals rather than the complete U_p, the determinant constraint, and the remaining prime, gcd, carry, C-coupling, mask, and source selectors.
24e13ac742ddd3c1.proof:
First compute the exact adjacent variation of chi_p. Let
S=sum_{n modulo p}chi_p(n(n+1)).                                     (7)
The number N of pairs (n,y) modulo p satisfying y^2=n(n+1) is
N=sum_{n modulo p}[1+chi_p(n(n+1))]=p+S.                              (8)
Because p is odd, the invertible change of variables X=2n+1 and Y=2y transforms the equation into
X^2-Y^2=1.                                                           (9)
Every solution of (9) has t=X-Y nonzero and X+Y=t^(-1). Conversely, each t in the nonzero residues modulo p gives the unique solution
X=(t+t^(-1))/2,  Y=(t^(-1)-t)/2.                                    (10)
Hence N=p-1, so (8) gives S=-1.

The terms n=0 and n=-1 in (7) vanish. For n=1,...,p-2, both chi_p(n) and chi_p(n+1) belong to {1,-1}, and
chi_p(n(n+1))=chi_p(n)chi_p(n+1).                                    (11)
Let A be the number of these p-2 adjacent pairs with equal signs and B the number with opposite signs. Equations (7) and (11) give
A+B=p-2,  A-B=-1,                                                     (12)
so B=(p-1)/2. Therefore the discrete total variation is
sum_{a=1}^{p-2}|chi_p(a+1)-chi_p(a)|=2B=p-1.                          (13)

Project (1) against chi_p in the b-variable. For each a in U_p there is exactly one b in U_p with ab=K modulo p, namely b=Ka^(-1), and therefore
sum_{b in U_p}P_K(a,b)chi_p(b)=chi_p(K)chi_p(a).                      (14)
Here chi_p(a^(-1))=chi_p(a) because chi_p(a) belongs to {1,-1}. Applying the same projection to (2), define
c_j=sum_{b in U_p}beta_j(b)chi_p(b).                                  (15)
Then
chi_p(K)chi_p(a)=sum_{j in I}c_jF_j(a).                              (16)
Cauchy--Schwarz and sum_b|chi_p(b)|^2=p-1 give
|c_j|<=sqrt(p-1)||beta_j||_2.                                        (17)

Take discrete total variation of (16). The left side has variation p-1 by (13), because |chi_p(K)|=1. For each j, the fundamental theorem of calculus and (3) give
sum_{a=1}^{p-2}|F_j(a+1)-F_j(a)|
 <=(p-2)sup_x|F_j'(x)|
 <=eta_j.                                                            (18)
The triangle inequality, (17), and (18) now yield
p-1<=sum_j|c_j|eta_j
 <=sqrt(p-1)sum_jeta_j||beta_j||_2
 =sqrt(p-1)Q_smooth.                                                  (19)
Division by sqrt(p-1) proves (5). If eta_j>=1, then eta_j^(3/2)>=eta_j termwise, so (6) follows. The final specialization uses the exact conductor-collapse identity in fact 4f2052945785b331 and states only the scope supported by (1)-(6).

glossary.P_K: the product-permutation matrix on U_p defined by ab=K modulo p
glossary.Q_smooth: the derivative-weighted separated column cost of a smooth-row decomposition of P_K
glossary.U_p: the integer representatives 1 through p-1 of the nonzero residues modulo p
glossary.chi_p: the Legendre quadratic character modulo the odd prime p

24e911b7685090c1.title: LITERAL FORWARD-REVERSE INTERVAL-PRIME A CLOSURE IN THE FIRST POST-LOW-BETA BUFFER. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100,
24e911b7685090c1.author: slava chan
24e911b7685090c1.statement:
LITERAL FORWARD-REVERSE INTERVAL-PRIME A CLOSURE IN THE FIRST POST-LOW-BETA BUFFER. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100,
beta_0=6/5-2kappa, beta_1=6/5-3sigma,
kappa_0=1/200, and fix 0<eta<sigma. Let x>=3 and N be a positive integer comparable to x. Work with the literal paired nonzero-Poisson source atoms, exact outer-gcd normalization d=ga,r=gb with g=gcd(d,r)|N, and normalized marker partition of facts 15425579cb248eff and a71f777ad842c886.

In the forward orientation assume
R>D, c_1x<=DM<=C_1x,
c_Dx^(1/2)(log x)^(-A_D)<=D<=C_Dx^(1/2),
and R>x^(9/16-kappa_0).
In the reverse orientation assume
D>R, c_1x<=RK<=C_1x,
c_Rx^(1/2)(log x)^(-A_R)<=R<=C_Rx^(1/2),
and D>x^(9/16-kappa_0).
Here all displayed c_i,C_i are fixed positive constants, A_D,A_R are fixed nonnegative constants, and every physical scale D,M,R,K is at most Cx for a fixed C.

Forward put Q=D/g, B=R/g=Q^beta, G=M/Q, H_T=B/Q, H_P=B/M, and L_src=N/g. Reverse put Q=R/g, B=D/g=Q^beta, G=K/Q, H_T=B/Q, H_P=B/K, and L_src=N/g. Let R_A,buf be the sum of every normalized interval-prime A atom in either strict orientation for which
beta_0<beta<=beta_1,
over every actual G>0 and every exact outer gcd g|N. Retain every frozen parent, source amplitude, fixed-U, high-label, smooth/projective, Fourier, exact target-gcd, prime-order, collision, and deletion label of the literal source.

Then there is a fixed delta_A,buf>0 such that
|R_A,buf| << x^(1-delta_A,buf).
No target-gcd incidence, G-range, Fourier block, parent, or outer-g layer is deleted. The theorem estimates only the interval-prime A anatomy in the displayed normalized-beta buffer. It does not estimate B,C1,C2,C3, the later beta_1<beta<6/5 sliver, beta>=6/5, endpoint parents, PMD, logical bad-N capture, or Goldbach.
24e911b7685090c1.proof:
The standard marker is valid throughout the displayed buffer because beta_1=6/5-3sigma is smaller than beta_m=6/5-12sigma/5 in fact 15425579cb248eff. That fact also proves that every actual G<1 lies in the near-balanced strip Q^(-sigma+eta)<=G<=Q^(sigma-eta), while every G>=1 lies in the full-G regime. We estimate the A anatomy on each exact g-layer and orientation.

Forward, write d=ga,r=gb, Q=D/g, B=R/g=Q^beta, G=M/Q, and L_src=N/g. The exact interval-prime marker writes b=up with UY comparable to B and
H_TQ^sigma/2<=Y<=Z,
where H_T=B/Q and Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma). Put
c=gcd(a,L_src).
Fact 1c64020b89f097c4 gives
a=cq, k=ck_1, L_src=cL_1,
gcd(c,q)=gcd(c,b)=gcd(q,b)=gcd(q,L_1)=1.                         (1)
The forward reciprocity character descends exactly:
e_a(-L_src h b^(-1))=e_q(-L_1h b^(-1)).                       (2)
Squarefreeness gives gcd(u,p)=1 and (1) gives gcd(up,cq)=1.

The forced-high condition and beta<6/5 give a polynomial target bound without using the old beta_0 ceiling. Indeed
Q^(beta-1)=R/D>x^(1/16-kappa_0+o(1)).
Since beta-1<1/5, Q>=x^c for a fixed c>0. Also
|L_src|=(N/D)Q<=x^(1/2+o(1))Q,
so |L_src|<=Q^C_A for a fixed C_A depending only on kappa. Thus all target-size hypotheses below are met.

Split c at
C_cut=H_TQ^(sigma/4).
For c<=C_cut, the exact literal Fourier separation and marker coefficients match fact 6ca1f83e2233669a, including every retained label. If G>=1, Part (i) gives
sum_{c<=C_cut}|T_c|<<GQ^(2-delta_1).                            (3)
If G<1, Part (ii) gives
sum_{c<=C_cut}|T_c|<<Q^(2-delta_2).                             (4)
For c>C_cut, fact 5fbdbbebf99aec55 applies with arbitrary deletion masks and gives
sum_{c>C_cut}|T_c|<<Q^(2-sigma/4+epsilon),                      (5)
because B<=Q^(6/5), H_P<=H_T/G is polynomially bounded on the actual source, and the literal Fourier transform supplies arbitrary fixed-order decay.

When G>=1, combine (3),(5) and use DM=gGQ^2 comparable to x:
the exact-g contribution is
<<(x/g)Q^(-delta_3).
Sum g|N using sum 1/g=x^o(1) and Q>=x^c.

When G<1, combine (4),(5). Since Q=D/g, summing the exact-g bounds gives
sum_{g|N}Q^(2-delta_4)
 <=D^(2-delta_4)sum_{g>=1}g^(-2+delta_4)
 <<D^(2-delta_4)
 <<x^(1-delta_4/3),                                             (6)
after decreasing delta_4; the physical source has D<=C_Dx^(1/2). This proves the forward assertion.

For the reverse orientation, interchange
(d,m,D,M) with (r,k,R,K) and reindex the complete nonzero frequency family by h to -h exactly as in fact 65b10e9a052e9479. The normalized parameters become Q=R/g, B=D/g, G=K/Q; the marked factor is a=up and the reciprocal modulus is b. Put c=gcd(b,L_src). Fact 1c64020b89f097c4 after the same coordinate interchange gives
b=cq, m=cm_1, L_src=cL_1,
with q coprime to a and L_1. The reverse phase is
e_q(+L_1h a^(-1)).
Apply fact 6ca1f83e2233669a with its signed parameter L_src replaced by -L_src, so its displayed phase is exactly the last character. The retained archimedean reciprocity factor stays inside the scaled-smooth amplitude, as verified in fact 65b10e9a052e9479. The small-c estimates (3)-(4), large-c tail (5), target bound, and exact-g summations now repeat with R replacing D in (6). This proves the reverse assertion.

There are only polylogarithmically many inherited labels. Absorb them and take the minimum of the fixed saving exponents. No other anatomy or beta range has been used.

glossary.R_A,buf: The complete literal forward and reverse interval-prime A contribution in the first post-low-beta buffer.
glossary.delta_A,buf: The resulting fixed global power-saving exponent.

24eb84562bd3081e.title: ABL PROPOSITION 4.1 EXACT RECTANGLE INTERFACE, SIGNED NO-IMPORT, AND TWO MISSING LITERAL PAYMENTS. Define
24eb84562bd3081e.author: slava chan
24eb84562bd3081e.statement:
ABL PROPOSITION 4.1 EXACT RECTANGLE INTERFACE, SIGNED NO-IMPORT, AND TWO MISSING LITERAL PAYMENTS. Define
u_R(z;q)=1_{z congruent 1 (mod q)}
 -phi(q)^(-1)sum_{chi (mod q),cond(chi)<=R}chi(z),                (1)
with characters zero on nonunits. The only external theorem imported here is Assing--Blomer--Li, arXiv:2005.13915, Proposition 4.1.

Let M,N,Q,R>=1, let A>=1, put x_rect=MN, let a_1,a_2 be nonzero integers, let c_ABL be positive, and let (c_0,c_ABL)=1. Let alpha_m and beta_n be supported on M<m<=2M and N<n<=2N and satisfy
|alpha_m|<=tau(m)^A, |beta_n|<=tau(n)^A.                         (2)
For sufficiently small eta>0 there are delta=delta(eta)>0 and D_log=D_log(eta,A) such that
x_rect^eta<=N<=x_rect^(1/4+eta),
Q<=x_rect^(1/2+delta),
c_ABL,R,|a_2|<=x_rect^delta,
|a_1|<=x_rect^(1+delta)                                         (3)
imply
sum_{Q<=q<=2Q,(q,a_1a_2)=1,q congruent c_0 (mod c_ABL)}
 sum_{m,n,(n,a_2)=1}alpha_m beta_n
 u_R(mn*inverse(a_1)*a_2;q)
 <<_{eta,A}c_ABL*x_rect*(log x_rect)^D_log/R.                    (4)
The published q-coefficient in (4) is one.

Fix an h-row of fact edabb9a0d2959b41. Retain its smooth partition functions Psi_D(d),Psi_M(m_lit). Insert additionally the exact sharp partitions
1=sum_{U power of 2}1_{U<d<=2U},
1=sum_{V power of 2}1_{V<m_lit<=2V}.                            (5)
This refines every smooth cell into finitely many active ABL-width rectangles while retaining Psi_D,Psi_M and every other literal weight. On one such rectangle put x_rect=UV. If it meets
X_h<=d*m_lit<2X_h,                                               (6)
then
X_h/4<=x_rect<2X_h.                                              (7)
The exact arithmetic map on this rectangle is
a_1=ell, a_2=kappa h, Q=Q_c,
and ABL's variables are (d,m_lit), ordered so its N is the chosen factor scale. (8)
One has
d*m_lit*inverse(ell)*(kappa h) congruent 1 (mod q)
if and only if
d*m_lit congruent ell*inverse(kappa h) (mod q).                  (9)
The literal radical coprimality makes both factors coprime to a_2. An ABL citation is eligible only if this exact rectangle satisfies (2)-(3) with x_rect=UV, including every coefficient hypothesis required by the routed sequences. The X_h conditions in fact edabb9a0d2959b41 remain necessary scale checks but do not replace these rectangle checks.

The literal amplitude and outer mu(q) require a new theorem. Fix J>=0 and B_sm>=0. For any gamma define the extended norm
||gamma||_{S(J)}
 =max_{0<=j<=J}Q^(j-B_sm*delta*j)||gamma^(j)||_infinity          (10)
if gamma is in C_c^J((0,infinity)) and supported in [Q/2,3Q/2], and define it as infinity otherwise. Put
||alpha||_A=sup_m |alpha_m|/tau(m)^A.                            (11)
For G(q,m,n), let P_ABL,J(G) be the infimum of
sum_j |lambda_j| ||gamma_j||_{S(J)}
 ||alpha_j||_A||beta_j||_A                                     (12)
over countable exact representations
G(q,m,n)=sum_j lambda_j gamma_j(q)alpha_j(m)beta_j(n)            (13)
such that (12) is finite and (13) converges absolutely on every active integer triple.

Let H_mu(G) be the left side of (4) with summand multiplied by mu(q)G(q,m,n). The missing theorem ABL-MUQ-HIGH-LSHIFT is
|H_mu(G)|<<P_ABL,J(G)c_ABL*x_rect*(log x_rect)^D_log/R           (14)
for a proved J and the complete literal class. It is not asserted. The per-q one-variable Mellin quantity M_1 of fact edabb9a0d2959b41 does not supply the additionally required q-regularity aggregate
integral_R ||q maps to Vhat_{q,kappa,h}(tau)||_{S(J)}d tau.       (15)

Define
L_R(z;q)=phi(q)^(-1)
 sum_{chi (mod q),1<cond(chi)<=R}chi(z).                         (16)
Then exactly
1_{z congruent 1 (mod q)}-phi(q)^(-1)1_{(z,q)=1}
 =u_R(z;q)+L_R(z;q).                                             (17)
Therefore (14) would still leave the separate low-conductor estimate
|sum_q mu(q)sum_{m,n}G(q,m,n)L_R(mn*inverse(a_1)*a_2;q)|
 <<_A P_ABL,J(G)c_ABL*x_rect*(log x_rect)^(-A),                  (18)
which is not asserted.

Under all hypotheses of fact 53e70bf4e327e6bd, define
E_explicit=
 L_proj*B*(log B)^(-A)
 +L*(1+log(2BQ_c))^2*
  [B/P+Q_cP+omega_P(c)*(B/P+Q_c)].                              (19)
Then
sum_{(q,r) in cal S}|D_{qr}^{med}|<<_{A,K}E_explicit
and
|sum_{(q,r) in cal S}mu(qr)D_{qr}^{med}|<<_{A,K}E_explicit.      (20)
This absorption covers neither prime moduli nor moduli outside the convenient family cal S. No estimate (14) or (18), complete middle-window payment, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
24eb84562bd3081e.proof:
Equations (1)-(4), including A>=1 and the separate one-variable divisor bounds, are the cited Proposition 4.1. Its q-coefficient is one.

The half-open power-of-two intervals in (5) partition the positive integers exactly. Multiplication by them does not remove any smooth Psi weight, and only finitely many meet a fixed finite source support. On one rectangle, d<=2U and m_lit<=2V, so (6) gives X_h<=4UV and hence X_h/4<=x_rect. Also d>U and m_lit>V give d*m_lit>UV; together with d*m_lit<2X_h this gives x_rect<2X_h. Thus (7) is exact.

On active support (q,ell*kappa*h)=1. Multiplication by ell proves (9). Every prime of kappa h divides rad(kappa), since h divides rad(kappa), so the literal product coprimality forces each factor to be coprime to a_2. The selected sharp factor intervals are exactly those required in (2).

Definitions (10)-(13) specify differentiability, support, and absolute convergence, so the projective norm is extended-valued and well-defined. A Mellin construction would use q-profile Vhat(tau); controlling its projective cost requires (15). The accepted prior fact supplies only fixed-q L1 Mellin costs and no q-derivative aggregate.

For (17), split the cond(chi)<=R sum in (1) into the principal conductor-one character and the nonprincipal characters in (16). The principal character is the unit indicator. Rearrangement proves (17).

Finally, (19) is the full right side of fact 53e70bf4e327e6bd, including its corrections. Triangle inequality and |mu(qr)|<=1 give the second estimate in (20) from the first. The family cal S is only the convenient factorizable support of that fact.

glossary.P_ABL,J: The extended projective norm defined in (10)-(13).
glossary.x_rect: The exact product UV of the sharp dyadic rectangle scales.

25595026334d7350.title: Let μ be the Möbius function and let Λ be the von Mangoldt function. For an integer q>1 define the four signed sibling sectors
25595026334d7350.author: slava chan
25595026334d7350.statement:
Let μ be the Möbius function and let Λ be the von Mangoldt function. For an integer q>1 define the four signed sibling sectors
L(q)=Σ_{rk=q, r≤q^(1/2)} μ(r)log k,
M(q)=Σ_{rk=q, q^(1/2)<r<q^(2/3)} μ(r)log k,
E(q)=Σ_{rk=q, q^(2/3)≤r≤q^(3/4)} μ(r)log k,
T(q)=Σ_{rk=q, r>q^(3/4)} μ(r)log k.
Then
Λ(q)=L(q)+M(q)+E(q)+T(q).
If q is a prime power, M(q)=E(q)=T(q)=0 and L(q)=Λ(q). If q is not a prime power, then Λ(q)=0 and
M(q)+E(q)+T(q)=-L(q).

More generally, let I be a finite set, and for every i∈I let q_i>1 be an integer and a_i be an arbitrary complex coefficient which is independent of the choice of divisor sibling r k=q_i. Then
Σ_{i∈I}a_i(M(q_i)+E(q_i)+T(q_i))
=-Σ_{i∈I:q_i is not a prime power}a_i L(q_i).
Thus the complete large-divisor half r>sqrt(q) contains no direct prime-power von-Mangoldt mass. Its endpoint sector q^(2/3)≤r≤q^(3/4) and its supercritical sector r>q^(3/4) may be separated only as signed parts of zero-total composite families; after recombining all three large-divisor sectors, their aggregate is exactly the negative of the low-divisor composite aggregate. The coefficient-independence condition is essential: the identity is a sibling recombination statement and does not assert the same formula after different siblings are assigned unrelated weights.
25595026334d7350.proof:
The four ranges
r≤q^(1/2),
q^(1/2)<r<q^(2/3),
q^(2/3)≤r≤q^(3/4),
r>q^(3/4)
are pairwise disjoint and cover all positive r, because q>1 implies q^(1/2)<q^(2/3)≤q^(3/4). Hence their four sums add to the complete sibling sum Σ_{rk=q}μ(r)log k, which equals Λ(q) by fact b7fcb27a091203e5.

If q is a prime power, the same fact proves that every nonzero sibling has r≤sqrt(q). Therefore all three sectors above sqrt(q) vanish and L(q)=Λ(q). If q is not a prime power, Λ(q)=0. Subtracting L(q) from the four-sector identity gives M(q)+E(q)+T(q)=-L(q).

Multiply this pointwise identity by a_i and sum over i. For prime-power q_i the left large-divisor contribution is zero. For non-prime-power q_i it equals -a_iL(q_i). This proves the weighted formula. Independence of a_i from r is exactly what permits multiplication of the complete pointwise sibling identity by one common coefficient; with sibling-dependent coefficients the cancellation need not survive.

glossary.E(q): the signed endpoint sibling sum with q^(2/3)≤r≤q^(3/4)
glossary.I: a finite index set for weighted sibling-complete fibres
glossary.L(q): the signed sibling sum with r≤q^(1/2)
glossary.M(q): the signed sibling sum with q^(1/2)<r<q^(2/3)
glossary.T(q): the signed supercritical sibling sum with r>q^(3/4)
glossary.a_i: a coefficient common to every divisor sibling of q_i
glossary.q_i: the reflected integer attached to index i

256c10f372b85755.title: TERMINAL-INC-CHAR: EXACT SQUARED-MARKER CHARACTER TRANSPOSE AND THE REMAINING n-SOURCE TRANSFORM
256c10f372b85755.author: slava chan
256c10f372b85755.statement:
TERMINAL-INC-CHAR: EXACT SQUARED-MARKER CHARACTER TRANSPOSE AND THE REMAINING n-SOURCE TRANSFORM.

Fix B>=1, Z>2, and the complete terminal edge set of fact c384d36af25e96a6 before restriction to one dilator block. For every integer j>=0 put D_j=2^j and let E_j be the edges with
D_j<=d_e<2D_j.                                                    (1)
These half-open intervals are pairwise disjoint and partition the positive integers, so every positive-integer terminal dilator belongs to exactly one E_j.

Attach the exact marker coefficient a_e: on an A-edge over n,
a_e=mu(n)/r(n),
and on the unique C_j edge,
a_e=mu(n).                                                        (2)
Let m>=2 and let chi be a Dirichlet character modulo m. Restrict every E_j to edges satisfying gcd(n_e,m)=1. Then d_e and v_e are units modulo m because n_e=d_ev_e.

Fix j>=0, write D=D_j, and for a complex sequence f(n) define
(S_{chi,D}f)(d)
 =sum_{e in E_j:d_e=d}|a_e|^2 chi(v_e)f(n_e),                    (3)
sigma_D(n)=sum_{e in E_j:n_e=n}|a_e|^2.                          (4)
Then
sum_{D<=d<2D}chi(d)(S_{chi,D}f)(d)
 =sum_{B/2<=n<=2B}sigma_D(n)chi(n)f(n).                          (TERMINAL-INC-CHAR)

One has
0<=sigma_D(n)<=1/r(n) in the A alternative,
0<=sigma_D(n)<=1 in the C alternative.                           (5)
For every retained n with gcd(n,m)=1,
sum_{j>=0}sigma_{D_j}(n)=
  1/r(n) in the A alternative,
  1 in the C alternative.                                       (6)
Only finitely many terms are nonzero. For nonunit n, every character-restricted edge set has zero mass over n.

The squared-marker incidence operator satisfies
sum_d|(S_{chi,D}f)(d)|^2
 <=10(B/D)sum_n|f(n)|^2.                                        (7)

There is an exact conditional match to the literal centered-source transpose. Fact eb01e7b374521a0c defines
A_{m,c,chi}(d)
 =sum chi(v_lambda)B_lambda(R)conjugate(B_lambda(R')),           (8)
where the sum retains all exact children and ray pairs with d_lambda=d, m_q=m, and C_q congruent c modulo m, together with every hard and pair-dependent selector. It also proves
Zhat_{m,c}(chi)=sum_d chi(d)A_{m,c,chi}(d).                      (9)
Fact 50ef6972010758a6 gives, in every same-copy summand,
B_lambda(R)conjugate(B_lambda(R'))
 =|a_lambda(n)|^2
  B_lambda^flat(R)conjugate(B_lambda^flat(R')).                  (10)

Freeze m,c,chi, one ray-pair coordinate and every child-independent coordinate in (8). Separate every edge-dependent exception. If the retained flat product in (10), including every remaining selector, is common across terminal children over n, define
f(n)=B_lambda^flat(R)conjugate(B_lambda^flat(R')).               (11)
Then the retained child contribution to (8) on D<=d<2D is exactly (3), with e=lambda, d_e=d_lambda, v_e=v_lambda, and n_e=n. Under this explicitly conditional common-flat factorization, equations (9) and TERMINAL-INC-CHAR identify the remaining input as the weighted n-character transform sigma_D(n)chi(n)f(n). No claim that all literal coordinates satisfy (11) is made.

The Schur norm (7) alone does not force B/D for the complete character test. One always has
sum_{D<=d<2D}|chi(d)|^2<=D,                                     (12)
and this can be of order D, for example for characters modulo 3. Hence Cauchy may cancel D^{-1}. Equivalently, on an abstract retained C fibre, f(n)=conjugate(chi(n)) makes the right side of TERMINAL-INC-CHAR equal the number of retained C integers. This is a method no-fit, not a literal saturator.

Thus terminal incidence supplies the B/D squared operator norm, but its complete centered consumer still requires cancellation in the actual n-source transform (11), or a stronger factorization. The theorem proves no such estimate, no C-qSRC-BV-SUP or C-qSRC-SUP, no F>Q principal estimate, no small-dilator projected-incidence estimate, no tail payment, and no Goldbach conclusion.
256c10f372b85755.proof:
Expanding the left side of TERMINAL-INC-CHAR gives
sum_{e in E_j}|a_e|^2chi(d_e)chi(v_e)f(n_e).                    (13)
Every retained n_e is a unit and equals d_ev_e, so multiplicativity gives chi(d_e)chi(v_e)=chi(n_e). Group by n_e to obtain TERMINAL-INC-CHAR. Nonunit n have no retained edge.

In A, each retained edge has squared weight 1/r(n)^2 and at most r(n) edges enter one block, giving sigma_D(n)<=1/r(n). In C there is one edge of squared weight one. This proves (5).

Fix a unit n. The intervals [2^j,2^(j+1)), j>=0, partition all positive integer dilators. An A integer has r(n) edges, each of squared weight 1/r(n)^2, so their all-block mass is 1/r(n). A C integer has one edge of mass one. This proves (6).

Since |a_e|^2<=|a_e| and |chi(v_e)|<=1, the absolute row and column sums in (3) are bounded by those of fact c384d36af25e96a6 on the same block. Here D=2^j>=1, so that fact applies and Schur's test gives (7).

For the literal match, substitute (10) into the exact profile (8). After the stated coordinates are frozen and the explicitly assumed common-flat factorization (11) holds, each retained child lambda contributes
|a_lambda(n)|^2 chi(v_lambda)f(n)
to the unique output d=d_lambda. This is exactly the edge summand in (3), with every selector retained either in the restricted edge set or in f(n). Summing (3) against chi(d) is exactly the corresponding part of (9), so TERMINAL-INC-CHAR gives the claimed conditional handoff.

Equation (12) follows from |chi(d)|<=1. For modulus 3, |chi(d)| is one precisely off multiples of 3, so the squared norm on a length-D interval is of order D. In the abstract C example, sigma_D(n)=1 and chi(n)f(n)=1. These prove only the stated no-fit. All exclusions follow.

glossary.S_{chi,D}: The squared-marker terminal incidence operator on one dyadic dilator block.
glossary.TERMINAL-INC-CHAR: The exact transpose from a d-character test to a weighted n-character source transform.
glossary.sigma_D(n): The squared terminal marker mass from unit n into one dyadic dilator block.

25edb4cc4e748e6e.title: Fix x>1 with N=2x integral. Let D_*≥1, let W be a real function, let ψ be a real function satisfying ψ(u)=1 for u≥2, and let Φ be a real dyadic cutoff. For positive dyadic D,M,R,K define
25edb4cc4e748e6e.author: slava chan
25edb4cc4e748e6e.statement:
Fix x>1 with N=2x integral. Let D_*≥1, let W be a real function, let ψ be a real function satisfying ψ(u)=1 for u≥2, and let Φ be a real dyadic cutoff. For positive dyadic D,M,R,K define
Q(D,M;R,K)=Σ_{d,m,r,k≥1;dm+rk=N} μ(d)μ(r)log(m)log(k)W(dm/x)ψ(d/D_*)Φ(d/D)Φ(m/M)Φ(r/R)Φ(k/K).
Put ι(D,M;R,K)=(R,K;D,M). Assume that Φ(d/D)Φ(r/R) can be nonzero only when d,r≥2D_*.

If (D,M,R,K)≠(R,K,D,M), then
Q(D,M;R,K)+Q(R,K;D,M)
=Σ_{d,m,r,k≥1;dm+rk=N} μ(d)μ(r)log(m)log(k)
 [W(dm/x)+W(rk/x)]
 Φ(d/D)Φ(m/M)Φ(r/R)Φ(k/K).
If (D,M,R,K)=(R,K,D,M), then Q(D,M;R,K) is one half of the right-hand side. Thus every legal bi-deep swap orbit has an exact single-orientation representation with the symmetrized joint weight W(u)+W(2-u), u=dm/x, while retaining the same fixed N and both Möbius signs. The identity is an orbit-sum identity; it does not assert equality of the two oriented blocks.
25edb4cc4e748e6e.proof:
On every summand under consideration, d,r≥2D_*. Hence ψ(d/D_*)=ψ(r/D_*)=1.

In Q(R,K;D,M), make the bijective change of variables
(d,m,r,k)↦(r,k,d,m).
The equation dm+rk=N, the product μ(d)μ(r), and the product log(m)log(k) are invariant. The four dyadic factors become, in their original order,
Φ(d/D)Φ(m/M)Φ(r/R)Φ(k/K).
The source weight W(dm/x) becomes W(rk/x), and the cutoff ψ becomes ψ(r/D_*)=1. Adding the unchanged Q(D,M;R,K), for which ψ(d/D_*)=1, proves the displayed formula for a nonfixed orbit.

For a fixed label, the same change of variables proves that Q(D,M;D,M) equals the identical sum with W(rk/x) in place of W(dm/x). Adding these two equal expressions gives the symmetrized right-hand side, so the original block is half of it. Finally rk/x=(N-dm)/x=2-dm/x, which gives W(u)+W(2-u). No step takes an absolute value or changes N or either Möbius factor.

glossary.Q(D,M;R,K): the fixed-N signed dyadic block in this statement
glossary.ι: the swap of the two divisor-complement scale pairs

2679e2cb5e61a245.title: Let x≥2 be real with N=2x an integer, and assume that N is not the sum of two primes. Fix real numbers 1/2<a<b<1, a nonnegative real function W supported in [a,b], a real function b_N on the positive integers, a real number D_* with 1≤D_*≤x, and a real function ψ on the positive reals. Define
2679e2cb5e61a245.author: slava chan
2679e2cb5e61a245.statement:
Let x≥2 be real with N=2x an integer, and assume that N is not the sum of two primes. Fix real numbers 1/2<a<b<1, a nonnegative real function W supported in [a,b], a real function b_N on the positive integers, a real number D_* with 1≤D_*≤x, and a real function ψ on the positive reals. Define
R_{N,W}=Σ_{n≥1}W(n/x)Λ(n)Λ(N-n),
M_{N,W}=Σ_{n≥1}W(n/x)b_N(n)Λ(n),
H_{N,W,ψ}=Σ_{d,m≥1;d≥2}μ(d)log(m)W(dm/x)ψ(d/D_*)Λ(N-dm),
E_{0,N}=Σ_{n≥1}W(n/x)log(n)(Λ(N-n)-b_N(n)),
E_{sh,N}=Σ_{d,m≥1;d≥2}μ(d)log(m)W(dm/x)(1-ψ(d/D_*))(Λ(N-dm)-b_N(dm)),
and
E_{b,N}=Σ_{d,m≥1;d≥2}μ(d)log(m)W(dm/x)ψ(d/D_*)b_N(dm).
Then the exact smooth comparison identity
R_{N,W}=M_{N,W}+H_{N,W,ψ}+E_{0,N}+E_{sh,N}-E_{b,N}
holds. Define P_N=Σ_{e=2}^{floor(log_2(N-1))}floor((N-1)^(1/e)). Then
0≤R_{N,W}≤2||W||_∞(log N)^2P_N.
Consequently, let A_N>0 and 0<δ≤1/6. If
|M_{N,W}-A_N|≤δA_N,
|E_{0,N}|+|E_{sh,N}|+|E_{b,N}|≤δA_N,
and
2||W||_∞(log N)^2P_N≤δA_N,
then
|H_{N,W,ψ}+A_N|≤3δA_N
and in particular H_{N,W,ψ}≤-A_N/2. All assertions are pointwise for the fixed N; if the three displayed input bounds hold uniformly over a family of bad N, so does the conclusion.
2679e2cb5e61a245.proof:
For every positive integer n, the elementary divisor identity Λ(n)=Σ_{dm=n}μ(d)log m holds. Separating the d=1 term gives Λ(n)=log n+Σ_{dm=n,d≥2}μ(d)log m. Put w_N(t)=Λ(N-t)-b_N(t). Since W is supported in [a,b] with b<1 and N=2x, every argument N-n or N-dm occurring on the support is positive. Therefore
R_{N,W}-M_{N,W}=Σ_{n≥1}W(n/x)Λ(n)w_N(n)
=E_{0,N}+Σ_{d,m≥1;d≥2}μ(d)log(m)W(dm/x)w_N(dm).
Insert 1=(1-ψ(d/D_*))+ψ(d/D_*) into the last sum. The part with 1-ψ is E_{sh,N}. The part with ψ is
Σ_{d,m≥1;d≥2}μ(d)log(m)W(dm/x)ψ(d/D_*)[Λ(N-dm)-b_N(dm)]
=H_{N,W,ψ}-E_{b,N}.
This proves the exact comparison identity.

Because W is nonnegative and the von Mangoldt function is nonnegative, R_{N,W}≥0. Consider a nonzero summand in R_{N,W}. Then n and N-n are positive prime powers. Since N is not a sum of two primes, they cannot both be primes. Thus at least one of n and N-n is a proper prime power p^e with e≥2. Every positive integer below N of the form p^e with e≥2 is included among at most P_N possibilities: indeed p≤(N-1)^(1/e), and e≤floor(log_2(N-1)). By the union bound, at most 2P_N integers n can index a nonzero summand. On the support, n<N and N-n<N, so Λ(n)≤log N and Λ(N-n)≤log N. Also W(n/x)≤||W||_∞. Hence R_{N,W}≤2||W||_∞(log N)^2P_N.

Rearranging the exact identity gives
H_{N,W,ψ}+A_N=R_{N,W}-(M_{N,W}-A_N)-E_{0,N}-E_{sh,N}+E_{b,N}.
The prime-power bound and the three quantitative hypotheses imply, by the triangle inequality,
|H_{N,W,ψ}+A_N|≤δA_N+δA_N+δA_N=3δA_N.
Since δ≤1/6, this yields H_{N,W,ψ}≤-A_N+3δA_N≤-A_N/2. No step changes or averages the fixed integer N.

glossary.A_N: a positive real comparison main-term magnitude
glossary.E_{0,N}: the logarithmic shallow discrepancy defined in the statement
glossary.E_{b,N}: the comparison-weight deep Möbius tail defined in the statement
glossary.E_{sh,N}: the proper-divisor discrepancy localized by 1-ψ, defined in the statement
glossary.H_{N,W,ψ}: the smooth reflected Möbius source defined in the statement
glossary.M_{N,W}: the weighted comparison correlation defined in the statement
glossary.P_N: the explicit upper bound for the number of proper prime powers below N
glossary.R_{N,W}: the weighted Goldbach von-Mangoldt correlation defined in the statement
glossary.W: a nonnegative real weight supported in [a,b]
glossary.b_N: a real comparison weight on positive integers
glossary.ψ: a real cutoff function on the positive reals

27540b4094f677f4.title: EXACT ALL-SHIFT RATIONAL-SLOPE DIAGONAL SUBTRACTION
27540b4094f677f4.author: slava chan
27540b4094f677f4.statement:
EXACT ALL-SHIFT RATIONAL-SLOPE DIAGONAL SUBTRACTION.

Let p be a prime, let A be an integer, let cal Q be a finite set of positive integers not divisible by p, and let b_q be arbitrary complex coefficients supported on cal Q. Put
  e_p(t)=exp(2 pi i t/p),
  S_p(h)=sum_{q in cal Q}b_q e_p(hA qbar),                 (1)
where bars denote inverses modulo p. For an ordered pair define its exact rational reciprocal slope
  lambda(q_1,q_2)=(q_2-q_1)/(q_1q_2)=1/q_1-1/q_2.         (2)
For every rational slope lambda represented by cal Q put
  B_lambda=sum_{lambda(q_1,q_2)=lambda}
                 b_{q_1}conjugate(b_{q_2}),                (3)
and let rho_{p,lambda} be the common residue
  A(q_2-q_1)(q_1q_2)^(-1) modulo p                         (4)
for pairs in that fibre. This is well defined.

For k modulo p define
  T(k)=sum_{h modulo p; h nonzero, h-k nonzero}
          |S_p(h)|^2|S_p(h-k)|^2,                          (5)
and
  m_p(k)=p-1 if k=0,  and  m_p(k)=p-2 if k is nonzero.     (6)
Then the complete contribution to T(k) from quadruples with equal exact rational slopes is
  T_0(k)=m_p(k)sum_lambda |B_lambda|^2
                         e_p(k rho_{p,lambda}).             (7)
In particular, the rational-slope diagonal contributes at every shift k. It is not confined to k=0.

Let W be any complex function modulo p, put
  What(k)=sum_{r modulo p}W(r)e_p(-kr),                     (8)
and define the physical centered kernel
  Gamma_W(x,y)=sum_{r modulo p}W(r)
        [1_{r=x}-1/p][1_{r=y}-1/p].                         (9)
Then
  1/p^2 sum_{k modulo p}What(k)T_0(k)
   =sum_lambda |B_lambda|^2
       Gamma_W(rho_{p,lambda},rho_{p,lambda})               (10)
   =sum_lambda |B_lambda|^2
       [(1-2/p)W(rho_{p,lambda})
          +(sum_rW(r))/p^2].                               (11)

Define the all-shift rational-diagonal-subtracted correlation
  T_neq(k)=T(k)-T_0(k).                                    (12)
For q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4 in cal Q put
  Delta=(q_2-q_1)q_3q_4-(q_4-q_3)q_1q_2,                  (13)
  rho_12=A(q_2-q_1)(q_1q_2)^(-1) modulo p,
  rho_34=A(q_4-q_3)(q_3q_4)^(-1) modulo p.                 (14)
Then exactly
  1/p^2 sum_kWhat(k)T_neq(k)
  =sum_{q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4; Delta nonzero}
    b_{q_1}conjugate(b_{q_2})conjugate(b_{q_3})b_{q_4}
    Gamma_W(rho_12,rho_34).                                (15)
Thus subtracting (7) at every shift is exactly the same as deleting the integer determinant Delta=0 in the physical incidence/cross/center assembly. The right side of (15) retains all three terms of Gamma_W and is generally signed.

If 0<=W<=1 is real, then the quantity in (10) is nonnegative and
  0<=1/p^2 sum_kWhat(k)T_0(k)
    <=sum_lambda|B_lambda|^2
    <<_epsilon Q^epsilon(sum_q|b_q|^2)^2                  (16)
when cal Q is contained in [Q,2Q), by fact e7458a42217c2756. Consequently every PMD short-window density theorem may pay (16) separately, but its remaining target must be the full signed sum (15), including k=0 and every k nonzero. Removing only T(0)'s rational diagonal does not perform the required subtraction.
27540b4094f677f4.proof:
Exact equality of rational slopes makes (4) independent of the chosen representing pair, because reducing
  A lambda(q_1,q_2)
modulo p is legitimate when q_1q_2 is a unit.

Expand the first square in (5) as
  |S_p(h)|^2=sum_{q_1,q_2}
     b_{q_1}conjugate(b_{q_2})e_p(h rho_12).                (17)
After interchanging q_3 and q_4 in the second square, write it as
  |S_p(h-k)|^2=sum_{q_3,q_4}
     conjugate(b_{q_3})b_{q_4}
     e_p(-(h-k)rho_34).                                    (18)
The product phase is
  e_p(h(rho_12-rho_34))e_p(k rho_34).                      (19)
On the integer-diagonal set Delta=0, fact e7458a42217c2756 gives
  lambda(q_1,q_2)=lambda(q_3,q_4).
Hence rho_12=rho_34=rho_{p,lambda}, the h-dependent factor in (19) is one, and the coefficient sum over the two pair fibres is |B_lambda|^2. The number of allowed h in (5) is p-1 when k=0 and p-2 when k is nonzero, proving (6)-(7).

For a fixed residue rho, finite Fourier inversion gives
  sum_kWhat(k)e_p(k rho)=pW(rho).                           (20)
Using What(0)=sum_rW(r), equations (6)-(7) give
  1/p^2 sum_kWhat(k)m_p(k)e_p(k rho)
  =1/p^2[(p-1)What(0)
       +(p-2)sum_{k nonzero}What(k)e_p(k rho)]
  =(1-2/p)W(rho)+(sum_rW(r))/p^2.                          (21)
Direct expansion of (9) at x=y=rho gives the same expression, so summing (21) with weights |B_lambda|^2 proves (10)-(11).

Fact b0662c5a5e8a7772 proves the complete shifted identity
  1/p^2 sum_kWhat(k)T(k)
  =sum_{q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4}
    b_{q_1}conjugate(b_{q_2})conjugate(b_{q_3})b_{q_4}
    Gamma_W(rho_12,rho_34).                                (22)
Equations (10) and (13), together with the equivalence Delta=0 if and only if the exact slopes are equal from fact e7458a42217c2756, show that subtracting (10) from (22) deletes exactly the Delta=0 quadruples. This proves (12)-(15).

Finally assume 0<=W<=1. Since 0<=sum_rW(r)<=p, the bracket in (11) lies between zero and one for every p, including p=2. Therefore (10) is bounded by sum_lambda|B_lambda|^2. The verified reciprocal-slope energy estimate in fact e7458a42217c2756 gives (16). The final scope statement follows from the exact all-shift identity (15).

glossary.B_lambda: The coefficient sum over one exact rational reciprocal-slope fibre.
glossary.T_0(k): The contribution of equal rational slopes to the shifted fourth correlation at frequency difference k.
glossary.T_neq(k): The signed all-shift fourth correlation after subtracting T_0(k), equivalently the sum over nonzero integer determinants.
glossary.m_p(k): The number of residues h modulo p for which h and h-k are both nonzero.

2775909b4db4ae24.title: DYADIC FIXED-POWER PAYMENT FOR HIGH-DENOMINATOR GENUINELY SEPARATED LONG TWO-ROW FIBRES
2775909b4db4ae24.author: slava chan
2775909b4db4ae24.proof:
Since \(P\ge3\), every prime in the dyadic block is greater than 2. Fact 6ab529accdede090 therefore applies to every fibre (4)--(6). Its long-fibre conclusion, the polynomial bound on the denominators, and the uniform \(Q^{o(1)}\) weight constants give
\[
 |\mathcal T_{e,\nu}|
 \ll_{C,\varepsilon}Q^{\varepsilon+o(1)}
 {L_{e,\nu,1}L_{e,\nu,2}\over
  p(d_{e,\nu,1}d_{e,\nu,2})^{1/2}}. \tag{12}
\]
By (3), (7), and \(p\ge P\),
\[
 \sum_{\nu\in\mathcal F_e}
 |\rho_{e,\nu}\mathcal T_{e,\nu}|
 \ll Q^{2+\varepsilon+o(1)}/(PD). \tag{13}
\]

For i=1,2 put
\[
 g_i(p)^2=\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_i(p)}|\gamma_b|^2. \tag{14}
\]
Every member of \(\mathcal B_i(p)\) is a multiple of p and is less than 2B, so
\[
 \#\mathcal B_i(p)\le3B/p. \tag{15}
\]
Cauchy's inequality gives
\[
 \sum_{b_i\in\mathcal B_i(p)}
 |\gamma_{b_1}\gamma_{b_2}|
 \le {3B\over p}g_1(p)g_2(p). \tag{16}
\]
Disjointness of the first-row sets and (1) imply
\[
 \sum_p g_1(p)^2\le1. \tag{17}
\]
The bounded membership of the second-row sets implies
\[
 \sum_p g_2(p)^2\le Q^{o(1)}. \tag{18}
\]
Hence Cauchy's inequality in p, followed by \(p\ge P\), yields
\[
 \sum_{p,b_1,b_2}|\gamma_{b_1}\gamma_{b_2}|
 \ll Q^{o(1)}B/P. \tag{19}
\]
Combine (8), (13), and (19) to obtain
\[
 |\mathcal T(P,D)|
 \ll Q^{\varepsilon+o(1)}
 {B\over P}{Q^2\over PD},
\]
which is (9). Under (10), (9) becomes
\[
 Q^{\varepsilon+o(1)}BQ^{1-\omega}
 =Q^{7/3-\omega+\varepsilon+o(1)},
\]
proving (11). The scope restrictions follow from the explicitly separated hypotheses and fact f271bfac142ef5e0.

glossary.D: The common lower bound for the geometric mean of the two additive denominators.
glossary.\\mathcal F_e: The finite separated smooth-fibre labels attached to one directed outer edge.
glossary.\\mathcal T(P,D): The dyadic aggregate of the selected separated fibres.
glossary.\\mathcal T_{e,\\nu}: One centered separated two-row incidence fibre.

2827630745a3225b.title: Fix real numbers 1/2<a<b<1, a nonzero nonnegative continuously differentiable real function W supported in [a,b], and a continuously differentiable real function ψ on the positive reals with 0≤ψ≤1, ψ(u)=0 for 0<u≤1, and ψ(u)=1 for u≥2. There exists B=B(W,ψ)>0 such that the following holds as x tends to infinity through values for which N=2x is an even integer not representable as a sum of two primes. Define
2827630745a3225b.author: slava chan
2827630745a3225b.statement:
Fix real numbers 1/2<a<b<1, a nonzero nonnegative continuously differentiable real function W supported in [a,b], and a continuously differentiable real function ψ on the positive reals with 0≤ψ≤1, ψ(u)=0 for 0<u≤1, and ψ(u)=1 for u≥2. There exists B=B(W,ψ)>0 such that the following holds as x tends to infinity through values for which N=2x is an even integer not representable as a sum of two primes. Define
D_*=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B),
C_2=∏_{p>2}p(p-2)/(p-1)^2,
𝔠(N)=C_2∏_{p|N,p>2}(p-1)/(p-2),
Q_N=rad(2N),
r_N(n)=1_{gcd(n,Q_N)=1}∏_{p|n,p∤Q_N}(p-1)/(p-2),
b_N(n)=2𝔠(N)r_N(n),
and
H_{N,W,ψ}=Σ_{d,m≥1}μ(d)log(m)W(dm/x)ψ(d/D_*)Λ(N-dm).
Then, with c_W=2∫_0^∞W(u)du>0,
H_{N,W,ψ}=-c_W𝔠(N)x+o_{W,ψ}(𝔠(N)x),
uniformly over these bad even integers N.

Fix additionally a real function Φ supported in [1/2,2] satisfying Σ_{j∈Z}Φ(t/2^j)=1 for every t>0, and for positive dyadic D,M,R,K define
Q_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;R,K)=Σ_{d,m,r,k≥1;dm+rk=N}μ(d)μ(r)log(m)log(k)W(dm/x)ψ(d/D_*)Φ(d/D)Φ(m/M)Φ(r/R)Φ(k/K).
Then
H_{N,W,ψ}=Σ_{D,M,R,K}Q_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;R,K)
exactly, and every sufficiently large bad N has a positive dyadic quadruple satisfying
Q_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;R,K)≤-c_W𝔠(N)x/[2(ceil(log_2 x)+4)^4].
Thus the negative block is real, has an explicit fourth-power logarithmic loss, preserves both Möbius signs, and is obtained pointwise for the same fixed N.
2827630745a3225b.proof:
Apply fact 7a161d479c94ccb0 with target exponent A=2, and choose the resulting B. It gives, for D_*=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B),
E_{sh,N}=o_{W,ψ}(𝔠(N)x)
uniformly in N. Fact 0b3642c89b136065 gives for the same fixed B, W, and ψ,
E_{b,N}=o_{W,ψ}(𝔠(N)x)
uniformly in N. All definitions in these two estimates agree with those reproduced in the statement.

The hypotheses of fact b0eae7ccb6da25c7 are therefore satisfied. That fact proves
H_{N,W,ψ}=-c_W𝔠(N)x+o_{W,ψ}(𝔠(N)x)
and, after insertion of the stated dyadic partition Φ, proves the exact four-parameter decomposition and the existence for every sufficiently large bad N of a block bounded above by
-c_W𝔠(N)x/[2(ceil(log_2 x)+4)^4].
The d=1 term in H vanishes because D_*≥1 for sufficiently large x and ψ(1/D_*)=0, so the definition of H here is identical to the d≥2 definition used in the source comparison facts. The positivity of c_W follows from W being continuous, nonnegative, and nonzero. The exact sign preservation and fixed-N nature of the block are part of facts cdb5cefbc7333591 and 6f82723a1b084485, which are predecessors of fact b0eae7ccb6da25c7.

glossary.Q_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;R,K): the four-parameter dyadic block defined in the statement
glossary.W: a nonzero nonnegative continuously differentiable weight supported in [a,b]
glossary.c_W: the positive constant 2 times the integral of W
glossary.r_N(n): the local-density weight defined in the statement
glossary.ψ: a continuously differentiable cutoff from zero to one
glossary.𝔠(N): the Goldbach singular factor defined in the statement

28b8af5697fa64eb.title: ACTUAL-SOURCE SLOPE DIAMETER AND CONSTANT-SIZED CRITICAL CLUSTER COVER
28b8af5697fa64eb.author: slava chan
28b8af5697fa64eb.statement:
ACTUAL-SOURCE SLOPE DIAMETER AND CONSTANT-SIZED CRITICAL CLUSTER COVER.

Fix C_A>=1 and real numbers Q,H,n with Q>=2, H>=2, n>=QH. Let A be an integer satisfying
  |A|<=C_A Q^2.                                             (1)
Let cal X be a nonempty finite set of integer triples x=(q,m,k) satisfying
  Q<=q,m<2Q,  qm+nk=A.                                     (2)
For x in cal X put lambda_x=k/q. Then
  lambda_x=A/(nq)-m/n,                                     (3)
and
  max_{x,y in cal X}|lambda_x-lambda_y|
  <=(C_A/2+1)/H.                                           (4)
Consequently the slope set is covered by at most
  K_cl=ceil(12(C_A/2+1))+1                                 (5)
real intervals of length at most 1/(12H), and at least one such interval contains at least
  #cal X/K_cl                                               (6)
source atoms.

More precisely, let cal Y be any retained subset of one covering interval with cardinality Y>=2 and pairwise distinct exact rational slopes. Let I be a finite integer interval contained either in [H,2H) or in (-2H,-H], and put L=#I. With the constant height-separated coefficients a_h(x)=1 on cal Y,
  T_cluster
   =sum_{h in I}sum_{x_1,x_2 in cal Y, x_1 not equal x_2}
      e(h[lambda_{x_1}-lambda_{x_2}])
  >= (L/2)Y(Y-1).                                          (7)
Thus the actual source equation places all slopes inside O_{C_A}(1) critical-resolution clusters, and any retained distinct-slope cluster obeys the explicit coherent lower bound (7).

This theorem asserts only the cover and the conditional retained-cluster estimate. It does not construct a family with Y tending to infinity, does not assert that a natural literal mask selects a cluster, does not estimate a naturally weighted row, and gives no PMD or Goldbach conclusion.
28b8af5697fa64eb.proof:
Divide qm+nk=A by nq. This gives
  m/n+k/q=A/(nq),
which rearranges to (3).

For x=(q_x,m_x,k_x) and y=(q_y,m_y,k_y), equation (3) gives
  |lambda_x-lambda_y|
  <=|A|/n |1/q_x-1/q_y|+|m_x-m_y|/n.                       (8)
Since Q<=q_x,q_y<2Q,
  |1/q_x-1/q_y|<=1/Q-1/(2Q)=1/(2Q).                        (9)
Also |m_x-m_y|<Q. Insert (1), (9), and n>=QH into (8):
  |lambda_x-lambda_y|
  <=C_AQ^2/(2nQ)+Q/n
  <=C_A/(2H)+1/H.
This proves (4).

The nonempty finite slope set lies in a closed real interval of length at most (C_A/2+1)/H. Partition this interval into at most ceil(12(C_A/2+1))+1 closed subintervals of length at most 1/(12H), assigning shared endpoints consistently to one adjacent piece. This proves (5). The pigeonhole principle proves (6).

Now let cal Y and I satisfy the additional hypotheses. The phase set {lambda_x:x in cal Y} lies in an interval of length at most 1/(12H), has Y>=2 elements, and its slopes are distinct. All hypotheses of fact 714f3597f5ef527c hold. That fact proves that the ordered constant-coefficient Gram is real and at least (L/2)Y(Y-1), which is (7). No asymptotic impossibility assertion is needed for the stated cover and conditional estimate, proving all scope qualifications.

glossary.Kcl: A constant-sized cover number for one nonempty actual source row by slope intervals of length 1/(12H).

294ac3b02b065aec.title: LITERAL PMD L2 PRE-CAUCHY CONTRACT, PAID q-DIAGONAL, AND THE SINGLE SAME-HEIGHT TT-STAR SUPPLIER
294ac3b02b065aec.author: slava chan
294ac3b02b065aec.statement:
LITERAL PMD L2 PRE-CAUCHY CONTRACT, PAID q-DIAGONAL, AND THE SINGLE SAME-HEIGHT TT-STAR SUPPLIER.

Fix constants C>=1 and J>=1. Let Q>=2 and let real numbers H,V,P,B satisfy
  2<=H<=Q^(1/3),  2<=V<H,  P=QH/V,  B>=1.                 (1)
Let A be a nonzero integer with |A|<=Q^C. Let cal L be a finite set. For ell in cal L let eta_ell be a complex projective coefficient and let I_ell be an integer interval contained either in [H,2H) or in (-2H,-H]. Let xi_v be supported on integers V<=v<2V and satisfy |xi_v|<=tau_J(v).

For ell,v,p,h,q in the ranges
  ell in cal L, V<=v<2V,
  P<=p<2P with p prime and gcd(v,p)=1,
  h in I_ell, Q<=q<2Q with gcd(q,vp)=1,                    (2)
let
  w_{ell,v,p,h}(q)
   =c_q nu_h U_ell(q,h,v,p)
      e(Ah/(qvp))chi_ell(v,p,h,q),                          (3)
where every literal coefficient, scaled-smooth/projective factor, and zero-one source mask is retained in the displayed factors. Assume
  |w_{ell,v,p,h}(q)|<=B.                                    (4)
Put
  x_{ell,v,p,h}(q)
    =w_{ell,v,p,h}(q)e_{vp}(-Ahqbar),                       (5)
  X_{ell,v,p}(theta)
    =sum_{h in I_ell}sum_qx_{ell,v,p,h}(q)e(h theta),        (6)
  S_lit=H^(-1)sum_{ell,v,p}eta_ell xi_v
                  X_{ell,v,p}(0),                           (7)
where qbar is the inverse of q modulo vp and every q-sum is over (2). Define
  M_2^lit=sum_{ell,v,p}integral_{R/Z}
                  |X_{ell,v,p}(theta)|^2dtheta.             (8)

Assume subpolynomial label and coefficient complexity: for every delta>0,
  B+#cal L+sum_{ell in cal L}|eta_ell| <<_{C,J,delta}Q^delta. (9)
Then for every epsilon>0,
  |S_lit|^2<<_{C,J,epsilon}Q^(1+epsilon)M_2^lit.             (10)
Consequently the estimate
  M_2^lit<<_{C,J,epsilon}P Q^(5/3+epsilon)                  (11)
is sufficient for
  |S_lit|^2<<_{C,J,epsilon}P Q^(8/3+epsilon).               (12)

There is an exact same-height TT-star expansion
  M_2^lit=D_2+O_2,                                          (13)
where
  D_2=sum_{ell,v,p}sum_{h in I_ell}sum_q
          |w_{ell,v,p,h}(q)|^2,                             (14)
and
  O_2=sum_{ell,v,p}sum_{h in I_ell}
       sum_{q_1 not equal to q_2}
        w_{ell,v,p,h}(q_1)
        conjugate(w_{ell,v,p,h}(q_2))
        e_{vp}(-Ah(q_1bar-q_2bar)).                          (15)
The ordered-pair sum O_2 is real. It retains the same h, v, p, ell, every source mask, the Archimedean phases inside w, and the exact reciprocal phase modulo vp; no generic coefficient replacement or absolute value has been made.

The diagonal is paid:
  D_2<<_{C,J,epsilon}Q^(2+epsilon)H^2.                      (16)
Algebraically,
  Q^2H^2<=P Q^(5/3)
if and only if
  VH<=Q^(2/3).                                               (17)
The legal range (1) satisfies (17), because V<H and H<=Q^(1/3). Therefore the single remaining sufficient literal supplier in the exact decomposition (13) is the one-sided signed bound
  O_2<<_{C,J,epsilon}P Q^(5/3+epsilon).                     (18)
An absolute-value bound at the same scale would be stronger than needed.

There is a conditional envelope-only comparison. Suppose, in addition, that the exact coefficient identity and common translated-envelope hypotheses of fact 05cbed389411618a hold with one common translated interval of length O(vp/H) in every fixed ell,v,p row, physical amplitude L_0=Q^{o(1)}, and normalized row X_{ell,v,p}=H R_{ell,v,p}. Then
  M_2^lit<<Q^(3+epsilon)H.                                  (19)
Relative to (11), the power ratio in (19) is
  [Q^3H]/[P Q^(5/3)]=VQ^(1/3).                             (20)
The corresponding direct L4 ratio from fact 05cbed389411618a is Q^(2/3)V^2/H, larger than (20) by the factor Q^(1/3)V/H>=2. These are deficits of two particular upper-bound insertions, not lower bounds for the literal moments.

No estimate for (18), no PMD closure, and no Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
294ac3b02b065aec.proof:
Put
  C_2^2=sum_{ell,v,p}|eta_ell xi_v|^2.                      (21)
Cauchy's inequality in the outer variables gives
  |S_lit|^2
  <=H^(-2)C_2^2 sum_{ell,v,p}|X_{ell,v,p}(0)|^2.            (22)
Every I_ell contains at most H+1<=2H integers. A second Cauchy inequality in h, followed by Parseval in theta, gives
  |X_{ell,v,p}(0)|^2
  =|sum_{h in I_ell}sum_qx_{ell,v,p,h}(q)|^2
  <=2H sum_{h in I_ell}|sum_qx_{ell,v,p,h}(q)|^2
  =2H integral_{R/Z}|X_{ell,v,p}(theta)|^2dtheta.           (23)

Fact d061fc4dc153e309 proves
  sum_{V<=v<2V}|xi_v|^2/v<<_{J,epsilon}V^epsilon.
Since v<2V on this interval, it follows directly that
  sum_{V<=v<2V}|xi_v|^2
  <=2V sum_{V<=v<2V}|xi_v|^2/v
  <<_{J,epsilon}V^(1+epsilon)
  <<_{J,epsilon}VQ^epsilon.                                (24)
There are at most 2P integers, hence at most 2P primes, in [P,2P). Also
  sum_ell|eta_ell|^2<=(sum_ell|eta_ell|)^2.
Thus (9), (21), (24), and VP=QH imply
  C_2^2<<_{C,J,epsilon}Q^epsilon VP
       =Q^(1+epsilon)H.                                    (25)
Insert (23) and (25) in (22). The two factors H cancel, proving (10). Equations (11)-(12) follow immediately.

Parseval applied directly to (6) gives
  M_2^lit
   =sum_{ell,v,p}sum_{h in I_ell}
      |sum_qx_{ell,v,p,h}(q)|^2.                            (26)
Expand each square and split q_1=q_2 from q_1 not equal to q_2. Since the modular phase in (5) has modulus one, the equal-q part is (14). For unequal q, multiplying (5) by its conjugate gives exactly (15). Interchanging q_1 and q_2 conjugates a summand and preserves the ordered support, so O_2 is real. This proves (13)-(15) and all retention claims.

There are O(#cal L VPHQ) diagonal indices. Taking absolute values only on the diagonal and using (4) gives
  D_2<<B^2(#cal L)VPHQ.
Use (9) and VP=QH to obtain (16). Since P=QH/V,
  [Q^2H^2]/[P Q^(5/3)]
   =[Q^2H^2]/[Q^(8/3)H/V]
   =VH/Q^(2/3).
This proves (17). From V<H and H<=Q^(1/3),
  VH<H^2<=Q^(2/3),
so the diagonal is within (11). Equations (13), (16), and a one-sided upper bound (18) then imply (11); no estimate for the negative part of O_2 is required.

We prove the conditional comparison. Under the hypotheses cited there, write X_{ell,v,p}=H R_{ell,v,p}. The h-support has span less than p by the frequency and prime hypotheses in fact 05cbed389411618a. Therefore discrete orthogonality gives the L2 sampling identity
  integral_{R/Z}|R_{ell,v,p}(theta)|^2dtheta
   =p^(-1)sum_{t modulo p}|R_{ell,v,p}(t/p)|^2.             (27)
Indeed, after expanding both sides, the average over t kills h_1-h_2 unless p divides it; the span condition then forces h_1=h_2, exactly as continuous orthogonality does.

The translated target is -A. Facts 84bf915e8a88d8d3 and 3450c52083a2e548, with A replaced by -A, identify each sampled q-row with its common-envelope soft source and give uniformly in t
  |R_{ell,v,p}(t/p)|
  <=sum_q|b_{ell,v,p,t}(q)|
  <<L_0Q^(1+epsilon)/H.                                    (28)
Insert (28) in (27):
  integral|R_{ell,v,p}|^2
  <<L_0^2Q^(2+epsilon)/H^2.                                (29)
There are O(VP)=O(QH) outer pairs. Sum (29), multiply by H^2 because X=HR, and sum the subpolynomial labels. Absorb L_0 and the label count by renaming epsilon. This proves (19). Equation (20) follows from P=QH/V. Dividing the L4 ratio in fact 05cbed389411618a by (20) gives Q^(1/3)V/H, which is at least two by V>=2 and H<=Q^(1/3). The final comparison concerns only these derived upper bounds, proving all scope statements.

glossary.D_2: The q_1=q_2 diagonal in the exact Parseval expansion of M_2^lit.
glossary.M_2^lit: The sum of the integrated squared literal finite-band outer rows.
glossary.O_2: The real signed q_1 not equal to q_2 same-height TT-star kernel in the exact Parseval expansion of M_2^lit.

297d187974b59da2.title: FIXED-SMALL-EFFECTIVE-MODULUS COUNTEREXAMPLE TO UNIFORM BALANCED PRODUCT-BV POWER SAVING. For every sufficiently large integer R, put Q=R^2, n=2, C=1, c=1, and
297d187974b59da2.author: slava chan
297d187974b59da2.statement:
FIXED-SMALL-EFFECTIVE-MODULUS COUNTEREXAMPLE TO UNIFORM BALANCED PRODUCT-BV POWER SAVING. For every sufficiently large integer R, put Q=R^2, n=2, C=1, c=1, and
I={u in Z:R<=u<2R}.
Let W be the integer function equal to one on Q<=k<2Q and zero elsewhere. Then n is squarefree, m_eff=n/gcd(C,n)=2, V_Q(W)=3, and
S_R=sum_{u_1,u_2 in I;gcd(u_1u_2,2)=1}W(u_1u_2)e_2((u_1u_2)^(-1))
satisfies
|S_R|>=Q/100
for all sufficiently large R. Consequently no estimate |S_R|<=Q^(1-delta+o(1)) with fixed delta>0 can hold uniformly for the general balanced product-BV reciprocal class over all m_eff>1. This counterexample is an abstract one-row coefficient-class obstruction. It does not assert that n=2 occurs in the literal strict-top C1 support; that separate support question remains open.
297d187974b59da2.proof:
The function W has supremum one and exactly two unit jumps after zero extension, so V_Q(W)=1+2=3. The gate gcd(u_1u_2,2)=1 is equivalent to u_1 and u_2 both being odd. For every such pair, u_1u_2 is a unit modulo 2 and its inverse is congruent to one modulo 2. Therefore
e_2((u_1u_2)^(-1))=e_2(1)=-1.                              (1)
All nonzero summands have the same sign.

Restrict to the subset
R<=u_i<5R/4,  u_i odd,  i=1,2.
For these pairs,
Q=R^2<=u_1u_2<(5R/4)^2=25Q/16<2Q,
so W(u_1u_2)=1. Each interval [R,5R/4) contains at least R/10 odd integers for sufficiently large R. Hence this subset contains at least R^2/100=Q/100 pairs. By (1), every one contributes -1, and all other nonzero terms also contribute -1. Thus |S_R| is at least Q/100.

If a uniform bound Q^(1-delta+o(1)) held for some fixed delta>0, its ratio to Q would tend to zero, contradicting the displayed lower bound. The construction satisfies the general squarefree-modulus, unit-numerator, balanced-interval, product-BV, and coprimality hypotheses but imposes no literal C1 rough-prime support, proving precisely the stated scope.

glossary.tiny-effective complete-period obstructi: A fixed small effective modulus for which the unit reciprocal phase has nonzero complete-period mean and a BV product box has linear-size mass.

29c43cef40f2e79b.title: EXACT VAUGHAN IDENTITY AND (P^{1/3})-TO-(P^{1/2}) BOX RANGES
29c43cef40f2e79b.author: slava chan

glossary.Lambda_{>U}: The von Mangoldt function truncated to integers greater than U.
glossary.P: The scale of the decomposed von Mangoldt variable.
glossary.U: The Vaughan cutoff, specialized to P^(1/3).
glossary.mu_{<=U}: The Möbius function truncated to integers at most U.
glossary.mu_{>U}: The Möbius function truncated to integers greater than U.

2b4989d9d25f33cc.title: OFF-SCALE JOINT-COPRIMALITY CORRELATED ENERGY WITH QUARTER-POWER IMBALANCE
2b4989d9d25f33cc.author: slava chan
2b4989d9d25f33cc.statement:
OFF-SCALE JOINT-COPRIMALITY CORRELATED ENERGY WITH QUARTER-POWER IMBALANCE.

Fix integers J,C>=1, a real number tau>0, and real scales Q,H_P,H_T,U,Y>=1. Let G>=1 and assume
H_T=G H_P,
C^(-1)QH_T<=UY<=CQH_T,                                      (1)
H_T^2Q^tau<=Y<=Q^(1-tau)/H_T^2.                             (2)
For each integer q with Q<=q<2Q choose a unit V_q modulo q. Let A be a fixed nonzero integer. Let complex coefficients nu_h,alpha_u,beta_y be supported on
H_P<=h<2H_P, U<=u<2U, Y<=y<2Y
and satisfy
|nu_h|<=tau_J(h), |alpha_u|<=tau_J(u), |beta_y|<=tau_J(y).
Define
W_q^cop=sum_{h,u,y;(uy,q)=1,(u,y)=1}
 nu_h alpha_u beta_y e_q(A V_q h(uy)^(-1)).
Then for every epsilon>0,
H_P^(-1)sum_{Q<=q<2Q}|W_q^cop|
 <<_{J,C,tau,epsilon}
 (|A|QH_PUY)^epsilon
 [G^(1/4)Q^(2-tau/4)+Q^(2-tau/2)].                           (3)
In particular the only polynomial imbalance loss is G^(1/4). No condition gcd(A,q)=1 or gcd(h,q)=1 is imposed.
2b4989d9d25f33cc.proof:
Insert the exact Möbius identity
1_{(u,y)=1}=sum_{e|u,e|y}mu(e).
Write u=et and y=es. The condition (uy,q)=1 implies (e,q)=1, so the phase unit V_q is replaced by the unit V_qe^(-2) modulo q. Cover the resulting t- and s-intervals by an absolute number of dyadic intervals of scales T_e comparable to U/e and S_e comparable to Y/e. As in fact bd1ef0652fa7b940, after normalizing the coefficients by tau_J(e)^2, their fixed divisor bounds remain admissible.

Apply the full fixed-target estimate of fact 73fb9efe1286f7e9 with frequency H_P, first inverse factor S_e, and second inverse factor T_e. Divide by H_P and expand the two fourth roots. Using UY comparable to QH_T=GQH_P, the four terms for fixed e, apart from the common epsilon factor and tau_J(e)^2, are
e^(-5/4)G^(1/4)Q^2H_T^(1/2)Y^(-1/4),                       (4)
e^(-7/4)G^(1/4)Q^(7/4)H_T^(1/2)Y^(1/4),                    (5)
e^(-3/2)Q^2H_TY^(-1/2),                                     (6)
e^(-2)Q^(7/4)H_T.                                           (7)
For completeness, before replacing H_P by H_T/G, the first expression is
e^(-5/4)G^(3/4)Q^2H_P^(1/2)Y^(-1/4);
the other three follow by the same direct expansion. Thus (4)-(7) agree with the natural-frequency ledger 42720f6d803c4640 and retain the additional e-powers produced by joint-coprimality removal.

For every fixed J and every exponent a>1,
sum_{e>=1}tau_J(e)^2e^(-a)<infinity,
as proved in fact bd1ef0652fa7b940 by its convergent Euler product. Hence the e-sums in (4)-(7) converge absolutely.

From (2),
H_T^(1/2)Y^(-1/4)<=Q^(-tau/4),
H_T^(1/2)Y^(1/4)<=Q^((1-tau)/4),
H_TY^(-1/2)<=Q^(-tau/2).                                    (8)
The two inequalities in (2) also imply
H_T<=Q^(1/4-tau/2).                                         (9)
Equations (4)-(9), after summing e, bound the first two terms by
G^(1/4)Q^(2-tau/4)
and the last two by Q^(2-tau/2). Restoring the fixed-target epsilon factor proves (3). The fixed-target extension of fact 73fb9efe1286f7e9 permits arbitrary gcd(A,q), the unit twist remains a unit after multiplication by e^(-2), and that fact imposes no gcd condition on h.

glossary.G: The imbalance ratio H_T/H_P in the off-scale coprime trace.
glossary.H_P: The natural Poisson frequency scale in the off-scale coprime trace.
glossary.H_T: The model trace frequency scale controlling the total inverse-product length.

2b5e86cdf81bb711.title: STRICT-TOP MIXED \(J_qI_n\) PAYMENT BY RECIPROCITY BACK TO THE SHORT MODULUS. Retain the literal complete-provenance signed-block source \(\Phi_F(q,n)\) of fact a21645b0ae152b3f and the exact DOUBLE-VAUGHAN-QN operators of fact a75ea6a8a40dd1f8. Thus
2b5e86cdf81bb711.author: slava chan
2b5e86cdf81bb711.statement:
STRICT-TOP MIXED \(J_qI_n\) PAYMENT BY RECIPROCITY BACK TO THE SHORT MODULUS. Retain the literal complete-provenance signed-block source \(\Phi_F(q,n)\) of fact a21645b0ae152b3f and the exact DOUBLE-VAUGHAN-QN operators of fact a75ea6a8a40dd1f8. Thus
\[
 \beta_m<\beta<6/5,\qquad B=Q^\beta,
\]
and the phase in \(\Phi_F\) is
\[
 e_n(\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\overline q).
\]
Choose integer cutoffs
\[
 {1\over2}Q^{1/12}\le V_q,V_n\le Q^{1/12}                  \tag{1}
\]
for sufficiently large \(Q\). These are legal because \(V_q\le Q_0^{1/2}\) and \(V_n\le B_0^{1/2}\).

For one signed dyadic frequency block define
\[
 {\cal T}_{J_qI_n,F}
 ={\cal J}_{q,V_q}{\cal I}_{n,V_n}\Phi_F.                  \tag{2}
\]
For every fixed \(A>0\),
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 |{\cal T}_{J_qI_n,F}|
 \ll_A Q^{o(1)}
 \left(B+V_n^2Q^{3/2}\right)
 {F\over H_P}(1+F/H_P)^{-A}.
 \quad}                                                     \tag{3}
\]
