Consequently, after the complete signed dyadic-frequency and standard source/projective reconstruction,
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \sum_F|{\cal T}_{J_qI_n,F}|
 \ll Q^{o(1)}(B+Q^{5/3})
 \ll Q^{2-1/4}.
 \quad}                                                     \tag{4}
\]
Thus, together with fact a21645b0ae152b3f, every DOUBLE-VAUGHAN-QN term except \(J_qJ_n\) is paid with a fixed power saving throughout \(\beta_m<\beta<6/5\). The exact remaining term retains both long Möbius factors \(\mu(m)\mu(\ell)\), both frequency signs, the fixed possibly nonunit target, and all literal gcd gates. No estimate for \(J_qJ_n\), no critical \(\beta\ge6/5\) payment, and no post-A or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
2b5e86cdf81bb711.proof:
Expand (2) using fact a75ea6a8a40dd1f8:
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 {\cal T}_{J_qI_n,F}
 ={1\over H_P}
 \sum_{\substack{V_q<d\le Q_1/V_q\\e\le V_n^2}}
 b_{V_q}(d)a_{V_n}(e)
 \sum_{\substack{\max\{V_q,Q_0/d\}<m\le Q_1/d\\
                  B_0/e<\ell\le B_1/e}}
 &\mu(m)\,
 {\bf1}_{(g,dm\,e\ell)=(dm,e\ell)=1}\\
 &\times\sum_{F\le|h|<2F}
 {\cal C}^{\flat}_{g,dm,e\ell}(h)
 e_{e\ell}(\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\overline{dm}).
                                                               \tag{5}
 \end{aligned}
\]
Here the notation \({\cal C}^{\flat}\) is that of fact ecd6325d7ef2bc37; any harmless normalized projective factor can be kept inside this literal coefficient.

For coprime \(q,n\), fact ecd6325d7ef2bc37 gives the exact reverse form of additive reciprocity
\[
 e_n(\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\overline q)
 =
 e\!\left({\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\over qn}\right)
 e_q(-\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\overline n).                    \tag{6}
\]
Put \(q=dm\), \(n=e\ell\), and combine the ordinary exponential in (6) with the literal coefficient:
\[
 {\cal C}^{\sharp}_{g,q,n}(h)
 ={\cal C}^{\flat}_{g,q,n}(h)
 e\!\left({\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\over qn}\right).            \tag{7}
\]
This is exactly the complete-provenance Archimedean coefficient audited in facts 062a7f6f0c58b1f2 and 544c7ba4db45c06f.

Fix \(d,m,e,h\) on a nonzero row. Equation (10) in fact 062a7f6f0c58b1f2, composed with the normalized variable \(n/B=e\ell/B\), proves
\[
 \sup_\ell|{\cal C}^{\sharp}_{g,dm,e\ell}(h)|
 +\sum_\ell|{\cal C}^{\sharp}_{g,dm,e(\ell+1)}(h)
             -{\cal C}^{\sharp}_{g,dm,e\ell}(h)|
 \ll_A(\log x)^C(1+F/H_P)^{-A},                             \tag{8}
\]
including the two endpoint jumps from zero extension. This uses the full derivative audit, not merely the separated supremum bound.

A nonzero row in (5) has \((e,qg)=1\) and \((q,g)=1\). Its remaining \(\ell\)-conditions are
\[
 (\ell,q)=1,\qquad(\ell,g)=1,
\]
and (6) gives the reciprocal phase
\[
 e_q(-\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\,\overline e\,\overline\ell).   \tag{9}
\]
Apply Abel summation using (8), then expand \({\bf1}_{(\ell,g)=1}\). Exactly as in fact 8138369f26f88aad, divisors of \(g\) which are not units modulo \(q\) give empty rows, while the others become unit multipliers in the numerator. Irving's incomplete reciprocal-sum estimate, reproduced in that fact, yields
\[
 \sum_{\substack{B_0/e<\ell\le B_1/e\\(\ell,qg)=1}}
 {\cal C}^{\sharp}_{g,q,e\ell}(h)
 e_q(-\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\overline{e\ell})
 \ll_A(\log x)^C(1+F/H_P)^{-A}\tau(g)q^\varepsilon
 \left((L_{\rm src}h,q)\left({B\over eq}+1\right)+q^{1/2}\right).
                                                               \tag{10}
\]
No coprimality of \(L_{\rm src}h\) with \(q\) is required.

We sum (10) over the q-Type-II representations. For \(Q_0<q\le Q_1\), their absolute multiplicity is at most
\[
 w(q)=\sum_{d\mid q}|b_{V_q}(d)|
 \le2\sum_{d\mid q}\tau(d)=2\tau_3(q)\ll q^{o(1)},           \tag{11}
\]
where enlarging the actual Type-II d-range only increases the right side. For every nonzero integer \(a\),
\[
 \sum_{q\asymp Q}(a,q)\ll Q\tau(|a|),                       \tag{12}
\]
by the divisor argument used in fact a21645b0ae152b3f. Since \(q\asymp Q\), (10)-(12) give, for fixed \(e,h\),
\[
 \sum_{\substack{d,m\\dm\asymp Q}}
 |b_{V_q}(d)\mu(m)|\,|\hbox{the \(\ell\)-sum}|
 \ll_A Q^{o(1)}(\log x)^C(1+F/H_P)^{-A}
 \left({B\over e}+Q+Q^{3/2}\right).                         \tag{13}
\]
The fixed source gates only delete terms.

Fact a75ea6a8a40dd1f8 gives \(|a_{V_n}(e)|\le2\tau(e)\). Therefore
\[
 \sum_{e\le V_n^2}{|a_{V_n}(e)|\over e}\ll Q^{o(1)},\qquad
 \sum_{e\le V_n^2}|a_{V_n}(e)|\ll V_n^2Q^{o(1)}.             \tag{14}
\]
Combining (13)-(14), summing the \(O(F)\) h-values and dividing by \(H_P\), proves (3). The factors involving \(g,L_{\rm src},h\) are absorbed exactly as in fact a21645b0ae152b3f, using the strict-top polynomial size relations and arbitrary-order frequency decay.

For \(A>3\), the dyadic sum of
\[
 {F\over H_P}(1+F/H_P)^{-A}
\]
is bounded, including \(H_P<1\). The complete source reconstruction costs only \(Q^{o(1)}\) by facts ecd6325d7ef2bc37 and 544c7ba4db45c06f. From (1),
\[
 V_n^2Q^{3/2}\le Q^{5/3},\qquad B=Q^\beta<Q^{6/5}.           \tag{15}
\]
A uniform \(Q^{o(1)}\) factor is at most \(Q^{1/12}\) for sufficiently large \(Q\); (15) then gives (4).

Fact a21645b0ae152b3f pays \(I_q(I_n+J_n)\), while the present result pays \(J_qI_n\). Exact exhaustiveness of fact a75ea6a8a40dd1f8 leaves only \(J_qJ_n\), whose displayed formula contains \(\mu(m)\mu(\ell)\). This proves the ledger and retention assertions.

glossary.mathcal C^{sharp}: The literal coefficient C^{flat} after the Archimedean reciprocity phase is restored.
glossary.mathcal T_{J_qI_n,F}: The complete signed-frequency-block mixed Type-II/Type-I term in DOUBLE-VAUGHAN-QN.

2b772de4be61298c.title: MODULUS-DEPENDENT-UNIT EXTENSION OF THE RAISED-STOPPING TRACE. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, integers J>=1 and C_A>=1, and put sigma=kappa/100. Let 1<=beta<=6/5-2kappa. For sufficiently large Q define
2b772de4be61298c.author: slava chan
2b772de4be61298c.statement:
MODULUS-DEPENDENT-UNIT EXTENSION OF THE RAISED-STOPPING TRACE. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, integers J>=1 and C_A>=1, and put sigma=kappa/100. Let 1<=beta<=6/5-2kappa. For sufficiently large Q define
R=Q^beta, H=R/Q, L=H Q^sigma, S_0=H^2 Q^(3sigma), Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma), I=(L,Z).
For an integer u define
omega_L(u)=#{p: p is prime, p divides u, p<=L},
j_I(u)=#{p: p is prime, p divides u, L<p<Z}.
For k>=2 define
Gamma_k(y)=1_{y squarefree, omega_L(y)=k, P^+(y)<=L, S_0<y}
times k^(-1) #{p: p is prime, p divides y, y/p<=S_0}.
Let U,Y>=1 be dyadic scales for which there exist integers u,y satisfying
U<=u<2U, Y<=y<2Y, R<=uy<2R, Gamma_k(y) nonzero.
Let A be a nonzero integer with |A|<=Q^(C_A). For every integer q with Q<=q<2Q choose an invertible residue V_q modulo q. Let complex coefficients c_q and nu_h satisfy |c_q|<=1 and |nu_h|<=tau_J(h), supported respectively on Q<=q<2Q and H<=h<2H. Let Psi range over a fixed bounded scaled-smooth family on the positive four-dimensional orthant, supported in [1,2]^4, with every logarithmic derivative uniformly bounded. Put e_q(t)=exp(2 pi i t/q), and define
cal T^V_{k,U,Y}(Psi;A)
=H^(-1) sum_{Q<=q<2Q} c_q
 sum_{H<=h<2H, U<=u<2U, Y<=y<2Y, gcd(uy,q)=1, gcd(u,y)=1}
nu_h [(-1)^k mu(u) 1_{j_I(u)=0} Gamma_k(y)/binom(k+omega_L(u),k)]
Psi(q/Q,h/H,u/U,y/Y) e_q(A V_q h (uy)^(-1)).
Then, uniformly in every choice of the units V_q,
|cal T^V_{k,U,Y}(Psi;A)| <<_{kappa,J,C_A,Psi} Q^(2-delta),
where delta=sigma/8 is admissible. The same bound, with the implied constant adjusted, holds after summing by the triangle inequality over all nonempty triples (k,U,Y) above, whose number is O_kappa((log Q)^3), and over at most O((log Q)^C) further dyadic, sign, or scaled-smooth separation labels for any fixed C. No condition gcd(A,q)=1 is required.
2b772de4be61298c.proof:
Predecessor e18b670f5d48f500 applies to the displayed scales. It gives
H^2 Q^(2sigma) <= Y <= Q^(1-2sigma)/H^2
and
(1/4)QH < UY < 2QH.
Thus the hypotheses of predecessor bd1ef0652fa7b940 hold with exponent margin tau=2sigma and comparability constant 4.

We separate Psi exactly as in the proof of predecessor 533acf4056cf5bee. In logarithmic coordinates on its fixed compact support, extend Psi to a smooth function on a fixed four-dimensional torus. Its Fourier series is an absolutely summable linear combination of products
f_n(q) g_n(h) a_n(u) b_n(y),
where every one-variable factor has absolute value at most one and the sum of the absolute Fourier coefficients is bounded uniformly over the scaled-smooth family.

For one Fourier mode, absorb g_n into nu_h and put
alpha_u=a_n(u)(-1)^k mu(u)1_{j_I(u)=0}/binom(k+omega_L(u),k),
beta_y=b_n(y)Gamma_k(y).
The definitions give |alpha_u|<=1 and |beta_y|<=1. Absorb f_n into c_q. Equation (7) of predecessor bd1ef0652fa7b940 explicitly permits the fixed nonzero integer A multiplied by an arbitrary unit V_q modulo q, without assuming gcd(A,q)=1. It also retains gcd(u,y)=1 and imposes no coprimality condition on h. Therefore, for every epsilon>0, it yields
|cal T^V_{k,U,Y}(Psi;A)| << (|A|QHUY)^epsilon Q^(2-sigma/2)
for one Fourier mode. Absolute summability of the Fourier coefficients gives the same estimate for Psi.

All displayed scales and |A| are bounded by fixed powers of Q. Choose epsilon sufficiently small in terms of sigma and C_A so that the epsilon factor is at most Q^(sigma/4). We obtain Q^(2-sigma/4), which implies the stated Q^(2-sigma/8).

Finally, nonempty support gives 2^k<=y<2R, hence k=O_kappa(log Q). Both u and y are below 2R and therefore occupy O_kappa(log Q) dyadic intervals each. The nonempty triples number O_kappa((log Q)^3). The stated O((log Q)^C) auxiliary labels contribute only Q^(o(1)), absorbed by the gap between sigma/4 and sigma/8. Summing Gamma_k over k is the exact stopping coefficient by predecessor 533acf4056cf5bee; V_q changes only the phase and not that identity.

glossary.Gamma_k: The k-prime first-crossing stopping weight defined in the statement.
glossary.V_q: An arbitrary invertible residue class modulo q.
glossary.cal T^V_{k,U,Y}: The raised-stopping reciprocal trace with a fixed target multiplied by the modulus-dependent unit V_q.
glossary.e_q: The additive character e_q(t)=exp(2 pi i t/q).
glossary.j_I: The number of distinct prime divisors in the prime interval I.
glossary.omega_L: The number of distinct prime divisors at most L.

2bc35b8e8ac55aff.title: PRIMITIVE--PRIMITIVE COUPLING CANCELS THE PARTNER-MODULUS EVALUATIONS. Let r,r'>1 be coprime positive integers, put L=rr', and let c,c',h be integers coprime to L. For m>=1 put e_m(x)=exp(2 pi i x/m), let G_m be the group of units modulo m, and for a Dirichlet character theta modulo m put tau_m(theta)=sum_{x in G_m} theta(x)e_m(x). Let chi modulo r and psi modulo r' be primitive characters. For a function w:G_L->C define
2bc35b8e8ac55aff.author: slava chan
2bc35b8e8ac55aff.statement:
PRIMITIVE--PRIMITIVE COUPLING CANCELS THE PARTNER-MODULUS EVALUATIONS. Let r,r'>1 be coprime positive integers, put L=rr', and let c,c',h be integers coprime to L. For m>=1 put e_m(x)=exp(2 pi i x/m), let G_m be the group of units modulo m, and for a Dirichlet character theta modulo m put tau_m(theta)=sum_{x in G_m} theta(x)e_m(x). Let chi modulo r and psi modulo r' be primitive characters. For a function w:G_L->C define
widehat w_L(t)=sum_{j in G_L}w(j)e_L(-tj)  (t modulo L).
For unit residues, bars denote multiplicative inverses in the modulus of the character being evaluated. Define
Sigma_{chi,psi}(w;h)=sum_{t in G_L} widehat w_L(t) chi(ht) overline{chi(r')} overline{psi(-ht)} psi(r).
Then
Sigma_{chi,psi}(w;h)
=tau_r(chi)tau_{r'}(overline psi)
 sum_{j in G_L} w(j) chi(-h overline j) psi(j overline h).                 (1)
In particular the partner evaluations overline{chi(r')}psi(r) have disappeared exactly; they must not be estimated separately before the t-sum. If
m_{r,c}(chi)=chi(c)tau_r(overline chi)^2/r,
m_{r',c'}(psi)=psi(c')tau_{r'}(overline psi)^2/r',
then
m_{r,c}(chi) overline{m_{r',c'}(psi)} Sigma_{chi,psi}(w;h)
=chi(-c)overline{psi(-c')}tau_r(overline chi)tau_{r'}(psi)
 sum_{j in G_L} w(j)chi(-h overline j)psi(j overline h).                  (2)
The scalar prefactor on the right of (2) has absolute value sqrt(L). Equations (1)--(2) are exact identities for each primitive character pair and each common physical weight w; they assert no large-sieve or operator-norm estimate.
2bc35b8e8ac55aff.proof:
Lift chi and overline psi to characters modulo L and put eta=chi overline psi. Since r and r' are coprime and chi and psi are primitive, the CRT decomposition G_L=G_r x G_{r'} shows that eta is primitive modulo L.

We first record two elementary Gauss identities. If theta is primitive modulo m and (a,m)=1, then
sum_{x in G_m}theta(x)e_m(ax)=overline{theta(a)}tau_m(theta).             (3)
This follows by the bijection x -> overline a x. Also
tau_m(theta)tau_m(overline theta)=theta(-1)m.                            (4)
Indeed, expanding the product and writing the first variable as uy with u,y in G_m gives
tau_m(theta)tau_m(overline theta)
=sum_{u in G_m}theta(u) sum_{y in G_m}e_m((u+1)y).
For primitive theta, the inner Ramanujan-sum calculation (or the standard additive-Parseval proof) gives (4). For completeness, one may instead first prove |tau_m(theta)|^2=m: the additive Fourier transform of the zero extension of theta is overline{theta(a)}tau_m(theta) at every unit a by (3), and is zero at every nonunit a because primitivity supplies a unit u congruent to 1 modulo m/(m,a) with theta(u) !=1, so multiplication by u fixes the additive phase and forces that Fourier coefficient to vanish. Additive Parseval then gives phi(m)|tau_m(theta)|^2=m phi(m). Finally conjugating the definition gives overline{tau_m(theta)}=overline{theta(-1)}tau_m(overline theta), which yields (4).

Expand widehat w_L in the definition of Sigma. Applying (3) to eta with additive coefficient -j gives
sum_{t in G_L}eta(t)e_L(-tj)=overline{eta(-j)}tau_L(eta).
Therefore
Sigma_{chi,psi}
=chi(h)overline{psi(-h)}overline{chi(r')}psi(r)tau_L(eta)
 sum_{j in G_L}w(j)overline{eta(-j)}.                                   (5)
The CRT decomposition of the additive character is
e_L(x)=e_r(x overline{r'})e_{r'}(x overline r).
Consequently
tau_L(eta)
=[sum_{x in G_r}chi(x)e_r(x overline{r'})]
 [sum_{y in G_{r'}}overline{psi(y)}e_{r'}(y overline r)]
=chi(r')overline{psi(r)}tau_r(chi)tau_{r'}(overline psi),                (6)
where (3) was used in each factor. Substitution of (6) into (5) cancels overline{chi(r')}psi(r). Moreover
chi(h)overline{chi(-j)}=chi(-h overline j),
overline{psi(-h)}psi(-j)=psi(j overline h).
This proves (1).

It remains to combine the local multipliers. By (4),
m_{r,c}(chi)tau_r(chi)
=chi(c)tau_r(overline chi)^2 tau_r(chi)/r
=chi(-c)tau_r(overline chi).                                            (7)
Conjugating the definition of m_{r',c'} and using (4) similarly gives
overline{m_{r',c'}(psi)}tau_{r'}(overline psi)
=overline{psi(-c')}tau_{r'}(psi).                                       (8)
Multiplying (1) by the two multipliers and using (7)--(8) proves (2). The proof of (4) above also gives |tau_r(overline chi)|=sqrt(r) and |tau_{r'}(psi)|=sqrt(r'), hence the last magnitude assertion.

glossary.Sigma_{chi,psi}(w;h): the coupled unit-axis completion sum for a primitive character pair
glossary.eta: the CRT product character chi times conjugate(psi) modulo L

2ccb8f56e6084b34.title: SYMMETRIC LARGE-FACTOR HC-MED MARKING: AUTOMATIC ALLOCATION AND NORMALIZED PROJECTIVE MAIN ROW. Adopt one h-row of fact edabb9a0d2959b41, put X=X_h=B/h, and assume
2ccb8f56e6084b34.author: slava chan
2ccb8f56e6084b34.statement:
SYMMETRIC LARGE-FACTOR HC-MED MARKING: AUTOMATIC ALLOCATION AND NORMALIZED PROJECTIVE MAIN ROW. Adopt one h-row of fact edabb9a0d2959b41, put X=X_h=B/h, and assume
Q_c=X^(1/2+delta_h), eta<=3/20+6delta_h.                       (1)
Restrict to the fundamental-domain HC-MED support
d<=m, X^eta<=d<=X^(1/4+eta), X<=dm<2X.                           (2)
Let the selected prime scale satisfy Maynard's necessary lower bound
P>=X^(2/5+6delta_h)(log X)^(2C),                                (3)
and apply the fractional-Ramare identity of fact e59f666ecac4d4cb to the large factor rho_{1/2}(m), writing m=pm'. Then every selected p and every retained d satisfy p>d. Hence d<m automatically, the fundamental-domain weight omega_diag is exactly 2, and it cancels the fractional-Ramare factor -1/2.

Put v=dm', c_*=cR_kappa, C_D=||Psi_D||_infinity, C_M=||Psi_M||_infinity, H_D=max(1,C_D), and let L_lit bound |A_lit|. Before the p|m' correction, define the auxiliary all-selected-primes main coefficient
Vtilde^{large}_{q,kappa,h}(p,v)
 =-1_{(v,c_*)=1} sum_{dm'=v,X^eta<=d<=X^(1/4+eta)}
 rho_{1/2}(d)b_{P,c_*}^{rho}(m')
 Psi_D(d)Psi_M(pm')
 A_lit(q,kappa,hpv;(ell-kappa hpv)/q),                            (4)
with all original sampled supports retained but without imposing (p,c_*)=1. On (p,c_*)=1, (4) is exactly the actual unrestricted symmetric large-factor marked main coefficient on this HC-MED cell.

There are countable modes with theta_{j,k}=tau_j+sigma_k,
A^*_{j,k}(p)=1_{p prime}1_{P<=p<2P}
 p^(i theta_{j,k})/(1+|theta_{j,k}|),                            (5)
B^{large,*}_{j,k}(v)
 =H_D^(-1)v^(i tau_j)1_{(v,c_*)=1}
  sum_{d|v,X^eta<=d<=X^(1/4+eta)}
  rho_{1/2}(d)b_{P,c_*}^{rho}(v/d)
  (v/d)^(i sigma_k)Psi_D(d),                                    (6)
and outer coefficients
Lambda^{large,*}_{j,k;q,kappa,h}
 =-H_D lambda_{j,q,kappa,h}a_k(1+|theta_{j,k}|)                 (7)
such that (4) equals
sum_{j,k}Lambda^{large,*}_{j,k;q,kappa,h}
 A^*_{j,k}(p)B^{large,*}_{j,k}(v).                              (8)
The series is absolutely and uniformly convergent,
sum_{j,k}sup_{q,kappa,h}|Lambda^{large,*}_{j,k;q,kappa,h}|
 <<(log x)^(C_large),                                            (9)
|A^*_{j,k}(n)|<=1, |B^{large,*}_{j,k}(n)|<=tau(n),
|Vtilde^{large}_{q,kappa,h}(p,v)|<=L_lit C_D C_M tau(v),         (10)
and all prime modes satisfy Maynard's Siegel-Walfisz condition uniformly.

Thus the main-row coefficient hypotheses of the direct folded theorem e3c0786d33d7e576 are fulfilled for the symmetric large-factor marked HC-MED sector. Under that theorem's additional factorable-modulus, squarefree, injective, reduced-residue, and (s,c_*)=1 hypotheses, the main row is paid with its stated Type-II bound and explicit p|c_* deletion cost. The p|m' fractional-Ramare correction, omega_P(m)=0 complement, nonfactorable/no-scale modulus rows, boundary aggregation, and complete HC-MED or critical-tail payment are not asserted.
2ccb8f56e6084b34.proof:
From (2), d<=X^(1/4+eta). From (1), eta<=3/20+6delta_h, so d<=X^(2/5+6delta_h). Every selected p satisfies p>=P. Equation (3) therefore gives p>d for sufficiently large X because of the positive logarithmic factor. Since m=pm', this implies d<m. Thus omega_diag(d,m)=2 by fact edabb9a0d2959b41. Fact e59f666ecac4d4cb contributes -1/2 to the unrestricted fractional-Ramare main term, and their product is -1. Folding v=dm' gives exactly (4), including the HC-MED d-marker, both smooth cutoffs, the unit condition on v, and the literal product pv=dm. Omitting (p,c_*)=1 only defines the auxiliary extension needed before the prime-unit comparison.

Fact 97cfedc76bcae0ad gives
A_lit(q,kappa,hpv;(ell-kappa hpv)/q)
 =sum_j lambda_{j,q,kappa,h}p^(i tau_j)v^(i tau_j)
on the complete sampled rectangle. Its all-order logarithmic derivative bounds and three integrations by parts give
sum_j sup|lambda_j|(1+|tau_j|)<<(log x)^(C_1).                  (11)
Apply the same compact-interval Fourier construction to Psi_M(pm') as a function of log(pm'):
Psi_M(pm')=sum_k a_k p^(i sigma_k)(m')^(i sigma_k),
sum_k|a_k|(1+|sigma_k|)<<1.                                     (12)
Substitute m'=v/d into (4), insert (11)-(12), and collect the p powers. Definitions (5)-(7) then give (8) exactly. The HC-MED restriction stays inside the divisor sum in (6); it is independent of p and does not affect projectivity.

Since 1+|tau_j+sigma_k|<=(1+|tau_j|)(1+|sigma_k|), equations (11)-(12) prove (9). Facts 5999a1878276ac78 and e59f666ecac4d4cb give |rho_{1/2}|<=1 and |b_{P,c_*}^{rho}|<=1. Hence the unnormalized sum in (6) is at most C_D tau(v), proving its bound after division by H_D. The same divisor count applied to (4), with |Psi_M|<=C_M and |A_lit|<=L_lit, proves the reconstructed bound in (10).

Fact 0025283165f465c4 proves uniform Maynard Siegel-Walfisz for the normalized twist on P<p<=2P. The support in (5) is P<=p<2P. The two supports differ only at the integer endpoints P and 2P. In any centered progression discrepancy, changing one endpoint prime changes the physical sum by at most 1 and the principal sum by at most 1/phi(q)<=1; the normalization (1+|theta|)^(-1) makes this bound uniform in theta. Thus changing both endpoints costs at most 4. For P>=3 this is absorbed into C_A P(log P)^(-A) after enlarging the A-dependent constant, including the bounded range of P. Therefore every mode (5) satisfies Maynard's condition uniformly.

Consequently (8)-(10) are exactly the coefficient assumptions of fact e3c0786d33d7e576. That theorem consumes the already-folded coefficient without inserting another Ramaré factor and legally restores (p,c_*)=1 under (s,c_*)=1. The final exclusions record the terms not contained in the unrestricted main row (4).

glossary.B^{large,*}_{j,k}(v): The normalized cofactor mode after folding v=dm' in the large-factor marking.
glossary.C_large: A fixed exponent controlling the large-factor weighted projective norm.
glossary.Lambda^{large,*}_{j,k;q,kappa,h}: The weighted outer Fourier coefficient for the large-factor marking.
glossary.Vtilde^{large}_{q,kappa,h}(p,v): The auxiliary already-folded main coefficient obtained by marking a selected prime in the large half-convolution factor m.

2d553c87dc18dd6c.title: AUTOMATIC CLEANNESS AND FIXED-TARGET EXCEPTION BOUND ON THE DIAGONAL-COMPATIBLE \(E_{11}\) DILATOR RANGE. Fix real numbers
2d553c87dc18dd6c.author: slava chan
2d553c87dc18dd6c.statement:
AUTOMATIC CLEANNESS AND FIXED-TARGET EXCEPTION BOUND ON THE DIAGONAL-COMPATIBLE \(E_{11}\) DILATOR RANGE. Fix real numbers
\[
 0<\eta<1/120,\qquad 4/3\le\beta\le4/3+6\eta,\qquad \delta>0,
\]
and put
\[
 a_E=1/3-15\eta,\qquad
 R=D^\beta,\qquad
 Y=\frac12(R/D)D^{a_E}. \tag{1}
\]
Let \(D\) be sufficiently large in terms of \(\eta,\delta\), let
\[
 \theta\ge2(\beta-1)+\delta,\qquad P\ge D^\theta, \tag{2}
\]
and let \(a,b\) be distinct primes in \([P,2P]\). Let \(m,r\) be positive integers and \(h\ne0\) be an integer such that
\[
 |h|<Y,\qquad am\ \hbox{and}\ bm\ \hbox{are squarefree},\qquad
 (am,r)=(bm,r)=1. \tag{3}
\]
Then
\[
 (ab,mhr)=1. \tag{4}
\]
Consequently, for every positive integer \(N\) satisfying \((ab,N)=1\), the full clean-dilator condition
\[
 (ab,mhrN)=1 \tag{5}
\]
holds.

There is also a uniform exceptional-target ledger. Suppose \(N\ge2\), \(X\le C_1D\), and complex numbers \(z_n\), \(1\le n\le X\), satisfy
\[
 |z_n|\le ZR \tag{6}
\]
for fixed \(C_1,Z>0\). Then
\[
 \sum_{\substack{a\ {\rm prime}\\P\le a\le2P\\a\mid N}}
 \ \sum_{m\le X/a}|z_{am}|
 \le C_1 ZR\frac DP\frac{\log N}{\log P}. \tag{7}
\]
If, in addition,
\[
 N\le C_2D^2(\log D)^{C_3} \tag{8}
\]
for fixed \(C_2,C_3>0\), then
\[
 \sum_{\substack{a\ {\rm prime}\\P\le a\le2P\\a\mid N}}
 \ \sum_{m\le X/a}|z_{am}|
 \ll_{\eta,\delta,C_1,C_2,C_3} ZD^{5/3-\delta}. \tag{9}
\]
Thus the only failure of (5) on this range, a dilator dividing the fixed target \(N\), has an absolute power-saving ledger relative to the \(D^2\) scale whenever \(Z\le D^{o(1)}\).
2d553c87dc18dd6c.proof:
From (1),
\[
 Y=\frac12D^{\beta-2/3-15\eta}. \tag{10}
\]
The exponent gap between the lower bound for \(\theta\) in (2) and the exponent in (10) is
\[
 2(\beta-1)+\delta-(\beta-2/3-15\eta)
 =\beta-4/3+15\eta+\delta
 \ge15\eta+\delta>0. \tag{11}
\]
Hence, for sufficiently large \(D\),
\[
 a,b\ge P\ge D^\theta>Y>|h|.
\]
Since \(h\ne0\), neither \(a\) nor \(b\) divides \(h\).

Squarefreeness of \(am\) gives \(a\nmid m\), and squarefreeness of \(bm\) gives \(b\nmid m\). Also \((am,r)=1\) gives \(a\nmid r\), while \((bm,r)=1\) gives \(b\nmid r\). Because \(a,b\) are distinct primes, these observations prove (4). Adding \((ab,N)=1\) proves (5).

Let \(k\) be the number of primes \(a\in[P,2P]\) dividing \(N\). Their product divides \(N\) and is at least \(P^k\), so
\[
 k\log P\le\log N,\qquad k\le\frac{\log N}{\log P}. \tag{12}
\]
For each such \(a\), (6) gives
\[
 \sum_{m\le X/a}|z_{am}|
 \le ZR\frac Xa
 \le C_1ZR\frac DP.
\]
Summing this over the at most \(k\) primes and using (12) proves (7).

Under (8) and \(P\ge D^\theta\), the quotient \(\log N/\log P\) is bounded by a constant depending only on the displayed fixed parameters when \(D\) is sufficiently large. Therefore (7) is
\[
 \ll ZR D/P
 \le ZD^{\beta+1-\theta}
 \le ZD^{3-\beta-\delta}
 \le ZD^{5/3-\delta}, \tag{13}
\]
because \(\theta\ge2(\beta-1)+\delta\) and \(\beta\ge4/3\). This proves (9) and every assertion.

glossary.Y: the E11 frequency cutoff one half times (R/D)D^(a_E)
glossary.theta: the logarithmic D-exponent of the dilator scale P
glossary.z_n: an arbitrary scalar sequence with coordinate-envelope bound ZR

2d6fadb9f8bc513b.title: EXACT MULTIPLICATIVE CONDUCTOR-GENERATING TENSOR AND MELLIN RECOMBINATION OF SMOOTH CEN-MZB BLOCKS
2d6fadb9f8bc513b.author: slava chan
2d6fadb9f8bc513b.statement:
EXACT MULTIPLICATIVE CONDUCTOR-GENERATING TENSOR AND MELLIN RECOMBINATION OF SMOOTH CEN-MZB BLOCKS.

Let b be squarefree and let (a,b)=1. For each prime p|b with p not dividing N, choose an arbitrary complex number z_p. Define
 G_b(z;a)
  =sum_{f|b;(f,N)=1}
     [c_{b/f}(N)/phi(b/f)]
     [product_{p|f}z_p]R_{b,f}(a),                           (1)
where the empty product is one. Then exactly
 G_b(z;a)
  =product_{p|b;p not dividing N}
    {z_p e_p(N[a(b/p)]^(-1))+(z_p-1)/(p-1)}.                (2)
Primes p|b with p|N contribute the local factor one and are omitted from the product.

The normalized complete-unit mean is independent of all z_p:
 1/phi(b) sum_{a modulo b;(a,b)=1}G_b(z;a)
  =c_b(N)/phi(b).                                           (3)
This is exactly the f=1 term in (1).

For real t set z_p=p^(it) and write G_{b,t}(a)=G_b(z;a). Let W be an infinitely differentiable complex function compactly supported in the positive reals, let F>0, and define
 W_hat(t)=integral_0^infinity W(y)y^(-it)dy/y.                (4)
Define the smooth conductor block
 H_{b,W,F}(a)
  =sum_{f|b;(f,N)=1}
     W(f/F)c_{b/f}(N)R_{b,f}(a)/phi(b/f).                   (5)
Then Mellin inversion gives the exact identity
 H_{b,W,F}(a)
  =1/(2pi) integral_R W_hat(t)F^(-it)G_{b,t}(a)dt.           (6)
Its complete-unit mean is
 1/phi(b)sum_{a modulo b;(a,b)=1}H_{b,W,F}(a)
  =W(1/F)c_b(N)/phi(b).                                     (7)
In particular, if W(1/F)=0, the smooth block is globally centered on the unit group modulo b.

For real t,
 |G_{b,t}(a)|
 <=product_{p|b;p not dividing N}[1+2/(p-1)]
 <<_epsilon b^epsilon                                       (8)
for every fixed epsilon>0.

The individual product G_{b,t} is generally not primewise centered: at each p not dividing N its local normalized unit mean is -1/(p-1). In (6), when W(1/F)=0, global centering is recovered only after the t-integral cancels the f=1 term. Thus applying absolute values separately in t is not an exact centering-preserving replacement unless that constant mode is separately paid. No estimate for a smooth block, the sharp cutoff f>F_0, CEN-MZB, C_small, or Goldbach is asserted.
2d6fadb9f8bc513b.proof:
Fix p|b. Because b is squarefree, membership of p in f is an independent local choice in the divisor sum (1).

Suppose first that p does not divide N. If p|f, its local contribution is
 z_p[e_p(N[a(b/p)]^(-1))+1/(p-1)]
by the definition of R_{b,f} in fact 14fe68fdcbfd99ff. If p does not divide f, then p divides b/f and the local cofactor contribution is
 c_p(N)/phi(p)=-1/(p-1).
Adding the two choices gives
 z_p e_p(N[a(b/p)]^(-1))+(z_p-1)/(p-1).                     (9)

If p|N, the condition (f,N)=1 forbids p|f. Hence p must lie in b/f, and
 c_p(N)/phi(p)=(p-1)/(p-1)=1.                               (10)
Multiplying (9) and (10) over p|b proves (2).

For p not dividing N, inversion and multiplication by the nonzero residue N(b/p)^(-1) permute the p-1 units, so
 1/(p-1)sum_{u modulo p;u nonzero}
   e_p(N[u(b/p)]^(-1))=-1/(p-1).                            (11)
The local normalized mean of (9) is therefore
 -z_p/(p-1)+(z_p-1)/(p-1)=-1/(p-1),                         (12)
independent of z_p. CRT multiplies the local means. Primes p|b,p|N contribute one by (10), while primes p|b,p not dividing N contribute -1/(p-1). For squarefree b this product is exactly c_b(N)/phi(b), proving (3). In (1), the f=1 term is c_b(N)/phi(b), so the final assertion following (3) also holds.

For compactly supported infinitely differentiable W, multiplicative Mellin inversion states
 W(y)=1/(2pi)integral_R W_hat(t)y^(it)dt.                    (13)
The transform W_hat decays faster than every fixed inverse power of 1+|t|, so the integral is absolutely convergent. Insert y=f/F into (13), multiply by the finite f-term in (5), and interchange the finite divisor sum with the absolutely convergent integral. Since
 f^(it)=product_{p|f}p^(it),
the inner divisor sum is G_{b,t}(a). This proves (6).

Average (6) over the complete unit group and use (3). Absolute convergence permits the interchange:
 1/phi(b)sum_a^*H_{b,W,F}(a)
 =c_b(N)/phi(b) times
   [1/(2pi)integral_R W_hat(t)F^(-it)dt].
By (13) at y=1/F, the bracket is W(1/F), proving (7).

For real t, |p^(it)|=1. The triangle inequality in each local factor of (2) gives
 |p^(it)e_p(*)+(p^(it)-1)/(p-1)|
 <=1+2/(p-1).
To prove (8), fix epsilon>0 and choose P_epsilon so that
 1+2/(p-1)<=p^epsilon
for all primes p>P_epsilon. The product over p<=P_epsilon is a constant depending only on epsilon, and the product over the remaining prime divisors is at most b^epsilon.

Finally, (12) proves that the individual t-product is not locally centered. Equation (7) shows that a block excluding f=1 is globally centered because its Mellin integral cancels the t-independent complete mean. This proves the stated warning and all scope restrictions.

glossary.G_b(z;a): The all-conductor centered generating tensor with arbitrary local conductor weights z_p.
glossary.H_{b,W,F}(a): A smooth conductor block of the complete centered conductor superposition.
glossary.W_hat(t): The multiplicative Mellin transform of W.

2d7140db8b7ad566.title: TWO-ENDPOINT PRIME-DILATION SCALE IDENTITY. Let p be an odd prime and put
2d7140db8b7ad566.author: slava chan
2d7140db8b7ad566.statement:
TWO-ENDPOINT PRIME-DILATION SCALE IDENTITY. Let p be an odd prime and put
lambda_p=p(p-2)/(p-1).                                          (1)
For i in {1,2}, let F_i be a continuous compactly supported complex function on R and define
G_i(s)=F_i(s/p).                                                  (2)
With the Fourier convention
widehat F_i(xi)=integral_R F_i(t)e(-xi t)dt,                      (3)
one has
widehat F_i(xi)={1/p}widehat G_i(xi/p),                           (4)
||G_i||_2^2=p||F_i||_2^2.                                       (5)
Consequently, for all real xi_1,xi_2,
lambda_p widehat F_1(xi_1)conjugate(widehat F_2(xi_2))
 ={p-2over p(p-1)}
  widehat G_1(xi_1/p)conjugate(widehat G_2(xi_2/p)),              (6)
and the coefficient on the right times the product of the two dilated L2 norms satisfies the exact scale identity
{p-2over p(p-1)}||G_1||_2||G_2||_2
 ={p-2over p-1}||F_1||_2||F_2||_2.                             (7)

Here lambda_p is the unique large p-local multiplier verified in fact 122bdf7f46de05e6. Equations (6)-(7) are only an abstract dilation ledger. They make no assertion that a particular literal Good-W endpoint aggregate is represented by F_i, and no claim about a pointwise Fourier bound or a complete bilinear Plancherel estimate. They prove no source cancellation, prime trace estimate, C-HILBERT-OP-SUP, tail payment, or Goldbach.
2d7140db8b7ad566.proof:
Continuity and compact support imply that every F_i belongs to both L1(R) and L2(R), so all displayed Fourier integrals and norms are finite. Substitute s=pt in the Fourier integral:
widehat G_i(eta)
 =integral_R F_i(s/p)e(-eta s)ds
 =p integral_R F_i(t)e(-p eta t)dt
 =p widehat F_i(p eta).
Taking eta=xi/p proves (4).

The same substitution gives
||G_i||_2^2
 =integral_R|F_i(s/p)|^2ds
 =p integral_R|F_i(t)|^2dt
 =p||F_i||_2^2,
proving (5).

Insert (4) for i=1,2 into the left side of (6). Since
lambda_p/p^2
 =[p(p-2)/(p-1)]/p^2
 =(p-2)/[p(p-1)],
equation (6) follows. Taking square roots in (5) gives
||G_1||_2||G_2||_2=p||F_1||_2||F_2||_2.
Multiplication by (p-2)/[p(p-1)] proves (7).

glossary.lambda_p: The unique large p-local multiplier p(p-2)/(p-1).
glossary.prime-dilation scale identity: The exact relation between the order-p multiplier, two Fourier dilations, and the corresponding L2 norm scaling.

2d839168a73eedfa.title: Fix
2d839168a73eedfa.author: slava chan
2d839168a73eedfa.proof:
If \((m,N)>1\), choose a prime \(p\mid(m,N)\). Then
\(p\mid P_1,P_2\). On a nonzero term of (1), both \(P_i\) are powers of
\(p\). The support of \(W\) gives
\[
 (2-\beta)x\le P_i\le(2-\alpha)x<2x.
\]
A genuine prime in this interval cannot divide \(N=2x\), because
\(N/p\) would be an integer strictly between one and two. Thus both
\(P_i\) are proper prime powers. The proper-prime-power count in fact
\(967520f427b111c5\), equation (10), gives (3).

Now assume \((m,N)=1\). Möbius inversion gives
\[
 \Lambda(P_i)=\sum_{q_i\mid P_i}\mu(q_i)\log(P_i/q_i),
\]
and the positive-part logarithm agrees with the ordinary logarithm on
the divisor support. This proves the expansion by (4).

Let \(p\mid q_i\) on a nonzero divisor tuple. If \(p\mid N\), then
\(p\mid P_i=N-mw_i\), where \(w_1=w,w_2=w-h\), would imply
\(p\mid mw_i\). This contradicts \((m,N)=1\) and
\(w_i\in{\cal I}_D\). Hence \((N,q_1q_2)=1\). If
\(p\mid(q_1,q_2)\), then \(p\mid P_2-P_1=mh\). Also \(p\nmid m\),
because \(p\mid q_1\mid N-mw\) and \(p\mid m\) would imply \(p\mid N\).
Thus \(p\mid h\). Active \(q_i\) are squarefree, proving (5).

Finite Fourier inversion and TMC-EXACT from fact
\(967520f427b111c5\) now split the complete unit-\(m\) face exactly into
the frequency union \(k=0\) or \(r=0\), with the intersection subtracted
once, and the complement \(kr\ne0\). This proves UNIT-M-PRECOMB for
both signs of \(h\).

We prove (9) by adapting ZERO-RECOMB from fact
\(4a1d6a8cfcc6d864\). On the \(k=0\) axis, exact Ramanujan inversion and
fact \(cd8d7d0fe163be6e\) replace the complete \(q_1,q_2\) convolution
by
\[
 R_N\mathfrak S_N(w,w-h)+O_A((\log x)^{-A}).            \tag{11}
\]
For a bounded-variation function \(G\),
\[
 \sum_mG(m){\bf1}_{(m,N)=1}
 =\frac{\phi(N)}N\int_{\mathbb R}G(t)\,dt
  +O(\tau(\operatorname {rad}N)(\|G\|_\infty+
                                      \operatorname {Var}G)).       \tag{12}
\]
This follows by expanding the indicator over
\(e\mid\operatorname {rad}N\) and applying the progression discrepancy
to each \(e\). The main terms sum to \(\phi(N)/N\). The elementary bound
\(\tau(n)\ll_\varepsilon n^\varepsilon\) follows by treating small
prime factors directly and using \(a+1\le p^{\varepsilon a}\) for all
sufficiently large primes.

The integral main in (12), summed over the two signed slopes, is
\(\phi(N)/N\) times the singular main of fact
\(5b7b0955c5efaa1b\), hence has arbitrary logarithmic saving. The error
from (12), summed over \(O(D^2)\) slope pairs, is
\(O_\varepsilon(D^2x^\varepsilon(\log x)^{C_1})\), power-smaller than
(9) after fixing \(\varepsilon<1/4\). The convolution error in (11) is
handled identically. The small and outer-edge slope sectors contain
\(O(DH_0)\) pairs; the pointwise local-product bound from fact
\(4a1d6a8cfcc6d864\) makes their total
\[
 \ll xH_0(\log\log(3x))^{C_2}
 \ll xD(\log x)^{-6-\eta-\rho/3}.                       \tag{13}
\]

For the \(r=0,\ k\ne0\) axis, exact physical inversion gives
\[
\begin{split}
 \sum_{h,m,w}&{\bf1}_{(m,N)=1}\mu(w)\mu(w-h)\Omega(m,w,h)\\
 {}\times\sum_{\substack{q_1,q_2\ge1\\(N,c)=1\\d\mid h}}
 &\frac{\mu(q_1)\mu(q_2)}c
 \log(P_1/q_1)_+\log(P_2/q_2)_+
 \left({\bf1}_{(m,c)=1}-\frac{\phi(c)}c\right).          \tag{14}
\end{split}
\]
Since \((N,c)=1\), expansion of both reduced-residue indicators shows
that the progression main vanishes:
\[
 \sum_{e\mid\operatorname {rad}N}\frac{\mu(e)}e
 \left(\sum_{f\mid c}\frac{\mu(f)}f-\frac{\phi(c)}c\right)=0.
\]
The bounded-variation discrepancy is at most
\(\tau(\operatorname {rad}N)\tau(c)(\log x)^2\) for fixed outer labels.
The harmonic lcm sum in fact \(4a1d6a8cfcc6d864\) is
\(O((\log x)^6)\), so (14) is
\(O_\varepsilon(D^2x^\varepsilon(\log x)^8)\), again power-smaller than
(9). Combining these bounds proves (9), and (3) then gives (10).

glossary.A^times: the moving-log TMC coefficient restricted to gcd(m,N)=1
glossary.UNIT-M-PRECOMB: the legal recombine-before-expand removal of the noncoprime center face
glossary.cal E_{mN}: the recombined sector of the actual correlation with gcd(m,N)>1
glossary.cal N_mid^times: the complete unit-m TMC family with both frequencies nonzero
glossary.cal Z_mid^times: the complete zero-frequency union after unit-m precombination

2dc98afb562413fe.title: ENDPOINT PMD-BDH BOUND WITH THE COMPLETE LITERAL (v,s) FAMILY
2dc98afb562413fe.author: slava chan
2dc98afb562413fe.statement:
ENDPOINT PMD-BDH BOUND WITH THE COMPLETE LITERAL (v,s) FAMILY.

Fix C>=1 and J>=1. Let Q>=2, and let P,V satisfy
  Q^(-C)<=P<=Q^C,  2<=V<=Q^C.                              (1)
Let A be a nonzero integer with |A|<=Q^C, and let cal P be any set of primes p in [P,2P). For every v in [V,2V), p in cal P with gcd(v,p)=1, and s modulo v, let a_{v,p,q} be complex coefficients supported on positive integers q in [Q,2Q) satisfying gcd(q,vp)=1, with
  |a_{v,p,q}|<=1.                                          (2)
Put
  b_{v,s,p}(q)=a_{v,p,q}e_v(sA qbar),                      (3)
where e_v(t)=exp(2 pi i t/v) and the bar is inversion modulo v. Define
  C_{v,s,p}(r)=sum_{q_1,q_2}
   b_{v,s,p}(q_1)conjugate(b_{v,s,p}(q_2))
   [1_{p|A(q_2-q_1)-r q_1q_2}-1/p]                        (4)
for r modulo p.

Let xi_v be supported on V<=v<2V and satisfy |xi_v|<=tau_J(v), where tau_J is the J-fold divisor function. For every v,s,p let W_{v,s,p} be a real function modulo p satisfying
  0<=W_{v,s,p}(r)<=1.                                      (5)
Define
  E_BDH=sum_{V<=v<2V}sum_{s modulo v}|xi_v/v|^2
       sum_{p in cal P; p not dividing v}
       sum_{r modulo p}W_{v,s,p}(r)|C_{v,s,p}(r)|^2.        (6)
Then for every epsilon>0,
  E_BDH<<_{C,J,epsilon}Q^epsilon(PQ^2+Q^4).                (7)

Thus the complete literal (v,s) Fourier family costs only a subpolynomial factor in an averaged centered reciprocal-slope BDH bound. The estimate is uniform for arbitrary moving residue intervals and other weights bounded between zero and one. It is an endpoint bound: it gains no factor equal to the window density, and therefore does not prove the short-window PMD-SHIFTED-4MOM estimate isolated in fact b0662c5a5e8a7772.
2dc98afb562413fe.proof:
Fix v and s. Since 0<=W_{v,s,p}<=1,
  sum_r W_{v,s,p}(r)|C_{v,s,p}(r)|^2
  <=sum_r|C_{v,s,p}(r)|^2.                                (8)
We bound the sum of the right side over p.

For a fixed p abbreviate b_q=b_{v,s,p}(q). For two ordered q-pairs define
  rho_p(q_1,q_2)=A(q_2-q_1)(q_1q_2)^(-1) modulo p,
and for a quadruple define
  Delta=(q_2-q_1)q_3q_4-(q_4-q_3)q_1q_2.                  (9)
Expanding the complete centered energy, or equivalently applying the complete-window physical formula in fact b0662c5a5e8a7772, gives
  sum_r|C_{v,s,p}(r)|^2
  =sum_{q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4}
    b_{q_1}conjugate(b_{q_2})conjugate(b_{q_3})b_{q_4}
    [1_{rho_p(q_1,q_2)=rho_p(q_3,q_4)}-1/p].               (10)

First take the terms with Delta=0 in the incidence part of (10). They are exactly the rational reciprocal-slope energy
  sum_lambda |sum_{(q_1,q_2): (q_2-q_1)/(q_1q_2)=lambda}
                   b_{q_1}conjugate(b_{q_2})|^2.            (11)
Fact e7458a42217c2756 bounds (11) by
  Q^epsilon(sum_q|b_q|^2)^2<<Q^(2+epsilon),                (12)
because there are O(Q) supported q and |b_q|=|a_{v,p,q}|<=1. Summing (12) over p in cal P costs at most
  P Q^(2+epsilon).                                         (13)

Now take Delta nonzero. Fact a67bcae890e720ae gives the exact implication
  rho_p(q_1,q_2)=rho_p(q_3,q_4)
  implies p|A Delta.                                       (14)
For each fixed quadruple, A Delta is a nonzero integer. Also |Delta|<<Q^3 and |A|<=Q^C. The fixed-power divisor estimate in fact e705401df9f0709e therefore shows that A Delta has O_{C,epsilon}(Q^epsilon) prime divisors in cal P. Since every coefficient in (10) has magnitude at most one, summing the absolute values of all nonzero-Delta incidence terms first over p and then over O(Q^4) quadruples gives
  <<_{C,epsilon}Q^(4+epsilon).                              (15)
This remains valid although the coefficients and their supports may depend on p, because for every fixed quadruple only primes dividing the same nonzero integer A Delta can contribute.

Finally, the centered constant in (10), after summing the quadruples, is
  -1/p |sum_q b_q|^4<=0.                                  (16)
It may be discarded in an upper bound. Equations (8), (13), (15), and (16) prove, for each fixed v,s,
  sum_{p in cal P; p not dividing v}
  sum_r W_{v,s,p}(r)|C_{v,s,p}(r)|^2
  <<_{C,epsilon}Q^epsilon(PQ^2+Q^4).                       (17)

Fact d061fc4dc153e309, also recorded as equation (21) of fact b0662c5a5e8a7772, gives
  sum_{V<=v<2V}sum_{s modulo v}|xi_v/v|^2
  =sum_{V<=v<2V}|xi_v|^2/v<<_{J,epsilon}V^epsilon.         (18)
Since V<=Q^C, the factor V^epsilon can be absorbed by adjusting epsilon. Multiplying (17) by the weights in (18) and summing v,s proves (7). The final scope statement follows because (8) uses only domination by the complete window and hence retains no dependence on the support length of W.

glossary.E_BDH: The literal (v,s)-weighted average of local centered reciprocal-slope energies over prime moduli.
glossary.endpoint PMD-BDH: The complete-window-scale bound PQ^2+Q^4 obtained from rational-slope compression and prime-divisor switching, without a short-window gain.

2dd1ed95db5b458c.title: ZERO-ADDITIVE-FREQUENCY RECYCLING IN THE SOFT-SOURCE MODULAR MEAN
2dd1ed95db5b458c.author: slava chan
2dd1ed95db5b458c.statement:
ZERO-ADDITIVE-FREQUENCY RECYCLING IN THE SOFT-SOURCE MODULAR MEAN.

Adopt all hypotheses and notation of fact 16eaa93099f0bcdc. In particular, for each outer pair j=(v,p) and twist t modulo p, let b_{j,t} be the finite-band soft-source q-row, let cal J_{j,t} be its modular reciprocal-phase fourth moment, and let cal M_4, cal J_vec, cal D_vec, and cal M_vec be the vector quantities in that fact. Define the nonzero-additive-frequency modular mean
 cal J_vec^*
 =sum_{j in cal O}p^(-1)sum_{t modulo p}
    sum_{ell modulo p;ell nonzero}
    |sum_q b_{j,t}(q)e_p(ell A qbar)|^4.                   (1)
Then
 cal J_vec=cal M_4+cal J_vec^*,                             (2)
 cal J_vec^*>=0,                                            (3)
and
 cal M_vec=cal J_vec^*-cal D_vec.                           (4)

Consequently the exact decomposition
 cal M_4=cal J_vec-cal D_vec-cal M_vec                      (5)
does not by itself reduce the desired positive fourth moment to smaller auxiliary quantities: after deleting the ell=0 term from cal J_vec, equation (5) becomes the identity (4) and contains no cal M_4. A bound
 cal J_vec<<P^2Q^(7/3+epsilon)                              (6)
is a valid sufficient supplier because cal M_4<=cal J_vec, but it already bounds a nonnegative quantity containing cal M_4 as an exact summand. A theorem controlling only cal J_vec^*, cal D_vec, and cal M_vec cannot imply a bound for cal M_4 through equations (2)-(5) alone.

Thus the noncircular sufficient inputs currently available are either a direct literal finite-band vector estimate for cal M_4 at the target scale, or another inequality using additional structure beyond the modular decomposition (2)-(5). This is a theorem-interface statement. It does not assert that a modular-mean theorem is impossible, does not estimate any of the displayed moments, and makes no PMD or Goldbach conclusion.
2dd1ed95db5b458c.proof:
For every fixed j,t, fact 16eaa93099f0bcdc proves by additive orthogonality that
 cal J_{j,t}
 =p^(-1)sum_{ell modulo p}
   |sum_qb_{j,t}(q)e_p(ell A qbar)|^4.                     (7)
Separate ell=0 in (7). Its contribution is
 p^(-1)|sum_qb_{j,t}(q)|^4.                                (8)
Sum (8) over t and j. The exact finite-band sampling identity in the same fact gives
 sum_{j in cal O}p^(-1)sum_{t modulo p}
  |sum_qb_{j,t}(q)|^4
 =sum_{j in cal O}integral_{R/Z}|A_j(theta)|^4dtheta
 =cal M_4.                                                  (9)
The sum of the remaining nonzero-ell contributions is exactly the right side of (1). This proves (2). Every summand in (1) is nonnegative, proving (3).

Fact 16eaa93099f0bcdc also proves (5). Substitute (2) into (5) and cancel cal M_4 from both sides:
 0=cal J_vec^*-cal D_vec-cal M_vec.
This is (4).

Nonnegativity in (2) gives cal M_4<=cal J_vec, so (6) is sufficient. Conversely, after replacing cal J_vec by cal M_4+cal J_vec^*, the only relation among the three auxiliary quantities is (4), which is independent of cal M_4. Therefore equations (2)-(5) alone cannot turn bounds on only those three quantities into a bound for cal M_4. The final scope statement follows.

glossary.cal J_vec^*: The nonzero-additive-frequency part of the outer soft-source modular mean.
glossary.zero-additive-frequency recycling: The identity that the ell=0 portion of cal J_vec is exactly cal M_4.

2e0b40b1ba77fb6f.title: REVERSE LITERAL-C3 SOURCE-TO-TRACE THEOREM WITH EXACT OUTER-g COLLISION PAYMENT
2e0b40b1ba77fb6f.author: slava chan
2e0b40b1ba77fb6f.statement:
REVERSE LITERAL-C3 SOURCE-TO-TRACE THEOREM WITH EXACT OUTER-g COLLISION PAYMENT.

Fix constants C,c_0,C_0,c_1,C_1>=1 and 0<kappa<=1/100. Put sigma=kappa/100 and beta_1=6/5-3sigma. Let x>=3, c_0x<=N<=C_0x, and let D,M,R,K satisfy D>R, c_1^(-1)x<=DM,RK<=C_1x, R<=Cx^(1/2), D<=Cx, and D/R>x^(23/400). Fix g|N and put Q=R/g>1, B=D/g=Q^beta, G=K/Q, H_T=B/Q, H_P=B/K, L_src=N/g, L=H_TQ^sigma, S_0=H_T^2Q^(3sigma), Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma), with 1<=beta<=beta_1.

Let W be fixed scaled-smooth on a compact four-variable box. Define
F'_{g,b,a}(t)=log(t)log((L_src-bt)/a)
 W(ga/D,(L_src-bt)/(aM),gb/R,t/K)
and its Fourier transform Fhat'. Let T_rev,C3(g) be the sum over h>0, b comparable to Q, squarefree v<=S_0 with all prime factors at most L, and distinct ordered primes Z<=p_1<p_2<p_3, where a=vp_1p_2p_3 is comparable to B, gcd(a,b)=1, ga and gb are squarefree, of
2mu(b)(-mu(v))Re[a^(-1)Fhat'_{g,b,a}(h/a)e_a(L_src h b^(-1))].
Use complete dyadic prime cells and exact equal-cell inclusion-exclusion, with no further joint deletion.

Then there are fixed delta_1,delta_2>0 such that
|T_rev,C3(g)|<<GQ^(2-delta_1) for G>=1,
and
|T_rev,C3(g)|<<Q^(2-delta_2)
for Q^(-sigma+eta)<=G<=Q^(sigma-eta), 0<eta<sigma.
The physical reciprocal representation has modulus b, marked inverse argument a, and target +L_src after complete h-sign reindexing. The result includes H_P<1, all frequencies, nonunit target, prime order/equal cells, repeated-prime bookkeeping, and exact p_i|g collisions. It asserts no hard deletion, later beta, actual-Z, endpoint, PMD, DCE, bad-N, or Goldbach conclusion.
2e0b40b1ba77fb6f.proof:
Set
(D',M',R',K')=(R,K,D,M), a'=b, b'=a,
and define W'(x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4)=W(x_3,x_4,x_1,x_2).
Then R'>D', D'<=Cx^(1/2), R'<=Cx, R'/D'=D/R>x^(23/400), and
D'M'=RK, R'K'=DM
are comparable to x. The normalized parameters Q,B,G,H_T,H_P,L_src,L,S_0,Z are unchanged.

The forward function in fact da22464a2f614042 for the primed variables is
log(t)log((L_src-a't)/b')
 W'(ga'/D',t/M',gb'/R',(L_src-a't)/(b'K')),
which becomes exactly F'_{g,b,a}(t) after substitution. Its complete C3 sum becomes exactly T_rev,C3(g): the primed reciprocal modulus a'=b has scale Q, the primed marked factor b'=a equals vp_1p_2p_3, and the primed Mobius coefficient is mu(b)(-mu(v)). All squarefreeness and p_i not dividing g restrictions, equal-cell terms and collision corrections are identical under this permutation. Therefore both estimates follow directly from fact da22464a2f614042, including the strip G<1 and H_P<1.

It remains only to record the physical target sign. The function F' is real, so
Re[Fhat'(h/a)e_a(L_src h b^(-1))]
=Re[Fhat'(-h/a)e_a(-L_src h b^(-1))].
Reciprocity gives
e_a(-L_src h b^(-1))
=e_b(+L_src h a^(-1))e(-L_src h/(ab)).
Thus the conjugate member of the complete real h-pair has reciprocal modulus b, marked inverse argument a, target +L_src, and the archimedean factor retained in the smooth amplitude. This is the claimed physical reverse representation and completes the proof.

glossary.F'_{g,b,a}: The reverse one-variable source amplitude obtained by Poisson summation in the k-coordinate.
glossary.T_rev,C3(g): The complete reverse exact-g C3 paired-Poisson sum with source squarefreeness retained.

2e80012db28da736.title: EXACT LARGE SHARED-CONDUCTOR-CORE EXPANSION OF THE CROSSED MZB-ENERGY KERNEL
2e80012db28da736.author: slava chan
2e80012db28da736.statement:
EXACT LARGE SHARED-CONDUCTOR-CORE EXPANSION OF THE CROSSED MZB-ENERGY KERNEL.

Assume the notation and actual g=1, |h|=1 very-large-conductor setting of fact 050efa07f87f374a. Fix eta with 0<eta<1/12 and put
F_0=x^(1/2-eta).
Thus
Q=x^(1/2+o(1)), B=Q^(4/3+o(1)),
and every modulus b in the energy is squarefree and satisfies b asymp B.

For a divisor f|b and (a,b)=1 define
K_f(b;a)
 =product_{p|f}
  [1+(p-1)e_p(-N[a(b/p)]^(-1))],                            (1)
where inverses are modulo p. Then the high-conductor projector in fact 050efa07f87f374a has the exact Euler-response form
Pi_{b,>F_0}(a)
 =1/phi(b) sum_{f|b;f>F_0,(f,N)=1}
   c_{b/f}(N) overline(K_f(b;a)).                            (2)

Let E_cross be the unequal-a part of the energy in that fact. Then
E_cross
 =sum_{a_1!=a_2}alpha_{a_1}overline(alpha_{a_2})
   C_{F_0}(a_1,a_2),                                        (3)
where
C_{F_0}(a_1,a_2)
 =sum_{b asymp B;b squarefree;(a_1a_2,b)=1}1/phi(b)^2
   sum_{f_1,f_2|b;f_1,f_2>F_0;(f_1f_2,N)=1}
   c_{b/f_1}(N)c_{b/f_2}(N)
   overline(K_{f_1}(b;a_1))K_{f_2}(b;a_2).                  (4)

Every term of (4) has a unique parametrization
d=(f_1,f_2), f_1=dr_1, f_2=dr_2,
b=dr_1r_2t,                                                  (5)
where d,r_1,r_2,t are pairwise coprime and squarefree. The two complementary factors are
b/f_1=r_2t, b/f_2=r_1t.                                      (6)
Moreover,
d>=f_1f_2/b>F_0^2/b
  =Q^(2/3-4eta+o(1)),                                        (7)
and
r_1r_2t=b/d<=Q^(2/3+4eta+o(1)).                              (8)

For a prime p|d, put
X_i=N[a_i(b/p)]^(-1) modulo p, i=1,2.
The exact common-core local factor in
overline(K_{dr_1}(b;a_1))K_{dr_2}(b;a_2)
is
[1+(p-1)e_p(X_1)][1+(p-1)e_p(-X_2)]
 =1+(p-1)e_p(X_1)+(p-1)e_p(-X_2)
  +(p-1)^2 e_p(N(a_1^(-1)-a_2^(-1))(b/p)^(-1)).             (9)
Thus the crossed inverse-difference phase occurs precisely on every prime of the large common conductor core d. Primes in r_1 carry only the conjugated a_1 response, primes in r_2 only the a_2 response, and t occurs in both Ramanujan weights c_{r_2t}(N), c_{r_1t}(N) but in neither response product.

Equations (3)-(9) are identities and support geometry only. They do not bound E_cross. A sufficient theorem still has to sum the large varying squarefree core d together with the pairwise-coprime residual factors r_1,r_2,t, the two Ramanujan weights, every local one-sided term in (9), the actual alpha coefficients and the dyadic b condition at the Q^(8/3-omega) energy scale. No estimate for C_small from fact d53bd13f391dd6e4, endpoint capture, C3, or Goldbach is asserted.
2e80012db28da736.proof:
Fact adb3b38d14670d3c, with q=b, dilator 1, t=1 and u=a, gives
P_{b,1}^{>F_0}(1,a)
 =1/phi(b)sum_{f|b;f>F_0,(f,N)=1}c_{b/f}(N)K_f(b;a).
As proved in fact 050efa07f87f374a, Pi_{b,>F_0}(a) is the complex conjugate of this projector. Ramanujan sums c_s(N) are real: pairing the residue z with -z in their defining sum proves this directly. Conjugating the displayed divisor formula gives (2).

Expand the square defining E_{>F_0}(alpha) in fact 050efa07f87f374a and delete its equal-a part. Inserting (2) in the two rows gives (3)-(4). All sums are finite and the a-coprimality conditions combine to (a_1a_2,b)=1, so no interchange issue occurs.

Because b is squarefree, its divisors f_1 and f_2 are squarefree. Put d=(f_1,f_2), r_i=f_i/d. Then d,r_1,r_2 are pairwise coprime. Their least common multiple is dr_1r_2 and divides b, so t=b/(dr_1r_2) is an integer coprime to each of them. This proves the uniqueness and coprimality in (5), and division gives (6).

Also
lcm(f_1,f_2)=f_1f_2/d<=b,
so d>=f_1f_2/b>F_0^2/b. Since
F_0=x^(1/2-eta)=Q^(1-2eta+o(1))
and b=Q^(4/3+o(1)), this is (7). Equation (8) follows from r_1r_2t=b/d and (7).

Finally, if p|d, then p divides both f_1 and f_2. The p-factor in overline(K_{f_1}(b;a_1)) is
1+(p-1)e_p(X_1),
while the p-factor in K_{f_2}(b;a_2) is
1+(p-1)e_p(-X_2).
Multiplication gives the first three terms in (9) and the double term e_p(X_1-X_2). Because b/p is a unit modulo p,
X_1-X_2
 =N(a_1^(-1)-a_2^(-1))(b/p)^(-1) modulo p,
which proves (9). If p|r_1, it occurs only in f_1; if p|r_2, only in f_2; and primes dividing t occur in neither conductor. Formula (6) places t in both Ramanujan factors. This proves every identity and scope statement.

glossary.C_{F_0}(a_1,a_2): the crossed unequal-a high-conductor kernel in (4)
glossary.K_f(b;a): the explicit prime-local Euler response in (1)
glossary.r_1,r_2: the conductor factors unique to f_1 and f_2
glossary.t: the factor of b outside lcm(f_1,f_2)

2efa7a0caa7e0a15.title: GENERAL ITERATED A^k-PROCESS SUPPLIER FOR A FACTORABLE EFFECTIVE MODULUS. Fix integers k>=1 and J>=1. Let n>1 be squarefree, let C be an integer, put g=gcd(C,n) and m_eff=n/g>1, and suppose
2efa7a0caa7e0a15.author: slava chan
2efa7a0caa7e0a15.statement:
GENERAL ITERATED A^k-PROCESS SUPPLIER FOR A FACTORABLE EFFECTIVE MODULUS. Fix integers k>=1 and J>=1. Let n>1 be squarefree, let C be an integer, put g=gcd(C,n) and m_eff=n/g>1, and suppose
m_eff=q_0q_1...q_k                                                   (1)
with positive integers q_0,...,q_k; equivalently, because m_eff is squarefree, these factors are squarefree and pairwise coprime. Let X,A,B>=1. Let alpha_a be supported on A<=a<2A with |alpha_a|<=tau_J(a). Let c be squarefree. Let W be extended by zero, supported on X<=x<2X, and put V_X(W)=sup_x|W(x)|+sum_x|W(x+1)-W(x)|. Then, for every epsilon>0,
|sum_{a,b;gcd(ab,nc)=1}alpha_a W(ab)e_n(C(ab)^(-1))|
 <<_{k,J,epsilon} V_X(W)tau(nc)(m_eff AB)^epsilon A times
 [sum_{j=1}^k B^(1-1/2^j)q_j^(1/2^j)
  +Bq_0^(-1/2^(k+1))
  +B^(1-1/2^k)q_0^(1/2^(k+1))],                        (2)
where b is otherwise unweighted and B<=b<2B.

Consequently, fix u>0. If AB is comparable to X, nc<=X^K for a fixed K, V_X(W)<=X^epsilon for every fixed epsilon, and the factorization (1) satisfies
q_j<=B X^(-2^j u) for 1<=j<=k,                                  (3)
X^(2^(k+1)u)<=q_0<=B^2X^(-2^(k+1)u),                            (4)
then the sum in (2) is at most X^(1-u+o(1)). This theorem retains the literal BV product weight, divisor-bounded carrier, possibly nonunit original numerator, and complete auxiliary coprimality gate. For k=1, conditions (3)-(4) recover the fixed-slack factor-size pattern underlying fact 629ed652df233d7b; no assertion is made that every residual modulus admits a factorization (1),(3),(4).
2efa7a0caa7e0a15.proof:
Write C=gC'. Then gcd(C',m_eff)=1 and, on the unit support,
e_n(C(ab)^(-1))=e_{m_eff}(C'(ab)^(-1)).                         (5)
Fix a with gcd(a,nc)=1. Let
s=rad(nc)/gcd(rad(nc),m_eff).
Then gcd(s,m_eff)=1, and the remaining auxiliary b-gate is
1_{gcd(b,s)=1}=sum_{d|s,d|b}mu(d).                              (6)
For one d put b=dr. The variable r lies in an interval of length N<=B/d, is coprime to m_eff, and its reciprocal numerator C'(ad)^(-1) is a unit modulo m_eff.

We use Dartyge--Martin, arXiv:1802.09090, Lemma 12. In the notation relevant here, their complete statement says: if q=q_0...q_k is squarefree and coprime to the numerator, I is an interval of length N, and the rational auxiliary twist R(r)/delta is set to zero with delta=1, then
|sum_{r in I;gcd(r,q)=1}e_q(alpha r^(-1))|
 <<_k sum_{j=1}^k N^(1-1/2^j)q_j^(1/2^j)
 +N^(1-1/2^k)q_0^(1/2^(k+1))(2^(k+2)+4)^(omega(q_0)/2^k)
  [(N/q_0)^(1/2^k)+(log q)^(1/2^k)].                            (7)
The paper obtains (7) by k consecutive van der Corput A-process steps, followed by completion modulo q_0; the final rational functions have at most 2^k+1 poles and are nonconstant by the subset-sum parity lemma used there.

For fixed k, the factor involving omega(q_0) and log q is at most (m_eff AB)^epsilon after enlarging the implied constant. Using N<=B, split the final bracket in (7). Its first part is bounded by
B^(1-1/2^k)q_0^(1/2^(k+1))(B/q_0)^(1/2^k)
 =Bq_0^(-1/2^(k+1)),                                            (8)
and its logarithmic part is bounded by
(m_eff AB)^epsilon B^(1-1/2^k)q_0^(1/2^(k+1)).                 (9)
Partial summation inserts W(adr): the increasing map r to adr makes its supremum plus variation at most V_X(W). Summing (7)-(9) over d|s costs at most tau(s)<=tau(nc). Finally sum |alpha_a| over a, costing A^(1+epsilon). Absorbing the extra A^epsilon proves (2).

Assume (3)-(4). After multiplication by A, divide each term in (2) by AB, which is comparable to X. For 1<=j<=k the relative j-th term is
(q_j/B)^(1/2^j)<=X^(-u).                                        (10)
The relative complete-period term is
q_0^(-1/2^(k+1))<=X^(-u)                                       (11)
by the lower bound in (4). The final relative term is
B^(-1/2^k)q_0^(1/2^(k+1))
 =(q_0/B^2)^(1/2^(k+1))<=X^(-u)                                (12)
by the upper bound in (4). The divisor, variation, epsilon, and fixed-k constants contribute X^o(1), proving X^(1-u+o(1)). When k=1, (3) reads q_1<=BX^(-2u) and (4) reads X^(4u)<=q_0<=B^2X^(-4u), exactly the factor-size pattern used in the one-step supplier. This proves every scope statement.

glossary.q_0,...,q_k: The pairwise coprime factors of the squarefree effective modulus used in the iterated A-process.
glossary.u: A fixed positive target saving exponent in the factor-size corollary.

2f339e96f361bf0c.title: SOURCE-ALIGNED MULTI-q SATURATION OF THE GENERIC SOFT-SOURCE VECTOR FOURTH MOMENT
2f339e96f361bf0c.author: slava chan
2f339e96f361bf0c.statement:
SOURCE-ALIGNED MULTI-q SATURATION OF THE GENERIC SOFT-SOURCE VECTOR FOURTH MOMENT.

There exist fixed smooth compactly supported real functions Phi and phi and a fixed constant c_*>0 with the following property. The support of Phi is contained in [1,2], Phi is nonnegative, the support of phi is contained in a fixed interval [-delta,delta], phi is nonnegative, and
  w(u)=Phi(u)phihat(u)                                       (1)
is nonnegative for every real u and satisfies
  w(u)>=c_* for 5/4<=u<=7/4.                                (2)

Fix Q>=2 and a real H>=8. Let cal O be a finite set of pairs j=(v,p), where v is a positive integer, p is prime, gcd(v,p)=1, and
  p>4H+2.                                                     (3)
For j=(v,p) put
  n_j=vp,  Y_j=n_j/H.                                       (4)
For every j let cal Q_j be any finite set of positive integers q satisfying gcd(q,n_j)=1, and put N_j=#cal Q_j. Fix A=1. For every j and q in cal Q_j choose an integer m_{j,q} satisfying
  q m_{j,q} congruent 1 modulo n_j,                          (5)
and define the integer
  k_{j,q}=(1-qm_{j,q})/n_j.                                 (6)
Define
  F_{j,q}(x)=phi((x-m_{j,q})/Y_j).                           (7)
Then F_{j,q} is smooth, has a uniform bounded amplitude, is supported in an interval of length 2delta Y_j, and the exact source equation
  q m_{j,q}+n_j k_{j,q}=1                                   (8)
holds.

For theta in R/Z define
  A_j(theta)=sum_{q in cal Q_j} n_j^(-1)sum_{h in Z}
    Phi(h/H)Fhat_{j,q}(h/n_j)
    e_{n_j}(h qbar)e(h theta),                               (9)
where e(t)=exp(2 pi i t), e_n(t)=e(t/n), and qbar is the inverse of q modulo n_j. Put
  cal M_4=sum_{j in cal O}integral_{R/Z}|A_j(theta)|^4dtheta. (10)
Then exactly
  A_j(theta)=(N_j/H)sum_{h in Z}w(h/H)e(h theta),            (11)
and
  cal M_4>=c_0 H^(-1)sum_{j in cal O}N_j^4                  (12)
for a fixed constant c_0>0 depending only on Phi and phi.

Consequently, a fourth-moment estimate for the generic soft-source class in (9) cannot be deduced uniformly from smoothness, bounded amplitude, support length O(Y_j), the bandpass condition Phi(0)=0, and the source equation alone at any target smaller than the right side of (12). In particular, if R=#cal O and N_j>=N for every j, the lower bound is c_0 R N^4/H. Any proposed target P^2Q^(7/3+epsilon) fails whenever
  c_0 R N^4/H>P^2Q^(7/3+epsilon).                            (13)

This is a coefficient-class counterexample for q-dependent translated amplitudes. It is not a counterexample for the literal common physical source weight of the project, because the centers m_{j,q} in (7) may vary arbitrarily with j and q. It shows that a viable vector OSC or finite-band fourth-moment theorem must retain a literal common-support/location restriction, or another hypothesis excluding source-aligned q-dependent translations. No PMD or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
2f339e96f361bf0c.proof:
Choose a nonnegative smooth function psi supported in [-delta/2,delta/2] with integral one, and put
  phi=psi*tilde psi,
where tilde psi(x)=psi(-x). Then phi is nonnegative, smooth, and supported in [-delta,delta], while
  phihat(u)=|psihat(u)|^2>=0                                (14)
for every real u. Choose delta sufficiently small that
  cos(2 pi u x)>=3/4
for |x|<=delta/2 and 1<=u<=2. Then
  Re psihat(u)=integral psi(x)cos(2 pi ux)dx>=3/4,
so
  phihat(u)>=9/16                                           (15)
on [1,2].

Choose a fixed nonnegative smooth function Phi supported in [1,2] and satisfying Phi(u)>=1 on [5/4,7/4]. Equations (14)-(15) prove (1)-(2) with c_*=9/16.

For each j,q, Fourier scaling and translation in (7) give
  Fhat_{j,q}(xi)
  =Y_j e(-m_{j,q}xi)phihat(Y_jxi).                          (16)
Equation (5) says qbar is congruent to m_{j,q} modulo n_j. Substitute xi=h/n_j into (16). The translation character and progression character cancel:
  e(-h m_{j,q}/n_j)e_{n_j}(h qbar)=1.                       (17)
Also Y_j/n_j=1/H and Y_j h/n_j=h/H. Therefore every q-summand in (9) is the same, and summing the N_j copies proves (11).

All Fourier coefficients w(h/H) in (11) are nonnegative by (1). Parseval applied to the square of the trigonometric polynomial gives
  integral_{R/Z}|sum_h w(h/H)e(h theta)|^4dtheta
  =sum_{h_1+h_2=h_3+h_4}
     w(h_1/H)w(h_2/H)w(h_3/H)w(h_4/H).                     (18)
Let I_H be the consecutive set of integers h satisfying
  5H/4<=h<=7H/4.
For H>=8 its cardinality L_H is at least H/4. On I_H every factor in (18) is at least c_* by (2). The number of ordered quadruples from a consecutive interval of L_H integers satisfying h_1+h_2=h_3+h_4 is
  (2L_H^3+L_H)/3.                                          (19)
This follows because the pair-sum multiplicities are
  1,2,...,L_H-1,L_H,L_H-1,...,2,1
and the sum of their squares is the displayed value.

Every term in (18) is nonnegative, so retaining only the quadruples from I_H and using L_H>=H/4 gives
  integral_{R/Z}|sum_h w(h/H)e(h theta)|^4dtheta
  >=c_*^4(2L_H^3+L_H)/3
  >=c_*^4 H^3/96.                                          (20)
Multiply (20) by N_j^4/H^4 using (11), then sum over j. This proves (12) with c_0=c_*^4/96.

The amplitude and support assertions for F_{j,q} follow directly from (7) and the corresponding fixed properties of phi. Equation (6) is integral by (5), and substitution proves (8). Thus every generic smoothness, support, bandpass, and source hypothesis listed in the statement is satisfied. Inequality (13) is the direct comparison of (12) with the proposed target. The centers were chosen separately from the residue class (5), so no common physical location law has been imposed. This proves the counterexample and every scope statement.

glossary.N_j: The cardinality of the q-row cal Q_j.
glossary.m_{j,q}: A chosen integer representative of the source residue q^{-1} modulo n_j.
glossary.w(u): The common nonnegative band profile Phi(u)phihat(u).

2ff1c15aef183bac.title: FIXED-TARGET \(v p\) ENDPOINT CLOSURE BELOW \(\beta=6/5\)
2ff1c15aef183bac.author: slava chan
2ff1c15aef183bac.statement:
FIXED-TARGET \(v p\) ENDPOINT CLOSURE BELOW \(\beta=6/5\).

Fix \(0<\kappa\le1/100\), integers \(J,C_A\ge1\), and put
\[
 \sigma=\kappa/100,\qquad
 1\le\beta\le\frac65-2\kappa.
\]
For sufficiently large \(Q\), define
\[
 R=Q^\beta,\qquad H=R/Q,\qquad
 L=HQ^\sigma,\qquad S_0=H^2Q^{3\sigma},\qquad
 Z=Q^{3/2-\beta-3\sigma}. \tag{1}
\]
Let \(1\le V\le S_0\), put
\[
 P=R/V, \tag{2}
\]
and let \(\xi_v\) be supported on squarefree integers \(V\le v<2V\) whose prime divisors are at most \(L\), with
\[
 |\xi_v|\le\tau_J(v). \tag{3}
\]
Let \(A\) be a fixed nonzero integer with \(|A|\le Q^{C_A}\). Let \(|c_q|\le1\) for \(Q\le q<2Q\), and let \(\nu_h\) be supported on \(H\le|h|<2H\) with \(|\nu_h|\le\tau_J(|h|)\). Let \(\Psi\) belong to a fixed bounded scaled-smooth family on \((0,\infty)^4\), supported in \([1,2]^4\), with all logarithmic derivatives uniformly bounded. Define
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 {\cal V}_{V,P}(\Psi;A)
 =H^{-1}\sum_{Q\le q<2Q}c_q
 \sum_{\substack{H\le|h|<2H\\V\le v<2V\\P\le p<2P\\
                  p\ {\rm prime}\\(vp,q)=1}}
 \nu_h\xi_v\Psi(q/Q,|h|/H,v/V,p/P)
 e_q\!\left(Ah(vp)^{-1}\right).
 \end{aligned} \tag{4}
\]
Then there exists \(\delta=\delta(\kappa,C_A)>0\) such that
\[
 |{\cal V}_{V,P}(\Psi;A)|
 \ll_{\kappa,J,C_A,\Psi}Q^{2-\delta}. \tag{5}
\]
The estimate remains valid after a polylogarithmic number of dyadic, sign, and scaled-smooth separation labels, after decreasing \(\delta\).

Because \(P\ge R/S_0>Z\) for large \(Q\), every prime \(p\) in (4) is greater than every prime divisor of \(v\); hence \((v,p)=1\) automatically. Taking \(\xi_v=-\mu(v)\) gives the exact one-rough-prime coefficient in alternative (C) of fact \(6414b11506a84ff0\). This theorem does not estimate the two- or three-rough-prime endpoints or perform the outer common-gcd \(g=(d,r)\) assembly.
2ff1c15aef183bac.proof:
Put
\[
 \nu=\log V/\log Q.
\]
From \(V\le S_0=Q^{2\beta-2+3\sigma}\),
\[
 0\le\nu\le2\beta-2+3\sigma. \tag{6}
\]
Also
\[
 P=Q^{\beta-\nu}. \tag{7}
\]
Since
\[
 \log_Q(R/S_0)=2-\beta-3\sigma
\]
and
\[
 \log_Q Z=\frac32-\beta-3\sigma,
\]
one has \(P\ge R/S_0=Q^{1/2}Z>Z\). Thus the final coprimality assertion in the statement is valid.

We first replace the prime indicator. On \(P\le n<2P\), write
\[
 {\bf1}_{n\ {\rm prime}}
 =\frac{\Lambda(n)}{\log n}
 -{\bf1}_{n=p^j,\ p\ {\rm prime},\ j\ge2}\frac1j. \tag{8}
\]
The factor \(1/\log n\), the amplitude \(\Psi\), and every product cutoff are scaled-smooth on their dyadic supports. In logarithmic coordinates they have uniformly summable Fourier expansions into products of one-variable factors. After a factorization \(n=lm\), a mode depending on \(\log n=\log l+\log m\) separates multiplicatively. The Fourier coefficients decay faster than any power, so all projective norms and derivative costs below are polylogarithmic and can be absorbed into \(Q^\epsilon\).

The proper-prime-power contribution in (8) is small trivially. There are
\[
 O(P^{1/2}\log(2P))
\]
proper prime powers in \([P,2P)\), because for each \(j\ge2\) there are at most \((2P)^{1/j}\) possible bases and \(j\le\log(2P)/\log2\). Summing all other variables absolutely and including the factor \(H^{-1}\) gives
\[
 \ll Q^\epsilon QV P^{1/2}
 =Q^{1+\epsilon}(VR)^{1/2}. \tag{9}
\]
Since \(V\le S_0=Q^{2\beta-2+3\sigma}\),
\[
 1+\frac{\log_Q(VR)}2
 \le\frac{3\beta}{2}+\frac{3\sigma}{2}
 \le\frac95-3\kappa+\frac{3\kappa}{200}<2-\kappa. \tag{10}
\]
Thus (9) is power-saving.

It remains to treat the \(\Lambda\)-sum. Apply the exact Vaughan identity and range theorem \(29c43cef40f2e79b\) to the \(n\)-variable at scale \(P\), with cutoff \(P^{1/3}\). After dyadic subdivision, each Type-II box has two factors \(l,m\), and after interchanging them,
\[
 \frac{\beta-\nu}{3}+O(1/\log Q)
 \le\lambda=\frac{\log L_1}{\log Q}
 \le\frac{\beta-\nu}{2}+O(1/\log Q), \tag{11}
\]
where \(L_1\) is the smaller factor scale. Each Type-I box has a coefficient-bearing factor of exponent
\[
 0\le\lambda\le\frac{\beta-\nu}{3}+O(1/\log Q). \tag{12}
\]
All Vaughan coefficients are bounded by a fixed divisor function times a logarithm, by that fact.

Consider a Type-II box. Ignoring the vanishing \(O(1/\log Q)\) endpoint displacement for a moment, part (A) of the slot-selection fact \(461b4af4d8047ab5\) says that either the grouped factor \(vl\), of exponent \(w=\nu+\lambda\), or its complementary factor \(m\), of exponent \(\beta-w\), lies between
\[
 2\beta-2+4\sigma
 \quad\hbox{and}\quad
 3-2\beta-4\sigma. \tag{13}
\]
For large \(Q\), the dyadic endpoint displacement in (11) is less than \(\sigma/2\), so the selected scale \(S\) satisfies
\[
 H^2Q^{3\sigma}\le S\le\frac{Q^{1-3\sigma}}{H^2}. \tag{14}
\]
Combine the remaining variables into the complementary scale \(T\). Since the complete product is \(v n\asymp VP=R=QH\),
\[
 ST\asymp QH. \tag{15}
\]
The convolution coefficient created by grouping \(v\) with \(l\) is still divisor-bounded: the number of representations of an integer as \(vl\) and the product of the two fixed-order divisor bounds are bounded by another fixed-order divisor function. Smooth separation preserves the same property.

Apply the full fixed-target estimate (2) of fact \(73fb9efe1286f7e9\) with target \(A\). The same four-term expansion used in its balanced corollary, now with (14)-(15), gives after the \(H^{-1}\) prefactor
\[
 \ll Q^\epsilon\left[
 Q^2H^{1/2}S^{-1/4}
 +Q^{7/4}H^{1/2}S^{1/4}
 +Q^2HS^{-1/2}
 +Q^{7/4}H\right]. \tag{16}
\]
The first three terms are at most
\[
 Q^{2-3\sigma/4},\quad
 Q^{2-3\sigma/4},\quad
 Q^{2-3\sigma/2}. \tag{17}
\]
The simultaneous bounds (14) imply \(H\le Q^{1/4-3\sigma/2}\), so the fourth term is at most \(Q^{2-3\sigma/2}\). The fixed target contributes only \((|A|QHST)^\epsilon\), which is absorbed by choosing \(\epsilon\) sufficiently small.

Now consider a Type-I box and put \(w_0=\nu+\lambda\). Part (B) of fact \(461b4af4d8047ab5\), again with the dyadic endpoint error absorbed into one unit of \(\sigma\), gives three branches.

If \(w_0\le1/2-3\sigma\), group \(v\) with the short Vaughan factor. Its length is at most \(Q^{1/2-3\sigma}\), while the total product is \(R=Q^\beta\le Q^{6/5}\). Apply the fixed-target \(h\)-averaged Type-I consumer \(bbcb9f66597c667c\), with its parameter \(\tau\) chosen as \(2\sigma\). Both hypotheses
\[
 R\le Q^{2-2\sigma},\qquad
 Q^{w_0}\le Q^{1/2-2\sigma}
\]
hold, and this box is \(O(Q^{2-\sigma})\).

If \(1/2-3\sigma<w_0\le3-2\beta-3\sigma\), select \(S=vl\). The lower bound \(1/2-3\sigma>2\beta-2+2\sigma\) follows uniformly from \(\beta\le6/5-2\kappa\). If \(w_0>3-2\beta-3\sigma\), select the unweighted complementary factor; part (B) places its exponent inside the same buffered window. In both cases, the correlated estimate (16)-(17) applies.

This treats every Vaughan box. There are only polylogarithmically many dyadic boxes, Vaughan components, Fourier modes after truncation, and signs; the Fourier tails are summable and the finite label cost is absorbed into a smaller fixed power saving. Combining the Vaughan contribution with the prime-power estimate (9)-(10) proves (5).

glossary.L_1: The smaller Vaughan Type-II factor scale.
glossary.cal V_{V,P}: The fixed-target reciprocal trace for a small product v and one prime p.
glossary.lambda: The Q-exponent of the selected Vaughan factor.

3089501f7fb49c18.title: GA-LOW-qCOND: ABSOLUTE PAYMENT BY THE EFFECTIVE PHYSICAL RAY CONDUCTOR
3089501f7fb49c18.author: slava chan
3089501f7fb49c18.statement:
GA-LOW-qCOND: ABSOLUTE PAYMENT BY THE EFFECTIVE PHYSICAL RAY CONDUCTOR.

Adopt one exact orientation, anatomy, source/projective fibre, frequency block
\[
1\le F\le x^3,\qquad F\le|h|<2F,
\]
and dilator block
\[
\mathcal D\le d_\lambda<2\mathcal D
\]
from facts e55b27d39c593164 and 57a4d0753d8f290d. Let
\[
T\ne0
\]
be the signed integer target on this fibre, with \(|T|\le x^{O(1)}\). Retain the exact primitive rays
\[
R=(\epsilon,a,b),\qquad
R'=(\epsilon',a',b'),
\]
the exact post-reciprocity ray coefficients \(C_\lambda(R)\), and the ray phases \(P_\lambda(R)\) from fact 57a4d0753d8f290d. Put
\[
\Delta_0=\epsilon ba'-\epsilon'b'a
\]
and, for \(R\ne R'\), define
\[
m_q={aa'\over(aa',T\Delta_0)}.                                  \tag{1}
\]
Let \(1\le Y\le x^{O(1)}\). Let
\(\Theta(n,\lambda,R,R')\in\{0,1\}\) be any existing literal selector on the exact ray-pair sum. Then
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\left|
\sum_{n,\lambda}
\sum_{\substack{R\ne R'\\m_q\le Y}}
&\Theta(n,\lambda,R,R')
P_\lambda(R)\overline{P_\lambda(R')}\\
&\times
C_\lambda(R)\overline{C_\lambda(R')}
\right|
\le x^{o(1)}|\omega_F|^2BYF^2.
\end{aligned}
}                                                                 \tag{GA-LOW-qCOND}
\]
Every marker, Möbius, Fourier, target-gcd, fixed-\(U\), high, source, parent, ordering, equality, collision, deletion, provenance, coprimality and projective mask remains literal. The estimate is absolute, so \(\Theta\) and all those masks only delete terms. The same bound remains valid after a union of \(x^{o(1)}\) exact copy, orientation, anatomy or frozen-label families.

More precisely, nonzero support of the Möbius coefficient implies that \(a\) and \(a'\) are squarefree. Put
\[
g=(a,a'),\qquad a=g\alpha,\qquad a'=g\beta,
\]
and
\[
L_0=\epsilon b\beta-\epsilon'b'\alpha.
\]
Then \(g,\alpha,\beta\) are pairwise coprime and squarefree,
\[
\Delta_0=gL_0,\qquad(\alpha\beta,L_0)=1,
\]
and
\[
\boxed{
m_q=
{g\over(g,TL_0)}
{\alpha\beta\over(\alpha\beta,T)}.
}                                                                 \tag{2}
\]

The theorem requires \(T\ne0\). It also concerns only \(R\ne R'\); fact 57a4d0753d8f290d then gives \(\Delta_0\ne0\). No assertion is made for \(T=0\) or \(\Delta_0=0\).

As a consumer, if
\[
\mathcal D\le Q^2,
\]
take
\[
Y={Q^2\over\mathcal D}\ge1.
\]
Then the subfamily \(m_q\le Q^2/\mathcal D\) is bounded by
\[
x^{o(1)}|\omega_F|^2{BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}.                    \tag{3}
\]
If \(\mathcal D>Q^2\), the same formal threshold is less than one, so no positive integer \(m_q\) satisfies it; in particular this consumer does not pay the coherent \(m_q=1\) slice. The theorem proves no bound for the complementary large-\(m_q\) form, no coherent-core estimate when \(\mathcal D>Q^2\), no full GA-RAY-SPEC or GA-NR-DIL estimate, no tail payment, and no Goldbach conclusion.
3089501f7fb49c18.proof:
Expand every ray coefficient using fact 57a4d0753d8f290d:
\[
C_\lambda(R)
=\sum_{k\in\mathscr I_\lambda(R)}
\widetilde c_\lambda(ka,\epsilon kb).                            \tag{4}
\]
If one summand in (4) is nonzero, equation (9) of fact e55b27d39c593164 shows that
\[
\mu(ka)\ne0.
\]
Hence \(ka\) is squarefree. In particular \(a\) is squarefree. The same argument gives squarefreeness of \(a'\).

Put \(g=(a,a')\), \(a=g\alpha\), and \(a'=g\beta\). Since \(a,a'\) are squarefree,
\[
(g,\alpha)=(g,\beta)=(\alpha,\beta)=1,
\]
and \(g,\alpha,\beta\) are squarefree. Direct substitution gives
\[
\Delta_0
=\epsilon b(g\beta)-\epsilon'b'(g\alpha)
=gL_0.
\]
We prove \((\alpha\beta,L_0)=1\). If a prime \(p\mid\alpha\), then
\[
p\nmid b
\]
because \((a,b)=1\), and \(p\nmid\beta\). Reducing \(L_0\) modulo \(p\) gives
\[
L_0\equiv\epsilon b\beta\not\equiv0\pmod p.
\]
If \(p\mid\beta\), the same argument using \((a',b')=1\) gives
\[
L_0\equiv-\epsilon'b'\alpha\not\equiv0\pmod p.
\]
This proves the claimed coprimality.

Now
\[
aa'=g^2\alpha\beta,\qquad
T\Delta_0=TgL_0.
\]
Therefore
\[
(aa',T\Delta_0)
=g\,(g\alpha\beta,TL_0).
\]
Since \(g\) is coprime to \(\alpha\beta\), and
\((\alpha\beta,L_0)=1\),
\[
(g\alpha\beta,TL_0)
=(g,TL_0)(\alpha\beta,T).
\]
Divide \(aa'=g^2\alpha\beta\) by this greatest common divisor. This proves (2).

We next count primitive ray pairs. Fix \(b,b'\), the two signs, and dyadic blocks
\[
A\le a<2A,\qquad A'\le a'<2A'.
\]
Put
\[
t=(\alpha\beta,T),\qquad
u={\alpha\beta\over t},\qquad
r=(g,T).
\]
Then \(t\mid |T|\), \(r\mid |T|\), and
\[
\alpha\beta=tu.                                                   \tag{5}
\]
Because \(g\) is squarefree, writing \(g=rs\) gives
\[
(s,T)=1.
\]
Let
\[
s_0=(s,L_0),\qquad s_1=s/s_0.
\]
Then \(s_0\mid |L_0|\), and
\[
(g,TL_0)=r(s,L_0)=rs_0.
\]
Equation (2) becomes
\[
m_q=us_1.                                                         \tag{6}
\]

The data
\[
t,\ u,\ \alpha,\ \beta,\ r,\ s_0,\ s_1
\]
determine \(g=rs_0s_1\), hence \(a=g\alpha\) and \(a'=g\beta\). We may therefore overcount admissible pairs as follows. There are
\[
\tau(|T|)=x^{o(1)}
\]
choices for each of \(t\) and \(r\). Once \(t,u\) are fixed, the number of ordered factorizations
\[
tu=\alpha\beta
\]
is at most \(\tau(tu)=x^{o(1)}\). Then \(L_0\) is fixed, and there are at most
\[
\tau(|L_0|)=x^{o(1)}
\]
choices for \(s_0\). Conditions such as squarefreeness, the displayed coprimalities and membership in the two dyadic \(a\)-blocks only delete choices. Finally, (6) and \(m_q\le Y\) give
\[
us_1\le Y.
\]
The number of positive ordered pairs \((u,s_1)\) with this property is at most
\[
\sum_{u\le Y}\left\lfloor{Y\over u}\right\rfloor
\le Y(1+\log Y)=x^{o(1)}Y.
\]
All quantities are polynomially bounded in \(x\): \(T,Y,Q,F,a,a',b,b'\) are, and fact 57a4d0753d8f290d gives \(0<|\Delta_0|<8QF\), hence \(L_0\ne0\) has polynomial size. Thus the divisor estimates are uniform. We have proved that for fixed \(b,b'\), signs and dyadic \(a,a'\)-blocks,
\[
\#\{(a,a'):m_q\le Y\}\le x^{o(1)}Y.                              \tag{7}
\]

We now include the scaling multipliers. If \(F\le1/2\), the signed integer interval
\[
F\le|h|<2F
\]
is empty, because \(h\ne0\); the theorem is then immediate. Assume \(F>1/2\). On the block \(A\le a<2A\), a supported coordinate
\[
q=ka,\qquad h=\epsilon kb
\]
satisfies
\[
{Q\over2A}<k<{2Q\over A}.                                       \tag{8}
\]
Hence the number of possible positive integers \(k\) for one ray is at most
\[
K_A=1+{2Q\over A}.                                               \tag{9}
\]
Since \(|h|=kb<2F\), equation (8) gives
\[
b<{4FA\over Q}.                                                  \tag{10}
\]
Let \(B_A\) be the number of positive integers \(b\) allowed by (10). If the block is nonempty, then \(4FA/Q>1\), and
\[
B_A\le {4FA\over Q}.
\]
Every supported \(a<2Q\), so a nonempty dyadic block has \(A<2Q\). Consequently
\[
B_AK_A
\le {4FA\over Q}\left(1+{2Q\over A}\right)
={4FA\over Q}+8F
\le16F.                                                          \tag{11}
\]
The identical estimate
\[
B_{A'}K_{A'}\le16F                                               \tag{12}
\]
holds in the second coordinate.

For the fixed two dyadic blocks, sum first over \(b,b'\) and signs, use (7), and then count the at most \(K_AK_{A'}\) supported multiplier pairs for each ray pair. Equations (11)--(12) give
\[
\#\{(q_1,h_1,q_2,h_2):m_q\le Y\}
\le x^{o(1)}YF^2.                                                \tag{13}
\]
There are only \(O(\log(2Q))\) dyadic blocks for each of \(a,a'\), and the four sign choices are constant, so their sum is absorbed into \(x^{o(1)}\).

It remains to apply the literal envelopes. Fact e55b27d39c593164 proves, after extracting the fixed-frequency scalar \(\omega_F\),
\[
|\widetilde c_\lambda(q,h)|
\le x^{o(1)}|\omega_F|
\]
