on the fixed fibre, and proves that the number of exact marked copies over \(n\asymp B\), including divisor-bounded marker multiplicity, is
\[
Bx^{o(1)}.
\]
Expand both ray coefficients by (4). The phase product has modulus one, and every zero-one selector only deletes terms. Multiply the coordinate count (13) by the coefficient-product envelope and the copy count. This proves GA-LOW-qCOND.

When \(\mathcal D\le Q^2\), substitution of
\(Y=Q^2/\mathcal D\) gives (3). If
\(\mathcal D>Q^2\), this value of \(Y\) is less than one, outside the theorem's stated range; since \(m_q\) is a positive integer, the corresponding subfamily is empty and \(m_q=1\) is not included. All scope exclusions follow.

glossary.GA-LOW-qCOND: The absolute literal ray-pair payment for effective physical additive conductor m_q at most Y, with cost x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 B Y F^2.
glossary.effective physical ray conductor: The positive integer aa'/gcd(aa',T Delta_0) after reduction of the physical primitive-ray pair phase.

308b3f12b1d814db.title: Let m be a positive odd integer, let s belong to {1,-1}, let K be an integer with gcd(K,m)=1, and let W be a complex-valued function on the residues modulo m. Let G_unit be the multiplicative group of units modulo m^2. Form the matrix M_W with rows and columns indexed by G_unit by
308b3f12b1d814db.author: slava chan
308b3f12b1d814db.statement:
Let m be a positive odd integer, let s belong to {1,-1}, let K be an integer with gcd(K,m)=1, and let W be a complex-valued function on the residues modulo m. Let G_unit be the multiplicative group of units modulo m^2. Form the matrix M_W with rows and columns indexed by G_unit by
M_W(a,b)=sum_{u modulo m}W(u)Delta_{m^2}(ab-K-2smu).                  (1)
Define
W_hat(ell)=sum_{u modulo m}W(u)e_m(-ell u).
Let P_digit be the projective ell^2 tensor norm
P_digit=inf_{M_W=sum_j beta_j tensor alpha_j}
              sum_j||beta_j||_2||alpha_j||_2,                         (2)
where the infimum is over all finite exact decompositions into one-variable complex sequences on G_unit. Then
P_digit=phi(m)sum_{ell modulo m}|W_hat(ell)|.                          (3)
Equivalently, the singular values of M_W are the m numbers
|W_hat(ell)|, ell modulo m, each repeated exactly phi(m) times.

In particular:
(a) if W is the indicator of one fixed digit u_0, then P_digit=phi(m^2);
(b) if W is identically one, so that M_W is the full unweighted union of all m digit graphs and equals the indicator of ab=K modulo m, then again P_digit=phi(m^2);
(c) the sum of the projective norms of the m fixed-digit matrices is m phi(m^2), a factor m larger than the projective norm of their actual unweighted union;
(d) if sum_uW(u)=0, then
P_digit=phi(m)sum_{ell nonzero modulo m}|W_hat(ell)|.                  (4)

Thus the full digit assembly has a genuine factor-m projective-norm collapse even though the fixed-digit supports are disjoint. Lower bounds or exact costs for individual digit slices cannot be added to obtain the norm of their assembled union. The theorem concerns only the modular normal-digit product selector; multiplying it by prime, box, carry, gcd, mask, source, or other joint selectors may change the singular spectrum and requires a new norm calculation.
308b3f12b1d814db.proof:
Put
H_digit={1+mt modulo m^2:t modulo m}.
Every element of H_digit is a unit, the displayed parametrization is injective, and
(1+mt)(1+mt')=1+m(t+t') modulo m^2.
Thus H_digit is a subgroup of G_unit isomorphic to the additive group modulo m and has order m. Reduction modulo m maps G_unit onto the unit group modulo m: every unit residue modulo m has unit lifts modulo m^2. Its kernel is H_digit. Hence
|G_unit/H_digit|=phi(m^2)/m=phi(m).

For u modulo m put c_u=K+2smu modulo m^2. Since K is a unit,
c_u=K(1+m gamma u) modulo m^2,
where gamma=2sK^(-1) modulo m is a unit. Now permute the columns of M_W by replacing b with b^(-1), and then permute the rows by replacing a with Ka. These are unitary permutation operations and do not change singular values or the projective norm. The resulting matrix N satisfies
N(a,y)=W(u) if a y^(-1)=1+m gamma u modulo m^2
and is zero otherwise.                                                            (5)

Condition (5) implies that a and y lie in the same coset of H_digit. Therefore N is block diagonal over the phi(m) cosets of H_digit. Choose a representative g for one coset and write
a=g(1+mx), y=g(1+my), with x,y modulo m.
Then
a y^(-1)=1+m(x-y) modulo m^2,
so the block has entries
C_{x,y}=W(gamma^(-1)(x-y)).                                         (6)
Every coset gives the same m by m circulant block C.

The additive characters x -> e_m(ell x) diagonalize C. Direct substitution in (6) shows that its eigenvalue at frequency ell is
sum_{z modulo m}W(gamma^(-1)z)e_m(-ell z)
 =W_hat(ell gamma),
up to replacing ell by its negative according to the eigenvector convention. Since gamma is a unit, ell -> ell gamma permutes the residues modulo m. A circulant matrix is normal, so its singular values are the absolute values of its eigenvalues. Thus one block has singular values |W_hat(ell)|, ell modulo m, and the phi(m) identical blocks give each of them with multiplicity phi(m).

For a finite matrix between Hilbert spaces, the infimum in (2) equals its nuclear norm, the sum of its singular values. Indeed, a singular-value decomposition gives a decomposition attaining that sum. Conversely, let U be the partial isometry in the polar decomposition of M_W, so ||U||_op<=1 and the matrix inner product of U with M_W equals the sum of the singular values. Pairing U with any exact rank-one decomposition gives
sum of singular values
 <=sum_j||U||_op||beta_j||_2||alpha_j||_2
 <=sum_j||beta_j||_2||alpha_j||_2.
Taking the infimum proves equality. The singular-value list therefore proves (3).

For a fixed digit, every Fourier coefficient W_hat has absolute value one, so (3) gives phi(m)m=phi(m^2). For W identically one, W_hat(0)=m and all other coefficients vanish, giving the same norm. Summing the first value over m digits gives m phi(m^2), proving (a)-(c). If W is centered then W_hat(0)=0, and (4) follows from (3). The final scope statement follows because the calculation used the exact convolution structure (5), which additional selectors need not preserve.

glossary.G_unit: the multiplicative unit group modulo m^2
glossary.H_digit: the kernel of reduction from units modulo m^2 to units modulo m
glossary.M_W: the matrix of the weighted normal-digit product selector on units modulo m^2
glossary.P_digit: the projective ell^2 tensor norm of M_W

308c7c0d43bda909.title: Assume all hypotheses and notation of facts bc46ed5832faeade and 02a763eba051c761. Thus \(N=2x\), \(1/2<a<b<1\), \(D\le2x^{1/2}\),
308c7c0d43bda909.author: slava chan
308c7c0d43bda909.statement:
Assume all hypotheses and notation of facts bc46ed5832faeade and 02a763eba051c761. Thus \(N=2x\), \(1/2<a<b<1\), \(D\le2x^{1/2}\),
\[
 D\ge {1\over2}x^{1/2}(\log x)^{-B_{\rm src}},\qquad
 T_x=(\log x)^{6+\eta+\rho},
\]
\[
 {\cal I}_D=\{d\ge2:(d,N)=1,\ \mu(d)\ne0,\ d\le x^{1/2},\
                    \Phi(d/D)\ne0\},
\quad
 V_{d,m}=W(dm/x)\Phi((N-dm)/U),
\]
and \({\mathfrak C}_\star^\Lambda\) is the hard-core covariance with full von Mangoldt factors from fact 02a763eba051c761.

For nonzero integers \(H\) and integers \(p\), define the complete physical-shift coefficient
\[
\begin{split}
 {\cal A}_N(H,p)=\sum_{\substack{m\ge1\\m\mid H\\m\mid N-p}}
 &{\bf1}_{\substack{d=(N-p)/m\in{\cal I}_D,\ d+H/m\in{\cal I}_D\\
                    |H|/m>D/T_x,\ (d,H/m)<T_x}}
 \mu(d)\mu(d+H/m)\Phi(d/D)\Phi((d+H/m)/D)\\
 &\times W((N-p)/x)W((N-p+H)/x)
 \Phi(p/U)\Phi((p-H)/U).
\end{split}                                                            \tag{1}
\]
Then the following identity is exact:
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 {\mathfrak C}_\star^\Lambda
 =\sum_{H\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}}\sum_{p\in\mathbb Z}
 {\cal A}_N(H,p)\Lambda(p)\Lambda(p-H).\quad}             \tag{2}
\]
Every nonzero summand in (2) has the macroscopic physical-shift range
\[
 {ax\over2T_x}<|H|\le(b-a)x.                              \tag{3}
\]
Moreover, for every fixed \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 |{\cal A}_N(H,p)|\ll_{\varepsilon,W,\Phi}x^\varepsilon,  \tag{4}
\]
\[
 \sum_{H,p}|{\cal A}_N(H,p)|\ll_{W,\Phi,a,b}xD,           \tag{5}
\]
and
\[
 \sum_{H,p}|{\cal A}_N(H,p)|^2
 \ll_{\varepsilon,W,\Phi,a,b}x^{1+\varepsilon}D.          \tag{6}
\]

Consequently the smallest physical-shift replacement estimate may be stated one-sidedly as
\[
 \sum_{\substack{H,p\in\mathbb Z\\H\ne0}}
 {\cal A}_N(H,p)\Lambda(p)\Lambda(p-H)
 \ll_{W,\Phi,a,b,\eta,\rho}xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta}.          \tag{TB-PHYS}
\]
The estimate (TB-PHYS) is equivalent to the full-von-Mangoldt form of (TB-HARD), and by the prime-power removal in fact 02a763eba051c761 it implies (TB-HARD) itself. Hence it implies all top-band consequences in fact bc46ed5832faeade.

The coefficient in (1) preserves the complete double Möbius weight and the fixed center \(N\). In particular it is not replaced by an arbitrary coefficient: its summation variable \(m\) must simultaneously divide \(H\) and \(N-p\), and its signs are exactly
\[
 \mu((N-p)/m)\mu((N-p+H)/m).
\]
Equations (2)--(6) do not prove (TB-PHYS).
308c7c0d43bda909.proof:
Start with the exact reindexing (5) of fact 02a763eba051c761. There the modulus difference is denoted by \(h=d_2-d_1\), the first von Mangoldt argument is \(p=N-d_1m\), and the second is \(p-hm\). Put
\[
 H=hm.
\]
Then \(m\mid H\), \(m\mid N-p\),
\[
 d_1={N-p\over m},\qquad d_2=d_1+{H\over m},             \tag{7}
\]
and the second von Mangoldt argument is \(p-H\). The hard-core conditions become
\[
 {|H|\over m}>{D\over T_x},\qquad
 \left({N-p\over m},{H\over m}\right)<T_x,               \tag{8}
\]
because \((d_1,d_2)=(d_1,d_2-d_1)\). The remaining smooth factors in the summand of fact 02a763eba051c761 become precisely those in (1). Thus grouping the finite sum by \(H=hm\) proves (2).

We prove (3). A nonzero summand has
\[
 W(d_1m/x)W(d_2m/x)\ne0.
\]
Since \(W\) is supported in \([a,b]\),
\[
 ax\le d_1m,d_2m\le bx.                                  \tag{9}
\]
Their difference is \(H=(d_2-d_1)m\), so (9) gives
\[
 |H|\le(b-a)x.                                            \tag{10}
\]
Also \(\Phi(d_1/D)\ne0\) and the support of \(\Phi\) give \(d_1\le2D\). Hence (9) gives
\[
 m\ge {ax\over2D}.                                        \tag{11}
\]
The hard difference condition in (8) and (11) yield
\[
 |H|=m|d_2-d_1|>{ax\over2D}{D\over T_x}
 ={ax\over2T_x},
\]
proving (3).

For (4), every contributing \(m\) divides \(\gcd(|H|,|N-p|)\). The number of such \(m\) is at most
\(\tau(\gcd(|H|,|N-p|))\). The elementary estimate
\[
 \tau(n)\ll_\varepsilon n^\varepsilon
\]
was proved explicitly in fact 02a763eba051c761. On the support in (1), (9)--(10) and \(N=2x\) give
\[
 |H|\ll x,\qquad |N-p|=d_1m\ll x.
\]
All smooth weights are bounded and the Möbius factors have absolute value at most one. This proves (4).

For (5), expand the absolute value of (1) by the triangle inequality before grouping equal \((H,p)\). Every resulting incidence is uniquely determined by a triple
\((d_1,d_2,m)\) with \(d_1,d_2\in{\cal I}_D\) and both weights in (9) nonzero. There are \(O(D)\) choices for each \(d_i\). For fixed \(d_1,d_2\), (9) gives
\[
 m\le {bx\over\max(d_1,d_2)}\ll_{a,b}{x\over D},
\]
because \(d_i\ge D/2\). Thus the total number of triples is
\[
 O(D^2 x/D)=O(xD).
\]
Multiplying by the uniform bound for the smooth weights proves (5).

Finally,
\[
 \sum_{H,p}|{\cal A}_N(H,p)|^2
 \le\left(\sup_{H,p}|{\cal A}_N(H,p)|\right)
       \sum_{H,p}|{\cal A}_N(H,p)|.
\]
Use (4), with its exponent renamed if necessary, and (5) to obtain (6).

Identity (2) shows that (TB-PHYS) is exactly the full-von-Mangoldt hard-core upper bound. Fact 02a763eba051c761 proves that the difference between the full-von-Mangoldt and prime-only hard cores is \(o_A(xD(\log x)^{-A})\) for every fixed \(A\). Taking \(A>4+\eta\) proves the implication to (TB-HARD), and fact bc46ed5832faeade supplies the remaining consequences.

glossary.TB-PHYS: the one-sided physical-shift estimate equivalent, up to prime powers, to TB-HARD
glossary.cal A_N(H,p): the complete fixed-N raw-double-Mobius common-divisor coefficient at physical shift H and first prime argument p

31b158a7a3ce80d3.title: EXACT SHARED-PRIME C4 COMPLETION TABLE: THE p^2 COLLISION IS THE ONLY NUMERATOR DEGENERATION. Let p,a,b be pairwise coprime squarefree positive integers with p prime, and put r=pa, r'=pb, L=pab. Let C_p,C'_p be nonzero residues modulo p. Let C_a be a unit modulo every prime dividing a and C'_b a unit modulo every prime dividing b. For q in G_L define
31b158a7a3ce80d3.author: slava chan
31b158a7a3ce80d3.statement:
EXACT SHARED-PRIME C4 COMPLETION TABLE: THE p^2 COLLISION IS THE ONLY NUMERATOR DEGENERATION. Let p,a,b be pairwise coprime squarefree positive integers with p prime, and put r=pa, r'=pb, L=pab. Let C_p,C'_p be nonzero residues modulo p. Let C_a be a unit modulo every prime dividing a and C'_b a unit modulo every prime dividing b. For q in G_L define

 U(q)=e_p((C_p-C'_p)q^{-1})
      product_{ell|a}e_ell(C_ell q^{-1})
      product_{ell|b}e_ell(-C'_ell q^{-1}),                         (1)

where C_ell and C'_ell denote the displayed unit local parameters. For t modulo L, the normalized complete transform factors as

 L^{-1}sum_{q in G_L}U(q)e_L(tq)
 =[p^{-1}S_p(t(ab)^{-1},C_p-C'_p)]
  product_{ell|a}[ell^{-1}S_ell(t(L/ell)^{-1},C_ell)]
  product_{ell|b}[ell^{-1}S_ell(t(L/ell)^{-1},-C'_ell)].             (2)

The shared-prime factor in (2) has the exact table

 p^{-1}S_p(t(ab)^{-1},C_p-C'_p)=
 (p-1)/p,  if C_p=C'_p and p|t;
 -1/p,     if C_p=C'_p and p does not divide t;
 -1/p,     if C_p is not equal to C'_p and p|t;
 a number of absolute value at most 2/sqrt(p),
             if C_p is not equal to C'_p and p does not divide t.   (3)

In the same-target literal C4 specialization, with E=hn'-h'n, facts df97bf1eba0495be and 67d49768ecdc058e give

 C_p=C'_p modulo p if and only if p^2 divides E.                     (4)

At every prime belonging only to a or only to b, the corresponding inverse numerator in (2) is a unit. Hence (4) is the only possible numerator degeneration in the shared-prime completed product. Moreover it creates an order-one local factor only on the simultaneous stratum p^2|E and p|t; on the collision stratum with p not dividing t the factor is exactly -1/p, and off collision the p|t stratum is also exactly -1/p.

Thus the already verified p^2 collision condition is sufficient for the complete shared-prime numerator-gcd audit. This local theorem does not aggregate the simultaneous collision/p|t block, prove shared-prime PMLS, control literal row weights, prove C4-VEC, another anatomy bound, or Goldbach.
31b158a7a3ce80d3.proof:
The CRT identity for the additive character modulo L says
 e_L(tq)=product_{ell|L}e_ell(t(L/ell)^{-1}q).                       (5)
The unit group G_L is the Cartesian product of the local unit groups. Insert (1) and (5), then separate the local sums. At p the inverse numerator is C_p-C'_p, at ell|a it is C_ell, and at ell|b it is -C'_ell. This gives exactly (2), with S_m as in the standard definition sum_{u in G_m}e_m(alpha u+beta u^{-1}).

For the p-factor there are four cases. If both arguments are zero, every summand is one and S_p(0,0)=p-1. If exactly one argument is nonzero, either the identity map or inversion permutes F_p^*, so the sum is the sum of a nontrivial additive character over F_p^*, namely -1. If both arguments are nonzero, fact 4f9aec67f5be35db, after undoing its normalized Fourier convention, gives the Weil bound |S_p(alpha,beta)|<=2sqrt(p). Since ab is a unit modulo p, t(ab)^{-1} vanishes modulo p exactly when p|t. These observations prove the four lines of (3).

For literal same-target rows sharing p, fact df97bf1eba0495be proves that equality of the two local inverse slopes is equivalent to p^2|hn'-h'n; fact 67d49768ecdc058e is its natural C4 specialization. Those slopes are precisely C_p,C'_p in (1), proving (4). Fact 3330e83b6d253b69 proves that every active local parameter is nonzero; therefore the parameters at primes unique to a and b are units and cannot degenerate. This proves the uniqueness and all stated scope assertions.

glossary.shared-prime completion factor: The normalized p-local Kloosterman factor after completing the common output variable modulo lcm(r,r').

31c1bb8e5ea4b34b.title: GA-GOODW-RAY-NREG-LIFT: EXACT PRIMITIVE-RAY SCALING VARIATION LEDGER, ARITHMETIC-GATE NONTRANSFER, AND RESIDUAL-BRANCH INVENTORY. Adopt one complete Good-W outer row after the legal genealogy recombination of fact 18c3a93006507edb, a frequency block 1<=F<=x^3, and the one-coordinate functions C_{q,h}(y) of fact 1e357f0a9f079ca2. Let R=(epsilon,a,b) be a primitive signed ray, with epsilon in {-1,1}, a,b positive and gcd(a,b)=1, and define
31c1bb8e5ea4b34b.author: slava chan
31c1bb8e5ea4b34b.statement:
GA-GOODW-RAY-NREG-LIFT: EXACT PRIMITIVE-RAY SCALING VARIATION LEDGER, ARITHMETIC-GATE NONTRANSFER, AND RESIDUAL-BRANCH INVENTORY. Adopt one complete Good-W outer row after the legal genealogy recombination of fact 18c3a93006507edb, a frequency block 1<=F<=x^3, and the one-coordinate functions C_{q,h}(y) of fact 1e357f0a9f079ca2. Let R=(epsilon,a,b) be a primitive signed ray, with epsilon in {-1,1}, a,b positive and gcd(a,b)=1, and define
I(R)={k positive: Q<=ak<2Q, F<=bk<2F, and mu(ak) is nonzero},
M(R)=|I(R)|.                                                     (1)
Then the exact flat primitive-ray coefficient of fact bab94ab4a0e20bc0 is
B_n^base(R)=mu(a) sum_{k in I(R), gcd(ak,n)=1} mu(k) C_{ak,epsilon kb}(n/B).   (2)
If only the displayed arithmetic gate is removed, put
B_R^circ(y)=mu(a) sum_{k in I(R)}mu(k)C_{ak,epsilon kb}(y).      (3)
For every fixed A>0,
cal V_y(B_R^circ) <<_A M(R)(log x)^{C_0}(1+F/H_P)^{-A},          (4)
and
M(R)<=1+min(Q/a,F/b).                                           (5)
The factor M(R) cannot be removed as a formal consequence of the uniform one-coordinate bound: for any continuously differentiable compactly supported g, the abstract family C_{ak,epsilon kb}(y)=mu(a)mu(k)g(y) has the same coordinatewise variation norm for every k but gives B_R^circ=M(R)g. This is an abstract logical no-fit, not a claim about the literal Fourier family.

More generally, let P_{m,c} be any set of retained ordered distinct ray pairs (R,R') having fixed physical ray conductor m and numerator c, with a selector theta(R,R') independent of y and satisfying |theta(R,R')|<=1. Put
M_{m,c}^sc=sum_{(R,R') in P_{m,c}}M(R)M(R').                     (6)
The corresponding mask-free pair aggregate
F_{m,c}^circ(y)=sum_{(R,R') in P_{m,c}}theta(R,R')B_R^circ(y)conjugate(B_{R'}^circ(y))
satisfies, for every fixed A>0,
cal V_y(F_{m,c}^circ) <<_A (log x)^{2C_0}(1+F/H_P)^{-A}M_{m,c}^sc. (7)
Every supported pair (q,h) belongs to a unique primitive signed ray and scaling, so
sum_R M(R)<=4QF,
sum_{m,c}M_{m,c}^sc<=16Q^2F^2.                                 (8)
Thus absolute lifting of the verified one-coordinate regularity through all scalings, ray pairs and conductor classes supplies the scale Q^2F^2, not QF^2. Equations (7)-(8) preserve the ray-pair/conductor partition but do not assert cancellation between its terms.

The arithmetic gate omitted in (3) is a genuine variation boundary. If p is an odd prime, q=2p, J is an integer interval of length L, and u_q(n)=1_J(n)1_{gcd(n,q)=1}, extended by zero, then
sum_n|u_q(n+1)-u_q(n)| >= L/3-8.                                (9)
Hence multiplication by gcd(q,n)=1 can turn the constant smooth function on J into a sequence of linear discrete variation. Equation (9) is a structural no-transfer example; it is not asserted to be a nonzero literal Good-W Fourier coordinate. It proves that (4) alone does not control the actual arithmetic-gated coefficient (2).

Finally adopt the exact supported A/C terminal profiles of fact 875cb4f04516b35e on D<=d<2D. If the C profile is nonempty, then
B/8<D<=2B, and hence 1/2<=B/D<8.                                (10)
If the A profile is nonempty through n=dp, then its marked prime satisfies
B/(4D)<p<=2B/D.                                                  (11)
Thus the C profile has no asymptotically small terminal-incidence factor: it remains the supported squarefree Z-rough character sum with v in {1,2}. The A profile has only O(B/D) possible marked-prime extensions before its exact weight 1/(r_Z(d)+1)^2, support, coprimality and f(dp) are imposed.

Consequently neither N-qSRC-SUP nor C-qSRC-PV-BV-SUP follows from facts 1e357f0a9f079ca2 and 875cb4f04516b35e by absolute variation lifting. In the C range, the relaxed PV-BV budget BQF^2/D is of order QF^2 by (10), while the mask-free absolute aggregation ledger (8) is of order Q^2F^2, already one factor Q larger, before paying the arithmetic gate, squarefreeness, roughness, inherited finite support, Gauss weights, or terminal-dependent f(dv). This comparison is a method ledger, not a lower bound for the literal source. The first remaining arithmetic mechanism is joint cancellation across primitive-ray scalings and ray-pair/conductor classes while retaining those terminal conditions.

The separate branch inventory is exact. On D>Q^2 and F<=Q, fact cd13b5e0a78656f1 pays the complete principal source by the first BQF moment term. For D>Q^2 and F>Q, that fact does not apply and the principal source remains separate from N-qSRC-SUP. For D<=Q^2, the N-transform fact bab94ab4a0e20bc0 does not apply; fact 3089501f7fb49c18 pays only the low physical-conductor projection, while fact c384d36af25e96a6 supplies the terminal Schur norm but not its complete projected analytic consumer. No F>Q principal estimate, small-D projected-incidence estimate, N-qSRC-SUP, C-qSRC-PV-BV-SUP, tail payment, or Goldbach conclusion is proved.
31c1bb8e5ea4b34b.proof:
Equation (3) of fact 18c3a93006507edb gives the mask-free pre-copy coefficient mu(q)C_{q,h}(n/B), with the separate arithmetic restriction gcd(q,n)=1. On R substitute q=ak and h=epsilon kb. Nonzero mu(ak) makes ak squarefree, so gcd(a,k)=1 and mu(ak)=mu(a)mu(k), exactly as in fact a36284a9dbec7837. Summing the supported scalings gives (2), and deleting only gcd(ak,n)=1 gives (3).

The variation norm is subadditive. Fact 1e357f0a9f079ca2 bounds every summand in (3), with an implied constant depending on A, by the quantity in (4). This proves (4) with the displayed <<_A notation. The k-range is the intersection of two half-open real intervals of respective lengths Q/a and F/b. An interval of length L_0 contains at most L_0+1 integers, proving (5). In the displayed abstract family, squarefreeness on I(R) gives mu(a)^2=mu(k)^2=1, so every summand in (3) equals g and their sum is M(R)g. This proves the sharp logical no-fit.

For cal V=supremum plus total variation, cal V(f conjugate(g))<=3 cal V(f)cal V(g): the supremum costs at most sup(f)sup(g), and the derivative integral costs at most sup(f)int|g'|+sup(g)int|f'|. Apply this to each pair in (6), invoke (4) with a sufficiently large fixed exponent, and use the triangle inequality. The A-dependent constants remain inside <<_A, proving (7). Each supported nonzero integer pair (q,h) has the unique representation k=gcd(q,|h|), a=q/k, b=|h|/k, epsilon=sgn(h). There are fewer than 2Q choices for q and fewer than 2F choices for signed h in the dyadic blocks, proving the first inequality (8). Summing M(R)M(R') over any subfamily of ordered ray pairs is at most (sum_R M(R))^2, proving the second.

For (9), every integer coprime to q=2p is odd, and both adjacent integers are even and hence not coprime to q. Apart from the two endpoints of J, each coprime integer therefore contributes two distinct unit jumps. Among L consecutive integers, at least (L-2)/2-1 are odd interior integers, and at most L/p+2 of them are divisible by p. Since p>=3, the number of interior units is at least L/6-4. Twice this number proves (9).

For C, fact 875cb4f04516b35e gives n=dv with v in {1,2}, B/2<=n<=2B and D<=d<2D. Hence B/4<=d<=2B. From d<2D and D<=d one obtains B/8<D<=2B, proving (10). For A the same fact gives n=dp. The inequalities n>=B/2 and d<2D give p>B/(4D), while n<=2B and d>=D give p<=2B/D, proving (11).

The comparison with the relaxed budget uses only (8), (10), and the exact right side BQF^2/D in fact e6c2db667302ed26. It is explicitly an audit of what absolute lifting proves, so it makes no assertion that the literal signed aggregate attains that upper scale. The final branch inventory is exactly the hypothesis and exclusion ledger of facts cd13b5e0a78656f1, bab94ab4a0e20bc0, 3089501f7fb49c18 and c384d36af25e96a6.

glossary.B_R^circ(y): The continuously interpolated primitive-ray coefficient with only the arithmetic gate gcd(ak,n)=1 removed.
glossary.F_{m,c}^circ(y): The mask-free ray-pair aggregate indexed by P_{m,c}.
glossary.I(R): The positive scaling set of a primitive signed ray after complete Good-W genealogy recombination, before the n-coprimality gate.
glossary.M_{m,c}^sc: The sum of M(R)M(R') over P_{m,c}.
glossary.P_{m,c}: A retained set of ordered distinct primitive-ray pairs with physical conductor m and numerator c.

31ebcf364862d83a.title: GLOBAL PRIMITIVE-RAY SPECTRAL DIAGONALIZATION FOR A CANONICAL MARKED-DILATOR COPY, AND THE EXACT GOOD-\(\mathscr W\)/TOP-CS5 CONSUMERS
31ebcf364862d83a.author: slava chan
31ebcf364862d83a.statement:
GLOBAL PRIMITIVE-RAY SPECTRAL DIAGONALIZATION FOR A CANONICAL MARKED-DILATOR COPY, AND THE EXACT GOOD-\(\mathscr W\)/TOP-CS5 CONSUMERS.

Let \(\mathscr A_{\rm tar}\ne0\) be an integer. Let \(\lambda\) be any exact canonical marked-dilator copy whose reciprocal row has the form
\[
 K_\lambda
 =
 \sum_{q,h}\widetilde c_\lambda(q,h)
 e_{d_\lambda}\!\left(
 \mathscr A_{\rm tar}h(qv_\lambda)^{-1}\right),                  \tag{1}
\]
where
\[
 n=d_\lambda v_\lambda,\qquad (d_\lambda,v_\lambda)=1,
\]
\(d_\lambda\) is squarefree, and the complete literal coefficient
\(\widetilde c_\lambda(q,h)\), extended by zero, is supported only on
\[
 Q\le q<2Q,\qquad F\le |h|<2F,\qquad (q,n)=1.                    \tag{2}
\]
This includes every canonical top \(B,C1,C2,C3,C4\) copy in fact
41b56ed8e64bdba6. It also includes every good-\(\mathscr W\)
\(A,C_\ell\) copy in fact e55b27d39c593164, in either orientation after using its exact reverse reindexing and the corresponding signed nonzero target.

Put
\[
 c_\lambda=(d_\lambda,\mathscr A_{\rm tar}),\qquad
 \delta_\lambda={d_\lambda\over c_\lambda},\qquad
 A_{\lambda,0}={\mathscr A_{\rm tar}\over c_\lambda}.            \tag{3}
\]
Then
\[
 (A_{\lambda,0},\delta_\lambda)=1.                               \tag{4}
\]
Every supported signed pair \((q,h)\) has the unique form
\[
 (q,h)=k(q_\gamma,h_\gamma),\qquad
 k\text{ a positive integer},\quad q_\gamma>0,\quad
 (q_\gamma,|h_\gamma|)=1.                                       \tag{5}
\]
Let \(\Gamma_\lambda\) be the finite set of primitive signed rays
\(\gamma=(q_\gamma,h_\gamma)\) occurring in (5), and define
\[
 S_\lambda(\gamma)
 =
 \sum_{\substack{k\text{ positive}\\
 \widetilde c_\lambda(kq_\gamma,kh_\gamma)\ne0}}
 \widetilde c_\lambda(kq_\gamma,kh_\gamma).                     \tag{6}
\]
For \(\gamma\in\Gamma_\lambda\), define
\[
 x_{\lambda,\gamma}
 \equiv h_\gamma q_\gamma^{-1}\pmod{\delta_\lambda},\qquad
 \xi_\lambda
 \equiv A_{\lambda,0}v_\lambda^{-1}\pmod{\delta_\lambda}.        \tag{7}
\]
When \(\delta_\lambda=1\), these are the unique residues modulo one. Put
\[
 R_\lambda(x)
 =
 \sum_{\substack{\gamma\in\Gamma_\lambda\\
 x_{\lambda,\gamma}=x}}
 S_\lambda(\gamma)
 \qquad(x\pmod{\delta_\lambda}),                                 \tag{8}
\]
and use the unnormalized additive Fourier transform
\[
 \widehat R_\lambda(\eta)
 =
 \sum_{x\ ({\rm mod}\ \delta_\lambda)}
 R_\lambda(x)e_{\delta_\lambda}(\eta x)
 \qquad(\eta\pmod{\delta_\lambda}).                              \tag{9}
\]
Then the complete literal row satisfies
\[
 \boxed{K_\lambda=\widehat R_\lambda(\xi_\lambda).}              \tag{10}
\]

For two primitive signed rays \(\gamma_i=(q_i^\circ,h_i^\circ)\), put
\[
 \Delta^\circ(\gamma_1,\gamma_2)
 =
 h_1^\circ q_2^\circ-h_2^\circ q_1^\circ.                       \tag{11}
\]
For supported scalings \(k_1,k_2\), the original TT-star determinant is
\[
 \Delta
 =
 (k_1h_1^\circ)(k_2q_2^\circ)
 -(k_2h_2^\circ)(k_1q_1^\circ)
 =
 k_1k_2\Delta^\circ(\gamma_1,\gamma_2).                          \tag{12}
\]
One has
\[
 \Delta=0
 \Longleftrightarrow
 \gamma_1=\gamma_2,                                              \tag{13}
\]
and, for distinct rays,
\[
 d_\lambda\mid\mathscr A_{\rm tar}\Delta
 \Longleftrightarrow
 \delta_\lambda\mid\Delta^\circ(\gamma_1,\gamma_2)
 \Longleftrightarrow
 x_{\lambda,\gamma_1}=x_{\lambda,\gamma_2}.                      \tag{14}
\]
Thus distinct rays are fully resonant exactly when they have the same reduced slope.

Let \(M_\lambda^{(0)}\), \(M_\lambda^{({\rm FR})}\), and
\(M_\lambda^{({\rm NR})}\) denote the three restrictions of the expansion of
\(|K_\lambda|^2\) defined by
\[
 \Delta=0,\qquad
 \Delta\ne0,\ d_\lambda\mid\mathscr A_{\rm tar}\Delta,\qquad
 \Delta\ne0,\ d_\lambda\nmid\mathscr A_{\rm tar}\Delta,
\]
respectively. Then
\[
 \boxed{
 M_\lambda^{(0)}+M_\lambda^{({\rm FR})}
 =
 \sum_{x\ ({\rm mod}\ \delta_\lambda)}|R_\lambda(x)|^2
 =
 {1\over\delta_\lambda}
 \sum_{\eta\ ({\rm mod}\ \delta_\lambda)}
 |\widehat R_\lambda(\eta)|^2,
 }                                                               \tag{15}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 M_\lambda^{({\rm NR})}
 =
 |\widehat R_\lambda(\xi_\lambda)|^2
 -{1\over\delta_\lambda}
  \sum_{\eta\ ({\rm mod}\ \delta_\lambda)}
  |\widehat R_\lambda(\eta)|^2.
 }                                                               \tag{RAY-SPECTRAL}
\]
For \(\delta_\lambda=1\), the right side of RAY-SPECTRAL is zero.
If
\[
 \delta_\lambda>8QF,                                             \tag{16}
\]
then the map \(\gamma\mapsto x_{\lambda,\gamma}\) is injective and
\(M_\lambda^{({\rm FR})}=0\).

The identity is literal: every marker, Möbius, physical Fourier, target-gcd,
fixed-\(U\), high, source, parent, ordering, equality, collision, deletion,
provenance, coprimality, and projective factor remains inside the coefficient
summed in (6). No mask is replaced by an arbitrary coefficient and no absolute value is taken before RAY-SPECTRAL.

There are two exact consumers.

First, in the fixed-anatomy good-\(\mathscr W\) setting of facts
e55b27d39c593164 and c7970d9d1337bd09, sum RAY-SPECTRAL over the exact
\((n,\lambda)\)-copies in one anatomy
\(\mathfrak a\in\{A,C_\ell\}\), one frequency block
\(1\le F\le x^3\), and one dilator block
\(\mathcal D\le d_\lambda<2\mathcal D\). The required estimate is
\[
 \boxed{
 \left|
 \sum_{n,\lambda}
 \left(
 |\widehat R_\lambda(\xi_\lambda)|^2
 -{1\over\delta_\lambda}
  \sum_{\eta\ ({\rm mod}\ \delta_\lambda)}
  |\widehat R_\lambda(\eta)|^2
 \right)
 \right|
 \ll_\varepsilon
 x^\varepsilon|\omega_F|^2{BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}.
 }                                                               \tag{GA-RAY-SPEC}
\]
GA-RAY-SPEC is exactly the anatomy-restricted GA-NR-DIL estimate and, together with the already paid sectors, supplies the good-\(\mathscr W\) block consumer.

Second, for the canonical top \(B,C1,C2,C3,C4\) copies of fact
41b56ed8e64bdba6, the analogous sum of RAY-SPECTRAL over every exact anatomy and copy in a fixed canonical dilator block is precisely the unpaid nonresonant sector of its candidate canonical marked-dilator moment. Thus the source-specific bound
\[
 \left|\sum_{\mathfrak a\in\{B,C1,C2,C3,C4\}}
       \sum_{n,\lambda\ {\rm of}\ \mathfrak a}
       M_\lambda^{({\rm NR})}\right|
 \ll_\varepsilon
 Q^\varepsilon{BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}                           \tag{TOP-CS5-RAY-SPEC}
\]
together with fact 54029717e980dcb7 closes the canonical moment target
\[
 Q^\varepsilon\left(BQF+{BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}\right)
\]
for this complete top five-anatomy family. TOP-CS5-RAY-SPEC is an explicit
unproved consumer, not a conclusion.

Generic Parseval does not prove either consumer. For any integer
\(\delta>1\) and specified residue \(\xi\), the abstract array
\[
 R(x)=e_\delta(-\xi x)
\]
has
\[
 |\widehat R(\xi)|^2=\delta^2,\qquad
 {1\over\delta}\sum_\eta|\widehat R(\eta)|^2=\delta,
\]
so its spectral discrepancy is \(\delta(\delta-1)\). This array is not asserted to arise from the literal source. It proves only that the specified-frequency-minus-average expression needs source-specific cancellation across the actual
\(d_\lambda,v_\lambda\), ray coefficients, and masks; Parseval or a generic norm comparison alone cannot pay it.

No GA-RAY-SPEC estimate, no TOP-CS5-RAY-SPEC estimate, no complete good-\(\mathscr W\) or top-CS5 payment, and no Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
31ebcf364862d83a.proof:
For every supported \((q,h)\), define
\[
 k=(q,|h|),\qquad q_\gamma=q/k,\qquad h_\gamma=h/k.
\]
Then \(k>0\), \(q_\gamma>0\), and
\((q_\gamma,|h_\gamma|)=1\). This representation is unique, proving (5).

Because \((q,n)=1\), with \(q=kq_\gamma\) and
\(n=d_\lambda v_\lambda\), every one of
\[
 k,\quad q_\gamma,\quad v_\lambda
\]
is a unit modulo \(d_\lambda\), hence also modulo
\(\delta_\lambda\). Write
\[
 d_\lambda=c_\lambda\delta_\lambda,\qquad
 \mathscr A_{\rm tar}=c_\lambda A_{\lambda,0}.
\]
Definition (3) gives (4). For a supported pair on ray \(\gamma\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 e_{d_\lambda}\!\left(
 \mathscr A_{\rm tar}(kh_\gamma)
 (kq_\gamma v_\lambda)^{-1}\right)
 &=
 e_{\delta_\lambda}\!\left(
 A_{\lambda,0}h_\gamma
 (q_\gamma v_\lambda)^{-1}\right)\\
 &=
 e_{\delta_\lambda}(\xi_\lambda x_{\lambda,\gamma}).
 \end{aligned}                                                   \tag{17}
\]
The phase is independent of \(k\). Group (1) first by primitive signed ray,
using (6), and then by the slope fibres in (8). Equation (17) gives
\[
 K_\lambda
 =\sum_xR_\lambda(x)e_{\delta_\lambda}(\xi_\lambda x)
 =\widehat R_\lambda(\xi_\lambda),
\]
which proves (10).

Equation (12) follows by substitution. If
\(\gamma_1=\gamma_2\), then \(\Delta^\circ=0\), hence \(\Delta=0\).
Conversely, if \(\Delta=0\), then
\[
 {h_1^\circ\over q_1^\circ}
 ={h_2^\circ\over q_2^\circ}.
\]
The denominators are positive and both signed numerator-denominator pairs are primitive. Equality of the reduced signed fractions forces
\[
 q_1^\circ=q_2^\circ,\qquad h_1^\circ=h_2^\circ,
\]
which proves (13).

For distinct rays, \(\Delta^\circ\ne0\). Both supported scalings are units modulo \(d_\lambda\), so
\[
 d_\lambda\mid\mathscr A_{\rm tar}\Delta
 \Longleftrightarrow
 d_\lambda\mid\mathscr A_{\rm tar}\Delta^\circ
 \Longleftrightarrow
 \delta_\lambda\mid\Delta^\circ,                                \tag{18}
\]
where the last equivalence uses (3)--(4). On the other hand,
\[
 x_{\lambda,\gamma_1}-x_{\lambda,\gamma_2}
 \equiv
 \Delta^\circ(\gamma_1,\gamma_2)
 (q_1^\circ q_2^\circ)^{-1}
 \pmod{\delta_\lambda}.                                         \tag{19}
\]
The denominator in (19) is a unit. Equations (18)--(19) prove (14).

Expand (10):
\[
 |K_\lambda|^2
 =
 \sum_{x,y}
 e_{\delta_\lambda}(\xi_\lambda(x-y))
 R_\lambda(x)\overline{R_\lambda(y)}.                            \tag{20}
\]
By (13)--(14), the terms with \(x=y\) consist exactly of the ray diagonals
\(\Delta=0\) and the distinct-ray fully resonant terms. Therefore
\[
 M_\lambda^{(0)}+M_\lambda^{({\rm FR})}
 =\sum_x|R_\lambda(x)|^2.                                       \tag{21}
\]
Finite-group Parseval for the transform (9) gives
\[
 \sum_x|R_\lambda(x)|^2
 ={1\over\delta_\lambda}\sum_\eta|\widehat R_\lambda(\eta)|^2.
\]
This proves (15). Subtract (15) from
\(|K_\lambda|^2=|\widehat R_\lambda(\xi_\lambda)|^2\); the remaining terms
in (20) have \(x\ne y\), which are exactly the NR terms by (14). This proves
RAY-SPECTRAL, including \(\delta_\lambda=1\).

For distinct rays, support in (2) gives
\[
 q_i^\circ<2Q,\qquad |h_i^\circ|<2F.
\]
Consequently
\[
 0<|\Delta^\circ(\gamma_1,\gamma_2)|<8QF.                        \tag{22}
\]
Under (16), \(\delta_\lambda\) cannot divide the nonzero integer in (22).
Equations (14) and (19) show that all slopes are distinct and no distinct-ray
FR term exists. This proves the collision-free assertion.

Facts 41b56ed8e64bdba6 and e55b27d39c593164 supply (1)--(2) with their exact
literal coefficients for, respectively, the top canonical copies and the
good-\(\mathscr W\) copies. The proof above only regroups those coefficients,
so every literal factor remains in (6).

In the good-\(\mathscr W\) specialization, RAY-SPECTRAL summed over the fixed
anatomy is, by the exact sector definition in e55b27d39c593164, precisely
\(\mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{({\rm NR})}(\mathcal D)\).
Fact c7970d9d1337bd09 identifies its required bound with the right side of
GA-RAY-SPEC and records the already paid proportional and fully resonant
sectors. This proves the first consumer equivalence.

In the top specialization, fact 41b56ed8e64bdba6 defines the canonical
moment by summing \(|K_\lambda|^2\) over all exact
\(B,C1,C2,C3,C4\) copies. Fact 54029717e980dcb7 bounds its \(\Delta=0\)
sector by \(Q^\varepsilon BQF\) and its fully resonant sector by
\(Q^\varepsilon BQ^2F^2/\mathcal D\). RAY-SPECTRAL is exactly its remaining
NR sector. Therefore TOP-CS5-RAY-SPEC plus those two bounds gives the displayed
canonical moment target. This proves the second consumer equivalence without
asserting the consumer estimate.

Finally, for the abstract array \(R(x)=e_\delta(-\xi x)\),
\[
 \widehat R(\eta)
 =\sum_{x\ ({\rm mod}\ \delta)}e_\delta((\eta-\xi)x)
 =
 \begin{cases}
 \delta,&\eta=\xi,\\
 0,&\eta\ne\xi.
 \end{cases}
\]
The two displayed values and the discrepancy follow. Since this calculation
uses an abstract array rather than (6), it is only the stated generic
Parseval no-fit. All limitations follow.

glossary.GA-RAY-SPEC: The good-W summed specified-frequency-minus-average estimate displayed in the statement.
glossary.R_lambda(x): The sum of primitive-ray coefficients having reduced slope x modulo delta_lambda.
glossary.S_lambda(gamma): The complete literal coefficient summed over all supported positive scalings on one primitive signed ray.
glossary.TOP-CS5-RAY-SPEC: The analogous complete top B,C1,C2,C3,C4 ray-spectral estimate displayed in the statement.
glossary.global primitive-ray spectral diagonaliz: The exact expression of one canonical marked-dilator NR moment as a specified additive spectral value minus the complete spectral average.
glossary.xi_lambda: The specified additive frequency A_lambda,0 v_lambda^(-1) modulo delta_lambda.

3207666028864f95.title: EXACT CONSTANT-eta EXTRACTION FROM GA-CqADD-ETA AND THE MEAN-ZERO RESIDUAL SPECTRUM
3207666028864f95.author: slava chan
3207666028864f95.statement:
EXACT CONSTANT-eta EXTRACTION FROM GA-CqADD-ETA AND THE MEAN-ZERO RESIDUAL SPECTRUM.

Adopt GA-CqADD-ETA and the notation of fact f0fa4ee49bb23934. Fix one positive squarefree additive conductor t and let eta run over the units modulo t. Put
Zbar_t(n)=phi(t)^{-1}sum_eta^* Z_{t,eta}^{agg}(n),
Gbar_t=phi(t)^{-1}sum_eta^* G_{t,eta}^{agg},                         (1)
and
G_{t,eta}^{perp}=G_{t,eta}^{agg}-Gbar_t.                            (2)
Then
sum_eta^*G_{t,eta}^{perp}=0.                                        (3)

The normalized Kloosterman columns satisfy the exact identity
sum_eta^*V_{t;eta}=t^{-1/2} 1_t,                                   (4)
where 1_t is the vector that is identically one on the primitive additive-frequency coordinates a modulo t. Consequently the fixed-t part of GA-CqADD-ETA decomposes exactly as
sum_eta^*<V_{t;eta},G_{t,eta}^{agg}>
 =
 [mu(t)/(t phi(t))]
 sum_eta^*sum_n Z_{t,eta}^{agg}(n)
 +sum_eta^*<V_{t;eta},G_{t,eta}^{perp}>.                            (GA-ETA-MEAN)
Every literal coefficient and pair-dependent deletion remains inside Z_{t,eta}^{agg}.

The first term of GA-ETA-MEAN is the complete constant-eta component. It carries the explicit factor 1/(t phi(t)); no cancellation estimate for its remaining total coefficient is asserted. The second term is exactly mean-zero in the eta index.

Let M_t be the column Gram from fact f0fa4ee49bb23934. Its global constant eta-vector has eigenvalue 1/t. If t has an odd prime divisor, let p_*(t) be its least odd prime divisor. On the orthogonal complement of the global constant eta-vector, the least eigenvalue of M_t is
p_*(t)^2/t.                                                         (5)
If t is a power of two, squarefreeness leaves only t=1 or t=2; for t=2 the eta space is one-dimensional and the mean-zero residual in GA-ETA-MEAN is zero.

Thus extracting the explicit constant mode removes the unique global 1/t column direction. Any further use of the column spectrum on the residual begins at p_*(t)^2/t, while its top eigenvalue remains at most t. This is an exact spectral and source decomposition only. It does not prove that the constant term is at the canonical scale, estimate the mean-zero residual, prove GA-qCENT, a tail payment, or Goldbach.
3207666028864f95.proof:
By definition,
G_{t,eta}^{agg}
 =sum_n conjugate(Z_{t,eta}^{agg}(n))E_{t;n}.
Averaging this identity over eta gives
Gbar_t=sum_n conjugate(Zbar_t(n))E_{t;n}.
Equation (3) follows immediately from (1)-(2).

We prove (4). From fact f0fa4ee49bb23934,
V_{t;eta}(a)=t^{-1/2}S_t(a,eta)
 =t^{-1/2}sum_{x (mod t)}^*e_t(ax+eta x^{-1}).
Therefore
sum_eta^*V_{t;eta}(a)
 =t^{-1/2}sum_x^*e_t(ax)sum_eta^*e_t(eta x^{-1}).                   (6)
Because x is a unit, multiplication by x^{-1} permutes the units, so the inner sum is the Ramanujan sum c_t(1)=mu(t). Since a is also a unit, the outer x-sum is c_t(a)=mu(t). The conductor t is squarefree, so mu(t)^2=1. Equation (6) is therefore t^{-1/2}, independently of a, proving (4).

Decompose
G_{t,eta}^{agg}=Gbar_t+G_{t,eta}^{perp}
inside the fixed-t part of GA-CqADD-ETA and sum over eta:
sum_eta<V_{t;eta},G_{t,eta}^{agg}>
 =<sum_eta V_{t;eta},Gbar_t>
  +sum_eta<V_{t;eta},G_{t,eta}^{perp}>.                             (7)
Use (4) in the first term. For every supported physical source value n, fact 7ee795d9bff04bb2 gives gcd(n,t)=1. Hence
<t^{-1/2}1_t,E_{t;n}>
 =t^{-1}sum_{a (mod t)}^*e_t(-an)
 =mu(t)/t.                                                          (8)
The inner product is linear in its first argument and conjugate-linear in its second. Since
Gbar_t=sum_n conjugate(Zbar_t(n))E_{t;n},
equation (8) gives
<t^{-1/2}1_t,Gbar_t>
 =[mu(t)/t]sum_n Zbar_t(n)
 =[mu(t)/(t phi(t))]sum_eta sum_n Z_{t,eta}^{agg}(n).               (9)
Substitution in (7) proves GA-ETA-MEAN.

It remains to prove (5). Fact f0fa4ee49bb23934 identifies M_t, under CRT, with the tensor product of local matrices M_p. At every odd p, the local constant vector has eigenvalue p^{-1}, while its perpendicular complement has eigenvalue p. At p=2 only the one-dimensional constant vector and eigenvalue 1/2 occur. The global constant tensor chooses p^{-1} at every prime and has eigenvalue product_{p|t}p^{-1}=1/t.

A tensor eigenvector perpendicular to the global constant tensor must choose a perpendicular local eigenvector at at least one odd prime p. Replacing the local choice p^{-1} by p multiplies the global eigenvalue by p^2. The least possible multiplier is therefore p_*(t)^2, achieved by making this replacement only at the least odd prime and keeping every other local factor constant. This proves (5). If t=2 there is no local perpendicular direction, so (3) forces the one-dimensional eta residual to vanish. All scope statements follow from the exact decomposition.

glossary.1_t: The vector identically equal to one on the unit additive-frequency coordinates modulo t.
glossary.GA-ETA-MEAN: The exact decomposition of one fixed-t GA-CqADD-ETA block into its constant-eta scalar component and mean-zero residual.
glossary.Gbar_t: The corresponding eta-average primitive additive-frequency source vector.
glossary.Zbar_t(n): The average over unit inverse-argument classes eta of the exact aggregate coefficient Z_{t,eta}^{agg}(n).
glossary.p_*(t): The least odd prime divisor of t, when one exists.

323499eb9e75ce72.title: QUANTITATIVE SELECTED FIXED-BAD-\(N\) POST-\(A,B\) REMAINDER
323499eb9e75ce72.author: slava chan
323499eb9e75ce72.statement:
QUANTITATIVE SELECTED FIXED-BAD-\(N\) POST-\(A,B\) REMAINDER.

Assume the hypotheses and notation of facts \(c155c30b0450a4f9\) and
\(771d292cffc890c1\). Thus \(\mathscr R_{\rm postA,sel}\) is the same-bad-\(N\)
negative post-\(A\) remainder satisfying
\[
 \mathscr R_{\rm postA,sel}
 \le -c_{\rm dir}\mathfrak c(N)\frac{x}{\log x}
 +o\!\left(\mathfrak c(N)\frac{x}{\log x}\right),              \tag{1}
\]
and in the first buffer
\[
 \beta_0<\beta_{\rm norm}\le\beta_1
\]
it has parent \(U_{\rm low}\) and anatomy in \(B,C1,C2,C3\).

Let \(\mathscr R_{B,U_{\rm low}}\) be the complete selected raised-stopping
\(B\) aggregate inside \(\mathscr R_{\rm postA,sel}\) in that first buffer,
with all target-gcd, prime-order, collision, Fourier, and other auxiliary
refinements summed to completion. Define
\[
 \mathscr R_{\rm postAB,sel}
 =
 \mathscr R_{\rm postA,sel}-\mathscr R_{B,U_{\rm low}}.        \tag{2}
\]
Then there is a fixed \(\delta_B>0\) such that
\[
 |\mathscr R_{B,U_{\rm low}}|\ll x^{1-\delta_B},               \tag{3}
\]
and
\[
 \mathscr R_{\rm postAB,sel}
 \le -c_{\rm dir}\mathfrak c(N)\frac{x}{\log x}
 +o\!\left(\mathfrak c(N)\frac{x}{\log x}\right).              \tag{4}
\]

Within \(\beta_0<\beta_{\rm norm}\le\beta_1\), the exact remaining anatomy
list is
\[
 C1,\ C2,\ C3,
\]
and the parent remains \(U_{\rm low}\). No arbitrary joint deletion mask is
inserted: the frozen \(U_{\rm low}\) parent is a label scalar allowed by fact
\(771d292cffc890c1\), while all auxiliary \(B\) refinements are recombined
before estimation.

No \(C1,C2,C3\), actual-\(Z\), endpoint, terminal, or \(C2\)-negative
selection and no Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
323499eb9e75ce72.proof:
Fact \(c155c30b0450a4f9\) proves (1) and the exact
first-buffer parent/anatomy list \(U_{\rm low}\times\{B,C1,C2,C3\}\).

Fact \(771d292cffc890c1\) proves a fixed power saving for the complete literal
raised-stopping \(B\) aggregate throughout the same normalized-beta buffer,
over every actual imbalance and exact outer gcd. Its statement explicitly
permits inherited frozen parent labels acting as label scalars and explicitly
requires all inherited target-gcd, prime-order, collision, and deletion
refinements to be summed to completion rather than imposed as arbitrary
joint masks. Therefore it applies to the \(U_{\rm low}\)-parent complete
\(B\) aggregate defined in the statement and proves (3).

The lower bound \(\mathfrak c(N)\ge C_2>0\) inherited from the fixed-bad-\(N\)
source makes (3) equal to
\(o(\mathfrak c(N)x/\log x)\). Subtract (3) in the exact identity (2) and use
(1) to obtain (4). Removing the \(B\) coordinate from the exact disjoint list
\(B,C1,C2,C3\) leaves \(C1,C2,C3\). No other selector is used, which proves
all scope statements.

glossary.delta_B: A fixed positive power-saving exponent for the selected U_low-parent complete B-buffer aggregate.
glossary.mathscr R_{B,U_low}: The complete selected U_low-parent raised-stopping B aggregate in the first post-low normalized-beta buffer, with all auxiliary refinements recombined.
glossary.mathscr R_{postAB,sel}: The selected same-bad-N negative remainder after independently subtracting the accepted A and complete B buffers.

328503a935cabe60.title: CRIT-SAME-MASK-ZERO: COMPLETE CRITICAL-PROJECTION DELETION RECOMBINATION AND THE LITERAL PHYSICAL MINUS ZERO-MODE IDENTITY. Fix tau>0. Work with the complete selected same-N critical projection obtained from the beta>=6/5 part of the post-low source of fact 7ffe3d237362a451, after the complete top-sliver subtraction of fact 3f2f255ea6845a50, and restrict by the outer scale condition mathscr W<Q^tau. Fix one orientation and all outer coordinates g,c,q,n and frozen source, dyadic, fixed-U, high, parent, provenance and factorization labels, but do not select a proper deletion leaf or marker descendant. Use the exact descent of fact 8d9feea8c44da2c8:
328503a935cabe60.author: slava chan
328503a935cabe60.statement:
CRIT-SAME-MASK-ZERO: COMPLETE CRITICAL-PROJECTION DELETION RECOMBINATION AND THE LITERAL PHYSICAL MINUS ZERO-MODE IDENTITY. Fix tau>0. Work with the complete selected same-N critical projection obtained from the beta>=6/5 part of the post-low source of fact 7ffe3d237362a451, after the complete top-sliver subtraction of fact 3f2f255ea6845a50, and restrict by the outer scale condition mathscr W<Q^tau. Fix one orientation and all outer coordinates g,c,q,n and frozen source, dyadic, fixed-U, high, parent, provenance and factorization labels, but do not select a proper deletion leaf or marker descendant. Use the exact descent of fact 8d9feea8c44da2c8:
q t+n kappa=ell, ell=N/(gc).                                     (1)

On this complete critical projection, the product of all surviving t- or kappa-dependent zero-one deletion selectors recombines pointwise to one on every integer solution of (1). More precisely:

(a) The original selected physical source is the literal smooth double-Mobius source displayed in fact dde1e246a629bcc4; its t- and kappa-dependence consists of logarithms and specified smooth W, psi and Phi factors. It contains no independent zero-one source deletion.

(b) Every target-gcd, order, equal-cell, collision, deletion or provenance coordinate introduced in a marker/anatomy refinement is an auxiliary finite partition. Whenever the corresponding full coordinate is retained, summing its complementary siblings returns the pre-refinement coefficient. All marker-dependent descendants are first recombined to the literal normalized Mobius factor by fact a71f777ad842c886. The beta>=6/5 family is inherited unchanged through fact 3f2f255ea6845a50, because that fact subtracts only a strict beta<6/5 projection.

(c) Fact 7ffe3d237362a451 explicitly inserts no actual-(r,k) Z_mid deletion into the selected post-low source. Its paid C91, bounded-base and low-beta removals are complete label/normalized-layer projections, not a proper t- or kappa-deletion.

Consequently, if E(t,kappa) denotes any auxiliary zero-one deletion leaf appearing in a refinement of the fixed outer atom, its complementary siblings are present in the complete projection and
sum over all deletion siblings E_sib(t,kappa)=1                    (2)
pointwise on (1). There is no nonzero unrecombined physical deletion remainder in the complete projection.

Let F_{q,n} be the complete smooth one-variable physical amplitude after substituting
kappa(y)=(ell-qy)/n.                                              (3)
It includes both source logarithms and every smooth source, fixed-U and dyadic factor. Explicitly its core orientation-specific W factor is
W(gcq/D,y/M,gn/R,c kappa(y)/K)                                  (4F)
forward and
W(gn/D,c kappa(y)/M,gcq/R,y/K)                                  (4R)
reverse. Extend the complete product smoothly by zero off its compact positive source support. Every remaining high, parent, target-gcd and factorization predicate fixed above is an outer scalar. With Fourier convention
Fhat_{q,n}(xi)=integral_R F_{q,n}(y)e(-xi y)dy,                  (5)
one has exactly
sum_{t,kappa in Z: qt+n kappa=ell}F_{q,n}(t)
 =n^(-1)sum_{h in Z}Fhat_{q,n}(h/n)e_n(h ell qbar),              (6)
where qbar is the inverse of q modulo n. The same-mask zero mode is therefore
Z_{q,n}^{lit}=n^(-1)Fhat_{q,n}(0)
 =n^(-1)integral_R F_{q,n}(y)dy,                                (7)
and the complete nonzero-frequency row is exactly
sum_{h nonzero}n^(-1)Fhat_{q,n}(h/n)e_n(h ell qbar)
 =sum_{qt+n kappa=ell}F_{q,n}(t)-Z_{q,n}^{lit}.                  (8)
Every smooth t/kappa mask occurs on both terms through the same F_{q,n}; every fixed outer mask multiplies both terms. No arbitrary smooth alias is chosen.

For comparison only, if one deliberately projects to a proper deletion leaf E and does not restore its siblings, define
r_{q,E}=sum_{qt+n kappa=ell}(1-E(t,kappa))F_{q,n}(t).            (9)
Then the deleted physical row equals the complete physical row minus r_{q,E}. If the t-support of F_{q,n} is contained in an interval of length less than n, then
|r_{q,E}|<=sup_y|F_{q,n}(y)|,                                   (10)
because at most one integer t in that support satisfies qt congruent to ell modulo n. At fixed g,c and one dyadic/frozen outer block, absolute summation of this one-point bound over q in a set of at most C_q Q_c integers and n in a set of at most C_n B integers costs at most
C_q C_n Q_c B sup_{q,n,y}|F_{q,n}(y)|.                           (11)
This is the full elementary outer tax of that deliberately deleted block; it generally has no logarithmic saving. In the complete projection of (2), r_{q,E} is replaced by the sum over all complementary deletion siblings and cancels identically, so its actual outer tax is zero.

No Bombieri-Vinogradov estimate, primitive-character estimate, critical-tail payment or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
328503a935cabe60.proof:
Fact dde1e246a629bcc4 displays the selected source before the later anatomy projections:
sum_{dm+rk=N}mu(d)mu(r)log(m)log(k)W(dm/x)psi(d/D_*)
 Phi(d/D)Phi(m/M)Phi(rk/U)Phi(r/R)Phi(k/K).
Every factor depending on m or k in this formula is a logarithm or one of the specified smooth functions. Thus no independent zero-one E(m,k) occurs in the original source.

Fact 7ffe3d237362a451 constructs the post-low remainder by subtracting a complete C91 aggregate and complete bounded-base/low-beta label families. Its statement and proof say that no proper C91 deletion occurs and explicitly exclude an actual-(r,k) Z_mid deletion. These subtractions depend on complete labels and normalized scale layers, so fixing their surviving outer label does not impose a new t- or kappa-dependent selector.

Facts 32f645844f1ca9a1 and dde1e246a629bcc4 show how the word deletion enters the intermediate ledgers: it is one among auxiliary finite refinements, and every paid complete anatomy is formed after all such refinements are summed to completion; both facts explicitly say no arbitrary joint deletion is inserted. Their subtractions are supported below beta<=beta_1<6/5. Fact 3f2f255ea6845a50 likewise subtracts only the strict beta<6/5 A projection and states that beta>=6/5 is inherited unchanged. Fact a71f777ad842c886 proves pointwise recombination of every old marker leaf and marker-dependent descendant to mu(n), without changing the source. Therefore, on the complete beta>=6/5 critical projection, choosing no proper refinement leaf retains every complementary sibling. Since a finite zero-one partition sums pointwise to one, (2) follows. In particular the generic deletion coordinate retained in descriptive ledgers does not define an independent hard source mask on this complete projection.

Fact 8d9feea8c44da2c8 gives (1), the two orientation weights (4F)-(4R), both logarithms and gcd(q,n)=1. Substituting (3) in every smooth physical factor produces the single smooth compactly supported F_{q,n}. The fixed high, parent and factorization labels do not vary along the progression and factor out.

Because gcd(q,n)=1, t maps to the unique residue ell qbar modulo n on the solutions of (1). Poisson summation on this complete progression gives (6) with the stated Fourier convention. Separating h=0 proves (7)-(8). Equation (2) shows that no independent E remains to change the integral, so this is the same literal mask on the physical and zero terms, not a freely chosen extension.

For a deliberately retained proper leaf, partition the complete physical sum into E and 1-E, giving (9). If the support interval has length less than n, it contains at most one integer in the fixed residue class ell qbar modulo n; since 0<=1-E<=1, (10) follows. There are at most C_qQ_c choices of q and C_nB choices of n in the stated fixed dyadic block, so triangle inequality proves (11). Finally, summing E over the complementary siblings makes 1-E sum to zero pointwise, hence the complete-projection remainder and its tax vanish.

glossary.E_sib: One member of the complete finite family of complementary deletion siblings.
glossary.F_{q,n}: The complete smooth physical progression amplitude after substituting kappa=(ell-qy)/n.
glossary.Z_{q,n}^{lit}: The literal same-mask zero Poisson mode of the complete physical progression.
glossary.r_{q,E}: The exact physical remainder caused by deliberately retaining one proper deletion leaf.

3286b0e75a3ea94a.title: LITERAL SCALAR BOUNDED-VARIATION HEIGHT MAJORANT FOR EVERY TOP B,C1,C2,C3,C4 MARKER COPY
3286b0e75a3ea94a.author: slava chan
3286b0e75a3ea94a.statement:
LITERAL SCALAR BOUNDED-VARIATION HEIGHT MAJORANT FOR EVERY TOP B,C1,C2,C3,C4 MARKER COPY.

Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100 and beta_m=6/5-12sigma/5, and let Q be sufficiently large. Fix beta_m<beta<6/5 and one exact pre-marker top-sliver source atom and orientation from fact b0a38f5e9ae7feb6. Let n be its normalized marked integer, so B/2<=n<=2B. Put
M_+=M,quad M_-=K,
where M is used in the forward orientation and K in the reverse orientation. Thus
H_P=B/M_epsilon                                                     (1)
for the applicable orientation epsilon in {+1,-1}. Let
F^epsilon_{g,s,n}
be the exact one-variable smooth source amplitude in equations (3F)-(3R) of fact b0a38f5e9ae7feb6.

Apply the exact six-anatomy marker of fact e58fc7c00f1683e6, and fix one resulting B,C1,C2,C3, or C4 coefficient copy lambda. Let a_lambda(n) be its scalar marker coefficient. Then
|a_lambda(n)|<=1.                                                  (2)
After retaining any later zero-one or unit-modulus target-gcd, order, collision, deletion, orientation, source and provenance factors, the dimensionless literal Fourier coefficient c_lambda^epsilon(s,n,h) at every nonzero integer height h satisfies, for every fixed A>=2 and every epsilon_0>0,
|c_lambda^epsilon(s,n,h)|
 <=C_{A,epsilon_0} Q^epsilon_0
   (1+|h|/H_P)^(-A).                                              (3)
The constant is uniform in the displayed top-sliver source atom, marker anatomy, exact marker copy, and h.

Fix a signed dyadic height interval I_H equal either to
{h in Z:H<=h<2H}
or
{h in Z:-2H<h<=-H},
where H>=1. Put
w_{A,H}(h)=(1+|h|/H_P)^(-A) for h in I_H.                          (4)
Then w_{A,H} is nonnegative and
sup_{h in I_H}w_{A,H}(h)
 +Var_{I_H}(w_{A,H})
 <=2 sup_{h in I_H}w_{A,H}(h).                                   (5)
Consequently the literal scalar Poisson coefficient on every signed dyadic block has exactly the bounded-variation height shape required by the numerator-weight slot of fact 9ea2dddfbbbd191a, up to the harmless factor Q^epsilon_0. Taking absolute values of marker weights and dropping masks creates no height-l1 sum.

This theorem is scalar. It does not prove that a common-X completion exists, that a remaining-face vector norm is dominated by the same height profile, that the cofactor/source-copy factor is separated and bounded, or that the U_p/Y_p envelope is controlled by the target joint-completion Hilbert norm. It therefore does not by itself apply fact 9ea2dddfbbbd191a to a complete literal row.
3286b0e75a3ea94a.proof:
Fact b0a38f5e9ae7feb6 defines
F^+_{g,s,n}(t)
=log(t)log((L_src-st)/n)
 W(gs/D,t/M,gn/R,(L_src-st)/(nK))
in the forward orientation, and the same expression with the displayed swapped coordinates in the reverse orientation. The fixed source weight W is smooth with compact scaled support. On its support, the physical t-variable has length comparable to M_epsilon, every logarithm is bounded by a fixed power of log(2Q), and differentiating j times in t costs at most a constant times M_epsilon^(-j), apart from another fixed power of log(2Q). The smooth zero extension has no boundary term. Therefore repeated integration by parts gives, for every fixed A>=2,
|Fhat^epsilon_{g,s,n}(xi)|
 <=C_A M_epsilon (log(2Q))^{C_A}
   (1+|xi|M_epsilon)^(-A).                                      (6)
This argument uses only the fixed scaled derivative bounds of W and is uniform in the frozen source labels.

Insert xi=epsilon h/n and multiply (6) by H_P/n. By (1),
H_PM_epsilon/n=B/n,
and B/2<=n<=2B, so
1/2<=H_PM_epsilon/n<=2.                                         (7)
Also
|h|M_epsilon/n=(B/n)|h|/H_P,
which lies between (1/2)|h|/H_P and 2|h|/H_P.                    (8)
Equations (6)-(8), together with
(log(2Q))^{C_A}<=C_{A,epsilon_0}Q^epsilon_0
for sufficiently large Q, give
|(H_P/n)Fhat^epsilon_{g,s,n}(epsilon h/n)|
 <=C_{A,epsilon_0}Q^epsilon_0(1+|h|/H_P)^(-A).                 (9)
Every Archimedean reciprocity phase and every retained modular phase has modulus one, while every retained zero-one mask has modulus at most one.

It remains to prove (2). On a Cj copy, fact e58fc7c00f1683e6 gives the exact coefficient (-1)^jmu(v), which has modulus one on its squarefree support. On a B copy, the generalized stopping formula in that fact has, for one exact factorization n=uy and one stopping length k,
a_lambda(n)=(-1)^k mu(u)1_{j_(L,Z)(u)=0}
 Gamma_{k;L,S_0}(y)/binom(k+omega_L(u),k).
The definition of Gamma in fact 7c1f38cfbb8d0569 is a probability weight, so 0<=Gamma<=1, and the binomial coefficient is at least one. Hence |a_lambda(n)|<=1. Multiplying (9) by a_lambda and by the retained unit or zero-one factors proves (3).

On the positive signed interval, w_{A,H} is nonincreasing. On the negative signed interval it is nondecreasing as h increases. For any nonnegative monotone sequence, its discrete total variation is the absolute difference of its endpoint values and is at most its supremum. Therefore
Var_{I_H}(w_{A,H})<=sup_{I_H}w_{A,H},
which proves (5). The final scope paragraph records the difference between this scalar modulus estimate and the unproved vector/source-envelope hypotheses.

glossary.M_epsilon: The physical one-variable source length M in the forward orientation and K in the reverse orientation.
glossary.a_lambda(n): The exact scalar coefficient of one B or Cj marker copy over the normalized marked integer n.
glossary.c_lambda^epsilon(s,n,h): The dimensionless literal scalar Fourier coefficient of one exact marker copy after retained unit and zero-one factors.
glossary.w_{A,H}: The nonnegative Fourier-decay height majorant on one signed dyadic interval.

32f645844f1ca9a1.title: QUANTITATIVE SELECTED FIXED-BAD-N POST-A,B,C1,C2 REMAINDER AND EXACT C3 FIRST-BUFFER LEDGER
32f645844f1ca9a1.author: slava chan
32f645844f1ca9a1.statement:
QUANTITATIVE SELECTED FIXED-BAD-N POST-A,B,C1,C2 REMAINDER AND EXACT C3 FIRST-BUFFER LEDGER.

Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, beta_0=6/5-2kappa, beta_1=6/5-3sigma, kappa_0=1/200, and fix 0<eta<sigma. Let x be sufficiently large and let N=2x be one of the selected bad even integers in the fixed-bad-N source construction, with singular factor c(N)>=C_2>0.

Work with the literal paired nonzero-Poisson selected source atoms and exact normalization d=ga, r=gb, g=gcd(d,r) dividing N. In the forward orientation use
R>D, c_1x<=DM<=C_1x,
c_Dx^(1/2)(log x)^(-A_D)<=D<=C_Dx^(1/2),
R>x^(9/16-kappa_0),
Q=D/g, B=R/g=Q^beta, G=M/Q, H_T=B/Q, H_P=B/M, L_src=N/g.
In the reverse orientation use
D>R, c_1x<=RK<=C_1x,
c_Rx^(1/2)(log x)^(-A_R)<=R<=C_Rx^(1/2),
D>x^(9/16-kappa_0),
Q=R/g, B=D/g=Q^beta, G=K/Q, H_T=B/Q, H_P=B/K, L_src=N/g.
All displayed c_i,C_i,C_2 are fixed positive constants, A_D,A_R are fixed nonnegative constants, and all physical scales are at most Cx.

Let R_postABC1,sel be the finite real selected same-bad-N aggregate supplied by fact 3edf35eeb12b56e8 after the complete A, B and C1 first-buffer coordinates have been subtracted. Thus
R_postABC1,sel<=-c_dir c(N)x/log x+o(c(N)x/log x)                     (1)
for fixed c_dir>0, and every atom in this remainder with
beta_0<beta<=beta_1                                                    (2)
has frozen parent U_low and normalized anatomy in the exact disjoint list C2,C3. All selected source, fixed-U, high, smooth/projective, Fourier, target-gcd, rough-prime ordering, equal-cell, collision, deletion, orientation, parent, provenance and exact outer-gcd coordinates are retained.

Let R_C2,U_low be the complete aggregate of all atoms of R_postABC1,sel satisfying (2) and having normalized anatomy C2, with both rough-prime orderings and every auxiliary target-gcd, equal-cell, outer-gcd/rough-prime collision, repeated-prime-diagonal bookkeeping, Fourier, deletion and provenance refinement summed to completion. Define
R_postABC2,sel=R_postABC1,sel-R_C2,U_low.                             (3)

Then there is a fixed delta_C2>0 such that
|R_C2,U_low|<<x^(1-delta_C2),                                       (4)
and
R_postABC2,sel<=-c_dir c(N)x/log x+o(c(N)x/log x).                   (5)
Within (2), the exact remaining parent/anatomy ledger is
U_low times {C3}.                                                     (6)

Thus C3 is the sole remaining first-buffer standard anatomy coordinate. The theorem does not assert that the fixed selected bad N has a C3 atom in every right-neighborhood of beta_0, does not identify the first actually nonempty selected cell, and does not assert that an individual C3 cell is negative.

No arbitrary joint deletion mask is inserted. No C3 estimate, moving actual-Z selector, endpoint, terminal selection, diagonal C2 selection, DCE, PMD, logical Goldbach implication, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
32f645844f1ca9a1.proof:
Fact 3edf35eeb12b56e8 establishes the explicitly stated selected same-bad-N bound (1), the lower bound c(N)>=C_2, and the exact first-buffer selected ledger
U_low times {C2,C3}.                                                  (7)

Fact 5051635f817e7a22 proves a fixed power saving for the complete literal C2 aggregate throughout the same parameter range (2), in both orientations, for every actual G and every exact outer gcd. Its proof applies the accepted local trace fact 989b464fc741150b separately with each frozen source, parent, fixed-U, high and provenance label acting as a label scalar. It recombines both rough-prime orderings and every target-gcd, equal-cell, collision, deletion and provenance refinement before analytic estimation, and it includes the repeated-prime symmetrization bookkeeping.

The definition of R_C2,U_low satisfies exactly these conditions: it fixes only the retained selected-source, fixed-U and U_low-parent labels and sums every auxiliary C2 refinement to completion. Therefore fact 5051635f817e7a22 applies and proves (4). This is not an application of a reciprocal estimate to an arbitrary hard deletion.

Since c(N)>=C_2>0,
x^(1-delta_C2)=o(c(N)x/log x).                                       (8)
Use the exact real identity (3), the upper bound (1), the absolute bound (4), and (8) to obtain (5). Since C2 and C3 are disjoint exhaustive normalized anatomy coordinates in (7), removing the complete C2 coordinate leaves exactly C3 and does not change the sole parent U_low. This proves (6).

The final scope statement follows because (7) is an exhaustive list conditional on atom membership, not a support theorem forcing a prescribed cell to be nonempty for the already fixed bad N. Neither fact 3edf35eeb12b56e8 nor fact 5051635f817e7a22 supplies such a fixed-N support assertion. Hence C3 is the sole remaining coordinate in the buffer, while actual cell nonemptiness and individual negativity remain unproved.

glossary.R_C2,U_low: The complete selected U_low-parent C2 aggregate in the first post-low-beta buffer.
glossary.R_postABC2,sel: The same-bad-N selected remainder after subtracting the accepted A, B, C1 and complete C2 first-buffer aggregates.
glossary.delta_C2: The fixed power-saving exponent for the selected complete C2 buffer.

3330e83b6d253b69.title: EXACT NONRESONANT FIXED-ACTIVE-PRODUCT COMPLETION AND THE LITERAL WEIGHTED-TENSOR-GRAM INTERFACE
3330e83b6d253b69.author: slava chan
3330e83b6d253b69.statement:
EXACT NONRESONANT FIXED-ACTIVE-PRODUCT COMPLETION AND THE LITERAL WEIGHTED-TENSOR-GRAM INTERFACE.

Fix one same-target literal C4 layer of fact 9bee61f3627bd506 on a signed natural frequency interval of fact 67d49768ecdc058e. A row j has
n_j=d_jv_j,
where d_j is the product of the four distinct rough C4 primes, gcd(d_j,v_j)=1, p>=Z for every p|d_j, and 0<|h_j|<Z for sufficiently large Q. Let A be the common nonzero signed reduced target and put
d_j^x=d_j/gcd(d_j,A).                                               (1)
Let r be a nonempty squarefree divisor of d_j^x and put
a_{j,r}=d_j^x/r.                                                     (2)
Then gcd(Ah_j,r)=1.

For p|r define
g_{p,j}(x)=1_{x!=0}e_p(Ah_j(n_j/p)^{-1}x^{-1})
and let ghat_{p,j} be its normalized additive Fourier transform. Put
Omega_r=product_{p|r}F_p^*,
V_{j,r}(rho)=product_{p|r}ghat_{p,j}(rho_p),
chi_rho(q)=product_{p|r}e_p(rho_p q).                                (3)
With phi_{p,j}(x)=g_{p,j}(x)+1/p, one has
p^{-1}sum_{x mod p}g_{p,j}(x)=-1/p,
so phi_{p,j} has zero Fourier mode zero. Consequently the all-active centered r-face is exactly
Phi_{j,r}^{act}(q)
 =sum_{rho in Omega_r}V_{j,r}(rho)chi_rho(q).                        (4)

Let C_epsilon(c,q,n_j,v_j,h_j) be the exact coefficient from fact 9bee61f3627bd506 and define
D_j^0(q)=C_epsilon(c,q,n_j,v_j,h_j)e(-Ah_j/(qn_j)),                  (5)
D_{j,r}(q)=D_j^0(q)
 e_{v_j}(Ah_j(qd_j)^{-1}) mu(a_{j,r})/a_{j,r}.                      (6)
Thus D_j^0 retains mu(c)mu(q)mu(v_j), the dimensionless physical Fourier amplitude and every literal target-gcd, source, orientation, frequency, deletion and provenance mask, but not a second copy of the Archimedean factor. The coefficient D_{j,r} additionally retains the exact small-v_j CRT phase and all inactive nonresonant rough-prime factors. Rough primes dividing gcd(d_j,A) have constant local phase one and contribute neither to r nor to a_{j,r}.

Put
W_{j,r}(rho)=sum_qD_{j,r}(q)chi_rho(q).                              (7)
Then the exact literal contribution of the nonempty r-face in row j, apart from the common external factor H_P^{-1}, is
sum_qD_{j,r}(q)Phi_{j,r}^{act}(q)
 =sum_{rho in Omega_r}V_{j,r}(rho)W_{j,r}(rho).                     (8)

For rows j,k sharing the same nonresonant active product r and satisfying the displayed hypotheses, the coordinatewise weighted vector Gram is exactly
G_r^W(j,k)=sum_{rho in Omega_r}
 W_{j,r}(rho)conjugate(W_{k,r}(rho))
 V_{j,r}(rho)conjugate(V_{k,r}(rho)).                               (9)
If W_{j,r}(rho)=b_j is independent of rho for each j, then
G_r^W(j,k)=b_jconjugate(b_k)G_r(n_j,h_j;n_k,h_k),                    (10)
and all hypotheses of facts df97bf1eba0495be and d9a096ed4e597b2b hold, so their fixed-r square-divisor Schur/Bessel bound applies. For general mode-dependent W_{j,r}, equation (10) is false, and fact 7b88f3f21d0836c8 proves that arbitrary dual-frequency modulations do not preserve the bare off-slope reciprocal Gram.

Therefore the first unproved fixed-r vector input is a source-specific estimate for (9) with the exact W_{j,r} of (6)-(7); call it C4-WTG_r. Across distinct nonresonant active products, all local phase parameters are nonzero, so fact 3fde81ce051bff7b makes the unweighted complete-lcm face Gram zero. Hence the varying-r continuation is the incomplete/source-weighted cross-product discrepancy formed with the r-dependent coefficients D_{j,r}, including their inactive-prime factors and small-v_j phases.

Equations (1)-(10) are exact identities and a scoped reduction. No C4-WTG_r estimate, varying-r estimate, C4-VEC, C4 moment, other-anatomy estimate, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
3330e83b6d253b69.proof:
Fact 9bee61f3627bd506 gives the exact summand
H_P^{-1}C_epsilon(c,q,n_j,v_j,h_j)e_q(-Ah_j n_j^{-1})
and states that C_epsilon contains e(Ah_j/(qn_j)). Its reconstruction identity gives
e(Ah_j/(qn_j))e_q(-Ah_jn_j^{-1})
 =e_{n_j}(Ah_jq^{-1}).                                             (11)
Definition (5) therefore rewrites the summand exactly as
H_P^{-1}D_j^0(q)e_{n_j}(Ah_jq^{-1}),                               (12)
with the Archimedean factor consumed once.

Since n_j=d_jv_j and gcd(d_j,v_j)=1, CRT gives
e_{n_j}(Ah_jq^{-1})
 =e_{d_j}(Ah_j(qv_j)^{-1})
  e_{v_j}(Ah_j(qd_j)^{-1}).                                        (13)
The second factor is retained in (6). For p|d_j, the p-local factor of the first term in (13) is
e_p(Ah_j(n_j/p)^{-1}q^{-1}).                                       (14)
If p|gcd(d_j,A), this factor is identically one. Such p is removed in d_j^x and supplies no centered coordinate. If p|d_j^x, then p does not divide A. Fact 67d49768ecdc058e gives p>=Z and |h_j|<Z on the natural block for sufficiently large Q, so p does not divide h_j. Hence the parameter Ah_j(n_j/p)^{-1} is nonzero modulo p.

For such a nonresonant p, inversion permutes F_p^*, and therefore
p^{-1}sum_xg_{p,j}(x)
 =p^{-1}sum_{y in F_p^*}e_p(Ah_j(n_j/p)^{-1}y)
 =-1/p.                                                            (15)
Thus phi_{p,j}=g_{p,j}+1/p has zero complete mean and
g_{p,j}(q)=-1/p+phi_{p,j}(q).                                      (16)
Expand (16) over all primes of d_j^x. The face active exactly at r has inactive coefficient
product_{p|a_{j,r}}(-1/p)=mu(a_{j,r})/a_{j,r},                      (17)
while primes dividing gcd(d_j,A) retain the factor one. Equations (12)-(17) prove that the coefficient of the active function product_{p|r}phi_{p,j}(q) is exactly D_{j,r}(q) in (6).

Normalized Fourier inversion and the zero mean from (15) give
phi_{p,j}(x)
 =sum_{rho_p in F_p^*}ghat_{p,j}(rho_p)e_p(rho_p x).                (18)
Multiply (18) over p|r to prove (4). Multiplying by D_{j,r}(q), summing q, and interchanging finite sums proves (7)-(8).

Expanding the coordinatewise inner product of the vectors
(W_{j,r}(rho)V_{j,r}(rho)) gives (9). Under the scalar hypothesis, the b_j factors leave the rho-sum, whose remainder is exactly the tensor Gram in fact df97bf1eba0495be. For two compared rows, the common hypotheses give gcd(Ah_jh_k,r)=1, r divides gcd(n_j,n_k), and squarefreeness gives gcd(r,n_j/r)=gcd(r,n_k/r)=1. Thus df97 applies, and fact d9a096ed4e597b2b supplies the scalar Schur/Bessel consequence. Fact 7b88f3f21d0836c8 proves the failure of an arbitrary mode-dependent lift.

Finally, for every active product used here each local parameter is nonzero by (1) and the natural-frequency argument above. Therefore fact 3fde81ce051bff7b applies to distinct active products and gives zero unweighted complete-lcm Gram. Inserting (6)-(7) is exactly the remaining incomplete/source-weighted discrepancy. This proves every identity and scope assertion.

glossary.C4-WTG_r: The unproved source-specific bound for G_r^W.
glossary.D_j^0: The literal coefficient after the Archimedean reciprocity factor has been consumed.
glossary.D_{j,r}: The exact r-face coefficient including the small-v_j CRT phase and inactive nonresonant rough-prime factor.
glossary.Omega_r: The Cartesian product of nonzero additive dual coordinates at the primes dividing r.
glossary.V_{j,r}: The standard all-active tensor Kloosterman Fourier vector of row j.
glossary.W_{j,r}: The active-modulus Fourier transform of D_{j,r}.
glossary.a_{j,r}: The inactive nonresonant rough-prime product d_j^x/r.
glossary.chi_rho: The CRT product additive character associated with rho.

3405d0cb4853555f.title: MAYNARD/RAMARE SUPPORT NO-EXHAUSTION. Assume all scale hypotheses (1)-(3) of fact 53e70bf4e327e6bd:
3405d0cb4853555f.author: slava chan
3405d0cb4853555f.statement:
MAYNARD/RAMARE SUPPORT NO-EXHAUSTION. Assume all scale hypotheses (1)-(3) of fact 53e70bf4e327e6bd:
Q_1R_1=B^(1/2+delta),
R_1<=B^(1/10-3delta)(log B)^(-C),
P>=Q_1B^(2delta)(log B)^C.                                      (1)
Then necessarily
Q_1>=B^(2/5+4delta)(log B)^C,
P>=B^(2/5+6delta)(log B)^(2C).                                  (2)
In particular, when delta>=0 and B is sufficiently large, no prime below B^(2/5) belongs to the selected interval
cal P={p prime:P<=p<2P}.                                         (3)
Thus the existence of a factor in the range
B^(1/4+eta)<r<B^(2/5)                                            (4)
(for any eta for which this interval is nonempty), or of an arbitrary smaller HC factor d<B^eta, does not by itself put an integer into the sector paid by fact 53e70bf4e327e6bd. That fact requires an independently marked prime p in cal P and all its other factorable-modulus, projective, and Siegel-Walfisz hypotheses.

More sharply, every squarefree n in [B,2B) satisfying
p|n implies p notin cal P                                       (5)
has omega_P(n)=0 and is absent from D_d^{med} of fact 512ccc143b3d5fd9. This includes, whenever such an integer occurs in the ambient support, a prime n with n>2P, and a product n=p_1p_2p_3 of three distinct primes each smaller than P; in particular the latter condition holds for p_i asymptotic to B^(1/3) under (2) when delta>=0 and B is large.

The squareful correction E_d in fact 512ccc143b3d5fd9 does not cover any omega_P(n)=0 term: every summand defining E_d still contains an explicitly selected p in cal P and has n=pm. Therefore D_d^{med}=T_d+E_d is an identity and estimate only for the marked sector omega_P(n)>0. This is a support no-exhaustion statement. It does not assert that any literal critical-source amplitude or mask is nonzero on the displayed residual examples, and it does not disprove the possibility that a different theorem pays them.
3405d0cb4853555f.proof:
From the first two relations in (1), Q_1=B^(1/2+delta)/R_1 >=B^(1/2+delta-(1/10-3delta))(log B)^C =B^(2/5+4delta)(log B)^C. Multiplying this inequality by the lower factor B^(2delta)(log B)^C in the third relation of (1) gives the second inequality in (2). If delta>=0, then P/B^(2/5)>=B^(6delta)(log B)^(2C), which exceeds one for all sufficiently large B. Hence every prime below B^(2/5) is smaller than P and cannot lie in cal P, proving (3). The range (4) is entirely below P, so merely exhibiting such a factor cannot exhibit the marked prime required by fact 53e70bf4e327e6bd. Likewise, that theorem has no hypothesis or conclusion saying that an arbitrary HC factor d0. This proves the stated scope distinction. By definition in fact 512ccc143b3d5fd9, omega_P(n)=#{p in cal P:p divides n}, and D_d^{med} contains the indicator 1_{omega_P(n)>0}. Condition (5) therefore gives omega_P(n)=0 and deletes n from D_d^{med}. If n is prime and n>2P, its only prime divisor is outside [P,2P), so (5) holds. If n=p_1p_2p_3 is squarefree and every p_i1/3 imply K_0B^(1/3)

=0. Finally, the exact definition of E_d in fact 512ccc143b3d5fd9 is a sum over p in cal P and m with p|m, evaluated at n=pm. Thus each of its summands contains a cal-P prime divisor p of n and has omega_P(n)>0. It has empty intersection with (5). The identity D_d^{med}=T_d+E_d was obtained by adding and subtracting the p|m part of the same marked Ramaré row; it does not add the complementary indicator omega_P(n)=0. This proves the no-exhaustion and the final scope statements.

glossary.support no-exhaustion: The assertion that the marked sector of a decomposition does not cover every arithmetic support type of the ambient source.

3450c52083a2e548.title: COMMON-ENVELOPE POINTWISE SOFT-SOURCE OCCUPANCY
3450c52083a2e548.author: slava chan
3450c52083a2e548.statement:
COMMON-ENVELOPE POINTWISE SOFT-SOURCE OCCUPANCY.

Fix Q>=2 and real numbers H,V,P satisfying
  2<=H<=Q^(1/3),  2<=V<H,  P=QH/V.                          (1)
Let v be an integer in [V,2V), let p be a prime in [P,2P), assume gcd(v,p)=1, and put
  n=vp,  Y=n/H.                                               (2)
Let A be an integer with gcd(A,n)=1. Let cal Q be any subset of one integer interval of length at most Q, and assume gcd(q,n)=1 for every q in cal Q.

Let Phi be a fixed smooth compactly supported complex function on the real line whose support does not contain zero. Define
