  psi_Y(x)=Y^(-1)Phicheck(x/Y),                              (3)
where Phicheck is the inverse Fourier transform with convention
  Phicheck(x)=integral_R Phi(xi)exp(2 pi i x xi)dxi.
Let J be one real interval of length at most C_0Y, where C_0>=1 is fixed. For every q in cal Q let F_q be smooth, compactly supported inside J, and satisfy
  |F_q(x)|<=B                                                (4)
for all real x, where B>=1. Put
  G_q=F_q*psi_Y.                                             (5)
For t modulo p define
  z_t(q)=sum_{m in Z;qm congruent A modulo n}G_q(m+vt),
  Z_t=sum_{q in cal Q}|z_t(q)|.                              (6)

Then, for every epsilon>0,
  Z_t<<_{Phi,C_0,epsilon} BQ^epsilon[Q/H+n^(1/2)]            (7)
uniformly in t. Under (1)-(2),
  n<=4QH
and H^3<=Q, so
  n^(1/2)<=2Q/H.                                             (8)
Consequently
  Z_t<<_{Phi,C_0,epsilon} BQ^(1+epsilon)/H                  (9)
for every t modulo p.

This improves the twist-average mass bound in fact 84bf915e8a88d8d3 to a pointwise bound under the additional common-envelope hypothesis supp(F_q) subset J for all q. It is stable under arbitrary deletion of q-values and arbitrary q-dependent amplitudes inside the same envelope. It does not estimate the vector fourth moment or the all-nonzero OSC cross Gram by itself, and it makes no PMD or Goldbach conclusion.
3450c52083a2e548.proof:
The inverse Fourier transform of the fixed smooth compactly supported Phi is Schwartz. Exactly as in fact 84bf915e8a88d8d3, for every integer M>=3 there is a constant C_M depending only on Phi,C_0,M such that
  |G_q(x)|<=C_MB(1+dist(x,J)/Y)^(-M)                        (10)
for every q and real x. The key extra fact is that the same interval J occurs for every q.

Define real sets
  K_0={x:dist(x,J)<Y},
and, for integers s>=1,
  K_s={x:2^(s-1)Y<=dist(x,J)<2^sY}.                         (11)
Each K_s is a union of at most two ordinary intervals and has total length at most
  C_2 2^sY,                                                  (12)
where C_2 depends only on C_0. By (10),
  |G_q(x)|<=C_3B2^(-Ms)                                     (13)
for x in K_s, with a changed constant C_3.

For fixed t and s, let N_s be the number of pairs (q,m) with q in cal Q,
  qm congruent A modulo n,
  m+vt in K_s.                                               (14)
Enlarge cal Q to its containing interval of length at most Q. Translate every component of K_s by -vt. Then N_s is bounded by the number of modular-hyperbola pairs
  qx congruent A modulo n                                   (15)
with q in one interval of length at most Q and x in at most two ordinary intervals of total length at most C_2 2^sY.

Partition each x-interval into ordinary subintervals of length at most n. The number of pieces is at most
  C_4(1+2^sY/n)=C_4(1+2^s/H).                               (16)
Fact d43944f35c05a407 applies to each pair of the q-interval and one x-piece because gcd(A,n)=1, Q<=n, and both lengths are at most n. Summing its bound over the pieces gives
  N_s<<_epsilon n^epsilon[
       2^sQY/n+(1+2^s/H)n^(1/2)]
     =n^epsilon[
       2^sQ/H+(1+2^s/H)n^(1/2)].                            (17)
All interval-wrap multiplicities are absorbed in the implied constant.

By (6), the triangle inequality, and the partition (11),
  Z_t
  <=sum_{q in cal Q}sum_{m;qm congruent A mod n}|G_q(m+vt)|
  <=C_3Bsum_{s>=0}2^(-Ms)N_s.                               (18)
Insert (17). Since M>=3,
  sum_{s>=0}2^{-(M-1)s}<infinity
and
  sum_{s>=0}2^{-Ms}<infinity.
Therefore
  Z_t<<_{Phi,C_0,epsilon}
   Bn^epsilon[Q/H+n^(1/2)+n^(1/2)/H].                       (19)
The last term is absorbed by n^(1/2). From (1)-(2),
  n=vp<4VP=4QH,                                             (20)
and n is bounded by a fixed power of Q. Absorb n^epsilon into Q^epsilon after renaming epsilon. This proves (7).

Finally, H<=Q^(1/3) gives H^3<=Q. Hence
  (2Q/H)^2=4Q^2/H^2>=4QH>=n,
which proves (8). Substitute (8) in (7) to prove (9). The comparison with fact 84bf915e8a88d8d3 is exact: that fact permits a different support interval J_q for each q and obtains only twist-average mass, whereas the present proof used the common interval J in (14)-(17). No fourth-moment estimate has been applied, proving the scope statements.

glossary.J: The single common physical support interval containing every F_q.
glossary.K_s: The s-th dyadic distance shell around the common interval J.
glossary.N_s: The number of source pairs falling in the s-th translated common-envelope shell.

34d306bcb630f9df.title: GENERAL PRIMITIVE-RAY PHASE, GATE, AND SCOPED 2+2 PRIMITIVE-SIBLING KERNEL FOR A LITERAL C4 ROW. Let D=p_1p_2p_3p_4 be a product of four distinct odd primes, let v be a positive squarefree integer with gcd(D,v)=1, put n=Dv, and let A be a nonzero integer. Let q>0 and h!=0 satisfy gcd(q,Dv)=1 and gcd(Ah,D)=1. Write uniquely
34d306bcb630f9df.author: slava chan
34d306bcb630f9df.statement:
GENERAL PRIMITIVE-RAY PHASE, GATE, AND SCOPED 2+2 PRIMITIVE-SIBLING KERNEL FOR A LITERAL C4 ROW. Let D=p_1p_2p_3p_4 be a product of four distinct odd primes, let v be a positive squarefree integer with gcd(D,v)=1, put n=Dv, and let A be a nonzero integer. Let q>0 and h!=0 satisfy gcd(q,Dv)=1 and gcd(Ah,D)=1. Write uniquely
q=kappa a,  h=epsilon kappa b,  kappa=gcd(q,|h|),
epsilon in {+1,-1},  a,b>0,  gcd(a,b)=1.                            (1)
Then the rough-D and small-v CRT phases in fact 41b56ed8e64bdba6 reduce exactly to
e_D(Ah(qv)^{-1})=e_D(A epsilon b(av)^{-1}),                         (2)
e_v(Ah(qD)^{-1})=e_v(A epsilon b(aD)^{-1}).                         (3)
They are independent of the ray scale kappa. The literal squarefree and unit gate remains
mu(q)^2 1_{gcd(q,Dv)=1}
=mu(kappa a)^2 1_{gcd(kappa a,Dv)=1};                              (4)
it is not replaced by separate unrestricted gates in kappa and a.

For p dividing D define the exact prime-local ray phase
zeta_p(epsilon,a,b)
=e_p(A epsilon b [a(n/p)]^{-1}).                                   (5)
For every such p, let delta_x be the point mass at x=(n/p)^{-1} modulo p and let P_{p,p} be projection onto primitive characters modulo p, namely the nonprincipal characters. Then the exact Gauss/totient-normalized active-prime factor is
Gamma_p(epsilon,a,b)
=sum_{y in G_p}(P_{p,p}delta_x)(y)e_p(A epsilon b a^{-1}y)
=1/(p-1) sum_{chi modulo p; chi nonprincipal}
 overline{chi(A epsilon b a^{-1}x)} tau_p(chi)
=zeta_p(epsilon,a,b)+1/(p-1),                                     (6)
where tau_p(chi)=sum_{y in G_p}chi(y)e_p(y). There is no omitted square-root or phi(p) factor.

Define the scoped 2+2 primitive-sibling kernel by summing exactly the six active semiprime faces:
K_{2,D,v}(epsilon,a,b)
=sum_{S subset {p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4}; |S|=2}
 product_{p in S}Gamma_p(epsilon,a,b)
 product_{p in {p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4} minus S}(-1/p).                    (7)
Then (7) is exactly the rowwise sum of the primitive-conductor parts of those six centered faces: active primes carry all Gauss and totient normalizations through (6), and inactive primes carry the literal centered-face coefficient -1/p. Including the small-v phase gives the full scale-independent ray kernel
K_{2,D,v}^{full}(epsilon,a,b)
=e_v(A epsilon b(aD)^{-1})K_{2,D,v}(epsilon,a,b).                   (8)

Accordingly, for any literal coefficient c_lambda(q,h) and any retained zero-one or signed masks M_lambda(q,h), the contribution of this scoped six-face family on one primitive ray is exactly
sum_{kappa>=1}
 c_lambda(kappa a,epsilon kappa b)
 M_lambda(kappa a,epsilon kappa b)
 mu(kappa a)^2 1_{gcd(kappa a,Dv)=1}
 K_{2,D,v}^{full}(epsilon,a,b),                                    (9)
with the sum restricted to the original q,h support. Thus amplitudes, masks, heights, squarefreeness and all unit gates remain in the kappa-sum; only the two CRT phases and the primitive rough sibling kernel are scale-independent.

Two primitive rays (epsilon,a,b) and (epsilon',a',b') contribute a Delta=0 ordered pair in the TT-star determinant Delta=hq'-h'q exactly when
(epsilon,a,b)=(epsilon',a',b').                                   (10)
Hence their same-ray squares are contained in the already paid Delta=0 sector of fact 54029717e980dcb7. The b=1 family is only the primitive-frequency-one slice. On a block F<=|h|<2F and Q<=q<2Q, its scale kappa satisfies kappa comparable to F and its a-variable has interval length O(Q/F); this is not a statement about all primitive rays. Equations (1)-(10) give no estimate for cross terms between distinct primitive rays, no fully resonant subtraction beyond the cited paid sector, no varying-lambda/common-row bound, no full centered-face recombination, no C4 estimate, and no Goldbach conclusion.
34d306bcb630f9df.proof:
The representation (1) is the standard reduction of the positive pair (q,|h|) by their greatest common divisor, with epsilon the sign of h. It is unique and gives gcd(a,b)=1.

The two CRT phases before rough-face centering are equations (4)-(5) of fact 41b56ed8e64bdba6:
e_D(Ah(qv)^{-1}),  e_v(Ah(qD)^{-1}).                               (11)
The gate gcd(q,Dv)=1 makes kappa a a unit modulo both D and v, so kappa is a unit modulo both. Substitute q=kappa a and h=epsilon kappa b in (11), then cancel kappa in each displayed modulus. This proves (2)-(3). Substitution in the unchanged source gate proves (4); no multiplicative separation of mu(kappa a)^2 is made.

CRT factorization of (2) at p|D gives
e_p(A epsilon b(av)^{-1}(D/p)^{-1})
=e_p(A epsilon b[a v(D/p)]^{-1})
=e_p(A epsilon b[a(n/p)]^{-1}),
which is (5).

We prove (6) with all normalizations. On G_p, multiplicative Fourier inversion gives
P_{p,p}delta_x(y)
=1/(p-1) sum_{chi nonprincipal}overline{chi(x)}chi(y).              (12)
Multiply by e_p(A epsilon b a^{-1}y) and sum over y. Since Aepsilon b a^{-1} is a unit modulo p by the hypotheses, the Gauss identity gives
sum_{y in G_p}chi(y)e_p(A epsilon b a^{-1}y)
=overline{chi(A epsilon b a^{-1})}tau_p(chi).                       (13)
Equations (12)-(13) give the middle expression of (6). Alternatively,
P_{p,p}delta_x=delta_x-(p-1)^{-1}1_{G_p}.                           (14)
The additive phase at x is zeta_p by (5), while the sum of the nontrivial additive character over G_p is -1. Substitution in (14) yields
zeta_p-(-1)/(p-1)=zeta_p+1/(p-1),
proving the last equality of (6).

For a semiprime r formed from S, the primitive-character projector modulo r is the tensor product over p in S of the nonprincipal projectors P_{p,p}, because r is squarefree and a character modulo r is primitive exactly when each prime-local character is nonprincipal. CRT therefore makes its projected additive evaluation the product of Gamma_p over p in S. Fact 3330e83b6d253b69 gives the inactive centered coefficient
mu(D/r)/(D/r)=product_{p|D/r}(-1/p).                                (15)
Summing (15) times the primitive evaluation over the six subsets |S|=2 proves (7). Multiplication by the exact small-v phase (3) proves (8). Since every other source amplitude and mask is scalar at the physical pair (q,h), substituting (1), (4), and (8) gives (9) without deleting any coefficient.

For two primitive-ray representations, direct substitution gives
Delta
=kappa kappa'[epsilon b a'-epsilon' b'a].                          (16)
If the primitive triples agree, this is zero. Conversely, if it is zero, positivity of a,a',b,b' forces epsilon=epsilon'. Then ba'=b'a. The coprimalities gcd(a,b)=gcd(a',b')=1 imply a=a' and b=b'. This proves (10). Fact 54029717e980dcb7 pays every Delta=0 pair absolutely, so all same-ray squares are in that sector.

Finally, on b=1 one has |h|=kappa. The h block gives F<=kappa<2F, while q=kappa a in [Q,2Q) places a in an interval contained in [Q/(2F),2Q/F), of cardinality O(Q/F). This proves the scoped length statement and all exclusions.

glossary.Gamma_p: the exact Gauss/totient-normalized primitive active-prime ray factor
glossary.K_{2,D,v}: the scoped sum of the six primitive active-semiprime centered-face siblings
glossary.K_{2,D,v}^{full}: the scoped six-face kernel including the exact small-v ray phase
glossary.primitive ray: the unique triple (epsilon,a,b) with q=kappa a, h=epsilon kappa b and gcd(a,b)=1

3566675481b2284a.title: DISCRETE BOUNDED-VARIATION COPRIME MOBIUS CANCELLATION AND THE EXACT CONSTANT-EFFECTIVE-PHASE LIMITATION. Fix real constants C_0>0 and eta_0>0. Let x>=3, let X>=x^(eta_0), and let c be a positive integer with c<=x^(C_0). Let W be a complex function on the integers, extended by zero and supported on X<=q<2X. Define V_X(W)=sup_q|W(q)|+sum_q|W(q+1)-W(q)|. Then, for every A_0>0,
3566675481b2284a.author: slava chan
3566675481b2284a.statement:
DISCRETE BOUNDED-VARIATION COPRIME MOBIUS CANCELLATION AND THE EXACT CONSTANT-EFFECTIVE-PHASE LIMITATION. Fix real constants C_0>0 and eta_0>0. Let x>=3, let X>=x^(eta_0), and let c be a positive integer with c<=x^(C_0). Let W be a complex function on the integers, extended by zero and supported on X<=q<2X. Define V_X(W)=sup_q|W(q)|+sum_q|W(q+1)-W(q)|. Then, for every A_0>0,
|sum_{q;(q,c)=1}mu(q)W(q)| <<_{A_0,C_0,eta_0} V_X(W)X(log x)^(-A_0).                            (1)
In the literal C1 row of fact 79ffbcb2ffe4049f, put C=mathscr A h and m_eff=n/gcd(C,n). If m_eff=1, then e_n(Cq^(-1))=1 for every supported q. Hence (1) applies to each separated literal mode with its complete remaining q-weight, and the sum of those mode bounds is at most
Q(log x)^(-A_0) times the exact sum of their coefficient absolute values multiplied by their V_Q variation norms.                         (2)
Equation (2) is an arbitrary-logarithmic estimate with the variation-weighted mode mass retained. If that mass is only known to be Q^(o(1)), (2) does not yield Q^(1-delta) for any fixed delta>0. Thus the constant effective-phase chamber is not a fixed-power consequence of classical coprime Mobius cancellation alone.
3566675481b2284a.proof:
Put f_c(q)=mu(q)1_{gcd(q,c)=1}. We first prove a uniform estimate for its partial sums. The proof of fact 71389b22e6f49e13 defines nonnegative coefficients a_c(r) by
sum_r a_c(r)r^(-s)=product_{ell|c}(1-ell^(-s))^(-1)
and proves f_c=mu*a_c. It also proves, uniformly for c<=x^(C_0),
sum_r a_c(r)r^(-1)=x^(o(1)),  sum_r a_c(r)r^(-3/4)=x^(o(1)).
Let Y be a real number with X/2<=Y<=2X. Then
sum_{q<=Y}f_c(q)=sum_r a_c(r)sum_{d<=Y/r}mu(d).
For r<=Y^(1/2), the summatory-Mobius estimate used in fact 71389b22e6f49e13 gives
sum_{d<=Y/r}mu(d) << (Y/r)exp(-c_1 sqrt(log Y))
after decreasing the positive absolute constant c_1, because Y/r>=Y^(1/2). Summing over r gives
<<Y exp(-c_1 sqrt(log Y))x^(o(1)).
For r>Y^(1/2), the trivial bound for the inner sum gives at most Y/r. Since r^(-1)<=Y^(-1/8)r^(-3/4) on this range, its total is
<<Y^(7/8)x^(o(1)).
Because Y is comparable to X and X>=x^(eta_0), both contributions are
<<_{A_0,C_0,eta_0}X(log x)^(-A_0)
for every fixed A_0. Consequently every interval partial sum
S(t)=sum_{X<=q<=t}f_c(q),  X<=t<2X,
satisfies the same bound, since it is the difference of two initial partial sums.

Discrete summation by parts gives
|sum_{X<=q<2X}f_c(q)W(q)|
<=sup_{X<=t<2X}|S(t)| {sup_q|W(q)|+sum_q|W(q+1)-W(q)|}.
Substitution of the partial-sum estimate proves (1).

For the C1 specialization, m_eff=1 means gcd(C,n)=n, so n divides C. Every supported q is coprime to n by fact 79ffbcb2ffe4049f. Therefore Cq^(-1) is divisible by n and e_n(Cq^(-1))=1. Apply (1) separately to each separated literal q-mode and multiply by the absolute value of its outer coefficient. Summing these inequalities gives exactly (2), because V_Q of the complete remaining mode weight is retained in the sum. Finally, for any fixed A_0 and any fixed delta>0, the quotient Q(log x)^(-A_0)/Q^(1-delta)=Q^delta(log x)^(-A_0) tends to infinity when Q is a fixed positive power of x. Thus an arbitrary fixed logarithmic saving, even before a Q^(o(1)) loss, does not imply a fixed-power saving. This proves the final limitation without asserting a lower bound for the literal sum.

glossary.constant effective-phase chamber: The sector m_eff=1, equivalently n divides the reciprocal-phase numerator C, on which e_n(Cq^{-1}) equals one for every supported q-unit.
glossary.variation-weighted mode mass: The sum over separated q-modes of the absolute outer coefficient times the V_Q norm of that mode's complete remaining q-weight.

35e599ec4bc284fe.title: INACTIVE-FACE-WEIGHTED TENSOR BESSEL BOUND WITH A VARIABLE COMPLEMENT, AND THE LITERAL GA \(A\)-ROW SPECIALIZATION
35e599ec4bc284fe.author: slava chan
35e599ec4bc284fe.statement:
INACTIVE-FACE-WEIGHTED TENSOR BESSEL BOUND WITH A VARIABLE COMPLEMENT, AND THE LITERAL GA \(A\)-ROW SPECIALIZATION.

Let \(X\ge2\), \(D\ge1\), let \(A\ne0\) be an integer, let \(r\) be a nonempty squarefree positive integer, let \(J\) be a finite integer interval of cardinality \(V\) not containing \(0\), and let \(\mathcal V\) be a finite set of positive integers of cardinality \(P\). Assume that \(A,r,D\), the endpoints of \(J\), and the elements of \(\mathcal V\) are bounded by a fixed power of \(X\). Let \(\mathcal R\) be a finite set of distinct triples
\[
 j=(d_j,v_j,h_j)
\]
such that
\[
 D\le d_j<2D,\quad v_j\in\mathcal V,\quad h_j\in J,\quad
 d_j\ \hbox{and}\ n_j=d_jv_j\ \hbox{are squarefree}.                 \tag{1}
\]
Put
\[
 d_j^{\rm u}=\prod_{\substack{p\mid d_j\\p\nmid Ah_j}}p,
 \qquad r\mid d_j^{\rm u},\qquad
 a_j={d_j^{\rm u}\over r},\qquad
 \alpha_j={\mu(a_j)\over a_j}.                                      \tag{2}
\]
For every \(p\mid r\), define \(g_{p;j}\), its normalized Fourier transform \(\widehat g_{p;j}\), the product frequency set \(\Omega_r\), and
\[
 V_j(\boldsymbol\rho)=\prod_{p\mid r}\widehat g_{p;j}(\rho_p)
\]
exactly as in fact df97bf1eba0495be with \((n,h)=(n_j,h_j)\).

Then, for every complex coefficient array \((c_j)_{j\in\mathcal R}\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 \sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r}
 \left|\sum_{j\in\mathcal R}c_j\alpha_jV_j(\boldsymbol\rho)\right|^2
 \ll_\varepsilon X^\varepsilon VP\sum_{j\in\mathcal R}|c_j|^2.     \tag{3}
\]
If \(\mathcal T\) is finite and
\[
 Y_j(\boldsymbol\rho)=\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}
 \beta_{j,t}Z_t(\boldsymbol\rho),                                  \tag{4}
\]
define
\[
 \mathfrak P_{\mathcal V}(Y)=
 \sum_{t\in\mathcal T}
 \left(\sup_{j\in\mathcal R}|\beta_{j,t}|\right)
 \left(\sup_{\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r}|Z_t(\boldsymbol\rho)|\right).
                                                                         \tag{5}
\]
Then
\[
 \sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r}
 \left|\sum_{j\in\mathcal R}
 c_j\alpha_jY_j(\boldsymbol\rho)V_j(\boldsymbol\rho)\right|^2
 \ll_\varepsilon X^\varepsilon VP\,
 \mathfrak P_{\mathcal V}(Y)^2\sum_{j\in\mathcal R}|c_j|^2.        \tag{6}
\]

For the specialization, work in the forward GA-tail setting of facts e55b27d39c593164 and 0aa821ade9a14b45 after fixing one orientation, one exact outer gcd \(g\), one frozen layer, one parent, and one source/projective fiber. Thus
\[
 \mathscr A=N/g\ne0
\]
and \(B,Q,\omega_F\), as well as all polynomial-envelope data, are common on the family. Fix one \(A\)-anatomy dilator block
\[
 1\le\mathcal D\le d_\lambda<2\mathcal D,
\]
one signed frequency block \(1\le F\le x^3\), \(F\le|h|<2F\), and one common nonempty active product \(r\). An \(A\)-copy has
\[
 n=d_\lambda p,\qquad 2<p<Z_\theta,
\]
with \(p\) prime. For any set \(\mathcal R_r^A\) of actual rows in this fixed family with no repeated triple \((d_\lambda,p,h)\), the literal transforms satisfy
\[
 \sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r}
 \left|\sum_{j\in\mathcal R_r^A}
 c_jW_{j,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)V_{j,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)\right|^2
 \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon|\omega_F|^2Q^2F\,{B\over\mathcal D}
 \sum_{j\in\mathcal R_r^A}|c_j|^2.                                \tag{7}
\]
All literal marker, Möbius, physical Fourier, target-gcd, fixed-\(U\), high, source, parent, ordering, equality, collision, deletion, provenance, coprimality, inactive-prime, and \(p\)-CRT phase factors are retained.

This proves only the common-\(r\), coordinatewise weighted tensor estimate for the \(A\)-anatomy in the polynomial frequency range. It proves no pair-dependent nonresonance deletion, no distinct-\(r\) discrepancy, no centered-face recombination, no GA-NR-DIL estimate, no payment of the good-\(\mathscr W\) tail, and no Goldbach conclusion.
35e599ec4bc284fe.proof:
We prove (3). For a row \(j\), every prime divisor of \(r\) divides \(d_j^{\rm u}\). Hence
\[
 (Ah_j,r)=1,\qquad r\mid d_j,\qquad
 \left(r,{n_j\over r}\right)=1.
\]
Thus fact df97bf1eba0495be applies to every row pair. Put
\[
 m_j={d_j\over r},\qquad s_j=(d_j,Ah_j).
\]
Squarefreeness and \((r,Ah_j)=1\) give
\[
 d_j^{\rm u}={d_j\over s_j},\qquad
 a_j={m_j\over s_j},\qquad |\alpha_j|={s_j\over m_j}.             \tag{8}
\]
Also \(n_j/r=m_jv_j\). For two rows \(j,k\), fact df97bf1eba0495be gives
\[
 \left|\sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r}
 V_j(\boldsymbol\rho)\overline{V_k(\boldsymbol\rho)}\right|
 \le 2^{\omega(r)}{\gcd(r,T_{jk})\over r},                         \tag{9}
\]
where
\[
 T_{jk}=h_jm_kv_k-h_km_jv_j,                                      \tag{10}
\]
because \(h_jn_k-h_kn_j=rT_{jk}\) and \(r\) is squarefree.

Fix \(j\) and use
\[
 \gcd(r,T)=\sum_{\substack{t\mid r\\t\mid T}}\varphi(t).           \tag{11}
\]
For fixed \(t\mid r\), \(h_k\in J\), and \(v_k\in\mathcal V\), the congruence \(t\mid T_{jk}\) restricts \(m_k\) to one residue class modulo \(t\), since
\[
 (h_jv_k,t)=1.                                                     \tag{12}
\]
Indeed, \((h_j,r)=1\), while squarefreeness of \(d_kv_k\) and \(r\mid d_k\) give \((v_k,r)=1\).

Let \(M=D/r\). A nonempty family has \(r\le d_k<2D\), so \(M>1/2\). Put \(L=|Ah_k|>0\). Dropping all squarefree and row restrictions, the exact inactive magnitude in this residue class is bounded by
\[
 \sum_{\substack{M\le m<2M\\m\equiv c\ ({\rm mod}\ t)}}
 {\gcd(m,L)\over m}.                                               \tag{13}
\]
Using
\[
 \gcd(m,L)=\sum_{\substack{s\mid L\\s\mid m}}\varphi(s)            \tag{14}
\]
and \((L,t)=1\), the simultaneous conditions occupy one residue class modulo \(st\). Hence
\[
 (13)\ll {1\over M}\sum_{\substack{s\mid L\\s\le2M}}\varphi(s)
 \left({M\over st}+1\right)
 \le {\tau(L)\over t}+2\tau(L).                                   \tag{15}
\]
Fact e705401df9f0709e and the polynomial envelope give
\[
 \tau(L)+\tau(r)+2^{\omega(r)}\ll_\varepsilon X^\varepsilon.       \tag{16}
\]
There are \(V\) choices for \(h_k\) and \(P\) choices for \(v_k\). Equations (8)--(16), \(|\alpha_j|\le1\), \(\sum_{t\mid r}\varphi(t)=r\), and
\(\sum_{t\mid r}\varphi(t)/t\le\tau(r)\) show that every row and column sum of the positive majorant of the \(\alpha\)-weighted Gram is
\[
 \ll_\varepsilon X^\varepsilon VP.                                \tag{17}
\]
Schur's test proves (3). Since \(\mathcal T\) is finite, Minkowski's inequality in \(\ell^2(\Omega_r)\), followed termwise by (3), proves (6).

We prove the scoped GA specialization. In the fixed family, set \(A=\mathscr A=N/g\). An \(A\)-copy has \(n=d_\lambda p\). The support conditions
\[
 {B\over2}\le d_\lambda p\le2B,\qquad
 \mathcal D\le d_\lambda<2\mathcal D
\]
put every possible \(p\) in
\[
 {B\over4\mathcal D}<p\le {2B\over\mathcal D}.                    \tag{18}
\]
A nonempty family has \(\mathcal D\le2B\); therefore the number \(P\) of possible integer values of \(p\) is
\[
 P\ll {B\over\mathcal D}.                                         \tag{19}
\]

Equation (4) of fact 0aa821ade9a14b45 gives
\[
 B_{\lambda,h,r}(q)
 ={\mu(a_j)\over a_j}b_{\lambda,h}(q)
 e_p\!\left(\mathscr Ah(qd_\lambda)^{-1}\right).                  \tag{20}
\]
Keep the \(p\)-CRT phase inside
\[
 Y_j(\boldsymbol\rho)
 =\sum_{\substack{Q\le q<2Q\\(q,n_j)=1}}
 b_{\lambda,h}(q)e_p\!\left(\mathscr Ah(qd_\lambda)^{-1}\right)
 \chi_{\boldsymbol\rho}(q),                                       \tag{21}
\]
so \(W_{j,r}=\alpha_jY_j\). Use the finite delta-\(q\) decomposition
\[
 Y_j(\boldsymbol\rho)
 =\sum_{Q\le q_0<2Q}\beta_{j,q_0}\chi_{\boldsymbol\rho}(q_0),      \tag{22}
\]
where, piecewise,
\[
 \beta_{j,q_0}=
 \begin{cases}
 b_{\lambda,h}(q_0)e_p\!\left(\mathscr Ah(q_0d_\lambda)^{-1}\right),
   &(q_0,n_j)=1,\\
 0,&(q_0,n_j)>1.
 \end{cases}                                                       \tag{23}
\]
The inverse in the first line exists, and its exponential has modulus one. Because the exact \(g\), frozen layer, parent, and source/projective fiber are fixed, fact e55b27d39c593164 gives uniformly in \(1\le F\le x^3\)
\[
 \sup_{j,q_0}|\beta_{j,q_0}|
 \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon|\omega_F|.                         \tag{24}
\]
Thus
\[
 \mathfrak P_{\mathcal V}(Y)
 \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon Q|\omega_F|.                       \tag{25}
\]
Apply (6) with \(X=x\), common target \(A=\mathscr A\), \(D=\mathcal D\ge1\), \(V\ll F\), (19), and (25). After shrinking the auxiliary epsilon this proves (7). Equations (20)--(23) retain every literal factor, and all limitations are explicit.

glossary.literal GA A-row WTG: The common-active-product coordinatewise weighted tensor estimate for GA A-marker copies.
glossary.variable-complement inactive-face tensor: The fixed-active-product tensor estimate retaining inactive-prime weights when the complementary factor v ranges over a finite set.

35ff1e5855450319.title: EXACT OUTPUT-PROFILE FORM OF THE MEAN-ZERO RECIPROCAL-SLOPE DISCREPANCY
35ff1e5855450319.author: slava chan
35ff1e5855450319.statement:
EXACT OUTPUT-PROFILE FORM OF THE MEAN-ZERO RECIPROCAL-SLOPE DISCREPANCY.

Let p be a prime, let A be an integer, let cal Q be a finite set of positive integers not divisible by p, and let b_q be complex coefficients supported on cal Q. For every exact rational reciprocal slope lambda represented by an ordered pair from cal Q, let B_lambda and rho_{p,lambda} be as in fact 27540b4094f677f4. Define, for r modulo p,
  F_p(r)=sum_{lambda:rho_{p,lambda}=r}B_lambda,
  D_p(r)=sum_{lambda:rho_{p,lambda}=r}|B_lambda|^2,          (1)
and put
  S_0=sum_lambda B_lambda
     =|sum_{q in cal Q}b_q|^2.                              (2)
Define the modular unequal-slope output profile
  G_p(r)=|F_p(r)|^2-(1-2/p)D_p(r)
       -p^(-1)[F_p(r)conjugate(S_0)
                    +conjugate(F_p(r))S_0].                 (3)

For every complex function W on Z/pZ with
  sum_{r modulo p}W(r)=0,                                   (4)
the exact all-shift rational-slope-subtracted energy of fact 27540b4094f677f4 satisfies
  E_p(W;b)=sum_{r modulo p}W(r)G_p(r).                       (5)
Equivalently, only pairs of distinct exact rational slopes occur in G_p: congruence of their reductions supplies the incidence part, while both displayed linear terms are the two centered cross terms. Since W has mean zero, for every complex constant c,
  E_p(W;b)=sum_rW(r)[G_p(r)-c].                              (6)
Thus the remaining full-kernel mean-zero contract is exactly an output-residue discrepancy estimate for the profile G_p, not a bound for its total mass. No estimate for G_p is asserted.
35ff1e5855450319.proof:
First, summing definition (3) of B_lambda in fact 27540b4094f677f4 over all represented slopes sums over every ordered pair (q_1,q_2). Therefore
  sum_lambda B_lambda
   =sum_{q_1,q_2}b_{q_1}conjugate(b_{q_2})
   =|sum_qb_q|^2,
which proves (2).

By equation (15) of fact 27540b4094f677f4, E_p(W;b) is the sum over ordered pairs of exact slopes lambda and mu with lambda not equal to mu of
  B_lambda conjugate(B_mu)
       Gamma_W(rho_{p,lambda},rho_{p,mu}).                  (7)
Condition (4) reduces the physical kernel to
  Gamma_W(x,y)=1_{x=y}W(x)-[W(x)+W(y)]/p.                   (8)

Group the incidence term in (7) by the common output residue r. All ordered slope pairs, including equal ones, contribute |F_p(r)|^2. Removing the equal-slope pairs leaves
  sum_rW(r)[|F_p(r)|^2-D_p(r)].                             (9)

For the first cross term in (8), sum first over mu not equal to lambda. Its contribution is
 -p^(-1)sum_lambda W(rho_{p,lambda})B_lambda
       [conjugate(S_0)-conjugate(B_lambda)]
 =-p^(-1)sum_rW(r)[F_p(r)conjugate(S_0)-D_p(r)].            (10)
Similarly, the second cross term is
 -p^(-1)sum_rW(r)[conjugate(F_p(r))S_0-D_p(r)].             (11)
Adding (9)-(11) gives precisely (3)-(5). Finally (4) implies sum_rW(r)c=0 for every constant c, which proves (6).

glossary.D_p: The exact-slope diagonal mass inside one output residue.
glossary.F_p: The sum of exact-slope fibre coefficients whose reductions have one output residue modulo p.
glossary.G_p: The modular unequal-slope output discrepancy profile.

36c43b23e4b3c052.title: ABSTRACT TOP-SLIVER COMPLETE-FREQUENCY TARGET-GCD-DESCENDED INTERVAL-PRIME TRACE WITH THE ORIGINAL ROUGH CUTOFF
36c43b23e4b3c052.author: slava chan
36c43b23e4b3c052.statement:
ABSTRACT TOP-SLIVER COMPLETE-FREQUENCY TARGET-GCD-DESCENDED INTERVAL-PRIME TRACE WITH THE ORIGINAL ROUGH CUTOFF.

Fix integers \(J,C_A,K\ge1\), constants \(C\ge1\), \(0<\kappa\le1/100\), and put
\[
 \sigma=\kappa/100,\qquad \beta_m=6/5-12\sigma/5.
\]
Let
\[
 \beta_m<\beta<6/5,\qquad B=Q^\beta,\qquad H_T=B/Q,
\]
where \(Q\) is sufficiently large, and put
\[
 L_0=H_TQ^\sigma,\qquad Z=Q^{3/2-\beta-3\sigma}.
\]
Fix a nonzero integer \(L_{\rm src}\) with \(|L_{\rm src}|\le Q^{C_A}\). Let \(\mathcal C\) be any set of squarefree divisors \(c\mid L_{\rm src}\) satisfying
\[
 c\le H_TQ^{\sigma/4}.
\]
For \(c\in\mathcal C\), put \(Q_c=Q/c\) and choose \(U_c,Y_c\ge1\) satisfying
\[
 C^{-1}B\le U_cY_c\le CB,\qquad L_0/2\le Y_c\le Z.
\]
For \(Q_c\le q<2Q_c\), let \(|d_{c,q}|\le1\), supported on squarefree \(q\) for which
\[
 (c,q)=(L_{\rm src}/c,q)=1.
\]
For every dyadic \(F\ge1\), let \(\nu_{c,F}(h)\), \(\alpha_{c,F}(u)\), and \(\gamma_{c,F}(p)\) have fixed divisor-function bounds and supports
\[
 F\le |h|<2F,\qquad U_c\le u<2U_c,
\]
and primes \(Y_c\le p<2Y_c\) satisfying \(L_0<p<Z\). Let \(\Psi_{c,F}\) be a uniformly scaled-smooth projective amplitude of fixed complexity and uniformly bounded projective Fourier norm. Let
\[
 |\omega_{c,F}|\le C_{J_0}\min\{1,(F/H_P)^{-J_0}\}
\]
for every fixed integer \(J_0\ge1\). Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
 T_c={1\over H_P}\sum_F\omega_{c,F}
 &\sum_{Q_c\le q<2Q_c}d_{c,q}
 \sum_{F\le|h|<2F}\nu_{c,F}(h)\\
 &\times\sum_{\substack{U_c\le u<2U_c\\
 Y_c\le p<2Y_c,\ p\ {\rm prime}\\
 (up,cq)=1,\ (u,p)=1}}
 \alpha_{c,F}(u)\gamma_{c,F}(p)
 \Psi_{c,F}\!\left({q\over Q_c},{|h|\over F},
 {u\over U_c},{p\over Y_c}\right)
 e_q\!\left(-{L_{\rm src}\over c}h(up)^{-1}\right).
\end{aligned} \tag{1}
\]

(i) If \(G\ge1\) and \(H_P=H_T/G\), then there is a fixed \(\delta_{A,\rm top,F}>0\) such that
\[
 \sum_{c\in\mathcal C}|T_c|\ll GQ^{2-\delta_{A,\rm top,F}}. \tag{2}
\]

(ii) If \(0<\eta<\sigma\),
\[
 Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\le G\le Q^{\sigma-\eta},\qquad H_P=H_T/G,
\]
then there is a fixed \(\delta_{A,\rm top,N}>0\) such that
\[
 \sum_{c\in\mathcal C}|T_c|\ll Q^{2-\delta_{A,\rm top,N}}. \tag{3}
\]

The constants and savings may depend on \(\kappa,\eta,C_A,J,K,C\) and the fixed projective norm, but not on \(Q,G,H_P,L_{\rm src},\mathcal C\), or the displayed coefficients. Both conclusions include \(H_P<1\), every actual integer-frequency block, all displayed coprimalities, and any additional labels already absorbed into the one-variable coefficients or stated projective amplitude. No literal-source identification, large-target-gcd tail, outer-\(g\) assembly, other anatomy, \(\beta\ge6/5\), or Goldbach assertion is made.
36c43b23e4b3c052.proof:
Put
\[
 v=F/H_P,\qquad q_0=Q_c=Q/c.
\]
We reproduce the complete fixed-\(q\) lifting because the new range and the change from \(2Z\) to \(Z\) must be checked explicitly.

Expand \(\Psi_{c,F}\) in an absolutely summable Fourier series in its four logarithmic scaled variables. Its coefficient \(\ell^1\)-norm is uniformly bounded. Absorb the separated one-variable Fourier modes into \(d_{c,q},\nu_{c,F},\alpha_{c,F},\gamma_{c,F}\). The condition \((up,c)=1\) separates as \((u,c)=(p,c)=1\). The condition \((up,q)=1\) is retained as the complete-product coprimality in fact \(4cae52efa792b9ef\). Write exactly
\[
 {\bf1}_{(u,p)=1}=1-{\bf1}_{p\mid u}. \tag{4}
\]

Fix \(c,F\). For the unrestricted term in (4), suppose temporarily that
\[
 2F\le Y_c,\qquad 8FY_c<q
\]
throughout \(q\asymp q_0\). Since \(U_cY_c\asymp B\) and \(Y_c\ge L_0/2\),
\[
 U_c\ll B/Y_c\ll Q^{1-\sigma}. \tag{5}
\]
Also
\[
 q_0=Q/c\ge Q^{2-\beta-\sigma/4}>Q^{4/5-\sigma/4}. \tag{6}
\]
Thus \(u\le q^2\) on the support for sufficiently large \(Q\). Apply fact \(4cae52efa792b9ef\) for each fixed \(q\), each Fourier mode, and each sign of \(h\), and sum its two terms over the \(O(q_0)\) moduli. Restoring \(H_P^{-1}\) and using \(U_cY_c\asymp B\) gives, up to \(Q^\varepsilon|\omega_{c,F}|\), the three contributions
\[
 A_1=c^{-1}G^{1/2}Q^2(H_T/Y_c)^{1/2}v^{1/2}, \tag{7}
\]
\[
 A_2=c^{-5/4}Q^{7/4}(H_TY_c)^{1/2}v, \tag{8}
\]
\[
 A_3=c^{-3/4}Q^{7/4}H_Tv. \tag{9}
\]
Indeed the first fixed-\(q\) term gives
\[
 H_P^{-1}q_0U_c(FY_c)^{1/2}=A_1
\]
up to fixed constants. For the second fixed-\(q\) term use
\[
 \{U_c(1+U_c/q_0)\}^{1/2}\le U_c^{1/2}+U_cq_0^{-1/2};
\]
after multiplication by the other factors and summation over \(q\), these two summands are (8) and (9).

For the diagonal term \(p\mid u\), write \(u=pu'\). The number of supported pairs \((u,p)\) is \(O(Q^\varepsilon U_c)\), because each \(u\) has divisor-function many prime divisors. Absolute summation over \(q,h\), using \(H_P^{-1}F=v\), gives
\[
 A_4\ll Q^\varepsilon|\omega_{c,F}|q_0vU_c
 \ll Q^\varepsilon|\omega_{c,F}|c^{-1}Q^{2-\sigma}v. \tag{10}
\]
This proves the four-term lifting and retains every displayed coprimality.

We first prove (2). Restrict to
\[
 v\le Q^{\sigma/2}. \tag{11}
\]
Since \(Y_c\ge H_TQ^\sigma/2\) and \(G\ge1\),
\[
 {2F\over Y_c}\le {4v\over GQ^\sigma}<1
\]
for sufficiently large \(Q\). Moreover \(c\le H_TQ^{\sigma/4}\), \(Y_c\le Z\), and
\[
 H_TZ=Q^{1/2-3\sigma}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 {q_0\over H_PY_c}
 ={QG\over cH_TY_c}
 \gg GQ^{3/2-\beta+11\sigma/4}
 >GQ^{3/10+11\sigma/4}. \tag{12}
\]
Equations (11)-(12) imply \(8FY_c<q\) for sufficiently large \(Q\), so (7)-(10) apply.

Divide (7)-(10) by \(GQ^2\). Using \(G\ge1\), \(Y_c\ge H_TQ^\sigma/2\), \(H_TY_c\le H_TZ=Q^{1/2-3\sigma}\), and \(\beta<6/5\), the ratios are at most constant multiples of
\[
 c^{-1}Q^{-\sigma/2}v^{1/2},\qquad
 c^{-5/4}Q^{-3\sigma/2}v,\qquad
 c^{-3/4}Q^{\beta-5/4}v,\qquad
 c^{-1}Q^{-\sigma}v. \tag{13}
\]
The third power is uniformly bounded by \(Q^{-1/20}v\). Summing dyadic \(v\le Q^{\sigma/2}\) in (13) leaves a fixed positive power saving, since \(0<\sigma\le10^{-4}\).

For \(v>Q^{\sigma/2}\), direct counting in (1) gives
\[
 |T_{c,F}|\ll Q^\varepsilon c^{-1}Q^2H_Tv|\omega_{c,F}|. \tag{14}
\]
Uniformly for \(\beta<6/5\), \(H_T\le Q^{1/5}\). Choose one available fixed decay order \(J_*\) such that
\[
 (J_*-1)\sigma/2>1/5+\sigma.
\]
The dyadic sum of (14) is \(O(c^{-1}GQ^{2-\delta})\) for a fixed \(\delta>0\), since \(G\ge1\). Finally, because every \(c\) is a divisor of \(L_{\rm src}\) and \(|L_{\rm src}|\le Q^{C_A}\),
\[
 \sum_{c\in\mathcal C}(c^{-1}+c^{-3/4}+c^{-5/4})\ll Q^\varepsilon.
\]
After decreasing the saving to absorb this divisor factor, (2) follows.

For (3), restrict first to
\[
 v\le Q^{\eta/2}. \tag{15}
\]
The lower bound on \(G\) gives
\[
 Y_c/H_P\ge GQ^\sigma/2\ge Q^\eta/2,
\]
so \(2F\le Y_c\) for sufficiently large \(Q\). Equation (12), now with \(G\ge Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\), again gives \(8FY_c<q\) throughout (15). Divide (7)-(10) by \(Q^2\). For the first term,
\[
 G^{1/2}(H_T/Y_c)^{1/2}
 \ll Q^{(\sigma-\eta)/2}Q^{-\sigma/2}=Q^{-\eta/2}. \tag{16}
\]
The remaining three ratios are at most constant multiples of
\[
 c^{-5/4}Q^{-3\sigma/2}v,\qquad
 c^{-3/4}Q^{-1/20}v,\qquad
 c^{-1}Q^{-\sigma}v. \tag{17}
\]
Summing dyadic \(v\le Q^{\eta/2}\) in (16)-(17) leaves a fixed positive power saving because \(0<\eta<\sigma\le10^{-4}\).

For \(v>Q^{\eta/2}\), direct counting gives
\[
 |T_{c,F}|\ll Q^\varepsilon c^{-1}QBv|\omega_{c,F}|
 =Q^\varepsilon c^{-1}Q^2H_Tv|\omega_{c,F}|. \tag{18}
\]
Choose the available fixed decay order so that
\[
 (J_*-1)\eta/2>1/5+\eta.
\]
Since \(H_T\le Q^{1/5}\), the dyadic sum of (18) is \(O(c^{-1}Q^{2-\delta'})\) for a fixed \(\delta'>0\). The same divisor sum proves (3).

If \(H_P<1\), every integer \(F\ge1\) has \(v>1\), but it lies in exactly one of the analytic and decaying ranges above. The projective Fourier modes and all legal inherited labels have uniformly bounded \(\ell^1\)-cost and are absorbed by decreasing the fixed savings. The use of the smaller original cutoff \(Z\), rather than \(2Z\), only strengthens \(Y_c\le Z\), \(H_TY_c\le Q^{1/2-3\sigma}\), and the frequency-separation bound. This completes the proof.

glossary.delta_{A,top,F}: The fixed full-G power-saving exponent in the abstract original-cutoff top-sliver interval-prime trace.
glossary.delta_{A,top,N}: The fixed near-balanced power-saving exponent in the abstract original-cutoff top-sliver interval-prime trace.

3704d40c75e8269c.title: BOURGAIN--GARAEV COMPLETE RECIPROCAL ENERGY LEAVES THE SHORT-WINDOW COLLISION BULK UNLOCALIZED
3704d40c75e8269c.author: slava chan
3704d40c75e8269c.statement:
BOURGAIN--GARAEV COMPLETE RECIPROCAL ENERGY LEAVES THE SHORT-WINDOW COLLISION BULK UNLOCALIZED.

Let Q>=2, let p>2Q be a prime, and let A be an integer not divisible by p. Put
  I_Q={q in Z: Q<=q<2Q}.
Let b_q be complex coefficients supported on I_Q with |b_q|<=1. For q_1,q_2 in I_Q put
  rho_p(q_1,q_2)=A(q_2-q_1)(q_1q_2)^(-1) modulo p,
where inversion is modulo p. For q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4 in I_Q put
  Delta=(q_2-q_1)q_3q_4-(q_4-q_3)q_1q_2.
For a complex function W on Z/pZ and x,y in Z/pZ define
  Gamma_W(x,y)=1_{x=y}W(x)-[W(x)+W(y)]/p
                  +(sum_{r modulo p}W(r))/p^2.
Define
  E_p(W;b)=sum_{q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4 in I_Q; Delta nonzero}
   b_{q_1}conjugate(b_{q_2})conjugate(b_{q_3})b_{q_4}
   Gamma_W(rho_p(q_1,q_2),rho_p(q_3,q_4)).                 (1)
If |W(r)|<=1 for every r modulo p, then for every epsilon>0,
  |E_p(W;b)|<<_epsilon Q^epsilon[Q^(8/3)+Q^4/p].           (2)
The bound is independent of the support length of W.

There is a complete weighted-family version. Fix an integer J>=1, and let tau_J(n) be the number of ordered J-tuples of positive integers with product n. Let P>2Q, let cal P be any set of primes in [P,2P), and let V>=2. Let xi_v be supported on integers V<=v<2V with |xi_v|<=tau_J(v). For every such v and every residue s modulo v, let b_{v,s}(q) be supported on I_Q, satisfy |b_{v,s}(q)|<=1, and be independent of p. For every v,s,p let W_{v,s,p} be a complex function on Z/pZ of modulus at most one, and put
 E_{v,s,p}=E_p(W_{v,s,p};b_{v,s}).
Then
 |sum_{V<=v<2V}sum_{s modulo v}|xi_v/v|^2
       sum_{p in cal P} E_{v,s,p}|
 <<_{J,epsilon} (QV)^epsilon[P Q^(8/3)+Q^4].               (3)

Now fix 1<=L<=P. Consider the strictly stronger localized comparison target
 |sum_{V<=v<2V}sum_{s modulo v}|xi_v/v|^2
       sum_{p in cal P} E_{v,s,p}|
 <<_{J,epsilon} (QV)^epsilon
       [P Q^(8/3)+(L/P)Q^4]                                (4)
under the additional hypothesis that every W_{v,s,p} is supported on at most L consecutive residues modulo p. The cited complete reciprocal-energy theorem of Bourgain and Garaev, arXiv:1211.4184, Theorem 1 with k=2, does not directly imply (4): its statement counts all output residues and contains no parameter L, while domination by |W|<=1 gives exactly (3). Thus a proof of (4) needs an additional output-residue localization argument which is absent from that complete theorem. This is a theorem-interface no-direct-import statement, not an assertion that (4) is false.
3704d40c75e8269c.proof:
Because p>2Q, every q in I_Q is nonzero modulo p. Since p does not divide A,
 rho_p(q_1,q_2)=rho_p(q_3,q_4)
is equivalent to
 q_1^(-1)-q_2^(-1)=q_3^(-1)-q_4^(-1) modulo p,
or, after moving two terms,
 q_1^(-1)+q_4^(-1)=q_2^(-1)+q_3^(-1) modulo p.             (5)

Bourgain and Garaev, arXiv:1211.4184, Theorem 1, states the following. If I is a nonzero interval in the finite field Z/pZ and k is a fixed positive integer, then the number J_{2k} of solutions
 x_1^(-1)+...+x_k^(-1)=x_{k+1}^(-1)+...+x_{2k}^(-1),
 x_1,...,x_{2k} in I,
satisfies
 J_{2k}<(|I|^(2k^2/(k+1))+|I|^(2k)/p)|I|^{o(1)}.          (6)
Apply (6) with I=I_Q and k=2. The number J_4(p,Q) of all quadruples satisfying (5) obeys
 J_4(p,Q)<<_epsilon Q^epsilon[Q^(8/3)+Q^4/p].              (7)
The restriction Delta nonzero only deletes quadruples, so the same upper bound applies to the number of incidence quadruples occurring in (1).

Expand Gamma_W in (1). The absolute value of the incidence-incidence contribution is at most J_4(p,Q), because |b_q| and |W| are at most one. Each of the two cross contributions is at most Q^4/p by the triangle inequality. The center contribution is at most
 p^(-2)|sum_r W(r)|Q^4<=Q^4/p.                             (8)
Equations (7)-(8) prove (2), after enlarging the implied constant. Exact deletion of Delta=0 is the all-shift rational-slope subtraction of fact 27540b4094f677f4.

For (3), apply (2) for each p,v,s. The number of primes in [P,2P) is at most 2P, and p>=P, hence
 sum_{p in cal P}[Q^(8/3)+Q^4/p]
 <=2P Q^(8/3)+2Q^4.                                       (9)
Fact d061fc4dc153e309 gives
 sum_{V<=v<2V}sum_{s modulo v}|xi_v/v|^2
 <<_{J,epsilon}V^epsilon.                                  (10)
Multiplying (9) by (10) proves (3), with epsilon adjusted.

Finally assume each W is supported on at most L residues. The complete count (6) does not distinguish the common reciprocal-difference value in (5). The derivation of (2) used only |W|<=1, so its Q^4/p term is unchanged. Summation over p in (9) therefore gives Q^4. By contrast, a factor L/p on the Q^4/p term at each prime would give LQ^4/p^2 per prime, whose sum over at most 2P primes p>=P is at most 2(L/P)Q^4. This is the second term of (4). Since no such L/p factor occurs in (6), the cited theorem plus the displayed domination argument proves (3) but not (4). This proves the no-direct-import conclusion.

glossary.E_p: The signed nonzero-integer-determinant centered reciprocal-difference energy.
glossary.E_{v,s,p}: The energy E_p for the coefficient row b_{v,s} and weight W_{v,s,p}.
glossary.I_Q: The integer interval of q-values from Q inclusive to 2Q exclusive.
glossary.J_4(p,Q): The number of four-tuples in I_Q whose two reciprocal differences agree modulo p.
glossary.cal P: The selected set of prime moduli in the interval from P to 2P.

37da2f2d258dd004.title: COMPLETE FIXED-POWER PAYMENT OF THE BALANCED LARGE-EFFECTIVE STRICT-TOP C1 TWO-FREE CELL. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, and let beta_m<=beta<6/5 in the literal strict-top C1 setting. Thus n=pv is squarefree, p is the unique rough prime, gcd(p,v)=1, every prime divisor of v is at most Q^(beta-1+sigma), C=mathscr A h, and m_eff=n/gcd(C,n). Let c be squarefree with nc<=Q^K for a fixed K. Assume
37da2f2d258dd004.author: slava chan
37da2f2d258dd004.statement:
COMPLETE FIXED-POWER PAYMENT OF THE BALANCED LARGE-EFFECTIVE STRICT-TOP C1 TWO-FREE CELL. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, and let beta_m<=beta<6/5 in the literal strict-top C1 setting. Thus n=pv is squarefree, p is the unique rough prime, gcd(p,v)=1, every prime divisor of v is at most Q^(beta-1+sigma), C=mathscr A h, and m_eff=n/gcd(C,n). Let c be squarefree with nc<=Q^K for a fixed K. Assume
Q/2<=m_eff<=2Q.
Let I_i=[U_i,2U_i) intersect Z with Q^(1/2)/4<=U_i<=4Q^(1/2), and let W be extended by zero, supported on Q<=q<2Q, with V_Q(W)<=Q^epsilon for every fixed epsilon>0. Consider the balanced two-free factor-box sum
S_bal=sum_{u_1 in I_1,u_2 in I_2;gcd(u_1u_2,nc)=1}W(u_1u_2)e_n(C(u_1u_2)^(-1)),
including any fixed signed combinatorial prefactor from the j=3, d_1=d_2=d_3=1 truncated-inverse box of fact 3dabf494e3ed99fd. Then
|S_bal|<=Q^(1-1/2000+o(1)).
Consequently the balanced large-effective C1 two-free cell is completely paid, including p dividing C and the prime case of m_eff. This theorem is confined to the balanced cell and does not estimate general unbalanced A-ROUTING RESIDUAL boxes.
37da2f2d258dd004.proof:
Choose delta=rho=1/2000 in fact 8eb30e55bdef6b27. Then
4(delta+rho)=1/250<1/200.                                      (1)
Apply fact c72a96984158fa33. If p divides C, or if p does not divide C and r_eff=m_eff/p satisfies r_eff>=Q^(1/100), that fact supplies a divisor in the window with lambda=1/200 and, by (1), places the balanced cell in the disjoint A-PAID(delta,rho) class. Fact 8eb30e55bdef6b27 then gives
|S_bal|<=Q^(1-1/2000)                                          (2)
throughout this first class, retaining W, the complete coprimality gate, the reduced unit numerator, every sign, and the fixed factor positions.

It remains to treat the exact complement. By c72a96984158fa33 it has
p not dividing C, m_eff=p r_eff, r_eff<Q^(1/100).               (3)
Put g=gcd(C,n) and C'=C/g. Since n is squarefree, n=g m_eff and gcd(C',m_eff)=1. For every q coprime to n,
e_n(Cq^(-1))=e_{m_eff}(C'q^(-1)).                              (4)
Indeed C=gC', so the quotient in the additive character reduces by the common factor g.

Let c'=rad(nc). It is squarefree, polynomially bounded in Q, and
1_{gcd(q,nc)=1}=1_{gcd(q,c'm_eff)=1},                           (5)
because m_eff divides n and repeated prime factors do not affect coprimality. Apply fact 7a5079a9f524eb92 with its p equal to the selected rough prime, its r equal to r_eff, its numerator equal to C', its auxiliary squarefree integer equal to c', and theta=1/100. Hypotheses (3)-(5), Q/2<=m_eff<=2Q, the square-root interval bounds, and the BV hypothesis are exactly its inputs. It yields
|S_bal|<=Q^(1-79/9600+o(1)).                                   (6)
The fixed j=3 combinatorial prefactor depends only on the fixed truncation order and is absorbed in the implied constant.

The first class and (3) are disjoint and exhaustive by c72a96984158fa33. Since 79/9600>1/2000, equations (2) and (6) prove the displayed uniform bound. No unbalanced box has been included.

glossary.balanced large-effective C1 closure: Fixed-power payment of the full square-root two-free factor cell for m_eff comparable to Q, including its ultra-near-prime factor-gap case.

3822f8ceb13a081b.title: Assume the forward-1x1 source hypotheses and notation of facts 3bb378b0a49679f9 and a94835cfd97853a0, with fixed positive integer target N. Let Z_large be any finite family of its incidences with D_z>64. For z in Z_large write
3822f8ceb13a081b.author: slava chan
3822f8ceb13a081b.statement:
Assume the forward-1x1 source hypotheses and notation of facts 3bb378b0a49679f9 and a94835cfd97853a0, with fixed positive integer target N. Let Z_large be any finite family of its incidences with D_z>64. For z in Z_large write
S(z)={p_z,ell_z}, g_z=gcd(d_z,p_zell_z), and b_z=p_zell_z/g_z.
Let P_N be the set of odd prime divisors of N and let omega_odd(N)=|P_N|.

(A) Every z in Z_large belongs to exactly one of the disjoint layers
Z_1={z:g_z=1},
Z_r={z:g_z=r}, r in P_N.
Thus
Z_large=Z_1 disjoint_union (disjoint_union_{r in P_N}Z_r),
with empty layers allowed, and the number of possible gcd-provenance labels is at most
1+omega_odd(N)<=1+log(N)/log(3).

(B) If z belongs to Z_r with r in P_N, then r is exactly one of p_z,ell_z and b_z is the other displayed prime. In particular the only nontrivial physical primitive additive conductor retaining all quotient primes on this layer is the one-prime conductor b_z; the missing displayed prime r is forced to divide the fixed target N.

(C) For an ordered support-disjoint pair (z,z') in Z_large^2, the exact number of primitive displayed primes left in b_zb_{z'} is four, three, or two according as zero, one, or two of z,z' lie outside Z_1. If both lie outside Z_1, their gcd labels r and r' are distinct members of P_N. Consequently the ordered pair family has an exact disjoint decomposition into at most
(1+omega_odd(N))^2
gcd-provenance blocks, and only the (1,1) block can feed a literal four-prime primitive packet.

(D) Support avoidance is a sufficient criterion for the gcd-one layer:
S(z) intersect P_N=emptyset implies g_z=1.
No converse is asserted or supplied by this ledger; in particular this implication alone does not identify support avoidance with the exact gcd-one selector.

This is a logarithmic-complexity provenance ledger only. It neither bounds the total weight of the bad layers nor makes their deletion sign-preserving.
3822f8ceb13a081b.proof:
Fact 3bb378b0a49679f9 proves that g_z belongs to {1,p_z,ell_z,p_zell_z} and that g_z divides N. Fact a94835cfd97853a0 proves that D_z>64 excludes g_z=p_zell_z. Therefore g_z is 1, p_z, or ell_z. In either nontrivial case it is an odd prime dividing N, hence belongs to P_N. Since g_z is uniquely determined by z, the displayed layers are disjoint and exhaustive.

If t=omega_odd(N), the product of the t distinct odd prime divisors of N divides N and is at least 3^t. Hence 3^t<=N, so t<=log(N)/log(3). This proves (A).

For (B), if g_z=p_z then b_z=ell_z, while if g_z=ell_z then b_z=p_z. These are the only non-gcd-one cases by (A). Fact 3bb378b0a49679f9 proves that physical primitive additive conductors are divisors of b_z. Since b_z is now prime, its only nontrivial divisor is b_z itself. The prime removed from the quotient is g_z, which divides N.

For (C), fact c882223fd3a1511a proves for a support-disjoint pair that
Omega(b_zb_{z'})=4-Omega(g_z)-Omega(g_{z'}).
On Z_large each g has either zero or one prime factor, so the right side is four, three, or two according to the number of non-gcd-one sides. If both gcds are nontrivial and equal to the same prime r, then r belongs to both displayed supports, contradicting their disjointness. Hence their labels are distinct. Applying the disjoint layer partition from (A) independently to z and z' gives at most (1+omega_odd(N))^2 ordered blocks. The formula shows that only label pair (1,1) retains four primes.

For (D), suppose g_z>1. Part (A) shows that g_z is a displayed prime lying in P_N, so S(z) meets P_N. Taking the contrapositive proves that support avoidance implies g_z=1. Nothing in this argument proves the reverse implication, so no reverse is included.

The final scope follows because the argument counts only possible gcd labels. It contains no estimate for the sums of the original signed weights inside those layers and no positivity statement for deleting them.

glossary.P_N: the set of odd prime divisors of the fixed target N
glossary.Z_large: a finite family of forward-1x1 source incidences with D_z>64
glossary.Z_r: the source layer whose exact gcd label is the odd target prime r
glossary.r: an odd prime divisor of N used as a gcd-provenance label
glossary.r': the gcd-provenance label of the second incidence in a pair

382dadf452a0f461.title: Let m>1 be odd, let K be coprime to m, put q=m^2, let G be the unit group modulo q, and put n=phi(q). Extend every multiplicative character of G to all residues modulo q by zero on nonunits. For characters chi,psi of G and unit residues n_1,n_2 modulo q define the complete row-character determinant sum
382dadf452a0f461.author: slava chan
382dadf452a0f461.statement:
Let m>1 be odd, let K be coprime to m, put q=m^2, let G be the unit group modulo q, and put n=phi(q). Extend every multiplicative character of G to all residues modulo q by zero on nonunits. For characters chi,psi of G and unit residues n_1,n_2 modulo q define the complete row-character determinant sum
R_{chi,psi}(n_1,n_2)
 =sum_{a,c modulo q; a n_2-c n_1=2K modulo q}chi(a)psi(c),            (1)
and define the Jacobi sum
J(chi,psi)=sum_{y modulo q}chi(1+y)psi(y).                            (2)
Then
R_{chi,psi}(n_1,n_2)
 =chi(2K n_2^(-1))psi(2K n_1^(-1))J(chi,psi).                        (3)

Now let s belong to {1,-1}, let W be a complex-valued function modulo m, let T_W be the shared normal-digit tensor of fact 8230d44e6677f45b, and let
S(chi,psi)=sum_{u modulo m}W(u)
 conjugate(chi(K+2smu)psi(K-2smu))                                  (4)
be its exact character coefficient. Define the complete-row character assembly at the unit columns n_1,n_2 by
C_W(n_1,n_2)
 =n^(-2)sum_{chi,psi}S(chi,psi)chi(n_2)psi(-n_1)
 R_{chi,psi}(n_1,n_2).                                               (5)
Then
C_W(n_1,n_2)
 =sum_{a,c in G; a n_2-c n_1=2K modulo q}T_W(a,n_2,c,-n_1)
 =sum_{u modulo m}W(u).                                              (6)
Consequently C_W(n_1,n_2)=0 for every pair of unit columns whenever W is centered. In particular, every pure nonzero digit Fourier mode W_ell(u)=e_m(ell u), ell nonzero modulo m, cancels exactly after both determinant row variables are restored and completed modulo m^2.

This complete-row cancellation and the nonzero formal column assembly in facts a170364aba04897b and 15dc89545ee8244b are compatible: the former includes the row-character factors and a complete residue sum of length m^2, whereas the latter applies the untwisted Bettin--Chandee column functional after the row characters have no legal slot. The literal near-maximal row boxes have length comparable to m, not m^2. Therefore (3)-(6) isolate the minimal analytic repair as control of incomplete, smoothly truncated two-row-character determinant sums relative to the complete centered value, with all coefficient costs retained; no such bound is asserted here.
382dadf452a0f461.proof:
Because m is odd and K is coprime to m, 2K is a unit modulo q. Fix n_1,n_2 in G. For every residue c modulo q, the determinant congruence in (1) determines the unique residue
a=(2K+c n_1)n_2^(-1) modulo q.                                      (7)
Make the bijective change of variables
y=c n_1(2K)^(-1) modulo q.                                           (8)
Then
c=2K y n_1^(-1),  a=2K(1+y)n_2^(-1) modulo q.                       (9)
The characters are multiplicative on units and are zero on nonunits. Since all displayed prefactors are units, substituting (9) into (1) gives
R_{chi,psi}(n_1,n_2)
=chi(2K n_2^(-1))psi(2K n_1^(-1))
 sum_{y modulo q}chi(1+y)psi(y),
which is (3).

Fact 8230d44e6677f45b gives the exact expansion
T_W(a,b,c,d)
=n^(-2)sum_{chi,psi}S(chi,psi)chi(a)chi(b)psi(c)psi(d)               (10)
on G^4, with S as in (4). Insert b=n_2 and d=-n_1 in (10), sum over a,c in G satisfying the determinant congruence, and use the definition (1). This gives the first equality between (5) and the middle expression in (6).

It remains to evaluate that middle expression without characters. From the definition of T_W in fact 8230d44e6677f45b,
T_W(a,n_2,c,-n_1)
=sum_{u modulo m}W(u)
 Delta_q(a n_2-K-2smu)
 Delta_q(-c n_1-K+2smu).                                            (11)
Fix u. Because n_1,n_2 are units and K+2smu and K-2smu are units modulo q, the two deltas in (11) force the unique unit residues
a=(K+2smu)n_2^(-1),
c=(-K+2smu)n_1^(-1) modulo q.                                      (12)
For this forced pair,
a n_2-c n_1
=(K+2smu)-(-K+2smu)=2K modulo q.                                   (13)
Thus the determinant restriction in the middle expression of (6) removes none of the unique pairs (12). Conversely, every nonzero term of (11) is one of those pairs. Summing first over a,c and then over u therefore gives exactly
sum_{u modulo m}W(u),
which proves the second equality in (6).

If W is centered, its displayed sum is zero. For W_ell(u)=e_m(ell u) with ell nonzero, additive orthogonality gives sum_uW_ell(u)=0. This proves the cancellation assertions. Facts a170364aba04897b and 15dc89545ee8244b define and bound a different object: a formal assembly of the untwisted column main-term functional, while fact a695dcaf05aaa83d proves that the row characters in (10) are not admissible smooth row profiles in the existing theorem. The final scope comparison follows directly.

glossary.C_W: the complete-row character assembly of the shared normal-digit tensor at fixed unit columns
glossary.J(chi,psi): the complete Jacobi sum sum_y chi(1+y)psi(y) modulo m^2
glossary.R_{chi,psi}: the complete modulo-m^2 sum of the two multiplicative row characters on a determinant congruence with fixed unit columns

3845a81c13f5cf81.title: Under the hypotheses and notation of fact c9ed24359b1f5321, for each u in U define the prime-fibre aggregate
3845a81c13f5cf81.author: slava chan
3845a81c13f5cf81.statement:
Under the hypotheses and notation of fact c9ed24359b1f5321, for each u in U define the prime-fibre aggregate
A_u=sum_{z in Z:u in S(z)}w_z.
Define the incidence operator R from real functions on Z to real functions on U by
(Rw)(u)=A_u.
Then the exact prime-fibre collision identity is
||Rw||_2^2=sum_{u in U}A_u^2=Q_1+2Q_2.                         (PF)
Consequently
Q_1=sum_u A_u^2-2Q_2,
Q_1+Q_2=sum_u A_u^2-Q_2,
Q_0=(sum_z w_z)^2-sum_u A_u^2+Q_2.                            (IE)
In particular Q_1>=-2Q_2, and the combined collision block Q_1+Q_2 is an exact difference of two nonnegative fibre energies rather than a nonnegative form in general.

The lower bound Q_1>=-2Q_2 is sharp. Take four distinct elements a,b,c,d of U, supports
S_1={a,b}, S_2={b,c}, S_3={c,d}, S_4={d,a},
and weights (w_1,w_2,w_3,w_4)=(1,-1,1,-1). Then every A_u is zero,
Q_2=4, Q_1=-8, Q_0=4, and the complete square is zero.
Thus even after the positive prime-fibre Gram bundle Q_1+2Q_2 is exposed, recovering the actual collision sum requires subtracting the equal-support square Q_2. No support-only positive-semidefinite replacement of Q_1+Q_2 follows from this identity.
3845a81c13f5cf81.proof:
By definition,
sum_u A_u^2
=sum_u sum_{z:u in S(z)}sum_{z':u in S(z')}w_z w_{z'}.
Interchanging the finite sums gives
sum_{z,z'}w_z w_{z'} sum_u 1_{u in S(z) intersect S(z')}
=sum_{z,z'} |S(z) intersect S(z')| w_z w_{z'}.
Pairs with intersection cardinality zero contribute zero, those with cardinality one contribute exactly Q_1, and those with cardinality two contribute twice Q_2. This proves (PF). The definition of R makes its left side ||Rw||_2^2.

The first two identities in (IE) are rearrangements of (PF). Fact c9ed24359b1f5321 gives
Q_2=sum_E W_E^2>=0.
Also the ordered pair partition gives
(sum_z w_z)^2=Q_0+Q_1+Q_2.
Substituting Q_1+Q_2=sum_uA_u^2-Q_2 and rearranging proves the formula for Q_0. Nonnegativity of ||Rw||_2^2 in (PF) gives Q_1>=-2Q_2.

For the four-cycle example, at a the incident weights are w_1+w_4=1-1=0; at b they are w_1+w_2=1-1=0; at c they are w_2+w_3=-1+1=0; and at d they are w_3+w_4=1-1=0. Hence every A_u=0. The four supports are distinct, so fact c9ed24359b1f5321 gives Q_2=sum_iw_i^2=4. Identity (PF) then gives Q_1=-2Q_2=-8. The only disjoint unordered support pairs are (S_1,S_3) and (S_2,S_4); each product of weights is one and each appears in both orders, so Q_0=4. Finally the total weight is zero, and Q_0+Q_1+Q_2=4-8+4=0 agrees with its square.

The final scope statement follows because the exact combined collision form is ||Rw||_2^2-Q_2 and the example makes it negative. Additional arithmetic restrictions could control that difference, but support incidence alone does not make it positive.

glossary.A_u: the aggregate weight of all incidences whose two-element support contains u
glossary.R: the support-incidence operator sending incidence weights to prime-fibre aggregate weights
glossary.S_i: the i-th two-element support in the four-cycle example
glossary.a: the first element in the four-cycle example
glossary.b: the second element in the four-cycle example
glossary.c: the third element in the four-cycle example
glossary.d: the fourth element in the four-cycle example

38816e40c0ab1a02.title: POINTWISE CENTERED-ROW BOUND AND ORDINARY CHARACTER-LARGE-SIEVE NO-FIT ON THE ISOLATED FULL-CONDUCTOR CEN-MZB COMPONENT
38816e40c0ab1a02.author: slava chan
38816e40c0ab1a02.statement:
POINTWISE CENTERED-ROW BOUND AND ORDINARY CHARACTER-LARGE-SIEVE NO-FIT ON THE ISOLATED FULL-CONDUCTOR CEN-MZB COMPONENT.

Assume the actual high-conductor scales and notation of facts 050efa07f87f374a and 14fe68fdcbfd99ff. Thus Q>=2, B=Q^(4/3+o(1)), b in [B,2B) is squarefree, and alpha is supported on a in [Q,2Q) with
  sum_a |alpha_a|^2 <= Q^(1+o(1)).                           (1)

For every active f|b with (f,N)=1 and every (a,b)=1,
  |R_{b,f}(a)| <= f/phi(f) <<_epsilon f^epsilon              (2)
for every fixed epsilon>0.

Restrict now to squarefree b in [B,2B) with (b,N)=1 and isolate only the full-conductor row
  Y_b(alpha)=S_{b,b}(alpha),                                 (3)
  E_fc(alpha)=sum_{B<=b<2B; b squarefree,(b,N)=1}
                   |Y_b(alpha)|^2.                           (4)
For a primitive character psi modulo b, extended by zero to nonunits, define
  A_b(psi;alpha)=sum_{Q<=a<2Q}alpha_a psi(a).                 (5)
Then exactly
  Y_b(alpha)
   =phi(b)^(-1) sum_{psi modulo b primitive}
       overline(psi(N)) tau_b(psi) A_b(psi;alpha),            (6)
and direct Cauchy followed by the ordinary primitive-character large sieve gives
  E_fc(alpha)
   <= C (Q+4B^2) sum_a|alpha_a|^2
   << Q^(11/3+o(1)),                                         (7)
where C is an absolute large-sieve constant.

The direct right side in (7) is larger than the desired CEN-MZB scale Q^(8/3-omega) by Q^(1+omega+o(1)) for every fixed omega>0. Consequently, isolating f=b, applying Cauchy in its primitive characters, and then inserting only the ordinary character large sieve does not supply CEN-MZB.

This last conclusion is solely a no-fit for that direct upper-bound route. It is not a lower bound for E_fc, does not assert that the full-conductor row may be separated from the complete signed centered f-superposition in fact 14fe68fdcbfd99ff, and does not preclude cancellation among conductors before the b-square. No estimate for the complete CEN-MZB operator, C_small, or Goldbach is asserted.
38816e40c0ab1a02.proof:
By fact 14fe68fdcbfd99ff,
  R_{b,f}(a)=product_{p|f}[e_p(N[a(b/p)]^(-1))+1/(p-1)].
For each p|f, the triangle inequality gives
  |e_p(N[a(b/p)]^(-1))+1/(p-1)|
  <=1+1/(p-1)=p/(p-1).
Since f is squarefree, multiplying over p|f gives
  |R_{b,f}(a)|<=product_{p|f}p/(p-1)=f/phi(f).
To prove the second inequality in (2), fix epsilon>0. Choose P_epsilon so that p/(p-1)<=p^epsilon for every prime p>P_epsilon. The product of p/(p-1) over primes p<=P_epsilon is a constant C_epsilon. Splitting the prime divisors of f at P_epsilon gives
  f/phi(f)<=C_epsilon product_{p|f,p>P_epsilon}p^epsilon
            <=C_epsilon f^epsilon.
This proves (2).

Fact 050efa07f87f374a gives, for b=f and (a,b)=1, the exact full-conductor contribution
  R_{b,b}(a)
   =phi(b)^(-1) sum_{psi modulo b primitive}
      overline(psi(N))psi(a)tau_b(psi).
Indeed, in its conductor--cofactor formula the cofactor is b/f=1, while fact 14fe68fdcbfd99ff identifies that conductor contribution with R_{b,b}. Multiply this identity by alpha_a and sum over Q<=a<2Q with (a,b)=1. Since primitive characters are extended by zero to nonunits, the unit restriction can be omitted inside A_b, and (6) follows.

For every primitive psi modulo b in (6), fact 3afa321a72a3612b gives
  |tau_b(psi)|^2=b.
The number of primitive characters modulo b is at most phi(b). Therefore Cauchy's inequality in the primitive characters gives
  |Y_b(alpha)|^2
   <=phi(b)^(-2) phi(b)
      sum_{psi primitive}|tau_b(psi)A_b(psi;alpha)|^2
   =b/phi(b) sum_{psi primitive}|A_b(psi;alpha)|^2.           (8)
Sum (8) over the b in (4) and enlarge the modulus range to all integers b<=2B. Lemma 2.4 of Akbary--Felix, arXiv:1404.5700, states that for coefficients z_n on an interval containing L integers,
  sum_{q<=M} q/phi(q) sum_{chi modulo q primitive}
      |sum_n z_n chi(n)|^2
  <=C(L+M^2)sum_n|z_n|^2.
Apply it with z_a=alpha_a, L<=Q+1, and M=2B. Enlarging C if necessary to absorb the harmless endpoint constant gives
  E_fc(alpha)<=C(Q+4B^2)sum_a|alpha_a|^2,
which is the first inequality in (7).

Finally, (1) and B=Q^(4/3+o(1)) give
  (Q+4B^2)sum_a|alpha_a|^2
  <=Q^(8/3+o(1))Q^(1+o(1))
  =Q^(11/3+o(1)).
The exponent difference from 8/3-omega is
  11/3-(8/3-omega)=1+omega.
Thus this direct large-sieve right side cannot imply CEN-MZB. The argument treated only the isolated summand f=b and used Cauchy before any cancellation with proper divisors f|b, so it establishes exactly the scoped no-fit stated and no broader obstruction.

glossary.A_b(psi;alpha): The multiplicative-character transform of alpha in modulus b.
glossary.E_fc(alpha): The squared l2 norm over b of the isolated full-conductor centered row.
glossary.Y_b(alpha): The isolated full-conductor centered row S_{b,b}(alpha).

38bc0e88e17aef0e.title: UPSTREAM RECIPROCAL-MODULUS MÖBIUS PROVENANCE AND A PRIME-q ACTUAL-SOURCE CRITICAL-CLUSTER SATURATOR
38bc0e88e17aef0e.author: slava chan
38bc0e88e17aef0e.statement:
UPSTREAM RECIPROCAL-MODULUS MÖBIUS PROVENANCE AND A PRIME-q ACTUAL-SOURCE CRITICAL-CLUSTER SATURATOR.

First, let g,q,v be positive squarefree integers and let p be a prime. Assume that g,q,v,p are pairwise coprime, and put
  d=gq,  r=gvp.                                             (1)
Then exactly
  mu(d)mu(r)=-mu(q)mu(v).                                   (2)
Consequently, in the normalized one-rough endpoint obtained from an original double-Möbius coefficient mu(d)mu(r), after the exact outer gcd g and the small factor v are frozen, the reciprocal-modulus q-slot retains the exact factor mu(q). This factor is upstream of any generic bounded-coefficient replacement.

This exact sign by itself does not imply the critical-cluster saving in fact 3b2d15db39ad0217. More precisely, let p tend through sufficiently large primes and put
  Q=floor(p^(4/5)),  V=2,  H=3p/(2Q),  P=3p/4,
  v=2,  n=vp=2p.                                           (3)
Then
  5<=H<=Q^(1/3),  2<=V<H,  P=QH/V,
  P<=p<2P,  gcd(v,p)=1,  p>2Q                              (4)
for all sufficiently large p. Put
  cal P_Q={q:Q<=q<2Q and q is prime}.                       (5)
There is an integer A satisfying
  1<=A<2p,  gcd(A,2p)=1,  A<=Q^2                           (6)
for which the actual source set
  cal X={x=(q,m,k):
          q in cal P_Q, Q<=m<2Q, m is odd,
          k=(A-qm)/(2p) is an integer}                      (7)
has cardinality
  X_src>>Q/(H log Q).                                       (8)
Every x in cal X satisfies
  Q<=q,m<2Q,  qm+nk=A,  gcd(qm,n)=1.                       (9)

For x=(q,m,k) put lambda_x=k/q. There is a subset cal Y of cal X whose slopes are pairwise distinct, all lie in one interval of length at most 1/(12H), and, for every epsilon>0,
  Y:=#cal Y>>_epsilon Q^(1-epsilon)/H.                     (10)
In particular Y>=2 for all sufficiently large p.

Let I be any nonempty integer interval contained either in [H,2H) or in (-2H,-H], and define
  a_h(x)=mu(q)=-1  for h in I and x=(q,m,k) in cal Y.       (11)
Regard cal Y as one nonempty critical cluster in fact 3b2d15db39ad0217. Its critical-cluster ratio satisfies
  Theta_cl>=(Y+1)/(2Y)>=1/2.                               (12)
On the other hand,
  Gadd=VQ^(1/3)/H=4Q^(4/3)/(3p)>>Q^(1/12).                 (13)
Hence the actual source equation, coprimality, natural target bound, source occupancy, pairwise-distinct critical slopes, and the exact upstream reciprocal-modulus Möbius sign do not imply
  Theta_cl<<Gadd^(-1)Q^epsilon                             (14)
for every epsilon>0.

This is a source-specific obstruction only to extracting the missing factor from mu(q) itself. It does not identify (11) with the full literal coefficient c_q nu_h U_ell chi_ell, does not assert that a natural literal mask selects cal Y, and does not exclude cancellation from the remaining smooth, height, projective, or mask factors or from an earlier complete signed assembly. It gives no global lower bound for Aadd, no PMD closure, and no Goldbach conclusion.
38bc0e88e17aef0e.proof:
Because the integers in (1) are squarefree and pairwise coprime,
  mu(d)mu(r)
  =mu(g)mu(q)mu(g)mu(v)mu(p)
  =mu(g)^2mu(q)mu(v)(-1)
  =-mu(q)mu(v),
which proves (2). In the notation of the exact outer-gcd reduction in fact efb6934a518932be, q is the normalized divisor a=d/g and b=r/g=vp. That fact proves on nonzero Möbius support that g,a,b are pairwise coprime and squarefree and that the original coefficient is mu(a)mu(b). Thus (2) is exactly the q-sign provenance asserted here, before any bounded-coefficient theorem is applied.

The scale verification in (4) is the same elementary calculation as follows. For sufficiently large p,
  (1/2)p^(4/5)<=Q<=p^(4/5).
Hence H>=3p^(1/5)/2>=5 and H<=3p^(1/5)<=Q^(1/3), because 1/5<4/15. The remaining equalities follow from (3), while
  3p/4=P<=p<3p/2=2P
and p>2Q for sufficiently large p.

We use the explicit prime-counting inequalities of Dusart, arXiv:1002.0442, theorem labeled Ross:th:pi. For all sufficiently large x they give
  pi(x)>=x/log x (1+1/log x),
  pi(x)<=x/log x (1+1.2762/log x).                         (15)
Applying the lower bound at 2Q and the upper bound at Q, and observing that
  [2Q/log(2Q)]/[Q/log Q] tends to 2,
shows that, for all sufficiently large Q,
  #cal P_Q=pi(2Q-)-pi(Q-)>>Q/log Q.                        (16)
Only this dyadic consequence of the cited theorem is used.

The interval [Q,2Q) contains at least Q/3 odd integers for sufficiently large Q. Every q in cal P_Q is odd and q<2Q<p, and every chosen m is odd with m<2Q<p. Hence q and m are units modulo 2p. Their products occupy the
  phi(2p)=p-1
unit residue classes. By the pigeonhole principle, some unit residue A modulo 2p is represented by
  >>[(Q/log Q)Q]/p
  >>Q^2/(p log Q)
  >>Q/(H log Q)                                             (17)
ordered pairs (q,m). Choose 1<=A<2p in that class. Each represented pair gives a distinct triple in (7), proving (8). The residue A is a unit modulo 2p. Also Q^2>2p for sufficiently large p, so (6) holds. Equations (7) and the unit properties prove (9).

Apply fact 28b8af5697fa64eb with C_A=1. Its condition n>=QH holds because n=2p=(4/3)QH. It covers all slopes by nineteen intervals of length at most 1/(12H), so one contains at least X_src/19 source atoms. Within that interval, fact 2359a25d9fc6dd9b bounds every exact-slope fibre by tau(A). Select one atom from every nonempty fibre and call the result cal Y. Then
  Y>=X_src/[19 tau(A)]
   >>Q/[H(log Q)tau(A)].                                   (18)
Since A<=Q^2, the fixed-power divisor estimate in fact 2359a25d9fc6dd9b gives tau(A)<<_epsilon Q^epsilon. Absorb log Q into an arbitrarily small additional power of Q to obtain (10). Because H<=Q^(1/3), this tends to infinity for a sufficiently small fixed epsilon, so Y>=2 eventually.

Every q in cal Y is prime, hence (11) is the exact Möbius sign and is constant. Multiplying all constant coefficients in the coherent-cluster calculation by -1 does not change any Gram product. Fact 714f3597f5ef527c therefore gives
  sum_{h in I}sum_{x_1 not equal x_2 in cal Y}
    a_h(x_1)conjugate(a_h(x_2))
    e(h[lambda_{x_1}-lambda_{x_2}])
  >=(#I/2)Y(Y-1).                                         (19)
Adding the #I times Y diagonal terms gives
  E_cl>=(#I/2)Y(Y+1),
whereas W_cl=(#I)Y^2. Division proves (12).

Finally, (3) gives the equality in (13). The bounds
  Q>=(1/2)p^(4/5),  Q<=p^(4/5)
give
  Gadd>=c p^(1/15)>=cQ^(1/12)
for an absolute c>0. If (14) followed uniformly from the listed properties for every epsilon>0, choose epsilon<1/12. Equations (12)-(13) would force a fixed positive number to tend to zero, a contradiction. This proves the stated obstruction. Since the construction imposed only the Möbius factor and selected cal Y existentially, none of the stronger literal or global conclusions excluded in the statement has been used.

glossary.cal P_Q: The set of prime reciprocal moduli q in the dyadic interval [Q,2Q).
glossary.prime-q Möbius saturator: An actual-source critical cluster supported on prime q-values, on which the exact upstream factor mu(q) is constant.

39071136bb037885.title: FIXED-POWER PAYMENT OF THE LARGE CROSS-GCD SUBRANGE IN BOTH DYADIC CROSS-INCIDENCE ARRAYS
39071136bb037885.author: slava chan
39071136bb037885.statement:
FIXED-POWER PAYMENT OF THE LARGE CROSS-GCD SUBRANGE IN BOTH DYADIC CROSS-INCIDENCE ARRAYS.

Let Q tend to infinity, put
 U=Q^(1/3), B=Q^(4/3+o(1)),
and let cal B be a set of squarefree integers in [B,2B). Let gamma_b be complex numbers satisfying
 sum_{b in cal B}|gamma_b|^2<=1.                            (1)
Fix 1<=P<=Q. For every prime p in [P,2P), let cal B_1(p),cal B_2(p) be subsets of cal B such that every b in either set is divisible by p. Assume that the sets cal B_1(p) are disjoint as p varies and that every b belongs to at most Q^(o(1)) sets cal B_2(p). For b_i in cal B_i(p) put
 s_1=b_1/p, q_2=b_2/p, g_{12}=(s_1,q_2).                   (2)

For each of at most two labels tau and each positive a<=2U, let beta_{tau,a}(u) be supported on
 cal U_a={u:Q<=au<2Q}
and satisfy |beta_{tau,a}(u)|<=Q^epsilon for every epsilon>0. (3)
Let cal Z^0 and cal Z^R be kernels supported on
 (au_1,b_1)=(au_2,b_2)=1
and satisfying respectively
 |cal Z^0_{a,u_1,u_2;b_1,b_2}|<=Q^epsilon,                 (4)
 |cal Z^R_{a,u_1,u_2;b_1,b_2}|
 <=Q^epsilon{1_{u_1s_1 congruent u_2q_2 modulo p}+1/p}.     (5)
For G>=1 define
 cal K_j(P,G)
 =sum_tau sum_{a<=2U}sum_{u_1,u_2 in cal U_a}
   sum_{P<=p<2P}
   sum_{substack{b_i in cal B_i(p)\g_{12}>=G}}
 beta_{tau,a}(u_1)overline(beta_{tau,a}(u_2))
 overline(gamma_{b_1})gamma_{b_2}
 cal Z^j_{a,u_1,u_2;b_1,b_2},                              (6)
where j is 0 or R. Then
 |cal K_0(P,G)|<<Q^(epsilon+o(1)) BQ^2/(PG),                (7)
 |cal K_R(P,G)|
 <<Q^(epsilon+o(1))B{Q^2/(P^2G)+Qlog Q/(PG)}.              (8)

Fix 0<delta<1 and put
 G_0=Q^(1+delta)/P,
 G_R=max{1,Q^(1+delta)/P^2}.                               (9)
Then G_0>=1 and
 |cal K_0(P,G_0)|<<Q^(7/3-delta+epsilon+o(1)),              (10)
 |cal K_R(P,G_R)|<<Q^(7/3-delta+epsilon+o(1)).              (11)

In the literal arrays of fact b9560e346963b9e0, restrict to an actual tensor coefficient of fact 050efa07f87f374a and take cal B_1(p)={b:pi(b)=p}, cal B_2(p)={b:p|s(b)}. The exact K_inc^main restricted to one dyadic p-block is an instance of cal K_0, and the exact K_inc^rem is an instance of cal K_R. Hence (10) pays every actual main pair with
 (s_1,q_2)>=Q^(1+delta)/P.
Equation (11) pays every actual remainder pair with
 (s_1,q_2)>=max{1,Q^(1+delta)/P^2};
when Q^(1+delta)/P^2<1 this condition includes every pair. Neither application changes either literal beta family, either gamma coefficient, the congruence A=D, or any row tensor.

No estimate for the complementary small-cross-gcd arrays, the whole of K_inc^main or K_inc^rem, another incidence cell, C_small or Goldbach is asserted.
39071136bb037885.proof:
Partition the pairs in (6) by the exact value g=g_{12}. For fixed p,g put
 G_i(p,g)^2
 =sum_{substack{b in cal B_i(p)\g|b/p}}|gamma_b|^2.        (12)
Every b counted here is divisible by pg. Since b<2B,
 #{b in cal B_i(p):g|b/p}<=3B/(pg)                         (13)
whenever the set is nonempty. Cauchy's inequality and (13) give
 sum_{substack{b_i in cal B_i(p)\(b_1/p,b_2/p)=g}}
 |gamma_{b_1}gamma_{b_2}|
 <=3B G_1(p,g)G_2(p,g)/(pg).                               (14)

We sum (14) over p and g>=G. The first-row p-blocks are disjoint, and for each b the possible g in (12) are divisors of b/p. Thus
 sum_{p,g}G_1(p,g)^2<=Q^(o(1)).                             (15)
On row two, each b belongs to at most Q^(o(1)) p-blocks by hypothesis, and again g is a divisor of b/p. Hence
 sum_{p,g}G_2(p,g)^2<=Q^(o(1)).                             (16)
Using p>=P, g>=G, and Cauchy's inequality in (p,g), equations (14)--(16) yield
 sum_{substack{p,b_1,b_2\g_{12}>=G}}
 |gamma_{b_1}gamma_{b_2}|
 <<Q^(o(1))B/(PG).                                         (17)

Put V_a=#cal U_a<=2Q/a. For the bounded kernel (4), there are at most V_a^2 pairs u_1,u_2. Apply (3), (4), and (17), then use
 sum_{a<=2U}V_a^2<<Q^2.
This proves (7).

For (5), the squarefree factors s_1,q_2 are units modulo p on the displayed support. For each u_1 the congruence in (5) selects at most V_a/p+1 values of u_2. Therefore its number of solutions is at most
 V_a^2/p+V_a.                                              (18)
The separate 1/p term contributes V_a^2/p. Combine (17)--(18), use p>=P, and use
 sum_aV_a^2<<Q^2, sum_aV_a<<Qlog Q.
This proves (8).

Since P<=Q, G_0>=Q^delta>=1. Insert G_0 in (7) to obtain (10). If Q^(1+delta)/P^2>=1, insert that value in (8). The first term is BQ^(1-delta), and the second is BPQ^(-delta+o(1))<=BQ^(1-delta+o(1)), proving (11) in this case.

If Q^(1+delta)/P^2<1, then G_R=1 and P^2>Q^(1+delta). Equation (8) gives a first term
 BQ^2/P^2<BQ^(1-delta).
Its second term is BQ/P. Since P>Q^((1+delta)/2) and 0<delta<1,
 BQ/P<=BQ^((1-delta)/2)<BQ^(1-delta).
Thus (11) also holds in this case.

For the literal application, the disjointness of cal B_1(p) is immediate from the uniqueness of pi(b). Fact a4c3df18327fbfb1 proves that each literal row-two b belongs to at most three relevant p-blocks in the actual incidence range. For actual tensor coefficients from fact 050efa07f87f374a, it also proves the beta bounds and the kernel bound (5) for K_inc^rem. The tensor divisor bounds in the same fact show that each of the two K_inc^main local expressions is Q^(epsilon+o(1)), proving (4) for their sum. Thus all hypotheses apply coefficientwise to the exact actual arrays, completing the proof and scope statement.

glossary.cal K_0(P,G): a bounded-kernel dyadic cross-incidence array restricted by g_{12}>=G
glossary.cal K_R(P,G): a Gram-plus-1/p dyadic cross-incidence array restricted by g_{12}>=G

391896a807980083.title: ONE-SIDED HUANG--VAUGHAN IDENTITY, COLLAPSED \(B_X\) COEFFICIENT, AND THE EXACT ULTRA-LONG/ENDPOINT COMPLEMENT
391896a807980083.author: slava chan
391896a807980083.statement:
ONE-SIDED HUANG--VAUGHAN IDENTITY, COLLAPSED \(B_X\) COEFFICIENT, AND THE EXACT ULTRA-LONG/ENDPOINT COMPLEMENT.

Let \(X\ge1\) be real. For every integer \(n>X\), define
\[
 A_X(r)=-\mu(r)\mathbf 1_{r\le X},                           \tag{1}
\]
and
\[
 B_X(r)=\sum_{\substack{dm=r\\d>1,\ m>X}}\mu(d)\mu(m).       \tag{2}
\]
Then the specialization \(U=X,V=1\) of Huang's restricted Vaughan
identity gives exactly
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \mu(n)=\sum_{rw=n}A_X(r)+\sum_{rw=n}B_X(r).
 \quad}                                                     \tag{3}
\]
Expanding (2), writing \(n=dmw\), and putting \(t=dw\) gives
\[
 \sum_{rw=n}B_X(r)
 =\sum_{\substack{dmw=n\\d>1,\ m>X}}\mu(d)\mu(m)
 =-\sum_{\substack{mt=n\\m>X,\ t>1}}\mu(m).                 \tag{4}
\]
Thus (3) is equivalently the exact one-sided identity
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \mu(n)
 =-\sum_{\substack{rw=n\\r\le X}}\mu(r)
  -\sum_{\substack{mt=n\\m>X,\ t>1}}\mu(m).
 \quad}                                                     \tag{5}
\]
For every fixed positive integer \(g\), multiplying (3)--(5) by
\(\mathbf1_{(n,g)=1}\) is exact; in the \(rw\)-rows this condition is
\((r,g)=(w,g)=1\), and in the \(mt\)-rows it is
\((m,g)=(t,g)=1\). No factor of the reciprocal-modulus Möbius coefficient
is expanded.

Now let
\[
 \beta_m<\beta<6/5,\qquad B=Q^\beta,
\]
fix \(0<\tau<1/100\) sufficiently small, and put
\[
 a=2\beta-2+\tau,\qquad b=3-2\beta-\tau,\qquad
 X=Q^{\,b-\tau}=Q^{3-2\beta-2\tau}.                         \tag{6}
\]
For sufficiently large \(Q\),
\[
 0<a<b,\qquad Q^a<X<Q^b,\qquad X<B/2.                       \tag{7}
\]
Restrict \(n\) to the exact source interval
\[
 B/2\le n\le2B.                                             \tag{8}
\]
Call a \(B_X\)-tuple in (4) clean if at least one of \(m,t\) lies in
\[
 Q^a\le S\le Q^b.                                           \tag{9}
\]
Then the complement of the clean tuples in the second sum of (5) is
exactly the disjoint union
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 {\rm ULTRA\hbox{-}LONG\hbox{-}MU\hbox{-}N}:&
 \qquad m>Q^b,\quad 1<t<Q^a,\\
 {\rm ENDPOINT\hbox{-}DIAGONAL\hbox{-}N}:&
 \qquad m>Q^b,\quad t>Q^b.
 \end{aligned}}                                             \tag{10}
\]
There is no additional EXTREME-\(N\) class. On ULTRA-LONG-MU-\(N\),
\[
