 m>{B\over2Q^a}
 ={1\over2}Q^{\,2-\beta-\tau}
 >Q^{\,4/5-\tau-\zeta}                                     \tag{11}
\]
for every fixed \(\zeta>0\) and sufficiently large \(Q\). The
ENDPOINT-DIAGONAL-\(N\) class can be nonempty only if
\[
 \beta>{6\over5}-{2\tau\over5}-{\log2\over5\log Q}.          \tag{12}
\]

In the full-modulus source normal form of fact
\(b0a38f5e9ae7feb6\), (5) is applied only to the restored \(n\)-side
factor \(\mu(n)\mathbf1_{(n,g)=1}\). The coefficient
\(\mu(s)\mathbf1_{(s,g)=1}\) on the original reciprocal modulus
\(s\asymp Q\), the fixed possibly nonunit target
\(-\epsilon L_{\rm src}\), the source amplitude and every explicit
pre-marker selector remain untouched. After legal dyadic/projective
separation, every clean \(B_X\) row has the no-\((m,t)\)-condition
two-factor coefficient class and factor window accepted by fact
\(f7b5ba9fa0d6cfc8\). This last sentence is an exact interface
identification, not an estimate for the complete source: it does not
assert that an arbitrary surviving pre-marker selector is projectively
separable, does not pay the \(A_X\) rows or either class in (10), and
does not sum outer-\(g\) layers.
391896a807980083.proof:
Bingrong Huang, arXiv:1412.2237, Lemma 3.5, states
that for \(U,V\ge1\) and \(n>\max(U,V)\),
\[
 \mu(n)
 =-\sum_{\substack{lmd=n\\1\le d\le V\\1\le m\le U}}
   \mu(d)\mu(m)
 +\sum_{\substack{lmd=n\\d>V\\m>U}}\mu(d)\mu(m).             \tag{13}
\]
Take \(U=X,V=1\). In the first sum \(d=1\); putting \(r=m,w=l\)
gives
\[
 -\sum_{\substack{rw=n\\r\le X}}\mu(r)
 =\sum_{rw=n}A_X(r).
\]
In the second sum put \(r=dm,w=l\); its coefficient at fixed \(r\) is
exactly (2). This proves (3).

To prove (4), expand the finite sums and put \(t=dw\):
\[
 \sum_{\substack{dmw=n\\d>1,\ m>X}}\mu(d)\mu(m)
 =\sum_{\substack{mt=n\\m>X}}\mu(m)
   \sum_{\substack{d\mid t\\d>1}}\mu(d).
\]
For \(t=1\) the inner sum is empty. For \(t>1\),
\[
 \sum_{\substack{d\mid t\\d>1}}\mu(d)
 =\sum_{d\mid t}\mu(d)-1=-1.
\]
This proves (4), hence (5). If \(rw=n\), then
\((n,g)=1\) is equivalent to \((r,g)=(w,g)=1\); the corresponding
equivalence for \(mt=n\) is identical. This proves the fixed-core
statement.

We verify (7). Since \(\beta<6/5\) and \(\tau<1/100\),
\[
 b-a=5-4\beta-2\tau>1/5-2\tau>0.
\]
Also \(b-\tau-a=5-4\beta-3\tau>1/5-3\tau>0\), while
\(b-(b-\tau)=\tau>0\). Finally
\[
 \beta-(b-\tau)=3\beta-3+2\tau>0
\]
because \(\beta>\beta_m>1\). Thus \(X/B\) tends to zero by a fixed
power, proving \(X<B/2\) for sufficiently large \(Q\).

Consider a tuple in the second sum of (5). It has \(m>X>Q^a\).
If \(m\le Q^b\), it is clean. Hence every nonclean tuple has \(m>Q^b\).
For such a tuple, it is clean precisely when \(Q^a\le t\le Q^b\).
Because \(t>1\), failure of this condition is exactly either
\(1<t<Q^a\) or \(t>Q^b\). These cases are disjoint and give (10).
Thus no third residual class exists.

On the first class in (10), (8) and \(mt=n\) give
\[
 m={n\over t}>{B\over2Q^a}
 ={1\over2}Q^{\beta-(2\beta-2+\tau)}
 ={1\over2}Q^{2-\beta-\tau},
\]
which is the first part of (11). Since \(\beta<6/5\),
\(2-\beta-\tau>4/5-\tau\); a fixed factor \(1/2\) is absorbed by
\(Q^\zeta\) for sufficiently large \(Q\), proving the last inequality.

On the second class in (10),
\[
 n=mt>Q^{2b}.
\]
Together with \(n\le2Q^\beta\), this gives
\[
 Q^{2(3-2\beta-\tau)}<2Q^\beta.
\]
Taking logarithms and rearranging proves (12).

Finally, fact \(b0a38f5e9ae7feb6\) places the literal
\(\mu(n)\mathbf1_{(n,g)=1}\) in a reciprocal phase modulo the untouched
\(s\asymp Q\). Substitution of (5) changes only that \(n\)-coefficient.
In the \(mt\)-form, the source gate \((n,s)=1\) becomes \((mt,s)=1\),
and the fixed-core gate separates as already proved. The \(m\)-coefficient
is Möbius and the \(t\)-coefficient is the bounded constant \(-1\) on
\(t>1\). Fact \(f7b5ba9fa0d6cfc8\) explicitly permits either the
condition \((m,t)=1\) or no condition between the factors, and it assumes
only \(G>0\). Its full four-term conclusion is therefore the correct
analytic interface for these unrestricted clean rows. Condition (9) is
its clean factor window because \(H_T=B/Q=Q^{\beta-1}\). No use of the
more restrictive coprime corollary \(2b4989d9d25f33cc\) is made.

glossary.ENDPOINT-DIAGONAL-N: The exact B_X residual with m>Q^b and t>Q^b.
glossary.ULTRA-LONG-MU-N: The exact B_X residual with m>Q^b and 1<t<Q^a after t=dw.

397f417416c4cb9d.title: Let r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4 be pairwise distinct odd primes, put G=r_1r_2 and T=r_3r_4, and let I_1,I_2,I_3,I_4 be finite subsets of the integers. Assume the literal-window shortness conditions
397f417416c4cb9d.author: slava chan
397f417416c4cb9d.statement:
Let r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4 be pairwise distinct odd primes, put G=r_1r_2 and T=r_3r_4, and let I_1,I_2,I_3,I_4 be finite subsets of the integers. Assume the literal-window shortness conditions
|b_1r_2+b_2r_1|<G/2 and |b_1r_2-b_2r_1|<G/2
for every b_1 in I_1 and b_2 in I_2, and
|b_3r_4-b_4r_3|<T/2
for every b_3 in I_3 and b_4 in I_4.
Let <x>_m denote the unique integer in (-m/2,m/2] congruent to the integer x modulo the positive integer m. Let zeta_G be the unique residue class modulo G satisfying zeta_G congruent to 1 modulo r_1 and zeta_G congruent to -1 modulo r_2. Let eta_T be the unique residue class modulo T satisfying eta_T congruent to 1 modulo r_3 and eta_T congruent to -1 modulo r_4.

For an integer C define
B_C=<C T^{-1}>_G,
z_C=<B_C zeta_G>_G,
D_C=(C-B_CT)/G,
w_C=<C G^{-1}eta_T>_T,
where the inverses exist because gcd(G,T)=1. Then the following are equivalent.

(I) There is a quadruple (b_1,b_2,b_3,b_4) in I_1 times I_2 times I_3 times I_4 such that, on defining
B=b_1r_2+b_2r_1, z=b_1r_2-b_2r_1,
D=b_3r_4+b_4r_3, w=b_3r_4-b_4r_3,
one has C=BT+GD.

(II) One has B_C congruent to z_C modulo 2 and D_C congruent to w_C modulo 2, and the four integers
b_1^*=(B_C+z_C)/(2r_2),
b_2^*=(B_C-z_C)/(2r_1),
b_3^*=(D_C+w_C)/(2r_4),
b_4^*=(D_C-w_C)/(2r_3)
belong respectively to I_1,I_2,I_3,I_4.

When these conditions hold, the quadruple in (I) is unique and equals (b_1^*,b_2^*,b_3^*,b_4^*). Thus, for a fixed ordered prime quadruple and carrier C, the literal parity-and-window three-gate test is exactly equivalent to the existence of the corresponding literal packet; it is not a majorization.

If the two primes inside G are regarded as unordered, reversing their orientation replaces zeta_G and z_C by their negatives and interchanges b_1^* and b_2^*. Reversing the orientation inside T similarly negates eta_T and w_C and interchanges b_3^* and b_4^*. Consequently forgetting both internal orientations has multiplicity at most four.
397f417416c4cb9d.proof:
The Chinese remainder theorem gives zeta_G and eta_T uniquely. Pairwise distinctness of the four primes gives gcd(G,T)=1, so the two inverses in the definitions exist. Also C-B_CT is divisible by G by the definition of B_C, so D_C is an integer.

Assume (I). Reducing C=BT+GD modulo G gives C T^{-1} congruent to B modulo G. The window shortness hypothesis places B strictly inside (-G/2,G/2), so B_C=B. Modulo r_1, the definitions of B and z give B congruent to b_1r_2 and z congruent to b_1r_2, while zeta_G is congruent to 1. Modulo r_2, they give B congruent to b_2r_1 and z congruent to -b_2r_1, while zeta_G is congruent to -1. Therefore z congruent to B zeta_G modulo both r_1 and r_2, hence modulo G. Window shortness places z strictly inside (-G/2,G/2), so z_C=z. It follows from C=BT+GD and B_C=B that D_C=D.

Reducing C=BT+GD modulo T and multiplying by G^{-1}eta_T gives C G^{-1}eta_T congruent to D eta_T modulo T. Modulo r_3, D congruent to b_3r_4 and eta_T congruent to 1, while w congruent to b_3r_4. Modulo r_4, D congruent to b_4r_3 and eta_T congruent to -1, while w congruent to -b_4r_3. Hence w congruent to D eta_T modulo T. The window shortness hypothesis places w strictly inside (-T/2,T/2), so w_C=w. The identities
B+z=2b_1r_2, B-z=2b_2r_1,
D+w=2b_3r_4, D-w=2b_4r_3
show the two parity congruences and show that the recovered integers in (II) are the original b_i. Thus (II) holds.

Conversely assume (II). The congruence z_C congruent to B_C zeta_G modulo G implies z_C congruent to B_C modulo r_1 and z_C congruent to -B_C modulo r_2. Therefore r_1 divides B_C-z_C and r_2 divides B_C+z_C. The parity hypothesis says that 2 divides both numerators. Since r_1 and r_2 are odd, the displayed b_1^* and b_2^* are integers. Their definitions give
b_1^*r_2+b_2^*r_1=B_C and
b_1^*r_2-b_2^*r_1=z_C.
Similarly, w_C congruent to D_C eta_T modulo T implies w_C congruent to D_C modulo r_3 and w_C congruent to -D_C modulo r_4. The second parity hypothesis and oddness of the primes show that b_3^*,b_4^* are integers, and their definitions give
b_3^*r_4+b_4^*r_3=D_C and
b_3^*r_4-b_4^*r_3=w_C.
Membership in the four windows is assumed in (II). Finally the definition of D_C rearranges to C=B_CT+GD_C. Thus the recovered quadruple satisfies (I).

The four linear recovery formulas show uniqueness: any quadruple in (I) produces B_C,z_C,D_C,w_C by the already proved forward direction and is therefore equal to the displayed recovered quadruple.

If r_1 and r_2 and their window labels are interchanged, the two Chinese remainder signs defining zeta_G are interchanged, so the new involution is -zeta_G modulo G. The symmetric quantity B_C is unchanged and z_C changes sign. Substitution in the recovery formulas interchanges the first two recovered integers. The same calculation for r_3,r_4 negates eta_T and w_C and interchanges the last two recovered integers. Each of the two semiprimes therefore has at most two orientations, giving total multiplicity at most 2 times 2=4.

glossary.B_C: the centered first semiprime carrier coordinate recovered from C
glossary.D_C: the integral second semiprime carrier coordinate recovered from C and B_C
glossary.I_1: the literal integer frequency window attached to r_1
glossary.I_2: the literal integer frequency window attached to r_2
glossary.I_3: the literal integer frequency window attached to r_3
glossary.I_4: the literal integer frequency window attached to r_4
glossary.b_1^*: the first frequency recovered from the parity-and-window gate
glossary.b_2^*: the second frequency recovered from the parity-and-window gate
glossary.b_3^*: the third frequency recovered from the parity-and-window gate
glossary.b_4^*: the fourth frequency recovered from the parity-and-window gate
glossary.eta_T: the oriented nontrivial CRT involution modulo T
glossary.w_C: the centered mixed-root coordinate on T recovered from C
glossary.z_C: the centered mixed-root coordinate on G recovered from C
glossary.zeta_G: the oriented nontrivial CRT involution modulo G

3a07e1cfd1359c45.title: SAFE SECOND-BUFFER COMPLETE-FREQUENCY FIVE-ANATOMY TRACE PALETTE
3a07e1cfd1359c45.author: slava chan
3a07e1cfd1359c45.statement:
SAFE SECOND-BUFFER COMPLETE-FREQUENCY FIVE-ANATOMY TRACE PALETTE.

Fix integers \(J,C_A,K\ge1\), a constant \(C\ge1\), and
\(0<\kappa\le1/100\).  Put
\[
 \sigma=\kappa/100,\qquad \rho=\sigma/5,qquad
 \beta_2=\beta_m-\rho=6/5-13\sigma/5,
 \qquad \beta_m=6/5-12\sigma/5.
\]
Let \(Q\) be sufficiently large, \(1\le\beta\le\beta_2\), and put
\[
 B=Q^\beta,\quad H_T=B/Q,\quad
 L=H_TQ^\sigma,\quad S_0=H_T^2Q^{3\sigma},\quad
 Z=Q^{3/2-\beta-3\sigma}.
\]
Let \(G>0\) and \(H_P=H_T/G\).  Use actual dyadic integer-frequency
blocks \(F\ge1\), the literal prefactor \(H_P^{-1}\), and scalar
Fourier weights satisfying arbitrary fixed-order decay in \(F/H_P\).
Allow a fixed nonzero possibly nonunit reciprocal target of size at most a
fixed power of \(Q\), unrestricted gcd of the frequency with the modulus,
and the coefficient, coprimality, smooth/projective, ordering, equality,
collision and provenance hypotheses in the exact definitions of the five
complete traces below.

The following five conclusions hold with fixed positive saving exponents.

(A) For the target-gcd-descended interval-prime trace \(T_A\) defined
exactly as \(T_c\) in fact \(6ca1f83e2233669a\), including the sum over
squarefree target divisors \(c\le H_TQ^{\sigma/4}\), primes in
\((L,Z)\), and all its deletion masks,
\[
 \sum_c|T_A(c)|\ll GQ^{2-\delta_{A,F}}\quad(G\ge1),
\]
and, for each fixed \(0<\eta<\sigma\),
\[
 \sum_c|T_A(c)|\ll Q^{2-\delta_{A,N}}
 \quad\bigl(Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\le G\le Q^{\sigma-\eta}\bigr).
                                                                    \tag{1}
\]

(B) For the complete raised-stopping trace \(T_B\), with the exact
coefficient \(\Gamma_{k;L,S_0}\) and hypotheses of fact
\(df4b02d6fa1181f0\),
\[
 T_B\ll GQ^{2-\delta_{B,F}}\quad(G\ge1),\qquad
 T_B\ll Q^{2-\delta_{B,N}}
 \quad\bigl(Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\le G\le Q^{\sigma-\eta}\bigr).
                                                                    \tag{2}
\]

(C1) For the complete one-rough-prime trace \(T_{C1}\) of fact
\(76040270e1ddf949\), with \(v\le S_0\), all prime factors of \(v\)
at most \(L\), and one prime \(p\ge Z\),
\[
 T_{C1}\ll GQ^{2-\delta_{C1,F}}\quad(G\ge1),\qquad
 T_{C1}\ll Q^{2-\delta_{C1,N}}
 \quad\bigl(Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\le G\le Q^{\sigma-\eta}\bigr).
                                                                    \tag{3}
\]
The same bounds hold for the separated-outer variant of fact
\(d399d1df6821854c\), where the factor \(v\) is only divisor-bounded and
is assumed termwise coprime to the final prime.

(C2) For the complete two-rough-prime trace \(T_{C2}\) of fact
\(989b464fc741150b\), including both prime orderings, equal prime-scale
cells and the repeated-prime diagonal created by exact symmetrization,
\[
 T_{C2}\ll GQ^{2-\delta_{C2,F}}\quad(G\ge1),\qquad
 T_{C2}\ll Q^{2-\delta_{C2,N}}
 \quad\bigl(Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\le G\le Q^{\sigma-\eta}\bigr).
                                                                    \tag{4}
\]

(C3) For the complete three-rough-prime trace \(T_{C3}\) of fact
\(73b711f7dea1a0ee\), including all prime-slot permutations, equal cells,
and pair- and triple-collision terms from exact symmetrization,
\[
 T_{C3}\ll GQ^{2-\delta_{C3,F}}\quad(G\ge1),\qquad
 T_{C3}\ll Q^{2-\delta_{C3,N}}
 \quad\bigl(Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\le G\le Q^{\sigma-\eta}\bigr).
                                                                    \tag{5}
\]

Every conclusion includes \(H_P<1\) and every actual frequency block.
Uniformly many inherited frozen source, fixed-\(U\), high, parent,
orientation, sign, target-gcd, prime-order, collision, deletion and
provenance labels are permitted exactly to the extent stated in the
corresponding trace definition; no arbitrary joint deletion mask is added.
The theorem is a local reciprocal-trace palette only.  It makes no
outer-\(g\) assembly, selected-negative handoff, assertion at
\(\beta>\beta_2\), general-marker, endpoint, PMD, DCE, or Goldbach
claim.
3a07e1cfd1359c45.proof:
We repeat the beta-dependent parts of the five accepted proofs; none
of their conclusions is invoked beyond its stated \(\beta_1\)-range.  The
single new endpoint identity is
\[
 6-5\beta\ge 6-5\beta_2=13\sigma,                               \tag{6}
\]
while the standard marker has the strict endpoint margin
\[
 \log_Q(Z^4/B)=6-5\beta-12\sigma\ge\sigma.                     \tag{7}
\]
All fixed dyadic endpoint errors are absorbed by taking \(Q\) sufficiently
large.

For (A), the target-gcd descent of fact \(6ca1f83e2233669a\) only needs
the following beta-dependent checks.  If \(q_0=Q/c\) and
\(c\le H_TQ^{\sigma/4}\), then
\[
 q_0\ge Q^{2-\beta-\sigma/4}
      \ge Q^{4/5+47\sigma/20}.
\]
Also \(U_c\ll Q^{1-\sigma}\), so \(U_c<q_0^2\).  The identity
\(H_TZ=Q^{1/2-3\sigma}\) is unchanged.  On the analytic frequency
range, the four descended terms relative to \(GQ^2\), respectively to
\(Q^2\), have the same first, second and fourth savings as in the accepted
proof.  The only beta-dependent fourth baseline is
\[
 Q^{7/4}H_T/Q^2=Q^{\beta-5/4}
 \le Q^{-1/20-13\sigma/5}.                                      \tag{8}
\]
The determinant inequalities are stronger: for example
\[
 {q_0\over H_PY_c}\ge
 GQ^{3/2-\beta+11\sigma/4}
 \ge GQ^{3/10+107\sigma/20}.
\]
The complementary frequency tail is summed by choosing the available fixed
decay order after using \(H_T\le Q^{1/5-13\sigma/5}\).
Thus the exact proof of the two estimates in (1), including the divisor sum
over \(c\), goes through with new fixed savings.

For (B), first
\[
 \log_Q(Z/L)=5/2-2\beta-4\sigma
 \ge1/10+6\sigma/5>0,
quad
 \log_Q(B/S_0)=2-\beta-3\sigma\ge4/5-2\sigma/5>0.
\]
Together with (7), this verifies the exact stopping identity.  Its stopping
factor scale \(Y\) satisfies
\[
 H_T^2Q^{2\sigma}\le Y\le Q^{1-2\sigma}/H_T^2,
\]
because the upper-window logarithmic gap is
\[
 6-5\beta-6\sigma\ge7\sigma.                                   \tag{9}
\]
The four complete-frequency energy ratios are consequently, exactly as in
the proof of \(df4b02d6fa1181f0\),
\[
 G^{-3/4}Q^{-\sigma/2}, G^{-3/4}Q^{-\sigma/2}, G^{-1}Q^{-\sigma}, G^{-1}Q^{\beta-5/4}
\]
in the full-\(G\) regime, and the corresponding ratios without the
negative powers of \(G\) in the near-balanced regime.  Equation (8) and
\(G^{1/4}\le Q^{(\sigma-\eta)/4}\) give fixed savings.  Arbitrary
fixed-order decay sums the actual \(F\)-blocks, including \(H_P<1\).
This proves (2).

For (C1), write \(\nu=\log V/\log Q\), so
\(0\le\nu\le2\beta-2+3\sigma\).  The proper-prime-power correction
has size at most
\[
 Q^{3\beta/2+3\sigma/2+\epsilon}
 \le Q^{9/5-12\sigma/5+\epsilon}.                               \tag{10}
\]
After Vaughan decomposition, the three beta-dependent grouping margins
used in the Type-II and long Type-I branches become
\[
 {6-5\beta\over3}-4\sigma\ge\sigma/3,qquad
 {6-5\beta-11\sigma\over2}\ge\sigma,qquad
 6-5\beta-8\sigma\ge5\sigma.                                   \tag{11}
\]
The remaining Type-I comparison
\[
 5/2-2\beta-7\sigma\ge1/10-9\sigma/5
\]
is positive because \(\sigma\le10^{-4}\), and its complementary lower
margin is larger than a fixed absolute constant.  After dyadic endpoint
absorption, every correlated box therefore still supplies a factor
\[
 H_T^2Q^{3\sigma}\le S\le Q^{1-3\sigma}/H_T^2.                 \tag{12}
\]
The four energy baselines and their frequency-ratio costs are unchanged;
(12) gives fixed savings, and the near-balanced factor \(G^{1/4}\) uses
only part of them.  The short Type-I branch has coefficient scale at most
\(Q^{1/2-3\sigma}\); its multiplier-one bound is
\[
 Q^\epsilon\{B+Q^{3/2}Q^{1/2-3\sigma}\}
 \ll Q^{2-3\sigma+\epsilon},
\]
because \(B\le Q^{\beta_2}<Q^{6/5}\).  Also
\(H_P\le Q^{\beta-1+\sigma-\eta}<Q^{1/4}\), so the remaining large
actual frequencies are absolutely paid by Fourier decay.  This proves
(3).  The separated-outer proof uses only \(V\le S_0\), divisor bounds,
and termwise coprimality with the final prime after its opening comparison;
hence the identical renewed audit proves its extension too.

For (C2), retain the three exhaustive grouping cases of
\(989b464fc741150b\).  In the small grouped-factor case, separation from
the final prime has exponent
\[
 4-3\beta-6\sigma\ge2/5+9\sigma/5.
\]
In the two correlated cases the only endpoint margins are
\[
 6-5\beta-8\sigma\ge5\sigma,qquad
 {6-5\beta-11\sigma\over2}\ge\sigma.                          \tag{13}
\]
Thus the same correlated window
\[
 H_T^2Q^{2\sigma}\le S\le Q^{1-3\sigma}/H_T^2
\]
holds.  Its four baselines retain the accepted fixed savings in both
\(G\)-regimes.  Exact equal-cell symmetrization creates only the
repeated-prime diagonal
\[
 QB/Z=Q^{2\beta-1/2+3\sigma}
 \le Q^{19/10-11\sigma/5},                                       \tag{14}
\]
which is power-small.  This proves (4), including both orderings and all
actual frequency blocks.

For (C3), write the three rough-prime exponents as \(a_i\).  For every
\(i\), the accepted upper grouping comparison now has margin
\[
 6-5\beta-10\sigma\ge3\sigma.                                 \tag{15}
\]
The averaging lower comparison has margin
\[
 {6-5\beta-6\sigma\over3}\ge7\sigma/3.                        \tag{16}
\]
After absorbing the fixed product-constant error, some \(VP_i\) therefore
lies in
\[
 H_T^2Q^\sigma\le VP_i\le Q^{1-3\sigma}/H_T^2.                 \tag{17}
\]
The four correlated-energy baselines derived from (17) save respectively
\(\sigma/4,3\sigma/4,\sigma/2,\sigma\); in the near-balanced regime
the first loses only \((\sigma-\eta)/4\), leaving \(\eta/4\).
All frequency ratios are summable by fixed-order decay.  Pair and triple
collisions have the same bound (14).  Finally (7), together with
\(L<Z\), \(B>S_0\), and squarefreeness, verifies the literal C3 marker
coefficient through the new endpoint.  This proves (5).

The accepted proofs already show that the listed label families cost only
polylogarithmic factors and that their permitted restrictions enter as
one-variable coefficients, label scalars, or uniformly bounded projective
amplitudes.  Shrinking the minimum of the displayed positive margins absorbs
those factors.  No assertion outside the five renewed local trace
definitions has been used.

glossary.T_A: The complete target-gcd-descended interval-prime reciprocal trace in clause (A).
glossary.T_B: The complete raised-stopping reciprocal trace in clause (B).
glossary.T_C1: The complete one-rough-prime reciprocal trace in clause (C1).
glossary.T_C2: The complete two-rough-prime reciprocal trace in clause (C2).
glossary.T_C3: The complete three-rough-prime reciprocal trace in clause (C3).
glossary.rho: The fixed safe-interior margin sigma/5 below beta_m.

3a2713341f432a02.title: TRUE ROUGH-FACE INCIDENCE AND SQUARE-DIVISOR LAYERING AT FIXED HEIGHT. Let A and h be nonzero integers. Let Rcal be a finite family of odd squarefree integers r>1 satisfying gcd(Ah,r)=1, and let Zcal be a finite row-label set. For each r let Zcal_r be a subset of Zcal. Attach to rho in Zcal_r an integer n_rho divisible by r with gcd(n_rho/r,r)=1 and a complex scalar alpha_{r,rho}. For z in C^{Zcal} define
3a2713341f432a02.author: slava chan
3a2713341f432a02.statement:
TRUE ROUGH-FACE INCIDENCE AND SQUARE-DIVISOR LAYERING AT FIXED HEIGHT. Let A and h be nonzero integers. Let Rcal be a finite family of odd squarefree integers r>1 satisfying gcd(Ah,r)=1, and let Zcal be a finite row-label set. For each r let Zcal_r be a subset of Zcal. Attach to rho in Zcal_r an integer n_rho divisible by r with gcd(n_rho/r,r)=1 and a complex scalar alpha_{r,rho}. For z in C^{Zcal} define
x_{r,rho}=(n_rho/r)^{-1} modulo r,                                  (1)
(I_rz)(x)=sum_{rho in Zcal_r;x_{r,rho}=x}alpha_{r,rho}z_rho.         (2)
Then, whenever gcd(q,r)=1,
sum_{rho in Zcal_r}alpha_{r,rho}z_rho
 product_{p|r}e_p(Ah(n_rho/p)^{-1}q^{-1})
=sum_{x in G_r}(I_rz)(x)e_r(Ahxq^{-1}).                              (3)

Let beta be finitely supported on the positive integers. The identity
mu(q)^2=sum_{k^2|q}mu(k)                                             (4)
gives, for every disjoint r,r' in Rcal,
sum_{q>=1;gcd(q,rr')=1}mu(q)^2beta(q)R_r(q)overline{R_{r'}(q)}
=sum_{k>=1;gcd(k,rr')=1}B_{r,r'}(I_rz,I_{r'}z;w_k,h,k),              (5)
where
R_r(q)=sum_{x in G_r}(I_rz)(x)e_r(Ahxq^{-1}),                        (6)
w_k(j)=mu(k)beta(k^2j) for j>=1 and w_k(j)=0 for j<=0.               (7)
For fixed k put Rcal_k={r in Rcal:gcd(k,r)=1}. Summing the right side of (5) over ordered coprime distinct pairs in Rcal_k is exactly the quadratic form <Iz,A_kIz> of fact 18a0de57eaf35171 with the fixed height set {h}, restricted to Rcal_k.

Under the full literal nonresonant hypotheses of fact 3330e83b6d253b69, equation (3) is the raw rough-face incidence for its r. Moreover the raw local phase g_{p,rho} and its centered version phi_{p,rho}=g_{p,rho}+1/p have equal additive Fourier coefficients at every nonzero local frequency. Therefore the unit-completion block, whose frequency is nonzero modulo every p|r, has the incidence (2). This last assertion identifies only that unit local Fourier block; the literal small-v phase, masks, inactive coefficients and nonunit strata remain as in facts 3330e83b6d253b69, 4d4bc6711163794c and 67ebf7acc95b59b6. No PMLS estimate or C4 conclusion is asserted.
3a2713341f432a02.proof:
For squarefree r, CRT gives
e_r(Y)=product_{p|r}e_p(Y(r/p)^{-1}).                               (8)
By (1), for p|r,
x_{r,rho}(r/p)^{-1}
=(n_rho/r)^{-1}(r/p)^{-1}
=(n_rho/p)^{-1} modulo p.                                           (9)
Apply (8) with Y=Ahx_{r,rho}q^{-1}, then group equal x_{r,rho}; this proves (3).

Both sides of (4) are multiplicative in q. At p^a the right side is one for a=0,1 and is 1+mu(p)=0 for a>=2, equal to mu(p^a)^2. Insert (4) in the left side of (5), write q=k^2j, and note that the unit condition is gcd(kj,rr')=1. On it, q^{-1}=k^{-2}j^{-1} modulo r and r'. Thus the inner j-sum is
sum_{j;gcd(j,rr')=1}w_k(j)
 [sum_x(I_rz)(x)e_r(Ak^{-2}hxj^{-1})]
 conjugate([sum_y(I_{r'}z)(y)e_{r'}(Ak^{-2}hyj^{-1})]),
which is B_{r,r'} from fact 18a0de57eaf35171. Its unit hypotheses hold because gcd(Ah,rr')=gcd(k,rr')=1. This proves (5). For fixed k every occurring modulus lies in Rcal_k, and the incidence maps are independent of the singleton height h, so equations (13)--(15) of that fact give the stated quadratic form.

Finally, under fact 3330e83b6d253b69, its nonresonance argument gives precisely gcd(Ah,r)=1 and its prime-local raw phase is the left side of (3). The normalized additive Fourier transform of the constant 1/p is supported only at frequency zero modulo p. Hence g_{p,rho} and phi_{p,rho} have equal nonzero-frequency coefficients. A unit completion frequency modulo r is nonzero at every p|r, proving the final scoped identification.

glossary.I_r: the fixed-height row-linear rough-face incidence map
glossary.R_r: the raw rough-face row sum generated by I_r
glossary.Rcal_k: the active-product family coprime to the square-divisor k
glossary.x_{r,rho}: the true rough-face incidence coordinate (n_rho/r)^{-1} modulo r

3afa321a72a3612b.title: PRIMITIVE-CHARACTER LARGE-SIEVE DELETION THROUGH CONDUCTOR x^(1/2-eta) FOR THE ACTUAL-Z_MID UPPER BOUNDARY. Assume the actual-Z_mid g=1, |h|=1 upper-boundary packet and character reconstruction of facts 58c03698e1b077c3, c9accda871a70b43, and 5a651793cab6648b. Put A_0=x^(1/2+o(1)) and B_0=x^(2/3+o(1)). For F_dy>=2, let mathfrak B^{np}_{1,1}(F_dy) be the complete part with nonprincipal primitive conductor
3afa321a72a3612b.author: slava chan
3afa321a72a3612b.statement:
PRIMITIVE-CHARACTER LARGE-SIEVE DELETION THROUGH CONDUCTOR x^(1/2-eta) FOR THE ACTUAL-Z_MID UPPER BOUNDARY. Assume the actual-Z_mid g=1, |h|=1 upper-boundary packet and character reconstruction of facts 58c03698e1b077c3, c9accda871a70b43, and 5a651793cab6648b. Put A_0=x^(1/2+o(1)) and B_0=x^(2/3+o(1)). For F_dy>=2, let mathfrak B^{np}_{1,1}(F_dy) be the complete part with nonprincipal primitive conductor
F_dy<=f<2F_dy,
retaining both conjugate frequencies, the smooth endpoint amplitude, and every literal natural mask. Then, uniformly for 2<=F_dy<=B_0,
|mathfrak B^{np}_{1,1}(F_dy)|
 <=x^(o(1)) A_0^(1/2)F_dy^(1/2)(A_0+F_dy^2)^(1/2).                 (1)

Consequently, for every fixed eta with 0<eta<1/2, there is delta_eta>0 such that the complete principal component together with every nonprincipal component of primitive conductor
f<=x^(1/2-eta)
is O(x^(1-delta_eta)).                                               (2)
Thus the first unresolved actual-Z_mid g=1, |h|=1 hard upper-boundary packet may be restricted, up to a fixed-power error, to
f>x^(1/2-eta), (f,N)=1, b=fs asymp x^(2/3), s<x^(1/6+eta+o(1)).      (3)
No estimate for the large-conductor component in (3), for |h|>1, for g>1, or for the derivative-integral and boundary-strip terms is asserted.
3afa321a72a3612b.proof:
Fact 58c03698e1b077c3 represents the packet as x^(o(1)) finitely many forms
sum_{a asymp A_0,b asymp B_0,(a,b)=1}
 alpha_a beta_b G_end(a,b)e_b(Na^{-1}),                              (4)
with pointwise x^(o(1)) coefficients and endpoint amplitude; the pointwise assertion was also used and verified in c9accda871a70b43. The scaled derivative bounds through order two in each variable permit a two-variable Fourier tensor separation
G_end(a,b)=sum_rho c_rho G_{1,rho}(a)G_{2,rho}(b),                  (5)
where the one-variable factors are uniformly bounded and
sum_rho|c_rho|<=x^(o(1)).
Indeed, after scaling a/A_0 and b/B_0 and using a finite smooth extension to a two-dimensional torus, two integrations by parts in each Fourier coordinate bound the tensor coefficients by x^(o(1))(1+|m|)^(-2)(1+|n|)^(-2), whose double sum converges. It therefore suffices to prove (1) for one tensor in (5).

On the squarefree literal b-support, write b=fs for a character induced from a primitive character psi^* modulo f. Fact 5a651793cab6648b gives, for (f,N)=1,
G^+_{N,b}(chi)
 =c_s(N)overline{psi^*(N)}psi^*(s)tau_f(psi^*),
 |tau_f(psi^*)|=sqrt(f),                                            (6)
and gives zero when (f,N)>1. The induced character evaluated at a is
chi(a)=psi^*(a)1_{(a,s)=1}; coprimality with f is already encoded by extending psi^* by zero to nonunits. Expand the remaining coupling exactly as
1_{(a,s)=1}=sum_{d|a,d|s}mu(d).                                    (7)

Fix d. Apart from factors of absolute value one, the a-side character sum is
X_{d,f}(psi^*)=
 sum_{a asymp A_0,d|a}alpha_aG_1(a)psi^*(a).                        (8)
Since d|s and (f,s)=1, one has (d,f)=1. Writing a=dn turns (8), up to the constant psi^*(d), into a primitive-character sum over an interval of length comparable to A_0/d with coefficient square norm at most
x^(o(1))A_0/d.                                                      (9)
The multiplicative large sieve in Akbary--Felix, arXiv:1404.5700, Lemma 2.4, states that for arbitrary complex coefficients on an interval of length L,
sum_{q<=Q}q/phi(q) sum_{psi modulo q primitive}
 |sum_n z_n psi(n)|^2
 <=C(L+Q^2)sum_n|z_n|^2.
Apply it with Q=2F_dy and the sequence in (8). Since q/phi(q)>=1, restriction to f in [F_dy,2F_dy) gives
sum_{f asymp F_dy}sum_{psi^* primitive modulo f}
 |X_{d,f}(psi^*)|^2
 <=x^(o(1))(F_dy^2+A_0/d)(A_0/d).                                  (10)

The complementary side is
Y_{d,f}(psi^*)=
 sum_{s asymp B_0/f,d|s,(s,f)=1}
 beta_{fs}G_2(fs)c_s(N)psi^*(s)/phi(s),                             (11)
with any additional b-only natural masks retained in beta_{fs}. Pointwise boundedness and |c_s(N)|<=(s,N) give
|Y_{d,f}(psi^*)|<=C_d,
C_d<=x^(o(1))(d,N)/d.                                               (12)
To prove (12), write s=dt and use
(dt,N)<=(d,N)(t,N),  1/phi(dt)<=x^(o(1))/(dt).
The dyadic divisor calculation used in c9accda871a70b43 gives
sum_{t asymp B_0/(fd)}(t,N)/t<=x^(o(1)),
uniformly when the interval is nonempty, proving (12).

For f asymp F_dy, (6) and phi(f)>=f x^(-o(1)) give
|tau_f(psi^*)|/phi(f)<=x^(o(1))F_dy^(-1/2).                         (13)
Cauchy's inequality over f and primitive psi^*, followed by (10), (12), and
sum_{f asymp F_dy}#{psi^* primitive modulo f}
 <=sum_{f asymp F_dy}phi(f)<=4F_dy^2,
bounds the fixed-d contribution by
x^(o(1))F_dy^(1/2)C_d
 [(F_dy^2+A_0/d)(A_0/d)]^(1/2).                                    (14)
This is at most
x^(o(1))A_0^(1/2)F_dy^(1/2)(A_0+F_dy^2)^(1/2)
 (d,N)/d^(3/2).                                                     (15)
Finally,
sum_{d>=1}(d,N)/d^(3/2)
 =sum_{e|N}phi(e)sum_{m>=1}(em)^(-3/2)
 <=zeta(3/2)sum_{e|N}e^(-1/2)
 <=x^(o(1)).                                                        (16)
Summing (15) proves (1), including all coprimality layers and the tensor inventory.

For F_dy<=A_0^(1/2), (1) is at most x^(o(1))A_0F_dy^(1/2), hence at most x^(5/8+o(1)). For
A_0^(1/2)<F_dy<=x^(1/2-eta),
it is at most
x^(o(1))A_0^(1/2)F_dy^(3/2)
 <=x^(1-3eta/2+o(1)).
There are only O(log x) dyadic conductor intervals. Add the principal estimate x^(1/2+o(1)) from c9accda871a70b43 and absorb the o(1) terms to obtain (2) for some fixed delta_eta>0. Finally f>x^(1/2-eta) and b=fs=B_0x^(o(1)) imply s<x^(1/6+eta+o(1)), proving (3).

glossary.C_d: The absolute complementary-factor mass after the coprimality divisor d is fixed.
glossary.F_dy: A dyadic scale for the primitive conductor f.
glossary.mathfrak B^{np}_{1,1}(F_dy): The part of the actual-Z_mid g=1, |h|=1 upper-boundary packet with nonprincipal primitive conductor in [F_dy,2F_dy).

3afaf4d03db90bcf.title: Fix real numbers 1/2<a<b<1, a nonzero nonnegative continuously differentiable real function W supported in [a,b], and a continuously differentiable real function psi with 0<=psi<=1, psi(u)=0 for 0<u<=1, and psi(u)=1 for u>=2. Fix a positive cofinal source exponent B_src supplied by fact 5084a731a9f78a09, and let x tend to infinity through values for which N_0=2x is an even integer not representable as a sum of two primes. Put D_*=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B_src), and choose Phi to be the nonnegative smooth dyadic partition of fact 3ef233e014331fc3. Let D,M,U be positive dyadic numbers satisfying ax/4<=DM<=4bx and (2-b)x/2<=U<=2(2-a)x. For every integer center H define the frozen high-divisor genuine-prime block T_H^>(x;D,M,U)=sum_{d,m>=1, p prime, d>sqrt(x), dm+p=H}mu(d)log(m)log(p)W(dm/x)psi(d/D_*)Phi(d/D)Phi(m/M)Phi(p/U). Then, for every K>0, sum_{H in Z}|T_H^>(x;D,M,U)|^2 <<_{K,a,b,B_src,W,psi,Phi} x^3(log x)^(-K), uniformly in the allowed D,M,U. Consequently, for every B_0>0 and L>0, the number of integer centers H for which |T_H^>(x;D,M,U)|>x(log x)^(-B_0) is O_{B_0,L,a,b,B_src,W,psi,Phi}(x(log x)^(-L)). For the distinguished bad center H=N_0, the quantity T_{N_0}^> is exactly the d>sqrt(x) part of the cofinal genuine-prime block P_{N_0}^{B_src}(D,M;U) from fact 5084a731a9f78a09, equivalently the high-divisor part in the exact split of fact 96ed928a9fc80276 with this cofinal cutoff. Nevertheless the theorem gives no estimate for N_0 itself and no every-bad-center conclusion, because N_0 may belong to the exceptional set
3afaf4d03db90bcf.author: slava chan
3afaf4d03db90bcf.statement: Fix real numbers 1/2<a<b<1, a nonzero nonnegative continuously differentiable real function W supported in [a,b], and a continuously differentiable real function psi with 0<=psi<=1, psi(u)=0 for 0<u<=1, and psi(u)=1 for u>=2. Fix a positive cofinal source exponent B_src supplied by fact 5084a731a9f78a09, and let x tend to infinity through values for which N_0=2x is an even integer not representable as a sum of two primes. Put D_*=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B_src), and choose Phi to be the nonnegative smooth dyadic partition of fact 3ef233e014331fc3. Let D,M,U be positive dyadic numbers satisfying ax/4<=DM<=4bx and (2-b)x/2<=U<=2(2-a)x. For every integer center H define the frozen high-divisor genuine-prime block T_H^>(x;D,M,U)=sum_{d,m>=1, p prime, d>sqrt(x), dm+p=H}mu(d)log(m)log(p)W(dm/x)psi(d/D_*)Phi(d/D)Phi(m/M)Phi(p/U). Then, for every K>0, sum_{H in Z}|T_H^>(x;D,M,U)|^2 <<_{K,a,b,B_src,W,psi,Phi} x^3(log x)^(-K), uniformly in the allowed D,M,U. Consequently, for every B_0>0 and L>0, the number of integer centers H for which |T_H^>(x;D,M,U)|>x(log x)^(-B_0) is O_{B_0,L,a,b,B_src,W,psi,Phi}(x(log x)^(-L)). For the distinguished bad center H=N_0, the quantity T_{N_0}^> is exactly the d>sqrt(x) part of the cofinal genuine-prime block P_{N_0}^{B_src}(D,M;U) from fact 5084a731a9f78a09, equivalently the high-divisor part in the exact split of fact 96ed928a9fc80276 with this cofinal cutoff. Nevertheless the theorem gives no estimate for N_0 itself and no every-bad-center conclusion, because N_0 may belong to the exceptional set.
3afaf4d03db90bcf.proof:
All coefficients in this proof are frozen as the integer center H varies. Define
a_{x,D,M}(n)=sum_{d,m>=1, d>sqrt(x), dm=n}mu(d)log(m)W(dm/x)psi(d/D_*)Phi(d/D)Phi(m/M)
and
b_{x,U}(p)=1_{p is prime}log(p)Phi(p/U),
with b_{x,U}(n)=0 for nonprime integers. Then T_H^>=sum_n a_{x,D,M}(n)b_{x,U}(H-n). Put e(t)=exp(2 pi i t) and form
A(alpha)=sum_n a_{x,D,M}(n)e(n alpha),   B(alpha)=sum_n b_{x,U}(n)e(n alpha).
Thus T_H^> is the H-th Fourier coefficient of A(alpha)B(alpha), and Parseval gives
sum_{H in Z}|T_H^>|^2=int_0^1|A(alpha)B(alpha)|^2d alpha
<=||A||_infinity^2 sum_n|b_{x,U}(n)|^2.                                      (1)

We first bound A uniformly. Since B_src>0, every d>sqrt(x) satisfies d/D_*>(log x)^(B_src)>2 for all sufficiently large x. Hence psi(d/D_*)=1 throughout T_H^>. For a fixed positive integer m define
S_m(alpha)=sum_{d>sqrt(x)}mu(d)W(md/x)Phi(d/D)e(md alpha).
If S_m is nonzero, then Phi(d/D) is nonzero for some d>sqrt(x), so d<=2D forces D>sqrt(x)/2. Also, simultaneous nonvanishing of Phi(d/D) and W(md/x) implies mD/x<=2b. On the interval obtained by intersecting [D/2,2D] with d>sqrt(x), the weight as a function of t=d/D is W(mDt/x)Phi(t). Its supremum and total variation are bounded uniformly in m,D,x: indeed mD/x<=2b, so differentiation gives a bound depending only on W and Phi.

We record the external estimate. Liu and Sarnak [LS13, Lemma 2.1] state that for a fixed congruence class modulo a fixed positive integer and a real polynomial phi of positive degree,
sum_{n<=Y}mu(n)e(phi(n))<<_{J}Y(log Y)^(-J)
for every J>0, with the constant independent of all coefficients of phi. With modulus one and phi(n)=beta n, this is Davenport's estimate, uniform in every real beta. Partial summation on the interval just described, including the possible boundary at sqrt(x), therefore gives, for every J>0,
|S_m(alpha)|<<_{J,W,Phi}D(log D)^(-J)<<_{J,W,Phi}D(log x)^(-J),                (2)
uniformly in alpha and m. The last comparison uses D>sqrt(x)/2; if S_m is zero there is nothing to prove.

Now
A(alpha)=sum_{m>=1}log(m)Phi(m/M)S_m(alpha).
The term m=1 vanishes. If another term is nonzero, Phi(m/M) forces M/2<=m<=2M, and hence M>=1. There are O(M) such integers and log(m)<<log(2M). Because D>sqrt(x)/2 in the nonempty case and DM<=4bx, one has M<=8b sqrt(x), so log(2M)<<_b log x. Using (2) and DM<=4bx gives
||A||_infinity<<_{J,a,b,W,Phi}MD(log x)^(1-J)<<_{J,a,b,W,Phi}x(log x)^(1-J).  (3)
Since J is arbitrary, (3) supplies any prescribed fixed logarithmic saving.

For the prime side, Phi(p/U) can be nonzero only when p<=2U<=4(2-a)x. Therefore there are O_a(x) possible integers p and log(p)<<_a log x. By orthogonality,
int_0^1|B(alpha)|^2d alpha=sum_p(log p)^2|Phi(p/U)|^2<<_{a,Phi}x(log x)^2.       (4)
No prime number theorem is used here. Given K>0, choose J so large that 2J-4>=K. Substituting (3) and (4) into (1) proves
sum_H|T_H^>|^2<<x^3(log x)^(-K).

Let E be the set of centers satisfying |T_H^>|>x(log x)^(-B_0). Apply the energy estimate with exponent K=L+2B_0. Then
|E|x^2(log x)^(-2B_0)<sum_H|T_H^>|^2<<x^3(log x)^(-L-2B_0),
which gives |E|<<x(log x)^(-L).

It remains only to verify the scoped project specialization. Here N_0=2x is, by hypothesis, an integer bad center; W, psi, B_src and the same nonnegative dyadic partition Phi are exactly those in fact 5084a731a9f78a09; and D,M,U are positive dyadic source-admissible scales. That fact defines P_{N_0}^{B_src}(D,M;U) by the identical termwise sum over dm+p=N_0. Restricting its d-variable to d>sqrt(x) gives exactly T_{N_0}^>. Fact 96ed928a9fc80276 records the same exact low/high split and its divisor-switched form; only the cutoff exponent has been chosen cofinally here. Finally, the exceptional-set estimate controls only the number of H in E and contains no assertion excluding N_0 from E. Thus it is compatible with every hypothetical bad center belonging to its corresponding exceptional set.

glossary.B_src: the positive cofinal source cutoff exponent from fact 5084a731a9f78a09
glossary.H: the integer additive center varied in the Parseval average
glossary.S_m(alpha): the fixed-m Möbius exponential sum inside the divisor–cofactor Fourier transform
glossary.T_H^>: the frozen d>sqrt(x) genuine-prime dyadic block at center H

3b1bda56ad927c5e.title: FIXED-TARGET TWO-ROUGH-PRIME ENDPOINT BELOW \(\beta=6/5\)
3b1bda56ad927c5e.author: slava chan
3b1bda56ad927c5e.statement:
FIXED-TARGET TWO-ROUGH-PRIME ENDPOINT BELOW \(\beta=6/5\).

Fix \(0<\kappa\le1/100\) and integers \(J,C_A\ge1\), put \(\sigma=\kappa/100\), and suppose
\[
 1\le\beta\le6/5-2\kappa.
\]
For sufficiently large \(Q\), define
\[
 R=Q^\beta,\quad H=R/Q,\quad
 L=HQ^\sigma,\quad S_0=H^2Q^{3\sigma},\quad
 Z=Q^{3/2-\beta-3\sigma}. \tag{1}
\]
Let
\[
 V=Q^\nu,\quad P_1=Q^a,\quad P_2=Q^b,
\]
where
\[
 0\le\nu\le2\beta-2+3\sigma,\quad
 a\le b,\quad a,b\ge\frac32-\beta-3\sigma,\quad
 \nu+a+b=\beta. \tag{2}
\]
Let \(\xi_v\) be supported on squarefree \(V\le v<2V\), all of whose prime divisors are at most \(L\), with \(|\xi_v|\le\tau_J(v)\). Let \(A\ne0\) be fixed with \(|A|\le Q^{C_A}\), let \(|c_q|\le1\), and let \(|\nu_h|\le\tau_J(|h|)\) on \(H\le|h|<2H\).

Let \(\mathfrak F\) be a fixed uniformly scaled-smooth family on \([1,2]^5\). For \(\Psi\in\mathfrak F\), define
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 {\cal S}_{V,P_1,P_2}
 =H^{-1}\sum_{Q\le q<2Q}c_q
 \sum_{\substack{H\le|h|<2H\\v\sim V\\p_1\sim P_1,\ p_2\sim P_2\\
 p_1,p_2\ {\rm prime}\\p_1<p_2\\(vp_1p_2,q)=1}}
 \nu_h\xi_v\Psi(q/Q,|h|/H,v/V,p_1/P_1,p_2/P_2)
 e_q\!\left(Ah(vp_1p_2)^{-1}\right).
 \end{aligned} \tag{3}
\]
Here \(n\sim X\) means \(X\le n<2X\). Assume the ordered prime cells have been refined so that either \(P_2\ge2P_1\), in which case \(p_1<p_2\) is automatic, or \(P_1=P_2\) and the full coefficient and amplitude in (3), before imposing \(p_1<p_2\), are symmetric under \(p_1\leftrightarrow p_2\).

Then there exists \(\delta=\delta(\kappa,C_A)>0\) such that
\[
 |{\cal S}_{V,P_1,P_2}|
 \ll_{\kappa,J,C_A,\mathfrak F}Q^{2-\delta}. \tag{4}
\]
The same bound holds after a polylogarithmic number of refined prime cells and smooth labels. Taking \(\xi_v=\mu(v)\) gives the exact sign of the two-rough-prime alternative in fact \(6414b11506a84ff0\). No three-rough-prime or outer-\(g\) estimate is asserted.
3b1bda56ad927c5e.proof:
Put
\[
 L_\beta=2\beta-2,\qquad U_\beta=3-2\beta,\qquad w=\nu+a.
\]
Part (C) of fact \(461b4af4d8047ab5\) gives three mutually exclusive and exhaustive cases.

Case 1: \(w\le L_\beta+3\sigma\). Group \(v\) and \(p_1\) into an outer variable \(s=vp_1\), of scale
\[
 V'=VP_1=Q^w\le H^2Q^{3\sigma}. \tag{5}
\]
This grouped coefficient is divisor-bounded after scaled-smooth Fourier separation, since the number of representations \(s=vp_1\) is at most \(\tau(s)\).

The final prime block is separated from every prime divisor of \(s\). The prime divisors inherited from \(v\) are at most \(L<Z\le P_2\). Also
\[
 b=\beta-w\ge2-\beta-3\sigma,
\]
whereas
\[
 a\le w\le2\beta-2+3\sigma.
\]
Thus
\[
 b-a\ge4-3\beta-6\sigma
 \ge\frac25+6\kappa-\frac{6\kappa}{100}>0. \tag{6}
\]
For large \(Q\), every \(p_1\sim P_1\) is smaller than every \(p_2\sim P_2\). Therefore every supported \(s\) is coprime to every final prime \(p_2\). Apply the separated-outer endpoint fact \(af579dffb21039b1\) with outer scale \(V'\) and prime scale \(P_2\). It gives a fixed power saving.

Case 2:
\[
 L_\beta+3\sigma<w\le U_\beta-4\sigma.
\]
Select
\[
 S=VP_1=Q^w,\qquad T=P_2.
\]
After absorbing fixed dyadic endpoint constants, these satisfy
\[
 H^2Q^{2\sigma}\le S\le Q^{1-3\sigma}/H^2,\qquad ST\asymp R=QH. \tag{7}
\]
The coefficient on \(S\), obtained by convolving \(\xi_v\) with the prime indicator, is divisor-bounded. The coefficient on \(T\) is bounded by one.

Case 3: \(w>U_\beta-4\sigma\). Fact \(461b4af4d8047ab5\) gives
\[
 L_\beta+4\sigma<b=\beta-w<U_\beta-4\sigma.
\]
Select
\[
 S=P_2,\qquad T=VP_1.
\]
Again (7) holds, with even larger lower margin.

In Cases 2 and 3, first use logarithmic Fourier expansion to separate the scaled-smooth amplitude. Apply the full fixed-target correlated estimate in fact \(73fb9efe1286f7e9\). Expanding its two fourth roots after the \(H^{-1}\) prefactor gives
\[
 Q^2H^{1/2}S^{-1/4},\quad
 Q^{7/4}H^{1/2}S^{1/4},\quad
 Q^2HS^{-1/2},\quad
 Q^{7/4}H.
\]
The window (7) bounds all four by \(Q^{2-\delta_0}\) for some \(\delta_0\gg\sigma\). The fixed target and all divisor and Fourier coefficients cost only \(Q^\epsilon\), absorbed by choosing \(\epsilon\) sufficiently small.

It remains to justify the ordered-prime convention. If \(P_2\ge2P_1\), the order is automatic, with a possible empty shared endpoint. If \(P_1=P_2\), symmetry gives the exact identity
\[
 \sum_{p_1<p_2}F(p_1,p_2)
 =\frac12\left(\sum_{p_1,p_2}F(p_1,p_2)
               -\sum_pF(p,p)\right). \tag{8}
\]
The unrestricted product is handled by the preceding three cases. The repeated-prime diagonal is bounded absolutely. There are at most \(O(VP_1)\) pairs \((v,p)\), so after the \(q\)-sum, the \(h\)-sum, and the \(H^{-1}\) prefactor it contributes
\[
 \ll Q^\epsilon QVP_1
 =Q^\epsilon QR/P_2
 \le Q^\epsilon QR/Z. \tag{9}
\]
Using (1),
\[
 \log_Q(QR/Z)
 =2\beta-\frac12+3\sigma
 \le\frac{19}{10}-4\kappa+\frac{3\kappa}{100}<2-\kappa. \tag{10}
\]
Thus the diagonal is power-saving. Pairing distinct dyadic cells and treating equal cells by (8) yields the stated refined partition. Summing its polylogarithmically many pieces proves (4).

glossary.cal S_{V,P_1,P_2}: The fixed-target reciprocal trace for a small factor and two ordered rough primes.

3b2d15db39ad0217.title: LITERAL CRITICAL-CLUSTER ENERGY INTERFACE AND THE EXACT Gadd^(-1) LOCAL SAVING FOR Aadd
3b2d15db39ad0217.author: slava chan
3b2d15db39ad0217.statement:
LITERAL CRITICAL-CLUSTER ENERGY INTERFACE AND THE EXACT Gadd^(-1) LOCAL SAVING FOR Aadd.

Fix a constant C_A>=1. Let Q>=8 and let real numbers H,V,P,B satisfy
  2<=H<=Q^(1/3),  2<=V<H,  P=QH/V,  B>=1.                 (1)
Let A be a nonzero integer with
  |A|<=C_A Q^2.                                             (2)
Let cal L be a finite label set. For every outer row o=(ell,v,p), where ell belongs to cal L, V<=v<2V is an integer, p is prime in [P,2P), and gcd(v,p)=1, put n=vp. Let cal X_o be a finite set of triples x=(q,m,k) satisfying
  Q<=q,m<2Q,  qm+nk=A,  gcd(qm,n)=1.                       (3)
For each ell let I_ell be an integer interval contained either in [H,2H) or in (-2H,-H]. Let a_{o,h}(x) be complex coefficients satisfying
  |a_{o,h}(x)|<=B.                                         (4)
For x=(q,m,k) define
  d_x=gcd(|A|,q),  r_x=q/d_x,  t_x=k/d_x,
  lambda_x=t_x/r_x=k/q.                                    (5)
Define the unequal exact-rational-phase additive Gram
  Aadd
   =sum_o sum_{h in I_ell}
      sum_{x_1,x_2 in cal X_o, lambda_{x_1} not equal lambda_{x_2}}
       a_{o,h}(x_1)conjugate(a_{o,h}(x_2))
       e(h[lambda_{x_1}-lambda_{x_2}]).                     (6)

Put
  K_cl=ceil(12(C_A/2+1))+1.                                (7)
For every nonempty row choose a partition
  cal X_o=disjoint union_{1<=j<=K_cl} cal X_{o,j}           (8)
such that the slopes in each nonempty cal X_{o,j} lie in a real interval of length at most 1/(12H), padding by empty sets when necessary. Such a partition always exists. Define
  Z_{o,h,j}=sum_{x in cal X_{o,j}}a_{o,h}(x)e(h lambda_x),  (9)
  E_cl=sum_o sum_{h in I_ell}sum_{j=1}^{K_cl}|Z_{o,h,j}|^2,(10)
  W_cl=sum_o sum_{h in I_ell}sum_{j=1}^{K_cl}
              (sum_{x in cal X_{o,j}}|a_{o,h}(x)|)^2.      (11)
If W_cl>0 put Theta_cl=E_cl/W_cl, and put Theta_cl=0 when W_cl=0. Then
  0<=Theta_cl<=1,                                          (12)
and exactly
  Aadd=sum_o sum_{h in I_ell}
       [|sum_{j=1}^{K_cl}Z_{o,h,j}|^2
        -sum_lambda|sum_{x in cal X_o:lambda_x=lambda}
                         a_{o,h}(x)|^2].                   (13)
Consequently
  Aadd<=K_cl E_cl=K_cl Theta_cl W_cl.                      (14)
For every epsilon>0,
  W_cl<<_{C_A,epsilon}B^2(#cal L)Q^(3+epsilon).            (15)

Define
  Gadd=VQ^(1/3)/H.                                         (16)
Thus
  Q^3/Gadd=P Q^(5/3).                                      (17)
In particular, the naturally weighted critical-cluster estimate
  Theta_cl<<_{C_A,epsilon}Gadd^(-1)Q^epsilon               (18)
implies the one-sided remaining supplier
  Aadd<<_{C_A,epsilon}B^2(#cal L)P Q^(5/3+epsilon).        (19)
If B and #cal L are subpolynomial and the normalized principal-row hypotheses of fact 4b89ec4ce7a7b67a hold, then (19) supplies its remaining one-sided Aadd estimate. This is a sufficient local interface; cancellation between distinct clusters could also make Aadd small, so no necessity or converse is asserted.

For the exact literal row of facts 294ac3b02b065aec and 1a9cfcfe3eedd5e2, source restoration takes
  a_{o,h}(x)=c_q nu_h U_ell(q,h,v,p)chi_ell(v,p,h,q),       (20)
while e(h lambda_x) is exactly the restored source phase. Hence (9)-(18) retain every factor in the literal coefficient, every zero-one source mask in chi_ell, the same ell,v,p,h row, and the unequal-phase deletion in (6). The divisor-selected prime p of fact 7f63ca7922a7fab9 remains inside the source row; no independent saving from p dividing its three displayed integers is used.

The factor Gadd^(-1) in (18) is not implied by the current abstract coefficient hypotheses. For the phase-aligned coefficients of fact 4bc8d22f796384d3 one has Theta_cl=1 for every partition with W_cl>0. For the one-cluster constant-coefficient model of fact 714f3597f5ef527c with Y>=2 distinct slopes, one has
  Theta_cl>=(Y+1)/(2Y)>=1/2.                               (21)
Thus boundedness, normalized finite-band factorization, height separation, source occupancy, and resolution-scale clustering do not yield (18). A proof on a fixed-power interior range Gadd>=Q^delta must use arithmetic cancellation in the literal coefficient (20), or cancellation from an earlier signed assembly. No estimate for (18), no PMD closure outside the verified endpoint strip, and no Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
3b2d15db39ad0217.proof:
Fact 1a9cfcfe3eedd5e2 proves that d_x divides k and that t_x/r_x=k/q, proving the last equality in (5). Since n=vp>=VP=QH, equations (2)-(3) satisfy the hypotheses of fact 28b8af5697fa64eb. That fact covers the slope set of each nonempty row by at most K_cl intervals of length at most 1/(12H). Assign every source atom lying in more than one covering interval to one such interval. This gives the disjoint partition (8); empty rows use only empty pieces.

Fix o and h. Expanding the complete square gives
  |sum_j Z_{o,h,j}|^2
   =sum_{x_1,x_2 in cal X_o}
      a_{o,h}(x_1)conjugate(a_{o,h}(x_2))
      e(h[lambda_{x_1}-lambda_{x_2}]).                     (22)
On the equal-slope subdomain the exponential factor is one. Grouping that subdomain by its common value lambda gives
  sum_lambda|sum_{x in cal X_o:lambda_x=lambda}
                    a_{o,h}(x)|^2.                         (23)
Subtract (23) from (22), then sum over o,h. The remaining ordered domain is exactly (6), proving (13). Every term in (23) is nonnegative. Cauchy's inequality in the at most K_cl cluster indices gives
  |sum_j Z_{o,h,j}|^2<=K_cl sum_j|Z_{o,h,j}|^2.            (24)
Equations (13), (23), and (24) prove (14).

The triangle inequality in (9) gives
  |Z_{o,h,j}|<=sum_{x in cal X_{o,j}}|a_{o,h}(x)|.         (25)
Thus 0<=E_cl<=W_cl. If W_cl>0, division proves (12); if W_cl=0 then every coefficient is zero, so E_cl=0 and (12) follows from the definition.

We prove (15). The nonnegative numbers
  u_j=sum_{x in cal X_{o,j}}|a_{o,h}(x)|
satisfy sum_j u_j^2<=(sum_j u_j)^2. Hence (4) gives
  W_cl<=sum_o sum_{h in I_ell}(sum_{x in cal X_o}|a_{o,h}(x)|)^2
       <=B^2 sum_o (#I_ell)(#cal X_o)^2.                   (26)
Here P=QH/V>Q because H>V. Therefore fact 914048233fada05f applies to every source row and gives, for every positive epsilon,
  #cal X_o<<_{epsilon}Q^epsilon(1+Q^2/(vp))
           <<_{epsilon}Q^(1+epsilon)/H,                    (27)
because vp>=VP=QH and H<=Q. Every I_ell contains at most 2H integers. There are fewer than 4(#cal L)VP outer rows. Insert (27) into (26), distribute a sufficiently small exponent budget, and use VP=QH:
  W_cl
  <<B^2(#cal L)(VP)H(Q/H)^2Q^epsilon
  =B^2(#cal L)Q^(3+epsilon).                               (28)
This is (15).

Using P=QH/V and (16),
  Gadd P Q^(5/3)
   =[VQ^(1/3)/H][QH/V]Q^(5/3)=Q^3,                        (29)
which proves (17). Combine (14), (15), and (18), absorb the fixed K_cl into the constant, and rename the exponent budget to prove (19). Fact 4b89ec4ce7a7b67a states that a one-sided estimate of the form (19), together with its displayed normalized principal-row hypotheses and the already paid correction terms, is the remaining supplier. This proves the conditional consumer statement.

We verify the literal identification. In fact 294ac3b02b065aec the q-row is
  c_q nu_h U_ell(q,h,v,p)e(Ah/(qvp))
  chi_ell(v,p,h,q)e_{vp}(-Ah qbar).
Fact 1a9cfcfe3eedd5e2 proves exactly that the product of the two displayed phases is e_{r_x}(ht_x)=e(h lambda_x), without changing any other coefficient or mask. Removing only that phase leaves (20). This proves every retention claim. Fact 7f63ca7922a7fab9 proves that the selected p divisibilities are algebraic consequences of the same source equations, so the present proof neither deletes nor double-counts that condition.

For the abstract phase-aligned array of fact 4bc8d22f796384d3, substitution gives
  a_h(x)e(h lambda_x)=1.
Thus on every cluster Z_{h,j}=#cal X_j, and equality holds in (25). Summing gives E_cl=W_cl, so Theta_cl=1 when the source is nonempty.

Finally consider the one-cluster constant array of fact 714f3597f5ef527c with L=#I heights and Y distinct slopes. Its off-diagonal sum T_cluster is at least (L/2)Y(Y-1). Adding the L Y diagonal terms gives
  E_cl=sum_{h in I}|sum_x e(h lambda_x)|^2
       >=L Y+(L/2)Y(Y-1)
       =(L/2)Y(Y+1).                                      (30)
Here W_cl=L Y^2, so division gives (21). These two examples prove the abstract obstruction and all scope qualifications.

glossary.E_cl: The total squared energy of the naturally weighted critical-cluster sums Z_{o,h,j}.
glossary.Theta_cl: The ratio E_cl/W_cl, defined as zero when W_cl is zero.
glossary.W_cl: The clusterwise squared l1 envelope of the literal coefficients.
glossary.Z_{o,h,j}: The naturally weighted literal exponential sum over the j-th critical source-slope cluster in outer row o at height h.
glossary.lambda_x: The exact reduced rational source slope t_x/r_x=k/q attached to a source atom x.

3b7a426b783fe6a5.title: ABSOLUTE PAYMENT OF THE COMPLETE CONSTANT-eta LARGE-ADDITIVE-CONDUCTOR MODE
3b7a426b783fe6a5.author: slava chan
3b7a426b783fe6a5.statement:
ABSOLUTE PAYMENT OF THE COMPLETE CONSTANT-eta LARGE-ADDITIVE-CONDUCTOR MODE.

Adopt the exact Good-W setting
Dcal<=Q^2,  Y=Q^2/Dcal>=1                                           (1)
of facts d3278c2897e20003 and 3207666028864f95. Let
H_C^{q-add-large,const}
 =sum_{t>Y}
  [mu(t)/(t phi(t))]
  sum_eta^*sum_n Z_{t,eta}^{agg}(n)                                (2)
be the complete constant-eta term supplied by GA-ETA-MEAN, with every large additive conductor t, all inverse-argument classes eta, and every literal coefficient and pair-dependent deletion retained. Then
|H_C^{q-add-large,const}|
 <=x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 B F^2
 <=x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 B Y F^2.                                   (GA-ETA-CONST)
Thus the complete constant-eta mode is paid at the canonical large-conductor target.

Define the mean-zero large-conductor residual
H_C^{q-add-large,perp}
 =sum_{t>Y}sum_eta^*
  <V_{t;eta},G_{t,eta}^{perp}>.                                   (3)
Then exactly
H_C^{q-add-large}
 =H_C^{q-add-large,const}
  +H_C^{q-add-large,perp}.                                        (4)
Consequently, after the already accepted low-additive-conductor and centering-correction payments, the only remaining Dcal<=Q^2 additive-conductor supplier is
|H_C^{q-add-large,perp}|
 <=x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 B YF^2.                                    (GA-ETA-PERP-SUP)
Estimate GA-ETA-PERP-SUP is not asserted.

The absolute payment GA-ETA-CONST is Good-W-specific because it uses the accepted literal harmonic conductor ledger. The algebraic constant-eta extraction and mean-zero decomposition are anatomy-independent for any row family satisfying fact 3207666028864f95. This theorem proves no estimate for the mean-zero residual, no full GA-qCENT estimate, no tail payment, and no Goldbach conclusion.
3b7a426b783fe6a5.proof:
Fix an exact retained ordered ray pair in the large additive-conductor source. It has squarefree physical conductor
m_q=st
with t>Y. Because m_q is squarefree, s and t are coprime and
mu(s)mu(t)=mu(m_q).                                                 (5)

By fact 7ee795d9bff04bb2,
Z_gamma(n)
 =sum_{dv=n}
  sum_{exact retained pairs with m_q=st and C_q=c}
  [mu(s)/s]
  <B_bold_{d,v}(R),B_bold_{d,v}(R')>.                              (6)
The inverse-argument classes eta partition the possible triples gamma=(t,s,c). Therefore, for fixed t, summing Z_{t,eta}^{agg}(n) over eta and n sums (6) once over every exact retained pair having that t, without changing any selector.

Multiply its coefficient mu(s)/s from (6) by the constant-mode coefficient mu(t)/(t phi(t)) from (2). By (5),
[mu(t)/(t phi(t))][mu(s)/s]
 =mu(m_q)/[m_q phi(t)].                                            (7)

We now account for every eligible additive-conductor factorization of one physical ray pair before applying the harmonic ledger. Reorder the complete absolute sum first by the retained physical coordinate and its squarefree conductor m_q. Its total divisor weight is at most
(1/m_q)sum_{t|m_q,t>Y}1/phi(t)
 <=(1/m_q)sum_{t|m_q}1/phi(t).                                    (8)
For squarefree m_q, multiplicativity gives
sum_{t|m_q}1/phi(t)
 =product_{p|m_q}(1+1/(p-1))
 =product_{p|m_q}p/(p-1)
 =m_q/phi(m_q).                                                    (9)
Hence (8) equals at most
1/phi(m_q)
 =(m_q/phi(m_q))/m_q
 <=x^{o(1)}/m_q,                                                   (10)
uniformly because every conductor is polynomially bounded. Equations (8)-(10) explicitly count every divisor t>Y belonging to the complete constant-eta sum.

The proof of GA-qPRINC in fact 764588e99974a6d9 establishes over the identical retained physical scaling-coordinate universe the harmonic bound
sum_coordinates 1/m_q<=x^{o(1)}F^2,                               (11)
together with the pointwise coefficient-product envelope x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 and Bx^{o(1)} exact marked copies. Its argument permits every existing zero-one pair deletion because it takes absolute values after retaining the literal index set. Apply that ledger to (10). This proves the first inequality in GA-ETA-CONST. Since Y>=1, the second inequality follows.

For each fixed t, fact 3207666028864f95 proves GA-ETA-MEAN:
sum_eta<V_{t;eta},G_{t,eta}^{agg}>
 =
 [mu(t)/(t phi(t))]sum_eta sum_n Z_{t,eta}^{agg}(n)
 +sum_eta<V_{t;eta},G_{t,eta}^{perp}>.                             (12)
Sum (12) over all t>Y. The first terms give definition (2), the second terms give (3), and the left sides give GA-CqADD-ETA, which equals H_C^{q-add-large} by fact f0fa4ee49bb23934. This proves (4).

Fact d3278c2897e20003 already pays the low additive conductors at scale x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2BYF^2, and fact a08224dfb222c580 pays the centering correction at that scale. Combining those accepted payments, GA-ETA-CONST, and (4) leaves exactly GA-ETA-PERP-SUP. Since that estimate is displayed only as the remaining supplier, all final scope exclusions follow.

glossary.GA-ETA-CONST: The canonical absolute payment of the full constant-eta large-conductor mode.
glossary.GA-ETA-PERP-SUP: The sole remaining mean-zero eta supplier after the constant mode is paid.
glossary.H_C^{q-add-large,const}: The sum of the exact constant-eta components over every additive conductor t>Y.
glossary.H_C^{q-add-large,perp}: The complete large-additive-conductor residual formed from the eta-mean-zero source vectors G_{t,eta}^{perp}.

3bb378b0a49679f9.title: Assume the hypotheses and notation of fact ae1febd328547ccc, and fix z in its forward 1x1 component Z_{F,11}. Put p=y(z) and ell_p=t(z), so p and ell_p are distinct primes and r=p ell_p. Define
3bb378b0a49679f9.author: slava chan
3bb378b0a49679f9.statement:
Assume the hypotheses and notation of fact ae1febd328547ccc, and fix z in its forward 1x1 component Z_{F,11}. Put p=y(z) and ell_p=t(z), so p and ell_p are distinct primes and r=p ell_p. Define
g_z=gcd(d,p ell_p), a_z=d/g_z, b_z=p ell_p/g_z, and n_z=N/g_z.
Then d is squarefree, g_z belongs to {1,p,ell_p,p ell_p}, gcd(a_z,b_z)=1, g_z divides N, and the fixed-N incidence equation is exactly
a_z m+b_z k=n_z.
Thus Z_{F,11} is the disjoint union of at most four exact gcd layers according to g_z. For fixed normalized data a_z,b_z,n_z, its positive integer solutions are in bijection with the positive integers m satisfying a_z m<n_z and
a_z m congruent to n_z modulo b_z;
the corresponding value of k is uniquely
k=(n_z-a_zm)/b_z.
When b_z>1 this congruence is equivalently m congruent to a_z^{-1}n_z modulo b_z, and for b_z=1 it is automatic.

For every positive integer b and integer X define the additive character e_b(X)=exp(2 pi i X/b), with e_1(X)=1, and for every divisor e of b define the Ramanujan sum
c_e(X)=sum_{u modulo e, gcd(u,e)=1}e_e(uX),
where c_1(X)=1. Then the exact quotient-modulus selector has the primitive-conductor decomposition
1_{b divides X}=b^{-1}sum_{h modulo b}e_b(hX)=b^{-1}sum_{e divides b}c_e(X).
Applied with b=b_z and X=a_zm-n_z, every additive character in the e-summand has primitive conductor e. Because b_z is a squarefree divisor of p ell_p, the only possible physical primitive conductors are divisors of b_z among 1,p,ell_p,p ell_p. Hence the actual forward-1x1 fixed-N equation has an exact four-layer gcd normalization and an exact divisor-indexed primitive additive-conductor detector. This is a selector-level partial transform only: it does not define the primitive unit-residue fourth moments, carrier, external window cell, packet coefficients, or later same-cell/cross-cell energy required by facts f5b31dd3643732ac and 4a9a213a428b7e8c.
3bb378b0a49679f9.proof:
Fact ae1febd328547ccc proves that p and ell_p are distinct primes, r=p ell_p, and the original weight is nonzero. Nonzero weight also gives mu(d) nonzero, so d is squarefree. Therefore g_z=gcd(d,p ell_p) is a squarefree divisor of the product of two distinct primes and belongs to {1,p,ell_p,p ell_p}. By the definition of a_z and b_z, gcd(a_z,b_z)=1.

The original equation is dm+p ell_p k=N. Its left side is divisible by g_z, hence g_z divides N and n_z is an integer. Dividing the equation by g_z gives a_zm+b_zk=n_z. Conversely multiplication by g_z recovers the original equation, so the normalization is exact. The value of g_z is uniquely determined by the incidence, so the four gcd classes are disjoint.

Fix a_z,b_z,n_z. If m,k are positive and solve a_zm+b_zk=n_z, then a_zm<n_z and a_zm is congruent to n_z modulo b_z. Conversely, if m is positive, a_zm<n_z, and the congruence holds, then k=(n_z-a_zm)/b_z is a positive integer and solves the equation. These operations are inverse, proving the bijection. If b_z>1, gcd(a_z,b_z)=1 gives an inverse of a_z modulo b_z and the displayed single residue class. The modulus-one case imposes no restriction.

Finite additive orthogonality gives b^{-1}sum_{h modulo b}e_b(hX)=1 when X is divisible by b and zero otherwise. To decompose the h-sum, associate to h modulo b the additive conductor e=b/gcd(h,b), using gcd(0,b)=b so h=0 has e=1. For fixed e dividing b, the residues of exact additive conductor e are uniquely h=(b/e)u modulo b with u modulo e and gcd(u,e)=1. Their contribution is
sum_{u modulo e,gcd(u,e)=1}e_b((b/e)uX)=sum_{u modulo e,gcd(u,e)=1}e_e(uX)=c_e(X).
Summing over e proves the second equality. Since b_z divides p ell_p and p ell_p is squarefree, its divisors are a subset of {1,p,ell_p,p ell_p}. The final scope sentence lists data not constructed by this elementary selector identity, so no moment or analytic estimate is inferred.

glossary.b_z: the normalized semiprime quotient p ell_p/g_z
glossary.c_e(X): the Ramanujan sum over unit additive frequencies modulo e
glossary.ell_p: the second canonical prime factor t(z) in a forward 1x1 incidence
glossary.g_z: the exact gcd of d with the canonical semiprime p ell_p
glossary.p: the first canonical prime factor y(z) in a forward 1x1 incidence

3bcd070f8558ce6f.title: Fix B>0 and a real number vartheta_AP with 1/2<vartheta_AP<1. As x tends to infinity put
3bcd070f8558ce6f.author: slava chan
3bcd070f8558ce6f.statement:
Fix B>0 and a real number vartheta_AP with 1/2<vartheta_AP<1. As x tends to infinity put
D_*=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B),  Q_lvl=x^(vartheta_AP).
Let psi be any real cutoff with psi(u)=1 for u>=2, and choose the nonnegative smooth dyadic partition Phi constructed in fact 3ef233e014331fc3, which is positive on 1/2<t<2. For a positive dyadic D define the raw modulus weight
lambda_D(d)=mu(d)psi(d/D_*)Phi(d/D).
Then, for every sufficiently large x, there is a positive dyadic D satisfying
2D_*<=D<4D_*,  D>Q_lvl^(1/3),  2D<Q_lvl,
and there is a prime ell with D<ell<2D for which lambda_D(ell) is nonzero.

Every triply well-factorable sequence of level Q_lvl in the sense of Lichtman, arXiv:2309.08522, Definition 1.4, vanishes at every prime ell>Q_lvl^(1/3). Hence the raw sequence lambda_D above is not triply well-factorable of level Q_lvl. Lichtman's Theorem 1.7 has a clause uniform over residues 0<|a|<x^(1+epsilon), so its residue range can contain a varying Goldbach residue a=N of size comparable to x; nevertheless that theorem cannot be applied directly with modulus weight lambda_D because its triply well-factorable hypothesis fails.

Runbo Li, arXiv:2602.20917v6, Theorem 1.1, permits a bilinear product of divisor-bounded modulus weights lambda_1(q_1)lambda_2(q_2) under
Q_1^2 Q_2<x^(1-epsilon),  Q_1^7 Q_2^12<x^(4-epsilon),
but its residue a is fixed independently of x. Thus it supplies no stated uniform quantifier for a=N comparable to x. Independently, if a prime modulus ell occurs in a direct bilinear factorization ell=q_1q_2, then either q_1=ell,q_2=1 and the first range condition forces ell<x^(1/2-epsilon/2), or q_1=1,q_2=ell and the second condition forces ell<x^(1/3-epsilon/12). For ell in the high raw support ell comparable to x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B), both alternatives fail for every fixed epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large x.

Consequently neither published theorem is a direct large-modulus supplier for the genuine-prime raw weight lambda_D with the required varying residue. This is only a theorem-interface obstruction: it does not rule out a different decomposition, a separately proved factorable majorant or comparison, a theorem uniform in a growing residue with another coefficient class, or a new estimate for the raw weight.
3bcd070f8558ce6f.proof:
First choose D to be the least positive power of two which is at least 2D_*. Then 2D_*<=D<4D_*. Since vartheta_AP<1,
D_*/Q_lvl^(1/3)=x^(1/2-vartheta_AP/3)(log x)^(-B) tends to infinity,
so D>Q_lvl^(1/3) for sufficiently large x. Since vartheta_AP>1/2,
D_*/Q_lvl=x^(1/2-vartheta_AP)(log x)^(-B) tends to zero,
so 2D<Q_lvl for sufficiently large x. Also D>3. Bertrand's prime-in-an-interval theorem gives a prime ell satisfying D<ell<2D. Because ell/D is in (1,2), the explicit partition in fact 3ef233e014331fc3 has Phi(ell/D)>0. Also ell>D>=2D_*, so psi(ell/D_*)=1, and mu(ell)=-1. Therefore
lambda_D(ell)=-Phi(ell/D) is nonzero.

We now reproduce the relevant weight definition from Lichtman. A sequence lambda(q) is triply well-factorable of level Q_lvl if, for every factorization Q_lvl=Q_1Q_2Q_3 with Q_i>=1, there exist 1-bounded sequences gamma_i supported on positive integers q_i<=Q_i such that
lambda(q)=sum_{q=q_1q_2q_3}gamma_1(q_1)gamma_2(q_2)gamma_3(q_3).
Take the balanced factorization Q_1=Q_2=Q_3=Q_lvl^(1/3). If ell>Q_lvl^(1/3) is prime, then in every positive integer factorization ell=q_1q_2q_3 one of q_1,q_2,q_3 equals ell and the other two equal one. The factor equal to ell lies outside its permitted support, so the convolution sum is empty and lambda(ell)=0. The raw lambda_D has a prime ell with the opposite property, and therefore is not triply well-factorable.

Lichtman's Theorem 1.7 states two prime-discrepancy estimates for triply well-factorable lambda(q). Its second clause uses modulus level x^((5-theta_Sel)/8-epsilon) and takes a supremum over 0<|a|<x^(1+epsilon), where theta_Sel is the paper's exponent toward Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture. Thus a residue N comparable to x is within that stated residue range. The preceding support argument proves that the raw lambda_D does not satisfy the theorem's weight hypothesis whenever the chosen level is greater than x^(1/2), as in the setup above. Therefore adequate residue uniformity does not repair the coefficient-slot mismatch.

Runbo Li's Theorem 1.1 states that, for divisor-bounded lambda_1 and lambda_2 and the two displayed inequalities on Q_1,Q_2, the bilinearly weighted prime discrepancy is bounded by x(log x)^(-A) for any fixed nonzero integer a. A quantity N which varies with x and is comparable to x is not a fixed integer in this quantifier, so the theorem statement gives no required uniform estimate in that residue.

There is a separate range obstruction even if the residue issue is ignored. If ell=q_1q_2 is prime, unique factorization gives either (q_1,q_2)=(ell,1) or (1,ell). In the first case Q_1>=ell and Q_2>=1, so Q_1^2Q_2<x^(1-epsilon) implies ell^2<x^(1-epsilon), hence ell<x^(1/2-epsilon/2). In the second case Q_1>=1 and Q_2>=ell, so Q_1^7Q_2^12<x^(4-epsilon) implies ell^12<x^(4-epsilon), hence ell<x^(1/3-epsilon/12). But for ell>D>=2x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B), the ratio of ell to x^(1/2-epsilon/2) is at least 2x^(epsilon/2)(log x)^(-B), which tends to infinity. Therefore the first alternative fails, and the second, being still smaller, fails as well. This proves the direct bilinear range mismatch.

The proof has checked only the hypotheses of the two published theorems against the raw weight and residue. It makes no claim that other decompositions or new theorems are impossible, which proves the final scope sentence.

glossary.Q_lvl: the proposed level of distribution x^(vartheta_AP)
glossary.lambda_D: the raw modulus weight d mapped to mu(d)psi(d/D_*)Phi(d/D)
glossary.vartheta_AP: a fixed exponent strictly between one half and one

3c92603bdcab54d5.title: Fix real numbers L>=1 and epsilon>0 and a real number H>=2. Let C be a nonzero integer with |C|<=H^L. Let N_0(C;H) be the number of ordered tuples
3c92603bdcab54d5.author: slava chan
3c92603bdcab54d5.statement:
Fix real numbers L>=1 and epsilon>0 and a real number H>=2. Let C be a nonzero integer with |C|<=H^L. Let N_0(C;H) be the number of ordered tuples
(r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4,b_1,b_2,b_3)
such that r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4 are pairwise distinct primes in [H^2,2H^2), b_1,b_2,b_3 are nonzero integers with |b_i|<=H, and
C=r_4(b_1r_2r_3+b_2r_1r_3+b_3r_1r_2).
Then
N_0(C;H)<<_{L,epsilon} H^{5+epsilon}
uniformly in C and H.

More generally, fix B>=0. Give each such tuple a nonnegative weight at most (log(2H))^B, and let L_H(C) be any nonnegative function supported on the nonzero integers C with |C|<=H^L and satisfying
sum_C L_H(C)<=H^9(log(2H))^B.
Then the weighted b_4=0 aggregate satisfies
sum_C L_H(C) sum_{tuples counted by N_0(C;H)} weight(tuple)
<<_{L,B,epsilon} H^{14+epsilon}.
Thus a common left-carrier mass of size H^{9+o(1)} pays the restored-fourth-frequency boundary b_4=0 at the H^{14+o(1)} scale.
3c92603bdcab54d5.proof:
Fix a tuple counted by N_0(C;H). Since r_4 divides C and C is nonzero, the number of possible r_4 is at most the number of distinct prime divisors of C. This is at most log_2|C| when |C|>=2, and is zero when |C|=1. Hence there are O_L(log(2H)) choices for r_4. Put N=C/r_4.

There are fewer than 2H^2 choices for r_1, and fewer than (2H+1)^3 choices for the ordered triple (b_1,b_2,b_3). For fixed r_4,r_1,b_1,b_2,b_3, every solution satisfies the exact factorization
(b_1r_2+b_2r_1)(b_1r_3+b_3r_1)
=b_1N+b_2b_3r_1^2.
Indeed expansion of the left side is
b_1^2r_2r_3+b_1b_3r_2r_1+b_1b_2r_1r_3+b_2b_3r_1^2,
while multiplying the carrier equation divided by r_4 by b_1 gives the first three terms.

The integer M=b_1N+b_2b_3r_1^2 on the right is nonzero for every counted tuple. If M were zero, the displayed product would be zero. Then either b_1r_2+b_2r_1=0 or b_1r_3+b_3r_1=0. In the first case r_1 divides b_1r_2. Since r_1 and r_2 are distinct primes, r_1 divides b_1, which is impossible because 0<|b_1|<=H<r_1. The second case is identical.

For fixed nonzero M, there are at most 2 tau(|M|) ordered integer factor pairs (A,D) with AD=M. Once A=b_1r_2+b_2r_1 is fixed, the nonzero integer b_1 makes r_2=(A-b_2r_1)/b_1 unique. Once D=b_1r_3+b_3r_1 is fixed, r_3=(D-b_3r_1)/b_1 is unique. Thus the number of possible (r_2,r_3) is at most 2 tau(|M|).

We use the elementary divisor bound: for every delta>0 there is a constant c_delta such that tau(n)<=c_delta n^delta for every positive integer n. To prove it, choose P=2^{1/delta}. For a prime p>P and an integer a>=1, a+1<=2^a<p^{delta a}. For each of the finitely many primes p<=P, the quantity sup_{a>=0}(a+1)p^{-delta a} is finite. Multiplying these finitely many suprema and the inequalities for p>P over the prime factorization of n proves the bound.

Here
|M|<=H|C/r_4|+H^2(2H^2)^2
<=H^{L+1}+4H^6.
Choose delta sufficiently small in terms of L and epsilon. The divisor bound gives tau(|M|)<<_{L,epsilon}H^{epsilon/2}. Also log(2H)<<_epsilon H^{epsilon/2}. Multiplying the choices for r_4, r_1, the three frequencies, and the factor pair yields
N_0(C;H)<<_{L,epsilon}H^{epsilon/2} H^2 H^3 H^{epsilon/2}
<<_{L,epsilon}H^{5+epsilon}.
All primality, interval, and pairwise-distinctness requirements only decrease this upper bound.

For the weighted assertion, apply the first bound with epsilon replaced by epsilon/3. The tuple weight contributes at most (log(2H))^B and the total L_H-mass contributes at most H^9(log(2H))^B. Hence the aggregate is at most
H^9(log(2H))^B (log(2H))^B O_{L,epsilon}(H^{5+epsilon/3}).
For fixed B and epsilon, (log(2H))^{2B}<<_{B,epsilon}H^{2epsilon/3}. This gives the claimed O_{L,B,epsilon}(H^{14+epsilon}) bound.

glossary.L_H(C): an arbitrary nonnegative common left-carrier weight at scale H
glossary.N_0(C;H): the number of ordered b_4=0 four-prime carrier packets at fixed C and scale H
glossary.weight(tuple): the nonnegative right-packet weight attached to a counted b_4=0 tuple

3d10fd30e2a42246.title: EXACT MIXED-FOURIER GRAM AND THE RATIONAL-SLOPE EXCEPTIONAL LOCUS
3d10fd30e2a42246.author: slava chan
3d10fd30e2a42246.proof:
Normalized Parseval applied to (1) gives
[
 sum_rwidehat g_{h,c}(r)
 overline{widehat g_{h',c'}(r)}
 ={1over p}sum_x g_{h,c}(x)overline{g_{h',c'}(x)}.
]
The summand vanishes at (x=0), while for (x
e0) it is
[
 e_p((hc^{-1}-h'c'^{-1})x^{-1}).
]
Inversion permutes (mathbb F_p^	imes). If
(hc^{-1}=h'c'^{-1}), equivalently (hc'=h'c), the sum over (x
e0) is (p-1). Otherwise it is the sum of a nontrivial additive character over (mathbb F_p^	imes), hence equals (-1). Division by (p) proves (2).

Fact (4f9aec67f5be35db), or the same one-line inversion calculation, gives
[
 widehat g_{h,c}(0)=-1/p
]
for every nonzero (h,c). The contribution of (r=0) to the Gram is therefore (p^{-2}). Subtracting it from (2) proves (3), and the off-exceptional bound follows because
[
 p^{-1}+p^{-2}le2/p.
]

For the source specialization, fact (4f9aec67f5be35db) shows that the exact (p)-local phase after writing (d=pm) is
[
 e_p(mathscr A h v^{-1}m^{-1}q^{-1})
 =e_p((mathscr A h)(vm)^{-1}q^{-1}).
]
Thus it is (g_{mathscr A h,c}(q)) with (c=vm). For a second row it is (g_{mathscr A h',c'}(q)). The exceptional congruence from (4) is
[
 mathscr A h c'=mathscr A h'cpmod p.
]
The selected prime does not divide (mathscr A), so cancellation of that common unit yields (5). The final scope sentence records the remaining global summations absent from this exact local identity.

glossary.mixed Fourier Gram: The inner product over nonzero additive dual frequencies of two completed inverse-phase rows.
glossary.rational-slope collision: The congruence h c'=h' c modulo the selected nonresonant prime.

3d29c397c4c006e4.title: SIEGEL-WALFISZ-NORMALIZED COUNTABLE PROJECTIVE EXTENSION OF THE LITERAL MARKED HC ROW. Adopt the hypotheses and notation of fact fcba64a06e489c96 on one sampled dyadic p,d',m rectangle, and put c_*=cR_kappa and v=d'm. Let C_D=||Psi_D||_infinity, C_M=||Psi_M||_infinity, H_M=max(1,C_M), and let L_lit be a uniform upper bound for the absolute value of A_lit on the frozen block. Define an auxiliary already-folded coefficient for every selected prime p, including p|c_*, by
3d29c397c4c006e4.author: slava chan
3d29c397c4c006e4.statement:
SIEGEL-WALFISZ-NORMALIZED COUNTABLE PROJECTIVE EXTENSION OF THE LITERAL MARKED HC ROW. Adopt the hypotheses and notation of fact fcba64a06e489c96 on one sampled dyadic p,d',m rectangle, and put c_*=cR_kappa and v=d'm. Let C_D=||Psi_D||_infinity, C_M=||Psi_M||_infinity, H_M=max(1,C_M), and let L_lit be a uniform upper bound for the absolute value of A_lit on the frozen block. Define an auxiliary already-folded coefficient for every selected prime p, including p|c_*, by
Vtilde_{q,kappa,h}(p,v)
 =-1/2 1_{(v,c_*)=1} sum_{d'm=v}
 b_{P,c_*}^{rho}(d')rho_{1/2}(m)
 Psi_D(pd')Psi_M(m)
 A_lit(q,kappa,hpv;(ell-kappa hpv)/q),                            (1)
with the same smooth sampled supports as in fact fcba64a06e489c96 but without imposing (p,c_*)=1. On primes with (p,c_*)=1, (1) equals the actual unrestricted marked-row coefficient C_{q,kappa,h}^{mark}(p,v) of that fact.

There are countably many indices (j,k), real frequencies
theta_{j,k}=tau_j+sigma_k,                                       (2)
prime modes
A^*_{j,k}(p)=1_{p prime}1_{P<=p<2P}
 p^(i theta_{j,k})/(1+|theta_{j,k}|),                            (3)
cofactor modes
B^*_{j,k}(v)
 =H_M^(-1)v^(i tau_j)1_{(v,c_*)=1}
  sum_{d'|v}b_{P,c_*}^{rho}(d')rho_{1/2}(v/d')
  d'^(i sigma_k)Psi_M(v/d'),                                    (4)
and outer coefficients
Lambda^*_{j,k;q,kappa,h}
 =-H_M lambda_{j,q,kappa,h}a_k(1+|theta_{j,k}|)/2                (5)
such that, for every selected p and sampled v,
Vtilde_{q,kappa,h}(p,v)
 =sum_{j,k in Z}Lambda^*_{j,k;q,kappa,h}
  A^*_{j,k}(p)B^*_{j,k}(v).                                     (6)
The series is absolutely and uniformly convergent,
sum_{j,k}sup_{q,kappa,h}|Lambda^*_{j,k;q,kappa,h}|
 <<(log x)^(C_SWproj),                                           (7)
and
|A^*_{j,k}(n)|<=1, |B^*_{j,k}(n)|<=tau(n),
|Vtilde_{q,kappa,h}(p,v)|<=(L_lit C_D C_M/2)tau(v).              (8)
Moreover every prime sequence A^*_{j,k} satisfies Maynard's Siegel-Walfisz condition uniformly in j,k and all displayed parameters.

Consequently all countable-projective, divisor-bound, reconstructed pointwise-bound, and uniform Siegel-Walfisz coefficient hypotheses of fact e3c0786d33d7e576 are fulfilled by (1). Whenever a family of these rows also satisfies that fact's factorable-modulus scale, squarefreeness, injectivity, reduced-residue, and modulus-coprimality hypotheses, including (s,c_*)=1 for every modulus s, its restriction (p,c_*)=1 is bounded by that theorem with L_proj given by (7) and L_W=L_lit C_D C_M/2. No such geometric hypotheses, omega_P=0 sector, complete HC-MED payment, or critical-tail conclusion are asserted here.
3d29c397c4c006e4.proof:
Fact 97cfedc76bcae0ad supplies the frequencies tau_j and coefficients lambda_{j,q,kappa,h}. Its derivative estimate holds for every fixed order. Applying three integrations by parts to the compactly periodized logarithmic profile used in its proof gives
sum_j sup_{q,kappa,h}|lambda_{j,q,kappa,h}|(1+|tau_j|)
 <<(log x)^(C_1)                                                 (9)
for a fixed exponent C_1: the jth coefficient is bounded by a fixed polylogarithm times (1+|j|)^(-3), while |tau_j| is comparable to |j|.

The same argument applies to the fixed smooth function Psi_D(e^y) in equation (2) of fact fcba64a06e489c96. Its periodized Fourier coefficients satisfy
sum_k|a_k|(1+|sigma_k|)<<1.                                     (10)
Since
1+|theta_{j,k}|<=1+|tau_j|+|sigma_k|
 <=(1+|tau_j|)(1+|sigma_k|),                                    (11)
equations (9)-(10) give (7) from definition (5).
