Insert the two exact Fourier expansions into (1), substitute m=v/d', and use (2)-(5). The factors H_M and 1+|theta_{j,k}| cancel between the outer coefficient and the normalized modes, giving (6) exactly. The weighted absolute estimates (9)-(10), together with the finite divisor sum, justify all rearrangements and uniform convergence. No prime-unit indicator is inserted into A^*: equation (1) is deliberately an auxiliary extension to all selected primes. When (p,c_*)=1 it is identical to the actual coefficient in fact fcba64a06e489c96.

The first two bounds in (8) follow as follows. The prime-mode bound is immediate. Facts 5999a1878276ac78 and e59f666ecac4d4cb give |rho_{1/2}|<=1 and |b_{P,c_*}^{rho}|<=1. Therefore the unnormalized divisor sum in (4) has modulus at most C_M tau(v), and division by H_M>=C_M proves |B^*_{j,k}(v)|<=tau(v). Applying the same termwise estimate directly to (1), using |Psi_D|<=C_D, |Psi_M|<=C_M, and |A_lit|<=L_lit, gives
|Vtilde_{q,kappa,h}(p,v)|<=(L_lit C_D C_M/2)tau(v),
which is the third bound in (8).

Fact 0025283165f465c4 states exactly that the normalized logarithmic prime twist
1_{p prime}1_{P<p<=2P}p^(i theta)/(1+|theta|)
satisfies Maynard's Siegel-Walfisz condition uniformly for every real theta. Endpoint conventions at p=P change at most one prime and are absorbed in the arbitrary-logarithmic bound. Apply it with theta=theta_{j,k}.

Finally, fact e3c0786d33d7e576 consumes an already-folded coefficient W_s(p,v) directly; it does not multiply it by an additional Ramaré cofactor. Taking W_s to be (1), equations (6)-(8) provide exactly its coefficient hypotheses. Under the explicitly required condition (s,c_*)=1, its all-primes auxiliary row uses the extension (1), and its final p-dividing-c comparison with c=c_* restores (p,c_*)=1. On that restricted row, (1) equals the actual literal coefficient, so there is no duplicated arithmetic factor.

glossary.A^*_{j,k}(p): The normalized logarithmic prime twist used in Maynard's Siegel-Walfisz slot.
glossary.B^*_{j,k}(v): The cofactor divisor mode normalized to be bounded by tau(v).
glossary.C_D: The supremum norm of the fixed d-cell cutoff Psi_D.
glossary.C_M: The supremum norm of the fixed m-cell cutoff Psi_M.
glossary.C_SWproj: A fixed exponent controlling the weighted projective l1 norm.
glossary.L_lit: A uniform supremum bound for the literal smooth amplitude on the frozen block.
glossary.Lambda^*_{j,k;q,kappa,h}: The outer projective coefficient after absorbing frequency and cutoff normalizations.
glossary.Vtilde_{q,kappa,h}(p,v): The auxiliary already-folded literal amplitude extended to selected primes dividing c_* by omitting only the prime-unit restriction.
glossary.theta_{j,k}: The combined logarithmic Fourier frequency tau_j+sigma_k.

3d343e417a673e84.title: ALL-ROUGH-COUNT SIGNED LEAF IDENTITY, FORCE-A-LEAF DEFICIT, AND CURRENT TRACE-SLOT AUDIT
3d343e417a673e84.author: slava chan
3d343e417a673e84.statement:
ALL-ROUGH-COUNT SIGNED LEAF IDENTITY, FORCE-A-LEAF DEFICIT, AND CURRENT TRACE-SLOT AUDIT.

Let mathcal Z_0 be a finite set of records z. Each z has a label lambda, positive integers d and r with mu(d)mu(r) nonzero, a real coefficient
w_z=mu(d)mu(r)q_z
with q_z real, and one frozen parent P(z) in a finite set mathcal P. The factor q_z may contain a conjugate-paired Poisson h-phase, fixed target, smooth weights, source masks, and every other provenance coordinate; it will not be altered.

For every label lambda choose real numbers
2<=L_lambda<=S_lambda, L_lambda<Z_lambda,
and a positive integer J_lambda such that every r at that label satisfies
r>S_lambda, Z_lambda^(J_lambda+1)>r.
Define the exact marker coefficients c_A(r),c_B(r),c_{C_j}(r) by fact 7c1f38cfbb8d0569: c_A is the interval-prime identity when an (L_lambda,Z_lambda)-prime divides r; c_B is the independent-height stopping identity when no interval prime divides r and v_{L_lambda}(r)>S_lambda; otherwise r=v p_1...p_j uniquely with v<=S_lambda and distinct
Z_lambda<=p_1<...<p_j,
and c_{C_j}(r)=(-1)^jmu(v). All inapplicable coefficients are zero. Then
mu(r)=c_A(r)+c_B(r)+sum_{j=1}^{J_lambda}c_{C_j}(r).           (1)

Put J_max=max_lambda J_lambda, with absent C_j coefficients interpreted as zero, and define
T_{P,X}=sum_{z:P(z)=P}mu(d)q_z c_X(r)
for P in mathcal P and X in {A,B,C_1,...,C_{J_max}}. Then the exact exhaustive signed identity is
T_all=sum_{z in mathcal Z_0}w_z
     =sum_{P in mathcal P}
       (T_{P,A}+T_{P,B}+sum_{j=1}^{J_max}T_{P,C_j}).          (2)
Every q_z and every frozen parent is unchanged. In particular, applying this theorem to the real high Poisson atoms and nine parents constructed in fact 77d7a3419a07305c gives a literal common refinement of the 60b high mask, the swap-closed least-tag anatomy, and the full A/B/C_1/C_2/C_3/... rough-count alphabet. It does not rename the high anomaly as terminal or C2.

Let mathcal E be the nonempty primary leaves in (2), M_leaf=|mathcal E|, and suppose
T_all<=-A_0+epsilon_0
with A_0>epsilon_0. Then some leaf ell in mathcal E satisfies
T_ell<=(-A_0+epsilon_0)/M_leaf.                               (3)
Since
M_leaf<=|mathcal P|(J_max+2),                                (4)
a quantitative total anomaly always forces one quantitative all-alphabet leaf, although its type is not predetermined.

More generally, let mathcal S be any selected subcollection, put
T_S=sum_{ell in mathcal S}T_ell,
and let T_comp be the sum over ell outside mathcal S. For 0<theta<=1 and real rho_err,
T_S<=-theta A_0+rho_err                                      (5)
is equivalent to
T_comp>=T_all+theta A_0-rho_err.                             (6)
If only T_all<=-A_0+epsilon_0 is used, the sharp uniform sufficient aggregate bound is
T_comp>=-(1-theta)A_0+epsilon_0-rho_err.                     (7)
A collection of leafwise lower bounds
T_ell>=-B_ell for ell outside mathcal S                      (8)
is sufficient precisely through the summed allowance
sum_{ell outside mathcal S}B_ell
 <=(1-theta)A_0-epsilon_0+rho_err.                           (9)
The aggregate condition (7) is weaker than requiring (8) leaf by leaf.

The following is the exact status of currently verified analytic inputs on the raised-stopping scale. Fix kappa in (0,1/100), sigma_1=kappa/100, a base Q, and
1<=beta<=6/5-2kappa,
R=Q^beta, H=R/Q,
L=H Q^sigma_1,
S_0=H^2Q^(3sigma_1),
Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma_1).
Fact e18b670f5d48f500 verifies that these parameters give the five primary marker types
A,B,C_1,C_2,C_3.

(i) Fact 664a92777dc5f5db gives a power saving for the complete interval-prime coefficient A only when the leaf has its displayed unit-target reciprocal phase, divisor-bounded separated coefficients, and scaled-smooth four-variable weight.

(ii) Fact 533acf4056cf5bee gives a power saving for the complete stopping coefficient B only when the leaf has its displayed reciprocal phase, divisor-bounded separated coefficients, and scaled-smooth weight.

Neither theorem admits an arbitrary bounded joint least-tag parent selector depending on the full arithmetic tuple. Therefore boundedness of P(z) alone does not verify (8) for the parent-refined A or B leaves in (2). They become paid complements only after an additional coefficient-separation theorem with total norm x^(o(1)), or a trace theorem uniform in the literal joint parent selector.

(iii) For a one-rough leaf r=vp at total scale B=VP=Q^beta, the first term in the direct one-prime bound of fact a0cf2b6037398f9f is
Q^(11/10)B^(4/5)=Q^(11/10+4beta/5).                          (10)
It is a fixed-power saving from Q^2 only when beta<9/8. At beta>=9/8, (10) is at least Q^2, so that verified bound, applied directly, supplies no power saving. Since the forced high band of fact 77d7a3419a07305c begins at beta=9/8 up to fixed buffers, the present one-rough estimate does not pay the C1 complement throughout that band.

(iv) If a selected leaf is genuinely C2 and its literal sum is negative of size at least c x(log x)^(-B_0), fact 707345f56faff29e conditionally routes it to a full-conductor four-prime carrier only through its buffered R<=x^(7/12-kappa') range and still leaves modular-window localization open.

Thus the verified stopping and interval-prime traces identify potentially payable unparented smooth complements below beta=6/5, but they do not yet prove the complement inequalities (7)--(9) for the literal common refinement. No current fact forces C2; the unconditional conclusion is the all-leaf statement (3).
3d343e417a673e84.proof:
Fact 7c1f38cfbb8d0569 proves the pointwise identity (1), including exact signs and exhaustive rough counts. Multiplying it by the unchanged real factor mu(d)q_z and summing first over the unique frozen parent and then over z proves (2). Since the marker is inserted after the parent is frozen, internal interval-prime and stopping copies retain the original parent and q_z.

There are at most |mathcal P|(J_max+2) formal parent-marker pairs, proving (4). If every nonempty leaf exceeded the right side of (3), their sum in (2) would exceed -A_0+epsilon_0, a contradiction. This proves (3).

The identity T_all=T_S+T_comp makes (5) equivalent to (6) by rearrangement. Under only the upper bound for T_all, the largest possible right side of (6) is the right side of (7), proving the sharp uniform sufficient condition. From (8),
T_comp>=-sum B_ell.
This implies (7) exactly under (9). The aggregate bound can hold through cancellation among complement leaves even when some individual lower bound fails, so it is weaker than the leafwise collection.

The raised-stopping five-way geometry is the statement of fact e18b670f5d48f500. Parts (i) and (ii) quote the exact coefficient classes in facts 664a92777dc5f5db and 533acf4056cf5bee. Their hypotheses list separated one-variable coefficients and a bounded scaled-smooth weight; neither conclusion quantifies over arbitrary tuple-dependent zero-one selectors. The parent P in fact 77d7a3419a07305c depends jointly on labels and least eligible divisors. Merely multiplying a trace by that selector therefore leaves the stated theorem class unless a further separation or uniform-selector result is proved. This is a theorem-slot mismatch, not a cancellation no-go.

For (iii), substitute B=Q^beta into the first displayed term of fact a0cf2b6037398f9f. Its exponent is 11/10+4beta/5. The strict inequality
11/10+4beta/5<2
is equivalent to beta<9/8. Since the cited upper bound is a sum of nonnegative terms, at beta>=9/8 its direct numerical value is not a power saving from Q^2. The high-band relation beta=2rho+o(1) is verified in fact 77d7a3419a07305c. Part (iv) is exactly the conditional scope of fact 707345f56faff29e.

No step asserts that failure of a direct theorem application is an arithmetic counterexample. The final conclusion records only which complement estimates have and have not been verifier-gated.

glossary.B_ell: a nonnegative lower-deficit allowance for complement leaf ell
glossary.J_lambda: the maximum rough-prime count at label lambda
glossary.M_leaf: the total number of nonempty primary parent-marker leaves
glossary.T_{P,A}: the interval-prime leaf sum with parent P
glossary.T_{P,B}: the stopping leaf sum with parent P
glossary.T_{P,C_j}: the j-rough-prime leaf sum with parent P
glossary.beta: the large-divisor exponent log R/log Q in the raised-stopping geometry
glossary.mathcal S: a selected collection of primary leaves
glossary.mathcal Z_0: a finite real atom family with frozen provenance parents

3da45f614a415600.title: PRIME-LOCAL MOBIUS TRACE FOLLOWED BY ABSOLUTE LONG-MODULUS SUMMATION: A STRICT-TOP NO-FIT. Adopt one signed projective block in fact ecd6325d7ef2bc37 with
3da45f614a415600.author: slava chan
3da45f614a415600.statement:
PRIME-LOCAL MOBIUS TRACE FOLLOWED BY ABSOLUTE LONG-MODULUS SUMMATION: A STRICT-TOP NO-FIT. Adopt one signed projective block in fact ecd6325d7ef2bc37 with
\[
 B=Q^\beta,\qquad \max\{\beta_m,7/6\}<\beta<6/5,
 \qquad F\leq H_P.
\]
Grant all of the following favorable hypotheses, which are stronger than the actual complete source: every supported n is prime; the residue epsilon L_src h is nonzero modulo n for every supported h; the q-profile in each row has the bounded-variation norm required by fact c23ca78883ba83d9; the exact outer gcd g is squarefree and satisfies g<=Q^{C_0} for one fixed C_0; and the residual composite-modulus cofactor obstruction of fact 79ffbcb2ffe4049f is absent. Apply fact c23ca78883ba83d9 with auxiliary squarefree modulus c=g to the q-sum separately for each fixed pair (n,h), and then take absolute values in n and h. Its displayed admissible saving satisfies
\[
 0<\delta_{\rm tr}<{19\over12000}.                         \tag{1}
\]
The resulting normalized source-block bound is
\[
 \boxed{|T_F|\ll BQ^{1-\delta_{\rm tr}+o(1)}.}            \tag{2}
\]
In order for (2) to imply the DOUBLE-MU-RECIP-N target Q^{2-delta_D} for some fixed delta_D>0, it is necessary that
\[
 \delta_{\rm tr}>\beta-1+\delta_D.                        \tag{3}
\]
But beta>7/6 makes the right side exceed 1/6, while 19/12000<1/6. Therefore PRIME-ROW-ABS does not furnish any fixed-power DOUBLE-MU-RECIP-N saving in the displayed strict-top chamber, even under the favorable prime-modulus, unit-target, and polynomial squarefree-g grants.

This is a no-fit only for the operation 'apply c23ca78883ba83d9 rowwise and sum the n,h rows absolutely.' It is not a lower bound for the literal source. It does not exclude simultaneous n-averaging, cancellation from mu(n), a composite-modulus trace theorem, a pre-Cauchy vector form, or a two-axis Vaughan/dispersion decomposition. No strict-top payment, post-A conclusion, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
3da45f614a415600.proof:
For a prime row n asymp B, set the auxiliary modulus in fact c23ca78883ba83d9 to c=g. The statement grants exactly that g is squarefree and g<=Q^{C_0}. The theorem therefore applies to
\[
 \sum_{q\asymp Q}\mu(q){\bf1}_{(q,g)=1}A(q)
 K_{n,\epsilon L_{\rm src}h}(q).
\]
Its trace K_{n,\epsilon L_src h}(q) is defined to be zero when n divides q and otherwise equals e_n(epsilon L_src h inverse(q)). Hence its zero extension supplies exactly the additional source gate (q,n)=1; together with c=g, all q-side coprimality is retained.

Since beta<6/5, the prime-size hypothesis n<=2Q^{6/5} holds after the harmless dyadic support constant. Since beta>1, its lower-prime hypothesis holds with a fixed positive zeta. The theorem states that one may take any fixed saving smaller than
\[
 {1\over2}\min\{\zeta/50,19/6000,1/40\},
\]
which is always at most 19/12000. This proves (1) and gives Q^{1-delta_tr+o(1)} for each fixed (n,h) row after including the bounded-variation profile norm.

There are O(B) possible n and O(F) integers h in the signed block. The h-coefficient in fact ecd6325d7ef2bc37 has supremum at most its variation norm, and that norm is normalized to one on the present projective block. Taking absolute values in n and h and using F/H_P<=1 gives
\[
 {1\over H_P}\sum_{n\asymp B}\sum_{F\leq|h|<2F}
 Q^{1-\delta_{\rm tr}+o(1)}
 \ll BQ^{1-\delta_{\rm tr}+o(1)},
\]
which is (2). With B=Q^beta, the exponent in (2) is 1+beta-delta_tr. For it to be at most 2-delta_D, one must have (3). The inequalities beta-1>1/6 and delta_tr<19/12000<1/6 are incompatible.

The actual source is harder than the granted model: n is squarefree composite in general, the target can be nonunit, and fact 79ffbcb2ffe4049f proves that splitting the residual cofactor phase into residue classes destroys the prime-local bounded-variation saving. These observations are not needed for the exponent contradiction, which already holds in the favorable prime-row model. Because the argument compares only the displayed upper bound with the required target, it proves exactly the scoped method no-fit and no lower bound.

glossary.PRIME-ROW-ABS: The method that applies a prime-local q-row estimate for each n and then sums the n-rows absolutely.
glossary.delta_tr: The fixed saving exponent in the prime-local Möbius reciprocal-trace theorem c23ca78883ba83d9.

3dabf494e3ed99fd.title: SHARP BALANCED TWO-FREE THEOREM-RIGHT-HAND-SIDE NO-FIT IN THE LARGE-EFFECTIVE-MODULUS MOBIUS ROUTING. Fix 0<kappa<1/2 and put eta=kappa/20. In fact df45be7aead3cec9 restrict to an effective modulus m_eff comparable to Q, so theta_eff=1+o(1). Its buffered medium exponents are a=4eta+o(1) and b=1/2-4eta+o(1). In the j=3 term of the exact truncated-inverse identity, consider a dyadic factor cell in which d_1=d_2=d_3=1 and the two unweighted factors u_1,u_2 both have scale Q^(1/2+o(1)), with u_1u_2 on the Q-scale. This cell is in the composite-Mobius multi-free residual: no subcollection has product scale in [Q^a,Q^b], the maximal carrier below Q^b is the unit carrier, and exactly two nonunit unweighted factors are omitted
3dabf494e3ed99fd.author: slava chan
3dabf494e3ed99fd.statement:
SHARP BALANCED TWO-FREE THEOREM-RIGHT-HAND-SIDE NO-FIT IN THE LARGE-EFFECTIVE-MODULUS MOBIUS ROUTING. Fix 0<kappa<1/2 and put eta=kappa/20. In fact df45be7aead3cec9 restrict to an effective modulus m_eff comparable to Q, so theta_eff=1+o(1). Its buffered medium exponents are a=4eta+o(1) and b=1/2-4eta+o(1). In the j=3 term of the exact truncated-inverse identity, consider a dyadic factor cell in which d_1=d_2=d_3=1 and the two unweighted factors u_1,u_2 both have scale Q^(1/2+o(1)), with u_1u_2 on the Q-scale. This cell is in the composite-Mobius multi-free residual: no subcollection has product scale in [Q^a,Q^b], the maximal carrier below Q^b is the unit carrier, and exactly two nonunit unweighted factors are omitted.

For this cell, every direct grouping admitted by fact b390149c13836271 has a right-hand side of order at least Q^(1-o(1)), and each direct choice of one of u_1,u_2 as the free factor in fact 9be4b1c96a2620dc has a right-hand side of order Q^(1+o(1)). Hence neither verified supplier certifies Q^(1-delta) for any fixed delta>0 on this balanced two-free cell. Grouping u_1u_2 into one variable does not repair the Type-I application because its convolution coefficient is not the unweighted coefficient required in fact 9be4b1c96a2620dc. This is a theorem-right-hand-side no-fit, not a lower bound for the exponential sum.
3dabf494e3ed99fd.proof:
With theta_eff=1+o(1), the definitions in fact df45be7aead3cec9 give
a=max{2eta,1-theta_eff+4eta}=4eta+o(1)
and
b=min{theta_eff-4eta,1-theta_eff/2-4eta}=1/2-4eta+o(1).
Choose Q sufficiently large that 0<a<b<1/2. In the j=3 term of the exact identity there are three Mobius-bearing factors d_i and two unweighted factors u_i. The cell d_1=d_2=d_3=1, u_i of scale Q^(1/2+o(1)), u_1u_2 of scale Q is an allowed dyadic scale cell of that term. A subcollection of its five factor positions has scale 1, Q^(1/2+o(1)), or Q^(1+o(1)). The first is below Q^a and the other two are above Q^b. Thus no subcollection lies in the medium window. Among subcollections of scale at most Q^b, the inclusion-maximal one contains precisely the three unit d_i positions and has numerical product one. Both u_i are omitted, proving the stated residual classification.

Now inspect fact b390149c13836271. Apart from unit factors, a two-group partition has Y on one of the three scales 1, Q^(1/2+o(1)), Q^(1+o(1)); the complementary scale U satisfies UY comparable to Q. If Y has unit scale, its first bracketed term UY^(1/2) has scale Q^(1+o(1)). If Y has scale Q^(1/2+o(1)), then U has the same scale and m_eff has scale Q, so the second bracketed term is
U^(1/2)Y m_eff^(1/4)=Q^(1/4+o(1))Q^(1/2+o(1))Q^(1/4+o(1))=Q^(1+o(1)).
If Y has scale Q^(1+o(1)), the required condition 4Y<m_eff fails after choosing the cell and effective-modulus dyadic constants with Y comparable to Q and m_eff comparable to Q; even if one ignores that failure, this grouping supplies no displayed fixed-power corollary. Exchanging the two groups produces the same list. Therefore no direct b390 grouping has a certified fixed-power right-hand side.

For fact 9be4b1c96a2620dc, choose u_1 as the otherwise-unweighted free factor b. Then B has scale Q^(1/2+o(1)), while the carrier a contains u_2 and the unit d_i, so A has scale Q^(1/2+o(1)). Its two retained terms have scales
AB/m_eff=Q^(o(1)),  A m_eff^(1/2)=Q^(1+o(1)).
The second is critical. The same calculation holds with u_2 free. If u_1u_2 is folded together, the resulting coefficient counts factorizations from the two fixed unweighted positions and is not coefficient one; fact 9be4b1c96a2620dc explicitly requires b to be otherwise unweighted. Thus this fold is outside that theorem's hypotheses. These cases exhaust direct uses of the two suppliers on the displayed factor positions and prove the no-fit. No estimate from below for the signed sum has been used.

glossary.balanced two-free cell: The j=3 truncated-inverse dyadic cell with three unit Mobius-bearing factors and two unweighted factors of scale Q^(1/2), whose product lies on the Q-scale.

3db20da48fdfac31.title: LITERAL CENTERED-RESIDUE EXPANSION AND CRITICAL-GRAM SUPPLIER INTERFACE. Assume the hypotheses and notation of facts ffa8f6d3f766b9f5 and 7264046d8776d59f. For a residue a modulo S and a nonzero residue k modulo S define
3db20da48fdfac31.author: slava chan
3db20da48fdfac31.statement:
LITERAL CENTERED-RESIDUE EXPANSION AND CRITICAL-GRAM SUPPLIER INTERFACE. Assume the hypotheses and notation of facts ffa8f6d3f766b9f5 and 7264046d8776d59f. For a residue a modulo S and a nonzero residue k modulo S define
Delta_{S,k}(a)=S*1_{(a,S)=1}e_S(kNa^{-1})-c_S(kN),
where the first term is zero when (a,S)>1. Then the complete signed response has the exact literal expansion
Y_{S,bold t}(k)=sum_{q_1,q_2: [q_1,q_2]=S} c_{q_1,q_2}(bold t) sum_{h in cal H_mid: (q_1,q_2)|h} sum_w g_{h,bold t}(w) Delta_{S,k}(gamma_{q_1,q_2,h}-w).                                                        (1)
All restrictions in the predecessor definitions remain in force, so (1) retains the moving logarithms, both Mobius signs, the q_1,q_2,h aggregation, and the CRT translation before any norm.

Let cal S be any finite set of active total moduli S with S>=M_0. For each S in cal S let cal K_S be a set of nonzero residues modulo S satisfying |cal K_S|<=C_0 S/M_0, where C_0 is fixed. Define
cal G_{S,bold t}(cal K_S)=sum_{k in cal K_S}|Y_{S,bold t}(k)|^2
and
cal T_crit(cal S,{cal K_S})=sum_{S in cal S}S^{-2} integral_{R^2} sum_{k in cal K_S}B_{S,bold t}(k)Y_{S,bold t}(k)d bold t.                  (2)
Then
|cal T_crit(cal S,{cal K_S})| <<_{chi,C_0} sum_{S in cal S} M_0^{1/2}S^{-3/2} integral_{R^2} cal G_{S,bold t}(cal K_S)^{1/2}d bold t.        (3)
Moreover cal G is exactly the signed Dirichlet-kernel form in equation (7) of fact 7264046d8776d59f, with cal K=cal K_S. Consequently, for any A>0, the literal signed-family supplier estimate
sum_{S in cal S} M_0^{1/2}S^{-3/2} integral cal G_{S,bold t}(cal K_S)^{1/2}d bold t << xD(log x)^{-A}                                  (SUPPLIER_A)
implies the same xD(log x)^{-A} bound for the critical TMC contribution (2). This is an exact sufficient interface, not a proof of SUPPLIER_A. In view of fact a05e9cd7387e457c, SUPPLIER_A cannot be deduced uniformly from centering and the unit-inversion transform for arbitrary rows; its unresolved content is cancellation in the literal coefficient family displayed in (1).
3db20da48fdfac31.proof:
By equation (3) of fact 7264046d8776d59f, a fixed tuple q_1,q_2,h,w in H_{S,bold t}(z) occurs for precisely the residue
z congruent to gamma_{q_1,q_2,h}-w modulo S.                                      (4)
By equation (5) of that fact, the same coefficient occurs once in A_{S,bold t}(0)=sum_{z mod S}H_{S,bold t}(z). Substitute Z=SH-A(0) into equation (6) of that fact. The contribution of the fixed tuple to the part SH(u), summed over unit u, is
S*1_{(gamma-w,S)=1}e_S(kN(gamma-w)^{-1}).                    (5)
Its contribution through -A(0), which is independent of u, is
-sum_{u mod S,(u,S)=1}e_S(kNu^{-1}).                         (6)
Inversion permutes the unit residues, and multiplication by N also permutes them because (N,S)=1. Hence the sum in (6) is the Ramanujan sum c_S(kN). Combining (5) and (6), then summing all q_1,q_2,h,w coefficients with the unchanged c_{q_1,q_2}(bold t) and g_{h,bold t}(w), proves (1). In particular no absolute value has been inserted into any of those sums.

The pointwise estimate for B proved in fact ffa8f6d3f766b9f5 is |B_{S,bold t}(k)|<<_chi M_0. Therefore, using |cal K_S|<=C_0S/M_0,
(sum_{k in cal K_S}|B_{S,bold t}(k)|^2)^{1/2}<<_{chi,C_0}(SM_0)^{1/2}.              (7)
Apply Cauchy-Schwarz only to the already aggregated k-sum in (2). Equations (2) and (7) give, for each S,
S^{-2}|sum_{k in cal K_S}B(k)Y(k)|<<_{chi,C_0}M_0^{1/2}S^{-3/2}cal G_{S,bold t}(cal K_S)^{1/2}.                                      (8)
Integrating (8) in bold t and summing S proves (3). Equation (7) of fact 7264046d8776d59f identifies cal G with the incomplete signed Dirichlet-kernel Gram before any q_1,q_2,h triangle. Substitution of SUPPLIER_A into (3) proves its stated consequence. Finally, fact a05e9cd7387e457c constructs centered arbitrary rows with critical-frequency concentration, so it establishes the scoped warning that the missing supplier estimate must use the literal family (1).

glossary.C_0: a fixed positive constant controlling critical-band cardinality
glossary.Delta_{S,k}: the centered response of one physical residue: S times its unit inverse phase minus the Ramanujan mean
glossary.SUPPLIER_A: the normalized literal signed-family Gram estimate sufficient for an xD(log x)^{-A} critical contribution
glossary.cal G_{S,bold t}: the literal incomplete signed response Gram over cal K_S
glossary.cal K_S: a selected nonzero critical frequency set modulo S of cardinality at most C_0 S/M_0
glossary.cal S: a finite set of active total moduli at least M_0
glossary.cal T_crit: the TMC contribution restricted to the selected critical frequency sets

3dee3375b9261448.title: GA-SOURCE-PRIME-DESCENT-SLICE: EXACT q=pq_0 AMPLITUDE DESCENT CREATES A p-DIVISIBILITY LATTICE MASK. Let p,q_0,n be positive integers, let p be prime, let gcd(pq_0,n)=1, and let T be an integer. Let W(t,u) be any continuously differentiable compactly supported complex function on R^2. Define the one-variable amplitudes
3dee3375b9261448.author: slava chan
3dee3375b9261448.statement:
GA-SOURCE-PRIME-DESCENT-SLICE: EXACT q=pq_0 AMPLITUDE DESCENT CREATES A p-DIVISIBILITY LATTICE MASK. Let p,q_0,n be positive integers, let p be prime, let gcd(pq_0,n)=1, and let T be an integer. Let W(t,u) be any continuously differentiable compactly supported complex function on R^2. Define the one-variable amplitudes
F_{pq_0,n}(t)=W(t,(T-pq_0t)/n),                                 (1)
G^{(p)}_{q_0,n}(s)=W(s/p,(T-q_0s)/n).                           (2)
Use the Fourier convention
widehat F(xi)=integral_R F(t)e(-xi t)dt.                          (3)
Then
G^{(p)}_{q_0,n}(pt)=F_{pq_0,n}(t),                               (4)
widehat G^{(p)}_{q_0,n}(xi)
 =p widehat F_{pq_0,n}(p xi),                                    (5)
and hence, for every integer h,
widehat F_{pq_0,n}(h/n)
 ={1/p}widehat G^{(p)}_{q_0,n}(h/(pn)).                          (6)

At the discrete source level there is the exact bijection
{(t,u) in Z^2:pq_0t+nu=T}
 ->{(s,u) in Z^2:q_0s+nu=T, p divides s},
(t,u)->(pt,u).                                                   (7)
Consequently
sum_{pq_0t+nu=T}W(t,u)
 =sum_{q_0s+nu=T}1_{p divides s}W(s/p,u)                         (8)
 ={1/p}sum_{j (mod p)}
   sum_{q_0s+nu=T}e_p(js)W(s/p,u).                               (9)

Apply this to one fixed forward physical source fibre in fact f1cd394ea025163e, with q=pq_0. All logarithmic, smooth, dyadic, fixed-U and outer-row factors may be kept inside W, while factors constant in t,u remain outside. Equation (6) gives an exact q_0-rescaled representation of the original q-indexed Fourier amplitude, but equations (8)-(9) show that the corresponding discrete q_0 source is restricted by p divides s. Therefore the prime-descent alias of fact f1cd394ea025163e can be regarded as a q_0-phase row only together with this p-divisibility slice, or equivalently all p additive filter modes in (9).

There is no automatic factor 1/p from (9): on the actual image s=pt every character e_p(js) equals one, so the p terms reassemble exactly to the original source. Any recursive q-to-q_0 estimate must prove cancellation among the nonzero filter modes or estimate the p-divisible slice directly; deleting the mask changes the source.

This theorem is an exact change of variables and Fourier scaling only. It proves no cancellation for the p-filter modes, no estimate for the prime-descent alias, no common-core or one-end trace estimate, no C-HILBERT-OP-SUP, tail payment, or Goldbach.
3dee3375b9261448.proof:
Substitute s=pt in (2):
G^{(p)}_{q_0,n}(pt)
 =W(t,(T-pq_0t)/n)
 =F_{pq_0,n}(t),
proving (4).

For the Fourier transform, substitute s=pt and ds=p dt:
widehat G^{(p)}_{q_0,n}(xi)
 =integral_R W(s/p,(T-q_0s)/n)e(-xi s)ds
 =p integral_R W(t,(T-pq_0t)/n)e(-p xi t)dt
 =p widehat F_{pq_0,n}(p xi).
This proves (5), and xi=h/(pn) gives (6).

If pq_0t+nu=T, then s=pt is divisible by p and satisfies q_0s+nu=T. Conversely, if q_0s+nu=T and p divides s, then t=s/p is an integer and pq_0t+nu=T. These maps are inverse and preserve W through W(t,u)=W(s/p,u), proving (7)-(8).

The finite root-of-unity identity
1_{p divides s}={1/p}sum_{j (mod p)}e_p(js)
proves (9). On s=pt, every summand e_p(js) is one, proving the no-free-factor statement. Fact 1e357f0a9f079ca2 describes the literal source amplitude as a smooth compactly supported function of t and u=(T-qt)/n, with the remaining fixed labels as outer scalars, so the specialization retains those factors exactly. All exclusions follow.

glossary.G^{(p)}_{q_0,n}: The q_0-rescaled physical source amplitude obtained from the q=pq_0 amplitude by s=pt.
glossary.p-divisibility lattice mask: The exact restriction p divides s appearing after source-modulus descent.

3e326f797b2e04e4.title: FULL DYADIC FOURIER-AMPLITUDE COMPLETION OF THE BUFFERED NATURAL-FREQUENCY FIVE-LEAF TRANSFER. Fix the parameters Q,B,beta,kappa,sigma,eta,H_T,G,H_P,L,S_0,Z and the five natural-frequency deformations exactly as follows: 0<kappa<=1/100, sigma=kappa/100, 0<eta<sigma, 1<=beta<=6/5-2kappa, B=Q^beta, H_T=B/Q, H_P=H_T/G>0, Q^{-sigma+eta}<=G<=Q^{sigma-eta}, L=H_TQ^sigma, S_0=H_T^2Q^{3sigma}, Z=Q^{3/2-beta-3sigma}. Retain the factor scales, coefficients, cutoffs, prime ordering and product scale B of facts 664a92777dc5f5db, 533acf4056cf5bee, 2ff1c15aef183bac, 3b1bda56ad927c5e and 0576f567200d41f1
3e326f797b2e04e4.author: slava chan
3e326f797b2e04e4.statement:
FULL DYADIC FOURIER-AMPLITUDE COMPLETION OF THE BUFFERED NATURAL-FREQUENCY FIVE-LEAF TRANSFER. Fix the parameters Q,B,beta,kappa,sigma,eta,H_T,G,H_P,L,S_0,Z and the five natural-frequency deformations exactly as follows: 0<kappa<=1/100, sigma=kappa/100, 0<eta<sigma, 1<=beta<=6/5-2kappa, B=Q^beta, H_T=B/Q, H_P=H_T/G>0, Q^{-sigma+eta}<=G<=Q^{sigma-eta}, L=H_TQ^sigma, S_0=H_T^2Q^{3sigma}, Z=Q^{3/2-beta-3sigma}. Retain the factor scales, coefficients, cutoffs, prime ordering and product scale B of facts 664a92777dc5f5db, 533acf4056cf5bee, 2ff1c15aef183bac, 3b1bda56ad927c5e and 0576f567200d41f1.
For every dyadic integer scale F>=1, replace the h-support by F<=|h|<2F, use |h|/F as the scaled h-coordinate, but retain the literal Poisson prefactor H_P^{-1}. Suppose that after extracting a scalar omega_F, the remaining amplitudes form a fixed uniformly bounded scaled-smooth family, and that for every integer J_0>=1 one has |omega_F|<=C_{J_0}min(1,(F/H_P)^{-J_0}), with constants uniform in all other parameters. Sum each of the five deformed traces over all dyadic F>=1. In A retain its unit phase numerator A_q modulo q. In B,C1,C2,C3 retain a fixed nonzero target A with |A|<=Q^{C_A}.
Then, for Q sufficiently large, each complete dyadic-frequency sum is O(Q^{2-delta}) for some delta=delta(kappa,eta,C_A)>0. This holds whether H_P is below or above one and after all polylogarithmic labels permitted in the five predecessor facts. A still requires a unit numerator. B,C1,C2,C3 permit a nonunit fixed target and unrestricted gcd(h,q). Correlated-energy pieces may carry a q-dependent unit twist, but no new such twist is permitted in the Type-I pieces.
The literal Poisson transform in fact df9748efe29ab475 satisfies the displayed omega_F hypothesis by repeated integration by parts. Hence, on the imbalance strip, the entire nonzero-frequency amplitude of every literal source leaf which otherwise matches one of the five trace shapes is controlled, including H_P<1 and all off-central h-blocks. The remaining exclusions are nonunit interval-prime A sectors, outer-g layers outside the G-strip, and Type-I sectors with an additional modulus-dependent unit.
3e326f797b2e04e4.proof:
Put u_F=F/H_P and G_F=H_T/F=G/u_F.

For every correlated B or C block, apply fact 42720f6d803c4640 at frequency F, model product frequency H_T, and imbalance G_F; for B use the joint-coprimality version 95626318cdcc099f. Both facts apply because F,H_T and all factor scales are at least one. Their normalized prefactor is F^{-1}, so restoring H_P^{-1} multiplies the estimate by u_F. The first two four-term expressions also contain G_F^{1/4}=G^{1/4}u_F^{-1/4}; therefore, relative to the central H_P calculation, their total frequency factor is |omega_F|u_F^{3/4}. The last two have factor |omega_F|u_F. If u_F<=1 these factors are at most one. If u_F>1, choose J_0>3; then they are at most constant multiples of u_F^{3/4-J_0} and u_F^{1-J_0}, whose sums over dyadic F converge. Thus every correlated calculation in the proof of d26acaefc372b4d0, including the gcd-aware stopping block, sums with the same power saving. This argument also covers H_P<1, since then every F>=1 has u_F>1 and no analytic theorem is invoked below frequency one.

For A, first consider F satisfying 2F<=Y and 8FY<q throughout q comparable to Q. Apply 4a101b703d4499f6 with frequency parameter 2F. Its U<=q condition is unchanged. With normalized prefactor F^{-1}, the first term in the proof of d26acaefc372b4d0 has G_F^{1/2} in place of G^{1/2}; after restoring H_P^{-1} and omega_F its frequency factor relative to the central bound is |omega_F|u_F^{1/2}. The second term and the p|u diagonal acquire |omega_F|u_F. These factors are at most one for u_F<=1 and are dyadically summable for u_F>1 after choosing J_0>3.
The pointwise hypotheses hold on a long upper interval. Indeed Y/H_P>=GQ^sigma/2>=Q^eta/2. Also, using Y<=Z and H_TZ=Q^{1/2-3sigma}, one has Q/(H_PY)>=GQ^{1/2+3sigma}>=Q^{1/2+2sigma+eta}. Therefore every F with u_F<=cQ^eta, for a fixed sufficiently small c, satisfies 2F<=Y and 8FY<q. For the remaining A blocks u_F>cQ^eta, bound absolutely. Up to a Q^epsilon divisor factor, there are at most B choices of the factor pair, Q moduli, and F frequencies, so after H_P^{-1} the block is at most Q^{1+beta+epsilon}u_F|omega_F|. Since beta<=6/5, choosing J_0 sufficiently large in terms of eta makes the dyadic sum over u_F>cQ^eta bounded by Q^{2-delta}. This proves A, including H_P<1. If H_P<1, the first integer block F=1 satisfies the pointwise hypotheses directly because Y>=H_TQ^sigma/2>=Q^sigma/2 and Z<Q/16 for large Q.

For every low Type-I box, apply bbcb9f66597c667c at frequency F as long as F is bounded by a chosen fixed power Q^{C_0}, with C_0 larger than C_A+10. Its normalized bound is independent of F apart from epsilon factors. Restoring H_P^{-1} gives the dyadic factor |omega_F|u_F, harmless below H_P and summable above it. For F>Q^{C_0}, the same absolute estimate Q^{1+beta+epsilon}u_F|omega_F| and a sufficiently large J_0 give an arbitrarily large power saving. Proper-prime-power errors and repeated-prime collision strata have their original bounds multiplied by the same |omega_F|u_F, so their dyadic sums preserve the predecessor power savings. Prime ordering and separation are unchanged.

Finally, fact df9748efe29ab475 performs Poisson summation in a compactly supported smooth m-weight. On h comparable to F, repeated integration by parts gives (1+F/H_P)^{-J_0} for every J_0. After this factor is extracted, scaled derivatives in all compact logarithmic coordinates remain uniformly bounded. This is exactly the omega_F hypothesis. The fixed target and reciprocity amplitude are already paid by d26acaefc372b4d0. Summing the five audits proves the theorem and its stated exclusions.

glossary.F: A dyadic positive integer frequency scale.
glossary.G_F: The effective product imbalance H_T/F at frequency F.
glossary.complete dyadic-frequency sum: The sum of all positive and negative nonzero Poisson frequency blocks F>=1.
glossary.omega_F: The scalar Fourier-decay factor extracted from a dyadic frequency block.

3edf35eeb12b56e8.title: QUANTITATIVE SELECTED FIXED-BAD-N POST-A,B,C1 REMAINDER AND EXACT FIRST-BUFFER LEDGER
3edf35eeb12b56e8.author: slava chan
3edf35eeb12b56e8.statement:
QUANTITATIVE SELECTED FIXED-BAD-N POST-A,B,C1 REMAINDER AND EXACT FIRST-BUFFER LEDGER.

Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, beta_0=6/5-2kappa, beta_1=6/5-3sigma, kappa_0=1/200, and fix 0<eta<sigma. Let x be sufficiently large and let N=2x be one of the selected bad even integers in the fixed-bad-N source construction. Let c(N) be its singular factor and assume the inherited uniform lower bound c(N)>=C_2>0.

Work with the literal paired nonzero-Poisson selected source atoms and exact normalization d=ga, r=gb, g=gcd(d,r) dividing N. In a forward atom assume
R>D, c_1x<=DM<=C_1x,
c_D x^(1/2)(log x)^(-A_D)<=D<=C_D x^(1/2),
R>x^(9/16-kappa_0),
and put Q=D/g, B=R/g=Q^beta, G=M/Q, H_T=B/Q, H_P=B/M and L_src=N/g.
In a reverse atom assume
D>R, c_1x<=RK<=C_1x,
c_R x^(1/2)(log x)^(-A_R)<=R<=C_R x^(1/2),
D>x^(9/16-kappa_0),
and put Q=R/g, B=D/g=Q^beta, G=K/Q, H_T=B/Q, H_P=B/K and L_src=N/g.
All displayed c_i,C_i,C_2 are fixed positive constants, A_D,A_R are fixed nonnegative constants, and all physical scales are at most Cx for a fixed C.

Let R_postAB,sel be the finite real selected same-bad-N aggregate supplied by fact 323499eb9e75ce72 after the complete A and B first-buffer coordinates have been subtracted. Thus
R_postAB,sel <= -c_dir c(N)x/log x+o(c(N)x/log x)                     (1)
for a fixed c_dir>0, and every atom of R_postAB,sel with
beta_0<beta<=beta_1                                                    (2)
has frozen parent U_low and normalized anatomy in the exact disjoint list C1,C2,C3. All selected source, fixed-U, high, smooth/projective, Fourier, target-gcd, prime-order, collision, deletion, orientation, parent, provenance and exact outer-gcd coordinates are retained.

Let R_C1,U_low be the complete aggregate of all atoms of R_postAB,sel satisfying (2) and having normalized anatomy C1, with every auxiliary target-gcd, prime-order, outer-gcd/rough-prime collision, Fourier, deletion and provenance refinement summed to completion. Define
R_postABC1,sel=R_postAB,sel-R_C1,U_low.                               (3)

Then there is a fixed delta_C1>0 such that
|R_C1,U_low|<<x^(1-delta_C1),                                       (4)
and
R_postABC1,sel <= -c_dir c(N)x/log x+o(c(N)x/log x).                 (5)
Within (2), the exact remaining parent/anatomy ledger is
U_low times {C2,C3}.                                                  (6)

The data in this theorem do not determine that the fixed selected bad N has a C2 atom, or any atom, in every right-neighborhood of beta_0. In particular, an unrestricted structural construction that chooses d,m,r,k and then defines a new even integer by N=dm+rk does not prove support inside this same-bad-N selected ledger. Therefore (6) identifies C2 as the next candidate standard anatomy coordinate, but it does not identify the first actually nonempty selected cell or assert that any individual C2 or C3 cell is negative.

No arbitrary joint deletion mask is inserted. No C2 or C3 estimate, moving actual-Z selector, endpoint, terminal selection, C2-negative localization, PMD, logical Goldbach implication, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
3edf35eeb12b56e8.proof:
Fact 323499eb9e75ce72 establishes the explicitly stated hypothesis (1), the lower bound c(N)>=C_2, and the exact first-buffer selected ledger
U_low times {C1,C2,C3}.                                               (7)

Fact efd5ace01f0a6c11 proves a fixed power saving for the complete literal C1 aggregate throughout the same parameter range (2), in both orientations, for every actual G and every exact outer gcd. Its proof applies the accepted trace fact 76040270e1ddf949 separately with each frozen source, parent, fixed-U, high and provenance label acting as a label scalar. It requires every target-gcd, prime-order, collision and deletion refinement to be recombined before estimation. The definition of R_C1,U_low does exactly this and merely fixes the already retained selected-source, fixed-U and U_low-parent labels. Therefore efd5ace01f0a6c11 applies and proves (4).

Because c(N)>=C_2>0,
x^(1-delta_C1)=o(c(N)x/log x).                                       (8)
Use the exact identity (3), the real upper bound (1), the absolute bound (4), and (8) to obtain (5). Since C1,C2,C3 are disjoint normalized anatomy coordinates in (7), removing the complete C1 coordinate leaves exactly C2,C3 and does not change the sole parent U_low. This proves (6).

We finally justify the no-fit statement. Every atom in this theorem satisfies the fixed source equation
N=dm+rk                                                               (9)
for the already selected bad N and carries the selected source and fixed-U provenance. A construction that freely chooses d,m,r,k and then defines the right side of (9) to be a new integer verifies support only in an unrestricted structural ledger. It gives no equality with the fixed N in this theorem and no membership in its selected source or fixed-U labels. None of the predecessors 323499eb9e75ce72, efd5ace01f0a6c11, or 76040270e1ddf949 supplies a uniform fixed-N solution of (9) with C2 anatomy arbitrarily close to beta_0. Thus (7) is an exhaustive list conditional on atom membership, but it does not force either listed coordinate to be nonempty at a prescribed beta. This proves the exact scope of the no-fit and completes the theorem.

glossary.R_C1,U_low: The complete selected U_low-parent C1 aggregate in the first post-low-beta buffer.
glossary.R_postABC1,sel: The same-bad-N selected remainder after subtracting the accepted A, B and complete C1 first-buffer aggregates.
glossary.delta_C1: The fixed power-saving exponent for the selected complete C1 buffer.

3ef233e014331fc3.title: There exists a nonnegative infinitely differentiable real function Phi supported in [1/2,2] such that
3ef233e014331fc3.author: slava chan
3ef233e014331fc3.statement:
There exists a nonnegative infinitely differentiable real function Phi supported in [1/2,2] such that
sum_{j in Z}Phi(t/2^j)=1
for every real t>0. Consequently, in the setting of fact ef53db9a50c698b0 one may choose the dyadic partition function Phi to be nonnegative. With that choice, the controlled dyadic mask Xi_C in that fact satisfies
0<=Xi_C(d,m,r,k)<=1
for every positive integer tuple (d,m,r,k). Hence the tuple coefficient in C_N+U_{T,N} is exactly one when r<k^2 and is Xi_C in [0,1] when r>=k^2, while the tuple coefficient in T_N is zero when r<k^2 and is 1-Xi_C in [0,1] when r>=k^2. These are honest nonnegative masks on the original signed integer-tuple weight, but they do not give either aggregate a pointwise sign: fact 175907af543c5308 shows that the underlying truncated divisor-sibling coefficients take both signs.
3ef233e014331fc3.proof:
Define the real function g_0 on the positive reals by
g_0(t)=exp(-1/((t-1/2)(2-t))) when 1/2<t<2,
and g_0(t)=0 otherwise. This is nonnegative, positive on (1/2,2), supported in [1/2,2], and infinitely differentiable: at either endpoint the exponential tends to zero faster than every reciprocal power of the distance to the endpoint, so every one-sided derivative matches the zero derivative of the exterior function.

For t>0 put
G_dy(t)=sum_{j in Z}g_0(t/2^j).
Near any fixed t only finitely many summands are nonzero, because nonzero support requires 1/2<t/2^j<2. Thus G_dy is infinitely differentiable. It is positive: choose an integer j with 1<=t/2^j<2; then the corresponding summand is positive. Reindexing the locally finite sum gives G_dy(t/2^j)=G_dy(t) for every integer j.

Define Phi(t)=g_0(t)/G_dy(t). It is nonnegative and infinitely differentiable on the positive reals, and its support is contained in [1/2,2]. By dyadic invariance of the denominator,
sum_{j in Z}Phi(t/2^j)
=sum_{j in Z}g_0(t/2^j)/G_dy(t)
=1.
This proves existence.

Now use this Phi in fact ef53db9a50c698b0. Every fourfold dyadic weight
Phi(d/D)Phi(m/M)Phi(r/R)Phi(k/K)
is nonnegative. Its sum over all positive dyadic quadruples is the product of the four one-variable partition sums and hence equals one. Xi_C is the partial sum over the controlled label set 𝒞, so it lies between zero and one. The coefficient descriptions then follow immediately from the exact formulas in fact ef53db9a50c698b0. Finally, nonnegativity of these masks does not remove the Moebius signs from the integer-tuple weight; the cited opposite-sign examples in fact 175907af543c5308 prove the final limitation.

glossary.G_dy: the positive dyadically invariant sum of all dyadic translates of g_0
glossary.g_0: the explicit nonnegative smooth bump supported in [1/2,2]

3f2f255ea6845a50.title: COMPLETE SAME-SELECTED-\(N\) TOP-SLIVER A-ANATOMY PAYMENT AND NEGATIVE HANDOFF TO THE FIVE NON-A ANATOMIES
3f2f255ea6845a50.author: slava chan
3f2f255ea6845a50.statement:
COMPLETE SAME-SELECTED-\(N\) TOP-SLIVER A-ANATOMY PAYMENT AND NEGATIVE HANDOFF TO THE FIVE NON-A ANATOMIES.

Fix
\[
 0<\kappa\le 1/100,\qquad \sigma=\kappa/100,\qquad
 \beta_m=6/5-12\sigma/5,
\]
and fix \(0<\eta<\sigma\) and \(\omega>0\). Put
\[
 \Gamma_{BC}(\beta)=\max\{0,(19\beta-20)/17\}.
\]
Let \(x\to\infty\) through the selected values for which \(N=2x\) is the fixed bad even integer and use the same selected smooth source and active dyadic labels as in fact 60b26a9b6f79467a. Thus, in every active strict-orientation label,
\[
 DM\asymp x,\qquad RK\asymp x,
\]
the smaller divisor scale is at most \(2x^{1/2}\) and at least \(x^{1/2}(\log x)^{-O(1)}\), and the larger divisor scale exceeds \(x^{9/16-1/200}\).

For the exact outer gcd \(g=(d,r)\), write \(d=ga\), \(r=gb\). In the forward orientation define
\[
 Q=D/g,\quad B=R/g=Q^\beta,\quad G=M/Q,\quad
 H_T=B/Q,\quad H_P=B/M,\quad L_{\rm src}=N/g,
\]
and in the reverse orientation define
\[
 Q=R/g,\quad B=D/g=Q^\beta,\quad G=K/Q,\quad
 H_T=B/Q,\quad H_P=B/K,\quad L_{\rm src}=N/g.
\]
On the strict band \(\beta_m<\beta<6/5\), assume the inherited actual imbalance range
\[
 Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\le G<
 Q^{\Gamma_{BC}(\beta)+\omega}.
\]
Put
\[
 L=Q^{\beta-1+\sigma},\qquad
 S_0=Q^{2\beta-2+3\sigma},\qquad
 Z=Q^{3/2-\beta-3\sigma}.
\]
At each fixed pre-marker source atom, restore the literal normalized Möbius coefficient and apply the exact original-cutoff terminal marker with these \(L,S_0,Z\). Its exact disjoint anatomy list on this band is
\[
 A,\quad B,\quad C1,\quad C2,\quad C3,\quad C4,
\]
with sole inherited parent \(U_{\rm low}\), both orientations, and all selected-source, active-scale, fixed-\(U\), high, smooth/projective, paired-frequency, target-gcd, prime-order/equal-cell, collision, deletion, provenance, actual-\(G\), and exact outer-\(g\) coordinates retained.

Let \(\mathcal T_{>\beta_m,\mathrm{sel}}\) be the real same-selected-\(N\) source of fact c98f3e5b2172abec. It is supported on \(\beta>\beta_m\) and satisfies
\[
 \mathcal T_{>\beta_m,\mathrm{sel}}
 \le -c_{\rm dir}\,\mathfrak c(N)\frac{x}{\log x}
      +o\!\left(\mathfrak c(N)\frac{x}{\log x}\right),
 \qquad c_{\rm dir}>0,\quad \mathfrak c(N)\ge C_2>0.
\]
Let \(\mathcal R_{A,\mathrm{top},\mathrm{sel}}\) be the complete exact projection of this source onto \(\beta_m<\beta<6/5\) and anatomy A, after recombining every coordinate just listed. Then there is a fixed \(\delta_{A,\mathrm{top}}>0\), depending only on the fixed hierarchy, such that
\[
 \left|\mathcal R_{A,\mathrm{top},\mathrm{sel}}\right|
 \ll x^{1-\delta_{A,\mathrm{top}}}.
\]
Consequently, if
\[
 \mathcal T_{\mathrm{post}A,\mathrm{sel}}
 =\mathcal T_{>\beta_m,\mathrm{sel}}
  -\mathcal R_{A,\mathrm{top},\mathrm{sel}},
\]
then
\[
 \mathcal T_{\mathrm{post}A,\mathrm{sel}}
 \le -c_{\rm dir}\,\mathfrak c(N)\frac{x}{\log x}
      +o\!\left(\mathfrak c(N)\frac{x}{\log x}\right).
\]
On \(\beta_m<\beta<6/5\), its exact remaining ledger consists of B, C1, C2, C3, C4, with the same sole \(U_{\rm low}\), actual \(G\)-range, and all inherited coordinates and masks unchanged. Its part with \(\beta\ge6/5\) is inherited unchanged. No sign is asserted for an individual A-cell, and no estimate is asserted here for \(\beta\ge6/5\).
3f2f255ea6845a50.proof:
Write a selected source cell in the exact source-preserving coordinates stated above.

1. Exact forward reduction.  The source equation is
\[
 am+bk=L_{\rm src}.
\]
In anatomy A the normalized marked factor is \(b=up\), with \(up\asymp B\) and \(L<p<Z\).  This follows from the exact source-preserving ledger e58fc7c00f1683e6, which retains all accompanying masks without domination or alteration.

For each target-gcd value set
\[
 c=(a,L_{\rm src}),\qquad a=cq,\qquad L_{\rm src}=cL_1.
\]
Fact 1c64020b89f097c4 gives \(c\mid k\); writing \(k=ck_1\), it also gives the exact descended coprimalities needed for inversion.  Poisson summation in the complete source variable, as in df9748efe29ab475, and additive reciprocity put the oscillatory factor into the exact descended form
\[
 e_q\!\left(-L_1h\,\overline{up}\right),
\]
with the archimedean reciprocity factor retained in the smooth amplitude.  Fact d8ba46800ba433c2 supplies arbitrary decay outside the natural frequency range and an absolutely summable Fourier decomposition of the source masks.

Take
\[
 C_{\rm cut}=H_TQ^{\sigma/4}.
\]
For \(c\le C_{\rm cut}\), the resulting complete-frequency, target-gcd-descended trace is exactly an instance of the abstract top-sliver theorem 36c43b23e4b3c052, with the original cutoff \(Z\), the inherited actual \(G\), and all projective masks. Thus, for a fixed physical \(g\),
\[
 \sum_{c\le C_{\rm cut}} |\mathcal T_c|
 \ll
 \begin{cases}
   GQ^{2-\delta_0},&G\ge1,\\
   Q^{2-\delta_0},&Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\le G\le Q^{\sigma-\eta},
 \end{cases}
\]
for a fixed \(\delta_0>0\). For \(c>C_{\rm cut}\), fact 5fbdbbebf99aec55 applies with every present restriction and mask and gives
\[
 \sum_{c>C_{\rm cut}}|\mathcal T_c|
 \ll Q^\varepsilon\frac{QB}{C_{\rm cut}}
 =Q^{2-\sigma/4+\varepsilon},
\]
because \(B=QH_T\). After decreasing the fixed saving, the same two-case bound holds for the complete forward A-cell, including all frequencies and all target-gcd values.

The smoothness hypotheses in 36c43b23e4b3c052 are uniform here. Indeed the scaled derivative of the retained reciprocity phase is controlled by
\[
 \frac{|L_{\rm src}|}{QM}=\frac{N}{DM}=O(1)
\]
on the selected source support, while df9748efe29ab475 and d8ba46800ba433c2 give arbitrary Fourier decay for the other scaled source variables. Recombining the finitely many projective pieces and polylogarithmically many dyadic labels preserves a fixed power saving.

2. Reverse orientation. Interchange the divisor-complement pairs in the exact source ledger and reindex the complete Poisson frequency by \(h\mapsto-h\). The target becomes \(+L_{\rm src}\); the same target-gcd descent gives modulus \(b/c\) and the same descended inverse phase with the corresponding sign. The theorem 36c43b23e4b3c052 is uniform in the signed target, so it applies unchanged. The retained archimedean phase is uniformly smooth because
\[
 \frac{|L_{\rm src}|}{QK}=\frac{N}{RK}=O(1).
\]
The large-target-gcd estimate 5fbdbbebf99aec55 is orientation-free. Thus the identical complete-cell bound holds in the reverse orientation, with every frequency, target-gcd value, actual \(G\), and inherited mask included.

3. Coverage of the actual \(G\)-range. If \(G\ge1\), use the full-\(G\) estimate. If \(G<1\), then
\[
 Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\le G<1\le Q^{\sigma-\eta},
\]
so the near-balanced estimate applies. Hence no actual \(G\)-cell is omitted.

4. Exact outer-\(g\) summation. The forced high prime and the square-root upper bound for the smaller member of the divisor-complement pair give, exactly as in c98f3e5b2172abec,
\[
 Q^{\beta-1}>x^{1/16-1/200+o(1)}.
\]
Since \(\beta-1<1/5\), there is a fixed \(c_0>0\) such that \(Q\ge x^{c_0}\). The selected support also gives \(|L_{\rm src}|\ll x^{1/2+o(1)}Q\), so the polynomial target-size hypothesis in 36c43b23e4b3c052 is uniform.

For \(G\ge1\), the physical normalization is \(DM\asymp x\) forward and \(RK\asymp x\) reverse; consequently
\[
 GQ^{2-\delta_0}\asymp \frac{x}{g}Q^{-\delta_0}.
\]
Summing over the exact divisors \(g\mid N\) yields
\[
 \sum_{g\mid N}\frac{x}{g}Q^{-\delta_0}
 \ll x^{1-c_0\delta_0+o(1)}.
\]
For \(G<1\), use \(Q=D/g\) forward and \(Q=R/g\) reverse. The smaller physical scale is at most \(2x^{1/2}\), and hence
\[
 \sum_{g\mid N}Q^{2-\delta_0}
 \le D^{2-\delta_0}\sum_{g\mid N}g^{-2+\delta_0}
 \ll x^{1-\delta_0/3}
\]
after decreasing the fixed exponent; the reverse sum is identical with \(R\). The inherited sign, congruence, dyadic, well-factorable, and projective labels number at most \(x^{o(1)}\), which is absorbed by a further decrease of the exponent. This proves the asserted absolute bound.

5. Ledger subtraction and negativity. Fact c98f3e5b2172abec changes the selected source only on \(\beta\le\beta_m\); therefore its strict \(\beta>\beta_m\) part has exactly the top-sliver ledger of e58fc7c00f1683e6. That ledger is an exact disjoint source decomposition. Removing its complete A projection leaves precisely B, C1, C2, C3, C4 and the sole inherited \(U_{\rm low}\) on \(\beta_m<\beta<6/5\), with the actual \(G\)-range and every coordinate and mask unchanged. Since the projection is supported strictly below \(6/5\), the \(\beta\ge6/5\) source is untouched.

Finally \(\mathfrak c(N)\ge C_2>0\), while the proved payment is \(o(x/\log x)\). Subtracting the A projection therefore preserves the stated negative main term. Absolute values were used throughout the payment, so no sign of an individual A-cell is required.

glossary.R_A,top,sel: The complete same-selected-N projection onto source anatomy A in the strict top sliver beta_m<beta<6/5.
glossary.T_postA,sel: The selected negative source remaining after subtracting the complete strict-top-sliver A projection.
glossary.delta_A,top: A fixed power-saving exponent for the complete selected top-sliver A projection.

3fde81ce051bff7b.title: COMPLETE-LCM ORTHOGONALITY OF DISTINCT CENTERED ACTIVE PRODUCTS
3fde81ce051bff7b.author: slava chan
3fde81ce051bff7b.statement:
COMPLETE-LCM ORTHOGONALITY OF DISTINCT CENTERED ACTIVE PRODUCTS.

For a prime p and a nonzero residue C modulo p define
phi_{p,C}(x)=1_{x!=0} e_p(Cx^{-1})+1/p
on F_p. Let r and r' be nonempty squarefree positive integers. For every p|r choose a nonzero C_p modulo p, and for every p|r' choose a nonzero C'_p modulo p. Define periodic functions
Phi_r(x)=product_{p|r} phi_{p,C_p}(x mod p),
Phi'_{r'}(x)=product_{p|r'} phi_{p,C'_p}(x mod p),
and put L=lcm(r,r').

Then
(1/L) sum_{x mod L} Phi_r(x) conjugate(Phi'_{r'}(x))=0               (1)
whenever r!=r'. If r=r', the normalized complete Gram is
product_{p|r} gamma_p,                                                (2)
where
gamma_p=(p-1)/p-p^{-2} if C_p=C'_p modulo p,
gamma_p=-p^{-1}-p^{-2} if C_p!=C'_p modulo p.                          (3)

Thus the centered faces attached to distinct active prime products are exactly orthogonal under complete averaging modulo their lcm. For equal active product, (2)-(3) are the simultaneous local tensor factors of fact df97bf1eba0495be. Consequently any cross-active-product term in the literal C4 problem is entirely an incomplete-row/source-weight discrepancy; it is absent from the complete residue Gram.

This result does not bound that incomplete discrepancy, sum literal faces, control arbitrary q-dependent weights, prove C4-VEC, the C4 moment, or Goldbach.
3fde81ce051bff7b.proof:
Fact 60ec98d195b61bc1 gives
(1/p)sum_{x mod p}phi_{p,C}(x)=0                                      (4)
for every nonzero C.

By the Chinese remainder theorem, the normalized average in (1) factors into one local normalized average for each prime dividing L. Suppose r!=r'. Choose a prime p in the symmetric difference of their prime supports. If p|r and p does not divide r', the p-local factor of the integrand is phi_{p,C_p}(x), while Phi'_{r'} is independent of the p-coordinate. Hence the p-local normalized average is zero by (4). The case p|r' and p does not divide r is identical after conjugation. Therefore the full product is zero, proving (1).

Now suppose r=r'. The complete average factors as
product_{p|r} (1/p)sum_{x mod p}phi_{p,C_p}(x)conjugate(phi_{p,C'_p}(x)).       (5)
The local factor in (5) is the complete inner product of the centered inverse rows. Equivalently, since centering removes exactly their common zero Fourier mode, it is the mixed nonzero-mode Gram computed in fact 3d10fd30e2a42246. That fact gives precisely the two values in (3), according as the two inverse-phase parameters agree or differ. Multiplication over p proves (2).

Under the C4 specialization, equality of the local parameters is the square-divisor collision identified in fact df97bf1eba0495be, so its product formula is exactly (2)-(3). The final discrepancy and scope statements follow because (1) is a complete-residue identity; replacing the complete average by an incomplete q interval with q-dependent source weights is an additional operation not estimated here.

glossary.L: The least common multiple of the two active products r and r'.
glossary.Phi'_{r'}: A second centered CRT face function with active prime product r'.
glossary.Phi_r: The centered CRT face function with nonempty active prime product r.

415fa7afad9006c5.title: Fix B≥0. Let x≥3, let N=2x be an even integer, and put D_*=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B). Let G range over a family of continuously differentiable complex functions supported in [1/2,2] with uniformly bounded supremum and total variation. For D≥D_*/2 define
415fa7afad9006c5.author: slava chan
415fa7afad9006c5.statement:
Fix B≥0. Let x≥3, let N=2x be an even integer, and put D_*=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B). Let G range over a family of continuously differentiable complex functions supported in [1/2,2] with uniformly bounded supremum and total variation. For D≥D_*/2 define
S_N(D;G)=Σ_{d≥1, gcd(d,N)=1} μ(d)G(d/D)/φ(d).
Then, for every A>0,
S_N(D;G)≪_{A,B,G}(log x)^(-A)
uniformly in the even integer N, in D≥D_*/2, and in the stated bounded family of G.

More precisely, for Re(s)>0,
Σ_{d≥1, gcd(d,N)=1} μ(d)φ(d)^(-1)d^(-s)
=ζ(s+1)^(-1)𝓗_N(s),
where
𝓗_N(s)=∏_{p|N}(1-p^(-s-1))^(-1)
 ∏_{p∤N}[1-p^(-s)/(p-1)]/[1-p^(-s-1)].
If
C_2=∏_{p>2}p(p-2)/(p-1)^2
and
𝔠(N)=C_2∏_{p|N,p>2}(p-1)/(p-2),
then
𝓗_N(0)=2𝔠(N).
Thus the point s=0 is an inverse-zeta zero of the complete signed coefficient series, not a main pole.

For the following application, additionally assume all source hypotheses of fact d6fd2c2cf8b5d0f0 explicitly as follows. Let 1/2<a<b<1. Let W be a nonzero nonnegative continuously differentiable real function supported in [a,b]. Let ψ be continuously differentiable with 0≤ψ≤1, ψ(u)=0 for 0<u≤1 and ψ(u)=1 for u≥2. Let B=B(W,ψ)>0 be the exponent supplied by fact 2827630745a3225b, let x be sufficiently large, and assume that N=2x is an even integer not representable as a sum of two primes. Let Φ be continuously differentiable, supported in [1/2,2], and satisfy Σ_{j∈Z}Φ(t/2^j)=1 for every t>0. Let D,M,U be positive dyadic scales satisfying
D_*/2≤D≤2bx,
ax/4≤DM≤4bx,
and
(2-b)x/2≤U≤2(2-a)x.
Define
𝓜_N(D,M;U)
=Σ_{d≥1, gcd(d,N)=1} μ(d)ψ(d/D_*)Φ(d/D)/φ(d)
 Σ_{p prime, p<N} log(p)log((N-p)/d)W((N-p)/x)
 Φ((N-p)/(dM))Φ(p/U),
where a summand is zero unless N-p>0. Then, for every A>0,
𝓜_N(D,M;U)≪_{A,W,ψ,Φ}x(log x)^(-A).

For the genuine-prime block P_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;U) of fact d6fd2c2cf8b5d0f0, put
F_d(p)=log(p)log((N-p)/d)W((N-p)/x)
 Φ((N-p)/(dM))Φ(p/U)
and
Δ_d(N)=Σ_{p prime, p<N, p≡N (mod d)}F_d(p)
 -φ(d)^(-1)Σ_{p prime, p<N}F_d(p).
Then
P_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;U)
=𝓜_N(D,M;U)
 +Σ_{d≥2,gcd(d,N)=1}μ(d)ψ(d/D_*)Φ(d/D)Δ_d(N)
exactly. Hence the full unrestricted-prime comparison main is smaller than every logarithmic power; no prime-number-theorem substitution inside a residue class is used. The remaining analytic obstacle is exactly the displayed signed progression discrepancy.

The cancellation is genuinely a complete-squarefree-modulus phenomenon. Fix η>0, 1/2<α<β<2, and a nonnegative continuously differentiable G_0 supported in [1/2,2] with G_0(t)≥c_0>0 on [α,β]. If x^η≤D≤x and
S_N^pr(D;G_0)=Σ_{d prime, gcd(d,N)=1} μ(d)G_0(d/D)/φ(d),
then
[c_0(β-α)+o(1)]/(β log D)
≤|S_N^pr(D;G_0)|≪_{G_0}1/log D.
Thus the prime-modulus coefficient has order 1/log D, not arbitrary logarithmic saving. In a separated comparison slice consisting of this coefficient, an independent unrestricted-prime factor of order x, and a cofactor log M with log M comparable to log D, the total size is comparable to x. Prime moduli therefore cannot be discarded before their cancellation with composite squarefree moduli in S_N(D;G).
415fa7afad9006c5.proof:
Put a_N(d)=μ(d)1_{gcd(d,N)=1}/φ(d). Since μ is supported on squarefree integers, the Euler factor of Σ a_N(d)d^(-s) is 1 when p|N and is 1-p^(-s)/(p-1) when p∤N. Extracting ζ(s+1)^(-1)=∏_p(1-p^(-s-1)) gives the displayed 𝓗_N(s).

At s=0, a prime p|N contributes p/(p-1), while a prime p∤N contributes p(p-2)/(p-1)^2. Since 2|N, separating p=2 and comparing the odd factors gives
𝓗_N(0)=2C_2∏_{p|N,p>2}(p-1)/(p-2)=2𝔠(N).

Let h_N(k) be the Dirichlet coefficients of 𝓗_N(s). If p|N, then h_N(p^j)=p^(-j). If p∤N and j≥1, then h_N(p^j)=-1/[p^j(p-1)]. Hence
Σ_k|h_N(k)|
=∏_{p|N}(1-p^(-1))^(-1)∏_{p∤N}(1+1/(p-1)^2)
≪(log(2N))^C.
The second product converges. If p_1<...<p_r are the distinct prime divisors of N, then p_j≥j+1 and r≤log_2N, so the logarithm of the first product is O(1+Σ_{j≤r}1/j)=O(log log(2N)). Likewise
Σ_k|h_N(k)|k^(1/2)
=∏_{p|N}(1-p^(-1/2))^(-1)
 ∏_{p∤N}(1+1/[(p-1)(p^(1/2)-1)])
≤exp(O(sqrt(log(2N)))).
The second product again converges, and the first follows from Σ_{j≤r}j^(-1/2)=O(sqrt(r)).

Coefficient convolution gives
a_N(d)=Σ_{kn=d}h_N(k)μ(n)/n,
and therefore
S_N(D;G)=Σ_k h_N(k)Σ_n μ(n)G(kn/D)/n.                 (1)
Split at k=D^(1/2). For k≤D^(1/2), put Y=D/k≥D^(1/2). Fact 0b3642c89b136065 reproduces
|Σ_{n≤y}μ(n)|≪y exp(-c sqrt(log y)).
Partial summation on n/Y∈[1/2,2] gives
Σ_n μ(n)G(n/Y)/n≪exp(-c_1 sqrt(log Y))
uniformly in the bounded G-family. Thus the small-k part is at most
(log(2N))^C exp(-c_2 sqrt(log D)).
For k>D^(1/2), the inner sum in (1) is O_G(1), since n is comparable to D/k and the sum of 1/n on a fixed multiplicative interval is bounded. Therefore the large-k part is at most
D^(-1/4)Σ_k|h_N(k)|k^(1/2)
≤D^(-1/4)exp(O(sqrt(log(2N)))).
Because N=2x and D≥x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B)/2, both parts are O_{A,B}((log x)^(-A)) for every A. This proves the inverse-zeta estimate.

We apply it to 𝓜_N by exchanging the finite p and d sums. For every p on the support of W((N-p)/x)Φ(p/U), put
G_p(t)=ψ(Dt/D_*)Φ(t)log((N-p)/(Dt))
 Φ((N-p)/(DMt)).
Then the d-sum is S_N(D;G_p). The family (log(2x))^(-1)G_p has uniformly bounded supremum and total variation. Indeed Φ(t) restricts t to [1/2,2]. If the derivative of ψ(Dt/D_*) is nonzero, then 1≤Dt/D_*≤2, so D/D_* is bounded there; otherwise that derivative is zero. If the last Φ is nonzero, its argument lies in [1/2,2], so its derivative after the chain rule is bounded. The scale hypotheses and W-support give |log((N-p)/(Dt))|≪log(2x), while its t-derivative is -1/t.

Apply the first part with an exponent two larger than the desired one. The inner d-sum is O((log x)^(-A-1)). The remaining p-sum is O(x). For completeness, if θ(y)=Σ_{p≤y}log p, every prime n<p≤2n divides the integer binomial coefficient (2n choose n)<4^n, so θ(2n)-θ(n)≤2n log 2; dyadic summation gives θ(y)≪y. This proves 𝓜_N≪x(log x)^(-A).

Under the explicitly reproduced source hypotheses, fact d6fd2c2cf8b5d0f0 gives the prime-progression normal form and proves gcd(d,N)=1 for every contributing incidence. Adding and subtracting φ(d)^(-1)Σ_pF_d(p) gives the displayed identity. The d=1 term causes no mismatch: D_*≥1 for sufficiently large x and ψ(1/D_*)=0; independently, Δ_1(N)=0 because every integer is congruent to N modulo 1 and φ(1)=1.

For prime moduli, μ(d)=-1 and φ(d)=d-1, so every term of S_N^pr is nonpositive. The cited Prime Number Theorem, Subham De, arXiv:2308.16303, Theorem 2.2.1, states π(y)~y/log y. It gives
#{d prime: αD≤d≤βD}=[β-α+o(1)]D/log D.
At most log N/log(αD)=O_η(1) of these primes divide N, because their product divides N. Each remaining prime contributes at least c_0/(βD) in absolute value, proving the lower bound. For the upper bound, support of G_0 restricts d to [D/2,2D], each summand has magnitude at most 3||G_0||_∞/D for large D, and the same prime number theorem gives π(2D)≪D/log D. Thus |S_N^pr|≪_{G_0}1/log D. Multiplying this order by the two explicitly stated independent factors proves the final separated-slice scale assertion. It is a scope example, not a claim that every coupled literal block has that size.

glossary.S_N(D;G): the smooth coprime sum of μ(d)/φ(d) at scale D
glossary.S_N^pr(D;G_0): the restriction of S_N(D;G_0) to prime moduli
glossary.Δ_d(N): the difference between the actual prime progression at residue N modulo d and its unrestricted 1/φ(d) comparison
glossary.𝓗_N(s): the Euler product left after extracting ζ(s+1)^(-1) from the μ(d)/φ(d) Dirichlet series
glossary.𝓜_N(D,M;U): the unrestricted-prime comparison main term for a genuine-prime block

The normalized Poisson calculation in fact (df9748efe29ab475), followed by the orientation convention in fact (e58fc7c00f1683e6), has exact prefactor
[

Thus (2) is the literal fixed-frequency, fixed-fiber, fixed-(D) source contribution.

 e_q(-mathscr A h(dv)^{-1})
 =

]
Since ((d,v)=1), the Chinese remainder identity
[
 e_{dv}(x)=e_d(xv^{-1})e_v(xd^{-1})
]

Multiply (5) by its complex conjugate. In the (d)-phase,

 h_1(q_1v)^{-1}-h_2(q_2v)^{-1}

It remains to prove the normalization. The exact stopping copies over (n), the rough-prime copies, and the exact Vaughan/convolution refinements used for (C1) are bounded by (	au_J(n)) for one fixed (J). Hence
[
 sum_{B/2le nle2B}|Lambda_D(n)|ll_arepsilon BQ^arepsilon.
]
Apply Cauchy to (2) over the pairs ((n,lambda)) and use (3); this gives (10).

Assume (CMD) and (Fll H_P). Substitution into (10), followed by the square-root inequality, yields

42104ea7b4b24b0b.title: LITERAL COMMON-CELL TOP/PRIME-STAR EXPANSION AND DELETION-MASK OBSTRUCTION
42104ea7b4b24b0b.author: slava chan
42104ea7b4b24b0b.statement:
LITERAL COMMON-CELL TOP/PRIME-STAR EXPANSION AND DELETION-MASK OBSTRUCTION.

Use the literal normalized C2 common-cell source of facts d8ba46800ba433c2 and 0abb9119d9247de6. Thus a retained index is
z=(g,a,v,p,q,h),   b_z=vpq,   G_z=pq,   L_z=N/g,
where p<q are distinct primes in one fixed cell, b_z is squarefree, gcd(a,b_z)=1, h is nonzero, and
mu(ga)mu(gvpq) is nonzero.
Let Fhat_{g,a,b} be the literal Fourier transform in fact d8ba46800ba433c2, and define the complete phased atom
c_z=mu(ga)mu(gvpq)b_z^(-1)Fhat_{g,a,b_z}(h/b_z)
     e_{b_z}(L_zh a^(-1)).                                   (1)

(A) The exact Möbius and phase expansions are
mu(ga)mu(gvpq)=mu(a)mu(v),                                  (2)
c_z=mu(a)mu(v)b_z^(-1)Fhat_{g,a,b_z}(h/b_z)
     e_{v}(m_zhG_z^(-1))e_{G_z}(B_z),                        (3)
and
c_z=mu(a)mu(v)b_z^(-1)Fhat_{g,a,b_z}(h/b_z)
     exp(2 pi i L_zh/(ab_z))e_a(-L_zhb_z^(-1)).              (4)
Here m_z is any representative of the residue class
a m_z congruent to L_z modulo b_z,
and B_z is the rough carrier coordinate of fact 0d3dbb6b3e7b8abd. In particular the two rough primes p,q create no Möbius sign in (1); all remaining arithmetic sign is mu(a)mu(v).

The rough factor e_{G_z}(B_z) has full primitive denominator G_z exactly when
gcd(m_zh,G_z)=1.                                             (5)
In the short common-cell family of fact 0abb9119d9247de6, where
0<|h|<Z_0<=p,q, condition (5) is equivalent to
gcd(L_z,G_z)=1.                                              (6)

(B) Let mathcal L be any finite retained family satisfying the preceding conditions and the full-conductor condition. For every active semiprime G put
gamma_G=sum_{z in mathcal L:G_z=G}c_z,
kappa_G=phi(G)/G, and x_G=kappa_Ggamma_G.
Then the literal common-cell top and prime-star sums are exactly
T=sum_Gx_G=sum_{z in mathcal L}kappa_{G_z}c_z,                (7)
S_r=sum_{G:r|G}x_G
   =sum_{z in mathcal L:r|G_z}kappa_{G_z}c_z.                (8)
The support-disjoint full-face scalar is
M=T^2-sum_rS_r^2+sum_Gx_G^2.                                 (9)
Equations (7)-(9) preserve every retained source mask and both phase representations (3)-(4).

(C) Let I be any finite set and let w_j be complex numbers. Put
L_1=sum_j|w_j|,   E_2=sum_j|w_j|^2,
and, when E_2>0,
N_eff=L_1^2/E_2.
There is a zero-one deletion vector delta=(delta_j) such that
|sum_jdelta_jw_j|>=L_1/6
 =(1/6)sqrt(N_eff E_2).                                      (10)
Consequently, if a bound
|sum_jdelta_jw_j|<=U                                        (11)
holds for every zero-one deletion, then necessarily L_1<=6U. If instead the right side of (11) is C E_2^(1/2), then necessarily
N_eff<=36C^2.                                                (12)

Apply this lemma with w_z=kappa_{G_z}c_z on any finite literal source subfamily. It gives a phase-adaptive source deletion with (10) for the top sum. Applying it to the subfamily r|G_z gives the same conclusion for any one fixed prime-star sum. These deletions preserve all conditions imposed before the deletion, including the common cell and full conductor. Thus a theorem uniform under arbitrary zero-one source deletion cannot obtain cancellation of every top or prime-star atom family from its l2 energy alone; it needs, for each family to which it is applied, a separate l1 bound, a bounded effective-support statement, or another hypothesis excluding the phase-adaptive mask.

(D) Suppose now that the base masks are invariant under h replacing -h. Use one representative j from every pair {h,-h}, and put
w_j=kappa_{G_j}c_j,
t_j=c_j+conjugate(c_j)=2Re(c_j),
q_j=w_j+conjugate(w_j)=kappa_{G_j}t_j,
P_1=sum_j|q_j|,   E_R=sum_jq_j^2.
There is an h-symmetric zero-one deletion, obtained by retaining both signs of h for one sign class of q_j, such that
|sum_jdelta_jq_j|>=P_1/2.                                   (13)
If E_R>0 and N_eff^R=P_1^2/E_R, a bound by C E_R^(1/2) uniform over every h-symmetric deletion forces
N_eff^R<=4C^2.                                               (14)

If the negative sign class has mass at least P_1/2, retain that class and call the resulting unweighted literal source sum
T_C2=sum_jdelta_jt_j.
Since 0<kappa_{G_j}<1 and q_j=kappa_{G_j}t_j<0 on the selected class,
t_j=q_j/kappa_{G_j}<=q_j.
Therefore
T_C2<=sum_jdelta_jq_j<=-P_1/2.                              (15)
Assume additionally all scale and rough-prime-cutoff hypotheses of fact 707345f56faff29e for this selected C2 restriction, and let E_comp be its complement quantity. The selected mask is h-symmetric and is an allowed restriction in that fact. If
(P_1/2)^2>2E_comp,                                           (16)
then fact 707345f56faff29e applies with A_0=P_1/2 and yields its sign-preserving four-prime routing conclusion. If the positive sign class is larger, (13) gives only a positive absolute-value obstruction, not the negative hypothesis of that routing theorem.

The paired real mass P_1 cannot be replaced by the unpaired complex mass 2sum_j|w_j|: a purely imaginary w_j has q_j=0. Equal positive abstract atoms show that N_eff can equal the cardinality of I, so no support-independent l2-only deletion bound follows from (10). These finite examples need not be realizable by the natural arithmetic selector or literal source. This theorem is an arbitrary-mask obstruction only. It is not a constructed counterexample for the natural selector, not a varying-fibre bound, not common-cell or cross-cell capture, and not a Goldbach implication. No analytic large-sieve estimate is asserted.
42104ea7b4b24b0b.proof:
Because mu(ga) and mu(gvpq) are nonzero, both ga and gvpq are squarefree. Hence gcd(g,a)=gcd(g,vpq)=1. The hypotheses gcd(a,vpq)=1 and squarefreeness of vpq also give the remaining coprimalities needed below. Complete multiplicativity of mu on coprime squarefree factors gives
mu(ga)mu(gvpq)
 =mu(g)mu(a)mu(g)mu(v)mu(p)mu(q).
Here mu(g)^2=1 and mu(p)mu(q)=(-1)(-1)=1, proving (2).

The congruence a m_z congruent to L_z modulo b_z gives
e_{b_z}(L_zh a^(-1))=e_{b_z}(m_zh).
Since b_z=vG_z is squarefree, CRT gives
e_{b_z}(m_zh)
 =e_v(m_zhG_z^(-1))e_{G_z}(m_zhv^(-1)).
Fact 0d3dbb6b3e7b8abd defines B_z congruent to m_zhv^(-1) modulo G_z, proving (3).

For coprime a,b_z, additive reciprocity is
a^(-1)/b_z+b_z^(-1)/a congruent to 1/(ab_z) modulo one.
Multiplying by L_zh and exponentiating gives
e_{b_z}(L_zh a^(-1))
 =exp(2 pi i L_zh/(ab_z))e_a(-L_zhb_z^(-1)),
which proves (4).

Again by fact 0d3dbb6b3e7b8abd,
gcd(B_z,G_z)=gcd(m_zh,G_z).
The reduced denominator of e_{G_z}(B_z) is therefore G_z exactly under (5). In the short family, neither p nor q divides h because 0<|h|<Z_0<=p,q. Thus (5) is equivalent to gcd(m_z,G_z)=1. Reducing a m_z congruent to L_z modulo p and q, and using that a is a unit modulo both primes, shows that a rough prime divides m_z exactly when it divides L_z. This proves (6).

Equations (7) and (8) follow by substituting the definitions of gamma_G and x_G and interchanging finite sums. Equation (9) is exactly the top/prime-star/diagonal identity in fact 890c794f463db36a. This proves (B).

We prove (10) by an explicit three-sector partition. Ignore zero w_j. Partition the arguments of the nonzero w_j into three half-open arcs of angular width 2pi/3, centered at
theta_k=2pi k/3,  k=0,1,2.
Let I_k be the indices in the k-th arc and L_k=sum_{j in I_k}|w_j|. Since the arcs partition the nonzero indices,
max_k L_k>=L_1/3.
Choose such a k and set delta_j=1 on I_k and zero elsewhere. Every angle in I_k differs from theta_k by at most pi/3, with at most an irrelevant half-open endpoint. Therefore
Re(e^(-i theta_k)sum_{j in I_k}w_j)
 =sum_{j in I_k}|w_j|cos(arg(w_j)-theta_k)
 >=L_k/2>=L_1/6.
The modulus dominates this real part, proving (10). The equality with N_eff is its definition. Taking the particular deletion supplied by (10) in (11) proves L_1<=6U and then (12). Facts d8ba46800ba433c2 and 0abb9119d9247de6 explicitly permit further zero-one deletion of their retained source arrays, so the phase-selected subset is an admissible arbitrary source deletion. Equations (7) and (8) give the top and fixed-star applications.

For (D), reality of the literal smooth source amplitude gives
c_{-h}=conjugate(c_h), as stated in facts 0abb9119d9247de6 and 707345f56faff29e. Multiplication by the positive real kappa_G preserves conjugacy. Put
P_+=sum_{j:q_j>0}q_j,
P_-=-sum_{j:q_j<0}q_j.
Then P_+,P_- are nonnegative and P_++P_-=P_1. Hence max(P_+,P_-)>=P_1/2. Retain both h and -h for every pair in the larger sign class. This deletion is h-symmetric, and its kappa-weighted sum is P_+ or -P_-, proving (13). The argument leading to (14) is the same as for (12), now with constant 1/2.

Suppose the negative class is larger. For its selected indices q_j<0. Since kappa_{G_j}=phi(G_j)/G_j lies strictly between zero and one, t_j=q_j/kappa_{G_j}<=q_j. Summing gives (15). The selected family is obtained from the original C2 array solely by an h-symmetric zero-one deletion, so when the original family also has the scales, rough-prime lower bound, squarefreeness and source conditions of fact 707345f56faff29e, it is one of the restrictions allowed there. Its literal sum is exactly the T_C2 in that fact. Inequality (15) supplies the hypothesis T_C2<=-A_0 with A_0=P_1/2, and (16) is exactly the remaining size hypothesis A_0^2>2E_comp. The cited routing conclusion follows.

Finally, w=i gives w+conjugate(w)=0 while 2|w|=2. For s equal positive atoms, L_1=s, E_2=s and N_eff=s. These examples prove the two claimed limitations of the finite lemmas. They are abstract coefficient examples and no step identifies them with the natural source selector, proving the final scope statements.

glossary.E_R: The squared l2 mass of the kappa-weighted real conjugate-pair coefficients q_j.
glossary.N_eff: The effective support L_1^2/E_2 of a finite complex coefficient family.
glossary.N_eff^R: The effective support P_1^2/E_R of the conjugate-paired real coefficient family.
glossary.P_1: The l1 mass of the kappa-weighted real conjugate-pair coefficients q_j.
glossary.c_z: The complete literal phased nonzero-Poisson atom after C2 factorization.
glossary.q_j: The kappa-weighted real contribution of one h,-h pair.
glossary.t_j: The unweighted literal real contribution c_j+conjugate(c_j) of one h,-h pair.

42720f6d803c4640.author: slava chan
42720f6d803c4640.statement:
NATURAL-FREQUENCY FOUR-TERM CORRELATED-ENERGY LEDGER. Fix integers J,C>=1. Let Q,H_P,H_T,S,T be real numbers at least one and let G>0. Assume H_T=G H_P and C^{-1}QH_T<=ST<=CQH_T. For every integer q with Q<=q<2Q choose a unit V_q modulo q. Let A be a fixed nonzero integer. Let complex coefficients nu_h,a_s,b_t be supported respectively on H_P<=h<2H_P, S<=s<2S, T<=t<2T and satisfy |nu_h|<=tau_J(h), |a_s|<=tau_J(s), |b_t|<=tau_J(t). Define W_q as the sum, over these h,s,t with gcd(st,q)=1, of nu_h a_s b_t e_q(A V_q h (st)^{-1}). Then for every epsilon>0,
H_P^{-1} sum_{Q<=q<2Q}|W_q| <<_{J,C,epsilon} (|A|QH_PST)^epsilon [G^{1/4}Q^2H_T^{1/2}S^{-1/4}+G^{1/4}Q^{7/4}H_T^{1/2}S^{1/4}+Q^2H_TS^{-1/2}+Q^{7/4}H_T].
No condition gcd(A,q)=1 or gcd(h,q)=1 is imposed. In particular, this exact bound contains no negative power of G: only its first two displayed terms carry an imbalance factor, and that factor is G^{1/4}.
42720f6d803c4640.proof:
Apply fact 73fb9efe1286f7e9 with its frequency parameter H set equal to H_P and with fixed numerator A and unit twist V_q. Its fixed-target extension gives, before the epsilon factor,
H_P^{-1} sum_q |W_q| << (Q/H_P)(H_PT)^{1/2}[H_PT+(H_PT)^2/Q]^{1/4}[QS^2+S^4]^{1/4}.
The product hypothesis gives T comparable, with constants depending only on C, to QH_T/S=GQH_P/S. Expand each fourth root into its two summands. Direct simplification gives the four terms
G^{3/4}Q^2H_P^{1/2}S^{-1/4},
G^{3/4}Q^{7/4}H_P^{1/2}S^{1/4},
GQ^2H_PS^{-1/2},
and GQ^{7/4}H_P.
Using H_T=GH_P turns these exactly into
G^{1/4}Q^2H_T^{1/2}S^{-1/4},
G^{1/4}Q^{7/4}H_T^{1/2}S^{1/4},
Q^2H_TS^{-1/2},
and Q^{7/4}H_T.
Restoring the epsilon factor proves the estimate. Fact 73fb9efe1286f7e9 explicitly permits a fixed nonzero numerator A with arbitrary common divisors with q, an arbitrary unit twist V_q, and unrestricted gcd(h,q). The final observation follows by inspection of the four exact terms.

glossary.H_T: The model trace frequency scale, equal to G times H_P.

42ae728764073a1a.title: RECTANGULAR PRIME-CELL CAPTURE AND THE EXACT DIAGONAL-DEFICIT SEAM
42ae728764073a1a.author: slava chan
42ae728764073a1a.statement:
RECTANGULAR PRIME-CELL CAPTURE AND THE EXACT DIAGONAL-DEFICIT SEAM.

Use the literal phased atoms c_z and the h-symmetric C2 source family of fact 42104ea7b4b24b0b. Let mathcal L be any finite retained family invariant under h replacing -h, and let
T_C2=sum_{z in mathcal L}c_z.
Thus T_C2 is real. Partition the finite set of active rough primes into K pairwise disjoint, phase-independent sets
