mathcal P_1,...,mathcal P_K,
where K is a positive integer. For 1<=i<=j<=K, let mathcal L_ij consist of the labels z whose unordered two-prime rough support has one prime in mathcal P_i and one prime in mathcal P_j, with both primes in mathcal P_i when i=j, and put
T_ij=sum_{z in mathcal L_ij}c_z.

(A) Every mathcal L_ij is h-symmetric, every T_ij is real, and
T_C2=sum_{1<=i<=j<=K}T_ij.                                  (1)
If A>0 and T_C2<=-A, then for some i<=j,
T_ij<=-2A/[K(K+1)].                                         (2)
Thus a phase-independent scale partition with K<<log x gives unconditional rectangular capture with only O((log x)^2) signed pigeonhole loss.

(B) Define
T_diag=sum_{i=1}^K T_ii,    T_off=sum_{1<=i<j<=K}T_ij.
Then
T_diag=T_C2-T_off.                                           (3)
For every B>0, the condition T_diag<=-B is equivalent to
T_off>=T_C2+B.                                               (4)
In particular, if 0<=rho<A and
T_off>=-rho,                                                 (5)
then for some i,
T_ii<=-(A-rho)/K.                                            (6)

No diagonal conclusion follows from (1), h-symmetry, and T_C2<=-A alone. Indeed, in the abstract finite coefficient model with K=2, take one formal rough support meeting both cells and one h,-h pair with
c_h=c_{-h}=-A/2.
Then T_C2=T_12=-A and T_11=T_22=0. This is a coefficient-interface countermodel, not a construction in the literal Poisson source.

(C) Each cell-pair restriction mathcal L_ij preserves every condition imposed before the phase-independent cell deletion, including h-symmetry. Assume a selected restriction also satisfies all scale, cutoff, squarefreeness, coprimality, and C2 hypotheses of fact 707345f56faff29e, and let E_comp,ij be the complement quantity of that fact for this restriction. For some real A_ij>0, if
T_ij<=-A_ij    and    A_ij^2>2E_comp,ij,                      (7)
then its support-disjoint full-rough-conductor carrier F_4,ij satisfies
Re(F_4,ij)>=A_ij^2-E_comp,ij>=A_ij^2/2.                      (8)
Consequently (2), together with the corresponding instance of (7), routes a negative total C2 source into some rectangular four-prime cell-pair block. Under (5), equation (6), together with (7) for that diagonal restriction, routes it into a diagonal block; if mathcal P_i is contained in one common prime cell, all four rough primes in F_4,ii lie in that common cell.

Fact 7c1f38cfbb8d0569 shows that a negative total high-source anomaly does not itself supply the assumed negative C2 total. This theorem supplies no bound of the form (5) for the natural source. It proves no two-scale rectangular decoder estimate, no importance-sampled varying-fibre cancellation, no fixed-fibre capture, no common-cell or cross-cell analytic bound, and no Goldbach implication.
42ae728764073a1a.proof:
By fact 42104ea7b4b24b0b, replacing h by -h conjugates c_z. The rough-prime support of z does not depend on the sign of h. Therefore every mathcal L_ij is invariant under h replacing -h, and its terms pair into conjugates, so T_ij is real.

The sets mathcal P_i partition the active rough primes. Every label z has an unordered support consisting of two distinct active rough primes. There is therefore a unique unordered cell pair {i,j}, written with i<=j, containing its support. Hence the sets mathcal L_ij are pairwise disjoint and have union mathcal L. Summing c_z over this disjoint union proves (1).

There are K(K+1)/2 index pairs with i<=j. If every T_ij were greater than -2A/[K(K+1)], then (1) would give T_C2>-A, contradicting T_C2<=-A. This proves (2). When K<<log x, the displayed number of cell pairs is O((log x)^2), proving the scale-partition sentence without any analytic input.

The diagonal and off-diagonal index pairs partition the pairs in (1), so
T_C2=T_diag+T_off.
Rearrangement gives (3). For B>0,
T_diag<=-B
is equivalent, using (3), to
T_C2-T_off<=-B,
which is equivalent to T_off>=T_C2+B. This proves (4). Under T_C2<=-A and (5), equation (3) gives
T_diag<=-A+rho=-(A-rho).
If every one of the K diagonal sums were greater than -(A-rho)/K, their sum would be greater than -(A-rho), a contradiction. This proves (6).

For the countermodel, the two equal real coefficients obey
c_{-h}=conjugate(c_h).
Their support belongs to the unique off-diagonal pair (1,2), so T_12=-A and the two diagonal sums vanish. All assumptions of the finite signed partition and h-symmetry hold, while every diagonal conclusion fails. No arithmetic formula for these formal coefficients is asserted.

Finally, membership in a fixed cell pair depends only on the two rough primes and is independent of h and of every coefficient phase. Passing from mathcal L to mathcal L_ij is therefore an additional zero-one deletion that preserves h-symmetry and all previously imposed pointwise source conditions. Under the explicit extra hypotheses in (C), fact 707345f56faff29e applies to that selected restriction with the positive threshold A_0=A_ij and gives
Re(F_4,ij)>=A_ij^2-E_comp,ij.
The strict inequality in (7) implies E_comp,ij<A_ij^2/2, proving (8). Each of the two source supports used in this routed pair has its rough primes in mathcal P_i and mathcal P_j. When i=j and mathcal P_i is contained in one common prime cell, all four support-disjoint rough primes therefore lie in that cell.

The last paragraph is a scope ledger. The present proof starts after a negative C2 total is assumed; fact 7c1f38cfbb8d0569 proves that terminal anatomy and total sign alone do not furnish it. Equations (1)-(8) are finite signed identities and conditional use of fact 707345f56faff29e. They contain no estimate for T_off and no decoder or varying-fibre analysis.

glossary.A_ij: A positive magnitude threshold for a selected rectangular cell sum.
glossary.E_comp,ij: The complement quantity from fact 707345f56faff29e for the cell-pair restriction mathcal L_ij.
glossary.F_4,ij: The support-disjoint full-rough-conductor carrier obtained from fact 707345f56faff29e for mathcal L_ij.
glossary.T_diag: The sum of the diagonal cell contributions T_ii.
glossary.T_ii: The diagonal source sum in cell i.
glossary.T_ij: The real literal C2 source sum over mathcal L_ij.
glossary.T_off: The sum of the off-diagonal cell contributions T_ij with i<j.
glossary.mathcal L_ij: The retained literal C2 labels whose two rough primes lie in cells i and j.
glossary.mathcal P_i: The i-th phase-independent cell in a finite partition of the active rough primes.
glossary.mathcal P_j: The j-th phase-independent cell in that partition.

43c14e02f4c983a4.title: TARGET-GCD CONDUCTOR DESCENT, EXACT REDUCED-SLOPE PROJECTOR, AND BOUNDED-CONDUCTOR PAYMENT FOR THE RAY-COMPRESSED GA MOMENT
43c14e02f4c983a4.author: slava chan
43c14e02f4c983a4.statement:
TARGET-GCD CONDUCTOR DESCENT, EXACT REDUCED-SLOPE PROJECTOR, AND BOUNDED-CONDUCTOR PAYMENT FOR THE RAY-COMPRESSED GA MOMENT.

Adopt the fixed orientation, anatomy
\(\mathfrak a\in\{A,C_\ell\}\), frequency block
\[
 1\le F\le x^3,\qquad F\le |h|<2F,
\]
and dilator block
\[
 \mathcal D\le d_\lambda<2\mathcal D
\]
of fact 57a4d0753d8f290d. Retain its primitive signed rays
\(R=(\epsilon,a,b)\), ray coefficients \(C_\lambda(R)\), ray phases
\(P_\lambda(R)\), and primitive ray determinant
\[
 \delta(R,R')=\epsilon ba'-\epsilon'b'a.
\]
Put
\[
 c_\lambda=(d_\lambda,\mathscr A),\qquad
 r_\lambda={d_\lambda\over c_\lambda},\qquad
 \mathscr A_\lambda={\mathscr A\over c_\lambda}.                 \tag{1}
\]
Then
\[
 (\mathscr A_\lambda,r_\lambda)=1.                               \tag{2}
\]
For \(R=(\epsilon,a,b)\in\mathscr R_\lambda\), define its reduced ray slope
\[
 x_\lambda(R)
 \equiv \epsilon b(a v_\lambda)^{-1}\pmod {r_\lambda}.            \tag{3}
\]
When \(r_\lambda=1\), the residue group has one element and every inverse in (3) is interpreted in that group. The exact ray phase descends as
\[
 P_\lambda(R)
 =
 e_{r_\lambda}\!\left(\mathscr A_\lambda x_\lambda(R)\right).    \tag{4}
\]

For two rays \(R,R'\in\mathscr R_\lambda\),
\[
 x_\lambda(R)=x_\lambda(R')
 \Longleftrightarrow
 r_\lambda\mid\delta(R,R')
 \Longleftrightarrow
 d_\lambda\mid\mathscr A\delta(R,R').                            \tag{5}
\]
Thus, for distinct rays, equality of reduced slopes is exactly the fully resonant condition of fact 57a4d0753d8f290d. In particular:

1. if \(r_\lambda=1\), every distinct ray pair is fully resonant and the nonresonant sector on this copy is empty;

2. if \(r_\lambda>8QF\), the map \(R\mapsto x_\lambda(R)\) is injective and the fully resonant sector on this copy is empty.                       \(\tag{6}\)

For each residue \(x\) modulo \(r_\lambda\), put
\[
 G_\lambda(x)
 =
 \sum_{\substack{R\in\mathscr R_\lambda\\x_\lambda(R)=x}}
 C_\lambda(R),                                                    \tag{7}
\]
with an empty sum equal to zero. Then
\[
 K_\lambda
 =
 \sum_{x\ ({\rm mod}\ r_\lambda)}
 e_{r_\lambda}(\mathscr A_\lambda x)G_\lambda(x).                \tag{8}
\]
The anatomy-restricted moments of facts e55b27d39c593164 and
57a4d0753d8f290d satisfy the exact positive equal-slope identity
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{(0)}(\mathcal D)
 +\mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{({\rm FR})}(\mathcal D)
 =
 \sum_{n,\lambda}\sum_{x\ ({\rm mod}\ r_\lambda)}
 |G_\lambda(x)|^2
 \ge0,
 }                                                               \tag{9}
\]
and the exact centered off-slope identity
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{({\rm NR})}(\mathcal D)
 =
 \sum_{n,\lambda}
 \sum_{\substack{x,y\ ({\rm mod}\ r_\lambda)\\x\ne y}}
 e_{r_\lambda}\!\left(\mathscr A_\lambda(x-y)\right)
 G_\lambda(x)\overline{G_\lambda(y)}.
 }                                                               \tag{10}
\]
Hence the pair-dependent nonresonance deletion is precisely the deletion of the equal reduced-slope classes after target-gcd descent.

Let \(\mathscr L\) be any subfamily of the exact \((n,\lambda)\)-copies, and let the superscript \(\mathscr L\) denote restriction of all four moments to this subfamily. Suppose
\[
 r_\lambda\le R_0\qquad(\lambda\in\mathscr L)                    \tag{11}
\]
for a real number \(R_0\ge1\). Then
\[
 \left|
 \mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{({\rm NR}),\mathscr L}(\mathcal D)
 \right|
 \le
 \max\{R_0-1,0\}
 \left(
 \mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{(0),\mathscr L}(\mathcal D)
 +\mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{({\rm FR}),\mathscr L}(\mathcal D)
 \right),                                                        \tag{12}
\]
and the parenthesized quantity is nonnegative. Consequently, for every
\(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 \left|
 \mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{({\rm NR}),\mathscr L}(\mathcal D)
 \right|
 \ll_\varepsilon
 \max\{R_0-1,0\}x^\varepsilon|\omega_F|^2
 \left(BQF+{BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}\right).                      \tag{13}
\]
In particular, the subfamily with
\[
 r_\lambda\le2,\qquad \mathcal D\le QF                           \tag{14}
\]
satisfies GA-NR-DIL:
\[
 \left|
 \mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{({\rm NR}),\mathscr L}(\mathcal D)
 \right|
 \ll_\varepsilon
 x^\varepsilon|\omega_F|^2{BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}.              \tag{15}
\]
For arbitrary \(\mathcal D\), the subfamily \(r_\lambda=1\) has zero nonresonant moment.

Equations (9)--(10) are the exact reduced-conductor physical projector requested after the dual-shift no-fit of fact 83d01a70b7f16e15. They prove no estimate for reduced conductors greater than \(2\) in the large-\(\mathcal D\) range, no complete GA-OFF-SYN or GA-NR-DIL estimate, no good-\(\mathscr W\) payment, and no Goldbach conclusion.
43c14e02f4c983a4.proof:
Write
\[
 d_\lambda=c_\lambda r_\lambda,\qquad
 \mathscr A=c_\lambda\mathscr A_\lambda.
\]
The definition \(c_\lambda=(d_\lambda,\mathscr A)\) gives (2). Every
\(R\in\mathscr R_\lambda\) contains at least one supported modulus \(ka\).
Fact 57a4d0753d8f290d proves
\[
 (av_\lambda,d_\lambda)=1,
\]
so \(av_\lambda\) is also a unit modulo \(r_\lambda\), and (3) is defined.
Using the definition \(e_m(z)=\exp(2\pi iz/m)\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_\lambda(R)
 &=e_{d_\lambda}\!\left(
   \mathscr A\epsilon b(av_\lambda)^{-1}\right)\\
 &=e_{c_\lambda r_\lambda}\!\left(
   c_\lambda\mathscr A_\lambda\epsilon b(av_\lambda)^{-1}\right)\\
 &=e_{r_\lambda}\!\left(
   \mathscr A_\lambda\epsilon b(av_\lambda)^{-1}\right),
 \end{aligned}
\]
which is (4).

Let \(R=(\epsilon,a,b)\) and
\(R'=(\epsilon',a',b')\). By putting the two slopes over the common unit denominator \(aa'v_\lambda\) modulo \(r_\lambda\),
\[
 x_\lambda(R)-x_\lambda(R')
 \equiv
 \delta(R,R')(aa'v_\lambda)^{-1}\pmod {r_\lambda}.               \tag{16}
\]
Therefore their slopes are equal if and only if
\(r_\lambda\mid\delta(R,R')\). Since
\((\mathscr A_\lambda,r_\lambda)=1\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 d_\lambda\mid\mathscr A\delta(R,R')
 &\Longleftrightarrow
 c_\lambda r_\lambda
 \mid c_\lambda\mathscr A_\lambda\delta(R,R')\\
 &\Longleftrightarrow
 r_\lambda\mid\delta(R,R').
 \end{aligned}
\]
This proves (5).

If \(r_\lambda=1\), equation (5) makes every distinct ray pair fully resonant, so no pair remains in the NR sector. If
\(r_\lambda>8QF\), fact 57a4d0753d8f290d gives
\[
 0<|\delta(R,R')|<8QF<r_\lambda
\]
for distinct rays, so \(r_\lambda\nmid\delta(R,R')\). This proves (6).

Group equation (4) of fact 57a4d0753d8f290d according to the fibres of
\(x_\lambda\). Equations (4) and (7) give (8). Expanding (8) yields
\[
 |K_\lambda|^2
 =
 \sum_{x,y\ ({\rm mod}\ r_\lambda)}
 e_{r_\lambda}\!\left(\mathscr A_\lambda(x-y)\right)
 G_\lambda(x)\overline{G_\lambda(y)}.                            \tag{17}
\]
The terms \(x=y\) equal \(\sum_x|G_\lambda(x)|^2\). Expanding (7), these are exactly all ordered ray pairs with equal reduced slope. By (5), their ray diagonals are the \(\Delta=0\) sector and their distinct-ray terms are the fully resonant sector. Summing over the exact fixed-anatomy copies proves (9). The terms \(x\ne y\) are, by (5), exactly the nonresonant sector, proving (10).

We prove (12). For one \(\lambda\), let
\[
 t_\lambda
 =
 |\{x\pmod {r_\lambda}:G_\lambda(x)\ne0\}|.
\]
Then
\[
 t_\lambda\le r_\lambda\le R_0.
\]
On the \(t_\lambda\)-dimensional occupied residue space, the quadratic form in (10) is
\[
 |\langle u_\lambda,G_\lambda\rangle|^2-\|G_\lambda\|_2^2,
 \qquad
 u_\lambda(x)=e_{r_\lambda}(-\mathscr A_\lambda x).
\]
The rank-one calculation in fact 57a4d0753d8f290d applies with
\(m_\lambda\) replaced by \(t_\lambda\): its operator norm is \(0\) for
\(t_\lambda=1\) and \(t_\lambda-1\) for \(t_\lambda\ge2\). Hence the absolute value of the \(\lambda\)-summand is at most
\[
 \max\{R_0-1,0\}\sum_x|G_\lambda(x)|^2.
\]
Sum this inequality over \(\mathscr L\) and use the restricted version of the positive identity (9). This proves (12).

The proof of the \(\Delta=0\) estimate (17) in fact e55b27d39c593164 is an absolute count, and the proof of its fully resonant estimate (18) is also an absolute count. Therefore both estimates remain valid after restriction to the fixed anatomy and the subfamily \(\mathscr L\):
\[
 \mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{(0),\mathscr L}(\mathcal D)
 \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon|\omega_F|^2BQF,
\]
\[
 \left|
 \mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{({\rm FR}),\mathscr L}(\mathcal D)
 \right|
 \ll_\varepsilon
 x^\varepsilon|\omega_F|^2{BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}.
\]
The restricted version of (9) is nonnegative, so it is bounded above by the sum of these two absolute bounds. Insert them into (12) to prove (13).

Under (14), \(\max\{R_0-1,0\}\le1\), and
\[
 BQF
 \le {BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}
\]
because \(\mathcal D\le QF\). Equation (13) proves (15). The assertion for \(r_\lambda=1\) was proved directly from (5), so it holds for every \(\mathcal D\). All remaining limitations are explicit.

glossary.G_lambda(x): The sum of primitive-ray coefficients in one reduced-slope residue class.
glossary.equal reduced-slope energy: The positive quantity M^(0)+M^(FR), equal to the sum of |G_lambda(x)|^2.
glossary.reduced ray slope: The residue x_lambda(R)=epsilon b(a v_lambda)^(-1) modulo the target-coprime ray conductor.

444b45f182bff0fc.title: INVERSE-PRODUCT CONSUMER NO-FIT AT THE ACTUAL-Z_MID ENDPOINT. Assume the actual-Z_mid upper-boundary setting and exact reciprocity reduction of fact 58c03698e1b077c3 with g=1 and |h|=1. Thus the reciprocal phase, apart from the smooth joint endpoint weight, is
444b45f182bff0fc.author: slava chan
444b45f182bff0fc.statement:
INVERSE-PRODUCT CONSUMER NO-FIT AT THE ACTUAL-Z_MID ENDPOINT. Assume the actual-Z_mid upper-boundary setting and exact reciprocity reduction of fact 58c03698e1b077c3 with g=1 and |h|=1. Thus the reciprocal phase, apart from the smooth joint endpoint weight, is
e_b(N a^{-1}),
where a has dyadic length A_0=x^(1/2+o(1)) and the modulus b has dyadic length B_0=x^(2/3+o(1)).

Grant, in the most favorable possible form for a direct use of fact 73fb9efe1286f7e9, that a dyadic block has been factored as a=st with separated divisor-bounded coefficients, S<=s<2S, T<=t<2T, and ST=A_0 up to fixed dyadic constants, and that all inherited masks and the smooth endpoint weight have been separated at negligible x^(o(1)) cost. Set the frequency length H=1 and the modulus scale Q=B_0 in that fact. Its raw right-hand side is
E(S,T;A_0,B_0)
 =B_0 T^(1/2)[T+T^2/B_0]^(1/4)[B_0S^2+S^4]^(1/4).                    (1)
For every S,T>=1 with ST=A_0 and A_0<=B_0,
E(S,T;A_0,B_0)/(B_0A_0)
 >=(2sqrt(B_0)/A_0)^(1/4).                                          (2)
Conversely, choosing S=sqrt(B_0) and T=A_0/sqrt(B_0), whenever these are admissible up to fixed dyadic constants, makes the two sides of (2) comparable. Hence at the natural endpoint scales the optimized exponent supplied by the right-hand side of fact 73fb9efe1286f7e9 is
inf_{ST=A_0} E(S,T;A_0,B_0)=x^(9/8+o(1)).                            (3)
This is weaker than the Duke--Friedlander--Iwaniec bound x^(13/12+o(1)) already obtained in fact 58c03698e1b077c3, and it is above the x^(1-delta) bound required by the moving-boundary theorem for every fixed delta>0. Therefore direct factorization of the Möbius variable followed solely by fact 73fb9efe1286f7e9 cannot close the actual-Z_mid g=1, |h|=1 upper boundary. This is a sharp no-fit for that theorem's displayed right-hand side; it does not assert a lower bound for the original exponential sum and does not exclude a stronger hyper-inverse theorem or cancellation before the separated-block triangle inequality.
444b45f182bff0fc.proof:
By fact 58c03698e1b077c3, additive reciprocity converts the g=1, h=1 upper-face phase exactly to e_b(N a^{-1}) times a smooth joint weight. Under the favorable separated factorization assumed in the statement, write a=st. Since (a,b)=1, both s and t are coprime to b and
a^{-1}=(st)^{-1} modulo b.
Thus the character is exactly e_b(N(st)^{-1}). It matches (1) of fact 73fb9efe1286f7e9 with modulus q=b, its fixed target A=N, unit twist U_q=1, and a single frequency h=1, so H=1. The fixed-target extension in that fact permits N to be noncoprime to b and costs only N^epsilon, which is x^epsilon because N is comparable to x. Substitution of Q=B_0 and H=1 into (2) of that fact gives (1), apart from the permitted x^epsilon factor.

It remains to optimize the displayed algebraic expression. Divide (1) by the absolute block scale B_0ST=B_0A_0. Factoring powers of S and T gives
(E/(B_0A_0))^4
 =((B_0+S^2)(1+T/B_0))/(S^2T).
Since ST=A_0, this equals
((B_0+S^2)(1+T/B_0))/(SA_0)
and is at least
(B_0+S^2)/(SA_0)
 =(B_0/S+S)/A_0.
The arithmetic-geometric mean inequality gives B_0/S+S>=2sqrt(B_0), proving (2).

At S=sqrt(B_0) and T=A_0/sqrt(B_0), the exact fourth power of the normalized expression is
(2sqrt(B_0)/A_0)(1+A_0/B_0^(3/2)).
Because A_0<=B_0, the final factor is bounded above and below by positive absolute constants. Thus (2) is sharp up to an absolute factor whenever the balanced factor lengths are available, and fixed dyadic perturbations do not alter its exponent.

Finally, A_0=x^(1/2+o(1)) and B_0=x^(2/3+o(1)). Therefore
B_0A_0(2sqrt(B_0)/A_0)^(1/4)
 =x^(2/3+1/2+(1/3-1/2)/4+o(1))
 =x^(9/8+o(1)).
This proves (3). The comparison with x^(13/12+o(1)) and with x^(1-delta) is immediate because 13/12<9/8 and 1-delta<1<9/8. The conclusion is only about what follows from the literal right-hand side in fact 73fb9efe1286f7e9, so it makes no claim that the original sum itself is large.

glossary.A_0: The dyadic length of the factorized reciprocal argument on the actual-Z_mid upper boundary.
glossary.B_0: The dyadic modulus length on the actual-Z_mid upper boundary.
glossary.E(S,T;A_0,B_0): The raw right-hand side of the inverse-product estimate 73fb9efe1286f7e9 after setting its frequency length to one.

4476fc604b6534ac.title: For each i in {1,2,3,4}, let p_i be an odd prime, let A_i and R_count be positive integers with A_i<p_i/2, and define the symmetric nonzero low-frequency block
4476fc604b6534ac.author: slava chan
4476fc604b6534ac.statement:
For each i in {1,2,3,4}, let p_i be an odd prime, let A_i and R_count be positive integers with A_i<p_i/2, and define the symmetric nonzero low-frequency block
B_i={a modulo p_i: the least absolute integer representative a_tilde satisfies 1<=|a_tilde|<=A_i}.
Let t_i be an integer and W_i a nonnegative integer. For every 1<=r<=R_count let
I_{i,r}={s_{i,r},s_{i,r}+1,...,s_{i,r}+L_{i,r}-1}
be an interval of integers such that
I_{i,r} is contained in [t_i-W_i,t_i+W_i]
and
1<=L_{i,0}<=L_{i,r}<=L_{i,1}.
Put
theta_i=2 pi A_i W_i/p_i
and assume theta_i<pi/4.
For a in B_i define
D_{i,r}(a)=sum_{n in I_{i,r}} exp(-2 pi i a_tilde n/p_i),
let H_i=l^2(B_i) with counting measure, and put
phi_{i,r}=D_{i,r}/||D_{i,r}||_{H_i}.
Define
kappa_i=cos(2theta_i)(L_{i,0}cos(theta_i)/L_{i,1})^2.

Then the following hold.

(i) For every r,s, the Gram entry <phi_{i,r},phi_{i,s}>_{H_i} is real and is at least kappa_i>0. Hence the synthesis operator S_i:C^{R_count}->H_i given by S_i bold_e_r=phi_{i,r} satisfies
||S_i||^2>=kappa_i R_count.

(ii) In the four-fold Hilbert tensor product H^{(4)}=H_1 tensor H_2 tensor H_3 tensor H_4, put
Phi_r=phi_{1,r} tensor phi_{2,r} tensor phi_{3,r} tensor phi_{4,r}
and define S^{(4)}:C^{R_count}->H^{(4)} by S^{(4)}bold_e_r=Phi_r. Then
||S^{(4)}||^2 >= R_count product_{i=1}^4 kappa_i.
For every exact factorization S^{(4)}=VU through a complex Hilbert space K,
||U||^2||V||^2 >= R_count product_{i=1}^4 kappa_i.
Thus a contractive coefficient-copy map forces the folding map to pay this tax, while a contractive folding map forces the coefficient map to pay it.

(iii) At one fixed frequency a in B_i, each normalized value D_{i,r}(a)/|D_{i,r}(a)| is merely a scalar of modulus one. The associated singleton synthesis C^{R_count}->C has squared norm exactly R_count and rank one. This singleton fact uses a frequency-dependent phase and supplies no simultaneous realization of the full block B_i. Part (i), by contrast, is one Gram estimate for the entire symmetric low-frequency block with the same coefficient vector across every frequency.

This is a finite-dimensional shifted-window common-cone theorem under the displayed common-window-span hypotheses. It is not an arithmetic PAVG27 counterexample, and its factorization product tax is not by itself a bound for any one named coefficient constant in an arithmetic Hilbert realization.
4476fc604b6534ac.proof:
Fix i and abbreviate p=p_i, A=A_i, t=t_i, W=W_i, theta=theta_i, B=B_i, I_r=I_{i,r}, L_r=L_{i,r}, D_r=D_{i,r}, and H=H_i.

For a in B let a_tilde be its least absolute representative and rotate the interval transform by the common phase:
Z_r(a)=exp(2 pi i a_tilde t/p)D_r(a)
      =sum_{n in I_r} exp(-2 pi i a_tilde(n-t)/p).
Every n in I_r satisfies |n-t|<=W, and |a_tilde|<=A. Therefore every summand in Z_r(a) has argument in [-theta,theta]. Since theta<pi/4, their real parts are positive. It follows that Z_r(a) itself has argument in [-theta,theta] and
L_r cos(theta)<=|Z_r(a)|<=L_r.
In particular D_r(a) is nonzero. Using the length bounds gives
L_{i,0}cos(theta)<=|D_r(a)|<=L_{i,1}.                                    (1)

For any r,s, the common phase cancels in D_r(a)overline(D_s(a)). The arguments of Z_r(a) and Z_s(a) both lie in [-theta,theta], so
Re(D_r(a)overline(D_s(a)))
 =Re(Z_r(a)overline(Z_s(a)))
 >=cos(2theta)|D_r(a)||D_s(a)|.                                           (2)
The block B is symmetric under a_tilde -> -a_tilde, and D_r(-a)=overline(D_r(a)). Consequently
< D_r,D_s>_H=sum_{a in B}D_r(a)overline(D_s(a))
is real. Summing (2), using (1), and using ||D_r||_H<=|B|^{1/2}L_{i,1}, gives
<phi_{i,r},phi_{i,s}>_H
 >= |B|cos(2theta)(L_{i,0}cos(theta))^2/(|B|L_{i,1}^2)
 =kappa_i.                                                               (3)
This proves the common-cone Gram bound.

Let G_i=S_i^*S_i and let bold_one be the vector in C^{R_count} all of whose coordinates equal one. By (3),
< G_i bold_one,bold_one> >=kappa_i R_count^2.
Since ||bold_one||^2=R_count, the Rayleigh quotient gives
||S_i||^2=||G_i||>=kappa_iR_count.
This proves (i).

For (ii), the Hilbert tensor-product inner product factorizes:
<Phi_r,Phi_s>_{H^{(4)}}
 =product_{i=1}^4 <phi_{i,r},phi_{i,s}>_{H_i}.
Every factor is real and at least kappa_i by (i), hence every four-tensor Gram entry is at least product_i kappa_i. Applying the same all-ones Rayleigh quotient proves
||S^{(4)}||^2>=R_count product_i kappa_i.
If S^{(4)}=VU, operator-norm submultiplicativity gives
||S^{(4)}||<=||V||||U||.
Squaring yields the stated product tax. The two contractive-convention conclusions follow immediately.

Finally fix one a in B. By (1), every D_r(a) is nonzero, so psi_r=D_r(a)/|D_r(a)| is defined and has modulus one. The singleton synthesis is the row functional c -> sum_r c_r psi_r. Its squared operator norm is the squared l^2 norm of its coefficient row, namely sum_r|psi_r|^2=R_count, and its range is one-dimensional. The normalizing phases psi_r depend on a, so this calculation does not construct one factorization or one Gram comparison valid simultaneously for all a in B. This proves (iii) and the claimed distinction.

glossary.B_i: symmetric block of the 2A_i smallest nonzero frequencies modulo p_i
glossary.D_{i,r}: Fourier transform of the shifted interval I_{i,r}, restricted to B_i
glossary.H^{(4)}: four-fold Hilbert tensor product of H_1,H_2,H_3,H_4
glossary.H_i: complex Hilbert space l^2(B_i) with counting measure
glossary.I_{i,r}: r-th lifted integer interval in the i-th common window
glossary.Phi_r: tensor product of the four normalized profiles bearing the common index r
glossary.W_i: radius of the common lifted window containing all I_{i,r}
glossary.a_tilde: least absolute integer representative of a residue in B_i
glossary.kappa_i: explicit positive common-cone Gram lower bound
glossary.theta_i: maximum phase excursion 2 pi A_i W_i/p_i on the low-frequency block

44e700816602dd36.title: H-TWIST L4 PRE-CAUCHY CONTRACT AND THE FINITE-BAND/COMPLETE-SOURCE SUPPLIER GAP
44e700816602dd36.author: slava chan
44e700816602dd36.statement:
H-TWIST L4 PRE-CAUCHY CONTRACT AND THE FINITE-BAND/COMPLETE-SOURCE SUPPLIER GAP.

Let cal O be a finite outer index set. Let I be a finite set of integers contained in an interval of N consecutive integers. For j in cal O and h in I let x_{j,h}(q) be a finite complex row on a finite q-set, and let c_j be a complex outer coefficient. Put
  y_{j,h}=sum_qx_{j,h}(q),
  A_j(theta)=sum_{h in I}y_{j,h}e(htheta),
  S_pre=H^(-1)sum_{j in cal O}c_jA_j(0),                    (1)
where e(theta)=exp(2 pi i theta), H>0, and theta is in R/Z. Define
  C_{4/3}=(sum_j|c_j|^(4/3))^(3/4),
  cal M_4=integral_{R/Z}sum_j|A_j(theta)|^4dtheta.           (2)
Then
 |S_pre|^2
 <=H^(-2)|I+I|^(1/2)C_{4/3}^2cal M_4^(1/2)
 <=H^(-2)(2N-1)^(1/2)C_{4/3}^2cal M_4^(1/2).                (3)
The factor N^(1/2) in this squared point-evaluation inequality is sharp up to an absolute constant.

Suppose cal O consists of pairs (v,p) in V<=v<2V and P<=p<2P, with p prime, N<<H, |c_{v,p}|<=B, and
  VP=QH.                                                     (4)
Then
 |S_pre|^2<<B^2Q^(3/2)cal M_4^(1/2).                        (5)
Thus, solely through (5), the estimate
  cal M_4<<P^2Q^(7/3)                                      (6)
is sufficient for |S_pre|^2<<B^2P Q^(8/3), up to subpolynomial coefficient losses. Likewise cal M_4<<B^(-4)Q^(5-2eta) is sufficient for |S_pre|^2<<Q^(4-eta). No necessity or converse is asserted.

There are two exact but distinct twist statements.

FINITE BAND. If j=(v,p), the frequency span of I is D, and p>2D, then
 integral_{R/Z}|A_{v,p}(theta)|^4dtheta
 =p^(-1)sum_{t modulo p}|A_{v,p}(t/p)|^4.                   (7)
This applies to the finite-band polynomial in (1), but supplies no Poisson source identity for a proper h-subblock.

COMPLETE ROW. Put n=vp, assume gcd(v,p)=1, and let every F_q be a smooth compactly supported complex function on R. Use the Fourier convention
 Fhat_q(xi)=integral_R F_q(x)e(-xi x)dx.                    (8)
For gcd(q,n)=1 define
 a_q(theta)=n^(-1)sum_{h in Z;h nonzero}
   Fhat_q(h/n)e_n(hAqbar)e(htheta),                          (9)
where e_n(z)=e(z/n) and qbar is the inverse modulo n. For t modulo p,
 a_q(t/p)=u_t(q)-z_q,                                      (10)
 u_t(q)=sum_{m in Z;qm congruent A modulo n}F_q(m+vt),
 z_q=n^(-1)Fhat_q(0).                                      (11)
Thus the twist preserves qm+nk=A after a change of variable and translates the amplitude by vt. Equations (10)-(11) require the restored complete nonzero h-family, which is generally not finite-band and therefore is not covered by (7).

Assume additionally that q ranges over a set cal Q of cardinality at most Q, |F_q(x)|<=B for all real x, and F_q is supported in an interval of length at most Cn/H, with fixed C and H>C. Put
 X_t=#{q in cal Q:u_t(q) is nonzero}.                       (12)
Then
 X_t<=Q,
 sum_{t modulo p}X_t<=Q(1+Cp/H).                            (13)
If p>2H, then for every fixed integer r>=1,
 p^(-1)sum_tX_t^r<<_C Q^r/H.                               (14)
Thus average occupancy is O(Q/H), but pointwise occupancy is only O(Q). Relative to an unjustified pointwise bound X_t<<Q/H, equation (14) loses H^2 for r=3 and H^3 for r=4.

For the complete twisted q-row b_t(q)=u_t(q)-z_q, assume p does not divide Aq for q in cal Q. Define
 rho_{12}=A(q_2-q_1)(q_1q_2)^(-1) modulo p,
 beta_t=b_t(q_1)conjugate(b_t(q_2))
          conjugate(b_t(q_3))b_t(q_4),
and let Delta be the exact reciprocal-slope determinant of fact ace362082848a702. Put
 cal J_t=sum_{rho_{12}=rho_{34}}beta_t,
 cal D_t=sum_{Delta=0}beta_t,
 cal M_t=M_1(b_t,b_t,b_t,b_t),                              (15)
where M_1 is the Delta-nonzero centered form with constant physical kernel W=1. Then
 cal J_t=p^(-1)sum_{ell modulo p}
   |sum_qb_t(q)e_p(ell A qbar)|^4>=0,
 cal D_t=sum_lambda|B_{lambda,t}|^2>=0,                     (16)
and
 |sum_qb_t(q)|^4
 =p cal J_t-(p-1)cal D_t-p cal M_t.                         (17)

The accepted suppliers have the following scope.
(a) Fact ace362082848a702 gives b_t=u_t-z and the sixteen-term U/Z expansion only for cal M_t; it does not estimate cal J_t or cal D_t.
(b) Fact 914048233fada05f estimates the all-U Delta-nonzero term only when the source row is an eligible fixed-interval injective graph. Equations (13)-(14) give average, not pointwise, twist sparsity.
(c) Facts 0e8ef74ba484418d and 11ec605c5135a640 require mean-zero physical kernels and pointwise type-(U)/(Z) rows. The kernel W=1 in (15) is not mean-zero, and (13) does not supply their pointwise hypothesis.
(d) Fact 4792a797443e9961 separates the physical mean after a post-Cauchy PMD energy has been formed; it does not estimate cal M_4 or cal J_t.
(e) Fact 27540b4094f677f4 identifies the exact-slope diagonal but gives no complete-source twist average of it.

Therefore one rigorous sufficient new pre-Cauchy supplier is the finite-band vector estimate (6) for the literal x_{v,p,h}(q), with every outer coefficient, source mask, and scaled-smooth/projective label retained. A source-preserving alternative needs two new statements: first, a controlled band-restoration or alias formula connecting the finite-band moment in (7) to the complete rows in (10); second, estimates at the scale in (6) for the exact complete-row decomposition (17), including its modular-mean and exact-slope terms and a twist-stable extension of the Delta-nonzero U/Z estimates. None of these new estimates or bridges is asserted. This is a theorem-interface result only and makes no impossibility or Goldbach claim.
44e700816602dd36.proof:
For each outer index j define
 d_j(s)=sum_{h_1,h_2 in I;h_1+h_2=s}
          y_{j,h_1}y_{j,h_2}.                              (18)
Then A_j(0)^2=sum_sd_j(s). Cauchy's inequality over I+I gives
 |A_j(0)|^4<=|I+I|sum_s|d_j(s)|^2.                          (19)
Parseval applied to A_j(theta)^2 gives
 sum_s|d_j(s)|^2=integral_{R/Z}|A_j(theta)|^4dtheta.         (20)
Hölder over j gives
 |sum_jc_jA_j(0)|^2
 <=C_{4/3}^2(sum_j|A_j(0)|^4)^(1/2).                        (21)
Sum (19), use (20), and multiply by H^(-2). This proves (3), because |I+I|<=2N-1.

For sharpness, take one outer index, I={0,...,N-1}, and y_h=1. Then A(0)=N, while
 integral|A(theta)|^4dtheta
 =N^2+2sum_{r=1}^{N-1}r^2=(2N^3+N)/3.                      (22)
Thus |A(0)|^4 divided by its fourth moment is asymptotic to 3N/2.

Under (4), there are O(VP) outer pairs, so
 C_{4/3}^2<<B^2(VP)^(3/2).                                 (23)
Insert N<<H and VP=QH into (3):
 H^(-2)H^(1/2)(QH)^(3/2)=Q^(3/2).
This proves (5). Substituting either displayed sufficient bound for cal M_4 into (5) proves its stated implication.

The frequencies of |A(theta)|^4 lie between -2D and 2D. When p>2D, no nonzero frequency in this range is divisible by p. Averaging over theta=t/p and integrating both retain only the zero frequency, proving (7).

For (10), fix q and t and define the translated smooth compactly supported function
 G_{q,t}(x)=F_q(x+vt).                                      (24)
With convention (8), substitution y=x+vt gives
 Ghat_{q,t}(xi)=e(xi vt)Fhat_q(xi).                         (25)
Apply the progression Poisson identity of fact ace362082848a702 to G_{q,t}:
 n^(-1)sum_{h in Z}Ghat_{q,t}(h/n)e_n(hAqbar)
 =sum_{m congruent Aqbar mod n}G_{q,t}(m).                  (26)
By (25), the left side of (26) is the complete h-sum in (9) evaluated at theta=t/p, with its h=0 term included. The right side is
 sum_{m congruent Aqbar mod n}F_q(m+vt).
Delete h=0; it equals z_q because Ghat_{q,t}(0)=Fhat_q(0). This proves (10)-(11), with every Poisson hypothesis verified. A proper h-subblock cannot use (26), because its omitted Fourier siblings are part of the identity.

The support length is less than n, so fixed q,t admits at most one integer m in (11). For fixed q, as t runs modulo p, the integers m+vt lie in one residue class modulo v, and every such integer corresponds to one t modulo p after changing m by multiples of n. An interval of length at most Cvp/H contains at most 1+Cp/H integers in one residue class modulo v. Sum over q to prove (13). Since X_t<=Q,
 sum_tX_t^r<=Q^(r-1)sum_tX_t.
Divide by p and use p>2H to obtain (14).

Additive orthogonality modulo p proves the formula for cal J_t in (16). Equality of exact rational slopes is Delta=0, and grouping ordered pairs by their exact slope gives cal D_t=sum_lambda|B_{lambda,t}|^2.

Let I_t be the sum of beta_t over Delta nonzero and rho_{12}=rho_{34}, and let O_t be the sum over all Delta-nonzero quadruples. Since Gamma_1(x,y)=1_{x=y}-1/p,
 cal M_t=I_t-O_t/p.                                        (27)
Also cal J_t=cal D_t+I_t and
 |sum_qb_t(q)|^4=cal D_t+O_t.                               (28)
Equations (27)-(28) give (17).

Items (a)-(e) follow by direct comparison with the accepted statements: ace expands only M_W; 914 requires a fixed-interval injective source; 0e8 and 11ec require mean-zero W and pointwise U/Z control; 4792 acts on the post-Cauchy physical kernel; and 275 identifies but does not twist-average the slope diagonal. Finally, (7) and (10) concern different rows unless a new bridge is proved. Hence (6) is a valid sufficient finite-band supplier, while a source-preserving route needs the two additional classes of statement listed in the conclusion. No converse or minimality claim is used.

glossary.A_j: The finite-band trigonometric polynomial attached to outer index j.
glossary.C_{4/3}: The ell^{4/3} norm of the outer coefficient family.
glossary.S_pre: The normalized finite-band pre-Cauchy sum in equation (1).
glossary.X_t: The number of nonzero q-rows in the complete source-preserving twist u_t.
glossary.cal D_t: The exact rational reciprocal-slope diagonal of a twisted q-row.
glossary.cal J_t: The complete modular reciprocal-phase fourth moment of a twisted q-row.
glossary.cal M_4: The integrated outer-vector fourth moment in equation (2).
glossary.cal M_t: The Delta-nonzero centered form with constant physical kernel W=1.
glossary.finite-band/complete-row gap: The incompatibility between exact finite p-sampling for a proper h-band and exact Poisson source reassembly for the restored complete h-family.

461b4af4d8047ab5.title: BUFFERED (6/5) SLOT-SELECTION GEOMETRY
461b4af4d8047ab5.author: slava chan

glossary.L_beta: The lower correlated-window exponent 2 beta minus 2.
glossary.U_beta: The upper correlated-window exponent 3 minus 2 beta.
glossary.nu: The exponent of the small product v.
glossary.w: The grouped Type-II or semiprime exponent.
glossary.z: The rough-prime lower exponent 3/2 minus beta minus 3 sigma.

477302317fddbf3c.title: Let Lambda_P(n)=1_{n is prime}log(n) for positive integers n and Lambda_P(n)=0 otherwise. Fix real constants 0<rho<=1, C>=1 and V>=1. Let Y tend to infinity, and let D,M,U>=1 satisfy Y^rho<=D<=CY, DM<=CY and U<=CY. Let c_m be complex coefficients supported on positive integers M/2<=m<=2M and satisfying sum_m|c_m|<=CM log(2M). For every such m let u_m be a complex function of bounded variation on the positive reals, supported in [D/2,2D], with ||u_m||_infinity+Var(u_m)<=V. Let v be a complex sequence supported on positive integers n<=CY with |v(n)|<=V. For every integer N define F_N=sum_m c_m sum_{d>=1}mu(d)u_m(d)Lambda_P(N-md)v(N-md). Then, for every L>0, sum_{N in Z}|F_N|^2<<_{L,rho,C,V}Y^3(log Y)^(-L)
477302317fddbf3c.author: slava chan
477302317fddbf3c.statement:
Let Lambda_P(n)=1_{n is prime}log(n) for positive integers n and Lambda_P(n)=0 otherwise. Fix real constants 0<rho<=1, C>=1 and V>=1. Let Y tend to infinity, and let D,M,U>=1 satisfy Y^rho<=D<=CY, DM<=CY and U<=CY. Let c_m be complex coefficients supported on positive integers M/2<=m<=2M and satisfying sum_m|c_m|<=CM log(2M). For every such m let u_m be a complex function of bounded variation on the positive reals, supported in [D/2,2D], with ||u_m||_infinity+Var(u_m)<=V. Let v be a complex sequence supported on positive integers n<=CY with |v(n)|<=V. For every integer N define F_N=sum_m c_m sum_{d>=1}mu(d)u_m(d)Lambda_P(N-md)v(N-md). Then, for every L>0, sum_{N in Z}|F_N|^2<<_{L,rho,C,V}Y^3(log Y)^(-L).

Now assume the hypotheses and notation of fact f144376ade9a27f0, and additionally assume Y^rho<=D, DM<=CY and U<=CY. Thus P_N^{mov}(D,M;U), for integers Y<=N<=2Y, contains the actual moving factors W(2dm/N) and psi(d/D_*(N)). Then, for every L>0, sum_{Y<=N<=2Y}|P_N^{mov}(D,M;U)|^2<<_{L,rho,C,W,psi,Phi}Y^3(log Y)^(-L). More precisely, this follows by using K_hat=ceil((log Y)^(L+4)) center subintervals in fact f144376ade9a27f0 and a sufficiently strong frozen logarithmic exponent. Consequently, for every A>0 and B>0, all but O_{A,B,rho,C,W,psi,Phi}(Y(log Y)^(-A)) integer centers N in [Y,2Y] satisfy |P_N^{mov}(D,M;U)|<=Y(log Y)^(-B). This is only an almost-all-center result. It gives no bound at a specified bad center and no every-bad-N conclusion, because every hypothetical bad center may lie in the exceptional set. Its exceptional-set cardinality Y(log Y)^(-A) is also asymptotically larger than the known power bound E(X)<X^0.72 for Goldbach-exceptional even integers from Pintz, arXiv:1804.09084, Theorem 1; moreover the two exceptional sets are not the same.
477302317fddbf3c.proof:
We prove the general frozen estimate first. Put e(t)=exp(2 pi i t) and define
A(alpha)=sum_m c_m sum_{d>=1}mu(d)u_m(d)e(md alpha),
B(alpha)=sum_{n in Z}Lambda_P(n)v(n)e(n alpha).
The coefficient of e(N alpha) in A(alpha)B(alpha) is exactly F_N. Hence Parseval gives
sum_{N in Z}|F_N|^2=int_0^1|A(alpha)B(alpha)|^2d alpha
<=||A||_infinity^2 sum_n|Lambda_P(n)v(n)|^2.                              (1)

We state the external cancellation input. Liu and Sarnak [LS13, Lemma 2.1] prove that for a fixed residue class modulo a fixed positive integer and any real polynomial phi of positive degree,
sum_{n<=X}mu(n)e(phi(n))<<_J X(log X)^(-J)
for every J>0, with the implied constant independent of all coefficients of phi. Choose modulus one and phi(n)=beta n. For every real beta, the resulting partial sums are therefore O_J(X(log X)^(-J)) uniformly in beta.

Fix m and alpha and apply Stieltjes partial summation to u_m on [D/2,2D]. Since u_m has supremum plus total variation at most V, and the Möbius exponential partial sums are bounded uniformly for beta=m alpha, one obtains
|sum_d mu(d)u_m(d)e(md alpha)|<<_{J,rho,V}D(log D)^(-J)
<<_{J,rho,V}D(log Y)^(-J).                                                (2)
The second inequality uses D>=Y^rho. Summing (2) with the coefficients c_m gives
||A||_infinity<<D(log Y)^(-J)sum_m|c_m|
<<_{C,V}DM log(2M)(log Y)^(-J).
Because DM<=CY and M<=CY, the factor log(2M) is O_C(log Y). Thus, since J is arbitrary, for every R>0,
||A||_infinity<<_{R,rho,C,V}Y(log Y)^(-R).                                (3)

The sequence in B is supported on at most CY positive integers. On its support Lambda_P(n)<=log(CY), so
sum_n|Lambda_P(n)v(n)|^2<<_{C,V}Y(log Y)^2.                               (4)
Given L, choose R>(L+2)/2. Substitution of (3) and (4) into (1) proves
sum_N|F_N|^2<<Y^3(log Y)^(-L).

We now apply this estimate to the center hats. Let K_hat=ceil((log Y)^(L+4)) and use fact f144376ade9a27f0. It gives
P_N^{mov}=sum_{j=0}^{K_hat}h_j(N)T_{j,N}+E_N,                              (5)
where the h_j are nonnegative and sum to one, the node weights u_{j,m} are N-independent, supported in [D/2,2D], and have a uniform supremum-plus-variation bound, and
|E_N|<<DM log(2M)log(2Y)/K_hat.                                            (6)
For each fixed j, T_{j,N} has the general frozen form with
c_m=log(m)Phi(m/M),  u_m=u_{j,m},  v(n)=Phi(n/U).
The coefficient sum satisfies sum_m|c_m|<<_Phi Mlog(2M), and v is bounded and supported on n<=2U<=2CY. Hence the general theorem applies to every j, uniformly in j.

By convexity of the squared absolute value and the properties of the hats,
|sum_jh_j(N)T_{j,N}|^2<=sum_jh_j(N)|T_{j,N}|^2.
Sum this over Y<=N<=2Y and then enlarge each center sum to all integers. Apply the frozen theorem with exponent 2L+10. The result is
sum_{Y<=N<=2Y}|sum_jh_j(N)T_{j,N}|^2
<=sum_{j=0}^{K_hat}sum_{N in Z}|T_{j,N}|^2
<<K_hat Y^3(log Y)^(-2L-10)<<Y^3(log Y)^(-L-5).                           (7)
On the other hand, DM<=CY and (6) give
sum_{Y<=N<=2Y}|E_N|^2<<Y^3(log Y)^4/K_hat^2<<Y^3(log Y)^(-L).              (8)
The inequality |z+w|^2<=2|z|^2+2|w|^2, together with (5), (7) and (8), proves the moving-center L2 estimate.

For the exceptional-set assertion, apply the moving-center estimate with exponent L'=A+2B. If Q is the set of centers with |P_N^{mov}|>Y(log Y)^(-B), then
|Q|Y^2(log Y)^(-2B)<sum_{Y<=N<=2Y}|P_N^{mov}|^2<<Y^3(log Y)^(-A-2B),
so |Q|<<Y(log Y)^(-A). This argument contains no information about which centers belong to Q. In particular it cannot exclude any specified bad even N or show that a bad-center anomaly propagates.

For the final quantitative comparison, Pintz [Pin18, Theorem 1] defines E(X) as the number of even integers at most X which are not sums of two primes and proves E(X)<X^0.72 for every sufficiently large X. For each fixed A, Y(log Y)^(-A)/Y^0.72=Y^0.28(log Y)^(-A) tends to infinity. Thus the logarithmic exceptional count obtained here is numerically weaker than that known power bound. The present exceptional set also concerns a large value of one moving dyadic block, rather than failure of Goldbach representation, so no set inclusion is asserted.

glossary.E(X): the number of even integers at most X which are not sums of two primes
glossary.F_N: the general frozen m-window affine Möbius-prime convolution
glossary.K_hat: the number of center interpolation subintervals used in the application
glossary.Q: the exceptional set of centers for the moving block
glossary.Var(u_m): the total variation of u_m on the positive real axis

4792a797443e9961.title: FULL-KERNEL MEAN-ZERO REDUCTION FOR COMPLEX PMD WINDOW WEIGHTS
4792a797443e9961.author: slava chan
4792a797443e9961.statement:
FULL-KERNEL MEAN-ZERO REDUCTION FOR COMPLEX PMD WINDOW WEIGHTS.

Adopt the coefficient, prime, and (v,s)-family hypotheses of fact 3704d40c75e8269c: P>2Q, cal P is a set of primes in [P,2P), J>=1, V>=2, |xi_v|<=tau_J(v), and b_{v,s}(q) is bounded by one and independent of p. For every v,s,p let W_{v,s,p} be an arbitrary complex function on Z/pZ satisfying
  sum_{r modulo p}|W_{v,s,p}(r)|<=L,                       (1)
where 1<=L<=P. Define its exact residue mean and centered part by
  alpha_{v,s,p}=p^(-1)sum_{r modulo p}W_{v,s,p}(r),
  W^circ_{v,s,p}(r)=W_{v,s,p}(r)-alpha_{v,s,p}.             (2)
Then
  sum_r W^circ_{v,s,p}(r)=0,
  |alpha_{v,s,p}|<=L/p.                                    (3)

For fixed v,s,p, let E_p(W;b), T_neq(k), and
  What(k)=sum_rW(r)e_p(-kr)
be as in facts 3704d40c75e8269c and 27540b4094f677f4. Then exactly
 E_p(W_{v,s,p};b_{v,s})
  =alpha_{v,s,p}E_p(1;b_{v,s})
      +E_p(W^circ_{v,s,p};b_{v,s})                         (4)
  =alpha_{v,s,p}p^(-1)T_neq(0)
      +p^(-2)sum_{k modulo p; k nonzero}
         What_{v,s,p}(k)T_neq(k).                          (5)
Thus the complete complex Fourier kernel What(k), including every sign and phase, is preserved at all nonzero shifts. Its zero shift is retained exactly in the complete-density term.

The complete-density part obeys, for every epsilon>0,
 sum_{V<=v<2V}sum_{s modulo v}|xi_v/v|^2
  sum_{p in cal P}
   |alpha_{v,s,p}E_p(1;b_{v,s})|
 <<_{J,epsilon}(QV)^epsilon
   [LQ^(8/3)+(L/P)Q^4].                                   (6)
Consequently the full-kernel localized estimate
 |sum_{V<=v<2V}sum_{s modulo v}|xi_v/v|^2
   sum_{p in cal P}E_p(W_{v,s,p};b_{v,s})|
 <<_{J,epsilon}(QV)^epsilon
   [PQ^(8/3)+(L/P)Q^4]                                    (7)
would follow from
 |sum_{V<=v<2V}sum_{s modulo v}|xi_v/v|^2
   sum_{p in cal P}E_p(W^circ_{v,s,p};b_{v,s})|
 <<_{J,epsilon}(QV)^epsilon P Q^(8/3).                     (8)
This is an exact reduction for arbitrary complex kernels satisfying (1), not a proof of (8).
4792a797443e9961.proof:
The definition of Gamma_W in fact 3704d40c75e8269c is complex-linear in W, and therefore so is E_p(W;b). Equations (2) give (4), while summing W^circ over residues proves the first part of (3). The second part follows from
 |alpha|<=p^(-1)sum_r|W(r)|<=L/p.                          (9)

By fact 27540b4094f677f4,
 E_p(W;b)=p^(-2)sum_{k modulo p}What(k)T_neq(k).            (10)
The transform of W^circ equals zero at k=0 and equals What(k) at every nonzero k. The transform of the constant function alpha equals p alpha at k=0 and zero otherwise. Also E_p(1;b)=p^(-1)T_neq(0). Substitution in (4) proves (5). No absolute value has been applied to the nonzero-shift sum.

Fact 3704d40c75e8269c gives
 |E_p(1;b_{v,s})|
 <<_epsilon Q^epsilon[Q^(8/3)+Q^4/p].                     (11)
Use |alpha|<=L/p, p>=P, and at most 2P primes in cal P:
 sum_{p in cal P}|alpha E_p(1;b)|
 <<Q^epsilon[LQ^(8/3)+(L/P)Q^4].                          (12)
The squared (v,s)-mass is at most V^epsilon by fact d061fc4dc153e309. This proves (6), after adjusting epsilon.

Finally sum (4) with the squared (v,s)-weights and over p. Apply the triangle inequality only between the two complete global pieces in (4), use (6) for the first and assume (8) for the second. Since L<=P, the term LQ^(8/3) is at most PQ^(8/3), yielding (7). This proves the implication while preserving the full complex kernel in (5).

glossary.full-kernel localized estimate: Inequality (7) for arbitrary complex physical weights of controlled l1 mass.
glossary.full-kernel mean-zero discrepancy: The sufficient estimate (8) for the exactly centered complex kernel.

4832817b6b759101.title: Assume the normalized unit-state hypotheses of fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb and also K nonzero. Define U=(b r_3)^2+(d r_2)^2, V=b r_3+d r_2, L=2K r_2r_3, and g=gcd(U,|L|). Then
4832817b6b759101.author: slava chan
4832817b6b759101.statement:
Assume the normalized unit-state hypotheses of fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb and also K nonzero. Define U=(b r_3)^2+(d r_2)^2, V=b r_3+d r_2, L=2K r_2r_3, and g=gcd(U,|L|). Then
U r_4-2CV=L r_1.
For fixed integers b,d,r_2,r_3,C,K, the number of integer pairs (r_1,r_4) in I_H x I_H satisfying this equation is at most
1+H^2 g/max(U,|L|).
The same bound therefore holds after restricting r_1,r_4 to distinct primes and imposing all remaining normalized unit-state conditions. In particular, if g<=max(U,|L|)/H^2, there are at most two such pairs.
4832817b6b759101.proof:
Fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb gives
b r_3r_4-a r_1r_2=2C,  d r_2r_4-c r_1r_3=2C,
and ab+cd=2K. Rearranging the first two identities gives
a r_1r_2=b r_3r_4-2C,  c r_1r_3=d r_2r_4-2C.
Multiply ab+cd=2K by r_1r_2r_3. In the first term substitute for a r_1r_2, and in the second substitute for c r_1r_3:
2K r_1r_2r_3=b r_3(b r_3r_4-2C)+d r_2(d r_2r_4-2C).
Collecting terms yields
r_4((b r_3)^2+(d r_2)^2)-2C(b r_3+d r_2)=2K r_1r_2r_3,
which is U r_4-2CV=L r_1.

Now fix b,d,r_2,r_3,C,K. Since K,r_2,r_3 are nonzero, L is nonzero; also U is positive because fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb makes b,d nonzero. If (r_1,r_4) and (r_1',r_4') are two integer solutions, subtraction gives U(r_4-r_4')=L(r_1-r_1'). Writing g=gcd(U,|L|), the coprime integers U/g and L/g imply that for some integer t,
r_1-r_1'=(U/g)t,  r_4-r_4'=(L/g)t.
Both coordinates lie in I_H=[H^2,2H^2), an interval of length H^2. Therefore the possible t-values lie in an interval of length at most
min(H^2g/U,H^2g/|L|)=H^2g/max(U,|L|).
An interval of real length T contains at most 1+T integers. This proves the displayed bound. Restricting the solution set cannot increase it. If g<=max(U,|L|)/H^2, the bound is at most two.

glossary.g: The greatest common divisor of U and |L|.

4833384bb6a7419e.title: ALL-BLOCK, ALL-LOCAL-HEIGHT ACTUAL C1 FOUR-ROW q-PAYMENT AT A FIXED SELECTED PRIME. Adopt one actual strict-top C1 block and the row-mode expansions of facts ff228b0e569531f8 and 71f1a10b52148348. Fix a selected prime p with Q^zeta<=p<=2Q^(6/5). Let each physical height h_i be a nonzero integer in a signed dyadic block H<=|h_i|<2H, with no restriction comparing H and p. Let each natural C1 cofactor t_i=n_i/p lie in an arbitrary finite integer block contained in the exact C1 support; in particular p does not divide t_i. Give the four positions signs sigma_1=sigma_2=+1 and sigma_3=sigma_4=-1, and pair them into two disjoint TT-star pairs, each containing one positive and one negative position. Retain on each pair its exact C1 first-nonresonant determinant mask
4833384bb6a7419e.author: slava chan
4833384bb6a7419e.statement:
ALL-BLOCK, ALL-LOCAL-HEIGHT ACTUAL C1 FOUR-ROW q-PAYMENT AT A FIXED SELECTED PRIME. Adopt one actual strict-top C1 block and the row-mode expansions of facts ff228b0e569531f8 and 71f1a10b52148348. Fix a selected prime p with Q^zeta<=p<=2Q^(6/5). Let each physical height h_i be a nonzero integer in a signed dyadic block H<=|h_i|<2H, with no restriction comparing H and p. Let each natural C1 cofactor t_i=n_i/p lie in an arbitrary finite integer block contained in the exact C1 support; in particular p does not divide t_i. Give the four positions signs sigma_1=sigma_2=+1 and sigma_3=sigma_4=-1, and pair them into two disjoint TT-star pairs, each containing one positive and one negative position. Retain on each pair its exact C1 first-nonresonant determinant mask.

For a physical four-tuple let E_p^0 be the indicator that the rational function
R(X)=sum_{i=1}^4 sigma_i h_i/[t_i(X+q_i)] over F_p
is zero. Equivalently, after indices with p dividing h_i are discarded, every residue a represented by the remaining q_i satisfies
sum_{i:q_i=a} sigma_i h_i/t_i=0 mod p.
Let S_{p,H,T}^{all} be the signed sum of the actual four row-mode products, their p-local reciprocal phases, and the two exact C1 pair masks, summed over q_i in [Q,2Q), all displayed h_i and a cofactor block of cardinality at most T in each row, with the exact cross-pair nonexceptional deletion 1-E_p^0 retained. No further non-row-factorable q-dependent mask is inserted.

Let delta_0 be an exponent from fact c23ca78883ba83d9 and delta_1 an exponent from fact a8d14bd3414bf66e, and put delta_2=min(delta_0,delta_1). Then
|S_{p,H,T}^{all}| << Q^{o(1)}(1+H/H_P)^(-4A)(HT)^4
 {Q^(4-2delta_2)+Q^4p^(-1)+Q^3}.
Consequently for every omega<min(2delta_2,zeta,1),
|S_{p,H,T}^{all}| << Q^(4-omega+o(1))(1+H/H_P)^(-4A)(HT)^4.
This fixed-p theorem includes every short cofactor block and every physical height, including p-divisible local heights. It therefore supersedes the long/zero exclusions of fact 77987a35ae17ca77 at the scalar q-profile level. It does not sum varying selected primes, treat four-row terms whose two TT-star pairs select different primes, or compare the scalar block envelope with the complete upstream Hilbert norm.
4833384bb6a7419e.proof:
Consider first one of the two TT-star pairs and fix its two physical heights, cofactors and row modes. Its exact C1 mask is inequality of the two local slopes h_i t_i^{-1}q_i^{-1} modulo p. There are three cases. If p divides both heights, both slopes are zero and the mask vanishes identically. If p divides exactly one height, the mask is identically one because the other slope is nonzero. The pair q-sum then factorizes into one unphased Mobius row, bounded trivially by V_Q(A)Q, and one row with a nonzero reciprocal numerator, bounded by fact c23ca78883ba83d9 by V_Q(A)Q^(1-delta_0). If neither height is divisible by p, fact a8d14bd3414bf66e applies and bounds the masked pair by Q^(2-delta_1) times the two variation norms. Thus every fixed pair is bounded by Q^(2-delta_2) times its profile norms. Applying this independently to the two disjoint pairs, then using fact 71f1a10b52148348 to sum the actual mode masses and summing the at most O((HT)^4) height-cofactor choices, bounds the four-row expression before the factor 1-E_p^0 by
Q^(4-2delta_2+o(1))(1+H/H_P)^(-4A)(HT)^4.                    (1)

It remains to add back the E_p^0 restriction. On the support of the two pair masks, no pair can have both heights divisible by p. Hence the number z of indices with p dividing h_i is 0, 1, or 2. Discarding those zero-coefficient indices, the displayed partial-fraction identity shows that R=0 exactly when every residue block among the remaining 4-z indices has coefficient sum zero. In particular no such block is a singleton.

Put R_{p,Q} for the number of nonzero residues modulo p represented in [Q,2Q) and L_q=1+Q/p. If z=0, there are at most two residue blocks, so the number of exceptional physical q-tuples is O(R_{p,Q}^2 L_q^4). If z=1, the remaining three indices must form one block, while the zero-height row is arbitrary, giving O(Q R_{p,Q}L_q^3). If z=2, the two remaining indices form one block and the two zero-height rows are arbitrary, giving O(Q^2R_{p,Q}L_q^2). These counts ignore the coefficient-balance equations and therefore are valid upper bounds.

When p<=Q, use R_{p,Q}<=p and L_q<=2Q/p. The three bounds are respectively O(Q^4/p^2), O(Q^4/p^2), and O(Q^4/p). When p>Q, use R_{p,Q}<=Q+1 and L_q<2; all three are O(Q^3). Thus in every case the exceptional q-tuples number O(Q^4p^(-1)+Q^3). Bound every row mode by its variation norm, sum actual mode mass using fact 71f1a10b52148348, and sum the h_i,t_i choices. This gives
|S^{exc}|<<Q^{o(1)}(1+H/H_P)^(-4A)(HT)^4(Q^4p^(-1)+Q^3).     (2)
The exact identity S^{all}=S^{full}-S^{exc}, together with (1)-(2), proves the first estimate. Since p>=Q^zeta, both exceptional terms save Q^{-min(zeta,1)}, proving the final exponent statement. No long-block, height-unit, or cofactor-length hypothesis was used.

glossary.E_p^0: The exact zero rational-phase locus after local p-zero height coefficients are allowed and discarded from the pole list.
glossary.L_q: The elementary upper bound 1+Q/p for physical lifts of one residue modulo p in [Q,2Q).
glossary.S_{p,H,T}^{all}: The actual fixed-p C1 four-row q-profile sum over an arbitrary cofactor block and all physical heights, with two pair masks and the exact nonexceptional deletion.
glossary.delta_2: The minimum of the verified one-row and two-row C1 Mobius reciprocal-trace saving exponents.

483cc60c2483957e.title: FULL-RESONANCE PAYMENT IN SIGNED-QPAIR-DISP. Retain the exact signed off-diagonal \({\cal O}_h\) of fact 0895975a7f3918e9, with
483cc60c2483957e.author: slava chan
483cc60c2483957e.statement:
FULL-RESONANCE PAYMENT IN SIGNED-QPAIR-DISP. Retain the exact signed off-diagonal \({\cal O}_h\) of fact 0895975a7f3918e9, with
\[
 q_1,q_2\asymp Q,\quad q_1\ne q_2,\quad B=Q^\beta,\quad \beta<6/5,
 \quad a_h=\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\ne0,
\]
all exact outer and n-coprimality gates, the literal coefficients \({\cal C}^{\flat}_{g,q_i,n}(h)\), and the weights \(\alpha_J(q_1)\overline{\alpha_J(q_2)}\).  For one ordered pair put
\[
 c=(q_1,q_2),\qquad q_i=c r_i,
\]
so \((r_1,r_2)=1\).  Define the fully resonant restriction \({\cal O}_h^{\rm FR}\) by
\[
 c r_1r_2\mid a_h(r_2-r_1).                                      \tag{1}
\]
This is precisely the condition that the reduced reciprocal phase in equation (8) of fact de324f84f27469cf is identically one.

For every fixed \(A>0\),
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 |{\cal O}_h^{\rm FR}|
 \ll_A (\log x)^{2C_0}(1+F/H_P)^{-2A} BQ^{o(1)}.
 \quad}                                                          \tag{2}
\]
Here \(C_0\) is the fixed source-smoothness exponent.  Consequently, for every fixed
\[
 0<\delta<1/4,
\]
the fully resonant stratum satisfies the SIGNED-QPAIR-DISP target
\[
 |{\cal O}_h^{\rm FR}|
 \ll_A (\log x)^{2C_0}(1+F/H_P)^{-2A}
 Q^{4-\beta-2\delta-1},                                        \tag{3}
\]
after increasing \(Q\); in particular it is paid absolutely through fact 0895975a7f3918e9.  Thus the unresolved low-common-gcd residual from fact de324f84f27469cf may additionally be restricted to the nonresonant condition
\[
 c r_1r_2\nmid a_h(r_2-r_1).                                   \tag{4}
\]
No estimate for (4), no complete SIGNED-QPAIR-DISP theorem, and no post-A or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
483cc60c2483957e.proof:
Because \((r_1,r_2)=1\),
\[
 (r_2-r_1,r_1r_2)=1.                                           \tag{5}
\]
It follows that (1) is equivalent to the two simultaneous divisibility conditions
\[
 r_1r_2\mid a_h,\qquad
 c\mid {a_h(r_2-r_1)\over r_1r_2}.                           \tag{6}
\]
Indeed, (1) first implies \(r_1r_2\mid a_h(r_2-r_1)\), and (5) gives the first condition in (6); division by \(r_1r_2\) then gives the second.  The converse follows by multiplication.

The first condition in (6) gives at most \(\tau(|a_h|)^2\) ordered choices for \((r_1,r_2)\), even before imposing their coprimality and the dyadic restrictions \(cr_i\asymp Q\).  For each such ordered pair, the integer
\[
 K={a_h(r_2-r_1)\over r_1r_2}
\]
is nonzero because \(a_h\ne0\) and \(r_1\ne r_2\), the latter following from \(q_1\ne q_2\).  The second condition in (6) therefore gives at most \(\tau(|K|)\) choices for \(c\).

Facts 15425579cb248eff and 3f2f255ea6845a50 give fixed polynomial bounds in \(Q\) for the strict-top physical parameters, hence for \(|a_h|\) on a fixed dyadic frequency block after its arbitrary-order decay is retained.  Also \(r_i\le 2Q\), so \(|K|\) has fixed polynomial size in \(Q\) and in the dyadic frequency parameter.  The elementary fixed-polynomial divisor bound used in fact de324f84f27469cf therefore gives
\[
 \tau(|a_h|)^2\tau(|K|)=Q^{o(1)},                            \tag{7}
\]
with the harmless frequency power absorbed by decreasing the arbitrary decay order.  Thus only \(Q^{o(1)}\) ordered fully resonant q-pairs occur.

For each retained pair, drop the exact gcd gates only to obtain an upper bound.  Fact 0895975a7f3918e9 gives
\[
 |\alpha_J(q_i)|\le2\tau_3(q_i)=Q^{o(1)},                 \tag{8}
\]
and its literal coefficient audit gives
\[
 |{\cal C}^{\flat}_{g,q_1,n}(h)
   \overline{{\cal C}^{\flat}_{g,q_2,n}(h)}|
 \ll_A(\log x)^{2C_0}(1+F/H_P)^{-2A}.                     \tag{9}
\]
There are \(O(B)\) integers in the n-window.  On (1) the reduced additive character is one, but taking absolute values already suffices.  Combining (7)-(9) proves (2).

Finally,
\[
 (4-\beta-2\delta-1)-\beta
 =3-2\beta-2\delta>3-\frac{12}{5}-\frac12=\frac1{10}. \tag{10}
\]
Hence the \(Q^{o(1)}\) factor in (2) is absorbed into the fixed margin in (10), proving (3).  Fact 0895975a7f3918e9 converts this regional off-diagonal estimate into the stated regional \(J_qJ_n\) payment.  Removing (1) from the low-common-gcd residual leaves exactly (4).

glossary.mathcal O_h^{FR}: The fully resonant restriction of the exact signed off-diagonal O_h, on which the reduced reciprocal conductor divides the reduced numerator.

487a65cdbb7ab2fc.title: LITERAL GIANT1 PROJECTIVE FOLDING AND MAYNARD NEAR-SQUARE-ROOT PAYMENT ON ONE ZHANG-ELIGIBLE HC-MED CELL. Fix A>0 and epsilon>0. Adopt one literal h-row, X,Q_c,delta_h,eta,c_*=c rad(kappa), P_-,H, and the GIANT1 branch of facts edabb9a0d2959b41 and 52e1736c39e88aee. Thus
487a65cdbb7ab2fc.author: slava chan
487a65cdbb7ab2fc.statement: LITERAL GIANT1 PROJECTIVE FOLDING AND MAYNARD NEAR-SQUARE-ROOT PAYMENT ON ONE ZHANG-ELIGIBLE HC-MED CELL. Fix A>0 and epsilon>0. Adopt one literal h-row, X,Q_c,delta_h,eta,c_*=c rad(kappa), P_-,H, and the GIANT1 branch of facts edabb9a0d2959b41 and 52e1736c39e88aee. Thus Q_c=X^(1/2+delta_h),quad delta_h>=0, 0=H, (3) where P^+(1)=1. Fix powers of two D_0,M_m,P,M_v with P>=H. Restrict to P=0 and Q_{1,alpha}^7Q_{2,alpha}^12
487a65cdbb7ab2fc.proof:
The nonempty compatible window in fact 52e1736c39e88aee gives
X^(2/5+6delta_h)(log X)^(2C)
 <=X^(1/2-3delta_h)(log X)^(-C)                                 (18)
for the same sufficiently large fixed C used there. From (1),
d<=X^(1/4+eta)<=X^(2/5+6delta_h).                               (19)
The definition of H in fact 52e1736c39e88aee gives
H>X^(1/2-3delta_h)(log X)^(-C).                                 (20)
Equations (18)-(20) imply H/d>=(log X)^(2C)>1. Thus p>=H>d. Since m=ap>=p, one has d<m, so the fundamental-domain multiplicity in fact edabb9a0d2959b41 is exactly 2. Fact 5999a1878276ac78 gives rho_{1/2}(p)=-1/2. Hence
2rho_{1/2}(d)rho_{1/2}(a)rho_{1/2}(p)
 =-rho_{1/2}(d)rho_{1/2}(a),                                    (21)
which proves the sign and coefficient in (10) after folding v=da. The centered bracket of fact edabb9a0d2959b41 becomes exactly the bracket in (11) because pv=dm.

On (2)-(4), X/(2P)<v<2X/P. This proves M_v<=2X/P and PM_v comparable to X for every nonempty dyadic v-cell, giving (5).

Fact 97cfedc76bcae0ad gives the exact logarithmic Fourier expansion
A_lit(s,kappa,hpv;(ell-kappa hpv)/s)
 =sum_j lambda_{j,s,kappa,h}p^(i tau_j)v^(i tau_j),
with weighted l1 frequency norm bounded by a fixed power of log x. Apply the same compact logarithmic Fourier construction to the fixed smooth profile Psi_{M_m}(ap):
Psi_{M_m}(ap)=sum_k a_k p^(i sigma_k)a^(i sigma_k),
with
sum_k|a_k|(1+|sigma_k|)<<1.                                     (22)
Substituting a=v/d in (10) gives cofactor modes proportional to
1_{M_v<v<=2M_v}v^(i tau_j)1_{(v,c_*)=1}
 sum_{d|v, X^eta<=d<=X^(1/4+eta), P^+(v/d)<P_-}
 rho_{1/2}(d)rho_{1/2}(v/d)
 (v/d)^(i sigma_k)Psi_{D_0}(d).                                 (23)
Fact 5999a1878276ac78 gives |rho_{1/2}|<=1. Thus (23), after division by max(1,C_{D_0}), is bounded by tau(v). Normalize the prime mode by 1+|tau_j+sigma_k| and multiply the outer coefficient by the same factor. The weighted Fourier estimates used in fact 2ccb8f56e6084b34 then prove (12). Direct divisor summation in (10), using the supremum bounds L_lit,C_{D_0},C_{M_m}, proves (14). Fact 0025283165f465c4 gives the uniform Siegel-Walfisz condition for (13), with exactly the interval P<p<=2P.

Facts cbbc7f1404df765c and 8d9feea8c44da2c8 prove that every nonzero literal modulus is squarefree and coprime to c rad(kappa), while ell and kappa h are units modulo s. This proves (15). Since q_1 divides s, reducing (15) modulo q_1 gives (16), independently of q_2. The canonical first-factorization rule makes the product map injective, exactly as in fact cbbc7f1404df765c.

Fix alpha. Equations (5)-(16) verify every hypothesis of fact 868d2c2698f73b86 with its cofactor scale M=M_v and c=c_*. It gives a main contribution
O_{A,epsilon}(L_proj,G1 X(log X)^(-A))
and a prime-unit deletion
O(L_W,G1 omega_P(c_*)[
 M_v(1+log(2M_v Q_{1,alpha}Q_{2,alpha}))^3
 +Q_{1,alpha}Q_{2,alpha}sqrt(M_v)
  (1+log(2M_v Q_{1,alpha}Q_{2,alpha}))^2]).                     (24)
For a nonempty box, a selected product lies in both [Q_c,2Q_c) and
(Q_{1,alpha}Q_{2,alpha},4Q_{1,alpha}Q_{2,alpha}], so
Q_{1,alpha}Q_{2,alpha}<2Q_c.                                   (25)
Use M_v<=2X/P and (25) in (24), then sum N_Z(P) boxes. This proves (17). Equation (21) shows that (11) is the actual literal GIANT1 cell, not an auxiliary marked sector, and therefore there is no Ramaré correction.

Finally, the P-ranges and the cell labels in cal C are disjoint by hypothesis. Hence every original tuple (p,d,a) belongs to at most one member of cal C. The triangle inequality sums the already proved bound (17) without duplication. No estimate for a cell outside cal C or a different structural branch was used.

glossary.C_G1: A fixed exponent controlling the GIANT1 projective norm.
glossary.D_0: The fixed inherited smooth dyadic scale of the smaller HC factor d.
glossary.Gtilde_s(p,v): The auxiliary all-selected-primes folded GIANT1 coefficient on one fixed cell.
glossary.L_W,G1: The reconstructed pointwise divisor-bound constant for the fixed-cell GIANT1 row.
glossary.L_proj,G1: The l1 projective norm of the fixed-cell GIANT1 prime/cofactor expansion.
glossary.M_m: The fixed inherited smooth dyadic scale of the original large HC factor m=ap.
glossary.M_v: The fixed dyadic scale of the folded cofactor v=da.
glossary.N_Z(P): The number of nonempty canonical Zhang factor boxes at P.
glossary.U_s^{G1}(P;D_0,M_m,M_v): The actual prime-unit folded GIANT1 centered row on one fixed cell.
glossary.Zhang factor box: A two-factor literal modulus box satisfying the scale inequalities of Maynard's near-square-root Type-II theorem.
glossary.cal C: A finite disjoint collection of fixed literal GIANT1 cells.
glossary.cal S_Z(P): The canonically selected Zhang-eligible literal modulus set at giant-prime scale P.

49b7d26830c92063.title: Fix real numbers \(1/2<\alpha<\beta<1\), \(\eta>0\), and \(\rho\ge0\). Let \(W\) be a bounded function supported in \([\alpha,\beta]\), and let \(\Phi\) be a bounded function supported in \([1/2,2]\). Let \(x\ge3\), let \(N=2x\) be an integer, let \(D,U>0\), and let
49b7d26830c92063.author: slava chan
49b7d26830c92063.statement:
Fix real numbers \(1/2<\alpha<\beta<1\), \(\eta>0\), and \(\rho\ge0\). Let \(W\) be a bounded function supported in \([\alpha,\beta]\), and let \(\Phi\) be a bounded function supported in \([1/2,2]\). Let \(x\ge3\), let \(N=2x\) be an integer, let \(D,U>0\), and let
\[
 T_x=(\log x)^{6+\eta+\rho}.
\]
Define
\[
 {\cal I}_D=\{d\ge2:(d,N)=1,\ \mu(d)\ne0,\ d\le x^{1/2},\
                    \Phi(d/D)\ne0\}.
\]
For nonzero integers \(H\) and integers \(p\), define
\[
\begin{split}
 {\cal A}_N(H,p)=\sum_{\substack{m\ge1\\m\mid H\\m\mid N-p}}
 &{\bf1}_{\substack{d=(N-p)/m\in{\cal I}_D,\ d+H/m\in{\cal I}_D\\
                    |H|/m>D/T_x,\ (d,H/m)<T_x}}
 \mu(d)\mu(d+H/m)\Phi(d/D)\Phi((d+H/m)/D)\\
 &\times W((N-p)/x)W((N-p+H)/x)
 \Phi(p/U)\Phi((p-H)/U).                                \tag{1}
\end{split}
\]
Assume additionally the literal \(\ell^1\) ledger
\[
 \sum_{H,p}|{\cal A}_N(H,p)|
 \ll_{W,\Phi,\alpha,\beta}xD,                            \tag{2}
\]
which is verified under the source-admissible top-band hypotheses in fact
308c7c0d43bda909.

For a nonzero term of \({\cal A}_N(H,p)\), put
\[
 n=N-p,\qquad G=\gcd(n,|H|),\qquad
 u={n\over G},\qquad v={H\over G}.                       \tag{3}
\]
Then \(n>0\), \(G\ge1\), \(u\ge1\), \(v\ne0\),
\[
 \gcd(u,v)=1,\qquad u+v>0.                               \tag{4}
\]
Define
\[
 {\cal K}_D(u,v;G)=
 \sum_{\substack{g\mid G\\1\le g<T_x}}
 {\bf1}_{\substack{ug\in{\cal I}_D,\ (u+v)g\in{\cal I}_D\\
                    |v|g>D/T_x}}
 \Phi(ug/D)\Phi((u+v)g/D).                               \tag{5}
\]
Then the physical coefficient has the exact compressed form
\[
\boxed{
\begin{split}
 {\cal A}_N(H,p)={}&
 W((N-p)/x)W((N-p+H)/x)
 \Phi(p/U)\Phi((p-H)/U)\\
 &\times\mu(u)\mu(u+v)\,{\cal K}_D(u,v;G).
\end{split}}                                             \tag{6}
\]
In every nonzero summand of (5), the original common-divisor variable and the two moduli are recovered uniquely by
\[
 m={G\over g},\qquad d_1=ug,\qquad d_2=(u+v)g,            \tag{7}
\]
and
\[
 \gcd(d_1,d_2)=g.                                        \tag{8}
\]
Squarefreeness forces
\[
 \mu(d_1)\mu(d_2)=\mu(u)\mu(u+v),                         \tag{9}
\]
so no Möbius sign is discarded in (6). The reduced variables obey
\[
 u>{D\over2T_x},\qquad u+v>{D\over2T_x},\qquad
 |v|>{D\over T_x^2}.                                     \tag{10}
\]
Furthermore
\[
 |{\cal A}_N(H,p)|\ll_{W,\Phi}T_x,                        \tag{11}
\]
and
\[
 \sum_{H,p}|{\cal A}_N(H,p)|^2
 \ll_{W,\Phi,\alpha,\beta}T_x\,xD.                       \tag{12}
\]

Under the full source-admissible hypotheses of fact 308c7c0d43bda909, its identity
\[
 {\mathfrak C}_\star^\Lambda
 =\sum_{H\ne0}\sum_p{\cal A}_N(H,p)\Lambda(p)\Lambda(p-H)
\]
therefore becomes exactly a fixed-\(N\), macroscopic shifted-prime correlation weighted by the shifted reduced Möbius pair
\(\mu(u)\mu(u+v)\) and only a polylogarithmic residual \(g<T_x\) sum. Equations (6)--(12) are an exact compression and coefficient ledger; they do not estimate the shifted-prime correlation and do not prove (TB-PHYS).
49b7d26830c92063.proof:
Take one summand indexed by \(m\) in (1). It satisfies
\(m\mid H\) and \(m\mid n=N-p\), hence \(m\mid G\). Put
\[
 g={G\over m}.
\]
Using (3),
\[
 d_1={n\over m}={n\over G}g=ug,\qquad
 {H\over m}={H\over G}g=vg,
\]
and therefore
\[
 d_2=d_1+{H\over m}=(u+v)g.                             \tag{13}
\]
Because \(G=\gcd(n,|H|)\), division by \(G\) gives
\(\gcd(u,v)=1\). Since \(d_2>0\), (13) gives \(u+v>0\). This proves (4) and (7).

Conversely, if \(g\mid G\), set \(m=G/g\). Then \(m\mid n,H\), and (13) reverses. Thus the change of variables \(m\leftrightarrow g=G/m\) is a bijection between the summands in (1) and those in (5), once their displayed selectors are imposed.

Since \(\gcd(u,v)=1\),
\[
 \gcd(u,u+v)=\gcd(u,v)=1.
\]
Equation (13) therefore gives
\[
 \gcd(d_1,d_2)=g\gcd(u,u+v)=g,
\]
which proves (8). Hence the hard-core gcd condition is exactly \(g<T_x\), while the hard difference condition is exactly
\[
 |d_2-d_1|=|v|g>D/T_x.
\]
This gives all selectors in (5).

Both \(d_1\) and \(d_2\) belong to \({\cal I}_D\), so they are squarefree. Since their greatest common divisor is \(g\), this implies that \(g,u,u+v\) are squarefree,
\[
 \gcd(g,u)=\gcd(g,u+v)=1,
\]
and \(\gcd(u,u+v)=1\). Multiplicativity of the Möbius function gives
\[
 \mu(ug)\mu((u+v)g)
 =\mu(u)\mu(g)\mu(u+v)\mu(g)
 =\mu(u)\mu(u+v),
\]
because \(\mu(g)^2=1\). This proves (9). All remaining factors in (1) are independent of \(m\), except for the two displayed dyadic modulus selectors, and substitution of (13) gives (5)--(6).

The support of \(\Phi\) gives
\[
 ug\ge D/2,\qquad (u+v)g\ge D/2.
\]
Since \(g<T_x\), the first two bounds in (10) follow. The hard difference inequality
\(|v|g>D/T_x\), again with \(g<T_x\), gives the third.

The sum (5) has fewer than \(T_x\) possible positive integers \(g\), and all smooth factors are uniformly bounded. This proves (11). Finally,
\[
 \sum_{H,p}|{\cal A}_N(H,p)|^2
 \le\left(\sup_{H,p}|{\cal A}_N(H,p)|\right)
      \sum_{H,p}|{\cal A}_N(H,p)|.
\]
Use (11) and the assumed ledger (2) to obtain (12).

glossary.cal K_D(u,v;G): the residual small-g selector sum after physical gcd compression
glossary.g: the residual common gcd of the two squarefree moduli, equal to G/m

4a101b703d4499f6.title: Fix an integer J≥1. Let q>1 be squarefree, let A be an integer with gcd(A,q)=1, and let U,Y,H≥1 satisfy
4a101b703d4499f6.author: slava chan
4a101b703d4499f6.statement:
Fix an integer J≥1. Let q>1 be squarefree, let A be an integer with gcd(A,q)=1, and let U,Y,H≥1 satisfy
U≤q,   H≤Y,   4HY<q.                                           (1)
Let α_u, γ_y, and ν_h be complex coefficients supported respectively on
U≤u<2U,   Y≤y<2Y,   0<|h|≤H,
and bounded in absolute value by τ_J(|u|), τ_J(|y|), and τ_J(|h|). In every summand below require gcd(uy,q)=1, and put R=UY. Then for every ε>0,
|Σ_u α_u Σ_y γ_y Σ_{0<|h|≤H}ν_h e_q(Ah(uy)^(-1))|
≪_{J,ε}(qUYH)^ε
 [R(H/Y)^(1/2)+H(RY)^(1/2)q^(1/4)].                         (2)
4a101b703d4499f6.proof:
Denote the sum in (2) by T. Cauchy's inequality in u, together with the fixed divisor-function bounds, gives
|T|²≪(qUYH)^ε U
 Σ_{U≤u<2U,gcd(u,q)=1}
 |Σ_{y,h,gcd(y,q)=1}γ_yν_h e_q(Ah y^(-1)u^(-1))|².            (3)
Expand the square. The inner u-sum attached to (h_1,y_1,h_2,y_2) is
Σ_{u∼U,gcd(u,q)=1}
 e_q(A(h_1y_1^(-1)-h_2y_2^(-1))u^(-1)).                      (4)
Because y_1y_2 is a unit modulo q, its phase numerator vanishes modulo q exactly when
Δ=h_1y_2-h_2y_1
is divisible by q. The support gives |Δ|<4HY<q, so q|Δ is equivalent to Δ=0.

We first bound the Δ=0 contribution. The equation h_1y_2=h_2y_1 can be parameterized by
h_1=va, h_2=vb, gcd(a,b)=1, y_1=bc, y_2=ac,
with signs incorporated into v,a,b. Summing the fixed divisor-function weights over this parameterization gives
Σ_{h_1y_2=h_2y_1}|ν_{h_1}ν_{h_2}γ_{y_1}γ_{y_2}|
≪(qUYH)^ε HY.                                                (5)
For these tuples, (4) has absolute value at most U. Hence their contribution to the last sum in (3) is
≪(qUYH)^ε UHY.                                               (6)

For Δ≠0 we use Irving, arXiv:1301.6372, Lemma 2.1. In the present notation it states that for real C<D,
Σ_{C<n≤D,gcd(n,q)=1}e_q(cn^(-1))
≪_ε[(c,q)((D-C)/q+1)+q^(1/2)]q^ε.                           (7)
Since U≤q and 1≤(c,q)≤q, the bracket in (7) is
≪q^(1/2)(c,q)^(1/2).
Applying (7) to (4), and using gcd(Ay_1y_2,q)=1, bounds (4) by
≪(qUYH)^ε q^(1/2)(Δ,q)^(1/2).                               (8)

It remains to sum the gcd factor. The elementary inequality
(Δ,q)^(1/2)≤Σ_{v|q, v|Δ}v^(1/2)                              (9)
reduces the problem to counting the congruence
h_1y_2≡h_2y_1 (mod v).                                      (10)
Because q is squarefree and y_1y_2 is coprime to q, for each divisor v|q the common value c=gcd(h_1,v)=gcd(h_2,v) may be extracted; after division by c, one h-variable is invertible modulo v/c and (10) places one y-variable in one residue class modulo v/c. Summing over c|v and over the remaining three variables gives
#{(h_1,h_2,y_1,y_2):(10)}
≪(qUYH)^ε[H²Y²/v+H²Y].                                     (11)
For Δ≠0, any divisor v in (9) is at most |Δ|<4HY. Equations (9)-(11), the divisor bound, and H≤Y therefore give
Σ_{Δ≠0}(Δ,q)^(1/2)
≪(qUYH)^ε[
 H²Y² Σ_{v|q}v^(-1/2)
 +H²Y Σ_{v|q,v<4HY}v^(1/2)]
≪(qUYH)^ε[(HY)²+H²Y(HY)^(1/2)]
≪(qUYH)^ε(HY)².                                             (12)
Thus (8) shows that the off-diagonal contribution to the last sum in (3) is
≪(qUYH)^ε q^(1/2)(HY)².                                    (13)

Combining (3), (6), and (13),
|T|²≪(qUYH)^ε U[UHY+q^(1/2)(HY)²].
Taking square roots and using R=UY gives
U(HY)^(1/2)=R(H/Y)^(1/2),
U^(1/2)HY=H(RY)^(1/2),
which proves (2).

glossary.A: The numerator of the reciprocal phase, coprime to q.
glossary.J: The fixed order of the divisor-function bounds.
glossary.T: The trilinear reciprocal sum in the statement.
glossary.Y: The dyadic marker scale of y.
glossary.ν_h: The coefficient on the frequency h.

4a18a6fc30232be9.title: NUMERICAL SCALE OF THE C4 ELEVEN-MODE LARGE-SIEVE SUPPLIER FOR THE CANONICAL MARKED-DILATOR TARGET. Adopt the literal pre-6/5 C4 setting of facts 01ecc6fab24e57c6 and a3132ecd1bd44382. Fix one canonical-dilator block
4a18a6fc30232be9.author: slava chan
4a18a6fc30232be9.statement:
NUMERICAL SCALE OF THE C4 ELEVEN-MODE LARGE-SIEVE SUPPLIER FOR THE CANONICAL MARKED-DILATOR TARGET. Adopt the literal pre-6/5 C4 setting of facts 01ecc6fab24e57c6 and a3132ecd1bd44382. Fix one canonical-dilator block
Dcal<=D_lambda<2Dcal
with normalized scales B,Q,F and rough cutoff Z. For the common-row formulation define
E_11(z)=sum_lambda sum_{r|D_lambda, omega(r)<=2}
 c_lambda(r)|S_lambda,r(z)|^2,                                   (1)
where the sum is over the exact literal C4 copies in the block and c_lambda(r), S_lambda,r are those of fact a3132ecd1bd44382. The explicit sufficient numerical supplier is
E_11(z)
<<_epsilon Q^epsilon Z^2
 [BQF+BQ^2F^2/Dcal] ||z||_2^2.                                  (C4-11-LS)
Indeed, C4-11-LS implies
sum_lambda|T_lambda(z)|^2
<<_epsilon Q^epsilon
 [BQF+BQ^2F^2/Dcal]||z||_2^2.                                   (2)
For a scalar literal specialization to which the already verified sector bounds of fact 54029717e980dcb7 apply, the exact trichotomy then gives the same canonical scale for the scoped signed off-ray remainder after adding back the absolutely paid same-ray and fully resonant terms.

Since B=Q^beta and Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma), the right side of C4-11-LS before ||z||_2^2 is exactly
Q^epsilon [Q^(4-beta-6sigma)F
 +Q^(5-beta-6sigma)F^2/Dcal].                                    (3)
Thus the previously symbolic constant Lcal in fact a3132ecd1bd44382 must be proved at the scale in C4-11-LS. If instead the right side of C4-11-LS carries an additional unbounded multiplicative loss R>=1, that same loss R survives the weighted-Cauchy conversion; in particular generic losses such as the number of primitive rays, D_lambda, or an extra factor Z^2 are not absorbed by this reduction. No C4-11-LS estimate, vector transfer of the scalar paid-sector bounds, C4 closure, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
4a18a6fc30232be9.proof:
Fact a3132ecd1bd44382 proves, with all literal coefficients retained,
sum_lambda |T_lambda(z)|^2
<=C_* E_11(z),                                                    (4)
where
C_*=max_lambda sum_{r|D_lambda, omega(r)<=2}c_lambda(r).
Every rough prime in a literal C4 row is at least Z. Equation (5) of the same fact therefore gives
C_*<=27/(2Z^2).                                                    (5)
Insert C4-11-LS into (4), then use (5). The factor Z^2 cancels Z^(-2), and the fixed factor 27/2 is absorbed in the implied constant. This proves (2).

Fact 134b03fc362a7cf1 gives the exact identity
R_lambda^{off}=|T_lambda|^2-D_lambda^{ray}-R_lambda^{FR}.
For a scalar literal coefficient family, fact 54029717e980dcb7 bounds the sum of the same-ray terms by Q^epsilon BQF and the fully resonant terms by Q^epsilon BQ^2F^2/Dcal. Hence the triangle inequality combines (2) with those two already paid terms at the same displayed canonical scale. This invocation is restricted to the scalar literal specialization and does not claim a new vector-valued transfer of fact 540.

Finally,
Z^2=Q^(3-2beta-6sigma).
Multiplying first by BQF=Q^(beta+1)F gives Q^(4-beta-6sigma)F. Multiplying instead by BQ^2F^2/Dcal=Q^(beta+2)F^2/Dcal gives Q^(5-beta-6sigma)F^2/Dcal. This proves (3).
