If an attempted estimate for E_11 has the right side in C4-11-LS multiplied by R>=1, equations (4)-(5) cancel only Z^2 against Z^(-2), leaving R in the final full-moment estimate. Therefore an unbounded ray-count, D_lambda, or extra Z^2 loss is not removed by this weighted-Cauchy step. This proves the corrected warning.

glossary.C4-11-LS: The explicit numerical source-specific eleven-mode large-sieve supplier.
glossary.Dcal: The dyadic scale of the canonical marked dilator D_lambda.
glossary.E_11: The coefficient-weighted energy of the eleven reciprocal-slope transforms.
glossary.R: An arbitrary multiplicative loss factor at least one in an attempted supplier estimate.

4a1d6a8cfcc6d864.title: Fix
4a1d6a8cfcc6d864.author: slava chan
4a1d6a8cfcc6d864.statement:
Fix
\[
 \frac12<\alpha<\beta<1,\qquad \eta>0,\qquad\rho>0,\qquad
 B_{\rm src}>0.
\]
Let \(W,\Phi\) be continuously differentiable real functions of bounded
supremum and total variation, supported respectively in
\([\alpha,\beta]\) and \([1/2,2]\). Let \(N=2x\) be an integer with
\(x\ge3\), put
\[
 T_x=(\log x)^{6+\eta+\rho},
\]
and assume
\[
 \frac12x^{1/2}(\log x)^{-B_{\rm src}}\le D\le2x^{1/2},
 \qquad D>2T_x,\qquad U>0.
\]
Define
\[
 {\cal I}_D=\{w\ge2:(w,N)=1,\ \mu(w)\ne0,\ w\le x^{1/2},\
                         \Phi(w/D)\ne0\},
\]
\[
 H_0=D(\log x)^{-6-\eta-\rho/2},
 \qquad
 {\cal H}_{\rm mid}=\{h\in\mathbb Z:
 H_0<|h|\le3D/2-H_0\}.                                  \tag{1}
\]
For \(h\in{\cal H}_{\rm mid}\), positive \(m,w,w-h,q_1,q_2\), put
\[
 P_1=N-mw,\qquad P_2=N-m(w-h),
\]
and define the full-shell moving-log coefficient
\[
\begin{split}
 A^+_{h,q_1,q_2}(m,w)=&
 {\bf1}_{w,w-h\in{\cal I}_D}\mu(w)\mu(w-h)\mu(q_1)\mu(q_2)\\
 &\times\Phi(w/D)\Phi((w-h)/D)
 W(mw/x)W(m(w-h)/x)\Phi(P_1/U)\Phi(P_2/U)\\
 &\times\log(P_1/q_1)_+\log(P_2/q_2)_+ .                \tag{2}
\end{split}
\]
The value is zero unless \(P_1,P_2>0\). For an active pair put
\[
 d=(q_1,q_2),\qquad c=[q_1,q_2],\qquad b=q_2/d.
\]
Periodize (2) modulo \(c\) and take the positive finite transform
\[
 \widehat A^+(k,r)=
 \sum_{a_1,a_2\ ({\rm mod}\ c)}
 \sum_{\substack{m\equiv a_1\ ({\rm mod}\ c)\\
                 w\equiv a_2\ ({\rm mod}\ c)}}
 A^+_{h,q_1,q_2}(m,w)e_c(ka_1+ra_2).                   \tag{3}
\]
Define the complete-shell middle zero union
\[
\begin{split}
 {\cal Z}_{\rm mid}^+=
 \sum_{\substack{h\in{\cal H}_{\rm mid}\\q_1,q_2\ge1\\
                 (N,c)=1,\ d\mid h}}
 \frac1{c^2}\Bigg\{&
 \sum_{r\ ({\rm mod}\ c)}
 \widehat A^+(0,r)e_b(-rhq_1^{-1})c_c(r)\\
 &+\sum_{k\ ({\rm mod}\ c)}\widehat A^+(k,0)c_c(k)
 -\widehat A^+(0,0)\phi(c)\Bigg\}.                      \tag{4}
\end{split}
\]
Every sum is finite because the positive-part logarithms vanish for
\(q_i\ge P_i\).

Then there is an exact physical decomposition
\[
 \boxed{{\cal Z}_{\rm mid}^+={\cal K}_{\rm mid}
                              +{\cal R}_{\rm mid}}       \tag{5}
\]
where, with
\[
\begin{split}
 \Omega(m,w,h)=&
 {\bf1}_{w,w-h\in{\cal I}_D}
 \Phi(w/D)\Phi((w-h)/D)W(mw/x)W(m(w-h)/x)\\
 &\times\Phi(P_1/U)\Phi(P_2/U),
\end{split}
\]
one has
\[
\begin{split}
 {\cal K}_{\rm mid}=
 \sum_{\substack{h\in{\cal H}_{\rm mid}\\m,w\ge1}}
 &\mu(w)\mu(w-h)\Omega(m,w,h)\\
 {}\times\sum_{q_1,q_2\ge1}
 &\frac{\mu(q_1)\mu(q_2)}{[q_1,q_2]}
 \log(P_1/q_1)_+\log(P_2/q_2)_+\\
 &\times{\bf1}_{(N,[q_1,q_2])=1}
 {\bf1}_{(q_1,w)=1}{\bf1}_{(q_2,w-h)=1}
 {\bf1}_{(q_1,q_2)\mid h},                              \tag{6}
\end{split}
\]
and
\[
\begin{split}
 {\cal R}_{\rm mid}=
 \sum_{\substack{h\in{\cal H}_{\rm mid}\\m,w\ge1}}
 &\mu(w)\mu(w-h)\Omega(m,w,h)\\
 {}\times\sum_{\substack{q_1,q_2\ge1\\(N,c)=1\\d\mid h}}
 &\frac{\mu(q_1)\mu(q_2)}c
 \log(P_1/q_1)_+\log(P_2/q_2)_+
 \left({\bf1}_{(m,c)=1}-\frac{\phi(c)}c\right).          \tag{7}
\end{split}
\]
Thus (7) is exactly the \(r=0,\ k\ne0\) axis; the double zero has been
subtracted once, not estimated separately.

Uniformly as \(x\) tends to infinity,
\[
 {\cal R}_{\rm mid}\ll_{W,\Phi}D^2(\log x)^8,            \tag{8}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{
 {\cal Z}_{\rm mid}^+
 \ll_{W,\Phi,\alpha,\beta,\eta,\rho,B_{\rm src}}
 xD(\log x)^{-6-\eta-\rho/3}.
 }                                                       \tag{ZERO-RECOMB}
\]
In particular the globally recombined zero union is smaller than the
\(xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta}\) target.

Finally define
\[
\begin{split}
 {\cal N}_{\rm mid}^+=
 \sum_{\substack{h\in{\cal H}_{\rm mid}\\q_1,q_2\ge1\\
                 (N,c)=1,\ d\mid h}}
 \frac1{c^2}
 \sum_{\substack{k,r\ ({\rm mod}\ c)\\k\ne0,\ r\ne0}}
 \widehat A^+(k,r)e_b(-rhq_1^{-1})S(r,kN;c).             \tag{9}
\end{split}
\]
On the coprime TMC face, finite Fourier inversion gives exactly
\[
 {\cal V}_{\rm mid}^{\rm cop,+}
 ={\cal Z}_{\rm mid}^+ +{\cal N}_{\rm mid}^+.            \tag{10}
\]
The coefficient in (9) retains the literal moving bounded-variation
masks \(\log(P_i/q_i)_+\). No estimate for (9) is asserted. Equation
(10) is only the coprime face: it does not discard the separately defined
noncoprime support remainder of fact \(a88b7867c1bc2fd9\).

The omitted actual-correlation sectors \(0<|h|\le H_0\) and
\(3D/2-H_0<|h|\le3D/2\) have total absolute size respectively
\[
 \ll xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta-\rho/2},\qquad
 \ll xD(\log x)^{-10-2\eta-\rho},                       \tag{11}
\]
by fact \(ca9ce191fbd75de1\). Hence returning from the trimmed middle
family to the full off-diagonal physical correlation costs less than
the target.
4a1d6a8cfcc6d864.proof:
We first invert the two Ramanujan axes exactly. In the notation of
fact \(967520f427b111c5\), choose \(C\pmod c\) with
\[
 C\equiv0\pmod {q_1},\qquad C\equiv h\pmod {q_2}.
\]
The twist in (4) is \(e_c(-rC)\). Since
\[
 c_c(r)=\sum_{\substack{z\ ({\rm mod}\ c)\\(z,c)=1}}e_c(rz),
\]
finite orthogonality gives
\[
 \frac1{c^2}\sum_{r\ ({\rm mod}\ c)}
 \widehat A^+(0,r)e_c(-rC)c_c(r)
 =
 \frac1c\sum_{m,w}A^+(m,w){\bf1}_{(w-C,c)=1}.            \tag{12}
\]
Prime by prime, the last condition is
\[
 {\bf1}_{(w-C,c)=1}
 ={\bf1}_{(q_1,w)=1}{\bf1}_{(q_2,w-h)=1}.               \tag{13}
\]
Indeed \(C\equiv0\pmod {q_1}\) and \(C\equiv h\pmod {q_2}\);
on a common prime, \(d\mid h\) makes the two conditions identical.
Likewise
\[
 \frac1{c^2}\sum_{k\ ({\rm mod}\ c)}
 \widehat A^+(k,0)c_c(k)
 =
 \frac1c\sum_{m,w}A^+(m,w){\bf1}_{(m,c)=1},              \tag{14}
\]
and
\[
 \frac{\phi(c)}{c^2}\widehat A^+(0,0)
 =\frac1c\sum_{m,w}A^+(m,w)\frac{\phi(c)}c.              \tag{15}
\]
Insert (12)--(15) into (4), sum the complete \(q_1,q_2\) shells, and
separate the factors independent of those moduli. This proves exactly
(5)--(7). In particular (14) minus (15), rather than (14) alone, is the
\(r=0,\ k\ne0\) axis.

We bound (7). For fixed \(w,h,q_1,q_2\), the function of the real
variable \(m\) obtained from (7) without the centered coprimality factor
has
\[
 \|G\|_\infty+\operatorname {Var}(G)\ll_{W,\Phi}(\log x)^2. \tag{16}
\]
The support of \(W\) gives \(m\asymp x/D\) and
\[
 (2-\beta)x\le P_1,P_2\le(2-\alpha)x.
\]
The positive-part logarithm is continuous at \(P_i=q_i\); where it is
nonzero its derivative in \(m\) has magnitude at most \(O(D/x)\).
The chain rule and the support of \(\Phi(P_i/U)\) prove (16), also when
the whole function vanishes.

Möbius inversion of the reduced-residue indicator gives
\[
 {\bf1}_{(m,c)=1}-\frac{\phi(c)}c
 =\sum_{e\mid c}\mu(e)\left({\bf1}_{e\mid m}-\frac1e\right).
\]
For a bounded-variation function on the real line, the discrepancy
between a sum on one progression modulo \(e\) and \(1/e\) times the
complete integer sum is at most a constant times its supremum plus total
variation. Therefore the \(m\)-sum in (7), for fixed outer labels, is
\[
 \ll_{W,\Phi}\tau(c)(\log x)^2.                         \tag{17}
\]
Since the positive logarithms force \(q_i<2x\),
\[
\begin{split}
 \sum_{q_1,q_2<2x}\frac{\mu(q_1)^2\mu(q_2)^2\tau([q_1,q_2])}
 {[q_1,q_2]}
 &\le
 \sum_{g<2x}\frac{\tau(g)}g
 \left(\sum_{a<2x/g}\frac{\tau(a)}a\right)^2\\
 &\ll(\log x)^6.                                        \tag{18}
\end{split}
\]
Here \(q_1=ga,q_2=gb\) with \(g=(q_1,q_2)\); dropping the resulting
coprimality conditions only enlarges the sum, and
\(\sum_{n\le y}\tau(n)/n\ll\log^2(2y)\) follows by writing \(n=uv\).
There are \(O(D^2)\) pairs \((w,h)\) for which \(w,w-h\in{\cal I}_D\).
Equations (16)--(18) prove (8).

We turn to (6). For each active \(m,w,h\), apply fact
\(cd8d7d0fe163be6e\) with
\[
 d_1=w,\qquad d_2=w-h,\qquad P_i=N-md_i.
\]
All its hypotheses hold: the two \(d_i\) are distinct squarefree
integers coprime to \(N\), bounded by \(x^{1/2}\), and the displayed
support bounds give \(P_i\asymp x\). Thus, for every \(A>0\), the inner
sum in (6) is
\[
 R_N\mathfrak S_N(w,w-h)+O_A((\log x)^{-A}),             \tag{19}
\]
where
\[
 R_N=\prod_{p\mid N}(1-1/p)^{-1}.
\]
There are \(O(D^2)\) slope pairs and \(O(x/D)\) integers \(m\) per pair.
Choosing the exponent in (19) after the desired one shows that the total
error is \(O_A(xD(\log x)^{-A})\).

First sum (19) over every ordered distinct pair \(w,w'\in{\cal I}_D\),
with \(w'=w-h\), without the two exclusions in (1). For fixed \(w,w'\),
Euler summation and bounded variation give
\[
\begin{split}
 &\sum_m W(wm/x)W(w'm/x)
 \Phi((N-wm)/U)\Phi((N-w'm)/U)\\
 &\quad=
 \int_0^\infty W(wt/x)W(w't/x)
 \Phi((N-wt)/U)\Phi((N-w't)/U)\,dt+O_{W,\Phi}(1).        \tag{20}
\end{split}
\]
The integral, after restoring the two outer \(\Phi\)-weights and Möbius
signs, is exactly the aggregate singular main
\({\cal H}_{\rm sing}(D,M;U)\) of fact \(5b7b0955c5efaa1b\), with the
irrelevant scale name \(M\) determined by \(m\asymp x/D\). That fact,
applied with an arbitrarily large logarithmic exponent, gives
\[
 {\cal H}_{\rm sing}\ll_A\mathfrak c(N)xD(\log x)^{-A}.  \tag{21}
\]
The elementary increasing-prime argument in the proofs of facts
\(5b7b0955c5efaa1b\) and \(cd8d7d0fe163be6e\) gives
\[
 R_N\mathfrak c(N)\ll(\log\log(3x))^{C_1}.              \tag{22}
\]
The same argument applied to the exact local product of fact
\(b164cd7d1e02e173\) gives, pointwise on the present ranges,
\[
 \mathfrak S_N(w,w')\ll(\log\log(3x))^{C_2}.             \tag{23}
\]
Indeed each exceptional product is maximized by using the smallest
primes, whose product is at most a fixed power of \(x\).
Consequently the accumulated \(O(1)\) error in (20) is
\[
 \ll D^2(\log\log(3x))^{C_2}
 =O_A(xD(\log x)^{-A})                                  \tag{24}
\]
for every fixed \(A\), since \(D\le2x^{1/2}\). Equations
(19)--(24) show that the complete all-pair \(k=0\) axis has arbitrary
logarithmic saving.

It remains to restore the two pair sectors omitted in (1). The number
of ordered pairs in
\[
 0<|w-w'|\le H_0
\]
is \(O(DH_0)\). Because both slopes lie in \([D/2,2D]\), the number with
\[
 3D/2-H_0<|w-w'|\le3D/2
\]
is also \(O(DH_0)\). For each pair there are \(O(x/D)\) integers \(m\).
Using (19), (22), and (23), their combined \(k=0\) contribution is
\[
 \ll xH_0(\log\log(3x))^{C_3}
      +O_A(xH_0(\log x)^{-A})
 \ll xD(\log x)^{-6-\eta-\rho/3}.                       \tag{25}
\]
Subtracting these sectors from the all-pair estimate proves the same
bound for \({\cal K}_{\rm mid}\). Together with (8), whose size is
power-smaller because \(D\le2x^{1/2}\), equation (5) proves
ZERO-RECOMB.

For (9)--(10), repeat the finite Fourier inversion in fact
\(a88b7867c1bc2fd9\) with the coefficient (2). On the original
congruence support, \(q_i\mid P_i\), so
\(\log(P_i/q_i)_+=\log(P_i/q_i)\); hence this altered off-support
extension represents the same physical block. Split the frequency
square into the union \(k=0\) or \(r=0\), already evaluated in (4), and
the complement \(kr\ne0\). TMC-EXACT from fact
\(967520f427b111c5\) gives the multiplier in (9), proving (10). The
dependence of (2) on \(q_i\) through the positive-part logarithms is
literal and has the bounded-variation property proved in (16).

Finally, (11) is exactly equations (8)--(9) of fact
\(ca9ce191fbd75de1\). This proves the stated restoration of the physical
small and outer-edge sectors without assigning those terms to an
individual Fourier mode.

glossary.A^+_{h,q_1,q_2}: the full-shell TMC coefficient using the positive-part moving logarithms
glossary.cal H_mid: the union of every trimmed nonzero middle-shift block
glossary.cal K_mid: the physical k=0 logarithmic-sieve axis after exact Ramanujan inversion
glossary.cal N_mid^+: the full-shell middle-shift TMC aggregate with both finite frequencies nonzero
glossary.cal R_mid: the centered r=0,k nonzero reduced-residue remainder
glossary.cal Z_mid^+: the complete q-shell and middle-shift aggregate of the k=0 or r=0 TMC frequency union

4a9a213a428b7e8c.title: Use the six parent cells Z_C, Z_11, Z_21, Z_22, Z_asym and Z_U and the primitive-conductor data of fact 676c6a2cb3ebf7cc. Thus, for each labelled incidence z, q_z>1 is its primitive additive conductor, P_z(q_z) is its primitive unit-residue fourth moment, a_z is an arbitrary complex provenance coefficient, and for each parent cell X one has T_X=sum_{z in Z_X} a_z P_z(q_z). Fix any set Y of parent-cell labels and put T_Y=sum_{X in Y}T_X. Then the exact identities from facts 91db48815d136d4c and 676c6a2cb3ebf7cc give
4a9a213a428b7e8c.author: slava chan
4a9a213a428b7e8c.statement:
Use the six parent cells Z_C, Z_11, Z_21, Z_22, Z_asym and Z_U and the primitive-conductor data of fact 676c6a2cb3ebf7cc. Thus, for each labelled incidence z, q_z>1 is its primitive additive conductor, P_z(q_z) is its primitive unit-residue fourth moment, a_z is an arbitrary complex provenance coefficient, and for each parent cell X one has T_X=sum_{z in Z_X} a_z P_z(q_z). Fix any set Y of parent-cell labels and put T_Y=sum_{X in Y}T_X. Then the exact identities from facts 91db48815d136d4c and 676c6a2cb3ebf7cc give
T_Y=sum_{X in Y} sum_{z in Z_X} a_z sum_{e dividing q_z} mu(q_z/e) \widetilde C_z(e),
with every incidence remaining in its unique parent cell and with the common zero mode and every proper reduced conductor cancelling before any Hilbert-space inequality.

Suppose, in addition, that a literal primitive-conductor leaf reconstruction of T_Y has been supplied in the following exact weighted form. Let L be a finite set whose leaves retain maps to a parent cell X(lambda) in Y, an incidence z(lambda) in Z_{X(lambda)}, its primitive conductor q_{z(lambda)}, an overlap-face label F(lambda), and an external window-cell label omega(lambda). For every lambda in L let Q_lambda and T_lambda be finite sets, let c_lambda, gamma_{lambda,q}, b_{lambda,t} and X_{lambda,q,t} be complex numbers, and let H_lambda>0. Assume exactly that
T_Y=sum_{lambda in L} c_lambda H_lambda^{-1} sum_{q in Q_lambda} gamma_{lambda,q} sum_{t in T_lambda} b_{lambda,t}X_{lambda,q,t}.
Let R be real, set Q=R+Re(T_Y), and define
M=sum_{lambda in L}sum_{q in Q_lambda}sum_{t in T_lambda}|X_{lambda,q,t}|^2
and
A^2=sum_{lambda in L}|c_lambda|^2H_lambda^{-2}(sum_{q in Q_lambda}|gamma_{lambda,q}|^2)(sum_{t in T_lambda}|b_{lambda,t}|^2).
Then
(-Q)_+<=A M^{1/2}+|R|.
If nonnegative numbers E,b,R_2 also satisfy M<=bE^{1/2}+R_2, then for every c>0,
(-Q)_+<=cE^{1/2}+A^2b/(4c)+A R_2^{1/2}+|R|.
In particular, if P>1, epsilon>0, A<=P^{3/2+epsilon/6}, b<=P^{6+epsilon/6}, and |R|+A R_2^{1/2}<=P^6(log P)^{-B}, then taking c=P^{3+epsilon} gives
(-Q)_+<=P^{3+epsilon}E^{1/2}+P^{6-epsilon/2}/4+P^6(log P)^{-B}.
Thus the first-level coefficient budget is the displayed literal weighted sum A^2; parent cells, centered primitive conductors, overlap faces and external window cells cannot be counted merely by their cardinalities or silently discarded.

There is also an exact full overlap and cross-cell ledger for every four-prime terminal family. Let Sigma and Tau be finite packet sets. Give each sigma in Sigma a carrier C_sigma, support S_sigma and external window-cell label omega_sigma. Give each tau in Tau a carrier C_tau, external window-cell label omega_tau, and an ordered support S_tau={r_1(tau),r_2(tau),r_3(tau),r_4(tau)} of four distinct primes. Let w_{sigma,tau} be arbitrary complex pair weights. For window cells omega,omega' and a subset F of {1,2,3,4}, define
U_{omega,omega',F}=sum_{sigma,tau: omega_sigma=omega, omega_tau=omega', C_sigma=C_tau} w_{sigma,tau} product_{i in F}1_{r_i(tau) in S_sigma}.
Define the complete support-disjoint equal-carrier pair sum
D=sum_{sigma,tau:C_sigma=C_tau}w_{sigma,tau}1_{S_sigma intersect S_tau is empty}.
Then
D=sum_{omega,omega'}sum_{F subset {1,2,3,4}}(-1)^{|F|}U_{omega,omega',F}=D_same+D_cross,
where D_same is the part with omega=omega' and D_cross is the part with omega different from omega'. For each ordered window pair there is one unrestricted face F empty and exactly fifteen nonempty overlap faces. If, at a fixed external modulus and fixed window cell, w_{sigma,tau}=a_sigma b_tau with the nonnegative data of fact d659d90d40151040, then that fact's literal consumer E_{0,q} is exactly the corresponding diagonal support-disjoint term and also equals its exact support-dependent Fourier transpose. It controls neither a different diagonal terminal family nor D_cross.

Consequently a full terminal reconstruction may either keep a support-dependent diagonal consumer bundled, as in d659d90d40151040, or expand it into all sixteen inclusion-exclusion faces, but it cannot drop any of the fifteen nonempty faces. It must also retain D_cross as a separate input. Fact 6f97cd0bbc7daa5a shows that positive semidefiniteness, perfect same-cell off-diagonal cancellation and small pointwise cross entries alone do not bound that cross-cell operator with a power saving. The theorem above is therefore an exact conditional two-level Hilbert/Ursell reconstruction contract; it does not supply the missing literal all-anatomy leaf map, prove the second-stage bound M<=bE^{1/2}+R_2, prove a cross-cell PAVG26/PAVG27 estimate, or complete the Goldbach argument.
4a9a213a428b7e8c.proof:
The first displayed identity is obtained by summing the identity of fact 676c6a2cb3ebf7cc over X in Y. Fact 91db48815d136d4c gives a disjoint six-way parent partition and permits arbitrary auxiliary provenance coefficients without moving or duplicating an incidence. Fact 676c6a2cb3ebf7cc applies centered conductor descent independently inside each such cell. It proves that the common zero-frequency term has total Möbius coefficient zero, every proper reduced conductor has total coefficient zero, and only q_z remains. Therefore the identity is exact before any absolute value or Cauchy-Schwarz inequality.

Under the literal leaf-reconstruction hypothesis, apply fact 6dcbe1a64e6c4b2d to the displayed weighted sum for T_Y. Its squared coefficient norm is exactly A^2 and its direct-sum squared coordinate norm is M, so |T_Y|<=A M^{1/2}. Since Q=R+Re(T_Y), one has (-Q)_+<=|T_Y|+|R|, proving the first inequality. Now apply fact f21be13a19bbb435 with its variables a and R_1 specialized to A and |R|. This gives the inequality with arbitrary c. The scale specialization is exactly the scale calculation in that fact and yields the stated P^{3+epsilon} bound and remainders.

For the overlap identity, fix sigma and tau. Because the four primes in S_tau are distinct,
1_{S_sigma intersect S_tau is empty}=product_{i=1}^4(1-1_{r_i(tau) in S_sigma}).
Expanding this four-factor product gives
sum_{F subset {1,2,3,4}}(-1)^{|F|}product_{i in F}1_{r_i(tau) in S_sigma}.
Multiply by w_{sigma,tau}1_{C_sigma=C_tau} and sum over the finite packet sets. Then group first by omega_sigma and omega_tau. This gives the displayed formula for D. Splitting the ordered window pairs according as omega=omega' or omega is different from omega' gives the exact and disjoint same-cell/cross-cell decomposition. A four-element set has sixteen subsets, of which exactly one is empty, so there are exactly fifteen nonempty overlap faces.

For the d659 specialization, choose one fixed external window cell and weights w_{sigma,tau}=a_sigma b_tau. The definitions then give
D=sum_{tau in Tau}b_tau sum_{sigma in Sigma:C_sigma=C_tau,S_sigma intersect S_tau empty}a_sigma,
which is exactly E_{0,q} in fact d659d90d40151040. That fact proves its exact support-dependent Fourier transpose. Its quantifiers fix one external modulus and one such packet family, so it makes no assertion about terms with a different window-cell pair.

The inclusion-exclusion expansion is an equality. Omitting a nonempty face changes its right-hand side in general: for example, if one pair has r_i(tau) in S_sigma exactly for the slots in a nonempty set F_0, then its contribution to the product is recovered only by the complete subset expansion over subsets of F_0. Likewise the same/cross decomposition is an equality over disjoint index sets, so same-cell control cannot delete the cross index set. The final formal limitation is precisely fact 6f97cd0bbc7daa5a. This proves every asserted identity, inequality, and scope statement.

glossary.A: The exact nonnegative first-stage weighted Hilbert coefficient norm.
glossary.D: The complete support-disjoint equal-carrier packet-pair sum.
glossary.D_cross: The part of D whose two external window-cell labels are different.
glossary.D_same: The part of D whose two external window-cell labels are equal.
glossary.E: A nonnegative terminal energy in the second-stage hypothesis.
glossary.F(lambda): The overlap-face label retained by leaf lambda.
glossary.L: The finite literal leaf set in the reconstruction hypothesis.
glossary.M: The nonnegative first-stage direct-sum squared coordinate norm.
glossary.R: The real reconstruction remainder before the first Hilbert inequality.
glossary.R_2: The nonnegative remainder in the second-stage moment estimate.
glossary.T_Y: The sum of the primitive-conductor aggregates T_X over parent cells X in Y.
glossary.U_{omega,omega',F}: The carrier-equal packet-pair face requiring the right support primes in slots F to lie in the left support, with external cells omega and omega'.
glossary.X(lambda): The unique parent-cell label retained by leaf lambda.
glossary.Y: A selected subset of the six parent-cell labels.
glossary.full overlap ledger: The inclusion-exclusion identity containing the unrestricted face and all fifteen nonempty four-prime overlap faces.
glossary.literal primitive-conductor leaf reconst: An exact weighted sampled formula for T_Y whose leaves retain parent-cell, incidence, primitive-conductor, overlap-face and external-window provenance.
glossary.omega(lambda): The external window-cell label retained by leaf lambda.
glossary.omega_sigma: The external window-cell label of a left packet sigma.
glossary.omega_tau: The external window-cell label of a right packet tau.
glossary.w_{sigma,tau}: An arbitrary complex weight attached to a left-right packet pair.
glossary.z(lambda): The unique labelled incidence retained by leaf lambda.

4b73e72865a65e16.title: COMPLETE FIXED-POWER PAYMENT OF THE p-DIVIDES-C UNBALANCED MIDDLE-EFFECTIVE STRICT-TOP C1 ROW. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100 and eta=kappa/20, and fix K_0>=2 and zeta>0. Let Q be sufficiently large. In the literal strict-top C1 setting let beta_m<=beta<6/5 and let n=pv be squarefree, where p is the unique rough prime, gcd(p,v)=1, and every prime divisor of v is at most Q^(beta-1+sigma). Let C=mathscr A h, assume p divides C, put m_eff=n/gcd(C,n), and write t=log(m_eff)/log(Q). Assume
4b73e72865a65e16.author: slava chan
4b73e72865a65e16.statement:
COMPLETE FIXED-POWER PAYMENT OF THE p-DIVIDES-C UNBALANCED MIDDLE-EFFECTIVE STRICT-TOP C1 ROW. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100 and eta=kappa/20, and fix K_0>=2 and zeta>0. Let Q be sufficiently large. In the literal strict-top C1 setting let beta_m<=beta<6/5 and let n=pv be squarefree, where p is the unique rough prime, gcd(p,v)=1, and every prime divisor of v is at most Q^(beta-1+sigma). Let C=mathscr A h, assume p divides C, put m_eff=n/gcd(C,n), and write t=log(m_eff)/log(Q). Assume
16/25+127kappa/500+zeta<=t<=28/25-97kappa/250-zeta.             (1)
Let c be squarefree with nc<=Q^K_0. Let W be extended by zero, supported on Q<=q<2Q, and satisfy V_Q(W)<=Q^epsilon for every fixed epsilon>0. Then the complete composite-Mobius reciprocal row
S=sum_{q;gcd(q,nc)=1}mu(q)W(q)e_n(Cq^(-1))
satisfies
|S|<=Q^(1-kappa/200+o(1)).                                      (2)
The o(1) is uniform in the displayed fixed hierarchy. Thus the p-divides-C chamber has no unbalanced A-routing residual in the middle-effective band (1). No assertion is made for the lower and upper effective-exponent edge strips.
4b73e72865a65e16.proof:
The lower endpoint in (1) exceeds
3/5+63kappa/250+zeta
because
16/25-3/5=1/25
and
127/500-63/250=1/500.
The upper endpoint in (1) is smaller than
6/5-48kappa/125-zeta
because
28/25<6/5
and 97/250>48/125. Hence (1) lies inside the fixed-slack middle-effective band of fact 8f9c29373de3486c.

Apply the exact finite routing of fact df45be7aead3cec9 to S. Its MEDIUM and original TYPE I boxes contribute in total Q^(1-eta+o(1)). Every remaining box is MULTI-FREE. On each such box choose delta=rho=kappa/200, so s=delta+rho=kappa/100, and apply the disjoint refinement of fact 8eb30e55bdef6b27 into A-PAID and A-ROUTING RESIDUAL. Every A-PAID box is bounded by Q^(1-kappa/200), up to the Q^o(1) number of boxes.

It remains to show that no A-ROUTING RESIDUAL box occurs. Fact 8f9c29373de3486c proves that class R1 is empty for every effective exponent in the present range, and that R2 is empty throughout the band containing (1). Therefore any residual box would have to lie in the genuine divisor-gap class R3.

Fact 13cb8b02b12d19bc applies to every such literal C1 R3 box. On the effective-exponent band (1), it proves that the two width-failure alternatives G1 and G2 are empty. Fact 0437c7a25bf0c1c5 gives the exact remaining alternative G3, whose defining conditions include p does not divide C. This contradicts the present hypothesis p divides C. Thus R3 is empty as well, and there is no A-ROUTING RESIDUAL box.

All boxes are therefore either MEDIUM, original TYPE I, or A-PAID. Since eta=kappa/20>kappa/200, summing the Q^o(1) exact convolution and dyadic boxes gives (2). Every literal weight, gate, and nonunit numerator reduction is retained by the cited routing facts.

4b89ec4ce7a7b67a.title: RAMANUJAN-CORRECTION PAYMENT AND REDUCTION OF CNP2 TO THE UNCENTERED ADDITIVE CROSSED GRAM
4b89ec4ce7a7b67a.author: slava chan
4b89ec4ce7a7b67a.statement:
RAMANUJAN-CORRECTION PAYMENT AND REDUCTION OF CNP2 TO THE UNCENTERED ADDITIVE CROSSED GRAM.

Fix constants C>=1 and J>=3. Let Q>=8 and let real numbers H,V,P,B satisfy
  2<=H<=Q^(1/3),  2<=V<H,  P=QH/V,  B>=1.                 (1)
Let A be a nonzero integer with |A|<=Q^C. Let cal L be a finite label set. For each outer row
  o=(ell,v,p),
where ell belongs to cal L, V<=v<2V is an integer, p is prime in [P,2P), and gcd(v,p)=1, put n=vp. Let cal X_o be a finite set of triples x=(q,m,k) satisfying
  Q<=q,m<2Q,  qm+nk=A,  gcd(qm,n)=1.                       (2)
For ell in cal L let I_ell be an integer interval contained either in [H,2H) or in (-2H,-H]. For x=(q,m,k) in cal X_o define
  d_x=gcd(|A|,q),  r_x=q/d_x,  t_x=k/d_x,
  pi_{x,h}=c_{r_x}(h)/phi(r_x),                             (3)
where c_r(h) is the Ramanujan sum.

For every o,h,x assume independently both the pointwise bound
  |a_{o,h}(x)|<=B                                           (4)
and the normalized factorization
  a_{o,h}(x)=alpha_{q,h}w_{q,h},                            (5)
where
  |alpha_{q,h}|<=tau(r_x),
  |w_{q,h}|<=C_J(L_pr/H)(1+|h|/H)^(-J),
  L_pr<=BH.                                                 (6)
Extend these q-coefficients by zero outside the q-projection of cal X_o. Assume subpolynomial label and coefficient complexity: for every delta>0,
  B+C_J+#cal L<<_{C,J,delta}Q^delta.                        (7)

Define
  Aadd
   =sum_o sum_{h in I_ell}
      sum_{x_1,x_2 in cal X_o,
           t_{x_1}/r_{x_1} not equal t_{x_2}/r_{x_2}}
       a_{o,h}(x_1)conjugate(a_{o,h}(x_2))
       e(h[t_{x_1}/r_{x_1}-t_{x_2}/r_{x_2}]).               (8)
Then Aadd is real and the exact unequal-phase centered form O_2^cross of fact 1a9cfcfe3eedd5e2 satisfies
  O_2^cross=Aadd+Rram,                                      (9)
where Rram is the sum over the same domain as (8) of
  a_{o,h}(x_1)conjugate(a_{o,h}(x_2))
  [-pi_{x_1,h}e(-h t_{x_2}/r_{x_2})
   -pi_{x_2,h}e(h t_{x_1}/r_{x_1})
   +pi_{x_1,h}pi_{x_2,h}].                                 (10)
For every epsilon>0,
  |Rram|<<_{C,J,epsilon}B^2(#cal L)Q^(2+epsilon)H
        <<_{C,J,epsilon}P Q^(5/3+epsilon).                  (11)
Consequently the remaining one-sided supplier may be weakened from CNP2 to
  Aadd<<_{C,J,epsilon}P Q^(5/3+epsilon).                    (12)
An absolute-value estimate in (12) is stronger than necessary. Every source and outer mask remains inside a_{o,h}. No estimate for (12), no PMD closure, and no Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
4b89ec4ce7a7b67a.proof:
Fact 1a9cfcfe3eedd5e2 proves that d_x divides k, gcd(t_x,r_x)=1, and
  eta_{x,h}=e_{r_x}(ht_x)-pi_{x,h}.                         (13)
It also proves the exact kernel identity
  eta_{x_1,h}conjugate(eta_{x_2,h})
   =e(h[t_{x_1}/r_{x_1}-t_{x_2}/r_{x_2}])
    -pi_{x_1,h}e(-h t_{x_2}/r_{x_2})
    -pi_{x_2,h}e(h t_{x_1}/r_{x_1})
    +pi_{x_1,h}pi_{x_2,h}.                                 (14)
The q-projection on cal X_o is injective by fact 914048233fada05f. Therefore unequal exact rational phases imply distinct atoms and hence distinct q-values. Thus the domain in (8) is exactly the domain defining O_2^cross. Summing (14) proves (9)-(10). Interchanging x_1 and x_2 conjugates each summand and preserves the ordered domain, so Aadd is real.

Fix one outer row o and define
  Poh=sum_{x in cal X_o}a_{o,h}(x)pi_{x,h},
  Noh=sum_{x in cal X_o}a_{o,h}(x)e(h t_x/r_x),             (15)
where h is the free height variable. Since J>=3, the factorization (5)-(6), after zero extension, satisfies fact 6836789040c87b6f. That fact gives
  sum_{h in I_ell}|Poh|
   <<_{C,J,epsilon}L_pr Q^epsilon
   <<_{C,J,epsilon}BH Q^epsilon.                            (16)

Since vp>=VP=QH and H<=Q, fact 914048233fada05f gives
  Xo:=#cal X_o<<_{C,epsilon}Q^(1+epsilon)/H.                (17)
The independent pointwise hypothesis (4) and |pi_{x,h}|<=1 give
  |Noh|<=BXo<<_{C,epsilon}B Q^(1+epsilon)/H,
  |Poh|<=BXo<<_{C,epsilon}B Q^(1+epsilon)/H.                (18)
The complete ordered-pair sums of the three terms in (10), before imposing unequal exact rational phases, are
  -Poh conjugate(Noh),  -Noh conjugate(Poh),  |Poh|^2.      (19)
Equations (16)-(18) show that their total absolute contribution after summing h in one row is
  <<_{C,J,epsilon}
   [2 max_h|Noh|+max_h|Poh|]sum_h|Poh|
  <<_{C,J,epsilon}B^2Q^(1+epsilon).                         (20)

To impose the unequal-phase restriction, subtract the exact-rational equal-phase pairs from (19). Fact 2359a25d9fc6dd9b and the equal-phase proof in fact 1a9cfcfe3eedd5e2 show that every exact rational value t_x/r_x has a fibre of cardinality at most
  DA<<_{C,epsilon}Q^epsilon:                                (21)
the fibre is indexed by the possible divisors d_x of A. If n_lambda is the cardinality of the fibre with exact rational value lambda, then
  sum_lambda n_lambda^2<=DA sum_lambda n_lambda=DA Xo.      (22)
Taking absolute values on the equal-phase pairs in each of the three correction terms, using (4), |pi|<=1, and (17), (21), and (22), gives for each h
  <<B^2DA Xo<<_{C,epsilon}B^2Q^(1+epsilon)/H.               (23)
The interval I_ell contains at most 2H integers, so the total exact-rational equal-phase correction in one row is
  <<_{C,epsilon}B^2Q^(1+epsilon).                           (24)
Combining (20) and (24), the unequal-phase correction contribution of one outer row is
  <<_{C,J,epsilon}B^2Q^(1+epsilon).                         (25)

There are fewer than 4(#cal L)VP=4(#cal L)QH outer rows. Summing (25) and renaming epsilon proves the first inequality in (11). Finally,
  [Q^2H]/[P Q^(5/3)]
   =[Q^2H]/[(QH/V)Q^(5/3)]
   =V/Q^(2/3)
   <H/Q^(2/3)
   <=Q^(-1/3).                                              (26)
The subpolynomial factors in (7) are absorbed by renaming epsilon, proving the second inequality in (11).

The pointwise bound (4), factorization (5)-(6), and subpolynomial assumptions are exactly the coefficient hypotheses used in fact 1a9cfcfe3eedd5e2. Facts 294ac3b02b065aec and c5f49ab9e8bd2c60, through that fact, pay the q-diagonal and principal row; fact 1a9cfcfe3eedd5e2 also pays the equal exact-rational phase part. Therefore (9), (11), and the one-sided estimate (12) imply the required one-sided bound for O_2^cross. This proves all assertions.
