glossary.CJ: A positive constant controlling the finite-band decay profile.
glossary.DA: A divisor-sized upper bound for an exact reduced-rational-phase fibre.
glossary.Lpr: The normalized finite-band principal-row amplitude parameter.
glossary.Noh: The uncentered additive-phase aggregate in one outer row at one height.
glossary.Poh: The principal Ramanujan aggregate in one outer row at one height.
glossary.Rram: The sum of the three Ramanujan-principal correction terms over unequal exact rational phases.
glossary.Xo: The cardinality of one actual source row.

4bc8d22f796384d3.title: PHASE-ALIGNMENT SATURATION OF ONE ABSTRACT ADDITIVE CROSSED L2 ROW
4bc8d22f796384d3.author: slava chan
4bc8d22f796384d3.statement:
PHASE-ALIGNMENT SATURATION OF ONE ABSTRACT ADDITIVE CROSSED L2 ROW.

Let H>=2 and let I be a finite integer interval contained either in [H,2H) or in (-2H,-H]. Put L=#I. Let cal X be a finite set. For every x in cal X let r_x be a positive integer and t_x an integer. Partition cal X into fibres of the exact rational value
  lambda_x=t_x/r_x,
and write n_lambda for the cardinality of the lambda-fibre. Put X_src=#cal X.

For h in I and x in cal X define
  a_h(x)=e(-h t_x/r_x).                                    (1)
Then |a_h(x)|=1. Define the unequal exact-rational-phase Gram
  T_align2
   =sum_{h in I}
      sum_{x_1,x_2 in cal X,
           t_{x_1}/r_{x_1} not equal t_{x_2}/r_{x_2}}
       a_h(x_1)conjugate(a_h(x_2))
       e(h[t_{x_1}/r_{x_1}-t_{x_2}/r_{x_2}]).               (2)
Then exactly
  T_align2=L[X_src^2-sum_lambda n_lambda^2].                (3)
In particular, if all exact rational phases are distinct, then
  T_align2=L X_src(X_src-1).                               (4)

For every fixed J>=3, the coefficient array (1), extended by zero outside I, satisfies the abstract normalized principal-row coefficient hypotheses of fact 4b89ec4ce7a7b67a with
  B=1, alpha_{q,h}=1, L_pr=H, C_J=3^J                      (5)
after assigning a distinct q-coordinate to each x and taking any r_x<=q with tau(r_x)>=1. Therefore boundedness, source occupancy, and the displayed finite-band factorization alone cannot give a fixed-power saving from the one-row unequal-phase scale in (3). Any fixed-power interior estimate for the literal Aadd must use additional structure of its actual coefficients or an assembly property not encoded by those abstract hypotheses.

This is a coefficient-class obstruction only. It does not assert that (1) is a literal Poisson coefficient, does not give a global lower bound for Aadd, does not contradict the endpoint upper bound in fact 5db1ff60efd872b4, and gives no PMD or Goldbach conclusion.
4bc8d22f796384d3.proof:
For every h,x_1,x_2, substitution of (1) into a summand of (2) gives
  e(-h t_{x_1}/r_{x_1})
  e(h t_{x_2}/r_{x_2})
  e(h[t_{x_1}/r_{x_1}-t_{x_2}/r_{x_2}])
  =1.                                                       (6)
Thus T_align2 equals L times the number of ordered pairs with unequal exact rational phases. There are X_src^2 total ordered pairs. The number of ordered pairs with equal exact rational phase is sum_lambda n_lambda^2. This proves (3). If every fibre has cardinality one, the latter sum is X_src, proving (4).

We verify (5). Assign each x a distinct formal q-coordinate and put alpha_{q,h}=1 on its coordinate. Since tau(r_x)>=1, the alpha bound in fact 4b89ec4ce7a7b67a holds. Put w_{q,h}=a_h(x) for h in I and zero otherwise. Then a_h(x)=alpha_{q,h}w_{q,h} and |a_h(x)|=1=B. For h in I one has |h|/H<=2, hence
  (1+|h|/H)^(-J)>=3^(-J).
With L_pr=H and C_J=3^J,
  C_J(L_pr/H)(1+|h|/H)^(-J)>=1=|w_{q,h}|.                 (7)
Outside I the left coefficient is zero, so the same inequality holds. Also L_pr=H=BH. The constants B and C_J are independent of every scale, hence subpolynomial. Thus all coefficient-size and normalized factorization conditions are satisfied.

Equations (3)-(4) show that this abstract class contains arrays attaining the full unequal-pair count in one row. Hence no fixed-power saving uniform over only these hypotheses can follow at the row level. The construction does not identify these coefficients with the literal source coefficients, proving the scope qualifications.

glossary.Talign2: The phase-aligned value of the unequal-slope additive L2 Gram in one source row.

4cae52efa792b9ef.title: SHIFTED AND LONG-u INTERVAL-PRIME RECIPROCAL ESTIMATE. Fix integers J,K>=1. Let q>1 be squarefree, let A be an integer with gcd(A,q)=1, and let H,Y>=1 satisfy H<=Y and 4HY<q. Let I be any interval of positive integers contained in [1,q^K], of cardinality U>=1. Let alpha_u, gamma_y, and nu_h be complex coefficients supported respectively on u in I, Y<=y<2Y, and 0<|h|<=H, with absolute values at most tau_J(u), tau_J(y), and tau_J(|h|). In every summand require gcd(uy,q)=1. Then, for every epsilon>0,
4cae52efa792b9ef.author: slava chan
4cae52efa792b9ef.statement:
SHIFTED AND LONG-u INTERVAL-PRIME RECIPROCAL ESTIMATE. Fix integers J,K>=1. Let q>1 be squarefree, let A be an integer with gcd(A,q)=1, and let H,Y>=1 satisfy H<=Y and 4HY<q. Let I be any interval of positive integers contained in [1,q^K], of cardinality U>=1. Let alpha_u, gamma_y, and nu_h be complex coefficients supported respectively on u in I, Y<=y<2Y, and 0<|h|<=H, with absolute values at most tau_J(u), tau_J(y), and tau_J(|h|). In every summand require gcd(uy,q)=1. Then, for every epsilon>0,
|sum_{u in I} alpha_u sum_{Y<=y<2Y} gamma_y sum_{0<|h|<=H} nu_h e_q(Ah(uy)^(-1))|
<<_{J,K,epsilon} (qUYH)^epsilon [ U(HY)^(1/2) + HY q^(1/4){U(1+U/q)}^(1/2) ].
More precisely, if I has cardinality W<=q, the second term may be replaced by W^(1/2)HYq^(1/4). The same bounds hold for a union of consecutive integer subintervals after summing their displayed right sides.
4cae52efa792b9ef.proof:
We first prove the assertion for an arbitrary interval I=(C,D] intersect Z of cardinality W<=q. This is a shifted version of the proof of fact 4a101b703d4499f6; we give the details showing that no condition on the location C is used.

Cauchy's inequality in u and the pointwise divisor bound tau_J(u)<<_{J,epsilon}q^epsilon, valid because u<=q^K, give
|T_I|^2 << q^epsilon W sum_{u in I,(u,q)=1}|sum_{y,h,(y,q)=1} gamma_y nu_h e_q(Ah y^(-1)u^(-1))|^2.  (1)
After expansion, the u-sum attached to (h_1,y_1,h_2,y_2) is
sum_{u in I,(u,q)=1}e_q(A(h_1y_1^(-1)-h_2y_2^(-1))u^(-1)).  (2)
Put Delta=h_1y_2-h_2y_1. Since y_1y_2 is a unit modulo q and |Delta|<4HY<q, the phase in (2) vanishes modulo q exactly when Delta=0.

The exact-product diagonal is counted in the proof of fact 4a101b703d4499f6: with the same divisor weights,
sum_{h_1y_2=h_2y_1}|nu_{h_1}nu_{h_2}gamma_{y_1}gamma_{y_2}| << q^epsilon HY.  (3)
For these tuples (2) is at most W, so after the outer factor W in (1) their contribution is O(q^epsilon W^2HY).

For Delta nonzero, equation (7) in the accepted proof of fact 4a101b703d4499f6 applies to every real pair of endpoints C<D. Since W<=q, it bounds (2) by
q^epsilon[(Delta,q)(W/q+1)+q^(1/2)]
<< q^(1/2+epsilon)(Delta,q)^(1/2),  (4)
where 1<=(Delta,q)<=q. The determinant-divisor count (9)-(12) of that same fact is independent of the u interval and gives
sum_{Delta nonzero}(Delta,q)^(1/2)<<q^epsilon(HY)^2.  (5)
Thus the off-diagonal contribution after the outer Cauchy factor is
O(q^(1/2+epsilon)W(HY)^2).
Taking square roots together with the diagonal proves
|T_I|<<q^epsilon[W(HY)^(1/2)+W^(1/2)HYq^(1/4)].  (6)
This proves the precise short-interval assertion for an interval situated anywhere in [1,q^K].

For a general interval I of cardinality U, partition it into t consecutive integer intervals I_i of cardinalities W_i<=q, with t<=1+U/q and sum_i W_i=U. Apply (6) to each piece and use the triangle inequality. The first terms sum to U(HY)^(1/2). For the second terms, Cauchy's inequality across pieces gives
sum_i W_i^(1/2)<=t^(1/2)(sum_iW_i)^(1/2)<={U(1+U/q)}^(1/2).  (7)
Substitution into (6) proves the stated long-interval estimate. The union assertion follows by applying the same argument componentwise. All divisor weights and fixed powers of the polynomial support are absorbed into the displayed epsilon factor.

glossary.I: An arbitrary interval of positive u-values, not required to begin below q.
glossary.T_I: The reciprocal exponential sum restricted to I.
glossary.U: The cardinality of the full u interval I.
glossary.W: The cardinality of one shifted subinterval of length at most q.
glossary.e_q(t): The additive character exp(2 pi i t/q).

4d2585a7863f65b6.title: ABSTRACT CLOSED-ENDPOINT COMPLETE-FREQUENCY TWO-ROUGH-PRIME \(C2_*\) TRACE
4d2585a7863f65b6.author: slava chan
4d2585a7863f65b6.statement:
ABSTRACT CLOSED-ENDPOINT COMPLETE-FREQUENCY TWO-ROUGH-PRIME \(C2_*\) TRACE.

Fix integers \(J,C_A,K\ge1\), constants \(C\ge1\),
\(0<\kappa\le1/100\), and put
\[
 \sigma=\kappa/100,quad
 \beta_1=6/5-3\sigma,quad
 \beta_m=6/5-12\sigma/5.
\]
Let \(Q\) be sufficiently large, \(\beta_1<\beta\le\beta_m\), and
put
\[
 B=Q^\beta,quad H_T=B/Q,quad
 L=H_TQ^\sigma,quad S_0=H_T^2Q^{3\sigma},quad
 Z_*=2Q^{3/2-\beta-3\sigma}.
\]
Let dyadic \(V,P_1,P_2\ge1\) satisfy
\[
 C^{-1}B\le VP_1P_2\le CB.                                      \tag{1}
\]
Put
\[
 \nu={\log V\over\log Q},quad
 a={\log P_1\over\log Q},quad
 b={\log P_2\over\log Q},
\]
and assume
\[
 0\le\nu\le2\beta-2+3\sigma,qquad
 a\le b,qquad a,b\ge3/2-\beta-3\sigma.                        \tag{2}
\]
Let \(\xi_v\) be supported on squarefree \(V\le v<2V\), with
\[
 v\le S_0,qquad p\mid v\Longrightarrow p\le L,qquad
 |\xi_v|\le\tau_J(v).
\]
Fix \(A\ne0\), \(|A|\le Q^{C_A}\), let \(|c_q|\le1\) on
\(Q\le q<2Q\), let \(G>0\), and put \(H_P=H_T/G\).  For every
dyadic integer \(F\ge1\), let \(|\nu_F(h)|\le\tau_J(|h|)\) on
\(F\le|h|<2F\), let
\[
 |\omega_F|\le C(J_0)\min\{1,(F/H_P)^{-J_0}\}
\]
for every fixed \(J_0\ge1\), and let \(\Psi_F\) be a
fixed-complexity uniformly scaled-smooth projective amplitude of uniformly
bounded norm on the full dyadic rectangle in \(q,h,v,p_1,p_2\).

Define \(T_{C2_*}\) with literal prefactor \(H_P^{-1}\), summed over
all \(F,q,h,v\) and distinct ordered primes
\[
 P_i\le p_i<2P_i,qquad p_i\ge Z_*,qquad p_1<p_2,
\]
with \((vp_1p_2,q)=1\), coefficient
\(\omega_Fc_q\nu_F(h)\xi_v\Psi_F\), and phase
\[
 e_q(Ah(vp_1p_2)^{-1}).                                            \tag{3}
\]
There is no sharp product mask; (1) is a dyadic scale relation.  Refine
prime cells so that either \(P_2\ge2P_1\), when order is automatic, or
\(P_1=P_2\), when the full coefficient and amplitude before imposing
\(p_1<p_2\) are symmetric in the two primes.

If \(G\ge1\), then
\[
 T_{C2_*}\ll GQ^{2-\delta_{C2,F}}.                               \tag{4}
\]
If \(0<\eta<\sigma\) and
\(Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\le G\le Q^{\sigma-\eta}\), then
\[
 T_{C2_*}\ll Q^{2-\delta_{C2,N}}.                                \tag{5}
\]
The fixed savings and constants depend only on the fixed parameters,
divisor orders and projective norm.  They include \(H_P<1\), all actual
frequencies, both scale orderings, equal cells and the repeated-prime
diagonal created by exact symmetrization.  Legal one-variable,
label-scalar and bounded-projective factors are permitted; arbitrary joint
masks are not.  Taking \(\xi_v=\mu(v)\) gives the abstract
\(C2_*\) marker coefficient.  No literal-source, outer-\(g\), selected
diagonal, PMD, DCE, or Goldbach claim is made.
4d2585a7863f65b6.proof:
Fixed dyadic constants contribute \(O(1/\log Q)\); all windows
below have fixed \(\sigma\)-margins.  Thus write
\[
 \nu+a+b=\beta.                                                   \tag{6}
\]
Put
\[
 \ell=2\beta-2+3\sigma/2,qquad
 r=3-2\beta-3\sigma/2,qquad w=\nu+a.                            \tag{7}
\]
The following three cases are disjoint and exhaustive.

Case 1: \(w\le2\beta-2+2\sigma\).  Group \(v\) and \(p_1\)
into \(s=vp_1\).  Its scale satisfies
\[
 VP_1\le Q^{2\beta-2+2\sigma}\le S_0.                          \tag{8}
\]
The grouped coefficient is divisor-bounded.  Since every prime divisor of
\(v\) is at most \(L<Z_*\le p_2\), and \(p_1\ne p_2\), every
supported \(s\) is coprime to the final prime \(p_2\).  Moreover
\[
 b=\beta-w\ge2-\beta-2\sigma,qquad
 a\le w\le2\beta-2+2\sigma,
\]
so
\[
 b-a\ge4-3\beta-4\sigma\ge2/5+16\sigma/5.                     \tag{9}
\]
Thus the final prime is separated by a fixed power, and fact
\(714b7538b3f03070\) applies to the full rectangle with outer scale
\(VP_1\), final scale \(P_2\), and product scale (1).  It proves both
(4) and (5) in this case.  Equation (9) excludes equal prime-scale cells
from Case 1.

Case 2:
\[
 2\beta-2+2\sigma<w\le3-2\beta-2\sigma.
\]
Choose \(S=VP_1\), \(T=P_2\).  After absorbing dyadic errors,
\[
 Q^\ell\le S\le Q^r.                                           \tag{10}
\]

Case 3: \(w>3-2\beta-2\sigma\).  Choose \(S=P_2\),
\(T=VP_1\).  From \(a\le b\), (2), and (6),
\[
 b\ge(\beta-\nu)/2\ge1-\beta/2-3\sigma/2.
\]
Its margin over \(\ell\) is
\[
 {6-5\beta-6\sigma\over2}\ge3\sigma.                          \tag{11}
\]
Also
\[
 b=\beta-w<3\beta-3+2\sigma,
\]
whose upper margin below \(r\) is
\[
 6-5\beta-7\sigma/2\ge17\sigma/2.                              \tag{12}
\]
Thus (10) holds in Case 3 as well.  In both Cases 2 and 3,
\[
 ST\asymp B=QH_T.                                                  \tag{13}
\]

Projectively expand \(\Psi_F\) and any smooth product localization.
The coefficient on \(S\) is divisor-bounded: in Case 2 it is the
convolution of \(\xi_v\) with the first-prime indicator, and in Case 3
it is the second-prime indicator.  The complementary coefficient is also
divisor-bounded.  The sole joint condition is the complete-product
coprimality required below.

On an actual frequency block put
\[
 u_F=F/H_P,qquad G_F=H_T/F=G/u_F.
\]
Apply fact \(42720f6d803c4640\) with frequency \(F\), scales
\(S,T\), relation (13), and imbalance \(G_F\).  It permits the fixed
possibly nonunit target \(A\) and unrestricted \((h,q)\).  Replacing
its \(F^{-1}\) normalization by \(H_P^{-1}=u_FF^{-1}\) gives
\[
 G^{1/4}u_F^{3/4}Q^2H_T^{1/2}S^{-1/4},
\quad
 G^{1/4}u_F^{3/4}Q^{7/4}H_T^{1/2}S^{1/4},
\]
\[
 u_FQ^2H_TS^{-1/2},qquad u_FQ^{7/4}H_T.                           \tag{14}
\]
Window (10) bounds the four baselines by
\[
 Q^{2-3\sigma/8},quad Q^{2-3\sigma/8},quad
 Q^{2-3\sigma/4},quad Q^{2-1/20-12\sigma/5}.                   \tag{15}
\]
The decay hypothesis gives
\[
 \sum_F|\omega_F|u_F^{3/4+\epsilon}
 +\sum_F|\omega_F|u_F^{1+\epsilon}\ll1.                        \tag{16}
\]
For \(G\ge1\), use \(G^{1/4}\le G\).  In the near-balanced range,
\(G^{1/4}\le Q^{(\sigma-\eta)/4}\), so the first two baselines retain
saving \(\sigma/8+\eta/4\).  This proves (4)-(5) for unrestricted
prime pairs in Cases 2 and 3, including \(H_P<1\).

It remains to impose order in an equal cell.  Symmetry gives exactly
\[
 \sum_{p_1<p_2}\Phi(p_1,p_2)
 ={1\over2}\left(
   \sum_{p_1,p_2}\Phi(p_1,p_2)-\sum_p\Phi(p,p)\right).         \tag{17}
\]
The unrestricted double sum is covered above; Case 1 is impossible by
(9).  The diagonal in (17) is not a source atom and is paid absolutely.
On a block its total is
\[
 \ll Q^\epsilon|\omega_F|u_FQVP_1
 \ll Q^\epsilon|\omega_F|u_FQB/P_2
 \le Q^\epsilon|\omega_F|u_FQB/Z_*.
\]
Since
\[
 QB/Z_*\ll Q^{2\beta-1/2+3\sigma}
 \le Q^{19/10-9\sigma/5},                                       \tag{18}
\]
summing by (16) is power-small relative to \(Q^2\), and hence to
\(GQ^2\) for \(G\ge1\).  Equations (8)-(18) cover every scale
ordering, equal cell and repeated-prime bookkeeping term.  Polylogarithmic
cell and projective-mode counts are absorbed by shrinking the fixed
savings.

glossary.T_C2*: The abstract complete-frequency two-rough-prime trace with cutoff Z_*.
glossary.delta_C2,F: The fixed full-G saving exponent for the endpoint C2_* trace.
glossary.delta_C2,N: The fixed near-balanced saving exponent for the endpoint C2_* trace.

4d26de51cb52d44d.title: EXACT CORRELATION BUDGET FOR CLOSING AN ENVELOPE-WEIGHTED UNIQUE-DILATOR STRATUM. Let \(D\ge2\), let \(R=D^\beta\) with \(\beta>1\), let \(P=D^\theta\), and let \(\sigma>0\). Let \(\mathcal H\) be a complex Hilbert space, let \(X\le D\), and suppose the data \(U_n,\mathcal P,\lambda_{a,m},S,\mathcal C_{\rm off}\) satisfy all hypotheses and definitions of fact 0fd3b33d63081ee3 with this \(X,P\). Let \(r_0\in\mathcal H\) and \(Z\ge1\) satisfy
4d26de51cb52d44d.author: slava chan
4d26de51cb52d44d.statement:
EXACT CORRELATION BUDGET FOR CLOSING AN ENVELOPE-WEIGHTED UNIQUE-DILATOR STRATUM. Let \(D\ge2\), let \(R=D^\beta\) with \(\beta>1\), let \(P=D^\theta\), and let \(\sigma>0\). Let \(\mathcal H\) be a complex Hilbert space, let \(X\le D\), and suppose the data \(U_n,\mathcal P,\lambda_{a,m},S,\mathcal C_{\rm off}\) satisfy all hypotheses and definitions of fact 0fd3b33d63081ee3 with this \(X,P\). Let \(r_0\in\mathcal H\) and \(Z\ge1\) satisfy
\[
 \|U_n\|_{\mathcal H}\le ZR^{1/2}\quad(1\le n\le X),
 \qquad
 \|r_0\|_{\mathcal H}\le ZR^{1/2}. \tag{1}
\]
If
\[
 \theta\ge2(\beta-1)+2\sigma \tag{2}
\]
and
\[
 \mathcal C_{\rm off}
 \le Z^2\frac{P D^{3-2\sigma}}{R}, \tag{3}
\]
then
\[
 |\langle S,r_0\rangle_{\mathcal H}|
 \le 2Z^2D^{2-\sigma}. \tag{4}
\]
Thus, once the diagonal-compatible dilator condition (2) holds, the exact smallest off-diagonal supplier for a \(D^{-\sigma}\) saving relative to \(D^2\) is the correlation budget (3), up to harmless changes of the fixed constant.

glossary.r_0: the Hilbert reconstruction vector for the unique-dilator stratum
glossary.sigma: the desired positive saving exponent on the D scale

4d283c085f098253.title: LITERAL SEPARATED-TWO-GIANT PROJECTIVE FOLDING AND ZHANG-ELIGIBLE FIXED-CELL PAYMENT. Fix A>0 and epsilon>0. Adopt one literal h-row, X,Q_c,delta_h,eta,c_*=c rad(kappa), P_-,H, and the GIANT2D branch of facts edabb9a0d2959b41 and 52e1736c39e88aee. Thus
4d283c085f098253.author: slava chan
4d283c085f098253.statement:
LITERAL SEPARATED-TWO-GIANT PROJECTIVE FOLDING AND ZHANG-ELIGIBLE FIXED-CELL PAYMENT. Fix A>0 and epsilon>0. Adopt one literal h-row, X,Q_c,delta_h,eta,c_*=c rad(kappa), P_-,H, and the GIANT2D branch of facts edabb9a0d2959b41 and 52e1736c39e88aee. Thus
Q_c=X^(1/2+delta_h),quad delta_h>=0,
0<eta<=1/4,quad eta<=3/20+6delta_h,                             (1)
the compatible selected-prime window is nonempty, and
d<=m,quad X^eta<=d<=X^(1/4+eta),quad X<=dm<2X.                (2)
Fix powers of two D_0,M_m,R,P,M_v satisfying
H<=R,qquad 2R<=P.                                               (3)
Restrict to the separated GIANT2D cell
m=a r p,quad P^+(a)<P_-,quad
R<r<=2R,quad P<p<=2P,                                          (4)
where r,p are prime, and to
M_v<v=dar<=2M_v,                                                 (5)
retaining the inherited smooth cells Psi_{D_0}(d)Psi_{M_m}(arp). Assume the cell is nonempty. Then
M_v<=2X/P,qquad PM_vasymp X.                                  (6)

Use the Zhang factor boxes, admissibility conditions (6)-(9), canonical sets cal S_alpha, cal S_Z(P), and count N_Z(P) from fact 487a65cdbb7ab2fc at the present selected-prime scale P. Define the all-selected-primes folded coefficient
Gtilde_s^{2G}(p,v)
 ={1over2}1_{M_v<v<=2M_v}1_{(v,c_*)=1}
  sum_{d r a=v}
  rho_{1/2}(d)rho_{1/2}(a)
  1_{X^eta<=d<=X^(1/4+eta)}
  1_{R<r<=2R, r {m prime}}
  1_{P^+(a)<P_-}
  Psi_{D_0}(d)Psi_{M_m}(arp)
  A_lit(s,kappa,hpv;(ell-kappa hpv)/s),                          (7)
with all other original sampled supports retained, but without imposing (p,c_*)=1. Put
U_s^{2G}(P,R;D_0,M_m,M_v)
 =sum_{P<p<=2P, p {m prime}, (p,c_*)=1}sum_v
 Gtilde_s^{2G}(p,v)
 [1_{pv congruent ell*(kappa h)^(-1) (mod s)}
  -phi(s)^(-1)1_{(pv,s)=1}].                                    (8)

The coefficient (7) has an absolutely and uniformly convergent countable prime/cofactor projective expansion with outer norm
L_proj,2G<<(log x)^(C_2G),                                      (9)
uniform normalized logarithmic prime modes supported on P<p<=2P, and cofactor modes bounded by tau(v). Also
|Gtilde_s^{2G}(p,v)|<=L_W,2G tau(v),qquad
L_W,2G={1over2}L_lit C_{D_0}C_{M_m}.                           (10)
Every prime mode satisfies Maynard's Siegel-Walfisz condition uniformly.

Consequently, with L_log=1+log(2XQ_c),
sum_{s in cal S_Z(P)}|U_s^{2G}(P,R;D_0,M_m,M_v)|
 <<_{A,epsilon}N_Z(P)L_proj,2G X(log X)^(-A)
 +N_Z(P)L_W,2G omega_P(c_*)
 [X P^(-1)L_log^3+Q_c sqrt(X/P)L_log^2].                        (11)
This pays the actual fixed separated-two-giant cell on Zhang-eligible modulus rows, including the explicit p|c_* deletion. There is no Ramaré or diagonal correction. GIANT2D cells with comparable giant scales P<2R, GIANT2S, cells with no admissible factor box, and every other residual sector are not asserted. Under the hypothesis of fact 76092d9557115380, all two-giant cells are empty, so (11) is needed only in the complementary transition chamber.
4d283c085f098253.proof:
From (3)-(4),
r<=2R<=P<p,
so r and p are distinct and p is canonically the larger prime. As in the proof of fact 487a65cdbb7ab2fc, the nonempty compatible window and (1) imply H>d. Thus
p>r>=H>d,
and m=arp>d. The fundamental-domain multiplicity is exactly 2. Fact 5999a1878276ac78 gives
rho_{1/2}(r)=rho_{1/2}(p)=-1/2.
Therefore
2rho_{1/2}(d)rho_{1/2}(a)rho_{1/2}(r)rho_{1/2}(p)
 ={1over2}rho_{1/2}(d)rho_{1/2}(a),                            (12)
which is the coefficient in (7). Since pv=darp=dm, the bracket in (8) is the exact literal centered bracket. This proves that (8) is the actual separated GIANT2D cell, with no selected-prime identity or correction.

The support X<=pv<2X and P<p<=2P gives X/(2P)<v<2X/P. This proves (6).

We next prove the cofactor divisor bound. For fixed v and d|v, there is at most one prime r satisfying
R<r<=2R,quad r|(v/d),quad P^+((v/d)/r)<P_-.                  (13)
Indeed, if distinct r_1,r_2 both satisfied (13), then after removing r_1 the integer (v/d)/r_1 would still be divisible by r_2. But r_2>R>=H>P_-, contradicting the last condition in (13). Hence the number of pairs d,r in (7) is at most tau(v). Fact 5999a1878276ac78 gives |rho_{1/2}|<=1, proving the pointwise bound (10).

For projectivity, use fact 97cfedc76bcae0ad to expand A_lit as a weighted-l1 sum of p^(i tau)v^(i tau). Expand the fixed smooth profile
Psi_{M_m}(arp)=Psi_{M_m}(p(ar))
as
sum_k a_k p^(i sigma_k)(ar)^(i sigma_k),
with weighted l1 coefficient norm bounded absolutely. Since ar=v/d, the cofactor mode is proportional to
1_{M_v<v<=2M_v}v^(i tau)1_{(v,c_*)=1}
 sum_{d r a=v}
 rho_{1/2}(d)rho_{1/2}(a)
 1_{d {m in the HC range}}
 1_{R<r<=2R, r {m prime}}
 1_{P^+(a)<P_-}
 (v/d)^(i sigma)Psi_{D_0}(d).                                   (14)
The uniqueness argument (13) bounds (14), after normalization by max(1,C_{D_0}), by tau(v). Normalizing the combined prime frequency by 1+|tau+sigma| and using the weighted Fourier estimates from fact 2ccb8f56e6084b34 proves (9). Fact 0025283165f465c4 supplies the uniform Siegel-Walfisz property on P<p<=2P.

The literal modulus geometry, nested residue compatibility, canonical injectivity, and every Zhang exponent hypothesis for cal S_Z(P) were proved in fact 487a65cdbb7ab2fc and are unchanged here. Equations (6),(9)-(10) verify the remaining coefficient and cofactor-scale hypotheses of fact 868d2c2698f73b86. Applying that fact box by box and using
Q_{1,alpha}Q_{2,alpha}<2Q_c,qquad M_v<=2X/P,
exactly as in the proof of fact 487a65cdbb7ab2fc, gives (11).

Finally, the scale separation in (3) excludes p=r and fixes which giant prime is selected, so no diagonal or orientation correction occurs. Fact 76092d9557115380 gives the stated independent emptiness condition.

glossary.C_2G: A fixed exponent controlling the separated-two-giant projective norm.
glossary.Gtilde_s^{2G}(p,v): The auxiliary all-selected-primes folded separated-two-giant coefficient on one fixed cell.
glossary.L_W,2G: The reconstructed pointwise divisor-bound constant for the separated-two-giant row.
glossary.L_proj,2G: The l1 projective norm of the separated-two-giant prime/cofactor expansion.
glossary.U_s^{2G}(P,R;D_0,M_m,M_v): The actual prime-unit separated-two-giant centered row on one fixed cell.

4d4b8ff2a3989f8b.title: Let A_B>0 and 0<η≤1. Let B,G,Z_term,Z_comp,U be real numbers satisfying
4d4b8ff2a3989f8b.author: slava chan
4d4b8ff2a3989f8b.statement:
Let A_B>0 and 0<η≤1. Let B,G,Z_term,Z_comp,U be real numbers satisfying
B=G+Z_term+Z_comp,
G=B,
Z_term+Z_comp=0,
and
U=G+Z_comp.
Then B=Z_term+U and the following exact equivalence holds for every real R:
Z_term≤-η A_B+R
if and only if
U≥B+η A_B-R.

Suppose only that B≤-A_B is known. Then the sharp uniform B-independent sufficient lower bound, valid for every such B, is
NONEND-DEFICIT(η,R): U≥-(1-η)A_B-R.
It implies
Z_term≤-η A_B+R.
It is sharp among uniform B-independent thresholds derived solely from B≤-A_B: the maximum of B+ηA_B-R over all B≤-A_B is attained at B=-A_B and equals -(1-η)A_B-R.

Consequently, along an asymptotic family, the exact weakest B-dependent condition for
Z_term≤-ηA_B+o(ηA_B)
is
U≥B+ηA_B-o(ηA_B).
If one uses only the certified inequality B≤-A_B, the sharp uniform B-independent sufficient version is
NONEND-DEFICIT(η): U≥-(1-η)A_B-o(ηA_B).
No two-sided bound for U is needed.

This applies to a sibling-complete negative coarse block from fact 0880dc648c429047 as follows. Put G equal to the genuine coarse von-Mangoldt block B. Split the zero-total composite divisor-sibling families into a chosen terminal union Z_term and its full signed complement Z_comp, retaining one common coefficient across all siblings of each reflected integer. Facts b7fcb27a091203e5 and 25595026334d7350 ensure Z_term+Z_comp=0 when the terminal union is, for example, the intrinsic endpoint sector together with the intrinsic supercritical sector and Z_comp contains all complementary siblings. Then NONEND-DEFICIT(η) forces an η-share of the certified coarse negative magnitude into that endpoint-or-supercritical terminal union. It does not assert a sign for any individual sibling.
4d4b8ff2a3989f8b.proof:
From G=B and Z_term+Z_comp=0,
Z_term+U=Z_term+G+Z_comp=B.
Hence Z_term=B-U. Therefore
Z_term≤-ηA_B+R
is equivalent to
U≥B+ηA_B-R.
This proves the exact equivalence and the exact weakest B-dependent threshold.

Now allow B to range over all real numbers satisfying B≤-A_B. The right side B+ηA_B-R is increasing in B, so its maximum on this half-line occurs at B=-A_B and equals
-A_B+ηA_B-R=-(1-η)A_B-R.
Therefore U≥-(1-η)A_B-R implies the required B-dependent inequality for every permitted B and hence implies Z_term≤-ηA_B+R. Conversely, no smaller uniform lower threshold can work for every B solely from B≤-A_B, because at the boundary value B=-A_B the exact equivalence requires precisely U≥-(1-η)A_B-R. This proves the stated sharp uniform scope.

Taking R=o(ηA_B) gives both asymptotic formulations. A positive excess in U only makes Z_term more negative, so an upper bound for U is irrelevant.

Fact 0880dc648c429047 supplies a fixed-N sibling-complete coarse block B with an explicit negative upper bound. Fact b7fcb27a091203e5 proves that every nonzero large-divisor sibling attached to a non-prime-power reflected integer belongs to a complete zero-total composite family. Fact 25595026334d7350 gives the exact signed partition of such a family into low, medium, endpoint, and supercritical sectors, provided the coefficient is common to all siblings. Choosing any union of those sectors as Z_term and the remaining sectors as Z_comp therefore gives Z_term+Z_comp=0. The preceding algebra applies without assigning a sign to a component sibling.

glossary.A_B: a positive certified magnitude for the negative coarse block B
glossary.B: a sibling-complete negative coarse von-Mangoldt block
glossary.G: the genuine source component, equal to B
glossary.NONEND-DEFICIT(η,R): the sharp uniform B-independent sufficient bound U≥-(1-η)A_B-R
glossary.Z_comp: the full signed complement of Z_term inside the same zero-total composite sibling families
glossary.Z_term: the chosen signed terminal union of zero-total composite sibling sectors
glossary.η: the desired fractional share of A_B routed to the terminal union

4d4bc6711163794c.title: EXACT HILBERT-VALUED FOURIERIZATION OF THE LITERAL SMALL-v PHASE AND ITS ACTIVE-r TENSOR. Let v be a positive integer and C an integer. For s modulo v define
4d4bc6711163794c.author: slava chan
4d4bc6711163794c.statement:
EXACT HILBERT-VALUED FOURIERIZATION OF THE LITERAL SMALL-v PHASE AND ITS ACTIVE-r TENSOR. Let v be a positive integer and C an integer. For s modulo v define

 kappa_{v,C}(s)=v^{-1}sum_{x mod v,gcd(x,v)=1}e_v(Cx^{-1}-sx).        (1)

Then, for every integer q,

 1_{gcd(q,v)=1}e_v(Cq^{-1})
 =sum_{s mod v}kappa_{v,C}(s)e_v(sq),                               (2)

and

 sum_{s mod v}|kappa_{v,C}(s)|^2=phi(v)/v<=1.                       (3)

No coprimality between C and v is required.

Let r be squarefree and coprime to v. Let V_{j,r}(rho), rho=(rho_p) in Omega_r, be one exact active-r tensor Fourier vector from fact 3330e83b6d253b69. Define

 a_rho=sum_{p|r}rho_p(r/p) modulo r.                                (4)

Then chi_rho(q)=e_r(a_rho q), and gcd(a_rho,r)=1. Put

 b_{rho,s}=a_rho v+sr modulo rv.                                    (5)

The map (rho,s) mapsto b_{rho,s} is injective. For every arbitrary complex output multiplier H_j(q),

 H_j(q)1_{gcd(q,v)=1}e_v(Cq^{-1})Phi_{j,r}^{act}(q)
 =H_j(q)sum_{rho in Omega_r}sum_{s mod v}
 V_{j,r}(rho)kappa_{v,C}(s)e_{rv}(b_{rho,s}q).                      (6)

The coefficient tensor before the retained output multiplier H_j has exact squared l2 mass

 sum_{rho,s}|V_{j,r}(rho)kappa_{v,C}(s)|^2
 =[phi(v)/v]product_{p|r}[(p-1)/p-p^{-2}]<=1.                      (7)

For the literal C4 row of fact 3330e83b6d253b69, take v=v_j,
 C congruent Ah_jd_j^{-1} modulo v_j,                               (8)
and
 H_j(q)=D_j^0(q)mu(a_{j,r})/a_{j,r}.                               (9)
Because D_j^0 retains the complete literal source support, including gcd(q,d_jv_j)=1, equation (6) is then exactly the literal product D_{j,r}(q)Phi_{j,r}^{act}(q). Thus the small-v dependence can be kept in a norm-one l2 Hilbert slot even when C is nonunit. In the narrower specialization v=p an odd prime and gcd(C,p)=1, this l2 formulation avoids the sqrt(p) additive l1 tax proved in fact b76df03232475208. The resulting additive frequencies have product modulus rv. This identity does not bound the family across varying r or v, control or remove H_j(q), prove a partner-multiplier large sieve, C4-WTG_r, C4-VEC, another anatomy estimate, or Goldbach.
4d4bc6711163794c.proof:
Let f_{v,C}(x) on Z/vZ equal e_v(Cx^{-1}) on units and zero on nonunits. Equation (1) is its normalized additive Fourier transform. Finite Fourier inversion gives (2), and normalized Parseval gives
 sum_s|kappa_{v,C}(s)|^2=v^{-1}sum_x|f_{v,C}(x)|^2=phi(v)/v,        (10)
proving (3) without a unit hypothesis on C.

Fact 3330e83b6d253b69 gives
 Phi_{j,r}^{act}(q)=sum_{rho in Omega_r}V_{j,r}(rho)chi_rho(q),      (11)
where chi_rho(q)=product_{p|r}e_p(rho_pq). From (4),
 e_r(a_rho q)=e(sum_{p|r}rho_pq/p)=product_{p|r}e_p(rho_pq),        (12)
so (4) gives the correct global character coefficient. Modulo p|r,
 a_rho is congruent to rho_p(r/p), which is nonzero because rho_p and r/p are units modulo p. Hence gcd(a_rho,r)=1.

Since gcd(r,v)=1,
 e_r(a_rho q)e_v(sq)=e_{rv}((a_rho v+sr)q).                        (13)
Multiply (2) and (11), then multiply both sides by the arbitrary H_j(q), to prove (6). If two values in (5) agree modulo rv, reduction modulo r and multiplication by v^{-1} gives a_rho=a_{rho'} modulo r and therefore rho=rho' by (4). Reduction modulo v and multiplication by r^{-1} then gives s=s'. This proves injectivity.

The coefficient in (6) is a tensor product, so its squared l2 mass factors. The kappa factor is (3). The V factor is the diagonal active-r Gram from fact df97bf1eba0495be: comparing the row with itself makes the cross determinant zero, so every local factor is (p-1)/p-p^{-2}. This proves (7).

In the literal row, gcd(d_j,v_j)=1 and the small-v factor is e_{v_j}(Ah_j(qd_j)^{-1}). On the support retained by D_j^0 this equals e_{v_j}(Cq^{-1}) with C as in (8). Fact 3330e83b6d253b69 defines D_{j,r}=D_j^0 e_{v_j}(Ah_j(qd_j)^{-1})mu(a_{j,r})/a_{j,r}; hence choosing (9) makes the left side of (6) exactly D_{j,r}Phi_{j,r}^{act}, including zero extension away from every literal unit and source mask. The qualified comparison with b76 uses precisely its odd-prime and unit-C hypotheses. All remaining scope statements follow from the retained H_j and product modulus in (6).

glossary.a_rho: The global additive frequency sum_{p|r}rho_p(r/p) modulo r corresponding to the product character chi_rho.
glossary.b_{rho,s}: The combined additive frequency a_rho v+sr modulo rv.
glossary.kappa_{v,C}: The normalized additive Fourier transform of the zero-extended inverse phase modulo v.

4ddedcc7bb2b58de.title: Assume the finite labelled-incidence set and its six parent cells from fact 91db48815d136d4c, and suppose one parent cell Z_X is nonempty. Fix an incidence z_0 in Z_X while keeping the entire original incidence set, its partition, and all original source weights w(z) unchanged. Under the hypotheses of fact 676c6a2cb3ebf7cc, the auxiliary conductor/Fourier data do not determine the primitive-moment aggregate T_X from those source data. More precisely:
4ddedcc7bb2b58de.author: slava chan
4ddedcc7bb2b58de.statement:
Assume the finite labelled-incidence set and its six parent cells from fact 91db48815d136d4c, and suppose one parent cell Z_X is nonempty. Fix an incidence z_0 in Z_X while keeping the entire original incidence set, its partition, and all original source weights w(z) unchanged. Under the hypotheses of fact 676c6a2cb3ebf7cc, the auxiliary conductor/Fourier data do not determine the primitive-moment aggregate T_X from those source data. More precisely:

(1) For every complex number xi, there is an allowed choice of the integers q_z>1, finite Fourier sets J_z, Fourier coefficients z_{z,j}, phase labels x_{z,j}, and arbitrary provenance coefficients a_z for which T_X=xi and T_{X'}=0 for every other parent cell X'.

(2) Even if the provenance coefficients are fixed to the original real incidence weights a_z=w(z), there is a one-parameter family of allowed Fourier data for which every T_{X'} with X' different from X is zero and
T_X=w(z_0)|t|^4
for an arbitrary complex parameter t. Since w(z_0) is nonzero by the definition of the labelled-incidence set, |T_X| is unbounded as |t| tends to infinity while the original source incidence set, weights and partition stay fixed.

Consequently facts 91db48815d136d4c and 676c6a2cb3ebf7cc prove exact partition and within-cell centered-conductor provenance only after auxiliary moment data are supplied. They imply no literal identity or nontrivial quantitative bound mapping an original terminal source component to T_X. In particular they do not discharge the component-specific literal primitive-conductor transform hypothesis in facts 4a9a213a428b7e8c or f5b31dd3643732ac. This is a formal interface countermodel inside the freedom of the abstract moment data, not an arithmetic counterexample to a future explicitly defined WF-RPS transform.
4ddedcc7bb2b58de.proof:
Choose q_z=2 for every incidence z. If z is different from z_0, take J_z to be a singleton, set its sole Fourier coefficient to zero, and choose any integer phase label. Then F_{z,2}(a)=0 for the unique unit residue a modulo 2, so P_z(2)=0.

For z_0, take J_{z_0} to be a singleton and set its phase label equal to zero. First set its sole Fourier coefficient equal to 1. The unique unit residue modulo 2 is a=1, and therefore
F_{z_0,2}(1)=1,
P_{z_0}(2)=sum_{a modulo 2,(a,2)=1}|F_{z_0,2}(a)|^4=1.
Set a_{z_0}=xi and set a_z=0 for every z different from z_0. By the definition
T_{X''}=sum_{z in Z_{X''}}a_zP_z(q_z),
one gets T_X=xi and T_{X'}=0 for X' different from X. All these choices are expressly allowed in fact 676c6a2cb3ebf7cc, proving (1).

For (2), keep q_z=2 and the zero Fourier data for z different from z_0, but set a_z=w(z) for every z. Give the sole coefficient at z_0 the value t. Then
F_{z_0,2}(1)=t
and P_{z_0}(2)=|t|^4. Every other primitive moment is zero, so T_X=w(z_0)|t|^4 and all other T_{X'} vanish. Fact 91db48815d136d4c defines the labelled-incidence set using nonzero weights w(z), hence w(z_0) is nonzero. Thus |T_X|=|w(z_0)||t|^4 is unbounded with the source data fixed.

The centered-conductor identity of fact 676c6a2cb3ebf7cc remains valid for every member of these families; it only rewrites each chosen primitive moment in centered quotient-conductor form. It does not relate the freely chosen Fourier coefficients to w(z). Therefore neither that identity nor the parent partition supplies the missing source-to-moment transform. The final scope statement follows because a future arithmetic transform would add explicit relations absent from the abstract hypotheses used here.

glossary.source-to-primitive-moment transform: An explicit relation deriving primitive-conductor Fourier moment data from the original fixed source incidences and weights.
glossary.t: An arbitrary complex Fourier amplitude in the second construction.
glossary.xi: An arbitrary complex target value assigned to T_X in the first construction.
glossary.z_0: A selected labelled incidence in a nonempty parent cell.

4de1331320de4724.title: SHARP POST-RECURSION ROWWISE SQUARE-ROOT AGGREGATION BARRIER
4de1331320de4724.author: slava chan
4de1331320de4724.statement:
SHARP POST-RECURSION ROWWISE SQUARE-ROOT AGGREGATION BARRIER.

Let Q>8, put U=Q^(1/3), and let B=Q^(4/3+o(1)). Let cal A be a set of positive integers contained in [1,2U], let cal B_0 be a finite row set with cardinality at most Q^(o(1))B, and let V_a be nonnegative real numbers satisfying
 V_a<=2Q/aqquad(a in cal A).                               (1)
Let gamma_b be complex numbers with
 sum_{b in cal B_0}|gamma_b|^2=1.                           (2)
Suppose complex row outputs S_b(a) satisfy, for every fixed epsilon>0,
 |S_b(a)|^2<=Q^epsilon V_a                                 (3)
uniformly in a,b. Then
 sum_{a in cal A}
  |sum_{b in cal B_0}overline(gamma_b)S_b(a)|^2
 <=Q^(7/3+epsilon+o(1)).                                   (4)

The power in this deduction is sharp under hypotheses (1)-(3). More precisely, if cal B_0 has R elements, take gamma_b=R^(-1/2) and S_b(a)=V_a^(1/2) for all a,b. Then
 sum_a|sum_b overline(gamma_b)S_b(a)|^2
 =R sum_a V_a.                                             (5)
If R=B up to Q^(o(1)), cal A contains the integers 1<=a<=U, and V_a=Q/a, the right side of (5) is
 Q^(7/3+o(1)).                                              (6)

Consequently, a proof architecture for the TRI-CROSS target Q^(7/3-omega) that uses only a fixed-b square-root bound of the form (3), followed by Cauchy's inequality in the Hilbert-dual b-row, has no fixed power margin. In particular, a pointwise unweighted q-van der Corput estimate applied after fixing b cannot close TRI-CROSS through this aggregation alone, even if it is favorably replaced by the ideal bound (3). This is a sharp no-fit for the stated deduction and an abstract saturator; it is not a lower bound for the literal K_inc^main of fact b9560e346963b9e0 and does not assert that its source rows realize (5).

No TRI-CROSS, ROP, CEN-MZB, C_small or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
4de1331320de4724.proof:
For fixed a, Cauchy's inequality and (2) give
 |sum_b overline(gamma_b)S_b(a)|^2
 <=sum_b|S_b(a)|^2
 <=#cal B_0 Q^epsilon V_a.                                  (7)
By (1),
 sum_{a in cal A}V_a
 <=2Q sum_{1<=a<=2U}1/a
 <=2Q(1+log(2U)).                                           (8)
Since #cal B_0<=Q^(o(1))B and B=Q^(4/3+o(1)), summing (7) and using (8) proves
 Q^epsilon Q^(4/3+o(1))Q log Q
 =Q^(7/3+epsilon+o(1)),
which is (4).

For the displayed example, (2) is immediate. Also |S_b(a)|^2=V_a, so (3) holds with epsilon=0. For each a,
 sum_b overline(gamma_b)S_b(a)
 =R R^(-1/2)V_a^(1/2)
 =R^(1/2)V_a^(1/2).
Squaring and summing gives (5). Under the final choices,
 R sum_{a<=U}V_a
 =BQ sum_{a<=U}1/a
 =Q^(4/3+o(1))Q(log U+O(1))
 =Q^(7/3+o(1)),
proving (6).

Fact 09416be97c36d374 identifies Q^(7/3-omega) as the required TRI-CROSS scale, while fact b9560e346963b9e0 identifies the literal cross-incidence target inside it. Since the abstract example attains the endpoint from hypotheses (1)-(3), those hypotheses and this positive aggregation alone cannot imply a uniform fixed-power improvement. No claim is made about additional signed cross-b structure absent from the example.

glossary.R: the cardinality of the row set in the sharpness example
glossary.S_b(a): the abstract fixed-b row output at short fibre a
glossary.V_a: the allowed squared scale of one fixed-b complementary-variable row
glossary.cal A: the abstract set of common short Vaughan fibres

4ec72320713a9a47.title: EXACT TWO-DILATE PHASE COLLAPSE AND A DIRECT DFI CORRELATION BOUND FOR b-SIDE PRIME EXTRACTION
4ec72320713a9a47.author: slava chan
4ec72320713a9a47.statement:
EXACT TWO-DILATE PHASE COLLAPSE AND A DIRECT DFI CORRELATION BOUND FOR b-SIDE PRIME EXTRACTION.

Let N be a nonzero integer, let p and q be distinct primes, and let a,m be positive integers with (a,pqm)=1. Then
e_{pm}(Na^(-1)) overline(e_{qm}(Na^(-1)))
 =e_{pqm}(N(q-p)a^(-1)).                                    (1)

Let x>=3 and assume A_0,M_0,P_0 are between x^(-C_0) and x^(C_0) for one fixed C_0>0, with A_0,M_0>=2. Let p,q asymp P_0, p!=q, and let alpha_a and gamma_m be arbitrary complex coefficients supported on a asymp A_0 and m asymp M_0. Define
C_{p,q}
 =sum_{a asymp A_0,m asymp M_0;(a,pqm)=1}
   alpha_a gamma_m
   e_{pm}(Na^(-1))overline(e_{qm}(Na^(-1))).                  (2)
For every epsilon>0,
|C_{p,q}|
 <<_{epsilon,C_0}
 ||alpha||_2||gamma||_2 x^epsilon
 { (A_0+P_0^2M_0)^(1/2)
   +(1+|N||q-p|/(A_0P_0^2M_0))^(1/2)
       min(A_0,P_0^2M_0)}.                                   (3)

Put B_0=P_0M_0. At the actual-Z_mid endpoint scales
A_0=x^(1/2+o(1)), B_0=x^(2/3+o(1)), P_0=x^(theta+o(1)),
with 0<=theta<=1/3, |N| asymp x, |alpha_a|,|gamma_m|<=x^(o(1)), and |q-p|<=2P_0, equation (3) gives
|C_{p,q}|<<_epsilon x^(13/12-theta/2+epsilon+o(1)).           (4)
Relative to A_0M_0=x^(7/6-theta+o(1)), this is a gain
x^(-1/12+theta/2+epsilon+o(1)),                               (5)
which is a fixed power when theta<1/6.

This is a fixed ordered prime-pair and one separated cofactor-tensor estimate. It does not supply an exact prime-extraction identity for mu(b), sum over p and q, control of a rough remainder, the very-large-conductor projector of fact 050efa07f87f374a, the complete small-g packet in fact d53bd13f391dd6e4, or Goldbach.
4ec72320713a9a47.proof:
Let a_bar be an inverse of a modulo pqm. Its reduction modulo pm is an inverse of a modulo pm, and its reduction modulo qm is an inverse modulo qm. Therefore
e_{pm}(Na^(-1))=e_{pqm}(Nq a_bar),
overline(e_{qm}(Na^(-1)))=e_{pqm}(-Np a_bar).
Multiplying proves (1). This common-denominator argument requires no coprimality between m and pq.

Set n=pqm. As m runs over its dyadic interval, n runs over a sparse subset of an interval of length comparable to P_0^2M_0. Define delta_{pqm}=gamma_m on this subset and delta_n=0 otherwise. The map m to pqm is injective, so
||delta||_2=||gamma||_2.                                     (6)
Equation (1) turns (2) into
sum_{a,n;(a,n)=1}alpha_a delta_n e_n(Ca^(-1)),
C=N(q-p).                                                     (7)
Because N is nonzero and p!=q, C is nonzero. If C>0, apply DFI Theorem 1 directly to (7), with lengths A_0 and P_0^2M_0 and target C. If C<0, conjugate (7), apply the theorem to |C| and conjugated coefficients, and conjugate back. The original theorem is uniform in its positive integer numerator and has an epsilon factor depending on the two dyadic lengths. Since those lengths are bounded by fixed powers of x, that factor is absorbed into x^epsilon. Together with (6), the theorem gives (3). No additive reciprocity factor or joint smooth weight is used.

For the endpoint calculation,
M_0=B_0/P_0=x^(2/3-theta+o(1)),
P_0^2M_0=P_0B_0=x^(2/3+theta+o(1)).
The two coefficient norms are at most
x^(1/4+o(1)), x^(1/3-theta/2+o(1)).                          (8)
For theta<=1/3, the second term in braces in (3) is x^(1/2+o(1)): A_0<=P_0^2M_0 and
|N||q-p|/(A_0P_0^2M_0)
 <=x^(1+theta-(1/2+2/3+theta)+o(1))
 =x^(-1/6+o(1)).
The first term is
x^(1/3+theta/2+o(1))<=x^(1/2+o(1)).
Multiplying (8) by x^(1/2+o(1)) proves (4). Subtracting
1/2+(2/3-theta)=7/6-theta
from 13/12-theta/2 gives -1/12+theta/2, proving (5).

glossary.C_{p,q}: the fixed ordered two-prime-dilate reciprocal correlation in (2)
glossary.P_0: the dyadic scale of p and q
glossary.delta_n: the sparse coefficient supported at n=pqm

4f2052945785b331.title: Let m be a positive odd integer, let s belong to {1,-1}, and let K,a,b be integers. For a positive integer q define Delta_q(n)=1 if q divides n and Delta_q(n)=0 otherwise. Then
4f2052945785b331.author: slava chan
4f2052945785b331.statement:
Let m be a positive odd integer, let s belong to {1,-1}, and let K,a,b be integers. For a positive integer q define Delta_q(n)=1 if q divides n and Delta_q(n)=0 otherwise. Then
sum_{u modulo m} Delta_{m^2}(ab-K-2smu)=Delta_m(ab-K).                                      (1)
If W_digit is any complex-valued function on the residues modulo m, then
sum_{u modulo m} W_digit(u) Delta_{m^2}(ab-K-2smu)
 =Delta_m(ab-K) W_digit(nu_m(a,b;K,s)),                                                    (2)
where, when m divides ab-K,
nu_m(a,b;K,s)=(2s)^{-1}(ab-K)/m modulo m.                                                  (3)
Here (2s)^{-1} is taken modulo m; the value of nu_m is needed only on the support of Delta_m(ab-K).

Writing e_q(z)=exp(2 pi i z/q), identity (1) also has the exact dual form
m^{-2} sum_{h modulo m^2} e_{m^2}(h(ab-K))
       sum_{u modulo m}e_m(-2shu)
 =m^{-1}sum_{ell modulo m}e_m(ell(ab-K))
 =Delta_m(ab-K).                                                                           (4)
Thus the full unweighted u-sum forces h=m ell and replaces a modulus-m^2 selector by a modulus-m selector. The normalized average m^{-1}sum_u in (1) is m^{-1}Delta_m(ab-K), not Delta_m(ab-K).

If gcd(K,m)=1, then for every fixed u modulo m the congruence
ab=K+2smu modulo m^2
has exactly phi(m^2) ordered solutions (a,b) modulo m^2, all with a and b units. The union over all u modulo m is disjoint and has exactly m phi(m^2) ordered pairs; it is precisely the set of unit pairs satisfying ab=K modulo m.

In the normalized family of fact d90ec957015b32b5, fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb gives v=sm and ab=K+2uv, hence every state satisfies ab=K+2smu exactly. Consequently, an unweighted full residue scan in the normal digit u cannot retain a modulus-m^2 saving: it collapses by (1) to the modulus-m product condition. A nonconstant weight retains the additional digit nu_m through (2). For every fixed delta in (0,3), fact d90ec957015b32b5 already bounds the complete range m<=H^{3-delta} by H^{6-delta+epsilon}; the range left by that fact is exactly
H^{3-delta}<m<=2ceil(LH^3).
The present identities concern the residue digit u modulo m and do not themselves bound that remaining near-maximal range.
4f2052945785b331.proof:
Because m is odd and s is a sign, gcd(2s,m)=1. Suppose first that m^2 divides ab-K-2smu for some residue u modulo m. Reducing modulo m gives m divides ab-K. Conversely, if m divides ab-K, write n=(ab-K)/m. The divisibility condition is equivalent to
n=2su modulo m.
Since 2s is invertible modulo m, this congruence has the unique solution
u=(2s)^{-1}n modulo m.
This proves (1), the definition (3), and the weighted identity (2).

For (4), expand the modulus-m^2 divisibility indicator by additive-character orthogonality:
sum_{u modulo m} Delta_{m^2}(ab-K-2smu)
 =m^{-2}sum_{h modulo m^2}e_{m^2}(h(ab-K))
       sum_{u modulo m}e_m(-2shu).
The inner sum is m when h=0 modulo m and is zero otherwise, again because 2s is invertible modulo m. Write h=m ell for the surviving frequencies. The expression becomes
m^{-1}sum_{ell modulo m}e_m(ell(ab-K)),
which is Delta_m(ab-K) by orthogonality. Dividing (1) by m proves the assertion about the normalized average.

Assume now gcd(K,m)=1. For fixed u, the residue K+2smu is a unit modulo m^2. Every choice of a in the unit group modulo m^2 determines exactly one unit b=(K+2smu)a^{-1} modulo m^2, and every solution arises this way. Hence there are phi(m^2) solutions. The uniqueness of u already proved shows that the solution sets for distinct u are disjoint. Their union therefore has m phi(m^2) elements. On the other hand, for every unit a modulo m^2, the condition ab=K modulo m fixes b modulo m and permits exactly m lifts modulo m^2, all units. This independently gives m phi(m^2) pairs and shows that the union is precisely the modulus-m product graph.

For the normalized-family specialization, fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb gives q=2|v|, v=sq/2, and ab=K+2uv. In the exact stratum q=2m this gives v=sm and hence ab=K+2smu. Applying (1) and (2) proves the asserted conductor collapse and the persistence of a nonconstant digit weight. Finally, the quoted submaximal estimate and the exact complementary interval are the conclusion of fact d90ec957015b32b5. No estimate for the complementary interval is inferred from the elementary identities.

glossary.Delta_q: the divisibility indicator: Delta_q(n)=1 if q divides n and Delta_q(n)=0 otherwise
glossary.W_digit: an arbitrary complex weight on residues modulo m
glossary.nu_m: the unique normal digit modulo m selected by a product ab when m divides ab-K

4f9aec67f5be35db.title: PRIME-LOCAL FOURIER SPECTRUM AT THE FIRST NONRESONANT MARKED-DILATOR PRIME
4f9aec67f5be35db.author: slava chan
4f9aec67f5be35db.statement:
PRIME-LOCAL FOURIER SPECTRUM AT THE FIRST NONRESONANT MARKED-DILATOR PRIME.

[
 e_p(t)=exp(2pi i t/p).
]
For (C

[
 f_C(x)=
  egin{cases}
 e_p(Cx^{-1}),&x
e0,\
 0,&x=0,
 end{cases}
]
and its normalized additive Fourier transform by
[
 widehat f_C(r)={1over p}sum_{xinmathbb F_p}
 f_C(x)e_p(-rx).                                             	ag{1}
]
Then
[
 widehat f_C(0)=-{1over p},                                 	ag{2}
]
[
 |widehat f_C(r)|le {2oversqrt p}qquad(r
e0),            	ag{3}
]
and
[
 sum_{rinmathbb F_p}|widehat f_C(r)|^2={p-1over p}.       	ag{4}
]
Consequently
[
 max_{r
e0}|widehat f_C(r)|
 ge {1oversqrt p}sqrt{1-{1over p}-{1over p^2}},         	ag{5}
]
so the square-root scale in (3) cannot be replaced by a uniform (O(p^{-1})) bound for all nonzero Fourier modes.

Now consider one nonresonant TT-star term from fact (41b56ed8e64bdba6). Thus (d) is squarefree,
[
 Delta=h_1q_2-h_2q_1
e0,qquad d
midmathscr ADelta,
]
and let
[
 p=min{ell:ellmid d, ell
midmathscr ADelta}.
]
Write
[
 d=pm.
]
Then (p
midmathscr A), (p
midDelta), ((p,m)=1), and at least one of (h_1,h_2) is nonzero modulo (p). Choose the least such index (i). The exact (p)-local CRT factor of the TT-star phase contains
[
 e_p(C_iq_i^{-1}),
]
where
[
 C_1=mathscr A h_1v^{-1}m^{-1}pmod p,qquad
 C_2=-mathscr A h_2v^{-1}m^{-1}pmod p
]
according as (i=1) or (i=2). The selected (C_i) is nonzero. Completing the designated (q_i)-coordinate modulo (p) therefore gives the exact Fourier coefficients (1): its zero dual mode gains (p^{-1}), but its nonzero modes have only the square-root bound (3), and some nonzero mode has the square-root lower bound (5).

This is a local transform statement. It does not estimate the literal incomplete (q_i)-sum, sum the mixed modes, or prove NR-DIL. In particular, a global NR-DIL proof may not grant the full factor (p^{-1}) to every mixed dual mode without an additional cross-row argument.
4f9aec67f5be35db.proof:
For (r=0), inversion permutes (mathbb F_p^	imes), so
[
 pwidehat f_C(0)
 =sum_{yinmathbb F_p^	imes}e_p(Cy)=-1,
]
because (C
e0). This proves (2).

Suppose first that (p) is odd. For (r
e0),
[
 pwidehat f_C(r)
 =sum_{xinmathbb F_p^	imes}e_p(-rx+Cx^{-1})
]
is the classical Kloosterman sum (K(-r,C)). The published Weil bound recorded in Covert--Koh--Pi, arXiv:1403.6138, Remark 2.3, in its characteristic-not-two setting, states that for nonzero (a,binmathbb F_p),
[
 left|sum_{xinmathbb F_p^	imes}e_p(ax+bx^{-1})ight|
 le2sqrt p.
]
Since (-r) and (C) are nonzero, division by (p) proves (3) for odd (p).

If (p=2), then (C=1), (f_C(0)=0), and (f_C(1)=-1). Thus
[
 widehat f_C(0)=-1/2,qquad widehat f_C(1)=1/2.
]
This proves (3) directly for (p=2), without invoking the external result.

Normalized Parseval gives
[
 sum_r|widehat f_C(r)|^2
 ={1over p}sum_x|f_C(x)|^2={p-1over p},
]
which is (4). After subtracting the zero-mode energy, the average over the (p-1) nonzero modes is exactly
[
 {((p-1)/p)-p^{-2}over p-1}
 ={p^2-p-1over p^2(p-1)}.
]
Since
[
 {p^2-p-1over p^2(p-1)}
 ge {1over p}left(1-{1over p}-{1over p^2}ight),
]
at least one nonzero mode satisfies (5).

For the TT-star corollary, (p
midmathscr ADelta) implies separately
(p
midmathscr A) and (p
midDelta). If (p) divided both (h_1) and (h_2), then it would divide
(Delta=h_1q_2-h_2q_1), a contradiction. Thus the designated index exists. The supported term has ((q_1q_2v,d)=1), and squarefreeness gives (d=pm) with ((p,m)=1).

For every integer (z), the CRT decomposition is
[
 e_{pm}(z)=e_p(zm^{-1})e_m(zp^{-1}),                         	ag{6}
]
where the inverses are taken in the displayed moduli. Apply (6) to
[
 z=mathscr ADelta(q_1q_2v)^{-1}pmod d.
]
The (p)-local factor is
[
 e_p!left(mathscr ADelta(q_1q_2v)^{-1}m^{-1}ight)
 =
