]
The designated factor is (f_{C_i}(q_i)) with the displayed (C_i). All factors in (C_i) are units modulo (p), including (h_i) by designation, so (C_i
e0). Fourier inversion using (1) proves the completion assertion. The final limitations record that this prime-local identity does not control the remaining variables or the sum of nonzero modes.

glossary.designated NR coordinate: The least TT-star coordinate whose frequency is nonzero modulo the first nonresonant prime.
glossary.f_C: The zero-extended inverse additive phase on the prime field.

4ffcbb6426f230cc.title: EXACT LITERAL SUPPLIER FOR THE CRITICAL PASCADI MN TERM. Assume the hypotheses and notation of facts bc591aa66c8b299b and 7264046d8776d59f. Define the residue mean
4ffcbb6426f230cc.author: slava chan
4ffcbb6426f230cc.statement:
EXACT LITERAL SUPPLIER FOR THE CRITICAL PASCADI MN TERM. Assume the hypotheses and notation of facts bc591aa66c8b299b and 7264046d8776d59f. Define the residue mean
bar H_{S,bold t}=S^{-1}sum_{a mod S}H_{S,bold t}(a).                       (1)
For a finite family cal S of active total moduli and epsilon>0 define
cal L_MN(epsilon;cal S)=sum_{S in cal S}S^epsilon integral_{R^2}sum_{z mod S}|H_{S,bold t}(z)-bar H_{S,bold t}|d bold t.                     (2)
Let cal K_S be centered critical intervals satisfying |cal K_S|<=C_0S/M_0. After the S^{-2} TMC normalization, the sum over S and bold t of the explicit SK_0/MN term on the right side of Pascadi's frequency-concentration estimate in fact bc591aa66c8b299b is
<<_{chi,C_0,epsilon}cal L_MN(epsilon;cal S).                              (3)
Consequently, for every A>0, the literal source estimate
cal L_MN(epsilon;cal S)<<xD(log x)^{-A}                                  (MN-L1-SUPPLIER_A)
pays the complete critical Pascadi MN contribution at the same target. The oscillation in (2) contains the exact q_1,q_2,h/Mobius row, actual Mellin average, moving source masks, and CRT translations. Through fact 16c145000d211540 it is explicitly a centered two-reflected-form Perron-Euler row. This is the first missing arithmetic input for the published MN term; no estimate MN-L1-SUPPLIER_A is asserted, and paying this term alone does not estimate the separate frequency-concentration T-term in Pascadi's theorem.
4ffcbb6426f230cc.proof:
Equation (5) of fact bc591aa66c8b299b states that at fixed S and bold t, after the TMC normalization, Pascadi's explicit SK_0 term is
<<_{chi,epsilon}S^epsilon(K_0M_0/S^2)sum_{z mod S}|Z_{S,bold t}(z)|.       (4)
The same calculation applies to either ordinary interval composing a centered critical interval. If K_0<=C_0S/M_0, (4) is
<<_{chi,C_0,epsilon}S^epsilon S^{-1}sum_z|Z_{S,bold t}(z)|.               (5)

Equations (4) and (5) of fact 7264046d8776d59f give
Z_{S,bold t}(z)=S H_{S,bold t}(z)-A_{S,bold t}(0),
A_{S,bold t}(0)=sum_{a mod S}H_{S,bold t}(a).
Using (1), this is the pointwise identity
Z_{S,bold t}(z)=S(H_{S,bold t}(z)-bar H_{S,bold t}).                     (6)
Therefore
S^{-1}sum_z|Z_{S,bold t}(z)|=sum_z|H_{S,bold t}(z)-bar H_{S,bold t}|.    (7)
Substitute (7) into (5), integrate in the actual bold t variables, and sum S in cal S. This proves (3). MN-L1-SUPPLIER_A then gives the asserted target bound. Fact 16c145000d211540 is an exact identity for H before the centering in (1), so it proves the stated literal Perron-Euler description without changing (2). The final scope restriction follows because equation (4) of fact bc591aa66c8b299b has a distinct frequency-concentration term in addition to SK_0.

glossary.MN-L1-SUPPLIER_A: the literal arithmetic estimate sufficient to pay Pascadi's critical SK0/MN term
glossary.bar H_{S,bold t}: the residue mean of the literal physical row H at S and bold t
glossary.cal L_MN: the varying-modulus Mellin-averaged l1 oscillation of H in equation (2)

5051635f817e7a22.title: LITERAL FORWARD-REVERSE TWO-ROUGH-PRIME C2 CLOSURE IN THE FIRST POST-LOW-BETA BUFFER
5051635f817e7a22.author: slava chan
5051635f817e7a22.statement:
LITERAL FORWARD-REVERSE TWO-ROUGH-PRIME C2 CLOSURE IN THE FIRST POST-LOW-BETA BUFFER.

Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, beta_0=6/5-2kappa, beta_1=6/5-3sigma, kappa_0=1/200, and fix 0<eta<sigma. Let x>=3 and let N be a positive integer comparable to x. Work with the literal paired nonzero-Poisson source atoms, exact outer-gcd normalization d=ga, r=gb with g=gcd(d,r) dividing N, the unrestricted normalized post-B first-buffer ledger of fact cbfebc160d4bc310, and the complete unrestricted C1 closure of fact efd5ace01f0a6c11.

In the forward orientation assume
R>D, c_1x<=DM<=C_1x,
c_Dx^(1/2)(log x)^(-A_D)<=D<=C_Dx^(1/2),
and R>x^(9/16-kappa_0).
In the reverse orientation assume
D>R, c_1x<=RK<=C_1x,
c_Rx^(1/2)(log x)^(-A_R)<=R<=C_Rx^(1/2),
and D>x^(9/16-kappa_0).
All displayed c_i,C_i are fixed positive constants, A_D,A_R are fixed nonnegative constants, and every physical scale D,M,R,K is at most Cx for a fixed C.

Forward put Q=D/g, B=R/g=Q^beta, G=M/Q, H_T=B/Q, H_P=B/M and L_src=N/g. Reverse put Q=R/g, B=D/g=Q^beta, G=K/Q, H_T=B/Q, H_P=B/K and L_src=N/g. On a normalized C2 atom write the normalized marked factor b=vp_1p_2 forward and a=vp_1p_2 reverse, where v<=S_0=H_T^2Q^(3sigma), every prime divisor of v is at most L=H_TQ^sigma, Z<=p_1<p_2 are distinct primes with Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma), and the exact marker coefficient is mu(v).

Let R_C2,buf be the sum of every normalized C2 atom in either strict orientation for which beta_0<beta<=beta_1, over every actual G>0 and exact outer gcd g dividing N. Include every frozen source phase, parent, fixed-U, high, smooth/projective, Fourier and provenance coordinate. Include all atoms in every inherited target-gcd, rough-prime ordering, equal prime-scale, outer-gcd/rough-prime collision, repeated-prime-diagonal bookkeeping and deletion refinement. The auxiliary refinements and both rough-prime orderings are summed to completion within R_C2,buf before analytic estimation.

Then there is a fixed delta_C2,buf>0 such that
|R_C2,buf|<<x^(1-delta_C2,buf).
No C2 atom, G-range, frequency block, parent, orientation, outer-g layer, ordered/equal prime cell, collision stratum, repeated-prime bookkeeping term, or provenance coordinate in the complete displayed buffer is deleted. The theorem estimates only complete C2 anatomy. It does not select a diagonal C2 cell and does not estimate C3, A/B/C1 above beta_1, later beta, moving actual-Z, endpoints, PMD, DCE, a logical bad-N localization, or Goldbach.
5051635f817e7a22.proof:
Fact cbfebc160d4bc310 gives, for arbitrary N and every retained parent, orientation, actual G, outer gcd and provenance coordinate, the exact unrestricted post-B first-buffer anatomy list
C1,C2,C3.                                                            (1)
Fact efd5ace01f0a6c11 proves a power saving for the complete unrestricted C1 coordinate in exactly this buffer, for all parents, orientations, actual G and outer gcds, after every auxiliary refinement is recombined. Removing that complete disjoint coordinate from (1) leaves the unrestricted exact post-C1 list
C2,C3                                                               (2)
with every other coordinate unchanged. We may therefore select the complete C2 coordinate in (2). This deduction uses no selected fixed-bad-N or fixed-U enlargement.

The normalized marker identity in fact 6414b11506a84ff0 gives uniquely
b=vp_1p_2, mu(b)=mu(v), Z<=p_1<p_2                              (3)
forward, and the same formula with marked factor a in reverse. Every prime divisor of v is at most L<Z, so v,p_1,p_2 are pairwise coprime.

All auxiliary rough-prime order, target-gcd, outer-gcd collision, deletion and provenance refinements are finite disjoint partitions of this complete coefficient by (2). Sum them to completion before estimating. In unequal dyadic prime cells the order is automatic. In an equal prime-scale cell, recombining the two stored rough-prime orientations restores a coefficient and source amplitude symmetric in p_1,p_2: the literal source equation, Mobius coefficient, reciprocal phase and smooth source masks depend on the product p_1p_2, while orientation labels have been summed out. The repeated-prime term is not a source atom; it is exactly the symmetrization subtraction paid inside fact 989b464fc741150b. Thus every ordered and equal cell matches that fact, with xi_v=mu(v).

Fix a forward exact-g layer. The normalized source equation is
am+bk=L_src.                                                         (4)
Since gcd(a,b)=1, it gives
m congruent to L_src a^(-1) modulo b.                               (5)
Poisson summation in m with the literal forward sign convention produces
e_b(L_src h a^(-1)).
Additive reciprocity gives
e_b(L_src h a^(-1))
=e_a(-L_src h b^(-1))e(L_src h/(ab)).                               (6)
Using (3), the reciprocal trace in (6) has modulus a comparable to Q, product vp_1p_2 comparable to B, fixed target -L_src, and no modulus-dependent unit multiplier in the separated-outer Type-I subtrace of fact 989b464fc741150b.

On every actual integer-frequency block F<=|h|<2F, facts df9748efe29ab475 and 0d53c27d174b26ed give the literal prefactor H_P^(-1), a scalar omega_F with arbitrary fixed-order decay in F/H_P, and after extracting it a uniformly bounded projective amplitude in a/Q, |h|/F, v/V, p_1/P_1 and p_2/P_2. The archimedean factor in (6) is included because
L_src/(QM)=N/(DM)=O(1).                                             (7)
The source, fixed-U and dyadic masks are fixed-complexity smooth restrictions; high and parent are frozen label scalars. Every joint auxiliary refinement was recombined before this step. Therefore fact 989b464fc741150b applies to every complete forward C2 cell and includes H_P<1, both prime orderings, equal cells, the repeated-prime diagonal and all Fourier tails.

Forced high gives
Q^(beta-1)=R/D>x^(1/16-kappa_0+o(1)).
Since beta-1<=1/5, Q>=x^c for a fixed c=c(kappa)>0. Also
|L_src|=(N/D)Q<=x^(1/2+o(1))Q<=Q^(C_src)                            (8)
for a fixed C_src, so the target-size hypothesis holds.

Fact 15425579cb248eff proves that every actual forward G<1 lies in
Q^(-sigma+eta)<=G<=Q^(sigma-eta), while every actual G>=1 lies in the full-G regime. Fact 989b464fc741150b therefore gives at fixed g
O(GQ^(2-delta_1))=O((x/g)Q^(-delta_1))                              (9)
when G>=1, because DM=gGQ^2 is comparable to x, and gives
O(Q^(2-delta_2))                                                     (10)
when G<1.

For reverse atoms interchange (d,m,D,M) with (r,k,R,K) and reindex the complete signed frequency family by h to -h, as in fact 65b10e9a052e9479. Now Q=R/g, B=D/g, G=K/Q, the normalized C2 marked factor is a=vp_1p_2, and the reciprocal modulus is b. The verified reverse chart gives the phase
e_b(+L_src h a^(-1)),                                                (11)
so fact 989b464fc741150b applies with target +L_src. Its projective factor is uniform because
L_src/(QK)=N/(RK)=O(1).                                             (12)
The coefficient, symmetrization, target bound and local estimates (9)-(10) are unchanged.

Sum exact outer gcds. In the G>=1 case, Q>=x^c and (9) give
sum_{g|N}(x/g)Q^(-delta_1)<<x^(1-c delta_1+o(1)).                   (13)
In the G<1 case Q=D/g forward and Q=R/g reverse. After decreasing delta_2 below one,
sum_{g|N}(D/g)^(2-delta_2)
<=D^(2-delta_2)sum_{g>=1}g^(-2+delta_2),
with the analogous R bound in reverse. The physical upper bounds D,R<<x^(1/2) make this
O(x^(1-delta_2/3))                                                   (14)
after shrinking the saving. All fixed labels are polylogarithmically numerous. Equations (13)-(14) prove the asserted global saving with no C2 incidence or bookkeeping term omitted.

glossary.R_C2,buf: The complete literal forward and reverse two-rough-prime contribution in the first post-low-beta buffer.
glossary.delta_C2,buf: The fixed global power-saving exponent for the complete C2 buffer.

5084a731a9f78a09.title: Fix real numbers 1/2<a<b<1. Let W be a nonzero nonnegative continuously differentiable real function supported in [a,b]. Let ψ be a continuously differentiable real function on the positive reals such that 0≤ψ≤1, ψ(u)=0 for 0<u≤1, and ψ(u)=1 for u≥2. Let L>0 and B_floor≥0 be arbitrary fixed real numbers
5084a731a9f78a09.author: slava chan
5084a731a9f78a09.statement:
Fix real numbers 1/2<a<b<1. Let W be a nonzero nonnegative continuously differentiable real function supported in [a,b]. Let ψ be a continuously differentiable real function on the positive reals such that 0≤ψ≤1, ψ(u)=0 for 0<u≤1, and ψ(u)=1 for u≥2. Let L>0 and B_floor≥0 be arbitrary fixed real numbers.

There exists a fixed exponent
B_src=B_src(L,B_floor,W,ψ)>B_floor
such that the following holds uniformly as x tends to infinity through values for which N=2x is an even integer. Put
D_*=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B_src),
C_2=∏_{p>2}p(p-2)/(p-1)^2,
𝔠(N)=C_2∏_{p|N,p>2}(p-1)/(p-2),
Q_N=rad(2N),
r_N(n)=1_{gcd(n,Q_N)=1}∏_{p|n,p∤Q_N}(p-1)/(p-2),
and b_N(n)=2𝔠(N)r_N(n).
Then the shallow reflected discrepancy
E_{sh,N}^{B_src}
=Σ_{d,m≥1;d≥2}μ(d)log(m)W(dm/x)
 [1-ψ(d/D_*)][Λ(N-dm)-b_N(dm)]
satisfies
E_{sh,N}^{B_src}≪_{L,W,ψ}𝔠(N)x(log x)^(-L).

For the same fixed B_src, the deep comparison tail
E_{b,N}^{B_src}
=Σ_{d,m≥1;d≥2}μ(d)log(m)W(dm/x)ψ(d/D_*)b_N(dm)
is smaller than 𝔠(N)x times every fixed negative power of log x. Consequently, along sufficiently large even N=2x which are not sums of two primes, the source
H_N^{B_src}
=Σ_{d,m≥1}μ(d)log(m)W(dm/x)ψ(d/D_*)Λ(N-dm)
satisfies
H_N^{B_src}=-c_W𝔠(N)x+o_{W,ψ,B_src}(𝔠(N)x),
where c_W=2∫_0^∞W(u)du>0. Thus the admissible source cutoff exponents are cofinal: an exponent may be chosen above any prescribed fixed floor without losing the same-N bad-source asymptotic.

Choose Φ to be the nonnegative smooth dyadic partition of fact 3ef233e014331fc3. Split the source into its genuine-prime part H_N^{prime,B_src} and its higher-prime-power part. Then, for every ε>0,
H_N^{prime,B_src}=-c_W𝔠(N)x+o(𝔠(N)x),
and the higher-prime-power part is O_{ε,W,ψ}(x^(1/2+ε)).
For positive dyadic D,M,U define
P_N^{B_src}(D,M;U)
=Σ_{d,m≥1,p prime;dm+p=N}μ(d)log(m)log(p)
 W(dm/x)ψ(d/D_*)Φ(d/D)Φ(m/M)Φ(p/U).
Put
J_x=ceil(log_2x)+4,
L_DM=ceil(log_2(16b/a))+1,
L_U=ceil(log_2(4(2-a)/(2-b)))+1.
At most J_xL_DML_U of these blocks are nonzero, and every sufficiently large bad N has a block satisfying
P_N^{B_src}(D,M;U)
≤-c_W𝔠(N)x/(2J_xL_DML_U).
Every incidence of such a block has d≥2, p>x>d, gcd(d,N)=1, and the exact p≡N modulo d normal form of fact d6fd2c2cf8b5d0f0, with D_* formed from this same cofinally chosen B_src.
5084a731a9f78a09.proof:
We make the choice of B_src explicit. Sedunova's maximal Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem, arXiv:1705.06660, in the form reproduced in fact 7a161d479c94ccb0, says that for every T>0 there is B_0(T)>0 such that, whenever
Q≤Y^(1/2)(log Y)^(-B_0(T)),
the sum over q≤Q of the maximum prime-progression discrepancy, maximized over the progression endpoint and over reduced residue classes, is O_T(Y(log Y)^(-T)).

Choose T≥L+4 and then choose
B_src>max(B_floor,B_0(T)+2).
This is a fixed number depending only on the displayed fixed data. For all sufficiently large x,
2D_*=2x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B_src)
≤(2x)^(1/2)(log(2x))^(-B_0(T)).                         (1)
Increasing B_src beyond this choice only decreases D_* and therefore preserves (1).

We reproduce the shallow-discrepancy argument to check every other occurrence of B_src. Put χ_d=1-ψ(d/D_*). Then χ_d=0 for d≥2D_*, and μ(d) restricts d to squarefree integers.

If gcd(d,N)>1, then b_N(dm)=0. A nonzero Λ(N-dm) is a prime power whose underlying prime divides gcd(d,N). For each d there are O(log N) exponents, and every term is O_W((log N)^2). Hence the whole noncoprime contribution is
O_W(D_*(log N)^3)
=O_W(x^(1/2)(log x)^(3-B_src))
=o_L(𝔠(N)x(log x)^(-L)),                              (2)
using 𝔠(N)≥C_2>0 from fact f41f5f91b52e0d13. This estimate remains valid, and improves, when B_src is increased.

Now suppose gcd(d,N)=1. The proof of fact 7a161d479c94ccb0 defines the multiplicative factor R_{N,d} by
r_N(dm)=r_N(d)R_{N,d}(m)
and a squarefree convolution coefficient h_{N,d} such that
R_{N,d}(m)=Σ_{e|m}h_{N,d}(e).
Its exact mean κ_{N,d}=Σ_eh_{N,d}(e)/e satisfies
2𝔠(N)r_N(d)κ_{N,d}=d/φ(d).                            (3)
Moreover, uniformly in d and N,
Σ_e|h_{N,d}(e)|e^(-3/4)≤exp(O((log N)^(1/4)))=N^{o(1)}. (4)
At X=x/d, the weighted Riemann-sum calculation gives
Σ_mR_{N,d}(m)log(m)W(m/X)
=κ_{N,d}X∫_0^∞log(Xu)W(u)du
 +O_W(X^(3/4)N^{o(1)}log x).                           (5)
On d≤2D_* one has
X≥x/(2D_*)=(1/2)x^(1/2)(log x)^(B_src),
so increasing B_src only lengthens this mean-value sum.

After multiplying (5) by 2𝔠(N)r_N(d), using (3), and summing μ(d)χ_d, the aggregate baseline error is, exactly as in fact 7a161d479c94ccb0,
≪𝔠(N)x^(3/4+o(1))Σ_{d≤2D_*}τ(d)d^(-3/4)log x
≪𝔠(N)x^(7/8+o(1))
=o_L(𝔠(N)x(log x)^(-L)).                              (6)
The last displayed upper bound used only D_*≤x^(1/2); a larger B_src makes the actual d-range smaller.

For the reflected prime term at coprime d, partial summation bounds the difference from the normalized main (3) by
O_W(log x) max_{2≤y≤2x}|ψ_AP(y;d,N)-y/φ(d)|.
The residue N modulo d is reduced. Sum over d≤2D_* and apply Sedunova using (1). The result is
O_{T,W}(x(log x)^(-T+1))
=O_{L,W}(𝔠(N)x(log x)^(-L)),                          (7)
again using 𝔠(N)≥C_2. Equations (2), (6), and (7) prove the cofinal shallow estimate.

Fact 0b3642c89b136065 holds for every fixed B≥0 and gives arbitrary logarithmic saving for E_b with B=B_src. Facts 0e9a1691fd933c33 and f41f5f91b52e0d13 give the comparison main and logarithmic normalization uniformly in N, independently of B_src. The exact comparison identity in fact 2679e2cb5e61a245, or equivalently its assembled corollary b0eae7ccb6da25c7, therefore yields
H_N^{B_src}=-c_W𝔠(N)x+o(𝔠(N)x)
on the bad even integers, with precisely this fixed B_src. The d=1 term vanishes because D_*≥1 for sufficiently large x and ψ(1/D_*)=0.

Finally, the higher-prime-power estimate and the one-logarithm block extraction are insensitive to the numerical value of the fixed cutoff exponent. Reproduce the proof of fact d6fd2c2cf8b5d0f0 with B_src: higher prime powers q=r^j, j≥2, number O(x^(1/2+ε)), and for each q the divisor sum over dm=N-q is O_ε(x^ε), so their total is O_ε(x^(1/2+ε)). The remaining prime source has the same negative asymptotic. Dyadic partition in d,m,p is exact. For fixed D, support ax/4≤DM≤4bx permits at most L_DM choices of M, while (2-b)x/2≤U≤2(2-a)x permits at most L_U choices of U; at most J_x values of D occur. Pigeonholing gives the stated block. Since ψ(d/D_*) is nonzero only for d>D_*, the d=1 term vanishes and D>D_*/2. The inequalities p≥(2-b)x>x and d≤dm≤bx<x give p>d and gcd(d,N)=gcd(d,p)=1. Substituting m=(N-p)/d gives the claimed progression normal form with the same B_src.

glossary.B_floor: an arbitrarily prescribed fixed lower bound for the source cutoff exponent
glossary.B_src: the cofinally chosen fixed source cutoff exponent
glossary.H_{N}^{prime,B_src}: the genuine-prime part of the bad-N source formed with cutoff exponent B_src

50ef6972010758a6.title: C-qSRC-MARK-SQUARE: TERMINAL-MARKER SIGNS SQUARE AWAY IN THE COPYWISE CENTERED SOURCE
50ef6972010758a6.author: slava chan
50ef6972010758a6.statement:
C-qSRC-MARK-SQUARE: TERMINAL-MARKER SIGNS SQUARE AWAY IN THE COPYWISE CENTERED SOURCE.

Adopt one exact good-W terminal-marker family and coefficient c_lambda(q,h) from fact e55b27d39c593164. Its scalar marker coefficient is a_lambda(n), independent of q,h. For every copy with a_lambda(n) nonzero and every primitive ray R, define
B_lambda^flat(R)=B_lambda(R)/a_lambda(n),                         (1)
where B_lambda(R) is the complete pre-reciprocity ray coefficient of fact 7e9251670db3e1c9. Then
B_lambda(R)=a_lambda(n)B_lambda^flat(R),                         (2)
and every copywise ray-pair coefficient in P-qSRC or C-qSRC>=2 is
B_lambda(R)conjugate(B_lambda(R'))
 =|a_lambda(n)|^2
  B_lambda^flat(R)conjugate(B_lambda^flat(R')).                  (C-qSRC-MARK-SQUARE)

In particular, on every C_j copy of fact e55b27d39c593164,
a_lambda(n)=(-1)^j mu(v_lambda), v_lambda in {1,2},
so
|a_lambda(n)|^2=1.                                              (3)
Thus the alternating C_j marker sign is absent from the copywise quadratic source before the residue and dilator transposes of facts d5cfc4a905989cc8 and eb01e7b374521a0c.

Consequently the exact linear terminal-marker recombination that restores the pre-marker factor mu(n) cannot be inserted into C-qSRC>=2 after the copywise moment has been formed. A marker-based proof of the aggregate dilator- or n-variation must either operate before the first copywise Cauchy/moment step, or establish a new cross-copy identity that supplies the missing lambda!=lambda' terms. The algebraic obstruction is sharp for an abstract two-copy profile: marker coefficients 1 and -1 with identical flat row X have linear sum X-X=0, while their copywise quadratic sum is |X|^2+|-X|^2=2|X|^2. This example is not asserted to occur in the literal source.

This theorem proves only the exact marker factorization and scoped method no-fit. It proves no lower bound for the literal centered source, no failure of a pre-Cauchy recombination, no C-qSRC-BV-SUP, no C-qSRC-SUP, no tail payment, and no Goldbach conclusion.
50ef6972010758a6.proof:
Equation (9) of fact e55b27d39c593164 is
c_lambda(q,h)
 =a_lambda(n) mu(q)(H_P/n)
  Fhat_{q,n}(epsilon_or h/n)
  e(epsilon_or mathscr A h/(qn))
  Xi_lambda(q,h,n).                                             (4)
For fixed n and lambda, a_lambda(n) is independent of q and h. The primitive-ray coefficient is the finite sum
B_lambda(R)
 =sum_{k:c_lambda(ka,epsilon kb) nonzero}
   c_lambda(ka,epsilon kb).                                    (5)
Extracting a_lambda(n) from (5) proves (2), with (1) defining the remaining literal flat coefficient and retaining every other factor and mask.

Both P-qSRC and C-qSRC>=2 in fact e9e9563501147a1a pair two rays inside the same exact copy lambda. Substitute (2) for both ray coefficients:
B_lambda(R)conjugate(B_lambda(R'))
 =a_lambda(n)conjugate(a_lambda(n))
  B_lambda^flat(R)conjugate(B_lambda^flat(R')),
which proves C-qSRC-MARK-SQUARE.

Fact e55b27d39c593164 states that a C_j copy has
n=v_lambda p_1...p_j,
v_lambda in {1,2},
and marker weight
a_lambda(n)=(-1)^j mu(v_lambda).
Both possible v_lambda are squarefree, so |mu(v_lambda)|=1. This proves (3).

The terminal-marker identity in that fact is linear in the marker coefficients: it reconstructs the pre-marker mu(n) before the new copies are treated separately. C-qSRC-MARK-SQUARE shows that the copywise quadratic form contains |a_lambda(n)|^2 instead. In general there is no identity replacing a sum of squared coefficients by the square or linear sum of the coefficients without cross-copy terms. The displayed two-copy calculation proves this algebraically and establishes only the claimed method no-fit. All exclusions follow.

glossary.B_lambda^flat(R): The complete primitive-ray coefficient with the scalar terminal-marker coefficient a_lambda(n) removed.
glossary.C-qSRC-MARK-SQUARE: The exact cancellation of the terminal-marker sign inside each same-copy ray-pair coefficient.

512b50816bb8e5ef.title: FINITE TRUNCATED DIRICHLET-INVERSE IDENTITY AND EXACT NO-SUBSET ANATOMY
512b50816bb8e5ef.author: slava chan

glossary.HB-nonsplittable representation: A representation satisfying both the no-clean-subset condition and all single-free-variable complement lower bounds.
glossary.M_z: The truncated Möbius function M_z(d)=mu(d) for d<=z and zero otherwise.
glossary.P: An inclusion-maximal subset product of maximal numerical value among subset products at most Q^b.

512ccc143b3d5fd9.title: MEDIUM-PRIME RAMARE DECOMPOSITION OF A CENTERED MOBIUS PROGRESSION, WITH THE EXACT SQUAREFUL CORRECTION. Let B>=4, P>=2, Q_0>=1 and L>=0 be real numbers, and let c be a positive integer. Put
512ccc143b3d5fd9.author: slava chan
512ccc143b3d5fd9.statement:
MEDIUM-PRIME RAMARE DECOMPOSITION OF A CENTERED MOBIUS PROGRESSION, WITH THE EXACT SQUAREFUL CORRECTION. Let B>=4, P>=2, Q_0>=1 and L>=0 be real numbers, and let c be a positive integer. Put
cal P={p prime:P<=p<2P},  omega_P(n)=#{p in cal P:p divides n},
and
b_{P,c}(m)=mu(m)1_{(m,c)=1}/(1+omega_P(m)).                       (1)
Let cal D be any finite set of squarefree positive integers d in [Q_0,2Q_0). For each d in cal D choose an integer a_d with (a_d,d)=1 and a complex function V_d on the positive integers which vanishes outside [B,2B) and satisfies |V_d(n)|<=L.

Define
D_d^{med}
=sum_{n>=1}mu(n)1_{(n,c)=1}1_{omega_P(n)>0}V_d(n)
 [1_{n congruent a_d (mod d)}-1_{(n,d)=1}/phi(d)],               (2)
T_d
=-sum_{p in cal P,(p,c)=1}sum_{m>=1}b_{P,c}(m)V_d(pm)
 [1_{pm congruent a_d (mod d)}-1_{(pm,d)=1}/phi(d)],             (3)
and
E_d
=sum_{p in cal P,(p,c)=1}sum_{m>=1,p divides m}b_{P,c}(m)V_d(pm)
 [1_{pm congruent a_d (mod d)}-1_{(pm,d)=1}/phi(d)].             (4)
Then, for every d in cal D,
D_d^{med}=T_d+E_d.                                                (5)
Moreover
sum_{d in cal D}|E_d|
 << L(1+log(2BQ_0))^2(B/P+Q_0P),                                 (6)
with an absolute implied constant.

Thus the medium-prime part of a centered Mobius progression is exactly an unrestricted prime-by-Mobius bilinear discrepancy, in which the prime factor is a Siegel-Walfisz candidate, plus the explicitly bounded squareful correction. In particular, whenever
P>=(log(2BQ_0))^{A+3},  Q_0P<=B(log(2BQ_0))^{-A-3},               (7)
equation (6) is
sum_{d in cal D}|E_d|<<_A LB(log(2BQ_0))^{-A}.                    (8)
No estimate for T_d is asserted.
512ccc143b3d5fd9.proof:
If mu(n) is nonzero, then n is squarefree. For such an n with omega_P(n)>0, every p in cal P dividing n occurs exactly once. Writing n=pm gives (p,m)=1,
mu(m)=-mu(n), and
1+omega_P(m)=omega_P(n).
Consequently
mu(n)1_{omega_P(n)>0}
=-sum_{p in cal P, p divides n} mu(n/p)/(1+omega_P(n/p))
=-sum_{substack{p in cal P,m>=1\\pm=n,(p,m)=1}} mu(m)/(1+omega_P(m)).       (9)
If additionally (n,c)=1, then (p,c)=(m,c)=1. Conversely every pair in the last sum with (p,m)=1, (p,c)=1 and (m,c)=1 has pm squarefree whenever mu(m) is nonzero, and (9) supplies its correct coefficient. Multiply (9) by
V_d(n)[1_{n congruent a_d (mod d)}-1_{(n,d)=1}/phi(d)]
and sum n. Absolute convergence is finite because V_d is supported on [B,2B). This gives
D_d^{med}
=-sum_{p in cal P,(p,c)=1}sum_{substack{m>=1\\(p,m)=1}}
 b_{P,c}(m)V_d(pm)
 [1_{pm congruent a_d (mod d)}-1_{(pm,d)=1}/phi(d)].              (10)
Splitting the unrestricted sum in (3) into (p,m)=1 and p divides m shows directly that its coprime part is (10), while its p-divides-m part is the negative of (4). Hence (5).

It remains to prove (6). Since |b_{P,c}(m)|<=1 and |V_d(pm)|<=L, the absolute value of (4) is at most L times the sum of its physical and principal counting terms. In the p-divides-m part write m=pu. Support of V_d(p^2u) forces B<=p^2u<2B.

For the physical term, if p divides d there are no solutions to p^2u congruent a_d modulo d because (a_d,d)=1. If (p,d)=1, this congruence fixes one residue class of u modulo d. Its intersection with B/p^2<=u<2B/p^2 has at most 2B/(p^2d)+1 integers. Since p>=P and cal P contains at most 2P integers, for each d the physical count is at most
4B/(Pd)+2P.                                                      (11)
There are at most 2Q_0 integers in [Q_0,2Q_0), and
sum_{d in cal D}1/d<=2.
Summing (11) over d gives
sum_{d in cal D}(physical count)<<B/P+Q_0P.                       (12)

For the principal term, before the coprimality deletion there are at most 2B/p^2+1 possible u for each p. Hence the count for a fixed d, including the factor 1/phi(d), is at most
phi(d)^{-1}(4B/P+2P).                                            (13)
For squarefree d,
d/phi(d)=product_{p divides d}(1-1/p)^{-1}
<=product_{p divides d}(1+2/p)
<=product_{p divides d}(1+1/p)^2
=[sum_{r divides d}1/r]^2
<=(1+log d)^2.                                                    (14)
Here (1-1/p)^{-1}<=1+2/p for every prime p, and the final inequality follows from sum_{r divides d}1/r<=sum_{1<=r<=d}1/r<=1+log d. Since d>=Q_0 and #cal D<=2Q_0, (13)-(14) give
sum_{d in cal D}(principal count)
<< (1+log(2Q_0))^2(B/P+P).                                      (15)
Multiplying (12) and (15) by L, and using P<=Q_0P and 1+log(2Q_0)<=1+log(2BQ_0), proves (6). Under (7), each of B/P and Q_0P is at most B(log(2BQ_0))^{-A-3}; multiplying by the logarithmic square in (6) gives (8).

glossary.D_d^{med}: The centered d-progression discrepancy restricted to integers having a prime factor in cal P.
glossary.E_d: The squareful p-divides-m correction between the exact Ramaré row and the unrestricted bilinear row.
glossary.T_d: The unrestricted prime-by-Mobius bilinear discrepancy produced by the Ramaré decomposition.
glossary.cal P: The dyadic set of primes p with P<=p<2P used in the medium-prime decomposition.
glossary.omega_P(n): The number of distinct prime divisors of n belonging to cal P.

51861749711881ca.title: SMALL-IMBALANCE FIXED-TARGET CORRELATED-ENERGY COROLLARY
51861749711881ca.author: slava chan
51861749711881ca.statement:
SMALL-IMBALANCE FIXED-TARGET CORRELATED-ENERGY COROLLARY.

Fix integers \(J\ge1\), \(C\ge1\), a nonzero integer \(A\), and real numbers \(\tau>0\), \(Q,H,S,T,G\ge1\). For each \(q\) with \(Q\le q<2Q\), choose a unit \(V_q\) modulo \(q\). Let coefficients \(\nu_h,a_s,b_t\) be supported on
\[
 H\le h<2H,\qquad S\le s<2S,\qquad T\le t<2T,
\]
and satisfy
\[
 |\nu_h|\le\tau_J(h),\qquad |a_s|\le\tau_J(s),\qquad
 |b_t|\le\tau_J(t).
\]
Define
\[
 W_q=\sum_{\substack{h,s,t\\(st,q)=1}}
 \nu_ha_sb_t e_q\!\left(AV_qh(st)^{-1}\right). \tag{1}
\]
Assume
\[
 C^{-1}GQH\le ST\le CGQH,\qquad G\le Q^{\tau/8}, \tag{2}
\]
and
\[
 H^2Q^\tau\le S\le\frac{Q^{1-\tau}}{H^2}. \tag{3}
\]
Then, for every \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
 H^{-1}\sum_{Q\le q<2Q}|W_q|
 \ll_{J,C,\tau,\epsilon}(|A|QHST)^\epsilon Q^{2-\tau/8}. \tag{4}
\]
No condition \((A,q)=1\) or \((h,q)=1\) is imposed.
51861749711881ca.proof:
Apply the fixed-target extension in fact \(73fb9efe1286f7e9\). Before the epsilon factor, it gives
\[
 H^{-1}\sum_{q\sim Q}|W_q|
 \ll \frac QH(HT)^{1/2}
 \left(HT+\frac{(HT)^2}{Q}\right)^{1/4}
 (QS^2+S^4)^{1/4}. \tag{5}
\]
From (2),
\[
 T\asymp_C\frac{GQH}{S},\qquad
 HT\asymp_C\frac{GQH^2}{S}. \tag{6}
\]
Expand the two fourth roots in (5). The four resulting terms are
\[
 E_1=G^{3/4}Q^2H^{1/2}S^{-1/4},\qquad
 E_2=G^{3/4}Q^{7/4}H^{1/2}S^{1/4}, \tag{7}
\]
\[
 E_3=GQ^2HS^{-1/2},\qquad
 E_4=GQ^{7/4}H. \tag{8}
\]
The lower and upper inequalities in (3) give
\[
 H^{1/2}S^{-1/4}\le Q^{-\tau/4},\quad
 H^{1/2}S^{1/4}\le Q^{(1-\tau)/4},\quad
 HS^{-1/2}\le Q^{-\tau/2}. \tag{9}
\]
They also imply
\[
 H^4\le Q^{1-2\tau},\qquad
 H\le Q^{1/4-\tau/2}. \tag{10}
\]
Using \(G\le Q^{\tau/8}\), (7)-(10) yield
\[
 E_1,E_2\le
 Q^{2-\tau/4+3\tau/32}=Q^{2-5\tau/32}, \tag{11}
\]
\[
 E_3,E_4\le
 Q^{2-\tau/2+\tau/8}=Q^{2-3\tau/8}. \tag{12}
\]
Every exponent in (11)-(12) is at most \(2-\tau/8\). Restoring the epsilon factor from fact \(73fb9efe1286f7e9\) proves (4). That fact's fixed-target extension explicitly splits \((A,q)\), permits the unit twist \(V_q\), and imposes no coprimality condition on \(h\), proving the final sentence.

glossary.G: The small multiplicative imbalance between ST and QH.
glossary.V_q: An arbitrary unit twist modulo q.

528c091515d833fc.title: Fix an integer J≥1 and a smooth function w supported in [1,2], with all derivatives bounded. Let Q,V,P≥2 be real numbers, put B=VP, and assume
528c091515d833fc.author: slava chan
528c091515d833fc.statement:
Fix an integer J≥1 and a smooth function w supported in [1,2], with all derivatives bounded. Let Q,V,P≥2 be real numbers, put B=VP, and assume
Q≤P,                                                               (1)
B≤Q^(4/3).                                                         (2)
Let (β_v) be complex coefficients supported on V≤v<2V and satisfying |β_v|≤τ_J(v), where τ_J is the J-fold divisor function. For q≥1 write e_q(t)=exp(2πit/q), and interpret the inverse of vp modulo q only when gcd(vp,q)=1. Then for every ε>0,
Σ_{Q≤q<2Q} max_{gcd(a,q)=1}
 |Σ_{V≤v<2V} β_v Σ_{p prime, P≤p<2P, gcd(vp,q)=1}
   w(p/P)e_q(a(vp)^(-1))|
 ≪_{J,w,ε} (QVP)^ε Q^(11/10)B^(4/5).                         (3)
The modulus q need not be prime. The maximum in (3) is taken separately for each q.
528c091515d833fc.proof:
We use two published estimates of Irving, arXiv:1301.6372, in exactly the notation needed here. His Lemma 3.1 says that if 1≤L_1,M_1≤Q and coefficients α_l,γ_m are bounded by 1, then for every fixed integer k≥1,
Σ_{Q≤q<2Q} max_{gcd(a,q)=1}
 |Σ_{l∼L_1,m∼M_1,gcd(lm,q)=1} α_lγ_m e_q(a(lm)^(-1))|
≪_{k,ε}Q^(1+ε)[Q^(1/(2k))L_1^((2k-1)/(2k))M_1^(1/2)
 +L_1^((2k-1)/(2k))M_1].                                    (4)
His Lemma 3.4 says that when γ_m=1, the corresponding Type-I sum satisfies
Σ_{Q≤q<2Q} max_{gcd(a,q)=1}|W_{a,q}|
≪_ε(L_1M_1+Q^(3/2)L_1)Q^ε.                                  (5)
Both results hold for arbitrary integer moduli in the displayed dyadic interval. Fixed divisor-function bounds and a fixed number of smooth or dyadic decompositions cost at most (QVP)^ε, so below we apply (4)-(5) to normalized bounded coefficients and absorb this cost.

We first replace the prime indicator by the von Mangoldt function Λ. The elementary convolution identity
Λ=μ_{≤U}*log-μ_{≤U}*Λ_{≤U}*1+μ_{>U}*Λ_{>U}*1+Λ_{≤U}             (6)
holds for every U≥1. Indeed Λ=μ*log, log=Λ*1, and
μ_{>U}*Λ_{≤U}*1=(μ-μ_{≤U})*Λ_{≤U}*1
=Λ_{≤U}-μ_{≤U}*Λ_{≤U}*1,
because μ*1 is the convolution identity. We take U=P^(1/3). On n∼P the last term of (6) vanishes. Dyadic decomposition of the other three terms gives Type-I sums with a coefficient variable l≤U and a free complementary variable, and Type-II sums in which both factors exceed U. A Type-I block with U<l≤U² may be treated as Type II, because both l and its complementary factor are then at least U. Thus in every Type-II block the shorter Vaughan factor s satisfies
U≤s≤P^(1/2),                                                   (7)
and the other factor has length comparable to P/s.

Combine the v-variable with the longer Vaughan factor. The resulting two Type-II lengths are
A=B/s,   C=s.                                                   (8)
They are legal in (4). Indeed C≤P^(1/2)≤B^(1/2)≤Q^(2/3)<Q. Also V=B/P≤B/Q by (1), and (7) gives
A≤B/P^(1/3)=B^(2/3)V^(1/3)≤B Q^(-1/3)≤Q
by (2).

Apply (4) first with k=3 and then with k=2, taking L_1=A and M_1=C. Apart from the common harmless factor, the respective bounds are
Q^(7/6)B^(5/6)s^(-1/3)+QB^(5/6)s^(1/6),                      (9)
Q^(5/4)B^(3/4)s^(-1/4)+QB^(3/4)s^(1/4).                      (10)
Because P≥Q, (7) begins at s≥Q^(1/3). Up to s=Q^(1/2), the increasing second term of (9) and the decreasing first term of (10) cross at
s_0=(Q³/B)^(1/5),                                             (11)
and their common value is
Q^(11/10)B^(4/5).                                             (12)
If s_0 is outside the actual interval, monotonicity makes the bound at the nearest endpoint no larger than the formal value (12). For s≥Q^(1/2), use the second term of (10); by (7) it is at most
QB^(3/4)P^(1/8)=QB^(7/8)V^(-1/8)≤QB^(7/8).
Condition (2) implies QB^(7/8)≤Q^(11/10)B^(4/5). Hence all Type-II blocks satisfy (12), up to (QVP)^ε.

For Type I, combine v with the coefficient variable l≤U. Its length is at most
VU=VP^(1/3)=B^(1/3)V^(2/3).
The product of the two Type-I lengths is B. Formula (5), with partial summation for a possible logarithm on the free variable, gives
B+Q^(3/2)B^(1/3)V^(2/3).                                     (13)
Since V≤B/Q and B≤Q^(4/3), the second term in (13) is at most
Q^(5/6)B≤Q^(11/10)B^(4/5);
the first term is smaller as well. Thus the Λ-weighted prime trace obeys (3).

Finally, Λ includes prime powers. There are O(P^(1/2)) proper prime powers in [P,2P], each logarithm is O(log P), and the v-sum has O(V) terms up to a divisor-function factor. Their contribution after summing the Q moduli is
≪(QVP)^ε QVP^(1/2)= (QVP)^ε QB^(1/2)V^(1/2)
≤(QVP)^ε Q^(1/2)B,
where V≤B/Q was used. This is at most the right side of (3) under (2). Removing the logarithmic prime weight and inserting w by partial summation costs only another logarithmic factor, absorbed by (QVP)^ε. This proves (3).

glossary.J: The fixed order of the divisor-function bound on β_v.
glossary.L_1: The first length in Irving's bilinear trace.
glossary.M_1: The second length in Irving's bilinear trace.
glossary.V: The dyadic scale of the auxiliary variable v.
glossary.s: The shorter factor in a Vaughan Type-II block.
glossary.w: The fixed smooth weight on the prime variable.
glossary.Λ_{>U}: The von Mangoldt function restricted to positive integers greater than U.
glossary.Λ_{≤U}: The von Mangoldt function restricted to positive integers at most U.
glossary.α_l: A bounded coefficient in Irving's Type-II estimate.
glossary.γ_m: The second bounded coefficient in Irving's Type-II estimate.
glossary.μ_{>U}: The Möbius function restricted to positive integers greater than U.
glossary.μ_{≤U}: The Möbius function restricted to positive integers at most U.

52e1736c39e88aee.title: MAXIMAL COMPATIBLE-SCALE CLASSIFICATION OF THE MULTISCALE-UNMARKED LARGE HC FACTOR. Fix A>0 and C=C(A,2)>0, and adopt X,delta_h,eta and the HC-MED support of fact f702d90f3491c7c0. Put
52e1736c39e88aee.author: slava chan
52e1736c39e88aee.statement:
MAXIMAL COMPATIBLE-SCALE CLASSIFICATION OF THE MULTISCALE-UNMARKED LARGE HC FACTOR. Fix A>0 and C=C(A,2)>0, and adopt X,delta_h,eta and the HC-MED support of fact f702d90f3491c7c0. Put
L_P=X^(2/5+6delta_h)(log X)^(2C),qquad
U_P=X^(1/2-3delta_h)(log X)^(-C).                               (1)
Assume that there is at least one power of two P with L_P<=P<=U_P. Let P_- be the least power of two not smaller than L_P, let P_+ be the greatest power of two not larger than U_P, and take the consecutive multiscale family
P_j=2^(j-1)P_- quad (1<=j<=J),qquad P_J=P_+.                 (2)
Thus its selected-prime intervals are the disjoint half-open intervals
[P_j,2P_j), and their union is exactly [P_-,2P_+).              (3)
Put H=2P_+.

If (s,m) lies in MS-UNMARK of fact f702d90f3491c7c0 for the family (2), then m has a unique factorization
m=a b,qquad (a,b)=1,                                           (4)
such that every prime divisor of a is smaller than P_- and every prime divisor of b is at least H. Moreover
Omega(b)<=2,                                                     (5)
where Omega counts prime factors with multiplicity. Consequently exactly one of the following four disjoint alternatives holds:
SMOOTH: b=1;
GIANT1: b=p with p prime and p>=H;
GIANT2D: b=p_1p_2 with distinct primes H<=p_1<p_2;
GIANT2S: b=p^2 with p prime and p>=H.                            (6)
For the fractional-Mobius coefficient of fact 5999a1878276ac78,
rho_{1/2}(m)=rho_{1/2}(a),quad
-1/2 rho_{1/2}(a),quad
1/4 rho_{1/2}(a),quad
-1/8 rho_{1/2}(a),                                               (7)
in the four respective alternatives of (6).

Thus the exact MS-UNMARK residual in the maximal consecutive compatible-scale family is a P_--smooth branch plus one- and two-very-large-prime branches; it is not an unspecified omega_P=0 set. No estimate for any branch in (6), for MS-FIRST-NOSCALE, or for any other HC or critical sector is asserted.
52e1736c39e88aee.proof:
The definitions of P_- and P_+ and the existence hypothesis imply P_-<=P_+. Consecutive doubling makes the half-open intervals
[P_-,2P_-),[2P_-,4P_-),...,[P_+,2P_+)
pairwise disjoint and gives their union (3).

By definition of MS-UNMARK in fact f702d90f3491c7c0, no prime divisor of m lies in any selected interval, hence no prime divisor lies in [P_-,H). Define a to be the product, with their full exponents, of the prime powers p^{v_p(m)} with p<P_-, and define b to be the product of the remaining prime powers. Every prime divisor of b is at least H, the two prime sets are disjoint, and ab=m. This proves existence and coprimality in (4). Uniqueness follows because every prime divisor of m lies on exactly one side of the fixed cut.

It remains to prove (5). Since P_+ is the greatest power of two not exceeding U_P, one has P_+>U_P/2 and therefore
H=2P_+>U_P.                                                      (8)
The existence of a power of two between L_P and U_P implies L_P<=U_P, hence
X^(1/10-9delta_h)>=(log X)^(3C).                                (9)
Using (1), (8), and (9),
H^3>U_P^3
 =X^(3/2-9delta_h)(log X)^(-3C)
 =X^(1-eta)
  [X^(2/5+eta)X^(1/10-9delta_h)(log X)^(-3C)]
 >=X^(1-eta)X^(2/5+eta).                                       (10)
For sufficiently large X, the final quantity exceeds 2X^(1-eta). On the HC-MED support,
d>=X^eta,qquad dm<2X,
so
m<2X/d<=2X^(1-eta).                                             (11)
Equations (10)-(11) give H^3>m. If Omega(b)>=3, then b>=H^3 because every prime factor of b, counted with multiplicity, is at least H. This contradicts b<=m. Hence Omega(b)<=2.

A positive integer with all prime factors at least H and Omega at most two is uniquely one of 1, a prime p, a product of two distinct primes ordered increasingly, or a prime square. This proves the disjoint list (6).

Fact 5999a1878276ac78 defines rho_{1/2} multiplicatively, with
rho_{1/2}(p)=-1/2
and
rho_{1/2}(p^2)=(-1)^2 binom(1/2,2)=-1/8.
For distinct primes p_1,p_2, multiplicativity gives
rho_{1/2}(p_1p_2)=rho_{1/2}(p_1)rho_{1/2}(p_2)=1/4.
Since (a,b)=1, rho_{1/2}(m)=rho_{1/2}(a)rho_{1/2}(b), proving (7). No analytic estimate was used.

glossary.GIANT1: The MS-UNMARK branch with exactly one prime factor at least H.
glossary.GIANT2D: The MS-UNMARK branch with two distinct prime factors at least H.
glossary.GIANT2S: The MS-UNMARK branch with one squared prime factor at least H.
glossary.H: The upper endpoint 2P_+ of the maximal consecutive selected-prime union.
glossary.L_P: The lower endpoint of the compatible selected-prime scale window.
glossary.Omega(b): The number of prime factors of b counted with multiplicity.
glossary.P_+: The greatest power-of-two selected-prime scale not above U_P.
glossary.P_-: The least power-of-two selected-prime scale not below L_P.
glossary.SMOOTH: The MS-UNMARK branch with no prime factor at least H.
glossary.U_P: The upper endpoint of the compatible selected-prime scale window.

533ac9e10cc62519.title: CAN-MARK-RANK: A LEGAL SQUAREFREE DYADIC SLICE WITH POLYNOMIALLY LARGE EXACT SEPARATION RANK. Fix a real number eta with 0<eta<=1/4. For every sufficiently large real X there exist real numbers B,Y,Z,P_scale, distinct primes A,L,p_1,...,p_k,r_1,...,r_k, and positive integers D_i,M_j for 1<=i,j<=k with the following properties
533ac9e10cc62519.author: slava chan
533ac9e10cc62519.statement:
CAN-MARK-RANK: A LEGAL SQUAREFREE DYADIC SLICE WITH POLYNOMIALLY LARGE EXACT SEPARATION RANK. Fix a real number eta with 0<eta<=1/4. For every sufficiently large real X there exist real numbers B,Y,Z,P_scale, distinct primes A,L,p_1,...,p_k,r_1,...,r_k, and positive integers D_i,M_j for 1<=i,j<=k with the following properties.

Put Y=B^eta, Z=B^(1/4+eta), D_i=A p_i, and M_j=r_j L. The primes interlace as
p_1<r_1<p_2<r_2<...<p_k<r_k.
Every D_i and M_j is squarefree, gcd(D_i,M_j)=1, all D_i lie in [A P_scale,1.1 A P_scale], all M_j lie in [L P_scale,1.1 L P_scale], and
B<D_iM_j<2B.
For every i,j the least divisor D_med^*(D_iM_j) in the closed interval [Y,Z] exists and
D_med^*(D_iM_j)=A min(p_i,r_j).
Consequently the canonical marker matrix
H_mark(i,j)=1_{D_i=D_med^*(D_iM_j)}
satisfies
H_mark(i,j)=1_{i<=j}.
It has rank k over the complex numbers, and
k >>_eta B^(13eta/16)/log B.

Therefore, if on this slice one has an exact rank-one separation
H_mark(i,j)=sum_{h=1}^R alpha_h(D_i) beta_h(M_j)
with arbitrary complex functions alpha_h,beta_h, then R>=k. In particular no bound R=O((log B)^C_0), for any fixed C_0, can hold uniformly on all legal squarefree dyadic slices. This is an obstruction to exact polylogarithmic rank-one separation of the canonical least-medium-divisor marker; it does not rule out approximation in a specified weaker norm or a different non-rank-one operator treatment.
533ac9e10cc62519.proof:
Set
a=eta/4,  b=13eta/16,  l=1-15eta/8.
Then
a+2b+l=1,
0<a<b<eta,
eta<a+b=17eta/16<eta+1/4,
and
l-(eta+1/4)=3/4-23eta/8>=1/32>0.

Let P_scale=X^b. We use Lemma 2.3 of Pingzhi Yuan, Coefficients of cyclotomic polynomials, arXiv:0909.0995. Its complete statement is: if a_0 and m_0 are coprime natural numbers and pi(x;m_0,a_0) counts primes p<=x with p congruent to a_0 modulo m_0, then pi(x;m_0,a_0) is asymptotic to x/[phi(m_0)log x] as x tends to infinity. Apply it with m_0=a_0=1. Subtracting its asymptotic at x=1.1T and x=T shows that the number of primes in (T,1.1T) is asymptotic to 0.1T/log T. Hence, for all sufficiently large X, choose a prime A in (X^a,1.1X^a), a prime L in (X^l,1.1X^l), and at least 2k distinct primes in (P_scale,1.1P_scale), where k>>_eta P_scale/log P_scale. Put those last primes in increasing order and name them
p_1,r_1,p_2,r_2,...,p_k,r_k.
The exponent inequalities a<b<l show that for large X all these primes are mutually distinct.

Define B=A L P_scale^2. Since A is between X^a and 1.1X^a, L is between X^l and 1.1X^l, and a+2b+l=1, one has
X<B<1.21X.
For every i,j,
D_iM_j=A L p_i r_j.
Because p_i,r_j>P_scale, this is greater than B. Because p_i,r_j<1.1P_scale, it is less than 1.21B<2B. The claimed fixed-ratio row and column slices follow directly from the same inequalities. Each product has the four distinct prime factors A,p_i,r_j,L, so D_i,M_j and D_iM_j are squarefree and gcd(D_i,M_j)=1.

We next compare the prime factors with Y and Z. Since B is between X and 1.21X, every fixed strict exponent inequality below dominates the constant 1.21 for sufficiently large X. From a,b<eta, one obtains A,p_i,r_j<Y. From a+b>eta, one obtains A p_i>Y and A r_j>Y. From a+b<eta+1/4, one obtains A p_i<Z and A r_j<Z. From l>eta+1/4, one obtains L>Z. Finally b>a gives p_i,r_j>A.

Fix i,j and put n=D_iM_j=A p_i r_j L. Its single-prime divisors A,p_i,r_j are below Y, while L is above Z. The two divisors A p_i and A r_j lie in [Y,Z]. Every divisor containing L is above Z. Among divisors formed from A,p_i,r_j, the only remaining two-prime divisor is p_i r_j; because p_i,r_j>A, one has p_i r_j>A p_i and p_i r_j>A r_j. Every three-prime divisor is larger still. Therefore the least divisor of n in [Y,Z] is exactly min(Ap_i,Ar_j)=A min(p_i,r_j).

It follows that
H_mark(i,j)=1
if and only if Ap_i=A min(p_i,r_j), which, since p_i and r_j are distinct, is equivalent to p_i<r_j. By interlacing, p_i<r_j holds exactly when i<=j. Hence H_mark is upper triangular with every diagonal entry equal to one. Its determinant is one and its rank over the complex numbers is k.

Since P_scale=X^b and B is comparable to X, the prime count gives k>>_eta B^b/log B=B^(13eta/16)/log B. If H_mark is a sum of R rank-one matrices, its rank is at most R, so R>=k. A fixed power of log B is eventually smaller than B^(13eta/16)/log B, proving the asserted no-polylog conclusion. The argument concerns exact matrix equality only, which is why no approximation claim is made.

glossary.D_med^*(n): The least positive divisor of n in the closed interval [Y,Z], when that set of divisors is nonempty.
glossary.H_mark: The canonical least-medium-divisor marker matrix on the constructed row and column slices.
glossary.P_scale: The common real scale X^(13eta/16) of the interlaced primes.

533acf4056cf5bee.title: SMOOTH RAISED-STOPPING TRACE BOUND BELOW ( eta=6/5)
533acf4056cf5bee.author: slava chan

glossary.C_A: A fixed exponent bounding the size of the target integer A.
glossary.Gamma_k: The exact k-prime first-crossing weight at stopping height S_0.
glossary.Psi: A member of a uniformly bounded scaled-smooth amplitude family.
glossary.cal T_{k,U,Y}: A dyadic fixed-k reciprocal trace carrying the exact raised-stopping coefficient.

53737f4b1646ac1c.title: GA-PRIME-SLOPE-SPEC: EXACT HIGH-ROUGH HARD-SLOPE KERNEL AND CHAMBERWISE SOURCE-WEIGHTED FOURIER FACTORIZATION. Adopt the high-rough C setting of fact d92616c2bca6126f, put T=mathscr A, and put L=(log(2x))^C>1. Fix v in {1,2}, a retained C dilator d, and two distinct supported rays
53737f4b1646ac1c.author: slava chan
53737f4b1646ac1c.statement:
GA-PRIME-SLOPE-SPEC: EXACT HIGH-ROUGH HARD-SLOPE KERNEL AND CHAMBERWISE SOURCE-WEIGHTED FOURIER FACTORIZATION. Adopt the high-rough C setting of fact d92616c2bca6126f, put T=mathscr A, and put L=(log(2x))^C>1. Fix v in {1,2}, a retained C dilator d, and two distinct supported rays
R=(epsilon,a,b), R'=(epsilon',a',b').
Write
g=gcd(a,a'), a=g alpha, a'=g beta,
L_0=epsilon b beta-epsilon'b'alpha, Delta_0=gL_0,                (1)
and
rho_d=d/gcd(d,T).                                                (2)
Then gcd(d,aa')=1, hence gcd(rho_d,g)=1, and the exact effective hard conductor is
m_d=rho_d/gcd(rho_d,L_0).                                       (3)
Thus the conjunction m_d>L and the explicit nonresonance deletion is exactly
H_{rho_d,L}(L_0)
 =1_{rho_d/gcd(rho_d,L_0)>L}.                                   (4)
In particular, after the terminal integer and denominator class are frozen, this whole hard pair selector is a periodic function of the slope difference L_0 modulo rho_d.

Assume in addition that the physical conductor m_q is an odd prime p. Use the two disjoint chambers and the unit gamma of fact fd22069145f59332, and put z=dv modulo p.

(I) In the common-core survivor chamber, write g=pg_0. Define
Psi^{core}_{d,v}(ell)
 =1_{gcd(g,T ell)=g_0} H_{rho_d,L}(ell)
  [e_p(-gamma ell z^{-1})+1/(p-1)].                              (5)
Because gcd(g,rho_d)=1 and p divides g, this is periodic modulo
M_core=g rho_d.                                                  (6)
For residues x modulo M_core define the actual incomplete-ray source aggregates
A_{d,v}(x)
 =sum_{supported R=(epsilon,g alpha,b):
       epsilon b beta congruent x (mod M_core)}
   b_{v,R}(dv/B),                                                (7)
B_{d,v}(x)
 =sum_{supported R'=(epsilon',g beta,b'):
       epsilon'b'alpha congruent x (mod M_core)}
   b_{v,R'}(dv/B).                                               (8)
Let Q^{core}_{d,v;p,g_0,alpha,beta} be the exact source-weighted ordered-pair sum over these two ray families with the common-core prime-conductor class, m_d>L, and the centered prime kernel, but before multiplication by any additional inherited pair selector not determined by these displayed arithmetic conditions. Then
Q^{core}_{d,v;p,g_0,alpha,beta}
 =sum_{x,y (mod M_core)}
   Psi^{core}_{d,v}(x-y)A_{d,v}(x)conjugate(B_{d,v}(y)).          (9)
For a function f modulo M define
F_M f(k)=sum_{x (mod M)}f(x)e_M(-kx),                            (10)
and for a difference kernel Psi define
F_M^+Psi(k)=sum_{ell (mod M)}Psi(ell)e_M(k ell).                 (11)
Then the actual weighted block has the exact Fourier factorization
Q^{core}_{d,v;p,g_0,alpha,beta}
 ={1/M_core}sum_{k (mod M_core)}
  F_{M_core}^+Psi^{core}_{d,v}(k)
  F_{M_core}A_{d,v}(k)
  conjugate(F_{M_core}B_{d,v}(k)).                              (12)

(II) In the one-end survivor chamber define the difference mask
Psi^{end}_{d}(ell)
 =1_{g divides T ell}H_{rho_d,L}(ell),                           (13)
and put
M_end=p g rho_d.                                                 (14)
The three factors p,g,rho_d are pairwise coprime. Lift Psi^{end}_d periodically to residues modulo M_end. Define A_{d,v},B_{d,v} as in (7)-(8), now modulo M_end with g in place of pg_0. If p divides alpha, define
A^{tw}_{d,v}(x)
 =[e_p(-gamma x z^{-1})+1/(p-1)]A_{d,v}(x).                     (15)
Then the exact one-end arithmetic block, with the same scope concerning any additional inherited selector, is
Q^{end,L}_{d,v;p,g,alpha,beta}
 =sum_{x,y (mod M_end)}
   Psi^{end}_d(x-y)A^{tw}_{d,v}(x)conjugate(B_{d,v}(y))           (16)
 ={1/M_end}sum_{k (mod M_end)}
   F_{M_end}^+Psi^{end}_d(k)
   F_{M_end}A^{tw}_{d,v}(k)
   conjugate(F_{M_end}B_{d,v}(k)).                              (17)
If p divides beta, define instead
B^{tw}_{d,v}(y)
 =[e_p(-gamma y z^{-1})+1/(p-1)]B_{d,v}(y).                     (18)
Then
Q^{end,R}_{d,v;p,g,alpha,beta}
 =sum_{x,y (mod M_end)}
   Psi^{end}_d(x-y)A_{d,v}(x)conjugate(B^{tw}_{d,v}(y)),         (19)
with the analogous Fourier formula obtained from (17) by replacing A^{tw},B with A,B^{tw}.

Equations (9), (16), and (19) retain the actual moving ray coefficients and the incomplete supported ray sets. They also retain exactly the prime conductor class, numerator, low-d-conductor complement, and nonresonance deletion. Any additional literal pair selector not determined by these arithmetic conditions remains outside the convolution formulas; unless it is itself a function of x-y or a one-end multiplier, it can destroy (12), (17), and (19). Therefore the exact remaining source question is not generic full-ray equidistribution: it is a chamberwise Fourier estimate for the displayed actual source aggregates, together with a proof that every remaining literal selector fits one of these convolution slots or an estimate before that selector is separated.

This theorem proves the exact hard-slope and chamberwise Fourier normal forms only. It proves no estimate for their Fourier sums, no claim that an unspecified additional selector factorizes, no PRIME-PAIR-DISC, prime trace estimate, composite-conductor estimate, C-HILBERT-OP-SUP, tail payment, or Goldbach.
53737f4b1646ac1c.proof:
Every supported coordinate q=ka is coprime to n=dv in the high-rough C chamber. Hence a is coprime to d. The same argument for the second ray gives gcd(a',d)=1, so gcd(aa',d)=1 and therefore gcd(g,rho_d)=1.

By the definition in fact cff9d29efb555b8e,
m_d=rho_d/gcd(rho_d,Delta_0).
Using Delta_0=gL_0 and gcd(rho_d,g)=1 gives (3). Fact 1acbe88cc741c6f1 proves that m_d>L>1 already implies nonresonance, so the conjunction of the hard condition and explicit deletion is exactly (4).

In the common-core chamber, fact fd22069145f59332 gives g=pg_0, the exact class condition gcd(g,TL_0)=g_0, and
K^circ_{p,C_q}(z)
 =e_p(-gamma L_0 z^{-1})+1/(p-1).                               (20)
Multiplying the class indicator, (4), and (20) gives (5). The first indicator is periodic modulo g, the second modulo rho_d, and the phase modulo p. Since p divides g and gcd(g,rho_d)=1, their product is periodic modulo g rho_d, proving (6).

For a left ray and right ray in the frozen denominator class, set
x=epsilon b beta, y=epsilon'b'alpha.
Then L_0=x-y. Group the exact source coefficients by these two residue classes. The condition encoded by (5) vanishes unless the pair is in the common-core prime class and hard range, and on that pair it equals the exact centered kernel. Expanding the grouped sums (7)-(8) therefore gives (9). The class mask vanishes at every inadmissible pair, including any coincident-ray case, so no omitted diagonal correction is introduced.

Fourier inversion with the conventions (10)-(11) gives
Psi(x-y)={1/M}sum_k F_M^+Psi(k)e_M(-k(x-y)).
Insert this into the double sum, separate x and y, and use
sum_x A(x)e_M(-kx)=F_MA(k),
sum_y conjugate(B(y))e_M(ky)=conjugate(F_MB(k)).
This proves (12).

In the one-end chamber, fact fd22069145f59332 gives the exact class condition g divides TL_0 and the hard selector remains (4), proving (13). Here p divides alpha beta while g is coprime to alpha beta, and rho_d is coprime to g alpha beta because d is coprime to aa'. Hence p,g,rho_d are pairwise coprime, proving (14).

If p divides alpha, the same fact gives
K^circ_{p,C_q}(z)
 =e_p(-gamma epsilon b beta z^{-1})+1/(p-1).
Thus with x=epsilon b beta the centered kernel is exactly the multiplier in (15), while the class and hard conditions depend only on x-y through (13). Grouping the actual source coefficients modulo M_end proves (16), and the Fourier-inversion calculation used for (12) proves (17).

If p divides beta, fact fd22069145f59332 gives C_q congruent -gamma epsilon'b'alpha modulo p. Therefore
K^circ_{p,C_q}(z)
 =e_p(+gamma y z^{-1})+1/(p-1)
 =conjugate(e_p(-gamma y z^{-1})+1/(p-1)).
Multiplying B(y) by the expression in (18) places its conjugate in the bilinear form, proving (19) and its Fourier version.

The formulas include precisely the arithmetic indicators displayed in their definitions. Entrywise multiplication by a further arbitrary pair selector is not in general a convolution or a one-end multiplier, so the final limitation is formal and necessary. All exclusions follow.

538182294674b266.title: PRIME SHORT-SUPPORT NO-FIT FOR THE GA-CqADD RAMANUJAN-GRAM NORM
538182294674b266.author: slava chan
538182294674b266.statement:
PRIME SHORT-SUPPORT NO-FIT FOR THE GA-CqADD RAMANUJAN-GRAM NORM.

Adopt the vectors E_{t;n} and source vectors G_gamma of fact 7ee795d9bff04bb2. More generally, let t be a positive squarefree integer and let Z(n) be any finitely supported complex sequence. Put
Q_t(Z)=||sum_n conjugate(Z(n))E_{t;n}||_2^2.                         (1)
Then the exact divisor-congruence decomposition is
Q_t(Z)
 =sum_{s|t} mu(s)/s
  sum_{r (mod t/s)}
  |sum_{n congruent r (mod t/s)}conjugate(Z(n))|^2.                 (2)

Suppose t=p is prime and the support of Z consists of N>=1 integers occupying distinct residue classes modulo p. Then
Q_p(Z)
 =sum_n|Z(n)|^2-(1/p)|sum_n Z(n)|^2.                               (3)
Equivalently, on those N source coordinates the Gram matrix is
I_N-p^{-1}J_N,                                                       (4)
whose eigenvalues are 1 with multiplicity N-1 and 1-N/p with multiplicity one. Consequently
(1-N/p)sum_n|Z(n)|^2
 <=Q_p(Z)
 <=sum_n|Z(n)|^2.                                                    (5)
The lower constant in (5) is sharp for every N: it is attained by every nonzero constant coefficient array on the N supported coordinates. If N>=2, the upper constant is also sharp and is attained by every nonzero coefficient array whose coordinate sum is zero. If N=1, the exact identity is
Q_p(Z)=(1-1/p)|Z|^2,                                                 (5a)
so the optimal lower and upper constants are both 1-1/p.

Apply this to one literal gamma=(p,s,c) row of fact 7ee795d9bff04bb2, with Z=Z_gamma and N=N_gamma the number of its supported physical source values. If N_gamma<=p/2, then
(1/2)sum_n|Z_gamma(n)|^2
 <=||G_gamma||_2^2
 <=sum_n|Z_gamma(n)|^2.                                             (6)
Thus, on every nonzero literal prime-additive-conductor row with N_gamma<=p/2, the signed off-diagonal Ramanujan term cannot provide any fixed-power suppression of ||G_gamma||_2^2 relative to the literal coefficient l2 mass. In particular, for any fixed eta>0, an estimate
||G_gamma||_2^2<=p^{-eta}sum_n|Z_gamma(n)|^2                         (7)
is false on every such nonzero row for all sufficiently large p.

This is a sharp no-fit only for obtaining the large-conductor supplier of fact 7ee795d9bff04bb2 by suppressing each individual source norm through cross-n Ramanujan cancellation. It does not assert that such a literal row is nonzero, give a lower bound for the complete GA block, estimate sum_n|Z_gamma(n)|^2, exclude cancellation between different gamma before Cauchy, or exclude a direct estimate of <V_gamma,G_gamma>. It proves no GA-qCENT estimate, no good-W tail payment, and no Goldbach conclusion.
538182294674b266.proof:
Fact 7ee795d9bff04bb2 proves
<E_{t;n},E_{t;n'}>=c_t(n-n')/t.                                    (8)
For every positive integer t and integer k, the Ramanujan sum has the elementary divisor formula
c_t(k)=sum_{d|t, d|k} d mu(t/d).                                    (9)
Indeed,
c_t(k)=sum_{a (mod t), gcd(a,t)=1}e_t(ak).
Insert the identity
1_{gcd(a,t)=1}=sum_{d|gcd(a,t)}mu(d),
interchange the finite sums, and in the inner additive sum use
sum_{b (mod t/d)}e_{t/d}(bk)=t/d if (t/d)|k and zero otherwise.
Renaming the divisor proves (9).

Divide (9) by t and write s=t/d. This gives
c_t(k)/t
 =sum_{s|t, (t/s)|k}mu(s)/s.                                       (10)
Expand (1) using (8), insert (10), and interchange the finite sums:
Q_t(Z)
 =sum_{s|t}mu(s)/s
  sum_{n,n': n congruent n' (mod t/s)}
  conjugate(Z(n))Z(n').                                            (11)
For a fixed modulus t/s, grouping n and n' by their common residue class turns the inner double sum into
sum_{r (mod t/s)}
 |sum_{n congruent r (mod t/s)}conjugate(Z(n))|^2.
This proves (2).

Now let t=p be prime. Formula (2) has only s=1 and s=p. Since the supported integers occupy distinct residue classes modulo p, the s=1 term is sum_n|Z(n)|^2. Since mu(p)=-1, the s=p term is
-(1/p)|sum_n Z(n)|^2.
This proves (3).

After ordering the N supported coordinates, the Hermitian quadratic form in (3) has matrix I_N-p^{-1}J_N. The all-ones vector is an eigenvector of J_N with eigenvalue N, and every vector perpendicular to it is killed by J_N. Hence the eigenvalues in (4) are exactly 1-N/p once and 1 with multiplicity N-1. This proves (5). A constant nonzero coefficient vector lies on the all-ones line and attains the lower eigenvalue. When N>=2, a nonzero zero-sum vector lies in its perpendicular complement and attains the upper eigenvalue. When N=1, formula (3) directly gives (5a). This proves every sharpness statement.

For a literal gamma=(p,s,c) row, fact 7ee795d9bff04bb2 defines
G_gamma=sum_n conjugate(Z_gamma(n))E_{p;n}.
If its N_gamma supported source values occupy distinct residues and N_gamma<=p/2, apply (5) to obtain (6). In the actual Good-W setting the supported n are positive integers in one B-scale interval, so distinctness is automatic whenever that interval has length less than p; the theorem states the exact residue hypothesis and does not require a coarse replacement.

If Z_gamma is nonzero, (6) gives
||G_gamma||_2^2/(sum_n|Z_gamma(n)|^2)>=1/2.
For fixed eta>0 one has p^{-eta}<1/2 for all sufficiently large p, contradicting (7). This proves the scoped method no-fit. Since the argument concerns only the individual source norm, it makes none of the excluded inferences about coefficient energy, cross-gamma cancellation, direct alignment, the complete block, or downstream targets.

glossary.I_N: The N by N identity matrix.
glossary.J_N: The N by N matrix all of whose entries are one.
glossary.N_gamma: The number of physical source values n for which the literal coefficient Z_gamma(n) is nonzero.
glossary.Q_t(Z): The primitive-additive-frequency Gram energy of a finitely supported complex coefficient sequence Z at conductor t.

53d1025f57369596.title: ABSOLUTE SOURCE-OCCUPANCY BASELINE, BOUNDARY PAYOFF, AND EXACT SAVING GAP FOR THE ADDITIVE CROSSED GRAM
53d1025f57369596.author: slava chan
53d1025f57369596.statement:
ABSOLUTE SOURCE-OCCUPANCY BASELINE, BOUNDARY PAYOFF, AND EXACT SAVING GAP FOR THE ADDITIVE CROSSED GRAM.

Fix C>=1 and Q>=8. Let real numbers H,V,P,B satisfy
  2<=H<=Q^(1/3),  2<=V<H,  P=QH/V,  B>=1.                 (1)
Let A be a nonzero integer with |A|<=Q^C, and let cal L be a finite label set. For each outer row o=(ell,v,p), where ell belongs to cal L, V<=v<2V is an integer, p is prime in [P,2P), and gcd(v,p)=1, put n=vp. Let cal X_o be any finite set of triples x=(q,m,k) satisfying
  Q<=q,m<2Q,  qm+nk=A,  gcd(qm,n)=1.                       (2)
For each ell let I_ell be an integer interval contained either in [H,2H) or in (-2H,-H]. Let a_{o,h}(x) be complex coefficients satisfying
  |a_{o,h}(x)|<=B.                                         (3)
For x=(q,m,k) define
  d_x=gcd(|A|,q),  r_x=q/d_x,  t_x=k/d_x.                  (4)
Define
  Aadd
   =sum_o sum_{h in I_ell}
      sum_{x_1,x_2 in cal X_o,
           t_{x_1}/r_{x_1} not equal t_{x_2}/r_{x_2}}
       a_{o,h}(x_1)conjugate(a_{o,h}(x_2))
       e(h[t_{x_1}/r_{x_1}-t_{x_2}/r_{x_2}]).               (5)
Then for every epsilon>0,
  |Aadd|<<_{C,epsilon}B^2(#cal L)Q^(3+epsilon).             (6)
Relative to the sufficient target in fact 4b89ec4ce7a7b67a,
  P Q^(5/3)=Q^(8/3)H/V,
the exact ratio of the displayed powers is
  Gadd=Q^3/[P Q^(5/3)]=VQ^(1/3)/H>=2.                      (7)

If B and #cal L are subpolynomial and
  Gadd=Q^{o(1)},                                            (8)
then (6) implies, for every epsilon>0,
  |Aadd|<<_{C,epsilon}P Q^(5/3+epsilon).                   (9)
In particular, the absolute source-occupancy argument reaches the target on the nonempty boundary regime H comparable to Q^(1/3) and bounded V. More quantitatively, on a subrange with
  Gadd<=Q^gamma                                             (10)
for a fixed gamma>=0, (6) gives the target with an additional factor Q^(gamma+epsilon). Thus a genuine additional power saving is required from this benchmark only on subranges where Gadd>=Q^delta for some fixed delta>0.

In the divisor-selected coordinates of fact 7f63ca7922a7fab9, the same prime p divides both source cofactors D_1,D_2, and the crossed integer E_12=vp delta_12. The E_12 divisibility is forced algebraically by the two source equations, so it is not an additional independent incidence saving. Equations (6)-(10) are an upper-bound ledger, not a lower bound for Aadd. No estimate beyond (9), no PMD closure outside (8), and no Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
53d1025f57369596.proof:
Fix one outer row o and put Xo=#cal X_o. The restriction to unequal exact rational phases only deletes ordered pairs. Taking absolute values in (5) and using (3) gives for each height h
  |sum_{x_1,x_2 in the unequal-phase domain}
      a_{o,h}(x_1)conjugate(a_{o,h}(x_2))
      e(h[t_{x_1}/r_{x_1}-t_{x_2}/r_{x_2}])|
  <=B^2Xo^2.                                                (11)

The scale assumptions imply p>=P=QH/V>Q because V<H. Also
  n=vp>=VP=QH.
Fact 914048233fada05f therefore applies to (2) and gives
  Xo<<_{C,epsilon}Q^(1+epsilon)/H.                          (12)
Each I_ell contains at most 2H integers. The number of pairs (v,p) in the displayed ranges is less than 4VP. Summing (11), using (12), and distributing a sufficiently small exponent budget before renaming epsilon gives
  |Aadd|
  <<B^2(#cal L)(VP)H(Q/H)^2Q^epsilon
  =B^2(#cal L)Q^(3+epsilon),                               (13)
because VP=QH. This proves (6).

Using P=QH/V,
  Q^3/[P Q^(5/3)]
   =Q^3/[(QH/V)Q^(5/3)]
   =VQ^(1/3)/H.                                             (14)
Since V>=2 and H<=Q^(1/3), the last quantity is at least two, proving (7). If Gadd=Q^{o(1)}, then for every fixed positive epsilon and all sufficiently large Q one has Gadd<=Q^(epsilon/3). Apply (6) with epsilon/3 in place of epsilon, absorb the subpolynomial B and label factors with another epsilon/3, and use Q^3=Gadd P Q^(5/3). This proves (9). If H is bounded below by a fixed positive multiple of Q^(1/3) and V is bounded above by a fixed constant, then Gadd is bounded, hence satisfies (8), proving the stated boundary example. Under (10), the same calculation gives the additional factor Q^(gamma+epsilon), proving the quantitative assertion.

Finally, fact 7f63ca7922a7fab9 proves
  E_12=vp delta_12
on every source pair, and also proves the exact reindexing by primes p dividing D_1 and D_2. Therefore p divides E_12 automatically on the unequal-phase source support; imposing this third divisibility condition does not delete any term from (5). This proves the divisor-incidence scope assertion and completes the proof.

glossary.Gadd: The ratio V Q^(1/3)/H between the absolute source-occupancy benchmark for Aadd and its target.

53e70bf4e327e6bd.title: MAYNARD TYPE-II PAYMENT OF THE FACTORABLE-MODULUS MEDIUM-PRIME MOBIUS SECTOR. Fix real A>0 and an integer K>=1. Let B be sufficiently large, let delta be real, and let Q_1,R_1,P,M>=2 satisfy
53e70bf4e327e6bd.author: slava chan
53e70bf4e327e6bd.statement:
MAYNARD TYPE-II PAYMENT OF THE FACTORABLE-MODULUS MEDIUM-PRIME MOBIUS SECTOR. Fix real A>0 and an integer K>=1. Let B be sufficiently large, let delta be real, and let Q_1,R_1,P,M>=2 satisfy
Q_1R_1=B^(1/2+delta),  PM asymptotic to B,                      (1)
B^(6delta)(log B)^C <=R_1<=B^(1/10-3delta)(log B)^(-C),          (2)
Q_1B^(2delta)(log B)^C<=P<=B^(1/2-3delta)(log B)^(-C),           (3)
where C=C(A,K)>0 is sufficiently large. Put Q_c=Q_1R_1. Let c be a positive integer.

Let cal S be a set of ordered pairs (q,r) with
Q_1<=q<2Q_1, R_1<=r<2R_1,                                      (4)
such that the product map (q,r) maps injectively to d=qr, every d is squarefree, and (d,c)=1. For each (q,r) in cal S choose a unit residue a_{q,r} modulo d and a function V_d supported on B<=n<2B with |V_d(n)|<=L.

Let cal P, omega_P, b_{P,c}, and D_d^{med} have the meanings in fact 512ccc143b3d5fd9. Assume that there are finitely many indices j, complex numbers lambda_{j,d}, sequences A_j(p) supported on primes P<=p<2P, and sequences B_j(m) supported on M<=m<2M such that
V_d(pm)=sum_j lambda_{j,d}A_j(p)B_j(m)                           (5)
for every prime p in [P,2P) and every positive integer m. Assume
sum_j sup_{d=qr,(q,r) in cal S}|lambda_{j,d}|<=L_proj,            (6)
|A_j(n)|<=tau_K(n), |B_j(n)|<=tau_K(n),                          (7)
and that every sequence alpha_{j,n}=1_{n prime}A_j(n) satisfies Maynard's Siegel-Walfisz condition (4.1), uniformly in j and in all displayed parameters.

Then
sum_{(q,r) in cal S}|D_{qr}^{med}|
<<_{A,K} L_proj B(log B)^(-A)
 +L(1+log(2BQ_c))^2
  [B/P+Q_cP+omega_P(c)(B/P+Q_c)].                                (8)
Here omega_P(c)=#{p prime:P<=p<2P,p divides c}. In particular, if L and L_proj are at most fixed powers of log B and the three explicit correction quantities
B/P, Q_cP, omega_P(c)(B/P+Q_c)                                  (9)
are each at most B times a sufficiently large negative power of log B, then the complete MED sector in (8) is O_A(B(log B)^(-A)) after increasing C and the correction saving powers.

The supremum over primitive residues in Maynard's theorem permits a_{q,r} to vary arbitrarily with q,r. No estimate is asserted when the current modulus has no factor R_1 satisfying (2), when no prime scale P satisfies (3), for the complementary omega_P(n)=0 sector, or for a nonprojective V_d.
53e70bf4e327e6bd.proof:
For d=qr put
T'_d=-sum_{p in cal P}sum_{m>=1}b_{P,c}(m)V_d(pm)
 [1_{pm congruent a_{q,r} (mod d)}-1_{(pm,d)=1}/phi(d)].          (10)
By fact 512ccc143b3d5fd9,
D_d^{med}=T_d+E_d,                                               (11)
where T_d is (10) with the additional restriction (p,c)=1, and
sum_{(q,r) in cal S}|E_{qr}|
<<L(1+log(2BQ_c))^2(B/P+Q_cP).                                  (12)
The injectivity of the product map makes the products d a set, so the cited fact applies with Q_0=Q_c; changing dyadic endpoint constants only changes the absolute implied constant.

We first estimate T'_d. Insert (5) into (10). For a fixed j define
alpha_p=1_{p prime}A_j(p),  beta_m=b_{P,c}(m)B_j(m).              (13)
The sequence alpha is supported at scale P, satisfies the Siegel-Walfisz condition by hypothesis, and is divisor bounded. Since |b_{P,c}(m)|<=1, beta is also divisor bounded and is supported at scale M. Therefore Proposition 5.1 of James Maynard, Primes in arithmetic progressions to large moduli III: Uniform residue classes, arXiv:2006.08250, applies with its variables
x=B, Q=Q_1, R=R_1, N=P, M=M.                                   (14)
Its hypotheses QR=x^(1/2+delta), NM asymptotic to x and its two displayed range conditions are exactly (1)-(3). The proposition states that
sum_{q asymptotic to Q_1}sum_{r asymptotic to R_1}
 sup_{(a,qr)=1}
 |sum_{m asymptotic to M}sum_{p asymptotic to P}
 alpha_p beta_m
 [1_{pm congruent a (mod qr)}-1_{(pm,qr)=1}/phi(qr)]|
 <<_{A,K}B(log B)^(-A),                                         (15)
after choosing its internal logarithmic exponent C sufficiently large in terms of A and the fixed divisor-bound exponent K. Restricting the outer pairs to cal S only decreases the nonnegative left side. For each pair, a_{q,r} is a unit, so its discrepancy is bounded by the supremum in (15). Multiplying by lambda_{j,d}, using the triangle inequality, summing the pairs, and then using (6) gives
sum_{(q,r) in cal S}|T'_{qr}|
<<_{A,K}L_proj B(log B)^(-A).                                   (16)

It remains to compare T_d and T'_d. Their difference is supported on p dividing c:
T_d-T'_d
=sum_{substack{p in cal P\\p divides c}}sum_m b_{P,c}(m)V_d(pm)
 [1_{pm congruent a_{q,r} (mod d)}-1_{(pm,d)=1}/phi(d)].         (17)
Because (d,c)=1, every p in (17) is a unit modulo d. Support of V_d gives B<=pm<2B. For fixed d,p, the physical congruence in (17) fixes one residue class of m modulo d and therefore has at most 2B/(Pd)+1 solutions. Since the product map on cal S is injective, #cal S<=4Q_c and
sum_{(q,r) in cal S}1/(qr)<=4.                                  (18)
Thus the total physical count in (17), for one p, is O(B/P+Q_c).

For the principal part, squarefreeness of d and the elementary estimate proved in fact 512ccc143b3d5fd9 give
1/phi(d)<=(1+log d)^2/d.                                        (19)
There are O(B/P) possible m before the coprimality deletion. Equations (18)-(19) show that the total principal count for one p is
O((1+log(2Q_c))^2B/P).                                          (20)
There are omega_P(c) possible primes p. Using |b_{P,c}|<=1 and |V_d|<=L in (17), and combining the physical and principal counts, gives
sum_{(q,r) in cal S}|T_{qr}-T'_{qr}|
<<L omega_P(c)(1+log(2BQ_c))^2(B/P+Q_c).                        (21)
Finally, (11)-(12), (16), and (21) prove (8). The last assertion follows by choosing the internal saving in (15) and the three correction saving powers larger than A plus the fixed logarithmic exponents of L and L_proj. The scope exclusions name precisely the hypotheses used in (2), (3), omega_P(n)>0 in fact 512ccc143b3d5fd9, and (5).

glossary.L_proj: The common projective coefficient norm in the prime/cofactor separation of V_d.
glossary.Q_1: The first dyadic factor scale of the current modulus in Maynard's Proposition 5.1.
glossary.R_1: The convenient-divisor dyadic factor scale of the current modulus in Maynard's Proposition 5.1.
glossary.T'_d: The unrestricted prime-by-Mobius bilinear row obtained after also allowing primes p dividing c.
glossary.cal S: The injectively selected family of convenient factorizations d=qr.
glossary.omega_P(c): The number of prime divisors of c in the selected medium-prime interval.

54029717e980dcb7.title: ABSOLUTE PAYMENT OF THE PROPORTIONAL-PAIR DIAGONAL AND THE FULLY RESONANT CANONICAL-DILATOR SECTOR
54029717e980dcb7.author: slava chan
54029717e980dcb7.statement:
ABSOLUTE PAYMENT OF THE PROPORTIONAL-PAIR DIAGONAL AND THE FULLY RESONANT CANONICAL-DILATOR SECTOR.

Use the notation and exact TT-star expansion of fact (41b56ed8e64bdba6). Assume all physical scales and the nonzero integer target satisfy, for one fixed (C_0),
[
 1le B,F,|mathscr A|le Q^{C_0},
]
and assume the literal coefficients and the number of exact marker/convolution copies obey a fixed divisor-function envelope:
[
 |widetilde c_lambda(q,h)|
 le 	au_J(nqh)(log(2Q))^C,qquad
 #Lambda_D(n)le	au_J(n)                                  	ag{1}
]
for fixed (J,C). Let (mathcal M_F^{(0)}(D)) be the part of the expansion of (mathcal M_F(D)) with
[
 Delta=h_1q_2-h_2q_1=0,
]
and let (mathcal M_F^{(mathrm{FR})}(D)) be the part with
[
 Delta
e0,qquad d_lambdamidmathscr ADelta.
]
Then, for every (arepsilon>0),
[
 |mathcal M_F^{(0)}(D)|
 ll_{arepsilon,J,C,C_0} Q^arepsilon BQF,                	ag{2}
]
[
 |mathcal M_F^{(mathrm{FR})}(D)|
 ll_{arepsilon,J,C,C_0}
 Q^arepsilon {BQ^2F^2over D}.                             	ag{3}
