544c7ba4db45c06f.title: STRICT-TOP COMPLETE PRE-MARKER GENEALOGY COLLAPSE AND REMOVAL OF THE PROVENANCE SELECTOR. Fix the strict top sliver
544c7ba4db45c06f.author: slava chan
544c7ba4db45c06f.statement:
STRICT-TOP COMPLETE PRE-MARKER GENEALOGY COLLAPSE AND REMOVAL OF THE PROVENANCE SELECTOR. Fix the strict top sliver
\[
 \beta_m<\beta<6/5
\]
of facts \(e58fc7c00f1683e6\) and \(b0a38f5e9ae7feb6\), before the proper strict-top \(A\)-projection is subtracted. Fix the selected integer \(N\), one active physical dyadic label \((D,M,R,K)\), one exact outer gcd \(g\), one orientation \(\epsilon\), and one smooth/projective source fibre. Retain the complete unmarked pre-marker source at those fixed outer data: do not select a proper old marker leaf, deletion leaf, or provenance leaf.

Then every inherited zero-one provenance coordinate is an auxiliary finite sibling partition, and its complete pointwise sum is
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 \sum_{\pi\in{\cal P}_{\rm prov}}\Pi_\pi(s,n,h)=1
 \qquad}                                                         \tag{1}
\]
on every supported integer tuple \((s,n,h)\). Here \({\cal P}_{\rm prov}\) is the finite family of all inherited provenance siblings over the fixed outer row and \(\Pi_\pi\) is the zero-one selector of one sibling. In particular, the factor denoted by
\[
 \Pi_{\rm prov}(s,n,h)
\]
in fact \(062a7f6f0c58b1f2\) is absent after the complete provenance coordinate is recombined; it is not an additional literal source mask.

Precisely, the selector audit inside \(\Theta^\epsilon_\lambda\) and the Archimedean coefficient has the following result. Selected \(N\), active scales, \(60\)-residual/high status, exclusion of the complete \(C91\) and bounded-base/low-\(\beta\) families, exact \(g\), orientation, the strict-top \(\beta\)-range, the residual actual-\(G\) range, and the forced parent \(U_{\rm low}\) are fixed outer-row data. The logarithmic and specified smooth \(W,\psi,\Phi\), dyadic, and fixed-\(U\) dependence is already contained in the literal amplitude \(F^\epsilon_{g,s,n}\) of fact \(b0a38f5e9ae7feb6\). After splitting sign and a dyadic block
\[
 F\le |h|<2F,
\]
the paired-frequency selector is one-variable. No further physical or provenance hard selector remains inside \(\Theta^\epsilon_\lambda\) or the Archimedean coefficient.

The arithmetic Möbius factors, the gates \((g,sn)=(s,n)=1\), and, after a one-sided factorization, all factorization thresholds and tuple-dependent occupancy masks remain explicit outside that coefficient; they are not removed or smoothed by this theorem.

As a corollary, fix dyadic factor scales \(M_1,V_1\) and restrict
\[
 M_1\le m<2M_1,\qquad V_1\le v<2V_1,\qquad M_1V_1\asymp B,
 \qquad n=mv.                                                     \tag{2}
\]
On either signed frequency block, the full complete-provenance coefficient has the exact expansion
\[
 {\bf1}_{F\le |h|<2F}{H_P\over mv}
 \widehat F^\epsilon_{g,s,mv}(\epsilon h/(mv))
 e\!\left({\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\over smv}\right)
 =
 \sum_\rho\eta_\rho A_\rho(s)C_\rho(m)D_\rho(v)E_\rho(h),        \tag{3}
\]
with the bounds proved in fact \(062a7f6f0c58b1f2\):
\[
 \sum_\rho|\eta_\rho|\,{\cal V}_F(E_\rho)
 =O_A\!\left((\log x)^2(1+F/H_P)^{-A}\right),
 \qquad
 \|A_\rho\|_\infty,\|C_\rho\|_\infty,\|D_\rho\|_\infty\le1        \tag{4}
\]
after normalization, for every fixed \(A>0\). The complete dyadic \(F\)-sum has \(x^{o(1)}\) total cost on each fixed factor box. Summing a standard dyadic partition of the \(m,v\) ranges introduces at most \(O((\log x)^2)\) further coefficient mass and therefore still has total cost \(x^{o(1)}\).

This is a definition-level source-genealogy statement for the complete unmarked projection. It does not assert that one proper provenance leaf is regular, and it does not permit deleting provenance siblings before recombination. It proves no reciprocal-energy estimate, Type-I estimate, endpoint payment, critical-tail payment, post-\(A\) bound, or Goldbach conclusion.
544c7ba4db45c06f.proof:
We audit the genealogy from the literal source.

Fact \(60b26a9b6f79467a\) displays the selected physical source as
\[
 \sum_{dm+rk=N}\mu(d)\mu(r)\log m\log k\,
 W(dm/x)\psi(d/D_*)\Phi(d/D)\Phi(m/M)
 \Phi(rk/U)\Phi(r/R)\Phi(k/K).                                  \tag{5}
\]
Thus its dependence on the integer solution, apart from the two Möbius factors, consists only of logarithms and the specified smooth functions. There is no independent zero-one provenance mask in (5). Fact \(328503a935cabe60\), part (a), records this same definition-level conclusion.

We inspect every subtraction before the strict-top re-marker. Fact \(7ffe3d237362a451\) obtains the post-low source by subtracting the complete \(C91\) aggregate and complete bounded-base/low-normalized-\(\beta\) families. Its statement explicitly says that this inserts no actual-\((r,k)\) or anatomy selector. Hence, on a fixed surviving outer row, these are scalar membership tests and create no \(s,n,h\)-dependent provenance factor. This is also the source-genealogy conclusion used in part (c) of fact \(328503a935cabe60\).

The first-buffer anatomy subtractions used to construct the selected late aggregate of fact \(dde1e246a629bcc4\) are supported in
\[
 \beta\le\beta_1<\beta_m.
\]
They therefore remove no atom in the present strict range. The only intervening subtraction which meets the present beta range is the complete high-imbalance projection of fact \(01b550792363535d\),
\[
 G\ge Q^{\Gamma_{BC}(\beta)+\omega}.
\]
By its definition, every other retained coordinate is recombined to completion inside that projection. Its strict-top complement is therefore selected only by
\[
 Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\le G<Q^{\Gamma_{BC}(\beta)+\omega},
\]
which is fixed outer-scale data once the dyadic label, exact \(g\), orientation, and normalized layer are fixed. It does not select a proper provenance sibling.

Fact \(be94f5e014ad4d3d\) subsequently subtracts only
\[
 \beta_1<\beta\le\beta_2,\qquad
 \beta_2=\beta_m-\sigma/5<\beta_m,
\]
disjoint from the present strict top sliver. Its paid projection also recombines every provenance coordinate to completion.

Fact \(e58fc7c00f1683e6\) then projects onto the top sliver and, before choosing any new anatomy, recombines every inherited marker anatomy and all marker-dependent target-gcd, order/equal-cell, collision, deletion, and provenance descendants at each pre-marker source atom. This restores the literal normalized Möbius factor \(\mu(n)\). Part (b) of fact \(328503a935cabe60\) states the general finite-partition principle used here: every provenance coordinate introduced in a marker/anatomy refinement is an auxiliary finite partition, and retaining the full coordinate makes its complementary siblings sum to the pre-refinement coefficient. Since (5) had no independent physical provenance mask, no intervening subtraction selected a proper provenance leaf on this beta range, and the full inherited marker genealogy is recombined, all inherited provenance siblings are present. Their selectors sum pointwise to one. This proves (1).

At fixed outer data, all outer restrictions named in the statement are scalars. Fact \(b0a38f5e9ae7feb6\) places the logarithmic and physical smooth dependence in \(F^\epsilon_{g,s,n}\). The signed dyadic frequency block is a one-variable interval. Equation (1) removes the only provenance factor left unresolved by the audit in fact \(062a7f6f0c58b1f2\). This proves the scoped selector classification, while leaving every arithmetic and later factorization gate explicit as stated.

Now impose the dyadic factor-box hypotheses (2). Fact \(062a7f6f0c58b1f2\) proves exactly (3)--(4), the negative-sign reindexing, and the complete dyadic-frequency summability after removing only \(\Pi_{\rm prov}\). Equation (1) shows that the complete unmarked source has that factor replaced by one, so the cited expansion applies without alteration on this fixed box. Finally, a standard dyadic partition has \(O(\log x)\) possible scales for each positive factor and hence at most \(O((\log x)^2)\) pairs \((M_1,V_1)\). Triangle inequality multiplies the coefficient mass by at most this quantity, which is \(x^{o(1)}\). The scope exclusions follow because no analytic estimate has been applied.

glossary.Pi_pi: The zero-one selector of the inherited provenance sibling indexed by pi.
glossary.Pi_{prov}: The previously unresolved inherited pre-marker provenance selector in the strict-top unmarked coefficient.
glossary.U_{low}: The sole inherited parent on the strict top sliver.
glossary.cal P_{prov}: The finite family of all inherited provenance siblings above one fixed strict-top outer row.
glossary.complete-provenance strict-top unmarked: The literal strict-top unmarked coefficient after summing every inherited provenance sibling and before subtracting the proper new A projection.

549328a9f587f158.title: SOURCE-WEIGHTED FOURTH-MOMENT OCCUPANCY OF ALL RANK-ONE REPEATED-POLE STRATA AT ONE PRIME. Let \(p\) be a prime. Let \(\mathcal I\subset\mathbb F_p^\times\) be a nonzero additive interval of cardinality \(L\ge1\), and let \(\mathcal H\subset\mathbb F_p^\times\) and \(\mathcal R_0\subset\mathbb F_p\) be finite sets. For every \((r,h,t)\in\mathcal R_0\times\mathcal H\times\mathcal I\), let \(\Lambda_p(r,h,t)\) be a finite set of literal source copies and let \(c_{p,\lambda}(r,h,t)\in\mathbb C\). Put
549328a9f587f158.author: slava chan
549328a9f587f158.statement:
SOURCE-WEIGHTED FOURTH-MOMENT OCCUPANCY OF ALL RANK-ONE REPEATED-POLE STRATA AT ONE PRIME. Let \(p\) be a prime. Let \(\mathcal I\subset\mathbb F_p^\times\) be a nonzero additive interval of cardinality \(L\ge1\), and let \(\mathcal H\subset\mathbb F_p^\times\) and \(\mathcal R_0\subset\mathbb F_p\) be finite sets. For every \((r,h,t)\in\mathcal R_0\times\mathcal H\times\mathcal I\), let \(\Lambda_p(r,h,t)\) be a finite set of literal source copies and let \(c_{p,\lambda}(r,h,t)\in\mathbb C\). Put
\[
 A_p(r,h,t)=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda_p(r,h,t)}
 |c_{p,\lambda}(r,h,t)|,\qquad
 U_p(r)=\sum_{h\in\mathcal H}\max_{t\in\mathcal I}A_p(r,h,t). \tag{1}
\]
For each ordered quadruple of source copies, allow an arbitrary factor
\[
 0\le D_p((r_i,h_i,t_i,\lambda_i)_{i=1}^4)\le1. \tag{2}
\]
Thus \(D_p\) may retain a pair-dependent deletion, the condition that \(p\) is the selected first active prime, source masks, and any other zero-one bookkeeping condition.

Give the four positions the signs \((+,+,-,-)\). Let \(\mathscr O_p\) be the sum of
\[
 D_p((r_i,h_i,t_i,\lambda_i)_{i=1}^4)
 prod_{i=1}^4|c_{p,\lambda_i}(r_i,h_i,t_i)| \tag{3}
\]
over all ordered quadruples for which the equalities among \(r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4\) form a set partition with no singleton block and for every equal-\(r\) block \(B\),
\[
 sum_{\substack{i\in B\\i\le2}}h_it_i^{-1}
 =
 sum_{\substack{i\in B\\i\ge3}}h_it_i^{-1}
 \quad\text{in }\mathbb F_p. \tag{4}
\]
Then, for every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \mathscr O_p
 \ll_\varepsilon
 L^\varepsilon\left(L^{8/3}+\frac{L^4}{p}+3L^2\right)
 \left(\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_0}U_p(r)^2\right)^2.
 \quad} \tag{5}
\]
Every source multiplicity and coefficient is retained in the envelope (1), and every tuple mask is retained in (3) before the final domination.

The unique one-block stratum \(r_1=r_2=r_3=r_4\) has precisely the exceptional relation
\[
 \frac{h_1}{t_1}+\frac{h_2}{t_2}
 =
 \frac{h_3}{t_3}+\frac{h_4}{t_4}\pmod p. \tag{6}
\]
If \(L\ge p^\delta\) for a fixed \(\delta>0\), then for every fixed
\[
 0<\eta<\min\{4\delta/3,1\}
\]
and all sufficiently large \(p\), the right side of (5) is
\[
 \ll_{\delta,\eta}
 L^4p^{-\eta}\left(\sum_rU_p(r)^2\right)^2. \tag{7}
\]
Consequently, in any fourth-moment completion in which the trivial repeated-pole occupancy is \(L^4(\sum_rU_p(r)^2)^2\) and this occupancy enters under a fourth root, (7) gives the fixed factor \(p^{-\eta/4}\). This conclusion is confined to a fixed prime and a single interval of cofactor residues.

In the local row of fact \(3d10fd30e2a42246\), write the marked dilator as \(d=pm\), put \(t=vm=n/p\), and translate the completed literal modulus coordinate as \(q=X+r\). The local phase is
\[
 e_p(\mathscr A h t^{-1}(X+r)^{-1})
 =K(s(X+r)),\qquad K(x)=e_p(\mathscr A x^{-1}),\quad s=th^{-1}. \tag{8}
\]
Hence \(s^{-1}=ht^{-1}\), so fact \(7d341c8eec44f7a3\) maps its pole-balance equations exactly to (4), and its four-index one-block equation exactly to (6). Formula (5) therefore pays the full source-weighted rank-one exceptional occupancy on any literal first-active-prime subrange for which the cofactor residues \(t=n/p\) lie in one nonzero additive interval \(\mathcal I\). It does not estimate the complementary cofactor geometry, sum varying selected primes without their displayed envelopes, tensorize the remaining prime faces, or prove the complete joint-completion, strict-top, or Goldbach estimate.
549328a9f587f158.proof:
By fact \(7d341c8eec44f7a3\), an exceptional four-row rank-one reciprocal-pole tuple has an equality partition of the four pole shifts with no singleton block, and on every block it satisfies the signed reciprocal-scale balance. There are exactly four set partitions of \(\{1,2,3,4\}\) with no singleton: the one-block partition and the three partitions into two blocks of size two. We bound their source-weighted occupancies separately. Since \(0\le D_p\le1\), dropping \(D_p\) is valid after taking the nonnegative absolute coefficient product (3). Summing the absolute values of all source copies at fixed \((r,h,t)\) gives exactly \(A_p(r,h,t)\), so no source-copy multiplicity is discarded.

First consider the one-block partition. Fix \(r\in\mathcal R_0\) and \(h_1,h_2,h_3,h_4\in\mathcal H\). Let \(N(h_1,h_2,h_3,h_4)\) be the number of \((t_1,t_2,t_3,t_4)\in\mathcal I^4\) satisfying (6). For \(a\in\mathbb F_p\), put
\[
 S_a(x)=\sum_{t\in\mathcal I}e_p(xat^{-1}).
\]
Additive orthogonality gives
\[
 N(h_1,h_2,h_3,h_4)
 =\frac1p\sum_{x\in\mathbb F_p}
 S_{h_1}(x)S_{h_2}(x)
 \overline{S_{h_3}(x)S_{h_4}(x)}. \tag{9}
\]
Hölder's inequality implies
\[
 N(h_1,h_2,h_3,h_4)
 \le\prod_{i=1}^4
 \left(\frac1p\sum_x|S_{h_i}(x)|^4\right)^{1/4}. \tag{10}
\]
Because each \(h_i\ne0\), multiplication by \(h_i\) permutes \(\mathbb F_p\). Thus every factor on the right of (10) is the fourth-root of the same number \(J_4(p,\mathcal I)\), where \(J_4(p,\mathcal I)\) counts
\[
 t_1^{-1}+t_2^{-1}=t_3^{-1}+t_4^{-1},
 \qquad t_i\in\mathcal I. \tag{11}
\]
Therefore
\[
 N(h_1,h_2,h_3,h_4)\le J_4(p,\mathcal I). \tag{12}
\]
Bourgain and Garaev, arXiv:1211.4184, Theorem 1 with \(k=2\), states for every nonzero interval \(\mathcal I\subset\mathbb F_p\) that
\[
 J_4(p,\mathcal I)
 \ll_\varepsilon L^\varepsilon
 \left(L^{8/3}+\frac{L^4}{p}\right). \tag{13}
\]
The paper's interval means an additive interval in \(\mathbb F_p\), inversion is in \(\mathbb F_p^\times\), and our hypotheses give exactly those definitions. Dilating the reciprocal set by any fixed nonzero \(h_i\) is handled by the permutation of the Fourier variable in (10); no claim that a dilated interval is itself an interval is used.

For fixed \(r,h_1,h_2,h_3,h_4\), each term in the weighted sum is at most
\[
 \prod_{i=1}^4\max_{t\in\mathcal I}A_p(r,h_i,t).
\]
Using (12), summing the heights, and then summing \(r\), the one-block contribution is at most
\[
 J_4(p,\mathcal I)\sum_rU_p(r)^4
 \le J_4(p,\mathcal I)\left(\sum_rU_p(r)^2\right)^2. \tag{14}
\]

Now fix one of the three two-block partitions. On a two-element block \(\{i,j\}\), equation (4) has the form
\[
 h_it_i^{-1}=h_jt_j^{-1}
 \quad\text{or}\quad
 h_it_i^{-1}=-h_jt_j^{-1}, \tag{15}
\]
according to whether the two signs are opposite or equal. Once \(t_i\in\mathcal I\) is fixed, (15) determines at most one residue \(t_j\in\mathbb F_p\), because \(h_i,h_j,t_i\) are nonzero. Hence there are at most \(L\) pairs \((t_i,t_j)\in\mathcal I^2\) satisfying (15). For a block whose common pole is \(r\), its weighted occupancy is consequently at most
\[
 L\left(\sum_{h\in\mathcal H}
       \max_{t\in\mathcal I}A_p(r,h,t)\right)^2
 =L U_p(r)^2. \tag{16}
\]
The two blocks have distinct common poles on the exact partition stratum. Dropping that inequality only enlarges the sum. Thus one two-block partition contributes at most
\[
 L^2\sum_{r,r'}U_p(r)^2U_p(r')^2
 =L^2\left(\sum_rU_p(r)^2\right)^2. \tag{17}
\]
There are three such partitions. Combining (13), (14), and three copies of (17) proves (5).

Assume next that \(L\ge p^\delta\). Relative to \(L^4\), the three terms in parentheses in (5), including the harmless factor \(L^\varepsilon\), have ratios
\[
 L^{-4/3+\varepsilon},\qquad p^{-1}L^\varepsilon,
 \qquad 3L^{-2+\varepsilon}.
\]
Given \(\eta<\min\{4\delta/3,1\}\), choose the epsilon used in (5) sufficiently small in terms of \(\delta\) and \(\eta\). The displayed ratios are then \(O_{\delta,\eta}(p^{-\eta})\) for sufficiently large \(p\). This proves (7), and taking a fourth root proves the stated completion-factor implication.

Finally, fact \(3d10fd30e2a42246\) gives the exact selected-prime local phase
\[
 e_p(\mathscr A h(vm)^{-1}q^{-1}).
\]
With \(t=vm=n/p\) and \(q=X+r\), direct substitution gives (8). Since \(\mathscr A,h,t\) are units on that local row, \(K\) and \(s=th^{-1}\) are well-defined. The reciprocal-scale variable in fact \(7d341c8eec44f7a3\) is therefore \(s^{-1}=ht^{-1}\), which proves the claimed exact mapping and all scope statements.

glossary.A_p(r,h,t): The l1 mass of all literal source-copy coefficients with fixed selected prime, shift, height, and cofactor residue.
glossary.D_p: An arbitrary tuple mask retaining pair-dependent deletion, selected-first-prime, source, and bookkeeping conditions.
glossary.J_4(p,\\\\mathcal I): The number of four-tuples in the interval whose two sums of reciprocal residues agree modulo p.
glossary.U_p(r): The height-l1 and cofactor-l-infinity source envelope at fixed pole shift r.
glossary.\\\\Lambda_p(r,h,t): The finite set of literal source copies with fixed prime-local row parameters.
glossary.\\\\mathscr O_p: The full absolute source-weighted occupancy of all four-index rank-one exceptional equal-pole partition strata at the fixed prime p.

54e9fd98e7191261.title: OPPOSITE-RAY \(m_q=1\) COHERENCE AND SIGN-TWIN AUDIT IN ONE EXACT GOOD-\(\mathscr W\) COPY
54e9fd98e7191261.author: slava chan
54e9fd98e7191261.statement:
OPPOSITE-RAY \(m_q=1\) COHERENCE AND SIGN-TWIN AUDIT IN ONE EXACT GOOD-\(\mathscr W\) COPY.

Adopt a forward-orientation good-\(\mathscr W\) fibre from fact e55b27d39c593164 in the range
\[
6/5\le\beta<4/3,
\]
so its exact parent is \(U_{\rm low}\). Fix one anatomy, one frozen source/projective fibre, one frequency and dilator block, and one exact marked copy \(\lambda\), with
\[
n=d_\lambda v_\lambda,\qquad T=\mathscr A\ne0.
\]
Let \(a,b\) be positive integers satisfying
\[
(a,b)=1,
\]
and suppose the two opposite primitive signed rays
\[
R_+=(+1,a,b),\qquad R_-=(-1,a,b)
\]
are both supported by the copy. Nonzero Möbius support makes \(a\) squarefree. For the ordered pair \((R_+,R_-)\),
\[
\Delta_0=2ab,\qquad
m_q={a^2\over(a^2,2Tab)}
={a\over(a,2T)}.                                                  \tag{1}
\]
Consequently
\[
\boxed{m_q=1\Longleftrightarrow a\mid2T.}                         \tag{2}
\]

The CRT-combined modular phase of fact 7e9251670db3e1c9 is
\[
e_n\!\left(T\Delta_0(a^2)^{-1}\right),                           \tag{3}
\]
where the inverse is modulo \(n\). After multiplying its Archimedean reciprocity companion, the full physical phase is
\[
e_{a^2}\!\left(-T\Delta_0n^{-1}\right).                          \tag{4}
\]
If \(a\mid2T\), then \(a^2\mid T\Delta_0\), so the phase in (4) equals one. Thus this opposite-ray \(m_q=1\) slice is arithmetically coherent.

Write the exact RAY-MU coefficients from fact a36284a9dbec7837 as
\[
B_\lambda(R_\pm)
=\mathcal A_{\lambda,\pm}\mathcal U_{\lambda,\pm},               \tag{5}
\]
where
\[
\mathcal A_{\lambda,\pm}
=
a_\lambda(n)\mu(a){H_P\over n}
e\!\left(\pm{\varepsilon_{\rm or}Tb\over an}\right),             \tag{6}
\]
and
\[
\mathcal U_{\lambda,\pm}
=
\sum_{k\in\mathscr I_\lambda(R_\pm)}
\mu(k)
\widehat{\mathcal F}_{ka,n}
\!\left(\pm{\varepsilon_{\rm or}kb\over n}\right)
\Xi_\lambda(ka,\pm kb,n).                                        \tag{7}
\]
Equations (6)--(7) are the exact sign-twin premise ledger. The dyadic box is expressed using \(|h|\). Survival of both rays means only that the two separately defined sets
\[
\mathscr I_\lambda(R_+),\qquad\mathscr I_\lambda(R_-)
\]
are both nonempty; they need not be equal. Nonzero mass on both rays requires the two complete sums in (7) to be nonzero, which can fail through either masking, zero Fourier values, or internal signed cancellation.

Conditionally suppose that
\[
\mathscr I_\lambda(R_+)=\mathscr I_\lambda(R_-),\qquad
\Xi_\lambda(ka,kb,n)=\Xi_\lambda(ka,-kb,n)\in\mathbb R            \tag{8}
\]
on this common set, and that every physical source function
\(\mathcal F_{ka,n}\) is real-valued. Then
\[
\mathcal U_{\lambda,-}
=\overline{\mathcal U_{\lambda,+}},\qquad
\mathcal A_{\lambda,-}
=\overline{\mathcal A_{\lambda,+}},\qquad
B_\lambda(R_-)=\overline{B_\lambda(R_+)}.                        \tag{9}
\]
Even under (8)--(9), the two ordered coherent cross terms equal
\[
\boxed{
B_\lambda(R_+)\overline{B_\lambda(R_-)}
+
B_\lambda(R_-)\overline{B_\lambda(R_+)}
=
2\operatorname {Re}\!\left(B_\lambda(R_+)^2\right),
}                                                                 \tag{10}
\]
not \(2|B_\lambda(R_+)|^2\). The right side of (10) can be positive, negative, or zero; for example it is zero whenever a nonzero \(B_\lambda(R_+)\) has argument \(\pi/4\) modulo \(\pi/2\).

The presently verified exact-copy facts do not establish the conditional sign-twin premises (8), nor do they establish nonvanishing of either complete sum in (7). Fact e55b27d39c593164 records \(\Xi_\lambda\) only as the complete product of inherited target-gcd, fixed-\(U\), high, source, parent, ordering, equality, collision, deletion and provenance factors. Fact a36284a9dbec7837 retains those factors in (7) and assumes neither \(h\)-sign symmetry nor Fourier nonvanishing. In the chosen \(U_{\rm low}\) fibre, the parent, orientation, anatomy, marker-copy and provenance labels are fixed and the frequency box uses \(|h|\), but the unresolved \(h\)-dependent source/deletion content remains inside \(\Xi_\lambda\) and the indexed Fourier family.

Therefore SIGN-TWIN-AUDIT has the following exact outcome. If either scaling set is empty, the opposite-ray cross term is absent. If both are nonempty but the complete sum on one side vanishes, the cross term is again absent. If both signs survive with the additional conditional conjugacy (9), arithmetic coherence still supplies only the signed real square (10), not a positive lower bound. No literal opposite-ray mass lower bound follows from the verified facts. Any use of this slice must first prove sign symmetry and nonvanishing in the actual exact copy and must then estimate its signed cross-copy/ray aggregation. This fact proves no lower bound, no GA-SIGNED-RAY-MU estimate, no GA-RAY-SPEC, no tail payment, and no Goldbach conclusion.
54e9fd98e7191261.proof:
Because \(R_\pm\) are supported, fact a36284a9dbec7837 gives a positive integer \(k\) with
\[
\mu(ka)\ne0.
\]
Thus \(ka\), and hence \(a\), is squarefree.

For \(R_+\) and \(R_-\), the primitive ray determinant is
\[
\Delta_0=(+1)ba-(-1)ba=2ab.
\]
The product of the primitive positive denominators is \(a^2\). Since \(a\) is squarefree and \((a,b)=1\), prime-by-prime valuation gives
\[
(a^2,2Tab)=a(a,2T).
\]
Indeed, every prime \(p\mid a\) occurs once in \(2Tab\) from the displayed factor \(a\), and it occurs a second time exactly when \(p\mid2T\), because \(p\nmid b\). Dividing \(a^2\) by this greatest common divisor proves (1), and (2) follows.

Fact 7e9251670db3e1c9 gives (3) as the CRT-combined ray phase and (4) as the exact full physical phase after the Archimedean factor is restored. If \(a\mid2T\), write \(2T=ac\) with \(c\in\mathbb Z\). Then
\[
T\Delta_0=T(2ab)=a^2cb,
\]
so \(a^2\mid T\Delta_0\). Therefore the additive character modulo \(a^2\) in (4) equals one. This proves arithmetic coherence without making a coefficient-size assertion.

Equations (5)--(7) are the specialization of RAY-MU in fact a36284a9dbec7837 to signs \(+1\) and \(-1\). By the definition of \(\mathscr I_\lambda(R)\) in that fact, a ray is supported exactly when its own scaling set is nonempty. This proves the precise survival statement without identifying the two sets.

Now assume (8) and real-valuedness of the physical source functions. For a real integrable function, the Fourier convention used in fact e55b27d39c593164 satisfies
\[
\widehat{\mathcal F}_{ka,n}(-\xi)
=
\overline{\widehat{\mathcal F}_{ka,n}(\xi)}.
\]
The Möbius value \(\mu(k)\) and the common mask in (8) are real. Termwise conjugation of the common finite sum in (7) proves
\[
\mathcal U_{\lambda,-}
=\overline{\mathcal U_{\lambda,+}}.
\]
The marker weight, \(\mu(a)\), \(H_P\), and \(n\) in (6) are real, while the two exponential factors are conjugates. Hence
\[
\mathcal A_{\lambda,-}
=\overline{\mathcal A_{\lambda,+}}.
\]
Multiplying proves the last identity in (9).

On the coherent slice the phase is one. Substitute the last identity in (9) into the two ordered cross terms:
\[
B_+\overline{B_-}
+B_-\overline{B_+}
=B_+B_++\overline{B_+}\,\overline{B_+}
=2\operatorname {Re}(B_+^2).
\]
This is (10). Taking \(B_+=re^{\pi i/4}\) with \(r>0\) gives
\[
\operatorname {Re}(B_+^2)=\operatorname {Re}(ir^2)=0,
\]
which proves that conditional sign twins and phase coherence alone do not imply a positive contribution.

Finally, inspect the exact hypotheses of facts e55b27d39c593164 and a36284a9dbec7837. The former defines \(\Xi_\lambda(q,h,n)\) as one product of all retained masks but states no invariance under \(h\mapsto-h\) and no nonvanishing theorem for its indexed Fourier transform. The latter preserves this product separately in the two signed sums and explicitly adds no regularity or symmetry assumption. The chosen range has only parent \(U_{\rm low}\) by the parent ledger in fact e55b27d39c593164, and fixing the copy freezes its marker and provenance data, but neither operation removes the unresolved \(h\)-dependent factors named in \(\Xi_\lambda\). Thus (8) and nonvanishing cannot be inferred from the cited exact-copy facts. The three possible audit outcomes and every scope exclusion follow.

glossary.SIGN-TWIN-AUDIT: The exact audit of support symmetry, Fourier conjugacy and signed cross-term behavior for the two opposite primitive rays (+,a,b) and (-,a,b).
glossary.opposite-ray coherent slice: The supported opposite-ray subfamily with squarefree a dividing 2T, equivalently m_q=1.

54f71c4dcc1bc9bb.title: Fix real numbers \(1/2<a<b<1\). Let \(W\) be a nonzero nonnegative continuously differentiable real function supported in \([a,b]\). Let \(\psi\) be continuously differentiable with \(0\le\psi\le1\), \(\psi(u)=0\) for \(0<u\le1\), and \(\psi(u)=1\) for \(u\ge2\). Let \(\Phi\) be the nonnegative smooth dyadic partition of fact 3ef233e014331fc3
54f71c4dcc1bc9bb.author: slava chan
54f71c4dcc1bc9bb.statement:
Fix real numbers \(1/2<a<b<1\). Let \(W\) be a nonzero nonnegative continuously differentiable real function supported in \([a,b]\). Let \(\psi\) be continuously differentiable with \(0\le\psi\le1\), \(\psi(u)=0\) for \(0<u\le1\), and \(\psi(u)=1\) for \(u\ge2\). Let \(\Phi\) be the nonnegative smooth dyadic partition of fact 3ef233e014331fc3.

Apply fact 052064336e86e65c with large parameter \(2x\), target exponent \(8\), and variation exponent \(5\); denote its fixed exponent by \(B_{\rm init}\). Apply fact 5084a731a9f78a09 with requested accuracy \(8\) and prescribed floor \(B_{\rm init}+1\); denote its fixed exponent by \(B_{\rm src}>B_{\rm init}+1\). Let \(x\) tend to infinity through positive integers for which \(N=2x\) is not representable as a sum of two primes. Put
\[
 D_*=x^{1/2}(\log x)^{-B_{\rm src}},\qquad
 Q_{\rm init}=(2x)^{1/2}(\log(2x))^{-B_{\rm init}}.
\]
Let \(D,M,U\) be positive dyadic real numbers satisfying
\[
 {D_*\over2}\le D\le2bx,\qquad
 {ax\over4}\le DM\le4bx,\qquad
 {(2-b)x\over2}\le U\le2(2-a)x,\qquad
 2D>Q_{\rm init}.                                         \tag{1}
\]
Define
\[
 {\cal I}_D=\{d\ge2:(d,N)=1,\ \mu(d)\ne0,\ d\le x^{1/2},\
                  \Phi(d/D)\ne0\},
\]
\[
 V_{d,m}=W(dm/x)\Phi((N-dm)/U),
\]
and
\[
 \Lambda_{\rm pr}(n)=
 \begin{cases}\log n,&n\text{ is prime},\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}
\]
For distinct \(d_1,d_2\in{\cal I}_D\), let \(\mathfrak S_N(d_1,d_2)\) be the singular series of fact b164cd7d1e02e173 and define
\[
 {\cal R}_N(d_1,d_2)=
 \sum_{m\ge1}V_{d_1,m}V_{d_2,m}
 \Lambda_{\rm pr}(N-d_1m)\Lambda_{\rm pr}(N-d_2m)
 -\mathfrak S_N(d_1,d_2)
  \int_0^\infty V_{d_1,t}V_{d_2,t}\,dt.                 \tag{2}
\]
Define
\[
 {\cal R}_{\rm agg}(N;D,M,U)=
 \sum_{\substack{d_1,d_2\in{\cal I}_D\\d_1\ne d_2}}
 \mu(d_1)\mu(d_2)\Phi(d_1/D)\Phi(d_2/D)
 {\cal R}_N(d_1,d_2),                                    \tag{3}
\]
and
\[
 \mathfrak C_{\rm off}=
 \sum_{\substack{d_1,d_2\in{\cal I}_D\\d_1\ne d_2}}
 \mu(d_1)\mu(d_2)\Phi(d_1/D)\Phi(d_2/D)
 \sum_{m\ge1}V_{d_1,m}V_{d_2,m}
 \Lambda_{\rm pr}(N-d_1m)\Lambda_{\rm pr}(N-d_2m).       \tag{4}
\]
Then
\[
 \mathfrak C_{\rm off}
 ={\cal R}_{\rm agg}(N;D,M,U)+{\cal H}_{\rm sing}(D,M;U) \tag{5}
\]
exactly, where \({\cal H}_{\rm sing}\) is the literal singular main of fact 5b7b0955c5efaa1b. For every \(A>0\),
\[
 {\cal H}_{\rm sing}(D,M;U)
 \ll_{A,W,\Phi}xD(\log x)^{-A}.                          \tag{6}
\]

Consequently, the following uniform estimate over all labels satisfying (1) with \(D\le2x^{1/2}\) is sufficient:
\[
 {\cal R}_{\rm agg}(N;D,M,U)
 =o_{W,\Phi}\!\left(xD(\log x)^{-4}\right).               \tag{TB-ERR4}
\]
It implies (TB-COV4) of fact 9e1ff55fe17bc513. Hence it makes the literal top-band discrepancy \(o(x/\log x)\). For the selected same-\(N\) negative block of fact 1de7f7c45ccfee10, either \(D>2x^{1/2}\), in which case \({\cal I}_D\) is empty, or \(D\le2x^{1/2}\), in which case (TB-ERR4) applies. In both cases (TB-ERR4) transfers a negative discrepancy of order \(\mathfrak c(N)x/\log x\) to the exact \(d>x^{1/2}\) divisor-switched component.

Thus, after facts 9e1ff55fe17bc513 and 5b7b0955c5efaa1b, the remaining top-band input can be stated purely as the aggregate actual-minus-singular error (TB-ERR4). No assertion that (TB-ERR4) is proved is made.
54f71c4dcc1bc9bb.proof:
The definition of \({\cal I}_D\) ensures that every \(d\in{\cal I}_D\) is odd and squarefree and is coprime to the positive even integer \(N\). Thus fact b164cd7d1e02e173 applies to every pair for which (2) is defined.

Insert (2) into (3). The sum of the actual-prime terms is exactly (4). The sum of the subtracted terms is
\[
 {\cal H}_{\rm sing}(D,M;U)=
 \int_0^\infty
 \sum_{\substack{d_1,d_2\in{\cal I}_D\\d_1\ne d_2}}
 \mu(d_1)\mu(d_2)\Phi(d_1/D)\Phi(d_2/D)
 V_{d_1,t}V_{d_2,t}\mathfrak S_N(d_1,d_2)\,dt,
\]
which is exactly the literal singular main in fact 5b7b0955c5efaa1b. This proves (5).

All hypotheses of the literal consequence of fact 5b7b0955c5efaa1b are present: \(N=2x\) is a positive even integer; \(W,\Phi\) have the required regularity and support; (1) gives \(DM\asymp x\) and \(U\asymp x\); and \({\cal I}_D\) is the same squarefree-supported top set because terms with \(\mu(d)=0\) vanish in that fact. Therefore, for every \(A_1>0\),
\[
 {\cal H}_{\rm sing}\ll_{A_1,W,\Phi}
 \mathfrak c(N)xD(\log x)^{-A_1}.                       \tag{7}
\]

We prove directly that \(\mathfrak c(N)\) has at most a fixed logarithmic growth. Let
\(3\le p_1<\cdots<p_r\) be the distinct odd prime divisors of \(N\). Then \(p_j\ge j+2\), while \(2^r\le N\), so \(r\le\log_2N\). Since
\[
 {p-1\over p-2}=1+{1\over p-2}\le\exp(3/p)\qquad(p\ge3),
\]
one has
\[
 {\mathfrak c(N)\over C_2}
 \le\exp\left(3\sum_{j=1}^r{1\over p_j}\right)
 \le\exp\left(3\sum_{j=1}^r{1\over j+2}\right)
 \ll (r+2)^3\ll(\log(2N))^3.                            \tag{8}
\]
Take \(A_1=A+5\) in (7), use \(N=2x\), and obtain (6).

Assume (TB-ERR4). Choose \(A>6\) in (6). Equation (5) gives
\[
 \mathfrak C_{\rm off}
 =o(xD(\log x)^{-4})+O(xD(\log x)^{-A})
 =o(xD(\log x)^{-4}),
\]
which is (TB-COV4). Fact 9e1ff55fe17bc513 proves that this estimate, uniformly over the exact labels (1), makes the top genuine-prime block and top discrepancy \(o(x/\log x)\).

It remains only to check the selected label. Fact 1de7f7c45ccfee10 supplies a same-\(N\) negative block satisfying exactly (1). If its \(D>2x^{1/2}\), then \(\Phi(d/D)\ne0\) implies \(d\ge D/2>x^{1/2}\), so \({\cal I}_D\) is empty and its top discrepancy is zero. If \(D\le2x^{1/2}\), the uniform hypothesis (TB-ERR4) applies. In either case the top discrepancy is \(o(x/\log x)\). Fact 9e1ff55fe17bc513 then combines this with the full negative discrepancy of fact 1de7f7c45ccfee10 and \(\mathfrak c(N)\ge C_2>0\) to force the stated negative \(d>x^{1/2}\) component. No estimate for \({\cal R}_{\rm agg}\) is asserted without the explicit hypothesis (TB-ERR4).

glossary.TB-ERR4: the sufficient uniform estimate R_agg=o(xD(log x)^(-4))
glossary.cal R_N(d1,d2): the actual two-prime correlation minus its singular-series integral for one squarefree ordered pair
glossary.cal R_agg(N;D,M,U): the complete raw-Mobius aggregate of the pair errors

55314e158bcbdc91.title: CONSTANT-AMPLITUDE FULL-DISPLAY INTERFACE SATURATOR. Use the prime-q actual-source family and its subset cal Y from fact 38bc0e88e17aef0e. Thus, for all sufficiently large primes p, there are parameters Q,V,H,P,v,n,A, a finite source set cal X of triples x=(q,m,k), a subset cal Y of cal X with pairwise distinct slopes lambda_x=k/q lying in one interval of length at most 1/(12H), and a nonempty integer height interval I, such that
55314e158bcbdc91.author: slava chan
55314e158bcbdc91.statement:
CONSTANT-AMPLITUDE FULL-DISPLAY INTERFACE SATURATOR. Use the prime-q actual-source family and its subset cal Y from fact 38bc0e88e17aef0e. Thus, for all sufficiently large primes p, there are parameters Q,V,H,P,v,n,A, a finite source set cal X of triples x=(q,m,k), a subset cal Y of cal X with pairwise distinct slopes lambda_x=k/q lying in one interval of length at most 1/(12H), and a nonempty integer height interval I, such that
Theta_cl >= 1/2
when cal Y is one critical cluster with coefficient a_h(x)=mu(q), and
Gadd >> Q^(1/12).                                           (1)

Let cal L={ell_0} be a singleton label set. On the recovered source row define
c_q=mu(q),  nu_h=1,  U_{ell_0}(q,h,v,p)=1,                 (2)
and define the zero-one source-supported mask
chi_{ell_0}(v,p,h,q)=1
exactly when h belongs to I and the unique source atom in cal X having q-coordinate q belongs to cal Y, and define it to be zero otherwise. Then, on every retained atom x=(q,m,k) in cal Y and h in I,
a_h(x)=c_q nu_h U_{ell_0}(q,h,v,p)chi_{ell_0}(v,p,h,q)
      =mu(q)=-1.                                            (3)
The amplitude U_{ell_0} is constant, hence it is a one-term separated scaled-smooth projective amplitude with projective norm one, and chi_{ell_0} is a zero-one mask supported on actual source atoms.

Consequently the actual source equation and coprimality conditions, the exact reciprocal-modulus Mobius factor, an arbitrary common height scalar, the bounded separated scaled-smooth/projective type of U_ell, and the zero-one source-supported type of chi_ell do not, as abstract interface properties, imply
Theta_cl << Gadd^(-1) Q^epsilon                             (4)
for every epsilon>0. Indeed (4) fails on this family for every fixed epsilon<1/12 and all sufficiently large p.

This is a counterexample only to a theorem uniform over the displayed factor types and arbitrary source-supported zero-one masks. It does not assert that chi_{ell_0} is the undisclosed natural literal mask product of fact 294ac3b02b065aec, does not show that the actual literal U_ell chi_ell saturates, does not give a global lower bound for Aadd, and proves no PMD closure or Goldbach conclusion. Therefore a literal fixed-power proof must use an additional proved formula or structural property of the natural mask/amplitude beyond these abstract types, or cancellation from an earlier signed assembly.
55314e158bcbdc91.proof:
Fact 38bc0e88e17aef0e supplies the parameters and the actual-source subset cal Y in the first sentence, including the source equation qm+2pk=A because v=2 and n=2p, the bounds Q<=q,m<2Q and p>2Q, coprimality gcd(qm,2p)=1, the critical slope interval, the coefficient a_h(x)=mu(q)=-1 because every q in cal Y is prime, the lower bound Theta_cl>=1/2, and Gadd>>Q^(1/12).

We first prove that the q-coordinate is injective on all of cal X. Suppose (q,m_1,k_1) and (q,m_2,k_2) belong to cal X. Subtracting their two source equations gives
q(m_1-m_2)+2p(k_1-k_2)=0.
Since gcd(q,2p)=1, it follows that 2p divides m_1-m_2. But Q<=m_1,m_2<2Q gives |m_1-m_2|<Q, and the predecessor gives Q<2p. Hence m_1-m_2=0, so m_1=m_2; substituting back gives k_1=k_2. Therefore the source atom with a given q-coordinate is unique whenever it exists, and the definition of chi_{ell_0} is unambiguous.

The mask chi_{ell_0} has values zero or one, and its support is contained in the actual source set cal X. The definitions in (2) give, for every retained pair (h,x) with h in I and x=(q,m,k) in cal Y,
c_q nu_h U_{ell_0}(q,h,v,p)chi_{ell_0}(v,p,h,q)
=mu(q)*1*1*1=mu(q),
which proves (3). The constant function one is separated as the product of four constant one-variable functions, every scaled derivative of positive order vanishes, and its one-term projective norm is one. Thus all abstract factor-type assertions in the statement are satisfied.

Suppose (4) held uniformly for every coefficient family satisfying only those abstract assertions. Fix epsilon with 0<epsilon<1/12. On the constructed family, (1) gives Theta_cl>=1/2, while Gadd>>Q^(1/12), so Gadd^(-1)Q^epsilon<<Q^(-1/12+epsilon), which tends to zero as p, and hence Q=floor(p^(4/5)), tends to infinity. This contradicts Theta_cl>=1/2 for all sufficiently large p. Therefore (4) cannot follow uniformly from the listed abstract properties.

The final scope limitation follows because the constructed chi_{ell_0} was defined from cal Y for the purpose of the counterexample; no cited predecessor identifies it with the natural literal mask product. The proof therefore makes no assertion about cancellation for that undisclosed literal coefficient.

glossary.U_ell: A generic label-dependent separated scaled-smooth projective amplitude of the accepted coefficient interface.
glossary.U_{ell_0}: The constant-one separated scaled-smooth projective amplitude in the constructed coefficient.
glossary.a_h(x): The full coefficient assigned to source atom x at height h.
glossary.cal L: The singleton projective-label set used in this factorized counterexample.
glossary.chi_ell: A generic label-dependent zero-one source mask of the accepted coefficient interface.
glossary.chi_{ell_0}: The constructed zero-one mask selecting exactly the actual-source atoms in cal Y over the height interval I.
glossary.ell_0: The unique label in cal L.
glossary.nu_h: The common scalar height coefficient, set equal to one in this construction.

555ec032e5c78720.title: TINY STRICT-TOP C1 SELECTED-p RESONANCE FORCES HIGH POISSON HEIGHT. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100 and eta=kappa/20, and work in the literal strict-top C1 setting with beta_m<beta<6/5. Thus n=pv is squarefree, p is its unique rough prime, C=mathscr A h, m_eff=n/gcd(C,n), and h is a nonzero integer. Assume 1<=m_eff<Q^eta and that this same prime p is the prescribed first-nonresonant prime in an active exact pair mask D_{p,lambda} of fact ff228b0e569531f8. Let H<=|h|<2H be the signed dyadic height block containing h, and let H_P be the applicable Poisson height scale of fact 3286b0e75a3ea94a. Then p does not divide mathscr A, p divides h, H>=p/2, and for every fixed A>=2 and epsilon_0>0 the literal scalar marker-copy coefficient satisfies |c_lambda^epsilon(s,n,h)| <= C_{A,epsilon_0} Q^epsilon_0 (1+p/(2H_P))^(-A). Consequently, for every fixed zeta>0 and target B>0, after choosing A in terms of zeta,B,epsilon_0, the subchamber p>=H_P Q^zeta has scalar coefficient O_{B,zeta}(Q^(-B)). Hence the only tiny selected-p subchamber not eliminated by scalar Fourier decay is p<H_P Q^zeta. This is a literal support and scalar-coefficient localization. It does not infer p does not divide mathscr A h, does not delete m_eff=1, and does not by itself prove a complete source/modulus aggregate estimate
555ec032e5c78720.author: slava chan
555ec032e5c78720.statement: TINY STRICT-TOP C1 SELECTED-p RESONANCE FORCES HIGH POISSON HEIGHT. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100 and eta=kappa/20, and work in the literal strict-top C1 setting with beta_m<beta<6/5. Thus n=pv is squarefree, p is its unique rough prime, C=mathscr A h, m_eff=n/gcd(C,n), and h is a nonzero integer. Assume 1<=m_eff<Q^eta and that this same prime p is the prescribed first-nonresonant prime in an active exact pair mask D_{p,lambda} of fact ff228b0e569531f8. Let H<=|h|<2H be the signed dyadic height block containing h, and let H_P be the applicable Poisson height scale of fact 3286b0e75a3ea94a. Then p does not divide mathscr A, p divides h, H>=p/2, and for every fixed A>=2 and epsilon_0>0 the literal scalar marker-copy coefficient satisfies |c_lambda^epsilon(s,n,h)| <= C_{A,epsilon_0} Q^epsilon_0 (1+p/(2H_P))^(-A). Consequently, for every fixed zeta>0 and target B>0, after choosing A in terms of zeta,B,epsilon_0, the subchamber p>=H_P Q^zeta has scalar coefficient O_{B,zeta}(Q^(-B)). Hence the only tiny selected-p subchamber not eliminated by scalar Fourier decay is p<H_P Q^zeta. This is a literal support and scalar-coefficient localization. It does not infer p does not divide mathscr A h, does not delete m_eff=1, and does not by itself prove a complete source/modulus aggregate estimate.
555ec032e5c78720.proof:
Fact 9e3be7086c095ecb applies in the displayed literal C1 tiny range and proves p divides C=mathscr A h. On the other hand, equation (10) of fact ff228b0e569531f8 shows that the active prescribed-p pair mask contains the factor 1_{p does not divide mathscr A Delta}, where Delta is the pair determinant. If p divided mathscr A, then p would divide mathscr A Delta for every integer Delta, so that factor would vanish. Since the active mask is nonzero, p does not divide mathscr A. Combining p divides mathscr A h with p not dividing mathscr A and using primality of p yields p divides h.

The height h is nonzero. Therefore |h| is a positive multiple of p and |h|>=p. Since H<=|h|<2H, one has H>|h|/2>=p/2; weakening the strict inequality gives H>=p/2.

Fact 3286b0e75a3ea94a proves for every fixed A>=2 and epsilon_0>0 that
|c_lambda^epsilon(s,n,h)| <= C_{A,epsilon_0}Q^epsilon_0(1+|h|/H_P)^(-A).
Because |h|>=p, its right side is at most
C_{A,epsilon_0}Q^epsilon_0(1+p/H_P)^(-A),
and hence also at most the weaker displayed bound with p/(2H_P).

Now fix zeta>0 and B>0. If p>=H_P Q^zeta, then for sufficiently large Q,
(1+p/(2H_P))^(-A) <= 2^A Q^(-A zeta).
Choose epsilon_0>0 and then choose the fixed integer A so that A zeta>B+epsilon_0+1. The fixed factor 2^A C_{A,epsilon_0} is at most Q for sufficiently large Q, giving the asserted O_{B,zeta}(Q^(-B)) bound. The argument used the pair mask only to infer p does not divide mathscr A; it did not infer p does not divide the row numerator mathscr A h. Indeed it proves the opposite divisibility p divides mathscr A h in this chamber, so it is consistent with the no-go fact 02d47d6aa2984aae. No summation or vector-envelope estimate was used, proving the scope assertions.

glossary.tiny selected-p chamber: The literal strict-top C1 subchamber in which the unique rough prime p is the active pair-selected first-nonresonant prime and 1<=m_eff<Q^(kappa/20).
glossary.zeta: An arbitrary fixed positive exponent used to compare the selected prime p with the Poisson height scale H_P.

55733dfba03775a2.title: PRIMITIVE-CONDUCTOR DECOMPOSITION OF THE MIXED ROW KERNEL
55733dfba03775a2.author: slava chan
55733dfba03775a2.statement:
PRIMITIVE-CONDUCTOR DECOMPOSITION OF THE MIXED ROW KERNEL.

Let m>1 be an odd integer and put q=m^2. Define e_q(x)=exp(2 pi i x/q). Let a_0,c_0,u_1,u_2 be integers satisfying gcd(u_1u_2,q)=1. Let chi and psi be Dirichlet characters modulo q, extended by zero to integers not coprime to q. For ell modulo q define
 R_{chi,psi}(ell)
 =sum_{t modulo q}chi(a_0+u_1t)psi(c_0+u_2t)e_q(ell t).               (1)
Let chi be induced by a primitive Dirichlet character chi_star of conductor c_chi dividing q, and let psi be induced by a primitive Dirichlet character psi_star of conductor c_psi dividing q. Extend chi_star and psi_star to integers by zero on integers not coprime to their respective conductors. Put rad_m equal to the product of the distinct prime divisors of m. For squarefree d,e dividing rad_m define
 R_{d,e}(ell)
 =sum_{t modulo q;
       a_0+u_1t=0 modulo d;
       c_0+u_2t=0 modulo e}
   chi_star(a_0+u_1t)psi_star(c_0+u_2t)e_q(ell t).                    (2)
Then
 R_{chi,psi}(ell)
 =sum_{d dividing rad_m}sum_{e dividing rad_m}mu(d)mu(e)R_{d,e}(ell). (3)

For each pair d,e, the congruences in (2) are either incompatible, in which case R_{d,e}(ell)=0, or define one residue class
 t=t_{d,e} modulo lcm(d,e).                                         (4)
In the compatible case, with l_{d,e}=lcm(d,e),
 R_{d,e}(ell)
 =e_q(ell t_{d,e})
  sum_{z modulo q/l_{d,e}}
   chi_star(A_{d,e}+u_1l_{d,e}z)
   psi_star(C_{d,e}+u_2l_{d,e}z)
   e_{q/l_{d,e}}(ell z),                                            (5)
where
 A_{d,e}=a_0+u_1t_{d,e},  C_{d,e}=c_0+u_2t_{d,e}.                    (6)
Thus (3) contains at most
 tau(rad_m)^2=4^(omega(m))                                          (7)
progression pieces. For every epsilon>0 there is a constant C_epsilon such that
 4^(omega(m))<=C_epsilon m^epsilon.                                 (8)

Equations (3)-(8) are an exact conductor and additive-twist ledger. They do not estimate any piece in (5). Each nonzero piece retains two shifted primitive multiplicative characters, the additive twist modulo q/l_{d,e}, and shifts A_{d,e},C_{d,e}; no ordinary one-character Burgess or character-large-sieve theorem is asserted to apply.
55733dfba03775a2.proof:
For any integer x, an imprimitive character modulo q induced by chi_star satisfies
 chi(x)=chi_star(x)1_{gcd(x,q)=1}.                                   (9)
The unit indicator has the exact expansion
 1_{gcd(x,q)=1}
 =sum_{d dividing rad_m; d divides x}mu(d).                          (10)
Apply (9)-(10) to a_0+u_1t and c_0+u_2t in (1), expand, and interchange finite sums. This proves (3).

Because u_1 is a unit modulo every d dividing rad_m, the first congruence in (2) defines one residue class modulo d. The second similarly defines one class modulo e. The generalized Chinese remainder criterion shows they are compatible exactly when they agree modulo gcd(d,e), and then their intersection is one class modulo lcm(d,e), proving (4).

The integer l_{d,e} divides rad_m and hence q. Every t modulo q in (4) is uniquely t=t_{d,e}+l_{d,e}z with z modulo q/l_{d,e}. Substitute this into (2). The phase is
 e_q(ell t_{d,e})e_q(ell l_{d,e}z)
 =e_q(ell t_{d,e})e_{q/l_{d,e}}(ell z),
and the character arguments give (5)-(6).

There are 2^(omega(m)) divisors of rad_m, proving (7). Fix epsilon>0 and put P_0=4^(1/epsilon). Then
 4^(omega(m))=product_{p dividing m}4.
For every prime divisor p>=P_0 one has 4<=p^epsilon. The product over prime divisors p<P_0 is bounded by the finite constant
 C_epsilon=product_{p prime, p<P_0}max(1,4p^(-epsilon)).
Therefore
 4^(omega(m))
 <=C_epsilon product_{p dividing m}p^epsilon
 =C_epsilon rad_m^epsilon
 <=C_epsilon m^epsilon,
which proves (8).

glossary.A_{d,e}: the first shifted primitive-character argument at the progression origin
glossary.C_{d,e}: the second shifted primitive-character argument at the progression origin
glossary.R_{d,e}(ell): one primitive-character progression piece of the imprimitive mixed row kernel
glossary.chi_star: the primitive Dirichlet character inducing chi modulo m^2
glossary.l_{d,e}: the least common multiple of the unit-gate divisors d and e
glossary.psi_star: the primitive Dirichlet character inducing psi modulo m^2
glossary.rad_m: the product of the distinct prime divisors of m

55b350a4925c7e1b.title: ABSTRACT CLOSED-ENDPOINT COMPLETE-FREQUENCY THREE-ROUGH-PRIME \(C3_*\) TRACE
55b350a4925c7e1b.author: slava chan
55b350a4925c7e1b.statement:
ABSTRACT CLOSED-ENDPOINT COMPLETE-FREQUENCY THREE-ROUGH-PRIME \(C3_*\) TRACE.

Fix integers \(J,C_A,K\ge1\), a constant \(C\ge1\), and
\(0<\kappa\le1/100\). Put
\[
 \sigma=\kappa/100,\qquad
 \beta_1=6/5-3\sigma,\qquad
 \beta_m=6/5-12\sigma/5.
\]
Let \(Q\) be sufficiently large, let
\(\beta_1<\beta\le\beta_m\), and put
\[
 B=Q^\beta,\qquad H_T=B/Q,\qquad
 L=H_TQ^\sigma,\qquad S_0=H_T^2Q^{3\sigma},\qquad
 Z_*=2Q^{3/2-\beta-3\sigma}.
\]
Let dyadic \(V,P_1,P_2,P_3\ge1\) satisfy
\[
 C^{-1}B\le VP_1P_2P_3\le CB.                                  \tag{1}
\]
Put
\[
 \nu={\log V\over\log Q},\qquad
 a_i={\log P_i\over\log Q}\quad(1\le i\le3),
\]
and assume
\[
 0\le\nu\le2\beta-2+3\sigma,\qquad
 a_i\ge3/2-\beta-3\sigma\quad(1\le i\le3).                    \tag{2}
\]
Let \(\xi_v\) be supported on squarefree \(V\le v<2V\), with
\[
 v\le S_0,\qquad p\mid v\Longrightarrow p\le L,\qquad
 |\xi_v|\le\tau_J(v).
\]
Fix \(A\ne0\), \(|A|\le Q^{C_A}\), let \(|c_q|\le1\) on
\(Q\le q<2Q\), let \(G>0\), and put \(H_P=H_T/G\).
For every dyadic integer \(F\ge1\), let \(\nu_F(h)\) be supported on
\(F\le|h|<2F\) with
\[
 |\nu_F(h)|\le\tau_J(|h|),
\]
let
\[
 |\omega_F|\le C(J_0)\min\{1,(F/H_P)^{-J_0}\}
\]
for every fixed integer \(J_0\ge1\), and let \(\Psi_F\) be a
fixed-complexity uniformly scaled-smooth projective amplitude of projective
Fourier norm bounded by a fixed constant depending only on \(K\), supported
on the full dyadic rectangle in \(q,h,v,p_1,p_2,p_3\).

Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
T_{C3_*}={1\over H_P}\sum_F\omega_F
 &\sum_{Q\le q<2Q}c_q
 \sum_{F\le|h|<2F}\nu_F(h)\\
 &\sum_{\substack{V\le v<2V\\
 P_i\le p_i<2P_i,\ p_i\ {\rm prime}\ (1\le i\le3)\\
 p_i\ge Z_*,\ p_1<p_2<p_3,\ (vp_1p_2p_3,q)=1}}
 \xi_v\Psi_F\!\left({q\over Q},{|h|\over F},{v\over V},
                    {p_1\over P_1},{p_2\over P_2},{p_3\over P_3}\right)
 e_q\!\left(Ah(vp_1p_2p_3)^{-1}\right).
\end{aligned}                                                     \tag{3}
\]
There is no sharp joint product mask; (1) is a dyadic scale relation.
Assume the prime cells are refined so that order between different cells is
automatic, while before imposing distinct order the complete coefficient
and amplitude are symmetric under permutations of variables belonging to
the same cell.

If \(G\ge1\), then for some fixed \(\delta_{C3,F}>0\),
\[
 T_{C3_*}\ll GQ^{2-\delta_{C3,F}}.                              \tag{4}
\]
If \(0<\eta<\sigma\) and
\[
 Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\le G\le Q^{\sigma-\eta},
\]
then for some fixed \(\delta_{C3,N}>0\),
\[
 T_{C3_*}\ll Q^{2-\delta_{C3,N}}.                               \tag{5}
\]
The fixed savings and implied constants depend only on the displayed fixed
parameters, divisor orders and projective norm. The estimates include
\(H_P<1\), every actual integer-frequency block, all prime-slot
permutations after cell refinement, equal prime-scale cells, and every
pair- and triple-collision term introduced by exact symmetrization. They
permit legal one-variable, label-scalar and bounded-projective factors, but
no arbitrary joint mask. Taking \(\xi_v=-\mu(v)\) gives the abstract
\(C3_*\) marker coefficient. No literal-source, outer-\(g\), selected-cell,
PMD, DCE, endpoint-parent, or Goldbach claim is made.
55b350a4925c7e1b.proof:
Write
\[
 \epsilon_Q={\log(VP_1P_2P_3/B)\over\log Q}.
\]
By (1),
\[
 |\epsilon_Q|\le{\log C\over\log Q},\qquad
 \nu+a_1+a_2+a_3=\beta+\epsilon_Q.                              \tag{6}
\]
Choose \(Q\) sufficiently large that \(|\epsilon_Q|\le\sigma/4\).
Put
\[
 \ell=2\beta-2+3\sigma/2,\qquad
 r=3-2\beta-3\sigma/2,\qquad s_i=\nu+a_i.                       \tag{7}
\]
If \(\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}\), then (2) and (6) give
\[
 s_i=\beta+\epsilon_Q-a_j-a_k
 \le3\beta-3+6\sigma+\epsilon_Q.                                \tag{8}
\]
The gap from the right side of (8) to \(r\) is
\[
 6-5\beta-15\sigma/2-\epsilon_Q
 \ge9\sigma/2-\epsilon_Q
 \ge17\sigma/4.                                                  \tag{9}
\]
Here the first inequality uses \(\beta\le\beta_m\). Thus every
\(s_i\le r-4\sigma\).

On the other hand,
\[
 \max_i s_i\ge {s_1+s_2+s_3\over3}
 ={\,\beta+\epsilon_Q+2\nu\,\over3}
 \ge{\beta+\epsilon_Q\over3}.                                   \tag{10}
\]
The gap from the last expression to \(\ell\) is
\[
 {6-5\beta\over3}-{3\sigma\over2}+{\epsilon_Q\over3}
 \ge {5\sigma\over2}+{\epsilon_Q\over3}
 \ge {29\sigma\over12}>2\sigma.                                \tag{11}
\]
Choose an index \(i\) attaining the maximum in (10), and put formally
\(S=VP_i\), \(T=P_jP_k\). Equations (9)-(11) place the formal
\(S\)-exponent in
\[
 \ell+2\sigma<s_i<r-4\sigma.                                    \tag{12}
\]

We now pay the dyadic and coefficient taxes explicitly. Expand the
scaled-smooth projective amplitude into an absolutely summable logarithmic
Fourier series and absorb each one-variable mode into the corresponding
coefficient. The product \(vp_i\) lies in an interval of ratio four and
the product \(p_jp_k\) does also. Split each grouped product into at most
two dyadic intervals. The resulting fixed multiplicative endpoint changes
are \(O(1/\log Q)\) in exponent. Increasing \(Q\) once more, (12) leaves
every resulting \(S\)-block inside
\[
 Q^\ell\le S\le Q^r,\qquad ST\asymp B=QH_T.                     \tag{13}
\]
The grouped coefficient on \(S\) is divisor-bounded because
\[
 \sum_{vp_i=s}\tau_J(v)\le\tau_{J+2}(s),
\]
after allowing the prime indicator and the bounded Fourier mode. The
coefficient on \(T\), obtained by convolving the other two prime
indicators, is also bounded by a fixed divisor function. The condition
\((vp_1p_2p_3,q)=1\) becomes exactly \((st,q)=1\). No condition
\((s,t)=1\) and no sharp joint product mask is needed by fact
\(42720f6d803c4640\).

Fix an actual frequency block \(F\) and put
\[
 u_F=F/H_P,\qquad G_F=H_T/F=G/u_F.                              \tag{14}
\]
Split the block into \(h>0\) and \(h<0\). On the negative block write
\(n=-h\); its target is \(-A\), and its coefficient has the same divisor
bound. Apply fact \(42720f6d803c4640\) separately with target \(A\)
and target \(-A\), frequency length \(F\), factor scales \(S,T\),
and imbalance \(G_F\). The fact permits a fixed nonunit target and
unrestricted \((h,q)\). Its \(F^{-1}\) normalization is changed to the
literal \(H_P^{-1}=u_FF^{-1}\) normalization. Apart from a
\(Q^\epsilon|\omega_F|\) factor and an additional \(u_F^\epsilon\)
absorbed below, the four resulting terms are
\[
 G^{1/4}u_F^{3/4}Q^2H_T^{1/2}S^{-1/4},\qquad
 G^{1/4}u_F^{3/4}Q^{7/4}H_T^{1/2}S^{1/4},
\]
\[
 u_FQ^2H_TS^{-1/2},\qquad u_FQ^{7/4}H_T.                         \tag{15}
\]
Window (13) bounds their four baseline expressions by
\[
 Q^{2-3\sigma/8},\qquad Q^{2-3\sigma/8},\qquad
 Q^{2-3\sigma/4},\qquad Q^{2-1/20-12\sigma/5},                 \tag{16}
\]
respectively. The last inequality uses
\(\beta\le\beta_m\), since \(Q^{7/4}H_T=Q^{\beta+3/4}\).

Choose the epsilon in the energy estimate sufficiently small and choose
\(J_0\) sufficiently large. The arbitrary fixed-order decay gives
\[
 \sum_F|\omega_F|u_F^{3/4+\epsilon}
 +\sum_F|\omega_F|u_F^{1+\epsilon}\ll1.                         \tag{17}
\]
For \(u_F\le1\) this is a convergent geometric dyadic sum; for
\(u_F>1\) it follows from the stated decay. Thus (17) also includes
\(H_P<1\), when every actual integer \(F\ge1\) has \(u_F>1\).

If \(G\ge1\), use \(G^{1/4}\le G\) in the first two terms of
(15) and \(1\le G\) in the last two. Equations (16)-(17), with
epsilon smaller than the least displayed saving, prove (4) for
unrestricted prime boxes. In the range of (5),
\[
 G^{1/4}\le Q^{(\sigma-\eta)/4}.
\]
The first two terms in (16) therefore retain saving
\(\sigma/8+\eta/4\); the last two retain their displayed savings.
This proves (5) for unrestricted prime boxes.

It remains to impose distinct order inside equal prime cells. If exactly
two slots belong to one cell, symmetry gives
\[
 \sum_{p_1<p_2}\Phi(p_1,p_2)
 ={1\over2}\left(\sum_{p_1,p_2}\Phi(p_1,p_2)
                 -\sum_p\Phi(p,p)\right)                       \tag{18}
\]
for those slots, with the third slot fixed in its different cell. If all
three slots belong to one cell, symmetry and inclusion-exclusion give
\[
 \sum_{p_1<p_2<p_3}\Phi(p_1,p_2,p_3)
 ={1\over6}\left(\sum_{p_1,p_2,p_3}\Phi
 -\sum_{1\le i<j\le3}\sum_{p_i=p_j}\Phi
 +2\sum_{p_1=p_2=p_3}\Phi\right).                               \tag{19}
\]
These identities cover every equal-cell pattern; order between distinct
cells is automatic by hypothesis.

Consider a pair-collision term. Equality is possible only for two slots
on the same dyadic scale \(P\). Up to fixed divisor and logarithmic
factors, its remaining multiplicative mass is
\[
 VP P_k\ll B/P\ll B/Z_*,
\]
because the nonempty prime support \(p\in[P,2P)\), \(p\ge Z_*\),
implies \(P\ge Z_*/2\). A triple collision has mass
\(VP\ll B/P^2\ll B/Z_*\) and is no larger. Therefore on the \(F\)
block every collision term in (18)-(19) is bounded absolutely by
\[
 Q^\epsilon|\omega_F|u_F\,{QB\over Z_*}.                        \tag{20}
\]
Now
\[
 {QB\over Z_*}\ll Q^{2\beta-1/2+3\sigma}
 \le Q^{19/10-9\sigma/5}.                                      \tag{21}
\]
Summing (20) by (17), with epsilon sufficiently small, is
power-saving relative to \(Q^2\), and hence also relative to
\(GQ^2\) when \(G\ge1\). Thus every pair and triple collision created
by exact symmetrization is paid.

There are only finitely many equality partitions and
polylogarithmically many dyadic, sign, projective and legal inherited label
blocks. Shrinking the fixed savings absorbs them. Fact
\(047f4bc01579ce66\) identifies the abstract \(C3_*\) coefficient after
the constant-safe re-marker as \(-\mu(v)\); the analytic argument above
allows the more general divisor-bounded \(\xi_v\), so the stated
specialization follows without making a literal-source or outer-\(g\)
assertion.

glossary.T_C3*: The abstract complete-frequency three-rough-prime reciprocal trace with the constant-safe cutoff Z_*.
glossary.delta_C3,F: A fixed full-G saving exponent for the endpoint C3_* trace.
glossary.delta_C3,N: A fixed near-balanced saving exponent for the endpoint C3_* trace.

55c6f91ec7fd414f.title: DYADIC MEDIUM-SHARED-PRIME REMAINDER REDUCTION TO SHORT COMMON FIBRES AND LARGE ADDITIVE DENOMINATORS
55c6f91ec7fd414f.author: slava chan
55c6f91ec7fd414f.statement:
DYADIC MEDIUM-SHARED-PRIME REMAINDER REDUCTION TO SHORT COMMON FIBRES AND LARGE ADDITIVE DENOMINATORS.

Fix real numbers
 0<eta<1/12, 0<delta<4eta, 0<theta<1/2,
and let Q tend to infinity. Put
 U=Q^(1/3), B=Q^(4/3+o(1)), F_0=Q^(1-2eta+o(1)).            (1)
Let cal B be the squarefree integers b in [B,2B). For b in cal B put
 L_b=product_{r|b; b/r<F_0}r.                               (2)
Let cal R consist of those b for which L_b>1 and (L_b,N)=1, where N is a fixed positive integer. For b in cal R let pi(b) be the largest prime divisor of L_b and put s(b)=b/pi(b).

For a prime p define
 cal B_1(p)={b in cal R:pi(b)=p},
 cal B_2(p)={b in cal R:p|s(b)}.                             (3)
Let complex coefficients gamma_b satisfy
 sum_{b in cal R}|gamma_b|^2<=1.                             (4)
For each of at most two labels tau and each positive integer a<=2U, let beta_{tau,a}(u) be supported on
 cal U_a={u:Q<=au<2Q}
and satisfy |beta_{tau,a}(u)|<=Q^epsilon for every epsilon>0. (5)

For b_1 in cal B_1(p), put s_1=b_1/p. Let M_1 be the residue modulo s_1 determined by
 pM_1 congruent N modulo s_1,
with M_1=1 if s_1=1. For (n,s_1)=1 define
 C_1(n)=sum_{h|s_1; h>F_0/p; (h,M_1)=1}
       c_{s_1/h}(M_1)R^{M_1}_{s_1,h}(n)/phi(s_1/h),          (6)
where
 R^{M_1}_{s_1,h}(n)
 =product_{r|h}{e_r(M_1[n(s_1/r)]^(-1))+1/(r-1)}.            (7)

For b_2 in cal B_2(p), put q_2=b_2/p. Let
 cal Z_{a,u_1,u_2;b_1,b_2}
be arbitrary complex kernels supported on
 (au_1,b_1)=(au_2,b_2)=1
and satisfying
 |cal Z_{a,u_1,u_2;b_1,b_2}|
 <=Q^epsilon{1_{u_1s_1 congruent u_2q_2 modulo p}+1/p}.      (8)
For a dyadic P satisfying
 Q^(1/3+2eta+o(1))<=P<=Q^(1/2+theta),                        (9)
define
 cal K(P)
 =sum_tau sum_{a<=2U}sum_{u_1,u_2 in cal U_a}
   sum_{P<=p<2P}
   sum_{b_1 in cal B_1(p),b_2 in cal B_2(p)}
 beta_{tau,a}(u_1)overline(beta_{tau,a}(u_2))
 overline(gamma_{b_1})gamma_{b_2}
 C_1(au_1)cal Z_{a,u_1,u_2;b_1,b_2}.                        (10)
For an additional restriction S, write cal K(P;S) for the corresponding restricted array. Put
 A_P=Q^(1+delta)/P^2.                                       (11)

Then
 |cal K(P;a>=A_P)|
 <<Q^(7/3-delta+epsilon+o(1))+Q^(2+epsilon+o(1)).            (12)
Consequently every block P>=Q^((1+delta)/2) is completely paid by (12).

There is an exact additive-subface expansion
 R^{M_1}_{s_1,h}(n)
 =sum_{d|h} 1/phi(h/d)
   e_d(M_1[n(s_1/d)]^(-1)),                                 (13)
where e_1=1. In (13) put e=h/d. Define cal K(P;e>=A_P) by substituting (13) into (6) and retaining every pair (h,d) with e>=A_P. Then
 |cal K(P;e>=A_P)|
 <<Q^(7/3-delta+epsilon+o(1)).                               (14)
Thus the only additive subfaces not covered by (12) and (14) satisfy simultaneously
 a<A_P, e<A_P,
 d=h/e>F_0P/(2Q^(1+delta))
       =P Q^(-2eta-delta+o(1)).                              (15)
If 2P<=F_0^(1/2), every parent conductor h in this residual array has at least two prime factors.

The exact K_inc^rem array in fact b9560e346963b9e0, on an actual tensor of fact a4c3df18327fbfb1, satisfies (3)--(10): its expression outside C_1 is a kernel cal Z satisfying (8). Hence (12)--(15) apply without discarding its congruence A=D, its two literal Vaughan coefficient families, either gamma coefficient, or either row-two tensor.

No estimate for the residual array in (15), K_inc^main, another incidence cell, TRI-CROSS, ROP, CEN-MZB, C_small or Goldbach is asserted.
55c6f91ec7fd414f.proof:
For each p put
 g_i(p)^2=sum_{b in cal B_i(p)}|gamma_b|^2.
Both sets in (3) consist of multiples of p and have at most 3B/p elements. Hence Cauchy's inequality gives
 sum_{b_1 in cal B_1(p),b_2 in cal B_2(p)}
 |gamma_{b_1}gamma_{b_2}|
 <=3B g_1(p)g_2(p)/p.                                      (16)
The sets cal B_1(p) are disjoint. Every p in (9) exceeds B/F_0. A squarefree b<2B has at most three prime divisors exceeding B/F_0, because the product of four such primes is greater than 2B for large Q. Therefore
 sum_p g_1(p)^2<=1, sum_p g_2(p)^2<=3,
 sum_p g_1(p)g_2(p)<=sqrt(3).                               (17)

Put V_a=#cal U_a. The factors s_1 and q_2 are units modulo p. Thus
 #{u_1,u_2 in cal U_a:
   u_1s_1 congruent u_2q_2 modulo p}
 <=V_a^2/p+V_a.                                             (18)
Each local factor in (7) is at most 1+1/(r-1), the Ramanujan ratio in (6) is at most one, and the number of divisors is Q^(o(1)). Hence |C_1(n)|<=Q^(epsilon+o(1)). Using (5), (8), and (16)--(18) gives, for every set S of a-indices,
 |cal K(P;a in S)|
 <<Q^(epsilon+o(1))B{
      P^(-2)sum_{a in S}V_a^2+
      P^(-1)sum_{a in S}V_a}.                               (19)
Since V_a<=2Q/a,
 sum_{a>=A_P}V_a^2<<Q^2/A_P,
 sum_{a>=A_P}V_a<<Q log Q.                                 (20)
Equations (11), (19), and (20) give a first term BQ^(1-delta) and a second term BQ/P times a logarithm. The lower bound in (9) makes the second term Q^(2-2eta+o(1)). This proves (12). If P>=Q^((1+delta)/2), then A_P<=1 and all positive a occur in (12), proving the complete-block assertion.

To prove (13), expand the product in (7). Let d be the product of primes at which the exponential term is selected. The constants at the other primes multiply to 1/phi(h/d). At r|d, the r-local component of
 e_d(M_1[n(s_1/d)]^(-1))
is
 e_r(M_1[n(s_1/d)(d/r)]^(-1))
 =e_r(M_1[n(s_1/r)]^(-1)).
Thus CRT combines the selected local exponentials into the phase in (13).

The coefficient of the (h,d) subface after insertion in (6) is
 c_{s_1/h}(M_1)/
 {phi(s_1/h)phi(e)}, e=h/d.                                 (21)
For squarefree integers, the first Ramanujan ratio has modulus at most one and
 1/phi(e)<=Q^(epsilon+o(1))/e.
There are Q^(epsilon+o(1)) divisor pairs (h,d). Therefore selecting e>=A_P costs at most Q^(epsilon+o(1))/A_P relative to the unrestricted envelope in (19). With all a retained, (19) and the bounds
 sum_aV_a^2<<Q^2, sum_aV_a<<Q log Q
give
 |cal K(P;e>=A_P)|
 <<Q^(epsilon+o(1))A_P^(-1)
   {BQ^2/P^2+BQ/P}.                                        (22)
The first term is BQ^(1-delta). The second is
 BPQ^(-delta+o(1)), which is at most BQ^(1-delta+o(1)) because (9) and theta<1/2 imply P<Q for large Q. This proves (14).

On the complementary subfaces, a<A_P and e<A_P. Every parent h in (6) satisfies h>F_0/p>=F_0/(2P). Therefore
 d=h/e>F_0/(2PA_P)=F_0P/(2Q^(1+delta)),
which proves (15). If 2P<=F_0^(1/2), then every p in the dyadic block satisfies p^2<=F_0. Fact a547a4eea4d234ef now implies that every active h has at least two prime factors.

Finally, fact b9560e346963b9e0 defines the exact literal C_1 by (6)--(7). Its remainder bracket after factoring out C_1 consists of the Gram term and the three 1/(p-1) terms multiplied by the literal H_2 or J_2 tensor. Equations (21)--(24) in fact a4c3df18327fbfb1 prove exactly the bound (8), and its final coefficient argument proves (5) for both actual beta families. Thus the literal application satisfies every displayed hypothesis and all restrictions are coefficientwise, establishing the final application and scope.

glossary.A_P: the cutoff Q^(1+delta)/P^2 for the common short variable and the omitted centered cofactor
glossary.cal B_1(p): the squarefree modulus rows whose canonical prime is p
glossary.cal B_2(p): the squarefree modulus rows whose canonical complement is divisible by p
glossary.cal K(P;S): the dyadic abstract remainder array restricted by the additional condition S
glossary.cal Z: the row-two remainder kernel after the row-one shifted projector has been factored out
glossary.e: the omitted active-prime cofactor h/d in an additive subface

55dee3162ad8a011.title: GA-LOW-PRIM-PROD AND GA-LOW-dCOND: TWO ABSOLUTE PAYMENTS INSIDE THE LITERAL GOOD-\(\mathscr W\) NONRESONANT RAY MOMENT
55dee3162ad8a011.author: slava chan
55dee3162ad8a011.statement:
GA-LOW-PRIM-PROD AND GA-LOW-dCOND: TWO ABSOLUTE PAYMENTS INSIDE THE LITERAL GOOD-\(\mathscr W\) NONRESONANT RAY MOMENT.

Adopt one fixed orientation, anatomy \(\mathfrak a\in\{A,C_j\}\), frozen source/projective fibre, frequency block
\[
1\le F\le x^3,\qquad F\le |h|<2F,
\]
and dilator block
\[
\mathcal D\le d_\lambda<2\mathcal D
\]
from fact e55b27d39c593164. Retain its exact coefficient \(\widetilde c_\lambda(q,h)\), every literal mask in that coefficient, its nonzero integer target \(\mathscr A\), and its exact nonresonant moment
\[
\mathcal M_F^{({\rm NR})}(\mathcal D).
\]
For each supported coordinate \((q_i,h_i)\), \(i\in\{1,2\}\), put
\[
k_i=(q_i,|h_i|),\qquad
a_i=q_i/k_i,\qquad
b_i=|h_i|/k_i,\qquad
\epsilon_i=\operatorname {sgn}(h_i).
\]
Then \(k_i,a_i,b_i\) are positive integers, \((a_i,b_i)=1\), and
\[
(q_i,h_i)=k_i(a_i,\epsilon_i b_i).
\]
Put
\[
\Delta_0=\epsilon_1b_1a_2-\epsilon_2b_2a_1.
\]
The TT-star determinant in fact e55b27d39c593164 is
\[
\Delta=k_1k_2\Delta_0.
\]

Define \(\mathcal M_{F,{\rm lowpp}}^{({\rm NR})}(\mathcal D)\) by restricting the exact sum defining \(\mathcal M_F^{({\rm NR})}(\mathcal D)\) to
\[
a_1a_2\le {Q^2\over\mathcal D}.                                  \tag{1}
\]
Then
\[
\boxed{
\left|\mathcal M_{F,{\rm lowpp}}^{({\rm NR})}(\mathcal D)\right|
\le x^{o(1)}|\omega_F|^2{BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}.
}                                                                  \tag{GA-LOW-PRIM-PROD}
\]

For a term of the nonresonant moment put
\[
d=d_\lambda,\qquad
r={d\over(d,\mathscr A)},\qquad
m_d={r\over(r,\Delta_0)}.                                         \tag{2}
\]
Then
\[
m_d>1,\qquad d\mid \mathscr A\,m_d\,\Delta_0.                     \tag{3}
\]
Fix a real constant \(C>0\), and define
\(\mathcal M_{F,{\rm lowcond},C}^{({\rm NR})}(\mathcal D)\) by restricting the exact nonresonant moment to
\[
m_d\le(\log(2x))^C.                                               \tag{4}
\]
Then
\[
\boxed{
\left|\mathcal M_{F,{\rm lowcond},C}^{({\rm NR})}(\mathcal D)\right|
\le x^{o(1)}|\omega_F|^2{BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}.
}                                                                  \tag{GA-LOW-dCOND}
\]

Both estimates are absolute payments: every marker, Möbius, Fourier, target-gcd, fixed-\(U\), high, source, parent, ordering, equality, collision, deletion, provenance, coprimality and projective factor remains literal and only restricts the counted support. The same estimates remain valid after a union of \(x^{o(1)}\) exact copy, anatomy, orientation or frozen-label families. Consequently these two subfamilies may be removed from GA-RAY-SPEC in fact 31ebcf364862d83a. No estimate for the complementary subfamily, no full GA-RAY-SPEC or GA-NR-DIL estimate, no good-\(\mathscr W\) tail payment, and no Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
55dee3162ad8a011.proof:
Fact e55b27d39c593164 proves the following literal envelopes on the fixed fibre after extracting \(\omega_F\). First, for every supported coordinate,
\[
|\widetilde c_\lambda(q,h)|\le x^{o(1)}|\omega_F|.
                                                                    \tag{5}
\]
Second, the number of exact marked copies over \(B/2\le n\le2B\), including the divisor-bounded marker multiplicity, is
\[
Bx^{o(1)}.                                                         \tag{6}
\]
All physical quantities occurring below have polynomial size in \(x\), so every fixed divisor-function and logarithmic loss is \(x^{o(1)}\). We use (5)--(6) only as upper bounds; all literal masks remain present and can only decrease the absolute count.

We first prove GA-LOW-PRIM-PROD. For a positive integer \(a\), let \(N(a)\) be the number of signed coordinate pairs \((q,h)\) satisfying
\[
Q\le q<2Q,\qquad F\le |h|<2F,
\]
whose primitive positive denominator is
\[
q/(q,|h|)=a.
\]
Writing \(q=ka\), \(h=\epsilon kb\) gives
\[
Q/a\le k<2Q/a,\qquad F/k\le b<2F/k.
\]
If this set is nonempty, then \(b\ge1\) forces \(k<2F\). For each admissible \(k\), after dropping the condition \((a,b)=1\), the number of positive \(b\) is at most
\[
F/k+1.
\]
Both signs contribute a factor \(2\). The admissible positive integers \(k\) lie in an interval of ratio at most \(2\), and there are fewer than \(2F\) of them. Therefore
\[
N(a)\le
2\sum_{\substack{Q/a\le k<2Q/a\\k<2F}}(F/k+1)
\ll F.                                                            \tag{7}
\]
The implied constant is absolute, including the cases in which the interval contains only one integer. Also \(a<2Q\) whenever \(N(a)\ne0\).

Put \(X=Q^2/\mathcal D\). If \(X<1\), condition (1) is empty. If \(X\ge1\), then
\[
\#\{(a_1,a_2)\in\mathbb Z_{>0}^2:a_1a_2\le X\}
\le\sum_{a_1\le X}\left\lfloor{X\over a_1}\right\rfloor
\le X(1+\log X)
\ll {Q^2\over\mathcal D}\log(2Q).                                \tag{8}
\]
Equations (7)--(8) show that the number of ordered coordinate pairs satisfying (1) is
\[
\ll F^2{Q^2\over\mathcal D}\log(2Q)
=x^{o(1)}{Q^2F^2\over\mathcal D}.                                \tag{9}
\]
For each exact copy and each such coordinate pair, (5) bounds the absolute value of the coefficient product by
\(x^{o(1)}|\omega_F|^2\), while the additive phase has modulus one. Multiplying (9) by the copy count (6) proves GA-LOW-PRIM-PROD. This argument never removes a mask or separates a signed coefficient.

We next prove (3). Write
\[
c=(d,\mathscr A),\qquad d=cr,\qquad
\mathscr A=c\mathscr A_0.
\]
Then \((\mathscr A_0,r)=1\). Put \(g=(r,\Delta_0)\). Definition (2) gives \(m_d=r/g\). Since \(g\mid\Delta_0\),
\[
r\mid m_d\Delta_0.
\]
Hence
\[
d=cr\mid c\mathscr A_0m_d\Delta_0
=\mathscr A m_d\Delta_0,
\]
which proves the divisibility in (3). Facts 31ebcf364862d83a and 43c14e02f4c983a4 give
\[
d\mid\mathscr A\Delta
\Longleftrightarrow
r\mid\Delta_0,
\]
because the supported \(k_1k_2\) are units modulo \(d\). A term of the nonresonant moment has \(d\nmid\mathscr A\Delta\), so \(r\nmid\Delta_0\). Therefore \((r,\Delta_0)<r\) and \(m_d>1\), completing (3).

It remains to count (4). Fix an ordered supported coordinate pair in the nonresonant sector. Its primitive data and its nonzero integer \(\Delta_0\) are then fixed. Put
\[
L=(\log(2x))^C.
\]
For any contributing exact copy with \(m_d\le L\), equation (3) shows that for one integer \(m\) with \(1<m\le L\),
\[
d\mid\mathscr A m\Delta_0.                                      \tag{10}
\]
The integer on the right of (10) is nonzero and has polynomial size in \(x\): \(\mathscr A\ne0\), \(m\) is polylogarithmic, and fact 31ebcf364862d83a gives
\[
0<|\Delta_0|<8QF.
\]
Thus, for each fixed \(m\), the number of positive \(d\) satisfying (10) is at most
\[
\tau(|\mathscr A m\Delta_0|)=x^{o(1)}.
\]
Summing the at most \(L\) possible values of \(m\) still gives \(x^{o(1)}\) possible dilators \(d\).

For a fixed such \(d\in[\mathcal D,2\mathcal D)\), every copy has
\[
n=dv,\qquad B/2\le n\le2B.
\]
There are \(O(B/\mathcal D+1)=O(B/\mathcal D)\) possible positive integers \(v\): the existence of such a copy implies \(\mathcal D\le2B\), so the added \(1\) is absorbed by a constant multiple of \(B/\mathcal D\). The exact marker multiplicity for fixed \(n,d\) is \(x^{o(1)}\) by fact e55b27d39c593164. Consequently, for the fixed coordinate pair, the number of exact copies satisfying (4) is
\[
x^{o(1)}{B\over\mathcal D}.                                     \tag{11}
\]
There are \(O(Q^2F^2)\) ordered coordinate pairs in the two dyadic boxes. Multiplying this count by (11), the coefficient-product envelope (5), and the unit modulus of the phase proves GA-LOW-dCOND.

A union of \(x^{o(1)}\) exact families only enlarges the displayed \(x^{o(1)}\) factors. Both restrictions are literal subfamilies of the exact nonresonant moment, so fact 31ebcf364862d83a identifies their removal as a legal restriction of GA-RAY-SPEC. The stated exclusions follow because no term in the complementary subfamily was estimated.

glossary.GA-LOW-PRIM-PROD: The absolute payment for the literal good-W nonresonant ray-pair subfamily with primitive denominator product a_1a_2 at most Q^2 divided by the dilator-block scale.
glossary.GA-LOW-dCOND: The absolute payment for the literal good-W nonresonant ray-pair subfamily whose effective divisibility multiplier m_d is at most a fixed power of log(2x).
glossary.m_d: For one nonzero primitive ray determinant Delta_0 and one dilator d, the quotient [d/gcd(d,mathscr A)] divided by its gcd with Delta_0.

5772f2de626492b3.title: CRIT-LITERAL-NREG: SOURCE-SPECIFIC n-REGULARITY AND A UNIFORM FIXED-POWER LONG SCALE FOR THE COMPLETE CRITICAL PHYSICAL BLOCK. Fix tau>0 and one orientation. Work on the complete selected same-N critical projection of fact 328503a935cabe60, with selected bad target N=2x, and fix exact g,c, the cofactor variables d,e,kappa with q=de, and one frozen source, dyadic, fixed-U, high, parent, provenance, factorization and projective block. Do not isolate a proper deletion or marker leaf. Let
5772f2de626492b3.author: slava chan
5772f2de626492b3.statement:
CRIT-LITERAL-NREG: SOURCE-SPECIFIC n-REGULARITY AND A UNIFORM FIXED-POWER LONG SCALE FOR THE COMPLETE CRITICAL PHYSICAL BLOCK. Fix tau>0 and one orientation. Work on the complete selected same-N critical projection of fact 328503a935cabe60, with selected bad target N=2x, and fix exact g,c, the cofactor variables d,e,kappa with q=de, and one frozen source, dyadic, fixed-U, high, parent, provenance, factorization and projective block. Do not isolate a proper deletion or marker leaf. Let
t(n)=(ell-kappa n)/(de),                                        (1)
and let w_{d,e,kappa}(n) be the literal physical amplitude inherited from the source formula of fact dde1e246a629bcc4 after the orientation-neutral descent of fact 8d9feea8c44da2c8, excluding only mu(n) and exact arithmetic unit conditions.

Every nonunit label or predicate retained in this block is either:

(i) an outer scalar independent of n after the displayed outer data and block are fixed; or

(ii) one of the specified smooth source, fixed-U or dyadic factors in the original source formula, evaluated at n and t(n).

All auxiliary t- or kappa-dependent zero-one deletion and marker siblings have recombined pointwise to one by fact 328503a935cabe60. In particular no unrecombined hard n-selector occurs in w_{d,e,kappa}.

There is a fixed exponent C_reg, independent of the active block, such that
2 sup_y |w_{d,e,kappa}(By)|
 + integral_R |d/dy[w_{d,e,kappa}(By)]|dy
 + sup_y |d/dy[w_{d,e,kappa}(By)]|
 << (log x)^(C_reg).                                            (2)
The support in y is contained in a fixed compact interval of bounded complexity. Thus the family n maps to w_{d,e,kappa}(n) has uniformly logarithmic supremum, total-variation and scaled-Lipschitz norms.

Moreover, uniformly on the complete critical projection and in both orientations,
B >> x^(23/400),                                                 (3)
and hence, for all sufficiently large x,
B >= x^(1/20).                                                   (4)
Therefore the fixed-power length hypothesis B>=x^eta in fact 71389b22e6f49e13 is valid with eta=1/20 on every such block. No Mobius progression estimate, primitive-sector payment, critical-tail payment, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
5772f2de626492b3.proof:
We first audit every literal factor. Before later refinements, fact dde1e246a629bcc4 gives the physical source
mu(d_src)mu(r_src) log(m)log(k) W(dm/x) psi(d_src/D_*)
 Phi(d_src/D)Phi(m/M)Phi(r_src k/U)Phi(r_src/R)Phi(k/K),          (5)
where d_src and r_src are the two original source divisors, W, psi and Phi are fixed smooth functions, Phi has compact dyadic support, and all active dyadic product scales satisfy DM asymptotic to x and RK asymptotic to x.

In the forward orientation, the descent of fact 8d9feea8c44da2c8 is
d_src=gcq, r_src=gn, m=t(n), k=c kappa.
Thus the complete n-dependent part of (5), apart from the two logarithms, is
W(gcq t(n)/x) psi(gcq/D_*) Phi(gcq/D) Phi(t(n)/M)
 Phi(gn c kappa/U) Phi(gn/R) Phi(c kappa/K).                    (6F)
In the reverse orientation it is
d_src=gn, r_src=gcq, m=c kappa, k=t(n),
and the corresponding product is
W(gn c kappa/x) psi(gn/D_*) Phi(gn/D) Phi(c kappa/M)
 Phi(gcq t(n)/U) Phi(gcq/R) Phi(t(n)/K).                        (6R)
The logarithms are log(t(n))log(c kappa) in both orientations.

Fact 328503a935cabe60 proves on this complete projection that every auxiliary t- or kappa-dependent zero-one deletion sibling and marker descendant recombines to one. Its statement also identifies the remaining high, parent, target-gcd and factorization predicates, once their labels are fixed, as outer scalars. Source, provenance and projective labels merely select one of finitely or polylogarithmically many fixed smooth source blocks and do not impose a new pointwise n-selector. Hence (6F)-(6R), with their fixed smooth projective factors, exhaust all n-dependence. This proves the classification (i)-(ii).

Put n=By. The support Phi(n/B) implicit in the fixed dyadic block confines y to a fixed compact interval. From fact 8d9feea8c44da2c8,
q=de asymptotic to Q_c, kappa asymptotic to K_c,
t(n) asymptotic to T, and BK_c asymptotic to Q_cT.                (7)
Therefore
