|d/dy[t(By)/T]|=kappa B/(de T)=O(1),                             (8)
and
|d/dy log t(By)|=kappa B/(de t(By))=O(1),                        (9)
because de t(By) is asymptotic to Q_cT, which is asymptotic to BK_c, while kappa is asymptotic to K_c. Every t-dependent dyadic factor in (6F)-(6R) consequently has bounded y-derivative.

The factors depending directly on n have the same property. For example, gB is the physical dyadic divisor scale attached to n, so d/dy Phi(gBy/R) or d/dy Phi(gBy/D) is bounded on the corresponding orientation. In (6F),
gB(c kappa)/U is bounded
because gn is on the r_src-scale, c kappa is on the k-scale, and r_src k is restricted by Phi(r_src k/U). In (6R),
the derivative of gcq t(By)/U has magnitude gc kappa B/U and is bounded
because gc kappa times gB is the active dm-product scale appearing in the fixed-U cutoff. The W(dm/x) derivatives are identical, using DM asymptotic to x. Finally, psi(gBy/D_*) is either constant, or its derivative is supported where gBy/D_* lies in the fixed transition interval; on that transition its y-derivative is bounded. All higher fixed-order scaled derivatives obey the same bounds.

Thus every smooth factor has bounded y-supremum and first derivative on a fixed compact support. Only the two source logarithms contribute logarithmic size. The product rule proves the supremum and Lipschitz terms in (2), and integration over the fixed compact y-support proves its total-variation term.

It remains to prove the scale lower bound. Fact 3f2f255ea6845a50 records for every active strict-orientation selected label that the smaller physical divisor scale is at most 2x^(1/2), while the larger physical divisor scale exceeds
x^(9/16-1/200).                                                  (10)
In either orientation, B is the larger physical divisor scale divided by the exact outer gcd g. Since g divides both source divisors, it is at most a fixed factor times the smaller dyadic scale; the support of Phi gives
g <= 4x^(1/2).                                                   (11)
Consequently
B >> x^(9/16-1/200-1/2)=x^(23/400),                             (12)
which is (3). Since 23/400>1/20, (4) follows for sufficiently large x. This supplies the exact fixed eta required by fact 71389b22e6f49e13, without yet applying that fact.

glossary.C_reg: A fixed exponent controlling the logarithmic supremum, total variation, and scaled Lipschitz norm of the complete literal n-amplitude.
glossary.d_src: The original first source divisor d before outer-gcd normalization.
glossary.r_src: The original second source divisor r before outer-gcd normalization.
glossary.w_{d,e,kappa}: The source-specific complete literal physical amplitude as a function of n after q=de and kappa are fixed, excluding mu(n) and exact arithmetic unit conditions.

57a4d0753d8f290d.title: PRIMITIVE-SIGNED-RAY COMPRESSION OF ONE LITERAL GA ANATOMY, EXACT PHYSICAL PROPORTIONAL-RAY PROJECTOR, AND RAY-LEVEL RESONANCE
57a4d0753d8f290d.author: slava chan
57a4d0753d8f290d.statement:
PRIMITIVE-SIGNED-RAY COMPRESSION OF ONE LITERAL GA ANATOMY, EXACT PHYSICAL PROPORTIONAL-RAY PROJECTOR, AND RAY-LEVEL RESONANCE.

Adopt the exact one-orientation setting of fact e55b27d39c593164. Fix one anatomy
\[
 \mathfrak a\in\{A,C_\ell\},
\]
one dilator block
\[
 \mathcal D\le d_\lambda<2\mathcal D,
\]
and one frequency block
\[
 1\le F\le x^3,\qquad F\le |h|<2F.
\]
Restrict every marked copy and moment below to this fixed anatomy and these blocks. Every exact marked copy \(\lambda\) has
\[
 n=d_\lambda v_\lambda,\qquad (d_\lambda,v_\lambda)=1,
\]
and its post-reciprocity coefficient
\(\widetilde c_\lambda(q,h)\), extended by zero to all integer pairs, is supported only when
\[
 Q\le q<2Q,\qquad F\le |h|<2F,\qquad (q,n)=1.
\]
Put \(\mathscr A=N/g\ne0\), and define the exact row
\[
 K_{\lambda}
 =
 \sum_{q,h}\widetilde c_\lambda(q,h)
 e_{d_\lambda}\!\left(\mathscr A h(qv_\lambda)^{-1}\right).       \tag{1}
\]

A primitive signed ray is a triple
\[
 R=(\epsilon,a,b),\qquad
 \epsilon\in\{-1,1\},\quad a,b\text{ positive integers},\quad (a,b)=1.
\]
For a fixed \(\lambda\), let \(\mathscr R_\lambda\) be the finite set of primitive signed rays for which
\[
 \mathscr I_\lambda(R)
 =
 \{k\text{ a positive integer}:
   \widetilde c_\lambda(ka,\epsilon kb)\ne0\}
\]
is nonempty. Define
\[
 C_\lambda(R)
 =\sum_{k\in\mathscr I_\lambda(R)}
   \widetilde c_\lambda(ka,\epsilon kb),                         \tag{2}
\]
and
\[
 P_\lambda(R)
 =e_{d_\lambda}\!\left(
   \mathscr A\epsilon b(a v_\lambda)^{-1}\right).                \tag{3}
\]
The inverse in (3) exists. Then
\[
 K_{\lambda}
 =\sum_{R\in\mathscr R_\lambda}P_\lambda(R)C_\lambda(R).         \tag{4}
\]

For two rays
\[
 R=(\epsilon,a,b),\qquad R'=(\epsilon',a',b'),
\]
put
\[
 \delta(R,R')=\epsilon b a'-\epsilon' b'a.                       \tag{5}
\]
If \(R\ne R'\), then
\[
 \delta(R,R')\ne0,\qquad |\delta(R,R')|<8QF.                     \tag{6}
\]
Moreover
\[
 P_\lambda(R)\overline{P_\lambda(R')}
 =
 e_{d_\lambda}\!\left(
 \mathscr A\delta(R,R')(aa'v_\lambda)^{-1}\right).               \tag{7}
\]
For supported scalings \(k\in\mathscr I_\lambda(R)\) and
\(k'\in\mathscr I_\lambda(R')\), put
\[
 q_1=ka,\quad h_1=\epsilon kb,\quad
 q_2=k'a',\quad h_2=\epsilon'k'b',
\]
and
\[
 \Delta=h_1q_2-h_2q_1.
\]
Then
\[
 \Delta=kk'\delta(R,R'),\qquad
 d_\lambda\mid\mathscr A\Delta
 \Longleftrightarrow
 d_\lambda\mid\mathscr A\delta(R,R').                            \tag{8}
\]
Thus the fully-resonant/nonresonant selector is constant on every ordered pair of primitive signed rays; it is independent of both scaling variables.

Let
\(\mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}(\mathcal D)\),
\(\mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{(0)}(\mathcal D)\),
\(\mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{({\rm FR})}(\mathcal D)\), and
\(\mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{({\rm NR})}(\mathcal D)\)
be the restrictions to the fixed anatomy of the exact moments in fact e55b27d39c593164. Then
\[
 \mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{(0)}(\mathcal D)
 =\sum_{n,\lambda}\sum_{R\in\mathscr R_\lambda}
 |C_\lambda(R)|^2,                                               \tag{9}
\]
\[
 \mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}(\mathcal D)
 -\mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{(0)}(\mathcal D)
 =
 \sum_{n,\lambda}
 \sum_{\substack{R,R'\in\mathscr R_\lambda\\R\ne R'}}
 P_\lambda(R)\overline{P_\lambda(R')}
 C_\lambda(R)\overline{C_\lambda(R')},                           \tag{10}
\]
and, for each of the two labels \(S={\rm FR}\) and \(S={\rm NR}\),
\[
 \mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{(S)}(\mathcal D)
 =
 \sum_{n,\lambda}
 \sum_{\substack{R,R'\in\mathscr R_\lambda\\R\ne R'}}
 {\bf1}_{S}\!\left(d_\lambda,\mathscr A\delta(R,R')\right)
 P_\lambda(R)\overline{P_\lambda(R')}
 C_\lambda(R)\overline{C_\lambda(R')},                           \tag{11}
\]
where
\[
 {\bf1}_{\rm FR}(d,X)={\bf1}_{d\mid X},\qquad
 {\bf1}_{\rm NR}(d,X)={\bf1}_{d\nmid X}.
\]
Consequently GA-OFF-SYN from fact c7970d9d1337bd09 is exactly the estimate of the signed anatomy-restricted off-ray form (10), and the anatomy-restricted GA-NR-DIL sector is exactly the nonresonant ray-pair form in (11). The physical proportional-ray projector has been inserted before any dual-shift transform, row-pair absolute value, or norm.

There is a sharp generic ray-space obstruction. For one fixed \(\lambda\), put \(m_\lambda=|\mathscr R_\lambda|\), and let \(T_\lambda\) be the Hermitian operator whose quadratic form is the \(\lambda\)-summand of (10). If \(m_\lambda\ge1\), the eigenvalues of \(T_\lambda\) are
\[
 m_\lambda-1\quad\hbox{with multiplicity }1,\qquad
 -1\quad\hbox{with multiplicity }m_\lambda-1.                    \tag{12}
\]
In particular,
\[
 \|T_\lambda\|_{\ell^2(\mathscr R_\lambda)\to
                    \ell^2(\mathscr R_\lambda)}
 =
 \begin{cases}
 0,&m_\lambda=1,\\
 m_\lambda-1,&m_\lambda\ge2.
 \end{cases}                                                     \tag{13}
\]
Thus subtracting the proportional-ray diagonal before a generic ray \(\ell^2\) norm does not itself give a saving; a proof of GA-OFF-SYN must exploit the literal dependence of \(C_\lambda(R)\), \(d_\lambda\), \(v_\lambda\), and the masks across marked copies or ray pairs. No estimate for (10) or (11), no GA-OFF-SYN, no GA-NR-DIL, no good-\(\mathscr W\) payment, and no Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
57a4d0753d8f290d.proof:
Every pair in the support of \(\widetilde c_\lambda\) has a unique representation
\[
 \epsilon=\operatorname{sgn}(h),\qquad
 k=(q,|h|),\qquad
 a=q/k,\qquad b=|h|/k.
\]
Then \(R=(\epsilon,a,b)\) is a primitive signed ray and
\((q,h)=(ka,\epsilon kb)\). Conversely every
\(R\in\mathscr R_\lambda\) and \(k\in\mathscr I_\lambda(R)\)
gives one supported pair. This is a bijection.

For a supported pair, \((q,n)=1\), with \(q=ka\) and
\(n=d_\lambda v_\lambda\). Hence
\[
 (ka,d_\lambda v_\lambda)=1.
\]
In particular
\[
 (k,d_\lambda)=(a,d_\lambda)=(v_\lambda,d_\lambda)=1.
\]
The last coprimality also follows from the defining factorization of \(n\).
Therefore
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 e_{d_\lambda}\!\left(
 \mathscr A(\epsilon kb)(ka v_\lambda)^{-1}\right)
 &=
 e_{d_\lambda}\!\left(
 \mathscr A\epsilon b(a v_\lambda)^{-1}\right)\\
 &=P_\lambda(R).
 \end{aligned}                                                   \tag{14}
\]
The right side is independent of \(k\). Group (1) by the displayed bijection and use (2). This proves (3)--(4).

For two rays, equation (7) follows by putting the two fractions over the common invertible denominator \(aa'v_\lambda\):
\[
 \epsilon b(a v_\lambda)^{-1}
 -\epsilon'b'(a'v_\lambda)^{-1}
 \equiv
 \delta(R,R')(aa'v_\lambda)^{-1}\pmod {d_\lambda}.
\]
If \(\epsilon\ne\epsilon'\), then
\[
 |\delta(R,R')|=ba'+b'a>0.
\]
If \(\epsilon=\epsilon'\) and \(\delta(R,R')=0\), then
\(b/a=b'/a'\). Since both positive pairs are coprime, this forces
\(a=a'\), \(b=b'\), and hence \(R=R'\). This proves the first part of (6). Because every ray has a supported scaling, one has
\[
 a<2Q,\qquad b<2F,\qquad a'<2Q,\qquad b'<2F.
\]
Therefore
\[
 |\delta(R,R')|
 \le ba'+b'a<8QF,
\]
proving the second part of (6).

For supported scalings, direct substitution gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \Delta
 &=h_1q_2-h_2q_1\\
 &=(\epsilon kb)(k'a')-(\epsilon'k'b')(ka)\\
 &=kk'\delta(R,R').
 \end{aligned}
\]
Both supported moduli \(ka\) and \(k'a'\) are coprime to
\(n=d_\lambda v_\lambda\), so
\((kk',d_\lambda)=1\). Multiplication by the unit \(kk'\) modulo
\(d_\lambda\) proves the equivalence in (8).

Expand (4):
\[
 |K_{\lambda}|^2
 =
 \sum_{R,R'\in\mathscr R_\lambda}
 P_\lambda(R)\overline{P_\lambda(R')}
 C_\lambda(R)\overline{C_\lambda(R')}.                           \tag{15}
\]
By the unique primitive-ray representation, \(\Delta=0\) holds exactly when
\(R=R'\): equality when \(R=R'\) follows from the factorization above, while for distinct rays it is excluded by (6). On the diagonal,
\(|P_\lambda(R)|=1\). Summing the diagonal of (15) over the exact fixed-anatomy
\((n,\lambda)\)-support gives (9); summing its complement gives (10).

For \(R\ne R'\), equation (6) gives \(\Delta\ne0\), and equation (8) makes the FR/NR selector constant across \(k,k'\). Therefore the sums over \(k,k'\) factor into
\(C_\lambda(R)\overline{C_\lambda(R')}\). Equation (7) is the remaining phase. Summing over all exact fixed-anatomy copies proves (11). Fact c7970d9d1337bd09 defines GA-OFF-SYN for precisely this fixed anatomy and the range \(1\le F\le x^3\); fact e55b27d39c593164 defines its restricted NR sector. This proves the stated interface consequences.

It remains to prove (12)--(13). Fix \(\lambda\), write
\[
 u_\lambda(R)=\overline{P_\lambda(R)},
\]
and regard \(C_\lambda=(C_\lambda(R))_R\) as a column vector. Since
\(|P_\lambda(R)|=1\),
\[
 \|u_\lambda\|_2^2=m_\lambda.
\]
The \(\lambda\)-summand of (10) is
\[
 C_\lambda^*
 \left(u_\lambda u_\lambda^*-I\right)C_\lambda.                 \tag{16}
\]
The rank-one operator \(u_\lambda u_\lambda^*\) has eigenvalue
\(m_\lambda\) on the span of \(u_\lambda\) and eigenvalue \(0\) on its orthogonal complement. Subtracting \(I\) gives (12). When \(m_\lambda=1\), the only eigenvalue is \(0\). When \(m_\lambda\ge2\), the largest absolute eigenvalue is \(m_\lambda-1\). This proves (13). Because no estimate for the literal vectors \(C_\lambda\) or their cross-copy arithmetic was used, all final limitations follow.

glossary.C_lambda(R): The exact sum of literal post-reciprocity coefficients over all supported scalings on one primitive signed ray.
glossary.K_lambda: The exact post-reciprocity reciprocal row for one marked copy in the fixed anatomy and blocks.
glossary.M_a,F^(S)(D): The restriction of the exact GA moment sector S to the fixed anatomy a, frequency block F, and dilator block D.
glossary.P_lambda(R): The reciprocal phase attached to one primitive signed ray.
glossary.T_lambda: The Hermitian off-ray operator for one marked copy.
glossary.physical proportional-ray projector: The raywise diagonal whose quadratic form is the Delta-zero moment.
glossary.primitive ray determinant: The nonzero integer delta(R,R')=epsilon b a'-epsilon' b'a attached to two distinct primitive signed rays.
glossary.primitive signed ray: A triple R=(epsilon,a,b) with sign epsilon and coprime positive coordinates a,b, representing the supported pairs (q,h)=(ka,epsilon kb).

58c03698e1b077c3.title: EXACT DUKE--FRIEDLANDER--IWANIEC REDUCTION AND SHARP POWER GAP FOR THE ACTUAL-Z_mid g=1, |h|=1 UPPER BOUNDARY
58c03698e1b077c3.author: slava chan
58c03698e1b077c3.statement:
EXACT DUKE--FRIEDLANDER--IWANIEC REDUCTION AND SHARP POWER GAP FOR THE ACTUAL-Z_mid g=1, |h|=1 UPPER BOUNDARY.

Assume the selected forced-high forward literal source and notation of facts 152484e836f90c47 and 06aa6fe1a991b7b5. Restrict the only potentially nonzero hard upper face to the exact outer-gcd layer g=1 and the conjugate frequency pair h=±1. Put Q=D, B=R and
u_{a,b}=(N-b^(3/2))/a.
Let mathfrak B_{1,1} be the complete packet on one fixed dyadic source label, with every literal Möbius, logarithmic, smooth, dyadic, fixed-U, high, parent, tag, unit, anatomy and provenance factor inherited from facts 60b26a9b6f79467a, 77d7a3419a07305c and 7131a06664967733, but with no additional arbitrary joint deletion mask.

The packet is an x^{o(1)}-cost finite sum of forms

  sum_{a~Q,b~B,(a,b)=1} alpha_a beta_b G_end(a,b) e_b(N a^{-1}),     (1)

where bars denote multiplicative inverses, ||alpha||_2<=Q^(1/2)x^{o(1)}, ||beta||_2<=B^(1/2)x^{o(1)}, and, for 0<=j,k<=2,

  |partial_a^j partial_b^k G_end(a,b)|
     <= x^{o(1)} Q^{-j}B^{-k}.                                      (2)

More precisely, apart from the harmless constant from pairing h=±1,

  G_end(a,b)=F_{1,a,b}(u_{a,b}) e(-u_{a,b}/b),                       (3)

with the literal smooth and logarithmic factors retained.

Duke--Friedlander--Iwaniec, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), Theorem 1 and its weighted Corollary therefore give

 |mathfrak B_{1,1}|
  <= x^{o(1)} Q^(1/2)B^(1/2)
       {(Q+B)^(1/2)+(1+N/(QB))^(1/2)Q}.                              (4)

If the endpoint amplitude in (3) is nonzero, the physical source support forces

 Q=x^(1/2+o(1)),   B=x^(2/3+o(1))=Q^(4/3+o(1)),
 N/(QB)=x^(-1/6+o(1)).                                               (5)

Consequently (4) becomes

 |mathfrak B_{1,1}| <= x^(13/12+o(1)).                               (6)

Relative to the absolute QB=x^(7/6+o(1)) boundary scale, this is a gain x^(-1/12+o(1))=Q^(-1/6+o(1)). It does not imply the MZB target O(x^(1-delta)) for any fixed delta>0: after (6) an additional x^(-1/12-delta), equivalently Q^(-1/6-2delta+o(1)), is still required. Thus a total Q^(-1/3-fixed) boundary gain is the first unresolved quantitative supplier even in this smallest g=1, |h|=1 packet.

This is an exact positive theorem application and scale no-fit, not an impossibility theorem. It asserts no estimate for |h|>1, g>1, the derivative-integral term, arbitrary joint masks, the complete MZB operator, endpoint capture, C2 selection, four-prime equivalence, or Goldbach.
58c03698e1b077c3.proof:
1. Exact reciprocity and the DFI kernel.

For g=1 and h=1, fact 152484e836f90c47 gives the upper face, up to the fixed factor -1/(2 pi i), as

 F_{1,a,b}(u_{a,b}) e_a(-N b^{-1}) e(sqrt(b)/a),
 u_{a,b}=(N-b^(3/2))/a.                                               (7)

The additive reciprocity identity already proved in that fact is

 e_a(-N b^{-1})=e_b(N a^{-1})e(-N/(ab)).                              (8)

Because

 sqrt(b)/a-N/(ab)=(b^(3/2)-N)/(ab)=-u_{a,b}/b,                        (9)

(7) is exactly

 F_{1,a,b}(u_{a,b})e(-u_{a,b}/b)e_b(N a^{-1}).                        (10)

There is no Taylor approximation and no discarded square-root error. The h=-1 face is the complex conjugate because the literal source amplitude and every inherited mask are real and h-symmetric, as in facts 152484e836f90c47 and 77d7a3419a07305c. It costs only a factor two. Formula (10) is the kernel in (1) with the fixed positive DFI numerator N, inverse variable a and varying modulus b.

2. Literal-mask separation.

On g=1 one has d=a, r=b and (a,b)=1. In the source formula of fact 60b26a9b6f79467a, mu(a) and every d-side cutoff are a-only coefficients. The factor mu(b), every condition on the factorization of r=b, the forward parent and least-divisor tag of fact 77d7a3419a07305c, every target-unit condition, and every normalized anatomy or marker-provenance coefficient are b-only coefficients once the dyadic label, g and h are fixed. The high/residual and fixed-parent predicates are label scalars. All fixed-U, logarithmic, W, psi and Phi factors are either one-variable smooth factors or are already part of the literal joint amplitude F_{1,a,b}(u_{a,b}); none is deleted.

The parent/tag predicates may be inserted into beta_b because DFI permits arbitrary complex one-variable coefficients. For each aggregate anatomy class, fact 7131a06664967733 proves that its recombined b-coefficient has absolute value at most one, and that the total absolute variation of its internal interval-prime or stopping copies is one. The finitely many parent, sign, tag and provenance classes and the polylogarithmically many smooth/dyadic separations therefore cost x^{o(1)}. It follows that the resulting coefficient sequences satisfy

 ||alpha||_2<=Q^(1/2)x^{o(1)},  ||beta||_2<=B^(1/2)x^{o(1)}.           (11)

This proves the asserted exact mask interface. An arbitrary new joint zero-one mask depending simultaneously on a and b would not have this separation and is explicitly excluded.

3. Endpoint smoothness.

Suppose G_end(a,b) is nonzero. Scaled support gives

 a~D=Q, b~R=B, u_{a,b}~M, sqrt(b)~K,
 DM~x, RK~x.                                                          (12)

The first two scaled derivatives of u are generated by

 a partial_a u=-u,
 b partial_b u=-(3/2)b^(3/2)/a.                                      (13)

The endpoint support sqrt(b)~K together with b~R and RK~x gives b^(3/2)~x. Since aM~DM~x, both expressions in (13), and their first further scaled derivatives, are O(M). The original source family is uniformly scaled-smooth. The product and chain rules therefore give, for 0<=j,k<=2,

 |partial_a^j partial_b^k F_{1,a,b}(u_{a,b})|
   <= (log x)^2 Q^{-j}B^{-k}                                         (14)

after harmless enlargement of the fixed source constant. Moreover u/b~M/B, and (12) below will give M/B=x^(-1/6+o(1)); directly from (13), every first or second scaled derivative of u/b is O(1) on the endpoint support. Thus multiplication by e(-u/b) preserves (14). Absorbing (log x)^2 and the finite separations into x^{o(1)} proves (2).

4. The external theorem and its application.

DFI97 Theorem 1 states the following. Let A_DFI be a positive integer and let alpha_m,beta_n be arbitrary complex coefficients supported on M_DFI<m<=2M_DFI and N_DFI<n<=2N_DFI. Then

 |sum_{(m,n)=1} alpha_m beta_n e_n(A_DFI m^{-1})|
 <= C_epsilon ||alpha||_2||beta||_2
    {(M_DFI+N_DFI)^(1/2)
      +(1+A_DFI/(M_DFI N_DFI))^(1/2)min(M_DFI,N_DFI)}
    (A_DFI M_DFI N_DFI)^epsilon.                                    (15)

Its weighted Corollary states that the same bound holds after multiplication by a joint smooth weight G(m,n) satisfying

 |partial_m^j partial_n^k G(m,n)|<=eta^(j+k)m^(-j)n^(-k),
 0<=j,k<=2, eta>=1,                                                   (16)

with an additional factor eta^2. The proof extends the weight to a slightly larger dyadic rectangle and uses two-dimensional Fourier inversion; hence it accepts the joint endpoint weight (3), not only a product weight.

Apply (15)-(16) with

 A_DFI=N, M_DFI=Q, N_DFI=B, m=a, n=b.                                 (17)

Equations (1)-(3), (11) and the scaled derivative bound (2) verify every hypothesis; the factor eta^2 is x^{o(1)}. Since B>Q on the selected forward source, min(Q,B)=Q. This gives (4).

5. Physical scale and the sharp gap.

The source-cutoff label in fact 60b26a9b6f79467a satisfies

 D_*/2<D<=2x^(1/2),
 D_*=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B_src),                                         (18)

so Q=D=x^(1/2+o(1)). If the endpoint amplitude is nonzero, (12) gives b~B, sqrt(b)~K and BK=RK~x. Hence

 B^(3/2)~x,
 B=x^(2/3+o(1))=Q^(4/3+o(1)).                                       (19)

Also N=2x, so

 N/(QB)=x^(-1/6+o(1)).                                                (20)

Now B^(1/2)=x^(1/3+o(1)) while Q=x^(1/2+o(1)). Therefore the braces in (4) are Qx^{o(1)}, and (11) gives

 |mathfrak B_{1,1}|
 <=x^{o(1)}(QB)^(1/2)Q
 =Q^(3/2)B^(1/2)x^{o(1)}
 =x^(13/12+o(1)),                                                     (21)

which proves (6). The term count/absolute coefficient scale is QB=x^(7/6+o(1)), so (21) saves x^(-1/12+o(1))=Q^(-1/6+o(1)). To reach x^(1-delta), one must improve (21) by x^(-1/12-delta), equivalently Q^(-1/6-2delta+o(1)); relative to QB this is a total Q^(-1/3-2delta+o(1)) gain. No cited theorem supplies that additional power. This proves the precise no-fit and every stated scope restriction.

glossary.DFI97: Duke--Friedlander--Iwaniec, Bilinear forms with Kloosterman fractions, Inventiones Mathematicae 128 (1997), 23–43.
glossary.G_{end}(a,b): The normalized joint smooth endpoint amplitude F_{1,a,b}(u)e(-u/b), including all literal smooth and logarithmic source factors.
glossary.mathfrak B_{1,1}: The complete literal conjugate-paired upper actual-Z_mid boundary packet on the exact outer-gcd layer g=1 and frequency pair h=±1.

58d4898b66be0334.title: ULTRA-LONG-MU-\(N\): EXACT SIGNED CROSS-MODULUS MÖBIUS-CHARACTER VECTOR HANDOFF WITH JOINT \((h,t)\) ENERGY. Fix one strict-top outer row and orientation from facts \(f26c5b12eea4a623\) and \(544c7ba4db45c06f\). Write the original reciprocal modulus as \(q\asymp Q\), put
58d4898b66be0334.author: slava chan
58d4898b66be0334.proof:
The ULTRA-LONG term in fact \(391896a807980083\) is
\[
 -\sum_{\substack{mt=n\\m>Q^b,\ 1<t<Q^a}}\mu(m).
\]
Insert it into the exact row of fact \(b0a38f5e9ae7feb6\), fix (1), and use the complete-provenance expansion (2). The source gates
\[
 (g,qmt)=(q,mt)=1
\]
become \((q,g)=(m,g)=(t,g)=1\), together with \((mt,q)=1\). The latter is implemented automatically by characters extended by zero. Hence the box before character expansion is
\[
 -{1\over H_P}\sum_\rho\eta_\rho
 \sum_{\substack{q,m,t,h\\(q,g)=(m,g)=(t,g)=1\\(mt,q)=1}}
 \mu(q)\mu(m)A_\rho(q)C_\rho(m)D_\rho(t)E_\rho(h)
 e_q(Ah\overline{mt}).                                         \tag{9}
\]

For every unit \(u\pmod q\), orthogonality gives
\[
 {1\over\varphi(q)}
 \sum_{\chi\pmod q}\chi(u){\cal G}_q(\chi;c)
 =e_q(c\overline u).                                           \tag{10}
\]
Indeed, after inserting (3), the character sum forces \(uy\equiv1\pmod q\). This holds for arbitrary integer \(c\), so the target need not be a unit. Apply (10) with \(u=mt,c=Ah\). Since \(\chi(mt)=\chi(m)\chi(t)\), the \(m\)-sum is (4), the \(h,t\)-sum is the conjugate of (5), and the character sum is the inner product in (6). This proves (6) without taking an absolute value or deleting \(\mu(q)\).

For (7), let \(K_{\rho,q,g}(\chi)\) denote the unconjugated expression inside (5). Terms with \((t,q)>1\) vanish because \(\chi(t)=0\). On the remaining terms, \(t\) is a unit and
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \varphi(q)K_{\rho,q,g}(\chi)
 &=\sum_{\substack{h,t\\(t,qg)=1}}
 E_\rho(h)D_\rho(t)
 \sum_{y\pmod q}^{*}\chi(yt)e_q(Ahy)\\
 &=\sum_{x\pmod q}^{*}\chi(x)
 \sum_{\substack{h,t\\(t,qg)=1}}
 E_\rho(h)D_\rho(t)e_q(Axh\overline t),                       \tag{11}
\end{aligned}
\]
where \(x=yt\). Character orthogonality in (11) yields
\[
 \sum_{\chi\pmod q}|K_{\rho,q,g}(\chi)|^2
 ={1\over\varphi(q)}
 \sum_{x\pmod q}^{*}
 \left|\sum_{\substack{h,t\\(t,qg)=1}}
 E_\rho(h)D_\rho(t)e_q(Axh\overline t)\right|^2.
\]
Conjugation preserves the norm, proving (7).

Expanding (4) and applying character orthogonality gives
\[
 \sum_{\chi\pmod q}\chi(m_1)\overline{\chi(m_2)}
 =\varphi(q)
\]
exactly when \(m_1\equiv m_2\pmod q\) and both are units, and gives zero otherwise. Together with the \(g\)-gates this proves (8), including both Möbius signs.

Summing (6) over signed frequency blocks and dyadic \(M,T\) boxes reconstructs the complete ULTRA-LONG family. Fact \(544c7ba4db45c06f\) gives total projective mass \(x^{o(1)}\). If ULTRA-MU-VECTOR holds, the outer-\(g\) summation used in facts \(f26c5b12eea4a623\) and \(22ee06fc82829016\) converts the fixed-\(g\) bound into a fixed power saving at scale \(x\). The final scope statement follows because replacing the signed \(q\)-sum by a sum of \(q\)-wise norm products is a different, weaker operation.

glossary.ULTRA-MU-VECTOR: The signed cross-modulus bilinear vector estimate sufficient to pay ULTRA-LONG-MU-N without deleting the outer Mobius coefficient.
glossary.bf H_{rho,q,g}: The conjugated joint h,t Gauss/Farey source vector on the same character space.
glossary.bf M_{rho,q,g}: The long Möbius-character vector on one dyadic m-box.
glossary.cal G_q: The complete multiplicative Gauss transform of the additive phase modulo q.
glossary.delta_U: A proposed fixed positive saving exponent in ULTRA-MU-VECTOR.

5999a1878276ac78.title: HALF-CONV ALGEBRA ON ALL PRIME POWERS. For every integer j>=0 put a_j^{(1/2)}=(-1)^j binom(1/2,j). Define the multiplicative arithmetic function rho_{1/2} by rho_{1/2}(p^j)=a_j^{(1/2)} for every prime p and every j>=0. Equivalently, as a formal power series, sum_{j>=0}rho_{1/2}(p^j)X^j=(1-X)^(1/2). For arithmetic functions f,g define their Dirichlet convolution by (f*g)(n)=sum_{dm=n}f(d)g(m), with no coprimality condition on d,m. Then
5999a1878276ac78.author: slava chan
5999a1878276ac78.statement:
HALF-CONV ALGEBRA ON ALL PRIME POWERS. For every integer j>=0 put a_j^{(1/2)}=(-1)^j binom(1/2,j). Define the multiplicative arithmetic function rho_{1/2} by rho_{1/2}(p^j)=a_j^{(1/2)} for every prime p and every j>=0. Equivalently, as a formal power series, sum_{j>=0}rho_{1/2}(p^j)X^j=(1-X)^(1/2). For arithmetic functions f,g define their Dirichlet convolution by (f*g)(n)=sum_{dm=n}f(d)g(m), with no coprimality condition on d,m. Then
rho_{1/2}*rho_{1/2}=mu
on every positive integer, and |rho_{1/2}(n)|<=1 for every positive integer n. These conclusions require neither n nor either convolution factor d,m to be squarefree.
5999a1878276ac78.proof:
Write a_j=a_j^{(1/2)}. The generalized binomial expansion in the ring of formal power series gives sum_{j>=0}a_jX^j=(1-X)^(1/2). Therefore
(sum_{j>=0}a_jX^j)^2=1-X.
Comparing the coefficient of X^j yields
sum_{i=0}^j a_i a_{j-i}=1 if j=0, equals -1 if j=1, and equals 0 if j>=2.

The Dirichlet convolution of two multiplicative functions is multiplicative. For completeness, if gcd(m,n)=1, every factorization de=mn splits uniquely as d=d_1d_2 and e=e_1e_2 with d_1e_1=m, d_2e_2=n, gcd(d_1d_2,e_1e_2) not required; multiplicativity of the two functions then factors the convolution sum into the product of the corresponding sums for m and n. Hence rho_{1/2}*rho_{1/2} is multiplicative.

At a prime power p^j, the definition of convolution and the coefficient calculation give
(rho_{1/2}*rho_{1/2})(p^j)=sum_{i=0}^j a_i a_{j-i}.
This is 1 for j=0, -1 for j=1, and 0 for j>=2, exactly the prime-power values of mu. Since both sides are multiplicative, they agree on every positive integer. The sum at p^j includes all pairs p^i,p^(j-i), including pairs with a nontrivial common factor when 2<=i+(j-i); no coprimality restriction was inserted.

It remains to bound rho_{1/2}. One has a_0=1 and a_1=-1/2. For j>=2, the generalized binomial recurrence gives
a_j/a_{j-1}=(j-3/2)/j.
This ratio lies in [0,1) for j>=2. Thus |a_j|<=|a_1|=1/2 for every j>=1. If n=product_p p^{v_p(n)}, multiplicativity gives
|rho_{1/2}(n)|=product_{p|n}|a_{v_p(n)}|<=1.
This proof includes arbitrary prime exponents v_p(n), so it does not assume squarefreeness.

glossary.a_j^{(1/2)}: The coefficient (-1)^j times the generalized binomial coefficient binom(1/2,j).
glossary.rho_{1/2}: The multiplicative arithmetic function whose prime-power generating series is (1-X)^(1/2).

5a055e5081dba501.title: BOURGAIN--GARAEV FIXED-MODULUS BILINEAR RIGHT-HAND-SIDE CAP IN THE ULTRA-MU BENCHMARK. Let \(Q\) tend to infinity, let
5a055e5081dba501.author: slava chan
5a055e5081dba501.statement:
BOURGAIN--GARAEV FIXED-MODULUS BILINEAR RIGHT-HAND-SIDE CAP IN THE ULTRA-MU BENCHMARK. Let \(Q\) tend to infinity, let
\[
 \beta>{25\over24},
\]
and consider an idealized finite HB atom with total unweighted factor volume \(Q^{\beta+o(1)}\). Give all non-bilinear factor coordinates, all source masks, all coprimality taxes, and the normalized \(h\)-average for free. Fix two remaining factor axes of lengths
\[
 N_1=Q^{s_1},\qquad N_2=Q^{s_2},\qquad
 0<s_1,s_2<{1\over2}.
\]
For each fixed modulus \(m\asymp Q\), also grant a unit reciprocal target and initial intervals \([1,N_1]\), \([1,N_2]\), so that Bourgain--Garaev, arXiv:1309.1124, Theorem 3 applies directly.

For positive integers \(k_1,k_2\), the scale-dependent part of that theorem's right-hand side, divided by the trivial volume \(N_1N_2\), is
\[
 \mathcal R_{k_1,k_2}
 =
 \left(
 Q^{(k_1-1)s_1-1/2}+Q^{1/2-k_1s_1}
 \right)^{1/(2k_1k_2)}
 \left(
 Q^{(k_2-1)s_2-1/2}+Q^{1/2-k_2s_2}
 \right)^{1/(2k_1k_2)},                                      \tag{1}
\]
apart from factors which are \(Q^{o(1)}\) when \(k_1,k_2\) are fixed. Uniformly over all \(s_1,s_2\in(0,1/2)\) and all positive integers \(k_1,k_2\),
\[
 \boxed{\qquad \mathcal R_{k_1,k_2}\ge Q^{-1/24}. \qquad}      \tag{2}
\]
Thus the strongest fixed-power saving visible in the displayed Bourgain--Garaev bound on this ideal two-axis benchmark is at most \(Q^{-1/24}\).

Applying that theorem separately for every \(m\asymp Q\), and then summing the modulus and all frozen factor coordinates by absolute values, gives an ideal total right-hand side no smaller than
\[
 Q^{1+\beta-1/24+o(1)}.                                      \tag{3}
\]
Because \(\beta>25/24\), the exponent in (3) is larger than \(2\). Hence this direct fixed-modulus application cannot prove an \(O(Q^{2-\delta})\) ULTRA-MU estimate for any fixed \(\delta>0\), even after all the favorable simplifications above.

This is only a displayed-right-hand-side no-fit for a termwise fixed-modulus use of Bourgain--Garaev Theorem 3. It is not a lower bound for the actual source and does not exclude cross-\(q\) cancellation, more than two active axes, pre-absolute-value assembly, a source-linked Hilbert-valued theorem, or a different method. In the literal problem the target may be nonunit, the intervals are dyadic rather than initial, the modulus is varying squarefree, the joint \((h,t)\) vector and every mask must be retained, and the cross-\(q\) factor \(\mu(q)\) may not be deleted. No ULTRA-MU-VECTOR, ENDPOINT-DIAGONAL-\(N\), post-\(A\) tail, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
5a055e5081dba501.proof:
Bourgain--Garaev, arXiv:1309.1124, Theorem 3 states the following. Let \(I_1=[1,N_1]\), \(I_2=[1,N_2]\), let \(|\alpha_i(x)|\le1\), and let \((a,m)=1\). Uniformly for positive integers \(k_1,k_2\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \left|\sum_{x_1\in I_1}\sum_{x_2\in I_2}
 \alpha_1(x_1)\alpha_2(x_2)e_m(a\overline{x_1}\,\overline{x_2})\right|
 &<
 (2k_1)^{45k_1^2/k_2}(2k_2)^{45k_2^2/k_1}
 (\log m)^{2(k_1/k_2+k_2/k_1)}\\
 &\quad\times
 \left({N_1^{k_1-1}\over m^{1/2}}+{m^{1/2}\over N_1^{k_1}}\right)^{1/(2k_1k_2)}
 \left({N_2^{k_2-1}\over m^{1/2}}+{m^{1/2}\over N_2^{k_2}}\right)^{1/(2k_1k_2)}
 N_1N_2.
\end{aligned}
\]
The proof in that paper applies Hölder twice, reduces to reciprocal-energy moments \(J_{2k_i}(N_i)\), and inserts the paper's bound for those moments. Substituting \(m\asymp Q\) and \(N_i=Q^{s_i}\) gives (1).

If \(k_i=1\), then \(s_i<1/2\) makes the second summand
\[
 Q^{1/2-s_i}>1,
\]
so that axis supplies no negative power. Suppose \(k_i\ge2\). If both exponents in its parenthesis are negative, the negative saving exponent contributed before the outer power is
\[
 g_i(s_i)
 =\min\left\{{1\over2}-(k_i-1)s_i,\ k_is_i-{1\over2}\right\}.
\]
If one exponent is nonnegative, put \(g_i(s_i)=0\). The maximum of the displayed minimum occurs when its two entries are equal, namely at
\[
 s_i={1\over2k_i-1},
\]
and equals
\[
 g_i(s_i)\le {1\over2(2k_i-1)}.                              \tag{4}
\]
Therefore
\[
 \mathcal R_{k_1,k_2}
 \ge
 Q^{-\Delta(k_1,k_2)},
\]
where
\[
 \Delta(k_1,k_2)
 \le {1\over2k_1k_2}
 \left\{
 {1\over2(2k_1-1)}+{1\over2(2k_2-1)}
 \right\}.                                                   \tag{5}
\]
For \(k_1,k_2\ge2\), the right side decreases when either integer increases, so its maximum is attained at \(k_1=k_2=2\). There it equals
\[
 {1\over8}\left({1\over6}+{1\over6}\right)={1\over24}.
\]
Together with the \(k_i=1\) case this proves (2).

In the ideal benchmark, before cancellation there are \(Q^{\beta+o(1)}\) factor tuples and \(Q^{1+o(1)}\) moduli. A termwise application of the fixed-modulus theorem followed by absolute summation can reduce the two-axis tuple volume by at most the factor in (2). This yields (3). Finally,
\[
 1+\beta-{1\over24}>2
\]
is equivalent to \(\beta>25/24\). Thus the displayed theorem cannot imply the \(Q^{2-\delta}\) target in this benchmark.

glossary.Delta(k_1,k_2): The total possible negative exponent in the two scale-dependent parentheses.
glossary.g_i(s_i): The negative exponent available from the i-th parenthesis before the common outer moment power.
glossary.mathcal R_{k_1,k_2}: The scale-dependent relative right-hand-side factor in Bourgain--Garaev Theorem 3.

5a334011a0da2a70.title: SOURCE-PRESERVING ell=vk REINDEXING AND DIVISOR-SIZED v ASSEMBLY
5a334011a0da2a70.author: slava chan
5a334011a0da2a70.statement:
SOURCE-PRESERVING ell=vk REINDEXING AND DIVISOR-SIZED v ASSEMBLY.

Fix constants C>=1 and J>=1. Let Q>=2, let A be a nonzero integer with |A|<=Q^C, and let q,m be integers in [Q,2Q). Let p and v be positive integers and k an integer. Put
  ell=vk.                                                    (1)
Then the actual-source equation
  qm+vpk=A                                                  (2)
is equivalent to
  A-qm=p ell,  v divides ell,  k=ell/v.                     (3)
On this support the source phase of fact db067f4633c13fed becomes
  e_q(hk)=e_q(h ell/v)                                      (4)
for every integer h.

There is an exact reindexing with arbitrary provenance. Let cal P be any finite set of positive primes, let cal V be any finite set of positive integers, let xi_v be arbitrary complex weights on cal V, and let F(v,p,q,m,k) be any complex function. Then
  sum_{v in cal V}xi_v sum_{p in cal P}
    sum_{k in Z:qm+vpk=A}F(v,p,q,m,k)
 =
  sum_{p in cal P:p divides A-qm}
    sum_{v in cal V:v divides ell_p}
      xi_v F(v,p,q,m,ell_p/v),                              (5)
where
  ell_p=(A-qm)/p.                                           (6)
If ell_p is nonzero, the inner v-sum in (5) has at most tau(|ell_p|) terms.

Assume now that cal V is contained in [V,2V) with V<=Q^C and
  |xi_v|<=tau_J(v).                                         (7)
For every epsilon>0 and every nonzero ell_p,
  sum_{v in cal V:v divides ell_p}|xi_v|
  <<_{C,J,epsilon}Q^epsilon.                                (8)
The exceptional zero-cofactor sector is exact:
  ell_p=0  if and only if  qm=A,
and then (2) forces k=0 while every v in cal V is allowed. The number of pairs (q,m) in [Q,2Q)^2 with qm=A is at most tau(|A|)<<_{C,epsilon}Q^epsilon.   (9)

For a four-atom source tuple with common v and p, put
  ell_i=(A-q_i m_i)/p.
If at least one ell_i is nonzero, the common v must divide
  gcd{|ell_i|:ell_i nonzero},                               (10)
so its weighted l1 assembly is Q^epsilon under (7). If all four ell_i vanish, then all k_i vanish and every pair (q_i,m_i) lies on q_i m_i=A, a divisor-sized set by (9).

Thus ell=vk gives a source-preserving divisor-sized projective assembly of the v-coordinate after p,q,m are fixed, except for an explicitly divisor-sparse all-zero-cofactor sector. This is an exact coefficient reindexing only. It does not by itself estimate the OSC cross Gram of fact ad79e2b004abf5ec, does not grant the post-Cauchy xi_v/v norm before Cauchy, and makes no PMD or Goldbach conclusion.
5a334011a0da2a70.proof:
Definition (1) gives vp k=p ell, so (2) immediately implies the first equation in (3), v divides ell, and k=ell/v. Conversely, substituting (3) gives
  qm+vpk=qm+p ell=A,
proving the equivalence. Equation (4) is substitution into the phase identity of fact db067f4633c13fed.

For fixed p with p dividing A-qm, equation (6) fixes ell_p. The solutions (v,k) of vk=ell_p are exactly the positive divisors v of ell_p with k=ell_p/v. If p does not divide A-qm there is no integer ell and hence no source solution. Applying this bijection term by term proves (5). For ell_p nonzero, the number of positive divisors v is at most tau(|ell_p|).

The integer |A-qm| is at most Q^C+4Q^2, so every nonzero |ell_p| is bounded by a fixed power of Q depending only on C. Fact e705401df9f0709e gives
  tau(|ell_p|)<<_{C,epsilon}Q^(epsilon/2).
Also tau_J(v)<=tau(v)^(J-1), as proved in fact d061fc4dc153e309, and the same fixed-power divisor estimate gives
  max_{V<=v<2V}tau_J(v)<<_{C,J,epsilon}Q^(epsilon/2)
after renaming epsilon. Multiplying the number of eligible divisors by the maximum weight proves (8).

If ell_p=0, then A-qm=0. Equation vk=0 with v>0 forces k=0, and conversely these conditions solve (2) for every v. The number of positive factor pairs qm=A is at most tau(|A|), and the fixed-power divisor estimate proves (9).

For four atoms, every common positive v divides each nonzero ell_i, hence divides the gcd in (10). Apply the same argument as for (8). If there is no nonzero ell_i, then all k_i=0 and (9) applies independently to each pair. This proves every assertion and the final scope statement.

glossary.cal P: A finite allowed set of primes in the exact reindexing.
glossary.cal V: A finite allowed set of positive v-values in the exact reindexing.
glossary.ell_p: The fixed cofactor (A-qm)/p for a chosen prime p.

5a651793cab6648b.title: LOW-CONDUCTOR DELETION FOR THE ACTUAL-Z_MID g=1, |h|=1 UPPER BOUNDARY. Assume the packet, natural endpoint scales, and multiplicative-character reconstruction of facts 58c03698e1b077c3 and c9accda871a70b43. On the literal support, b is squarefree. If a nonprincipal character chi modulo b has primitive conductor f, write b=fs and let psi^* be the primitive character modulo f inducing chi. Then (f,s)=1 and
5a651793cab6648b.author: slava chan
5a651793cab6648b.statement:
LOW-CONDUCTOR DELETION FOR THE ACTUAL-Z_MID g=1, |h|=1 UPPER BOUNDARY. Assume the packet, natural endpoint scales, and multiplicative-character reconstruction of facts 58c03698e1b077c3 and c9accda871a70b43. On the literal support, b is squarefree. If a nonprincipal character chi modulo b has primitive conductor f, write b=fs and let psi^* be the primitive character modulo f inducing chi. Then (f,s)=1 and
G^+_{N,b}(chi)=0 when (f,N)>1,                                      (1)
whereas, when (f,N)=1,
G^+_{N,b}(chi)
 =c_s(N) overline{psi^*(N)}psi^*(s)tau_f(psi^*),                    (2)
with
tau_f(psi^*)=sum_{v modulo f}psi^*(v)e_f(v),
and |tau_f(psi^*)|=sqrt(f).

For 2<=F_char<=x^(1/3), let mathfrak B^{np,<=F_char}_{1,1} be the complete nonprincipal part of the actual-Z_mid g=1, |h|=1 upper-boundary packet for which f<=F_char, retaining both conjugate frequencies and every literal natural mask and endpoint weight. Uniformly in F_char,
|mathfrak B^{np,<=F_char}_{1,1}|
 <=x^(1/2+o(1))F_char^(3/2).                                       (3)
Consequently, for every fixed eta with 0<eta<1/3, the choice
F_char=x^(1/3-eta)
gives
|mathfrak B^{np,<=F_char}_{1,1}|
 <=x^(1-3eta/2+o(1)).                                               (4)
Together with c9accda871a70b43, this reduces the first unresolved hard upper-boundary packet, up to a fixed-power error, to primitive conductors f>x^(1/3-eta) with (f,N)=1. No estimate for that large-conductor component, for |h|>1, for g>1, or for the derivative-integral and boundary-strip terms is asserted.
5a651793cab6648b.proof:
Because the literal b-coefficient contains mu(b), every nonzero term has squarefree b. Hence the primitive conductor f of chi divides b, b=fs, and (f,s)=1.

We first prove (1)-(2). The Chinese remainder theorem factorizes the additive character as
e_{fs}(Nu)=e_f(Nu s^{-1})e_s(Nu f^{-1}),
where the inverses are taken in the indicated moduli. Since chi is induced by psi^*, its value on a reduced residue u is psi^*(u modulo f). Therefore
G^+_{N,b}(chi)
 =[sum_{u modulo f,(u,f)=1}psi^*(u)e_f(Nu s^{-1})]
  [sum_{v modulo s,(v,s)=1}e_s(Nv f^{-1})].                         (5)
The second bracket is c_s(N), because f is a unit modulo s. The verified induced-conductor Gauss-sum calculation in fact 9a80432a29fc15d2 applies after complex conjugation and replacing its signed additive numerator by the present numerator: it states that a primitive-character additive twist vanishes when its numerator is not coprime to f, while for a coprime numerator k it equals the corresponding character value times the primitive Gauss sum, whose magnitude is exactly sqrt(f). Here k=Ns^{-1}. Thus the first bracket vanishes when (f,N)>1. When (f,N)=1, changing the reduced-residue variable by the unit Ns^{-1} gives explicitly
sum_{u modulo f}psi^*(u)e_f(Ns^{-1}u)
 =overline{psi^*(Ns^{-1})}tau_f(psi^*)
 =overline{psi^*(N)}psi^*(s)tau_f(psi^*).
This proves (1)-(2), including |tau_f(psi^*)|=sqrt(f), now with the signed predecessor fact 9a80432a29fc15d2 supplying the primitive Gauss-sum norm and noncoprime vanishing.

Now use the finite literal separated representation in fact 58c03698e1b077c3. All one-variable coefficients, natural selectors, and the endpoint amplitude are pointwise x^(o(1)); hence taking absolute values in the a-variable costs at most
A_0x^(o(1))=x^(1/2+o(1)).                                          (6)
For fixed f, the number of primitive characters modulo f is at most phi(f). Formula (2), the factorization phi(fs)=phi(f)phi(s), and (6) show that the total contribution of conductor f is at most
x^(1/2+o(1))sqrt(f)
 sum_{s asymp B_0/f}|c_s(N)|/phi(s),                                (7)
where dropping squarefreeness, coprimality, and natural zero-one restrictions only enlarges the absolute bound.

Uniformly for f<=F_char<=x^(1/3), the s-length B_0/f is a positive power of x. As in the proof of c9accda871a70b43, use |c_s(N)|<=(s,N), phi(s)^(-1)<=x^(o(1))/s, and
(s,N)=sum_{d|(s,N)}phi(d).
Summing first over s and then over d|N gives
sum_{s asymp B_0/f}|c_s(N)|/phi(s)<=x^(o(1)),                       (8)
uniformly in f. Summing (7) over 2<=f<=F_char and using
sum_{f<=F_char}sqrt(f)<=F_char^(3/2)
proves (3). Substitution F_char=x^(1/3-eta) gives
x^(1/2+o(1))x^(1/2-3eta/2)
 =x^(1-3eta/2+o(1)),
which is (4).

glossary.F_char: The upper cutoff for primitive conductors in the actual-Z_mid character reconstruction.
glossary.mathfrak B^{np,<=F_char}_{1,1}: The nonprincipal part of the actual-Z_mid g=1, |h|=1 upper-boundary packet whose primitive character conductor is at most F_char.
glossary.psi^*: A primitive Dirichlet character inducing a character modulo the squarefree modulus b.

5a7bf376fe94485e.title: EXACT DOUBLE-NONZERO ADDITIVE-COMPLETION FORMULA FOR A FULL-DENOMINATOR CENTERED BLOCK. Let p>2 be prime. For i=1,2 let d_i>1 be squarefree and coprime to p, let C_i be a unit modulo d_i, and let c be a unit modulo p. For f,g in F_p^times put G_c(f,g)=p/(p-1){1_{g=cf}-1/(p-1)}. For k_i modulo pd_i define
5a7bf376fe94485e.author: slava chan
5a7bf376fe94485e.statement:
EXACT DOUBLE-NONZERO ADDITIVE-COMPLETION FORMULA FOR A FULL-DENOMINATOR CENTERED BLOCK. Let p>2 be prime. For i=1,2 let d_i>1 be squarefree and coprime to p, let C_i be a unit modulo d_i, and let c be a unit modulo p. For f,g in F_p^times put G_c(f,g)=p/(p-1){1_{g=cf}-1/(p-1)}. For k_i modulo pd_i define
S(k_1,k_2)=sum_{x modulo pd_1,(x,pd_1)=1}sum_{y modulo pd_2,(y,pd_2)=1} G_c(x mod p,y mod p)e_{d_1}(C_1x^(-1))e_{d_2}(C_2y^(-1))e_{pd_1}(k_1x)e_{pd_2}(k_2y). (1)
Let bar d_i denote the inverse of d_i modulo p and bar p_i the inverse of p modulo d_i, and put
K_i(k_i)=sum_{z modulo d_i,(z,d_i)=1}e_{d_i}(C_i z^(-1)+k_i bar p_i z),
alpha_i=k_i bar d_i modulo p. (2)
Then S(k_1,k_2)=0 if p divides k_1k_2, while if p does not divide k_1k_2,
S(k_1,k_2)=K_1(k_1)K_2(k_2) p^2/(p-1)^2{(p-1)1_{alpha_1+c alpha_2=0}-1}. (3)
Consequently let a_i be arbitrary finitely supported complex sequences and periodize them on unit residues by tilde a_i(z)=sum_{n congruent to z modulo pd_i}a_i(n), extended by zero to nonunits. Define hat a_i(k)=sum_{z modulo pd_i}tilde a_i(z)e_{pd_i}(-kz). The incomplete full-denominator block
B(a_1,a_2)=sum_{x,y in Z}a_1(x)a_2(y)1_{(x,pd_1)=(y,pd_2)=1}G_c(x mod p,y mod p)e_{d_1}(C_1x^(-1))e_{d_2}(C_2y^(-1)) (4)
has the exact expansion
B(a_1,a_2)=1/(p^2d_1d_2) sum_{k_1 modulo pd_1,k_2 modulo pd_2,p not dividing k_1k_2}hat a_1(k_1)hat a_2(k_2)K_1(k_1)K_2(k_2)p^2/(p-1)^2{(p-1)1_{alpha_1+c alpha_2=0}-1}. (5)
In particular every cofactor-only completion mode, meaning p|k_i on at least one row, cancels exactly. For the literal supplier E_full(P) of fact f439118e1e8818a1, take d_1=s,d_2=q,c=sq^(-1) modulo p, C_1=M_1a^(-1) modulo s, C_2=-M_12a^(-1) modulo q, a_1(u)=beta_{tau,a}(u)1_{(au,ps)=1}, and a_2(u)=conjugate(beta_{tau,a}(u))1_{(au,pq)=1}. Thus its exact fixed-edge supplier is the double-nonzero tensor (5), with both arbitrary literal Vaughan rows retained. No estimate for (5), its cross-edge aggregate, E_full(P), or Goldbach is asserted.
5a7bf376fe94485e.proof:
Use the Chinese remainder theorem to write x as the pair (f,z) in F_p^times times (Z/d_1Z)^times. The standard CRT additive-character identity gives
e_{pd_1}(k_1x)=e_p(k_1 bar d_1 f)e_{d_1}(k_1 bar p_1 z). (6)
The inverse phase depends only on z. Hence the x-row in (1), after summing its d_1-coordinate, is K_1(k_1)e_p(alpha_1f). The y-row is analogously K_2(k_2)e_p(alpha_2g). Therefore
S(k_1,k_2)=K_1(k_1)K_2(k_2) T(alpha_1,alpha_2), (7)
where
T(alpha_1,alpha_2)=sum_{f,g in F_p^times}G_c(f,g)e_p(alpha_1f+alpha_2g). (8)
From the definition of G_c,
T=p/(p-1){sum_{f nonzero}e_p((alpha_1+c alpha_2)f)-1/(p-1)(sum_{f nonzero}e_p(alpha_1f))(sum_{g nonzero}e_p(alpha_2g))}. (9)
If exactly one alpha_i is zero, the first sum in braces is -1 and the product contribution is also -1; if both are zero, both contributions are p-1. Thus T=0 whenever alpha_1alpha_2=0, equivalently whenever p|k_1k_2. If both alpha_i are nonzero, each separate sum is -1. The first sum in (9) is p-1 on the resonance alpha_1+c alpha_2=0 and -1 otherwise. Direct substitution gives
T=p^2/(p-1)^2{(p-1)1_{alpha_1+c alpha_2=0}-1},
which proves (3).
The kernel in (4) is periodic modulo pd_1 in x and pd_2 in y, so (4) is the pairing of the unit-periodized sequences tilde a_i through that kernel. Fourier inversion on the two complete cyclic groups is
tilde a_i(z)=1/(pd_i)sum_{k_i modulo pd_i}hat a_i(k_i)e_{pd_i}(k_i z). (10)
Insert (10) twice into (4), interchange finite sums, and use (1)--(3). Every term with p|k_1k_2 vanishes and the remaining terms give exactly (5).
For the literal specialization, fact f439118e1e8818a1 identifies the two full-denominator phases as e_s(M_1(au_1)^(-1)) and e_q(-M_12(au_2)^(-1)). Since a is a unit on the displayed supports, these are e_s((M_1a^(-1))u_1^(-1)) and e_q((-M_12a^(-1))u_2^(-1)). Its centered congruence is u_2 congruent to sq^(-1)u_1 modulo p. Hence the displayed choices match (4) term by term, proving the final exact supplier statement.

glossary.K_i(k_i): The complete cofactor Kloosterman sum in row i.
glossary.S(k_1,k_2): The complete two-row mode at additive completion frequencies k_1,k_2.
glossary.alpha_i: The shared-prime additive frequency k_i d_i^(-1) modulo p.
glossary.cofactor-only completion mode: A mode with p dividing at least one additive frequency, so that row is constant in its shared-prime CRT coordinate.
glossary.hat a_i(k): The additive Fourier transform of tilde a_i modulo pd_i.
glossary.tilde a_i: The unit-residue periodization of the i-th incomplete coefficient sequence.

5a9588474e09a334.title: ABSTRACT CLOSED-ENDPOINT COMPLETE-FREQUENCY RAISED-STOPPING \(B_*\) TRACE ON FULL DYADIC RECTANGLES
5a9588474e09a334.author: slava chan
5a9588474e09a334.statement:
ABSTRACT CLOSED-ENDPOINT COMPLETE-FREQUENCY RAISED-STOPPING \(B_*\) TRACE ON FULL DYADIC RECTANGLES.

Fix integers \(J,C_A\ge1\), a constant \(C\ge1\), and
\(0<\kappa\le1/100\).  Put
\[
 \sigma=\kappa/100,quad
 \beta_1=6/5-3\sigma,quad
 \beta_m=6/5-12\sigma/5,
\]
and let \(\beta_1<\beta\le\beta_m\).  For sufficiently large \(Q\)
put
\[
 B=Q^\beta,quad H_T=B/Q,quad
 L=H_TQ^\sigma,quad S_0=H_T^2Q^{3\sigma},quad
 Z_*=2Q^{3/2-\beta-3\sigma},quad I_*=(L,Z_*).
\]
Use the exact coefficient \(\Gamma_{k;L,S_0}(y)\) of fact
\(6414b11506a84ff0\).

For each \(k\ge2\) and each pair of dyadic scales \(U,Y\) satisfying
\[
 C^{-1}B\le UY\le CB                                             \tag{1}
\]
and for which the stopping support below is nonempty, let
\(|c_q|\le1\) on \(Q\le q<2Q\), let \(V_q\) be a unit modulo
\(q\), and fix \(A\ne0\), \(|A|\le Q^{C_A}\).  On every dyadic
integer-frequency block \(F\le|h|<2F\), use divisor-bounded
\(h\)-coefficients and the one-variable coefficients
\[
 \alpha_u={(-1)^k\mu(u)1_{j_{I_*}(u)=0}
            \over {k+\omega_L(u)\choose k}},
 \qquad
 \gamma_y=\Gamma_{k;L,S_0}(y)                                   \tag{2}
\]
on the full dyadic rectangle
\[
 U\le u<2U,qquad Y\le y<2Y.
\]
Impose only
\[
 (uy,q)=(u,y)=1.                                                    \tag{3}
\]
Let \(\Psi_F(q/Q,|h|/F,u/U,y/Y)\) be a fixed-complexity uniformly
scaled-smooth projective amplitude of uniformly bounded projective norm.
In particular, any smooth product localization is part of \(\Psi_F\);
there is no sharp joint product mask.  Let
\[
 |\omega_F|\le C(J_0)\min\{1,(F/H_P)^{-J_0}\}
\]
for every fixed \(J_0\ge1\).  Let \(T_{B_*}\) be the sum over both
signs and all nonempty \(k,U,Y,F\) blocks, with prefactor
\(H_P^{-1}\), coefficient
\(\omega_Fc_q\nu_F(h)\alpha_u\gamma_y\Psi_F\), and phase
\[
 e_q(AV_qh(uy)^{-1}).                                               \tag{4}
\]

If \(G\ge1\), \(H_P=H_T/G\), then
\[
 T_{B_*}\ll GQ^{2-\delta_{B,F}}.                                 \tag{5}
\]
If \(0<\eta<\sigma\),
\[
 Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\le G\le Q^{\sigma-\eta},qquad H_P=H_T/G,
\]
then
\[
 T_{B_*}\ll Q^{2-\delta_{B,N}}.                                  \tag{6}
\]
The fixed savings and implied constants depend only on the displayed fixed
parameters, divisor orders and projective norm.  The bounds include
\(H_P<1\), every actual integer-frequency block, arbitrary \(V_q\),
possibly nonunit fixed \(A\), unrestricted \((h,q)\), and
polylogarithmically many legal label scalars or one-variable/projective
factors.  No arbitrary joint mask, literal-source, outer-\(g\), other
anatomy, PMD, DCE, or Goldbach claim is made.
5a9588474e09a334.proof:
Fact \(047f4bc01579ce66\) and fact
\(6414b11506a84ff0\) give the exact \(B_*\) coefficient (2) on the
stated beta range.  The predicate \(1_{j_{I_*}(u)=0}\) is one-variable,
\(|\alpha_u|\le1\), and \(0\le\gamma_y\le1\).  A nonzero
\(\gamma_y\) satisfies
\[
 S_0<y\le S_0L.                                                    \tag{7}
\]
Thus any nonempty dyadic \(Y\)-block satisfies, after fixed endpoint
constants are absorbed,
\[
 H_T^2Q^{2\sigma}\le Y\le Q^{1-2\sigma}/H_T^2.                 \tag{8}
\]
For the upper bound, the logarithmic gap between its right side and
\(S_0L\) is
\[
 6-5\beta-6\sigma\ge6\sigma.                                  \tag{9}
\]
The scale relation \(UY\asymp B=QH_T\) is the explicit hypothesis (1);
it is not imposed pointwise inside the rectangle.

Expand \(\Psi_F\) in an absolutely summable projective Fourier series
and absorb every one-variable mode into
\(c_q,\nu_F,\alpha_u,\gamma_y\).  Because no sharp product condition
occurs, the only remaining joint condition besides the complete-product
coprimality is exactly \((u,y)=1\), as in (3).

Put
\[
 u_F=F/H_P,qquad G_F=H_T/F=G/u_F.
\]
Apply fact \(95626318cdcc099f\) on the full rectangle, with frequency
\(F\), factor scales \(S=Y,T=U\), product-scale relation (1), and
imbalance \(G_F\).  Its statement explicitly permits arbitrary
\(V_q\), fixed possibly nonunit \(A\), unrestricted \((h,q)\), and
the two coprimalities in (3).  Replacing its \(F^{-1}\) prefactor by
\(H_P^{-1}=u_FF^{-1}\) gives, apart from
\(Q^\epsilon|\omega_F|\),
\[
 u_F^{3/4}E_1,quad u_F^{3/4}E_2,quad u_FE_3,quad u_FE_4,         \tag{10}
\]
where
\[
 E_1=G^{1/4}Q^2H_T^{1/2}Y^{-1/4},
\quad E_2=G^{1/4}Q^{7/4}H_T^{1/2}Y^{1/4},
\]
\[
 E_3=Q^2H_TY^{-1/2},qquad E_4=Q^{7/4}H_T.                         \tag{11}
\]
The arbitrary fixed-order decay gives
\[
 \sum_F|\omega_F|u_F^{3/4+\epsilon}
 +\sum_F|\omega_F|u_F^{1+\epsilon}\ll1                         \tag{12}
\]
for one fixed order greater than three.  If \(H_P<1\), every integer
block has \(u_F>1\) and is included in the same convergent sums.
Therefore the complete trace is
\(O(Q^\epsilon(E_1+E_2+E_3+E_4))\).

For \(G\ge1\), divide (11) by \(GQ^2\).  From (8) the four ratios are
\[
 \ll G^{-3/4}Q^{-\sigma/2},quad
 G^{-3/4}Q^{-\sigma/2},quad
 G^{-1}Q^{-\sigma},quad
 G^{-1}Q^{\beta-5/4}.                                             \tag{13}
\]
Since
\[
 \beta-5/4\le-1/20-12\sigma/5,
\]
all have fixed savings.  The \(O(\log Q)\) possible \(k,U,Y\)
blocks and fixed projective cost are absorbed by shrinking the least
saving, proving (5).

In the near-balanced range, divide (11) by \(Q^2\).  The ratios are
\[
 \ll G^{1/4}Q^{-\sigma/2},quad
 G^{1/4}Q^{-\sigma/2},quad Q^{-\sigma},quad
 Q^{\beta-5/4}.                                                    \tag{14}
\]
Because \(G^{1/4}\le Q^{(\sigma-\eta)/4}\), the first two save at
least \(\sigma/4+\eta/4\); the other two have fixed savings.  This
proves (6).

Finally \(\gamma_y\ne0\) implies \(2^k\le y<2Y\), with \(Y\) a
fixed power of \(Q\), so \(k=O(\log Q)\).  All stated block counts
are polylogarithmic.  The application used only the full dyadic rectangle,
the legal one-variable/projective factors, and the exact joint
coprimalities permitted by \(95626318cdcc099f\).

glossary.T_B*: The abstract full-rectangle complete-frequency B_* trace.
glossary.delta_B,F: The fixed full-G saving exponent for the endpoint B_* trace.
glossary.delta_B,N: The fixed near-balanced saving exponent for the endpoint B_* trace.

5b7b0955c5efaa1b.title: Fix a real constant \(C>0\). Let \(D\ge3\) tend to infinity, let \(N\) be a positive even integer satisfying \(N\le D^C\), and define
5b7b0955c5efaa1b.author: slava chan
5b7b0955c5efaa1b.statement:
Fix a real constant \(C>0\). Let \(D\ge3\) tend to infinity, let \(N\) be a positive even integer satisfying \(N\le D^C\), and define
\[
 C_2=\prod_{p>2}{p(p-2)\over(p-1)^2},\qquad
 \mathfrak c(N)=C_2\prod_{\substack{p\mid N\\p>2}}{p-1\over p-2}.
\]
Let \(G_1,G_2\) range over families of complex functions supported in \([1/2,2]\), with uniformly bounded supremum and total variation. For distinct positive integers \(d_1,d_2\) with \(\mu(d_1)\mu(d_2)\ne0\) and \(\gcd(d_1d_2,N)=1\), let \(\mathfrak S_N(d_1,d_2)\) be the two-affine-form singular series of fact b164cd7d1e02e173.

Then, for every real \(A>0\),
\[
 \sum_{\substack{d_1\ne d_2\\(d_1d_2,N)=1}}
 \mu(d_1)\mu(d_2)G_1(d_1/D)G_2(d_2/D)
 \mathfrak S_N(d_1,d_2)
 \ll_{A,C,G_1,G_2}
 \mathfrak c(N)D^2(\log D)^{-A},                         \tag{1}
\]
uniformly in \(N\) and in the stated bounded-variation families.

Let \(T>0\). For \(i=1,2\), suppose \((t,u)\mapsto G_{i,t}(u)\) is jointly measurable on \([0,T]\times\mathbb R\), every \(G_{i,t}\) is supported in \([1/2,2]\), and the suprema and total variations of all \(G_{i,t}\) are uniformly bounded. Then
\[
 \int_0^T
 \sum_{\substack{d_1\ne d_2\\(d_1d_2,N)=1}}
 \mu(d_1)\mu(d_2)G_{1,t}(d_1/D)G_{2,t}(d_2/D)
 \mathfrak S_N(d_1,d_2)\,dt
 \ll_A \mathfrak c(N)TD^2(\log D)^{-A}.                  \tag{2}
\]

For a literal consequence, assume additionally all notation and hypotheses of fact 9e1ff55fe17bc513, including \(N=2x\), the source-admissible scales \(DM\asymp x\), \(U\asymp x\), and the top set
\[
 {\cal I}_D=\{d\ge2:(d,N)=1,\ d\le x^{1/2},\ \Phi(d/D)\ne0\}.
\]
Define the aggregate singular main
\[
 {\cal H}_{\rm sing}(D,M;U)=
 \int_0^\infty
 \sum_{\substack{d_1,d_2\in{\cal I}_D\\d_1\ne d_2}}
 \mu(d_1)\mu(d_2)\Phi(d_1/D)\Phi(d_2/D)
 W(d_1t/x)W(d_2t/x)
 \Phi((N-d_1t)/U)\Phi((N-d_2t)/U)
 \mathfrak S_N(d_1,d_2)\,dt.                           \tag{3}
\]
Then, for every \(A>0\),
\[
 {\cal H}_{\rm sing}(D,M;U)
 \ll_{A,W,\Phi}\mathfrak c(N)MD^2(\log x)^{-A}
 \asymp_{a,b}\mathfrak c(N)xD(\log x)^{-A}.              \tag{4}
\]
Thus the formal Hardy--Littlewood singular main associated with the off-diagonal covariance of fact 9e1ff55fe17bc513 has arbitrary logarithmic cancellation after the complete \(\mu(d_1)\mu(d_2)\) sum. Equation (4) does not estimate the difference between the actual prime-pair covariance and this main and therefore does not prove (TB-COV4).
5b7b0955c5efaa1b.proof:
Because \(N\) is even and \((d_1d_2,N)=1\), both \(d_1,d_2\) are odd. Define
\[
 A_0(d)=\prod_{p\mid d}{p-1\over p-2}
\]
on odd squarefree integers. Fact b164cd7d1e02e173 gives, with \(g=(d_1,d_2)\),
\[
 \mathfrak S_N(d_1,d_2)
 =2\mathfrak c(N)A_0(d_1)A_0(d_2)B(g)C_N(d_1,d_2),       \tag{5}
\]
where
\[
 B(g)=\prod_{p\mid g}\left(1-{1\over(p-1)^2}\right)        \tag{6}
\]
and
\[
 C_N(d_1,d_2)=
 \prod_{\substack{p\mid d_1-d_2\\p\nmid Nd_1d_2}}
 \left(1+{1\over p-2}\right).                             \tag{7}
\]
The factors at primes dividing \(N\) have been absorbed into \(\mathfrak c(N)/C_2\). At a prime dividing both moduli,
\[
 \left({p-1\over p-2}\right)^2
 \left(1-{1\over(p-1)^2}\right)={p\over p-2},
\]
so (5) follows exactly from the three products in fact b164cd7d1e02e173.

Expand
\[
 B(g)=\sum_{r\mid g}\beta(r),\qquad
 \beta(r)=\mu(r)^2\prod_{p\mid r}{-1\over(p-1)^2}.         \tag{8}
\]
Writing \(d_i=re_i\), squarefreeness gives \((r,e_i)=1\), and
\[
 \mu(d_1)\mu(d_2)A_0(d_1)A_0(d_2)\beta(r)
 =\delta(r)f(e_1)f(e_2),                                 \tag{9}
\]
where
\[
 \delta(r)=\mu(r)^2\prod_{p\mid r}{-1\over(p-2)^2},\qquad
 f(e)=\mu(e)A_0(e).                                       \tag{10}
\]
The coefficients are absolutely summable:
\[
 \sum_{r\ge1}|\delta(r)|
 =\prod_{p>2}\left(1+{1\over(p-2)^2}\right)<\infty.        \tag{11}
\]

For \(e_1\ne e_2\), expand (7) as
\[
 C_N(re_1,re_2)=
 \sum_{\substack{q\mid e_1-e_2\\(q,Nre_1e_2)=1}}\gamma(q),               \tag{12}
\]
where
\[
 \gamma(q)=\mu(q)^2\prod_{p\mid q}{1\over p-2}
\]
for odd \(q\), and \(\gamma(q)=0\) for even \(q\). The following elementary estimates hold for an absolute constant \(C_0\):
\[
 \sum_{q\le Y}\gamma(q)\ll(\log(2Y))^{C_0},\qquad
 \sum_{q>Q_0}{\gamma(q)\over q}\ll Q_0^{-1/2}.                           \tag{13}
\]
The first follows from the Euler product
\(\prod_{3\le p\le Y}(1+1/(p-2))\) and
\(\sum_{p\le Y}p^{-1}\ll\log\log(3Y)\). For the second,
\[
 \sum_{q>Q_0}{\gamma(q)\over q}
 \le Q_0^{-1/2}\prod_{p>2}
 \left(1+{1\over(p-2)p^{1/2}}\right),
\]
and the product converges.

We record two mean-value bounds. First,
\[
 \sum_{e\le Y}\mu(e)^2A_0(e)^2\ll Y.                    \tag{14}
\]
For squarefree \(e\),
\[
 A_0(e)^2=\prod_{p\mid e}(1+\kappa(p))
          =\sum_{s\mid e}\kappa(s),
\]
where \(\kappa\) is squarefree multiplicative and
\[
 \kappa(p)=\left({p-1\over p-2}\right)^2-1
 ={2p-3\over(p-2)^2}=O(1/p).
\]
Hence
\[
 \sum_s{|\kappa(s)|\over s}
 =\prod_{p>2}\left(1+{|\kappa(p)|\over p}\right)<\infty,
\]
and
\[
 \sum_{e\le Y}\mu(e)^2A_0(e)^2
 \le\sum_{s\le Y}|\kappa(s)|\lfloor Y/s\rfloor\ll Y.
\]
Second, the same divisor-expansion argument gives
\[
 \sum_{e\le Y}A_0(e)\ll Y.                              \tag{15}
\]
Indeed \(A_0(e)=\sum_{s\mid e}\gamma(s)\) on odd squarefree \(e\), and
\(\sum_s\gamma(s)/s<\infty\).

We next prove a weighted Möbius cancellation lemma. Let \(Q\le D^{C_1}\), let \(X\ge D^{1/4}\), and let \(G\) be supported in \([1/2,2]\) with bounded supremum and total variation. Then, uniformly in real \(\alpha\),
\[
 \sum_{\substack{e\ge1\\(e,Q)=1}}
 \mu(e)A_0(e)G(e/X)e^{2\pi i\alpha e}
 \ll_{J,C_1,G}X(\log D)^{-J}                              \tag{16}
\]
for every \(J>0\).

Put \(f_Q(e)=\mu(e)A_0(e)1_{(e,Q)=1}\). There is a multiplicative function \(h_Q\) with \(f_Q=\mu*h_Q\), whose prime-power values for \(j\ge1\) are
\[
 h_Q(p^j)=
 \begin{cases}
 1,&p\mid Q,\\
 -1/(p-2),&p\nmid Q,\ p>2.
 \end{cases}                                             \tag{17}
\]
In the applications \(2\mid Q\). At a prime not dividing \(Q\),
\[
 -1+h_Q(p)=-(p-1)/(p-2)=f_Q(p),
\]
and \(h_Q(p^j)-h_Q(p^{j-1})=0=f_Q(p^j)\) for \(j\ge2\). At a prime dividing \(Q\), both convolution coefficients vanish. Thus (17) proves the convolution identity.

Euler products give, for absolute constants \(C_2',C_3'\),
\[
 \sum_k{|h_Q(k)|\over k}\ll(\log(2Q))^{C_2'},             \tag{18}
\]
and
\[
 \sum_k{|h_Q(k)|\over k^{3/4}}
 \le\exp(C_3'(\log(2Q))^{1/4})=D^{o(1)}.                 \tag{19}
\]
For (18), primes outside \(Q\) give the convergent product
\(\prod_{p>2}(1+1/((p-2)(p-1)))\), while primes in \(Q\) give
\(\prod_{p\mid Q}(1-1/p)^{-1}\ll(\log(2Q))^{C_2'}\).
For (19), the outside product converges, and the \(Q\)-part is at most
\(\exp(O(\sum_{j\le\log_2Q}j^{-3/4}))\).

Expand \(f_Q=\mu*h_Q\) in (16). For \(k\le X^{1/2}\), the inner \(\mu\)-sum has length comparable to \(X/k\ge X^{1/2}\). Liu--Sarnak, arXiv:1303.4957, Lemma 2.1 with modulus \(1\) and a linear polynomial phase, gives arbitrary logarithmic saving uniformly in that phase. Stieltjes partial summation applies to a bounded-variation weight and gives
\[
 \sum_e\mu(e)G(ke/X)e^{2\pi i\alpha ke}
 \ll_J {X\over k}(\log D)^{-J-C_2'-3}.
\]
After (18), the small-\(k\) contribution is \(O_J(X(\log D)^{-J})\).

For \(k>X^{1/2}\), use the trivial bound \(O(X/k+1)\). Equation (19) gives
\[
 X\sum_{k>X^{1/2}}{|h_Q(k)|\over k}
 \le X^{7/8}\sum_k{|h_Q(k)|\over k^{3/4}}
 =X^{7/8}D^{o(1)}
\]
and
\[
 \sum_{X^{1/2}<k\le2X}|h_Q(k)|
 \le(2X)^{3/4}\sum_k{|h_Q(k)|\over k^{3/4}}
 =X^{3/4}D^{o(1)}.
\]
Since \(X\ge D^{1/4}\), these are \(O_J(X(\log D)^{-J})\). This proves (16).

Additive-character orthogonality now gives, uniformly for \(q,Q\le D^{C_1}\) and every residue \(a\pmod q\),
\[
 \sum_{\substack{e\equiv a\ ({\rm mod}\ q)\\(e,Q)=1}}
 \mu(e)A_0(e)G(e/X)
 \ll_J X(\log D)^{-J}.                                    \tag{20}
\]

We insert (5), (8), and (12) into the left side of (1). Fix \(r\le D^{1/2}\), put \(X=D/r\), and choose \(Q_0=(\log D)^H\). For \(q\le Q_0\), set \(Q=Nrq\), which is polynomially bounded in \(D\). Apply (20) to the two \(e_i\)-sums in each reduced residue class modulo \(q\). The contribution with \(e_1\equiv e_2\pmod q\), before deleting \(e_1=e_2\), is
\[
 \sum_{\substack{a\bmod q\\(a,q)=1}}S_1(a)S_2(a)
 \ll qX^2(\log D)^{-2J}.
\]
By (14), the deleted diagonal is \(O(X)\). Summing with \(\gamma(q)\) for \(q\le Q_0\), using (13), and choosing \(J\) sufficiently large gives
\[
 \ll X^2(\log D)^{-A-10}+X(\log D)^{C_4}.                \tag{21}
\]

For \(q>Q_0\), use absolute values. Expanding \(A_0(e_i)\) by (15) and counting progressions gives
\[
 \sum_{\substack{e_1,e_2\asymp X\\e_1\equiv e_2\ ({\rm mod}\ q)}}
 A_0(e_1)A_0(e_2)
 \ll\left({X^2\over q}+X\right)(\log(2X))^{C_5}.           \tag{22}
\]
To prove (22), write \(e_i=s_ik_i\). On the support from (12), \((s_i,q)=1\). For each \(k_1\), the congruence fixes \(k_2\) to one residue modulo \(q\), yielding
\[
 O\left({X^2\over s_1s_2q}+{X\over s_1}\right)
\]
pairs. Sum with \(\gamma(s_1)\gamma(s_2)\), use
\(\sum_s\gamma(s)/s<\infty\), use (13) for the unweighted divisor sum, and symmetrize. This proves (22).

Equations (13) and (22) yield
\[
 \sum_{q>Q_0}\gamma(q)
 \sum_{\substack{e_1,e_2\asymp X\\e_1\equiv e_2\ ({\rm mod}\ q)}}
 A_0(e_1)A_0(e_2)
 \ll X^2Q_0^{-1/2}(\log D)^{C_5}
     +X(\log D)^{C_6}.                                    \tag{23}
\]
Choose \(H\) sufficiently large. Combining (21) and (23), the \(e_1,e_2\)-sum for every \(r\le D^{1/2}\) is
\[
 \ll {D^2\over r^2}(\log D)^{-A-2}
    +{D\over r}(\log D)^{C_7}.                            \tag{24}
\]

For \(r>D^{1/2}\), use (22)--(23) without small-\(q\) cancellation. The absolute bound is
\[
 \ll (D/r)^2(\log D)^{C_8}+(D/r)(\log D)^{C_8}.
\]
After multiplication by \(|\delta(r)|\), (11) gives total \(O(D(\log D)^{C_8})\), which is \(O_A(D^2(\log D)^{-A})\). For \(r\le D^{1/2}\), multiply (24) by \(|\delta(r)|\), sum using (11), and absorb the \(D(\log D)^{C_7}\) term. Restoring \(2\mathfrak c(N)\) from (5) proves (1).

For (2), joint measurability makes the finite \(d_1,d_2\)-sum a measurable function of \(t\). Apply (1) pointwise and integrate over \([0,T]\).

We finally prove (4) without a smoothness mismatch. For \(t\ge0\) and \(u\in\mathbb R\), define
\[
 G_{1,t}(u)=G_{2,t}(u)=
 1_{Du\le x^{1/2}}\Phi(u)W(Dut/x)\Phi((N-Dut)/U).          \tag{25}
\]
These functions are jointly measurable. They are supported in \([1/2,2]\). Their suprema are uniformly bounded. Their total variations are uniformly bounded on the \(t\)-range where they are nonzero: the indicator contributes one jump, \(\Phi(u)\) has fixed variation, and the chain-rule variation of the last two factors is bounded because nonzero support gives \(Dt\asymp x\), while \(U\asymp x\). Outside an interval of length \(O(M)\), they vanish identically, since \(u\asymp1\), \(Dut/x\in[a,b]\), and \(DM\asymp x\).

With (25), the integrand in (2) is exactly the integrand defining (3), including the sharp cutoff \(d_i\le x^{1/2}\). Apply (2) on an interval of length \(O(M)\). This gives
\[
 {\cal H}_{\rm sing}\ll_A\mathfrak c(N)MD^2(\log D)^{-A}.
\]
In the top band \(D\) is a fixed-power scale of \(x\), so \(\log D\asymp\log x\); and \(DM\asymp x\) by source admissibility. This proves (4).

glossary.A_0(d): the product over odd primes p dividing d of (p-1)/(p-2)
glossary.C_N(d1,d2): the determinant-difference correction product after extracting primes dividing N
glossary.cal H_sing(D,M;U): the aggregate literal singular main for the off-diagonal top-band covariance
glossary.delta(r): the absolutely summable common-divisor coefficient after extracting r

5b9e0311f7e49ea2.title: ONE-COLUMN SQUARE-MODULUS KLOOSTERMAN TRANSFERENCE AND IJOP TAX CONTRACT
5b9e0311f7e49ea2.author: slava chan
5b9e0311f7e49ea2.statement:
ONE-COLUMN SQUARE-MODULUS KLOOSTERMAN TRANSFERENCE AND IJOP TAX CONTRACT.

Fix L>0. Let m>2L+1 be odd and put q=m^2. Let C be a complex function on Z/qZ which vanishes on nonunits. Let F be a complex function on Z supported on one integer interval of cardinality at most Lm. Define
 F_per(y)=sum_{a congruent y modulo q}F(a),
 C_hat(p)=sum_{x modulo q}C(x)e_q(-px),
 F_hat(h)=sum_{y modulo q}F_per(y)e_q(-hy),                          (1)
where e_q(z)=exp(2 pi i z/q). Put
 V_F=||F||_infinity+sum_{a in Z}|F(a+1)-F(a)|                       (2)
and
 T(C,F)=sum_{x modulo q;gcd(x,q)=1}C(x)F_per(x^(-1)).                (3)
Then
 T(C,F)=q^(-2)sum_{p modulo q}sum_{h modulo q}
 C_hat(p)F_hat(h)S(p,h;q),                                         (4)
where
 S(p,h;q)=sum_{x modulo q;gcd(x,q)=1}e_q(px+h x^(-1)),               (5)
and, for every epsilon>0,
 |T(C,F)|<=C_{L,epsilon}q^(-1/32+epsilon)V_F||C_hat||_2.             (6)

Partition a complete set of integer representatives modulo q into O(m) consecutive intervals of cardinality at most m. If B_C is the sum of the l2 norms of C_hat on these intervals, then
 B_C<=Cq^(1/4)||C_hat||_2.                                         (7)
For a divisor g of q with 1<=g<=m, let B_F(g) be the sum of the block l2 norms of F_hat restricted to g dividing h. Then
 B_F(g)<=C_Lq^(3/4)g^(-1/2)V_Flog(2q).                              (8)
After splitting by g=gcd(p,h,q), lowering to modulus q/g, and applying Blomer--Pascadi, arXiv:2607.24311, Theorem 1.1 blockwise, all sectors g<=m contribute the right side of (6). The sectors g>m contribute
 O_{L,epsilon}(q^(-19/64+epsilon)V_F||C_hat||_2),                   (9)
and h=0 contributes
 O_{L,epsilon}(q^(-1/2+epsilon)V_F||C_hat||_2).                     (10)

Suppose now that a shared-lift IJOP core supplies functions C_j,F_j and column sequences alpha_j,beta_j such that
 ||C_hat_j||_2
 <=A_jq^(1/2+epsilon)||W_j||_2||alpha_j||_2||beta_j||_2             (11)
for every epsilon>0, where A_j is an explicitly declared subpolynomial fibre constant and W_j is its digit weight. Then
 |T(C_j,F_j)|
 <=C_{L,epsilon}m^(15/16+epsilon)
 A_jV_{F_j}||W_j||_2||alpha_j||_2||beta_j||_2.                     (12)
Fact 212d1415bf03c2a7 supplies (11), with A_j=m^{o(1)}, for its literal shared-integer-lift model retaining the second row window, both columns and every bounded gate in a divisor-degree fibre.

For a finite assembly with coefficients lambda_j define
 P_IJOP=sum_j|lambda_j|A_jV_{F_j}||W_j||_2
                    ||alpha_j||_2||beta_j||_2.                      (13)
Then
 |sum_jlambda_jT(C_j,F_j)|
 <=C_{L,epsilon}m^(15/16+epsilon)P_IJOP.                            (14)
If the atoms arise from common column sequences alpha_0,beta_0 by unit-modulus character multiplication or zero-one coordinate gates and
 ||alpha_0||_2||beta_0||_2>0,
define
 L_IJOP_core=P_IJOP/(||alpha_0||_2||beta_0||_2).                    (15)
If one common norm is zero, every gated atom vanishes and the assembled sum is zero, so no normalized ledger is needed. For positive common norms, the sufficient tax condition
 L_IJOP_core<=m^(1/80-delta)                                       (16)
with fixed delta>=0 gives
 |sum_jlambda_jT(C_j,F_j)|
 <=C_{L,epsilon}m^(19/20-delta+epsilon)
   ||alpha_0||_2||beta_0||_2.                                     (17)

The tax in (13)-(16) must include every decomposition needed to obtain one common first-row profile per atom: digit-mode assembly, moving-profile separation, sign sectors, gate amplitudes, and any outer prime, gcd, carrier, shell, mask, source, or lift-selector projective cost not retained inside one bounded finite-degree fibre. The primitive/imprimitive progression count of fact 55733dfba03775a2 is m^{o(1)}. Gcd lowering and h=0 are already included in (6). Fact 8592875ae5046498 shows that arbitrary independently column-dependent finite row selectors cannot receive a subpolynomial loss; (12) applies to the literal IJOP only through the bounded-window, shared-lift fibre model of fact 212d1415bf03c2a7. No varying-m or full-shell bound is asserted unless its complete outer tax satisfies (16).
5b9e0311f7e49ea2.proof:
Fourier inversion on Z/qZ gives
 C(x)=q^(-1)sum_p C_hat(p)e_q(px),
 F_per(x^(-1))=q^(-1)sum_h F_hat(h)e_q(hx^(-1)).
Insert these formulas into (3) and use (5), proving (4).

Cauchy--Schwarz over the O(m) frequency blocks proves
 B_C<=Cm^(1/2)||C_hat||_2=Cq^(1/4)||C_hat||_2,
which is (7).

Directly, |F_hat(h)|<=Lm||F||_infinity. For h nonzero modulo q, discrete summation by parts gives
 (1-e_q(-h))F_hat(h)
 =sum_y(F_per(y)-F_per(y-1))e_q(-hy).
The cyclic total variation is at most C_LV_F. If |h| is the least absolute representative, then |1-e_q(-h)|>=4|h|/q. Therefore
 |F_hat(h)|<=C_Lmin(m||F||_infinity,qV_F/|h|).                     (18)
A block of length m contains at most 1+m/g multiples of g. In the blocks at distance comparable to jm from zero, (18) is at most C_LmV_F/(1+j). Their restricted l2 norms are at most
 C_Lm^(3/2)g^(-1/2)V_F/(1+j).
Summing over the blocks proves (8).

We reproduce the external result used. Blomer--Pascadi, arXiv:2607.24311, Theorem 1.1 states that for c>=1, 1<=N<=c, arbitrary complex sequences supported on two integer intervals of cardinality at most N, and a unit modulo c,
 |sum_{r,t;gcd(r,t,c)=1}gamma_rdelta_tS(ar,t;c)|
 <=C_epsilon||gamma||_2||delta||_2c^(1+epsilon)
 [N^(1/8)c^(-3/32)+N^(5/16)c^(-3/16)
  +N^(2/3)c^(-7/18)].                                               (19)
Its S is the unnormalized sum (5).

For each p,h put g=gcd(p,h,q). Reduction of units modulo q/g is surjective with kernel size phi(q)/phi(q/g), so
 S(gp',gh';q)=[phi(q)/phi(q/g)]S(p',h';q/g),                        (20)
where gcd(p',h',q/g)=1, and
 phi(q)/phi(q/g)<=g.                                                (21)

Let g<=m. Dividing the intersection of one original block with the multiples of g gives an interval of cardinality at most 1+m/g. Apply (19) with c=q/g, a=1 and N comparable to m/g. The three coefficient-free factors are at most
 C_epsilon q^(31/32+epsilon)g^(-33/32),
 C_epsilon q^(31/32+epsilon)g^(-9/8),
 C_epsilon q^(17/18+epsilon)g^(-23/18).                             (22)
Use (7), (8), (21), and q^(-2). The exact-g sector is at most the sum of
 Cq^(-1/32+epsilon)g^(-17/32),
 Cq^(-1/32+epsilon)g^(-5/8),
 Cq^(-1/18+epsilon)g^(-7/9),                                       (23)
times V_F||C_hat||_2. The self-contained divisor estimate in fact 212d1415bf03c2a7 shows that q has q^{o(1)} divisors. Summing (23) over g<=m gives (6) for these sectors.

Let g>m and exclude h=0. Put c=q/g. Use singleton blocks in (19), so N=1 and one reduced Kloosterman sum is at most C_epsilon c^(29/32+epsilon). Cauchy--Schwarz gives
 sum_{g divides p}|C_hat(p)|<=C(q/g)^(1/2)||C_hat||_2.              (24)
Equations (18) and q/g<m give
 sum_{g divides h}|F_hat(h)|<=C_LmV_Flog(2q).                       (25)
Combining q^(-2), (21), (24), (25), and c^(29/32+epsilon), the exact-g sector is at most
 Cq^(-3/32+epsilon)g^(-13/32)V_F||C_hat||_2.
Since g>m=q^(1/2), this is (9). The other terms in (19) are smaller, and a divisor sum is subpolynomial.

For h=0, S(p,0;q) is a Ramanujan sum. If d=gcd(p,q), unit-indicator inclusion-exclusion gives
 S(p,0;q)=mu(q/d)phi(q)/phi(q/d),
so |S(p,0;q)|<=d. Also
 sum_{p modulo q}gcd(p,q)^2
 <=qsum_{d divides q}d
 <=q^2tau(q)
 <=C_epsilon q^(2+epsilon),                                        (26)
using the divisor estimate from fact 212d1415bf03c2a7. Since |F_hat(0)|<=LmV_F, Cauchy--Schwarz in p and (26) bound the normalized h=0 term by
 Cq^(-1/2+epsilon)V_F||C_hat||_2,
which is (10). Equations (6), (9), and (10) prove (6).

Under (11), substitute q=m^2 into (6):
 q^(-1/32)q^(1/2)=q^(15/32)=m^(15/16).
This proves (12). Fact 212d1415bf03c2a7 proves (11) for its shared-lift model. Summing (12) proves (14). Unit-modulus character multiplication preserves l2 norms and zero-one gates contract them. If a common norm is zero, the corresponding common sequence and every gated atom are zero. Otherwise (15) is defined, and
 15/16+1/80=19/20,
so (16) implies (17). Fact 55733dfba03775a2 supplies the stated subpolynomial primitive/imprimitive count, and fact 8592875ae5046498 supplies the unrestricted-selector obstruction. The remaining tax and scope clauses follow from (13)-(16).
