glossary.B_F(g): the l1(l2) norm of F_hat restricted to frequencies divisible by g over blocks of length m
glossary.L_IJOP_core: P_IJOP normalized by the two nonzero external column l2 norms
glossary.P_IJOP: the complete projective tax of a finite shared-lift core assembly
glossary.V_F: the supremum-plus-total-variation norm of the separated interval profile F

5ba70b46990216f1.title: BOUNDED-ROUGH-PRIME LOWERING OF THE TWO-ACTIVE PRIMITIVE-SIBLING KERNEL: FOUR MODES FOR C2, SEVEN FOR C3, ELEVEN FOR C4. Let J be one of 2,3,4. Let D be the product of a set P of J distinct odd primes, let v be a positive squarefree integer with gcd(D,v)=1, put n=Dv, and let A be a nonzero integer. Let rho=(epsilon,a,b) be a primitive ray with epsilon in {+1,-1}, a,b positive, gcd(a,b)=1, gcd(a,Dv)=1, and gcd(Ab,D)=1. For p in P define
5ba70b46990216f1.author: slava chan
5ba70b46990216f1.statement:
BOUNDED-ROUGH-PRIME LOWERING OF THE TWO-ACTIVE PRIMITIVE-SIBLING KERNEL: FOUR MODES FOR C2, SEVEN FOR C3, ELEVEN FOR C4. Let J be one of 2,3,4. Let D be the product of a set P of J distinct odd primes, let v be a positive squarefree integer with gcd(D,v)=1, put n=Dv, and let A be a nonzero integer. Let rho=(epsilon,a,b) be a primitive ray with epsilon in {+1,-1}, a,b positive, gcd(a,b)=1, gcd(a,Dv)=1, and gcd(Ab,D)=1. For p in P define
zeta_p(rho)=e_p(A epsilon b[a(n/p)]^{-1}),
Gamma_p(rho)=zeta_p(rho)+1/(p-1).                                 (1)
Define the scoped complete two-active primitive-sibling kernel
K_{2;J,D,v}(rho)
=sum_{S subset P, |S|=2}
 (product_{p in S}Gamma_p(rho))
 (product_{p in P minus S}(-1/p)),                                 (2)
and include the small-v phase by
K_{2;J,D,v}^{full}(rho)
=e_v(A epsilon b(aD)^{-1})K_{2;J,D,v}(rho).                         (3)

For every squarefree r dividing D with omega(r)<=2, let R be its prime support and put
c_{J,D}(r)=sum_{S subset P, |S|=2, R subset S}
 (product_{p in S minus R}1/(p-1))
 (product_{p in P minus S}(-1/p)).                                 (4)
All nonzero c_{J,D}(r) have the common sign (-1)^(J-2), and
K_{2;J,D,v}^{full}(rho)
=sum_{r|D, omega(r)<=2}
 c_{J,D}(r)e_{vr}(A epsilon b[a(D/r)]^{-1}).                        (5)
There are exactly
1+J+binom(J,2)
modes: four for J=2, seven for J=3, and eleven for J=4. If Z is a positive real number such that every p|D satisfies p>=Z, then
sum_{r|D, omega(r)<=2}|c_{J,D}(r)|
<= (9/4)binom(J,2) Z^(-(J-2)).                                    (6)
Hence, for any anatomy-specific primitive-ray scale coefficients B_lambda^{(J)}(rho;z), the full two-active sibling row
T_lambda^{(J)}(z)=sum_rho B_lambda^{(J)}(rho;z)K_{2;J,D_lambda,v_lambda}^{full}(rho)
is a signed weighted sum of exactly four, seven, or eleven reciprocal-slope transforms, and weighted Cauchy-Schwarz reduces its full square to the corresponding coefficient-weighted transform energy with loss at most the coefficient mass in (6).

This is the exact algebraic bounded-prime lowering needed to formulate C2 and C3 analogues of the C4 eleven-mode supplier in fact a3132ecd1bd44382. It does not transfer the C4 ray-scale coefficient B_lambda to C2 or C3: each B_lambda^{(J)} must retain that anatomy's own terminal sign mu(v)(-1)^J, source amplitude, masks, gates, heights, convolution or stopping slots, and original support. It also does not assert that an unrecombined literal C2 or C3 row equals only the two-active primitive-sibling family (2), does not pay proper-conductor or other centered faces, and proves no C2, C3, C4, canonical moment, or Goldbach estimate.
5ba70b46990216f1.proof:
The local identity in (1) is proved exactly as equation (6) of fact 34d306bcb630f9df and does not depend on the number of other primes in D. Namely, primitive projection modulo p gives
P_{p,p}delta_x=delta_x-(p-1)^{-1}1,
and the nontrivial additive phase sums to -1 on the unit group, so its projected evaluation is zeta_p+1/(p-1).

Expand the product over active primes in (2). For a fixed two-element active set S, choose a subset R of S at which the zeta_p term is taken; the primes in S minus R contribute 1/(p-1), and the primes outside S contribute -1/p. Grouping by R gives (4). Since |S|=2, only |R|<=2 occurs.

Every summand in (4) has exactly J-2 factors -1/p, independently of R and S. All its remaining factors are positive. Therefore every nonzero coefficient has the common sign (-1)^(J-2).

The product of local phases over p|r is, by CRT,
product_{p|r}zeta_p(rho)
=e_r(A epsilon b[a(Dv/r)]^{-1}).                                  (7)
Combining (7) with the small-v phase in (3), again by CRT, gives
e_v(A epsilon b(aD)^{-1})
 product_{p|r}zeta_p(rho)
=e_{vr}(A epsilon b[a(D/r)]^{-1}).                                 (8)
This remains valid for r=1, when the right side is exactly the small-v phase. Grouping the expansion using (4), then applying (8), proves (5).

The possible prime supports R have sizes zero, one, and two, giving
1+J+binom(J,2)
terms. Substitution of J=2,3,4 gives 4,7,11.

To prove (6), take absolute values after observing the common sign and sum the coefficients before grouping. This gives
sum_r|c_{J,D}(r)|
=sum_{S subset P, |S|=2}
 product_{p in S}[1+1/(p-1)]
 product_{p in P minus S}(1/p).                                   (9)
For odd p, 1+1/(p-1)<=3/2. Because Z>0 and p>=Z, each inactive reciprocal factor satisfies 1/p<=Z^{-1}. There are binom(J,2) choices of S and J-2 inactive reciprocal factors, so equation (9) yields (6).

Finally substitute (5) into the definition of T_lambda^{(J)} and interchange finite sums. After removing the common sign from c_{J,D}, all coefficient magnitudes are positive, so
|sum_r c_{J,D}(r)S_r|^2
<=[sum_r|c_{J,D}(r)|][sum_r|c_{J,D}(r)||S_r|^2]
by weighted Cauchy-Schwarz. This proves the stated reduction. The argument never identifies coefficient families belonging to distinct terminal anatomies; the terminal sign and every literal slot must remain in the anatomy-specific B_lambda^{(J)}. Hence all scope exclusions follow.

glossary.B_lambda^{(J)}: An anatomy-specific primitive-ray scale coefficient; it is not transferred between C2, C3, and C4.
glossary.K_{2;J,D,v}: The complete family of centered primitive siblings with exactly two active primes among J rough primes.
glossary.K_{2;J,D,v}^{full}: The same kernel multiplied by its exact small-v phase.
glossary.T_lambda^{(J)}: The full two-active sibling row formed from B_lambda^{(J)} and K_{2;J,D,v}^{full}.
glossary.Z: A positive lower bound for every rough prime dividing D.
glossary.c_{J,D}(r): The reciprocal-slope mode coefficient in the J-prime two-active kernel.

5c2e3d6320031fbf.title: GA-PRIME-LITERAL-DISC: EXACT PAIR-SPECIFIC PRIME-CONDUCTOR RESIDUE DISCREPANCY, HILBERT-SCHMIDT SUPPLIER, AND ACTUAL TRACE REASSEMBLY. Adopt the complete high-rough C chamber, ray Hilbert space H_ray, exact C-edge support, hard selector theta_{d,v}(R,R'), ray coefficients b_{v,R}(y), operators K_{d,v}, and trace formula of fact d92616c2bca6126f. Thus D>Q^2, Z>=2Q, v is in {1,2}, and every retained terminal integer is n=dv with D<=d<2D
5c2e3d6320031fbf.author: slava chan
5c2e3d6320031fbf.statement:
GA-PRIME-LITERAL-DISC: EXACT PAIR-SPECIFIC PRIME-CONDUCTOR RESIDUE DISCREPANCY, HILBERT-SCHMIDT SUPPLIER, AND ACTUAL TRACE REASSEMBLY. Adopt the complete high-rough C chamber, ray Hilbert space H_ray, exact C-edge support, hard selector theta_{d,v}(R,R'), ray coefficients b_{v,R}(y), operators K_{d,v}, and trace formula of fact d92616c2bca6126f. Thus D>Q^2, Z>=2Q, v is in {1,2}, and every retained terminal integer is n=dv with D<=d<2D.

Let eta_v(d) be one when d>1 is squarefree, P^-(d)>=Z, and the exact C edge n=dv is retained, and zero otherwise. Let rho=(R,R') be an ordered pair of distinct supported primitive rays. If its physical conductor m_q(rho) is an odd prime p, put c_rho=C_q(rho) modulo p; this is a unit residue. For D<=t<2D and every unit residue z modulo p define the literal pair occupancy
N_{rho,v,t}(z)
 =sum_{D<=d<=t, dv congruent z (mod p)}
   eta_v(d)theta_{d,v}(R,R'),                                    (1)
its mass H_{rho,v,t}=sum_z^*N_{rho,v,t}(z), and its discrepancy
delta_{rho,v,t}(z)
 =N_{rho,v,t}(z)-H_{rho,v,t}/(p-1).                              (2)
Define the inverse-residue additive Fourier coefficient
Dhat_{rho,v,t}(c)
 =sum_{z (mod p)}^* e_p(-c z^{-1})delta_{rho,v,t}(z).            (3)

Let K^{prime}_{d,v} be the restriction of K_{d,v} to ordered ray pairs whose physical conductor m_q is an odd prime, and put
A^{prime}_v(t)=sum_{D<=d<=t}K^{prime}_{d,v}.                     (4)
Then A^{prime}_v(t) has zero diagonal, and for every rho with prime conductor p,
(A^{prime}_v(t))_{R',R}=Dhat_{rho,v,t}(c_rho).                   (5)
Consequently there is the exact Hilbert-Schmidt identity
||A^{prime}_v(t)||_{HS}^2
 =sum_{rho:m_q(rho) is an odd prime}
   |Dhat_{rho,v,t}(c_rho)|^2,                                   (6)
and hence
||A^{prime}_v(t)||_{op}
 <=[sum_{rho:m_q(rho) is an odd prime}
   |Dhat_{rho,v,t}(c_rho)|^2]^{1/2}.                             (7)
In particular the source-specific discrepancy estimate
max_{D<=t<2D}
 [sum_{rho:m_q(rho) is an odd prime}
   |Dhat_{rho,v,t}(c_rho)|^2]^{1/2}
 <=x^{o(1)}BQF/D                                                (PRIME-PAIR-DISC)
would prove C-HILBERT-OP-SUP at the required scale for the odd-prime-conductor component. PRIME-PAIR-DISC is not asserted.

There is also an exact identity retaining the actual terminal source weights. For every rho of odd-prime conductor p and unit z modulo p put
W_{rho,v}(z)
 =sum_{D<=d<2D, dv congruent z (mod p)}
   eta_v(d)theta_{d,v}(R,R')
   b_{v,R}(dv/B)conjugate(b_{v,R'}(dv/B)),                       (8)
let Wbar_{rho,v}=(p-1)^{-1}sum_z^*W_{rho,v}(z), and define
What_{rho,v}(c)
 =sum_{z (mod p)}^*e_p(-c z^{-1})
   [W_{rho,v}(z)-Wbar_{rho,v}].                                 (9)
If C-qSRC_C^{prime} denotes the restriction of the exact trace in fact d92616c2bca6126f to odd-prime physical conductors, then
C-qSRC_C^{prime}
 =sum_{v in {1,2}}
  sum_{rho:m_q(rho) is an odd prime}
   What_{rho,v}(c_rho).                                         (10)
Thus the literal incomplete ray family, terminal weights, conductor and numerator classes, and every pair-dependent hard deletion occur inside (1)-(3) and (8)-(10); no full-ray completion or unweighted occupancy is inserted.

The unweighted full-ray discrepancy of fact ad3e98d3e74ae7a5 does not formally control (1). More precisely, even if a finite terminal set has exactly the same number of values dv in every unit residue modulo p, a zero-one pair selector can retain only one chosen residue z_0 for one ordered pair. For that pair, (3) equals
e_p(-c z_0^{-1})+1/(p-1),
whose modulus is at least 1-1/(p-1). Repeating the construction scales this quantity linearly while preserving exact equidistribution of the undeleted terminal set. Likewise, undeleted unweighted occupancies do not determine (8), because its complex source factor varies with d and with the ordered ray pair. These are formal no-transfer examples for arbitrary zero-one selectors or weights; they are not asserted to occur for the literal Good-W selector or source.

Therefore the finite-dimensional cancellation in fact ad3e98d3e74ae7a5 survives literally only after proving pair-specific weighted discrepancy or a factorization that removes the d-dependence of theta_{d,v}(R,R') and the ordered-pair dependence of the source weights. Absent such an input, equation (10), rather than the unweighted full-ray operator, is the exact weaker source-specific frontier. This theorem proves only the identities and implications above. It proves neither PRIME-PAIR-DISC, nor the odd-prime trace estimate, nor the composite-conductor component, C-HILBERT-OP-SUP, C-qSRC-SUP, a tail payment, or Goldbach.
5c2e3d6320031fbf.proof:
For an ordered pair rho=(R,R') of odd-prime conductor p, fact 764588e99974a6d9 gives, for every retained unit n=dv modulo p,
K^circ_{p,c_rho}(dv)
 =e_p(-c_rho(dv)^{-1})+1/(p-1).                                (11)
The definition of K_{d,v} in fact d92616c2bca6126f places theta_{d,v}(R,R') times (11) in the reversed matrix slot (R',R), and makes the entry zero unless the exact C edge is retained. Group the partial d-sum by z=dv modulo p. This gives
(A^{prime}_v(t))_{R',R}
 =sum_z^*[e_p(-c_rho z^{-1})+1/(p-1)]N_{rho,v,t}(z).             (12)

For every unit c modulo p, inversion permutes the nonzero residues and the complete nontrivial additive-character sum is
sum_z^*e_p(-c z^{-1})=-1.
Therefore
sum_z^*[e_p(-c z^{-1})+1/(p-1)]=0.                              (13)
Subtracting H_{rho,v,t}/(p-1) from every occupancy in (12) changes nothing by (13). The constant 1/(p-1) then contributes zero because sum_z^*delta_{rho,v,t}(z)=0. The result is exactly (3), proving (5).

The diagonal of every K_{d,v} is zero, so A^{prime}_v(t) has zero diagonal. Its off-diagonal matrix slots are in bijection with ordered ray pairs rho. The squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm is the sum of the squared moduli of all matrix entries, so (5) proves (6). The operator norm is at most the Hilbert-Schmidt norm, proving (7). Taking the maximum over t proves the stated implication from PRIME-PAIR-DISC to the odd-prime component of C-HILBERT-OP-SUP.

For the trace identity, fact d92616c2bca6126f gives
trace(K_{d,v}T_v(dv/B))
 =sum_{R!=R'}theta_{d,v}(R,R')
  K^circ_{m_q,C_q}(dv)
  b_{v,R}(dv/B)conjugate(b_{v,R'}(dv/B)).                       (14)
Restrict (14) to odd-prime m_q, sum d and v, and group first by rho and then by z=dv modulo p. Equations (11) and (8) give
C-qSRC_C^{prime}
 =sum_v sum_rho sum_z^*
 [e_p(-c_rho z^{-1})+1/(p-1)]W_{rho,v}(z).                      (15)
Subtract Wbar_{rho,v} from every residue by (13). The remaining constant 1/(p-1) vanishes because the centered W-profile has sum zero. The inner sum is precisely (9), proving (10).

For the first no-transfer example, take an undeleted finite multiset with the same multiplicity in every unit z and let one abstract pair selector be one exactly on the copies occupying z_0. Its selected occupancy has value one at z_0 and zero elsewhere after one-copy normalization. Its discrepancy is 1-1/(p-1) at z_0 and -1/(p-1) elsewhere. Substitution in (3), using the complete additive sum -1, gives
Dhat(c)=e_p(-c z_0^{-1})+1/(p-1).
The reverse triangle inequality gives modulus at least 1-1/(p-1). Replicating every undeleted residue equally and selecting all copies at z_0 multiplies this Fourier coefficient by the replication factor, while the undeleted global occupancy remains exactly uniform. This proves that global unweighted discrepancy alone cannot control the pair-selected discrepancy. Formula (8) itself proves the analogous logical dependence on the actual complex source weights. The examples are explicitly formal and make no claim about the literal theta or b. All scope limitations follow.

glossary.A^{prime}_v(t): The partial sum of K^{prime}_{d,v} up to t.
glossary.C-qSRC_C^{prime}: The odd-prime-physical-conductor restriction of the exact high-rough C centered trace.
glossary.Dhat_{rho,v,t}(c): The inverse-residue additive Fourier coefficient of the pair-selected discrepancy.
glossary.K^{prime}_{d,v}: The odd-prime-physical-conductor restriction of the literal ray operator K_{d,v}.
glossary.N_{rho,v,t}(z): The pair-selected number of retained C dilators up to t whose terminal integer dv occupies residue z modulo the prime physical conductor.
glossary.PRIME-PAIR-DISC: The pairwise Fourier-discrepancy energy estimate sufficient for the prime-conductor part of C-HILBERT-OP-SUP.
glossary.W_{rho,v}(z): The pair-selected residue occupancy weighted by the two actual moving ray coefficients.
glossary.What_{rho,v}(c): The inverse-residue additive Fourier coefficient of the centered weighted occupancy.
glossary.eta_v(d): The zero-one indicator that d supplies the exact retained high-rough C edge n=dv.
glossary.rho: An ordered pair (R,R') of distinct supported primitive rays.

5c6cc8f5c261c259.title: EXACT ONE-SIDED H-SYMMETRIC DELETION DUALITY
5c6cc8f5c261c259.author: slava chan
5c6cc8f5c261c259.statement:
EXACT ONE-SIDED H-SYMMETRIC DELETION DUALITY.

Let mathcal O be any finite h-symmetric subfamily of the literal C2 atoms c_z of fact 42104ea7b4b24b0b. Choose one representative j from each pair {h,-h} in mathcal O and put
t_j=c_j+conjugate(c_j)=2Re(c_j).
Thus t_j is real. An h-symmetric zero-one deletion is specified by numbers delta_j in {0,1}, where delta_j=1 retains both labels in the pair. Put
T_mathcal O(delta)=sum_j delta_j t_j,
P_+=sum_j max(t_j,0),   P_-=sum_j max(-t_j,0),               (1)
and
E_-=sum_{j:t_j<0}t_j^2.                                     (2)

(A) The exact extrema over all h-symmetric zero-one deletions are
min_delta T_mathcal O(delta)=-P_-,
max_delta T_mathcal O(delta)=P_+,
max_delta |T_mathcal O(delta)|=max(P_+,P_-).                 (3)
Consequently, for every U>=0,
T_mathcal O(delta)>=-U for every h-symmetric deletion delta
if and only if P_-<=U.                                       (4)
Likewise,
|T_mathcal O(delta)|<=U for every h-symmetric deletion delta
if and only if max(P_+,P_-)<=U.                              (5)

(B) If E_->0, define the negative effective support
N_eff^-=P_-^2/E_-.
For every C>=0, the estimate
T_mathcal O(delta)>=-C E_-^(1/2)
for every h-symmetric deletion delta                           (6)
holds if and only if
N_eff^-<=C^2.                                                 (7)
If E_-=0, every t_j is nonnegative and (6) holds automatically.

(C) Take mathcal O to be the union of the off-diagonal cell-pair families mathcal L_ij with i<j in fact 42ae728764073a1a. Then (4) says that a lower bound
T_off(delta)>=-rho
uniform over every h-symmetric source deletion is exactly equivalent to the source-specific negative paired-real mass bound
P_-<=rho.                                                     (8)
In contrast, the natural undeleted off-diagonal sum is
T_off(1)=P_+-P_-.                                            (9)
Equation (9) may vanish while P_-=P_+ is arbitrarily large: take n atoms with t_j=1 and n atoms with t_j=-1. Thus a bound for the natural selector cannot be upgraded to an arbitrary-mask lower bound from h-symmetry or l2 energy alone.

This theorem identifies the exact finite mass hypothesis for a mask-uniform off-diagonal lower bound. It does not prove (8) for the literal arithmetic source, does not construct a counterexample for the natural selector, and supplies no rectangular decoder estimate, varying-fibre cancellation, common-cell or cross-cell analytic bound, or Goldbach implication.
5c6cc8f5c261c259.proof:
For each j, the contribution delta_j t_j is independent of every other index. To minimize the sum, take delta_j=1 when t_j<0 and delta_j=0 when t_j>=0. This gives
sum_{t_j<0}t_j=-sum_jmax(-t_j,0)=-P_-.
Any other deletion either removes a negative term, which increases the sum, or adds a nonnegative term, which also does not decrease it. This proves the first identity in (3). The same argument with signs reversed shows that the maximum is obtained by retaining precisely t_j>0 and equals P_+. The maximum absolute value is the larger of the magnitude of the minimum and the maximum, proving the third identity.

A family of real numbers is bounded below by -U for every deletion exactly when its minimum is at least -U. By (3), this is equivalent to -P_- >= -U, or P_-<=U, proving (4). The uniform absolute-value assertion is equivalent to the minimum being at least -U and the maximum being at most U. By (3), these are P_-<=U and P_+<=U, proving (5).

Assume E_->0. By (4), equation (6) is equivalent to
P_-<=C E_-^(1/2).
Both sides are nonnegative, so squaring and dividing by E_- gives
P_-^2/E_-<=C^2,
which is exactly (7). If E_-=0, no t_j is negative, so every deleted sum is nonnegative and (6) is immediate.

For (C), fact 42ae728764073a1a defines the off-diagonal union by a phase-independent rough-prime cell label. Therefore this union is h-symmetric, and every h-symmetric deletion is represented by a vector delta as above. Its deleted off-diagonal sum is T_mathcal O(delta). Applying (4) with U=rho proves (8). Retaining all pairs gives
sum_j t_j=sum_{t_j>0}t_j+sum_{t_j<0}t_j=P_+-P_-,
which proves (9). With n entries equal to one and n entries equal to minus one, both P_+ and P_- equal n while (9) is zero and E_-=n. This also shows that neither h-symmetry nor a support-independent multiple of E_-^(1/2) controls every deletion.

The final paragraph is a scope statement: all steps are exact finite subset-sum identities.

glossary.E_-: The squared l2 mass of the negative paired-real atoms.
glossary.N_eff^-: The negative effective support P_- squared divided by E_-.
glossary.P_+: The total positive paired-real mass in mathcal O.
glossary.P_-: The total negative paired-real mass in mathcal O.
glossary.T_mathcal O(delta): The real sum over an h-symmetric zero-one deletion of mathcal O.
glossary.mathcal O: A finite h-symmetric subfamily of literal C2 atoms.

5ce54dcef3d61da1.title: GA-PRECOPY-MOM: EXACT GOOD-W TERMINAL-COPY AGGREGATION BEFORE THE FIRST CAUCHY STEP
5ce54dcef3d61da1.author: slava chan
5ce54dcef3d61da1.statement:
GA-PRECOPY-MOM: EXACT GOOD-W TERMINAL-COPY AGGREGATION BEFORE THE FIRST CAUCHY STEP.

Fix tau>0 and all exact data required in fact e55b27d39c593164 before its dilator-block restriction: the selected integer N, one orientation, exact outer gcd g, normalized layer, original source atom, active dyadic label, fixed-U, high, actual-G, parent, target-gcd, source, smooth/projective, ordering, equality, collision, deletion, provenance, and every other frozen coordinate of that fact. Fix one frequency block
1<=F<=x^3.
Thus Q,B,H_P and the target mathscr A are common fixed parameters.

For every integer j let Lambda_j(n) be the exact terminal copies lambda over n whose unique marked dilator satisfies
2^j<=d_lambda<2^(j+1).
Let J_dil be the finite set of j for which such a copy occurs. Define the disjoint union
Lambda_term(n)=bigsqcup_{j in J_dil}Lambda_j(n).                 (1)
Every terminal A or C_j copy occurs exactly once in (1), because it has one positive integer marked dilator d_lambda and the half-open power-of-two intervals partition the positive integers. Let K_F(n,lambda) be the physical row in equations (10)-(11) of fact e55b27d39c593164 and define
K_F^agg(n)=sum_{lambda in Lambda_term(n)}K_F(n,lambda),          (2)
M_F^precopy=sum_{B/2<=n<=2B}|K_F^agg(n)|^2.                     (3)
Then the sum of the complete fixed-family frequency contributions over all marked-dilator blocks is exactly
T_F^term
 =sum_{j in J_dil}T_{F,2^j}
 =H_P^{-1}sum_{B/2<=n<=2B}K_F^agg(n),                           (4)
and
|T_F^term|^2<=2B H_P^{-2}M_F^precopy.                           (GA-PRECOPY-CS)

The pre-copy moment has the exact expansion
M_F^precopy
 =sum_n sum_{lambda,lambda' in Lambda_term(n)}
   K_F(n,lambda)conjugate(K_F(n,lambda')).                      (5)
Writing
K_F(n,lambda)=a_lambda(n)K_F^flat(n,lambda)
with the scalar terminal-marker coefficient removed gives
M_F^precopy
 =sum_n sum_{lambda,lambda'}
   a_lambda(n)conjugate(a_lambda'(n))
   K_F^flat(n,lambda)conjugate(K_F^flat(n,lambda')).             (6)
Thus every relative terminal-marker sign and every lambda!=lambda' cross-copy term missing from the copywise moments is retained in (6).

There is no loss in using this interface as a sufficient moment target:
M_F^precopy
 <=x^{o(1)}
   sum_n sum_{lambda in Lambda_term(n)}|K_F(n,lambda)|^2.        (7)
Consequently every collection of accepted copywise moment estimates implies the corresponding pre-copy estimate up to x^{o(1)}, while a direct proof of the pre-copy estimate may additionally exploit cross-copy marker cancellation.

This theorem is exact regrouping and Cauchy only. It asserts no pre-copy moment estimate, no identity that automatically cancels the lambda-dependent dilator or hard selectors, no C-qSRC-BV-SUP, no GA-NR-DIL, no tail payment, and no Goldbach conclusion.
5ce54dcef3d61da1.proof:
For fixed j, equation (10) of fact e55b27d39c593164 applied to the half-open block
2^j<=d_lambda<2^(j+1)
is
T_{F,2^j}
 =H_P^{-1}sum_{B/2<=n<=2B}
  sum_{lambda in Lambda_j(n)}K_F(n,lambda).                    (8)
All parameters outside the dilator block were fixed in the statement, so B,H_P and K_F have the same meaning for every j. Each exact terminal copy has one marked dilator, hence belongs to exactly one Lambda_j(n). The terminal marker is complete, so summing (8) over the finite set J_dil proves (4) with the disjoint union (1). No coefficient or selector is changed.

There are fewer than 2B integers in B/2<=n<=2B. Cauchy--Schwarz in the n-sum in (4) gives
|T_F^term|^2
 <=H_P^{-2}(2B)sum_n|K_F^agg(n)|^2,
which is GA-PRECOPY-CS.

Expanding the square in (3) proves (5). Equation (9) of fact e55b27d39c593164 shows that a_lambda(n) is a scalar factor independent of q,h in the complete row. Hence it factors from K_F(n,lambda); define K_F^flat by division on each nonzero exact copy. Substitution in (5) proves (6). In particular the coefficient on a cross-copy term is a_lambda conjugate(a_lambda'), rather than |a_lambda|^2, so the relative signs identified in fact 50ef6972010758a6 are present.

For fixed n, Cauchy--Schwarz in the finite disjoint copy set gives
|sum_lambda K_F(n,lambda)|^2
 <=|Lambda_term(n)|sum_lambda|K_F(n,lambda)|^2.                 (9)
The copy ledger in fact e55b27d39c593164 is divisor-bounded over each n: A interval-prime copies are divisor-bounded, the C_j representation is unique for fixed j, the number of allowed j is at most O(log(2B)), and every retained auxiliary exact label has x^{o(1)} multiplicity. Also d_lambda<=n<=2B, so J_dil has O(log(2B))=x^{o(1)} indices. Because the union in (1) is disjoint, these bounds give
|Lambda_term(n)|<=x^{o(1)}
uniformly. Sum (9) over n to prove (7). All stated exclusions follow.

glossary.GA-PRECOPY-MOM: The exact pre-copy moment interface retaining all cross-copy marker signs.
glossary.K_F^agg(n): The complete Good-W terminal-copy row aggregated at fixed marked integer n before Cauchy.
glossary.Lambda_term(n): The disjoint union over half-open dyadic marked-dilator blocks of all exact Good-W terminal copies over n in one fully frozen family.
glossary.M_F^precopy: The n-summed square of the fully aggregated terminal-copy row.

5ce79780e36b1ce1.title: PRIME-MODULUS MOBIUS--TRACE THEOREM NO-FIT AT THE ACTUAL-Z_MID CRITICAL LENGTH. Assume the natural actual-Z_mid g=1, |h|=1 endpoint scales of fact 58c03698e1b077c3. Restrict hypothetically to the most favorable full-conductor prime-modulus slice b=p with p not dividing N, remove every a-side arithmetic mask except mu(a), and retain only a fixed smooth weight on a asymp A_p. Then
5ce79780e36b1ce1.author: slava chan
5ce79780e36b1ce1.statement:
PRIME-MODULUS MOBIUS--TRACE THEOREM NO-FIT AT THE ACTUAL-Z_MID CRITICAL LENGTH. Assume the natural actual-Z_mid g=1, |h|=1 endpoint scales of fact 58c03698e1b077c3. Restrict hypothetically to the most favorable full-conductor prime-modulus slice b=p with p not dividing N, remove every a-side arithmetic mask except mu(a), and retain only a fixed smooth weight on a asymp A_p. Then
p=x^(2/3+o(1)), A_p=x^(1/2+o(1))=p^(3/4+o(1)),
and the reciprocal kernel is
K_p(a)=e_p(Na^{-1}).                                                (1)

The Fouvry--Kowalski--Michel bound in arXiv:1207.0617, Theorem 2.5, specializes to
sum_{a<=A_p}mu(a)K_p(a)
 <=C_eta A_p(1+p/A_p)^(1/12)p^(-eta)
for every fixed eta<1/48.                                          (2)
At the critical length in (1), the factor after A_p in (2) is
p^(1/48-eta+o(1)),                                                  (3)
so (2) supplies no fixed-power saving over the trivial A_p bound.

The Korolev--Shparlinski bound in arXiv:1804.01337, Theorem 2.1, applies throughout A_p>=p^(1/2+epsilon) for fixed epsilon>0, but gives only
sum_{a<=A_p}mu(a)K_p(a)
 <=C_epsilon A_p loglog(p)/log(p).                                  (4)
Thus (4) is logarithmically, not fixed-power, smaller than A_p. Direct absolute summation of (4) over p asymp x^(2/3) remains x^(7/6+o(1)), above x^(1-delta) for every fixed delta>0.

Therefore neither published theorem, used directly modulus by modulus, supplies the fixed-power actual-Z_mid boundary estimate even on this ideal unmasked prime full-conductor slice. This is a sharp theorem-right-hand-side no-fit, not a lower bound for the prime slice and not an impossibility theorem. It does not exclude cancellation across p, a critical-length power theorem, use of both Möbius variables before absolute values, or a stronger theorem for the complete natural-mask packet.
5ce79780e36b1ce1.proof:
For p not dividing N, the function in (1) is an additive trace function of the rational function N/X modulo p. Korolev--Shparlinski, arXiv:1804.01337, describe exponential functions e_p(Psi(n)) for rational Psi as bounded-conductor isotypic trace functions and exclude only functions proportional to e_p(cn)chi(n). The rational function N/X has a pole at zero and is not of that exceptional linear-additive times multiplicative form. Hence their Theorem 2.1 applies to K_p. The same nonexceptional trace-function hypothesis is the hypothesis in Fouvry--Kowalski--Michel, arXiv:1207.0617, Theorem 2.5. Fixed smooth weights on the interval are inserted by partial summation, without altering any power or logarithmic exponent.

Theorem 2.5 of Fouvry--Kowalski--Michel states exactly the bound in (2) for every eta<1/48. Since A_p=p^(3/4+o(1)),
(1+p/A_p)^(1/12)
 =p^((1-3/4)/12+o(1))
 =p^(1/48+o(1)).
Multiplication by p^(-eta) proves (3). Because eta is required to be strictly less than 1/48, the displayed exponent 1/48-eta is positive for every admissible fixed eta. Thus the theorem's right-hand side is not A_pp^(-delta) for any fixed delta>0 at the critical length. This agrees with the authors' explicit statement that their bound is nontrivial only for lengths exceeding p^(3/4+epsilon).

Theorem 2.1 of Korolev--Shparlinski states (4) under A_p>=p^(1/2+epsilon). The critical A_p=p^(3/4+o(1)) satisfies this hypothesis for any fixed epsilon<1/4 and all sufficiently large p. But loglog(p)/log(p)=p^(o(1)), not p^(-delta) for a fixed delta>0, so the gain is only logarithmic.

Finally, even the crude count of at most O(p) prime moduli p in a dyadic interval of scale x^(2/3+o(1)) turns the modulus-by-modulus absolute use of (4) into at best
x^(2/3+o(1))x^(1/2+o(1))=x^(7/6+o(1)).
This cannot imply x^(1-delta). Every reduction was made in favor of applicability by deleting masks, so the conclusion is precisely the claimed direct-consumer no-fit and makes no assertion about cancellation discarded by those reductions.

glossary.A_p: The length of the Möbius-twisted a-interval on the prime full-conductor slice.
glossary.K_p: The prime-modulus reciprocal trace function K_p(a)=e_p(Na^{-1}) on nonzero residues modulo p.

5ced883d5560f772.title: EXACT NORMALIZED POISSON PHASE AND FIRST NO-FIT TO THE EXISTING LOW-BETA CONSUMERS
5ced883d5560f772.author: slava chan
5ced883d5560f772.statement:
EXACT NORMALIZED POISSON PHASE AND FIRST NO-FIT TO THE EXISTING LOW-BETA CONSUMERS.

Work in a forward frozen layer of fact a71f777ad842c886, so R>D, d=ga, r=gb, the normalized marked factor is b, the normalized reciprocal modulus is a, and
am+bk=L_0=N/g.
Put
Q_0=D/g, B_0=R/g, H_src=B_0/M, H_RS=B_0/Q_0.
Assume Q_0>1 and B_0=Q_0^beta with
1<=beta<=6/5-2kappa, 0<kappa<=1/100.
Then the normalized A,B,C_1,C_2,C_3 marker leaves have the correct Möbius coefficient mu(a)c_X(b), coprimality (a,b)=1, fixed target L_0, and label-scalar parent supplied by fact a71f777ad842c886.

For every nonzero Poisson frequency h, the literal forward phase from fact df9748efe29ab475 satisfies the exact reciprocity identity
e_b(L_0 h a^(-1))
 =exp(2 pi i L_0 h/(ab)) e_a(-L_0 h b^(-1)),                 (1)
where each inverse is taken in its displayed coprime modulus. Thus after reciprocity the marker is on exactly the inverse-product factor b required by the A/B/C_j reciprocal consumers, and no marker-on-r versus trace-on-b mismatch remains.

However, the normalized identity is not by itself a direct instance of facts 533acf4056cf5bee, 664a92777dc5f5db, 2ff1c15aef183bac, 3b1bda56ad927c5e, or 0576f567200d41f1. The literal Poisson transform has natural frequency scale and prefactor
H_src=B_0/M, H_src^(-1)=M/B_0,                               (2)
whereas all five cited raised-stopping consumers impose
H_RS=B_0/Q_0, H_RS^(-1)=Q_0/B_0.                             (3)
Their ratio is
H_RS/H_src=M/Q_0.                                            (4)
Consequently a literal h-block at the source scale, with its unchanged prefactor and amplitude, meets the displayed h-support and normalization of those consumers only when an additional comparison M asymp Q_0, or a new off-scale trace theorem, is supplied. Low beta, the high-R mask, and parent scalarity do not imply this comparison.

The smooth-amplitude slot has the same obstruction. On h asymp H_src, the archimedean reciprocity factor in (1) has logarithmic phase size
L_0 H_src/(Q_0B_0)=L_0/(Q_0M),
which is bounded on the literal source support because N asymp DM and L_0=N/g, Q_0=D/g. If it is instead forced onto h asymp H_RS, its logarithmic phase size is
L_0 H_RS/(Q_0B_0)=L_0/Q_0^2 asymp M/Q_0.                    (5)
Therefore the factor belongs to a fixed uniformly scaled-smooth family only under an additional uniform bound on M/Q_0; otherwise its logarithmic derivatives and the projective separation cost are not uniformly bounded.

The fixed-target size is not the first obstruction on the forced high low-beta band. More precisely, assume D=x^(1/2+o(1)), N asymp x, and
R>x^(9/16-kappa_0), kappa_0=1/200.
Then (B_0/Q_0)=R/D=Q_0^(beta-1) and beta-1<=1/5-2kappa imply
Q_0>=x^{c_kappa+o(1)}, where
c_kappa=(1/16-kappa_0)/(1/5-2kappa)>0.                       (6)
Hence
L_0=(N/D)Q_0<=Q_0^{C_A}                                     (7)
for some fixed C_A depending only on kappa and all sufficiently large x. Thus the fixed noncoprime target condition in the B and C_j consumers can be met after exact g is frozen.

By contrast, the A-consumer 664a92777dc5f5db requires its phase numerator to be a unit modulo the reciprocal modulus. The source equation gives
gcd(L_0,a)=gcd(bk,a),
which need not equal one. Therefore the normalized A leaf is a direct instance of that consumer only after the additional selector gcd(L_0,a)=1 or a verified nonunit-target extension.

These are exact theorem-slot no-fits, not arithmetic lower bounds. In particular, they do not rule out summing the off-scale full reciprocal-energy bound over g, using Fourier decay on H_src<1 layers, proving a nonunit interval-prime extension, or developing a new outer-gcd-assembled theorem.
5ced883d5560f772.proof:
Fact df9748efe29ab475 gives, after fixing g=gcd(d,r), the normalized equation am+bk=L_0 and Poisson summation in the progression
m congruent to L_0 a^(-1) modulo b.
Its nonzero phase is e_b(L_0 h a^(-1)), and it identifies the natural frequency length as R/(gM)=B_0/M, proving (2).

For coprime positive integers a,b, choose inverses a_bar modulo b and b_bar modulo a. The integer a a_bar+b b_bar is congruent to one modulo both a and b, so, because gcd(a,b)=1, it is congruent to one modulo ab. Hence
a_bar/b+b_bar/a congruent to 1/(ab) modulo 1.
Multiplying by L_0h and exponentiating gives
e_b(L_0h a_bar)=exp(2 pi i L_0h/(ab))e_a(-L_0h b_bar),
which is (1).

The definitions in each of the five cited consumers set the total inverse-product scale equal to Q_0 H_RS=B_0 and place h at H_RS with the prefactor H_RS^(-1). This proves (3). Dividing (3) by (2) gives (4). Neither the exact normalized identity nor the inequality on beta contains M/Q_0, so no comparison follows formally.

There is also a concrete exponent-scale family showing that the ratio can be a fixed power while all displayed scale inequalities remain compatible. Fix beta=6/5-2kappa and choose a constant c with
(1/16-kappa_0)/(beta-1)<c<1/2.
For a growing scale x put
D=M=x^(1/2), Q_0=x^c, g=D/Q_0, B_0=Q_0^beta, and R=gB_0.
Then DM=x, R/D=Q_0^(beta-1), and
R=x^(1/2+c(beta-1))>x^(9/16-kappa_0),
while M/Q_0=x^(1/2-c) tends to infinity as a fixed power. This is a scale-compatibility counterexample to deriving M asymp Q_0 from the stated scale hypotheses; it is not asserted to construct an individual integer Poisson atom.

For (5), on dyadic support a asymp Q_0 and b asymp B_0. The logarithmic derivative in h of the exponent in the archimedean factor has magnitude comparable to L_0h/(Q_0B_0). Substituting h asymp H_src gives L_0/(Q_0M). Since L_0=N/g, Q_0=D/g, and N asymp DM, this is bounded above and below by constants depending only on the dyadic support. Substituting h asymp H_RS gives L_0/Q_0^2, and the same relations make this comparable to M/Q_0. Thus a growing ratio produces a growing scaled derivative, outside the fixed uniformly smooth families required in the cited facts.

To prove (6), use
R/D=B_0/Q_0=Q_0^(beta-1).
The hypotheses D=x^(1/2+o(1)) and R>x^(9/16-kappa_0) give
Q_0^(beta-1)>x^(1/16-kappa_0+o(1)).
Since beta-1<=1/5-2kappa, taking logarithms yields (6). Also
L_0=N/g=(N/D)Q_0=x^(1/2+o(1))Q_0.
Because (6) bounds x by a fixed power of Q_0, this proves (7) for a fixed C_A.

Finally, reducing am+bk=L_0 modulo a gives L_0 congruent to bk modulo a. Since gcd(a,b)=1,
gcd(L_0,a)=gcd(k,a), which is unrestricted by the normalized identity. For example a=2,b=3,m=1,k=2 gives L_0=8 and gcd(a,b)=1 but gcd(L_0,a)=2. Hence the unit-numerator hypothesis of fact 664a92777dc5f5db is not automatic. The other cited fixed-target consumers explicitly do not require target-modulus coprimality, so their target-size slot is covered by (7), while their frequency and fixed-smooth-family slots still fail without extra input. This proves every stated scope conclusion.

glossary.B_0: The normalized marked-factor dyadic scale R/g in the forward orientation.
glossary.H_RS: The raised-stopping consumer frequency scale B_0/Q_0.
glossary.H_src: The natural literal Poisson frequency scale B_0/M after fixing the outer gcd.
glossary.L_0: The fixed normalized target N/g on an exact outer-gcd layer.
glossary.Q_0: The normalized reciprocal-modulus dyadic scale D/g in the forward orientation.

5db1ff60efd872b4.title: ENDPOINT-STRIP CLOSURE OF THE COMPLETE SOURCE-SPECIALIZED PMD L2 ROW
5db1ff60efd872b4.author: slava chan
5db1ff60efd872b4.statement:
ENDPOINT-STRIP CLOSURE OF THE COMPLETE SOURCE-SPECIALIZED PMD L2 ROW.

Fix constants C>=1, J>=3, and C_end>=1. Let Q>=8 and let real numbers H,V,P,B satisfy
  2<=H<=Q^(1/3),  2<=V<H,  P=QH/V,  B>=1,
  VQ^(1/3)<=C_end H.                                      (1)
Let A be a nonzero integer with |A|<=Q^C. Let cal L be a finite label set. For every outer row o=(ell,v,p), where ell belongs to cal L, V<=v<2V is an integer, p is prime in [P,2P), and gcd(v,p)=1, put n=vp. Let cal X_o be a finite set of triples x=(q,m,k) satisfying
  Q<=q,m<2Q,  qm+nk=A,  gcd(qm,n)=1.                       (2)
For h in an integer interval I_ell contained either in [H,2H) or in (-2H,-H], let a_{o,h}(x) be complex coefficients satisfying
  |a_{o,h}(x)|<=B.                                         (3)
For x=(q,m,k) put
  d_x=gcd(|A|,q), r_x=q/d_x, t_x=k/d_x,
  pi_{x,h}=c_{r_x}(h)/phi(r_x),
  eta_{x,h}=e_{r_x}(ht_x)-pi_{x,h}.                        (4)
Assume also the normalized principal-row factorization
  a_{o,h}(x)=alpha_{q,h}w_{q,h},
  |alpha_{q,h}|<=tau(r_x),
  |w_{q,h}|<=C_J(L_pr/H)(1+|h|/H)^(-J),
  L_pr<=BH,                                                 (5)
after zero extension outside the q-projection of cal X_o. Assume that B,C_J,#cal L are subpolynomial in Q.

Define
  M_2^src=sum_o sum_{h in I_ell}
    |sum_{x in cal X_o}a_{o,h}(x)e_{r_x}(ht_x)|^2.          (6)
Then for every epsilon>0,
  M_2^src<<_{C,J,C_end,epsilon}P Q^(5/3+epsilon).           (7)
Consequently, whenever this source row is the exact same-gauge literal finite-band row in the L2 contract of fact 294ac3b02b065aec, that fact gives
  |S_lit|^2<<_{C,J,C_end,epsilon}P Q^(8/3+epsilon).         (8)
This is a closure only of the displayed endpoint strip and the exact source-specialized row. It asserts no PMD estimate outside (1) and no Goldbach conclusion.
5db1ff60efd872b4.proof:
Fact c5f49ab9e8bd2c60 splits the row in (6) exactly as
  Y_{o,h}=P_{o,h}+N_{o,h},
where P_{o,h} is the principal Ramanujan aggregate and N_{o,h} is the same-gauge nonprincipal aggregate. It proves
  M_2^src<=2M_2^pr+2M_2^np                                (9)
and, under (5),
  M_2^pr<<_{C,J,epsilon}P Q^(5/3+epsilon).                 (10)

Expand M_2^np into q_1=q_2 and q_1 not equal to q_2. Fact 294ac3b02b065aec pays the q-diagonal at the target scale. Fact 1a9cfcfe3eedd5e2 splits the q-offdiagonal into equal exact rational phases and unequal exact rational phases. It proves
  |O_2^eq|<<_{C,J,epsilon}P Q^(5/3+epsilon).                (11)

For the unequal-phase term, fact 4b89ec4ce7a7b67a gives
  O_2^cross=Aadd+Rram,                                     (12)
where
  |Rram|<<_{C,J,epsilon}P Q^(5/3+epsilon)                  (13)
and Aadd is the exact uncentered additive crossed Gram with every coefficient in (3) retained. Fact 53d1025f57369596 gives
  |Aadd|<<_{C,epsilon}B^2(#cal L)Q^(3+epsilon).             (14)
The endpoint hypothesis in (1) gives
  Q^3=[VQ^(1/3)/H]P Q^(5/3)
      <=C_end P Q^(5/3).                                   (15)
Since B and #cal L are subpolynomial, apply (14) with a sufficiently small exponent budget and absorb those factors and C_end into the implicit constant. This yields
  |Aadd|<<_{C,C_end,epsilon}P Q^(5/3+epsilon).              (16)
Equations (12)-(16) pay O_2^cross. Together with the q-diagonal and (11), this proves
  M_2^np<<_{C,J,C_end,epsilon}P Q^(5/3+epsilon).            (17)
Insert (10) and (17) into (9) to prove (7).

Finally, fact 294ac3b02b065aec proves that its exact literal identification and the L2 estimate (7) imply (8). The source equation, reduced phase, coefficient bounds, factorization, masks, and scale assumptions in the present statement are exactly the source-specialized hypotheses used in the cited chain. No statement outside the endpoint condition is used. This proves all assertions.

glossary.Cend: A fixed positive constant bounding the endpoint ratio V Q^(1/3)/H.

5dec521df02ef076.title: PRIME-rho UNIT-RAY NONCONSTANT-MODE PAYMENT AND REDUCTION TO ONE COMPLETE U_lambda AGGREGATE
5dec521df02ef076.author: slava chan
5dec521df02ef076.statement:
PRIME-rho UNIT-RAY NONCONSTANT-MODE PAYMENT AND REDUCTION TO ONE COMPLETE U_lambda AGGREGATE.

Adopt UNIT-RAY-RAM-SPEC from fact eb589e60e7e30a33 on a family of exact copies in one block
Dcal<=d_lambda<2Dcal.
Assume every copy in the family has
rho_lambda=p_lambda prime,
p_lambda>L,
p_lambda>=P_0                                                     (1)
for a positive real P_0. Put
S_lambda
 =sum_{supported (epsilon,b)}
   A_lambda(epsilon,b)U_lambda(epsilon,b).                         (2)
Then the exact prime-rho hard unit-ray form is
sum_lambda Q_lambda^{unit}
 =sum_lambda|S_lambda|^2-E_unit,                                   (3)
where
0<=E_unit
 =sum_lambda sum_{z (mod p_lambda)}|C_lambda(z)|^2
 <=(1+4F/P_0)
   sum_lambda sum_{supported (epsilon,b)}
   |B_lambda(epsilon,1,b)|^2                                      (4)
and
E_unit
 <=x^{o(1)}(1+4F/P_0)|omega_F|^2 BQF.                            (5)

Consequently, on the chamber
Dcal(1+4F/P_0)<=QF,                                                (6)
the complete nonconstant residue contribution E_unit is at most
x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 BQ^2F^2/Dcal.                                (7)
On this chamber, the sole remaining sufficient unit-ray prime-rho supplier is
sum_lambda|S_lambda|^2
 <=x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 BQ^2F^2/Dcal.                              (PRIME-rho-CONST-U)
Estimate PRIME-rho-CONST-U is not asserted. If it holds, equations (3) and (7) give the canonical bound for the whole prime-rho unit-ray family.

In particular, if P_0>4F and
2Dcal<=QF,                                                         (8)
then (6) holds. Thus on (8) every nonconstant residue mode is already paid and the only unresolved mode is the complete signed ray/copy aggregate (2).

This theorem retains every exact U_lambda transform and literal ray mask. It proves the nonconstant-mode payment and reduction only, not PRIME-rho-CONST-U, no complete unit-ray estimate outside the displayed chamber, no P-qSRC-SUP, no tail payment, and no Goldbach conclusion.
5dec521df02ef076.proof:
Fact eb589e60e7e30a33 proves for every prime-rho copy that
Q_lambda^{unit}
 =|S_lambda|^2
  -sum_{z (mod p_lambda)}|C_lambda(z)|^2.
Summing this identity gives (3) and the definition and nonnegativity of E_unit.

A supported unit ray has signed numerator m=epsilon b with
0<|m|<2F,
because the exact frequency support is F<=|h|<2F and h=epsilon k b with k>=1. In any fixed residue class modulo p_lambda, an interval of signed integers of total length less than 4F contains at most
1+4F/p_lambda
such values. Therefore each residue aggregate in fact eb589e60e7e30a33 contains at most that many ray coefficients. Cauchy inside each residue class gives
sum_z|C_lambda(z)|^2
 <=(1+4F/p_lambda)
   sum_{supported (epsilon,b)}|B_lambda(epsilon,1,b)|^2.           (9)
Use p_lambda>=P_0 and sum over lambda to prove (4).

Fact 7e9251670db3e1c9 proves that B_lambda(R) is the complete coefficient on one primitive ray and that the Delta=0 sector after ray compression is
sum_lambda sum_R|B_lambda(R)|^2.
The unit rays are a subfamily of this nonnegative sum. Fact e55b27d39c593164 bounds the complete Delta=0 sector by
x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2BQF.
Combining this bound with (4) proves (5).

Under (6),
(1+4F/P_0)BQF
 <=BQ^2F^2/Dcal.
This proves (7). Apply the triangle inequality to (3); if PRIME-rho-CONST-U also holds, the two terms are each at the canonical scale, proving the asserted sufficient implication.

If P_0>4F, then 1+4F/P_0<2. Under (8),
Dcal(1+4F/P_0)<2Dcal<=QF,
so (6) follows. No complete U_lambda coefficient was altered in these comparisons, and all exclusions follow.

glossary.E_unit: The nonconstant residue energy sum_z|C_lambda(z)|^2 over the prime-rho unit-ray copies.
glossary.PRIME-rho-CONST-U: The remaining complete signed U_lambda aggregate supplier after nonconstant prime-rho modes are paid.

5e021455b7c48b01.title: EXACT GRAM-SUBTRACTED NORMAL FORM FOR TWO PRIME RECIPROCAL-FRAME ROWS
5e021455b7c48b01.author: slava chan
5e021455b7c48b01.statement:
EXACT GRAM-SUBTRACTED NORMAL FORM FOR TWO PRIME RECIPROCAL-FRAME ROWS.

Let p>3 be a prime. For nonzero residues C,a modulo p define
 r_C(a)=e_p(Ca^(-1))+1/(p-1).                              (1)
For a residue H modulo p and nonzero a define
 rho_p(H;a)=
  e_p(Ha^(-1))+1/(p-1), if H is nonzero,
  0,                    if H is zero.                      (2)
For nonzero residues A,D define the normalized complete Gram
 G_p(A,D)
  =1/(p-1) sum_{x modulo p;x nonzero}r_A(x)overline(r_D(x))
  =p/(p-1){1_{A=D}-1/(p-1)}.                              (3)
Then, for every nonzero a,
 r_A(a)overline(r_D(a))-G_p(A,D)
 =
 1_{A!=D}rho_p(A-D;a)
 +1/(p-1)rho_p(A;a)
 +1/(p-1)rho_p(-D;a).                                     (4)
Moreover, for every residue H modulo p,
 sum_{a modulo p;a nonzero}rho_p(H;a)=0.                   (5)

Consequently, after exact Gram subtraction, the only coefficient-one local response in (4), even after coincident modes are collected, is the off-local-diagonal inverse-difference mode rho_p(A-D;a), and it is absent when A=D. Both displayed centered single-index summands carry the coefficient 1/(p-1); if they coincide, their combined coefficient is 2/(p-1)<1. This is an exact local algebraic normal form. No aggregate estimate for a complementary tensor or cutoff boundary, no ROP estimate, no CEN-MZB estimate, no C_small estimate and no Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
5e021455b7c48b01.proof:
Put c=1/(p-1). Equation (3) is the Gram identity of fact 0d1daae6c3854186, which applies because p>3 implies p>2.

Suppose first that A is not equal to D. Then A-D is nonzero and (3) gives
 G_p(A,D)=-p/(p-1)^2=-c-c^2.
Direct expansion gives
 r_A(a)overline(r_D(a))
 =e_p((A-D)a^(-1))
  +c e_p(Aa^(-1))+c e_p(-Da^(-1))+c^2.
Subtracting the Gram therefore gives
 e_p((A-D)a^(-1))+c
 +c{e_p(Aa^(-1))+c}
 +c{e_p(-Da^(-1))+c},
which is the right side of (4).

Suppose now that A=D. The first term on the right side of (4) is zero by definition. Equation (3) gives
 G_p(A,A)=p/(p-1)(1-c)=1-c^2.
On the other hand,
 |r_A(a)|^2
 =1+c e_p(Aa^(-1))+c e_p(-Aa^(-1))+c^2.
Subtracting 1-c^2 leaves
 c{e_p(Aa^(-1))+c}+c{e_p(-Aa^(-1))+c},
which is again the right side of (4).

If H=0, equation (5) follows from the zero definition in (2). If H is nonzero, inversion permutes the nonzero residues modulo p and
 sum_{a nonzero}e_p(Ha^(-1))=-1.
Adding (p-1)c=1 proves (5).

In (4) the difference summand has coefficient one. Each single-index summand has coefficient c<1. If their modes coincide, their combined coefficient is 2c<1 because p>3. A single-index mode can also coincide with the difference mode only if D=0 or A=0, respectively, which the hypotheses exclude. This proves the final coefficient assertion.

glossary.G_p(A,D): the normalized complete-unit Gram of the reciprocal-frame rows indexed by A and D
glossary.rho_p(H;a): the centered inverse additive character at nonzero local frequency H, extended to be zero at H=0

5f60a4633e6b0b70.title: Let m>1 be an odd integer and let U_cut>=2 be an integer. Define the nonnegative residue weight
5f60a4633e6b0b70.author: slava chan
5f60a4633e6b0b70.statement:
Let m>1 be an odd integer and let U_cut>=2 be an integer. Define the nonnegative residue weight
W_{U,m}(nu)=#{u in Z:0<|u|<U_cut and u=nu modulo m}.                  (1)
Its additive Fourier transform is
W_hat_{U,m}(ell)=sum_{nu modulo m}W_{U,m}(nu)e_m(-ell nu)
                =sum_{0<|u|<U_cut}e_m(-ell u).                        (2)
Then
W_hat_{U,m}(0)=2(U_cut-1)                                             (3)
and
sum_{ell modulo m}|W_hat_{U,m}(ell)|
 <=2(U_cut-1)+4m(1+log m).                                            (4)

Now let s belong to {1,-1}, let K be coprime to m, and on the unit group modulo m^2 form the weighted digit product matrix
M_{U,m}(a,b)=sum_{nu modulo m}W_{U,m}(nu)
 Delta_{m^2}(ab-K-2smnu).
Let P_{U,m} be its projective ell^2 tensor norm as in fact 308b3f12b1d814db. Then
P_{U,m}=phi(m)sum_ell|W_hat_{U,m}(ell)|                               (5)
and consequently
P_{U,m}/phi(m^2)
 <=2(U_cut-1)/m+4(1+log m).                                           (6)

In the normalized coefficient family of fact d90ec957015b32b5, put
X=ceil(LH^3) and U_cut=2X. Every recovered normal coordinate u obeys 0<|u|<U_cut. Hence the coarse literal Archimedean u-range induces exactly the weight (1). For every fixed delta in (0,3), on the remaining range
H^(3-delta)<m<=2X
one has
P_{2X,m}/phi(m^2) <<_L H^delta+log(2H).                               (7)
On the top subrange m>=cH^3 for a fixed c>0, this sharpens to
P_{2X,m}/phi(m^2) <<_{L,c} log(2H).                                   (8)

These are digit-axis projective costs relative to the natural dense unit-pair scale phi(m^2). They pay only the unavoidable integer range of u. They do not assert that the full literal normalized-family coefficient factors through W_{U,m}; prime quotients, the second product relation, exact gcd, signs, boxes in the other variables, coupling, masks, and source weights can change the projective norm. In particular, (7) is not by itself a Bettin--Chandee Pi_BC estimate or a cancellation theorem.
5f60a4633e6b0b70.proof:
Identity (2) follows by interchanging the finite residue sum with the finite set of integers in (1). At ell=0 there are exactly 2(U_cut-1) integers with 0<|u|<U_cut, proving (3).

Fix a nonzero ell modulo m and put d_ell=min(ell,m-ell), using the representative ell in {1,...,m-1}. The negative-u sum is the complex conjugate, up to replacing ell by -ell, of the positive-u sum, so
|W_hat_{U,m}(ell)|
 <=2|sum_{u=1}^{U_cut-1}e_m(-ell u)|.                                 (9)
Write U_cut-1=qm+r with 0<=r<m. Since ell is nonzero, every complete block of m consecutive residues has exponential sum zero. Thus the sum on the right of (9) is a geometric sum of at most r terms. The geometric-series formula gives
|sum_{u=1}^{r}e_m(-ell u)|
 <=min(r,1/|sin(pi ell/m)|).
For 1<=d_ell<=m/2, the inequality sin x>=2x/pi on [0,pi/2] gives
|sin(pi ell/m)|=sin(pi d_ell/m)>=2d_ell/m.
Therefore
|W_hat_{U,m}(ell)|<=min(2m,m/d_ell)<=m/d_ell times an absolute factor two; retaining a generous bound gives
|W_hat_{U,m}(ell)|<=2m/d_ell.                                         (10)
There are at most two ell with each value of d_ell. Summing (10) and using
sum_{d=1}^{floor(m/2)}1/d<=1+log m
gives
sum_{ell nonzero}|W_hat_{U,m}(ell)|<=4m(1+log m).
Adding (3) proves (4).

Fact 308b3f12b1d814db applies to the weight W_{U,m} and gives the equality (5). Since phi(m^2)=m phi(m), division of (4) by m proves (6).

In the proof of fact d90ec957015b32b5, every normalized state in the X-box has a nonzero recovered integer u with |u|<2X. Thus the exact coarse integer-range multiplicity after reducing u modulo m is (1) with U_cut=2X. If m>H^(3-delta), then
X/m<=ceil(LH^3)/H^(3-delta)<<_L H^delta.
Also m<=2X<<_LH^3 implies log m<<_Llog(2H). Substitution in (6) proves (7). If m>=cH^3, then X/m<<_{L,c}1, proving (8). The final limitations follow because (5) uses only the modular product selector and the range weight; none of the additional literal selectors was included in its convolution matrix.

glossary.P_{U,m}: the projective ell^2 tensor norm of the corresponding weighted digit product selector
glossary.U_cut: the positive integer Archimedean cutoff for the normal coordinate
glossary.W_{U,m}: the residue multiplicity weight induced by the integer interval 0<|u|<U

5fbdbbebf99aec55.title: LARGE TARGET-GCD ABSOLUTE TAIL FOR INTERVAL-PRIME TRACES. Fix integers J,C_A,K>=1, C>=1, and a constant C_omega>=1. Let Q>=2 and let 1<=B<=Q^K and 0<H_P<=Q^K. Fix a nonzero integer L_src with |L_src|<=Q^{C_A}, let C_0>=1, and let C_large be any set of divisors c of L_src with c>=C_0. For each c choose 1<=U_c,Y_c<=Q^K with U_cY_c<=CB. For every dyadic F>=1 choose coefficients d_{c,q},nu_{c,F}(h),alpha_{c,F}(u),gamma_{c,F}(p), a scalar omega_{c,F}, and an amplitude Psi_{c,F}, satisfying |d_{c,q}|<=1, |nu_{c,F}(h)|<=tau_J(|h|), |alpha_{c,F}(u)|<=tau_J(u), |gamma_{c,F}(p)|<=1, |Psi_{c,F}|<=1, and |omega_{c,F}|<=C_omega min(1,(F/H_P)^{-(J+4)}). Support q on Q/c<=q<2Q/c, h on F<=|h|<2F, u on U_c<=u<2U_c, and p on any subset of Y_c<=p<2Y_c. Let zeta_{c,q,h,u,p} have modulus at most one. Define
5fbdbbebf99aec55.author: slava chan
5fbdbbebf99aec55.statement:
LARGE TARGET-GCD ABSOLUTE TAIL FOR INTERVAL-PRIME TRACES. Fix integers J,C_A,K>=1, C>=1, and a constant C_omega>=1. Let Q>=2 and let 1<=B<=Q^K and 0<H_P<=Q^K. Fix a nonzero integer L_src with |L_src|<=Q^{C_A}, let C_0>=1, and let C_large be any set of divisors c of L_src with c>=C_0. For each c choose 1<=U_c,Y_c<=Q^K with U_cY_c<=CB. For every dyadic F>=1 choose coefficients d_{c,q},nu_{c,F}(h),alpha_{c,F}(u),gamma_{c,F}(p), a scalar omega_{c,F}, and an amplitude Psi_{c,F}, satisfying |d_{c,q}|<=1, |nu_{c,F}(h)|<=tau_J(|h|), |alpha_{c,F}(u)|<=tau_J(u), |gamma_{c,F}(p)|<=1, |Psi_{c,F}|<=1, and |omega_{c,F}|<=C_omega min(1,(F/H_P)^{-(J+4)}). Support q on Q/c<=q<2Q/c, h on F<=|h|<2F, u on U_c<=u<2U_c, and p on any subset of Y_c<=p<2Y_c. Let zeta_{c,q,h,u,p} have modulus at most one. Define
T_c=H_P^{-1}sum_{F dyadic,F>=1}omega_{c,F}sum_q d_{c,q}sum_h nu_{c,F}(h)sum_u alpha_{c,F}(u)sum_p gamma_{c,F}(p)Psi_{c,F}(q,h,u,p)zeta_{c,q,h,u,p}.
Then for every epsilon>0,
sum_{c in C_large}|T_c| <<_{epsilon,J,C,C_A,K,C_omega} QBQ^epsilon/C_0.
In particular, if B=QH_T and C_0=H_TQ^xi, the tail is O(Q^{2-xi+epsilon}). Arbitrary deletion conditions, prime restrictions, phases, gcd selectors, and bounded smooth masks are permitted.
5fbdbbebf99aec55.proof:
We use the elementary divisor-average estimate
sum_{n<=X}tau_J(n)<<_J X(1+log(2X))^{J-1}.
It follows by writing tau_J(n) as the number of ordered J-tuples with product n, summing the last coordinate, and inducting with the harmonic sum. The same estimate holds for any dyadic interval.
Fix c,F and put u_F=F/H_P. The q- and p-sums have at most O(Q/c) and O(Y_c) terms. The divisor-average estimate bounds the h- and u-sums by
O_J(F(1+log(2F))^{J-1}) and O_J(U_c(log Q)^{J-1}),
using U_c<=Q^K. Therefore the F-block is
<< (QB/c)u_F |omega_{c,F}| (log Q)^{J-1}(1+log(2F))^{J-1}.
If u_F<=1, then F<=H_P<=Q^K, so log(2F)<<_K log Q and the dyadic sum of u_F is O(1). If u_F>1, write log(2F)<=log(2H_P)+log(2u_F)<<_K log Q+log(2u_F). The decay u_F^{-(J+4)} makes the dyadic sum of
u_F^{-(J+3)}(log Q+log(2u_F))^{J-1}
O_J((log Q)^{J-1}). Hence
|T_c|<<_{J,K,C_omega}(QB/c)(log Q)^{2J-2}.
Summing c gives sum_{c in C_large}1/c<=tau(|L_src|)/C_0<<Q^epsilon/C_0. The fixed logarithmic power is absorbed by decreasing epsilon. This proves the first bound. If B=QH_T and C_0=H_TQ^xi, then QB/C_0=Q^{2-xi}. Optional restrictions only reduce the absolute sum.

glossary.C_0: The lower cutoff for the large target gcd.
glossary.C_large: The selected large exact target-gcd divisor layers.
glossary.zeta_{c,q,h,u,p}: An arbitrary phase or deletion factor of modulus at most one.

5fc5975b76bffe88.title: MINIMAL FIXED-MARGIN BALANCED-\(G\), LARGE-CROSS-\(y\)-CONDUCTOR TOP-\(B\) VECTOR SUPPLIER. Fix constants
5fc5975b76bffe88.author: slava chan
5fc5975b76bffe88.statement:
MINIMAL FIXED-MARGIN BALANCED-\(G\), LARGE-CROSS-\(y\)-CONDUCTOR TOP-\(B\) VECTOR SUPPLIER. Fix constants
\[
 0<\tau\le1/10,\qquad \eta_0>0,\qquad \gamma_0>0,\qquad A_0\ge0.
\]
Use one recombined singleton top-\(B\) fibre of fact
\(d63101722d12c88c\), with
\[
 B=Q^\beta,\quad U\le u<2U,\quad Y\le y<2Y,\quad UY\asymp B,
\]
\[
 Q\le q<2Q,\quad F\le|h|<2F,
\]
nonzero target \(\mathscr A\), and \(G=H_T/H_P\). Restrict to
\[
 \beta>{6\over5}-{2\tau\over5}+{2\eta_0\over5},               \tag{1}
\]
\[
 {\log U\over\log Q}\ge3-2\beta-\tau+\eta_0,\qquad
 {\log Y\over\log Q}\ge3-2\beta-\tau+\eta_0,                  \tag{2}
\]
\[
 Q^{-\gamma_0}<G<Q^{\gamma_0}.                                \tag{3}
\]
For every supported coordinate define
\[
 \widehat c_y^{\rm rec}(u,q,h)
 =
 c_k^{\rm rec}(u,y;q,h)
 e\!\left(-{\mathscr A h\over quy}\right)
 e_u\!\left(\mathscr A h(qy)^{-1}\right).                     \tag{4}
\]
For an ordered pair put
\[
 \Omega=h_1q_2u_2-h_2q_1u_1,\qquad
 r_y={y\over(y,\mathscr A\Omega)}\quad(\Omega\ne0),
\]
and \(L_0=(\log(2Q))^{A_0}\). Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
 V_{\rm deep}
 =
 \sum_y\sum_{u_1,u_2}\sum_{q_1,h_1,q_2,h_2}
 &1_{\Omega\ne0}1_{r_y>L_0}
 \widehat c_y^{\rm rec}(u_1,q_1,h_1)
 \overline{\widehat c_y^{\rm rec}(u_2,q_2,h_2)}\\
 &\times e_y\!\left(
 \mathscr A\Omega(q_1q_2u_1u_2)^{-1}\right).                  \tag{5}
\end{aligned}
\]
Then exactly
\[
 V_{\rm rec}^{(\mathrm{NR})}
 =
 V_{\rm rec}^{(\mathrm{near\text{-}FR},A_0)}+V_{\rm deep},     \tag{6}
\]
where fact \(1feb8a751976e771\) bounds the first term. Consequently
\[
 \boxed{
 |V_{\rm deep}|
 \ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon
 (UBQF+U^2Q^2F^2)
 }                                                             \tag{TOP-B-BALG-DEEP-NR-SPEC}
\]
would imply
\[
 |V_{\rm rec}^{(\mathrm{NR})}|
 \ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon(UBQF+U^2Q^2F^2)                \tag{7}
\]
and then
\[
 |\mathcal T_{B,F}(U,Y)|
 \ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon
 \left(B\sqrt{Q/H_P}+{BQ\over\sqrt Y}\right).                 \tag{8}
\]

Formula (5) retains both inverse-\(y\) phases modulo \(u_1,u_2\) inside
(4), the inverse-\(u_i\) difference phase modulo \(y\), and every literal
singleton coefficient and selector. Only the accepted sector
\(1<r_y\le L_0\) is removed.

Fact \(bf0b2dfc2f3a23ad\) power-saves exact scalar \(f7b5\)-fibres
outside (3) when their two factor exponents have a fixed endpoint margin.
Conditions (1)-(2) provide that margin. Hence, after a separate
verifier-accepted source-to-\(f7b5\) insertion that preserves at least
this \(\eta_0\) margin, new fixed-margin endpoint-diagonal vector work
may be restricted to (3) and (5). This theorem neither supplies that
insertion nor proves TOP-B-BALG-DEEP-NR-SPEC.
5fc5975b76bffe88.proof:
For \(\Omega\ne0\), the nonresonant condition is
\[
 y\nmid\mathscr A\Omega\Longleftrightarrow r_y>1.
\]
The disjoint alternatives \(1<r_y\le L_0\) and \(r_y>L_0\) therefore
partition the exact nonresonant expansion. The first is precisely the
sector of fact 1feb8a751976e771 and the second is (5), proving (6).
That fact gives
\[
 |V_{\rm rec}^{(\mathrm{near\text{-}FR},A_0)}|
 \ll Q^\varepsilon U^2Q^2F^2.
\]
Adding this to TOP-B-BALG-DEEP-NR-SPEC proves (7).

Fact d63101722d12c88c gives on the same singleton coefficient
\[
 |V_{\rm rec}^{(0)}|\ll Q^\varepsilon BQF,\qquad
 |V_{\rm rec}^{(\mathrm{FR})}|
 \ll Q^\varepsilon U^2Q^2F^2.
\]
Together with \(UY\asymp B\), the algebra of fact
61cf02eb05b38a54 converts these bounds and (7) into
\[
 V_{\rm rec}\ll Q^\varepsilon U
 \left(BQF+{BQ^2F^2\over Y}\right).
\]
Fact 66a8c3bb4822f841 then proves (8).

The exact CRT identity is
\[
 e_q(-\mathscr A h(uy)^{-1})
 =
 e(-\mathscr A h/(quy))
 e_u(\mathscr A h(qy)^{-1})
 e_y(\mathscr A h(qu)^{-1}).
\]
The first two factors are exactly (4). Multiplication of two final
\(y\)-phases produces the phase in (5), proving that both inverse
dependencies and every coefficient remain literal.

Finally set
\[
 s={\log U\over\log Q},\qquad t={\log Y\over\log Q}.
\]
Condition (2) says both factor exponents exceed
\(3-2\beta-\tau\) by the fixed margin \(\eta_0\); (1) is the corresponding
nonempty-band condition. Thus, if a separate source insertion identifies
the literal fibre with the scalar interface while preserving this
margin, every hypothesis of bf0b2dfc2f3a23ad is present. That fact removes
\(G\ge Q^{\gamma_0}\) and \(G\le Q^{-\gamma_0}\), leaving (3). No such
insertion is inferred here.

glossary.TOP-B-BALG-DEEP-NR-SPEC: The fixed-margin endpoint-diagonal, balanced-G, polylog-large cross-y conductor specified-spectrum supplier for the recombined pre-Cauchy energy.
glossary.V_deep: The exact recombined nonresonant energy after deleting only the accepted polylogarithmic cross-y near-resonance sector.

60b26a9b6f79467a.title: Fix real numbers 1/2<a<b<1 and 0<σ<1/100. Let W be a nonzero nonnegative smooth function supported in [a,b]. Let ψ be smooth with 0≤ψ≤1, ψ(t)=0 for 0<t≤1, and ψ(t)=1 for t≥2. Let Φ be a nonnegative smooth function supported in [1/2,2] such that Σ_{j∈Z}Φ(t/2^j)=1 for t>0. Fix B_src>0 and c_dir>0. For x≥3 put
60b26a9b6f79467a.author: slava chan
60b26a9b6f79467a.statement:
Fix real numbers 1/2<a<b<1 and 0<σ<1/100. Let W be a nonzero nonnegative smooth function supported in [a,b]. Let ψ be smooth with 0≤ψ≤1, ψ(t)=0 for 0<t≤1, and ψ(t)=1 for t≥2. Let Φ be a nonnegative smooth function supported in [1/2,2] such that Σ_{j∈Z}Φ(t/2^j)=1 for t>0. Fix B_src>0 and c_dir>0. For x≥3 put
N=2x,  D_*=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B_src),
C_2=∏_{p>2}p(p-2)/(p-1)²,
𝔠(N)=C_2∏_{p|N,p>2}(p-1)/(p-2).                            (1)

Suppose x tends to infinity through values for which N is an even integer not representable as a sum of two primes, and for each x there are dyadic D,M,U satisfying
D_*/2<D≤2x^(1/2),                                             (2)
ax/4≤DM≤4bx,  (2-b)x/2≤U≤2(2-a)x.                            (3)
Define the genuine-prime block
P_N=Σ_{dm+p=N,p prime}μ(d)log(m)log(p)W(dm/x)ψ(d/D_*)
 Φ(d/D)Φ(m/M)Φ(p/U),                                         (4)
and assume
P_N≤-c_dir𝔠(N)x/log x.                                        (5)
Define
B_N=Σ_{dm+q=N}μ(d)log(m)W(dm/x)ψ(d/D_*)Λ(q)
 Φ(d/D)Φ(m/M)Φ(q/U),                                         (6)
PP_N=B_N-P_N,                                                 (7)
and, for dyadic R,K,
Q_N(R,K)=Σ_{dm+rk=N}μ(d)μ(r)log(m)log(k)W(dm/x)ψ(d/D_*)
 Φ(d/D)Φ(m/M)Φ(rk/U)Φ(r/R)Φ(k/K).                            (8)

Call an active label (R,K) controlled if at least one of the following holds:
R/M≤x^(-σ);
R≤D, D^19R^14≤x^(17-σ), D^8R^7≤x^(8-σ);
R>D, D^14R^19≤x^(17-σ), D^7R^8≤x^(8-σ).                     (9)
Let C_dir,N be the sum of Q_N(R,K) over controlled labels. For every residual active label, use the Poisson decomposition of fact df9748efe29ab475,
Q_N(R,K)=Q_N^(0)(R,K)+Q_N^(≠0)(R,K),
and define
Z_res,N^(0)=Σ_{residual (R,K)}Q_N^(0)(R,K),
R_res,N^(≠0)=Σ_{residual (R,K)}Q_N^(≠0)(R,K).                (10)
Assume the verified hybrid identities and estimates
P_N=C_dir,N+Z_res,N^(0)+R_res,N^(≠0)-PP_N,                   (11)
C_dir,N=o(x/log x),  Z_res,N^(0)=o(x/log x),
PP_N=o(x/log x).                                             (12)

Put κ_0=1/200 and split
R_low,N=Σ_{residual (R,K), R≤x^(9/16-κ_0)}Q_N^(≠0)(R,K),
R_high,N=Σ_{residual (R,K), R>x^(9/16-κ_0)}Q_N^(≠0)(R,K).    (13)
Then
R_low,N=o(x/log x),                                          (14)
R_high,N≤-c_dir𝔠(N)x/log x+o(𝔠(N)x/log x).                  (15)
Thus the top-log negative nonzero-frequency anomaly is forced beyond the buffered exponent 9/16. No absolute bound for R_high,N, no estimate at the exact endpoint 9/16, and no terminal-anatomy identification are asserted. Facts 1e2d635f6691e832 and f41f5f91b52e0d13 supply hypotheses (5), (11)-(12), and 𝔠(N)≥C_2>0 for their forced top-log block.
60b26a9b6f79467a.proof:
From (2),
D=x^(1/2+o(1)).
Equation (3) then gives
M=x^(1/2+o(1)).                                                (16)
Fix the balance parameter η supplied by fact efb6934a518932be for κ=κ_0 and for the uniformly bounded scaled-smooth family generated by W,ψ,Φ in (8). Then
x^(1/2-η)≤D,M≤x^(1/2+η)                                      (17)
for sufficiently large x.

Write δ_D=log D/log x, ν=log M/log x, and ρ=log R/log x. Thus δ_D=ν=1/2+o(1). From the definition (9), a label with R≤D is residual only if
ρ>max(ν-σ,min((17-σ-19δ_D)/14,(8-σ-8δ_D)/7)).
In particular,
ρ>(17-σ-19δ_D)/14=(15/2-σ)/14+o(1)>1/2+c_σ               (18)
for some c_σ>0. But R≤D gives ρ≤δ_D=1/2+o(1), contradicting (18). Hence every residual label has R>D.

For R>D, residuality in (9) requires
ρ>max(ν-σ,min((17-σ-14δ_D)/19,(8-σ-7δ_D)/8)).
At δ_D=ν=1/2+o(1), the smaller of the two displayed Bettin--Chandee boundaries is the first, and it exceeds the Fourier-tail boundary. Therefore
ρ>(10-σ)/19+o(1).                                             (19)
Since
(10-σ)/19-1/2=(1-2σ)/38>0.025
and κ_0=0.005, (19) implies
R≥x^(1/2+κ_0)                                                 (20)
for sufficiently large x.

Every label in R_low,N now satisfies (17), (20), and
R≤x^(9/16-κ_0).
Fact efb6934a518932be applies to its entire nonzero Poisson piece and supplies a fixed δ_0>0 such that
Q_N^(≠0)(R,K)=O(x^(1-δ_0)).
There are O((log x)²) active dyadic labels, hence
R_low,N=O(x^(1-δ_0/2))=o(x/log x),                           (21)
which proves (14).

Equations (5), (11), and (12) give
R_res,N^(≠0)
≤-c_dir𝔠(N)x/log x+o(x/log x).                               (22)
By fact f41f5f91b52e0d13, 𝔠(N)≥C_2>0, so the error in (22) is
o(𝔠(N)x/log x). The two sums in (13) partition the residual labels exactly:
R_res,N^(≠0)=R_low,N+R_high,N.
Subtract (14) from (22), again using 𝔠(N)≥C_2, to obtain (15).

glossary.B_N: The sibling-complete von Mangoldt block in (6).
glossary.C_dir,N: The aggregate of controlled labels defined by (9).
glossary.R_low,N: The residual nonzero aggregate with R≤x^(9/16-κ_0).
glossary.δ_0: The power-saving exponent supplied by fact efb6934a518932be.

60ec98d195b61bc1.title: EXACT CENTERED CRT-FACE EXPANSION OF A SQUAREFREE NONRESONANT INVERSE KERNEL
60ec98d195b61bc1.author: slava chan
60ec98d195b61bc1.proof:
For a prime (pmid r), inversion permutes (mathbb F_p^	imes). Therefore
[
 sum_{xinmathbb F_p}f_p(x)
 =sum_{yinmathbb F_p^	imes}e_p(A_py)=-1,
]
because (A_p
e0). Hence the normalized mean of (f_p) is (-1/p), and (2) follows from the definition of (arphi_p).

The CRT additive-character identity for squarefree (r) is
[
 e_r(z)=prod_{pmid r}e_p(zr_p^{-1}).
]
If ((q,r)=1), apply this with (z=Aq^{-1}). The (p)-factor is
[
 e_p(Ar_p^{-1}q^{-1})=f_p(q).
]
If ((q,r)>1), at least one prime coordinate of (q) is zero and both
({ f1}_{(q,r)=1}) and the corresponding product of the zero-extended (f_p)'s vanish. Thus
[
 { f1}_{(q,r)=1}e_r(Aq^{-1})=prod_{pmid r}f_p(q).
]
Since (f_p=-1/p+arphi_p), this proves (3), and multiplication gives (4). For (S=arnothing), the coefficient is
[
 prod_{pmid r}(-1/p)=(-1)^{omega(r)}/r=mu(r)/r,
]
proving (5).

Fix a nonempty (S) and (pin S). The face factors as
(arphi_p(q)) times a function independent of the (p)-coordinate. Summing completely over that coordinate gives zero by (2). Fourier transformation on the CRT product group is a tensor product. The constant (-1/p) has only zero dual frequency, while the centered (arphi_p) has zero coefficient at zero. This proves the Fourier-support assertion.

For the source specialization, (d) is squarefree by fact (41b56ed8e64bdba6). Hence
[
 d_0=d/(d,mathscr ADelta)
]
is squarefree, and every prime of (d_0) does not divide (mathscr ADelta), proving the coprimality. In the (d)-phase
[
 e_d(mathscr ADelta(q_1q_2v)^{-1}),
]
the CRT factors at primes dividing ((d,mathscr ADelta)) equal one. The product over the remaining primes is an inverse kernel modulo (d_0) with a parameter equal to (mathscr ADelta) times CRT idempotents and the unit ((q_1q_2v)^{-1}). Reassigning the fixed CRT idempotents prime by prime is exactly the definition of the (A_p) in (1). Thus (3)-(5) apply and the all-zero face has magnitude (d_0^{-1}). Equation (2) is a complete residue identity only, so it does not annihilate an incomplete source-weighted row; this proves the scope statement.
