61cf02eb05b38a54.title: TOP-B-PRECAUCHY-CROSSU-DFR. Use one block and the notation of TOP-B-PRECAUCHY-TRACE-RED, fact 66a8c3bb4822f841. In particular,
61cf02eb05b38a54.author: slava chan
61cf02eb05b38a54.statement:
TOP-B-PRECAUCHY-CROSSU-DFR. Use one block and the notation of TOP-B-PRECAUCHY-TRACE-RED, fact 66a8c3bb4822f841. In particular,
\[
 U\le u<2U,\qquad Y\le y<2Y,\qquad
 C_B^{-1}B\le UY\le C_BB,
\]
\[
 Q\le q<2Q,\qquad F\le |h|<2F,
\]
and every supported top-\(B\) stopping copy has \(n=uy\), \((u,y)=1\), and \((q,uy)=1\). Thus \((q,u)=(q,y)=1\). Assume that \(B,U,Y,F\) and the nonzero integer target \(\mathscr A\) are at most \(Q^{C_0}\), for one fixed \(C_0\), and impose the literal divisor/copy envelope
\[
 |c_\lambda(q,h)|\le
 \tau_J(uyqh)(\log(2Q))^C,\qquad
 \#\Lambda(u,y)\le\tau_J(uy) \tag{1}
\]
for fixed \(J,C\). Every source, marker, Möbius, Fourier, target-gcd, fixed-\(U\), parent, sign, order/equal-cell, collision, deletion, coprimality and provenance mask is retained in the zero-extended coefficient \(c_\lambda(q,h)\).

For every supported coordinate, CRT reciprocity gives
\[
 e_q\!\left(-\mathscr A h(uy)^{-1}\right)
 =
 e\!\left(-{\mathscr A h\over quy}\right)
 e_u\!\left(\mathscr A h(qy)^{-1}\right)
 e_y\!\left(\mathscr A h(qu)^{-1}\right). \tag{2}
\]
Put
\[
 \widehat c_{\lambda,y}(u,q,h)
 :=
 c_\lambda(q,h)
 e\!\left(-{\mathscr A h\over quy}\right)
 e_u\!\left(\mathscr A h(qy)^{-1}\right). \tag{3}
\]
Then the pre-Cauchy energy \(V=\sum_y|G_y|^2\) of fact 66a8c3bb4822f841 has the exact expansion
\[
 V=
 \sum_y\sum_{u_1,u_2}\sum_{q_1,h_1,q_2,h_2}
 \sum_{\lambda_i\in\Lambda(u_i,y)}
 \widehat c_{\lambda_1,y}(u_1,q_1,h_1)
 \overline{\widehat c_{\lambda_2,y}(u_2,q_2,h_2)}
 e_y\!\left(
 \mathscr A\Omega(q_1q_2u_1u_2)^{-1}\right), \tag{4}
\]
where both signs of each nonzero \(h_i\) are included and
\[
 \Omega=h_1q_2u_2-h_2q_1u_1. \tag{5}
\]
Partition (4) identically as
\[
 V=V^{(0)}+V^{(\mathrm{FR})}+V^{(\mathrm{NR})}, \tag{6}
\]
according as
\[
 \Omega=0;\qquad
 \Omega\ne0\ \hbox{ and }\ y\mid\mathscr A\Omega;\qquad
 y\nmid\mathscr A\Omega, \tag{7}
\]
respectively. Then, for every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 |V^{(0)}|\ll_{\varepsilon,J,C,C_0,C_B}
 Q^\varepsilon BQF, \tag{8}
\]
\[
 |V^{(\mathrm{FR})}|\ll_{\varepsilon,J,C,C_0}
 Q^\varepsilon Q^2U^2F^2. \tag{9}
\]
Consequently the specified-spectrum estimate
\[
 |V^{(\mathrm{NR})}|
 \ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon
 \left(UBQF+U^2Q^2F^2\right) \tag{TOP-B-PRECAUCHY-NR-SPEC}
\]
would imply
\[
 V\ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon U
 \left(BQF+{BQ^2F^2\over Y}\right), \tag{10}
\]
and hence, by fact 66a8c3bb4822f841, the physical trace bound
\[
 |\mathcal T_{B,F}(U,Y)|
 \ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon
 \left(B\sqrt{Q/H_P}+{BQ\over\sqrt Y}\right). \tag{11}
\]
The envelope (1) is essential to (8)-(9): no corresponding arbitrary-weight estimate is asserted. TOP-B-PRECAUCHY-NR-SPEC itself remains open.
61cf02eb05b38a54.proof:
Equation (2) follows exactly as in fact 41b56ed8e64bdba6. First apply additive reciprocity with the coprime integers \(q\) and \(uy\):
\[
 e_q(-\mathscr A h(uy)^{-1})
 =e(-\mathscr A h/(quy))e_{uy}(\mathscr A hq^{-1}).
\]
Then use \((u,y)=1\) and the CRT identity
\[
 e_{uy}(x)=e_u(xy^{-1})e_y(xu^{-1}).
\]
This proves (2). Substitute it into the definition of \(K_{u,y}\) in fact 66a8c3bb4822f841 and sum over \(u\). Squaring \(G_y\) gives (4), because the difference of the two \(y\)-phases is
\[
 h_1(q_1u_1)^{-1}-h_2(q_2u_2)^{-1}
 \equiv
 \Omega(q_1q_2u_1u_2)^{-1}\pmod y.
\]
The three alternatives in (7) are disjoint and exhaustive, proving (6).

We prove (8). Put \(x_i=q_iu_i\). Then
\[
 UQ\le x_i<4UQ.
\]
For each fixed \(x_i\), the number of admissible representations \(x_i=q_iu_i\) is at most \(\tau(x_i)\). If \(\Omega=0\), then
\[
 h_1x_2=h_2x_1.
\]
Since each \(x_i\) is positive and each \(h_i\) is nonzero, the two \(h_i\) have the same sign. There are two choices of their common sign. Write uniquely
\[
 (x_i,|h_i|)=k_i(a,b),\qquad (a,b)=1.
\]
The displayed rectangles force \(k_1/k_2\) to lie between fixed positive constants. For fixed \((k_1,k_2)\), with \(k=\max(k_1,k_2)\), there are
\[
 O(UQ/k)
 \quad\hbox{choices for }a,qquad
 O(F/k)
 \quad\hbox{choices for }b.
\]
For fixed \(k\), there are \(O(k)\) ordered pairs \((k_1,k_2)\) with comparable entries and maximum \(k\). Hence the number of ordered quadruples \((x_1,h_1,x_2,h_2)\) is
\[
 \ll UQF\sum_{k\le 4UQ+2F}{1\over k}
 \ll UQF\log(2UQF). \tag{12}
\]
Restoring the factorizations \(x_i=q_iu_i\), the two copy indices, and the coefficient weights in (1) costs \(Q^\varepsilon\), since every displayed variable is at most a fixed power of \(Q\). There are fewer than \(2Y\) possible integers \(y\). Thus absolute summation and (12) give
\[
 |V^{(0)}|\ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon YUQF
 \ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon BQF
\]
by \(UY\le C_BB\). This is (8).

For (9), fix \((u_1,q_1,h_1,u_2,q_2,h_2)\) with \(\Omega\ne0\). Because \(\mathscr A\ne0\), the integer \(\mathscr A\Omega\) is nonzero. It has polynomial size in \(Q\), so the number of its positive divisors, and hence the number of \(y\in[Y,2Y)\) satisfying \(y\mid\mathscr A\Omega\), is \(O_\varepsilon(Q^\varepsilon)\). The inherited support restrictions, including \((u_i,y)=1\), \((q_i,u_iy)=1\), endpoints, and all deletion masks, only reduce this count. There are
\[
 O(U^2Q^2F^2)
\]
ordered coordinate sextuples. The two coefficient weights and the two copy multiplicities again cost only \(Q^\varepsilon\) by (1). Absolute summation proves (9).

Finally \(U\ge1\), so (8) is at most \(Q^\varepsilon UBQF\). Also (1)'s scale relation gives \(B/Y\asymp U\), whence
\[
 U{BQ^2F^2\over Y}\asymp U^2Q^2F^2.
\]
Combining (6), (8), (9), and TOP-B-PRECAUCHY-NR-SPEC gives (10). Fact 66a8c3bb4822f841 then gives (11).

glossary.Omega: the cross-u determinant h_1 q_2 u_2-h_2 q_1 u_1
glossary.TOP-B-PRECAUCHY-NR-SPEC: the remaining source-specific nonresonant cross-u energy estimate
glossary.V^(0): the Omega=0 sector of the pre-Cauchy y-energy
glossary.V^(FR): the Omega nonzero sector for which y divides the target times Omega
glossary.V^(NR): the sector for which y does not divide the target times Omega
glossary.widehat c_{lambda,y}(u,q,h): the literal top-B coefficient with the Archimedean and inverse-y modulo u reciprocity factors retained

62501fbd8d58b5bb.title: GA-COMMON-CORE-TWO-END-DESCENT: EXACT LITERAL p^{-1} DESCENT ON BOTH ENDPOINT SOURCE PROJECTIONS. Adopt the forward common-core setting of fact f1cd394ea025163e. Thus
62501fbd8d58b5bb.author: slava chan
62501fbd8d58b5bb.statement:
GA-COMMON-CORE-TWO-END-DESCENT: EXACT LITERAL p^{-1} DESCENT ON BOTH ENDPOINT SOURCE PROJECTIONS. Adopt the forward common-core setting of fact f1cd394ea025163e. Thus
g=pg_0, alpha beta divides T, n=dv,
gamma congruent [T/(alpha beta)]g_0^{-1} (mod p),
a_n=gamma n^{-1} (mod p).                                       (1)
Put m_0=g_0rho_d, where rho_d=d/gcd(d,T); then gcd(p,m_0)=1. Let psi be any additive character modulo m_0.

Define the left distinguished source projection
A^{dist}_{psi}
 =sum_{supported R=(epsilon,pg_0alpha,b)}
   psi(epsilon b beta)
   b_{v,R}(n/B)e_p(-a_n epsilon b beta),                         (2)
and the right distinguished source projection
B^{dist}_{psi}
 =sum_{supported R'=(epsilon',pg_0beta,b')}
   psi(epsilon'b'alpha)
   b_{v,R'}(n/B)e_p(-a_n epsilon'b'alpha).                       (3)
For a supported scaling k on the left put
q=kpg_0alpha, h=epsilon kb, q_0=q/p.                              (4)
Let G^{(p)}_{q_0,n} be the rescaled physical amplitude from fact 3dee3375b9261448 corresponding to the literal q-indexed amplitude in C_{q,h}. Define
D^L_{psi}
 =mu(pg_0alpha)
  sum_{supported R} psi(epsilon b beta)
  sum_{k in I_v(R)}mu(k){H_Pover np}
   widehat G^{(p)}_{q_0,n}(h/(pn))
   e_{q_0n}(Th p^{-1}).                                         (5)
Define D^R_{psi} analogously with
R'=(epsilon',pg_0beta,b'), q'=k'pg_0beta,
h'=epsilon'k'b', q'_0=q'/p,                                     (6)
and with psi(epsilon'b'alpha) in place of the left character. Then
A^{dist}_{psi}=D^L_{psi},                                        (7)
B^{dist}_{psi}=D^R_{psi}.                                        (8)
Here the factor p^{-1} from amplitude descent is already displayed in H_P/(np) in (5) and its right analogue.

Equivalently, if one defines unnormalized descended rows
E^L_{psi}=pD^L_{psi}, E^R_{psi}=pD^R_{psi},                      (9)
then
A^{dist}_{psi}=p^{-1}E^L_{psi},
B^{dist}_{psi}=p^{-1}E^R_{psi}.                                 (10)
Therefore the unique large p-local Fourier factor lambda_p=p(p-2)/(p-1) acts on the exact two-endpoint product by
lambda_p A^{dist}_{psi}conjugate(B^{dist}_{psi})
 ={p-2over p(p-1)}
  E^L_{psi}conjugate(E^R_{psi}).                                (11)

All sums in (2)-(8) retain the actual incomplete ray sets, squarefree Mobius signs, scaling intervals, gcd(q,v) gates, q-indexed physical source before rescaling, and the remaining m_0 slope character psi. The rescaled amplitudes in (5)-(6) carry the exact p-divisibility source slice of fact 3dee3375b9261448. Equation (11) is an exact literal coefficient identity for the distinguished common-core p-mode; it is not a numerical saving because no norm estimate for E^L_{psi},E^R_{psi} is asserted.

This theorem proves no estimate for the descended rows, no cancellation among p-filter modes, no sum over psi,p,g_0,rho_d or terminal d, no reverse-orientation statement, prime trace estimate, C-HILBERT-OP-SUP, tail payment, or Goldbach.
62501fbd8d58b5bb.proof:
For a left scaling (4), fact f1cd394ea025163e proves
C_{q,h}(n/B)e_p(-a_n epsilon b beta)
 ={H_Pover n}widehat{mathcal F}_{q,n}(h/n)
  e_{q_0n}(Th p^{-1}).                                          (12)
Fact 3dee3375b9261448 gives for the same literal smooth physical source fibre
widehat{mathcal F}_{q,n}(h/n)
 ={1/p}widehat G^{(p)}_{q_0,n}(h/(pn)).                          (13)
Insert (13) into (12), multiply by the unchanged factor
psi(epsilon b beta), and use
b_{v,R}(n/B)
 =mu(pg_0alpha)sum_{k in I_v(R)}mu(k)C_{q,h}(n/B).
Summing the exact supported left rays and scalings gives (7).

We prove the right endpoint directly. For a right scaling (6),
T=alpha beta[T/(alpha beta)] and q'_0=k'g_0beta give
Th'(q'_0)^{-1}n^{-1}
 congruent [T/(alpha beta)]g_0^{-1}n^{-1}
            epsilon'b'alpha
 congruent a_n epsilon'b'alpha (mod p).                          (14)
The same additive-reciprocity calculation as in fact f1cd394ea025163e therefore gives
C_{q',h'}(n/B)e_p(-a_n epsilon'b'alpha)
 ={H_Pover n}widehat{mathcal F}_{q',n}(h'/n)
  e_{q'_0n}(Th'p^{-1}).                                         (15)
Apply fact 3dee3375b9261448 to the right physical source amplitude, obtaining the analogue of (13). Multiply by psi(epsilon'b'alpha), insert
b_{v,R'}(n/B)
 =mu(pg_0beta)sum_{k' in I_v(R')}mu(k')C_{q',h'}(n/B),
and sum. This proves (8).

Definitions (9) immediately give (10). Multiply the two identities in (10), with conjugation on the right, and use
lambda_p/p^2
 =[p(p-2)/(p-1)]/p^2
 =(p-2)/[p(p-1)]
to prove (11). Every additional character and literal support factor was carried multiplicatively through the termwise identities, proving the stated retention and exclusions.

glossary.A^{dist}_{psi}: The left actual source projection at the distinguished p-frequency and a remaining m_0 slope character.
glossary.B^{dist}_{psi}: The right actual source projection at the distinguished p-frequency and a remaining m_0 slope character.
glossary.D^L_{psi}: The normalized descended left source row including its p^{-1} amplitude factor.
glossary.D^R_{psi}: The normalized descended right source row including its p^{-1} amplitude factor.
glossary.E^L_{psi}: The unnormalized descended left source row pD^L_{psi}.
glossary.E^R_{psi}: The unnormalized descended right source row pD^R_{psi}.

629ed652df233d7b.title: FACTORABLE-EFFECTIVE-MODULUS A-PROCESS TYPE-I SUPPLIER, INCLUDING THE BALANCED TWO-FREE CELL. Fix J>=1. Let n>1 be squarefree, let C be an integer, put g=gcd(C,n), and put m_eff=n/g>1. Suppose m_eff=m_0m_1 with coprime positive integers m_0,m_1. Let X,A,B>=1. Let alpha_a be supported on A<=a<2A with |alpha_a|<=tau_J(a). Let c be squarefree. Let W be extended by zero and supported on X<=k<2X, and define V_X(W)=sup_k|W(k)|+sum_k|W(k+1)-W(k)|. Then, for every epsilon>0,
629ed652df233d7b.author: slava chan
629ed652df233d7b.statement:
FACTORABLE-EFFECTIVE-MODULUS A-PROCESS TYPE-I SUPPLIER, INCLUDING THE BALANCED TWO-FREE CELL. Fix J>=1. Let n>1 be squarefree, let C be an integer, put g=gcd(C,n), and put m_eff=n/g>1. Suppose m_eff=m_0m_1 with coprime positive integers m_0,m_1. Let X,A,B>=1. Let alpha_a be supported on A<=a<2A with |alpha_a|<=tau_J(a). Let c be squarefree. Let W be extended by zero and supported on X<=k<2X, and define V_X(W)=sup_k|W(k)|+sum_k|W(k+1)-W(k)|. Then, for every epsilon>0,
|sum_{a,b;(ab,nc)=1}alpha_a W(ab)e_n(C(ab)^(-1))|
<<_{J,epsilon} V_X(W)tau(nc)(m_eff AB)^epsilon A
[ (Bm_1)^(1/2)+Bm_0^(-1/4)+B^(1/2)m_0^(1/4)].                    (1)
Here b is otherwise unweighted and B<=b<2B.

Fix lambda>0. If AB is comparable to X, m_eff is comparable to X, A and B are both comparable to X^(1/2), nc<=X^K for a fixed K, V_X(W)<=X^epsilon, and
m_eff^lambda<=m_1<=m_eff^(1/2-lambda),                           (2)
then (1) is <<X^(1-lambda/4+O(epsilon)). In particular this pays the balanced two-free cell of fact 3dabf494e3ed99fd whenever the effective modulus has a squarefree divisor in the factor window (2). It does not pay a prime or factor-gap effective modulus having no such divisor, and it does not by itself route every multi-free residual box.
629ed652df233d7b.proof:
Write C=gC'. Then gcd(C',m_eff)=1 and, on the unit support,
e_n(C(ab)^(-1))=e_{m_eff}(C'(ab)^(-1)).
Fix a with gcd(a,nc)=1. The inverse phase restricts b to gcd(b,m_eff)=1. Let
s=rad(nc)/gcd(rad(nc),m_eff).
Then gcd(s,m_eff)=1, and the remaining b-gate is
1_{gcd(b,s)=1}=sum_{d|s,d|b}mu(d).
For a fixed divisor d put b=dr. The variable r lies in an interval of length at most B/d, is coprime to m_eff, and the phase is
e_{m_eff}(C'(ad)^(-1)r^(-1)).                                  (3)

We use Dartyge and Martin, arXiv:1802.09090, Lemma 12, with their k=1, q_0=m_0, q_1=m_1, delta=1, R=0, interval length N=B/d, and unit numerator alpha=C'(ad)^(-1) modulo m_eff. Their complete statement gives
|sum_{r in I;gcd(r,m_eff)=1}e_{m_eff}(C'(ad)^(-1)r^(-1))|
<< (B/d)^(1/2)m_1^(1/2)
 +(B/d)^(1/2)m_0^(1/4)12^(omega(m_0)/2)
  {((B/d)/m_0)^(1/2)+(log m_eff)^(1/2)}.                       (4)
The hypotheses hold because m_eff is squarefree, m_0m_1=m_eff, and the numerator in (3) is a unit. The proof of the cited lemma iterates the van der Corput A-process and completes the remaining m_0-sum; its nonconstant rational-function complete sums are bounded prime by prime by the Weil bound. Thus its factorization roles are exactly the displayed m_0,m_1 roles and no unmentioned averaging is used.

Because m_0 is squarefree, 12^(omega(m_0)/2)(log m_eff)^(1/2)<=(m_eff AB)^epsilon after enlarging the implied constant. Partial summation applies (4) to the weight W(adr). The map r to adr is increasing, so its supremum plus total variation on every resulting interval is at most V_X(W). Consequently the fixed-d weighted r-sum is
<<epsilon V_X(W)(m_eff AB)^epsilon
[(Bm_1/d)^(1/2)+(B/d)m_0^(-1/4)+(B/d)^(1/2)m_0^(1/4)].          (5)
Sum (5) over d|s. The sums of d^(-1/2) and d^(-1) over these divisors are at most tau(s), which is at most tau(nc). This bounds the fixed-a inner sum by the right-hand bracket in (1), with the displayed common factors. Finally,
sum_{A<=a<2A}|alpha_a|<<_{J,epsilon}A^(1+epsilon),
and the extra A^epsilon is absorbed by (m_eff AB)^epsilon. This proves (1).

For the corollary, write m_eff on the X-scale. Under (2), m_0=m_eff/m_1 satisfies
m_eff^(1/2+lambda)<=m_0<=m_eff^(1-lambda).
After multiplication by A, the three terms in (1) are respectively at most
X^(1-lambda/2+o(1)),
X^(7/8-lambda/4+o(1)),
X^(1-lambda/4+o(1)).
Indeed A and B are on the X^(1/2)-scale. The last exponent is the largest, proving X^(1-lambda/4+O(epsilon)). In the balanced cell of fact 3dabf494e3ed99fd, one of the two free variables may be the b-variable and the other, together with all unit Mobius-bearing factors, is the a-carrier, so A and B are both on the X^(1/2)-scale. This proves the stated application and every limitation.

630165d40f5dd2de.title: Fix a nonzero integer Delta and fixed smooth functions F and G compactly supported in (1/2,1). Let H>=2 and X=H^3. Let M_1,M_2,N_1,N_2 lie between X and 2X, put f(x)=F(x/M_1) and g(x)=G(x/M_2), and let alpha and beta be complex sequences of absolute value at most one supported respectively on [N_1/2,N_1] and [N_2/2,N_2]. Let T be the sum of f(m_1)g(m_2)alpha(n_1)beta(n_2) over positive integers satisfying m_1n_2-m_2n_1=Delta. Let Z be the sum, over positive n_1,n_2 in the sequence supports with gcd(n_1,n_2) dividing Delta, of (gcd(n_1,n_2)/(n_1n_2))alpha(n_1)beta(n_2) times the integral over real x of f((x+Delta)/n_2)g(x/n_1). Then, for every epsilon>0, |T-Z| is at most a constant depending on Delta,F,G,epsilon times H^(117/20+epsilon), and |Z| is at most a constant depending on Delta,F,G times H^6. In addition, there exist fixed nonnegative smooth profiles F,G compactly supported in (1/2,1), equal length parameters M_1=M_2=N_1=N_2=2X, and nonnegative sequences alpha,beta of absolute value at most one for which Z is at least a positive constant times H^6 for all sufficiently large H. On the sign sector a>0,c>0,d<0,b>0, the substitution (m_1,m_2,n_1,n_2)=(a,c,-d,b) changes the determinant equation into ab+cd=Delta and gives the slope identity a/(-d)-c/b=Delta/((-d)b)
630165d40f5dd2de.author: slava chan
630165d40f5dd2de.statement: Fix a nonzero integer Delta and fixed smooth functions F and G compactly supported in (1/2,1). Let H>=2 and X=H^3. Let M_1,M_2,N_1,N_2 lie between X and 2X, put f(x)=F(x/M_1) and g(x)=G(x/M_2), and let alpha and beta be complex sequences of absolute value at most one supported respectively on [N_1/2,N_1] and [N_2/2,N_2]. Let T be the sum of f(m_1)g(m_2)alpha(n_1)beta(n_2) over positive integers satisfying m_1n_2-m_2n_1=Delta. Let Z be the sum, over positive n_1,n_2 in the sequence supports with gcd(n_1,n_2) dividing Delta, of (gcd(n_1,n_2)/(n_1n_2))alpha(n_1)beta(n_2) times the integral over real x of f((x+Delta)/n_2)g(x/n_1). Then, for every epsilon>0, |T-Z| is at most a constant depending on Delta,F,G,epsilon times H^(117/20+epsilon), and |Z| is at most a constant depending on Delta,F,G times H^6. In addition, there exist fixed nonnegative smooth profiles F,G compactly supported in (1/2,1), equal length parameters M_1=M_2=N_1=N_2=2X, and nonnegative sequences alpha,beta of absolute value at most one for which Z is at least a positive constant times H^6 for all sufficiently large H. On the sign sector a>0,c>0,d<0,b>0, the substitution (m_1,m_2,n_1,n_2)=(a,c,-d,b) changes the determinant equation into ab+cd=Delta and gives the slope identity a/(-d)-c/b=Delta/((-d)b).
630165d40f5dd2de.proof:
Bettin--Chandee, arXiv:1502.00769, Corollary 1 states that T equals Z plus an error bounded by
(eta R)^(3/2) ||alpha||_2 ||beta||_2 (N_1N_2)^(7/20)(N_1+N_2)^(1/4+epsilon)(M_1M_2)^epsilon,
where R=M_1N_2/(M_2N_1)+M_2N_1/(M_1N_2), and eta records the smoothness constants. For the fixed scaled profiles f(x)=F(x/M_1) and g(x)=G(x/M_2), their derivatives satisfy bounds with constants depending only on the fixed profile and the derivative order, exactly as required in the cited corollary; hence eta and the implied constant depend only on F and G. Since all four length parameters lie between X and 2X, R is bounded, ||alpha||_2||beta||_2 is at most a constant times X, (N_1N_2)^(7/20) is at most a constant times X^(7/10), and (N_1+N_2)^(1/4) is at most a constant times X^(1/4). Absorbing the factor (M_1M_2)^epsilon by renaming epsilon gives |T-Z| at most a constant times X^(39/20+epsilon)=H^(117/20+epsilon).

For the upper bound on Z, gcd(n_1,n_2)<=|Delta| whenever it divides Delta. The integral has absolute value at most a constant depending on F,G times X^2, while n_1n_2 is bounded below by a constant times X^2. Hence each denominator pair contributes at most a constant depending on Delta,F,G, and there are O(X^2) pairs. Thus |Z| is O(X^2)=O(H^6).

For the saturation assertion, choose fixed nonnegative smooth functions F and G supported in (1/2,1) and equal to one on [7/10,4/5]. Set all four length parameters equal to 2X, so f and g equal one on [7X/5,8X/5]. Let alpha and beta be the indicators of the integers in I=[99X/50,2X]. If n_1,n_2 belong to I, the intervals [7n_1X/5,8n_1X/5] and [7n_2X/5-Delta,8n_2X/5-Delta], on which the two factors in the integrand are one, overlap in an interval of length at least a fixed positive multiple of X^2 for all sufficiently large H. Since n_1n_2 is at most 4X^2, every coprime pair in I contributes at least a fixed positive constant to Z.

A positive proportion of pairs in I are coprime. Indeed, the number having a common prime divisor is at most the sum over primes p<=2X of (|I|/p+1)^2. The quadratic main part is at most |I|^2 sum_p p^(-2), and sum_p p^(-2)<=sum_{n=2}^infinity n^(-2)=pi^2/6-1<1; the remaining terms are o(X^2). Hence at least a fixed positive multiple of |I|^2, and therefore of X^2, pairs are coprime. Every such pair has gcd one, which divides Delta. Therefore Z is at least a positive constant times X^2=H^6.

Finally, on the stated sign sector the four substituted variables are positive. Direct substitution gives m_1n_2-m_2n_1=ab-c(-d)=ab+cd=Delta. Dividing this identity by (-d)b gives the displayed slope identity.

6507639658c780d5.title: HC-MED SMALLER-FACTOR MAYNARD MARKING NO-FIT AND FORCED SYMMETRIC PIVOT. Fix an h-row of fact edabb9a0d2959b41, put X=X_h=B/h, and restrict to its fundamental-domain HC-MED region
6507639658c780d5.author: slava chan
6507639658c780d5.statement:
HC-MED SMALLER-FACTOR MAYNARD MARKING NO-FIT AND FORCED SYMMETRIC PIVOT. Fix an h-row of fact edabb9a0d2959b41, put X=X_h=B/h, and restrict to its fundamental-domain HC-MED region
d<=m, X^eta<=d<=X^(1/4+eta), X<=dm<2X.                           (1)
Suppose the centered modulus has scale
Q_c=X^(1/2+delta_h)                                              (2)
and a proposed application of Maynard's factorable-modulus Type-II hypotheses uses a selected prime scale cal P={p prime:P<=p<2P} and marks a prime p dividing the smaller factor d. Then those hypotheses force
P>=X^(2/5+6delta_h)(log X)^(2C)                                 (3)
for a sufficiently large fixed C. Consequently, if
eta<=3/20+6delta_h,                                              (4)
the marked-inside-d sector is empty for all sufficiently large X.

Thus in the usual small-eta near-half chamber, the verified coefficient pipeline obtained by marking d cannot by itself pay any HC-MED term. A potentially nonempty symmetric Maynard route must instead mark the large factor m (or use a different analytic theorem): write m=pm' and fold v=dm', so that pv=dm. This is a scale/support pivot only; it does not assert that m has a selected prime, that the factorable modulus hypotheses hold, or that the symmetric marked sector is paid.
6507639658c780d5.proof:
Fact 3405d0cb4853555f derives from Maynard's scale hypotheses that every admissible selected-prime scale satisfies
P>=X^(2/5+6delta_h)(log X)^(2C),                                 (5)
after replacing that fact's ambient variable B by the present row length X. This substitution is exact because the bilinear product in the h-row is dm on the X-scale and the centered modulus is Q_c=X^(1/2+delta_h).

If p is selected and divides d, then P<=p<=d. The HC-MED support (1) gives d<=X^(1/4+eta). Hence
X^(2/5+6delta_h)(log X)^(2C)
 <=P<=X^(1/4+eta).                                               (6)
Under (4), 1/4+eta<=2/5+6delta_h. The left side of (6) is then larger than the right side for sufficiently large X because of the positive logarithmic factor. This contradiction proves emptiness.

The exact summand in fact edabb9a0d2959b41 is symmetric in d,m before the fundamental-domain choice: rho_{1/2}(d)rho_{1/2}(m), the unit conditions, the centered discrepancy, the quotient, and A_lit depend symmetrically or only through dm. Therefore the fractional-Ramare marking may algebraically be applied to m instead, writing m=pm'. Folding v=dm' preserves pv=dm and hence preserves the centered residue and literal product amplitude. This establishes only the stated legal pivot, not its analytic hypotheses or coverage.

glossary.delta_h: The rowwise excess-modulus exponent defined by Q_c=X_h^(1/2+delta_h).
glossary.symmetric Maynard route: The alternative marking in which a selected prime is extracted from the large half-convolution factor m rather than the smaller factor d.

Let Q be sufficiently large, put B=Q^beta and H_T=B/Q, and choose any G>=1; put H_P=H_T/G, L_0=H_TQ^sigma, and Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma). Fix a nonzero integer L_src with |L_src|<=Q^C_A. For Q_c<=q<2Q_c let |d_{c,q}|<=1, supported only when q is squarefree, gcd(c,q)=1, and gcd(L_src/c,q)=1. For each dyadic F>=1 choose coefficients nu_{c,F}(h), alpha_{c,F}(u), gamma_{c,F}(p), a scalar omega_{c,F}, and a uniformly scaled-smooth projective amplitude Psi_{c,F} of fixed complexity K. Assume divisor bounds of order J, supports F<=|h|<2F, U_c<=u<2U_c, and primes Y_c<=p<2Y_c with L_0<p<Z, and assume that for every integer J_0>=1 there is a fixed constant C_{J_0} such that |omega_{c,F}|<=C_{J_0}min(1,(F/H_P)^(-J_0)). Define
653b56b5854f603b.author: slava chan
653b56b5854f603b.statement:
FULL-G COMPLETE-FREQUENCY TARGET-GCD-DESCENDED INTERVAL-PRIME TRACE. Fix integers J,C_A,K>=1, a constant C>=1, 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, and let 1<=beta<=6/5-2kappa. Let Q be sufficiently large, put B=Q^beta and H_T=B/Q, and choose any G>=1; put H_P=H_T/G, L_0=H_TQ^sigma, and Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma). Fix a nonzero integer L_src with |L_src|<=Q^C_A. Let C_med be any set of squarefree divisors c of L_src satisfying c<=H_TQ^(sigma/4). For each c in C_med put Q_c=Q/c and choose U_c,Y_c>=1 with C^(-1)B<=U_cY_c<=CB and L_0/2<=Y_c<=Z. For Q_c<=q<2Q_c let |d_{c,q}|<=1, supported only when q is squarefree, gcd(c,q)=1, and gcd(L_src/c,q)=1. For each dyadic F>=1 choose coefficients nu_{c,F}(h), alpha_{c,F}(u), gamma_{c,F}(p), a scalar omega_{c,F}, and a uniformly scaled-smooth projective amplitude Psi_{c,F} of fixed complexity K. Assume divisor bounds of order J, supports F<=|h|<2F, U_c<=u<2U_c, and primes Y_c<=p<2Y_c with L_0<p<Z, and assume that for every integer J_0>=1 there is a fixed constant C_{J_0} such that |omega_{c,F}|<=C_{J_0}min(1,(F/H_P)^(-J_0)). Define
T_c=H_P^(-1) sum_{F dyadic} omega_{c,F} sum_{Q_c<=q<2Q_c}d_{c,q} sum_{F<=|h|<2F}nu_{c,F}(h) sum_{U_c<=u<2U_c; Y_c<=p<2Y_c, p prime; gcd(up,cq)=1; gcd(u,p)=1} alpha_{c,F}(u)gamma_{c,F}(p)Psi_{c,F}(q/Q_c,|h|/F,u/U_c,p/Y_c)e_q(-(L_src/c)h(up)^(-1)).
Then there exists delta=delta(kappa,C_A,J,K,C)>0 such that
sum_{c in C_med}|T_c| << GQ^(2-delta).
The estimate is uniform in the divisor set C_med and in all deletion masks and polylogarithmically many smooth, dyadic, sign, parent, high, fixed-U, source, and projective-separation labels absorbable into the displayed coefficients or the fixed projective family. It holds whether H_P is below or above one.
653b56b5854f603b.proof:
Put v=F/H_P and q_0=Q/c. We separate the explicitly stated analytic frequency range
v<=Q^(sigma/2).                                                     (1)
We first check all scale hypotheses needed for the interval-prime estimate in fact 4cae52efa792b9ef, exactly in the descended setup used in fact 97e9b97caca25b8d.

Since Y_c>=L_0/2=H_TQ^sigma/2 and F=vH_P=vH_T/G, (1) and G>=1 give
2F/Y_c <= 4v/(GQ^sigma) <=4Q^(-sigma/2)<1.                         (2)
Also c<=H_TQ^(sigma/4) and Y_c<=Z imply
q_0/(H_PY_c)
 = QG/(cH_TY_c)
 >= GQ^(3/2-beta+11sigma/4).                                       (3)
At beta<=6/5-2kappa, the exponent on the right after omitting G is at least
3/10+2kappa+11sigma/4,
which is strictly larger than sigma/2. Hence, uniformly on (1), 8FY_c<q for every sufficiently large Q and every supported q. Finally,
U_c << B/Y_c << Q^(1-sigma),
whereas
q_0 >= Q^(2-beta-sigma/4).
Because beta<=6/5-2kappa, this gives U_c<q^2 for sufficiently large Q. Thus every analytic hypothesis used in the proof of fact 97e9b97caca25b8d is valid here without any upper or lower power restriction on G beyond G>=1.

For a fixed c and F in (1), the projective separation, removal of gcd(u,p)=1, application of fact 4cae52efa792b9ef to the p not dividing u part, and elementary quotient count for the p dividing u diagonal in the accepted proof of fact 97e9b97caca25b8d give, up to Q^epsilon|omega_{c,F}|, the following four contributions:
A_1=c^(-1)G^(1/2)Q^2(H_T/Y_c)^(1/2)v^(1/2),
A_2=c^(-5/4)Q^(7/4)(H_TY_c)^(1/2)v,
A_3=c^(-3/4)Q^(7/4)H_Tv,
A_4<=c^(-1)Q^(2-sigma)v.                                          (4)
Here A_4 is precisely the p dividing u diagonal. These estimates are local in c,F; the former near-balanced hypothesis in fact 97e9b97caca25b8d was used only later to compare them with Q^2 and to verify the analytic scale inequalities, which have instead been verified directly in (2)-(3).

Divide (4) by GQ^2. Since G>=1, Y_c>=H_TQ^sigma/2, H_TY_c<=H_TZ=Q^(1/2-3sigma), and H_T=Q^(beta-1), the resulting four ratios are at most, respectively,
c^(-1)Q^(-sigma/2)v^(1/2),
c^(-5/4)Q^(-3sigma/2)v,
c^(-3/4)Q^(-1/20-2kappa)v,
c^(-1)Q^(-sigma)v,                                                 (5)
up to fixed constants. For dyadic v<=1 the sums of v^(1/2) and v are bounded geometric sums. For 1<v<=Q^(sigma/2), use only the fixed second-order estimate |omega_{c,F}|<=C_2v^(-2); the dyadic sums of v^(1/2)|omega_{c,F}| and v|omega_{c,F}| are again bounded. Thus the whole analytic range has a fixed power saving relative to GQ^2 after choosing epsilon sufficiently small.

It remains to treat the complementary, nonanalytic frequency range
v>Q^(sigma/2).                                                      (6)
Here we do not invoke the interval-prime estimate. Direct counting of q,h,u,p with the divisor bounds gives
|T_{c,F}| << Q^epsilon H_P^(-1)F(Q/c)B|omega_{c,F}|
 =Q^epsilon c^(-1)Q^2H_T v|omega_{c,F}|.                           (7)
This is valid for every H_P, including H_P<1. Choose one fixed integer J_* so large that
(J_*-1)sigma/2 > 1/5+sigma.
Only here, outside the analytic range (1), use the arbitrary-order Fourier decay with order J_*. Since H_T<=Q^(1/5-2kappa), dyadic summation of (7) over (6) is
<<c^(-1)Q^epsilon Q^2H_T Q^(-(J_*-1)sigma/2)
<<c^(-1)GQ^(2-delta_1)                                            (8)
for some fixed delta_1>0, using G>=1.

Every c is a divisor of the fixed nonzero integer L_src with |L_src|<=Q^C_A. Therefore each of the sums of c^(-1), c^(-3/4), c^(-5/4) over C_med is at most tau(|L_src|)<<Q^epsilon. Combining (5) and (8), and absorbing the finitely or polylogarithmically many permitted labels into Q^epsilon, proves the assertion with a fixed delta>0. If H_P<1, every integer F has v>1, but it still lies in exactly one of (1) or (6), so no separate case or missing Fourier block remains.

65b10e9a052e9479.title: REVERSE FULL-G ALL-LEAF ASSEMBLY THROUGH THE FULL LOW-BETA RANGE. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100 and put sigma=kappa/100 and kappa_0=1/200. Consider the literal reverse forced-high frozen source layers obtained from the swap-closed source and normalized marker identity of fact a71f777ad842c886. Thus D>R, R=x^(1/2+o(1)), D>x^(9/16-kappa_0), d=ga, r=gb, g=gcd(d,r) divides N, and
65b10e9a052e9479.author: slava chan
65b10e9a052e9479.statement:
REVERSE FULL-G ALL-LEAF ASSEMBLY THROUGH THE FULL LOW-BETA RANGE. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100 and put sigma=kappa/100 and kappa_0=1/200. Consider the literal reverse forced-high frozen source layers obtained from the swap-closed source and normalized marker identity of fact a71f777ad842c886. Thus D>R, R=x^(1/2+o(1)), D>x^(9/16-kappa_0), d=ga, r=gb, g=gcd(d,r) divides N, and
Q=R/g>1, B=D/g=Q^beta, 1<=beta<=6/5-2kappa,
G=K/Q>=1, H_T=B/Q, H_P=B/K=H_T/G,
L_src=N/g, and RK=gGQ^2 is comparable to x.
Use the reverse convention: the reciprocal modulus is b, the normalized marked inverse argument is a, and the reciprocal phase has target +L_src. Let R_rev,low be the complete literal reverse nonzero-Poisson sum of all such exact g-layers, retaining every frozen low-beta parent, every normalized marker leaf C0,A,B,C1,C2,C3, every Fourier block, exact target-gcd layer, source coefficient, smooth/projective label, prime-order label, fixed-U mask, high-label mask, parent mask, collision stratum, and deletion selector occurring in the source identity. Then there is a fixed delta_rev=delta_rev(kappa)>0 such that
|R_rev,low| << x^(1-delta_rev).
No reverse interval-prime A target-gcd incidence is deleted, and the estimate includes H_P<1. The assertion is only for the displayed reverse forced-high, actual-G>=1, low-beta layers. It makes no assertion about beta>=6/5, endpoint parents, PMD, a logical bad-N conclusion, or Goldbach.
65b10e9a052e9479.proof:
We first perform the reverse literal check, because this is the only part of the forward proof c6a3ee810402825f that is not orientation-neutral. Relabel
(d',m',D',M')=(r,k,R,K), (r',k',R',K')=(d,m,D,M).
Then R'>D', D'=R=x^(1/2+o(1)), R'=D>x^(9/16-kappa_0), and D'M'=RK is comparable to x. After the exact outer-gcd split the primed normalized variables in fact df9748efe29ab475 are a'=b and b'=a. Poisson summation in the primed first complementary variable gives the raw character
e_a(L_src h b^(-1))
and coefficient a^(-1) Fhat'_{g,b,a}(h/a), with natural frequency length a/K comparable to B/K=H_P and prefactor K/a comparable to H_P^(-1).

For coprime a,b, additive reciprocity gives
e_a(L_src h b^(-1))=e(L_src h/(ab))e_b(-L_src h a^(-1)).
Reindexing the complete nonzero-frequency family by h to -h gives the exact summand
a^(-1) Fhat'_{g,b,a}(-h/a)e(-L_src h/(ab))e_b(+L_src h a^(-1)).       (1)
Thus the reverse reciprocal phase has sign +, modulus b, and marked inverse argument a. No archimedean reciprocity factor has been discarded: the factor e(-L_src h/(ab)) in (1) remains inside the smooth amplitude.

The proof of d8ba46800ba433c2, applied to the primed coordinate permutation, gives for every fixed A_1
|Fhat'_{g,b,a}(-h/a)| << K(log x)^2(1+|h|/H_P)^(-A_1).              (2)
On a signed dyadic block F<=|h|<2F put v=F/H_P. The logarithmic phase size of the retained factor in (1) is
|L_src|F/(QB)=v |L_src|/(QK)=v N/(RK),
which is O(v). Differentiating any fixed number of times in the scaled variables therefore costs only a fixed power of v, and (2) with correspondingly more integrations by parts absorbs that power. The torus-Fourier separation used in the proof of 0d53c27d174b26ed consequently gives the reverse projective norm
<<(log x)^2(1+F/H_P)^(-A_1)                                    (3)
for arbitrary fixed A_1, with the literal prefactor H_P^(-1). The coordinate swap merely permutes the two logarithmic weights and the smooth source coordinates. A cutoff on the original d-coordinate becomes a bounded deletion mask on the marked a-coordinate. The complete h-sign family is permuted, and every frozen parent, high label, fixed-U label, source label, prime-order label, collision label, and deletion selector is retained. Fact a71f777ad842c886 supplies the literal reverse marker on a and makes the surviving low-beta parent a label scalar.

We next audit the orientation-neutral part of the forward proof. On a separated marker block write a=st with S=Q^s and ST comparable to B. Apply f7b5ba9fa0d6cfc8 to the reverse phase e_b(+L_src h(st)^(-1)), using reciprocal-modulus scale Q, target A=+L_src, unit multiplier one, natural scale H_P, and projective norm (3). This gives exactly
G^(1/4)Q^2H_T^(1/2)S^(-1/4)
+G^(1/4)Q^(7/4)H_T^(1/2)S^(1/4)
+Q^2H_TS^(-1/2)+Q^(7/4)H_T,                                  (4)
up to x^epsilon and the projective norm. The proof of 0d53c27d174b26ed compares (4) with GQ^2 and uses only Q,B,G,H_T and the factor scale S, not the original orientation.

For the B leaf, e18b670f5d48f500 and 533acf4056cf5bee select the same balanced stopping factor. For C3, fact 461b4af4d8047ab5 selects a factor inside the full CELL-G window and 0576f567200d41f1 pays the coefficient grouping and collisions. For C2, the three cases and equal-cell collisions are paid by 3b1bda56ad927c5e. For C1, fact 2ff1c15aef183bac supplies the Type-II and medium/large Type-I factors, while its low Type-I blocks are consumed by bbcb9f66597c667c. Fact df2841924153b718 checks literally that every reverse Type-I character has fixed target +L_src, and after target-gcd descent +L_1, with no modulus-dependent unit multiplier. Prime-power and collision errors in those four leaf facts are absolute after the frequency prefactor cancels the frequency count, so (3) sums their complete frequency families. Hence every reverse B,C1,C2,C3 leaf is O(GQ^(2-delta_0)) at fixed g for some delta_0>0 whenever H_P>=1.

If H_P<1, apply the fixed-g theorem 7131a06664967733 to the primed source coordinates. Its forward variables are exactly (D',M',R',K')=(R,K,D,M), so its normalized parameters are the present Q,B,G,H_T,H_P, and its arbitrary bounded anatomy coefficient accepts every reverse marker leaf and retained deletion mask. As in the proof of 0d53c27d174b26ed, forced high and H_P<1 imply beta>20/19, while
beta-1-(19beta-20)/17=(3-2beta)/17>=3/85.
Thus G>H_T places the whole leaf in the fixed-g Bettin-Chandee sector with a fixed buffer, proving the same O(GQ^(2-delta_0)) estimate for every aggregate leaf when H_P<1.

The C0 layer is also literal after the coordinate permutation. Apply 8bf5ca45f71b8c2c with its physical scales renamed (D,R)=(R,D) and its marked integer n=a. For sufficiently large Q the C0 condition a<=S_0 is empty. The bounded-Q C0 layers have complete nonzero-Poisson mass O(x^(1/2+epsilon)) and are therefore power-saving. This closes C0 without a reverse symmetry assumption.

It remains to close every target-gcd layer of the interval-prime A leaf. Fix exact g and put
c=gcd(b,L_src).
Because b is squarefree, c is squarefree. Apply 1c64020b89f097c4 after interchanging (a,m) with (b,k). There are positive integers q,m_1,L_1 such that
b=cq, m=cm_1, L_src=cL_1,
gcd(c,q)=gcd(c,a)=gcd(q,a)=gcd(q,L_1)=1.                     (5)
The reverse phase in (1) descends exactly:
e_b(+L_src h a^(-1))=e_q(+L_1h a^(-1)).                     (6)

The reverse A marker writes a=up with U_cY_c comparable to B and
H_TQ^sigma/2<=Y_c<=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma).
Squarefreeness of a gives gcd(u,p)=1, while (5) gives gcd(up,cq)=1. The descended modulus satisfies q comparable to Q/c. The reverse source is the primed forward source, so the polynomial target estimate of 5ced883d5560f772 applies after the same coordinate renaming and gives |L_src|<=Q^C_A for a fixed C_A depending only on kappa. Equations (3),(5),(6), the marker divisor bounds, and all retained labels now match every slot of 653b56b5854f603b. In that fact choose its signed target parameter to be -L_src. Its displayed character is then
e_q(-((-L_src)/c)h(up)^(-1))=e_q(+L_1h(up)^(-1)),
which is exactly (6); its unit-target hypothesis is gcd(q,L_1)=1.

Put C_cut=H_TQ^(sigma/4). Fact 653b56b5854f603b gives
sum_{c<=C_cut}|T_c| << GQ^(2-delta_1)                         (7)
for some fixed delta_1>0, uniformly in the complete reverse label inventory and whether H_P is below or above one. For c>C_cut, apply 5fbdbbebf99aec55. Its hypotheses hold because B=QH_T<=Q^(6/5), H_P<=H_T<=Q^(1/5), (3) supplies arbitrary fixed Fourier decay, and every phase, gcd selector, prime restriction, collision condition, smooth mask, and deletion condition is allowed. With epsilon<sigma/8 it gives
sum_{c>C_cut}|T_c| << Q^(2-sigma/4+epsilon)
                         << GQ^(2-sigma/8),                   (8)
using G>=1. Combining (7),(8) proves O(GQ^(2-delta_2)) for the complete reverse A contribution on the exact g-layer, with no target-gcd deletion.

Together with the non-A and C0 estimates, the complete exact-g reverse layer is
<<GQ^(2-delta_3)=(RK/g)Q^(-delta_3)<<(x/g)Q^(-delta_3).       (9)
After the primed coordinate renaming, 5ced883d5560f772 also gives Q>=x^(c_kappa+o(1)) for a fixed c_kappa>0 on these reverse forced-high low-beta layers. Since every exact outer gcd divides N,
sum_{g|N}1/g<=tau(N)=x^o(1).
Summing (9) over g and absorbing the polylogarithmically many source, projective, dyadic, sign, parent, prime-cell, collision, and deletion labels yields O(x^(1-delta_rev)) after decreasing the fixed saving exponent. This proves the statement.

glossary.R_rev,low: The complete literal reverse forced-high nonzero-Poisson sum over actual G>=1 and 1<=beta<=6/5-2kappa.
glossary.delta_rev: A fixed positive saving exponent for the complete reverse full-G low-beta assembly.

66185bf160c191f4.title: TWO COMPLEMENTARY LITERAL POINTWISE FALLBACKS FOR THE FULL SCOPED SIX-FACE C4 MOMENT. Adopt the literal scalar canonical-dilator block of facts 01ecc6fab24e57c6 and 134b03fc362a7cf1, with Dcal<=D_lambda<2Dcal, B/2<=n_lambda<=2B, the fixed divisor-function coefficient and copy envelopes of fact 54029717e980dcb7, and z=1. Then, for every epsilon>0,
66185bf160c191f4.author: slava chan
66185bf160c191f4.statement:
TWO COMPLEMENTARY LITERAL POINTWISE FALLBACKS FOR THE FULL SCOPED SIX-FACE C4 MOMENT. Adopt the literal scalar canonical-dilator block of facts 01ecc6fab24e57c6 and 134b03fc362a7cf1, with Dcal<=D_lambda<2Dcal, B/2<=n_lambda<=2B, the fixed divisor-function coefficient and copy envelopes of fact 54029717e980dcb7, and z=1. Then, for every epsilon>0,
sum_lambda |T_lambda(1)|^2
<<_epsilon Q^epsilon
 min{Dcal/Z^4,B/Z^4}
 [BQ^2F^2/Dcal].                                                   (1)
Equivalently, the two separately valid estimates are
sum_lambda |T_lambda(1)|^2
<<_epsilon Q^epsilon BQ^2F^2/Z^4,                                 (2)
sum_lambda |T_lambda(1)|^2
<<_epsilon Q^epsilon B^2Q^2F^2/(Dcal Z^4).                         (3)
On the pre-6/5 sliver, B/Z^4<=Q^(12sigma), so (3) gives the uniform fallback
sum_lambda |T_lambda(1)|^2
<<_epsilon Q^(epsilon+12sigma)BQ^2F^2/Dcal.                        (4)
The displayed replacement loss Q^(12sigma) in (4) is a fixed project power and cannot itself be relabeled Q^epsilon in a theorem quantified for every epsilon. This statement does not assert that the actual ratios Dcal/Z^4 or B/Z^4 are always unbounded or non-absorbable. No canonical CMD bound without the losses in (1), signed off-ray estimate, C4 closure, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
66185bf160c191f4.proof:
By fact 134b03fc362a7cf1, primitive-ray grouping is an exact partition of the supported physical pairs. Hence
T_lambda(1)
=sum_{q,h}c_lambda(q,h;1)mu(q)^2
 1_{gcd(q,D_lambda v_lambda)=1}
 K_lambda(rho(q,h)),                                               (5)
where rho(q,h) is the unique primitive ray and every literal mask remains inside c_lambda.

There are O(QF) physical pairs in the block. Cauchy-Schwarz gives
|T_lambda(1)|^2
<<QF sum_{q,h}|c_lambda(q,h;1)|^2
 |K_lambda(rho(q,h))|^2.                                          (6)
The fixed divisor-function envelope absorbs the coefficient squares into Q^epsilon. Fact 01ecc6fab24e57c6 gives both
|K_lambda(rho)|^2<=729/(4Z^4),                                    (7)
|K_lambda(rho)|^2<=(729/2)B/(D_lambda Z^4)
<=(729/2)B/(Dcal Z^4).                                            (8)
Insert (7) into (6) and count the O(QF) terms:
|T_lambda(1)|^2
<<_epsilon Q^epsilon Q^2F^2/Z^4.                                  (9)
Insert (8) instead:
|T_lambda(1)|^2
<<_epsilon Q^epsilon Q^2F^2B/(Dcal Z^4).                           (10)

The literal copy count used in fact 54029717e980dcb7 is
sum_n#Lambda_D(n)<<_epsilon Q^epsilon B.                           (11)
Summing (9) with (11) proves (2), and summing (10) proves (3). Divide each by the canonical second term BQ^2F^2/Dcal and take the better bound. This proves (1).

Finally fact 01ecc6fab24e57c6 computes
B/Z^4=Q^(5beta-6+12sigma)<=Q^(12sigma)
because beta<6/5. Substitution into (3) proves (4). No lower bound for B/Z^4 or Dcal/Z^4 has been used or claimed.

664a92777dc5f5db.title: UNIT-TARGET INTERVAL-PRIME TRACE BELOW ( eta=6/5)
664a92777dc5f5db.author: slava chan

glossary.A_q: An arbitrary unit numerator modulo q.
glossary.H': The frequency support parameter 2H used in fact 4a101b703d4499f6.
glossary.R_0: The product scale UY of the two reciprocal factors.

66a8c3bb4822f841.title: TOP-B-PRECAUCHY-TRACE-RED. Fix the top-sliver parameters and one exact orientation, outer-gcd layer, normalized base Q, normalized marked scale B, nonzero source target \(\mathscr A\), fixed source/parent/fixed-\(U\)/smooth-projective fibre, and one literal nonzero frequency block \(F\le |h|<2F\) in the top \(B\) anatomy of facts e58fc7c00f1683e6, f0f6807663d3ef3c, and 41b56ed8e64bdba6. Thus every exact stopping copy has \(n=uy\), \((u,y)=1\), and its canonical marked dilator is \(y\). Fix one of the boundedly many dyadic \(u\)-blocks and one dyadic \(y\)-block
66a8c3bb4822f841.author: slava chan
66a8c3bb4822f841.statement:
TOP-B-PRECAUCHY-TRACE-RED. Fix the top-sliver parameters and one exact orientation, outer-gcd layer, normalized base Q, normalized marked scale B, nonzero source target \(\mathscr A\), fixed source/parent/fixed-\(U\)/smooth-projective fibre, and one literal nonzero frequency block \(F\le |h|<2F\) in the top \(B\) anatomy of facts e58fc7c00f1683e6, f0f6807663d3ef3c, and 41b56ed8e64bdba6. Thus every exact stopping copy has \(n=uy\), \((u,y)=1\), and its canonical marked dilator is \(y\). Fix one of the boundedly many dyadic \(u\)-blocks and one dyadic \(y\)-block
\[
 U\le u<2U,\qquad Y\le y<2Y,
\]
such that, for a fixed constant \(C_B\ge1\),
\[
 C_B^{-1}B\le UY\le C_BB. \tag{1}
\]
Assume \(1\le F\le C_FH_P\), where \(C_F\ge1\) is fixed.

For each supported pair \((u,y)\), let \(\Lambda(u,y)\) be the complete finite family of exact top-\(B\) stopping copies having this pair after all auxiliary-sibling copies belonging to the fixed fibre have been recombined at \((u,y)\), before taking any absolute value. Every literal source, marker, Möbius, Fourier, target-gcd, fixed-\(U\), parent, sign, order/equal-cell, collision, deletion, coprimality and provenance factor is retained in the corresponding coefficient \(c_\lambda(q,h)\), extended by zero unless
\[
 Q\le q<2Q,quad F\le |h|<2F,quad (q,uy)=1,quad h\ne0.
\]
Define
\[
 K_{u,y}:=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda(u,y)}
 \sum_{q,h}c_\lambda(q,h)
 e_q\!\left(-\mathscr A h(uy)^{-1}\right),\qquad
 G_y:=\sum_{U\le u<2U}K_{u,y}, \tag{2}
\]
and
\[
 V:=\sum_{Y\le y<2Y}|G_y|^2. \tag{3}
\]
The complete physical contribution of this block is exactly
\[
 \mathcal T_{B,F}(U,Y)=H_P^{-1}\sum_{Y\le y<2Y}G_y. \tag{4}
\]
Consequently
\[
 |\mathcal T_{B,F}(U,Y)|\le 2^{1/2}H_P^{-1}Y^{1/2}V^{1/2}. \tag{5}
\]
In particular, if for every \(\varepsilon>0\)
\[
 V\ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon U
 \left(BQF+{BQ^2F^2\over Y}\right), \tag{6}
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{
 |\mathcal T_{B,F}(U,Y)|
 \ll_{\varepsilon,C_B,C_F}
 Q^\varepsilon\left(
 B\sqrt{Q/H_P}+{BQ\over\sqrt Y}\right).} \tag{7}
\]
This theorem is only exact regrouping and Cauchy before the first absolute value. It deletes no literal coordinate and asserts neither (6), a cross-\(u\) estimate, the other five top anatomies, nor any endpoint or Goldbach conclusion.
66a8c3bb4822f841.proof:
Facts e58fc7c00f1683e6 and f0f6807663d3ef3c give the exact source-preserving top-\(B\) stopping copies \(n=uy\), with every inherited coordinate retained and with \(y\) the canonical marked dilator. Fact 41b56ed8e64bdba6 gives the literal reciprocal row and the physical Poisson prefactor \(H_P^{-1}\). Restricting by the stated dyadic partition and then summing every exact copy having the same pair \((u,y)\) gives (2). Since this is a finite reassociation of the original sum and no absolute value has yet been taken, summing first over \(u\) and then over \(y\) gives the identity (4). All masks and labels listed in the statement remain factors of \(c_\lambda(q,h)\); none is suppressed in this reassociation.

There are at most \(Y+1\le2Y\) integers in \([Y,2Y)\), since \(Y\ge1\). Cauchy's inequality applied only to the outer \(y\)-sum in (4) therefore gives
\[
 |\mathcal T_{B,F}(U,Y)|
 \le H_P^{-1}(2Y)^{1/2}
 \left(\sum_{Y\le y<2Y}|G_y|^2\right)^{1/2},
\]
which is (5).

Assume (6). After replacing \(\varepsilon\) there by \(2\varepsilon\) and using \(\sqrt{x+x'}\le\sqrt x+\sqrt{x'}\), (5) gives
\[
 |\mathcal T_{B,F}(U,Y)|
 \ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon H_P^{-1}
 \left(\sqrt{YUBQF}+QF\sqrt{UB}\right). \tag{8}
\]
By (1), \(UY\le C_BB\) and \(U\le C_BB/Y\). Hence the two terms in (8) are respectively at most
\[
 C_B^{1/2}H_P^{-1}B\sqrt{QF},
 \qquad
 C_B^{1/2}H_P^{-1}{BQF\over\sqrt Y}.
\]
Finally \(F\le C_FH_P\) implies
\[
 H_P^{-1}\sqrt F\le C_F^{1/2}H_P^{-1/2},
 \qquad
 H_P^{-1}F\le C_F.
\]
Substitution proves (7). No analytic estimate other than the assumed (6) has been used.

glossary.G_y: the sum of K_{u,y} over the fixed dyadic u-block
glossary.K_{u,y}: the complete literal reciprocal-row aggregate over Lambda(u,y)
glossary.Lambda(u,y): the complete family of exact top-B stopping copies at the fixed pair (u,y) inside the frozen fibre
glossary.T_{B,F}(U,Y): the corresponding physical top-B trace block including the factor H_P^{-1}
glossary.V: the pre-Cauchy y-energy sum of |G_y| squared

670a97b5f2366250.title: ALL-NONZERO SOURCE-TRANSMUTED DIVISOR-GRAPH FORM OF OSC AND ITS MINIMAL SUPPLIER
670a97b5f2366250.author: slava chan
670a97b5f2366250.statement:
ALL-NONZERO SOURCE-TRANSMUTED DIVISOR-GRAPH FORM OF OSC AND ITS MINIMAL SUPPLIER.

Fix C>=1 and Q>=2. Let A be a nonzero integer with |A|<=Q^C. Let real scales H,V,P satisfy
  2<=H<=Q^(1/3),  2<=V<H,  P=QH/V.                          (1)
Let cal L be a finite set. For each lambda in cal L, let I_lambda be an integer interval contained either in [H,2H) or in (-2H,-H]. For every lambda, integer V<=v<2V, and prime P<=p<2P with gcd(v,p)=1, let cal X_{lambda,v,p} be a finite set of integer triples x=(q,m,k) satisfying
  Q<=q,m<2Q,  qm+vpk=A,  gcd(qm,vp)=1.                      (2)
For h in I_lambda let
  c_{lambda,v,p,h}(q,m,k)
be a complex function on integer triples, extended by zero off cal X_{lambda,v,p}, and assume
  |c_{lambda,v,p,h}(q,m,k)|<=B.                             (3)
Thus c may retain arbitrary projective coefficients, smooth factors, forced small-v graph factors, and zero-one source masks. Define e_q(t)=exp(2 pi i t/q), put epsilon_1=epsilon_2=1 and epsilon_3=epsilon_4=-1, and write z^{[1]}=z and z^{[-1]}=conjugate(z).

For four q-variables and heights define
  Delta_h=sum_{i=1}^4 epsilon_i h_i product_{j!=i}q_j.       (4)
Define the all-nonzero hard-source OSC contribution
  T_OSC^nz
  =sum_{lambda in cal L}
    sum_{V<=v<2V}
    sum_{P<=p<2P, p prime, gcd(v,p)=1}
    sum_{h_i in I_lambda, h_1+h_2=h_3+h_4}
    sum_{x_i=(q_i,m_i,k_i) in cal X_{lambda,v,p},
         vk_i nonzero for every i,
         Delta_h nonzero,
         p does not divide A Delta_h}
      product_{i=1}^4 c_{lambda,v,p,h_i}(q_i,m_i,k_i)^{[epsilon_i]}
      product_{i=1}^4 e_{q_i}(epsilon_i h_i k_i).            (5)

For each prime p and each outer choice q_i,m_i for which p divides A-q_i m_i, put
  ell_i=(A-q_i m_i)/p,
and, when all ell_i are nonzero, put
  g_p=gcd(|ell_1|,|ell_2|,|ell_3|,|ell_4|).
Then exactly
  T_OSC^nz
  =sum_{lambda in cal L}
    sum_{P<=p<2P, p prime}
    sum_{h_i in I_lambda, h_1+h_2=h_3+h_4}
    sum_{Q<=q_i,m_i<2Q:
         p divides A-q_i m_i for every i,
         ell_i nonzero for every i,
         Delta_h nonzero,
         p does not divide A Delta_h}
      sum_{V<=v<2V:
           v divides g_p,
           gcd(v,p)=1}
        product_{i=1}^4
          c_{lambda,v,p,h_i}(q_i,m_i,ell_i/v)^{[epsilon_i]}
        product_{i=1}^4 e_{q_i}(epsilon_i h_i ell_i/v).      (6)
Every support condition in (5) is retained exactly in (6), because c is zero off cal X_{lambda,v,p}.

For fixed lambda,p,h_i,q_i,m_i in (6), the eligible common v-values are divisors of g_p. In particular, if any additional original v-weight is bounded by a fixed generalized divisor function, its weighted l1 assembly is O_{C,J,epsilon}(Q^epsilon) for every fixed J>=1 and epsilon>0, by fact 5a334011a0da2a70.

Assume explicitly that for every delta>0,
  B^4 #cal L <<_delta Q^delta.                              (7)
Facts ad79e2b004abf5ec and 02510b4e3b1c1fc3 pay the complete hard-source diagonal and every hard-source tuple with at least one zero cofactor. Therefore, for every epsilon>0, the single remaining hard-source assertion
  |T_OSC^nz| <<_{C,epsilon} Q^epsilon P^2 Q^(7/3)           (8)
is sufficient for the full hard-source fourth moment at the same target. Formula (6) and this sufficiency reduction do not prove (8), PMD closure, or Goldbach.
670a97b5f2366250.proof:
Fact db067f4633c13fed proves on every atom satisfying (2) that the original reciprocal source phase equals
  e_q(Ah(vp)^(-1))=e_q(hk).
Thus a literal coefficient may be written in the form used in (5) by factoring out this unit phase; all remaining factors are included in c. The OSC restriction is exactly
  Delta_h!=0,  p does not divide A Delta_h
by fact ad79e2b004abf5ec.

For each of the four source atoms, fact 5a334011a0da2a70 gives the bijection
  ell_i=vk_i=(A-q_i m_i)/p,
  p divides A-q_i m_i,
  v divides ell_i,
  k_i=ell_i/v.                                               (9)
On the all-nonzero sector, a common positive v divides all four ell_i if and only if it divides
  g_p=gcd(|ell_1|,|ell_2|,|ell_3|,|ell_4|).                  (10)

Apply (9) simultaneously to the four atom sums in (5), then move the v-sum inside the p,q_i,m_i sums. Substitute k_i=ell_i/v in the coefficients and phases. The two conjugated atoms contribute
  conjugate(c e_q(hk))=conjugate(c)e_q(-hk),
which is exactly the epsilon notation in (6). This proves that every term of (5) appears once in (6).

Conversely, every term in (6) has p|(A-q_i m_i), v|ell_i, and k_i=ell_i/v. Equation (9) reconstructs
  q_i m_i+vp k_i=A.
The zero extension of c ensures x_i belongs to the original cal X_{lambda,v,p}, including every mask encoded in that support. Hence every term of (6) appears once in (5), proving the exact identity.

The divisor-assembly statement follows directly from (10) and the weighted divisor estimate in fact 5a334011a0da2a70. It controls only the eligible v-values, not the correlated outer sum.

Finally, fact ad79e2b004abf5ec decomposes the hard-source fourth moment into the paid exact-slope/MOD diagonal and OSC. Fact 02510b4e3b1c1fc3 pays the part of OSC with at least one zero cofactor. Under (7), those bounds lie within Q^epsilon P^2Q^(7/3) after renaming epsilon. The only remaining term is therefore (5), equivalently (6), so assumption (8) supplies the full hard-source target. No proof of (8) is used or claimed.

glossary.T_OSC^nz: The hard-source OSC contribution restricted to four nonzero source cofactors.
glossary.c_{lambda,v,p,h}: A source-supported coefficient after the exact source phase e_q(hk) is factored out.
glossary.g_p: The gcd of the four nonzero source cofactors for a fixed prime p.

672108cb6ea6f2ca.title: NATURAL C2 PRIME-CELL PARTITION, RECTANGULAR CAPTURE, AND DIAGONAL DECODER INTERFACE
672108cb6ea6f2ca.author: slava chan
672108cb6ea6f2ca.statement:
NATURAL C2 PRIME-CELL PARTITION, RECTANGULAR CAPTURE, AND DIAGONAL DECODER INTERFACE.

Assume the literal h-symmetric C2 source hypotheses of fact 707345f56faff29e. Thus
0<kappa<1/100,  0<eta<=kappa/12,
D<=x^(1/2+eta),  R<=x^(7/12-kappa),
Z_0=x^(3/4-4eta)/R,
and every active rough prime lies in [Z_0,2R]. Let K_cell be the least positive integer such that
(3/2)^(K_cell)Z_0>=2R.
For 0<=i<K_cell put
Y_i=(3/2)^i Z_0,
mathcal P_i={p prime:Y_i<=p<Y_{i+1}},
and
H_i=floor(Y_i^(1/2)).                                        (1)

(A) For all sufficiently large x, the sets mathcal P_i are a fixed phase-independent half-open partition of the active rough primes,
K_cell=O(log x),                                              (2)
and every cell is contained in one accepted common-cell interval:
mathcal P_i subset [H_i^2,2H_i^2).                            (3)

Let c_z be the complete literal phased atom of fact 42104ea7b4b24b0b, let mathcal L be the retained h-symmetric C2 family, and put
T_C2=sum_{z in mathcal L}c_z.
This sum is absolutely convergent. For 0<=i<=j<K_cell, let mathcal L_ij consist of the labels whose unordered two-prime rough support has one prime in mathcal P_i and one in mathcal P_j, and put
T_ij=sum_{z in mathcal L_ij}c_z.
Then every T_ij is absolutely convergent and real, and
T_C2=sum_{0<=i<=j<K_cell}T_ij.                               (4)
If A>0 and T_C2<=-A, some rectangular cell satisfies
T_ij<=-2A/[K_cell(K_cell+1)].                                (5)

(B) Put
T_diag=sum_iT_ii,    T_off=sum_{i<j}T_ij.
Then
T_diag=T_C2-T_off.                                           (6)
For every B>0,
T_diag<=-B  if and only if  T_off>=T_C2+B.                   (7)
In particular, if 0<=rho<A and T_off>=-rho, then some diagonal cell satisfies
T_ii<=-(A-rho)/K_cell.                                       (8)

No such diagonal conclusion follows from (4) and h-symmetry alone. The finite abstract model with one real conjugate h,-h pair of total coefficient -A supported in one off-diagonal cell has T_C2=-A and every T_ii=0. This is not a literal-source construction and uses no phase-adaptive deletion.

(C) Fix a diagonal cell i satisfying
T_ii<=-A_i
for some A_i>0. Regard mathcal L_ii as a zero-one restriction of the original source and let E_comp,i be the complement quantity of fact 707345f56faff29e for this restriction. If
A_i^2>2E_comp,i,                                             (9)
then the support-disjoint full-rough-conductor carrier of that fact satisfies
Re(F_4,i)>=A_i^2-E_comp,i>=A_i^2/2.                          (10)
Every rough prime in F_4,i lies in [H_i^2,2H_i^2).

Group the short full-conductor selected source in F_4,i by its active semiprime supports G, with coefficients gamma_G and kappa_G=phi(G)/G as in the labelwise-short extension aa5909e2714da395. Then the scalar carrier in (10) is exactly
F_4,i=sum_{G,G' active;gcd(G,G')=1}
       alpha_{G,G'}gamma_Ggamma_G',
alpha_{G,G'}=kappa_Gkappa_G'.                                (11)
For each ordered coprime pair (G,G'), let mathcal E_{G,G'} and N_E(G,G') be the eligible common-cell decoder samples from facts dcabcf2f566b5721 and aa5909e2714da395, and define the labelled copy coefficient
d_{G,G',bold c}
 =alpha_{G,G'}gamma_Ggamma_G'/N_E(G,G')
for bold c in mathcal E_{G,G'}. Then
F_4,i=sum_{G,G';gcd(G,G')=1}
      sum_{bold c in mathcal E_{G,G'}}d_{G,G',bold c}.        (12)
For each fixed ordered pair,
N_E(G,G')>>H_i^4/(log(2H_i))^2,
and the map from bold c to its decoder coordinates (m,C_dec,K_dec) is injective already in (m,C_dec). Thus (12) preserves the total scalar only after all eligible copies are summed. It gives no conclusion that one fixed decoder fibre captures a positive proportion of (10), and it gives no norm or cancellation estimate after different support pairs with equal decoder coordinates are aggregated.

Fact 7c1f38cfbb8d0569 supplies an earlier independent obstruction: a negative total high-source anomaly and the terminal anatomy partition do not force a negative C2 total. The present theorem starts only after such a C2 deficit is assumed. It proves no lower bound for the natural T_off, no rectangular decoder theorem, no phase-adaptive deletion theorem, no varying-fibre analytic estimate, no common-cell or cross-cell cancellation bound, no four-prime equivalence, and no Goldbach implication.
672108cb6ea6f2ca.proof:
On the dyadic support used in facts d8ba46800ba433c2 and 707345f56faff29e, b_z<=2R. Since b_z=v_zp_zq_z with v_z a positive integer, every active rough prime is at most 2R; the C2 restriction gives the lower bound Z_0. Hence the half-open intervals in (1), up to the first endpoint at least 2R, partition all active rough primes. Their definitions use only prime size and are independent of h and every source phase.

The scale hypotheses give
Z_0>=x^(3/4-4eta-(7/12-kappa))
 =x^(1/6+kappa-4eta).
Because eta<=kappa/12, this tends to infinity. Thus Z_0>=64 for sufficiently large x. From the definition of the least positive K_cell,
K_cell<=1+max(0,log(2R/Z_0)/log(3/2)).
Since R<=x^(7/12) and Z_0>1, this is O(log x), proving (2), including the case of an empty active family with 2R<Z_0.

Fix i. Since H_i=floor(sqrt(Y_i)),
H_i^2<=Y_i.
Also H_i>=sqrt(Y_i)-1, so
2H_i^2>=2Y_i-4sqrt(Y_i)+2.
For Y_i>=64, the right side is at least (3/2)Y_i=Y_{i+1}. Therefore
[Y_i,Y_{i+1}) subset [H_i^2,2H_i^2),
which proves (3).

Fact d8ba46800ba433c2 gives
sum_{z in mathcal L}|c_z|<<DR(log x)^2,
because every phase has modulus one. Thus T_C2 and every T_ij converge absolutely. Truncate the family symmetrically to |h|<=Q for a positive integer Q. Compact support leaves finitely many remaining indices, so fact 42ae728764073a1a applies to each truncation and proves its real cell-pair decomposition and identities. Let Q tend to infinity. Absolute convergence preserves the identities and inequalities, while h-symmetry makes every limiting T_ij real. This proves (4). The finite number K_cell(K_cell+1)/2 of real cell sums then gives (5) by the same signed pigeonhole argument. Equations (6)-(8) follow by rearranging the absolutely convergent finite cell decomposition, exactly as in fact 42ae728764073a1a. Its abstract off-diagonal model proves the stated counterpressure.

Now fix the diagonal restriction mathcal L_ii. It is obtained solely by a phase-independent zero-one deletion and remains h-symmetric. Under (9), fact 707345f56faff29e applies with A_0=A_i and gives (10). Every selected source support has both rough primes in mathcal P_i. The carrier in (10) pairs two support-disjoint selected sources, so all four rough primes lie in mathcal P_i and hence in the common interval (3).

The carrier F_4,i of fact 707345f56faff29e is formed from its short-frequency full-conductor labels, which satisfy
|h|<Z_0<=p,q.
Hence every such label satisfies the labelwise-short condition |h|<min(p,q). Fact aa5909e2714da395 therefore applies in the common cell [H_i^2,2H_i^2), including i=0 without requiring Z_0<=H_i^2. Its fixed-semiprime grouping proves (11). The cell mathcal P_i may be a proper subset of the common interval; this is only an additional zero-one prime selector.

For sufficiently large x, H_i is sufficiently large for fact dcabcf2f566b5721. The decoder-copy part of fact aa5909e2714da395, extending the identities of fact d016de3f6c03e65c, defines exactly d_{G,G',bold c}, proves
sum_{bold c in mathcal E_{G,G'}}d_{G,G',bold c}
 =alpha_{G,G'}gamma_Ggamma_G',
gives the displayed lower bound for N_E, and proves fixed-support injectivity already in (m,C_dec). Summing its scalar identity over the ordered pairs proves (12). Therefore each fixed-pair scalar is distributed among many distinct decoder fibres. The accepted facts make no injectivity claim after (G,G') is forgotten and no estimate for aggregating equal coordinates across different pairs. Hence neither one-fibre capture nor varying-fibre cancellation follows from (12).

Finally, fact 7c1f38cfbb8d0569 proves that total sign and the terminal anatomy partition alone cannot select C2. All other final assertions record operations absent from the proof.

glossary.E_comp,i: The complement quantity from fact 707345f56faff29e for the i-th diagonal restriction.
glossary.F_4,i: The routed support-disjoint full-conductor carrier for the i-th diagonal restriction.
glossary.H_i: The integer floor of sqrt(Y_i) whose common-cell interval contains mathcal P_i.
glossary.K_cell: The number of natural half-open rough-prime size cells.
glossary.K_dec: The auxiliary decoder determinant parameter attached to one importance-sampled copy.
glossary.Y_i: The lower endpoint (3/2)^i Z_0 of the i-th natural cell.
glossary.mathcal P_i: The i-th natural half-open rough-prime size cell.

674a62f128f05a44.title: CHARACTER-DEPENDENT SLOPE DIAGONALIZATION WITH AN EXACT SMALL-COMMON-DIVISOR CUTOFF. Let p>2 be prime, let G>1 be real, and let \(\mathcal S,\mathcal Q\) be finite sets of positive integers coprime to p. For \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(q\in\mathcal Q\), let \(X_s,Y_q:\mathbb F_p^\times\to\mathbb C\). For a multiplicative character \(\chi\) of \(\mathbb F_p^\times\), define
674a62f128f05a44.author: slava chan
674a62f128f05a44.proof:
For any functions X,Y on \(\mathbb F_p^\times\), the definition (2) gives
\[
 \sum_{f,g}G_c(f,g)X(f)Y(g)
 ={p\over p-1}\left(\sum_fX(f)Y(cf)
 -{1\over p-1}\sum_fX(f)\sum_gY(g)\right).\tag{8}
\]
Multiplicative Fourier inversion in the convention (1) is
\[
 Y(g)={1\over p-1}\sum_\chi\widehat Y(\chi)\chi(g).\tag{9}
\]
It follows that
\[
 \sum_fX(f)Y(cf)
 ={1\over p-1}\sum_\chi
 \chi(c)\widehat X(\overline\chi)\widehat Y(\chi).\tag{10}
\]
The principal-character term in (10) is
\[
 {1\over p-1}\sum_fX(f)\sum_gY(g),
\]
so it is exactly cancelled by the second term of (8). Hence
\[
 \sum_{f,g}G_c(f,g)X(f)Y(g)
 ={p\over(p-1)^2}\sum_{\chi\ne\chi_0}
 \chi(c)\widehat X(\overline\chi)\widehat Y(\chi).\tag{11}
\]
Apply (11) to every pair \((X_s,Y_q)\) in (5) and interchange finite sums. The inner sum at fixed character is precisely (3), proving (6).

For every positive integer n,
\[
 \sum_{h\mid n}\kappa_G(h)
 =\sum_{h\mid n}\sum_{\substack{d\mid h\\d<G}}\mu(h/d)
 =\sum_{\substack{d\mid n\\d<G}}\sum_{r\mid n/d}\mu(r)
 =\mathbf1_{n<G}.\tag{12}
\]
Indeed, the inner Möbius sum vanishes unless \(n/d=1\). Take \(n=(s,q)\) in (12) and insert it into the first formula in (3). Since
\[
 \chi(sq^{-1})=\chi(s)\overline{\chi(q)},
\]
the s- and q-sums separate for every h, giving (7). The final scope statement follows from the definitions: dependence on chi occurs through the two Fourier projections in (3), while fact a3829b00a5a4b238 concerns scalar coefficients multiplying common kernels.

glossary.\\Lambda_G(\\chi): The nonprincipal slope transform in the range gcd(s,q)<G.
glossary.\\kappa_G(h): The exact Möbius coefficient implementing the strict common-divisor cutoff.
glossary.\\lambda_c(\\chi): The slope-c weight after the two row vectors have been projected to multiplicative-character mode chi.
glossary.\\mathcal K_G: The centered two-row slope aggregate restricted by gcd(s,q)<G.

676c6a2cb3ebf7cc.title: Let 𝒵 be the finite set of labelled incidences in fact 91db48815d136d4c, partitioned there into the six cells 𝒵_C, 𝒵_11, 𝒵_21, 𝒵_22, 𝒵_asym, and 𝒵_U. For every z∈𝒵 fix an integer q_z>1, a finite set J_z, complex coefficients z_{z,j}, and integer phase labels x_{z,j}. For every divisor e of q_z and residue v modulo e define
676c6a2cb3ebf7cc.author: slava chan
676c6a2cb3ebf7cc.statement:
Let 𝒵 be the finite set of labelled incidences in fact 91db48815d136d4c, partitioned there into the six cells 𝒵_C, 𝒵_11, 𝒵_21, 𝒵_22, 𝒵_asym, and 𝒵_U. For every z∈𝒵 fix an integer q_z>1, a finite set J_z, complex coefficients z_{z,j}, and integer phase labels x_{z,j}. For every divisor e of q_z and residue v modulo e define
F_{z,e}(v)=Σ_{j∈J_z} z_{z,j} exp(2πivx_{z,j}/e),
C_z(e)=Σ_{v (mod e)}|F_{z,e}(v)|^4,
S_z=Σ_{j∈J_z}z_{z,j},
\widetilde C_z(e)=C_z(e)-|S_z|^4,
and
P_z(q_z)=Σ_{a (mod q_z),(a,q_z)=1}|F_{z,q_z}(a)|^4.
Let a_z be arbitrary complex provenance coefficients. For each parent cell X∈{C,11,21,22,asym,U}, define
T_X=Σ_{z∈𝒵_X}a_z P_z(q_z).
Then
T_X=Σ_{z∈𝒵_X}a_z Σ_{e|q_z} μ(q_z/e)\widetilde C_z(e)
for every X. Thus centered signed quotient-conductor descent can be performed independently inside each controlled, endpoint-anatomy, or nonendpoint parent cell, without moving an incidence between cells: its common zero mode has net coefficient zero, every proper reduced conductor cancels, and only the primitive conductor q_z remains. By contrast, if S_z≠0 then the unsigned raw sum Σ_{e|q_z}C_z(e) contains the same zero-mode term |S_z|^4 once for each divisor of q_z and therefore is not a disjoint conductor refinement of that incidence.
676c6a2cb3ebf7cc.proof:
Fix z∈𝒵. Apply fact b02d45f4a07a5524 with q=q_z, J=J_z, coefficients z_j=z_{z,j}, and phases x_j=x_{z,j}. It gives the exact identity
P_z(q_z)=Σ_{e|q_z}μ(q_z/e)\widetilde C_z(e).
It also proves that the common term |S_z|^4 cancels because Σ_{e|q_z}μ(q_z/e)=0, and that after the centered moments are decomposed by reduced additive conductor, Möbius inversion gives coefficient zero to every proper conductor and coefficient one to q_z.

Multiply the displayed identity by the arbitrary coefficient a_z and sum over z in one fixed parent cell 𝒵_X. All sums are finite, so their order may be interchanged. This proves the formula for T_X. Since no term with index z is assigned to a parent cell other than the unique one supplied by fact 91db48815d136d4c, conductor descent preserves the six-way incidence partition and all provenance carried by a_z.

Finally, fact b02d45f4a07a5524 gives C_z(e)≥|S_z|^4 for every e|q_z. Hence Σ_{e|q_z}C_z(e)≥τ(q_z)|S_z|^4, although the exact signed coefficient of this common term is zero. This proves that the raw unsigned quotient moments cannot be interpreted as disjoint conductor states.

glossary.C_z(e): the complete fourth moment of incidence z at quotient modulus e
glossary.F_{z,e}(v): the additive Fourier sum of incidence z at quotient modulus e
glossary.J_z: the finite Fourier coefficient index set attached to incidence z
glossary.P_z(q_z): the primitive unit-residue fourth moment at conductor q_z
glossary.S_z: the common zero-frequency sum for incidence z
glossary.T_X: the primitive-conductor aggregate inside parent cell X
glossary.\\widetilde C_z(e): the centered complete fourth moment of incidence z at quotient modulus e
glossary.a_z: an arbitrary provenance coefficient attached to incidence z
glossary.q_z: the primitive additive conductor attached to incidence z
glossary.x_{z,j}: the integer phase label j attached to incidence z
glossary.z_{z,j}: the complex Fourier coefficient j attached to incidence z
glossary.𝒵: the finite labelled-incidence set partitioned in fact 91db48815d136d4c
glossary.𝒵_C: the controlled parent cell of labelled incidences

67d49768ecdc058e.title: C4 PRIME-LOCAL SQUARE-DIVISOR EXCEPTIONAL SYSTEM AND NATURAL-FREQUENCY SAME-ROW DIAGONAL
67d49768ecdc058e.author: slava chan
67d49768ecdc058e.statement:
C4 PRIME-LOCAL SQUARE-DIVISOR EXCEPTIONAL SYSTEM AND NATURAL-FREQUENCY SAME-ROW DIAGONAL.

Fix the literal top-sliver C4 setting of facts e58fc7c00f1683e6 and 9bee61f3627bd506. Thus
beta_m<=beta<6/5,   B=Q^beta,   H_T=B/Q,
Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma),   H_P=H_T/G,
G>=Q^(-sigma+eta),                                                     (1)
where 0<eta<sigma. Let
n=dv,   d=p_1p_2p_3p_4                                                 (2)
be one C4 marked row, and let p be a selected nonresonant prime dividing d. Write d=pm. On a natural frequency block
F<=|h|<2F,   F<=C_F H_P                                                (3)
with fixed C_F, the local cofactor in the prime-p slope of fact 79e2c44e5110d7a0 is
vm=n/p.                                                               (4)

Consider two C4 rows (n,h) and (n',h') that share the same selected prime p and the same fixed target coordinate A. Assume p does not divide A and that the designated frequencies are nonzero modulo p. Then A is a common unit multiplier in the two local slopes. Their prime-local mixed-Fourier Gram has order-one exceptional energy exactly when
p^2 divides h n'-h'n.                                                  (5)
Off (5), its exact Gram has magnitude at most 2/p, as in fact 3d10fd30e2a42246.

The exceptional system has the following two exact specializations.

(i) If n=n', then (5) is equivalent to h=h' for all sufficiently large Q.

(ii) Put E=h n'-h'n. If E!=0, the number of primes p that can satisfy (5) for this fixed ordered row pair is at most tau(|E|), hence is Q^epsilon by fact e705401df9f0709e. If E=0, the total number of ordered integer quadruples
(n,h,n',h')
with
B/2<=n,n'<=2B,   F<=|h|,|h'|<2F                                    (6)
is
O(BF log(2F)).                                                         (7)
The bound remains valid after imposing p|n, p|n' and all literal C4 masks.

These are unweighted incidence statements. They do not bound a literal weighted slope-class amplitude, compare rows whose selected primes differ or whose target coordinates differ, sum the nonempty centered CRT faces, prove NR-DIL, or imply Goldbach.
67d49768ecdc058e.proof:
Fact 79e2c44e5110d7a0 states that, after writing d=pm and n=dv, the prime-p slope attached to a designated nonzero frequency h is
A h(vm)^(-1) modulo p,                                                 (8)
where the fixed target A is a common unit and may be cancelled only between rows with that same target coordinate. In C4, (2) gives
vm=v(d/p)=n/p,                                                         (9)
which is a unit modulo p because n is squarefree. For a second row sharing both p and A, the exceptional congruence from that fact is therefore
A h(n'/p)=A h'(n/p) modulo p.                                         (10)
Cancel the common unit A. Both n and n' are divisible by p exactly once. Multiplying the resulting congruence by p gives
h n'=h'n modulo p^2.
Conversely, division by p in this integer congruence recovers (10) after multiplying by A. This proves (5). The off-exceptional Gram bound is exactly the off-slope case of fact 3d10fd30e2a42246.

If n=n', then (10) reduces to h=h' modulo p because A(n/p) is a unit. From (1),
Z/H_P=G Q^(5/2-2beta-3sigma)
 >=Q^(5/2-2beta-4sigma+eta).                                         (11)
Since beta<6/5 and sigma<=10^(-4), the exponent on the right is greater than 1/10-4sigma+eta>0. Thus Z/H_P tends to infinity. Because p>=Z and (3) holds, p>4F for all sufficiently large Q. The two signed integers h,h' satisfy |h-h'|<4F<p, so their congruence modulo p implies h=h'. This proves (i).

For E!=0, every prime satisfying (5) has p^2|E and in particular p|E. The number of such primes is at most tau(|E|). Equations (1), (3), and (6) give
H_P<=Q^(beta-1+sigma-eta),
|E|<=|h|n'+|h'|n
 <8 C_F H_P B
 <=8 C_F Q^(2beta-1+sigma-eta)
 <=8 C_F Q^(7/5+sigma).                                             (12)
Thus |E| is bounded by a fixed power of Q. Fact e705401df9f0709e states uniformly that tau(u)<<Q^epsilon for positive integers u bounded by a fixed power of Q, after choosing its parameters accordingly. It therefore gives the asserted Q^epsilon bound for the number of possible p.

It remains to count E=0. Let g_0=gcd(n,n') and write
n=g_0a,   n'=g_0b,   gcd(a,b)=1.                                   (13)
The equation hn'=h'n becomes hb=h'a. Coprimality in (13) gives
h=at,   h'=bt                                                       (14)
for a nonzero signed integer t. The dyadic n,n' conditions force a and b to be comparable within an absolute factor. For u=max(a,b), there are at most 8u ordered pairs (a,b) with this comparability. For each such pair, (6) allows at most 1+2B/u values of g_0 and at most 1+2F/u values of t. Whenever a term is nonempty, u<=2B and u<=2F, so these quantities are at most 5B/u and 5F/u respectively. Hence the total is at most a fixed constant times
sum_{1<=u<=2F} u(B/u)(F/u)
 <=BF(1+log(2F)),                                                   (15)
which proves (7). Extra divisibility and literal masks only remove quadruples. This proves all assertions.

glossary.C4 square-divisor exceptional system: The same-target prime-local collision condition p^2|h n'-h'n for two C4 rows sharing p.
glossary.E: The C4 cross-row determinant h n'-h'n.

67ebf7acc95b59b6.title: EXACT NONUNIT-FREQUENCY RESIDUE COLLAPSE FOR THE DISJOINT PMLS NORMAL FORM. Assume the notation of fact 18a0de57eaf35171, but allow a descended modulus equal to one with the following conventions: G_1 has one element, phi(1)=1, and T_{1,c} is the identity on C. Let r be squarefree, let d divide r, put s=r/d, and define the normalized residue-collapse map C_{r,d}:l2(G_r)->l2(G_s) by
67ebf7acc95b59b6.author: slava chan
67ebf7acc95b59b6.statement:
EXACT NONUNIT-FREQUENCY RESIDUE COLLAPSE FOR THE DISJOINT PMLS NORMAL FORM. Assume the notation of fact 18a0de57eaf35171, but allow a descended modulus equal to one with the following conventions: G_1 has one element, phi(1)=1, and T_{1,c} is the identity on C. Let r be squarefree, let d divide r, put s=r/d, and define the normalized residue-collapse map C_{r,d}:l2(G_r)->l2(G_s) by
(C_{r,d}f)(y)=phi(d)^(-1/2) sum_{x in G_r; x congruent y (mod s)}f(x).       (1)
Then
||C_{r,d}f||_2<=||f||_2.                                                   (2)
Let r,r'>1 be coprime squarefree integers, let t be an integer, put
d=(t,r), e=(t,r'), s=r/d, s'=r'/e,                                        (3)
where each gcd is taken with an integer representative of t. For the two local transforms in equation (5) of fact 18a0de57eaf35171 one has exactly
Kcal_{r,c,h}f(t(r')^{-1})
=mu(d) sqrt(phi(d))/d
 (T_{s,c}C_{r,d}f)(h(t/d)(r'd)^{-1}),                                    (4)
Kcal_{r',c',h}g(-tr^{-1})
=mu(e) sqrt(phi(e))/e
 (T_{s',c'}C_{r',e}g)(-h(t/e)(re)^{-1}),                                 (5)
where the inverses and evaluations on the right of (4) and (5) are taken modulo s and s', respectively. Thus the (d,e) completion stratum has the exact scalar attenuation
lambda_{d,e}=mu(d)mu(e)sqrt(phi(d)phi(e))/(de),                            (6)
and
|lambda_{d,e}|<=(de)^(-1/2).                                               (7)
The hard unit-frequency stratum is d=e=1. Equations (4)--(7) are exact local conductor descent and norm contraction only; they do not sum the nonunit strata or prove the C4 PMLS operator bound.
67ebf7acc95b59b6.proof:
Each residue y in G_s has exactly phi(d) lifts x in G_r, because r=ds is squarefree and (d,s)=1. By Cauchy--Schwarz on each fibre,
|(C_{r,d}f)(y)|^2
<=sum_{x in G_r;x=y (mod s)}|f(x)|^2.
Summing over y proves (2).

We prove (4). More generally, let a be any integer with (a,r)=d and let b be a unit modulo r. CRT factorization of the classical Kloosterman sum gives
S_r(a,b)
=S_d(a s^{-1},b s^{-1}) S_s(a d^{-1},b d^{-1}).                         (8)
The first additive coefficient in the d-factor is zero modulo d. Since b s^{-1} is a unit and d is squarefree,
S_d(0,b s^{-1})=sum_{u in G_d}e_d(b s^{-1}u^{-1})=mu(d).                 (9)
In the s-factor, a d^{-1} is a unit. The substitution in the Kloosterman sum which makes its first coefficient one yields
S_s(a d^{-1},b d^{-1})=S_s(1,ab d^{-2}).                                (10)
Here and below d^{-1},d^{-2} mean inverses modulo s. Combining (8)--(10), taking b=chx, and grouping x by its residue y modulo s gives
sum_{x in G_r}f(x)r^{-1}S_r(a,chx)
=mu(d)/d sum_{x in G_r}f(x)s^{-1}S_s(1,cx(ha d^{-2}))
=mu(d)sqrt(phi(d))/d (T_{s,c}C_{r,d}f)(ha d^{-2}).                       (11)
The formula also holds for s=1 by the stated conventions.

In the first local transform of fact 18a0de57eaf35171, a=t(r')^{-1} modulo r. Since d=(t,r) and r' is a unit modulo r, (a,r)=d; moreover
a d^{-2} congruent (t/d)(r'd)^{-1} (mod s).
Substitution in (11) proves (4). Applying the same argument with r', e, s', and a=-tr^{-1} proves (5). Multiplication gives (6). Finally phi(d)<=d and phi(e)<=e imply (7).

glossary.C_{r,d}: the normalized residue-collapse contraction from l2(G_r) to l2(G_{r/d})
glossary.lambda_{d,e}: the exact product attenuation in the completion stratum with gcds d and e

6836789040c87b6f.title: SAME-GAUGE FINITE-BAND q_0-PRINCIPAL LIFT AND RAMANUJAN LEDGER
6836789040c87b6f.author: slava chan
6836789040c87b6f.statement:
SAME-GAUGE FINITE-BAND q_0-PRINCIPAL LIFT AND RAMANUJAN LEDGER.
