Fix constants C>=1 and J>=3. Let Q>=2, let A be a nonzero integer with |A|<=Q^C, and for every positive integer q with Q<=q<2Q put
  d_q=gcd(|A|,q),  q_0(q)=q/d_q.                            (1)
For r>=1 let X(r) be the group of Dirichlet characters modulo r, with the one-element convention when r=1. Put
  e_r(x)=exp(2 pi i x/r),  e_1(x)=1,
and for chi in X(r) define
  G_{r,h}(chi)=sum_{u modulo r, gcd(u,r)=1}
                 e_r(hu) conjugate(chi(u)).                 (2)
Then, for every integer t with gcd(t,r)=1,
  e_r(ht)=phi(r)^(-1)sum_{chi in X(r)}G_{r,h}(chi)chi(t).    (3)
For the principal character chi_0 modulo r,
  G_{r,h}(chi_0)=c_r(h),                                    (4)
where c_r(h) is the Ramanujan sum. If h is nonzero and g=gcd(r,|h|), then
  |c_r(h)|/phi(r)=|mu(r/g)|/phi(r/g).                       (5)
In particular, when gcd(h,r)=1, the principal coefficient in (3) is
  mu(r)/phi(r).                                              (6)

Uniformly for nonzero integers h with |h|<=Q^C and every epsilon>0,
  sum_{Q<=q<2Q}
    tau(q_0(q)) |c_{q_0(q)}(h)|/phi(q_0(q))
  <<_{C,epsilon} Q^epsilon.                                 (7)
Consequently, let n,M,H_0,L be positive real numbers with H_0=n/M>=1. For every q in [Q,2Q) let w_{q,h}, h nonzero, be complex numbers satisfying
  |w_{q,h}|<=C_J(L/H_0)(1+|h|/H_0)^(-J),                   (8)
and supported on |h|<=Q^C. If alpha_{q,h} are arbitrary complex numbers satisfying
  |alpha_{q,h}|<=tau(q_0(q)),                               (9)
then the complete q_0-principal part of the same-gauge lift obeys
  sum_{h nonzero} |
    sum_{Q<=q<2Q} alpha_{q,h}w_{q,h}
      c_{q_0(q)}(h)/phi(q_0(q)) |
  <<_{C,J,epsilon} C_J L Q^epsilon.                         (10)
The same bound holds after any deletion of nonzero h-values, including a finite dyadic band.

In the gcd-reduced source notation of fact 7670948dedd78714, r=q_0, t=k/d_q and gcd(t,q_0)=1, so (3) is an exact multiplicative-character lift of the literal phase e_{q_0}(ht) in the same gauge. Equations (7)-(10) pay the q_0-principal character, including a divisor-sized lift/provenance multiplicity. They do not yield a factor H_0^(-1): the H_0^(-1) pointwise scale in (8) is exactly consumed when the H_0 relevant frequencies are summed. The nonprincipal characters reconstruct the remainder of the original nonzero band. Therefore this result supplies no bound for the all-nonzero OSC term T_OSC^nz of fact 670a97b5f2366250 and no PMD or Goldbach conclusion.
6836789040c87b6f.proof:
Orthogonality of the characters of the finite abelian group (Z/rZ)^* gives
  phi(r)^(-1)sum_{chi in X(r)}
    conjugate(chi(u))chi(t)=1_{u congruent t (mod r)}
for units u,t. Multiplying by e_r(hu) and summing over units u proves (3). Taking chi=chi_0 in (2) gives (4).

The elementary Ramanujan-sum formula is
  c_r(h)=sum_{a|gcd(r,h)}a mu(r/a).                          (11)
Equivalently, if g=gcd(r,|h|), then
  c_r(h)=mu(r/g) phi(r)/phi(r/g)                             (12)
when mu(r/g) is nonzero, and both sides are zero otherwise. To see the equivalence directly, both sides are multiplicative in r for fixed h. For r=p^a, formula (11) is zero if p^(a-1) does not divide h, equals -p^(a-1) if p^(a-1) exactly divides h, and equals phi(p^a) if p^a divides h; this is exactly (12). Division by phi(r) proves (5), and g=1 proves (6).

We prove (7). Every q in the sum determines d=d_q and r=q_0(q), with
  d|A, q=dr, gcd(A/d,r)=1.                                  (13)
For this r put g=gcd(r,|h|) and s=r/g. By (5),
  tau(r)|c_r(h)|/phi(r)
  <=tau(g)tau(s)/phi(s)
  <=tau(|h|)tau(s)/phi(s).                                  (14)
For fixed d|A and g|h, relation q=dgs in [Q,2Q) restricts s to one dyadic interval
  Q/(dg)<=s<2Q/(dg).                                        (15)
Dropping the coprimality conditions can only enlarge the sum. The standard elementary divisor estimates, for every delta>0,
  tau(m)<<_delta m^delta,  m/phi(m)<<_delta m^delta,         (16)
give, for x>=1,
  sum_{x<=s<2x}tau(s)/phi(s)<<_delta x^(2delta),             (17)
and when x<1 the interval contains at most one positive integer relevant to (15), contributing O(1). Hence (13)-(17) give
  sum_{Q<=q<2Q}
    tau(r)|c_r(h)|/phi(r)
  <<_{delta} tau(|A|)tau(|h|)Q^(2delta).                    (18)
Since |A|,|h|<=Q^C, apply (16) to the two divisor counts and choose delta sufficiently small in terms of epsilon and C. This proves (7).

By the triangle inequality, (7), (8), and (9), the left side of (10) is at most
  C_{C,epsilon}Q^epsilon
  sum_{h nonzero}(C_JL/H_0)(1+|h|/H_0)^(-J).               (19)
Because H_0>=1 and J>=3, comparison with the integral of (1+x/H_0)^(-J) shows that the last sum is O_J(C_JL). This proves (10). Deleting h-values only decreases the absolute majorant.

Fact 7670948dedd78714 proves in its notation that d_q divides k, t=k/d_q is a unit modulo q_0, and e_q(hk)=e_{q_0}(ht); thus (3) applies without changing gauge. Its finite-band Fourier coefficients satisfy a bound of the form (8). The proof of (19) also shows why no H_0^(-1) survives. Character inversion (3) is exact, so after removing the principal summand, the remaining characters give exactly the nonprincipal remainder of the original phase. Fact 20609f1342ff4558 proves that the legal mask order leaves the original nonzero OSC unchanged. This proves all scope assertions.

glossary.G_{r,h}(chi): The multiplicative Fourier coefficient of the additive phase u maps to e_r(hu) on the unit group.
glossary.X(r): The finite group of Dirichlet characters modulo r.
glossary.c_r(h): The Ramanujan sum over units modulo r.
glossary.w_{q,h}: A generic literal finite-band coefficient satisfying the Poisson decay profile.

6951622549da0aa4.title: POWER-SAVING-SCALE SQUAREFUL CORRECTION FOR A SYMMETRIC LARGE-FACTOR HC-MED MARKING. Let X>=4, delta>=0, 0<eta<=1/4, and C>0. Put
6951622549da0aa4.author: slava chan
6951622549da0aa4.statement:
POWER-SAVING-SCALE SQUAREFUL CORRECTION FOR A SYMMETRIC LARGE-FACTOR HC-MED MARKING. Let X>=4, delta>=0, 0<eta<=1/4, and C>0. Put
Q_0=X^(1/2+delta),                                               (1)
and suppose
X^(2/5+6delta)(log X)^(2C)<=P
 <=X^(1/2-3delta)(log X)^(-C).                                  (2)
Let c_* be a positive integer. Let cal S be any set of distinct squarefree integers s in [Q_0,4Q_0), each coprime to c_*, and choose a unit residue a_s modulo s. Put
cal P={p prime:P<=p<2P},
omega_P(n)=#{p in cal P:p|n}.                                   (3)
For p in cal P and p|r, put A_p(r)=v_p(r)+1 and define
e_P^{rho}(p,r)
 =rho_{1/2}(r)[(A_p(r)-3/2)/(A_p(r)omega_P(r))
               +1/(2(1+omega_P(r)))].                           (4)
Let F_s(p,d,u) be arbitrary complex coefficients supported on
p in cal P, X^eta<=d<=X^(1/4+eta), u>=1,
X<=p^2du<2X, (pdu,c_*)=1,                                      (5)
and satisfying |F_s(p,d,u)|<=L_0. Define
Delta_s(n)=1_{n congruent a_s (mod s)}
 -phi(s)^(-1)1_{(n,s)=1},                                       (6)
and
E_s^{large}
 =2 sum_{p in cal P}sum_{d,u>=1}
 rho_{1/2}(d)e_P^{rho}(p,pu)F_s(p,d,u)Delta_s(p^2du),            (7)
where the support and unit restrictions in (5) are understood.

Then
sum_{s in cal S}|E_s^{large}|
 <<L_0(1+log(2XQ_0))^4[Q_0X/P^2+X/P],                           (8)
with an absolute implied constant. In particular, the bracket in (8) is at most
X^(7/10-11delta)(log X)^(-4C)
 +X^(3/5-6delta)(log X)^(-2C).                                  (9)
Thus (8) is L_0 times a fixed-power-saving scale relative to X. When F_s is the product of the two HC smooth cells and the complete literal amplitude, equation (7) is exactly the p|m' correction obtained by applying the fractional-Ramare identity to the large half-convolution factor m=pm', writing m'=pu and retaining the fundamental-domain weight 2 in the chamber eta<=3/20+6delta. No estimate for the unmarked omega_P(m)=0 sector or for any main row is asserted.
6951622549da0aa4.proof:
The definition (4) is exactly the correction coefficient of fact e59f666ecac4d4cb. Its proof gives
|e_P^{rho}(p,r)|<=5/4.                                          (10)
Fact 5999a1878276ac78 gives |rho_{1/2}(d)|<=1. Write w=du. For fixed p,w, the number of pairs d,u with du=w and d in the interval (5) is at most tau(w). All unit indicators have modulus at most one and |F_s|<=L_0. Therefore the absolute folded coefficient for p,w in (7) is at most
(5/2)L_0 tau(w).                                                 (11)
The support p^2w<2X gives
w<2X/P^2=:W.                                                     (12)

Consider the physical part of (6). A contributing pair obeys
p^2w congruent a_s (mod s).                                     (13)
Since a_s is a unit, (pw,s)=1. For fixed squarefree s and unit w, (13) is a square-root congruence for p. It has at most two roots modulo each odd prime dividing s and at most one modulo 2, hence at most 2^(omega(s)+1) residue classes modulo s. Equations (1)-(2) give
P/Q_0<=X^(-4delta)(log X)^(-C)<1,
so P<Q_0<=s. The half-open interval [P,2P) has length P<s; therefore each residue class modulo s contains at most one integer in that interval. Hence 2^(omega(s)+1) bounds the number of integers p in [P,2P) satisfying (13), uniformly with an absolute constant.

Elementary divisor summation gives
sum_{w<=W}tau(w)=sum_{ab<=W}1
 <=W sum_{a<=W}1/a<=W(1+log W).                                 (14)
Also 2^omega(s)<=tau(s), and
sum_{s in cal S}tau(s)
 <=sum_{n<=4Q_0}tau(n)
 =sum_{ab<=4Q_0}1
 <=4Q_0(1+log(4Q_0)).                                           (15)
Equations (11)-(15) bound the total physical contribution by
<<L_0 Q_0X/P^2(1+log(2XQ_0))^2.                                 (16)

For the principal part, discard all unit restrictions. There are at most 2P integers p in [P,2P), and (14) bounds the w-sum, so the total coefficient mass before the factor 1/phi(s) is
<<L_0 P W(1+log W)
 <<L_0 X/P(1+log W).                                            (17)
For squarefree s,
s/phi(s)
 =product_{l|s}(1-1/l)^(-1)
 <=product_{l|s}(1+1/l)^2
 =(sum_{e|s}1/e)^2
 <=(1+log s)^2.                                                  (18)
Since cal S consists of distinct s in [Q_0,4Q_0),
sum_{s in cal S}1/phi(s)
 =sum_s(s/phi(s))/s
 <<(1+log(4Q_0))^2.                                              (19)
Equations (17)-(19) bound the principal contribution by
<<L_0 X/P(1+log(2XQ_0))^3.                                      (20)
The common fourth logarithmic power in (8) contains (16) and (20).

Finally, (1)-(2) give
Q_0X/P^2
 <=X^(1/2+delta+1-4/5-12delta)(log X)^(-4C)
 =X^(7/10-11delta)(log X)^(-4C)
and
X/P<=X^(3/5-6delta)(log X)^(-2C),
which proves (9).

For the final identification, fact 6507639658c780d5 shows that eta<=3/20+6delta and (2) force p>d, so the fundamental-domain multiplicity is 2. Applying fact e59f666ecac4d4cb to rho_{1/2}(m), writing m=pm' and then m'=pu, gives p^2du as in (7); the remaining half-convolution coefficient is rho_{1/2}(d), and the literal smooth product is F_s. Hence (7) is exactly that correction under the displayed specialization.

glossary.A_p(r): The integer v_p(r)+1 used in the fractional-Ramare correction coefficient.
glossary.E_s^{large}: The squareful selected-prime correction after marking the large factor and writing m'=pu.
glossary.F_s(p,d,u): The complete retained smooth/literal amplitude in the correction, abstracted as an L_0-bounded coefficient.
glossary.L_0: A uniform absolute bound for F_s.
glossary.W: The correction cofactor ceiling 2X/P^2 after folding w=du.

697d75223ebc7a8a.title: Let I be a finite set. For each u in I let O_u be a subset of {1,2,3,4}, let H_u be a complex Hilbert space, and let v_u belong to H_u. Form the expanded Hilbert direct sum over pairs (u,F) with u in I and F a subset of O_u, and put v_{u,F}=(-1)^{|F|}v_u in the copy of H_u indexed by (u,F). Then
697d75223ebc7a8a.author: slava chan
697d75223ebc7a8a.statement:
Let I be a finite set. For each u in I let O_u be a subset of {1,2,3,4}, let H_u be a complex Hilbert space, and let v_u belong to H_u. Form the expanded Hilbert direct sum over pairs (u,F) with u in I and F a subset of O_u, and put v_{u,F}=(-1)^{|F|}v_u in the copy of H_u indexed by (u,F). Then
sum_{u in I}sum_{F subset O_u}||v_{u,F}||^2=sum_{u in I}2^{|O_u|}||v_u||^2<=16 sum_{u in I}||v_u||^2.
Consequently the norm of the complete one-unrestricted-plus-fifteen-overlap-face coefficient array is at most four times the norm of the base coefficient array. If only the nonempty correction faces are retained, then
sum_{u in I}sum_{empty different from F subset O_u}||v_{u,F}||^2=sum_{u in I}(2^{|O_u|}-1)||v_u||^2<=15 sum_{u in I}||v_u||^2,
so their coefficient norm is at most sqrt(15) times the base norm. Both constants are sharp when the base array is nonzero and all its coefficient mass is supported on indices u with O_u={1,2,3,4}.

Applied to the exact four-prime inclusion-exclusion ledger of fact 4a9a213a428b7e8c, O_u is the set of right-prime slots that lie in the left support at a base leaf. Therefore orthogonally recording all sixteen Ursell faces changes the first-level Hilbert coefficient norm by at most an absolute factor four and creates no power of the scale parameter. This conclusion concerns only the coefficient-side duplication. It does not bound the coordinate energy carried by the faces, justify a triangle inequality between signed face values, construct the literal all-anatomy leaf map, or control the independent cross-cell term.
697d75223ebc7a8a.proof:
For fixed u, every expanded coefficient v_{u,F} has norm ||v_u|| because its scalar sign has absolute value one. A set O_u has exactly 2^{|O_u|} subsets. Hence summing the squared norms over all F subset O_u gives 2^{|O_u|}||v_u||^2. Since O_u is a subset of a four-element set, |O_u|<=4 and 2^{|O_u|}<=16. Summing over u proves the first identity and inequality. Taking nonnegative square roots gives the factor four for coefficient norms.

There are 2^{|O_u|}-1 nonempty subsets of O_u. Repeating the same squared-norm calculation over nonempty F gives the second identity, and 2^{|O_u|}-1<=2^4-1=15. Taking square roots gives sqrt(15).

If every u carrying a nonzero v_u has O_u={1,2,3,4}, then 2^{|O_u|}=16 and 2^{|O_u|}-1=15 for every nonzero summand, so equality holds in both bounds. This proves sharpness.

Fact 4a9a213a428b7e8c proves that the four-prime disjointness indicator expands into the unrestricted face and all fifteen nonempty overlap faces. At a fixed base packet pair, exactly the subsets of the actual overlap-slot set O_u give nonzero face indicators. Thus the abstract expansion above is precisely the coefficient duplication induced by storing those nonzero faces in an orthogonal Hilbert direct sum. The final scope follows because the proof calculates only coefficient-vector norms; it makes no assertion about the separate coordinate vectors, their signed sums, or off-diagonal window-cell interactions.

glossary.H_u: The complex Hilbert space attached to base leaf u.
glossary.I: The finite base leaf index set.
glossary.O_u: The subset of the four overlap slots active at base leaf u.
glossary.base coefficient array: The tuple of coefficient vectors v_u before overlap-face duplication.
glossary.expanded Hilbert direct sum: The orthogonal direct sum with one coordinate for each pair (u,F) with F contained in O_u.
glossary.v_u: The coefficient vector at base leaf u.
glossary.v_{u,F}: The signed copy of v_u in overlap face F.

69e79ebdfba646b4.title: EXACT LARGE-CONDUCTOR FORWARD \(E_{11}\) HILBERT--KATAI/BSZ INTERFACE, OFF-SQUAREFREE EXTENSION, AND TWO-DILATE SUPPLIER. Assume the hypotheses and notation of facts fc442085ff47a053, 75d461ea0320c1a8, 12515655a5e7ed7c, and 9a80432a29fc15d2. Fix
69e79ebdfba646b4.author: slava chan
69e79ebdfba646b4.proof:
We prove the four parts in order.

1. Exact reconstruction. On a squarefree literal source value \(n=d\), fact fc442085ff47a053 gives \(g=1\), \((n,p\ell)=1\), \((p\ell,N)=1\), and \(0<|h|<Y_E\). Fact 75d461ea0320c1a8 puts \(c_n=(n,h)\), \(Q_n=n/c_n\), \(h_n=h/c_n\), and rewrites the phase of this atom as
\[
 e\!\left(\frac{Nh}{np\ell}\right)\frac1{\phi(Q_n)}
 \sum_{\chi\ ({\rm mod}\ Q_n)}
 G_{N,Q_n}(\chi)\chi(h_n)\overline{\chi(p)}\overline{\chi(\ell)}.                 \tag{13}
\]
Fact 9a80432a29fc15d2 proves that the principal and primitive-conductor-at-most-\(F_0\) terms have already been deleted with a fixed-power total error and that every remaining nonzero term has primitive conductor coprime to \(N\). Therefore restricting the character sum in (13) exactly as in (1) gives precisely the surviving large-conductor atom.

At \(g=1,d=n,r=p\ell\), fact 0a39d6be778e7dc9 gives the original coefficient
\[
 \mu(n)\mu(p\ell)(p\ell)^{-1}
 \widehat F_{\iota,n,p\ell}(h/(p\ell)).
\]
The exact literal copy coefficient and all deletion masks multiply this expression by \(\kappa_\iota\). Removing only \(\mu(n)\) leaves (2), and multiplying (2) by the restricted version of (13) gives (3). Summing first over the common coordinates and then over \(n\) proves the first equality in (4). For the declared inner product,
\(\langle z,{\bf1}_{\mathscr A_E}\rangle=\sum_\alpha z(\alpha)\), which proves the second equality. Since every coordinate absent for a particular \(n\) was assigned value zero, all vector additions and inner products take place in the one fixed space \(\mathcal H_E\).

2. Off-squarefree extension and boundedness. For every positive integer \(n\), the defining property of the Möbius function gives
\[
 \mu(n)\mu(n)^2=\mu(n):
\]
both sides equal \(\mu(n)\) when \(n\) is squarefree and both vanish otherwise. Multiplication by \(V_n\) proves (5). Thus values assigned by (1)--(3) at nonsquarefree \(n\) do not change the original sum. They are an auxiliary extension only.

We next prove (6) without any conductor factorization at nonsquarefree \(n\). Fourier Parseval on the finite unit group modulo \(Q_n\), by the same calculation as equation (5) in fact 75d461ea0320c1a8, gives
\[
 \sum_{\chi\ ({\rm mod}\ Q_n)}|G_{N,Q_n}(\chi)|^2=\phi(Q_n)^2.                    \tag{14}
\]
The character values in (1) have modulus one on its unit support. Cauchy--Schwarz over the subset of characters used in (1) gives
\[
 |\Pi_{>F_0}|
 \le\phi(Q_n)^{-1}\phi(Q_n)^{1/2}
       \left(\sum_\chi|G_{N,Q_n}(\chi)|^2\right)^{1/2}
 =\phi(Q_n)^{1/2},
\]
which proves (6).

For any fixed \(J\ge3\), equation (4) of fact 0a39d6be778e7dc9 gives
\[
 |(p\ell)^{-1}\widehat F_{\iota,n,p\ell}(h/(p\ell))|
 \ll_J \frac{M}{p\ell}(\log x)^2
       (1+|h|M/(p\ell))^{-J}.                                                      \tag{15}
\]
The actual marker-copy total variation is bounded by an absolute constant on the two-prime integer \(p\ell\), as proved in fc442085ff47a053, while the remaining literal label inventory has cardinality at most a fixed power of \(\log x\). The number of ordered distinct-prime pairs with \(p\ell\asymp R\) is at most \(O(R)\). On the E11 strip \(p\ell/M>1\), as used in facts 12515655a5e7ed7c and 9a80432a29fc15d2, and hence
\[
 \sum_{h\ne0}(1+|h|M/(p\ell))^{-2J}\ll p\ell/M\ll R/M.                            \tag{16}
\]
Using (6), (15), and (16), and enlarging all literal masks, gives for every \(n\) in the \(D\)-scale support
\[
 \|V_n\|^2
 \ll (\log x)^{C}
 R\left(\frac{M}{R}\right)^2\frac{R}{M}\,n
 \ll Mn(\log x)^C
 \ll x(\log x)^C,                                                                 \tag{17}
\]
because \(n\ll D\) and \(DM\asymp x\). Outside this support \(V_n=0\). Taking square roots proves (7). This proof used only pointwise definitions and Parseval; it used no relation between \(V_{n_1n_2}\), \(V_{n_1}\), and \(V_{n_2}\).

3. Finite Hilbert--Katai inequality. Abbreviate \(X=X_E\), \(L=L_{\mathcal P}\), and \(\Omega=\Omega_{\mathcal P}\). Put
\[
 S=\sum_{n\le X}\mu(n)V_n,\qquad
 A=\sum_{n\le X}\mu(n)V_n\Omega(n).
\]
By the triangle inequality followed by scalar Cauchy--Schwarz,
\[
 \|S-L^{-1}A\|
 \le \frac{B_E X^{1/2}}L
      \left(\sum_{n\le X}(\Omega(n)-L)^2\right)^{1/2}.                             \tag{18}
\]
Opening the divisor count gives
\[
 A=\sum_{a\in\mathcal P}\sum_{m\le X/a}\mu(am)V_{am}
   =-\sum_{a\in\mathcal P}
      \sum_{\substack{m\le X/a\\a\nmid m}}\mu(m)V_{am},                           \tag{19}
\]
because \(\mu(am)=-\mu(m)\) when \(a\nmid m\), while both sides of that relation are not used when \(a\mid m\). Define
\[
 A'=-\sum_{a\in\mathcal P}\sum_{m\le X/a}\mu(m)V_{am}.
\]
The terms added to (19) have \(a\mid m\), so boundedness gives
\[
 \|A-A'\|\le B_E\sum_{a\in\mathcal P}\lfloor X/a^2\rfloor.                       \tag{20}
\]
This is the only squareful-dilation exceptional term.

For \(m\le X/P_-\), put
\[
 Z_m=\sum_{\substack{a\in\mathcal P\\am\le X}}V_{am}.
\]
Then \(A'=-\sum_{m\le X/P_-}\mu(m)Z_m\). Since \(|\mu(m)|\le1\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \|A'\|^2
 \le\lfloor X/P_-\rfloor\sum_{m\le X/P_-}\|Z_m\|^2.                              \tag{21}
\]
Expansion in the common Hilbert space gives the exact Gram identity
\[
 \sum_m\|Z_m\|^2
 =\sum_{a,b\in\mathcal P}
   \sum_{m\le X/\max(a,b)}\langle V_{am},V_{bm}\rangle.                           \tag{22}
\]
The diagonal part of (22) is at most
\[
 \sum_{a\in\mathcal P}\lfloor X/a\rfloor B_E^2
 \le B_E^2XL.                                                                     \tag{23}
\]
Pairing conjugate off-diagonal terms and then applying the triangle inequality bounds the rest by
\(\sum_{a\ne b}|\mathfrak C_{a,b}|\). Combining (18), (20), (21), (22), and (23), and using
\(\|S\|\le\|S-L^{-1}A\|+L^{-1}\|A-A'\|+L^{-1}\|A'\|\), proves (9).

For completeness, expand the variance. The floor identities give
\[
 \sum_{n\le X}\Omega(n)=XL+O(|\mathcal P|)
\]
and
\[
 \sum_{n\le X}\Omega(n)^2
 =X\left(L^2+\sum_{a\in\mathcal P}(1/a-1/a^2)\right)
  +O(|\mathcal P|^2).
\]
Substitution into
\(\sum(\Omega-L)^2=\sum\Omega^2-2L\sum\Omega+XL^2\) proves (10). Equations (19)--(23) show explicitly why neither multiplicativity of \(V_n\) nor a factor \(\mu(m)^2\) is present in (8): only the multiplicativity of \(\mu\) off \(a\mid m\) is used, and then \(|\mu(m)|\le1\) is used in (21).

4. Exact correlation kernel. Substitute (3) into the common-coordinate inner product. The coefficient product is the first line of (11). The product of the two continuous reciprocity phases is
\[
 e\!\left(\frac{Nh}{amp\ell}\right)
 \overline{e\!\left(\frac{Nh}{bmp\ell}\right)}
 =
 e\!\left(\frac{Nh}{mp\ell}(1/a-1/b)\right).
\]
The two large-conductor projectors remain exactly as written. This proves (11), including every zero-extension intersection mask through the two factors \(C_\iota\) and the two projectors.

If instead the sum in (1) is taken over every character modulo \(Q_n\), finite-group Fourier inversion in fact 75d461ea0320c1a8 says that the projector equals
\(e_{Q_n}(-Nh_n(p\ell)^{-1})\). Multiplication by the continuous factor then recovers the original physical phase \(e_{p\ell}(Nh\,n^{-1})\). For \(n=am\) and \(n=bm\), the common literal coordinate is nonzero only when both are coprime to \(p\ell\). Their phase product is therefore
\[
 e_{p\ell}(Nh(am)^{-1})\overline{e_{p\ell}(Nh(bm)^{-1})}
 =e_{p\ell}(Nh\,m^{-1}(a^{-1}-b^{-1})),
\]
which proves (12). Fourier inversion permits this recombination only for the complete character sum. The projector (1) omits the principal and low-conductor characters, so its product must remain the product displayed in (11). Finally, (4) and Cauchy--Schwarz yield
\[
 |T_{E11}^{>F_0}|
 \le\|{\bf1}_{\mathscr A_E}\|
      \left\|\sum_n\mu(n)V_n\right\|,
\]
which records the reconstruction-functional tax and completes every scope assertion.

glossary.B_E: The supremum of the Hilbert norms of the auxiliary vectors V_n.
glossary.L_mathcal P: The reciprocal-prime mass sum_{a in mathcal P}1/a.
glossary.Pi_{>F_0}(n;h,p,ell): The exact character projector onto primitive conductors greater than F_0 and coprime to N for the descended modulus n/gcd(n,h).
glossary.V_n: The auxiliary E11 Hilbert vector at original divisor n after removing only the factor mu(n), with all other literal coefficients and masks retained.
glossary.mathcal P: A finite nonempty set of prime dilators used in the finite Hilbert Katai reduction.
glossary.mathfrak C_{a,b}: The same-coordinate correlation sum of the two auxiliary E11 vectors at the distinct prime dilates am and bm.
glossary.mathscr A_E: The q-independent coordinate set containing every literal E11 label, normalized-marker copy, nonzero frequency, and ordered canonical prime pair.

6a04596c7f520b05.title: HALF-CONV MEDIUM-UNION NO-FIT FOR THE CANONICAL MEDIUM-DIVISOR BRANCH. Let 1<Y<=Z be real numbers, let p,q be distinct primes with Y<=p<=Z<q, and put n=pq. Define
6a04596c7f520b05.author: slava chan
6a04596c7f520b05.statement:
HALF-CONV MEDIUM-UNION NO-FIT FOR THE CANONICAL MEDIUM-DIVISOR BRANCH. Let 1<Y<=Z be real numbers, let p,q be distinct primes with Y<=p<=Z<q, and put n=pq. Define
C_med(n;Y,Z)=sum_{dm=n, d in [Y,Z] or m in [Y,Z]}rho_{1/2}(d)rho_{1/2}(m),
where rho_{1/2} is the arithmetic function of fact 5999a1878276ac78 and the sum has no coprimality restriction. Then n is squarefree, p is its unique prime divisor in [Y,Z], and
C_med(n;Y,Z)=1/2,
whereas
mu(n)=1.
The complementary two convolution allocations (d,m)=(1,pq) and (pq,1), neither of which has a factor in [Y,Z], contribute the missing 1/2. Consequently the union of HALF-CONV terms with d or m medium is not a pointwise exact replacement for the canonical medium-divisor branch, even on squarefree integers with a unique medium prime. Any exact HALF-CONV replacement must retain the other convolution ranges or introduce and verify a different reweighting identity.
6a04596c7f520b05.proof:
The positive factorizations dm=n are exactly
(d,m)=(1,pq),(p,q),(q,p),(pq,1),
because p and q are distinct primes. Fact 5999a1878276ac78 gives
rho_{1/2}(1)=1,
rho_{1/2}(p)=rho_{1/2}(q)=-1/2,
and, by multiplicativity,
rho_{1/2}(pq)=rho_{1/2}(p)rho_{1/2}(q)=1/4.
Therefore each of the four displayed factorizations has coefficient 1/4, and their full sum is 1, in agreement with mu(pq)=1.

Since p lies in [Y,Z] and q>Z, among the four factorizations only (p,q) and (q,p) have at least one factor in [Y,Z]. Hence
C_med(n;Y,Z)=1/4+1/4=1/2.
The remaining factorizations (1,pq) and (pq,1) have neither factor in [Y,Z] because 1<Y and pq>q>Z; together they contribute 1/2. This proves every asserted identity and the exact-replacement no-fit.

glossary.C_med(n;Y,Z): The partial HALF-CONV coefficient obtained by summing over factorizations dm=n for which d or m lies in [Y,Z].

6a2652fb92d86417.title: Fix real numbers
6a2652fb92d86417.author: slava chan
6a2652fb92d86417.statement:
Fix real numbers
\[
 {1\over2}<\alpha<\beta<1,\qquad \eta>0,\qquad \rho>0,
 \qquad B_{\rm src}>0.
\]
Let \(W\) be a bounded real function supported in \([\alpha,\beta]\), and let \(\Phi\) be a bounded real function supported in \([1/2,2]\). Let \(x\ge3\), put \(N=2x\), and assume that \(N\) is an integer. Put
\[
 T_x=(\log x)^{6+\eta+\rho}.
\]
Let \(D,U>0\) satisfy
\[
 {1\over2}x^{1/2}(\log x)^{-B_{\rm src}}\le D\le2x^{1/2},
 \qquad D>2T_x.
\]
Let \(\mu\) be the Möbius function. Extend the von Mangoldt function
\(\Lambda\) by zero on nonpositive integers, and define
\[
 {\cal I}_D=
 \{d\ge2:(d,N)=1,\ \mu(d)\ne0,\ d\le x^{1/2},                  \Phi(d/D)\ne0\}.                    \tag{1}
\]
For positive integers \(s,m,w\), define
\[
\begin{split}
 f_{s,m}(w)={}&
 {\bf1}_{sw\in{\cal I}_D}\mu(w)\Phi(sw/D)W(smw/x)\\
 &\times\Phi((N-smw)/U)\Lambda(N-smw).                 \tag{2}
\end{split}
\]
Put \(e(t)=\exp(2\pi i t)\). For \(\theta\in\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\), define the finite Hilbert-valued Fourier polynomial
\[
 F_s(\theta)=
 \left(\sum_{w\ge1}f_{s,m}(w)e(\theta w)\right)_{m\ge1}
 \in\ell^2(\mathbb N).                                 \tag{3}
\]
For \(1\le s<T_x^2\), put
\[
 L_s={D\over sT_x}.                                      \tag{4}
\]
For all sufficiently large \(x\), \(L_s\ge2\). Define
\[
 J_s=
 \sup_{\theta_0\in\mathbb R/\mathbb Z}
 \int_{\theta_0-1/(2L_s)}^{\theta_0+1/(2L_s)}
 \|F_s(\theta)\|_{ell^2_m}^{,2}\,d\theta.          \tag{5}
\]
Define the signed small-projector energy
\[
 {\cal E}_{<}=
 \sum_{1\le g<T_x}\sum_{1\le r<T_x}
 \mu(r)\|F_{gr}(0)\|_{ell^2_m}^{,2}.                 \tag{6}
\]
Also define the full-von-Mangoldt hard covariance
\[
\begin{split}
 {\mathfrak C}_\star^\Lambda
 =\sum_{\substack{d_1,d_2\in{\cal I}_D\\
          |d_1-d_2|>D/T_x\\(d_1,d_2)<T_x}}
 &\mu(d_1)\mu(d_2)\Phi(d_1/D)\Phi(d_2/D)\\
 &\times\sum_{m\ge1}W(d_1m/x)W(d_2m/x)
 \Phi((N-d_1m)/U)\Phi((N-d_2m)/U)\\
 &\times\Lambda(N-d_1m)\Lambda(N-d_2m).               \tag{7}
\end{split}
\]

The Hilbert circle identities are exact:
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R/\mathbb Z}\|F_s(\theta)\|_{ell^2_m}^{,2}d\theta
 =\sum_{m,w}|f_{s,m}(w)|^2,                              \tag{8}
\]
and, for every integer \(h\),
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R/\mathbb Z}\|F_s(\theta)\|_{ell^2_m}^{,2}
 e(-h\theta)d\theta
 =\sum_m\sum_{w-w'=h}f_{s,m}(w)\overline{f_{s,m}(w')}. \tag{9}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \|F_s(0)\|_{ell^2_m}^{,2}
 \ll_{W,\Phi}{D^2\over s^2T_x}J_s,                    \tag{10}
\]
and
\[
 {\cal E}_{<}
 \ll_{W,\Phi}{D^2\over T_x}
 \sum_{g,r<T_x}{J_{gr}\over g^2r^2}.                   \tag{11}
\]

Therefore the weighted vector local-\(L^2\) estimate
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \sum_{g,r<T_x}{J_{gr}\over g^2r^2}
 \ll_{W,\Phi,\eta,\rho}
 {xT_x\over D}(\log x)^{-4-\eta}
 \quad}                                                  \tag{TB-VL2}
\]
implies
\[
 {\cal E}_{<}\ll xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta},                \tag{12}
\]
and consequently
\[
 {\mathfrak C}_\star^\Lambda
 \ll_{W,\Phi,\alpha,\beta,\eta,\rho}
 xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta}.                                 \tag{13}
\]
A stronger uniform estimate
\[
 J_s\ll {xT_x\over D}(\log x)^{-4-\eta}
 \qquad(1\le s<T_x^2)                                  \tag{14}
\]
also implies TB-VL2, with no power of \(T_x\) lost in the \((g,r)\)-sum.

Equations (8)--(11), including all \(g,r<T_x\) taxes, are proved here. Neither TB-VL2 nor (14) is asserted. Their new arithmetic content is a logarithmically saving local-energy estimate for the exact fixed-\(N\) reflected sequence \(\mu(w)\Lambda(N-smw)\), simultaneously in the modulus-fiber Hilbert space.

Fact 73fb9efe1286f7e9 does not directly supply this input. That fact permits three separated divisor-bounded coefficient sequences which are independent of its varying modulus \(q\), with \(q\)-dependence only in a unit phase numerator. If one identifies \(q=s\) here, the coefficient (2) depends jointly on \(q,m,w\) through
\[
 \Phi(qw/D)W(qmw/x)\Phi((N-qmw)/U)\Lambda(N-qmw).
\]
If \(q\) is instead a later Poisson modulus, a Heath--Brown or Vaughan decomposition must first separate the resulting \(q\)-dependent prime and selector coefficient into the independent slots required by fact 73fb9efe1286f7e9. No such separation or projective-cost estimate is presently available. This is a coefficient-slot mismatch, not an impossibility theorem.
6a2652fb92d86417.proof:
All sums in (2)--(3) are finite. If \(f_{s,m}(w)\ne0\), then
\[
 D/2\le sw\le2D.
\]
Thus the number of possible \(w\) for fixed \(s,m\) is
\[
 \ll D/s.                                                \tag{15}
\]
The lower bound for \(D\) is a fixed power of \(x\) divided by a fixed power of \(\log x\), whereas \(T_x\) is a fixed power of \(\log x\). Hence
\[
 D/T_x^3\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
For \(s<T_x^2\), this gives
\[
 L_s=D/(sT_x)>D/T_x^3\ge2                               \tag{16}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(x\).

Expand the squared Hilbert norm:
\[
 \|F_s(\theta)\|_{ell^2_m}^{,2}
 =\sum_m\sum_{w,w'}f_{s,m}(w)\overline{f_{s,m}(w')}
 e(\theta(w-w')).
\]
Termwise integration is legitimate because the sum is finite. Character orthogonality on \(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\) proves (8); multiplication by \(e(-h\theta)\) proves (9).

At \(\theta=0\), Cauchy--Schwarz in \(w\), followed by (15) and (8), gives
\[
 \|F_s(0)\|_{ell^2_m}^{,2}
 \ll {D\over s}
 \int_{\mathbb R/\mathbb Z}\|F_s(\theta)\|_{ell^2_m}^{,2}d\theta.
                                                                    \tag{17}
\]
By (16), the circle is covered by at most \(2L_s\) intervals of length \(1/L_s\). Every interval has energy at most \(J_s\), so the integral in (17) is at most \(2L_sJ_s\). Using \(L_s=D/(sT_x)\) proves (10).

We relate (6) to the exact coprimality projector. For positive \(g,r<T_x\), write \(s=gr\). Fact 83c98e3d3a11382b, equations (11)--(13), proves that after writing \(G=gm\) and \(u=rw\), the fixed-\((g,r,G)\) sum of fact 1f5316e61daf156d is
\[
 \mu(r)\sum_wf_{gr,m}(w).
\]
Its squared absolute value is the squared absolute value of the \(m\)-th coordinate of \(F_{gr}(0)\). Summing over \(m\) proves that the signed energy in fact 1f5316e61daf156d is exactly (6).

Because \(\mu(r)\le1\) and every squared norm is nonnegative,
\[
 {\cal E}_{<}\le\sum_{g,r<T_x}\|F_{gr}(0)\|^2.
\]
Apply (10) with \(s=gr\) to prove (11). Under TB-VL2, (11) gives
\[
 {\cal E}_{<}
 \ll {D^2\over T_x}{xT_x\over D}(\log x)^{-4-\eta}
 =xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta},
\]
which is (12).

Fact 1f5316e61daf156d, equation (5), states under the explicit hypotheses above that
\[
 {\mathfrak C}_\star^\Lambda
 ={\cal E}_{<}
 +O_{W,\Phi,\alpha,\beta}
   (xD(\log x)^2/T_x).
\]
Since
\[
 (\log x)^2/T_x=(\log x)^{-4-\eta-\rho},
\]
equation (12) implies (13).

Finally, (14) implies TB-VL2 because
\[
 \sum_{g,r<T_x}{1\over g^2r^2}
 \le\left(\sum_{n\ge1}{1\over n^2}\right)^2<\infty.
\]
Thus the two auxiliary divisor sums cost only an absolute constant; there is no \(T_x^2\) loss.

For the final no-fit assertion, fact 73fb9efe1286f7e9 states its three input coefficient sequences independently of \(q\). The displayed factor in (2) varies jointly with \(s,m,w\). Setting \(q=s\) violates that hypothesis literally. A distinct future modulus \(q\) would require an exact prior decomposition producing one-variable coefficients independent of \(q\), together with its coefficient norm. Neither conclusion follows from fact 73fb9efe1286f7e9.

glossary.F_s(theta): the Hilbert-valued Fourier polynomial whose m-th coordinate is the Fourier sum of f_{s,m}
glossary.J_s: the supremal local Hilbert L2 energy of F_s on a circle arc of length 1/L_s
glossary.L_s: the reduced hard-difference length D/(s T_x)
glossary.TB-VL2: the weighted vector local-L2 estimate sufficient for the signed coprimality-projector core
glossary.f_{s,m}(w): the exact reflected Möbius-von-Mangoldt coefficient at merged divisor s, modulus fiber m, and reduced variable w

6ab529accdede090.title: HYBRID TWO-ROW INCOMPLETE INCIDENCE BOUND WITHOUT MODEWISE RESONANT PAYMENT. Let p>2 be prime, let c be a nonzero residue modulo p, and let
6ab529accdede090.author: slava chan
6ab529accdede090.statement:
HYBRID TWO-ROW INCOMPLETE INCIDENCE BOUND WITHOUT MODEWISE RESONANT PAYMENT. Let p>2 be prime, let c be a nonzero residue modulo p, and let
\[
G_c(f,g)={p\over p-1}\left({\bf1}_{g=cf}-{1\over p-1}\right)
\qquad(f,g\in\mathbb F_p^\times).
\]
For i=1,2 let d_i be positive squarefree integers coprime to p, let \((C_i,d_i)=1\), let W_i be fixed compactly supported infinitely differentiable complex functions, and let X_i be real and L_i>0. Put
\[
A_f=\sum_{\substack{x\in\mathbb Z\\(x,pd_1)=1\\x\equiv f\ ({\rm mod}\ p)}}
 W_1((x-X_1)/L_1)e_{d_1}(C_1x^{-1}),
\]
\[
B_g=\sum_{\substack{y\in\mathbb Z\\(y,pd_2)=1\\y\equiv g\ ({\rm mod}\ p)}}
 W_2((y-X_2)/L_2)e_{d_2}(C_2y^{-1}),
\]
and
\[
\mathcal B=\sum_{f,g\in\mathbb F_p^\times}G_c(f,g)A_fB_g. \tag{1}
\]
For every \(\varepsilon>0\), define
\[
\mathcal N_i=\min\left\{
p^{1/2}d_i^{1/2+\varepsilon}\left(1+{L_i\over pd_i}\right),
\ C_{W_i}\bigl((1+L_i/p)(1+L_i)\bigr)^{1/2}
\right\}, \tag{2}
\]
where \(C_{W_i}\) depends only on the fixed support and supremum norm of W_i. Then
\[
|\mathcal B|\ll {p\over p-1}\mathcal N_1\mathcal N_2. \tag{3}
\]
In particular, if \(L_i\ge pd_i\) for i=1,2, then
\[
|\mathcal B|\ll_{W_1,W_2,\varepsilon}
{L_1L_2\over p(d_1d_2)^{1/2-\varepsilon}}. \tag{4}
\]
The estimate keeps the centered incidence operator assembled. In the fixed-subface literal J_2 setting of fact ce5de84556b212d9, one takes \(c=s_1q_2^{-1}\pmod p\) and the signed coefficients \(C_1,C_2\) displayed there; hence (3)--(4) apply whenever separated smooth weights have been extracted in both unit slots. No aggregation over literal subfaces or source coefficients is asserted.
6ab529accdede090.proof:
Let \(V=\mathbb C^{\mathbb F_p^\times}\) with counting-measure norm. The matrix G_c acts by
\[
(G_cv)(f)={p\over p-1}\left(v(cf)-{1\over p-1}\sum_{g\ne0}v(g)\right).
\]
The map \(v(f)\mapsto v(cf)\) is unitary and preserves constants, while the expression in parentheses is that permutation followed by the orthogonal projection onto the subspace perpendicular to constants. Therefore
\[
\|G_c\|_{V\to V}={p\over p-1}. \tag{5}
\]
Although (1) is bilinear rather than sesquilinear, it can be written as a Hermitian pairing with the conjugate of the second vector. Cauchy--Schwarz and (5) give
\[
|\mathcal B|\le {p\over p-1}\|A\|_2\|B\|_2. \tag{6}
\]

Apply equation (5) of fact d9c3f37492846fce separately to every nonzero residue f modulo p. Uniformly in f,
\[
|A_f|\ll_{W_1,\varepsilon}d_1^{1/2+\varepsilon}
\left(1+{L_1\over pd_1}\right).
\]
There are p-1 possible f, so
\[
\|A\|_2\ll_{W_1,\varepsilon}p^{1/2}d_1^{1/2+\varepsilon}
\left(1+{L_1\over pd_1}\right). \tag{7}
\]
The same argument gives the first alternative in (2) for B.

For the second alternative, let \(n_f\) be the number of integers x in the support of \(W_1((x-X_1)/L_1)\) satisfying x congruent f modulo p. Cauchy--Schwarz inside each residue class gives
\[
|A_f|^2\le n_f
\sum_{\substack{x\equiv f\ ({\rm mod}\ p)}}|W_1((x-X_1)/L_1)|^2.
\]
Because W_1 has fixed compact support, \(n_f\ll_{W_1}1+L_1/p\). Summing in f, using disjointness of the residue classes, and the bound
\[
\sum_{x\in\mathbb Z}|W_1((x-X_1)/L_1)|^2\ll_{W_1}1+L_1,
\]
gives
\[
\|A\|_2\ll_{W_1}\bigl((1+L_1/p)(1+L_1)\bigr)^{1/2}. \tag{8}
\]
The identical proof applies to B. Taking the better of (7) and (8) for each row and inserting the results into (6) proves (3).

If L_i is at least pd_i, the first alternative in (2) is at most
\[
2p^{1/2}d_i^{1/2+\varepsilon}{L_i\over pd_i}
={2L_i\over p^{1/2}d_i^{1/2-\varepsilon}}.
\]
Multiplication of the two row bounds in (6) proves (4). The final literal specialization follows directly from the signed fixed-subface identification in fact ce5de84556b212d9; no outer coefficient or subface sum has been estimated.

glossary.A_f: The first-row incomplete inverse-phase sum in residue class f modulo p.
glossary.B_g: The second-row incomplete inverse-phase sum in residue class g modulo p.
glossary.C_{W_i}: A constant depending only on the fixed smooth weight W_i.
glossary.\\mathcal B: The assembled centered two-row incidence form.
glossary.\\mathcal N_i: The hybrid fixed-fibre-completion/disjoint-class norm bound for row i.

6b791c88a1789494.title: SHORT-COMPLEMENT CRT/DFI NO-FIT FOR THE ACTUAL-Z_MID LARGE-CONDUCTOR SPECTRUM. Assume the actual-Z_mid g=1, |h|=1 endpoint scales and character-conductor factorization of facts 58c03698e1b077c3 and 3afa321a72a3612b. Put
6b791c88a1789494.author: slava chan
6b791c88a1789494.statement:
SHORT-COMPLEMENT CRT/DFI NO-FIT FOR THE ACTUAL-Z_MID LARGE-CONDUCTOR SPECTRUM. Assume the actual-Z_mid g=1, |h|=1 endpoint scales and character-conductor factorization of facts 58c03698e1b077c3 and 3afa321a72a3612b. Put
A_0=x^(1/2+o(1)), B_0=x^(2/3+o(1)).
Let
F_c=x^(r+o(1)), S_c=B_0/F_c=x^(2/3-r+o(1)),
where 1/2<=r<=2/3, and put M_c=A_0S_c=x^(7/6-r+o(1)).

For b=fs with (f,s)=1 and (a,fs)=1, the exact Chinese-remainder factorization is
e_{fs}(Na^{-1})
 =e_f(N(as)^{-1})e_s(N(af)^{-1}).                                  (1)
Fix s. Grant in favor of direct applicability that the second factor in (1), every natural mask, and the joint endpoint weight may be absorbed at x^(o(1)) cost into separated coefficients. Applying the Duke--Friedlander--Iwaniec theorem used in fact 58c03698e1b077c3 to the inverse variable as of scale M_c and the modulus f of scale F_c gives
E_DFI(F_c,S_c)
 =x^(1/4+3r/2+o(1)),  1/2<=r<=7/12,                                (2)
and
E_DFI(F_c,S_c)
 =x^(17/12-r/2+o(1)),  7/12<=r<=2/3.                               (3)

Ordinary absolute summation of (2)-(3) over s asymp S_c is never better than x^(13/12+o(1)). Even if one additionally grants a hypothetical square-root aggregation factor S_c^(1/2), the resulting optimized exponents are
x^(7/12+r+o(1)),  1/2<=r<=7/12,                                   (4)
and
x^(7/4-r+o(1)),  7/12<=r<=2/3,                                    (5)
whose minimum over 1/2<=r<=2/3 is exactly x^(13/12+o(1)). Therefore the plan consisting solely of CRT separation, a fixed-s DFI application, and absolute or square-root-size aggregation over s cannot improve the DFI endpoint exponent already verified in fact 58c03698e1b077c3, and cannot imply x^(1-delta) for fixed delta>0. This is a right-hand-side no-fit for that scoped plan. It does not exclude cancellation stronger than square-root across s or a theorem treating f and s jointly.
6b791c88a1789494.proof:
For coprime f and s, the Chinese remainder representation of a residue y modulo fs gives
e_{fs}(y)=e_f(ys^{-1})e_s(yf^{-1}).
Take y=N a^{-1} modulo fs. Reducing the inverse modulo each factor yields
e_{fs}(Na^{-1})
 =e_f(Na^{-1}s^{-1})e_s(Na^{-1}f^{-1})
 =e_f(N(as)^{-1})e_s(N(af)^{-1}),
which proves (1).

For fixed s, introduce the integer inverse variable m=as. It lies at scale
M_c=A_0S_c
and its coefficient sequence is supported only on multiples of s, with at most A_0 nonzero terms and l2 norm at most A_0^(1/2)x^(o(1)). The modulus coefficient has l2 norm at most F_c^(1/2)x^(o(1)). The weighted DFI bound quoted and applied in fact 58c03698e1b077c3 therefore gives
E_DFI
 <=x^(o(1))(A_0F_c)^(1/2)
 {(M_c+F_c)^(1/2)
 +(1+N/(M_cF_c))^(1/2)min(M_c,F_c)}.                               (6)
Because M_cF_c=A_0B_0=x^(7/6+o(1)) and N=x^(1+o(1)), the target factor in (6) is x^(o(1)).

If 1/2<=r<=7/12, then M_c>=F_c. The minimum term in (6) is F_c=x^(r+o(1)), while the square-root term has exponent
(7/6-r)/2=7/12-r/2.
Since r>=1/2, the F_c term is larger. Multiplying by
(A_0F_c)^(1/2)=x^(1/4+r/2+o(1))
proves (2).

If 7/12<=r<=2/3, then F_c>=M_c. The minimum term is
M_c=x^(7/6-r+o(1)),
while the square-root term has exponent r/2. Throughout this range
7/6-r>=r/2.
Multiplication by x^(1/4+r/2+o(1)) proves (3).

Absolute summation over the S_c possible complementary factors adds exponent 2/3-r. Applied to (2), this gives
11/12+r/2,
whose minimum on the first interval is 7/6. Applied to (3), it gives
25/12-3r/2,
whose minimum on the second interval is 13/12 at r=2/3. Hence ordinary summation never beats x^(13/12+o(1)).

For the more favorable hypothetical square-root aggregation, add only half the S_c exponent, namely 1/3-r/2. Adding this to (2) gives 7/12+r, proving (4); adding it to (3) gives 7/4-r, proving (5). The first expression is minimized at r=1/2 and the second at r=2/3, and both endpoint minima equal 13/12. This proves the scoped no-fit.

glossary.E_DFI(F_c,S_c): The DFI right-hand side for one fixed complementary factor s.
glossary.F_c: A dyadic primitive-conductor scale in the large-conductor spectrum.

6ca1f83e2233669a.title: BUFFER-EXTENDED COMPLETE-FREQUENCY TARGET-GCD-DESCENDED INTERVAL-PRIME TRACE. Fix integers J,C_A,K>=1, a constant C>=1, 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100 and beta_1=6/5-3sigma, and let 1<=beta<=beta_1. Let Q be sufficiently large, B=Q^beta, H_T=B/Q, L_0=H_TQ^sigma, and Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma). Fix a nonzero integer L_src with |L_src|<=Q^C_A. Let C_med be any set of squarefree divisors c of L_src with c<=H_TQ^(sigma/4). For each c put Q_c=Q/c and choose U_c,Y_c>=1 such that C^(-1)B<=U_cY_c<=CB and L_0/2<=Y_c<=Z. On q in [Q_c,2Q_c) use coefficients d_{c,q} of absolute value at most one, supported on squarefree q with gcd(c,q)=gcd(L_src/c,q)=1. For every dyadic F>=1 use divisor-bounded coefficients on F<=|h|<2F, U_c<=u<2U_c, and primes Y_c<=p<2Y_c with L_0<p<Z, impose gcd(up,cq)=gcd(u,p)=1, and use a fixed-complexity uniformly scaled-smooth projective amplitude. Let omega_{c,F} satisfy |omega_{c,F}|<=C_{J_0}min(1,(F/H_P)^(-J_0)) for every fixed J_0>=1. Define T_c exactly as in fact 653b56b5854f603b, with Poisson prefactor H_P^(-1) and phase
6ca1f83e2233669a.author: slava chan
6ca1f83e2233669a.statement:
BUFFER-EXTENDED COMPLETE-FREQUENCY TARGET-GCD-DESCENDED INTERVAL-PRIME TRACE. Fix integers J,C_A,K>=1, a constant C>=1, 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100 and beta_1=6/5-3sigma, and let 1<=beta<=beta_1. Let Q be sufficiently large, B=Q^beta, H_T=B/Q, L_0=H_TQ^sigma, and Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma). Fix a nonzero integer L_src with |L_src|<=Q^C_A. Let C_med be any set of squarefree divisors c of L_src with c<=H_TQ^(sigma/4). For each c put Q_c=Q/c and choose U_c,Y_c>=1 such that C^(-1)B<=U_cY_c<=CB and L_0/2<=Y_c<=Z. On q in [Q_c,2Q_c) use coefficients d_{c,q} of absolute value at most one, supported on squarefree q with gcd(c,q)=gcd(L_src/c,q)=1. For every dyadic F>=1 use divisor-bounded coefficients on F<=|h|<2F, U_c<=u<2U_c, and primes Y_c<=p<2Y_c with L_0<p<Z, impose gcd(up,cq)=gcd(u,p)=1, and use a fixed-complexity uniformly scaled-smooth projective amplitude. Let omega_{c,F} satisfy |omega_{c,F}|<=C_{J_0}min(1,(F/H_P)^(-J_0)) for every fixed J_0>=1. Define T_c exactly as in fact 653b56b5854f603b, with Poisson prefactor H_P^(-1) and phase
e_q(-(L_src/c)h(up)^(-1)).

The following two estimates hold.

(i) For arbitrary G>=1 and H_P=H_T/G, there is delta_F>0 such that
sum_{c in C_med}|T_c| << GQ^(2-delta_F).

(ii) Fix 0<eta<sigma. For Q^(-sigma+eta)<=G<=Q^(sigma-eta) and H_P=H_T/G, there is delta_N>0 such that
sum_{c in C_med}|T_c| << Q^(2-delta_N).

Both estimates are uniform in C_med, whether H_P is below or above one, all deletion masks, and polylogarithmically many smooth, dyadic, sign, parent, high, fixed-U, source, and projective-separation labels absorbable in the displayed coefficient families. No beta>=beta_1 extension, non-interval-prime anatomy estimate, outer-g assembly, endpoint, PMD, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
6ca1f83e2233669a.proof:
Put v=F/H_P and q_0=Q/c. We adapt the accepted proofs of facts 653b56b5854f603b and 97e9b97caca25b8d, recording every changed exponent.

First verify the common analytic hypotheses of fact 4cae52efa792b9ef. Since Y_c>=H_TQ^sigma/2 and U_cY_c is comparable to B,
U_c<<Q^(1-sigma).                                                     (1)
Also c<=H_TQ^(sigma/4), so
q_0>=Q^(2-beta-sigma/4)>=Q^(4/5+11sigma/4).                            (2)
Thus U_c<q_0^2 for sufficiently large Q.

For (i), restrict first to v<=Q^(sigma/2). Since G>=1,
2F/Y_c<=4v/(GQ^sigma)<=4Q^(-sigma/2)<1.                               (3)
Using Y_c<=Z gives
q_0/(H_PY_c)=QG/(cH_TY_c)
 >=GQ^(3/2-beta+11sigma/4)
 >=Q^(3/10+23sigma/4).                                                 (4)
This exponent is larger than sigma/2, so 8FY_c<q on the support. The local argument in the accepted proof of 653b56b5854f603b therefore gives, up to Q^epsilon|omega_{c,F}|, the four terms
c^(-1)G^(1/2)Q^2(H_T/Y_c)^(1/2)v^(1/2),
c^(-5/4)Q^(7/4)(H_TY_c)^(1/2)v,
c^(-3/4)Q^(7/4)H_Tv,
c^(-1)Q^(2-sigma)v.                                                (5)
After division by GQ^2, use G>=1, Y_c>=H_TQ^sigma/2, and
H_TY_c<=H_TZ=Q^(1/2-3sigma). The four ratios are at most
c^(-1)Q^(-sigma/2)v^(1/2),
c^(-5/4)Q^(-3sigma/2)v,
c^(-3/4)Q^(-1/20-3sigma)v,
c^(-1)Q^(-sigma)v.                                                  (6)
The third exponent follows from beta<=6/5-3sigma:
Q^(7/4)H_T/Q^2=Q^(beta-5/4)<=Q^(-1/20-3sigma).
Second-order Fourier decay sums (6) over dyadic v<=Q^(sigma/2).

For v>Q^(sigma/2), direct counting as in 653b56b5854f603b gives
|T_{c,F}|<<Q^epsilon c^(-1)Q^2H_Tv|omega_{c,F}|.                     (7)
Here H_T<=Q^(1/5-3sigma). Choose a fixed Fourier-decay order J_* with
(J_*-1)sigma/2>1/5+sigma.
The dyadic sum of (7) is then c^(-1)GQ^(2-delta) for a fixed delta>0. Summing c costs at most tau(|L_src|)Q^epsilon=Q^epsilon. This proves (i).

For (ii), use the analytic range v<=Q^(eta/2). The lower bound on G gives
Y_c/H_P>=GQ^sigma/2>=Q^eta/2,                                     (8)
so 2F<=Y_c. Also
q_0/(H_PY_c)
 >=GQ^(3/2-beta+11sigma/4)
 >=Q^(3/10+19sigma/4+eta),                                       (9)
so 8FY_c<q. The accepted proof of 97e9b97caca25b8d gives the same four terms (5). Relative now to Q^2, the first term saves eta/2 because
G^(1/2)(H_T/Y_c)^(1/2)
 <=Q^((sigma-eta)/2)Q^(-sigma/2)=Q^(-eta/2).                     (10)
The second, third and fourth terms save respectively 3sigma/2,
1/20+3sigma, and sigma. Arbitrary fixed third-order decay sums this analytic range.

For v>Q^(eta/2), direct counting gives
|T_{c,F}|<<Q^epsilon c^(-1)QBv|omega_{c,F}|.                      (11)
Since beta<=6/5-3sigma and eta is fixed, choose the fixed arbitrary Fourier-decay order sufficiently large in terms of eta and sigma. The dyadic tail in (11) is O(c^(-1)Q^(2-delta_N)). Sum c by the divisor bound. This proves (ii), including H_P<1 because every nonzero integer F belongs to exactly one of the two frequency ranges. Every additional label permitted in the statement is already uniform in the two predecessor proofs and costs only Q^epsilon.

glossary.T_c: The complete-frequency descended interval-prime trace on exact target-gcd layer c.

6d56c42d1d6a5518.title: R=5 FIXED-POWER PAYMENT OF A WIDE-IMBALANCE LITERAL C1 DYNAMIC NEAR-PRIME CHAMBER. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100 and K_0>=2. Let Q be sufficiently large. Let n=pv be squarefree, where p is prime and gcd(p,v)=1, put C=mathscr A h and m_eff=n/gcd(C,n), and assume Q^(1/2+kappa)<=m_eff<=Q^(6/5), p does not divide C, and m_eff=p r_eff with r_eff<=Q^(1/250). Let c be squarefree with nc<=Q^K_0. Let W be extended by zero, supported on Q<=q<2Q, and satisfy V_Q(W)<=Q^epsilon for every fixed epsilon>0
6d56c42d1d6a5518.author: slava chan
6d56c42d1d6a5518.statement:
R=5 FIXED-POWER PAYMENT OF A WIDE-IMBALANCE LITERAL C1 DYNAMIC NEAR-PRIME CHAMBER. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100 and K_0>=2. Let Q be sufficiently large. Let n=pv be squarefree, where p is prime and gcd(p,v)=1, put C=mathscr A h and m_eff=n/gcd(C,n), and assume Q^(1/2+kappa)<=m_eff<=Q^(6/5), p does not divide C, and m_eff=p r_eff with r_eff<=Q^(1/250). Let c be squarefree with nc<=Q^K_0. Let W be extended by zero, supported on Q<=q<2Q, and satisfy V_Q(W)<=Q^epsilon for every fixed epsilon>0.

Fix one MULTI-FREE dyadic box of fact 8eb30e55bdef6b27. Let B_* be its deterministically selected largest omitted coefficient-one scale and write B_*=Q^(b_*+o(1)). Convolve every other factor position into a variable a of scale A with divisor-bounded coefficient alpha_a, retain the selected free variable b of scale B_*, and assume
1/5<=b_*<=4/5,
Q^(17/20)<=p<=Q^(9/10).                                         (1)
Let S_box be the complete box sum with its signed convolution coefficient, literal product weight W(ab), gate gcd(ab,nc)=1, and phase e_n(C(ab)^(-1)). Then
|S_box|<=Q^(1-3/1000+o(1)).                                     (2)
In particular every genuine R3 dynamic near-prime box satisfying these hypotheses is paid. No estimate is asserted outside this wide-imbalance polygon or for r_eff>Q^(1/250).
6d56c42d1d6a5518.proof:
As in fact 17bda5948d58822e, squarefreeness and p not dividing C reduce the phase on the unit support exactly to a unit-numerator phase modulo m_eff=p r_eff. Fact 8eb30e55bdef6b27 gives AB_* comparable to Q, a fixed divisor-function bound for alpha_a, coefficient one on b, and retention of W and every coprimality gate. Thus fact 183c9310b93b9005 applies once its exponent inequalities are checked.

Put alpha=1-b_* and pi=log(p)/log(Q). From (1),
1/5<=alpha<=4/5,
17/20<=pi<=9/10.                                                 (3)
Consequently max(alpha,b_*)<=4/5<17/20<=pi with fixed slack. Moreover
b_*>=1/5>9/50>=pi/5,                                            (4)
so the interval hypothesis for the asymmetric supplier holds with moment parameter R=5.

For R=5, the two bracket gains of fact 183c9310b93b9005 are alpha and
1+b_*-(6/5)pi.
Equations (1),(3) give
alpha>=1/5,
1+b_*-(6/5)pi>=1+1/5-(6/5)(9/10)=3/25.                         (5)
Their minimum is at least 3/25. Hence the prime-modulus gain is at least
(7/(24*5))(3/25)=(7/120)(3/25)=7/1000.                         (6)
The CRT complement r_eff<=Q^(1/250) costs at most Q^(1/250). Since
7/1000-1/250=3/1000,                                            (7)
fact 183c9310b93b9005 proves (2), with every divisor, variation, dyadic, and fixed-convolution loss absorbed into Q^o(1). The R3 conclusion merely restricts the already bounded boxes.

6dcbe1a64e6c4b2d.title: Let L be a finite set. For each λ∈L let Q_λ and T_λ be finite sets, let γ_{λ,q}, b_{λ,t}, c_λ, and X_{λ,q,t} be complex numbers, and let H_λ>0. Define
6dcbe1a64e6c4b2d.author: slava chan
6dcbe1a64e6c4b2d.statement:
Let L be a finite set. For each λ∈L let Q_λ and T_λ be finite sets, let γ_{λ,q}, b_{λ,t}, c_λ, and X_{λ,q,t} be complex numbers, and let H_λ>0. Define
W=∑_{λ∈L} c_λ H_λ^{-1}∑_{q∈Q_λ}γ_{λ,q}∑_{t∈T_λ}b_{λ,t}X_{λ,q,t}
and E=∑_{λ∈L}∑_{q∈Q_λ}∑_{t∈T_λ}|X_{λ,q,t}|^2. Then
|W|≤A E^{1/2},
where
A^2=∑_{λ∈L}|c_λ|^2H_λ^{-2}(∑_{q∈Q_λ}|γ_{λ,q}|^2)(∑_{t∈T_λ}|b_{λ,t}|^2).
The constant A is sharp when the arrays X_{λ,q,t} are allowed to range over the full direct sum. In particular, let P≥1 and ε≥0. If, for every λ,
H_λ^{-2}(∑_{q∈Q_λ}|γ_{λ,q}|^2)(∑_{t∈T_λ}|b_{λ,t}|^2)≤P^{3+ε}
and if ∑_{λ∈L}|c_λ|^2≤P^{3+ε}, then |W|≤P^{3+ε}E^{1/2}. For one leaf with H_λ≥P, |Q_λ|≤P^3, |γ_{λ,q}|≤P^{ε/6}, and ∑_{t∈T_λ}|b_{λ,t}|^2≤P^{2+ε/3}, the corresponding squared coefficient norm is at most P^{3+2ε/3}, and hence the coefficient norm is at most P^{3/2+ε/3}.
6dcbe1a64e6c4b2d.proof:
Regard all coordinates (λ,q,t) as one finite Hilbert direct sum of copies of C. The coefficient of X_{λ,q,t} in W is
a_{λ,q,t}=c_λH_λ^{-1}γ_{λ,q}b_{λ,t}.
Therefore
∑_{λ,q,t}|a_{λ,q,t}|^2
=∑_{λ}|c_λ|^2H_λ^{-2}
 (∑_q|γ_{λ,q}|^2)(∑_t|b_{λ,t}|^2)
=A^2.
Cauchy–Schwarz gives |W|≤AE^{1/2}. Choosing the full array X proportional to the complex conjugate of the coefficient array, with the harmless conjugation adjusted to the displayed linear convention, shows that equality is attainable when A>0; when A=0 the claim is immediate. Thus A is sharp.

Under the first two power hypotheses,
A^2≤P^{3+ε}∑_λ|c_λ|^2≤P^{6+2ε}.
Since P≥1, taking nonnegative square roots gives A≤P^{3+ε}, proving the multi-leaf consequence.

For the final single-leaf assertion, the stated hypotheses give
H_λ^{-2}∑_q|γ_{λ,q}|^2∑_t|b_{λ,t}|^2
≤P^{-2}·P^3·P^{ε/3}·P^{2+ε/3}
=P^{3+2ε/3}.
Taking the nonnegative square root gives P^{3/2+ε/3}, as claimed.

glossary.A: The nonnegative ℓ2 norm of the full coefficient array.
glossary.E: The direct-sum squared energy of the X coordinates.
glossary.H_λ: The positive normalization scale in leaf λ.
glossary.L: A finite set of outer or separated leaf labels.
glossary.P: A real scale parameter satisfying P≥1.
glossary.Q_λ: The finite modulus-index set in leaf λ.
glossary.T_λ: The finite sample-index set in leaf λ.
glossary.X_{λ,q,t}: An arbitrary complex carrier or transformed coordinate.
glossary.b_{λ,t}: The sample coefficient in leaf λ.
glossary.c_λ: The outer reconstruction coefficient of leaf λ.
glossary.γ_{λ,q}: The modulus coefficient in leaf λ.

6e68e64eb87d4f42.title: CANONICAL RANK-THREE ROUGH TENSOR FOLLOWED BY A NO-COMPULSORY-PRIME SMOOTH RESIDUAL
6e68e64eb87d4f42.author: slava chan
6e68e64eb87d4f42.statement:
CANONICAL RANK-THREE ROUGH TENSOR FOLLOWED BY A NO-COMPULSORY-PRIME SMOOTH RESIDUAL.

Assume the actual scales and canonical factors L_b,b_0 from fact 9fd295b783317ab1. Put
 y_b=b/F_0,                                                   (1)
 F_b'=F_0/L_b.                                                (2)
Then
 L_b=product_{p|b;p>y_b}p,                                   (3)
and every prime divisor q of b_0 satisfies
 q<=y_b.                                                      (4)
Thus b_0 is y_b-smooth.

The residual scale ratio is exactly
 b_0/F_b'=b/F_0=y_b.                                         (5)
Consequently, for every prime q|b_0,
 b_0/q>=F_b'.                                                 (6)
Equivalently, the recursive centered projector
 P^{N_{L_b,b_0}}_{b_0,>F_b'}
in fact 9fd295b783317ab1 has no compulsory prime factor: there is no prime q|b_0 for which b_0/q<F_b'.

At the actual scales,
 y_b=Q^(1/3+2eta+o(1)),                                      (7)
and fact 9fd295b783317ab1 gives omega(L_b)<=3. Hence every nonzero high-conductor projector has the exact architecture
 P_b(a)
  =[a product of at most three compulsory centered
    prime-local traces]
   times
   [a centered projector on a Q^(1/3+2eta+o(1))-smooth
    squarefree residual modulus with no compulsory prime].  (8)

Equation (8) is a structural identity through its reference to the exact factorization in fact 9fd295b783317ab1; it is not an estimate. No A-process bound, ROP estimate, CEN-MZB estimate, C_small estimate or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
6e68e64eb87d4f42.proof:
For a prime p|b, the defining condition in fact 9fd295b783317ab1 is
 b/p<F_0.
Because all quantities are positive, this is equivalent to
 p>b/F_0=y_b.                                                (9)
Therefore definition (2) of L_b in that fact is exactly (3).

The prime divisors of b_0=b/L_b are precisely the prime divisors of b not selected into L_b. By (9), each such prime q satisfies q<=y_b, proving (4).

Using b=L_bb_0 and definition (2),
 b_0/F_b'
 =(b/L_b)/(F_0/L_b)
 =b/F_0
 =y_b,
which proves (5). If q|b_0, equation (4) and (5) give
 q<=y_b=b_0/F_b'.
Rearranging gives b_0/q>=F_b', proving (6). The last condition is the negation of the compulsory-prime condition for the residual modulus and cutoff, so the residual projector has no compulsory prime.

Finally, the actual scales in fact 9fd295b783317ab1 are
 b=Q^(4/3+o(1)), F_0=Q^(1-2eta+o(1)).
Their quotient is (7). That fact also proves omega(L_b)<=3 and the exact projector factorization. Combining these statements with (4)-(6) gives the architecture (8). This proves all assertions and scope restrictions.

6e7f7bb2682c39eb.title: Let H>=2 and let I_H=[H^2,2H^2) intersect Z. Let C,K,a,b,c,d be integers with C nonzero, a,b,c,d even, Q=((a,c),(-d,b)), and det(Q)=ab+cd=2K. Let r_2,r_3 be distinct primes in I_H. Define
6e7f7bb2682c39eb.author: slava chan
6e7f7bb2682c39eb.statement:
Let H>=2 and let I_H=[H^2,2H^2) intersect Z. Let C,K,a,b,c,d be integers with C nonzero, a,b,c,d even, Q=((a,c),(-d,b)), and det(Q)=ab+cd=2K. Let r_2,r_3 be distinct primes in I_H. Define
A=b r_3-d r_2,  B=a r_2-c r_3,  q=gcd(|A|,|B|),
D=a d r_2^2-b c r_3^2,  J=ab-cd.
The following are equivalent.

(I) There exist integers u,v and primes r_1,r_4 in I_H such that r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4 are pairwise distinct, uv is nonzero, P=r_1r_2r_3r_4 satisfies gcd(C,P)=1, and
A=2v r_1, B=2v r_4, q=2|v|, D=4vC, J=4uv.

(II) One has AB>0; q is a positive even integer; with s=1 if A>0 and s=-1 if A<0, the integers
r_1=|A|/q and r_4=|B|/q
are primes in I_H and are pairwise distinct from each other and from r_2,r_3; gcd(C,r_1r_2r_3r_4)=1; D=2sqC; and J is a nonzero multiple of 2q.

When these conditions hold, the recovery is unique:
v=sq/2, u=sJ/(2q), r_1=|A|/q, r_4=|B|/q.
Moreover all four coefficients a,b,c,d are automatically nonzero, and
b r_3r_4-a r_1r_2=d r_2r_4-c r_1r_3=2C,
b r_4+c r_1=2u r_2, d r_4+a r_1=2u r_3,
ab=K+2uv, cd=K-2uv, and
abcd=K^2-4u^2v^2 is nonzero.
Consequently every exceptional stratum A=0, B=0, AB<0, q odd, J=0, D=0, C=0, 2q not dividing J, a nonintegral/nonprime/out-of-range/repeated recovered corner, failure of gcd(C,P)=1, a zero coefficient, or K^2=4u^2v^2 contains no normalized unit state of type (I).
6e7f7bb2682c39eb.proof:
Assume (I). Since r_1 and r_4 are distinct primes, gcd(r_1,r_4)=1. Therefore
q=gcd(|2vr_1|,|2vr_4|)=2|v|.
Both A and B have the sign of v, so AB>0 and, writing s for this common sign, v=sq/2. The displayed formulas in (I) give D=4vC=2sqC and J=4uv=2sq u. Hence J is nonzero and 2q divides J, with u=sJ/(2q). Dividing |A| and |B| by q gives r_1 and r_4. The prime, dyadic, distinctness, and coprimality clauses in (II) are exactly those in (I).

Conversely assume (II) and define r_1,r_4,u,v by the recovery formulas. The parity of q and the divisibility 2q|J make u,v integers, and q>0 and J nonzero make uv nonzero. Since A and B have common sign s,
2v r_1=sq(|A|/q)=A and 2v r_4=sq(|B|/q)=B.
Also 2|v|=q, 4vC=2sqC=D, and
4uv=4(sq/2)(sJ/(2q))=J.
All remaining clauses of (I) are hypotheses in (II). This proves the equivalence and uniqueness.

It remains to derive the auxiliary identities and exceptional exclusions. From
a r_2-c r_3=2v r_4 and b r_3-d r_2=2v r_1,
we obtain
D=d r_2(a r_2)-c r_3(b r_3)
 =d r_2(c r_3+2v r_4)-c r_3(d r_2+2v r_1)
 =2v(d r_2r_4-c r_1r_3).
Since D=4vC and v is nonzero, division by 2v gives
d r_2r_4-c r_1r_3=2C.
Moreover
b r_3r_4-a r_1r_2
 =(d r_2+2v r_1)r_4-(c r_3+2v r_4)r_1
 =d r_2r_4-c r_1r_3=2C.

The two elementary inverse identities
bB+cA=(ab-cd)r_2=Jr_2,
dB+aA=(ab-cd)r_3=Jr_3
become, after substituting A=2vr_1, B=2vr_4, J=4uv and dividing by 2v,
b r_4+c r_1=2u r_2,
d r_4+a r_1=2u r_3.
Finally ab+cd=2K and ab-cd=4uv imply, by addition and subtraction,
ab=K+2uv and cd=K-2uv; multiplying yields abcd=K^2-4u^2v^2.

No coefficient can vanish. If a=0, the first complete-intersection identity gives b r_3r_4=2C, so the odd prime r_3 divides C, contrary to gcd(C,P)=1. If b=0, the same identity makes r_1 divide C. If c=0, the second identity makes r_2 divide C; if d=0, it makes r_1 divide C. Thus abcd is nonzero, and the last displayed product shows K^2-4u^2v^2 is nonzero. Also A,B,D,J,C are nonzero under (I). Every other listed exceptional case is precisely the negation of a necessary clause of (II), so the proved equivalence makes its normalized unit stratum empty.

glossary.A: the linear form b r_3-d r_2
glossary.B: the linear form a r_2-c r_3
glossary.D: the diagonal quadratic form a d r_2^2-b c r_3^2
glossary.J: the signed determinant ab-cd of the transport matrix
glossary.Q: the integer matrix with rows (a,c) and (-d,b)
glossary.d: negative of the lower-left coefficient of Q
glossary.r_i: the i-th ordered prime corner, for i=1,2,3,4
glossary.s: the common sign of A and B
glossary.u: the first recovered nonzero signed short coordinate
glossary.v: the second recovered nonzero signed short coordinate

6eacfadbc9a83247.title: EXACT FORWARD C1 COEFFICIENT NORMAL FORM, HARD-SOURCE POSITIVITY EXCLUSION, AND THE FINITE-BAND PROVENANCE GAP. Fix one forward literal high-source dyadic label and one exact outer-gcd layer of facts d8ba46800ba433c2 and 7131a06664967733. Thus
6eacfadbc9a83247.author: slava chan
6eacfadbc9a83247.statement:
EXACT FORWARD C1 COEFFICIENT NORMAL FORM, HARD-SOURCE POSITIVITY EXCLUSION, AND THE FINITE-BAND PROVENANCE GAP. Fix one forward literal high-source dyadic label and one exact outer-gcd layer of facts d8ba46800ba433c2 and 7131a06664967733. Thus
d=gs, r=gn, gcd(s,n)=1, L_0=N/g,
s m+n k=L_0,                                                (1)
and the literal forward source amplitude is
F_{g,s,n}(t)
 =log(t)log((L_0-st)/n)
  cal W(gs/D,t/M,gn/R,(L_0-st)/(nK)),                       (2)
extended by zero outside its compact positive support. Its Fourier transform is
Fhat_{g,s,n}(xi)=integral_R F_{g,s,n}(t)e(-xi t)dt.          (3)
For h nonzero, the original nonzero-Poisson coefficient is
mu(gs)mu(gn)n^(-1)Fhat_{g,s,n}(h/n),                        (4)
and the source phase is e_n(L_0 h sbar).

Fix a complete one-rough-prime C1 coordinate as in fact efd5ace01f0a6c11, so
n=vp,                                                        (5)
where v is squarefree, p is prime, gcd(v,p)=1, p does not divide gsv, and the exact C1 marker sign is -mu(v). Put
c=gcd(s,L_0), s=cq, L_0=cA.                                 (6)
Then g,c,q,n are pairwise coprime squarefree positive integers, gcd(q,A)=1, and
mu(gs)mu(gn)=-mu(c)mu(q)mu(v).                              (7)
Moreover
e_n(L_0 h sbar)
 =e_n(Ah qbar)
 =e(Ah/(qn))e_q(-Ah nbar).                                 (8)
Consequently, after extracting the external normalization H_P^(-1), the exact coefficient multiplying the reduced reciprocal phase e_q(-Ah nbar) is
C_C1(c,q,v,p,h)
 =-mu(c)mu(q)mu(v)
   [H_P/(vp)]Fhat_{g,cq,vp}(h/(vp))
   e(Ah/(qvp)),                                             (9)
times every retained literal zero-one or signed bookkeeping factor at that exact coordinate. In the notation of fact 294ac3b02b065aec, before any further projective separation one may therefore identify
c_q=mu(q), xi_v=mu(v), eta_c=-mu(c),
U_nat(q,h,v,p)=[H_P/(vp)]Fhat_{g,cq,vp}(h/(vp)),            (10)
with the Archimedean factor e(Ah/(qvp)) kept exactly, while the remaining chi_nat is precisely the product of inherited bookkeeping factors not written in (9). Formula (9) does not permit an unrecombined q-dependent deletion to be absorbed into mu(q).

The original hard source has a positivity property absent from the abstract source set of fact 38bc0e88e17aef0e. If an integer pair (m,k) contributes to (1)-(2), then m>0 and k>0. The equation
cq m+(vp)k=cA
and gcd(c,vp)=1 imply c divides k. Define the reduced complementary variable
k_red=k/c.                                                  (11)
Then
q m+(vp)k_red=A,  k_red>0, and hence qm<A.                  (12)
By contrast, on the prime-q actual-source family cal X of fact 38bc0e88e17aef0e one has v=2, n=2p, Q=floor(p^(4/5)), 1<=A<2p, and Q<=q,m<2Q. For every sufficiently large p,
qm>=Q^2>2p>A,
so its reduced source variable is
k_red=(A-qm)/(2p)<0.                                        (13)
Thus every atom of that accepted coherent prime-q saturator is excluded by the genuine hard-source positivity condition (12).

There remains an exact provenance gap before this exclusion can be used inside the finite-band PMD window of facts 294ac3b02b065aec and 0a7dc0c20f026253. Fact 44e700816602dd36 states that a proper finite h-band has no complete Poisson source identity, and fact 05cbed389411618a states that the accepted finite-band coefficient hypotheses do not supply an h-independent physical Fourier representation retaining every mask. Therefore (9)-(13) do not by themselves prove that the finite-band coefficient chi_ell in fact 294ac3b02b065aec contains the hard-source positivity selector (12). The exact missing bridge is a band-restoration or coefficient identity which maps the complete natural coefficient (9), with the positive support of (2), to the finite-band row while preserving every inherited mask. This theorem proves the natural forward C1 coefficient formula and removes the previously used prime-q saturator from the complete hard source, but proves no Gadd^(-1) estimate, no finite-band PMD closure, and no Goldbach conclusion.
6eacfadbc9a83247.proof:
Facts d8ba46800ba433c2 and 7131a06664967733 give (1)-(4), including the exact amplitude (2), the Fourier convention, and the phase e_n(L_0hsbar). Fact efd5ace01f0a6c11 gives the complete C1 factorization n=vp, squarefreeness, coprimality, and the marker sign -mu(v).

Because mu(gs)mu(gn) is nonzero, gs and gn are squarefree. Hence g,s,n are squarefree and gcd(g,s)=gcd(g,n)=1. The source also has gcd(s,n)=1. Since c divides s and q=s/c, the integers c,q are coprime squarefree, and both are coprime to g and n. Since c=gcd(s,L_0), dividing s=cq and L_0=cA by c gives gcd(q,A)=1. Therefore
mu(gs)mu(gn)=mu(g)^2mu(s)mu(n)
=mu(c)mu(q)mu(v)mu(p)
=-mu(c)mu(q)mu(v),
because mu(g)^2=1, n=vp, gcd(v,p)=1, and mu(p)=-1. This proves (7).

Modulo n, multiplication by c sends the inverse of cq to the inverse of q, so
L_0 sbar=cA (cq)bar is congruent to A qbar modulo n.
This proves the first equality in (8). For coprime q,n, additive reciprocity gives
qbar/n is congruent modulo one to 1/(qn)-nbar/q.
Multiplying by Ah and exponentiating proves the second equality in (8).

Multiply (4) by the source phase and use (7)-(8). The resulting summand is
-mu(c)mu(q)mu(v)n^(-1)Fhat_{g,cq,n}(h/n)
 e(Ah/(qn))e_q(-Ah nbar).
Writing n=vp and n^(-1)=H_P^(-1)[H_P/(vp)] proves (9). Definitions (10) are then direct, with every other inherited factor left where the cited literal source facts place it.

The amplitude (2) is extended by zero outside its compact positive support. If an integer t=m contributes, then its two source variables m and
k=(L_0-sm)/n=(cA-cqm)/(vp)
are positive. The equality cq m+(vp)k=cA reduced modulo c gives
(vp)k congruent 0 modulo c.
Because c is coprime to n=vp, c divides k. Thus k_red=k/c is a positive integer. Dividing the source equation by c gives
qm+(vp)k_red=A.
Therefore qm<A, proving (11)-(12).

For the family in fact 38bc0e88e17aef0e, Q=floor(p^(4/5)). For all sufficiently large p, Q>=p^(4/5)/2, hence
Q^2>=p^(8/5)/4>2p.
Since q,m>=Q and A<2p, qm>=Q^2>2p>A. Hence (A-qm)/(2p)<0, proving (13). This variable is exactly the reduced variable k_red in the normalized equation qm+(vp)k_red=A. Therefore none of those atoms obeys (12).

Finally, fact 44e700816602dd36 explicitly separates the finite-band identity from the complete source identity, and fact 05cbed389411618a explicitly states that the accepted literal finite-band hypotheses do not furnish the required h-independent physical coefficient formula with all masks. Thus no cited predecessor licenses transporting (12) into the finite-band chi_ell. The final paragraph states exactly this missing implication and does not claim it.

glossary.U_nat: The unseparated natural Fourier amplitude H_P/(vp) times Fhat at h/(vp).
glossary.cal W: The fixed scaled-smooth compactly supported four-variable source weight.
glossary.chi_nat: The product of inherited literal bookkeeping factors not explicitly displayed in C_C1.
glossary.k_red: The positive reduced complementary source variable k/c after target-gcd descent.

6edc174d83447911.title: LEGAL ANATOMY-BY-ANATOMY ENDPOINT CRITICAL BLOCKS, SHARP DIRECT FOUR-TERM DEFICITS, AND THE LITERAL FIVE-ANATOMY CONSUMER
6edc174d83447911.author: slava chan
6edc174d83447911.statement:
LEGAL ANATOMY-BY-ANATOMY ENDPOINT CRITICAL BLOCKS, SHARP DIRECT FOUR-TERM DEFICITS, AND THE LITERAL FIVE-ANATOMY CONSUMER.

Fix \(0<\kappa\le1/100\), put
\[
 \sigma=\kappa/100,\qquad \beta_m=6/5-12\sigma/5,
\]
and let
\[
 \beta=\beta(Q)=6/5-C/\log Q                                \tag{1}
\]
for a fixed \(C>0\) and sufficiently large \(Q\). Put
\[
 B=Q^\beta,\qquad H_T=B/Q,
\]
and work at \(G=1\), hence \(H_P=H_T\).

Each of the following is a genuine nonempty factor block in the exact
stopping, Vaughan, or rough-prime coefficient calculus and satisfies every
scale, bounded-coefficient, product and coprimality hypothesis needed for a
direct application of fact \(95626318cdcc099f\).

(i) \(B\): an exact first-crossing block \(r=uy\) in which \(u\) and
\(y\) each consist of three distinct primes of scale
\(Q^{\beta/6+O(1/\log Q)}\). Its two factor exponents are
\[
 \beta/2+O(1/\log Q),\qquad \beta/2+O(1/\log Q).              \tag{2}
\]

(ii) \(C1\): after the exact von-Mangoldt replacement and Vaughan identity
of fact \(29c43cef40f2e79b\), a nonzero lower-end Type-II box whose
two factor exponents are
\[
 \beta/3+O(1/\log Q),\qquad 2\beta/3+O(1/\log Q).             \tag{3}
\]

(iii) \(C2\): a unit small factor followed by two distinct rough primes,
each of exponent
\[
 \beta/2+O(1/\log Q).                                        \tag{4}
\]

(iv) \(C3\): a unit small factor followed by three distinct rough primes,
each of exponent
\[
 \beta/3+O(1/\log Q).                                        \tag{5}
\]

(v) \(C4\): a unit small factor followed by four distinct rough primes,
each of exponent
\[
 \beta/4+O(1/\log Q).                                        \tag{6}
\]
The \(C4\) scale is legal precisely on the structural top range
\(\beta\ge\beta_m\), up to the harmless dyadic endpoint error.

Among the direct two-slot applications supplied by these displayed
factorizations, the best endpoint choice has \(s=\beta/2+O(1/\log Q)\)
for \(B,C2,C4\), and \(s=\beta/3+O(1/\log Q)\) for \(C1,C3\).
Consequently fact \(175003bf27fb8e0f\) gives the following worst
certified right-hand-side savings:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
 \text{anatomy}&\text{binding direct four-term saving}\\ \hline
 B&(6-5\beta)/8+o(1)\\
 C1&(6-5\beta)/12+o(1)\\
 C2&(6-5\beta)/8+o(1)\\
 C3&(6-5\beta)/12+o(1)\\
 C4&(6-5\beta)/8+o(1).
\end{array}                                                   \tag{7}
\]
For \(C1,C3\), the third four-term expression has the larger but still
vanishing saving \((6-5\beta)/6+o(1)\). Under (1), all gains in
(7) are only constants. Thus the existing direct four-term local supplier
does not certify one fixed power \(Q^{-\delta}\), uniformly in the complete
pre-\(6/5\) range, for any of the five anatomy coefficient classes.

This conclusion is solely a no-fit for direct use of the displayed
nonnegative theorem right-hand side on legal nonempty coefficient blocks.
It is not a lower bound for the literal selected trace, does not assert
that its source coefficients saturate the theorem, and does not rule out
source-specific cancellation, a different factorization, or a different
theorem.

Define the literal non-\(A\) top-sliver aggregate
\[
 \mathcal T_{\rm nonA,top}
 =\mathcal T_B+\mathcal T_{C1}+\mathcal T_{C2}
   +\mathcal T_{C3}+\mathcal T_{C4}                            \tag{8}
\]
by the exact source-preserving ledger of fact \(e58fc7c00f1683e6\).
The smallest single uniform supplier with full required anatomy coverage,
while still permitting cancellation between different anatomies, is the
joint estimate
\[
 |\mathcal T_{\rm nonA,top}|
 \ll GQ^{2-\delta_*}\qquad(G\ge1),                            \tag{CS5-F}
\]
and
\[
 |\mathcal T_{\rm nonA,top}|
 \ll Q^{2-\delta_*}
 \quad(Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\le G\le Q^{\sigma-\eta}),             \tag{CS5-N}
\]
for one fixed \(\delta_*>0\), uniformly for
\(\beta_m\le\beta<6/5\). The sum in (8) must retain, before its first
absolute value, the selected \(N\), literal source coefficient, fixed
\(U\), parent, orientation, exact outer gcd \(g\), actual \(G\), target,
every paired actual frequency and phase, target-gcd, prime-order/equal-cell,
collision, deletion and provenance coordinate of
\(e58fc7c00f1683e6\). The normalization in (CS5-F)--(CS5-N) is the
literal fixed-\(g\) consumer normalization. CS5 is an open interface, not
a proved estimate.

A \(C4\)-only estimate cannot replace CS5 unless a verifier-accepted
estimate controls the \(B,C1,C2,C3\) complement or a verifier-accepted
sign/localization theorem removes it. No estimate for the separate \(A\)
anatomy, complete top sliver, endpoint, or Goldbach is asserted.
6edc174d83447911.proof:
We construct the five legal critical blocks using only text-based prime
selection. Fact \(b7fcb27a091203e5\), through its cited prime-in-a-dyadic-
interval theorem, supplies a prime between \(X\) and \(2X\) for every
sufficiently large \(X\). Applying it to finitely many disjoint
constant multiples of the same power scale gives any fixed number of
distinct primes on that exponent scale. Constant factors contribute only
\(O(1/\log Q)\) to logarithmic exponents.

For \(B\), choose six distinct primes
\(\pi_i=Q^{\beta/6+O(1/\log Q)}\). Since (1) approaches \(6/5\),
for sufficiently large \(Q\)
\[
 {\beta\over6}<\beta-1+\sigma,                                \tag{9}
\]
\[
 {\beta\over3}<2\beta-2+3\sigma
 <{\beta\over2}.                                              \tag{10}
\]
Thus every \(\pi_i\le L=Q^{\beta-1+\sigma}\), every product of two
of them is at most the stopping height
\(S_0=Q^{2\beta-2+3\sigma}\), and every product of three exceeds
\(S_0\). Put \(y=\pi_1\pi_2\pi_3\) and
\(u=\pi_4\pi_5\pi_6\). There is no prime in \((L,Z)\), and
\(j_{(L,Z)}(u)=0\). In the definition of
\(\Gamma_{3;L,S_0}(y)\), removal of any one prime leaves a two-prime
product at most \(S_0\), so \(\Gamma_{3;L,S_0}(y)=1\).
The exact \(B\) coefficient in fact \(7c1f38cfbb8d0569\) is therefore
nonzero. Also \((u,y)=1\), \(uy\asymp B=QH_T\), and (2) follows.
Taking bounded singleton coefficients on these factors, a modulus
\(q\asymp Q\) coprime to \(uy\), target \(A=1\), unit twist one, and a
singleton frequency gives a nonempty input satisfying every hypothesis
of fact \(95626318cdcc099f\).

For \(C2,C3,C4\), take the small factor \(v=1\) and respectively
\(j=2,3,4\) distinct primes
\[
 p_i=Q^{\beta/j+O(1/\log Q)}.
\]
Their product is comparable to \(B\), they are pairwise coprime, and their
convolution coefficients are bounded by a fixed divisor function. They
are rough because
\[
 {\beta\over2}>{3\over2}-\beta-3\sigma,\qquad
 {\beta\over3}>{3\over2}-\beta-3\sigma
\]
near \(6/5\), while
\[
 {\beta\over4}\ge {3\over2}-\beta-3\sigma
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \beta\ge6/5-12\sigma/5=\beta_m.                              \tag{11}
\]
There are no small or interval primes in these products, so fact
\(7c1f38cfbb8d0569\) places them in the exact \(C2,C3,C4\)
classes with nonzero signs. Splitting the distinct prime set into two
nonempty groups preserves joint coprimality and gives a legal two-slot
input to fact \(95626318cdcc099f\), after the same harmless choice of
\(q,A,h\) as above.

For \(C1\), take its small factor \(v=1\) and prime-variable scale
\(P=Q^{\beta+O(1/\log Q)}\). Replace the prime indicator by
\(\Lambda(n)/\log n\) minus the exact proper-prime-power correction;
this identity is pointwise. Apply fact \(29c43cef40f2e79b\) with
\(U=P^{1/3}\). We show that its lower Type-II range is genuinely
nonempty, not merely allowed by an inequality. Choose distinct primes
\(d,m\) of scales \(P^{1/6+O(1/\log P)}\), with constant multiples
chosen so that
\[
 l=dm>U,\qquad d,m\le U.
\]
Choose \(k=P^{2/3+O(1/\log P)}\), coprime to \(l\), and restrict to
the dyadic product box \(lk\asymp P\). In the second convolution term of
the exact Vaughan identity, the coefficient of \(l\) is
\[
 a_l=\sum_{\substack{d'm'=l\\d'\le U,\ m'\le U}}
       \mu(d')\Lambda(m').
\]
Because \(l=dm>U\) with \(d,m\) distinct primes, the only nonzero
terms are \((d',m')=(d,m)\) and \((m,d)\), and
\[
 a_l=-\log m-\log d\ne0.                                     \tag{12}
\]
Thus this is a genuine nonzero Type-II box, with divisor-log coefficient,
factor exponents (3), product scale \(P\asymp B\), and coprime slots.
After normalizing its bounded singleton coefficients, it is a legal input
to fact \(95626318cdcc099f\). This is a statement about the direct
Vaughan-box calculus, not a claim that the original prime-only term is
large; the exact identity may cancel different boxes.

It remains to identify the best direct grouping and its RHS deficit.
For \(B\), the exact separated stopping slots are the two three-prime
factors in (2); swapping them changes nothing. For \(C2\), the only
nontrivial split has exponent \(\beta/2\). For \(C4\), a one-versus-three
split has \(s=\beta/4\) or \(3\beta/4\), which is outside the balanced
window near \(6/5\), while the two-versus-two split has \(s=\beta/2\).
For the \(C1\) Type-II box, the two orientations are
\(s=\beta/3\) and \(2\beta/3\); the latter is above the upper balanced
wall near \(6/5\), so the former is best. The same comparison for \(C3\)
selects one prime, \(s=\beta/3\), rather than two. Apply the exact RHS
calculation in fact \(175003bf27fb8e0f\): \(s=\beta/2\) gives
the second-term saving \((6-5\beta)/8+o(1)\), and
\(s=\beta/3\) gives the first- and third-term savings
\((6-5\beta)/12+o(1)\) and
\((6-5\beta)/6+o(1)\). This proves (7). Under (1) those factors are
constants, so the nonnegative RHS of the direct theorem cannot certify a
uniform fixed power. No lower bound for the input sums has been inferred.

Finally fact \(e58fc7c00f1683e6\) gives exactly (8), with all listed
coordinates retained and no sign on a proper anatomy. Hence CS5 is one
