joint interface with complete anatomy coverage and permits cross-anatomy
cancellation. Fact \(7c1f38cfbb8d0569\) proves by an explicit signed
one-incidence model that total negativity and exact anatomy alone do not
force mass into a prescribed class. Put that negative incidence in any of
\(B,C1,C2,C3\) and the \(C4\) sum is zero; therefore \(C4\)-only
control requires an independent complement estimate or sign theorem. The
statement explicitly leaves \(A\) and the full top sliver outside scope.

glossary.CS5_lit: The proposed single joint literal fixed-power trace estimate for the complete B,C1,C2,C3,C4 top-sliver projection.
glossary.critical B block: A nonempty exact first-crossing block with stopping factor and complement both of exponent beta/2.
glossary.critical C1 box: A nonzero lower-end Type-II box of the exact Vaughan expansion with exponents beta/3 and 2 beta/3.
glossary.critical Cj block: A j-rough-prime block whose rough-prime exponents are all beta/j and whose small factor is one.

6efd6c9a3a904a9e.title: FIXED-PRIME SCALAR RECIPROCAL-FRAME LARGE SIEVE WITH THE LITERAL UNIT MASK
6efd6c9a3a904a9e.author: slava chan
6efd6c9a3a904a9e.statement:
FIXED-PRIME SCALAR RECIPROCAL-FRAME LARGE SIEVE WITH THE LITERAL UNIT MASK.

Let p>2 be prime, let A be a nonzero residue modulo p, and let Q,S>=1 be real. Let cal I and cal J be finite intervals of consecutive integers of lengths at most Q and S, respectively. Let eta_u be arbitrary complex coefficients supported on u in cal J. For a in cal I define
 T_{p,A}eta(a)
  =sum_{u in cal J;p does not divide u}
    eta_u{e_p(A(au)^(-1))+1/(p-1)},                         (1)
where (au)^(-1) is taken modulo p and the transform is evaluated only when p does not divide a.

Then
 sum_{a in cal I;p does not divide a}|T_{p,A}eta(a)|^2
 <=(Q/p+1)(S+p)
   sum_{u in cal J;p does not divide u}|eta_u|^2.            (2)
If Q>=p and S>=p, then
 sum_{a in cal I;p does not divide a}|T_{p,A}eta(a)|^2
 <=4QS/p
   sum_{u in cal J;p does not divide u}|eta_u|^2.            (3)
In particular, (3) is stronger than the same bound with an additional factor Q^epsilon for any epsilon>0 and Q>=1.

The theorem is scalar: eta_u is independent of a. It does not allow the recursive complementary projector to be inserted as an arbitrary a-dependent coefficient. No vector-modulated estimate, TRI-CROSS or ROP estimate, CEN-MZB estimate, C_small estimate or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
6efd6c9a3a904a9e.proof:
For each nonzero residue C modulo p put
 E_C
  =sum_{u in cal J;p does not divide u;Au^(-1)=C mod p}eta_u. (4)
Because A is nonzero, u mod p -> Au^(-1) mod p is a permutation of the nonzero residues. For every nonzero a,
 T_{p,A}eta(a)
  =sum_{C nonzero}E_C
    {e_p(Ca^(-1))+1/(p-1)}.                                 (5)

Fact 0d1daae6c3854186 gives the normalized tight-frame identity
 1/(p-1)sum_{a mod p;a nonzero}
  |sum_{C nonzero}E_C
    {e_p(Ca^(-1))+1/(p-1)}|^2
 =
 p/(p-1)
 {sum_C|E_C|^2
  -1/(p-1)|sum_CE_C|^2}.                                   (6)
Delete the final nonnegative subtraction and multiply by p-1. This gives
 sum_{a mod p;a nonzero}|T_{p,A}eta(a)|^2
 <=p sum_C|E_C|^2.                                          (7)

Every residue modulo p occurs among the consecutive integers in cal I at most Q/p+1 times. Therefore
 sum_{a in cal I;p does not divide a}|T_{p,A}eta(a)|^2
 <=(Q/p+1)
   sum_{a mod p;a nonzero}|T_{p,A}eta(a)|^2.                (8)

For fixed C, the corresponding u in (4) occupy one residue class modulo p, which occurs in cal J at most S/p+1 times. Cauchy's inequality in that residue class gives
 |E_C|^2
 <=(S/p+1)
   sum_{u in cal J;Au^(-1)=C mod p}|eta_u|^2.               (9)
Sum (9) over C:
 sum_C|E_C|^2
 <=(S/p+1)
   sum_{u in cal J;p does not divide u}|eta_u|^2.           (10)
Combining (7), (8) and (10) gives the coefficient
 (Q/p+1)p(S/p+1)
 =(Q/p+1)(S+p),
which proves (2).

If Q>=p, then Q/p+1<=2Q/p. If S>=p, then S+p<=2S. Insert these two inequalities into (2) to obtain (3). Since Q^epsilon>=1 for Q>=1, the final comparison follows. The proof uses eta_u only through the scalar residue sums (4), so it makes no vector-dependent claim. This proves all scope restrictions.

glossary.T_{p,A}eta(a): The fixed-p scalar centered reciprocal-frame transform of eta.

6f82723a1b084485.title: Let x≥2 be real with N=2x an integer. Fix real numbers 1/2<a<b<1, a real function W supported in [a,b], a real function ψ on the positive reals with ψ(u)=0 for 0<u≤1, a real number D_* with 1≤D_*≤x, and a real function Φ supported in [1/2,2] such that Σ_{j∈Z}Φ(t/2^j)=1 for every t>0. Define
6f82723a1b084485.author: slava chan
6f82723a1b084485.statement:
Let x≥2 be real with N=2x an integer. Fix real numbers 1/2<a<b<1, a real function W supported in [a,b], a real function ψ on the positive reals with ψ(u)=0 for 0<u≤1, a real number D_* with 1≤D_*≤x, and a real function Φ supported in [1/2,2] such that Σ_{j∈Z}Φ(t/2^j)=1 for every t>0. Define
H_{N,W,ψ}=Σ_{d,m≥1} μ(d)log(m)W(dm/x)ψ(d/D_*)Λ(N-dm).
For positive dyadic D,M,R,K define
Q_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;R,K)=Σ_{d,m,r,k≥1;dm+rk=N} μ(d)μ(r)log(m)log(k)W(dm/x)ψ(d/D_*)Φ(d/D)Φ(m/M)Φ(r/R)Φ(k/K).
Let A_N>0 and E_N be real numbers such that H_{N,W,ψ}=-A_N + E_N and |E_N|≤A_N/2. Then there exists a positive dyadic quadruple (D,M,R,K) satisfying
Q_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;R,K)≤-A_N/[2(ceil(log_2 x)+4)^4].
In particular, if for this fixed N one has A_N=c_W 𝔠(N)x with c_W>0 and 𝔠(N)>0, then this same N has a real negative dyadic block of absolute size at least c_W𝔠(N)x/[2(ceil(log_2 x)+4)^4]. No averaging over N is used.
6f82723a1b084485.proof: Fact cdb5cefbc7333591 proves, for exactly the definitions reproduced in the statement, that H_{N,W,ψ} is the sum of at most L_x=(ceil(log_2 x)+4)^4 nonzero real dyadic blocks Q_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;R,K). The assumed identity and error bound give H_{N,W,ψ}=-A_N+E_N≤-A_N/2. Suppose, for contradiction, that every nonzero block were greater than -A_N/(2L_x). If J is the number of nonzero blocks, then J≤L_x and their sum would be greater than -J A_N/(2L_x), which is at least -A_N/2. This contradicts H_{N,W,ψ}≤-A_N/2. Hence one block satisfies Q_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;R,K)≤-A_N/(2L_x). Substituting A_N=c_W𝔠(N)x gives the displayed specialization. The argument fixes N throughout and therefore contains no average over N.

glossary.A_N: a positive real main-term magnitude for the fixed integer N
glossary.E_N: the real error in the identity for H_{N,W,ψ}
glossary.H_{N,W,ψ}: the smooth reflected Möbius source defined in the statement
glossary.Q_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;R,K): the dyadic block defined in the statement
glossary.Φ: a real dyadic partition function supported in [1/2,2]
glossary.𝔠(N): a positive real arithmetic factor attached to N

6f97cd0bbc7daa5a.title: Let c and r be integers at least 2. Let J_c and J_r denote the all-ones matrices of sizes c and r, let I_c and I_{cr} denote identity matrices, and set A=(J_c-I_c) tensor (J_r/r) and G=I_{cr}+A, with rows and columns indexed by pairs (i,a) with 1<=i<=c and 1<=a<=r. Then A is real symmetric with spectrum consisting of c-1 with multiplicity one, -1 with multiplicity c-1, and 0 with multiplicity c(r-1); G is positive semidefinite with spectrum consisting of c with multiplicity one, 0 with multiplicity c-1, and 1 with multiplicity c(r-1). Entrywise, G_{(i,a),(i,a)}=1, G_{(i,a),(i,b)}=0 for a different from b, and G_{(i,a),(j,b)}=1/r for i different from j. Moreover every row of A has absolute row sum c-1, the operator norm of A is c-1, and the Hilbert-Schmidt norm of A is sqrt(c(c-1)). Consequently, for every integer H at least 2, taking c=H, r=H^2 and multiplying G and A by s=H^15 gives a positive semidefinite Gram matrix with diagonal H^15, zero same-cell off-diagonal entries, and cross-cell entries H^13, while the absolute cross-row sum and cross-cell operator norm are H^15(H-1), and the cross-cell Hilbert-Schmidt norm is H^15 sqrt(H(H-1)). In particular, positive semidefiniteness, Hermitian symmetry, perfect same-cell off-diagonal cancellation, and the pointwise cross-edge bound H^13 do not by themselves imply an o(H^15), or an O(H^(15-delta)) for any fixed delta>0, cross-cell operator bound. Thus these formal Gram inputs alone cannot prove any PAVG26/PAVG27-type conclusion whose required normalized cross-cell operator is o(1) or has a fixed-power saving. This is an abstract finite-dimensional Gram countermodel to that method of inference, not an arithmetic counterexample and not a claim that an actual WF-RPS Gram matrix has these entries
6f97cd0bbc7daa5a.author: slava chan
6f97cd0bbc7daa5a.statement: Let c and r be integers at least 2. Let J_c and J_r denote the all-ones matrices of sizes c and r, let I_c and I_{cr} denote identity matrices, and set A=(J_c-I_c) tensor (J_r/r) and G=I_{cr}+A, with rows and columns indexed by pairs (i,a) with 1<=i<=c and 1<=a<=r. Then A is real symmetric with spectrum consisting of c-1 with multiplicity one, -1 with multiplicity c-1, and 0 with multiplicity c(r-1); G is positive semidefinite with spectrum consisting of c with multiplicity one, 0 with multiplicity c-1, and 1 with multiplicity c(r-1). Entrywise, G_{(i,a),(i,a)}=1, G_{(i,a),(i,b)}=0 for a different from b, and G_{(i,a),(j,b)}=1/r for i different from j. Moreover every row of A has absolute row sum c-1, the operator norm of A is c-1, and the Hilbert-Schmidt norm of A is sqrt(c(c-1)). Consequently, for every integer H at least 2, taking c=H, r=H^2 and multiplying G and A by s=H^15 gives a positive semidefinite Gram matrix with diagonal H^15, zero same-cell off-diagonal entries, and cross-cell entries H^13, while the absolute cross-row sum and cross-cell operator norm are H^15(H-1), and the cross-cell Hilbert-Schmidt norm is H^15 sqrt(H(H-1)). In particular, positive semidefiniteness, Hermitian symmetry, perfect same-cell off-diagonal cancellation, and the pointwise cross-edge bound H^13 do not by themselves imply an o(H^15), or an O(H^(15-delta)) for any fixed delta>0, cross-cell operator bound. Thus these formal Gram inputs alone cannot prove any PAVG26/PAVG27-type conclusion whose required normalized cross-cell operator is o(1) or has a fixed-power saving. This is an abstract finite-dimensional Gram countermodel to that method of inference, not an arithmetic counterexample and not a claim that an actual WF-RPS Gram matrix has these entries.
6f97cd0bbc7daa5a.proof:
The all-ones matrix J_c has eigenvalue c on the constant vector and eigenvalue 0 on its orthogonal complement. Hence J_c-I_c has eigenvalue c-1 on the constant vector and eigenvalue -1 with multiplicity c-1. Likewise J_r/r is the orthogonal projection onto the constant vectors in the r-dimensional factor, so its eigenvalues are 1 once and 0 with multiplicity r-1. The eigenvalues of a tensor product are the pairwise products of the eigenvalues of its factors. Therefore A has eigenvalue c-1 once, eigenvalue -1 with multiplicity c-1, and eigenvalue 0 with multiplicity c(r-1). Adding the identity gives the asserted spectrum of G. All its eigenvalues are nonnegative, so G is positive semidefinite. In particular it is the Gram matrix of some finite family of vectors, for example the columns obtained from a positive semidefinite square root of G.

For the entries, (J_c-I_c)_{ij} is zero when i=j and one when i is different from j, whereas every entry of J_r/r is 1/r. Thus A_{(i,a),(j,b)} is zero when i=j and 1/r when i is different from j. Adding I_{cr} gives diagonal entries one, zero off-diagonal entries inside each cell, and cross-cell entries 1/r.

Fix a row (i,a). There are (c-1)r cross-cell columns, each of absolute value 1/r, and all other entries of A in that row vanish. Therefore its absolute row sum is (c-1)r/r=c-1. Since A is real symmetric, its operator norm is the largest absolute value of its eigenvalues, namely c-1. Its squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm is the sum of the squares of its eigenvalues, namely (c-1)^2+(c-1)=c(c-1). Equivalently, there are c(c-1)r^2 ordered cross-cell entries of size 1/r. This proves the norm formulas.

Now put c=H, r=H^2 and s=H^15. Multiplication by s preserves positive semidefiniteness. The diagonal becomes H^15, same-cell off-diagonal entries remain zero, and cross-cell entries equal s/r=H^13. The absolute cross-row sum and operator norm of sA both equal s(c-1)=H^15(H-1), while its Hilbert-Schmidt norm is s sqrt(c(c-1))=H^15 sqrt(H(H-1)). Dividing the operator norm by H^15 gives H-1, which neither tends to zero nor is bounded by H^(-delta) for any fixed positive delta. Hence no universal implication from the listed formal hypotheses to such a cross-operator saving can hold. The construction uses no arithmetic packet, window, phase, support, or Ursell data, so it only disproves that abstract method of inference and makes no arithmetic counterexample claim.

glossary.H: An integer scale parameter at least two.
glossary.I_c: The c by c identity matrix.
glossary.I_{cr}: The identity matrix of size cr.
glossary.J_c: The c by c matrix whose entries are all one.
glossary.J_r: The r by r matrix whose entries are all one.
glossary.PAVG26/PAVG27-type conclusion: Any target in the project requiring the cross-cell operator normalized by H^15 to tend to zero or save a fixed power.
glossary.c: The number of cells in the block Gram model.
glossary.r: The number of replica indices in each cell.
glossary.s: The positive scalar used to set the diagonal scale.

703f9c67394fc2fc.title: CRIT-PRIM-ORTH(tau): EXACT PRIMITIVE-CHARACTER ORTHOGONALITY AND SQUAREFREE COFACTOR KERNEL FOR A CLEAN CRITICAL PHYSICAL AP BLOCK. Fix tau>0 and one orientation, exact g,c and selected target ell=N/(gc) in the critical-W projection of facts 8d9feea8c44da2c8 and a3103a7fbc2dc2ed. Thus the descended physical equation is
703f9c67394fc2fc.author: slava chan
703f9c67394fc2fc.statement:
CRIT-PRIM-ORTH(tau): EXACT PRIMITIVE-CHARACTER ORTHOGONALITY AND SQUAREFREE COFACTOR KERNEL FOR A CLEAN CRITICAL PHYSICAL AP BLOCK. Fix tau>0 and one orientation, exact g,c and selected target ell=N/(gc) in the critical-W projection of facts 8d9feea8c44da2c8 and a3103a7fbc2dc2ed. Thus the descended physical equation is
q t+kappa n=ell,                                                  (1)
q is squarefree on the nonzero Mobius support, and
gcd(q,ell)=gcd(q,n)=1.                                           (2)
Put m=kappa n. Fix a finite literal amplitude A_lit(q,kappa,n), defined on every integer triple in its support, with
t=(ell-kappa n)/q                                                (3)
retained as its actual quotient argument. It may contain the q/source dyadic weights, psi, Phi, both source logarithms, the appropriate orientation-specific W, every surviving gcd and source mask, and every frozen label. Assume this is a clean character-expandable block: every discrete mask has either been legally recombined or has a specified extension as part of A_lit. No projective separation of A_lit is assumed.

Define its clean physical AP sum
S_clean=mu(c) sum_{q,kappa,n} mu(q)mu(n)
 A_lit(q,kappa,n) 1_{q divides kappa n-ell}.                     (4)
All sums are over the fixed finite literal support. Dirichlet characters are extended by zero on nonunits. Then exactly
S_clean=mu(c) sum_{q,kappa,n}{mu(q)mu(n)A_lit(q,kappa,n)over phi(q)}
 sum_{chi (mod q)}chi(kappa n) conjugate(chi(ell)).               (5)
Let S_prim be the full-primitive-conductor component of (5):
S_prim=mu(c) sum_{q,kappa,n}{mu(q)mu(n)A_lit(q,kappa,n)over phi(q)}
 sum_{chi (mod q)}^*chi(kappa n) conjugate(chi(ell)),             (6)
where the star means primitive characters modulo q. Terms with gcd(kappa n,q)>1 vanish, so the unit condition may be inserted in (6).

For arbitrary positive q and integers m,ell satisfying gcd(m ell,q)=1, one has the exact primitive orthogonality identity
sum_{chi (mod q)}^*chi(m)conjugate(chi(ell))
 =sum_{d divides q, d divides m-ell}phi(d)mu(q/d).                (7)
Consequently, because every active q is squarefree, writing q=de gives the exact cofactor-kernel form
S_prim=mu(c) sum_{d,e,kappa,n}
 {mu(d)mu(n)over phi(e)}
 1_{de squarefree}
 1_{d divides kappa n-ell}
 1_{gcd(kappa n ell,de)=1}
 A_lit(de,kappa,n).                                              (8)
In particular, the factor mu(e) has squared away; the literal e-dependence remains inside A_lit(de,kappa,n), its quotient
t=(ell-kappa n)/(de),                                            (9)
its dyadic source weight, and its masks. Formula (8) supplies no legal factorization or cancellation in e.

For any real E_0>=1, define S_prim^{large e}(E_0) and S_prim^{small e}(E_0) by restricting (8), respectively, to e>=E_0 and e<E_0. Then
S_prim=S_prim^{large e}(E_0)+S_prim^{small e}(E_0)               (10)
exactly. Fix C>0 and assume B>1. If the literal q-support has q<=2Q_c and
E_0>=2Q_c(log B)^C/sqrt(B),                                     (11)
then every divisor modulus d in S_prim^{large e}(E_0) satisfies
d<=sqrt(B)/(log B)^C.                                           (12)
This only places d in the classical Mobius Bombieri-Vinogradov modulus range. Applying such a theorem still requires, uniformly in e,kappa and every retained label, that n mapsto A_lit(de,kappa,n), including (9) and all n-dependent masks, satisfy the needed bounded-variation or maximal-partial-summation hypotheses. No such regularity follows merely from (4)-(8).

The endpoint e=1 is exactly
S_prim^{e=1}
=mu(c) sum_{d,kappa,n}mu(d)mu(n)
 1_{d squarefree}
 1_{d divides kappa n-ell}
 1_{gcd(ell,d)=1}
 A_lit(d,kappa,n),                                               (13)
where gcd(kappa n,d)=1 follows from the displayed divisibility and gcd(ell,d)=1. Thus the endpoint retains the top-scale truncated Mobius divisor kernel and the full literal quotient/source dependence. Primitive orthogonality creates no complementary e-sign there. No estimate for either part of (10), no Mobius Bombieri-Vinogradov application, no critical-tail payment and no Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
703f9c67394fc2fc.proof:
Since c=gcd(s,L_src), writing s=cq and L_src=c ell gives gcd(q,ell)=1. Fact 8d9feea8c44da2c8 gives gcd(q,n)=1 and squarefreeness of q on the nonzero Mobius support. On the physical congruence kappa n congruent ell modulo q, the left member is therefore a unit modulo q.

For any q and ell coprime to q, character orthogonality on the unit group gives
1_{m congruent ell (mod q)}
 ={1over phi(q)}sum_{chi (mod q)}chi(m)conjugate(chi(ell))
when m is a unit. If m is not a unit, the right side is zero by the zero extension, while the left side is also zero because ell is a unit. Taking m=kappa n, multiplying by the complete literal coefficient and summing proves (5). Definition (6) merely selects the primitive characters and deletes no literal coefficient.

We prove (7). For a unit residue m ell^(-1) modulo q, full character orthogonality says
sum_{chi (mod q)}chi(m)conjugate(chi(ell))
 =phi(q)1_{q divides m-ell}.                                    (14)
Every character modulo q has a unique primitive conductor f dividing q. On unit arguments its values equal those of its inducing primitive character. Hence, if
P(f)=sum_{chi (mod f)}^*chi(m)conjugate(chi(ell)),
equation (14) is
phi(q)1_{q divides m-ell}=sum_{f divides q}P(f).                 (15)
Mobius inversion of (15) gives
P(q)=sum_{d divides q}mu(q/d)phi(d)1_{d divides m-ell},
which is (7). This proof includes q=1 under the unique trivial character convention.

Insert (7), with m=kappa n, into (6). Write q=de where d is the divisor in (7). Since q is squarefree, d and e are coprime and squarefree. Therefore
{mu(q)over phi(q)}phi(d)mu(e)
={mu(d)mu(e)over phi(d)phi(e)}phi(d)mu(e)
={mu(d)over phi(e)}.                                           (16)
The primitive characters vanish unless gcd(kappa n,q)=1, and (2) gives gcd(ell,q)=1. Keeping these exact unit conditions and replacing q by de proves (8). At no point was A_lit altered or separated, so (9) and every named literal dependence remain.

Equation (10) is the disjoint partition e>=E_0 or e<E_0. On the q-support, d=q/e<=2Q_c/E_0. Assumption (11) proves (12).

Finally set e=1 in (8). The conditions become d squarefree, d|(kappa n-ell), and gcd(kappa n ell,d)=1. If d divides kappa n-ell and gcd(ell,d)=1, then gcd(kappa n,d)=1; conversely the full unit condition implies gcd(ell,d)=1. This proves the equivalent endpoint formula (13). Its coefficient is mu(d), so no e-sign survives. The final scope statements follow because all transformations were identities and no analytic estimate was invoked.

glossary.A_lit: The chosen full literal amplitude of the clean character-expandable critical AP block, with no assumed projective separation.
glossary.E_0: The exact cofactor threshold separating large-e and small-e terms.
glossary.S_clean: The clean physical arithmetic-progression block at fixed orientation, g and c.
glossary.S_prim: The component of the character expansion carried by primitive characters of full modulus q.
glossary.S_prim^{e=1}: The e=1 endpoint of the primitive cofactor kernel.

707345f56faff29e.title: CONDITIONAL HIGH-C2 SIGN-PRESERVING ROUTING THROUGH THE 7/12 RANGE
707345f56faff29e.author: slava chan
707345f56faff29e.statement:
CONDITIONAL HIGH-C2 SIGN-PRESERVING ROUTING THROUGH THE 7/12 RANGE.

Fix the literal normalized Poisson setup and coefficients lambda_{g,a,b,h} of fact d8ba46800ba433c2. Let
0<kappa<1/100, 0<eta<=kappa/12,
and assume
D<=x^(1/2+eta), R<=x^(7/12-kappa).
Put
Z_0=x^(3/4-4eta)/R.
Let mathcal L_all be any restriction of the nonzero-Poisson coefficient array to the C2 class
z=(g,a,b,h), b=v p q,
where p,q are distinct primes at least Z_0, b is squarefree, gcd(a,b)=1, and h is nonzero. Assume the retained masks are invariant under h replacing -h. Retain every original coefficient and phase, and define
T_C2=sum_{z in mathcal L_all}
 lambda_z e_{b_z}((N/g_z)h_z a_z^(-1)).
Then T_C2 is real.

Let mathcal L_short be the subfamily with 0<|h_z|<Z_0. For z in mathcal L_short, let S_z={p_z,q_z}; let bar m_z be the unique residue class modulo b_z satisfying
a_z bar m_z congruent to N/g_z modulo b_z;
and put
J_z={r in S_z:r divides bar m_z h_z}.
For a support-disjoint ordered pair (z,z') with J_z=J_{z'}=emptyset, let alpha_{z,z'} be the full-face coefficient
product_{r in S_z union S_{z'}}(1-1/r).
Use the exact two-target carrier C_{z,z'} and small-v phases of fact 0d3dbb6b3e7b8abd, and define F_4 to be the sum over these good ordered pairs of
alpha_{z,z'} lambda_z lambda_{z'}
times their two exact small-v phases and the exact four-rough-prime phase
e_{G_zG_{z'}}(C_{z,z'}).

Then
|T_C2^2-F_4|
<=E_comp
<<D^2R^2Z_0^(-1)(log x)^5+O_A(D^2R^2x^(-A))
<<x^(2-kappa)                                                   (1)
for every fixed sufficiently large A and all sufficiently large x. The four contributions inside E_comp are exactly:
all repeated-prime Q_1/Q_2 pairs, every nonempty frequency-conductor layer, every pair having a frequency |h|>=Z_0, and the aggregate of the fifteen proper-conductor faces on the remaining good block.

Consequently, if for some A_0>0 the actual signed C2 sub-sum satisfies
T_C2<=-A_0
and A_0^2>2E_comp, then
Re(F_4)>=A_0^2-E_comp>=A_0^2/2.                               (2)
In particular, if A_0 is at least c x(log x)^(-B) for fixed c>0 and B>0, then (2) holds for all sufficiently large x.

This is a conditional sign-preserving routing from a large C2 source into a quantitatively large support-disjoint, full-conductor four-prime carrier block. It remains valid above the cube threshold because the C2 family is restricted explicitly rather than claimed to exhaust the terminal anatomy. Fact 7c1f38cfbb8d0569 shows that the forced total high-R anomaly alone does not supply the required C2 lower bound. Moreover F_4 still contains the exact small-v phases and does not force the induced centered prime lifts into literal DCE windows. No literal DCE majorant and no Goldbach implication is asserted.
707345f56faff29e.proof:
The smooth source amplitude is real. Its Fourier transform satisfies
widehat F(-xi)=conjugate(widehat F(xi)).
All remaining arithmetic coefficients are real, and the additive phase at -h is the conjugate of the phase at h. The h-symmetric mask therefore pairs every retained h with -h, proving that T_C2 is real.

The estimates behind fact 0d3dbb6b3e7b8abd do not use the cube inequality Z_0^3>R once the C2 restriction is imposed explicitly. We repeat their scale-independent forms. The total absolute coefficient mass is
L_abs<<DR(log x)^2.
For every rough prime r>=Z_0, the fixed-prime fibre mass is
A_r<<DR r^(-1)(log x)^2.
Therefore all ordered pairs sharing at least one rough prime have mass at most
sum_r A_r^2
<<D^2R^2Z_0^(-1)(log x)^4.                                  (3)

On the short-frequency family, divisibility of bar m_z h_z by r in S_z is well defined. Since |h_z|<Z_0<=r, it is equivalent to r dividing bar m_z, and the congruence defining bar m_z makes this equivalent to r dividing N/g_z. Hence every lost-conductor prime divides N. Summing the fixed-prime fibre bounds over the at most O(log x) prime divisors of N shows that the bad coefficient mass is
<<DR Z_0^(-1)(log x)^3.
Multiplication by the total absolute mass shows that all ordered pairs with at least one nonempty J-label have mass
<<D^2R^2Z_0^(-1)(log x)^5.                                  (4)

Repeated integration by parts in the literal Fourier transform gives arbitrary-power decay for |h|>=Z_0 provided Z_0M/b is a positive power of x. Here b<=2R and M is bounded below by a positive constant times x/D, so
Z_0M/b >> x^(7/4-4eta)/(D R^2)
>=x^(1/12+2kappa-5eta).
This is a positive power because eta<=kappa/12. Thus the absolute long-frequency mass is O_A(DR x^(-A)); the long-short, short-long, and long-long ordered-pair blocks together have mass
O_A(D^2R^2x^(-A))                                             (5)
after increasing A.

After removing (3)--(5), every remaining pair is support-disjoint, short-frequency, and full rough conductor. Fact 7bcf6f85c0df5948 bounds the difference between this good paired sum and its unique full four-prime face by
<<D^2R^2Z_0^(-1)(log x)^4.                                  (6)
Fact 0d3dbb6b3e7b8abd proves for every such pair, including pairs with different outer gcds, that the original two phases equal the two retained small-v phases times e_{G_zG_{z'}}(C_{z,z'}). Thus the full face in (6) is exactly F_4.

Equations (3)--(6), with a union bound, prove the first estimate in (1). For the scale estimate,
D^2R^2/Z_0=D^2R^3x^(-3/4+4eta)
<=x^(1+2eta) x^(7/4-3kappa) x^(-3/4+4eta)
=x^(2+6eta-3kappa).
Since eta<=kappa/12, this is at most x^(2-(5/2)kappa). For sufficiently large x the fifth logarithmic power is at most x^kappa, proving the final x^(2-kappa) bound after weakening the saving. The arbitrary-power term is smaller.

Because T_C2 is real and at most -A_0, its square is at least A_0^2. The first inequality in (1) gives
Re(F_4)>=T_C2^2-E_comp>=A_0^2-E_comp,
which proves (2). If A_0>=c x(log x)^(-B), then A_0^2 is at least c^2x^2(log x)^(-2B), while E_comp<<x^(2-kappa); their ratio tends to zero.

The final paragraph records the exact scope. Explicit C2 restriction makes no claim that A,B,C1,C2 exhaust the high anatomy. Facts 7c1f38cfbb8d0569 and 0aa454c6baf243c0 respectively leave the C2 selection and modular-window localization as separate obligations.

glossary.A_0: a positive lower bound for the magnitude of the signed C2 source
glossary.E_comp: the absolute complement budget between T_C2 squared and F_4
glossary.F_4: the support-disjoint full-rough-conductor full-face four-prime carrier sum
glossary.T_C2: the complete signed phased sum over mathcal L_all
glossary.Z_0: the rough-prime and short-frequency cutoff x^(3/4-4 eta)/R
glossary.alpha_{z,z'}: the full four-prime face coefficient product over the four rough primes of (1-1/r)
glossary.mathcal L_all: the literal C2 nonzero-Poisson coefficient family before frequency truncation

7131a06664967733.title: EXACT OUTER-GCD POISSON TAIL, NORMALIZED FIXED-\(g\) BETTIN--CHANDEE LEDGER, AND THEIR GLOBAL-\(x\) THRESHOLDS
7131a06664967733.author: slava chan
7131a06664967733.statement:
EXACT OUTER-GCD POISSON TAIL, NORMALIZED FIXED-\(g\) BETTIN--CHANDEE LEDGER, AND THEIR GLOBAL-\(x\) THRESHOLDS.

Fix one forward literal high-source dyadic label of facts \(60b26a9b6f79467a\), \(77d7a3419a07305c\), and \(a71f777ad842c886\), with
\[
 R>D,\qquad c_1x\le DM,RK\le C_1x,
\]
where \(c_1,C_1>0\) are fixed. Fix an exact outer gcd \(g=(d,r)\), so \(g\mid N\), \(d=ga\), \(r=gb\), \((a,b)=1\), and
\[
 am+bk=L_0=N/g.
\]
Put
\[
 Q=D/g,\qquad B=R/g,\qquad G_*=M/Q,\qquad
 H_T=B/Q=R/D,\qquad H_P=B/M=H_T/G_*.
\]
Assume \(Q>1\), and define \(\beta=\log B/\log Q\), so \(B=Q^\beta\).

Use the literal function \(F_{g,a,b}\), Fourier transform \(\widehat F_{g,a,b}\), and nonzero-Poisson coefficient
\[
 \lambda_{g,a,b,h}=\mu(ga)\mu(gb)b^{-1}\widehat F_{g,a,b}(h/b)
\]
of fact \(d8ba46800ba433c2\). Pair \(h\) with \(-h\), so after removing only \(\mu(ga)\mu(gb)\) the real atom coefficient is
\[
 q_{g,a,b,h}
 =2\operatorname {Re}\!\left[
 b^{-1}\widehat F_{g,a,b}(h/b)e_b(L_0h\bar a)
 \right]\quad(h>0),
\]
where \(a\bar a\equiv1\pmod b\). Retain every literal logarithm, smooth and dyadic source weight, fixed-\(U\) mask, high-label mask, and frozen parent mask inside \(F_{g,a,b}\) or as a deletion of indices.

For any one normalized anatomy class
\[
 X\in\{C_0,A,B,C_1,\ldots,C_{J_{\max}}\}
\]
of fact \(a71f777ad842c886\), and any frozen parent \(P\), let \(\mathcal L_{g,P,X}(T)\) be the total absolute mass of the corresponding literal real atoms with \(h\ge T\), where \(T\ge1\). If an \(A\)- or \(B\)-coefficient is expanded into its exact internal marker copies, take the sum of the absolute masses of those copies. Then for every integer \(J\ge2\),
\[
 \mathcal L_{g,P,X}(T)
 \ll_{J,\mathcal W,c_1,C_1}
 QB(\log x)^2\left(\frac{H_P}{T}\right)^{J-1}.                 \tag{1}
\]
Equivalently, because \(DM=gG_*Q^2\) and \(H_P=H_T/G_*\),
\[
 \mathcal L_{g,P,X}(T)
 \ll
 \frac{DM}{g}(\log x)^2T^{1-J}
 \left(\frac{H_T}{G_*}\right)^J
 \ll
 \frac{x}{g}(\log x)^2T^{1-J}
 \left(\frac{H_T}{G_*}\right)^J.                              \tag{2}
\]
The constants are uniform in \(N\), \(g\mid N\), \(P\), \(X\), and every deletion mask just listed.

The fixed-\(g\) Bettin--Chandee calculation inside fact \(df9748efe29ab475\), applied to the same aggregate parent/anatomy leaf, gives for every \(\epsilon>0\)
\[
 |T_{g,P,X}|
 \ll_\epsilon x^\epsilon
 \left(G_*^{3/20}QB^{19/20}+Q^{7/8}B\right),                  \tag{3}
\]
where \(T_{g,P,X}\) is the complete nonzero-frequency signed leaf on this exact \(g\)-layer. Relative to the global source scale \(DM\asymp x\), (3) is
\[
 \frac{|T_{g,P,X}|}{x}
 \ll_\epsilon x^\epsilon\left[
 \frac1gG_*^{-17/20}Q^{-1+19\beta/20}
 +\frac1gG_*^{-1}Q^{\beta-9/8}\right].                        \tag{4}
\]
Define
\[
 \Gamma_{\rm BC}(\beta)
 =\max\!\left(0,\frac{19\beta-20}{17}\right).                 \tag{5}
\]
For every \(\beta\ge1\),
\[
 \Gamma_{\rm BC}(\beta)\ge\beta-\frac98.                      \tag{6}
\]
Hence, for any fixed \(\omega>0\), the condition
\[
 G_*\ge Q^{\Gamma_{\rm BC}(\beta)+\omega}                     \tag{7}
\]
makes both terms in (4) power-saving in \(Q\). Uniformly for
\[
 1\le\beta\le\frac65-2\kappa,
\]
one has
\[
 \Gamma_{\rm BC}(\beta)
 \le \max\!\left(0,\frac{14}{85}-\frac{38\kappa}{17}\right).  \tag{8}
\]

There is also an independent absolute-tail threshold. If
\[
 G_*\ge H_TQ^\omega
 \quad\text{equivalently}\quad H_P\le Q^{-\omega},            \tag{9}
\]
then (2) with \(T=1\) is
\[
 \mathcal L_{g,P,X}(1)\ll \frac{x}{g}Q^{-J\omega}(\log x)^2.  \tag{10}
\]

Finally assume the forced-high hypotheses
\[
 D=x^{1/2+o(1)},\qquad R>x^{9/16-\kappa_0},
 \qquad1\le\beta\le6/5-2\kappa
\]
of fact \(5ced883d5560f772\). Then \(Q\ge x^{c_\kappa+o(1)}\) for the positive constant \(c_\kappa\) in that fact. After summing over all exact \(g\mid N\), all fixed parent/anatomy classes, and the polylogarithmically many literal dyadic and smooth-separation labels, either (7) or (9) therefore gives \(O(x^{1-\delta})=o(x/\log x)\) for some fixed \(\delta>0\) after choosing \(\epsilon\) sufficiently small and, for (9), choosing \(J\) sufficiently large. This conclusion concerns only the indicated exact-\(g\) sectors. It does not estimate the complementary medium-\(G_*\) cells, and it does not convert an expanded marker class into any theorem requiring additional factor slots.
7131a06664967733.proof:
Fact \(d8ba46800ba433c2\) defines
\[
 F_{g,a,b}(t)=\log t\log((L_0-at)/b)\,
 \mathcal W(ga/D,t/M,gb/R,(L_0-at)/(bK))
\]
with all literal source factors included, extended by zero. Its proof gives, for every integer \(J\ge2\),
\[
 |\widehat F_{g,a,b}(h/b)|
 \ll_J M(\log x)^2(1+hM/b)^{-J}.                              \tag{11}
\]
A fixed parent mask on the asserted low-\(\beta\) layer is a label scalar by fact \(a71f777ad842c886\); the high-label mask is also a label predicate. Every remaining literal source factor is already contained in \(F_{g,a,b}\). Deleting indices cannot increase an absolute sum.

For a fixed \(b\asymp B\), \(H_P=B/M\), and \(h\ge T\ge1\), (11) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_{h\ge T}b^{-1}|\widehat F_{g,a,b}(h/b)|
 &\ll_J (M/b)(\log x)^2
       \sum_{h\ge T}(h/H_P)^{-J}\\
 &\ll_J(\log x)^2H_P^{J-1}T^{1-J}.                            \tag{12}
 \end{aligned}
\]
There are \(O(Q)\) supported integers \(a\) and \(O(B)\) supported integers \(b\). Pairing \(h\) and \(-h\) costs at most a factor two because
\[
 |q_{g,a,b,h}|\le2b^{-1}|\widehat F_{g,a,b}(h/b)|.
\]

It remains to check the marker-copy variation. In class \(C_0\) or \(C_j\) there is one coefficient of absolute value one. In class \(A\), the proof of fact \(7c1f38cfbb8d0569\) shows that all interval-prime summands have the same sign and that their positive weights sum to one. In class \(B\), the stopping-prefix probabilities in that same proof are nonnegative and sum to one, while every nonzero copy has the common sign \(\mu(b)\). Therefore the total absolute marker-copy weight at each fixed \(b\) is exactly one in its active class and zero in every inactive class. Multiplication by \(|\mu(a)|\le1\) changes nothing. Summing (12) over \(a,b\) proves (1).

The identities
\[
 QB=(D/g)(R/g),\qquad
 H_P=R/(gM),\qquad
 QBH_P^{J-1}=(DM/g)H_P^J
\]
prove (2). Also \(D=gQ\), \(M=G_*Q\), hence \(DM=gG_*Q^2\).

We next extract the fixed-\(g\) estimate. In the proof of fact \(df9748efe29ab475\), before its summation over \(g\mid N\), the two Bettin--Chandee terms in the forward orientation are
\[
 g^{-9/5}M^{3/20}D^{17/20}R^{19/20},
 \qquad
 g^{-15/8}D^{7/8}R.                                           \tag{13}
\]
The theorem used there permits arbitrary bounded coefficients in the \(b\)-slot. As checked above, the aggregate coefficient \(c_X(b)\) of each anatomy class has absolute value at most one, and the low-\(\beta\) parent is a label scalar. Thus the same calculation applies after restricting to one aggregate parent/anatomy leaf. The scaled-smooth source separation and the two logarithms cost \(x^\epsilon\), as in that fact.

Substitute
\[
 D=gQ,\qquad M=G_*Q,\qquad R=gB
\]
into (13). The powers of \(g\) cancel in each term:
\[
 g^{-9/5}(G_*Q)^{3/20}(gQ)^{17/20}(gB)^{19/20}
 =G_*^{3/20}QB^{19/20},
\]
\[
 g^{-15/8}(gQ)^{7/8}(gB)=Q^{7/8}B.
\]
This proves (3). Dividing by \(DM=gG_*Q^2\) and using \(B=Q^\beta\) proves (4).

If \(G_*\ge Q^{\Gamma_{\rm BC}(\beta)+\omega}\), the exponent of \(Q\) in the first bracket of (4), apart from \(-17\omega/20\), is nonpositive by the definition (5). To treat the second bracket, if \(\beta\le20/19\), then \(\Gamma_{\rm BC}=0\) and \(\beta-9/8<0\). If \(\beta>20/19\), direct subtraction gives
\[
 \frac{19\beta-20}{17}-\left(\beta-\frac98\right)
 =\frac{2\beta-7/8}{17}>0.
\]
This proves (6) and the power saving from (7). Substituting \(\beta\le6/5-2\kappa\) into (5) proves (8).

Condition (9) and (2) with \(T=1\) immediately give (10). Under the final forced-high hypotheses, fact \(5ced883d5560f772\), equation (6) there, gives \(Q\ge x^{c_\kappa+o(1)}\). The number of active scale, sign, and smooth-separation labels is polylogarithmic. Also
\[
 \sum_{g\mid N}\frac1g\le\tau(N)=x^{o(1)}.
\]
Thus a fixed negative power of \(Q\) in (4) or (10) becomes a fixed negative power of \(x\) after absorbing the divisor and polylogarithmic factors. Choose the \(\epsilon\) in (3) sufficiently small; in the absolute-tail case choose \(J\) so that \(J\omega c_\kappa\) dominates those factors. This proves the final assertion and all scope statements.

glossary.Gamma_BC: The exact normalized imbalance threshold max(0,(19 beta-20)/17) for the two fixed-g Bettin--Chandee terms.
glossary.mathcal L_{g,P,X}(T): The total absolute literal paired-Poisson mass on exact outer-gcd layer g, frozen parent P, anatomy class X, and frequencies h at least T.

71389b22e6f49e13.title: Fix constants C>0 and η>0. Let x≥3, let Q be a positive integer with Q≤x^C, and let X≥x^η. Let F be a continuously differentiable complex function supported in [1/2,2], with bounded supremum and total variation. Then for every A>0,
71389b22e6f49e13.author: slava chan
71389b22e6f49e13.statement:
Fix constants C>0 and η>0. Let x≥3, let Q be a positive integer with Q≤x^C, and let X≥x^η. Let F be a continuously differentiable complex function supported in [1/2,2], with bounded supremum and total variation. Then for every A>0,
Σ_{n≥1,(n,Q)=1} μ(n)F(n/X)
≪_{A,C,η,F} X(log x)^(-A),
uniformly in Q,X,x.

The same estimate holds for a uniformly bounded family of such weights and after imposing finitely many additional coprimality conditions by replacing Q with their product, provided the resulting integer remains polynomially bounded in x.
71389b22e6f49e13.proof:
We use the classical summatory Möbius estimate recorded and applied in fact 0b3642c89b136065: there are absolute constants c_1,C_1>0 such that
|Σ_{n≤Y}μ(n)|≤C_1Y exp(-c_1 sqrt(log Y))
for all sufficiently large Y. Partial summation gives the same bound, up to a constant depending on the supremum and total variation, for a continuously differentiable weight on a fixed dyadic interval.

Define f_Q(n)=μ(n)1_{(n,Q)=1}. Its Dirichlet series factors as
Σ_{n≥1}f_Q(n)n^(-s)=ζ(s)^(-1)A_Q(s),
where
A_Q(s)=∏_{p|Q}(1-p^(-s))^(-1).
Let a_Q(h) be the Dirichlet coefficients of A_Q. They are nonnegative and f_Q=μ*a_Q.

We need uniform coefficient norms. Let k be the number of distinct prime factors of Q and list them increasingly. The j-th is at least j+1. Therefore
Σ_h a_Q(h)h^(-3/4)
=∏_{p|Q}(1-p^(-3/4))^(-1)
≤exp(O(Σ_{j≤k}j^(-3/4)))
=exp(O(k^(1/4))).
Since the product of the first k positive integers is at most Q≤x^C, one has k=O_C(log x/log log x). Consequently
Σ_h a_Q(h)h^(-3/4)=exp(O_C((log x)^(1/4)))=x^{o(1)}.
The identical argument at exponent 1 gives
Σ_h a_Q(h)/h=x^{o(1)}.
Both estimates are uniform in Q.

By convolution,
Σ_{(n,Q)=1}μ(n)F(n/X)
=Σ_h a_Q(h)Σ_m μ(m)F(hm/X).
Split at h=X^(1/2). For h≤X^(1/2), the inner variable has length X/h≥X^(1/2), so the summatory Möbius estimate and partial summation give
Σ_m μ(m)F(hm/X)
≪_F (X/h)exp(-c_2 sqrt(log X))
for an absolute c_2>0. Summing with the exponent-1 coefficient norm gives
≪X exp(-c_2 sqrt(log X))x^{o(1)}.
Because X≥x^η, this is O_{A,C,η,F}(X(log x)^(-A)) for every fixed A.

For h>X^(1/2), use the trivial bound O_F(X/h). Since h^(-1)≤X^(-1/8)h^(-3/4) in this range, the contribution is
≪X^(7/8)Σ_h a_Q(h)h^(-3/4)
≤X^(7/8)x^{o(1)}.
Again X≥x^η makes this O_{A,C,η,F}(X(log x)^(-A)) for every fixed A. Adding the two ranges proves the estimate.

Additional coprimality conditions are absorbed by enlarging Q. The proof depends on Q only through its polynomial size, so the same conclusion holds.

714b7538b3f03070.title: SELF-CONTAINED CLOSED-ENDPOINT SEPARATED-OUTER ONE-PRIME TRACE
714b7538b3f03070.author: slava chan
714b7538b3f03070.statement:
SELF-CONTAINED CLOSED-ENDPOINT SEPARATED-OUTER ONE-PRIME TRACE.

Fix integers \(J,C_A,K\ge1\), a constant \(C\ge1\), and
\(0<\kappa\le1/100\).  Put
\[
 \sigma=\kappa/100,quad
 \beta_1=6/5-3\sigma,quad
 \beta_m=6/5-12\sigma/5.
\]
Let \(Q\) be sufficiently large, let
\(\beta_1<\beta\le\beta_m\), and put
\[
 B=Q^\beta,qquad H_T=B/Q,qquad S_0=H_T^2Q^{3\sigma}.
\]
Let dyadic \(V,P\ge1\) satisfy
\[
 V\le S_0,qquad C^{-1}B\le VP\le CB.                           \tag{1}
\]
Let \(\xi_v\) be supported on squarefree \(V\le v<2V\) with
\[
 |\xi_v|\le\tau_J(v).
\]
No restriction is imposed on the sizes of the prime divisors of \(v\).
Instead assume directly that every supported \(v\) is coprime to every
prime \(p\in[P,2P)\) occurring below.

Fix a nonzero integer \(A\) with \(|A|\le Q^{C_A}\), and coefficients
\(|c_q|\le1\) on \(Q\le q<2Q\).  Let \(G>0\) and put
\[
 H_P=H_T/G.
\]
For every dyadic integer \(F\ge1\), let \(\nu_F(h)\) be supported on
\(F\le|h|<2F\) with
\[
 |\nu_F(h)|\le\tau_J(|h|),
\]
let
\[
 |\omega_F|\le C(J_0)\min\{1,(F/H_P)^{-J_0}\}
\]
for every fixed \(J_0\ge1\), and let \(\Psi_F\) be a
fixed-complexity uniformly scaled-smooth projective amplitude in
\(q/Q,|h|/F,v/V,p/P\), supported on the full dyadic rectangle and having
projective Fourier norm bounded by a fixed constant depending only on
\(K\).  Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
T_{\rm sep,*}={1\over H_P}\sum_F\omega_F
 &\sum_{Q\le q<2Q}c_q
 \sum_{F\le|h|<2F}\nu_F(h)\\
 &\sum_{\substack{V\le v<2V\cr
 P\le p<2P, p\ {m prime}\cr
 (vp,q)=1}}
 \xi_v\Psi_F\!\left({q\over Q},{|h|\over F},
                       {v\over V},{p\over P}\right)
 e_q(Ah(vp)^{-1}).
\end{aligned}                                                     \tag{2}
\]
There is no sharp product mask in (2); (1) is only a dyadic scale relation.

If \(G\ge1\), then for some fixed \(\delta_{\rm sep,F}>0\),
\[
 T_{\rm sep,*}\ll GQ^{2-\delta_{\rm sep,F}}.                   \tag{3}
\]
If \(0<\eta<\sigma\) and
\[
 Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\le G\le Q^{\sigma-\eta},
\]
then for some fixed \(\delta_{\rm sep,N}>0\),
\[
 T_{\rm sep,*}\ll Q^{2-\delta_{\rm sep,N}}.                    \tag{4}
\]
The constants and savings depend only on the displayed fixed parameters,
divisor orders and projective norm.  The estimates include \(H_P<1\),
every actual integer frequency, proper-prime powers, all Vaughan
Type-I/II branches, a possibly nonunit target \(A\), and unrestricted
\((h,q)\).  Legal one-variable, label-scalar and bounded-projective
factors are permitted; arbitrary joint masks are not.  No marker,
literal-source, outer-\(g\), other-anatomy, PMD, DCE, or Goldbach claim
is made.
714b7538b3f03070.proof:
Compare (2) with the accepted endpoint \(C1_*\) trace of fact
\(7767c0ebde1c24a7\).  The present statement reproduces every one of its
analytic hypotheses except the condition that every prime divisor of
\(v\) is at most the small cutoff and the lower rough cutoff on \(p\).
Those conditions were used in the predecessor only to deduce
\((v,p)=1\).  The present theorem assumes that conclusion directly.

Indeed, the scale exponent \(\nu=\log V/\log Q\) obeys
\[
 0\le\nu\le2\beta-2+3\sigma+O(1/\log Q)
\]
solely because \(V\le S_0\), and
\(P=Q^{\beta-\nu+O(1/\log Q)}\) solely because \(VP\asymp B\).
After the opening coprimality step, every line of the predecessor proof
uses only:

1. \(V\le S_0\) and the divisor bound on \(\xi_v\);
2. the exact prime-indicator and proper-prime-power decomposition;
3. the signed Vaughan theorem \(29c43cef40f2e79b\);
4. the endpoint Type-I/II switch inequalities proved in
   \(7767c0ebde1c24a7\);
5. the correlated-energy theorem \(42720f6d803c4640\);
6. the multiplier-one Type-I theorem \(bbcb9f66597c667c\);
7. the explicitly restated arbitrary fixed-order frequency decay.

None of these steps factors \(v\) or bounds its prime divisors.  When a
Vaughan factor \(l\) is grouped with \(v\), the coefficient at
\(s=vl\) is divisor-bounded:
\[
 \sum_{vl=s}\tau_J(v)\tau_K(l)\log(2P)
 \le\tau_{J+K+2}(s)\log(2P).
\]
The complete-product condition \((vp,q)=1\) becomes exactly the grouped
coprimality required by both analytic consumers.

For completeness, the proper-prime-power contribution is bounded by
\[
 Q^\epsilon\sum_F|\omega_F|(F/H_P)Q(VB)^{1/2}
 \ll Q^{9/5-2\sigma}.
\]
Every nonshort Vaughan box lies in the accepted endpoint window
\[
 H_T^2Q^{3\sigma/2}\le S\le
 Q^{1-3\sigma/2}/H_T^2,
\]
and therefore has the four baseline savings and the
\((F/H_P)^{3/4}\), \(F/H_P\) costs proved in
\(7767c0ebde1c24a7\).  The short coefficient scale is at most
\(Q^{1/2-5\sigma/2}\), so fact \(bbcb9f66597c667c\) applies with
\(\tau=2\sigma\).  Finally
\[
 \sum_F|\omega_F|(F/H_P)^{3/4+\epsilon}
 +\sum_F|\omega_F|(F/H_P)^{1+\epsilon}\ll1,
\]
including when \(H_P<1\).

Thus the accepted analytic proof transfers after replacing its derived
coprimality by the present direct pairwise hypothesis.  It yields (3) and
(4) with exactly the self-contained coefficient, support, target,
frequency and norm classes stated above.

glossary.T_sep,*: The self-contained closed-endpoint separated-outer one-prime trace.

714f3597f5ef527c.title: HEIGHT-SEPARATED CLUSTER SATURATION OF AN ABSTRACT ADDITIVE CROSSED L2 ROW
714f3597f5ef527c.author: slava chan
714f3597f5ef527c.statement:
HEIGHT-SEPARATED CLUSTER SATURATION OF AN ABSTRACT ADDITIVE CROSSED L2 ROW.

Let H>=2 and let I be a finite integer interval contained either in [H,2H) or in (-2H,-H]. Put L=#I. Let cal X be a finite set of cardinality X_src>=2. For every x in cal X let lambda_x be a distinct rational number. Assume all lambda_x lie in one real interval of length at most
  1/(12H).                                                  (1)
Put a_h(x)=1 for h in I and x in cal X, and define
  T_cluster
   =sum_{h in I}sum_{x_1 not equal x_2}
      e(h[lambda_{x_1}-lambda_{x_2}]).                      (2)
Then T_cluster is real and
  T_cluster>=(L/2)X_src(X_src-1).                           (3)
The coefficient is exactly height-separated:
  a_h(x)=z_h b_x,  z_h=1, b_x=1.                            (4)
It also satisfies the normalized finite-band factorization in fact 4b89ec4ce7a7b67a with B=1, alpha=1, L_pr=H and C_J=3^J for every fixed J>=3, after zero extension outside I.

Consequently pointwise boundedness, source occupancy, height separation, and the displayed normalized finite-band factorization do not by themselves imply a fixed-power one-row saving if a source deletion may select a phase cluster of width comparable to H^(-1). A fixed-power interior theorem for literal Aadd must additionally use quantitative anti-clustering of the actual source slopes, arithmetic cancellation in the literal coefficients, or an earlier signed assembly that excludes such cluster selection.

This is an abstract coefficient/phase-set obstruction. It does not construct a clustered literal source row, does not assert that the natural masks select such a cluster, does not contradict fact 5db1ff60efd872b4, and gives no PMD or Goldbach conclusion.
714f3597f5ef527c.proof:
Interchanging x_1 and x_2 conjugates a summand of (2), so the ordered sum T_cluster is real. For h in I one has |h|<2H. By (1),
  |2 pi h(lambda_{x_1}-lambda_{x_2})|
  <=2 pi(2H)/(12H)=pi/3.                                   (5)
Therefore
  Re e(h[lambda_{x_1}-lambda_{x_2}])
  =cos(2 pi h[lambda_{x_1}-lambda_{x_2}])
  >=1/2.                                                    (6)
There are L heights and X_src(X_src-1) ordered unequal pairs. Summing (6) and using realness proves (3).

Equation (4) is immediate. For the normalized factorization, assign a distinct q-coordinate to each x, take alpha_{q,h}=1, and let w_{q,h}=1 on I and zero outside I. For h in I, |h|/H<=2. With L_pr=H and C_J=3^J,
  C_J(L_pr/H)(1+|h|/H)^(-J)>=1=|w_{q,h}|.                 (7)
Outside I the coefficient is zero. Also alpha=1<=tau(r) for every positive integer r, and L_pr=H=BH. Thus the coefficient assumptions stated in fact 4b89ec4ce7a7b67a hold.

The lower bound (3) is a constant proportion of the full unequal-pair count. Hence the listed abstract hypotheses cannot force a fixed-power saving uniformly over clustered phase sets. The proof makes no assertion that such a phase set is realized by the literal arithmetic source, establishing all scope qualifications.

glossary.Tcluster: The additive crossed L2 Gram of a tightly clustered exact-rational phase set with constant coefficients.

71f1a10b52148348.title: BOUNDED-VARIATION q-PROFILE REFINEMENT OF THE ACTUAL STRICT-TOP C1,C2,C3,C4 SOURCE NORMAL FORM
71f1a10b52148348.author: slava chan
71f1a10b52148348.statement:
BOUNDED-VARIATION q-PROFILE REFINEMENT OF THE ACTUAL STRICT-TOP C1,C2,C3,C4 SOURCE NORMAL FORM.

Adopt the actual one-row C1-C4 q-profile expansion of fact ff228b0e569531f8 on one fixed strict-top outer row, one signed frequency block F<=|h|<2F, and one dyadic factor box n=mv with m asymp M_1, v asymp V_1. For a complex function A on the integer interval Q<=s<2Q define
  V_Q(A)=sup_{Q<=s<2Q}|A(s)|
         +sum_{Q<=s<2Q-1}|A(s+1)-A(s)|.                       (1)

For every fixed A_0>0, the expansion in that fact may be chosen so that
  c_lambda(s,n,h)
  =sum_rho kappa_{lambda,rho}(n,h)
    mu(s)1_{s asymp Q}1_{(s,gn)=1}A_rho(s),                   (2)
with
  sum_rho|kappa_{lambda,rho}(n,h)|V_Q(A_rho)
  <<_{A_0}(log x)^2(1+F/H_P)^(-A_0).                         (3)
The same choice simultaneously retains the bounded-variation h-profile and bounded m,v profiles of facts 062a7f6f0c58b1f2 and 544c7ba4db45c06f. After summing all dyadic F,M_1,V_1 boxes, the total weighted coefficient mass in (3) is x^{o(1)}.

The refinement is made before the pair-dependent first-nonresonant-prime mask. Hence, in any fixed-p TT-star pair or four-row occupancy, every one-row q-profile has the form
  mu(q)1_{(q,gn)=1}A_rho(q)                                   (4)
with the bounded-variation norm (1), while the exact determinant masks D_{p,lambda} of fact ff228b0e569531f8 remain outside. This theorem proves no Möbius-trace cancellation, no deletion-aware pair or four-linear estimate, no cross-modulus assembly, and no trace or Goldbach conclusion.
71f1a10b52148348.proof:
The proof of fact 062a7f6f0c58b1f2 introduces the normalized reciprocal-modulus coordinate
  x_1=s/Q
and proves, in its equations (8)-(10), fixed-order derivative bounds of arbitrary order in x_1 together with the normalized m,v,h coordinates. It then extends the coefficient smoothly to a fixed four-torus and takes an absolutely convergent Fourier expansion. The cited proof used its derivative budget to weight the h-Fourier index, because only h-variation was needed there.

Repeat the same Fourier construction with a larger fixed derivative order. If xi_s and xi_h are the Fourier indices in the normalized s and h coordinates, repeated integration by parts gives an absolutely summable coefficient family even after multiplication by
  (1+|xi_s|)(1+|xi_h|).                                       (5)
All other Fourier indices remain absolutely summable as before. This uses only the arbitrary fixed-order derivative bounds already proved there.

For one normalized s-mode exp(2pi i xi_s s/Q), the mean-value theorem gives
  sup_{Q<=s<2Q}|exp(2pi i xi_s s/Q)|
  +sum_{Q<=s<2Q-1}
   |exp(2pi i xi_s(s+1)/Q)-exp(2pi i xi_s s/Q)|
  <<1+|xi_s|.                                                  (6)
The fixed smooth cutoff to Q<=s<2Q contributes only a constant number of endpoint jumps. Therefore the q-factor of each separated Fourier mode has V_Q norm O(1+|xi_s|). Absorb this factor into its Fourier coefficient. The weighted absolute summability (5) proves (3). The simultaneous factor 1+|xi_h| retains the h-variation estimate, while the m and v factors retain supremum at most one.

Facts 544c7ba4db45c06f and ff228b0e569531f8 then multiply this smooth expansion only by the n-side factors mu(n), the Cj marker coefficient, and fixed outer/unit scalars. All have modulus at most one and are independent of s. Thus the q-variation estimate survives legal re-marking. The dyadic summability argument in those facts is unchanged; the additional fixed Fourier-index weight was already absorbed by (5), so the total remains x^{o(1)}.

Finally, fact ff228b0e569531f8 proves that the first-nonresonant-prime selector is imposed only after two one-row profiles are formed. It therefore does not alter (1)-(4) and remains a joint mask. This proves the refinement and every scope statement.

glossary.V_Q(A): The supremum plus discrete total variation of a one-variable physical q-profile on Q<=q<2Q.

7264046d8776d59f.title: EXACT PHYSICAL-RESIDUE GRAM FOR THE CRITICAL TOTAL-MODULUS TMC BAND
7264046d8776d59f.author: slava chan
7264046d8776d59f.proof:
Choose an integer \(a\) with
\(a\equiv hq_1^{-1}\pmod b\).  The CRT construction in the proof of
TMC-EXACT, fact \(967520f427b111c5\), gives
\(\gamma_{q_1,q_2,h}\equiv q_1a\pmod S\).  Therefore
\[
 e_b(-rhq_1^{-1})=e_b(-ra)=e_S(-r\gamma_{q_1,q_2,h}).   \tag{10}
\]
Insert (10) and
\[
 G_{S,h,{\bf t}}(r)=\sum_wg_{h,{\bf t}}(w)e_S(rw)
\]
into the definition of \(A_{S,{\bf t}}(r)\) in fact
\(ffa8f6d3f766b9f5\).  Finite Fourier orthogonality gives
\[
 \sum_{r\ ({\rm mod}\ S)}
 A_{S,{\bf t}}(r)e_S(rz)=S H_{S,{\bf t}}(z).            \tag{11}
\]
Summing (3) over \(z\) counts every integer \(w\) once modulo \(S\);
this proves (5).  Removing the \(r=0\) summand from (11) yields
\[
 \sum_{\substack{r\ ({\rm mod}\ S)\\r\ne0}}
 A_{S,{\bf t}}(r)e_S(rz)=Z_{S,{\bf t}}(z).              \tag{12}
\]

Expand the Kloosterman sum in the definition of \(Y\), interchange the
finite \(r\)- and unit sums, and apply (12):
\[
\begin{split}
 Y_{S,{\bf t}}(k)
 &=\sum_{(u,S)=1}e_S(kNu^{-1})
   \sum_{r\ne0}A_{S,{\bf t}}(r)e_S(ru)\\
 &=\sum_{(u,S)=1}Z_{S,{\bf t}}(u)e_S(kNu^{-1}),
\end{split}
\]
which proves (6).

Expanding the square of (6) and summing over \(k\in{\cal K}\) proves
(7).  Since \((N,S)=1\), the map
\(u\mapsto Nu^{-1}\) permutes the unit residues.  Finite Parseval applied
to (6) therefore gives
\[
 \sum_{k\ ({\rm mod}\ S)}|Y_{S,{\bf t}}(k)|^2
 =S\sum_{(u,S)=1}|Z_{S,{\bf t}}(u)|^2.
\]
At \(k=0\), equation (6) equals \(\sum_{(u,S)=1}Z_{S,{\bf t}}(u)\).
Subtracting its square proves (8).  Substitution into the definition of
\({\cal E}_S\) proves (9).  The final paragraph merely identifies the
exact specialization of (7) and does not invoke an estimate.

glossary.H_{S,bold t}: the complete signed physical residue row at total modulus S
glossary.Z_{S,bold t}: the r=0-centered physical residue row S H-A(0)
glossary.cal D_cal K: the finite Dirichlet kernel of a selected k-frequency set
glossary.cal K_crit: the centered natural k-frequency band of length comparable to S/M0
glossary.gamma_{q_1,q_2,h}: the CRT translation residue congruent to zero modulo q1 and h modulo q2

727e54e160fb7774.title: COMPLETE ABSOLUTE SCALAR-TENSOR PAYMENT WHEN ONE STRICT-TOP C1 ROW IS TINY SELECTED-p. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100 and beta_m=6/5-12sigma/5, fix an imbalance slack 0<eta_G<sigma, and fix an integer 1<=r<=4 and a sufficiently large common Q. For each 1<=i<=r fix an actual strict-top B,C1,C2,C3, or C4 scalar marker-copy row in one orientation, with q-variable Q<=q_i<2Q, marked integer B_i/2<=n_i<=2B_i where B_i=Q^(beta_i) and beta_m<beta_i<6/5, nonzero integer height h_i, and physical Poisson scale H_{P,i}>0. Let c_i(q_i,n_i,h_i) be its dimensionless literal scalar coefficient, including any retained rowwise zero-one and unit-modulus factors. Thus, for every fixed A>=2 and epsilon_0>0,
727e54e160fb7774.author: slava chan
727e54e160fb7774.statement:
COMPLETE ABSOLUTE SCALAR-TENSOR PAYMENT WHEN ONE STRICT-TOP C1 ROW IS TINY SELECTED-p. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100 and beta_m=6/5-12sigma/5, fix an imbalance slack 0<eta_G<sigma, and fix an integer 1<=r<=4 and a sufficiently large common Q. For each 1<=i<=r fix an actual strict-top B,C1,C2,C3, or C4 scalar marker-copy row in one orientation, with q-variable Q<=q_i<2Q, marked integer B_i/2<=n_i<=2B_i where B_i=Q^(beta_i) and beta_m<beta_i<6/5, nonzero integer height h_i, and physical Poisson scale H_{P,i}>0. Let c_i(q_i,n_i,h_i) be its dimensionless literal scalar coefficient, including any retained rowwise zero-one and unit-modulus factors. Thus, for every fixed A>=2 and epsilon_0>0,
|c_i(q_i,n_i,h_i)|<=C_{A,epsilon_0}Q^epsilon_0(1+|h_i|/H_{P,i})^(-A).  (1)
Let D of the full r-row tuple be any complex joint mask with |D|<=1; it may contain the exact first-prime pair masks and any pair or tuple deletions. Define the normalized scalar tensor
T_r=(product_{i=1}^r H_{P,i}^(-1)) sum D product_{i=1}^r c_i(q_i,n_i,h_i),
where the sum is over the displayed q_i,n_i,h_i supports and any further literal restrictions.

Assume that one distinguished row j is a literal strict-top C1 row with n_j=p_jv_j squarefree, p_j its unique rough prime, gcd(p_j,v_j)=1, C_j=mathscr A h_j, and m_eff,j=n_j/gcd(C_j,n_j). Assume 1<=m_eff,j<Q^(kappa/20), that this same p_j is the prescribed first-nonresonant prime in an active exact pair mask, and that its actual imbalance parameter G_j satisfies G_j>=Q^(-sigma+eta_G), with H_{P,j}=Q^(beta_j-1)/G_j and p_j>=Q^(3/2-beta_j-3sigma). Then, for every target E>0,
|T_r|<<_E Q^(-E).                                                (2)
In particular every actual two-row or four-row scalar suboccupancy containing a tiny selected-p C1 row is arbitrarily power-small even with all joint masks retained. This theorem is already a complete scalar source/modulus aggregate; it does not identify T_r with, or estimate, an additional vector-valued Hilbert/completion object.
727e54e160fb7774.proof:
Fact 3286b0e75a3ea94a proves (1) uniformly for every exact row and marker copy listed in the statement. Fact 555ec032e5c78720 applies to the fully displayed distinguished tiny selected-p row and proves that p_j divides h_j. The stated scale inequalities also give
H_{P,j}<=Q^(beta_j-1+sigma-eta_G),
so
p_j/H_{P,j}>=Q^(5/2-2beta_j-4sigma+eta_G)>Q^(9/100).            (3)
Indeed beta_j<6/5 and 4sigma<=1/2500 imply that the exponent is strictly larger than 1/10-1/2500>9/100. This is also the conclusion of fact ed8954118b71276a.

We first bound one ordinary row absolutely. For every H>0 and fixed A>=2,
H^(-1) sum_{h in Z, h!=0}(1+|h|/H)^(-A)<<_A 1.                 (4)
Indeed, if H>=1, compare the decreasing summand with its integral, which is O_A(H); if 0<H<1, bound the sum by 2H^A sum_{m>=1}m^(-A)=O_A(H^A), and divide by H. Since there are O(QB_i) choices of q_i,n_i, equations (1) and (4) give ordinary row absolute mass
<<_{A,epsilon_0} QB_i Q^epsilon_0.                              (5)

For the distinguished row, restrict the height sum using p_j|h_j. Write h_j=k p_j with k a nonzero integer. Since (3) is larger than one for large Q,
H_{P,j}^(-1) sum_{k!=0}(1+|k|p_j/H_{P,j})^(-A)
 <=2 zeta(A)H_{P,j}^(A-1)p_j^(-A)
 =2 zeta(A)p_j^(-1)(p_j/H_{P,j})^(1-A)
 <<_A Q^(-(9/100)(A-1)).                                       (6)
The factor p_j^(-1) was merely discarded. Thus its row absolute mass is
<<_{A,epsilon_0}QB_jQ^epsilon_0 Q^(-(9/100)(A-1)).              (7)

Take absolute values in T_r and discard D and every further restriction. The remaining majorant factors into the r row masses. Since beta_i<6/5,
product_{i=1}^r QB_i <=Q^((11/5)r)<=Q^(44/5).                  (8)
Combining (5),(7),(8) gives
|T_r|<<_{A,epsilon_0}Q^(44/5+r epsilon_0-(9/100)(A-1)).         (9)
Given E>0, first fix epsilon_0>0 and then choose the fixed integer A so large that the exponent in (9) is below -E-1. The fixed implied constant is absorbed for sufficiently large Q, proving (2). Because D was arbitrary subject only to |D|<=1, the conclusion retains every exact pair and tuple mask. No vector norm or completion was used, proving the scope statement.

glossary.scalar r-row tensor: A product of r normalized literal nonzero-Poisson scalar rows, restricted by an arbitrary bounded joint mask, before any additional vector-valued Hilbert completion.

72d96a78c44a83a3.title: EXACT ONE-SIDED PHYSICAL PROFILE FOR THE NATURAL FORWARD C1 PMD AMPLITUDE. Use the complete forward C1 coordinate of facts 6eacfadbc9a83247 and ee6886ba9ed393f1. Thus n=vp, s=cq, L_0=cA, and
72d96a78c44a83a3.author: slava chan
72d96a78c44a83a3.statement:
EXACT ONE-SIDED PHYSICAL PROFILE FOR THE NATURAL FORWARD C1 PMD AMPLITUDE. Use the complete forward C1 coordinate of facts 6eacfadbc9a83247 and ee6886ba9ed393f1. Thus n=vp, s=cq, L_0=cA, and
F_{g,cq,n}(t)
 =log(t)log((cA-cqt)/n)
  cal W(gcq/D,t/M,gn/R,(cA-cqt)/(nK)),                     (1)
extended by zero outside its compact positive source support, with Fourier convention
Fhat_{g,cq,n}(xi)=integral_R F_{g,cq,n}(t)e(-xi t)dt.       (2)
For each retained q define the translated physical profile
G_{g,c,q,n,A}(y)=F_{g,cq,n}(y+A/q).                        (3)
Then G is independent of the Poisson height h and has the explicit formula
G_{g,c,q,n,A}(y)
 =log(y+A/q)log(-cqy/n)
  cal W(gcq/D,(y+A/q)/M,gn/R,-cqy/(nK)),                   (4)
again extended by zero outside the source support. Its Fourier transform satisfies, for every real xi,
Ghat_{g,c,q,n,A}(xi)
 =e(Axi/q)Fhat_{g,cq,n}(xi).                               (5)
In particular,
Ghat_{g,c,q,n,A}(-h/n)
 =e(-Ah/(qn))Fhat_{g,cq,n}(-h/n),                          (6)
and the exact natural PMD amplitude of fact ee6886ba9ed393f1 is
U_PMD(q,h,v,p)
 =(H_P/n)Ghat_{g,c,q,n,A}(-h/n).                           (7)
Thus the full exact reindexed q-coefficient is
a_h^PMD(q)
 =-mu(c)mu(v)mu(q)(H_P/n)
   Ghat_{g,c,q,n,A}(-h/n)chi_nat(v,p,h,q).                 (8)

The translated physical profile is one-sided. If G_{g,c,q,n,A}(y) is nonzero, then
y+A/q>0,  -cqy/n>0,
and consequently
-A/q<y<0.                                                   (9)
For every integer hard-source atom obeying
qm+n k_red=A,  k_red>0,                                    (10)
the translated coordinate and the fourth physical source variable are exactly
y=m-A/q=-n k_red/q<0,
-cqy/n=c k_red.                                            (11)
If A>0 and q lies in [Q,2Q), all the profiles (3) are therefore supported in the common one-sided interval (-A/Q,0), although its length A/Q need not be O(n/H).

Equations (3)-(8) supply the previously missing h-independent physical representation of the natural Fourier amplitude itself: the compensating Archimedean factor is precisely a translation factor, not an arbitrary h-dependent multiplier. They do not absorb chi_nat into an h-independent profile. In particular, any height-dependent inherited cutoff, projective partition, collision condition, or other literal bookkeeping factor remains explicitly in chi_nat. Nor does one-sided support survive as a pointwise support statement after restriction to a proper finite h-band, by fact 7596cf19a80bf8f3. No completed-window estimate, Gadd^(-1) saving, PMD closure, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
72d96a78c44a83a3.proof:
Substitute t=y+A/q into (1). Since
cA-cq(y+A/q)=-cqy,
formula (1) becomes exactly (4), proving the explicit profile identity.

For any real xi, use t=y+A/q, so y=t-A/q and dy=dt. Then
Ghat(xi)
 =integral_R F(t)e(-xi(t-A/q))dt
 =e(Axi/q)integral_R F(t)e(-xi t)dt
 =e(Axi/q)Fhat(xi).
This proves (5), and xi=-h/n gives (6). Equation (8) of fact ee6886ba9ed393f1 defines
U_PMD(q,h,v,p)
 =(H_P/n)Fhat_{g,cq,n}(-h/n)e(-Ah/(qn)).
Substitution of (6) proves (7). Multiplying by the exact signs and the inherited factor chi_nat from equation (5) of that fact proves (8).

The original physical source in fact 6eacfadbc9a83247 is supported where both t and (cA-cqt)/n are positive. With t=y+A/q and (cA-cqt)/n=-cqy/n, nonvanishing of G implies y+A/q>0 and -cqy/n>0. All of c,q,n are positive, so these inequalities give y>-A/q and y<0, proving (9).

For a hard-source atom, equation (10) gives A-qm=n k_red. Dividing by q and changing sign yields
m-A/q=-n k_red/q.
Putting y=m-A/q into -cqy/n then gives c k_red. This proves (11). If A>0 and Q<=q<2Q, then A/q<=A/Q, so (-A/q,0) is contained in (-A/Q,0), proving the common interval assertion.

Fact 05cbed389411618a identified an h-independent physical Fourier representation as a missing interface condition for the abstract literal coefficient. Equations (3)-(8) prove that representation for the actual natural amplitude U_PMD, while leaving chi_nat explicit. The final limitation follows from fact 7596cf19a80bf8f3, which proves that a nonzero proper finite Fourier band is nonlocal in the physical variable.

glossary.G_{g,c,q,n,A}: The natural forward C1 physical source profile translated from t to the corrected coordinate y=t-A/q.
glossary.Ghat_{g,c,q,n,A}: The Fourier transform of the translated natural profile G_{g,c,q,n,A}.
glossary.y: The corrected physical coordinate t-A/q, equal to m-A/q on a hard-source atom.

730507ae5291672a.title: PMD WINDOW-RATIO AND RESIDUE-INJECTIVITY DICHOTOMY
730507ae5291672a.author: slava chan
730507ae5291672a.statement:
PMD WINDOW-RATIO AND RESIDUE-INJECTIVITY DICHOTOMY.

Let Q>=2 and let H,V be positive real numbers. Put
  P=QH/V.                                                   (1)
Let v,p,q range over integers satisfying
  V<=v<2V,
  P<=p<2P,  with p prime,
  Q<=q<2Q.                                                  (2)
Define
  M_{v,p}=vp/H.                                             (3)
Then
  M_{v,p}/p=v/H,                                           (4)
and hence
  V/H<=M_{v,p}/p<2V/H.                                     (5)

If V<H, then P>Q and every allowed p satisfies p>Q. Consequently reduction modulo p is injective on the integers q in [Q,2Q): if q_1,q_2 lie in this interval and q_1 is congruent to q_2 modulo p, then q_1=q_2.

Conversely, if two distinct integers q_1,q_2 in [Q,2Q) are congruent modulo an allowed p, then
  p<=|q_1-q_2|<Q,                                          (6)
so P<Q and V>H. In particular every congruent-support block of fact 9b8cce52a98d22c8 that contains at least two distinct q-values in [Q,2Q) lies in a residue-aliasing scale with
  M_{v,p}/p>1.                                             (7)

More quantitatively, for every fixed theta in (0,1), if
  V<=H Q^(-theta),                                         (8)
then
  p>=Q^(1+theta),
  M_{v,p}/p<2Q^(-theta),                                   (9)
and reduction modulo p is injective on [Q,2Q). Thus the power-short window scale and nontrivial congruent-support residue aliasing are disjoint.
730507ae5291672a.proof:
Equation (4) follows directly from (3), and (5) follows from V<=v<2V.

If V<H, then (1) gives P>Q, so every p>=P satisfies p>Q. Suppose q_1,q_2 are in [Q,2Q) and congruent modulo p. Then p divides q_1-q_2, while
  |q_1-q_2|<Q<p.
The only multiple of p with absolute value less than p is zero, so q_1=q_2. This proves injectivity.

Conversely, if q_1 and q_2 are distinct and congruent modulo p, then |q_1-q_2| is a positive multiple of p. Since both integers belong to an interval of length Q, this gives (6). Because p>=P, equation (6) implies P<Q. Substitution of P=QH/V then gives H/V<1, or V>H. For a congruent-support block containing at least two distinct q-values, choose those two values and apply the preceding argument. Since v>=V, equation (4) gives (7).

Finally, Q>=2 and theta>0 imply Q^(-theta)<1, so (8) implies V<H. The injectivity conclusion already proved therefore applies. Equations (1) and (8) give
  P>=Q^(1+theta),
hence p>=P>=Q^(1+theta). Equations (5) and (8) give the second inequality in (9). This proves every assertion.

glossary.nontrivial residue-aliasing block: A coefficient support containing at least two distinct q-values in [Q,2Q) that are congruent modulo p.
glossary.short-window injective regime: The scale V<H, equivalently P=QH/V>Q, in which reduction modulo p is injective on q in [Q,2Q).

731aecc74ff42615.title: EXACT PRIMITIVE SINGLE-OUTPUT SATURATOR FOR THE ABSTRACT PMLS BLOCK. Let r>1 be odd and squarefree, let C be a unit modulo r, and put v_C(x)=e_r(-Cx) for x in G_r. Let P_{r,r} be the primitive-conductor projector from fact b4934b4981fc5817. Then
731aecc74ff42615.author: slava chan
731aecc74ff42615.statement:
EXACT PRIMITIVE SINGLE-OUTPUT SATURATOR FOR THE ABSTRACT PMLS BLOCK. Let r>1 be odd and squarefree, let C be a unit modulo r, and put v_C(x)=e_r(-Cx) for x in G_r. Let P_{r,r} be the primitive-conductor projector from fact b4934b4981fc5817. Then
||P_{r,r}v_C||_2^2=phi^*(r)r/phi(r).                                (1)
Consequently there is a unit vector f_C in l2(G_r), supported entirely on primitive multiplicative characters, such that
sum_{x in G_r}f_C(x)e_r(Cx)=sqrt(phi^*(r)r/phi(r)).                  (2)

Let r,r'>1 be coprime odd squarefree integers. Use the notation of fact 18a0de57eaf35171, fix one unit physical output j_0 and units c,c',h, and take w(j)=1 if j=j_0 and zero otherwise. There are unit vectors f in the primitive sector modulo r and g in the primitive sector modulo r' for which
|B_{r,r'}(f,g;w,h,k)|
=sqrt(phi^*(r)r/phi(r))sqrt(phi^*(r')r'/phi(r')).                    (3)
In particular, for odd semiprimes whose prime factors tend to infinity, the right side is (1+o(1))sqrt(rr'). Hence an arbitrary-weight, arbitrary-incidence version of the primitive PMLS block cannot have a uniform operator constant smaller than this single-output scale. This does not refute a literal C4 estimate with its fixed interval weight and restricted common-row incidence; it proves those structures are essential.
731aecc74ff42615.proof:
For a multiplicative character chi modulo r, use the normalized transform of fact 18a0de57eaf35171:
widehat v_C(chi)=phi(r)^(-1)sum_{x in G_r}e_r(-Cx)overline{chi(x)}.   (4)
If chi is primitive, the primitive Gauss identity gives
sum_{x in G_r}overline{chi(x)}e_r(-Cx)
=chi(-C)tau_r(overline chi),                                        (5)
whose absolute value is sqrt(r). There are phi^*(r) primitive characters. Multiplicative Parseval and orthogonal projection therefore give
||P_{r,r}v_C||_2^2
=phi(r)sum_{chi primitive}|widehat v_C(chi)|^2
=phi(r)phi^*(r)r/phi(r)^2,
which is (1).

Set f_C=P_{r,r}v_C/||P_{r,r}v_C||_2. The denominator is nonzero because r is odd, so phi^*(r)>0. Since P_{r,r} is self-adjoint,
sum_x f_C(x)e_r(Cx)
=<f_C,v_C>
=<f_C,P_{r,r}v_C>
=||P_{r,r}v_C||_2,
proving (2).

For (3), put C=chj_0^{-1} modulo r and C'=c'hj_0^{-1} modulo r'. Choose f=f_C. Choose g=f_{C'}; then the first bracket in equation (3) of fact 18a0de57eaf35171 equals the positive quantity in (2), and so does the second bracket before conjugation. Since w is supported only at j_0, their product is exactly (3).

Finally, if r=pq with p,q distinct odd primes, then
phi^*(r)/phi(r)=[(p-2)/(p-1)][(q-2)/(q-1)],
which tends to one when both primes tend to infinity. The same holds for r', proving the asymptotic assertion and the scoped consequence.

glossary.f_C: the normalized primitive projection of v_C
glossary.v_C: the additive phase vector x mapsto e_r(-Cx) on G_r

73b711f7dea1a0ee.title: BUFFER-EXTENDED COMPLETE-FREQUENCY THREE-ROUGH-PRIME C3 TRACE
73b711f7dea1a0ee.author: slava chan
73b711f7dea1a0ee.statement:
BUFFER-EXTENDED COMPLETE-FREQUENCY THREE-ROUGH-PRIME C3 TRACE.

Fix integers J,C_A>=1, a constant C>=1, and 0<kappa<=1/100. Put sigma=kappa/100 and beta_1=6/5-3sigma. Let Q be sufficiently large, let 1<=beta<=beta_1, and put
B=Q^beta, H_T=B/Q, L=H_T Q^sigma, S_0=H_T^2 Q^(3sigma), Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma).
Let V,P_1,P_2,P_3>=1 be dyadic scales, put nu=log V/log Q and a_i=log P_i/log Q for 1<=i<=3, and assume
0<=nu<=2beta-2+3sigma, a_i>=3/2-beta-3sigma,
and C^(-1)B<=VP_1P_2P_3<=CB.
Let xi_v be supported on squarefree V<=v<2V, with v<=S_0, every prime divisor of v at most L, and |xi_v|<=tau_J(v). Let A be a fixed nonzero integer with |A|<=Q^(C_A), let |c_q|<=1 for Q<=q<2Q, let G>0, and put H_P=H_T/G.

For every dyadic integer F>=1, let nu_F(h) be supported on F<=|h|<2F with |nu_F(h)|<=tau_J(|h|), let omega_F satisfy, for every fixed J_0>=1,
|omega_F|<=C(J_0)min(1,(F/H_P)^(-J_0)),
and let Psi_F be a fixed-complexity uniformly scaled-smooth projective amplitude in q/Q, |h|/F, v/V and p_i/P_i for 1<=i<=3. Define T_C3,buf with the literal prefactor H_P^(-1), summed over all F,q,h,v and distinct ordered primes p_1<p_2<p_3 with p_i on P_i, p_i>=Z and gcd(vp_1p_2p_3,q)=1, coefficient omega_F c_q nu_F(h) xi_v Psi_F, and phase
e_q(Ah(vp_1p_2p_3)^(-1)).
Assume the prime cells are refined so that order between different cells is automatic, while before imposing distinct order the complete coefficient and amplitude are symmetric under permutations of variables belonging to the same cell.

(i) If G>=1, then T_C3,buf=O(GQ^(2-delta_1)) for some fixed delta_1>0.
(ii) If 0<eta<sigma and Q^(-sigma+eta)<=G<=Q^(sigma-eta), then T_C3,buf=O(Q^(2-delta_2)) for some fixed delta_2>0.

The estimate includes H_P<1, every actual dyadic integer-frequency block, a fixed possibly nonunit target A, unrestricted gcd(h,q), every permutation of the three rough-prime slots after cell refinement, equal prime-scale cells, and all pair- and triple-collision bookkeeping terms introduced by equal-cell symmetrization. It is uniform under polylogarithmically many inherited source, parent, fixed-U, high, collision, provenance, sign, dyadic and uniformly projective smooth labels acting as label scalars or absorbable into the displayed coefficient class. No arbitrary joint deletion mask is allowed. Taking xi_v=-mu(v) gives the literal C3 marker coefficient of fact 6414b11506a84ff0. The theorem estimates only complete C3 anatomy and asserts no later-beta, moving actual-Z, endpoint, PMD, DCE, logical bad-N, four-prime-capture, or Goldbach conclusion.
73b711f7dea1a0ee.proof:
We first prove the grouped-slot geometry through beta_1, rather than importing the shorter beta range of fact 0576f567200d41f1. The fixed product constant gives
nu+a_1+a_2+a_3=beta+epsilon_Q, with |epsilon_Q|<=log C/log Q.                         (1)
Choose Q so large that |epsilon_Q|<=sigma/4. Put
L_beta=2beta-2 and U_beta=3-2beta.
For distinct indices i,j,k,
nu+a_i=beta+epsilon_Q-a_j-a_k
<=beta+epsilon_Q-2(3/2-beta-3sigma)
=3beta-3+6sigma+epsilon_Q.                                           (2)
Since beta<=6/5-3sigma,
(U_beta-4sigma)-(3beta-3+6sigma+epsilon_Q)
=6-5beta-10sigma-epsilon_Q
>=5sigma-epsilon_Q>0.                                                 (3)
Thus every nu+a_i<U_beta-4sigma.

Moreover,
max_i(nu+a_i)>=(beta+epsilon_Q+2nu)/3
>=(beta-|epsilon_Q|)/3.                                              (4)
At beta<=6/5-3sigma,
beta/3-(L_beta+2sigma)
=(6-5beta-6sigma)/3>=3sigma.                                         (5)
Equations (4)-(5) and |epsilon_Q|<=sigma/4 show that some index i satisfies
L_beta+2sigma<nu+a_i<U_beta-4sigma.                                  (6)
Fix such i and put S=VP_i and T=P_jP_k. Fixed dyadic endpoint constants may be absorbed by increasing Q. Weakening (6) by one sigma gives
H_T^2 Q^sigma<=S<=Q^(1-3sigma)/H_T^2,                                (7)
and ST is comparable to B=QH_T. All primes dividing v are at most L<Z, so v is coprime to each rough prime.

Expand the scaled-smooth amplitude into logarithmic Fourier modes. Its projective coefficient norm is uniformly summable. The coefficient of S, obtained by convolving xi_v with one prime indicator, is bounded by a fixed divisor function. The coefficient of T, obtained by convolving the other two prime indicators, is also divisor-bounded.

Fix an actual integer-frequency block F and put u_F=F/H_P. Split it into h>0 and h<0. On the negative block reindex n=-h; its phase has target -A and its coefficient remains divisor-bounded. Apply fact 42720f6d803c4640 separately to the positive block with target A and the reindexed negative block with target -A, with frequency parameter F, model parameter H_T, first multiplicative length S, and imbalance
G_F=H_T/F=G/u_F.
The fact applies to both signs because F>=1, H_T>=1, ST is comparable to QH_T, each of A and -A is fixed and may be nonunit, and gcd(n,q) is unrestricted. It gives a bound with F^(-1) normalization. Multiplication by F/H_P=u_F converts this to the literal H_P^(-1) normalization. Summing the two sign bounds changes only an absolute constant. Apart from Q^epsilon, the resulting four terms are
G^(1/4)u_F^(3/4)Q^2H_T^(1/2)S^(-1/4),
G^(1/4)u_F^(3/4)Q^(7/4)H_T^(1/2)S^(1/4),
u_FQ^2H_TS^(-1/2),
u_FQ^(7/4)H_T.                                                       (8)
The two bounds in (7) give the first three baseline estimates
Q^(2-sigma/4), Q^(2-3sigma/4), Q^(2-sigma/2),                       (9)
respectively. Nonemptiness of (7) implies
H_T^4<=Q^(1-4sigma),                                                 (10)
so the fourth baseline expression is at most Q^(2-sigma).

Choose J_0 large. The dyadic decay hypothesis gives
sum_F |omega_F|u_F^(3/4)+sum_F |omega_F|u_F=O(1),                   (11)
also when H_P<1, because then every actual F>=1 has u_F>1 and the same arbitrary fixed-order decay applies.

If G>=1, use G^(1/4)<=G in (8)-(11), and also 1<=G for the last two terms. After choosing epsilon sufficiently small, this proves (i). On the strip in (ii),
G^(1/4)<=Q^((sigma-eta)/4).
The first term in (9) therefore retains a saving eta/4, the second retains a larger saving, and the last two retain their displayed savings. This proves (ii) for the unrestricted prime boxes.

It remains to impose distinct order in equal prime-scale cells. On a cell containing m of the three prime variables, symmetry expresses the ordered distinct sum as 1/m! times the unrestricted sum after inclusion-exclusion over equality partitions. There are finitely many pair- and triple-collision partitions. If p_i=p_j=p on a pair-collision stratum, the number of choices for the remaining multiplicative variables is, up to divisor and logarithmic factors,
O(VP_iP_k)=O(B/P_i)=O(B/Z).
A triple collision is no larger. On each F block, summing q and h and applying the literal prefactor bounds all collision strata by
Q^epsilon |omega_F|(F/H_P)QB/Z.
Their total is therefore O(Q^(1+beta-(3/2-beta-3sigma)+epsilon)) by (11), namely
O(Q^(2beta-1/2+3sigma+epsilon))
=O(Q^(19/10-3sigma+epsilon))                                       (12)
at beta<=beta_1. This is power-saving relative to Q^2, hence also relative to GQ^2 when G>=1. Equations (8)-(12) include every permutation, pair collision and triple collision created by the exact symmetrization.

We finally verify the literal marker claim rather than merely naming fact 6414b11506a84ff0. Let r=vp_1p_2p_3 on distinct-prime support. For sufficiently large Q, L>=2. Also
S_0/L=H_TQ^(2sigma)>=Q^(2sigma),
so L<=S_0. Furthermore
Z/L=Q^(5/2-2beta-4sigma)>=Q^(1/10+2sigma),
so L<Z. The integer r is squarefree because v is squarefree, the p_i are distinct, and every prime divisor of v is at most L<Z<=p_i. There is no prime divisor of r in the open interval (L,Z). The product assumption and
B/S_0=Q^(2-beta-3sigma)
show r>S_0 after absorbing C, while
Z^4/B=Q^(6-5beta-12sigma)>=Q^(3sigma)
shows Z^4>r after absorbing C. Thus fact 6414b11506a84ff0 applies with stopping height S_0, places r in its unique three-rough-prime alternative, and gives coefficient -mu(v). This completes the marker identification and proves both estimates with all stated bookkeeping.

glossary.Psi_F: The uniformly scaled-smooth projective amplitude on a C3 block.
glossary.T_C3,buf: The complete buffer-extended reciprocal trace with a small factor and three ordered rough primes.
glossary.delta_C3,loc: A fixed power-saving exponent for the local complete C3 trace.
glossary.nu_F(h): The divisor-bounded coefficient on one actual dyadic Poisson-frequency block.
glossary.omega_F: The scalar Fourier-decay coefficient attached to the block of length F.
glossary.u_F: The ratio F/H_P of the actual integer-frequency length to the natural Poisson frequency scale.
glossary.xi_v: The divisor-bounded coefficient on the normalized C3 small factor v.

73fb9efe1286f7e9.title: Fix an integer J≥1. Let Q,H,S,T≥1. For each integer q with Q≤q<2Q choose a unit A_q modulo q. Let ν_h,a_s,b_t be complex coefficients supported respectively on
