73fb9efe1286f7e9.author: slava chan
73fb9efe1286f7e9.statement:
Fix an integer J≥1. Let Q,H,S,T≥1. For each integer q with Q≤q<2Q choose a unit A_q modulo q. Let ν_h,a_s,b_t be complex coefficients supported respectively on
H≤h<2H,  S≤s<2S,  T≤t<2T,
and satisfying
|ν_h|≤τ_J(h), |a_s|≤τ_J(s), |b_t|≤τ_J(t).
Define
W_q=Σ_{h,s,t,gcd(st,q)=1}ν_ha_sb_t e_q(A_qh(st)^(-1)).       (1)
Then for every ε>0,
Σ_{Q≤q<2Q}|W_q|
≪_{J,ε}(QHST)^ε Q(HT)^(1/2)
 [HT+(HT)²/Q]^(1/4)[QS²+S⁴]^(1/4).                          (2)
The same bound, with an additional factor |A|^ε absorbed into the epsilon factor, holds if A is a fixed nonzero integer, U_q is an arbitrary unit modulo q, and A_q in (1) is replaced by AU_q without assuming gcd(A,q)=1. Crucially, no coprimality condition on h is required.

As a balanced corollary, suppose ST=QH and, for some τ>0,
H²Q^τ≤S≤Q^(1-τ)/H².                                        (3)
Then
H^(-1)Σ_{Q≤q<2Q}|W_q|
≪_{J,ε,τ}(QHST)^ε Q^(2-τ/4).                                (4)
73fb9efe1286f7e9.proof:
First assume every A_q is a unit. For z modulo q define
γ_q(z)=Σ_{h,t:gcd(t,q)=1, h t^(-1)≡z (mod q)}ν_hb_t.          (5)
The divisor-function bounds give
||γ_q||_1≪(QHST)^ε HT.                                       (6)
Expanding its squared norm reduces collisions to
h_1t_2-h_2t_1=kq,                                            (7)
with |k|≪HT/q+1. If T≥H, fix h_1,h_2,k. The integer solutions (t_1,t_2) in their dyadic intervals to (7) lie on one affine lattice line and number
≪1+T gcd(h_1,h_2)/H.
Summing over h_1,h_2 and using
Σ_{h_1,h_2∼H}gcd(h_1,h_2)≪H²log(2H)
shows that each k contributes ≪(QHST)^ε HT. If T≤H, interchange the h- and t-pairs and use the analogous gcd sum. This also includes k=0. Since there are O(HT/q+1) possible k,
||γ_q||_2²≪(QHST)^ε[HT+(HT)²/q].                            (8)
Interpolation between (6) and (8) gives
||γ_q||_(4/3)
≪(QHST)^ε(HT)^(1/2)[HT+(HT)²/q]^(1/4).                      (9)

Define the unweighted reciprocal fourth energy
J_4(S;q)=#{(s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4):
 s_i∈[S,2S), gcd(s_i,q)=1,
 s_1^(-1)+s_2^(-1)≡s_3^(-1)+s_4^(-1) (mod q)}.              (10)
We claim
Σ_{Q≤q<2Q}J_4(S;q)≪(QS)^arepsilon[QS²+S⁴].                (11)
After clearing denominators, the congruence in (10) says q divides
Δ=(s_1+s_2)s_3s_4-(s_3+s_4)s_1s_2.                          (12)
If Δ≠0, a fixed quadruple permits at most τ(|Δ|) moduli q, giving O(S^(4+ε)) in total. If Δ=0, then
1/s_1+1/s_2=1/s_3+1/s_4.
For fixed s_1,s_2, reduce their common value to u/v. The other pair satisfies
(us_3-v)(us_4-v)=v²,                                        (13)
so divisor counting gives O(S^ε) choices. Hence there are O(S^(2+ε)) rational-diagonal quadruples, each allowing O(Q) moduli. This proves (11).

For z modulo q put
F_q(z)=Σ_{s:gcd(s,q)=1}a_s e_q(A_qz s^(-1)).                 (14)
Because A_q is a unit, additive orthogonality and the divisor-function bounds yield
Σ_{z mod q}|F_q(z)|⁴≪(QHST)^ε qJ_4(S;q).                    (15)
Also W_q=Σ_zγ_q(z)F_q(z). Hölder with exponents 4/3 and 4, followed by (9) and (15), gives
|W_q|≪(QHST)^ε(HT)^(1/2)
 [HT+(HT)²/q]^(1/4)q^(1/4)J_4(S;q)^(1/4).                   (16)
Sum over q. Since q is comparable to Q, Hölder in q and (11) give
Σ_q q^(1/4)J_4(S;q)^(1/4)
≪Q·[QS²+S⁴]^(1/4).
Substitution in (16) proves (2).

Now let A be fixed and nonzero. Split the moduli by c=gcd(A,q), writing q=cq_0 and A=cA_0. The phase reduces to modulus q_0 and A_0U_q is a unit there. The original unit condition implies gcd(st,c)=1, which is the product of a condition on s and one on t and can be absorbed into their separate coefficients. For fixed c|A, apply (2) with modulus scale Q/c. Expanding the two fourth-root brackets gives four terms whose c-powers are respectively c^(-5/4), c^(-1), c^(-1), and c^(-3/4). They are summable over c|A up to |A|^ε. This proves the fixed-target extension. Notice that the split uses gcd(A,q), not gcd(Ah,q), so h remains inside γ_q.

Finally assume ST=QH. Expanding the right side of (2), dividing by H, and normalizing by Q² gives four factors
(H²/S)^(1/4),
(H²S/Q)^(1/4),
(H²/S)^(1/2),
(H⁴/Q)^(1/4).                                                (17)
The lower bound in (3) makes the first and third at most Q^(-τ/4) and Q^(-τ/2). The upper bound makes the second at most Q^(-τ/4). Since the interval (3) is nonempty, H⁴≤Q^(1-2τ), so the fourth is at most Q^(-τ/2). Thus every term saves at least Q^(-τ/4), proving (4).

glossary.A: A fixed nonzero target numerator in the noncoprime extension.
glossary.A_q: A unit phase numerator modulo q.
glossary.F_q: The reciprocal Fourier sum in the s-variable.
glossary.J_4(S;q): The fourth reciprocal energy defined in (10).
glossary.γ_q: The residue distribution of h times the inverse of t modulo q.

74272e88a5f750f8.title: FIXED-ACTIVE-PRODUCT AVERAGE OF THE C4 EXCEPTIONAL TENSOR KERNEL
74272e88a5f750f8.author: slava chan
74272e88a5f750f8.statement:
FIXED-ACTIVE-PRODUCT AVERAGE OF THE C4 EXCEPTIONAL TENSOR KERNEL.

Let r be a squarefree positive integer, and let h,h' be integers with
gcd(hh',r)=1.                                                         (1)
For an integer T define
s(r,T)=product_{p|r, p^2|T}p.                                        (2)
Let I and J be finite integer intervals of cardinalities U_1 and U_2. Then
sum_{u in I}sum_{u' in J}
 s(r,hru'-h'ru)/r
 <=tau(r)U_1U_2/r+min(U_1,U_2).                                      (3)

In particular, suppose r, B and all interval endpoints are bounded by a fixed power of Q and
U_1,U_2<=C B/r                                                     (4)
for a fixed C. Then fact e705401df9f0709e gives, for every epsilon>0,
sum_{u in I}sum_{u' in J}
 s(r,hru'-h'ru)/r
 <<_{C,epsilon}Q^epsilon(B^2/r^3+B/r).                               (5)

Under the simultaneous tensor Gram of fact df97bf1eba0495be, write n=ru and n'=ru'. Formula (5) is therefore an unweighted fixed-r average for its exceptional factor s/r. It remains valid after restricting to squarefree n,n', to C4 marked rows, or by any zero-one literal mask. It does not handle arbitrary complex weights by cancellation, sum varying active products r, restore inactive-prime face coefficients, estimate a complete centered face, prove NR-DIL, or imply Goldbach.
74272e88a5f750f8.proof:
Put
T=hu'-h'u.                                                           (6)
Since r is squarefree, for every p|r one has
p^2|rT if and only if p|T.
Therefore
s(r,hru'-h'ru)=product_{p|r,p|T}p=gcd(r,T).                          (7)

Use the elementary identity
gcd(r,T)=sum_{t|r,t|T}phi(t).                                        (8)
For fixed t|r, the congruence
hu'=h'u modulo t                                                     (9)
has one residue class for u' modulo t after u is fixed, because h is a unit modulo t by (1). Hence the number N_t of pairs (u,u') in I times J satisfying (9) is at most
U_1(U_2/t+1).
Solving instead for u after u' is fixed gives
N_t<=U_2(U_1/t+1).
Consequently
N_t<=U_1U_2/t+min(U_1,U_2).                                         (10)

Insert (8)-(10) and use
sum_{t|r}phi(t)=r,
sum_{t|r}phi(t)/t<=tau(r).
This yields
sum_{u,u'}gcd(r,T)/r
 <=U_1U_2 tau(r)/r+min(U_1,U_2),
which is (3) by (7).

Under (4), the first term in (3) is at most
C^2 tau(r)B^2/r^3,
and the second is at most CB/r. Fact e705401df9f0709e supplies tau(r)<<Q^epsilon when r is bounded by a fixed power of Q. This proves (5). The final specialization follows from the definition of the kernel in fact df97bf1eba0495be; restrictions only remove nonnegative summands from the left side of (3).

glossary.fixed-active-product exceptional average: The average of s(r,hn'-h'n)/r over marked rows n,n' divisible by one fixed squarefree active product r.

75432ab3881c2178.title: EXACT TWO-SIDED FULL-CARRIER NORMAL FORM FOR EVERY ADDITIVE SUBFACE OF LIT-INC-VLS
75432ab3881c2178.author: slava chan
75432ab3881c2178.statement:
EXACT TWO-SIDED FULL-CARRIER NORMAL FORM FOR EVERY ADDITIVE SUBFACE OF LIT-INC-VLS.

Let p be a prime. For i=1,2 let d_i,k_i be positive integers such that p,d_i,k_i are pairwise coprime within each fixed i. Let N,n_1,n_2 be coprime to p d_1d_2k_1k_2. Put
 s_1=d_1k_1, q_2=d_2k_2.                                   (1)
Define the two row additive phases
 E_1=e_{d_1}(N[pn_1k_1]^(-1)),
 E_2=e_{d_2}(-N[pn_2k_2]^(-1)),                             (2)
and the p-difference phase
 E_p=e_p(N[n_1s_1]^(-1)-N[n_2q_2]^(-1)).                   (3)
Then exactly
 E_1E_pE_2
 =e_{pd_1}(N[n_1k_1]^(-1))
  e_{pd_2}(-N[n_2k_2]^(-1)).                               (4)
Denote the right side by cal C_{d_1,d_2}. It is a two-sided coefficient-one inverse-difference carrier whose two moduli share the canonical prime p.

In the literal notation of fact b9560e346963b9e0, put n_i=au_i. Expand C_1 into parent h_1 and additive denominator d_1|h_1 by fact 55c6f91ec7fd414f. Expand either H_2 or J_2 prime by prime in the analogous form
 R^{M_{12}}_{q_2,h_2}(n_2)
 =sum_{d_2|h_2}1/phi(h_2/d_2)
   e_{d_2}(M_{12}[n_2(q_2/d_2)]^(-1)),                     (5)
where h_2=q_2 for H_2 and h_2 runs through the literal boundary parents for J_2. Put k_i equal to the corresponding full cofactor in (1). Then the exponential part of every selected (d_1,d_2) subface in either main face is exactly cal C_{d_1,d_2}. All literal parent and subface coefficients, both beta and gamma coefficients, the full/boundary restrictions, and in the J_2 face the indicator A!=D remain unchanged.

For the J_2 face, replacing the p exponential by
 rho_p(A-D;a)=e_p((A-D)a^(-1))+1/(p-1)
under A!=D adds exactly the correction
 1_{A!=D}E_1E_2/(p-1)                                     (6)
beside cal C_{d_1,d_2}. Thus every coefficient-one exponential in LIT-INC-VLS is in the common two-sided carrier (4); the only term created by its centered rho notation is explicitly 1/(p-1).

No estimate for the aggregate of (4), the correction (6), LIT-INC-VLS, K_inc^rem, another incidence cell, C_small or Goldbach is asserted.
75432ab3881c2178.proof:
We prove both fusions directly. The p-local component of
 e_{pd_1}(N[n_1k_1]^(-1))
is
 e_p(N[n_1k_1]^(-1)d_1^(-1))
 =e_p(N[n_1d_1k_1]^(-1))
 =e_p(N[n_1s_1]^(-1)).                                    (7)
Its d_1-local component is
 e_{d_1}(N[n_1k_1]^(-1)p^(-1))
 =e_{d_1}(N[pn_1k_1]^(-1))=E_1.                            (8)
Since (p,d_1)=1, CRT combines (7) and (8), giving
 E_1e_p(N[n_1s_1]^(-1))
 =e_{pd_1}(N[n_1k_1]^(-1)).                                (9)

Likewise, the p-local component of
 e_{pd_2}(-N[n_2k_2]^(-1))
is
 e_p(-N[n_2k_2]^(-1)d_2^(-1))
 =e_p(-N[n_2d_2k_2]^(-1))
 =e_p(-N[n_2q_2]^(-1)),                                    (10)
and its d_2-local component is
 e_{d_2}(-N[n_2k_2]^(-1)p^(-1))
 =e_{d_2}(-N[pn_2k_2]^(-1))=E_2.                           (11)
CRT combines (10) and (11). Multiplying that identity by (9) proves (4).

We verify the literal row-two expansion. The proof of equation (13) in fact 55c6f91ec7fd414f is a primewise expansion of a centered product and applies with q_2,M_{12},n_2,h_2 in place of s_1,M_1,n_1,h_1. This gives (5). Since
 pM_{12}=N modulo q_2,
reducing modulo d_2 and putting k_2=q_2/d_2 identifies the conjugate phase in (5) as
 e_{d_2}(-N[pn_2k_2]^(-1))=E_2.
The analogous row-one identification, recorded in fact e035633108f2b250 for the literal squarefree s_1, gives E_1. Also, by the definitions of A,D and n_i=au_i in fact b9560e346963b9e0,
 e_p((A-D)a^(-1))=E_p.
Thus (4) applies coefficientwise to every additive subface in both literal tensors, without changing any outer coefficient or mask.

Finally, when A!=D,
 rho_p(A-D;a)=e_p((A-D)a^(-1))+1/(p-1).
Multiplying by E_1E_2 and using (4) gives cal C_{d_1,d_2}+E_1E_2/(p-1). Multiplication by the unchanged indicator proves (6). This establishes the exact normal form and all scope restrictions.

glossary.cal C_{d_1,d_2}: the two-sided full inverse-difference carrier at moduli pd_1 and pd_2
glossary.d_2: the selected additive denominator in an expanded row-two tensor

75483b80daf0b690.title: Fix L>=1 and epsilon>0. Let H>=2, let C be a nonzero integer with |C|<=H^L, and let E be any integer. Let N(C,E;H) be the number of ordered tuples
75483b80daf0b690.author: slava chan
75483b80daf0b690.statement:
Fix L>=1 and epsilon>0. Let H>=2, let C be a nonzero integer with |C|<=H^L, and let E be any integer. Let N(C,E;H) be the number of ordered tuples
(r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4,b_1,b_2,b_3,b_4)
such that r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4 are pairwise distinct primes in [H^2,2H^2), b_1,b_2,b_3,b_4 are nonzero integers with |b_i|<=H, and, on putting
G=r_1r_2, T=r_3r_4,
B=b_1r_2+b_2r_1, D=b_3r_4+b_4r_3,
one has
C=BT+GD and E=BT-GD.
Then
N(C,E;H)<<_{L,epsilon}H^epsilon
uniformly in C,E,H. Consequently, for every real interval J of length V>=0,
#{tuples at fixed C with E in J}<<_{L,epsilon}(V+1)H^epsilon.

More generally, fix B_0>=0. Give every tuple a nonnegative weight at most (log(2H))^{B_0}, and let L_H(C) be a nonnegative common carrier weight supported on nonzero |C|<=H^L with
sum_C L_H(C)<=H^9(log(2H))^{B_0}.
Then the aggregate of all tuples satisfying |E|<=H^5 is
<<_{L,B_0,epsilon}H^{14+epsilon}
after weighting by L_H(C). Thus the small top-contrast layer |BT-GD|<=H^5 is paid at the DCE H^{14+o(1)} scale.
75483b80daf0b690.proof:
Adding and subtracting the two equations for C and E gives
2BT=C+E and 2GD=C-E.
The integers B and D are nonzero for every counted tuple. Indeed B=0 would imply r_1 divides b_1r_2, hence r_1 divides b_1 because r_1 and r_2 are distinct primes. This is impossible since 0<|b_1|<=H<r_1. The proof for D is identical. Therefore neither C+E nor C-E can vanish for a counted tuple.

Every realizable top contrast has polynomial size independently of the stated E. The bounds |b_i|<=H and r_i<2H^2 give |B|<4H^3, |D|<4H^3, G<4H^4, and T<4H^4. Hence |E|=|BT-GD|<32H^7. Thus, if |E|>=32H^7, N(C,E;H)=0.

Now suppose E is realizable and put M_+=(C+E)/2 and M_-=(C-E)/2. If either is not an integer or is zero, N(C,E;H)=0. Otherwise BT=M_+ and GD=M_-. The number of integer divisor pairs (B,T) is at most 2tau(|M_+|). For each possible positive T, the number of ordered prime factorizations T=r_3r_4 is at most tau(T). Since T divides |M_+|, tau(T)<=tau(|M_+|). Thus the number of possibilities for B,r_3,r_4 is at most 2tau(|M_+|)^2. Similarly the number of possibilities for D,r_1,r_2 is at most 2tau(|M_-|)^2. Pairwise distinctness and the prime interval restrictions only decrease these counts.

Once B,r_1,r_2 are fixed, the equation B=b_1r_2+b_2r_1 has at most one solution with |b_1|,|b_2|<=H for all sufficiently large H. Reduction modulo r_1 determines b_1 modulo r_1, and the interval [-H,H] has length 2H<r_1; then b_2 is fixed. Bounded smaller H are absorbed in the implied constant. The same argument uniquely recovers b_3,b_4 from D,r_3,r_4.

For realizable E,
|M_+|,|M_-|<H^L+32H^7.
This is bounded by a fixed power of H depending only on L. The elementary divisor bound proved in fact 3c92603bdcab54d5 therefore gives tau(|M_+|),tau(|M_-|)<<_{L,epsilon}H^{epsilon/4} after choosing the auxiliary exponent appropriately. Hence
N(C,E;H)<=4tau(|M_+|)^2tau(|M_-|)^2<<_{L,epsilon}H^epsilon.
Together with the zero count for nonrealizable E, this is uniform over every integer E.

A real interval of length V contains at most floor(V)+1<=V+1 integers, so summing the uniform fixed-E bound proves the interval assertion.

For the weighted aggregate with |E|<=H^5, use the interval assertion with J=[-H^5,H^5], whose length is 2H^5. With epsilon replaced by epsilon/3, the weighted number of right tuples at each fixed C is
<<_{L,B_0,epsilon}H^{5+epsilon/3}(log(2H))^{B_0}.
Multiplying by the total L_H-mass H^9(log(2H))^{B_0} gives
<<H^{14+epsilon/3}(log(2H))^{2B_0}
<<_{B_0,epsilon}H^{14+epsilon}.
This proves the final assertion.

glossary.B_0: a fixed exponent controlling polylogarithmic packet weights
glossary.J: a real interval in the top-contrast coordinate
glossary.N(C,E;H): the fixed-carrier fixed-top-contrast four-prime packet count

754cf92eea3a7532.title: EXACT PHYSICAL-FRAME DECOMPOSITION, EQUAL-FREQUENCY PAYMENT, AND NONZERO CROSSED INVERSE PHASE FOR THE CORRECTED FORWARD-E11 LEADING MODE. Let \(x\ge3\), \(D\ge2\), \(R=D^\beta\), \(P\ge1\), and \(\sigma>0\) satisfy
754cf92eea3a7532.author: slava chan
754cf92eea3a7532.statement:
EXACT PHYSICAL-FRAME DECOMPOSITION, EQUAL-FREQUENCY PAYMENT, AND NONZERO CROSSED INVERSE PHASE FOR THE CORRECTED FORWARD-E11 LEADING MODE. Let \(x\ge3\), \(D\ge2\), \(R=D^\beta\), \(P\ge1\), and \(\sigma>0\) satisfy
\[
 P\ge (R/D)^2D^{2\sigma},\qquad \beta+2\sigma\le3/2.                 \tag{1}
\]
Let \(N\) be a positive integer and \(\mathcal P\) a finite set of primes in \([P,2P]\). Let \(\mathscr A\) be a finite set of \(\alpha=(\iota,h,p,\ell)\), where \(p,\ell\) are distinct primes and \(h\ne0\). Put
\[
 \gamma(\alpha)=(h,u),\quad u=p\ell,quad
 \mathscr A_\gamma=\{\alpha:\gamma(\alpha)=\gamma\}.
\]
Let \(E_\alpha>0\), and assume for every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 \max_\gamma|\mathscr A_\gamma|\ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon,quad
 \max_\alpha E_\alpha\ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon D/R,quad
 \sum_\alpha E_\alpha\ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon R.              \tag{2}
\]
For \(a\in\mathcal P\), \(m\ge1\), and \(\alpha=(\iota,h,p,\ell)\), let \(C_a(m;\alpha)\) be complex and satisfy
\[
 |C_a(m;\alpha)|\ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon E_\alpha.             \tag{3}
\]
Extend it by zero unless
\[
 am\le D,quad m\text{ squarefree},quad
 (a,mhuN)=1,quad(m,u)=1,quad(Nh,u)=1,quad0<|h|<u/2.                   \tag{4}
\]
Define in \(\ell^2(\mathscr A)\)
\[
 X_{a,m}(\alpha)=\mu(m)\frac{C_a(m;\alpha)}{\sqrt{E_\alpha}}
 \cdot e_u\!\left(Nh(am)^{-1}\right).                               \tag{5}
\]
For \(a\ne b\), put
\[
 K_m(a,b)=\langle X_{a,m},X_{b,m}\rangle,
\]
and put \(K_m(a,a)=0\). Define
\[
 A_{a,b,m}(\gamma)=\mu(m)^2\sum_{\alpha\in\mathscr A_\gamma}
 \frac{C_a(m;\alpha)\overline{C_b(m;\alpha)}}{E_\alpha}.             \tag{6}
\]
Then, explicitly for \(a\ne b\),
\[
 K_m(a,b)=\sum_\gamma A_{a,b,m}(\gamma)
 e_u\!\left(Nh\,m^{-1}(a^{-1}-b^{-1})\right).                        \tag{7}
\]
Put
\[
 \mathfrak D_m=\sum_{a\ne b}\sum_\gamma|A_{a,b,m}(\gamma)|^2,      \tag{8}
\]
\[
 \mathfrak O_m=\sum_{a\ne b}\sum_{\gamma_1\ne\gamma_2}
 A_{a,b,m}(\gamma_1)\overline{A_{a,b,m}(\gamma_2)}
 \Phi_{a,b,m}(\gamma_1,\gamma_2),                                    \tag{9}
\]
where \(\Phi\) is the quotient of the two phases in (7). Then
\[
 \|K_m\|_{HS}^2=\mathfrak D_m+\mathfrak O_m,qquad
 \mathfrak D_m\ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon P^2D,                   \tag{10}
\]
so the equal-frequency square-root contribution is
\[
 \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon P\sqrt D
 \le x^\varepsilon P D^{2-2\sigma}/R.                                \tag{11}
\]

For \(\gamma_i=(h_i,u_i)\), put
\[
 L_{12}={\rm lcm}(u_1,u_2),quad
 B_{12}=L_{12}h_1/u_1-L_{12}h_2/u_2,quad
 A_{12,m}\equiv Nm^{-1}B_{12}\pmod{L_{12}}.                            \tag{12}
\]
Every nonzero crossed summand satisfies
\[
 \Phi_{a,b,m}(\gamma_1,\gamma_2)
 =e_{L_{12}}\!\left(A_{12,m}(a^{-1}-b^{-1})\right),                   \tag{13}
\]
and
\[
 \gamma_1\ne\gamma_2\Longrightarrow
 A_{12,m}\not\equiv0\pmod{L_{12}}.                                   \tag{14}
\]
No descended common-core divisibility condition is present.

The remaining sufficient supplier is
\[
 \boxed{|\mathfrak O_m|\ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon R^2
 \text{ uniformly in }m.}                                              \tag{OFF-FRAME}
\]
It is not asserted. If it holds, then
\[
 \sup_m\|K_m\|_{HS}
 \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon(P\sqrt D+R)
 \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon P D^{2-2\sigma}/R,                    \tag{15}
\]
and fact d2c6c6e9be57e257 supplies the open physical \(C_{LL}\) estimate of corrected fact bc1b67324480d454.

For the literal forward-E11 coordinates, use the raw coefficient
\[
 C_a(m;\alpha)=C_\iota(am;h,p,\ell)
\]
with the zero extensions of corrected fact bc1b67324480d454. Equation (15) of fact 69e79ebdfba646b4 is the raw Fourier estimate which gives (3) for the envelope of fact a5f73e19fca8e2d5. Those facts and fc442085ff47a053 give (2), (4), fixed-\((h,p\ell)\) multiplicity \(x^{o(1)}\), and the exact physical identification, without deleting the retained \((m,h)>1\) or \((m,N)>1\) sectors. No off-frequency estimate, E11 closure, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
754cf92eea3a7532.proof:
For \(a\ne b\), expansion of (5) gives
\[
 \langle X_{a,m},X_{b,m}\rangle
 =\mu(m)^2\sum_{\alpha=(\iota,h,p,\ell)}
 \frac{C_a(m;\alpha)\overline{C_b(m;\alpha)}}{E_\alpha}
 e_{p\ell}\!\left(Nh\,m^{-1}(a^{-1}-b^{-1})\right).                 \tag{16}
\]
The inverses exist by (4). Grouping by \(\gamma=(h,p\ell)\) proves (6)--(7) on the stated off-diagonal domain. Squaring (7), summing over \(a\ne b\), and separating equal from distinct \(\gamma\) proves the exact identity in (10).

Put \(E_\gamma=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathscr A_\gamma}E_\alpha\). From (3),
\[
 |A_{a,b,m}(\gamma)|\ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon E_\gamma.
\]
Since \(|\mathcal P|\le2P\),
\[
 \mathfrak D_m\ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon P^2\sum_\gamma E_\gamma^2.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz in each fibre and (2), applied with a sufficiently small fraction of \(\varepsilon\), give
\[
\begin{split}
 \sum_\gamma E_\gamma^2
 &\le(\max_\gamma|\mathscr A_\gamma|)\sum_\alpha E_\alpha^2\\
 &\le(\max_\gamma|\mathscr A_\gamma|)
 (\max_\alpha E_\alpha)\sum_\alpha E_\alpha
 \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon D.                                    \tag{17}
\end{split}
\]
This proves (10). Equation (11) follows from \(R=D^\beta\) and \(\beta+2\sigma\le3/2\).

For a nonzero crossed summand, (4) gives
\[
 (abmN,L_{12})=1,qquad(h_i,u_i)=1.
\]
Lifting both phases to modulus \(L_{12}\) proves (12)--(13). Also
\[
 |B_{12}/L_{12}|=|h_1/u_1-h_2/u_2|<1.                                  \tag{18}
\]
If \(B_{12}\equiv0\pmod{L_{12}}\), then (18) gives \(B_{12}=0\). The fractions \(h_i/u_i\) are reduced with positive denominators, so equality forces \(h_1=h_2\) and \(u_1=u_2\), contrary to \(\gamma_1\ne\gamma_2\). Thus \(B_{12}\) is nonzero modulo \(L_{12}\), and multiplication by the unit \(Nm^{-1}\) proves (14).

Assuming (OFF-FRAME), (10) gives
\[
 \|K_m\|_{HS}\ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon(P\sqrt D+R).
\]
The first term is paid by (11). The second is paid because
\[
 R\le P D^{2-2\sigma}/R
 \Longleftrightarrow P\ge(R/D)^2D^{2\sigma}.
\]
This proves (15), and fact d2c6c6e9be57e257 gives the aggregate implication.

For the literal specialization, equation (15) of fact 69e79ebdfba646b4 states
\[
 |(p\ell)^{-1}\widehat F_{\iota,n,p\ell}(h/(p\ell))|
 \ll_J \frac{M}{p\ell}(\log x)^2
 (1+|h|M/(p\ell))^{-J}.
\]
Its definition of \(C_\iota\) is this raw expression multiplied by the literal copy coefficient, whose total variation is bounded on the two-prime integer \(p\ell\). Choose \(E_\alpha\) as in equation (1) of fact a5f73e19fca8e2d5. The displayed raw estimate, with the polylogarithmic literal label loss absorbed into \(x^\varepsilon\), proves (3) directly, without dividing by a truncated projector.

Equation (2) of fact a5f73e19fca8e2d5 gives \(\sum E_\alpha\ll x^\varepsilon R\). Fact fc442085ff47a053 gives \(DM\asymp x\), \(D=x^{1/2+o(1)}\), and \(p\ell\asymp R\), so \(\max E_\alpha\ll x^\varepsilon D/R\). The proof of a5f73e19fca8e2d5 records only polylogarithmic label loss, and fixed \(p\ell\) has at most two ordered distinct-prime factorizations, proving the fibre bound. Fact fc442085ff47a053 gives \((p\ell,N)=1\), \((p\ell,h)=1\), \((m,p\ell)=1\), \(0<|h|<Y_E\), and \(p,\ell\ge2Y_E\), which are (4) without imposing \((m,h)=1\) or \((m,N)=1\). The clean dilator masks and physical identity are those of bc1b67324480d454. Hence the literal kernel is (16). Since (OFF-FRAME) remains unproved, the scope restrictions follow.

glossary.L_{12}: The lcm of the two physical moduli.
glossary.mathscr A_gamma: The provenance fibre at fixed physical frequency.

7592d1548541e1a6.title: HEIGHT-FIBRE MEAN DECOMPOSITION OF THE PRE-CAUCHY DEFECT AND THE EXACT ALL-BAND MEAN-LEAKAGE FRONTIER. Let cal A be a finite set. For each a in cal A let cal H_a be a nonempty finite height fibre of cardinality L_a, let beta_a be complex, and let z_{a,h} be complex for h in cal H_a. Put
7592d1548541e1a6.author: slava chan
7592d1548541e1a6.statement:
HEIGHT-FIBRE MEAN DECOMPOSITION OF THE PRE-CAUCHY DEFECT AND THE EXACT ALL-BAND MEAN-LEAKAGE FRONTIER. Let cal A be a finite set. For each a in cal A let cal H_a be a nonempty finite height fibre of cardinality L_a, let beta_a be complex, and let z_{a,h} be complex for h in cal H_a. Put
b_{a,h}=beta_a,
C_src=sum_a L_a|beta_a|^2>0,                               (1)
zbar_a=L_a^(-1)sum_{h in cal H_a}z_{a,h},
z_{a,h}^circ=z_{a,h}-zbar_a.                               (2)
For outer vectors y=(y_a) define
||y||_L^2=sum_a L_a|y_a|^2,
(P_{beta,L}^perp y)_a
 =y_a-[sum_c L_c beta_c y_c/C_src]conjugate(beta_a).        (3)
Let
T_src=sum_a sum_{h in cal H_a}beta_a z_{a,h},
M_src=sum_a sum_{h in cal H_a}|z_{a,h}|^2,                 (4)
and let D_pre be the Lagrange defect of fact 87fee9c7e02513f9 on the full index set of pairs (a,h). Then exactly
T_src=sum_a L_a beta_a zbar_a,                              (5)
M_src=sum_a sum_h|z_{a,h}^circ|^2+||zbar||_L^2,             (6)
D_pre=C_src[
 sum_a sum_h|z_{a,h}^circ|^2
 +||P_{beta,L}^perp zbar||_L^2].                            (7)
Thus every within-height mean-zero component is automatically perpendicular to the source-coefficient line, while the signed assembly T_src sees only the height means.

Suppose now that the all-band identity of fact e7e8025bde57f04f is arranged on each fibre with a common complete source-minus-density value w_a, independent of h, and exact literal leakage r_{a,h}, so
z_{a,h}=w_a-r_{a,h}.                                       (8)
Put
rbar_a=L_a^(-1)sum_h r_{a,h},
r_{a,h}^circ=r_{a,h}-rbar_a.                               (9)
Then
zbar=w-rbar, z_{a,h}^circ=-r_{a,h}^circ,                   (10)
and the exact defect becomes
D_pre=C_src[
 sum_a sum_h|r_{a,h}^circ|^2
 +||P_{beta,L}^perp(w-rbar)||_L^2].                         (11)
The complete signed assembly is
T_src=sum_a L_a beta_a(w_a-rbar_a).                         (12)
Consequently the mean-zero leakage r^circ drops out of T_src exactly. It contributes positively to D_pre, but it also contributes by the identical amount C_src sum|r^circ|^2 to C_src M_src in the Lagrange identity. Therefore, for any target B>=0,
|T_src|^2<=B                                                (13)
is equivalent to
C_src||P_{beta,L}^perp(w-rbar)||_L^2
 >=C_src||w-rbar||_L^2-B.                                  (14)
The within-height leakage energy cancels completely from this equivalence. Hence the sharp all-band bridge for an earlier signed estimate is an estimate of the outer weighted height-mean vector w-rbar, not a bound for the full leakage norm and not a pointwise support statement in one band.

For the natural forward C1 row, one may take a to collect every non-height coordinate (including the frozen outer-gcd, target-gcd, projective, v, and p data), choose one common h-independent q-universe and the same physical functions F_{a,q} throughout cal H_a, and put every height-dependent cutoff, q-deletion, conductor, collision, and provenance condition into the bounded multipliers kappa_{a,h}(q,t) of fact e7e8025bde57f04f. Then
w_a=u_a-d_a                                                   (15)
is the complete Mobius-weighted hard-source-minus-density row and is independent of h, while r_{a,h} is the exact omitted-family vector. Formula (12) preserves the compensating Archimedean phase through the exact negative-frequency identification before it cancels in the natural term. The same decomposition applies separately in the reverse orientation once its own common Poisson data are inserted; no forward-reverse equality is asserted.

For the literal PMD specialization of fact 87fee9c7e02513f9, take a=(ell,v,p), beta_a=eta_ell xi_v, and cal H_a=I_ell. Then T_src=H S_lit. Thus the desired estimate
|S_lit|^2<=P Q^(8/3+epsilon)                               (16)
is exactly (13) with
B=H^2 P Q^(8/3+epsilon),                                   (17)
or equivalently the height-mean condition (14). No estimate for w-rbar, no bound for S_lit, no PMD closure, and no Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
7592d1548541e1a6.proof:
By definition, sum_h z_{a,h}^circ=0 for every a. Therefore
sum_h|z_{a,h}|^2
 =sum_h|zbar_a+z_{a,h}^circ|^2
 =L_a|zbar_a|^2+sum_h|z_{a,h}^circ|^2.
Summing a proves (6), while (5) follows by summing z_{a,h} over h.

The conjugate source-coefficient vector on the full fibre is constant in h and equals conjugate(beta_a). Every mean-zero fibre vector z^circ is orthogonal to every fibre-constant vector, hence in particular to that source line. The fibre-constant lift of zbar has squared norm ||zbar||_L^2, and its orthogonal projection away from the source line is the fibre-constant lift of P_{beta,L}^perp zbar. Fact fa68efb06f0ec564 gives D_pre=C_src times the squared norm of the full perpendicular projection. The orthogonality of the mean-zero and fibre-constant subspaces therefore proves (7).

Under (8), averaging in h gives zbar_a=w_a-rbar_a. Subtracting this equality from (8) gives z_{a,h}^circ=-r_{a,h}^circ. Substitution into (7) proves (11), and substitution into (5) proves (12).

Using (6) and (10),
M_src=sum_{a,h}|r_{a,h}^circ|^2+||w-rbar||_L^2.
Insert this and (11) into the exact identity
D_pre=C_src M_src-|T_src|^2
from fact 87fee9c7e02513f9. The terms
C_src sum|r^circ|^2
occur on both sides and cancel. Rearrangement proves the equivalence of (13) and (14).

Fact e7e8025bde57f04f supplies (8) when the complete physical and zero-density data are chosen independently of the height coordinate and all height dependence is left in its bounded literal multiplier kappa. Its natural specialization also proves the asserted hard-source meaning of w and preserves the negative-frequency phase identification. Finally, fact 87fee9c7e02513f9 supplies T_src=H S_lit for a=(ell,v,p), beta_a=eta_ell xi_v and h in I_ell. Substituting this equality proves (16)-(17).

glossary.P_{beta,L}^perp: The weighted outer projection away from the conjugate beta source line.
glossary.rbar_a: The height average of the exact omitted-family leakage.
glossary.zbar_a: The exact average of the literal q-row over the height fibre attached to outer coordinate a.

7596cf19a80bf8f3.title: EXACT FINITE-BAND PHYSICAL KERNEL AND NONLOCALITY OF HARD-SOURCE SUPPORT. Let n be a positive integer, let cal I be a nonempty finite set of integers whose elements are pairwise distinct modulo n, and let F be a smooth compactly supported complex function on R. Use
7596cf19a80bf8f3.author: slava chan
7596cf19a80bf8f3.statement:
EXACT FINITE-BAND PHYSICAL KERNEL AND NONLOCALITY OF HARD-SOURCE SUPPORT. Let n be a positive integer, let cal I be a nonempty finite set of integers whose elements are pairwise distinct modulo n, and let F be a smooth compactly supported complex function on R. Use
Fhat(xi)=integral_R F(t)e(-xi t)dt,
e_n(y)=e(y/n).
Define
R_calI(y)=n^(-1)sum_{h in cal I}Fhat(h/n)e_n(hy)            (1)
for real y, and define the finite-band kernel
K_calI(u)=n^(-1)sum_{h in cal I}e_n(hu).                   (2)
Then exactly
R_calI(y)=integral_R F(t)K_calI(y-t)dt.                    (3)

If Fhat(h/n) is nonzero for at least one h in cal I, then R_calI is a nonzero real-analytic exponential polynomial. In particular, it cannot vanish on any nonempty open real interval. Therefore a nonzero finite-band projection of a compactly supported hard-source amplitude is not itself compactly supported and cannot inherit the original hard support as an exact pointwise zero-one selector in its physical variable.

Specialize to the natural forward C1 amplitude of fact 6eacfadbc9a83247 with n=vp and
F=F_{g,cq,vp}.                                              (4)
For a finite frequency interval cal I of length less than n, its normalized physical reconstruction is exactly (1), while its individual frequency coefficient is the factor
[H_P/n]Fhat_{g,cq,n}(h/n)                                  (5)
inside U_nat. The original hard amplitude (4) is supported only where the reduced source variables satisfy
m>0, k_red>0, qm+n k_red=A.                                (6)
But unless every coefficient in (5) vanishes on cal I, the finite-band reconstruction (1) cannot vanish on the complementary open physical region merely because (4) vanishes there. Hence the hard positivity exclusion in fact 6eacfadbc9a83247 is not transported into a proper finite-band PMD row by Fourier truncation alone.

This is an exact analytic obstruction to support preservation, not an obstruction to cancellation after restoring all bands or combining signed labels. It proves no lower bound for the finite-band row, no failure of a source-specific band-restoration theorem with correction terms, no Gadd^(-1) estimate, no PMD closure, and no Goldbach conclusion.
7596cf19a80bf8f3.proof:
Insert the definition of Fhat into (1). Because cal I is finite and F is compactly supported, interchange the finite sum and the integral:
R_calI(y)
=n^(-1)sum_{h in cal I} integral_R F(t)e(-ht/n)e(hy/n)dt
=integral_R F(t)[n^(-1)sum_{h in cal I}e(h(y-t)/n)]dt.
The bracket equals K_calI(y-t), proving (3).

Equation (1) is a finite linear combination of the real-analytic functions y maps to exp(2 pi i h y/n), hence is real analytic. Suppose it vanished on a nonempty open interval. A real-analytic finite exponential polynomial which vanishes on an open interval vanishes identically. To verify that its coefficients must then be zero, choose any h_0 in cal I and integrate the identically zero function R_calI(y)e_n(-h_0y) over y in [0,n]. Orthogonality gives
0=integral_0^n R_calI(y)e_n(-h_0y)dy=Fhat(h_0/n),
because the residues of the elements of cal I modulo n are distinct. Thus Fhat(h/n)=0 for every h in cal I. The contrapositive proves that if one coefficient is nonzero, R_calI is nonzero and cannot vanish on an open interval.

For the specialization, fact 6eacfadbc9a83247 identifies (5) as the exact natural unseparated finite-frequency factor and proves the hard support condition (6). A finite interval of length less than n has distinct residues modulo n, so the preceding argument applies. The complement of the compact positive hard support contains nonempty open real intervals. If the finite-band reconstruction vanished there solely by inheriting the hard support, it would vanish on such an interval and hence all its band coefficients would be zero. Therefore every nonzero proper band is physically nonlocal. This proves the stated scope and no more.

glossary.R_calI: The physical reconstruction obtained from only the frequencies in cal I.
glossary.cal I: A finite frequency set with distinct residues modulo n.

75d461ea0320c1a8.title: EXACT FREQUENCY-GCD DESCENT AND CUBIC CHARACTER SPECTRAL FORM OF THE FORWARD E11 CRITICAL TRACE. Assume the hypotheses and notation of fact fc442085ff47a053, and let one atom of T_E11^crit have variables d,r,h and canonical distinct primes p,ell with r=p ell. For all sufficiently large x put c_E=(d,h), q_E=d/c_E, and h_E=h/c_E. Then q_E>1, q_E is squarefree, and (c_E,q_E)=(h_E,q_E)=(p ell,q_E)=1. For a Dirichlet character chi modulo q_E define
75d461ea0320c1a8.author: slava chan
75d461ea0320c1a8.statement:
EXACT FREQUENCY-GCD DESCENT AND CUBIC CHARACTER SPECTRAL FORM OF THE FORWARD E11 CRITICAL TRACE. Assume the hypotheses and notation of fact fc442085ff47a053, and let one atom of T_E11^crit have variables d,r,h and canonical distinct primes p,ell with r=p ell. For all sufficiently large x put c_E=(d,h), q_E=d/c_E, and h_E=h/c_E. Then q_E>1, q_E is squarefree, and (c_E,q_E)=(h_E,q_E)=(p ell,q_E)=1. For a Dirichlet character chi modulo q_E define
G_{N,q_E}(chi)=sum_{u (mod q_E),(u,q_E)=1} e_{q_E}(-Nu) conjugate(chi(u)).
Then the exact atomwise identity
 e_r(Nh d^(-1))
 = e(Nh/(dr)) phi(q_E)^(-1) sum_{chi (mod q_E)} G_{N,q_E}(chi) chi(h_E) conjugate(chi(p)) conjugate(chi(ell))
holds, where d^(-1) is taken modulo r. Moreover
 sum_{chi (mod q_E)} |G_{N,q_E}(chi)|^2=phi(q_E)^2,
and the principal-character coefficient is the Ramanujan sum c_{q_E}(N). Replacing every phase in T_E11^crit by this identity gives an exact cubic-character spectral reconstruction of the complete literal trace. It deletes no frequency-gcd or target-gcd layer and preserves every fixed-U, high-label, dyadic, smooth, logarithmic, parent, least-tag, normalized-marker and conjugate-frequency coefficient. No cancellation estimate for the reconstructed trace, no E21/E22 assertion and no Goldbach implication is claimed.
75d461ea0320c1a8.proof:
Fact fc442085ff47a053 gives, on every atom of T_E11^crit,
 (d,r)=1,  r=p ell with p and ell distinct primes,  (Nh,r)=1,
 0<|h|<Y_E,
and beta_E<=4/3+6 eta_t. Its definitions give a_E=1/3-15 eta_t and
 Y_E=(1/2)(R/D)D^{a_E}=(1/2)D^{beta_E-2/3-15 eta_t}
 <=(1/2)D^{2/3-9 eta_t}.
The literal dyadic support has d>=D/2. Hence Y_E<d for all sufficiently large D; bounded D is absent for sufficiently large x in this source. Thus 0<|h|<d.

Because the atom has nonzero mu(d), d is squarefree. Put c_E=(d,h), d=c_E q_E and h=c_E h_E. Since 0<|h|<d, q_E>1. Squarefreeness of d yields (c_E,q_E)=1 and makes q_E squarefree. The definition of the gcd gives (h_E,q_E)=1. Since (d,r)=1 and r=p ell, also (p ell,q_E)=1.

We first use additive reciprocity. Choose inverses d_bar modulo r and r_bar modulo d. The integer d d_bar+r r_bar is congruent to one modulo both coprime integers d and r, so
 d d_bar+r r_bar congruent to 1 (mod dr).
After division by dr and exponentiation,
 e_r(Nh d_bar)=e(Nh/(dr))e_d(-Nh r_bar).                 (1)
Since d=c_Eq_E and h=c_Eh_E, reduction of r_bar modulo q_E is an inverse of r modulo q_E and
 e_d(-Nh r_bar)=e_{q_E}(-Nh_E r^(-1)).                    (2)
No coprimality between N and q_E is needed in (2).

Let U=(Z/q_E Z)^*. For chi in the character group of U define G_{N,q_E}(chi) as in the statement. Fourier inversion on the finite abelian group U says, for every t in U,
 e_{q_E}(-Nt)=phi(q_E)^(-1)sum_chi G_{N,q_E}(chi)chi(t). (3)
Take t=h_Er^(-1). The established coprimalities put t in U, and multiplicativity gives
 chi(t)=chi(h_E)conjugate(chi(r))
       =chi(h_E)conjugate(chi(p))conjugate(chi(ell)).      (4)
Combining (1)--(4) proves the displayed atomwise spectral identity.

Parseval on U gives
 sum_chi|G_{N,q_E}(chi)|^2
 =phi(q_E)sum_{u in U}|e_{q_E}(-Nu)|^2
 =phi(q_E)^2.                                             (5)
For the principal character, the defining sum is sum_{u in U}e_{q_E}(-Nu)=c_{q_E}(-N)=c_{q_E}(N), because Ramanujan sums are real and even.

The replacement is an equality for each original atom. It changes none of that atom's coefficient or membership masks and only rewrites its additive phase. Summing the identities therefore reconstructs the entire T_E11^crit with every literal coefficient listed in the statement. The final scope restrictions follow because no estimate or other parent decomposition has been used.

glossary.G_{N,q_E}(chi): The multiplicative Fourier coefficient of the additive unit-group function u mapsto e_{q_E}(-Nu).
glossary.c_E: The exact frequency gcd gcd(d,h) in a forward E11 critical atom.

76040270e1ddf949.title: BUFFER-EXTENDED COMPLETE-FREQUENCY ONE-ROUGH-PRIME C1 TRACE
76040270e1ddf949.author: slava chan
76040270e1ddf949.statement:
BUFFER-EXTENDED COMPLETE-FREQUENCY ONE-ROUGH-PRIME C1 TRACE.

Fix integers J,C_A>=1, a constant C>=1, and 0<kappa<=1/100. Put sigma=kappa/100 and beta_1=6/5-3sigma. Let Q be sufficiently large, let 1<=beta<=beta_1, and put
B=Q^beta, H_T=B/Q, L=H_T Q^sigma, S_0=H_T^2 Q^(3sigma), Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma).
Let V,P>=1 be dyadic scales. Let xi_v be supported on squarefree integers v with V<=v<2V, v<=S_0, and every prime divisor of v at most L, with |xi_v|<=tau_J(v). Let p denote a prime with P<=p<2P, p>=Z, and assume the amplitude is supported where C^(-1)B<=vp<=CB. Thus p is the unique Z-rough prime in the C1 factorization and, for sufficiently large Q, p is larger than every prime divisor of v.

Let A be a fixed nonzero integer with |A|<=Q^(C_A), and let |c_q|<=1 for Q<=q<2Q. Let G>0 and put H_P=H_T/G. For every dyadic integer frequency scale F>=1, let nu_F(h) be supported on F<=|h|<2F with |nu_F(h)|<=tau_J(|h|), let omega_F be a scalar such that for every fixed integer J_0>=1,
|omega_F|<=C(J_0) min(1,(F/H_P)^(-J_0)),
and let Psi_F be a fixed-complexity uniformly scaled-smooth projective amplitude in q/Q, |h|/F, v/V, p/P, with projective norm bounded uniformly in F and all displayed parameters. Define
T_C1=H_P^(-1) sum_F omega_F sum_{Q<=q<2Q} c_q
 sum_{F<=|h|<2F} nu_F(h)
 sum_{v,p; p prime; gcd(vp,q)=1}
 xi_v Psi_F(q/Q,|h|/F,v/V,p/P)
 e_q(Ah(vp)^(-1)),
where both signs of h and all nonempty dyadic V,P,F blocks are included.

(i) If G>=1, then T_C1=O(G Q^(2-delta_1)) for some fixed delta_1>0.

(ii) Fix 0<eta<sigma. If Q^(-sigma+eta)<=G<=Q^(sigma-eta), then T_C1=O(Q^(2-delta_2)) for some fixed delta_2>0.

The estimates are uniform in the displayed coefficients, in a possibly nonunit fixed target A, in H_P below or above one, in proper-prime-power subtraction, and under polylogarithmically many inherited source, fixed-U, high, parent, sign, prime-order, collision, provenance, Vaughan, dyadic, and smooth labels that act as label scalars or are absorbable into the displayed one-variable coefficients or uniformly bounded projective amplitude. No modulus-dependent unit multiplier is permitted in the short Type-I branch; the literal C1 reciprocity chart has multiplier one there. No arbitrary joint deletion mask is allowed. The theorem estimates only the complete C1 anatomy and asserts no C2, C3, later-beta, endpoint, actual-Z deletion, PMD, logical bad-N, or Goldbach conclusion.
76040270e1ddf949.proof:
Write nu=log V/log Q, with dyadic endpoint constants absorbed as O(1/log Q). Since v<=S_0,
0<=nu<=2beta-2+3sigma+O(1/log Q).                                      (1)
The support vp comparable to B gives P=Q^(beta-nu+O(1/log Q)). In particular
P>=Q^(2-beta-3sigma+O(1/log Q))=Q^(1/2+O(1/log Q))Z.
Thus for sufficiently large Q every supported p exceeds Z and every prime divisor of v, so gcd(v,p)=1 and the ordering and unique-rough-prime assertions are exact. Taking xi_v=-mu(v) recovers the literal C1 coefficient from fact 6414b11506a84ff0.

We replace the prime indicator on the dyadic p-range by
1_{n prime}=Lambda(n)/log n-1_{n=rho^j, rho prime, j>=2}/j.            (2)
The letter rho in (2) is only the prime base of a proper prime power. Factors 1/log n, product cutoffs, and every displayed scaled-smooth amplitude have uniformly summable Fourier expansions in logarithmic coordinates. After n=lm, a mode in log n separates as a product of modes in log l and log m. The projective costs are Q^epsilon after truncation, and the discarded Fourier tails are smaller than any fixed power.

First bound the proper-prime-power term. There are O(P^(1/2)log(2P)) proper prime powers in the p-range. On the F block put u_F=F/H_P. Absolute summation, including the literal H_P^(-1) prefactor, gives
O(Q^epsilon |omega_F| u_F Q V P^(1/2))
=O(Q^epsilon |omega_F| u_F Q(VB)^(1/2)).                           (3)
By V<=S_0 and beta<=beta_1,
Q(VB)^(1/2)<=Q^(3beta/2+3sigma/2)
<=Q^(9/5-3sigma).                                                   (4)
The dyadic sum of |omega_F|u_F is bounded: for u_F<=1 it is a geometric sum, and for u_F>1 use the hypothesis with J_0>=3. Hence all proper prime powers contribute O(Q^(9/5-2sigma)) after choosing epsilon small.

Apply the exact Vaughan identity and box theorem of fact 29c43cef40f2e79b to Lambda(n) at scale P with cutoff P^(1/3). The Type-II smaller-factor exponent lambda satisfies
(beta-nu)/3+O(1/log Q)<=lambda<=(beta-nu)/2+O(1/log Q),               (5)
and a Type-I coefficient-bearing factor has
0<=lambda<=(beta-nu)/3+O(1/log Q).                                  (6)
All resulting coefficients are bounded by a fixed divisor function times a logarithm.

We now prove the slot extension directly; we do not invoke the beta<=6/5-2kappa conclusion of fact 2ff1c15aef183bac. The key inequality at the new endpoint is
6-5beta>=15sigma.                                                     (7)

For a Type-II box put w=nu+lambda. From (1) and (5),
w>=beta/3+O(1/log Q), and
beta/3-(2beta-2+4sigma)=(6-5beta)/3-4sigma>=sigma.                   (8)
If w<=3-2beta-4sigma, choose the grouped factor vl. Otherwise choose the complementary Vaughan factor. In the latter case,
beta-w>=1-beta/2-3sigma/2+O(1/log Q),                                (9)
whose difference from 2beta-2+4sigma is
(6-5beta-11sigma)/2>=2sigma,                                        (10)
while
(3-2beta-4sigma)-(3beta-3+4sigma)=6-5beta-8sigma>=7sigma.           (11)
After absorbing dyadic endpoint errors, the selected factor scale S therefore satisfies
H_T^2 Q^(3sigma)<=S<=Q^(1-3sigma)/H_T^2.                            (12)
Let T be the complementary grouped scale. Then ST is comparable to B=QH_T.

For Type I put w_0=nu+lambda. Equations (1) and (6) give
w_0<=(5beta-4)/3+2sigma+O(1/log Q).                                  (13)
Use three disjoint branches. If w_0<=1/2-4sigma, then after dyadic endpoint absorption the grouped coefficient-bearing factor vl has scale at most Q^(1/2-3sigma). If
1/2-4sigma<w_0<=3-2beta-4sigma,
select vl. Its lower margin over 2beta-2+3sigma is positive because
5/2-2beta-7sigma>=1/10-sigma>0.                                     (14)
If w_0>3-2beta-4sigma, select the complementary unweighted factor. By (13), its lower margin over 2beta-2+3sigma is at least
(10-8beta)/3-5sigma>=2/15+3sigma,                                   (15)
and its upper margin follows from (11). Thus the latter two Type-I branches also satisfy (12).

We estimate every correlated Type-II and latter Type-I box on each actual integer-frequency block. Apply fact 42720f6d803c4640 with its frequency parameter equal to F, its total-product parameter equal to H_T, and its imbalance equal to
G_F=H_T/F=G/u_F.
Because ST is comparable to QH_T, and because the literal prefactor is H_P^(-1)=u_F F^(-1), that fact gives, apart from Q^epsilon,
G^(1/4)u_F^(3/4)Q^2H_T^(1/2)S^(-1/4)
+G^(1/4)u_F^(3/4)Q^(7/4)H_T^(1/2)S^(1/4)
+u_F Q^2H_TS^(-1/2)
+u_F Q^(7/4)H_T.                                                     (16)
Fact 42720f6d803c4640 permits the fixed nonunit A and unrestricted gcd(h,q). It also permits a q-dependent unit in these correlated pieces, although none is needed for the literal C1 trace.

From (12), the four expressions in (16), without their G and u_F factors, are at most respectively
Q^(2-3sigma/4), Q^(2-3sigma/4), Q^(2-3sigma/2), Q^(2-3sigma/2).      (17)
For the last bound, nonemptiness of (12) implies H_T<=Q^(1/4-3sigma/2). Summing over F is harmless because
sum_F |omega_F|u_F^(3/4)+sum_F |omega_F|u_F=O(1).                   (18)
If G>=1, (16)-(18) are O(GQ^(2-delta)) because G^(1/4)<=G. If
Q^(-sigma+eta)<=G<=Q^(sigma-eta), the first two terms are at most
Q^(2-sigma/2-eta/4+epsilon), and the last two are at most Q^(2-3sigma/2+epsilon). This proves the required bounds for every correlated box.

It remains to treat the short Type-I branch. Let L_I be its grouped coefficient-bearing scale and M_I the unweighted complementary scale. Then
L_I<=Q^(1/2-3sigma), L_IM_I is comparable to B<=Q^beta_1.            (19)
For frequency blocks F<=Q^(C_A+3), apply fact bbcb9f66597c667c with its parameter tau=2sigma, fixed target A, frequency length F, and coefficient-bearing scale L_I. Its precise estimate, multiplied by u_F because the literal prefactor is H_P^(-1) rather than F^(-1), is
O(Q^epsilon |omega_F|u_F [B+Q^(3/2)L_I])
=O(Q^epsilon |omega_F|u_F [Q^(6/5)+Q^(2-3sigma)]).                  (20)
There is no modulus-dependent unit multiplier in this application. This is exactly the multiplier-one phase produced by the literal C1 reciprocity chart. Sum (20) using (18).

For F>Q^(C_A+3), use absolute summation, which is
O(Q^epsilon |omega_F|u_F QB).                                      (21)
In both claimed G-ranges one has H_P<=Q^(1/4) for sufficiently large Q: for G>=1 this follows from H_P<=H_T, and on the near-balanced strip it follows from H_P<=H_TQ^(sigma-eta) and beta<=beta_1. Hence F>Q^(C_A+3) implies u_F>Q^(C_A+11/4). Choosing J_0 in the Fourier-decay hypothesis sufficiently large makes the sum of (21) smaller than Q^(-10). Thus every short Type-I block is O(Q^(2-2sigma)) after shrinking epsilon.

All Vaughan dyadic boxes, signs, smooth-separation modes, prime-order and provenance labels are polylogarithmically numerous. The conditions gcd(vp,q)=1 and gcd(v,p)=1 are retained exactly; Vaughan factorization does not require a new joint-coprimality estimate because the correlated consumer only assumes coprimality of the complete grouped product with q, and the Type-I consumer has the same complete-product condition. Combining (3)-(21) and shrinking the fixed savings proves (i) and (ii). No arbitrary joint deletion has been inserted.

glossary.G_F: The blockwise imbalance H_T/F used when applying the natural-frequency correlated ledger.
glossary.L_I: The grouped coefficient-bearing scale in the short Vaughan Type-I branch.
glossary.M_I: The complementary unweighted scale in the short Vaughan Type-I branch.
glossary.T_C1: The complete dyadic-frequency one-rough-prime reciprocal trace in this fact.
glossary.u_F: The ratio F/H_P between an actual dyadic integer-frequency block and the natural physical Poisson frequency.

76092d9557115380.title: TWO-GIANT EMPTINESS IN THE HC-MED CHAMBER ABOVE THE LINE eta=6delta_h. Adopt X,delta_h,eta,C,U_P,H and the GIANT2D and GIANT2S branches of fact 52e1736c39e88aee. Assume
76092d9557115380.author: slava chan
76092d9557115380.statement:
TWO-GIANT EMPTINESS IN THE HC-MED CHAMBER ABOVE THE LINE eta=6delta_h. Adopt X,delta_h,eta,C,U_P,H and the GIANT2D and GIANT2S branches of fact 52e1736c39e88aee. Assume
X^(eta-6delta_h)>2(log X)^(2C).                                 (1)
Then GIANT2D and GIANT2S are empty. In particular, for every fixed xi>0, both branches are empty for all sufficiently large X whenever
eta>=6delta_h+xi.                                                (2)
No assertion is made on the boundary eta-6delta_h tending to zero, or on SMOOTH, GIANT1, MS-FIRST-NOSCALE, or another HC sector.
76092d9557115380.proof:
Fact 52e1736c39e88aee defines
U_P=X^(1/2-3delta_h)(log X)^(-C)
and proves
H>U_P.                                                           (3)
Every m in GIANT2D is divisible by two distinct primes at least H. Every m in GIANT2S is divisible by the square of a prime at least H. Thus in either branch
m>=H^2>U_P^2
 =X^(1-6delta_h)(log X)^(-2C).                                  (4)
The HC-MED support in the same fact has
d>=X^eta,qquad dm<2X.                                          (5)
Equations (4)-(5) give
dm>X^(1+eta-6delta_h)(log X)^(-2C).                              (6)
Under (1), the right side of (6) exceeds 2X, contradicting (5). Hence both branches are empty.

If (2) holds, then
X^(eta-6delta_h)>=X^xi>2(log X)^(2C)
for sufficiently large X. Therefore (1) follows and the first conclusion applies. The final exclusions are branches for which the two-large-prime lower bound (4) is unavailable.

761a75d801b6688c.title: EXACT FOUR-ROW TRANSLATION/FOURIER IDENTITY, JOINT POLE-FREQUENCY EXCEPTION, AND THE L2-ONLY NO-FIT
761a75d801b6688c.author: slava chan
761a75d801b6688c.statement:
EXACT FOUR-ROW TRANSLATION/FOURIER IDENTITY, JOINT POLE-FREQUENCY EXCEPTION, AND THE L2-ONLY NO-FIT.

Let p>=7 be prime. For i=1,2,3,4 let c_i be in F_p and define
\[
 k_i(q)={\bf1}_{q\ne0}e_p(c_iq^{-1}),\qquad q\in F_p.            \tag{1}
\]
Let a_i:F_p->C be arbitrary row profiles and let M:F_p^4->C be an arbitrary tuple profile. Put
\[
 S=\sum_{q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4\in F_p}
 M(q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4)\prod_{i=1}^4a_i(q_i)k_i(q_i).               \tag{2}
\]
Then the translation lift is the exact identity
\[
 \boxed{S={1\over p}\sum_{X\in F_p}
 \sum_{r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4\in F_p}
 M(X+r_1,\ldots,X+r_4)
 \prod_{i=1}^4a_i(X+r_i)k_i(X+r_i).}                            \tag{3}
\]
Thus an arbitrary literal zero-one deletion/provenance mask may be retained as M.

Fix the shift tuple r=(r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4). Define
\[
 m_r(X)=M(X+r_1,\ldots,X+r_4),                                  \tag{4}
\]
\[
 R_r(X)=\sum_{i=1}^4{c_i\over X+r_i},\qquad
 K_r(X)=\prod_{i=1}^4k_i(X+r_i).                                \tag{5}
\]
For f:F_p->C use the unitary Fourier transform
\[
 \widetilde f(\xi)=p^{-1/2}\sum_{X\in F_p}f(X)e_p(-\xi X).       \tag{6}
\]
Then
\[
 I_r:={1\over p}\sum_Xm_r(X)\prod_{i=1}^4a_i(X+r_i)K_r(X)
\]
has the exact expansion
\[
 \boxed{
 I_r=p^{-3}\sum_{\mu,\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_4\in F_p}
 \widetilde m_r(\mu)\prod_{i=1}^4\widetilde a_i(\xi_i)
 e_p\!\left(\sum_i\xi_ir_i\right)
 \widetilde K_r\!\left(-\mu-\sum_i\xi_i\right).}                \tag{7}
\]

For each pole value b in F_p put
\[
 C_b=\sum_{i:r_i=b}c_i.                                         \tag{8}
\]
The rational function R_r is constant if and only if
\[
 C_b=0\quad\hbox{for every represented pole }b,                 \tag{9}
\]
and then R_r=0. Uniformly in every eta in F_p,
\[
 R_r\ne0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 |\widetilde K_r(\eta)|\le10,                                   \tag{10}
\]
whereas if R_r=0 then
\[
 \widetilde K_r(0)={\#\{X:X+r_i\ne0\ \forall i\}\over\sqrt p},
 \qquad
 |\widetilde K_r(\eta)|\le{4\over\sqrt p}\quad(\eta\ne0).        \tag{11}
\]
Consequently the only square-root-size kernel coefficient in (7) occurs when both
\[
 C_b=0\ \hbox{for every b},\qquad
 \mu+\xi_1+\xi_2+\xi_3+\xi_4=0.                                \tag{12}
\]
Thus Fourier expansion adds an exact total-linear-frequency constraint to the repeated-pole balance; when the tuple mask varies with X, its diagonal frequency mu must be included.

Equations (3), (7), and (10) do not give a nonexceptional saving from unitary l2/Hilbert normalization alone. Indeed, choose any c_i and r_i for which R_r is nonconstant, take M=1, and set
\[
 a_i(q)={\bf1}_{q\ne0}e_p(-c_iq^{-1}).                          \tag{13}
\]
Then every normalized row l2 norm
\[
 \left(p^{-1}\sum_q|a_i(q)|^2\right)^{1/2}
\]
is at most one, but
\[
 I_r={\#\{X:X+r_i\ne0\ \forall i\}\over p}
 \ge1-{4\over p}.                                               \tag{14}
\]
Hence no estimate uniform over bounded row profiles can insert a factor p^{-delta}, delta>0, on the right of the normalized l2 product merely from nonconstancy of R_r and the translation/Fourier lift.

For the Top-B translation proposal, the literal choice is
\(c_i=\sigma_i\mathscr A h_iT_i^{-1}\), with signs (+,+,-,-), while M retains selected-largest-prime, pair deletion and provenance. The accepted source facts presently give only divisor bounds and bounded smooth projective factors, not the nonzero-frequency sparsity, decay, low Fourier projective cost or source-linked cancellation needed to defeat (14). Thus TRANSLATION-LIFT-JCOMP is not implied by translation unitarity and l2 normalization alone. A successful theorem must use additional literal q-profile structure. This is a coefficient-class no-fit, not a literal Top-B counterexample, and it proves no TOP-B-BALG-DEEP-NR-SPEC, POST-A-TAIL, or Goldbach conclusion.
761a75d801b6688c.proof:
For every fixed physical tuple q=(q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4) and every X in F_p there is exactly one shift tuple r with r_i=q_i-X. Thus the right side of (3) counts every summand of (2) exactly p times and divides by p. This proves (3), including arbitrary M.

Fourier inversion for (6) is
\[
 f(X)=p^{-1/2}\sum_{\xi\in F_p}\widetilde f(\xi)e_p(\xi X).
\]
Apply it to m_r(X) and each of the four functions a_i(X+r_i). Their product contributes the scalar p^{-5/2}, the phase
\[
 e_p\!\left(X(\mu+\xi_1+\cdots+\xi_4)+\sum_i\xi_ir_i\right),
\]
and the product of the five Fourier coefficients. By definition,
\[
 \sum_XK_r(X)e_p(X\nu)=\sqrt p\,\widetilde K_r(-\nu).
\]
Multiplying by the outside p^{-1} gives p^{-3}, proving (7).

Group equal denominators in (5):
\[
 R_r(X)=\sum_b{C_b\over X+b}.
\]
This rational function tends to zero at infinity. Distinct simple-pole functions are linearly independent: multiplying a linear relation by the product of its distinct denominators and evaluating at X=-b shows C_b=0. Therefore R_r is constant exactly under (9), and the constant is zero.

Assume R_r is nonzero. It has at least one finite pole of order one. For eta=0, reduce R_r=f/g to lowest terms. The denominator has degree at most four and at most four distinct roots, while deg f<=deg g. It is not H^p-H over the algebraic closure because a pole of any nonconstant H^p-H has order divisible by p, whereas R_r has a simple pole. Makhul and Winterhof, arXiv:2106.12218, Lemma 2, gives
\[
 \left|\sum_{g(X)\ne0}e_p(f(X)/g(X))\right|
 \le(\deg g+s-2)\sqrt p+1\le6\sqrt p+1.
\]
The domain of K_r may additionally delete at most four regular points arising from zero C_b or repeated shifts, so its unnormalized sum is at most \(6\sqrt p+5\le8\sqrt p\).

For eta nonzero, reduce \(R_r(X)-\eta X=f_\eta/g_\eta\). Its numerator degree is one larger than its denominator degree, at most five, and its denominator has at most four distinct roots. It is not H^p-H because the linear term gives a simple pole at infinity; any surviving finite pole is also simple. Amadio Guidi, Lindqvist and Micheli, arXiv:1712.05258, Theorem 6.3, gives
\[
 \left|\sum_{g_\eta(X)\ne0}e_p(f_\eta(X)/g_\eta(X))\right|
 \le(\deg f_\eta+v-1)\sqrt p\le8\sqrt p.
\]
Deleting at most four additional regular points gives \(8\sqrt p+4\le10\sqrt p\). Division by \(\sqrt p\) proves (10).

If R_r=0, K_r is the indicator of the common nonpole domain. At eta=0 its unitary transform is the first expression in (11). At eta nonzero, the complete linear-character sum on F_p is zero, so the sum over the common domain is the negative of the sum over at most four excluded points. This proves the second bound in (11). Substitution into (7) proves (12).

For (13), on every X in the common nonpole domain,
\[
 \prod_i a_i(X+r_i)K_r(X)
 =e_p(-R_r(X))e_p(R_r(X))=1.
\]
The mask is one. Hence (14) follows, and the normalized row l2 bounds are immediate. This proves the l2-only no-fit. The Top-B specialization and scope statements compare the displayed exact slots with facts b69e09aaac3766d9, 97b9d86408362df2, c641ed6b2cda758b, and 93d8472aee4d44da; none supplies additional literal nonzero-mode control.

glossary.TRANSLATION-LIFT-JCOMP: A source-specific common-X joint-completion theorem that controls the X-dependent literal q profiles without an l1-frequency or l2-trivial tax.
glossary.\\widetilde f: The unitary additive Fourier transform p^(-1/2) sum_X f(X)e_p(-xi X).
glossary.m_r: The diagonal tuple-mask profile X -> M(X+r_1,...,X+r_4) at fixed shifts.

764588e99974a6d9.title: GA-qPRINC: PRINCIPAL RAMANUJAN PAYMENT FOR THE PHYSICAL RAY CONDUCTOR AND THE EXACT CENTERED RESIDUAL
764588e99974a6d9.author: slava chan
764588e99974a6d9.statement:
GA-qPRINC: PRINCIPAL RAMANUJAN PAYMENT FOR THE PHYSICAL RAY CONDUCTOR AND THE EXACT CENTERED RESIDUAL.

Adopt one fixed exact good-\(\mathscr W\) orientation, anatomy, frozen source/projective fibre, frequency block and dilator block
\[
1\le F\le x^3,\qquad F\le |h|<2F,\qquad
\mathcal D\le d_\lambda<2\mathcal D
\]
from facts e55b27d39c593164 and cff9d29efb555b8e. Put
\[
L=(\log(2x))^C
\]
for a fixed real \(C>0\), and retain the exact hard ray-pair conditions
\[
R\ne R',\qquad aa'>{Q^2\over\mathcal D},\qquad
m_d>L,\qquad d_\lambda\nmid\mathscr A\Delta_0.
\tag{1}
\]
Use the notation
\[
m=m_q={aa'\over(aa',\mathscr A\Delta_0)},\qquad
c=C_q={\mathscr A\Delta_0\over(aa',\mathscr A\Delta_0)},\qquad
n=d_\lambda v_\lambda
\tag{2}
\]
of fact cff9d29efb555b8e.

For \(m>1\), let \(\chi_0\) denote the principal Dirichlet character modulo \(m\), put
\[
G_{m,c}(\chi)=
\sum_{\substack{z\ ({\rm mod}\ m)\\(z,m)=1}}
e_m(-cz)\chi(z),
\tag{3}
\]
and define, for \((u,m)=1\),
\[
K^\circ_{m,c}(u)=
{1\over\phi(m)}
\sum_{\substack{\chi\ ({\rm mod}\ m)\\\chi\ne\chi_0}}
G_{m,c}(\chi)\chi(u).
\tag{4}
\]
For \(m=1\), define \(K^\circ_{1,c}(u)=0\). Then every supported pair has \(m\) squarefree, \((c,m)=(n,m)=1\), and
\[
\boxed{\quad
e_m(-c n^{-1})={\mu(m)\over\phi(m)}+K^\circ_{m,c}(n).
\quad}
\tag{5}
\]
Moreover \(K^\circ_{m,c}\) has mean zero on the unit residue classes modulo \(m\).

Let \(\Theta_\lambda(R,R')\in\{0,1\}\) be any existing literal selector on the exact hard ray-pair sum, including any restriction in (1) and any further inherited pair-dependent deletion. Define its principal component by
\[
\mathfrak H_{\Theta}^{\rm prin}
=
\sum_\lambda\sum_{R\ne R'}
\Theta_\lambda(R,R')
B_\lambda(R)\overline{B_\lambda(R')}
{\mu(m_q)\over\phi(m_q)},
\tag{6}
\]
where \(B_\lambda(R)\) is the complete literal pre-reciprocity ray coefficient of fact 7e9251670db3e1c9. Then
\[
\boxed{\quad
|\mathfrak H_{\Theta}^{\rm prin}|
\le
x^{o(1)}|\omega_F|^2 B F^2.
\quad}
\tag{GA-qPRINC}
\]
This bound retains the exact copy inventory and every marker, Möbius, Fourier, target-gcd, fixed-\(U\), high, source, parent, ordering, equality, collision, deletion, provenance, coprimality and projective mask; in the absolute proof these selectors only delete terms. It remains valid after a union of \(x^{o(1)}\) exact frozen-label families.

There is the following exact consumer. Suppose
\[
\mathcal D\le Q^2,\qquad Y={Q^2\over\mathcal D}\ge1.
\tag{7}
\]
Fact 3089501f7fb49c18 pays the hard subfamily \(m_q\le Y\). On the complementary hard subfamily \(m_q>Y\), equation (5) splits the form into (6) and
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\mathfrak H_C^{q\text{-}{\rm cent}}
=
\sum_\lambda
\sum_{\substack{R\ne R'\\
aa'>Q^2/\mathcal D,\ m_d>L,\ m_q>Q^2/\mathcal D\\
d_\lambda\nmid\mathscr A\Delta_0}}
&B_\lambda(R)\overline{B_\lambda(R')}\\
&\times
K^\circ_{m_q,C_q}(d_\lambda v_\lambda).
\end{aligned}
}
\tag{GA-qCENT}
\]
Every literal joint coefficient and selector is retained in this formula. Since \(Y\ge1\), GA-qPRINC gives
\[
|\mathfrak H_{\Theta}^{\rm prin}|
\le
x^{o(1)}|\omega_F|^2{BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}.
\tag{8}
\]
Consequently, for \(\mathcal D\le Q^2\), after the already accepted low-product, low-\(d\)-conductor and low-\(q\)-conductor payments, the sole remaining estimate on this exact hard block is
\[
|\mathfrak H_C^{q\text{-}{\rm cent}}|
\le
x^{o(1)}|\omega_F|^2{BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}.
\tag{9}
\]
Estimate (9) is an unproved supplier, not a conclusion.

When \(\mathcal D>Q^2\), GA-qPRINC remains true, but its right side need not be at most the target containing \(Q^2/\mathcal D<1\); no consumer is asserted in that range. In particular, no coherent \(m_q=1\) payment, no estimate for GA-qCENT, no GA-RAY-SPEC or GA-NR-DIL estimate, no tail payment and no Goldbach conclusion are asserted.
764588e99974a6d9.proof:
Fact cff9d29efb555b8e proves directly that
\[
(c,m)=1,\qquad (n,m)=1.
\tag{10}
\]
We verify squarefreeness. Fact 3089501f7fb49c18 writes
\[
a=g\alpha,\qquad a'=g\beta,
\]
where \(g,\alpha,\beta\) are pairwise coprime and squarefree, and proves
\[
m_q=
{g\over(g,\mathscr A L_0)}
{\alpha\beta\over(\alpha\beta,\mathscr A)}.
\tag{11}
\]
Each quotient in (11) is squarefree, and the two quotients are coprime because \(g\) is coprime to \(\alpha\beta\). Hence \(m=m_q\) is squarefree.

Assume first \(m>1\). On the finite abelian group of units modulo \(m\), apply character inversion to
\[
f(u)=e_m(-cu^{-1}).
\]
Its coefficient at a character \(\chi\) is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat f(\chi)
&=\sum_{\substack{u\ ({\rm mod}\ m)\\(u,m)=1}}
e_m(-cu^{-1})\overline{\chi(u)}\\
&=\sum_{\substack{z\ ({\rm mod}\ m)\\(z,m)=1}}
e_m(-cz)\chi(z)
=G_{m,c}(\chi),
\end{aligned}
\tag{12}
\]
where \(z=u^{-1}\) and
\(\overline{\chi(z^{-1})}=\chi(z)\). Therefore
\[
e_m(-cu^{-1})
={1\over\phi(m)}
\sum_{\chi\ ({\rm mod}\ m)}
G_{m,c}(\chi)\chi(u).
\tag{13}
\]
For the principal character,
\[
G_{m,c}(\chi_0)
=\sum_{\substack{z\ ({\rm mod}\ m)\\(z,m)=1}}e_m(-cz)
=c_m(-c),
\tag{14}
\]
the Ramanujan sum. Because \((c,m)=1\) and \(m\) is squarefree, a primewise Chinese-remainder calculation gives
\[
c_m(-c)=\prod_{p\mid m}
\sum_{z\in(\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)^\times}e_p(-c z(m/p)^{-1})
=\prod_{p\mid m}(-1)=\mu(m).
\tag{15}
\]
Equations (13)--(15) prove (5) for \(m>1\). For \(m=1\), both the additive phase and \(\mu(1)/\phi(1)\) equal one, so the definition \(K^\circ_{1,c}=0\) proves (5). Summing (4) over all unit \(u\) gives zero by orthogonality of every nonprincipal character. Thus the residual is centered.

We next prove the absolute principal bound. Expand both complete ray coefficients using fact 7e9251670db3e1c9:
\[
B_\lambda(R)=
\sum_{k\in\mathscr I_\lambda(R)}
c_\lambda(ka,\epsilon kb).
\tag{16}
\]
The unit reciprocity factors distinguishing pre- and post-reciprocity coefficients do not change their magnitudes. After extracting the fixed projective frequency scalar, fact e55b27d39c593164 gives
\[
|c_\lambda(q,h)|\le x^{o(1)}|\omega_F|
\tag{17}
\]
and gives a total of
\[
Bx^{o(1)}
\tag{18}
\]
exact marked copies over \(n\asymp B\), including the divisor-bounded marker/copy multiplicity.

It remains to sum the reciprocal conductor over the scaling coordinates in (16). Let
\[
N_0(Y)=
\#\{(q_1,h_1,q_2,h_2):
m_q\le Y\}
\tag{19}
\]
on the complete coordinate universe of the fixed fibre and blocks, before any literal selector deletes coordinates. The counting proof of fact 3089501f7fb49c18 proves uniformly for \(1\le Y\le x^{O(1)}\) that
\[
N_0(Y)\le x^{o(1)}YF^2.
\tag{20}
\]
Every primitive denominator satisfies \(a,a'<2Q\), so
\[
m_q\le aa'<4Q^2\le x^{O(1)}.
\tag{21}
\]
Let \(M\) be a polynomial upper bound in (21). Abel summation for the step function \(N_0(t)\) gives
\[
\sum_{\rm coordinates}{1\over m_q}
=
{N_0(M)\over M}
+\int_{1^-}^{M}{N_0(t)\over t^2}\,dt
\le x^{o(1)}F^2(1+\log M)
=x^{o(1)}F^2.
\tag{22}
\]
Equivalently, one may partition \(m_q\) into dyadic intervals; each interval costs \(x^{o(1)}F^2\), and there are \(O(\log x)\) intervals.

Since \(m_q\) is squarefree,
\[
{m_q\over\phi(m_q)}
=\prod_{p\mid m_q}{p\over p-1}
\le 2^{\omega(m_q)}
=\tau(m_q)
\le x^{o(1)}.
\tag{23}
\]
Consequently (22) implies
\[
\sum_{\rm coordinates}{1\over\phi(m_q)}
\le x^{o(1)}F^2.
\tag{24}
\]
Take absolute values in (6), expand by (16), and use
\(|\mu(m_q)|\le1\). Every exact selector, including the pair-dependent nonresonance deletion, can only remove terms from this absolute sum. Multiplying (24) by the coefficient-product envelope from (17) and by the complete copy count (18) yields
\[
|\mathfrak H_{\Theta}^{\rm prin}|
\le x^{o(1)}|\omega_F|^2BF^2.
\]
This proves GA-qPRINC with the full literal multiplicity. A union of \(x^{o(1)}\) exact frozen-label families is absorbed into the same notation.

Finally assume (7). Fact 3089501f7fb49c18 gives the target bound for \(m_q\le Y\). On \(m_q>Y\), substitute the exact identity (5) into the physical phase in the hard form of fact cff9d29efb555b8e. The principal term is exactly (6), and the other term is exactly GA-qCENT. Since \(Y=Q^2/\mathcal D\ge1\), the principal bound is at most (8). This proves the exact reduction to the unproved supplier (9). If \(\mathcal D>Q^2\), the same comparison fails because \(Q^2/\mathcal D<1\), so the stated limitation is necessary.

glossary.GA-qCENT: The exact hard residual after replacing the reduced physical ray-conductor phase by its mean-zero nonprincipal-character part.
glossary.GA-qPRINC: The absolute payment of the principal multiplicative-character component of the reduced physical ray-conductor phase.
glossary.K^circ_{m,c}: The mean-zero nonprincipal multiplicative-character part of the function u mapsto e_m(-c u^{-1}) on the unit group modulo m.

7670948dedd78714.title: GCD-REDUCED kappa-POISSON IDENTITY, POINTWISE ZERO-ALIAS CANCELLATION, AND NONZERO-BAND LEDGER
7670948dedd78714.author: slava chan
7670948dedd78714.statement:
GCD-REDUCED kappa-POISSON IDENTITY, POINTWISE ZERO-ALIAS CANCELLATION, AND NONZERO-BAND LEDGER.

Let v,p,q be positive integers with p prime, put n=vp, and let A be a nonzero integer. Assume
  gcd(A,n)=gcd(q,n)=1.
Put
  d=gcd(|A|,q),  A=d A_0,  q=d q_0,
with the sign of A carried by A_0. Let F be a smooth compactly supported complex function on the real line, with Fourier transform
  Fhat(xi)=integral_R F(y)exp(-2 pi i xi y)dy.
For every integer solution (m,k) of
  qm+n k=A,                                                   (1)
put
  ell=vk.
Then
  d divides k,
and, on writing
  k=d t,  kappa=v t,
one has
  ell=d kappa,  v divides kappa,
  n t=A_0-q_0m,  gcd(t,q_0)=gcd(kappa,q_0)=1.                (2)
Moreover, for every integer h,
  e_q(hk)=e_{q_0}(ht)
         =e_{q_0}(h kappa v^(-1)),                           (3)
where v^(-1) is taken modulo q_0 and e_r(z)=exp(2 pi i z/r), with e_1=1.

There is an exact Poisson identity in the reduced complementary coordinate:
  sum_{m,k in Z:qm+nk=A}F(m)
  =sum_{t in Z:nt congruent A_0 (mod q_0)}
      F((A_0-nt)/q_0)
  =n^(-1)sum_{h in Z}Fhat(h/n)e_n(h A_0 q_0^(-1))
  =n^(-1)sum_{h in Z}Fhat(h/n)e_n(h A q^(-1)).               (4)
The h=0 term in (4) is exactly
  z_q=n^(-1)Fhat(0).                                         (5)
Consequently, pointwise in (q,v,p), the zero alias in kappa-Poisson summation cancels the literal negative h=0 density in the complete nonzero-Poisson row of fact ace362082848a702. The sum of all nonzero kappa aliases is exactly the original nonzero h-row
  a_q=n^(-1)sum_{h nonzero}Fhat(h/n)e_n(h A q^(-1));          (6)
it is not a new independent oscillatory family.

For a quantitative band ledger, assume M>0, H_0=n/M>=1, L>=0, and that for every integer J>=2,
  |Fhat(xi)|<=C_J M L(1+M|xi|)^(-J).                         (7)
Then for every T>=1,
  n^(-1)sum_{T<=|h|<2T}|Fhat(h/n)|
  <<_J C_J L (T/H_0)(1+T/H_0)^(-J),                         (8)
and
  n^(-1)sum_{h nonzero}|Fhat(h/n)|<<_J C_J L.                (9)
For every Y>=1, the union of dyadic bands with |h|>=YH_0 has total l1 mass
  <<_J C_J L Y^(1-J).                                       (10)
Thus every signed dyadic nonzero band is absolutely summable with its literal Poisson normalization.

The cancellation (5) requires completion of the whole reduced progression before Poisson summation. More precisely, let Psi:R->C be smooth and assume
  u maps to Psi(u)F((A_0-nu)/q_0)
is smooth and compactly supported. If this factor is inserted before progression Poisson summation, its zero alias is
  q_0^(-1) integral_R Psi(u)F((A_0-nu)/q_0)du,              (11)
which need not equal z_q. A literal deletion mask specified only on integer t has no canonical real zero alias: different smooth extensions can have different integrals in (11). Therefore such a discrete kappa- or m-deletion must be reassembled to the complete progression, or supplied with a specific smooth extension and its own zero-mode analysis, before pointwise principal cancellation is claimed.

Equations (4)-(10) do not reduce the all-nonzero OSC cross Gram of fact 670a97b5f2366250: after zero-alias cancellation, the surviving aliases are exactly the same nonzero h-coefficients and phases. No PMD or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
7670948dedd78714.proof:
Because q=dq_0 and A=dA_0, equation (1) gives
  n k=d(A_0-q_0m).
The assumption gcd(A,n)=1 implies gcd(d,n)=1. Therefore d|k; write k=dt. Dividing by d gives
  q_0m+n t=A_0.
This proves the first identities in (2). Reducing modulo q_0 gives
  n t congruent A_0 (mod q_0).
Now gcd(A_0,q_0)=1 by the definition of d, and gcd(n,q_0)=1 because q_0|q and gcd(q,n)=1. Hence gcd(t,q_0)=1. Also gcd(v,q_0)=1, so kappa=vt is coprime to q_0. Formula (3) follows from
  e_{dq_0}(hdt)=e_{q_0}(ht)
and t=kappa v^(-1) modulo q_0.

The map
  t maps to m=(A_0-nt)/q_0
is a bijection from integers satisfying nt congruent A_0 modulo q_0 to integer solutions of q_0m+nt=A_0, and then k=dt reconstructs (1). This proves the first equality in (4).

Let a be the residue A_0 n^(-1) modulo q_0 and put
  G(u)=F((A_0-nu)/q_0).
Poisson summation on u congruent a modulo q_0 gives
  sum_{u congruent a (mod q_0)}G(u)
  =q_0^(-1)sum_{r in Z}Ghat(r/q_0)e_{q_0}(ar).               (12)
A change of variables y=(A_0-nu)/q_0 yields
  Ghat(xi)=(q_0/n)e(-xi A_0/n)Fhat(-xi q_0/n).               (13)
Substitute xi=r/q_0 into (12). Additive reciprocity for the coprime integers n,q_0 gives
  e_{q_0}(rA_0 n^(-1))e(-rA_0/(nq_0))
  =e_n(-rA_0 q_0^(-1)).
Therefore (12) equals
  n^(-1)sum_{r in Z}Fhat(-r/n)e_n(-rA_0q_0^(-1)).
Replace r by -h to obtain the third expression in (4). Finally,
  A q^(-1)=dA_0(dq_0)^(-1) congruent A_0q_0^(-1) (mod n),
because d is invertible modulo n. This proves the last expression.

The term r=0, equivalently h=0, is exactly (5). Removing it from (4) gives (6), which is the complete nonzero-Poisson identity of fact ace362082848a702 in the reduced coordinates.

For (8), apply (7) with xi=h/n. There are O(T) integers in the displayed band, so
  n^(-1)sum_{T<=|h|<2T}|Fhat(h/n)|
  << C_J (TM/n)L(1+TM/n)^(-J).
Since H_0=n/M, this is (8). Summing directly over h and comparing with the integral of (1+u/H_0)^(-J), using H_0>=1, proves (9). Summing (8) over dyadic T>=YH_0 proves (10), after weakening the convergent geometric exponent by one.

Under the stated smoothness and compact-support condition on Psi G, the same progression Poisson formula applies to Psi(u)G(u). Its zero Fourier coefficient is exactly (11). The warning for a mask given only on integers follows because progression data do not determine a unique smooth extension or its integral. Since (6) is an identity with the original nonzero h-row, the final scope statement follows.

glossary.kappa: The reduced complementary cofactor ell/gcd(A,q)=v k/gcd(A,q).

76a9cd4315f7cd7d.title: OUTER-SIGN-FREE LARGE-COMMON-DENOMINATOR EXCLUSION
76a9cd4315f7cd7d.author: slava chan
76a9cd4315f7cd7d.statement:
OUTER-SIGN-FREE LARGE-COMMON-DENOMINATOR EXCLUSION.

Adopt the exact outer-sign-free source OSF-SLOPE in fact 1ea36d543252d94d on one modulus block Q<=q<2Q and frequency block F<=|h|<2F. Let a nonzero exact retained term have rays
R=(epsilon,a,b), R'=(epsilon',a',b'),
g=gcd(a,a'), alpha=a/g, beta=a'/g,
L_0=epsilon b beta-epsilon'b'alpha,
c_g=gcd(g,T), r_g=g/c_g,
where T=mathscr A. Then
0<r_g<=|L_0|<2F(alpha+beta)<8QF/g.                                 (1)
Equivalently,
g r_g=g^2/c_g<8QF,
g^2<8c_g QF.                                                       (2)

Consequently the exact outer-sign-free hard source is empty on the chamber
g^2>=8 gcd(g,T) QF.                                                (3)
In particular, on gcd(g,T)=1 it is empty for
g>=sqrt(8QF).                                                       (4)
More generally, for every positive real C_0, its restriction to gcd(g,T)<=C_0 is empty when
g>=sqrt(8C_0 QF).                                                   (5)

For the reduced-equal-denominator slice alpha=beta=1, equation (1) sharpens to
r_g<=|epsilon b-epsilon'b'|<4F.                                    (6)
Thus this slice is empty for r_g>=4F.

Every complete U_lambda transform and every literal selector is retained; the result deletes only an arithmetically impossible parameter chamber. It proves no estimate on the complementary chamber, no P-qSRC-SUP, no C-qSRC-SUP, no tail payment, and no Goldbach conclusion.
76a9cd4315f7cd7d.proof:
Fact 1ea36d543252d94d proves on every outer-sign-free pair that
r_g|L_0.                                                           (7)
It also proves
m_d=rho_lambda/gcd(rho_lambda,g r_g ell_g),
where ell_g=L_0/r_g, and that the hard condition is m_d>L with L>1. If L_0=0, then Delta_0=gL_0=0 and therefore m_d=1, contradicting m_d>L. Hence L_0 is nonzero. Together with (7), this gives
r_g<=|L_0|.                                                        (8)

For an exact supported ray, fact a36284a9dbec7837 writes
q=ka, h=epsilon kb
with a positive integer k. The literal block in fact e55b27d39c593164 has
Q<=q<2Q, F<=|h|<2F.
Therefore
a<=q<2Q, b<=|h|<2F.                                                (9)
The same bounds hold for a',b'. Since a=g alpha and a'=g beta,
alpha<2Q/g, beta<2Q/g.                                             (10)
Now the triangle inequality gives
|L_0|
 <=b beta+b'alpha
 <2F(beta+alpha)
 <2F(4Q/g)
 =8QF/g.                                                           (11)
Equations (8) and (11) prove (1). Multiplication by g and the identity
g r_g=g^2/c_g
prove (2). The contrapositive gives (3), and (4)-(5) are immediate specializations.

If alpha=beta=1, then
L_0=epsilon b-epsilon'b'.
Using b,b'<2F in place of (10) gives
|L_0|<4F.
Combine with (8) to prove (6). Since every argument was applied to the exact retained ray support and did not alter a coefficient or mask, all scope statements follow.

771d292cffc890c1.title: LITERAL FORWARD-REVERSE RAISED-STOPPING B CLOSURE IN THE FIRST POST-LOW-BETA BUFFER. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, beta_0=6/5-2kappa, beta_1=6/5-3sigma, kappa_0=1/200, and fix 0<eta<sigma. Let x>=3 and let N be a positive integer comparable to x. Work with the literal paired nonzero-Poisson source atoms, exact outer-gcd normalization d=ga,r=gb with g=gcd(d,r) dividing N, normalized marker partition, and post-A residual ledger of facts 15425579cb248eff and aeffec374578707c
771d292cffc890c1.author: slava chan
771d292cffc890c1.statement:
LITERAL FORWARD-REVERSE RAISED-STOPPING B CLOSURE IN THE FIRST POST-LOW-BETA BUFFER. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, beta_0=6/5-2kappa, beta_1=6/5-3sigma, kappa_0=1/200, and fix 0<eta<sigma. Let x>=3 and let N be a positive integer comparable to x. Work with the literal paired nonzero-Poisson source atoms, exact outer-gcd normalization d=ga,r=gb with g=gcd(d,r) dividing N, normalized marker partition, and post-A residual ledger of facts 15425579cb248eff and aeffec374578707c.

In the forward orientation assume
R>D, c_1 x<=DM<=C_1 x,
c_D x^(1/2)(log x)^(-A_D)<=D<=C_D x^(1/2),
and R>x^(9/16-kappa_0).
In the reverse orientation assume
D>R, c_1 x<=RK<=C_1 x,
c_R x^(1/2)(log x)^(-A_R)<=R<=C_R x^(1/2),
and D>x^(9/16-kappa_0).
All displayed c_i,C_i are fixed positive constants, A_D,A_R are fixed nonnegative constants, and every physical scale D,M,R,K is at most Cx for a fixed C.

Forward put Q=D/g, B=R/g=Q^beta, G=M/Q, H_T=B/Q, H_P=B/M and L_src=N/g. Reverse put Q=R/g, B=D/g=Q^beta, G=K/Q, H_T=B/Q, H_P=B/K and L_src=N/g. Let R_B,buf be the sum of every normalized raised-stopping B atom in either strict orientation for which
beta_0<beta<=beta_1,
over every actual G>0 and every exact outer gcd g dividing N. Include every frozen source, parent, fixed-U, high, smooth/projective and Fourier label. Include all atoms in every inherited target-gcd, prime-order, collision and deletion refinement; these auxiliary refinements are summed to completion within R_B,buf rather than imposed as arbitrary joint masks on the separated trace.

Then there is a fixed delta_B,buf>0 such that
|R_B,buf| << x^(1-delta_B,buf).
No B atom, G-range, frequency block, parent, orientation, or outer-g layer in the displayed buffer is deleted. The theorem estimates only the complete raised-stopping B anatomy in the displayed normalized-beta buffer. It does not estimate A above beta_1, C1, C2, C3, the later beta_1<beta<6/5 range, higher anatomies, endpoints, PMD, logical bad-N capture, or Goldbach.
771d292cffc890c1.proof:
The standard five-way marker is valid throughout the displayed buffer because beta_1=6/5-3sigma is smaller than beta_m=6/5-12sigma/5 in fact 15425579cb248eff. Fact aeffec374578707c proves that, after the A anatomy is removed in this slab, the complete B anatomy remains as a disjoint coordinate for both orientations, every parent and every actual G. Its proof removes atoms only by the A-anatomy and beta selectors. Therefore the auxiliary target-gcd, prime-order, collision and deletion refinements on B may be summed back to their complete B coefficient before analytic estimation.
