This is not an application of a reciprocal estimate with an arbitrary joint mask.

We match that complete coefficient to fact df4b02d6fa1181f0. Fix first a forward exact-g layer. Write d=ga,r=gb, so Q=D/g, B=R/g, G=M/Q and L_src=N/g. The normalized stopping identity of fact 6414b11506a84ff0 writes the B coefficient exactly as a sum over b=uy with gcd(u,y)=1 and coefficient
(-1)^k mu(u)1_{j_I(u)=0}Gamma_{k;L,S_0}(y)/binom(k+omega_L(u),k).                    (1)
Squarefreeness and gcd(a,b)=1 give gcd(uy,a)=1. Additive reciprocity gives
e_b(L_src h a^(-1))
 =e_a(-L_src h b^(-1)) e(L_src h/(ab)).                            (2)
Thus the reciprocal trace has modulus a comparable to Q, factor product uy comparable to B, fixed target A=-L_src, and no target-gcd descent is required because df4b02d6fa1181f0 permits a fixed nonunit target and unrestricted gcd(h,a).

The literal source, fixed-U and dyadic masks are fixed-complexity smooth restrictions. The high and parent predicates are label scalars by facts 77d7a3419a07305c and a71f777ad842c886. On a dyadic frequency block F<=|h|<2F, the Poisson proof in df9748efe29ab475 and the projective audit in fact 0d53c27d174b26ed give the literal prefactor H_P^(-1) and, after extracting omega_F,
|omega_F|<<_{J_0}min(1,(F/H_P)^(-J_0))                               (3)
for every fixed J_0. The remaining amplitude in the scaled variables a/Q, |h|/F, u/U and y/Y has uniformly bounded projective Fourier norm. The archimedean factor in (2) is included in this audit: its logarithmic phase size is controlled by
L_src/(QM)=N/(DM)=O(1)                                             (4)
after the F/H_P decay is extracted. Hence every fixed source, high, parent and smooth label matches exactly the allowed restriction class of df4b02d6fa1181f0. The finitely many auxiliary refinements were already recombined and do not appear as joint masks.

The target-size hypothesis also holds. The forced-high condition gives
Q^(beta-1)=R/D>x^(1/16-kappa_0+o(1)).
Since beta-1<1/5, Q>=x^c for a fixed c>0. Also
|L_src|=(N/D)Q<=x^(1/2+o(1))Q,
so |L_src|<=Q^(C_B) for a fixed C_B depending only on kappa. This is the same physical target calculation verified in fact 24e911b7685090c1.

Fact 15425579cb248eff proves that every actual forward G<1 lies in
Q^(-sigma+eta)<=G<=Q^(sigma-eta),
while every actual G>=1 lies in the full-G regime. If G>=1, Part (i) of df4b02d6fa1181f0 gives the fixed-g complete B contribution
<<GQ^(2-delta_1).                                                  (5)
Since DM=gGQ^2 is comparable to x, (5) is
<<(x/g)Q^(-delta_1).                                               (6)
If G<1, Part (ii) gives
<<Q^(2-delta_2).                                                    (7)

For the reverse orientation interchange (d,m,D,M) with (r,k,R,K) and reindex the complete signed frequency family by h to -h, exactly as in fact 65b10e9a052e9479. Now Q=R/g, B=D/g, G=K/Q, and the normalized marked factor is a=uy while the reciprocal modulus is b. The phase after the sign reindexing is
e_b(+L_src h a^(-1)),
so apply df4b02d6fa1181f0 with A=+L_src. The retained archimedean reciprocity factor is part of the scaled-smooth amplitude because L_src/(QK)=N/(RK)=O(1), as proved in fact 65b10e9a052e9479. The exact stopping coefficient (1), the projective decay (3), target bound, and estimates (5)-(7) are otherwise unchanged.

It remains to sum exact outer gcds and fixed labels. In either orientation forced high gave Q>=x^c. Therefore (6), summed with sum_{g|N}1/g=x^o(1), is O(x^(1-delta_3)) after decreasing delta_3. For (7), forward Q=D/g and reverse Q=R/g. Hence
sum_{g|N}Q^(2-delta_2)
 <=D^(2-delta_2)sum_{g>=1}g^(-2+delta_2)
or
 <=R^(2-delta_2)sum_{g>=1}g^(-2+delta_2).                         (8)
Decrease delta_2 below one. The physical square-root upper bounds on D and R make (8) O(x^(1-delta_2/3)) after shrinking the exponent. All inherited fixed source, parent and smooth labels are polylogarithmically numerous and are absorbed into the minimum fixed saving. This proves the assertion without estimating any other anatomy or beta range.

glossary.C_B: A fixed exponent bounding the normalized target size in the literal B trace.
glossary.R_B,buf: The complete literal forward and reverse raised-stopping B contribution in the first post-low-beta buffer.
glossary.delta_B,buf: The resulting fixed global power-saving exponent.

7767c0ebde1c24a7.title: ABSTRACT CLOSED-ENDPOINT COMPLETE-FREQUENCY ONE-ROUGH-PRIME \(C1_*\) TRACE
7767c0ebde1c24a7.author: slava chan
7767c0ebde1c24a7.statement:
ABSTRACT CLOSED-ENDPOINT COMPLETE-FREQUENCY ONE-ROUGH-PRIME \(C1_*\) TRACE.

Fix integers \(J,C_A\ge1\), a constant \(C\ge1\), and
\(0<\kappa\le1/100\).  Put
\[
 \sigma=\kappa/100,quad
 \beta_1=6/5-3\sigma,quad
 \beta_m=6/5-12\sigma/5,
\]
and let \(\beta_1<\beta\le\beta_m\).  For sufficiently large \(Q\)
put
\[
 B=Q^\beta,quad H_T=B/Q,quad
 L=H_TQ^\sigma,quad S_0=H_T^2Q^{3\sigma},quad
 Z_*=2Q^{3/2-\beta-3\sigma}.
\]
Let \(V,P\ge1\) be dyadic scales satisfying
\[
 C^{-1}B\le VP\le CB.                                            \tag{1}
\]
Let \(\xi_v\) be supported on squarefree \(V\le v<2V\) with
\[
 v\le S_0,qquad p\mid v\Longrightarrow p\le L,
\qquad |\xi_v|\le\tau_J(v).
\]
Let the other factor be a prime \(P\le p<2P\), \(p\ge Z_*\).
Fix \(A\ne0\), \(|A|\le Q^{C_A}\), and \(|c_q|\le1\) on
\(Q\le q<2Q\).  Let \(G>0\), \(H_P=H_T/G\).  For every dyadic
integer \(F\ge1\), let \(\nu_F(h)\) be supported on
\(F\le|h|<2F\) with a fixed divisor bound, let
\[
 |\omega_F|\le C(J_0)\min\{1,(F/H_P)^{-J_0}\}
\]
for every fixed \(J_0\ge1\), and let \(\Psi_F\) be a uniformly
scaled-smooth projective amplitude of fixed complexity and norm on the full
rectangle in \(q,h,v,p\).  Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
T_{C1_*}={1\over H_P}\sum_F\omega_F
 &\sum_{Q\le q<2Q}c_q
 \sum_{F\le|h|<2F}\nu_F(h)\\
 &\sum_{\substack{V\le v<2V\cr
 P\le p<2P, p\ {m prime}\cr
 (vp,q)=1}}
 \xi_v\Psi_F\!\left({q\over Q},{|h|\over F},
                       {v\over V},{p\over P}\right)
 e_q(Ah(vp)^{-1}).
\end{aligned}                                                     \tag{2}
\]
There is no sharp product mask in (2); (1) is a dyadic scale relation.

If \(G\ge1\), then
\[
 T_{C1_*}\ll GQ^{2-\delta_{C1,F}}.                               \tag{3}
\]
If \(0<\eta<\sigma\) and
\[
 Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\le G\le Q^{\sigma-\eta},
\]
then
\[
 T_{C1_*}\ll Q^{2-\delta_{C1,N}}.                                \tag{4}
\]
The fixed savings and constants depend only on the fixed parameters,
divisor orders and projective norm.  The bounds include \(H_P<1\), all
actual integer frequencies, the possibly nonunit target \(A\),
unrestricted \((h,q)\), the proper-prime-power subtraction and every
Vaughan Type-I/Type-II box.  They are uniform under legal one-variable,
label-scalar and projective factors, but not arbitrary joint masks.
Taking \(\xi_v=-\mu(v)\) gives the abstract coefficient of the
source-preserving \(C1_*\) marker.  No literal-source, outer-\(g\),
other-anatomy, PMD, DCE, or Goldbach claim is made.
7767c0ebde1c24a7.proof:
Put
\[
 \nu={\log V\over\log Q}.
\]
Fixed dyadic constants contribute \(O(1/\log Q)\), absorbed below by
the displayed fixed \(\sigma\)-margins.  Since \(V\le S_0\),
\[
 0\le\nu\le2\beta-2+3\sigma.                                 \tag{5}
\]
From (1), \(P=Q^{\beta-\nu+O(1/\log Q)}\).  Every prime divisor of
\(v\) is at most \(L<Z_*\le p\), so \((v,p)=1\) automatically.

Use the exact identity
\[
 1_{n\ {m prime}}
 ={\Lambda(n)\over\log n}
 -\sum_{\substack{n=r^j\cr r\ {m prime},\ j\ge2}}{1\over j}.
                                                                    \tag{6}
\]
Logarithmic Fourier separation absorbs \(1/\log n\), the smooth
amplitude and smooth dyadic endpoint factors into legal one-variable
coefficients with \(Q^\epsilon\) total cost.

For the proper-prime-power part of (6), there are
\(O(P^{1/2}\log(2P))\) possibilities.  On a block put
\[
 u_F=F/H_P.
\]
Absolute summation in (2) gives
\[
 \ll Q^\epsilon|\omega_F|u_FQV P^{1/2}
 \ll Q^\epsilon|\omega_F|u_FQ(VB)^{1/2}.                        \tag{7}
\]
Since \(V\le S_0\) and \(\beta\le\beta_m\),
\[
 Q(VB)^{1/2}
 \le Q^{3\beta/2+3\sigma/2}
 \le Q^{9/5-21\sigma/10}.                                       \tag{8}
\]
The dyadic sum of \(|\omega_F|u_F\) is bounded, so (7) is
power-small relative to \(Q^2\), hence also to \(GQ^2\) for
\(G\ge1\).

Apply the exact Vaughan identity and box decomposition of fact
\(29c43cef40f2e79b\) to \(\Lambda\) at scale \(P\), with cutoff
\(P^{1/3}\).  It gives divisor-bounded coefficients.  A Type-II
smaller-factor exponent \(\lambda\) satisfies
\[
 {\beta-\nu\over3}+O(1/\log Q)
 \le\lambda\le
 {\beta-\nu\over2}+O(1/\log Q),                                \tag{9}
\]
while a Type-I coefficient-bearing exponent satisfies
\[
 0\le\lambda\le {\beta-\nu\over3}+O(1/\log Q).              \tag{10}
\]

Set
\[
 \ell=2\beta-2+3\sigma/2,qquad
 r=3-2\beta-3\sigma/2.                                          \tag{11}
\]
We show every nonshort box has one grouped factor exponent in
\([\ell,r]\).

For Type II put \(w=\nu+\lambda\).  By (9),
\[
 w\ge\beta/3+O(1/\log Q).
\]
If \(w\le3-2\beta-2\sigma\), choose the grouped factor \(vl\).
Its lower margin before endpoint errors is
\[
 {\beta\over3}-\ell
 ={6-5\beta\over3}-{3\sigma\over2}
 \ge {5\sigma\over2}.                                          \tag{12}
\]
If \(w>3-2\beta-2\sigma\), choose the complementary Vaughan
factor.  From the upper bound in (9) and (5),
\[
 \beta-w\ge1-\beta/2-3\sigma/2+O(1/\log Q),
\]
whose margin over \(\ell\) is
\[
 {6-5\beta-6\sigma\over2}\ge3\sigma.                          \tag{13}
\]
Its upper margin below \(r\) is at least
\[
 6-5\beta-7\sigma/2\ge17\sigma/2.                              \tag{14}
\]
Thus Type II is exhausted.

For Type I put \(w_0=\nu+\lambda\).  By (5),(10),
\[
 w_0\le {5\beta-4\over3}+2\sigma+O(1/\log Q).                 \tag{15}
\]
Use three disjoint branches.

If \(w_0\le1/2-3\sigma\), retain it as the short
coefficient-bearing factor; after endpoint absorption its scale
\(L_I\) is at most \(Q^{1/2-5\sigma/2}\).

If
\[
 1/2-3\sigma<w_0\le3-2\beta-2\sigma,
\]
choose the grouped factor.  Its lower margin over \(\ell\) is at least
\[
 5/2-2\beta-9\sigma/2
 \ge1/10+3\sigma/10>0,                                          \tag{16}
\]
and its upper bound is stronger than \(r\).

If \(w_0>3-2\beta-2\sigma\), choose the complementary unweighted
factor.  From (15), its lower margin over \(\ell\) is at least
\[
 {10-8\beta\over3}-{7\sigma\over2}>0,                          \tag{17}
\]
while (14) gives its upper margin.  This exhausts Type I.

For every nonshort box let \(S\) be the selected factor and \(T\) its
complement.  Equations (11)-(17) give
\[
 H_T^2Q^{3\sigma/2}\le S\le
 Q^{1-3\sigma/2}/H_T^2,qquad ST\asymp QH_T.                    \tag{18}
\]
Expand the remaining smooth product and amplitude factors
projectively.  Their modes preserve divisor bounds on the grouped
coefficients.

Fix an actual block and put
\[
 G_F=H_T/F=G/u_F.
\]
Apply fact \(42720f6d803c4640\) with frequency \(F\), factor scales
\(S,T\), and imbalance \(G_F\).  It permits fixed nonunit \(A\) and
unrestricted \((h,q)\).  Replacing its \(F^{-1}\) normalization by
\(H_P^{-1}=u_FF^{-1}\) gives, apart from \(Q^\epsilon|\omega_F|\),
\[
 G^{1/4}u_F^{3/4}Q^2H_T^{1/2}S^{-1/4},
\quad
 G^{1/4}u_F^{3/4}Q^{7/4}H_T^{1/2}S^{1/4},
\]
\[
 u_FQ^2H_TS^{-1/2},qquad u_FQ^{7/4}H_T.                           \tag{19}
\]
Window (18) bounds the four baseline expressions by
\[
 Q^{2-3\sigma/8},quad Q^{2-3\sigma/8},quad
 Q^{2-3\sigma/4},quad Q^{2-1/20-12\sigma/5}.                   \tag{20}
\]
The decay hypothesis gives
\[
 \sum_F|\omega_F|u_F^{3/4+\epsilon}
 +\sum_F|\omega_F|u_F^{1+\epsilon}\ll1.                        \tag{21}
\]
For \(G\ge1\), use \(G^{1/4}\le G\), proving (3) on all nonshort
boxes.  In the near-balanced range,
\(G^{1/4}\le Q^{(\sigma-\eta)/4}\); the first two baselines retain
saving \(\sigma/8+\eta/4\), and the last two retain their displayed
savings.  This proves (4) on nonshort boxes.

For the short Type-I branch, apply fact \(bbcb9f66597c667c\) with
\(\tau=2\sigma\) on every
\(F\le Q^{C_A+3}\).  The hypotheses hold because
\[
 L_I\le Q^{1/2-5\sigma/2}<Q^{1/2-2\sigma},qquad
 L_IM_I\asymp B<Q^{2-2\sigma}.
\]
After multiplication by \(u_F\), its precise bound is
\[
 \ll Q^\epsilon|\omega_F|u_F
 \{B+Q^{3/2}L_I\}
 \ll Q^\epsilon|\omega_F|u_FQ^{2-2\sigma}.                    \tag{22}
\]
Sum by (21).  For \(F>Q^{C_A+3}\), absolute counting gives
\[
 \ll Q^\epsilon|\omega_F|u_FQB.
\]
In both regimes
\[
 H_P\le Q^{\beta-1+\sigma-\eta}<Q^{1/4}
\]
(with the \(-\eta\) omitted and a stronger bound when \(G\ge1\)).
Thus the large-\(F\) range has a fixed large lower bound on \(u_F\)
and is negligible by choosing the available decay order.

All Vaughan boxes, signs and projective modes are polylogarithmically
numerous.  If \(H_P<1\), every actual \(F\) has \(u_F>1\) and is
still summed by (21).  Combining the proper-power, nonshort and short
branches proves (3)-(4) with all stated uniformity.

glossary.T_C1*: The abstract complete-frequency one-rough-prime trace with cutoff Z_*.
glossary.delta_C1,F: The fixed full-G saving exponent for the endpoint C1_* trace.
glossary.delta_C1,N: The fixed near-balanced saving exponent for the endpoint C1_* trace.

Fix a selected prime p, signed nonzero height blocks H<=|h_i|<2H, and natural C1 cofactor blocks T<=t_i=n_i/p<2T, and assume
77987a35ae17ca77.author: slava chan
77987a35ae17ca77.statement:
DELETION-AWARE ACTUAL C1 FOUR-ROW q-PAYMENT IN ONE LONG FIXED-PRIME CHAMBER. Adopt one actual strict-top C1 block and its four scalar row-mode expansions from facts ff228b0e569531f8 and 71f1a10b52148348. Fix a selected prime p, signed nonzero height blocks H<=|h_i|<2H, and natural C1 cofactor blocks T<=t_i=n_i/p<2T, and assume
Q^zeta<=p<=2Q^(6/5), 2H<p, 2T<p, H,T>=p^delta,
where zeta,delta>0 are fixed. Give the four positions signs sigma_1=sigma_2=+1 and sigma_3=sigma_4=-1. Pair the positions into two disjoint TT-star pairs, each containing one positive and one negative position, and retain on each pair its exact C1 first-nonresonant determinant mask. For a physical four-tuple define E_p to be the indicator that the equality partition of q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4 modulo p has no singleton and that, on every equal-residue block B,
sum_{i in B} sigma_i h_i/t_i=0 mod p.
Thus E_p is exactly the zero-Fourier repeated-pole exceptional locus of fact a9a0e9af2477d71d. Let S_{p,H,T}^{non} be the signed sum of the actual four row-mode products, their p-local reciprocal phases, and the two exact C1 pair masks, over all displayed physical q_i,h_i,t_i and source modes, with the cross-pair deletion 1-E_p retained. No further non-row-factorable q-dependent mask is inserted.

Let delta_1 be any exponent allowed in fact a8d14bd3414bf66e. For every 0<rho<min(1,2delta), after decreasing epsilon_0>0 if necessary,
|S_{p,H,T}^{non}| << Q^{o(1)}(1+H/H_P)^(-4A)(HT)^4
 {Q^(4-2delta_1)+(1+Q/p)^4 R_{p,Q}^2 p^(-rho)},
where R_{p,Q} is the number of nonzero residues modulo p represented in [Q,2Q), so R_{p,Q}<=min(p-1,Q+1). Consequently, for some fixed omega=omega(zeta,delta)>0,
|S_{p,H,T}^{non}| << Q^{4-omega+o(1)}(1+H/H_P)^(-4A)(HT)^4.
One may take any omega<min(2delta_1,zeta rho). This conclusion sums varying n_i=p t_i and all physical signed nonzero heights inside the fixed long blocks, pays the exact cross-pair exceptional deletion, and preserves the two pair masks. It remains fixed in p and excludes short cofactor blocks, zero-height or p-divisible-height cases, and global envelope/completion comparison.
77987a35ae17ca77.proof:
First ignore the factor 1-E_p while retaining the two C1 pair masks. For every fixed choice of the four h_i,t_i and source modes, the q-dependent expression is the tensor product of the two disjoint TT-star pair expressions in fact a8d14bd3414bf66e. The hypotheses 2H

77b42a63e0f65307.title: EXACT COLLAPSE OF THE CROSS-INCIDENCE HIGH FACE TO ONE FULL CONDUCTOR
77b42a63e0f65307.author: slava chan
77b42a63e0f65307.statement:
EXACT COLLAPSE OF THE CROSS-INCIDENCE HIGH FACE TO ONE FULL CONDUCTOR.

Assume the actual scales B,Q,F_0 and target N of fact 2234aaf28e165b88. Let
 b_1=p_1s_1, b_2=p_2s_2
satisfy
 B<=b_i<2B,
 b_i squarefree,
 p_i prime,
 1<=s_i<F_0,
 p_i does not divide N.                                    (1)
Let Q<=a_i<2Q and (a_i,b_i)=1. Assume
 p_1|s_2,                                                    (2)
and put
 q_2=b_2/p_1=p_2(s_2/p_1).                                  (3)
Then q_2>1 and is squarefree.

If s_1>1, let M_1 be the unique integer with
 1<=M_1<=s_1, p_1M_1 congruent N (mod s_1);
if s_1=1, put M_1=1.
Let M_{12} be the unique integer with
 1<=M_{12}<=q_2, p_1M_{12} congruent N (mod q_2).            (4)

For a squarefree q>1, target M, divisor h|q and unit a modulo q define
 R^M_{q,h}(a)
  =product_{r|h}
    [e_r(M[a(q/r)]^(-1))+1/(r-1)],                          (5)
 P^M_{q,>Y}(a)
  =sum_{h|q;h>Y;(h,M)=1}
    c_{q/h}(M)R^M_{q,h}(a)/phi(q/h),                        (6)
 B^M_{q;(F_0/p,F_0]}(a)
  =sum_{h|q;F_0/p<h<=F_0;(h,M)=1}
    c_{q/h}(M)R^M_{q,h}(a)/phi(q/h).                        (7)
For q=1 set P^1_{1,>Y}=1_{Y<1}. For a prime p|b put
 r_{p,b}(a)=e_p(N[a(b/p)]^(-1))+1/(p-1).                    (8)

Then
 p_1>B/F_0,                                                  (9)
 q_2<2F_0.                                                   (10)
The transported high residual projector on row two is exactly
 P^{M_{12}}_{q_2,>F_0}(a_2)
 =
 1_{q_2>F_0}1_{(q_2,M_{12})=1}
 R^{M_{12}}_{q_2,q_2}(a_2).                                 (11)
Define the right side of (11) to be H_{12}(a_2).

With P_{b_i}(a_i) denoting the complete high-conductor projectors from fact 2234aaf28e165b88, their exact cross-row product is
 P_{b_1}(a_1)overline(P_{b_2}(a_2))
 =
 r_{p_1,b_1}(a_1)P^{M_1}_{s_1,>F_0/p_1}(a_1)
 times the complex conjugate of
 {e_{p_1}(N[a_2q_2]^(-1))H_{12}(a_2)
  +r_{p_1,b_2}(a_2)
   B^{M_{12}}_{q_2;(F_0/p_1,F_0]}(a_2)}.                    (12)
Here the factor P^{M_1}_{s_1,>F_0/p_1} is interpreted by the q=1 convention when s_1=1.

Thus the fused high face is zero or one full-conductor centered response. Every proper q_2-conductor face is confined to the explicit boundary block in (12).

No estimate for the full-conductor leading face or the boundary block, no TRI-CROSS or ROP estimate, no CEN-MZB estimate, no C_small estimate and no Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
77b42a63e0f65307.proof:
From b_1=p_1s_1, b_1>=B and s_1<F_0,
 p_1=b_1/s_1>B/F_0,
which proves (9). Since b_2<2B,
 q_2=b_2/p_1
 <2B/(B/F_0)
 =2F_0,
proving (10).

By definition (6),
 P^{M_{12}}_{q_2,>F_0}(a_2)
 =
 sum_{h|q_2;h>F_0;(h,M_{12})=1}
  c_{q_2/h}(M_{12})
  R^{M_{12}}_{q_2,h}(a_2)/phi(q_2/h).                      (13)
Because q_2 is squarefree, every proper divisor h<q_2 satisfies h<=q_2/2. Equation (10) gives q_2/2<F_0. Hence no proper divisor occurs in (13). If q_2<=F_0, the sum is empty. If q_2>F_0, the only possible divisor is h=q_2, and it occurs precisely when (q_2,M_{12})=1. Its cofactor is one, c_1(M_{12})/phi(1)=1, and its response is R^{M_{12}}_{q_2,q_2}(a_2). This proves (11).

Fact 2234aaf28e165b88, under exactly hypotheses (1)-(4) and the stated unit hypotheses, proves
 P_{b_1}(a_1)overline(P_{b_2}(a_2))
 =
 r_{p_1,b_1}(a_1)P^{M_1}_{s_1,>F_0/p_1}(a_1)
 times the complex conjugate of
 {e_{p_1}(N[a_2q_2]^(-1))P^{M_{12}}_{q_2,>F_0}(a_2)
  +r_{p_1,b_2}(a_2)
   B^{M_{12}}_{q_2;(F_0/p_1,F_0]}(a_2)}.                    (14)
That fact includes the same q=1 convention for s_1=1. Substitute (11) into (14) to obtain (12).

Every h in the boundary block satisfies h<=F_0 by (7). Every proper divisor h of q_2 is <F_0 by the divisor argument above. Therefore all proper q_2-conductor faces are confined to the boundary term. This proves every identity and scope restriction.

glossary.H_{12}(a_2): The collapsed cross-incidence high face on row two.

77d7a3419a07305c.title: SELF-CONTAINED HIGH-MASKED-POISSON PARTITION AND SHARP C2 DEFICIT
77d7a3419a07305c.author: slava chan
77d7a3419a07305c.statement:
SELF-CONTAINED HIGH-MASKED-POISSON PARTITION AND SHARP C2 DEFICIT.

Fix real numbers x>1, sigma in (0,1/100), kappa_0=1/200, kappa_t in (0,1/6), eta_t in (0,kappa_t/20), D_*>=1, and X_bal>=1. Put N=2x and assume N is an integer. Let mathcal L be a finite set of positive dyadic labels lambda=(D,M,R,K), and define
iota(D,M,R,K)=(R,K,D,M).

Define the 60-controlled predicate as the union of:
R/M<=x^(-sigma);
R<=D, D^19R^14<=x^(17-sigma), D^8R^7<=x^(8-sigma);
R>D, D^14R^19<=x^(17-sigma), D^7R^8<=x^(8-sigma).
Call lambda 60-residual if none holds.

Define mathcal A as the union of:
D<=X_bal and R<=x^(2/3-kappa_t);
D>X_bal and R<=M x^(-eta_t);
D>X_bal, max(D,R)>=x^(eta_t), and either
R<=D, D^19R^14<=x^(17-eta_t), D^8R^7<=x^(8-eta_t),
or
R>D, D^14R^19<=x^(17-eta_t), D^7R^8<=x^(8-eta_t).
Put
mathcal G={lambda in mathcal L:D>=4D_*, R>=4D_*},
mathcal C_91=mathcal A union iota(mathcal A intersect mathcal G).

Let mathcal Z be a finite set of records
z=(lambda;d,m,r,k;g,a,b,h)
where lambda belongs to mathcal L; d,m,r,k,g,a,b,h are positive integers;
dm+rk=N;
g=gcd(d,r), d=ga, r=gb, gcd(a,b)=1;
and mu(d)mu(r) is nonzero.
The positive h represents the conjugate-paired frequencies {h,-h}. Give z an arbitrary real coefficient
w_z=mu(d)mu(r)q_z.
For the literal Poisson source, q_z is twice the real part of the h-frequency Fourier coefficient times its additive phase, with every fixed target, logarithm, smooth, dyadic, fixed-U, and source mask retained. More abstractly q_z may be any real number; no factor inside it will be changed.

Let mathcal H be the atoms whose label is 60-residual and satisfies
R>x^(9/16-kappa_0),
and put
R_high=sum_{z in mathcal H}w_z.                               (1)

For z in mathcal H give the original atom one parent by the following precedence.

First, if lambda belongs to mathcal C_91, set P(z)=C91.

Otherwise define forward boundary admissibility by
D>1, 4/3<=beta_f=log R/log D<=3/2-kappa_t,
and existence of a divisor y of r such that, with t=r/y and y<=t,
D^(2-beta_f-3eta_t)<=y,t<=D^(2(beta_f-1)+3eta_t).
Define reverse admissibility by the same rule after replacing
(D,M,R,K;d,r) by (R,K,D,M;r,d).
The orientations are mutually exclusive. In an admissible orientation choose the least eligible y and its complement t. If its beta lies in [4/3,4/3+6eta_t], give tag 11 when
(Omega(y),Omega(t))=(1,1),
tag 21 when the unordered pair is {1,2},
and tag 22 when it is (2,2).
Give every other admissible atom tag asym.
Set P(z)=E_11,E_21,E_22, or E_asym accordingly.

Every remaining z is nonendpoint. If min(D,R)<4D_*, put P(z)=U_sh. Otherwise define
beta_z=log R/log D when R>D,
beta_z=log D/log R when D>R,
and beta_z=1 when D=R.
Put P(z)=U_low when beta_z<4/3, U_gap when
4/3<=beta_z<=3/2-kappa_t,
and U_sup when beta_z>3/2-kappa_t.
Let
mathcal P_H={C91,E_11,E_21,E_22,E_asym,U_sh,U_low,U_gap,U_sup}. (2)

For each label lambda occurring in mathcal H choose L_lambda,Z_lambda satisfying
2<=L_lambda<Z_lambda
and, for every atom at lambda,
r>L_lambda, Z_lambda^3>r.
On a support R/2<=r<=2R, one may take
L_lambda=2, Z_lambda=(4R)^(1/3)
for sufficiently large R.
Define the four real marker coefficients c_A,c_B,c_C1,c_C2 as follows. If r has a prime divisor in (L_lambda,Z_lambda), c_A is
-sum_{up=r, p prime, L_lambda<p<Z_lambda}mu(u)/(1+j(u)),
where j(u) counts interval-prime divisors of u, and the other three vanish. If there is no interval prime and the product v of prime divisors of r at most L_lambda exceeds L_lambda, c_B is the stopping sum of fact 85e63a9328d91711 and the others vanish. Otherwise r=vw uniquely, v<=L_lambda, and w is one prime p>=Z_lambda or two distinct primes Z_lambda<=p<q; set respectively
c_C1=-mu(v), c_C2=mu(v),
with the other coefficients zero. Then
mu(r)=c_A+c_B+c_C1+c_C2.                                     (3)

For P in mathcal P_H and X in {A,B,C1,C2}, define the real leaf sum
T_{P,X}=sum_{z in mathcal H:P(z)=P}
        mu(d)q_z c_{lambda,X}(r).                             (4)
Then
R_high=sum_{P in mathcal P_H}sum_X T_{P,X}                   (5)
exactly. Every q_z and hence every original paired h-phase and source mask is unchanged. The parent is frozen before expanding the internal A or B marker sum.

A C2 atom has r=vpq with distinct primes Z_lambda<=p<q. Define
delta_z={s in {p,q}:s divides g}.
Only delta_z=emptyset retains both p,q in b. In that case g divides v; writing v_0=v/g gives
b=v_0pq
and the source equation becomes
a m+b k=N/g                                                     (6)
with a positive integer target N/g. Split this layer into |h|>=Z_lambda and 0<h<Z_lambda. On the short layer put
J_z={s in {p,q}:s divides mh}.
Then every T_{P,C2} has an exact refinement by delta_z, frequency length, and short-frequency J_z. The cell
delta_z=emptyset, 0<h<Z_lambda, J_z=emptyset                  (7)
is the unique short-frequency cell in this refinement with both rough primes retained and full rough frequency conductor. Long atoms remain separate and may also be primitive.

For an asymptotic sequence with D=x^(1/2+o(1)), put rho=log R/log x. If
R>D and 9/16-kappa_0<rho<=2/3-epsilon
for fixed epsilon>0, then beta_z=2rho+o(1)<4/3. Therefore such an atom has parent C91 when lambda belongs to mathcal C_91; otherwise it is never in an E parent and lies in U_sh if D<4D_* and U_low if D>=4D_*. Thus the high mask (1) is not a terminal mask.

Finally choose any union mathcal G_leaf of refined leaves of (5), let its real sum be T_G, and put
mathcal R_comp=R_high-T_G.
Suppose
R_high<=-A_0+epsilon_0
with A_0>0. For 0<theta<=1 and real rho_err,
T_G<=-theta A_0+rho_err                                      (8)
is equivalent to
mathcal R_comp>=R_high+theta A_0-rho_err.                    (9)
Using only the upper bound for R_high, the sharp uniform sufficient condition is
mathcal R_comp>=-(1-theta)A_0+epsilon_0-rho_err.              (10)
If mathcal G_leaf contains m disjoint real leaves, (8) forces one leaf to be at most
-theta A_0/m+rho_err/m.
Thus a quantitative good C2 or terminal leaf requires a one-sided lower bound for its complete real signed complement. No such estimate, four-prime majorant, modular-window localization, or Goldbach implication is asserted.
77d7a3419a07305c.proof:
The parent construction is disjoint and exhaustive. C91 has first precedence. Outside it, forward admissibility implies R>D and reverse admissibility implies D>R, so both cannot hold. The least eligible divisor and tag are unique. The remaining atoms are split by min(D,R) and the three disjoint beta intervals. This is the explicit set partition established in facts 91db48815d136d4c and 79eb78ffa67de31c.

The source equation and outer gcd normalization give
N=dm+rk=g(am+bk).
Hence g divides N and (6) holds before any C2 specialization. The h-pairing is legitimate for the literal source because its smooth amplitude is real: the -h Fourier coefficient and phase are conjugates of their h counterparts. Every parent and marker mask is independent of the sign of h, so pairing first makes each q_z and every refined leaf real.

The marker hypotheses and squarefreeness are explicit. Fact 85e63a9328d91711 proves (3). Since w_z=mu(d)mu(r)q_z, replacing only mu(r) by (3) and using the unique parent gives (5). No part of q_z changes. Marker A and B may create several weighted factorization copies, but all inherit the original parent; retagging them is not this identity.

For C2, g divides squarefree r. Thus delta_z is an exact subset label. If it is empty, every prime factor of g lies in v, so g divides v and b=(v/g)pq=v_0pq. Equation (6), squarefreeness of b, gcd(a,b)=1, positivity of a,m,b,k,N/g, distinct p,q, and 0<h<Z_lambda<=p,q verify the normalized-incidence hypotheses of fact 7cc27e1367d85c60. On this short layer its conductor ledger says that the rough primitive denominator is pq exactly when neither p nor q divides mh, namely J_z empty. The long layer is retained separately and no nonprimitivity claim is made for it.

For the exponent statement,
beta_z=(log R/log x)/(log D/log x)=rho/(1/2+o(1))=2rho+o(1).
The upper bound rho<=2/3-epsilon gives beta_z<4/3. Thus the boundary predicate fails. If lambda is in mathcal C_91, first precedence gives C91. Otherwise the explicit nonendpoint rule gives U_sh or U_low according as D<4D_* or not.

All quantities in the final paragraph are real. Since mathcal R_comp=R_high-T_G, rearranging (8) gives (9). Under only R_high<=-A_0+epsilon_0, the largest right side of (9) is (10). Equality at R_high=-A_0+epsilon_0 proves sharpness among uniform conditions independent of the actual total. The final leaf bound is the real pigeonhole principle.

glossary.c_{lambda,X}(r): the exact marker coefficient in X=A,B,C1,C2
glossary.delta_z: the subset of the C2 rough primes absorbed by the outer gcd
glossary.mathcal G_leaf: a chosen union of refined C2 leaves
glossary.mathcal P_H: the nine frozen high parent cells
glossary.mathcal R_comp: the real signed complement of mathcal G_leaf
glossary.mathcal Z: the finite provenance-preserving h-paired Poisson atom set
glossary.q_z: the real complete h-paired atom coefficient after removing only mu(d)mu(r)

7819d8e026c08b9c.title: Let H>=2 and K be a nonzero integer. Consider the normalized unit family of fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb, with pairwise distinct odd primes r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4 in [H^2,2H^2), coefficient matrix ((a,c),(-d,b)), coupling integer C, prime product P=r_1r_2r_3r_4, and gcd(C,P)=1. For fixed b,d,r_2,r_3,C,K, there is at most one ordered pair (r_1,r_4) in [H^2,2H^2) that can occur in such a normalized state
7819d8e026c08b9c.author: slava chan
7819d8e026c08b9c.statement: Let H>=2 and K be a nonzero integer. Consider the normalized unit family of fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb, with pairwise distinct odd primes r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4 in [H^2,2H^2), coefficient matrix ((a,c),(-d,b)), coupling integer C, prime product P=r_1r_2r_3r_4, and gcd(C,P)=1. For fixed b,d,r_2,r_3,C,K, there is at most one ordered pair (r_1,r_4) in [H^2,2H^2) that can occur in such a normalized state.
7819d8e026c08b9c.proof:
Invoke fact 4832817b6b759101 and set U=(b r_3)^2+(d r_2)^2, V=b r_3+d r_2, L=2K r_2r_3, and g=gcd(U,|L|). It gives the exact identity U r_4-2CV=L r_1 and bounds the number of integer pairs (r_1,r_4) in [H^2,2H^2)^2 satisfying this identity by 1+H^2 g/max(U,|L|).

We first prove r_2 does not divide b. Suppose r_2|b. The inverse relation b r_4+c r_1=2u r_2 from fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb then implies r_2|c r_1. Since r_1 and r_2 are distinct primes, r_2|c. The coupling relation d r_2r_4-c r_1r_3=2C from the same predecessor would then imply r_2|2C. As r_2 is odd, this gives r_2|C, contradicting gcd(C,P)=1.

Similarly r_3 does not divide d. Indeed, if r_3|d, then d r_4+a r_1=2u r_3 implies r_3|a because r_1 and r_3 are distinct. The other coupling relation b r_3r_4-a r_1r_2=2C would then yield r_3|2C, hence r_3|C, again contradicting gcd(C,P)=1.

Reducing U modulo r_2 gives U congruent to (b r_3)^2 modulo r_2. This is nonzero modulo r_2 because r_2 does not divide b and r_2 is distinct from r_3. Reducing U modulo r_3 gives U congruent to (d r_2)^2 modulo r_3, which is nonzero for the analogous reason. Therefore gcd(U,r_2r_3)=1. Because L=2K r_2r_3, it follows that g=gcd(U,2|K|), so g<=2|K|.

Since max(U,|L|)>=|L|=2|K|r_2r_3, the multiplicity bound from fact 4832817b6b759101 is at most 1+H^2/(r_2r_3). The interval condition gives r_2r_3>=H^4, and H>=2, so this upper bound is strictly less than 2. The number of pairs is an integer, hence it is at most one.

787d693bb7ba13dc.title: TOP-\(B\) CLEAN-WINDOW FULL-FREQUENCY PAYMENT AND EXACT ENDPOINT-DIAGONAL COMPLEMENT
787d693bb7ba13dc.author: slava chan
787d693bb7ba13dc.statement:
TOP-\(B\) CLEAN-WINDOW FULL-FREQUENCY PAYMENT AND EXACT ENDPOINT-DIAGONAL COMPLEMENT.

Fix \(0<\kappa\le1/100\), put
\[
 \sigma=\kappa/100,\qquad \beta_m=6/5-12\sigma/5,
\]
fix \(0<\tau<3\sigma\), and let \(Q\) be sufficiently large. Let
\[
 \beta_m\le\beta<6/5,\qquad B=Q^\beta,\qquad
 H_T=B/Q,\qquad G>0,\qquad H_P=H_T/G,
\]
and
\[
 L=Q^{\beta-1+\sigma},\qquad
 S_0=Q^{2\beta-2+3\sigma},\qquad
 Z=Q^{3/2-\beta-3\sigma}.
\]
Fix one exact orientation, outer-gcd layer \(g\), selected source, parent,
fixed-\(U\), high and smooth/projective fibre from fact
\(b69e09aaac3766d9\). The fixed literal source target
\(\mathscr A\ne0\) may be nonunit modulo \(q\), and all displayed source
parameters and \(|\mathscr A|\) are bounded by a fixed power of \(Q\).

For every stopping length \(k\ge2\), dyadic stopping scales \(U,Y\) and
dyadic integer-frequency scale \(F\ge1\), retain the literal recombined
top-\(B\) contribution
\[
 \mathcal T^{(k)}_{B,F}(U,Y)
 ={\omega_F\over H_P}
 \sum_{\substack{q\asymp Q,\ F\le |h|<2F\\
                  u\asymp U,\ y\asymp Y\\
                  (uy,q)=(u,y)=1}}
 a_qb_h\alpha_k(u)\gamma_k(y)
 \Psi_F(q/Q,|h|/F,u/U,y/Y)
 e_q\!\left(-\mathscr A h(uy)^{-1}\right),                 \tag{1}
\]
where
\[
 \alpha_k(u)=
 {(-1)^k\mu(u)1_{j_{(L,Z)}(u)=0}\over {k+\omega_L(u)\choose k}},
 \qquad \gamma_k(y)=\Gamma_{k;L,S_0}(y),                    \tag{2}
\]
both signs of \(h\) occur, \(a_q,b_h\) are divisor-bounded, and
\(\Psi_F\) has uniformly bounded projective Fourier norm. Every
target-gcd, order/equal-cell, collision, deletion and provenance descendant
belonging to the fixed fibre is recombined inside (1); the orientation,
outer \(g\), selected source, parent, fixed-\(U\), high and provenance
coordinates remain frozen label scalars and are not discarded. The
frequency scalars satisfy, for every fixed \(J_0\ge1\),
\[
 |\omega_F|\ll_{J_0}\min\{1,(F/H_P)^{-J_0}\}.               \tag{3}
\]
There is a fixed \(C_B\ge1\) such that every nonempty cell satisfies
\[
 C_B^{-1}B\le UY\le C_BB,                                  \tag{4}
\]
and every supported \(y\) satisfies
\[
 S_0<y\le S_0L.                                             \tag{5}
\]

Call a cell clean if at least one of \(U,Y\), denoted by \(S\), satisfies
\[
 H_T^2Q^\tau\le S\le {Q^{1-\tau}\over H_T^2}.               \tag{6}
\]
Let \(\mathcal T_{B,\mathrm{clean}}\) be the sum of (1) over all nonempty
clean \(k,U,Y,F\) cells of this fixed literal fibre. Then there is a fixed
\(\delta_B>0\) such that
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 |\mathcal T_{B,\mathrm{clean}}|
 \ll \max(1,G)Q^{2-\delta_B}.
 \quad}                                                     \tag{7}
\]
This includes every actual nonzero integer frequency, both signs of \(h\),
and the subunit regime \(H_P<1\).

Moreover, for all sufficiently large \(Q\), both \(U\) and \(Y\) in every
nonempty top-\(B\) cell lie above the lower face in (6). Consequently the
exact complementary contribution is
\[
 \mathcal T_{B,\mathrm{end}}
 =
 \sum_{\substack{k,U,Y,F\ {\rm nonempty}\\
 U>Q^{1-\tau}/H_T^2,\quad
 Y>Q^{1-\tau}/H_T^2}}
 \mathcal T^{(k)}_{B,F}(U,Y).                               \tag{8}
\]
Thus, within the fixed fibre,
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \mathcal T_B=\mathcal T_{B,\mathrm{clean}}
              +\mathcal T_{B,\mathrm{end}},
 \quad}                                                     \tag{9}
\]
where (8), and only (8), is ENDPOINT-DIAGONAL-\(B\).
It can be nonempty only if
\[
 \beta>{6\over5}-{2\tau\over5}
       -{\log C_B\over5\log Q}.                             \tag{10}
\]
No estimate for \(\mathcal T_{B,\mathrm{end}}\), no summation over distinct
outer-\(g\) or source fibres, no other anatomy, no post-\(A\) tail estimate,
and no Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
787d693bb7ba13dc.proof:
Fact \(b69e09aaac3766d9\) gives (1)--(2) exactly on every
natural-frequency block, after the named auxiliary descendants are
recombined before any absolute value. It also gives the bounded projective
expansion of \(\Psi_F\), the divisor bounds, both frequency signs, the
literal possibly nonunit target, and the two coprimality conditions.
The fixed orientation, outer \(g\), source, parent, fixed-\(U\), high and
provenance data are explicitly label scalars in that fact.

We first record why the same representation is legitimate on every actual
dyadic integer-frequency block. In the smooth Poisson formula used in fact
\(b69e09aaac3766d9\), the Fourier variable has natural scale \(H_P\).
On a block \(F\le |h|<2F\), integrate the defining compactly supported
smooth Fourier integral by parts an arbitrary prescribed number of times.
This contributes
\[
 (1+F/H_P)^{-J}.
\]
Scaled differentiation of the remaining source amplitude and of the
Archimedean reciprocity factor costs at most a fixed polynomial in
\(1+F/H_P\): the latter phase has size \(O(F/H_P)\), because the physical
balances used in the proof of fact \(b69e09aaac3766d9\) give
\(|\mathscr A|H_P/(QB)=O(1)\). Choose the number of integrations larger
than that fixed derivative loss plus \(J_0\). Smooth Fourier separation on
the fixed scaled rectangle then gives a uniformly bounded projective norm
and leaves the scalar bound (3). This is the same repeated-integration
mechanism used for actual frequencies in fact \(df9748efe29ab475\).
Thus no integer-frequency block is omitted from (1).

Fix one clean cell and choose \(S\in\{U,Y\}\) satisfying (6), calling the
other factor \(T\). Expand \(\Psi_F\) projectively. In each separated mode,
the \(S\)- and \(T\)-coefficients are divisor-bounded, the \(q\)-factor may
be placed outside the \(q\)-wise absolute value at a divisor loss, and the
\(h\)-coefficient inherits (3). The relation (4) is
\[
 ST\asymp B=QH_T.
\]
Therefore every mode has exactly the input form of fact
\(f7b5ba9fa0d6cfc8\), with \(V_q=1\), fixed target
\(A=-\mathscr A\), and the allowed optional condition \((S,T)=1\).
Neither that fact nor its clean-window predecessor
\(2b4989d9d25f33cc\) requires \((\mathscr A,q)=1\) or \((h,q)=1\).

Suppose first that \(H_P\ge1\). Fact \(f7b5ba9fa0d6cfc8\), followed by
(6), bounds its four terms by
\[
 G^{1/4}Q^{2-\tau/4},\qquad
 G^{1/4}Q^{2-\tau/4},\qquad
 Q^{2-\tau/2},\qquad
 Q^{7/4}H_T.                                                 \tag{11}
\]
Indeed the first three inequalities are precisely the clean-window
simplification in fact \(2b4989d9d25f33cc\), and
\[
 Q^{7/4}H_T=Q^{\beta+3/4}\le Q^{2-1/20}
\]
because \(\beta<6/5\). If \(0<G\le1\), then \(G^{1/4}\le1\); if \(G\ge1\),
then \(G^{1/4}\le G\). Hence (11) is
\[
 \ll \max(1,G)Q^{2-\delta_0}
\]
after choosing the theorem epsilon sufficiently small, where
\(\delta_0>0\) depends only on \(\tau\) and the fixed polynomial bounds.

If \(H_P<1\), then \(H_T=Q^{\beta-1}>1\), so
\(G=H_T/H_P>1\). Apply the accepted reset fact
\(07bfa46055824600\) to each projective mode. Its clean-window conclusion
is
\[
 \ll GQ^{2-\delta_1}
 =\max(1,G)Q^{2-\delta_1}.                                   \tag{12}
\]
The exact coefficient rescaling in that fact preserves the literal
prefactor \(H_P^{-1}\), so (12) does not invoke the energy theorem at a
subunit parameter.

The projective \(\ell^1\)-norm is uniformly bounded on each \(F\)-block.
The dyadic sum of (3) is \(O(\log(2+H_P))\): there are only logarithmically
many blocks with \(F\le H_P\), and the blocks with \(F>H_P\) form a
convergent geometric tail after fixing \(J_0>1\). The stopping length and
the \(U,Y\) decompositions have only polylogarithmic multiplicity; indeed
\(\gamma_k(y)\ne0\) forces \(y\) squarefree with \(\omega(y)=k\), so
\(k=O(\log Q)\). Absorb all such factors and the divisor losses by reducing
\(\min(\delta_0,\delta_1)\). This proves (7).

It remains to identify the complement exactly. From (5), a supported
\(y\in[Y,2Y)\) gives
\[
 Y>S_0/2={1\over2}H_T^2Q^{3\sigma}.
\]
Since \(\tau<3\sigma\), for sufficiently large \(Q\),
\[
 Y\ge H_T^2Q^\tau.                                           \tag{13}
\]
Also \(Y\le S_0L\), and (4) gives
\[
 U\ge C_B^{-1}{B\over Y}
 \ge C_B^{-1}{B\over S_0L}
 =C_B^{-1}Q^{3-2\beta-4\sigma}.                              \tag{14}
\]
The ratio of the last quantity to \(H_T^2Q^\tau\) is
\[
 C_B^{-1}Q^{5-4\beta-4\sigma-\tau}.
\]
Since \(\beta<6/5\), \(\tau<3\sigma\), and
\(\sigma\le1/10000\), its exponent is larger than
\(1/5-7\sigma>0\). Hence, for sufficiently large \(Q\),
\[
 U\ge H_T^2Q^\tau.                                           \tag{15}
\]
Equations (13)--(15) show that neither factor can fail (6) through its
lower face. A cell is therefore nonclean if and only if both factors exceed
the upper face, which proves (8)--(9).

Finally, if (8) is nonempty, then
\[
 UY>{Q^{2-2\tau}\over H_T^4}
   =Q^{6-4\beta-2\tau}.
\]
Together with \(UY\le C_BQ^\beta\), this implies
\[
 Q^{6-5\beta-2\tau}<C_B.
\]
Taking logarithms and rearranging gives (10). This locates the exact
complement without assigning it any analytic estimate.

glossary.ENDPOINT-DIAGONAL-B: The exact set of top-B stopping cells with U>Q^{1-\tau}/H_T^2 and Y>Q^{1-\tau}/H_T^2.
glossary.\\mathcal T_{B,\\mathrm{clean}}: The sum of the literal recombined top-B stopping cells for which at least one of U,Y lies in the displayed reciprocal-energy window.
glossary.\\mathcal T_{B,\\mathrm{end}}: The exact complementary top-B sum over cells for which both U and Y exceed the upper face of that window.

79e2c44e5110d7a0.title: EXACT SLOPE-CLASS DIAGONALIZATION OF THE PRIME-LOCAL MIXED-MODE ENERGY
