79e2c44e5110d7a0.statement:
EXACT SLOPE-CLASS DIAGONALIZATION OF THE PRIME-LOCAL MIXED-MODE ENERGY.

Let (p) be a prime and let (mathcal J) be a finite index set. For every (jinmathcal J), choose nonzero residues
[
 h_j,c_jinmathbb F_p^	imes
]
and a complex coefficient (a_j). Put
[
 s_j=h_jc_j^{-1}inmathbb F_p^	imes.
]
Define
[
 g_j(x)=
  egin{cases}
 e_p(s_jx^{-1}),&x
e0,\
 0,&x=0,
 end{cases}
]
[
 widehat g_j(r)={1over p}sum_{xinmathbb F_p}g_j(x)e_p(-rx),
]
and for each slope (sinmathbb F_p^	imes) put
[
 A_s=sum_{substack{jinmathcal J\s_j=s}}a_j.
]
Then
[
 sum_{r
e0}left|sum_{jinmathcal J}a_jwidehat g_j(r)ight|^2
 =
 sum_{sinmathbb F_p^	imes}|A_s|^2
 -left({1over p}+{1over p^2}ight)
 left|sum_{sinmathbb F_p^	imes}A_sight|^2,             	ag{1}
]
and
[
 sum_{rinmathbb F_p}left|sum_{jinmathcal J}
 a_jwidehat g_j(r)ight|^2
 =
 sum_s|A_s|^2-{1over p}left|sum_sA_sight|^2.            	ag{2}
]
In particular,
[
 sum_{r
e0}left|sum_j a_jwidehat g_j(r)ight|^2
 lesum_s|A_s|^2,                                           	ag{3}
]
but there is no universal extra factor (p^{-1}) relative to the slope-class energy. For one nonzero coefficient, the left side of (1) is
[
 |a_j|^2left((p-1)/p-p^{-2}ight).
]

Under the first-nonresonant-prime specialization of fact (3d10fd30e2a42246), allow each row (j) to have its own factorization
[
 d_j=pm_j,qquad n_j=d_jv_j.
]
The local slope is
[
 s_j=h_j(v_jm_j)^{-1}pmod p
]
up to the common nonzero target factor. Thus two literal rows lie in the same slope class exactly when
[
 h_j(v_km_k)equiv h_k(v_jm_j)pmod p.                        	ag{4}
]
Prime-local completion therefore converts the mixed NR-DIL problem exactly into control of literal sums inside the collision classes (4). It does not itself supply a full (p^{-1}) gain. No estimate for those literal slope-class sums, iteration over other primes of the canonical dilator, or NR-DIL conclusion is asserted.
79e2c44e5110d7a0.proof:
Fact (3d10fd30e2a42246) gives
[
 sum_{r
e0}widehat g_j(r)overline{widehat g_k(r)}
 =
  egin{cases}
 a_0,&s_j=s_k,\
 b_0,&s_j
e s_k,
 end{cases}
]
where
[
 a_0={p-1over p}-{1over p^2},qquad
 b_0=-{1over p}-{1over p^2}.
]
Expand the left side of (1) and group pairs by slopes. The same-slope contribution is
[
 a_0sum_s|A_s|^2,
]
while the different-slope contribution is
[
 b_0left(left|sum_sA_sight|^2-sum_s|A_s|^2ight).
]
Since (a_0-b_0=1), their sum is exactly (1).

Every zero Fourier mode is (-1/p) by fact (4f9aec67f5be35db), so the (r=0) energy of the combined row is
[
 p^{-2}left|sum_j a_jight|^2
 =p^{-2}left|sum_sA_sight|^2.
]
Adding this to (1) proves (2). Formula (3) follows by dropping the nonnegative subtracted term. For one index, (1) gives the displayed order-one value.

For the source specialization, fact (3d10fd30e2a42246) gives on row (j) the local phase parameter
[
 mathscr A h_j(v_jm_j)^{-1}.
]
The target (mathscr A) is a common unit modulo the selected prime and does not affect slope equality. Two slopes are equal precisely when
[
 h_j(v_jm_j)^{-1}=h_k(v_km_k)^{-1}pmod p.
]
Multiplication by the units ((v_jm_j)(v_km_k)) gives (4). The final scope assertions follow because (1)-(2) are finite-field identities only.

glossary.prime-local mixed-mode energy: The squared l2 norm over nonzero additive Fourier modes after completing the inverse phase at p.
glossary.slope-class amplitude: The coefficient sum over rows having the same residue h/c modulo p.

79eb78ffa67de31c.title: Fix real numbers D_*≥1, 0<κ<1/6, and 0<η<κ/20. Let 𝒵_U be a finite set of tuples
79eb78ffa67de31c.author: slava chan
79eb78ffa67de31c.statement:
Fix real numbers D_*≥1, 0<κ<1/6, and 0<η<κ/20. Let 𝒵_U be a finite set of tuples
z=(D,M,R,K;d,m,r,k),
where D,M,R,K are positive dyadic real numbers and d,m,r,k are positive integers, and attach an arbitrary real weight w(z) to each tuple.

For z with D,R≥4D_*, define its large-divisor orientation as follows: if R>D, use base scale Q_z=D, large divisor n_z=r, and exponent β_z=log(R)/log(D); if D>R, use Q_z=R, n_z=d, and β_z=log(D)/log(R); if D=R, use Q_z=D, n_z=d, and β_z=1. Call z boundary-admissible if D,R≥4D_*, 4/3≤β_z≤3/2-κ, and there is a divisor y of n_z such that, with t=n_z/y,
y≤t and Q_z^(2-β_z-3η)≤y,t≤Q_z^(2(β_z-1)+3η).
Assume that no element of 𝒵_U is boundary-admissible, and define U=Σ_{z∈𝒵_U}w(z).

Partition 𝒵_U into four classes:
𝒵_sh={z:min(D,R)<4D_*};
𝒵_low={z:D,R≥4D_* and β_z<4/3};
𝒵_gap={z:D,R≥4D_* and 4/3≤β_z≤3/2-κ};
𝒵_sup={z:D,R≥4D_* and β_z>3/2-κ}.
Let U^sh,U^low,U^gap,U^sup be the sums of w(z) over these four classes. Then
U=U^sh+U^low+U^gap+U^sup
exactly and disjointly. Every z∈𝒵_gap has no factor pair satisfying the displayed boundary inequalities, while 𝒵_sup is the explicit bi-deep band beyond the endpoint exponent 3/2-κ.

This partition applies in particular whenever 𝒵_U is chosen to be the weighted nonendpoint incidence set produced by an exact prior C/E/U selector: it uses only the tuple and its unchanged weight and therefore introduces no absolute value or sign change.

Separately, let p and ℓ be distinct primes with p>ℓ^3, q=pℓ, and Q=(pℓ)^(1/2). The divisor scales 1 and ℓ are below Q^(1/2), while p and q are above Q^(3/2), and the three nonzero quantities log(pℓ), -log ℓ, -log p sum to zero. Thus this semiprime gives a general caution that divisor support alone does not force a sibling into an intermediate endpoint interval and that isolated nonzero siblings need not represent nonzero complete von-Mangoldt mass. No assertion is made that this semiprime configuration belongs to 𝒵_sup.
79eb78ffa67de31c.proof:
Every z∈𝒵_U either satisfies min(D,R)<4D_* or satisfies D,R≥4D_*. In the latter case Q_z≥4D_*>1 and β_z is well defined in all three branches, including D=R. Exactly one of
β_z<4/3,
4/3≤β_z≤3/2-κ,
β_z>3/2-κ
holds. These alternatives are pairwise disjoint and exhaustive. Together with the shallow alternative they prove that the four displayed sets form a partition of 𝒵_U. Multiplying the pointwise partition identity by the arbitrary real weight w(z) and summing gives U=U^sh+U^low+U^gap+U^sup without modifying any weight.

If z∈𝒵_gap had a divisor y satisfying the displayed inequalities, it would be boundary-admissible by definition, contrary to the standing assumption on 𝒵_U. The description of 𝒵_sup is exactly its defining inequality. Because no property of w(z) was used, the construction can be applied to any previously obtained nonendpoint weighted incidence set, including weights containing Möbius signs and auxiliary masks.

For the separate semiprime caution, fact d9eb8f470bce53ac proves the inequalities 1,ℓ<Q^(1/2)<Q^(3/2)<p,q under p>ℓ^3. It also computes the four divisor-sibling summands as log(pℓ), -log ℓ, -log p, and 0. The three nonzero terms sum to zero, so omitting the zero sibling changes nothing; accordingly the conclusion is stated only as a failure of support-only intermediate localization and of identifying isolated nonzero siblings with complete nonzero mass. No bridge to 𝒵_sup is claimed.

glossary.Q_z: the smaller divisor scale in the large-divisor orientation of z, with Q_z=D when D=R
glossary.U: the total signed weight of 𝒵_U
glossary.n_z: the integer divisor variable in the large-divisor orientation of z, with n_z=d when D=R
glossary.β_z: the logarithmic ratio of the larger divisor scale to Q_z, set equal to 1 when D=R
glossary.𝒵_U: a finite weighted nonendpoint incidence set
glossary.𝒵_gap: the bi-deep endpoint-ratio class without an admissible boundary pair
glossary.𝒵_low: the bi-deep class below endpoint ratio 4/3

79ffbcb2ffe4049f.title: EXACT COMPOSITE-RECIPROCAL PHASE IN THE CANONICAL C1 ROW AND THE RESIDUE-CLASS BV NO-FIT. Adopt one actual strict-top C1 copy in the canonical row of fact 41b56ed8e64bdba6. Thus n=pv, where p is the unique rough prime in the canonical dilator d_lambda=p, v=n/p, (p,v)=1, and every supported q is coprime to n. Let c_lambda(q,h) be the pre-reciprocity coefficient and widetilde c_lambda(q,h) the post-reciprocity coefficient of that fact. Then the exact row identity is
79ffbcb2ffe4049f.author: slava chan
79ffbcb2ffe4049f.statement:
EXACT COMPOSITE-RECIPROCAL PHASE IN THE CANONICAL C1 ROW AND THE RESIDUE-CLASS BV NO-FIT. Adopt one actual strict-top C1 copy in the canonical row of fact 41b56ed8e64bdba6. Thus n=pv, where p is the unique rough prime in the canonical dilator d_lambda=p, v=n/p, (p,v)=1, and every supported q is coprime to n. Let c_lambda(q,h) be the pre-reciprocity coefficient and widetilde c_lambda(q,h) the post-reciprocity coefficient of that fact. Then the exact row identity is
c_lambda(q,h)e_q(-mathscr A h n^(-1))
 =c_lambda(q,h)e(-mathscr A h/(qn))e_n(mathscr A h q^(-1))
 =widetilde c_lambda(q,h)e_p(mathscr A h(qv)^(-1)),
where
widetilde c_lambda(q,h)=c_lambda(q,h)e(-mathscr A h/(qn))e_v(mathscr A h(qp)^(-1)).
Therefore, after inserting one separated mode from facts ff228b0e569531f8 and 71f1a10b52148348, the literal canonical C1 one-row q-sum has the form
kappa(n,h) sum_{Q<=q<2Q} mu(q)1_{(q,gn)=1}A(q)e(-mathscr A h/(qn))e_n(mathscr A hq^(-1)).
The selected-prime determinant mask remains a two-row condition at p; it does not remove the residual v-part of the composite reciprocal phase.

The prime-modulus theorem c23ca78883ba83d9 does not directly estimate this sum when v>1. Indeed, on q coprime to v one has the exact residue decomposition
e_v(Cq^(-1))=sum_{a mod v,(a,v)=1}e_v(Ca^(-1))1_{q=a mod v}.
For every A supported on [Q,2Q),
sum_{a mod v,(a,v)=1} V_Q(A(q)1_{q=a mod v}) << V_Q(A)(Q+v).
Thus applying c23ca78883ba83d9 separately to these progression pieces incurs the bound
<<V_Q(A)(Q+v)Q^(1-delta_0),
which is larger than the trivial QV_Q(A) scale and gives no power saving. This is a no-fit of the residue-class BV lifting method, not a lower bound for the literal composite-phase sum.

A sufficient new one-row supplier is a uniform estimate
|sum_{Q<=q<2Q}mu(q)1_{(q,c)=1}A(q)e(-C_0/(qn))e_n(Cq^(-1))| <<V_Q(A)Q^(1-delta_comp)
for the actual squarefree n=pv, with p>=Q^zeta, n<=Q^C, the actual possibly nonunit C modulo v but nonzero p-component, polynomial auxiliary squarefree c, and all actual C1 ranges of v,h and outer labels. No such composite-modulus Mobius estimate is asserted here.
79ffbcb2ffe4049f.proof:
The first equality is elementary additive reciprocity: for (q,n)=1,
e_q(-mathscr A h n^(-1))=e(-mathscr A h/(qn))e_n(mathscr A hq^(-1)).
Since n=pv and (p,v)=1, the Chinese remainder identity gives
e_n(mathscr A hq^(-1))=e_p(mathscr A h(qv)^(-1))e_v(mathscr A h(qp)^(-1)).
Substituting the definition of widetilde c_lambda from fact 41b56ed8e64bdba6 proves all three equal expressions.

Facts ff228b0e569531f8 and 71f1a10b52148348 expand c_lambda(q,h), before the reciprocal phase, into modes kappa(n,h)mu(q)1_{(q,gn)=1}A(q) with variation-weighted coefficient mass. Multiplying one mode by the exact reciprocity identity gives the displayed literal composite-phase sum. The first-nonresonant mask is defined from the p-divisibility of the two-row determinant, while the v-character is present in each one-row identity; therefore selection at p does not delete it.

For the residue decomposition, every supported q has a unique unit residue a modulo v, and q^(-1)=a^(-1) modulo v, proving the identity. Fix a. The function A(q)1_{q=a mod v} has supremum at most V_Q(A). If v>=2, consecutive integers cannot both lie in the same residue class, so each retained point contributes at most two jumps, each at most V_Q(A); the progression has at most 1+Q/v points in [Q,2Q). Hence
V_Q(A1_{q=a mod v})<=V_Q(A){1+2(1+Q/v)}.
For v=1 the bound is immediate. Summing over at most v unit residues gives O(V_Q(A)(v+Q)). Applying fact c23ca78883ba83d9 to each progression amplitude and summing absolute values proves the displayed method bound. Since Q+v>=Q, it is at least of order Q^(2-delta_0)V_Q(A), so this argument is not nontrivial relative to QV_Q(A). The final displayed composite estimate would apply directly to every separated literal mode and is therefore sufficient as a one-row replacement; it is explicitly left unproved.

glossary.composite canonical C1 phase: The exact reciprocal additive character e_n(mathscr A hq^{-1}) with n=pv in the post-reciprocity C1 row.
glossary.delta_comp: A hypothetical positive saving exponent for the squarefree-composite Mobius reciprocal-phase estimate.
glossary.residue-class BV lifting: Decomposition of the v-modulus reciprocal phase into sharp progression indicators before applying the prime-p theorem.

7a161d479c94ccb0.title: Fix a target A>0, real numbers 1/2<a<b<1, a continuously differentiable real function W supported in [a,b], and a continuously differentiable real function ψ on the positive reals with 0≤ψ≤1, ψ(u)=0 for 0<u≤1, and ψ(u)=1 for u≥2. There exists B=B(A,W,ψ)>0 such that the following holds uniformly for even integers N=2x as x tends to infinity. Put D_*=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B), define
7a161d479c94ccb0.author: slava chan
7a161d479c94ccb0.statement:
Fix a target A>0, real numbers 1/2<a<b<1, a continuously differentiable real function W supported in [a,b], and a continuously differentiable real function ψ on the positive reals with 0≤ψ≤1, ψ(u)=0 for 0<u≤1, and ψ(u)=1 for u≥2. There exists B=B(A,W,ψ)>0 such that the following holds uniformly for even integers N=2x as x tends to infinity. Put D_*=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B), define
C_2=∏_{p>2}p(p-2)/(p-1)^2, 𝔠(N)=C_2∏_{p|N,p>2}(p-1)/(p-2), Q_N=rad(2N),
r_N(n)=1_{gcd(n,Q_N)=1}∏_{p|n,p∤Q_N}(p-1)/(p-2), and b_N(n)=2𝔠(N)r_N(n).
Then the small-divisor reflected discrepancy
E_{sh,N}=Σ_{d,m≥1;d≥2}μ(d)log(m)W(dm/x)(1-ψ(d/D_*))(Λ(N-dm)-b_N(dm))
satisfies
E_{sh,N}≪_{A,W,ψ}𝔠(N)x(log x)^(-A).
7a161d479c94ccb0.proof:
We use Sedunova's maximal Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem, arXiv:1705.06660, stated as follows: for every L>0 there exists B_0=B_0(L)>0 such that, for Q≤x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B_0),
Σ_{q≤Q} max_{2≤y≤x} max_{gcd(c,q)=1}|ψ_AP(y;q,c)-y/φ(q)|≪_L x(log x)^(-L),       (1)
where ψ_AP(y;q,c)=Σ_{n≤y,n≡c (mod q)}Λ(n). Choose L larger than A by a fixed amount, and then choose B>B_0(L) sufficiently large that 2D_*≤2x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B)≤(2x)^(1/2)(log(2x))^(-B_0(L)) for all sufficiently large x.

Put χ_d=1-ψ(d/D_*). Then |χ_d|≤1 and χ_d=0 for d≥2D_*. Since μ(d)=0 unless d is squarefree, only squarefree d≤2D_* occur. Split them according as gcd(d,N)>1 or gcd(d,N)=1.

If gcd(d,N)>1, then b_N(dm)=0 for every m because a prime dividing gcd(d,N) divides both Q_N and dm. If Λ(N-dm) is nonzero, q=N-dm is a prime power. Also gcd(d,N) divides q. Since d is squarefree, this is possible only when every prime in gcd(d,N) is the single underlying prime of q. For each d there are at most log_2(2N) possible exponents, and each summand has absolute value O_W((log N)^2). Hence the total contribution of all noncoprime d is
O_W(D_*(log N)^3)=O_{A,W}(x^(1/2)(log x)^(3-B))=o_A(x(log x)^(-A)).              (2)
Fact f41f5f91b52e0d13 gives 𝔠(N)≥C_2>0, so (2) is also o_A(𝔠(N)x(log x)^(-A)).

Now let gcd(d,N)=1. Then gcd(d,Q_N)=1. Define X=x/d and a multiplicative function R_{N,d} by
R_{N,d}(p^j)=0 if p|Q_N,
R_{N,d}(p^j)=1 if p|d,
and R_{N,d}(p^j)=(p-1)/(p-2) if p∤Q_Nd.
For every m one has r_N(dm)=r_N(d)R_{N,d}(m). Define h_{N,d}, supported on squarefree integers, by h_{N,d}(p)=-1 for p|Q_N, h_{N,d}(p)=0 for p|d, and h_{N,d}(p)=1/(p-2) otherwise. Then
R_{N,d}(m)=Σ_{e|m}h_{N,d}(e).                                             (3)
Its mean Euler product is
κ_{N,d}=Σ_e h_{N,d}(e)/e
=∏_{p|Q_N}(1-1/p)∏_{p∤Q_Nd}(1+1/[p(p-2)]).
Fact f41f5f91b52e0d13 computes κ_N=∏_{p|Q_N}(1-1/p)∏_{p∤Q_N}(1+1/[p(p-2)])=1/[2𝔠(N)]. Removing from κ_N the local factor (p-1)^2/[p(p-2)] for every p|d, and using r_N(d)=∏_{p|d}(p-1)/(p-2), gives the exact normalization
2𝔠(N)r_N(d)κ_{N,d}=∏_{p|d}p/(p-1)=d/φ(d).                               (4)

We also need a uniform weighted mean estimate. Exactly as in the Euler-product bound in fact f41f5f91b52e0d13, for σ=3/4,
Σ_e |h_{N,d}(e)|e^(-3/4)≤exp(O((log N)^(1/4)))=N^{o(1)},                 (5)
uniformly in d, because setting h_{N,d}(p)=0 at p|d only decreases the absolute Euler product. Insert (3) into the sum over m with F_X(m)=log(m)W(m/X). A Riemann-sum estimate, (5), and the tail inequality
Σ_{e>X}|h_{N,d}(e)|/e≤X^(-1/4)Σ_e|h_{N,d}(e)|e^(-3/4)
then give
Σ_m R_{N,d}(m)log(m)W(m/X)
=κ_{N,d}X∫_0^∞log(Xu)W(u)du+O_W(X^(3/4)N^{o(1)}log x).                    (6)
Here X=x/d≥x/(2D_*)=x^(1/2)(log x)^B/2, so the estimates are uniform.

Multiplying (6) by 2𝔠(N)r_N(d), using (4), multiplying by μ(d)χ_d, and summing d≤2D_*, the aggregate baseline error is at most
𝔠(N)x^(3/4+o(1))Σ_{d≤2D_*}τ(d)d^(-3/4)log x.
Since Σ_{d≤Y}τ(d)/d≤(1+log Y)^2, the last sum is at most Y^(1/4)(1+log Y)^2. With Y=2D_*≤2x^(1/2), the baseline error is
𝔠(N)x^(7/8+o(1)}=o_A(𝔠(N)x(log x)^(-A)).                                (7)
Thus the baseline for each coprime d has main term
(d/φ(d))X∫_0^∞log(Xu)W(u)du.                                             (8)

For the reflected prime sum at the same d, write q=N-dm. Partial summation expresses
Σ_m log(m)W(dm/x)Λ(N-dm)
minus the main term in (8) as a Stieltjes integral against
ψ_AP(y;d,N)-y/φ(d).
The weight has supremum and total variation O_W(log x), because m is restricted by W to aX≤dm≤bX and hence m is bounded away from zero. Therefore its absolute value is at most
O_W(log x) max_{2≤y≤2x}|ψ_AP(y;d,N)-y/φ(d)|.                             (9)
The residue N is reduced modulo d because gcd(d,N)=1. Summing (9) over d≤2D_* and applying (1) with 2x in place of x gives O_{L,W}(x(log x)^(-L+1)). Choose L≥A+3. Combining this with (2) and (7), and using 𝔠(N)≥C_2 to write the prime-progression error relative to 𝔠(N)x, proves the stated bound.

glossary.W: a continuously differentiable weight supported in [a,b]
glossary.h_{N,d}(e): the squarefree convolution coefficient for R_{N,d}
glossary.r_N(n): the local-density weight defined in the statement
glossary.ψ: a continuously differentiable cutoff from zero to one
glossary.ψ_AP(y;q,c): the von-Mangoldt summatory function in the residue class c modulo q
glossary.𝔠(N): the Goldbach singular factor defined in the statement

7a5079a9f524eb92.title: PRODUCT-BV BILINEAR PAYMENT FOR A SQUARE-ROOT ULTRA-NEAR-PRIME RECIPROCAL CELL. Fix K_0>=1 and 0<=theta<7/384. Let Q be sufficiently large. Let p be prime and r a positive squarefree integer satisfying gcd(p,r)=1, Q/2<=pr<=2Q, and r<=Q^theta. Let C be an integer with gcd(C,pr)=1, and let c be a positive squarefree integer with c<=Q^K_0. Let I_i=[U_i,2U_i) intersect Z for i=1,2, where Q^(1/2)/4<=U_i<=4Q^(1/2). Let W be extended by zero, supported on Q<=k<2Q, and satisfy V_Q(W)<=Q^epsilon for every fixed epsilon>0. Then
7a5079a9f524eb92.author: slava chan
7a5079a9f524eb92.statement:
PRODUCT-BV BILINEAR PAYMENT FOR A SQUARE-ROOT ULTRA-NEAR-PRIME RECIPROCAL CELL. Fix K_0>=1 and 0<=theta<7/384. Let Q be sufficiently large. Let p be prime and r a positive squarefree integer satisfying gcd(p,r)=1, Q/2<=pr<=2Q, and r<=Q^theta. Let C be an integer with gcd(C,pr)=1, and let c be a positive squarefree integer with c<=Q^K_0. Let I_i=[U_i,2U_i) intersect Z for i=1,2, where Q^(1/2)/4<=U_i<=4Q^(1/2). Let W be extended by zero, supported on Q<=k<2Q, and satisfy V_Q(W)<=Q^epsilon for every fixed epsilon>0. Then
S=sum_{u_1 in I_1,u_2 in I_2;gcd(u_1u_2,cpr)=1}W(u_1u_2)e_{pr}(C(u_1u_2)^(-1))
satisfies |S|<=Q^(1-7/384+theta+o(1)). The inverse in the phase is taken modulo pr. The o(1) is uniform in all displayed data with K_0 and theta fixed. In particular, for theta=1/100, |S|<=Q^(1-79/9600+o(1)), so the cell has a fixed-power saving. The bound retains the full product-BV weight and every displayed unit and auxiliary coprimality gate.
7a5079a9f524eb92.proof:
Partition each real dyadic interval [U_i,2U_i) into two half-open multiplicative intervals, [U_i,sqrt(2)U_i) and [sqrt(2)U_i,2U_i). This creates four integer subrectangles. Discard a subrectangle if none of its products lies in [Q,2Q), because W vanishes there. On every retained subrectangle, the ratio of the largest possible product to the smallest is at most two. Since it meets [Q,2Q), its entire product range lies in [Q/2,4Q], hence in [Q/4,4Q]. Each side length is a fixed positive multiple of U_i and is therefore comparable to Q^(1/2). It is enough to prove the asserted bound on one retained subrectangle and sum four bounds.

Apply fact e446377f3ab5a559 with a parameter A so large that its aggregate remainder over the retained rectangle is O(Q^(-10)). It writes W(u_1u_2) on the entire rectangle, including its zero values outside [Q,2Q), as a superposition of products f_tau(u_1)g_tau(u_2), where |f_tau|,|g_tau|<=1 and the total absolute coefficient mass is at most V_Q(W)log Q times an A-dependent constant, hence Q^o(1). The pointwise remainder summed over O(Q) pairs is power-small. The gate gcd(u_1u_2,cpr)=1 is the product of the two one-variable gates gcd(u_i,cpr)=1, so it is absorbed into f_tau and g_tau. Thus it suffices to bound one separated tensor with bounded coefficients.

We record the external input. Kerr--Shparlinski--Wu--Xi, arXiv:2204.05038, Theorem 2.5 states that if p is prime, s is a fixed positive integer, mathcal M is an arbitrary subset of F_p of cardinality M, mathcal K is an interval in F_p^* of length K>=p^(1/s), alpha_m and gamma_k are arbitrary bounded separated coefficients, and A_0 is a unit modulo p, then
|sum_{m in mathcal M}sum_{k in mathcal K}alpha_m gamma_k e_p(A_0 m k^(-1))|
<=M K p^o(1)[1/M+p^(1+1/s)/(M K^2)]^(7/(24s))
up to a fixed implied constant. We use s=4. The source proof decomposes the arbitrary set by additive energy, applies the Vinogradov shift to the interval variable, and uses Holder together with a 2s-th reciprocal rational-function moment. Its coefficients are precisely separated as above.

We split the CRT phase. If r>1, let r_p^(-1) be the inverse of r modulo p and p_r^(-1) the inverse of p modulo r. For z=u_1u_2,
e_{pr}(Cz^(-1))=e_p(Cr_p^(-1)z^(-1))e_r(Cp_r^(-1)z^(-1)).
Split u_2 according to its unit residue a modulo r. There are at most r classes. On one class the second factor is e_r(Cp_r^(-1)a^(-1)u_1^(-1)), a bounded one-variable coefficient in u_1; the residue indicator is a bounded coefficient in u_2. When r=1, omit the second factor and use one class.

For one class, map u_1 to m=u_1^(-1) modulo p and put k=u_2. Since p>=Q^(1-theta)/2 and theta<7/384<1/2, all four subinterval endpoints are below p for sufficiently large Q. Hence the u_2 subinterval is an interval in F_p^*, and inversion maps the permitted u_1 values injectively to an arbitrary set mathcal M.

Let M be its cardinality and put t=rad(cpr). Inclusion-exclusion on the u_1 subinterval gives M=length times phi(t)/t+O(tau(t)). Since t<=Q^(K_0+3), the elementary uniform estimates phi(t)/t=Q^(-o(1)) and tau(t)=Q^o(1) imply M=Q^(1/2+o(1)) and M>=Q^(1/2-o(1)). The u_2 subinterval length K is comparable to Q^(1/2), so K>=p^(1/4). The p-phase is exactly e_p(A_0 m k^(-1)) with the unit A_0=Cr_p^(-1) modulo p.

With s=4, M=Q^(1/2+o(1)), K comparable to Q^(1/2), and p<=2Q, the theorem bracket satisfies
1/M+p^(5/4)/(M K^2)<=Q^(-1/4+o(1)).
Thus each residue-class tensor is at most Q^(1-7/384+o(1)). Summing at most r<=Q^theta classes, restoring the Q^o(1) projective mass, and then summing the four subrectangles proves |S|<=Q^(1-7/384+theta+o(1)). For theta=1/100, 7/384-1/100=79/9600. All gates and the complete product amplitude remain present.

glossary.near-prime CRT tensor bound: The prime-modulus bilinear estimate after separating a small complementary CRT modulus into residue classes.

7a82b1642af6c8c2.title: LITERAL INCOMPLETE ROW-CHARACTER KERNEL AND EXACT CHARACTER NORMALIZATION
7a82b1642af6c8c2.author: slava chan
7a82b1642af6c8c2.statement:
LITERAL INCOMPLETE ROW-CHARACTER KERNEL AND EXACT CHARACTER NORMALIZATION.

Let m>1 be odd, q=m^2, and let Delta be a nonzero integer coprime to q. Let n_1,n_2 be positive integers coprime to q such that h=gcd(n_1,n_2) divides Delta. Put u_1=n_1/h, u_2=n_2/h, and D=Delta/h. Choose integers a_0,c_0 satisfying
 a_0u_2-c_0u_1=D.                                                    (1)
Let chi,psi be characters of the unit group modulo q, extended by zero to nonunits. Let F and G be arbitrary finitely supported complex functions on the integers and define
 w_{n_1,n_2}(t)=F(a_0+u_1t)G(c_0+u_2t),                              (2)
 K_{chi,psi}(n_1,n_2)
 =sum_{t in Z}w_{n_1,n_2}(t)
   chi(a_0+u_1t)psi(c_0+u_2t).                                      (3)
For ell modulo q define
 R_{chi,psi}(ell;n_1,n_2)
 =sum_{t modulo q}chi(a_0+u_1t)psi(c_0+u_2t)e_q(ell t)               (4)
and
 What_{n_1,n_2}(ell)
 =sum_{t in Z}w_{n_1,n_2}(t)e_q(-ell t).                             (5)
Then
 K_{chi,psi}(n_1,n_2)
 =q^(-1)sum_{ell modulo q}
   R_{chi,psi}(ell;n_1,n_2)What_{n_1,n_2}(ell).                   (6)
The value of (3) and the right side of (6) are independent of the chosen solution (a_0,c_0), after the corresponding translation of t.

Every integer solution of
 a n_2-c n_1=Delta                                                   (7)
is uniquely
 (a,c)=(a_0+u_1t,c_0+u_2t), t in Z.                                 (8)
Thus (2) is the exact moving row-box weight. The zero additive frequency is
 R_{chi,psi}(0;n_1,n_2)
 =sum_{a,c modulo q; a n_2-c n_1=Delta modulo q}chi(a)psi(c)         (9)
 =chi(Delta n_2^(-1))psi(Delta n_1^(-1))J(chi,psi),                  (10)
where
 J(chi,psi)=sum_{y modulo q}chi(1+y)psi(y).                           (11)
Consequently, for Delta=2K and the exact centered shared-digit assembly of fact 382dadf452a0f461, the assembled ell=0 contribution is zero.

Suppose F and G are indicators of integer intervals of lengths at most L_1 and L_2. Then
 #{t:w_{n_1,n_2}(t) is nonzero}
 <=1+min(L_1/u_1,L_2/u_2).                                          (12)
In particular, if X>=2, X<=n_1,n_2<=2X, h<=|Delta|, and L_1,L_2<=C_box X for a fixed positive constant C_box, then
 #{t:w_{n_1,n_2}(t) is nonzero}<=1+C_box|Delta|.                     (13)
There exist unit integers A,C satisfying An_2-Cn_1=Delta. Taking F and G to be their singleton indicators makes (3) a single term of absolute value one. Hence the class of literal moving singleton row boxes admits no uniform absolute o(1) bound for the fixed-column kernel.

Finally, fix s in {1,-1}, assume gcd(K,m)=1, let W(u)=e_m(ell_0u) with ell_0 nonzero modulo m, let T_W be the shared digit tensor of fact 8230d44e6677f45b, and put n=phi(q). Then
 P_4(T_W)=n^2=phi(m^2)^2                                             (14)
and its attaining character expansion
 T_W=n^(-2)sum_{chi,psi}S(chi,psi)
       chi(a)chi(b)psi(c)psi(d)                                     (15)
satisfies
 n^(-2)sum_{chi,psi}|S(chi,psi)|=1.                                 (16)
For common arbitrary unit-supported column sequences alpha_0,beta_0, multiplication by the column characters in (15) preserves their ell^2 norms. Therefore the character-by-character absolute coefficient ledger before estimating the row kernels is exactly
 ||alpha_0||_2||beta_0||_2.                                         (17)
No estimate for the nonzero kernels in (4), no Burgess or character-large-sieve application, and no column-averaged operator bound is asserted.
7a82b1642af6c8c2.proof:
Because gcd(u_1,u_2)=1 and D is an integer, equation (1) has an integer solution. Divide (7) by h, subtract (1), and obtain
 (a-a_0)u_2=(c-c_0)u_1.
Coprimality implies u_1 divides a-a_0 and u_2 divides c-c_0, giving the unique parameter t in (8).

Put P(t)=chi(a_0+u_1t)psi(c_0+u_2t). It is periodic modulo q. Finite Fourier inversion with convention (4) gives
 P(t)=q^(-1)sum_ell R_{chi,psi}(ell;n_1,n_2)e_q(-ell t).
Multiplying by the finite weight (2), summing t, and using (5) proves (6). Any other solution is
 (a_0+u_1t_0,c_0+u_2t_0).
Translation of t by -t_0 leaves (3) invariant and multiplies the two Fourier factors in each summand of (6) by reciprocal phases.

Since n_1,n_2,h,u_1,u_2 are units modulo q, (8) modulo q is a bijection onto the solutions of (7) modulo q, proving (9). Parameterize c modulo q, put a=(Delta+cn_1)n_2^(-1), and set y=cn_1Delta^(-1). Then
 c=Delta y n_1^(-1), a=Delta(1+y)n_2^(-1),
which proves (10). Fact 382dadf452a0f461 proves the centered assembly conclusion at Delta=2K.

The two interval conditions in (2) confine t to real intervals of lengths at most L_1/u_1 and L_2/u_2. Their intersection contains at most one plus the smaller length, proving (12). Since u_i=n_i/h>=X/|Delta|, (13) follows.

To construct a unit exact solution, start from (8). For each prime r dividing m, u_1 and u_2 are nonzero modulo r. Exactly one residue class of t modulo r makes a_0+u_1t zero, and exactly one makes c_0+u_2t zero. These two forbidden classes are distinct: if they coincided, equation (7) would give Delta congruent to zero modulo r, contrary to gcd(Delta,m)=1. Since r is odd, at least one class modulo r remains allowed. The Chinese remainder theorem chooses t simultaneously outside the forbidden classes for every prime divisor r of m. The resulting A=a_0+u_1t and C=c_0+u_2t are coprime to m, hence are units modulo q, and satisfy the exact equation. Singleton F,G then give absolute value one.

For the final ledger, the pure mode has Fourier transform supported at ell_0 with absolute value m. Fact 8230d44e6677f45b gives
 P_4(T_W)=[n^2/m]sum_ell|W_hat(ell)|=n^2
and
 sum_{chi,psi}|S(chi,psi)|=n^2.
These prove (14) and (16). Multiplication of alpha_0,beta_0 by unit-modulus characters on unit support preserves their ell^2 norms, and (16) gives (17).

glossary.C_box: a fixed upper constant for the row interval lengths relative to X
glossary.K_{chi,psi}: the literal incomplete determinant-row character kernel at fixed columns
glossary.R_{chi,psi}(ell;n_1,n_2): the complete mixed additive-twist determinant-row character kernel modulo m^2
glossary.What_{n_1,n_2}(ell): the finite additive transform modulo m^2 of the moving row-box weight
glossary.w_{n_1,n_2}(t): the moving row-box weight pulled back to the determinant solution parameter

7a9257c915a47f6b.title: P-qSRC DUAL MÖBIUS NORMAL FORM AND THE EXACT COHERENT OUTER-SIGN-FREE SUBSOURCE
7a9257c915a47f6b.author: slava chan
7a9257c915a47f6b.statement:
P-qSRC DUAL MÖBIUS NORMAL FORM AND THE EXACT COHERENT OUTER-SIGN-FREE SUBSOURCE.

Adopt the exact Dcal>Q^2 principal source P-qSRC of fact e9e9563501147a1a. Put T=mathscr A>0. For every exact retained ordered primitive-ray pair
R=(epsilon,a,b),  R'=(epsilon',a',b'),
write
g=gcd(a,a'),  a=g alpha,  a'=g beta,
L_0=epsilon b beta-epsilon'b'alpha.                                (1)
Then g,alpha,beta are pairwise coprime and squarefree and
gcd(alpha beta,L_0)=1. Define
g_0=g/gcd(g,T L_0),
alpha_T=gcd(alpha,T),  alpha_0=alpha/alpha_T,
beta_T=gcd(beta,T),    beta_0=beta/beta_T,                           (2)
and define the dual principal-sign conductor
m_P=g_0 alpha_T beta_T.                                              (3)
The physical ray conductor is
m_q=g_0 alpha_0 beta_0.                                              (4)
All six factors in (2) are squarefree, and the three factors in either (3) or (4) are pairwise coprime. The exact Möbius-sign identity is
mu(a)mu(a')mu(m_q)=mu(m_P).                                         (5)

Use the exact RAY-MU notation of fact a36284a9dbec7837:
B_lambda(R)=mu(a) A^0_lambda(R) U_lambda(R),                         (6)
where U_lambda(R) is the complete signed scaling Möbius transform with every literal Fourier and mask factor retained. Then P-qSRC has the exact dual-sign normal form
P-qSRC
 =sum_lambda sum_{exact retained R != R'}
  [mu(m_P)/phi(m_q)]
  A^0_lambda(R)conjugate(A^0_lambda(R'))
  U_lambda(R)conjugate(U_lambda(R')).                               (P-qSRC-DUALMU)
No selector or coefficient is changed in this identity.

The outer-sign-free subsource m_P=1 has the exact classification
m_P=1
 if and only if
 g divides T L_0,  gcd(alpha beta,T)=1.                              (7)
On this subsource,
m_q=alpha beta                                                       (8)
and P-qSRC-DUALMU has the positive outer arithmetic coefficient
1/phi(alpha beta).                                                   (9)
Thus the conductor Möbius sign can cancel completely against the two intrinsic primitive-ray Möbius signs even when m_q>=2. This subsource contains the unit-ray case a=a'=1, but is not algebraically restricted to it.

At the opposite extreme, on m_q=1 one has
g_0=alpha_0=beta_0=1,
m_P=alpha beta,                                                      (10)
so (5) recovers exactly the mu(alpha)mu(beta) sign in MQ1-MU-N of fact e80321eac8f26079.

Consequently P-qSRC cannot be treated as a source with an independent or untouched mu(m_q) sign. Its exact outer sign is mu(m_P), and on (7) no outer Möbius cancellation remains at all; any cancellation there must come from the two complete signed transforms U_lambda, their ray/copy aggregation, or other literal structure. This is an exact coefficient reduction and scoped method no-fit. It does not assert that the subsource (7) is nonempty, estimate either its coefficient mass or its signed total, prove P-qSRC-SUP, C-qSRC-SUP, a good-W tail payment, or Goldbach.
7a9257c915a47f6b.proof:
Fact 3089501f7fb49c18 proves for the decomposition (1) that g,alpha,beta are pairwise coprime and squarefree, that gcd(alpha beta,L_0)=1, and that
m_q=
 [g/gcd(g,T L_0)]
 [alpha beta/gcd(alpha beta,T)].                                    (11)
Since alpha and beta are coprime, their divisors alpha_T and beta_T are coprime, and
gcd(alpha beta,T)=alpha_T beta_T.
Therefore
alpha beta/gcd(alpha beta,T)=alpha_0 beta_0.
Substitution in (11) proves (4).

Every factor in (2) divides one of the squarefree, pairwise coprime integers g, alpha, beta. Hence each factor is squarefree; g_0,alpha_T,beta_T are pairwise coprime, and g_0,alpha_0,beta_0 are pairwise coprime. This proves all squarefreeness and coprimality assertions about (3)-(4).

Because a=g alpha and a'=g beta with pairwise coprime squarefree factors,
mu(a)mu(a')
 =mu(g)^2mu(alpha)mu(beta)
 =mu(alpha)mu(beta).                                                 (12)
Moreover
mu(alpha)=mu(alpha_T)mu(alpha_0),
mu(beta)=mu(beta_T)mu(beta_0),                                      (13)
and by (4)
mu(m_q)=mu(g_0)mu(alpha_0)mu(beta_0).                               (14)
Multiply (12)-(14). Since every displayed Möbius value is in {-1,1},
mu(alpha_0)^2=mu(beta_0)^2=1.
The product becomes
mu(g_0)mu(alpha_T)mu(beta_T)=mu(m_P),
where the last equality uses the pairwise coprimality in (3). This proves (5).

Fact a36284a9dbec7837 gives (6) exactly for every retained Good-W ray, with U_lambda(R) containing the complete scaling Möbius sum and every literal source and deletion mask. Insert (6) in both coefficient slots of the definition
P-qSRC
 =sum_lambda sum_{exact retained R != R'}
 B_lambda(R)conjugate(B_lambda(R'))
 mu(m_q)/phi(m_q)
from fact e9e9563501147a1a. The values mu(a),mu(a') are real, so the combined outer factor is
mu(a)mu(a')mu(m_q)/phi(m_q).
Replace its numerator by (5). This proves P-qSRC-DUALMU. The substitution is termwise on the identical finite retained index set, so every literal selector and coefficient remains unchanged.

Because the three factors in (3) are positive integers, m_P=1 holds exactly when
g_0=alpha_T=beta_T=1.                                               (15)
By definition, g_0=1 is equivalent to g|T L_0. Also alpha_T=beta_T=1 is equivalent to gcd(alpha beta,T)=1 because alpha and beta are coprime. This proves (7). Under (7), alpha_0=alpha and beta_0=beta, so (4) gives (8). Equations (3), (5), and m_P=1 give the positive coefficient (9). The choice a=a'=1 has g=alpha=beta=1 and satisfies (7), proving the containment statement. Since (7) itself does not impose alpha beta=1, the algebraic class also permits m_q=alpha beta>=2; no literal nonemptiness is asserted.

If m_q=1, the pairwise coprime positive factors in (4) must all equal one. Thus g_0=alpha_0=beta_0=1. The last two equalities give alpha_T=alpha and beta_T=beta, and (3) gives (10). Substitution in (5) yields mu(alpha)mu(beta), exactly the outer sign in MQ1-MU-N of fact e80321eac8f26079.

The coherent class (7) has outer coefficient +1/phi(alpha beta), but the two U_lambda factors in P-qSRC-DUALMU remain the exact signed scaling Möbius transforms. Therefore only the combined outer ray/conductor sign has disappeared. No cancellation estimate or nonemptiness follows, and every scope exclusion in the statement is respected.

glossary.P-qSRC-DUALMU: The exact Dcal>Q^2 principal signed source after the intrinsic ray Möbius signs are combined with mu(m_q).
glossary.m_P: The squarefree dual principal-sign conductor g_0 alpha_T beta_T whose Möbius value is the combined outer ray/conductor sign in P-qSRC.
glossary.outer-sign-free subsource: The exact m_P=1 restriction of P-qSRC-DUALMU, where the combined ray/conductor Möbius factor equals positive one.

7b88f3f21d0836c8.title: DUAL-FREQUENCY MODULATION OBSTRUCTION TO LIFTING THE SCALAR C4 TENSOR GRAM
7b88f3f21d0836c8.author: slava chan
7b88f3f21d0836c8.statement:
DUAL-FREQUENCY MODULATION OBSTRUCTION TO LIFTING THE SCALAR C4 TENSOR GRAM.

Let p>=11 be prime. For C in F_p^* define
f_C(x)=1_{x!=0}e_p(Cx^{-1}),
fhat_C(rho)=p^{-1}sum_{x mod p}f_C(x)e_p(-rho x).
There exist distinct C,C' in F_p^* and complex numbers b_C(rho), b_{C'}(rho), indexed by rho in F_p^*, with
|b_C(rho)|<=1,   |b_{C'}(rho)|<=1,
such that
sum_{rho in F_p^*}
 b_C(rho)fhat_C(rho)
 conjugate(b_{C'}(rho)fhat_{C'}(rho)) >=1/10.                (1)
In contrast, without the coordinatewise modulations,
|sum_{rho in F_p^*}fhat_C(rho)conjugate(fhat_{C'}(rho))|
 =p^{-1}+p^{-2}<=2/p.                                       (2)

Therefore the off-slope reciprocal factor in the scalar mixed Gram cannot be lifted uniformly to rows carrying arbitrary independent dual-frequency multipliers. In particular, the fixed-active-product scalar Schur bound of fact d9a096ed4e597b2b does not by itself prove a C4 Kloosterman-vector Bessel bound if the completed literal coefficient is allowed to depend arbitrarily on the dual frequency. A valid lift must prove additional common-scalar, projective-norm, or source-specific structure of that coefficient.

This is an abstract finite-field modulation counterexample only. It is not a counterexample for the literal C4 source coefficient, the natural deletion masks, C4-VEC, the C4 moment, or Goldbach.
7b88f3f21d0836c8.proof:
Put
a(rho)=|fhat_1(rho)|   for rho in F_p^*,
E=sum_{rho in F_p^*}a(rho)^2.
Facts 4f9aec67f5be35db and 3d10fd30e2a42246 give
E=(p-1)/p-p^{-2}=1-p^{-1}-p^{-2},                            (3)
max_{rho!=0}a(rho)<=2/sqrt(p).                                (4)
Consequently
sum_{rho!=0}a(rho)
 >=E/max a
 >=E sqrt(p)/2.                                               (5)

For lambda in F_p^* define
C(lambda)=sum_{rho!=0}a(rho)a(lambda rho).
Multiplication by lambda permutes F_p^*, so
sum_{lambda in F_p^*}C(lambda)
 =(sum_{rho!=0}a(rho))^2
 >=E^2p/4.                                                    (6)
Also C(1)=E. Hence some lambda!=1 satisfies
C(lambda)>=(E^2p/4-E)/(p-2).                                 (7)
For p>=11, equation (3) gives E>=9/10. The right side of (7) is then at least
((81/100)p/4-1)/(p-2)>=1/10,                                 (8)
where the final inequality holds for p>=11.

A change of variable x=C y in the normalized Fourier transform gives the exact scaling relation
fhat_C(rho)=fhat_1(Crho).                                     (9)
Choose C=1 and C'=lambda from (7). They are distinct. For every nonzero rho define
b_C(rho)=conjugate(fhat_C(rho))/|fhat_C(rho)|
when fhat_C(rho)!=0 and put b_C(rho)=0 otherwise; define b_{C'} in the same way. Then
b_C(rho)fhat_C(rho)=|fhat_C(rho)|,
b_{C'}(rho)fhat_{C'}(rho)=|fhat_{C'}(rho)|.
Using (9), the left side of (1) is therefore
sum_{rho!=0}a(rho)a(lambda rho)=C(lambda)>=1/10,
proving (1).

Because C!=C', fact 3d10fd30e2a42246 gives the unmodulated mixed-mode Gram exactly as
-p^{-1}-p^{-2},
which proves (2). The contrast between (1) and (2) proves the obstruction and every scope statement.

glossary.C(lambda): The magnitude correlation sum over nonzero Fourier coordinates after multiplicative permutation by lambda.
glossary.b_C: A row-dependent coordinatewise unit modulation of the nonzero Fourier spectrum attached to C.

7bcf6f85c0df5948.title: Let r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4 be pairwise distinct primes, put b=r_1r_2 and b'=r_3r_4, and let X,Y be integers. For e dividing b and f dividing b' define the paired primitive-conductor face
7bcf6f85c0df5948.author: slava chan
7bcf6f85c0df5948.statement:
Let r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4 be pairwise distinct primes, put b=r_1r_2 and b'=r_3r_4, and let X,Y be integers. For e dividing b and f dividing b' define the paired primitive-conductor face
F_{e,f}(X,Y)=c_e(X)c_f(Y)/(bb'),
where c_e is the Ramanujan sum defined in fact 3bb378b0a49679f9.

(A) The exact paired selector has the sixteen-face decomposition
1_{b divides X}1_{b' divides Y}
 =sum_{e divides b}sum_{f divides b'}F_{e,f}(X,Y).               (CF)
The faces with Omega(e)+Omega(f)=k number binomial(4,k) for 0<=k<=4. Only the single face (e,f)=(b,b') has all four primitive prime factors.

(B) On the paired-selector support b divides X and b' divides Y, every face is nonnegative and
F_{e,f}(X,Y)=phi(e)phi(f)/(bb').
In particular the full-four-prime face is the fraction
alpha=F_{b,b'}(X,Y)
 =phi(b)phi(b')/(bb')
 =product_{i=1}^4(1-1/r_i)
of the exact selector value one, and the total of the other fifteen faces is exactly 1-alpha.

If r_i>=H>1 for all i, then
0<=1-alpha<=sum_{i=1}^4 1/r_i<=4/H.                              (TAX)

(C) Let A be any finite set of paired-selector-supported data a, each carrying four pairwise distinct primes r_i(a)>=H, integers X_a,Y_a divisible by b_a=r_1(a)r_2(a) and b'_a=r_3(a)r_4(a), and a real or complex coefficient lambda_a. Let alpha_a be its full-face fraction. Then the original weighted selector total S and its full-four-prime face total S_full satisfy
S=sum_{a in A}lambda_a,
S_full=sum_{a in A}alpha_a lambda_a,
and the deletion estimate
|S-S_full|<=4H^{-1}sum_{a in A}|lambda_a|.                       (WD)
Thus full-conductor extraction has a pointwise small relative coefficient tax on paired-selector-supported large-prime data, while the resulting aggregate estimate depends on the l1 coefficient mass. No optimality or necessity of this l1 estimate is asserted.

(D) Off the selector support, the individual faces are signed and the full face is neither the selector nor a nonnegative majorant of it. If r_1 divides X but r_2 does not, while b' divides Y, then
F_{b,b'}(X,Y)=-(r_1-1)phi(b')/(bb')<0
whereas the paired selector is zero. If gcd(X,bb')=gcd(Y,bb')=1, then
F_{b,b'}(X,Y)=1/(bb')>0
whereas the paired selector is again zero.

The divisor pair (e,f) is an additional primitive-conductor index in any application of (CF). Formula (WD) supplies one uniform way to delete the fifteen proper-conductor faces on selector-supported data. This proof gives no better bound absent an additional cancellation or norm estimate, and it gives no positive termwise deletion off the selector support.
7bcf6f85c0df5948.proof:
Fact 3bb378b0a49679f9 proves for every positive integer q and integer Z that
1_{q divides Z}=q^{-1}sum_{d divides q}c_d(Z).
Apply this with (q,Z)=(b,X) and (b',Y), then multiply the two finite identities. This gives (CF).

A divisor e of b selects an arbitrary subset of {r_1,r_2}, and a divisor f of b' selects an arbitrary subset of {r_3,r_4}. Thus the pair (e,f) is equivalent to a subset of four primes. Exactly binomial(4,k) choices contain k primes, and only the full subset gives (b,b'). This proves (A).

If e divides X, every unit residue u modulo e has e_e(uX)=1, so the definition of the Ramanujan sum gives c_e(X)=phi(e). On b divides X every e dividing b also divides X, and similarly for f,Y. This proves the face formula in (B). Summing all sixteen faces gives the selector value one by (CF), so the proper-face sum is 1-alpha.

The totient of a product of distinct primes gives
alpha=product_i(1-1/r_i).
For numbers x_i in [0,1], the elementary inequality
1-product_i(1-x_i)<=sum_i x_i
follows inductively from 1-(1-x)(1-y)=x+y-xy<=x+y. Apply x_i=1/r_i. Nonnegativity is immediate, and r_i>=H gives the last inequality in (TAX).

For (C), each datum lies on the paired-selector support, so its exact selector coefficient is one and its full-face coefficient is alpha_a. Therefore the displayed formulas for S and S_full are definitions after applying (B). The triangle inequality and (TAX) give
|S-S_full|=|sum_a(1-alpha_a)lambda_a|
 <=sum_a(1-alpha_a)|lambda_a|
 <=4H^{-1}sum_a|lambda_a|.
No cancellation or norm conversion is used, and no claim that this bound is optimal is made.

For (D), Ramanujan sums are multiplicative across the coprime prime moduli. For a prime r,
c_r(Z)=r-1 when r divides Z and c_r(Z)=-1 otherwise, directly from the sum of all nontrivial additive characters modulo r. If r_1 divides X and r_2 does not, then
c_b(X)=c_{r_1}(X)c_{r_2}(X)=-(r_1-1).
If b' divides Y, then c_{b'}(Y)=phi(b'), proving the negative formula. If both X and Y are coprime to bb', then each of the four prime Ramanujan sums is -1, so c_b(X)=c_{b'}(Y)=1, proving the positive formula. The paired selector vanishes in both examples.

The final scope statements merely summarize (CF), (WD), and the two signed examples. They do not assert that the l1 estimate is necessary or exclude improvements from additional structure.

glossary.A: a finite family of paired-selector-supported data
glossary.F_{e,f}: the normalized paired primitive-conductor face indexed by divisors e and f
glossary.H: a common lower bound for the four primes
glossary.X: the integer tested by the first semiprime selector
glossary.X_a: the first selector-tested integer attached to datum a
glossary.Y: the integer tested by the second semiprime selector
glossary.Y_a: the second selector-tested integer attached to datum a
glossary.alpha: the full-four-prime face fraction on selector support
glossary.alpha_a: the full-face fraction of datum a
glossary.b'_a: the second semiprime attached to datum a
glossary.b_a: the first semiprime attached to datum a

7c06abcd88417706.title: CRIT-DEEP-SUBHALF-PAYMENT: COMPLETE LITERAL CRITICAL-W PAYMENT IN THE DEEP MODULUS RANGE, INCLUDING ALL OUTER-c COPRIMALITY LAYERS. Fix tau>0 and the complete selected same-N critical-W projection of fact 328503a935cabe60. For each exact active g,c and either orientation use the scales and target
7c06abcd88417706.author: slava chan
7c06abcd88417706.statement:
CRIT-DEEP-SUBHALF-PAYMENT: COMPLETE LITERAL CRITICAL-W PAYMENT IN THE DEEP MODULUS RANGE, INCLUDING ALL OUTER-c COPRIMALITY LAYERS. Fix tau>0 and the complete selected same-N critical-W projection of fact 328503a935cabe60. For each exact active g,c and either orientation use the scales and target
Gamma=Gc, Q_c=Q/c, K_c=K_sh/c, B=Q^beta,
ell=N/(gc), T=GQ,                                               (1)
so that
ell is asymptotic to BK_c, ell is asymptotic to Q_cT.           (2)
Let S_{g,c}^{deep}(C) be the complete literal nonzero-frequency block at fixed g,c, summed over every frozen source, dyadic, fixed-U, high, parent, provenance, factorization and projective label, and restricted to
Gamma>=K_c(log B)^(2C).                                        (3)
No proper deletion or marker leaf is isolated.

For every prescribed A_0>0 there is C=C(A_0)>0 such that, uniformly in both orientations,
|S_{g,c}^{deep}(C)|
 <<_{A_0} tau(c)^2 ell(log N)^(-A_0)                            (4)
after increasing the internal saving exponent by the fixed polylogarithmic label tax.

Let S_deep(C) be the sum of these blocks over both orientations and all exact active g,c. Then
|S_deep(C)|<<_{A_0}N(log N)^(-A_0).                             (5)
The estimate contains no Q^epsilon, c^epsilon, g^epsilon, x^epsilon or x^o(1) loss.

The physical AP principal average and the same-mask t-Poisson zero are paid as distinct terms. In particular, for fixed g,c the complete physical progression uses the sequence
f_c(n)=mu(n)1_{(n,c)=1},                                       (6)
in the moving reduced residue n congruent ell kappa^(-1) modulo q; its weighted centered discrepancy is paid by fact dbfdaaf10709eca0. Its principal term is
mu(c)sum_{q,kappa}{mu(q)over phi(q)}
 sum_{(n,qc)=1}mu(n)w_{q,kappa}(n),                            (7)
whereas its same-mask Poisson zero is
mu(c)sum_qmu(q)sum_{(n,qc)=1}mu(n)
 {1over n}integral_R F_{q,n}(y)dy.                             (8)
Both (7) and (8) are separately O_A(ell(log N)^(-A)). No estimate is asserted for the complementary range Gamma<K_c(log B)^(2C), for the near-half LOW-R/MED/ROUGH3 interfaces, for the complete critical tail, or for Goldbach.
7c06abcd88417706.proof:
By fact a3103a7fbc2dc2ed, condition (3) is exactly equivalent to
Q_c<=sqrt(B)/(log B)^C.                                        (9)
Fact 5772f2de626492b3 proves B>=x^(1/20) and the uniform logarithmic supremum, total-variation and scaled-Lipschitz norms of the actual complete literal n-amplitude w_{q,kappa}. Thus, after choosing C large enough in terms of A_0 and the fixed source norms, all hypotheses of fact dbfdaaf10709eca0 hold with Q=Q_c, V_q=w_{q,kappa}, and the exact squarefree auxiliary integer c.

Fix kappa. Fact dbfdaaf10709eca0 gives
sum_{q asymptotic to Q_c}
 |sum_{n congruent ell kappa^(-1) (mod q),(n,c)=1}
       mu(n)w_{q,kappa}(n)
  -phi(q)^(-1)sum_{(n,qc)=1}mu(n)w_{q,kappa}(n)|
 <<_A tau(c)^2 B(log N)^(-A).                                  (10)
All active q are squarefree and coprime to c by fact 8d9feea8c44da2c8. Multiplication by the literal outer coefficient mu(q) is absorbed by (10). Summing the O(K_c) values of kappa and using BK_c asymptotic to ell gives
<<_A tau(c)^2 ell(log N)^(-A).                                 (11)
This pays the complete centered physical AP discrepancy, including the outer condition (n,c)=1 that remained open in fact c1c141e3d7fb562f.

The principal term left by (10) is exactly (7), because the progression residue is a unit modulo q and f_c(n) already imposes (n,c)=1. Fact c1c141e3d7fb562f, equation (9), proves
|(7)|<<_A ell(log N)^(-A)                                      (12)
from fact 71389b22e6f49e13 and the literal regularity lemma.

Fact 328503a935cabe60 gives the complete nonzero-frequency row as the physical progression minus its same-mask zero. Its exact fixed-g,c zero is (8), not (7). Fact c1c141e3d7fb562f, equations (10)-(12), separately proves
|(8)|<<_A Q_cT(log N)^(-A)
 <<_A ell(log N)^(-A).                                         (13)
Combining (11)-(13) proves the fixed-label form of (4). The number and projective norm of the complete frozen source, dyadic, fixed-U, high, parent, provenance and factorization labels cost a fixed power of log N, as recorded in the source provenance facts 328503a935cabe60 and 5772f2de626492b3. Choose the input A larger by this fixed amount to obtain (4) as stated.

It remains to aggregate exact g,c without an epsilon loss. Fact dbfdaaf10709eca0 proves
sum_{g,c active}tau(c)^2/(gc)
 <=product_{p|N}(1+5/p)
 <=(1+log N)^5.                                                 (14)
Since ell=N/(gc), sum (4) over all active g,c, both orientations and the remaining fixed logarithmic labels. Choose the local saving exponent larger than A_0+5 plus every fixed label tax. Equation (14) then gives
sum_{g,c}|S_{g,c}^{deep}(C)|
 <<N(log N)^(-A_0),                                             (15)
which is (5). Every step used an exact logarithmic ledger, so no epsilon or x^o(1) factor occurs. The scope exclusions follow because (9) was essential to the auxiliary-coprime transfer.

7c172c29ca9cbd31.title: EXACT COMPULSORY-ROUGH-PRIME OPERATOR TARGET AND OPTIMISTIC FIXED-PRIME TYPE III NO-FIT
7c172c29ca9cbd31.author: slava chan
7c172c29ca9cbd31.statement:
EXACT COMPULSORY-ROUGH-PRIME OPERATOR TARGET AND OPTIMISTIC FIXED-PRIME TYPE III NO-FIT.

Assume the actual scales and notation of facts 050efa07f87f374a and bab04e002177e282. Thus B=Q^(4/3+o(1)), b is squarefree and B<=b<2B. For every such b let p be its largest prime factor and put b'=b/p. Define
 cal B_rough
  ={b:B<=b<2B, b squarefree, b'<F_0}.                       (1)
For b in cal B_rough and (a,b)=1 use the compulsory local factor r_{p,b}(a) and the full shifted-cutoff complementary superposition
 P^{(p)}_{b',>F_0/p}(a)
from fact bab04e002177e282. For a complex coefficient sequence alpha supported on Q<=a<2Q define
 E_rough(alpha)
  =sum_{b in cal B_rough;p does not divide N}
    |sum_{Q<=a<2Q;(a,b)=1}
      alpha_a r_{p,b}(a)P^{(p)}_{b',>F_0/p}(a)|^2.           (2)
The omitted rows with p|N are identically zero. Hence (2) is exactly the restriction of E_{>F_0}(alpha) to cal B_rough.

For every fixed omega>0, the normalized operator estimate
 E_rough(alpha)
  <<Q^(5/3-omega)sum_a|alpha_a|^2                            (ROP)
would give
 E_rough(alpha)<<Q^(8/3-omega+o(1))                          (3)
for every actual tensor alpha in fact 050efa07f87f374a. Thus Q^(5/3-omega) is the exact operator-square scale corresponding to the Q^(8/3-omega) CEN-MZB energy scale after the actual input energy sum_a|alpha_a|^2<=Q^(1+o(1)) is restored.

There is a sharp direct-theorem no-fit for obtaining ROP by a fixed-p pointwise Type III estimate followed only by cardinality summation over b. Grant all of the following favorable replacements for free:
(i) delete P^{(p)}_{b',>F_0/p}(a);
(ii) delete the constant 1/(p-1) from r_{p,b}(a);
(iii) replace the literal product-coupled coefficient w_{ldm} by three separated coefficients of modulus at most one;
(iv) restrict to the balanced lengths 1<=l,d,m<=U=Q^(1/3);
(v) replace the right side supplied at every p by the smallest power it can attain as p varies.

Fouvry--Kowalski--Michel, arXiv:1304.3199, Theorem 3.2, applied to the reciprocal trace e_p(C(ldm)^(-1)) with C nonzero modulo p, gives before replacement (v)
 Q^(1/2+epsilon)
 {Q/p^(1/2)+Q^(2/3)+Q^(1/3)p^(1/2)}^(1/2).                 (4)
If p=Q^(rho+o(1)), the Q-exponent in (4), apart from epsilon and o(1), is
 max{1-rho/4, 5/6, 2/3+rho/4}.                              (5)
The minimum over real rho is 5/6, attained at rho=2/3. Thus even the favorable uniform pointwise substitute
 |one b-row|<<Q^(5/6+epsilon)                                (6)
followed by the standard O(B) row-cardinality summation gives only
 E_rough<<B Q^(5/3+epsilon)
        =Q^(3+epsilon+o(1)).                                 (7)
This is larger than Q^(8/3-omega) by Q^(1/3+omega+epsilon+o(1)) and, after division by an input energy of scale Q, larger than the ROP scale Q^(5/3-omega) by the same power.

Therefore the unchanged architecture “fixed-p Type III pointwise bound, then sum b absolutely” does not supply ROP, even after the five favorable replacements. This is a theorem-right-hand-side and aggregation no-fit, not a lower bound for E_rough. The actual row (2) is harder for this direct application because it must retain P^{(p)}_{b',>F_0/p}(a), the local centering correction and w_{ldm}; no separated-coefficient representation of those factors is asserted. The conclusion does not rule out a vector-valued Type III theorem, cancellation across b before positive norms, a source-specific low-projective-mass decomposition, or a joint rough-prime/complementary-modulus estimate.

No estimate for ROP, the complementary smooth-modulus branch, complete CEN-MZB, C_small or Goldbach is asserted.
7c172c29ca9cbd31.proof:
For b in cal B_rough, fact bab04e002177e282 proves that if p|N then P_b(a)=0 for every unit a. If p does not divide N, it proves the exact factorization
 P_b(a)
  =r_{p,b}(a)P^{(p)}_{b',>F_0/p}(a).                        (8)
Insert (8) into the definition of E_{>F_0}(alpha) in fact 050efa07f87f374a and retain exactly the b in cal B_rough. This gives (2), including the zero-row assertion.

If ROP holds and alpha is an actual tensor, fact 050efa07f87f374a gives
 sum_a|alpha_a|^2<=Q^(1+o(1)).
Multiplication by Q^(5/3-omega) proves (3). Equivalently, after replacing omega by any fixed smaller positive number, the o(1) is absorbed and gives a fixed-power CEN-scale bound on the rough branch. This proves the exact normalized target statement.

We now verify the theorem-right-hand-side audit. Under replacements (i)-(iv), the oscillatory function is
 K(n)=e_p(Cn^(-1))
on nonzero residues, where C=N(b')^(-1) modulo p. In the nonzero branch p does not divide N, and squarefreeness gives p does not divide b', so C is nonzero modulo p. Fact 5ce79780e36b1ce1 verifies that this reciprocal rational phase is a bounded-conductor nonexceptional trace function. Fouvry--Kowalski--Michel, arXiv:1304.3199, Theorem 3.2, states that for a prime p, a geometrically irreducible nonexceptional trace function K, three coefficient sequences bounded by one and lengths N_1,N_2,N_3,
 |sum_{1<=|n_i|<=N_i;p does not divide n_3}
   alpha(n_1)beta(n_2)gamma(n_3)K(n_1n_2n_3)|
 <<(log p)^(1/2)(N_1N_2N_3)^(1/2+epsilon)
   {N_1N_2N_3/p^(1/2)+N_1N_2+N_3p^(1/2)}^(1/2).            (9)
Its implied constant is polynomial in the fixed trace conductor. Apply (9) with N_1=N_2=N_3=U=Q^(1/3). The logarithm is absorbed into Q^epsilon. Since U^3=Q and U^2=Q^(2/3), formula (9) becomes (4).

Write p=Q^(rho+o(1)). The three terms inside braces in (4) have exponents
 1-rho/2, 2/3, 1/3+rho/2.
Taking the square root and multiplying by Q^(1/2) gives respectively
 1-rho/4, 5/6, 2/3+rho/4.
The exponent of their sum is their maximum, proving (5). The maximum is at least 5/6. Equality requires simultaneously
 1-rho/4<=5/6 and 2/3+rho/4<=5/6,
which give rho>=2/3 and rho<=2/3. Hence the unique minimizing scale is rho=2/3 and the minimum is 5/6. This proves (6) as the most favorable power one could substitute uniformly in this right-hand-side audit.

There are fewer than 2B integers in [B,2B), so pointwise squaring (6) and summing solely by row cardinality gives (7). Since B=Q^(4/3+o(1)),
 BQ^(5/3+epsilon)=Q^(3+epsilon+o(1)).
Subtracting the desired energy exponent 8/3-omega gives 1/3+omega+epsilon+o(1). Dividing both exponents by the common input-energy scale Q subtracts one from each and leaves the same gap. This proves the scoped direct-theorem no-fit.

Every favorable replacement deletes structure rather than proving an identity for (2). In particular, fact b3c1cdc5cb47ae63 states explicitly that w_{ldm} remains product-coupled, and fact bab04e002177e282 retains the full shifted-cutoff complementary superposition. Therefore the FKM application above is an optimistic interface audit, not a claimed estimate for the actual row. This proves all scope restrictions.

glossary.E_rough(alpha): The squared l2 energy of the exact compulsory-rough-prime rows.
glossary.cal B_rough: The squarefree b-family whose largest prime factor p satisfies b/p<F_0.

7c1f38cfbb8d0569.title: GENERAL TERMINAL ANATOMY, HIGH-WEDGE ROUGH-COUNT THRESHOLDS, AND A C2 SIGN-ROUTING NO-GO
7c1f38cfbb8d0569.author: slava chan
7c1f38cfbb8d0569.statement:
GENERAL TERMINAL ANATOMY, HIGH-WEDGE ROUGH-COUNT THRESHOLDS, AND A C2 SIGN-ROUTING NO-GO.

Let J be a positive integer. Let L,S,Z be real numbers satisfying
2<=L<=S, L<Z,
and let r be a squarefree positive integer satisfying
r>S, Z^(J+1)>r.
Define v_L(r), omega_L, I=(L,Z), j_I, and the stopping coefficients Gamma_{k;L,S} exactly as in fact 6414b11506a84ff0. Then exactly one of the following alternatives applies.

(A) j_I(r)>0, with the exact interval-prime identity
mu(r)=-sum_{up=r, p prime, L<p<Z} mu(u)/(1+j_I(u)).

(B) j_I(r)=0 and v_L(r)>S, with the exact stopping identity
mu(r)=sum_{k>=2}(-1)^k
 sum_{uy=r, gcd(u,y)=1}
 mu(u) 1_{j_I(u)=0} Gamma_{k;L,S}(y)
 /binom(k+omega_L(u),k).
Every nonzero stopping factor y satisfies S<y<=SL.

(C_j) For one unique j in {1,...,J}, one has j_I(r)=0, v=v_L(r)<=S, and
r=v p_1...p_j
with distinct primes Z<=p_1<...<p_j. In this case
mu(r)=(-1)^j mu(v).

Thus A, B, C_1,...,C_J form an exact sign-preserving partition. In particular the four classes A,B,C_1,C_2 are exhaustive only when the available hypotheses exclude three Z-rough prime factors.

Now let x>1, eta>0, R>1, and put
Z_0=x^(3/4-4eta)/R>1.
For squarefree integers r<=2R define
J_R=max(1,floor(log(2R)/log Z_0)).
Whenever the preceding stopping hypotheses hold with Z=Z_0, the scale-uniform exact terminal partition is
A,B,C_1,...,C_{J_R}.
The four-cell conclusion A,B,C_1,C_2 is guaranteed by the scale inequalities precisely when
2R<Z_0^3,
equivalently
2R^4<x^(9/4-12eta).                                          (1)
If (1) is not known, the stopping hypotheses do not exclude C_3. For example L=S=2, Z=5, and r=5*7*11=385 satisfy r>S and Z^4>r; this r lies in C_3 and in none of A,B,C_1,C_2.

Finally let a finite signed coefficient family be partitioned by these exact anatomy classes, and denote its class sums by T_A,T_B,T_{C_1},...,T_{C_J}. If
T=T_A+T_B+sum_{j=1}^J T_{C_j}<=-A_0
with A_0>0, then only the pigeonhole conclusion
min(T_A,T_B,T_{C_1},...,T_{C_J})<=-A_0/(J+2)                 (2)
follows from anatomy and sign preservation alone. There is no positive universal c for which these hypotheses imply
T_{C_2}<=-c A_0.
Indeed, a one-incidence family of coefficient -A_0 supported in any non-C_2 class satisfies the total anomaly and has T_{C_2}=0. The explicit C_3 integer above shows that this countermodel may respect the arithmetic anatomy itself.

Consequently the forced high-R anomaly of fact 60b26a9b6f79467a cannot be routed quantitatively into the C2 class, and hence cannot be routed into a C2xC2 four-prime block, from the stopping partition and total sign alone. Such a routing requires separate one-sided or absolute estimates for A, B, C_1 and every C_j with j>=3 that is allowed at the relevant scale. This is a scoped source-anatomy no-go; it does not assert that the actual Poisson coefficients realize the one-incidence countermodel, and it does not rule out source-specific cancellation estimates.
7c1f38cfbb8d0569.proof:
The proofs of (A) and (B) are independent of the exponent J. They are the interval-prime count and random-order stopping calculation of fact 6414b11506a84ff0. We recall the only points needed here. If j_I(r)>0, then for each p in I dividing r one has mu(r/p)=-mu(r) and 1+j_I(r/p)=j_I(r), so the displayed A-sum equals mu(r). If j_I(r)=0 and v_L(r)>S, stop a uniformly random ordering of the prime divisors of v_L(r) at the first prefix product exceeding S. The probability of each stopping subset gives the displayed binomial coefficient and Gamma_{k;L,S}. If y is a nonzero stopped product, then y>S and y/p<=S for its last prime p<=L, hence y<=SL.

Suppose now j_I(r)=0 and v=v_L(r)<=S. Put w=r/v. This factorization is unique because r is squarefree and v is the product of exactly the prime divisors at most L. Every prime divisor of w is greater than L; none lies in I, so every one is at least Z. Also w is not 1, since otherwise r=v<=S, contrary to r>S. If w had at least J+1 distinct prime divisors, then w>=Z^(J+1), whence r=vw>=Z^(J+1), contradicting the strict hypothesis. Thus w has a unique number j of prime divisors with 1<=j<=J. Ordering them gives C_j. Multiplicativity of mu and squarefreeness give
mu(r)=mu(v)(-1)^j.
The conditions defining A, B, and the C_j are disjoint and the preceding alternatives exhaust every r, proving the general partition.

For the scale application, the definition of J_R gives
J_R+1>log(2R)/log Z_0.
Since Z_0>1, exponentiation yields
Z_0^(J_R+1)>2R>=r,
so the general theorem applies with J=J_R. A scale-uniform guarantee that at most two rough primes occur is exactly the strict inequality 2R<Z_0^3. Substitution of Z_0=x^(3/4-4eta)/R gives
2R<x^(9/4-12eta)R^(-3),
which is equivalent to (1).

For the explicit omitted class, with L=S=2 and Z=5 one has v_L(385)=1<=2 and j_I(385)=0 because the interval (2,5) contains only the prime 3, which does not divide 385. The complementary factor is 385=5*7*11, and 5^4=625>385. Hence it is C_3 and is not in the other four classes.

There are J+2 real class sums. If all exceeded -A_0/(J+2), then their sum would exceed -A_0, contradicting the assumed anomaly; this proves (2). To disprove a C2-specific conclusion from these data, take a family consisting of one incidence in a non-C2 class and assign it coefficient -A_0. Its total is -A_0 and its C2 sum is zero. This construction concerns only what follows from the exact anatomy and arbitrary retained coefficients; the final scope paragraph explicitly does not identify it with the literal Poisson coefficient array. Fact 60b26a9b6f79467a supplies only a total negative high-R aggregate and no anatomy-specific bounds, so the claimed routing does not follow from its hypotheses plus this partition.

glossary.A_0: a positive magnitude of a total signed anomaly
glossary.C_j: the terminal class whose Z-rough factor has exactly j distinct prime factors
glossary.J: the maximum number of Z-rough prime factors allowed in the generalized terminal factor
glossary.J_R: the scale-uniform rough-prime count floor(log(2R)/log Z_0)
glossary.T_A: the signed coefficient sum in interval-prime class A
glossary.T_B: the signed coefficient sum in stopping-composite class B
glossary.T_{C_j}: the signed coefficient sum in rough-factor class C_j
glossary.Z_0: the analytic rough cutoff x^(3/4-4 eta)/R

7cc27e1367d85c60.title: Fix a positive integer L_0 and a real number R_0>1. Let Z be a finite family of normalized C2 Poisson incidences
7cc27e1367d85c60.author: slava chan
7cc27e1367d85c60.statement:
Fix a positive integer L_0 and a real number R_0>1. Let Z be a finite family of normalized C2 Poisson incidences
z=(a_z,m_z,k_z,v_z,p_z,q_z,h_z)
such that a_z,m_z,k_z,v_z are positive integers, h_z is a nonzero integer, p_z,q_z are distinct odd primes, b_z=v_zp_zq_z is squarefree,
gcd(a_z,b_z)=1,
a_zm_z+b_zk_z=L_0,
and
p_z,q_z>=R_0, 0<|h_z|<R_0.
Give z a real coefficient w_z and put S(z)={p_z,q_z}. Define its rough frequency-conductor loss set
J(z)={r in S(z):r divides m_zh_z},
and let P_{L_0} be the set of odd prime divisors of L_0.

(A) One has
J(z) subset S(z) intersect P_{L_0}.
The rough phase of z has full primitive denominator p_zq_z exactly when J(z)=emptyset. Hence the exact layer partition by J(z) has at most
1+omega_odd(L_0)+binomial(omega_odd(L_0),2)
 <=(1+log(L_0)/log(3))^2
possible labels. For a support-disjoint ordered pair (z,z'), the number of retained primitive rough primes is
4-|J(z)|-|J(z')|.
In particular only the layer J(z)=J(z')=emptyset can retain all four rough primes.

This frequency-conductor ledger is not the gcd-provenance ledger of fact 3822f8ceb13a081b: that fact labels gcd(d,pell) in the forward-1x1 source, whereas J(z) labels divisors of m_zh_z after the hybrid outer gcd normalization. The two selectors cannot be identified; if both are present in a reconstruction, both labels must be retained.

(B) Let
P_good={(z,z') in Z^2:S(z) intersect S(z')=emptyset, J(z)=J(z')=emptyset}.
For (z,z') in P_good define
alpha_{z,z'}=product_{r in S(z) union S(z')}(1-1/r).
Let
S_good=sum_{(z,z') in P_good}w_zw_{z'},
S_full=sum_{(z,z') in P_good}alpha_{z,z'}w_zw_{z'},
and
L_1=sum_{z:J(z)=emptyset}|w_z|.
Then the full-conductor deletion estimate is
|S_good-S_full|<=4R_0^{-1}L_1^2.                                (FC)
Consequently an error target E>0 is met by this triangle method whenever
L_1^2<=E R_0/4.
For an asymptotic target o(E), the corresponding sufficient condition is L_1^2=o(ER_0). No necessity or optimality is asserted.

(C) The factor R_0^{-1} in (FC) is not by itself an affordability theorem. The rank-one all-pairs coefficient matrix ww^T has projective/nuclear norm sum_z|w_z|^2 by fact c882223fd3a1511a, while L_1^2 cannot be bounded by a universal constant times that norm. Indeed, on n full-conductor labels of unit weight,
L_1^2=n^2 and sum_z|w_z|^2=n.
Thus the currently verified projective budget alone does not show that (FC) is smaller than a prescribed analytic target; a source-specific l1 estimate or cancellation among the proper-conductor faces is still required.

(D) The complete square ledger remains
(sum_z w_z)^2=Q_0+Q_1+Q_2.
Within Q_0 there is the further exact disjoint decomposition by the ordered pair (J(z),J(z')), with P_good as its unique four-full-conductor block. The collision identities are
Q_2=sum_E (sum_{z:S(z)=E}w_z)^2,
Q_1+2Q_2=sum_{r}(sum_{z:r in S(z)}w_z)^2.
Therefore Q_1 and Q_2, and every nonempty J-layer of Q_0, remain explicit remainder blocks. Facts c9ed24359b1f5321 and 3845a81c13f5cf81 show that support combinatorics alone neither absorbs them into P_good nor makes Q_1+Q_2 nonnegative.

(E) On every pair in P_good, fact 0aa454c6baf243c0 supplies an exact carrier
C=B_1G_2+G_1B_2
with all source coefficients and small-v phases preserved. It also proves that short h-windows do not force the induced local rough-prime lifts into the literal windows of fact 397f417416c4cb9d. Hence even if (FC) is affordable and every remainder in (D) is separately controlled, a literal DCE transfer still requires a new arithmetic localization theorem for those modular lifts. No C2xC2 estimate and no implication to Goldbach is asserted here.
7cc27e1367d85c60.proof:
Let r belong to J(z). Then r is p_z or q_z and divides m_zh_z. Since r>=R_0>|h_z|>0 and r is prime, r does not divide h_z. Hence r divides m_z. Reducing
a_zm_z+v_zp_zq_zk_z=L_0
modulo r shows r divides L_0. This proves
J(z) subset S(z) intersect P_{L_0}.

Fact 0aa454c6baf243c0 proves that the primitive denominator of the rough phase is
p_zq_z/gcd(m_zh_z,p_zq_z).
Because the rough semiprime is squarefree, this denominator retains precisely the primes outside J(z), proving the full-denominator and pair-count assertions.

If t=omega_odd(L_0), J(z) is a subset of P_{L_0} of cardinality at most two. There are at most 1+t+binomial(t,2) such subsets. The product of the t distinct odd prime divisors of L_0 is at least 3^t and divides L_0, so t<=log(L_0)/log(3). This proves (A). The difference from fact 3822f8ceb13a081b follows directly from the two definitions: its label is a gcd involving d, whereas J(z) involves m_zh_z after normalization. No equality of these data has been established.

For (B), fact 7bcf6f85c0df5948 proves on four-prime selector-supported data that the full-conductor fraction is alpha and
0<=1-alpha<=sum_r1/r<=4/R_0.
Therefore
|S_good-S_full|
=|sum_{P_good}(1-alpha_{z,z'})w_zw_{z'}|
<=4R_0^{-1}sum_{P_good}|w_z||w_{z'}|
<=4R_0^{-1}(sum_{z:J(z)=emptyset}|w_z|)^2.
This is (FC). The sufficient conditions follow by substitution, with no converse claimed.

For (C), fact c882223fd3a1511a gives the exact nuclear norm of ww^T. For n unit coefficients, the l1 mass is n, so its square is n^2, while the squared l2 mass and the nuclear norm are n. Their ratio is n and is unbounded. Therefore no dimension-free implication from that projective budget to the l1 requirement is available.

For (D), fact c882223fd3a1511a proves the Q_0,Q_1,Q_2 partition. The unique value of J(z) assigns every incidence to exactly one layer, so applying it on both coordinates partitions Q_0, and by (A) only the empty-empty layer has four full rough conductors. Fact c9ed24359b1f5321 proves the displayed Q_2 identity, and fact 3845a81c13f5cf81 proves the displayed prime-fibre identity. Their star and alternating-cycle configurations prove the stated nonabsorption and sign limitations.

Part (E) is exactly the combination of Parts (B) and (D) of fact 0aa454c6baf243c0: its carrier equality preserves the external small-v phases and coefficients, while its common-target counterconfiguration has h_1=h_2=1, full rough conductors, local lifts outside the prescribed windows, and a failed centered parity gate. Thus conductor extraction and collision control do not remove the independent location obstruction.

glossary.J(z): the subset of rough primes lost from the primitive Poisson denominator
glossary.L_1: the l1 mass of the full-rough-conductor source coefficients
glossary.P_good: the ordered support-disjoint pair block with no rough conductor loss on either side
glossary.P_{L_0}: the set of odd prime divisors of the normalized target L_0
glossary.Q_j: the ordered source-square block with rough-support intersection size j
glossary.R_0: the common lower bound for all rough primes and strict upper bound for the Poisson frequency magnitudes
glossary.S_full: the weighted unique full-four-prime conductor-face total
glossary.S_good: the weighted exact selector-supported good-pair total
glossary.Z: the finite family of normalized C2 Poisson incidences
glossary.alpha_{z,z'}: the full four-prime conductor fraction on pair (z,z')
glossary.b_z: the full normalized residual modulus v_zp_zq_z

7cdcef43ec0d4940.title: CENTERED WINDOWED INCOMPLETE-JACOBI OPERATOR CONTRACT AND SCOPED NO-DIRECT KLOOSTERMAN TRANSFERENCE
7cdcef43ec0d4940.author: slava chan
7cdcef43ec0d4940.statement:
CENTERED WINDOWED INCOMPLETE-JACOBI OPERATOR CONTRACT AND SCOPED NO-DIRECT KLOOSTERMAN TRANSFERENCE.

Let m>1 be odd, q=m^2, n=phi(q), s in {1,-1}, and let K be an integer coprime to m. Put Delta=2K. Let W be a centered complex function modulo m, so sum_u W(u)=0, and define
 S(chi,psi)=sum_{u modulo m}W(u)
  conjugate(chi(K+2smu)psi(K-2smu))                                 (1)
for characters chi,psi of the unit group modulo q. Extend every such character by zero to integers not coprime to q. Let I_1,I_2 be finite sets of positive integers, all coprime to q, and assume gcd(n_1,n_2) divides Delta for every pair under consideration.

For each (n_1,n_2) in I_1 times I_2, put h=gcd(n_1,n_2), u_1=n_1/h, u_2=n_2/h, D=Delta/h, and choose a_0,c_0 with a_0u_2-c_0u_1=D. Let omega_{n_1,n_2}(a,c) be an arbitrary finitely supported complex row weight. It may contain both moving row windows and any literal lift selector, and it is required to be independent of chi,psi. Define
 w_{n_1,n_2}(t)
 =omega_{n_1,n_2}(a_0+u_1t,c_0+u_2t),                               (2)
 What_{n_1,n_2}(ell)
 =sum_{t in Z}w_{n_1,n_2}(t)e_q(-ell t),                             (3)
and
 R_{chi,psi}(ell;n_1,n_2)
 =sum_{t modulo q}chi(a_0+u_1t)psi(c_0+u_2t)e_q(ell t).               (4)
Define
 M_W(n_1,n_2)
 =q^(-1)n^(-2)sum_{chi,psi}
   S(chi,psi)chi(n_2)psi(-n_1)
   sum_{ell modulo q; ell nonzero}
    R_{chi,psi}(ell;n_1,n_2)What_{n_1,n_2}(ell).                     (5)

Then the exact centered shared-digit determinant assembly with row weight omega and arbitrary column sequences alpha on I_1 and beta on I_2 is
 T_W(alpha,beta)
 =sum_{n_1 in I_1}sum_{n_2 in I_2}
   alpha(n_1)beta(n_2)M_W(n_1,n_2).                                 (6)
The complete ell=0 Jacobi contribution is absent from (5) because it cancels exactly after the full centered character assembly.

Let A_W:l^2(I_1)->l^2(I_2) be
 (A_Wx)(n_2)=sum_{n_1 in I_1}M_W(n_1,n_2)x(n_1).                     (7)
Then
 |T_W(alpha,beta)|
 <=||A_W||_op||alpha||_2||beta||_2.                                 (8)
Consequently the minimal balanced IJOP_{1/20} contract is the assertion that, for I_1,I_2 contained in [X,2X], all admitted moving row weights and lift selectors, and every epsilon>0,
 ||A_W||_op
 <=C_epsilon X^(19/20+epsilon)L_IJOP,                               (9)
where L_IJOP is an explicitly supplied nonnegative conductor, window, and lift-selector loss. Under (9),
 |T_W(alpha,beta)|
 <=C_epsilon X^(19/20+epsilon)L_IJOP
   ||alpha||_2||beta||_2.                                           (10)
Thus (9) is an X^(-1/20) operator saving relative to the declared dense X-scale, before L_IJOP. No assertion is made that (9) holds.

For the pure mode W(u)=e_m(ell_0u), ell_0 nonzero modulo m, fact 8230d44e6677f45b gives
 P_4(T_W)=n^2,  n^(-2)sum_{chi,psi}|S(chi,psi)|=1.                  (11)
Hence the raw four-fold norm n^2 is removed exactly by the n^(-2) character normalization in (5); it is not an additional factor in L_IJOP. Primitive and imprimitive characters are both retained in (5). Fact 55733dfba03775a2 shows that separating their unit gates into primitive-conductor progression pieces costs at most 4^(omega(m)), but does not remove either shifted primitive character or the additive twist.

There is a scoped no-direct-transference conclusion for two standard transforms.

First, expanding the row characters into additive Gauss modes and applying the untwisted Bettin--Chandee theorem term by term does not supply (9): fact d5ebef8af499c18f proves on q=p^2, X=p that the full centered pure-mode character assembly has absolute Gauss derivative ledger at least a constant times p^(7/2), and its termwise continuous main is not the complete centered Jacobi main.

Second, direct inverse-variable Fourier completion into classical Kloosterman sums does not supply (9) through the current fixed-modulus Blomer--Pascadi estimates. Fact d3fde76ac4c8c20d proves that this completion creates a full dual axis of length q and that the explicit unequal-length factor satisfies H_BP(q,N,q)>=1 for every second length N<=q. Therefore that direct completed theorem gives no q^(-eta) saving for any eta>0 relative to its Fourier-trivial l2 scale, even before the character, moving-window, literal-lift, and arbitrary-column assembly in (5) is paid.

These are no-direct-import statements only. They do not rule out cancellation inside the full sums in (5), a transform preserving two short axes, a character-pair large sieve adapted to the coupled shifts, or a direct proof of IJOP_{1/20}.
7cdcef43ec0d4940.proof:
Fix n_1,n_2. Fact 7a82b1642af6c8c2 gives
 (a,c)=(a_0+u_1t,c_0+u_2t)
and
 sum_t w_{n_1,n_2}(t)chi(a_0+u_1t)psi(c_0+u_2t)
 =q^(-1)sum_{ell modulo q}
  R_{chi,psi}(ell;n_1,n_2)What_{n_1,n_2}(ell).                       (12)
The zero extension in the statement is exactly the convention in that fact. Fact 8230d44e6677f45b gives
 T_W(a,b,c,d)
 =n^(-2)sum_{chi,psi}S(chi,psi)
   chi(a)chi(b)psi(c)psi(d).                                        (13)
In the legal orientation (m_1,m_2,n_1,n_2)=(a,c,-d,b), substitute b=n_2 and d=-n_1. Multiply (12) by chi(n_2)psi(-n_1)n^(-2)S(chi,psi), and sum chi,psi.

For ell=0, fact 382dadf452a0f461 proves
 n^(-2)sum_{chi,psi}S(chi,psi)chi(n_2)psi(-n_1)
 R_{chi,psi}(0;n_1,n_2)
 =sum_{u modulo m}W(u)=0.                                           (14)
The factor What_{n_1,n_2}(0) is independent of chi,psi, so it multiplies zero. The remaining frequencies are exactly (5). Multiplication by alpha(n_1)beta(n_2) and summation proves (6), with omega and every included selector retained before cancellation.

Write (6) as the l2 inner product of A_W alpha with the coordinatewise conjugate of beta. Cauchy--Schwarz gives (8), and (10) follows from (9). The exponent 19/20 in (9) is by definition an X^(-1/20) saving relative to the declared X-scale; no proof of (9) is claimed.

Fact 8230d44e6677f45b proves (11), and fact 55733dfba03775a2 proves the conductor progression ledger. This proves the normalization statements.

The first no-direct assertion is Part (C) of fact d5ebef8af499c18f, which treats the full centered pure-mode assembly and proves both the p^(7/2) ledger and the main mismatch. This exceeds the target scale in (9) for X=p.

For the second assertion, fact d3fde76ac4c8c20d proves the exact inverse-variable completion, its full dual axis, and H_BP(q,N,q)>=1 from Blomer--Pascadi Theorem 5.5. A displayed theorem factor at least one gives no fixed negative power of q relative to its baseline. Additional character, window, lift, or column sums require a new cancellation theorem and are not supplied by that direct application.

glossary.A_W: the two-column operator with matrix M_W
glossary.IJOP_{1/20}: the X^(19/20+epsilon) spectral-norm contract for the centered assembled incomplete-Jacobi matrix
glossary.L_IJOP: the explicitly declared conductor, moving-window, and lift-selector loss in IJOP_{1/20}
