glossary.M_W(n_1,n_2): the exact centered windowed incomplete-Jacobi matrix entry after full character and nonzero-additive-frequency assembly
glossary.omega_{n_1,n_2}(a,c): the common finite row weight retaining both moving windows and any literal lift selector

7d26c3f3b82d9b71.title: CRITICAL k=3 FIRST-CROSSING COEFFICIENT AND SAME-LEVEL WELL-FACTORABILITY SUPPORT OBSTRUCTION. Let 2<=L<=S, let L<Z, and put I=(L,Z). Let p_1,...,p_6 be six distinct primes not exceeding L. Put
7d26c3f3b82d9b71.author: slava chan
7d26c3f3b82d9b71.statement:
CRITICAL k=3 FIRST-CROSSING COEFFICIENT AND SAME-LEVEL WELL-FACTORABILITY SUPPORT OBSTRUCTION. Let 2<=L<=S, let L<Z, and put I=(L,Z). Let p_1,...,p_6 be six distinct primes not exceeding L. Put
y=p_1p_2p_3,  u=p_4p_5p_6,  X=min(p_1,p_2,p_3),
and assume
S<y,  y/p_i<=S for i=1,2,3,
and that none of the prime factors of u lies in I. For positive integers y' define
lambda_u(y')=(-1)^3 mu(u) 1_{j_I(u)=0} Gamma_{3;L,S}(y')/binom(3+omega_L(u),3),
where Gamma, j_I and omega_L are given by the displayed formulas in the proof below. Then
Gamma_{3;L,S}(y)=1,  lambda_u(y)=1/20.                    (1)

Let D_f be a real number such that
y<=D_f<X^4.                                                (2)
A complex sequence lambda is called well-factorable of level D_f if, for every real factorization D_f=D_1D_2 with D_i>=1, it is a Dirichlet convolution lambda=gamma_1*gamma_2 of 1-bounded sequences gamma_i supported on positive integers at most D_i. It is triply well-factorable of level D_f if the analogous statement holds for every D_f=D_1D_2D_3, with three 1-bounded supported sequences. Every well-factorable or triply well-factorable sequence of level D_f vanishes at y. Consequently lambda_u is neither well-factorable nor triply well-factorable of level D_f. It is not a finite complex linear combination of sequences in either same-level class, and it admits no pointwise nonnegative majorant in either class.

In the genuine endpoint top-B block of fact 6edc174d83447911 one may take p_i=Q^(beta/6+O(1/log Q)), beta=6/5-C/log Q, with u and y the exact two three-prime stopping factors. With X=min(p_1,p_2,p_3), one has
y=Q^(beta/2+O(1/log Q)),  X^4=Q^(2beta/3+O(1/log Q)).
For every natural factorability level D_f in the nonempty interval
y<=D_f<X^4,                                                  (3)
including any available level D_f=Q^(3/5+o(1)) which contains the chosen y and remains below X^4, the exact nonzero top-B coefficient (1) cannot itself occupy a well-factorable or triply well-factorable coefficient slot. This is a pointwise coefficient-class no-fit. It does not rule out pre-Cauchy cancellation, a qu-product or Type-III transformation, a change of level or variables, a problem-specific seminorm comparison, or a new distribution theorem, and it proves no bound for top B, TOP-BC123-CMD-RED, the other anatomies, or Goldbach.
7d26c3f3b82d9b71.proof:
For completeness define
omega_L(v)=#{p:p is prime,p|v,p<=L},
j_I(v)=#{p:p is prime,p|v,L<p<Z},
and
Gamma_{3;L,S}(v)=1_{v squarefree, omega(v)=3, P^+(v)<=L, S<v}
times (1/3)#{p:p is prime,p|v,v/p<=S}.
The integer y is squarefree with exactly three prime factors, all at most L, it exceeds S, and removal of each of its three prime factors leaves a number at most S. Hence the counted set has cardinality three and Gamma_{3;L,S}(y)=1. Since u is the product of three distinct primes at most L, mu(u)=-1, omega_L(u)=3 and j_I(u)=0. Therefore
lambda_u(y)=(-1)^3(-1)/binom(6,3)=1/20,
proving (1). This is exactly the k=3 summand of the first-crossing identity in fact 6414b11506a84ff0, and fact 6edc174d83447911 verifies that such a genuine balanced block occurs in the endpoint top-B calculus.

We next prove the support obstruction directly from the reproduced definitions, which agree with Maynard arXiv:2006.07088, Definitions 1 and 2, and Lichtman--Drappeau arXiv:2309.08522, Definitions 1.3 and 1.4. Suppose lambda is well-factorable of level D_f and use the permitted factorization
D_f=sqrt(D_f) sqrt(D_f).
If a summand gamma_1(a)gamma_2(b) in lambda(y) were nonzero, then ab=y and a,b<=sqrt(D_f). The three distinct primes p_1,p_2,p_3 must be partitioned between a and b. One of a,b contains at least two of them and is therefore at least X^2. But D_f<X^4 gives sqrt(D_f)<X^2, a contradiction. Hence the convolution sum is empty and lambda(y)=0.

If lambda is triply well-factorable, use the permitted factorization
D_f=1 times sqrt(D_f) times sqrt(D_f).
A nonzero convolution summand at y has first factor equal to one. The other two factors must partition all three primes, so again one contains at least two primes and is at least X^2>sqrt(D_f), a contradiction. Thus every sequence in either class vanishes at y. Finite complex linear combinations also vanish there. A pointwise nonnegative majorant M in either class would satisfy M(y)=0 but would have to obey M(y)>=|lambda_u(y)|=1/20, which is impossible.

Finally the endpoint scale assertions follow from fact 6edc174d83447911. Each p_i has scale Q^(beta/6+O(1/log Q)); hence their minimum X has the same scale. Multiplying three such scales gives y=Q^(beta/2+O(1/log Q)), and raising X to the fourth power gives X^4=Q^(2beta/3+O(1/log Q)). Since beta tends to 6/5, these are respectively Q^(3/5+o(1)) and Q^(4/5+o(1)), so (3) is nonempty for sufficiently large Q, and any natural Q^(3/5+o(1)) level which contains y and remains below X^4 falls under the support obstruction. The final scope sentence follows because the proof uses only pointwise support of the proposed coefficient class and makes no estimate for the assembled source.

glossary.X: the least of the three prime factors of the selected stopping variable y
glossary.lambda_u(y'): the fixed-u, k=3 first-crossing coefficient as a sequence of the marked stopping variable y'

7d341c8eec44f7a3.title: RANK-ONE RECIPROCAL-POLE STRATIFICATION WITH REPEATED POLES. Let \(\Bbbk\) be a field, let \(c\ge 1\) and \(l\ge 1\) be integers, and for \(1\le i\le 2l\) put \(\sigma_i=1\) when \(i\le l\) and \(\sigma_i=-1\) when \(i>l\). For \(r_i\in\Bbbk\) and \(s_i\in\Bbbk^\times\), define
7d341c8eec44f7a3.author: slava chan
7d341c8eec44f7a3.statement:
RANK-ONE RECIPROCAL-POLE STRATIFICATION WITH REPEATED POLES. Let \(\Bbbk\) be a field, let \(c\ge 1\) and \(l\ge 1\) be integers, and for \(1\le i\le 2l\) put \(\sigma_i=1\) when \(i\le l\) and \(\sigma_i=-1\) when \(i>l\). For \(r_i\in\Bbbk\) and \(s_i\in\Bbbk^\times\), define
\[
 \mathcal R(X)=\sum_{i=1}^{2l}\frac{\sigma_i}{s_i(X+r_i)^c}\in\Bbbk(X). \tag{1}
\]
Then the following conditions are equivalent:
\[
 \mathcal R(X)\text{ is constant}, \tag{2}
\]
\[
 \mathcal R(X)=0, \tag{3}
\]
and, for every \(a\in\Bbbk\) which occurs among \(r_1,\ldots,r_{2l}\),
\[
 \sum_{\substack{1\le i\le 2l\\ r_i=a}}\frac{\sigma_i}{s_i}=0. \tag{4}
\]
Consequently, the exceptional locus \(\mathcal E_l\) of tuples \((r_1,\ldots,r_{2l},s_1,\ldots,s_{2l})\in\mathbb A^{2l}_{\Bbbk}\times(\mathbb G_{m,\Bbbk})^{2l}\) satisfying (2) is a finite union of equal-pole partition strata. Its Zariski closure in \(\mathbb A^{4l}_{\Bbbk}\) has dimension at most \(2l\) and degree at most \((2l)^{4l}\). More precisely, if a set partition \(\pi\) of \(\{1,\ldots,2l\}\) has blocks \(B\), its stratum is empty when a block is a singleton; otherwise its closure has dimension at most \(2l\) and degree at most
\[
 \prod_{B\in\pi}(|B|-1). \tag{5}
\]
Thus pairwise matching of the two signed collections is only a special case of (4): repeated poles permit every signed reciprocal-scale relation in (4), not only pairwise coincidences.
7d341c8eec44f7a3.proof:
First prove (2) if and only if (3). Put \(Y=X^{-1}\). In the local coordinate \(Y\) at infinity, every summand of (1) is
\[
 \frac{\sigma_iY^c}{s_i(1+r_iY)^c}.
\]
It is regular at \(Y=0\) and vanishes there because \(c\ge1\). Hence \(\mathcal R\) vanishes at infinity. If \(\mathcal R\) is a constant rational function, that constant must therefore be zero. Conversely, the zero rational function is constant.

Let \(A\) be the finite set of distinct values among the \(r_i\), and for \(a\in A\) put
\[
 C_a=\sum_{i:r_i=a}\sigma_i s_i^{-1}.
\]
Grouping the terms in (1) with the same denominator gives the exact identity
\[
 \mathcal R(X)=\sum_{a\in A}C_a(X+a)^{-c}. \tag{6}
\]
If every \(C_a\) is zero, (6) gives (3). Conversely, suppose (3) holds and fix \(a\in A\). Multiply (6) by \((X+a)^c\) and evaluate at \(X=-a\). The summand indexed by \(a\) becomes \(C_a\). For every \(b\in A\) with \(b\ne a\), the corresponding summand becomes
\[
 C_b\frac{(X+a)^c}{(X+b)^c},
\]
which is regular at \(X=-a\) and has value zero there. Therefore \(C_a=0\). Since \(a\) was arbitrary, this proves (4), and the three conditions are equivalent.

It remains to prove the dimension and degree assertions. Fix a set partition \(\pi\) with \(b\) blocks. The exact \(\pi\)-stratum is cut out by \(r_i=r_j\) for indices in the same block, by the open inequalities requiring the \(r\)-values of different blocks to be distinct, by \(s_i\ne0\), and, for each block \(B\), by
\[
 \sum_{i\in B}\frac{\sigma_i}{s_i}=0. \tag{7}
\]
After multiplication by the nonzero product \(\prod_{j\in B}s_j\), equation (7) becomes
\[
 F_B((s_i)_{i\in B})
 =\sum_{i\in B}\sigma_i\prod_{\substack{j\in B\\j\ne i}}s_j=0. \tag{8}
\]
If \(|B|=1\), then \(F_B=\sigma_i\ne0\), so the stratum is empty. Assume henceforth that every block has at least two elements. The monomials in (8) are distinct and each coefficient \(\sigma_i\) is nonzero in \(\Bbbk\), including in characteristic two. Thus \(F_B\) is a nonzero polynomial of degree \(|B|-1\).

The equalities among the \(r_i\) leave one free \(r\)-coordinate per block, hence an affine space of dimension \(b\). The polynomials \(F_B\) use mutually disjoint groups of \(s\)-variables. Imposing one nonzero polynomial in each such group gives a product of hypersurfaces of dimension
\[
 \sum_{B\in\pi}(|B|-1)=2l-b
\]
in the \(2l\) scale coordinates. Therefore the closed set defined by the within-block \(r\)-equalities and all equations (8) has dimension
\[
 b+(2l-b)=2l. \tag{9}
\]
The exact stratum is its intersection with open conditions. Its closure is a union of irreducible components of that closed set, so its dimension is at most \(2l\). Because the equations (8) involve disjoint coordinate groups, their product of hypersurfaces has degree \(\prod_{B\in\pi}(|B|-1)\); the linear \(r\)-equalities do not change the degree. A union of components has degree at most the degree of the entire closed set, proving (5).

Finally, the equality pattern of the \(2l\) pole coordinates determines one of finitely many set partitions, so \(\mathcal E_l\) is the union of the corresponding strata. The number of partitions of a \(2l\)-element set is at most \((2l)^{2l}\), since every partition can be encoded non-injectively by assigning each element one of \(2l\) labels. For each partition, (5) is at most \((2l)^{2l}\). Degree is subadditive under finite unions of closed algebraic sets, hence
\[
 \deg\overline{\mathcal E_l}\le (2l)^{2l}(2l)^{2l}=(2l)^{4l}.
\]
Dimension under finite unions is the maximum of the component dimensions, hence is at most \(2l\). The final sentence follows directly from (4), whose block equations allow blocks with more than two indices.

glossary.F_B: The polynomial obtained by clearing the nonzero scale denominators in the pole-balance equation for block B.
glossary.\\\\mathcal E_l: The exceptional locus on which the rational function in equation (1) is constant.
glossary.\\\\mathcal R: The signed rank-one reciprocal-pole rational function defined in equation (1).
glossary.\\\\sigma_i: The fixed sign, equal to +1 in the first l positions and -1 in the last l positions.
glossary.equal-pole partition stratum: The locally closed locus on which a fixed set partition records exactly which pole shifts r_i are equal.

7dd43da40a79e813.title: ANATOMY-INDEPENDENT PRIME-LOCAL SQUARE-DIVISOR COLLISION FOR GA-TAIL-MARK ROWS
7dd43da40a79e813.author: slava chan
7dd43da40a79e813.statement:
ANATOMY-INDEPENDENT PRIME-LOCAL SQUARE-DIVISOR COLLISION FOR GA-TAIL-MARK ROWS.

Fix a prime \(p\). Let \(j=1,2\) index two exact marker copies from fact \(e55b27d39c593164\), with
\[
 n_j=d_jv_j,\qquad d_j=pm_j,\qquad (d_j,v_j)=1,
\]
and suppose \(p\) is a selected nonresonant prime for both copies. Let the two copies have the same nonzero integer target \(\mathscr A\), with \(p\nmid\mathscr A\), and let their designated signed frequencies \(h_1,h_2\) be nonzero modulo \(p\). In the prime-\(p\) completion of the reciprocal rows, the local inverse phases have slopes
\[
 s_j=\mathscr A h_j(v_jm_j)^{-1}\in\mathbb F_p^\times.
\]
Then
\[
 s_1=s_2
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 p^2\mid h_1n_2-h_2n_1.                                      \tag{1}
\]
Consequently, the exact nonzero-mode prime-local mixed Fourier Gram has order-one exceptional energy precisely on (1); off (1), its absolute value is at most \(2/p\).

This statement applies equally to the \(A\)-copies and every \(C_j\)-copy of GA-TAIL-MARK. It is only a local collision identity. It does not count the collision locus with literal weights, compare different selected primes or targets, prove GA-NR-DIL, estimate the good-\(\mathscr W\) tail, or imply Goldbach.
7dd43da40a79e813.proof:
Fact \(e55b27d39c593164\) proves for every exact \(A\)- or \(C_j\)-copy that \(n_j=d_jv_j\), with \(d_j=d_\star^{\rm tail}\) squarefree and \((d_j,v_j)=1\). Since \(p\mid d_j\) and \(d_j\) is squarefree, writing \(d_j=pm_j\) gives
\[
 p\nmid v_jm_j,\qquad v_jm_j={n_j\over p}.                    \tag{2}
\]
The selected prime is nonresonant, so in particular \(p\nmid\mathscr A\), and the hypotheses give \(p\nmid h_j\). Thus both displayed slopes are nonzero.

Facts \(3d10fd30e2a42246\) and \(79e2c44e5110d7a0\) prove that, for two rows with common selected prime and common target, the order-one mixed-mode exceptional locus is exactly equality of these local slopes. Since the common factor \(\mathscr A\) is a unit modulo \(p\), slope equality is equivalent to
\[
 h_1(v_1m_1)^{-1}\equiv h_2(v_2m_2)^{-1}\pmod p.
\]
Cross-multiplication by the two units and substitution of (2) give
\[
 h_1{n_2\over p}\equiv h_2{n_1\over p}\pmod p.
\]
Both \(n_1,n_2\) are divisible by \(p\), so the last congruence is equivalent over the integers to
\[
 p^2\mid h_1n_2-h_2n_1.
\]
This proves (1). Fact \(3d10fd30e2a42246\) gives the exact mixed-mode Gram and its off-collision absolute bound \(2/p\). No step uses the anatomy that produced \(d_j\), proving anatomy independence and the stated scope.

glossary.GA-tail prime-local collision: The common-p square-divisor exceptional relation p^2 dividing h_1 n_2-h_2 n_1.

7e8410900fa35f34.title: EXACT CARRIER-CORRELATED DIGIT GRAM BEFORE THE GENERIC L2 MAJORANT
7e8410900fa35f34.author: slava chan
7e8410900fa35f34.statement:
EXACT CARRIER-CORRELATED DIGIT GRAM BEFORE THE GENERIC L2 MAJORANT.

Let m>=9 be odd, put q=m^2, let s belong to {1,-1}, and let K be coprime to m. Choose an inverse K_bar of K modulo q. Let I be a finite set of integers n coprime to m. For every n in I and u modulo m let Z_{n,u} be a finite auxiliary label set. For z in Z_{n,u}, let h(n,u,z) be complex and let a(n,u,z) be an integer satisfying
 a(n,u,z)n congruent to A_u=K+2smu modulo q.                       (1)
Let beta be a complex sequence on I and W a complex function modulo m. Define
 H_n(u)=sum_{z in Z_{n,u}}h(n,u,z),qquad
 f_n(u)=W(u)H_n(u),                                                (2)
and
 C_corr(p)=sum_{n in I}sum_{u modulo m}sum_{z in Z_{n,u}}
 beta(n)W(u)h(n,u,z)e_q(-p a(n,u,z)^(-1))                          (3)
for p modulo q. Every inverse in (3) exists.

Put
 f_n_hat(ell)=sum_{u modulo m}f_n(u)e_m(-ell u),qquad
 gamma_n congruent to 2snK_bar^2 modulo m.                         (4)
Then
 C_corr(p)=sum_{n in I}beta(n)e_q(-pnK_bar)
 f_n_hat(-gamma_n p),                                              (5)
where p in the last argument is reduced modulo m.

Terms indexed by n,n' are orthogonal unless
 n is congruent to n' modulo m.                                   (6)
For n congruent to n' modulo m put
 j_{n,n'}=(n-n')/m
and
 tau_{n,n'} congruent to gamma_n^(-1)K_bar j_{n,n'} modulo m.       (7)
Then the exact Gram identity is
 ||C_corr||_2^2
 =m^2 sum_{n,n' in I;n congruent n' modulo m}
 beta(n)conjugate(beta(n'))
 sum_{u modulo m}f_n(u)conjugate(f_{n'}(u-tau_{n,n'})).             (8)
In particular, if I contains at most one representative of every residue modulo m, then
 ||C_corr||_2^2
 =m^2sum_{n in I}|beta(n)|^2||W H_n||_2^2.                         (9)

The complete fixed-fibre coefficient C_outer_hat of fact f23bad095a2e6a52 is an exact specialization: take n=n_2 and let z record (a,c,n_1,k,r_2,r_3), every recovered-prime, carrier, parity, moving-window and source selector, and the factor alpha(n_1)Omega_outer. Thus all genuine carrier correlations enter (5)-(9) only through the joint functions H_n(u) and, when a column interval contains repeated residue classes modulo m, through the finitely many shifted correlations in (8).

For a column block with at most one representative per residue and beta nonzero, define
 E_corr=
 [sum_n|beta(n)|^2||W H_n||_2^2]/||beta||_2^2.                    (10)
Then
 ||C_corr||_2/[q^(1/2)||beta||_2]=E_corr^(1/2).                    (11)
Fix delta>=0. If, after separately normalizing any external alpha/source scale inside H_n, this coefficient-norm route is required to satisfy, for every epsilon>0,
 E_corr^(1/2)<=m^(1/80-delta+epsilon),                             (12)
then necessarily, for every epsilon>0,
 E_corr<=m^(1/40-2delta+epsilon).                                  (13)
For H_n identically one and the literal W_star of fact 076bc0ba8fc2536a,
 E_corr=||W_star||_2^2>=m/6.                                      (14)
Thus the exact carrier-correlated question is an energy depletion of size nearly m^(-39/40), not support shortening of W_star alone. Equations (8)-(13) are a precise target, not a proof that the actual H_n has or lacks the required depletion.
7e8410900fa35f34.proof:
The congruence (1) and the unitness of n and A_u show that every a(n,u,z) is a unit modulo q and
 a(n,u,z)^(-1) congruent to nA_u^(-1) modulo q,                    (15)
independently of z. Fact c585f0febfbab2f4 gives
 A_u^(-1) congruent to K_bar-2smuK_bar^2 modulo q
and hence
 e_q(-pa(n,u,z)^(-1))
 =e_q(-pnK_bar)e_m(gamma_npu).                                    (16)
Sum (16) first over z and then over u. By (4), the result is (5).

For n,n' in I, their cross contribution to the squared norm is
 beta(n)conjugate(beta(n'))
 sum_{p modulo q}e_q(-pK_bar(n-n'))
 f_n_hat(-gamma_np)conjugate(f_{n'}_hat(-gamma_{n'}p)).             (17)
Write uniquely p=r+mt with r,t modulo m. The two Fourier factors depend only on r. The sum over t in (17) is
 sum_{t modulo m}e_m(-tK_bar(n-n')),
which is zero unless n is congruent to n' modulo m, and equals m otherwise. This proves (6).

Assume n-n'=mj_{n,n'}. Then gamma_n=gamma_{n'} modulo m. The remaining r-sum in (17), including the factor m from the t-sum, is
 m sum_{r modulo m}e_m(-rK_bar j_{n,n'})
 f_n_hat(-gamma_nr)conjugate(f_{n'}_hat(-gamma_nr)).                (18)
Change variables ell=-gamma_nr. The phase becomes
 e_m(tau_{n,n'}ell).
Expanding both Fourier transforms and using additive orthogonality gives
 sum_{ell modulo m}f_n_hat(ell)conjugate(f_{n'}_hat(ell))
 e_m(tau ell)
 =m sum_{u modulo m}f_n(u)conjugate(f_{n'}(u-tau)).                 (19)
Combining (18)-(19) gives (8). If I has no two congruent elements, only n=n' remains, j=tau=0, and (9) follows.

In fact f23bad095a2e6a52, every admitted tuple satisfies an_2 congruent to A_u modulo q, and its coefficient C_outer_hat is obtained by summing its weight against e_q(-pa^(-1)). Grouping the tuple labels other than n_2,u into z gives exactly (2)-(3), including all displayed gates and weights. This proves the specialization.

Divide (9) by q||beta||_2^2=m^2||beta||_2^2 to prove (11). Apply (12) with epsilon/2 in place of epsilon and square it; this gives (13). If H_n=1, (10) is ||W||_2^2, and fact 076bc0ba8fc2536a applies because m>=9, giving (14) for W_star. Comparing exponents 1 and 1/40-2delta is the energy form of the 39/80 amplitude gap in fact c1f29a6ce884c5ae. No property of the genuine H_n beyond its exact definition was assumed.

glossary.C_corr: the exact inverse-column Fourier coefficient with all auxiliary labels retained
glossary.H_n: the exact aggregate of all non-digit literal labels at fixed second column n and digit u
glossary.f_n: the joint digit-carrier coefficient W times H_n
glossary.tau_{n,n'}: the digit-correlation shift between two columns congruent modulo m

7e9251670db3e1c9.title: CRT-COMBINED-RAY-PHASE AUDIT, THE COHERENT UNIT-DENOMINATOR SLICE, AND THE GENUINE TWO-PARAMETER RAY-PAIR SUPPLIER
7e9251670db3e1c9.author: slava chan
7e9251670db3e1c9.statement:
CRT-COMBINED-RAY-PHASE AUDIT, THE COHERENT UNIT-DENOMINATOR SLICE, AND THE GENUINE TWO-PARAMETER RAY-PAIR SUPPLIER.

Adopt one exact canonical marked-dilator copy from fact 31ebcf364862d83a. Thus its normalized marked integer is
\[
 n=d_\lambda v_\lambda,\qquad (d_\lambda,v_\lambda)=1,
\]
its nonzero integer target is \(\mathscr A_{\rm tar}\), and its supported coordinates satisfy
\[
 (q,n)=1,\qquad (q,h)=k(a,\epsilon b)
\]
on a unique primitive signed ray
\[
 R=(\epsilon,a,b),\qquad \epsilon\in\{-1,1\},\quad a,b>0,\quad (a,b)=1.
\]
Let \(c_\lambda(q,h)\) be the complete literal coefficient before the reciprocity factors displayed in fact 41b56ed8e64bdba6 for the top \(B,C1,C2,C3,C4\) copies and in fact e55b27d39c593164 for the good-\(\mathscr W\) \(A,C_j\) copies. Define
\[
 B_\lambda(R)=\sum_{k:\ c_\lambda(ka,\epsilon kb)\ne0}
 c_\lambda(ka,\epsilon kb).                                      \tag{1}
\]
Every source, marker, Möbius, Fourier, target-gcd, fixed-\(U\), parent, order, equality, collision, deletion, provenance, coprimality and projective factor stays inside (1).

Put
\[
 I_{\infty,\lambda}(R)
 =e\!\left(-{\mathscr A_{\rm tar}\epsilon b\over
                    a d_\lambda v_\lambda}\right),\qquad
 I_{v,\lambda}(R)
 =e_{v_\lambda}\!\left(
   \mathscr A_{\rm tar}\epsilon b(a d_\lambda)^{-1}\right).   \tag{2}
\]
If \(S_\lambda(R)\) is the post-reciprocity primitive-ray coefficient in facts 57a4d0753d8f290d and 31ebcf364862d83a, then
\[
 \boxed{S_\lambda(R)
 =I_{\infty,\lambda}(R)I_{v,\lambda}(R)B_\lambda(R).}          \tag{3}
\]
In particular, the spectral array \(R_\lambda(x)\) in fact
31ebcf364862d83a contains the two ray-dependent multipliers in (2).

For two rays
\[
 R=(\epsilon,a,b),\qquad R'=(\epsilon',a',b'),
\]
write
\[
 \Delta_0(R,R')=\epsilon ba'-\epsilon'b'a.                     \tag{4}
\]
On every supported ordered pair, \((aa',d_\lambda v_\lambda)=1\), and the product of the \(d_\lambda\)-modulus ray phase and the exposed \(v_\lambda\)-modulus ray phase is exactly
\[
 \boxed{
 e_{d_\lambda v_\lambda}\!\left(
 \mathscr A_{\rm tar}\Delta_0(R,R')(aa')^{-1}\right).
 }                                                                 \tag{CRT-COMBINED-RAY-PHASE}
\]
The product of the two Archimedean factors is
\[
 e\!\left(-{\mathscr A_{\rm tar}\Delta_0(R,R')
                   \over aa'd_\lambda v_\lambda}\right).
\]
Consequently additive reciprocity gives the exact full physical ray-pair phase
\[
 \boxed{
 e_{aa'}\!\left(
 -\mathscr A_{\rm tar}\Delta_0(R,R')
 (d_\lambda v_\lambda)^{-1}\right).
 }                                                                 \tag{5}
\]
Equivalently, the original row before reciprocity has the ray compression
\[
 K_\lambda
 =\sum_R B_\lambda(R)
 e_a\!\left(-\mathscr A_{\rm tar}\epsilon b
 (d_\lambda v_\lambda)^{-1}\right).                            \tag{6}
\]

The slice \(a=a'=1\) is exactly coherent: for every supported pair on this slice the phase in (5) is the unique additive character modulo one and hence equals \(1\), including when \(R\ne R'\) and the pair is nonresonant. In the CRT representation, the factor
\[
 e_{d_\lambda v_\lambda}
   (\mathscr A_{\rm tar}\Delta_0)
\]
is canceled exactly by its Archimedean companion
\[
 e(-\mathscr A_{\rm tar}\Delta_0/(d_\lambda v_\lambda)).
\]
This asserts neither existence nor largeness of the literal coefficient mass on that slice. It proves that inverse-\(v_\lambda\) randomness supplies no physical phase cancellation there.

The literal complementary-factor inventory is as follows.

1. On a good-\(\mathscr W\) \(C_j\) copy of fact e55b27d39c593164, \(v_\lambda\in\{1,2\}\).
2. On a good-\(\mathscr W\) \(A\) copy, \(v_\lambda=p\) is the marked prime with \(2<p<Z_\theta\).
3. On a top \(B\) copy of fact f0f6807663d3ef3c, \(v_\lambda=u\) in the exact stopping representation \(n=uy\), \(d_\lambda=y\), with \(S_0<y\le S_0L\), and in particular \(u<2B/S_0\).
4. On a top \(C_j\) copy, \(v_\lambda\) is the exact small cofactor satisfying \(v_\lambda\le S_0\); it is not asserted to lie in \(\{1,2\}\).

Thus the good-\(\mathscr W\) \(C_j\) branch has no long \(v_\lambda\)-average, while the good-\(\mathscr W\) \(A\) and top \(B,C_j\) branches have respectively prime or source-constrained small complementary factors.

Let \(\mathscr L\) be any one of the exact fixed-orientation, fixed-anatomy, fixed-frequency and fixed-dilator-block families above. Define the signed two-parameter nonresonant ray-pair form
\[
 \mathfrak S_{\mathscr L}^{\rm NR}
 =
 \sum_{\lambda\in\mathscr L}
 \sum_{\substack{R\ne R'\\
 d_\lambda\nmid
 \mathscr A_{\rm tar}\Delta_0(R,R')}}
 B_\lambda(R)\overline{B_\lambda(R')}
 e_{aa'}\!\left(
 -\mathscr A_{\rm tar}\Delta_0(R,R')
 (d_\lambda v_\lambda)^{-1}\right).                            \tag{7}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{\mathfrak S_{\mathscr L}^{\rm NR}
 =\mathcal M_{\mathscr L}^{({\rm NR})}.}                       \tag{8}
\]
For a good-\(\mathscr W\) anatomy in a block
\(\mathcal D\le d_\lambda<2\mathcal D\), the genuinely source-specific supplier is therefore
\[
 |\mathfrak S_{\mathscr L}^{\rm NR}|
 \ll_\varepsilon
 x^\varepsilon|\omega_F|^2{BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}.           \tag{DV-RAY-PAIR}
\]
It is exactly GA-RAY-SPEC, equivalently the anatomy-restricted GA-NR-DIL consumer of fact 31ebcf364862d83a. Summing (7) over the exact top
\(B,C1,C2,C3,C4\) copies and replacing the right side by
\[
 Q^\varepsilon{BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}
\]
is exactly TOP-CS5-RAY-SPEC.

The specified reduced-conductor frequency in fact 31ebcf364862d83a is
\[
 \xi_\lambda\equiv
 (\mathscr A_{\rm tar}/(d_\lambda,\mathscr A_{\rm tar}))
 v_\lambda^{-1}
 \pmod{d_\lambda/(d_\lambda,\mathscr A_{\rm tar})}.
\]
Equations (2)--(3) show that, as \(v_\lambda\) varies, the sampled array
\(R_\lambda\) also varies ray by ray, even before accounting for the
literal \(v_\lambda\)-dependence of \(B_\lambda\). Therefore generic equidistribution of \(\xi_\lambda\) is not a legal independent-sample proof of DV-RAY-PAIR.

Finally, Bettin--Chandee's separated scalar trilinear Kloosterman-fraction theorem, in the exact verified form quoted in fact df9748efe29ab475, does not directly specialize to (7). Its coefficient is a product of three independent sequences and its phase has one separated numerator, one inverse variable and one modulus. In (7), the coefficient \(B_\lambda(R)\overline{B_\lambda(R')}\) depends jointly on \(d_\lambda,v_\lambda,R,R'\) through the literal source and masks; the numerator \(\Delta_0\) and modulus \(aa'\) both depend on the same ray pair; and the deletion
\(d_\lambda\nmid\mathscr A_{\rm tar}\Delta_0\) is pair-dependent. Hence a direct substitution into that theorem would require an unproved source-specific separated or bounded-projective decomposition preserving the signed sum and the deletion. This is a scoped no-direct-specialization statement. It does not rule out such a decomposition or a new vector-valued/two-parameter theorem, and it proves neither DV-RAY-PAIR, GA-RAY-SPEC, TOP-CS5-RAY-SPEC, a tail payment, nor Goldbach.
7e9251670db3e1c9.proof:
For a supported point on \(R=(\epsilon,a,b)\), write
\[
 (q,h)=(ka,\epsilon kb).
\]
Because \((q,d_\lambda v_\lambda)=1\), each of
\(k,a,d_\lambda,v_\lambda\) is coprime to every modulus in which it is inverted below. The two factors used to pass from the pre-reciprocity coefficient to the post-reciprocity coefficient are, by facts 41b56ed8e64bdba6 and e55b27d39c593164,
\[
 e\!\left(-{\mathscr A_{\rm tar}h\over
 qd_\lambda v_\lambda}\right)
 e_{v_\lambda}\!\left(
 \mathscr A_{\rm tar}h(qd_\lambda)^{-1}\right).
\]
Substituting \(q=ka\), \(h=\epsilon kb\) cancels \(k\) in both factors and gives exactly (2). They are constant along the supported scaling set of one primitive ray. Summing the defining identity for the post-reciprocity coefficient over \(k\) proves (3).

The \(d_\lambda\)-modulus ray factor from fact
57a4d0753d8f290d is
\[
 P_{d,\lambda}(R)
 =
 e_{d_\lambda}\!\left(
 \mathscr A_{\rm tar}\epsilon b(av_\lambda)^{-1}\right).
\]
For two rays, putting the difference over the common unit denominator
\(aa'v_\lambda\) gives
\[
 P_{d,\lambda}(R)\overline{P_{d,\lambda}(R')}
 =
 e_{d_\lambda}\!\left(
 \mathscr A_{\rm tar}\Delta_0(aa'v_\lambda)^{-1}\right).     \tag{9}
\]
The analogous calculation with the second factor in (2) gives
\[
 I_{v,\lambda}(R)\overline{I_{v,\lambda}(R')}
 =
 e_{v_\lambda}\!\left(
 \mathscr A_{\rm tar}\Delta_0(aa'd_\lambda)^{-1}\right).     \tag{10}
\]
Since \((d_\lambda,v_\lambda)=1\), the Chinese remainder identity
\[
 e_d(Xv^{-1})e_v(Xd^{-1})=e_{dv}(X)
\]
applied to
\[
 X=\mathscr A_{\rm tar}\Delta_0(aa')^{-1}
\]
multiplies (9) and (10) into CRT-COMBINED-RAY-PHASE.

The first factors in (2) give
\[
 I_{\infty,\lambda}(R)
 \overline{I_{\infty,\lambda}(R')}
 =
 e\!\left(-{\mathscr A_{\rm tar}\Delta_0
                 \over aa'd_\lambda v_\lambda}\right).       \tag{11}
\]
The elementary additive reciprocity identity, valid for coprime positive integers \(m,n\),
\[
 e_n(Xm^{-1})e(-X/(mn))=e_m(-Xn^{-1}),
\]
with \(m=aa'\), \(n=d_\lambda v_\lambda\), proves (5) from CRT-COMBINED-RAY-PHASE and (11). Applying the same identity to one ray, or simply substituting \((q,h)=(ka,\epsilon kb)\) in the original character, gives
\[
 e_q(-\mathscr A_{\rm tar}h(d_\lambda v_\lambda)^{-1})
 =
 e_a(-\mathscr A_{\rm tar}\epsilon b
          (d_\lambda v_\lambda)^{-1}),
\]
which proves (6).

If \(a=a'=1\), the modulus in (5) is one, so the phase equals one. In the preceding representation, CRT-COMBINED-RAY-PHASE is
\[
 e_{d_\lambda v_\lambda}
 (\mathscr A_{\rm tar}\Delta_0),
\]
while (11) is its inverse. This proves the coherent-slice assertion without any claim about the size of its coefficient.

The four complementary-factor descriptions follow directly from the exact marker definitions in facts e55b27d39c593164 and f0f6807663d3ef3c. In the top \(B\) case,
\(n<2B\) and \(d_\lambda=y>S_0\), so
\[
 v_\lambda=u=n/y<2B/S_0.
\]
No stronger inventory is used.

Expand \(|K_\lambda|^2\) using (6). Fact
57a4d0753d8f290d proves that for supported scalings the TT-star determinant is a unit multiple of \(\Delta_0\), so the nonresonant selector is exactly
\[
 d_\lambda\nmid\mathscr A_{\rm tar}\Delta_0
\]
and is constant on the ordered ray pair. The off-diagonal ray-pair phase is (5). Therefore the nonresonant restriction of the expansion is exactly the \(\lambda\)-summand in (7). Summing over \(\mathscr L\) proves (8). Fact
31ebcf364862d83a identifies the required good-\(\mathscr W\) and top bounds for this same nonresonant moment, proving the consumer equivalences.

To see the correlation in the spectral form, use (3) in the definition
\[
 R_\lambda(x)
 =\sum_{R:\ x_\lambda(R)=x}S_\lambda(R)
\]
from fact 31ebcf364862d83a. Both multipliers in (2) depend on the ray through \(\epsilon b/a\) and on \(v_\lambda\); moreover the literal pre-reciprocity coefficient in (1) may itself depend on \(v_\lambda\). Thus changing \(v_\lambda\) changes both the specified frequency and the array being sampled. This proves the independent-sample no-fit.

Fact df9748efe29ab475 states the exact three-separated-sequence interface of the Bettin--Chandee theorem. Inspection of (7) gives the three listed mismatches: joint coefficient dependence, shared ray dependence of numerator and modulus, and pair-dependent deletion. Therefore no direct variable substitution is licensed. This is only the stated interface comparison, so all final limitations follow.

glossary.B_lambda(R): The complete pre-reciprocity literal coefficient summed over supported positive scalings on the primitive signed ray R.
glossary.CRT-COMBINED-RAY-PHASE: The product of the d_lambda- and v_lambda-modulus primitive-ray pair phases before restoring the Archimedean reciprocity factor.
glossary.DV-RAY-PAIR: The source-specific signed two-parameter d_lambda,v_lambda and ordered-ray-pair estimate displayed in the statement.
glossary.Delta_0(R,R'): The primitive ray-pair determinant epsilon b a'-epsilon' b'a.
glossary.I_infinity,lambda(R): The Archimedean reciprocity multiplier on one primitive ray.
glossary.I_v,lambda(R): The complementary-factor v_lambda-modulus CRT multiplier on one primitive ray.
glossary.unit-denominator ray slice: The ordered primitive-ray pairs with a=a'=1, on which the full physical phase is identically one.

7ee795d9bff04bb2.title: GA-CqADD-TT*: EXACT LITERAL SOURCE RAMANUJAN GRAM, POLYLOGARITHMIC TRANSITION PAYMENT, AND THE FIRST MISSING CROSS-n CORRELATION
7ee795d9bff04bb2.author: slava chan
7ee795d9bff04bb2.statement:
GA-CqADD-TT*: EXACT LITERAL SOURCE RAMANUJAN GRAM, POLYLOGARITHMIC TRANSITION PAYMENT, AND THE FIRST MISSING CROSS-n CORRELATION.

Adopt the exact GA-CqADD-VEC setting of fact d3278c2897e20003. Thus
Dcal<=Q^2,  Y=Q^2/Dcal>=1,                                           (1)
and fix one dyadic additive-conductor block
T<=t<2T,  t>Y.                                                       (2)
Every retained term has a squarefree physical conductor
m_q=st,
a unit c=C_q modulo t, a physical source value
n=dv,
the exact Hilbert ray coefficient B_bold_{d,v}(R), and every pair-dependent literal selector of that fact.

Let Gamma_T be the finite set of triples
gamma=(t,s,c)                                                        (3)
that occur in the retained block. For gamma=(t,s,c) and a positive integer n, define
Z_gamma(n)
 =sum_{d v=n}
  sum_{exact retained R != R' with m_q=st and C_q=c}
  mu(s)/s
  <B_bold_{d,v}(R),B_bold_{d,v}(R')>.                               (4)
All conditions in the phrase "exact retained" are exactly those of GA-CqADD-VEC, including the hard source support and pair-dependent deletion; unsupported terms are zero. No coefficient or selector is replaced.

On l2((Z/tZ)^*) use the vectors of fact d3278c2897e20003,
V_gamma=V_{t;c,s},
E_{t;n}(a)=t^{-1/2}e_t(an),                                          (5)
and define the exact source vector
G_gamma=sum_n conjugate(Z_gamma(n))E_{t;n}.                           (6)
Then the literal dyadic block has the exact TT-star form
H_C^{q-add-large}(T)
 =sum_{gamma in Gamma_T}<V_gamma,G_gamma>.                           (7)

For every positive squarefree t and all integers n,n',
<E_{t;n},E_{t;n'}>
 =c_t(n-n')/t,                                                       (8)
where c_t is the Ramanujan sum. Consequently
||G_gamma||_2^2
 ={1/t}sum_{n,n'}
  conjugate(Z_gamma(n))Z_gamma(n')c_t(n-n')                          (9)
 ={phi(t)over t}sum_n|Z_gamma(n)|^2
  +{1over t}sum_{n!=n'}
   conjugate(Z_gamma(n))Z_gamma(n')c_t(n-n').                        (10)
For squarefree t, if g=gcd(t,n-n'), then
c_t(n-n')=mu(t/g)phi(g).                                             (11)
Thus (9) is the exact signed cross-n Ramanujan Gram of the actual n=dv source family.

For arbitrary positive weights rho_gamma, Cauchy in the direct sum of the primitive additive-frequency spaces gives
|H_C^{q-add-large}(T)|^2
 <=[
 sum_gamma rho_gamma
 product_{p|t_gamma}(p-1-1/p)]
 [
 sum_gamma rho_gamma^{-1}
 {1over t_gamma}sum_{n,n'}
 conjugate(Z_gamma(n))Z_gamma(n')c_{t_gamma}(n-n')
 ].                                                                  (GA-RAM-GRAM(T))
The first bracket uses the exact norm
||V_gamma||_2^2=product_{p|t_gamma}(p-1-1/p)
from fact d3278c2897e20003. Therefore a sufficient deletion-preserving source-specific supplier for this block is that the right side of GA-RAM-GRAM(T) be at most
x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^4 B^2Y^2F^4.                                     (12)
Under (12),
|H_C^{q-add-large}(T)|
 <=x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 B YF^2,                                     (13)
the required canonical scale. Estimate (12) is not asserted.

There are two exact scope audits.

First, the source values n=dv lie in an interval of length O(B). Additive Plancherel and residue-class Cauchy give
||G_gamma||_2^2
 <=sum_{r (mod t)}
   |sum_{n congruent r (mod t)}conjugate(Z_gamma(n))|^2
 <<(1+B/t)sum_n|Z_gamma(n)|^2.                                     (14)
This occupancy bound is not a fixed-power gain over the diagonal term in (10). Hence support length and distinct physical values alone do not remove the t^{1/2+o(1)} norm scale of V_gamma. A successful use of GA-RAM-GRAM(T) must prove additional cancellation in the literal signed off-diagonal term of (10), exploit cancellation between different gamma before Cauchy, or supply another source-specific correlation. This is a theorem-interface statement, not a lower bound for the literal block.

Second, fix a real C_0>0. Fact d3278c2897e20003 proves absolutely
|H_C^{q-add}(T)|
 <=x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 BTF^2.                                      (15)
Therefore every transition block satisfying
Y<T<=Y(log(2x))^{C_0}                                                (16)
is already paid at the canonical scale (13), after absorbing the fixed polylogarithm into x^{o(1)}. This does not close additive conductors beyond every fixed-polylogarithmic multiple of Y.

The identities (8)-(11), the weighted direct-sum inequality GA-RAM-GRAM(T), and the implication (12) to (13) are anatomy-independent for any finite row family that supplies grouped coefficients Z_gamma(n). The literal definition (4), the support n=dv in a B-scale interval, the target (12), and the absolute transition payment (15)-(16) are Good-W-specific.

This theorem proves the exact TT-star/Ramanujan-Gram reduction, (14), and the polylogarithmic transition payment. It does not prove (12) on the genuinely large range, all of GA-qCENT, P-qSRC-SUP, C-qSRC-SUP, GA-RAY-SPEC, GA-NR-DIL, a good-W tail payment, or Goldbach.
7ee795d9bff04bb2.proof:
Start from GA-CqADD-VEC in fact d3278c2897e20003 and restrict its finite divisor sum to (2). Every term is indexed by d,v,R,R',s,t and has value
mu(s)/s
<B_bold_{d,v}(R),B_bold_{d,v}(R')>
<V_{t;C_q,s},E_{t;dv}>.                                             (17)
Group this finite sum first by gamma=(t,s,C_q), and then by n=dv. The scalar coefficient left after this grouping is exactly (4). Because the inner product convention is linear in its first argument and conjugate-linear in its second,
Z_gamma(n)<V_gamma,E_{t;n}>
 =<V_gamma,conjugate(Z_gamma(n))E_{t;n}>.                            (18)
Sum (18) over n and gamma. This proves (6)-(7). Since the grouping is finite and (4) sums only exact retained terms, every source coefficient and pair deletion is unchanged.

For (8), use the definition (5):
<E_{t;n},E_{t;n'}>
 ={1over t}sum_{a (mod t)}^*
 e_t(an)conjugate(e_t(an'))
 ={1over t}sum_{a (mod t)}^*e_t(a(n-n'))
 ={c_t(n-n')over t}.                                                (19)
Expand the squared norm of (6) using (19). This gives (9). The diagonal n=n' has c_t(0)=phi(t), giving (10). The standard formula
c_t(k)=mu(t/g)phi(t)/phi(t/g),  g=gcd(t,k),                           (20)
reduces to (11) when t is squarefree because g and t/g are coprime and phi(t)=phi(g)phi(t/g).

For positive rho_gamma, write
<V_gamma,G_gamma>
 =<rho_gamma^{1/2}V_gamma,rho_gamma^{-1/2}G_gamma>
inside the Hilbert direct sum over gamma. Cauchy gives
|sum_gamma<V_gamma,G_gamma>|^2
 <=(sum_gamma rho_gamma||V_gamma||_2^2)
   (sum_gamma rho_gamma^{-1}||G_gamma||_2^2).                         (21)
Insert the exact V norm from d3278c2897e20003 and (9). This proves GA-RAM-GRAM(T). If its right side satisfies (12), taking square roots proves (13).

We prove (14). The primitive-frequency sum is bounded by the full additive-frequency sum:
||G_gamma||_2^2
 ={1over t}sum_{a (mod t)}^*
  |sum_n conjugate(Z_gamma(n))e_t(an)|^2
 <={1over t}sum_{a (mod t)}
  |sum_n conjugate(Z_gamma(n))e_t(an)|^2.                            (22)
Full additive Plancherel makes the last expression
sum_{r (mod t)}
 |sum_{n congruent r (mod t)}conjugate(Z_gamma(n))|^2.               (23)
Facts cff9d29efb555b8e and d3278c2897e20003 retain n=dv on one B-scale source interval, so each residue class contains O(1+B/t) possible n. Apply Cauchy inside each residue class and then sum to prove (14). The diagonal term in (10) is phi(t)/t times sum|Z|^2, with phi(t)/t=t^{o(1)}; therefore (14) alone supplies no fixed-power suppression of that diagonal. This proves the stated method limitation without asserting that the off-diagonal literal sum cannot cancel it.

Finally, (15) is equation (12) of fact d3278c2897e20003 for the identical dyadic block with all selectors retained. Under (16),
BTF^2<=BYF^2(log(2x))^{C_0}.
A fixed power of log(2x) is x^{o(1)}, so (15) implies (13). The implication uses no TT-star estimate and does not extend beyond a fixed-polylogarithmic transition. All anatomy-independence and Good-W-specific scope statements follow by inspection of which inputs were used, and every exclusion follows.

glossary.GA-RAM-GRAM(T): The exact weighted TT-star Ramanujan-Gram supplier for one dyadic large additive-conductor block t asymptotic to T.
glossary.G_gamma: The primitive additive-frequency source vector sum_n conjugate(Z_gamma(n))E_{t;n}.
glossary.Z_gamma(n): The exact signed Good-W source coefficient at physical value n after grouping a dyadic additive-conductor block by gamma=(t,s,C_q).

7f267d0a3e5b2b52.title: EXACT TENSOR TIGHT FRAME FOR THE SIMULTANEOUS COMPULSORY ROUGH FACTOR
7f267d0a3e5b2b52.author: slava chan
7f267d0a3e5b2b52.statement:
EXACT TENSOR TIGHT FRAME FOR THE SIMULTANEOUS COMPULSORY ROUGH FACTOR.

Let L>1 be odd and squarefree. Identify its unit group
 U_L=(Z/LZ)^*
with the product of the nonzero residue groups modulo p over p|L. For C,a in U_L write C_p,a_p for their p-coordinates and define
 r_{L,C}(a)
  =product_{p|L}
    [e_p(C_p a_p^(-1))+1/(p-1)].                            (1)

For a complex function eta on U_L and a prime p|L define the coordinatewise mean-zero projection
 (Pi_p eta)(C)
  =eta(C)
   -1/(p-1)
    sum_{D in U_L;D_q=C_q for every q|L,q!=p}eta(D).         (2)
The projections Pi_p commute. Put
 Pi_L=product_{p|L}Pi_p.                                    (3)
Then for C,D in U_L,
 1/phi(L)sum_{a in U_L}
  r_{L,C}(a)overline(r_{L,D}(a))
 =
 L/phi(L)
 product_{p|L}[1_{C_p=D_p}-1/(p-1)].                        (4)
Consequently,
 1/phi(L)sum_{a in U_L}
  |sum_{C in U_L}eta(C)r_{L,C}(a)|^2
 =
 L/phi(L)sum_{C in U_L}|(Pi_L eta)(C)|^2.                   (5)
Thus the nonzero frame eigenvalue is exactly L/phi(L), and the kernel consists of the orthogonal complement of the subspace of functions that have zero mean separately in every prime coordinate.

Assume now the nonzero canonical factorization b=Lb_0 from fact 9fd295b783317ab1, with L=L_b. For all sufficiently large Q, fact 6e68e64eb87d4f42 gives every p|L the inequality
 p>b/F_0=Q^(1/3+2eta+o(1))>2,
so this actual L is odd. Also (L,Nb_0)=1. For each prime p|L define
 C_p(b_0)
  =N[(L/p)b_0]^(-1) (mod p).                                (6)
There is a unique C(b_0) in U_L with these local coordinates, and
 R_{b,L}(a)=r_{L,C(b_0)}(a).                                (7)
As b_0 ranges through a complete reduced residue system modulo L, C(b_0) also ranges through a complete reduced residue system modulo L. Hence the complementary residue b_0 modulo L is exactly a permuted tensor-frame index.

Equations (4)-(5) apply to scalar coefficients eta(C) independent of a. They do not by themselves control the actual a-dependent recursive projector multiplying (7). No incomplete-a vector restriction estimate, ROP estimate, CEN-MZB estimate, C_small estimate or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
7f267d0a3e5b2b52.proof:
Every prime divisor p of the odd integer L satisfies p>2. Therefore fact 0d1daae6c3854186 applies at each p and proves the local Gram identity
 1/(p-1)sum_{a_p nonzero}
  r_{p,C_p}(a_p)overline(r_{p,D_p}(a_p))
 =
 p/(p-1)[1_{C_p=D_p}-1/(p-1)],                              (8)
where
 r_{p,C_p}(a_p)=e_p(C_pa_p^(-1))+1/(p-1).

Because L is squarefree, the Chinese remainder theorem identifies the unit variable a with the independent tuple (a_p)_{p|L}. Definition (1) is the product of the corresponding local rows. Therefore the normalized Gram on the left of (4) factors as the product of (8). The product of the scalar factors p/(p-1) is L/phi(L), proving (4).

For fixed p, formula (2) is the orthogonal projection that subtracts the p-coordinate average while keeping all other coordinates fixed. Projections acting in distinct coordinates commute, so Pi_L is an orthogonal projection. Its matrix entry from D to C is
 product_{p|L}[1_{C_p=D_p}-1/(p-1)].                         (9)
Multiply (4) by eta(C)overline(eta(D)) and sum over C,D. The right side is L/phi(L) times the quadratic form of the orthogonal projection Pi_L. Since Pi_L is self-adjoint and idempotent, that quadratic form equals
 sum_C|(Pi_Leta)(C)|^2.
This proves (5). Because every p>2, each local mean-zero subspace has positive dimension p-2, so the range of Pi_L is nonzero. The frame operator is L/phi(L)Pi_L, proving the stated nonzero eigenvalue and kernel.

Now assume b=Lb_0 is the canonical factorization. Fact 6e68e64eb87d4f42 proves that every p|L satisfies p>b/F_0 and that b/F_0=Q^(1/3+2eta+o(1)). Since eta>0 is fixed, this lower bound exceeds two for all sufficiently large Q. Hence the actual L is odd and the preceding frame theorem applies. Squarefreeness gives (L,b_0)=1, and the nonzero condition in fact 9fd295b783317ab1 gives (L,N)=1. Thus every residue in (6) is nonzero and invertible.

The p-local factor in R_{b,L}(a) is
 e_p(N[a(b/p)]^(-1))+1/(p-1).
Since b/p=(L/p)b_0,
 N[a(b/p)]^(-1)
 =N[(L/p)b_0]^(-1)a_p^(-1)
 =C_p(b_0)a_p^(-1) (mod p).                                 (10)
Multiplying (10) over p|L proves (7).

For each p|L, the map
 b_0 (mod p) -> N(L/p)^(-1)b_0^(-1) (mod p)
is a permutation of the nonzero residues because inversion and multiplication by a fixed nonzero residue are permutations. Taking the product over p and using the Chinese remainder theorem proves that b_0 modulo L maps bijectively to C(b_0) in U_L.

Formula (5) holds for one fixed scalar vector eta while a is averaged. The recursive factor in fact 9fd295b783317ab1 varies with a, so no substitution of that factor as eta is made. This proves all scope restrictions.

glossary.Pi_L: The product of the coordinatewise mean-zero projections on functions on U_L.
glossary.U_L: The unit group modulo the odd squarefree integer L.
glossary.r_{L,C}(a): The tensor product of centered reciprocal traces over primes dividing L.

7f63ca7922a7fab9.title: DIVISOR-SELECTED CROSSED-NUMERATOR REINDEXING FOR CNP2
7f63ca7922a7fab9.author: slava chan
7f63ca7922a7fab9.statement:
DIVISOR-SELECTED CROSSED-NUMERATOR REINDEXING FOR CNP2.

Let A be a nonzero integer, let v,p be coprime positive integers with p prime, and put n=vp. For i=1,2 let q_i,m_i,k_i be integers satisfying
  q_i m_i+n k_i=A,  gcd(q_i m_i,n)=1.                      (1)
Put
  d_i=gcd(|A|,q_i),  r_i=q_i/d_i,  t_i=k_i/d_i,            (2)
  g=gcd(r_1,r_2),  r_i=gu_i,  gcd(u_1,u_2)=1,
  delta_12=u_2t_1-u_1t_2.                                 (3)
Then d_i divides k_i and
  E_12:=(A/d_1)u_2-(A/d_2)u_1
          -g u_1u_2(m_1-m_2)
       =vp delta_12.                                       (4)
In particular, on the unequal reduced-phase sector delta_12 nonzero of fact 1a9cfcfe3eedd5e2, E_12 is a nonzero integer divisible by both v and p. The additive core of the centered crossed kernel is
  e_{g u_1u_2}(h delta_12)
  =e_{g u_1u_2}(h E_12 (vp)bar)                            (5)
for every integer h, where the inverse is modulo g u_1u_2.

There is an exact divisor-selected reindexing. Fix v,q_i,m_i and put
  D_i=(A-q_i m_i)/v.                                       (6)
Let cal P be any finite set of primes not dividing v, let K_i be arbitrary integer sets, let omega(p) be any complex prime weight, and let F be any complex function of (p,k_1,k_2). Then
  sum_{p in cal P}omega(p)
    sum_{k_i in K_i, q_i m_i+vp k_i=A for i=1,2}
      F(p,k_1,k_2)
  =
  sum_{p in cal P, p divides D_1, p divides D_2}
    omega(p) product_{i=1}^2 1_{D_i/p in K_i}
      F(p,D_1/p,D_2/p).                                   (7)
Every literal p-dependent source, least-prime, marker, fixed-U, frequency, collision, provenance, or projective mask may be retained in omega and F. On the CNP2 support delta_12 nonzero, the selected p in (7) also divides the nonzero crossed integer E_12 in (4).

Thus the remaining CNP2 theorem can be viewed as a centered crossed dispersion estimate over large prime divisors selected jointly by D_1,D_2 and E_12; p is not a free character or additive-large-sieve modulus. Equations (4)-(7) are identities only. They prove no CNP2 estimate, PMD closure, or Goldbach conclusion.
7f63ca7922a7fab9.proof:
Fact 1a9cfcfe3eedd5e2, via the gcd reduction in fact 7670948dedd78714, proves d_i|k_i. Divide (1) by d_i:
  r_i m_i+n t_i=A/d_i.                                     (8)
Using r_i=gu_i, multiply the i=1 equation by u_2 and the i=2 equation by u_1. Subtraction gives
  g u_1u_2(m_1-m_2)+n(u_2t_1-u_1t_2)
   =(A/d_1)u_2-(A/d_2)u_1.
Rearrangement and n=vp prove (4). If delta_12 is nonzero, (4) makes E_12 nonzero and divisible by v,p. Also gcd(q_i,n)=1 implies gcd(r_i,n)=1, hence gcd(g u_1u_2,vp)=1. Therefore (vp)bar in (5) exists, and (4) reduced modulo g u_1u_2 proves (5).

For (7), equation q_i m_i+vp k_i=A is equivalent, after fixing v,q_i,m_i,p, to
  D_i=p k_i.                                                (9)
It has the unique solution k_i=D_i/p when p|D_i and no integer solution otherwise. Requiring k_i in K_i gives exactly the indicators on the right of (7). Apply this independently for i=1,2 and sum over p. Every additional mask may remain in omega or F because the reindexing is termwise. Finally, (4) proves the extra p|E_12 assertion on the crossed support. This proves all claims.

glossary.E_12: The crossed source numerator equal to vp times delta_12.

7fa6e823cd299d09.title: SQUAREFREE-MASKED HILBERT NORM WITH A TRUNCATED CONDUCTOR PROJECTOR. Fix constants \(A\ge0\), \(C_0\ge1\), and an integer \(J\ge3\). Let \(x\ge3\), let \(N\) be a positive integer, and let \(D,M,R,F\ge1\) satisfy
7fa6e823cd299d09.author: slava chan
7fa6e823cd299d09.statement:
SQUAREFREE-MASKED HILBERT NORM WITH A TRUNCATED CONDUCTOR PROJECTOR. Fix constants \(A\ge0\), \(C_0\ge1\), and an integer \(J\ge3\). Let \(x\ge3\), let \(N\) be a positive integer, and let \(D,M,R,F\ge1\) satisfy
\[
 DM\le C_0x,\qquad R/M>1. \tag{1}
\]
Let \(\mathcal R\) be a finite set of ordered pairs \((p,\ell)\) of positive integers such that, writing \(r=p\ell\),
\[
 R/C_0\le r\le C_0R,\qquad |\mathcal R|\le C_0R. \tag{2}
\]
Let \(\mathfrak L\) be a finite label set. For every positive integer \(n\le C_0D\), every nonzero integer \(h\), and every \((p,\ell)\in\mathcal R\), let complex coefficients \(C_\iota(n;h,p,\ell)\), indexed by \(\iota\in\mathfrak L\), satisfy
\[
 \sum_{\iota\in\mathfrak L}|C_\iota(n;h,p,\ell)|^2
 \le C_0(\log x)^A\left(\frac Mr\right)^2
       \left(1+\frac{|h|M}{r}\right)^{-2J}. \tag{3}
\]
For \(n>C_0D\), put every such coefficient equal to zero. For positive \(n\) and nonzero \(h\), put
\[
 c_n=(n,h),\qquad Q_n=n/c_n,\qquad h_n=h/c_n. \tag{4}
\]
For a Dirichlet character \(\chi\) modulo \(Q_n\), put
\[
 G_{N,Q_n}(\chi)=
 \sum_{\substack{z\ ({\rm mod}\ Q_n)\\(z,Q_n)=1}}
 e_{Q_n}(-Nz)\overline{\chi(z)},
 \qquad e_v(y)=\exp(2\pi i y/v),
\]
and let \({\rm cond}(\chi)\) be its primitive conductor. Define
\[
 \Pi_{>F}(n;h,p,\ell)=
 {\bf1}_{Q_n>1}{\bf1}_{(h_nr,Q_n)=1}
 \frac1{\phi(Q_n)}
 \sum_{\substack{\chi\ ({\rm mod}\ Q_n)\\{\rm cond}(\chi)>F\\({\rm cond}(\chi),N)=1}}
 G_{N,Q_n}(\chi)\chi(h_n)\overline{\chi(r)}. \tag{5}
\]
In the Hilbert space
\[
 \mathcal H=\ell^2(\mathfrak L\times(\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\})\times\mathcal R),
\]
define
\[
 V_n(\iota,h,p,\ell)=
 C_\iota(n;h,p,\ell)e\!\left(\frac{Nh}{nr}\right)
 \Pi_{>F}(n;h,p,\ell),\qquad e(y)=\exp(2\pi i y), \tag{6}
\]
and \(W_n=\mu(n)^2V_n\), where \(\mu\) is the Möbius function. Then, for every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 \sup_{n\ge1}\|W_n\|_{\mathcal H}
 \ll_{\varepsilon,A,C_0,J} M^{1/2}x^\varepsilon. \tag{7}
\]
No multiplicativity of \(V_n\) or \(W_n\) is assumed.

glossary.C_iota(n;h,p,ell): the coordinate coefficient before the reciprocity phase and conductor projector
glossary.Pi_{>F}(n;h,p,ell): the character projector modulo Q_n restricted to primitive conductor greater than F
glossary.Q_n: the modulus n divided by the greatest common divisor of n and h
glossary.V_n: the auxiliary Hilbert vector before the squarefree mask
glossary.h_n: the frequency h divided by the greatest common divisor of n and h
glossary.mathcal R: the finite set of ordered two-factor coordinate pairs

7fb1e62c5a0e5efa.title: EXACT COMMON-TRANSLATION/FOURIER IDENTITY AND SHARP GENERIC-HILBERT NO-FIT ON THE FULLY NONEXCEPTIONAL FOUR-RESIDUE LOCUS
7fb1e62c5a0e5efa.author: slava chan
7fb1e62c5a0e5efa.statement:
EXACT COMMON-TRANSLATION/FOURIER IDENTITY AND SHARP GENERIC-HILBERT NO-FIT ON THE FULLY NONEXCEPTIONAL FOUR-RESIDUE LOCUS.

Let p>=7 be prime, let sigma_1=sigma_2=+1 and sigma_3=sigma_4=-1, and fix h_i,t_i in F_p^* for 1<=i<=4. Let a_i:F_p^*->C be arbitrary row arrays and let
  0<=W(q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4)<=1
be an arbitrary four-row tuple mask. Define
  S_p(a,W)
  =sum_{q_i in F_p^*}
    W(q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4) product_{i=1}^4 a_i(q_i)
    e_p(sum_{i=1}^4 sigma_i h_i t_i^(-1)q_i^(-1)).             (1)
For r=(r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4) in F_p^4 and X in F_p put
  B_r(X)
  =1_{X+r_i!=0 for every i}
   W(X+r_1,X+r_2,X+r_3,X+r_4)
   product_{i=1}^4 a_i(X+r_i),                                (2)
and use the unitary Fourier transform
  Bhat_r(xi)=p^(-1/2)sum_{X in F_p}B_r(X)e_p(-xi X).            (3)
Let C_p(r,h,t;xi) be the complete correlation in fact a9a0e9af2477d71d. Then
  S_p(a,W)
  =p^(-1)sum_{X in F_p}sum_{r in F_p^4}
    B_r(X)e_p(sum_i sigma_i h_i/[t_i(X+r_i)])                 (4)
and
  S_p(a,W)
  =p^(-3/2)sum_{r in F_p^4}sum_{xi in F_p}
    Bhat_r(xi)C_p(r,h,t;xi).                                  (5)
Every physical tuple and every tuple mask is retained exactly. In particular, the common-translation average has no bare-point-evaluation tax. Fact a9a0e9af2477d71d gives |C_p|<=10sqrt(p) at every Fourier coordinate except xi=0 on its exact repeated-pole block-balance locus.

Nevertheless, translation unitarity, Fourier l2 control, and those pointwise nonexceptional square-root bounds do not by themselves give any fixed p-power saving for (1), even when the physical tuple mask is supported entirely on four distinct q-residues. Indeed, take
  h_i=t_i=1,
  a_i(q)=e_p(-sigma_i q^(-1)),
  W(q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4)=1_{q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4 pairwise distinct}.    (6)
Put
  N_p=(p-1)(p-2)(p-3)(p-4).                                   (7)
Then every retained physical tuple has four singleton residue blocks and is nonexceptional, while
  S_p(a,W)=N_p.                                                (8)
If
  B(q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4)=W(q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4)product_i a_i(q_i),
then
  ||B||_{ell^2((F_p^*)^4)}=sqrt(N_p),                          (9)
and (8) is equality in the trivial Hilbert bound
  |S_p(a,W)|<=sqrt(N_p)||B||_2.                               (10)
Consequently no estimate of the form
  |S_p(a,W)|<=p^(-theta)sqrt(N_p)||B||_2                       (11)
with any fixed theta>0 can follow uniformly from the common-translation identity, Fourier l2 unitarity, the pointwise bound of fact a9a0e9af2477d71d, and an arbitrary tuple mask.

This is an abstract sharp no-fit for arbitrary row profiles, not a counterexample for the literal C1-C4 source arrays. It proves that a successful unequal-residue theorem must use additional source-specific q-profile structure, such as a common-envelope restriction, signed source recombination, or a stronger norm than unrestricted physical ell2. It does not refute a literal common-X operator, estimate an actual C1-C4 row, assemble varying primes, or prove a trace or Goldbach conclusion.
7fb1e62c5a0e5efa.proof:
For fixed X and a physical tuple q=(q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4), the equations
  r_i=q_i-X
determine a unique r in F_p^4. Conversely, q_i=X+r_i. Therefore, as X ranges over F_p, the inner r-sum in (4) reproduces every summand of (1) once for each of the p choices of X. Division by p proves (4). The zero condition in (2) is exactly q_i!=0, and W is evaluated on the unchanged physical tuple, so no mask is altered.

Fourier inversion for (3) gives
  B_r(X)=p^(-1/2)sum_{xi in F_p}Bhat_r(xi)e_p(xi X).
Insert this into (4) and interchange the finite sums. The inner X-sum is precisely C_p(r,h,t;xi), proving (5). The exceptional/nonexceptional sentence is the dichotomy of fact a9a0e9af2477d71d.

Now use (6). For every retained physical tuple,
  product_i a_i(q_i)
  e_p(sum_i sigma_i q_i^(-1))
  =1.
There are p-1 choices for q_1, then p-2 for q_2, p-3 for q_3 and p-4 for q_4, so (7)-(8) follow. Because the four residues are distinct, their equality partition consists of four singleton blocks. A singleton block cannot satisfy the nonzero balance sigma_i/t_i=0, so every retained tuple is outside the repeated-pole exceptional locus.

The array B has modulus one on exactly N_p tuples and zero elsewhere. This proves (9). Equation (1) is the ell2 inner product of B with the unit-modulus reciprocal-phase array restricted to the same N_p tuples. Cauchy's inequality gives (10), and (8)-(9) show equality. Thus (11) fails for the arrays (6) as p tends to infinity. Since (4)-(5) are identities and all their complete nonexceptional correlations obey fact a9a0e9af2477d71d, the failure occurs in the aggregation over shifts and Fourier coordinates, proving the claimed generic-Hilbert no-fit and every scope statement.

glossary.B_r(X): The translated physical four-row coefficient profile at fixed shifts r.
glossary.Bhat_r(xi): The unitary Fourier transform in the common translation variable.
glossary.N_p: The number of ordered quadruples of pairwise distinct nonzero residues modulo p.
glossary.S_p(a,W): The four-row physical-residue reciprocal-phase sum before the common-translation lift.

7ffe3d237362a451.title: QUANTITATIVE FIXED-BAD-\(N\) POST-LOW RESIDUAL AFTER COMPLETE C91 SUBTRACTION
7ffe3d237362a451.author: slava chan
7ffe3d237362a451.statement:
QUANTITATIVE FIXED-BAD-\(N\) POST-LOW RESIDUAL AFTER COMPLETE C91 SUBTRACTION.

Assume the selected fixed-bad-\(N\) source, parameters and notation of facts
\(60b26a9b6f79467a\), \(15425579cb248eff\), and
\(af06640e8d8e4102\). In particular, \(R_{\rm high,N}\) is the complete selected
\(60\)-residual paired nonzero-Poisson aggregate with
\(R>x^{9/16-\kappa_0}\), and
\[
 R_{\rm high,N}\le
 -c_{\rm dir}\mathfrak c(N)\frac{x}{\log x}
 +o\!\left(\mathfrak c(N)\frac{x}{\log x}\right).             \tag{1}
\]
Fix a sufficiently large constant \(Q_0\) for which the large-base assertions of
fact \(15425579cb248eff\) apply. Let
\(\mathscr R_{\rm low,out}\) be the disjoint sum of all selected high atoms
whose parent is not \(C91\) and which satisfy either

(i) \(0<Q=D/g\le Q_0\); or

(ii) \(Q>Q_0\) and
\[
 B=R/g=Q^{\beta_{\rm norm}},
 \qquad 1\le\beta_{\rm norm}\le\beta_0,
 \qquad \beta_0=6/5-2\kappa.
\]

Let \(\mathcal R^{\ne0}_{C91,\mathrm{sel}}\) be the complete selected C91
aggregate of fact \(af06640e8d8e4102\), and define
\[
 \mathscr R_{\rm postlow,sel}
 =
 R_{\rm high,N}
 -\mathcal R^{\ne0}_{C91,\mathrm{sel}}
 -\mathscr R_{\rm low,out}.                                   \tag{2}
\]
Then there is a fixed \(\delta_{\rm low}>0\) such that
\[
 |\mathscr R_{\rm low,out}|\ll x^{1-\delta_{\rm low}},         \tag{3}
\]
and
\[
 \mathscr R_{\rm postlow,sel}
 \le
 -c_{\rm dir}\mathfrak c(N)\frac{x}{\log x}
 +o\!\left(\mathfrak c(N)\frac{x}{\log x}\right).              \tag{4}
\]

The aggregate in (2) is an exact complete-label and exact-normalized-layer
remainder. Every one of its atoms has parent different from \(C91\), has
\(Q>Q_0\), and has \(\beta_{\rm norm}>\beta_0\). The parent \(U_{\rm sh}\) is
empty. In its subrange
\[
 \beta_0<\beta_{\rm norm}<6/5
\]
the only possible parent is \(U_{\rm low}\). Thus the first standard-marker
interface of this actual negative remainder is the \(U_{\rm low}\) post-low
ledger of fact \(15425579cb248eff\). No interval-prime-\(A\) subtraction from
that ledger is made here.

No actual-\((r,k)\) \(Z_{\rm mid}\) deletion, anatomy selection, endpoint
selection, \(C2\) selection, terminal conclusion, or Goldbach conclusion is
asserted.
7ffe3d237362a451.proof:
Fact \(15425579cb248eff\), Part (A), proves that after
all exact outer gcds and the polylogarithmically many source labels are summed,
every fixed bounded-normalized-base family \(0<Q\le Q_0\) has size
\(O(x^{1/2+\epsilon})\). Choose a fixed \(\epsilon<1/4\).

For \(Q>Q_0\), Part (C) of the same fact proves a fixed power saving for every
actual imbalance \(G>0\), every exact outer gcd, and every parent mask when
\(1\le\beta_{\rm norm}\le\beta_0\). In particular it applies to the union of
the parents outside \(C91\). There are finitely many parent types and
polylogarithmically many inherited labels, already included in that fact's
global assertion. Taking the smaller of its saving exponent and \(1/4\)
gives a fixed \(\delta_{\rm low}>0\) and proves (3).

The parent selector has first precedence and the bounded-base/normalized-beta
selectors are applied only on its complement. Hence
\(\mathcal R^{\ne0}_{C91,\mathrm{sel}}\),
\(\mathscr R_{\rm low,out}\), and
\(\mathscr R_{\rm postlow,sel}\) form the exact disjoint decomposition (2) of
\(R_{\rm high,N}\). No inclusion-exclusion and no proper deletion of a C91
label occurs.

Fact \(af06640e8d8e4102\) gives, for every fixed \(A>0\),
\[
 |\mathcal R^{\ne0}_{C91,\mathrm{sel}}|
 \ll x^{1-\eta/40}+x(\log x)^{-A}
 =o(x/\log x).                                                \tag{5}
\]
Fact \(f41f5f91b52e0d13\), already a predecessor of fact
\(60b26a9b6f79467a\), gives
\(\mathfrak c(N)\ge C_2>0\). Thus (3) and (5) are both
\(o(\mathfrak c(N)x/\log x)\). Rearranging (2) and inserting (1), (3), and
(5) proves (4).

By construction, every remaining atom is outside \(C91\), outside the
bounded-base set, and outside the normalized low-beta set. Fact
\(af06640e8d8e4102\) proves that \(U_{\rm sh}\) is empty on the entire selected
high family. Fact \(15425579cb248eff\), Part (B), proves
\(\beta_{\rm orig}\le\beta_{\rm norm}\). Therefore
\(\beta_{\rm norm}<6/5<4/3\) excludes all endpoint parents,
\(U_{\rm gap}\), and \(U_{\rm sup}\). The only remaining parent in that
subrange is \(U_{\rm low}\). This proves the asserted interface.

The definition (2) removed only whole C91 labels and the complete
bounded-base/low-beta families independently estimated by the cited facts.
It did not insert any actual-\((r,k)\) or anatomy selector. The scope
exclusions therefore follow directly.

glossary.delta_low: A fixed positive power-saving exponent for the complete paid bounded-base and low-beta aggregate outside C91.
glossary.mathscr R_{low,out}: The complete selected high aggregate outside C91 in bounded normalized bases or in normalized beta at most beta_0.
glossary.mathscr R_{postlow,sel}: The exact selected fixed-bad-N high remainder after subtracting the complete C91 and paid bounded-base/low-beta aggregates.

8138369f26f88aad.title: VARIABLE-AMPLITUDE, AUXILIARY-COPRIMALITY TYPE-I RECIPROCAL CONSUMER. Fix integers \(J\ge1\), \(C_A\ge1\), a real \(\tau>0\), and real parameters
8138369f26f88aad.author: slava chan
8138369f26f88aad.statement:
VARIABLE-AMPLITUDE, AUXILIARY-COPRIMALITY TYPE-I RECIPROCAL CONSUMER. Fix integers \(J\ge1\), \(C_A\ge1\), a real \(\tau>0\), and real parameters
\[
 Q\ge2,\qquad H,L,M\ge1.
\]
Let \(A_0\ne0\) and \(g\ge1\) be integers satisfying
\[
 |A_0|,\ H,\ g\le Q^{C_A}.                                    \tag{1}
\]
Let
\[
 |\nu_h|\le\tau_J(|h|),\qquad |\alpha_l|\le\tau_J(l),
\]
with \(\nu_h\) supported on \(H\le |h|<2H\) and \(\alpha_l\) supported on \(L\le l<2L\). For every \(Q\le q<2Q\), supported \(l,h\), let \(W_{q,l,h}\) be a complex continuously differentiable function supported in \([M,2M]\), allowed to depend arbitrarily on \(q,l,h\), and suppose uniformly that
\[
 \|W_{q,l,h}\|_\infty+\int_M^{2M}|W'_{q,l,h}(t)|\,dt\le {\cal V}. \tag{2}
\]
Define
\[
 {\cal I}_g={1\over H}\sum_{H\le|h|<2H}|\nu_h|
 \sum_{Q\le q<2Q}\left|
 \sum_{\substack{L\le l<2L,\ M\le m<2M\\
                 (lm,q)=1,\ (lm,g)=1}}
 \alpha_l W_{q,l,h}(m)
 e_q\!\left(A_0h(lm)^{-1}\right)\right|.                      \tag{3}
\]
No coprimality of \(A_0h\) with \(q\), and no separability of \(W_{q,l,h}\) in its outer indices, is assumed. Then for every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 {\cal I}_g\ll_{J,\varepsilon}{\cal V}\,
 (|A_0|HgQLM)^\varepsilon
 \bigl(LM+Q^{3/2}L\bigr).
 \quad}                                                       \tag{4}
\]
In particular, if
\[
 LM\le Q^{2-\tau},\qquad L\le Q^{1/2-\tau},\qquad
 {\cal V}\le Q^{\tau/4},                                      \tag{5}
\]
then
\[
 {\cal I}_g\ll_{J,C_A,\tau}Q^{2-\tau/2}                       \tag{6}
\]
after choosing the harmless epsilon in (4) sufficiently small.

The order in the proof is load-bearing: first apply partial summation to the original long variable \(m\); only afterwards expand \({\bf1}_{(m,g)=1}\). The divisor \(d\mid g\) produced by that expansion is absorbed as a unit multiplier in the reciprocal numerator, so the short Type-I scale remains the original \(L\), not \(Ld\). Thus (5) imposes shortness only on the original coefficient-bearing factor. The fixed target \(A_0\) may be nonunit modulo \(q\), both frequency signs are allowed, and the modulus remains \(q\asymp Q\).
8138369f26f88aad.proof:
We use the following complete external input. Irving, arXiv:1301.6372v2, Lemma 2.1, states that for integers \(a,q\), \(q>1\), and reals \(Y<Z\),
\[
 \sum_{\substack{Y<n\le Z\\(n,q)=1}}e_q(a\overline n)
 \ll_\varepsilon
 \left((a,q)\left({Z-Y\over q}+1\right)+q^{1/2}\right)q^\varepsilon. \tag{7}
\]
The paper obtains its Type-I Lemmas 3.3-3.4 by applying (7) to the unweighted long variable. Fact \(bbcb9f66597c667c\) records the resulting fixed-smooth-weight theorem. We return to (7) because the present weight may depend on \(q,l,h\).

Fix \(q,l,h\) occurring in (3). The condition \((lm,g)=1\) makes the row zero unless \((l,g)=1\); retain that one-variable gate on \(l\). Abel summation and (2) give
\[
 \left|\sum_{\substack{M\le m<2M\\(m,qg)=1}}
 W_{q,l,h}(m)e_q(A_0h\overline l\,\overline m)\right|
 \le {\cal V}\sup_{M\le Y\le2M}
 \left|\sum_{\substack{M\le m\le Y\\(m,qg)=1}}
 e_q(A_0h\overline l\,\overline m)\right|.                    \tag{8}
\]
This is the promised partial summation before any divisor expansion.

Now use
\[
 {\bf1}_{(m,g)=1}=\sum_{\substack{d\mid g\\d\mid m}}\mu(d).
\]
If \((d,q)>1\), the corresponding terms are empty because \(d\mid m\) and \((m,q)=1\). If \((d,q)=1\), put \(m=dr\). The inner interval has length at most \(M/d\), \((r,q)=1\), and its phase is
\[
 e_q(A_0h\,\overline{ld}\,\overline r).
\]
Because \(ld\) is a unit modulo \(q\),
\[
 (A_0h\,\overline{ld},q)=(A_0h,q).                            \tag{9}
\]
Applying (7) and summing \(d\mid g\) therefore bounds the supremum in (8) by
\[
 \ll_\varepsilon \tau(g)
 \left((A_0h,q)\left({M\over q}+1\right)+q^{1/2}\right)
 (qg)^\varepsilon.                                            \tag{10}
\]
Crucially, no \(Ld\) occurs.

Take absolute values of the divisor-bounded \(\alpha_l\), sum \(l\asymp L\), and then sum \(q\asymp Q\). For every nonzero integer \(a\),
\[
 \sum_{Q\le q<2Q}(a,q)
 \le\sum_{\substack{d\mid a\\d\le2Q}}d\left({2Q\over d}+1\right)
 \le4Q\tau(|a|).                                               \tag{11}
\]
Also
\[
 \sum_{Q\le q<2Q}q^{1/2}\ll Q^{3/2}.
\]
Equations (8)-(11) give, for each fixed \(h\),
\[
 \sum_{Q\le q<2Q}\left|\sum_{l,m}\cdots\right|
 \ll_{J,\varepsilon}{\cal V}\tau(g)
 (|A_0h|gQLM)^\varepsilon
 \bigl(LM+QL+Q^{3/2}L\bigr).                                  \tag{12}
\]
Since \(Q\ge2\), the middle term is absorbed by \(Q^{3/2}L\).

Finally,
\[
 {1\over H}\sum_{H\le|h|<2H}|\nu_h|\tau(|A_0h|)
 \ll_{J,\varepsilon}(|A_0|H)^\varepsilon,
\]
and \(\tau(g)\ll_\varepsilon g^\varepsilon\). Substitution in (12) proves (4). Under (5), both displayed main terms in (4) are at most \(Q^{2-\tau}\). The quantities in the epsilon factor are bounded by fixed powers of \(Q\) using (1), \(L\le Q^{1/2}\), and \(M\le Q^2/L\) on a nonempty row. Choose epsilon small enough that this factor is at most \(Q^{\tau/4}\); together with \({\cal V}\le Q^{\tau/4}\), this proves (6).

glossary.A_0: The fixed nonzero reciprocal target before multiplication by h.
glossary.VARIABLE-AMPLITUDE TYPE-I: The Type-I reciprocal estimate with an outer-row-dependent bounded-variation long-variable weight.
glossary.W_{q,l,h}: The long-variable amplitude, allowed arbitrary dependence on the outer row q,l,h.
glossary.{\\cal I}_g: The h-averaged Type-I form with the auxiliary coprimality condition (lm,g)=1.
glossary.{\\cal V}: The uniform supremum-plus-total-variation bound for W_{q,l,h}.

81b9c007aa483a7f.title: Fix
81b9c007aa483a7f.author: slava chan
81b9c007aa483a7f.statement:
Fix
\[
 1/2<\alpha<\beta<1,\quad \eta>0,\quad\rho>0,\quad
 B_{\rm src}>0.
\]
Let \(W\) and \(\Phi\) be bounded real functions supported in
\([\alpha,\beta]\) and \([1/2,2]\), respectively. Let \(N=2x\) be an integer with \(x\ge3\), put
\[
 T_x=(\log x)^{6+\eta+\rho},
\]
and assume
\[
 {1\over2}x^{1/2}(\log x)^{-B_{\rm src}}\le D\le2x^{1/2},
 \qquad D>2T_x,qquad U>0.
\]
Let \(\mu\) be the Möbius function, extend \(\Lambda\) by zero on nonpositive integers, and put
\[
 {\cal I}_D=\{d\ge2:(d,N)=1,\ \mu(d)\ne0, d\le x^{1/2},\ \Phi(d/D)\ne0\}.
\]
For positive integers \(s,m,w\), define
\[
 f_{s,m}(w)=
 {\bf1}_{sw\in{\cal I}_D}\mu(w)\Phi(sw/D)W(smw/x)
 \Phi((N-smw)/U)\Lambda(N-smw),
\]
\[
 F_s(\theta)=
 \left(\sum_w f_{s,m}(w)e(\theta w)\right)_{m\ge1},
 \qquad e(t)=\exp(2\pi it),
\]
and, for \(1\le s<T_x^2\), put
\[
 L_s={D\over sT_x}.
\]
For sufficiently large \(x\), \(L_s\ge2\). Define
\[
 I_s(\theta_0)=
 \int_{\theta_0-1/(2L_s)}^{\theta_0+1/(2L_s)}
 \|F_s(\theta)\|_{ell^2_m}^{,2}\,d\theta,
\]
\[
 J_s=\sup_{\theta_0\in\mathbb R/\mathbb Z}I_s(\theta_0),
 \qquad
 \Delta_s=\sum_{m,w}|f_{s,m}(w)|^2.
\]
Then exactly
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R/\mathbb Z}I_s(\theta_0)\,d\theta_0
 ={\Delta_s\over L_s},                                  \tag{1}
\]
and consequently
\[
 J_s\ge {\Delta_s\over L_s}.                           \tag{2}
\]

In particular, the sufficient uncentered vector estimate TB-VL2 from fact 6a2652fb92d86417,
\[
 \sum_{g,r<T_x}{J_{gr}\over g^2r^2}
 \ll {xT_x\over D}(\log x)^{-4-\eta},                 \tag{3}
\]
would force
\[
 \Delta_1\ll x(\log x)^{-4-\eta}.                     \tag{4}
\]
On the other hand,
\[
 \Delta_1\ll_{W,\Phi,\alpha,\beta}x(\log x)^2,       \tag{5}
\]
and
\[
 x(\log x)^2=o\left(xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta}\right).     \tag{6}
\]
Thus the diagonal at its elementary scale is already negligible for the desired hard-core bound, whereas the particular uncentered positive local-energy interface (3) asks it to have the extra logarithmic saving (4). TB-VL2 remains a correct sufficient condition, but is stronger than what is needed merely to pay this diagonal. Subtracting \(\Delta_s\) before a local-frequency estimate, or retaining the signed \(\mu(r)\) projector longer, are two possible ways to seek a sharper continuation; neither alternative is asserted to be necessary or sufficient here.
81b9c007aa483a7f.proof:
By Fubini's theorem,
\[
\begin{split}
 \int_{\mathbb R/\mathbb Z}I_s(\theta_0)d\theta_0
 &=\int_{\mathbb R/\mathbb Z}
   \|F_s(\theta)\|_2^2
   \left(\int_{\mathbb R/\mathbb Z}
    {\bf1}_{\|\theta-\theta_0\|\le1/(2L_s)}
    d\theta_0\right)d\theta\\
 &={1\over L_s}
   \int_{\mathbb R/\mathbb Z}\|F_s(\theta)\|_2^2d\theta.
\end{split}
\]
Circular distance is used. Since \(L_s\ge2\), the inner arc has measure \(1/L_s\). Parseval, equation (8) of fact 6a2652fb92d86417, identifies the last integral with \(\Delta_s\). This proves (1), and a supremum is at least an average, proving (2).

The term \(g=r=1\) occurs in the nonnegative left side of (3), so
\[
 J_1\ll {xT_x\over D}(\log x)^{-4-\eta}.
\]
Equation (2) and \(L_1=D/T_x\) imply (4).

For (5), if \(f_{1,m}(w)\ne0\), then
\[
 D/2\le w\le2D,qquad \alpha x\le mw\le\beta x.
\]
There are \(O(D)\) choices for \(w\), and for each one there are
\(O(x/D)\) choices for \(m\). Thus there are \(O(x)\) pairs.
All smooth factors and the Möbius factor are bounded, while
\(|\Lambda(N-mw)|\le\log(2x)\). This proves (5).

Finally,
\[
 {x(\log x)^2\over xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta}}
 \ll x^{-1/2}(\log x)^{B_{\rm src}+6+\eta}\longrightarrow0,
\]
which proves (6). Fact 1f5316e61daf156d identifies
\(xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta}\) as the sufficient hard-core scale. Therefore the elementary diagonal can be paid at that scale without the stronger bound (4). The final two suggestions alter the interface and are stated only as possible research directions.

glossary.Delta_s: the global diagonal Hilbert energy sum_{m,w}|f_{s,m}(w)|^2
glossary.I_s(theta_0): the local Hilbert energy of F_s on the arc of length 1/L_s centered at theta_0

8230d44e6677f45b.title: Let m>1 be odd, let s belong to {1,-1}, let K be an integer with gcd(K,m)=1, and let W be a complex-valued function modulo m. Put W_hat(ell)=sum_{u modulo m}W(u)e_m(-ell u). Let G be the multiplicative group of units modulo m^2, and define the tensor T_W on G^4 by
8230d44e6677f45b.author: slava chan
8230d44e6677f45b.statement:
Let m>1 be odd, let s belong to {1,-1}, let K be an integer with gcd(K,m)=1, and let W be a complex-valued function modulo m. Put W_hat(ell)=sum_{u modulo m}W(u)e_m(-ell u). Let G be the multiplicative group of units modulo m^2, and define the tensor T_W on G^4 by
T_W(a,b,c,d)=sum_{u modulo m}W(u) Delta_{m^2}(ab-K-2smu) Delta_{m^2}(cd-K+2smu).                     (1)
Define its four-fold projective ell^2 tensor norm by
P_4(T_W)=inf sum_j ||A_j||_2||B_j||_2||C_j||_2||D_j||_2,               (2)
where the infimum is over all finite exact decompositions
T_W(a,b,c,d)=sum_j A_j(a)B_j(b)C_j(c)D_j(d).                           (3)
Then
P_4(T_W)=[phi(m^2)^2/m] sum_{ell modulo m}|W_hat(ell)|.                 (4)
Thus P_4(T_W) is exactly equal to the (a,c) versus (b,d) projective norm P_digit^{(2)} computed in fact be21aada9cf60ec5; requiring individual-variable factorization introduces no additional projective cost for this modular tensor.

More generally, let omega_a,omega_b,omega_c,omega_d be arbitrary complex-valued functions on G, each of supremum norm at most one, and put
T_W^{gate}(a,b,c,d)=omega_a(a)omega_b(b)omega_c(c)omega_d(d)T_W(a,b,c,d). (5)
Then
P_4(T_W^{gate})<=P_4(T_W).                                             (6)
Consequently independent one-variable coefficient gates do not increase this four-fold modular digit cost. Equations (4)-(6) do not identify this cost with the normalized Bettin--Chandee quantity Pi_BC in fact b1398db2962d7491: the decomposition proving (4) places multiplicative characters on all four variables, whereas that fact permits arbitrary sequences only in its two n-slots and requires fixed smooth profiles in its two m-slots.
8230d44e6677f45b.proof:
Write n=|G|=phi(m^2). For a finite abelian group, its multiplicative characters form an orthogonal basis, so for x,y in G,
Delta_{m^2}(x-y)=n^(-1)sum_{chi in dual(G)}chi(x)conjugate(chi(y)).      (7)
For every u modulo m, both K+2smu and K-2smu are in G because each is congruent to K modulo m and gcd(K,m)=1. Applying (7) to the two delta factors in (1) gives the exact expansion
T_W(a,b,c,d)=n^(-2)sum_{chi,psi in dual(G)} S(chi,psi) chi(a)chi(b)psi(c)psi(d), (8)
where
S(chi,psi)=sum_{u modulo m}W(u)conjugate(chi(K+2smu)psi(K-2smu)).       (9)
Every character vector on G has ell^2 norm n^(1/2). Hence the rank-one term in (8) indexed by (chi,psi) has projective cost |S(chi,psi)|. It follows that
P_4(T_W)<=sum_{chi,psi}|S(chi,psi)|.                                  (10)

Let H_0={1+mt modulo m^2:t modulo m}, an order-m subgroup of G, and let gamma be the unit residue 2sK^(-1) modulo m. For each chi in dual(G), there is a unique residue r_chi modulo m such that
chi(1+mt)=e_m(r_chi t) for every t modulo m.                           (11)
The restriction map from dual(G) to dual(H_0) is onto. Here is a direct extension argument. Given a character theta on a proper subgroup H_1 of a finite abelian group and an element g outside H_1, let r be the order of g+H_1 in the quotient. Choose a unit complex number z with z^r=theta(rg), and define theta'(h+jg)=theta(h)z^j for h in H_1 and 0<=j<r. The minimality of r shows that this is well defined and multiplicative. Iterating extends every character of H_0 to G. Since a finite abelian group has as many characters as elements, as follows by decomposing it into cyclic groups, the onto restriction map has fibres of cardinality |G|/|H_0|=n/m. Thus each residue r modulo m occurs as r_chi for exactly n/m characters chi.

The congruences
K+2smu=K(1+m gamma u),   K-2smu=K(1-m gamma u) modulo m^2             (12)
and (11) transform (9) into
S(chi,psi)=conjugate(chi(K)psi(K)) W_hat(gamma(r_chi-r_psi)).          (13)
The leading character value has absolute value one. For each ell modulo m, the number of ordered pairs (chi,psi) satisfying gamma(r_chi-r_psi)=ell is
m(n/m)^2=n^2/m: choose r_chi arbitrarily, then r_psi is determined, and lift each restriction in n/m ways. Therefore
sum_{chi,psi}|S(chi,psi)|=(n^2/m)sum_{ell modulo m}|W_hat(ell)|.       (14)
Equations (10) and (14) prove the upper bound in (4).

For the reverse bound, take any decomposition (3) and group its variables as (a,c) and (b,d):
T_W((a,c),(b,d))=sum_j [A_j(a)C_j(c)][B_j(b)D_j(d)].                  (15)
The two grouped ell^2 norms are respectively ||A_j||_2||C_j||_2 and ||B_j||_2||D_j||_2. Hence (15) is an admissible decomposition for the (a,c) versus (b,d) projective norm in fact be21aada9cf60ec5, and that fact gives
[phi(m^2)^2/m]sum_ell|W_hat(ell)|
 <=sum_j||A_j||_2||B_j||_2||C_j||_2||D_j||_2.                         (16)
Taking the infimum over (3) proves the lower bound in (4). Together with (14), it also shows that the character decomposition (8) attains the exact value.

Finally multiply, in every rank-one term of (8), the chi(a), chi(b), psi(c), psi(d) factors by omega_a(a), omega_b(b), omega_c(c), omega_d(d), respectively. Each new factor has ell^2 norm at most the old norm because the corresponding gate has supremum norm at most one. This is an exact decomposition of (5) with cost at most the right side of (14), which equals P_4(T_W) by (4). This proves (6). The final scope statement follows by comparing the four arbitrary character factors in (8) with the asymmetric smooth-profile and arbitrary-sequence slots stated in fact b1398db2962d7491; no Bettin--Chandee application is asserted.

glossary.P_4: the four-fold projective ell^2 tensor norm across the individual variables a,b,c,d
glossary.T_W: the determinant-compatible shared normal-digit tensor on four copies of the unit group modulo m^2
glossary.T_W^{gate}: the tensor T_W multiplied by four independent one-variable gates
