831d32b948e6dcdb.title: ZERO-HEIGHT REPEATED-POLE OCCUPANCY AND ITS LITERAL SMALL-p NATURAL-COFACTOR ENVELOPE
831d32b948e6dcdb.author: slava chan

glossary.C_p: The uniform literal source-copy mass bound at one shift, height residue and natural-cofactor residue.
glossary.E: The shift-l2 energy of the nonzero-height envelope U(r).
glossary.R_p: The number of shift residues represented by physical q in the fixed interval.
glossary.Z(r): The cofactor-l-infinity source mass at zero local height and shift r.
glossary.Z_1: The sum of Z(r) over all represented shifts.
glossary.\\mathscr B_{0,p,k,X}: The coarse literal fourth-moment source envelope for one selected-prime natural-cofactor block, including all height residues.
glossary.\\mathscr O_j: The absolute exceptional four-row occupancy with exactly j zero local heights.

8346861a976aa604.title: EXACT OUTER-G POISSON L1 MASS AND LARGE-IMBALANCE TAIL. Fix positive constants c_i,C_i. Let x>=3, let c_0x<=N<=C_0x, c_1x<=DM<=C_1x, c_2x<=RK<=C_2x, and assume 1<=D,M,R,K<=C_3x. Let mathcal W be a fixed smooth function supported where each of its four positive coordinates lies in [1/2,2], with uniformly bounded scaled derivatives. Fix a positive integer g dividing N and put Q=D/g, B=R/g, L=N/g. For integers a,b with a comparable to Q, b comparable to B, gcd(a,b)=1, define
8346861a976aa604.author: slava chan
8346861a976aa604.statement:
EXACT OUTER-G POISSON L1 MASS AND LARGE-IMBALANCE TAIL. Fix positive constants c_i,C_i. Let x>=3, let c_0x<=N<=C_0x, c_1x<=DM<=C_1x, c_2x<=RK<=C_2x, and assume 1<=D,M,R,K<=C_3x. Let mathcal W be a fixed smooth function supported where each of its four positive coordinates lies in [1/2,2], with uniformly bounded scaled derivatives. Fix a positive integer g dividing N and put Q=D/g, B=R/g, L=N/g. For integers a,b with a comparable to Q, b comparable to B, gcd(a,b)=1, define
F_{g,a,b}(t)=log(t)log((L-at)/b) mathcal W(ga/D,t/M,gb/R,(L-at)/(bK)),
extended by zero, and define Fhat_{g,a,b}(xi)=integral_R F_{g,a,b}(t)e(-xi t)dt. For h nonzero put lambda_{g,a,b,h}=mu(ga)mu(gb)b^{-1}Fhat_{g,a,b}(h/b). Then
sum_{a comparable to Q,b comparable to B,gcd(a,b)=1,h nonzero}|lambda_{g,a,b,h}| << QB(log x)^2,
with a constant depending only on the displayed fixed data. The same bound holds after arbitrary deletion of indices.
Put H_T=B/Q and G=M/Q. Since D=gQ, one has g/G=D/M and DM=gGQ^2=G^2(D/M)Q^2. Consequently, if xi>0 and G^2(D/M)>=H_TQ^xi, then the complete exact-g nonzero-Poisson contribution, and every deleted subfamily, is O(xQ^{-xi}(log x)^2). This is o(x) if Q^xi/(log x)^2 tends to infinity. If Q>=x^{delta_Q} for a fixed delta_Q>0, it is O(x^{1-delta_Qxi/2}) for sufficiently large x. If Q^{-chi}<=D/M<=Q^chi, the sufficient condition G>=H_T^{1/2}Q^{(xi+chi)/2} implies the large-imbalance hypothesis.
8346861a976aa604.proof:
On the support, t is comparable to M and k(t)=(L-at)/b is comparable to K. The polynomial scale assumptions give |log t|+|log k(t)|<<log x. Every t-derivative of a scaled t/M cutoff costs O(M^{-1}). Also
|a/(bk(t))| is comparable to Q/(BK)=D/(RK),
which is O(1/M) because DM and RK are both comparable to x. Thus repeated product and chain rules give the correct pointwise bound
|F_{g,a,b}^{(J)}(t)|<<_J M^{-J}(log x)^2.
The support has length O(M), hence its L1 derivative norm is O_J(M^{1-J}(log x)^2). Repeated integration by parts now gives
|Fhat_{g,a,b}(h/b)|<<_J M(log x)^2(1+|h|M/b)^{-J}.
Write H_b=b/M. If H_b>=1, the sum over h nonzero of (1+|h|/H_b)^{-J} is O(H_b) for J>2. If H_b<1, it is O(H_b^J). Therefore
b^{-1}sum_{h nonzero}|Fhat_{g,a,b}(h/b)|<< (log x)^2,
using MH_b/b=1 in the first case and (M/b)H_b^J=H_b^{J-1}<=1 in the second. The Mobius factors are bounded by one, and there are O(QB) pairs a,b. This proves the l1 estimate; deletion only decreases it.
The identities D=gQ,M=GQ give D/M=g/G, so g=G(D/M), and DM=gGQ^2=G^2(D/M)Q^2. Also QB=Q^2H_T. Under G^2(D/M)>=H_TQ^xi, QB<=DM Q^{-xi}<<xQ^{-xi}, proving the tail bound. The two asymptotic consequences follow from the stated quantitative conditions. Finally D/M>=Q^{-chi}, so G>=H_T^{1/2}Q^{(xi+chi)/2} implies G^2(D/M)>=H_TQ^{xi+chi}Q^{-chi}=H_TQ^xi.

glossary.F_{g,a,b}: The exact fixed-g source amplitude before Poisson summation.
glossary.delta_Q: A fixed lower exponent for Q relative to x.
glossary.lambda_{g,a,b,h}: The exact nonzero-Poisson coefficient at outer gcd g.

8349d056bf34d112.title: EXACT NATURAL FORWARD C1 MOVING-WINDOW COMPLETION IN THE PMD GAUGE. Let Q>=8 and H>=2, let n be a positive integer with n>=QH, and let A be an integer with gcd(A,n)=1. Fix a forward C1 coordinate from fact ee6886ba9ed393f1, so n=vp with v a positive integer and p a prime, and fix its outer-gcd coordinate g, target-gcd coordinate c, positive normalization H_P, and finite height set cal I. For h in cal I let cal Q_h be the exact global q-support of this C1 coordinate: every q in cal Q_h is an integer in [Q,2Q), gcd(q,n)=1, every inherited literal bookkeeping mask is satisfied, and the unique integer m_n(q) in [Q,2Q) satisfying
8349d056bf34d112.author: slava chan
8349d056bf34d112.statement:
EXACT NATURAL FORWARD C1 MOVING-WINDOW COMPLETION IN THE PMD GAUGE. Let Q>=8 and H>=2, let n be a positive integer with n>=QH, and let A be an integer with gcd(A,n)=1. Fix a forward C1 coordinate from fact ee6886ba9ed393f1, so n=vp with v a positive integer and p a prime, and fix its outer-gcd coordinate g, target-gcd coordinate c, positive normalization H_P, and finite height set cal I. For h in cal I let cal Q_h be the exact global q-support of this C1 coordinate: every q in cal Q_h is an integer in [Q,2Q), gcd(q,n)=1, every inherited literal bookkeeping mask is satisfied, and the unique integer m_n(q) in [Q,2Q) satisfying
q m_n(q) congruent A modulo n                              (1)
exists.

Let chi_nat(v,p,h,q) be the reindexed product of all inherited bookkeeping factors, extended by zero outside cal Q_h, and define
B_h^nat(q)
 =-mu(c)mu(v)mu(q)[H_P/n]
   Fhat_{g,cq,n}(-h/n)e(-Ah/(qn))
   chi_nat(v,p,h,q).                                       (2)
For a real interval W put
cal M_W(q)={m in Z:Q<=m<2Q, m-A/q belongs to W},            (3)
and define
Z_h^nat(W)
 =sum_{Q<=q<2Q,gcd(q,n)=1}B_h^nat(q)
   sum_{m in cal M_W(q)}
    1_{qm congruent A modulo n}
    e(h[A/(nq)-m/n]).                                      (4)
For r modulo n define the natural completed row
C_{h,W}^nat(r)
 =-mu(c)mu(v)[H_P/n]
   sum_{Q<=q<2Q,gcd(q,n)=1}
    mu(q)Fhat_{g,cq,n}(-h/n)chi_nat(v,p,h,q)
    sum_{m in cal M_W(q)}e_n(m(rq-h)).                      (5)
Then exactly
Z_h^nat(W)=n^(-1)sum_{r modulo n}e_n(-rA)C_{h,W}^nat(r).    (6)
In particular, the two Archimedean factors from (2) and (4) cancel before the additive completion, which is why no factor e(Ah/(qn)) appears in (5).

Let W_1,...,W_K be pairwise disjoint real intervals. Put
E_same^nat=sum_{h in cal I}sum_{j=1}^K|Z_h^nat(W_j)|^2,     (7)
E_cross^nat=sum_{h in cal I}sum_{j not equal t}
 Z_h^nat(W_j)conjugate(Z_h^nat(W_t)).                       (8)
Then E_cross^nat is real and
E_same^nat
 =n^(-2)sum_{h in cal I}sum_j
  sum_{r_1,r_2 modulo n}e_n(A(r_2-r_1))
  C_{h,W_j}^nat(r_1)conjugate(C_{h,W_j}^nat(r_2)),          (9)
E_cross^nat
 =n^(-2)sum_{h in cal I}sum_{j not equal t}
  sum_{r_1,r_2 modulo n}e_n(A(r_2-r_1))
  C_{h,W_j}^nat(r_1)conjugate(C_{h,W_t}^nat(r_2)).          (10)
No absolute value has been inserted into either completed sector.

Now assume the exact retained q-support comes from a finite source row cal X of integer triples x=(q,m,k_red) satisfying
Q<=q,m<2Q, q m+n k_red=A, gcd(qm,n)=1,                     (11)
and every inherited mask, with q-coordinate injective. Put lambda_x=k_red/q. Let J_1,...,J_K be pairwise disjoint real intervals such that
cal X_j={x in cal X:lambda_x belongs to J_j}                (12)
partitions cal X, and put W_j=-nJ_j. Then
x=(q,m_n(q),k_red) belongs to cal X_j
if and only if
m_n(q)-A/q belongs to W_j.                                 (13)
If every J_j has length at most 1/(12H), then every W_j has length at most n/(12H). The unequal-slope natural Gram on this row is exactly
E_same^nat+E_cross^nat
 -sum_{h in cal I}sum_lambda
   |sum_{x in cal X:lambda_x=lambda}
     B_h^nat(q_x)e(h lambda_x)|^2.                          (14)

Equations (5), (9), and (10) are therefore the exact natural forward C1 same-window/cross-window operator: they retain mu(q), Fhat_{g,cq,n}(-h/n), chi_nat, the corrected moving interval m-A/q in W, the full composite modulus n=vp, and all window interactions before absolute values. Fact 7596cf19a80bf8f3 shows that the complete hard positivity support cannot be inserted into this proper finite-band coefficient solely by Fourier truncation. No estimate for (9)-(10), no Gadd^(-1) saving, no PMD closure, and no Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
8349d056bf34d112.proof:
Equation (2) is exactly the coefficient a_h^PMD(q) of fact ee6886ba9ed393f1. That fact proves that multiplying (2) by the explicit PMD phase in (4) reproduces the reindexed negative natural Poisson term. Directly, the two ordinary exponential factors cancel:
e(-Ah/(qn))e(hA/(nq))=1.
Thus the coefficient remaining before the modular phase e_n(-hm) is
-mu(c)mu(v)mu(q)[H_P/n]
 Fhat_{g,cq,n}(-h/n)chi_nat.

Insert additive orthogonality
1_{qm congruent A modulo n}
=n^(-1)sum_{r modulo n}e_n(r(qm-A))
into (4). After the preceding cancellation and interchange of finite sums,
Z_h^nat(W)
=n^(-1)sum_r e_n(-rA)
 [-mu(c)mu(v)(H_P/n)
  sum_q mu(q)Fhat_{g,cq,n}(-h/n)chi_nat
  sum_{m in cal M_W(q)}e_n(m(rq-h))].
The bracket is exactly (5), proving (6).

Multiplying (6) by its conjugate for windows W_j,W_t gives
Z_h^nat(W_j)conjugate(Z_h^nat(W_t))
=n^(-2)sum_{r_1,r_2}e_n(A(r_2-r_1))
 C_{h,W_j}^nat(r_1)conjugate(C_{h,W_t}^nat(r_2)).
Summing j=t proves (9), and summing ordered j not equal to t proves (10). Pairing the ordered pair (j,t) with (t,j) proves that E_cross^nat is real.

For x=(q,m,k_red) satisfying (11),
lambda_x=k_red/q=A/(nq)-m/n
=-(m-A/q)/n.
Therefore lambda_x belongs to J_j if and only if m-A/q belongs to -nJ_j=W_j, proving (13). The length assertion follows by multiplying interval length by n. Since the W_j partition the source atoms, the full square over all windows is E_same^nat+E_cross^nat. Removing the pairs with equal lambda gives exactly the subtraction in (14). This is the same algebraic unequal-slope deletion as fact 0a7dc0c20f026253, now with the exact natural coefficient (2). The final support limitation is fact 7596cf19a80bf8f3.

glossary.B_h^nat: The exact natural PMD-gauge q-coefficient on the reindexed negative-frequency half.
glossary.C_{h,W}^nat: The exact additively completed natural moving-window row.
glossary.E_cross^nat: The exact natural ordered cross-window energy.
glossary.Z_h^nat: The exact natural corrected-window source sum.

83c98e3d3a11382b.title: Fix real numbers \(1/2<\alpha<\beta<1\), \(\eta>0\), and \(\rho>0\). Let \(W\) be a bounded real function supported in \([\alpha,\beta]\), let \(\Phi\) be a bounded real function supported in \([1/2,2]\), let \(x\ge3\), \(N=2x\) be an integer, and let \(D,U>0\) satisfy
83c98e3d3a11382b.author: slava chan
83c98e3d3a11382b.statement:
Fix real numbers \(1/2<\alpha<\beta<1\), \(\eta>0\), and \(\rho>0\). Let \(W\) be a bounded real function supported in \([\alpha,\beta]\), let \(\Phi\) be a bounded real function supported in \([1/2,2]\), let \(x\ge3\), \(N=2x\) be an integer, and let \(D,U>0\) satisfy
\[
 D\le2x^{1/2},\qquad D>2T_x,\qquad
 T_x=(\log x)^{6+\eta+\rho}.
\]
Define
\[
 {\cal I}_D=\{d\ge2:(d,N)=1,\ \mu(d)\ne0,\ d\le x^{1/2},\
                    \Phi(d/D)\ne0\},
\]
and extend \(\Lambda\) by zero on nonpositive integers. For positive integers \(s,m\), define
\[
 T_{s,m}=
 \sum_{\substack{w\ge1\\sw\in{\cal I}_D}}
 \mu(w)\Phi(sw/D)W(smw/x)
 \Phi((N-smw)/U)\Lambda(N-smw).                          \tag{1}
\]
Put
\[
 c_{T_x}(s)=
 \sum_{\substack{gr=s\\1\le g<T_x\\1\le r<T_x}}\mu(r).   \tag{2}
\]
Let \({\cal E}_{<}\) be the double-small-divisor signed energy in fact
1f5316e61daf156d. Then exactly
\[
 {\cal E}_{<}=\sum_{s<T_x^2}c_{T_x}(s)\sum_{m\ge1}|T_{s,m}|^2.           \tag{3}
\]
The complete interior coefficients are
\[
 c_{T_x}(1)=1,\qquad c_{T_x}(s)=0\quad(1<s<T_x).          \tag{4}
\]
Define the full-von-Mangoldt top-band dispersion
\[
 {\mathfrak D}_N^\Lambda=
 \sum_{m\ge1}\left|
 \sum_{d\in{\cal I}_D}
 \mu(d)\Phi(d/D)W(dm/x)
 \Phi((N-dm)/U)\Lambda(N-dm)
 \right|^2.                                               \tag{5}
\]
Then
\[
 {\mathfrak D}_N^\Lambda=\sum_{m\ge1}|T_{1,m}|^2,         \tag{6}
\]
and
\[
 {\cal E}_{<}
 ={\mathfrak D}_N^\Lambda
 +O_{W,\Phi,\alpha,\beta}\!\left(
 {xD(\log x)^2\log(2T_x)\over T_x}\right).               \tag{7}
\]
Since \(\rho>0\),
\[
 {xD(\log x)^2\log(2T_x)\over T_x}
 =o\!\left(xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta}\right).                  \tag{8}
\]

Consequently (TB-COP-CORE) of fact 1f5316e61daf156d is, up to the negligible boundary (8), the original full-von-Mangoldt dispersion estimate
\[
 {\mathfrak D}_N^\Lambda
 \ll xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta}.                               \tag{9}
\]
Thus the sequence of exact physical-shift grouping, residual-gcd compression, and coprimality Möbius inversion does not by itself yield a weaker positive mean-square consumer: the complete interior Möbius recombination returns the \(s=1\) dispersion square. This is a scoped algebraic loop for that transformation sequence, not an impossibility theorem for spectral, bilinear, or shifted-prime estimates applied before the final recombination. No estimate for \({\mathfrak D}_N^\Lambda\) is asserted.
83c98e3d3a11382b.proof:
Recall from fact 1f5316e61daf156d that
\[
 {\cal E}_{<}=
 \sum_{g<T_x}\sum_{\substack{G\ge1\\g\mid G}}
 \sum_{r<T_x}\mu(r)|S_{g,G,r}|^2,                        \tag{10}
\]
where
\[
 S_{g,G,r}=\sum_{\substack{u\ge1\\r\mid u}}
 {\bf1}_{gu\in{\cal I}_D}
 \mu(u)\Phi(gu/D)W(uG/x)
 \Phi((N-uG)/U)\Lambda(N-uG).                            \tag{11}
\]
Write
\[
 G=gm,\qquad u=rw,\qquad s=gr.
\]
If the summand in (11) is nonzero, then \(gu=grw=sw\) is squarefree.
Hence \(r\) and \(w\) are squarefree and coprime, and
\[
 \mu(u)=\mu(rw)=\mu(r)\mu(w).                             \tag{12}
\]
Also
\[
 gu=sw,\qquad uG=rwgm=smw.
\]
Substitution into (11) gives
\[
 S_{g,gm,r}=\mu(r)T_{gr,m}.                               \tag{13}
\]
The factor \(\mu(r)\) disappears after taking the squared absolute value. Inserting (13) into (10) and grouping by \(s=gr\) proves (3).

If \(1\le s<T_x\), then every positive divisor \(r\mid s\) satisfies
\(r<T_x\), and its complementary divisor \(g=s/r\) also satisfies
\(g<T_x\). Therefore
\[
 c_{T_x}(s)=\sum_{r\mid s}\mu(r).
\]
The elementary Möbius divisor identity gives value \(1\) at \(s=1\) and
\(0\) for \(s>1\), proving (4). Equation (1) with \(s=1\) is exactly the inner sum in (5), proving (6).

It remains to bound the boundary \(T_x\le s<T_x^2\). Trivially
\[
 |c_{T_x}(s)|\le\tau(s).                                 \tag{14}
\]
If \(T_{s,m}\ne0\), the supports give
\[
 D/2\le sw\le2D,\qquad \alpha x\le smw\le\beta x.
\]
For fixed \(s,m\), there are \(O(D/s)\) possible \(w\), and every summand in (1) is \(O_{W,\Phi}(\log x)\). Thus
\[
 |T_{s,m}|\ll_{W,\Phi}{D\log x\over s}.                  \tag{15}
\]
For fixed \(s\), the existence of such a \(w\) forces
\[
 {\alpha x\over2D}\le m\le{2\beta x\over D},
\]
so there are \(O_{\alpha,\beta}(x/D)\) possible \(m\). Hence
\[
 \sum_m|T_{s,m}|^2
 \ll_{W,\Phi,\alpha,\beta}{xD(\log x)^2\over s^2}.        \tag{16}
\]

We use
\[
 \sum_{s\ge Y}{\tau(s)\over s^2}\ll{\log(2Y)\over Y}
 \qquad(Y\ge1).                                          \tag{17}
\]
Indeed,
\[
 \sum_{n\le Z}\tau(n)
 =\sum_{ab\le Z}1
 \le Z\sum_{a\le Z}{1\over a}
 \ll Z\log(2Z),
\]
and dyadic decomposition of \(s\ge Y\) proves (17). Equations
(14)--(17) give
\[
 \sum_{T_x\le s<T_x^2}
 |c_{T_x}(s)|\sum_m|T_{s,m}|^2
 \ll {xD(\log x)^2\log(2T_x)\over T_x},
\]
which proves (7).

Finally \(T_x=(\log x)^{6+\eta+\rho}\) with \(\rho>0\), while
\(\log(2T_x)\ll\log\log x=o((\log x)^\rho)\). This proves (8), and
(9) follows from (7).

glossary.T_{s,m}: the reflected Möbius-prime sum after merging the residual gcd g and coprimality divisor r into s=gr
glossary.c_T(s): the truncated divisor coefficient sum over gr=s with g,r<T_x

83d01a70b7f16e15.title: DUAL-SHIFT FOURIER INVERSION PRESERVES THE LITERAL SOURCE BUT DOES NOT REMOVE THE PROPORTIONAL-RAY DIAGONAL
83d01a70b7f16e15.author: slava chan
83d01a70b7f16e15.statement:
DUAL-SHIFT FOURIER INVERSION PRESERVES THE LITERAL SOURCE BUT DOES NOT REMOVE THE PROPORTIONAL-RAY DIAGONAL.

Let \(r,r'\) be nonempty squarefree positive integers and put \(L=\operatorname{lcm}(r,r')\). For a forward or reverse GA-tail centered face, let
\[
 \Phi_{j,r}(q)=\prod_{p\mid r}\phi_{p,j}(q)
\]
be the exact physical centered face from fact 0aa821ade9a14b45, with reverse orientation obtained by the swap in fact e55b27d39c593164. Put
\[
 G_L=\prod_{p\mid L}\mathbb F_p.
\]
Define
\[
 \widetilde V_{j,r}^{\,L}(\boldsymbol\rho)
 =
 \left(\prod_{p\mid r}{\bf1}_{\rho_p\ne0}\widehat f_{p,j}(\rho_p)\right)
 \left(\prod_{\substack{p\mid L\\p\nmid r}}{\bf1}_{\rho_p=0}\right).
                                                                    \tag{1}
\]
Then
\[
 \Phi_{j,r}(q)
 =\sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\in G_L}
 \widetilde V_{j,r}^{\,L}(\boldsymbol\rho)
 \chi_{\boldsymbol\rho}^{L}(q),\qquad
 \chi_{\boldsymbol\rho}^{L}(q)=\prod_{p\mid L}e_p(\rho_pq).       \tag{2}
\]
For \(\boldsymbol t\in G_L\) and an integer \(s\), define
\[
 \mathcal H_{r,r'}^{L}(j,k;\boldsymbol t,s)
 =
 \sum_{\boldsymbol\sigma\in G_L}
 \widetilde V_{j,r}^{\,L}(\boldsymbol\sigma+\boldsymbol t)
 \overline{\widetilde V_{k,r'}^{\,L}(\boldsymbol\sigma)}
 \chi_{\boldsymbol\sigma}^{L}(s).                                \tag{3}
\]
For every \(q_1,q_2\), with \(s=q_1-q_2\),
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_{\boldsymbol t\in G_L}
 \chi_{\boldsymbol t}^{L}(q_1)
 \mathcal H_{r,r'}^{L}(j,k;\boldsymbol t,q_1-q_2)
 =
 \Phi_{j,r}(q_1)\overline{\Phi_{k,r'}(q_2)}.
 }                                                               \tag{4}
\]
Thus dual-shift inversion preserves the complete literal physical source: multiplying (4) by
\(B_{j,r}(q_1)\overline{B_{k,r'}(q_2)}\) and summing all indices reconstructs the original weighted scalar face product with every literal mask unchanged.

If \(r=r'\), the \(\boldsymbol t=\boldsymbol0\) term is exactly the same-\(r\) coordinatewise dual diagonal in physical variables, and the nonzero shifts are the off-dual discrepancy of fact e08b28d0e17e861c. If \(r\ne r'\), then
\[
 \mathcal H_{r,r'}^{L}(j,k;\boldsymbol0,s)=0                     \tag{5}
\]
because distinct squarefree positive integers have different prime supports. Thus every distinct-\(r\) incomplete cross term lies on nonzero shifts; (4) reconstructs rather than annihilates it. The complete lcm orthogonality of fact 3fde81ce051bff7b requires an additional complete physical average absent from the literal \(q\)-source.

For the Plancherel audit, let \(G\) be a finite product of prime fields, let \(A:G\to\mathbb C\), and put
\[
 R_A(\boldsymbol t)
 =\sum_{\boldsymbol\sigma\in G}
 A(\boldsymbol\sigma+\boldsymbol t)\overline{A(\boldsymbol\sigma)},
 \qquad
 \widehat A(x)=\sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\in G}
 A(\boldsymbol\rho)\chi_{\boldsymbol\rho}(x).                    \tag{6}
\]
Then
\[
 \sum_{\boldsymbol t\in G}R_A(\boldsymbol t)\chi_{\boldsymbol t}(x)
 =|\widehat A(x)|^2,                                             \tag{7}
\]
and
\[
 \sum_{\boldsymbol t\in G}|R_A(\boldsymbol t)|^2
 ={1\over|G|}\sum_{x\in G}|\widehat A(x)|^4.                     \tag{8}
\]
For fixed \(r\), take \(G=G_r=\prod_{p\mid r}\mathbb F_p\), define
\[
 A(\boldsymbol\rho)
 =
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle\sum_jc_jV_{j,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)W_{j,r}(\boldsymbol\rho),
   &\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r,\\
 0,&\boldsymbol\rho\notin\Omega_r.
 \end{cases}                                                     \tag{9}
\]
Then
\[
 R_A(\boldsymbol0)=\mathcal D_r(c),\qquad
 \sum_{\boldsymbol t\ne\boldsymbol0}R_A(\boldsymbol t)
 =\mathcal O_r(c).                                               \tag{10}
\]
Thus shift Plancherel replaces the known coordinate \(L^2\) bound by the physical fourth moment in (8), for which no estimate is supplied. Generic scalar conversion loses the sharp factor
\[
 |\Omega_r|=\prod_{p\mid r}(p-1)
\]
of fact 9128d43a5ac4e1bb, while literal shiftwise absolute summation costs \(r^{1/2+o(1)}\) by fact e08b28d0e17e861c.

The zero dual shift is not the proportional-ray diagonal. With
\[
 q_1=q+s,\qquad q_2=q,
\]
a row pair with frequencies \(h_j,h_k\) has
\[
 \Delta=h_jq-h_k(q+s).                                          \tag{11}
\]
The condition \(\boldsymbol t=\boldsymbol0\) is independent of (11): \(s=0\), \(h_j\ne h_k\) permits \(\Delta\ne0\) with zero shift, whereas \(s=0\), \(h_j=h_k\) permits \(\Delta=0\) with nonzero shift. Hence dual-shift inversion and Plancherel do not remove
\(\mathcal M_F^{(0)}(\mathcal D)\) before the norm.

Consequently:

1. On \(\mathcal D\le QF\), a full scalar moment estimate at
\[
 x^\varepsilon|\omega_F|^2BQ^2F^2/\mathcal D
\]
would imply GA-NR-DIL by fact c7970d9d1337bd09, but (4)--(10) do not prove it.

2. On \(\mathcal D>QF\), full-moment subtraction has the exact excess \(\mathcal D/(QF)\). The required theorem remains
\[
 \left|\mathcal M_F(\mathcal D)-\mathcal M_F^{(0)}(\mathcal D)\right|
 \ll_\varepsilon
 x^\varepsilon|\omega_F|^2{BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D},              \tag{GA-OFF-SYN}
\]
with the proportional-ray projector inserted in the physical
\((j,k,s,q)\) source before any shift or row-pair absolute value.

This proves no scalar fixed-\(r\) estimate, distinct-\(r\) incomplete estimate, GA-OFF-SYN, GA-NR-DIL, good-\(\mathscr W\) payment, or Goldbach conclusion.
83d01a70b7f16e15.proof:
For \(p\mid r\), fact 0aa821ade9a14b45 gives
\[
 \phi_{p,j}(q)=\sum_{\rho_p\ne0}\widehat f_{p,j}(\rho_p)e_p(\rho_pq).
\]
At \(p\mid L\), \(p\nmid r\), the absent factor has Fourier support only at zero with coefficient one. Multiplication proves (1)--(2), in either orientation.

Expand the left side of (4):
\[
 \sum_{\boldsymbol t,\boldsymbol\sigma}
 \widetilde V_{j,r}^{\,L}(\boldsymbol\sigma+\boldsymbol t)
 \overline{\widetilde V_{k,r'}^{\,L}(\boldsymbol\sigma)}
 \chi_{\boldsymbol t}^{L}(q_1)
 \chi_{\boldsymbol\sigma}^{L}(q_1-q_2).
\]
Set \(\boldsymbol\rho=\boldsymbol\sigma+\boldsymbol t\). Since
\[
 \chi_{\boldsymbol t}^{L}(q_1)\chi_{\boldsymbol\sigma}^{L}(q_1-q_2)
 =\chi_{\boldsymbol\rho}^{L}(q_1)
  \overline{\chi_{\boldsymbol\sigma}^{L}(q_2)},
\]
the sum factors into the two Fourier inversions in (2), proving (4). Finite summation against the zero-extended literal \(B\)'s preserves every source factor.

For \(r=r'\), the zero-shift term in (3) is the physical expansion of the coordinatewise dual diagonal, and the complement is fact e08b28d0e17e861c. For distinct squarefree positive \(r,r'\), choose a prime in their support symmetric difference. At zero shift, one embedded vector requires that coordinate nonzero and the other requires it zero. Their product vanishes, proving (5). Equation (4) and fact 3fde81ce051bff7b prove the incomplete-versus-complete distinction.

To prove (7), expand its left side and set
\(\boldsymbol\rho=\boldsymbol\sigma+\boldsymbol t\):
\[
 \sum_{\boldsymbol\rho,\boldsymbol\sigma}
 A(\boldsymbol\rho)\overline{A(\boldsymbol\sigma)}
 \chi_{\boldsymbol\rho-\boldsymbol\sigma}(x)
 =|\widehat A(x)|^2.
\]
Parseval for the unnormalized transform gives (8). Definition (9) makes \(A\) a function on all of \(G_r\). Then
\[
 R_A(\boldsymbol0)
 =\sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r}
 \left|\sum_jc_jV_{j,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)W_{j,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)\right|^2
 =\mathcal D_r(c).
\]
For nonzero \(\boldsymbol t\), the zero extension restricts both
\(\boldsymbol\sigma\) and \(\boldsymbol\sigma+\boldsymbol t\) to \(\Omega_r\). The bijection to the unequal pair
\((\boldsymbol\rho,\boldsymbol\sigma)\) proves the second identity in (10). The two cited facts give the displayed generic losses.

The determinant in fact e55b27d39c593164 is
\(\Delta=h_1q_2-h_2q_1\). Substitution of
\(q_1=q+s,q_2=q\), with row names interchanged if necessary, gives (11) up to a simultaneous sign, which does not change its zero set. The two examples prove independence of zero shift and zero determinant.

Fact c7970d9d1337bd09 proves the legality of full-minus subtraction on
\(\mathcal D\le QF\), the exact excess \(\mathcal D/(QF)\) above that range, and the sufficiency of GA-OFF-SYN. These substitutions prove the final two statements. All limitations are explicit.

glossary.cross-face shift kernel: The lcm-level correlation of two embedded face Fourier vectors at a dual shift and physical displacement.
glossary.dual-shift Plancherel no-fit: The exact fact that shift Fourier inversion returns the physical face product and shift Plancherel requires an uncontrolled physical fourth moment.
glossary.embedded face Fourier vector: The centered-face Fourier vector extended to the lcm prime product by zero frequencies at absent active primes.

8456d95ce27b28b8.title: For a positive integer \(P\), define
8456d95ce27b28b8.author: slava chan
8456d95ce27b28b8.statement:
For a positive integer \(P\), define
\[
 L(P;q)={\bf1}_{q\mid P}\mu(q)\log(P/q)_+,
 \qquad y_+=\max(y,0).
\]
Then
\[
 \sum_{q\ge1}L(P;q)=\Lambda(P).                         \tag{1}
\]
Consequently, for all positive integers \(P_1,P_2\),
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_{q_1,q_2\ge1}L(P_1;q_1)L(P_2;q_2)
 =\Lambda(P_1)\Lambda(P_2).
 }                                                       \tag{2}
\]
If \(K(P)=\lceil\log_2P\rceil\), then
\[
 \sum_{j=0}^{K(P)}
 \sum_{2^j\le q<2^{j+1}}L(P;q)=\Lambda(P),              \tag{3}
\]
and the analogous double dyadic-shell sum equals the right side of (2),
with no truncation error.

Let
\[
 P_1=N-mw,\qquad P_2=N-m(w-h)
\]
be positive integers, and let \(B(m,w,h)\) be any finitely supported
complex coefficient independent of \(q_1,q_2\). Then
\[
\begin{split}
 &\sum_{q_1,q_2\ge1}\sum_{m,w,h}
 B(m,w,h)L(P_1;q_1)L(P_2;q_2)\\
 &\qquad=
 \sum_{m,w,h}B(m,w,h)\Lambda(P_1)\Lambda(P_2).          \tag{4}
\end{split}
\]
Thus complete divisor shells may be recombined with zero error before any
\(q_1,q_2\)-dependent transform.

If a further weight is not independent of \(q_1,q_2\), identities (1)--(4)
do not by themselves evaluate the resulting weighted divisor convolution.
In particular, the TMC zero modes in fact a88b7867c1bc2fd9 contain
\[
 [q_1,q_2]^{-2},\qquad
 c_{[q_1,q_2]}(r),\qquad
 e_{q_2/(q_1,q_2)}(-rhq_1^{-1}),                       \tag{5}
\]
which depend on \(q_1,q_2\). Identifying the complete shell sum weighted
by (5) with the two-linear-form singular series requires a separate local
Euler/convolution calculation. The arbitrary-logarithmic cancellation in
fact 5b7b0955c5efaa1b applies after such a singular-series main has been
identified; it does not perform this identification automatically.
8456d95ce27b28b8.proof:
Every divisor \(q\mid P\) satisfies \(q\le P\), so
\(\log(P/q)_+=\log(P/q)\). Möbius inversion of
\[
 \log P=\sum_{d\mid P}\Lambda(d)
\]
gives
\[
 \Lambda(P)=\sum_{q\mid P}\mu(q)\log(P/q),
\]
proving (1). Multiplication proves (2).

Every positive \(q\le P\) belongs to exactly one half-open shell
\([2^j,2^{j+1})\) with \(0\le j\le K(P)\), while every divisor \(q>P\)
contributes zero. This proves (3) and its double version.

For each fixed \((m,w,h)\), equation (2) evaluates the inner divisor sum
in (4). All sums are finite, so their order may be interchanged, proving
(4).

This argument factors the divisor sums because \(B\) is independent of
\(q_1,q_2\). The three quantities in (5) vary with those divisors, so
(1)--(4) alone do not evaluate the resulting different convolution.
Fact 5b7b0955c5efaa1b estimates the already defined singular-series
weighted two-slope sum; it contains no assertion equating that series to
the divisor convolution with (5). This proves only the stated need for a
separate calculation.

glossary.L(P;q): the exact Möbius-log divisor sibling coefficient 1_{q|P}mu(q)log(P/q)_+
glossary.TMC shell recombination: the complete q_1,q_2 dyadic divisor sum before inserting any q_1,q_2-dependent TMC multiplier

84bf915e8a88d8d3.title: EXACT BANDPASS-POISSON SOFT-SOURCE BRIDGE AND ITS SHARP AVERAGE/POINTWISE TAX
84bf915e8a88d8d3.author: slava chan
84bf915e8a88d8d3.statement:
EXACT BANDPASS-POISSON SOFT-SOURCE BRIDGE AND ITS SHARP AVERAGE/POINTWISE TAX.

Use e(x)=exp(2 pi i x), and for an integrable function f on R use
 fhat(xi)=integral_R f(x)e(-xi x)dx,
 fcheck(x)=integral_R f(xi)e(x xi)dx.                       (1)
Let n=vp, where v and p are coprime positive integers and p is prime. Let H>1 and put
 Y=n/H.                                                      (2)
Let Phi be a fixed smooth compactly supported complex function on R whose support does not contain zero. Define
 psi_Y(x)=Y^(-1)Phicheck(x/Y).                              (3)
Let cal Q be a finite set of positive integers q with gcd(q,n)=1. For each q in cal Q let F_q be a smooth compactly supported complex function, and put
 G_q=F_q*psi_Y.                                              (4)
Then
 Ghat_q(xi)=Fhat_q(xi)Phi(Yxi).                              (5)

Fix an integer A. For t modulo p define the finite bandpass row
 a_{q,t}=n^(-1)sum_{h in Z}
   Phi(h/H)Fhat_q(h/n)e_n(hAqbar)e_p(ht),                   (6)
where e_m(x)=e(x/m) and qbar is the inverse of q modulo n. The h-sum is finite and excludes h=0 automatically. One has the exact soft-source identity
 a_{q,t}=sum_{m in Z;qm congruent A modulo n}G_q(m+vt).     (7)
Thus the proper finite h-band has an exact source-preserving Poisson representation, but its source amplitude is the noncompact Schwartz-tailed function G_q rather than the compactly supported F_q.

Assume additionally that |cal Q|<=Q, that every |F_q(x)|<=B, and that the support interval J_q of F_q has length at most C_0Y, where B>=1 and C_0>=1 are fixed. Then for every fixed integer M>=2 there is a constant C_M depending only on Phi,C_0,M such that
 |G_q(x)|<=C_MB(1+dist(x,J_q)/Y)^(-M).                      (8)
Put
 z_t(q)=sum_{m;qm congruent A mod n}G_q(m+vt),
 Z_t=sum_{q in cal Q}|z_t(q)|.                              (9)
Then
 Z_t<<_{Phi,C_0}BQ,                                        (10)
 sum_{t modulo p}Z_t<<_{Phi,C_0}BQ(1+p/H).                 (11)
If p>2H, then for every fixed integer r>=1,
 p^(-1)sum_{t modulo p}Z_t^r
 <<_{Phi,C_0,r}B^rQ^r/H.                                   (12)
Consequently the bandpass bridge recovers only average soft-source mass BQ/H; it does not give the pointwise type-(U) support Q/H required by facts 914048233fada05f, 0e8ef74ba484418d, or 11ec605c5135a640. Relative to such a pointwise hypothesis, (12) has an H^2 loss at r=3 and an H^3 loss at r=4.

Finally suppose the support of Phi is contained in an interval of length D_0. Then the h-support in (6) has span at most D_0H+1. If
 p>2(D_0H+1),                                               (13)
and A_{v,p}(theta)=sum_q n^(-1)sum_h
 Phi(h/H)Fhat_q(h/n)e_n(hAqbar)e(htheta),                   (14)
then
 integral_{R/Z}|A_{v,p}(theta)|^4dtheta
 =p^(-1)sum_{t modulo p}|sum_qa_{q,t}|^4.                  (15)
Equations (7) and (15) are a common-row bridge between the finite-band L4 contract of fact 44e700816602dd36 and an exact source equation. They do not prove the required fourth-moment saving: the source is soft and has only the average tax (12), so the modular-mean, exact-slope, and Delta-nonzero vector estimates at the target P^2Q^(7/3) remain new analytic inputs. No impossibility or Goldbach claim is made.
84bf915e8a88d8d3.proof:
Equation (3) and Fourier scaling give
 psihat_Y(xi)=Phi(Yxi).                                     (16)
The convolution theorem then proves (5).

Fix q and t and put c=Aqbar modulo n. The function G_q is Schwartz: psi_Y is Schwartz because Phi is smooth and compactly supported, and convolution with compactly supported smooth F_q preserves Schwartz decay. Its Fourier transform in (5) is smooth and compactly supported. Periodize G_q on the progression c+nZ. Absolute convergence permits Fourier expansion, and its h-th coefficient is
 n^(-1)Ghat_q(h/n)e_n(hc).                                 (17)
Because Ghat_q is compactly supported, this Fourier series is finite. Evaluating the periodization after translation by vt gives
 sum_{m congruent c mod n}G_q(m+vt)
 =n^(-1)sum_hGhat_q(h/n)e_n(h(c+vt)).                      (18)
Use (5), Y=n/H, and e_n(hvt)=e_p(ht). Equation (18) becomes (6), proving (7). The congruence m congruent Aqbar modulo n is equivalent to qm congruent A modulo n.

Since Phicheck is Schwartz, for every M>=2,
 |psi_Y(s)|<=C_{Phi,M}Y^(-1)(1+|s|/Y)^(-M).                (19)
If x is at distance d from J_q, then |x-y|>=d for y in J_q. Using |F_q|<=B and |J_q|<=C_0Y in the convolution integral gives
 |G_q(x)|
 <=B integral_{J_q}|psi_Y(x-y)|dy
 <<_{Phi,C_0,M}B(1+d/Y)^(-M),
which is (8).

For fixed q,t the points m+vt in (9) are spaced by n=HY. Apply (8). At most O_{C_0}(1) points lie within distance O(Y) of J_q, and the remaining normalized distances grow in steps comparable to H. Since M>=2, their decay sum is bounded independently of H. Therefore
 |z_t(q)|<<_{Phi,C_0}B.                                    (20)
Summing over q proves (10).

For fixed q, write the progression m=c+nk. The map
 (t,k) -> r=t+pk
is a bijection from (Z/pZ) times Z to Z, and
 m+vt=c+v(t+pk)=c+vr.                                      (21)
Hence
 sum_{t modulo p}|z_t(q)|
 <=sum_{r in Z}|G_q(c+vr)|.                                (22)
Use (8) again. The number of v-spaced points within distance O(Y) of J_q is O_{C_0}(1+Y/v)=O_{C_0}(1+p/H), and the Schwartz tails have the same bound by summing dyadic distance shells. Thus
 sum_t|z_t(q)|<<_{Phi,C_0}B(1+p/H).                        (23)
Sum over q to prove (11).

By (10),
 sum_tZ_t^r
 <=(C_{Phi,C_0}BQ)^(r-1)sum_tZ_t.
Use (11), divide by p, and use p>2H to absorb the term p^(-1) into H^(-1). This proves (12) and the displayed loss comparison.

The h-values in (14) lie in H times the fixed support interval of Phi, so their span is at most D_0H+1. Under (13), the frequencies of |A_{v,p}(theta)|^4 have absolute value less than p. Averaging over theta=t/p and integrating both retain exactly the zero Fourier coefficient. This proves (15). Because the sampled value in (14) is exactly sum_qa_{q,t}, equation (7) applies to the same finite-band row. The final scope statement follows from (10)-(12) and from the sufficient target in fact 44e700816602dd36.

glossary.G_q: The bandpass-smoothed source amplitude F_q convolved with psi_Y.
glossary.Z_t: The total absolute q-row mass of the soft source at discrete twist t.
glossary.psi_Y: The inverse-Fourier bandpass kernel at physical width Y.
glossary.soft-source bridge: The exact finite-band Poisson identity (8), whose source amplitude is Schwartz-tailed rather than compactly supported.

84fecb4344bb7024.title: Let r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4 be pairwise distinct odd primes, let A be an integer coprime to their product, and write e_q(z)=exp(2 pi i z/q). For h modulo r_1r_2 and k modulo r_1r_3, one has the exact crossed-gate CRT identity
84fecb4344bb7024.author: slava chan
84fecb4344bb7024.statement:
Let r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4 be pairwise distinct odd primes, let A be an integer coprime to their product, and write e_q(z)=exp(2 pi i z/q). For h modulo r_1r_2 and k modulo r_1r_3, one has the exact crossed-gate CRT identity
 e_{r_1r_2}(A h (r_3r_4)^(-1)) e_{r_1r_3}(A k (r_2r_4)^(-1))
 =e_{r_2}(A h (r_1r_3r_4)^(-1)) e_{r_3}(A k (r_1r_2r_4)^(-1)) e_{r_1}(A(h+k)(r_2r_3r_4)^(-1)),
where every inverse is taken modulo the subscripted prime or product. The map
(h modulo r_1r_2,k modulo r_1r_3) -> (h modulo r_2,k modulo r_3,h+k modulo r_1)
is surjective and every fibre has exactly r_1 elements. Consequently the frequency domain has an exact disjoint partition indexed by subsets S of {1,2,3}, according to which of the three local axes h modulo r_2, k modulo r_3, h+k modulo r_1 vanish; the stratum on which exactly the axes in S vanish has r_1 times the product of (r_i-1) over the nonvanishing corresponding prime axes elements.

Let p be an odd prime and eta a nonzero residue modulo p. Define the simultaneous two-axis complete kernel
 H_p(h,k;eta)=sum over nonzero x,y modulo p of e_p(hx+ky+eta(h+k)(xy)^(-1)).
Define the unnormalized rank-3 hyper-Kloosterman sum Kl_3(z;p)=sum over nonzero X,Y modulo p of e_p(X+Y+z(XY)^(-1)). If h,k,h+k are all nonzero modulo p, then
 H_p(h,k;eta)=Kl_3(eta h k(h+k);p).
If (h,k) is not (0,0) and lies on one of the three planes h=0, k=0, or h+k=0 modulo p, then H_p(h,k;eta)=1. At their common intersection (h,k)=(0,0), one has H_p(0,0;eta)=(p-1)^2. Thus simultaneous completion of the two crossed axes has a generic rank-3 hyper-Kloosterman kernel and three explicitly paid degenerate planes; it is not the one-variable classical Kloosterman kernel Kl_2.
84fecb4344bb7024.proof:
For coprime positive integers u,v, the CRT identity e_{uv}(z)=e_u(z v^(-1))e_v(z u^(-1)) holds. Apply it first to r_1r_2. The component modulo r_2 is e_{r_2}(A h (r_1r_3r_4)^(-1)), while the component modulo r_1 is e_{r_1}(A h (r_2r_3r_4)^(-1)). Applying the same identity to r_1r_3 gives the displayed r_3 component and the r_1 component e_{r_1}(A k (r_2r_3r_4)^(-1)). Multiplying the two r_1 components adds their numerators and gives the h+k factor. This proves the crossed-gate identity.

To prove the fibre claim, prescribe residues alpha modulo r_2, beta modulo r_3, and gamma modulo r_1. There are exactly r_1 choices for the residue h_1=h modulo r_1. Once h_1 is chosen, k modulo r_1 must be gamma-h_1. The CRT then gives a unique h modulo r_1r_2 with components h_1 and alpha, and a unique k modulo r_1r_3 with components gamma-h_1 and beta. Thus the map is onto with r_1-element fibres. Requiring a specified subset of alpha,beta,gamma to be zero and the complementary coordinates to be nonzero gives the asserted exact stratum sizes.

For the complete kernel, suppose h,k,h+k are all nonzero modulo p. Make the bijective changes of variables X=hx and Y=ky on the two unit groups. Since (xy)^(-1)=hk(XY)^(-1), the phase becomes X+Y+eta h k(h+k)(XY)^(-1). This is exactly Kl_3(eta h k(h+k);p).

If h=0 and k is nonzero, then h+k=k. For each fixed nonzero y, the sum over nonzero x of e_p(eta k (xy)^(-1)) is -1, because x^(-1) runs through the nonzero residues and its coefficient is nonzero. The remaining sum is -sum_{y nonzero}e_p(ky)=1. The case k=0,h nonzero is symmetric. If h+k=0 with h nonzero, the inverse-product term vanishes and the complete sum factors as (sum_{x nonzero}e_p(hx))(sum_{y nonzero}e_p(-hy))=(-1)(-1)=1. Since p is odd, two of the three equations h=0,k=0,h+k=0 imply all three, so their only common intersections occur at h=k=0. At that origin the phase is identically zero and there are (p-1)^2 pairs. The generic kernel has two independent unit summation variables, which by definition is rank 3 rather than the one-unit-variable classical Kloosterman sum.

glossary.H_p: the simultaneous two-axis complete crossed-gate kernel
glossary.Kl_3: the unnormalized rank-3 hyper-Kloosterman sum over two unit variables
glossary.S: a subset specifying which of the three local frequency axes vanish

8592875ae5046498.title: EXACT PRECOMPLETION COLLAPSE AND GLOBAL SELECTOR OBSTRUCTION FOR THE UNRESTRICTED IJOP CLASS
8592875ae5046498.author: slava chan
8592875ae5046498.statement:
EXACT PRECOMPLETION COLLAPSE AND GLOBAL SELECTOR OBSTRUCTION FOR THE UNRESTRICTED IJOP CLASS.

Let m>1 be odd, put q=m^2 and n=phi(q), let s belong to {1,-1}, and let K be an integer coprime to m. A function W:Z/mZ -> C is called centered when
 sum_{u modulo m}W(u)=0.                                             (1)
Every multiplicative character chi of the unit group modulo q is extended to all integers by setting chi(z)=0 when gcd(z,q)>1. For two such characters define
 S(chi,psi)=sum_{u modulo m}W(u)
  conjugate(chi(K+2smu)psi(K-2smu)).                                (2)

Let I_1,I_2 be finite sets of positive integers coprime to q, and suppose gcd(n_1,n_2) divides 2K for every pair in I_1 times I_2. For each pair put
 h=gcd(n_1,n_2), u_1=n_1/h, u_2=n_2/h, D=2K/h,
and choose integers a_0,c_0 satisfying
 a_0u_2-c_0u_1=D.                                                    (3)
Let omega_{n_1,n_2}:Z^2 -> C be finitely supported and independent of chi,psi. Define the centered assembled matrix
 M_W(n_1,n_2)
 =n^(-2)sum_{chi,psi}S(chi,psi)chi(n_2)psi(-n_1)
   sum_{t in Z}omega_{n_1,n_2}(a_0+u_1t,c_0+u_2t)
     chi(a_0+u_1t)psi(c_0+u_2t),                                    (4)
where the outer sum is over every ordered character pair. Define A_W:l^2(I_1)->l^2(I_2) by
 (A_Wx)(n_2)=sum_{n_1 in I_1}M_W(n_1,n_2)x(n_1).                    (5)
Let U_IJOP denote the class obtained by allowing the weights omega_{n_1,n_2} in (4) to be chosen independently for every column pair, subject only to finite support and independence from chi,psi.

For every allowed pair and every centered W, multiplicative-character orthogonality gives the exact precompletion formula
 M_W(n_1,n_2)
 =sum_{t in Z}omega_{n_1,n_2}(a_0+u_1t,c_0+u_2t)
   sum_{u modulo m}W(u)
    1_{(a_0+u_1t)n_2 congruent K+2smu modulo q}.                     (6)
The other shared-digit congruence is redundant: the exact identity
 (a_0+u_1t)n_2-(c_0+u_2t)n_1=2K                                   (7)
shows that the congruence in (6) implies
 -(c_0+u_2t)n_1 congruent K-2smu modulo q.                           (8)
For centered W, the matrix (4) is the same nonzero-additive-frequency IJOP matrix as in fact 7cdcef43ec0d4940.

The class U_IJOP has a global all-ones obstruction. For every sufficiently large power of two X, put
 m=X+1, q=m^2, K=s=1, and W(u)=exp(2 pi i u/m).                      (9)
Let P_X be the set of odd primes in [6X/5,8X/5]. There are disjoint subsets I_1,I_2 of P_X and an absolute constant c>0 such that
 |I_1|>=cX/log X,  |I_2|>=cX/log X.                                 (10)
Every column is coprime to q and every cross gcd is one. For each column pair choose a_0,c_0 satisfying a_0n_2-c_0n_1=2. There is a unique residue t_0 modulo q such that
 (a_0+n_1t_0)n_2 congruent 1 modulo q.                              (11)
Choose one integer representative t_0 and define omega_{n_1,n_2} to be the indicator of the singleton
 {(a_0+n_1t_0,c_0+n_2t_0)}.                                        (12)
Then
 M_W(n_1,n_2)=1                                                     (13)
for every pair, so A_W is the all-ones I_2 by I_1 matrix and
 ||A_W||_op=sqrt(|I_1||I_2|)>=cX/log X.                             (14)

Consequently, suppose that for some fixed epsilon in (0,1/20), a positive constant C_epsilon independent of X, and a nonnegative selector loss L_sel(X), every member of U_IJOP in the construction (9)-(12) satisfied
 ||A_W||_op<=C_epsilon X^(19/20+epsilon)L_sel(X).                   (15)
Then necessarily
 L_sel(X)>=(c/C_epsilon)X^(1/20-epsilon)/log X                      (16)
along the powers of two. In particular, L_sel(X)=X^{o(1)} is impossible.

This is a global two-column operator counterexample, not merely a pointwise singleton bound. Its scope is strict: the row points in (12) are not asserted to lie in the actual balanced Archimedean row windows of the WF-RPS application. It is not a counterexample to an IJOP theorem for those literal moving windows. It proves that a positive theorem must exploit a genuine common window/lift-selector coherence hypothesis or pay the selector loss in (16); arbitrary independently column-dependent finite selectors are too broad.
8592875ae5046498.proof:
We prove (6). Insert (2) into (4), interchange the finite character and u sums, and combine the character factors. Since gcd(K,m)=1, both K+2smu and K-2smu are units modulo q. Multiplicative-character orthogonality on the unit group modulo q gives
 n^(-2)sum_{chi,psi}S(chi,psi)
  chi((a_0+u_1t)n_2)psi(-(c_0+u_2t)n_1)
 =sum_{u modulo m}W(u)
  1_{(a_0+u_1t)n_2 congruent K+2smu modulo q}
  1_{-(c_0+u_2t)n_1 congruent K-2smu modulo q}.                     (17)
Equation (3), together with n_1=hu_1 and n_2=hu_2, gives (7). Therefore the first indicator in (17) implies the second, proving (6) and (8). Fact 7cdcef43ec0d4940 proves that the zero additive frequency in this complete assembly vanishes for centered W, so (4) equals its nonzero-frequency IJOP matrix.

We prove (10) from fact 0e9a1691fd933c33. Fix a nonzero nonnegative continuously differentiable function V supported inside [3/5,4/5]. In that fact take its large real parameter to be x_0=2X and its even integer to be N=2x_0=4X. When X is a power of two, N is a power of two, so rad(2N)=2 and the Goldbach Euler factor in that fact is the fixed positive constant C_2. On every odd prime power p^k, the factor denoted r_N in that fact equals (p-1)/(p-2), which lies between one and two. Its accepted asymptotic therefore implies
 sum_{j>=1} sum_{p prime}V(p^j/(2X))log p >=c_1X                (18)
for a fixed c_1>0 and all sufficiently large powers of two X.

For j>=2, every contributing prime satisfies p<=(2X)^(1/2). For each such p, the sum of log p over the exponents j>=2 with p^j<=2X is at most log(2X). There are at most (2X)^(1/2) possible positive integer values of p. Thus the total contribution of j>=2 is at most (2X)^(1/2)log(2X), which is less than c_1X/2 for sufficiently large X. The prime terms in (18) therefore contribute at least c_1X/2. Every such prime belongs to P_X, and each term is at most ||V||_infinity log(2X). Hence |P_X|>=c_2X/log X for a fixed c_2>0. Partition P_X into two subsets whose sizes differ by at most one, and reduce the constant to obtain (10).

Now m=X+1 is odd. Every member of P_X is larger than m for sufficiently large X, so it cannot divide m. Thus all columns are units modulo q. Columns in the two disjoint prime sets are distinct, so their cross gcd is one.

Fix one column pair. Here h=1, u_1=n_1 and u_2=n_2. The coefficient n_1n_2 of t in (a_0+n_1t)n_2 is a unit modulo q. Therefore (11) has exactly one solution modulo q. Equation (7) shows that its singleton row point still has exact determinant two. Formula (6) applies.

For W in (9), the congruence inside (6) at t=t_0 is
 1 congruent 1+2mu modulo m^2.
Since m is odd and u is taken modulo m, this holds exactly for u=0. Thus the inner u sum is W(0)=1. The singleton weight (12) has value one there and vanishes at every other row point. This proves (13).

An all-ones matrix from l^2(I_1) to l^2(I_2) maps the constant unit vector on I_1 to the vector with every coordinate equal to sqrt(|I_1|). Its operator norm is sqrt(|I_1||I_2|), proving (14). Combining (14) and (15) and dividing by C_epsilon X^(19/20+epsilon) proves (16).

Finally, if L_sel(X)=X^{o(1)}, then for the fixed positive number 1/20-epsilon it is eventually smaller than X^((1/20-epsilon)/2), whereas the right side of (16) is larger than a fixed positive multiple of X^(1/20-epsilon)/log X. This is a contradiction. The row points were selected only by a congruence modulo q and no Archimedean bound was imposed on them, which proves the final scope limitation.

glossary.L_sel: the selector loss in a proposed IJOP operator estimate
glossary.P_X: the set of odd primes in the fixed interval [6X/5,8X/5]
glossary.U_IJOP: the unrestricted class of independently column-pair-dependent finitely supported row weights

85c90a4160baba8d.title: COMMON-ENVELOPE FINITE-BAND VECTOR FOURTH-MOMENT RANGE
85c90a4160baba8d.author: slava chan
85c90a4160baba8d.statement:
COMMON-ENVELOPE FINITE-BAND VECTOR FOURTH-MOMENT RANGE.

Fix Q>=2 and real numbers H,V,P,B satisfying
  2<=H<=Q^(1/3),  2<=V<H,  P=QH/V,  B>=1.                  (1)
Let cal O be a set of pairs j=(v,p), where v is an integer in [V,2V), p is prime in [P,2P), and gcd(v,p)=1. For each j put
  n_j=vp,  Y_j=n_j/H.                                       (2)
Let Phi be a fixed smooth compactly supported complex function whose support avoids zero and has length at most D_0. For every j let cal Q_j be a set of positive integers contained in one integer interval of length at most Q, with gcd(q,n_j)=1 for q in cal Q_j. Fix an integer A satisfying
  gcd(A,n_j)=1                                               (3)
for every j.

For each j assume there is one real interval J_j of length at most C_0Y_j such that every smooth function F_{j,q}, q in cal Q_j, is supported inside J_j and satisfies
  |F_{j,q}(x)|<=B                                            (4)
for all real x. Define
  A_j(theta)=sum_{q in cal Q_j}n_j^(-1)sum_{h in Z}
    Phi(h/H)Fhat_{j,q}(h/n_j)e_{n_j}(hAqbar)e(h theta),      (5)
where e(x)=exp(2 pi i x), e_n(x)=e(x/n), and qbar is the inverse of q modulo n_j. Assume
  p>2(D_0H+1)                                                (6)
for every j. Put
  cal M_4=sum_{j in cal O}integral_{R/Z}|A_j(theta)|^4dtheta. (7)

Then for every epsilon>0,
  cal M_4<<_{Phi,C_0,epsilon}B^4Q^(5+epsilon)/H^3.          (8)
Consequently, if
  V^2Q^(2/3)<=H^5,                                          (9)
then
  cal M_4<<_{Phi,C_0,epsilon}B^4P^2Q^(7/3+epsilon).         (10)
If B is subpolynomial, its fourth power is absorbed by renaming epsilon, and (10) is the finite-band vector target required by fact 44e700816602dd36.

This theorem uses the additional common-envelope condition (4), separately for every outer row j. It does not cover q-dependent translated envelopes such as fact 2f339e96f361bf0c, and it asserts no estimate in the complementary range V^2Q^(2/3)>H^5. No PMD or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
85c90a4160baba8d.proof:
For j=(v,p) and t modulo p define
  b_{j,t}(q)=n_j^(-1)sum_{h in Z}
    Phi(h/H)Fhat_{j,q}(h/n_j)e_{n_j}(hAqbar)e_p(ht).         (11)
The frequency span in (5) is at most D_0H+1. Under (6), fact 84bf915e8a88d8d3 gives the exact sampling identity
  integral_{R/Z}|A_j(theta)|^4dtheta
  =p^(-1)sum_{t modulo p}|sum_qb_{j,t}(q)|^4.               (12)
Its positivity hypothesis on q is satisfied because every cal Q_j consists of positive integers.

For each fixed j, the hypotheses of fact 3450c52083a2e548 hold with the common interval J=J_j, n=n_j, and the same amplitude bound B. Its soft-source identity identifies b_{j,t}(q) with z_t(q), and its pointwise conclusion gives
  sum_{q in cal Q_j}|b_{j,t}(q)|
  <<_{Phi,C_0,epsilon}BQ^(1+epsilon)/H                      (13)
for every t. Therefore
  |sum_qb_{j,t}(q)|^4
  <=[sum_q|b_{j,t}(q)|]^4
  <<B^4Q^(4+epsilon)/H^4,                                   (14)
after renaming epsilon.

Average (14) over t in (12). The factor p^(-1) cancels the number p of twists, so the same upper bound holds for the integral attached to each j. There are at most 2V possible integers v and at most 2P possible primes p, hence
  #cal O<=4VP.                                               (15)
Sum (14) over j and use VP=QH:
  cal M_4
  <<B^4VPQ^(4+epsilon)/H^4
  =B^4Q^(5+epsilon)/H^3.                                    (16)
This proves (8).

Using P=QH/V,
  [Q^5/H^3]/[P^2Q^(7/3)]
  =Q^(2/3)V^2/H^5.                                         (17)
Condition (9) makes the right side at most one, proving (10). Fact 44e700816602dd36 states that the vector estimate at scale P^2Q^(7/3) is sufficient for its pre-Cauchy target. The subpolynomial absorption and all scope statements follow directly.

glossary.J_j: The common physical support interval containing every F_{j,q} in the fixed outer row j.

85e63a9328d91711.title: Let 2≤L<Z be real numbers and let r be a squarefree positive integer satisfying r>L and Z³>r. Put
85e63a9328d91711.author: slava chan
85e63a9328d91711.statement:
Let 2≤L<Z be real numbers and let r be a squarefree positive integer satisfying r>L and Z³>r. Put
I=(L,Z),  j_I(n)=#{p:p is prime, p|n, L<p<Z},
and v=v_L(r), where v_L is defined in fact 9ba4d2d84f0b37d6. Then exactly one of the following three alternatives holds.

(A) j_I(r)>0. In this case the exact interval-prime marker identity is
μ(r)=-Σ_{u p=r, p prime, L<p<Z} μ(u)/(1+j_I(u)).                         (1)

(B) j_I(r)=0 and v_L(r)>L. In this case
μ(r)=Σ_{k≥2}(-1)^k Σ_{u y=r, gcd(u,y)=1}
 μ(u)1_{j_I(u)=0}Γ_k(y)/binom(k+ω_L(u),k),                              (2)
where Γ_k is defined in fact 9ba4d2d84f0b37d6. Every nonzero marked factor in (2) satisfies L<y≤L² and has all prime divisors at most L.

(C) j_I(r)=0 and v≤L. In this case the factorization r=vw is unique, every prime divisor of w is at least Z, and exactly one of the following holds:
(C1) w=p is prime and μ(r)=-μ(v);
(C2) w=pq for distinct primes Z≤p<q and μ(r)=μ(v).                       (3)

Thus every such r is covered exactly by an interval-prime marker, a stopping composite marker, a small-prime product times one Z-rough prime, or a small-prime product times two Z-rough primes. The identities retain the exact sign μ(r); they are not upper- or lower-bound sieve inequalities.
85e63a9328d91711.proof:
The conditions j_I(r)>0 and j_I(r)=0 partition the possibilities. Suppose first that j_I(r)>0. For every prime p|r in I, squarefreeness gives μ(r/p)=-μ(r). There are j_I(r) such primes, and if u=r/p then j_I(r)=1+j_I(u). Therefore the right side of (1) is
-[j_I(r)·(-μ(r))]/j_I(r)=μ(r).
This proves (1).

Now suppose j_I(r)=0. If v_L(r)>L, fact 9ba4d2d84f0b37d6 gives its stopping identity. In every nonzero term of that identity, all prime divisors of y are at most L. Hence y has no prime divisor in I. Since r=uy, the condition j_I(r)=0 is therefore equivalent, term by term, to j_I(u)=0. Inserting its indicator into the coefficient of u leaves the equality unchanged and yields (2). The support assertion L<y≤L² is also part of fact 9ba4d2d84f0b37d6.

It remains to consider j_I(r)=0 and v=v_L(r)≤L. Define w=r/v. Because r is squarefree, v is exactly the product of all prime divisors of r at most L, so gcd(v,w)=1 and this factorization is unique. A prime divisor of w is greater than L. It cannot lie in I because j_I(r)=0; hence it is at least Z. Also w≠1, since otherwise r=v≤L, contrary to r>L.

If w had at least three prime divisors, squarefreeness and the preceding lower bound would give w≥Z³. Then r=vw≥w≥Z³, contrary to Z³>r. Thus w has one or two distinct prime divisors. In the first case w=p is prime and multiplicativity gives μ(r)=μ(v)μ(p)=-μ(v). In the second case w=pq for distinct primes; order them as p<q. Then μ(w)=1 and μ(r)=μ(v), proving (3). These cases are mutually exclusive and exhaust the remaining alternative, completing the proof.

glossary.I: The open interval (L,Z) from which an interval-prime marker is selected.
glossary.j_I(n): The number of prime divisors of n lying strictly between L and Z.
glossary.p: A prime factor selected either from I or from the Z-rough factor.
glossary.q: The larger prime in the two-prime Z-rough factor.
glossary.v: The product v_L(r) of all prime divisors of r at most L.

868d2c2698f73b86.title: COUNTABLE MAYNARD NEAR-SQUARE-ROOT TYPE-II ESTIMATE FOR AN ALREADY-FOLDED PRIME/COFACTOR ROW WITH COMPATIBLE VARYING RESIDUES AND PRIME-UNIT DELETION. Fix A>0 and epsilon>0. Let X be sufficiently large, let delta>=0, and let Q_1,Q_2,P,M>=2 satisfy
868d2c2698f73b86.author: slava chan
868d2c2698f73b86.statement:
COUNTABLE MAYNARD NEAR-SQUARE-ROOT TYPE-II ESTIMATE FOR AN ALREADY-FOLDED PRIME/COFACTOR ROW WITH COMPATIBLE VARYING RESIDUES AND PRIME-UNIT DELETION. Fix A>0 and epsilon>0. Let X be sufficiently large, let delta>=0, and let Q_1,Q_2,P,M>=2 satisfy
Q_1Q_2=X^(1/2+delta),qquad PMasymp X,                          (1)
Q_1^7 Q_2^12<X^(4-10epsilon),                                   (2)
Q_1 X^(2delta+epsilon)<P<X^(1-epsilon)/Q_1.                     (3)
Put Q_0=Q_1Q_2. Let c be a positive integer. Let cal S be a set of ordered pairs (q_1,q_2), with
Q_1<q_1<=2Q_1,qquad Q_2<q_2<=2Q_2,                             (4)
such that the product map is injective to squarefree s=q_1q_2 and (s,c)=1. For each q_1 occurring in cal S choose a unit residue b_{q_1} modulo q_1. For every (q_1,q_2) in cal S choose a unit residue a_s modulo s satisfying
a_s congruent b_{q_1} modulo q_1.                               (5)

For each s let W_s(p,v) be supported on primes P<p<=2P and integers M<v<=2M. Assume a finite or countable projective expansion
W_s(p,v)=sum_{j in cal J}lambda_{j,s}A_j(p)B_j(v),               (6)
which is absolutely convergent and satisfies
sum_{j in cal J}sup_s|lambda_{j,s}|<=L_proj,
|A_j(n)|<=tau(n),qquad |B_j(n)|<=tau(n).                        (7)
Assume every A_j is supported on primes P<n<=2P and, as a sequence on the positive integers, satisfies Maynard's Siegel-Walfisz condition uniformly in j and all displayed parameters. Assume also
|W_s(p,v)|<=L_W tau(v).                                         (8)
Define
U_s=sum_{p,(p,c)=1}sum_v W_s(p,v)
 [1_{pv congruent a_s (mod s)}
  -phi(s)^(-1)1_{(pv,s)=1}].                                    (9)
Then
sum_{(q_1,q_2) in cal S}|U_{q_1q_2}|
 <<_{A,epsilon}L_proj X(log X)^(-A)
 +L_W omega_P(c)
  [M(1+log(2MQ_0))^3
   +Q_0 sqrt(M)(1+log(2MQ_0))^2],                               (10)
where
omega_P(c)=#{p prime:P<p<=2P, p|c}.                             (11)
The theorem consumes an already-folded row and inserts no Ramaré coefficient. It permits a residue varying with both q_1,q_2, provided its reduction modulo q_1 is the fixed b_{q_1}. No estimate is asserted without (2)-(3), without delta>=0, without the compatibility (5), or for a nonprojective row.
868d2c2698f73b86.proof:
First allow all selected primes and put
U'_s=sum_p sum_v W_s(p,v)
 [1_{pv congruent a_s (mod s)}
  -phi(s)^(-1)1_{(pv,s)=1}].                                    (12)
For a fixed projective mode j, take alpha_p=A_j(p) and beta_v=B_j(v). Proposition 5.3, the Type II estimate near X^(1/2), of James Maynard, Primes in arithmetic progressions to large moduli III: Uniform residue classes, arXiv:2006.08250, states the following. If Q_1Q_2=X^(1/2+delta), PM is comparable to X,
Q_1^7Q_2^12<X^(4-10epsilon),
and
Q_1X^(2delta+epsilon)<P<X^(1-epsilon)/Q_1,
then for divisor-bounded alpha,beta with alpha satisfying the Siegel-Walfisz condition,
sum_{Q_1<q_1<=2Q_1} sup_{(b,q_1)=1}
 sum_{Q_2<q_2<=2Q_2}
 sup_{(a,q_1q_2)=1, a congruent b (mod q_1)}
 |sum_{P<p<=2P}sum_{M<v<=2M}
 alpha_p beta_v
 [1_{pv congruent a (mod q_1q_2)}
  -phi(q_1q_2)^(-1)1_{(pv,q_1q_2)=1}]|
 <<_{A,epsilon}X(log X)^(-A).                                   (13)
Hypothesis (7) and the explicit prime support and Siegel-Walfisz assumption on A_j give its coefficient hypotheses. Conditions (1)-(3), with delta>=0, are its nondegenerate asymptotic scale hypotheses, and in particular (3) forces P>X^epsilon while its upper bound and PM comparable to X force M to grow at least as a fixed positive power of X. For every fixed q_1, choose b=b_{q_1}; then (5) places every a_s inside the corresponding inner supremum. The interval conventions in (4),(6) are exactly those in (13). Restricting the nonnegative outer sums to cal S can only decrease them.

Absolute convergence in (6), Tonelli's theorem, the triangle inequality, and (7) therefore give
sum_{(q_1,q_2) in cal S}|U'_{q_1q_2}|
 <<_{A,epsilon}L_proj X(log X)^(-A).                             (14)

It remains to compare U_s and U'_s. Their difference contains only primes p in (P,2P] dividing c. Since (s,c)=1, every such p is a unit modulo s. Fix one exceptional p. By (8), the physical part is bounded by L_W times
sum_s sum_{M<v<=2M, v congruent p^(-1)a_s (mod s)}tau(v).       (15)
For every positive integer v,
tau(v)<=2 sum_{e|v, e<=sqrt(v)}1.                              (16)
If e|v in the physical progression, then (e,s)=1 because v is a unit modulo s. Writing v=ef leaves one residue class for f modulo s. Thus, for fixed s,
sum_{M<v<=2M, v congruent p^(-1)a_s (mod s)}tau(v)
 <<M(1+log(2M))/s+sqrt(M).                                      (17)
Injectivity gives at most a constant times Q_0 moduli in (Q_0,4Q_0], and their reciprocal sum is bounded by an absolute constant. Therefore the physical aggregate for the fixed p is
<<L_W[M(1+log(2M))+Q_0sqrt(M)].                                 (18)

For the principal part,
sum_{M<v<=2M}tau(v)<<M(1+log(2M)).                              (19)
Every s is squarefree, so
s/phi(s)<=(1+log s)^2,
and injectivity gives
sum_s1/phi(s)<<(1+log(4Q_0))^2.                                 (20)
Equations (19)-(20) bound the principal aggregate for the fixed exceptional p by
<<L_W M(1+log(2M))(1+log(4Q_0))^2.                              (21)
The right sides of (18) and (21) are bounded by the bracket in (10). Summing over the omega_P(c) exceptional primes and combining with (14) proves (10).

glossary.L_proj: The l1 outer norm of the countable prime/cofactor projective expansion.
glossary.U'_s: The auxiliary folded row containing every selected prime before prime-unit deletion.
glossary.U_s: The folded row after deleting selected primes dividing c.
glossary.b_{q_1}: The residue modulo the first modulus factor to which every full residue above q_1 must reduce.

875cb4f04516b35e.title: GA-TERMINAL-SQPROFILE: EXACT SUPPORTED A/C FORM OF THE SQUARED-MARKER DILATOR PROFILE AND MULTIPLICATIVE INTEGRAL WEIGHT. Fix the finite supported set mathcal N of squarefree integers from fact c384d36af25e96a6, with B/2<=n<=2B, and adopt its terminal marker with cutoff Z>2. For a squarefree integer d define
875cb4f04516b35e.author: slava chan
875cb4f04516b35e.proof:
Fix d. In the A alternative, fact f234dbd4fdda994e indexes the terminal children over each supported n in mathcal N by the primes p dividing n with 2<p<Z. The marked dilator and cofactor are d_lambda=n/p and v_lambda=p. Thus an A edge in the supported edge universe with d_lambda=d is uniquely n=dp, where p is in the displayed prime interval, p does not divide d, and dp belongs to mathcal N. Since n is squarefree, d is squarefree. Conversely, when dp belongs to mathcal N and the displayed arithmetic conditions hold, p is an interval-prime divisor of that supported n and therefore gives exactly its A edge.

For n=dp, the interval-prime divisors of n are the interval-prime divisors of d together with p, because p does not divide d. Hence r(n)=r_Z(d)+1. Fact f234dbd4fdda994e gives a_lambda(n)=mu(n)/r(n), so its squared modulus is 1/(r_Z(d)+1)^2. The definition of S_{chi,D} in fact 256c10f372b85755 multiplies this by chi(v_lambda)f(n)=chi(p)f(dp). Summing the supported A edges proves (2).

In the C alternative, fact f234dbd4fdda994e gives the unique factorization n=dv with v in {1,2}, d equal to a product of j>=1 ordered prime factors at least Z, and (d,v)=1. Therefore d>1, d is squarefree, and P^-(d)>=Z. Conversely, if dv belongs to mathcal N and these displayed conditions hold, then n=dv has no interval-prime divisor and its rough factorization has at least one rough prime, so it is the unique supported C_j edge. Its terminal coefficient is mu(n), so its squared modulus is one, and chi(v_lambda)f(n)=chi(v)f(dv). This proves (3). The A and C alternatives are disjoint and exhaustive on the supported edge universe, proving their sum is S_{chi,D}f.

Finally,
[
 int_0^1t^r(-log t),dt
 =- rac{d}{dr}int_0^1t^r,dt
 =- rac{d}{dr} rac1{r+1}
 = rac1{(r+1)^2}.
]
Substitute this into (2). The supported prime sum is finite, so it may be interchanged with the integral, proving (5). Fact bab94ab4a0e20bc0 identifies its enlarged centered profile with S_{chi,D}F_{m,c} on the inherited terminal support, yielding the scoped specialization.

glossary.A^A_{chi,D}(d): The A-anatomy part of the squared-marker character-incidence profile at dilator d.
glossary.A^C_{chi,D}(d): The C-anatomy part of the squared-marker character-incidence profile at dilator d.
glossary.r_Z(d): The number of prime divisors p of d satisfying 2<p<Z.

876e206eb9190ca9.title: HALF-CONV LITERAL SOURCE LIFT, EXACT UNIT SPLIT, DYADIC RANGE LEDGER, AND LARGE-LARGE RESIDUAL. Fix one orientation and one exact active pair g,c in the complete selected critical source of facts 328503a935cabe60 and 8d9feea8c44da2c8. Thus c,q,n are pairwise coprime, q,kappa,t,n are positive integers on finite fixed supports, q t+kappa n=ell, and the fixed-g,c physical source is
876e206eb9190ca9.author: slava chan
876e206eb9190ca9.statement:
HALF-CONV LITERAL SOURCE LIFT, EXACT UNIT SPLIT, DYADIC RANGE LEDGER, AND LARGE-LARGE RESIDUAL. Fix one orientation and one exact active pair g,c in the complete selected critical source of facts 328503a935cabe60 and 8d9feea8c44da2c8. Thus c,q,n are pairwise coprime, q,kappa,t,n are positive integers on finite fixed supports, q t+kappa n=ell, and the fixed-g,c physical source is
P_{g,c}^{phys}=mu(c) sum_{q,kappa,n,t: qt+kappa n=ell} mu(q)mu(n) A_{q,kappa,n}(t).
Here A_{q,kappa,n}(t) retains every literal source, dyadic, fixed-U, high, parent, target-gcd, factorization, provenance and projective weight or mask that survives the complete sibling recombination, and excludes only mu(c)mu(q)mu(n). In particular its orientation-specific smooth core is
W(gcq/D,t/M,gn/R,c kappa/K) log(t)log(c kappa)
in the forward orientation and
W(gn/D,c kappa/M,gcq/R,t/K) log(t)log(c kappa)
in the reverse orientation, together with all the other physical factors specified in the cited facts.

Let rho_{1/2} be the arithmetic function of fact 5999a1878276ac78. Then exactly
P_{g,c}^{phys}=mu(c) sum_{q,kappa,d,m} mu(q)rho_{1/2}(d)rho_{1/2}(m)
 1_{q divides ell-kappa dm} 1_{(dm,qc)=1}
 A_{q,kappa,dm}((ell-kappa dm)/q),
with the same finite physical supports and every original mask evaluated at n=dm and t=(ell-kappa dm)/q. There is no condition (d,m)=1 and no squarefree condition on d or m. The literal unit condition splits exactly as
1_{(dm,qc)=1}=1_{(d,qc)=1}1_{(m,qc)=1},
while (c,q)=1 and every condition involving only q,kappa,g,c remains an outer condition. Any mask or physical weight depending on n remains a joint function of the product dm unless a separate projective decomposition is proved.

For j>=0 put I_j^{dy}={d positive integer:2^j<=d<2^(j+1)}. Since n=dm lies on the B-scale, only finitely many j occur, and insertion of sum_j 1_{d in I_j^{dy}}=1 gives an exact dyadic partition of the lifted source. For any real numbers 1<Y<Z, refining these cells by d<Y, Y<=d<=Z, and d>Z gives the exact three-part ledger
P_{g,c}^{phys}=P_{g,c}^{<Y}+P_{g,c}^{med}+P_{g,c}^{>Z}.
The full lifted summand is invariant under d and m being interchanged. Hence it also has the exact fundamental-domain form
P_{g,c}^{phys}=2 sum_{d<m}(lifted summand)+sum_{d=m}(lifted summand).
After this fundamental-domain restriction, the part with min(d,m)>Z is exactly a both-large residual d>Z and m>Z. It cannot be moved into the medium range by d-m symmetry. In particular, exact separability or an analytic payment of the range Y<=d<=Z alone does not pay the ranges min(d,m)<Y or d,m>Z.

The coefficient bounds |rho_{1/2}(d)|,|rho_{1/2}(m)|,|mu(q)|<=1 supply divisor-boundedness. They do not by themselves supply a Siegel-Walfisz hypothesis, a projective decomposition of the joint physical amplitude, a low-conductor summation, or an analytic estimate for any of the three ranges. A Type-I/II or Maynard import is licensed only after checking all of the following for its exact theorem statement: the sequence placed in its Siegel-Walfisz slot really has that property; its other sequence may contain rho_{1/2}; the theorem is uniform in the moving reduced residue ell kappa^{-1} modulo q; the outer mu(q) is harmless under the theorem's modulus-by-modulus absolute value or supremum; the factors 1_{(d,qc)=1} and 1_{(m,qc)=1} fit its coefficient and unit conventions; and the complete q,kappa-dependent physical weight has an exact separated/projective representation with the required norm. No such analytic payment is asserted here.
876e206eb9190ca9.proof:
Fact 328503a935cabe60 gives the complete physical critical progression after every auxiliary deletion sibling has been recombined. Fact 8d9feea8c44da2c8 gives the exact equation qt+kappa n=ell, pairwise coprimality of c,q,n, the coefficient mu(c)mu(q)mu(n), both displayed orientation weights, and literal transport of every surviving mask. This gives the defining formula for P_{g,c}^{phys} in the statement.

By fact 5999a1878276ac78, for every positive integer n one has the unrestricted Dirichlet-convolution identity
mu(n)=sum_{dm=n}rho_{1/2}(d)rho_{1/2}(m).
Insert this finite identity into the n-sum. Reordering finite sums replaces n by dm everywhere and replaces the source equation by qt+kappa dm=ell. Solving it for t gives t=(ell-kappa dm)/q and contributes the exact divisibility condition q divides ell-kappa dm. Every physical factor and mask formerly evaluated at n,t is therefore evaluated at dm,(ell-kappa dm)/q; none is removed or averaged. This proves the lifted identity.

For arbitrary positive d,m,q,c, a prime divides dm and qc simultaneously if and only if it divides at least one of d,m and also qc. Thus gcd(dm,qc)=1 if and only if both gcd(d,qc)=1 and gcd(m,qc)=1, proving the unit split. The convolution identity in fact 5999a1878276ac78 explicitly has no gcd(d,m)=1 restriction and is valid on all prime powers, so adding coprimality or squarefreeness of d,m would change the identity.

The B-scale support bounds n=dm above by a fixed multiple of B. Hence d<=n is bounded, so only finitely many half-open cells I_j^{dy} occur. Every positive integer d belongs to exactly one such cell, proving the dyadic partition. The three inequalities d<Y, Y<=d<=Z, d>Z form a disjoint exhaustive partition, proving the three-part ledger even when Y or Z is integral; the closed endpoints have been assigned explicitly to the middle range.

For fixed q,kappa and product dm, every displayed factor in the lifted summand depends on d,m either through the symmetric product dm, through the symmetric product unit indicator, or through rho_{1/2}(d)rho_{1/2}(m). Therefore interchanging d,m leaves the summand unchanged. Pairing each ordered pair d<m with m>d proves the fundamental-domain identity, with the diagonal d=m retained once. On d<=m, the condition min(d,m)>Z is exactly d>Z, which forces both d>Z and m>Z. Symmetry preserves this region rather than moving it into Y<=d<=Z. Thus a medium-range estimate leaves the stated small-minimum and both-large regions.

Finally, the three pointwise coefficient bounds follow from fact 5999a1878276ac78 and the elementary inequality |mu(q)|<=1. A pointwise bound does not imply distribution in arithmetic progressions, does not factor a joint function of dm and q, and does not estimate a sum over kappa. The final checklist therefore records necessary theorem hypotheses rather than conclusions. The exact identity proves none of those analytic inputs, so no range payment follows from it alone.

glossary.A_{q,kappa,n}(t): The complete literal physical amplitude of one fixed critical source atom, with all inherited smooth weights and outer masks retained, excluding the three Möbius factors mu(c)mu(q)mu(n).
glossary.I_j^{dy}: The half-open dyadic cell of positive integers d with 2^j<=d<2^(j+1).
glossary.P_{g,c}^{phys}: The complete fixed-g,c physical critical source before subtraction of its same-mask Poisson zero mode.

87fee9c7e02513f9.title: EXACT PRE-CAUCHY LAGRANGE DEFECT AND THE MINIMAL EARLIER SIGNED PMD ASSEMBLY
87fee9c7e02513f9.author: slava chan
87fee9c7e02513f9.statement:
EXACT PRE-CAUCHY LAGRANGE DEFECT AND THE MINIMAL EARLIER SIGNED PMD ASSEMBLY.

Let cal I be a finite set. For every i in cal I let b_i and z_i be complex numbers. Put
  C_src=sum_{i in cal I}|b_i|^2,
  M_src=sum_{i in cal I}|z_i|^2,
  T_src=sum_{i in cal I}b_i z_i,                            (1)
and define the pre-Cauchy defect
  D_pre
   =(1/2)sum_{i,j in cal I}
       |conjugate(b_i)z_j-conjugate(b_j)z_i|^2.             (2)
Then exactly
  C_src M_src-|T_src|^2=D_pre>=0.                           (3)

Specialize to the complete literal finite-band row of fact 294ac3b02b065aec. Thus let
  i=(ell,v,p,h),qquad
  b_i=eta_ell xi_v,qquad
  z_i=sum_q x_{ell,v,p,h}(q),                              (4)
where
  x_{ell,v,p,h}(q)
   =c_q nu_h U_ell(q,h,v,p)chi_ell(v,p,h,q)
      e(Ah/(qvp))e_{vp}(-Ahqbar),                           (5)
and every range, coprimality condition, zero-one source mask, and zero extension is exactly the one in that fact. Then
  T_src=H S_lit,qquad M_src=M_2^lit,                       (6)
and hence
  C_src M_2^lit-H^2|S_lit|^2=D_pre.                         (7)

Consequently, for every epsilon>0, the desired earlier signed estimate
  |S_lit|^2<=P Q^(8/3+epsilon)                              (8)
is equivalent to the exact defect lower bound
  D_pre>=C_src M_2^lit-H^2P Q^(8/3+epsilon).                (9)
Thus, within the accepted literal finite-band row, the minimal earlier alternative to bounding M_2^lit is either the direct pre-Cauchy estimate (8) or the algebraically equivalent bound (9). Formula (2) retains every ordered cross-height, cross-v, cross-p, and cross-projective-label comparison which is absent after replacing the signed assembly by the scalar moment M_2^lit. It also retains every q-coefficient and source mask inside z_i.

The accepted coefficient provenance currently stops at a sharp interface. Fact 38bc0e88e17aef0e identifies the exact upstream reciprocal-modulus factor mu(q), while fact a1b0c0ad5a923524 proves that the common height factor nu_h cannot itself create fixed-height source cancellation. Fact 0a7dc0c20f026253 gives the exact same-window/cross-window completion retaining U_ell chi_ell. Fact 05cbed389411618a states that the accepted literal hypotheses do not by themselves supply the stronger h-independent physical Fourier identity for c_q nu_h U_ell chi_ell displayed there. Therefore the currently verified interfaces leave two nonexclusive new theorem slots: a source-specific estimate for the U_ell chi_ell-weighted completed modular windows, or the earlier signed estimate (8), equivalently (9).

This is an exact identity and a theorem-interface statement. It does not assert (8) or (9), does not say that the actual U_ell chi_ell coefficient saturates a local window, and proves no PMD closure or Goldbach conclusion.
87fee9c7e02513f9.proof:
Expand (2). For fixed i,j,
  |conjugate(b_i)z_j-conjugate(b_j)z_i|^2
   =|b_i|^2|z_j|^2+|b_j|^2|z_i|^2
    -2 Re(conjugate(b_i)b_j z_j conjugate(z_i)).            (10)
After summing over i,j and dividing by two, the first two terms together give
  (sum_i|b_i|^2)(sum_j|z_j|^2)=C_src M_src.                 (11)
The complete cross term is
  Re sum_{i,j}conjugate(b_i)b_j z_j conjugate(z_i)
   =|sum_j b_jz_j|^2
   =|T_src|^2.                                              (12)
Equations (10)-(12) prove (3). Nonnegativity also follows directly from the sum of squares in (2).

For the literal specialization, fact 294ac3b02b065aec defines
  S_lit=H^(-1)sum_{ell,v,p}eta_ell xi_v
              sum_h sum_q x_{ell,v,p,h}(q).                (13)
With the index and definitions in (4), the right side after multiplication by H is exactly sum_i b_i z_i=T_src. This proves the first identity in (6). The exact Parseval expansion in that fact gives
  M_2^lit=sum_{ell,v,p}sum_h
             |sum_qx_{ell,v,p,h}(q)|^2
          =sum_i|z_i|^2=M_src,                              (14)
which proves the second identity. Substitute (6) into (3) to obtain (7).

Subtract C_src M_2^lit from both sides of (7). The inequality
  H^2|S_lit|^2<=H^2P Q^(8/3+epsilon)
is then equivalent, with no loss in either direction, to (9). Since H is positive, division by H^2 gives (8). This proves the equivalence.

Every literal factor in (5) remains inside the unreplaced number z_i. The ordered pairs in (2) range independently over the complete indices i=(ell,v,p,h) and j=(ell',v',p',h'), so they include cross-height, cross-v, cross-p, and cross-label comparisons. By contrast, (14) is the sum of the separate same-i squared q-rows. Hence (2) records exactly the information lost by the Cauchy passage from (13) to the scalar moment, proving the retention claim.

The final provenance paragraph only invokes assertions already verifier-gated in the cited predecessors. Fact 38bc0e88e17aef0e gives the exact mu(q) source factor and its limited scope. Fact a1b0c0ad5a923524 gives the exact common-height weighted-average identity and its limitation. Fact 0a7dc0c20f026253 gives the completed literal U_ell chi_ell window formulas without an estimate. Fact 05cbed389411618a explicitly states that its physical Fourier coefficient identity is not implied by the accepted literal interface. Accordingly, the two listed theorem slots are alternatives, not claimed estimates or impossibility results. This proves all scope qualifications.

glossary.C_src: The squared l2 mass of the outer/projective coefficients repeated over the complete literal height index.
glossary.D_pre: The exact nonnegative complex Lagrange defect between the signed pre-Cauchy assembly and the product C_src M_src.
glossary.M_src: The unweighted squared l2 mass of the inner row values z_i.
glossary.T_src: The complete signed pre-Cauchy linear assembly sum_i b_i z_i.

884d8d453b95d5ad.title: MINIMAL UPPER-FACE CROSSING BLOCK INSIDE A LEGALLY SEPARATED HB CELL. Fix \(0<\tau<1/100\) and \(\beta>1\), and put
884d8d453b95d5ad.author: slava chan
884d8d453b95d5ad.statement:
MINIMAL UPPER-FACE CROSSING BLOCK INSIDE A LEGALLY SEPARATED HB CELL. Fix \(0<\tau<1/100\) and \(\beta>1\), and put
\[
 a=2\beta-2+\tau,\qquad b=3-2\beta-\tau,\qquad
 c_0=\min\{a/2,(b-a)/2\},\qquad z=Q^{c_0}/16.
\]
Assume \(0<a<b<\beta\), so \(a+b=1\). Fix a positive integer \(K\) with \(Kc_0>\beta\), and let \(Q\) be sufficiently large in terms of the fixed parameters. Let \(2\le j\le K\), and let positive integers
\[
 d_1,\ldots,d_j,\quad u_1,\ldots,u_{j-1},\quad t,\quad m,\quad n
\]
satisfy
\[
 m=d_1\cdots d_j u_1\cdots u_{j-1},\qquad n=mt,
\]
\[
 m>Q^b,\qquad 1<t<Q^a,\qquad
 {1\over2}Q^\beta\le n\le2Q^\beta,\qquad 1\le d_i\le z.
\]
Assume that no submultiset product of
\[
 \{d_1,\ldots,d_j,u_1,\ldots,u_{j-1},t\}
\]
lies in \([Q^a,Q^b]\), and that
\[
 n/u_r\ge Q^a\qquad(1\le r\le j-1).                           \tag{1}
\]
Let \(P<Q^a\) be the final greedy carrier of fact \(aaf7242ef22ecd10\), and let \(\mathcal O\) be its omitted multiset. Thus \(\mathcal O\) has at least two elements, consists only of factors from
\[
 \{u_1,\ldots,u_{j-1},t\},
\]
and satisfies
\[
 y>Q^{b-a}\qquad(y\in\mathcal O).                             \tag{2}
\]
Then
\[
 \prod_{y\in\mathcal O}y>Q^b.                                \tag{3}
\]
Consequently there is an inclusion-minimal nonempty submultiset \(\mathcal Y\subseteq\mathcal O\) whose product
\[
 Y=\prod_{y\in\mathcal Y}y
\]
exceeds \(Q^b\). Every proper submultiset \(\mathcal Y'\subsetneq\mathcal Y\) satisfies
\[
 \prod_{y\in\mathcal Y'}y<Q^a.                               \tag{4}
\]
Hence exactly one of the following occurs.

(i) \(\mathcal Y\) is a singleton, whose unique factor exceeds \(Q^b\).

(ii) \(r=|\mathcal Y|\ge2\), every factor and every proper subproduct of \(\mathcal Y\) is smaller than \(Q^a\), and
\[
 2\le r\le \left\lceil {a\over b-a}\right\rceil.              \tag{5}
\]

Fix an order of all submultisets of the omitted-coordinate set and select the first \(\mathcal Y\) satisfying the preceding minimality conditions. Its selector, together with any fixed greedy-cell selector from fact \(aaf7242ef22ecd10\), has a separated sharp-Perron expansion of total coefficient mass
\[
 (\log Q)^{O_K(1)}
\]
plus an arbitrarily power-small paid remainder. Every new Perron factor depends only on \(d_i,u_r,t\), so it introduces no \(q\)- or \(h\)-dependence. Thus an outer cross-\(q\) coefficient \(\mu(q)\) and the original joint \((h,t)\) coordinate are retained. This theorem gives finite-arity geometry and separation only; it gives no reciprocal-energy estimate, ULTRA-MU-VECTOR, ENDPOINT-DIAGONAL-\(N\), post-\(A\) payment, or Goldbach conclusion.
884d8d453b95d5ad.proof:
