Because \(P\) contains every selected factor and \(\mathcal O\) is the omitted multiset,
\[
 n=P\prod_{y\in\mathcal O}y.
\]
The lower bound for \(n\) and \(P<Q^a\) imply
\[
 \prod_{y\in\mathcal O}y>{1\over2}Q^{\beta-a}.
\]
Since \(a+b=1\), one has \(\beta-a-b=\beta-1>0\). The sufficiently-large-\(Q\) hypothesis therefore makes the last quantity exceed \(Q^b\), proving (3).

Choose an inclusion-minimal nonempty \(\mathcal Y\) with product above \(Q^b\). Every proper subproduct is at most \(Q^b\), and the no-subset condition then forces it below \(Q^a\), proving (4). A singleton gives (i). If \(r\ge2\), every singleton is proper and hence below \(Q^a\). Removing any one factor leaves a proper subproduct below \(Q^a\), whereas (2) makes that product exceed \(Q^{(r-1)(b-a)}\). Thus \((r-1)(b-a)<a\), which gives (5).

For completeness we prove the new first-minimal selector separation rather than importing it from the earlier test list. Gorodetsky, arXiv:2111.12662, Lemma 3.1 states that, if \(F(s)=\sum_{v\ge1}a_vv^{-s}\) has finite abscissa of absolute convergence \(\sigma_a\), \(\kappa>\max\{0,\sigma_a\}\), \(T\ge1\), and \(x\ge1\), then
\[
 \sum_{v\le x}a_v
 ={1\over2\pi i}\int_{\kappa-iT}^{\kappa+iT}F(s)x^s{ds\over s}
 +O\left(x^\kappa\sum_{v\ge1}
 { |a_v|\over v^\kappa(1+T|\log(x/v)|)}\right).
\]

For each coordinate submultiset \(S\), write \(v_S\) for its product and put
\[
 X^\sharp=\lfloor Q^b\rfloor+1/2.
\]
Every \(v_S\) is a positive integer not exceeding \(n\le2Q^\beta\), so
\[
 |v_S-X^\sharp|\ge1/2,\qquad
 |\log(X^\sharp/v_S)|\gg Q^{-\beta-2}.
\]
Apply the quoted lemma to \(F(s)=v_S^{-s}\) with
\[
 \kappa=1/\log Q,\qquad T=Q^{A_1+\beta+3}.
\]
This gives
\[
 {\bf1}_{v_S\le Q^b}
 ={1\over2\pi i}\int_{\kappa-iT}^{\kappa+iT}
 {(X^\sharp)^s\over s}\prod_{\xi\in S}\xi^{-s}\,ds
 +O_{A_1}(Q^{-A_1}).
\]
The integral is separated. Its normalized coordinate arrays have modulus at most one, and its coefficient mass is
\[
 O\left(\int_{-T}^T{d\upsilon\over|\kappa+i\upsilon|}\right)
 =O(\log Q).
\]
The complementary threshold has one additional constant atom.

For a candidate block \(S\), define
\[
 B_S={\bf1}_{v_S>Q^b}
 \prod_{S'\subsetneq S}{\bf1}_{v_{S'}\le Q^b}.
\]
This says exactly that \(S\) crosses the upper face and every proper submultiset does not. If the candidates are ordered, its first-candidate selector is
\[
 B_S\prod_{R<S}(1-B_R).
\]
These are finite sums and products of the separated threshold atoms. The number of candidates depends only on \(K\). Multiplication with the fixed greedy-cell selector from fact \(aaf7242ef22ecd10\) therefore has mass \((\log Q)^{O_K(1)}\). A finite telescoping-product estimate gives a pointwise remainder \(O_{A_1,K}(Q^{-A_1})(\log Q)^{O_K(1)}\), which is arbitrarily power-small after increasing \(A_1\).

The new atoms contain only powers of \(d_i,u_r,t\). They contain no \(q\) or \(h\), so the cross-\(q\) coefficient and the \(h\)-array remain unchanged; a power of \(t\) only twists its existing one-variable array.

glossary.B_S: The conjunction that S crosses Q^b and every proper submultiset stays at most Q^b.
glossary.Y: The product of the factors in the minimal crossing block.
glossary.mathcal O: The multiset of unweighted factors omitted by the greedy carrier.
glossary.mathcal Y: An inclusion-minimal omitted submultiset whose product exceeds Q^b.
glossary.r: The cardinality of the minimal crossing block.
glossary.upsilon: The real integration coordinate on the effective Perron contour.

88d5e14f4865c93b.title: Fix real numbers
88d5e14f4865c93b.author: slava chan
88d5e14f4865c93b.statement:
Fix real numbers
\[
 \frac12<\alpha<\beta<1,\qquad B_{\rm src}>0.
\]
Let \(W,\Phi\) be continuously differentiable complex functions with
bounded first derivatives, supported respectively in
\([\alpha,\beta]\) and \([1/2,2]\). Let \(N=2x\) be an integer with
\(x\ge3\), and assume
\[
 \frac12x^{1/2}(\log x)^{-B_{\rm src}}\le D\le2x^{1/2},
 \qquad U>0.
\]
Define
\[
 {\cal I}_D=\{w\ge2:(w,N)=1,\ \mu(w)\ne0,\ w\le x^{1/2},\
                         \Phi(w/D)\ne0\}.
\]
Fix a nonzero integer \(h\) with \(|h|\le2D\), and fix positive
integers \(q_1,q_2\) such that
\[
 \mu(q_1)\mu(q_2)\ne0,\qquad
 d=(q_1,q_2)\mid h,\qquad
 c=[q_1,q_2]>1,\qquad (N,c)=1.
\]
Put \(b=q_2/d\). The active moduli are squarefree, so \((q_1,b)=1\);
\(q_1^{-1}\) below denotes its inverse modulo \(b\), and every twist
modulo \(b=1\) is defined to be one.

For positive integers \(m,w,w-h\), put
\[
 P_1=N-mw,\qquad P_2=N-m(w-h),
\]
and define
\[
\begin{split}
 A^+(m,w)=&
 {\bf1}_{w,w-h\in{\cal I}_D}\mu(w)\mu(w-h)\mu(q_1)\mu(q_2)\\
 &\times\Phi(w/D)\Phi((w-h)/D)
 W(mw/x)W(m(w-h)/x)\Phi(P_1/U)\Phi(P_2/U)\\
 &\times\log(P_1/q_1)_+\log(P_2/q_2)_+,
\end{split}                                                   \tag{1}
\]
with value zero unless \(P_1,P_2>0\). Periodize modulo \(c\) and define
\[
 \widehat A^+(k,r)=
 \sum_{a_1,a_2\ ({\rm mod}\ c)}
 \sum_{\substack{m\equiv a_1\ ({\rm mod}\ c)\\
                 w\equiv a_2\ ({\rm mod}\ c)}}
 A^+(m,w)e_c(ka_1+ra_2).                              \tag{2}
\]
Put \(M_0=x/D\), and define
\[
 {\cal P}(A^+)=
 \inf_{\widehat A^+(k,r)=\int_{\cal Z}\alpha_z(r)\beta_z(k)\,d\nu(z)}
 \int_{\cal Z}\|\alpha_z\|_{\ell^2(\mathbb Z/c\mathbb Z)}
                  \|\beta_z\|_{\ell^2(\mathbb Z/c\mathbb Z)}
 \,d|\nu|(z).                                           \tag{3}
\]
The infimum is over exact integral decompositions. Then
\[
 \boxed{
 {\cal P}(A^+)
 \ll_{W,\Phi,\alpha,\beta}
 (\log x)^2
 \{M_0D(c+M_0)(c+D)\}^{1/2}.
 }                                                       \tag{MOVING-BV-PROJ}
\]
Thus the literal masks \(\log(P_i/q_i)_+\) admit an exact separated
representation with only a fixed logarithmic cost; no smoothing error
and no deletion of the moving cuts \(q_i<P_i\) occurs.

Define the fixed-tuple nonzero contribution
\[
 {\cal T}_{h,q_1,q_2}
 =\frac1{c^2}
 \sum_{\substack{k,r\ ({\rm mod}\ c)\\k\ne0,\ r\ne0}}
 \widehat A^+(k,r)e_b(-rhq_1^{-1})S(r,kN;c).             \tag{4}
\]
For all complex vectors \(a(r),b_0(k)\),
\[
 \left|\sum_{k,r\ ({\rm mod}\ c)}
       a(r)b_0(k)S(r,kN;c)\right|
 \le c\|a\|_2\|b_0\|_2.                                 \tag{5}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \boxed{
 |{\cal T}_{h,q_1,q_2}|
 \le\frac{{\cal P}(A^+)}c
 \ll(\log x)^2(M_0D)^{1/2}
 \left(1+\frac{M_0}{c}\right)^{1/2}
 \left(1+\frac D c\right)^{1/2}.
 }                                                       \tag{6}
\]
The restrictions \(k,r\ne0\) only decrease the coordinate norms.

Equations (3)--(6) are pointwise in one active tuple. Absolute summation
of (6) over active \((h,q_1,q_2)\) would retain the domain restriction
\((q_1,q_2)\mid h\), but would discard the Möbius signs and translation
phases. No bound for that outer sum is asserted.
88d5e14f4865c93b.proof:
For \(q\ge1\) and \(u>0\), define
\[
 F_q(u)=W(u)\Phi(x(2-u)/U)\log(x(2-u)/q)_+,
\]
extended by zero off the support of \(W\). On that support \(2-u\) is
bounded above and below by positive constants. If
\(\Phi(x(2-u)/U)\ne0\), then \(U\asymp x\); otherwise the function is
zero. Hence
\[
 \|F_q(e^y)\|_{H^1(\mathbb R_y)}
 \ll_{W,\Phi}\log(2x)                                   \tag{7}
\]
uniformly in \(q\). The positive-part logarithm is continuous where
\(x(2-u)=q\); its weak first derivative has only a bounded jump and is
square integrable.

Let
\[
 \widetilde F_q(t)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^\infty
 F_q(u)u^{-it}\frac{du}{u}.
\]
Plancherel in \(y=\log u\) and Cauchy--Schwarz give
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R}|\widetilde F_q(t)|\,dt
 \ll_{W,\Phi}\log(2x).                                  \tag{8}
\]
Fourier inversion on the logarithmic line gives exactly
\[
 F_q(u)=\int_{\mathbb R}\widetilde F_q(t)u^{it}\,dt.     \tag{9}
\]

Choose a fixed smooth function \(\chi\), depending only on
\(\alpha,\beta\), which equals one on
\([\alpha/2,2\beta]\) and is supported in
\([\alpha/4,4\beta]\). If (1) is nonzero, then
\[
 \alpha x\le mw,m(w-h)\le\beta x,\qquad
 D/2\le w,w-h\le2D,
\]
so \(\chi(mD/x)=1\). Using (9) twice gives
\[
\begin{split}
 A^+(m,w)
 =\mu(q_1)\mu(q_2)\int_{\mathbb R^2}
 &\widetilde F_{q_1}(t_1)\widetilde F_{q_2}(t_2)
 f_{t_1,t_2}(m)g_{t_1,t_2}(w)\,dt_1dt_2,                \tag{10}\\
 f_{t_1,t_2}(m)
 ={}&\chi(mD/x)(mD/x)^{i(t_1+t_2)},\\
 g_{t_1,t_2}(w)
 ={}&{\bf1}_{w,w-h\in{\cal I}_D}\mu(w)\mu(w-h)
 \Phi(w/D)\Phi((w-h)/D)\\
 &\times(w/D)^{it_1}((w-h)/D)^{it_2}.
\end{split}
\]
The sums are finite after insertion of \(\chi\), and (8) makes the
double integral absolutely convergent. Periodization and finite Fourier
transformation give an exact decomposition in (3), with
\[
 \beta_{t_1,t_2}(k)=\sum_m f_{t_1,t_2}(m)e_c(km),
 \qquad
 \alpha_{t_1,t_2}(r)=\sum_w g_{t_1,t_2}(w)e_c(rw).       \tag{11}
\]

If a finite sequence \(v\) is supported on an interval of length \(L\),
finite Parseval and Cauchy's inequality in each residue class give
\[
 \sum_{j\ ({\rm mod}\ c)}
 \left|\sum_n v(n)e_c(jn)\right|^2
 \le c(1+L/c)\sum_n|v(n)|^2.                            \tag{12}
\]
The \(m\)-sequence in (11) has length and squared norm \(O(M_0)\); the
\(w\)-sequence has length and squared norm \(O(D)\). Therefore
\[
 \|\beta_{t_1,t_2}\|_2\ll\{M_0(c+M_0)\}^{1/2},\qquad
 \|\alpha_{t_1,t_2}\|_2\ll\{D(c+D)\}^{1/2}.              \tag{13}
\]
Integrating (13) with (8) proves MOVING-BV-PROJ.

We prove (5). For a vector \(b_0\), put
\[
 \widehat b_0(y)=\sum_{k\ ({\rm mod}\ c)}b_0(k)e_c(ky).
\]
By the definition of the classical Kloosterman sum,
\[
 \sum_kS(r,kN;c)b_0(k)
 =
 \sum_{\substack{z\ ({\rm mod}\ c)\\(z,c)=1}}
 e_c(rz)\widehat b_0(Nz^{-1}).                          \tag{14}
\]
This is the finite Fourier transform in \(z\) of the vector which equals
\(\widehat b_0(Nz^{-1})\) on units and zero elsewhere. Since
\((N,c)=1\), inversion and multiplication by \(N\) permute the unit
residues. Parseval twice gives
\[
 \left\|\left(\sum_kS(r,kN;c)b_0(k)\right)_r\right\|_2
 \le \sqrt c\,\|\widehat b_0\|_2
 =c\|b_0\|_2.                                           \tag{15}
\]
Cauchy's inequality in \(r\) proves (5).

For each separated term in (3), multiplication of the \(r\)-vector by
the translation phase in (4) preserves its norm. Deleting zero
coordinates is an orthogonal projection and cannot increase a norm.
Apply (5), integrate the projective decomposition, and include the
normalization \(c^{-2}\):
\[
 |{\cal T}_{h,q_1,q_2}|\le c^{-1}{\cal P}(A^+).
\]
Inserting MOVING-BV-PROJ proves (6). The final paragraph only records
which data are removed by taking absolute values and makes no estimate
for the resulting outer sum.

glossary.MOVING-BV-PROJ: the exact Mellin separation and polylogarithmic projective bound for the moving positive-part logarithms
glossary.M_0: the natural m-length x/D in the top-band TMC coefficient
glossary.cal P(A^+): the projective ell-two norm of the separated finite-frequency transform of the moving-log coefficient
glossary.cal T_{h,q_1,q_2}: one fixed active-tuple nonzero TMC Kloosterman contribution

890c794f463db36a.title: COMMON-CELL FULL-FACE TOP/PRIME-STAR DECOMPOSITION AND DENSE-MODE OBSTRUCTION
890c794f463db36a.author: slava chan
890c794f463db36a.statement:
COMMON-CELL FULL-FACE TOP/PRIME-STAR DECOMPOSITION AND DENSE-MODE OBSTRUCTION.

Let mathcal P be a finite set of primes and let mathcal S be any finite family of two-element subsets G={p,q} of mathcal P. Identify G with the squarefree semiprime pq. Give every G in mathcal S a complex coefficient gamma_G, put
kappa_G=phi(G)/G,   x_G=kappa_G gamma_G,
and define the ordered support-disjoint full-face form
M=sum_{substack{G,G' in mathcal S\gcd(G,G')=1}}x_Gx_{G'}.
For r in mathcal P put
S_r=sum_{substack{G in mathcal S\r|G}}x_G.
All squares below are algebraic squares, not squared absolute values.

(A) The exact top/prime-star/diagonal identity is
M=(sum_{G in mathcal S}x_G)^2
  -sum_{r in mathcal P}S_r^2
  +sum_{G in mathcal S}x_G^2.                                 (1)

(B) Fix H>=2 and choose L>=4 distinct primes
mathcal P_L={r_1,...,r_L} contained in [H^2,2H^2). Let mathcal S consist of all
n_L=binom(L,2)
two-prime supports from mathcal P_L, and choose
gamma_G=kappa_G^{-1},
so that x_G=1 for every G. The disjointness graph on mathcal S is regular of exact degree
d_L=binom(L-2,2),                                             (2)
and
M=n_Ld_L
 =binom(L,2)binom(L-2,2).                                     (3)
Equivalently, the three terms on the right side of (1) are
n_L^2,   L(L-1)^2,   n_L,
respectively.

Moreover
n_L<=sum_G|gamma_G|^2
 <=n_L(1-H^{-2})^{-4},                                       (4)
and hence
M/(sum_G|gamma_G|^2)
 >=d_L(1-H^{-2})^4.                                          (5)
Consequently, along any sequence of such cells for which
L>=cH^2/log(2H)                                               (6)
with a fixed c>0, and for every fixed epsilon with
0<epsilon<51/16,
there is no constant C_epsilon for which the uniform arbitrary-coefficient estimate
|M|<=C_epsilon H^{13/16+epsilon}sum_G|gamma_G|^2              (7)
holds for all sufficiently large H. In particular, a theorem customarily asserted with (7) for every epsilon>0 is false on arbitrary gamma_G.

(C) Now assume H is sufficiently large for facts dcabcf2f566b5721 and d016de3f6c03e65c. In the actual fixed-semiprime source family of facts 0abb9119d9247de6 and d016de3f6c03e65c, the decoder-copy coefficient satisfies
d_{G,G',bold c}
 =x_Gx_{G'}/N_E(G,G')
for every ordered coprime active pair and every
bold c in mathcal E_{G,G'}. Therefore
sum_{substack{G,G'\gcd(G,G')=1}}
 sum_{bold c in mathcal E_{G,G'}}d_{G,G',bold c}
 =M.                                                          (8)
Thus the actual importance-sampled copies sum exactly back to the same scalar full-face kernel. If all actual x_G are nonnegative, every summand in (8) is nonnegative.

For a separate finite coefficient model showing that labelled l2 dilution alone cannot create scalar orthogonality, use the dense coefficients of (B) and only the eligible sets and cardinality bound supplied by dcabcf2f566b5721. Define synthetic coefficients
d^{syn}_{G,G',bold c}=1/N_E(G,G')
for every ordered disjoint pair and every bold c in mathcal E_{G,G'}. These are not asserted to reopen an actual source face. They satisfy
sum_{substack{G,G'\gcd(G,G')=1}}
 sum_{bold c in mathcal E_{G,G'}}d^{syn}_{G,G',bold c}=M,      (9)
and
sum_{substack{G,G'\gcd(G,G')=1}}
 sum_{bold c in mathcal E_{G,G'}}|d^{syn}_{G,G',bold c}|^2
 =sum_{substack{G,G'\gcd(G,G')=1}}1/N_E(G,G')
 <<H^{-4}(log(2H))^2 M.                                     (10)
Every synthetic copy is positive, yet its scalar sum is the full dense kernel M. Hence a labelled l2 dilution by N_E^{-1} does not, by itself, imply orthogonality or cancellation after copies are combined into a scalar varying-fibre expression.

The coefficients in (B), and therefore the synthetic copies in (9)-(10), need not be realizable as the literal source coefficients gamma_G of fact 0abb9119d9247de6. Thus (B) does not rule out source-specific cancellation between the top square and the prime-star squares in (1). This theorem asserts no lower bound for the literal source, no varying-fibre estimate, no common-cell capture, no cross-cell control, and no Goldbach implication.
890c794f463db36a.proof:
Expand the right side of (1). For an ordered pair (G,G'), the top square gives coefficient one. The prime-star sum subtracts one for every prime in G intersect G', and the final diagonal adds one exactly when G=G'. Since G and G' each have two distinct prime factors, there are exactly three cases. If they are disjoint, their coefficient is one. If they are distinct and share one prime, their coefficient is 1-1=0. If G=G', their coefficient is 1-2+1=0. Thus precisely the ordered coprime pairs remain, proving (1).

For the complete family of two-subsets of mathcal P_L, a fixed G uses two primes, and a support disjoint from G is obtained by choosing any two of the remaining L-2 primes. This proves the exact degree d_L in (2). Since all x_G are one, summing the degree over all n_L vertices proves (3). The top sum is n_L, every prime belongs to L-1 supports and hence has S_r=L-1, and the diagonal has n_L terms. This gives the three displayed values. It also checks directly that
n_L^2-L(L-1)^2+n_L=n_Ld_L.

For G=pq with p,q in [H^2,2H^2),
kappa_G=(1-1/p)(1-1/q).
Hence
(1-H^{-2})^2<=kappa_G<1.
The choice gamma_G=kappa_G^{-1} therefore gives
1<|gamma_G|^2<=(1-H^{-2})^{-4}.
Summing over the n_L supports proves (4), and division of (3) by the upper bound in (4) proves (5).

Under (6), for all sufficiently large H we have L-3>=L/2 and L-2>=L/2, so
d_L=(L-2)(L-3)/2>>H^4/(log(2H))^2.
If (7) held, (5) would force
H^4/(log(2H))^2<<H^{13/16+epsilon}.
But the quotient of the left side by the right side is
H^{51/16-epsilon}/(log(2H))^2,
which tends to infinity for epsilon<51/16. This contradiction proves (B). Notice that (6) is an explicit hypothesis; no prime-counting theorem is used in this finite argument.

For the actual-source assertion in (C), fact d016de3f6c03e65c defines
d_{G,G',bold c}
 =alpha_{G,G'}gamma_Ggamma_{G'}/N_E(G,G'),
where
alpha_{G,G'}=kappa_Gkappa_{G'}.
Thus its numerator is x_Gx_{G'}. The same fact gives exactly N_E(G,G') eligible copies for a fixed ordered coprime pair, so their sum is x_Gx_{G'}. Summing over the ordered coprime pairs proves (8). Nonnegativity is immediate when the x_G are nonnegative.

For the separate synthetic model, define the coefficients exactly as in the statement. There are N_E(G,G') copies for each ordered disjoint pair, so their sum for that pair is one. The number of ordered disjoint pairs is M by (3), proving (9). Their squared l2 contribution for that pair is
N_E(G,G')N_E(G,G')^{-2}=N_E(G,G')^{-1},
which proves the equality in (10). Fact dcabcf2f566b5721 supplies, for sufficiently large H,
N_E(G,G')>>H^4/(log(2H))^2
uniformly in the ordered common-cell prime tuple. Applying the reciprocal estimate to every one of the M ordered disjoint pairs proves the inequality in (10).

All synthetic copies are positive and sum coherently to M, so their small labelled squared l2 mass records only the splitting into N_E labels and supplies no scalar cancellation. They were defined solely as a finite coefficient model on the eligible label sets, not as an actual provenance coefficient. The arbitrary gamma_G in (B) likewise was not produced from a literal Poisson source, which proves the final scope assertions.

89a3f1716a20a7e7.title: HC-SMALL EXACT CHARACTER/DIVISOR-SWITCH TRANSPOSE AND ROWWISE TYPE-I NO-FIT. Fix one orientation, one exact active pair g,c, one complete frozen selected critical source block, and the notation of fact edabb9a0d2959b41. Fix kappa with (kappa,q)=1 on every retained q-row, fix h|R_kappa with (h,c)=1, and fix powers of two D,M in the exact smooth partition of that fact. Put
89a3f1716a20a7e7.author: slava chan
89a3f1716a20a7e7.statement:
HC-SMALL EXACT CHARACTER/DIVISOR-SWITCH TRANSPOSE AND ROWWISE TYPE-I NO-FIT. Fix one orientation, one exact active pair g,c, one complete frozen selected critical source block, and the notation of fact edabb9a0d2959b41. Fix kappa with (kappa,q)=1 on every retained q-row, fix h|R_kappa with (h,c)=1, and fix powers of two D,M in the exact smooth partition of that fact. Put
W_{q,kappa,h,d}(m)=Psi_D(d)Psi_M(m)
 A_lit(q,kappa,hdm;(ell-kappa hdm)/q).
Define the exact fundamental-domain rectangle
S_{D,M}(kappa,h)
 =mu(c)mu(h) sum_q mu(q)
  sum_{d<=m,(dm,c R_kappa)=1}
  omega_diag(d,m)rho_{1/2}(d)rho_{1/2}(m)
  W_{q,kappa,h,d}(m)
 [1_{dm congruent ell*(kappa h)^(-1) (mod q)}
  -phi(q)^(-1)1_{(dm,q)=1}],                                   (1)
where q has its original finite Q_c-scale support and every literal q,kappa-dependent weight and label inside A_lit is retained.

For every summand of (1), character orthogonality gives exactly
1_{dm congruent ell*(kappa h)^(-1) (mod q)}
 -phi(q)^(-1)1_{(dm,q)=1}
 =1_{(dm,q)=1}phi(q)^(-1)
  sum_{chi (mod q), chi nonprincipal}
  chi(kappa hdm*ell^(-1)).                                      (2)
Thus the exact long arithmetic coefficient in the character transpose is
rho_{1/2}(m)chi(m), not an unweighted smooth long slot.

There is also an exact physical divisor switch. Fix d and put
k_{sw}=kappa h d.                                                (3)
The physical pairs (q,m) in (1) are in bijection with pairs (q,t) satisfying
qt congruent ell (mod k_{sw}),                                  (4)
m=(ell-qt)/k_{sw} in the original M-cell,                        (5)
d<=m, and all original positivity, q-support, unit, and literal support conditions. Under this bijection the complete physical coefficient on the fixed d-slice is
mu(c)mu(h)rho_{1/2}(d)mu(q)
 omega_diag(d,m)rho_{1/2}(m)W_{q,kappa,h,d}(m),                  (6)
where m is the integer in (5), so A_lit inside W is still evaluated at the integer quotient t. The principal term in (1) is not included in (4): it remains the separate sum
-mu(c)mu(h) sum_q mu(q)/phi(q)
 sum_{d<=m,(dm,c q R_kappa)=1}
 omega_diag(d,m)rho_{1/2}(d)rho_{1/2}(m)
 W_{q,kappa,h,d}(m).                                             (7)

Consequently fact 8138369f26f88aad is not a direct analytic consumer of (1), (2), or (4)-(7). Its displayed form has the inverse-additive phase e_q(A_0 nu(lm)^(-1)) and requires the long m-dependence, apart from that phase, to be a continuously differentiable bounded-variation function. In (2) the phase is a multiplicative character and the long coefficient is rho_{1/2}(m)chi(m); after substituting (5) in (6), the long arithmetic coefficient is rho_{1/2}((ell-qt)/k_{sw}) jointly coupled to q,t. Fact 5772f2de626492b3 proves bounded variation only for the literal smooth amplitude A_lit along the product variable; it asserts no bounded-variation interpolation or cancellation theorem after multiplication by rho_{1/2}. The outer mu(q) can be discarded inside an absolute q-sum if a theorem otherwise matches, but it does not repair these phase and coefficient mismatches.

Even after granting those structural mismatches for free, the right side of fact 8138369f26f88aad is not uniformly within the HC-SMALL budget on the critical near-half scale simplex. Indeed, for a free parameter Z_0 tending to infinity, put
c=1, Q_c=Q=Z_0^5, beta=6/5, B=Z_0^6,
G=Gamma=Z_0^(-2), K_c=Z_0^2, T=Z_0^3.                           (8)
Then exactly
T=Gamma Q_c, B=Q_c^2 Gamma/K_c, Gamma K_c=1,                    (9)
so for every fixed tau_W>0 and C>0 the scale family satisfies
Gamma K_c<Q^(tau_W),
Gamma<K_c(log B)^(2C).                                          (10)
It is therefore inside the scale-defined critical near-half complement, not the already-paid deep-subhalf range. On the favorable smallest short box L=1,M=B, the Type-I length conditions
LM<=Q_c^(2-tau_I), L<=Q_c^(1/2-tau_I)                           (11)
hold for every fixed 0<tau_I<1/2 and all sufficiently large Z_0. But the deterministic bracket in the conclusion of fact 8138369f26f88aad satisfies
Q_c^(3/2)L/B=Z_0^(3/2)=Q_c^(3/10).                              (12)
Hence applying that theorem separately to kappa-rows and summing them absolutely cannot, from the scale identities alone, yield B K_c(log B)^(-A) for arbitrary A: its Q_c^(3/2)L term already exceeds the per-row B budget by a fixed power in (8).

Equations (2)-(7) are exact source-preserving identities, and (8)-(12) are a theorem-right-hand-side no-fit. No lower bound for S_{D,M}(kappa,h), impossibility of another Type-I or divisor-switch theorem, HC-SMALL estimate, other HC-range estimate, critical-tail payment, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
89a3f1716a20a7e7.proof:
Fact edabb9a0d2959b41 gives the exact centered h,d,m ledger, the smooth dyadic partition, the d<=m fundamental domain with omega_diag, the unit conditions, the moving residue, and the literal amplitude. Restricting that exact finite identity to one kappa,h,D,M rectangle gives (1), including its fixed factors mu(c)mu(h).

On every retained row, facts edabb9a0d2959b41 and 8d9feea8c44da2c8, the latter being a predecessor of edabb9a0d2959b41, give (ell,q)=1, (kappa,q)=1, and hence (h,q)=1 because h|rad(kappa). Let a be the unit residue ell*(kappa h)^(-1) modulo q. For a unit x modulo q, Dirichlet-character orthogonality says
phi(q)^(-1)sum_{chi (mod q)}chi(xa^(-1))=1_{x congruent a (mod q)}.
The principal character contributes phi(q)^(-1)1_{(x,q)=1}. Taking x=dm and subtracting this principal term gives
1_{dm congruent a}-phi(q)^(-1)1_{(dm,q)=1}
 =phi(q)^(-1)1_{(dm,q)=1}sum_{chi nonprincipal}chi(dm a^(-1)).
Since a^(-1) is congruent to kappa h ell^(-1) modulo q, this is (2). Multiplicativity of every Dirichlet character on units factors its m-dependence as chi(m), while rho_{1/2}(m) is already present in (1). This proves the stated long coefficient.

For the physical term, the congruence in (1) is equivalent to q|(ell-kappa hdm). Define t=(ell-kappa hdm)/q. Then
qt+kappa hdm=ell,
so qt is congruent to ell modulo k_{sw}=kappa h d and (5) holds. Conversely, if (4)-(5), d<=m, and all displayed support conditions hold, then substituting (5) gives qt+kappa hdm=ell, hence q|(ell-kappa hdm), and recovers the unique original m. The two maps are inverse. Substitution in every coefficient gives (6), including mu(c)mu(h), the fixed rho_{1/2}(d), the unchanged mu(q), rho_{1/2}(m), omega_diag, and A_lit evaluated at t. The principal term in (1) has no congruence q|(ell-kappa hdm); separating it before the switch gives exactly (7). This proves (3)-(7).

Compare these formulas with the exact statement of predecessor fact 8138369f26f88aad. Its form contains an inverse-additive character and one arithmetic coefficient alpha_l only in the short variable; its long-variable factor is required to have the differentiability and variation property in its equation (2). Formula (2) instead has the arithmetic coefficient rho_{1/2}(m)chi(m) in the long slot, and formula (6) has rho_{1/2} evaluated at the affine quotient (ell-qt)/k_{sw}. Fact 5772f2de626492b3 lists every source-dependent long-variable factor and proves the logarithmic bounded-variation estimate only after excluding mu(n); after the half-convolution, rho_{1/2}(m) is part of that excluded arithmetic coefficient. Fact 5999a1878276ac78 supplies only |rho_{1/2}(m)|<=1 and the convolution identity, not a continuously differentiable interpolation with the variation norm required by fact 8138369f26f88aad. Therefore the hypotheses of that predecessor are not verified for (1), (2), or (6). The assertion about mu(q) follows because |mu(q)|<=1 inside any modulus-by-modulus absolute sum.

It remains to check the numerical no-fit. Substitute (8):
Gamma Q_c=Z_0^(-2)Z_0^5=Z_0^3=T,
and
Q_c^2 Gamma/K_c=Z_0^10 Z_0^(-2)Z_0^(-2)=Z_0^6=B.
Also Gamma K_c=Z_0^(-2)Z_0^2=1, proving (9). For fixed tau_W>0, Q^(tau_W)>1 when Z_0>1. Moreover
K_c(log B)^(2C)=Z_0^2(log Z_0^6)^(2C)>Z_0^(-2)=Gamma
for sufficiently large Z_0, proving (10). By fact a3103a7fbc2dc2ed, (9)-(10) are exactly the critical scale identities, critical-W inequality, and near-half complement condition.

For L=1 and M=B=Q_c^(6/5), one has LM=Q_c^(6/5)<=Q_c^(2-tau_I) when tau_I<4/5, and 1<=Q_c^(1/2-tau_I) when tau_I<1/2. Hence both inequalities in (11) hold when 0<tau_I<1/2. Finally
Q_c^(3/2)L/B=(Z_0^5)^(3/2)/Z_0^6=Z_0^(15/2-6)=Z_0^(3/2)=Q_c^(3/10),
which is (12). Multiplication by the number of separately bounded kappa rows affects both the Type-I aggregate and the target comparison by the same K_c factor. Since a positive fixed power exceeds every fixed power of log B, the right side of fact 8138369f26f88aad cannot by itself imply B K_c(log B)^(-A) in this scale family. This is only a failure of that displayed upper-bound route, as stated.

89b262fc9d54d792.title: Let H>=2 and let S_H be the set of quadruples (a,b,c,d) of nonzero even integers such that |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|<=H^3 and ab+cd=4. Then, as H tends to infinity, one has H^6 << |S_H| <<_epsilon H^{6+epsilon} for every epsilon>0. Equivalently, the bare shell of nonzero even matrices Q=((a,c),(-d,b)) with det(Q)=4=2K for K=2 has cardinality H^{6+o(1)}. In particular, the fixed-determinant condition alone supplies no bound O(H^{6-delta}) for any fixed delta>0
89b262fc9d54d792.author: slava chan
89b262fc9d54d792.statement: Let H>=2 and let S_H be the set of quadruples (a,b,c,d) of nonzero even integers such that |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|<=H^3 and ab+cd=4. Then, as H tends to infinity, one has H^6 << |S_H| <<_epsilon H^{6+epsilon} for every epsilon>0. Equivalently, the bare shell of nonzero even matrices Q=((a,c),(-d,b)) with det(Q)=4=2K for K=2 has cardinality H^{6+o(1)}. In particular, the fixed-determinant condition alone supplies no bound O(H^{6-delta}) for any fixed delta>0.
89b262fc9d54d792.proof:
Put M=floor(H^3/16). For all sufficiently large H, consider ordered pairs (a_0,c_0) in the integer interval [M,2M] with gcd(a_0,c_0)=1. Choose b_0 to be the representative of the inverse of a_0 modulo c_0 satisfying |b_0|<=c_0/2, and put d_0=(1-a_0b_0)/c_0. Then a_0b_0+c_0d_0=1. Moreover |b_0|<=M and |d_0|<=1/c_0+a_0/2<=M+1/M. Since a_0,c_0>1, b_0 and d_0 are nonzero: b_0=0 would give c_0d_0=1, and d_0=0 would give a_0b_0=1. Therefore
(a,b,c,d)=(2a_0,2b_0,2c_0,2d_0)
has nonzero even entries, satisfies ab+cd=4, and lies in the H^3 box for all sufficiently large H.

There are >>M^2 admissible coprime pairs. Indeed, every noncoprime pair has a common prime divisor p<=2M, so their number is at most
sum_{p<=2M}(M/p+1)^2.
Now sum_p p^{-2}<=sum_{n=2}^infinity n^{-2}<3/4: the n=2 term is 1/4 and, for n>=3, 1/n^2<1/(n(n-1)), whose sum is 1/2. Also sum_{p<=2M}p^{-1}<=sum_{n<=2M}n^{-1}=O(log M), and the number of primes p<=2M is at most 2M. Thus the number of noncoprime pairs is at most (3/4)M^2+O(M log M), leaving >>M^2 coprime pairs. Distinct pairs give distinct quadruples, so |S_H|>>M^2>>H^6.

For the upper bound, set X=H^3 and ignore the parity restriction. Fix nonzero a,b with |a|,|b|<=X. If ab=4, then cd=0, impossible because c,d are nonzero. Otherwise n=4-ab is a nonzero integer of size O(X^2), and the number of ordered nonzero integer pairs (c,d) with cd=n is 2 tau(|n|). The elementary divisor estimate tau(n)<<_eta n^eta for every eta>0 follows from prime factorization: after fixing eta, factors k+1 are at most a constant times p^{eta k} for every prime power p^k, with the finitely many small primes absorbed into the constant. Hence for each (a,b) the number of (c,d) is O_eta(X^{2eta}), and there are O(X^2) choices of (a,b). Therefore |S_H|<<_eta X^{2+2eta}. Given epsilon>0, take eta=epsilon/6 to obtain |S_H|<<_epsilon H^{6+epsilon}.

The final assertion follows from the lower bound: H^6 cannot be O(H^{6-delta}) for any fixed positive delta.

glossary.K: Half of det(Q), fixed here to K=2.
glossary.Q: The two-by-two integer matrix with rows (a,c) and (-d,b).
glossary.S_H: The set of nonzero even coefficient quadruples in the H^3 box satisfying ab+cd=4.

8a72a40427f389ae.title: ARBITRARY-VECTOR FIXED-ACTIVE-PRODUCT BESSEL BOUND AND THE EXACT PHYSICAL-TO-DUAL PARSEVAL TAX
8a72a40427f389ae.author: slava chan
8a72a40427f389ae.statement:
ARBITRARY-VECTOR FIXED-ACTIVE-PRODUCT BESSEL BOUND AND THE EXACT PHYSICAL-TO-DUAL PARSEVAL TAX.

Let r be a nonempty squarefree positive integer. Let a finite row set be contained in I times J, where I and J are integer intervals of cardinalities U and V. For every row j and every rho in
Omega_r=product_{p|r}F_p^*
let
V_{j,r}(rho)=product_{p|r}ghat_{p,j}(rho_p)
be a tensor Kloosterman vector satisfying the hypotheses and normalization of fact 3330e83b6d253b69. Let W_{j,r}(rho) be arbitrary complex numbers and put
E_r(W)=sum_{rho in Omega_r}
 |sum_jW_{j,r}(rho)V_{j,r}(rho)|^2.                                 (1)
Then, for every epsilon>0,
E_r(W)<<_epsilon Q^epsilon(UV/r)
 sum_j sum_{rho in Omega_r}|W_{j,r}(rho)|^2.                         (2)

If
U<=C B/r,   V<=r,                                                    (3)
where C is fixed and all parameters are bounded by a fixed power of Q, then
E_r(W)<<_{C,epsilon}Q^epsilon(B/r)
 sum_j sum_{rho in Omega_r}|W_{j,r}(rho)|^2.                         (4)
Thus (4) remains valid for completely mode-dependent vectors; it uses pointwise tensor Weil rather than the sharper scalar square-divisor Gram.

Now suppose W_{j,r} is the exact literal multiplier of fact 3330e83b6d253b69:
W_{j,r}(rho)=sum_qD_{j,r}(q)chi_rho(q),                              (5)
where D_{j,r} is supported on an integer interval containing at most L_q integers. Then
sum_{rho in Omega_r}|W_{j,r}(rho)|^2
 <=(L_q+r)sum_q|D_{j,r}(q)|^2.                                     (6)
In particular, on the literal q-block L_q=O(Q),
sum_{rho in Omega_r}|W_{j,r}(rho)|^2
 <<(Q+r)sum_q|D_{j,r}(q)|^2.                                      (7)

Equations (4) and (7) show exactly what survives from the simultaneous tensor mechanism for arbitrary literal mode dependence. They do not by themselves prove C4-VEC: a target-scale proof must still exploit source structure to improve or aggregate the physical-to-dual tax Q+r and control distinct active products, or use the sharper scalar square-divisor mechanism after proving mode coherence. No varying-r bound, C4 moment, other-anatomy estimate, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
8a72a40427f389ae.proof:
Fact 4f9aec67f5be35db gives for every active prime p and nonzero local parameter
|ghat_{p,j}(rho_p)|<=2/sqrt(p)
when rho_p!=0. Therefore
|V_{j,r}(rho)|^2
 <=4^{omega(r)}/r
 <<_epsilon Q^epsilon/r,                                           (8)
using the fixed-power divisor bound for squarefree r.

Fix rho. Cauchy's inequality over the at most UV rows gives
|sum_jW_{j,r}(rho)V_{j,r}(rho)|^2
 <=UV sum_j|W_{j,r}(rho)|^2|V_{j,r}(rho)|^2
 <<_epsilon Q^epsilon(UV/r)sum_j|W_{j,r}(rho)|^2.                   (9)
Sum (9) over rho in Omega_r to prove (2). Under (3),
UV/r<=C(B/r)(V/r)<=CB/r,
which proves (4).

For the Parseval assertion, enlarge Omega_r to the full additive character group
Omega_r^all=product_{p|r}F_p.
The characters
chi_rho(x)=product_{p|r}e_p(rho_p x)
are exactly all additive characters of Z/rZ under CRT. Since the summands are nonnegative,
sum_{rho in Omega_r}|W_{j,r}(rho)|^2
 <=sum_{rho in Omega_r^all}|W_{j,r}(rho)|^2.                        (10)
Group D_{j,r}(q) by its residue x modulo r. Finite-group Parseval gives
sum_{rho in Omega_r^all}|W_{j,r}(rho)|^2
 =r sum_{x mod r}|sum_{q congruent x mod r}D_{j,r}(q)|^2.           (11)
Every residue class contains at most L_q/r+1 supported integers. Cauchy's inequality within each residue class yields
sum_{x mod r}|sum_{q congruent x mod r}D_{j,r}(q)|^2
 <=(L_q/r+1)sum_q|D_{j,r}(q)|^2.                                   (12)
Combine (10)-(12) to obtain (6), and use L_q=O(Q) for (7). The scope statements merely record the unestimated taxes left by these exact inequalities.

glossary.E_r(W): The fixed-active-product weighted tensor energy for arbitrary mode multipliers.
glossary.L_q: The cardinality bound for the physical q-support interval.
glossary.Omega_r^all: The full additive dual group product over all primes dividing r.
glossary.physical-to-dual Parseval tax: The factor L_q+r relating the mode-multiplier l2 norm to the physical q-coefficient l2 norm.

8ac2e2a9fb7d0806.title: P-qSRC-ALLF-MIDBETA: FOURIER-DECAY PAYMENT OF THE LARGE-F PRINCIPAL SOURCE WHEN beta<=2+tau. Adopt the Dcal>Q^2 hard Good-W block, the fixed tau>0, and the exact split H_C=P-qSRC+C-qSRC>=2 from facts e55b27d39c593164 and e9e9563501147a1a. Thus B=Q^beta, mathscr W=G^2Q^(2-beta)>=Q^tau, and H_P=B/(GQ). Assume
8ac2e2a9fb7d0806.author: slava chan
8ac2e2a9fb7d0806.statement:
P-qSRC-ALLF-MIDBETA: FOURIER-DECAY PAYMENT OF THE LARGE-F PRINCIPAL SOURCE WHEN beta<=2+tau. Adopt the Dcal>Q^2 hard Good-W block, the fixed tau>0, and the exact split H_C=P-qSRC+C-qSRC>=2 from facts e55b27d39c593164 and e9e9563501147a1a. Thus B=Q^beta, mathscr W=G^2Q^(2-beta)>=Q^tau, and H_P=B/(GQ). Assume
beta<=2+tau.                                                     (1)
For each fixed A>0 put
omega_{F,A}=(1+F/H_P)^(-A),                                     (2)
with the fixed logarithmic derivative costs of the physical source absorbed into x^{o(1)}. Then uniformly for every 1<=F<=x^3,
|P-qSRC|<=x^{o(1)}|omega_{F,A}|^2 BQF.                          (P-qSRC-ALLF-MIDBETA)
For F<=Q this is fact cd13b5e0a78656f1. For F>Q it follows by applying GA-qPRINC with one additional Fourier-decay order to each of its two coefficient factors.

Consequently, throughout the chamber Dcal>Q^2 and beta<=2+tau, the single centered estimate
|C-qSRC>=2|<=x^{o(1)}|omega_{F,A}|^2 BQ^2F^2/Dcal               (3)
would imply
|H_C|<=x^{o(1)}|omega_{F,A}|^2(BQF+BQ^2F^2/Dcal).               (4)
Thus the previously separate F>Q principal debt is removed in this beta-chamber. The range beta>2+tau remains untreated, as do C-qSRC>=2, N-qSRC-SUP, the small-Dcal projected-incidence branch, the tail and Goldbach.
8ac2e2a9fb7d0806.proof:
From mathscr W=G^2Q^(2-beta)>=Q^tau one obtains
G>=Q^((beta-2+tau)/2).                                          (5)
Since H_P=B/(GQ)=Q^(beta-1)/G, equation (5) gives
H_P<=Q^(beta/2-tau/2).                                          (6)
Assumption (1) makes the exponent in (6) at most one, hence
H_P<=Q.                                                         (7)

The proof of GA-qPRINC in fact 764588e99974a6d9 is an absolute homogeneous quadratic coefficient count. Its only analytic input is the pointwise physical Fourier envelope for each coefficient. Fact e55b27d39c593164 states that this envelope has arbitrary fixed-order decay in F/H_P. Therefore, for every fixed A>0, run the same proof using order A+1 instead of order A. With the notation (2), this gives
|P-qSRC|<=x^{o(1)}|omega_{F,A+1}|^2 BF^2.                       (8)
The change of fixed integration-by-parts order and its fixed logarithmic derivative costs are absorbed by x^{o(1)}.

If F<=Q, fact cd13b5e0a78656f1 already gives the claimed BQF bound at any prescribed fixed decay order. Suppose F>Q. By (2),
omega_{F,A+1}=omega_{F,A}(1+F/H_P)^(-1).                        (9)
Equations (7) and F>Q imply
(1+F/H_P)^(-1)<=H_P/F<=Q/F.                                    (10)
Insert (9)-(10) into (8):
|P-qSRC|<=x^{o(1)}|omega_{F,A}|^2 BF^2(Q/F)^2
          =x^{o(1)}|omega_{F,A}|^2 BQ^2
          <=x^{o(1)}|omega_{F,A}|^2 BQF,                        (11)
because Q<F. This proves P-qSRC-ALLF-MIDBETA for F>Q and hence for all F.

Finally use the exact decomposition H_C=P-qSRC+C-qSRC>=2 from fact e9e9563501147a1a, take absolute values, and insert P-qSRC-ALLF-MIDBETA and the conditional estimate (3). This gives (4). No estimate of the centered source or any excluded branch was used.

glossary.P-qSRC-ALLF-MIDBETA: The complete principal-source payment by the BQF moment term for beta<=2+tau at every frequency.
glossary.omega_{F,A}: The order-A normalized Fourier-decay envelope (1+F/H_P)^(-A), with fixed logarithmic constants absorbed into x^{o(1)}.

8b46abe31a5ae8d7.title: GA-qCENT-LOWFACE: EXACT PRIMEWISE CENTERING, ABSOLUTE LOW-ACTIVE-FACE PAYMENT, AND THE LARGE-ACTIVE-PRODUCT VECTOR RESIDUAL
8b46abe31a5ae8d7.author: slava chan
8b46abe31a5ae8d7.statement:
GA-qCENT-LOWFACE: EXACT PRIMEWISE CENTERING, ABSOLUTE LOW-ACTIVE-FACE PAYMENT, AND THE LARGE-ACTIVE-PRODUCT VECTOR RESIDUAL.

Adopt the setting and notation of GA-qCENT in fact 764588e99974a6d9. Thus
\[
\mathcal D\le Q^2,\qquad
Y={Q^2\over\mathcal D}\ge1,
\]
and every retained hard pair satisfies
\[
m=m_q>Y,\qquad
(c,m)=(n,m)=1,\qquad
c=C_q,\qquad n=d_\lambda v_\lambda,
\]
with \(m\) squarefree.

For every prime \(p\mid m\), put \(m_p=m/p\), let
\(\overline {m_p}\) denote its inverse modulo \(p\), and define on unit \(n\) modulo \(p\)
\[
f_{p;m,c}(n)
=e_p\!\left(-c\,n^{-1}\overline {m_p}\right),
\qquad
\kappa_{p;m,c}(n)
=f_{p;m,c}(n)+{1\over p-1}.
\tag{1}
\]
For \(r\mid m\), put
\[
\mathcal K_{r;m,c}(n)
=\prod_{p\mid r}\kappa_{p;m,c}(n),
\qquad
\mathcal K_{1;m,c}(n)=1.
\tag{2}
\]
Each \(\kappa_{p;m,c}\) has zero mean on
\((\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)^\times\). The centered kernel of fact
764588e99974a6d9 has the exact CRT-face expansion
\[
\boxed{
K^\circ_{m,c}(n)
=
\sum_{\substack{r\mid m\\r>1}}
{\mu(m/r)\over\phi(m/r)}
\mathcal K_{r;m,c}(n).
}
\tag{3}
\]

Split GA-qCENT according to \(r\le Y\) and \(r>Y\) in (3). The complete low-active-face part is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathfrak H_C^{q\text{-}{\rm lowface}}
=
\sum_\lambda
\sum_{\substack{R\ne R'\\
aa'>Q^2/\mathcal D,\ m_d>L,\ m_q>Y\\
d_\lambda\nmid\mathscr A\Delta_0}}
&B_\lambda(R)\overline{B_\lambda(R')}\\
&\times
\sum_{\substack{1<r\mid m_q\\r\le Y}}
{\mu(m_q/r)\over\phi(m_q/r)}
\mathcal K_{r;m_q,C_q}(d_\lambda v_\lambda).
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
Then
\[
\boxed{
|\mathfrak H_C^{q\text{-}{\rm lowface}}|
\le
x^{o(1)}|\omega_F|^2B YF^2
=
x^{o(1)}|\omega_F|^2{BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}.
}
\tag{GA-qCENT-LOWFACE}
\]
The estimate is absolute and retains the exact Hilbert copy inventory and every literal marker, Möbius, Fourier, target-gcd, fixed-\(U\), high, source, parent, ordering, equality, collision, deletion, provenance, coprimality and projective selector.

For fixed \((d,v)\), let
\[
\mathbf B_{d,v}(R)
=(B_\lambda(R))_{\lambda\in\Lambda(d,v)}
\]
be the exact Hilbert ray coefficient of fact cff9d29efb555b8e. The complementary exact residual is
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\mathfrak H_C^{q\text{-}{\rm largeface}}
=
\sum_{d,v}
\sum_{\substack{R\ne R'\\
aa'>Q^2/\mathcal D,\ m_d>L,\ m_q>Y\\
d\nmid\mathscr A\Delta_0}}
&
\left\langle\mathbf B_{d,v}(R),
\mathbf B_{d,v}(R')\right\rangle\\
&\times
\sum_{\substack{r\mid m_q\\r>Y}}
{\mu(m_q/r)\over\phi(m_q/r)}
\mathcal K_{r;m_q,C_q}(dv).
\end{aligned}
}
\tag{GA-CqKLOO-VEC}
\]
Thus
\[
\mathfrak H_C^{q\text{-}{\rm cent}}
=
\mathfrak H_C^{q\text{-}{\rm lowface}}
+
\mathfrak H_C^{q\text{-}{\rm largeface}}.
\tag{5}
\]
Every pair-dependent deletion, varying squarefree \(m_q\), varying unit
\(C_q\), marked modulus \(dv\), and literal joint source coefficient is preserved in GA-CqKLOO-VEC. After dyadically splitting its active product
\[
\mathcal R\le r<2\mathcal R,\qquad \mathcal R>Y,
\]
the remaining source-specific supplier is
\[
\boxed{
|\mathfrak H_C^{q\text{-}{\rm largeface}}|
\le
x^{o(1)}|\omega_F|^2{BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}.
}
\tag{6}
\]
It is enough to prove (6) on every such dyadic active-product block; the \(O(\log x)\) blocks are absorbed into \(x^{o(1)}\). Estimate (6) is not asserted here.

The reduction is sharp for any argument using only the inactive divisor coefficient: every \(m_q>Y\) has the full-active face \(r=m_q\), whose coefficient in (3) is exactly one. Hence no complete dyadic \(m_q\)-block is paid merely by the inactive factor \(\phi(m_q/r)^{-1}\). A proof of (6) must exploit cancellation in the exact centered tensor/source aggregation while retaining the pair-dependent conditions; applying a scalar reciprocal-fraction estimate after fixing one ray pair and then summing absolute values is not a payment of GA-CqKLOO-VEC.

This theorem proves the exact face expansion, GA-qCENT-LOWFACE, and the minimal residual only. It proves neither (6), nor all of GA-qCENT, nor the \(\mathcal D>Q^2\) principal or centered source traces, nor GA-RAY-SPEC, GA-NR-DIL, a tail payment or Goldbach.
8b46abe31a5ae8d7.proof:
Because \(m\) is squarefree, the Chinese remainder identity gives
\[
e_m(-cn^{-1})
=
\prod_{p\mid m}
e_p\!\left(-c\,n^{-1}\overline {m_p}\right)
=
\prod_{p\mid m}f_{p;m,c}(n).
\tag{7}
\]
Indeed, the integer
\[
\sum_{p\mid m}m_p\overline {m_p}
\]
is congruent to one modulo every prime dividing \(m\), hence modulo \(m\); division by \(m\) proves the additive-character factorization.

Since \(c\), \(n\), and \(m_p\) are units modulo \(p\), inversion permutes the nonzero residues and
\[
\sum_{u\in(\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)^\times}
f_{p;m,c}(u)
=
\sum_{z\in(\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)^\times}
e_p(-c z\overline {m_p})
=-1.
\tag{8}
\]
Thus the normalized unit mean is \(-1/(p-1)\), and (1) is mean zero.

Write
\[
f_{p;m,c}=\kappa_{p;m,c}-{1\over p-1}
\]
in (7) and expand the product over subsets of the prime divisors of \(m\). A subset with active-prime product \(r\mid m\) contributes
\[
\prod_{p\mid r}\kappa_{p;m,c}(n)
\prod_{p\mid m/r}\left(-{1\over p-1}\right)
=
{\mu(m/r)\over\phi(m/r)}
\mathcal K_{r;m,c}(n).
\tag{9}
\]
For \(r=1\), this is
\[
{\mu(m)\over\phi(m)},
\]
the principal term in fact 764588e99974a6d9. Subtracting it proves (3).

We estimate the faces \(1<r\le Y\). From (1),
\[
|\kappa_{p;m,c}(n)|
\le1+{1\over p-1}={p\over p-1}.
\]
Hence
\[
|\mathcal K_{r;m,c}(n)|
\le {r\over\phi(r)}
\le x^{o(1)}
\tag{10}
\]
uniformly, because every parameter is polynomially bounded in \(x\). Also
\[
{1\over\phi(m/r)}
\le x^{o(1)}{r\over m}.
\tag{11}
\]
Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{\substack{1<r\mid m\\r\le Y}}
{|\mathcal K_{r;m,c}(n)|\over\phi(m/r)}
&\le
{x^{o(1)}\over m}
\sum_{\substack{r\mid m\\r\le Y}}r\\
&\le
{x^{o(1)}Y\over m}\tau(m)
\le {x^{o(1)}Y\over m}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{12}
\]

The proof of GA-qPRINC in fact 764588e99974a6d9 derives from the cumulative GA-LOW-qCOND coordinate count the reciprocal-conductor ledger
\[
\sum_{\rm scaling\ coordinates}{1\over m_q}
\le x^{o(1)}F^2.
\tag{13}
\]
Expand both exact ray coefficients \(B_\lambda(R)\) into their supported scaling coordinates, exactly as in that proof. The pointwise coefficient-product envelope is
\[
x^{o(1)}|\omega_F|^2,
\]
and the complete number of exact marked copies over \(n\asymp B\), including divisor-bounded copy multiplicity, is
\[
Bx^{o(1)}.
\tag{14}
\]
Insert (12), then (13), and multiply by (14). Every selector in (4), including the hard pair-dependent deletion, only removes terms after absolute values are taken. We obtain
\[
|\mathfrak H_C^{q\text{-}{\rm lowface}}|
\le
x^{o(1)}|\omega_F|^2 B YF^2,
\]
which is GA-qCENT-LOWFACE.

Splitting the exact finite divisor sum (3) into \(r\le Y\) and \(r>Y\) proves (5). On the latter part, group all exact copies having
\[
(d_\lambda,v_\lambda)=(d,v).
\]
The kernel and all displayed pair conditions depend on the common \(d,v\) and ray pair, while
\[
\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda(d,v)}
B_\lambda(R)\overline{B_\lambda(R')}
=
\left\langle\mathbf B_{d,v}(R),
\mathbf B_{d,v}(R')\right\rangle.
\]
This gives GA-CqKLOO-VEC without changing any coefficient or deletion. Dyadic subdivision of \(r\) introduces only \(O(\log x)\) blocks because \(r\mid m_q<4Q^2\le x^{O(1)}\).

Finally, the divisor \(r=m\) is always present in (3) and has coefficient
\[
{\mu(1)\over\phi(1)}=1.
\]
Thus the inactive factor gives no saving on the full-active face. This proves the stated sharp scope limitation without asserting that the literal full-active source is large. All other exclusions follow.

glossary.GA-CqKLOO-VEC: The exact large-active-product, deletion-preserving Hilbert ray/Kloosterman residual after GA-qCENT-LOWFACE.
glossary.GA-qCENT-LOWFACE: The absolute canonical-scale payment of all centered physical-q-conductor CRT faces whose active prime product is at most Q^2/Dcal.
glossary.physical q-conductor active product: The divisor r of m_q indexing the primes at which the mean-zero local inverse kernel is selected in the centered CRT expansion.

8bf5ca45f71b8c2c.title: C0 DICHOTOMY FOR THE STANDARD LOW-BETA MARKER. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, and suppose 1<=beta<=6/5-2kappa. Let Q>=1, B=Q^beta, H_T=B/Q, and S_0=H_T^2Q^{3sigma}. Suppose a normalized marked integer n lies in a fixed dyadic support c_BB<=n<=C_BB with c_B,C_B>0. Then there is a constant Q_0=Q_0(kappa,c_B) such that for Q>=Q_0 one has n>S_0. Hence the C0 condition n<=S_0 in fact a71f777ad842c886 is empty on every standard low-beta layer of sufficiently large normalized base
8bf5ca45f71b8c2c.author: slava chan
8bf5ca45f71b8c2c.statement:
C0 DICHOTOMY FOR THE STANDARD LOW-BETA MARKER. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, and suppose 1<=beta<=6/5-2kappa. Let Q>=1, B=Q^beta, H_T=B/Q, and S_0=H_T^2Q^{3sigma}. Suppose a normalized marked integer n lies in a fixed dyadic support c_BB<=n<=C_BB with c_B,C_B>0. Then there is a constant Q_0=Q_0(kappa,c_B) such that for Q>=Q_0 one has n>S_0. Hence the C0 condition n<=S_0 in fact a71f777ad842c886 is empty on every standard low-beta layer of sufficiently large normalized base.
For the remaining bounded-base layers, assume the literal source scales satisfy x>=3, D>=c_Dx^{1/2}(log x)^{-A_D}, R<=C_Rx, g=D/Q is a positive integer, and all hypotheses of the exact-g l1 fact 8346861a976aa604. If 1<=Q<Q_0, then the complete exact-g nonzero-Poisson l1 mass is O(x^{1/2}(log x)^{A_D+2}), with constants depending on the fixed data. In particular every C0 subfamily is O(x^{1/2+epsilon}) for every epsilon>0. Thus the standard C0/small-normalized-base complement is power-saving and does not require a reciprocal trace theorem.
8bf5ca45f71b8c2c.proof:
Since H_T=Q^{beta-1},
S_0=Q^{2beta-2+3sigma},
and therefore
B/S_0=Q^{2-beta-3sigma}.
The beta range gives
2-beta-3sigma>=4/5+2kappa-3kappa/100>4/5.
Thus c_BB>S_0 once Q is larger than a constant depending only on c_B and kappa. Since n>=c_BB, the C0 inequality n<=S_0 is impossible. This proves the large-base assertion.
Now suppose Q<Q_0. Put B=R/g=RQ/D. The source scale bounds give
B<=C_Rc_D^{-1}Qx^{1/2}(log x)^{A_D}.
Fact 8346861a976aa604 bounds the complete exact-g nonzero-Poisson l1 mass by O(QB(log x)^2). Since Q<Q_0, this is
O(x^{1/2}(log x)^{A_D+2}).
A C0 leaf is obtained by deleting indices from the complete exact-g coefficient family, so its absolute value is no larger. Finally every fixed logarithmic power is O(x^epsilon), proving the stated power saving.

glossary.A_D: The fixed logarithmic balance exponent in the lower bound for D.
glossary.C_B: The fixed upper dyadic-support constant for the normalized marked factor.
glossary.Q_0: A fixed threshold above which the standard C0 leaf is empty.
glossary.c_B: The fixed lower dyadic-support constant for the normalized marked factor.

8d3b2d43277f6d33.title: EXACT FIRST LITERAL SMALL-CROSS-GCD SLOPE TRANSFORM WITH BOTH ADDITIVE TENSORS AND ITS REQUIRED SAVING
8d3b2d43277f6d33.author: slava chan
8d3b2d43277f6d33.proof:
Equations (12)--(13) are the exact primewise additive-subface expansions of the two interval tensors. The zero extensions (11) insert precisely the support conditions \((au,ps)=1\) and \((au,pq)=1\); hence every inverse displayed in (12)--(13) is defined on every nonzero summand.

Fix p, tau, and a. For \(s\in\mathcal S_p,q\in\mathcal Q_p\), the literal residues in fact b9560e346963b9e0 are
\[
 A=N[u_1s]^{-1},\qquad D=N[u_2q]^{-1}\pmod p. \tag{28}
\]
On the support (11), N, \(u_1s\), and \(u_2q\) are units modulo p. Therefore
\[
 A=D\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 u_1s\equiv u_2q\pmod p
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 u_2\equiv sq^{-1}u_1\pmod p. \tag{29}
\]
Thus the final factor of (22) is exactly
\[
 G_{sq^{-1}}(u_1\bmod p,u_2\bmod p)
 ={p\over p-1}\left(
 \mathbf1_{u_2\equiv sq^{-1}u_1\ ({\rm mod}\ p)}
 -{1\over p-1}\right). \tag{30}
\]
The definitions (2)--(3) are exactly the two beta families, label set, and a-ranges of fact b9560e346963b9e0. Substitute (14)--(15) into the abstract aggregate of fact 674a62f128f05a44. Equations (29)--(30) show term by term that it is (22), with precisely the same w, beta, gamma, tensor, support, and directed-incidence data. Formula (21) is equation (7) of that fact with \(G=G_R\), and formula (23) is its equation (6).

The triangle inequality in (23) proves that (24) is sufficient. The divisor bound applied to (2)--(3) and the hypothesis on w give \(|\beta_{\tau,a}(u)|\le Q^{\varepsilon+o(1)}\). Fact 39071136bb037885 therefore applies to the literal sets in (7), the coefficient hypothesis (6), and the support (11). Its remainder conclusion is exactly (25). Its equation (8), at G=1, gives the first expression in (26). When \(P^2\le Q\), the first term dominates the second, and substitution of \(B=Q^{4/3+o(1)}\) gives the second expression. Dividing the target in (24) by (26) gives (27).

Finally, character dependence is visible in the two transforms in (18). The last applicability and no-fit statements are exactly the conclusions of facts 6ab529accdede090 and f271bfac142ef5e0.

glossary.C_{p,s}(n): The zero-extended complete row-one shifted interval tensor.
glossary.J_{p,q}(n): The zero-extended complete row-two boundary interval tensor.
glossary.\\Lambda_{p,\\tau,a}(\\chi): The nonprincipal character transform of the literal slope weights.
glossary.\\lambda_{p,\\tau,a,c}(\\chi): The exact literal slope-c weight after both retained row tensors are projected to character chi.
glossary.\\mathcal K_{G,<}(P): The centered J2 remainder component in the small-cross-gcd range of a dyadic prime block.
glossary.\\mathcal Q_p: The row-two complementary cofactors containing the directed incidence prime p.
glossary.\\mathcal S_p: The row-one complementary cofactors attached to canonical prime p.
glossary.\\varkappa(d,m): The symmetry multiplicity in the literal long-long Vaughan coefficient.

8d42885a3d224404.title: BANKS--SHARLINSKI LEMMA 11: EXACT DOUBLE-MOBIUS DIRECT SUBSTITUTION AND STRICT-TOP EXPONENT NO-FIT. Fix one projective box in the additive-reciprocity normal form of fact ecd6325d7ef2bc37. Thus q is on a standard dyadic interval of scale Q, n is on a standard dyadic interval of scale B=Q^beta, (q,n)=1, the source target L_src is a nonzero integer, epsilon is in {-1,1}, and
8d42885a3d224404.author: slava chan
8d42885a3d224404.statement:
BANKS--SHARLINSKI LEMMA 11: EXACT DOUBLE-MOBIUS DIRECT SUBSTITUTION AND STRICT-TOP EXPONENT NO-FIT. Fix one projective box in the additive-reciprocity normal form of fact ecd6325d7ef2bc37. Thus q is on a standard dyadic interval of scale Q, n is on a standard dyadic interval of scale B=Q^beta, (q,n)=1, the source target L_src is a nonzero integer, epsilon is in {-1,1}, and
\[
 \alpha_q=\mu(q)A(q){\bf1}_{(g,q)=1},\qquad
 \gamma_n=\mu(n)C(n){\bf1}_{(g,n)=1},
 \qquad |A(q)|,|C(n)|\leq1.
\]
Let H_P be the physical Poisson scale inherited from that fact. Fix one sign of h and one dyadic block F<=|h|<2F with F<=H_P. Let E be supported on that signed block and let
\[
 {\cal V}_F(E)=\|E\|_\infty+
 \sum_{h,h+\sigma_h\text{ in the block}}|E(h+\sigma_h)-E(h)|
 \leq1,
 \qquad \sigma_h\in\{-1,1\}.
\]
Define
\[
 T_F={1\over H_P}
 \sum_{q\asymp Q}\sum_{\substack{n\asymp B\\(q,n)=1}}
 \alpha_q\gamma_n
 \sum_{F\leq |h|<2F}E(h)
 e_n(\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\overline q).                 \tag{1}
\]
A direct application of Banks--Shparlinski, arXiv:1411.1820, Lemma 11, after an exact signed-set decomposition of both bounded coefficient arrays, gives
\[
 |T_F|\ll
 \left(Q^{1/2}B^{11/8}+Q^{4/5}B^{23/20}\right)B^{o(1)}. \tag{2}
\]
The estimate is uniform in the two signs of h and retains both literal Möbius factors, every individual gcd gate, the cross-coprimality gate, and the fixed possibly nonunit target. The theorem's linear coefficient is zero, its reciprocal coefficient is epsilon L_src h, its inverse variable is q, and its modulus variable is n.

With B=Q^beta, the two powers of Q on the right of (2) are
\[
 {1\over2}+{11\beta\over8},
 \qquad
 {4\over5}+{23\beta\over20}.                              \tag{3}
\]
They are both below 2 only under, respectively,
\[
 \beta<{12\over11},\qquad \beta<{24\over23}.             \tag{4}
\]
More generally, they are both below 2-delta only under
\[
 \beta<{12\over11}-{8\delta\over11},\qquad
 \beta<{24\over23}-{20\delta\over23}.                     \tag{5}
\]
Consequently, throughout the scoped strict-top chamber
\[
 \max\{\beta_m,7/6\}<\beta<6/5,                          \tag{6}
\]
the displayed Banks--Shparlinski right-hand side does not furnish DOUBLE-MU-RECIP-N with any fixed positive saving. This is only a no-fit for this exact direct theorem insertion. It is not a lower bound for T_F and does not exclude cancellation from the actual joint Möbius signs, simultaneous denominator dispersion, another decomposition, or a source-linked vector estimate. It proves no strict-top payment, endpoint statement, post-A conclusion, or Goldbach conclusion.
8d42885a3d224404.proof:
Banks--Shparlinski Lemma 11 is reproduced, with its full hypotheses, in accepted fact 06aa6fe1a991b7b5. In that theorem set
\[
 m=q,\quad n=n,\quad M_{BS}\asymp Q,\quad N_{BS}\asymp B,
 \quad a=0,\quad b=\epsilon L_{\rm src}h.                \tag{7}
\]
The strict-top ordering Q<B verifies M_BS<=N_BS, the hypothesis |a|M_BS<=N_BS is automatic, and b is nonzero because L_src and h are nonzero. A fixed source dyadic interval is an admissible fixed choice of the moving interval in that lemma; the harmless endpoint conventions are handled by a constant number of half-open interval pieces.

We first prove that its arbitrary-set form retains the literal coefficients. For every complex z with |z|<=1,
\[
 z=\int_0^1({\bf1}_{\Re z>t}-{\bf1}_{\Re z<-t})\,dt
 +i\int_0^1({\bf1}_{\Im z>t}-{\bf1}_{\Im z<-t})\,dt.   \tag{8}
\]
Apply (8) to z=alpha_q and independently to z=gamma_n. Their product is therefore an exact double integral of sixteen arbitrary-set products, with scalar coefficients of modulus one. The conditions (g,q)=1 and (g,n)=1 are already part of these sets, while (q,n)=1 is precisely the coprimality condition in Lemma 11. Thus the theorem applies termwise and integration costs only an absolute constant. This retains mu(q)mu(n); no absolute value is taken before the theorem is used.

The target-size factor in Lemma 11 is harmless on F<=H_P. In the forward orientation, the source relations used in fact ecd6325d7ef2bc37 give
\[
 H_P=B/M,\qquad L_{\rm src}\asymp QM,
\]
and in the reverse orientation they give
\[
 H_P=B/K,\qquad L_{\rm src}\asymp QK.
\]
Hence in either orientation
\[
 {|L_{\rm src}h|\over QB}\ll {|h|\over H_P}\ll1.        \tag{9}
\]
Therefore the factor (1+|b|/(M_BS N_BS))^{1/4} is bounded. The |a|J M_BS/N_BS term vanishes because a=0.

For fixed h, use the full-density bounds for the two arbitrary sets. Lemma 11 then gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \left|\sum_{q\asymp Q}\sum_{\substack{n\asymp B\\(q,n)=1}}
 \alpha_q\gamma_n e_n(\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\overline q)\right|
 &\ll (QB)^{1/2}
 \left(B^{7/8}+Q^{3/10}B^{13/20}\right)B^{o(1)}\\
 &=\left(Q^{1/2}B^{11/8}
 +Q^{4/5}B^{23/20}\right)B^{o(1)}.                         \tag{10}
 \end{aligned}
\]
The signed block contains O(F) integers and |E(h)|<=1 by the variation hypothesis. Summing (10) against |E(h)| and dividing by H_P multiplies its right-hand side by O(F/H_P), which is O(1). This proves (2), identically for sigma_h=1 and sigma_h=-1 because the external theorem is uniform in the nonzero integer b and its bound depends on |b|.

Substituting B=Q^beta in (2) gives (3). Solving
\[
 1/2+11\beta/8<2-\delta,
 \qquad
 4/5+23\beta/20<2-\delta
\]
gives (5), and delta=0 gives (4). Since 7/6 exceeds both 12/11 and 24/23, neither term on the displayed theorem right-hand side is below Q^2 in (6). An upper bound larger than the required target does not imply a lower bound for the actual source sum; it only establishes the stated direct-insertion no-fit.

glossary.M_BS: The inverse-variable scale in Banks--Shparlinski Lemma 11.
glossary.N_BS: The modulus-variable scale in Banks--Shparlinski Lemma 11.
glossary.T_F: One normalized signed h-block after the additive-reciprocity handoff.
glossary.alpha_q: The complete bounded q-coefficient mu(q)A(q) with its individual gcd gate.
glossary.gamma_n: The complete bounded n-coefficient mu(n)C(n) with its individual gcd gate.

8d9feea8c44da2c8.title: EXACT ORIENTATION-NEUTRAL CRITICAL-ROW DESCENT AND THE FIRST SAME-MASK ZERO-MODE OBSTRUCTION. Work in one fixed selected same-N post-low critical-W source atom covered by facts 3f2f255ea6845a50 and e55b27d39c593164, after the old marker leaf and every marker-dependent descendant have been legally recombined by fact a71f777ad842c886. Let g=(d,r), write d=ga and r=gb, and put L_src=N/g. In the forward orientation set
8d9feea8c44da2c8.author: slava chan
8d9feea8c44da2c8.statement:
EXACT ORIENTATION-NEUTRAL CRITICAL-ROW DESCENT AND THE FIRST SAME-MASK ZERO-MODE OBSTRUCTION. Work in one fixed selected same-N post-low critical-W source atom covered by facts 3f2f255ea6845a50 and e55b27d39c593164, after the old marker leaf and every marker-dependent descendant have been legally recombined by fact a71f777ad842c886. Let g=(d,r), write d=ga and r=gb, and put L_src=N/g. In the forward orientation set
s=a, n=b, t=m, u=k, Q=D/g, B=R/g, G=M/Q, T=M;
in the reverse orientation set
s=b, n=a, t=k, u=m, Q=R/g, B=D/g, G=K/Q, T=K.
In either orientation the literal physical equation is
s t+n u=L_src,                                                    (1)
with s asymptotic to Q, n asymptotic to B, T=GQ, and
K_sh=GQ^(2-beta), B=Q^beta.                                      (2)
Put
c=gcd(s,L_src), s=cq, L_src=c ell.                               (3)
Then c divides u. Writing u=c kappa gives exactly
q t+kappa n=ell.                                                  (4)
Moreover
Q_c=Q/c, K_c=K_sh/c, q asymptotic to Q_c,
kappa asymptotic to K_c, t asymptotic to T, n asymptotic to B,    (5)
and on the positive compact source support
ell=N/(gc) asymptotic to Q_c T asymptotic to B K_c.               (6)
The squarefree outer-gcd coefficient descends exactly as
mu(s)mu(n)=mu(c)mu(q)mu(n),                                      (7)
where c,q,n are pairwise coprime. The two source logarithms become, in both orientations,
log(t)log(c kappa).                                               (8)
The orientation-specific smooth physical weight is
W(gcq/D,t/M,gn/R,c kappa/K)                                      (9F)
in the forward orientation and
W(gn/D,c kappa/M,gcq/R,t/K)                                      (9R)
in the reverse orientation. Every target-gcd, fixed-U, high, source, parent, ordering, equality, collision, deletion, provenance, frozen-parent and projective label that survives the legal marker recombination is transported literally by the bijection (3)-(4); no such mask is discarded by this descent.

There is an exact zero-mode scope statement. For fixed outer data s,n and a smooth compactly supported physical amplitude F(t), completion of the whole progression st+nu=L_src and Poisson summation in t has zero mode
Z_{s,n}(F)=n^(-1) integral_R F(y)dy.                              (10)
If a surviving mask is outer data, it multiplies both the physical row and (10). If a surviving t- or u-dependent factor has a specified smooth compactly supported extension Psi along u=(L_src-st)/n, then its same-mask zero mode is
Z_{s,n}(Psi F)=n^(-1) integral_R
 Psi((L_src-sy)/n)F(y)dy.                                        (11)
Thus the complete nonzero-frequency row is exactly the physical source carrying that same smooth mask minus (11).

However, the cited accepted facts prove exact sibling recombination only for the old marker descendants. They retain, rather than recombine, the other source, ordering, equality, collision, deletion and provenance masks. A zero-one deletion or other factor specified only on the integer source solutions has no canonical real extension and therefore no canonical same-mask zero mode: two smooth extensions agreeing at all supported integer solutions may have different integrals in (11). Consequently the accepted ledger presently licenses (1)-(9) with all surviving masks transported literally, but it does not by itself license replacing the complete critical nonzero-frequency row by one physical row minus a same-mask zero mode until each t- or u-dependent discrete mask has either been recombined to the complete progression or furnished with a specified smooth extension and its own zero-mode analysis. This is the first mask-compatibility obstruction to applying a max-residue Mobius Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem to the full literal critical row. No Bombieri-Vinogradov estimate, complementary-range estimate, critical-tail payment, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
8d9feea8c44da2c8.proof:
Because mu(d)mu(r) is nonzero, fact a71f777ad842c886 proves that g,a,b are pairwise coprime and squarefree and that, after exact recombination of all old marker descendants, the coefficient is mu(s)mu(n), where {s,n}={a,b}. In the forward orientation the normalized source equation am+bk=L_src is (1) under the displayed assignments. In the reverse orientation it is the same equation after interchanging the two divisor-complement pairs, again giving (1).

Let c=(s,L_src). From st+nu=L_src, c divides nu. Since c divides s and (s,n)=1, one has (c,n)=1; hence c divides u. Substitution of s=cq, L_src=c ell and u=c kappa into (1), followed by division by c, proves (4). Conversely every integer solution of (4) gives the unique source solution of (1) by these substitutions, so all masks and labels can be transported literally and no multiplicity is introduced.

Since s is squarefree, its complementary divisors c and q are coprime. Both are also coprime to n because (s,n)=1. Multiplicativity therefore gives mu(s)=mu(c)mu(q), proving (7). Equation (8) follows because the original logarithms are log(m)log(k): forward has (m,k)=(t,c kappa), while reverse has (m,k)=(c kappa,t), and multiplication is commutative. Substitution d=ga=gcq, r=gb=gn, m=t, k=c kappa in the forward weight proves (9F). Substitution d=ga=gn, m=c kappa, r=gb=gcq, k=t in the reverse weight proves (9R).

For the scales, forward has s=a asymptotic to D/g=Q, n=b asymptotic to R/g=B, and t=m asymptotic to M=T=GQ. Also DM and RK are comparable to N, so K is comparable to DM/R=(gQ)(GQ)/(gB)=GQ^(2-beta)=K_sh; hence u=k is asymptotic to K_sh. Reverse has s=b asymptotic to R/g=Q, n=a asymptotic to D/g=B, t=k asymptotic to K=T=GQ, and M is comparable to RK/D=(gQ)(GQ)/(gB)=K_sh; hence u=m is asymptotic to K_sh. Dividing s and u by c proves (5). The compact positive support and (4) show ell is comparable to each of qt and kappa n and to their sum; the preceding scales give qt asymptotic to Q_c T and kappa n asymptotic to BK_c. This proves (6).

Fact df9748efe29ab475 supplies Poisson summation in the complete physical source progression with every smooth physical factor included in its one-variable amplitude. The elementary progression-Poisson identity recorded with its precise deletion scope in fact 7670948dedd78714 gives (10). Replacing F(y) by the specified smooth function Psi((L_src-sy)/n)F(y) gives (11), and separating the zero frequency proves the asserted physical-source-minus-zero-mode identity.

Finally, fact a71f777ad842c886 says exactly that the marker operation changes only mu(n) and leaves all listed masks unchanged; it does not give sibling identities for those other masks. Fact 7670948dedd78714 proves that a deletion given only on integer progression points has no canonical real zero alias. Concretely, because only finitely many integers lie in the compact support, one may add to any smooth extension a nonzero smooth bump supported in a small interval avoiding those integers; the values on every supported integer remain unchanged while its integral changes. Applied to the progression parameter, this changes (11). Therefore the final obstruction follows from the exact scope of the cited recombination and Poisson facts.

glossary.T: The long complement scale, M forward and K reverse.
glossary.Z_{s,n}(F): The zero Poisson mode of the complete physical progression with smooth amplitude F.
glossary.c: The exact greatest common divisor of s and L_src.
glossary.n: The normalized marked factor in the orientation-neutral equation: b forward and a reverse.
glossary.s: The normalized source coefficient in the orientation-neutral equation: a forward and b reverse.
glossary.t: The long physical complement: m forward and k reverse.
glossary.u: The short physical complement: k forward and m reverse.

8e7d9e9ad0eff274.title: COMPLETE ABSOLUTE SCALAR-TENSOR PAYMENT FOR EVERY SELECTED-p p-DIVIDES-C STRICT-TOP C1 ROW. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100 and beta_m=6/5-12sigma/5, fix 0<eta_G<sigma, an integer 1<=r<=4, and sufficiently large Q. For each 1<=i<=r fix an actual strict-top scalar marker-copy row with q-variable Q<=q_i<2Q, marked integer B_i/2<=n_i<=2B_i where B_i=Q^(beta_i) and beta_m<beta_i<6/5, nonzero height h_i, physical scale H_{P,i}>0, and literal scalar coefficient c_i satisfying, for every fixed A>=2 and epsilon_0>0,
8e7d9e9ad0eff274.author: slava chan
8e7d9e9ad0eff274.statement:
COMPLETE ABSOLUTE SCALAR-TENSOR PAYMENT FOR EVERY SELECTED-p p-DIVIDES-C STRICT-TOP C1 ROW. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100 and beta_m=6/5-12sigma/5, fix 0<eta_G<sigma, an integer 1<=r<=4, and sufficiently large Q. For each 1<=i<=r fix an actual strict-top scalar marker-copy row with q-variable Q<=q_i<2Q, marked integer B_i/2<=n_i<=2B_i where B_i=Q^(beta_i) and beta_m<beta_i<6/5, nonzero height h_i, physical scale H_{P,i}>0, and literal scalar coefficient c_i satisfying, for every fixed A>=2 and epsilon_0>0,
|c_i(q_i,n_i,h_i)|<=C_{A,epsilon_0}Q^epsilon_0(1+|h_i|/H_{P,i})^(-A).  (1)
Let D be any complex joint mask with |D|<=1, including any exact first-prime pair masks and pair or tuple deletions, and define
T_r=(product_i H_{P,i}^(-1)) sum D product_i c_i(q_i,n_i,h_i),
where the sum is over all displayed row supports and any further literal restrictions.

Assume one distinguished row j is a literal strict-top C1 row with n_j=p_jv_j squarefree, p_j its unique rough prime, gcd(p_j,v_j)=1, C_j=mathscr A h_j, and p_j divides C_j. Assume this same p_j is the prescribed first-nonresonant prime in a nonzero active exact pair mask, and its actual scales satisfy G_j>=Q^(-sigma+eta_G), H_{P,j}=Q^(beta_j-1)/G_j, and p_j>=Q^(3/2-beta_j-3sigma). Then, for every E>0,
|T_r|<<_E Q^(-E).                                                (2)
This conclusion is independent of m_eff,j. Thus every actual two-row or four-row scalar suboccupancy containing a selected-p p-divides-C C1 row is arbitrarily power-small with all joint masks retained. No additional vector-valued Hilbert/completion object is estimated.
8e7d9e9ad0eff274.proof:
The active prescribed-p_j mask is the exact mask of fact ff228b0e569531f8 and contains the nonzero factor
1_{p_j does not divide mathscr A Delta}.
If p_j divided mathscr A, this factor would vanish for every integer Delta. Hence p_j does not divide mathscr A. The hypothesis p_j divides C_j=mathscr A h_j and primality of p_j now imply
p_j divides h_j.                                                  (3)

The actual scale assumptions give
H_{P,j}<=Q^(beta_j-1+sigma-eta_G),
so
p_j/H_{P,j}>=Q^(5/2-2beta_j-4sigma+eta_G)>Q^(9/100),             (4)
using beta_j<6/5 and 4sigma<=1/2500. This is the scale calculation verified in fact ed8954118b71276a and does not use any effective-modulus hypothesis.

Fact 3286b0e75a3ea94a proves (1). For an ordinary row, direct comparison with an integral gives
H_{P,i}^(-1)sum_{h_i!=0}(1+|h_i|/H_{P,i})^(-A)<<_A1.            (5)
For the distinguished row, (3) lets us write h_j=k p_j. Equations (3)-(4) give
H_{P,j}^(-1)sum_{k!=0}(1+|k|p_j/H_{P,j})^(-A)
 <<_A p_j^(-1)(p_j/H_{P,j})^(1-A)
 <<_A Q^(-(9/100)(A-1)).                                        (6)
There are O(QB_i) choices of q_i,n_i in row i and B_i<Q^(6/5). Taking absolute values, discarding D and every further restriction, and factoring the resulting majorant therefore gives
|T_r|<<_{A,epsilon_0}Q^(44/5+r epsilon_0-(9/100)(A-1)),          (7)
exactly as in the absolute aggregation proof of fact 727e54e160fb7774. Given E, choose the fixed integration-by-parts order A so large that the exponent in (7) is below -E-1. This proves (2). No property of m_eff,j was used, and no vector-valued completion entered the absolute scalar tensor.

8eb30e55bdef6b27.title: DISJOINT FIXED-SLACK A-PROCESS REFINEMENT OF THE MULTI-FREE ROUTING. Fix constants 0<kappa<=1/100, rho>0, delta>0, and an integer K_0>=2. Let Q be sufficiently large. Let n be squarefree, let C be an integer, let c be squarefree, and put
8eb30e55bdef6b27.author: slava chan
8eb30e55bdef6b27.statement:
DISJOINT FIXED-SLACK A-PROCESS REFINEMENT OF THE MULTI-FREE ROUTING. Fix constants 0<kappa<=1/100, rho>0, delta>0, and an integer K_0>=2. Let Q be sufficiently large. Let n be squarefree, let C be an integer, let c be squarefree, and put
m_eff=n/gcd(C,n).
Assume
Q^(1/2+kappa)<=m_eff<=Q^(6/5),  nc<=Q^K_0.                     (1)
Write
theta_eff=log(m_eff)/log(Q),  eta=kappa/20,
a=max{2eta,1-theta_eff+4eta},
b=min{theta_eff-4eta,1-theta_eff/2-4eta}.                       (2)
Let W be extended by zero, supported on Q<=q<2Q, and satisfy V_Q(W)<=Q^epsilon for every fixed epsilon>0.

Use the exact finite truncated-inverse expansion and dyadic subdivision of fact df45be7aead3cec9. Thus each still-unpaid MULTI-FREE box has a fixed finite list of factor positions; a fixed maximal carrier of dyadic scale P<Q^a contains every Möbius-bearing factor; and r>=2 omitted nonunit positions are coefficient-one factors of dyadic scales B_1,...,B_r, each larger than Q^(b-a-o(1)). The product of all positions has Q-scale.

For one such box define
B_* = max{B_i:1<=i<=r},
and use the earliest position in a fixed ordering to break a tie. Let A be the dyadic scale of the product of all other positions, so A B_* is comparable to Q.

Define A-PAID(delta,rho) to consist of the boxes for which there exists a factorization
m_eff=m_0 m_1                                                     (3)
such that
m_1<=B_* Q^(-2(delta+rho)),
Q^(4(delta+rho))<=m_0<=B_*^2 Q^(-4(delta+rho)).                 (4)
Because m_eff is squarefree, m_0 and m_1 are coprime. Choose the least eligible m_1 as a deterministic witness. Then every A-PAID(delta,rho) box is bounded by
Q^(1-delta)                                                       (5)
after increasing Q in terms of the fixed parameters. The literal W, the complete gate (q,nc)=1, the reduction of the possibly nonunit numerator C to a unit numerator modulo m_eff, and every sign and factor position are retained.

Define A-ROUTING RESIDUAL(delta,rho) by the exact complementary condition: for every factorization (3), at least one of
m_1>B_* Q^(-2(delta+rho)),
m_0<Q^(4(delta+rho)),
m_0>B_*^2 Q^(-4(delta+rho))                                    (6)
holds. It is enough to test B_*: failure of (4) for B_* implies failure for every smaller omitted scale. Therefore the ordered classes
MEDIUM, original TYPE I, A-PAID(delta,rho), A-ROUTING RESIDUAL(delta,rho)
are disjoint and exhaustive, and no sum over factorizations of m_eff is introduced.

For a literal strict-top C1 specialization, assume additionally that beta_m<=beta<6/5, sigma=kappa/100, n=pv is the squarefree C1 factorization with p the unique rough prime, gcd(p,v)=1, every prime divisor of v at most L=Q^(beta-1+sigma), and C=mathscr A h. If m_eff and B_* are respectively comparable to Q and Q^(1/2), then, for sufficiently small fixed delta,rho>0, the balanced two-free cell is A-PAID unless
p does not divide C,  m_eff=p r_eff,  r_eff<m_eff^(1/40).       (7)
In particular p divides C is fully A-PAID on that balanced cell. General unbalanced boxes may remain in (6) even when m_eff has a divisor in a fixed factor window. This theorem makes no estimate for (6), for the class (7), for 1<m_eff<Q^(1/2+kappa), or for m_eff=1.
8eb30e55bdef6b27.proof:
Fact df45be7aead3cec9 supplies the finite expansion, the paid MEDIUM and original TYPE I classes, and the stated MULTI-FREE anatomy under hypotheses (1)-(2). Fix one MULTI-FREE dyadic box. Its factor positions and dyadic scales are fixed before summation. Choose the B_*-position by the stated deterministic rule. Convolve the carrier and every omitted position other than B_* into one integer variable a. The number of positions is bounded in terms of kappa. Hence the resulting coefficient alpha_a is bounded by a fixed divisor function. The selected integer variable b retains coefficient one. After a bounded further dyadic subdivision, a has scale A, b has scale B_*, and A B_* is comparable to Q. The function W(ab), the gate (ab,nc)=1, and the reciprocal phase are unchanged. This is the input shape of fact 629ed652df233d7b.

Fix an eligible factorization (3). Apply equation (1) of fact 629ed652df233d7b with B=B_*. Since A is comparable to Q/B_*, the three bracketed contributions after multiplication by A, divided by Q, are bounded up to an absolute dyadic constant by
(m_1/B_*)^(1/2),  m_0^(-1/4),  (m_0/B_*^2)^(1/4).              (8)
Conditions (4) bound all three quantities in (8) by Q^(-delta-rho). The variation, divisor, and epsilon factors in the cited theorem are Q^o(1): V_Q(W)<=Q^epsilon for every fixed epsilon, nc<=Q^K_0, m_eff<=Q^(6/5), A B_* is comparable to Q, and all relevant divisor functions have fixed order. For sufficiently large Q their product is at most Q^rho. Thus the complete box is at most Q^(1-delta), proving (5).

Condition (6) is the literal logical negation of the existence condition (4), so it is exactly the set-theoretic complement of the defined A-PAID class. No necessity claim about the numerical size of the actual weighted sum is made. If B is a smaller omitted scale, both upper bounds m_1<=B Q^(-2(delta+rho)) and m_0<=B^2 Q^(-4(delta+rho)) are at least as restrictive as for B_*, while the lower bound on m_0 is unchanged. Hence eligibility of any omitted position implies eligibility of B_*. This proves the largest-position reduction. Removing MEDIUM and original TYPE I first, then using the existence dichotomy (4)/(6), and selecting one witness rather than summing witnesses proves disjointness and exhaustiveness.

For the strict-top C1 corollary, fact da9b97f255e8bc97 applies under the additional hypotheses stated here. It gives, except exactly for (7), a divisor m_1 satisfying
m_eff^(1/40)<=m_1<=m_eff^(19/40).                               (9)
Put m_0=m_eff/m_1. When m_eff is comparable to Q and B_* is comparable to Q^(1/2), equations (9) give
m_1<=Q^(1/2-1/40+o(1)),
Q^(1/2+1/40+o(1))<=m_0<=Q^(1-1/40+o(1)).                       (10)
Choose fixed delta,rho>0 with 4(delta+rho)<1/40. Equations (10) imply (4) for sufficiently large Q. Therefore the balanced cell is A-PAID outside (7). If p divides C, fact da9b97f255e8bc97 always supplies (9), proving the final p-divides-C claim. No conclusion about the complementary classes is used.

glossary.A-ROUTING RESIDUAL: The exact set-theoretic complement, inside MULTI-FREE, of the boxes assigned to the fixed-slack A-process criterion.
glossary.B_*: The largest dyadic scale among the omitted coefficient-one positions of a fixed MULTI-FREE box.

8ef886f6d36920d0.title: LITERAL RESIDUE-CLASS MULTIPLICITY LEDGER IN THE ALIASING PMD RANGE
8ef886f6d36920d0.author: slava chan
8ef886f6d36920d0.statement:
LITERAL RESIDUE-CLASS MULTIPLICITY LEDGER IN THE ALIASING PMD RANGE.

Fix an integer J>=1 and real numbers kappa,sigma satisfying
  0<kappa<1/10,  0<=sigma<3kappa.
Let Q be sufficiently large, and let H,V be positive real numbers with
  1<=H<=Q^(1/3-kappa),
  2<=V<=H^2Q^sigma,
  V>=H.                                                     (1)
Put
  P=QH/V
and assume P>=2. Let cal P be any set of primes p in [P,2P). Let xi_v be supported on integers V<=v<2V and satisfy
  |xi_v|<=tau_J(v),
where tau_J is the J-fold divisor function.

For every v in [V,2V), s modulo v, and p in cal P, let b_{v,s,p}(q) be complex coefficients supported on integers Q<=q<2Q not divisible by p, with |b_{v,s,p}(q)|<=1. Define
 mu_{v,s,p}=max_{a modulo p}
   #{q:Q<=q<2Q, b_{v,s,p}(q) nonzero, q congruent a modulo p},       (2)
 N_{v,s,p}=sum_q|b_{v,s,p}(q)|^2,                                  (3)
and define the squared residue-multiplicity ledger
 R_mult=sum_{V<=v<2V}sum_{s modulo v}|xi_v/v|^2
          sum_{p in cal P}mu_{v,s,p}^2 N_{v,s,p}^2.                 (4)
Then, for every epsilon>0,
 R_mult<<_{J,epsilon}(QV)^epsilon
       [P Q^2+Q^3+Q^4/P]                                          (5)
 <<_{J,epsilon}(QV)^epsilon Q^3(V/H)                               (6)
 <=Q^(10/3-kappa+sigma+epsilon).                                  (7)
In particular, after choosing epsilon sufficiently small,
