 R_mult<<Q^(4-eta_alias)                                          (8)
for some eta_alias=eta_alias(kappa,sigma)>0; one may take any
 eta_alias<2/3+kappa-sigma.

The scale mu^2 N^2 is forced by the congruent-support obstruction. In the rank-one configuration of fact 9b8cce52a98d22c8 with M supported q-values in one residue class, one has
  mu=M,  N=M,  mu^2N^2=M^4,                                      (9)
while its singleton-window, all-shift D=0-subtracted remainder is (1+o(1))M^4 along the growing realization in that fact. Thus a general short-window theorem that covers residue aliasing cannot omit a term of this size. Equations (5)-(8) show that the literal interval source pays this forced multiplicity scale throughout the PMD range V>=H. This fact is only the multiplicity ledger; it does not prove the remaining signed shifted-fourth-moment estimate.
8ef886f6d36920d0.proof: An interval of real length Q contains at most 1+Q/p integers in any fixed residue class modulo p. Therefore, uniformly in v,s,p, mu_{v,s,p}<=1+Q/p<=1+Q/P. (10) There are at most Q+1 integers in [Q,2Q), so Q sufficiently large and |b|<=1 give N_{v,s,p}<=Q+1<=2Q. (11) The set cal P contains at most 2P primes. Hence, for each fixed v,s, sum_{p in cal P}mu_{v,s,p}^2N_{v,s,p}^2 <=H, the definition P=QH/V gives P<=Q. Consequently P Q^2<=Q^3<=Q^4/P, so (5) is bounded by a constant times (QV)^epsilon Q^4/P=(QV)^epsilon Q^3(V/H), (14) which proves (6). From V<=H^2Q^sigma and H<=Q^(1/3-kappa), V/H<=H Q^sigma<=Q^(1/3-kappa+sigma). (15) Equations (14)-(15) prove (7). Since 4-(10/3-kappa+sigma)=2/3+kappa-sigma, and sigma<3kappa with kappa<1/10 gives 2/3+kappa-sigma>2/3-2kappa>0, one may absorb the factor (QV)^epsilon by choosing epsilon sufficiently small. This proves (8). Finally, in the rank-one configuration of fact 9b8cce52a98d22c8, all M nonzero coefficients equal one and occupy one residue class. Definitions (2)-(3) give mu=M and N=M, proving (9). That fact proves that the D=0-subtracted singleton-window remainder is asymptotic to M^4. Hence the multiplicity scale in (4) exactly matches the obstruction. This establishes the forced-scale and literal-payment assertions without claiming that the multiplicity term by itself proves the full shifted estimate.

glossary.N_{v,s,p}: The squared l2 mass of one q-coefficient row.
glossary.R_mult: The prime- and (v,s)-averaged squared residue-multiplicity ledger.
glossary.eta_alias: A positive exponent saving in the aliasing range.
glossary.mu_{v,s,p}: The maximum number of supported q-values in one residue class modulo p.

8f111039bd9bc8ac.title: Let Q,P≥2 satisfy
8f111039bd9bc8ac.author: slava chan
8f111039bd9bc8ac.statement:
Let Q,P≥2 satisfy
P≤Q^(4/3),   P^(2/3)≤Q.                                      (1)
Let w be a fixed smooth function supported in [1,2]. Then for every ε>0,
Σ_{Q≤q<2Q} max_{gcd(a,q)=1}
 |Σ_{p prime,P≤p<2P,gcd(p,q)=1}w(p/P)e_q(ap^(-1))|
≪_{w,ε}(QP)^ε[
 Q^(11/10)P^(4/5)+Q^(7/6)P^(13/18)+QP^(7/8)
 +Q^(3/2)P^(1/3)+P+QP^(1/2)].                               (2)
The modulus q is arbitrary. This is the auxiliary-length-one endpoint omitted from the hypotheses of fact a0cf2b6037398f9f.
8f111039bd9bc8ac.proof:
Replace the prime indicator by Λ and use the exact Vaughan identity with cutoff U=P^(1/3), exactly as in the proof of fact a0cf2b6037398f9f. In a Type-II block the shorter factor satisfies U≤s≤P^(1/2), and the two lengths are A=P/s and C=s. They are at most Q because A≤P^(2/3)≤Q and C≤P^(1/2)≤Q^(2/3).

Irving, arXiv:1301.6372, Lemma 3.1 with k=3 and k=2 gives
Q^(7/6)P^(5/6)s^(-1/3)+QP^(5/6)s^(1/6),                     (3)
Q^(5/4)P^(3/4)s^(-1/4)+QP^(3/4)s^(1/4).                     (4)
For s<Q^(1/3), the first term of (3) is maximal at s=U and equals
Q^(7/6)P^(13/18).                                            (5)
On Q^(1/3)≤s≤Q^(1/2), the increasing second term of (3) and decreasing first term of (4) meet at s=(Q³/P)^(1/5), with common value
Q^(11/10)P^(4/5).                                            (6)
For s>Q^(1/2), the second term of (4) is at most QP^(7/8). This proves the first three terms in (2).

The Type-I length is at most U=P^(1/3), and the product of the Type-I lengths is P. Irving's Lemma 3.4 gives
P+Q^(3/2)P^(1/3).                                            (7)
Proper prime powers contribute at most (QP)^ε QP^(1/2). Removing the Λ weight and inserting w by partial summation costs only logarithmic factors. Combining (5)-(7) proves (2).

8f9c29373de3486c.title: FIXED-SLACK LOCALIZATION OF UNBALANCED A-ROUTING RESIDUALS TO TWO EDGE STRIPS AND A GENUINE DIVISOR GAP. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100 and use the MULTI-FREE setting of fact 8eb30e55bdef6b27. Put eta=kappa/20, choose delta=rho=kappa/200, and hence put s=delta+rho=kappa/100. Let t=log(m_eff)/log Q, so 1/2+kappa<=t<=6/5, and let a,b be the routing exponents
8f9c29373de3486c.author: slava chan
8f9c29373de3486c.statement:
FIXED-SLACK LOCALIZATION OF UNBALANCED A-ROUTING RESIDUALS TO TWO EDGE STRIPS AND A GENUINE DIVISOR GAP. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100 and use the MULTI-FREE setting of fact 8eb30e55bdef6b27. Put eta=kappa/20, choose delta=rho=kappa/200, and hence put s=delta+rho=kappa/100. Let t=log(m_eff)/log Q, so 1/2+kappa<=t<=6/5, and let a,b be the routing exponents
a=max{2eta,1-t+4eta},
b=min{t-4eta,1-t/2-4eta}.
For every MULTI-FREE box let B_* be its largest omitted coefficient-one scale. Then, for sufficiently large Q, class (R1) of fact 1c42e0c22d9a5cca is empty.

Fix zeta>0. If
3/5+63kappa/250+zeta<=t<=6/5-48kappa/125-zeta,
then class (R2) of that fact is also empty for sufficiently large Q. Consequently every A-ROUTING RESIDUAL box in this middle-effective band belongs to the genuine divisor-gap class (R3): the nonempty interval
[max{Q^(4s),m_eff Q^(2s)/B_*}, B_*^2Q^(-4s)]
contains no divisor of m_eff.
Thus the two pure scale-failure residuals can occur only outside the displayed middle band: the cube-root-short class is confined to the lower and upper effective-exponent edge strips, while the absolute-short class never occurs for this fixed-slack choice. No estimate for the remaining divisor-gap boxes or edge strips is asserted.
8f9c29373de3486c.proof:
Fact 8eb30e55bdef6b27 gives
B_*>Q^(b-a-o(1)).                                               (1)
We first compute b-a. If 1/2+kappa<=t<=2/3, then
a=1-t+4eta, b=t-4eta,
so b-a=2t-1-8eta.                                               (2)
If 2/3<=t<=1+2eta, then
a=1-t+4eta, b=1-t/2-4eta,
so b-a=t/2-8eta.                                                (3)
If 1+2eta<=t<=6/5, then
a=2eta, b=1-t/2-4eta,
so b-a=1-t/2-6eta.                                              (4)
On the first interval (2) is at least 2kappa-8eta=8kappa/5. On the second interval (3) is at least 1/3-8eta, and on the third interval (4) is at least 2/5-6eta. For kappa<=1/100 both latter lower bounds exceed 8kappa/5. Therefore b-a>=8kappa/5 throughout. Since 4s=kappa/25, equation (1) gives B_*>Q^(4s) for sufficiently large Q. By fact 1c42e0c22d9a5cca, (R1) is impossible.

Class (R2) requires B_*^3<m_eff Q^(6s). By (1), it is impossible whenever
3(b-a)>t+6s                                                   (5)
with fixed positive slack. On the first interval, substitution of (2) turns (5) into
5t>3+24eta+6s,
that is
t>3/5+63kappa/250,                                             (6)
because eta=kappa/20 and s=kappa/100. On the second interval, substitution of (3) gives
t/2>24eta+6s,
which holds uniformly there because t/2>=1/3 while 24eta+6s=63kappa/50<=63/5000. On the third interval, substitution of (4) turns (5) into
3-(5/2)t-18eta-6s>0,
that is
t<6/5-48kappa/125.                                             (7)
The fixed margins zeta in the statement make the left side of (5) at least min{5zeta,(5/2)zeta} in the edge pieces; they also absorb the o(1) in (1). Hence (R2) is absent throughout the displayed band for sufficiently large Q.

Fact 1c42e0c22d9a5cca is an exact disjoint partition into (R1), (R2), and (R3). With the first two absent, every residual box is in (R3), whose divisor interval is exactly the one displayed. The complement of the middle band consists of the stated two edge strips. This proves all conclusions.

glossary.middle-effective genuine-gap band: The effective-exponent band on which both pure scale-failure parts of A-ROUTING RESIDUAL are absent.

90c7573be6671013.title: Proposition (scoped no-go for two quadratic-form Bombieri–Vinogradov interfaces at the determinant-carrier scale). Let H tend to infinity. For each integer matrix Q=(a,c;-d,b) with |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|<=H^{3+o(1)}, define F_Q(x,y)=ad x^2-bc y^2. On any nondegenerate slice on which |disc(F_Q)|=|4abcd|=H^{12+o(1)} and |x|,|y|=H^{2+o(1)}, every represented value F_Q(x,y) has size at most H^{10+o(1)}. (1) The range hypotheses in Ditchen's arXiv:1312.1502, Theorems 1.1 and 1.2, fail on this slice, including the conditional Lindelof relaxations stated in Remark 1.6. (2) Lam's arXiv:1812.08823, Proposition 1, does not average over Q or over F_Q: it fixes one primitive positive-definite binary quadratic form and averages auxiliary congruence moduli. (3) Both cited results put primality on the represented integer F(m,n), whereas the determinant carrier requires x and y themselves to be prime and F_Q(x,y) to equal a fixed, generally composite integer. Consequently neither cited theorem, without an additional cross-form transfer theorem changing its quantifiers and primality slots, is an applicable source of a fixed-power saving for the varying det(Q)=ab+cd shell
90c7573be6671013.author: slava chan
90c7573be6671013.statement: Proposition (scoped no-go for two quadratic-form Bombieri–Vinogradov interfaces at the determinant-carrier scale). Let H tend to infinity. For each integer matrix Q=(a,c;-d,b) with |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|<=H^{3+o(1)}, define F_Q(x,y)=ad x^2-bc y^2. On any nondegenerate slice on which |disc(F_Q)|=|4abcd|=H^{12+o(1)} and |x|,|y|=H^{2+o(1)}, every represented value F_Q(x,y) has size at most H^{10+o(1)}. (1) The range hypotheses in Ditchen's arXiv:1312.1502, Theorems 1.1 and 1.2, fail on this slice, including the conditional Lindelof relaxations stated in Remark 1.6. (2) Lam's arXiv:1812.08823, Proposition 1, does not average over Q or over F_Q: it fixes one primitive positive-definite binary quadratic form and averages auxiliary congruence moduli. (3) Both cited results put primality on the represented integer F(m,n), whereas the determinant carrier requires x and y themselves to be prime and F_Q(x,y) to equal a fixed, generally composite integer. Consequently neither cited theorem, without an additional cross-form transfer theorem changing its quantifiers and primality slots, is an applicable source of a fixed-power saving for the varying det(Q)=ab+cd shell.
90c7573be6671013.proof:
For a diagonal binary quadratic form alpha x^2+gamma y^2 the discriminant is -4 alpha gamma. Here alpha=ad and gamma=-bc, so disc(F_Q)=4abcd. The coefficient bounds give |ad|,|bc|<=H^{6+o(1)}. With |x|,|y|=H^{2+o(1)}, the triangle inequality gives |F_Q(x,y)|<=|ad|x^2+|bc|y^2<=H^{10+o(1)}. Thus a theorem covering a critical discriminant slice must permit a discriminant cutoff R=H^{12+o(1)} and a represented-value cutoff X=H^{10+o(1)}.

Ditchen's Theorem 1.1 states an average prime-representation error estimate over negative fundamental discriminants |q|<=R, subject to R^{20/3+epsilon}<=X(log X)^{-B}. At the displayed carrier scales, the left side of the range condition is H^{80+o(1)}, while the right side is at most H^{10+o(1)}; hence the condition fails. Theorem 1.2 requires R^{3+epsilon}<=X(log X)^{-2A-4}, whose left side is H^{36+o(1)}, so it also fails. Remark 1.6 says that, assuming the Lindelof hypothesis for the relevant Rankin–Selberg convolutions, the respective exponents 20/3 and 3 may be replaced by 2 and 1. These relaxed left sides are H^{24+o(1)} and H^{12+o(1)}, still larger than H^{10+o(1)}. This proves (1). Ditchen's definitions additionally restrict the averaged objects to integral primitive positive-definite forms of negative fundamental discriminant and define the counting function using rational primes represented by a form class; those are not the general carrier's form and primality slots.

Lam's Proposition 1 begins: let F be a primitive positive-definite binary quadratic form satisfying stated discriminant restrictions. Its conclusion then sums over auxiliary integers q<X^theta and residue classes of the two input variables modulo q. The form F is outside every displayed summation. The proof fixes the imaginary quadratic field attached to F, converts F(m,n) to norms of ideals in that one field, and invokes Huxley's ray-class Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem. Therefore the theorem's averaging variable is an auxiliary congruence modulus, not a coefficient matrix Q and not the discriminant of F_Q. This proves (2).

Finally, the summands in both published results contain the characteristic function or counting function of rational primes represented as F(m,n). The determinant-carrier equation instead has the form F_Q(x,y)=N with x and y restricted to prime dyadic boxes and N fixed by the carrier invariants; N is not required to be prime. These predicates are logically different and neither implies the other. This proves (3). The final consequence is only the stated scoped applicability conclusion: a result with fixed F or with the failed discriminant/value range and opposite primality predicate cannot by itself instantiate a theorem whose outer variable is the varying determinant shell. Any bridge would have to add precisely those missing quantifiers and slots.

glossary.F_Q: The diagonal integral binary quadratic form F_Q(x,y)=ad x^2-bc y^2.
glossary.H: A positive real carrier-height parameter tending to infinity.
glossary.Q: The integer matrix with rows (a,c) and (-d,b).
glossary.R: The upper bound for absolute discriminants in Ditchen's varying-discriminant theorems.
glossary.X: The upper bound for integers represented by binary quadratic forms in the cited theorems.

90ee649f2811580d.title: CENTERED DILATOR-INVERSE SQUARE FORM OF THE CROSSED PHYSICAL FRAME. Let \(N,m\) be positive integers and \(\mathcal P\) a finite set of integers. Let \(\mathscr A\) be a finite set of coordinates
90ee649f2811580d.author: slava chan
90ee649f2811580d.proof:
If \(a\notin\mathcal P_{12}\), then a prime divides both \(a\) and at least one of \(u_1,u_2\). The zero-extension rule makes the corresponding one of \(C_a(\alpha_1),C_a(\alpha_2)\) zero, proving \(Z_{a,m}=0\). Every inverse in (4)--(5) is therefore taken only on \(\mathcal P_{12}\) and is defined.

Fix \((\alpha_1,\alpha_2)\). Expanding its square in (5) gives
\[
 \sum_{a,b\in\mathcal P_{12}}Z_{a,m}\overline{Z_{b,m}}
 e_{L_{12}}(A_{12,m}(a^{-1}-b^{-1})).
\]
Subtracting \(\sum_{a\in\mathcal P_{12}}|Z_{a,m}|^2\) removes exactly the \(a=b\) terms. Summation proves (5).

For fact 754cf92eea3a7532, expand
\(A_{a,b,m}(\gamma_1)\overline{A_{a,b,m}(\gamma_2)}\) over its unchanged provenance coordinates \((\iota,h,p,\ell)\). The coefficient is exactly
\[
 Z_{a,m}(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)\overline{Z_{b,m}(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)}.
\]
Its zero extension is precisely the coordinatewise rule used above, so deleting nonunit \(a,b\) loses only zero terms. Equations (12)--(14) of that fact supply the phase in (4). Hence \(\mathfrak O_m^{\rm coord}=\mathfrak O_m\).

glossary.Z_{a,m}(alpha_1,alpha_2): The dilator coefficient for one crossed provenance pair.
glossary.mathcal P_{12}: The dilators which are units modulo the lcm of one crossed coordinate pair.

9128d43a5ac4e1bb.title: EXACT OFF-DUAL DISCREPANCY FOR A SCALAR CENTERED FACE
9128d43a5ac4e1bb.author: slava chan
9128d43a5ac4e1bb.statement:
EXACT OFF-DUAL DISCREPANCY FOR A SCALAR CENTERED FACE.

Let \(r\) be a nonempty squarefree integer and let
\[
 \Omega_r=\prod_{p\mid r}\mathbb F_p^\times.
\]
Let \(\mathcal R\) be a finite row set. For every \(j\in\mathcal R\) and
\(\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r\), let \(V_j(\boldsymbol\rho)\) and
\(W_j(\boldsymbol\rho)\) be complex numbers, and put
\[
 X_j(\boldsymbol\rho)=V_j(\boldsymbol\rho)W_j(\boldsymbol\rho),
 \qquad
 K_j=\sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r}X_j(\boldsymbol\rho).        \tag{1}
\]
Then for every complex coefficient array \((c_j)\),
\[
 \left|\sum_jc_jK_j\right|^2=\mathcal D_r(c)+\mathcal O_r(c),      \tag{2}
\]
where
\[
 \mathcal D_r(c)=
 \sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r}
 \left|\sum_jc_jX_j(\boldsymbol\rho)\right|^2                     \tag{3}
\]
and
\[
 \mathcal O_r(c)=
 \sum_{\substack{\boldsymbol\rho,\boldsymbol\sigma\in\Omega_r\\
                  \boldsymbol\rho\ne\boldsymbol\sigma}}
 \left(\sum_jc_jX_j(\boldsymbol\rho)\right)
 \overline{\left(\sum_kc_kX_k(\boldsymbol\sigma)\right)}.          \tag{4}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \left|\sum_jc_jK_j\right|^2
 \le |\Omega_r|\,\mathcal D_r(c),                                 \tag{5}
\]
and the factor \(|\Omega_r|\) in (5) is sharp for arbitrary arrays \(X_j\).

In the exact forward GA face completion of fact 0aa821ade9a14b45, take
\[
 X_j(\boldsymbol\rho)
 =V_{j,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)W_{j,r}(\boldsymbol\rho).
\]
Then \(K_j\) in (1) is exactly the scalar active-face row
\(K_{\lambda,h,r}\), while \(\mathcal D_r(c)\) is exactly the coordinatewise weighted tensor quadratic form controlled for \(C_\ell\)-rows by fact e2e971fd4983bd94 and for \(A\)-rows by fact 35e599ec4bc284fe. The still-uncontrolled same-\(r\) term is precisely (4). Expanding the literal transform
\[
 W_{j,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)
 =\sum_qB_{j,r}(q)\chi_{\boldsymbol\rho}(q)
\]
gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal O_r(c)
 =\sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\ne\boldsymbol\sigma}
 \sum_{j,k}\sum_{q_1,q_2}
 c_j\overline{c_k}\,
 B_{j,r}(q_1)\overline{B_{k,r}(q_2)}
 V_{j,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)\overline{V_{k,r}(\boldsymbol\sigma)}
 \chi_{\boldsymbol\rho}(q_1)
 \overline{\chi_{\boldsymbol\sigma}(q_2)}.                         \tag{6}
 \end{aligned}
\]
All sums in (6) retain their literal support.

Thus the coordinatewise WTG facts alone do not bound the scalar common-\(r\) face at their stated scale: using only (5) costs
\[
 |\Omega_r|=\prod_{p\mid r}(p-1),
\]
and this loss is sharp without additional structure. A scalar-face proof must also bound the off-dual discrepancy (6), or produce an exact averaging operation that annihilates it. This result proves no estimate for (6), no distinct-\(r\) discrepancy, no pair-dependent nonresonance deletion, no GA-NR-DIL estimate, and no Goldbach conclusion.
9128d43a5ac4e1bb.proof:
Put
\[
 A(\boldsymbol\rho)=\sum_jc_jX_j(\boldsymbol\rho).
\]
By (1),
\[
 \sum_jc_jK_j=\sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r}A(\boldsymbol\rho).
\]
Expanding the absolute square gives
\[
 \left|\sum_{\boldsymbol\rho}A(\boldsymbol\rho)\right|^2
 =\sum_{\boldsymbol\rho}|A(\boldsymbol\rho)|^2
 +\sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\ne\boldsymbol\sigma}
 A(\boldsymbol\rho)\overline{A(\boldsymbol\sigma)},
\]
which is exactly (2)--(4). Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \left|\sum_{\boldsymbol\rho}A(\boldsymbol\rho)\right|^2
 \le|\Omega_r|\sum_{\boldsymbol\rho}|A(\boldsymbol\rho)|^2,
\]
proving (5). Sharpness follows already with one row and
\(X_1(\boldsymbol\rho)=1\) for every \(\boldsymbol\rho\): the two sides before the factor are \(|\Omega_r|^2\) and \(|\Omega_r|\).

For the GA specialization, equation (9) of fact 0aa821ade9a14b45 states exactly
\[
 K_{\lambda,h,r}
 =\sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r}
 V_{\lambda,h,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)
 W_{\lambda,h,r}(\boldsymbol\rho),
\]
so (1) is the literal scalar face row. Equation (3) is the quadratic form appearing in facts e2e971fd4983bd94 and 35e599ec4bc284fe. Substituting equation (8) of fact 0aa821ade9a14b45 into (4) and interchanging finite sums gives (6). Finally
\[
 |\Omega_r|=\prod_{p\mid r}|\mathbb F_p^\times|
 =\prod_{p\mid r}(p-1).
\]
The sharpness example proves that no better implication from the coordinatewise diagonal form alone is valid. Every scope limitation is explicit.

glossary.off-dual discrepancy: The rho not equal to sigma part of the scalar face Gram after dual Fourier completion.
glossary.scalar centered face: The contraction K_j obtained by summing every active dual coordinate of one centered face.

914048233fada05f.title: INJECTIVE ACTUAL-SOURCE PMD ENERGY BOUND
914048233fada05f.author: slava chan
914048233fada05f.statement:
INJECTIVE ACTUAL-SOURCE PMD ENERGY BOUND.

Fix an integer J>=1. Let Q>=2, let p be a prime, let v be a positive integer, put n=vp, and assume gcd(v,p)=1. Let I_q and I_m be integer subintervals of [Q,2Q), and assume p>Q. Let A be an integer. Let cal X be any subset of triples x=(q,m,k) satisfying
  q in I_q,  m in I_m,  k in Z,
  qm+nk=A,  gcd(qm,n)=1.                                  (1)
For x in cal X let c_x be a complex coefficient with |c_x|<=1, and put X_src=#cal X.

Both coordinate projections x->q modulo p and x->m modulo p are injective. For x_i=(q_i,m_i,k_i) define
  rho_p(x_1,x_2)=A(q_2-q_1)(q_1q_2)^(-1) modulo p.          (2)
Then
  rho_p(x_1,x_2)=m_1-m_2 modulo p.                         (3)

For a complex function W on Z/pZ with |W(r)|<=1 define
  C_p(r)=sum_{x_1,x_2 in cal X}c_{x_1}conjugate(c_{x_2})
          [1_{r=rho_p(x_1,x_2)}-1/p],                      (4)
  E_p(W)=sum_{r modulo p}W(r)|C_p(r)|^2.                   (5)
Regard c_x as a q-coefficient by the injective q-projection. Define the exact rational reciprocal-slope contribution E_{p,0}(W) and the all-shift D=0-subtracted remainder
  E_{p,neq}(W)=E_p(W)-E_{p,0}(W)                           (6)
as in facts 27540b4094f677f4 and e7458a42217c2756. Then for every epsilon>0,
  |E_p(W)|<=X_src^3,                                      (7)
  |E_{p,0}(W)|<<_epsilon Q^epsilon X_src^2,                (8)
  |E_{p,neq}(W)|<<_epsilon Q^epsilon X_src^3.              (9)
These estimates retain the complete signed physical kernel W, equivalently its full Fourier-shift assembly; no triangle over Fourier shifts occurs.

The source cardinality satisfies
  X_src<<_epsilon Q^epsilon(1+Q^2/n).                      (10)
Consequently let H,V,P be positive real numbers satisfying
  1<=H<=Q,  2<=V<H,  P=QH/V,                              (11)
and let V<=v<2V, P<=p<2P. For every such v,p let cal X_{v,p} be a source set of the preceding kind, and for every s modulo v allow coefficients c_{v,s,p,x} of modulus at most one on the same set. If xi_v is supported on V<=v<2V and |xi_v|<=tau_J(v), then
 sum_{V<=v<2V}sum_{s modulo v}|xi_v/v|^2
   sum_{P<=p<2P, p prime}|E_{v,s,p,neq}(W_{v,s,p})|
 <<_{J,epsilon}Q^epsilon Q^4/(V H^2)                      (12)
uniformly for all |W_{v,s,p}|<=1. In particular, if H>=Q^alpha for a fixed alpha>0, (12) is at most Q^(4-2alpha+epsilon).

This is an actual-source graph estimate: it applies while the equation qm+vpk=A and all deletion masks defining cal X are retained. It does not assert that a generic separated post-Poisson coefficient b_q is source-supported; using (12) for such coefficients requires an exact reassembly of their smooth Fourier modes before absolute values.
914048233fada05f.proof:
First prove injectivity. Suppose x_1,x_2 in cal X have q_1 congruent to q_2 modulo p. Since both q_i lie in an interval of cardinality at most Q<p, one has q_1=q_2=q. Reducing (1) modulo p gives qm_i congruent A modulo p. The condition gcd(q,n)=1 makes q a unit modulo p, so m_1 congruent m_2 modulo p. Both m_i lie in an interval of cardinality at most Q<p, hence m_1=m_2. Equation (1) then gives k_1=k_2. Thus x->q modulo p is injective. The same argument with q and m interchanged proves injectivity of x->m modulo p.

Reducing (1) modulo p gives
  qm congruent A modulo p.
Since q is a unit modulo p,
  A q^(-1) congruent m modulo p.                           (13)
Therefore
 A(q_2-q_1)(q_1q_2)^(-1)
 =Aq_1^(-1)-Aq_2^(-1)
 congruent m_1-m_2 modulo p,
which proves (3).

Put
  R(r)=sum_{x_1,x_2}c_{x_1}conjugate(c_{x_2})
        1_{r=m_1-m_2 modulo p},
and S=sum_x c_x. By (3),
  C_p(r)=R(r)-|S|^2/p.                                    (14)
The sum over r of R(r) is |S|^2. Hence expansion of the square gives the exact orthogonal-centering identity
 sum_r|C_p(r)|^2=sum_r|R(r)|^2-|S|^4/p
                 <=sum_r|R(r)|^2.                         (15)
After expanding the last sum, every contributing ordered quadruple satisfies
  m_1-m_2=m_3-m_4 modulo p.                               (16)
Choose x_1,x_2,x_3. Equation (16) determines m_4 modulo p, and injectivity of the m-projection shows that at most one x_4 in cal X has that residue. Since |c_x|<=1,
  sum_r|R(r)|^2<=X_src^3.                                 (17)
Now |W|<=1 and (15)-(17) give
 |E_p(W)|<=sum_r|C_p(r)|^2<=X_src^3,
proving (7).

For the rational-slope term, use the notation B_lambda of fact 27540b4094f677f4. The q-projection is injective, so b_q is well defined by b_q=c_x on represented q and zero otherwise. Its support is contained in [Q,2Q), so fact e7458a42217c2756 applies and gives
 sum_lambda|B_lambda|^2
 <<_epsilon Q^epsilon(sum_q|b_q|^2)^2
 <=Q^epsilon X_src^2.                                     (18)
Fact 27540b4094f677f4 identifies
 E_{p,0}(W)=sum_lambda|B_lambda|^2
              Gamma_W(rho_{p,lambda},rho_{p,lambda}).      (19)
For |W|<=1,
 |Gamma_W(t,t)|
 =|(1-2/p)W(t)+p^(-2)sum_rW(r)|
 <=1+1/p<=2.                                               (20)
Equations (18)-(20) prove (8). Equation (9) follows from (6)-(8), with the empty-source case trivial and X_src^2<=X_src^3 when X_src>=1. No Fourier coefficient of W has been estimated separately.

It remains to count the source. As q and m range in subintervals of [Q,2Q), their product qm ranges in an interval of length less than 4Q^2. From (1),
  qm=A-nk.                                                 (21)
Thus k belongs to an interval containing at most
  1+4Q^2/n                                                 (22)
integers. For each fixed k, the positive integer A-nk=qm is less than 4Q^2. Its number of ordered positive factorizations is at most its divisor function. Fact e705401df9f0709e gives the fixed-power divisor estimate O_epsilon(Q^epsilon) on this polynomial range. Any interval, coprimality, Möbius, or source mask only deletes factorizations. This proves (10).

Under (11), n=vp>=VP=QH, so (10) and H<=Q give, after adjusting epsilon,
  X_src<<_epsilon Q^(1+epsilon)/H.                         (23)
The estimate (9) is uniform in s and p. Sum it with the squared coefficients. Fact d061fc4dc153e309 gives
 sum_{V<=v<2V}sum_{s modulo v}|xi_v/v|^2
 <<_{J,epsilon}V^epsilon.                                  (24)
There are at most 2P primes in [P,2P). Combining (9), (23), and (24) yields
 <<_{J,epsilon}Q^epsilon P(Q/H)^3
 =Q^epsilon(QH/V)Q^3/H^3
 =Q^epsilon Q^4/(VH^2),
which is (12). The final assertion follows from V>=1 and H>=Q^alpha.

glossary.E_{p,0}: The exact rational reciprocal-slope contribution to the physical centered energy.
glossary.X_src: The cardinality of the retained actual-source graph.
glossary.cal X: The retained actual-source graph of triples (q,m,k) satisfying qm+vpk=A.

91db48815d136d4c.title: Fix real numbers x>1, 0<κ<1/6, 0<η<κ/20, and X_bal≥1, and put N=2x, assumed integral. Let W, ψ, D_*, Φ and Q_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;R,K) be as in fact 0880dc648c429047. Let ℒ be the set of positive dyadic labels λ=(D,M,R,K) for which the defining sum for Q_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;R,K) has a nonzero summand, and define ι(D,M,R,K)=(R,K,D,M). Put
91db48815d136d4c.author: slava chan
91db48815d136d4c.statement:
Fix real numbers x>1, 0<κ<1/6, 0<η<κ/20, and X_bal≥1, and put N=2x, assumed integral. Let W, ψ, D_*, Φ and Q_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;R,K) be as in fact 0880dc648c429047. Let ℒ be the set of positive dyadic labels λ=(D,M,R,K) for which the defining sum for Q_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;R,K) has a nonzero summand, and define ι(D,M,R,K)=(R,K,D,M). Put
𝒢={λ∈ℒ:D≥4D_* and R≥4D_*}.
Define the base controlled-label set 𝒜 as the union of the following three subsets of ℒ:
(i) 𝒜_bal={λ:D≤X_bal and R≤x^(2/3-κ)};
(ii) 𝒜_FT={λ:D>X_bal and R≤M x^(-η)};
(iii) 𝒜_UBC, consisting of labels with D>X_bal, max(D,R)≥x^η, and satisfying either
R≤D, D^19 R^14≤x^(17-η), D^8 R^7≤x^(8-η),
or
R>D, D^14 R^19≤x^(17-η), D^7 R^8≤x^(8-η).
Define the legal swap closure
𝒞=𝒜∪ι(𝒜∩𝒢)
and
C_N=Σ_{λ∈𝒞}Q_{N,W,ψ}(λ).

A labelled incidence is a tuple z=(D,M,R,K;d,m,r,k) of positive dyadic D,M,R,K and positive integers d,m,r,k satisfying dm+rk=N and for which
w(z)=μ(d)μ(r)log(m)log(k)W(dm/x)ψ(d/D_*)Φ(d/D)Φ(m/M)Φ(r/R)Φ(k/K)
is nonzero. The label of z is λ(z)=(D,M,R,K). For a labelled incidence z with λ(z)∉𝒞, call its forward orientation boundary-admissible if D>1, β=log(R)/log(D) satisfies 4/3≤β≤3/2-κ, and there is a divisor y of r such that, with t=r/y,
y≤t and D^(2-β-3η)≤y,t≤D^(2(β-1)+3η).
Call its reverse orientation boundary-admissible if the same conditions hold after simultaneously replacing (D,M,R,K;d,m,r,k) by (R,K,D,M;r,k,d,m). The two orientations cannot both be boundary-admissible, because the forward condition implies R>D while the reverse condition implies D>R.

For a boundary-admissible orientation, let y(z) be the least positive divisor y satisfying the displayed conditions and let t(z) be the complementary divisor. Let Ω(n) denote the number of prime factors of a positive squarefree integer n. Give z exactly one anatomy tag as follows. If its admissible exponent β lies in [4/3,4/3+6η], tag it 1×1 when (Ω(y(z)),Ω(t(z)))=(1,1), tag it 2×1 when the unordered pair is {1,2}, and tag it 2×2 when it is (2,2). Tag every other boundary-admissible incidence asymmetric. For a∈{1×1,2×1,2×2,asymmetric}, let E_{a,N} be the sum of w(z) over labelled incidences z with λ(z)∉𝒞 that are boundary-admissible and have tag a. Put E_N=Σ_a E_{a,N}. Let U_N be the sum of w(z) over all remaining labelled incidences, namely those with λ(z)∉𝒞 for which neither orientation is boundary-admissible. Finally put
H_N=Σ_{D,M,R,K}Q_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;R,K).

Then all sums are finite and
H_N=C_N+E_N+U_N
exactly, before taking any absolute value. More precisely, every labelled incidence occurs in exactly one of C_N, E_{1×1,N}, E_{2×1,N}, E_{2×2,N}, E_{asymmetric,N}, U_N, and occurs there with its original fixed N, Möbius factor μ(d)μ(r), logarithmic factors, smooth masks, and dyadic weights unchanged. The same partition identity remains true after multiplying w(z) by an arbitrary auxiliary coefficient depending on the entire labelled incidence; hence pre-existing target, gcd, unit, stopping, overlap, or conductor-provenance masks are transported without deletion or duplication. No assertion is made about the sign of an individual divisor sibling or of an individual anatomy term.
91db48815d136d4c.proof:
Fact 0880dc648c429047 shows that H_N is the exact sum of the dyadic blocks Q_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;R,K), and each block is the sum of the displayed weights w(z). Its support argument also shows that only finitely many dyadic labels and integer variables can occur.

The definition of 𝒞 is hierarchical: first take every label in 𝒜, and then add the swapped label only when the original label lies in the explicitly declared bi-deep set 𝒢. Thus a label either belongs to 𝒞 or does not; overlaps inside the union do not create multiplicity because C_N is summed over the set 𝒞, not over a list of reasons for membership.

Fix a labelled incidence z whose label is outside 𝒞. If its forward orientation is boundary-admissible, then β≥4/3>1, so log R>log D and R>D. If its reverse orientation is boundary-admissible, the same argument with D and R interchanged gives D>R. Therefore the two alternatives are disjoint. In either alternative the set of admissible positive divisors y is finite and nonempty, so its least element y(z) exists and determines t(z) uniquely. The four anatomy rules are disjoint by construction: the first three specify three distinct unordered pairs of prime-factor counts in the central strip, and asymmetric is their complement among boundary-admissible incidences. Hence every incidence outside 𝒞 is in exactly one of the four endpoint classes if an orientation is boundary-admissible, and otherwise is in U_N.

Consequently, pointwise on the finite set of labelled incidences,
1=1_{λ(z)∈𝒞}+1_{λ(z)∉𝒞}1_{z boundary-admissible}+1_{λ(z)∉𝒞}1_{z not boundary-admissible},
and the middle indicator is the disjoint sum of the four anatomy indicators. Multiplying this identity by w(z) and summing proves H_N=C_N+E_N+U_N and the sharper six-way partition. Since the operation only multiplies the original weight by zero-one selectors, none of N, μ(d)μ(r), the logarithms, W, ψ, or the four Φ factors changes. The proof is identical with an arbitrary auxiliary coefficient inserted into w(z), which proves the mask-provenance statement.

The final scope sentence is necessary: fact d9eb8f470bce53ac gives an explicit squarefree-semiprime example in which nonzero divisor siblings cancel only after complete signed recombination. The present identity partitions signed incidences and never converts it into positivity of a proper sibling subset.

glossary.C_N: the signed aggregate over the controlled label set 𝒞
glossary.E_N: the sum of all four signed endpoint anatomy aggregates
glossary.E_{a,N}: the signed endpoint aggregate of anatomy a
glossary.H_N: the complete fixed-N dyadic source sum
glossary.U_N: the full signed aggregate of remaining nonendpoint incidences
glossary.X_bal: a positive threshold separating the balanced and D-large label ranges
glossary.t(z): the complementary boundary divisor to y(z)
glossary.w(z): the original signed weight of a labelled incidence z
glossary.y(z): the least admissible boundary divisor in the unique admissible orientation of z
glossary.Ω(n): the number of prime factors of a positive squarefree integer n
glossary.η: a positive fixed exponent buffer smaller than κ/20
glossary.ℒ: the finite set of active positive dyadic scale labels
glossary.𝒜: the union of the declared balanced low-R, Fourier-tail, and UBC base label regions
glossary.𝒞: the base controlled-label set together with its legal bi-deep swap closure

925b3fb5df2c17cc.title: Let p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4 be distinct primes greater than 3 and put P=p_1p_2p_3p_4. Use the centered interval-weighted companion definitions M_q,C_q,E_q and Gamma from fact be4e5ad5378f0122. For each i put L_i=(p_i-1)/2 and let B_i={0,1,...,L_i-1} modulo p_i. Put X_2=0 and X_3=2^{-1}-3^{-1} modulo P. For q=2,3 define the local cyclic interval I_{i,q}=B_i+(X_q modulo p_i). Then every local interval has density (p_i-1)/(2p_i), and the q=2 and q=3 families have the same interval shape at each prime and differ only by a common CRT translation
925b3fb5df2c17cc.author: slava chan
925b3fb5df2c17cc.statement:
Let p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4 be distinct primes greater than 3 and put P=p_1p_2p_3p_4. Use the centered interval-weighted companion definitions M_q,C_q,E_q and Gamma from fact be4e5ad5378f0122. For each i put L_i=(p_i-1)/2 and let B_i={0,1,...,L_i-1} modulo p_i. Put X_2=0 and X_3=2^{-1}-3^{-1} modulo P. For q=2,3 define the local cyclic interval I_{i,q}=B_i+(X_q modulo p_i). Then every local interval has density (p_i-1)/(2p_i), and the q=2 and q=3 families have the same interval shape at each prime and differ only by a common CRT translation.

For these explicit half-density intervals, define k_i by p_i=6k_i+1 or p_i=6k_i-1 and put
r_i=-(3k_i-1)/(3(3k_i+1)) if p_i=6k_i+1,
r_i=-(3k_i+1)/(3(3k_i-1)) if p_i=6k_i-1,
and R=product_{i=1}^4 r_i. Then 0<R<1 and the normalized two-column Gram satisfies
||Gamma-I||_op=sqrt((1+R)/2)>1/sqrt(2).
Consequently, two-sided bounds on interval densities, even densities tending to one half with identical local shapes for q=2 and q=3, do not imply an o(1) companion-flatness estimate when q-dependent translations are unrestricted. Any literal positive theorem must use the arithmetic relation governing the q-dependent interval locations or another hypothesis that excludes this alignment. This is a half-density companion countermodel, not an arithmetic PAVG27 counterexample and not a counterexample to a fully specified WF-RPS window family.
925b3fb5df2c17cc.proof:
All primes greater than 3 are congruent to 1 or -1 modulo 6, so each displayed integer k_i exists and is positive. Fix one prime p and omit the index i. Put L=(p-1)/2, B={0,1,...,L-1} modulo p, and let
A(t)=|B intersect (B+t)|-L^2/p
be the centered cyclic autocorrelation. Let a=3^{-1} modulo p and let d=min(a,p-a) for representatives in {1,...,p-1}.

If p=6k+1, then a=4k+1, d=2k, L=3k, and |B intersect (B+a)|=L-d=k. Hence
A(0)=L-L^2/p=3k(3k+1)/p,
A(a)=k-L^2/p=-k(3k-1)/p,
so A(a)/A(0)=-(3k-1)/(3(3k+1)).                         (1)
If p=6k-1, then a=2k, d=2k, L=3k-1, and |B intersect (B+a)|=L-d=k-1. Hence
A(0)=3k(3k-1)/p,
A(a)=-k(3k+1)/p,
so A(a)/A(0)=-(3k+1)/(3(3k-1)).                         (2)
The autocorrelation is even, so the same ratios hold at -a. Each ratio in (1)-(2) is strictly between -1 and 0.

Let f_i be the centered indicator of B_i, let fhat_i be its additive Fourier transform, and define the common unshifted fourfold multiplier
M_0(h)=product_{i=1}^4 fhat_i(rho_i(h)),
with rho_i as in fact be4e5ad5378f0122. Translating every B_i by X_q modulo p_i multiplies the i-th Fourier transform by e_{p_i}(-rho_i(h)X_q). The CRT character identity in fact be4e5ad5378f0122 therefore gives
M_q(h)=M_0(h)e_P(-hX_q).                                      (3)
The number S=sum_h|M_0(h)|^2 is positive. Indeed, choose by CRT an h for which rho_i(h)=1 modulo p_i for all i. This h is primitive, and each local value fhat_i(1)=sum_{x=0}^{L_i-1}e_{p_i}(-x) is nonzero because 0<L_i<p_i, so M_0(h) is nonzero.

For q=2 the companion has one atom, while for q=3 it has two. By (3) and the choice X_3=2^{-1}-3^{-1}, write
C_2=x,
C_3=x+y,
where
x(h)=M_0(h)e_P(-h2^{-1}),
y(h)=M_0(h)e_P(-h(2^{-1}+3^{-1})).                         (4)
Thus ||x||^2=||y||^2=S. Moreover
<x,y>=sum_h |M_0(h)|^2 e_P(-h3^{-1}).                      (5)
Apply the exact CRT collision factorization from fact be4e5ad5378f0122 to the same base interval in both slots. At z=0 it gives
S=P product_i A_i(0),
and at z=-3^{-1} it gives
<x,y>=P product_i A_i(-3^{-1} modulo p_i).
Using the evenness of A_i and (1)-(2), one obtains
<x,y>/S=product_i r_i=R.                                  (6)
Every r_i is negative and there are four factors, so R>0; since |r_i|<1, also R<1.

Equations (4)-(6) give
E_2=S,
E_3=||x+y||^2=2S(1+R),
<C_2,C_3>=S(1+R).
Therefore the modulus of the normalized off-diagonal Gram entry is
S(1+R)/sqrt(S times 2S(1+R))=sqrt((1+R)/2)>1/sqrt(2).
A two-by-two normalized Hermitian Gram has diagonal entries one, so the operator norm of Gamma-I is the modulus of this off-diagonal entry. This proves the formula, the failure of o(1) flatness under density-and-shape assumptions alone, and the stated scope limitations.

glossary.A(t): the centered cyclic autocorrelation of one base half-density interval
glossary.B_i: the base half-density cyclic interval at the prime p_i
glossary.I_{i,q}: the translated half-density local interval at coordinate i and companion index q
glossary.M_0: the common unshifted fourfold centered interval multiplier
glossary.R: the product of the four normalized local autocorrelations r_i
glossary.X_2: the zero global CRT translation for the q=2 windows
glossary.X_3: the global CRT translation 2^{-1}-3^{-1} for the q=3 windows
glossary.half-density companion countermodel: the q=2,3 translated common-shape family in this statement
glossary.r_i: the normalized local centered autocorrelation at the inverse-three shift

93d8472aee4d44da.title: DELETION-AWARE PAIR-DIFFERENCE COMMON-X SUPPLIER AND ITS EXACT WIENER-NORM INTERFACE
93d8472aee4d44da.author: slava chan
93d8472aee4d44da.statement:
DELETION-AWARE PAIR-DIFFERENCE COMMON-X SUPPLIER AND ITS EXACT WIENER-NORM INTERFACE.

Let p>=5 be prime. For a,b,r in F_p assume
\[
 r\ne0\ \Longrightarrow\ (a,b)\ne(0,0),\qquad
 r=0\ \Longrightarrow\ a\ne b.                                 \tag{1}
\]
On
\[
 D_r=\{X\in F_p:X\ne0,\ X+r\ne0\}
\]
put
\[
 \Phi_{a,b,r}(X)=aX^{-1}-b(X+r)^{-1}.                            \tag{2}
\]
Then \(\Phi_{a,b,r}\) is nonconstant. For every \(\xi\in F_p\),
\[
 \boxed{\left|\sum_{X\in D_r}
 e_p\!\left(\Phi_{a,b,r}(X)+\xi X\right)\right|
 \le 5\sqrt p.}                                                  \tag{3}
\]

For W:F_p->C define its normalized additive Fourier transform and Wiener norm by
\[
 \widehat W(\xi)={1\over p}\sum_{X\in F_p}W(X)e_p(-\xi X),
 \qquad
 \|W\|_{\mathcal A_p}=\sum_{\xi\in F_p}|\widehat W(\xi)|.         \tag{4}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{\left|\sum_{X\in D_r}W(X)e_p(\Phi_{a,b,r}(X))\right|
 \le5\sqrt p\,\|W\|_{\mathcal A_p}.}                              \tag{5}
\]
This is sharp in coefficient-class scale: for
\[
 W_{\rm align}(X)=
 \begin{cases}
 e_p(-\Phi_{a,b,r}(X)),&X\in D_r,\\
 0,&X\notin D_r,
 \end{cases}
\]
one has
\[
 \|W_{\rm align}\|_{\mathcal A_p}
 \ge {p-2\over5\sqrt p}.                                        \tag{6}
\]

Now take one LARGE-ACTIVE-PRIME ordered pair from facts 975285ea0f932fe6 and c641ed6b2cda758b, with the canonical selected prime p=P^+(r_y). Put
\[
 t_y=y/p,\qquad T_i=u_it_y,\qquad
 a=\mathscr A h_1T_1^{-1},\quad b=\mathscr A h_2T_2^{-1}\pmod p, \tag{7}
\]
\[
 X=q_1\pmod p,\qquad r=q_2-q_1\pmod p.                           \tag{8}
\]
The local nonresonance p\nmid\mathscr A\Omega is exactly
\[
 \Phi_{a,b,r}(X)\ne0                                             \tag{9}
\]
at the physical point. It implies (1), even when one of the local heights is zero. Hence (3)-(5) apply to this exact selected pair.

After fixing all outer labels and r, aggregate every physical lift, residual CRT phase, source coefficient, selected-largest-prime condition, pair deletion and zero-one provenance mask having the same X into one function W(X). Equation (5) is then an exact deletion-aware common-X estimate before any positive row factorization or fourth moment. A sufficient remaining source theorem is a bound for the aggregate sum of the literal norms
\[
 \|W\|_{\mathcal A_p}                                           \tag{10}
\]
at the TOP-B-BALG-DEEP-NR-SPEC budget; call this missing theorem TOP-B-FIRSTP-PAIR-WIENER.

The bounded projective source identity in fact b69e09aaac3766d9 does not by itself prove that missing theorem: after reciprocity its q-factor is only known to be divisor-bounded, and the selected-prime/pair-deletion mask is pair-dependent. Equation (6) shows that pointwise boundedness alone permits the full square-root Wiener tax. This is an abstract coefficient-class obstruction, not a claim that the literal Top-B coefficient aligns. The present theorem proves neither TOP-B-FIRSTP-PAIR-WIENER, TOP-B-FIRSTP-JCOMP-ENV, TOP-B-BALG-DEEP-NR-SPEC, POST-A-TAIL, nor Goldbach.
93d8472aee4d44da.proof:
We first prove nonconstancy. If r is nonzero, the possible finite poles 0 and -r are distinct. A constant rational function has zero residue at both, so (2) could be constant only if a=b=0, contrary to (1). If r=0, then
\[
 \Phi_{a,b,0}(X)=(a-b)X^{-1},
\]
which is nonconstant because a!=b.

Fix xi. First suppose xi=0. Write (2) in lowest terms as f(X)/g(X). Its denominator has degree at most two and at most two distinct roots, while its numerator has degree no larger than its denominator. It is not of the form H^p-H over the algebraic closure: it has a finite pole of order one, whereas every pole of a nonconstant H^p-H has order divisible by p. Makhul and Winterhof, arXiv:2106.12218, Lemma 2, states that if f/g over F_p is not H^p-H, deg f<=deg g, and g has s distinct roots, then
\[
 \left|\sum_{g(X)\ne0}e_p(f(X)/g(X))\right|
 \le(\deg g+s-2)\sqrt p+1.
\]
Here deg g<=2 and s<=2, so this complete reduced-domain sum is at most \(2\sqrt p+1\). If r is nonzero and exactly one of a,b vanishes, reduction cancels one denominator factor; the reduced domain then contains exactly one of the two points deleted from D_r. Removing that one modulus-one term costs at most 1. In every other case the reduced domain equals D_r. Thus the D_r sum is at most \(2\sqrt p+2\le4\sqrt p\).

Suppose xi is nonzero. In lowest terms,
\[
 \Phi_{a,b,r}(X)+\xi X={f_\xi(X)\over g_\xi(X)}
\]
has \(\deg f_\xi=\deg g_\xi+1\), with \(\deg f_\xi\le3\), and \(g_\xi\) has at most two distinct roots. It is again not H^p-H: it has a pole of order one, at infinity from the nonzero linear term and also possibly at a finite pole. Amadio Guidi, Lindqvist and Micheli, arXiv:1712.05258, Theorem 6.3, states that when deg f>deg g and f/g is not H^p-H,
\[
 \left|\sum_{g(X)\ne0}e_p(f(X)/g(X))\right|
 \le(\deg f+v-1)\sqrt p,
\]
where v is the number of distinct roots of g. The present degrees give at most \(4\sqrt p\). As above, when r is nonzero and exactly one of a,b vanishes, the reduced domain contains one extra regular point; removing it costs 1. Thus the D_r sum is at most \(4\sqrt p+1\le5\sqrt p\). This proves (3).

Fourier inversion for the normalization (4) gives
\[
 W(X)=\sum_{\xi\in F_p}\widehat W(\xi)e_p(\xi X).
\]
Insert this into the left side of (5), interchange the finite sums, apply (3) to each xi, and use the triangle inequality. This proves (5). For W_align every summand on the left of (5) equals one, so the left side is \(\#D_r\ge p-2\). Rearranging (5) proves (6).

We verify the literal map. Since p divides r_y, facts 97b9d86408362df2 and c641ed6b2cda758b give p\nmid \(\mathscr A\Omega\), p\nmid y/p, and units q_i,u_i modulo p. With \(t_y=y/p\) and the definitions (7),
\[
 a q_1^{-1}-b q_2^{-1}
 ={\mathscr A h_1\over u_1t_yq_1}
  -{\mathscr A h_2\over u_2t_yq_2}
 ={\mathscr A\Omega\over u_1u_2t_yq_1q_2}\pmod p.                \tag{11}
\]
The denominator is a unit, so (11) proves (9). If r is nonzero and a=b=0, the left side of (11) is zero; if r=0 and a=b, it is also zero. Both contradict p\nmid\(\mathscr A\Omega\). Hence (1) holds, including the cases a=0 or b=0.

For fixed outer labels and r, equations (7)-(8) identify every pair with its first residue X. Summing all literal copies at a fixed X defines W(X); every pair-dependent selector remains inside that coefficient rather than being factorized. By fact 97b9d86408362df2 and the natural-cofactor identity, the p-local exponential is now exactly \(e_p(\Phi_{a,b,r}(X))\), including the target factor \(\mathscr A\), while the residual factors have been included in W. Thus (5) gives the claimed deletion-aware estimate for exactly the literal aggregate W. The final limitation follows because fact b69e09aaac3766d9 supplies bounded projective smooth factors and a divisor bound, not a bound for (10), while (6) is an explicit bounded coefficient array with the square-root Wiener cost.

glossary.TOP-B-FIRSTP-PAIR-WIENER: The missing aggregate bound for the literal selected-pair coefficient Wiener norms after pair-difference localization.
glossary.\\Phi_{a,b,r}: The pair-difference rational phase a/X-b/(X+r) over F_p.
glossary.\\|W\\|_{\\mathcal A_p}: The normalized additive Wiener norm of a function W on F_p.

95058e339b3441a3.title: CUBIC HARD-SOURCE PAYOFF FOR THE FINITE-BAND MODULAR-ALIAS SECTOR
95058e339b3441a3.author: slava chan
95058e339b3441a3.statement:
CUBIC HARD-SOURCE PAYOFF FOR THE FINITE-BAND MODULAR-ALIAS SECTOR.

Fix constants C>=1 and J>=1. Let Q be sufficiently large, and let real numbers H,V,P satisfy
  2<=H<=Q^(1/3),  2<=V<H,  P=QH/V.                         (1)
Let A be a nonzero integer with |A|<=Q^C, and let cal L be a finite set of literal projective labels. For every ell in cal L choose an integer interval I_ell contained either in [H,2H) or in (-2H,-H].

For every ell, integer v in [V,2V), and prime p in [P,2P) with gcd(v,p)=1, let cal X_{ell,v,p} be any subset of triples x=(q,m,k) satisfying
  q in I_q,  m in I_m,  k in Z,
  qm+vpk=A,  gcd(qm,vp)=1,                                 (2)
where I_q and I_m are integer subintervals of [Q,2Q). Put X_{ell,v,p}=#cal X_{ell,v,p}. For h in I_ell and x in cal X_{ell,v,p}, let a_{ell,v,p,h}(x) be a complex coefficient of modulus at most B. It may contain every literal zero-one source mask, the projective coefficient, the phase e_q(hk) from fact db067f4633c13fed, and every retained bounded scaled-smooth factor.

For four source atoms x_i=(q_i,m_i,k_i), put epsilon_1=epsilon_2=1, epsilon_3=epsilon_4=-1 and
  Delta_h=h_1q_2q_3q_4+h_2q_1q_3q_4
          -h_3q_1q_2q_4-h_4q_1q_2q_3.                     (3)
For each i let s_i be the unique residue modulo v satisfying
  h_i+p s_i congruent 0 modulo v.                           (4)
Let omega_{ell,v,p}(h_1,...,h_4;x_1,...,x_4) be any complex number of modulus at most one supported on the forced graph
  s_1+s_2 congruent s_3+s_4 modulo v.                       (5)
Thus omega may retain the complete small-v CRT phase and any further literal phase or deletion mask, but there is no independent s-sum.

Define the hard-source MOD contribution
  M_MOD^src
  =sum_{ell in cal L}sum_{V<=v<2V}
    sum_{P<=p<2P, p prime, gcd(v,p)=1}
    sum_{h_i in I_ell, h_1+h_2=h_3+h_4}
    sum_{x_i in cal X_{ell,v,p},
         Delta_h nonzero, p divides A Delta_h}
      a_1a_2 conjugate(a_3a_4) omega,                       (6)
with the natural abbreviations. Then for every epsilon>0,
  |M_MOD^src|
  <<_{C,J,epsilon} B^4 #cal L Q^(4+epsilon)H.               (7)
Moreover,
  Q^4H<=P^2Q^(7/3),                                        (8)
so if B and #cal L are subpolynomial, (7) is within the literal vector target
  |M_MOD^src|<<Q^epsilon P^2Q^(7/3).                        (9)

The proof retains the actual source equations, the additive h relation, every projective/source coefficient, and the forced s=-h p^(-1) graph. The theorem is only for hard source rows whose m-coordinate lies in a fixed Q-interval as in (2). It does not apply pointwise to the Schwartz-translated soft-source rows of fact 84bf915e8a88d8d3, does not estimate OSC, and makes no PMD or Goldbach conclusion.
95058e339b3441a3.proof:
The scale assumptions imply p>Q. Indeed P=QH/V>Q. They also imply p>2H for sufficiently large Q, so every h_i is a nonzero residue modulo p.

Fact 914048233fada05f proves two properties for every source set in (2):
  X_{ell,v,p}<<_{C,epsilon}Q^epsilon(1+Q^2/(vp)),           (10)
and the projection x=(q,m,k) -> m modulo p is injective. Since vp>=VP=QH and H<=Q,
  X_{ell,v,p}<<_{C,epsilon}Q^epsilon Q/H.                  (11)

By fact db067f4633c13fed, on four actual-source atoms,
  p divides A Delta_h
if and only if
  p divides R_h=sum_{i=1}^4 epsilon_i h_i m_i.              (12)
We now count the support of (6) for fixed ell,v,p. Choose h_1,h_2,h_3; there are O(H^3) choices, and h_4=h_1+h_2-h_3 is then determined. Requiring h_4 in I_ell only deletes choices. Choose x_1,x_2,x_3; there are at most X_{ell,v,p}^3 choices. Condition (12) forces
  h_4m_4 congruent h_1m_1+h_2m_2-h_3m_3 modulo p.          (13)
Because h_4 is a unit modulo p, (13) determines m_4 modulo p. The injectivity of the source projection x->m modulo p leaves at most one possible x_4. The conditions Delta_h nonzero, (4)-(5), and all literal masks only delete choices. Hence the number of summands for fixed ell,v,p is at most
  O(H^3 X_{ell,v,p}^3).                                    (14)
Taking absolute values only after this source-graph count and using |a_i|<=B and |omega|<=1 gives
  |M_MOD^src|
  <<B^4 #cal L V P H^3 (Q^epsilon Q/H)^3
  <<B^4 #cal L Q^epsilon V P Q^3.
Since VP=QH, this is (7).

Finally,
  Q^4H/[P^2Q^(7/3)]
  =V^2/(Q^(1/3)H)
  <H/Q^(1/3)
  <=1,                                                      (15)
where V<H and H<=Q^(1/3). This proves (8)-(9). The last scope paragraph follows because the proof used the fixed-interval source-cardinality and injectivity statement (10), which fact 84bf915e8a88d8d3 explicitly does not provide pointwise for its translated soft rows.

glossary.a_{ell,v,p,h}: The complete bounded literal coefficient on a height and hard source atom.
glossary.cal X_{ell,v,p}: The retained hard actual-source graph at one label, v, and p.
glossary.omega_{ell,v,p}: The retained modulus-one phase and mask on a source quartic, supported on the forced small-v graph.

95626318cdcc099f.title: JOINT-COPRIMALITY NATURAL-FREQUENCY FOUR-TERM LEDGER. Fix integers J,C>=1. Let Q,H_P,H_T,S,T be real numbers at least one and let G>0. Assume H_T=GH_P and C^{-1}QH_T<=ST<=CQH_T. For every integer q with Q<=q<2Q choose a unit V_q modulo q, and fix a nonzero integer A. Let complex coefficients nu_h,alpha_s,beta_t be supported respectively on H_P<=h<2H_P, S<=s<2S, T<=t<2T and bounded by tau_J(h), tau_J(s), tau_J(t). Define W_q^{cop} as the sum of nu_h alpha_s beta_t e_q(AV_qh(st)^{-1}) over the displayed supports subject to gcd(st,q)=1 and gcd(s,t)=1. Then for every epsilon>0,
95626318cdcc099f.author: slava chan
95626318cdcc099f.statement:
JOINT-COPRIMALITY NATURAL-FREQUENCY FOUR-TERM LEDGER. Fix integers J,C>=1. Let Q,H_P,H_T,S,T be real numbers at least one and let G>0. Assume H_T=GH_P and C^{-1}QH_T<=ST<=CQH_T. For every integer q with Q<=q<2Q choose a unit V_q modulo q, and fix a nonzero integer A. Let complex coefficients nu_h,alpha_s,beta_t be supported respectively on H_P<=h<2H_P, S<=s<2S, T<=t<2T and bounded by tau_J(h), tau_J(s), tau_J(t). Define W_q^{cop} as the sum of nu_h alpha_s beta_t e_q(AV_qh(st)^{-1}) over the displayed supports subject to gcd(st,q)=1 and gcd(s,t)=1. Then for every epsilon>0,
H_P^{-1}sum_{Q<=q<2Q}|W_q^{cop}| <<_{J,C,epsilon} (|A|QH_PST)^epsilon [G^{1/4}Q^2H_T^{1/2}S^{-1/4}+G^{1/4}Q^{7/4}H_T^{1/2}S^{1/4}+Q^2H_TS^{-1/2}+Q^{7/4}H_T].
No condition gcd(A,q)=1 or gcd(h,q)=1 is imposed.
95626318cdcc099f.proof:
Use the exact identity 1_{gcd(s,t)=1}=sum_{e|s,e|t}mu(e). For a fixed e write s=es_1 and t=et_1. The condition gcd(st,q)=1 implies gcd(e,q)=1, and the reciprocal phase becomes e_q(AV_qe^{-2}h(s_1t_1)^{-1}), where V_qe^{-2} is a unit modulo q. Cover the resulting integer supports of s_1 and t_1 by an absolute number of dyadic intervals with lower endpoints S_e,T_e at least one and comparable to S/e,T/e. By submultiplicativity, after normalization their coefficient bounds cost at most tau_J(e)^2.
Apply the full fixed-target inequality of fact 73fb9efe1286f7e9 directly to each such e-block with frequency scale H_P and factor scales S_e,T_e. This application requires only Q,H_P,S_e,T_e>=1, all of which hold; it does not introduce a model-frequency parameter. Divide its bound by H_P and expand the two fourth roots. Since T_e is comparable to T/e and ST is comparable to GQH_P, direct substitution gives the four terms
 tau_J(e)^2 e^{-5/4}G^{3/4}Q^2H_P^{1/2}S^{-1/4},
 tau_J(e)^2 e^{-7/4}G^{3/4}Q^{7/4}H_P^{1/2}S^{1/4},
 tau_J(e)^2 e^{-3/2}GQ^2H_PS^{-1/2},
 tau_J(e)^2 e^{-2}GQ^{7/4}H_P,
up to constants depending only on C,J and the dyadic covers. For example, the first e-power is e^{-1/2} from (H_PT_e)^{1/2}, e^{-1/4} from (H_PT_e)^{1/4}, and e^{-1/2} from (QS_e^2)^{1/4}. The other three expansions give e^{-7/4},e^{-3/2},e^{-2}.
For every a>1 the series sum_{e>=1}tau_J(e)^2e^{-a} converges, by the Euler-product proof in fact bd1ef0652fa7b940. Thus all four e-sums converge absolutely. Finally H_T=GH_P changes the four G,H_P expressions into exactly the four displayed G,H_T expressions in the statement. Reduced-scale epsilon factors are no larger than an adjusted original epsilon factor. Fact 73fb9efe1286f7e9 supplies the nonunit fixed target, the unit twist, and unrestricted gcd(h,q), completing the proof.

glossary.S_e: A dyadic scale comparable to S/e after joint-gcd removal.
glossary.T_e: A dyadic scale comparable to T/e after joint-gcd removal.
glossary.W_q^{cop}: The natural-frequency reciprocal sum with the additional joint coprimality condition gcd(s,t)=1.

95ee390225a4bfe8.title: THE UNGATED LITERAL CENTERED QUARTER-RANGE DIGIT HAS ALMOST FULL DUAL SUPPORT
95ee390225a4bfe8.author: slava chan
95ee390225a4bfe8.statement:
THE UNGATED LITERAL CENTERED QUARTER-RANGE DIGIT HAS ALMOST FULL DUAL SUPPORT.

Let m>=9 be odd and put
 k_quarter=floor(m/4),qquad N=2k_quarter.                           (1)
Let E be the subset of residues modulo m represented by
 {-k_quarter,...,-1,1,...,k_quarter}
and define
 W_star(u)=1_E(u)-N/m.                                              (2)
With
 W_star_hat(ell)=sum_{u modulo m}W_star(u)e_m(-ell u),              (3)
one has W_star_hat(0)=0. Among the m-1 nonzero residues ell modulo m,
 W_star_hat(ell)=0
if and only if
 m divides k_quarter ell.                                          (4)
Consequently the number of nonzero ell with W_star_hat(ell)=0 is
 gcd(k_quarter,m)-1<=2,                                            (5)
and
 #{ell modulo m:W_star_hat(ell) is nonzero}>=m-3.                  (6)
More precisely, there are no nonzero zeros when m=4k_quarter+1, and when m=4k_quarter+3 there are either none or exactly the two residues m/3,2m/3.

Now assume the arithmetic hypotheses of fact c585f0febfbab2f4: q=m^2, s belongs to {1,-1}, gcd(Kn,m)=1,
 A_u=K+2smu,qquad an congruent to A_u modulo q.                    (7)
With no additional u-dependent gate, the exact inverse-column u-assembly is
 sum_{u modulo m}W_star(u)e_q(-pnA_u^(-1))
 =e_q(-pnK_bar)W_star_hat(-gamma_n p),                              (8)
in the notation of that fact. Since gamma_n is a unit modulo m, (6) implies that (8) is nonzero for at least m-3 residue classes p modulo m, hence for at least
 m(m-3)=q-3m                                                        (9)
values p modulo q.

Thus support sparsity of the literal digit transform W_star alone cannot shorten the ungated Kloosterman p-axis. Any proposed saving that leaves all additional u-dependent factors constant cannot come from short p-support and still faces the eta_trace>=39/80+delta exponent requirement of fact c1f29a6ce884c5ae.

If a genuine recovered-prime, carrier, moving-window, or source gate G(u) is inserted, fact c585f0febfbab2f4 shows that the relevant transform is the Fourier transform of W_star(u)G(u), not W_star_hat alone. The present theorem neither proves nor excludes sparsity of that joint transform. It therefore identifies, but does not solve, the precise carrier-correlated interface.
95ee390225a4bfe8.proof:
The set E has N distinct residues because k_quarter<m/2. Its centered indicator has total sum zero, proving W_star_hat(0)=0. For a nonzero residue ell represented by 1<=ell<=m-1, the constant term -N/m contributes zero to the Fourier coefficient. Put x=pi ell/m. The symmetric geometric sum gives
 1+W_star_hat(ell)
 =sum_{j=-k_quarter}^{k_quarter}e_m(-ell j)
 =sin((2k_quarter+1)x)/sin(x).                                    (10)
The denominator is nonzero. Therefore W_star_hat(ell)=0 if and only if
 sin((2k_quarter+1)x)=sin(x).                                     (11)
The identity
 sin A-sin B=2cos((A+B)/2)sin((A-B)/2)
shows that (11) holds in exactly one of the following two cases:
 k_quarter ell/m is an integer,                                   (12)
or
 2(k_quarter+1)ell=m(2t+1)                                       (13)
for some integer t. Case (13) is impossible because its left side is even and its right side is odd: m and 2t+1 are both odd. Thus (11) is equivalent to (12), which is exactly (4).

The number of residues ell modulo m satisfying m divides k_quarter ell is gcd(k_quarter,m); one of them is ell=0. This proves the exact zero count in (5). If m=4k_quarter+1, then
 gcd(k_quarter,m)=gcd(k_quarter,1)=1.
If m=4k_quarter+3, then
 gcd(k_quarter,m)=gcd(k_quarter,3)<=3.
This proves (5)-(6). In the latter case equality three occurs exactly when 3 divides k_quarter, and the two nonzero solutions are m/3 and 2m/3.

Equation (8) is equation (8) of fact c585f0febfbab2f4 with the additional gate identically one. Multiplication by the unit -gamma_n permutes residues modulo m, so the number of p classes for which its Fourier coefficient is nonzero equals the support size in (6). Every p class modulo m has exactly m lifts modulo m^2. This proves (9).

The first scope conclusion is precisely the ungated calculation (8)-(9), together with the necessary exponent ledger in fact c1f29a6ce884c5ae. For a nonconstant gate G, equation (8) of fact c585f0febfbab2f4 replaces W_star_hat by the transform of W_star G. Since multiplication in the digit variable is convolution in frequency, no support conclusion for that joint transform follows from (6) alone. This proves the final limitations.

glossary.k_quarter: the integer floor(m/4) defining the symmetric literal quarter-range digit

967520f427b111c5.title: Let \(q_1,q_2\) be positive squarefree integers and put
967520f427b111c5.author: slava chan
967520f427b111c5.statement:
Let \(q_1,q_2\) be positive squarefree integers and put
\[
 d=(q_1,q_2),\qquad c=[q_1,q_2]={q_1q_2\over d},
 \qquad b=q_2/d.
\]
Let \(N,h\in\mathbb Z\) satisfy
\[
 (N,c)=1,\qquad d\mid h.                               \tag{1}
\]
For \(r,k\in\mathbb Z\), define
\[
 {\cal K}_{q_1,q_2}(r,k;N,h)=
 \sum_{\substack{m,w\ ({\rm mod}\ c)\\
                  mw\equiv N\ ({\rm mod}\ q_1)\\
                  m(w-h)\equiv N\ ({\rm mod}\ q_2)}}
 e_c(-km-rw),                                           \tag{2}
\]
where \(e_c(t)=\exp(2\pi it/c)\), and define
\[
 S(a_1,a_2;c)=
 \sum_{\substack{z\ ({\rm mod}\ c)\\(z,c)=1}}
 e_c(a_1z+a_2z^{-1}).                                  \tag{3}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 {\cal K}_{q_1,q_2}(r,k;N,h)
 =
 e_b(-rhq_1^{-1})S(r,kN;c).
 }                                                       \tag{TMC-EXACT}
\]
The inverse is taken modulo \(b\), and the twist is one when \(b=1\).

If \({\cal A}\) is a compactly supported infinitely differentiable complex
function on \(\mathbb R^2\), put
\[
 \widetilde{\cal A}(\xi,\zeta)=
 \int_{\mathbb R^2}{\cal A}(t,y)e(\xi t+\zeta y)\,dt\,dy.
\]
Then
\[
\begin{split}
 &\sum_{\substack{m,w\in\mathbb Z\\
                  q_1\mid N-mw\\q_2\mid N-m(w-h)}}
 {\cal A}(m,w)\\
 &\qquad={1\over c^2}\sum_{k,r\in\mathbb Z}
 \widetilde{\cal A}(k/c,r/c)
 e_b(-rhq_1^{-1})S(r,kN;c).                            \tag{4}
\end{split}
\]
If
\[
 c_c(n)=\sum_{\substack{z\ ({\rm mod}\ c)\\(z,c)=1}}e_c(nz),
\]
then the complete zero faces are
\[
 S(0,0;c)=\phi(c),\qquad S(r,0;c)=c_c(r),\qquad
 S(0,kN;c)=c_c(k).                                     \tag{5}
\]

For the support application, fix
\[
 1/2<\alpha<\beta<1,\qquad B_{\rm src}>0,\qquad U>0.
\]
Let \(N=2x\) be an integer with \(x\ge3\), and suppose
\[
 {1\over2}x^{1/2}(\log x)^{-B_{\rm src}}\le D\le2x^{1/2}.
\]
Let \(W,\Phi\) be bounded real functions supported in
\([\alpha,\beta]\) and \([1/2,2]\), and define
\[
 {\cal I}_D=\{w\ge2:(w,N)=1,\ \mu(w)\ne0,\ w\le x^{1/2},\
 \Phi(w/D)\ne0\}.
\]
Let \(h\ne0\) with \(|h|\le2D\). For \(m,w,w-h\ge1\), put
\[
 p=N-mw,\qquad p'=N-m(w-h).
\]
On the support of
\[
 {\bf1}_{w,w-h\in{\cal I}_D}W(mw/x)W(m(w-h)/x)
 \Phi(p/U)\Phi(p'/U)\Lambda(p)\Lambda(p'),             \tag{6}
\]
one has
\[
 x<p,p'<2x.                                             \tag{7}
\]
Under
\[
 \Lambda(n)=-\sum_{q\mid n}\mu(q)\log q,               \tag{8}
\]
each nonzero divisor term has \(q\) equal to the underlying prime of the
prime power \(n\). If \(p,p'\) are genuine primes, the corresponding
\(q_1=p,q_2=p'\) satisfy
\[
 q_1\ne q_2,\qquad(q_1q_2,N)=1,\qquad(q_1,q_2)=1.      \tag{9}
\]
If \((q_1,q_2)>1\), or if \((q_1q_2,N)>1\), at least one of \(p,p'\)
is a proper prime power.

Uniformly over all such shifts, the total absolute contribution in (6)
for which at least one of \(p,p'\) is a proper prime power is
\[
 \ll_{\varepsilon,W,\Phi}
 D x^{1/2+\varepsilon}(\log x)^2
 =o_{A,W,\Phi}\left(xD(\log x)^{-A}\right)             \tag{10}
\]
for every fixed \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(A>0\). Hence every noncoprime or
common-modulus support face of the nonzero-shift assembly is power-small,
and the genuine-prime face satisfies TMC-EXACT with \(d=1\).
967520f427b111c5.proof:
Squarefreeness gives \((q_1,b)=1\). Choose \(t\pmod b\) with
\(t\equiv hq_1^{-1}\pmod b\), and put \(C=q_1t\pmod c\).
Writing \(q_1=da,q_2=db,h=dh_0\) proves
\[
 C\equiv0\pmod{q_1},\qquad C\equiv h\pmod{q_2}.         \tag{11}
\]
Under (1), every \(m\) in (2) is a unit modulo \(c\). For each unit \(m\),
the unique CRT solution is
\[
 w\equiv Nm^{-1}+C\pmod c.                             \tag{12}
\]
Therefore
\[
 {\cal K}_{q_1,q_2}
 =e_b(-rhq_1^{-1})
 \sum_{\substack{m\ ({\rm mod}\ c)\\(m,c)=1}}
 e_c(-km-rNm^{-1}).                                    \tag{13}
\]
The bijection \(z=-Nm^{-1}\) has \(m=-Nz^{-1}\), and turns the last sum
into \(S(r,kN;c)\). This proves TMC-EXACT.

For residues \(a_1,a_2\pmod c\), two-dimensional Poisson summation gives
\[
 \sum_{\substack{m\equiv a_1\ ({\rm mod}\ c)\\
                 w\equiv a_2\ ({\rm mod}\ c)}}{\cal A}(m,w)
 ={1\over c^2}\sum_{k,r\in\mathbb Z}
 \widetilde{\cal A}(k/c,r/c)e_c(-ka_1-ra_2).           \tag{14}
\]
Summing (14) over the residue pairs satisfying the reflected congruences
and applying TMC-EXACT proves (4). Formula (5) follows directly from (3);
multiplication by the unit \(N\) permutes the reduced residues, so
\(c_c(kN)=c_c(k)\).

Identity (8) is Möbius inversion of
\(\log n=\sum_{a\mid n}\Lambda(a)\). If \(\Lambda(n)\ne0\), then
\(n=\ell^j\) for a prime \(\ell\), and the only divisor with
\(\mu(q)\log q\ne0\) is \(q=\ell\).
The support of \(W\) gives
\[
 \alpha x\le mw,m(w-h)\le\beta x,
\]
which proves (7). A genuine prime in \((x,2x)\) cannot divide \(N=2x\),
because the integer \(N/p\) would lie strictly between one and two.
Since \(h\ne0\), \(p'-p=mh\ne0\). Thus genuine \(p,p'\) are distinct
and coprime to \(N\), proving (9). If their underlying primes coincide,
their distinct prime powers cannot both have exponent one. If an
underlying prime divides \(N\), its prime power in \((x,2x)\) cannot have
exponent one. This proves the support-face alternatives.

There are \(O(x^{1/2}\log x)\) proper prime powers below \(2x\). For a
fixed one, \(mw=N-p\) has at most
\(\tau(N-p)\ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon\) positive solutions.
For each \((m,w)\), the condition \(w-h\in{\cal I}_D\) permits \(O(D)\)
shifts. The same count applies to a proper prime power in the second
argument. Multiplication by the two logarithmic weights proves the first
bound in (10), after increasing \(\varepsilon\) to absorb a logarithm.
Its ratio to \(xD(\log x)^{-A}\) tends to zero for fixed
\(\varepsilon<1/2\), proving the last assertion.

glossary.TMC-EXACT: the exact twisted Kloosterman evaluation of the two-modulus complete sum
glossary.TMC-SUPPORT-FACES: the power-small removal of common-modulus and noncoprime faces via proper-prime-power counting
glossary.cal K_{q_1,q_2}: the complete mixed m,w sum for the two reflected congruences

96ed928a9fc80276.title: Fix 1/2<a<b<1. Let W be a nonzero nonnegative continuously differentiable real function supported in [a,b]. Let ψ be continuously differentiable with 0≤ψ≤1, ψ(u)=0 for 0<u≤1, and ψ(u)=1 for u≥2. Let B=B(W,ψ)>0 be supplied by fact 2827630745a3225b. Let x tend to infinity through values for which N=2x is an even integer not representable as a sum of two primes, and put D_*=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B). Choose Φ to be the nonnegative smooth dyadic partition of fact 3ef233e014331fc3
96ed928a9fc80276.author: slava chan
96ed928a9fc80276.statement:
Fix 1/2<a<b<1. Let W be a nonzero nonnegative continuously differentiable real function supported in [a,b]. Let ψ be continuously differentiable with 0≤ψ≤1, ψ(u)=0 for 0<u≤1, and ψ(u)=1 for u≥2. Let B=B(W,ψ)>0 be supplied by fact 2827630745a3225b. Let x tend to infinity through values for which N=2x is an even integer not representable as a sum of two primes, and put D_*=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B). Choose Φ to be the nonnegative smooth dyadic partition of fact 3ef233e014331fc3.

Apply fact 052064336e86e65c with its large parameter equal to 2x, target exponent A=4, and variation exponent C=5. Let B_BV be the resulting constant and put
Q_BV=(2x)^(1/2)(log(2x))^(-B_BV).
For positive dyadic D,M,U let P_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;U) be the genuine-prime block of fact d6fd2c2cf8b5d0f0.

If 2D≤Q_BV, then
P_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;U)≪_{W,ψ,Φ}x(log x)^(-3)
uniformly in the fixed bad N and in the source-admissible M,U. Consequently the negative block supplied by fact d6fd2c2cf8b5d0f0 must satisfy
2D>Q_BV
for every sufficiently large bad N.

For any source-admissible D,M,U, split the block exactly as
P_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;U)=P_N^{≤}(D,M;U)+P_N^{>}(D,M;U)
according as d≤sqrt(x) or d>sqrt(x). The high-divisor part has the exact divisor-switched form
P_N^{>}(D,M;U)
=Σ_{m≥3, m odd, gcd(m,N)=1} log(m)Φ(m/M)
 Σ_{p prime, p<N, p≡N (mod m), (N-p)/m>sqrt(x)}
 log(p) μ((N-p)/m) W((N-p)/x)
 ψ((N-p)/(mD_*)) Φ((N-p)/(mD)) Φ(p/U).
Every nonzero term here has
3≤m<b sqrt(x), m odd, gcd(m,N)=1,
and the quotient (N-p)/m is an odd squarefree integer exceeding sqrt(x).

For the forced negative block, 2D>Q_BV and Φ(d/D)≠0 imply d>Q_BV/4 in every nonzero incidence. Hence its d≤sqrt(x) part is confined to the top logarithmic band
Q_BV/4<d≤sqrt(x),
while its d>sqrt(x) part is exactly the displayed odd-coprime divisor-switched family. This is an exact range reduction, not an estimate for either remaining hard family.
96ed928a9fc80276.proof:
We first prove the classical initial-label estimate. Write λ_D(d)=μ(d)ψ(d/D_*)Φ(d/D). Because Φ is nonnegative and belongs to a nonnegative partition of unity, 0≤Φ≤1, hence |λ_D(d)|≤1.

Replace the genuine prime p in the definition of P(D,M;U) by a von Mangoldt variable n and define
F_d(t)=log((N-t)/d)W((N-t)/x)Φ((N-t)/(dM))Φ(t/U)
on 2≤t≤2x, interpreting it as zero off the set where N-t>0. The W-support confines N-t to [ax,bx], so F_d is continuously differentiable after the zero extension. On every d in the Φ(d/D)-support, its supremum plus total variation is O_{W,Φ}((log x)^5); in fact only a fixed power is needed. The logarithm costs O(log x), and differentiating W((N-t)/x), Φ(t/U), or Φ((N-t)/(dM)) costs the reciprocal of its natural support length, whose integral over that support is bounded.

Assume 2D≤Q_BV. Then Φ(d/D)≠0 implies d≤2D≤Q_BV. Apply fact 052064336e86e65c with large parameter 2x, residue a_d congruent to N modulo d on the coprime moduli, coefficient λ_D(d), and profile F_d. It gives
Σ_{d,gcd(d,N)=1}λ_D(d)Σ_{n≡N (mod d)}Λ(n)F_d(n)
=Σ_{d,gcd(d,N)=1}λ_D(d)φ(d)^(-1)∫_2^(2x)F_d(t)dt
 +O(x(log x)^(-4)).                                      (1)

The density main in (1) is smaller than every logarithmic power. Indeed, exchange d and t. For fixed t the d-profile
G_t(s)=ψ(Ds/D_*)Φ(s)log((N-t)/(Ds))
 W((N-t)/x)Φ((N-t)/(DMs))
is supported in [1/2,2]. After division by log(2x), its supremum and total variation are uniformly bounded, by exactly the scaled-C1 check in fact 415fa7afad9006c5: if ψ' is active then D/D_* is bounded, and if the last Φ is active then its scaled argument is bounded. Apply the first assertion of fact 415fa7afad9006c5 with exponent 6 and integrate over an interval of length at most 2x. The density main is O(x(log x)^(-5)).

It remains to return from Λ(n) to genuine primes. The difference is supported on n=q^j with q prime and j≥2. For each such n, the equation dm=N-n and the fixed block weights give an absolute contribution at most O_{W,ψ,Φ}(τ(N-n)log(2x)^2). The self-contained divisor estimate proved in fact d6fd2c2cf8b5d0f0 and the count of higher prime powers there show that the total difference is O_ε(x^(1/2+ε)). Taking ε<1/4 and combining with (1) proves P(D,M;U)≪x(log x)^(-3).

Fact d6fd2c2cf8b5d0f0 supplies a block satisfying
P(D,M;U)≤-c_W𝔠(N)x/(2J_xL_DML_U),
where J_x=ceil(log_2x)+4 and L_DM,L_U are fixed positive constants. Fact f41f5f91b52e0d13 gives 𝔠(N)≥C_2>0. Its magnitude is therefore much larger than x(log x)^(-3) for large x, so that selected block cannot satisfy 2D≤Q_BV.

The split at d=sqrt(x) is disjoint and exhaustive. In the d>sqrt(x) part, the equation dm+p=N gives d=(N-p)/m and is a bijection between the original incidences and the displayed pairs (m,p). Substitution gives every displayed factor exactly.

Finally, W forces dm≤bx. Thus d>sqrt(x) implies m<b sqrt(x). Fact d6fd2c2cf8b5d0f0 gives p>x, so p is an odd prime and p>m. Since N is even, N-p=dm is odd; hence both d and m are odd. The m=1 term vanishes because log(1)=0, so every nonzero m is odd and at least 3. Also gcd(m,N)=gcd(m,p)=1 because p is prime and p>m. Nonzero μ(d) makes d=(N-p)/m squarefree. For the forced block, Φ(d/D)≠0 gives d≥D/2>Q_BV/4. Combining this with the split at sqrt(x) proves the final range description.

glossary.P_N^{>}: the part of a genuine-prime block with d>sqrt(x)
glossary.P_N^{≤}: the part of a genuine-prime block with d≤sqrt(x)
glossary.Q_BV: the classical initial modulus ceiling at scale (2x)^(1/2) times a fixed inverse logarithm

975285ea0f932fe6.title: TOP-\(B\) EPSILON-NEAR-RESONANCE PAYMENT AND EXACT LARGE-PRIME/SMOOTH-ACTIVE-PRODUCT SPLIT
975285ea0f932fe6.author: slava chan
975285ea0f932fe6.statement:
TOP-\(B\) EPSILON-NEAR-RESONANCE PAYMENT AND EXACT LARGE-PRIME/SMOOTH-ACTIVE-PRODUCT SPLIT.

Use the recombined singleton top-\(B\) nonresonant energy of facts
\(d63101722d12c88c\) and \(5fc5975b76bffe88\). Thus
\[
 U\le u<2U,\quad Y\le y<2Y,\quad Q\le q<2Q,\quad
 F\le |h|<2F,
\]
all displayed variables and the nonzero target \(\mathscr A\) have fixed polynomial size in \(Q\), every supported \(y\) is squarefree, and the two recombined coefficients have a fixed divisor envelope. For an ordered pair put
\[
 \Omega=h_1q_2u_2-h_2q_1u_1,\qquad
 r_y={y\over(y,\mathscr A\Omega)}\quad(\Omega\ne0).           \tag{1}
\]

For every \(\varepsilon>0\), define
\[
 \rho=\min\left({\varepsilon\over4},{1\over100}\right),\qquad
 \zeta={\rho\over2}.                                          \tag{2}
\]
Let \(V_{\rm rec}^{(\varepsilon\text{-near})}\) be the exact restriction of the expanded energy to
\[
 \Omega\ne0,\qquad 1<r_y\le Q^\rho.                           \tag{3}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 |V_{\rm rec}^{(\varepsilon\text{-near})}|
 \ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon U^2Q^2F^2.
 }                                                             \tag{4}
\]
Every literal source, marker, Fourier, target-gcd, fixed-\(U\), parent, sign, order/equal-cell, collision, deletion, coprimality, provenance, and reciprocity phase remains present before the absolute divisor count. This is an \(\varepsilon\)-dependent conductor threshold, not a fixed-power saving theorem.

On the remaining sector \(r_y>Q^\rho\), define the disjoint alternatives
\[
 {\rm LARGE\!-\!ACTIVE\!-\!PRIME}:
 \quad P^+(r_y)\ge Q^\zeta,                                   \tag{5}
\]
\[
 {\rm SMOOTH\!-\!ACTIVE\!-\!PRODUCT}:
 \quad P^+(r_y)<Q^\zeta.                                      \tag{6}
\]
Then the exact nonresonant energy has the partition
\[
 V_{\rm rec}^{(\mathrm{NR})}
 =
 V_{\rm rec}^{(\varepsilon\text{-near})}
 +V_{\rm rec}^{(\mathrm{large\text{-}active\text{-}prime})}
 +V_{\rm rec}^{(\mathrm{smooth\text{-}active\text{-}product})}.
                                                                    \tag{7}
\]
Every prime divisor of \(r_y\) is a prime divisor of \(y\), and hence is at most
\[
 L=Q^{\beta-1+\sigma}.                                        \tag{8}
\]
Moreover, every term in the smooth-active-product sector has
\[
 \omega(r_y)\ge3.                                             \tag{9}
\]
Thus the large-active-prime sector contains a canonical active prime of size at least \(Q^\zeta\), while the smooth sector is a genuinely multi-prime active product. Fact \(a84f95a82329a894\)'s one-selected-prime aggregation does not by itself supply an iterated product gain for (6).

Equations (4)-(9) pay only epsilon-near resonance and classify the residual. They prove no estimate for either residual branch, no common-\(X\) completion, no TOP-B-FIRSTP-JCOMP-ENV, no TOP-B-BALG-DEEP-NR-SPEC, no POST-A-TAIL statement, and no Goldbach conclusion.
975285ea0f932fe6.proof:
Fix an ordered row sextuple
\[
 (u_1,q_1,h_1,u_2,q_2,h_2)
\]
with \(\Omega\ne0\), and put
\[
 M=\mathscr A\Omega.
\]
Then \(M\ne0\) and has fixed polynomial size in \(Q\). For a supported \(y\), set
\[
 d=(y,M),\qquad r=y/d.
\]
One has \(d\mid |M|\), \(y=dr\), and \(r=r_y\). Therefore the number of supported \(y\) with \(1<r_y\le Q^\rho\) is at most
\[
 \lfloor Q^\rho\rfloor\tau(|M|).                              \tag{10}
\]
This is the divisor enumeration used in fact \(1feb8a751976e771\); no polylogarithmic property of its former threshold is used in (10).

Allocate the output exponent \(\varepsilon\) as follows. Since \(M\) has fixed polynomial size,
\[
 \tau(|M|)\ll_\varepsilon Q^{\varepsilon/4}.
\]
The fixed divisor envelope in fact \(d63101722d12c88c\) gives, for the product of the two recombined coefficient absolute values,
\[
 \left|
 \widehat c_y^{\rm rec}(u_1,q_1,h_1)
 \overline{\widehat c_y^{\rm rec}(u_2,q_2,h_2)}
 \right|
 \ll_\varepsilon Q^{\varepsilon/4},
\]
after choosing the divisor-bound exponent sufficiently small and absorbing fixed logarithms. By (2),
\[
 Q^\rho\le Q^{\varepsilon/4}.
\]
There are \(O(U^2Q^2F^2)\) ordered row sextuples. Every exponential factor has modulus one, and every literal selector only deletes a term. Absolute summation using (10) is therefore
\[
 \ll_\varepsilon
 Q^{3\varepsilon/4}U^2Q^2F^2
 \ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon U^2Q^2F^2,
\]
which proves (4). The fixed-\(k\) statement is displayed; summing the \(O(\log Q)\) possible stopping lengths from fact \(d63101722d12c88c\) is absorbed by the unused exponent margin.

The conditions (3), (5), and (6) are disjoint and exhaustive on \(r_y>1\), proving (7). Since \(r_y\mid y\), every prime of \(r_y\) divides \(y\). Facts \(6414b11506a84ff0\) and \(d63101722d12c88c\) give
\[
 P^+(y)\le L,
\]
so (8) follows.

Finally suppose (6) holds and \(\omega(r_y)\le2\). Squarefreeness of \(y\) implies squarefreeness of \(r_y\). If \(r_y\) has one or two prime factors, each strictly below \(Q^\zeta\), then
\[
 r_y<Q^{2\zeta}=Q^\rho,
\]
contradicting the residual condition \(r_y>Q^\rho\). Hence (9) holds. The scope comparison with fact \(a84f95a82329a894\) follows from its statement: it aggregates one selected-prime occupancy and explicitly leaves tensorization of remaining prime faces open.

glossary.LARGE-ACTIVE-PRIME: The polynomial-conductor residual whose largest active prime is at least Q^zeta.
glossary.SMOOTH-ACTIVE-PRODUCT: The polynomial-conductor residual all of whose active prime factors are below Q^zeta.
glossary.epsilon-near resonance: The nonresonant sector with effective cross-y conductor at most Q raised to the epsilon-dependent exponent rho.

97b9d86408362df2.title: EXACT FIRST-ACTIVE-PRIME CRT MAP FOR \(V_{\rm deep}\), WITH THE ALL-ACTIVE RANK-ONE MATCH AND THE PRECISE CONSUMER GAPS
97b9d86408362df2.author: slava chan
97b9d86408362df2.statement:
EXACT FIRST-ACTIVE-PRIME CRT MAP FOR \(V_{\rm deep}\), WITH THE ALL-ACTIVE RANK-ONE MATCH AND THE PRECISE CONSUMER GAPS.

Work in formula (5) of fact \(5fc5975b76bffe88\). For one supported pair set
\[
 \Omega=h_1q_2u_2-h_2q_1u_1,\qquad
 r_y={y\over(y,\mathscr A\Omega)},
\]
assume \(r_y>1\), let \(p\) be the least prime divisor of \(r_y\), and put
\[
 t=y/p,\qquad \widetilde h_i=h_iu_i^{-1}\pmod p.              \tag{1}
\]
Then \(p\nmid\mathscr A\Omega\), \((p,t)=1\), and the exact pair summand equals
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\widehat c_y^{\rm rec}(u_1,q_1,h_1)
 \overline{\widehat c_y^{\rm rec}(u_2,q_2,h_2)}
 e_y\!\left(\mathscr A\Omega(q_1q_2u_1u_2)^{-1}\right)\\
 &=
 d_{p,t}(u_1,q_1,h_1)\overline{d_{p,t}(u_2,q_2,h_2)}
 e_p\!\left(
 \mathscr A\widetilde h_1t^{-1}q_1^{-1}
 -\mathscr A\widetilde h_2t^{-1}q_2^{-1}\right),              \tag{2}
\end{aligned}
\]
where
\[
 d_{p,t}(u,q,h)=
 \widehat c_{pt}^{\rm rec}(u,q,h)
 e_t\!\left(\mathscr A h(pqu)^{-1}\right),                    \tag{3}
\]
and \(e_1=1\). Moreover,
\[
 |d_{p,t}(u,q,h)|=|c_k^{\rm rec}(u,pt;q,h)|.                  \tag{4}
\]
Thus (3) retains both inverse-\(y\) phases modulo \(u\), the Archimedean phase, the recombined singleton coefficient, and every literal selector.

Consider four such rows localized at the same \(p\), ordered with signs \((+,+,-,-)\). Suppose a separate source-preserving completion supplies a common residue variable \(X\) and shifts \(r_i\) with
\[
 q_i=X+r_i\pmod p.                                             \tag{5}
\]
