If every \(\widetilde h_i\ne0\), their local rational phase, apart from the common nonzero scalar \(\mathscr A\), is
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^4{\sigma_i\widetilde h_i\over t_i(X+r_i)}.         \tag{6}
\]
Putting \(s_i=t_i\widetilde h_i^{-1}\), formula (6) is exactly the \(c=1,l=2\) function in fact \(7d341c8eec44f7a3\). It is constant exactly when every equal-shift block \(B\) has
\[
 \sum_{i\in B}\sigma_i{\widetilde h_i\over t_i}=0\pmod p,     \tag{7}
\]
and no exceptional equality partition has a singleton. Hence the exact dictionary for fact \(549328a9f587f158\) is
\[
 \text{shift }r_i,\qquad
 \text{height }\widetilde h_i,\qquad
 \text{cofactor }t_i=y_i/p.                                  \tag{8}
\]
It matches the one-block and all three two-block repeated-pole partitions. First-prime selection, pair deletion, pairwise equality of cofactors, and source bookkeeping may remain in its arbitrary tuple mask.

The residual factors in (3) also satisfy the formal contraction hypothesis of fact \(a84f95a82329a894\) at the pointwise scalar level. Namely take
\[
 E_p=\mathbb C^2,\qquad \|(z_1,z_2)\|=\max(|z_1|,|z_2|),\qquad
 v(d)=(d,\overline d).
\]
For each four-row tuple, multiplication of the first coordinates in the two positive positions and the second coordinates in the two negative positions, followed by multiplication by any retained unit scalar and mask in \([0,1]\), is a complex four-linear functional of norm at most one. This does not construct a contraction for a further joint-completion operator absent from (2)-(5).

The all-active condition is automatic if
\[
 p>2F.                                                         \tag{9}
\]
It is not implied by \(p\mid r_y\). For distinct primes \(p_1,p_2\), take
\[
 y=p_1p_2,\quad u_1=u_2=1,\quad q_1=q_2=q_0,\quad
 h_1=p_1,\quad h_2=p_2,
\]
where \((q_0p_1p_2,\mathscr A)=1\) is not required, but
\[
 (q_0,p_1p_2)=1,\qquad(\mathscr A,p_1p_2)=1.
\]
Then \(\Omega=q_0(p_1-p_2)\), \(r_y=y\), but \(p_1\mid h_1\) and \(p_2\mid h_2\). No prime divisor of \(r_y\) makes both rows active. This is an arithmetic no-inference example, not a claim that its literal coefficient is nonzero.

For fixed \(p\), every supported cofactor \(t=y/p\) lies in the consecutive integer interval
\[
 \mathcal J_p(Y)=\{t>0:Y\le pt<2Y\},\qquad
 L_p=\#\mathcal J_p(Y),                                       \tag{10}
\]
and \(p\nmid t\). If \(L_p<p\), fact \(bbd687d016ee3ff6\) applies to this entire integer block after zero extension: reduction modulo \(p\) is injective and the nonzero image is contained in at most two additive intervals. Its fixed-power conclusion is therefore available when its further hypotheses \(L_p\ge p^\delta\), \(p\ge Q^\zeta\), the literal source envelope, and the remaining-face contraction are separately verified.

Three interfaces are still absent from the accepted \(V_{\rm deep}\) facts:
(i) formula (5) of fact \(5fc5975b76bffe88\) has independent physical \(q_i\) and does not supply the common-\(X\) completion (5);
(ii) outside (9), zero-height local faces remain;
(iii) no accepted fact compares the \(U_p\) envelope produced after \(\widetilde h=hu^{-1}\) with the target joint-completion baseline. Fact \(9ea2dddfbbbd191a\) does not directly supply (iii): preserving the interval cofactor \(t=y/p\) replaces its interval numerator \(h\) by the \(u\)-dependent residue \(\widetilde h\), while preserving \(h\) replaces its denominator \(t\) by \(ut\).

Call the missing theorem supplying (5), the zero-height payment, any further non-scalar contraction, and the literal envelope comparison \({\rm TOP\!-\!B\!-\!FIRSTP\!-\!JCOMP\!-\!ENV}\). The present theorem proves the exact map, pointwise contraction, and cofactor geometry only. It proves neither that missing theorem, TOP-B-BALG-DEEP-NR-SPEC, POST-A-TAIL, nor Goldbach.
97b9d86408362df2.proof:
Fact \(d63101722d12c88c\) gives squarefree \(y\), the support coprimalities \((q_i u_i,y)=1\), and equality of the absolute values in (4) before the additional factor in (3). Because \(p\mid r_y\), one has \(p\mid y\) and \(p\nmid\mathscr A\Omega\). Squarefreeness gives \(y=pt\) with \((p,t)=1\).

Choose integers \(a,b\) satisfying
\[
 at\equiv1\pmod p,\qquad bp\equiv1\pmod t.
\]
For every integer \(z\), not necessarily a unit modulo \(pt\),
\[
 e_{pt}(z)=e_p(az)e_t(bz).                                    \tag{11}
\]
Indeed, \(at+bp\equiv1\) modulo both \(p\) and \(t\), hence modulo \(pt\); therefore
\[
 {az\over p}+{bz\over t}-{z\over pt}
 ={z(at+bp-1)\over pt}
\]
is an integer. This proves (11).

Apply (11) to the residue
\[
 z=\mathscr A\Omega(q_1q_2u_1u_2)^{-1}\pmod {pt}.
\]
The inverse exists because \((q_1q_2u_1u_2,pt)=1\); no coprimality of \(\mathscr A\Omega\) with \(t\) is needed. The \(p\)-part is
\[
 e_p\!\left(
 \mathscr A t^{-1}
 [h_1(q_1u_1)^{-1}-h_2(q_2u_2)^{-1}]
 \right),
\]
which is the exponential in (2) after using (1). The \(t\)-part is
\[
 e_t\!\left(
 \mathscr A h_1(pq_1u_1)^{-1}
 -\mathscr A h_2(pq_2u_2)^{-1}
 \right).
\]
Absorbing its two row factors gives (2)-(3). All absorbed exponentials have modulus one, proving (4) and the retention assertion.

Under (5), multiplication of two localized pairs and reordering positive and negative rows gives (6). If all \(\widetilde h_i\) are nonzero, \(s_i=t_i\widetilde h_i^{-1}\) is a unit and \(\widetilde h_i/t_i=s_i^{-1}\). Multiplication by the common unit \(\mathscr A\) does not affect constancy. Fact \(7d341c8eec44f7a3\), with \(c=1,l=2\), proves (7) and excludes singleton blocks. Fact \(549328a9f587f158\) uses exactly the balance (7) after the dictionary (8), proving the full partition match.

For the contraction, every vector \(v(d)\) has norm \(|d|\). The coordinate-selection map
\[
 \mathcal K(w_1,w_2,w_3,w_4)
 =\xi D\,(w_1)_1(w_2)_1(w_3)_2(w_4)_2,
\]
where \(|\xi|=1\) and \(0\le D\le1\), is complex-linear in each argument and satisfies
\[
 |\mathcal K(w_1,w_2,w_3,w_4)|
 \le\prod_{i=1}^4\|w_i\|.
\]
At \(w_i=v(d_i)\) it equals the required retained unit factor and mask times
\(d_1d_2\overline d_3\overline d_4\). This proves the stated pointwise instance of the hypothesis in fact \(a84f95a82329a894\).

If \(p>2F\), supported heights satisfy \(0<|h_i|<2F<p\), so \(p\nmid h_i\). Since \(u_i\) is a unit modulo \(p\), all \(\widetilde h_i\) are nonzero. This proves (9).

In the example,
\[
 \Omega=q_0(p_1-p_2).
\]
Modulo \(p_1\) it is \(-q_0p_2\ne0\), and modulo \(p_2\) it is \(q_0p_1\ne0\). Multiplication by \(\mathscr A\) preserves nonvanishing. Hence
\((y,\mathscr A\Omega)=1\) and \(r_y=y\), while the displayed height divisibilities prove the failure of all-row activity.

The equivalence \(Y\le y<2Y\) and \(y=pt\) gives the consecutive interval (10). Squarefreeness gives \(p\nmid t\). Under \(L_p<p\), the integer-block corollary of fact \(bbd687d016ee3ff6\) gives injectivity and at most two nonzero additive interval components, together with the stated conditional fixed-power conclusion.

Finally, fact \(5fc5975b76bffe88\) states no common-\(X\) completion. Facts \(549328a9f587f158\), \(a84f95a82329a894\), and \(bbd687d016ee3ff6\) explicitly leave the literal envelope and complete joint completion open. Fact \(9ea2dddfbbbd191a\) assumes separated integer interval variables with a bounded-variation numerator slot; equation (1) replaces its numerator by \(hu^{-1}\), or equivalently replaces its denominator by \(ut\). The cited facts prove neither separated literal representation. These exact statement comparisons establish the three remaining interfaces and the final scope limitations.

glossary.TOP-B-FIRSTP-JCOMP-ENV: The missing source-preserving first-prime joint completion, zero-height payment, further contraction, and literal envelope comparison for V_deep.
glossary.\\mathcal J_p(Y): The consecutive integer cofactor interval defined by Y<=pt<2Y.
glossary.\\widetilde h: The selected-prime height residue h u^{-1} modulo p.
glossary.d_{p,t}: The recombined Top-B coefficient after the residual cofactor-modulus CRT phase is absorbed at selected prime p and t=y/p.

97cfedc76bcae0ad.title: EXACT LOGARITHMIC-FOURIER PROJECTIVE SEPARATION OF THE COMPLETE LITERAL CRITICAL PRODUCT AMPLITUDE ON A DYADIC PRODUCT RECTANGLE. Fix one orientation, one exact active pair g,c, one complete frozen selected critical source block, and the notation of fact edabb9a0d2959b41. Fix kappa and h|R_kappa with (h,c)=1, put X_h=B/h, and for each retained q define
97cfedc76bcae0ad.author: slava chan
97cfedc76bcae0ad.statement:
EXACT LOGARITHMIC-FOURIER PROJECTIVE SEPARATION OF THE COMPLETE LITERAL CRITICAL PRODUCT AMPLITUDE ON A DYADIC PRODUCT RECTANGLE. Fix one orientation, one exact active pair g,c, one complete frozen selected critical source block, and the notation of fact edabb9a0d2959b41. Fix kappa and h|R_kappa with (h,c)=1, put X_h=B/h, and for each retained q define
V_{q,kappa,h}(u)
 =A_lit(q,kappa,hX_hu;(ell-kappa hX_hu)/q)                      (1)
on the complete positive product support, extended smoothly by zero as in that fact.

There is a fixed compact interval [a_0,b_0] in the logarithmic variable y=log u, independent of q,kappa,h and of the active scales, and for every fixed integer J>=0 there is a fixed exponent C_J such that
sup_{q,kappa,h} sup_y
 |(d/dy)^J V_{q,kappa,h}(e^y)|
 <<_J(log x)^(C_J),                                             (2)
with support in [a_0,b_0].

Let I_0 be any fixed compact interval containing [a_0,b_0] in its interior and containing every value log(pv/X_h) sampled by one fixed dyadic prime/cofactor rectangle under consideration. Choose L_0 larger than the length of I_0 by at least two, embed I_0 into the interior of a circle of length L_0, and put
tau_j=2 pi j/L_0 for j in Z.                                    (3)
Then there are coefficients c_j(q,kappa,h) such that
V_{q,kappa,h}(e^y)
 =sum_{j in Z}c_j(q,kappa,h)e^(i tau_j y)                        (4)
for every y in I_0. The series converges absolutely and uniformly on I_0, and for some fixed exponent C_proj,
sum_{j in Z}sup_{q,kappa,h}|c_j(q,kappa,h)|
 <<(log x)^(C_proj).                                            (5)
The supremum in (5) is over the fixed frozen block and its original finite supports. Outside I_0, the right side of (4) represents the periodized logarithmic profile and no equality with the zero-extended amplitude is asserted.

Consequently, for every sampled product n=hpv in the fixed dyadic rectangle, so that log(pv/X_h) belongs to I_0,
A_lit(q,kappa,hpv;(ell-kappa hpv)/q)
 =sum_{j in Z}lambda_{j,q,kappa,h}p^(i tau_j)v^(i tau_j),        (6)
where
lambda_{j,q,kappa,h}=c_j(q,kappa,h)X_h^(-i tau_j)                (7)
and
sum_j sup_{q,kappa,h}|lambda_{j,q,kappa,h}|
 <<(log x)^(C_proj).                                            (8)
Thus, on every complete sampled dyadic prime/cofactor rectangle, the literal smooth amplitude has an exact countable projective decomposition of polylogarithmic norm while retaining its q,kappa dependence in the outer coefficient. This statement does not give a global identity outside the sampled rectangle, separate an additional sharp factor-allocation marker, prove a uniform Siegel-Walfisz condition for all modes, handle the omega_P=0 or nonfactorable-modulus complements, or pay HC-MED.
97cfedc76bcae0ad.proof:
Fact 5772f2de626492b3 writes the complete n-dependent literal amplitude explicitly in both orientations. After n=B u, every source factor is either a fixed smooth function of u, a fixed smooth function of the affine quotient t(Bu)/T, or one of the two logarithms log t(Bu) and log(c kappa). The complete sibling recombination in fact 328503a935cabe60 removes every hard n-dependent deletion; all remaining predicates are outer scalars on the frozen block.

For (1), n=hX_hu=Bu. Its dyadic source support lies in a fixed compact subset of the positive reals; taking logarithms gives a fixed compact interval [a_0,b_0].

We prove (2) by repeated differentiation. The scale relation in fact 5772f2de626492b3 is qT asymptotic to B K_c, while kappa is asymptotic to K_c. Hence
d/du [t(Bu)/T]=-kappa B/(qT),
whose absolute value is bounded by a fixed constant. The quotient t(Bu)/T is affine in u and is bounded above and below by positive constants on the support. Therefore every derivative with respect to y=log u of a fixed smooth function of t(Bu)/T is bounded, with a bound depending only on the derivative order. The same holds for every fixed smooth factor depending directly on u. Every other scaled source argument listed in equations (6F)-(6R) of fact 5772f2de626492b3 has bounded first scaled derivative by the scale comparisons proved there; because each argument is affine or a fixed smooth composition of affine scaled variables, repeated chain rule gives bounded derivatives at every fixed order. Derivatives of log t(Bu) are bounded on the positive support except for the unchanged magnitude log t(Bu), which is O(log x), and log(c kappa) is independent of u and O(log x). Repeated product rule proves (2).

Put f_{q,kappa,h}(y)=V_{q,kappa,h}(e^y). Its smooth zero extension vanishes near both endpoints of I_0 because [a_0,b_0] lies in the interior of I_0. Embed I_0 in (0,L_0) by a fixed translation, extend by zero over the rest of (0,L_0), and periodize with period L_0. The resulting function is smooth and periodic and agrees with the original zero-extended f on every y in I_0. Define
c_j(q,kappa,h)
 =L_0^(-1)integral_0^{L_0}
 f_{q,kappa,h}^{per}(y)e^(-2 pi i j y/L_0)dy,                    (9)
where f^{per} is this periodized profile and the fixed translation phase is included in c_j.

For j nonzero, integrating (9) by parts J times and using periodicity gives
|c_j(q,kappa,h)|
 <=C'_J(log x)^(C_J)(1+|j|)^(-J).                              (10)
For j=0 the same type of bound follows directly from (2). Choose J=3. Summing (10) proves (5). Fourier inversion for a smooth periodic function gives its pointwise Fourier series, and (5) gives absolute uniform convergence. Since the periodized profile equals the original zero extension on I_0, this proves (4) exactly on the asserted domain. It also explains why no equality is claimed outside I_0.

For a sampled p,v put y=log(pv/X_h), which belongs to I_0 by hypothesis. Substitute this y in (4). Then
e^(i tau_j y)=X_h^(-i tau_j)p^(i tau_j)v^(i tau_j).
This proves (6)-(7). Since |X_h^(-i tau_j)|=1, (8) is identical to (5). Every q,kappa-dependent literal smooth factor was retained in the coefficient (9).

glossary.I_0: The fixed fundamental logarithmic interval containing the complete sampled dyadic product rectangle.
glossary.L_0: A fixed period longer than the chosen fundamental logarithmic sampling interval.
glossary.c_j(q,kappa,h): The j-th logarithmic Fourier coefficient of the periodized complete literal product profile.
glossary.tau_j: The fixed real frequency 2 pi j/L_0 in the logarithmic Fourier expansion.

97e496ab242dcab8.title: EXACT SHORT-INTERVAL CHARACTER SECOND MOMENT AND A FIXED-PRIME DIAGONAL BARRIER. Let f be a prime, let I_A be an integer interval containing at most A integers, and assume
97e496ab242dcab8.author: slava chan
97e496ab242dcab8.statement:
EXACT SHORT-INTERVAL CHARACTER SECOND MOMENT AND A FIXED-PRIME DIAGONAL BARRIER. Let f be a prime, let I_A be an integer interval containing at most A integers, and assume
f>A+1.
Let z_a be arbitrary complex coefficients supported on integers a in I_A with f not dividing a. Then
sum_{chi modulo f, chi nonprincipal}
 |sum_{a in I_A}z_a chi(a)|^2
 =(f-1)sum_{a in I_A}|z_a|^2-|sum_{a in I_A}z_a|^2.                 (1)
Every nonprincipal character in (1) is primitive. Consequently,
sum_{chi modulo f, chi primitive}
 |sum_{a in I_A}z_a chi(a)|^2
 >=(f-1-A)sum_{a in I_A}|z_a|^2.                                   (2)
In particular, if f>=2A+2, the left side of (2) is at least
(f/2)sum_{a in I_A}|z_a|^2.                                        (3)

Thus, for any fixed delta>0, no estimate of the form
sum_{chi modulo f, chi primitive}
 |sum_{a in I_A}z_a chi(a)|^2
 <=C_delta f^(1-delta)sum_{a in I_A}|z_a|^2                         (4)
can hold uniformly for all primes f>=2A+2 and all nonzero sequences z_a. This is only a fixed-prime obstruction for the isolated full primitive-character second moment. It asserts no dyadic conductor aggregate and no lower bound or exhaustive method restriction for the complete actual-Z_mid packet.
97e496ab242dcab8.proof:
Orthogonality of all multiplicative characters on the unit group modulo the prime f gives
sum_{chi modulo f}
 |sum_{a in I_A}z_a chi(a)|^2
 =(f-1)sum_{a_1,a_2 in I_A, a_1 congruent to a_2 modulo f}
 z_{a_1}overline{z_{a_2}}.                                         (5)
The difference of two integers in I_A has absolute value less than f because I_A contains at most A integers and f>A+1. Therefore the congruence in (5) forces a_1=a_2, and (5) is
(f-1)sum_{a in I_A}|z_a|^2.                                        (6)
The principal character contributes
|sum_{a in I_A}z_a|^2.
For a prime modulus, every other character is primitive. Subtracting the principal contribution from (6) proves (1).

Cauchy's inequality and the cardinality bound for I_A give
|sum_{a in I_A}z_a|^2<=A sum_{a in I_A}|z_a|^2.
Substitution in (1) proves (2). If f>=2A+2, then f-1-A>=f/2, proving (3).

If (4) held uniformly for a fixed delta>0, then applying (3) to any nonzero sequence would give
f/2<=C_delta f^(1-delta),
or f^delta<=2C_delta, for every sufficiently large prime f. This is impossible as f tends to infinity. Therefore (4) cannot hold uniformly. No summation over f and no statement about other factors in an application has been used, which proves exactly the scoped final assertion.

glossary.I_A: An integer interval containing at most A integers.
glossary.z_a: An arbitrary complex coefficient supported on I_A.

97e9b97caca25b8d.title: COMPLETE-FREQUENCY TARGET-GCD-DESCENDED INTERVAL-PRIME TRACE THROUGH THE MEDIUM BAND. Fix integers J,C_A,K>=1, constants C>=1, 0<kappa<=1/100, sigma=kappa/100, 0<eta<sigma, and 1<=beta<=6/5-2kappa. Let Q be sufficiently large, put B=Q^beta, H_T=B/Q, and choose G with Q^(-sigma+eta)<=G<=Q^(sigma-eta); put H_P=H_T/G, L_0=H_TQ^sigma, and Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma). Fix a nonzero integer L_src with |L_src|<=Q^C_A. Let C_med be any set of squarefree divisors c of L_src satisfying c<=H_TQ^(sigma/4)
97e9b97caca25b8d.author: slava chan
97e9b97caca25b8d.statement:
COMPLETE-FREQUENCY TARGET-GCD-DESCENDED INTERVAL-PRIME TRACE THROUGH THE MEDIUM BAND. Fix integers J,C_A,K>=1, constants C>=1, 0<kappa<=1/100, sigma=kappa/100, 0<eta<sigma, and 1<=beta<=6/5-2kappa. Let Q be sufficiently large, put B=Q^beta, H_T=B/Q, and choose G with Q^(-sigma+eta)<=G<=Q^(sigma-eta); put H_P=H_T/G, L_0=H_TQ^sigma, and Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma). Fix a nonzero integer L_src with |L_src|<=Q^C_A. Let C_med be any set of squarefree divisors c of L_src satisfying c<=H_TQ^(sigma/4).
For each c in C_med put Q_c=Q/c and choose U_c,Y_c>=1 with C^(-1)B<=U_cY_c<=CB and L_0/2<=Y_c<=Z. For Q_c<=q<2Q_c let |d_{c,q}|<=1, supported only when q is squarefree, gcd(c,q)=1, and gcd(L_src/c,q)=1. For each dyadic F>=1 choose coefficients nu_{c,F}(h), alpha_{c,F}(u), gamma_{c,F}(p), a scalar omega_{c,F}, and a uniformly scaled-smooth amplitude Psi_{c,F}, with divisor bounds of fixed order J, supports F<=|h|<2F, U_c<=u<2U_c, and primes Y_c<=p<2Y_c with L_0<p<Z, and with |omega_{c,F}|<=C_{J_0}min(1,(F/H_P)^(-J_0)) for every J_0>=1. Define
T_c=H_P^(-1) sum_{F dyadic} omega_{c,F} sum_{q}d_{c,q} sum_h nu_{c,F}(h) sum_{u,p prime; gcd(up,cq)=1; gcd(u,p)=1} alpha_{c,F}(u)gamma_{c,F}(p)Psi_{c,F}(q/Q_c,|h|/F,u/U_c,p/Y_c)e_q(-(L_src/c)h(up)^(-1)).
Then there exists delta=delta(kappa,eta,C_A,J,K,C)>0 such that
sum_{c in C_med}|T_c|<<Q^(2-delta).
The estimate is uniform in the choice of the divisor set C_med and in all deletion masks and polylogarithmically many smooth, dyadic, sign, parent, and source labels that can be absorbed into the displayed coefficients or the uniformly bounded projective smooth family. In particular it includes the formerly residual range Q^(sigma/2)<c<H_TQ^(sigma/4), whether H_P is below or above one.
97e9b97caca25b8d.proof:
Separate each uniformly scaled-smooth amplitude in the four logarithmic coordinates by an absolutely summable Fourier series, exactly as in facts ec9d666ae1756a03 and 0d53c27d174b26ed. Absorb the four one-variable modes into d,nu,alpha,gamma. The condition gcd(up,c)=1 separates as gcd(u,c)=gcd(p,c)=1 and is also absorbed. Remove gcd(u,p)=1 by 1_{(u,p)=1}=1-1_{p|u}.

Fix c,F and write v=F/H_P. Put q_0=Q_c=Q/c. Before invoking fact 4cae52efa792b9ef, verify its polynomial u-support with the fixed exponent K'=2. From U_cY_c<=CB and Y_c>=H_TQ^sigma/2,
u<2U_c<<Q^(1-sigma).                                        (1)
On the other hand, c<=H_TQ^(sigma/4)=Q^(beta-1+sigma/4), so
q>=q_0=Q/c>=Q^(2-beta-sigma/4).                              (2)
Since beta<=6/5-2kappa, the exponent in (2) is greater than 3/4. Hence q^2>=Q^(3/2), and (1) gives u<=q^2 for all sufficiently large Q, uniformly in the fixed comparability constants. Thus the interval in u is contained in [1,q^2], as required by fact 4cae52efa792b9ef with K'=2.

We first treat the unrestricted term. The remaining hypotheses of fact 4cae52efa792b9ef hold with frequency parameter 2F whenever 2F<=Y_c and 8FY_c<q throughout q~q_0. Summing its estimate over O(q_0) moduli and restoring H_P^(-1), while using U_cY_c~B, gives
Q^epsilon |omega_{c,F}|[
 c^(-1)G^(1/2)Q^2(H_T/Y_c)^(1/2)v^(1/2)
 +c^(-5/4)Q^(7/4)(H_TY_c)^(1/2)v
 +c^(-3/4)Q^(7/4)H_T v].                                      (3)
Indeed the first term is q_0U_c(FY_c)^(1/2)/H_P. For the second use
{U_c(1+U_c/q_0)}^(1/2)<=U_c^(1/2)+U_cq_0^(-1/2);
the resulting terms are q_0^(5/4)(BY_c)^(1/2)v and q_0^(3/4)Bv, which are exactly the last two terms of (3).

For p|u, the number of supported (u,p) pairs is O(Q^epsilon U_c), by the quotient count in facts 664a92777dc5f5db and ea623cefa72d3a76. Summing q and h and restoring H_P^(-1) bounds this diagonal block by
Q^epsilon |omega_{c,F}| c^(-1)Q^2(H_T/Y_c)v
<=Q^epsilon |omega_{c,F}|c^(-1)Q^(2-sigma)v.                 (4)

We verify that (3)-(4) cover a long enough frequency range uniformly in c. Since Y_c>=H_TQ^sigma/2,
Y_c/H_P>=GQ^sigma/2>=Q^eta/2.                                (5)
Also c<=H_TQ^(sigma/4), Y_c<=Z, H_TZ=Q^(1/2-3sigma), and G>=Q^(-sigma+eta), hence
q_0/(H_PY_c)=QG/(cH_TY_c)
>=GQ^(3/2-beta+11sigma/4)
>=Q^(3/2-beta+7sigma/4+eta).                                 (6)
The final exponent is at least 3/10+7sigma/4+eta. Thus for every v<=Q^(eta/2), both 2F<=Y_c and 8FY_c<q hold for all sufficiently large Q.

The dyadic sums in this analytic range cost no power: |omega_{c,F}|v^(1/2) and |omega_{c,F}|v are bounded for v<=1 and summable for v>1 after choosing J_0>3. We now read off fixed savings from (3)-(4). First,
G^(1/2)(H_T/Y_c)^(1/2)
<=Q^((sigma-eta)/2)Q^(-sigma/2)=Q^(-eta/2).                  (7)
Second, H_TY_c<=H_TZ=Q^(1/2-3sigma), so
Q^(7/4)(H_TY_c)^(1/2)<=Q^(2-3sigma/2).                       (8)
Third,
Q^(7/4)H_T=Q^(beta+3/4)<=Q^(39/20-2kappa).                   (9)
The diagonal (4) saves sigma. Summing c costs only
sum_{c|L_src}(c^(-1)+c^(-5/4)+c^(-3/4))<=tau(|L_src|)<<Q^epsilon.  (10)
Thus the analytic frequency range contributes O(Q^(2-delta_1)) for a fixed delta_1>0.

For v>Q^(eta/2), bound the displayed sum directly. The q,u,p,h counts and H_P^(-1) give
<<Q^epsilon(QB/c)v|omega_{c,F}|.                              (11)
Sum c by the divisor bound and choose the fixed decay order J_0 sufficiently large in terms of eta and beta<=6/5. The dyadic tail in (11) is O(Q^(2-delta_2)). This also covers H_P<1: every integer frequency then has v>1, and it is treated by (3) when v<=Q^(eta/2) or by (11) otherwise.

Take delta smaller than delta_1 and delta_2 and absorb the fixed projective norm and polylogarithmic labels. The target in the displayed character is a unit modulo q by the theorem's explicit support condition gcd(L_src/c,q)=1; no incidence-level descent claim is needed for this abstract estimate. This proves the theorem.

glossary.C_med: The selected exact target-gcd divisors through the upper medium-band edge.
glossary.T_c: The complete-frequency descended interval-prime trace on exact target-gcd layer c.

985515aa5d2117fe.title: EXACT FOURIER FORM OF THE THREE-TERM CENTERED RECIPROCAL-SLOPE COVARIANCE
985515aa5d2117fe.author: slava chan
985515aa5d2117fe.statement:
EXACT FOURIER FORM OF THE THREE-TERM CENTERED RECIPROCAL-SLOPE COVARIANCE.

Let p be a prime, let cal Q be a finite set of positive integers none divisible by p, let A be an integer, and let a_q be arbitrary complex coefficients supported on cal Q. For r modulo p define

C_p(r)=sum_{q_1,q_2 in cal Q}a_{q_1}conjugate(a_{q_2})
 [1_{r congruent A(q_1bar-q_2bar) mod p}-1/p],              (1)
where bars denote inverses modulo p. For h modulo p put
  S_p(h)=sum_{q in cal Q}a_q e_p(hAqbar),                    (2)
where e_p(t)=exp(2 pi i t/p). Then exactly

C_p(r)=1/p sum_{h modulo p, h nonzero}|S_p(h)|^2e_p(-hr).   (3)

In particular the zero additive frequency is absent identically. For every function W on Z/pZ define
  What(k)=sum_{r modulo p}W(r)e_p(-kr).                      (4)
Then the weighted local covariance has the exact form

sum_{r modulo p}W(r)|C_p(r)|^2
 =1/p^2 sum_{h_1,h_2 nonzero modulo p}
   |S_p(h_1)|^2|S_p(h_2)|^2 What(h_1-h_2).                  (5)

For the complete residue window W=1 this reduces to

sum_{r modulo p}|C_p(r)|^2
 =1/p sum_{h nonzero modulo p}|S_p(h)|^4.                   (6)

Equations (3)-(6) retain the complete physical centering. Indeed, direct expansion of the left side of (5) gives, for two ordered q-pairs with
  I_1=1_{p|A(q_2-q_1)-rq_1q_2},
  I_2=1_{p|A(q_4-q_3)-rq_3q_4},                             (7)
the single bracket
  I_1I_2-(I_1+I_2)/p+1/p^2.                                (8)
Thus the incidence-incidence, cross, and center terms are the three parts of one nonnegative covariance; (3) shows that their assembly is exactly removal of h=0. Bounds obtained by taking absolute values of the three terms separately do not represent the nonzero-frequency fourth moment in (5).

If W is real and nonnegative, the left sides of (5)-(6) are nonnegative, although individual terms on the right side of (5) need not be. If W is an indicator or smooth weight supported on a short residue interval, (5) is the exact short-window fourth-moment form. No bound for (5) is asserted.
985515aa5d2117fe.proof:
Additive orthogonality gives

1_{r congruent A(q_1bar-q_2bar) mod p}
 =1/p sum_{h modulo p}
   e_p(h[Aq_1bar-Aq_2bar-r]).                               (9)

After multiplication by a_{q_1}conjugate(a_{q_2}) and summation over q_1,q_2, the h-th term in (9) is
  S_p(h)conjugate(S_p(h))e_p(-hr)=|S_p(h)|^2e_p(-hr).
At h=0 one has
  |S_p(0)|^2=|sum_q a_q|^2
 =sum_{q_1,q_2}a_{q_1}conjugate(a_{q_2}),                   (10)
which is exactly the contribution subtracted by 1/p in (1). Removing h=0 proves (3).

Multiply (3) by its complex conjugate:

|C_p(r)|^2=1/p^2 sum_{h_1,h_2 nonzero}
 |S_p(h_1)|^2|S_p(h_2)|^2e_p((h_2-h_1)r).                  (11)

Multiplying by W(r), summing r, and using definition (4) gives What(h_1-h_2), proving (5). If W=1, its transform is p at k=0 and zero otherwise, so (5) becomes (6).

Finally, substitute (1) and its conjugate into |C_p(r)|^2. The two real centered factors multiply as
  (I_1-1/p)(I_2-1/p)=I_1I_2-(I_1+I_2)/p+1/p^2,
which proves (7)-(8). Nonnegativity for W>=0 is immediate from the left side of (5).

glossary.C_p(r): The centered autocorrelation of the inverse-residue coefficient distribution at shift r modulo p.
glossary.S_p(h): The incomplete reciprocal exponential sum whose nonzero-frequency fourth moment equals the centered slope covariance.

989b464fc741150b.title: BUFFER-EXTENDED COMPLETE-FREQUENCY TWO-ROUGH-PRIME C2 TRACE
989b464fc741150b.author: slava chan
989b464fc741150b.statement:
BUFFER-EXTENDED COMPLETE-FREQUENCY TWO-ROUGH-PRIME C2 TRACE.

Fix integers J,C_A>=1, a constant C>=1, and 0<kappa<=1/100. Put sigma=kappa/100 and beta_1=6/5-3sigma. Let Q be sufficiently large, let 1<=beta<=beta_1, and put
B=Q^beta, H_T=B/Q, L=H_TQ^sigma, S_0=H_T^2Q^(3sigma), Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma).

Let V,P_1,P_2>=1 be dyadic scales, put
nu=log V/log Q, a=log P_1/log Q, b=log P_2/log Q,
and assume
0<=nu<=2beta-2+3sigma,
a<=b, a,b>=3/2-beta-3sigma,
and C^(-1)B<=VP_1P_2<=CB.
Let xi_v be supported on squarefree V<=v<2V, with v<=S_0 and every prime divisor of v at most L, and satisfy |xi_v|<=tau_J(v).

Let A be a fixed nonzero integer with |A|<=Q^(C_A), let |c_q|<=1 for Q<=q<2Q, let G>0 and put H_P=H_T/G. For every dyadic integer F>=1, let nu_F(h) be supported on F<=|h|<2F with |nu_F(h)|<=tau_J(|h|), let omega_F satisfy for every fixed J_0>=1
|omega_F|<=C(J_0)min(1,(F/H_P)^(-J_0)),
and let Psi_F be a fixed-complexity uniformly scaled-smooth projective amplitude in q/Q, |h|/F, v/V, p_1/P_1 and p_2/P_2.

Define T_C2 by the literal prefactor H_P^(-1), summed over all F, q, h, v and distinct ordered primes p_1<p_2 with p_i on P_i, p_i>=Z and gcd(vp_1p_2,q)=1, coefficient
omega_F c_q nu_F(h) xi_v Psi_F,
and phase
e_q(Ah(vp_1p_2)^(-1)).
Assume the ordered prime cells are refined so that either P_2>=2P_1, when p_1<p_2 is automatic, or P_1=P_2 and the full coefficient and amplitude before imposing p_1<p_2 are symmetric under p_1 and p_2.

(i) If G>=1, then T_C2=O(GQ^(2-delta_1)) for some fixed delta_1>0.
(ii) If 0<eta<sigma and Q^(-sigma+eta)<=G<=Q^(sigma-eta), then T_C2=O(Q^(2-delta_2)) for some fixed delta_2>0.

The estimate includes H_P<1, every actual dyadic integer-frequency block, a fixed possibly nonunit target A, unrestricted gcd(h,q), both rough-prime orderings after cell refinement, equal prime-scale cells, and the repeated-prime diagonal introduced by equal-cell symmetrization. It is uniform under polylogarithmically many inherited source, parent, fixed-U, high, collision, provenance, sign, dyadic and uniformly projective smooth labels acting as label scalars or absorbable into the displayed coefficient class. The phase has no modulus-dependent Type-I unit in the separated-outer subtrace. No arbitrary joint deletion mask is allowed. The theorem estimates only complete C2 anatomy and asserts no selected diagonal C2 cell, C3, later-beta, moving actual-Z, endpoint, PMD, logical bad-N, DCE, or Goldbach conclusion.
989b464fc741150b.proof:
Fixed dyadic endpoint constants change exponent equalities by O(1/log Q); every inequality below has a fixed sigma margin, so for sufficiently large Q these errors are absorbed by replacing one displayed sigma of margin when necessary. Thus we write
nu+a+b=beta                                                         (1)
inside the exponent audit.

Put L_beta=2beta-2, U_beta=3-2beta and w=nu+a. The following three comparisons are mutually exclusive and exhaustive:
Case 1: w<=L_beta+3sigma;
Case 2: L_beta+3sigma<w<=U_beta-4sigma;
Case 3: w>U_beta-4sigma.                                            (2)

In Case 1 group v and p_1 into s=vp_1, of scale
VP_1=Q^w<=H_T^2Q^(3sigma)=S_0.                                      (3)
The grouped coefficient is divisor-bounded after logarithmic Fourier separation because the number of representations s=vp_1 is at most tau(s). We prove global separation from the final prime. From (1)-(2),
b=beta-w>=2-beta-3sigma,                                             (4)
whereas a<=w<=2beta-2+3sigma. Hence
b-a>=4-3beta-6sigma.
At beta<=beta_1 this is at least
4-3(6/5-3sigma)-6sigma=2/5+3sigma>0.                                (5)
Therefore P_2/P_1 grows by a fixed power of Q. For large Q every supported p_1 is smaller than every supported p_2. Since every prime divisor of v is at most L<Z<=p_2, every supported s is coprime to every final prime p_2. Fact d399d1df6821854c applies with outer scale VP_1 and final prime scale P_2. It gives O(GQ^(2-delta)) in regime (i) and O(Q^(2-delta)) in regime (ii), including all frequencies and its internal proper-prime-power and Vaughan branches. Equation (5) also shows that an equal prime-scale cell cannot occur in Case 1.

In Case 2 select S=VP_1 and T=P_2. In Case 3 select S=P_2 and T=VP_1. We now recheck the endpoint geometry through beta_1 instead of citing the old beta range of fact 3b1bda56ad927c5e.

In Case 2, after absorbing dyadic endpoints,
H_T^2Q^(2sigma)<=S<=Q^(1-3sigma)/H_T^2.                             (6)
Indeed the strict lower exponent is L_beta+3sigma and the upper exponent is U_beta-4sigma.

For Case 3, the upper bound on the selected exponent b follows from
b=beta-w<beta-(U_beta-4sigma)=3beta-3+4sigma,
and
(U_beta-4sigma)-(3beta-3+4sigma)=6-5beta-8sigma>=7sigma.             (7)
For the lower bound, a<=b and a+b=beta-nu give
b>=(beta-nu)/2>=1-beta/2-3sigma/2.                                  (8)
The difference between the last expression and L_beta+4sigma is
(6-5beta-11sigma)/2>=2sigma.                                        (9)
Thus Case 3 satisfies (6), with at least as much margin. In both cases ST is comparable to B=QH_T.

The coefficient on S is divisor-bounded. In Case 2 it is the convolution of xi_v with the p_1 indicator; in Case 3 it is the p_2 indicator. The complementary coefficient is likewise bounded by a fixed divisor function. Smooth product cutoffs and the five-variable amplitude have uniformly summable logarithmic Fourier expansions, preserving these bounds and the fixed projective norm.

Fix an actual dyadic frequency block F and put u_F=F/H_P. Apply fact 42720f6d803c4640 with frequency parameter F, total-product parameter H_T and block imbalance
G_F=H_T/F=G/u_F.
Because the literal prefactor is H_P^(-1)=u_FF^(-1), the resulting four terms, apart from Q^epsilon, are
G^(1/4)u_F^(3/4)Q^2H_T^(1/2)S^(-1/4),
G^(1/4)u_F^(3/4)Q^(7/4)H_T^(1/2)S^(1/4),
u_FQ^2H_TS^(-1/2),
u_FQ^(7/4)H_T.                                                       (10)
The fixed target A may be nonunit and gcd(h,q) is unrestricted in that fact.

The window (6) bounds the four baseline expressions in (10) by
Q^(2-sigma/2), Q^(2-3sigma/4), Q^(2-sigma), Q^(2-5sigma/4),        (11)
respectively. For the fourth bound, nonemptiness of (6) gives
H_T^4<=Q^(1-5sigma).
The Fourier hypothesis gives
sum_F |omega_F|u_F^(3/4)+sum_F |omega_F|u_F=O(1).                   (12)
If G>=1, use G^(1/4)<=G in (10)-(12), proving the required GQ^2 normalization with a fixed saving. On the near-balanced strip,
G^(1/4)<=Q^((sigma-eta)/4).
The first two terms of (11) then retain savings at least sigma/4+eta/4 and sigma/2+eta/4; the last two retain their displayed savings. Thus Cases 2 and 3 satisfy (ii).

It remains to impose p_1<p_2. If P_2>=2P_1, the order is automatic apart from empty endpoints. If P_1=P_2, symmetry on each F block gives exactly
sum_{p_1<p_2}Phi(p_1,p_2)
=(1/2)(sum_{p_1,p_2}Phi(p_1,p_2)-sum_p Phi(p,p)).                    (13)
The unrestricted double-prime product in (13) is covered by Cases 2 and 3, because (5) excludes Case 1 in an equal cell. The repeated-prime diagonal is paid absolutely. On the F block it is at most
Q^epsilon |omega_F|u_F QVP_1
=Q^epsilon |omega_F|u_F QB/P_2
<=Q^epsilon |omega_F|u_F QB/Z.                                      (14)
Now
log_Q(QB/Z)=2beta-1/2+3sigma
<=19/10-3sigma.                                                       (15)
Summing (14) with (12) gives O(Q^(19/10-2sigma)), which is power-saving relative to Q^2 and hence also relative to GQ^2 for G>=1. This diagonal is only the exact subtraction term in (13); no repeated prime belongs to the squarefree C2 anatomy itself.

All ordered cell pairs, signs, source and projective labels are polylogarithmically numerous and are absorbed by shrinking the fixed saving. The original C2 coefficient is xi_v=mu(v), and p_1,p_2 are distinct and ordered; no collision or provenance coordinate is dropped. Combining the three cases and (13)-(15) proves (i) and (ii) with all scope restrictions.

glossary.T_C2: The complete dyadic-frequency two-rough-prime reciprocal trace in this fact.

9977e3b55fc1f8da.title: PHASE-CONJUGATION OBSTRUCTION TO AN INCIDENCE-ONLY C4 RECIPROCAL-SLOPE LARGE SIEVE. Let I be a finite nonempty set of mode rows i. For each i let X_i be a finite nonempty set and let Psi_i:X_i->C satisfy |Psi_i(x)|=1. For arbitrary coefficients a_i(x) define
9977e3b55fc1f8da.author: slava chan
9977e3b55fc1f8da.statement:
PHASE-CONJUGATION OBSTRUCTION TO AN INCIDENCE-ONLY C4 RECIPROCAL-SLOPE LARGE SIEVE. Let I be a finite nonempty set of mode rows i. For each i let X_i be a finite nonempty set and let Psi_i:X_i->C satisfy |Psi_i(x)|=1. For arbitrary coefficients a_i(x) define
S_i(a)=sum_{x in X_i}a_i(x)Psi_i(x).                               (1)
There exist coefficients with |a_i(x)|=1 for every i,x such that simultaneously
|S_i(a)|=#X_i                                                     (2)
for every i. Consequently no upper bound for the family of transforms (1) that improves the rowwise l1 bound can follow solely from the sets X_i, their incidence or fibre multiplicities, and the unit-modulus phases Psi_i if the coefficients are allowed to depend arbitrarily on i.

Apply this to the imbalanced semiprime modes remaining after fact e4b8a9247511a282: take i=(lambda,r), X_i to be any nonempty set of physical pairs (q,h) surviving the exact support and coprimality gates, and
Psi_i(q,h)=e_{v_lambda r}(A h[q(D_lambda/r)]^(-1)).                 (3)
Then the actual modulus ranges and reciprocal-slope incidence alone do not prove C4-PAIR-LS for arbitrary bounded row-dependent coefficient arrays. A successful supplier must use additional linkage satisfied by the literal source coefficients across lambda,r,q,h, or preserve an earlier signed recombination. This is a theorem-interface obstruction only: the phase-conjugating coefficients are not asserted to equal the literal C4 coefficients, and no failure of C4-PAIR-LS, C4, or Goldbach is asserted.
9977e3b55fc1f8da.proof:
For every i and x in X_i choose
a_i(x)=overline{Psi_i(x)}.                                        (4)
Then |a_i(x)|=1 and every summand in (1) equals one. Therefore
S_i(a)=sum_{x in X_i}1=#X_i,
which proves (2) simultaneously for all rows. The construction changes neither X_i nor any incidence relation among its elements.

Equation (3) has absolute value one because it is an additive character. Fact 16e3378d8ed3c224 proves that (3) is exactly the physical reciprocal-slope phase of one C4 mode, with every support and unit gate retained in X_i. Applying (4) independently on each surviving row preserves those gates and yields (2). Thus any proof whose hypotheses record only these supports, gates, modulus ceilings, slope fibres and a pointwise coefficient bound necessarily includes the phase-conjugating model and cannot deduce cancellation below its rowwise l1 scale. Since the literal coefficient has more structure than an arbitrary bounded row array, the construction makes only the stated no-inference conclusion.

9a34f6ae3a1ceca8.title: ACTUAL C1,C2,C3,C4 SAME-RESIDUE ALL-FOUR JOINT ENERGY FOR ALL PHYSICAL HEIGHT SIGNS
9a34f6ae3a1ceca8.author: slava chan
9a34f6ae3a1ceca8.statement:
ACTUAL C1,C2,C3,C4 SAME-RESIDUE ALL-FOUR JOINT ENERGY FOR ALL PHYSICAL HEIGHT SIGNS.

Adopt the hypotheses and notation of fact dbfaad4be3d523a8, except that the four physical heights need not lie in one common signed interval. Thus p is a selected first-nonresonant prime of an actual top C1,C2,C3, or C4 row, t=n/p lies in one natural dyadic interval T<=t<2T contained in J_p, and
2H<p,qquad 2T<p,qquad H,T>=p^delta                            (1)
for a fixed 0<delta<1. Each physical height h_i may independently lie in either
H<=h_i<2H
or
-2H<h_i<=-H.                                                    (2)

Fix a nonzero physical q-residue x modulo p. Let O_{p,x}^{all-sign} be any scalar source-weighted suboccupancy of the actual same-residue four-row balance
h_1/t_1+h_2/t_2=h_3/t_3+h_4/t_4 mod p,                         (3)
where q_i is congruent to x modulo p for every i, every literal tuple deletion may be retained, and the source-copy coefficients are the literal C1-C4 coefficients used in fact dbfaad4be3d523a8.

For every fixed A>=2, epsilon_0>0, and
0<eta<min(1,4delta),
O_{p,x}^{all-sign}
 <<_{A,delta,eta,epsilon_0}
 Q^(4epsilon_0)(1+Q/p)^4
 (1+H/H_P)^(-4A)
 (HT)^4p^(-eta).                                               (4)
If X_p is the set of nonzero residues represented by q in [Q,2Q), then
sum_{x in X_p}O_{p,x}^{all-sign}
 <<_{A,delta,eta,epsilon_0}
 Q^(4epsilon_0)min(p,Q+1)(1+Q/p)^4
 (1+H/H_P)^(-4A)
 (HT)^4p^(-eta).                                               (5)
Hence all sixteen physical-height sign sectors of the actual scalar C1-C4 all-four same-residue stratum receive the joint-energy saving, with no height-l1 tax.

The scope exclusions of fact dbfaad4be3d523a8 remain unchanged: this theorem does not pay the three two-block pole partitions, Top B, unequal q-residues, zero local heights outside (1), any remaining-face vector norm, or the complete joint-completion Hilbert assembly.
9a34f6ae3a1ceca8.proof:
Partition the occupancy in (3) according to the sixteen choices
s_i=sgn(h_i) in {+1,-1}.
For one fixed choice put
h_i^*=|h_i|,qquad H<=h_i^*<2H,
and let the TT-star position signs be
sigma_1=sigma_2=+1,qquad sigma_3=sigma_4=-1.
Then (3) is equivalent to
sum_{i=1}^4 epsilon_i h_i^*/t_i=0 mod p,qquad
epsilon_i=sigma_i s_i in {+1,-1}.                              (6)

The coefficient proof in fact dbfaad4be3d523a8 uses only |h| and fact 3286b0e75a3ea94a. It therefore gives, on each independently chosen signed interval, the same nonnegative domination
A_{p,x}(h^*,t)
 <<Q^epsilon_0(1+Q/p)(1+h^*/H_P)^(-A),                         (7)
and the numerator weight has supremum-plus-total-variation at most
2(1+H/H_P)^(-A).

Apply fact ae1623e3b77d7695 to the sign pattern (epsilon_i) in (6), using (1) and the weights in (7). Its equation (10) gives exactly the right side of (4) for this fixed physical-sign sector. There are sixteen sectors, so summing them changes only the implied constant and proves (4).

Fact dbfaad4be3d523a8 also proves
#X_p<=min(p-1,Q+1).
Summing (4) over x proves (5). No excluded sector or vector operator is introduced by the sign partition, which proves the scope paragraph.

glossary.O_{p,x}^{all-sign}: The actual scalar all-four same-q-residue occupancy after aggregating all sixteen physical-height sign patterns.

9a80432a29fc15d2.title: INDUCED-CONDUCTOR FACTORIZATION AND LOW-CONDUCTOR DELETION FOR THE FORWARD E11 SPECTRAL TRACE. Assume the hypotheses and notation of facts fc442085ff47a053, 75d461ea0320c1a8, and 12515655a5e7ed7c. Let chi be a nonprincipal character modulo the squarefree descended modulus q_E. Let f be its primitive conductor, write q_E=fs, and let chi^* be the primitive character modulo f inducing chi. Then (f,s)=1 and
9a80432a29fc15d2.author: slava chan
9a80432a29fc15d2.statement:
INDUCED-CONDUCTOR FACTORIZATION AND LOW-CONDUCTOR DELETION FOR THE FORWARD E11 SPECTRAL TRACE. Assume the hypotheses and notation of facts fc442085ff47a053, 75d461ea0320c1a8, and 12515655a5e7ed7c. Let chi be a nonprincipal character modulo the squarefree descended modulus q_E. Let f be its primitive conductor, write q_E=fs, and let chi^* be the primitive character modulo f inducing chi. Then (f,s)=1 and
 G_{N,q_E}(chi)=0 if (f,N)>1,
while, if (f,N)=1,
 G_{N,q_E}(chi)=c_s(N) chi^*(-N s^(-1)) tau_f(conjugate(chi^*)),
where s^(-1) is taken modulo f and
 tau_f(conjugate(chi^*))=sum_{u (mod f),(u,f)=1}e_f(u)conjugate(chi^*(u)).
In the nonzero case |tau_f(conjugate(chi^*))|=f^(1/2).

For F>=1, define T_E11^np,<=F to be the complete part of the exact character reconstruction of T_E11^crit from nonprincipal characters whose primitive conductor f satisfies f<=F, retaining every literal coefficient, character value, source mask and conjugate-frequency pair. Then for every epsilon>0, uniformly on each E11 central-strip label,
 |T_E11^np,<=F| <<_epsilon R F^(3/2)x^epsilon.              (1)
Fix omega with 0<omega<2/9-3eta_t and put F_0=x^(2/9-3eta_t-omega). After summing all literal labels and marker copies,
 |T_E11^np,<=F_0|<<x^(1-delta_low)                          (2)
for some fixed delta_low=delta_low(eta_t,omega)>0. Together with fact 12515655a5e7ed7c, this reduces T_E11^crit, up to a fixed-power error, to primitive conductors f>F_0 with (f,N)=1. No estimate for that large-conductor trace, no E21/E22 assertion and no Goldbach implication is made.
9a80432a29fc15d2.proof:
We first prove the exact conductor formula. Since q_E is squarefree, the character group modulo q_E is the product of the character groups modulo its prime factors. The primitive conductor f is the product of precisely those primes at which the local component of chi is nonprincipal; the remaining product is s=q_E/f. This proves (f,s)=1 and identifies chi with chi^* on the f-coordinate and the principal character on the s-coordinate.

Use the Chinese remainder parametrization u=(u_f,u_s) of the units modulo fs. Additive CRT gives
 e_{fs}(-Nu)=e_f(-N s^(-1)u_f)e_s(-N f^(-1)u_s),            (3)
where the displayed inverses are taken in the corresponding local modulus. Therefore the definition in fact 75d461ea0320c1a8 factors as
 G_{N,fs}(chi)
 =[sum_{u_f (mod f)}^*e_f(-N s^(-1)u_f)conjugate(chi^*(u_f))]
  [sum_{u_s (mod s)}^*e_s(-N f^(-1)u_s)].                  (4)
Multiplication by the unit f^(-1) permutes the units modulo s, so the second bracket is c_s(N).

Because f is squarefree and chi^* is primitive, every prime-local component of chi^* is nonprincipal. If a prime p divides both f and N, the p-local additive character in the first bracket of (4) is constant one, while the sum of a nonprincipal character over the units modulo p is zero. Hence the first bracket, and therefore G_{N,fs}(chi), vanishes when (f,N)>1.

Suppose now (f,N)=1. The multiplier A=-N s^(-1) is a unit modulo f. The change of variables v=Au in the first bracket of (4) gives
 sum_{u (mod f)}^*e_f(Au)conjugate(chi^*(u))
 =chi^*(A)tau_f(conjugate(chi^*)).                          (5)
This proves the exact displayed factorization. It remains to establish the magnitude without importing a theorem. By CRT, the Gauss sum in (5) is a product of prime-local Gauss sums up to unit character factors. For a nonprincipal character psi modulo a prime p and a unit A, put
 T=sum_{u (mod p)}^*e_p(Au)conjugate(psi(u)).
Then, after writing u=tv,
 |T|^2=sum_{t (mod p)}^*conjugate(psi(t))sum_{v (mod p)}^*e_p(Av(t-1)).
The inner sum is p-1 when t=1 and -1 otherwise. Since the sum of conjugate(psi(t)) over all units is zero, |T|^2=(p-1)+1=p. Multiplication over p|f gives |tau_f(conjugate(chi^*))|=f^(1/2).

We now prove (1). Use the pointwise literal Fourier majorant from fact 0a39d6be778e7dc9 on g=1:
 |lambda_{1,d,r,h}|<<_J(M/r)(log x)^2(1+|h|M/r)^(-J)       (6)
for any fixed J>=3. Every source and E11 restriction deletes indices, and fact fc442085ff47a053 proves that the total variation of the actual normalized-marker copies is bounded by an absolute constant. The continuous reciprocity factor in fact 75d461ea0320c1a8 has modulus one.

Fix h. Group squarefree d by c=(d,h), put q=d/c, and then q=fs according to the primitive conductor. In the nonzero case above, summing the absolute spectral coefficient over all primitive chi^* modulo f costs at most
 phi(f) [f^(1/2)|c_s(N)|]/[phi(f)phi(s)]
 =f^(1/2)|c_s(N)|/phi(s).                                  (7)
There are no more than phi(f) primitive characters, which justifies the inequality. Drop the exact gcd and coprimality conditions to enlarge the sum. Since c divides |h|, equations (7) and the squarefree Ramanujan-divisor calculation proved self-contained in fact 12515655a5e7ed7c give
 sum_{d comparable to D} sum_{nonprincipal chi (mod q), cond(chi)<=F}
 |G_{N,q}(chi)|/phi(q)
 <<tau(|h|)tau(N)log(2D)sum_{f<=F}f^(1/2)
 <<tau(|h|)tau(N)F^(3/2)log(2D).                            (8)
Indeed, at fixed c and f the remaining s-range is contained in s<=C D/(cf), and fact 12515655a5e7ed7c proves sum_s |c_s(N)|/phi(s)<<tau(N)log(2D).

Insert (8) into (6). On the E11 strip, the scale relations used in fact 12515655a5e7ed7c give r/M>1 for large x, and hence
 sum_{h nonzero}tau(|h|)(1+|h|M/r)^(-J)<<_epsilon(r/M)x^epsilon.
Thus the factors M/r cancel and the contribution at fixed r is O_epsilon(F^(3/2)x^epsilon). There are O(R) possible r, so (1) follows. Literal labels and marker copies cost only powers of log x.

Finally fc442085ff47a053 gives R<=D^(4/3+6eta_t), while D<=2x^(1/2). Hence R<<x^(2/3+3eta_t). With F=F_0, the exponent in (1) is at most
 2/3+3eta_t+(3/2)(2/9-3eta_t-omega)+epsilon
 =1-(3/2)(eta_t+omega)+epsilon.
Choose epsilon<(3/4)(eta_t+omega). This proves (2) with a fixed positive delta_low. Fact 12515655a5e7ed7c pays conductor one, and the exact vanishing above removes every remaining conductor sharing a prime with N. Therefore only the stated large primitive conductors remain.

glossary.F_0: The power cutoff x^(2/9-3eta_t-omega) for low primitive conductors.
glossary.T_E11^np,<=F: The complete nonprincipal E11 spectral component with primitive conductor at most F.
glossary.chi^*: The primitive character modulo f inducing chi.
glossary.delta_low: A fixed positive saving exponent for the low-conductor E11 component.
glossary.f: The primitive conductor of a nonprincipal character modulo q_E.

9aa1f62a0c74b011.title: Let \(N,P\) be positive integers. Define
9aa1f62a0c74b011.author: slava chan
9aa1f62a0c74b011.statement:
Let \(N,P\) be positive integers. Define
\[
 P_{\parallel N}=\prod_{p\mid N}p^{v_p(P)},\qquad
 P_{\perp N}=P/P_{\parallel N}.
\]
Thus every prime factor of \(P_{\parallel N}\) divides \(N\), and
\((P_{\perp N},N)=1\). Define the complete coprime divisor-sibling sum
\[
 C_N(P)=\sum_{\substack{q\mid P\\(q,N)=1}}
 \mu(q)\log(P/q),                                      \tag{1}
\]
and its complementary noncoprime face by
\[
 S_N^{\rm nc}(P)=
 \sum_{\substack{q\mid P\\(q,N)>1}}
 \mu(q)\log(P/q)
 =\Lambda(P)-C_N(P).                                   \tag{2}
\]
Then exactly
\[
 \boxed{
 C_N(P)=
 \begin{cases}
 \log P,&P_{\perp N}=1,\\
 \Lambda(P_{\perp N}),&P_{\perp N}>1.
 \end{cases}
 }                                                       \tag{3}
\]

In particular, let \(p,\ell\) be distinct primes with \(p\mid N\) and
\(\ell\nmid N\), and put \(P=p\ell\). Then
\[
 C_N(P)=\log\ell,\qquad \Lambda(P)=0,\qquad
 S_N^{\rm nc}(P)=-\log\ell.                             \tag{4}
\]
Thus, after the expansion
\[
 \Lambda(P)=\sum_{q\mid P}\mu(q)\log(P/q),
\]
the complete noncoprime divisor face can be nonzero on a composite
integer which is not a prime power. It cannot be deleted or bounded by
a proper-prime-power support count alone.

This does not contradict the support assertion in fact
\(967520f427b111c5\), which explicitly uses the different sibling
identity
\[
 \Lambda(P)=-\sum_{q\mid P}\mu(q)\log q.
\]
It proves that the support conclusion from that identity cannot be
transferred termwise to the moving \(\log(P/q)\) expansion used in
facts \(d97b0142b0d0a486\), \(a88b7867c1bc2fd9\), and
\(4a1d6a8cfcc6d864\).
9aa1f62a0c74b011.proof:
The divisors \(q\mid P\) satisfying \((q,N)=1\) are exactly the
divisors of \(P_{\perp N}\). Hence
\[
\begin{split}
 C_N(P)
 &=\sum_{q\mid P_{\perp N}}\mu(q)
   \{\log P-\log q\}\\
 &=\log P\sum_{q\mid P_{\perp N}}\mu(q)
   -\sum_{q\mid P_{\perp N}}\mu(q)\log q.               \tag{5}
\end{split}
\]
If \(P_{\perp N}=1\), the first divisor sum consists only of \(q=1\),
so (5) equals \(\log P\).

If \(P_{\perp N}>1\), then
\[
 \sum_{q\mid P_{\perp N}}\mu(q)=0.
\]
Möbius inversion of
\(\log n=\sum_{d\mid n}\Lambda(d)\) gives
\[
 -\sum_{q\mid n}\mu(q)\log q=\Lambda(n)\qquad(n>1).
\]
Applying this with \(n=P_{\perp N}\) proves (3).

For \(P=p\ell\) under the displayed prime hypotheses,
\(P_{\parallel N}=p\) and \(P_{\perp N}=\ell\). Equation (3) gives
\(C_N(P)=\Lambda(\ell)=\log\ell\). Since \(p\ell\) has two distinct
prime factors, \(\Lambda(p\ell)=0\), and (2) gives
\(S_N^{\rm nc}(P)=-\log\ell\). This proves (4) and the claimed
support obstruction.

Fact \(967520f427b111c5\) states its prime-power support consequence
under the \(-\mu(q)\log q\) expansion. Equations (1)--(5) concern the
\(\mu(q)\log(P/q)\) expansion, whose individual and restricted sibling
subtotals differ. Therefore the two statements are compatible, while
the proposed termwise migration is ruled out.

glossary.C_N(P): the complete log(P/q) divisor-sibling sum restricted to q coprime to N
glossary.P_{\\parallel N}: the factor of P supported on primes dividing N
glossary.P_{\\perp N}: the complementary factor of P coprime to N

9b36a7ed849198d9.title: SHARP FAILURE OF AN ARBITRARY a-DEPENDENT VECTOR EXTENSION OF THE COMPULSORY-PRIME TIGHT FRAME
9b36a7ed849198d9.author: slava chan
9b36a7ed849198d9.statement:
SHARP FAILURE OF AN ARBITRARY a-DEPENDENT VECTOR EXTENSION OF THE COMPULSORY-PRIME TIGHT FRAME.

Assume p>2 and use r_C(a) from fact 0d1daae6c3854186, with C and a ranging over the nonzero residues modulo p. Define
 S_p=sum_{C nonzero}|r_C(a)|^2.                              (1)
Then S_p is independent of the nonzero residue a and equals
 S_p=p-1-1/(p-1).                                           (2)

Define the a-dependent coefficient vector
 eta_C(a)=overline(r_C(a)).                                  (3)
Then exactly
 1/(p-1)sum_{a nonzero}
  |sum_{C nonzero}eta_C(a)r_C(a)|^2
 =S_p
  {1/(p-1)sum_{a nonzero}sum_{C nonzero}|eta_C(a)|^2}.      (4)
Consequently no inequality
 1/(p-1)sum_a
  |sum_C v_C(a)r_C(a)|^2
 <=K
  {1/(p-1)sum_asum_C|v_C(a)|^2}                            (5)
can hold for every a-dependent coefficient family v_C(a) with a constant K independent of p. This remains true when |v_C(a)|<=1 is imposed.

The counterexample is scoped to arbitrary a-dependent vector coefficients. It does not assert that the actual shifted complementary projector P^{(p)}_{b',>F_0/p}(a) can realize (3), and it does not refute a source-specific vector restriction theorem for that projector. No ROP, CEN-MZB, C_small or Goldbach estimate is asserted.
9b36a7ed849198d9.proof:
Put c=1/(p-1). By definition,
 r_C(a)=e_p(Ca^(-1))+c.
For fixed nonzero a,
 |r_C(a)|^2
 =1+c^2+c e_p(Ca^(-1))+c e_p(-Ca^(-1)).                    (6)
As C ranges over the nonzero residues, multiplication by a^(-1) permutes those residues. Hence
 sum_{C nonzero}e_p(Ca^(-1))
 =sum_{C nonzero}e_p(-Ca^(-1))
 =-1.                                                        (7)
Summing (6) and using (7) gives
 S_p=(p-1)(1+c^2)-2c
    =p-1+(p-1)c^2-2c
    =p-1-c
    =p-1-1/(p-1).                                           (8)
This proves (2) and its independence of a.

For (3),
 sum_C eta_C(a)r_C(a)
 =sum_C|r_C(a)|^2
 =S_p                                                        (9)
for every nonzero a. Also
 sum_C|eta_C(a)|^2=S_p.                                     (10)
The normalized a-average of the squared magnitude in (9) is S_p^2, while the normalized coefficient energy in braces in (4) is S_p. This proves (4).

If (5) held for every a-dependent family, inserting (3) would give S_p<=K. But S_p tends to infinity with p, so no p-independent K exists. Finally
 |r_C(a)|<=1+c=p/(p-1).
Replace (3) by
 v_C(a)=(p-1)/p overline(r_C(a)).
Then |v_C(a)|<=1. Both sides of the ratio in (4) are multiplied by the same factor ((p-1)/p)^2, so the ratio remains S_p. This proves the bounded-coefficient assertion and every scope restriction.

glossary.S_p: The pointwise squared l2 mass sum_C|r_C(a)|^2.

9b40bc10b4d5e5fb.title: ABSOLUTE PAYMENT OF THE ZERO-PRIME AND ONE-PRIME C4 MODES, LEAVING ONLY THE SIX SEMIPRIME MODES. Adopt the literal scalar canonical-dilator block of facts 54029717e980dcb7, a3132ecd1bd44382 and 4a18a6fc30232be9. Thus Dcal<=D_lambda<2Dcal, B/2<=n_lambda<=2B, n_lambda=D_lambda v_lambda, every prime dividing D_lambda is at least Z, and the literal coefficients obey a fixed divisor-function envelope. Set z=1 in the transforms S_lambda,r of fact 16e3378d8ed3c224 and define
9b40bc10b4d5e5fb.author: slava chan
9b40bc10b4d5e5fb.statement:
ABSOLUTE PAYMENT OF THE ZERO-PRIME AND ONE-PRIME C4 MODES, LEAVING ONLY THE SIX SEMIPRIME MODES. Adopt the literal scalar canonical-dilator block of facts 54029717e980dcb7, a3132ecd1bd44382 and 4a18a6fc30232be9. Thus Dcal<=D_lambda<2Dcal, B/2<=n_lambda<=2B, n_lambda=D_lambda v_lambda, every prime dividing D_lambda is at least Z, and the literal coefficients obey a fixed divisor-function envelope. Set z=1 in the transforms S_lambda,r of fact 16e3378d8ed3c224 and define
E_j=sum_lambda sum_{r|D_lambda, omega(r)=j}
 c_lambda(r)|S_lambda,r(1)|^2,  j=0,1,2.                           (1)
Then, for every epsilon>0,
E_0<<_epsilon Q^epsilon BQ^2F^2/Dcal,                              (2)
E_1<<_epsilon Q^epsilon Z^2 BQ^2F^2/Dcal.                          (3)
Consequently E_0+E_1 is already bounded by the second term of the scalar C4-11-LS target and all five modes with omega(r)<=1 are paid absolutely.

For the remaining six modes, direct absolute summation gives
E_2<<_epsilon Q^epsilon BQ^2F^2/Z^2
=Q^epsilon (Dcal/Z^4)
 [Z^2 BQ^2F^2/Dcal].                                               (4)
Thus the first exact unabsorbed loss in the same absolute argument is Dcal/Z^4. The sole remaining scalar eleven-mode supplier may be restricted to
sum_lambda sum_{r|D_lambda, omega(r)=2}
 (r/D_lambda)|S_lambda,r(1)|^2
<<_epsilon Q^epsilon Z^2
 [BQF+BQ^2F^2/Dcal].                                               (C4-PAIR-LS)
This theorem identifies the six semiprime modes as the entire unpaid scalar core. Equation (4) is an upper bound and a no-fit of this direct absolute argument; it is not a lower bound for the literal coefficients and does not prove that C4-PAIR-LS is false. No vector-valued payment, C4-PAIR-LS estimate, C4 closure, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
9b40bc10b4d5e5fb.proof:
The fixed divisor-function envelope in fact 54029717e980dcb7 permits all coefficient, copy and logarithmic losses below to be absorbed into Q^epsilon. For one lambda and one r, equation (6) of fact 16e3378d8ed3c224 is a sum over
Q<=q<2Q, F<=|h|<2F.
There are O(QF) such pairs. Every additive phase and every zero-one or signed literal mask has absolute value at most one, while the scalar literal amplitude has the fixed divisor-function envelope. Therefore
|S_lambda,r(1)|<<_epsilon Q^epsilon QF.                             (5)
The same copy-count input used in fact 54029717e980dcb7 gives
sum_{B/2<=n<=2B}#Lambda_D(n)<<_epsilon Q^epsilon B.                 (6)

For r=1, fact a3132ecd1bd44382 gives
c_lambda(1)<=27/(2D_lambda)<=27/(2Dcal).                            (7)
Apply (5)-(7) and sum over lambda. This proves (2).

For r=p prime, the same fact gives
c_lambda(p)<=9p/(2D_lambda).
For each p|D_lambda, the quotient D_lambda/p is the product of the other three rough primes, so
p/D_lambda=1/(D_lambda/p)<=Z^(-3).
There are four prime divisors. Hence
sum_{p|D_lambda}c_lambda(p)<=18Z^(-3).                              (8)
We next use the literal pre-6/5 geometry. The existence of a row in this block gives
Dcal<=D_lambda<=n_lambda<=2B.                                      (9)
The proof of fact e58fc7c00f1683e6 establishes, uniformly on the pre-6/5 sliver and for sufficiently large Q,
Z^5>2B.                                                            (10)
Equations (9)-(10) give Dcal<Z^5, and therefore
Z^(-3)<Z^2/Dcal.                                                   (11)
Apply (5), (6), (8), and (11). This proves (3).

Finally suppose omega(r)=2. Fact a3132ecd1bd44382 gives
c_lambda(r)=r/D_lambda=1/(D_lambda/r).
The complementary factor D_lambda/r is a product of two rough primes, so
c_lambda(r)<=Z^(-2).
There are six such divisors r. Hence
sum_{r|D_lambda, omega(r)=2}c_lambda(r)<=6Z^(-2).                   (12)
Equations (5), (6), and (12) prove the first expression in (4). The displayed identity in (4) is algebraic.

Since the eleven modes are the disjoint union of j=0,1,2, equations (2)-(3) pay the first five modes. The j=2 coefficient is exactly r/D_lambda, so after deleting the already paid terms, the remaining assertion is precisely C4-PAIR-LS. The first term Z^2BQF has merely been retained in that sufficient target; the absolute estimate (4) compares to its second term. No cancellation estimate was used.

glossary.C4-PAIR-LS: The remaining scalar large-sieve estimate for the six modes with two active rough primes.
glossary.E_j: The scalar eleven-mode energy restricted to mode divisors r with omega(r)=j.

9b8cce52a98d22c8.title: CONGRUENT-SUPPORT RANK-ONE OBSTRUCTION TO A PURE SHORT-WINDOW DENSITY BOUND
9b8cce52a98d22c8.author: slava chan
9b8cce52a98d22c8.statement:
CONGRUENT-SUPPORT RANK-ONE OBSTRUCTION TO A PURE SHORT-WINDOW DENSITY BOUND.

Let p be a prime, let A be an integer not divisible by p, and let q_1,...,q_M be distinct positive integers, none divisible by p, which are all congruent to the same residue q_0 modulo p. Put b_{q_j}=1 and b_q=0 otherwise. Define S_p(h), T(k), T_0(k), T_neq(k), the exact slope-fibre sums B_lambda, and m_p(k) as in fact 27540b4094f677f4. Put
  D_slope=sum_lambda|B_lambda|^2.                            (1)
Then for every h and k modulo p,
  S_p(h)=M e_p(hA q_0^(-1)),                               (2)
  T(k)=m_p(k)M^4,                                          (3)
  T_0(k)=m_p(k)D_slope,                                    (4)
  T_neq(k)=m_p(k)(M^4-D_slope).                            (5)
Thus the rational-slope diagonal has been subtracted at every shift, but the remaining shifted family is still rank one.

Let W be the indicator of the singleton residue interval {0}. Then What(k)=1 for every k and
  1/p^2 sum_kWhat(k)T_neq(k)
   =(1-1/p)^2(M^4-D_slope).                                (6)
In particular this remainder has no universal factor 1/p coming solely from the singleton window.

There is an explicit dyadic growing-prime realization. Let p tend to infinity through the primes, put
  Q=p^2,  M=floor(p/2),                                    (7)
choose q_0 in [Q,Q+p) not divisible by p, and put
  q_j=q_0+jp,  0<=j<M.                                    (8)
Then all q_j lie in [Q,2Q), and for every eta>0,
  D_slope<<_eta Q^eta M^2.                                 (9)
In particular, choosing any fixed eta<1/2 gives
  D_slope=o(M^4),                                          (10)
and the left side of (6) is
  (1+o(1))M^4.                                             (11)
Its ratio to the density-scaled quantity M^4/p tends to infinity like p.

Therefore no PMD-SHIFTED-4MOM theorem for arbitrary bounded coefficients can assert only a rational-slope-diagonal term plus a pure L/p multiple of the remaining fourth-moment scale across all coefficient lengths. A valid theorem must also control congruent-support rank-one blocks, for example through a maximum residue-class multiplicity term, a range condition relating the q-length to p, or the actual non-arbitrary PMD source coefficients. This is a coefficient-class and range obstruction; it is not a counterexample to the literal arithmetic PMD estimate.
9b8cce52a98d22c8.proof:
Since every q_j is congruent to q_0 modulo p, their inverses are all congruent to q_0^(-1). Therefore definition (1) of S_p in fact 27540b4094f677f4 gives (2), and |S_p(h)|=M for every h. The number of h satisfying h nonzero and h-k nonzero is m_p(k), so (3) follows from the definition of T(k).

For any ordered pair q_i,q_j, its modular reciprocal difference is zero because q_i^(-1)=q_j^(-1) modulo p. Hence every exact rational slope lambda represented by these pairs has rho_{p,lambda}=0. Formula (7) of fact 27540b4094f677f4 therefore gives
  T_0(k)=m_p(k)sum_lambda|B_lambda|^2,
which is (4), and subtraction gives (5).

For W=1_{0}, definition of What gives What(k)=1. There is one zero shift with m_p(0)=p-1 and p-1 nonzero shifts, each with m_p(k)=p-2. Hence
  sum_km_p(k)=(p-1)+(p-1)(p-2)=(p-1)^2.                   (12)
Insert (5) and (12) into the left side of (6) to prove (6).

For the dyadic construction, an interval of p consecutive integers contains every residue class modulo p, so q_0 can be chosen in [Q,Q+p) with p not dividing q_0. For 0<=j<M,
  Q<=q_j<Q+p+Mp<Q+p+p^2/2<2Q                            (13)
for all sufficiently large p, because Q=p^2. Thus all q_j lie in the required dyadic interval.

Apply equation (7) of fact e7458a42217c2756 directly to the coefficient family b_q=1 on these M points. It gives, for every eta>0,
  D_slope<<_eta Q^eta(sum_q|b_q|^2)^2
          =Q^eta M^2,                                     (14)
which is (9). Since Q=p^2 and M is comparable to p, choosing eta<1/2 yields
  D_slope/M^4<<p^(2eta) p^2/p^4=p^(-2+2eta),
which tends to zero. This proves (10). Because p tends to infinity, (1-1/p)^2 tends to one, and (6) gives (11). Dividing (11) by M^4/p gives a ratio asymptotic to p. The final alternatives and scope are logical consequences of this explicit construction.

glossary.D_slope: The exact rational reciprocal-slope energy of the congruent-support coefficient family.
glossary.congruent-support rank-one block: A coefficient support on which every q has the same nonzero residue modulo p, so all reciprocal phase columns coincide.

9ba4d2d84f0b37d6.title: Let L≥2 be a real number and let r be a positive squarefree integer. Define
9ba4d2d84f0b37d6.author: slava chan
9ba4d2d84f0b37d6.statement:
Let L≥2 be a real number and let r be a positive squarefree integer. Define
v_L(r)=∏_{p prime, p|r, p≤L}p
(the empty product being 1), and for every positive integer u define
ω_L(u)=#{p:p is prime, p|u, p≤L}.
For every integer k≥2 and positive integer y define
Γ_k(y)=1_{y is squarefree, ω(y)=k, P^+(y)≤L<y} · (1/k) #{p:p is prime, p|y, y/p≤L},
where ω(y) is the number of distinct prime divisors of y and P^+(y) is the largest prime divisor of y. If v_L(r)>L, then
μ(r)=Σ_{k≥2}(-1)^k Σ_{u y=r, gcd(u,y)=1} μ(u) Γ_k(y)/binom(k+ω_L(u),k).                                            (1)
All sums in (1) are finite. Moreover 0≤Γ_k(y)≤1, and Γ_k(y)≠0 implies
L<y≤L².                                                                  (2)
9ba4d2d84f0b37d6.proof:
Put S={p:p is prime, p|r, p≤L} and t=#S. Choose a permutation (p_1,...,p_t) of S uniformly at random. The assumption v_L(r)>L says that ∏_{i=1}^t p_i>L, so the stopping time
K=min{j:∏_{i=1}^j p_i>L}
exists. Since every p_i≤L, one has K≥2.

Fix k≥2 and a k-element subset Y of S, and write y=∏_{p∈Y}p. The probability that the unordered set of the first k entries of the random permutation is Y equals 1/binom(t,k). Conditional on that event, p_k is uniformly distributed over Y. The event K=k occurs precisely when y>L and y/p_k≤L: the latter inequality says that the product through time k-1 is at most L, while the former says that adjoining p_k crosses L. Since every prime in Y is at most L and y is squarefree with exactly k prime factors, the conditional probability of K=k is exactly Γ_k(y). The mutually disjoint events {K=k} exhaust the probability space. Consequently
1=Σ_{k≥2} Σ_{Y⊂S, #Y=k} Γ_k(∏_{p∈Y}p)/binom(t,k).                       (3)

Every subset Y in (3) determines the coprime factorization r=uy with y=∏_{p∈Y}p. Conversely, every factorization occurring with Γ_k(y)≠0 arises from such a k-element subset Y, because all prime divisors of y are at most L. In this factorization ω_L(u)=t-k, and hence
binom(k+ω_L(u),k)=binom(t,k).
Since r is squarefree and gcd(u,y)=1,
μ(r)=μ(u)μ(y)=(-1)^k μ(u).
Multiplying (3) by μ(r) and using these two identities term by term proves (1).

The definition immediately gives 0≤Γ_k(y)≤1. If Γ_k(y)≠0, then y>L and there is a prime p|y such that y/p≤L. Also p≤P^+(y)≤L. Therefore y=p(y/p)≤L², proving (2).

glossary.K: The first index at which the product of a uniformly random ordering of S exceeds L.
glossary.P^+(y): The largest prime divisor of y.
glossary.S: The set of prime divisors of r not exceeding L.
glossary.v_L(r): The product of the prime divisors p of r with p≤L.
glossary.Γ_k(y): The stopping coefficient: for squarefree y with k prime factors all at most L and y>L, the fraction of its prime divisors p for which y/p≤L.
glossary.ω_L(u): The number of prime divisors p of u with p≤L.

9bca80a481f88303.title: CRITICAL JOINT-COMPLETION SCALE LEDGER ON THE H_P=B/(QG) GEOMETRY. Assume the exact frequency-scale identity
9bca80a481f88303.author: slava chan
9bca80a481f88303.statement:
CRITICAL JOINT-COMPLETION SCALE LEDGER ON THE H_P=B/(QG) GEOMETRY. Assume the exact frequency-scale identity
H_P=B/(QG)
from fact e55b27d39c593164, where Q,B,G,H_P are positive real numbers. Let M_len,T_len be positive real length scales, and fix positive constants c_- and c_+ such that
c_- B <= M_len T_len <= c_+ B.
Define the Q-modulus-summed joint-completion scale and the unnormalized target scale by
C_joint=Q sqrt(Q M_len H_P T_len),
U_target=H_P G Q^2.
Then
sqrt(c_-) BQ/sqrt(G) <= C_joint <= sqrt(c_+) BQ/sqrt(G),
while exactly
U_target=BQ.
Consequently
sqrt(c_-)/sqrt(G) <= C_joint/U_target <= sqrt(c_+)/sqrt(G).
If M_len T_len=B, then the identities sharpen to
C_joint=BQ/sqrt(G),  U_target=BQ,  C_joint/U_target=G^(-1/2).
In particular, at G=1 and M_len T_len=B the joint-completion scale is exactly the unnormalized target, so this scale ledger contains no power-saving slack. If G>=Q^omega for a fixed omega>0, the ledger has the formal scale margin C_joint/U_target<=sqrt(c_+)Q^(-omega/2). This is an algebraic benchmark only: it supplies no cancellation, no estimate for a source coefficient, no nonzero-completion-vector theorem, no squarefree-modulus assembly, and no Goldbach conclusion.
9bca80a481f88303.proof:
By the predecessor identity H_P=B/(QG),
Q M_len H_P T_len
=Q M_len [B/(QG)] T_len
=B(M_len T_len)/G.
The assumed two-sided product comparison therefore gives
c_- B^2/G <= Q M_len H_P T_len <= c_+ B^2/G.
All quantities are positive, so taking square roots and multiplying by Q yields
sqrt(c_-) BQ/sqrt(G) <= C_joint <= sqrt(c_+) BQ/sqrt(G).
Also, directly from H_P=B/(QG),
U_target=H_P GQ^2=[B/(QG)]GQ^2=BQ.
Dividing the preceding two-sided estimate by the positive number U_target proves the ratio bounds.

If M_len T_len=B, the middle quantity before the square root is exactly B^2/G, so C_joint=BQ/sqrt(G), and the exact ratio is G^(-1/2). Substituting G=1 gives equality of C_joint and U_target. If G>=Q^omega, then G^(-1/2)<=Q^(-omega/2), and the upper ratio bound gives the stated formal margin. Every step is an identity or inequality among positive scale parameters; no oscillatory estimate is used.

glossary.C_joint: The Q-modulus-summed joint-completion scale Q sqrt(Q M_len H_P T_len).
glossary.M_len: The first positive length scale in the joint-completion benchmark.
glossary.T_len: The second positive length scale in the joint-completion benchmark.
glossary.U_target: The unnormalized target scale H_P G Q^2.
glossary.c_+: The fixed positive upper comparison constant in M_len T_len comparable to B.
glossary.c_-: The fixed positive lower comparison constant in M_len T_len comparable to B.

9be4b1c96a2620dc.title: BV-WEIGHTED FREE-FACTOR TYPE-I SUPPLIER FOR A COMPOSITE RECIPROCAL PHASE, WITH THE COMPLETE-PERIOD TERM RETAINED. Fix J>=1. Let n>1 be squarefree, C an integer, g=gcd(C,n), and m_eff=n/g>1. Let X,A,B>=1. Let alpha_a be supported on A<=a<2A with |alpha_a|<=tau_J(a). Let c be a squarefree positive integer. Let W be extended by zero and supported on X<=k<2X, with V_X(W) as in fact b390149c13836271. Then, for every epsilon>0,
9be4b1c96a2620dc.author: slava chan
9be4b1c96a2620dc.statement:
BV-WEIGHTED FREE-FACTOR TYPE-I SUPPLIER FOR A COMPOSITE RECIPROCAL PHASE, WITH THE COMPLETE-PERIOD TERM RETAINED. Fix J>=1. Let n>1 be squarefree, C an integer, g=gcd(C,n), and m_eff=n/g>1. Let X,A,B>=1. Let alpha_a be supported on A<=a<2A with |alpha_a|<=tau_J(a). Let c be a squarefree positive integer. Let W be extended by zero and supported on X<=k<2X, with V_X(W) as in fact b390149c13836271. Then, for every epsilon>0,
|sum_{a,b;(ab,nc)=1}alpha_a W(ab)e_n(C(ab)^(-1))|
 <<_{J,epsilon} V_X(W)tau(nc)(m_eff AB)^epsilon
 [AB/m_eff+A m_eff^(1/2)].                                     (1)
Here b is otherwise unweighted and the sum is restricted to B<=b<2B. Thus, if AB is comparable to X, nc<=X^K for a fixed K, V_X(W)<=X^epsilon, and for fixed delta_0,delta_1>0
m_eff>=X^(delta_0),  B>=m_eff^(1/2)X^(delta_1),                 (2)
then (1) is
<<X^(1-min(delta_0,delta_1)+O(epsilon)).                         (3)

Consequently, after an exact finite Heath-Brown decomposition of the physical Möbius variable in the literal C1 row of fact 79ffbcb2ffe4049f, every factor box in which all Möbius-bearing and all but one unweighted factors can be grouped into a carrier of scale A, leaving one free factor of scale B satisfying (2), is paid at the one-row level. In the actual C1 nonzero-p-component chamber, m_eff contains p>=Q^zeta, so the first condition in (2) holds with delta_0=zeta when X is comparable to Q. This does not prove that all decomposition boxes have the stated single-free-factor form, does not pay a box with two or more unweighted factors outside a sub-medium carrier, and does not prove the full composite-Möbius supplier.
9be4b1c96a2620dc.proof:
Write C=gC'. On the unit support,
e_n(C(ab)^(-1))=e_{m_eff}(C'(ab)^(-1)),
with gcd(C',m_eff)=1. Fix a in the support. It is a unit modulo nc. The inverse phase itself already restricts b to units modulo m_eff. The additional primes in the gate (b,nc)=1 are those dividing the squarefree integer
s=rad(nc)/gcd(rad(nc),m_eff).                                    (4)
They are all coprime to m_eff. Use
1_{(b,s)=1}=sum_{d|s,d|b}mu(d).                                 (5)
For one d write b=dr. Then ad is a unit modulo m_eff and the phase is
e_{m_eff}(C'(ad)^(-1)r^(-1)).                                   (6)
The remaining unit condition is exactly (r,m_eff)=1.

The function r maps increasingly to the subsequence adr of the integer axis. Thus the supremum plus total variation of W(adr), on any interval produced by the support and dyadic b-range, is at most V_X(W). Partial summation and the incomplete-period estimate in equations (9)-(10) of fact 2290690807ca8ff2, applied with the unit numerator C'(ad)^(-1), give
|sum_{r in I,(r,m_eff)=1}W(adr)e_{m_eff}(C'(ad)^(-1)r^(-1))|
 <<epsilon V_X(W)(m_eff AB)^epsilon
 [B/(d m_eff)+m_eff^(1/2)].                                    (7)
The first term is the complete-period contribution: every complete unit period has Ramanujan sum mu(m_eff), and it is intentionally retained.

Sum (7) over d|s. Since
sum_{d|s}1/d<=tau(s),  sum_{d|s}1=tau(s),  tau(s)<=tau(nc),
the fixed-a inner sum is
<<epsilon V_X(W)tau(nc)(m_eff AB)^epsilon
 [B/m_eff+m_eff^(1/2)].                                       (8)
Finally sum |alpha_a| over A<=a<2A, costing <<_{J,epsilon}A^{1+epsilon}. This proves (1).

If AB is comparable to X, the two bracketed contributions after multiplication by A are comparable to
X/m_eff,  X m_eff^(1/2)/B.
Conditions (2) bound these by X^(1-delta_0) and X^(1-delta_1), respectively. Squarefree nc<=X^K has tau(nc)=X^{o(1)}, and the variation and epsilon factors are X^{O(epsilon)}. This proves (3).

In a finite Heath-Brown representation, every Möbius-bearing short factor and every chosen unweighted factor may be convolved into alpha_a; fixed-order convolution preserves a fixed divisor-function bound. If exactly one unweighted factor remains outside, it has coefficient one and is the b-variable above. Fact 79ffbcb2ffe4049f gives n=pv and C=mathscr A h; if p does not divide C, then p divides m_eff. Together with p>=Q^zeta this verifies only the first condition in (2), leaving the length of the free factor to the box routing. This proves the stated conditional C1 application and no stronger assembly claim.

glossary.free-factor Type-I box: A separated product q=ab in which all arithmetic coefficients are carried by a and the b-variable has only the product weight and coprimality gates.

9bee61f3627bd506.title: EXACT LITERAL C4 FULL-n COEFFICIENT NORMAL FORM AFTER TARGET-GCD DESCENT
9bee61f3627bd506.author: slava chan
9bee61f3627bd506.statement:
EXACT LITERAL C4 FULL-n COEFFICIENT NORMAL FORM AFTER TARGET-GCD DESCENT.

Fix an exact outer-gcd layer g, one active top-sliver dyadic label, and one complete C4 coordinate in the literal source of fact e58fc7c00f1683e6. Write L_src=N/g. In the forward orientation let s=a be the normalized base factor and n=b the normalized marked factor; in the reverse orientation let s=b and n=a. Thus the normalized source equations are
s m+n k=L_src  (forward),      n m+s k=L_src  (reverse).       (1)
In both orientations s and n are coprime squarefree positive integers. On C4,
n=v p_1p_2p_3p_4,                                                  (2)
where p_1<p_2<p_3<p_4 are the four distinct rough primes of the exact terminal anatomy and v is its small squarefree cofactor.

Put
c=gcd(s,L_src),   s=cq,   L_src=cL_1.                              (3)
Then g,c,q,n are pairwise coprime squarefree integers,
gcd(q,L_1)=1, and
mu(s)mu(n)=mu(c)mu(q)mu(v).                                        (4)

Let e(z)=exp(2 pi i z), e_r(z)=e(z/r), and let a bar over a residue denote its inverse in the displayed modulus. Let F^+_{g,s,n} be the literal forward one-variable source amplitude
F^+_{g,s,n}(t)=log(t)log((L_src-st)/n)
 W(gs/D,t/M,gn/R,(L_src-st)/(nK)),                                 (5)
extended by zero, and let F^-_{g,s,n} be the swapped reverse amplitude
F^-_{g,s,n}(t)=log(t)log((L_src-st)/n)
 W(gn/D,(L_src-st)/(nM),gs/R,t/K),                                 (6)
also extended by zero. Write their Fourier transforms with kernel e(-xi t) as Fhat^+ and Fhat^-.

For every nonzero integer h, define the orientation sign eps and reduced target A by
(eps,A)=(+1,L_1) in the forward orientation,
(eps,A)=(-1,-L_1) in the reverse orientation.                       (7)
After reindexing every reverse frequency and every reverse h-dependent mask by h -> -h, the exact coefficient of the reduced reciprocal phase is
C_eps(c,q,n,v,h)
 =mu(c)mu(q)mu(v) (H_P/n)
   Fhat^eps_{g,cq,n}(eps h/n) e(Ah/(qn)),                            (8)
times all retained literal zero-one or signed bookkeeping factors at that exact coordinate. The corresponding nonzero-Poisson summand is
H_P^(-1) C_eps(c,q,n,v,h) e_q(-Ah n_bar).                           (9)
Thus the external Poisson normalization is H_P^(-1), and the Fourier amplitude in (8) is the dimensionless quantity
(H_P/n)Fhat^eps_{g,cq,n}(eps h/n); there is no prefactor (cq)^(-1).

The Archimedean reciprocity factor in (8) is essential and satisfies the exact reconstruction identity
e(Ah/(qn)) e_q(-Ah n_bar)=e_n(Ah q_bar).                            (10)
Hence it is not an independently discardable phase. Formula (10) restores the original forward n-modulus phase when A=L_1 and the exactly reindexed reverse n-modulus phase when A=-L_1.

Before (2) is formed, every inherited general-marker leaf and every marker-dependent deletion descendant must be recombined at a fixed pre-marker atom, as in fact e58fc7c00f1683e6, to restore the literal mu(n). After C4 is formed, every target-gcd, prime-order/equal-cell, outer-g/rough-prime collision, deletion and provenance refinement is handled in exactly one of two ways: it is retained explicitly among the bookkeeping factors multiplying (8), or all of its complementary siblings are recombined. In particular, an unrecombined q-dependent deletion cannot be silently absorbed into the bare factor mu(c)mu(q)mu(v).

This is a coefficient identity only. It gives no estimate for the C4 trace, no separated-coefficient theorem, no NR-DIL estimate, no other-anatomy identity, and no Goldbach conclusion.
9bee61f3627bd506.proof:
Fact a71f777ad842c886 proves on every nonzero outer-gcd-normalized source atom that g,s,n are pairwise coprime and squarefree and that the original outer Möbius product is mu(s)mu(n).
