Fact e58fc7c00f1683e6 first recombines the inherited marker-dependent descendants to restore mu(n), and then applies the exact terminal anatomy with J=4. On C4 this gives (2) with distinct rough primes and
mu(n)=(-1)^4mu(v)=mu(v).                                          (11)

From (3), c divides the squarefree integer s and q=s/c. Therefore c and q are squarefree and coprime. Since c=gcd(s,L_src), any prime dividing both q and L_1 would divide both s and L_src but not c, contradicting the definition of c. Hence gcd(q,L_1)=1. The already known coprimalities of g,s,n imply that g,c,q,n are pairwise coprime. Multiplicativity on s=cq and (11) now gives
mu(s)mu(n)=mu(c)mu(q)mu(v),
proving (4).

We next derive the forward coefficient. The exact Poisson formula in fact d8ba46800ba433c2 gives, before pairing signs,
mu(s)mu(n) n^(-1)Fhat^+_{g,s,n}(h/n)
 e_n(L_src h s_bar).                                             (12)
Because s=cq, L_src=cL_1 and c is a unit modulo n,
e_n(L_src h s_bar)=e_n(L_1h q_bar).                              (13)
Additive reciprocity for the coprime integers q,n is
e_n(Ah q_bar)=e_q(-Ah n_bar)e(Ah/(qn)).                           (14)
Use A=L_1 in (13)-(14), insert (4), and write
n^(-1)=H_P^(-1)(H_P/n).
This gives (8)-(9) in the forward orientation.

For the reverse orientation, fact 2e0b40b1ba77fb6f gives the literal coefficient
mu(s)mu(n)n^(-1)Fhat^-_{g,s,n}(h/n)e_n(L_src h s_bar).             (15)
The complete nonzero-frequency sum is invariant under h -> -h, provided every h-dependent mask is reindexed at the same time. Thus (15) becomes
mu(s)mu(n)n^(-1)Fhat^-_{g,s,n}(-h/n)e_n(-L_src h s_bar).           (16)
As in (13), the last phase is e_n(-L_1h q_bar). Apply (14) with A=-L_1 and again insert (4) and n^(-1)=H_P^(-1)(H_P/n). This proves (8)-(9) in the reverse orientation. It also shows directly why the reverse Fourier argument is -h/n and why the Poisson denominator remains n rather than cq.

Equation (10) is exactly equation (14) rearranged. The statements about masks follow from the source-preserving recombination and exact finite-partition assertions of fact e58fc7c00f1683e6: recombining all children returns the parent coefficient, while retaining a proper child retains its literal mask. Neither operation changes the algebra above, but only the former permits that mask to disappear. This proves the claimed normal form and every scope assertion.

glossary.A: The signed reduced target, L_1 forward and -L_1 reverse.
glossary.C_eps: The dimensionless full-n coefficient multiplying the reduced reciprocal phase after extracting H_P^(-1).
glossary.F^+_{g,s,n}: The literal forward one-variable physical source amplitude.
glossary.F^-_{g,s,n}: The swapped literal reverse one-variable physical source amplitude.
glossary.eps: The orientation sign, +1 forward and -1 reverse.
glossary.n: The outer-gcd-normalized marked C4 factor: b forward and a reverse.
glossary.s: The outer-gcd-normalized base factor: a forward and b reverse.

9c4dbe65bb8d44be.title: Assume a family of moving-center blocks satisfies the uniform conclusion of fact 477302317fddbf3c: for every L>0 and every admissible label lambda, sum_{Y<=N<=2Y}|P_{lambda,N}|^2<<_L Y^3(log Y)^(-L), with a constant uniform in lambda. Fix positive constants c_0,c_1 and nonnegative real numbers B,G,R. For each sufficiently large Y let L_Y be a set of admissible labels with |L_Y|<=c_1^(-1)(log Y)^R. Then there cannot exist, for infinitely many Y, a set S_Y contained in [Y,2Y] intersect Z with |S_Y|>=c_1Y(log Y)^(-G) and a choice lambda(N) in L_Y for every N in S_Y such that |P_{lambda(N),N}|>=c_0Y(log Y)^(-B) for every N in S_Y. In particular, a near-linear polylogarithmic-density propagation of a block anomaly across only polylogarithmically many labels would contradict fact 477302317fddbf3c. This conditional criterion supplies no such propagation: one anomalous center, or even O(Y^theta) anomalous centers in [Y,2Y] for any fixed theta<1, is compatible with the stated L2 estimates
9c4dbe65bb8d44be.author: slava chan
9c4dbe65bb8d44be.statement: Assume a family of moving-center blocks satisfies the uniform conclusion of fact 477302317fddbf3c: for every L>0 and every admissible label lambda, sum_{Y<=N<=2Y}|P_{lambda,N}|^2<<_L Y^3(log Y)^(-L), with a constant uniform in lambda. Fix positive constants c_0,c_1 and nonnegative real numbers B,G,R. For each sufficiently large Y let L_Y be a set of admissible labels with |L_Y|<=c_1^(-1)(log Y)^R. Then there cannot exist, for infinitely many Y, a set S_Y contained in [Y,2Y] intersect Z with |S_Y|>=c_1Y(log Y)^(-G) and a choice lambda(N) in L_Y for every N in S_Y such that |P_{lambda(N),N}|>=c_0Y(log Y)^(-B) for every N in S_Y. In particular, a near-linear polylogarithmic-density propagation of a block anomaly across only polylogarithmically many labels would contradict fact 477302317fddbf3c. This conditional criterion supplies no such propagation: one anomalous center, or even O(Y^theta) anomalous centers in [Y,2Y] for any fixed theta<1, is compatible with the stated L2 estimates.
9c4dbe65bb8d44be.proof:
Suppose the asserted data existed for infinitely many Y. By the pigeonhole principle, for each such Y there would be one label lambda_Y in L_Y for which the set
S_{Y,lambda_Y}={N in S_Y:lambda(N)=lambda_Y}
has cardinality at least
|S_Y|/|L_Y|>=c_1^2Y(log Y)^(-G-R).
Because S_Y is contained in [Y,2Y] intersect Z, so is S_{Y,lambda_Y}. The assumed pointwise lower bound would therefore give
sum_{Y<=N<=2Y}|P_{lambda_Y,N}|^2
>=sum_{N in S_{Y,lambda_Y}}|P_{lambda_Y,N}|^2
>=c_0^2c_1^2Y^3(log Y)^(-G-R-2B).                                         (1)
On the other hand, apply the uniform L2 conclusion of fact 477302317fddbf3c with the fixed exponent
L=G+R+2B+1.
It gives
sum_{Y<=N<=2Y}|P_{lambda_Y,N}|^2
<<Y^3(log Y)^(-G-R-2B-1).                                                  (2)
For sufficiently large Y, (2) is smaller than (1), because their ratio is O(1/log Y) while c_0 and c_1 are fixed positive constants. This contradiction proves the first assertion.

For the final scope statement, suppose only O(Y^theta) centers in [Y,2Y], with a fixed theta<1, have values of size Y(log Y)^(-B). Their forced lower energy has scale at most Y^(2+theta) times logarithmic factors. For every fixed L, this is asymptotically smaller than Y^3(log Y)^(-L), since Y^(1-theta) dominates every fixed power of log Y. Hence the numerical L2 upper bound does not contradict such a sparse anomalous set. The theorem is solely a conditional propagation interface and does not derive recurrence of an anomaly from Goldbach failure or from any other premise.

glossary.L_Y: the label family available at scale Y
glossary.S_Y: the subset of [Y,2Y] carrying a large anomaly
glossary.S_{Y,lambda_Y}: the pigeonholed subset using one common label

9c6a58bbb96eadae.title: CRITICAL-RIGHT-HAND-SIDE NO-FIT FOR EVERY TWO-FACTOR REGROUPING OF A DEEP HB CELL. Fix \(0<\tau<1/100\), \(\beta>1\), and put
9c6a58bbb96eadae.author: slava chan
9c6a58bbb96eadae.statement:
CRITICAL-RIGHT-HAND-SIDE NO-FIT FOR EVERY TWO-FACTOR REGROUPING OF A DEEP HB CELL. Fix \(0<\tau<1/100\), \(\beta>1\), and put
\[
 a=2\beta-2+\tau,\qquad b=3-2\beta-\tau,\qquad
 H_T=Q^{\beta-1}.
\]
Assume \(0<a<b\), let \(Q\) be sufficiently large, and set \(G=1\). Consider the four-term right-hand side in fact \(f7b5ba9fa0d6cfc8\), with a factor scale
\[
 S=Q^s
\]
and complementary scale \(T\) satisfying \(ST\asymp QH_T=Q^\beta\). Apart from the harmless \(Q^\varepsilon\) factor and fixed constants, its first two terms are
\[
 R_1=Q^2H_T^{1/2}S^{-1/4},\qquad
 R_2=Q^{7/4}H_T^{1/2}S^{1/4}.                               \tag{1}
\]
Their exponents satisfy the exact identities
\[
 \log_Q R_1
 =2-{\tau\over4}+{a-s\over4},\qquad
 \log_Q R_2
 =2-{\tau\over4}+{s-b\over4}.                               \tag{2}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 s\le a-\tau\quad\Longrightarrow\quad R_1\ge Q^2,            \tag{3}
\]
and
\[
 s\ge b+\tau\quad\Longrightarrow\quad R_2\ge Q^2.            \tag{4}
\]
Thus direct use of the displayed bound in fact \(f7b5ba9fa0d6cfc8\) cannot prove \(O(Q^{2-\delta})\) for any fixed \(\delta>0\) in either range, even if all other three terms, every coefficient tax, and every source mask are deleted for free.

In particular, consider a legally separated HB cell from facts \(aaf7242ef22ecd10\) and \(884d8d453b95d5ad\) with the additional deep-gap property that every nonempty subset product \(S\) used as one side of a two-factor regrouping satisfies
\[
 S\le Q^{a-\tau}\quad\hbox{or}\quad S\ge Q^{b+\tau}.           \tag{5}
\]
Then every direct regrouping of that cell into the two factor slots of fact \(f7b5ba9fa0d6cfc8\) has a displayed right-hand side at least \(Q^2\). The accepted theorem therefore supplies no fixed-power ULTRA-MU-VECTOR estimate on this deep cell.

This is a right-hand-side no-fit for direct use of one existing estimate at \(G=1\). It is not a lower bound for the actual sum and does not exclude cancellation among regroupings, a genuinely multilinear estimate, a source-linked cross-\(q\) vector theorem, a treatment of near-face cells, or a different analytic method. It proves no ENDPOINT-DIAGONAL-\(N\), post-\(A\) tail, or Goldbach conclusion.
9c6a58bbb96eadae.proof:
Substitute \(H_T=Q^{\beta-1}\) and \(S=Q^s\) into (1). Then
\[
 \log_QR_1=2+{\beta-1\over2}-{s\over4}.
\]
Since \(a=2\beta-2+\tau\),
\[
 {\beta-1\over2}={a-\tau\over4},
\]
which gives the first identity in (2). Likewise,
\[
 \log_QR_2={7\over4}+{\beta-1\over2}+{s\over4}.
\]
The relation \(b=3-2\beta-\tau\) is equivalent to
\[
 {7\over4}+{\beta-1\over2}+{b\over4}=2-{\tau\over4},
\]
which gives the second identity in (2).

If \(s\le a-\tau\), then \(a-s\ge\tau\), so the first identity yields \(\log_QR_1\ge2\). If \(s\ge b+\tau\), the second yields \(\log_QR_2\ge2\). This proves (3)--(4).

On a cell satisfying (5), any chosen grouped factor scale falls into one of those two cases. The upper bound furnished by fact \(f7b5ba9fa0d6cfc8\) is a sum of nonnegative displayed terms and therefore is at least the offending \(R_1\) or \(R_2\). Such a right-hand side cannot imply a bound \(O(Q^{2-\delta})\). All scope qualifications follow because no assertion has been made about the size of the underlying oscillatory sum.

glossary.R_1: The first term of the critical full-frequency reciprocal-energy right-hand side.
glossary.R_2: The second term of the critical full-frequency reciprocal-energy right-hand side.
glossary.deep-gap property: Every nonempty subset grouping lies at least tau below the lower face or at least tau above the upper face.

9d1a11eb8a597a64.title: EXACT SAME-OUTPUT GRAM FACTORIZATION OF THE PRIMITIVE DISJOINT PMLS UNIT BLOCK. Let r,r'>1 be coprime odd squarefree integers, let c,c',h be units modulo rr', and let f on G_r and g on G_{r'}. For j coprime to r define
9d1a11eb8a597a64.author: slava chan
9d1a11eb8a597a64.statement:
EXACT SAME-OUTPUT GRAM FACTORIZATION OF THE PRIMITIVE DISJOINT PMLS UNIT BLOCK. Let r,r'>1 be coprime odd squarefree integers, let c,c',h be units modulo rr', and let f on G_r and g on G_{r'}. For j coprime to r define
A_{r,c}(f;j,h)
=sum_{chi primitive mod r} fhat(overline chi)chi(-c)
 tau_r(overline chi)chi(-h j^{-1}),                                  (1)
and define A_{r',c'} analogously. Let w be a complex function on G_{rr'}. Define the primitive-pair completed block by
P_{r,r'}^{prim}(f,g;w,h)
=sum_{chi primitive mod r}sum_{psi primitive mod r'}
 fhat(overline chi)overline{ghat(overline psi)}
 m_{r,c}(chi)overline{m_{r',c'}(psi)}
 Sigma_{chi,psi}(w;h),                                               (2)
where m and Sigma are exactly those of facts 18a0de57eaf35171 and 2bc35b8e8ac55aff. Then
P_{r,r'}^{prim}(f,g;w,h)
=sum_{j in G_{rr'}}w(j)A_{r,c}(f;j,h)
 overline{A_{r',c'}(g;j,h)}.                                        (3)
Thus after the CRT/Gauss cancellation the primitive disjoint block is a common-output Gram, with no partner-modulus character evaluations.

For one modulus, complete output Parseval gives
sum_{j in G_r}|A_{r,c}(f;j,h)|^2
=r||P_{r,r}f||_2^2,                                                  (4)
where P_{r,r} is the primitive-conductor projector of fact b4934b4981fc5817. Equation (4) is exact and shows that the complete primitive synthesis has average scale sqrt(r); it gives no saving on a short common-output set. Equations (3)--(4) do not estimate the varying-r common-z synthesis or prove C4.
9d1a11eb8a597a64.proof:
Apply equation (2) of fact 2bc35b8e8ac55aff to every pair in (2). It gives
m_{r,c}(chi)overline{m_{r',c'}(psi)}Sigma_{chi,psi}(w;h)
=chi(-c)overline{psi(-c')}tau_r(overline chi)tau_{r'}(psi)
 sum_jw(j)chi(-h j^{-1})psi(jh^{-1}).                               (5)
Insert (5), interchange the finite sums, and group the chi factors. They are exactly A_{r,c}(f;j,h).

For the psi factors, conjugating (1) at modulus r' gives
overline{A_{r',c'}(g;j,h)}
=sum_psi overline{ghat(overline psi)}overline{psi(-c')}
 overline{tau_{r'}(overline psi)}overline{psi(-h j^{-1})}.           (6)
Conjugation of a Gauss sum gives
overline{tau_{r'}(overline psi)}=psi(-1)tau_{r'}(psi).               (7)
Also
psi(-1)overline{psi(-h j^{-1})}=psi(jh^{-1}).                       (8)
Substitution of (7)--(8) in (6) makes it exactly the psi factor in (5). This proves (3).

For (4), multiplicative character orthogonality in j applied to (1) yields
sum_{j in G_r}|A_{r,c}(f;j,h)|^2
=phi(r)sum_{chi primitive}|fhat(overline chi)|^2
 |tau_r(overline chi)|^2.                                           (9)
Every chi in this sum is primitive, so its Gauss magnitude squared is r. Multiplicative Parseval gives
||P_{r,r}f||_2^2
=phi(r)sum_{chi primitive}|fhat(chi)|^2.                             (10)
Character conjugation permutes the primitive set. Equations (9)--(10) prove (4).

glossary.A_{r,c}(f;j,h): the primitive Gauss-weighted common-output synthesis at modulus r
glossary.P_{r,r'}^{prim}: the primitive-character-pair part of the completed disjoint unit-frequency block

9d4d1788b80a398f.title: Assume the hypotheses of fact 2827630745a3225b along a sequence of sufficiently large even integers N=2x that are not sums of two primes, and use the exact signed partition
9d4d1788b80a398f.author: slava chan
9d4d1788b80a398f.statement:
Assume the hypotheses of fact 2827630745a3225b along a sequence of sufficiently large even integers N=2x that are not sums of two primes, and use the exact signed partition
H_N=C_N+E_N+U_N,
E_N=E_{1×1,N}+E_{2×1,N}+E_{2×2,N}+E_{asymmetric,N}
from fact 91db48815d136d4c. Put A_N=c_W𝔠(N)x. Suppose there are nonnegative real numbers ε_N, δ_N, γ_N tending to zero along the sequence such that
H_N≤-(1-ε_N)A_N,
|C_N|≤δ_N A_N,
and
U_N≥-γ_N A_N.
Then
E_N≤-(1-ε_N-δ_N-γ_N)A_N
and
min(E_{1×1,N},E_{2×1,N},E_{2×2,N},E_{asymmetric,N})
≤-(1-ε_N-δ_N-γ_N)A_N/4.
Consequently the pair of asymptotic hypotheses
C_N=o(𝔠(N)x)
and
NONEND-ORBIT-OSER: U_N≥-o(𝔠(N)x)
is sufficient to force
E_N≤-c_W𝔠(N)x+o(𝔠(N)x)
and a negative endpoint anatomy of size at least (c_W/4)𝔠(N)x up to a lower-order term. No upper bound on U_N, no absolute-value estimate for U_N, and no sign assertion for an individual divisor sibling is required.
9d4d1788b80a398f.proof:
From the exact identity in fact 91db48815d136d4c,
E_N=H_N-C_N-U_N.
The three assumed inequalities give
H_N≤-A_N+ε_NA_N,
-C_N≤|C_N|≤δ_NA_N,
and
-U_N≤γ_NA_N.
Adding them yields
E_N≤-(1-ε_N-δ_N-γ_N)A_N.

The four endpoint-anatomy terms sum to E_N. For any four real numbers their minimum is at most their arithmetic mean. Therefore
min(E_{1×1,N},E_{2×1,N},E_{2×2,N},E_{asymmetric,N})≤E_N/4,
which gives the second displayed inequality.

Fact 2827630745a3225b gives H_N=-A_N+o(A_N), because fact 91db48815d136d4c partitions the same exact dyadic source. The two stated asymptotic hypotheses allow ε_N,δ_N,γ_N→0, and c_W is fixed and positive. Substitution proves the asymptotic conclusions. Only the lower bound for U_N was used: a positive value of U_N makes -U_N more negative and therefore strengthens the endpoint conclusion. The sibling-scope sentence follows because the argument concerns only complete signed aggregates from fact 91db48815d136d4c.

glossary.NONEND-ORBIT-OSER: the one-sided lower bound U_N≥-o(𝔠(N)x) for the complete nonendpoint aggregate
glossary.γ_N: the relative negative-part bound for the nonendpoint aggregate
glossary.δ_N: the relative absolute bound for the controlled aggregate
glossary.ε_N: the relative error in the negative source upper bound

9dc06d0e888914a5.title: EXACT EXCEPTIONAL-SECTOR LEDGER FOR THE ODD UNIT SHARED-LIFT CORE
9dc06d0e888914a5.author: slava chan
9dc06d0e888914a5.statement:
EXACT EXCEPTIONAL-SECTOR LEDGER FOR THE ODD UNIT SHARED-LIFT CORE.

Let H>=2, let C be a nonzero integer, let K be an integer, and let
 (a,b,c,d,r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4,u,v)
be any normalized unit state of type (I) in fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb. Thus a,b,c,d are even, the four r_i are pairwise distinct primes in [H^2,2H^2), gcd(C,r_1r_2r_3r_4)=1, uv is nonzero, and, with
 A=b r_3-d r_2,  B=a r_2-c r_3,
 q=gcd(|A|,|B|),                                                   (1)
one has
 A=2vr_1, B=2vr_4, q=2|v|,
 ab+cd=2K.                                                         (2)
Put
 m_state=q/2=|v|,qquad s=sign(v).                                 (3)

Then m_state,s,K and C are recovered uniquely from the coefficient matrix and ordered prime data by
 m_state=gcd(|A|,|B|)/2,quad s=sign(A)=sign(B),quad
 K=(ab+cd)/2,quad
 C=(ad r_2^2-bc r_3^2)/(2sq).                                     (4)
The recovered short coordinate is
 u=s(ab-cd)/(2q).                                                   (5)

Every normalized state belongs to exactly one of the following five disjoint sectors:
 G: m_state>1 is odd and gcd(m_state,K r_2r_3)=1;
 E_one: m_state=1;
 E_even: m_state is even;
 E_K: m_state>1 is odd and gcd(m_state,K)>1;
 E_corner: m_state>1 is odd, gcd(m_state,K)=1, and
           gcd(m_state,r_2r_3)>1.                                 (6)
This partition is exhaustive.

On G,
 ab is congruent to cd and to K modulo m_state,                     (7)
so a,b,c,d are units modulo m_state and modulo m_state^2. Moreover 2s is invertible modulo m_state, all torus inverses by r_2,r_3 exist, and the canonical even-lift chart of fact 17557ebe80636618 applies. Hence G is exactly the arithmetic conductor class addressed by fact f23bad095a2e6a52, apart from that fact's additional lower bound on m_state and its scale, interval, fixed-parameter, and source-weight hypotheses.

On E_K, at least one of a,b and at least one of c,d is a nonunit modulo m_state. Therefore the all-four-coordinate unit torus and the hypotheses of fact f23bad095a2e6a52 fail. This does not imply that a itself is always a nonunit; a pointwise inverse-column transform can still exist in a subcase. On E_corner, at least one of r_2,r_3 is a nonunit modulo m_state, so the unit-torus parametrization by r_2^(-1),r_3^(-1) is unavailable. On E_even, 2s is not invertible modulo m_state and the odd-modulus shared-digit and canonical-even-lift steps are unavailable. The finite sector E_one is outside the m>1 hypothesis of fact 17557ebe80636618 and the large-modulus hypotheses of f23bad095a2e6a52.

There is no coefficient-parity failure layer inside the normalized unit states of fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb: evenness of a,b,c,d is part of their definition. Likewise, after defining the intrinsic modulus by (3), there is no separate layer q not equal to 2m_state. Odd coefficients or a mismatch with an externally prescribed half-conductor can occur only before the source has been routed into these normalized states and must be handled by a separate source-to-state theorem.

This result is only an exact partition and applicability audit. It supplies no estimate for E_one, E_even, E_K, or E_corner and no aggregation over different m_state.
9dc06d0e888914a5.proof:
Fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb proves q=2|v| and that A,B have the common sign of v. Therefore (3) and the first two recovery formulas in (4) are unique. The determinant identity gives the formula for K. The same fact gives
 D=ad r_2^2-bc r_3^2=4vC=2sqC,
which gives the displayed formula for C. It also gives
 J=ab-cd=4uv.
Substitution of v=sm_state=sq/2 gives u=sJ/(2q), proving (5).

The five conditions in (6) are disjoint by construction. If m_state=1 it is in E_one. Otherwise, if it is not even, it is odd and greater than one. For odd m_state>1, either gcd(m_state,K)>1 or gcd(m_state,K)=1. In the latter case either gcd(m_state,r_2r_3)=1, which is G, or it is greater than one, which is E_corner. This proves exhaustiveness.

The normalized identities in fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb give
 ab=K+2uv,qquad cd=K-2uv.
Since v=sm_state, both products are congruent to K modulo m_state, proving (7). In G, K is a unit modulo m_state, so both factors in each product ab and cd are units; unitness modulo m_state is equivalent to unitness modulo its square. The definition of G also makes r_2,r_3 units. Oddness makes 2s a unit. Since m_state>1, these are exactly the unit, parity, and size hypotheses used by the torus and shared-lift constructions of fact 17557ebe80636618. Fact f23bad095a2e6a52 imposes the same arithmetic conditions and then adds its stronger lower bound and its scale and interval hypotheses.

In E_K, choose a prime p dividing gcd(m_state,K). The congruences ab congruent K and cd congruent K modulo m_state imply p divides ab and cd. Hence p divides at least one of a,b and at least one of c,d. This proves failure of the all-four-unit torus and therefore failure of the hypotheses of f23bad095a2e6a52, without deciding which member of either pair is nonunit. In E_corner, a prime divisor of gcd(m_state,r_2r_3) divides r_2 or r_3, so the corresponding inverse does not exist modulo m_state. If m_state is even, gcd(2s,m_state)>1, so the shared digit cannot be recovered by multiplying by (2s)^(-1); the uniqueness of even representatives used in fact 17557ebe80636618 was proved only for odd modulus. The statements about E_one follow directly from the numerical hypotheses of the two cited facts.

Finally, the opening hypotheses copied from fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb explicitly require all four coefficients even. Equation (3) is a definition from the intrinsic q, so q=2m_state tautologically. This proves the two empty/misrouting observations and all stated scope limitations.

glossary.E_K: the odd-half-conductor sector sharing a prime with K

9df0368f36fc350a.title: Let H>=3, let I_H=[H^2,2H^2) intersect Z, let C be an integer, and let r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4 be pairwise distinct primes in I_H. Among integer quadruples (a,b,c,d) with |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|<=H^3, there is at most one satisfying
9df0368f36fc350a.author: slava chan
9df0368f36fc350a.statement:
Let H>=3, let I_H=[H^2,2H^2) intersect Z, let C be an integer, and let r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4 be pairwise distinct primes in I_H. Among integer quadruples (a,b,c,d) with |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|<=H^3, there is at most one satisfying
b r_3r_4-a r_1r_2=2C,   d r_2r_4-c r_1r_3=2C.
More explicitly, let rho_m(z) denote the unique integer in (-m/2,m/2] congruent to z modulo m. Since opposite prime products are coprime, any such quadruple must satisfy
b=rho_{r_1r_2}(2C (r_3r_4)^{-1}),  a=(b r_3r_4-2C)/(r_1r_2),
d=rho_{r_1r_3}(2C (r_2r_4)^{-1}),  c=(d r_2r_4-2C)/(r_1r_3),
where inverses are taken modulo the subscripted modulus; existence further requires these four integers to lie in the box and satisfy any desired parity restrictions. Consequently, for fixed C and H, projection of the normalized unit states in fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb to their ordered prime-corner quadruple (r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4) is injective.
9df0368f36fc350a.proof:
Set R_12=r_1r_2 and R_34=r_3r_4. Pairwise distinctness gives gcd(R_12,R_34)=1. If (a,b) and (a',b') are two solutions of the first equation in the H^3 box, subtraction gives
(b-b')R_34=(a-a')R_12.
Coprimality implies R_12 divides b-b'. But |b-b'|<=2H^3, while R_12>=H^4>2H^3 for H>=3. Thus b=b', and then a=a'. This proves uniqueness of the first pair. Reducing the first equation modulo R_12 gives bR_34 congruent to 2C modulo R_12. Since R_34 is invertible modulo R_12, b is congruent to 2C(R_34)^{-1}. The interval [-H^3,H^3] has length 2H^3<R_12, so it contains at most one representative of this residue class. If it contains one, it equals the centered representative rho_{R_12}(2C(R_34)^{-1}), because its absolute value is strictly below R_12/2; division then gives the displayed formula for a.

Apply the same argument to R_13=r_1r_3 and R_24=r_2r_4. These are coprime, R_13>=H^4>2H^3, and subtraction of two solutions of dR_24-cR_13=2C gives R_13|(d-d'). Hence d and c are unique, with the displayed centered-residue formulas.

Fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb proves that every normalized unit state satisfies exactly these two equations and has pairwise distinct prime corners in I_H. Therefore two normalized unit states with the same ordered prime-corner quadruple have the same a,b,c,d. The remaining recovered values q,s,u,v are unique in that fact, so the projection is injective.

glossary.rho_m: For a positive integer m, rho_m(z) is the unique integer in (-m/2,m/2] congruent to z modulo m.

9e1ff55fe17bc513.title: Fix real numbers \(1/2<a<b<1\). Let \(W\) be a nonzero nonnegative continuously differentiable real function supported in \([a,b]\). Let \(\psi\) be continuously differentiable on the positive reals with \(0\le\psi\le1\), \(\psi(u)=0\) for \(0<u\le1\), and \(\psi(u)=1\) for \(u\ge2\). Let \(\Phi\) be the nonnegative infinitely differentiable function supported in \([1/2,2]\) supplied by fact 3ef233e014331fc3, so that
9e1ff55fe17bc513.author: slava chan
9e1ff55fe17bc513.statement:
Fix real numbers \(1/2<a<b<1\). Let \(W\) be a nonzero nonnegative continuously differentiable real function supported in \([a,b]\). Let \(\psi\) be continuously differentiable on the positive reals with \(0\le\psi\le1\), \(\psi(u)=0\) for \(0<u\le1\), and \(\psi(u)=1\) for \(u\ge2\). Let \(\Phi\) be the nonnegative infinitely differentiable function supported in \([1/2,2]\) supplied by fact 3ef233e014331fc3, so that
\[
 \sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}\Phi(t/2^j)=1\qquad(t>0).
\]

Apply fact 052064336e86e65c with large parameter \(2x\), target exponent \(8\), and variation exponent \(5\); denote its fixed modulus exponent by \(B_{\rm init}>0\). Apply fact 5084a731a9f78a09 with requested accuracy \(8\) and prescribed floor \(B_{\rm init}+1\); denote its fixed source exponent by \(B_{\rm src}>B_{\rm init}+1\). For \(x\ge3\) put
\[
 N=2x,\qquad
 D_*=x^{1/2}(\log x)^{-B_{\rm src}},\qquad
 Q_{\rm init}=(2x)^{1/2}(\log(2x))^{-B_{\rm init}}.
\]
Let \(x\) tend to infinity through values for which \(N\) is an even integer not representable as a sum of two primes.

Let \(D,M,U\) be positive dyadic real numbers satisfying the exact source-admissible scale bounds
\[
 {D_*\over2}\le D\le2bx,\qquad
 {ax\over4}\le DM\le4bx,\qquad
 {(2-b)x\over2}\le U\le2(2-a)x,                           \tag{1}
\]
and suppose that
\[
 2D>Q_{\rm init}.                                         \tag{2}
\]
For every integer \(d\ge1\) and real \(t\), define
\[
 F_d(t)=
 \begin{cases}
 \log((N-t)/d)W((N-t)/x)
 \Phi((N-t)/(dM))\Phi(t/U),&2\le t<N,\\
 0,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
For \(d\ge1\) with \((d,N)=1\), define
\[
 \Delta_d^F(N)=
 \sum_{\substack{p<N\\p\ {\rm prime}\\p\equiv N\ ({\rm mod}\ d)}}\log p\,F_d(p)
 -{1\over\phi(d)}\sum_{\substack{p<N\\p\ {\rm prime}}}\log p\,F_d(p).    \tag{3}
\]
Let
\[
 \Lambda_{\rm pr}(n)=
 \begin{cases}\log n,&n\text{ is prime},\\0,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}
\]
and
\[
 {\cal I}_D=\{d\ge2:(d,N)=1,\ d\le x^{1/2},\ \Phi(d/D)\ne0\}.             \tag{4}
\]
Every \(d\in{\cal I}_D\) satisfies
\[
 Q_{\rm init}/4<d\le x^{1/2},\qquad \psi(d/D_*)=1                       \tag{5}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(x\).

The literal top-band discrepancies satisfy the baseline mean-square estimate
\[
 \sum_{d\in{\cal I}_D}\mu(d)^2\Phi(d/D)^2|\Delta_d^F(N)|^2
 \ll_{W,\Phi}{x^2\over D}(\log x)^4
 \ll_{W,\Phi}xD(\log x)^{2B_{\rm init}+4}.                              \tag{6}
\]
This has positive logarithmic loss and supplies no contradiction to a discrepancy of order \(x/\log x\).

For completeness, define the projective norm of the literal \(d,t\)-family by
\[
 {\cal P}(F)=\inf\int_{\cal Z}
 \sup_{\substack{D/2\le d\le2D\\d\ {\rm integer}}}|A_z(d)|
 \sup_{2\le t<N}|B_z(t)|\,d|\nu|(z),                                   \tag{7}
\]
where the infimum is over all parameter spaces \({\cal Z}\), finite complex measures \(\nu\), and exact representations
\[
 F_d(t)=\int_{\cal Z}A_z(d)B_z(t)\,d\nu(z)
\]
on the displayed ranges. Then
\[
 {\cal P}(F)\ll_{W,\Phi}\log x.                                        \tag{8}
\]
For every \(R>0\), the primitive-conductor portion on \(R<r\le2R\) satisfies
\[
 \sum_{\substack{r\in{\cal I}_D\\R<r\le2R}}{1\over\phi(r)}
 \sum_{\chi\ ({\rm mod}\ r)}^{*}
 \left|\sum_{\substack{p<N\\p\ {\rm prime}}}\log p\,F_r(p)\chi(p)\right|^2
 \ll_{W,\Phi}\left({x\over R}+R\right)x(\log x)^5.                      \tag{9}
\]
When \(R\) is comparable to \(D\), (2) makes the right side
\[
 \ll_{W,\Phi}xD(\log x)^{2B_{\rm init}+5}.                              \tag{10}
\]
Thus the squared literal projective cost contributes two logarithms, the prime \(L^2\) norm contributes one, and the maximal primitive large sieve contributes two.

Define
\[
 V_{d,m}=W(dm/x)\Phi((N-dm)/U)                                        \tag{11}
\]
and the exact top-band genuine-prime block
\[
 P_N^{\rm top}(D,M;U)=
 \sum_{m\ge1}\log m\,\Phi(m/M)
 \sum_{d\in{\cal I}_D}\mu(d)\Phi(d/D)V_{d,m}
 \Lambda_{\rm pr}(N-dm).                                               \tag{12}
\]
Put
\[
 {\mathfrak D}_N(D,M;U)=
 \sum_{m\ge1}\left|
 \sum_{d\in{\cal I}_D}\mu(d)\Phi(d/D)V_{d,m}
 \Lambda_{\rm pr}(N-dm)\right|^2.                                     \tag{13}
\]
Then Cauchy--Schwarz only in \(m\) gives
\[
 |P_N^{\rm top}(D,M;U)|^2
 \ll_\Phi M(\log x)^2{\mathfrak D}_N(D,M;U).                            \tag{14}
\]
The dispersion has the exact expansion
\[
 {\mathfrak D}_N={\mathfrak D}_{\rm diag}+{\mathfrak C}_{\rm off},      \tag{15}
\]
where
\[
 {\mathfrak D}_{\rm diag}=
 \sum_{d\in{\cal I}_D}\mu(d)^2\Phi(d/D)^2
 \sum_{m\ge1}V_{d,m}^2\Lambda_{\rm pr}(N-dm)^2
 \ll_{W,\Phi}x(\log x)^2,                                              \tag{16}
\]
and
\[
 {\mathfrak C}_{\rm off}=
 \sum_{\substack{d_1,d_2\in{\cal I}_D\\d_1\ne d_2}}
 \mu(d_1)\mu(d_2)\Phi(d_1/D)\Phi(d_2/D)
 \sum_{m\ge1}V_{d_1,m}V_{d_2,m}
 \Lambda_{\rm pr}(N-d_1m)\Lambda_{\rm pr}(N-d_2m).                     \tag{17}
\]

A sufficient open estimate for this exact reduction is
\[
 {\mathfrak C}_{\rm off}
 =o_{W,\Phi}\!\left(xD(\log x)^{-4}\right),                             \tag{TB-COV4}
\]
uniformly in the fixed growing center \(N=2x\) and the labels satisfying (1)--(2). If (TB-COV4) holds, then
\[
 {\mathfrak D}_N=o_{W,\Phi}\!\left(xD(\log x)^{-4}\right)                \tag{18}
\]
and
\[
 P_N^{\rm top}(D,M;U)=o_{W,\Phi}(x/\log x).                            \tag{19}
\]

Define the top comparison main
\[
 {\cal M}_N^{\rm top}(D,M;U)=
 \sum_{d\in{\cal I}_D}{\mu(d)\Phi(d/D)\over\phi(d)}
 \sum_{\substack{p<N\\p\ {\rm prime}}}\log p\,F_d(p).                   \tag{20}
\]
For every \(A>0\),
\[
 {\cal M}_N^{\rm top}(D,M;U)\ll_{A,W,\Phi}x(\log x)^{-A}.               \tag{21}
\]
Hence, under (TB-COV4), the top part
\[
 {\cal E}_N^{\rm top}=
 \sum_{d\in{\cal I}_D}\mu(d)\Phi(d/D)\Delta_d^F(N)
 =P_N^{\rm top}-{\cal M}_N^{\rm top}                                  \tag{22}
\]
is \(o(x/\log x)\).

To state the consequence for the selected block self-containedly, put
\[
 C_2=\prod_{p>2}{p(p-2)\over(p-1)^2},\qquad
 \mathfrak c(N)=C_2\prod_{\substack{p\mid N\\p>2}}{p-1\over p-2},
\]
\[
 c_W=2\int_0^\infty W(u)\,du,\quad
 L_{DM}=\lceil\log_2(16b/a)\rceil+1,\quad
 L_U=\lceil\log_2(4(2-a)/(2-b))\rceil+1,
\]
and \(c_{\rm dir}=c_W/(12L_{DM}L_U)>0\). If \(D,M,U\) is the same triple supplied by fact 1de7f7c45ccfee10, then its full discrepancy
\[
 {\cal E}_N(D,M;U)=
 \sum_{\substack{d\ge2\\(d,N)=1}}\mu(d)\psi(d/D_*)\Phi(d/D)\Delta_d^F(N)
\]
satisfies
\[
 {\cal E}_N(D,M;U)\le-c_{\rm dir}{\mathfrak c(N)x\over\log x}.          \tag{23}
\]
Under (TB-COV4), its complementary part \({\cal E}_N^{>}\), defined by the same sum restricted to \(d>x^{1/2}\), satisfies
\[
 {\cal E}_N^{>}\le-{c_{\rm dir}\over2}{\mathfrak c(N)x\over\log x}      \tag{24}
\]
for sufficiently large \(x\). Thus (TB-COV4) would eliminate the entire \(Q_{\rm init}/4<d\le x^{1/2}\) family and transfer the same-\(N\) negative discrepancy to the exact divisor-switched component of fact 96ed928a9fc80276.

No cited theorem directly proves (TB-COV4). Lewko--Lewko's classical Barban--Davenport--Halberstam theorem assumes \(Q\ge x(\log x)^{-A}\), outside the present range \(d\le x^{1/2}\); their multiplicative large sieve yields only (9)--(10). Facts 3bcd070f8558ce6f and eeee52899369d087 show that the raw \(\mu(d)\) coefficient, including prime moduli near \(x^{1/2}\), is neither directly triply well-factorable nor approximable by finite same-level triply well-factorable combinations in the required coefficient norms. Fact 0747c1083be2ef08 shows that the direct Banks--Shparlinski specialization is too large and that prime-index compression changes the Möbius coefficient. Finally, a Vaughan or Heath--Brown expansion \(rs=N-d_1m\) leaves both \(d_1\mid N-rs\) and the second prime form
\[
 N-d_2m=((d_1-d_2)N+d_2rs)/d_1.
\]
This identity does not estimate (17). Within the exact Cauchy reduction (14)--(17), (17) is therefore the sole unproved term. This is a no-direct-import statement, not an impossibility theorem.
9e1ff55fe17bc513.proof:
From (2) and the support of \(\Phi(d/D)\), every \(d\in{\cal I}_D\) satisfies
\[
 d\ge D/2>Q_{\rm init}/4.
\]
Moreover
\[
 {Q_{\rm init}\over D_*}
 =\sqrt2\,{(\log x)^{B_{\rm src}}\over(\log(2x))^{B_{\rm init}}}
 \longrightarrow\infty
\]
because \(B_{\rm src}>B_{\rm init}+1\). Hence \(Q_{\rm init}/4>2D_*\) for sufficiently large \(x\). It follows that \(d>2D_*\), and the defining property of \(\psi\) gives \(\psi(d/D_*)=1\). This proves (5).

We prove (6). On the support of \(F_d(p)\), the support of \(W\) gives
\[
 p=N-dm\in[(2-b)x,(2-a)x],
\]
so in particular \(p>x\). For fixed \(d\le x^{1/2}\), the number of integers in this interval congruent to \(N\) modulo \(d\) is \(O(x/d)\). Every summand \(\log p\,F_d(p)\) is \(O_{W,\Phi}((\log x)^2)\), and therefore
\[
 \left|\sum_{\substack{p<N,\ p\ {\rm prime}\\p\equiv N\ ({\rm mod}\ d)}}
 \log p\,F_d(p)\right|
 \ll_{W,\Phi}{x\over d}(\log x)^2.                                     \tag{25}
\]
The Chebyshev bound \(\sum_{p\le2x}\log p\ll x\), reproduced in fact 415fa7afad9006c5, gives
\[
 {1\over\phi(d)}
 \left|\sum_{\substack{p<N\\p\ {\rm prime}}}\log p\,F_d(p)\right|
 \ll_{W,\Phi}{x\log x\over\phi(d)}.                                    \tag{26}
\]

We use the squarefree average
\[
 \sum_{D/2<d<2D}{\mu(d)^2\over\phi(d)^2}\ll D^{-1}.                     \tag{27}
\]
For squarefree \(d\), put \(f(d)=(d/\phi(d))^2\). On squarefree integers write \(f=1*g\). The multiplicative function \(g\) satisfies
\[
 g(p)=(1-1/p)^{-2}-1=O(1/p)
\]
and is supported on squarefree integers. Consequently
\[
 \sum_{k\ge1}{|g(k)|\over k}
 =\prod_p\left(1+{|g(p)|\over p}\right)<\infty.
\]
Thus
\[
 \sum_{\substack{d\le Y\\d\ {\rm squarefree}}}f(d)
 \le\sum_{k\le Y}|g(k)|\lfloor Y/k\rfloor\ll Y.
\]
For \(D/2<d<2D\), \(1/\phi(d)^2\le4f(d)/D^2\), proving (27). Squaring (25)--(26), summing, and also using
\(\sum_{D/2<d<2D}d^{-2}\ll D^{-1}\), proves the first estimate in (6). Since \(D>Q_{\rm init}/2\), one has \(x/D^2\ll(\log x)^{2B_{\rm init}}\), proving the second.

We next prove (8)--(10). Define
\[
 \widehat\Phi(t)=\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)u^{it}{du\over u}.
\]
Repeated integration by parts is valid because \(\Phi\) is infinitely differentiable and compactly supported, and gives
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R}(1+|t|)^2|\widehat\Phi(t)|\,dt<\infty.
\]
Mellin inversion gives
\[
 \Phi((N-p)/(dM))
 ={1\over2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}\widehat\Phi(t)
 ((N-p)/M)^{-it}d^{it}\,dt.                                             \tag{28}
\]
Also
\[
 \log((N-p)/d)=\log((N-p)/D)-\log(d/D).                                \tag{29}
\]
All remaining factors of \(F_d(p)\) depend only on \(d\) or only on \(p\). Equations (28)--(29) are an exact projective representation, and their total variation measure has bounded mass apart from one factor \(O(\log x)\). This proves (8).

Lewko and Lewko, arXiv:1111.6190, Lemma 24, state that for a sequence supported in an interval of length at most \(x\),
\[
 \sum_{q\le Q}{q\over\phi(q)}
 \sum_{\chi\ ({\rm mod}\ q)}^*
 \max_I\left|\sum_{n\in I}a_n\chi(n)\right|^2
 \ll(\log x)^2(x+Q^2)\sum_n|a_n|^2.                                    \tag{30}
\]
For \(R<r\le2R\), \(1/\phi(r)\le2R^{-1}r/\phi(r)\). Apply (30) to each separated profile from (28)--(29), restrict the nonnegative left side to \(r\in{\cal I}_D\), and use Minkowski's inequality in the projective parameter. The prime coefficients obey
\[
 \sum_{p\le2x}(\log p)^2
 \le\log(2x)\sum_{p\le2x}\log p\ll x\log x.
\]
The factors are: \((\log x)^2\) from (30), \((\log x)^2\) from the square of (8), and \(\log x\) from the prime \(L^2\) norm. This proves (9). If \(R\) is comparable to \(D\), then (2) gives
\(x/R\ll R(\log x)^{2B_{\rm init}}\), proving (10).

Lewko and Lewko's Theorem 1 states its Barban--Davenport--Halberstam bound under the hypothesis
\[
 x(\log x)^{-A}\le Q\le x.
\]
For every fixed \(A\), the present upper endpoint \(x^{1/2}\) is smaller than \(x(\log x)^{-A}\) for sufficiently large \(x\). Hence that theorem cannot be applied at the present modulus level. Taking a much larger \(Q\) would include additional moduli and yield a bound at the much larger \(xQ\log x\) scale, not a localized saving for (4).

We prove (12)--(19). On a top-band genuine-prime incidence, put \(p=N-dm\). Substitution into the original block gives (12), because (5) makes the source cutoff equal to one. Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 |P_N^{\rm top}|^2
 \le\left(\sum_{m\ge1}(\log m)^2\Phi(m/M)^2\right){\mathfrak D}_N.
\]
The first factor is \(O_\Phi(M(\log x)^2)\), proving (14).

Expanding the square in (13), the terms \(d_1=d_2\) give (16) and those with \(d_1\ne d_2\) give (17), proving (15). All fixed weights are bounded, \(\Lambda_{\rm pr}(N-dm)^2\le(\log(2x))^2\), and the number of possible pairs \((d,m)\) is \(O(DM)\). By (1), \(DM\ll x\), which proves (16).

Assume (TB-COV4). Since \(D>Q_{\rm init}/2\),
\[
 {x(\log x)^2\over xD(\log x)^{-4}}={(\log x)^6\over D}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus (16), (15), and (TB-COV4) prove (18). From (1), \(M\ll x/D\). Combining this with (14) and (18) gives
\[
 |P_N^{\rm top}|^2=o\!\left(
 {x\over D}(\log x)^2\cdot xD(\log x)^{-4}\right)
 =o(x^2(\log x)^{-2}),
\]
which proves (19).

We prove (21). Exchange the finite \(p\)- and \(d\)-sums in (20). For fixed \(p\), the \(d/D\)-profile divided by \(\log(2x)\) has bounded supremum and bounded total variation, by the scaled-profile check in fact 415fa7afad9006c5. Multiplication by the interval indicator \(1_{d\le x^{1/2}}\) introduces one jump and increases total variation by at most twice the supremum. The convolution proof of the first assertion of fact 415fa7afad9006c5 uses partial summation against the \(d\)-profile and therefore applies unchanged to bounded-variation profiles with finitely many jumps. Since \(D\ge D_*/2\) by (1), it gives arbitrary logarithmic saving in the \(d\)-sum. The remaining prime sum is \(O(x)\) by Chebyshev, proving (21).

Adding and subtracting (20) gives (22) exactly. Under (TB-COV4), equations (19) and (21) show \({\cal E}_N^{\rm top}=o(x/\log x)\). Fact 1de7f7c45ccfee10 gives (23) for its selected same-\(N\) triple and fact f41f5f91b52e0d13 gives \(\mathfrak c(N)\ge C_2>0\). Therefore
\[
 {\cal E}_N^{>}={\cal E}_N-{\cal E}_N^{\rm top}
 \le-c_{\rm dir}{\mathfrak c(N)x\over\log x}
   +o({\mathfrak c(N)x\over\log x}),
\]
which proves (24).

The theorem-interface statements follow from the exact statements of the cited facts. The final displayed affine form follows by writing \(rs=N-d_1m\), so that \(m=(N-rs)/d_1\), and substituting this into \(N-d_2m\). It is recorded only to identify the output of a Vaughan or Heath--Brown expansion; no bound for it is claimed.

glossary.Delta_d^F(N): the F_d-weighted prime discrepancy at residue N modulo d
glossary.F_d(t): the cofactor and smooth-selector profile in the prime variable
glossary.P_N^top(D,M;U): the d<=sqrt(x) portion of the genuine-prime block
glossary.TB-COV4: the sufficient little-o covariance estimate at xD(log x)^(-4)
glossary.cal I_D: the literal top-band modulus set inside one dyadic block
glossary.cal M_N^top(D,M;U): the unrestricted-prime comparison main restricted to d<=sqrt(x)
glossary.cal P(F): the projective L1 norm of exact separated d,t representations of F_d(t)
glossary.mathfrak C_off: the d1 not equal d2 raw two-linear-form covariance
glossary.mathfrak D_N(D,M;U): the raw-Mobius dispersion after Cauchy only in m
glossary.mathfrak D_diag: the d1=d2 diagonal of the dispersion

9e3be7086c095ecb.title: BALANCED LOW-EFFECTIVE C1 TYPE-I PAYMENT AND EXACT TINY RESIDUAL. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100 and eta=kappa/20, and let beta_m<=beta<6/5 in the literal strict-top C1 setting. Thus n=pv is squarefree, p is the unique rough prime, gcd(p,v)=1, p>=Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma), C=mathscr A h, and m_eff=n/gcd(C,n). Let c be squarefree with nc<=Q^K for a fixed K. Let W be extended by zero, supported on Q<=k<2Q, with V_Q(W)<=Q^epsilon for every fixed epsilon>0. Let I_i=[U_i,2U_i) intersect Z, where U_i is comparable to Q^(1/2), and consider
9e3be7086c095ecb.author: slava chan
9e3be7086c095ecb.statement:
BALANCED LOW-EFFECTIVE C1 TYPE-I PAYMENT AND EXACT TINY RESIDUAL. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100 and eta=kappa/20, and let beta_m<=beta<6/5 in the literal strict-top C1 setting. Thus n=pv is squarefree, p is the unique rough prime, gcd(p,v)=1, p>=Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma), C=mathscr A h, and m_eff=n/gcd(C,n). Let c be squarefree with nc<=Q^K for a fixed K. Let W be extended by zero, supported on Q<=k<2Q, with V_Q(W)<=Q^epsilon for every fixed epsilon>0. Let I_i=[U_i,2U_i) intersect Z, where U_i is comparable to Q^(1/2), and consider
S=sum_{u_1 in I_1,u_2 in I_2;gcd(u_1u_2,nc)=1}W(u_1u_2)e_n(C(u_1u_2)^(-1)).
If
Q^eta<=m_eff<Q^(1/2+kappa),
then
|S|<=Q^(1-eta+o(1)).
If instead 1<=m_eff<Q^eta, then necessarily p divides C. Consequently the balanced low-effective range is the disjoint union of the paid chamber Q^eta<=m_eff<Q^(1/2+kappa) and the tiny p-resonant chamber
p divides C, 1<=m_eff<Q^eta.
The subchamber m_eff=1 remains governed only by fact 3566675481b2284a; no fixed-power estimate for the tiny p-resonant chamber is asserted here.
9e3be7086c095ecb.proof:
Assume first m_eff>1 and m_eff>=Q^eta. Apply fact 9be4b1c96a2620dc with a=u_1, b=u_2, A comparable to Q^(1/2), B comparable to Q^(1/2), X=Q, and alpha_a=1 on I_1. The b-variable is otherwise unweighted. The product weight, phase, and complete gate are exactly those in the statement. Since nc is polynomially bounded and V_Q(W)=Q^o(1), that fact gives
|S|<=Q^o(1)[Q/m_eff+Q^(1/2)m_eff^(1/2)].                       (1)
The lower bound m_eff>=Q^eta makes the first term at most Q^(1-eta). The upper bound m_eff<Q^(1/2+kappa) makes the second term at most
Q^(3/4+kappa/2).
For kappa<=1/100 one has 3/4+kappa/2<1-kappa/20=1-eta. Thus (1) proves the displayed payment.

It remains to classify m_eff<Q^eta. The strict-top rough-prime lower bound gives
p>=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma)>Q^(3/10-3/10000)>Q^(29/100).             (2)
Since eta=kappa/20<=1/2000, equation (2) implies p>Q^eta. Because n is squarefree, m_eff is the product of the prime divisors of n not dividing C. If p did not divide C, then p would divide m_eff, contradicting m_eff<Q^eta. Hence p divides C throughout the tiny range. The alternatives m_eff>=Q^eta and m_eff<Q^eta are disjoint and exhaustive. When m_eff=1, fact 9be4b1c96a2620dc is outside its m_eff>1 hypothesis, and fact 3566675481b2284a supplies only its explicitly variation-mass-retaining logarithmic statement. This proves the final scope assertion.

glossary.tiny-effective p-resonant chamber: The balanced C1 range in which p divides the numerator and 1<=m_eff<Q^(kappa/20).

9e63ab11cf963ef5.title: ACTUAL-SOURCE PRODUCT-RESIDUE SATURATOR FOR A CRITICAL SLOPE CLUSTER
9e63ab11cf963ef5.author: slava chan
9e63ab11cf963ef5.statement:
ACTUAL-SOURCE PRODUCT-RESIDUE SATURATOR FOR A CRITICAL SLOPE CLUSTER.

Let p tend through sufficiently large primes and put
  Q=floor(p^(4/5)),  V=2,  H=3p/(2Q),  P=QH/V=3p/4,
  v=2,  n=vp=2p.                                           (1)
Then
  5<=H<=Q^(1/3),  2<=V<H,  P=QH/V,
  P<=p<2P,  gcd(v,p)=1,  p>2Q                              (2)
for all sufficiently large p. Let
  cal U={q in Z:Q<=q<2Q and q is odd}.                     (3)
There is an integer A with
  1<=A<2p,  gcd(A,2p)=1,  A<=Q^2,                          (4)
for which the set
  cal X={x=(q,m,k):q,m in cal U,
                    k=(A-qm)/(2p) is an integer}            (5)
has cardinality
  X_src:=#cal X>=Q/(6H).                                   (6)
Every x in cal X satisfies
  Q<=q,m<2Q,  qm+n k=A,  gcd(qm,n)=1.                      (7)

For x=(q,m,k) put lambda_x=k/q. There is a subset cal Y of cal X such that its slopes lambda_x are pairwise distinct, all lie in one real interval of length at most 1/(12H), and, for every epsilon>0,
  Y:=#cal Y>>_epsilon Q^(1-epsilon)/H.                     (8)
In particular Y>=2 for all sufficiently large p.

Let I be any nonempty integer interval contained either in [H,2H) or in (-2H,-H], put L=#I, and take the constant coefficients
  a_h(x)=1  for h in I and x in cal Y.                     (9)
Regard cal Y as one outer source row and partition it as one nonempty critical cluster in fact 3b2d15db39ad0217. Then its critical-cluster ratio satisfies
  Theta_cl>=(Y+1)/(2Y)>=1/2.                               (10)
On the other hand,
  Gadd=VQ^(1/3)/H=4Q^(4/3)/(3p)
       >=c Q^(1/12)                                        (11)
for an absolute constant c>0 and all sufficiently large p. Hence the source equation, coprimality, natural target bound, source occupancy, bounded critical cover, pairwise distinct slopes, and constant height-separated coefficients do not imply
  Theta_cl<<Gadd^(-1)Q^epsilon                             (12)
for every epsilon>0. In particular, (12) fails on this family when epsilon<1/12 is sufficiently small.

This is an actual-source coefficient-class obstruction to deriving the fixed-power estimate of fact 3b2d15db39ad0217 from source geometry alone. It does not assert that a natural literal mask selects cal Y, does not identify (9) with the full arithmetic coefficient c_q nu_h U_ell chi_ell, gives no global lower bound for Aadd, and does not contradict the verified endpoint strip. Any successful fixed-power literal theorem must use a property of the exact arithmetic weight or cancellation from a larger signed assembly. No PMD closure and no Goldbach conclusion are asserted.
9e63ab11cf963ef5.proof:
We first verify the scale assertions. Since Q=floor(p^(4/5)), for sufficiently large p,
  (1/2)p^(4/5)<=Q<=p^(4/5).                                (13)
Therefore
  H=3p/(2Q)>=3p^(1/5)/2,
so H>=5. Also
  H<=3p^(1/5).
The lower bound in (13) gives
  Q^(1/3)>=2^(-1/3)p^(4/15).
Since 4/15>1/5, one has 3p^(1/5)<=2^(-1/3)p^(4/15) for all sufficiently large p. Hence H<=Q^(1/3). The remaining scale equalities follow from (1), and
  P=3p/4<=p<3p/2=2P.
Also p>2Q for sufficiently large p because Q<=p^(4/5). This proves (2).

The interval [Q,2Q) contains exactly Q integers. At least (Q-1)/2 of them are odd, so, for Q>=3,
  #cal U>=Q/3.                                              (14)
Because every q in cal U is odd and q<2Q<p, every q in cal U is a unit modulo 2p. Thus every product qm with q,m in cal U lies in the unit group modulo 2p. This group has
  phi(2p)=p-1
residue classes. By the pigeonhole principle, there is a unit residue class A modulo 2p represented by at least
  (#cal U)^2/(p-1)>Q^2/(9p)                                (15)
ordered products qm. Choose its representative with 1<=A<2p. For every represented pair, k=(A-qm)/(2p) is an integer, so (5) defines one source triple. Distinct ordered pairs give distinct triples. Equations (14)-(15) therefore give
  X_src>Q^2/(9p).
Since H=3p/(2Q),
  Q/(6H)=Q^2/(9p),                                         (16)
which proves (6).

The chosen residue A is a unit modulo 2p, proving gcd(A,2p)=1. Also A<2p. From (13),
  Q^2>=p^(8/5)/4>2p
for sufficiently large p, proving A<=Q^2. Every q,m in cal U is a unit modulo 2p, so gcd(qm,n)=1. The definition of k gives qm+nk=A. This proves (4) and (7).

Apply fact 28b8af5697fa64eb with C_A=1 and n=2p. Its condition n>=QH holds because, by (1),
  n=2p=(4/3)QH.
That fact covers the slopes of cal X by
  K_cl=ceil(12(1/2+1))+1=19                               (17)
intervals of length at most 1/(12H). Hence one such interval contains at least X_src/19 atoms.

Within this interval group atoms by the exact rational slope k/q. Fact 2359a25d9fc6dd9b proves that every such fibre has cardinality at most tau(A). Select one atom from each nonempty fibre and call the resulting set cal Y. Its slopes are pairwise distinct and
  Y>=X_src/[19 tau(A)]
    >=Q/[114H tau(A)].                                     (18)
Since A<=Q^2, the fixed-power divisor estimate in fact 2359a25d9fc6dd9b gives, for every epsilon>0,
  tau(A)<<_epsilon Q^epsilon.
Insert this in (18) and adjust epsilon to prove (8). Since H<=Q^(1/3), the right side of (8) tends to infinity after choosing epsilon<2/3, so Y>=2 for sufficiently large p.

The slopes in cal Y lie in one interval of length at most 1/(12H), and they are distinct. Fact 714f3597f5ef527c gives for the constant coefficients (9)
  sum_{h in I}sum_{x_1,x_2 in cal Y,x_1 not equal x_2}
    e(h[lambda_{x_1}-lambda_{x_2}])
  >=(L/2)Y(Y-1).                                           (19)
Add the L Y diagonal terms. For the one-cluster partition in fact 3b2d15db39ad0217 this gives
  E_cl=sum_{h in I}|sum_{x in cal Y}e(h lambda_x)|^2
       >=L Y+(L/2)Y(Y-1)
       =(L/2)Y(Y+1).                                       (20)
The clusterwise l1 envelope is
  W_cl=L Y^2.
Thus Theta_cl=E_cl/W_cl>=(Y+1)/(2Y), proving (10).

Finally, equations (1) give the equality in (11). From (13),
  Gadd
  =4Q^(4/3)/(3p)
  >=[4/(3*2^(4/3))]p^(1/15).                              (21)
The upper bound Q<=p^(4/5) gives Q^(1/12)<=p^(1/15). Thus (21) proves the lower bound in (11).

If (12) held for every epsilon>0 with a constant uniform in this family, choose any epsilon<1/12. Equations (10)-(11) would force a fixed positive number to be at most a quantity tending to zero, a contradiction. This proves the coefficient-class obstruction. The construction selected cal Y by an existential residue pigeonhole and critical-cluster pigeonhole, so it makes no assertion that one of the project's natural masks selects this set. It also used constant weights rather than the exact arithmetic weight. These observations prove all scope qualifications.

glossary.cal U: The set of odd integers in the dyadic interval [Q,2Q) used in the product-residue construction.
glossary.cal Y: A retained subset of one critical source-slope cluster containing one representative from each exact-slope fibre.

9ea2dddfbbbd191a.title: SOURCE-WEIGHTED JOINT-(h,t) FOURTH ENERGY FROM ONE-SIDED FAREY CANCELLATION, WITH THE EXACT BOUNDED-VARIATION COEFFICIENT SLOT
9ea2dddfbbbd191a.author: slava chan
9ea2dddfbbbd191a.statement:
SOURCE-WEIGHTED JOINT-(h,t) FOURTH ENERGY FROM ONE-SIDED FAREY CANCELLATION, WITH THE EXACT BOUNDED-VARIATION COEFFICIENT SLOT. Let p be prime and let H,T>=1 satisfy 2H

=p^delta for a fixed delta>0, then for every 0
9ea2dddfbbbd191a.proof:
Because all weights are nonnegative, the full weighted occupancy of (2) is exactly
sum_z |(gamma*gamma)(z)|^2.
Any occupancy with an additional mask between zero and one is at most this full occupancy, proving (4).

For a in F_p put
S(a)=sum_z gamma(z)e_p(az)
    =sum_{h,t}w_hb_t e_p(aht^{-1}).                              (7)
Fourier inversion on the additive group and Parseval give
sum_z |(gamma*gamma)(z)|^2
 =p^{-1}sum_{a in F_p}|S(a)|^4.                                  (8)

If B=0, then every b_t is zero, hence gamma, O_p, and both sides of (4)-(6) are zero. All conclusions are immediate. Henceforth assume B>0.

The zero frequency satisfies
|S(0)|<=WBHT<=BVHT.                                               (9)
For nonzero a, apply the b=0 Farey-fraction estimate recorded in Shparlinski, arXiv:1504.03192v2, Section 1.1, to the rectangle
[T,2T)x[H,2H).
After division by the now positive number B, the denominator weights b_t/B have modulus at most one. The theorem gives the bound O((H+T)p^{o(1)}) for an unweighted numerator interval, uniformly in its upper endpoint because a truncated rectangle is again convex. Discrete partial summation in h therefore gives
max_{a!=0}|S(a)| << BV(H+T)p^{o(1)}.                              (10)

It remains to control the second moment. Additive Parseval gives
p^{-1}sum_a|S(a)|^2=sum_z gamma(z)^2.                             (11)
After expanding the right side, every collision obeys
h_1t_2-h_2t_1=kp
for an integer k of size O(HT/p+1). The collision argument in fact 73fb9efe1286f7e9, equation (8), proves that the unweighted number of these solutions is
<<p^{o(1)}[HT+(HT)^2/p].
Every weighted collision has weight at most W^2B^2. Hence
sum_z gamma(z)^2
 <<W^2B^2p^{o(1)}[HT+(HT)^2/p].                                 (12)

Split (8) into a=0 and a!=0. Equations (9)-(12) give
p^{-1}|S(0)|^4
 <=(BV)^4(HT)^4/p
and
p^{-1}sum_{a!=0}|S(a)|^4
 <=max_{a!=0}|S(a)|^2 p^{-1}sum_a|S(a)|^2
 <<B^4V^2W^2p^{o(1)}
 (H+T)^2[HT+(HT)^2/p].
Since W<=V, these estimates prove (5).

Assume H,T>=p^delta and put m=min(H,T), M=max(H,T). Relative to (HT)^4, the three terms in (5) are
p^{-1},
(H+T)^2/(H^3T^3),
(H+T)^2/(pH^2T^2).
Because H+T<=2M, the last two are at most
4/(m^3M)<=4p^{-4delta},
4/(pm^2)<=4p^{-1-2delta}.
Absorb p^{o(1)} by choosing p sufficiently large in terms of delta and eta. This proves (6). The final scope statements merely record the exact coefficient hypotheses used in (10), which are not conclusions of the cited literal source facts.

glossary.B: The supremum norm of the arbitrary denominator weight b_t.
glossary.O_p: A masked source-weighted suboccupancy of the all-four repeated-pole balance.
glossary.V: The supremum plus total variation norm of the numerator-height weight w_h.
glossary.gamma(z): The nonnegative source-weighted residue distribution of the ratio h/t modulo p.

9ed3e4d0fa15562c.title: EXACT CANCELLATION OF THE DESIGNATED DILATOR-PRIME PHASE BY THE FORCED SOURCE-SHIFT FACTOR
9ed3e4d0fa15562c.author: slava chan
9ed3e4d0fa15562c.statement:
EXACT CANCELLATION OF THE DESIGNATED DILATOR-PRIME PHASE BY THE FORCED SOURCE-SHIFT FACTOR.

Put \(e(z)=\exp(2\pi iz)\) and \(e_q(z)=e(z/q)\). Let \(N,m,a,u_1,u_2\) be positive integers such that \(a\) is prime and
\[
 (a,m u_1u_2)=1,\qquad (m,u_1u_2)=1.
\]
Let \(h_1,h_2\) be nonzero integers, put
\[
 U_{12}=u_1u_2,\qquad
 \Delta_{12}=h_2u_1-h_1u_2,
\]
and assume \(\Delta_{12}\ne0\). For \(i=1,2\), let \(F_i\) be an integrable complex function on \(\mathbb R\), use
\[
 \widehat F_i(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R}F_i(t)e(-\xi t)\,dt,
\]
and define the forced source-shifted transforms
\[
 \mathcal J_i
 =e\!\left(\frac{Nh_i}{amu_i}\right)
  \widehat F_i(h_i/u_i).
\]
Every inverse below is taken in the displayed coprime modulus. Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal J_1\overline{\mathcal J_2}\,
 e_a\!\left(N\Delta_{12}(mU_{12})^{-1}\right)
 =
 \widehat F_1(h_1/u_1)\overline{\widehat F_2(h_2/u_2)}\,
 e_{mU_{12}}\!\left(-N\Delta_{12}a^{-1}\right).
 }                                                               \tag{1}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal J_1\overline{\mathcal J_2}\,
 e_{am}\!\left(N\Delta_{12}U_{12}^{-1}\right)
 =
 \widehat F_1(h_1/u_1)\overline{\widehat F_2(h_2/u_2)}\,
 e_{U_{12}}\!left(-N\Delta_{12}(am)^{-1}\right).
 }                                                               \tag{2}
\]
If
\[
 d_{12}=(u_1,u_2),\qquad
 L_{12}=\operatorname {lcm}(u_1,u_2)=U_{12}/d_{12},\qquad
 \delta_{12}=\Delta_{12}/d_{12},
\]
then \(\delta_{12}\) is a nonzero integer and the right side of (2) is
\[
 \widehat F_1(h_1/u_1)\overline{\widehat F_2(h_2/u_2)}\,
 e_{L_{12}}\!\left(-N\delta_{12}(am)^{-1}\right).              \tag{3}
\]

Consequently, in the source-side NR-FRAME identity of fact b62f6ddbc641c393, suppose \(a\nmid N\Delta_{12}\), so its designated prime factor
\[
 e_a\!\left(N\Delta_{12}(mU_{12})^{-1}\right)
\]
is nontrivial. If one extracts from
\(\mathcal J_{a,m}(\alpha_1)
 \overline{\mathcal J_{a,m}(\alpha_2)}\)
the mandatory scalar source-shift phase and leaves the two raw Fourier transforms as coefficients, then (1) removes the modulus-\(a\) character exactly and replaces it by a character modulo \(mU_{12}\); with the full CRT factor, (2)--(3) return exactly to the original lcm-modulus crossed phase. Therefore a direct fixed-prime scalar-theorem splice cannot both strip off that mandatory source-shift phase and still claim the displayed nontrivial modulus-\(a\) oscillation. To retain the prime oscillation, an analytic theorem must accept the coupled shifted transforms \(\mathcal J\), or a further source-specific transform must produce a new cancellation mechanism. This is only an exact no-fit for that phase-extraction splice: it is not a bound for NR-FRAME and does not rule out other source-specific or vector-valued arguments.
9ed3e4d0fa15562c.proof:
By definition,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathcal J_1\overline{\mathcal J_2}
 &=
 e\!\left(\frac{N}{am}
       \left(\frac{h_1}{u_1}-\frac{h_2}{u_2}\right)\right)
 \widehat F_1(h_1/u_1)
 \overline{\widehat F_2(h_2/u_2)}\\
 &=
 e\!\left(-\frac{N\Delta_{12}}{amU_{12}}\right)
 \widehat F_1(h_1/u_1)
 \overline{\widehat F_2(h_2/u_2)}.                       \tag{4}
\end{aligned}
\]
For coprime positive integers \(r,s\) and every integer \(z\), additive reciprocity gives
\[
 e_r(zs^{-1})=e\!\left(\frac{z}{rs}\right)e_s(-zr^{-1}). \tag{5}
\]
Indeed, if \(\bar s\) is an inverse of \(s\) modulo \(r\) and \(\bar r\) is an inverse of \(r\) modulo \(s\), then
\[
 s\bar s+r\bar r\equiv1\pmod{rs};
\]
dividing by \(rs\) and exponentiating proves (5).

Apply (5) with \(r=a\), \(s=mU_{12}\), and \(z=N\Delta_{12}\). The hypotheses make \(a\) and \(mU_{12}\) coprime, so
\[
 e_a\!\left(N\Delta_{12}(mU_{12})^{-1}\right)
 =
 e\!\left(\frac{N\Delta_{12}}{amU_{12}}\right)
 e_{mU_{12}}\!\left(-N\Delta_{12}a^{-1}\right).         \tag{6}
\]
Multiplying (6) by (4) cancels the two ordinary exponential factors and proves (1).

Next apply (5) with \(r=am\), \(s=U_{12}\), and the same \(z\). The assumption \((am,U_{12})=1\) gives
\[
 e_{am}\!\left(N\Delta_{12}U_{12}^{-1}\right)
 =
 e\!\left(\frac{N\Delta_{12}}{amU_{12}}\right)
 e_{U_{12}}\!\left(-N\Delta_{12}(am)^{-1}\right).       \tag{7}
\]
Multiplication by (4) proves (2).

Since \(d_{12}\) divides both \(u_1\) and \(u_2\), it divides
\(h_2u_1-h_1u_2=\Delta_{12}\). Thus
\(\delta_{12}=\Delta_{12}/d_{12}\) is an integer, and it is nonzero because \(\Delta_{12}\ne0\). Also \(U_{12}=d_{12}L_{12}\). Therefore
\[
 e_{U_{12}}\!\left(-N\Delta_{12}(am)^{-1}\right)
 =
 e_{d_{12}L_{12}}\!\left(-Nd_{12}\delta_{12}(am)^{-1}\right)
 =
 e_{L_{12}}\!\left(-N\delta_{12}(am)^{-1}\right),       \tag{8}
\]
where reducing an inverse of \(am\) modulo \(U_{12}\) modulo \(L_{12}\) gives an inverse modulo \(L_{12}\). This proves (3).

In fact b62f6ddbc641c393, the displayed \(\mathcal J_{a,m}(\alpha)\) has exactly the form used here, and its designated prime factor is the left character in (1). On the nonresonant sector \(a\nmid N\Delta_{12}\), that character is nontrivial because \(mU_{12}\) is a unit modulo \(a\). But equation (1) is an exact identity: after the scalar factor in (4) is extracted, no modulus-\(a\) character remains. Equation (2), followed by (3), identifies the full source-modulus phase with the original lcm phase. Hence the stated fixed-prime phase-extraction splice has no matching kernel. The final alternatives and scope limitation assert no analytic estimate and follow directly from these identities.

9ef4a136053bd1e1.title: EXACT RECURSION OF THE COMPULSORY-ROUGH-PRIME COMPLEMENTARY PROJECTOR
9ef4a136053bd1e1.author: slava chan
9ef4a136053bd1e1.statement:
EXACT RECURSION OF THE COMPULSORY-ROUGH-PRIME COMPLEMENTARY PROJECTOR.

Assume the nonzero branch and notation of fact bab04e002177e282. Thus b=pb' is squarefree, p is prime, b'<F_0, p does not divide N, and (a,b)=1. Assume b'>1. Let N_{p,b'} be the unique integer with
 1<=N_{p,b'}<=b',
 pN_{p,b'} congruent N (mod b').                           (1)
For h|b' with (h,N_{p,b'})=1 define the standard target-shifted centered response
 R^{N_{p,b'}}_{b',h}(a)
  =product_{q|h}
    [e_q(N_{p,b'}[a(b'/q)]^(-1))+1/(q-1)].                 (2)
Define
 P^{N_{p,b'}}_{b',>F_0/p}(a)
  =sum_{h|b';h>F_0/p;(h,N_{p,b'})=1}
    c_{b'/h}(N_{p,b'})
    R^{N_{p,b'}}_{b',h}(a)/phi(b'/h).                       (3)
Then the full shifted-cutoff complementary superposition of fact bab04e002177e282 satisfies exactly
 P^{(p)}_{b',>F_0/p}(a)
  =P^{N_{p,b'}}_{b',>F_0/p}(a).                             (4)
Consequently,
 P_b(a)
  =r_{p,b}(a)P^{N_{p,b'}}_{b',>F_0/p}(a).                   (5)

Thus after the compulsory p-local centered factor is removed, the remaining factor is again a complete primewise-centered conductor projector of the same form, now on the smaller squarefree modulus b', with shifted target N_{p,b'} and shifted cutoff F_0/p. The target depends on p and b'; (4) does not create a common target across different complementary moduli.

If b'=1 and p>F_0, the shifted complementary superposition in fact bab04e002177e282 consists only of h=1 and equals one, so (5) reduces to P_p(a)=r_{p,p}(a).

No estimate for the recursive projector, ROP, CEN-MZB, C_small or Goldbach is asserted.
9ef4a136053bd1e1.proof:
Because b is squarefree and b=pb', one has (p,b')=1. Therefore multiplication by p is invertible modulo b', and the representative N_{p,b'} in (1) exists uniquely.

Fix q|h|b'. Reducing (1) modulo q gives
 N_{p,b'} congruent Np^(-1) (mod q).                         (6)
Also
 [ap(b'/q)]^(-1)
 =p^(-1)[a(b'/q)]^(-1) (mod q).                             (7)
Hence the q-local exponential in the response from fact bab04e002177e282 is
 e_q(N[ap(b'/q)]^(-1))
 =e_q(Np^(-1)[a(b'/q)]^(-1))
 =e_q(N_{p,b'}[a(b'/q)]^(-1)).                              (8)
The centering constants 1/(q-1) are unchanged. Multiplying (8) over q|h proves
 R^{(p)}_{b',h}(a)=R^{N_{p,b'}}_{b',h}(a).                  (9)

Next fix a prime q|b'. Since p is a unit modulo q, equation (1) implies
 q divides N_{p,b'} if and only if q divides N.              (10)
Every divisor s|b' is squarefree. For a prime q,
 c_q(M)=q-1 when q|M and c_q(M)=-1 when q does not divide M: this follows from the defining sum over nonzero residues, which is q-1 in the first case and the sum of all nontrivial q-th roots except the zero residue in the second case. Ramanujan sums are multiplicative on squarefree moduli by the Chinese remainder theorem. Therefore (10) gives
 c_s(N_{p,b'})=c_s(N)                                       (11)
for every s|b'. The same equivalence gives
 (h,N_{p,b'})=1 if and only if (h,N)=1.                     (12)

Finally ph>F_0 is equivalent to h>F_0/p. Insert (9), (11) and (12) into formula (4) of fact bab04e002177e282:
 P^{(p)}_{b',>F_0/p}(a)
  =sum_{h|b';ph>F_0;(h,N)=1}
    c_{b'/h}(N)R^{(p)}_{b',h}(a)/phi(b'/h).
The resulting sum is exactly (3), proving (4). Equation (5) follows from formula (6) of fact bab04e002177e282.

If b'=1, the only divisor h is one, the empty response product is one, c_1(N)=phi(1)=1, and the condition ph>F_0 is p>F_0. Hence the complementary sum is one in the stated case. This proves the final identity and all scope restrictions.

glossary.N_{p,b'}: The positive residue representative satisfying pN_{p,b'} congruent N modulo b'.
glossary.P^{N_{p,b'}}_{b',>F_0/p}(a): The standard complete centered conductor projector on modulus b', target N_{p,b'}, and cutoff F_0/p.

9ef7fac8978ac244.title: DIVISOR BOUND FOR A SQUAREFREE COMMON-CORE CONDUCTOR PROJECTOR. Let \(N\) be a positive integer, let \(q\ge2\) be squarefree, let \(a,t,u\) be integers satisfying
9ef7fac8978ac244.author: slava chan
9ef7fac8978ac244.proof:
For a positive integer \(s\), define the Ramanujan sum
\[
 c_s(N)=\sum_{\substack{z\ ({\rm mod}\ s)\\(z,s)=1}}e_s(Nz).
\]
For every divisor \(f\mid q\), define
\[
 \mathcal K_f^{(a)}(q;t,u)=
 \prod_{p\mid f}\left[1+(p-1)e_p\!\left(-Nt[au(q/p)]^{-1}\right)\right],
\]
where the inverse is taken modulo \(p\). By fact adb3b38d14670d3c,
\[
 \mathcal P_{q,a}^{>T}(t,u)=\frac1{\phi(q)}
 \sum_{\substack{f\mid q\\ f>T\\(f,N)=1}}
 c_{q/f}(N)\mathcal K_f^{(a)}(q;t,u). \tag{4}
\]
The defining sum for \(c_s(N)\) has at most \(s\) summands, each of absolute value one. Hence
\[
 |c_{q/f}(N)|\le q/f. \tag{5}
\]
For each prime \(p\mid f\), the corresponding factor in \(\mathcal K_f^{(a)}\) has absolute value at most
\[
 |1+(p-1)e_p(\cdots)|\le 1+(p-1)=p.
\]
Since \(q\), and therefore \(f\), is squarefree, multiplication over \(p\mid f\) gives
\[
 |\mathcal K_f^{(a)}(q;t,u)|\le\prod_{p\mid f}p=f. \tag{6}
\]
Thus every summand in (4), before division by \(\phi(q)\), has absolute value at most \(q\). There are at most \(\tau(q)\) divisors \(f\mid q\), proving the first inequality in (2).

As \(q\) is squarefree,
\[
 \frac q{\phi(q)}=\prod_{p\mid q}\frac p{p-1}
 \le\prod_{p\mid q}2=2^{\omega(q)}=\tau(q),
\]
which proves the second inequality in (2).

Finally fix \(\varepsilon>0\). Choose a real \(P_\varepsilon\) such that \(4\le p^\varepsilon\) for every prime \(p>P_\varepsilon\). Since \(q\) is squarefree,
\[
 \tau(q)^2=4^{\omega(q)}
 =\prod_{p\mid q}4
 \le \left(\prod_{p\le P_\varepsilon}4\right)
       \prod_{\substack{p\mid q\\p>P_\varepsilon}}p^\varepsilon
 \le C_\varepsilon q^\varepsilon,
\]
where the first product is over the finitely many primes at most \(P_\varepsilon\). Combining this with (2) proves (3).
