glossary.G_Nq(psi): the N-twisted Gauss sum of psi modulo q
glossary.K_f^(a)(q;t,u): the explicit prime-local Euler response product for the conductor divisor f
glossary.P_epsilon: a threshold beyond which every prime p satisfies 4 at most p to the epsilon
glossary.P_q,a^{>T}(t,u): the common-core character projector restricted to primitive conductor greater than T and coprime to N
glossary.c_s(N): the Ramanujan sum of N modulo s
glossary.f_psi: the primitive conductor of the Dirichlet character psi
glossary.omega(q): the number of distinct prime divisors of q
glossary.tau(q): the number of positive divisors of q

9fa397ffcac491a6.title: Let U_4={1,2,3,4}. Define the support-disjointness matrix J_1 on the two supports emptyset and {1} by
9fa397ffcac491a6.author: slava chan
9fa397ffcac491a6.statement:
Let U_4={1,2,3,4}. Define the support-disjointness matrix J_1 on the two supports emptyset and {1} by
J_1(A,B)=1_{A intersect B is empty}.
Then
J_1=[[1,1],[1,0]]
is not positive semidefinite. On the full family of subsets of U_4, the support-disjointness matrix
J_4(F,G)=1_{F intersect G is empty}
equals the four-fold Kronecker tensor power J_1 tensor J_1 tensor J_1 tensor J_1 and is also indefinite. Consequently, the signed sixteen-face expansion of a four-prime support-disjoint mask is not, merely by being an exact inclusion-exclusion identity, a positive-semidefinite Gram decomposition.

Nevertheless every literal finite rectangular packet kernel has a canonical positive block dilation with an exact norm cost. Precisely, let H_left and H_right be finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces and let K:H_right->H_left be any linear operator, including a literal equal-carrier support-disjoint packet kernel with all weights, windows, partition indices, and support-face indices already bundled. Define
P_K=
[[(KK^*)^{1/2}, K],
 [K^*, (K^*K)^{1/2}]]
on H_left direct_sum H_right.
Then P_K is positive semidefinite, its off-diagonal corner is exactly K, and
||P_K||_op=2||K||_op.
For B>=0, the scalar-diagonal block matrix
D_{B,K}=[[B I_{H_left},K],[K^*,B I_{H_right}]]
is positive semidefinite if and only if ||K||_op<=B. Thus a positive dilation exists on the actual packet span, but it either pays the square-root diagonal operators in P_K or assumes exactly the operator bound ||K||<=B that one seeks. It does not make K itself positive and does not make the individual signed faces positive.

Finally, for every product P of four distinct odd primes let Q_P be any finite actual companion index set with positive column energies, and let Gamma_P be the normalized weighted companion Gram defined in fact be4e5ad5378f0122 after all q-dependent centered window multipliers have been inserted. For a prescribed nonnegative function delta(P), the exact all-P arbitrary-coefficient quadratic-form target is
for every such P and every z=(z_q)_{q in Q_P},
|sum_{q,q' in Q_P}overline(z_q)(Gamma_P(q,q')-1_{q=q'})z_{q'}|
 <=delta(P)sum_{q in Q_P}|z_q|^2.                                        (T)
Statement (T) is equivalent for every P to
||Gamma_P-I||_op<=delta(P).
A fixed-power companion compression would require a separately proved eta>0 and a uniform estimate delta(P)<=P^{-eta} in the literal arithmetic family. No such eta, no positivity of the signed support-face ledger, and no PAVG27 estimate is asserted here.
9fa397ffcac491a6.proof:
The matrix J_1 has determinant -1, so its two real eigenvalues have opposite signs and it is indefinite. For subsets F,G of U_4, disjointness holds exactly when, independently at each coordinate i, the two membership bits are not both one. Hence
J_4(F,G)=product_{i=1}^4 J_1(1_{i in F},1_{i in G}),
which is the Kronecker tensor identity. If lambda_plus>0 and lambda_minus<0 are the two eigenvalues of J_1, then lambda_minus lambda_plus^3 is an eigenvalue of J_4, so J_4 is indefinite. Inclusion-exclusion gives the entries of this matrix but cannot change its spectrum; therefore exactness of the sixteen-face identity does not prove positive semidefiniteness.

Let K=U|K| be the polar decomposition, where |K|=(K^*K)^{1/2}. On the support of |K| one has (KK^*)^{1/2}=U|K|U^*. Consequently
P_K=
[U; I]|K|[U^*, I]
on the nonzero singular subspaces, with zero action on the remaining kernel directions. This is positive semidefinite and its off-diagonal corner is U|K|=K. Equivalently, a singular-value decomposition splits P_K into two-by-two blocks
[[s,s],[s,s]]
for the singular values s of K, together with zero blocks. Every such block has eigenvalues 0 and 2s. Therefore ||P_K||=2||K||.

If ||K||<=B and B>0, then K/B is a contraction. The quadratic form of
[[I,K/B],[(K/B)^*,I]]
at (x,y) is
||x||^2+||y||^2+2Re<(K/B)y,x>
>=||x||^2+||y||^2-2||x||||y||
=(||x||-||y||)^2>=0.
Multiplying this positive block by B proves D_{B,K} is positive. Conversely, if D_{B,K} is positive, take unit vectors x,y with |<Ky,x>| arbitrarily close to ||K|| and multiply one vector by a phase so that Re<Ky,x> is negative. Positivity applied to (x,y) gives 2B-2|<Ky,x>|>=0. Passing to the supremum yields ||K||<=B. When B=0 the same argument forces K=0, and the equivalence follows.

For the last assertion, Gamma_P-I is Hermitian because Gamma_P is a Gram matrix. The operator norm of a finite-dimensional Hermitian matrix A equals
sup_{z nonzero}|<Az,z>|/||z||^2.
Applying this with A=Gamma_P-I shows that (T) is exactly equivalent to the displayed operator inequality for each P. Requiring delta(P)<=P^{-eta} is an additional quantitative theorem, not a consequence of the dilation identities.

glossary.D_{B,K}: scalar-diagonal block completion of K at diagonal level B
glossary.Gamma_P: actual diagonally normalized weighted companion Gram at modulus product P
glossary.J_1: one-prime support-disjointness matrix on the empty and occupied support states
glossary.J_4: four-prime support-disjointness matrix on all sixteen support subsets
glossary.P_K: canonical positive block dilation of a rectangular packet kernel K
glossary.all-P arbitrary-coefficient target: the quadratic-form inequality (T), required uniformly for every allowed P and every coefficient vector z
glossary.delta(P): unproved target bound for the centered normalized Gram at P

9fd295b783317ab1.title: SIMULTANEOUS FACTORIZATION OF ALL COMPULSORY ROUGH PRIMES AND THE THREE-PRIME LIMIT
9fd295b783317ab1.author: slava chan
9fd295b783317ab1.statement:
SIMULTANEOUS FACTORIZATION OF ALL COMPULSORY ROUGH PRIMES AND THE THREE-PRIME LIMIT.

Assume the actual high-conductor notation and scales of fact 14fe68fdcbfd99ff. Thus b is squarefree, b=Q^(4/3+o(1)), F_0=Q^(1-2eta+o(1)) with fixed 0<eta<1/12, and
 P_b(a)
  =sum_{f|b;f>F_0,(f,N)=1}
    c_{b/f}(N)R_{b,f}(a)/phi(b/f)                            (1)
for (a,b)=1.

Define
 L_b=product_{p|b;b/p<F_0}p,                                 (2)
with the empty product equal to one, and put b_0=b/L_b. Every active conductor f in (1) contains L_b. If (L_b,N)>1, then
 P_b(a)=0.                                                   (3)

Assume (L_b,N)=1 and b_0>1. Let N_{L_b,b_0} be the unique integer satisfying
 1<=N_{L_b,b_0}<=b_0,
 L_bN_{L_b,b_0} congruent N (mod b_0).                       (4)
For h|b_0 define
 R^{N_{L_b,b_0}}_{b_0,h}(a)
  =product_{q|h}
    [e_q(N_{L_b,b_0}[a(b_0/q)]^(-1))+1/(q-1)],              (5)
and define the residual centered projector
 P^{N_{L_b,b_0}}_{b_0,>F_0/L_b}(a)
  =sum_{h|b_0;h>F_0/L_b;(h,N_{L_b,b_0})=1}
    c_{b_0/h}(N_{L_b,b_0})
    R^{N_{L_b,b_0}}_{b_0,h}(a)/phi(b_0/h).                  (6)
Then exactly
 P_b(a)
  =R_{b,L_b}(a)
    P^{N_{L_b,b_0}}_{b_0,>F_0/L_b}(a).                      (7)
If b_0=1, equation (7) holds with the residual factor interpreted as one; in that case L_b=b>F_0.

For all sufficiently large Q,
 omega(L_b)<=3,                                              (8)
where omega(L_b) is the number of distinct prime divisors of L_b. Thus the common factor R_{b,L_b} in (7) is a product of at most three compulsory centered prime-local traces.

No estimate for either factor in (7), the residual smooth-modulus branch, ROP, CEN-MZB, C_small or Goldbach is asserted.
9fd295b783317ab1.proof:
Let p be a prime divisor of L_b. By definition b/p<F_0. If an active divisor f|b did not contain p, then squarefreeness would give f|b/p and hence f<=b/p<F_0, contradicting f>F_0. Therefore every active f contains every prime divisor of L_b, hence contains L_b.

If (L_b,N)>1, some p|L_b also divides N. The activity condition (f,N)=1 forbids p|f, contradicting the compulsory containment just proved. Thus there are no active conductors and the sum (1) is empty, proving (3).

Assume (L_b,N)=1. Every active conductor has a unique form
 f=L_bh,  h|b_0,  L_bh>F_0,  (h,N)=1.                      (9)
Its cofactor is b/f=b_0/h. Primewise multiplicativity of the response gives
 R_{b,L_bh}(a)
  =R_{b,L_b}(a)
   product_{q|h}
    [e_q(N[aL_b(b_0/q)]^(-1))+1/(q-1)].                    (10)
The factor R_{b,L_b}(a) is independent of h.

Because (L_b,b_0)=1, the transported target in (4) exists uniquely. For q|b_0,
 N_{L_b,b_0} congruent NL_b^(-1) (mod q).                   (11)
Also
 [aL_b(b_0/q)]^(-1)
 =L_b^(-1)[a(b_0/q)]^(-1) (mod q).                          (12)
Equations (11)-(12) identify the q-product in (10) with (5).

For every prime q|b_0, equation (4) and (q,L_b)=1 show that q divides N_{L_b,b_0} if and only if q divides N. As proved in fact 9ef4a136053bd1e1, this equality of prime divisibility patterns on squarefree divisors gives
 (h,N)=1 iff (h,N_{L_b,b_0})=1,
 c_s(N)=c_s(N_{L_b,b_0})                                    (13)
for all h,s|b_0. Finally L_bh>F_0 is equivalent to h>F_0/L_b. Insert (9)-(13) into (1), factor out R_{b,L_b}(a), and the remaining sum is (6). This proves (7) when b_0>1.

If b_0=1, then L_b=b. Since b=Q^(4/3+o(1)) and F_0=Q^(1-2eta+o(1)), one has b>F_0 for sufficiently large Q. The only active complementary divisor is h=1, its response is the empty product one, and c_1(N)/phi(1)=1. Hence the residual factor is one and (7) remains valid.

It remains to prove (8). Every p|L_b satisfies p>b/F_0. If omega(L_b)>=4, choose four distinct prime divisors p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4 of L_b. Since their product divides the squarefree integer b,
 b>=p_1p_2p_3p_4>(b/F_0)^4.                                 (14)
Equation (14) implies F_0^4>b^3. But the actual scales give
 b^3/F_0^4
 =Q^(4+o(1))/Q^(4-8eta+o(1))
 =Q^(8eta+o(1)),
which tends to infinity because eta>0 is fixed. Thus b^3>F_0^4 for sufficiently large Q, contradicting (14). Hence omega(L_b)<=3. This proves (8) and all scope restrictions.

glossary.L_b: The product of all prime divisors p of b for which b/p<F_0.
glossary.N_{L_b,b_0}: The transported target satisfying L_bN_{L_b,b_0} congruent N modulo b_0.

a05e9cd7387e457c.title: CENTERED-ROW CRITICAL-FREQUENCY SATURATION NO-FIT. Let p be a prime, let N be an integer with p not dividing N, and let k_0 be a nonzero residue modulo p. There exists a row Z on Z/pZ satisfying sum_{z mod p} Z(z)=0 such that its unit-inversion Fourier response Y(k)=sum_{u mod p, u nonzero} Z(u)e_p(kNu^{-1}) obeys Y(k_0)=p-1 and Y(k)=-1 for every k not congruent to k_0 modulo p. Consequently, for every set K of residues modulo p containing k_0, sum_{k in K}|Y(k)|^2=(p-1)^2+|K|-1, while sum_{k mod p, k nonzero}|Y(k)|^2=p^2-p-1. Hence even a short critical band containing k_0 can carry asymptotically all complete nonzero-frequency energy. In particular, exact total centering together with the unit-inversion Fourier/Dirichlet-kernel structure of fact 7264046d8776d59f cannot alone yield a band-density or logarithmic saving. This assertion concerns arbitrary centered rows in that formal transform and does not assert that the constructed row is realizable by the literal reflected q_1,q_2,h/Mobius family H_{S,bold t}
a05e9cd7387e457c.author: slava chan
a05e9cd7387e457c.statement: CENTERED-ROW CRITICAL-FREQUENCY SATURATION NO-FIT. Let p be a prime, let N be an integer with p not dividing N, and let k_0 be a nonzero residue modulo p. There exists a row Z on Z/pZ satisfying sum_{z mod p} Z(z)=0 such that its unit-inversion Fourier response Y(k)=sum_{u mod p, u nonzero} Z(u)e_p(kNu^{-1}) obeys Y(k_0)=p-1 and Y(k)=-1 for every k not congruent to k_0 modulo p. Consequently, for every set K of residues modulo p containing k_0, sum_{k in K}|Y(k)|^2=(p-1)^2+|K|-1, while sum_{k mod p, k nonzero}|Y(k)|^2=p^2-p-1. Hence even a short critical band containing k_0 can carry asymptotically all complete nonzero-frequency energy. In particular, exact total centering together with the unit-inversion Fourier/Dirichlet-kernel structure of fact 7264046d8776d59f cannot alone yield a band-density or logarithmic saving. This assertion concerns arbitrary centered rows in that formal transform and does not assert that the constructed row is realizable by the literal reflected q_1,q_2,h/Mobius family H_{S,bold t}.
a05e9cd7387e457c.proof:
Define Z(0)=1 and, for every nonzero u modulo p, define Z(u)=e_p(-k_0Nu^{-1}). Because p does not divide k_0N, inversion followed by multiplication by -k_0N permutes the nonzero residues modulo p. The complete additive-character sum over all residues is zero, so
sum_{u nonzero} Z(u)=sum_{a nonzero}e_p(a)=-1.
It follows that sum_{z mod p}Z(z)=Z(0)+sum_{u nonzero}Z(u)=1-1=0.

For any residue k modulo p, substitute the definition of Z into the response:
Y(k)=sum_{u nonzero}e_p((k-k_0)Nu^{-1}).
If k=k_0, every summand equals one, so Y(k_0)=p-1. If k is not k_0, then (k-k_0)N is nonzero modulo p, and inversion followed by multiplication by (k-k_0)N again permutes the nonzero residues. Therefore Y(k)=sum_{a nonzero}e_p(a)=-1.

If K contains k_0, exactly one term in its energy has square (p-1)^2 and each of the other |K|-1 terms has square 1. This proves
sum_{k in K}|Y(k)|^2=(p-1)^2+|K|-1.
Since k_0 is nonzero, the set of all nonzero frequencies contains k_0 and p-2 other residues, hence
sum_{k nonzero}|Y(k)|^2=(p-1)^2+(p-2)=p^2-p-1.
For any family of frequency sets K containing k_0, including sets whose cardinality is comparable to p/M_0 when that is a short critical scale, the ratio of the displayed band energy to the complete nonzero energy is at least (p-1)^2/(p^2-p-1), which tends to one as p tends to infinity. Thus no uniform estimate gaining a factor determined only by short band density, and in particular no uniform logarithmic saving, follows from centering and the formal unit-inversion transform alone. The final scope restriction is explicit: the construction supplies an arbitrary centered row, not a realization of the literal H-row from the predecessor.

glossary.K: a selected set of residue frequencies containing k_0
glossary.Y: the unit-inversion Fourier response of Z
glossary.Z: an abstract centered row on the residue classes modulo p
glossary.k_0: the prescribed nonzero residue frequency at which the response concentrates

a08224dfb222c580.title: EXACT ADDITIVE-FOURIER CONDUCTOR LEDGER FOR THE MULTIPLICATIVELY CENTERED PHYSICAL RAY KERNEL, INCLUDING THE m=2 CANCELLATION AND THE CONSTANT-CORRECTION PAYMENT
a08224dfb222c580.author: slava chan
a08224dfb222c580.statement:
EXACT ADDITIVE-FOURIER CONDUCTOR LEDGER FOR THE MULTIPLICATIVELY CENTERED PHYSICAL RAY KERNEL, INCLUDING THE m=2 CANCELLATION AND THE CONSTANT-CORRECTION PAYMENT.

Let m be a positive squarefree integer and let c,n be integers satisfying
gcd(cn,m)=1. For every positive divisor t of m and integers a,b, put
S_t(a,b)=sum_{x (mod t), gcd(x,t)=1} e_t(a x+b x^{-1}).                 (1)
If st=m and t>1, let s^{-1} denote the inverse of s modulo t and define
P_{t;c,s}(n)
 = (1/t) sum_{a (mod t), gcd(a,t)=1}
       S_t(a,-c s^{-1}) e_t(-a n).                                    (2)
Then
e_m(-c n^{-1})-mu(m)/m
 = sum_{st=m, t>1} mu(s) P_{t;c,s}(n)/s,                              (3)
and therefore
e_m(-c n^{-1})-mu(m)/phi(m)
 = sum_{st=m, t>1} mu(s) P_{t;c,s}(n)/s
   +mu(m)(1/m-1/phi(m)).                                               (4)
Thus the additive t=1 term in the full Fourier decomposition is mu(m)/m; it is not GA-qPRINC, which is the multiplicative-character principal term mu(m)/phi(m) of fact 764588e99974a6d9.

For m=2, the sole term in the sum in (4) equals -1/2 and the constant correction equals +1/2. Hence both cancel and
e_2(-c n^{-1})-mu(2)/phi(2)=0,                                       (5)
in agreement with K^circ_{2,c}(n)=0.

There is also an exact literal consumer. Adopt one fixed good-W hard family, coefficient B_lambda(R), literal selector Theta_lambda(R,R'), and physical conductors m_q from fact 764588e99974a6d9. Define the correction form
H_Theta^corr
 = sum_lambda sum_{R != R'}
   Theta_lambda(R,R') B_lambda(R) conjugate(B_lambda(R'))
   mu(m_q)(1/m_q-1/phi(m_q)).                                         (6)
Then
|H_Theta^corr| <= x^{o(1)} |omega_F|^2 B F^2.                         (7)
Every exact marker, source, target-gcd, fixed-U, ordering, collision, deletion, provenance, coprimality and projective selector is retained in (6); in proving (7), these selectors only delete terms after absolute values. The same bound holds for a union of x^{o(1)} exact frozen-label families. In particular, if Dcal<=Q^2, then
|H_Theta^corr|
 <= x^{o(1)} |omega_F|^2 B Q^2 F^2/Dcal.                              (8)

Equations (3)-(8) are an identity and an already-paid correction ledger only. They do not estimate any nonconstant P_{t;c,s} face, prove GA-qCENT, GA-CqKLOO-VEC, GA-RAY-SPEC, GA-NR-DIL, a good-W tail payment, or Goldbach.
a08224dfb222c580.proof:
Assume first m>1. Full additive Fourier inversion on Z/mZ gives
e_m(-c n^{-1})
 = (1/m) sum_{a (mod m)} S_m(a,-c)e_m(-an).                           (9)
Indeed, after inserting (1) with t=m, the inner sum over a is m if the unit variable x is congruent to n modulo m and is zero otherwise.

Partition the frequencies a modulo m by s=gcd(a,m), using gcd(0,m)=m. Put t=m/s. For t>1, every frequency in this stratum has a unique representation
a=s a' (mod m),  a' (mod t), gcd(a',t)=1.                             (10)
Because m is squarefree, s and t are coprime and squarefree. Let t^{-1} denote the inverse of t modulo s and s^{-1} the inverse of s modulo t. The CRT identity
e_m(y)=e_s(y t^{-1})e_t(y s^{-1})                                    (11)
and the CRT parametrization of the unit group give
S_m(sa',-c)
 = [sum_{x (mod s)}^* e_s(-c t^{-1}x^{-1})]
   [sum_{x (mod t)}^* e_t(a'x-c s^{-1}x^{-1})].                       (12)
The first bracket is the Ramanujan sum c_s(-c t^{-1}). Its argument is a unit modulo the squarefree integer s, so
c_s(-c t^{-1})=mu(s).                                                  (13)
The second bracket is S_t(a',-c s^{-1}). Also
e_m(-sa'n)=e_t(-a'n).                                                  (14)
Consequently, the contribution of the exact gcd stratum s to (9) is
(mu(s)/s) (1/t) sum_{a' (mod t)}^*
 S_t(a',-c s^{-1})e_t(-a'n)
 =mu(s)P_{t;c,s}(n)/s.                                                 (15)

The remaining frequency is a=0, corresponding to s=m,t=1. Its contribution is
S_m(0,-c)/m=c_m(-c)/m=mu(m)/m,                                        (16)
again because c is a unit and m is squarefree. Summing (15) and (16) proves (3). Subtracting mu(m)/phi(m) from both sides proves (4). When m=1, both sides of (3) and (4) are zero, so the identities also hold in that case.

Now let m=2. The only factorization in (4) with t>1 is s=1,t=2. Since c and n are odd, the only unit residues a,x modulo 2 both equal 1, and
S_2(1,-c)=e_2(1-c)=1,
P_{2;c,1}(n)=(1/2)e_2(-n)=-1/2.                                      (17)
On the other hand
mu(2)(1/2-1/phi(2))=(-1)(1/2-1)=1/2.                                 (18)
Equations (17)-(18) prove (5). Fact 764588e99974a6d9 identifies the left side of (4) with K^circ_{m,c}(n), so this also proves the asserted agreement with K^circ_{2,c}=0.

It remains to prove the literal correction bound. Since phi(m)<=m for every positive integer m,
|1/m-1/phi(m)|=1/phi(m)-1/m <=1/phi(m).                              (19)
The absolute proof of GA-qPRINC in fact 764588e99974a6d9 expands the exact ray coefficients into their scaling coordinates and proves
sum_coordinates 1/phi(m_q) <=x^{o(1)}F^2.                            (20)
The same proof supplies the pointwise coefficient-product envelope
x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2
and the complete exact marked-copy count
Bx^{o(1)}.                                                            (21)
Taking absolute values in (6), using |mu(m_q)|<=1 and (19), and then applying (20)-(21) proves (7). Every listed selector can only delete terms from this absolute sum, exactly as in the predecessor proof. A union of x^{o(1)} frozen families is absorbed by the same notation. Finally Dcal<=Q^2 implies Q^2/Dcal>=1, so (7) implies (8). No estimate for the nonconstant terms in (4) has been used.

glossary.P_{t;c,s}(n): The normalized sum over unit additive frequencies modulo t defined in equation (2), where st=m.
glossary.S_t(a,b): The Kloosterman sum over unit residues x modulo t, with phase e_t(ax+b x^{-1}).

a091dd4ea1922f73.title: REVERSE NEAR-BALANCED ALL-PARENT ASSEMBLY IN THE VERY-LOW-BETA STRIP. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, sigma=kappa/100, and 0<eta<sigma. Consider the literal normalized source atoms with D>R and exact outer gcd d=ga,r=gb. Use the reverse convention of fact a71f777ad842c886: Q=R/g, B=D/g, H_T=B/Q, G=K/Q, H_P=B/K, L_src=N/g, reciprocal modulus b, and marked inverse argument a. Use L=H_TQ^sigma, S_0=H_T^2Q^{3sigma}, Z=Q^{3/2-beta-3sigma}, beta=log B/log Q
a091dd4ea1922f73.author: slava chan
a091dd4ea1922f73.statement:
REVERSE NEAR-BALANCED ALL-PARENT ASSEMBLY IN THE VERY-LOW-BETA STRIP. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, sigma=kappa/100, and 0<eta<sigma. Consider the literal normalized source atoms with D>R and exact outer gcd d=ga,r=gb. Use the reverse convention of fact a71f777ad842c886: Q=R/g, B=D/g, H_T=B/Q, G=K/Q, H_P=B/K, L_src=N/g, reciprocal modulus b, and marked inverse argument a. Use L=H_TQ^sigma, S_0=H_T^2Q^{3sigma}, Z=Q^{3/2-beta-3sigma}, beta=log B/log Q.
Assume c_1x<=DM,RK<=C_1x, c_Rx^{1/2}(log x)^{-A_R}<=R<=C_Rx^{1/2}, and all physical scales are at most Cx. Let mathcal G_rev be the exact g|N layers with Q sufficiently large, 1<=beta<=1+sigma/4, and Q^{-sigma+eta}<=G<=Q^{sigma-eta}. Let R_near^rev be the complete reverse literal nonzero-Poisson sum over mathcal G_rev, every frozen low-beta parent and every leaf C0,A,B,C1,C2,C3, retaining every source mask and amplitude; include bounded-base C0 layers.
Then |R_near^rev|<<x^{1-delta} for some delta=delta(kappa,eta)>0. For 1+sigma/4<beta<=6/5-2kappa, the same estimate holds after deleting only reverse A incidences whose exact target gcd c=gcd(b,L_src) satisfies Q^{sigma/2}<c<H_TQ^{sigma/4}. Outer-g layers outside the G strip and this medium target-gcd band are outside the assertion.
a091dd4ea1922f73.proof:
Relabel the source by (d',m',D',M')=(r,k,R,K) and (r',k',R',K')=(d,m,D,M). The equation, Mobius factors and logarithms are unchanged up to order. The fixed source weight becomes a fixed smooth coordinate permutation; a cutoff on d becomes a coefficient mask on r', the marked factor.
Apply df9748efe29ab475 to the primed variables. Its normalized variables are a'=d'/g=b and b'=r'/g=a. Thus its raw character is e_a(L_src h b^{-1}), and its Fourier coefficient has the form a^{-1}Fhat'_{g,b,a}(h/a), where F' is the relabeled compactly supported k-amplitude. Additive reciprocity gives
e_a(L_src h b^{-1})=e(L_src h/(ab))e_b(-L_src h a^{-1}).
The complete nonzero-frequency sum contains both signs. Reindex h to -h. Its summand becomes
 a^{-1}Fhat'_{g,b,a}(-h/a)e(-L_src h/(ab))e_b(L_src h a^{-1}).
This is exactly the reverse reciprocal character with fixed target +L_src. Every source mask is unchanged because the reindexing only permutes the complete positive and negative frequency set; sign dyadic labels are interchanged in pairs. After extracting the Fourier decay, the transformed amplitude remains uniformly scaled-smooth: its archimedean argument on natural frequencies has size L_srcH_P/(QB)=L_src/(QK)=N/(RK), bounded by the product hypothesis, and logarithmic derivatives have the same bound. The natural length is a/K=B/K=H_P and the Poisson prefactor is K/a=H_P^{-1}. This establishes the exact reverse source-to-trace map required by df2841924153b718.
Now apply the forward assembly proof af2d16567b876aaf to the relabeled scales. Facts d26acaefc372b4d0 and 3e326f797b2e04e4 control B,C1,C2,C3, and df2841924153b718 supplies fixed-target Type-I phase with unit one. Reverse target gcd is gcd(b,L_src); apply 1c64020b89f097c4 after interchanging (a,m) with (b,k). Facts ec9d666ae1756a03 and 5fbdbbebf99aec55 pay c<=Q^{sigma/2} and c>=H_TQ^{sigma/4}, overlapping when beta<=1+sigma/4 and leaving the stated band otherwise.
Fact a71f777ad842c886 explicitly supplies the reverse marker identity and parent scalarity. Apply 8bf5ca45f71b8c2c to the primed balance scales D'=R,M'=K to remove C0 and bounded Q. Finally Q=R/g, so summing a uniform Q^{2-delta_0} fixed-g estimate gives at most R^{2-delta_0}sum_g g^{-2+delta_0}<<x^{1-delta_0/2}. Polylogarithmic labels are absorbed by decreasing the saving.

glossary.A_R: The fixed logarithmic balance exponent in the lower bound for R.
glossary.F': The relabeled compactly supported k-variable Poisson amplitude.
glossary.R_near^rev: The complete literal reverse all-parent sum over mathcal G_rev plus bounded-base C0.
glossary.mathcal G_rev: The exact reverse outer-gcd layers in the near-balanced very-low-beta strip.

a0a35db8dccc10c0.title: VARYING-MODULUS QUADRATIC CRITICAL-GRAM SUPPLIER. Assume the hypotheses and notation of fact 3db20da48fdfac31. For each S in cal S put
a0a35db8dccc10c0.author: slava chan
a0a35db8dccc10c0.statement:
VARYING-MODULUS QUADRATIC CRITICAL-GRAM SUPPLIER. Assume the hypotheses and notation of fact 3db20da48fdfac31. For each S in cal S put
I_S=integral_{R^2}cal G_{S,bold t}(cal K_S)^{1/2}d bold t,
and define
cal Q_crit=sum_{S in cal S}(M_0/S^2)I_S^2.                         (1)
Then
|cal T_crit(cal S,{cal K_S})|<<_{chi,C_0}(log x)^{1/2}cal Q_crit^{1/2}.        (2)
Consequently, for every A>0, the varying-modulus signed Gram estimate
cal Q_crit<<(xD)^2(log x)^{-2A-1}                                (QUAD-SUPPLIER_A)
implies
|cal T_crit(cal S,{cal K_S})|<<xD(log x)^{-A}.                    (3)
The quantity in (1) contains the incomplete signed Dirichlet-kernel Gram of fact 7264046d8776d59f, not its complete Parseval majorant. Through fact 16c145000d211540 it also retains the exact two-reflected-form Perron-Euler row inside each Gram. This is a sufficient quadratic family interface and does not assert QUAD-SUPPLIER_A.
a0a35db8dccc10c0.proof:
Fact 3db20da48fdfac31 gives
|cal T_crit|<<sum_{S in cal S}M_0^{1/2}S^{-3/2}I_S.
Rewrite the summand as
M_0^{1/2}S^{-3/2}I_S=S^{-1/2}(M_0^{1/2}S^{-1}I_S).
Cauchy-Schwarz in the already aggregated total modulus S yields
|cal T_crit|<< (sum_{S in cal S}S^{-1})^{1/2}(sum_{S in cal S}M_0S^{-2}I_S^2)^{1/2}.             (4)

It remains only to bound the first factor. In the definition of F_q in fact ffa8f6d3f766b9f5, u lies in the support of W, which is contained in (0,1). Thus x(2-u)<2x. If q>=2x, then log(x(2-u)/q)_+=0 for every u, so F_q and widetilde F_q vanish. Every active q_1,q_2 is therefore less than 2x, and every active S=[q_1,q_2] is less than 4x^2. Since cal S contains positive integers,
sum_{S in cal S}S^{-1}<=sum_{1<=S<4x^2}S^{-1}<<log x.              (5)
Substitution of (5) into (4) proves (2). QUAD-SUPPLIER_A and (2) give (3). The final structural statements follow directly from the definitions of cal G in fact 3db20da48fdfac31, equation (7) of fact 7264046d8776d59f, and the row identity in fact 16c145000d211540; no replacement by complete energy occurs.

glossary.I_S: the Mellin-variable integral of the square root of the literal critical Gram at S
glossary.QUAD-SUPPLIER_A: the quadratic family estimate sufficient for target exponent A
glossary.cal Q_crit: the varying-modulus quadratic critical Gram supplier in equation (1)

a0cf2b6037398f9f.title: Fix an integer J≥1 and a smooth function w supported in [1,2], with all derivatives bounded. Let Q,V,P≥2, put B=VP, and assume
a0cf2b6037398f9f.author: slava chan
a0cf2b6037398f9f.statement:
Fix an integer J≥1 and a smooth function w supported in [1,2], with all derivatives bounded. Let Q,V,P≥2, put B=VP, and assume
B≤Q^(4/3),   B^(2/3)V^(1/3)≤Q.                                (1)
Let β_v be supported on V≤v<2V with |β_v|≤τ_J(v). Then for every ε>0,
Σ_{Q≤q<2Q} max_{gcd(a,q)=1}
 |Σ_{V≤v<2V}β_v Σ_{p prime,P≤p<2P,gcd(vp,q)=1}
   w(p/P)e_q(a(vp)^(-1))|
≪_{J,w,ε}(QVP)^ε [
 Q^(11/10)B^(4/5)
 +Q^(7/6)B^(13/18)V^(1/9)
 +QB^(7/8)
 +Q^(3/2)B^(1/3)V^(2/3)
 +B+QB^(1/2)V^(1/2)].                                      (2)
The modulus q is arbitrary, and the maximum is taken separately for each q. Fact 528c091515d833fc is the cleaner specialization obtained when Q≤P.
a0cf2b6037398f9f.proof:
Use the exact Vaughan identity and dyadic decomposition proved in fact 528c091515d833fc, with U=P^(1/3). In a Type-II block let s be the shorter Vaughan factor. Then
U≤s≤P^(1/2),                                                   (3)
and after combining v with the longer factor the two lengths are
A=B/s, C=s.                                                    (4)
They are both at most Q: the second inequality in (1) gives A≤B/U=B^(2/3)V^(1/3)≤Q, while C≤P^(1/2)≤B^(1/2)≤Q^(2/3).

Irving, arXiv:1301.6372, Lemma 3.1 applied with moments k=3 and k=2 gives, respectively,
Q^(7/6)B^(5/6)s^(-1/3)+QB^(5/6)s^(1/6),                       (5)
Q^(5/4)B^(3/4)s^(-1/4)+QB^(3/4)s^(1/4),                       (6)
up to the common epsilon factor. On the transition range s<Q^(1/3), use the decreasing first term of (5). Its maximum occurs at s=U=P^(1/3), where it equals
Q^(7/6)B^(5/6)P^(-1/9)
=Q^(7/6)B^(13/18)V^(1/9).                                    (7)
On Q^(1/3)≤s≤Q^(1/2), the increasing second term of (5) and the decreasing first term of (6) cross at
s_0=(Q³/B)^(1/5)
with common value Q^(11/10)B^(4/5). If this point lies outside the actual overlap interval, monotonicity gives no larger value at the nearest endpoint. For s>Q^(1/2), the second term of (6) is at most
QB^(3/4)P^(1/8)=QB^(7/8)V^(-1/8)≤QB^(7/8).                   (8)
This accounts for the first three terms in (2).

For Type I, the coefficient length after combining v with a factor l≤U is at most
VU=B^(1/3)V^(2/3),
and the product of the two lengths is B. Irving's Lemma 3.4, with partial summation for a logarithmic free weight, gives
B+Q^(3/2)B^(1/3)V^(2/3).                                     (9)
Finally, replacing the prime indicator by Λ introduces proper prime powers. There are O(P^(1/2)) of them in [P,2P], so their trivially averaged contribution is
≪(QVP)^ε QVP^(1/2)
=(QVP)^ε QB^(1/2)V^(1/2).                                    (10)
The fixed smooth weight and all dyadic decompositions cost logarithmic factors absorbed into (QVP)^ε. Combining (7)-(10) proves (2).

a1031b4f75b68faa.title: MAYNARD LEMMA 20.7 HAS NO DIRECT \(E_{11}\) MODULUS-FACTOR INSTANCE. Assume the forward \(E_{11}\) central-strip source hypotheses of fact fc442085ff47a053, in particular
a1031b4f75b68faa.author: slava chan
a1031b4f75b68faa.statement:
MAYNARD LEMMA 20.7 HAS NO DIRECT \(E_{11}\) MODULUS-FACTOR INSTANCE. Assume the forward \(E_{11}\) central-strip source hypotheses of fact fc442085ff47a053, in particular
\[
 D=x^{1/2+o(1)},\qquad
 4/3\le\beta_E\le4/3+6\eta_t,qquad
 0<\eta_t<1/120,
\]
and
\[
 r=p\ell,qquad
 p,\ell\ge D^{,2-\beta_E-3\eta_t}.
\]
Let \(P_1,P_2\) be dyadic scales containing \(p,\ell\), in either order. Then
\[
 P_1,P_2\ge x^{,1/3-(9/2)\eta_t+o(1)}.                  \tag{1}
\]

Maynard, arXiv:2006.06572v2, Lemma 20.7, takes parameters \(X,M_0,N_1,N_2,N_3,Q_1,Q_2\) with
\[
 X^{2\epsilon}\le N_1\le N_2\le N_3,quad
 X^\epsilon\le M_0,quad
 N_1N_2N_3M_0\asymp X,quad Q_1Q_2\le X^{1-\epsilon},
\]
and requires
\[
 \frac{M_0Q_1^{5/2}Q_2^3}{X^{1-15\epsilon}}
 \le N_3\le
 \frac{X^{2-15\epsilon}}{Q_1^3Q_2^2M_0}.                 \tag{2}
\]
Under these hypotheses it bounds, with arbitrary one-bounded \(M_0\)-slot coefficients, the average over \(q_1\asymp Q_1,q_2\asymp Q_2\) of the absolute discrepancy for the congruence
\[
 m n_1n_2n_3\equiv a\pmod {q_1q_2},
\]
where each \(n_j\) lies in a prescribed interval and their product has the displayed roughness restriction.

There is no choice of the remaining Lemma 20.7 parameters for which (2) holds after the direct literal modulus-factor identification
\[
 X=x,qquad (Q_1,Q_2)=(P_1,P_2)
\]
or its swap. Therefore Lemma 20.7 cannot be directly applied to the critical primitive \(E_{11}\) trace by merely putting its two canonical prime modulus factors into Maynard's \((q_1,q_2)\) slots. Lemma 20.4 of the same paper is the reduction step inside this incompatible parameter architecture and does not remove the size failure. This is a scoped no-direct-fit only. It does not rule out a different decomposition of the source, a different assignment of modulus factors, another theorem from the paper, or a new amplified estimate for the literal trace.
a1031b4f75b68faa.proof:
From the central-strip lower bound and \(\beta_E\le4/3+6\eta_t\),
\[
 p,\ell\ge D^{,2-(4/3+6\eta_t)-3\eta_t}
 =D^{,2/3-9\eta_t}.
\]
Since \(D=x^{1/2+o(1)}\), every dyadic scale containing either prime satisfies (1).

A necessary condition for the two inequalities in (2) to have any common value of \(N_3\) is that their lower endpoint not exceed their upper endpoint. Multiplying by the positive denominators gives the exact necessary condition
\[
 M_0^2Q_1^{11/2}Q_2^5\le X^{3-30\epsilon}.               \tag{3}
\]
Since \(X\ge1\), this implies the weaker necessary condition
\[
 M_0^2Q_1^{11/2}Q_2^5\le X^3.                             \tag{4}
\]
Under the direct identification \(X=x\), \((Q_1,Q_2)=(P_1,P_2)\), and using \(M_0\ge x^\epsilon\ge1\), equation (1) gives
\[
 M_0^2Q_1^{11/2}Q_2^5
 \ge x^{(21/2)(1/3-(9/2)\eta_t)+o(1)}
 =x^{,7/2-(189/4)\eta_t+o(1)}.                            \tag{5}
\]
Because \(\eta_t<1/120\),
\[
 7/2-(189/4)\eta_t
 >7/2-189/480
 =3+17/160.                                                 \tag{6}
\]
For sufficiently large \(x\), (5)-(6) contradict even the weaker necessary condition (4), and therefore also contradict the exact condition (3). The same calculation holds after swapping \(Q_1,Q_2\), since both scales obey the same lower bound (1).

The quoted Lemma 20.7 conclusion is conditional on all its displayed parameter hypotheses, so failure of the necessary overlap condition prevents this direct application before any coefficient or roughness matching is considered. In Maynard's proof, Lemma 20.4 reduces that same discrepancy architecture to an exponential sum which is subsequently estimated and assembled into Lemma 20.7; it is not an independent conclusion that bypasses (2). Hence the stated literal slot map is unavailable, while every alternative listed in the final scope sentence remains logically open.

glossary.M_0: Maynard's coefficient-bearing convolution scale, renamed to avoid collision with the source scale M.
glossary.N_3: Maynard's third and largest interval-variable scale.
glossary.P_1: A dyadic scale of one canonical E11 prime factor.
glossary.P_2: A dyadic scale of the other canonical E11 prime factor.
glossary.X: The main size parameter in Maynard's Lemma 20.7.
glossary.n_1: The first interval variable in Maynard's discrepancy.
glossary.n_2: The second interval variable in Maynard's discrepancy.
glossary.n_3: The third interval variable in Maynard's discrepancy.
glossary.q_1: The first modulus variable in Maynard's discrepancy average.
glossary.q_2: The second modulus variable in Maynard's discrepancy average.

a170364aba04897b.title: Let m>1 be odd, let s belong to {1,-1}, let K be an integer coprime to m, let G be the unit group modulo m^2, and put n=phi(m^2). Let W be a complex-valued function modulo m. For multiplicative characters chi,psi of G define
a170364aba04897b.author: slava chan
a170364aba04897b.statement:
Let m>1 be odd, let s belong to {1,-1}, let K be an integer coprime to m, let G be the unit group modulo m^2, and put n=phi(m^2). Let W be a complex-valued function modulo m. For multiplicative characters chi,psi of G define
S(chi,psi)=sum_{u modulo m} W(u) conjugate(chi(K+2smu)psi(K-2smu)).                 (1)
Extend every character to the positive integers by zero outside the integers coprime to m. Let S_1,S_2 be finite positive-integer intervals, let Delta be a nonzero integer, and let f,g be smooth compactly supported functions on the positive reals. Define
Z_{chi,psi}=sum_{n_1 in S_1,n_2 in S_2; gcd(n_1,n_2) divides Delta}
 [gcd(n_1,n_2)/(n_1n_2)] psi(n_1)chi(n_2)
 integral_R f((x+Delta)/n_2)g(x/n_1) dx,                              (2)
and define the sign-adjusted complete character assembly of these formal Bettin--Chandee column main terms by
Z_W^{ass}=n^(-2)sum_{chi,psi} S(chi,psi)psi(-1)Z_{chi,psi}.            (3)
Then the exact identity
Z_W^{ass}
=sum_{n_1 in S_1,n_2 in S_2; gcd(n_1,n_2) divides Delta}
 [gcd(n_1,n_2)/(n_1n_2)]
 integral_R f((x+Delta)/n_2)g(x/n_1) dx
 times sum_{u modulo m}W(u)
 Delta_{m^2}(n_2-K-2smu) Delta_{m^2}(-n_1-K+2smu)                    (4)
holds.

In particular, complete character orthogonality does not force the assembled formal column main term of a centered nonzero digit mode to vanish before any outer summation. More precisely, let m>=7 be odd, set K=s=Delta=1, X=m+1, S_1=S_2=[X,2X] intersect Z, and fix a nonzero residue ell modulo m. Put W_ell(u)=e_m(ell u), which has mean zero. There exist nonnegative infinitely differentiable f and g, each compactly supported inside (X,2X) and satisfying the scaled Bettin--Chandee profile hypotheses for a finite derivative parameter, such that
Z_{W_ell}^{ass} is nonzero.                                           (5)
Thus summing every character pair in the exact digit expansion still does not give a formal column-main-term orthogonality cancellation. This remains a column-functional identity, not a direct Bettin--Chandee application: fact a695dcaf05aaa83d shows that the same character atoms retain multiplicative characters in the two smooth row slots. Formula (5) does not exclude cancellation after restoring a valid twisted-row theorem, the actual row-character main term, the outer variables m,r_2,r_3, or the remaining literal selectors.
a170364aba04897b.proof:
Fact 8230d44e6677f45b gives (1) as the coefficient of the character atom chi(a)chi(b)psi(c)psi(d) in the exact shared-digit expansion, with the common factor n^(-2). In the sign sector d<0, writing n_1=-d contributes the constant sign factor psi(-1), which explains (3). Fact 0aa36f583d53cb82 identifies (2) as the explicit Bettin--Chandee column main-term functional for the column sequences alpha(n_1)=psi(n_1), beta(n_2)=chi(n_2).

Insert (1) and (2) into (3) and interchange the finite sums. For fixed u,n_1,n_2, the character-dependent factor splits as
[n^(-1)sum_chi chi(n_2)conjugate(chi(K+2smu))]
times
[n^(-1)sum_psi psi(-n_1)conjugate(psi(K-2smu))].                     (6)
Both K+2smu and K-2smu are units modulo m^2 because they are congruent to K modulo m. Multiplicative-character orthogonality on G says that the first bracket in (6) is
Delta_{m^2}(n_2-K-2smu),
and the second is
Delta_{m^2}(-n_1-K+2smu).                                            (7)
If n_1 or n_2 is not a unit, its extended character values vanish and the corresponding delta in (7) also vanishes because its comparison target is a unit. Thus (7) is valid for every positive n_1,n_2 in the intervals. Substitution of (7) proves (4).

It remains to prove the nonvanishing assertion. Put
n_1^*=2m-1,  n_2^*=2m+1,  u^*=1.                                    (8)
Because X=m+1 and m>=7, both n_1^* and n_2^* lie in [X,2X]. Moreover
gcd(n_1^*,n_2^*)=gcd(2m-1,2)=1,                                     (9)
and the two exact equalities
n_2^*=1+2mu^*,   -n_1^*=1-2mu^*                                     (10)
show that the two deltas in (4) equal one at this triple. Since m is odd, multiplication by 2 is invertible modulo m, so for this fixed column pair the simultaneous congruences in (4) determine u=u^*=1 modulo m.

We now choose f and g so that no other coprime column pair contributes. For every coprime pair (n_1,n_2) in S_1 times S_2 define
L_{n_1,n_2}(t)=(n_1t+1)/n_2.                                        (11)
If L_{n_1,n_2} is identical to L_{n_1^*,n_2^*}, comparison of constant terms gives n_2=n_2^*, and comparison of slopes then gives n_1=n_1^*. Hence, for every other coprime pair, the equation
L_{n_1,n_2}(t)=L_{n_1^*,n_2^*}(t)                                   (12)
has at most one real solution. There are finitely many pairs. Choose
t_0 in (4X/3,3X/2)                                                    (13)
outside all the finitely many solution sets in (12), and put
q_0=L_{n_1^*,n_2^*}(t_0).                                            (14)
The lower endpoint in (13) and m>=7 give
q_0>((2m-1)(4X/3))/(2m+1)>X,
because 4(2m-1)>3(2m+1). The upper endpoint gives
q_0<3X/2<2X.                                                         (15)
By (12)-(15), continuity and finiteness provide open intervals J_g and J_f containing t_0 and q_0 respectively, with closures contained in (X,2X), such that
t in J_g and L_{n_1,n_2}(t) in J_f
for a coprime pair in S_1 times S_2 imply
(n_1,n_2)=(n_1^*,n_2^*).                                             (16)
Choose nonzero nonnegative infinitely differentiable functions g and f supported in J_g and J_f and positive at t_0 and q_0. Since their supports are compact subsets of (X,2X), after scaling by 2X they satisfy the fixed-profile support and derivative conditions in fact b1398db2962d7491 for some finite derivative parameter.

If the integral in (4) for a coprime pair is nonzero, then for some real x one has x/n_1 in J_g and (x+1)/n_2 in J_f. Taking t=x/n_1 and using (11) and (16) forces the target pair (n_1^*,n_2^*). Conversely, the target integral is strictly positive on a neighborhood of x=n_1^*t_0. Therefore (4), (9), and (10) reduce to
Z_{W_ell}^{ass}
= [W_ell(1)/(n_1^*n_2^*)]
 integral_R f((x+1)/n_2^*)g(x/n_1^*) dx.                              (17)
The integral is positive and W_ell(1)=e_m(ell) is nonzero, so (17) is nonzero. Finally, additive orthogonality gives sum_{u modulo m}W_ell(u)=0 because ell is nonzero, proving that the example is a centered nonzero digit mode. The scope limitations follow from fact a695dcaf05aaa83d: the existing theorem has no legal row slots for these full character atoms, so (3)-(5) are an exact audit of the formal column functional only.

glossary.Z_W^{ass}: the sign-adjusted complete character assembly of the formal Bettin--Chandee column main terms associated with a shared normal-digit weight W

a1b0c0ad5a923524.title: HEIGHT-FACTOR INVARIANCE OF THE LITERAL CRITICAL-CLUSTER RATIO AND THE mu(q)nu_h OBSTRUCTION
a1b0c0ad5a923524.author: slava chan
a1b0c0ad5a923524.statement:
HEIGHT-FACTOR INVARIANCE OF THE LITERAL CRITICAL-CLUSTER RATIO AND THE mu(q)nu_h OBSTRUCTION.

Use the source rows, critical-cluster partitions, and notation of fact 3b2d15db39ad0217. Suppose the coefficient factors as
  a_{o,h}(x)=nu_{o,h} b_{o,h}(x),                           (1)
where nu_{o,h} is a complex scalar independent of x. For every outer row o and height h put
  E_base(o,h)
   =sum_j |sum_{x in cal X_{o,j}}
                  b_{o,h}(x)e(h lambda_x)|^2,              (2)
  W_base(o,h)
   =sum_j (sum_{x in cal X_{o,j}}|b_{o,h}(x)|)^2.          (3)
Then exactly
  E_cl=sum_{o,h}|nu_{o,h}|^2 E_base(o,h),
  W_cl=sum_{o,h}|nu_{o,h}|^2 W_base(o,h).                  (4)
When W_cl>0,
  Theta_cl
   =[sum_{o,h}|nu_{o,h}|^2W_base(o,h) theta_{o,h}]
     /[sum_{o,h}|nu_{o,h}|^2W_base(o,h)],                  (5)
where theta_{o,h}=E_base(o,h)/W_base(o,h) if W_base(o,h)>0 and theta_{o,h}=0 otherwise. Thus Theta_cl is an exact nonnegative weighted average of the nonempty fixed-height base ratios. In particular, the phase or sign of the common height coefficient nu_{o,h} cannot itself produce cancellation among source atoms at a fixed height.

For the literal coefficient in fact 3b2d15db39ad0217,
  a_{o,h}(x)
   =c_q nu_h U_ell(q,h,v,p)chi_ell(v,p,h,q),               (6)
one may take
  b_{o,h}(x)=c_q U_ell(q,h,v,p)chi_ell(v,p,h,q).           (7)
Hence the literal factor nu_h has exactly the role described by (4)-(5).

There is a sharp source-specific limitation. On the prime-q actual-source cluster cal Y of fact 38bc0e88e17aef0e, take
  b_h(x)=mu(q)=-1                                          (8)
for every x in cal Y, and let nu_h be any complex height profile, not identically zero, on a nonempty interval I contained either in [H,2H) or in (-2H,-H]. Then
  Theta_cl>=1/2,                                           (9)
while that family has
  Gadd>>Q^(1/12).                                          (10)
Consequently the exact upstream Möbius factor mu(q), even together with an arbitrary common literal height factor nu_h, does not imply
  Theta_cl<<Gadd^(-1)Q^epsilon                             (11)
for every epsilon>0.

This result does not identify (8) with the full literal factor c_qU_ell chi_ell and does not assert that a natural project mask selects cal Y. It isolates the remaining local coefficient burden in the source-dependent factor U_ell chi_ell (including its support), or in cancellation from an earlier complete signed assembly. It gives no global Aadd lower bound, no PMD closure, and no Goldbach conclusion.
a1b0c0ad5a923524.proof:
For fixed o,h,j, insert (1) into the cluster sum:
  Z_{o,h,j}
   =nu_{o,h} sum_{x in cal X_{o,j}}
                   b_{o,h}(x)e(h lambda_x).                (12)
Taking squared absolute values and summing j proves the fixed-o,h contribution
  sum_j|Z_{o,h,j}|^2
   =|nu_{o,h}|^2E_base(o,h).                               (13)
Likewise
  sum_j (sum_{x in cal X_{o,j}}|a_{o,h}(x)|)^2
   =|nu_{o,h}|^2W_base(o,h).                               (14)
Summing (13)-(14) over o,h proves (4).

If W_base(o,h)=0, then every b_{o,h}(x) is zero, so E_base(o,h)=0 as well. For every remaining o,h, write
  E_base(o,h)=W_base(o,h)theta_{o,h}.
Substitution in (4) and division by W_cl proves (5). All weights in (5) are nonnegative. The argument uses only |nu_{o,h}|^2, proving the phase-invariance assertion.

Equation (6) is the exact literal identification in fact 3b2d15db39ad0217. Since nu_h is independent of the source atom x within fixed ell,v,p,h, equations (1) and (7) follow without changing any mask or phase.

Now use the source cluster cal Y from fact 38bc0e88e17aef0e. Its reciprocal moduli q are prime, so mu(q)=-1. Its slopes are pairwise distinct and lie in an interval of length at most 1/(12H). For every h with nu_h nonzero, the base coefficient (8) is constant. Multiplication by -1 leaves every Gram product unchanged. The coherent-cluster estimate in fact 714f3597f5ef527c, applied with a one-height interval when necessary or directly term by term from its cosine estimate, gives
  |sum_{x in cal Y}-e(h lambda_x)|^2
   >=Y+(1/2)Y(Y-1)
   =(1/2)Y(Y+1).                                           (15)
At that height,
  W_base(h)=Y^2,
so theta_h>=(Y+1)/(2Y)>=1/2. Formula (5) now gives (9) for every nonzero profile nu_h. Fact 38bc0e88e17aef0e gives (10). Choosing epsilon<1/12 shows that (11) cannot follow uniformly from these factors, exactly as in that fact. The scope paragraph follows because neither U_ell nor chi_ell has been identified with (8), and no sum over different clusters or outer rows has been lower-bounded.

glossary.E_base(o,h): The sum of squared cluster sums at fixed outer row and height after removing a common height scalar.
glossary.W_base(o,h): The sum of squared cluster l1 masses at fixed outer row and height after removing a common height scalar.

a1bbb2eea5df6260.title: ROW-COLUMN COHERENCE OF ODD K-NONUNIT PRIME POWERS
a1bbb2eea5df6260.author: slava chan
a1bbb2eea5df6260.statement:
ROW-COLUMN COHERENCE OF ODD K-NONUNIT PRIME POWERS.

Let
 (a,b,c,d,r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4,u,v)
be a normalized unit state of type (I) in fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb. Put
 A=b r_3-d r_2,quad B=a r_2-c r_3,quad
 q=gcd(|A|,|B|),quad m=q/2=|v|.                                  (1)
Let p be an odd prime dividing m and assume p does not divide r_2r_3. Put
 e_p=v_p(m)>=1. Then
 min(v_p(a),e_p)=min(v_p(c),e_p),qquad
 min(v_p(b),e_p)=min(v_p(d),e_p).                                 (2)

The exact normalized product identities imply
 ab is congruent to cd and to K modulo p^(e_p).                     (3)
If t_p=v_p(K)<e_p, then there are unique nonnegative integers x,y with
 x+y=t_p,qquad
 v_p(a)=v_p(c)=x,quad v_p(b)=v_p(d)=y.                            (4)
If v_p(K)>=e_p, then
 min(v_p(a),e_p)+min(v_p(b),e_p)>=e_p,                             (5)
and the same inequality for c,d is identical by (2).

In particular, if p divides gcd(m,K) and p does not divide r_2r_3, then modulo p every normalized state has one of exactly three coherent divisibility patterns:
 R: p divides a,c but not b,d;
 C: p divides b,d but not a,c;
 RC: p divides all four a,b,c,d.                                  (6)
There is no crossed pattern such as p dividing a,d but not b,c.

Thus odd nonunit conductor primes away from the base corners attach to an entire row pair (a,c), an entire column pair (b,d), or both. This is a structural input for a possible conductor-lowering decomposition; it does not itself prove that quotienting such factors preserves normalized prime quotients, the carrier C, or the one-column Kloosterman modulus.
a1bbb2eea5df6260.proof:
Since p^(e_p) divides m and q=2m, the odd prime power p^(e_p) divides q. Hence it divides both A and B. Because r_2 and r_3 are units modulo p^(e_p), the congruences
 b r_3 congruent to d r_2,qquad
 a r_2 congruent to c r_3                                      (7)
modulo p^(e_p) show that b is congruent to a unit multiple of d and a is congruent to a unit multiple of c modulo p^(e_p).

We use the elementary consequence: if integers X,Y satisfy X congruent to wY modulo p^e with p not dividing w, then
 min(v_p(X),e)=min(v_p(Y),e).
Indeed, if one valuation is below e and strictly smaller than the other, the difference X-wY has that smaller valuation and cannot be divisible by p^e; if both valuations are at least e their truncations are both e. Applying this observation to (7) proves (2).

Fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb gives
 ab=K+2uv,qquad cd=K-2uv.
Since v has absolute value m, p^(e_p) divides v. Therefore both correction terms 2uv are divisible by p^(e_p), proving (3).

Suppose t_p=v_p(K)<e_p. Any integer congruent to K modulo p^(e_p) has p-adic valuation exactly t_p: subtracting K changes it by a number of strictly larger valuation. Thus (3) gives
 v_p(a)+v_p(b)=t_p,qquad v_p(c)+v_p(d)=t_p.                       (8)
All four valuations in (8) are below e_p. The truncations in (2) are therefore the valuations themselves. Put x=v_p(a)=v_p(c) and y=v_p(b)=v_p(d). Equation (8) gives x+y=t_p and proves (4), including uniqueness.

If v_p(K)>=e_p, (3) says p^(e_p) divides ab and cd. For nonnegative valuations this is equivalent to
 v_p(a)+v_p(b)>=e_p,qquad v_p(c)+v_p(d)>=e_p.
Replacing either valuation larger than e_p by e_p does not change either inequality. Together with (2) this proves (5).

Finally assume p divides K. From (3), p divides ab and cd. Modulo p, (2) says p divides a exactly when it divides c, and p divides b exactly when it divides d. At least one of the two coherent pairs must be divisible because p divides ab. The possibilities are therefore precisely R,C,RC, and they are disjoint. This proves (6) and excludes crossed patterns. The last sentence is a scope statement: no quotient construction was made.

glossary.e_p: the exponent v_p(m) of an odd prime p in the half-conductor
glossary.v_p: the p-adic valuation on nonzero integers

a21645b0ae152b3f.title: STRICT-TOP q-TYPE-I AGGREGATE PAYMENT BEFORE n-AXIS ABSOLUTE VALUES. Fix one complete-provenance strict-top unmarked source row in the additive-reciprocity normal form of fact ecd6325d7ef2bc37. Thus
a21645b0ae152b3f.author: slava chan
a21645b0ae152b3f.statement:
STRICT-TOP q-TYPE-I AGGREGATE PAYMENT BEFORE n-AXIS ABSOLUTE VALUES. Fix one complete-provenance strict-top unmarked source row in the additive-reciprocity normal form of fact ecd6325d7ef2bc37. Thus
\[
 \beta_m<\beta<6/5,\qquad B=Q^\beta,\qquad
 (g,qn)=(q,n)=1,\qquad L_{\rm src}=N/g,
\]
and, on one signed dyadic frequency block \(F\le |h|<2F\), put
\[
 \Phi_F(q,n)={1\over H_P}\sum_{F\le |h|<2F}
 {\cal C}^{\flat}_{g,q,n}(h)
 e_n(\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\overline q),                    \tag{1}
\]
extended by zero away from the literal dyadic source support and gcd gates. Here \({\cal C}^{\flat}\) is the literal complete-provenance coefficient of that fact, before any projective expansion.

Choose an integer cutoff
\[
 {1\over2}Q^{1/12}\le V_q\le Q^{1/12}                       \tag{2}
\]
for sufficiently large \(Q\), and apply the exact q-axis Vaughan operator \({\cal I}_{q,V_q}\) of fact a75ea6a8a40dd1f8. Define the whole q-Type-I aggregate, with the n-Möbius sign still present, by
\[
 {\cal T}_{I_q,F}
 =-\sum_{n\asymp B}\mu(n)\,({\cal I}_{q,V_q}\Phi_F)(n).
                                                                    \tag{3}
\]
By the exact n-axis identity in that fact, (3) is precisely
\[
 {\cal I}_{q,V_q}({\cal I}_{n,V_n}+{\cal J}_{n,V_n})\Phi_F
\]
for every legal \(V_n\); in particular it is the sum of the \(I_qI_n\) and \(I_qJ_n\) terms before either is estimated separately.

For every fixed \(A>0\), uniformly in all literal outer labels and in \(F\),
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 |{\cal T}_{I_q,F}|
 \ll_A Q^{o(1)}V_q^2B^{3/2}
 {F\over H_P}(1+F/H_P)^{-A}.
 \quad}                                                        \tag{4}
\]
Consequently the complete signed dyadic-frequency sum and its standard \(x^{o(1)}\) source/projective reconstruction satisfy
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \sum_F|{\cal T}_{I_q,F}|
 \ll Q^{1/6}B^{3/2}Q^{o(1)}
 \ll Q^{2-1/100}.
 \quad}                                                        \tag{5}
\]
The last bound is uniform throughout \(\beta_m<\beta<6/5\) for sufficiently large \(Q\). Thus the whole q-Type-I side
\[
 I_qI_n+I_qJ_n
\]
of DOUBLE-VAUGHAN-QN is paid with a fixed power saving without estimating the two n-axis children separately. The complementary q-Type-II aggregate retains both long signs: the \(\mu(m)\) created by \({\cal J}_{q,V_q}\) and the original \(\mu(n)\). No estimate for \(J_qI_n+J_qJ_n\), no critical \(\beta\ge6/5\) payment, and no post-A or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
a21645b0ae152b3f.proof:
Fact a75ea6a8a40dd1f8 gives
\[
 ({\cal I}_{q,V_q}\Phi_F)(n)
 =\sum_{d\le V_q^2}a_{V_q}(d)
   \sum_{Q_0/d<m\le Q_1/d}\Phi_F(dm,n),                     \tag{6}
\]
where \(|a_{V_q}(d)|\le2\tau(d)\). We first record the literal coefficient regularity needed to estimate the m-sum. Equation (8) and derivative estimate (10) in fact 062a7f6f0c58b1f2 apply after the complete provenance recombination of fact 544c7ba4db45c06f. Before the Archimedean reciprocity factor is inserted they show directly that, in normalized variables
\[
 x_1=q/Q,\qquad y_1=n/B,\qquad z_1=h/F,
\]
the function \({\cal C}^{\flat}_{g,q,n}(h)\) and every fixed x_1-derivative are
\[
 O_A\bigl((\log x)^C(1+F/H_P)^{-A}\bigr)                    \tag{7}
\]
for a fixed \(C\), uniformly on a fixed compact box. Indeed, in either orientation the literal coefficient before the Archimedean phase is
\[
 {1\over y_1}\int {\cal W}_\epsilon(x_1,y_1,\tau_1)
 e\!\left(-{F\over H_P}{z_1\tau_1\over y_1}\right)d\tau_1,
                                                                    \tag{8}
\]
and integration by parts in \(\tau_1\), exactly as in that predecessor, gives arbitrary-order decay while x_1-differentiation only differentiates a fixed-box smooth amplitude.

Fix \(d,n,h\). Restrict \(m\) by \(dm\) lying in the literal q-box, and extend the resulting m-weight by zero. The mean-value theorem on the disjoint intervals from \(dm\) to \(d(m+1)\), together with (7), gives
\[
 \sup_m|{\cal C}^{\flat}_{g,dm,n}(h)|
 +\sum_m|{\cal C}^{\flat}_{g,d(m+1),n}(h)
              -{\cal C}^{\flat}_{g,dm,n}(h)|
 \ll_A(\log x)^C(1+F/H_P)^{-A}.                              \tag{9}
\]
The two endpoint jumps caused by zero extension obey the same bound.

A row in (6) is zero unless \((d,gn)=1\) and \((n,g)=1\). On a nonzero row the remaining arithmetic conditions on m are
\[
 (m,n)=1,\qquad(m,g)=1,                                      \tag{10}
\]
and the phase is
\[
 e_n(\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\,\overline d\,\overline m).       \tag{11}
\]
Apply Abel summation using (9), before expanding the second condition in (10). Then expand
\[
 {\bf1}_{(m,g)=1}=\sum_{\substack{c\mid g\\c\mid m}}\mu(c).
\]
Every term with \((c,n)>1\) is empty; otherwise \(m=cr\) turns \(c\) into a unit multiplier in (11). The incomplete reciprocal-sum estimate reproduced in fact 8138369f26f88aad (Irving, arXiv:1301.6372, Lemma 2.1) therefore yields
\[
 \sum_{\substack{m\ {\rm in\ the\ row}\\(m,n)=(m,g)=1}}
 {\cal C}^{\flat}_{g,dm,n}(h)
 e_n(\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\overline{dm})
 \ll_A(\log x)^C(1+F/H_P)^{-A}\tau(g)n^\varepsilon
 \left((L_{\rm src}h,n)\left({Q\over dn}+1\right)+n^{1/2}\right).
                                                                    \tag{12}
\]
No unit condition on \(L_{\rm src}h\) is used. Because \(n\asymp B=Q^\beta\), \(\beta>1\), and \(d\ge1\), the ratio \(Q/(dn)\) is less than a fixed constant for large \(Q\). Hence the last parentheses are
\[
 \ll (L_{\rm src}h,n)+n^{1/2}.                               \tag{13}
\]

We now sum n absolutely only after the complete q-Type-I row has received (12). For every nonzero integer \(a\),
\[
 \sum_{B_0<n\le B_1}(a,n)
 \le\sum_{\substack{r\mid a\\r\le B_1}}
 r\left({B_1-B_0\over r}+1\right)
 \ll B\tau(|a|),                                             \tag{14}
\]
because \(B_0\asymp B_1\asymp B\), while
\[
 \sum_{n\asymp B}n^{1/2}\ll B^{3/2}.                         \tag{15}
\]
Thus (12)-(15), with \(a=L_{\rm src}h\), give a total n-cost
\[
 \ll B^{3/2}Q^{o(1)}                                        \tag{16}
\]
uniformly after the divisor factors are included. The polynomial-size assertions needed here follow from the strict-top physical bounds and forced-high consequence \(Q\ge x^c\) in facts 15425579cb248eff and 3f2f255ea6845a50: \(g,L_{\rm src},H_P\) are bounded by fixed powers of \(Q\). The standard bounds for \(\tau(g)\) and \(\tau(|L_{\rm src}h|)\) may therefore be absorbed into \(Q^{o(1)}F^\varepsilon\); the arbitrary-order factor in (9) absorbs \(F^\varepsilon\) over the whole dyadic frequency ledger.

Finally,
\[
 \sum_{d\le V_q^2}|a_{V_q}(d)|
 \le2\sum_{d\le V_q^2}\tau(d)
 \ll V_q^2Q^{o(1)}.                                         \tag{17}
\]
There are \(O(F)\) integers in one signed h-block. Dividing by \(H_P\), and combining (9), (16), and (17), proves (4). For \(A>3\),
\[
 \sum_{F=2^j,\ j\ge0}{F\over H_P}(1+F/H_P)^{-A}\ll_A1,       \tag{18}
\]
including \(H_P<1\). Facts ecd6325d7ef2bc37 and 544c7ba4db45c06f give only \(x^{o(1)}=Q^{o(1)}\) further cost over the complete source reconstruction.

By (2),
\[
 V_q^2B^{3/2}\le Q^{1/6+3\beta/2}.
\]
Since \(\beta<6/5\),
\[
 {1\over6}+{3\beta\over2}
 <{1\over6}+{9\over5}
 ={59\over30}=2-{1\over30}.                                 \tag{19}
\]
The uniform \(Q^{o(1)}\) factor is at most \(Q^{7/300}\) for sufficiently large \(Q\), so (19) is at most \(Q^{2-1/100}\). This proves (5).

It remains only to identify the ledger. The one-axis identity in fact a75ea6a8a40dd1f8 says
\[
 \sum_n\mu(n)f(n)=-({\cal I}_{n,V_n}+{\cal J}_{n,V_n})f.
\]
Therefore the minus sign in (3) gives exactly
\({\cal I}_{q,V_q}({\cal I}_{n,V_n}+{\cal J}_{n,V_n})\Phi_F\).
The q-Type-II complement contains the literal \(\mu(m)\), while the n-axis has not yet been decomposed and still contains \(\mu(n)\). This proves all retention and scope assertions.

glossary.mathcal T_{I_q,F}: The complete signed-frequency-block q-Type-I aggregate before the n-axis Vaughan children are estimated separately.
glossary.q-Type-I aggregate: The sum I_q I_n + I_q J_n in DOUBLE-VAUGHAN-QN, equivalently minus the original n-Mobius sum of the q-Type-I operator.

a24910f2fc49b330.title: COMPLETE LARGE-OUTER-GCD SYMMETRIC FEJER PAYMENT FOR THE LITERAL ACTUAL-Z_MID PACKET
a24910f2fc49b330.author: slava chan
a24910f2fc49b330.statement:
COMPLETE LARGE-OUTER-GCD SYMMETRIC FEJER PAYMENT FOR THE LITERAL ACTUAL-Z_MID PACKET.

Assume the selected forced-high forward literal source setting of facts 60b26a9b6f79467a, 77d7a3419a07305c, 7131a06664967733, 152484e836f90c47 and af06640e8d8e4102. Thus N=2x is fixed, the selected divisor scale satisfies D<=2x^(1/2), every active source label satisfies DM asymp x and RK asymp x, and an exact outer-gcd layer has
d=ga, r=gb, (a,b)=1, L=N/g,
with a asymp D/g and b asymp R/g. Restrict every source incidence to the actual cell Z_mid, equivalently to
ell_{g,a,b}<m<u_{g,a,b}
with the strict endpoints of fact 152484e836f90c47.

Let R_mid^{ne0}(G) denote the complete literal nonzero-Poisson contribution of all these actual-Z_mid incidences with g>=G, where G>=1, reconstructed by the first Cesaro limit of the symmetric frequency sum. The word complete means that h and -h and all nonzero frequency blocks are recombined before the estimate. Every original real source coefficient is retained: the two Moebius factors, logarithms, smooth and dyadic weights, the fixed-U and high masks, and the frozen parent, tag, anatomy, marker and provenance coefficients. Exact internal A- and B-marker copies may be displayed separately. No frequency-dependent proper deletion is permitted inside R_mid^{ne0}(G).

Then
|R_mid^{ne0}(G)| << x^(o(1)) D R_max G^(-2),                 (1)
where R_max is the largest actual-Z_mid dyadic r-scale occurring in the selected packet. In particular, fact af06640e8d8e4102 gives R_max<<x^(2/3), and therefore
|R_mid^{ne0}(G)| << x^(7/6+o(1))G^(-2).                       (2)
For every fixed eta>0, taking
G=x^(1/12+eta)
gives
|R_mid^{ne0}(x^(1/12+eta))|=O_eta(x^(1-eta))=o(x/log x).      (3)

The symmetric pairing is literal in every representation from fact 152484e836f90c47. Before pairing, every retained coefficient and mask is real and independent of the sign of h. Consequently C^{mid}_{g,a,b,-h}=conjugate(C^{mid}_{g,a,b,h}). In the integration-by-parts representation, the potentially nonzero upper face and the derivative-integral term separately obey the same conjugacy, while the lower face is zero. For every admissible Delta, the smooth-interior transform of F_{g,a,b}I_Delta and the exact boundary-strip transform of F_{g,a,b}R_Delta separately obey it as well. Each paired contribution is therefore twice a real part.

Moreover, uniformly in Delta, the complete paired nonzero Cesaro contribution of each one of the full hard amplitude, the upper face, the derivative integral, the smooth interior, and the hard boundary strips is O((log x)^2) for each fixed admissible (g,a,b). The estimate (1) may thus be made either before or after the exact upper-plus-derivative or smooth-interior-plus-boundary-strip decomposition. This does not estimate a proper |h|-range, a frequency-conductor cell, or any other h-dependent deletion, and it asserts no small-g estimate, endpoint capture, C3 conclusion, or Goldbach conclusion.
a24910f2fc49b330.proof:
Put
kappa_H(h)=(1-|h|/(H+1))_+
and let
K_H(theta)=sum_{h=1}^H kappa_H(h) sin(2 pi h theta)/h.
If
F_H(theta)=sum_{|h|<=H}kappa_H(h)e(h theta)
is the Fejer kernel, then
K_H'(theta)=pi(F_H(theta)-1).
The Fejer kernel is nonnegative, one-periodic, and has integral one on [0,1]. Choosing theta modulo one in [0,1] and using K_H(0)=0 gives
|K_H(theta)|
 <=pi integral_0^theta(F_H(t)+1)dt
 <=2pi.                                                       (4)
This is uniform in H and theta.

We record the bounded-variation consequence of (4). Let A be a real compactly supported function of bounded variation, let b be a positive integer, and let c be real. For h nonzero, Stieltjes integration by parts gives
b^(-1)e(hc/b) integral_R A(t)e(-ht/b)dt
 =1/(2 pi i h) integral_R e(h(c-t)/b)dA(t).                  (5)
There is no boundary term because A is compactly supported. Pairing h with -h, inserting kappa_H(h), interchanging the finite h-sum with the finite signed measure dA, and applying (4) shows
|sum_{0<|h|<=H} kappa_H(h)b^(-1)e(hc/b) Ahat(h/b)|
 << Var(A),                                                   (6)
uniformly in H,b,c. Here Ahat is the Fourier transform with the convention of fact 152484e836f90c47. Since A is real, the -h summand in (6) is the complex conjugate of the h summand.

Apply (6) first to
A(t)=F_{g,a,b}(t)1_{ell_{g,a,b}<t<u_{g,a,b}}.
Fact 152484e836f90c47 proves
F_{g,a,b}(ell_{g,a,b})=0,
sup_t|F_{g,a,b}(t)|<< (log x)^2,
and
integral_R |F'_{g,a,b}(t)|dt << (log x)^2.
It also proves that the upper endpoint is not a source progression point. Hence the strict-open Fejer reconstruction has no endpoint half-weight, and
Var(A)
 <=|F(ell)|+|F(u)|+integral_ell^u|F'(t)|dt
 <<(log x)^2.                                                 (7)
Equations (6)-(7) give O((log x)^2) for the complete nonzero paired packet at each fixed (g,a,b).

The same calculation audits the integration-by-parts faces separately. In the notation of equation (4) of fact 152484e836f90c47, the lower face vanishes. The upper face is a real number F(u) times (2 pi i h)^(-1) and an h-th power of a unit complex number. Its symmetric Cesaro sum is O(|F(u)|) by (4), and replacing h by -h gives its complex conjugate. For the derivative term, interchange the finite h-sum and the t-integral; equation (4) bounds its paired sum by
O(integral_ell^u|F'(t)|dt).
It too is conjugated by h to -h because F' is real. Thus both surviving pieces are individually O((log x)^2).

Now use the exact Delta-decomposition in fact 152484e836f90c47. Both I_Delta and R_Delta are real and h-independent. The cutoff construction gives
integral_R|I_Delta'(t)|dt<<_chi 1.
Consequently
Var(F I_Delta)
 <=integral|F'|+sup|F| integral|I_Delta'|
 <<(log x)^2.                                                 (8)
Since
F R_Delta=F1_{ell<t<u}-F I_Delta,
subadditivity of total variation and (7)-(8) give
Var(F R_Delta)<< (log x)^2.                                   (9)
Apply (6) separately to the two amplitudes in (8)-(9). This proves the claimed exact conjugacy and uniform O((log x)^2) payment for the smooth interior and both hard boundary strips. Notice that the scaled derivative tax T_Delta from fact 152484e836f90c47 is not incurred: the present argument uses total variation, and a transition derivative of size Delta^(-1) is integrated only over length O(Delta).

It remains to sum the fixed-(g,a,b) bound. On a nonempty exact g-layer, dyadic support gives
a asymp D/g, b asymp R/g.
Thus there are
O((D/g)(R/g))
admissible ordered pairs (a,b); coprimality and all literal zero-one masks only delete pairs. All source weights not already included in F are real and h-independent. Facts 77d7a3419a07305c and 7131a06664967733 show that the parent and anatomy partitions preserve the original paired coefficient, and that the total absolute weight of the internal copies of an active A- or B-marker is exactly one. The finite parent/anatomy list, dyadic labels, smooth tensor separations and provenance copies cost x^(o(1)). Therefore the total contribution at exact g is
<<x^(o(1))DR/g^2.                                             (10)

The outer-gcd normalization gives g|N. Hence
sum_{g|N,g>=G}g^(-2)
 <=tau(N)G^(-2)=x^(o(1))G^(-2).                              (11)
Summing (10) and absorbing the polylogarithmic selected-label count proves (1).

Finally, an actual Z_mid incidence on a selected forced-high label has R<<x^(2/3) by fact af06640e8d8e4102, while D<=2x^(1/2) by fact 60b26a9b6f79467a. This proves (2). If G=x^(1/12+eta), then (2) is
x^(7/6-1/6-2eta+o(1))=x^(1-2eta+o(1)),
which is O_eta(x^(1-eta)) for sufficiently large x. This proves (3) and all scope statements.
