glossary.R_max: the largest dyadic r-scale among the actual-Z_mid labels included in R_mid^{ne0}(G)
glossary.R_mid^{ne0}(G): the complete symmetric first-Cesaro nonzero-Poisson contribution of actual-Z_mid source incidences on exact outer-gcd layers g at least G
glossary.Var(A): the total variation on the real line of a compactly supported bounded-variation function A

a274f28c67018d5f.title: Let m>1 be an odd integer, and let K,r_2,r_3 be integers with gcd(m,2 K r_2 r_3)=1. Let T_m be the set of quadruples (a,b,c,d) modulo m satisfying
a274f28c67018d5f.author: slava chan
a274f28c67018d5f.statement:
Let m>1 be an odd integer, and let K,r_2,r_3 be integers with gcd(m,2 K r_2 r_3)=1. Let T_m be the set of quadruples (a,b,c,d) modulo m satisfying
b r_3-d r_2=0, a r_2-c r_3=0, ab-cd=0, ab+cd=2 K  (mod m).
Define e_m(x)=exp(2 pi i x/m). For residues h_a,h_b,h_c,h_d modulo m define
F_m(h_a,h_b,h_c,h_d)
 =sum_{(a,b,c,d) in T_m} e_m(h_a a+h_b b+h_c c+h_d d).
Put
X_tor=h_a r_2^{-1}+h_c r_3^{-1},
Y_tor=K(h_b r_2+h_d r_3)  (mod m).
Then
F_m(h_a,h_b,h_c,h_d)=S(X_tor,Y_tor;m),
where S(X,Y;m) is the classical Kloosterman sum
sum_{t modulo m, gcd(t,m)=1} e_m(Xt+Yt^{-1}).

The homomorphism L_m from four frequency residues to two residues defined by
L_m(h_a,h_b,h_c,h_d)=(X_tor,Y_tor)
is surjective and every fibre has exactly m^2 elements. The pairs (X,Y) for which
Xt+Yt^{-1}=0  (mod m)
for every unit t modulo m are exactly
Y=-X and X=0  (mod m/gcd(m,3)).
There are therefore exactly gcd(m,3) such pairs and exactly gcd(m,3)m^2 frequency quadruples on which every summand in F_m equals 1. On each of those frequencies F_m=phi(m). Conversely, F_m=phi(m) only on those frequencies.

Consequently no estimate o(phi(m)) is uniform over the four raw frequency slots. When 3 does not divide m, the only full-mass fibre is ker(L_m); when 3 divides m, two additional exceptional fibres arise from the 3-primary component. Any nondegenerate Kloosterman argument must remove, center, project away, or pay all these fibres. This result controls only the modular torus and supplies no cancellation for the integer carries or literal lift selectors in fact d472dd752c1eb6a8.
a274f28c67018d5f.proof:
Fact d472dd752c1eb6a8, whose hypotheses have been restated here, proves that T_m is parameterized bijectively by units t modulo m through
(a,b,c,d)=(t r_2^{-1},K r_2 t^{-1},t r_3^{-1},K r_3 t^{-1}).
Substitution into the Fourier phase gives
h_a a+h_b b+h_c c+h_d d
 =(h_a r_2^{-1}+h_c r_3^{-1})t
  +K(h_b r_2+h_d r_3)t^{-1}
 =X_tor t+Y_tor t^{-1}.
This proves the Kloosterman identity directly and agrees with the definition in fact b302e2cd6d611a35.

The map L_m is an additive-group homomorphism. Given arbitrary target residues X_0,Y_0 modulo m, choose
h_a=X_0 r_2, h_c=0,
h_b=K^{-1}Y_0 r_2^{-1}, h_d=0.
The inverses exist by the coprimality hypothesis, and this frequency quadruple maps to (X_0,Y_0). Thus L_m is onto. Its domain and codomain have m^4 and m^2 elements, so every fibre, being a coset of the kernel, has m^2 elements.

It remains to classify identically zero phases. Suppose
Xt+Yt^{-1}=0
for every unit t. Taking t=1 gives Y=-X. Multiplication of the remaining identity by the unit t shows that the condition is equivalent to
X(t^2-1)=0  (mod m)
for every unit t. Factor m into odd prime powers and use the Chinese remainder theorem.

Fix a prime power p^k exactly dividing m. Choose, by the Chinese remainder theorem, a unit t modulo m whose component modulo p^k is 2 and whose components modulo every other prime-power factor are 1. If p>=5, then t^2-1 is 3 modulo p^k, which is a unit. Hence X=0 modulo p^k. This holds on every prime-power component except possibly the 3-primary one.

If 3^k exactly divides m, the same choice t=2 on that component gives
3X=0  (mod 3^k),
so X is divisible by 3^{k-1} on the 3-primary component. Conversely, every unit t modulo 3^k is congruent to 1 or -1 modulo 3, hence t^2-1 is divisible by 3. Therefore every X divisible by 3^{k-1} satisfies
X(t^2-1)=0  (mod 3^k)
for all units t. Combining the components, X must vanish modulo every p^k with p>=5 and has exactly three possible residues on the 3-primary component if 3|m; if 3 does not divide m, X is zero. Equivalently,
X=0  (mod m/gcd(m,3)).
With Y=-X this proves the classification and the count gcd(m,3) of phase-zero pairs. Since every fibre of L_m has m^2 elements, the number of corresponding raw frequency quadruples is gcd(m,3)m^2.

Every phase-zero frequency has F_m=phi(m). Conversely, F_m is a sum of phi(m) complex numbers of absolute value one. If it equals the positive real number phi(m), equality in the triangle inequality forces every summand to equal 1, so its phase is zero modulo m for every unit t. The proved classification is therefore also the exact classification of frequencies with F_m=phi(m). The final obstruction and scope statements follow.

glossary.F_m: the complete additive Fourier transform of the residue torus T_m in the four coefficient slots
glossary.L_m: the surjective frequency homomorphism from four coefficient frequencies to the two Kloosterman arguments
glossary.X_tor: the direct Kloosterman argument h_a r_2^{-1}+h_c r_3^{-1} modulo m
glossary.Y_tor: the inverse Kloosterman argument K(h_b r_2+h_d r_3) modulo m
glossary.e_m: the additive character e_m(x)=exp(2 pi i x/m)
glossary.h_a: the additive frequency paired with a modulo m
glossary.h_b: the additive frequency paired with b modulo m
glossary.h_c: the additive frequency paired with c modulo m
glossary.h_d: the additive frequency paired with d modulo m

a3103a7fbc2dc2ed.title: EXACT CRITICAL SCALE SIMPLEX, DEEP-SUBHALF EQUIVALENCE, SQUAREFREE DIVISOR AGGREGATION, AND RESIDUAL PARITY-CORE LEDGER. Fix tau>0. Assume the critical-row descent of fact 8d9feea8c44da2c8 in a fixed orientation, with B=Q^beta, Q_c=Q/c, K_c=GQ^(2-beta)/c, T=GQ and ell=N/(gc). Define the inherited critical-W projection to be the complementary projection to the good-W family of fact e55b27d39c593164, namely the atoms satisfying
a3103a7fbc2dc2ed.author: slava chan
a3103a7fbc2dc2ed.statement:
EXACT CRITICAL SCALE SIMPLEX, DEEP-SUBHALF EQUIVALENCE, SQUAREFREE DIVISOR AGGREGATION, AND RESIDUAL PARITY-CORE LEDGER. Fix tau>0. Assume the critical-row descent of fact 8d9feea8c44da2c8 in a fixed orientation, with B=Q^beta, Q_c=Q/c, K_c=GQ^(2-beta)/c, T=GQ and ell=N/(gc). Define the inherited critical-W projection to be the complementary projection to the good-W family of fact e55b27d39c593164, namely the atoms satisfying
mathscr W<Q^tau.                                                  (1)
Put
Gamma=Gc.                                                        (2)
Then exactly
T=Gamma Q_c,                                                     (3)
B=Q_c^2 Gamma/K_c,                                               (4)
ell asymptotic to Q_c T=Q_c^2 Gamma
and ell asymptotic to BK_c,                                      (5)
and
mathscr W=Gamma K_c.                                             (6)
For every fixed C>0, the deep-subhalf modulus condition
Q_c <= sqrt(B)/(log B)^C                                        (7)
is equivalent to
Gamma >= K_c(log B)^(2C).                                       (8)

The exact target-gcd aggregation has no hidden Q^epsilon tax. Every active pair (g,c) satisfies
gc divides N, gcd(g,c)=1, and mu^2(gc)=1.                         (9)
Consequently
sum over active (g,c) of 1/(gc)
 <= sum_{gc divides N,(g,c)=1,mu^2(gc)=1}1/(gc)
 =product_{p divides N}(1+2/p)                                  (10)
 <=(1+log N)^2.                                                  (11)
Hence any orientation-uniform local estimate
|S_{g,c}| <= C_A [N/(gc)](log N)^(-A)                           (12)
sums over all exact active g,c to
sum_{g,c}|S_{g,c}|
 <= C_A N(log N)^(-A)(1+log N)^2,                               (13)
before the fixed two-orientation and remaining explicitly counted polylogarithmic label taxes. Equation (13) does not absorb any factor Q^epsilon.

There is also an exact conditional residual-core ledger. Fix C,D>0. Name the deep range
cal R_BV(C)={Gamma >= K_c(log B)^(2C)}                            (14)
and name the parameter range in which a hypothetical centered estimate with relative gain min(Gamma,K_c)^(-1/2) would provide at least (log B)^(-D),
cal R_cen(D)={min(Gamma,K_c) >= (log B)^(2D)}.                   (15)
The complement of their union is exactly
cal R_core(C,D)
 ={Gamma<K_c(log B)^(2C) and
   min(Gamma,K_c)<(log B)^(2D)}.                                (16)
It is the disjoint union of
{Gamma<(log B)^(2D), Gamma<K_c(log B)^(2C)}                     (17a)
and
{Gamma>=(log B)^(2D), K_c<(log B)^(2D),
 Gamma<K_c(log B)^(2C)}.                                        (17b)
In particular (17b) forces
K_c<(log B)^(2D), Gamma<(log B)^(2C+2D).                         (18)
On the critical-W projection (1), equation (6) gives exactly
Gamma K_c<Q^tau.                                                 (19)
Thus after an eligible deep-subhalf Mobius Bombieri-Vinogradov supplier and an independently proved centered supplier of the stated relative strength, the exact unresolved method core is (16), with a genuinely low-Gamma branch (17a) and a bounded-polylog two-parameter branch (17b). No centered estimate, low-conductor payment, local bound (12), critical-tail payment, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
a3103a7fbc2dc2ed.proof:
By definition Q_c=Q/c and Gamma=Gc, so Gamma Q_c=(Gc)(Q/c)=GQ=T, proving (3). Moreover
Q_c^2 Gamma/K_c
=(Q^2/c^2)(Gc)/(GQ^(2-beta)/c)=Q^beta=B,
which proves (4). Fact 8d9feea8c44da2c8 proves ell is comparable to Q_cT and BK_c; substitution of (3) gives (5). Fact e55b27d39c593164 gives mathscr W=G K_sh with K_sh=GQ^(2-beta). Since Gamma K_c=(Gc)(K_sh/c)=GK_sh, this proves (6).

All quantities in (7) are positive. Squaring (7) and substituting (4) gives
Q_c^2 <= Q_c^2 Gamma/[K_c(log B)^(2C)].
Canceling Q_c^2 yields (8), and every step is reversible.

Fact a71f777ad842c886 proves that g and s are coprime and squarefree on every nonzero atom. Since c divides s, gcd(g,c)=1; definition c|(N/g) gives gc|N. Since g and c divide the pairwise coprime squarefree integers g and s, respectively, gc is squarefree. This proves (9).

For the squarefree majorant sum in (10), each p|N may divide neither g nor c, may divide g, or may divide c, contributing respectively 1,1/p,1/p. This gives the Euler product. For (11), pointwise
1+2/p <=(1+1/p)^2.
Therefore
product_{p|N}(1+2/p)
 <=[product_{p|N}(1+1/p)]^2
 =[sum_{d|rad(N)}1/d]^2
 <=[sum_{1<=d<=N}1/d]^2
 <=(1+log N)^2,
where the last inequality follows by comparing sum_{d=2}^N 1/d with integral_1^N dt/t. Summing (12) and using (10)-(11) proves (13).

The complement of a union is the intersection of the complements. Applying this to (14)-(15) gives (16). Split (16) according as Gamma<(log B)^(2D) or Gamma>=(log B)^(2D). In the second case, min(Gamma,K_c)<(log B)^(2D) forces K_c<(log B)^(2D), giving (17a)-(17b). The last inequality in (17b), together with K_c<(log B)^(2D), gives (18). Finally, the critical projection was explicitly defined by (1), so combining it with (6) proves (19). All analytic estimates mentioned after (19) are explicitly hypotheses of the ledger and are not used as proved statements.

glossary.cal R_BV(C): The exact deep-subhalf parameter range at logarithmic exponent C.
glossary.cal R_cen(D): The range where a hypothetical square-root aspect gain is at least log-power D.
glossary.cal R_core(C,D): The exact complement of the two named payable parameter ranges.

a3132ecd1bd44382.title: ELEVEN-MODE RECIPROCAL-SLOPE EXPANSION OF THE FULL C4 K2 RAY KERNEL AND A SOURCE-SPECIFIC LARGE-SIEVE SUPPLIER. Adopt the setting of fact 134b03fc362a7cf1. For one lambda write P_lambda for the set of four primes dividing D_lambda. For every squarefree r dividing D_lambda with at most two prime factors, let R be the set of primes dividing r and define the positive coefficient
a3132ecd1bd44382.author: slava chan
a3132ecd1bd44382.statement:
ELEVEN-MODE RECIPROCAL-SLOPE EXPANSION OF THE FULL C4 K2 RAY KERNEL AND A SOURCE-SPECIFIC LARGE-SIEVE SUPPLIER. Adopt the setting of fact 134b03fc362a7cf1. For one lambda write P_lambda for the set of four primes dividing D_lambda. For every squarefree r dividing D_lambda with at most two prime factors, let R be the set of primes dividing r and define the positive coefficient
c_lambda(r)=sum_{S subset P_lambda, |S|=2, R subset S}
 (product_{p in S minus R}1/(p-1))
 (product_{p in P_lambda minus S}(-1/p)).                          (1)
Then c_lambda(r)>0, and explicitly
c_lambda(r)=r/D_lambda if r has two prime factors,
c_lambda(p)<= (9/2)p/D_lambda if r=p is prime,
c_lambda(1)<=27/(2D_lambda).                                      (2)
For rho=(epsilon,a,b), put
Psi_{lambda,r}(rho)
=e_{v_lambda r}(A epsilon b [a(D_lambda/r)]^{-1}).                 (3)
Then the exact full six-sibling kernel has the eleven-mode expansion
K_lambda(rho)
=sum_{r|D_lambda, omega(r)<=2}c_lambda(r)Psi_{lambda,r}(rho).       (4)
There are one, four, and six terms with respectively zero, one, and two prime factors. In particular, if every prime dividing D_lambda is at least Z, then
C_lambda:=sum_{r|D_lambda, omega(r)<=2}c_lambda(r)
<=27/(2Z^2).                                                       (5)

With B_lambda(rho;z) and T_lambda(z) as in fact 134b03fc362a7cf1, define the eleven reciprocal-slope transforms
S_{lambda,r}(z)=sum_rho B_lambda(rho;z)Psi_{lambda,r}(rho).         (6)
Then exactly
T_lambda(z)=sum_{r|D_lambda, omega(r)<=2}c_lambda(r)S_{lambda,r}(z). (7)
Consequently, for nonnegative real theta_lambda and
C_* =max_lambda C_lambda,
sum_lambda theta_lambda |T_lambda(z)|^2
<=C_* sum_lambda theta_lambda
 sum_{r|D_lambda, omega(r)<=2}c_lambda(r)|S_{lambda,r}(z)|^2.       (8)
Thus a concrete sufficient source-specific large-sieve supplier is
sum_lambda theta_lambda
 sum_{r|D_lambda, omega(r)<=2}c_lambda(r)|S_{lambda,r}(z)|^2
<=Lcal ||z||_2^2.                                                  (9)
It gives the full scoped moment bound C_*Lcal||z||_2^2. After applying the exact trichotomy of fact 134b03fc362a7cf1, the corresponding off-ray quadratic form obeys
|sum_lambda theta_lambda R_lambda^{off}(z)|
<=C_*Lcal||z||_2^2
 +sum_lambda theta_lambda D_lambda^{ray}(z)
 +|sum_lambda theta_lambda R_lambda^{FR}(z)|.                      (10)
For literal coefficients, the last two terms are precisely the same-ray and fully resonant sector types already paid by fact 54029717e980dcb7. Equations (4)-(10) retain varying v_lambda, every ray-scale sum B_lambda, and every literal coefficient and mask inside it. No estimate (9), transfer of the numerical payments to a nonliteral family, full C4 estimate, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
a3132ecd1bd44382.proof:
Fix lambda and abbreviate D=D_lambda, v=v_lambda, P=P_lambda. Fact 34d306bcb630f9df gives
K_lambda(rho)
=e_v(A epsilon b(aD)^{-1})
 sum_{S subset P, |S|=2}
 (product_{p in S}[zeta_p(rho)+1/(p-1)])
 (product_{p in P minus S}[-1/p]),                                 (11)
where
zeta_p(rho)=e_p(A epsilon b[a(Dv/p)]^{-1}).                         (12)
Expand the active product in (11). If R is the subset of active primes at which zeta_p is selected, the remaining primes of S contribute 1/(p-1), while the primes outside S contribute -1/p. Grouping terms with the same R gives exactly the coefficient (1). Necessarily |R|<=2, so there are 1+4+6=11 groups.

Every summand in (1) is positive: P minus S has exactly two primes, so its two negative factors have positive product, and all other factors are positive. This proves c_lambda(r)>0.

If r has two prime factors, the only possible S is R, and
c_lambda(r)=product_{p in P minus R}1/p=r/D.
If r=p is prime, then
c_lambda(p)
=sum_{q in P minus {p}} [1/(q-1)] [1/(D/(pq))]
=sum_{q in P minus {p}} (p/D)[q/(q-1)].
Every prime in P is odd, hence q/(q-1)<=3/2. There are three terms, proving c_lambda(p)<=9p/(2D).
For r=1,
c_lambda(1)
=sum_{S={p,q}} 1/[(p-1)(q-1)] * 1/[D/(pq)]
=(1/D)sum_{S={p,q}}[p/(p-1)][q/(q-1)].
There are six terms and each is at most 9/4, proving the last bound in (2).

It remains to combine the phases in one R-group. Let r be the product of the primes in R, with r=1 allowed. CRT gives
product_{p|r}zeta_p(rho)
=e_r(A epsilon b[a(Dv/r)]^{-1}).                                  (13)
Indeed, its p-component is obtained by multiplying the argument on the right by (r/p)^{-1}, and
(Dv/r)(r/p)=Dv/p.
The small-v phase in (11) and (13) combine, again by CRT and gcd(v,r)=1, as
e_v(A epsilon b(aD)^{-1})
 e_r(A epsilon b[a(Dv/r)]^{-1})
=e_{vr}(A epsilon b[a(D/r)]^{-1}),                                 (14)
because the common CRT numerator modulo both v and r is
A epsilon b[a(D/r)]^{-1}.
For r=1, equation (14) is just the small-v phase. Equations (11)-(14), grouped by R, prove (3)-(4).

If every p|D is at least Z, evaluate the positive coefficient sum C_lambda before grouping by setting every zeta_p equal to one in the expanded expression:
C_lambda
=sum_{S subset P, |S|=2}
 product_{p in S}[1+1/(p-1)]
 product_{p in P minus S}(1/p).
Each active factor is at most 3/2 and each inactive reciprocal product is at most Z^{-2}. Six terms give (5).

Substitute (4) into the definitions F_lambda=B_lambda K_lambda and T_lambda=sum_rho F_lambda from fact 134b03fc362a7cf1. Interchange the two finite sums. This gives (6)-(7) with every coefficient inside B_lambda unchanged.

Since all c_lambda(r) are positive, weighted Cauchy-Schwarz gives
|sum_r c_lambda(r)S_{lambda,r}(z)|^2
<=[sum_r c_lambda(r)]
 [sum_r c_lambda(r)|S_{lambda,r}(z)|^2].
Multiply by theta_lambda>=0, sum lambda, and use C_lambda<=C_* to prove (8). Assumption (9) then gives the full moment bound.

Finally, equation (13) of fact 134b03fc362a7cf1 says
R_lambda^{off}=|T_lambda|^2-D_lambda^{ray}-R_lambda^{FR}.
Sum with nonnegative theta_lambda, take one absolute value, use nonnegativity of the full squares and of D_lambda^{ray}, and apply the triangle inequality. The full-square sum is bounded by (8)-(9), giving (10). The sector identification with fact 54029717e980dcb7 is already proved in fact 134b03fc362a7cf1. This completes the proof and preserves all stated exclusions.

glossary.C_lambda: The sum of the eleven positive mode coefficients.
glossary.Lcal: A placeholder constant in the explicitly unproved source-specific large-sieve supplier.
glossary.Psi_{lambda,r}: The unit-modulus reciprocal-slope phase modulo v_lambda r.
glossary.S_{lambda,r}: The literal ray-scale coefficient transformed against Psi_{lambda,r}.
glossary.c_lambda(r): The positive coefficient of the reciprocal-slope mode indexed by r in the eleven-mode expansion.

a36284a9dbec7837.title: GOOD-\(\mathscr W\) PRIMITIVE-RAY MÖBIUS NORMAL FORM AND THE EXACT COHERENT UNIT-DENOMINATOR SOURCE CORE
a36284a9dbec7837.author: slava chan
a36284a9dbec7837.statement:
GOOD-\(\mathscr W\) PRIMITIVE-RAY MÖBIUS NORMAL FORM AND THE EXACT COHERENT UNIT-DENOMINATOR SOURCE CORE.

Adopt one fixed-orientation, fixed-anatomy
\(\mathfrak a\in\{A,C_j\}\), fixed-frequency and fixed-dilator block from fact e55b27d39c593164. For one exact marked copy \(\lambda\), write
\[
 n=d_\lambda v_\lambda,\qquad (d_\lambda,v_\lambda)=1,
\]
retain its orientation sign \(\varepsilon_{\rm or}\), nonzero target
\(\mathscr A\), marker weight \(a_\lambda(n)\), literal Fourier transform
\(\widehat{\mathcal F}_{q,n}\), and complete mask
\(\Xi_\lambda(q,h,n)\). Let
\[
 R=(\epsilon,a,b),\qquad \epsilon\in\{-1,1\},\quad
 a,b>0,\quad(a,b)=1
\]
be a primitive signed ray, and put
\[
 \mathscr I_\lambda(R)
 =
 \{k>0:c_\lambda(ka,\epsilon kb)\ne0\},                    \tag{1}
\]
where \(c_\lambda\) is the exact pre-reciprocity coefficient in equation (9) of fact e55b27d39c593164. Define
\[
 \mathcal W_{\lambda,R}(k)
 =
 \widehat{\mathcal F}_{ka,n}
 \!\left({\varepsilon_{\rm or}\epsilon kb\over n}\right)
 \Xi_\lambda(ka,\epsilon kb,n),                              \tag{2}
\]
and
\[
 \mathcal A_\lambda(R)
 =
 a_\lambda(n)\mu(a){H_P\over n}
 e\!\left(
 {\varepsilon_{\rm or}\mathscr A\epsilon b\over an}
 \right).                                                       \tag{3}
\]
Then every \(k\in\mathscr I_\lambda(R)\) satisfies
\[
 \mu(ka)\ne0,qquad (k,a)=1,qquad
 \mu(ka)=\mu(k)\mu(a),                                       \tag{4}
\]
and the pre-reciprocity ray coefficient of fact 7e9251670db3e1c9 has the exact signed normal form
\[
 \boxed{
 B_\lambda(R)
 =
 \mathcal A_\lambda(R)
 \sum_{k\in\mathscr I_\lambda(R)}
 \mu(k)\mathcal W_{\lambda,R}(k).
 }                                                               \tag{RAY-MU}
\]
All conditions in (1) remain inside the summation; no raywise absolute value and no replacement of the literal mask is made. The post-reciprocity ray coefficient is still
\[
 S_\lambda(R)
 =
 I_{\infty,\lambda}(R)I_{v,\lambda}(R)B_\lambda(R)           \tag{5}
\]
with the exact multipliers of fact 7e9251670db3e1c9.

For the coherent unit-denominator rays put
\[
 \mathcal U_\lambda(\epsilon,b)
 =
 \sum_{\substack{k>0\\
 c_\lambda(k,\epsilon kb)\ne0}}
 \mu(k)
 \widehat{\mathcal F}_{k,n}
 \!\left({\varepsilon_{\rm or}\epsilon kb\over n}\right)
 \Xi_\lambda(k,\epsilon kb,n),                               \tag{6}
\]
\[
 \mathcal A_\lambda(\epsilon,b)
 =
 a_\lambda(n){H_P\over n}
 e\!\left(
 {\varepsilon_{\rm or}\mathscr A\epsilon b\over n}
 \right).                                                       \tag{7}
\]
The restriction of the exact good-\(\mathscr W\) nonresonant moment to ordered ray pairs with \(a=a'=1\) is
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathfrak U_{\mathfrak a,F}^{\rm NR}(\mathcal D)
 =
 \sum_{n,\lambda}
 \sum_{\substack{(\epsilon,b)\ne(\epsilon',b')\\
 d_\lambda\nmid
 \mathscr A(\epsilon b-\epsilon'b')}}
 &\mathcal A_\lambda(\epsilon,b)
 \overline{\mathcal A_\lambda(\epsilon',b')}\\
 &\times
 \mathcal U_\lambda(\epsilon,b)
 \overline{\mathcal U_\lambda(\epsilon',b')}.
 \end{aligned}
 }                                                               \tag{UNIT-RAY-SRC}
\]
There is no additional oscillatory phase in UNIT-RAY-SRC. In particular, any cancellation on this slice must come from the complete signed source transforms (6), their cross-ray correlation, or their aggregation across exact marked copies.

Fact 71389b22e6f49e13 does not directly specialize to an individual transform (6) under the present hypotheses. That fact requires a single continuously differentiable scaled weight of uniformly bounded supremum and total variation, possibly with coprimality conditions. In (6), the Fourier transform itself is indexed by the varying modulus \(k\), and the inherited factor
\(\Xi_\lambda(k,\epsilon kb,n)\) contains the exact hard source and deletion masks; fact e55b27d39c593164 assumes no bounded-variation representation of this combined \(k\)-weight. Therefore a direct Davenport substitution requires a prior source-specific recombination or projective decomposition which proves the needed regularity while preserving UNIT-RAY-SRC. Even after such a decomposition, a proof must estimate the complete signed quadratic form (UNIT-RAY-SRC), not sum raywise absolute bounds.

This is an exact coefficient and theorem-interface statement. It proves no estimate for UNIT-RAY-SRC, DV-RAY-PAIR, GA-RAY-SPEC, GA-NR-DIL, the good-\(\mathscr W\) tail, or Goldbach.
a36284a9dbec7837.proof:
Equation (9) of fact e55b27d39c593164 states
\[
 c_\lambda(q,h)
 =
 a_\lambda(n)\mu(q){H_P\over n}
 \widehat{\mathcal F}_{q,n}
 \!\left({\varepsilon_{\rm or}h\over n}\right)
 e\!\left(
 {\varepsilon_{\rm or}\mathscr A h\over qn}\right)
 \Xi_\lambda(q,h,n).                                          \tag{8}
\]
Let \(k\in\mathscr I_\lambda(R)\). By definition,
\(c_\lambda(ka,\epsilon kb)\ne0\). The factor \(\mu(ka)\) in (8) is therefore nonzero. Hence \(ka\) is squarefree. Since \(k\) and \(a\) are positive divisors of the squarefree integer \(ka\), each is squarefree and \((k,a)=1\). Multiplicativity of the Möbius function proves (4).

Substitute
\[
 q=ka,qquad h=\epsilon kb
\]
in (8). The Archimedean factor becomes
\[
 e\!\left(
 {\varepsilon_{\rm or}\mathscr A\epsilon kb
  \over ka n}\right)
 =
 e\!\left(
 {\varepsilon_{\rm or}\mathscr A\epsilon b
  \over an}\right),                                          \tag{9}
\]
which is independent of \(k\). Using (4), the remaining \(k\)-dependent factors are exactly
\[
 \mu(k)\mathcal W_{\lambda,R}(k).
\]
Summing (8) over the supported scaling set (1) and extracting the factors independent of \(k\) gives RAY-MU. Equation (5) is exactly the pre/post-reciprocity relation in fact 7e9251670db3e1c9.

Set \(a=1\) in RAY-MU. Since \(\mu(1)=1\), definitions (6)--(7) give
\[
 B_\lambda(\epsilon,1,b)
 =
 \mathcal A_\lambda(\epsilon,b)
 \mathcal U_\lambda(\epsilon,b).                              \tag{10}
\]
Fact 7e9251670db3e1c9 proves that for an ordered pair of primitive rays the nonresonant selector is
\[
 d_\lambda\nmid\mathscr A\Delta_0,
 \qquad
 \Delta_0=\epsilon ba'-\epsilon'b'a,
\]
and that the complete physical pair phase is
\[
 e_{aa'}(-\mathscr A\Delta_0(d_\lambda v_\lambda)^{-1}).
\]
For \(a=a'=1\), one has
\[
 \Delta_0=\epsilon b-\epsilon'b'
\]
and the modulus-one phase is identically one. Substitute (10) for both rays in the exact nonresonant ray-pair form of that fact. Distinctness of the two rays is exactly
\((\epsilon,b)\ne(\epsilon',b')\). This proves UNIT-RAY-SRC without taking an absolute value.

Finally, compare (6) with the hypotheses of fact 71389b22e6f49e13. The latter accepts \(\mu(k)F(k/X)\) for a uniformly bounded continuously differentiable family with bounded total variation, together with coprimality predicates. Formula (6) contains a \(k\)-indexed family
\(\widehat{\mathcal F}_{k,n}\) and the complete hard mask
\(\Xi_\lambda(k,\epsilon kb,n)\). No regularity or separated representation of their product as a function of \(k\) is among the assumptions of fact e55b27d39c593164. Thus the cited theorem cannot be invoked directly. This establishes only the stated interface no-fit; all limitations follow.

a3829b00a5a4b238.title: EXACT MULTIPLICATIVE-CHARACTER DIAGONALIZATION OF WEIGHTED CENTERED SLOPE KERNELS. Let p>2 be prime. For every \(c\in\mathbb F_p^\times\) define
a3829b00a5a4b238.author: slava chan
a3829b00a5a4b238.statement:
EXACT MULTIPLICATIVE-CHARACTER DIAGONALIZATION OF WEIGHTED CENTERED SLOPE KERNELS. Let p>2 be prime. For every \(c\in\mathbb F_p^\times\) define
\[
G_c(f,g)={p\over p-1}\left({\bf1}_{g=cf}-{1\over p-1}\right)
\qquad(f,g\in\mathbb F_p^\times).
\]
Let \(\lambda_c\) be arbitrary complex numbers and define the operator
\[
K_\lambda=\sum_{c\in\mathbb F_p^\times}\lambda_cG_c
\quad\hbox{on }\ell^2(\mathbb F_p^\times). \tag{1}
\]
For every multiplicative character \(\chi\) of \(\mathbb F_p^\times\), put
\[
\Lambda(\chi)=\sum_{c\in\mathbb F_p^\times}\lambda_c\chi(c). \tag{2}
\]
Then K_lambda kills the constant vector. Every nonprincipal multiplicative character chi is an eigenvector with eigenvalue
\[
{p\over p-1}\Lambda(\chi). \tag{3}
\]
Consequently
\[
\|K_\lambda\|_{\rm op}
={p\over p-1}\max_{\chi\ne\chi_0}|\Lambda(\chi)|, \tag{4}
\]
and
\[
\|K_\lambda\|_{\rm HS}^2
=\left({p\over p-1}\right)^2
\left((p-1)\sum_c|\lambda_c|^2-\left|\sum_c\lambda_c\right|^2\right). \tag{5}
\]
In particular, if lambda_c is independent of c, then K_lambda is the zero operator. Thus averaging centered incidence kernels over slopes yields a saving exactly to the extent that every nonprincipal multiplicative-character transform of the slope weights is small; slope cardinality or additive-Fourier resonant-line sparsity alone is not the relevant operator norm.

In the literal prime-local Gram factor of fact ce5de84556b212d9, the slope is c=s_1q_2^{-1} modulo p. Equations (3)--(5) therefore identify the exact p-local supplier after one has grouped literal outer pairs by this slope. They apply directly only when the remaining d_i-tensors and source coefficients have been aligned so that their slope weight lambda_c is independent of the unit residues f,g. No such alignment or bound for the literal lambda_c, K_inc^rem, K_inc^main, or Goldbach is asserted.
a3829b00a5a4b238.proof:
For a vector v on \(\mathbb F_p^\times\), direct summation gives
\[
(K_\lambda v)(f)
={p\over p-1}\left(
\sum_c\lambda_cv(cf)
-{\sum_c\lambda_c\over p-1}\sum_{g\ne0}v(g)
\right). \tag{6}
\]
If v is constant, the two terms in parentheses are equal, so K_lambda v=0.

Let chi be nonprincipal and put v(f)=chi(f). Then \(\sum_g\chi(g)=0\), while
\[
\sum_c\lambda_c\chi(cf)
=\chi(f)\sum_c\lambda_c\chi(c)
=\Lambda(\chi)v(f).
\]
This proves (3). The p-1 multiplicative characters form an orthogonal basis of \(\ell^2(\mathbb F_p^\times)\). In that basis K_lambda is diagonal, with eigenvalue zero on the principal character and the eigenvalues (3) on all nonprincipal characters. Hence its operator norm is (4).

The squared Hilbert--Schmidt norm is the sum of the squared absolute eigenvalues. Multiplicative Parseval in the unnormalised convention (2) gives
\[
\sum_\chi|\Lambda(\chi)|^2=(p-1)\sum_c|\lambda_c|^2.
\]
The principal term is \(|\Lambda(\chi_0)|^2=|\sum_c\lambda_c|^2\). Removing it and multiplying by \((p/(p-1))^2\) proves (5). If lambda_c is constant, every nonprincipal character sum vanishes, so (4) gives K_lambda=0.

Finally, the literal slope identification is the one proved in fact ce5de84556b212d9. The qualification about aligned remaining tensors is necessary because equations (1)--(6) concern scalar slope weights multiplying the same prime-local matrices; they do not move or separate any d_i-dependent factor.

glossary.K_\\lambda: The weighted aggregate of centered slope-incidence operators.
glossary.\\Lambda(\\chi): The unnormalised multiplicative-character transform of the slope weights.
glossary.\\chi_0: The principal multiplicative character modulo p.
glossary.\\lambda_c: The complex scalar weight assigned to slope c.

a4065b4002385422.title: SCOPED WRIGHT FIXED-\(v\) AUDIT FOR A LITERAL \(C_3\) BLOCK. Work in the fixed-\(g\), low-\(\beta\) normalization
a4065b4002385422.author: slava chan
a4065b4002385422.statement:
SCOPED WRIGHT FIXED-\(v\) AUDIT FOR A LITERAL \(C_3\) BLOCK. Work in the fixed-\(g\), low-\(\beta\) normalization
\[
 B=Q^\beta,\qquad G_*=Q^\gamma\ge1,\qquad H_P=Q^{\beta-1-\gamma},\qquad x/g\asymp G_*Q^2,
\]
with \(Q>1\), \(1\le\beta\le6/5-2\kappa\), and \(H_P\ge1\). On a dyadic \(C_3\) block fix the small factor \(v\asymp V=Q^\nu\), combine the three remaining prime variables into \(n\asymp P=B/V=Q^{\beta-\nu}\), and suppose \(Q\ll P^2\). Under the literal identification in Thomas Wright's Theorem 2.1
\[
 (R_W,M_W,N_W,A_W,\vartheta)=(v,Q,P,H_P,Lsrc),
\]
where \(|Lsrc|\ll G_*Q^2\), applying that theorem separately for each \(v\) and then taking the triangle inequality over \(v\asymp V\) gives a power-saving upper bound relative to \(x/g\) exactly when
\[
 \gamma\ge0\quad\hbox{and}\quad
 \gamma>\max(\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2,\Gamma_3,\Gamma_4,\Gamma_5)+O_\epsilon(1),
\]
where the positive epsilon-dependent buffer tends to zero with the theorem's epsilon, and
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \Gamma_1&=(7\beta+5\nu-8)/8,\\
 \Gamma_2&=(9\beta+4\nu-10)/8,\\
 \Gamma_3&=(16\beta+10\nu-17)/19,\\
 \Gamma_4&=(20\beta+7\nu-21)/17,\\
 \Gamma_5&=(11\beta+\nu-12)/8.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus \(\gamma=0\) is included whenever all five raw thresholds are strictly negative by more than the chosen epsilon buffer. For the affine Bettin--Chandee term \(\Gamma_{\rm BC}^{\rm aff}(\beta)=(19\beta-20)/17\),
\[
 \Gamma_4-\Gamma_{\rm BC}^{\rm aff}(\beta)=\frac{\beta+7\nu-1}{17}.
\]
Consequently, throughout \(\beta\ge1,\nu\ge0\), the pointwise-in-\(v\) Wright bound supplies no \(\gamma\)-range beyond the effective fixed-\(g\) Bettin--Chandee condition
\[
 \gamma\ge0,qquad \gamma>\Gamma_{\rm BC}^{\rm aff}(\beta)+O_\epsilon(1).
\]
Equality in the raw fourth-term comparison occurs only at \((\beta,\nu)=(1,0)\).

Wright's proof treats \(R_W\) as fixed. It contains no estimate for a coefficient-weighted family with varying \(R_W\), and in particular no cross-\(v\) Gram estimate. Consequently the following is only a hypothetical bridge, not a consequence of the cited paper: a vector-\(R_W\) extension which replaces the outer \(V^{1+\epsilon}\) triangle tax by \(V^{1/2+\epsilon}\), while retaining the five Wright summands and the literal coefficient norms. Such a bridge would change the five raw thresholds to
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \Gamma_1^{\rm vec}&=(7\beta+\nu-8)/8,&
 \Gamma_2^{\rm vec}&=(9\beta-10)/8,\\
 \Gamma_3^{\rm vec}&=(16\beta-17)/19,&
 \Gamma_4^{\rm vec}&=(20\beta-3\nu-21)/17,\\
 \Gamma_5^{\rm vec}&=(11\beta-3\nu-12)/8.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Its fourth raw threshold is below the affine Bettin--Chandee term precisely when \(\nu>(\beta-1)/3\). In the actual lane \(\gamma\ge0\), this can yield an effective fourth-term improvement over the floored Bettin--Chandee boundary only when \(\beta>20/19\), and then precisely under the same inequality. This identifies only a possible subband: the other four vector thresholds, applicability conditions, and all literal taxes would still have to be checked.
a4065b4002385422.proof:
Wright's Theorem 2.1 states, for \(M_W\ll N_W^2\) and \(R_W\ll M_W^C\) with fixed \(C\), that the trilinear Kloosterman-fraction form is at most
\[
 Q^\epsilon\|\alpha\|_2\|\zeta\|_2\|\xi\|_2
 (A_W M_W N_W)^{1/2}R_W^{1/4}
 \left(1+\frac{|\vartheta|A_W}{M_W N_W}\right)^{1/4}
\]
times
\[
 N_W^{-1/8}+R_W^{1/8}N_W^{1/8}M_W^{-1/4}
 +M_W^{1/10}R_W^{-3/20}A_W^{-1/20}N_W^{-3/20}
 +N_W^{3/20}A_W^{-3/20}M_W^{-1/5}
 +N_W^{3/8}M_W^{-1/2}.
\]
The final display in the paper's proof has the stronger exponent \(A_W^{-3/10}\) in its third summand, whereas the theorem statement has \(A_W^{-1/20}\). Since here \(A_W=H_P\ge1\), the stronger displayed proof term is bounded by the theorem-statement term used above.

Facts 0576f567200d41f1 and f7b5ba9fa0d6cfc8 pay the prime-product multiplicity, divisor-bounded coefficients, collisions, and the projective separation of the literal smooth masks at a cost \(Q^\epsilon\). Hence for fixed \(v\),
\[
 \|\alpha\|_2\ll Q^{1/2+\epsilon},\qquad
 \|\zeta\|_2\ll P^{1/2+\epsilon},\qquad
 \|\xi\|_2\ll H_P^{1/2+\epsilon}.
\]
Moreover
\[
 \frac{|Lsrc|H_P}{QP}
 \ll \frac{G_*Q^2\,Q^{\beta-1-\gamma}}{Q\,Q^{\beta-\nu}}
 =Q^\nu=V.
\]
Thus the theorem's explicit \(R_W^{1/4}\) and Archimedean amplifier together cost at most \(V^{1/2}\). Multiplication by the literal Poisson prefactor \(H_P^{-1}\), the three coefficient norms, and the theorem's factor \((H_P Q P)^{1/2}\) leaves \(QPV^{1/2}\). The outer triangle inequality over the divisor-bounded \(v\)-coefficients costs \(V^{1+\epsilon}\). The common prefactor is therefore
\[
 QPV^{3/2}=Q^{1+\beta+\nu/2}.
\]

Substitution of \((M_W,N_W,R_W,A_W)=(Q,P,V,H_P)\) gives the following five total \(Q\)-exponents before comparison with \(x/g\asymp Q^{2+\gamma}\):
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_1&=1+7\beta/8+5\nu/8,\\
 E_2&=3/4+9\beta/8+\nu/2,\\
 E_3&=23/20+4\beta/5+\nu/2+\gamma/20,\\
 E_4&=19/20+\beta+7\nu/20+3\gamma/20,\\
 E_5&=1/2+11\beta/8+\nu/8.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Solving \(E_j<2+\gamma\) gives exactly \(\gamma>\Gamma_j\). The lane hypothesis supplies the separate weak inequality \(\gamma\ge0\). Therefore the precise simultaneous condition is \(\gamma\ge0\) together with \(\gamma>\max_j\Gamma_j\), plus the arbitrarily small positive theorem-epsilon buffer; zero is not inserted into the strict maximum. Fact 7131a06664967733 gives the fixed-\(g\) Bettin--Chandee condition \(\gamma\ge0\) and \(\gamma>(19\beta-20)/17\), with the same convention at a negative affine threshold. Since
\[
 \Gamma_4-(19\beta-20)/17=(\beta+7\nu-1)/17\ge0,
\]
the pointwise Wright range is contained in the BC range.

Finally, Wright's proof fixes \(R_W\), decomposes square-free divisors of that fixed integer, estimates the resulting fixed-\(R_W\) quadratic quantity, and applies Cauchy--Schwarz only after \(R_W\) has been fixed. There is no outer coefficient sequence indexed by \(R_W\), no sum over two distinct values of \(R_W\), and hence no off-diagonal cross-\(R_W\) Gram. The proposed vector bridge is therefore an additional theorem. Replacing only the outer tax \(V\) by \(V^{1/2}\) lowers every \(E_j\) by \(\nu/2\). Solving again gives the five \(\Gamma_j^{\rm vec}\). In particular
\[
 \Gamma_4^{\rm vec}-\Gamma_{\rm BC}^{\rm aff}(\beta)
 =\frac{\beta-3\nu-1}{17},
\]
which is negative exactly for \(\nu>(\beta-1)/3\). If \(\beta\le20/19\), the effective BC boundary in the lane \(\gamma\ge0\) is already zero, so lowering a raw threshold below zero does not enlarge the effective range. If \(\beta>20/19\), the effective and affine BC boundaries coincide, proving the final scoped comparison.

a411252e2c6ac7a7.title: CRT-coherent saturation and prime-imbalance scale of the scoped four-prime C4 kernel. Let D=p_1p_2p_3p_4, where p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4 are distinct primes satisfying 11<=p_1<p_2<p_3<p_4. Let v be a positive squarefree integer with gcd(D,v)=1, put n=Dv, and let A be an integer with gcd(A,D)=1. For each prime p dividing D, choose t modulo p by
a411252e2c6ac7a7.author: slava chan
a411252e2c6ac7a7.statement:
CRT-coherent saturation and prime-imbalance scale of the scoped four-prime C4 kernel. Let D=p_1p_2p_3p_4, where p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4 are distinct primes satisfying 11<=p_1<p_2<p_3<p_4. Let v be a positive squarefree integer with gcd(D,v)=1, put n=Dv, and let A be an integer with gcd(A,D)=1. For each prime p dividing D, choose t modulo p by
t == (n/p)A^{-1} (mod p),
and let t be the least positive integer in the resulting Chinese-remainder residue class modulo D. For the primitive ray rho=(1,1,t), the local phases and active factors from fact 34d306bcb630f9df satisfy
zeta_p(rho)=e_p(1),    Gamma_p(rho)=e_p(1)+1/(p-1).
Consequently its six-sibling kernel
K_{2,D,v}(rho)=sum_{S subset {p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4}, |S|=2} (product_{p in S} Gamma_p(rho))(product_{p dividing D, p notin S}(-1/p))
obeys
cos(4pi/11) sum_{1<=i<j<=4} 1/(p_ip_j)
 <= Re K_{2,D,v}(rho)
 <= |K_{2,D,v}(rho)|
 <= 8 sum_{1<=i<j<=4} 1/(p_ip_j).
In particular, if I(D)=p_3p_4/(p_1p_2), then
cos(4pi/11)^2 I(D)/D <= |K_{2,D,v}(rho)|^2 <= 48^2 I(D)/D.
The full kernel including the small-v unit phase has the same absolute value. Thus the six-sibling recombination does not by itself provide a uniform constant multiple of D^{-1/2} for arbitrary primitive-ray residues: when I(D) is large, this CRT-coherent residue has magnitude larger than D^{-1/2} by a constant multiple of I(D)^{1/2}. This is an algebraic obstruction only; the constructed least positive t need not belong to the literal short b-range of the C4 boxes.
a411252e2c6ac7a7.proof:
We use the primitive-ray phase and kernel identity in fact 34d306bcb630f9df.

For every p dividing D, the integer n/p is invertible modulo p because D is squarefree and gcd(D,v)=1. The integer A is also invertible modulo p. Hence the four displayed congruences determine one residue class t modulo D by the Chinese remainder theorem. For rho=(epsilon,a,b)=(1,1,t), fact 34d306bcb630f9df gives
zeta_p(rho)=e_p(A epsilon b [a(n/p)]^{-1}).
The defining congruence for t makes the argument congruent to 1 modulo p, so zeta_p(rho)=e_p(1). The same predecessor gives Gamma_p(rho)=zeta_p(rho)+1/(p-1), proving the first formulas.

Fix a two-element active subset S. Since the other two inactive factors have product positive, its contribution is
(product_{p in S} Gamma_p(rho))/(product_{p dividing D, p notin S}p).
If S={p_i,p_j}, then
Re(Gamma_{p_i}Gamma_{p_j})
=cos(2pi/p_i+2pi/p_j)
 +cos(2pi/p_i)/(p_j-1)
 +cos(2pi/p_j)/(p_i-1)
 +1/((p_i-1)(p_j-1)).
All four terms after the equality sign are nonnegative. Moreover,
0<2pi/p_i+2pi/p_j<=4pi/11<pi,
and cosine is decreasing on [0,pi], so the first term is at least cos(4pi/11)>0. Therefore every one of the six sibling contributions lies in the same open right half-plane and has real part at least cos(4pi/11) divided by its inactive prime product. As complementation permutes the two-element subsets of the four primes, summing gives
Re K_{2,D,v}(rho)>=cos(4pi/11) sum_{1<=i<j<=4}1/(p_ip_j).

Also |Gamma_p(rho)|<=1+1/(p-1)<=11/10. Thus each sibling term has magnitude at most 121/100 times the reciprocal of its inactive prime product. The triangle inequality and 121/100<8 give
|K_{2,D,v}(rho)|<=8 sum_{1<=i<j<=4}1/(p_ip_j).
The middle inequality Re K<=|K| is general.

Because p_1<p_2<p_3<p_4, the largest reciprocal pair is 1/(p_1p_2). Hence
1/(p_1p_2) <= sum_{i<j}1/(p_ip_j) <= 6/(p_1p_2).
Combining this with the preceding bounds yields
cos(4pi/11)/(p_1p_2)<=|K_{2,D,v}(rho)|<=48/(p_1p_2).
Squaring and using the exact identity
I(D)/D=[p_3p_4/(p_1p_2)]/[p_1p_2p_3p_4]=1/(p_1^2p_2^2)
proves the claimed prime-imbalance bounds.

Finally, fact 34d306bcb630f9df states that the full kernel differs from K_{2,D,v}(rho) only by the small-v phase e_v(A epsilon b(aD)^{-1}), which has absolute value one. Its magnitude is therefore unchanged. Since I(D) is unbounded over ordered quadruples of distinct primes, no uniform constant upper bound |K_{2,D,v}(rho)|<=C D^{-1/2} can follow from the six-term algebra alone. The last sentence merely records that CRT supplies a residue modulo D, not membership in any prescribed short interval for b, so this construction is not asserted to be a literal-box counterexample.

glossary.p_4: The largest of the four distinct prime factors used in the statement.
glossary.t: The least positive CRT representative specified in the statement.

a487dc8975ea1d2b.title: SUB-SQUARE-ROOT GEOMETRIC NO-FIT FOR THE SEPARATED MEDIUM-FACTOR SUPPLIER. Let Q>=1. Let U,Y,m_eff be positive real numbers. Suppose integers u,y satisfy
a487dc8975ea1d2b.author: slava chan
a487dc8975ea1d2b.statement:
SUB-SQUARE-ROOT GEOMETRIC NO-FIT FOR THE SEPARATED MEDIUM-FACTOR SUPPLIER. Let Q>=1. Let U,Y,m_eff be positive real numbers. Suppose integers u,y satisfy
U<=u<2U,  Y<=y<2Y,  Q<=uy<2Q.                                 (1)
If the scale hypotheses
U<=m_eff,  4Y<m_eff                                             (2)
of fact b390149c13836271 hold, then necessarily
m_eff>Q^(1/2).                                                   (3)
Consequently, in the literal composite C1 row of fact 79ffbcb2ffe4049f, no grouping of a Q-scale product q=uy can satisfy the hypotheses of fact b390149c13836271 when
1<m_eff<=Q^(1/2).
This is a theorem-hypothesis no-fit only. It leaves the transition range
Q^(1/2)<m_eff<Q^(1/2+kappa)
and does not rule out the free-factor Type-I supplier, the factorable-modulus A-process, or a source/modulus aggregate.
a487dc8975ea1d2b.proof:
From (1) and the upper dyadic bounds u<2U, y<2Y one obtains
Q<=uy<4UY,
so
Q<4UY.                                                          (4)
From (2) one has
4UY<U m_eff<=m_eff^2.                                          (5)
Combining (4)-(5) gives Q<m_eff^2, which is equivalent to (3).

Fact b390149c13836271 requires exactly the two scale inequalities in (2) for any separated grouping to which it is applied. Every nonzero term of the literal q-sum has q=uy in [Q,2Q), so (1) holds after dyadic subdivision. Therefore m_eff<=Q^(1/2) is incompatible with that theorem's hypotheses for every grouping. No assertion about the actual exponential sum or about another supplier has been made.

glossary.sub-square-root effective-modulus chambe: The range 1<m_eff<=Q^(1/2) for a reciprocal-modulus variable supported on the Q-scale.

a4c3df18327fbfb1.title: FIXED-POWER PAYMENT OF THE LARGE-SHARED-PRIME PART OF THE LITERAL CROSS-INCIDENCE REMAINDER
a4c3df18327fbfb1.author: slava chan
a4c3df18327fbfb1.statement:
FIXED-POWER PAYMENT OF THE LARGE-SHARED-PRIME PART OF THE LITERAL CROSS-INCIDENCE REMAINDER.

Fix 0<eta<1/12 and theta>0. Let Q tend to infinity and put
 U=Q^(1/3), B=Q^(4/3+o(1)),
 F_0=Q^(1-2eta+o(1)), P_0=Q^(1/2+theta).                   (1)
Let cal B be the squarefree b with B<=b<2B. Put
 L_b=product_{r|b;b/r<F_0}r.                                (2)
Let cal R consist of b with L_b>1 and (L_b,N)=1, for a fixed positive integer N. For b in cal R let pi(b) be the largest prime factor of L_b and put s(b)=b/pi(b). Define
 cal D_{>=P_0}
 ={(b_1,b_2) in cal R^2:
      p=pi(b_1)>=P_0, p|s(b_2)}.                          (3)
For a pair in (3) put s_1=b_1/p and q_2=b_2/p. Let gamma_b be complex numbers satisfying
 sum_{b in cal R}|gamma_b|^2<=1.                            (4)

For each tau in a set of at most two elements, let a range over a<=2U and let beta_{tau,a}(u) be supported on
 cal U_a={u:Q<=au<2Q}                                    (5)
and satisfy, for every epsilon>0,
 |beta_{tau,a}(u)|<=Q^epsilon.                              (6)
Assume kernels mathcal R_{a,u_1,u_2;b_1,b_2} satisfy
 |mathcal R_{a,u_1,u_2;b_1,b_2}|
 <=Q^epsilon{1_{u_1s_1 congruent u_2q_2 (mod p)}+1/p}.    (7)
Put
 mathcal K_{>=P_0}
 =sum_tau sum_{a<=2U}sum_{u_1,u_2 in cal U_a}
   sum_{(b_1,b_2) in cal D_{>=P_0}}
   beta_{tau,a}(u_1)overline(beta_{tau,a}(u_2))
   overline(gamma_{b_1})gamma_{b_2}
   mathcal R_{a,u_1,u_2;b_1,b_2}.                           (8)
Then
 |mathcal K_{>=P_0}|
 <<Q^(7/3-2theta+epsilon+o(1))
   +Q^(11/6-theta+epsilon+o(1)).                            (9)

The exact K_inc^rem of fact b9560e346963b9e0, restricted to p>=P_0 and to any actual tensor in fact 050efa07f87f374a, is an instance of (8). Consequently, after choosing epsilon<theta, this complete literal large-p remainder is O(Q^(7/3-omega_theta)) for some fixed omega_theta>0. The exact product-coupled Vaughan coefficient, both gamma factors, row-one shifted projector, row-two full-conductor response and literal boundary are retained.

No estimate for p<P_0, K_inc^main, another incidence cell, TRI-CROSS, ROP, CEN-MZB, C_small or Goldbach is asserted.
a4c3df18327fbfb1.proof:
For each p in (3), put
 cal B_1(p)={b in cal R:pi(b)=p},quad
 cal B_2(p)={b in cal R:p|s(b)},
and g_i(p)^2=sum_{b in cal B_i(p)}|gamma_b|^2.               (10)
Both sets contain multiples of p, hence
 #cal B_i(p)<=3B/p                                          (11)
for large Q. Cauchy's inequality gives
 sum_{b_1 in cal B_1(p),b_2 in cal B_2(p)}
 |gamma_{b_1}gamma_{b_2}|
 <=3B/p,g_1(p)g_2(p).                                     (12)
The first-row sets are disjoint, so sum_p g_1(p)^2<=1 by (4).

Every p appearing in cal B_2(p) is pi(b_1) for some b_1 and therefore
 p>B/F_0=Q^(1/3+2eta+o(1)).                                 (13)
A squarefree b<2B has at most three prime factors above B/F_0, since four would have product
 >(B/F_0)^4=Q^(4/3+8eta+o(1))>2B.
Thus each b belongs to at most three cal B_2(p), so
 sum_p g_2(p)^2<=3.                                         (14)
Cauchy's inequality in p gives
 sum_p g_1(p)g_2(p)<=sqrt(3).                               (15)

Let V_a=#cal U_a. Since a<=2U,
 V_a<=2Q/a.                                                 (16)
The squarefree cofactors s_1,q_2 are units modulo p. Hence the congruence in (7) has, for each u_1, at most V_a/p+1 choices of u_2:
 #{u_1,u_2 in cal U_a:u_1s_1=u_2q_2 (mod p)}
 <=V_a^2/p+V_a.                                             (17)
Equations (6)-(8),(12) give
 |mathcal K_{>=P_0}|
 <<Q^epsilon B sum_{p>=P_0}g_1(p)g_2(p)
 left{
 {1over p}sum_{a<=2U}(V_a^2/p+V_a)
 +{1over p^2}sum_{a<=2U}V_a^2
 ight}.                                                  (18)
Here the first 1/p is the incidence edge mass in (12); the bracket contains the congruence and 1/p kernel parts. From (16),
 sum_{a<=2U}V_a^2<<Q^2,qquad
 sum_{a<=2U}V_a<<Q log Q.                                  (19)
Use p>=P_0 and (15) in (18):
 |mathcal K_{>=P_0}|
 <<Q^(epsilon+o(1))
 {BQ^2/P_0^2+BQlog Q/P_0}.                              (20)
Substitution of (1) proves (9).

For the literal application, fact b9560e346963b9e0 gives the exact remainder kernel
 C_1left[
 {e_p(-Da^{-1})over p-1}overline{H_2}
 +{G_p(A,D)+(ho_p(A;a)+ho_p(-D;a))/(p-1)}
  overline{J_2}ight].                                    (21)
Each centered local response is at most 1+1/(r-1), so a squarefree product is at most q/phi(q)<<Q^epsilon. Each squarefree Ramanujan ratio satisfies |c_k(M)|/phi(k)<=1, and there are Q^epsilon divisors. Therefore
 |C_1|+|H_2|+|J_2|<<Q^epsilon.                              (22)
Also |rho_p|<=2, (p-1)^(-1)<=2/p, and
 |G_p(A,D)|<=2,1_{A=D}+2/p.                               (23)
The literal indices A=N(u_1s_1)^(-1), D=N(u_2q_2)^(-1) and p not dividing N give
 A=D iff u_1s_1 congruent u_2q_2 (mod p).                  (24)
Thus (21)-(24) prove (7).

It remains to justify (6) for the actual coefficient. Fact 050efa07f87f374a states that every actual tensor coefficient alpha_n is bounded by Q^(o(1)) and contains the literal mu(n) factor. Fact b3c1cdc5cb47ae63 writes this same coefficient exactly as
 alpha_n=mu(n)w_n.                                          (25)
If alpha_n is nonzero, its literal support has mu(n) nonzero, so |w_n|=|alpha_n|; define w_n=0 off that support. Hence |w_n|<=Q^(o(1)). The formulas in b9560e346963b9e0 are
 beta_{ss,a}(u)=mu(a)w_{au}sum_{m|u;m<=U}mu(m),
 beta_{ll,a}(u)=w_{au}sum_{dm=u;U<d<=m}kappa(d,m)mu(d)mu(m).
Divisor bounds now give (6).

Finally, b9560e346963b9e0 assumes sum over all b in cal B of |gamma_b|^2=1. Restricting its sum to cal R gives exactly hypothesis (4), not an equality requirement. Therefore the restricted literal K_inc^rem is an instance of (8), completing the proof.

glossary.cal D_{>=P_0}: the directed cross-incidence pairs with shared prime p at least P_0
glossary.cal U_a: the complementary product variables satisfying Q<=au<2Q
glossary.g_1(p): the restricted l2 gamma mass on canonical-p rows
glossary.g_2(p): the restricted l2 gamma mass on rows whose canonical complement contains p
glossary.mathcal R_{a,u_1,u_2;b_1,b_2}: a kernel with the Gram congruence plus 1/p envelope

a547a4eea4d234ef.title: MULTI-PRIME SUPPORT OF THE ROW-ONE SHIFTED PROJECTOR IN THE SMALL-SHARED-PRIME CROSS-INCIDENCE RANGE
a547a4eea4d234ef.author: slava chan
a547a4eea4d234ef.statement:
MULTI-PRIME SUPPORT OF THE ROW-ONE SHIFTED PROJECTOR IN THE SMALL-SHARED-PRIME CROSS-INCIDENCE RANGE.

Let F_0>1 and let b_1 be squarefree. Put
 L_{b_1}=product_{r|b_1;b_1/r<F_0}r,                        (1)
assume L_{b_1}>1, let p be the largest prime divisor of L_{b_1}, and put
 s_1=b_1/p.                                                 (2)
Then p is the largest prime divisor of b_1. In particular,
 r<=pqquad(r|s_1, r prime).                               (3)

Let M_1 be any integer and let the shifted centered projector be
 P^{M_1}_{s_1,>F_0/p}(a)
 =sum_{substack{h|s_1\h>F_0/p\(h,M_1)=1}}
  c_{s_1/h}(M_1)R^{M_1}_{s_1,h}(a)/phi(s_1/h),              (4)
where (a,s_1)=1 and
 R^{M_1}_{s_1,h}(a)
  =product_{r|h}
    [e_r(M_1[a(s_1/r)]^(-1))+1/(r-1)].                      (5)
If k>=1 is an integer and
 p^(k+1)<=F_0,                                               (6)
then every active conductor h in (4) satisfies
 omega(h)>=k+1.                                              (7)
In particular, if p^2<=F_0, the projector (4) has no prime-conductor face: every active h has at least two prime factors.

At the actual scales F_0=Q^(1-2eta+o(1)), this applies throughout
 p<=Q^(1/2-eta+o(1)). Thus the unresolved row-one modulation below the square-root transition is genuinely multi-prime before any rough/smooth factorization. No estimate for that tensor, K_inc^rem, K_inc^main, TRI-CROSS, ROP, CEN-MZB, C_small or Goldbach is asserted.
a547a4eea4d234ef.proof:
Let r be a prime divisor of b_1. If r|L_{b_1}, then r<=p because p is the largest prime divisor of L_{b_1}. If r does not divide L_{b_1}, the negation of the strict condition in (1) gives
 b_1/r>=F_0.
On the other hand, p|L_{b_1} gives
 b_1/p<F_0.
Combining these inequalities yields r<=b_1/F_0<p. Therefore every prime divisor of b_1 is at most p, proving that p is its largest prime divisor and proving (3).

Fix an active h in (4). If omega(h)<=k, squarefreeness and (3) give
 h<=p^k.
Under (6),
 p^k<=F_0/p.
This contradicts the strict activity condition h>F_0/p. Hence omega(h)>=k+1, proving (7). The case k=1 gives the prime-face assertion.

Finally, F_0=Q^(1-2eta+o(1)) implies
 F_0^(1/2)=Q^(1/2-eta+o(1)).
Thus p<=F_0^(1/2) is exactly the displayed actual range, up to the inherited o(1). The conclusion is structural only.

glossary.omega(h): the number of distinct prime divisors of the squarefree conductor h
glossary.prime-conductor face: a term in the shifted projector whose active conductor h is prime

a5a0d069b689bb5a.title: TWO-SCALE RECTANGULAR IMPORTANCE-SAMPLED IJOP PUSHFORWARD
a5a0d069b689bb5a.author: slava chan
a5a0d069b689bb5a.statement:
TWO-SCALE RECTANGULAR IMPORTANCE-SAMPLED IJOP PUSHFORWARD.

There are absolute constants c_0,C_0>0 with the following property. Let X be a sufficiently large positive integer and let Y be an integer with Y>=4X. Let r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4 be pairwise distinct primes such that
r_1,r_4 in [Y^2,2Y^2),    r_2,r_3 in [X^2,2X^2),
and put P=r_1r_2r_3r_4. Consider integer quadruples bold c=(c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4) satisfying
1<=c_1<=Y/16,
7X/8<=c_2<=X,
-X<=c_3<=-7X/8,
c_2 not congruent to c_3 modulo 2,
and 0<|c_4|<=Y.
Define
B=c_1r_2+c_2r_1,    D=c_3r_4+c_4r_3,
C=Br_3r_4+r_1r_2D,  m=c_2r_3-c_3r_2.
Let mathcal E_XY be the set of these quadruples for which
gcd(m,BD)=1    and    |C|>=X^4Y^3/4,
and put N_XY=|mathcal E_XY|. Then
N_XY>=c_0 X^2Y^2/(log(2XY))^2.                              (1)
Consequently
omega_XY=phi(P)/(X^2Y^2N_XY)
satisfies
0<omega_XY<=C_0(log(2XY))^2.                                (2)

Fix one paired-selector-supported full four-prime Ramanujan face whose ordered supports place r_1,r_4 in the Y-cell and r_2,r_3 in the X-cell, and let A_prov be its complete labelled provenance coefficient, independent of the auxiliary primitive residue. Put alpha=phi(P)/P. Then
(X^2Y^2)^(-1)sum_{rho in U_P}A_prov
 =omega_XY sum_{bold c in mathcal E_XY}A_prov,                (3)
alpha A_prov
 =(X^2Y^2/P)omega_XY sum_{bold c in mathcal E_XY}A_prov.      (4)
Thus (4) is an exact bounded-weight importance-sampled reopening of the rectangular full face.

Every sampled quadruple has the following exact two-scale decoder pushforward. Define
E=c_2r_4+c_4r_2,  F=c_1r_3+c_3r_1,
u=c_1r_4-c_4r_1,
a=-2D,  b=2B,  c=-2E,  d=2F,
n_1=-d,  n_2=b,  K_dec=(ab+cd)/2.                            (5)
Let u_0 be the representative of u modulo m in {0,...,m-1} and put
k=2(u-u_0)/m.
Then
a n_2=K_dec+2mu_0+km^2,   c n_1=a n_2-2K_dec,                (6)
(br_3-dr_2)/(2m)=r_1,     (ar_2-cr_3)/(2m)=r_4,              (7)
(ab-cd)/(4m)=u,                                               (8)
u congruent to u_0 modulo m,    k=2(u-u_0)/m,                 (9)
d r_2r_4-c r_3r_1=2C.                                       (10)
Moreover
7X^3/4<=m<=4X^3,                                             (11)
m is odd, n_1,n_2 and a are positive even integers, c is even,
max(|a|,|c|,n_1,n_2)<=6XY^2,                                (12)
X^4Y^3/4<=|C|<=25X^3Y^4,    |K_dec|<=36X^2Y^4,              (13)
gcd(m,r_2r_3)=1,  gcd(C,P)=1,  u is nonzero, and
gcd(m,2K_dec)=1.                                              (14)
The recovered corners in (7) are precisely the two Y-scale primes r_1,r_4.

For each fixed ordered prime quadruple, the map
bold c maps to (m(bold c),C(bold c))
is injective on mathcal E_XY. Thus the rectangular importance samples remain distinct exact (m,C,K_dec) fibres when the ordered support pair is retained.

This theorem constructs a pointwise two-scale rectangular localization and exact density identity only. It does not supply an analytic estimate for the resulting varying fibres. In particular it is not a direct instance of fact d4402b645abcaf56: that theorem requires all four primes in one interval [H^2,2H^2), whereas the present two prime scales are disjoint, and the natural common coefficient intervals in (12) have cardinality O(XY^2) while m is comparable to X^3, producing the ratio O((Y/X)^2), not a fixed interval-to-m constant when Y/X grows. No source projective norm, rectangular carrier cancellation, common-cell or cross-cell bound, total-deficit capture, or Goldbach implication is asserted.
a5a0d069b689bb5a.proof:
Fix c_2,c_3 in the displayed intervals with opposite parity. There are at least cX^2 such ordered pairs for an absolute c>0. Since r_2,r_3 are odd,
m=c_2r_3-c_3r_2
is odd. Both terms are positive, and the scale bounds give
7X^3/4<=m<=4X^3.
Modulo r_2 one has m congruent to c_2r_3, and modulo r_3 one has m congruent to -c_3r_2. Since 0<c_2,|c_3|<r_2,r_3 and the two primes are distinct, gcd(m,r_2r_3)=1.

We use the elementary interval sieve proved in fact dcabcf2f566b5721: if n>=3, I is an interval of L consecutive integers, and gcd(A,n)=1, then
#{t in I:gcd(At+B,n)=1}
 =L phi(n)/n+O(2^{omega(n)}).                                (15)
The same fact proves n/phi(n)<<log(2n) and 2^{omega(n)}=n^{o(1)}. Apply (15) with n=m, A=r_2, and c_1 in [1,Y/16]. Since Y>=4X and m<=4X^3, for sufficiently large X there are
>>Y/log(2XY)
choices of c_1 for which gcd(m,B)=1.

Fix one such c_1. As a function of c_4,
C=C_*+r_1r_2r_3c_4.
Let t_*=-C_*/(r_1r_2r_3). The closed Y/4-neighborhoods of the two endpoint intervals
[-Y,-3Y/4] and [3Y/4,Y]
are disjoint. Hence at least one of these intervals has distance at least Y/4 from t_*. On that interval,
|C|>=r_1r_2r_3Y/4>=X^4Y^3/4.                               (16)
Apply (15) on this chosen interval with n=m, A=r_3, and the affine form D=c_3r_4+c_4r_3. It supplies
>>Y/log(2XY)
choices of c_4 satisfying gcd(m,D)=1. These choices are nonzero and satisfy (16). Thus each of the >>X^2 initial pairs contributes
>>Y^2/(log(2XY))^2
eligible quadruples. This proves (1).

Since
P<16X^4Y^4,
equation (1) and phi(P)<=P give
omega_XY<=C(log(2XY))^2,
proving (2).

The full primitive face has
alpha=P^(-1)sum_{rho in U_P}1.
The coefficient A_prov is independent of rho and of the auxiliary sample. By definition,
omega_XY N_XY=phi(P)/(X^2Y^2).
These two equalities prove (3), and multiplication by X^2Y^2/P proves (4). Modulo r_i, the carrier C is congruent to c_iP/r_i. Every c_i is nonzero with absolute value less than r_i, so each sampled quadruple gives a primitive residue modulo P.

We now prove the pushforward identities by direct expansion. The definitions give
br_3-dr_2=2r_1(c_2r_3-c_3r_2)=2mr_1,
ar_2-cr_3=2r_4(c_2r_3-c_3r_2)=2mr_4.                        (17)
They also give
br_3r_4-ar_1r_2=dr_2r_4-cr_1r_3=2C,                         (18)
br_4+cr_1=2ur_2,    dr_4+ar_1=2ur_3,                         (19)
and
ab=K_dec+2mu,   cd=K_dec-2mu,   ab-cd=4mu.                  (20)
Writing u=u_0+(u-u_0) in the first identity of (20) proves (6), while (17), (20), and the second equality in (18) prove (7)-(10). Since m is odd, u-u_0 is divisible by m and k=2(u-u_0)/m is an even integer, hence an integer.

We verify the signs and sizes. Because Y>=4X,
B>=7XY^2/8>0,
F<=YX^2/8-7XY^2/8<0,
D<=-7XY^2/8+2YX^2<=-3XY^2/8<0.
Thus n_1=-2F, n_2=2B, and a=-2D are positive even integers. The direct upper bounds
|B|,|D|,|E|,|F|<=3XY^2
prove (12). Equation (16) gives the lower carrier bound. Expanding C as
C=sum_{i=1}^4 c_iP/r_i
and inserting the four boxes gives |C|<=25X^3Y^4. The coefficient bound in (12) gives |K_dec|<=36X^2Y^4. This proves (11)-(13).

We already proved gcd(m,r_2r_3)=1. Since C is congruent to c_iP/r_i modulo r_i and every c_i is a unit modulo r_i, gcd(C,P)=1. If u=0, then c_1r_4=c_4r_1. The distinct prime r_1 would divide c_1, contrary to 1<=c_1<r_1. Hence u is nonzero. Finally m is odd. If an odd prime ell divided both m and K_dec, the first identity in (20) would give ell dividing ab=-4BD, contradicting gcd(m,BD)=1. Hence gcd(m,2K_dec)=1, proving (14).

For injectivity, suppose bold c and bold c' have the same m and C, and write delta_i=c_i-c_i'. Equality of m gives
delta_2r_3=delta_3r_2.
Coprimality of the distinct primes implies r_2 divides delta_2 and r_3 divides delta_3. But |delta_2|<=X/8<r_2, so delta_2=delta_3=0. Equality of C then reduces, after division by r_2r_3, to
delta_1r_4+delta_4r_1=0.
Thus r_1 divides delta_1 and r_4 divides delta_4. Since |delta_1|<=Y/16<r_1, both vanish. Hence bold c=bold c', proving injectivity.

The final no-fit assertion is a direct comparison of hypotheses. The X-scale and Y-scale prime intervals are disjoint when Y>=4X, so no single H can place all four primes in [H^2,2H^2). Also (11)-(12) give the displayed coefficient-length to m ratio. No analytic estimate was used.

glossary.K_dec: The decoder determinant parameter (ab+cd)/2 in the two-scale pushforward.
glossary.X: The square-root scale of the two smaller rough primes.
glossary.Y: The square-root scale of the two larger rough primes.
glossary.mathcal E_XY: The eligible two-scale auxiliary residue sample set.
glossary.omega_XY: The exact two-scale importance weight phi(P)/(X^2Y^2N_XY).

a5f73e19fca8e2d5.title: CORRECTED ONE-CAUCHY FORWARD \(E_{11}\) DILATION, RECONSTRUCTION, CONDUCTOR-SHELL, AND TRACE-RANGE LEDGER. Assume the hypotheses and notation of facts fc442085ff47a053, 75d461ea0320c1a8, and 69e79ebdfba646b4. Write
a5f73e19fca8e2d5.author: slava chan
a5f73e19fca8e2d5.statement:
CORRECTED ONE-CAUCHY FORWARD \(E_{11}\) DILATION, RECONSTRUCTION, CONDUCTOR-SHELL, AND TRACE-RANGE LEDGER. Assume the hypotheses and notation of facts fc442085ff47a053, 75d461ea0320c1a8, and 69e79ebdfba646b4. Write
\[
 \eta=\eta_t,\quad R=D^\beta,\quad
 \frac43\le\beta\le\frac43+6\eta,\quad
 a_E=\frac13-15\eta,\quad
 Y_E=\frac12(R/D)D^{a_E},
\]
and put \(F=F_0\). Let \(\alpha=(\iota,h,p,\ell)\) run over the exact set \(\mathscr A_E\), and put \(r_\alpha=p\ell\).

There are positive \(E_\alpha\) such that, for fixed \(J\ge3\),
\[
 E_\alpha\ll x^\varepsilon\frac{M}{r_\alpha}
 \left(1+\frac{|h|M}{r_\alpha}\right)^{-J},\qquad
 |V_n(\alpha)|\le x^\varepsilon E_\alpha\quad(\mu(n)^2=1), \tag{1}
\]
and
\[
 \mathcal E_E:=\sum_\alpha E_\alpha\ll Rx^\varepsilon.     \tag{2}
\]
Define
\[
 U_n(\alpha)=\frac{\mu(n)^2V_n(\alpha)}{\sqrt{E_\alpha}},
 \qquad r_E(\alpha)=\sqrt{E_\alpha}.                        \tag{3}
\]
Then
\[
 T_{E11}^{>F}
 =\left\langle\sum_{n\le X_E}\mu(n)U_n,r_E\right\rangle,\qquad
 \sup_n\|U_n\|_2+\|r_E\|_2\ll R^{1/2}x^\varepsilon.         \tag{4}
\]

For distinct prime dilators \(a,b\), the exact kernel is
\[
\begin{split}
 \mathfrak K_{a,b}(m)
 ={}&\mu(m)^2{\bf1}_{(ab,m)=1}
 \sum_{\alpha=(\iota,h,p,\ell)}
 \frac{C_\iota(am;h,p,\ell)\overline{C_\iota(bm;h,p,\ell)}}{E_\alpha}\\
 &\times e\!\left(\frac{Nh}{mp\ell}\left(\frac1a-\frac1b\right)\right)
 \Pi_{>F}(am;h,p,\ell)
 \overline{\Pi_{>F}(bm;h,p,\ell)}.                         \tag{5}
\end{split}
\]
Thus both \(\mu(m)^2{\bf1}_{(ab,m)=1}\) and \(E_\alpha^{-1}\) are retained.

For a finite nonempty prime set \(\mathcal P\), put
\[
 L_{\mathcal P}=\sum_{a\in\mathcal P}a^{-1},\qquad
 \mathcal V_{\mathcal P}=|\mathcal P|^2+
 L_{\mathcal P}|\mathcal P|,\qquad
 \mathfrak C_{a,b}=\sum_m\mathfrak K_{a,b}(m).
\]
Then
\[
\begin{split}
 |T_{E11}^{>F}|\le \|r_E\|_2\bigg\{&
 \frac{B X_E^{1/2}}{L_{\mathcal P}}
 \left(\sum_{n\le X_E}
   (\Omega_{\mathcal P}(n)-L_{\mathcal P})^2\right)^{1/2}\\
 &+\frac{\lfloor X_E/P_-\rfloor^{1/2}}{L_{\mathcal P}}
 \left(B^2X_EL_{\mathcal P}
 +\sum_{a\ne b}|\mathfrak C_{a,b}|\right)^{1/2}\bigg\},     \tag{6}
\end{split}
\]
where \(B=\sup_n\|U_n\|_2\) and \(P_-=\min\mathcal P\). There is no \(a\mid m\) error. The variance part of (6) is
\[
 \ll R x^\varepsilon
 \left\{\frac{D}{L_{\mathcal P}^{1/2}}
 +\frac{D^{1/2}\mathcal V_{\mathcal P}^{1/2}}
 {L_{\mathcal P}}\right\}.                                 \tag{7}
\]
If \(L_{\mathcal P}^{-1}=D^{o(1)}\) and
\(\mathcal V_{\mathcal P}\le D L_{\mathcal P}D^{o(1)}\), this becomes
\(RDD^{o(1)}\), which does not furnish \(D^{2-\sigma}\). If the cardinality condition fails, the second term in (7) remains. This is only a no-fit for the displayed upper ledger.

Now bypass the variance by a unique-dilator stratum as in fact 0fd3b33d63081ee3. Let \(P=D^\theta\). A \(D^{2-\sigma}\) diagonal target requires
\[
 \theta\ge2(\beta-1)+2\sigma.                               \tag{8}
\]
On this range, fact 2d553c87dc18dd6c shows that \(a,b\) are automatically coprime to \(mhp\ell\) on the squarefree literal support. Only \(a\mid N\) or \(b\mid N\) is nonclean, and that scalar contribution is
\[
 \ll D^{5/3-2\sigma}x^\varepsilon.                          \tag{9}
\]

On the clean sector, put
\[
 c=(m,h),\qquad q=m/c,\qquad t=h/c,\qquad u=p\ell.
\]
For \(q\ge2\) and every real \(T>0\), define
\[
 \mathcal P_a(T)=\frac1{\phi(q)}
 \sum_{\substack{\psi\ ({\rm mod}\ q)\\
 {\rm cond}(\psi)>T\\({\rm cond}(\psi),N)=1}}
 G_{N,q}(\psi)\psi(t)\overline{\psi(au)}.                  \tag{10}
\]
Then
\[
 \Pi_{>F}(am;h,p,\ell)
 =\mathcal E_a\mathcal P_a(F/a)
 +\frac{\mathcal P_a(F/a)-\mathcal P_a(F)}{a-1},            \tag{11}
\]
and analogously for \(b\). Thus their product has the \(F/a,F/b\) common-core term and three shell corrections carrying \(1/(a-1)\), \(1/(b-1)\), and \(1/((a-1)(b-1))\). For every \(T>0\),
\[
 |\mathcal P_a(T)|\ll_\varepsilon q^\varepsilon.           \tag{12}
\]
Indeed facts adb3b38d14670d3c and 9ef7fac8978ac244 prove (12) for \(T\ge1\), while for \(0<T<1\) one has the exact split
\[
 \mathcal P_a(T)=\mathcal P_a(1)+\frac{c_q(N)}{\phi(q)},    \tag{13}
\]
whose second term has absolute value at most one. The \(q=1\) sector remains separately in (5).

Even the stronger complete-projector phase
\[
 e_{p\ell}\!\left(Nh\,m^{-1}(a^{-1}-b^{-1})\right)         \tag{14}
\]
has no compatible published range. Assume its numerator is a unit modulo \(p\ell\), put \(q_1=\max(p,\ell)\), \(q_2=\min(p,\ell)\), and let \(L_m\ll D/P\). Wu--Xi, arXiv:1603.07060, Theorem 8.1 gives
\[
 \ll L_m^{1+\varepsilon}
 \left\{\left(\frac{q_2}{L_m}\right)^{1/2}
 +\left(\frac{q_1}{L_m^2}\right)^{1/4}\right\}.            \tag{15}
\]
A fixed-power saving requires
\[
 L_m>q_2D^{o(1)},\qquad L_m^2>q_1D^{o(1)},                 \tag{16}
\]
and the literal prime bounds force
\[
 \theta<\beta-1+3\eta.                                     \tag{17}
\]
This is disjoint from (8).

Finite Fourier completion, using Wu--Xi Theorem A.1, gives the self-contained bound
\[
 \ll(p\ell)^{1/2}\log(2p\ell).                              \tag{18}
\]
As \(p\ell\asymp R=D^\beta\), it is nontrivial only if
\[
 \theta<1-\beta/2+o(1),                                    \tag{19}
\]
also disjoint from (8). If the numerator in (14) shares one of \(p,\ell\), the conductor drops to the other prime; Theorem 8.1 with \(J=2\) no longer applies, and completion treats only that degenerate sector.

The true kernel (5), including (11)-(13), the variable \(q=m/(m,h)\), source masks, and \(E_\alpha^{-1}\), is not a direct instance of (15) or (18). With the unique-dilator coefficients \(\lambda_{a,m}\), define
\[
 \mathcal C_{\rm TRUE}(P)
 =\sum_{\substack{a,b\in\mathcal P\\a\ne b}}
 \left|\sum_m\lambda_{a,m}\overline{\lambda_{b,m}}
 \mathfrak K_{a,b}(m)\right|.                              \tag{20}
\]
The sharply delimited sufficient new theorem is
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal C_{\rm TRUE}(P)
 \ll x^\varepsilon\frac{P D^{3-2\sigma}}{R}.}              \tag{21}
\]
Together with (8), (21) implies \(D^{2-\sigma+o(1)}\) for that stratum by fact 4d26de51cb52d44d. Estimate (21) must retain the selector, reciprocal envelope, \(q=1\) sector, all four shell products, and every literal mask. It is unproved. The unique-dilator complement or a joint pre-variance architecture remains separate. No assertion is made for \(E_{21}\), \(E_{22}\), or Goldbach.
a5f73e19fca8e2d5.proof:
1. Envelope and Katai ledger. Equation (15) in fact 69e79ebdfba646b4 gives the coefficient majorant in (1). On \(\mu(n)^2=1\), \(Q_n=n/(n,h)\) is squarefree, so facts adb3b38d14670d3c and 9ef7fac8978ac244 give the projector bound \(Q_n^\varepsilon\). The \(h\)-sum in fact 7fa6e823cd299d09 is \(O(1)\) after multiplication by \(M/(p\ell)\), and fact fc442085ff47a053 gives \(O(R)\) ordered pairs and only polylogarithmic label loss. This proves (1)-(2). Facts eeb2a1f90b2a4cb2 and cf6e2f624d3b1a82 prove (3)-(4); fact 1813c7a42cfeab55 shows the split is optimal among positive diagonal envelope rescalings.

Expanding (3) and using
\[
 \mu(am)^2\mu(bm)^2
 =\mu(m)^2{\bf1}_{(ab,m)=1}
\]
proves (5). Apply fact eeb2a1f90b2a4cb2 directly to \(U_n\). Its further squarefree mask is idempotent:
\(\mu(n)^2U_n=U_n\), and its correlation selector multiplied by
\(\langle U_{am},U_{bm}\rangle\) leaves that inner product unchanged because it already vanishes off the selector. This proves (6).

The verified variance is at most
\(X_EL_{\mathcal P}+O(\mathcal V_{\mathcal P})\).
Insert \(B,\|r_E\|\ll R^{1/2}x^\varepsilon\) and \(X_E\ll D\), then use \(\sqrt{A+B}\le\sqrt A+\sqrt B\). This proves (7), including its cardinality error. The two explicit extra hypotheses give \(RDD^{o(1)}\). Since \(R\ge D^{4/3}\), that substitution is \(D^{7/3+o(1)}\), too large for \(D^{2-\sigma}\); no lower bound is asserted.

2. Diagonal and clean sector. Facts 0fd3b33d63081ee3 and 4d26de51cb52d44d give reconstructed diagonal
\[
 \ll x^\varepsilon RD/P^{1/2}
 =x^\varepsilon D^{\beta+1-\theta/2},
\]
which yields (8). Fact 2d553c87dc18dd6c with its parameter \(\delta=2\sigma\) gives \(P>Y_E\), so \(a,b\nmid h\). Squarefreeness gives \(a,b\nmid m\), and the literal masks give \(a,b\nmid p\ell\). Thus only target divisibility is nonclean. From (1)-(2), \(z_n=\sum_\alpha V_n(\alpha)\) obeys \(|z_n|\ll x^\varepsilon R\); fact 2d553c87dc18dd6c proves (9).

3. Conductor thresholds. Fact d61bd0787abcc5ec gives the common descended modulus \(q\), the same \(t\), and the three local response ranges. Regrouping those ranges proves (11) from the definition (10). For \(T\ge1\), (12) is exactly fact 9ef7fac8978ac244, based on the Euler identity adb3b38d14670d3c.

Suppose \(0<T<1\). Primitive conductors are positive integers. The only term included by \({\rm cond}(\psi)>T\) but excluded by \({\rm cond}(\psi)>1\) is the principal character \(\psi_0\), whose conductor is one. Its character values at the units \(t,au\) are one, and
\[
 G_{N,q}(\psi_0)=
 \sum_{\substack{z\ ({\rm mod}\ q)\\(z,q)=1}}e_q(-Nz)
 =c_q(N).
\]
This proves (13). Directly from its definition,
\(|c_q(N)|\le\phi(q)\). Hence the principal term has absolute value at most one, and the \(T=1\) bound proves (12) for all \(T>0\). This repairs the subunit thresholds \(F/a,F/b\) without applying facts outside their hypotheses.

4. Wu--Xi range. Wu--Xi Definition 2.4 and Section 2.3 show that for \(f_1/f_2\) with \(\deg f_1<\deg f_2<s\), the middle-extension Artin--Schreier trace modulo a prime \(s\), extended by zero at poles, is infinity-amiable with conductor bounded in terms of the rational degree. Take \(f_1=A\), \(f_2=X\), where \(A\) is the unit numerator in (14). The two prime-local inverse traces therefore form a compositely \(2\)-amiable trace modulo \(p\ell\).

The exact \(J=2,\delta=1,W_1=1\) specialization of Wu--Xi Theorem 8.1, for an interval of length \(L<p\ell\), is
\[
 \sum_{m\in I}K(m)\ll L^{1+\varepsilon}
 \{(q_2/L)^{1/2}+(q_1/L^2)^{1/4}\}.
\]
Here \(L=L_m\ll D/P<D<p\ell\) for large \(D\), proving (15). Fixed-power nontriviality gives (16). Fact fc442085ff47a053 gives
\(q_2\ge D^{2-\beta-3\eta+o(1)}\); with
\(L_m\ll D^{1-\theta}\), this proves (17). The gap is
\[
 2(\beta-1)+2\sigma-(\beta-1+3\eta)
 =\beta-1+2\sigma-3\eta
 \ge\frac13-\frac1{40}+2\sigma>0.
\]

5. Explicit completion. Wu--Xi Theorem A.1 states that, for
\(\lambda=\lambda_1/\lambda_2\in\mathbb Z(X)\),
\[
 |\Sigma(\lambda,c)|
 \le c^{1/2}(\lambda,c^\flat)^{1/2}
 (\lambda,c^\flat)_*^{1/2}
 (\lambda',c^\ddagger)(2d(\lambda))^{\omega(c)}
 \Xi(c)^{1/2},
\]
with the notation defined immediately before that theorem. Let \(c=p\ell\) and let \(A\) be the unit numerator. Fourier inversion gives
\[
 \sum_{\substack{m\in I\\(m,c)=1}}e_c(A\overline m)
 =\frac1c\sum_{k\bmod c}\widehat{{\bf1}_I}(k)
 \Sigma\!\left(\frac{A-kX^2}{X},c\right).                 \tag{22}
\]
For \(\lambda_k=(A-kX^2)/X\), \(d(\lambda_k)\le3\),
\[
 (\lambda_k,c)_*=(A,k,c)=1,\qquad
 (\lambda_k,c)=(k,1,c)=1.
\]
Because \(c\) is squarefree, \(c^\ddagger=1\) and \(\Xi(c)=1\). Theorem A.1 gives
\[
 |\Sigma(\lambda_k,c)|\le c^{1/2}6^{\omega(c)}
 =36c^{1/2}.                                               \tag{23}
\]
For an interval of length \(L_m<c\),
\[
 |\widehat{{\bf1}_I}(k)|
 \le\min\!\left(L_m,\frac{c}{2|k|_c}\right)
\]
at nonzero least absolute residue \(|k|_c\), and the zero value is \(L_m\). Summation gives
\[
 \sum_{k\bmod c}|\widehat{{\bf1}_I}(k)|
 \ll c\log(2c).                                             \tag{24}
\]
Equations (22)-(24) prove (18). Since \(p\ell\asymp D^\beta\), (18) is \(D^{\beta/2+o(1)}\), proving (19). Its gap from (8) is
\[
 2(\beta-1)+2\sigma-(1-\beta/2)
 =\frac52\beta-3+2\sigma\ge\frac13+2\sigma>0.
\]
A numerator divisible by one canonical prime leaves only the other prime modulus, so it is not the \(J=2\) case.

6. Remaining supplier. Equation (20) is the off-diagonal quantity in fact 0fd3b33d63081ee3 after envelope rescaling. Fact 4d26de51cb52d44d proves that (21), (8), and (4) imply \(D^{2-\sigma+o(1)}\) for the unique-dilator stratum. No cited theorem pays its complement, another endpoint parent, or Goldbach.

a67bcae890e720ae.title: EXACT PRIME-DIVISOR COMPRESSION OF TWO RECIPROCAL-SLOPE ROWS
a67bcae890e720ae.author: slava chan
a67bcae890e720ae.statement:
EXACT PRIME-DIVISOR COMPRESSION OF TWO RECIPROCAL-SLOPE ROWS.

Let A be a nonzero integer, let r be an integer, and let q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4 be positive integers. Define
  F_12(r)=A(q_2-q_1)-rq_1q_2,
  F_34(r)=A(q_4-q_3)-rq_3q_4,                               (1)
and
  Delta=(q_2-q_1)q_3q_4-(q_4-q_3)q_1q_2.                   (2)
Then the exact integer identity
  q_3q_4F_12(r)-q_1q_2F_34(r)=A Delta                       (3)
holds for every r.

Let p be a prime not dividing q_1q_2q_3q_4. If p divides both F_12(r) and F_34(r), then p divides A Delta. Conversely, if p divides A Delta, then
  p|F_12(r) if and only if p|F_34(r).                        (4)
Thus on Delta nonzero the prime modulus in a simultaneous incidence is restricted to the prime divisors of the fixed nonzero integer A Delta. If additionally p does not divide A, it must divide Delta itself.

Assume |A|<=Q^C and Q<=q_i<2Q for a fixed C>=1. Let I be any real interval of length strictly less than P, and restrict p to primes P<=p<2P with p not dividing q_1q_2q_3q_4. For every quadruple with Delta nonzero, the number of pairs (p,r) with r an integer in I and
  p|F_12(r), p|F_34(r)                                      (5)
is O_{C,epsilon}(Q^epsilon) for every epsilon>0, provided P and Q are polynomially comparable. Indeed p is divisor-restricted by (3), and for each p the first congruence in (5) determines one residue class r modulo p, so I contains at most one representative.

When Delta=0, equations (3)-(4) show that the two prime-incidence rows coincide modulo every eligible p; this is the rational reciprocal-slope diagonal whose total weighted energy is controlled by fact e7458a42217c2756. The present compression concerns only the incidence-incidence support. It does not permit the two incidence terms to be bounded separately from the cross and center pieces of the three-term centered covariance in fact 985515aa5d2117fe.
a67bcae890e720ae.proof:
Expanding the left side of (3) gives

A(q_2-q_1)q_3q_4-rq_1q_2q_3q_4
 -A(q_4-q_3)q_1q_2+rq_1q_2q_3q_4,

and the r-terms cancel, leaving A Delta. This proves (3).

If p divides both F-values, (3) gives p|A Delta. Conversely suppose p|A Delta. If p|F_12(r), then (3) gives q_1q_2F_34(r) congruent zero modulo p. The stated unit hypothesis makes q_1q_2 invertible, so p|F_34(r). The reverse implication is identical. This proves (4), and the assertion for p not dividing A follows.

For Delta nonzero, A Delta is nonzero because A is nonzero. Moreover |A Delta| is bounded by a fixed power of Q: equation (2) gives |Delta|=O(Q^3), while |A|<=Q^C. If |A Delta|=1 it has no prime divisors. Otherwise the fixed-power divisor estimate in fact e705401df9f0709e gives O_{C,epsilon}(Q^epsilon) eligible prime divisors p. For each such p, q_1q_2 is a unit and
  F_12(r) congruent zero modulo p
uniquely determines
  r congruent A(q_2-q_1)(q_1q_2)^(-1) modulo p.
An interval of length less than p contains at most one integer in a prescribed residue class modulo p. Since p>=P and |I|<P, it contains at most one such r. This proves the pair count. The Delta=0 and scope statements follow directly from (3)-(4) and the cited facts.

glossary.F_12: The first affine-in-r PMD divisibility polynomial.
glossary.F_34: The second affine-in-r PMD divisibility polynomial.
glossary.prime-divisor compression: The restriction of a simultaneous two-row incidence to primes dividing A Delta.

a695dcaf05aaa83d.title: Let m>1 be odd, let s belong to {1,-1}, let K be coprime to m, and let the shared normal-digit tensor be expanded into the multiplicative-character atoms of fact 8230d44e6677f45b. Thus an atom indexed by characters chi and psi of the unit group modulo m^2 has, up to a scalar coefficient, the four-variable factor
a695dcaf05aaa83d.author: slava chan
a695dcaf05aaa83d.statement:
Let m>1 be odd, let s belong to {1,-1}, let K be coprime to m, and let the shared normal-digit tensor be expanded into the multiplicative-character atoms of fact 8230d44e6677f45b. Thus an atom indexed by characters chi and psi of the unit group modulo m^2 has, up to a scalar coefficient, the four-variable factor
chi(a)chi(b)psi(c)psi(d),                                             (1)
and its normal-digit Fourier frequency is
ell=gamma(r_chi-r_psi) modulo m,                                     (2)
where gamma=2sK^(-1) modulo m and r_chi,r_psi are the restriction frequencies on 1+mZ modulo m^2.

Fix a sign sector in which a,b,c,d are nonzero integers, and put A=|a|, B=|b|, C_abs=|c|, D_abs=|d|. A legal positive determinant substitution means a use-once relabeling of A,B,C_abs,D_abs into positive variables m_1,m_2,n_1,n_2 for which the equation
ab+cd=Delta                                                          (3)
becomes
m_1n_2-m_2n_1=Delta or m_1n_2-m_2n_1=-Delta.                         (4)
Such a substitution exists if and only if sign(ab)=-sign(cd). In every legal substitution, exactly one member of {A,B} occupies an m-slot and the other occupies an n-slot, while exactly one member of {C_abs,D_abs} occupies the other m-slot and the other occupies the other n-slot. Consequently the character atom (1), after absorbing constant factors chi(-1) and psi(-1) coming from signs, leaves one chi factor and one psi factor in the two m-slots for every legal sign sector and every legal orientation.

If ell is nonzero modulo m, then chi and psi cannot both be trivial. Hence every nonzero normal-digit mode leaves at least one nontrivial multiplicative-character factor in a Bettin--Chandee m-slot, regardless of the legal sign-sector substitution. The exact character expansion therefore does not directly satisfy fact b1398db2962d7491, which permits arbitrary sequences only in the two n-slots and requires fixed smooth profiles in the two m-slots. This is an exact no-direct-application statement, not a cancellation no-go. Two minimal types of additional input that would repair this particular slot mismatch are: a determinant discrepancy theorem uniform under multiplicative-character twists in both m-slots, including its explicit main term; or an exact decomposition of the two row-character factors into admissible smooth profiles with the full derivative, coefficient, discrepancy, and main-term costs summed. No assertion is made that either repair is available or sufficient for the literal determinant carrier.
a695dcaf05aaa83d.proof:
Let epsilon_ab=sign(ab) and epsilon_cd=sign(cd). Then (3) is
Delta=epsilon_ab AB+epsilon_cd C_abs D_abs.                           (5)
