A determinant of four positive variables in (4) is the difference of two positive monomials, and the use-once substitution must assign the variables in each original monomial together: otherwise its two products would mix one variable from {A,B} with one from {C_abs,D_abs} and would not equal the two monomials AB and C_abs D_abs in (5). Thus a legal substitution requires epsilon_ab=-epsilon_cd. Conversely, if the signs are opposite, multiply (5) by epsilon_ab to obtain
AB-C_abs D_abs=epsilon_ab Delta.                                     (6)
Choose either member of {A,B} for m_1 and put the other in n_2. Choose either member of {C_abs,D_abs} for m_2 and put the other in n_1. This gives all four substitutions realizing the left side of (6). Swapping the two product pairs gives the four substitutions realizing its negative. Thus these eight orientations are all legal substitutions, and every one chooses exactly one m-variable from each original product pair. This proves the sign-sector and slot classification.

If an original coefficient is negative, multiplicativity gives chi(-A)=chi(-1)chi(A), and similarly for the other variables; chi(-1) and psi(-1) are constants independent of A,B,C_abs,D_abs. Therefore (1) has one chi factor on both members of {A,B} and one psi factor on both members of {C_abs,D_abs}, up to constant signs. Since every legal substitution puts one member of each pair in an m-slot, one m-slot carries chi and the other carries psi.

For the subgroup H_0={1+mt modulo m^2}, fact 8230d44e6677f45b writes
chi(1+mt)=e_m(r_chi t),  psi(1+mt)=e_m(r_psi t),                       (7)
and proves that the coefficient of the atom is a digit Fourier coefficient at the frequency (2). If both chi and psi were trivial characters, then r_chi=r_psi=0 and (2) would give ell=0. Thus ell nonzero implies that at least one of chi,psi is nontrivial, and the preceding slot classification places that nontrivial factor in an m-slot in every orientation.

Facts 630165d40f5dd2de and b1398db2962d7491 state the Bettin--Chandee determinant interface: its m_1,m_2 factors are fixed smooth profiles satisfying scaled derivative bounds, while arbitrary one-variable sequences occur only in n_1,n_2. A nontrivial multiplicative character in an m-slot is not supplied as one of those arbitrary sequence slots, and the character expansion alone proves no admissible fixed-profile derivative bounds for its product with the row cutoff. Therefore no direct application follows. Allowing character-twisted row slots or first decomposing the row characters into admissible smooth profiles are precisely the two stated ways to change the missing hypothesis; both would also require their own discrepancy and main-term accounting. This proves the scoped conclusion.

glossary.legal positive determinant substitution: a use-once relabeling of four positive coefficient magnitudes into the positive variables m_1,m_2,n_1,n_2 that converts the signed two-product equation into m_1n_2-m_2n_1 equal to Delta or -Delta
glossary.r_chi: the additive frequency modulo m of the restriction of a multiplicative character chi to 1+mZ modulo m^2

a6a149cbfd5e46e5.title: TOP-B SINGLETON PRINCIPAL/LOW-ACTIVE-FACE TRANSFER AND THE EXACT LARGE-ACTIVE-PRODUCT REMAINDER. Use the exact recombined singleton canonical top-\(B\) rows and primitive-ray notation of fact \(fa4091851a622bcb\). Thus
a6a149cbfd5e46e5.author: slava chan
a6a149cbfd5e46e5.statement:
TOP-B SINGLETON PRINCIPAL/LOW-ACTIVE-FACE TRANSFER AND THE EXACT LARGE-ACTIVE-PRODUCT REMAINDER. Use the exact recombined singleton canonical top-\(B\) rows and primitive-ray notation of fact \(fa4091851a622bcb\). Thus
\[
 B/2\le n=uy<2B,\qquad
 \mathcal D\le y<2\mathcal D,\qquad B=Q^\beta,\qquad \beta<6/5,
\]
the nonzero target is \(\mathscr A\), and for distinct supported primitive signed rays
\[
 R=(\epsilon,a,b),\qquad R'=(\epsilon',a',b')
\]
one has
\[
 \Delta_0=\epsilon ba'-\epsilon'b'a,
\]
\[
 m=m_q={aa'\over(aa',\mathscr A\Delta_0)},\qquad
 c=C_q={\mathscr A\Delta_0\over(aa',\mathscr A\Delta_0)}.      \tag{1}
\]
Let
\[
 Y_0={Q^2\over\mathcal D}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(Q\),
\[
 \mathcal D\le2B<Q^2,\qquad Y_0\ge1.                            \tag{2}
\]
Every supported \(m\) is squarefree and
\[
 (c,m)=(uy,m)=1.                                               \tag{3}
\]

For \(m>1\), define on units \(z\) modulo \(m\)
\[
 K^\circ_{m,c}(z)
 =
 {1\over\phi(m)}
 \sum_{\substack{\chi\ ({\rm mod}\ m)\\\chi\ne\chi_0}}
 \left(\sum_{x\ ({\rm mod}\ m)}^*e_m(-cx)\chi(x)\right)\chi(z),
\]
and put \(K^\circ_{1,c}=0\). Then
\[
 e_m(-c z^{-1})={\mu(m)\over\phi(m)}+K^\circ_{m,c}(z).         \tag{4}
\]
The first term in (4), summed with the complete singleton ray
coefficients and any existing literal selector, satisfies
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 |\mathfrak H_{B}^{\rm prin}|
 \ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon BF^2
 \le Q^\varepsilon {BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}.
 \quad}                                                        \tag{TOP-B-qPRINC}
\]

For every prime \(p\mid m\), put \(m_p=m/p\) and define
\[
 \kappa_{p;m,c}(z)
 =
 e_p\!\left(-c z^{-1}\overline {m_p}\right)+{1\over p-1}.
\]
For \(r\mid m\), put
\[
 \mathcal K_{r;m,c}(z)=\prod_{p\mid r}\kappa_{p;m,c}(z),
 \qquad \mathcal K_{1;m,c}=1.
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 K^\circ_{m,c}(z)
 =
 \sum_{\substack{r\mid m\\r>1}}
 {\mu(m/r)\over\phi(m/r)}
 \mathcal K_{r;m,c}(z).
 }                                                               \tag{5}
\]
After the accepted payment in fact \(fa4091851a622bcb\) of all pairs
\(m_q\le Y_0\), restrict to \(m_q>Y_0\). The complete contribution in
(5) of the faces
\[
 1<r\le Y_0
\]
satisfies
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 |\mathfrak H_{B}^{q\text{-}{\rm lowface}}|
 \ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon BY_0F^2
 =
 Q^\varepsilon {BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}.
 \quad}                                                        \tag{TOP-B-qCENT-LOWFACE}
\]

Consequently the exact remaining singleton canonical \(B\) ray-pair
contribution is
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\mathfrak H_{B}^{q\text{-}{\rm largeface}}
=
\sum_{u,y}
\sum_{\substack{R\ne R'\\m_q>Y_0}}
&\Theta(u,y,R,R')\,
B_{u,y}(R)\overline{B_{u,y}(R')}\\
&\times
\sum_{\substack{r\mid m_q\\r>Y_0}}
{\mu(m_q/r)\over\phi(m_q/r)}
\mathcal K_{r;m_q,C_q}(uy),
\end{aligned}}                                                 \tag{TOP-B-CqKLOO-VEC}
\]
where \(\Theta\) retains every existing source, target-gcd,
fixed-\(U\), parent, sign, order/equal-cell, collision, deletion,
coprimality and provenance selector, including the canonical
nonresonant condition when imposed. Thus every term in the remainder
satisfies simultaneously
\[
 m_q>{Q^2\over\mathcal D},\qquad
 r>{Q^2\over\mathcal D}.                                      \tag{6}
\]
No estimate for TOP-B-CqKLOO-VEC is asserted. The theorem applies only
after singleton recombination and does not apply any absolute count to
the old unrecombined siblings. It is an individual-canonical-row
reduction and is separate from the cross-\(u\) pre-Cauchy energy.
a6a149cbfd5e46e5.proof:
Since \(y\mid n<2B\), one has
\(\mathcal D\le y<2B\), proving the first inequality in (2). Because
\(\beta<6/5<2\), \(2Q^\beta<Q^2\) for all sufficiently large \(Q\),
which proves the rest of (2).

Fact fa4091851a622bcb proves that every supported reciprocal modulus
\(q\) is squarefree. Hence the primitive ray denominators \(a,a'\),
which divide supported \(q,q'\), are squarefree. Its low-conductor proof
writes
\[
 a=g\alpha,\qquad a'=g\beta
\]
with \(g,\alpha,\beta\) pairwise coprime and squarefree, and obtains
\[
 m_q=
 {g\over(g,\mathscr A L_0)}
 {\alpha\beta\over(\alpha\beta,\mathscr A)}.
\]
The two displayed factors are coprime and squarefree, so \(m_q\) is
squarefree. By definition \((c,m)=1\). Also \(m\mid aa'\), while the
literal support gives \((aa',uy)=1\), proving (3).

We prove (4) by character inversion on the finite unit group modulo
\(m\). For \(f(z)=e_m(-cz^{-1})\), its coefficient at \(\chi\) is
\[
 \sum_x^*e_m(-cx)\chi(x).
\]
The principal coefficient is the Ramanujan sum \(c_m(-c)\), equal to
\(\mu(m)\) because \(m\) is squarefree and \((c,m)=1\). This gives (4);
for \(m=1\) both the additive phase and \(\mu(1)/\phi(1)\) equal one.

We next prove the principal estimate. The proof of
fa4091851a622bcb gives the cumulative singleton coordinate count
\[
 N(T):=\#\{(u,y,q_1,h_1,q_2,h_2):m_q\le T\}
 \ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon BTF^2                         \tag{7}
\]
for \(1\le T\le Q^{O(1)}\), before any selector deletes terms. Every
\(m_q<4Q^2\). Abel summation applied to (7) gives
\[
 \sum_{\rm singleton\ coordinates}{1\over m_q}
 \ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon BF^2.                          \tag{8}
\]
Since \(m_q\) is squarefree,
\[
 {m_q\over\phi(m_q)}\ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon,
\]
so (8) also gives
\[
 \sum_{\rm singleton\ coordinates}{1\over\phi(m_q)}
 \ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon BF^2.                          \tag{9}
\]
Equivalently, one may use the pointwise singleton coefficient envelope
inside the proof of (7); its fixed divisor factors are absorbed into
\(Q^\varepsilon\). Expanding both ray coefficients, taking absolute
values, and using (9) proves TOP-B-qPRINC. The comparison with the
canonical target follows from \(Y_0=Q^2/\mathcal D\ge1\).

For (5), squarefreeness and the Chinese remainder theorem give
\[
 e_m(-cz^{-1})
 =
 \prod_{p\mid m}e_p(-c z^{-1}\overline {m_p}).
\]
The mean of the \(p\)-local factor over nonzero residues is
\(-1/(p-1)\), so \(\kappa_{p;m,c}\) has mean zero. Substitute
\[
 e_p(-c z^{-1}\overline {m_p})
 =\kappa_{p;m,c}(z)-{1\over p-1}
\]
and expand over subsets of the prime divisors of \(m\). The inactive
product is
\[
 {\mu(m/r)\over\phi(m/r)},
\]
and the active product is \(\mathcal K_{r;m,c}\). The \(r=1\) term is
the principal term in (4); removing it proves (5).

For a fixed coordinate with \(m=m_q\),
\[
 |\mathcal K_{r;m,c}(uy)|
 \le {r\over\phi(r)}
 \ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon,
\]
and
\[
 {1\over\phi(m/r)}
 \ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon{r\over m}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \sum_{\substack{1<r\mid m\\r\le Y_0}}
 {|\mathcal K_{r;m,c}(uy)|\over\phi(m/r)}
 \ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon {Y_0\over m},                  \tag{10}
\]
where the divisor count of \(m\) is absorbed into \(Q^\varepsilon\).
Sum (10) over all singleton scaling coordinates and use (8). The
pointwise coefficient envelope and every frozen or literal multiplicity
are already included in the singleton count and contribute only another
\(Q^\varepsilon\). This proves TOP-B-qCENT-LOWFACE.

Finally fact fa4091851a622bcb pays all \(m_q\le Y_0\). On the
complement \(m_q>Y_0\), insert (4), pay its principal term, then split
the exact finite sum (5) into \(r\le Y_0\) and \(r>Y_0\). Paying the
first part leaves exactly TOP-B-CqKLOO-VEC, with every selector unchanged.
This proves (6) and every stated scope limitation.

glossary.TOP-B-CqKLOO-VEC: The exact singleton top-B remainder with both reduced physical conductor and active CRT product larger than Q^2/Dcal.
glossary.TOP-B-qCENT-LOWFACE: The singleton top-B centered physical ray-kernel faces with active product at most Q^2/Dcal.
glossary.TOP-B-qPRINC: The principal multiplicative-character component of the singleton top-B reduced physical ray kernel.

a71f777ad842c886.title: OUTER-GCD-NORMALIZED ALL-LEAF IDENTITY, FORCE-A-LEAF THEOREM, AND LOW-BETA PARENT COLLAPSE
a71f777ad842c886.author: slava chan
a71f777ad842c886.statement:
OUTER-GCD-NORMALIZED ALL-LEAF IDENTITY, FORCE-A-LEAF THEOREM, AND LOW-BETA PARENT COLLAPSE.

Assume the high real Poisson atom family ℓH, coefficients w_z=mu(d)mu(r)q_z, exact outer-gcd data d=ga, r=gb, and frozen parents P(z) in
{C91,E_11,E_21,E_22,E_asym,U_sh,U_low,U_gap,U_sup}
from fact 77d7a3419a07305c. Thus mu(d)mu(r) is nonzero, q_z is real, dm+rk=N, g=gcd(d,r), and am+bk=N/g.

For each atom define its orientation from its original dyadic label lambda=(D,M,R,K). If R>D use the forward convention n_z=b and s_z=a. If D>R use the reverse convention n_z=a and s_z=b. If D=R use the declared equal-scale convention n_z=b and s_z=a. Freeze
theta_z=(lambda,g,orientation)
before any marker expansion.

For every nonempty frozen layer theta choose real parameters L_theta,S_theta,Z_theta and a positive integer J_theta such that
2<=L_theta<=S_theta, L_theta<Z_theta,
and every atom in that layer with n_z>S_theta satisfies
Z_theta^(J_theta+1)>n_z.
For n_z<=S_theta define the small coefficient c_0(n_z)=mu(n_z). For n_z>S_theta define c_A(n_z), c_B(n_z), and c_{C_j}(n_z), 1<=j<=J_theta, by the complete sign-preserving marker identity of fact 7c1f38cfbb8d0569, with the marked squarefree integer there equal to n_z and with parameters L_theta,S_theta,Z_theta,J_theta. Set every inapplicable coefficient to zero. Then pointwise
mu(n_z)=c_0(n_z)+c_A(n_z)+c_B(n_z)+sum_{j=1}^{J_theta}c_{C_j}(n_z).                    (1)

Define
J_max=max({0} union {J_theta:theta is a nonempty frozen layer}).
When J_max=0, the list C_1,...,C_{J_max} and every sum over that list are empty. Interpret absent coefficients as zero. For every parent P and X in {C_0,A,B,C_1,...,C_{J_max}} define
T^norm_{P,X}=sum_{z in mathcal H:P(z)=P} mu(s_z)q_z c_X(n_z).                       (2)
Then
R_high=sum_{z in mathcal H}mu(d)mu(r)q_z
      =sum_P(T^norm_{P,C_0}+T^norm_{P,A}+T^norm_{P,B}
             +sum_{j=1}^{J_max}T^norm_{P,C_j})                                    (3)
exactly, including when mathcal H is empty. Every q_z, conjugate h-pair, target N/g, source mask, smooth amplitude, original dyadic label, exact g, and frozen parent is unchanged. In particular, no prime factor absorbed by g is marked again.

Let mathcal E_norm be the nonempty leaves in (3), and let M_norm be their number. If
R_high<=-A_0+epsilon_0
with A_0>epsilon_0, then M_norm>=1 and some normalized leaf ell satisfies
T^norm_ell<=(-A_0+epsilon_0)/M_norm,                                                (4)
and
M_norm<=9(J_max+3).                                                                (5)
Thus the normalized identity quantitatively forces one normalized leaf with only the finite leaf-count loss; it does not predetermine its marker type.

There is also an exact low-beta simplification. In a forward layer with R>D and D/g>1 put
Q_theta=D/g, B_theta=R/g, beta_theta=log(B_theta)/log(Q_theta).
In a reverse layer with D>R and R/g>1 put
Q_theta=R/g, B_theta=D/g, beta_theta=log(B_theta)/log(Q_theta).
Fix 0<kappa<=1/100. On every such layer satisfying
1<=beta_theta<=6/5-2kappa,                                                          (6)
the four endpoint parents E_11,E_21,E_22,E_asym and the two nonendpoint parents U_gap,U_sup are empty. Every atom in that layer has parent C91 if its dyadic label belongs to mathcal C_91; otherwise it has parent U_sh when min(D,R)<4D_*, and U_low when min(D,R)>=4D_*. Hence on the low-beta layer the surviving parent selector is a scalar depending only on the original dyadic label, not on a least divisor, rough-factorization copy, h, a, b, m, or k. The same conclusion holds for D=R, where the original label exponent is one. Layers whose normalized base is at most one and the explicit C_0 leaves remain in the exact identity (3), but (6) and any large-base analytic consumer are not asserted for them.
a71f777ad842c886.proof:
Because mu(d)mu(r) is nonzero, d and r are squarefree. Let p be a prime divisor of g. Since d=ga is squarefree, p does not divide a; since r=gb is squarefree, p does not divide b. Also gcd(a,b)=1 from the outer-gcd normalization in fact 77d7a3419a07305c. Hence g,a,b are pairwise coprime. Multiplicativity of mu on coprime factors gives
mu(d)mu(r)=mu(g)mu(a)mu(g)mu(b)=mu(g)^2mu(a)mu(b)=mu(a)mu(b),                       (7)
because squarefree g has mu(g)^2=1. In every orientation {s_z,n_z}={a,b}, so (7) is mu(s_z)mu(n_z).

If n_z<=S_theta, equation (1) holds by the definition c_0(n_z)=mu(n_z), with all other coefficients zero on that small branch. If n_z>S_theta, then n_z is squarefree and the displayed hypotheses on L_theta,S_theta,Z_theta,J_theta are precisely those of fact 7c1f38cfbb8d0569. That fact gives
mu(n_z)=c_A(n_z)+c_B(n_z)+sum_j c_{C_j}(n_z),
while c_0(n_z)=0. Thus (1) holds for every atom.

Multiply (1) by mu(s_z)q_z. By (7), the left side becomes the original atom weight mu(d)mu(r)q_z. Sum first inside each already frozen parent and exact theta layer, and then over all atoms. This proves (3). If mathcal H is empty, both sides and every leaf sum are zero under the displayed empty-list conventions. The operation changes only the factor mu(n_z), so every coordinate listed after (3) is retained. Since the marker is applied to n_z after division by the exact g, primes in g are absent from n_z and cannot occur in an internal marker factorization.

There are nine parents. For each parent there are at most one C_0 leaf, one A leaf, one B leaf, and J_max rough leaves, proving (5). Under A_0>epsilon_0 the right side -A_0+epsilon_0 is negative. Therefore the hypothesis for (4) implies R_high<0, so mathcal H and mathcal E_norm are nonempty and M_norm>=1. If every nonempty leaf were greater than the right side of (4), their sum would be greater than -A_0+epsilon_0, contradicting (3). This proves (4).

It remains to prove the low-beta parent statement. In a forward layer, fact b01d255ce4c5ff24 proves
log(R/g)/log(D/g)>=log R/log D
whenever D/g>1. Under (6),
log R/log D<=beta_theta<=6/5-2kappa<4/3.                                          (8)
Thus forward boundary admissibility in fact 77d7a3419a07305c fails before any least eligible divisor is considered. In a reverse layer, the reverse inequality in fact b01d255ce4c5ff24 gives
log D/log R<4/3,
so reverse boundary admissibility fails. Therefore no atom in either low-beta layer belongs to E_11,E_21,E_22, or E_asym.

Outside the first-precedence C91 parent, fact 77d7a3419a07305c sends a nonendpoint atom to U_sh if min(D,R)<4D_*. Otherwise its original label exponent is below 4/3 by (8) or its reverse analogue, so it is sent to U_low, not U_gap or U_sup. Membership in mathcal C_91, the inequality min(D,R)<4D_*, and the comparison of the original dyadic scales are label predicates. Hence the surviving parent is constant on the fixed dyadic label. When D=R, neither strict orientation is boundary-admissible and the declared nonendpoint exponent is one, so the same C91/U_sh/U_low conclusion follows directly from the parent definitions. The final small-base scope statement follows because beta_theta is used only when its denominator logarithm is positive, whereas the algebraic identity did not require a large normalized base.

glossary.C_0: The explicit small-normalized-factor leaf n_z at most S_theta.
glossary.beta_theta: The logarithmic exponent of the normalized larger dyadic scale over the normalized base scale.
glossary.n_z: The outer-gcd-normalized factor selected for marker expansion: b in the forward and equal-scale conventions, and a in the reverse convention.
glossary.s_z: The normalized factor complementary to n_z: a in the forward and equal-scale conventions, and b in the reverse convention.
glossary.theta_z: The frozen normalized layer consisting of the original dyadic label, exact outer gcd, and orientation convention.

a75ea6a8a40dd1f8.title: DOUBLE-VAUGHAN-QN: AN EXACT SIMULTANEOUS TYPE-I/TYPE-II DECOMPOSITION OF THE ADDITIVE-RECIPROCITY SOURCE. Let
a75ea6a8a40dd1f8.author: slava chan
a75ea6a8a40dd1f8.statement:
DOUBLE-VAUGHAN-QN: AN EXACT SIMULTANEOUS TYPE-I/TYPE-II DECOMPOSITION OF THE ADDITIVE-RECIPROCITY SOURCE. Let
\[
 1\le Q_0<Q_1\le2Q_0,\qquad
 1\le B_0<B_1\le2B_0
\]
be integer dyadic endpoints, and choose
\[
 1\le V_q\le Q_0^{1/2},\qquad
 1\le V_n\le B_0^{1/2}.                                    \tag{1}
\]
For V>=1 define
\[
 \mu_{\le V}(u)=\mu(u){\bf1}_{u\le V},
\]
\[
 a_V(d)=\sum_{uv=d}\mu_{\le V}(u)\mu_{\le V}(v),
 \qquad
 b_V(d)=-\sum_{\substack{c\mid d\\c>V}}\mu(c).          \tag{2}
\]
Then
\[
 |a_V(d)|+|b_V(d)|\le2\tau(d).                              \tag{3}
\]

For a function Phi(q,n) on the positive integer pairs, extended by zero away from all desired source gates, define the q-axis operators
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 ({\cal I}_{q,V_q}\Phi)(n)
 &=\sum_{d\le V_q^2}a_{V_q}(d)
   \sum_{Q_0/d<m\le Q_1/d}\Phi(dm,n),\\
 ({\cal J}_{q,V_q}\Phi)(n)
 &=\sum_{V_q<d\le Q_1/V_q}b_{V_q}(d)
   \sum_{\max\{V_q,Q_0/d\}<m\le Q_1/d}
   \mu(m)\Phi(dm,n).                                      \tag{4}
 \end{aligned}
\]
Define the n-axis operators analogously by replacing
\[
 (q,Q_0,Q_1,V_q,d,m)
 \quad\hbox{with}\quad
 (n,B_0,B_1,V_n,e,\ell).                                    \tag{5}
\]
The operators act on their indicated axes and commute. One has the exact identity
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_{Q_0<q\le Q_1}\sum_{B_0<n\le B_1}
 \mu(q)\mu(n)\Phi(q,n)
 =
 ({\cal I}_{q,V_q}+{\cal J}_{q,V_q})
 ({\cal I}_{n,V_n}+{\cal J}_{n,V_n})\Phi.
 }                                                            \tag{6}
\]
Thus the right side is the sum of exactly four source-preserving terms:
\[
 {\cal I}_q{\cal I}_n\Phi,quad
 {\cal I}_q{\cal J}_n\Phi,quad
 {\cal J}_q{\cal I}_n\Phi,quad
 {\cal J}_q{\cal J}_n\Phi.                                \tag{7}
\]

Apply (6) to one signed projective box of fact ecd6325d7ef2bc37 by putting
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \Phi(q,n)={1\over H_P}
 &A(q)C(n){\bf1}_{(g,qn)=(q,n)=1}\\
 &\times\sum_{F\le|h|<2F}E(h)
 e_n(\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\overline q),                   \tag{8}
 \end{aligned}
\]
with the literal dyadic endpoints and zero extension. Then (6)--(7) retain the complete h-average, target, both frequency signs, every gcd gate, and every projective atom before any absolute value. In particular the Type-II--Type-II term is exactly
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 {1\over H_P}
 \sum_{\substack{V_q<d\le Q_1/V_q\\
                   V_n<e\le B_1/V_n}}
 b_{V_q}(d)b_{V_n}(e)
 \sum_{\substack{\max\{V_q,Q_0/d\}<m\le Q_1/d\\
                   \max\{V_n,B_0/e\}<\ell\le B_1/e}}
 &\mu(m)\mu(\ell)A(dm)C(e\ell)\\
 &\times{\bf1}_{(g,dm e\ell)=(dm,e\ell)=1}
 \sum_{F\le|h|<2F}E(h)
 e_{e\ell}(\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\overline{dm}).           \tag{9}
 \end{aligned}
\]
Formula (9) is a genuine double-Möbius multilinear source term; neither remaining sign has been replaced by its modulus.

A fixed-power estimate of size Q^{2-delta} for each of the four terms in (7), uniformly over legal V_q,V_n and the actual projective boxes, is sufficient for DOUBLE-MU-RECIP-N after the existing finite dyadic/source reconstruction. No such estimate is asserted here. The identity alone does not pay any Type-I or Type-II term, does not permit a complement to be summed absolutely without an exponent audit, and proves no strict-top, endpoint, post-A, or Goldbach conclusion.
a75ea6a8a40dd1f8.proof:
We first prove the one-axis identity. Let mu_0=mu_{<=V} and mu_1=mu-mu_0. Dirichlet convolution is denoted by *. Since
\[
 \mu*{\bf1}=\varepsilon_0,
\]
where epsilon_0 is the convolution identity, associativity and commutativity give
\[
 \mu_1*\mu_1*{\bf1}
 =\mu-2\mu_0+\mu_0*\mu_0*{\bf1}.                       \tag{10}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \mu=2\mu_0-\mu_0*\mu_0*{\bf1}
      +\mu_1*\mu_1*{\bf1}.                               \tag{11}
\]
For an integer x>V, mu_0(x)=0, so
\[
 \mu(x)=-(a_V*{\bf1})(x)+(\mu_1*\mu_1*{\bf1})(x).       \tag{12}
\]
By (2),
\[
 b_V=-(\mu_1*{\bf1}).
\]
Hence the second term in (12) is -mu_1*b_V, and therefore
\[
 \mu(x)
 =-\sum_{\substack{d\mid x\\d\le V^2}}a_V(d)
  -\sum_{\substack{dm=x\\d>V,\ m>V}}b_V(d)\mu(m).      \tag{13}
\]
The support restrictions in (13) follow from the definitions: a_V(d)=0 for d>V^2 and mu_1(m)=0 for m<=V. Both coefficients in (2) are sums over divisors of d, proving (3).

Now sum (13) against an arbitrary function f(x) on X_0<x<=X_1, where V<=X_0^{1/2}. Interchanging finite sums gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_{X_0<x\le X_1}\mu(x)f(x)
 ={}&-\sum_{d\le V^2}a_V(d)
       \sum_{X_0/d<m\le X_1/d}f(dm)\\
 &-\sum_{V<d\le X_1/V}b_V(d)
       \sum_{\max\{V,X_0/d\}<m\le X_1/d}
       \mu(m)f(dm).                                        \tag{14}
 \end{aligned}
\]
This is the exact Möbius Vaughan identity also recorded as Lemma 9 of Dhakal--Munsch, arXiv:2304.08736; equation (14) has been derived here without using it as a black box.

Apply (14) first with x=q, X_0=Q_0, X_1=Q_1 and f(q)=Phi(q,n), keeping n fixed. This gives
\[
 \sum_q\mu(q)\Phi(q,n)
 =-({\cal I}_{q,V_q}\Phi)(n)
  -({\cal J}_{q,V_q}\Phi)(n).                              \tag{15}
\]
Apply the same identity to the n-axis. Multiplying the two negative decompositions yields the four positive compositions in (6)--(7). Finite sums justify the interchange, and the two axis operators commute because they replace different coordinates. No property of Phi has been used.

Finally substitute (8). All gates and coefficients are inside Phi and are therefore retained by zero extension. Expanding the J_q J_n composition gives (9) with exactly the ranges in (4)--(5). The remaining mu(m) and mu(ell) are the two mu_1 factors in (13), so no sign has been deleted. The conditional sufficiency statement follows by applying the triangle inequality only after the four complete terms have separately received the asserted bound and then using the finite projective/dyadic reconstruction already verified in fact ecd6325d7ef2bc37.

glossary.DOUBLE-VAUGHAN-QN: The exact four-term simultaneous Vaughan decomposition of the q- and n-Möbius axes.
glossary.a_V: The Type-I truncated Möbius-convolution coefficient at cutoff V.
glossary.b_V: The Type-II truncated Möbius-divisor coefficient at cutoff V.
glossary.mathcal I_{X,V}: The Type-I operator on one dyadic Möbius axis.
glossary.mathcal J_{X,V}: The Type-II operator on one dyadic Möbius axis.

a8324506c253b8f4.title: Let H>=2, let C and K be nonzero integers, let r_2 and r_3 be distinct primes in I_H=[H^2,2H^2), and let m>1 be odd with gcd(m,2 K r_2 r_3)=1. Fix a real number X_box>=0. For each unit t modulo m, let a0(t),b0(t),c0(t),d0(t) be the canonical even torus representatives of fact 17557ebe80636618. Let Z_t be the finite set of normalized unit states of fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb having q=2m, the fixed data C,K,r_2,r_3, coefficient box |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|<=X_box, and reduction modulo m corresponding to t. Thus, equivalently by fact 17557ebe80636618, Z_t is the set of exact affine-bilinear lifts over t satisfying all of that fact's literal normalized selectors and the coefficient box
a8324506c253b8f4.author: slava chan
a8324506c253b8f4.statement:
Let H>=2, let C and K be nonzero integers, let r_2 and r_3 be distinct primes in I_H=[H^2,2H^2), and let m>1 be odd with gcd(m,2 K r_2 r_3)=1. Fix a real number X_box>=0. For each unit t modulo m, let a0(t),b0(t),c0(t),d0(t) be the canonical even torus representatives of fact 17557ebe80636618. Let Z_t be the finite set of normalized unit states of fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb having q=2m, the fixed data C,K,r_2,r_3, coefficient box |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|<=X_box, and reduction modulo m corresponding to t. Thus, equivalently by fact 17557ebe80636618, Z_t is the set of exact affine-bilinear lifts over t satisfying all of that fact's literal normalized selectors and the coefficient box.

Give every state z in the disjoint union of the Z_t a complex weight omega_z with |omega_z|<=1, and put A_t=sum_{z in Z_t}omega_z. For residues h=(h_a,h_b,h_c,h_d) modulo m define
G_m(h)=sum_{t modulo m, gcd(t,m)=1} A_t e_m(h_a a0(t)+h_b b0(t)+h_c c0(t)+h_d d0(t)).
Put
X_tor=h_a r_2^(-1)+h_c r_3^(-1),
Y_tor=K(h_b r_2+h_d r_3) modulo m,
and delta_3=gcd(m,3). Define F_flat to be the set of raw frequency quadruples h for which Y_tor=-X_tor and X_tor=0 modulo m/delta_3. Then F_flat has exactly delta_3 m^2 elements, and for every h in F_flat one has G_m(h)=sum_t A_t. Moreover the exact energy identities are
sum_{h modulo m in four slots}|G_m(h)|^2=m^4 sum_t|A_t|^2,
sum_{h in F_flat}|G_m(h)|^2=delta_3 m^2 |sum_t A_t|^2,
and
sum_{h not in F_flat}|G_m(h)|^2=m^4 sum_t|A_t|^2-delta_3 m^2 |sum_t A_t|^2.

The exact lift multiplicities satisfy
|Z_t|<=(1+X_box/m)^2
for every unit t. Consequently, if N_lift=sum_t|Z_t|, then
sum_t|A_t|^2<=(1+X_box/m)^2 N_lift
and
sum_{h not in F_flat}|G_m(h)|^2<=m^4(1+X_box/m)^2 N_lift.
In particular, if X_box<=L H^3 for a fixed real L>=1 and m>=H^(3-delta) for a real delta>=0, then |Z_t|<=(1+L H^delta)^2 for every t; for the top range m>=H^3 this is at most (1+L)^2.

Thus the universally full-mass torus fibres are paid exactly before any cancellation claim, while all integer normal carries, prime quotients, signs, distinctness conditions, coupling conditions, and coefficient boxes remain inside the lift weights A_t. The theorem is an exact fixed-(m,r_2,r_3) energy and multiplicity interface; it does not by itself provide cancellation after summing over m,r_2,r_3 or the other packet variables.
a8324506c253b8f4.proof:
Fact 17557ebe80636618 proves that every normalized state under the hypotheses has a unique unit torus parameter t and a unique exact affine-bilinear lift over the canonical representatives a0(t),b0(t),c0(t),d0(t). It also proves that the normal carries and every literal normalized selector in the statement remain conditions on that integer lift. Hence the sets Z_t are disjoint and retain all the stated selectors.

By fact a274f28c67018d5f, substitution of the torus representatives into the four-slot phase gives
h_a a0(t)+h_b b0(t)+h_c c0(t)+h_d d0(t)=X_tor t+Y_tor t^(-1) modulo m.
The same fact proves that the homomorphism from raw frequencies h to (X_tor,Y_tor) is surjective and every fibre has m^2 elements. It also classifies the pairs for which X_tor t+Y_tor t^(-1)=0 modulo m for every unit t: they are exactly Y_tor=-X_tor with X_tor=0 modulo m/delta_3, and there are delta_3 such pairs. Their full raw preimage is therefore F_flat and has delta_3 m^2 elements. For every h in this set every phase equals one, so G_m(h)=sum_t A_t. This proves the flat-fibre count and its displayed energy contribution.

For the total energy, group raw frequencies by their image under the frequency homomorphism. Since each image has m^2 preimages,
sum_h|G_m(h)|^2
 =m^2 sum_{X,Y modulo m}|sum_{t unit}A_t e_m(Xt+Yt^(-1))|^2.
Expanding the square and interchanging finite sums, the inner frequency sum attached to units t and u is
sum_{X modulo m}e_m(X(t-u)) sum_{Y modulo m}e_m(Y(t^(-1)-u^(-1))).
The first factor is m when t=u and zero otherwise. When t=u, the second factor is also m. Thus orthogonality gives
sum_{X,Y}|sum_t A_t e_m(Xt+Yt^(-1))|^2=m^2 sum_t|A_t|^2.
Multiplication by the raw fibre size m^2 proves the total identity. Subtracting the already computed contribution of F_flat proves the exact nonflat identity.

It remains to prove the lift multiplicity bound. Fix a unit t. By fact 17557ebe80636618, every state in Z_t has
b=b0(t)+2m y and d=d0(t)+2m w
for integers y,w. The interval [-X_box,X_box] has length 2X_box, while successive allowed b-values, and likewise successive allowed d-values, differ by 2m. Hence there are at most 1+X_box/m choices for b and at most 1+X_box/m choices for d.

We prove that fixed b,d support at most one normalized state. Fact 4832817b6b759101 gives, for
U=(b r_3)^2+(d r_2)^2, V=b r_3+d r_2, L_0=2K r_2r_3,
the identity U r_4-2CV=L_0 r_1 and the bound
1+H^2 gcd(U,|L_0|)/max(U,|L_0|)
on the number of possible ordered pairs (r_1,r_4) in I_H^2.

The normalized identities in fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb show that r_2 does not divide b. Indeed, if r_2 divided b, then b r_4+c r_1=2u r_2 would imply r_2 divides c because r_1 and r_2 are distinct primes. The identity d r_2r_4-c r_1r_3=2C would then imply r_2 divides 2C, and since r_2 is odd this would contradict gcd(C,r_1r_2r_3r_4)=1. Similarly r_3 does not divide d: otherwise d r_4+a r_1=2u r_3 would give r_3|a, and b r_3r_4-a r_1r_2=2C would contradict the same unit condition.

Therefore U is nonzero modulo r_2, because U is congruent to (b r_3)^2 modulo r_2, and U is nonzero modulo r_3, because U is congruent to (d r_2)^2 modulo r_3. Thus gcd(U,r_2r_3)=1. It follows that gcd(U,|L_0|)<=2|K|, while max(U,|L_0|)>=|L_0|=2|K|r_2r_3. The multiplicity bound from fact 4832817b6b759101 is consequently at most
1+H^2/(r_2r_3)<2,
because r_2r_3>=H^4 and H>=2. Its left side counts an integer number of pairs, so at most one pair (r_1,r_4) is possible. Once b,d,r_1,r_4,r_2,r_3,C are fixed, the coupling identities from fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb,
a r_1r_2=b r_3r_4-2C and c r_1r_3=d r_2r_4-2C,
determine a and c uniquely. Hence fixed b,d support at most one state.

Multiplying the numbers of possible b and d values proves |Z_t|<=(1+X_box/m)^2. Since |A_t|<=|Z_t|, one has |A_t|^2<=|Z_t|^2<=(1+X_box/m)^2|Z_t|. Summation over t proves the coefficient-energy bound, and inserting it into the exact nonflat identity and discarding the nonnegative flat subtraction proves the displayed upper bound. Finally, X_box/m<=L H^delta under X_box<=LH^3 and m>=H^(3-delta), giving the last assertions. No step sums over the omitted outer variables, which proves the stated scope.

glossary.A_t: the total complex lift weight over Z_t
glossary.F_flat: the raw frequency preimage of all torus phases that vanish identically on every unit t
glossary.G_m: the four-slot Fourier transform of the lift-weighted torus family
glossary.N_lift: the total number sum_t |Z_t| of normalized lifts in the fixed data
glossary.Z_t: the exact normalized integer lift set over the unit torus point t with all literal selectors retained
glossary.delta_3: gcd(m,3), the number of universally phase-zero Kloosterman argument pairs

a84f95a82329a894.title: TENSOR-STABLE REPEATED-POLE OCCUPANCY AND VARYING-SELECTED-PRIME AGGREGATION WITHOUT A PRIME-CARDINALITY TAX. Let \(\mathcal P\) be a finite set of primes. For every \(p\in\mathcal P\), let \(\mathcal I_p\subset\mathbb F_p^\times\) be a nonzero additive interval of cardinality \(L_p\), and let \(\mathcal H_p\subset\mathbb F_p^\times\) and \(\mathcal R_p\subset\mathbb F_p\) be finite. Let \(E_p\) be a complex normed vector space. For every \((r,h,t)\in\mathcal R_p\times\mathcal H_p\times\mathcal I_p\), let \(\Lambda_p(r,h,t)\) be finite and let
a84f95a82329a894.author: slava chan
a84f95a82329a894.statement:
TENSOR-STABLE REPEATED-POLE OCCUPANCY AND VARYING-SELECTED-PRIME AGGREGATION WITHOUT A PRIME-CARDINALITY TAX. Let \(\mathcal P\) be a finite set of primes. For every \(p\in\mathcal P\), let \(\mathcal I_p\subset\mathbb F_p^\times\) be a nonzero additive interval of cardinality \(L_p\), and let \(\mathcal H_p\subset\mathbb F_p^\times\) and \(\mathcal R_p\subset\mathbb F_p\) be finite. Let \(E_p\) be a complex normed vector space. For every \((r,h,t)\in\mathcal R_p\times\mathcal H_p\times\mathcal I_p\), let \(\Lambda_p(r,h,t)\) be finite and let
\[
 v_{p,\lambda}(r,h,t)\in E_p.
\]
Define
\[
 A_p(r,h,t)=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda_p(r,h,t)}
 \|v_{p,\lambda}(r,h,t)\|_{E_p},\qquad
 U_p(r)=\sum_{h\in\mathcal H_p}\max_{t\in\mathcal I_p}A_p(r,h,t). \tag{1}
\]
For every ordered quadruple
\[
 \mathbf z=((r_i,h_i,t_i,\lambda_i))_{i=1}^4
\]
allow a possibly tuple-dependent four-linear functional
\[
 \mathcal K_{p,\mathbf z}:E_p^4\longrightarrow\mathbb C
\]
and a mask \(0\le D_{p,\mathbf z}\le1\), subject only to
\[
 |\mathcal K_{p,\mathbf z}(w_1,w_2,w_3,w_4)|
 \le D_{p,\mathbf z}\prod_{i=1}^4\|w_i\|_{E_p}. \tag{2}
\]
Let \(\mathscr V_p\) be the sum of the absolute values
\[
 |\mathcal K_{p,\mathbf z}(v_{p,\lambda_1},v_{p,\lambda_2},
 v_{p,\lambda_3},v_{p,\lambda_4})| \tag{3}
\]
over precisely the exceptional four-row equal-pole tuples of fact \(549328a9f587f158\): the signs are \((+,+,-,-)\), the equality partition of the \(r_i\) has no singleton, and every block satisfies the signed balance in \(h_it_i^{-1}\). Then, for every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 \mathscr V_p\ll_\varepsilon
 L_p^\varepsilon
 \left(L_p^{8/3}+\frac{L_p^4}{p}+3L_p^2\right)
 \left(\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_p}U_p(r)^2\right)^2. \tag{4}
\]
Thus all other completed prime faces may be retained inside \(E_p\), rather than summed mode by mode, whenever their exact four-row contraction has norm at most one as in (2). Pair-dependent deletion, the first-selected-prime condition, source masks, and cross-face bookkeeping may all remain in \(D_{p,\mathbf z}\).

There is no loss equal to \(\#\mathcal P\) when the selected prime varies. Fix \(\delta,\zeta>0\), assume
\[
 L_p\ge p^\delta,\qquad p\ge Q^\zeta\qquad(p\in\mathcal P), \tag{5}
\]
and fix
\[
 0<\eta<\min\{4\delta/3,1\}.
\]
Put
\[
 Y_p=L_p^2\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_p}U_p(r)^2. \tag{6}
\]
For all sufficiently large \(Q\),
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \sum_{p\in\mathcal P}\mathscr V_p
 \ll_{\delta,\eta,\zeta}
 Q^{-\zeta\eta}\left(\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}Y_p\right)^2.
 \quad} \tag{7}
\]
Consequently, if the varying-prime joint fourth-moment completion has trivial exceptional baseline \((\sum_pY_p)^2\) and enters under a fourth root, (7) gives a fixed factor \(Q^{-\zeta\eta/4}\), with no prime-cardinality factor. This conclusion is conditional only on the exact interval, lower-prime, and contraction hypotheses (2) and (5). It does not prove that the complete literal source admits one interval \(\mathcal I_p\) for every selected prime, that all remaining face operators form the contraction (2), or that distinct active products and cross-modulus source incidences have been assembled into these vectors.
a84f95a82329a894.proof:
Fix \(p\). By (2), every summand in (3) is at most
\[
 D_{p,\mathbf z}\prod_{i=1}^4
 \|v_{p,\lambda_i}(r_i,h_i,t_i)\|_{E_p}. \tag{8}
\]
This is exactly the scalar absolute source-copy product in fact \(549328a9f587f158\), with the scalar coefficient modulus replaced by the vector norm. Sum (8) first over the literal source labels \(\lambda_i\). The resulting fixed-row envelope is exactly the quantity \(A_p(r,h,t)\) in (1). All hypotheses of fact \(549328a9f587f158\) now hold with the same interval, height set, shift set, and tuple mask \(D_{p,\mathbf z}\). Its estimate (5) therefore gives (4). This argument never chooses coordinates in \(E_p\) and never sums a dual-mode basis; it uses only the contraction inequality (2). Hence normalized Hilbert tensor factors or any other remaining-face multilinear contraction can be kept inside \(E_p\).

Under (5), estimate (7) of fact \(549328a9f587f158\), applied at each \(p\), gives
\[
 \mathscr V_p\ll_{\delta,\eta}p^{-\eta}
 L_p^4\left(\sum_rU_p(r)^2\right)^2
 =p^{-\eta}Y_p^2. \tag{9}
\]
Since \(p\ge Q^\zeta\),
\[
 \sum_{p\in\mathcal P}\mathscr V_p
 \ll Q^{-\zeta\eta}\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}Y_p^2. \tag{10}
\]
Every \(Y_p\) is nonnegative, so
\[
 \sum_{p\in\mathcal P}Y_p^2
 \le\left(\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}Y_p\right)^2. \tag{11}
\]
Combining (10) and (11) proves (7). In particular, no estimate of \(\#\mathcal P\) was used. Taking a fourth root proves the final saving-factor statement. The last sentence lists the exact hypotheses not supplied by this abstract aggregation.

glossary.Y_p: The trivial fourth-moment scale L_p squared times the squared shift-envelope mass at the selected prime p.
glossary.\\\\mathcal K_{p,\\\\mathbf z}: A tuple-dependent four-linear contraction encoding the remaining completed prime faces and their bookkeeping.
glossary.\\\\mathscr V_p: The exceptional repeated-pole occupancy at p with all remaining face data retained in a normed vector and evaluated by a contractive four-linear form.

a88b7867c1bc2fd9.title: Fix
a88b7867c1bc2fd9.author: slava chan
a88b7867c1bc2fd9.statement:
Fix
\[
 1/2<\alpha<\beta<1,\qquad \eta>0,\qquad\rho>0,\qquad
 B_{\rm src}>0,\qquad U>0.
\]
Let \(W,\Phi\) be bounded real functions supported respectively in
\([\alpha,\beta]\) and \([1/2,2]\). Let \(N=2x\) be an integer with \(x\ge3\),
put
\[
 T_x=(\log x)^{6+\eta+\rho},
\]
and assume
\[
 {1\over2}x^{1/2}(\log x)^{-B_{\rm src}}\le D\le2x^{1/2},
 \qquad D>2T_x.
\]
Define
\[
 {\cal I}_D=\{w\ge2:(w,N)=1,\ \mu(w)\ne0,\ w\le x^{1/2},\
 \Phi(w/D)\ne0\},
\]
\[
 H_0=D(\log x)^{-6-\eta-\rho/2}.
\]
Fix a real number \(H\) with \(H_0\le H\le2D\), and put
\[
 {\cal H}_H=\{h\in\mathbb Z:H<|h|\le2H,\
                         |h|\le3D/2-H_0\}.             \tag{1}
\]
Fix dyadic real numbers \(Q_1,Q_2\ge1\). For \(h\in{\cal H}_H\) and
positive integers \(m,w,w-h,q_1,q_2\), put
\[
 p=N-mw,\qquad p'=N-m(w-h),
\]
and define
\[
\begin{split}
 A_{h,q_1,q_2}(m,w)=&
 {\bf1}_{w,w-h\in{\cal I}_D}{\bf1}_{p,p'>0}
 \mu(w)\mu(w-h)\mu(q_1)\mu(q_2)\\
 &\times\Phi(w/D)\Phi((w-h)/D)
 W(mw/x)W(m(w-h)/x)\Phi(p/U)\Phi(p'/U)\\
 &\times\log(p/q_1)\log(p'/q_2).                       \tag{2}
\end{split}
\]
Define the exact dyadic doubly expanded middle block
\[
\begin{split}
 {\cal V}_H(Q_1,Q_2)=
 \sum_{h\in{\cal H}_H}
 \sum_{\substack{Q_1\le q_1<2Q_1\\Q_2\le q_2<2Q_2}}
 \sum_{m,w}
 A_{h,q_1,q_2}(m,w)
 {\bf1}_{q_1\mid p}{\bf1}_{q_2\mid p'}.                \tag{3}
\end{split}
\]
Terms with \(\mu(q_1)\mu(q_2)=0\) vanish, so the active \(q_i\) are
squarefree. For an active tuple put
\[
 d=(q_1,q_2),\qquad c=[q_1,q_2],\qquad b=q_2/d.         \tag{4}
\]
Let \({\cal V}_H^{\rm cop}(Q_1,Q_2)\) be the restriction of (3) to
\[
 (N,c)=1,\qquad d\mid h,                                \tag{5}
\]
and define the exact support remainder
\[
 {\cal V}_H^{\rm supp}(Q_1,Q_2)
 ={\cal V}_H(Q_1,Q_2)-{\cal V}_H^{\rm cop}(Q_1,Q_2).    \tag{6}
\]
When \((N,c)=1\), the terms with \(d\nmid h\) are zero by congruence
compatibility. Thus (6) retains, rather than estimates, every noncoprime
divisor face of the full signed expansion.

For each tuple in (5), periodize (2) modulo \(c\):
\[
 A^{(c)}_{h,q_1,q_2}(a_1,a_2)=
 \sum_{\substack{m\equiv a_1\ ({\rm mod}\ c)\\
                 w\equiv a_2\ ({\rm mod}\ c)}}
 A_{h,q_1,q_2}(m,w),                                   \tag{7}
\]
and define its positive-sign finite Fourier transform
\[
 \widehat A_{h,q_1,q_2}(k,r)=
 \sum_{a_1,a_2\ ({\rm mod}\ c)}
 A^{(c)}_{h,q_1,q_2}(a_1,a_2)e_c(ka_1+ra_2).           \tag{8}
\]
Let
\[
 c_c(n)=\sum_{\substack{z\ ({\rm mod}\ c)\\(z,c)=1}}e_c(nz).
\]
Define
\[
\begin{split}
 {\cal Z}_H(Q_1,Q_2)=
 \sum_{\substack{h,q_1,q_2\ {\rm as\ in}\ (3)\\(N,c)=1,\ d\mid h}}
 {1\over c^2}\Bigg\{&
 \sum_{r\ ({\rm mod}\ c)}
 \widehat A(0,r)e_b(-rhq_1^{-1})c_c(r)\\
 &+\sum_{k\ ({\rm mod}\ c)}
 \widehat A(k,0)c_c(k)
 -\widehat A(0,0)\phi(c)\Bigg\},                       \tag{9}
\end{split}
\]
where the tuple subscripts on \(\widehat A\) are suppressed, and define
\[
\begin{split}
 {\cal N}_H(Q_1,Q_2)=
 \sum_{\substack{h,q_1,q_2\ {\rm as\ in}\ (3)\\(N,c)=1,\ d\mid h}}
 {1\over c^2}
 \sum_{\substack{k,r\ ({\rm mod}\ c)\\k\ne0,\ r\ne0}}
 \widehat A(k,r)e_b(-rhq_1^{-1})S(r,kN;c).             \tag{10}
\end{split}
\]
Then the exact literal decomposition is
\[
 \boxed{
 {\cal V}_H(Q_1,Q_2)
 =
 {\cal V}_H^{\rm supp}(Q_1,Q_2)
 +{\cal Z}_H(Q_1,Q_2)
 +{\cal N}_H(Q_1,Q_2).
 }                                                       \tag{11}
\]
The subtraction in (9) counts the intersection \(k=r=0\) exactly once.

Put
\[
 Y_{\rm mod}=
 {xD(\log x)^{-6-\eta}\over\log(2T_x)}.                \tag{12}
\]
The three one-sided estimates
\[
 {\cal V}_H^{\rm supp}(Q_1,Q_2)\ll Y_{\rm mod},\qquad
 {\cal Z}_H(Q_1,Q_2)\ll Y_{\rm mod},\qquad
 {\cal N}_H(Q_1,Q_2)\ll Y_{\rm mod}                    \tag{13}
\]
uniformly in the displayed dyadic parameters imply the
TWO-MOD-REFLECTED estimate of fact d97b0142b0d0a486, up to an absolute
factor three. The middle estimate in (13) is the precise
ZERO-MOD-REFLECTED contract for this literal family. No estimate in (13)
is proved here.

For a fixed tuple, a fixed-modulus bilinear Kloosterman theorem can be
applied to (10) only after an exact decomposition
\[
 \widehat A(k,r)=\sum_z\alpha_z(r)\beta_z(k)            \tag{14}
\]
and payment of the projective tax
\[
 {\cal P}(A)=
 \inf_{(14)}\sum_z\|\alpha_z\|_2\|\beta_z\|_2.          \tag{15}
\]
The outer assembly further requires the sum of these taxes over the
literal \(h,q_1,q_2\) family. Neither TMC-EXACT of fact
967520f427b111c5 nor finite Fourier inversion bounds (15). Fact
d3fde76ac4c8c20d shows that the recorded direct full-axis fixed-modulus
route gives no fixed-power saving when one arbitrary coefficient axis
has full length \(c\). This is a scoped no-direct-fit: it identifies the
literal family tax still required and makes no tuplewise arbitrary-row
claim about (8).
a88b7867c1bc2fd9.proof:
All sums in (2) are finite by the support of \(W\) and \(\Phi\).
For a fixed tuple in (5), let
\[
 I(a_1,a_2)=
 {\bf1}_{a_1a_2\equiv N\ ({\rm mod}\ q_1)}
 {\bf1}_{a_1(a_2-h)\equiv N\ ({\rm mod}\ q_2)}.
\]
Finite Fourier inversion and the convention (8) give
\[
\begin{split}
 \sum_{a_1,a_2\ ({\rm mod}\ c)}
 A^{(c)}(a_1,a_2)I(a_1,a_2)
 ={1\over c^2}\sum_{k,r\ ({\rm mod}\ c)}
 \widehat A(k,r){\cal K}_{q_1,q_2}(r,k;N,h),            \tag{16}
\end{split}
\]
where \({\cal K}_{q_1,q_2}\) is the negative-sign complete sum of fact
967520f427b111c5. That fact gives
\[
 {\cal K}_{q_1,q_2}(r,k;N,h)
 =e_b(-rhq_1^{-1})S(r,kN;c).                           \tag{17}
\]
The left side of (16) is exactly the \(m,w\) sum in (3) for this tuple,
by the periodization (7).

Split the finite frequency square into the union \(k=0\) or \(r=0\) and
its complement \(k\ne0,r\ne0\). Fact 967520f427b111c5 gives
\[
 S(r,0;c)=c_c(r),\qquad S(0,kN;c)=c_c(k),\qquad
 S(0,0;c)=\phi(c).                                     \tag{18}
\]
Adding the \(k=0\) line and the \(r=0\) line counts the origin twice, so
subtracting its value once gives exactly (9). The complementary frequency
set gives (10). Hence (16)--(18), summed over the tuples in (5), prove
\[
 {\cal V}_H^{\rm cop}={\cal Z}_H+{\cal N}_H.
\]
Adding the definition (6) proves (11).

The compatibility assertion following (6) is the generalized CRT
condition in fact d97b0142b0d0a486: when \((N,c)=1\), in particular
\((d,N)=1\), it reduces to \(d\mid h\). No noncoprime term is discarded.

Equation (11) and the three one-sided inequalities (13) give
\[
 {\cal V}_H(Q_1,Q_2)\ll3Y_{\rm mod}.
\]
This is the uniform dyadic estimate called TWO-MOD-REFLECTED in fact
d97b0142b0d0a486, with only a harmless change of implied constant. That
fact proves its sufficiency for TB-SHIFT-BLOCK and TB-FEJ-RES.

Finally, a bilinear Kloosterman estimate accepts separated coefficient
sequences in the two frequency variables. Formula (10) has the joint
literal array (8), so (14) is the exact required interface and the triangle
assembly costs (15). The tuple sum in (10) forces the corresponding outer
family sum. The cited facts supply neither decomposition nor tax bound;
fact d3fde76ac4c8c20d supplies only the stated direct full-axis
no-saving result. This proves the scoped no-direct-fit without asserting
that the literal row is arbitrary.

glossary.A^{(c)}_{h,q_1,q_2}: the exact residue-periodized literal signed coefficient modulo c
glossary.ZERO-MOD-REFLECTED: the one-sided target estimate for cal Z_H
glossary.cal N_H: the exact nonzero-k, nonzero-r literal TMC aggregate
glossary.cal P(A): the projective coefficient tax required to separate the two TMC frequency variables
glossary.cal V_H^supp: the exact noncoprime divisor-face remainder of the doubly expanded middle block
glossary.cal Z_H: the exact inclusion-exclusion aggregate of the k=0 or r=0 literal TMC modes
glossary.widehat A_{h,q_1,q_2}: the positive-sign two-dimensional finite Fourier transform of the literal periodized coefficient

a8d14bd3414bf66e.title: ACTUAL C1 FIXED-ROW FIRST-NONRESONANT-PRIME q-PAIR PAYMENT WITH THE EXACT DETERMINANT MASK
a8d14bd3414bf66e.author: slava chan
a8d14bd3414bf66e.statement:
ACTUAL C1 FIXED-ROW FIRST-NONRESONANT-PRIME q-PAIR PAYMENT WITH THE EXACT DETERMINANT MASK.

Adopt one actual strict-top C1 copy lambda from fact ff228b0e569531f8. Thus its canonical marked dilator is the unique rough prime
  d_lambda=p,                                                  (1)
its normalized marked integer is n=pv, and its physical reciprocal modulus is q in [Q,2Q). Fix two supported nonzero heights h_1,h_2 and the corresponding natural p-cofactor data, and assume the p-local numerators
  C_1,C_2 in F_p^*
are nonzero. Let c_i be squarefree auxiliary integers, polynomially bounded in Q, containing the exact row coprimality data gn_i. Let A_i be two physical q-profiles with
  V_Q(A_i)<infinity.                                           (2)
Put
  a_i(q)=mu(q)1_{(q,c_i)=1}A_i(q),                             (3)
extended by zero outside Q<=q<2Q, and define the exact C1 nonresonant pair sum
  P_p(A_1,A_2)
  =sum_{q_1,q_2}
    a_1(q_1)conjugate(a_2(q_2))
    e_p(C_1q_1^(-1)-C_2q_2^(-1))
    1_{C_1q_1^(-1)!=C_2q_2^(-1)}.                             (4)
The last factor is exactly the selected-first-nonresonant-prime determinant mask for C1, because d_lambda has no smaller divisor prime.

Fix zeta>0 and assume
  Q^zeta<=p<=2Q^(6/5).                                        (5)
Then there exists delta_1=delta_1(zeta)>0 such that
  |P_p(A_1,A_2)|
  <<_zeta V_Q(A_1)V_Q(A_2)Q^(2-delta_1).                      (6)
One may take any
  delta_1<(1/2)min{2delta_0,1,zeta},                           (7)
where delta_0 is an exponent furnished by fact c23ca78883ba83d9.

After inserting the actual mode expansions of fact 71f1a10b52148348 and summing their x^{o(1)} coefficient mass, every fixed-n,h_1,h_2 actual C1 pair with its exact first-p mask satisfies the same bound (6) up to Q^{o(1)} and the displayed Fourier-decay factors. All provenance siblings have already been recombined legally.

If a four-row expression is the product of two independent TT-star C1 pairs at the same p and its only q-dependent tuple mask is the product of their two exact determinant masks, then the q-sum factorizes and is
  <<Q^(4-2delta_1+o(1))                                       (8)
times the four bounded-variation profile norms and scalar mode coefficients.

This is a maximal fixed-row q-profile theorem. It does not cover an additional cross-pair tuple deletion, couple varying n,h,t or selected primes, compare the resulting local envelope with the complete joint-completion Hilbert norm, pay short/zero-height chambers, estimate C2-C4 lower-prime masks, or prove a complete C1 trace or Goldbach conclusion.
a8d14bd3414bf66e.proof:
Because the C1 representation has one rough prime, fact f0f6807663d3ef3c gives d_lambda=p. Fact 4f9aec67f5be35db says that a nonresonant TT-star pair selects the least prime dividing d_lambda which does not divide the target times the determinant. Under (1), this is p exactly when
  C_1q_1^(-1)!=C_2q_2^(-1),                                   (9)
equivalently when p does not divide the actual determinant after the verified natural-cofactor normalization. There is no smaller-prime condition.

Remove the mask in (4) and factor the unrestricted sum:
  S_1= sum_q a_1(q)e_p(C_1q^(-1)),
  S_2= sum_q a_2(q)e_p(C_2q^(-1)).
Then
  P_p(A_1,A_2)=S_1conjugate(S_2)-R_p,                          (10)
where R_p is the same weighted sum restricted to
  C_1q_1^(-1)=C_2q_2^(-1) mod p.                              (11)
Fact c23ca78883ba83d9 applies to each S_i under (2)-(5), giving
  |S_i|<<V_Q(A_i)Q^(1-delta_0).                               (12)
Hence
  |S_1S_2|<<V_Q(A_1)V_Q(A_2)Q^(2-2delta_0).                   (13)

For the resonant term, equation (11) is
  q_2=C_2C_1^(-1)q_1 mod p.                                   (14)
For each physical integer q_1 in [Q,2Q), the interval [Q,2Q) contains at most
  1+Q/p
integers q_2 in the residue (14). Since |mu(q_i)|<=1 and ||A_i||_infinity<=V_Q(A_i),
  |R_p|
  <=V_Q(A_1)V_Q(A_2)Q(1+Q/p)
  <<V_Q(A_1)V_Q(A_2)
    {Q+Q^(2-zeta)}.                                           (15)
Equations (13)-(15) prove (6)-(7).

Fact ff228b0e569531f8 gives the exact actual C1 q-profile mode by mode, including the squarefree auxiliary coprimality integer. Fact 71f1a10b52148348 proves that the sum of the scalar mode masses weighted by V_Q(A_i) is Q^{o(1)} with arbitrary Fourier decay. Apply (6) to every ordered pair of modes and sum their absolute coefficient masses. This proves the actual fixed-row specialization.

Finally, when a four-row q-dependent coefficient and mask are a tensor product of two such TT-star pair expressions, finite Fubini factorizes its q-sum into the product of two copies of (4). Applying (6) twice proves (8). No step controls a nonfactorizing cross-pair mask or any of the other variables, proving every scope limitation.

glossary.P_p(A_1,A_2): The actual fixed-row C1 two-row q-sum with p selected by the exact nonresonant determinant mask.
glossary.R_p: The excluded p-resonant slope-diagonal contribution in the C1 pair.

a924b399d9dcbd8a.title: DISCRETE HARD-MASK VARIATION OBSTRUCTION FOR A DYADIC MÖBIUS RAY
a924b399d9dcbd8a.author: slava chan
a924b399d9dcbd8a.statement:
DISCRETE HARD-MASK VARIATION OBSTRUCTION FOR A DYADIC MÖBIUS RAY.

Let \(K\ge64\) be an integer and let
\[
\mathcal S_K=\{k\in\mathbb Z:K\le k<2K,\ \mu(k)\ne0\}
=\{s_1<s_2<\cdots<s_M\}.
\]
Define a zero-one mask \(W_K\) on \(\mathcal S_K\) by
\[
W_K(s_j)=
\begin{cases}
0,&j\ {\rm odd},\\
1,&j\ {\rm even}.
\end{cases}
\]
Suppose that \(T\) is a finite set, \(\alpha_t\in\mathbb C\), and
\(f_t:[1,2]\to\mathbb C\) has bounded variation for every \(t\in T\), with
\[
\|f_t\|_\infty+\operatorname {Var}_{[1,2]}(f_t)\le1,
\]
and that the exact representation
\[
W_K(k)=\sum_{t\in T}\alpha_tf_t(k/K)                              \tag{1}
\]
holds for every \(k\in\mathcal S_K\). Then
\[
\boxed{\sum_{t\in T}|\alpha_t|\ge {K\over16}.}                    \tag{2}
\]

Consequently, dyadic localization, the support condition \(\mu(k)\ne0\), a zero-one hard mask, and a uniform pointwise envelope do not by themselves imply a \((\log K)^{O(1)}\)-cost exact decomposition into uniformly bounded-variation weights. Applied as a theorem-interface audit to facts e55b27d39c593164 and a36284a9dbec7837, this means that a fixed-polylogarithmic bounded-variation decomposition of the actual literal factor
\[
\widehat{\mathcal F}_{k,n}(\varepsilon_{\rm or}\epsilon kb/n)
\Xi_\lambda(k,\epsilon kb,n)
\]
requires an additional source-genealogy or recombination theorem; it cannot be deduced merely from the support, squarefreeness, pointwise coefficient envelope, and the fact that \(\Xi_\lambda\) is a zero-one hard mask. The constructed mask \(W_K\) is an abstract admissible support-mask model and is not asserted to equal the actual literal \(\Xi_\lambda\). This fact therefore proves a scoped no-inference result, not failure of a source-specific recombination, not a lower bound for UNIT-RAY-SRC, and not a Goldbach conclusion.
a924b399d9dcbd8a.proof:
An integer \(k\in[K,2K)\) fails to be squarefree only if \(m^2\mid k\) for some integer \(m\) satisfying
\[
2\le m\le\sqrt{2K}.
\]
For a fixed \(m\), the number of multiples of \(m^2\) in \([K,2K)\) is at most
\[
{K\over m^2}+1.
\]
Therefore the number of nonsquarefree integers in the interval is at most
\[
K\sum_{m=2}^\infty{1\over m^2}+\sqrt{2K}.
\]
The elementary integral comparison
\[
\sum_{m=2}^\infty{1\over m^2}
\le {1\over4}+{1\over9}+\int_3^\infty{dt\over t^2}
={25\over36}
\]
gives
\[
M=|\mathcal S_K|\ge {11K\over36}-\sqrt{2K}.                     \tag{3}
\]
For \(K\ge64\),
\[
{11K\over36}-\sqrt{2K}-{K\over8}
={13K\over72}-\sqrt{2K}\ge0,
\]
because
\[
{13\over72}\sqrt K\ge{13\over9}>\sqrt2.
\]
Thus
\[
M\ge K/8.                                                        \tag{4}
\]

By construction, consecutive values of \(W_K\) on the ordered squarefree support differ by one. Hence
\[
M-1
=\sum_{j=1}^{M-1}|W_K(s_{j+1})-W_K(s_j)|.                       \tag{5}
\]
Use (1) and the triangle inequality in (5):
\[
\begin{aligned}
M-1
&\le\sum_{j=1}^{M-1}\sum_{t\in T}
|\alpha_t|\,
|f_t(s_{j+1}/K)-f_t(s_j/K)|\\
&=\sum_{t\in T}|\alpha_t|
\sum_{j=1}^{M-1}
|f_t(s_{j+1}/K)-f_t(s_j/K)|\\
&\le\sum_{t\in T}|\alpha_t|
\operatorname {Var}_{[1,2]}(f_t)\\
&\le\sum_{t\in T}|\alpha_t|.
\end{aligned}                                                     \tag{6}
\]
Equation (4) and \(K\ge64\) imply
\[
M-1\ge K/8-1\ge K/16.
\]
Together with (6), this proves (2).

Fact a36284a9dbec7837 identifies the exact good-\(\mathscr W\) ray weight as the Fourier-and-mask product displayed in the statement and explicitly records that fact e55b27d39c593164 assumes no bounded-variation representation of that combined weight. The example above satisfies precisely the abstract numerical properties listed in the scoped consequence: dyadic support, squarefree Möbius support, zero-one masking and bounded magnitude. Its projective variation cost is linear in \(K\). Therefore those numerical properties alone cannot imply fixed-polylogarithmic cost. Since the example is not identified with the actual source mask, the conclusion is only the stated logical no-inference result and leaves a source-specific recombination open.

glossary.hard-mask variation obstruction: The linear lower bound for exact normalized bounded-variation projective representations of an alternating mask on squarefree dyadic support.

a94835cfd97853a0.title: Assume the hypotheses and notation of fact 3bb378b0a49679f9, and let z=(D,M,R,K;d,m,r,k) lie in its forward 1x1 component. If D>64, then r>d. Consequently the maximal-gcd layer g_z=p ell_p is empty on this range, and only g_z in {1,p,ell_p} can occur. In particular the physical quotient modulus b_z=p ell_p/g_z is respectively p ell_p, ell_p, or p and is always greater than one. Thus every forward-1x1 incidence with D>64 has at least one nontrivial primitive additive-conductor term in the exact quotient-modulus detector of fact 3bb378b0a49679f9. This removes the modulus-one alternative of fact eed7c65b2f8b19a3 on the large-D endpoint range, but it still does not construct a primitive unit-residue fourth moment or a carrier/window packet leaf
a94835cfd97853a0.author: slava chan
a94835cfd97853a0.statement: Assume the hypotheses and notation of fact 3bb378b0a49679f9, and let z=(D,M,R,K;d,m,r,k) lie in its forward 1x1 component. If D>64, then r>d. Consequently the maximal-gcd layer g_z=p ell_p is empty on this range, and only g_z in {1,p,ell_p} can occur. In particular the physical quotient modulus b_z=p ell_p/g_z is respectively p ell_p, ell_p, or p and is always greater than one. Thus every forward-1x1 incidence with D>64 has at least one nontrivial primitive additive-conductor term in the exact quotient-modulus detector of fact 3bb378b0a49679f9. This removes the modulus-one alternative of fact eed7c65b2f8b19a3 on the large-D endpoint range, but it still does not construct a primitive unit-residue fourth moment or a carrier/window packet leaf.
a94835cfd97853a0.proof:
Because z is an original labelled incidence with nonzero dyadic factors, the support of Phi in fact 91db48815d136d4c gives d/D in [1/2,2] and r/R in [1/2,2]. Hence d<=2D and r>=R/2. Forward boundary-admissibility defines beta=log(R)/log(D) and requires beta>=4/3. Since D>64>1, R=D^beta>=D^(4/3), so
r>=R/2>=D^(4/3)/2=D D^(1/3)/2>2D>=d,
because D^(1/3)>4. Therefore r>d.

Fact 3bb378b0a49679f9 gives r=p ell_p and g_z=gcd(d,r). If g_z=p ell_p=r, then r divides d and hence r<=d for positive integers, contradicting r>d. Thus g_z is not p ell_p. The same fact lists the only four possible gcd values, leaving 1,p,ell_p. Substitution into b_z=p ell_p/g_z gives p ell_p,ell_p,p, all greater than one because p and ell_p are primes. The detector in that fact includes primitive additive conductors e dividing b_z, in particular e=b_z>1. The final sentence only limits scope and makes no further inference.

a9a0e9af2477d71d.title: FOURIER-STABLE COMPLETE TRANSLATION CORRELATION FOR FOUR RANK-ONE RECIPROCAL POLES
a9a0e9af2477d71d.author: slava chan
a9a0e9af2477d71d.statement:
FOURIER-STABLE COMPLETE TRANSLATION CORRELATION FOR FOUR RANK-ONE RECIPROCAL POLES.

Let p>=7 be prime. Give four positions signs sigma_1=sigma_2=+1 and sigma_3=sigma_4=-1. Let
  r_i in F_p,  h_i,t_i in F_p^*  (1<=i<=4),
and put
  R(X)=sum_{i=1}^4 sigma_i h_i/[t_i(X+r_i)] in F_p(X).          (1)
For xi in F_p define the complete translation correlation
  C_p(r,h,t;xi)
  =sum_{X in F_p, X!=-r_i for every i}
    e_p(R(X)+xi X).                                            (2)
Let d(r) be the number of distinct residues among r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4.

Exactly one of the following alternatives holds.

EXCEPTIONAL ZERO-FOURIER MODE. One has xi=0 and, for every residue a represented among the r_i,
  sum_{i:r_i=a}sigma_i h_i/t_i=0 mod p.                        (3)
Then R=0 in F_p(X) and
  C_p(r,h,t;0)=p-d(r).                                         (4)

NONEXCEPTIONAL MODE. Condition (3) together with xi=0 fails. Then
  |C_p(r,h,t;xi)|<=10sqrt(p).                                  (5)

Thus adding the linear Fourier phase xi X creates no new order-p exceptional locus: every xi!=0 mode has square-root cancellation, and at xi=0 the order-p locus is exactly the no-singleton repeated-pole block-balance locus of fact 7d341c8eec44f7a3. The estimate is uniform in repeated shifts and in all physical-height sign sectors.

This is a complete one-prime correlation theorem. It does not control the Fourier l1 or l2 aggregation of moving literal q-profiles, create a source-preserving common-X operator, compare a translation-Hilbert envelope with the complete source norm, retain varying composite moduli, or prove a C1-C4 trace or Goldbach estimate.
a9a0e9af2477d71d.proof:
Group equal shifts in (1). If A is the set of distinct represented shifts, put
  c_a=sum_{i:r_i=a}sigma_i h_i/t_i.
Then
  R(X)+xi X=sum_{a in A}c_a/(X+a)+xi X.                        (6)
Fact 7d341c8eec44f7a3 proves that R is zero if and only if every c_a is zero. Hence if xi=0 and (3) holds, the phase is zero at every X retained in (2). Exactly d(r) residues are excluded, which proves (4).

Assume now that the exceptional alternative fails. Let m be the number of shifts a in A with c_a nonzero and k the number with c_a=0. Thus
  m+k=d(r)<=4.                                                 (7)
Delete from (6) every zero term and call the resulting reduced rational function F(X). If xi=0, then m>=1 and F has exactly m finite simple projective poles. If xi!=0, F has those m finite simple poles and one further simple pole at infinity, so it has s=m+1 projective poles. In either case F is nonconstant and 1<=s<=5.

There are p+1>=8 rational points on P^1(F_p), so one can choose a rational point b which is not a pole of F. Apply a fractional linear change of variable sending b to infinity. The transformed rational function is regular at infinity and has the same s distinct simple projective poles, now all finite. Write it in reduced form f(Y)/g(Y). Then g is a product of s distinct linear factors, so
  deg(g)=s,
and regularity at infinity gives
  deg(f)<=deg(g).                                               (8)

The transformed rational function is not of the form H(Y)^p-H(Y) over the algebraic closure. Indeed it has a simple pole, whereas every pole of H^p-H has order divisible by p: if H has a pole of order u, the H^p term has order pu and cannot be cancelled by the term H of order u.

Makhul and Winterhof, arXiv:2106.12218, Lemma 2, state that for a nontrivial additive character of F_q and a rational function f/g which is not H^p-H, if deg(f)<=deg(g) and g has s distinct algebraic roots, then
  |sum_{y in F_q:g(y)!=0} psi(f(y)/g(y))|
  <=(deg(g)+s-2)sqrt(q)+1.                                    (9)
Apply (9) with q=p.

We now compare domains while retaining the k original physical exclusions at which c_a=0. If xi!=0, then s=m+1, so (9) bounds the transformed reduced affine sum by
  2m sqrt(p)+1.
Returning to the original affine domain can change at most the k regular-but-physically-excluded points X=-a with c_a=0 and the one regular point b which the projective change sends to infinity. Therefore
  |C_p(r,h,t;xi)|<=2m sqrt(p)+k+2<=8sqrt(p)+2.                 (10)
Here the original point at infinity is a pole because xi!=0 and contributes no further comparison term.

If xi=0, then s=m, so (9) gives
  (2m-2)sqrt(p)+1.
The original point at infinity is regular, the k zero-coefficient physical shifts remain excluded, and the transformed point at infinity is the chosen regular point b. Accounting for all of them costs at most k+2 unit terms. Hence
  |C_p(r,h,t;0)|
  <=(2m-2)sqrt(p)+k+3<=6sqrt(p)+3.                             (11)
Equations (10)-(11) are at most 10sqrt(p) for p>=7, proving (5), the dichotomy, and all scope statements.

glossary.C_p(r,h,t;xi): The complete common-translation correlation of four reciprocal poles with an added linear Fourier frequency.
glossary.d(r): The number of distinct pole shifts among the four rows.

aa34b1862b993377.title: Assume all hypotheses and notation of fact 91db48815d136d4c. In particular, z=(D,M,R,K;d,m,r,k) ranges over the original finite set of labelled incidences with nonzero real weight w(z), the controlled-label aggregate C_N has first precedence, and forward and reverse boundary-admissibility and the four tags 1x1, 2x1, 2x2, asymmetric are those of that fact. For every labelled incidence outside the controlled label set put q_sib(z)=r k and
aa34b1862b993377.author: slava chan
aa34b1862b993377.statement:
Assume all hypotheses and notation of fact 91db48815d136d4c. In particular, z=(D,M,R,K;d,m,r,k) ranges over the original finite set of labelled incidences with nonzero real weight w(z), the controlled-label aggregate C_N has first precedence, and forward and reverse boundary-admissibility and the four tags 1x1, 2x1, 2x2, asymmetric are those of that fact. For every labelled incidence outside the controlled label set put q_sib(z)=r k and
beta_q(z)=2 log r/log(r k).
Because w(z) is nonzero, k>1. Partition these outside-controlled original labelled incidences into the following five cells using the actual sibling integers r,k:
Z_low: r<k;
Z_diag: r=k;
Z_mid: k<r<k^2;
Z_end: k^2<=r<k^3;
Z_sup: r>=k^3.
These cells are disjoint and exhaustive, and they are equivalently characterized by
beta_q<1, beta_q=1, 1<beta_q<4/3, 4/3<=beta_q<3/2, beta_q>=3/2,
respectively.

Refine Z_end as follows. For every tag a in {1x1,2x1,2x2,asymmetric}, let Z_end,F,a be the incidences in Z_end that are forward boundary-admissible with tag a, and let Z_end,R,a be the incidences in Z_end that are reverse boundary-admissible with tag a. Let Z_end,gap be the incidences in Z_end that are neither forward nor reverse boundary-admissible, namely the intersection of Z_end with the old U-cell of fact 91db48815d136d4c. The resulting nine sets are pairwise disjoint and have union Z_end. A reverse tag is computed after the swap in fact 91db48815d136d4c; its boundary divisors divide the original integer d, so it is a swapped-d-side tag and is not an r-anatomy tag.

Let E0_N be the sum of w(z) over these nine endpoint pieces, let S_N be the sum over Z_sup, let U_{T,N} be the sum over Z_low, Z_diag and Z_mid, and put T_N=E0_N+S_N. Then
H_N=C_N+T_N+U_{T,N}
exactly before any absolute value. Every original labelled incidence occurs exactly once with its fixed N, both Moebius signs, logarithms, smooth weights and dyadic factors unchanged. This remains true after multiplying w(z) by an arbitrary auxiliary coefficient depending on the entire labelled incidence, including target, gcd, unit, stopping, overlap, or centered-conductor provenance.

The classification is deliberately made on each original labelled incidence using its actual r,k. It is not made using the smooth labels R,K: the supports of Phi(r/R) and Phi(k/K) allow label overlap and do not turn inequalities between R,K into exact inequalities between r,k. If the same integer tuple occurs under more than one nonzero smooth label, each labelled occurrence is retained with its original partition weight. Forward and reverse incidences are not identified, and no quotient by swap orbits is taken.

Every terminal atom z in E0_N or S_N has a nonzero sibling factor mu(r)log k and belongs to a composite non-prime-power q_sib(z)=r k whose complete divisor-sibling sum is zero:
sum_{r' k'=q_sib(z)}mu(r')log k'=0.
This does not imply T_N=0, E0_N=0, or S_N=0, because the terminal, controlled-label, smooth-label, anatomy, and auxiliary selectors can split the complete sibling orbit. The diagonal cell Z_diag must in particular be retained in U_{T,N}: when r=k=p is prime, q_sib=p^2 and the sibling factor mu(p)log p=-log p is genuinely nonzero while Lambda(p^2)=log p.

Finally suppose H_N<0 and define A_N^*=-H_N>0. For every capture fraction theta_N in (0,1] and every real rho_N, the following two inequalities are equivalent:
C_N+U_{T,N}>=-(1-theta_N)A_N^*-rho_N,
T_N<=-theta_N A_N^*+rho_N.
Along any sequence for which rho_N=o(theta_N A_N^*), this is an exact deficit slot with a negligible relative error. In particular, the separated hypotheses
|C_N|=o(theta_N A_N^*)
and
U_{T,N}>=-(1-theta_N)A_N^*-o(theta_N A_N^*)
are sufficient for
T_N<=-theta_N A_N^*+o(theta_N A_N^*)
and hence
min(E0_N,S_N)<=-theta_N A_N^*/2+o(theta_N A_N^*).
For the bad even integers in fact 2827630745a3225b, H_N<0 for all sufficiently large N and A_N^*=c_W mathfrak_c(N)x+o(mathfrak_c(N)x). The theorem is an exact algebraic refinement and deficit interface; it supplies no analytic estimate for C_N or U_{T,N}, and it does not assert endpoint localization by support.
aa34b1862b993377.proof:
We first prove the five-cell equivalence. Since w(z) is nonzero and contains the factor log k, one has k>1. Put alpha=log r and gamma=log k. Then alpha>=0, gamma>0, and beta_q=2alpha/(alpha+gamma) has positive denominator. Direct cross multiplication gives
beta_q<1 iff 2alpha<alpha+gamma iff alpha<gamma iff r<k,
beta_q=1 iff alpha=gamma iff r=k.
Similarly,
beta_q<4/3 iff 6alpha<4alpha+4gamma iff alpha<2gamma iff r<k^2,
and
beta_q<3/2 iff 4alpha<3alpha+3gamma iff alpha<3gamma iff r<k^3.
Combining these comparisons with their complementary weak inequalities proves exactly the five displayed ranges, including the boundary conventions r=k^2 at beta_q=4/3 and r=k^3 at beta_q=3/2. The order alternatives for positive integers r,k are disjoint and exhaustive, so the five cells are a partition.

Now impose the C-precedence already verified in fact 91db48815d136d4c and fix an outside-controlled incidence in Z_end. Fact 91db48815d136d4c proves that forward and reverse boundary-admissibility are mutually exclusive. If one orientation is admissible, that fact assigns exactly one of the four tags. If neither is admissible, the incidence lies in its old U-cell. Intersecting this verified disjoint alternative with Z_end therefore produces exactly the four forward pieces, four reverse pieces, and one gap piece, with no overlap and with union Z_end. Under reverse admissibility the simultaneous swap replaces (d,m,r,k) by (r,k,d,m); hence the variable playing the boundary-divisor role after the swap is the original d. This proves the required interpretation of reverse tags.

Outside the controlled set, Z_low, Z_diag, Z_mid, Z_end and Z_sup partition every original labelled incidence. The definitions of E0_N, S_N and U_{T,N} group the fourth, fifth, and first three cells, respectively. Thus, pointwise on the finite original labelled-incidence set,
1=1_{controlled}+1_{Z_low union Z_diag union Z_mid}+1_{Z_end}+1_{Z_sup}.
Inside Z_end its indicator is the disjoint sum of the nine refined indicators proved in the previous paragraph. Multiplication by w(z) and summation gives H_N=C_N+T_N+U_{T,N} and T_N=E0_N+S_N. Fact 91db48815d136d4c proves that the controlled set is a set rather than a list of membership reasons and that its exact original weights are retained. The present refinement only multiplies outside-controlled weights by further zero-one selectors. Hence it preserves every factor and remains exact after insertion of an arbitrary incidence-dependent auxiliary coefficient. In particular, the centered conductor identity of fact 676c6a2cb3ebf7cc may be carried as such a coefficient within any refined cell without moving its parent incidence.

This proof partitions labelled incidences, not unlabelled integer tuples. Smooth support only says that r/R and k/K lie in the support interval of Phi; it does not identify r with R or k with K, and adjacent dyadic labels can both have nonzero Phi-weight for one integer. Since the new selectors inspect the actual r,k separately on every original labelled occurrence, such overlap causes no leakage across the five actual scale cells. The reverse predicate is used only as a predicate on the original incidence. No equivalence relation or swap quotient is introduced, so distinct original occurrences remain distinct.

We next prove the zero-orbit assertion. If z is terminal, then z lies in Z_end or Z_sup, so r>=k^2. Since k>1, one has r>k and therefore r>sqrt(r k). Nonzero w(z) also implies mu(r)log k is nonzero. Apply fact b7fcb27a091203e5 with q=q_sib(z)=r k. It proves that q_sib(z) is composite and not a prime power and that its complete sibling sum is zero. This is an assertion about the complete arithmetic family of every factorization r'k'=q_sib. The terminal selector retains only factorizations satisfying its actual-scale, controlled-label, admissibility, tag, smooth-label, and possible auxiliary predicates, so it need not retain the other siblings needed for the cancellation. Consequently no vanishing of a selected terminal aggregate follows.

For the diagonal warning, take r=k=p prime. Then mu(r)log k=mu(p)log p=-log p is nonzero, while q_sib=p^2 and the definition of the von Mangoldt function gives Lambda(p^2)=log p. This is also the j=2 case explicitly proved in fact b7fcb27a091203e5. Therefore deleting or terminalizing the full equality cell would discard genuine von-Mangoldt support.

It remains to prove the deficit statements. The exact partition and A_N^*=-H_N give
C_N+T_N+U_{T,N}=-A_N^*,
so
T_N=-A_N^*-(C_N+U_{T,N}).
For fixed theta_N and rho_N, the inequality
C_N+U_{T,N}>=-(1-theta_N)A_N^*-rho_N
is equivalent after multiplication by -1 and addition of -A_N^* to
T_N<=-A_N^*+(1-theta_N)A_N^*+rho_N=-theta_N A_N^*+rho_N.
This proves both directions of the equivalence with exactly the same error.

Under the separated hypotheses,
C_N+U_{T,N}>=-|C_N|+U_{T,N}
>=-(1-theta_N)A_N^*-o(theta_N A_N^*).
Apply the proved equivalence to obtain the asserted upper bound for T_N. Since E0_N and S_N are real and sum to T_N, their minimum is at most their arithmetic mean T_N/2, proving the final displayed estimate.

Finally fact 2827630745a3225b gives H_N=-c_W mathfrak_c(N)x+o(mathfrak_c(N)x) with c_W mathfrak_c(N)x positive along sufficiently large bad even N. Hence H_N<0 eventually and the formula for A_N^* follows. All other conclusions were exact finite partition or algebraic statements, so no analytic bound or support-based localization has been introduced.

glossary.E0_N: the signed sum over the nine forward, reverse, and old-U-gap refinements of Z_end
glossary.U_{T,N}: the signed sum over Z_low, Z_diag, and Z_mid
glossary.Z_diag: the outside-controlled original labelled incidences with r=k
glossary.Z_end: the outside-controlled original labelled incidences with k^2<=r<k^3
glossary.Z_low: the outside-controlled original labelled incidences with r<k
glossary.Z_mid: the outside-controlled original labelled incidences with k<r<k^2
glossary.Z_sup: the outside-controlled original labelled incidences with r>=k^3
glossary.beta_q(z): the actual sibling exponent 2 log r/log(r k)
glossary.q_sib(z): the sibling product r k attached to the labelled incidence z
glossary.rho_N: the error in the exact capture-deficit equivalence

aa5909e2714da395.title: LABELWISE-SHORT COMMON-CELL SOURCE GROUPING AND DECODER-COPY EXTENSION
aa5909e2714da395.author: slava chan
aa5909e2714da395.statement:
LABELWISE-SHORT COMMON-CELL SOURCE GROUPING AND DECODER-COPY EXTENSION.

Fix the literal normalized nonzero-Poisson setup and coefficients of fact d8ba46800ba433c2. Fix H>=2. Let mathcal L be any finite or countable zero-one restriction to C2 labels
z=(g,a,v,p,q,h),    b_z=vpq,    G_z=pq,    L_z=N/g,
where p<q are distinct primes in [H^2,2H^2), b_z is squarefree, gcd(a,b_z)=1, h is nonzero, and
|h|<min(p,q).                                                  (1)
Let m_z be any representative of the unique residue class
a m_z congruent to L_z modulo b_z,
and impose the full-rough-conductor condition
gcd(m_zh,G_z)=1.                                               (2)
Retain every original coefficient, phase, and inherited source mask. Define the complete phased atom
c_z=mu(ga)mu(gb_z)b_z^(-1)Fhat_{g,a,b_z}(h/b_z)
     e_{b_z}(L_zh a^(-1)).                                    (3)
For every active semiprime G put
gamma_G=sum_{z in mathcal L:G_z=G}c_z,    kappa_G=phi(G)/G.    (4)
All sums in (4) converge absolutely, and
sum_Gsum_{z:G_z=G}|c_z|<<DR(log x)^2.                          (5)

(A) For every ordered pair of coprime active semiprimes G,G', assume the retained pair selector is the Cartesian product of the two one-sided restrictions, as in the support-disjoint full face of fact 707345f56faff29e. Then its exact full-face scalar is
F_src(G,G')=kappa_Gkappa_G'gamma_Ggamma_G'.                   (6)
Thus the global cutoff hypothesis Z<=H^2 in fact 0abb9119d9247de6 may be replaced, for the exact grouping and scalar identity (6), by the actual labelwise condition (1). No energy estimate is asserted by this replacement.

(B) Assume H is sufficiently large for fact dcabcf2f566b5721. For each ordered coprime pair (G,G'), orient its four primes as in that fact, and let mathcal E_{G,G'} and N_E(G,G') be its eligible common-cell decoder samples. Put
alpha_{G,G'}=kappa_Gkappa_G'
and, for bold c in mathcal E_{G,G'}, define
d_{G,G',bold c}
 =alpha_{G,G'}gamma_Ggamma_G'/N_E(G,G').                     (7)
Then
sum_{bold c in mathcal E_{G,G'}}d_{G,G',bold c}
 =alpha_{G,G'}gamma_Ggamma_G',                               (8)
sum_{bold c in mathcal E_{G,G'}}|d_{G,G',bold c}|
 =alpha_{G,G'}|gamma_Ggamma_G'|,                              (9)
sum_{bold c in mathcal E_{G,G'}}|d_{G,G',bold c}|^2
 =alpha_{G,G'}^2|gamma_Ggamma_G'|^2/N_E(G,G').               (10)
Moreover
N_E(G,G')>>H^4/(log(2H))^2.                                  (11)

For each fixed ordered support pair, the map from bold c to its decoder coordinates (m,C_dec,K_dec) is injective, already after retaining only (m,C_dec). Therefore the scalar in (8) is split among N_E(G,G') distinct fixed-support decoder fibres. Equations (7)-(11) are exactly the labelled decoder-copy identities of fact d016de3f6c03e65c under the labelwise-short extension (1).

This theorem changes only the short-frequency interface for the exact source grouping and decoder reopening. It gives no estimate for the source energy, no fixed-fibre capture, no cancellation after different support pairs are aggregated at equal decoder coordinates, no varying-fibre analytic bound, no rectangular or cross-cell result, and no Goldbach implication.
aa5909e2714da395.proof:
The modulus b_z is squarefree and equals v_zG_z. The congruence defining m_z gives
e_{b_z}(L_zh a^(-1))=e_{b_z}(m_zh).
Chinese remainder factorization gives
e_{b_z}(m_zh)
 =e_{v_z}(m_zhG_z^(-1))e_{G_z}(m_zhv_z^(-1)).                (12)
Choose any residue B_z modulo G_z congruent to m_zhv_z^(-1). Then the rough factor in (12) is e_{G_z}(B_z), and
gcd(B_z,G_z)=gcd(m_zh,G_z).
Thus (2) is exactly the full primitive rough-conductor condition. The labelwise inequality (1) also shows, prime by prime, that a rough prime divides m_zh exactly when it divides m_z; reducing a m_z congruent to L_z modulo that prime gives the usual equivalence with divisibility of L_z. No comparison between a global cutoff and H^2 is needed.

The absolute value of c_z is the absolute value of the literal coefficient lambda_z from fact d8ba46800ba433c2, because its phase has modulus one. That fact proves the complete l1 estimate over every C2 restriction, and further deletion only decreases it. This proves (5), absolute convergence of (4), and legitimacy of every rearrangement below.

For a coprime pair G,G', define the actual source carrier
C_src(z,z')=B_zG'+GB_{z'}.
Then
e_{GG'}(C_src(z,z'))=e_G(B_z)e_{G'}(B_{z'}).                 (13)
