The product of (13), the two small-v factors in (12), and the two literal coefficients is c_zc_{z'}. On the four-distinct-prime full face, the Ramanujan coefficient is constant on the fixed support pair and equals
product_{r|GG'}(1-1/r)
 =kappa_Gkappa_G'.
The pair selector is Cartesian, so absolute convergence and distributivity give
F_src(G,G')
 =kappa_Gkappa_G'
  (sum_{z:G_z=G}c_z)(sum_{z':G_z'=G'}c_z')
 =kappa_Gkappa_G'gamma_Ggamma_G'.
This proves (6).

Fix an ordered coprime pair. Fact dcabcf2f566b5721 supplies the eligible set, the lower bound (11), and the exact importance-sampled reopening of a residue-independent full-face provenance coefficient. Here that coefficient is gamma_Ggamma_G', which is independent of the auxiliary primitive residue. Its full-face fraction is alpha_{G,G'}. The coefficient of each of the N_E(G,G') samples is therefore alpha_{G,G'}gamma_Ggamma_G'/N_E(G,G'), exactly (7). Summing, summing absolute values, and summing squared absolute values prove (8)-(10). This is the proof of the corresponding identities in fact d016de3f6c03e65c, and it uses (6) rather than the stronger cutoff packaging of fact 0abb9119d9247de6.

For completeness, injectivity uses only the sample boxes in fact dcabcf2f566b5721. Let bold c,bold c' have equal m and C_dec, and write delta_i=c_i-c_i'. Equality of
m=c_2r_3-c_3r_2
gives
delta_2r_3=delta_3r_2.
The primes r_2,r_3 are distinct, while the sample intervals have length less than either prime, so delta_2=delta_3=0. Equality of the carriers then reduces to
delta_1r_4+delta_4r_1=0.
The distinct primes r_1,r_4 and their longer-than-sample size similarly force delta_1=delta_4=0. Hence bold c=bold c'. Adding K_dec cannot destroy injectivity. This is exactly the algebraic argument of fact b583f09dabee72b5 and proves the final assertion.

All remaining claims are scope statements.

glossary.K_dec: The decoder determinant parameter in the fixed-support importance-sampled coordinates.
glossary.labelwise-short: The condition |h|<min(p,q) imposed on each literal C2 source label.

aaf7242ef22ecd10.title: SHARP-PERRON LEGALIZATION OF THE FINITE HB ROUTING AND A DETERMINISTIC GREEDY CARRIER. Let \(Q\ge2\), let
aaf7242ef22ecd10.author: slava chan
aaf7242ef22ecd10.statement:
SHARP-PERRON LEGALIZATION OF THE FINITE HB ROUTING AND A DETERMINISTIC GREEDY CARRIER. Let \(Q\ge2\), let
\[
 0<a<b<\beta,\qquad c_0=\min\{a/2,(b-a)/2\},\qquad z=Q^{c_0}/16,
\]
and let \(K\) be a fixed positive integer with \(Kc_0>\beta\). Let \(m,t,n\) be positive integers satisfying
\[
 n=mt,\qquad m>Q^b,\qquad 1<t<Q^a,\qquad n\le2Q^\beta.
\]
Let \(2\le j\le K\) and fix an ordered factorization
\[
 m=d_1\cdots d_j u_1\cdots u_{j-1},\qquad 1\le d_i\le z.
\]
Put
\[
 \mathcal V=\{d_1,\ldots,d_j,u_1,\ldots,u_{j-1},t\},
\]
as a multiset. Fix an order of all submultisets of \(\mathcal V\) and an order of \(u_1,\ldots,u_{j-1}\). Route the representation first to the earliest submultiset whose product lies in \([Q^a,Q^b]\), if one exists; if none exists, route it to the earliest \(u_r\) for which \(n/u_r<Q^a\), if one exists. The exact residual consists of the representations satisfying
\[
 \text{no submultiset product of \(\mathcal V\) lies in \([Q^a,Q^b]\),} \tag{HB1}
\]
and
\[
 n/u_r\ge Q^a\qquad(1\le r\le j-1). \tag{HB2}
\]

Assume (HB1)--(HB2). Put
\[
 D=\prod_{i=1}^j d_i.
\]
Choose any fixed order \(y_1,\ldots,y_j\) of the unweighted multiset
\[
 \{u_1,\ldots,u_{j-1},t\}.
\]
Define recursively
\[
 P_0=D,\qquad
 \varepsilon_r={\bf1}_{P_{r-1}y_r\le Q^b},\qquad
 P_r=P_{r-1}y_r^{\varepsilon_r}\quad(1\le r\le j).
\]
Then, for all sufficiently large \(Q\),
\[
 P_r<Q^a\quad(0\le r\le j).
\]
Every \(d_i\) belongs to the final carrier \(P_j\). At least two factors \(y_r\) with \(\varepsilon_r=0\) are nonunits, and every such omitted factor satisfies
\[
 y_r>Q^{b-a}\ge Q^{c_0}.
\]

All the routing and greedy-cell selectors above have a separated realization with polylogarithmic projective mass. Let \(\mathscr R\) be the finite list of integer product-threshold tests used by the fixed precedence rule and one fixed binary greedy cell. For every fixed \(A_1>0\), each test and its complement has, uniformly on the displayed support, a separated truncated-Perron expansion plus a pointwise remainder \(O_{A_1,K}(Q^{-A_1})\). After multiplication and expansion, every route and greedy cell is a projective superposition of products of one-coordinate arrays, each bounded after normalization, with total coefficient mass
\[
 (\log Q)^{O_K(1)},
\]
plus a pointwise remainder
\[
 O_{A_1,K}(Q^{-A_1})(\log Q)^{O_K(1)}.
\]
Against a finite source family of total absolute coefficient mass at most \(Q^{C_{\rm src}}\), where \(C_{\rm src}\) is fixed, the aggregate remainder is smaller than any prescribed power of \(Q\) after \(A_1\) is chosen sufficiently large in terms of \(C_{\rm src}\).

More explicitly, suppose a source atom is a product of one-coordinate arrays in
\[
 q,h,t,d_1,\ldots,d_j,u_1,\ldots,u_{j-1},
\]
and contains the outer factor \(\mu(q)\). Multiplication by any main Perron atom above changes only the arrays in \(t,d_i,u_r\); it leaves the \(q\)-array and the \(h\)-array unchanged. In particular \(\mu(q)\) remains inside the cross-\(q\) sum, and a threshold involving \(t\) merely multiplies its one-variable array, preserving the joint \((h,t)\) coordinate. This theorem legalizes the finite routing and carrier choice only. It gives no estimate for the multilinear residual, ULTRA-MU-VECTOR, ENDPOINT-DIAGONAL-\(N\), the post-\(A\) tail, or Goldbach.
aaf7242ef22ecd10.proof:
Fact 512b50816bb8e5ef proves, under exactly the displayed size and residual conditions, that every \(d_i\) belongs to an inclusion-maximal subset product smaller than \(Q^a\). Their product \(D\) is therefore at most that subset product, so \(P_0=D<Q^a\).

Assume \(P_{r-1}<Q^a\). The number \(P_{r-1}y_r\) is a submultiset product of \(\mathcal V\). If \(\varepsilon_r=1\), it is at most \(Q^b\); condition (HB1) then forces \(P_r=P_{r-1}y_r<Q^a\). If \(\varepsilon_r=0\), then \(P_r=P_{r-1}<Q^a\). Induction proves the carrier bound. All \(d_i\) occur in \(P_0\).

If \(y_r\) is omitted, then \(P_{r-1}y_r>Q^b\), and \(P_{r-1}<Q^a\) gives
\[
 y_r>Q^b/P_{r-1}>Q^{b-a}.
\]
Thus an omitted factor is a nonunit. If none were omitted, \(P_j=n>Q^b\), a contradiction. If exactly one were omitted and it were \(t\), then \(P_j=m>Q^b\), a contradiction. If exactly one were omitted and it were \(u_r\), then \(P_j=n/u_r\ge Q^a\) by (HB2), again a contradiction. Hence at least two are omitted. The inequality \(b-a\ge c_0\) is immediate from the definition of \(c_0\).

We use Gorodetsky, arXiv:2111.12662, Lemma 3.1. It states that if
\[
 F(s)=\sum_{v\ge1}a_vv^{-s}
\]
has finite abscissa of absolute convergence \(\sigma_a\), \(\kappa>\max\{0,\sigma_a\}\), \(T\ge1\), and \(x\ge1\), then
\[
 \sum_{v\le x}a_v
 ={1\over2\pi i}\int_{\kappa-iT}^{\kappa+iT}F(s)x^s{ds\over s}
 +O\left(x^\kappa\sum_{v\ge1}
 { |a_v|\over v^\kappa(1+T|\log(x/v)|)}\right),
\]
with an absolute implied constant.

Every Boolean test in the routing is a finite combination of inequalities
\[
 v_S\le X,\qquad v_S=\prod_{\xi\in S}\xi,
\]
where \(S\) is a coordinate submultiset and \(X\) comes from \(Q^a\) or \(Q^b\). Replace \(X\) by the equivalent positive half-integral threshold \(X^\sharp\). For example, \(v_S\le Q^b\) is equivalent to \(v_S\le\lfloor Q^b\rfloor+1/2\). Hence \(|v_S-X^\sharp|\ge1/2\), while \(v_S\le n\le2Q^\beta\).

Apply the quoted lemma to the one-term Dirichlet polynomial \(F(s)=v_S^{-s}\), whose abscissa is \(-\infty\), with
\[
 x=X^\sharp,\qquad \kappa=1/\log Q,\qquad
 T=Q^{A_1+\beta+3}.
\]
It gives
\[
 {\bf1}_{v_S\le X}
 =
 {1\over2\pi i}\int_{\kappa-iT}^{\kappa+iT}
 { (X^\sharp)^s\over s}\,v_S^{-s}\,ds
 +O\left({(X^\sharp/v_S)^\kappa
 \over1+T|\log(X^\sharp/v_S)|}\right).
\]
The half-integral gap and the polynomial bounds imply
\[
 |\log(X^\sharp/v_S)|\gg Q^{-\beta-2},
\]
so the error is \(O_{A_1}(Q^{-A_1})\). Furthermore
\[
 v_S^{-s}=\prod_{\xi\in S}\xi^{-s},
\]
which is separated. On \(\operatorname{Re}(s)=\kappa\), the coordinate factors have modulus at most one, \((X^\sharp)^\kappa=O_\beta(1)\), and
\[
 \int_{-T}^T{d\tau\over|\kappa+i\tau|}=O(\log Q).
\]
Thus one test has projective mass \(O(\log Q)\); its complement is one constant atom minus this expansion and has the same bound.

The number of tests, precedence factors, and binary cells depends only on \(K\). Multiplication therefore gives mass \((\log Q)^{O_K(1)}\). A finite telescoping-product estimate gives the asserted pointwise error after enlarging \(A_1\) by an amount depending only on \(K\). Multiplication by a source family of absolute mass \(Q^{C_{\rm src}}\) pays the error when \(A_1\) is chosen sufficiently large.

Finally, every Perron atom contains only the factor-coordinate powers \(\xi^{-s}\). It introduces no \(q\)- or \(h\)-dependence. Therefore it leaves the \(q\)- and \(h\)-arrays of a separated source atom unchanged; if \(\xi=t\), it only twists the existing \(t\)-array. The assertions about \(\mu(q)\) and the joint \((h,t)\) coordinate follow.

glossary.A_1: An arbitrarily large accuracy exponent in effective Perron separation.
glossary.C_src: A fixed exponent bounding the total absolute mass of a finite source family.
glossary.D: The product of all short Möbius-bearing factors d_i in one truncated-inverse term.
glossary.P_r: The running greedy carrier after the first r unweighted factors have been tested.
glossary.X^sharp: A positive half-integral threshold representing an exact integer inequality.
glossary.epsilon_r: The zero-one decision to admit y_r to the greedy carrier.
glossary.mathscr R: The fixed finite list of product-threshold tests in the routing and one greedy cell.
glossary.v_S: The product of the coordinates in the submultiset S.
glossary.y_r: The r-th unweighted factor in the fixed greedy order.

ab9163da69da1ad4.title: Let K,w be integers and X>=1. The number of quadruples (a,b,c,d) of nonzero integers with |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|<=X and
ab9163da69da1ad4.author: slava chan
ab9163da69da1ad4.statement:
Let K,w be integers and X>=1. The number of quadruples (a,b,c,d) of nonzero integers with |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|<=X and
ab+cd=2K,  ab-cd=4w
is zero if K^2=4w^2, and otherwise is at most
4 tau(|K+2w|) tau(|K-2w|).
The same bound holds after requiring a,b,c,d to be even.

In particular, in every normalized unit state of fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb one has the uniquely determined nonzero slice parameter
w=uv=J/4,
with
ab=K+2w, cd=K-2w, K^2 not equal to 4w^2,
and the coefficient matrix Q lies in a divisor-sized fixed-w slice. If |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|<=L H^3, then |w|<=L^2H^6/2, each fixed-w slice has H^{o(1)} matrices uniformly for polynomially bounded K,w, and summing the slices separately over w again incurs the full H^{6+o(1)} outer tax.
ab9163da69da1ad4.proof:
Adding and subtracting the two displayed equations gives
2ab=2K+4w and 2cd=2K-4w,
hence
ab=K+2w, cd=K-2w.                                                     (1)
Conversely, (1) implies the original two equations, so this is an exact equivalence.

For a nonzero integer n, every ordered nonzero integer factorization xy=n is obtained by choosing a signed divisor x of n and putting y=n/x. Thus there are at most 2tau(|n|) such ordered factorizations, and imposing |x|,|y|<=X can only reduce their number. If K+2w and K-2w are both nonzero, the choices of (a,b) and (c,d) in (1) are independent, giving at most
(2tau(|K+2w|))(2tau(|K-2w|))
quadruples. If K^2=4w^2, one of K+2w and K-2w is zero, so (1) would make ab=0 or cd=0, impossible because all four coefficients are required nonzero. Requiring even coefficients only removes factorizations.

For a normalized unit state, fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb gives J=4uv and also gives (1) with w=uv; it proves uv nonzero and K^2-4u^2v^2 nonzero. Therefore w=J/4 is an integer, is nonzero, and labels a nondegenerate divisor-sized coefficient slice uniquely.

Finally, from J=ab-cd and the coefficient bounds,
4|w|=|J|<=|ab|+|cd|<=2L^2H^6,
so |w|<=L^2H^6/2. For polynomially bounded K,w, the elementary divisor bound tau(n)<<_epsilon |n|^epsilon makes the fixed-w multiplicity H^{o(1)}. There are O_L(H^6) possible integer w in the displayed range, so summing those pointwise divisor bounds separately costs H^{6+o(1)}. This last summation is a tax ledger, not a cancellation theorem.

glossary.w: the product uv, equivalently J/4, indexing a signed-determinant coefficient slice

ac65d113d1ffe8cd.title: Let m>1 be odd, let s belong to {1,-1}, let K be an integer with gcd(K,m)=1, and let W be a nonzero complex-valued function modulo m. Let G be the unit group modulo m^2, put W_hat(ell)=sum_{u modulo m}W(u)e_m(-ell u), and let T_W be the shared normal-digit tensor
ac65d113d1ffe8cd.author: slava chan
ac65d113d1ffe8cd.statement:
Let m>1 be odd, let s belong to {1,-1}, let K be an integer with gcd(K,m)=1, and let W be a nonzero complex-valued function modulo m. Let G be the unit group modulo m^2, put W_hat(ell)=sum_{u modulo m}W(u)e_m(-ell u), and let T_W be the shared normal-digit tensor
T_W(a,b,c,d)=sum_{u modulo m}W(u) Delta_{m^2}(ab-K-2smu) Delta_{m^2}(cd-K+2smu)                (1)
on G^4. Let r_W be the number of residues ell modulo m for which W_hat(ell) is nonzero. Then the matrix obtained from T_W by grouping (a,c) as its row index and (b,d) as its column index has rank
rank(T_W)=[phi(m^2)^2/m] r_W >=phi(m^2)^2/m>1.                         (2)

Now let f and g be arbitrary complex-valued functions on G, let I be a finite set, and for every j in I let alpha_j and beta_j be arbitrary complex-valued functions on G. Define
R_common(a,b,c,d)=f(a)g(c)sum_{j in I}beta_j(b)alpha_j(d).              (3)
The (a,c) versus (b,d) matrix rank of R_common is at most one. Consequently T_W cannot equal R_common for any choices in (3).

On the determinant sign sector and variable placement of fact b1398db2962d7491, summing arbitrarily many Bettin--Chandee atoms while retaining one common pair of row profiles f(m_1),g(m_2) has exactly the form (3). Hence a nonzero dense modular shared-digit tensor cannot be inserted into that single-common-profile template. This is a scoped slot obstruction only. It does not exclude a decomposition using many different smooth row-profile pairs followed by separate Bettin--Chandee applications, and it makes no assertion about the rank after restricting to literal coefficient boxes, the exact determinant shell, prime quotients, gcd conditions, the C-coupling, masks, or source weights.
ac65d113d1ffe8cd.proof:
Fact be21aada9cf60ec5 computes every singular value of the (a,c) versus (b,d) flattening of T_W. For each residue ell modulo m, |W_hat(ell)| occurs with multiplicity phi(m^2)^2/m. The rank of a finite matrix is the number of its nonzero singular values counted with multiplicity. Therefore
rank(T_W)=[phi(m^2)^2/m] r_W.                                         (4)
Since W is nonzero, additive Fourier inversion modulo m implies that at least one W_hat(ell) is nonzero, so r_W>=1. Also m is odd and greater than one, hence m>=3 and phi(m)>=2. Since phi(m^2)=m phi(m),
phi(m^2)^2/m=m phi(m)^2>=12>1.                                       (5)
This proves (2).

Put
C(b,d)=sum_{j in I}beta_j(b)alpha_j(d).                               (6)
After grouping the variables, equation (3) becomes
R_common((a,c),(b,d))=[f(a)g(c)] C(b,d).                              (7)
Thus R_common is the outer product of the row-indexed vector (a,c) -> f(a)g(c) and the column-indexed vector (b,d) -> C(b,d). Every outer-product matrix has rank at most one, including rank zero if either vector vanishes. Equations (2) and (7) therefore make T_W=R_common impossible.

In fact b1398db2962d7491, the row profiles f and g are common to every atom indexed by j, while only alpha_j and beta_j vary. Under its displayed sign-sector substitution, the assembled four-variable coefficient is exactly of the algebraic form (3), up to the stated relabeling and sign of a column variable. Relabeling indices does not change matrix rank. This proves the scoped template incompatibility. The final limitations are explicit because allowing f and g to vary with j produces a sum of several row outer products, and restricting a matrix to literal subsets or multiplying it by additional joint selectors can change its rank.

glossary.R_common: a four-variable tensor with one common pair of row profiles and an arbitrary finite separated column expansion
glossary.r_W: the number of nonzero additive Fourier coefficients of W modulo m

ace362082848a702.title: NONZERO-POISSON SOURCE--DENSITY REASSEMBLY AND ITS QUARTIC INTERFACE
ace362082848a702.author: slava chan
ace362082848a702.statement:
NONZERO-POISSON SOURCE--DENSITY REASSEMBLY AND ITS QUARTIC INTERFACE.

Let n,q be positive integers with gcd(q,n)=1, let A be an integer, and write e_n(t)=exp(2 pi i t/n). For every smooth compactly supported complex function F_q on R define
  Fhat_q(xi)=integral_R F_q(t)exp(-2 pi i xi t)dt
and
  a_q=n^(-1)sum_{h in Z; h nonzero}
       Fhat_q(h/n)e_n(hA q^(-1)),                            (1)
where q^(-1) denotes the inverse of q modulo n. Put
  u_q=sum_{m in Z; qm congruent A modulo n}F_q(m),
  z_q=n^(-1)Fhat_q(0).                                      (2)
Then exactly
  a_q=u_q-z_q.                                              (3)
Equivalently, each summand in u_q is supported on an actual source triple
  (q,m,k),  qm+nk=A,  k in Z.                               (4)
If the support of F_q is contained in an interval of length strictly less than n, then u_q contains at most one summand.

Now let p be a prime dividing n, let cal Q be a finite set of positive integers coprime to n, and let W be a complex function on Z/pZ. For q_i in cal Q define
  Delta=(q_2-q_1)q_3q_4-(q_4-q_3)q_1q_2,
  rho_12=A(q_2-q_1)(q_1q_2)^(-1) modulo p,
  rho_34=A(q_4-q_3)(q_3q_4)^(-1) modulo p,
and
  Gamma_W(x,y)=sum_{r modulo p}W(r)
       [1_{r=x}-1/p][1_{r=y}-1/p].                          (5)
For four coefficient rows c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4 on cal Q put
  M_W(c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4)
   =sum_{q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4 in cal Q; Delta nonzero}
      c_1(q_1)conjugate(c_2(q_2))
      conjugate(c_3(q_3))c_4(q_4)
      Gamma_W(rho_12,rho_34).                               (6)
The D=0-subtracted fourth energy of the nonzero-Poisson row a is exactly
  M_W(a,a,a,a)
   =sum_{(c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4) in {u,z}^4}
      (-1)^{#{j:c_j=z}}M_W(c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4).                (7)
Thus the actual-source term M_W(u,u,u,u) is one of sixteen exact terms. Reassembling the full Fourier family does not identify the whole nonzero-Poisson fourth energy with the actual-source energy: fifteen pure-density or mixed source--density terms remain. No estimate for those fifteen terms is asserted.
ace362082848a702.proof:
Write c for the residue A q^(-1) modulo n. Poisson summation on the progression m congruent c modulo n, with the Fourier convention in the statement, gives
  sum_{m congruent c modulo n}F_q(m)
   =n^(-1)sum_{h in Z}Fhat_q(h/n)e_n(hc).                   (8)
The left side is u_q because qm congruent A modulo n is equivalent to m congruent c modulo n. The h=0 term on the right is z_q. Removing it proves (3).

The congruence qm congruent A modulo n is equivalent to n dividing A-qm. Hence k=(A-qm)/n is an integer and qm+nk=A, proving (4). If two integers m_1,m_2 in an interval of length less than n lie in the same residue class modulo n, then n divides m_1-m_2 while |m_1-m_2|<n, so m_1=m_2. This proves the uniqueness assertion.

For the quartic identity, equation (3) gives a=u-z and conjugate(a)=conjugate(u)-conjugate(z). Substitute these four binomials into definition (6). Distributivity produces one term for every ordered choice (c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4) in {u,z}^4. Every occurrence of z contributes one minus sign, including in the conjugated slots because conjugate(u-z)=conjugate(u)-conjugate(z). This is exactly (7).

Definition (6) is the nonzero-integer-determinant physical energy of facts 27540b4094f677f4 and 3704d40c75e8269c, with four possibly different coefficient rows. Therefore its all-u term is precisely the actual-source sector to which a source-graph estimate such as fact 914048233fada05f may apply when that fact's interval, injectivity, coefficient-size, and source-mask hypotheses hold. But the remaining fifteen choices contain at least one z row. Equations (2) and (8) show that z is the removed zero Fourier coefficient, not a source indicator. Hence no one of those terms is included in the all-u term merely by Fourier reassembly. This proves the asserted interface and its scope.

glossary.M_W: The four-row nonzero-determinant centered reciprocal-slope form.
glossary.source--density reassembly: The exact identity a_q=u_q-z_q for the nonzero-Poisson coefficient.
glossary.u_q: The actual-source coefficient obtained by summing F_q over the progression qm congruent A modulo n.

ad3e98d3e74ae7a5.title: PRIME FULL-RAY OPERATOR IS EXACTLY THE FOURIER IMAGE OF DILATOR RESIDUE DISCREPANCY. Adopt an odd prime p>=5, an integer T with gcd(T,p)=1, and the primitive rays R_s=(+1,p,p+s), 1<=s<=p-1, from fact d67c1ddb0bdcd135. Let D_set be any finite multiset of positive integers coprime to p. For every unit residue r modulo p put
ad3e98d3e74ae7a5.author: slava chan
ad3e98d3e74ae7a5.statement:
PRIME FULL-RAY OPERATOR IS EXACTLY THE FOURIER IMAGE OF DILATOR RESIDUE DISCREPANCY. Adopt an odd prime p>=5, an integer T with gcd(T,p)=1, and the primitive rays R_s=(+1,p,p+s), 1<=s<=p-1, from fact d67c1ddb0bdcd135. Let D_set be any finite multiset of positive integers coprime to p. For every unit residue r modulo p put
N_r=#{d in D_set:d congruent r (mod p)},                         (1)
H=sum_{r (mod p)}^*N_r,                                         (2)
delta_r=N_r-H/(p-1).                                            (3)
For each d in D_set let K_d be the zero-diagonal centered ray matrix
(K_d)_{R_t,R_s}
 =e_p(-T(s-t)d^{-1})+1/(p-1) for s!=t.                         (4)
For each unit r define u_r in C^{p-1} by
u_r(s)=e_p(Ts r^{-1}), 1<=s<=p-1.                               (5)
Then
sum_{d in D_set}K_d
 =sum_{r (mod p)}^*delta_r u_r tensor u_r^*.                    (6)

Let U be the square matrix with rows indexed by unit residues r and columns indexed by 1<=s<=p-1,
U_{r,s}=conjugate(u_r(s)).                                      (7)
Let I_{p-1} be the (p-1)-by-(p-1) identity matrix and let J_{p-1} be the (p-1)-by-(p-1) all-ones matrix. Then
UU^*=pI_{p-1}-J_{p-1},                                         (8)
so the singular values of U are sqrt(p), with multiplicity p-2, and 1, with multiplicity one. Consequently
||sum_{d in D_set}K_d||_{op}
 <=p max_{r (mod p)}^*|delta_r|.                                (9)
In particular exact equidistribution N_r=H/(p-1) makes the centered ray operator vanish, while
max_r^*|N_r-H/(p-1)|<=p                                        (10)
is sufficient for an operator bound at scale p^2.

This theorem is an exact finite-dimensional reduction. It does not assert (10) for the literal Good-W C support, does not include moving source weights or pair-dependent deletions, does not prove C-HILBERT-OP-SUP, and proves no centered-source, tail, or Goldbach estimate.
ad3e98d3e74ae7a5.proof:
For d congruent to r modulo p, equation (7) in the proof of fact d67c1ddb0bdcd135 gives
K_d=u_r tensor u_r^* +(1/(p-1))J_{p-1}-(p/(p-1))I_{p-1}.        (11)
Sum (11) over D_set and group by r:
sum_d K_d
 =sum_r N_r u_r tensor u_r^*
  +(H/(p-1))J_{p-1}-(Hp/(p-1))I_{p-1}.                         (12)

We compute the uniform sum. Its (t,s) entry is
sum_{r (mod p)}^* e_p(T(t-s)r^{-1}).
Inversion permutes the unit residues. If s=t this is p-1. If s!=t, then T(t-s) is nonzero modulo p and the sum over all nonzero residues of the corresponding additive character is -1. Hence
sum_r u_r tensor u_r^*=pI_{p-1}-J_{p-1}.                        (13)
Multiply (13) by H/(p-1) and subtract it from the first term in (12). The remaining constant matrices cancel:
(H/(p-1))(pI_{p-1}-J_{p-1})
 +(H/(p-1))J_{p-1}-(Hp/(p-1))I_{p-1}=0.
Using (3) proves (6).

By definition, U has row conjugate(u_r). Therefore
U^* diag(delta_r) U=sum_r delta_r u_r tensor u_r^*,
which is (6). The (r,r') entry of UU^* is
sum_{s=1}^{p-1}conjugate(u_r(s))u_{r'}(s)
 =sum_{s=1}^{p-1}e_p(Ts(r'^{-1}-r^{-1})).
It equals p-1 when r=r' and -1 otherwise. This is (8). The matrix J_{p-1} has eigenvalue p-1 on the constant vector and zero on its orthogonal complement. Hence pI_{p-1}-J_{p-1} has eigenvalue 1 on the constant vector and p on its orthogonal complement, proving the singular-value statement.

Finally,
||U^*diag(delta_r)U||_{op}
 <=||U||_{op}^2||diag(delta_r)||_{op}
 =p max_r|delta_r|,
which proves (9). Equations (6) and (9) give the final consequences and all scope limitations.

glossary.D_set: A finite multiset of dilators coprime to the prime conductor p.
glossary.N_r: The multiplicity of dilators in D_set occupying the unit residue r modulo p.
glossary.U: The restricted additive Fourier matrix whose r-th row is the conjugate of u_r.
glossary.delta_r: The discrepancy N_r-H/(p-1) from uniform unit-residue occupancy.

ad79e2b004abf5ec.title: EXACT HARD-SOURCE p-CROSS GRAM FOR OSC AND THE FIRST DIVISOR-SELECTED JOINT SUPPLIER
ad79e2b004abf5ec.author: slava chan
ad79e2b004abf5ec.statement:
EXACT HARD-SOURCE p-CROSS GRAM FOR OSC AND THE FIRST DIVISOR-SELECTED JOINT SUPPLIER.

Adopt the scale, label, hard-source graph, height intervals, and notation of fact 95058e339b3441a3. Thus
  2<=H<=Q^(1/3),  2<=V<H,  P=QH/V,                        (1)
and every source atom x=(q,m,k) in cal X_{ell,v,p} satisfies
  Q<=q,m<2Q,  qm+vpk=A,  gcd(qm,vp)=1.                     (2)
For h in I_ell let s=-h pbar modulo v. By reciprocity, CRT, and (2),
  e_q(Ah(vp)bar)
  =e(Ah/(qvp)) e_v(A s qbar) e_p(-h vbar m),               (3)
where every inverse is taken in the displayed modulus.

Let b_{ell,v,p,h}(x) be the complete literal coefficient after absorbing the first two factors on the right of (3), every projective/scaled-smooth factor, and every source mask, but not the last p-character. Assume |b_{ell,v,p,h}(x)|<=B. The dependence on p is retained: in particular, with
  D_{v,q,m}=(A-qm)/v,                                      (4)
the support of b contains the exact shifted-divisor selector
  D_{v,q,m}=pk.                                             (5)

For S in Z and r modulo p define the exact pair-output row
  B_{ell,v,p}(S,r)
  =sum_{h_1,h_2 in I_ell, h_1+h_2=S}
    sum_{x_1,x_2 in cal X_{ell,v,p},
         h_1m_1+h_2m_2 congruent r modulo p}
      b_{ell,v,p,h_1}(x_1)b_{ell,v,p,h_2}(x_2).             (6)
Then the complete hard-source quartic at fixed ell,v,p is exactly
  M_all(ell,v,p)
  =sum_S |sum_{r modulo p}
             B_{ell,v,p}(S,r)e_p(-vbar r)|^2.              (7)
Its p-modular diagonal and off-diagonal are
  M_diag(ell,v,p)=sum_Ssum_r|B_{ell,v,p}(S,r)|^2,           (8)
  M_OSC(ell,v,p)
   =sum_Ssum_{r_1 not congruent r_2 modulo p}
      B_{ell,v,p}(S,r_1)conjugate(B_{ell,v,p}(S,r_2))
      e_p(-vbar(r_1-r_2)),                                  (9)
and exactly
  M_all=M_diag+M_OSC.                                       (10)
The diagonal (8) is the union of the exact weighted-slope sector Delta_h=0 and the hard-source MOD sector Delta_h nonzero, p|A Delta_h. The off-diagonal (9) is exactly OSC: Delta_h is nonzero and p does not divide A Delta_h.

The source prime in every coefficient of (6) is not a free phase variable. Fixing v,q,m, equation (5) is equivalently
  p divides D_{v,q,m},  k=D_{v,q,m}/p.                      (11)
Thus (9) is a divisor-selected p-cross Gram whose row B_{ell,v,p} depends jointly on p through four source selectors, the forced residues s=-h pbar modulo v, and all literal masks.

There is an elementary absolute ledger. For every epsilon>0,
  |sum_{ell,v,p}M_OSC(ell,v,p)|
  <<_{C,epsilon}B^4 #cal L Q^(5+epsilon).                  (12)
Relative to B^4 #cal L times the required vector scale, its excess factor is
  G_OSC
  =Q^5/[P^2Q^(7/3)]
  =Q^(2/3)V^2/H^2.                                         (13)
Suppose, as in the literal projective assembly, that B and #cal L are subpolynomial in the explicit sense that for every delta>0,
  B^4 #cal L<<_delta Q^delta.                               (14)
Then the hard-source diagonal is fully paid by facts ddcb0baef17b6ab0 and 95058e339b3441a3 after renaming epsilon, while the first remaining joint input is
  |sum_{ell,v,p}M_OSC(ell,v,p)|
  <<Q^epsilon P^2Q^(7/3),                                  (15)
with B_{ell,v,p} exactly as in (6), before absolute values in p, v, or the cross outputs. Equivalently, (15) must save G_OSC whenever that factor is a fixed power of Q.

No standard separated large sieve follows from (6): the coefficient row itself changes with p through (4)-(5), and the small-v frequency vbar is coupled to the same p through s=-h pbar. Equations (7)-(15) are an exact interface and elementary ledger, not a proof of (15), PMD closure, or Goldbach.
ad79e2b004abf5ec.proof:
Equation (3) is the CRT form from fact ddcb0baef17b6ab0:
  e_q(Ah(vp)bar)
  =e(Ah/(qvp))e_v(A s qbar)e_p(-Ah vbar qbar).
Reducing the source equation (2) modulo p gives
  A qbar congruent m modulo p.
Substitution proves (3). Equation (5) is the rearrangement
  (A-qm)/v=pk
and is also the exact divisor-selected reindexing in fact db067f4633c13fed.

Expand the fourth power at fixed ell,v,p, retaining the additive Fourier relation
  h_1+h_2=h_3+h_4.
After (3), its p-character is
  e_p(-vbar[h_1m_1+h_2m_2-h_3m_3-h_4m_4]).
Group the left ordered atom pair by
  S=h_1+h_2,
  r_1=h_1m_1+h_2m_2 modulo p,
and the right ordered pair by the same S and its output r_2. This gives
  sum_Ssum_{r_1,r_2}
    B(S,r_1)conjugate(B(S,r_2))e_p(-vbar(r_1-r_2)),
which is both (7) and the sum of (8)-(9), proving (7)-(10).

Fact db067f4633c13fed gives
  p divides A Delta_h
if and only if
  p divides h_1m_1+h_2m_2-h_3m_3-h_4m_4.
Therefore r_1=r_2 is exactly the p-modular alias. If Delta_h=0 this is the exact weighted-slope sector; if Delta_h is nonzero it is MOD. If r_1 differs from r_2, then p does not divide A Delta_h, which also forces Delta_h nonzero; this is precisely OSC. This proves the sector identification.

For (12), fact 914048233fada05f gives
  X_{ell,v,p}<<Q^epsilon Q/H.
At fixed ell,v,p, choose h_1,h_2,h_3 and x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4 arbitrarily; h_4 is determined, and the OSC condition only deletes tuples. Thus the number of off-diagonal summands is at most
  O(H^3 X_{ell,v,p}^4)
  <<Q^epsilon Q^4/H.
Each has modulus at most B^4. Summing O(V) values of v, O(P) possible primes, and #cal L labels gives
  B^4 #cal L Q^epsilon VP Q^4/H
  =B^4 #cal L Q^(5+epsilon),
because VP=QH. This proves (12). Substitution of P=QH/V proves (13).

It remains to justify the diagonal-payoff citations with the atom indexing. Fact 914048233fada05f proves that x->q modulo p is injective on cal X_{ell,v,p}. Since q lies in an interval of cardinality Q<p, each represented q comes from exactly one source atom x(q). For fixed ell,v,p,h define the q-row
  w_{ell,v,p,h}(q)=b_{ell,v,p,h}(x(q))
on represented q and zero otherwise. The exact weighted-slope part of (8) is therefore exactly the q-indexed Delta_h=0 sector estimated in fact ddcb0baef17b6ab0. Its non-exact-slope diagonal is the atom-indexed hard-source MOD sector estimated in fact 95058e339b3441a3. Under (14), both lie within P^2Q^(7/3+epsilon) after renaming epsilon. Therefore (15) is sufficient for the remaining hard-source quartic. The coefficient dependence asserted after (15) follows directly from (4)-(6), so a theorem requiring a p-independent row cannot be inserted. No estimate beyond (12) has been claimed.

glossary.B_{ell,v,p}: The exact pair-output coefficient row indexed by additive height sum S and source output r modulo p.
glossary.G_OSC: The factor Q^(2/3)V^2/H^2 missing from the elementary OSC ledger.
glossary.M_OSC: The off-diagonal p-cross Gram, exactly the hard-source OSC sector.
glossary.M_all: The complete hard-source quartic at fixed label, v, and p.
glossary.M_diag: The p-modular diagonal of the hard-source pair-output Gram.

adb3b38d14670d3c.title: EXACT EULER RESPONSE OF A SQUAREFREE COMMON-CORE CONDUCTOR PROJECTOR. Let \(N\) be a positive integer, let \(q\ge2\) be squarefree, let \(a,t,u\) be integers with
adb3b38d14670d3c.author: slava chan
adb3b38d14670d3c.statement:
EXACT EULER RESPONSE OF A SQUAREFREE COMMON-CORE CONDUCTOR PROJECTOR. Let \(N\) be a positive integer, let \(q\ge2\) be squarefree, let \(a,t,u\) be integers with
\[
 (a,qtu)=1,\qquad (q,tu)=1,
\]
and let \(T\ge1\) be real. For a Dirichlet character \(\psi\) modulo \(q\), put
\[
 G_{N,q}(\psi)=
 \sum_{\substack{z\ ({\rm mod}\ q)\\(z,q)=1}}
 e_q(-Nz)\overline{\psi(z)},\qquad
 e_q(y)=\exp(2\pi i y/q),
\]
and let \(f_\psi={\rm cond}(\psi)\). Define the common-core threshold projector
\[
 \mathcal P_{q,a}^{>T}(t,u)=
 \frac1{\phi(q)}
 \sum_{\substack{\psi\ ({\rm mod}\ q)\\
 f_\psi>T\\(f_\psi,N)=1}}
 G_{N,q}(\psi)\psi(t)\overline{\psi(au)}. \tag{1}
\]
For a positive integer \(s\), let
\[
 c_s(N)=
 \sum_{\substack{z\ ({\rm mod}\ s)\\(z,s)=1}}e_s(Nz)
\]
be the Ramanujan sum. For every divisor \(f\mid q\), define
\[
 \mathcal K_f^{(a)}(q;t,u)=
 \prod_{p\mid f}
 \left[
  1+(p-1)
  e_p\!\left(-Nt\,[au(q/p)]^{-1}\right)
 \right], \tag{2}
\]
where each inverse in (2) is taken modulo \(p\); the empty product is one. Then
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \mathcal P_{q,a}^{>T}(t,u)=
 \frac1{\phi(q)}
 \sum_{\substack{f\mid q\\f>T\\(f,N)=1}}
 c_{q/f}(N)\,
 \mathcal K_f^{(a)}(q;t,u).
 \quad} \tag{3}
\]
Thus the character sum in (1) is exactly a divisor sum of explicit prime-local additive responses. Formula (3) is an identity only; it supplies no cancellation estimate for the divisor sum or for a product of two such projectors.
adb3b38d14670d3c.proof:
Because \(q\) is squarefree, a character \(\psi\) modulo \(q\) of primitive conductor \(f\) is uniquely induced by a primitive character \(\psi^*\) modulo \(f\), where
\[
 q=fs,\qquad (f,s)=1.
\]
For \(f>1\), the induced-conductor factorization proved in fact 9a80432a29fc15d2 gives, when \((f,N)=1\),
\[
 G_{N,q}(\psi)
 =c_s(N)\,
  \psi^*(-Ns^{-1})\,
  \tau_f(\overline{\psi^*}), \tag{4}
\]
where
\[
 \tau_f(\overline{\psi^*})
 =\sum_{\substack{v\ ({\rm mod}\ f)\\(v,f)=1}}
   e_f(v)\overline{\psi^*(v)}
\]
and the inverse in (4) is modulo \(f\). The cutoff \(T\ge1\) excludes \(f=1\), so (4) applies to every term of (1).

Since \((q,tu)=(a,q)=1\), the induced character values in (1) equal the corresponding primitive character values. Combining them with (4) gives
\[
 G_{N,q}(\psi)\psi(t)\overline{\psi(au)}
 =c_s(N)\tau_f(\overline{\psi^*})
  \psi^*\!\left(-Nt(aus)^{-1}\right). \tag{5}
\]
It remains to sum (5) over all primitive characters modulo the squarefree integer \(f\).

Put
\[
 A=-Nt(aus)^{-1}\pmod f.
\]
The set of primitive characters modulo squarefree \(f\) is the direct product, over \(p\mid f\), of the nonprincipal characters modulo \(p\). Additive CRT gives
\[
 e_f(v)=\prod_{p\mid f}
 e_p\!\left(v(f/p)^{-1}\right). \tag{6}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \sum_{\psi^*\ {\rm primitive}\ ({\rm mod}\ f)}
 \tau_f(\overline{\psi^*})\psi^*(A)
 =\prod_{p\mid f}\mathcal L_p, \tag{7}
\]
where
\[
 \mathcal L_p=
 \sum_{\substack{\xi\ ({\rm mod}\ p)\\\xi\ne\xi_0}}
 \left(
  \sum_{v=1}^{p-1}
   e_p\!\left(v(f/p)^{-1}\right)\overline{\xi(v)}
 \right)\xi(A). \tag{8}
\]

We evaluate (8) by first summing over every character modulo \(p\). Character orthogonality, or finite Fourier inversion on the unit group, gives
\[
 \sum_{\xi\ ({\rm mod}\ p)}
 \left(
  \sum_{v=1}^{p-1}
   e_p\!\left(v(f/p)^{-1}\right)\overline{\xi(v)}
 \right)\xi(A)
 =(p-1)e_p\!\left(A(f/p)^{-1}\right). \tag{9}
\]
The principal-character term omitted from (8) is
\[
 \sum_{v=1}^{p-1}e_p\!\left(v(f/p)^{-1}\right)=-1, \tag{10}
\]
because \((f/p)^{-1}\) is a unit modulo \(p\). Subtracting (10) from (9) yields
\[
 \mathcal L_p=
 1+(p-1)e_p\!\left(A(f/p)^{-1}\right). \tag{11}
\]
Since \(q=fs\), reduction modulo \(p\mid f\) gives
\[
 A(f/p)^{-1}
 \equiv -Nt[au\,s(f/p)]^{-1}
 \equiv -Nt[au(q/p)]^{-1}\pmod p. \tag{12}
\]
Equations (7), (11), and (12) show that the primitive-character sum in (5) is exactly \(\mathcal K_f^{(a)}(q;t,u)\).

Finally group (1) by \(f=f_\psi\), write \(s=q/f\), apply (5), and use the just-computed primitive-character sum. The result is (3). Every operation was a finite exact rearrangement, so no estimate is asserted.

glossary.mathcal K_f^{(a)}(q;t,u): The explicit product of prime-local additive responses for the primitive-conductor-f block.
glossary.mathcal P_{q,a}^{>T}(t,u): The common-core squarefree character projector above primitive-conductor threshold T, including the dilator twist a.

ae1623e3b77d7695.title: ARBITRARY FOUR-SIGN EXTENSION OF THE SOURCE-WEIGHTED JOINT-(h,t) FAREY ENERGY
ae1623e3b77d7695.author: slava chan
ae1623e3b77d7695.statement:
ARBITRARY FOUR-SIGN EXTENSION OF THE SOURCE-WEIGHTED JOINT-(h,t) FAREY ENERGY.

Let p be a prime. Let H,T be real numbers with
H>=1,qquad T>=1,qquad 2H<p,qquad 2T<p.                      (1)
Let w_h be nonnegative real weights on integers h, supported on
H<=h<2H, and let b_t be nonnegative real weights on integers t, supported on
T<=t<2T.
Define
W=sup_h w_h,qquad
V=W+Var_{[H,2H)}(w),qquad
B=sup_t b_t,                                                    (2)
where
Var_{[H,2H)}(w)
=sum_{H<=h<2H-1}|w_{h+1}-w_h|
is the discrete total variation, with the evident restriction to integer h in the interval. For z in F_p define
gamma(z)=sum_{h,t: h t^(-1)=z mod p}w_hb_t,                     (3)
where t^(-1) is the inverse of t modulo p. Put
e_p(u)=exp(2pi i u/p)
and
S(a)=sum_{h,t}w_hb_t e_p(aht^(-1))qquad(a in F_p).             (4)

Fix arbitrary signs
epsilon_1,epsilon_2,epsilon_3,epsilon_4 in {+1,-1}.              (5)
Let O_p(epsilon) be any source-weighted suboccupancy of
sum_{i=1}^4 epsilon_i h_i t_i^(-1)=0 mod p,                    (6)
in which each quadruple has weight at most
product_{i=1}^4 w_{h_i}b_{t_i}.
An arbitrary tuple-dependent mask between zero and one may be retained before domination.

Then
O_p(epsilon)
 <=p^(-1)sum_{a in F_p}|S(a)|^4,                               (7)
and
O_p(epsilon)
 <<(BV)^4p^(o(1))
 [(HT)^4/p+(H+T)^2{HT+(HT)^2/p}].                             (8)
The p^(o(1)) is uniform in the sign pattern and has the same interval uniformity as fact 9ea2dddfbbbd191a.

If, in addition,
H>=p^delta,qquad T>=p^delta                                  (9)
for a fixed delta>0, then for every
0<eta<min(1,4delta)
and sufficiently large p,
O_p(epsilon)
 <<_{delta,eta}(BV)^4(HT)^4p^(-eta).                            (10)
Thus the joint Farey energy has the same bound for all sixteen four-sign patterns. This theorem changes only the signs in the scalar balance. It does not supply a literal source envelope, a common-coordinate completion, a remaining-face vector contraction, or a complete top trace estimate.
ae1623e3b77d7695.proof:
Because all weights are nonnegative, it suffices to bound the full weighted occupancy of (6). Additive orthogonality gives that full occupancy as
p^(-1)sum_{a in F_p} product_{i=1}^4 S(epsilon_i a).             (11)
Expanding the product and summing a gives one exactly when the signed sum in (6) vanishes and zero otherwise.

The coefficients defining gamma are real and nonnegative. Hence
S(-a)=conjugate(S(a))
for every a. Therefore, for each sign pattern and every a,
|product_{i=1}^4S(epsilon_i a)|=|S(a)|^4.                        (12)
Taking the absolute value of (11) and using the triangle inequality proves (7). A tuple-dependent mask between zero and one only decreases the nonnegative full weighted occupancy, so the same bound holds for O_p(epsilon).

Equation (8) in the proof of fact 9ea2dddfbbbd191a identifies
p^(-1)sum_a|S(a)|^4
with the two-plus/two-minus convolution energy and proves, under the explicit hypotheses (1)-(4), from the zero mode, the one-sided Farey bound, bounded-variation partial summation, and the ratio-collision second moment that it is bounded by the right side of (8). Applying that verified estimate to (7) proves (8).

Under (9), equation (6) of fact 9ea2dddfbbbd191a proves that the same right side is at most the expression in (10) for every eta in the displayed range. This proves (10). No source-specific structure beyond the scalar nonnegative weights has been introduced, which proves the scope paragraph.

glossary.O_p(epsilon): A masked weighted occupancy of a four-term ratio balance with an arbitrary fixed sign pattern.

ae1febd328547ccc.title: Assume the hypotheses and notation of facts 91db48815d136d4c and aa34b1862b993377. Let Z_{F,11} be the forward 1x1 endpoint component: it consists of the original labelled incidences z=(D,M,R,K;d,m,r,k) with nonzero weight w(z), label outside the controlled set, k^2<=r<k^3, forward boundary-admissibility, and 1x1 tag. Let T_{F,11}=sum_{z in Z_{F,11}}w(z), which is the forward 1x1 component of fact f5b31dd3643732ac
ae1febd328547ccc.author: slava chan
ae1febd328547ccc.statement:
Assume the hypotheses and notation of facts 91db48815d136d4c and aa34b1862b993377. Let Z_{F,11} be the forward 1x1 endpoint component: it consists of the original labelled incidences z=(D,M,R,K;d,m,r,k) with nonzero weight w(z), label outside the controlled set, k^2<=r<k^3, forward boundary-admissibility, and 1x1 tag. Let T_{F,11}=sum_{z in Z_{F,11}}w(z), which is the forward 1x1 component of fact f5b31dd3643732ac.

For every z in Z_{F,11}, the canonical boundary factors y(z) and t(z) of fact 91db48815d136d4c are distinct primes, r=y(z)t(z), and mu(r)=1. Hence the map
z maps to (D,M,R,K;d,m,y(z),t(z),k)
is injective and gives the exact semiprime source reindexing
T_{F,11}=sum_{z in Z_{F,11}} mu(d) log(m)log(k) W(dm/x)psi(d/D_*)Phi(d/D)Phi(m/M)Phi(y(z)t(z)/R)Phi(k/K),
with the unchanged fixed equation dm+y(z)t(z)k=N. This reindexing preserves the original fixed N, the raw mu(d) sign, all four smooth labels and weights, the controlled-set complement, the actual endpoint selector, the stopping choice y(z), every gcd or unit mask already attached incidencewise, and the forward 1x1 parent-cell provenance. The second original Möbius factor is not discarded: it is forced to the exact value mu(r)=1 on this component.

Put S_src(z)={y(z),t(z)}. Then |S_src(z)|=2 for every z in Z_{F,11}. By contrast, every right packet tau in the DCE family of fact bf956b56ec0bf442 has support S_tau={r_1(tau),r_2(tau),r_3(tau),r_4(tau)} consisting of four pairwise distinct primes, so |S_tau|=4. Consequently, pointwise, there is no pair (z,tau) with z in Z_{F,11} and tau in that DCE family for which S_tau=S_src(z). If Z_{F,11} is nonempty, there is therefore no map from Z_{F,11} to that DCE right-packet family satisfying S_tau=S_src(z) for every z. Thus the literal four-prime DCE consumer is not an incidence-preserving leaf of the exact linear forward-1x1 source reindexing.

Its exact position inside any later four-prime packet ledger of the type in fact 4a9a213a428b7e8c is the following. Fix the DCE external modulus, one external window cell omega_0, and the particular nonnegative left and four-prime right packet families of facts d659d90d40151040 and bf956b56ec0bf442. Then the DCE same-cell support-disjoint consumer is the single bundled diagonal quantity
E_{0,q}=sum_{F subset {1,2,3,4}}(-1)^{|F|}U_{omega_0,omega_0,F}.
It is not the unrestricted face U_{omega_0,omega_0,emptyset} alone. Its fifteen nonempty overlap faces are, individually,
U_{omega_0,omega_0,{1}}, U_{omega_0,omega_0,{2}}, U_{omega_0,omega_0,{3}}, U_{omega_0,omega_0,{4}},
U_{omega_0,omega_0,{1,2}}, U_{omega_0,omega_0,{1,3}}, U_{omega_0,omega_0,{1,4}}, U_{omega_0,omega_0,{2,3}}, U_{omega_0,omega_0,{2,4}}, U_{omega_0,omega_0,{3,4}},
U_{omega_0,omega_0,{1,2,3}}, U_{omega_0,omega_0,{1,2,4}}, U_{omega_0,omega_0,{1,3,4}}, U_{omega_0,omega_0,{2,3,4}}, and U_{omega_0,omega_0,{1,2,3,4}}.
Fact bf956b56ec0bf442 bounds this bundled support-disjoint quantity under its explicit hypotheses; the value of the bundle alone does not determine any one of the fifteen individual face values. Indeed a single equal-carrier packet pair with S_tau contained in S_sigma has E_{0,q}=0 while all sixteen face quantities for that pair are equal to its positive pair weight. Every cross-cell quantity U_{omega,omega',F} with omega different from omega' is absent from E_{0,q} and is likewise not determined by it, for every F subset {1,2,3,4}; the same is true of a different diagonal terminal family not equal to the particular DCE family.

Within the component-specific literal primitive-conductor reconstruction architecture explicitly assumed in facts f5b31dd3643732ac and 4a9a213a428b7e8c, the semiprime reindexing above does not instantiate the additional formula T_{F,11}=R_{F,11}+Re(V_{F,11}) required there: it supplies no physical primitive-conductor Fourier data, carrier, external window cell, or four-prime packet coefficients. The pointwise support-cardinality argument shows only that such a formula cannot identify one forward-1x1 incidence with one support-preserving DCE right packet. A later equality or one-sided transfer could still pair source states, introduce additional packet data, or use a different majorization. If it introduces no new primes and forms each four-prime support as a union of source supports, at least two forward-1x1 semiprime states are required. For the particular DCE family, the fifteen faces are available only through the displayed alternating bundle unless additional face estimates are proved, and all cross-cell terms require separate input. Fact db54beb65db1bb72 further shows that arbitrary conductor declarations and a formally small standalone coefficient norm do not themselves instantiate the missing formula. No assertion is made that equality is the only possible route to a DCE estimate or that primitive-conductor data are necessary outside the stated f5b31dd3643732ac/4a9a213a428b7e8c architecture.
ae1febd328547ccc.proof:
Take z in Z_{F,11}. Nonzero w(z) implies mu(r) is nonzero, so r is squarefree. Forward boundary-admissibility gives the canonical complementary positive divisors y(z)t(z)=r. The 1x1 tag means Omega(y(z))=Omega(t(z))=1. A positive divisor of a squarefree integer with exactly one prime factor is a prime, so y(z) and t(z) are primes. They are distinct: equality would give r=y(z)^2, contradicting squarefreeness. Hence mu(r)=mu(y(z))mu(t(z))=(-1)(-1)=1.

The original labelled incidence z contains D,M,R,K,d,m,r,k, and r is recovered from the displayed image as y(z)t(z), so the reindexing map is injective. Substitute r=y(z)t(z) and mu(r)=1 into the definition of w(z) from fact 91db48815d136d4c. This gives exactly the displayed summand and changes no other factor. The defining incidence equation dm+rk=N becomes dm+y(z)t(z)k=N. Membership in Z_{F,11} is unchanged because the reindexing uses the same incidence and its canonical selector rather than replacing it by a new tuple. Facts aa34b1862b993377 and f5b31dd3643732ac prove that this component retains every incidence-dependent auxiliary mask and its parent provenance. This proves the exact partial transform and all stated preservation properties.

The source support S_src(z) has exactly two elements because y(z),t(z) are distinct primes. Fact bf956b56ec0bf442 requires each DCE right support to consist of four pairwise distinct primes, hence to have four elements. Equality of finite sets implies equality of their cardinalities, so no individual pair (z,tau) has S_tau=S_src(z). When Z_{F,11} is nonempty, any map to the DCE family has an image tau for each z, and that image fails the required support equality. This proves the conditional no-map assertion and the incidence-level nonidentification.

Fact 4a9a213a428b7e8c proves, for any fixed ordered window pair, the inclusion-exclusion identity for support disjointness. Specialize both window labels to omega_0 and the pair weights to the nonnegative factorized weights of fact d659d90d40151040. That fact identifies the resulting support-disjoint equal-carrier sum with E_{0,q}. Expanding the four factors 1-1_{r_i(tau) in S_sigma} gives exactly the displayed sum over all sixteen subsets F. A four-element set has the fifteen listed nonempty subsets, so the list is exhaustive.

To prove nondetermination of the separate faces by the bundle, take one left packet sigma and one right packet tau at the same carrier with positive pair weight, and assume S_tau is contained in S_sigma. The support-disjoint indicator is zero, so its contribution to E_{0,q} is zero. For every F subset {1,2,3,4}, every prime r_i(tau) with i in F lies in S_sigma, so the product of membership indicators in U_{omega_0,omega_0,F} is one. Thus all sixteen face contributions equal the same positive pair weight, while their alternating sum is (1-1)^4 times that weight, namely zero. Therefore the value of E_{0,q} alone does not recover any individual face value.

Every term used in E_{0,q} has the same fixed window label omega_0 on both sides. Therefore no pair with omega different from omega' occurs in it. In the exact ledger of fact 4a9a213a428b7e8c such pairs form the disjoint cross-cell sum, so changing or adjoining cross-cell pair weights does not change this fixed same-cell E_{0,q}. A different diagonal packet family is likewise not part of the particular specialization defining E_{0,q}.

Facts f5b31dd3643732ac and 4a9a213a428b7e8c state their Hilbert conclusions conditionally on an additional exact component-specific primitive-conductor leaf formula. The semiprime reindexing proved here defines only the original incidence variables and their canonical two-prime factorization, so it does not provide the auxiliary leaf data appearing in that additional hypothesis. The cardinality proof excludes only a one-incidence support equality. If a later construction forms a four-element support as a union of two-element source supports and introduces no other primes, one two-element set is insufficient, so at least two source supports are necessary. Fact db54beb65db1bb72 proves the final warning about arbitrary conductor declarations and gauge-rescaled coefficient norms. The final scope sentences explicitly leave other equalities and one-sided routes open, completing the proof without a universal nonimplication claim.

glossary.R_{F,11}: the real remainder in a hypothetical forward-1x1 component reconstruction
glossary.S_src(z): the two-prime support {y(z),t(z)} of a forward 1x1 source incidence
glossary.T_{F,11}: the signed sum of original incidence weights over Z_{F,11}
glossary.V_{F,11}: the primitive-conductor leaf sum in a hypothetical forward-1x1 component reconstruction
glossary.Z_{F,11}: the forward 1x1 endpoint terminal component of original labelled incidences
glossary.omega_0: the fixed external window cell of the particular DCE same-cell packet family

aeffec374578707c.title: POST-A BUFFER RESIDUAL LEDGER AND THE NEW FIRST OPEN CELL. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, fix 0<eta<sigma and omega>0, and define
aeffec374578707c.author: slava chan
aeffec374578707c.statement:
POST-A BUFFER RESIDUAL LEDGER AND THE NEW FIRST OPEN CELL. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, fix 0<eta<sigma and omega>0, and define
beta_0=6/5-2kappa,  beta_1=6/5-3sigma,  beta_m=6/5-12sigma/5,
Gamma_BC(beta)=max(0,(19beta-20)/17).
Use exactly the literal paired nonzero-Poisson forced-high source, physical balance hypotheses, exact outer-gcd normalization, forward/reverse conventions, original parent labels, and normalized anatomy partition of facts 15425579cb248eff and 24e911b7685090c1. Thus Q>1, beta is the normalized exponent, G is the actual normalized imbalance, and beta_orig is retained separately from beta.

Within the standard-marker post-low range beta_0<beta<beta_m, after removing the power-small families proved in facts 15425579cb248eff and 24e911b7685090c1, the complete still-unestimated ledger is the following disjoint union:
(I) beta_0<beta<=beta_1, orientation in {forward,reverse}, parent in {C91,U_sh,U_low}, anatomy in {B,C1,C2,C3}, and
Q^(-sigma+eta)<=G<Q^(Gamma_BC(beta)+omega);
(II) beta_1<beta<beta_m, the same orientation, parent and G ranges, and anatomy in {A,B,C1,C2,C3}.
All source, high, fixed-U, smooth/projective, Fourier, target-gcd, prime-order, collision, deletion, parent, orientation and exact outer-gcd labels remain part of this Cartesian refinement. The later sliver beta_m<=beta<6/5 retains the separate general normalized anatomy ledger of fact 15425579cb248eff and is not altered here.

The infimum of the normalized-beta values in the ledger is beta_0, and a structurally nonempty cell occurs in every sufficiently short right-neighborhood of beta_0 with forward orientation, parent U_low, anatomy B and G=1. Consequently, after anatomy A is paid through beta_1, one new first open standard-marker cell is
(parent,anatomy,beta,G)=(U_low,B,beta_0+,1).
This is an exact coverage/no-fit ledger. It gives no estimate for B,C1,C2,C3, for A above beta_1, for the later general-anatomy sliver, endpoints, PMD, logical bad-N capture or Goldbach.
aeffec374578707c.proof:
Fact 15425579cb248eff proves that, in beta_0<beta<beta_m, the unchanged source atoms have a disjoint exhaustive Cartesian refinement by the two strict orientations, parents C91,U_sh,U_low, anatomies A,B,C1,C2,C3 above the empty C0 cell, and actual G. It also proves that every actual G is at least a fixed positive constant for sufficiently large Q, hence no actual cell has 0<G<Q^(-sigma+eta), and that the complete fixed-g Poisson estimate pays every cell with G>=Q^(Gamma_BC(beta)+omega). It proves all cells with beta<=beta_0 are power-small, including bounded bases and every exact outer-gcd layer.

Fact 24e911b7685090c1 proves that every anatomy-A cell with beta_0<beta<=beta_1 is power-small for both orientations and every actual G>0, retaining every label listed in the statement. Removing these A cells from the disjoint ledger of fact 15425579cb248eff leaves exactly the anatomy set {B,C1,C2,C3} in slab (I). In slab (II), fact 24e911b7685090c1 makes no assertion, so the anatomy set remains {A,B,C1,C2,C3}. The G, parent, orientation and provenance coordinates are unchanged because the removal is by the anatomy-A and beta selectors only. This proves the two displayed residual families and their disjointness. The general-anatomy sliver is exactly the separate sliver stated in fact 15425579cb248eff, so no claim about its anatomy is added.

It remains to prove structural nonemptiness of the displayed B cell. Fix beta_* with
beta_0<beta_*<beta_1.
Because beta_1<beta_m, fact 6414b11506a84ff0 applies with the standard cutoffs
L=Q^(beta_*-1+sigma),  S_0=Q^(2beta_*-2+3sigma),  Z=Q^(3/2-beta_*-3sigma)
for all sufficiently large Q. Choose a real epsilon satisfying
0<epsilon<min(beta_*-1,1/2),
and put
a=(2beta_*-2+3sigma+epsilon)/3,
b_4=2-beta_*-3sigma-epsilon.
Then
a<beta_*-1+sigma
because 3(beta_*-1+sigma)-(2beta_*-2+3sigma+epsilon)=beta_*-1-epsilon>0,                 (1)
and
b_4>3/2-beta_*-3sigma
because b_4-(3/2-beta_*-3sigma)=1/2-epsilon>0.                                      (2)
Also
3a+b_4=beta_*.                                                                       (3)

Let T tend to infinity and put Q=T. By repeated use of the prime-in-(y,2y) theorem recorded in fact b7fcb27a091203e5, choose three distinct odd primes p_1,p_2,p_3, each within fixed constant multiples of T^a, and a fourth odd prime t within fixed constant multiples of T^b_4. The strict power inequalities (1)-(2) imply, for sufficiently large T,
p_i<L for 1<=i<=3,  and  t>Z.                                                        (4)
Put r=p_1p_2p_3t. Equation (3) gives r=T^(beta_*+o(1)). No prime divisor of r lies in (L,Z), while
v_L(r)=p_1p_2p_3=T^(2beta_*-2+3sigma+epsilon+o(1))>S_0.                              (5)
Thus the mutually exclusive alternative B of fact 6414b11506a84ff0 applies to r. Since beta_*<beta_m, its remaining hypothesis Z^4>r holds by fact 15425579cb248eff.

Embed r into the accepted structural source construction in Part (E) of fact 15425579cb248eff. Explicitly, choose an odd prime d of scale T distinct from the four primes above, set g=1 and m=d, choose a fixed constant c>1 as in that construction, choose an odd positive integer k=c d^2/r+O(1), put N=dm+rk and x=N/2, and take the active dyadic labels D,M,R,K around d,m,r,k. Then DM and RK are comparable to x, N is even, Q=D/g=T^(1+o(1)), normalized beta is beta_*+o(1), and G=M/Q=1+o(1); by choosing the dyadic normalization used in Part (E), this is the same G=1 structural cell. Replacing the former interval-prime factorization of r by (4)-(5) changes neither the scale exponents nor any source-parent predicate. Therefore the forced-high, 60-residual, outside-C91, deep-scale predicates proved in Part (E) remain valid, and the frozen parent is U_low. The marked factor now lies in anatomy B by (5).

Finally beta_* may be chosen in every sufficiently short right-neighborhood of beta_0 contained in (beta_0,beta_1). Since all beta<=beta_0 cells are power-small by fact 15425579cb248eff, the infimum of the remaining normalized-beta ledger is beta_0. The constructed B cell has G=1. Existing estimates cited by fact 15425579cb248eff do not pay it: their all-anatomy low-beta hypotheses stop at beta_0, and Gamma_BC(beta_*)>0 while G=1. Fact 24e911b7685090c1 pays only anatomy A. Hence (U_low,B,beta_0+,1) is a first open standard-marker cell in the asserted coverage sense. No estimate of its signed contribution has been made.

glossary.b_4: The exponent 2-beta_*-3sigma-epsilon of the fourth, Z-rough prime in the structural B-cell construction.
glossary.beta_*: A fixed normalized exponent strictly between beta_0 and beta_1 used in the structural B-cell construction.
glossary.mathscr R_postA: The disjoint standard-marker residual source ledger after the interval-prime A buffer is removed.

af06640e8d8e4102.title: SELECTED FIXED-BAD-\(N\) C91, SHALLOW, AND LOW-\(Z\) CLEANUP WITH A POST-LOW INTERFACE
af06640e8d8e4102.author: slava chan
af06640e8d8e4102.statement:
SELECTED FIXED-BAD-\(N\) C91, SHALLOW, AND LOW-\(Z\) CLEANUP WITH A POST-LOW INTERFACE.

Fix \(0<\kappa\le 1/100\), put \(\sigma=\kappa/100\), and fix \(0<\eta<\sigma\). Use the \(C^\infty\) functions \(W,\psi,\Phi\), the quantifier order, the fixed exponents \(B_{\rm init},B_{\rm src}\), the scales
\[
 Q_{\rm init}=(2x)^{1/2}(\log(2x))^{-B_{\rm init}},
 \qquad D_*=x^{1/2}(\log x)^{-B_{\rm src}},
\]
and the same selected dyadic block \((D,M,U)\) for every sufficiently large bad even integer \(N=2x\) from facts \(1de7f7c45ccfee10\) and \(1e2d635f6691e832\). Thus
\[
 B_{\rm src}>B_{\rm init}+1,\qquad 2D>Q_{\rm init}.             \tag{1}
\]
Set
\[
 X_{\rm bal}=Q_{\rm init}/2.                                   \tag{2}
\]
Use the parameters \(\kappa_t=\kappa,\eta_t=\eta\) in the parent construction of fact \(77d7a3419a07305c\). Let \(\mathcal R^{\ne0}_{C91,\mathrm{sel}}\) be the sum of all literal conjugate-paired nonzero-Poisson atoms in the selected \(60\)-residual high family of facts \(60b26a9b6f79467a\) and \(77d7a3419a07305c\) whose dyadic label has parent \(C91\).

Then, for every fixed \(A>0\), uniformly along the selected bad integers,
\[
 \left|\mathcal R^{\ne0}_{C91,\mathrm{sel}}\right|
 \ll_{A,\eta}x^{1-\eta/40}+x(\log x)^{-A}.                    \tag{3}
\]
This estimate is for each complete nonzero-frequency dyadic label before any anatomy, actual-\((r,k)\), exact-\(g\), or other incidence deletion.

More precisely, the following assertions hold for all sufficiently large \(x\).

(A) Depth and empty balanced/shallow clauses. One has
\[
 X_{\rm bal}\ge 4D_*,\qquad D>X_{\rm bal},\qquad R>D           \tag{4}
\]
on every selected residual-high label. Consequently the balanced base clause is empty both for an original base label and for the base scale tuple obtained after swapping the two divisor-complement pairs. Also \(D,R\ge4D_*\), so the parent \(U_{\rm sh}\) is empty on the selected high family.

(B) Exact swap-only seam. Write
\[
 \mathcal C_{91}=\mathcal A\cup\iota(\mathcal A\cap\mathcal G)
\]
as in fact \(77d7a3419a07305c\). A direct label in \(\mathcal A\) lies in
\(\mathcal A_{\rm FT}\cup\mathcal A_{\rm UBC}\). If
\[
 \lambda=(D,M,R,K)\in\iota(\mathcal A\cap\mathcal G)\setminus\mathcal A,
 \qquad
 \lambda^\dagger=\iota(\lambda)=(D',M',R',K')=(R,K,D,M),
\]
then no separate arithmetic orbit mate is imported. Inside the same complete sum make the exact change
\[
 (d',m',r',k')=(r,k,d,m).                                      \tag{5}
\]
The condition \(\lambda^\dagger\in\mathcal G\) gives
\(d,r\ge2D_*\) throughout the dyadic support, so both possible asymmetric factors
\(\psi(d/D_*)\) and \(\psi(r/D_*)\) equal one. The transformed complete arithmetic sum has the joint scaled weight
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal W}_{\lambda^\dagger}(s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4)
 =
 W\!\left(\frac{R'K's_3s_4}{x}\right)
 \Phi\!\left(\frac{D'M's_1s_2}{U}\right)
 \prod_{j=1}^4\Phi(s_j),                                      \tag{6}
\]
where \(D'M'=RK\asymp x\) and \(R'K'=DM\asymp x\). Thus the original fixed-\(U\) mask is retained, now on the first transformed product. The tuple \(\lambda^\dagger\) satisfies its declared FT or UBC hypotheses, and
\[
 \mathcal Q_{\lambda}^{(\ne0),\mathrm{orig}}
 =
 \mathcal Q_{N,\widetilde{\mathcal W}}(D',M';R',K')
 -
 \mathcal Q_{\lambda}^{(0),\mathrm{orig}}.                     \tag{7}
\]
The zero mode subtracted in (7) is the original forward zero mode; no equality between the original and swapped nonzero Poisson pieces is asserted.

(C) Actual low-\(Z\) support. On every original source incidence carried by a selected forced-high label,
\[
 r>k.                                                          \tag{8}
\]
Hence the exact actual-sibling cells \(Z_{\rm low}\) and \(Z_{\rm diag}\) of fact \(aa34b1862b993377\) are empty on these labels. After \(C91\) precedence, the exhaustive actual-incidence survivor list is
\[
 Z_{\rm mid}\ \sqcup\ Z_{\rm end}\ \sqcup\ Z_{\rm sup}.        \tag{9}
\]
For an incidence in \(Z_{\rm mid}\),
\[
 R\ll x^{2/3},\qquad
 \beta_{\rm orig}:=\frac{\log R}{\log D}\le \frac43+o(1).       \tag{10}
\]
The reverse endpoint orientation and \(U_{\rm sup}\) are therefore absent there. Outside \(C91\), a \(Z_{\rm mid}\) incidence may have parent \(U_{\rm low}\), one of the four forward endpoint parents, or \(U_{\rm gap}\); the last two possibilities can occur only in the endpoint-overlap region where the original label exponent reaches \(4/3\).

(D) Normalized-beta and post-low interface. On every forward exact-\(g\) layer with \(Q=D/g>1\), put
\[
 B=R/g=Q^{\beta_{\rm norm}}.
\]
Then \(1\le\beta_{\rm orig}\le\beta_{\rm norm}\). Hence when
\[
 \beta_{\rm norm}<\frac43,                                    \tag{11}
\]
and in particular throughout the accepted ledger \(\beta_{\rm norm}<6/5\), neither an endpoint parent nor \(U_{\rm gap}\) is possible. After (3) and (A), the only surviving nonterminal parent in that ledger is \(U_{\rm low}\). The band
\[
 6/5\le\beta_{\rm norm}<4/3
\]
has the same parent conclusion but is not estimated by fact \(15425579cb248eff\). When \(\beta_{\rm norm}\ge4/3\), the actual \(Z_{\rm mid}\) endpoint-overlap sliver described in (C) may contain forward endpoint parents or \(U_{\rm gap}\).

Within the standard-marker range \(\beta_0<\beta_{\rm norm}<\beta_m\) of fact \(15425579cb248eff\), the selected-block cleanup therefore changes its parent list
\(\{C91,U_{\rm sh},U_{\rm low}\}\) to the single parent \(U_{\rm low}\).
At the stage of fact \(15425579cb248eff\), its first structurally live cell was the
\(U_{\rm low}\), interval-prime \(A\), \(G=1\) buffer at
\(\beta_{\rm norm}=\beta_0+\). Thus the cleanup agrees with that interface.
After the later accepted estimate \(24e911b7685090c1\), fact
\(aeffec374578707c\) makes the current first open standard-marker cell
\[
 (U_{\rm low},B,\beta_0+,G=1).                                 \tag{12}
\]

(E) Deletion boundary. Equation (3) does not imply stability under an arbitrary proper incidence deletion. An already accepted independently power-small sector may be subtracted from a complete label or complete disjoint aggregate by the exact identity “remainder = complete aggregate minus paid sector.” In contrast, the hard selector
\(\mathbf 1_{r<k^2}\) defining \(Z_{\rm mid}\) is not a fixed \(C^\infty\) scaled-smooth joint weight, and one smooth dyadic label may meet both sides of \(r=k^2\). This is the first failed hypothesis in any attempt to apply fact \(df9748efe29ab475\) directly to an arbitrary \(Z_{\rm mid}\)-deleted Poisson piece.

No negative \(C2\) conclusion, terminal deficit, endpoint capture, four-prime equivalence, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
af06640e8d8e4102.proof:
We prove the assertions in order.

1. The depth calculation. By (1)-(2),
\[
 \frac{X_{\rm bal}}{4D_*}
 =
 \frac{\sqrt2}{8}\,
 \frac{(\log x)^{B_{\rm src}}}{(\log(2x))^{B_{\rm init}}}.
\]
Since \(B_{\rm src}>B_{\rm init}+1\), this ratio tends to infinity. Hence
\(X_{\rm bal}\ge4D_*\) for sufficiently large \(x\). The literal inequality
\(2D>Q_{\rm init}\) gives \(D>X_{\rm bal}\). Fact
\(60b26a9b6f79467a\) proves that every selected residual label has \(R>D\).
This proves (4).

The balanced clause in the base set \(\mathcal A\) requires its first divisor
scale to be at most \(X_{\rm bal}\). It therefore fails on the original tuple
because its first scale is \(D>X_{\rm bal}\). After swapping, its first divisor
scale is \(R>D>X_{\rm bal}\), so it fails there too. Finally
\(D,R\ge4D_*\), and the definition in fact \(77d7a3419a07305c\) assigns
\(U_{\rm sh}\) only when \(\min(D,R)<4D_*\). Thus \(U_{\rm sh}\) is empty.
This proves (A).

2. Direct base labels. Fix a selected high label belonging directly to
\(\mathcal A\). The preceding paragraph excludes \(\mathcal A_{\rm bal}\);
hence the label belongs to \(\mathcal A_{\rm FT}\) or
\(\mathcal A_{\rm UBC}\). On its support,
\[
 d\ge D/2>X_{\rm bal}/2\ge2D_*,
\]
so \(\psi(d/D_*)=1\). In the scaled variables
\(d=Ds_1,m=Ms_2,r=Rs_3,k=Ks_4\), the literal joint weight is
\[
 W\!\left(\frac{DM s_1s_2}{x}\right)
 \Phi\!\left(\frac{RK s_3s_4}{U}\right)\prod_{j=1}^4\Phi(s_j). \tag{13}
\]
Fact \(1e2d635f6691e832\) proves that active support gives \(DM\asymp x\)
and \(RK\asymp U\asymp x\). Therefore every scaled derivative of (13) is
uniformly bounded, exactly by the chain-rule check in that fact. The support
lies in the fixed product of the supports of the four one-variable \(\Phi\)'s.

Apply consequence (2) of fact \(df9748efe29ab475\) to an FT label and
consequence (1), with its parameter equal to \(\eta\), to a UBC label. This
bounds the complete arithmetic label. The original Poisson zero mode is
\(O_A(x(\log x)^{-A})\) by the zero-frequency assertion of the same fact,
because \(D>X_{\rm bal}\ge x^{2/5}\) for sufficiently large \(x\). Subtracting
that original zero mode bounds the complete original nonzero-frequency label.
No proper incidence selector has been inserted.

3. Swap-only labels. Let
\(\lambda\in\iota(\mathcal A\cap\mathcal G)\setminus\mathcal A\) and define
\(\lambda^\dagger\) as in (B). The membership
\(\lambda^\dagger\in\mathcal G\) says \(D',R'\ge4D_*\), equivalently
\(R,D\ge4D_*\). Hence the dyadic support gives \(d,r\ge2D_*\), and both
cutoffs mentioned in (B) equal one.

The change (5) is a bijection on the integer solutions: it sends
\[
 dm+rk=N
\quad\hbox{to}\quad
 d'm'+r'k'=N.
\]
It also preserves
\[
 \mu(d)\mu(r)=\mu(d')\mu(r'),\qquad
 \log m\log k=\log m'\log k'.
\]
The four dyadic factors are permuted. Moreover,
\[
 W(dm/x)=W(r'k'/x),\qquad
 \Phi(rk/U)=\Phi(d'm'/U).
\]
Writing the transformed variables in their scaled coordinates gives exactly
(6). Thus the fixed-\(U\) mask has not been dropped. Active support gives
\(D'M'=RK\asymp x\) and \(R'K'=DM\asymp x\), so the same chain-rule
argument as for (13) proves that (6) belongs to a uniformly scaled-smooth
compact family accepted by the general theorem in
\(df9748efe29ab475\).

The tuple \(\lambda^\dagger\) belongs to \(\mathcal A\). Its balanced clause
is impossible because its first scale is \(D'=R>D>X_{\rm bal}\).
Consequently it satisfies its declared FT or UBC inequalities. Apply the
corresponding consequence of \(df9748efe29ab475\) to the transformed
complete arithmetic sum. This is an internal variable change in the same
sum; no assertion that a separate selected source label at
\(\lambda^\dagger\) exists is used.

By definition of the original forward Poisson decomposition,
\[
 \mathcal Q_{\lambda}^{(\ne0),\mathrm{orig}}
 =\mathcal Q_{\lambda}-\mathcal Q_{\lambda}^{(0),\mathrm{orig}}.
\]
The change (5) identifies \(\mathcal Q_{\lambda}\) with the transformed whole
sum, and the original zero mode is logarithmically small by
\(df9748efe29ab475\), as in Step 2. This proves (7). It deliberately does
not compare the two Poisson nonzero pieces.

Facts \(1e2d635f6691e832\) and \(df9748efe29ab475\) give only
polylogarithmically many active dyadic labels. For every UBC label the
per-label power bound is \(x^{1-3\eta/80}\). Absorb the label count into
\(x^{\eta/80}\); for FT and zero-mode bounds apply the logarithmic estimate
with exponent \(A+5\) before summing. The direct and swap-only sets cover
\(\mathcal C_{91}\), with their overlap assigned to the direct set. This proves
(3).

4. Actual \(Z\)-support. On a selected high label, fact
\(60b26a9b6f79467a\) gives
\[
 R>x^{9/16-\kappa_0},\qquad \kappa_0=1/200.
\]
The dyadic support gives \(r\ge R/2\). Also \(RK\asymp x\), and the dyadic
support gives \(rk\ll x\). Therefore
\[
 \frac{r^2}{rk}\gg\frac{R^2}{x}
 >x^{\,1/8-2\kappa_0}/4,
\]
which tends to infinity. Thus \(r^2>rk\), equivalently \(r>k\), for all
sufficiently large \(x\). By the exact definitions in fact
\(aa34b1862b993377\), \(Z_{\rm low}\) and \(Z_{\rm diag}\) are empty.
Its five-way actual-incidence partition then leaves exactly (9) outside
\(C91\).

If the incidence is in \(Z_{\rm mid}\), then \(r<k^2\), so
\[
 r^3<(rk)^2\ll x^2.
\]
Thus \(r\ll x^{2/3}\), and the dyadic support gives \(R\le2r\ll x^{2/3}\).
On the other hand, Step 1 gives
\[
 D>X_{\rm bal}
 =\frac{(2x)^{1/2}}{2(\log(2x))^{B_{\rm init}}}.
\]
Taking logarithms proves (10). Fact \(60b26a9b6f79467a\) gives \(R>D\), so
reverse boundary admissibility is impossible. Since
\(\kappa<1/6\), (10) also gives
\(\beta_{\rm orig}<3/2-\kappa\) for sufficiently large \(x\), so
\(U_{\rm sup}\) is impossible. The parent precedence of fact
\(77d7a3419a07305c\) now leaves exactly \(U_{\rm low}\), a forward endpoint
tag when boundary admissibility holds, or \(U_{\rm gap}\) when the label is
in the endpoint exponent band but boundary admissibility fails. This proves
(C). It is an inventory of the accepted actual-incidence partition; no
Poisson estimate after the \(Z_{\rm mid}\) deletion has been inferred.

5. Normalized-beta ledger. Fact \(15425579cb248eff\) proves on every forward
exact-\(g\) layer with \(Q>1\) that
\[
 1\le\beta_{\rm orig}\le\beta_{\rm norm}.
\]
Hence (11) forces \(\beta_{\rm orig}<4/3\). The endpoint predicate and
\(U_{\rm gap}\) both require original label exponent at least \(4/3\), while
\(U_{\rm sup}\) requires an even larger exponent. After the already proved
absence of \(C91\) from the remaining aggregate and the emptiness of
\(U_{\rm sh}\), the only nonterminal parent is \(U_{\rm low}\). This applies
in particular for \(\beta_{\rm norm}<6/5\). The same implication applies in
the separate unestimated band \(6/5\le\beta_{\rm norm}<4/3\). When
\(\beta_{\rm norm}\ge4/3\), it no longer forces the original exponent below
\(4/3\), so the endpoint and \(U_{\rm gap}\) alternatives in Step 4 remain.

Part (D) of fact \(15425579cb248eff\) gives the exact standard-marker
post-low ledger with parents \(C91,U_{\rm sh},U_{\rm low}\). Removing the
first by (3) and the second by emptiness leaves \(U_{\rm low}\). Part (E) of
that fact identifies its first structural no-fit as the interval-prime
\(A\), \(G=1\), \(\beta_0+\) cell. Fact \(24e911b7685090c1\) subsequently
pays every \(A\) cell through its first buffer, and fact
\(aeffec374578707c\) proves that the current first open standard-marker cell
is (12). This proves (D).

6. Scope of subtraction. The proof of (3) applied
\(df9748efe29ab475\) to a complete smooth label and only then subtracted the
independently bounded original zero mode. If a disjoint sector \(E\) has an
independent accepted absolute bound, the exact identity
\[
 \mathcal Q_{\rm remainder}=\mathcal Q_{\rm complete}-E
\]
and the triangle inequality permit its subtraction. This does not give a
bound for an arbitrary sector.

In particular, \(\mathbf 1_{r<k^2}\) is discontinuous in the scaled variables.
Fact \(aa34b1862b993377\) also explicitly warns that the smooth labels \(R,K\)
do not determine the actual comparison of \(r\) and \(k\); one label may
straddle \(r=k^2\). Hence the fixed \(C^\infty\), uniformly scaled-smooth
joint-weight hypothesis of \(df9748efe29ab475\) is the first hypothesis that
fails for an arbitrary \(Z_{\rm mid}\)-deleted Poisson sum. This proves (E)
and all asserted scope exclusions.

glossary.lambda^dagger: The swapped scale tuple iota(lambda) used only to check the base FT or UBC hypothesis after an internal variable change.
glossary.mathcal R^{ne0}_{C91,sel}: The sum of complete literal paired nonzero-Poisson dyadic labels in the selected fixed-bad-N residual-high family whose frozen parent is C91.
glossary.widetilde mathcal W_{lambda^dagger}: The exact transformed joint scaled weight after interchanging the two divisor-complement variable pairs while retaining the fixed-U mask.

af160c5d26126afd.title: SHARP SELECTED-C3 NEGATIVITY NO-FIT: FIRST-BUFFER PROJECTION VERSUS THE FULL SAME-N REMAINDER
af160c5d26126afd.author: slava chan
af160c5d26126afd.statement:
SHARP SELECTED-C3 NEGATIVITY NO-FIT: FIRST-BUFFER PROJECTION VERSUS THE FULL SAME-N REMAINDER.

Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, beta_0=6/5-2kappa and beta_1=6/5-3sigma. Let x be sufficiently large, N=2x, and assume the selected fixed-N hypotheses of fact 32f645844f1ca9a1: c(N)>=C_2>0; forward atoms have R>D, DM comparable to x, D comparable to x^(1/2) up to logarithms and R>x^(9/16-1/200); reverse atoms have D>R, RK comparable to x, R comparable to x^(1/2) up to logarithms and D>x^(9/16-1/200); all physical scales are O(x); and every selected source, fixed-U, high, smooth, Fourier, target-gcd, prime-order, collision, deletion, orientation, parent, provenance and exact outer-gcd coordinate is retained.

Let R_full be the finite real aggregate called R_postABC2,sel in fact 32f645844f1ca9a1. Thus
R_full<=-A_x+epsilon_x,                                              (1)
where A_x=c_dir c(N)x/log x with c_dir>0 and epsilon_x=o(c(N)x/log x).

Let R_C3,buf be the projection of R_full onto atoms with beta_0<beta<=beta_1, and let
R_out=R_full-R_C3,buf.                                               (2)
Then the accepted ledger gives the exact identity
R_full=R_C3,buf+R_out,                                               (3)
and every atom of R_C3,buf has frozen parent U_low and sole anatomy C3. It does not give R_out=0.

For every 0<theta<=1 and every real rho,
R_C3,buf<=-theta A_x+rho                                             (4)
if and only if
R_out>=R_full+theta A_x-rho.                                        (5)
Using only (1), the sharp uniform sufficient complement inequality is
R_out>=-(1-theta)A_x+epsilon_x-rho.                                 (6)
In particular, a negative full same-N remainder does not imply any negative first-buffer C3 projection without a one-sided lower bound for R_out.

There is also an exact direct-theorem no-fit. The forward literal C3 trace fact da22464a2f614042 requires both DM and RK comparable to its physical scale, whereas the selected forward hypotheses above provide a two-sided comparison only for DM. The reverse fact 2e0b40b1ba77fb6f requires both products as well, whereas the selected reverse hypotheses provide a two-sided comparison only for RK. Therefore neither theorem directly estimates every selected C3 buffer layer from the hypotheses displayed here.

This is a coefficient/ledger and theorem-hypothesis no-fit, not an impossibility theorem. It gives no lower bound for R_out, no estimate for the complete selected C3 projection, no individual negative cell, no moving actual-Z, endpoint, PMD, DCE, four-prime capture, Goldbach implication, or Goldbach conclusion.
af160c5d26126afd.proof:
Fact 32f645844f1ca9a1 defines R_full by subtracting the complete selected C2 aggregate only on the normalized-beta range beta_0<beta<=beta_1 from the earlier full selected remainder. Its exact C3-only ledger is explicitly restricted to that same range. Therefore the beta-buffer projection of R_full is exactly the stated U_low,C3 aggregate R_C3,buf, while all atoms of R_full outside that projection form R_out. This proves (2)-(3) and shows that the predecessor does not assert R_out=0.

Equation (3) gives
R_C3,buf=R_full-R_out.
Thus (4) is equivalent to
R_full-R_out<=-theta A_x+rho,
which after rearrangement is exactly (5). By (1),
R_full+theta A_x-rho
<=-(1-theta)A_x+epsilon_x-rho.
Hence (6) implies (5), and therefore (4).

The sufficiency threshold is sharp using only (1): in the abstract real coefficient model take R_full=-A_x+epsilon_x and choose
R_out=-(1-theta)A_x+epsilon_x-rho.
Then R_C3,buf=R_full-R_out=-theta A_x+rho, so equality holds in (4) and (6). In particular, taking R_C3,buf=0 and R_out=-A_x gives a negative full aggregate with no negative C3 projection. This is an algebraic coefficient-interface model, not a claimed construction inside the literal source.

For the theorem-match statement, read the hypotheses of the two accepted exact-layer facts. Fact da22464a2f614042 assumes forward R>D and two-sided comparisons of both DM and RK with its scale x. The forward hypotheses restated here, exactly as in fact 32f645844f1ca9a1, give a two-sided comparison for DM but only an O(x) upper bound for the remaining physical scales; no positive lower bound RK>>x is present. Fact 2e0b40b1ba77fb6f is the reverse permutation and again assumes both products comparable. The selected reverse hypotheses give the two-sided comparison for RK but not for DM. A fixed rescaling of x changes constants but cannot create a missing lower bound. Consequently the accepted layer theorems cannot be applied to every selected buffer layer under only the displayed assumptions. This proves the direct-theorem no-fit and all scope statements.

glossary.A_x: The positive comparison scale c_dir c(N)x/log x.
glossary.R_C3,buf: The projection of R_full to beta_0<beta<=beta_1, whose sole anatomy is C3.
glossary.R_full: The full selected same-N post-A,B,C1,C2 remainder from fact 32f645844f1ca9a1.
glossary.R_out: The complement R_full-R_C3,buf outside the first normalized-beta buffer.
glossary.epsilon_x: The little-o error in the selected negative remainder bound.

af2d16567b876aaf.title: FINAL FORWARD NEAR-BALANCED ALL-PARENT ASSEMBLY IN THE VERY-LOW-BETA STRIP. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, sigma=kappa/100, and 0<eta<sigma. Use the literal forward high-source atom family, exact outer-gcd normalization d=ga,r=gb, paired nonzero-Poisson coefficients, frozen parents, and normalized marker coefficients of facts 7131a06664967733 and a71f777ad842c886. Thus R>D, Q=D/g, B=R/g, H_T=B/Q, G=M/Q, H_P=B/M, L_src=N/g, and each exact g-layer is the unchanged sum over parents P and standard marker leaves C0,A,B,C1,C2,C3 with cutoffs L=H_TQ^sigma, S_0=H_T^2Q^{3sigma}, Z=Q^{3/2-beta-3sigma}, where beta=log B/log Q
af2d16567b876aaf.author: slava chan
af2d16567b876aaf.statement:
FINAL FORWARD NEAR-BALANCED ALL-PARENT ASSEMBLY IN THE VERY-LOW-BETA STRIP. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, sigma=kappa/100, and 0<eta<sigma.
