Use the literal forward high-source atom family, exact outer-gcd normalization d=ga,r=gb, paired nonzero-Poisson coefficients, frozen parents, and normalized marker coefficients of facts 7131a06664967733 and a71f777ad842c886. Thus R>D, Q=D/g, B=R/g, H_T=B/Q, G=M/Q, H_P=B/M, L_src=N/g, and each exact g-layer is the unchanged sum over parents P and standard marker leaves C0,A,B,C1,C2,C3 with cutoffs L=H_TQ^sigma, S_0=H_T^2Q^{3sigma}, Z=Q^{3/2-beta-3sigma}, where beta=log B/log Q.
Assume c_1x<=DM,RK<=C_1x, c_Dx^{1/2}(log x)^{-A_D}<=D<=C_Dx^{1/2}, and all physical scales are at most Cx. Let mathcal G be the exact outer-gcd layers g|N for which Q is sufficiently large,
1<=beta<=1+sigma/4,
and Q^{-sigma+eta}<=G<=Q^{sigma-eta}. Let R_near be the sum of every parent and every normalized marker leaf on all g in mathcal G, retaining every literal source coefficient, phase, fixed-U mask, high-label mask and parent mask. Add also every bounded-normalized-base C0 layer from the same forward source.
Then there exists delta=delta(kappa,eta)>0 such that
|R_near|<<x^{1-delta}.
More generally, for 1+sigma/4<beta<=6/5-2kappa the same conclusion holds after deleting only those A incidences whose exact target gcd c=gcd(a,L_src) lies in the medium band Q^{sigma/2}<c<H_TQ^{sigma/4}. No B,C1,C2,C3,C0, Fourier-frequency, parent, collision, prime-order, source-amplitude, target-size, or Type-I-unit sector is deleted. This theorem does not estimate outer-g layers outside the displayed G strip or the displayed medium target-gcd A band.
af2d16567b876aaf.proof:
We work layer by layer and then sum g.

Exact anatomy and parents. Fact a71f777ad842c886 gives the pointwise normalized identity after cancelling the repeated outer-g Mobius sign, while preserving q_z, the fixed target, source masks, exact g and parent. On the low-beta forward range its only parents are C91,U_sh,U_low, and each parent predicate is a scalar depending only on the original dyadic label. With the standard cutoffs, fact 6414b11506a84ff0 and the geometry e18b670f5d48f500 give exactly A,B,C1,C2,C3 above S_0. Fact 8bf5ca45f71b8c2c shows C0 is empty for sufficiently large Q and pays every bounded-Q C0 layer by O(x^{1/2+epsilon}). Thus it remains to estimate A through C3 at fixed g.

Literal frequency and amplitude. Fact d26acaefc372b4d0 maps the exact forward reciprocity phase to the fixed target -L_src, proves |L_src|=O(GQ^2)<=Q^3 on the G strip, and shows the archimedean reciprocity factor is a uniformly scaled-smooth amplitude because L_src/(QM)=N/(DM). Fact 3e326f797b2e04e4 sums every dyadic nonzero frequency, including H_P<1, with the exact Fourier decay supplied by the literal Poisson transform. Hence B,C1,C2,C3 are each O(Q^{2-delta_1}) at fixed g for some uniform delta_1>0. The exact stopping gcd selector is paid by 95626318cdcc099f. Prime ordering, repeated-prime collisions, Vaughan boxes and all smooth labels are already included in 3e326f797b2e04e4. Fact df2841924153b718 proves orientation- and branchwise that every literal Type-I phase has unit multiplier one, so bbcb9f66597c667c is applied with its exact fixed-target hypothesis.

Target gcd in A. For each A incidence put c=gcd(a,L_src). Fact 1c64020b89f097c4 gives the exact descended unit target. Fact ec9d666ae1756a03 bounds the aggregate c<=Q^{sigma/2} full-frequency trace by O(Q^{2-delta_2}). For c>=H_TQ^{sigma/4}, fact 5fbdbbebf99aec55, with B=QH_T and xi=sigma/4, gives O(Q^{2-sigma/4+epsilon}). All of its polynomial scale hypotheses hold here because B<=Q^{6/5}, H_P<=H_TQ^{sigma-eta}<=Q, and every factor scale is at most B. If beta<=1+sigma/4, then H_T=Q^{beta-1}<=Q^{sigma/4}, so H_TQ^{sigma/4}<=Q^{sigma/2}; the small and large c ranges overlap and exhaust every squarefree target gcd c. For general beta, they exhaust every c outside exactly Q^{sigma/2}<c<H_TQ^{sigma/4}, proving the second scope.

Outer-g summation. Let delta_0 be the minimum of all fixed per-layer savings just obtained. The number of parents, anatomy types and auxiliary dyadic labels is polylogarithmic. Since Q=D/g,
sum_{g|N,Q large}Q^{2-delta_0}<=D^{2-delta_0}sum_{g>=1}g^{-2+delta_0}<<D^{2-delta_0}.
Using D<=C_Dx^{1/2}, this is O(x^{1-delta_0/2}). Divisor and logarithmic label factors are absorbed by reducing the exponent. Add the bounded-Q C0 estimate O(x^{1/2+epsilon}). This proves the first assertion and the deleted-band version. Every retained object listed in the scope sentence is preserved by the cited exact identity or explicitly paid by the cited analytic facts.

glossary.R_near: The complete literal forward all-parent sum over mathcal G plus bounded-base C0.
glossary.mathcal G: The exact outer-gcd layers in the near-balanced very-low-beta strip.
glossary.medium target-gcd A band: The exact c interval not covered by the verified small-c and large-c A estimates.

af579dffb21039b1.title: SEPARATED-OUTER EXTENSION OF THE FIXED-TARGET \(v p\) ENDPOINT
af579dffb21039b1.author: slava chan
af579dffb21039b1.statement:
SEPARATED-OUTER EXTENSION OF THE FIXED-TARGET \(v p\) ENDPOINT.

Fix \(0<\kappa\le1/100\) and integers \(J,C_A\ge1\), and put
\[
 \sigma=\kappa/100.
\]
Let
\[
 1\le\beta\le6/5-2\kappa.
\]
For \(Q\) sufficiently large in terms of \(\kappa,J,C_A\), define
\[
 R=Q^\beta,\qquad H=R/Q.
\]
Let
\[
 1\le V\le H^2Q^{3\sigma},\qquad P=R/V.
\]
Let \(\xi_v\) be supported on squarefree integers \(V\le v<2V\) and satisfy
\[
 |\xi_v|\le\tau_J(v).
\]
Assume that every supported \(v\) is coprime to every prime \(p\) with \(P\le p<2P\).

Let \(A\) be a fixed nonzero integer satisfying \(|A|\le Q^{C_A}\). Let \(c_q\) be complex coefficients supported on \(Q\le q<2Q\) with \(|c_q|\le1\). Let \(\nu_h\) be supported on \(H\le|h|<2H\) and satisfy
\[
 |\nu_h|\le\tau_J(|h|).
\]
Let \(\mathfrak F\) be a fixed family of smooth functions on \((0,\infty)^4\), each supported in \([1,2]^4\), such that for every derivative order all derivatives with respect to the logarithms of the four coordinates are uniformly bounded over \(\mathfrak F\). For \(\Psi\in\mathfrak F\), define
\[
 {\cal V}_{V,P}(\Psi;A)=
 H^{-1}\sum_{Q\le q<2Q}c_q
 \sum_{\substack{H\le|h|<2H\\V\le v<2V\\P\le p<2P\\
                  p\ {\rm prime}\\(vp,q)=1}}
 \nu_h\xi_v\Psi(q/Q,|h|/H,v/V,p/P)
 e_q\!\left(Ah(vp)^{-1}\right). \tag{1}
\]
Then there exists \(\delta=\delta(\kappa,C_A)>0\) such that
\[
 |{\cal V}_{V,P}(\Psi;A)|
 \ll_{\kappa,J,C_A,\mathfrak F}Q^{2-\delta}. \tag{2}
\]
The estimate is uniform in all displayed scales, coefficients, the fixed target \(A\), and \(\Psi\in\mathfrak F\).
af579dffb21039b1.proof:
We verify that the proof mechanism of fact \(2ff1c15aef183bac\) applies under the displayed hypotheses, rather than invoking its statement outside its scope.

In that proof, the original restriction on prime divisors of \(v\) occurs only in the opening comparison
\[
 P\ge R/S_0>Z>L,
\]
whose sole conclusion is that \((v,p)=1\) for every supported outer factor and every prime in the final block. The explicit coprimality hypothesis in the present statement supplies exactly that conclusion directly.

Every subsequent step uses only the following data, all retained here:

- \(V\le H^2Q^{3\sigma}\), which gives
  \[
  0\le\nu=\log_QV\le2\beta-2+3\sigma;
  \]
- the divisor bound on \(\xi_v\);
- the exact identity replacing the prime indicator by \(\Lambda/\log\) minus proper prime powers;
- the exact Vaughan decomposition and box ranges in fact \(29c43cef40f2e79b\);
- the slot-selection inequalities in fact \(461b4af4d8047ab5\);
- the fixed-target correlated estimate in fact \(73fb9efe1286f7e9\);
- the short Type-I estimate in fact \(bbcb9f66597c667c\);
- uniformly summable logarithmic Fourier separation, supplied by the uniform derivative bounds defining \(\mathfrak F\).

None of these steps factors \(v\) or uses an upper bound for its prime divisors. When \(v\) is grouped with a Vaughan factor \(l\), the new coefficient at \(s=vl\) is bounded by a fixed divisor function: if the Vaughan coefficient is bounded by \(\tau_K(l)\log(2P)\), then
\[
 \sum_{vl=s}\tau_J(v)\tau_K(l)\log(2P)
 \le\tau_{J+K+2}(s)\log(2P)
\]
after increasing the fixed order.

The proper-prime-power error is unchanged:
\[
 \ll Q^\epsilon QVP^{1/2}
 =Q^{1+\epsilon}(VR)^{1/2},
\]
and is power-saving solely from \(V\le H^2Q^{3\sigma}\) and \(\beta\le6/5-2\kappa\). The Type-II and medium/large Type-I boxes are placed in the correlated window solely by the exponents \(\nu,\lambda,\beta\); the low Type-I boxes use only their grouped length and total product \(VP=R\). The fixed target, frequency coefficients, and smooth modes satisfy exactly the hypotheses of the cited correlated and Type-I facts.

Thus the proof of fact \(2ff1c15aef183bac\), from its prime-indicator identity onward, is a complete proof under the present self-contained hypotheses. It supplies a fixed positive saving depending only on \(\kappa,C_A\), with uniform constants depending exactly as stated in (2).

glossary.mathfrak F: The fixed uniformly scaled-smooth amplitude family.
glossary.separated-outer condition: The requirement that every supported outer integer v is coprime to every prime in the final prime block.

b007d387ce9d31c1.title: BOUNDED DISTINCT-SEMIPRIME MULTIPLICITY OF THE SOURCE-SIDE CROSSED-FREQUENCY CHART. Let \(Y\ge1\). Let \(\mathscr G_Y\) be a finite set of pairs \(\gamma=(h,u)\) such that
b007d387ce9d31c1.author: slava chan
b007d387ce9d31c1.statement:
BOUNDED DISTINCT-SEMIPRIME MULTIPLICITY OF THE SOURCE-SIDE CROSSED-FREQUENCY CHART. Let \(Y\ge1\). Let \(\mathscr G_Y\) be a finite set of pairs \(\gamma=(h,u)\) such that
\[
 u=p\ell,\qquad p\ne\ell\text{ primes},\qquad p,\ell\ge2Y,\qquad
 0<|h|<Y,\qquad(h,u)=1.                                           \tag{1}
\]
For an ordered crossed pair \((\gamma_1,\gamma_2)\), meaning
\(\gamma_1\ne\gamma_2\), with \(\gamma_i=(h_i,u_i)\), define
\[
 \Delta=h_2u_1-h_1u_2,\qquad U=u_1u_2,\qquad
 \Psi(\gamma_1,\gamma_2)=(\Delta,U).                               \tag{2}
\]
On the sector \(u_1\ne u_2\), every fibre of \(\Psi\) has cardinality at most \(16\):
\[
 \#\{(\gamma_1,\gamma_2)\in\mathscr G_Y^2:
 \gamma_1\ne\gamma_2,\ u_1\ne u_2,\
 \Psi(\gamma_1,\gamma_2)=(\Delta,U)\}\le16.                         \tag{3}
\]
If each physical frequency \(\gamma\) has a provenance fibre
\(\mathscr A_\gamma\) of cardinality at most \(B\), then the corresponding ordered provenance-pair fibre over fixed \((\Delta,U)\), still restricted to crossed pairs with \(u_1\ne u_2\), has cardinality at most
\[
 16B^2.                                                            \tag{4}
\]

The complementary equal-modulus crossed sector has the exact form
\[
 u_1=u_2=u,\qquad U=u^2,\qquad \Delta=u(h_2-h_1),\qquad h_1\ne h_2. \tag{5}
\]
Thus the only possibly long physical fibres of the crossed \((\Delta,U)\) chart are frequency-difference fibres at one common modulus. In the literal forward-\(E_{11}\) data of fact 754cf92eea3a7532, fact fc442085ff47a053 supplies (1) with \(Y=Y_E\), and its provenance bound gives \(B\ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon\). Consequently the distinct-modulus part of the reduced nonresonant frame in fact b62f6ddbc641c393 may be reindexed by \((\Delta,U)\) with only \(x^\varepsilon\) multiplicity; the equal-modulus part must remain a separate frequency-difference convolution. No estimate for either part, OFF-FRAME closure, \(E_{11}\) closure, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
b007d387ce9d31c1.proof:
Fix \(U\). Because each \(u_i\) is a product of two distinct primes, \(U=u_1u_2\) has exactly four prime factors counted with multiplicity, and no prime exponent exceeds two. Hence
\[
 \tau(U)\le\max(2^4,3\cdot2^2,3^2)=16.                              \tag{6}
\]
The choice of the positive divisor \(u_1\mid U\) determines \(u_2=U/u_1\), so there are at most \(16\) possible ordered modulus pairs \((u_1,u_2)\). It remains to show that a fixed ordered pair with \(u_1\ne u_2\) supports at most one ordered frequency pair with a prescribed \(\Delta\).

Put \(g=(u_1,u_2)\), \(u_1=gr_1\), and \(u_2=gr_2\), so \((r_1,r_2)=1\). If \((h_1,h_2)\) and \((h'_1,h'_2)\) both satisfy
\[
 u_1h_2-u_2h_1=\Delta,
\]
then
\[
 r_1(h_2-h'_2)=r_2(h_1-h'_1).
\]
Coprimality gives an integer \(t\) such that
\[
 h_1-h'_1=r_1t,\qquad h_2-h'_2=r_2t.                               \tag{7}
\]
Two distinct semiprimes \(u_1,u_2\) share at most one prime. If they are coprime, then \(r_i=u_i\ge(2Y)^2\). If they share one prime, then each \(r_i\) is the other prime factor and is at least \(2Y\). Thus in every case
\[
 r_1,r_2\ge2Y.                                                      \tag{8}
\]
But \(h_i,h'_i\in(-Y,Y)\), so \(|h_i-h'_i|<2Y\). Equations (7)--(8) force \(t=0\), and hence \(h_i=h'_i\). Therefore each allowed ordered modulus pair contributes at most one physical frequency pair. Combining this with (6) proves (3).

For every physical pair counted in (3), there are at most
\(|\mathscr A_{\gamma_1}||\mathscr A_{\gamma_2}|\le B^2\)
ordered provenance pairs, proving (4). On the crossed domain, if \(u_1=u_2=u\), then \(\gamma_1\ne\gamma_2\) forces \(h_1\ne h_2\), and equations (2) give (5); conversely (5) describes every crossed pair on that sector.

Fact 754cf92eea3a7532 records the literal coordinates and the subpolynomial provenance-fibre bound. Its proof cites fact fc442085ff47a053 for the inequalities \(p,\ell\ge2Y_E\) and \(0<|h|<Y_E\). Hence (1)--(4) apply with \(Y=Y_E\). Fact b62f6ddbc641c393 uses exactly \(\Delta\) and \(U\) from (2), so its distinct-modulus nonresonant terms admit the asserted reindexing. The scope restrictions follow because no analytic estimate has been applied.

glossary.Psi: The map from an ordered crossed physical-frequency pair to (Delta,U).
glossary.mathscr G_Y: The set of reduced short frequencies with semiprime modulus whose prime factors exceed twice the frequency window.

b01d255ce4c5ff24.title: OUTER-GCD EXPONENT MONOTONICITY AND NO 533 CONSUMER FOR 91 ENDPOINT LEAVES
b01d255ce4c5ff24.author: slava chan
b01d255ce4c5ff24.statement:
OUTER-GCD EXPONENT MONOTONICITY AND NO 533 CONSUMER FOR 91 ENDPOINT LEAVES.

Let D,R>1 and g>=1.

In the forward orientation R>=D, put
beta_91=log R/log D.
If g<D, define
Q_RS=D/g>1, B_RS=R/g,
beta_RS=log B_RS/log Q_RS.
Then
beta_RS-beta_91
= [log g (log R-log D)]/[log D (log D-log g)]>=0.            (1)
Equality holds exactly when g=1 or R=D. In particular
beta_91>=4/3 implies beta_RS>=4/3.                            (2)
If instead g>=D, then Q_RS<=1.

In the reverse orientation D>=R, put
beta_91^rev=log D/log R.
If g<R, define
Q_RS^rev=R/g>1, B_RS^rev=D/g,
beta_RS^rev=log B_RS^rev/log Q_RS^rev.
Then
beta_RS^rev-beta_91^rev
= [log g (log D-log R)]/[log R (log R-log g)]>=0,             (3)
and beta_91^rev>=4/3 implies beta_RS^rev>=4/3.                (4)
If instead g>=R, then Q_RS^rev<=1.

Equivalently, when D=x^delta, R=x^rho, g=x^gamma and
0<=gamma<min(delta,rho), one has
beta_RS=(rho-gamma)/(delta-gamma)
in the forward orientation and
beta_RS^rev=(delta-gamma)/(rho-gamma)
in the reverse orientation.                                  (5)

Fix kappa>0. Fact 533acf4056cf5bee applies only above some fixed sufficiently-large base threshold Q_0 and requires
beta_RS<=6/5-2kappa.
Since
6/5-2kappa<4/3,
no forward or reverse boundary-admissible endpoint leaf of fact 91db48815d136d4c is a direct instance after outer-gcd normalization. Precisely, if the normalized base is at least Q_0, (2) or (4) gives the incompatible exponent lower bound. If it lies in (1,Q_0), the sufficiently-large-base premise fails. If it is at most one, that premise also fails. At the single value Q_RS=1 the logarithmic ratio beta_RS is undefined; for Q_RS<1 it may be algebraically defined, but fact 533acf4056cf5bee is still inapplicable because its base is not sufficiently large.

This no-direct-consumer conclusion covers both orientations and every outer-gcd size. It does not rule out a different trace theorem above exponent 4/3, cancellation using the least-tag mask itself, or recombination of endpoint leaves before analysis.
b01d255ce4c5ff24.proof:
In the forward case with g<D, put A=log D, B=log R, and G=log g. Then A>G>=0 and B>=A. Direct subtraction gives
(B-G)/(A-G)-B/A
=G(B-A)/[A(A-G)]>=0,
which is (1). The numerator vanishes exactly when G=0 or B=A. This proves (2). When g>=D, the definition Q_RS=D/g gives Q_RS<=1.

Interchanging D and R proves (3), (4), and the reverse small-base statement. Substitution of the three power parametrizations gives (5).

The numerical gap is
4/3-(6/5-2kappa)=2/15+2kappa>0.
Thus at Q_RS>=Q_0 the endpoint lower bound contradicts the stopping theorem's upper range. Every remaining positive Q_RS is below Q_0 and therefore violates the theorem's sufficiently-large-base premise. This proves the exhaustive case split without any assumption that Q_RS tends to infinity or is unbounded.

glossary.Q_0: a fixed sufficiently-large base threshold for fact 533acf4056cf5bee
glossary.beta_91: the original-label large-divisor exponent used by the 91 endpoint anatomy
glossary.beta_RS: the outer-gcd-normalized exponent seen by a reciprocal-stopping trace
glossary.gamma: the exponent log g/log x of the outer gcd

b02d45f4a07a5524.title: Let q>1 be an integer and let μ be the Möbius function. Let J be a finite set, let z_j∈C and x_j∈Z for j∈J, and, for every divisor e of q, define F_e(v)=∑_{j∈J} z_j exp(2πivx_j/e) for v modulo e. Define C(e)=∑_{v (mod e)}|F_e(v)|^4, S=∑_{j∈J}z_j, and, for every divisor r>1 of q, P(r)=∑_{a (mod r),(a,r)=1}|F_r(a)|^4. Then
b02d45f4a07a5524.author: slava chan
b02d45f4a07a5524.proof:
For an integer u modulo q, Möbius inversion gives 1_{(u,q)=1}=∑_{d|(u,q)}μ(d). Therefore
∑_{u (mod q),(u,q)=1}|F_q(u)|^4
=∑_{d|q}μ(d)∑_{u (mod q),d|u}|F_q(u)|^4.
Write e=q/d and u=dv with v modulo e. For every j,
exp(2πi(dv)x_j/q)=exp(2πivx_j/e),
so F_q(dv)=F_e(v). The inner sum is therefore C(e), proving (1) after replacing d by q/e.

The term v=0 in C(e) is |F_e(0)|^4=|S|^4, independently of e. Thus C(e)=|S|^4+\widetilde C(e), where \widetilde C(e) is the sum over nonzero residues v modulo e. Every nonzero v modulo e has a unique reduced additive conductor r=e/(v,e)>1: writing v=(e/r)a gives (a,r)=1, and for every j,
exp(2πivx_j/e)=exp(2πiax_j/r).
Conversely, each pair consisting of r|e, r>1, and a unit modulo r gives the residue v=(e/r)a modulo e. Hence the nonzero residues partition disjointly by their reduced conductor and
\widetilde C(e)=∑_{r|e,r>1}P(r).

Substitute this identity into the signed divisor sum and interchange the finite sums. The coefficient of P(r) is
∑_{e:r|e|q}μ(q/e)=∑_{s|q/r}μ((q/r)/s).
The last divisor sum equals 1 if r=q and 0 otherwise. Hence ∑_{e|q}μ(q/e)\widetilde C(e)=P(q), proving (2). Since q>1, the same divisor identity with r=1 gives ∑_{e|q}μ(q/e)=0, proving the asserted cancellation of the common zero mode.

Finally, every C(e) is nonnegative and contains the same summand |S|^4. There are τ(q) divisors e of q, so ∑_{e|q}C(e)≥τ(q)|S|^4. If S≠0 this is positive, while the net coefficient of that same zero-mode term in the exact signed decomposition is zero. This proves the stated overlap and repetition. The already proved identities show directly that subtracting |S|^4 from each C(e) and retaining the Möbius coefficients cancels every P(r) with proper r|q and leaves P(q).

glossary.C(e): The complete fourth moment of F_e over residues modulo e.
glossary.F_e(v): For each divisor e of q and residue v modulo e, the additive Fourier sum ∑_j z_j exp(2πivx_j/e). The same definition covers F_e(0), F_q(u), F_q(dv), and F_r(a).
glossary.J: A finite index set for the coefficients.
glossary.P(r): For any divisor r>1 of q, the fourth moment restricted to unit residues modulo r; this includes P(q).
glossary.\\widetilde C(e): The centered complete fourth moment C(e)-|S|^4.
glossary.q: The integer modulus, assumed greater than 1.
glossary.x_j: An integer phase label indexed by j.
glossary.z_j: A complex coefficient indexed by j.
glossary.τ(q): The number of positive divisors of q.

b0662c5a5e8a7772.title: LITERAL SMALL-v ASSEMBLY, EXACT SHIFTED FOURTH-MOMENT LEDGER, AND SHORT-WINDOW TRIANGLE TAX
b0662c5a5e8a7772.author: slava chan
b0662c5a5e8a7772.statement:
LITERAL SMALL-v ASSEMBLY, EXACT SHIFTED FOURTH-MOMENT LEDGER, AND SHORT-WINDOW TRIANGLE TAX. Let p be a prime, let v be a positive integer with gcd(v,p)=1, let A be an integer, and let cal Q be a finite set of positive integers q with gcd(q,vp)=1. Let a_q be arbitrary complex coefficients supported on cal Q. Put e_m(t)=exp(2 pi i t/m), with e_1(t)=1. Bars below denote inverses modulo the modulus of the displayed character. For q_1,q_2 in cal Q and r in Z define F_12(r)=A(q_2-q_1)-r q_1q_2, (1) and for t in Z define the centered punctual kernel K_p(t)=1_{p|t}-1/p. (2) For s modulo v put b_{v,s}(q)=a_q e_v(sA qbar), (3) C_{v,s,p}(r)=sum_{q_1,q_2 in cal Q} b_{v,s}(q_1) conjugate(b_{v,s}(q_2)) K_p(F_12(r)), (4) and, for h modulo p, S_{v,s,p}(h)=sum_{q in cal Q}b_{v,s}(q)e_p(hA qbar). (5) Then the exact literal-mask assembly is sum_{q_1,q_2}a_{q_1}conjugate(a_{q_2}) 1_{v|F_12(r)}K_p(F_12(r)) =1/v sum_{s modulo v}e_v(-sr)C_{v,s,p}(r). (6) Moreover, C_{v,s,p}(r)=1/p sum_{h modulo p, h nonzero} |S_{v,s,p}(h)|^2 e_p(-hr). (7) Let W be any complex function modulo p and define What(k)=sum_{r modulo p}W(r)e_p(-kr). (8) Then sum_{r modulo p}W(r)|C_{v,s,p}(r)|^2 =1/p^2 sum_{h_1,h_2 nonzero} |S_{v,s,p}(h_1)|^2|S_{v,s,p}(h_2)|^2 What(h_1-h_2) (9) =1/p^2 sum_{k modulo p}What(k)T_{v,s,p}(k), (10) where the complete shifted fourth correlation is T_{v,s,p}(k)=sum_{h modulo p; h nonzero, h-k nonzero} |S_{v,s,p}(h)|^2|S_{v,s,p}(h-k)|^2. (11) Thus (10) retains the zero shift T_{v,s,p}(0)=sum_{h nonzero}|S_{v,s,p}(h)|^4 (12) and every nonzero shift k in one signed Fourier assembly. There is an equivalent physical incidence/cross/center form. Define rho_p(q_1,q_2)=A(q_2-q_1)(q_1q_2)^(-1) modulo p. (13) For x,y modulo p put Gamma_W(x,y)=sum_{r modulo p}W(r) [1_{r=x}-1/p][1_{r=y}-1/p]. (14) Then exactly Gamma_W(x,y)=1_{x=y}W(x)-[W(x)+W(y)]/p +(sum_r W(r))/p^2, (15) and the left side of (9) is sum_{q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4} b(q_1)conjugate(b(q_2))conjugate(b(q_3))b(q_4) Gamma_W(rho_p(q_1,q_2),rho_p(q_3,q_4)), (16) where b=b_{v,s}. For W=1 on all residues, Gamma_1(x,y)=1_{x=y}-1/p. (17) Hence the complete-window two-row kernel is the centered punctual kernel in the slope difference. Equations (15)-(16) keep the incidence-incidence, both cross terms, and center term assembled; none may be discarded in passing to (9)-(10). Now let W be the indicator of a nonempty residue interval I of cardinality L, where 1<=L<=p. Then What(0)=L, sum_{k modulo p}|What(k)|^2=pL, max_k|What(k)|<=L, (18) and consequently p<=sum_k|What(k)|<=3p(1+log p). (19) In particular, suppose an input estimates the correlations (11) only separately, by |T_{v,s,p}(k)|<=B for every k. Applying it shift by shift and taking absolute values in (10) yields the coefficient ledger B/p^2 sum_k|What(k)|, (20) which is at least B/p, whereas the zero-shift coefficient is BL/p^2. Thus for L

=1, V>=2, and let xi_v be supported on V<=v<2V with |xi_v|<=tau_J(v), where tau_J is the J-fold divisor function from fact d061fc4dc153e309. The complete literal mask family satisfies, for every epsilon>0, sum_{V<=v<2V}sum_{s modulo v}|xi_v/v|^2 =sum_{V<=v<2V}|xi_v|^2/v <<_{J,epsilon}V^epsilon. (21) Thus (v,s) is one subpolynomial l2 coefficient slot in (6), not an atomwise l1 sum. At the scales of fact 0220ab16ae677eec, its actual-mask exceptional ledger is paid directly before (6): r=0, 0<|r|<=Q^(1-delta)/H, gcd(q_1,q_2)>=HQ^delta, F_12(r)=0 with r nonzero, and the pre-Poisson q-diagonal together contribute O(Q^(4-eta)) for some eta>0. Therefore this exact l2 assembly may be restricted to the remaining literal sector without applying a (v,s) triangle to the exceptional zones. No bound for the remaining weighted sum (10) is asserted.
b0662c5a5e8a7772.proof:
Because q_1q_2 is a unit modulo v, the congruence v|F_12(r) is equivalent to
  r congruent A(q_1bar-q_2bar) modulo v.
Additive orthogonality therefore gives
  1_{v|F_12(r)}
   =1/v sum_{s modulo v}
      e_v(sAq_1bar)e_v(-sAq_2bar)e_v(-sr).                 (22)
Multiply (22) by a_{q_1}conjugate(a_{q_2})K_p(F_12(r)), sum over q_1,q_2, and use (3)-(4). This proves (6). It is the normalized-q form of the outer-gcd-invariant separation in fact d061fc4dc153e309.

Modulo p, since q_1q_2 is a unit,
  K_p(F_12(r))
   =1_{r=rho_p(q_1,q_2)}-1/p.                              (23)
Also rho_p(q_1,q_2)=A(q_1bar-q_2bar). Applying the exact centered Fourier identity of fact 985515aa5d2117fe to the coefficients b_{v,s}(q) proves (7).

Multiply (7) by its complex conjugate, multiply by W(r), and sum over r modulo p. Definition (8) gives (9). In (9) put k=h_1-h_2 and h=h_1, so h_2=h-k. The restrictions h_1,h_2 nonzero become h nonzero and h-k nonzero. This proves (10)-(12).

For the physical form, expand (14). The product of the two point indicators is nonzero exactly when x=y=r, and its W-weighted sum is 1_{x=y}W(x). The first cross term is -W(x)/p, the second is -W(y)/p, and the constant term is p^(-2)sum_rW(r). This proves (15). Expanding |C_{v,s,p}(r)|^2 using (23) gives (16). If W=1, equation (15) becomes 1_{x=y}-2/p+p/p^2=1_{x=y}-1/p, proving (17).

For an interval indicator, What(0)=L and |What(k)|<=L follow directly. Finite Fourier Parseval with the convention (8) gives
  sum_k|What(k)|^2=p sum_r|W(r)|^2=pL.                     (24)
Since |What(k)|^2<=L|What(k)|, summing gives the lower bound in (19). For the upper bound, represent I as L consecutive residues. For 0<|k|<=p/2,
  |What(k)|=|sin(pi Lk/p)/sin(pi k/p)|
            <=min(L,p/(2|k|)),                             (25)
using |sin(pi k/p)|>=2|k|/p on this range. Summing (25) over positive and negative representatives, and including k=0, gives at most 3p(1+log p). This proves (18)-(19). Equation (20) is exactly the triangle inequality applied to (10); comparison with the k=0 coefficient What(0)/p^2=L/p^2 proves the factor p/L and the scoped no-direct-fit assertion.

Equation (21) is the coefficient identity and divisor-bound conclusion already proved in fact d061fc4dc153e309. The exceptional-zone conclusion is exactly fact 0220ab16ae677eec, whose ledger is defined on the literal coupled mask before any Fourier separation. Removing those tuples first and then applying the identity (6) to the complement introduces no triangle cost and proves the reconciliation statement. Every assertion follows.

glossary.Gamma_W: The weighted correlation of two centered punctual kernels with residue weight W.
glossary.centered punctual kernel: The function K_p(t)=1_{p divides t}-1/p on residues modulo a prime p.
glossary.shifted fourth correlation: The inner sum T(k) obtained by fixing the additive-frequency difference k=h_1-h_2 in the centered reciprocal fourth moment.
glossary.short-window triangle tax: The factor p/L lost when the Fourier shifts of a residue interval of length L are bounded separately and then summed absolutely.

b0a38f5e9ae7feb6.title: TOP-MU2-UNMARKED-FULL-SOURCE-NORMAL-FORM: EXACT FORWARD AND REVERSE RECOMBINE-FIRST IDENTITIES
b0a38f5e9ae7feb6.author: slava chan
b0a38f5e9ae7feb6.statement:
TOP-MU2-UNMARKED-FULL-SOURCE-NORMAL-FORM: EXACT FORWARD AND REVERSE RECOMBINE-FIRST IDENTITIES.

Work on the strict top sliver
\[
 \beta_m<\beta<6/5
\]
of facts \(e58fc7c00f1683e6\) and \(3f2f255ea6845a50\).
Fix one selected \(N\), one active dyadic label, exact outer gcd \(g\),
original pre-marker source atom, fixed-\(U\), high, parent, actual-\(G\),
smooth/projective and provenance data, and one orientation. Put
\[
 L_{\rm src}=N/g.
\]
In the forward orientation set
\[
 (s,n,t,u)=(a,b,m,k),\qquad
 Q=D/g,\quad B=R/g,\quad H_P=B/M,\quad \epsilon=+1,
\]
and in the reverse orientation set
\[
 (s,n,t,u)=(b,a,k,m),\qquad
 Q=R/g,\quad B=D/g,\quad H_P=B/K,\quad \epsilon=-1.
\]
Then in both orientations
\[
 st+nu=L_{\rm src},\qquad s\asymp Q,\qquad n\asymp B,         \tag{1}
\]
and nonzero source support implies
\[
 (g,sn)=(s,n)=1,\qquad
 \mu(gs)\mu(gn)=\mu(s)\mu(n).                               \tag{2}
\]

At this fixed pre-marker atom, first sum all six exact marker anatomies
\[
 A,\ B,\ C1,\ C2,\ C3,\ C4
\]
and every marker-dependent target-gcd, order/equal-cell, collision,
deletion and provenance sibling. Pointwise, their complete sum restores
the literal factor \(\mu(n)\). No such descendant survives as a selector
in the following formula.

Let \(\Theta^\epsilon_\lambda(s,n,h)\) denote, explicitly and extended by
zero, the product of any selectors already belonging to the fixed
pre-marker source atom: selected-source, active-scale, fixed-\(U\), high,
parent, actual-\(G\), paired-frequency and inherited provenance selectors.
It contains no marker anatomy or marker-dependent target-gcd, order,
collision, deletion or provenance mask. It is not absorbed into a smooth
amplitude.

Define the literal smooth one-variable source amplitudes
\[
\begin{aligned}
 F^+_{g,s,n}(t)
 &=\log t\log\!\left({L_{\rm src}-st\over n}\right)
 W\!\left({gs\over D},{t\over M},{gn\over R},
          {L_{\rm src}-st\over nK}\right),                  \tag{3F}\\
 F^-_{g,s,n}(t)
 &=\log t\log\!\left({L_{\rm src}-st\over n}\right)
 W\!\left({gn\over D},{L_{\rm src}-st\over nM},
          {gs\over R},{t\over K}\right),                    \tag{3R}
\end{aligned}
\]
extended smoothly by zero, and use the Fourier convention
\[
 \widehat F(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R}F(t)e(-\xi t)\,dt.
\]
The complete recombined nonzero-Poisson row of this fixed pre-marker atom
is exactly
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
 \mathcal U^\epsilon_\lambda
 ={1\over H_P}
 \sum_{\substack{s\asymp Q,\ n\asymp B\\
                  (g,sn)=(s,n)=1}}
 &\mu(s)\mu(n)\sum_{h\ne0}
 \Theta^\epsilon_\lambda(s,n,h)
 {H_P\over n}\widehat F^\epsilon_{g,s,n}(\epsilon h/n)\\
 &\times e\!\left({\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\over sn}\right)
 e_s\!\left(-\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\,\overline n\right).
\end{aligned}}                                               \tag{4}
\]
Thus the reciprocal modulus remains the original \(s\asymp Q\); the
fixed target is \(-\epsilon L_{\rm src}\), which may be nonunit modulo
\(s\); and no target-gcd descent or rescaling of \(Q\) has occurred. The
factor
\[
 {H_P\over n}\widehat F^\epsilon_{g,s,n}(\epsilon h/n)
 e(\epsilon L_{\rm src}h/(sn))                              \tag{5}
\]
is the literal Fourier/Archimedean coefficient, not a container for any
sharp selector listed separately in \(\Theta^\epsilon_\lambda\).

Let \(\mathcal T_{\rm top,unmarked}\) be the sum of (4) over the complete
fixed pre-marker source ledger before selecting a new anatomy, and let
\(\mathcal R_{A,\rm top}\) be the complete strict-top \(A\)-projection of
fact \(3f2f255ea6845a50\), with all its source siblings recombined before
taking an absolute value. Then exactly
\[
 \mathcal T_{\rm postA,top}
 =\mathcal T_{\rm top,unmarked}-\mathcal R_{A,\rm top},       \tag{6}
\]
and hence
\[
 |\mathcal T_{\rm postA,top}|
 \le |\mathcal T_{\rm top,unmarked}|
    +|\mathcal R_{A,\rm top}|.                               \tag{7}
\]
Accordingly the legal recombine-first route estimates the complete
unmarked source (4) before subtracting the already paid \(A\)-projection;
it does not estimate the five non-\(A\) anatomy masks separately.

This is an exact coefficient and ledger identity. It supplies no estimate
for \(\mathcal T_{\rm top,unmarked}\), no assertion that an arbitrary
surviving \(\Theta^\epsilon_\lambda\) is projectively separable, no
one-sided Vaughan bound, no critical-tail payment and no Goldbach
conclusion.
b0a38f5e9ae7feb6.proof:
Write \(d=ga,r=gb\) in the original physical equation
\[
 dm+rk=N.
\]
In the forward orientation, substituting
\((s,n,t,u)=(a,b,m,k)\) gives \(st+nu=L_{\rm src}\). In the reverse
orientation, substituting \((s,n,t,u)=(b,a,k,m)\) gives the same equation.
The scale definitions in fact \(e58fc7c00f1683e6\) give
\(s\asymp Q,n\asymp B\). On nonzero Möbius support, that fact gives
pairwise coprimality of \(g,s,n\). Therefore
\[
 \mu(gs)\mu(gn)
 =\mu(g)^2\mu(s)\mu(n)
 =\mu(s)\mu(n),
\]
which proves (1)--(2).

Fact \(e58fc7c00f1683e6\) proves pointwise, at each fixed pre-marker
source atom, that the complete inherited marker and all its
marker-dependent descendants sum back to \(\mu(n)\). It then applies the
exact exhaustive six-anatomy identity and proves that every canonical
target-gcd, order/equal-cell, collision, deletion and provenance
refinement introduced after an anatomy is formed is a finite sibling
partition whose recombination returns that anatomy coefficient. Summing
all six anatomies and all those siblings therefore restores \(\mu(n)\)
pointwise. The fixed pre-marker selectors are unchanged by this operation;
placing them explicitly in \(\Theta^\epsilon_\lambda\) neither deletes
nor smooths them.

For the forward row, solve (1) for
\[
 u=(L_{\rm src}-st)/n.
\]
The two logarithmic weights and the original smooth source weight become
exactly (3F). Poisson summation in the progression
\[
 st\equiv L_{\rm src}\pmod n
\]
gives, for the nonzero frequencies,
\[
 {1\over n}\sum_{h\ne0}
 \widehat F^+_{g,s,n}(h/n)
 e_n(L_{\rm src}h\,\overline s).                             \tag{8}
\]
The elementary additive reciprocity identity
\[
 e_n(X\overline s)
 =e_s(-X\overline n)e(X/(sn)),\qquad (s,n)=1,                \tag{9}
\]
with \(X=L_{\rm src}h\), turns (8) into the \(\epsilon=+1\)
summand in (4). Multiplying and dividing by \(H_P\) produces exactly the
external normalization and dimensionless Fourier factor in (4), with no
factor \(s^{-1}\).

For the reverse row, use \(t=k,u=m\). The same substitution gives (3R).
Reindex the complete nonzero frequency family by \(h\mapsto-h\), including
every inherited \(h\)-dependent pre-marker selector. Formula (8) then has
\(\widehat F^-_{g,s,n}(-h/n)\) and
\(e_n(-L_{\rm src}h\overline s)\). Applying (9) with
\(X=-L_{\rm src}h\) gives
\[
 e(-L_{\rm src}h/(sn))e_s(+L_{\rm src}h\overline n),
\]
which is precisely the \(\epsilon=-1\) summand in (4).
The same forward/reverse sign convention and the same absence of an
\(s^{-1}\) prefactor are independently recorded in the exact descended
coefficient fact \(9bee61f3627bd506\). This proves (3F)--(5).

No discrete selector has been inserted into \(F^\epsilon\). This
separation is necessary: fact \(8d9feea8c44da2c8\) proves that a discrete
source mask specified only on integer solutions has no canonical
same-mask zero mode, since different smooth extensions can agree on every
supported integer solution and have different integrals. Our formula
avoids that ambiguity by using only the original literal smooth source
weight in (3F)--(3R) and keeping every surviving pre-marker selector
visible in \(\Theta^\epsilon_\lambda\).

Finally, the pointwise six-anatomy identity gives
\[
 \mathcal T_{\rm top,unmarked}
 =\mathcal R_{A,\rm top}+\mathcal R_{B,\rm top}
  +\mathcal R_{C1,\rm top}+\mathcal R_{C2,\rm top}
  +\mathcal R_{C3,\rm top}+\mathcal R_{C4,\rm top}.
\]
Fact \(3f2f255ea6845a50\) defines the post-\(A\) source by subtracting the
complete \(A\)-projection only after its source coordinates have been
recombined. Restricting that identity to the strict top sliver proves
(6). The triangle inequality proves (7), without assigning a sign to
any proper anatomy.

glossary.TOP-MU2-UNMARKED-FULL-SOURCE-NORMAL-FORM: The exact forward/reverse full-modulus reciprocal form with literal coefficient mu(s)mu(n) after complete marker recombination.
glossary.\\Theta^\\epsilon_\\lambda: The explicit zero-extended product of all surviving pre-marker selectors; it contains no recombined marker-dependent selector.
glossary.\\mathcal U^\\epsilon_\\lambda: The complete unmarked nonzero-Poisson row for one fixed pre-marker source atom and orientation.

b0eae7ccb6da25c7.title: Let C_2=∏_{p>2}p(p-2)/(p-1)^2. Let x tend to infinity through values for which N=2x is an even integer that is not the sum of two primes. Define
b0eae7ccb6da25c7.author: slava chan
b0eae7ccb6da25c7.statement:
Let C_2=∏_{p>2}p(p-2)/(p-1)^2. Let x tend to infinity through values for which N=2x is an even integer that is not the sum of two primes. Define
𝔠(N)=C_2∏_{p|N,p>2}(p-1)/(p-2), Q_N=rad(2N),
r_N(n)=1_{gcd(n,Q_N)=1}∏_{p|n,p∤Q_N}(p-1)/(p-2), and b_N(n)=2𝔠(N)r_N(n).
Fix real numbers 1/2<a<b<1, a nonzero nonnegative continuously differentiable real function W supported in [a,b], a real number D_* with 1≤D_*≤x, and a real function ψ on the positive reals satisfying ψ(u)=0 for 0<u≤1. Define
H_{N,W,ψ}=Σ_{d,m≥1;d≥2}μ(d)log(m)W(dm/x)ψ(d/D_*)Λ(N-dm),
E_{sh,N}=Σ_{d,m≥1;d≥2}μ(d)log(m)W(dm/x)(1-ψ(d/D_*))(Λ(N-dm)-b_N(dm)),
and
E_{b,N}=Σ_{d,m≥1;d≥2}μ(d)log(m)W(dm/x)ψ(d/D_*)b_N(dm).
If |E_{sh,N}|+|E_{b,N}|=o_W(𝔠(N)x) uniformly along this family of bad N, then, with c_W=2∫_0^∞W(u)du>0,
H_{N,W,ψ}=-c_W𝔠(N)x+o_W(𝔠(N)x).
Now additionally fix a real function Φ supported in [1/2,2] such that Σ_{j∈Z}Φ(t/2^j)=1 for every t>0, and for positive dyadic D,M,R,K define
Q_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;R,K)=Σ_{d,m,r,k≥1;dm+rk=N}μ(d)μ(r)log(m)log(k)W(dm/x)ψ(d/D_*)Φ(d/D)Φ(m/M)Φ(r/R)Φ(k/K).
Then every sufficiently large bad N in the family has a positive dyadic quadruple (D,M,R,K) for which
Q_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;R,K)≤-c_W𝔠(N)x/[2(ceil(log_2 x)+4)^4].
The conclusion is pointwise in the same fixed N and uses no averaging over N.
b0eae7ccb6da25c7.proof:
Fact 0e9a1691fd933c33, applied to the comparison weight b_N reproduced in the statement, gives
M_{N,W}=Σ_n W(n/x)b_N(n)Λ(n)=c_W𝔠(N)x+o_W(𝔠(N)x).                         (1)
Fact f41f5f91b52e0d13 gives
E_{0,N}=Σ_n W(n/x)log(n)(Λ(N-n)-b_N(n))=o_W(𝔠(N)x).                      (2)
Fact 2679e2cb5e61a245 gives the exact identity
R_{N,W}=M_{N,W}+H_{N,W,ψ}+E_{0,N}+E_{sh,N}-E_{b,N},                     (3)
and, because N is not a sum of two primes,
0≤R_{N,W}≤2||W||_∞(log N)^2P_N,
where P_N=Σ_{e=2}^{floor(log_2(N-1))}floor((N-1)^(1/e)).
The elementary bound
P_N≤N^(1/2)+(log_2 N)N^(1/3)
shows that R_{N,W}=o_W(x). Fact f41f5f91b52e0d13 also proves 𝔠(N)≥C_2>0, so R_{N,W}=o_W(𝔠(N)x). Rearranging (3), then using (1), (2), and the assumed estimates for E_{sh,N} and E_{b,N}, proves
H_{N,W,ψ}=-c_W𝔠(N)x+o_W(𝔠(N)x).                                      (4)
The integral defining c_W is positive because W is nonnegative, nonzero, continuous, and supported on a compact interval.

Because ψ(u)=0 for u≤1 and D_*≥1, the d=1 term in the definition of H used in fact cdb5cefbc7333591 vanishes, so its H is identical to the H in this statement. That fact supplies the exact dyadic decomposition into the blocks Q_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;R,K). From (4), for all sufficiently large N in the family one may write H_{N,W,ψ}=-A_N+E_N with A_N=c_W𝔠(N)x and |E_N|≤A_N/2. Fact 6f82723a1b084485 then gives a dyadic quadruple satisfying
Q_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;R,K)≤-A_N/[2(ceil(log_2 x)+4)^4],
which is the claimed inequality. Every cited fact and every step fixes N, so no averaging over N occurs.

glossary.H_{N,W,ψ}: the deep smooth reflected Möbius source
glossary.Q_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;R,K): the four-parameter dyadic block defined in the statement
glossary.W: a nonzero nonnegative continuously differentiable weight supported in [a,b]
glossary.c_W: the positive constant 2 times the integral of W
glossary.r_N(n): the local-density weight defined in the statement
glossary.𝔠(N): the Goldbach singular factor defined in the statement

b1398db2962d7491.title: Fix a nonzero integer Delta and fixed smooth functions F and G compactly supported in (1/2,1). Let H>=2, put X=H^3, let M_1,M_2,N_1,N_2 lie between X and 2X, and put f(x)=F(x/M_1), g(x)=G(x/M_2). Let I be a finite index set. For each j in I, let alpha_j and beta_j be arbitrary complex sequences supported respectively on [N_1/2,N_1] and [N_2/2,N_2]. Define
b1398db2962d7491.author: slava chan
b1398db2962d7491.statement:
Fix a nonzero integer Delta and fixed smooth functions F and G compactly supported in (1/2,1). Let H>=2, put X=H^3, let M_1,M_2,N_1,N_2 lie between X and 2X, and put f(x)=F(x/M_1), g(x)=G(x/M_2). Let I be a finite index set. For each j in I, let alpha_j and beta_j be arbitrary complex sequences supported respectively on [N_1/2,N_1] and [N_2/2,N_2]. Define
T_j=sum_{m_1n_2-m_2n_1=Delta} f(m_1)g(m_2)alpha_j(n_1)beta_j(n_2),
where all four variables are positive integers. Let Z_j be the explicit Bettin--Chandee main term
sum_{n_1,n_2; gcd(n_1,n_2) divides Delta}
 [gcd(n_1,n_2)/(n_1n_2)] alpha_j(n_1)beta_j(n_2)
 integral_R f((x+Delta)/n_2)g(x/n_1) dx,
with n_1,n_2 restricted to the sequence supports. Put
T_tot=sum_j T_j, Z_tot=sum_j Z_j,
P_BC=sum_j ||alpha_j||_2||beta_j||_2, and Pi_BC=P_BC/X.                 (1)
Then, for every epsilon>0,
|T_tot-Z_tot| <<_{Delta,F,G,epsilon}
 X^(19/20+epsilon)P_BC
 =H^(117/20+epsilon)Pi_BC.                                             (2)

Consequently, for any fixed delta>0, the two separate estimates
Pi_BC << H^(3/20-delta),       |Z_tot| << H^(6-delta)                  (3)
imply
|T_tot| <<_{Delta,F,G,epsilon} H^(6-delta+epsilon).                    (4)
The first clause of (3) controls only the centered discrepancy; the second is an independent zero/main-term obligation.

This independence is sharp in scope. The positive saturating example in fact 630165d40f5dd2de consists of one atom with Pi_BC comparable to one and Z_tot bounded below by a positive constant times H^6. Hence, for every fixed delta in (0,3/20), the projective-cost clause of (3) alone is compatible with a full H^6 main term.

There is also a precise scoped recovered-prime norm floor. Under the hypotheses of fact de1c0ccbef73029b, let W be its incidence matrix and let L be its number of nonzero entries. With X=H^3, define
Pi_line=X^(-1) inf_{W=sum_j beta_j tensor alpha_j}
                 sum_j||beta_j||_2||alpha_j||_2.                       (5)
Then Pi_line=L/X>=c_0H^(-2). This is an exact normalized nonseparability cost for that one joint selector. It does not contradict the admissible budget Pi_BC<<H^(3/20-delta) when 0<delta<3/20 and therefore is not, by itself, a global obstruction to (4). For a signed union of recovered-prime slices or for additional gcd, carry, digit, mask, and source selectors, the relevant quantity is the projective norm of the actual assembled coefficient, not an unproved sum of the raw costs of its pieces.

On the literal determinant sign sector a>0,c>0,d<0,b>0, the substitution
(m_1,m_2,n_1,n_2)=(a,c,-d,b)
identifies the equation in T_tot with ab+cd=Delta, as in fact 630165d40f5dd2de. No assertion is made here for another sign sector without its own legal substitution and cutoffs.
b1398db2962d7491.proof:
Bettin--Chandee, arXiv:1502.00769, Corollary 1, in the notation reproduced in fact 630165d40f5dd2de, gives for each j
|T_j-Z_j|
 << (eta R)^(3/2)||alpha_j||_2||beta_j||_2
    (N_1N_2)^(7/20)(N_1+N_2)^(1/4+epsilon)(M_1M_2)^epsilon,
where eta depends only on the scaled smooth profiles and
R=M_1N_2/(M_2N_1)+M_2N_1/(M_1N_2).
Because all four length parameters lie in [X,2X], eta and R are bounded in terms of F and G, and the length factor, after renaming epsilon, is
X^(7/10+1/4+epsilon)=X^(19/20+epsilon).
Summing the resulting inequalities over j proves the first expression in (2). By (1), P_BC=X Pi_BC. Since X=H^3, the result is
X^(39/20+epsilon)Pi_BC=H^(117/20+epsilon)Pi_BC,
which is the second expression in (2).

Under (3), the centered error in (2) is at most
H^(117/20+epsilon) H^(3/20-delta)=H^(6-delta+epsilon).
Adding the separate bound for Z_tot proves (4).

For the asserted independence, use the saturating construction in fact 630165d40f5dd2de. Its alpha and beta are interval indicators on intervals containing a fixed positive proportion of X integers. Therefore each ell^2 norm is comparable to X^(1/2), so their product P_BC is comparable to X and Pi_BC is comparable to one. The same fact proves Z_tot>=cH^6. If 0<delta<3/20, then a constant Pi_BC satisfies Pi_BC<<H^(3/20-delta), while the claimed power-saving main-term estimate fails. Thus the projective clause cannot replace explicit centering or main-term control.

Fact de1c0ccbef73029b proves that the infimum in (5) is exactly L and that L>=c_0H. Dividing by X=H^3 gives Pi_line=L/X>=c_0H^(-2). For 0<delta<3/20 one has H^(-2)<=H^(3/20-delta), so this lower bound alone is compatible with the discrepancy budget in (3). A projective norm is defined after the final coefficient has been assembled; the triangle inequality gives an upper bound by summing a chosen decomposition, but no lower bound for a signed union follows merely by adding lower bounds for its individual slices. This proves the stated limitation. The final determinant identification is the direct sign-sector substitution already proved in fact 630165d40f5dd2de.

glossary.P_BC: the raw separated ell^2 projective coefficient cost sum_j ||alpha_j||_2||beta_j||_2
glossary.Pi_BC: the normalized Bettin--Chandee projective cost P_BC/X
glossary.T_tot: the sum of a finite family of separated determinant-count atoms
glossary.Z_tot: the sum of their explicit Bettin--Chandee main terms

b1523acd495fc99b.title: Let p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4 be distinct primes greater than 3 and put P=p_1p_2p_3p_4. Use the centered weighted-companion definitions rho_i, M_q, V_{P,q}, C_q, E_q, Gamma, and T from fact be4e5ad5378f0122. There are explicit centered complex local weights for the two distinct external units q=2 and q=3 for which both actual weighted companion columns are supported on the same single primitive frequency. For these weights,
b1523acd495fc99b.author: slava chan
b1523acd495fc99b.statement:
Let p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4 be distinct primes greater than 3 and put P=p_1p_2p_3p_4. Use the centered weighted-companion definitions rho_i, M_q, V_{P,q}, C_q, E_q, Gamma, and T from fact be4e5ad5378f0122. There are explicit centered complex local weights for the two distinct external units q=2 and q=3 for which both actual weighted companion columns are supported on the same single primitive frequency. For these weights,
||Gamma-I||_op=1
and
||T||^2=2.
Consequently, in the class of arbitrary complex centered q-dependent local weights, centering at all four primes, primitive-frequency support, the CRT product structure, and the exact companion phase do not imply any delta-flat estimate with delta<1. Any such estimate for the literal arithmetic companion must use additional restrictions on the local weights, such as their actual interval or Fejer form and their arithmetic dependence on q. This is a formal weighted-companion countermodel, not a counterexample for the literal interval-weight family and not an arithmetic PAVG27 counterexample.
b1523acd495fc99b.proof:
For each i define
a_i=(P/p_i)^{-1} modulo p_i.
For both q=2 and q=3 set
w_{i,q}(x)=p_i^{-1}e_{p_i}(a_i x), x modulo p_i.
Because a_i is nonzero modulo p_i, this function has mean zero, so its centered version f_{i,q} equals w_{i,q}. Its Fourier transform in the convention of fact be4e5ad5378f0122 is
fhat_{i,q}(a)
=p_i^{-1}sum_{x modulo p_i}e_{p_i}((a_i-a)x)
=1_{a=a_i modulo p_i}.
Since rho_i(h)=h(P/p_i)^{-1}=h a_i modulo p_i, all four factors fhat_{i,q}(rho_i(h)) equal one exactly when h=1 modulo p_i for every i. By CRT this occurs exactly when h=1 modulo P. Hence, for q=2 and q=3,
M_q(h)=1_{h=1 modulo P}.                                                     (1)

It remains to check that the two surviving companion values are nonzero. For q=2, V_{P,2}(1) is a single root of unity and is nonzero. For q=3,
V_{P,3}(1)=e_P(-3^{-1})+e_P(-2 times 3^{-1})
=e_P(-3^{-1})(1+e_P(-3^{-1})).
If this vanished, e_P(-3^{-1}) would have order two. This is impossible because it is a P-th root of unity and P is odd. Thus V_{P,3}(1) is also nonzero.

By (1), each C_q=M_qV_{P,q} is a nonzero scalar multiple of the same coordinate vector 1_{h=1}. After division by sqrt(E_q)=|V_{P,q}(1)|, the two columns of T are unit vectors on the same one-dimensional line. Therefore their normalized Gram has the form
Gamma=[[1,z],[overline(z),1]]
for a complex number z of modulus one. Its eigenvalues are 0 and 2. Hence Gamma-I has eigenvalues -1 and 1, so ||Gamma-I||_op=1, while ||T||^2=||Gamma||_op=2.

The constructed local weights are complex additive characters rather than interval indicators or Fejer weights. Therefore the countermodel excludes an inference from the broad centered/CRT axioms alone but does not decide the literal interval-weight problem.

glossary.a_i: the inverse of P/p_i modulo p_i, used to select the global CRT frequency h=1
glossary.formal weighted-companion countermodel: an example inside the arbitrary complex centered-weight class of fact be4e5ad5378f0122, without the literal interval or Fejer restriction

b164cd7d1e02e173.title: Let \(N\) be a positive even integer. Let \(d_1\ne d_2\) be positive odd squarefree integers satisfying
b164cd7d1e02e173.author: slava chan
b164cd7d1e02e173.statement:
Let \(N\) be a positive even integer. Let \(d_1\ne d_2\) be positive odd squarefree integers satisfying
\[
 \gcd(d_1d_2,N)=1.
\]
For a prime \(\ell\), let \(\nu_\ell(N;d_1,d_2)\) be the number of residue classes \(m\pmod\ell\) for which
\[
 (N-d_1m)(N-d_2m)\equiv0\pmod\ell.
\]
Define the two-linear-form singular series
\[
 {\mathfrak S}_N(d_1,d_2)
 =\prod_{\ell\ {\rm prime}}
 \left(1-{\nu_\ell(N;d_1,d_2)\over\ell}\right)
 \left(1-{1\over\ell}\right)^{-2}.                                    \tag{1}
\]
Then
\[
 \nu_\ell(N;d_1,d_2)=
 \begin{cases}
 0,&\ell\mid\gcd(d_1,d_2),\\
 1,&\ell\mid d_1d_2\text{ but }\ell\nmid\gcd(d_1,d_2),\\
 1,&\ell\nmid d_1d_2\text{ and }\ell\mid N(d_1-d_2),\\
 2,&\ell\nmid d_1d_2N(d_1-d_2).
 \end{cases}                                                          \tag{2}
\]
The cases are disjoint and exhaustive. In particular \(\nu_2=1\), every local factor is positive, and the product in (1) converges.

Put
\[
 C_2=\prod_{\ell>2}{\ell(\ell-2)\over(\ell-1)^2},\qquad
 g=\gcd(d_1,d_2),\qquad h={d_1d_2\over g^2}.
\]
Then the singular series has the exact formula
\[
 \boxed{
 {\mathfrak S}_N(d_1,d_2)
 =2C_2
 \prod_{\substack{\ell\mid g\\\ell>2}}{\ell\over\ell-2}
 \prod_{\substack{\ell\mid h\\\ell>2}}{\ell-1\over\ell-2}
 \prod_{\substack{\ell\mid N(d_1-d_2)\\
                   \ell\nmid d_1d_2\\\ell>2}}
                   {\ell-1\over\ell-2}.}                               \tag{3}
\]
Thus a conjectural or proved main term for the off-diagonal covariance in fact 9e1ff55fe17bc513 contains three distinct arithmetic layers: common prime factors of \(d_1,d_2\), prime factors belonging to exactly one modulus, and the genuinely coupled determinant factor \(N(d_1-d_2)\). Formula (3) is only the local-density calculation; it asserts no prime-pair asymptotic and no estimate for the covariance.
b164cd7d1e02e173.proof:
Fix a prime \(\ell\). We count roots of the two affine forms
\[
 L_1(m)=N-d_1m,\qquad L_2(m)=N-d_2m
\]
modulo \(\ell\).

Suppose first that \(\ell\mid d_1\) and \(\ell\mid d_2\). The hypothesis \(\gcd(d_1d_2,N)=1\) gives \(\ell\nmid N\). Hence both \(L_1(m)\) and \(L_2(m)\) are congruent to the nonzero residue \(N\) for every \(m\), so \(\nu_\ell=0\).

Suppose that \(\ell\) divides exactly one of \(d_1,d_2\), say \(\ell\mid d_1\) and \(\ell\nmid d_2\). Again \(\ell\nmid N\). The first form is never zero, while the second has the unique root
\[
 m\equiv Nd_2^{-1}\pmod\ell.
\]
Thus \(\nu_\ell=1\). The other orientation is identical.

Now suppose that \(\ell\nmid d_1d_2\). Each form has one root:
\[
 m\equiv Nd_1^{-1}\pmod\ell,\qquad
 m\equiv Nd_2^{-1}\pmod\ell.
\]
These roots coincide precisely when
\[
 N(d_2-d_1)\equiv0\pmod\ell.
\]
Indeed, multiplying their equality by the unit \(d_1d_2\) gives this congruence, and the implication reverses. Hence \(\nu_\ell=1\) if \(\ell\mid N(d_1-d_2)\), and \(\nu_\ell=2\) otherwise. This proves (2).

Because \(N\) is even and \(d_1,d_2\) are odd, the last analysis at \(\ell=2\) gives one common root, namely \(m\equiv0\pmod2\). Thus \(\nu_2=1\), and its local factor in (1) is
\[
 (1-1/2)(1-1/2)^{-2}=2.                                                \tag{4}
\]
For every odd prime, \(\nu_\ell\le2<\ell\), so its local factor is positive. Outside the finite set of primes dividing \(d_1d_2N(d_1-d_2)\), one has \(\nu_\ell=2\), and the local factor is
\[
 \left(1-{2\over\ell}\right)\left(1-{1\over\ell}\right)^{-2}
 ={\ell(\ell-2)\over(\ell-1)^2}
 =1-{1\over(\ell-1)^2}.                                                \tag{5}
\]
The product of the factors in (5) over odd primes converges absolutely to \(C_2>0\), because the sum of \(1/(\ell-1)^2\) converges. This proves convergence of (1).

It remains to compare each exceptional odd-prime factor with the generic factor (5). If \(\nu_\ell=0\), the actual local factor is
\[
 (1-1/\ell)^{-2}={\ell^2\over(\ell-1)^2},
\]
whose ratio to (5) is
\[
 {\ell\over\ell-2}.                                                     \tag{6}
\]
If \(\nu_\ell=1\), the actual local factor is
\[
 (1-1/\ell)^{-1}={\ell\over\ell-1},
\]
whose ratio to (5) is
\[
 {\ell-1\over\ell-2}.                                                   \tag{7}
\]

Since \(d_1,d_2\) are squarefree, the primes dividing \(g\) are exactly those dividing both moduli, while the primes dividing
\(h=d_1d_2/g^2\) are exactly those dividing one modulus but not the other. The remaining exceptional primes are exactly the primes dividing \(N(d_1-d_2)\) but not \(d_1d_2\). Multiplying the base factor (4), the generic odd-prime product \(C_2\), the ratios (6) on primes dividing \(g\), and the ratios (7) on the other two exceptional sets proves (3).

glossary.g: the greatest common divisor of d1 and d2
glossary.mathfrak S_N(d1,d2): the Hardy--Littlewood local-density product for the two affine forms
glossary.nu_ell(N;d1,d2): the number of local roots modulo ell of the product (N-d1 m)(N-d2 m)

b302e2cd6d611a35.title: Let c be a positive integer and define e_c(x)=exp(2 pi i x/c). For integers m,n define the classical Kloosterman sum S(m,n;c)=sum_{x modulo c, gcd(x,c)=1} e_c(mx+n x^{-1}), where x^{-1} is the inverse of x modulo c. Then for every integer A and every integer t coprime to c,
b302e2cd6d611a35.author: slava chan
b302e2cd6d611a35.statement:
Let c be a positive integer and define e_c(x)=exp(2 pi i x/c). For integers m,n define the classical Kloosterman sum S(m,n;c)=sum_{x modulo c, gcd(x,c)=1} e_c(mx+n x^{-1}), where x^{-1} is the inverse of x modulo c. Then for every integer A and every integer t coprime to c,
e_c(A t^{-1})=(1/c) sum_{k modulo c} S(-k,A;c)e_c(kt).
In particular, if m and n are each coprime to c, then
e_c(A (mn)^{-1})=(1/c) sum_{k modulo c}S(-k,A;c)e_c(kmn).
Thus additive Fourier completion of an inverse-product phase produces a full dual k-sum and a joint product phase e_c(kmn); it does not by itself produce a bilinear form whose kernel is S(am,n;c) with m and n as the two original variables.
b302e2cd6d611a35.proof:
Define f on residues modulo c by f(t)=e_c(A t^{-1}) when gcd(t,c)=1 and f(t)=0 otherwise. With the Fourier-transform convention hat f(k)=sum_{t modulo c}f(t)e_c(-kt), one has
hat f(k)=sum_{t modulo c, gcd(t,c)=1}e_c(-kt+A t^{-1})=S(-k,A;c)
by the definition of the Kloosterman sum. Finite Fourier inversion on Z/cZ gives
f(t)=(1/c)sum_{k modulo c}hat f(k)e_c(kt)=(1/c)sum_{k modulo c}S(-k,A;c)e_c(kt).
For gcd(t,c)=1 this is the first displayed identity. If gcd(mn,c)=1, substitute t=mn and use (mn)^{-1}=m^{-1}n^{-1} modulo c to obtain the second identity.

The last sentence is a literal description of the resulting formula: the summation variable k ranges over every residue modulo c, the original variables m,n occur together in e_c(kmn), and the Kloosterman sum has arguments (-k,A). No algebraic relabelling of this displayed identity alone yields S(am,n;c) with independent coefficients in the original m and n; an additional transform or estimate would be required.

glossary.S(m,n;c): The classical Kloosterman sum with arguments m,n and modulus c.
glossary.e_c: The additive character e_c(x)=exp(2 pi i x/c).

b390149c13836271.title: BV-WEIGHTED SEPARATED FACTOR-BOX SUPPLIER FOR A POSSIBLY NONUNIT SQUAREFREE COMPOSITE RECIPROCAL PHASE. Fix J>=1. Let n>1 be squarefree, let C be an integer, put g=gcd(C,n) and m_eff=n/g, and assume m_eff>1. Let X,U,Y>=1 satisfy
b390149c13836271.author: slava chan
b390149c13836271.statement:
BV-WEIGHTED SEPARATED FACTOR-BOX SUPPLIER FOR A POSSIBLY NONUNIT SQUAREFREE COMPOSITE RECIPROCAL PHASE. Fix J>=1. Let n>1 be squarefree, let C be an integer, put g=gcd(C,n) and m_eff=n/g, and assume m_eff>1. Let X,U,Y>=1 satisfy
U<=m_eff,  4Y<m_eff.                                               (1)
Let alpha_u and gamma_y be complex coefficients supported respectively on U<=u<2U and Y<=y<2Y and bounded by fixed divisor functions tau_J(u),tau_J(y). Let c be any positive integer. Let W be a complex function on the integers, extended by zero and supported on X<=k<2X, and define
V_X(W)=sup_k|W(k)|+sum_k|W(k+1)-W(k)|.                            (2)
Then, for every epsilon>0,
|sum_{u,y;(uy,nc)=1} alpha_u gamma_y W(uy)e_n(C(uy)^(-1))|
 <<_{J,epsilon} V_X(W)(m_eff UY)^epsilon
 [UY^(1/2)+U^(1/2)Y m_eff^(1/4)].                               (3)
All inverses are taken on the displayed coprime support. In particular, if UY is comparable to X, V_X(W)<=X^epsilon, and for some fixed delta>0
Y>=X^(2delta),  Y m_eff^(1/2)<=X^(1-2delta),                    (4)
then (3) is <<X^(1-delta+O(epsilon)).

For the literal C1 row of fact 79ffbcb2ffe4049f, with phase numerator C=mathscr A h and n=pv, the effective modulus m_eff contains p whenever p does not divide mathscr A h. Hence (3) is a genuine composite-modulus one-row supplier on every Möbius-decomposition factor box admitting a separated product q=uy and satisfying (1),(4), including an arbitrary squarefree auxiliary coprimality gate and the literal bounded-variation q-amplitude. It does not produce such a separated factorization of mu(q), does not pay factor boxes outside the medium-factor window, and therefore does not prove the full composite-Möbius supplier of fact 79ffbcb2ffe4049f.
b390149c13836271.proof:
Write C=gC' and n=gm_eff. Then gcd(C',m_eff)=1 and, on units,
e_n(C(uy)^(-1))=e_{m_eff}(C'(uy)^(-1)).                           (5)
The condition (uy,nc)=1 factors exactly as the product of a condition on u and a condition on y, so it may be absorbed into alpha_u and gamma_y without changing their fixed divisor-function bounds. Thus neither n nor c enters any subsequent estimate. It remains to prove (3) with unit numerator C' and modulus m_eff.

Apply Cauchy in u. The divisor-function bounds are absorbed into (m_eff UY)^epsilon, giving
|T|^2 <<(m_eff UY)^epsilon U
 sum_{u~U,(u,m_eff)=1}
 |sum_{y~Y,(y,m_eff)=1}gamma_y W(uy)e_{m_eff}(C' y^(-1)u^(-1))|^2. (6)
After expanding the square, the u-sum for y_1,y_2 is
sum_{u in I,(u,m_eff)=1}
 W(uy_1)conjugate(W(uy_2))
 e_{m_eff}(C'(y_1^(-1)-y_2^(-1))u^(-1)),                       (7)
where I is an interval contained in [U,2U).

For fixed y, the sequence u maps increasingly to the subsequence uy of the integer axis. Therefore
sum_u|W((u+1)y)-W(uy)|<=sum_k|W(k+1)-W(k)|.
The product in (7) consequently has supremum plus total variation at most a fixed constant times V_X(W)^2. Partial summation applied to equation (7) of fact 4a101b703d4499f6 therefore bounds (7), when its phase is nonconstant, by
<<epsilon V_X(W)^2(m_eff UY)^epsilon m_eff^(1/2)(y_2-y_1,m_eff)^(1/2). (8)
Indeed y_1y_2 is a unit, so the gcd of the phase numerator with m_eff is exactly (y_2-y_1,m_eff).

Because both y_i lie in [Y,2Y) and 4Y<m_eff, the phase in (7) is constant exactly when y_1=y_2. The diagonal contribution to the last sum in (6) is
<<V_X(W)^2(m_eff UY)^epsilon UY.                                (9)
For the off-diagonal, specialize the gcd-sum argument in equations (9)-(12) of fact 4a101b703d4499f6 to H=1. It gives
sum_{y_1!=y_2}(y_2-y_1,m_eff)^(1/2)
 <<epsilon (m_eff Y)^epsilon Y^2.                               (10)
Combining (8) and (10), the off-diagonal contribution to the last sum in (6) is
<<V_X(W)^2(m_eff UY)^epsilon m_eff^(1/2)Y^2.                     (11)
Insert (9),(11) into (6), enlarge epsilon once, and take square roots. The two resulting terms are
V_X(W)U Y^(1/2),  V_X(W)U^(1/2)Y m_eff^(1/4),
with the common factor (m_eff UY)^epsilon, which proves (3).

If UY is comparable to X, the first term in brackets is comparable to X Y^(-1/2), hence is at most X^(1-delta) under the first condition in (4). The second is comparable to X^(1/2)Y^(1/2)m_eff^(1/4), hence is at most X^(1-delta) under the second condition in (4). The second condition also implies m_eff<=X^(2-4delta), while UY is comparable to X. Thus (m_eff UY)^epsilon V_X(W)<=X^{O(epsilon)}, proving the power-saving corollary.

Finally fact 79ffbcb2ffe4049f identifies C=mathscr A h and n=pv. If p does not divide C, then p does not divide g, so p divides m_eff. The bounded-variation amplitude and auxiliary coprimality in that fact fit W and c in the present statement. The theorem itself does not create the separated alpha_u gamma_y factorization of mu(uy), so the final exclusions are exact.

glossary.V_X(W): The supremum plus discrete total variation of a zero-extended product weight W supported on [X,2X).
glossary.m_eff: The effective reciprocal modulus n/gcd(C,n) after removing the common divisor of the phase numerator and modulus.
glossary.medium-factor window: The pair of inequalities Y>=X^(2delta) and Y m_eff^(1/2)<=X^(1-2delta) which makes both terms of the weighted reciprocal factor-box estimate power-saving.

b3b1ffc1f4215692.title: Let \(H\ge1\) be an integer and define
b3b1ffc1f4215692.author: slava chan
b3b1ffc1f4215692.statement:
Let \(H\ge1\) be an integer and define
\[
 D_H(\theta)=\sum_{|h|\le H}e(h\theta),
 \qquad e(t)=\exp(2\pi it).
\]
If \(q\ge2\), \((a,q)=1\), and
\[
 \left|\theta-{a\over q}\right|\le {1\over4q},
\]
then
\[
 |D_H(\theta)|\le {1\over|\sin(\pi\theta)|}
 \ll q,                                                  \tag{1}
\]
where \(a/q\) is represented with circular distance at most \(1/2\) from zero. At zero,
\[
 D_H(0)=2H+1.                                             \tag{2}
\]

For the top-band recombination, fix
\[
 1/2<\alpha<\beta<1,\quad\eta>0,\quad\rho>0,
\]
let \(W\) and \(\Phi\) be bounded real functions supported in
\([\alpha,\beta]\) and \([1/2,2]\), let \(x\ge3\), let \(N=2x\) be an integer, and put
\[
 T_x=(\log x)^{6+\eta+\rho}.
\]
Let \(D,U>0\) satisfy
\[
 D\le2x^{1/2},\qquad D>2T_x.
\]
Let \(\mu\) be the Möbius function, extend \(\Lambda\) by zero on nonpositive integers, and put
\[
 {\cal I}_D=\{d\ge2:(d,N)=1,\ \mu(d)\ne0, d\le x^{1/2},\ \Phi(d/D)\ne0\}.
\]
For positive integers \(s,m\), define
\[
 T_{s,m}=
 \sum_{\substack{w\ge1\\sw\in{\cal I}_D}}
 \mu(w)\Phi(sw/D)W(smw/x)
 \Phi((N-smw)/U)\Lambda(N-smw),
\]
\[
 \mathbf T_s=(T_{s,m})_{m\ge1}\in\ell^2(\mathbb N),
\]
\[
 c_{T_x}(s)=
 \sum_{\substack{gr=s\\g<T_x,\ r<T_x}}\mu(r).
\]
Define
\[
 {\cal E}_{<}=\sum_{s<T_x^2}c_{T_x}(s)\|\mathbf T_s\|_2^2,
 \qquad
 {\mathfrak D}_N^\Lambda=\|\mathbf T_1\|_2^2,
 \qquad
 Y_{\rm tar}=xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta}.
\]
Then
\[
 c_{T_x}(1)=1,qquad c_{T_x}(s)=0\quad(1<s<T_x),         \tag{3}
\]
and
\[
 {\cal E}_{<}
 ={\mathfrak D}_N^\Lambda+
 O_{W,\Phi,\alpha,\beta}
 \left({xD(\log x)^2\log(2T_x)\over T_x}\right)
 ={\mathfrak D}_N^\Lambda+o(Y_{\rm tar}).              \tag{4}
\]
Thus every complete contribution placed solely on a level
\(1<s<T_x\) is annihilated by recombination, but the complete \(s=1\) contribution survives.

Let
\[
 \mathbf T_1=\mathbf A_1+\mathbf B_1                  \tag{5}
\]
be any decomposition in \(\ell^2(\mathbb N)\), interpreted abstractly as major plus minor. Then exactly
\[
 {\mathfrak D}_N^\Lambda
 =\|\mathbf A_1\|_2^2+
 2\operatorname{Re}\langle\mathbf A_1,\mathbf B_1\rangle+
 \|\mathbf B_1\|_2^2.                                 \tag{6}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \left|
 2\operatorname{Re}\langle\mathbf A_1,\mathbf B_1\rangle+
 \|\mathbf B_1\|_2^2
 \right|\ll Y_{\rm tar}                                \tag{7}
\]
implies
\[
 \|\mathbf A_1\|_2^2
 =\mathfrak D_N^\Lambda+O(Y_{\rm tar}),                \tag{8}
\]
and
\[
 {\cal E}_{<}=\|\mathbf A_1\|_2^2+O(Y_{\rm tar}).    \tag{9}
\]
A bound only for \(\|\mathbf B_1\|_2^2\) does not by itself imply (7), because the cross term remains.

Equations (1)--(9) are the scoped classical-major-recombination loop. They do not construct (5). The bare kernel estimate (1) cannot be promoted to an arithmetic nonzero-rational-arc estimate until its \(q\)-dependent prime and smooth coefficients have been separated with controlled norm. Even if such pieces are proved cheap, (4) and (8) show that the zero-level major vector remains target-close to the original full dispersion under (7).
b3b1ffc1f4215692.proof:
The geometric-sum identity gives
\[
 D_H(\theta)={\sin((2H+1)\pi\theta)\over\sin(\pi\theta)}
\]
away from integers. Choose the representative \(a\) with
\(1\le|a|\le q/2\). Then
\[
 \|\theta\|\ge {|a|\over q}-{1\over4q}\ge {3\over4q}.
\]
Since \(\sin(\pi t)\ge2t\) for \(0\le t\le1/2\),
\[
 |\sin(\pi\theta)|\gg q^{-1}.
\]
This proves (1), and (2) is immediate.

Fact 83c98e3d3a11382b proves under the displayed hypotheses
\[
 {\cal E}_{<}=\sum_{s<T_x^2}c_{T_x}(s)\sum_m|T_{s,m}|^2,
\]
the identities in (3), and
\[
 {\cal E}_{<}
 =\sum_m|T_{1,m}|^2+
 O\left({xD(\log x)^2\log(2T_x)\over T_x}\right).
\]
This proves the first equality in (4). Since
\[
 T_x=(\log x)^{6+\eta+\rho},
 \qquad \log(2T_x)=o((\log x)^\rho),
\]
the error is \(o(Y_{\rm tar})\).

Equation (6) is the Hilbert identity
\[
 \|\mathbf A_1+\mathbf B_1\|_2^2
 =\|\mathbf A_1\|_2^2+
 2\operatorname{Re}\langle\mathbf A_1,\mathbf B_1\rangle+
 \|\mathbf B_1\|_2^2,
\]
where
\[
 \langle\mathbf A_1,\mathbf B_1\rangle
 =\sum_mA_{1,m}\overline{B_{1,m}}.
\]
Rearrangement proves (8) from (7), and (9) follows from (4).

Finally,
\[
 |2\operatorname{Re}\langle\mathbf A_1,\mathbf B_1\rangle|
 \le2\|\mathbf A_1\|_2\|\mathbf B_1\|_2.
\]
Without a separate bound for \(\|\mathbf A_1\|_2\), an estimate for
\(\|\mathbf B_1\|_2^2\) alone need not make this product target-sized. This proves the stated scope.

glossary.Y_tar: the target hard-covariance scale xD(log x)^(-4-eta)
glossary.bold A_1: an abstract classical-major component of bold T_1
glossary.bold B_1: the complementary abstract minor component bold T_1-bold A_1

b3c1cdc5cb47ae63.title: EXACT TWO-SIDED VAUGHAN TRI-FACTOR DECOMPOSITION OF THE COMPLETE CENTERED ACTUAL-Z ROW
b3c1cdc5cb47ae63.author: slava chan
b3c1cdc5cb47ae63.statement:
EXACT TWO-SIDED VAUGHAN TRI-FACTOR DECOMPOSITION OF THE COMPLETE CENTERED ACTUAL-Z ROW.

Let Q>8, put U=Q^(1/3), and let w_n be arbitrary complex coefficients supported on integers Q<=n<2Q. Put
  alpha_n=mu(n)w_n.                                           (1)
Assume squarefree b and an active conductor f|b with (f,N)=1. Use the complete centered response R_{b,f} and row S_{b,f} of fact 14fe68fdcbfd99ff.

Define
 S^{ss}_{b,f}(w)
  =sum_{Q<=ldm<2Q; d<=U,m<=U;(ldm,b)=1}
     mu(d)mu(m)w_{ldm}R_{b,f}(ldm),                           (2)
 S^{ll}_{b,f}(w)
  =sum_{Q<=ldm<2Q; d>U,m>U;(ldm,b)=1}
     mu(d)mu(m)w_{ldm}R_{b,f}(ldm).                           (3)
Then exactly
  S_{b,f}(alpha)=-S^{ss}_{b,f}(w)+S^{ll}_{b,f}(w).            (4)

Every tuple in (2) satisfies l>=U. Every tuple in (3) satisfies l<2U. Moreover, by the symmetry d<->m, (3) is exactly
  S^{ll}_{b,f}(w)
   =sum_{Q<=ldm<2Q; U<d<=m;(ldm,b)=1}
      kappa(d,m)mu(d)mu(m)w_{ldm}R_{b,f}(ldm),                (5)
where kappa(d,m)=1 if d=m and kappa(d,m)=2 if d<m. On the support of (5),
  U<d<=sqrt(2Q).                                              (6)

On the unit support in (2), (3), or (5),
 R_{b,f}(ldm)
  =product_{p|f}
    [e_p(N l^(-1)d^(-1)m^(-1)(b/p)^(-1))+1/(p-1)].           (7)
For every p|f, after fixing two of l,d,m as units modulo p and fixing all CRT coordinates outside p, the sum of the local factor in (7) over the p-1 unit lifts of the remaining factor modulo p is zero. Thus the tri-factor decomposition preserves the complete primewise centering in each inverse slot.

Consequently, for every actual tensor alpha of fact 58c03698e1b077c3, after extracting its literal mu(n) factor as in (1), substituting (4) into every row of formulas (4) and (6) of fact 14fe68fdcbfd99ff gives an exact tri-factor reformulation of the complete CEN-MZB square. The difference -S^{ss}+S^{ll}, the signed f/cofactor superposition, and the b-square must remain assembled. No estimate for either tri-factor part separately, for complete CEN-MZB, for C_small, or for Goldbach is asserted. In particular, the identity does not claim that the product-coupled literal coefficient w_{ldm} has already been separated into one-variable coefficients.
b3c1cdc5cb47ae63.proof:
We first prove the two-sided Möbius identity used in (4). Let U_1,V_1>=1 and n>max(U_1,V_1). Partition
  T(n)=sum_{ldm=n}mu(d)mu(m)=(1*mu*mu)(n)=mu(n)             (8)
into the four regions according as d<=V_1 or d>V_1 and m<=U_1 or m>U_1. Denote the both-small contribution by A, the region d<=V_1,m>U_1 by B, the region d>V_1,m<=U_1 by C, and the both-large contribution by D.

The sum of the regions with d<=V_1 is
 sum_{d|n;d<=V_1}mu(d) sum_{m|n/d}mu(m).
Because d<=V_1<n, one has n/d>1, and the inner divisor sum is zero. Hence A+B=0. Similarly, because m<=U_1<n, summing first over d gives A+C=0. Therefore
  T(n)=A+B+C+D=D-A.                                          (9)
Together with (8), this proves
 mu(n)
  =-sum_{ldm=n;d<=V_1,m<=U_1}mu(d)mu(m)
   +sum_{ldm=n;d>V_1,m>U_1}mu(d)mu(m).                       (10)
This is also Lemma 3.5 of Li--Wu, arXiv:1412.2237, with equal truncations below.

Apply (10) with U_1=V_1=U=Q^(1/3) to every n in the support of (1), multiply by
  w_n R_{b,f}(n) 1_{(n,b)=1},
and sum over Q<=n<2Q. All sums are finite, so interchanging the divisor sums with the n-sum is exact. The two resulting terms are (2) and (3), proving (4).

In (2), dm<=U^2, so l=n/(dm)>=Q/U^2=U. In (3), dm>U^2, so l=n/(dm)<2Q/U^2=2U. The summand and every condition in (3) are invariant under exchanging d and m. Partitioning its ordered pairs into d=m, d<m, and m<d therefore gives (5) with the displayed kappa. If U<d<=m and ldm<2Q, then d^2<=dm<2Q/l<=2Q, since l>=1. Hence d<=sqrt(2Q), proving (6).

On (ldm,b)=1, each of l,d,m is a unit modulo every p|f and
  (ldm)^(-1)=l^(-1)d^(-1)m^(-1) modulo p.
Insert this identity into formula (1) of fact 14fe68fdcbfd99ff to obtain (7). Fix p|f and two of the three unit residues. Because (f,N)=1 and b is squarefree, the coefficient multiplying the inverse of the remaining unit in the exponential is nonzero modulo p. Inversion and multiplication by a fixed unit each permute the p-1 units. Therefore the exponential sums to -1 over those unit lifts. Adding p-1 copies of 1/(p-1) gives zero. This proves the separate local centering assertion.

Finally, the construction in fact 58c03698e1b077c3 places the literal mu(n) and every n-only mask and smooth factor in alpha_n, so it has the form (1), with w_n equal to the remaining n-only factor on the supported integers. Formula (4) can therefore be substituted into the exact conductor-row square of fact 14fe68fdcbfd99ff. Since the substitution is an identity for each (b,f), it preserves the outer signed conductor sum and its square without any triangle inequality. It leaves w_{ldm} as the exact product-coupled coefficient, so it proves precisely the stated reformulation and none of the excluded estimates.

glossary.S^{ll}_{b,f}(w): The both-large tri-factor part of a centered conductor row.
glossary.S^{ss}_{b,f}(w): The both-small tri-factor part of a centered conductor row.
glossary.kappa(d,m): The symmetry multiplicity, equal to one on d=m and two on d<m.

b40e31c2127d327d.title: AMBIENT-INTERVAL GENERALIZATION OF THE SHARED-LIFT FIBRE LEMMA
b40e31c2127d327d.author: slava chan
b40e31c2127d327d.statement:
AMBIENT-INTERVAL GENERALIZATION OF THE SHARED-LIFT FIBRE LEMMA.

Fix positive constants L and B. Let m>2L+1 be odd, put q=m^2, let s belong to {1,-1}, and let K be coprime to m. Represent u modulo m by 0<=u<m and put
 A_u=K+2smu.                                                         (1)
Let I_a,I_c,I_1,I_2 be arbitrary integer intervals of cardinality at most Lm, with I_1,I_2 consisting of positive integers. Let F be supported on I_a, let W be a function modulo m, and let alpha,beta be supported on I_1,I_2.

Let E_lift^unit be any subset of tuples
 (a,c,n_1,n_2,u,k) in I_a times I_c times I_1 times I_2 times {0,...,m-1} times Z
such that
 gcd(n_1n_2,q)=1,
 a n_2=A_u+kq,
 c n_1=a n_2-2K,
 1<=|a n_2-2K|<=q^B.                                                (2)
Let Gamma be a complex function on E_lift^unit with |Gamma|<=1 and define
 T_lift=sum_{E_lift^unit}F(a)W(u)alpha(n_1)beta(n_2)
             Gamma(a,c,n_1,n_2,u,k).                               (3)
Then
 -c n_1=K-2smu-kq.                                                   (4)

For a unit residue x modulo q put
 C_lift(x)=sum_{E_lift^unit;ax congruent 1 modulo q}
 W(u)alpha(n_1)beta(n_2)Gamma(a,c,n_1,n_2,u,k),                     (5)
and put C_lift(x)=0 on nonunits. Define
 F_per(y)=sum_{a congruent y modulo q}F(a),
 C_hat_lift(p)=sum_{x modulo q}C_lift(x)e_q(-px),
 F_hat(h)=sum_{y modulo q}F_per(y)e_q(-hy),                          (6)
where e_q(z)=exp(2 pi i z/q). Then
 T_lift=sum_{x unit modulo q}C_lift(x)F_per(x^(-1))                  (7)
and
 T_lift=q^(-2)sum_{p,h modulo q}C_hat_lift(p)F_hat(h)S(p,h;q),       (8)
where
 S(p,h;q)=sum_{x unit modulo q}e_q(px+h x^(-1)).                     (9)
For every epsilon>0,
 ||C_lift||_2<=C_{B,L,epsilon}q^epsilon
 ||W||_2||alpha||_2||beta||_2,                                    (10)
and
 ||C_hat_lift||_2=q^(1/2)||C_lift||_2
 <=C_{B,L,epsilon}q^(1/2+epsilon)
 ||W||_2||alpha||_2||beta||_2.                                    (11)

Thus the ambient column intervals may contain nonunits; only columns in admitted tuples must be units. Values of alpha,beta at nonunit ambient integers are never sampled, and no decomposition into unit-only ordinary intervals is required.
b40e31c2127d327d.proof:
Equation (4) follows from (2). The representative convention makes k unambiguous.

Every A_u is a unit modulo q. On an admitted tuple n_2 is a unit, so a is a unit. Since |I_a|<q, each residue has at most one representative a in I_a. Hence every tuple has a unique x congruent to a^(-1), and F(a)=F_per(x^(-1)). This proves (7). Fourier inversion of C_lift and F_per in (7) proves (8)-(9).

We prove (10). Fix a unit x. There is at most one a. Reducing a n_2=A_u+kq modulo m gives n_2 congruent Kx modulo m. The interval I_2 has at most L+1 representatives of this class. For fixed x,a,n_2, the equation determines u uniquely because 2s is a unit modulo odd m. Then positive n_1 divides the nonzero integer a n_2-2K and c is determined.

The proof of fact 212d1415bf03c2a7 gives self-containedly, for every delta>0, tau(N)<=C_delta N^delta. Since |a n_2-2K|<=q^B, each x-fibre has cardinality at most C_{B,L,epsilon}q^epsilon. Cauchy--Schwarz in each fibre gives
 sum_x|C_lift(x)|^2
 <=Cq^epsilon sum_{E_lift^unit}
 |W(u)|^2|alpha(n_1)|^2|beta(n_2)|^2.                              (12)
For fixed u,n_1,n_2, unitness of n_2 makes a unique modulo q; |I_a|<q gives at most one integer a, and then k,c are fixed. Thus E_lift^unit -> (u,n_1,n_2) has fibre at most one. The last sum in (12) is at most the product of the three squared norms, proving (10).

Additive Parseval gives ||C_hat_lift||_2=q^(1/2)||C_lift||_2, proving (11). This repeats the proof of fact 212d1415bf03c2a7 with one change: every inversion of n_1 or n_2 is made only on an admitted tuple and is supplied by gcd(n_1n_2,q)=1. No step uses unitness of an ambient interval value outside E_lift^unit.

glossary.E_lift^unit: the shared-lift incidence set whose admitted columns are units although its ambient column intervals may contain nonunits

b47f1acbf3a70dc0.title: COMPLETE p-DIVIDES-C STRICT-TOP C1 PAYMENT ABOVE A SINGLE LOWER EFFECTIVE EDGE. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100 and beta_m=6/5-12sigma/5, and fix K_0>=2. Let Q be sufficiently large and let beta_m<=beta<6/5. Let n=pv be squarefree, where p is prime, gcd(p,v)=1, every prime divisor of v is at most Q^(beta-1+sigma), n lies in a fixed dyadic interval of scale B=Q^beta, and p>=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma). Let C=mathscr A h, assume p divides C, put m_eff=n/gcd(C,n), and write t=log(m_eff)/log(Q). Assume
b47f1acbf3a70dc0.author: slava chan
b47f1acbf3a70dc0.statement:
COMPLETE p-DIVIDES-C STRICT-TOP C1 PAYMENT ABOVE A SINGLE LOWER EFFECTIVE EDGE. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100 and beta_m=6/5-12sigma/5, and fix K_0>=2. Let Q be sufficiently large and let beta_m<=beta<6/5. Let n=pv be squarefree, where p is prime, gcd(p,v)=1, every prime divisor of v is at most Q^(beta-1+sigma), n lies in a fixed dyadic interval of scale B=Q^beta, and p>=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma). Let C=mathscr A h, assume p divides C, put m_eff=n/gcd(C,n), and write t=log(m_eff)/log(Q). Assume
16/25+33kappa/125<=t<=6/5.                                      (1)
Let c be squarefree with nc<=Q^K_0. Let W be extended by zero, supported on Q<=q<2Q, and satisfy V_Q(W)<=Q^epsilon for every fixed epsilon>0. Then
S=sum_{q;gcd(q,nc)=1}mu(q)W(q)e_n(Cq^(-1))
satisfies
|S|<=Q^(1-kappa/200+o(1)).                                      (2)
Consequently, inside the large-effective routing range Q^(1/2+kappa)<=m_eff<=Q^(6/5), the only p-divides-C chamber not covered by this theorem is
1/2+kappa<=t<16/25+33kappa/125.                                 (3)
No estimate for (3) is asserted.
b47f1acbf3a70dc0.proof:
Because n=pv is squarefree and p divides C, the prime p is removed from m_eff=n/gcd(C,n). Hence m_eff divides v and
m_eff<=v=n/p.                                                    (4)
The dyadic support gives n<=2Q^beta. Using the rough-prime lower bound,
v<=2Q^beta Q^(-3/2+beta+3sigma)
 =2Q^(2beta-3/2+3sigma)
 <2Q^(9/10+3sigma),                                              (5)
because beta<6/5. Since sigma>0 is fixed, 2<=Q^sigma for sufficiently large Q, and therefore
t<=9/10+4sigma.                                                  (6)

All literal hypotheses of fact 4b73e72865a65e16 are now displayed explicitly, including the squarefree factorization, gcd(p,v)=1, and the bound Q^(beta-1+sigma) on every prime divisor of v. Apply that fact with its fixed slack zeta chosen equal to sigma=kappa/100. Its lower endpoint is
16/25+127kappa/500+kappa/100
 =16/25+132kappa/500
 =16/25+33kappa/125,                                             (7)
which is exactly the lower bound in (1). Its upper endpoint is
28/25-97kappa/250-kappa/100
 =28/25-199kappa/500.                                            (8)
For 0<kappa<=1/100,
9/10+4sigma<=9/10+1/2500
 <28/25-199/50000,
so (6) lies strictly below (8). Thus every actual row satisfying (1) meets both endpoint hypotheses of fact 4b73e72865a65e16. That fact gives (2).

The exact finite routing range of fact df45be7aead3cec9 begins at t=1/2+kappa. Intersecting it with the complement of (1) and with the actual upper bound (6) gives precisely (3). This is a set-theoretic frontier statement and supplies no estimate there.

b4934b4981fc5817.title: EXACT CONDUCTOR-SECTOR SINGULAR-VALUE LEDGER FOR THE ODD PMLS KLOOSTERMAN CONVOLUTION. Let r>1 be odd and squarefree, let c be a unit modulo r, and let T_{r,c}:l2(G_r)->l2(G_r) be the normalized Kloosterman convolution of fact 18a0de57eaf35171. For d|r let P_{r,d} be the orthogonal multiplicative-Fourier projector onto the characters modulo r whose primitive conductor is exactly d. Put
b4934b4981fc5817.author: slava chan
b4934b4981fc5817.statement:
EXACT CONDUCTOR-SECTOR SINGULAR-VALUE LEDGER FOR THE ODD PMLS KLOOSTERMAN CONVOLUTION. Let r>1 be odd and squarefree, let c be a unit modulo r, and let T_{r,c}:l2(G_r)->l2(G_r) be the normalized Kloosterman convolution of fact 18a0de57eaf35171. For d|r let P_{r,d} be the orthogonal multiplicative-Fourier projector onto the characters modulo r whose primitive conductor is exactly d. Put
