phi^*(d)=sum_{a|d}mu(d/a)phi(a),                                     (1)
the number of primitive Dirichlet characters modulo d. Then
||T_{r,c}P_{r,d}||_{op}=d/r,                                         (2)
||T_{r,c}P_{r,d}||_{HS}^2=phi^*(d)d^2/r^2.                           (3)
The conductor sectors are orthogonal on both input and output. Consequently, for every nonempty set D of divisors of r,
||T_{r,c}sum_{d in D}P_{r,d}||_{op}=max_{d in D}d/r,                 (4)
||T_{r,c}sum_{d in D}P_{r,d}||_{HS}^2
=sum_{d in D}phi^*(d)d^2/r^2.                                       (5)
In particular, if r=pq for distinct odd primes p,q, the whole imprimitive sector P_{r,<r}=P_{r,1}+P_{r,p}+P_{r,q} satisfies
||T_{r,c}P_{r,<r}||_{op}=1/min(p,q),                                (6)
||T_{r,c}P_{r,<r}||_{HS}^2
=1/(p^2q^2)+(p-2)/q^2+(q-2)/p^2,                                   (7)
whereas the primitive sector has operator norm one and Hilbert--Schmidt norm squared (p-2)(q-2). Thus every imprimitive odd-semiprime character sector is spectrally damped; only the primitive sector is undamped. These are exact one-modulus spectral identities and do not by themselves estimate a varying-r PMLS block.
b4934b4981fc5817.proof:
Use the normalized multiplicative Fourier transform
fhat(chi)=phi(r)^(-1)sum_{x in G_r}f(x)overline{chi(x)}
from fact 18a0de57eaf35171. Multiplicative Parseval says
sum_{x in G_r}|f(x)|^2=phi(r)sum_{chi mod r}|fhat(chi)|^2,            (8)
so, after multiplying Fourier coordinates by sqrt(phi(r)), the transform is unitary.

Equation (10) of fact 18a0de57eaf35171 is
widehat(T_{r,c}f)(chi)=m_{r,c}(chi)fhat(overline chi),                (9)
and equation (11) there gives
|m_{r,c}(chi)|=d_chi/r,                                              (10)
where d_chi is the primitive conductor of chi. Conjugating the character index is a permutation which preserves every conductor sector. Therefore all singular values of T_{r,c}P_{r,d} are d/r, one for each character modulo r of conductor d.

Characters modulo squarefree r of conductor exactly d are precisely the lifts of primitive characters modulo d. Their number is phi^*(d). Formula (1) follows from Möbius inversion applied to phi(d)=sum_{a|d}phi^*(a). Because r is odd, every divisor d is odd and phi^*(d)>0: explicitly phi^*(1)=1 and for d>1 squarefree, phi^*(d)=product_{p|d}(p-2)>0. Thus every displayed sector is nonempty. The largest singular value gives (2), and the sum of squared singular values gives (3). Distinct conductor sectors are supported on disjoint Fourier coordinates, proving (4)--(5) for nonempty D.

Now let r=pq with p,q distinct odd primes. Formula (1) gives
phi^*(1)=1, phi^*(p)=p-2, phi^*(q)=q-2,
phi^*(pq)=(p-2)(q-2).                                                 (11)
Among proper conductors 1,p,q, the largest ratio d/r is max(p,q)/(pq)=1/min(p,q), proving (6). Substitution of the first three values in (5) proves (7). The primitive-sector statements follow from d=r in (2)--(3).

glossary.P_{r,<r}: the sum of the proper-conductor projectors for odd semiprime r
glossary.P_{r,d}: the orthogonal multiplicative-Fourier projector onto characters modulo r of primitive conductor d
glossary.phi^*(d): the number of primitive Dirichlet characters modulo d

b50e26bd7448384e.title: Let P tend to infinity and let c>0, T≥0, L_0≥0, δ>0, and B_0>0 be fixed. Suppose A_B≥cP^6(log P)^(-3), put η_P=(log P)^(-T), and suppose a real terminal aggregate Z_P is a sum of L_P real leaves Z_{P,1},...,Z_{P,L_P}, where 1≤L_P≤(log P)^(L_0). If
b50e26bd7448384e.author: slava chan
b50e26bd7448384e.statement:
Let P tend to infinity and let c>0, T≥0, L_0≥0, δ>0, and B_0>0 be fixed. Suppose A_B≥cP^6(log P)^(-3), put η_P=(log P)^(-T), and suppose a real terminal aggregate Z_P is a sum of L_P real leaves Z_{P,1},...,Z_{P,L_P}, where 1≤L_P≤(log P)^(L_0). If
Z_P≤-η_P A_B+o(η_P A_B),
then for all sufficiently large P,
min_{1≤j≤L_P} Z_{P,j}
≤-(c/2)P^6(log P)^(-(T+L_0+3)).

Suppose a downstream estimate for each leaf has an additive nonnegative remainder
R_P≤P^(6-δ)+P^6(log P)^(-B_0).
If B_0>T+L_0+3, then
R_P=o(P^6(log P)^(-(T+L_0+3))),
so the forced negative leaf magnitude dominates the additive remainder. Therefore every prescribed fixed inverse-logarithmic share η_P=(log P)^(-T) survives any fixed polylogarithmic leaf count, an arbitrary fixed power-saving remainder, and an arbitrarily strong logarithmic remainder once the logarithmic saving exponent is chosen after T and L_0.

More generally, without the displayed power laws, the exact scale condition for this pigeonhole-plus-remainder step is
η_P A_B/L_P≫R_P.
Thus there is no smallest positive inverse-logarithmic exponent T: every fixed T is admissible under arbitrarily strong log-saving input, while a proposed η_P below the ratio L_P R_P/A_B cannot be certified by this argument.

For the fixed-N negative coarse block in fact 0880dc648c429047, A_B may be taken as c_W𝔠(N)x/(2J_x^3), with J_x=ceil(log_2 x)+4. On the endpoint scale x=P^6 and using 𝔠(N)≥C_2 from fact f41f5f91b52e0d13, this has the required lower form A_B≥cP^6(log P)^(-3) for a fixed c>0. The additive Hilbert linearization remainder in fact f21be13a19bbb435 has exactly the permitted shape P^(6-δ)/4+P^6(log P)^(-B_0), with δ=ε/2. Hence any fixed polylogarithmic deficit share is compatible with the verified coarse-block loss and the verified Hilbert remainder, provided all additional leaf counts are bounded by a fixed power of log P and the input logarithmic saving is chosen with B_0>T+L_0+3.
b50e26bd7448384e.proof:
The arithmetic mean of the L_P leaves is Z_P/L_P, so at least one leaf is at most this mean. Since
Z_P≤-η_PA_B+o(η_PA_B),
for sufficiently large P one has Z_P≤-(1/2)η_PA_B. Therefore
min_j Z_{P,j}≤-η_PA_B/(2L_P).
Using η_P=(log P)^(-T), A_B≥cP^6(log P)^(-3), and L_P≤(log P)^(L_0) gives the first displayed bound.

Divide the power-saving part of R_P by the forced scale:
P^(6-δ)/[P^6(log P)^(-(T+L_0+3))]
=P^(-δ)(log P)^(T+L_0+3),
which tends to zero. Divide the logarithmic part by the same scale:
P^6(log P)^(-B_0)/[P^6(log P)^(-(T+L_0+3))]
=(log P)^(-(B_0-T-L_0-3)),
which tends to zero exactly when B_0>T+L_0+3. This proves the survival assertion.

Before substituting power laws, the forced per-leaf scale is η_PA_B/L_P. An additive remainder can be absorbed by this step precisely when it is of smaller order, namely L_PR_P/(η_PA_B) tends to zero. This yields the general condition and explains why no maximal fixed T exists when the logarithmic input saving can be made arbitrarily strong.

Fact 0880dc648c429047 gives the stated A_B. Since x=P^6, J_x is bounded above by a constant times log P. Fact f41f5f91b52e0d13 gives a fixed positive lower bound C_2 for 𝔠(N), so A_B≥cP^6(log P)^(-3) after adjusting c. Finally, fact f21be13a19bbb435 gives the additive terms P^(6-ε/2)/4 and P^6(log P)^(-B_0), which are the two terms just analyzed.

glossary.L_0: a fixed exponent controlling the polylogarithmic leaf count

b583f09dabee72b5.title: FIXED-SUPPORT INJECTIVITY OF THE COMMON-CELL DECODER COORDINATES
b583f09dabee72b5.author: slava chan
b583f09dabee72b5.statement:
FIXED-SUPPORT INJECTIVITY OF THE COMMON-CELL DECODER COORDINATES.

Assume the hypotheses and notation of facts dcabcf2f566b5721 and d016de3f6c03e65c. Fix an ordered pair (G,G') of coprime active semiprimes, orient their four distinct primes as G=r_1r_2 with r_1<r_2 and G'=r_3r_4 with r_3<r_4, and let mathcal E_{G,G'} be the eligible auxiliary residue set. For bold c=(c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4) in mathcal E_{G,G'}, define
m(bold c)=c_2r_3-c_3r_2,
C_dec(bold c)
 =(c_1r_2+c_2r_1)r_3r_4
  +r_1r_2(c_3r_4+c_4r_3),
and let K(bold c) be the decoder parameter in fact dcabcf2f566b5721. Put
iota_{G,G'}(bold c)=(m(bold c),C_dec(bold c),K(bold c)).

(A) The map iota_{G,G'} is injective. In fact, already
bold c maps to (m(bold c),C_dec(bold c))
is injective.

(B) Let d_{G,G',bold c} be the fully labelled decoder-copy coefficient of fact d016de3f6c03e65c. On the fixed-support image of iota_{G,G'}, define
widetilde d_{G,G',m,C_dec,K}
 =sum_{bold c in mathcal E_{G,G'}:
       iota_{G,G'}(bold c)=(m,C_dec,K)}
   d_{G,G',bold c}.
Then every sum on the right has exactly one term, and hence
sum_{(m,C_dec,K) in iota_{G,G'}(mathcal E_{G,G'})}
 |widetilde d_{G,G',m,C_dec,K}|
 =alpha_{G,G'}|gamma_Ggamma_{G'}|,
sum_{(m,C_dec,K) in iota_{G,G'}(mathcal E_{G,G'})}
 |widetilde d_{G,G',m,C_dec,K}|^2
 =alpha_{G,G'}^2|gamma_Ggamma_{G'}|^2/N_E(G,G').

Consequently, with (G,G') retained as part of the label,
sum_{substack{G,G' in mathcal G_H\gcd(G,G')=1}}
 sum_{(m,C_dec,K) in iota_{G,G'}(mathcal E_{G,G'})}
 |widetilde d_{G,G',m,C_dec,K}|^2
 <<D^4R^4H^{-12}(log x)^8(log(2H))^2,
and in the literal nonempty dyadic source range this is
<<D^4R^4H^{-12}(log x)^10.

This theorem only changes coordinates inside each fixed ordered support pair. It asserts no injectivity after (G,G') is forgotten, no cancellation or norm bound when different support pairs with equal decoder coordinates are combined, no varying-(m,C_dec,K) analytic estimate, no common-cell capture, no cross-cell control, and no Goldbach implication.
b583f09dabee72b5.proof:
Take bold c,bold c' in mathcal E_{G,G'} with the same m and C_dec, and write delta_i=c_i-c_i'. Equality of m gives
delta_2r_3=delta_3r_2.                                        (1)
The primes r_2 and r_3 are distinct. Hence gcd(r_2,r_3)=1, so (1) implies r_2 divides delta_2 and r_3 divides delta_3. Both c_2 and c_2' lie in [7H/8,H], so |delta_2|<=H/8. Since r_2>=H^2 and H is sufficiently large, |delta_2|<r_2. Therefore delta_2=0, and then (1) gives delta_3=0.

Expanding the decoder carrier gives
C_dec(bold c)
 =c_1r_2r_3r_4+c_2r_1r_3r_4
  +c_3r_1r_2r_4+c_4r_1r_2r_3.
Since delta_2=delta_3=0, equality of the two carriers reduces, after division by the nonzero integer r_2r_3, to
delta_1r_4+delta_4r_1=0.                                     (2)
The primes r_1 and r_4 are distinct. Thus (2) implies r_1 divides delta_1 and r_4 divides delta_4. The conditions 0<|c_1|,|c_1'|<=H/16 give |delta_1|<=H/8<r_1. Hence delta_1=0, and (2) then gives delta_4=0. Thus bold c=bold c'. This proves injectivity of bold c maps to (m,C_dec), and therefore also of iota_{G,G'}.

By injectivity, for every point of the image iota_{G,G'}(mathcal E_{G,G'}), the defining sum for widetilde d has exactly one summand. Thus reindexing from bold c to (m,C_dec,K) while retaining (G,G') preserves the counting-measure l1 and squared l2 sums term by term. The two fixed-pair identities are therefore exactly equations (3) and (4) of fact d016de3f6c03e65c. Summing its squared l2 identity over the still-labelled ordered coprime support pairs gives its aggregate estimate (5), and its literal-range logarithmic simplification gives the final displayed estimate. No step identifies coordinates arising from different ordered support pairs, which proves the scope paragraph.

glossary.iota_{G,G'}: For a fixed ordered coprime semiprime pair, the map from an eligible auxiliary residue quadruple to its decoder triple (m,C_dec,K).
glossary.widetilde d_{G,G',m,C_dec,K}: The decoder-copy coefficient after reindexing eligible auxiliary residues by decoder coordinates while retaining the ordered support pair.

b5e4098704e627cf.title: ALL-MOMENT OPTIMIZATION OF IRVING'S TWO-TERM BALANCED-CELL RIGHT-HAND SIDE, INCLUDING A HYPOTHETICAL GROWING MOMENT
b5e4098704e627cf.author: slava chan
b5e4098704e627cf.statement:
ALL-MOMENT OPTIMIZATION OF IRVING'S TWO-TERM BALANCED-CELL RIGHT-HAND SIDE, INCLUDING A HYPOTHETICAL GROWING MOMENT.

Assume the ideal balanced actual-Z_mid reciprocal cell and notation of fact be534c7b21bd963f:
B=Q^(4/3), L=M=Q^(2/3).
For every fixed integer k>=1, Irving's arXiv:1301.6372, Lemma 3.1 has the two-term right-hand side
Q^(1+epsilon)
 [Q^(1/(2k))L^((2k-1)/(2k))M^(1/2)
  +L^((2k-1)/(2k))M].                                      (1)
At the displayed lengths, the two exponents before epsilon are
A_k=2+1/(6k),                                                (2)
B_k=7/3-1/(3k).                                              (3)
They satisfy
min_{integer k>=1} max(A_k,B_k)=13/6,                        (4)
with equality at k=1 and k=2. Hence direct domination by the complete displayed right-hand side (1), optimized over every legal fixed integer moment, is no better than
Q^(13/6+epsilon),                                            (5)
which misses the Q^2 tensor endpoint by Q^(1/6).

Irving's published statement is quantified for each fixed integer k and has an implied constant depending on k and epsilon. It therefore does not itself give an estimate with k=k(Q) tending to infinity. More strongly, even if one hypothetically granted a version with exactly the same two-term right-hand side and sufficient uniformity to allow an arbitrary growing integer k=k(Q), equation (4) would still hold pointwise in Q and (5) would remain the optimized exponent. Thus the constants/uniformity question cannot rescue this particular two-term right-hand side.

This is only a direct theorem-right-hand-side no-fit on the favorable separated balanced cell. It is not a lower bound for the reciprocal sum and does not exclude a different growing-moment inequality with a changed right-hand side, a different decomposition, pre-Cauchy cancellation, the varying-composite-modulus crossed operator in fact f71c0564150cb532, an estimate for C_small, or actual-Z_mid closure.
b5e4098704e627cf.proof:
Fact be534c7b21bd963f already proves (2). For the second term of (1), substitute L=M=Q^(2/3). Its exponent is
1+(2/3)(2k-1)/(2k)+2/3
 =1+(2/3-1/(3k))+2/3
 =7/3-1/(3k),
which proves (3).

For k=1,
A_1=13/6 and B_1=2,
so max(A_1,B_1)=13/6.
For k=2,
A_2=25/12 and B_2=13/6,
so the maximum is again 13/6.
For every integer k>=3,
B_k>=7/3-1/9=20/9>13/6.
These cases prove (4), and (5) follows by substituting the minimizing exponent into (1).

The exact published quantifier and constant dependence are recorded in fact dd7f18552d39e5d4: the estimate holds for every fixed integer k>=1 with implied constant depending on k and epsilon. This does not authorize choosing k as a function of Q without a further uniform theorem. The hypothetical uniform statement follows separately from elementary algebra: (4) holds for every integer value of k, so it also holds after substituting any integer-valued function k(Q). This proves every assertion and the stated scope.

glossary.A_k: The Q-exponent of Irving's first theorem term on the ideal balanced cell.
glossary.B_k: The Q-exponent of Irving's second theorem term on the ideal balanced cell.

b5e69f0c8c442adc.title: POWER-SAVING SCALE CONSEQUENCE OF THE MEAN-ZERO PMD DISCREPANCY CONTRACT
b5e69f0c8c442adc.author: slava chan
b5e69f0c8c442adc.statement:
POWER-SAVING SCALE CONSEQUENCE OF THE MEAN-ZERO PMD DISCREPANCY CONTRACT.

Fix real numbers kappa and theta with
  0<kappa<1/3,  0<theta<1.
Let Q be sufficiently large, and let H,V be positive real numbers satisfying
  1<=H<=Q^(1/3-kappa),
  1<=V<=H Q^(-theta).                                      (1)
Put
  P=QH/V.                                                   (2)
For v,p in the dyadic ranges
  V<=v<2V,  P<=p<2P,
put
  M_{v,p}=vp/H.                                             (3)
Then
  Q<=M_{v,p}<4Q,                                            (4)
  P>=Q^(1+theta),                                           (5)
  P<=Q^(4/3-kappa).                                         (6)
In particular p>2Q throughout the dyadic prime range for all sufficiently large Q.

Fix a constant C_L>=1 and let L<=C_L Q. The two terms in the localized comparison estimate (7) of fact d481cd487c91eb70 satisfy
  P Q^(8/3)<=Q^(4-kappa),                                   (7)
  (L/P)Q^4<=C_L Q^(4-theta).                                (8)
Consequently
  P Q^(8/3)+(L/P)Q^4
  <=(1+C_L)Q^(4-eta),                                      (9)
where
  eta=min(kappa,theta)>0.                                   (10)
Thus, at these scales, the mean-zero discrepancy estimate (8) of fact d481cd487c91eb70 implies a power-saving D=0-subtracted short-window fourth-moment bound. The natural physical kernel length M_{v,p} is admissible with L=4Q. This is only the exponent and scale implication; it does not prove the mean-zero discrepancy estimate.
b5e69f0c8c442adc.proof:
From (2) and the upper bound for V in (1),
 P=QH/V>=Q^(1+theta),
which proves (5). Since V>=1 and H<=Q^(1/3-kappa),
 P=QH/V<=QH<=Q^(4/3-kappa),
which proves (6). Equation (5) gives p>=P>=Q^(1+theta)>2Q for sufficiently large Q.

For (4), use (2) in (3):
 M_{v,p}=vp/H.
The lower dyadic bounds v>=V and p>=P give
 M_{v,p}>=VP/H=Q.
The upper dyadic bounds v<2V and p<2P give
 M_{v,p}<4VP/H=4Q.
This proves (4).

Multiply (6) by Q^(8/3) to obtain
 P Q^(8/3)<=Q^(4-kappa),
which is (7). From (2),
 Q/P=V/H.
Therefore L<=C_LQ and (1) give
 (L/P)Q^4<=C_L(Q/P)Q^4
  =C_L(V/H)Q^4
  <=C_LQ^(4-theta),
which is (8). Adding (7) and (8), and using eta=min(kappa,theta), proves (9).

Fact d481cd487c91eb70 shows that its mean-zero discrepancy estimate implies its localized comparison estimate with exactly the left side controlled by the two-term expression in (9). Hence (9) gives the stated power saving. Finally (4) shows that every natural kernel length M_{v,p} is at most 4Q, so C_L=4 is admissible for a window of that length. No analytic estimate beyond the cited implication has been assumed.

glossary.C_L: A fixed constant bounding the short-window length by C_L Q.

b62f6ddbc641c393.title: SOURCE-SIDE RECIPROCITY, AUTOMATIC DOUBLE-RESONANCE PAYMENT, AND THE REDUCED NONRESONANT OFF-FRAME INTERFACE. Put \(e(z)=\exp(2\pi iz)\) and \(e_q(z)=e(z/q)\). Let \(x\ge3\), let \(N,m\) be positive integers, let \(R\ge1\), and let \(\mathcal P\) be a finite set of primes. Let \(\mathscr A\) be a finite set of coordinates \(\alpha=(\iota,h,u)\), where \(u\) is a positive integer, \(h\ne0\), \((Nmh,u)=1\), \((h,u)=1\), and \(0<|h|<u/2\). Assume that \(N,u\le x^{C_0}\) for a fixed \(C_0>0\). Let \(E_\alpha>0\) satisfy, for every \(\varepsilon>0\),
b62f6ddbc641c393.author: slava chan
b62f6ddbc641c393.statement:
SOURCE-SIDE RECIPROCITY, AUTOMATIC DOUBLE-RESONANCE PAYMENT, AND THE REDUCED NONRESONANT OFF-FRAME INTERFACE. Put \(e(z)=\exp(2\pi iz)\) and \(e_q(z)=e(z/q)\). Let \(x\ge3\), let \(N,m\) be positive integers, let \(R\ge1\), and let \(\mathcal P\) be a finite set of primes. Let \(\mathscr A\) be a finite set of coordinates \(\alpha=(\iota,h,u)\), where \(u\) is a positive integer, \(h\ne0\), \((Nmh,u)=1\), \((h,u)=1\), and \(0<|h|<u/2\). Assume that \(N,u\le x^{C_0}\) for a fixed \(C_0>0\). Let \(E_\alpha>0\) satisfy, for every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 \sum_{\alpha\in\mathscr A}E_\alpha\ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon R.       \tag{1}
\]
For \(a\in\mathcal P\), extend all coefficients below by zero unless
\[
 (a,mhuN)=1.                                                            \tag{2}
\]
Let \(F_{a,m,\alpha}\) be an integrable function on \(\mathbb R\), use
\[
 \widehat F_{a,m,\alpha}(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R}F_{a,m,\alpha}(t)e(-\xi t)\,dt,
\]
let \(\kappa_a(\alpha)\) be complex, and define
\[
 C_a(\alpha)=\kappa_a(\alpha)\frac{\mu(u)}u
 \widehat F_{a,m,\alpha}(h/u).                                      \tag{3}
\]
Assume, for every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 |C_a(\alpha)|\ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon E_\alpha.                \tag{4}
\]
For an ordered pair \((\alpha_1,\alpha_2)\) with
\(\alpha_i=(\iota_i,h_i,u_i)\) and
\((h_1,u_1)\ne(h_2,u_2)\), put
\[
 L_{12}=\operatorname {lcm}(u_1,u_2),\qquad
 \mathcal P_{12}=\{a\in\mathcal P:(a,L_{12})=1\},
\]
\[
 A_{12,m}\equiv Nm^{-1}
 \left(\frac{L_{12}h_1}{u_1}-\frac{L_{12}h_2}{u_2}\right)
 \pmod {L_{12}},
\]
\[
 Z_{a,m}^{12}=\mu(m)^2
 \frac{C_a(\alpha_1)\overline{C_a(\alpha_2)}}
 {\sqrt{E_{\alpha_1}E_{\alpha_2}}}.                                 \tag{5}
\]
Define the crossed frame
\[
 \mathfrak O_m=
 \sum_{\substack{\alpha_1,\alpha_2\in\mathscr A\\
 (h_1,u_1)\ne(h_2,u_2)}}
 \sum_{\substack{a,b\in\mathcal P_{12}\\a\ne b}}
 Z_{a,m}^{12}\overline{Z_{b,m}^{12}}\,
 e_{L_{12}}\!\left(A_{12,m}(a^{-1}-b^{-1})\right).                  \tag{6}
\]

Put
\[
 \Delta_{12}=h_2u_1-h_1u_2,\qquad U_{12}=u_1u_2,                    \tag{7}
\]
and
\[
 \mathcal J_{a,m}(\alpha)
 =e\!\left(\frac{Nh}{amu}\right)
 \widehat F_{a,m,\alpha}(h/u)
 =\int_{\mathbb R}F_{a,m,\alpha}(t)
 e\!\left(\frac{h(N-amt)}{amu}\right)\,dt.                          \tag{8}
\]
Then \(\Delta_{12}\ne0\), and if
\[
 \mathcal W_{a,m}^{12}
 =\mu(m)^2
 \frac{\kappa_a(\alpha_1)\overline{\kappa_a(\alpha_2)}
       \mu(u_1)\mu(u_2)}
      {u_1u_2\sqrt{E_{\alpha_1}E_{\alpha_2}}}
 \mathcal J_{a,m}(\alpha_1)
 \overline{\mathcal J_{a,m}(\alpha_2)},                             \tag{9}
\]
one has, on every nonzero supported coordinate,
\[
 \boxed{
 Z_{a,m}^{12}e_{L_{12}}(A_{12,m}a^{-1})
 =\mathcal W_{a,m}^{12}
 e_{am}\!\left(N\Delta_{12}U_{12}^{-1}\right).
 }                                                                  \tag{10}
\]
Here and below an inverse is taken modulo the subscripted modulus.

Define the prime-resonant set
\[
 \mathcal R_{12}=\{a\in\mathcal P_{12}:a\mid N\Delta_{12}\}.          \tag{11}
\]
Let \(\mathfrak O_m^{RR}\) be the sub-sum of the right side of (6), after using (10) for both \(a\) and \(b\), on which
\(a,b\in\mathcal R_{12}\) and both coefficients are nonzero, and put
\[
 \mathfrak O_m^{NR}=\mathfrak O_m-\mathfrak O_m^{RR}.                \tag{12}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{|\mathfrak O_m^{RR}|\ll_{\varepsilon,C_0}x^\varepsilon R^2.} \tag{13}
\]
Consequently the OFF-FRAME estimate
\[
 |\mathfrak O_m|\ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon R^2                  \tag{14}
\]
follows from the strictly reduced supplier
\[
 \boxed{|\mathfrak O_m^{NR}|\ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon R^2.}     \tag{NR-FRAME}
\]
Every nonzero supported summand of \(\mathfrak O_m^{NR}\) has at least one designated dilator, say \(a\), for which
\[
 e_{am}\!\left(N\Delta_{12}U_{12}^{-1}\right)
 =
 e_a\!\left(N\Delta_{12}(mU_{12})^{-1}\right)
 e_m\!\left(N\Delta_{12}(aU_{12})^{-1}\right),                       \tag{15}
\]
and the first factor in (15) is nontrivial modulo the prime \(a\). The same conclusion holds with \(b\) designated for a nonzero supported summand when \(b\notin\mathcal R_{12}\).

For the literal forward-\(E_{11}\) source, take \(u=p\ell\),
\(F_{a,m,\alpha}=F_{\iota,am,p\ell}\), and
\[
 \kappa_a(\alpha)=
 \kappa_\iota(am,h,p,\ell)\mathbf1_{(a,mhuN)=1}.                    \tag{16}
\]
Then (3) is the raw coefficient of fact 69e79ebdfba646b4 with exactly the additional clean dilator zero extension of fact 754cf92eea3a7532, and (6) is the OFF-FRAME kernel of facts 754cf92eea3a7532 and 90ee649f2811580d. All other source, frequency, prime, least-tag, marker, smooth, dyadic, squarefree and support masks remain inside \(\kappa_\iota(am,h,p,\ell)\) and \(F_{\iota,am,p\ell}\). The argument imposes neither \((m,h)=1\) nor \((m,N)=1\).

The scalar Bettin--Chandee theorem quoted in fact df9748efe29ab475 does not directly supply (NR-FRAME): it accepts one trilinear scalar sum with separated product coefficients, whereas (12) is a jointly centered second moment whose literal coefficient contains the paired factors
\(\mathcal J_{a,m}(\alpha_1)\overline{\mathcal J_{a,m}(\alpha_2)}
 \overline{\mathcal J_{b,m}(\alpha_1)}\mathcal J_{b,m}(\alpha_2)\),
the pair-dependent resonant selector, both variable prime moduli, the fixed-\(m\) factors in (15), and all provenance masks. A direct application therefore requires an additional source-specific bounded-projective separation compatible with this full signed tensor, or a vector-valued theorem that accepts it. This is an exact theorem-interface no-fit, not a lower bound for the literal source. No estimate for (NR-FRAME), \(E_{11}\) closure, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
b62f6ddbc641c393.proof:
For \((am,u)=1\), elementary additive reciprocity gives
\[
 e_u(Nh(am)^{-1})
 =e\!\left(\frac{Nh}{amu}\right)e_{am}(-Nh\,u^{-1}).                \tag{17}
\]
Multiplying (3) by (17) and using (8) yields
\[
 C_a(\alpha)e_u(Nh(am)^{-1})
 =\kappa_a(\alpha)\frac{\mu(u)}u
 \mathcal J_{a,m}(\alpha)e_{am}(-Nh\,u^{-1}).                       \tag{18}
\]
The second equality in (8) follows directly by inserting the Fourier convention:
\[
 e(Nh/(amu))\widehat F(h/u)
 =\int_{\mathbb R}F(t)e(-ht/u+Nh/(amu))\,dt.
\]

For one crossed pair, the left side of (10) is \(Z_{a,m}^{12}\) times the quotient of the two physical phases in (18). The quotient of the two modulus-\(am\) factors is
\[
 e_{am}\!\left(N(h_2u_2^{-1}-h_1u_1^{-1})\right)
 =e_{am}\!\left(N(h_2u_1-h_1u_2)(u_1u_2)^{-1}\right).
\]
The remaining coefficient is exactly (9), proving (10) on its nonzero support. Because both fractions \(h_i/u_i\) are reduced and have positive denominators, \(\Delta_{12}=0\) would imply \(h_1/u_1=h_2/u_2\), hence \((h_1,u_1)=(h_2,u_2)\), contrary to the crossed-pair hypothesis. Thus \(\Delta_{12}\ne0\).

Since \(N,u_i\le x^{C_0}\) and \(|h_i|<u_i/2\),
\[
 0<|N\Delta_{12}|<N u_1u_2\le x^{3C_0}.                            \tag{19}
\]
If a nonzero integer has \(r\) distinct prime divisors, its absolute value is at least \(2^r\). Hence
\[
 |\mathcal R_{12}|\le \log_2|N\Delta_{12}|\ll_{C_0}\log x.          \tag{20}
\]
Moreover (10) and (4), with a harmless subdivision of \(\varepsilon\), give on nonzero support
\[
 |\mathcal W_{a,m}^{12}|=|Z_{a,m}^{12}|
 \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon\sqrt{E_{\alpha_1}E_{\alpha_2}}.      \tag{21}
\]
Therefore, for each crossed coordinate pair,
\[
 \sum_{\substack{a,b\in\mathcal R_{12}\\a\ne b\\
 Z_{a,m}^{12}Z_{b,m}^{12}\ne0}}
 |\mathcal W_{a,m}^{12}\overline{\mathcal W_{b,m}^{12}}|
 \ll_{\varepsilon,C_0}x^\varepsilon E_{\alpha_1}E_{\alpha_2}.       \tag{22}
\]
All phases have modulus one. Summing (22) over the ordered crossed coordinate pairs and using (1) gives
\[
 |\mathfrak O_m^{RR}|
 \ll_{\varepsilon,C_0}x^\varepsilon
 \sum_{\alpha_1,\alpha_2}E_{\alpha_1}E_{\alpha_2}
 =x^\varepsilon\left(\sum_\alpha E_\alpha\right)^2
 \ll_{\varepsilon,C_0}x^\varepsilon R^2,
\]
after again reallocating \(\varepsilon\). This proves (13), and (12) plus the triangle inequality proves the implication from (NR-FRAME) to (14).

For (15), a nonzero supported coefficient satisfies \((a,m)=1\) by (2), and \((am,U_{12})=1\). The Chinese remainder identity for additive characters modulo \(am\) gives
\[
 e_{am}(z)=e_a(zm^{-1})e_m(za^{-1}).
\]
Take \(z\equiv N\Delta_{12}U_{12}^{-1}\pmod {am}\) to obtain (15). If \(a\notin\mathcal R_{12}\), then \(a\nmid N\Delta_{12}\); since \(mU_{12}\) is a unit modulo \(a\), the numerator in the first factor of (15) is nonzero modulo \(a\). By definition, every nonzero supported term outside the double-resonant sector has \(a\notin\mathcal R_{12}\) or \(b\notin\mathcal R_{12}\), proving the designated-phase assertion.

In the literal specialization, fact 69e79ebdfba646b4 defines
\[
 C_\iota(am;h,p,\ell)=
 \kappa_\iota(am,h,p,\ell)\mu(p\ell)(p\ell)^{-1}
 \widehat F_{\iota,am,p\ell}(h/(p\ell)).
\]
Multiplying its \(\kappa_\iota\) by the indicator in (16) gives precisely (3) with the additional clean dilator mask in equations (3)--(4) of fact 754cf92eea3a7532. Facts 754cf92eea3a7532 and 90ee649f2811580d then identify (6) with the literal OFF-FRAME kernel, including all zero extensions and provenance. The coordinate hypotheses require only that \(m,N,h\) be units modulo \(p\ell\), not that these three integers be pairwise coprime. Thus the retained \((m,h)>1\) and \((m,N)>1\) sectors remain.

Finally, the Bettin--Chandee theorem as stated and applied in fact df9748efe29ab475 has a coefficient \(\nu_s\alpha_v\beta_q\) separated over three dyadic variables in one scalar trilinear form. Expansion of (12) displays simultaneously \(a,b,\alpha_1,\alpha_2\), the four source transforms listed in the statement, the selector that depends on \(N\Delta_{12}\), and the two CRT phases. None of the present hypotheses supplies a product decomposition or a bound for its projective norm. The theorem therefore has no direct hypothesis match. This proves only the stated interface claim and no estimate for (NR-FRAME).

glossary.mathcal J_{a,m}(alpha): The Fourier transform after absorbing the exact Archimedean reciprocity factor.
glossary.mathcal R_{12}: The set of dilator primes dividing N Delta_{12}.
glossary.mathcal W_{a,m}^{12}: The source-shifted coefficient for one crossed coordinate pair and one dilator.
glossary.mathfrak O_m^{NR}: The remaining crossed-frame sector, with at least one nonresonant dilator.
glossary.mathfrak O_m^{RR}: The crossed-frame sector in which both dilators are prime-resonant.

b67d5504c8454100.title: SCOPED DIRECT-IMPORT AND EXPONENT NO-FIT FOR THE FOUVRY--KOWALSKI--MICHEL TYPE-III ESTIMATE AND THE FOUVRY--RADZIWILL/BETTIN--CHANDEE TRILINEAR ESTIMATE ON ULTRA-MU-VECTOR. Fix one strict-top source row of facts \(b0a38f5e9ae7feb6\), \(f26c5b12eea4a623\), and \(58d4898b66be0334\), and restrict it to
b67d5504c8454100.author: slava chan
b67d5504c8454100.statement:
SCOPED DIRECT-IMPORT AND EXPONENT NO-FIT FOR THE FOUVRY--KOWALSKI--MICHEL TYPE-III ESTIMATE AND THE FOUVRY--RADZIWILL/BETTIN--CHANDEE TRILINEAR ESTIMATE ON ULTRA-MU-VECTOR. Fix one strict-top source row of facts \(b0a38f5e9ae7feb6\), \(f26c5b12eea4a623\), and \(58d4898b66be0334\), and restrict it to
\[
 \max\{\beta_m,7/6\}<\beta<6/5.
\]
Let
\[
 B=Q^\beta,\qquad G=1,\qquad H_P=B/Q.
\]

First consider arXiv:1304.3199, Theorem 3.2. Grant all of the following favorable reductions: the original modulus is prime; the reciprocal phase is an admissible trace function; every source mask and nonunit obstruction is absent; a product of arithmetic variables of scale \(Q^w\), where \(0\leq w\leq\beta\), is placed in the theorem's three slots; the designated third slot has scale \(Q^u\), where \(0\leq u\leq w\); the remaining arithmetic complement of scale \(Q^{\beta-w}\) is summed absolutely; and the \(h\)-sum divided by \(H_P\) costs one. After summing the fixed-prime estimate over \(Q\) moduli, define its displayed coefficient-envelope right-hand side by
\[
 R_{\rm FKM}(w,u)
 =Q^{\beta+3/4}
  +Q^{1+\beta-u/2}
  +Q^{\beta+5/4-w/2+u/2}.                                  \tag{1}
\]
No \(0\leq u\leq w\leq\beta\) makes (1) at most \(Q^{2-\delta}\) for any fixed \(\delta>0\). Thus this direct fixed-prime type-III RHS does not supply the required ULTRA-MU-VECTOR bound even under the stated favorable grants. Independently, the cited theorem is a theorem at one prime modulus and one fixed trace function; it contains no varying squarefree/composite \(q\)-sum, no outer coefficient \(\mu(q)\), and no joint \((h,t)\) vector output. Applying it separately and then summing absolute values therefore does not preserve the supplier in fact \(58d4898b66be0334\).

Next consider arXiv:1812.00562, Lemma 2.5, equivalently arXiv:1811.08672, Lemma 2.4. Split a dyadic block \(F\leq |h|<2F\) into its two signs. On the positive half the literal phase has the exact substitution
\[
 (a,m,n)=(h,r,q),\qquad \vartheta=-\epsilon L_{\rm src},                \tag{2+}
\]
and on the negative half put \(a=-h>0\), reindex the frequency coefficient, and use
\[
 (a,m,n)=(-h,r,q),\qquad \vartheta=+\epsilon L_{\rm src}.               \tag{2-}
\]
In both cases the three theorem lengths are \(F,B,Q\), and \(r\) is the complete arithmetic variable of scale \(B\). Both substitutions retain the separated coefficient \(\mu(q)A_\rho(q)\) inside the theorem's varying denominator slot. Grant normalized coefficient envelopes
\[
 \|\alpha\|_2\leq B^{1/2}Q^{o(1)},\qquad
 \|\gamma\|_2\leq Q^{1/2}Q^{o(1)},\qquad
 \|\nu\|_2\leq F^{1/2}Q^{o(1)}.
\]
On the dominant physical block \(F=H_P=B/Q\), the exact source scale \(|L_{\rm src}|\ll Q^2\) makes
\[
 1+{|\vartheta|F\over BQ}\ll1.                             \tag{3}
\]
Define \(R_{\rm BC}\) to be the result of substituting these coefficient envelopes into the displayed Bettin--Chandee right-hand side, dividing by \(H_P\), and adding the two frequency signs. Then
\[
 \boxed{
 R_{\rm BC}
 =Q^{o(1)}
  \left(Q^{,1+19\beta/20}+Q^{\,\beta+7/8}\right).
 }                                                            \tag{4}
\]
Because \(\beta>7/6>20/19\), this displayed coefficient-class consequence is not at most \(Q^{2-\delta}\) for any fixed \(\delta>0\).

This theorem audits only the direct substitutions (2+)--(2-). If the arithmetic variable is split before applying Bettin--Chandee, a simultaneous integer lift over a finite denominator support may exist and is not audited here. This theorem is only a direct-import and displayed-RHS no-fit. It is not a lower bound for the underlying oscillatory sum. It does not exclude cancellation among projective atoms, additive reciprocity, a source-linked vector extension, a simultaneous-lift transformation, squarefree-modulus factorization, or another dispersion argument, and it proves no ULTRA-MU-VECTOR, ENDPOINT-DIAGONAL-N, post-A, or Goldbach conclusion.
b67d5504c8454100.proof:
We quote the exact estimates being audited.

Fouvry--Kowalski--Michel, arXiv:1304.3199, Theorem 3.2 has the following setup. Let \(p_0\) be a modulus prime, let \(\ell\ne p_0\) be an auxiliary coefficient prime, and let \(K\) be the trace function modulo \(p_0\) of an \(\ell\)-adic middle-extension sheaf on the affine line over \(\mathbb F_{p_0}\), pointwise of weight zero, geometrically irreducible, and not geometrically isomorphic to a tensor product of an additive Artin--Schreier sheaf and a multiplicative Kummer sheaf. For coefficient sequences of modulus at most one supported on \(1\leq |n_i|\leq N_i\), with \(p_0\nmid n_3\), it gives
\[
 \sum_{n_1,n_2,n_3}\alpha(n_1)\beta(n_2)\gamma(n_3)K(n_1n_2n_3)
 \ll
 (\log p_0)^{1/2}(N_1N_2N_3)^{1/2+\varepsilon}
 \left(
 {N_1N_2N_3\over\sqrt {p_0}}+N_1N_2+N_3\sqrt {p_0}
 \right)^{1/2}.                                               \tag{5}
\]
The implicit constant is polynomial in the conductor.

Put \(N_1N_2N_3=Q^w\), \(N_3=Q^u\), and \(p_0\asymp Q\). Ignoring \(Q^{o(1)}\), the three summands obtained from (5) are
\[
 Q^{w-1/4},\qquad Q^{w-u/2},\qquad Q^{(w+u)/2+1/4}.          \tag{6}
\]
There are \(Q\) outer moduli, and the absolutely paid complement has scale \(Q^{\beta-w}\). Multiplying (6) by \(Q^{1+\beta-w}\) gives exactly the three terms in (1).

If the second term in (1) were at most \(Q^{2-\delta}\), then
\[
 u\geq2\beta-2+2\delta.                                    \tag{7}
\]
If the third term were at most \(Q^{2-\delta}\), then
\[
 w-u\geq2\beta-3/2+2\delta.                                \tag{8}
\]
Adding (7) and (8) gives
\[
 w\geq4\beta-7/2+4\delta.                                  \tag{9}
\]
But \(w\leq\beta\). Since \(\beta>7/6\), the right side of (9) is strictly larger than \(\beta\), a contradiction. This proves the fixed-prime exponent no-fit. The fixed-prime and fixed-trace quantifiers in (5) also prove the stated structural mismatch with the varying squarefree/composite source of fact \(58d4898b66be0334\).

Fouvry--Radziwill, arXiv:1812.00562, Lemma 2.5, and arXiv:1811.08672, Lemma 2.4 state the same Bettin--Chandee estimate. For a nonzero fixed integer \(\vartheta\), arbitrary complex sequences \(\alpha(m),\gamma(n),\nu(a)\), and positive lengths \(A,M,N\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \left|\sum_{a\asymp A}\sum_{m\asymp M}\sum_{n\asymp N}
 \nu(a)\alpha(m)\gamma(n)e\!\left({\vartheta a\overline m\over n}\right)\right|
 \ll_\varepsilon&
 \|\nu\|_2\|\alpha\|_2\|\gamma\|_2
 \left(1+{|\vartheta|A\over MN}\right)^{1/2}\\
 &\times\left[
 (AMN)^{7/20+\varepsilon}(M+N)^{1/4}
 +(AMN)^{3/8+\varepsilon}(AM+AN)^{1/8}
 \right].
                                                                    \tag{10}
\end{aligned}
\]
On \(h>0\), the exact source phase gives (2+). On \(h<0\), writing \(a=-h\) changes
\[
 e_q(-\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\overline r)
 =e_q(+\epsilon L_{\rm src}a\overline r),
\]
which gives (2-). Thus each positive \(a\)-sum has the form (10), and the two halves cost only a factor two.

Take \(F=H_P=B/Q\). Then
\[
 FBQ=B^2,qquad B+Q\asymp B,qquad FB+FQ\asymp FB={B^2\over Q},
                                                                    \tag{11}
\]
because \(\beta>1\). The product of the three coefficient envelopes is
\[
 (FBQ)^{1/2}Q^{o(1)}=BQ^{o(1)}.
\]
After division by \(H_P=B/Q\), its contribution is \(Q^{1+o(1)}\). The first bracket term in (10) is
\[
 (B^2)^{7/20}B^{1/4}=B^{19/20},
\]
and the second is
\[
 (B^2)^{3/8}(B^2/Q)^{1/8}=BQ^{-1/8}.
\]
Together with (3), these identities give (4). Its first exponent exceeds two because \(\beta>20/19\), and its second exceeds two because \(\beta>9/8\). This proves the direct Bettin--Chandee displayed-RHS no-fit and completes the scoped audit.

glossary.L_src: The fixed normalized source target N/g.
glossary.N_i: The length of the i-th variable in the Fouvry--Kowalski--Michel theorem.
glossary.R_BC: The coefficient-envelope right-hand side obtained by the direct Bettin--Chandee substitution.
glossary.R_FKM(w,u): The coefficient-envelope right-hand side obtained by a direct fixed-prime Fouvry--Kowalski--Michel substitution with selected-product exponent w and third-slot exponent u.
glossary.u: The base-Q logarithmic length of the designated third Fouvry--Kowalski--Michel slot.
glossary.vartheta: The single fixed nonzero integer numerator parameter in the Bettin--Chandee phase.
glossary.w: The base-Q logarithmic length of the total arithmetic product placed in the three Fouvry--Kowalski--Michel slots.

b69e09aaac3766d9.title: TOP-B-PRECAUCHY-SOURCE-PROJECTIVE AUDIT AND MAYNARD-P5.1 NO-DIRECT-IMPORT. Fix \(0<\kappa\le1/100\), put
b69e09aaac3766d9.author: slava chan
b69e09aaac3766d9.statement:
TOP-B-PRECAUCHY-SOURCE-PROJECTIVE AUDIT AND MAYNARD-P5.1 NO-DIRECT-IMPORT. Fix \(0<\kappa\le1/100\), put
\[
 \sigma=\kappa/100,\qquad \beta_m=6/5-12\sigma/5,
\]
and let \(Q\) be sufficiently large. Fix
\[
 \beta_m\le\beta<6/5,\qquad B=Q^\beta,
\]
one exact orientation, outer-gcd layer, selected source, parent, fixed-\(U\), high and smooth/projective fibre, one top-\(B\) stopping length \(k\ge2\), one pair of dyadic stopping blocks
\[
 U\le u<2U,\qquad Y\le y<2Y,\qquad UY\asymp B,
\]
and one nonzero frequency block \(F\le|h|<2F\) with \(F\ll H_P\). Recombine, before any absolute value or Cauchy inequality, every target-gcd, prime-order/equal-cell, collision, deletion and provenance descendant belonging to this fixed top-\(B\) fibre. Put
\[
 \alpha_k(u)=
 {(-1)^k\mu(u)1_{j_{(L,Z)}(u)=0}
  \over {k+\omega_L(u)\choose k}},
 \qquad
 \gamma_k(y)=\Gamma_{k;L,S_0}(y), \tag{1}
\]
with
\[
 L=Q^{\beta-1+\sigma},\qquad
 S_0=Q^{2\beta-2+3\sigma},\qquad
 Z=Q^{3/2-\beta-3\sigma}. \tag{2}
\]
Then the recombined literal coefficient has the exact source-projective form
\[
 \mathcal T^{(k)}_{B,F}(U,Y)
 ={\omega_F\over H_P}
 \sum_{q,h,u,y}
 a_q b_h\alpha_k(u)\gamma_k(y)
 \Psi_F(q/Q,|h|/F,u/U,y/Y)
 e_q\!\left(-\mathscr A h(uy)^{-1}\right), \tag{3}
\]
where the sum has the displayed dyadic supports, both signs of \(h\),
\[
 (uy,q)=(u,y)=1,
\]
\(\mathscr A\ne0\) is the literal source target, \(a_q,b_h\) are divisor-bounded, and \(\Psi_F\) has uniformly bounded projective Fourier norm. The source, parent, fixed-\(U\), high, orientation, outer-gcd and provenance data frozen above are label scalars in (3), not deleted coordinates. The Poisson scalar obeys fixed-order decay in \(F/H_P\). In particular there is an absolutely convergent representation
\[
 \Psi_F(q/Q,|h|/F,u/U,y/Y)
 =\sum_{\rho\in\mathcal R}\eta_\rho
 A_\rho(q)B_\rho(h)C_\rho(u)D_\rho(y),\qquad
 \sum_{\rho}|\eta_\rho|\ll1, \tag{4}
\]
with uniformly bounded one-variable factors. Thus the complete pre-reciprocity source coefficient has bounded projective rank, and squaring its row produces a double projective expansion of total coefficient \(\ell^1\)-mass bounded by an absolute constant depending only on the fixed smooth family.

This low-rank conclusion does not remove the remaining spectrum. Applying the exact CRT reciprocity of fact 61cf02eb05b38a54 to each mode of (4) inserts
\[
 e_u\!\left(\mathscr A h(qy)^{-1}\right) \tag{5}
\]
into the row and, after expanding the \(y\)-energy, inserts
\[
 e_y\!\left(
 \mathscr A\Omega(q_1q_2u_1u_2)^{-1}\right),
 \qquad
 \Omega=h_1q_2u_2-h_2q_1u_1, \tag{6}
\]
with the pair-dependent selector
\[
 y\nmid\mathscr A\Omega. \tag{7}
\]
Hence bounded projective rank of (3) reduces the actual coefficient to an \(\ell^1\)-bounded double family of one-variable source modes, but every mode pair still has both the inverse-\(y\) phase modulo \(u_i\) in (5) and the inverse-\(u_i\) phase modulo \(y\) in (6). It does not prove
\[
 |V^{(\mathrm{NR})}|
 \ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon
 \left(UBQF+U^2Q^2F^2\right). \tag{TOP-B-PRECAUCHY-NR-SPEC}
\]

For comparison, Maynard, “Primes in arithmetic progressions to large moduli III: Uniform residue classes,” arXiv:2006.08250, Proposition 5.1, has the following exact parameter dependence. Let \(A_M>0\), and let \(C_M=C_M(A_M)\) be sufficiently large in terms of \(A_M\). Let
\[
 Q_0R_0=X^{1/2+\delta_M},\qquad NM\asymp X,
\]
\[
 X^{6\delta_M}(\log X)^{C_M}\le R_0
 \le X^{1/10-3\delta_M}(\log X)^{-C_M},
\]
\[
 Q_0X^{2\delta_M}(\log X)^{C_M}\le N
 \le X^{1/2-3\delta_M}(\log X)^{-C_M}.
\]
Let
\[
 |\alpha_n|\le\tau(n)^{A_M},\qquad
 |\beta_m|\le\tau(m)^{A_M},
\]
and assume that \(\alpha_n\) satisfies Maynard's Siegel--Walfisz condition: for every \(d,q\ge1\), \((a,q)=1\), and every \(A'>1\),
\[
 \left|
 \sum_{\substack{n\sim N\ n\equiv a\ (\mathrm{mod}\ q)\ (n,d)=1}}\alpha_n
 -{1\over\varphi(q)}
 \sum_{\substack{n\sim N\ (n,dq)=1}}\alpha_n
 \right|
 \ll_{A'}{N\tau(d)^{O(1)}\over(\log N)^{A'}}. \tag{8}
\]
Then
\[
 \sum_{q_0\sim Q_0}\sum_{r_0\sim R_0}
 \sup_{(a,q_0r_0)=1}
 \left|\sum_{m\sim M}\sum_{n\sim N}
 \alpha_n\beta_m
 \left(1_{nm\equiv a\ (\mathrm{mod}\ q_0r_0)}
 -{1_{(nm,q_0r_0)=1}\over\varphi(q_0r_0)}\right)\right|
 \ll_{A_M} X(\log X)^{-A_M}. \tag{9}
\]
The numerical factorized-modulus and bilinear coefficient slots in (9) can resemble possible decompositions of the scales \(Y\) and \(U\). Nevertheless (9) does not directly specialize to TOP-B-PRECAUCHY-NR-SPEC: its input is a scalar centered product-congruence discrepancy with modulus-independent sequences \(\alpha_n,\beta_m\), and its output is an \(\ell^1\) sum over factorized moduli. Equations (5)-(7) instead require a modulus-\(y\) quadratic energy, a row depending jointly on \(y,q,h,u\) through the inverse phase modulo \(u\), a second specified inverse spectrum modulo \(y\), and a pair-dependent deletion. No direct variable substitution supplies those slots or converts (9) into the required \(y\)-\(\ell^2\) output. This is only a scoped no-direct-import statement; it does not rule out adapting Maynard's proof or proving a new factorized-modulus vector-valued theorem.
b69e09aaac3766d9.proof:
Fact e58fc7c00f1683e6 applies on the displayed top sliver for every sufficiently large \(Q\). Its proof verifies
\[
 2\le L\le S_0,\qquad L<Z,\qquad n>S_0,\qquad Z^5>n
\]
for every normalized marked integer \(n\) in its dyadic support, and therefore invokes the generalized \(J=4\) terminal anatomy of fact 7c1f38cfbb8d0569. On the resulting \(B\) anatomy that fact gives exactly
\[
 \mu(n)=\sum_{k\ge2}\sum_{uy=n,(u,y)=1}
 \alpha_k(u)\gamma_k(y),
\]
with (1), and every nonzero \(y\) satisfies \(S_0<y\le S_0L\). Fixing \(k,U,Y\) gives the two one-variable arithmetic coefficients in (3), each of absolute value at most one.

Fact e58fc7c00f1683e6 first recombines the inherited marker genealogy at every fixed pre-marker source atom, restoring the literal normalized Möbius factor. It also proves that the target-gcd, order/equal-cell, collision, deletion and provenance descendants introduced after a new anatomy is formed are exact finite partitions whose recombination returns the anatomy coefficient. Therefore the recombination in the statement neither deletes nor estimates a source term. The exact outer-gcd normalization and nonzero Möbius support give \((u,y)=1\), while the reciprocal row is zero-extended unless \((uy,q)=1\).

The Poisson decomposition in fact df9748efe29ab475 gives, on a fixed source fibre, the literal reciprocal row, its Poisson prefactor, and a fixed scaled-smooth joint amplitude; its proof separates that amplitude by smooth Fourier expansion with bounded projective norm. Fact a71f777ad842c886 proves that the normalized marker changes only the normalized Möbius factor, leaving every source mask, conjugate frequency pair, target, smooth amplitude, original label, exact outer gcd and parent unchanged. The literal raised-stopping matching in fact 771d292cffc890c1 then identifies the recombined coefficient as the exact stopping factors (1) times a bounded-projective amplitude in the scaled \(q,h,u,y\) variables. That coefficient-matching argument uses the Poisson source, exact stopping formula and auxiliary recombination; the beta restriction in that theorem is used later for its analytic estimate, not for this identity.

On \(F\ll H_P\), the Archimedean reciprocity factor is also scaled-smooth. Its logarithmic phase size is
\[
 \ll {|\mathscr A|F\over Q B}
 \ll {|\mathscr A|\over QM}.
\]
In the literal forward source this is \(N/(DM)\ll1\), and in the reverse source it is \(N/(RK)\ll1\), by physical balance. All other frozen labels are scalars. Expanding the fixed-complexity smooth amplitude proves (3)-(4). Absolute convergence gives
\[
 \sum_{\rho_1,\rho_2}
 |\eta_{\rho_1}\overline{\eta_{\rho_2}}|
 =\left(\sum_\rho|\eta_\rho|\right)^2\ll1,
\]
which proves the double-projective-rank assertion.

Fact 61cf02eb05b38a54 proves the exact CRT identity. Applied to a term of (3), its modulo-\(u\) factor is (5). Multiplying two rows in the \(y\)-energy gives (6), and the unpaid sector is exactly (7). Projective separation changes only the one-variable amplitudes, not these phases or the selector. Therefore every mode pair retains the displayed specified spectrum.

Equations (8)-(9) restate Maynard's definition and Proposition 5.1, including \(A_M>0\), the dependence \(C_M=C_M(A_M)\), the coefficient bounds, and the Siegel--Walfisz hypothesis. Inspection of (9) shows that its two coefficient sequences are independent of the modulus pair \((q_0,r_0)\), its oscillatory information is encoded through one scalar residue class in a centered product congruence, and its conclusion sums absolute scalar discrepancies over moduli. By contrast (5) depends simultaneously on \(y\) and \((u,q,h)\); after squaring, (6) depends on two rows and (7) depends on the ordered pair. The requested norm is the quadratic \(y\)-energy, not the scalar modulus \(\ell^1\) norm in (9). These are missing input and output slots, so a direct specialization is not licensed.

glossary.TOP-B-PRECAUCHY-NR-SPEC: the exact remaining nonresonant cross-u energy estimate

b72acbcde165c09a.title: Let H>=2, let C and K be nonzero integers, let r_2 and r_3 be distinct primes in I_H=[H^2,2H^2), and let m>1 be odd with gcd(m,2Kr_2r_3)=1. Fix X_box>=0. Consider all even integer quadruples (a,b,c,d) satisfying |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|<=X_box and ab+cd=2K for which, on putting
b72acbcde165c09a.author: slava chan
b72acbcde165c09a.statement:
Let H>=2, let C and K be nonzero integers, let r_2 and r_3 be distinct primes in I_H=[H^2,2H^2), and let m>1 be odd with gcd(m,2Kr_2r_3)=1. Fix X_box>=0. Consider all even integer quadruples (a,b,c,d) satisfying |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|<=X_box and ab+cd=2K for which, on putting
A=br_3-dr_2, B=ar_2-cr_3, q=gcd(|A|,|B|),
D=adr_2^2-bcr_3^2, J=ab-cd,
one has q=2m, AB>0, the quotients r_1=|A|/q and r_4=|B|/q are primes in I_H pairwise distinct from each other and from r_2,r_3, gcd(C,r_1r_2r_3r_4)=1, D=2sqC for the common sign s of A,B, and J is a nonzero multiple of 2q.

For each such state, its unique unit-torus parameter t modulo m is determined by
(a,b,c,d)=(t r_2^(-1),K r_2t^(-1),t r_3^(-1),K r_3t^(-1)) modulo m,
and its recovered normal coordinate is the integer u=sJ/(4m). For a unit t and a residue nu modulo m, let Z_{t,nu} be the set of these states with that t and with u=nu modulo m. Give each state z a complex weight omega_z with |omega_z|<=1 and put
A_{t,nu}=sum_{z in Z_{t,nu}}omega_z,   B_nu=sum_{t unit modulo m}A_{t,nu}.                 (1)

For every unit t let a0(t),b0(t),c0(t),d0(t) be the canonical even representatives defined in fact 17557ebe80636618. For h=(h_a,h_b,h_c,h_d) modulo m and ell modulo m define
G_joint(h,ell)=sum_{t unit modulo m}sum_{nu modulo m}A_{t,nu}
 e_m(h_a a0(t)+h_b b0(t)+h_c c0(t)+h_d d0(t)+ell nu).                  (2)
Put
X_tor=h_a r_2^(-1)+h_c r_3^(-1),
Y_tor=K(h_b r_2+h_d r_3) modulo m,
delta_3=gcd(m,3), and
F_flat={h:Y_tor=-X_tor and X_tor=0 modulo m/delta_3}.
Then |F_flat|=delta_3m^2 and the following exact energy identities hold:
sum_{h modulo m in four slots}sum_{ell modulo m}|G_joint(h,ell)|^2
 =m^5 sum_{t,nu}|A_{t,nu}|^2,                                         (3)
sum_{h in F_flat}sum_{ell modulo m}|G_joint(h,ell)|^2
 =delta_3 m^3 sum_nu|B_nu|^2,                                         (4)
sum_{h in F_flat}|G_joint(h,0)|^2
 =delta_3 m^2 |sum_nu B_nu|^2,                                        (5)
sum_{h in F_flat}sum_{ell nonzero modulo m}|G_joint(h,ell)|^2
 =delta_3 m^2 [m sum_nu|B_nu|^2-|sum_nu B_nu|^2],                      (6)
and
sum_{h not in F_flat}sum_{ell modulo m}|G_joint(h,ell)|^2
 =m^5 sum_{t,nu}|A_{t,nu}|^2-delta_3m^3sum_nu|B_nu|^2.                 (7)

Thus the universally full-mass sector of the joint transform is F_flat times {ell=0}. The sector F_flat times {ell nonzero} has exactly the centered normal-digit energy (6), while the complement h not in F_flat contains the nonflat torus energy. These two centering operations are nested and cannot be replaced by one another.

Moreover,
|Z_{t,nu}|<=(1+X_box/m)^2
for every t,nu. If N_lift=sum_{t,nu}|Z_{t,nu}|, then
sum_{t,nu}|A_{t,nu}|^2<=(1+X_box/m)^2N_lift,                           (8)
and the left side of (3) is at most
m^5(1+X_box/m)^2N_lift.                                                (9)
In particular, when X_box<=LH^3 and m>=H^3, the multiplicity factor in (8)-(9) is at most (1+L)^2. The identities do not themselves give cancellation after summing over m,r_2,r_3 or the remaining packet variables.
b72acbcde165c09a.proof:
The existence and uniqueness of t, and the recovery formula u=sJ/(4m), follow from facts 17557ebe80636618 and a8324506c253b8f4 under the displayed normalized-state conditions. The sets Z_{t,nu} are therefore a disjoint refinement of the fibres Z_t in fact a8324506c253b8f4.

Expand the squared absolute value in (3). Summation over ell modulo m is zero unless nu=nu' and is then m. Summation over all four independent components of h is zero unless the residue quadruples
(a0(t),b0(t),c0(t),d0(t)) and (a0(t'),b0(t'),c0(t'),d0(t'))
are equal modulo m, and is then m^4. Equality of the first components gives
t r_2^(-1)=t' r_2^(-1) modulo m, hence t=t'. Therefore only identical pairs (t,nu) survive, proving (3).

Fact a8324506c253b8f4 proves that F_flat has delta_3m^2 elements and that for every h in F_flat the torus phase
h_a a0(t)+h_b b0(t)+h_c c0(t)+h_d d0(t)
vanishes modulo m for every unit t. Consequently, for h in F_flat,
G_joint(h,ell)=sum_nu B_nu e_m(ell nu),                                (10)
independently of h. Parseval in ell gives
sum_ell|sum_nuB_nu e_m(ell nu)|^2=m sum_nu|B_nu|^2.
Multiplication by |F_flat|=delta_3m^2 proves (4). At ell=0, (10) is sum_nuB_nu; multiplication by |F_flat| proves (5). Subtracting (5) from (4) proves (6). Subtracting (4) from the total identity (3) proves (7).

The simultaneous phase in (2) is identically one for all possible t and nu precisely when the torus h-phase is identically one and ell=0. The former universal condition is h in F_flat by fact a8324506c253b8f4, while variation over all nu forces ell=0. This proves the stated universal full-mass description. Formula (6) is exactly additive Parseval after removal of ell=0, so it is the centered digit energy; (7) is exactly the complementary torus energy.

Because Z_{t,nu} is a subset of Z_t, the multiplicity bound in fact a8324506c253b8f4 gives
|Z_{t,nu}|<=|Z_t|<=(1+X_box/m)^2.
By Cauchy--Schwarz and |omega_z|<=1,
|A_{t,nu}|^2<=|Z_{t,nu}| sum_{z in Z_{t,nu}}|omega_z|^2
 <=(1+X_box/m)^2|Z_{t,nu}|.
Summing proves (8), and inserting (8) into (3) proves (9). The last scale specialization is immediate.

glossary.B_nu: the sum of A_{t,nu} over unit torus parameters t
glossary.Z_{t,nu}: the normalized-state fibre with torus parameter t and recovered normal digit congruent to nu modulo m

b76df03232475208.title: PRIME SMALL-v WIENER-NORM OBSTRUCTION TO THE NAIVE COMMON-OUTPUT FOURIER SEPARATION. Let p be an odd prime and let C be a nonzero residue modulo p. On F_p define f_C(q)=0 for q=0 and f_C(q)=e_p(Cq^{-1}) for q nonzero, and define fhat_C(s)=p^{-1}sum_{q in F_p}f_C(q)e_p(-sq). Then
b76df03232475208.author: slava chan
b76df03232475208.statement:
PRIME SMALL-v WIENER-NORM OBSTRUCTION TO THE NAIVE COMMON-OUTPUT FOURIER SEPARATION. Let p be an odd prime and let C be a nonzero residue modulo p. On F_p define f_C(q)=0 for q=0 and f_C(q)=e_p(Cq^{-1}) for q nonzero, and define fhat_C(s)=p^{-1}sum_{q in F_p}f_C(q)e_p(-sq). Then

 (p-1)/(2sqrt(p)) <= sum_{s in F_p}|fhat_C(s)| <= sqrt(p-1).          (1)

In particular, because additive Fourier coefficients are unique, every exact expansion

 f_C(q)=sum_{s in F_p}b_s e_p(sq)                                  (2)

has additive-character projective cost sum_s|b_s| comparable to sqrt(p), with the explicit bounds in (1).

For the exact literal coefficient D_{j,r}(q) of fact 3330e83b6d253b69, suppose its small cofactor is v_j=p and gcd(Ah_jd_j,p)=1. After zero extension away from the literal unit support gcd(q,p)=1, its small-v_j CRT factor is

 1_{q nonzero mod p} e_p(Ah_j(qd_j)^{-1})=f_C(q),
 C congruent Ah_j d_j^{-1} mod p.                                  (3)

Thus exporting this factor by an exact additive q-Fourier expansion before the fixed-r argument incurs a sqrt(p) coefficient l1 tax. Consequently the already verified smooth projective separation does not, by itself, turn the exact W_{j,r} into a scalar common-output coefficient at subpolynomial cost. This is a scoped no-fit for the additive-character separation of the small-v factor. It does not rule out retaining (v,s) in an l2 coefficient slot, a non-Fourier decomposition coupling several v, or a source-specific estimate acting directly on W_{j,r}; it proves no C4 bound or Goldbach conclusion.
b76df03232475208.proof:
Accepted fact 4f9aec67f5be35db applies to f_C and gives

 fhat_C(0)=-1/p,                                                     (4)
 max_{s in F_p}|fhat_C(s)|<=2/sqrt(p),                              (5)
 sum_{s in F_p}|fhat_C(s)|^2=(p-1)/p.                               (6)

The value in (4) also satisfies 1/p<=2/sqrt(p), so (5) holds for every s. For any finite sequence (u_s), sum_s|u_s|^2 <=(max_s|u_s|)sum_s|u_s|. Apply this with u_s=fhat_C(s), then use (5)-(6):

 sum_s|fhat_C(s)| >= [(p-1)/p]/[2/sqrt(p)]
                   =(p-1)/(2sqrt(p)).                               (7)

Cauchy's inequality and (6) give

 sum_s|fhat_C(s)|
 <=sqrt(p)(sum_s|fhat_C(s)|^2)^{1/2}
 =sqrt(p-1).                                                         (8)

Normalized finite Fourier inversion says f_C(q)=sum_s fhat_C(s)e_p(sq), and the characters e_p(sq) form a basis of the functions on F_p. Hence the coefficients in (2) are uniquely b_s=fhat_C(s). Equations (7)-(8) prove (1) and the asserted projective cost.

Under the literal specialization, v_j=p and gcd(Ah_jd_j,p)=1 make C=Ah_jd_j^{-1} a nonzero residue. For a supported q, gcd(q,p)=1 and (qd_j)^{-1}=q^{-1}d_j^{-1} modulo p, so the phase equals e_p(Cq^{-1}); for unsupported q the literal coefficient is zero. This proves (3). Therefore an additive-character export of that literal factor has exactly the cost already computed. Fact 0d53c27d174b26ed gives a subpolynomial projective separation only for the smooth physical kernel; it does not remove the arithmetic factor (3). The final limitations distinguish the rejected additive-Fourier shortcut from the still-open exact-W and l2-vector routes.

glossary.additive-character projective cost: The l1 norm of the unique coefficients in an exact expansion into additive characters of the output variable.
glossary.fhat_C: The normalized additive Fourier transform of the zero-extended inverse phase f_C.

b7fcb27a091203e5.title: Let mu be the Moebius function and let Lambda be the von Mangoldt function, with Lambda(1)=0 and, for every integer q>1, Lambda(q)=log p if q=p^j for a prime p and an integer j>=1, and Lambda(q)=0 otherwise. For every integer q>=1 define S(q)=sum_{r k=q} mu(r) log k, where r and k range over positive integers. Then S(q)=Lambda(q)
b7fcb27a091203e5.author: slava chan
b7fcb27a091203e5.statement:
Let mu be the Moebius function and let Lambda be the von Mangoldt function, with Lambda(1)=0 and, for every integer q>1, Lambda(q)=log p if q=p^j for a prime p and an integer j>=1, and Lambda(q)=0 otherwise. For every integer q>=1 define S(q)=sum_{r k=q} mu(r) log k, where r and k range over positive integers. Then S(q)=Lambda(q).

More precisely, if Lambda(q) is nonzero, write q=p^j with p prime and j>=1. If j=1, the only nonzero summand in S(q) is the r=1 summand, whose value is log p; the r=p summand is zero. If j>=2, the only nonzero summands are those with r=1 and r=p, and their values are respectively j log p and -(j-1)log p. In both cases every nonzero summand has r in {1,p} and r<=sqrt(q).

Consequently, if q>1, r k=q, mu(r)log k is nonzero, and r>sqrt(q), then q is a composite integer which is not a prime power and S(q)=Lambda(q)=0. In particular, putting Q=sqrt(q), the interval [Q^(4/3),Q^(3/2)] contains no r indexing a direct nonzero sibling of any q with nonzero Lambda(q). Every nonzero sibling occurring there belongs to a composite q whose complete sibling sum is zero. Hence direct localization of genuine von-Mangoldt mass to this endpoint by divisor support alone is impossible. This conclusion does not preclude an analytic one-sided estimate after the complementary zero-sum composite families have been recombined or bounded.

As an explicit three-region corollary, let ell and p be distinct primes with p>ell^3, put q=p ell and Q=sqrt(q), and partition the divisor indices into r<Q^(1/2), Q^(1/2)<=r<=Q^(3/2), and r>Q^(3/2). Then
sum_{r k=q, r<Q^(1/2)} mu(r)log k=log ell,
sum_{r k=q, Q^(1/2)<=r<=Q^(3/2)} mu(r)log k=0,
and
sum_{r k=q, r>Q^(3/2)} mu(r)log k=-log ell.
In particular the finer interval [Q^(4/3),Q^(3/2)] has sum zero. There are infinitely many distinct semiprimes q with this property; indeed, for every prime ell, one may choose a prime p satisfying ell^3<p<2ell^3.
b7fcb27a091203e5.proof: First suppose q=1. The only factorization r k=1 has r=k=1, so S(1)=mu(1)log(1)=0=Lambda(1). Now suppose q>1. Since k=q/r in every factorization, and since mu(r)=0 unless r is squarefree, S(q)=sum_{r|q}mu(r)(log q-log r). The squarefree divisors of q are the divisors of rad(q). Therefore sum_{r|q}mu(r)=product_{a|q, a prime}(1-1)=0, because q has at least one prime divisor. Hence S(q)=-sum_{r|q}mu(r)log r =-sum_{a|q, a prime}(log a) sum_{r|q, a|r}mu(r). (1) Fix a prime a dividing q. Every squarefree r dividing q and divisible by a has a unique expression r=a s, where s divides rad(q)/a, and mu(a s)=-mu(s). It follows that sum_{r|q, a|r}mu(r)=-sum_{s|rad(q)/a}mu(s). For every positive integer n, sum_{s|n}mu(s) equals 1 when n=1 and 0 when n>1: if n has distinct prime divisors a_1,...,a_t, the sum is product_{i=1}^t(1-1), with the empty product equal to 1. Thus the inner sum in (1) equals -1 exactly when a is the only distinct prime divisor of q, and equals 0 otherwise. If q has at least two distinct prime divisors, (1) gives S(q)=0. If q=p^j for a unique prime p and j>=1, (1) gives S(q)=log p. This is exactly S(q)=Lambda(q). Assume q=p^j. Its divisors are p^h for 0<=h<=j. The Moebius value is nonzero only for h=0 and h=1. The h=0 term, namely r=1 and k=p^j, is j log p. The h=1 term, namely r=p and k=p^(j-1), is -(j-1)log p. When j=1 the latter value is zero, and when j>=2 it is nonzero. Every h>=2 term vanishes because mu(p^h)=0. If j=1, the only nonzero index r=1 satisfies r<=sqrt(q). If j>=2, both possible indices satisfy 1<=sqrt(q) and p<=p^(j/2)=sqrt(q). This proves the detailed support assertion. Suppose now that q>1 and a nonzero sibling mu(r)log k has r>sqrt(q). If Lambda(q) were nonzero, the preceding support assertion would give r<=sqrt(q), a contradiction. Hence Lambda(q)=0. The sibling is nonzero, so k>1 and r>=2; consequently q=r k is composite. Since Lambda vanishes at q>1 exactly when q is not a prime power, q is a composite non-prime-power and the already proved identity gives S(q)=0. If Q=sqrt(q)>1, then Q^(4/3)>Q=sqrt(q), so every r in [Q^(4/3),Q^(3/2)] lies in the just-treated endpoint r>sqrt(q). The scoped localization conclusion follows: support in that region never directly carries a nonzero complete coefficient Lambda(q), although an inequality may still use analytically controlled sums of the zero-total composite families. For the three-region corollary, the four divisors of q=p ell are 1, ell, p, and q. Their sibling values are respectively log(p ell), -log p, -log ell, and 0. The hypothesis p>ell^3 implies ellQ^(3/2), because p>Q^(3/2) is equivalent after taking fourth powers to p^4>p^3 ell^3, again equivalent to p>ell^3. Finally 1Q^(3/2). Hence the first region contains exactly r=1,ell and its sum is log(p ell)-log p=log ell; the middle region contains no divisor and has sum zero; the third region contains exactly r=p,q and its sum is -log ell+0=-log ell. The finer interval is contained in the middle region. For infinitude, use the following published prime-in-interval theorem: for every integer n>3 there exists a prime p with nell^3 and p is distinct from ell. There are infinitely many primes ell: if only ell_1,...,ell_t existed, any prime divisor of ell_1...ell_t+1 would be absent from the list. Moreover p>ell, so ell is the smaller prime factor of q=p ell; unique prime factorization shows that different ell give different q. This proves the infinite-family assertion.

glossary.Q: the positive scale sqrt(q) in the endpoint and semiprime corollaries
glossary.S(q): the complete divisor-sibling sum sum_{r k=q} mu(r) log k

b91a6d12020b5415.title: SELF-CONTAINED PHASE-ALIGNMENT NO-GO FOR AN ARBITRARY-COEFFICIENT NONRESONANT DILATOR MOMENT
b91a6d12020b5415.author: slava chan
b91a6d12020b5415.statement:
SELF-CONTAINED PHASE-ALIGNMENT NO-GO FOR AN ARBITRARY-COEFFICIENT NONRESONANT DILATOR MOMENT.

]
Let (Q) tend to infinity and define
[

such that

every prime divisor of (d) is at least (Z), and (c_n(q,h)) is an arbitrary complex number of modulus at most one, allowed to depend jointly on (n,q,h), supported on
[
 Q<q<2Q,quad q {m prime},qquad
 F<h<2F,quad hinmathbb Z,qquad (q,n)=1.
]
For a finite family (mathcal R) of admissible rows define
[
 K(n)=sum_{q,h}c_n(q,h)e_q(-hn^{-1}),qquad
 mathcal M(mathcal R)=sum_{(n,d,v;c_n)inmathcal R}|K(n)|^2. 	ag{1}
]
In the TT-star expansion of (1), put
[
 Delta=h_1q_2-h_2q_1
]
and define (mathcal M_{m NR}(mathcal R)) to be the sum of the expanded terms satisfying
[
 Delta

]

There exists a family (mathcal R) of admissible rows for which
[
 mathcal M(mathcal R)
 gg {B^3over(log B)(log Q)^2},                            	ag{3}
]
[
 |mathcal M_{m NR}(mathcal R)|
 gg {B^3over(log B)(log Q)^2}.                            	ag{4}
]
Consequently neither (mathcal M) nor (mathcal M_{m NR}) satisfies, uniformly over all admissible arbitrary coefficient arrays, the candidate estimate
[
 ll_arepsilon
 Q^arepsilonleft(BQF+{BQ^2F^2over D}ight)              	ag{5}
]
for every (arepsilon>0). Indeed the expression in parentheses in (5) equals (2B^2).

Thus squarefree divisor geometry, a complete rough dilator, the lower bound (dgg H_T^2Q^{3sigma}), unit-size coefficients and pair-dependent nonresonance do not by themselves imply the desired moment. Any valid theorem of this scale must impose additional coefficient structure, such as the literal source-specific Poisson coefficients.
b91a6d12020b5415.proof:
Let (mathcal R) contain one row for every prime (n) in ((alpha B,gamma B)), and put
[
 d=n,qquad v=1,qquad c_n(q,h)=e_q(hn^{-1})
]
on the displayed (q,h)-support.

We verify every admissibility condition. A prime (n) is squarefree, (d=n), (v=1), and ((d,v)=1). Since (D=B) and (1<alpha<gamma<2), one has (D<d<2D). Also (v=1le S_0). Because
[
  eta-(3/2- eta-3sigma)
 =2 eta-3/2+3sigma>0,
]
the prime (d=nasymp B) exceeds (Z) for sufficiently large (Q). Moreover
[
 {dover H_T^2Q^{3sigma}}
 asymp Q^{2- eta-3sigma}longrightarrowinfty.
]
Finally ( eta>1), so (n>2Q) for sufficiently large (Q); hence every chosen prime (qasymp Q) is coprime to (n). The coefficients have modulus one and the permitted joint dependence.

For every supported pair ((q,h)),
[
 c_n(q,h)e_q(-hn^{-1})=1.
]
Thus (K(n)) equals the number of supported pairs. Fact (bc99edbd6281b83b) records the prime-number-theorem consequence that a fixed interior dyadic interval ((aX,bX)) contains
[
 [b-a+o(1)]X/log X
]
primes. Applied at (X=B) and (X=Q), this gives (gg B/log B) rows and (gg Q/log Q) allowed (q)'s. The (h)-interval contains (gg F) integers because (F=Q^{ eta-1}) tends to infinity. Hence
[
 |K(n)|gg QF/log Q
]
on every row, proving (3).

We next remove the two complementary TT-star sectors by direct counting. For (Delta=0), write uniquely
[
 q_i=k_iq_0,qquad h_i=k_ih_0,qquad (q_0,h_0)=1.
]
Dyadic support makes (k_1,k_2) comparable. On (k_iasymp K), there are (O(K^2)) multiplier pairs and (O((Q/K)(F/K))) primitive pairs. Therefore there are (O(QF)) proportional pairs per dyadic (K), and (O(QFlog(2B))) in total. Multiplying by (O(B/log B)) rows, the absolute (Delta=0) sector is
[

]

Now fix a coordinate pair with (Delta
e0). The support gives
[
 |Delta|le C QF=CB
]
for an absolute constant (C). If its row is fully resonant, then the row prime (n>alpha B) divides (Delta). A nonzero integer of modulus at most (CB) has (O_{C,alpha}(1)) prime divisors exceeding (alpha B): if it had (r) distinct such divisors, their product would be at least ((alpha B)^r) and at most (CB). Thus each of the (O(Q^2F^2)=O(B^2)) coordinate pairs contributes to only (O(1)) fully resonant rows. The absolute sector with (Delta
e0) and (dmidDelta) is therefore (O(B^2)).

The TT-star terms are partitioned exactly into (Delta=0), nonzero (dmidDelta), and the nonresonant set (2). By the triangle inequality,
[
 |mathcal M_{m NR}|

]
The lower bound (3) dominates this error, proving (4). Finally (QF=B) and (D=B), so

 BQF+BQ^2F^2/D=2B^2.
]
The quotient of (3) or (4) by (2B^2) is a positive power of (Q) up to logarithms. Choosing any sufficiently small fixed (arepsilon>0) proves failure of (5).

b93c84ae1cba3363.title: VARYING-SELECTED-PRIME SCALAR ASSEMBLY OF THE ACTUAL C1 PAIR AND SAME-PRIME DELETION PAYMENTS. Adopt the strict-top C1 scale B and the actual row profiles of facts ff228b0e569531f8 and 71f1a10b52148348. Let P be any set of selected C1 primes satisfying Z<=p<=2Q^(6/5), where Z>=Q^zeta, and for each p let J_p be the actual natural-cofactor support
b93c84ae1cba3363.author: slava chan
b93c84ae1cba3363.statement:
VARYING-SELECTED-PRIME SCALAR ASSEMBLY OF THE ACTUAL C1 PAIR AND SAME-PRIME DELETION PAYMENTS. Adopt the strict-top C1 scale B and the actual row profiles of facts ff228b0e569531f8 and 71f1a10b52148348. Let P be any set of selected C1 primes satisfying Z<=p<=2Q^(6/5), where Z>=Q^zeta, and for each p let J_p be the actual natural-cofactor support
J_p={t in Z: B/2<=pt<=2B, p does not divide t, and the fixed C1 source labels are supported}.
Put L_p=#J_p. Every nonempty J_p has p<=2B and L_p<=4B/p.

Fix one signed physical height block H<=|h|<2H. Let P_p be the complete actual scalar two-row C1 q-pair sum at selected prime p, summed over both supported h,t rows in this block and over all row modes, with its exact first-p determinant mask and with no additional non-row-factorable q-dependent mask. Let S_p be the corresponding actual four-row same-p sum of fact 4833384bb6a7419e, including its two pair masks and exact cross-pair nonexceptional deletion. Let delta_2 be as in that fact and let omega be any exponent allowed there. Then
sum_{p in P}|P_p| << Q^(2-delta_2+o(1))(1+H/H_P)^(-2A)H^2 B^2 Z^(-1),
and
sum_{p in P}|S_p| << Q^(4-omega+o(1))(1+H/H_P)^(-4A)H^4 B^4 Z^(-3).
Consequently the complete varying-prime tensor with no extra cross-prime q-coupling,
S_var =sum_{p!=p' in P} P_p conjugate(P_{p'}) +sum_{p in P} S_p,
satisfies
|S_var| << Q^(4-2delta_2+o(1))(1+H/H_P)^(-4A)H^4B^4Z^(-2)
       +Q^(4-omega+o(1))(1+H/H_P)^(-4A)H^4B^4Z^(-3).
Thus varying selected C1 primes and their complete short/long cofactor supports cause no prime-cardinality loss in this scalar assembly. This theorem does not identify S_var with a larger upstream Hilbert/completion object, nor does it control an additional non-row-factorable mask coupling a p-pair to a distinct p'-pair.
b93c84ae1cba3363.proof:
For a nonempty cofactor fibre, p t lies in [B/2,2B], so p<=2B. The number of integers t in this interval is at most 2B/p+1. Since p<=2B implies 1<=2B/p, this is at most 4B/p. Deleting unsupported t and the possible multiples of p can only decrease the cardinality, proving L_p<=4B/p.

The pairwise case analysis in the proof of fact 4833384bb6a7419e applies before the four-row formation. If both heights vanish modulo p the pair mask is zero; if exactly one does, fact c23ca78883ba83d9 saves Q^(-delta_0) on the nonzero row; if neither does, fact a8d14bd3414bf66e saves Q^(-delta_1) on the pair. Hence, with delta_2=min(delta_0,delta_1), summing the actual bounded-variation mode mass, the O(H^2) physical height pairs, and the L_p^2 cofactor pairs gives
|P_p|<<Q^(2-delta_2+o(1))(1+H/H_P)^(-2A)H^2L_p^2.             (1)
Fact 4833384bb6a7419e directly gives
|S_p|<<Q^(4-omega+o(1))(1+H/H_P)^(-4A)H^4L_p^4.               (2)

No prime-number theorem is needed. Since P is contained in the integers at least Z,
sum_{p in P}L_p^2 <=16B^2 sum_{m>=Z}m^(-2)<<B^2/Z,
and
sum_{p in P}L_p^4 <=256B^4 sum_{m>=Z}m^(-4)<<B^4/Z^3.         (3)
Summing (1) and (2) and using (3) proves the first two estimates.

For the distinct-prime tensor, finite Fubini gives exactly P_p conjugate(P_{p'}) because the hypothesis excludes any additional cross-prime q-dependent coupling. Therefore
|sum_{p!=p'}P_p conjugate(P_{p'})| <=(sum_p|P_p|)^2.
Insert the first estimate. Add the same-prime deleted contribution using the second estimate. This proves the displayed bound for S_var and every scope statement.
