glossary.P: The finite set of selected C1 primes in the fixed strict-top source block.
glossary.P_p: The complete actual two-row C1 scalar pair aggregate at fixed p over one height block and the full cofactor fibre.
glossary.S_p: The fixed-p deletion-aware four-row C1 aggregate supplied by fact 4833384bb6a7419e.
glossary.S_var: The scalar varying-prime tensor formed from distinct-prime pair products and the same-prime deletion-aware terms.

b9560e346963b9e0.title: EXACT COMMON-SHORT NORMAL FORM AND THE LITERAL CROSS-INCIDENCE VECTOR LARGE-SIEVE TARGET
b9560e346963b9e0.author: slava chan
b9560e346963b9e0.statement:
EXACT COMMON-SHORT NORMAL FORM AND THE LITERAL CROSS-INCIDENCE VECTOR LARGE-SIEVE TARGET.

Fix 0<eta<1/12. Let Q>8 tend to infinity, put
 U=Q^(1/3), B=Q^(4/3+o(1)), F_0=Q^(1-2eta+o(1)),            (1)
and let cal B={b:B<=b<2B, b squarefree}. Let N be positive, let w_n be arbitrary complex numbers supported on Q<=n<2Q, and let
 sum_{b in cal B}|gamma_b|^2=1.                             (2)
For tau in {ss,ll}, extend the following coefficients by zero unless Q<=au<2Q:
 beta_{ss,a}(u)
  =mu(a)w_{au}sum_{m|u;m<=U}mu(m), 1<=a<=U,                (3)
 beta_{ll,a}(u)
  =w_{au}sum_{dm=u;U<d<=m}kappa(d,m)mu(d)mu(m), 1<=a<2U,   (4)
where kappa(d,m)=1 for d=m and kappa(d,m)=2 for d<m.

For b in cal B put
 L_b=product_{r|b;b/r<F_0}r.                                (5)
Let cal R consist of b with L_b>1 and (L_b,N)=1. For b in cal R let pi(b) be the largest prime divisor of L_b and put s(b)=b/pi(b). Let
 cal D={(b_1,b_2) in cal R^2:pi(b_1)|s(b_2)}.               (6)
For a pair in cal D put
 p=pi(b_1), p_2=pi(b_2), s_1=b_1/p, s_2=b_2/p_2,
 q_2=b_2/p.                                                 (7)
Then p!=p_2, p|s_2, s_i<F_0, p does not divide N, and q_2<2F_0.

For squarefree q, h|q, target M and (n,q)=1 define
 R^M_{q,h}(n)
  =product_{r|h}[e_r(M[n(q/r)]^(-1))+1/(r-1)],              (8)
 I^M_{q;(Y_0,Y_1]}(n)
  =sum_{h|q;Y_0<h<=Y_1;(h,M)=1}
    c_{q/h}(M)R^M_{q,h}(n)/phi(q/h),                        (9)
with I^1_{1;(Y_0,Y_1]}=1_{Y_0<1<=Y_1}. Let M_1 satisfy
 pM_1 congruent N (mod s_1), with M_1=1 if s_1=1, and let
 pM_{12} congruent N (mod q_2).                              (10)
For supported a,u_1,u_2 put
 C_1=I^{M_1}_{s_1;(F_0/p,s_1]}(au_1),                       (11)
 J_2=I^{M_{12}}_{q_2;(F_0/p,F_0]}(au_2),                    (12)
 H_2=1_{q_2>F_0}1_{(q_2,M_{12})=1}
      R^{M_{12}}_{q_2,q_2}(au_2),                           (13)
and, modulo p,
 A=N[u_1s_1]^(-1), D=N[u_2q_2]^(-1).                        (14)
These residues are nonzero when
 (au_1,b_1)=(au_2,b_2)=1.

For nonzero C,a modulo p put
 r_{p,C}(a)=e_p(Ca^(-1))+1/(p-1).                           (15)
Put rho_p(H;a)=e_p(Ha^(-1))+1/(p-1) for H nonzero, and
 rho_p(0;a)=0, and put
 G_p(A,D)=p/(p-1){1_{A=D}-1/(p-1)}.                         (16)

Define
 K_inc
 =sum_{tau}sum_asum_{u_1,u_2}
  sum_{substack{(b_1,b_2) in cal D\
       (au_1,b_1)=(au_2,b_2)=1}}
  beta_{tau,a}(u_1)overline(beta_{tau,a}(u_2))
  overline(gamma_{b_1})gamma_{b_2}
  P_{b_1}(au_1)overline(P_{b_2}(au_2)),                     (17)
where
 P_b(n)=sum_{f|b;f>F_0;(f,N)=1}
        c_{b/f}(N)R^N_{b,f}(n)/phi(b/f),                    (18)
and a has the range in (3) or (4).

Define K_inc^main by replacing the final product in each summand of (17) by
 C_1[
  e_p((A-D)a^(-1))overline(H_2)
  +1_{A!=D}rho_p(A-D;a)overline(J_2)],                      (19)
and K_inc^rem by replacing it by
 C_1[
  1/(p-1)e_p(-Da^(-1))overline(H_2)
  +{G_p(A,D)+1/(p-1)rho_p(A;a)+1/(p-1)rho_p(-D;a)}
    overline(J_2)].                                         (20)
Then exactly
 K_inc=K_inc^main+K_inc^rem.                                 (21)
Thus every coefficient-one local oscillation in this directed cross-incidence cell is in (19). Both faces retain the same literal beta coefficient, the same gamma coefficient, the full row-one shifted projector C_1, and respectively the complete full-conductor tensor H_2 or the literal boundary J_2.

The literal cross-incidence vector large-sieve target is: for some fixed 0<omega<1/3,
 |K_inc^main|<<Q^(7/3-omega).                               (LIT-INC-VLS)
This bound is not asserted. It is a target only for the displayed literal arrays, not for arbitrary bounded a-dependent periodic functions.

There is an exact recursive dichotomy for its p-free interval tensors. Put
 L_1=L(s_1,F_0/p), L_2=L(q_2,F_0/p),                        (22)
where L(q,Y)=product_{r|q;q/r<=Y}r. If (L_1,M_1)>1 then C_1=0; otherwise C_1 factors as the product of at most two L_1-local centered traces and an interval projector on a Q^(1/3+2eta+o(1))-smooth no-compulsory-prime residual, retaining both divided endpoints. If (L_2,M_{12})>1 then J_2=0; otherwise J_2 has the analogous factorization with at most two L_2-local traces and both boundary endpoints retained. The full response H_2, when nonzero, splits into its prime factors above and below the same rough threshold, with at most two primes above it. Therefore every nonzero unresolved modulation in LIT-INC-VLS is a rank-at-most-two rough tensor coupled to its literal smooth residual.

No estimate for either part of (21), any other incidence cell, TRI-CROSS, ROP, CEN-MZB, C_small or Goldbach is asserted.
b9560e346963b9e0.proof:
Collapse the exact Vaughan fibres in fact 09416be97c36d374. In its small-small fibre fix d=a and put u=lm; summing over m|u, m<=U gives (3). In its long-long fibre fix l=a and put u=dm; the ordered restriction and symmetry multiplicity give (4). Thus expanding its K_tri square gives the beta products in (17), while expanding P_gamma(au_1)overline(P_gamma(au_2)) gives overline(gamma_{b_1})gamma_{b_2} and the projector product. Restricting that finite ordered sum to cal D is exactly (17).

For b in cal R, b/pi(b)<F_0 and pi(b) does not divide N. If p=pi(b_1) equalled p_2=pi(b_2), squarefreeness would contradict p|s(b_2). Hence p!=p_2 and p|s_2. Also s_i<F_0. From b_1>=B and s_1<F_0, p>B/F_0, whence
 q_2=b_2/p<2B/(B/F_0)=2F_0.
This proves the geometry after (7).

For a supported term n_i=au_i. Its row-one p-factor is r_{p,A}(a). Facts 2234aaf28e165b88 and 77b42a63e0f65307 give exactly
 P_{b_1}(au_1)=r_{p,A}(a)C_1,                               (23)
 P_{b_2}(au_2)=e_p(Da^(-1))H_2+r_{p,D}(a)J_2.              (24)
The leading local product is
 r_{p,A}(a)e_p(-Da^(-1))
 =e_p((A-D)a^(-1))+1/(p-1)e_p(-Da^(-1)).                   (25)
Since p>B/F_0 tends to infinity, p>3 for large Q. Fact 5e021455b7c48b01 gives
 r_{p,A}(a)overline(r_{p,D}(a))
 =G_p(A,D)+1_{A!=D}rho_p(A-D;a)
  +1/(p-1)rho_p(A;a)+1/(p-1)rho_p(-D;a).                   (26)
Insert (25)-(26) into (23) times the conjugate of (24). The coefficient-one terms are (19), and the remaining terms are (20). Summing with the same beta-gamma coefficient proves (21). Fact 09416be97c36d374 supplies the Q^(7/3-omega) TRI-CROSS scale, but no estimate is inferred.

Apply fact bf123016427a4eab to C_1 with q=s_1 and to J_2 with q=q_2. It gives exactly the two zero branches stated after (22). In each nonzero branch it gives the asserted factorization, endpoint retention and smooth residual. Here q/(F_0/p)=b_i/F_0=Q^(1/3+2eta+o(1)) and q<2F_0, so its actual-scale conclusion gives at most two rough factors. For H_2, nonvanishing includes (q_2,M_{12})=1. Partition the product (13) at the same threshold. Three primes above it would have product at least Q^(1+6eta+o(1)), larger than q_2<2F_0=Q^(1-2eta+o(1)); hence there are at most two. This proves the exact dichotomy and all scope restrictions.

glossary.K_inc: the cal D-restricted portion of the exact expanded short-fibre square
glossary.K_inc^main: the coefficient-one full-conductor and off-diagonal boundary faces
glossary.LIT-INC-VLS: the literal Q^(7/3-omega) target for K_inc^main
glossary.L_1: the maximal rough factor of the row-one shifted interval projector
glossary.L_2: the maximal rough factor of the row-two boundary interval projector
glossary.beta_{tau,a}(u): the exact product-coupled Vaughan coefficient after collapsing n=au in one common short fibre
glossary.cal D: the directed cross-incidence pairs for which pi(b_1) divides the complement of pi(b_2)
glossary.pi(b): the largest prime divisor of the canonical compulsory factor L_b

bab04e002177e282.title: COMPULSORY ROUGH-PRIME FACTORIZATION OF THE COMPLETE HIGH-CONDUCTOR CENTERED PROJECTOR
bab04e002177e282.author: slava chan
bab04e002177e282.statement:
COMPULSORY ROUGH-PRIME FACTORIZATION OF THE COMPLETE HIGH-CONDUCTOR CENTERED PROJECTOR.

Assume the notation of fact 14fe68fdcbfd99ff. Let b=pb' be squarefree, where p is prime, and assume
  b'=b/p<F_0.                                                (1)
For (a,b)=1 define
  r_{p,b}(a)
   =e_p(N[a b']^(-1))+1/(p-1).                              (2)
For h|b' with (h,N)=1 define
 R^{(p)}_{b',h}(a)
  =product_{q|h}
    [e_q(N[a p(b'/q)]^(-1))+1/(q-1)].                       (3)
Define the shifted-cutoff complementary superposition
 P^{(p)}_{b',>F_0/p}(a)
  =sum_{h|b';ph>F_0,(h,N)=1}
     c_{b'/h}(N)R^{(p)}_{b',h}(a)/phi(b'/h).                 (4)

If p|N, then
  P_b(a)=Pi_{b,>F_0}(a)=0.                                  (5)
If p does not divide N, then exactly
  P_b(a)=r_{p,b}(a)P^{(p)}_{b',>F_0/p}(a).                  (6)
Thus in the nonzero rough-prime branch, the same locally centered p-factor occurs in every active conductor and is factored only after the complete conductor sum is formed.

For p not dividing N, after fixing a unit residue modulo b', the sum of r_{p,b}(a) over the p-1 unit lifts modulo p is zero, and
  1/(p-1)sum_{a modulo p;a nonzero}|r_{p,b}(a)|^2
  =1-1/(p-1)^2.                                             (7)

No estimate for the complementary superposition, its product-coupled actual coefficient, CEN-MZB, C_small, or Goldbach is asserted. In particular, (6) does not authorize expanding or estimating the proper centering faces of the complementary factor separately.
bab04e002177e282.proof:
Let f|b satisfy f>F_0 and (f,N)=1. If p does not divide f, then f|b'. By (1), this gives f<=b'<F_0, a contradiction. Hence every active f contains p. If p|N, the condition (f,N)=1 forbids p|f, so no active f exists. Formula (3) of fact 14fe68fdcbfd99ff is then an empty sum and gives (5).

Assume now that p does not divide N. Every active conductor has a unique representation
  f=ph,  h|b',  ph>F_0,  (h,N)=1.                           (8)
Its cofactor is
  b/f=b'/h.                                                  (9)
By the primewise definition of R in fact 14fe68fdcbfd99ff, the p-local factor of R_{b,ph}(a) is exactly (2). For q|h, one has b/q=p(b'/q), so the q-local factor is exactly the corresponding factor in (3). Therefore
  R_{b,ph}(a)=r_{p,b}(a)R^{(p)}_{b',h}(a).                  (10)
Insert (8)-(10) into
 P_b(a)=sum_{f|b;f>F_0,(f,N)=1}
          c_{b/f}(N)R_{b,f}(a)/phi(b/f).
The factor r_{p,b}(a) is independent of h and may be taken outside the complete h-sum. The remaining sum is (4), proving (6).

Finally, because p does not divide N and p does not divide b', the coefficient Nb'^(-1) in (2) is nonzero modulo p. Inversion and multiplication by this coefficient permute the units. Hence the exponential in (2) has unit sum -1. Adding p-1 copies of 1/(p-1) gives zero. The same calculation as in fact 1d28c0f84d1aad83 gives the normalized squared norm 1-1/(p-1)^2, proving (7).

glossary.R^{(p)}_{b',h}(a): The complementary centered response after removing a compulsory p factor.
glossary.r_{p,b}(a): The compulsory p-local centered inverse trace.

bab73c9febc955ed.title: HALF-FRACTIONAL-CONV-GCD-STRIP. Let rho_{1/2} be the multiplicative function of fact 5999a1878276ac78. Thus rho_{1/2}(1)=1; for every prime p one has rho_{1/2}(p)=-1/2 and, for j>=2,
bab73c9febc955ed.author: slava chan
bab73c9febc955ed.statement:
HALF-FRACTIONAL-CONV-GCD-STRIP. Let rho_{1/2} be the multiplicative function of fact 5999a1878276ac78. Thus rho_{1/2}(1)=1; for every prime p one has rho_{1/2}(p)=-1/2 and, for j>=2,
rho_{1/2}(p^j)/rho_{1/2}(p^(j-1))=(j-3/2)/j,
so rho_{1/2}(p^j)<0 for every j>=1, |rho_{1/2}(n)|<=1, and rho_{1/2}*rho_{1/2}=mu without any coprimality condition on the convolution variables.

Let kappa and c be arbitrary positive integers, let R_kappa=rad(kappa), and let F be any finitely supported complex-valued function on the positive integers. Then exactly
sum_{n>=1} mu(n)F(n)
 =sum_{h|R_kappa} mu(h)
   sum_{d,m>=1,(dm,R_kappa)=1} rho_{1/2}(d)rho_{1/2}(m)F(hdm).       (1)
With the additional restriction (n,c)=1 one has exactly
sum_{n>=1,(n,c)=1} mu(n)F(n)
 =sum_{h|R_kappa,(h,c)=1} mu(h)
   sum_{d,m>=1,(dm,cR_kappa)=1} rho_{1/2}(d)rho_{1/2}(m)F(hdm).     (2)
No condition (d,m)=1 and no squarefree condition on d or m occurs in either identity; the vanishing at squareful n is produced by local coefficient cancellation.

If F is supported on B<=n<2B with B>0, then the h-row in (1) or (2) is supported on
X_h<=dm<2X_h,  where X_h=B/h.                                     (3)
Moreover,
sum_{h|R_kappa}1/h=product_{p|kappa}(1+1/p)<=1+log(kappa).          (4)
These identities assert no Siegel-Walfisz estimate, arithmetic-progression estimate, or other distribution property for rho_{1/2}.
bab73c9febc955ed.proof:
The coefficient statements for rho_{1/2}, the recurrence, its absolute bound, and the convolution identity rho_{1/2}*rho_{1/2}=mu are proved in fact 5999a1878276ac78. The recurrence ratio is positive and smaller than one for j>=2, while rho_{1/2}(p)=-1/2, so every rho_{1/2}(p^j) with j>=1 is negative.

Because F has finite support, every sum below is finite after imposing hdm in the support of F, so primewise coefficient comparison and regrouping are legitimate. Consider the coefficient of F(n) on the right side of (1). It is multiplicative as a function of n. If p does not divide R_kappa, then p never divides h and the local coefficient at p^a is
sum_{i=0}^a rho_{1/2}(p^i)rho_{1/2}(p^(a-i))=mu(p^a)
by fact 5999a1878276ac78. This includes all pairs i,a-i and hence allows p to divide both d and m.

If p divides R_kappa, the condition (dm,R_kappa)=1 forces the p-adic exponents of d and m to be zero. The divisor h of R_kappa has p-adic exponent either zero, with coefficient 1, or one, with coefficient mu(p)=-1. Thus the local generating polynomial is 1-X. Its coefficient at p^a is 1 for a=0, -1 for a=1, and zero for a>=2, again exactly mu(p^a). Multiplying the local coefficients over the finitely many primes dividing n proves (1). In particular, for a>=2 the zero coefficient explicitly accounts for squareful cancellation rather than deleting squareful d or m.

For (2), compare local coefficients again. If p does not divide cR_kappa, the preceding convolution calculation is unchanged. If p divides c but not R_kappa, then p cannot divide d or m and cannot divide h, so only exponent zero of n occurs, as required by (n,c)=1. If p divides R_kappa but not c, the local polynomial is 1-X as above. Finally, if p divides both c and R_kappa, the condition (h,c)=1 excludes p from h and (dm,cR_kappa)=1 excludes it from d and m, so again only exponent zero occurs. These four cases give exactly mu(n)1_{(n,c)=1}, proving (2).

If F(hdm) is nonzero under the displayed support hypothesis, then B<=hdm<2B. Division by h gives (3). Finally every divisor h of R_kappa is a distinct integer between 1 and R_kappa, and R_kappa<=kappa. Therefore
sum_{h|R_kappa}1/h<=sum_{1<=j<=kappa}1/j<=1+integral_1^kappa du/u=1+log(kappa),
with the same conclusion for kappa=1. The Euler-product equality in (4) follows by expanding product_{p|kappa}(1+1/p).

glossary.F: An arbitrary finitely supported complex-valued function on the positive integers.
glossary.R_kappa: The radical rad(kappa), namely the product of the distinct primes dividing the positive integer kappa.
glossary.X_h: The support scale B/h in the h-row.

bab94ab4a0e20bc0.title: GA-CqSRC-NTRANS: EXACT TERMINAL-UNION REDUCTION OF THE CENTERED SOURCE TO A WEIGHTED n-CHARACTER TRANSFORM, WITH LOW-d-CONDUCTOR AND RESONANT ENLARGEMENT ERRORS PAID SEPARATELY
bab94ab4a0e20bc0.author: slava chan
bab94ab4a0e20bc0.statement:
GA-CqSRC-NTRANS: EXACT TERMINAL-UNION REDUCTION OF THE CENTERED SOURCE TO A WEIGHTED n-CHARACTER TRANSFORM, WITH LOW-d-CONDUCTOR AND RESONANT ENLARGEMENT ERRORS PAID SEPARATELY.

Adopt one complete fixed Good-W terminal family before anatomy and dilator separation, as in fact 2223056b02c29f78. Fix
D<=d_lambda<2D,  D>Q^2,                                         (1)
a physical conductor m>=2, a unit c modulo m, and a nonprincipal character chi modulo m.

Remove the scalar a_lambda(n) from the exact physical coefficient and sum the remaining coefficient on a primitive signed ray R. This defines a common flat ray coefficient B_n^base(R) satisfying
B_lambda(R)=a_lambda(n)B_n^base(R)                              (2)
for every terminal child lambda over n.

For a distinct ray pair R,R', let m_q,C_q,m_d be as in fact e9e9563501147a1a. Let Theta_n(R,R') contain every retained selector independent of the terminal factorization n=d_lambda v_lambda, excluding only the dilator block, the condition m_d>L, and the nonresonance deletion. Define
F_{m,c}(n)
 =sum_{R!=R':m_q=m, C_q congruent c (mod m)}
 Theta_n(R,R')B_n^base(R)conjugate(B_n^base(R')).                (3)

Let E_D be the exact terminal edges lambda over n with (1) and gcd(n,m)=1. Define
A^{full}_{m,c,chi}(d)
 =sum_{lambda in E_D:d_lambda=d}
  |a_lambda(n)|^2chi(v_lambda)F_{m,c}(n),                        (4)
A^{hard}_{m,c,chi}(d)
 =sum_{lambda in E_D:d_lambda=d}
  sum_{R!=R':m_q=m,C_q congruent c}
  1_{m_d>L}Theta_n(R,R')|a_lambda(n)|^2chi(v_lambda)
  B_n^base(R)conjugate(B_n^base(R')),                            (5)
A^{lowNR}_{m,c,chi}(d)
 =sum over the same coordinates with 1<m_d<=L,                   (6)
and
A^{res}_{m,c,chi}(d)
 =sum over the same coordinates with m_d=1.                     (7)
Then
A^{full}=A^{hard}+A^{lowNR}+A^{res}.                             (8)
The explicit nonresonance deletion is redundant in A^{hard}, since m_d>L>1 implies d_lambda does not divide mathscr A Delta_0 by fact 1acbe88cc741c6f1. The profile A^{lowNR} belongs to the absolute GA-LOW-dCOND payment of fact 55dee3162ad8a011. The profile A^{res} is the fully resonant sector d_lambda divides mathscr A Delta_0.

Let sigma_D(n) be the squared marker mass of fact 256c10f372b85755. Then
sum_{D<=d<2D}chi(d)A^{full}_{m,c,chi}(d)
 =sum_{B/2<=n<=2B}sigma_D(n)chi(n)F_{m,c}(n).                   (GA-CqSRC-NTRANS)

After summing over m,c,chi with the exact Gauss weights from fact eb01e7b374521a0c, both enlargement errors A^{lowNR} and A^{res} are bounded at
x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 BQ^2F^2/D.                                 (9)
Consequently the original hard centered source reduces to the unproved weighted n-character supplier
sum_{m>=2}sum_{c (mod m)}^*1/phi(m)
 sum_{chi!=chi_0}G_{m,c}(chi)
 sum_n sigma_D(n)chi(n)F_{m,c}(n)
 <<x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 BQ^2F^2/D.                              (N-qSRC-SUP)

This is an exact source-specific handoff, not an estimate of N-qSRC-SUP. It retains the terminal incidence and complete ray-pair sum. It does not estimate the separate F>Q principal source or the small-D projected-incidence branch, and proves no tail payment or Goldbach conclusion.
bab94ab4a0e20bc0.proof:
Fact 2223056b02c29f78 proves from the exact physical coefficient that, after a_lambda(n) is removed, all remaining q,h and inherited frozen factors are common across terminal children. Primitive-ray grouping therefore gives (2).

Fact 50ef6972010758a6 gives
B_lambda(R)conjugate(B_lambda(R'))
=|a_lambda(n)|^2B_lambda^flat(R)conjugate(B_lambda^flat(R')).
By (2), the flat coefficients are B_n^base. The terminal re-marker changes none of the child-independent selectors in Theta_n, and m_q,C_q depend only on the ray pair and target. This proves the full profile (4).

Fact eb01e7b374521a0c defines the literal centered profile by summing
chi(v_lambda)B_lambda(R)conjugate(B_lambda(R'))
at fixed d_lambda,m_q,C_q, with all hard selectors retained. Substituting (2) and retaining m_d>L gives (5). Since m_d is a positive integer, exactly one of m_d>L, 1<m_d<=L, or m_d=1 holds, proving (6)-(8). Fact 1acbe88cc741c6f1 proves m_d=1 if and only if d_lambda divides mathscr A Delta_0, and proves m_d>L implies nonresonance.

Equation (4) is exactly the incidence profile S_{chi,D}F_{m,c} of fact 256c10f372b85755. Its TERMINAL-INC-CHAR identity proves GA-CqSRC-NTRANS.

It remains to justify (9) only after the exact character reassembly. Fact eb01e7b374521a0c and fact d5cfc4a905989cc8 identify
1/phi(m)sum_{chi!=chi_0}G_{m,c}(chi)chi(n)
 =K^circ_{m,c}(n).
The centered kernel satisfies
|K^circ_{m,c}(n)|
 <=|e_m(-c n^{-1})|+|mu(m)|/phi(m)<=2.                           (10)

On A^{lowNR}, all coordinates are nonresonant and have 1<m_d<=L. Fact 55dee3162ad8a011 proves GA-LOW-dCOND by absolute coordinate summation with every literal selector retained. Replacing the unit physical phase by the bounded multiplier K^circ costs at most the factor two in (10), so the reassembled A^{lowNR} contribution has the bound (9).

On A^{res}, m_d=1 is equivalent to d_lambda dividing mathscr A Delta_0. This is the fully resonant sector of equation (15) in fact e55b27d39c593164. The proof of its bound (18) is absolute: for each coordinate quadruple it counts only divisor-many d_lambda and then sums coefficient envelopes. Again (10) changes that absolute count by at most two. After the x^{o(1)} union of terminal children, the reassembled A^{res} contribution also has (9).

Finally insert (8) into the exact character formula for the hard centered source. Apply GA-CqSRC-NTRANS to A^{full} and move the two paid errors to the right. This yields the exact reduction to N-qSRC-SUP. No absolute value is applied to the remaining full ray-pair or character sum, and all exclusions follow.

glossary.A^{full}_{m,c,chi}(d): The enlarged terminal-union profile before the d-conductor split.
glossary.B_n^base(R): The common flat primitive-ray coefficient over n.
glossary.F_{m,c}(n): The complete child-independent flat ray-pair source aggregate.
glossary.GA-CqSRC-NTRANS: The exact reduction of the enlarged centered profile to sigma_D(n)chi(n)F_{m,c}(n).
glossary.N-qSRC-SUP: The remaining weighted n-character source estimate.

bb2e1cc4992df859.title: FIXED-PRIME FKMS DISPLAYED-BOUND EXPONENT CAP IN THE ULTRA-LONG BENCHMARK. Let Q tend to infinity through prime values. Fix real numbers beta_* with 3/4<beta_*<=6/5, gamma_*, rho_*>=0, and put
bb2e1cc4992df859.author: slava chan
bb2e1cc4992df859.statement:
FIXED-PRIME FKMS DISPLAYED-BOUND EXPONENT CAP IN THE ULTRA-LONG BENCHMARK. Let Q tend to infinity through prime values. Fix real numbers beta_* with 3/4<beta_*<=6/5, gamma_*, rho_*>=0, and put
B_*=Q^(beta_*),  G_*=Q^(gamma_*),  H_*=B_*/(QG_*)=Q^(theta_*),  theta_*=beta_*-1-gamma_*.
Assume theta_*>0. Let M_*=Q^(mu_*), T_*=Q^(nu_*) be positive scale parameters satisfying
mu_*+nu_*=beta_*,  nu_*<2beta_*-2+rho_*.
For an integer L_mom>=2 define the two multiplicative factors
F_II(L_mom)=
[Q^(-mu_*)+Q^{-[beta_*-3/4-7/(4L_mom)]/L_mom}]^(1/2),
and
F_tri(L_mom)=
[Q^(1/2-nu_*-theta_*)+
 Q^(1-L_mom mu_*-nu_*-theta_*)]^(1/(2L_mom)).
These are exactly the power-of-Q parts of, respectively, the displayed Type-II factor in Fouvry--Kowalski--Michel--Sawin, arXiv:2511.09459v3, Theorem 1.3(2), after setting the product of the two bilinear lengths equal to B_*, and the displayed trilinear factor in Theorem 1.4 after setting its first length equal to M_* and the product of its other two lengths equal to T_*H_*.

Ignoring Q^epsilon losses and granting every applicability and length hypothesis favorably, the largest saving exponent over the corresponding trivial coefficient-norm bound that F_II(L_mom) can certify is at most
s_II(L_mom)=[beta_*-3/4-7/(4L_mom)]/(2L_mom)
and, uniformly over all real L_mom>0 and hence over all integers L_mom>=2,
s_II(L_mom)<= (beta_*-3/4)^2/14 <=81/5600.
The largest nonnegative saving exponent that F_tri(L_mom) can certify is at most
max(0,[nu_*+theta_*-1/2]/(2L_mom))
<= max(0,[3beta_*-7/2-gamma_*+rho_*]/4).

Consequently, whenever
theta_*>81/5600,
the displayed Type-II right-hand side cannot by itself certify the saving Q^(theta_*) required to recover an H_*-length loss by fixed-h and fixed-Q triangle summation. Whenever
theta_*>max(0,[3beta_*-7/2-gamma_*+rho_*]/4),
the displayed trilinear right-hand side cannot certify that saving either. At the critical endpoint benchmark
beta_*=6/5, gamma_*=rho_*=0,
one has theta_*=1/5, while the two caps are respectively 81/5600 and at most 1/40.

This is a right-hand-side no-direct-import statement only. It is not a lower bound for any literal sum. Moreover, Theorems 1.1, 1.3 and 1.4 of arXiv:2511.09459v3 are stated for a fixed prime modulus and a gallant rank-at-least-two trace sheaf, whereas the reciprocal additive-character kernel discussed in Section 9.11 is rank one. The paper's Section 9.11 stratification mechanism is therefore not ruled out by this fact, but it requires a new rank-one specialization before use. No prime-to-squarefree extension, cross-Q assembly, literal source linkage, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
bb2e1cc4992df859.proof:
The relevant published statements are as follows. In arXiv:2511.09459v3, Theorem 1.3(2), for a prime modulus q, a gallant and light sheaf, an integer L_mom>=2, and lengths satisfying the theorem's displayed range, the Type-II sum is at most its coefficient-norm trivial scale times
q^epsilon [1/M+(q^(3/4+7/(4L_mom))/(MN))^(1/L_mom)]^(1/2).
In Theorem 1.4, under the hypotheses that its first length is at most four times q and that the product of its other two lengths is at most four times q, the trilinear sum is at most its trivial length product times
q^epsilon [q^(1/2)/(MN)+q/(J^(L_mom)MN)]^(1/(2L_mom)).
The paper's Definition 1.2 and Section 9.11 state that gallant sheaves have rank at least two and discuss the reciprocal additive-character example separately as a rank-one case.

Set q=Q and set the Type-II product MN=B_*=Q^(beta_*). Omitting Q^epsilon, the theorem's factor becomes F_II(L_mom). Because both terms inside its square root are nonnegative,
F_II(L_mom)>=
Q^{-[beta_*-3/4-7/(4L_mom)]/(2L_mom)}
=Q^(-s_II(L_mom)).
Thus an upper bound containing F_II(L_mom) cannot certify a power saving larger than s_II(L_mom); if s_II(L_mom)<=0, it certifies no positive saving from this term.

Put delta_*=beta_*-3/4>0 and regard L_mom temporarily as a positive real variable. Then
s_II(L_mom)=delta_*/(2L_mom)-7/(8L_mom^2).
Writing y=1/L_mom gives
s_II(L_mom)=(delta_*/2)y-(7/8)y^2
=delta_*^2/14-(7/8)(y-2delta_*/7)^2.
Therefore s_II(L_mom)<=delta_*^2/14 for every positive real L_mom. Since beta_*<=6/5,
delta_*<=6/5-3/4=9/20,
so
s_II(L_mom)<= (9/20)^2/14=81/5600.
This proves the Type-II cap without using, and therefore even after favorably ignoring, the theorem's integer-length restrictions. If theta_*>81/5600, this cap is strictly smaller than the required exponent theta_*.

For the trilinear theorem set its first length J=M_*=Q^(mu_*) and set the product of its other two lengths equal to T_*H_*=Q^(nu_*+theta_*). Omitting Q^epsilon gives F_tri(L_mom). Its first summand alone implies
F_tri(L_mom)>=Q^{(1/2-nu_*-theta_*)/(2L_mom)}.
If nu_*+theta_*<=1/2, this lower bound is at least one, so the displayed factor certifies no positive saving. If nu_*+theta_*>1/2, its saving is at most
[nu_*+theta_*-1/2]/(2L_mom)
<=[nu_*+theta_*-1/2]/4
because L_mom>=2.
Using theta_*=beta_*-1-gamma_* and the strict ultra-long inequality nu_*<2beta_*-2+rho_* gives
nu_*+theta_*-1/2
<3beta_*-7/2-gamma_*+rho_*.
If the quantity on the right is positive, division by four and the preceding inequalities give the desired cap. If it is nonpositive, then nu_*+theta_*-1/2 is negative as well, so both max-with-zero caps are zero. Thus in all cases
max(0,[nu_*+theta_*-1/2]/(2L_mom))
<=max(0,[3beta_*-7/2-gamma_*+rho_*]/4).
The second bracket term cannot improve this cap because the bracket is a sum of nonnegative terms.

Finally, at beta_*=6/5 and gamma_*=rho_*=0,
theta_*=6/5-1=1/5,
81/5600<1/5,
and
[3beta_*-7/2]/4
=[18/5-7/2]/4
=(1/10)/4=1/40<1/5.
Hence neither displayed fixed-prime right-hand side can recover the H_*=Q^(1/5) loss at the critical benchmark. All conclusions concern only what these nonnegative displayed right-hand sides certify; they do not estimate a literal arithmetic sum or preclude a new rank-one stratification argument.

glossary.B_*: The product scale Q^(beta_*) in this benchmark.
glossary.F_II: The function L_mom mapped to the power-of-Q multiplicative factor in the displayed fixed-prime Type-II right-hand side after the benchmark substitution.
glossary.F_II(L_mom): The value of F_II at the moment parameter L_mom.
glossary.F_tri: The function L_mom mapped to the power-of-Q multiplicative factor in the displayed fixed-prime trilinear right-hand side after the benchmark substitution.
glossary.F_tri(L_mom): The value of F_tri at the moment parameter L_mom.
glossary.G_*: The imbalance scale Q^(gamma_*) in this benchmark.
glossary.H_*: The frequency-length scale B_*/(QG_*) in this benchmark.
glossary.L_mom: The integer moment parameter called l in Theorems 1.3 and 1.4 of arXiv:2511.09459v3.
glossary.M_*: The first length Q^(mu_*) in the trilinear substitution.
glossary.T_*: The complementary length Q^(nu_*) in the trilinear substitution.
glossary.beta_*: The base-Q exponent of the product scale B_* in this fixed-prime benchmark.
glossary.delta_*: The positive difference beta_*-3/4 used in the Type-II optimization.
glossary.gamma_*: The base-Q exponent of the imbalance scale G_*.
glossary.mu_*: The base-Q exponent of the first trilinear length M_*.
glossary.nu_*: The base-Q exponent of the complementary length T_*.
glossary.rho_*: The nonnegative buffer in the ultra-long upper bound for nu_*.
glossary.s_II: The function L_mom mapped to the maximum saving exponent permitted by the second nonnegative term of F_II.
glossary.s_II(L_mom): The value of s_II at the moment parameter L_mom.
glossary.theta_*: The base-Q exponent of the frequency length H_*=B_*/(QG_*).

bbcb9f66597c667c.title: FIXED-TARGET (h)-AVERAGED TYPE-I RECIPROCAL CONSUMER
bbcb9f66597c667c.author: slava chan

glossary.A: The fixed numerator before multiplication by h.
glossary.cal I: The Poisson-prefactored h-average of fixed-target Type-I reciprocal boxes.
glossary.w: The fixed smooth weight on the unweighted Type-I factor.

bbd687d016ee3ff6.title: BOUNDED-UNION AND INJECTIVE DYADIC-COFACTOR EXTENSION OF THE TENSOR-STABLE RANK-ONE OCCUPANCY
bbd687d016ee3ff6.author: slava chan
bbd687d016ee3ff6.statement:
BOUNDED-UNION AND INJECTIVE DYADIC-COFACTOR EXTENSION OF THE TENSOR-STABLE RANK-ONE OCCUPANCY.

Fix an integer K>=1 and a prime p. Let S_p be contained in a union of at most K nonzero additive intervals I_{p,j} in F_p^*, and suppose the sum of their cardinalities is at most L_p. Retain all the data and notation of fact a84f95a82329a894, except that the cofactor residue t ranges over S_p rather than one interval, and define
A_p(r,h,t)=sum_{lambda in Lambda_p(r,h,t)} ||v_{p,lambda}(r,h,t)||_{E_p},
U_p(r)=sum_h max_{t in S_p} A_p(r,h,t).
Allow the same arbitrary tuple mask and the same tuple-dependent four-linear functional of norm at most one. Let V_p be the resulting absolute source-weighted occupancy of all exceptional four-row equal-pole strata: the signs are (+,+,-,-), the equality partition of the shifts has no singleton, and every equal-shift block obeys the signed balance in h t^{-1}. Then, for every epsilon>0,
V_p <<_{epsilon,K}
 L_p^epsilon ( L_p^{8/3}+L_p^4/p+3L_p^2 )
 (sum_r U_p(r)^2)^2.                                           (1)
Thus the one-prime and tensor-stable conclusions of facts 549328a9f587f158 and a84f95a82329a894 remain valid for any fixed bounded union of nonzero additive cofactor intervals.

In particular, let J_p be any interval of L_p consecutive integers with L_p<p, and restrict to literal rows for which the integer cofactor t=n/p lies in J_p and p does not divide t. Reduction modulo p is injective on J_p, and the nonzero residue image of J_p is a union of at most two nonzero additive intervals. Hence (1) applies with K=2 to this entire integer cofactor block, even if J_p crosses a multiple of p. No assertion that the set of actually occurring factorizable cofactors fills either interval is needed: missing residues are represented by zero coefficient.

If L_p>=p^delta for fixed delta>0, then for every eta with
0<eta<min(4delta/3,1)
and sufficiently large p,
V_p <<_{delta,eta,K}
 p^{-eta} L_p^4 (sum_r U_p(r)^2)^2.                              (2)
If in addition p>=Q^zeta and the selected prime varies over a finite set, then, with
Y_p=L_p^2 sum_r U_p(r)^2,
sum_p V_p <<_{delta,eta,zeta,K}
 Q^{-zeta eta} (sum_p Y_p)^2.                                   (3)
Thus a dyadic integer cofactor block of length below its selected prime and at least a fixed power of that prime gives a fixed fourth-moment saving, and hence a fourth-root saving Q^{-zeta eta/4}, under the exact contractive remaining-face hypothesis of fact a84f95a82329a894.

This theorem does not prove that every literal cofactor cell has length below p, compare the l1 envelope sum_p Y_p with the complete joint-completion norm, or construct the source-specific remaining-face contraction required by fact a84f95a82329a894.
bbd687d016ee3ff6.proof:
Partition the ambient union into disjoint nonzero additive intervals I_1,...,I_k, where k<=K, by deleting overlaps and, if necessary, subdividing; their total length is at most L_p. Extend every coefficient by zero from S_p to the ambient union.

For an interval I and x in F_p put
T_I(x)=sum_{t in I} e_p(x t^{-1}).
Normalized additive orthogonality identifies
(1/p)sum_x |T_I(x)|^4
with the reciprocal additive energy J_4(p,I). Bourgain and Garaev, arXiv:1211.4184, Theorem 1 with k=2, states
J_4(p,I) <<_epsilon |I|^epsilon (|I|^{8/3}+|I|^4/p).             (4)

Put T(x)=sum_{j=1}^k T_{I_j}(x). By Minkowski's inequality in normalized L^4(F_p),
((1/p)sum_x |T(x)|^4)^{1/4}
 <= sum_j J_4(p,I_j)^{1/4}.                                     (5)
Taking the fourth root of (4), using (a+b)^{1/4}<=a^{1/4}+b^{1/4}, and writing L_j=|I_j|, the right side of (5) is at most
C_{epsilon} L_p^{epsilon/4}
( sum_j L_j^{2/3} + p^{-1/4}sum_j L_j ).
By concavity and sum_j L_j<=L_p,
sum_j L_j^{2/3} <= k^{1/3} L_p^{2/3},
sum_j L_j <=L_p.
Using (a+b)^4<=8(a^4+b^4) therefore gives
(1/p)sum_x |T(x)|^4
 <<_{epsilon,K} L_p^epsilon
 (L_p^{8/3}+L_p^4/p).                                           (6)

The same estimate controls four independently height-dilated reciprocal sums. Indeed, for nonzero heights h_i define
T_{h_i}(x)=sum_{t in union_j I_j} e_p(x h_i t^{-1}).
Multiplication by h_i permutes F_p, so each T_{h_i} has the same normalized fourth moment as T. Orthogonality and Holder consequently show that the number of quadruples in the ambient union satisfying
h_1/t_1+h_2/t_2=h_3/t_3+h_4/t_4
is bounded by the right side of (6).

Now repeat the source-weighted proof of fact 549328a9f587f158. The contractive four-linear hypothesis first bounds each retained vector contribution by the product of its four vector norms, exactly as in fact a84f95a82329a894. Summing source labels gives A_p. For the one-block equal-shift stratum, use (6), dominate each coefficient by max_t A_p(r,h,t), sum the four heights, and then sum r. This gives
<<_{epsilon,K} L_p^epsilon
(L_p^{8/3}+L_p^4/p)(sum_r U_p(r)^2)^2.
For any of the three two-block partitions, once one t in a block and the two nonzero heights are fixed, the signed relation determines the other t uniquely in F_p. Hence each block has at most L_p possibilities in the ambient union. Exactly as in fact 549328a9f587f158, all three partitions together contribute at most
3L_p^2(sum_r U_p(r)^2)^2.
The arbitrary tuple mask can be dropped only after absolute values, and all source labels have already been retained in A_p. This proves (1).

For the integer corollary, if two integers in J_p have the same residue modulo p, their nonzero difference has absolute value below p and is divisible by p, a contradiction. Thus reduction is injective. A consecutive residue arc of length below p is one cyclic additive interval; deleting its possible zero residue splits it into at most two nonzero additive intervals. Literal support is contained in that union, so zero extension proves the corollary.

Relative to L_p^4, the terms in (1) have sizes, apart from L_p^epsilon,
L_p^{-4/3}, p^{-1}, and 3L_p^{-2}.
If L_p>=p^delta, choosing epsilon sufficiently small in terms of delta and eta proves (2) for every eta<min(4delta/3,1).

Finally, (2) gives V_p<<p^{-eta}Y_p^2. Under p>=Q^zeta, sum over p and use
sum_p Y_p^2 <= (sum_p Y_p)^2.
This proves (3) and the fourth-root consequence. The final scope limitations are precisely hypotheses not established by this argument.

glossary.J_p: An interval of consecutive integer cofactors of length strictly below the selected prime.
glossary.K: A fixed upper bound for the number of nonzero additive interval components.
glossary.S_p: The supported selected-prime cofactor residues, contained in a bounded union of nonzero additive intervals.

bbe9f66e9f057362.title: EXACT DOUBLE RECIPROCAL PHASE AND POWER-SIZED CONSTANT CORRECTION ON THE CROSS-INCIDENCE HIGH FACE
bbe9f66e9f057362.author: slava chan
bbe9f66e9f057362.statement:
EXACT DOUBLE RECIPROCAL PHASE AND POWER-SIZED CONSTANT CORRECTION ON THE CROSS-INCIDENCE HIGH FACE.

Fix 0<eta<1/12 and assume the actual scales
 B=Q^(4/3+o(1)),
 F_0=Q^(1-2eta+o(1)).
Let
 b_1=p_1s_1, b_2=p_2s_2
satisfy
 B<=b_i<2B,
 b_i squarefree,
 p_i prime,
 1<=s_i<F_0,
 p_i does not divide N.
Let Q<=a_i<2Q and (a_i,b_i)=1. Assume p_1|s_2 and put
 q_2=b_2/p_1.                                                (1)
Define
 r_{p_1,b_1}(a_1)
  =e_{p_1}(N[a_1s_1]^(-1))+1/(p_1-1),                       (2)
 Delta_{p_1}(a_1,a_2)
  =e_{p_1}(N([a_1s_1]^(-1)-[a_2q_2]^(-1))).                (3)
Then exactly
 r_{p_1,b_1}(a_1)
 overline(e_{p_1}(N[a_2q_2]^(-1)))
 =
 Delta_{p_1}(a_1,a_2)
 +1/(p_1-1)e_{p_1}(-N[a_2q_2]^(-1)).                        (4)

Moreover,
 1/(p_1-1)
 <<F_0/B
 =Q^(-1/3-2eta+o(1)).                                       (5)
Thus the local single-phase correction in (4) carries a fixed power coefficient at least as strong as Q^(-1/3-2eta+o(1)). The unsuppressed local term is precisely the double inverse-difference phase Delta_{p_1}.

Equation (5) is only a local scalar coefficient bound. No aggregate Hilbert--Schmidt payment of the correction, no estimate for the double phase or cutoff-boundary block, no TRI-CROSS or ROP estimate, no CEN-MZB estimate, no C_small estimate and no Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
bbe9f66e9f057362.proof:
All inverses in (2)-(4) exist. Indeed p_1|b_1 and (a_1,b_1)=1 give p_1 does not divide a_1s_1. Also p_1|b_2, q_2=b_2/p_1 and squarefreeness give p_1 does not divide q_2, while (a_2,b_2)=1 gives p_1 does not divide a_2.

The complex conjugate of the row-two phase is
 overline(e_{p_1}(N[a_2q_2]^(-1)))
 =e_{p_1}(-N[a_2q_2]^(-1)).                                 (6)
Multiply (2) and (6). The product of their exponential terms is (3), while the product of the constant in (2) with (6) is the second term in (4). This proves the exact split.

From b_1=p_1s_1, b_1>=B and s_1<F_0,
 p_1=b_1/s_1>B/F_0.                                         (7)
The quotient B/F_0=Q^(1/3+2eta+o(1)) tends to infinity, so p_1>2 for sufficiently large Q. Hence
 1/(p_1-1)<=2/p_1<2F_0/B.                                  (8)
The displayed actual scales give F_0/B=Q^(-1/3-2eta+o(1)), proving (5) and all scope restrictions.

glossary.Delta_{p_1}(a_1,a_2): The cross-incidence double reciprocal phase modulo p_1.

bc1b67324480d454.title: CORRECTED UNIVERSAL SUBUNIT COMPLETION, INDEPENDENT FOUR-MODE FORWARD-E11 DECOMPOSITION, CORRECTION PAYMENTS, AND EXACT PHYSICAL LEADING PHASE INCLUDING \(q=1\). Let \(x\) be sufficiently large. Fix real \(\eta,\omega,\sigma\) with
bc1b67324480d454.author: slava chan
bc1b67324480d454.statement:
CORRECTED UNIVERSAL SUBUNIT COMPLETION, INDEPENDENT FOUR-MODE FORWARD-E11 DECOMPOSITION, CORRECTION PAYMENTS, AND EXACT PHYSICAL LEADING PHASE INCLUDING \(q=1\). Let \(x\) be sufficiently large. Fix real \(\eta,\omega,\sigma\) with
\[
 0<\eta<1/120,\qquad 0<\omega<2/9-3\eta,\qquad \sigma>0.
\]
Let
\[
 x^{1/2}(\log x)^{-B}\le D\le2x^{1/2},\qquad
 R=D^\beta,\qquad 4/3\le\beta\le4/3+6\eta,
\]
for a fixed positive real \(B\), put \(F=x^{2/9-3\eta-\omega}\), and let
\[
 P\ge (R/D)^2D^{2\sigma}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal P\) be a finite set of primes in \([P,2P]\). Then \(a>F\) for every \(a\in\mathcal P\), for sufficiently large \(x\).

Let \(N\) be a positive integer. Let \(m,u\) be coprime positive integers, let \(h\ne0\), put
\[
 c=(m,h),\qquad q=m/c,\qquad t=h/c,
\]
and assume that \(m\) is squarefree and
\[
 (ab,mhuN)=1,qquad (q,tu)=1
\]
for distinct \(a,b\in\mathcal P\). For \(q\ge2\), \(T>0\), and a Dirichlet character \(\psi\) modulo \(q\), define
\[
 G_{N,q}(\psi)=\sum_{\substack{z\ ({\rm mod}\ q)\\(z,q)=1}}
 e_q(-Nz)\overline{\psi(z)},\qquad e_v(y)=\exp(2\pi i y/v),
\]
and
\[
 P_a(T;t,u)=\frac1{\phi(q)}
 \sum_{\substack{\psi\ ({\rm mod}\ q)\\
 {\rm cond}(\psi)>T\\({\rm cond}(\psi),N)=1}}
 G_{N,q}(\psi)\psi(t)\overline{\psi(au)}.                 \tag{1}
\]
Define \(P_b\) by replacing \(a\) with \(b\). For \(q=1\), define
\[
 P_a(T;t,u)=P_b(T;t,u)={\bf1}_{T<1}.                        \tag{2}
\]
For every squarefree \(q\ge2\), every positive integer \(N\), and \(0<T<1\),
\[
 P_a(T;t,u)=e_q\!\left(-Nt(au)^{-1}\right),               \tag{3}
\]
without any hypothesis \((q,N)=1\).

For every \(q\ge1\), put
\[
 E_a=e_a\!\left(-Nt(qu)^{-1}\right),\qquad
 E_b=e_b\!\left(-Nt(qu)^{-1}\right),                      \tag{4}
\]
where for \(q=1\) this means
\[
 E_a=e_a(-Nt u^{-1}),\qquad E_b=e_b(-Nt u^{-1}),            \tag{5}
\]
and all inverses in (4)--(5) are taken in the displayed prime modulus. Put
\[
 A_a=P_a(F/a;t,u),\quad B_a=P_a(F/a;t,u)-P_a(F;t,u),
\]
and define \(A_b,B_b\) similarly. Define the descended projectors
\[
 \Pi_a=\frac1{\phi(aq)}
 \sum_{\substack{\chi\ ({\rm mod}\ aq)\\
 {\rm cond}(\chi)>F\\({\rm cond}(\chi),N)=1}}
 G_{N,aq}(\chi)\chi(t)\overline{\chi(u)},                \tag{6}
\]
and \(\Pi_b\) by replacing \(a\) with \(b\). Then, without using facts \(70f0948e686a21c8\), \(d716d761596faa18\), \(f387dfb8f31400c6\), \(669f51715cd33aa0\), or \(866cdb3eb8c3bf0d\),
\[
 \Pi_a=L_a+D_a,\qquad L_a=E_aA_a,qquad D_a=B_a/(a-1),     \tag{7}
\]
and likewise for \(b\). In particular, when \(q=1\),
\[
 A_a=1,\quad B_a=1,\quad
 \Pi_a=e_a(-Nt u^{-1})+\frac1{a-1},                       \tag{8}
\]
and similarly for \(b\). Thus \(\Pi_a\overline{\Pi_b}\) is exactly the sum of the four modes \(LL,LD,DL,DD\).

Let \(\Alpha\) be a finite coordinate set \(\alpha=(\iota,h,p,\ell)\) with \(u=p\ell\), let \(E_\alpha>0\), and let \(C_\iota(n;h,p,\ell)\) be complex coefficients, extended by zero off all desired literal masks and off \((m,u)=1\), such that
\[
 |C_\iota(n;h,p,\ell)|\le x^\varepsilon E_\alpha
 \quad\hbox{for squarefree }n,qquad
 \sum_{\alpha\in\Alpha}E_\alpha\le Rx^\varepsilon.    \tag{9}
\]
Let \(\lambda_{a,m}\) be supported on \(a\in\mathcal P\), \(am\le D\), satisfy
\[
 \sum_{a,m}|\lambda_{a,m}|^2\le D,                        \tag{10}
\]
and vanish unless \(m\) is squarefree and all displayed clean conditions hold. Form the exact two-dilate correlation with coefficient
\[
 \mu(m)^2\lambda_{a,m}\overline{\lambda_{b,m}}
 \frac{C_\iota(am;h,p,\ell)\overline{C_\iota(bm;h,p,\ell)}}{E_\alpha},
                                                                         \tag{11}
\]
continuous phase
\[
 e\!\left(\frac{Nh}{mu}\left(\frac1a-\frac1b\right)\right),       \tag{12}
\]
and projector product \(\Pi_a\overline{\Pi_b}\). Let \(C_{LL},C_{LD},C_{DL},C_{DD}\) be the sums over ordered \(a\ne b\) of the absolute values of the corresponding inner mode sums. Then
\[
 C_{LD}+C_{DL}\ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon RD,qquad
 C_{DD}\ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon RD/P,                \tag{13}
\]
and all three correction aggregates are
\[
 \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon\frac{P D^{3-2\sigma}}R.  \tag{14}
\]
For every \(q\ge1\), including \(q=1\), the \(LL\) product together with (12) is exactly
\[
 e_{p\ell}\!\left(Nh\,m^{-1}(a^{-1}-b^{-1})\right).      \tag{15}
\]
Consequently \(C_{LL}\) is exactly the complete physical-phase trace obtained by replacing the \(LL\) projector product and the continuous phase by (15), leaving every coefficient and mask unchanged. The estimate
\[
 C_{LL}\ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon\frac{P D^{3-2\sigma}}R          \tag{16}
\]
is an open sufficient supplier and is not asserted. No E11 closure, C3, PMD, DCE, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
bc1b67324480d454.proof:
First,
\[
 P\ge D^{2\beta-2+2\sigma}\ge D^{2/3+2\sigma}.
\]
Because \(D\ge x^{1/2}(\log x)^{-B}\), the last expression exceeds \(x^{1/3+\sigma}(\log x)^{-O(1)}\), whereas \(F<x^{2/9}\). Hence every \(a\in\mathcal P\) exceeds \(F\) for large \(x\).

We prove (3) without a coprimality hypothesis between \(q\) and \(N\). Let \(\psi\) be a nonprincipal character modulo the squarefree integer \(q\), with primitive conductor \(f\). Write \(q=fs\). Squarefreeness gives \((f,s)=1\), and \(\psi\) is induced by a primitive character \(\psi_*\) modulo \(f\) and is principal on the \(s\)-coordinate. Additive Chinese remaindering factors \(G_{N,q}(\psi)\) into a Ramanujan sum on \(s\) times the primitive local sum
\[
 \sum_{v\ ({\rm mod}\ f)}^*
 e_f(-Ns^{-1}v)\overline{\psi_*(v)}.                      \tag{17}
\]
If a prime \(r\mid(f,N)\), the \(r\)-local additive character in (17) is constant one and the \(r\)-local component of \(\psi_*\) is nonprincipal. Its sum over the units modulo \(r\) is zero. Therefore
\[
 G_{N,q}(\psi)=0\qquad\hbox{whenever }({\rm cond}(\psi),N)>1.         \tag{18}
\]
When \(0<T<1\), every character conductor is a positive integer exceeding \(T\). Characters excluded in (1) by the condition \((\operatorname{cond}(\psi),N)=1\) have zero coefficient by (18). Thus (1) equals the complete character Fourier inversion on \((\mathbb Z/q\mathbb Z)^*\), which gives (3). Equation (2) is the separate one-element unit-group response for \(q=1\).

Suppose \(q\ge2\). Fact d61bd0787abcc5ec applies to (6), because all its displayed clean hypotheses hold, and its three conductor ranges regroup exactly as
\[
 \Pi_a=E_aP_a(F/a;t,u)
 +\frac{P_a(F/a;t,u)-P_a(F;t,u)}{a-1}.
\]
This is (7). Now let \(q=1\). The modulus in (6) is the prime \(a\). Since \(a>F\ge1\), every nonprincipal character modulo \(a\), whose conductor is \(a\), is retained, while the principal character, whose conductor is one, is deleted. Complete finite Fourier inversion gives the response \(e_a(-Nt u^{-1})\). Because \((a,N)=1\), the principal Gauss coefficient is
\[
 \sum_{z=1}^{a-1}e_a(-Nz)=-1,
\]
so deleting its normalized contribution adds \(1/(a-1)\). Therefore
\[
 \Pi_a=e_a(-Nt u^{-1})+1/(a-1).
\]
By (2), \(F/a<1\), and \(F\ge1\), one has \(A_a=1\) and \(B_a=1\). Together with (5), this proves (7)--(8) for \(q=1\). The proof for \(b\) is identical after replacing the displayed prime. Multiplying the two decompositions proves the four-mode identity.

We next bound the correction modes. For \(q\ge2\), fact 9ef7fac8978ac244 gives
\[
 |P_a(F;t,u)|\ll_\varepsilon q^\varepsilon,
\]
because \(F\ge1\), while (3) and \(F/a<1\) give \(|A_a|=1\). Hence \(|B_a|\ll_\varepsilon q^\varepsilon\), and the same holds for \(b\). For \(q=1\), (8) gives \(|A_a|=|B_a|=1\). At fixed \(a,b,m\), (9) gives
\[
 \sum_{\alpha\in\Alpha}
 \frac{|C_\iota(am;h,p,\ell)C_\iota(bm;h,p,\ell)|}{E_\alpha}
 \le x^{2\varepsilon}\sum_\alpha E_\alpha
 \le Rx^{3\varepsilon}.                                  \tag{19}
\]
Also
\[
 \sum_m\left(\sum_{a\in\mathcal P}|\lambda_{a,m}|\right)^2
 \le |\mathcal P|\sum_{a,m}|\lambda_{a,m}|^2
 \le2PD,                                                    \tag{20}
\]
because \(\mathcal P\subset[P,2P]\) has at most \(P+1\le2P\) elements. A one-correction mode has the additional factor \(O_\varepsilon(x^\varepsilon/P)\), and the double-correction mode has \(O_\varepsilon(x^\varepsilon/P^2)\). Applying the triangle inequality, then (19)--(20), proves (13). The hypothesis on \(P\) is equivalent to
\[
 RD\le \frac{P D^{3-2\sigma}}R,
\]
which proves (14).

Finally we prove (15), including \(q=1\). Equations (3)--(5) show in every case that
\[
 L_a=E_aA_a=e_{aq}(-Nt u^{-1}),qquad
 L_b=e_{bq}(-Nt u^{-1}),                                    \tag{21}
\]
where the inverse is taken modulo \(aq\) or \(bq\); for \(q=1\), (21) is exactly (5). Since \(m=cq\) and \(h=ct\),
\[
 e\!\left(\frac{Nh}{amu}\right)L_a
 =e\!\left(\frac{Nt}{aqu}\right)e_{aq}(-Nt u^{-1})
 =e_u\!\left(Nt(aq)^{-1}\right).                          \tag{22}
\]
To justify the last identity, choose inverses \(\bar u\) modulo \(aq\) and \(\overline{aq}\) modulo \(u\). The integer
\[
 aq\,\overline{aq}+u\bar u
]
is congruent to one modulo both coprime moduli \(aq\) and \(u\), hence to one modulo \(aqu\). Dividing by \(aqu\) and exponentiating gives (22). Because \((c,u)=1\), which follows from \((m,u)=1\),
\[
 Nt(aq)^{-1}\equiv Nh(am)^{-1}\pmod u.                    \tag{23}
\]
Apply (22)--(23) to the \(a\)-factor and the complex conjugate identities to the \(b\)-factor. Their product is (15). This argument used the corrected nontrivial factors (5) when \(q=1\). Substitution into the exact correlation proves the asserted identification of \(C_{LL}\), without changing any coefficient or mask. Since no estimate for that physical trace was proved, (16) remains only the stated open supplier, and all scope restrictions follow.

glossary.A_a: The universally completed common-core leading projector P_a(F/a;t,u).
glossary.E_a: The prime-dilator local additive factor, retained nontrivially also when q=1.
glossary.L_a: The corrected leading local factor E_a A_a.
glossary.P_a(T;t,u): The common-core conductor projector at dilator a, with a separate q=1 convention.

bc46ed5832faeade.title: Fix real numbers \(1/2<a<b<1\), \(\eta>0\), and \(\rho\ge0\). Let \(W,\psi,\Phi,B_{\rm init},B_{\rm src},x,N,D_*,Q_{\rm init},D,M,U,{\cal I}_D,V_{d,m}\), and \(\Lambda_{\rm pr}\) satisfy all hypotheses and definitions in fact 54f71c4dcc1bc9bb; in particular \(N=2x\), \(x\) tends to infinity through positive integers for which \(N\) is not a sum of two primes,
bc46ed5832faeade.author: slava chan
bc46ed5832faeade.statement:
Fix real numbers \(1/2<a<b<1\), \(\eta>0\), and \(\rho\ge0\). Let \(W,\psi,\Phi,B_{\rm init},B_{\rm src},x,N,D_*,Q_{\rm init},D,M,U,{\cal I}_D,V_{d,m}\), and \(\Lambda_{\rm pr}\) satisfy all hypotheses and definitions in fact 54f71c4dcc1bc9bb; in particular \(N=2x\), \(x\) tends to infinity through positive integers for which \(N\) is not a sum of two primes,
\[
 D_*/2\le D,\qquad 2D>Q_{\rm init},\qquad DM\asymp_{a,b}x,\qquad D\le2x^{1/2},
\]
\[
 {\cal I}_D=\{d\ge2:(d,N)=1,\ \mu(d)\ne0,\ d\le x^{1/2},\ \Phi(d/D)\ne0\},
 \qquad V_{d,m}=W(dm/x)\Phi((N-dm)/U).
\]
Put \(L=\log x\) and \(T_x=L^{6+\eta+\rho}\). Partition the ordered distinct pairs in \({\cal I}_D^2\) into
\[
 {\cal Z}_\Delta=\{(d_1,d_2):0<|d_1-d_2|\le D/T_x\},
\]
\[
 {\cal Z}_g=\{(d_1,d_2):|d_1-d_2|>D/T_x,\ (d_1,d_2)\ge T_x\},
\]
and
\[
 {\cal Z}_\star=\{(d_1,d_2):|d_1-d_2|>D/T_x,\ (d_1,d_2)<T_x\}.
\]
For any one of these zones \({\cal Z}\), define its literal signed covariance
\[
 {\mathfrak C}_{\cal Z}=
 \sum_{(d_1,d_2)\in{\cal Z}}
 \mu(d_1)\mu(d_2)\Phi(d_1/D)\Phi(d_2/D)
 \sum_{m\ge1}V_{d_1,m}V_{d_2,m}
 \Lambda_{\rm pr}(N-d_1m)\Lambda_{\rm pr}(N-d_2m).
\]
Then
\[
 |{\mathfrak C}_{{\cal Z}_\Delta}|+
 |{\mathfrak C}_{{\cal Z}_g}|
 \ll_{W,\Phi,a,b}xD\,L^{-4-\eta-\rho}.                 \tag{1}
\]
Moreover the diagonal in fact 9e1ff55fe17bc513 satisfies
\[
 {\mathfrak D}_{\rm diag}=o\!\left(xD L^{-4-\eta}\right). \tag{2}
\]

Consequently the following one-sided estimate on the exact hard core is sufficient:
\[
 {\mathfrak C}_\star\ll_{W,\Phi,a,b,\eta,\rho}
 xD L^{-4-\eta}.                                      \tag{TB-HARD}
\]
If (TB-HARD) holds uniformly over the source-admissible labels, then
\[
 {\mathfrak C}_{\rm off}=o(xD L^{-4}),
\]
so (TB-COV4) of fact 9e1ff55fe17bc513 holds. Hence the top-band genuine-prime block and discrepancy are \(o(x/\log x)\), and the selected same-\(N\) negative discrepancy of fact 1de7f7c45ccfee10 is forced into the \(d>x^{1/2}\) divisor-switched component.

Thus after the complete singular-main cancellation and exact error interface of fact 54f71c4dcc1bc9bb, the smallest remaining top-band assertion may be taken to be the one-sided hard-core estimate (TB-HARD): only pairs with polylogarithmically large difference and polylogarithmically small gcd remain. No assertion that (TB-HARD) is proved is made.
bc46ed5832faeade.proof:
Because \(\Phi\) is supported in \([1/2,2]\), every \(d\in{\cal I}_D\) lies in \([D/2,2D]\). The lower source bound and the fixed value of \(B_{\rm src}\) imply
\[
 D\ge \tfrac12x^{1/2}L^{-B_{\rm src}},
\]
so \(D/T_x\to\infty\).

For each fixed \(d_1\in[D/2,2D]\), there are at most \(2D/T_x+1\) integers \(d_2\) with \(0<|d_1-d_2|\le D/T_x\). Hence
\[
 \# {\cal Z}_\Delta\ll D(D/T_x+1)\ll D^2/T_x.           \tag{3}
\]
For the gcd zone, group pairs according to their exact gcd \(g\). Since \(d_i\le2D\), necessarily \(g\le2D\). For a fixed \(g\), the number of ordered pairs of multiples of \(g\) in \([D/2,2D]\) is at most
\[
 (2D/g+1)^2\le(4D/g)^2.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \# {\cal Z}_g
 \le\sum_{T_x\le g\le2D}16D^2/g^2
 \ll D^2/T_x.                                           \tag{4}
\]
The additional difference restriction in the definition of \({\cal Z}_g\) can only reduce this count.

For a fixed pair \(d_1,d_2\), a nonzero summand in the inner \(m\)-sum requires \(W(d_1m/x)\ne0\). Since \(W\) is supported in \([a,b]\) and \(d_1\asymp D\), the number of possible positive integers \(m\) is
\[
 \ll_{a,b}x/D+1\ll_{a,b}x/D.                            \tag{5}
\]
Here the last inequality follows from \(D\le2x^{1/2}\). Also \(V_{d,m}\ll_{W,\Phi}1\), while
\[
 0\le\Lambda_{\rm pr}(n)\le\log(2x)\ll L
\]
for every argument occurring in the sum. Thus the absolute value of the inner correlation for one pair is
\[
 \ll_{W,\Phi,a,b}(x/D)L^2.                              \tag{6}
\]
Multiplying (6) by the pair counts (3) and (4), and using \(|\mu|\le1\) and boundedness of \(\Phi\), proves
\[
 |{\mathfrak C}_{{\cal Z}_\Delta}|+
 |{\mathfrak C}_{{\cal Z}_g}|
 \ll (D^2/T_x)(x/D)L^2
 =xD L^{-4-\eta-\rho},
\]
which is (1).

Fact 9e1ff55fe17bc513 gives
\[
 {\mathfrak D}_{\rm diag}\ll xL^2.
\]
Since \(D\ge\tfrac12x^{1/2}L^{-B_{\rm src}}\) and \(B_{\rm src},\eta\) are fixed,
\[
 {xL^2\over xDL^{-4-\eta}}
 ={L^{6+\eta}\over D}\longrightarrow0.
\]
This proves (2).

The three zones form a disjoint partition of all ordered distinct pairs, so exactly
\[
 {\mathfrak C}_{\rm off}
 ={\mathfrak C}_{{\cal Z}_\Delta}
  +{\mathfrak C}_{{\cal Z}_g}
  +{\mathfrak C}_\star.                                \tag{7}
\]
Assume (TB-HARD). Because \(\eta>0\), equations (1) and (7) give the one-sided upper bound
\[
 {\mathfrak C}_{\rm off}\le o(xDL^{-4}).                 \tag{8}
\]
A lower bound of the same required strength follows without a two-sided hard-core hypothesis. The exact dispersion identity in fact 9e1ff55fe17bc513 is
\[
 {\mathfrak D}_N={\mathfrak D}_{\rm diag}+{\mathfrak C}_{\rm off},
\]
and \({\mathfrak D}_N\ge0\) because it is a sum of squared absolute values. Hence
\[
 {\mathfrak C}_{\rm off}\ge-{\mathfrak D}_{\rm diag}
 =-o(xDL^{-4})
\]
by (2). Together with (8), this proves
\[
 {\mathfrak C}_{\rm off}=o(xDL^{-4}),
\]
which is (TB-COV4). The remaining consequences are exactly those proved in facts 9e1ff55fe17bc513 and 54f71c4dcc1bc9bb.

glossary.TB-HARD: the one-sided hard-core covariance upper bound at xD(log x)^(-4-eta)
glossary.cal Z_delta: the off-diagonal modulus pairs with small difference
glossary.cal Z_g: the remaining off-diagonal modulus pairs with gcd at least T_x
glossary.cal Z_star: the hard-core pairs with difference greater than D/T_x and gcd less than T_x
glossary.mathfrak C_star: the signed literal prime-pair covariance restricted to the hard core

bc591aa66c8b299b.title: FREQUENCY-CONCENTRATION PASCADI MATCH AND CRITICAL \(MN\)-TERM NO-FIT
bc591aa66c8b299b.author: slava chan
bc591aa66c8b299b.statement:
FREQUENCY-CONCENTRATION PASCADI MATCH AND CRITICAL \(MN\)-TERM NO-FIT.

Assume the hypotheses and notation of facts \(ffa8f6d3f766b9f5\) and
\(7264046d8776d59f\). Fix \(S>1\), \({\bf t}\in\mathbb R^2\), and a
centered nonzero residue interval
\[
 {\cal K}=\{k\pmod S:0<\|k\|_S\le K_0\},
 \qquad 1\le K_0\le S/2.
\]
Write
\[
 A^*_{S,{\bf t}}(r)={\bf1}_{r\ne0}A_{S,{\bf t}}(r).
\]
On \(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\), define the finite complex measures
\[
 \nu_{S,{\bf t}}
 =\frac1S\sum_{z\ ({\rm mod}\ S)}
 Z_{S,{\bf t}}(z)\,\delta_{-z/S},\qquad
 \mu_{S,{\bf t}}
 =\sum_m f_{\bf t}(m)\,\delta_{m/S}.                    \tag{1}
\]
With
\[
 \check\omega(n)=\int_{\mathbb R/\mathbb Z}e(n\theta)\,d\omega(\theta),
\]
one has exactly
\[
 \check\nu_{S,{\bf t}}(r)=A^*_{S,{\bf t}}(r),\qquad
 \check\mu_{S,{\bf t}}(k)=B_{S,{\bf t}}(k),             \tag{2}
\]
and
\[
 |\nu_{S,{\bf t}}|(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)
 =\frac1S\sum_z|Z_{S,{\bf t}}(z)|,\qquad
 |\mu_{S,{\bf t}}|(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)\ll_\chi M_0.    \tag{3}
\]

For \(L_1,L_2>0\) and \(\theta_1,\theta_2\in\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\), put
\[
 T_{L_1,L_2}(\theta_1,\theta_2)
 =\min_{n\ge1}\{n+L_1\|n\theta_1\|+L_2\|n\theta_2\|\}.
\]
The frequency-concentration bilinear Kloosterman estimate of Pascadi,
arXiv:2404.04239v3, Proposition “Bilinear Kloosterman bound with
frequency concentration”, together with its displayed
arithmetic-progression variant, gives the direct bound
\[
\begin{split}
 &\left|
 \sum_{r\ ({\rm mod}\ S)}A^*_{S,{\bf t}}(r)
 \sum_{k\in{\cal K}}B_{S,{\bf t}}(k)S(r,Nk;S)
 \right|\\
 &\quad\ll_\varepsilon S^\varepsilon
 \iint\left\{
 S\,T_{S,K_0}(\theta_1,\theta_2)+SK_0
 \right\}
 d|\nu_{S,{\bf t}}|(\theta_1)
 d|\mu_{S,{\bf t}}|(\theta_2).                         \tag{4}
\end{split}
\]
The centered band is the union of at most two ordinary residue intervals,
so this changes only the implied constant. The multiplier \(N\) is a unit
modulo \(S\), as required.

The \(SK_0\) term occurring in the published right-hand side of (4),
after the \(S^{-2}\) normalization of the TMC contribution, is
\[
 \ll_{\chi,\varepsilon}
 S^\varepsilon\frac{K_0M_0}{S^2}
 \sum_{z\ ({\rm mod}\ S)}|Z_{S,{\bf t}}(z)|.            \tag{5}
\]
At the natural critical scale \(K_0\asymp S/M_0\), this is
\[
 \ll S^\varepsilon\,\frac1S\sum_z|Z_{S,{\bf t}}(z)|.    \tag{6}
\]
Thus this published theorem accepts the full \(r\)-axis through the exact
physical Fourier measure (1), but it does not by itself give a
critical-band logarithmic gain: its stated right-hand side retains the
endpoint \(\ell^1\) physical-row quantity (6).  A useful application would
need an independent logarithmically saving estimate for the literal
signed row \(Z_{S,{\bf t}}\), or a strengthening which cancels the
\(SK_0\) modular-hyperbola term. This is a scoped direct-theorem no-fit,
not a lower bound for the literal TMC sum and not an impossibility theorem.
bc591aa66c8b299b.proof:
Fact \(7264046d8776d59f\) proves
\[
 Z_{S,{\bf t}}(z)
 =\sum_{r\ne0}A_{S,{\bf t}}(r)e_S(rz).
\]
Fourier inversion therefore gives
\[
 A^*_{S,{\bf t}}(r)
 =\frac1S\sum_z Z_{S,{\bf t}}(z)e_S(-rz)
 =\check\nu_{S,{\bf t}}(r),
\]
including \(r=0\), where both sides vanish. The definition of
\(B_{S,{\bf t}}\) gives the second identity in (2). Total variation gives
(3), using the \(O_\chi(M_0)\)-point support and boundedness of
\(f_{\bf t}\).

Pascadi's proposition bounds two coefficient sequences on integer
intervals of lengths \(L_1,L_2\) by the double integral of
\[
 S\,T_{L_1,L_2}(\theta_1,\theta_2)
 +\gcd(a,S)L_1L_2
\]
against representing measures. Its adjacent arithmetic-progression
variant replaces the common multiplier by separate integer multipliers;
for \(S(r,Nk;S)\), these are \(1,N\), and the gcd factor is one because
\((N,S)=1\). Apply it with \(L_1=S\), \(L_2=K_0\), and the measures (1).
Splitting the centered \(k\)-set into its positive and negative intervals
proves (4). Substituting (3) into the \(SK_0\) part and multiplying by
\(S^{-2}\) proves (5); the critical relation proves (6). The final
paragraph only compares the printed upper-bound term with the requested
logarithmic saving.

glossary.MN-term: the length-product modular-hyperbola term in the frequency-concentration theorem
glossary.mu_{S,bold t}: the physical bounded-variation measure representing the k coefficient
glossary.nu_{S,bold t}: the physical bounded-variation measure representing the centered full r-axis

bc99edbd6281b83b.title: Fix B>0 and a real number vartheta_AP with 1/2<vartheta_AP<1. As x tends to infinity put D_*=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B) and Q_lvl=x^(vartheta_AP). Let psi be a real cutoff with psi(u)=1 for u>=2, and let Phi be the nonnegative smooth dyadic partition constructed in fact 3ef233e014331fc3. Let D be the least positive power of two with D>=2D_*, and define lambda_D(d)=mu(d)psi(d/D_*)Phi(d/D) for positive integers d. Fix real numbers 1<alpha<beta<2 and put c_Phi=min_{alpha<=t<=beta}Phi(t), which is positive. For each x let V_x be an arbitrary finite complex linear combination of sequences which are triply well-factorable of level Q_lvl in the sense reproduced in fact 3bcd070f8558ce6f. Then, uniformly over the choice of V_x,
bc99edbd6281b83b.author: slava chan
bc99edbd6281b83b.statement:
Fix B>0 and a real number vartheta_AP with 1/2<vartheta_AP<1. As x tends to infinity put D_*=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B) and Q_lvl=x^(vartheta_AP). Let psi be a real cutoff with psi(u)=1 for u>=2, and let Phi be the nonnegative smooth dyadic partition constructed in fact 3ef233e014331fc3. Let D be the least positive power of two with D>=2D_*, and define lambda_D(d)=mu(d)psi(d/D_*)Phi(d/D) for positive integers d. Fix real numbers 1<alpha<beta<2 and put c_Phi=min_{alpha<=t<=beta}Phi(t), which is positive. For each x let V_x be an arbitrary finite complex linear combination of sequences which are triply well-factorable of level Q_lvl in the sense reproduced in fact 3bcd070f8558ce6f. Then, uniformly over the choice of V_x,

sum_{D<d<2D}|lambda_D(d)-V_x(d)| >= [c_Phi(beta-alpha)+o(1)]D/log D,

sum_{D<d<2D}|lambda_D(d)-V_x(d)|^2 >= [c_Phi^2(beta-alpha)+o(1)]D/log D.

Consequently the raw high-divisor weight cannot be approximated by such finite same-level combinations with l1 error o(D/log D), nor with l2 error o((D/log D)^(1/2)), on its own dyadic support. This is a coefficient-norm obstruction only: it does not rule out cancellation-based transforms, changed moduli or levels, a different coefficient class, or approximation in a weaker problem-specific seminorm.
bc99edbd6281b83b.proof:
Fact 3ef233e014331fc3 constructs Phi as an infinitely differentiable function which is strictly positive on (1/2,2). Since [alpha,beta] is a compact subinterval of (1/2,2), continuity gives c_Phi>0.

By fact 3bcd070f8558ce6f, for all sufficiently large x the selected D satisfies D>Q_lvl^(1/3). That fact also reproduces the definition of triply well-factorable level-Q_lvl sequences and proves, by taking the balanced factorization Q_lvl=Q_lvl^(1/3)Q_lvl^(1/3)Q_lvl^(1/3), that every such sequence vanishes at every prime ell>Q_lvl^(1/3). Therefore every finite complex linear combination V_x of such sequences satisfies V_x(ell)=0 at every prime ell with alpha D<=ell<=beta D. This conclusion is independent of the number of summands and their coefficients, so it is uniform in V_x.

For each prime ell in this interval, one has ell>D>=2D_*, so psi(ell/D_*)=1, and mu(ell)=-1. Hence lambda_D(ell)=-Phi(ell/D). Since ell/D belongs to [alpha,beta],
|lambda_D(ell)-V_x(ell)|=Phi(ell/D)>=c_Phi,
and
|lambda_D(ell)-V_x(ell)|^2>=c_Phi^2.

The Prime Number Theorem in Subham De, arXiv:2308.16303, Theorem 2.2.1, states that the prime-counting function pi(y) satisfies pi(y)~y/log y as y tends to infinity. Because alpha and beta are fixed and D tends to infinity with x, it follows by subtraction that
pi(beta D)-pi(alpha D)=[beta-alpha+o(1)]D/log D.
Restricting each displayed sum in the statement to these primes and applying the preceding pointwise inequalities gives respectively
sum_{D<d<2D}|lambda_D(d)-V_x(d)| >= c_Phi[pi(beta D)-pi(alpha D)]
and
sum_{D<d<2D}|lambda_D(d)-V_x(d)|^2 >= c_Phi^2[pi(beta D)-pi(alpha D)].
These are the claimed asymptotic lower bounds. The two non-approximation consequences follow immediately; the final sentence only records the scope of the argument.

glossary.V_x: an arbitrary x-dependent finite complex linear combination of triply well-factorable sequences of level Q_lvl
glossary.beta: a fixed real number satisfying alpha<beta<2
glossary.c_Phi: the positive minimum of Phi on the compact interval [alpha,beta]

bd1ef0652fa7b940.title: JOINT-COPRIMALITY REMOVAL FOR CORRELATED RECIPROCAL ENERGY
bd1ef0652fa7b940.author: slava chan

be21aada9cf60ec5.title: Let m>1 be odd, let s belong to {1,-1}, let K be coprime to m, and let W be a complex-valued function modulo m with
be21aada9cf60ec5.author: slava chan
be21aada9cf60ec5.statement:
Let m>1 be odd, let s belong to {1,-1}, let K be coprime to m, and let W be a complex-valued function modulo m with
W_hat(ell)=sum_{u modulo m}W(u)e_m(-ell u).
Let G be the unit group modulo m^2. Form the matrix M_W^{(2)} whose rows are indexed by (a,c) in G times G and whose columns are indexed by (b,d) in G times G:
M_W^{(2)}((a,c),(b,d))
 =sum_{u modulo m}W(u)
  Delta_{m^2}(ab-K-2smu) Delta_{m^2}(cd-K+2smu).                      (1)
Let P_digit^{(2)} be its projective ell^2 tensor norm across this row-column grouping:
P_digit^{(2)}
 =inf_{M_W^{(2)}=sum_j Beta_j tensor Alpha_j}
       sum_j||Beta_j||_2||Alpha_j||_2.                                (2)
Then the singular values of M_W^{(2)} are
|W_hat(ell)|, ell modulo m,
each repeated exactly phi(m^2)^2/m times. Consequently,
P_digit^{(2)}
 =[phi(m^2)^2/m]sum_{ell modulo m}|W_hat(ell)|.                        (3)

For a fixed digit W=1_{u=u_0}, one has P_digit^{(2)}=phi(m^2)^2. For the full unweighted digit union W=1, one again has
P_digit^{(2)}=phi(m^2)^2,
whereas the sum of the m fixed-digit projective norms is
m phi(m^2)^2. Thus exact assembly removes a factor m in the simultaneous two-product selector as well.

For the literal interval multiplicity weight W_{U,m} of fact 5f60a4633e6b0b70,
P_{U,m}^{(2)}/phi(m^2)^2
 <=2(U_cut-1)/m+4(1+log m).                                           (4)
In particular, with X=ceil(LH^3), U_cut=2X and
H^(3-delta)<m<=2X, the normalized two-product digit cost is
<<_L H^delta+log(2H); if m>=cH^3, it is <<_{L,c}log(2H).

Every normalized state of fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb with q=2m and common sign s satisfies the exact integer identities
ab=K+2smu, cd=K-2smu.
Hence (1) is the simultaneous modular normal-digit selector aligned with the determinant-shell grouping (a,c) versus (b,d). The calculation still omits the exact determinant equality beyond its modular consequence, coefficient windows, recovered-prime and exact-gcd selectors, the C-coupling relation, signs beyond fixed s, masks, and source weights. Therefore (3)-(4) are a scoped two-product projective tax, not automatically the Bettin--Chandee Pi_BC of fact b1398db2962d7491 and not a cancellation estimate.
be21aada9cf60ec5.proof:
Let
H={1+mt modulo m^2:t modulo m}
inside G. As proved in fact 308b3f12b1d814db, H is an order-m subgroup isomorphic to the additive residues modulo m, and |G|=phi(m^2). Put gamma=2sK^(-1) modulo m. Then
K+2smu=K(1+m gamma u),
K-2smu=K(1-m gamma u) modulo m^2.                                    (5)

Invert both column coordinates, replacing (b,d) by (b^(-1),d^(-1)), and translate both row coordinates by K, replacing (a,c) by (Ka,Kc). These are unitary row and column permutations. After them, the matrix is supported on differences
(a b^(-1),c d^(-1))
 =(1+m gamma u,1-m gamma u).                                         (6)
The set
H_anti={(1+mt,1-mt):t modulo m}
is a subgroup of G times G: multiplication adds t modulo m because all cross terms contain m^2. It has order m. Formula (6) says that the transformed matrix is convolution on G times G by a weight supported on H_anti, with coefficient W(gamma^(-1)t) at its element indexed by t.

Such convolution is block diagonal over the cosets of H_anti. There are
|G times G|/|H_anti|=phi(m^2)^2/m
cosets. After choosing a representative of a coset and identifying H_anti with the additive residues t modulo m, every block is the same m by m circulant matrix with kernel W composed with multiplication by gamma^(-1). Its singular values are |W_hat(ell)|, ell modulo m, because additive characters diagonalize a circulant and multiplication by the unit gamma only permutes the frequencies. Thus the displayed singular values have exactly the claimed multiplicity.

The equality between the projective norm (2) and the nuclear norm follows from the singular-value decomposition and polar-duality argument given in fact 308b3f12b1d814db. Summing the singular values proves (3). For one fixed digit, every |W_hat(ell)| equals one, so (3) equals
[phi(m^2)^2/m]m=phi(m^2)^2.
For W identically one, only W_hat(0)=m is nonzero and the same value results. Summing over the m fixed digits proves the factor-m comparison.

For W_{U,m}, insert the Fourier l1 estimate of fact 5f60a4633e6b0b70 into (3) and divide by phi(m^2)^2 to obtain (4). The near-maximal specializations are exactly those proved in that fact. Finally, fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb gives v=sm and ab=K+2uv, cd=K-2uv on q=2m, which proves the normalized-state specialization and the stated scope.

glossary.H_anti: the anti-diagonal order-m subgroup in the square of the unit group modulo m^2
glossary.M_W^{(2)}: the simultaneous shared-digit two-product matrix grouped as (a,c) versus (b,d)
glossary.P_digit^{(2)}: the projective ell^2 tensor norm of M_W^{(2)}

be4e5ad5378f0122.title: Let p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4 be distinct odd primes and put P=p_1p_2p_3p_4. Write e_m(x)=exp(2 pi i x/m). Let q,q' be integers at least 2 such that gcd(qq',P)=1 and qq'<P. For a unit q modulo P, write q^{-1} for its inverse modulo P and define the companion column
be4e5ad5378f0122.author: slava chan
be4e5ad5378f0122.statement: Let p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4 be distinct odd primes and put P=p_1p_2p_3p_4. Write e_m(x)=exp(2 pi i x/m). Let q,q' be integers at least 2 such that gcd(qq',P)=1 and qq'C be an arbitrary function and center it by f_{i,q}(x)=w_{i,q}(x)-p_i^{-1}sum_{y modulo p_i}w_{i,q}(y). Define fhat_{i,q}(a)=sum_{x modulo p_i}f_{i,q}(x)e_{p_i}(-ax), rho_i(h)=h(P/p_i)^{-1} modulo p_i, and the centered four-window CRT multiplier M_q(h)=product_{i=1}^4 fhat_{i,q}(rho_i(h)). Then M_q(h)=0 unless gcd(h,P)=1. (D) For arbitrary q-dependent centered functions as in (C), define the weighted collision kernel K_{q,q'}(z)=sum_{h modulo P}M_q(h)overline(M_{q'}(h))e_P(hz). For z_i=z modulo p_i and C_{i;q,q'}(z_i)=sum_{x modulo p_i}f_{i,q}(x)overline(f_{i,q'}(x-z_i)), one has the exact CRT factorization K_{q,q'}(z)=P product_{i=1}^4 C_{i;q,q'}(z_i). Consequently the exact q-dependent weighted companion Gram G_w(q,q')= sum_{h modulo P}M_q(h)V_{P,q}(h) overline(M_{q'}(h)V_{P,q'}(h)) is G_w(q,q')= sum_{1<=u0 and define the normalized operator Gram by Gamma_{q,q'}=G_w(q',q)/sqrt(E_qE_{q'}) =sum_h overline(C_q(h))C_{q'}(h)/sqrt(E_qE_{q'}). If T:C^{Q_set}->l^2(Z/PZ) sends the q-th standard basis vector to C_q/sqrt(E_q), then T^*T=Gamma. Therefore the literal normalized centered weighted-Gram estimate needed for a delta-flat companion compression is exactly ||Gamma-I||_op<=delta, equivalently, for every coefficient vector a=(a_q), |sum_{q,q'}overline(a_q)(Gamma_{q,q'}-1_{q=q'})a_{q'}| <=delta sum_q|a_q|^2. A Bessel bound ||Gamma||_op<=B is equivalently ||T||^2<=B. Parts (A)-(D) show that full-h companion orthogonality or a full-h HAPD calculation cannot be transferred automatically to the actual centered four-window columns: centering deletes all nonprimitive frequencies, the primitive Gram has proper-divisor terms, and the actual kernel contains q-dependent interval correlations. No estimate with delta<1, no compression-flatness, and no common-cone property for the actual weighted columns is asserted.
be4e5ad5378f0122.proof:
For (A), expand the Gram and use complete additive-character orthogonality:
sum_{h modulo P}V_{P,q}(h)overline(V_{P,q'}(h))
=sum_{1<=u<q}sum_{1<=u'<q'}sum_{h modulo P}
 e_P(h(u'q'^{-1}-uq^{-1})).
The inner h-sum is P exactly when
u'q'^{-1}=uq^{-1} modulo P, equivalently u'q=uq' modulo P, and is zero otherwise. Both positive integers u'q and uq' are strictly less than qq'<P. Hence the congruence is an integer equality. Write q=g alpha and q'=g beta with g=gcd(q,q') and gcd(alpha,beta)=1. Then u'q=uq' becomes u'alpha=u beta. Coprimality gives u=k alpha and u'=k beta for a unique integer k, and the strict ranges are equivalent to 1<=k<g. There are g-1 solutions, proving (A).

For (B), the same expansion with h restricted to units gives
G_prim(q,q')=
sum_{u,u'}c_P(u'q'^{-1}-uq^{-1}).
The elementary Ramanujan identity
c_P(n)=sum_{d dividing P, n=0 modulo d}d mu(P/d)
follows by writing 1_{gcd(h,P)=1}=sum_{d dividing gcd(h,P)}mu(d), interchanging sums, and applying complete additive-character orthogonality. Since q and q' are units modulo every d dividing P,
u'q'^{-1}-uq^{-1}=0 modulo d
is equivalent after multiplication by qq' to u'q-uq'=0 modulo d. Interchanging the u,u' and d sums proves the divisor formula. If q=q'=2, there is one pair u=u'=1. Thus the full Gram from (A) is P, while the primitive Gram is c_P(0)=phi(P). This proves both the formula and the fact that the proper-divisor correction can be nonzero.

For (C), centering gives fhat_{i,q}(0)=0. If gcd(h,P)>1, then p_i divides h for at least one i because P is squarefree. For that i, rho_i(h)=0 modulo p_i, so the corresponding factor in M_q(h) vanishes. Hence M_q is supported on primitive h.

For (D), the map h modulo P -> (rho_1(h),rho_2(h),rho_3(h),rho_4(h)) is a CRT bijection. Also, if z_i is z modulo p_i, then
e_P(hz)=product_i e_{p_i}(rho_i(h)z_i).
Therefore K_{q,q'} factors as the product over i of
sum_{a modulo p_i}fhat_{i,q}(a)overline(fhat_{i,q'}(a))e_{p_i}(az_i).
Expanding the two Fourier transforms and summing over a gives
p_i sum_{x modulo p_i}f_{i,q}(x)overline(f_{i,q'}(x-z_i)}
=p_i C_{i;q,q'}(z_i).
Multiplying the four local identities proves
K_{q,q'}(z)=P product_i C_{i;q,q'}(z_i).

Next expand V_{P,q} and the conjugate of V_{P,q'} inside G_w. Their product contributes the phase
e_P(h(u'q'^{-1}-uq^{-1})).
The h-sum is exactly K_{q,q'} at that collision shift, proving the weighted Gram formula. For interval indicators, expand
f_{i,q}=1_{I_{i,q}}-L_{i,q}/p_i
inside C_{i;q,q'}. The indicator-indicator term counts
I_{i,q} intersect (I_{i,q'}+z_i);
the two cross terms and constant term combine to
-L_{i,q}L_{i,q'}/p_i.
This proves the interval-correlation specialization.

For (E), a set partition is an equivalence relation and is weighted in the fourth joint cumulant by the Mobius coefficient of the partition lattice, (-1)^{|pi|-1}(|pi|-1)!. A support face is a subset selected by expanding
product_{i=1}^4(1-X_i)=sum_{F subset {1,2,3,4}}(-1)^{|F|}product_{i in F}X_i.
There are respectively 15 and 16 such indices, and their coefficients depend on different statistics, namely number of blocks and subset cardinality. Applying both exact expansions produces their Cartesian product and coefficient
(-1)^{|pi|-1}(|pi|-1)!(-1)^{|F|}.
Thus neither structure absorbs the other.

For (F), the (q,q') entry of T^*T in the standard convention is
sum_h overline(C_q(h))C_{q'}(h)/sqrt(E_qE_{q'})
=G_w(q',q)/sqrt(E_qE_{q'})
=Gamma_{q,q'}.
The diagonal entries equal one. The displayed standard Hermitian quadratic-form inequality is exactly the operator-norm inequality ||Gamma-I||_op<=delta. Likewise ||T||^2=||T^*T||_op=||Gamma||_op. These are equivalences, not estimates.

Finally, (C) shows that the actual centered multiplier discards every nonprimitive h. The example q=q'=2 in (B) shows that even the flat primitive Gram differs from the full Gram. Formula (D) adds the literal q-dependent collision correlations. Hence (A) alone cannot imply a bound for Gamma, and the final non-assertion follows.

glossary.C_{i;q,q'}: local centered cyclic correlation of the two q-dependent window weights
glossary.G_prim: Gram matrix of flat companion columns restricted to primitive frequencies modulo P
glossary.G_w: q-dependent weighted companion pairing in the order C_q times conjugate C_q'
glossary.Gamma: standard normalized operator Gram with entries G_w(q',q)/sqrt(E_qE_q')
glossary.M_q: product of the four centered local Fourier multipliers
glossary.N_d(q,q'): number of companion integer pairs colliding modulo d
glossary.P: product p_1p_2p_3p_4 of four distinct odd primes
glossary.Pow({1,2,3,4}): power set indexing the sixteen support faces
glossary.V_{P,q}: flat companion column indexed by the external unit q
glossary.rho_i: CRT local frequency projection h(P/p_i)^{-1} modulo p_i

be534c7b21bd963f.title: IRVING FIXED-MOMENT NO-FIT ON THE IDEALLY BALANCED ACTUAL-Z_MID RECIPROCAL CELL
be534c7b21bd963f.author: slava chan
be534c7b21bd963f.statement:
IRVING FIXED-MOMENT NO-FIT ON THE IDEALLY BALANCED ACTUAL-Z_MID RECIPROCAL CELL.

Let Q tend to infinity, put
B=Q^(4/3),  L=M=B^(1/2)=Q^(2/3),
and let k>=1 be fixed. Consider the ideal separated bilinear reciprocal form accepted by Irving's average-modulus theorem:
S_k=sum_{Q<=q<2Q} max_{(c,q)=1}
 |sum_{l asymp L,m asymp M,(lm,q)=1}
   alpha_l beta_m e_q(c(lm)^(-1))|,
where the two coefficient sequences are bounded. Irving, arXiv:1301.6372, Lemma 3.1, gives
S_k<<_epsilon Q^(1+epsilon)
 [Q^(1/(2k))L^((2k-1)/(2k))M^(1/2)
  +L^((2k-1)/(2k))M].                                      (1)
At the displayed balanced lengths, the first term on the right of (1) is
Q^(2+1/(6k)+epsilon).                                       (2)
In particular, for k=3 it is Q^(2+1/18+epsilon).             (3)

The endpoint target for one actual-Z_mid tensor in fact 050efa07f87f374a is Q^(2-delta) for a fixed delta>0, or Q^(2+o(1)) at the nonsaving endpoint. Therefore direct application of (1) with any one fixed k does not prove either target even after granting all of the following favorable simplifications for free: exact balanced factorization of the b-variable, complete separation of every actual weight and mask, legality of both coefficient lengths, and deletion of the second nonnegative term in (1). The actual second term, Type-I cells, unbalanced cells, squarefree composite conductor projection and source masks are not used in this no-fit.

This is only a right-hand-side no-fit for direct use of Irving's fixed-k Lemma 3.1 on the ideal balanced cell. It is not a lower bound for the actual sum and does not exclude a theorem uniform in a growing moment, a different decomposition, pre-Cauchy cancellation between cells, the joint energy MZB-ENERGY of fact 050efa07f87f374a, or a complete small-g estimate.
be534c7b21bd963f.proof:
The exact theorem statement (1) is reproduced and applied in the proofs of facts dd7f18552d39e5d4 and 528c091515d833fc. Substitute L=M=Q^(2/3) into its first term. The exponent of Q, before epsilon, is
1+1/(2k)+(2/3)(2k-1)/(2k)+(2/3)(1/2).
Since
(2/3)(2k-1)/(2k)=2/3-1/(3k)
and
(2/3)(1/2)=1/3,
the exponent is
1+1/(2k)+2/3-1/(3k)+1/3
 =2+1/(6k).
This proves (2), and k=3 gives (3).

For every fixed k, 1/(6k)>0. Hence the theorem's displayed upper bound contains a term larger than Q^2 by a fixed positive power and cannot imply Q^(2+o(1)), much less Q^(2-delta), by direct domination. Discarding the other term only strengthens the hypothetical application, so its presence is irrelevant to this no-fit.
