Fact 050efa07f87f374a identifies Q^2 as the actual tensor target after the outer b norm and gives the distinct joint energy interface. The remaining scope clauses follow because no claim about the true size of S_k or the actual packet was made.

glossary.S_k: the ideal balanced average-modulus bilinear reciprocal form to which Irving's fixed-k theorem is directly applied
glossary.balanced actual-Z_mid reciprocal cell: the favorable hypothetical factorization B=LM with L=M=Q^(2/3) at B=Q^(4/3)

be6fb90ce3095e82.title: MAYNARD TYPE-II PAYMENT OF A FACTORABLE-MODULUS MARKED rho_{1/2} SECTOR. Fix real A>0 and an integer K>=1. Let B be sufficiently large, let delta be real, and let Q_1,R_1,P,M>=2 satisfy
be6fb90ce3095e82.author: slava chan
be6fb90ce3095e82.statement:
MAYNARD TYPE-II PAYMENT OF A FACTORABLE-MODULUS MARKED rho_{1/2} SECTOR. Fix real A>0 and an integer K>=1. Let B be sufficiently large, let delta be real, and let Q_1,R_1,P,M>=2 satisfy
Q_1R_1=B^(1/2+delta), PM asymptotic to B,                        (1)
B^(6delta)(log B)^C<=R_1<=B^(1/10-3delta)(log B)^(-C),           (2)
Q_1B^(2delta)(log B)^C<=P<=B^(1/2-3delta)(log B)^(-C),           (3)
where C=C(A,K)>0 is sufficiently large. Put Q_0=Q_1R_1 and let c be a positive integer.

Let cal S be a set of ordered pairs (q,r) with
Q_1<=q<2Q_1, R_1<=r<2R_1,                                      (4)
such that (q,r) maps injectively to s=qr, every s is squarefree, and (s,c)=1. For each (q,r) in cal S choose a unit residue a_{q,r} modulo s and a function V_s supported on B<=n<2B with |V_s(n)|<=L.

Let cal P, omega_P, b_{P,c}^{rho}, D_s^{rho,med}, T_s^{rho}, and E_s^{rho} be those of fact e59f666ecac4d4cb. Assume that there are finitely many indices j, complex numbers lambda_{j,s}, sequences A_j(p) supported on primes P<=p<2P, and sequences B_j(m) supported on M<=m<2M such that
V_s(pm)=sum_j lambda_{j,s}A_j(p)B_j(m)                           (5)
for every prime p in [P,2P) and every positive integer m. Assume
sum_j sup_{s=qr,(q,r) in cal S}|lambda_{j,s}|<=L_{proj,rho},      (6)
|A_j(n)|<=tau_K(n), |B_j(n)|<=tau_K(n),                          (7)
and every sequence alpha_{j,n}=1_{n prime}A_j(n) satisfies Maynard's Siegel-Walfisz condition uniformly in j and in all displayed parameters.

Then
sum_{(q,r) in cal S}|D_{qr}^{rho,med}|
 <<_{A,K}L_{proj,rho}B(log B)^(-A)
 +L(1+log(2BQ_0))^2
  [B/P+Q_0P+omega_P(c)(B/P+Q_0)].                               (8)
In particular, if L and L_{proj,rho} are at most fixed powers of log B and the three correction quantities
B/P, Q_0P, omega_P(c)(B/P+Q_0)                                  (9)
are each at most B times a sufficiently large negative power of log B, the complete marked rho_{1/2} sector in (8) is O_A(B(log B)^(-A)).

The residue a_{q,r} may vary arbitrarily because Maynard's theorem takes a supremum over primitive residues. A signed outer coefficient of modulus at most one on each s-row is harmless after the absolute value in (8). No estimate is asserted when the modulus has no factor R_1 satisfying (2), when no prime scale P satisfies (3), on omega_P(n)=0, or for a nonprojective V_s. No complete HC-MED or critical-tail payment is asserted.
be6fb90ce3095e82.proof:
For s=qr define the unrestricted row
T'_s=-1/2 sum_{p in cal P}sum_m b_{P,c}^{rho}(m)V_s(pm)
 [1_{pm congruent a_{q,r} (mod s)}
  -phi(s)^(-1)1_{(pm,s)=1}].                                   (10)
Insert (5). For fixed j put
alpha_p=1_{p prime}A_j(p),
beta_m=b_{P,c}^{rho}(m)B_j(m).                                  (11)
Fact 5999a1878276ac78, a predecessor of fact e59f666ecac4d4cb, gives |rho_{1/2}(m)|<=1. Hence |b_{P,c}^{rho}(m)|<=1, so beta_m is divisor bounded by (7), while alpha_p is divisor bounded and satisfies the assumed Siegel-Walfisz condition.

Maynard, arXiv:2006.08250, Proposition 5.1, in the exact form quoted and applied in predecessor fact 53e70bf4e327e6bd, applies with its variables
x=B, Q=Q_1, R=R_1, N=P, M=M.
Its scale hypotheses are exactly (1)-(3), and its primitive-residue supremum includes every a_{q,r}. Restricting its nonnegative outer absolute sum to cal S, inserting lambda_{j,s}, summing j, and using (6) gives
sum_{(q,r) in cal S}|T'_{qr}|
 <<_{A,K}L_{proj,rho}B(log B)^(-A).                             (12)
The fixed scalar -1/2 only improves this bound.

The exact fractional-Ramaré identity in fact e59f666ecac4d4cb gives
D_s^{rho,med}=T_s^{rho}+E_s^{rho},                              (13)
and
sum_{s in cal S}|E_s^{rho}|
 <<L(1+log(2BQ_0))^2(B/P+Q_0P),                                 (14)
because injectivity makes the products s a set of squarefree moduli in [Q_0,4Q_0), with endpoint constants affecting only the implied constant.

It remains to compare T_s^{rho} and T'_s. Their difference is supported on p|c. Since (s,c)=1, each such p is a unit modulo s. The same elementary count used in fact 53e70bf4e327e6bd gives, for one p, O(B/P+Q_0) total physical incidences after summing the injective modulus family, and O((1+log(2Q_0))^2B/P) for the principal part. The coefficient b_{P,c}^{rho}(m) has modulus at most one and |V_s(pm)|<=L. There are omega_P(c) selected primes p|c. Therefore
sum_{(q,r) in cal S}|T_{qr}^{rho}-T'_{qr}|
 <<L omega_P(c)(1+log(2BQ_0))^2(B/P+Q_0).                       (15)
Combining (12)-(15) proves (8). The final logarithmic-saving assertion follows by choosing the Maynard saving and each explicit correction saving larger than A plus the fixed logarithmic exponents of L and L_{proj,rho}. The assertion about an extra signed row coefficient follows from triangle inequality inside the already absolute outer sum.

glossary.L_{proj,rho}: The projective coefficient norm in the prime/cofactor separation used by the fractional-Mobius Maynard consumer.

be94f5e014ad4d3d.title: COMPLETE SAME-SELECTED-N SAFE SECOND-BUFFER PAYMENT AND NEGATIVE HANDOFF ABOVE \(\beta_2\)
be94f5e014ad4d3d.author: slava chan
be94f5e014ad4d3d.statement:
COMPLETE SAME-SELECTED-N SAFE SECOND-BUFFER PAYMENT AND NEGATIVE HANDOFF ABOVE \(\beta_2\).

Fix \(0<\kappa\le1/100\), put
\[
 \sigma=\kappa/100,\quad \rho=\sigma/5,\quad
 \beta_1=6/5-3\sigma,\quad
 \beta_2=6/5-13\sigma/5=\beta_m-\rho,
 \quad \beta_m=6/5-12\sigma/5,
\]
and fix \(0<\eta<\sigma\) and \(\omega>0\).  Use the fixed selected
bad even integer \(N=2x\), active dyadic labels and smooth source of fact
\(60b26a9b6f79467a\).  Thus every active label has
\[
 DM\asymp x,\qquad RK\asymp x,                                  \tag{1}
\]
the smaller divisor scale in either strict orientation is at most
\(2x^{1/2}\), and the larger divisor scale is forced above
\(x^{9/16-1/200}\).

Let \(T_{\rm postC3,sel}\) be the real same-selected-\(N\) aggregate of
fact \(01b550792363535d\).  It satisfies
\[
 T_{\rm postC3,sel}\le
 -c_{\rm dir}\mathfrak c(N){x\over\log x}
 +o\!\left(\mathfrak c(N){x\over\log x}\right),               \tag{2}
\]
where \(c_{\rm dir}>0\) and \(\mathfrak c(N)\ge C_2>0\).
For an exact outer gcd \(g=(d,r)\), use in the forward orientation
\[
 Q=D/g,\quad B=R/g=Q^\beta,\quad G=M/Q,
\]
and in the reverse orientation
\[
 Q=R/g,\quad B=D/g=Q^\beta,\quad G=K/Q.
\]

Let \(\mathcal R_{2,\rm sel}\) be the complete projection of
\(T_{\rm postC3,sel}\) onto
\[
 \beta_1<\beta\le\beta_2,                                      \tag{3}
\]
with every selected-source, active-scale, fixed-\(U\), high,
smooth/projective, paired-frequency, target-gcd, rough-prime ordering,
equal-cell, collision, deletion, parent, orientation, provenance,
actual-\(G\), and exact outer-\(g\) coordinate recombined to completion
inside that projection.  Equivalently, by the exact ledger, (3) has frozen
parent \(U_{\rm low}\), orientation forward or reverse, residual actual
imbalance
\[
 Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\le G<
 Q^{\Gamma_{BC}(\beta)+\omega},
 \qquad \Gamma_{BC}(\beta)=\max\{0,(19\beta-20)/17\},         \tag{4}
\]
and the exact disjoint standard anatomy list
\[
 A,\ B,\ C1,\ C2,\ C3.                                        \tag{5}
\]

There is a fixed \(\delta_2>0\) such that
\[
 |\mathcal R_{2,\rm sel}|\ll x^{1-\delta_2}.                   \tag{6}
\]
Define
\[
 T_{>\beta_2,\rm sel}
 =T_{\rm postC3,sel}-\mathcal R_{2,\rm sel}.                    \tag{7}
\]
Then
\[
 T_{>\beta_2,\rm sel}\le
 -c_{\rm dir}\mathfrak c(N){x\over\log x}
 +o\!\left(\mathfrak c(N){x\over\log x}\right),               \tag{8}
\]
and every atom of \(T_{>\beta_2,\rm sel}\) has
\[
 \beta>\beta_2.                                                   \tag{9}
\]

No sign is assigned to an individual anatomy or cell.  No assertion is made
beyond \(\beta_2\), at the moving marker endpoint, or about the
general-marker sliver, endpoint parents, PMD, DCE, four-prime capture,
Goldbach implication, or Goldbach.
be94f5e014ad4d3d.proof:
The exact ledger is immediate but important.  Fact
\(01b550792363535d\) proves that in
\(\beta_1<\beta<\beta_m\) the selected residual has sole parent
\(U_{\rm low}\), the five disjoint standard anatomies (5), both strict
orientations, and precisely the residual \(G\)-range (4), with every other
literal coordinate retained.  Since
\(\beta_2=\beta_m-\sigma/5<\beta_m\), its intersection with (3) is
exactly the aggregate stated above.  No first-buffer estimate is used on
this range.

We prove (6) anatomy by anatomy, always estimating the complete anatomy
coordinate and recombining all its auxiliary partitions before applying a
separated trace.  Fact \(3a07e1cfd1359c45\) supplies the renewed local
complete-frequency estimates uniformly for every
\(1\le\beta\le\beta_2\), in the regimes \(G\ge1\) and
\(Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\le G\le Q^{\sigma-\eta}\).  We now verify the
literal source interfaces rather than cite any first-buffer conclusion
outside its range.

For anatomy \(A\), the normalized interval-prime identity writes the
marked factor as \(up\), with \(up\asymp B\) and \(L<p<Z\).
In a forward layer put \(c=(a,N/g)\), write
\[
 a=cq,\qquad N/g=cL_1.
\]
The exact target-gcd descent of fact \(1c64020b89f097c4\) gives all
required coprimalities and
\[
 e_a(-(N/g)h(up)^{-1})=e_q(-L_1h(up)^{-1}).                        \tag{10}
\]
For \(c\le H_TQ^{\sigma/4}\), the literal Fourier amplitude and (10)
match clause (A) of \(3a07e1cfd1359c45\), including every retained
deletion coordinate.  For larger \(c\), the beta-uniform absolute
target-gcd tail of fact \(5fbdbbebf99aec55\) gives
\(O(Q^{2-\sigma/4+\epsilon})\); its only upper-beta input is
\(B\le Q^{6/5}\), which holds strictly here.  The reverse orientation is
the same after interchanging the divisor-complement pairs and reindexing
the complete real frequency pair by \(h\mapsto-h\); the target in the
renewed local theorem changes sign.  This is exactly the algebraic
source-to-trace derivation in the proof of \(24e911b7685090c1\), whose
beta-dependent analytic input has here been replaced by
\(3a07e1cfd1359c45\).

For anatomy \(B\), the exact marker coefficient is the separated
raised-stopping coefficient
\[
 {(-1)^k\mu(u)1_{j_I(u)=0}\Gamma_{k;L,S_0}(y)
  \over {k+\omega_L(u)\choose k}},qquad (u,y)=1.                \tag{11}
\]
Forward additive reciprocity converts the physical character to fixed
target \(-N/g\), and reverse to \(+N/g\) after the same complete
frequency-sign reindexing.  The high and \(U_{\rm low}\) predicates are
frozen label scalars; source and fixed-\(U\) masks are uniformly
projective; every auxiliary refinement has been recombined in the
definition of \(\mathcal R_{2,\rm sel}\).  Hence (11) matches clause
(B) of \(3a07e1cfd1359c45\).  This repeats the beta-uniform literal
interface proved in \(771d292cffc890c1\), using only the newly verified
trace estimate.

For \(C1\), forward the exact normalized factor is
\(b=vp\), with coefficient \(-\mu(v)\), \(v\le S_0\), all prime
factors of \(v\) at most \(L\), and \(p\ge Z\).  The source equation
\(am+bk=N/g\), Poisson summation in \(m\), and reciprocity give
\[
 e_b((N/g)ha^{-1})
 =e_a(-(N/g)hb^{-1})e((N/g)h/(ab)).                                \tag{12}
\]
The transformed amplitude has the literal \(H_P^{-1}\) prefactor and
arbitrary fixed-order decay in \(F/H_P\); the archimedean factor in
(12) is uniformly projective because
\[
 (N/g)/(QM)=N/(DM)=O(1).                                           \tag{13}
\]
Thus clause (C1) of \(3a07e1cfd1359c45\) applies, including its
multiplier-one short Type-I branch.  Reverse interchange gives target
\(+N/g\) and uses \(N/(RK)=O(1)\).  The same accepted literal
coefficient, prime-order and outer-g collision recombination as in the
algebraic proof of \(efd5ace01f0a6c11\) is unchanged by enlarging beta;
only its former local trace conclusion is replaced here.

For \(C2\), write forward
\(b=vp_1p_2\), with coefficient \(\mu(v)\) and
\(Z\le p_1<p_2\).  Equation (12) applies with this new \(b\).
Unequal prime cells have automatic order.  In an equal cell, recombining
the two stored orderings makes the full coefficient and amplitude symmetric,
so exact symmetrization is full-minus-repeated-prime diagonal.  Clause (C2)
of \(3a07e1cfd1359c45\) includes both terms, every actual frequency, and
the separated-outer subtrace.  The reverse swap, target sign, transformed
amplitude, and complete collision/provenance recombination are identical.
This is the beta-uniform source interface of the accepted proof
\(5051635f817e7a22\), again with the renewed local estimate inserted.

For \(C3\), we spell out the remaining outer-g collision payment.  Forward
write \(b=vp_1p_2p_3\) with coefficient \(-\mu(v)\).
Reciprocity is again (12), and the rescaled Fourier integral has projective
norm
\[
 O((\log x)^2(1+F/H_P)^{-J})
\]
for every fixed \(J\), by (13).  Completing the three conditions
\(p_i\nmid g\) gives the complete trace in clause (C3) of
\(3a07e1cfd1359c45\) plus seven nonempty correction types.  In every
correction at least one prime \(p\ge Z\) is fixed to a divisor of \(g\).
Absolute divisor counting and the complete Fourier \(l^1\)-bound give
total correction
\[
 \ll Q^\epsilon QB/Z
 =Q^{2\beta-1/2+3\sigma+\epsilon}
 \le Q^{19/10-11\sigma/5+\epsilon}
 \ll Q^{19/10-2\sigma}.                                         \tag{14}
\]
Pair/triple collisions and multiple fixed \(g\)-primes are no larger.
Equal-cell symmetrization is already included in clause (C3).  Reverse is
the exact coordinate swap and real \(h\)-pair conjugation, giving target
\(+N/g\).  Thus every literal C3 coordinate is paid.

We verify the remaining uniform physical inputs and sum \(g\).  Forced
high and \(\beta<6/5\) give
\[
 Q^{\beta-1}={\text{larger divisor scale}\over
                   \text{smaller divisor scale}}
 >x^{1/16-1/200+o(1)},
\]
so \(Q\ge x^{c_0}\) for a fixed \(c_0>0\).  Also
\[
 |N/g|\ll x^{1/2+o(1)}Q\le Q^{C_A}
\]
for a fixed \(C_A\).  Fixed constants in the stronger C3 ratio hypothesis
are absorbed, exactly as in \(dde1e246a629bcc4\), by replacing the
ambient \(x\) with one fixed positive multiple; (1), the target size, and
all power exponents are unchanged.

The physical balance also yields an actual fixed lower bound for \(G\).
Hence every actual \(G<1\) is in the near-balanced strip in the local
palette, while every \(G\ge1\) uses its full-\(G\) estimate.  At fixed
\(g\), every one of the five complete anatomy sums is therefore
\[
 O(GQ^{2-\delta})=O((x/g)Q^{-\delta})\quad(G\ge1),              \tag{15}
\]
or
\[
 O(Q^{2-\delta})quad(G<1),                                      \tag{16}
\]
after decreasing \(\delta\) to include (14) and the large target-gcd
tail.  In (15), use \(DM=gGQ^2\asymp x\) forward and
\(RK=gGQ^2\asymp x\) reverse.  Summing (15) over \(g\mid N\) uses
\(Q\ge x^{c_0}\) and \(\sum_{g\mid N}1/g=x^{o(1)}\).
For (16), \(Q=D/g\) forward and \(Q=R/g\) reverse, so the square-root
upper bound for the smaller divisor scale gives
\[
 \sum_{g\mid N}Q^{2-\delta}\ll x^{1-\delta/3}
\]
after decreasing \(\delta<1\).  The active labels and all complete
auxiliary partitions cost \(x^{o(1)}\).  Summing the five disjoint
anatomies proves (6).

Because \(\mathfrak c(N)\ge C_2>0\), (6) is
\(o(\mathfrak c(N)x/\log x)\).  Insert it in the exact identity (7)
and use (2) to prove (8).  Finally
\(T_{\rm postC3,sel}\) has no support at \(\beta\le\beta_1\), and
(7) removes its complete projection through \(\beta_2\); all its other
ledger sectors begin above \(\beta_2\).  This proves (9), without any
sign localization.

glossary.R_2,sel: The complete same-selected-N five-anatomy projection on beta_1<beta<=beta_2.
glossary.T_>beta2,sel: The selected negative remainder after subtracting the complete safe second-buffer projection.
glossary.delta_2: A fixed global power-saving exponent for the complete safe second-buffer palette.

bf0b2dfc2f3a23ad.title: G-PINCHED ENDPOINT-DIAGONAL COROLLARY OF THE FULL-FREQUENCY FOUR-TERM ESTIMATE. Fix constants
bf0b2dfc2f3a23ad.author: slava chan
bf0b2dfc2f3a23ad.statement:
G-PINCHED ENDPOINT-DIAGONAL COROLLARY OF THE FULL-FREQUENCY FOUR-TERM ESTIMATE. Fix constants
\[
 0<\tau\le {1\over10},\qquad \gamma_0>0,\qquad C_0\ge1.
\]
Let \(Q\) be sufficiently large, let
\[
 1\le\beta\le {6\over5},\qquad
 B=Q^\beta,\qquad H_T=Q^{\beta-1},
\]
and let \(H_P,S,T\ge1\) satisfy
\[
 C_0^{-1}QH_T\le ST\le C_0QH_T.
\]
Put
\[
 G={H_T\over H_P}=Q^\gamma.
\]
Assume that the exact scalar fibre satisfies every coefficient, target,
coprimality, frequency-decay and projective-family hypothesis of fact
\(f7b5ba9fa0d6cfc8\), with fixed divisor orders, polynomial-size target
and parameters, and projective \(\ell^1\)-norm at most a fixed power of
\(\log(2Q)\).

Write
\[
 S=Q^{s+O(1/\log Q)},\qquad T=Q^{t+O(1/\log Q)}.
\]
Interchange \(S,T\) and their coefficient slots if necessary so that
\[
 s\le t,\qquad s\le{\beta\over2}+O(1/\log Q).
\]
Assume the endpoint-diagonal lower bounds
\[
 s>3-2\beta-\tau,\qquad t>3-2\beta-\tau,                     \tag{1}
\]
with a fixed positive margin after absorbing the \(O(1/\log Q)\)
dyadic constants. Let \(\mathcal E(Q)\) denote the left side
\[
 H_P^{-1}\sum_{q\asymp Q}|W_q|
\]
or the corresponding absolute projective aggregate in fact
\(f7b5ba9fa0d6cfc8\).

Then there is
\[
 \delta=\delta(\gamma_0,\tau,C_0)>0
\]
such that:

1. If
\[
 G\ge Q^{\gamma_0},
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{\quad \mathcal E(Q)\ll GQ^{2-\delta}.\quad}           \tag{2}
\]

2. If
\[
 0<G\le Q^{-\gamma_0},
\]
then
\[
 \boxed{\quad \mathcal E(Q)\ll Q^{2-\delta}.\quad}            \tag{3}
\]

More explicitly, after division by the literal normalization \(GQ^2\)
in the first case, the four terms of fact \(f7b5ba9fa0d6cfc8\) have
relative \(Q\)-exponents
\[
 {\,\beta-1\,\over2}-{s\over4}-{3\gamma\over4},\qquad
 {\beta\over2}+{s\over4}-{3\over4}-{3\gamma\over4},            \tag{4}
\]
\[
 \beta-1-{s\over2}-\gamma,\qquad
 \beta-{5\over4}-\gamma.                                     \tag{5}
\]
After division by the literal normalization \(Q^2\) in the second case,
their relative exponents are
\[
 {\gamma\over4}+{\,\beta-1\,\over2}-{s\over4},\qquad
 {\gamma\over4}+{\beta\over2}+{s\over4}-{3\over4},             \tag{6}
\]
\[
 \beta-1-{s\over2},\qquad
 \beta-{5\over4}.                                             \tag{7}
\]
Thus, for each fixed \(\gamma_0>0\), every exact endpoint-diagonal
scalar fibre in the stated \(f7b5\) interface outside
\[
 Q^{-\gamma_0}<G<Q^{\gamma_0}                                 \tag{8}
\]
is paid with a fixed power saving. Only the balanced-\(G\) window (8)
remains for genuinely new vector work.

This is a scalar consequence of fact \(f7b5ba9fa0d6cfc8\). It does not
supply or duplicate the literal top-\(B\) source-to-\(f7b5\) coefficient
insertion, does not assert the hypotheses when \(H_P<1\), and does not
estimate a vector nonresonant specified-spectrum form.
bf0b2dfc2f3a23ad.proof:
Fact f7b5ba9fa0d6cfc8 gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal E(Q)\ll Q^\varepsilon\big[
&G^{1/4}Q^2H_T^{1/2}S^{-1/4}
+G^{1/4}Q^{7/4}H_T^{1/2}S^{1/4}\\
&+Q^2H_TS^{-1/2}+Q^{7/4}H_T\big],
\end{aligned}                                                   \tag{9}
\]
where the fixed polynomial parameter and polylogarithmic projective
factors are absorbed by choosing its internal \(\varepsilon\) sufficiently
small. Since \(H_T=Q^{\beta-1}\), \(S=Q^{s+O(1/\log Q)}\), and
\(G=Q^\gamma\), direct subtraction of the exponent \(2+\gamma\)
of \(GQ^2\) gives (4)-(5). Direct subtraction of the exponent \(2\) of
\(Q^2\) gives (6)-(7).

Assume first \(\gamma\ge\gamma_0\). The first exponent in (4), using
\(s>3-2\beta-\tau\), is at most
\[
 {4\beta-5+\tau-3\gamma\over4}
 \le -{1\over40}-{3\gamma_0\over4},                            \tag{10}
\]
because \(\beta\le6/5\) and \(\tau\le1/10\). The second exponent in
(4), using \(s\le\beta/2+O(1/\log Q)\), is at most
\[
 {5\beta\over8}-{3\over4}-{3\gamma\over4}+O(1/\log Q)
 \le -{3\gamma_0\over4}+O(1/\log Q).                           \tag{11}
\]
The two exponents in (5) are at most
\[
 2\beta-{5\over2}+{\tau\over2}-\gamma
 \le -{1\over20}-\gamma_0,                                    \tag{12}
\]
and
\[
 \beta-{5\over4}-\gamma
 \le -{1\over20}-\gamma_0.                                    \tag{13}
\]
Thus every term in (9), divided by \(GQ^2\), has a fixed negative
power of \(Q\).

Assume next \(\gamma\le-\gamma_0\). The first exponent in (6) is at
most
\[
 {\gamma+4\beta-5+\tau\over4}
 \le -{\gamma_0\over4}-{1\over40}.                             \tag{14}
\]
The second is at most
\[
 {\gamma\over4}+{5\beta\over8}-{3\over4}+O(1/\log Q)
 \le -{\gamma_0\over4}+O(1/\log Q).                            \tag{15}
\]
The two exponents in (7) are at most
\[
 2\beta-{5\over2}+{\tau\over2}\le-{1\over20},\qquad
 \beta-{5\over4}\le-{1\over20}.                               \tag{16}
\]
Again all four are uniformly negative.

Choose the internal \(\varepsilon\) in (9) small enough to absorb the
fixed polynomial epsilon-factor, the projective polylogarithm and the
dyadic \(O(1/\log Q)\) errors while retaining, for example, any
\[
 0<\delta<\min\left\{{\gamma_0\over8},{1\over80}\right\}.
\]
Equations (10)-(16) then prove (2)-(3). Interchanging \(S,T\) is legal
because the reciprocal product \(st\), coprimality condition and the two
divisor-bounded coefficient slots in the hypothesis of
f7b5ba9fa0d6cfc8 are symmetric. The final scope statements follow
because no source insertion or vector estimate was used.

glossary.G-PINCHED endpoint-diagonal corollary: The fixed-power scalar payment of exact f7b5 endpoint-diagonal fibres outside a prescribed fixed-power neighborhood of G=1.

bf123016427a4eab.title: MAXIMAL ROUGH FACTORIZATION OF A SHIFTED CENTERED CONDUCTOR INTERVAL
bf123016427a4eab.author: slava chan
bf123016427a4eab.statement:
MAXIMAL ROUGH FACTORIZATION OF A SHIFTED CENTERED CONDUCTOR INTERVAL.

Let q be a squarefree positive integer, let M be an integer, let a be an integer with (a,q)=1, and let 0<Y_0<Y_1 be real numbers. For h|q define
 R^M_{q,h}(a)
  =product_{r|h}
    [e_r(M[a(q/r)]^(-1))+1/(r-1)].                         (1)
Define
 I^M_{q;(Y_0,Y_1]}(a)
  =sum_{h|q;Y_0<h<=Y_1;(h,M)=1}
    c_{q/h}(M)R^M_{q,h}(a)/phi(q/h).                        (2)
For q=1, the sum has its literal empty-product meaning
 I^M_{1;(Y_0,Y_1]}(a)=1_{Y_0<1<=Y_1}.                       (3)

Put
 L=L(q,Y_0)=product_{r|q;q/r<=Y_0}r,qquad q_0=q/L,          (4)
where an empty product is one. Every active divisor h in (2) contains L. If (L,M)>1, then
 I^M_{q;(Y_0,Y_1]}(a)=0.                                    (5)

Assume (L,M)=1. If q_0>1, let M_0 be the unique integer satisfying
 1<=M_0<=q_0,qquad LM_0 congruent M (mod q_0).              (6)
If q_0=1, put M_0=1. Then exactly
 I^M_{q;(Y_0,Y_1]}(a)
 =
 R^M_{q,L}(a)
 I^{M_0}_{q_0;(Y_0/L,Y_1/L]}(a).                            (7)
Every prime t|q_0 satisfies
 t<q/Y_0,qquad q_0/t>Y_0/L.                                (8)
Thus q_0 is (q/Y_0)-smooth and the residual interval projector in (7) has no compulsory prime relative to its lower cutoff.

There is the following actual-scale specialization. Fix 0<eta<1/12, let Q tend to infinity, and assume
 B=Q^(4/3+o(1)),qquad F_0=Q^(1-2eta+o(1)).                 (9)
Let b=pq be squarefree, where p is prime, B<=b<2B, q<2F_0, and put
 Y_0=F_0/p,qquad y_b=b/F_0.                                (10)
Then q/Y_0=y_b=Q^(1/3+2eta+o(1)), and, for all sufficiently large Q,
 omega(L(q,Y_0))<=2.                                        (11)
Consequently (7) peels at most two additional rough prime-local factors from either of the two literal cross-incidence tensors
 P^{M_1}_{s_1,>F_0/p}(a)
  =I^{M_1}_{s_1;(F_0/p,s_1]}(a)
and
 B^{M_{12}}_{q_2;(F_0/p,F_0]}(a)
  =I^{M_{12}}_{q_2;(F_0/p,F_0]}(a),                         (12)
whenever b_1=ps_1 and b_2=pq_2 satisfy the displayed actual-scale hypotheses. In both cases the literal upper cutoff in (12) is retained after division by L.

This is an exact structural factorization, not an estimate. No incomplete-interval vector bound, TRI-CROSS estimate, ROP estimate, CEN-MZB estimate, C_small estimate or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
bf123016427a4eab.proof:
Fix an active divisor h in (2). If r|L and r did not divide h, squarefreeness would give h|q/r. Definition (4) would then give
 h<=q/r<=Y_0,
contradicting the strict lower condition h>Y_0. Hence L|h.

If (L,M)>1, choose a prime r|(L,M). Every divisor h in (2) contains r, so (h,M)>1. Thus there are no active divisors and (5) follows.

Assume (L,M)=1. Every active h has the unique form h=Lk with k|q_0. Primewise multiplicativity of (1) gives
 R^M_{q,Lk}(a)
 =R^M_{q,L}(a)
  product_{t|k}
   [e_t(M[aL(q_0/t)]^(-1))+1/(t-1)].                       (13)
For t|q_0, equation (6) gives M_0 congruent ML^(-1) modulo t, while
 [aL(q_0/t)]^(-1)
 =L^(-1)[a(q_0/t)]^(-1) (mod t).                            (14)
Therefore the t-factor in (13) equals
 e_t(M_0[a(q_0/t)]^(-1))+1/(t-1),
and the product over t|k is R^{M_0}_{q_0,k}(a).

For each prime t|q_0, multiplication by the unit L modulo t shows
 t|M_0 if and only if t|M. Hence
 (k,M_0)=1 if and only if (k,M)=1.                           (15)
On every squarefree divisor s|q_0, the same equality of prime divisibility patterns gives
 c_s(M_0)=c_s(M):                                            (16)
indeed c_t(X)=t-1 if t|X and c_t(X)=-1 otherwise, and Ramanujan sums multiply over coprime squarefree prime factors. The cofactor of h=Lk is q/h=q_0/k. Finally,
 Y_0<Lk<=Y_1
is equivalent to
 Y_0/L<k<=Y_1/L.                                             (17)
Insert (13)-(17) into (2), pull out R^M_{q,L}(a), and obtain (7). If q_0=1, the only possible k is one and equation (3) gives exactly the same conclusion.

If t|q_0, then t was not selected into L. The negation of the condition in (4) is q/t>Y_0. Thus t<q/Y_0. Dividing q/t>Y_0 by L gives q_0/t>Y_0/L. This proves (8).

For the actual specialization,
 q/Y_0=(b/p)/(F_0/p)=b/F_0=y_b,
and (9) gives the exponent in (11). Every prime r|L(q,Y_0) satisfies r>=q/Y_0=y_b. If L had at least three prime factors, their product would divide q and would be at least
 y_b^3=Q^(1+6eta+o(1)).
But q<2F_0=Q^(1-2eta+o(1)), and eta>0, a contradiction for sufficiently large Q. Thus omega(L)<=2.

The first tensor in (12) is the interval (2) because all divisors of s_1 are at most s_1; the second is its defining boundary interval. Apply (7) with q=s_1,Y_1=s_1 and with q=q_2,Y_1=F_0, respectively. Equation (17) shows that the upper endpoint is divided by the same L rather than discarded. This proves (12) and all scope restrictions.

glossary.I^M_{q;(Y_0,Y_1]}(a): the centered conductor projector restricted to the literal interval Y_0<h<=Y_1
glossary.L(q,Y_0): the product of every prime r|q whose cofactor q/r cannot exceed the lower cutoff Y_0
glossary.M_0: the target transported by multiplication with L(q,Y_0)^{-1} modulo q_0

bf68f61a7cf26b3c.title: TWO R=4 FIXED-POWER PAYMENTS BEYOND THE INITIAL LITERAL C1 G3 RECTANGLE. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100 and K_0>=2. Let Q be sufficiently large. Let n=pv be squarefree, where p is prime and gcd(p,v)=1, put C=mathscr A h and m_eff=n/gcd(C,n), and assume Q^(1/2+kappa)<=m_eff<=Q^(6/5), p does not divide C, and m_eff=p r_eff. Let c be squarefree with nc<=Q^K_0. Let W be extended by zero, supported on Q<=q<2Q, and satisfy V_Q(W)<=Q^epsilon for every fixed epsilon>0
bf68f61a7cf26b3c.author: slava chan
bf68f61a7cf26b3c.statement:
TWO R=4 FIXED-POWER PAYMENTS BEYOND THE INITIAL LITERAL C1 G3 RECTANGLE. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100 and K_0>=2. Let Q be sufficiently large. Let n=pv be squarefree, where p is prime and gcd(p,v)=1, put C=mathscr A h and m_eff=n/gcd(C,n), and assume Q^(1/2+kappa)<=m_eff<=Q^(6/5), p does not divide C, and m_eff=p r_eff. Let c be squarefree with nc<=Q^K_0. Let W be extended by zero, supported on Q<=q<2Q, and satisfy V_Q(W)<=Q^epsilon for every fixed epsilon>0.

Fix a MULTI-FREE box of fact 8eb30e55bdef6b27. Let B_*=Q^(b_*+o(1)) be its largest omitted coefficient-one scale, convolve all other positions into a divisor-bounded a-variable of scale A, and let S_box be the resulting complete literal box sum. Assume
2/5<=b_*<=3/5.                                                   (1)
Then each of the following disjointly ordered chambers is paid:
(L) 13/20<=log(p)/log(Q)<=4/5 and r_eff<=Q^(1/50), in which
|S_box|<=Q^(1-11/1200+o(1));                                    (2)
(H) 4/5<log(p)/log(Q)<=21/20 and r_eff<=Q^(1/200), in which
|S_box|<=Q^(1-53/38400+o(1)).                                   (3)
The sums retain the signed convolution coefficient, W(ab), gcd(ab,nc)=1, and e_n(C(ab)^(-1)). Consequently these bounds apply to every genuine R3 dynamic near-prime box in the displayed chambers. No estimate outside (L)-(H) is asserted.
bf68f61a7cf26b3c.proof:
As in fact 17bda5948d58822e, reduce the phase exactly to a unit-numerator reciprocal phase modulo m_eff=p r_eff. Fact 8eb30e55bdef6b27 gives AB_* comparable to Q, coefficient one on the B_*-variable, a fixed divisor-function bound on the a-variable, and retention of every literal weight and gate. Put alpha=1-b_* and pi=log(p)/log(Q). From (1),
2/5<=alpha<=3/5.                                                  (4)
We apply fact 183c9310b93b9005 with its moment parameter R=4.

In chamber (L), equations (1),(4) and pi>=13/20 give
max(alpha,b_*)<=3/5<13/20<=pi.
Also b_*>=2/5>1/5>=pi/4. The two bracket gains are alpha and
1+b_*-(5/4)pi.
Their minimum is at least 2/5, because
1+b_*-(5/4)pi>=1+2/5-(5/4)(4/5)=2/5.                            (5)
Thus the prime-modulus gain is at least
(7/96)(2/5)=7/240.
The tax r_eff<=Q^(1/50) leaves
7/240-1/50=11/1200,                                             (6)
which proves (2).

In chamber (H), again max(alpha,b_*)<=3/5<4/5<pi and
b_*>=2/5>21/80>=pi/4.
Now
1+b_*-(5/4)pi>=1+2/5-(5/4)(21/20)=7/80.                        (7)
Since alpha>=2/5, the bracket minimum is at least 7/80. The prime-modulus gain is at least
(7/96)(7/80)=49/7680.
After r_eff<=Q^(1/200), the net gain is
49/7680-1/200=53/38400,                                         (8)
proving (3). The strict inequality at the lower endpoint of (H) and weak upper endpoint in (L) make the two chambers disjoint. Every remaining loss is Q^o(1) by the cited literal matching facts.

bf956b56ec0bf442.title: Fix L>=1, B>=0, and epsilon>0. Let H be sufficiently large in terms of L,B,epsilon, and let q>=1 be an integer. Let Sigma be a finite family of left packets. Each sigma in Sigma has a nonnegative weight a_sigma, a finite support S_sigma, and a nonzero integer carrier C_sigma divisible by q with |C_sigma|<=H^L. Assume
bf956b56ec0bf442.author: slava chan
bf956b56ec0bf442.statement:
Fix L>=1, B>=0, and epsilon>0. Let H be sufficiently large in terms of L,B,epsilon, and let q>=1 be an integer. Let Sigma be a finite family of left packets. Each sigma in Sigma has a nonnegative weight a_sigma, a finite support S_sigma, and a nonzero integer carrier C_sigma divisible by q with |C_sigma|<=H^L. Assume
sum_{sigma in Sigma}a_sigma<=H^9(log(2H))^B.
Let Tau be a set of ordered tuples
tau=(r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4,b_1,b_2,b_3,b_4)
in which the r_i are pairwise distinct primes in [H^2,2H^2), the b_i are integers with |b_i|<=H, and either all four b_i are nonzero or b_1,b_2,b_3 are nonzero and b_4=0. Give tau a nonnegative weight v_tau<=(log(2H))^B, define its support S_tau={r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4}, and define its carrier
C_tau=b_1r_2r_3r_4+b_2r_1r_3r_4+b_3r_1r_2r_4+b_4r_1r_2r_3.
Assume every C_tau is nonzero, divisible by q, and has |C_tau|<=H^L. Assume also that every tau with all b_i nonzero satisfies gcd(C_tau,r_1r_2r_3r_4)=1.

For i<j and s in {+1,-1}, define S_{ij}^s(tau)=b_ir_j+s b_jr_i. Call an all-nonzero tau generic if
min_{i<j}|b_ib_j|>H,
|S_{ij}^s(tau)|min(|b_i|,|b_j|)>H^3 for every i<j and s,
and
H gcd(|C_tau|,|S_{ij}^s(tau)|)<|b_ib_j| for every i<j and s.

For every ordered prime quadruple as above put G=r_1r_2 and T=r_3r_4. Let zeta_G be 1 modulo r_1 and -1 modulo r_2, and let eta_T be 1 modulo r_3 and -1 modulo r_4. Let <x>_m be the unique integer in (-m/2,m/2] congruent to x modulo m. For an integer C define
B_C=<CT^{-1}>_G, z_C=<B_Czeta_G>_G,
D_C=(C-B_CT)/G, w_C=<CG^{-1}eta_T>_T,
and define the four recovered frequencies
beta_1=(B_C+z_C)/(2r_2), beta_2=(B_C-z_C)/(2r_1),
beta_3=(D_C+w_C)/(2r_4), beta_4=(D_C-w_C)/(2r_3).
Let Omega_C^* be the set of ordered prime quadruples for which B_C is congruent to z_C modulo 2, D_C is congruent to w_C modulo 2, the beta_i are nonzero integers with |beta_i|<=H, and the resulting ordered eight-tuple is generic. Put I_C^*=|Omega_C^*|.

Define the literal support-disjoint equal-carrier energy
E_{0,q}=sum_{tau in Tau}v_tau sum_{sigma in Sigma:S_sigma intersect S_tau is empty,C_sigma=C_tau}a_sigma.
Assume the single generic three-gate estimate
sum_C L_q(C)I_C^*<=H^{14}(log(2H))^B,
where
L_q(C)=sum_{sigma in Sigma:C_sigma=C}a_sigma.
Then
E_{0,q}<<_{L,B,epsilon}H^{14+epsilon}.
In particular the literal frozen same-cell disjoint consumer is H^{14+o(1)}. This theorem is a one-way implication from the common positive DCE34cu gate estimate to the literal source-dependent consumer; it does not assert the reverse implication or any implication to the complete Goldbach problem.
bf956b56ec0bf442.proof:
For any support S and carrier C define
L_{q,S}(C)=sum_{sigma in Sigma:S_sigma intersect S is empty,C_sigma=C}a_sigma.
Nonnegativity gives L_{q,S}(C)<=L_q(C). Also
sum_C L_q(C)=sum_{sigma in Sigma}a_sigma<=H^9(log(2H))^B.

Partition Tau into four disjoint pieces in this order: Tau_0 consists of b_4=0 packets; Tau_s consists of the remaining packets for which either min_{i<j}|b_ib_j|<=H or at least one signed small-strip inequality |S_{ij}^s|min(|b_i|,|b_j|)<=H^3 holds; Tau_g consists of the remaining packets for which at least one large-gcd inequality H gcd(|C_tau|,|S_{ij}^s|)>=|b_ib_j| holds; Tau_* is the remainder. By definition, Tau_* is exactly the generic all-nonzero family.

For Tau_0, pointwise support deletion bounds its energy contribution by
sum_C L_q(C) sum_{tau in Tau_0:C_tau=C}v_tau.
Fact 3c92603bdcab54d5 applies to the displayed carrier equation with b_4=0, the carrier height |C|<=H^L, the weight bound v_tau<=(log(2H))^B, and the common mass bound. It gives an O_{L,B,epsilon}(H^{14+epsilon}) bound for this contribution.

Before dyadically decomposing Tau_s and Tau_g, pay the bottom-scale packets for which at least one |b_i|=1. Fix such a slot i and any other slot j. Choose the ordered primes r_i,r_j in O(H^4) ways, choose b_i in two ways, and choose b_j in O(H) ways. Put G=r_ir_j and let T be the product of the two complementary primes. If B_0=b_ir_j+b_jr_i is the plus pair carrier, then gcd(B_0,G)=1 because b_i,b_j are nonzero and shorter than r_i,r_j. The carrier equation gives T congruent to C B_0^{-1} modulo G. Since both T and G have size H^4, there are O(1) possible integer T, each with H^{o(1)} ordered prime factorizations by the divisor bound in fact 3c92603bdcab54d5. Once the complementary primes are fixed, their two frequencies are recovered with O(1) multiplicity from their fixed plus carrier, by reduction modulo either prime exactly as in the proof of fact 06a7e3e83ec7551e. Thus the fixed-C bottom-scale count is O_{L,epsilon}(H^{5+epsilon}). There are four choices of i and three choices of j, so the same bound holds for their union. Pointwise support deletion, the right-weight bound, and the H^9(log(2H))^B common mass bound give O_{L,B,epsilon}(H^{14+epsilon}) for the bottom-scale energy contribution.

Now every remaining nonzero frequency has absolute value at least 2. Decompose each size into a canonical dyadic interval U_i<|b_i|<=2U_i with U_i in {1,2,4,...} and U_i<=H. There are O((log(2H))^4) boxes. The unit hypothesis gcd(C_tau,r_1r_2r_3r_4)=1 holds. Fact 06a7e3e83ec7551e applies to each of the six pairs and both signs. The conditions using the actual |b_i| imply its dyadic hypotheses: if |b_ib_j|<=H then U_iU_j<=H; if |S_{ij}^s|min(|b_i|,|b_j|)<=H^3 then |S_{ij}^s|min(U_i,U_j)<=H^3; and if H gcd(|C|,|S_{ij}^s|)>=|b_ib_j| then H gcd(|C|,|S_{ij}^s|)>=U_iU_j. The final weighted aggregate assertion of that fact, together with pointwise support deletion, gives O_{L,B,epsilon}(H^{14+epsilon}) for the remaining parts of each of Tau_s and Tau_g.

It remains to bound Tau_*. Use the literal windows I_i={b in Z:0<|b|<=H}. For sufficiently large H, these windows satisfy the shortness conditions of fact 397f417416c4cb9d because
|b_1r_2 plus or minus b_2r_1|<=4H^3<G/2
and
|b_3r_4-b_4r_3|<=4H^3<T/2.
For every tau in Tau_*, its carrier equation can be written
C_tau=(b_1r_2+b_2r_1)T+G(b_3r_4+b_4r_3).
Fact 397f417416c4cb9d therefore shows that the parity-and-window gate at the same ordered prime quadruple and carrier recovers exactly b_1,b_2,b_3,b_4. Since tau is generic, this ordered prime quadruple lies in Omega_{C_tau}^*. Conversely the uniqueness part of that fact shows that two distinct tuples in Tau_* cannot map to the same ordered prime quadruple at the same carrier.

Therefore, using support deletion and v_tau<=(log(2H))^B,
sum_{tau in Tau_*}v_tau L_{q,S_tau}(C_tau)
<= (log(2H))^B sum_C L_q(C)I_C^*
<=H^{14}(log(2H))^{2B}.
For fixed B and epsilon, the last expression is O_{B,epsilon}(H^{14+epsilon}). Adding all disjoint contributions proves the asserted bound.

Several operations in the proof are one-sided: support deletion replaces L_{q,S_tau} by L_q, right weights are replaced by their common upper bound, the image of Tau_* is enlarged to Omega_C^*, and boundary families are bounded from above. These steps establish no reverse comparison. The statement concerns only the finite packet families explicitly defined here and contains no cross-cell, other-anatomy, source-routing, or Goldbach completion assertion.

glossary.Omega_C^*: the set of ordered prime quadruples passing the literal generic parity-and-window three-gate test
glossary.S_tau: the four-prime support of a right packet
glossary.S_{ij}^s(tau): the signed pair carrier of a right packet
glossary.beta_1: the first frequency recovered by the oriented CRT gate
glossary.beta_2: the second frequency recovered by the oriented CRT gate
glossary.beta_3: the third frequency recovered by the oriented CRT gate
glossary.beta_4: the fourth frequency recovered by the oriented CRT gate
glossary.generic: the all-nonzero unit packet residual after small-frequency, signed-strip, and large-gcd deletions

c09a66219145acee.title: Fix L>=1 and epsilon>0. Let H>=2, let C be a nonzero integer with |C|<=H^L, let K be an integer, and let m be a positive integer. Put I_H=[H^2,2H^2) intersect Z and X=ceil(LH^3). Let U_{C,K,m}(H,L) be the set of tuples
c09a66219145acee.author: slava chan
c09a66219145acee.statement:
Fix L>=1 and epsilon>0. Let H>=2, let C be a nonzero integer with |C|<=H^L, let K be an integer, and let m be a positive integer. Put I_H=[H^2,2H^2) intersect Z and X=ceil(LH^3). Let U_{C,K,m}(H,L) be the set of tuples
(a,b,c,d,r_2,r_3)
such that:
(1) a,b,c,d are even integers of absolute value at most X and ab+cd=2 K;
(2) r_2,r_3 are distinct primes in I_H;
(3) with
A=b r_3-d r_2, B=a r_2-c r_3,
q=gcd(|A|,|B|), D=ad r_2^2-bc r_3^2, J=ab-cd,
one has q=2m, AB>0, and, writing s for the common sign of A and B, the integers
r_1=|A|/q, r_4=|B|/q
are primes in I_H such that r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4 are pairwise distinct;
(4) gcd(C,r_1r_2r_3r_4)=1, D=2sqC, and J is a nonzero multiple of 2q.

Then
|U_{C,K,m}(H,L)| <<_{L,epsilon} H^epsilon X^2/m
and hence
|U_{C,K,m}(H,L)| <<_{L,epsilon} H^{6+epsilon}/m.
If m>X^2/2, the set is empty. The same bounds hold after weighting each tuple by the product of the four von Mangoldt prime weights, or by any fixed polylogarithmically bounded weights.

Consequently, for every fixed delta>0, the union of any single fixed-m stratum with m>=H^delta satisfies
|U_{C,K,m}(H,L)| <<_{L,epsilon} H^{6-delta+epsilon}.
This is a genuine fixed-power saving for each polynomially large exact-conductor stratum. It is not a full cross-Q saving after summing all m: summing the displayed pointwise estimate over 1<=m<=X^2/2 gives only H^{6+epsilon} after absorbing a harmonic logarithm.
c09a66219145acee.proof:
The clauses defining U_{C,K,m}(H,L) are the intrinsic normalized-unit clauses (II) of fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb with the additional exact-conductor condition q=2m. That fact gives, for every tuple in U_{C,K,m}(H,L), unique nonzero integers u,v such that
q=2|v| and J=4uv.
Since q=2m, one has |v|=m. Put w=uv=J/4. Then w is a nonzero multiple of m.

The coefficient bounds give
4|w|=|J|=|ab-cd|<=|ab|+|cd|<=2X^2,
so |w|<=X^2/2. It follows immediately that there are no tuples when m>X^2/2. Otherwise, the number of possible nonzero multiples w of m in this interval is at most
2 floor(X^2/(2m))<=X^2/m.                                      (1)

For a fixed w, fact ab9163da69da1ad4 proves that the number of nonzero integer coefficient quadruples in the X-box satisfying
ab+cd=2 K and ab-cd=4w
is at most
4 tau(|K+2w|) tau(|K-2w|).                                    (2)
The same upper bound remains valid after requiring even coefficients. On a tuple in U_{C,K,m}(H,L), all four coefficients are nonzero by fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb, so (2) applies. Moreover
K+2w=ab and K-2w=cd,
hence both divisor-function arguments are nonzero and have absolute value at most X^2. The elementary uniform divisor bound gives, after allocating a small part of epsilon,
tau(|K+2w|)tau(|K-2w|)<<_{L,epsilon}H^epsilon.
Combining this with (1), the number of possible coefficient matrices Q is
<<_{L,epsilon} H^epsilon X^2/m.                               (3)

For each fixed coefficient matrix Q, fact 1218e64e51ba3131 proves uniformly that the number of ordered prime pairs (r_2,r_3) satisfying all intrinsic normalized-unit clauses is <<_{L,epsilon}H^epsilon. Restricting further to q=2m only decreases this number. Multiplying this fixed-Q bound by (3), and dividing epsilon between the two uses, proves
|U_{C,K,m}(H,L)|<<_{L,epsilon}H^epsilon X^2/m.
Since X<<_L H^3, the H^{6+epsilon}/m form follows.

Fact 1218e64e51ba3131 also states the same fixed-Q estimate with the four von Mangoldt weights, or any fixed polylogarithmic weights. Alternatively, each such weight is bounded by a fixed power of log H and can be absorbed into H^epsilon. This proves the weighted assertion.

If m>=H^delta, substitute this lower bound into H^{6+epsilon}/m. Finally,
sum_{m<=X^2/2}1/m<<log(2X),
so summing the pointwise conductor-stratum estimate over all m recovers only H^{6+epsilon} after absorbing the logarithm. This proves both the scoped saving and its stated limitation.

glossary.U_{C,K,m}(H,L): the bounded normalized unit-state family with exact gcd q=2m
glossary.m: half of the exact positive gcd q on a conductor stratum

c104777069f391cc.title: NON-CIRCULAR SLOPE-INCIDENCE AND FINITE-PARSEVAL BOUND FOR EVERY NONEMPTY FACE d|r. Let r be squarefree, let d be a nonempty divisor of r, and let A be coprime to d. Let I and J be finite integer intervals of cardinalities U and F. Let Rho be a finite row-label set with a map rho mapsto u_rho in I such that each u in I has at most kappa_prov preimages, and assume gcd(u_rho,d)=1. Define x_rho=((r/d)u_rho)^{-1} modulo d. Let Qcal be a finite integer interval of cardinality L_q. Restrict outputs to q in Qcal and h in J satisfying gcd(qh,d)=1. Let beta(q,h) be common to all rows and satisfy |beta(q,h)|<=1. For arbitrary complex alpha_rho,z_rho put
c104777069f391cc.author: slava chan
c104777069f391cc.statement:
NON-CIRCULAR SLOPE-INCIDENCE AND FINITE-PARSEVAL BOUND FOR EVERY NONEMPTY FACE d|r. Let r be squarefree, let d be a nonempty divisor of r, and let A be coprime to d. Let I and J be finite integer intervals of cardinalities U and F. Let Rho be a finite row-label set with a map rho mapsto u_rho in I such that each u in I has at most kappa_prov preimages, and assume gcd(u_rho,d)=1. Define x_rho=((r/d)u_rho)^{-1} modulo d. Let Qcal be a finite integer interval of cardinality L_q. Restrict outputs to q in Qcal and h in J satisfying gcd(qh,d)=1. Let beta(q,h) be common to all rows and satisfy |beta(q,h)|<=1. For arbitrary complex alpha_rho,z_rho put

 T_d(q,h)=(d/r)beta(q,h)sum_rho alpha_rho z_rho e_d(Ah q^{-1}x_rho). (1)

Then

 sum_{q,h}|T_d(q,h)|^2
 <=(d/r)^2dF(L_q/d+1)kappa_prov(U/d+1)
   sum_rho|alpha_rho z_rho|^2.                                     (2)

In particular, let B,C_1,C_2 be positive real numbers. If
 U<=C_1B/r,  B<=C_2r^2,  d<=L_q,                                   (3)
then

 sum_{q,h}|T_d(q,h)|^2
 <=2(C_1C_2+1)kappa_prov L_qF sum_rho|alpha_rho z_rho|^2.           (4)

Formula (2) proves the exact slope-fibre estimate
 max_x #{rho:x_rho=x}<=kappa_prov(U/d+1).                           (5)
In the literal centered face whose parent active product is r and whose active subface is d, the exact inactive local factor is mu(r/d)d/r. Its sign may be absorbed into the common beta, while d/r in (1) is its magnitude.

If a row-output projective decomposition is a sum of atoms (1), each with sup norms of alpha and beta at most one and scalar coefficient l1 norm P_proj, Minkowski gives (4) multiplied by P_proj^2 and with sum_rho|z_rho|^2 on the right. Thus Q^epsilon projective norm and kappa_prov<=Q^epsilon give the fixed-parent-r L_qF scale for every one of its finitely many nonempty faces, provided (3) holds.

For the literal C4 coefficient this remains conditional: fact 3330e83b6d253b69 retains the row-dependent factor e_{v_j}(Ah_j(qd_j)^{-1}) inside W_{j,r}, and fact b76df03232475208 proves that exporting its prime-v specialization by additive q-characters has sqrt(v), not subpolynomial, l1 cost. Hence this theorem does not assert that the exact W has a common beta and proves no C4-WTG_r, cross-r partner-multiplier inequality, another anatomy bound, or Goldbach.
c104777069f391cc.proof:
For x modulo d put a_x=sum_{rho:x_rho=x}alpha_rho z_rho and ahat(a)=sum_xa_xe_d(ax). The row sum in (1) is ahat(Ahq^{-1}). For a fixed a and fixed supported h, Ahq^{-1}=a modulo d has at most one q residue class, because A,h,q are units. Thus the number N_d(a) of output pairs selecting a satisfies N_d(a)<=F(L_q/d+1). Grouping outputs by a, using |beta|<=1, and applying finite Fourier Parseval gives

 sum_{q,h}|T_d(q,h)|^2
 <=(d/r)^2 max_aN_d(a) sum_{a mod d}|ahat(a)|^2
 =(d/r)^2 max_aN_d(a)d sum_x|a_x|^2.                               (6)

A fixed x_rho specifies one residue class of u_rho modulo d because r/d is a unit modulo d. The interval I contains at most U/d+1 integers in that class, each with at most kappa_prov labels. This proves (5). Cauchy in every fibre gives
 sum_x|a_x|^2<=kappa_prov(U/d+1)sum_rho|alpha_rho z_rho|^2.         (7)
Substitute (7) and the incidence bound into (6) to prove (2).

Because B,C_1,C_2 are positive, (3) gives
 U/d+1<=C_1B/(rd)+1<=C_1C_2r/d+1<=(C_1C_2+1)r/d.                   (8)
Insert (8) into (2). The scalar factor becomes
 (C_1C_2+1)F[(d/r)L_q+d^2/r]<=2(C_1C_2+1)L_qF,                    (9)
because d<=r and d<=L_q. This proves (4).

For the projective corollary, write the total operator as sum_t c_tT_{d,t}, with sum_t|c_t|<=P_proj. Equation (4) bounds each atom's output l2 norm using sum|z_rho|^2 because |alpha_{t,rho}|<=1. Minkowski and then squaring prove the P_proj^2 assertion. Fact 3330e83b6d253b69 gives the exact inactive coefficient mu(r/d)/(r/d), which is mu(r/d)d/r, justifying the sign convention. The stated literal limitation is exactly the obstruction of fact b76df03232475208.

glossary.T_d: One row-times-output atom on the centered face active at d.
glossary.kappa_prov: The maximum number of retained provenance labels above one integer marked cofactor u.
glossary.x_rho: The slope ((r/d)u_rho)^{-1} modulo the active face modulus d.

c155c30b0450a4f9.title: QUANTITATIVE SELECTED FIXED-BAD-\(N\) POST-\(A\) REMAINDER
c155c30b0450a4f9.author: slava chan
c155c30b0450a4f9.statement:
QUANTITATIVE SELECTED FIXED-BAD-\(N\) POST-\(A\) REMAINDER.

Assume the notation and hypotheses of facts \(7ffe3d237362a451\),
\(24e911b7685090c1\), and \(aeffec374578707c\). Thus
\(\mathscr R_{\rm postlow,sel}\) is the selected same-bad-\(N\) negative
remainder outside \(C91\), outside bounded normalized bases, and above
\(\beta_0=6/5-2\kappa\), satisfying
\[
 \mathscr R_{\rm postlow,sel}
 \le -c_{\rm dir}\mathfrak c(N)\frac{x}{\log x}
 +o\!\left(\mathfrak c(N)\frac{x}{\log x}\right).              \tag{1}
\]
Let \(\beta_1=6/5-3\sigma\). Let
\(\mathscr R_{A,U_{\rm low}}\) be the complete selected interval-prime
\(A\) aggregate inside \(\mathscr R_{\rm postlow,sel}\) with
\[
 \beta_0<\beta_{\rm norm}\le\beta_1.
\]
Every such atom has parent \(U_{\rm low}\). Define
\[
 \mathscr R_{\rm postA,sel}
 =
 \mathscr R_{\rm postlow,sel}-\mathscr R_{A,U_{\rm low}}.      \tag{2}
\]
Then there is a fixed \(\delta_A>0\) such that
\[
 |\mathscr R_{A,U_{\rm low}}|\ll x^{1-\delta_A},               \tag{3}
\]
and
\[
 \mathscr R_{\rm postA,sel}
 \le -c_{\rm dir}\mathfrak c(N)\frac{x}{\log x}
 +o\!\left(\mathfrak c(N)\frac{x}{\log x}\right).              \tag{4}
\]

Within the standard-marker slab
\[
 \beta_0<\beta_{\rm norm}\le\beta_1,
\]
the exact remaining anatomy list is
\[
 B,\ C1,\ C2,\ C3,
\]
and the parent is \(U_{\rm low}\). Hence the first standard-marker interface
of the actual negative remainder is the \(U_{\rm low}\), raised-stopping
\(B\), \(\beta_0+\), \(G=1\) cell of fact \(aeffec374578707c\).

The estimate (3) is supplied independently by the accepted \(A\)-buffer
chain with its retained parent coordinate. It is not inferred by deleting
the \(A\) anatomy from the whole-label C91 estimate of fact
\(af06640e8d8e4102\). No \(B\), \(C1\), \(C2\), \(C3\), actual-\(Z\),
endpoint, or terminal selection is made, and no Goldbach conclusion is
asserted.
c155c30b0450a4f9.proof:
Fact \(7ffe3d237362a451\) proves (1) and also proves
that throughout \(\beta_{\rm norm}<6/5\) the only parent of its remainder is
\(U_{\rm low}\). Hence every \(A\) atom in the displayed buffer has the
parent stated in the theorem.

Fact \(24e911b7685090c1\) gives a fixed power saving for the complete
interval-prime \(A\) buffer through \(\beta_1\), retaining every parent
coordinate. Fact \(aeffec374578707c\) applies this payment to the exact
disjoint parent/anatomy ledger: in its slab (I), the anatomy \(A\) is absent
from the still-unestimated family, while the parent coordinate remains part
of the Cartesian refinement. Therefore the \(U_{\rm low}\)-parent
\(A\)-aggregate appearing in (2) is an independently paid sector. This
proves (3) for the saving exponent supplied by that accepted chain.

Fact \(f41f5f91b52e0d13\), inherited through fact
\(60b26a9b6f79467a\) and hence through fact \(7ffe3d237362a451\), gives
\(\mathfrak c(N)\ge C_2>0\). Thus (3) is
\(o(\mathfrak c(N)x/\log x)\). Subtract (3) from the exact identity (2) and
use (1) to obtain (4).

The anatomy list \(B,C1,C2,C3\) and the first structural \(B\) cell are
exactly slab (I) and the final conclusion of fact
\(aeffec374578707c\). The parent has already collapsed to \(U_{\rm low}\) by
fact \(7ffe3d237362a451\). No other selector has been inserted. In
particular, the proof uses the independent accepted \(A\)-sector estimate
and never appeals to arbitrary anatomy-deletion stability of the C91
whole-label bound. This proves all scope statements.

glossary.delta_A: A fixed positive power-saving exponent for the accepted selected U_low-parent A-buffer aggregate.
glossary.mathscr R_{A,U_low}: The complete selected U_low-parent interval-prime A aggregate in the first post-low normalized-beta buffer.
glossary.mathscr R_{postA,sel}: The selected same-bad-N negative remainder after independently subtracting the accepted U_low-parent A buffer.

c1c141e3d7fb562f.title: CRIT-DEEP-DIRECT-AUDIT: COMPLETE BARE-MOBIUS DEEP-SUBHALF PAYMENT, SEPARATE PRINCIPAL AND SAME-MASK ZERO PAYMENTS, AND THE EXACT OUTER-c COPRIMALITY INTERFACE. Fix tau>0, one orientation, exact active g,c, and one complete frozen selected critical source block of facts 328503a935cabe60 and 5772f2de626492b3. Let
c1c141e3d7fb562f.author: slava chan
c1c141e3d7fb562f.statement:
CRIT-DEEP-DIRECT-AUDIT: COMPLETE BARE-MOBIUS DEEP-SUBHALF PAYMENT, SEPARATE PRINCIPAL AND SAME-MASK ZERO PAYMENTS, AND THE EXACT OUTER-c COPRIMALITY INTERFACE. Fix tau>0, one orientation, exact active g,c, and one complete frozen selected critical source block of facts 328503a935cabe60 and 5772f2de626492b3. Let
q be asymptotic to Q_c, kappa be asymptotic to K_c,
n be asymptotic to B, t=(ell-kappa n)/q be asymptotic to T,       (1)
with ell asymptotic to BK_c and ell asymptotic to Q_cT. The exact source coefficient is mu(c)mu(q)mu(n), c,q,n are pairwise coprime, and w_{q,kappa}(n) denotes the complete literal physical amplitude, excluding mu(n) and exact unit conditions.

Fix a desired A_0>0. Choose a sufficiently large C_deep=C_deep(A_0) and assume the deep-subhalf condition
Gamma>=K_c(log B)^(2C_deep).                                    (2)
By fact a3103a7fbc2dc2ed this is equivalent to
Q_c<=sqrt(B)/(log B)^(C_deep).                                  (3)

For a_{q,kappa}=ell kappa^(-1) modulo q, define the exact c-coprime reduced discrepancy
D^{(c)}_{q,kappa}
 =sum_{n congruent a_{q,kappa} (mod q),(n,c)=1}
      mu(n)w_{q,kappa}(n)
  -phi(q)^(-1)sum_{(n,qc)=1}mu(n)w_{q,kappa}(n).                (4)
Then
D^{(c)}_{q,kappa}
 =sum_{r divides c}mu(r)D_{q,kappa;r},                           (5)
where
D_{q,kappa;r}
 =sum_{n congruent a_{q,kappa} (mod q),r divides n}
      mu(n)w_{q,kappa}(n)
  -phi(q)^(-1)sum_{(n,q)=1,r divides n}
      mu(n)w_{q,kappa}(n).                                      (6)

The r=1 row is fully paid in the deep-subhalf range:
sum_{kappa} |sum_q mu(q)D_{q,kappa;1}|
 <<_{A_0} BK_c(log x)^(-A_0)
 <<_{A_0} ell(log x)^(-A_0),                                   (7)
uniformly in both orientations and all frozen labels. The outer mu(q) costs nothing beyond absolute summation.

The principal reduced average is separate from (7). Put
M_{g,c}=mu(c)sum_{q,kappa}{mu(q)over phi(q)}
             sum_{(n,qc)=1}mu(n)w_{q,kappa}(n).                 (8)
Then
|M_{g,c}|<<_{A_0}ell(log x)^(-A_0).                             (9)

The same-mask t-Poisson zero is a second, distinct non-AP term. Let F_{q,n}(y) be the complete smooth progression amplitude of fact 328503a935cabe60 and
z_{q,n}=n^(-1)integral_R F_{q,n}(y)dy.                          (10)
The exact zero contribution is
Z_{g,c}=mu(c)sum_q mu(q)sum_{(n,qc)=1}mu(n)z_{q,n}.             (11)
Then
|Z_{g,c}|<<_{A_0}Q_cT(log x)^(-A_0)
 <<_{A_0}ell(log x)^(-A_0).                                    (12)
In particular, (8) and (11) are not identified with one another.

The complete literal nonzero-frequency block at fixed g,c therefore has the exact form
S_{g,c}^{deep}
 =R_c+O_{A_0}(ell(log x)^(-A_0)),                               (13)
where
R_c=mu(c)sum_{q,kappa}mu(q)
       sum_{r divides c,r>1}mu(r)D_{q,kappa;r}.                 (14)
For r>1, since (r,q)=1, substitution n=rm rewrites the summand mu(r)D_{q,kappa;r} exactly as
sum_{m congruent a_{q,kappa}r^(-1) (mod q),(m,r)=1}
      mu(m)w_{q,kappa}(rm)
 -phi(q)^(-1)sum_{(m,q)=1,(m,r)=1}
      mu(m)w_{q,kappa}(rm).                                    (15)
Thus R_c is a family of coprime-restricted Mobius progressions of length B/r, varying with r|c. The cited Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem for bare mu does not include this uniform family, and fact 71389b22e6f49e13 only pays one-modulus non-AP smooth sums. Consequently (14)-(15) are the exact remaining deep-subhalf interface for general c. If c=1, R_c=0 and (13) gives the complete local bound |S_{g,1}^{deep}|<<_A ell(log x)^(-A). No estimate for R_c when c>1, no complementary near-half payment, no full critical-tail payment, and no Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
c1c141e3d7fb562f.proof:
The algebraic decomposition comes first. Pairwise coprimality of c,q,n is part of the exact descent in fact 8d9feea8c44da2c8. Since (kappa,q)=1, q|kappa n-ell is equivalent to n congruent a_{q,kappa} modulo q, and this residue is reduced. Insert
1_{(n,c)=1}=sum_{r|c,r|n}mu(r)
in both sums of (4). Because (q,c)=1, this gives (5)-(6) exactly.

We prove (7) from the precise theorem recorded in Xuancheng Shao, arXiv:1607.01814v2, Introduction, unnumbered Theorem (Bombieri-Vinogradov). It states that if X,Q>=2, A>=2 and Q<=sqrt(X)(log X)^(-B_S(A)) for a sufficiently large B_S(A), then for all but at most Q(log X)^(-A) moduli q<=Q,
sup_{(a,q)=1}|sum_{n<=X,n congruent a (mod q)}mu(n)
 -phi(q)^(-1)sum_{n<=X}mu(n)|
 <<_A X/[Q(log X)^A].                                          (16)
The paper explicitly says the displayed statement also holds for the Mobius function.

At each real endpoint u asymptotic to B, apply (16) with X=u and Q=max(2,2Q_c). Choose C_deep after the desired saving exponent so that (3), with fixed support constants absorbed, implies the modulus hypothesis. On q asymptotic to Q_c, every good modulus contributes at most
B/[Q_c(log B)^(A_1)]
to the unweighted discrepancy. There are O(Q_c) such q. The exceptional set has O(Q_c(log B)^(-A_1)) elements. For each exceptional q, trivial counting and the squarefree totient bound give
|sum_{n<=u,n congruent a (mod q)}mu(n)
 -phi(q)^(-1)sum_{n<=u}mu(n)|
 <<(B/Q_c+1)(log x)^2.                                         (17)
Therefore, uniformly for u on the B-scale,
sum_{q asymptotic to Q_c}max_{(a,q)=1}
 |sum_{n<=u,n congruent a (mod q)}mu(n)
 -phi(q)^(-1)sum_{n<=u}mu(n)|
 <<B(log x)^(-A_1+3),                                          (18)
after increasing A_1. This is the requested dyadic L1 estimate by good and exceptional moduli.

The r=1 discrepancy in (6) is centered against the q-coprime sum rather than the unrestricted sum in (16). Their difference is
phi(q)^(-1){sum_n mu(n)w(n)-sum_{(n,q)=1}mu(n)w(n)}.            (19)
Fact 71389b22e6f49e13 pays each of the two smooth non-AP sums uniformly, since q is polynomially bounded and fact 5772f2de626492b3 gives B>=x^(1/20) and the required source-specific smooth norm. Summing 1/phi(q) over q asymptotic to Q_c costs a fixed logarithmic power by the elementary bound in fact efcd2b6b9fb60a05.

For the progression part, use Abel summation exactly as in fact efcd2b6b9fb60a05. Fact 5772f2de626492b3 gives
sup|w|<<log^(C_reg)x and sup|w'|<<B^(-1)log^(C_reg)x
on an interval of length O(B), uniformly in q,kappa. Apply (18) at every integration endpoint. First choose A_1>A_0+C_reg plus all fixed divisor and label taxes, then choose C_deep large enough for B_S(A_1). This yields
sum_q|D_{q,kappa;1}|<<B(log x)^(-A_0-C_label)                   (20)
for each kappa. Multiplying by mu(q) before triangle changes nothing. Summing O(K_c) kappa-values and the fixed polylogarithmic label family gives (7).

For (9), fact 71389b22e6f49e13 applies directly to the inner sum in (8) with coprimality integer qc, which is polynomially bounded, and the verified literal smooth norm. It gives B times every desired negative log power. Sum q with 1/phi(q), using the same fixed logarithmic totient tax, and sum O(K_c) kappa-values. Since BK_c is asymptotic to ell, this proves (9).

We next justify (12) without confusing it with (9). In (10), change variables y=Tv. On the fixed compact v-support,
z_{q,n}={T over n} integral F_{q,n}(Tv)dv.                      (21)
For n=By, differentiate under the integral. Every direct n-factor is scaled by n/B. Along the progression, kappa(v,y)=(ell-qTv)/(By), so
y partial_y kappa(v,y)=-kappa(v,y).                             (22)
Because kappa is asymptotic to K_c on support, every smooth factor of kappa/K_c has bounded y-derivatives. The logarithm log(c kappa) also has bounded y-derivative, while log(Tv) is independent of y. The original source and dyadic factors are fixed-complexity smooth functions. Hence the normalized amplitude
(B/T)z_{q,By}
has logarithmic supremum, total variation and scaled-Lipschitz norm uniformly in q and every frozen label.

Apply fact 71389b22e6f49e13 to the n-sum in (11), with coprimality integer qc. After restoring the factor T/B from (21), each q contributes
<<_A T(log x)^(-A).
There are O(Q_c) q-values, and the outer mu(q) is absorbed by absolute summation. Since Q_cT is asymptotic to ell, all fixed label taxes are absorbed by increasing A, proving (12).

Finally, for r>1, squarefreeness and (r,q)=1 imply
mu(r)mu(rm)=mu(m)1_{(m,r)=1}.                                  (23)
The congruence rm congruent a_{q,kappa} modulo q is equivalent to the congruence in (15), and (rm,q)=1 is equivalent to (m,q)=1. This proves (15). The theorem (16) concerns bare mu(m), not mu(m)1_{(m,r)=1} uniformly over varying r, and its modulus-range condition at the shorter length B/r is also not automatic. Fact 71389b22e6f49e13 contains no arithmetic-progression average. Therefore no cited input estimates (14), and (13) is the exact proved reduction.

glossary.C_deep: The logarithmic depth exponent chosen after the desired saving so that Q_c lies in Shao's Möbius Bombieri-Vinogradov range.
glossary.D^{(c)}_{q,kappa}: The centered q-progression discrepancy with the exact outer-c coprimality restriction.
glossary.D_{q,kappa;r}: The r-divisibility row in the inclusion-exclusion of the outer-c coprimality restriction.
glossary.M_{g,c}: The principal reduced-residue average of the fixed g,c physical AP block.
glossary.R_c: The exact residual sum of all r>1 outer-c coprimality rows.
glossary.S_{g,c}^{deep}: The complete fixed-g,c critical nonzero-frequency block in the deep-subhalf range.
glossary.Z_{g,c}: The complete literal same-mask t-Poisson zero contribution at fixed g,c.
glossary.z_{q,n}: The literal same-mask zero amplitude n^{-1} times the integral of F_{q,n}.

c1f29a6ce884c5ae.title: LITERAL CENTERED-DIGIT FULL-AXIS NO-FIT AND THE REQUIRED CORRELATED GAIN
c1f29a6ce884c5ae.author: slava chan
c1f29a6ce884c5ae.statement:
LITERAL CENTERED-DIGIT FULL-AXIS NO-FIT AND THE REQUIRED CORRELATED GAIN.

Let m>=9 be odd, put q=m^2,
 U_cut=floor(m/4)+1,qquad N=2(U_cut-1),                            (1)
and let W_star be the centered literal interval-multiplicity weight of fact 076bc0ba8fc2536a:
 W_star(nu)=#{u in Z:0<|u|<U_cut, u congruent nu modulo m}-N/m.    (2)
Let u_0=1 and let G_u be the literal singleton gate
 G_u(u)=1 if u=u_0 modulo m and G_u(u)=0 otherwise.                 (3)
Then
 W_star(u_0)=1-N/m>=1/2.                                           (4)

Assume the arithmetic hypotheses of fact c585f0febfbab2f4: s belongs to {1,-1}, gcd(Kn,m)=1, A_u=K+2smu, an is congruent to A_u modulo q, and p runs modulo q. The u-dependent inverse-column assembly with the literal centered digit and gate (3) satisfies
 |sum_{u modulo m}W_star(u)G_u(u)e_q(-pnA_u^(-1))|
 =1-N/m>=1/2                                                       (5)
for every p modulo q. In particular it is nonzero on all q values of p. Thus, even for the actual centered interval digit, centering alone does not confine the Kloosterman p-axis to fewer residue classes uniformly over the bounded literal tuple gates allowed in fact f23bad095a2e6a52.

There is also an exact exponent requirement. The generic fixed-fibre theorem f23bad095a2e6a52 has the digit-dependent scale
 m^(15/16+epsilon)||W_star||_2.                                    (6)
Fact 076bc0ba8fc2536a gives ||W_star||_2>=m^(1/2)/sqrt(6). Suppose a proposed carrier-correlated refinement improves (6) by a factor m^(-eta_trace), with all other normalized profile and column factors unchanged. In order that its furnished bound meet
 m^(19/20-delta+epsilon)                                           (7)
for a fixed delta>=0, it is necessary at the exponent-ledger level that
 eta_trace>=39/80+delta.                                           (8)
Equivalently, the new theorem must recover essentially the whole square-root digit loss; an additional saving of size only m^(-1/80) is insufficient.

This is a no-fit for two specific natural shortcuts: digit support shortening uniformly over bounded literal gates, and a small perturbative improvement of the generic digit L2 bound. It does not lower-bound the actual full carrier sum, does not assert that the genuine source mask is a singleton, and does not rule out a joint trace theorem obtaining the large gain in (8) from the true prime, carrier, moving-window, and source correlations.
c1f29a6ce884c5ae.proof:
Since u_0=1 and 1<U_cut for m>=9, the residue u_0 belongs to the set counted in (2). Fact 076bc0ba8fc2536a proves that this set has N distinct residues and N<=m/2. Hence
 W_star(u_0)=1-N/m>=1/2,
which is (4).

Apply equation (8) of fact c585f0febfbab2f4 with W=W_star and the gate (3). The product f(u)=W_star(u)G_u(u) is supported only at u_0, so its Fourier transform has constant magnitude |W_star(u_0)| at every frequency. Equivalently, the sum in (5) consists of the single term
 W_star(u_0)e_q(-pnA_{u_0}^(-1)),
whose phase has absolute value one. This proves (5) for every p modulo q and therefore proves the full-axis assertion. Fact f23bad095a2e6a52 explicitly permits any bounded tuple gate independent of Fourier characters, so (3) lies in its declared gate class.

For the exponent ledger, insert the lower bound
 ||W_star||_2>=m^(1/2)/sqrt(6)
from fact 076bc0ba8fc2536a into (6). After a hypothetical gain m^(-eta_trace), its m-exponent is at least
 15/16+1/2-eta_trace=23/16-eta_trace.                              (9)
To be no larger than the target exponent 19/20-delta, it is necessary that
 23/16-eta_trace<=19/20-delta.
Rearrangement gives
 eta_trace>=23/16-19/20+delta
           =(115-76)/80+delta
           =39/80+delta,
which is (8). Constants and epsilon-powers do not alter this fixed exponent comparison. The final paragraph states exactly what was and was not inferred.

glossary.eta_trace: the exponent of a hypothetical multiplicative gain beyond the generic digit L2 factor

c23ca78883ba83d9.title: POWER-SAVING MOBIUS--RECIPROCAL-TRACE BOUND WITH A SQUAREFREE AUXILIARY COPRIMALITY GATE THROUGH p<=2Q^(6/5)
c23ca78883ba83d9.author: slava chan
c23ca78883ba83d9.statement:
POWER-SAVING MOBIUS--RECIPROCAL-TRACE BOUND WITH A SQUAREFREE AUXILIARY COPRIMALITY GATE THROUGH p<=2Q^(6/5).

Fix constants C_0>=1 and zeta>0. Let Q be sufficiently large, let p be a prime satisfying
  Q^zeta<=p<=2Q^(6/5),                                        (1)
let C in F_p^*, and let c be a squarefree positive integer with
  c<=Q^C_0.                                                    (2)
Extend the reciprocal trace by zero at nonunits:
  K_{p,C}(q)=1_{p does not divide q}e_p(Cq^(-1)).              (3)
Let A be a complex function on the integers, supported on Q<=q<2Q, and put
  V_Q(A)=sup_q|A(q)|+sum_q|A(q+1)-A(q)|.                       (4)
Then there exists
  delta=delta(C_0,zeta)>0
such that
  |sum_{q in Z}mu(q)1_{(q,c)=1}A(q)K_{p,C}(q)|
  <<_{C_0,zeta} V_Q(A)Q^(1-delta).                            (5)
The constant is uniform in p,C,c,A.

One may take any fixed delta smaller than
  (1/2)min{zeta/50,19/6000,1/40}.                             (6)
Consequently every one-row mode in fact 71f1a10b52148348 has a fixed Q-power saving at a selected C1 prime p, once its local numerator is a unit modulo p and the auxiliary integer gn is squarefree and polynomially bounded in Q.

This theorem is one-row and prime-local. It does not retain the pair-dependent first-nonresonant determinant mask, estimate the resonant pair diagonal, give a four-linear deletion-aware translation estimate, sum varying selected primes or prove a complete C1-C4 trace or Goldbach estimate.
c23ca78883ba83d9.proof:
Define u_c(b)=1 when every prime divisor of b divides c, including u_c(1)=1, and put u_c(b)=0 otherwise. Euler factors give the exact convolution identity
  mu(q)1_{(q,c)=1}=(mu*u_c)(q).                                (7)
Indeed, at a prime r not dividing c the local factor is 1-X, while at r dividing c it is
  (1-X)(1+X+X^2+...)=1,
which deletes every positive r-adic exponent.

Insert (7) into the left side of (5) and write q=ab. Terms with p dividing b vanish by (3). For p not dividing b,
  K_{p,C}(ab)=K_{p,Cb^(-1)}(a),                               (8)
where Cb^(-1) is a nonzero residue modulo p. Thus the sum is
  sum_{b: all prime divisors of b divide c, p does not divide b}
  sum_a mu(a)A(ab)K_{p,Cb^(-1)}(a).                           (9)

We use Fouvry--Kowalski--Michel, arXiv:1207.0617, Theorem 2.5. It states that if K is an isotypic bounded-conductor trace function modulo p whose sheaf is not geometrically a direct sum of additive-times-multiplicative rank-one sheaves, then for every X>=1 and every eta<1/48,
  |sum_{a<=X}mu(a)K(a)|
  << X(1+p/X)^(1/12)p^(-eta),                                (10)
with a constant polynomial in the conductor. The reciprocal phase K_{p,D}(a)=1_{a!=0}e_p(Da^(-1)), D!=0, has fixed conductor and a pole at zero, so it is not of the excluded additive-linear times multiplicative form. This applicability is also recorded in fact 5ce79780e36b1ce1.

Take eta=1/50 and split (9) at
  b<=D_0=Q^(1/20).                                            (11)
For such b, the a-weight A(ab) is supported on an interval of length comparable to
  X_b=Q/b>=Q^(19/20).
Sampling A on the progression ab does not increase its supremum-plus-total-variation norm. Partial summation and the difference of the two endpoint forms of (10) therefore bound the inner sum in (9) by
  <<V_Q(A)X_b(1+p/X_b)^(1/12)p^(-1/50).                      (12)

If p<=X_b, the factor after X_b in (12) is
  <<p^(-1/50)<=Q^(-zeta/50).                                 (13)
If p>X_b, equations (1) and (11) give
  X_b^(-1/12)p^(1/12-1/50)
  <<Q^(-19/240)Q^((6/5)(19/300))
  =Q^(-19/6000).                                              (14)
Hence, with
  delta_0=min{zeta/50,19/6000},
every b in (11) contributes
  <<V_Q(A)(Q/b)Q^(-delta_0).                                  (15)

The reciprocal mass of the c-smooth semigroup is subpower:
  sum_{b:u_c(b)=1}1/b
  =product_{r|c}(1-1/r)^(-1)=Q^o(1).                          (16)
For completeness, the last estimate follows already from squarefreeness and c<=Q^C_0: if k=omega(c), then c is at least the product of the first k positive primes and hence at least (k+1)!, so k=O(log Q/loglog Q); bounding each Euler factor by (1-1/2)^(-1) gives exp(O(k))=Q^o(1). Summing (15) proves
  <<V_Q(A)Q^(1-delta_0+o(1))                                 (17)
for the small-b range.

For b>D_0 use the trivial bound V_Q(A)Q/b for the inner sum. Since
  1/b<=D_0^(-1/2)b^(-1/2),
the large-b contribution is at most
  V_Q(A)Q D_0^(-1/2)
  product_{r|c}(1-r^(-1/2))^(-1).                             (18)
The product is Q^o(1): every factor is bounded by the absolute constant (1-2^(-1/2))^(-1), and the same bound k=O(log Q/loglog Q) applies. Since D_0^(-1/2)=Q^(-1/40), (18) is
  V_Q(A)Q^(1-1/40+o(1)).                                      (19)
Equations (17)-(19) prove (5)-(6) after taking Q sufficiently large.

For the final C1 specialization, fact f0f6807663d3ef3c gives d_lambda=p on C1 and p<=n<=2B<2Q^(6/5), while fact ec8a0fbdab03cda6 gives p>=Q^zeta. Nonzero first-p activity forces the local numerator to be a unit. Facts b0a38f5e9ae7feb6 and ff228b0e569531f8 give squarefree, polynomially bounded gn, and fact 71f1a10b52148348 gives exactly the norm (4) mode by mode. Thus all hypotheses are matched at the one-row level, proving only the stated specialization and no pair-mask estimate.

glossary.K_{p,C}: The reciprocal additive trace modulo p, extended by zero at multiples of p.
glossary.u_c: The indicator of the multiplicative semigroup generated by primes dividing the squarefree auxiliary integer c.

c384d36af25e96a6.title: TERMINAL-INC-SCHUR: WEIGHTED GOOD-W n-TO-d INCIDENCE HAS THE CANONICAL B/D OPERATOR SCALE
c384d36af25e96a6.author: slava chan
c384d36af25e96a6.statement:
TERMINAL-INC-SCHUR: WEIGHTED GOOD-W n-TO-d INCIDENCE HAS THE CANONICAL B/D OPERATOR SCALE.

Fix real numbers B>=1, D>=1 and Z>2. Let N be a finite set of squarefree integers n satisfying
B/2<=n<=2B.                                                       (1)
For n in N put
P_I(n)={p:p is prime, p divides n, and 2<p<Z},
r(n)=|P_I(n)|.                                                    (2)
Construct a terminal edge set E as follows.

If r(n)>0, for every p in P_I(n) for which
D<=n/p<2D                                                        (3)
include one A-edge e=(n,d,p), where d=n/p, with weight
w_e=1/r(n).                                                       (4)

If r(n)=0 and n has the unique terminal C_j factorization of fact f234dbd4fdda994e,
n=dv,  v in {1,2},                                                (5)
include its C-edge e=(n,d,v) when D<=d<2D, with weight
w_e=1.                                                            (6)

The A and C alternatives are disjoint. For arbitrary complex phases eta_e with |eta_e|<=1 define
(Tf)(d)=sum_{e in E:d_e=d}w_e eta_e f(n_e)                        (7)
on finitely supported complex functions f on N, where d ranges over integers in [D,2D). Then
sum_{e:n_e=n}|w_e|<=1                                             (8)
for every n, and
sum_{e:d_e=d}|w_e|<=10 B/D                                       (9)
for every d. Consequently
||Tf||_2^2<=10(B/D)||f||_2^2.                                    (TERMINAL-INC-SCHUR)

The same bound holds when f(n) takes values in a Hilbert space and every eta_e is replaced by a contraction on that Hilbert space.

For the literal Good-W terminal marker, the A-edge weights in (4) are the absolute values of the exact coefficients mu(n)/r(n), and the C-edge weight is the absolute value of mu(n). Thus TERMINAL-INC-SCHUR supplies exactly the canonical B/D squared-operator factor from terminal incidence, without using relative marker signs, bounded variation, primality estimates, or executable computation.

This is an abstract incidence supplier, not yet a complete analytic consumer. To apply it to C-qSRC or a projected pre-copy hard form, the remaining literal source/ray/provenance coefficient must be represented as a common input Hilbert vector f(n), with every edge-dependent factor acting contractively after the accepted low-d-conductor exceptions are removed. No such factorization is asserted here. The theorem does not estimate the F>Q principal source, the small-dilator projected-incidence branch, C-qSRC-BV-SUP, GA-NR-DIL, the tail, or Goldbach.
c384d36af25e96a6.proof:
Fix n. In the A alternative, the edges retained by (3) form a subset of the r(n) interval-prime factorizations. Every one has weight 1/r(n), so their total absolute weight is at most one. In the C alternative there is one unique factorization and its weight is one. The alternatives are disjoint by fact f234dbd4fdda994e. This proves (8).

Fix d. An A-edge ending at d is determined by its prime p, because n=dp. Condition (1) implies
B/(2d)<=p<=2B/d.                                                   (10)
Therefore the number of possible A-edges ending at d is at most
2B/d+1<=2B/D+1.                                                   (11)
If an A-edge exists, then p>2 and n<=2B give
d=n/p< B,
so D<=d<B and hence B/D>1. Thus in the A case the right side of (11) is at most 3B/D. Since each A weight is at most one, the A contribution to the left side of (9) is at most 3B/D.

A C-edge ending at d has v in {1,2}, so there are at most two such edges, corresponding to n=d and n=2d. If any C-edge in the block exists, then d<2D and d=n/v<=2B, while also d>=D; in particular D<=2B and 2<=4B/D. Hence the C contribution is at most 4B/D. Combining the two contributions gives at most 7B/D, which implies the displayed convenient bound (9).

Let M_{d,n} be the matrix coefficient in (7). The triangle inequality and (8)-(9) give
sup_n sum_d|M_{d,n}|<=1,
sup_d sum_n|M_{d,n}|<=10B/D.                                    (12)
Schur's test applied to (12) yields
||T||_{2 to 2}^2
 <=(sup_n sum_d|M_{d,n}|)(sup_d sum_n|M_{d,n}|)
 <=10B/D,
which is TERMINAL-INC-SCHUR.

For Hilbert-valued inputs, take norms in each output coordinate before applying the scalar matrix with entries sum_{e:d_e=d,n_e=n}|w_e|. Contractions have operator norm at most one, so the same two Schur sums (12) dominate the Hilbert-valued operator. This proves the extension.

Finally, fact f234dbd4fdda994e proves that the literal A coefficients have absolute value 1/r(n) and the unique C_j coefficient has absolute value one. Hence the abstract incidence exactly matches the marker weights at the stated level. The exclusions follow because no factorization of the remaining literal analytic coefficient through T was proved.

glossary.E: The terminal A/C edge set between marked integers n and marked dilators d.
glossary.TERMINAL-INC-SCHUR: The weighted terminal n-to-d incidence operator bound with squared norm O(B/D).
glossary.w_e: The absolute terminal marker weight attached to one incidence edge.

c3fa858e3f5e6b3d.title: EXACT NESTED FAILURE LEDGER FOR THE GIANT1 ZHANG NO-BOX COMPLEMENT AND UNIFORM NO-FIT CHAMBERS. Fix X>1, 0<epsilon<1/20, Q_c=X^(1/2+delta_h) with delta_h>=0, a giant-prime dyadic scale P>=2, and a literal modulus s in [Q_c,2Q_c). Assume s is squarefree, as in the literal rows of facts 487a65cdbb7ab2fc and 2301d9c5068afddd
c3fa858e3f5e6b3d.author: slava chan
c3fa858e3f5e6b3d.statement:
EXACT NESTED FAILURE LEDGER FOR THE GIANT1 ZHANG NO-BOX COMPLEMENT AND UNIFORM NO-FIT CHAMBERS. Fix X>1, 0<epsilon<1/20, Q_c=X^(1/2+delta_h) with delta_h>=0, a giant-prime dyadic scale P>=2, and a literal modulus s in [Q_c,2Q_c). Assume s is squarefree, as in the literal rows of facts 487a65cdbb7ab2fc and 2301d9c5068afddd.

Let cal R_0(s) be the finite set of ordered quadruples
alpha=(Q_1,Q_2;q_1,q_2)
such that Q_1,Q_2 are powers of two at least 2,
s=q_1q_2,
Q_1<q_1<=2Q_1,
Q_2<q_2<=2Q_2.                                                  (1)
For alpha in cal R_0(s), define delta_alpha by
Q_1Q_2=X^(1/2+delta_alpha).                                      (2)
Define the nested subsets
cal R_1={alpha in cal R_0:delta_alpha>=0},                        (3)
cal R_2={alpha in cal R_1:Q_1^7Q_2^12<X^(4-10epsilon)},           (4)
cal R_3={alpha in cal R_2:Q_1X^(2delta_alpha+epsilon)<P},          (5)
cal R_4={alpha in cal R_3:P<X^(1-epsilon)/Q_1}.                   (6)
Then s is Zhang-eligible at P in the sense of fact 487a65cdbb7ab2fc if and only if cal R_4(s,P) is nonempty. Hence the exact no-box complement is the following disjoint exhaustive ledger:
NB-ARITH: cal R_0 is empty;
NB-DELTA: cal R_0 is nonempty and cal R_1 is empty;
NB-SHAPE: cal R_1 is nonempty and cal R_2 is empty;
NB-LOWP: cal R_2 is nonempty and cal R_3 is empty;
NB-HIGHP: cal R_3 is nonempty and cal R_4 is empty.               (7)
For a squarefree s>=3, NB-ARITH holds if and only if s has at most one odd prime divisor; equivalently s is prime or twice an odd prime. Thus the literal nonfactorable-modulus obstruction is an exact named part of the GIANT1 no-box complement.

Put
lambda_X=log 2/log X,
delta_min=max(0,delta_h-2lambda_X).                              (8)
Every alpha in cal R_0 satisfies
delta_h-2lambda_X<=delta_alpha<delta_h+lambda_X.                 (9)
Consequently each of the following is a uniform no-box chamber:
P<=X^(2/5+(22/5)delta_min+3epsilon);                             (10)
