P>=X^(3/5-(12/5)delta_min-3epsilon);                             (11)
delta_h>=1/14-(10/7)epsilon+2lambda_X.                           (12)
In particular (11) contains the simpler chamber
P>=X^(3/5-3epsilon),                                             (13)
already isolated in fact e77206678441fe0d. In the scale chamber (12), every literal modulus s in [Q_c,2Q_c) is noneligible, regardless of its arithmetic factorization.

Equations (7), (10)-(12) classify but do not estimate the no-box row. The Zhang-eligible projection remains paid by fact 2301d9c5068afddd. No claim is made for the analytic size of NB-ARITH, NB-DELTA, NB-SHAPE, NB-LOWP or NB-HIGHP, for the boundary between the no-fit chambers, for SMOOTH, MS-FIRST-NOSCALE, other HC sectors, the complete critical tail or Goldbach.
c3fa858e3f5e6b3d.proof:
The four conditions defining a (P,epsilon)-admissible Zhang box in fact 487a65cdbb7ab2fc are exactly (3)-(6), in that order. Therefore a raw factorization (1) is admissible exactly when it belongs to cal R_4. This proves the eligibility equivalence.

The sets cal R_0 superset cal R_1 superset cal R_2 superset cal R_3 superset cal R_4 are nested. If cal R_4 is empty, either cal R_0 is empty, or there is a unique first index j in {1,2,3,4} for which cal R_{j-1} is nonempty and cal R_j is empty. These five alternatives are precisely (7), so they are disjoint and exhaustive.

Because Q_i>=2 and Q_i<q_i, every raw factorization has q_i>=3. Thus cal R_0 is nonempty exactly when s has a factorization into two integers at least 3. Suppose s>=3 is squarefree. If s has at most one odd prime divisor, it is either an odd prime or twice an odd prime (with the harmless exceptional value 2 excluded by s>=3); neither can be written as a product of two integers at least 3. Conversely, if s has at least two odd prime divisors, take one odd prime as q_1 and put q_2=s/q_1. Both are at least 3. Each integer q_i>=3 lies in a unique interval Q_i<q_i<=2Q_i with Q_i a power of two at least 2. This produces an element of cal R_0 and proves the arithmetic characterization.

For every alpha in cal R_0, equation (1) and Q_i<q_i<=2Q_i give
Q_1Q_2<s<=4Q_1Q_2.
Since Q_c<=s<2Q_c,
Q_c/4<=Q_1Q_2<2Q_c.                                            (14)
Taking logarithms base X and using Q_c=X^(1/2+delta_h) gives (9).

Assume cal R_4 is nonempty and choose alpha in it. Fact e77206678441fe0d applies with delta=delta_alpha and proves
P>X^(2/5+(22/5)delta_alpha+3epsilon),                            (15)
P<X^(3/5-(12/5)delta_alpha-3epsilon),                            (16)
delta_alpha<1/14-(10/7)epsilon.                                 (17)
Membership in cal R_4 also gives delta_alpha>=0. Combining this with (9) yields delta_alpha>=delta_min. Equation (15) excludes (10), and (16) excludes (11). If (12) holds, then (9) gives
delta_alpha>=delta_h-2lambda_X
 >=1/14-(10/7)epsilon,
contradicting (17). Thus (12) is also a no-box chamber. Since delta_min>=0, the exponent on the right of (11) is at most 3/5-3epsilon, proving (13). No estimate for an empty-cal R_4 row follows from this set-theoretic and exponent argument.

glossary.NB-ARITH: The no-box class with no raw factorization into two integers at least 3.
glossary.NB-DELTA: The no-box class in which no raw factor box has nonnegative delta_alpha.
glossary.NB-HIGHP: The no-box class in which the upper selected-prime-scale condition eliminates every surviving box.
glossary.NB-LOWP: The no-box class in which the lower selected-prime-scale condition eliminates every surviving box.
glossary.NB-SHAPE: The no-box class in which the Zhang Q_1^7Q_2^12 shape condition eliminates all delta-eligible raw boxes.
glossary.cal R_0(s): The finite set of raw ordered dyadic two-factor representations of the literal modulus s.
glossary.cal R_j: The raw factor representations surviving the first j Zhang admissibility conditions.
glossary.delta_min: The lower bound max(0,delta_h-2lambda_X) for delta_alpha in an admissible literal box.
glossary.lambda_X: The dyadic endpoint error log 2/log X.

c4c340e494e65ae3.title: EXACT PHASE MAP AND NO DIRECT ARBITRARY-COMMON-ROW SPECIALIZATION OF DRAPPEAU'S QUINTILINEAR THEOREM. Drappeau, arXiv:1504.05549, Theorem 2.1, has the following input form. For C,D,N,R,S>=1, an auxiliary modulus q_aux and reduced residues c_0,d_0 modulo q_aux, a sequence b_{n,r,s} supported on
c4c340e494e65ae3.author: slava chan
c4c340e494e65ae3.statement:
EXACT PHASE MAP AND NO DIRECT ARBITRARY-COMMON-ROW SPECIALIZATION OF DRAPPEAU'S QUINTILINEAR THEOREM. Drappeau, arXiv:1504.05549, Theorem 2.1, has the following input form. For C,D,N,R,S>=1, an auxiliary modulus q_aux and reduced residues c_0,d_0 modulo q_aux, a sequence b_{n,r,s} supported on
0<n<=N, R<r<=2R, S<s<=2S,
and a smooth function g(c,d,n,r,s), compactly supported on C<c<=2C and D<d<=2D and satisfying its stated scale-normalized derivative bounds, it estimates
sum b_{n,r,s}g(c,d,n,r,s)e(n inverse(rd)/(sc))                       (1)
over c,d,n,r,s with c=c_0 and d=d_0 modulo q_aux and gcd(q_aux rd,sc)=1 by
(q_aux CDNRS)^{epsilon+O(epsilon_0)}
 q_aux^{3/2}K(C,D,N,R,S)||b||_2,                                   (2)
where
K^2=q_aux CS(RS+N)(C+RD)
 +C^2DS sqrt((RS+N)R)+D^2NRS^{-1}.                                 (3)
In particular b_{n,r,s} is independent of the two smooth variables c,d.

For one literal C4 rough factorization
n_C4=v p_1p_2p_3p_4
and the raw active semiprime p_1p_2, put
c=p_1, s=p_2, r=n_C4/(p_1p_2), d=q_base, n_num=Ah.                  (4)
Then the phase in (1) is exactly
e_{p_1p_2}(Ah[(n_C4/(p_1p_2))q_base]^{-1}),                         (5)
the literal raw active-semiprime inverse phase.

However, (4) is not a direct specialization of Theorem 2.1 for an arbitrary common-row coefficient z_{p_1,p_2,r}: that coefficient depends on c=p_1 and therefore cannot be placed in b_{n_num,r,s}, while the theorem requires the c-dependence to lie in the uniformly smooth function g. The literal restriction that p_1 is prime is likewise not one of the theorem's smooth c weights. Moreover the theorem's numerator support parameter must satisfy N>=|A|F on a height block |h|<=F; replacing Ah by its residue modulo p_1p_2 would make the numerator coefficient depend on the smooth modulus factors c,s and is not the same input interface. Thus Theorem 2.1 supplies the exact phase geometry but not the arbitrary-common-z C4 PMLS estimate by one direct variable identification. This does not rule out a new prime decomposition, a proved projective representation of the c-dependent row, or an extension of the theorem.
c4c340e494e65ae3.proof:
The complete statement (1)--(3) is Theorem 2.1 of the cited paper, with variables renamed only to distinguish q_aux from the C4 base variable. Its derivative hypothesis singles out c,d as smooth summation variables, while b has indices n,r,s only. Inspection of its proof confirms this structure: the d-variable is Poisson-completed, producing Kloosterman sums modulo sc q_aux, and b_{n,r,s} remains outside the smooth c,d transform before the spectral large sieve is applied.

Under (4), sc=p_1p_2 and rd=(n_C4/(p_1p_2))q_base. Therefore
e(n_num inverse(rd)/(sc))
=e_{p_1p_2}(Ah[(n_C4/(p_1p_2))q_base]^{-1}),
which proves (5).

A direct identification must assign every arbitrary coefficient to an index of b or to an already admissible smooth weight. The array z_{p_1,p_2,r} varies with p_1=c, but b_{n_num,r,s}=b_{Ah,r,p_2} has no c index. Hence assigning z to b loses its p_1 dependence. Assigning an arbitrary z-array, or the discontinuous prime indicator, to g does not verify the theorem's uniform scale-normalized derivative hypotheses and therefore is not a direct application. Finally n_num=Ah ranges up to |A|F. Reducing it modulo sc depends on c and s, so the resulting coefficient would no longer occupy the c-independent numerator slot. These are exact input-slot statements, proving the scoped no-direct-specialization conclusion.

glossary.N_th: the numerator support scale in Drappeau Theorem 2.1
glossary.n_num: the numerator variable in the theorem mapping, equal to Ah
glossary.q_aux: the auxiliary congruence modulus in Drappeau Theorem 2.1

c57a4fa72a532b64.title: Let \(P_1,P_2,N\) be positive integers and let \(h\in\mathbb Z\). For
c57a4fa72a532b64.author: slava chan
c57a4fa72a532b64.statement:
Let \(P_1,P_2,N\) be positive integers and let \(h\in\mathbb Z\). For
complex \(z_1,z_2\), define the finite two-variable divisor function
\[
\begin{split}
 {\cal E}_{P_1,P_2;N,h}(z_1,z_2)=
 \sum_{\substack{q_1\mid P_1,\ q_2\mid P_2\\
                 (N,[q_1,q_2])=1\\
                 (q_1,q_2)\mid h}}
 &\mu(q_1)\mu(q_2)
 {\phi([q_1,q_2])\over[q_1,q_2]^2}\\
 &\times(P_1/q_1)^{z_1}(P_2/q_2)^{z_2}.                \tag{1}
\end{split}
\]
Then the logarithmically weighted double-zero divisor coefficient is
exactly
\[
\begin{split}
 &\sum_{\substack{q_1\mid P_1,\ q_2\mid P_2\\
                 (N,[q_1,q_2])=1\\
                 (q_1,q_2)\mid h}}
 \mu(q_1)\mu(q_2){\phi([q_1,q_2])\over[q_1,q_2]^2}
 \log(P_1/q_1)\log(P_2/q_2)\\
 &\qquad=
 \left.
 {\partial^2\over\partial z_1\partial z_2}
 {\cal E}_{P_1,P_2;N,h}(z_1,z_2)
 \right|_{z_1=z_2=0}.                                  \tag{2}
\end{split}
\]

Put
\[
 a_\ell={\ell-1\over\ell^2}
\]
for a prime \(\ell\). The exact finite Euler factorization is
\[
 {\cal E}_{P_1,P_2;N,h}(z_1,z_2)
 =
 P_1^{z_1}P_2^{z_2}\prod_\ell F_\ell(z_1,z_2),          \tag{3}
\]
where \(F_\ell=1\) if \(\ell\mid N\), and, for \(\ell\nmid N\),
\[
 F_\ell=
 \begin{cases}
 1,&\ell\nmid P_1P_2,\\
 1-a_\ell\ell^{-z_1},&\ell\mid P_1,\ \ell\nmid P_2,\\
 1-a_\ell\ell^{-z_2},&\ell\nmid P_1,\ \ell\mid P_2,\\
 1-a_\ell\ell^{-z_1}-a_\ell\ell^{-z_2}
 +{\bf1}_{\ell\mid h}a_\ell\ell^{-z_1-z_2},
   &\ell\mid(P_1,P_2).
 \end{cases}                                           \tag{4}
\]
Only finitely many factors differ from one.

Equations (2)--(4) are the exact local Euler/convolution formula for the
double-zero multiplier \(\phi([q_1,q_2])/[q_1,q_2]^2\) on the coprime TMC
face. They do not by themselves identify its sum over the reflected
variables \(P_1=N-mw\), \(P_2=N-m(w-h)\) with the two-linear-form singular
series of fact 5b7b0955c5efaa1b. Such an identification must also account
for the dependence of the local factors on the actual prime divisors of
\(P_1,P_2\) and on \(\ell\mid h\).
c57a4fa72a532b64.proof:
The sum in (1) is finite, so it may be differentiated term by term.
For every positive real \(X\),
\[
 {d\over dz}X^z\big|_{z=0}=\log X.
\]
Applying this identity once to each of the two powers proves (2).

We prove (3)--(4) prime by prime. Terms with a nonsquarefree \(q_i\)
vanish because of \(\mu(q_i)\), so at a prime \(\ell\) the exponents of
\(q_1,q_2\) are in \(\{0,1\}\). If \(\ell\mid N\), the condition
\((N,[q_1,q_2])=1\) forces both exponents to be zero, giving \(F_\ell=1\).

Assume \(\ell\nmid N\). The local weight is one when both exponents are
zero. If exactly one exponent is one, the Möbius sign is \(-1\), the lcm
is \(\ell\), and
\[
 {\phi(\ell)\over\ell^2}=a_\ell.
\]
The corresponding power contributes \(\ell^{-z_1}\) or
\(\ell^{-z_2}\) after the common factor \(P_1^{z_1}P_2^{z_2}\) is
removed. This gives the two one-sided factors in (4).

If both exponents are one, this choice is available only when
\(\ell\mid P_1\), \(\ell\mid P_2\), and the common-divisor condition
\((q_1,q_2)\mid h\) requires \(\ell\mid h\). The product of Möbius signs
is \(+1\), the lcm remains \(\ell\), and the local term is
\[
 a_\ell\ell^{-z_1-z_2}.
\]
Adding the four exponent choices proves the final line of (4).
Multiplication over primes proves (3). The final scope statement follows
because (3) is indexed by prime divisors of the two particular values
\(P_1,P_2\), whereas fact 5b7b0955c5efaa1b concerns the already defined
Hardy--Littlewood local-density product for two affine forms after
averaging the slope variables.

glossary.cal E_{P_1,P_2;N,h}: the two-variable finite Euler generating function for the TMC double-zero divisor coefficient

c585f0febfbab2f4.title: EXACT DIGIT-TO-KLOOSTERMAN-FREQUENCY TRANSPORT AND THE MOVING-GATE FULL-AXIS MISMATCH
c585f0febfbab2f4.author: slava chan
c585f0febfbab2f4.statement:
EXACT DIGIT-TO-KLOOSTERMAN-FREQUENCY TRANSPORT AND THE MOVING-GATE FULL-AXIS MISMATCH.

Let m>1 be odd, put q=m^2, let s belong to {1,-1}, and let K and n be integers with gcd(Kn,m)=1. Choose an inverse K_bar of K modulo q. For u modulo m put
 A_u=K+2smu.                                                        (1)
Then A_u is a unit modulo q and
 A_u^(-1) is congruent to K_bar-2smu K_bar^2 modulo q.              (2)
Consequently, whenever a is a unit modulo q and
 an is congruent to A_u modulo q,                                  (3)
one has
 a^(-1) is congruent to nK_bar-2smu nK_bar^2 modulo q.              (4)

For p modulo q define the unit residue modulo m
 gamma_n congruent to 2s nK_bar^2 modulo m.                         (5)
Then the exact inverse-column Fourier phase is
 e_q(-p a^(-1))
 =e_q(-pnK_bar)e_m(gamma_n p u).                                  (6)

Let W and G_u be arbitrary complex functions modulo m and define
 f(u)=W(u)G_u(u),qquad
 f_hat(ell)=sum_{u modulo m}f(u)e_m(-ell u).                        (7)
For fixed p,n the u-assembly of (6) is
 sum_{u modulo m}W(u)G_u(u)e_q(-pnA_u^(-1))
 =e_q(-pnK_bar) f_hat(-gamma_n p).                                 (8)
Here p on the right is reduced modulo m.

If W(u)=e_m(ell_0u) is a pure nonzero digit mode and G_u is identically one, (8) vanishes unless
 gamma_n p is congruent to -ell_0 modulo m.                         (9)
Thus this idealized u-independent coefficient confines the complete p-axis modulo q to one residue class modulo m, containing exactly m residues p modulo q.

For general G_u,
 f_hat(ell)=G_u_hat(ell-ell_0).                                    (10)
In particular, if G_u is the literal singleton gate of one residue u_0, then G_u_hat is nonzero at every frequency modulo m, and (8) is nonzero for every residue class p modulo m. Each such class has m lifts modulo q, so the full q-element p-axis is restored.

Equations (6)-(10) identify the exact phase coherence available before the coefficient L2 majorant in facts 212d1415bf03c2a7 and f23bad095a2e6a52. Pure digit centering alone shortens the p-axis only when every remaining gate is u-independent. A moving interval, carry, prime, carrier, or source gate may have full u-Fourier support, and the stated one-column theorems permit such bounded tuple gates. Therefore a trace theorem that uses the one-class support (9) must also control the Fourier support or variation of the actual combined u-dependent gate; it cannot infer the shortening from W alone.

This is an exact transform and theorem-interface statement. It does not assert that every actual source gate has full Fourier support, and it does not rule out a joint digit-carrier trace estimate that treats (8) before taking absolute values.
c585f0febfbab2f4.proof:
Because gcd(K,m)=1, K and every A_u are units modulo q. Multiply the proposed inverse in (2) by A_u:
 (K+2smu)(K_bar-2smuK_bar^2).
The product of the two terms containing m is divisible by m^2. The remaining expression is congruent modulo q to
 KK_bar+2smu(K_bar-KK_bar^2).
Now KK_bar is congruent to one modulo q, and
 K_bar-KK_bar^2=K_bar(1-KK_bar)
is divisible by q. Hence the product is congruent to one modulo q, proving (2).

From (3), multiplication by a^(-1)A_u^(-1) gives
 a^(-1) congruent to nA_u^(-1) modulo q. Inserting (2) proves (4). Substitute (4) into e_q(-pa^(-1)). The term containing m satisfies
 e_q(2smpunK_bar^2)=e_m(2spunK_bar^2),
which is exactly the second factor in (6) by (5). Since 2,s,n,K_bar are all units modulo m, gamma_n is a unit.

Multiplying (6) by W(u)G_u(u) and summing u gives
 e_q(-pnK_bar)sum_u f(u)e_m(gamma_npu)
 =e_q(-pnK_bar)f_hat(-gamma_np),
which proves (8).

For W(u)=e_m(ell_0u) and G_u=1, the inner sum is
 sum_u e_m((ell_0+gamma_np)u).
Orthogonality of additive characters modulo m makes it equal to m when (9) holds and zero otherwise. Since gamma_n is a unit, (9) selects exactly one p residue modulo m, and every residue modulo m has exactly m lifts modulo m^2.

For general G_u,
 f_hat(ell)=sum_uG_u(u)e_m(ell_0u)e_m(-ell u)
           =G_u_hat(ell-ell_0),
proving (10). If G_u is the indicator of u_0, then
 G_u_hat(r)=e_m(-ru_0),
which has absolute value one for every r. Equation (8) is therefore nonzero in every p class modulo m, and counting its lifts proves the full-axis assertion.

Facts 212d1415bf03c2a7 and f23bad095a2e6a52 form their one-column coefficient by summing W(u) against bounded tuple gates before applying Parseval and a coefficient L2 bound. Formula (8) is the exact Fourier transform of that u dependence in the simplified fixed-n slot. The two examples prove respectively the possible one-class collapse and its destruction by an allowed u-dependent gate. The final scope follows because no claim was made about the Fourier spectrum of a particular source gate.

glossary.A_u: the unit residue K+2smu modulo m squared
glossary.G_u: an additional u-dependent gate in the one-column coefficient
glossary.gamma_n: the unit residue 2s n K^{-2} modulo m governing digit-to-p frequency transport

c5f49ab9e8bd2c60.title: SAME-GAUGE NONPRINCIPAL SOURCE-PAIR L2 KERNEL AND ORDINARY CHARACTER-LARGE-SIEVE NO-FIT
c5f49ab9e8bd2c60.author: slava chan
c5f49ab9e8bd2c60.statement:
SAME-GAUGE NONPRINCIPAL SOURCE-PAIR L2 KERNEL AND ORDINARY CHARACTER-LARGE-SIEVE NO-FIT.

Fix constants C,J>=1. Let Q>=8 and let real numbers H,V,P,B satisfy
  2<=H<=Q^(1/3),  2<=V<H,  P=QH/V,  B>=1.                 (1)
Let A be a nonzero integer with |A|<=Q^C. Let cal L be a finite label set. For ell in cal L, an integer v in [V,2V), and a prime p in [P,2P) with gcd(v,p)=1, put n=vp and let cal X_{ell,v,p} be a finite set of triples x=(q,m,k) satisfying
  Q<=q,m<2Q,  qm+nk=A,  gcd(qm,n)=1.                       (2)
For h in an integer interval I_ell contained either in [H,2H) or in (-2H,-H], let a_{ell,v,p,h}(x) be a complex coefficient of modulus at most B. It may retain every literal source, least-prime, marker, fixed-U, frequency, collision, provenance, and projective mask, but it does not include the source phase e_q(hk).

For x=(q,m,k), put
  d_q=gcd(|A|,q),  q_0(q)=q/d_q,  t_x=k/d_q.               (3)
Facts 7670948dedd78714 and db067f4633c13fed give
  gcd(t_x,q_0(q))=1,  e_q(Ah nbar)=e_q(hk)=e_{q_0(q)}(ht_x). (4)
For r>=1 and a unit t modulo r define
  pi_{r,h}=c_r(h)/phi(r),                                   (5)
  eta_{r,h}(t)=e_r(ht)-pi_{r,h}.                            (6)
Then fact 6836789040c87b6f gives the exact same-gauge character formula
  eta_{r,h}(t)
   =phi(r)^(-1)sum_{chi modulo r, chi not equal chi_0}
       G_{r,h}(chi)chi(t).                                  (7)

Define, for each outer row o=(ell,v,p),
  Y_{o,h}=sum_{x in cal X_o}a_{o,h}(x)e_{q_0(q_x)}(ht_x),   (8)
  P_{o,h}=sum_{x in cal X_o}a_{o,h}(x)pi_{q_0(q_x),h},      (9)
  N_{o,h}=sum_{x in cal X_o}a_{o,h}(x)
                    eta_{q_0(q_x),h}(t_x).                 (10)
Then exactly Y_{o,h}=P_{o,h}+N_{o,h}. Put
  M_2^src=sum_o sum_{h in I_ell}|Y_{o,h}|^2,
  M_2^pr=sum_o sum_h|P_{o,h}|^2,
  M_2^np=sum_o sum_h|N_{o,h}|^2.                           (11)
One has
  M_2^src<=2M_2^pr+2M_2^np.                                (12)

Assume explicitly that the principal aggregate in every outer row has the normalized finite-band decay/provenance factorization of fact 6836789040c87b6f with its parameter L_pr satisfying L_pr<=BH. Assume also that B and #cal L are subpolynomial. Then, for every epsilon>0,
  M_2^pr<<_{C,J,epsilon}B^2Q^(1+epsilon)H^3
  <<_{C,J,epsilon}P Q^(5/3+epsilon).                       (13)
Thus it is sufficient for the source-specialized L2 target of fact 294ac3b02b065aec to prove the corresponding bound for M_2^np.

The nonprincipal mass has the exact source-pair expansion
  M_2^np
   =sum_o sum_h sum_{x_1,x_2 in cal X_o}
      a_{o,h}(x_1)conjugate(a_{o,h}(x_2))
      K_h^np(x_1,x_2),                                     (14)
where
  K_h^np(x_1,x_2)
   =eta_{q_0(q_1),h}(t_{x_1})
      conjugate(eta_{q_0(q_2),h}(t_{x_2}))                 (15)
  =[phi(q_0(q_1))phi(q_0(q_2))]^(-1)
    sum_{chi_1 not equal chi_{0,1}}
    sum_{chi_2 not equal chi_{0,2}}
      G_{q_0(q_1),h}(chi_1)
      conjugate(G_{q_0(q_2),h}(chi_2))
      chi_1(t_{x_1})conjugate(chi_2(t_{x_2}).               (16)
In particular, the q_1 not equal to q_2 part of (14) is the exact post-principal same-height TT-star kernel. The two reduced conductors remain separate; no character is lifted to a common gauge.

There is a precise no-fit for direct insertion of the ordinary character large sieve, even on a favorable separated prime-conductor slice. Suppose on such a slice:
(a) every supported q is prime, q does not divide A, and cal X_o has one atom x_q for every supported q;
(b) a_{o,h}(x_q)=z_{o,h}b_{o,q}, with |z_{o,h}|<=1 and |b_{o,q}|<=B.
Then the ordinary dual multiplicative large sieve gives
  sum_{h in I_ell}|N_{o,h}|^2
  <<B^2Q^(3+epsilon)/H                                     (17)
using only the available source-cardinality bound. Summed over all O(#cal L VP) outer rows, this gives only
  M_2^np(prime separated slice)
  <<B^2(#cal L)Q^(4+epsilon).                              (18)
Relative to P Q^(5/3), the ratio of the powers in (18) is
  Q^4/[P Q^(5/3)]=VQ^(4/3)/H>=2Q.                         (19)
Thus the standard character large sieve, applied directly after same-gauge principal removal and using the currently available source-cardinality envelope, does not supply the required L2 bound. This is a no-fit for that upper-bound insertion, not a lower bound for the literal kernel. It does not rule out a source-specific dispersion theorem using the joint variation of t_x, v, p, the divisor-selected source support, or the signed q_1 not equal to q_2 assembly.

No estimate for the full kernel (14)-(16), no PMD closure, and no Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
c5f49ab9e8bd2c60.proof:
Equation (2) and gcd(qm,n)=1 imply gcd(A,n)=1. Facts 7670948dedd78714 and db067f4633c13fed then prove every assertion in (4), including d_q|k and the same-gauge phase identity. Equations (5)-(7) are the principal/nonprincipal split in fact 6836789040c87b6f. Substitution into (8) proves Y=P+N. The elementary inequality |u+v|^2<=2|u|^2+2|v|^2, summed over o,h, proves (12).

We justify (13). The q-coordinate projection is injective on cal X_o by fact 914048233fada05f, so the coefficient may be regarded as one row indexed by q. Under the explicitly assumed normalized decay/provenance factorization, fact 6836789040c87b6f gives for each outer row
  sum_h|P_{o,h}|<<_{C,J,epsilon}L_prQ^epsilon
                  <=BHQ^epsilon.                           (20)
Therefore
  sum_h|P_{o,h}|^2<=(sum_h|P_{o,h}|)^2
                   <<B^2H^2Q^epsilon.                     (21)
There are O((#cal L)VP) outer rows. Since VP=QH and B,#cal L are subpolynomial, summing (21) gives the first bound in (13). Its ratio to P Q^(5/3) is
  [QH^3]/[Q^(8/3)H/V]=VH^2/Q^(5/3)
  <H^3/Q^(5/3)<=Q^(-2/3),
using V<H and H<=Q^(1/3). This proves the second bound.

Expand the square in M_2^np and use (10). This proves (14)-(15). Insert (7) independently for x_1 and x_2 to prove (16). At no point are q_0(q_1) and q_0(q_2) identified, proving the gauge assertion.

It remains to prove the method-specific bound. On the prime slice, d_q=1, q_0(q)=q, and t_x=k. Since |h|<2H<q, h is a unit modulo q. Every nonprincipal character modulo the prime q is primitive. Changing variables u to h^(-1)u in the definition of G gives
  G_{q,h}(chi)=chi(h)tau_q(conjugate(chi)),                 (22)
where
  tau_q(conjugate(chi))
    =sum_{u modulo q}conjugate(chi(u))e_q(u),
and |tau_q(conjugate(chi))|=q^(1/2). The latter Gauss-sum identity is included in the primitive-character formula used in fact 3afa321a72a3612b.

Equations (7), (10), and the separated coefficient hypothesis give
  N_{o,h}
   =z_{o,h}sum_q sum_{chi modulo q, chi not equal chi_0}
       C_{q,chi}chi(h),                                    (23)
where
  C_{q,chi}
   =b_{o,q}tau_q(conjugate(chi))chi(t_{x_q})/(q-1).         (24)
Because t_{x_q} is a unit modulo q,
  sum_{chi not equal chi_0}|C_{q,chi}|^2
  =|b_{o,q}|^2(q-2)q/(q-1)^2
  <=2|b_{o,q}|^2.                                          (25)

Fact 3afa321a72a3612b reproduces the multiplicative large sieve for primitive characters:
  sum_{r<=R}r/phi(r) sum_{chi modulo r primitive}
    |sum_h z_h chi(h)|^2
  <<(L_h+R^2)sum_h|z_h|^2                                 (26)
for coefficients on an interval of length L_h. Hilbert-space duality, and r/phi(r)>=1, give
  sum_{h in I_ell}|sum_{r<=2Q}sum_{chi primitive modulo r}
       C_{r,chi}chi(h)|^2
  <<(H+Q^2)sum_{r<=2Q}sum_{chi primitive}|C_{r,chi}|^2.   (27)
The factors z_{o,h} have modulus at most one, so they do not increase the left side when (23) is inserted. By (25), the right side is
  <<B^2Q^2 X_o,                                            (28)
where X_o=#cal X_o.

Fact 914048233fada05f gives
  X_o<<Q^epsilon(1+Q^2/n).
Here n=vp>=VP=QH, and Q/H>=1, so
  X_o<<Q^(1+epsilon)/H.                                    (29)
Equations (28)-(29) prove (17). The number of outer rows is O((#cal L)VP)=O((#cal L)QH); summation proves (18). Finally P=QH/V gives the equality in (19), while V>=2 and H<=Q^(1/3) give its lower bound. The argument used only an available upper envelope for X_o, so (18)-(19) are explicitly a theorem-insertion no-fit and not a lower bound. This proves all scope statements.

glossary.K_h^np: The exact product of two nonprincipal same-gauge remainders in the source-pair L2 kernel.
glossary.M_2^np: The L2 mass of the nonprincipal source rows after the principal row is split off.
glossary.eta_{q,h}(t): The nonprincipal same-gauge character remainder e_{q_0}(ht)-c_{q_0}(h)/phi(q_0).

c641ed6b2cda758b.title: LARGEST-ACTIVE-PRIME LOCALIZATION AND POWER-SMALL TOTAL SHORT-BLOCK BASELINE IN TOP-B
c641ed6b2cda758b.author: slava chan
c641ed6b2cda758b.proof:
Because y is squarefree, r_y is squarefree. If p divides r_y, then p divides y and p does not divide (mathscr AOmega). Also p does not divide y/p. These are the only properties of the selected prime used in the CRT proof of fact 97b9d86408362df2. Applying the same CRT identity with (t=y/p) gives its formulas (2)-(4) verbatim. Multiplying the p-local denominator (u(y/p)) gives the natural cofactor (T=n/p), proving (2). In the LARGE-ACTIVE-PRIME branch, (1) and fact 975285ea0f932fe6 give the lower bound in (3); its stopping-support bound gives the upper bound. Since ( eta<6/5) and (sigmale1/10000), one has ( eta-1+sigma<1), proving p<Q for large Q.

We prove (4). Since L_{p,k}<p, a fixed cofactor residue determines at most one physical integer T in the block. Hence n=pT is fixed, and the supported factorizations n=uy are divisor-many. A fixed r determines q modulo p, giving (O(1+Q/p)) physical lifts. A fixed H determines physical h modulo p and gives (O(1+F/p)) lifts in the two signed intervals. Fact d63101722d12c88c bounds the recombined coefficient by a fixed divisor function; the residual CRT factor in fact 97b9d86408362df2 has modulus one. Polynomial size absorbs all divisor losses into (Q^epsilon). This proves (4). The physical q interval represents at most p residues and contains at most Q+1 integers, proving (5).

The physical signed height intervals represent at most (H_p^0=min(p,4F)) residues. Therefore summing (4) over height residues, squaring, summing over at most R_p shifts and inserting the normalization (L_{p,k}^2) is bounded by (6). Moreover
[
 H_p^0(1+F/p)ll F.                                              	ag{12}
]
If p<=4F, the left side is at most (p+Fle5F); if p>4F, it is at most (4F(1+1/4)=5F). This proves (7). If p<=2F, then (H_p^0=p), while fact 831d32b948e6dcdb uses (p-1) in the corresponding coarse baseline. Hence the square of (6) dominates its (mathscr B_{0,p,k,X}), after aligning the identical harmless coefficient bound C_p. This proves the corrected comparison.

The deterministic partition in fact ec8a0fbdab03cda6 has every block except possibly the last of length (M_p=lfloor(p-1)/2floor). Since p>=Q^zeta tends to infinity, (M_pgesqrt p) for sufficiently large Q. This proves (8) and uniqueness of the possible short block.

Assume (9). Then (L_{p,k_{m term}}^2<p). From p<Q and (5),
[
 R_ple p,qquad 1+Q/pll Q/p.
]
Using these inequalities in (7) gives
[
 overline Y^0_{p,k_{m term},X}
 ll_epsilon Q^epsilon
 pcdot pcdot F^2{Q^2over p^2}
 =Q^epsilon Q^2F^2,
]
which is (10). The number of possible selected primes is at most p_max. Summing (10) proves the first bound in (11). Since (B=Q^ eta),
[
 p_{max}=Q^{ eta-1+sigma}=Q^{-1+sigma}B,
]
proving the identity in (11). Finally, nonnegativity gives
(sum Y^2le(sum Y)^2), proving the conditional fourth-moment assertion. The remaining limitations are precisely the hypotheses not constructed here.

glossary.H_p^0: The coarse number min(p,4F) of available local height-residue slots.
glossary.\\overline Y^0_{p,k,X}: The coarse all-height natural-cofactor baseline of one selected-prime block.
glossary.k_{\rm term}(p): The index of the unique terminal block in the deterministic partition of J_p.

c6a3ee810402825f.title: FORWARD FULL-G ALL-LEAF ASSEMBLY THROUGH THE FULL LOW-BETA RANGE. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100 and put sigma=kappa/100. Consider the literal forward forced-high frozen source layers of facts a71f777ad842c886, 5ced883d5560f772, and 0d53c27d174b26ed. Thus R>D, D=x^(1/2+o(1)), R>x^(9/16-kappa_0) with kappa_0=1/200, d=ga, r=gb, g=gcd(d,r) divides N, and
c6a3ee810402825f.author: slava chan
c6a3ee810402825f.statement:
FORWARD FULL-G ALL-LEAF ASSEMBLY THROUGH THE FULL LOW-BETA RANGE. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100 and put sigma=kappa/100. Consider the literal forward forced-high frozen source layers of facts a71f777ad842c886, 5ced883d5560f772, and 0d53c27d174b26ed. Thus R>D, D=x^(1/2+o(1)), R>x^(9/16-kappa_0) with kappa_0=1/200, d=ga, r=gb, g=gcd(d,r) divides N, and
Q=D/g>1, B=R/g=Q^beta, 1<=beta<=6/5-2kappa,
G=M/Q>=1, H_T=B/Q, H_P=B/M=H_T/G,
L_src=N/g, and DM=gGQ^2 asymp x.
Let R_fwd,low be the complete literal nonzero-Poisson sum of all such exact g-layers, retaining every frozen low-beta parent, every normalized marker leaf C0,A,B,C1,C2,C3, every Fourier block, exact target-gcd layer, source coefficient, smooth/projective label, prime-order label, fixed-U mask, high-label mask, parent mask, collision stratum, and deletion selector occurring in the source identity. Then there is a fixed delta=delta(kappa)>0 such that
|R_fwd,low| << x^(1-delta).
No interval-prime A target-gcd incidence is deleted, and the estimate includes H_P<1. The assertion is only for the displayed forward forced-high, actual-G>=1, low-beta layers. It makes no assertion about reverse orientation, beta>=6/5, endpoint parents, PMD, a logical bad-N conclusion, or Goldbach.
c6a3ee810402825f.proof:
Fact 0d53c27d174b26ed already proves the required complete-frequency power saving for every literal C0, B, C1, C2, and C3 leaf and for every A sector except the explicitly identified possibly nonunit low-G residual. It retains all labels listed in the statement and includes H_P<1. It is therefore enough to close that A residual, although the argument below in fact estimates every A target-gcd layer uniformly.

Fix an exact g-layer and a literal interval-prime A incidence. The source variables satisfy
am+bk=L_src, gcd(a,b)=1,
and a and b are squarefree. Put
c=gcd(a,L_src).
Fact 1c64020b89f097c4 gives
a=cq, k=ck_1, L_src=cL_1,
gcd(c,q)=gcd(c,b)=gcd(q,b)=1, and gcd(q,L_1)=1.               (1)
The exact reciprocal phase therefore descends without alteration of h or b:
e_a(-L_src h b^(-1))=e_q(-L_1h b^(-1)).                     (2)
Thus L_1=L_src/c is a unit modulo the descended reciprocal modulus q.

The literal all-frequency separation in the proof of fact 0d53c27d174b26ed is valid for every G>=1. On a signed dyadic block F<=|h|<2F it writes the literal kernel as a projective sum with total projective norm
<< (log x)^2(1+F/H_P)^(-A_1)                                (3)
for every fixed A_1, while retaining the literal prefactor H_P^(-1), every fixed-U and source mask, the high-label scalar, and the frozen parent scalar. The exact A marker writes b=up with U_cY_c asymp B and
H_TQ^sigma/2<=Y_c<=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma).
Squarefreeness and (1) give gcd(u,p)=1 and gcd(up,cq)=1. The descended modulus has size q asymp Q/c. Fact 5ced883d5560f772 gives, uniformly on these forced-high low-beta layers,
|L_src|<=Q^C_A                                                (4)
for a fixed C_A depending only on kappa. Consequently (1)-(4), the marker divisor bounds, and the literal projective expansion match every hypothesis of fact 653b56b5854f603b. Notice that (3) supplies its arbitrary fixed-order omega decay uniformly even when H_P<1; no near-balanced condition on G is used.

Set
C_cut=H_TQ^(sigma/4).
For the exact target-gcd divisors c<=C_cut, fact 653b56b5854f603b yields, on the fixed g-layer,
sum_{c<=C_cut}|T_c| << GQ^(2-delta_1)                         (5)
for some fixed delta_1>0, uniformly in every inherited label and deletion selector.

For c>C_cut use fact 5fbdbbebf99aec55. Its elementary absolute estimate applies because B=QH_T<=Q^(6/5), H_P<=H_T<=Q^(1/5), the literal coefficients obey fixed divisor bounds, and (3) provides the required fixed-order decay. With its lower cutoff C_0=C_cut and xi=sigma/4 it gives
sum_{c>C_cut}|T_c| << Q^(2-sigma/4+epsilon)
                   << GQ^(2-sigma/8)                         (6)
after fixing epsilon<sigma/8, since G>=1. The estimate permits all the phases, gcd selectors, prime restrictions, smooth masks, and deletion conditions present here.

Combining (5)-(6), and absorbing the polylogarithmically many projective, dyadic, sign, parent, source, prime-cell, and collision labels, gives for the complete A contribution on the exact g-layer
<<GQ^(2-delta_2)                                              (7)
with fixed delta_2>0. By DM=gGQ^2 asymp x, (7) is
<<(x/g)Q^(-delta_2).                                         (8)

Fact 5ced883d5560f772 also proves that throughout the forced-high low-beta source
Q>=x^(c_kappa+o(1))                                          (9)
for a fixed c_kappa>0 depending only on kappa. Since g divides N,
sum_{g|N}1/g <=tau(N)=x^o(1).
Summing (8) over exact g and using (9) therefore gives O(x^(1-delta_3)) for some fixed delta_3>0. Add the already established C0, B, C1, C2, C3, and complementary A sectors from fact 0d53c27d174b26ed and decrease delta once more to absorb the finite anatomy types and polylogarithmic labels. This proves the complete stated forward estimate with no A target-gcd deletion.

glossary.R_fwd,low: The complete literal forward forced-high nonzero-Poisson sum over actual G>=1 and 1<=beta<=6/5-2kappa.
glossary.delta_2: The fixed saving exponent for the complete A contribution at one exact g-layer.
glossary.delta_3: The fixed global saving exponent after summing exact outer gcds.

c72a96984158fa33.title: REFINED STRICT-TOP C1 SMOOTH-DIVISOR THRESHOLD BELOW 7/384. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, and let beta_m<=beta<6/5 in the literal strict-top C1 setting. Thus n=pv is squarefree, p is the unique rough prime, gcd(p,v)=1, every prime divisor of v is at most L=Q^(beta-1+sigma), C=mathscr A h, and m_eff=n/gcd(C,n). Assume Q^(1/2+kappa)<=m_eff<=Q^(6/5). Put theta=1/100 and lambda=1/200
c72a96984158fa33.author: slava chan
c72a96984158fa33.statement:
REFINED STRICT-TOP C1 SMOOTH-DIVISOR THRESHOLD BELOW 7/384. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, and let beta_m<=beta<6/5 in the literal strict-top C1 setting. Thus n=pv is squarefree, p is the unique rough prime, gcd(p,v)=1, every prime divisor of v is at most L=Q^(beta-1+sigma), C=mathscr A h, and m_eff=n/gcd(C,n). Assume Q^(1/2+kappa)<=m_eff<=Q^(6/5). Put theta=1/100 and lambda=1/200.

(i) If p divides C, then m_eff has a divisor m_1 satisfying
m_eff^lambda<=m_1<=m_eff^(1/2-lambda).
(ii) If p does not divide C, then p divides m_eff. Put r_eff=m_eff/p. If r_eff>=Q^theta, then m_eff has a divisor m_1 in the same window.

Consequently, in a balanced two-free cell with m_eff comparable to Q and B_* comparable to Q^(1/2), fact 8eb30e55bdef6b27 places the cell in A-PAID(delta,rho), for any fixed positive delta,rho satisfying 4(delta+rho)<1/200, except possibly when
p does not divide C, m_eff=p r_eff, r_eff<Q^(1/100).
The complement threshold 1/100 is strictly smaller than 7/384. This is a structural routing theorem only; it does not estimate the final displayed residual.
c72a96984158fa33.proof:
Because beta<6/5 and sigma<=1/10000, every prime divisor of v is at most
L=Q^(beta-1+sigma)<Q^(2001/10000).                              (1)
We prove a deterministic divisor statement. Let s be a squarefree divisor of v with s>=Q^(1/100). Multiply the prime divisors of s in any fixed order until their product d first reaches Q^(1/100). The product before the last prime is smaller than Q^(1/100), while the last prime is at most L. Hence
Q^(1/100)<=d<Q^(1/100)L<Q^(2101/10000).                         (2)
The upper bound m_eff<=Q^(6/5) gives
m_eff^(1/200)<=Q^(3/500)<Q^(1/100)<=d.                           (3)
The lower bound m_eff>=Q^(1/2+kappa) gives
m_eff^(99/200)>=Q^((1/2+kappa)99/200)>Q^(99/400).
Since 2101/10000<99/400, equations (2)-(3) imply
m_eff^(1/200)<=d<m_eff^(99/200)=m_eff^(1/2-1/200).               (4)
Thus every squarefree divisor s of v of size at least Q^(1/100) supplies a divisor d of m_eff in the asserted window whenever s divides m_eff.

Because n is squarefree, m_eff is the product of exactly those prime divisors of n which do not divide C. If p divides C, then m_eff divides v. It exceeds Q^(1/2+kappa), so apply the deterministic statement with s=m_eff to prove (i). If p does not divide C, then p divides m_eff and squarefreeness gives r_eff=m_eff/p dividing v. Under r_eff>=Q^(1/100), apply the same statement with s=r_eff to prove (ii).

For the balanced-cell conclusion, take the resulting divisor as m_1 and put m_0=m_eff/m_1. Since m_eff is comparable to Q, equations (4) imply
m_1<=Q^(1/2-1/200+o(1)),
Q^(1/2+1/200+o(1))<=m_0<=Q^(1-1/200+o(1)).                     (5)
Since B_* is comparable to Q^(1/2), every fixed delta,rho with 4(delta+rho)<1/200 makes (5), for sufficiently large Q, satisfy all three A-PAID inequalities (4) of fact 8eb30e55bdef6b27. The only case not covered by (i) or (ii) is the displayed r_eff<Q^(1/100) chamber with p not dividing C. Finally 1/100<7/384 because 384<700. This proves every assertion without estimating that chamber.

glossary.refined ultra-near-prime threshold: The residual condition r_eff<Q^(1/100), strictly below the prime-bilinear saving exponent 7/384.

c7970d9d1337bd09.title: COMPLETE LITERAL GOOD-\(\mathscr W\) GA COORDINATE TAX LEDGER, BOTH ORIENTATIONS, AND THE EXACT OFF-SLOPE RECOMBINATION FRONTIER
c7970d9d1337bd09.author: slava chan
c7970d9d1337bd09.statement:
COMPLETE LITERAL GOOD-\(\mathscr W\) GA COORDINATE TAX LEDGER, BOTH ORIENTATIONS, AND THE EXACT OFF-SLOPE RECOMBINATION FRONTIER.

Use the setting and notation of fact e55b27d39c593164. Fix one orientation, one exact outer gcd \(g\), one frozen normalized layer, one parent, one source/projective fibre, one signed frequency block
\[
 1\le F\le x^3,\qquad F\le |h|<2F,
\]
one anatomy \(\mathfrak a\in\{A,C_\ell\}\), and one tail-dilator block
\[
 \mathcal D\le d_\lambda<2\mathcal D.
\]
Let \(\mathcal U_{\mathfrak a,\mathcal D}\) be the finite set of physical marked copies \(u=(n,\lambda)\) in this fixed family and put
\[
 \|\mathbf z^{\rm phys}\|_2^2
 =\sum_{u\in\mathcal U_{\mathfrak a,\mathcal D}}
 |z^{\rm phys}_u|^2.
\]
For a frequency \(h\) on the fixed signed block, let \(d^{\rm u}_{u,h}\) be the product of the primes dividing \(d_\lambda\) but not \(\mathscr A h\), where \(\mathscr A=N/g\). For every nonempty \(r\mid d^{\rm u}_{u,h}\), let
\[
 X_{u,h,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)
 =W_{u,h,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)V_{u,h,r}(\boldsymbol\rho),
 \qquad \boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r,
\]
be the exact literal centered-face coordinate of fact 0aa821ade9a14b45 in the forward orientation. In the reverse orientation use the exact divisor-complement swap and \(h\mapsto-h\) of fact e55b27d39c593164; equivalently the same formulas hold with the signed target \(-\mathscr A\). Define
\[
 A_r(\boldsymbol\rho;\mathbf z^{\rm phys})
 =\sum_{\substack{u\in\mathcal U_{\mathfrak a,\mathcal D}\\
                   F\le |h|<2F\\
                   r\mid d^{\rm u}_{u,h}}}
 z^{\rm phys}_uX_{u,h,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)
\]
and the complete nonempty-face coordinate energy
\[
 \mathfrak E_{\mathfrak a,\mathcal D}(\mathbf z^{\rm phys})
 =\sum_{\substack{r\ne1\\
                   r\mid d^{\rm u}_{u,h}\ {\rm for\ at\ least\ one}\ (u,h)}}
   \ \sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r}
 |A_r(\boldsymbol\rho;\mathbf z^{\rm phys})|^2.
\]
Then, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), in both orientations,
\[
 \mathfrak E_{A,\mathcal D}(\mathbf z^{\rm phys})
 \ll_\varepsilon
 x^\varepsilon|\omega_F|^2Q^2F^2{B\over\mathcal D}
 \|\mathbf z^{\rm phys}\|_2^2,                                  \tag{1}
\]
and for every surviving \(C_\ell\),
\[
 \mathfrak E_{C_\ell,\mathcal D}(\mathbf z^{\rm phys})
 \ll_\varepsilon
 x^\varepsilon|\omega_F|^2Q^2F^2{B\over\mathcal D}
 \|\mathbf z^{\rm phys}\|_2^2.                                  \tag{2}
\]
The factor \(B/\mathcal D\) in (1) is exactly the possible \(A\)-complement multiplicity from fact 35e599ec4bc284fe. For \(C_\ell\), every nonempty block has
\[
 B/8<\mathcal D\le2B,                                            \tag{3}
\]
so the factor \(B/\mathcal D\) in (2) is bounded above and below by absolute positive constants.

Let \(K_{u,h,1}\) denote the empty active face in equation (6) of fact 0aa821ade9a14b45, with the reverse version defined by the same swap. The empty face satisfies, in both orientations,
\[
 \left|
 \sum_{u\in\mathcal U_{\mathfrak a,\mathcal D}}z^{\rm phys}_u
 \sum_{F\le|h|<2F}K_{u,h,1}
 \right|^2
 \ll_\varepsilon
 x^\varepsilon|\omega_F|^2Q^2F^2{B\over\mathcal D}
 \|\mathbf z^{\rm phys}\|_2^2.                                  \tag{4}
\]
Thus empty faces and the complete coordinatewise diagonal of all nonempty faces have exactly the GA-NR-DIL scale, with one common physical vector \(\mathbf z^{\rm phys}\); no face-dependent copy of that vector is introduced.

For the \(A\)-anatomy, let
\[
 d_{\min}=H_P^2Q^{\tau/3}.
\]
If the actual \(A\)-dilators are partitioned into dyadic blocks \([\mathcal D,2\mathcal D)\), then
\[
 \sum_{\mathcal D:\,[\mathcal D,2\mathcal D)\cap[d_{\min},2B]\ne\varnothing}
 {B\over\mathcal D}
 \le {4B\over d_{\min}}
 =4\mathscr WQ^{-\tau/3}.                                       \tag{5}
\]
Hence the \(A\)-block summation has a geometric endpoint cost and no logarithmic block tax. By (3), only \(O(1)\) dyadic dilator blocks occur for all \(C_\ell\)-copies; the number of possible \(\ell\) is \(x^{o(1)}\).

The remaining scalar synthesis is exact as follows. Put
\[
 \mathscr S_{\mathfrak a,\mathcal D}^{+}(\mathbf z^{\rm phys})
 =\sum_{r\ne1}\sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r}
 A_r(\boldsymbol\rho;\mathbf z^{\rm phys}).
\]
For fixed \(r\), generic Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \left|\sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r}
 A_r(\boldsymbol\rho;\mathbf z^{\rm phys})\right|^2
 \le|\Omega_r|\sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r}
 |A_r(\boldsymbol\rho;\mathbf z^{\rm phys})|^2,                  \tag{6}
\]
and the factor \(|\Omega_r|\) is sharp for arbitrary coordinate arrays by fact 9128d43a5ac4e1bb. Distinct \(r\) are orthogonal only after complete least-common-multiple averaging by fact 3fde81ce051bff7b. Therefore (1)--(4) do not by themselves estimate the signed scalar sum over same-\(r\) off-dual coordinates and distinct-\(r\) incomplete discrepancies. The shifted local table of fact de77752fa0dd5cf7 applies inside this discrepancy, but shiftwise absolute summation is not performed here.

Finally let
\(\mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}(\mathcal D)\),
\(\mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{(0)}(\mathcal D)\),
\(\mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{({\rm FR})}(\mathcal D)\), and
\(\mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{({\rm NR})}(\mathcal D)\)
be the restrictions of the four exact moments in fact e55b27d39c593164 to the chosen anatomy. Their exact trichotomy gives
\[
 \mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{({\rm NR})}(\mathcal D)
 =
 \left(\mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}(\mathcal D)
       -\mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{(0)}(\mathcal D)\right)
 -\mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{({\rm FR})}(\mathcal D).           \tag{7}
\]
Consequently the single signed estimate
\[
 \left|
 \mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}(\mathcal D)
 -\mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{(0)}(\mathcal D)
 \right|
 \ll_\varepsilon
 x^\varepsilon|\omega_F|^2{BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}              \tag{GA-OFF-SYN}
\]
together with the already verified fully resonant bound implies GA-NR-DIL for this anatomy and block. GA-OFF-SYN is the exact minimal remaining operator interface: it keeps the signed sum of every same-\(r\) off-dual term and every distinct-\(r\) incomplete discrepancy and removes the proportional-ray diagonal before taking an absolute value.

If instead one proves only the full scalar-moment estimate
\[
 \mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}(\mathcal D)
 \ll_\varepsilon
 x^\varepsilon|\omega_F|^2{BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D},              \tag{8}
\]
then (7), the verified diagonal bound, and the verified fully resonant bound yield only
\[
 |\mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{({\rm NR})}(\mathcal D)|
 \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon|\omega_F|^2{BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}
 \left(1+{\mathcal D\over QF}\right).                            \tag{9}
\]
Thus (8) closes GA-NR-DIL by full-minus-paid-sector subtraction on
\(\mathcal D\le QF\). On \(\mathcal D>QF\), the first exact excess factor in that argument is
\[
 {\mathcal D\over QF}.                                           \tag{10}
\]
A two-ray algebraic example shows that this is not a removable logical artifact: if one row has two non-fully-resonant coordinate packets on distinct rational rays with amplitudes \(L\) and \(-L\), then the full square is \(0\), the proportional-ray diagonal is \(2|L|^2\), and the nonresonant cross term is \(-2|L|^2\). This example does not assert that the literal GA coefficient realizes such alignment; it proves that a full norm bound alone cannot replace GA-OFF-SYN in the range \(\mathcal D>QF\).

No estimate for GA-OFF-SYN, no GA-NR-DIL conclusion, no payment of the good-\(\mathscr W\) tail, no assertion for \(\mathscr W<Q^\tau\), and no Goldbach conclusion is made.
c7970d9d1337bd09.proof:
For the forward orientation, fix a nonempty squarefree active product \(r\). Apply fact e2e971fd4983bd94 to a \(C_\ell\)-family with coefficient
\[
 c_{(u,h)}=z^{\rm phys}_u.
\]
Its left side is the \(r\)-summand of
\(\mathfrak E_{C_\ell,\mathcal D}(\mathbf z^{\rm phys})\), and its right side is
\[
 \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon|\omega_F|^2Q^2F
 \sum_{\substack{u,h\\r\mid d^{\rm u}_{u,h}}}|z^{\rm phys}_u|^2. \tag{11}
\]
For the \(A\)-anatomy, fact 35e599ec4bc284fe gives the identical assertion with the additional factor \(B/\mathcal D\).

Now sum (11) over all nonempty \(r\). A fixed row \((u,h)\) occurs once for every nonempty divisor of the squarefree integer \(d^{\rm u}_{u,h}\), hence at most
\[
 \tau(d^{\rm u}_{u,h})-1\ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon
\]
times; the polynomial envelope and the divisor bound used in the predecessors justify the last estimate. There are \(O(F)\) integers \(h\) in the signed block. Therefore
\[
 \sum_{r\ne1}\sum_{\substack{u,h\\r\mid d^{\rm u}_{u,h}}}
 |z^{\rm phys}_u|^2
 \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon F
 \|\mathbf z^{\rm phys}\|_2^2.                                  \tag{12}
\]
Equations (11)--(12) prove (1) for \(A\) and prove (2) without the displayed factor \(B/\mathcal D\) for \(C_\ell\).

On a \(C_\ell\)-copy, fact e55b27d39c593164 gives \(n=d_\lambda v\), \(B/2\le n\le2B\), and \(v\in\{1,2\}\). If
\(\mathcal D\le d_\lambda<2\mathcal D\), then
\[
 d_\lambda=n/v\ge B/4,\qquad d_\lambda\le2B.
\]
The first inequality and \(d_\lambda<2\mathcal D\) give
\(\mathcal D>B/8\); the second and \(\mathcal D\le d_\lambda\) give
\(\mathcal D\le2B\). This proves (3). In particular \(B/\mathcal D\ge1/2\), so the \(C_\ell\) estimate without that factor implies (2), after changing the absolute implied constant.

We prove (4). The empty face in equation (4) of fact 0aa821ade9a14b45 has
\[
 K_{u,h,1}
 ={\mu(d^{\rm u}_{u,h})\over d^{\rm u}_{u,h}}
 \sum_{\substack{Q\le q<2Q\\(q,n)=1}}
 b_{u,h}(q)e_{v_\lambda}\!\left(\mathscr Ah(qd_\lambda)^{-1}\right).
                                                                    \tag{13}
\]
The pointwise literal coefficient estimate used in facts e2e971fd4983bd94 and 35e599ec4bc284fe gives
\[
 |K_{u,h,1}|
 \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon Q|\omega_F|
 {1\over d^{\rm u}_{u,h}}.                                      \tag{14}
\]
For squarefree \(d=d_\lambda\),
\[
 d^{\rm u}_{u,h}={d\over(d,\mathscr Ah)}.                         \tag{15}
\]
Let \(L=|\mathscr Ah|>0\). Uniformly for every \(D_0\ge1\),
\[
 \sum_{D_0\le d<2D_0}
 \left({(d,L)\over d}\right)^2
 \ll \tau(L).                                                     \tag{16}
\]
Indeed, using the Jordan totient \(J_2\),
\[
 (d,L)^2=\sum_{s\mid(d,L)}J_2(s),\qquad 0\le J_2(s)\le s^2.
\]
Since \(d\ge D_0\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_{D_0\le d<2D_0}{(d,L)^2\over d^2}
 &\le {1\over D_0^2}
 \sum_{\substack{s\mid L\\s<2D_0}}s^2
 \left({D_0\over s}+1\right)\\
 &\le \sum_{\substack{s\mid L\\s<2D_0}}
 \left({s\over D_0}+{s^2\over D_0^2}\right)
 \le6\tau(L).
 \end{aligned}                                                    \tag{17}
\]
All restrictions omitted in (17) are zero-one restrictions, so the same upper bound holds for the actual rows.

For a \(C_\ell\)-family there are at most two possible values of \(v\). Equations (15)--(17) and the polynomial divisor bound give
\[
 \sum_{\substack{u\in\mathcal U_{C_\ell,\mathcal D}\\
                  F\le|h|<2F}}
 {1\over(d^{\rm u}_{u,h})^2}
 \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon F.                               \tag{18}
\]
For an \(A\)-copy, \(n=d_\lambda p\), and the support calculation in fact 35e599ec4bc284fe gives \(O(B/\mathcal D)\) possible values of the marker prime \(p\). Thus
\[
 \sum_{\substack{u\in\mathcal U_{A,\mathcal D}\\
                  F\le|h|<2F}}
 {1\over(d^{\rm u}_{u,h})^2}
 \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon F{B\over\mathcal D}.              \tag{19}
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz first in \(h\), then in \(u\), gives
\[
 \left|\sum_u z^{\rm phys}_u\sum_hK_{u,h,1}\right|^2
 \le\|\mathbf z^{\rm phys}\|_2^2
 \sum_u\left|\sum_hK_{u,h,1}\right|^2
 \le F\|\mathbf z^{\rm phys}\|_2^2\sum_{u,h}|K_{u,h,1}|^2.
\]
Insert (14), (18), and (19), and use (3) for \(C_\ell\). This proves (4).

The reverse orientation in fact e55b27d39c593164 is the exact interchange of the divisor-complement scale pairs followed by \(h\mapsto-h\). After that reindexing the active-prime formula is the forward formula with \(A=-\mathscr A\) in the abstract tensor bounds. The proofs of e2e971fd4983bd94 and 35e599ec4bc284fe use only that \(A\ne0\), the same squarefreeness and coprimality conditions, and the absolute pointwise bound for the literal coefficient. Equations (13)--(19) likewise use only \(|\mathscr Ah|\). Hence (1)--(4) hold with exactly the reverse copies and masks, without adding an orientation multiplicity. If the two orientations are later aggregated, their finite multiplicity is two.

Fact e55b27d39c593164 gives \(d_\lambda\ge d_{\min}\). A dyadic block meeting \([d_{\min},2B]\) has lower endpoint at least \(d_{\min}/2\). Therefore its possible lower endpoints are bounded below by
\(d_{\min}/2, d_{\min},2d_{\min},\ldots\), and
\[
 \sum_{\mathcal D}{B\over\mathcal D}
 \le {2B\over d_{\min}}\sum_{\nu\ge0}2^{-\nu}
 ={4B\over d_{\min}}.
\]
Equation (1) of fact e55b27d39c593164 gives
\(B/H_P^2=\mathscr W\), proving (5). Equation (3) confines \(C_\ell\) lower endpoints to an interval of ratio \(16\), hence to \(O(1)\) dyadic blocks. Also \(J_\theta\le\log(2B)/\log2+1=x^{o(1)}\), proving the remaining ledger assertions.

By equation (9) of fact 0aa821ade9a14b45,
\[
 K_{u,h,r}=\sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r}
 X_{u,h,r}(\boldsymbol\rho).
\]
Thus summing first over \(u,h\) with the common coefficient \(z^{\rm phys}_u\) gives exactly \(\mathscr S_{\mathfrak a,\mathcal D}^{+}\). Cauchy--Schwarz in \(\Omega_r\) proves (6), and fact 9128d43a5ac4e1bb proves its sharpness for arbitrary arrays. Fact 3fde81ce051bff7b proves exact distinct-product orthogonality only for complete least-common-multiple averages. Fact de77752fa0dd5cf7 supplies only local bounds for a fixed dual shift and explicitly performs no shifted-mode or distinct-product summation. These facts prove the stated exact frontier and show why no pairwise absolute-value continuation is included.

Restricting the exact trichotomy (16) of fact e55b27d39c593164 to one anatomy gives
\[
 \mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}
 =\mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{(0)}
  +\mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{({\rm FR})}
  +\mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{({\rm NR})}.
\]
Rearrangement proves (7). The proof of the fully resonant estimate (18) in that fact is by absolute restriction and therefore remains valid on one anatomy:
\[
 |\mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{({\rm FR})}(\mathcal D)|
 \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon|\omega_F|^2{BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}.
                                                                    \tag{20}
\]
Combining GA-OFF-SYN, (7), and (20) gives GA-NR-DIL.

If only (8) is assumed, the diagonal estimate (17) of fact e55b27d39c593164, restricted to one anatomy, is
\[
 |\mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{(0)}(\mathcal D)|
 \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon|\omega_F|^2BQF.                   \tag{21}
\]
The triangle inequality in (7), followed by (8), (20), and (21), gives
\[
 |\mathcal M_{\mathfrak a,F}^{({\rm NR})}(\mathcal D)|
 \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon|\omega_F|^2
 \left({BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}+BQF\right).
\]
Factoring the first term proves (9), and the quotient of the second term by the first is exactly \(\mathcal D/(QF)\), proving (10).

For the final algebraic test, take one row and two supported coordinate packets on distinct rational rays, so their ordered cross pairs have \(\Delta\ne0\), and choose a dilator for which those cross pairs are not fully resonant. Give the two packets amplitudes \(L\) and \(-L\). The full row amplitude is \(L-L=0\), so its full square is zero. The \(\Delta=0\) sector contains the two self-pairs and equals \(2|L|^2\). The two ordered cross pairs are nonresonant and sum to
\(L\overline{-L}+(-L)\overline L=-2|L|^2\). The fully resonant sector is empty. This proves the asserted logical obstruction while making no claim about realization by the literal GA source. All scope limitations follow.

glossary.GA-OFF-SYN: The signed off-proportional-ray centered-face recombination estimate displayed in the statement.
glossary.complete GA coordinate tax ledger: The sum over all nonempty active products and their dual coordinates while retaining one common physical row vector.
glossary.physical row vector: The coefficient vector z^{phys} indexed by actual marked copies u=(n,lambda), used unchanged across every active face.

c882223fd3a1511a.title: Let N=2x be fixed. Let Z be a finite set of source incidences
c882223fd3a1511a.author: slava chan
c882223fd3a1511a.statement:
Let N=2x be fixed. Let Z be a finite set of source incidences
z=(D_z,M_z,R_z,K_z;d_z,m_z,p_z,ell_z,k_z)
such that d_z,m_z,k_z are positive integers, p_z and ell_z are distinct odd primes,
d_z is squarefree,
d_z m_z+p_z ell_z k_z=N,
d_z<=2D_z, p_z ell_z>=R_z/2, and R_z>=D_z^(4/3).
Give z the complete real source weight
w_z=mu(d_z) log(m_z) log(k_z) W(d_zm_z/x) psi(d_z/D_*) Phi(d_z/D_z) Phi(m_z/M_z) Phi(p_zell_z/R_z) Phi(k_z/K_z),
and assume w_z is nonzero. Put S(z)={p_z,ell_z}, g_z=gcd(d_z,p_zell_z), b_z=p_zell_z/g_z, and T_Z=sum_{z in Z} w_z.

(A) The exact ordered square decomposes as
T_Z^2=Q_0+Q_1+Q_2,
where Q_j is the sum of w_z w_{z'} over ordered pairs (z,z') with |S(z) intersect S(z')|=j. The diagonal sum sum_z w_z^2 lies in Q_2; Q_2 also contains every off-diagonal equal-support collision, Q_1 contains the one-prime collisions, and only Q_0 contains four distinct displayed primes. Passing from ordered to unordered pairs gives multiplicity two off the diagonal and multiplicity one on the diagonal.

(B) For a disjoint pair S(z) intersect S(z')=emptyset,
Omega(b_z b_{z'})=4-Omega(g_z)-Omega(g_{z'}).
Consequently the quotient b_z b_{z'} has all four primitive displayed primes if and only if g_z=g_{z'}=1. In the exact divisor-indexed primitive additive-conductor decomposition of fact 3bb378b0a49679f9, retaining both primes p_z,ell_z on a gcd-one side requires choosing the divisor e_z=p_zell_z=b_z; analogously the other side requires e_{z'}=p_{z'}ell_{z'}=b_{z'}. Thus a literal four-prime primitive additive-character packet requires both gcds to be one and both selected primitive conductors to be the full semiprimes. If D_z>64, then p_z ell_z>d_z and hence b_z>1, but this size separation does not imply g_z=1: the cases g_z=p_z and g_z=ell_z still leave a one-prime quotient.

(C) Let w be the column vector (w_z)_{z in Z}. The all-pairs coefficient matrix A_all=w w^T has exact projective/nuclear norm
||A_all||_{S_1}=sum_z |w_z|^2.
The disjoint-support matrix
A_0(z,z')=1_{S(z) intersect S(z')=emptyset} w_z w_{z'}
has exact projective cost ||A_0||_{S_1}; coordinate projection to the disjoint-pair fibre contracts Frobenius mass. The masking is not generally a nuclear-norm contraction: for three unit-weight incidences with pairwise disjoint supports, A_all=J_3 has nuclear norm 3 whereas A_0=J_3-I_3 has nuclear norm 4.

For each disjoint ordered pair, suppose one records any subset of the four orientation choices theta in Theta obtained by choosing one prime from S(z) and one prime from S(z'). Let chi_theta(z,z') be the corresponding zero-one incidence mask, let
A_theta=chi_theta hadamard A_0,
and let m(z,z')=sum_{theta in Theta} chi_theta(z,z'). Then
sum_{theta in Theta} ||A_theta||_F^2
 =sum_{S(z) intersect S(z')=emptyset} m(z,z') |w_z|^2 |w_{z'}|^2
 <=4||A_0||_F^2.
If the four oriented matrices are stored in mutually orthogonal row and column blocks, the resulting block-diagonal operator has exact projective cost
sum_{theta in Theta} ||A_theta||_{S_1}.
Thus the multiplicity bound supplies the displayed exact l2 accounting, but by itself supplies no nuclear-norm contraction estimate used here; the relevant projective cost must be retained explicitly as the above sum.

(D) Fix a disjoint ordered pair and orient its four distinct odd primes as r_1,r_2 in S(z) and r_3,r_4 in S(z'). Put G=r_1r_2 and T=r_3r_4. Let I_1,I_2,I_3,I_4 be prescribed finite subsets of the integers satisfying
|c_1r_2+c_2r_1|<G/2 and |c_1r_2-c_2r_1|<G/2
for all c_1 in I_1,c_2 in I_2, and
|c_3r_4-c_4r_3|<T/2
for all c_3 in I_3,c_4 in I_4.
Define the finite attainable carrier set
C_att={ (c_1r_2+c_2r_1)T+G(c_3r_4+c_4r_3): c_i in I_i }.
For any integer carrier C, the literal interval-supported four-prime packet with this orientation and carrier exists exactly when C lies in C_att, by the CRT interval criterion of fact 397f417416c4cb9d. The source equations and the conductor quotients define neither C nor the four c_i. Hence a common carrier/window representation is an additional interface requirement, not a consequence of merely pairing two source incidences. In particular, since C_att is finite, a nonzero integer C_* outside it gives no packet; in the symbolic singleton case I_1=I_2=I_3=I_4={0}, one has C_att={0}.

Therefore an exact paired-source-to-literal-four-prime construction must separately (i) keep and pay Q_1 and Q_2, (ii) restrict to g_z=g_{z'}=1 and to full primitive conductors, (iii) retain the original ordered-pair multiplicities and complete weights, (iv) construct a common carrier and actual frequency windows satisfying the strict shortness and CRT conditions, and (v) retain the exact projective/orientation costs before invoking any common normalized pair-column coherence estimate. These conclusions do not assert a literal packet equality, a projective-norm saving, or absorption of collision terms.
c882223fd3a1511a.proof:
Part (A). Expanding the finite square gives
T_Z^2=sum_{(z,z') in Z^2} w_z w_{z'}.
Because every S(z) has exactly two distinct elements, the intersection size is exactly 0, 1, or 2. These three conditions partition Z^2 and give the displayed identity. If z=z', the intersection size is 2. If two different source incidences use the same unordered prime pair, they too have intersection size 2. An intersection of size 1 has exactly three distinct displayed primes, whereas size 0 has exactly four. The involution (z,z')->(z',z) has two-element orbits off the diagonal and singleton orbits on the diagonal, proving the ordered/unordered multiplicities.

Part (B). Since d_z is squarefree and p_z ell_z is a product of two distinct primes, g_z is one of 1,p_z,ell_z,p_zell_z. Thus b_z is squarefree and Omega(b_z)=2-Omega(g_z). Disjointness of the displayed prime supports makes b_z and b_{z'} coprime, so Omega is additive and proves the formula. It equals four exactly when both gcds are one.

Fact 3bb378b0a49679f9 proves the exact identity
1_{b_z divides X}=b_z^{-1} sum_{e divides b_z} c_e(X)
and proves that the summand indexed by e has exact primitive additive conductor e. On the gcd-one layer, b_z=p_zell_z. A conductor e retains both distinct prime factors precisely when e=p_zell_z; the alternatives 1,p_z,ell_z omit at least one. Thus one must choose e_z=b_z=p_zell_z, and the identical argument applies to z'. This proves the full-conductor assertion.

For the size claim, if D_z>64 then D_z^(1/3)>4, and hence
p_z ell_z >= R_z/2 >= D_z^(4/3)/2 > 2D_z >= d_z.
Therefore p_zell_z cannot divide d_z, so b_z>1. This excludes g_z=p_zell_z but not g_z=p_z or ell_z, proving the stated limitation.

Part (C). The rank-one singular value formula gives
||ww^T||_{S_1}=||w||_2^2=sum_z |w_z|^2.
The formula for A_0 is simply the exact entrywise deletion of non-disjoint pairs. Coordinate deletion contracts the Euclidean norm of the vectorized matrix, so ||A_0||_F<=||A_all||_F. To see that it need not contract nuclear norm, take three indices with pairwise disjoint supports and w_z=1. Then A_all=J_3 has eigenvalues 3,0,0 and nuclear norm 3. The deleted diagonal gives A_0=J_3-I_3, with eigenvalues 2,-1,-1 and nuclear norm 4.

For the orientation formula, every entry of A_theta is either A_0(z,z') or zero. Squaring absolute values and summing first over theta counts the entry (z,z') exactly m(z,z') times. There are at most four orientations, so 0<=m(z,z')<=4, yielding the equality and inequality. If matrices occupy orthogonal row and column blocks, their singular-value multisets concatenate; nuclear norm is therefore additive over those blocks, giving exactly sum_theta ||A_theta||_{S_1}. These identities prove the claimed l2 accounting and identify, without simplifying it, the projective cost that a later argument must control.

Part (D). The hypotheses now match fact 397f417416c4cb9d exactly: its first semiprime is G=r_1r_2, its second is T=r_3r_4, and the three strict shortness inequalities are precisely those displayed here. That fact proves that a quadruple in the four prescribed windows produces exactly
C=(c_1r_2+c_2r_1)T+G(c_3r_4+c_4r_3),
and conversely recovers a unique such quadruple from the literal parity-and-window gates. Thus the set of feasible carriers is exactly C_att.

The source equation contains d_z,m_z,p_z,ell_z,k_z and N but no chosen carrier C and no frequency lifts c_i; neither do the definitions of g_z and b_z. Thus no implication to C in C_att is available from those data. The set is finite because the windows are finite, so an integer outside it exists; choosing a nonzero one gives the obstruction. If every window is {0}, all strict shortness inequalities hold and substitution gives C_att={0}.

Combining Parts (A)-(D) yields each listed interface obligation. Facts f077de751a5189b6 and 104522049dda64e6 additionally explain why pair-fibre positivity and a common-column coherence statement must be kept separate from the original prime-set partition and from genuine connected-moment signs, but no extra claim from them is needed for the exact ledger proved above.

glossary.A_0: the coefficient matrix restricted to disjoint displayed-prime supports
glossary.A_theta: the entrywise masked oriented matrix chi_theta hadamard A_0
glossary.C_*: a chosen nonzero integer outside C_att
glossary.C_att: the finite set of carriers attainable from the four windows
glossary.D_*: a fixed positive normalization scale in the complete source weight
glossary.D_z: the dyadic d-scale attached to z
glossary.I_i: the prescribed finite integer frequency window for r_i
glossary.K_z: the dyadic k-scale attached to z
glossary.M_z: the dyadic m-scale attached to z
glossary.Omega: the number of distinct prime divisors of a squarefree positive integer
glossary.Phi: the fixed real dyadic cutoff function
glossary.Q_j: the ordered square contribution with displayed-prime support intersection size j
glossary.R_z: the dyadic semiprime scale attached to z
glossary.S_1: the Schatten-one, nuclear, or projective matrix norm
glossary.T_Z: the total weighted source sum over Z
glossary.Theta: the set of the four cross-pair prime orientation choices
glossary.W: the fixed real source weight function
glossary.Z: the finite set of source incidences in this statement
glossary.c_i: an integer frequency lift in I_i
glossary.chi_theta: the zero-one mask selecting ordered pairs carrying orientation theta
glossary.d_z: the squarefree source divisor attached to z
glossary.e_z: the divisor indexing the exact primitive additive conductor on side z
glossary.ell_z: the second odd displayed prime attached to z
glossary.k_z: the second source integer attached to z
glossary.m(z,z'): the number of recorded orientations for ordered pair (z,z')
glossary.m_z: the first source integer attached to z
glossary.p_z: the first odd displayed prime attached to z
glossary.psi: the fixed real source cutoff function
glossary.r_i: the i-th oriented odd prime, for 1<=i<=4
glossary.w_z: the complete real weight of source incidence z

c952f4808e23ff96.title: ANATOMY-INDEPENDENT HARMONIC ROW-FAMILY TRANSFER FOR THE CENTERING CORRECTION AND BOTH LOW-CONDUCTOR DECOMPOSITIONS
c952f4808e23ff96.author: slava chan
c952f4808e23ff96.statement:
ANATOMY-INDEPENDENT HARMONIC ROW-FAMILY TRANSFER FOR THE CENTERING CORRECTION AND BOTH LOW-CONDUCTOR DECOMPOSITIONS.

Fix real constants A>=1 and epsilon>0. Let X>=3, let J be a finite index set, and for every j in J let
m_j<=X^A                                                             (1)
be a positive squarefree integer, let c_j,n_j be integers with
gcd(c_j n_j,m_j)=1,                                                   (2)
and let w_j be an arbitrary complex number. Put
Harm(J)=sum_{j in J}|w_j|/m_j.                                       (3)
The index set J may already encode arbitrary pair-dependent deletions, and w_j may be an inner product of Hilbert-valued row coefficients; no product structure, positivity, or independence is assumed.

Use S_t and P_{t;c,s} from fact a08224dfb222c580. For every prime p|m_j use the centered local factor kappa_{p;m_j,c_j} and the active tensor Kcal_{r;m_j,c_j} from fact 8b46abe31a5ae8d7. Let Y>=1 and define
CORR(J)
 =sum_{j in J}w_j mu(m_j)(1/m_j-1/phi(m_j)),                         (4)
ADD-LOW(J,Y)
 =sum_{j in J}w_j
  sum_{s t=m_j,1<t<=Y}mu(s)P_{t;c_j,s}(n_j)/s,                       (5)
CRT-LOW(J,Y)
 =sum_{j in J}w_j
  sum_{r|m_j,1<r<=Y}
  mu(m_j/r)Kcal_{r;m_j,c_j}(n_j)/phi(m_j/r).                         (6)
Then
|CORR(J)| <<_{A,epsilon} X^epsilon Harm(J),                           (7)
|ADD-LOW(J,Y)| <<_{A,epsilon} X^epsilon Y Harm(J),                   (8)
|CRT-LOW(J,Y)| <<_{A,epsilon} X^epsilon Y Harm(J).                   (9)

Define ADD-HIGH(J,Y) by replacing 1<t<=Y in (5) with t>Y, and define CRT-HIGH(J,Y) by replacing 1<r<=Y in (6) with r>Y. Then the two exact weighted decompositions of the multiplicatively centered inverse kernel are
sum_{j in J}w_j[
 e_{m_j}(-c_j n_j^{-1})-mu(m_j)/phi(m_j)]
 =CORR(J)+ADD-LOW(J,Y)+ADD-HIGH(J,Y),                                (10)
and
sum_{j in J}w_j[
 e_{m_j}(-c_j n_j^{-1})-mu(m_j)/phi(m_j)]
 =CRT-LOW(J,Y)+CRT-HIGH(J,Y).                                       (11)

Consequently, every application of (7)-(9) needs only a harmonic envelope
Harm(J)<=H_0.                                                        (12)
Under (12), the correction costs X^epsilon H_0 and either low-conductor family costs X^epsilon YH_0, uniformly under every deletion already encoded by J. Establishing (12) from a literal source coefficient and copy inventory is anatomy-specific. The finite Fourier/CRT algebra and the implication (12) to (7)-(11) are anatomy-independent. This theorem asserts no estimate for ADD-HIGH or CRT-HIGH. Their coefficient-one full-conductor faces show only that the cofactor proof of (8)-(9) does not extend unchanged to give a low-conductor-type X^epsilon YH_0 saving on the high range.

This theorem proves only the abstract transfer and exact decompositions. It does not establish a harmonic envelope for any new anatomy, transfer a Good-W coefficient to a top row, estimate a large-conductor Hilbert/vector residual, prove GA-qCENT, P-qSRC, C-qSRC>=2, a tail payment, or Goldbach.
c952f4808e23ff96.proof:
We first record uniform elementary divisor bounds. Since every m_j<=X^A,
m_j/phi(m_j)<<_{A,epsilon}X^epsilon,
2^{omega(m_j)}<<_{A,epsilon}X^epsilon,
tau(m_j)<<_{A,epsilon}X^epsilon.                                    (13)
These follow from the standard elementary estimates m/phi(m)=m^{o(1)}, 2^{omega(m)}=m^{o(1)}, and tau(m)=m^{o(1)}, uniformly for m<=X^A.

Because phi(m_j)<=m_j,
|1/m_j-1/phi(m_j)|
 <=1/phi(m_j)
 =(m_j/phi(m_j))/m_j
 <<_{A,epsilon}X^epsilon/m_j.                                       (14)
Multiply by |w_j| and sum over j to prove (7).

We prove (8). The general calculation in fact d3278c2897e20003, which uses only squarefreeness and (2), gives
|P_{t;c_j,s}(n_j)|<=2^{omega(t)}
<<_{A,epsilon}X^epsilon                                              (15)
for every st=m_j and t>1. Since s=m_j/t,
sum_{st=m_j,1<t<=Y}
 |mu(s)P_{t;c_j,s}(n_j)|/s
 <<_{A,epsilon}
 X^epsilon m_j^{-1}
 sum_{t|m_j,t<=Y}t
 <=X^epsilon Y tau(m_j)/m_j
 <<_{A,epsilon}X^{2epsilon}Y/m_j.                                   (16)
Replace epsilon by epsilon/2 in the two elementary losses. Multiplying (16) by |w_j| and summing proves (8).

For (9), fact 8b46abe31a5ae8d7 gives
|Kcal_{r;m_j,c_j}(n_j)|<=r/phi(r).                                  (17)
Because m_j is squarefree and r|m_j, the integers r and m_j/r are coprime. By (13),
r/phi(r)<<_{A,epsilon}X^epsilon,
1/phi(m_j/r)
 =(m_j/r)/phi(m_j/r) times r/m_j
 <<_{A,epsilon}X^epsilon r/m_j.                                     (18)
Therefore
sum_{r|m_j,1<r<=Y}
 |Kcal_{r;m_j,c_j}(n_j)|/phi(m_j/r)
 <<_{A,epsilon}
 X^{2epsilon}m_j^{-1}
 sum_{r|m_j,r<=Y}r
 <<_{A,epsilon}X^{3epsilon}Y/m_j.                                   (19)
Again begin with epsilon/3 in the elementary bounds. Multiply by |w_j| and sum to prove (9).

For each j, fact a08224dfb222c580 gives the exact identity
e_{m_j}(-c_j n_j^{-1})-mu(m_j)/phi(m_j)
 =mu(m_j)(1/m_j-1/phi(m_j))
  +sum_{st=m_j,t>1}mu(s)P_{t;c_j,s}(n_j)/s.                          (20)
Split its finite divisor sum at t=Y, multiply by w_j, and sum over J. This proves (10).

For each j, the algebraic identity in fact 8b46abe31a5ae8d7 gives
e_{m_j}(-c_j n_j^{-1})-mu(m_j)/phi(m_j)
 =sum_{r|m_j,r>1}
  mu(m_j/r)Kcal_{r;m_j,c_j}(n_j)/phi(m_j/r).                         (21)
Split at r=Y, multiply by w_j, and sum. This proves (11).

Equations (7)-(9) immediately imply the consequence under (12). All estimates used only the rowwise hypotheses (1)-(3), so arbitrary restrictions already built into J are retained. The proofs of (8) and (9) obtain the factor Y/m_j only from t<=Y and r<=Y. At a full-conductor face t=m_j or r=m_j, the cofactor coefficient equals one, so this particular proof has no corresponding Y/m_j factor on the high range. This observation neither excludes other estimates nor asserts a lower bound. No high-conductor estimate is claimed, and every scope exclusion follows.

glossary.ADD-LOW(J,Y): The weighted sum of exact additive-conductor faces with conductor t at most Y.
glossary.CRT-LOW(J,Y): The weighted sum of primewise centered active faces with active product r at most Y.
glossary.Harm(J): The harmonic row mass sum over j in J of |w_j|/m_j.

c98f3e5b2172abec.title: COMPLETE SAME-SELECTED-\(N\) CONSTANT-SAFE FIVE-ANATOMY PAYMENT THROUGH \(\beta_m\), AND NEGATIVE HANDOFF ABOVE \(\beta_m\)
c98f3e5b2172abec.author: slava chan
c98f3e5b2172abec.statement:
COMPLETE SAME-SELECTED-\(N\) CONSTANT-SAFE FIVE-ANATOMY PAYMENT THROUGH \(\beta_m\), AND NEGATIVE HANDOFF ABOVE \(\beta_m\).

Fix \(0<\kappa\le1/100\), put
\[
 \sigma=\kappa/100,\qquad
 \beta_1=6/5-3\sigma,\qquad
 \beta_m=6/5-12\sigma/5,
\]
and fix \(0<\eta<\sigma\) and \(\omega>0\). Use the fixed selected bad
even integer \(N=2x\), the active dyadic labels, and the smooth source of
fact \(60b26a9b6f79467a\). Thus every active strict-orientation label has
\[
 DM\asymp x,\qquad RK\asymp x,                                  \tag{1}
\]
the smaller divisor scale is at most \(2x^{1/2}\) and at least
\(x^{1/2}(\log x)^{-O(1)}\), and the larger divisor scale exceeds
\(x^{9/16-1/200}\).

Let \(T_{\rm postC3,sel}\) be the real same-selected-\(N\) aggregate of
fact \(01b550792363535d\). It satisfies
\[
 T_{\rm postC3,sel}\le
 -c_{\rm dir}\mathfrak c(N){x\over\log x}
 +o\!\left(\mathfrak c(N){x\over\log x}\right),                 \tag{2}
\]
where \(c_{\rm dir}>0\) and \(\mathfrak c(N)\ge C_2>0\).
For an exact outer gcd \(g=(d,r)\), use in the forward orientation
\[
 Q=D/g,\quad B=R/g=Q^\beta,\quad G=M/Q,\quad
 H_T=B/Q,\quad H_P=B/M,\quad L_{\rm src}=N/g,
\]
and in the reverse orientation
\[
 Q=R/g,\quad B=D/g=Q^\beta,\quad G=K/Q,\quad
 H_T=B/Q,\quad H_P=B/K,\quad L_{\rm src}=N/g.
\]

Let \(\mathcal R_{m,\rm sel}\) be the complete projection of
\(T_{\rm postC3,sel}\) onto
\[
 \beta_1<\beta\le\beta_m,                                      \tag{3}
\]
after the exact constant-safe source-preserving re-marker of fact
\(047f4bc01579ce66\) is applied to that whole projection. Thus every
pre-marker atom is first restored to its literal Möbius coefficient and
then expanded, with
\[
 L=H_TQ^\sigma,\qquad S_0=H_T^2Q^{3\sigma},\qquad
 Z_*=2Q^{3/2-\beta-3\sigma},                                   \tag{4}
\]
into the exact disjoint anatomy list
\[
 A_*,\quad B_*,\quad C1_*,\quad C2_*,\quad C3_* .              \tag{5}
\]
In \(\mathcal R_{m,\rm sel}\), recombine to completion every selected
source, active-scale, fixed-\(U\), high, smooth/projective, paired
frequency, target-gcd, prime-order, equal-cell, outer-\(g\)/rough-prime
collision, deletion, parent, orientation, provenance, actual-\(G\), and
exact outer-\(g\) coordinate. The inherited actual imbalance satisfies
\[
 Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\le G<
 Q^{\Gamma_{BC}(\beta)+\omega},\qquad
 \Gamma_{BC}(\beta)=\max\{0,(19\beta-20)/17\}.                 \tag{6}
\]

There is a fixed \(\delta_m>0\) such that
\[
 |\mathcal R_{m,\rm sel}|\ll x^{1-\delta_m}.                    \tag{7}
\]
Define
\[
 T_{>\beta_m,\rm sel}
 =T_{\rm postC3,sel}-\mathcal R_{m,\rm sel}.                    \tag{8}
\]
Then
\[
 T_{>\beta_m,\rm sel}\le
 -c_{\rm dir}\mathfrak c(N){x\over\log x}
 +o\!\left(\mathfrak c(N){x\over\log x}\right),                 \tag{9}
\]
and every atom of \(T_{>\beta_m,\rm sel}\) has
\[
 \beta>\beta_m.                                                  \tag{10}
\]

No sign is assigned to an individual anatomy or cell. No assertion is made
on the open top sliver \(\beta_m<\beta<6/5\), on
\(\beta\ge6/5\), on endpoint parents, PMD, DCE, a Goldbach implication,
or Goldbach.
c98f3e5b2172abec.proof:
Fact \(01b550792363535d\) gives (2), the lower
bound \(\mathfrak c(N)\ge C_2\), and the exact support
\(\beta>\beta_1\), with every literal coordinate in the statement
retained. Fact \(047f4bc01579ce66\) is an exact pointwise identity on
the whole projection (3): it first recombines every old marker leaf and
marker-dependent descendant to the literal normalized Möbius factor and
then applies the constant-safe marker (4). It proves that (5) is disjoint
and exhaustive even at \(\beta=\beta_m\), preserves both orientations,
the selected \(N\), the sole inherited \(U_{\rm low}\) parent, the
actual \(G\), exact \(g\), paired frequency, target, source amplitude and
all provenance coordinates, and changes no pre-marker atom. Consequently
\(\mathcal R_{m,\rm sel}\) is exactly the complete projection (3), not a
selection of old anatomy labels.

We estimate the five complete new anatomies. All auxiliary descendants of
one new leaf are recombined before the analytic estimate, except when an
exact finite completion and its explicitly bounded correction are described
below. No arbitrary joint deletion is inserted.

For \(A_*\), the normalized marked factor is \(up\), with
\(up\asymp B\) and \(L<p<Z_*\). Fix a forward exact-\(g\) layer.
The normalized source equation is
\[
 am+bk=L_{\rm src}.                                               \tag{11}
\]
Put
\[
 c=(a,L_{\rm src}),\qquad a=cq,\qquad L_{\rm src}=cL_1.
\]
Fact \(1c64020b89f097c4\) proves that \(c\mid k\), that \(c\)
is squarefree, and that
\[
 (c,q)=(c,b)=(q,b)=(q,L_1)=1.
\]
The reciprocity character therefore descends exactly to
\[
 e_a(-L_{\rm src}h(up)^{-1})
 =e_q(-L_1h(up)^{-1}).                                         \tag{12}
\]
For
\[
 c\le C_{\rm cut}:=H_TQ^{\sigma/4},                            \tag{13}
\]
the dyadic \(u,p\) coefficient, the prime interval
\(L<p<Z_*\), the complete coprimalities, the fixed target
\(-L_{\rm src}/c\), and the literal scaled-smooth frequency amplitude
match fact \(ca3e3b73946c9248\). That fact sums all such \(c\) and
gives
\[
 \sum_{c\le C_{\rm cut}}|T_c|
 \ll GQ^{2-\delta_{A,F}}\quad(G\ge1),                           \tag{14}
\]
and
\[
 \sum_{c\le C_{\rm cut}}|T_c|
 \ll Q^{2-\delta_{A,N}}
 \quad(Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\le G\le Q^{\sigma-\eta}).              \tag{15}
\]
For \(c>C_{\rm cut}\), fact \(5fbdbbebf99aec55\), which permits
every retained bounded phase, gcd selector and deletion coordinate, gives
\[
 \sum_{c>C_{\rm cut}}|T_c|
 \ll Q^{2-\sigma/4+\epsilon}.                                  \tag{16}
\]
Indeed \(B=QH_T\), and (16) is the conclusion
\(QB/C_{\rm cut}\ll Q^{2-\sigma/4}\). The reverse orientation is
obtained by interchanging the two divisor-complement pairs and reindexing
the complete real frequency pair by \(h\mapsto-h\). Then the descended
modulus is \(b/c\), and fact \(ca3e3b73946c9248\) is applied with the
opposite signed target so that its displayed phase equals the physical
reverse phase. Equations (14)-(16) are unchanged. This pays both the small
target-gcd layers and the complete large target-gcd complement.

For \(B_*\), fact \(047f4bc01579ce66\) supplies the exact
raised-stopping coefficient
\[
 {(-1)^k\mu(u)1_{j_{(L,Z_*)}(u)=0}\Gamma_{k;L,S_0}(y)
  \over {k+\omega_L(u)\choose k}},\qquad (u,y)=1.               \tag{17}
\]
Forward reciprocity converts the source phase to modulus \(a\asymp Q\)
and fixed target \(-L_{\rm src}\); reverse reciprocity, after the complete
frequency-sign reindexing, gives modulus \(b\asymp Q\) and target
\(+L_{\rm src}\). The conditions involving the fixed squarefree \(g\)
are one-variable factors on the modulus, \(u\), and \(y\). All
smooth source and fixed-\(U\) masks are uniformly projective, while high
and parent are frozen label scalars. Thus the complete full-rectangle
coefficient (17) matches fact \(5a9588474e09a334\), which gives the
