corresponding full-\(G\) and near-balanced fixed power savings for every
actual frequency.

For \(C1_*\), forward write
\[
 b=vp,\qquad v\le S_0,\qquad
 p\mid v\Longrightarrow p\le L,\qquad p_{\rm rough}\ge Z_*,
\]
where the last displayed \(p_{\rm rough}\) denotes the unique rough prime
and the exact coefficient is \(-\mu(v)\). To avoid ambiguity, write that
rough prime as \(p_1\), so \(b=vp_1\). Poisson summation in \(m\) in
(11) gives \(e_b(L_{\rm src}ha^{-1})\), and additive reciprocity gives
\[
 e_b(L_{\rm src}ha^{-1})
 =e_a(-L_{\rm src}hb^{-1})e(L_{\rm src}h/(ab)).                 \tag{18}
\]
On \(F\le|h|<2F\), facts \(df9748efe29ab475\) and
\(0d53c27d174b26ed\) give the literal \(H_P^{-1}\) prefactor,
arbitrary fixed-order decay in \(F/H_P\), and a uniformly bounded
projective amplitude. The archimedean factor in (18) is included because
\[
 {L_{\rm src}\over QM}={N\over DM}=O(1).                        \tag{19}
\]
Thus the completed \(C1_*\) trace matches fact \(7767c0ebde1c24a7\)
with target \(-L_{\rm src}\). Reverse interchange gives target
\(+L_{\rm src}\) and uses \(N/(RK)=O(1)\).

The source also imposes \(p_1\nmid g\). Complete that one prime-slot
condition. The complete term is covered by the preceding trace. In the
correction, \(p_1\ge Z_*\) is fixed to a divisor of \(g\); divisor
counting and the complete Fourier \(l^1\)-bound give
\[
 \ll Q^\epsilon {QB\over Z_*}.                                  \tag{20}
\]
The factors \((v,g)=1\) and \((a,g)=1\) forward, or
\((v,g)=1\) and \((b,g)=1\) reverse, remain legal one-variable
coefficients.

For \(C2_*\), forward write
\[
 b=vp_1p_2,\qquad Z_*\le p_1<p_2,
\]
with coefficient \(\mu(v)\), and use (18). Unequal dyadic cells have
automatic order. In an equal cell, recombining both stored orderings makes
the coefficient and full source amplitude symmetric, and exact
symmetrization is one half of the unrestricted pair minus its
repeated-prime diagonal. Fact \(4d2585a7863f65b6\) includes both terms,
every actual frequency, and the full and near-balanced \(G\)-regimes.
Its only use of the separated one-prime theorem
\(714b7538b3f03070\) occurs inside Case 1 of its proof, where the
grouped outer scale is explicitly verified to satisfy
\[
 VP_1\le S_0.
\]
No separated one-prime estimate is applied here to an outer scale exceeding
\(S_0\).

Complete the two source conditions \(p_i\nmid g\). The main term is the
complete \(C2_*\) trace. Each of the three nonempty correction types fixes
at least one rough prime divisor of \(g\), and the same divisor-counting
and Fourier-\(l^1\) argument as in (20) bounds their total by
\(Q^\epsilon QB/Z_*\). Reverse gives target \(+L_{\rm src}\);
the coefficient, equal-cell identity, completion, and bound are unchanged.

For \(C3_*\), forward write
\[
 b=vp_1p_2p_3,\qquad Z_*\le p_1<p_2<p_3,
\]
with coefficient \(-\mu(v)\), and again use (18). Completing the three
conditions \(p_i\nmid g\) gives one complete trace plus seven nonempty
correction types. The complete trace, all prime-slot permutations, every
equal cell, and all pair/triple equality terms are covered by fact
\(55b350a4925c7e1b\). In every correction at least one rough prime
\(p\ge Z_*\) is fixed to a prime divisor of \(g\). The remaining
multiplicative tuple has total divisor-weighted mass
\(O(Q^\epsilon B/p)\). There are \(O(Q)\) reciprocal moduli, and the
literal Fourier \(l^1\)-bound removes the complete frequency family.
Summing the fixed rough prime over divisors of \(g\) gives
\[
 \ll Q^\epsilon {QB\over Z_*}.                                  \tag{21}
\]
Multiple fixed rough primes and overlaps with pair/triple equalities are no
larger. Reverse is the exact coordinate interchange and conjugation of the
complete real \(h\)-pair, giving target \(+L_{\rm src}\).

The correction bound in (20)-(21) is uniform through the closed endpoint:
\[
 {QB\over Z_*}\ll Q^{2\beta-1/2+3\sigma}
 \le Q^{19/10-9\sigma/5}.                                      \tag{22}
\]
After choosing epsilon sufficiently small, it has a fixed power saving
from \(Q^2\). It is therefore absorbed by every near-balanced estimate
and, since \(G\ge1\), by every full-\(G\) estimate.

We verify the common physical inputs. In either strict orientation,
forced high and the square-root bound for the smaller divisor scale give
\[
 Q^{\beta-1}
 ={\text{larger divisor scale}\over\text{smaller divisor scale}}
 >x^{1/16-1/200+o(1)}.
\]
Since \(\beta-1\le1/5\), there is a fixed \(c_0>0\) such that
\[
 Q\ge x^{c_0}.                                                    \tag{23}
\]
Also, using the lower square-root bound for the smaller divisor scale,
\[
 |L_{\rm src}|\ll x^{1/2+o(1)}Q\le Q^{C_A}                      \tag{24}
\]
for one fixed \(C_A\). This verifies the target hypotheses of all five
abstract traces. Equations (19) and its reverse analogue verify all
archimedean projective norms.

By (6), every actual \(G<1\) lies in
\[
 Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\le G<1\le Q^{\sigma-\eta},
\]
and every actual \(G\ge1\) uses the full-\(G\) conclusion. After
decreasing one common \(\delta>0\) to absorb (16), (22), dyadic cells,
legal projective modes and the five anatomies, the contribution at fixed
\(g\) is
\[
 O(GQ^{2-\delta})
 =O((x/g)Q^{-\delta})\qquad(G\ge1),                             \tag{25}
\]
because \(DM=gGQ^2\asymp x\) forward and
\(RK=gGQ^2\asymp x\) reverse. For \(G<1\), it is
\[
 O(Q^{2-\delta}).                                                \tag{26}
\]

Sum the exact outer gcds. By (23),
\[
 \sum_{g\mid N}{x\over g}Q^{-\delta}
 \ll x^{1-c_0\delta+o(1)}.                                      \tag{27}
\]
For (26), \(Q=D/g\) forward and \(Q=R/g\) reverse, where the displayed
physical scale is the smaller divisor scale. After decreasing
\(0<\delta<1\),
\[
 \sum_{g\mid N}Q^{2-\delta}
 \le D^{2-\delta}\sum_{g\ge1}g^{-2+\delta}
\]
forward, with the same estimate using \(R\) reverse. The square-root upper
bound gives
\[
 \sum_{g\mid N}Q^{2-\delta}\ll x^{1-\delta/3}                  \tag{28}
\]
after shrinking the exponent to absorb fixed constants and the
polylogarithmically many active labels. Equations (25)-(28) prove (7)
with every orientation, actual \(G\), target-gcd complement, equality,
collision and exact outer-\(g\) coordinate included.

Since \(\mathfrak c(N)\ge C_2>0\), (7) is
\(o(\mathfrak c(N)x/\log x)\). Insert it into the exact identity (8)
and use (2) to obtain (9). Finally
\(T_{\rm postC3,sel}\) has support \(\beta>\beta_1\), and
\(\mathcal R_{m,\rm sel}\) is exactly its complete projection onto
\(\beta_1<\beta\le\beta_m\). Hence the complement in (8) has support
\(\beta>\beta_m\), proving (10). Nothing in the proof estimates the
open top sliver or assigns a sign to a proper anatomy.

glossary.R_m,sel: The complete same-selected-N constant-safe five-anatomy projection on beta_1<beta<=beta_m.
glossary.T_>beta_m,sel: The selected negative remainder after subtracting the complete projection through beta_m.
glossary.delta_m: A fixed global power-saving exponent for the complete constant-safe endpoint palette.

c9accda871a70b43.title: PRINCIPAL-CHARACTER DELETION FOR THE ACTUAL-Z_MID g=1, |h|=1 UPPER BOUNDARY. Assume the packet mathfrak B_{1,1}, its finite separated representation, and the natural endpoint scales of fact 58c03698e1b077c3. For a Dirichlet character chi modulo b define
c9accda871a70b43.author: slava chan
c9accda871a70b43.statement:
PRINCIPAL-CHARACTER DELETION FOR THE ACTUAL-Z_MID g=1, |h|=1 UPPER BOUNDARY. Assume the packet mathfrak B_{1,1}, its finite separated representation, and the natural endpoint scales of fact 58c03698e1b077c3. For a Dirichlet character chi modulo b define
G^+_{N,b}(chi)
 =sum_{u modulo b, (u,b)=1} e_b(Nu)chi(u).
For every (a,b)=1 one has the exact multiplicative-character reconstruction
e_b(Na^{-1})
 =phi(b)^(-1)sum_{chi modulo b}G^+_{N,b}(chi)chi(a).                   (1)
Let mathfrak B^{prin}_{1,1} be the complete part of mathfrak B_{1,1} obtained by retaining only the principal character modulo b in (1), in every literal separated form and for both conjugate frequencies. Then
|mathfrak B^{prin}_{1,1}|
 <=x^(1/2+o(1)).                                                       (2)
In particular the principal component is O(x^(1-delta_prin)) for every fixed delta_prin<1/2. Consequently the unresolved part of the actual-Z_mid g=1, |h|=1 hard upper face may be restricted to nonprincipal multiplicative characters, up to the fixed-power error (2). No estimate for the nonprincipal component, for |h|>1, for g>1, or for the derivative-integral and boundary-strip terms is asserted.
c9accda871a70b43.proof:
The Dirichlet characters modulo b form an orthogonal basis for functions on the unit group modulo b. For a unit a, insert the unit-group orthogonality relation selecting u=a^{-1}:
e_b(Na^{-1})
 =phi(b)^(-1)sum_{chi modulo b}sum_{u modulo b,(u,b)=1}
 e_b(Nu)chi(u)overline{chi(a^{-1})}.
Since overline{chi(a^{-1})}=chi(a), this is exactly (1).

For the principal character chi_0 modulo b,
G^+_{N,b}(chi_0)
 =sum_{u modulo b,(u,b)=1}e_b(Nu)
 =c_b(N),
the Ramanujan sum. The elementary Ramanujan-sum formula implies
|c_b(N)|<=(b,N).                                                       (3)

Fact 58c03698e1b077c3 writes the complete packet as x^(o(1)) finitely many forms
sum_{a asymp A_0,b asymp B_0,(a,b)=1}
 alpha_a beta_b G_end(a,b)e_b(Na^{-1}),
where A_0=x^(1/2+o(1)), B_0=x^(2/3+o(1)), and every literal coefficient and the endpoint amplitude is pointwise x^(o(1)). The latter pointwise bound follows directly from the Möbius and zero-one selectors, the logarithmic weights, and the zeroth-derivative case of the scaled-smooth bound in that fact. Replacing the phase by its principal term and taking absolute values therefore gives
|mathfrak B^{prin}_{1,1}|
 <=x^(o(1)) A_0
   sum_{b asymp B_0}|c_b(N)|/phi(b).                                  (4)

Uniformly for b<=x^(O(1)), the elementary Euler-product bound gives
1/phi(b)<=x^(o(1))/b.
Together with (3) and b asymp B_0,
sum_{b asymp B_0}|c_b(N)|/phi(b)
 <=x^(o(1))B_0^(-1)sum_{b asymp B_0}(b,N).                            (5)
Use the divisor identity
(b,N)=sum_{d|(b,N)}phi(d).
Interchanging the d- and b-sums, and noting that d divides N, yields
sum_{b asymp B_0}(b,N)
 <=sum_{d|N,d<=2B_0}phi(d)(2B_0/d+1).
Because phi(d)<=d and the number of divisors of N is x^(o(1)), both terms on the right are at most B_0x^(o(1)). Hence (5) is x^(o(1)). Substitution into (4) proves
|mathfrak B^{prin}_{1,1}|<=A_0x^(o(1))=x^(1/2+o(1)),
which is (2). The conjugate frequency and the finite literal separation inventory change only the x^(o(1)) factor.

glossary.G^+_{N,b}(chi): The multiplicative Gauss coefficient sum over reduced residues u modulo b of e_b(Nu)chi(u).
glossary.mathfrak B^{prin}_{1,1}: The principal-character component of the actual-Z_mid g=1, |h|=1 upper-boundary packet.

c9ed24359b1f5321.title: Let Z be a finite set, let U be a set, let S(z) be a two-element subset of U for each z in Z, and let w_z be real. For j in {0,1,2} define the ordered collision forms
c9ed24359b1f5321.author: slava chan
c9ed24359b1f5321.statement:
Let Z be a finite set, let U be a set, let S(z) be a two-element subset of U for each z in Z, and let w_z be real. For j in {0,1,2} define the ordered collision forms
Q_j=sum_{(z,z') in Z^2: |S(z) intersect S(z')|=j} w_z w_{z'}.
For each two-element subset E of U put W_E=sum_{z:S(z)=E}w_z. Let G_1 be the simple graph on Z in which distinct z,z' are adjacent exactly when |S(z) intersect S(z')|=1, and let Delta_1 be its maximum degree, with Delta_1=0 when Z is empty.

Then:

(A) The equal-support block has the exact positive-square formula
Q_2=sum_{E subset U: |E|=2} W_E^2>=0.

(B) The one-prime block is the adjacency quadratic form of G_1 and obeys
|Q_1|<=Delta_1 sum_{z in Z}w_z^2.
This degree tax is sharp for arbitrarily large Delta_1.

(C) No constant independent of the support family can bound |Q_1| by Q_2, or bound |Q_1|+Q_2 by |Q_0|. More precisely, for any integer n>=2 choose distinct elements a,b_1,...,b_n of U, take Z={1,...,n}, S(i)={a,b_i}, and w_i=1. Then
Q_0=0, Q_1=n(n-1), Q_2=n, Delta_1=n-1,
so equality holds in (B) and |Q_1|/Q_2=n-1. If B_1 is the coefficient matrix
B_1(i,j)=1_{|S(i) intersect S(j)|=1}w_iw_j,
then in this example B_1=J_n-I_n and
||B_1||_{S_1}=2(n-1).

(D) Collision deletion can erase exact signed cancellation. In the n=3 star configuration with weights (1,1,-2),
Q_0=0, Q_2=6, Q_1=-6, and
(sum_i w_i)^2=Q_0+Q_1+Q_2=0.
Consequently, in the paired-source ledger of fact c882223fd3a1511a, the two collision blocks cannot be absorbed into the disjoint four-prime block by support combinatorics alone. Equal-support collisions form a positive square, while one-prime collisions require a separately controlled degree, spectral, or arithmetic cancellation input.
c9ed24359b1f5321.proof:
For (A), the condition |S(z) intersect S(z')|=2 is equivalent to S(z)=S(z'), because both supports have cardinality two. Grouping the ordered sum by their common support E gives
Q_2=sum_E sum_{z:S(z)=E}sum_{z':S(z')=E} w_z w_{z'}
   =sum_E (sum_{z:S(z)=E}w_z)^2
   =sum_E W_E^2.
All W_E are real, so this is nonnegative.

For (B), by definition
Q_1=sum_{z,z': z adjacent to z'}w_z w_{z'}.
The graph has no loops and each unordered edge {z,z'} occurs twice. Hence
|Q_1|<=2 sum_{{z,z'} an edge}|w_z w_{z'}|
       <=sum_{{z,z'} an edge}(w_z^2+w_{z'}^2)
       =sum_z deg_{G_1}(z)w_z^2
       <=Delta_1 sum_z w_z^2.
This proves the degree bound.

For (C), any two different star supports {a,b_i} and {a,b_j} meet in exactly the singleton {a}. Thus G_1 is the complete graph K_n, every degree is n-1, and there are no disjoint pairs. With all weights one, the ordered one-prime sum counts n(n-1) off-diagonal pairs, while the equal-support sum contains only the n diagonal pairs because the supports are distinct. This gives
Q_0=0, Q_1=n(n-1), Q_2=n
and proves equality in (B). The ratio n-1 is unbounded, while Q_0 remains zero, proving both no-universal-constant assertions.

In the same unit-weight star example, B_1 is the adjacency matrix J_n-I_n. The all-ones vector is an eigenvector with eigenvalue n-1, and every vector orthogonal to it is an eigenvector with eigenvalue -1. Therefore its singular values are n-1 followed by n-1 copies of 1, and its nuclear norm is 2(n-1).

For (D), in the three-vertex star every off-diagonal ordered pair lies in Q_1 and every diagonal pair lies in Q_2. Thus
Q_2=1^2+1^2+(-2)^2=6.
Also the complete ordered sum is (1+1-2)^2=0 and Q_0=0, so Q_1=-6. Directly, Q_1=2(1 times 1+1 times (-2)+1 times (-2))=-6. Hence the exact cancellation is verified.

Fact c882223fd3a1511a identifies these abstract Q_j with the support-intersection blocks in the actual paired-source square. The examples prove a combinatorial non-absorption statement only: an actual arithmetic family could still supply additional degree bounds or cancellation, but neither follows from the support partition itself.

glossary.B_1: the weighted one-prime collision coefficient matrix
glossary.G_1: the simple one-prime collision graph on Z
glossary.I_n: the n by n identity matrix
glossary.J_n: the n by n all-ones matrix
glossary.Q_j: the ordered weighted pair sum with support-intersection size j
glossary.S(z): the two-element support attached to z
glossary.S_1: the Schatten-one or nuclear matrix norm
glossary.U: the universe of possible prime-support labels
glossary.W_E: the aggregate weight of all incidences whose support equals E
glossary.a: the common element in the star-support examples
glossary.b_i: the i-th leaf element in the star-support examples
glossary.w_z: the real weight attached to z

ca3027882b24da1a.title: COUNTABLE l1 EXTENSION OF THE FACTORABLE-MODULUS MARKED rho_{1/2} TYPE-II PAYMENT. Fix real A>0 and an integer K>=1. Let B be sufficiently large, let delta be real, and let Q_1,R_1,P,M>=2 satisfy
ca3027882b24da1a.author: slava chan
ca3027882b24da1a.statement:
COUNTABLE l1 EXTENSION OF THE FACTORABLE-MODULUS MARKED rho_{1/2} TYPE-II PAYMENT. Fix real A>0 and an integer K>=1. Let B be sufficiently large, let delta be real, and let Q_1,R_1,P,M>=2 satisfy
Q_1R_1=B^(1/2+delta), PM asymptotic to B,
B^(6delta)(log B)^C<=R_1<=B^(1/10-3delta)(log B)^(-C),
Q_1B^(2delta)(log B)^C<=P<=B^(1/2-3delta)(log B)^(-C),           (1)
where C=C(A,K)>0 is sufficiently large. Put Q_0=Q_1R_1 and let c be a positive integer. Let cal S be a set of ordered pairs (q,r), with q in [Q_1,2Q_1) and r in [R_1,2R_1), such that (q,r) maps injectively to s=qr, every s is squarefree, and (s,c)=1. For each (q,r) choose a unit residue a_{q,r} modulo s and a function V_s supported on [B,2B) with |V_s(n)|<=L. Let cal P, omega_P, b_{P,c}^{rho}, D_s^{rho,med}, T_s^{rho}, and E_s^{rho} be those of fact e59f666ecac4d4cb.

Assume now that J is a finite or countable index set and that there are complex numbers lambda_{j,s}, sequences A_j(p) supported on primes P<=p<2P, and sequences B_j(m) supported on M<=m<2M such that, for every selected prime p and every positive integer m,
V_s(pm)=sum_{j in J}lambda_{j,s}A_j(p)B_j(m),                    (2)
the series being absolutely convergent, and
sum_{j in J}sup_{s=qr,(q,r) in cal S}|lambda_{j,s}|
 <=L_{proj,rho},                                                  (3)
|A_j(n)|<=tau_K(n), |B_j(n)|<=tau_K(n).                          (4)
Assume that every alpha_{j,n}=1_{n prime}A_j(n) satisfies Maynard's Siegel-Walfisz condition uniformly in j and in all displayed parameters.

Then
sum_{(q,r) in cal S}|D_{qr}^{rho,med}|
 <<_{A,K}L_{proj,rho}B(log B)^(-A)
 +L(1+log(2BQ_0))^2
  [B/P+Q_0P+omega_P(c)(B/P+Q_0)].                               (5)
Thus the word 'finitely' in the projective hypothesis of fact be6fb90ce3095e82 may be replaced by 'finitely or countably with finite l1 outer norm', provided support, divisor bounds, and Siegel-Walfisz constants are uniform. No assertion is made that any particular countable family satisfies the latter condition.
ca3027882b24da1a.proof:
For a modulus s=qr put
Delta_s(n)=1_{n congruent a_{q,r} (mod s)}
 -phi(s)^(-1)1_{(n,s)=1}.                                       (6)
Fact e59f666ecac4d4cb gives
D_s^{rho,med}=T_s^{rho}+E_s^{rho},                               (7)
where
T_s^{rho}
 =-1/2 sum_{p in cal P,(p,c)=1}sum_m
 b_{P,c}^{rho}(m)V_s(pm)Delta_s(pm).                             (8)
Introduce the genuinely unrestricted prime row
T'_s
 =-1/2 sum_{p in cal P}sum_m
 b_{P,c}^{rho}(m)V_s(pm)Delta_s(pm).                             (9)

The sums over p,m are finite. By (3)-(4),
sum_{j in J}|lambda_{j,s}A_j(p)B_j(m)|
 <=L_{proj,rho}tau_K(p)tau_K(m)<infinity.                        (10)
Thus (2) may be inserted into (9), and absolute convergence permits
T'_s=sum_{j in J}lambda_{j,s}T'_{s,j},                           (11)
where T'_{s,j} is the all-selected-primes centered bilinear row with prime coefficient A_j and cofactor coefficient b_{P,c}^{rho}B_j. Since |b_{P,c}^{rho}(m)|<=1, both coefficients remain divisor bounded after changing K by an amount depending only on K.

The single-mode application of Maynard's Proposition 5.1 verified in fact be6fb90ce3095e82 is precisely for this unrestricted row. Uniformly in j it gives
sum_{(q,r) in cal S}|T'_{qr,j}|<<_{A,K}B(log B)^(-A).             (12)
The hypotheses are (1), the common supports, (4), and the uniform Siegel-Walfisz condition; the varying unit residue is allowed by Maynard's supremum. The triangle inequality, Tonelli's theorem, (3), and (12) now yield
sum_{(q,r) in cal S}|T'_{qr}|
 <=sum_j sup_s|lambda_{j,s}|sum_{(q,r) in cal S}|T'_{qr,j}|
 <<_{A,K}L_{proj,rho}B(log B)^(-A).                              (13)

We next restore the omitted restriction (p,c)=1 at the level of the reconstructed rows. The difference T_s^{rho}-T'_s contains only p in cal P with p|c. Since (s,c)=1, every such p is a unit modulo s. For a fixed exceptional p and s, the physical congruence in Delta_s selects at most O(B/(Ps)+1) supported m, while the principal term contributes at most O(B/(P phi(s))). Here the harmless endpoint constants are absorbed because PM is comparable to B and P,M>=2.

We now sum these bounds without invoking an external reciprocal-totient estimate. Every s is squarefree, so
s/phi(s)=product_{l|s}(1-1/l)^(-1)
 <=product_{l|s}(1+1/l)^2
 =(sum_{d|s}1/d)^2
 <=(sum_{1<=d<=s}1/d)^2
 <=(1+log s)^2.                                                  (14)
The product inequality holds prime by prime. Injectivity gives at most O(Q_0) moduli s, all in [Q_0,4Q_0). Therefore
sum_{s}|1/s|<<1,
sum_s 1/phi(s)
 =sum_s (s/phi(s))/s
 <<(1+log(4Q_0))^2.                                              (15)
Consequently, after using |b_{P,c}^{rho}|<=1 and |V_s|<=L and then summing over the omega_P(c) exceptional primes,
sum_{(q,r) in cal S}|T_{qr}^{rho}-T'_{qr}|
 <<L omega_P(c)(1+log(2BQ_0))^2(B/P+Q_0).                        (16)

Finally, the genuine correction estimate of fact e59f666ecac4d4cb is
sum_{(q,r) in cal S}|E_{qr}^{rho}|
 <<L(1+log(2BQ_0))^2(B/P+Q_0P).                                 (17)
Combine (7), (13), (16), and (17) to obtain (5). The countable argument occurs only in the unrestricted row (11)-(13), where all constants and supports are uniform; no c-dependent Siegel-Walfisz assertion is used.

glossary.Delta_s(n): The centered residue-class discrepancy kernel at modulus s.
glossary.J: The finite or countable projective-mode index set.
glossary.L_{proj,rho}: The l1 outer projective norm of the countable decomposition.
glossary.T'_s: The unrestricted marked main row in which all selected primes are retained before the p-dividing-c comparison.
glossary.T'_{s,j}: The single projective-mode component of the unrestricted row T'_s.

ca3e3b73946c9248.title: ABSTRACT CLOSED-ENDPOINT COMPLETE-FREQUENCY TARGET-GCD-DESCENDED INTERVAL-PRIME TRACE
ca3e3b73946c9248.author: slava chan
ca3e3b73946c9248.statement:
ABSTRACT CLOSED-ENDPOINT COMPLETE-FREQUENCY TARGET-GCD-DESCENDED INTERVAL-PRIME TRACE.

Fix integers \(J,C_A,K\ge1\), constants \(C\ge1\),
\(0<\kappa\le1/100\), and put
\[
 \sigma=\kappa/100,quad
 \beta_1=6/5-3\sigma,quad
 \beta_m=6/5-12\sigma/5.
\]
Let \(\beta_1<\beta\le\beta_m\), let \(Q\) be sufficiently large,
and put
\[
 B=Q^\beta,quad H_T=B/Q,quad
 L_0=H_TQ^\sigma,quad Z_*=2Q^{3/2-\beta-3\sigma}.
\]
Fix a nonzero integer \(L_{\rm src}\) with
\(|L_{\rm src}|\le Q^{C_A}\).  Let \(\mathcal C\) be any set of
squarefree divisors \(c\mid L_{\rm src}\) with
\[
 c\le H_TQ^{\sigma/4}.
\]
For \(c\in\mathcal C\), put \(Q_c=Q/c\) and choose
\(U_c,Y_c\ge1\) satisfying
\[
 C^{-1}B\le U_cY_c\le CB,qquad
 L_0/2\le Y_c\le Z_*.
\]
For \(Q_c\le q<2Q_c\), let \(|d_{c,q}|\le1\), supported on
squarefree \(q\) for which
\[
 (c,q)=(L_{\rm src}/c,q)=1.
\]
For every dyadic \(F\ge1\), let
\(\nu_{c,F}(h),\alpha_{c,F}(u),\gamma_{c,F}(p)\) have fixed
divisor-function bounds and supports
\[
 F\le|h|<2F,quad U_c\le u<2U_c,
\]
and primes \(Y_c\le p<2Y_c\) with \(L_0<p<Z_*\).  Let
\(\Psi_{c,F}\) be a uniformly scaled-smooth projective amplitude of
fixed complexity and uniformly bounded projective Fourier norm.  Let
\[
 |\omega_{c,F}|\le C_{J_0}
 \min\{1,(F/H_P)^{-J_0}\}
\]
for every fixed integer \(J_0\ge1\).  Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
T_c={1\over H_P}\sum_F\omega_{c,F}
 &\sum_{Q_c\le q<2Q_c}d_{c,q}
 \sum_{F\le|h|<2F}\nu_{c,F}(h)\\
 &\sum_{\substack{U_c\le u<2U_c\cr
 Y_c\le p<2Y_c, p\ {m prime}\cr
 (up,cq)=1,\ (u,p)=1}}
 \alpha_{c,F}(u)\gamma_{c,F}(p)
 \Psi_{c,F}\!\left({q\over Q_c},{|h|\over F},
                      {u\over U_c},{p\over Y_c}\right)
 e_q\!\left(-{L_{\rm src}\over c}h(up)^{-1}\right).
\end{aligned}                                                     \tag{1}
\]

(i) If \(G\ge1\) and \(H_P=H_T/G\), then
\[
 sum_{c\in\mathcal C}|T_c|\ll GQ^{2-\delta_F}                 \tag{2}
\]
for a fixed \(\delta_F>0\).

(ii) If \(0<\eta<\sigma\),
\[
 Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\le G\le Q^{\sigma-\eta},qquad
 H_P=H_T/G,
\]
then
\[
 sum_{c\in\mathcal C}|T_c|\ll Q^{2-\delta_N}                 \tag{3}
\]
for a fixed \(\delta_N>0\).

The constants and savings may depend on
\(\kappa,\eta,C_A,J,K,C\) and the fixed projective norm, but not on
\(Q,G,H_P,L_{\rm src},\mathcal C\), or the displayed coefficients.
Both conclusions include \(H_P<1\), all actual integer-frequency blocks,
all explicitly displayed coprimalities, and any additional labels already
absorbed into the one-variable coefficients or the stated projective
amplitude.  No literal-source identification, large-target-gcd tail,
outer-\(g\) assembly, or other anatomy is asserted.
ca3e3b73946c9248.proof:
Put
\[
 v=F/H_P,qquad q_0=Q_c=Q/c.
\]
We first derive, rather than assume, the four-term bound on an analytic
frequency block.

Expand \(\Psi_{c,F}\) in an absolutely summable Fourier series in the
four logarithmic scaled variables.  Its coefficient \(\ell^1\)-norm is
uniformly bounded.  Absorb the separated one-variable Fourier modes into
\(d_{c,q},\nu_{c,F},\alpha_{c,F},\gamma_{c,F}\).
The condition \((up,c)=1\) separates as \((u,c)=(p,c)=1\) and is
absorbed into the \(u\)- and \(p\)-coefficients.  The condition
\((up,q)=1\) is precisely the complete-product coprimality required by
the reciprocal estimate.  Finally write
\[
 1_{(u,p)=1}=1-1_{p\mid u}.                                      \tag{4}
\]

Fix \(c,F\).  For the unrestricted term in (4), suppose
\[
 2F\le Y_c,qquad 8FY_c<q
\]
throughout \(q\asymp q_0\).  We verify the polynomial \(u\)-support
required by fact \(4cae52efa792b9ef\).  Since
\[
 U_c\ll B/Y_c\ll Q^{1-\sigma},                                 \tag{5}
\]
whereas
\[
 q_0\ge Q^{2-\beta-\sigma/4}
      \ge Q^{4/5+43\sigma/20},                                  \tag{6}
\]
one has \(u\le q^2\) for all supported \(u,q\) and large \(Q\).

Apply fact \(4cae52efa792b9ef\) for each fixed \(q\), separately to
each projective Fourier mode and each sign of \(h\), and sum its two
terms over the \(O(q_0)\) moduli.  Restoring the prefactor
\(H_P^{-1}\) and using \(U_cY_c\asymp B\) gives, up to
\(Q^\epsilon|\omega_{c,F}|\), three unrestricted contributions:
\[
 A_1=c^{-1}G^{1/2}Q^2(H_T/Y_c)^{1/2}v^{1/2},                       \tag{7}
\]
\[
 A_2=c^{-5/4}Q^{7/4}(H_TY_c)^{1/2}v,                              \tag{8}
\]
\[
 A_3=c^{-3/4}Q^{7/4}H_Tv.                                         \tag{9}
\]
Indeed the first fixed-\(q\) term gives
\[
 H_P^{-1}q_0U_c(FY_c)^{1/2}=A_1
\]
up to fixed constants.  For the second use
\[
 \{U_c(1+U_c/q_0)\}^{1/2}
 \le U_c^{1/2}+U_cq_0^{-1/2};
\]
after multiplication by the remaining fixed-\(q\) factors and summation
over \(q\), these are respectively (8) and (9).

For the diagonal term \(p\mid u\) in (4), write \(u=pu'\).
The number of supported pairs \((u,p)\) is
\[
 \ll Q^\epsilon U_c:
\]
for each supported \(u\), the number of prime divisors \(p\mid u\)
is at most a divisor function, and conversely the dyadic conditions only
decrease the count.  Absolute summation over \(q,h\), with
\(H_P^{-1}F=v\), gives
\[
 A_4\ll
 Q^\epsilon|\omega_{c,F}|q_0vU_c
 \ll Q^\epsilon|\omega_{c,F}|c^{-1}Q^{2-\sigma}v,              \tag{10}
\]
using (5).  Equations (7)-(10) are the required complete four-term lifting.
They retain the complete-product condition \((up,q)=1\), while every
other displayed mask has been separated exactly.

We prove (2).  Restrict first to
\[
 v\le Q^{\sigma/2}.                                               \tag{11}
\]
Since \(Y_c\ge H_TQ^\sigma/2\) and \(G\ge1\),
\[
 2F/Y_c\le4v/(GQ^\sigma)<1.                                     \tag{12}
\]
Also \(c\le H_TQ^{\sigma/4}\), \(Y_c\le Z_*\), and
\(H_TZ_*=2Q^{1/2-3\sigma}\), so
\[
 {q_0\over H_PY_c}
 ={QG\over cH_TY_c}
 \gg GQ^{3/2-\beta+11\sigma/4}
 \ge GQ^{3/10+103\sigma/20}.                                    \tag{13}
\]
Thus (11) implies \(8FY_c<q\) for large \(Q\), and the four terms
apply.

Divide (7)-(10) by \(GQ^2\).  From
\(Y_c\ge H_TQ^\sigma/2\),
\(H_TY_c\ll Q^{1/2-3\sigma}\), and
\(\beta\le\beta_m\), the ratios are at most constant multiples of
\[
 c^{-1}Q^{-\sigma/2}v^{1/2},quad
 c^{-5/4}Q^{-3\sigma/2}v,quad
 c^{-3/4}Q^{-1/20-12\sigma/5}v,quad
 c^{-1}Q^{-\sigma}v.                                              \tag{14}
\]
Second-order decay sums (14) over dyadic (11).

For \(v>Q^{\sigma/2}\), use direct counting in (1):
\[
 |T_{c,F}|\ll
 Q^\epsilon c^{-1}Q^2H_Tv|\omega_{c,F}|.                         \tag{15}
\]
Since \(H_T\le Q^{1/5-12\sigma/5}\), choose a fixed available decay
order \(J_*\) with
\[
 (J_*-1)\sigma/2>1/5+\sigma.
\]
The dyadic sum of (15) is
\(O(c^{-1}GQ^{2-\delta_F})\), using \(G\ge1\).
The divisor bound on \(L_{\rm src}\) gives
\[
 sum_{c\in\mathcal C}
 (c^{-1}+c^{-3/4}+c^{-5/4})\ll Q^\epsilon.
\]
This proves (2).

For (3), use the analytic range
\[
 v\le Q^{\eta/2}.                                                 \tag{16}
\]
The lower bound on \(G\) yields
\[
 Y_c/H_P\ge GQ^\sigma/2\ge Q^\eta/2,
\]
so \(2F\le Y_c\).  From (13) and
\(G\ge Q^{-\sigma+\eta}\), one again obtains
\(8FY_c<q\) throughout (16).  Relative to \(Q^2\), the first term
saves because
\[
 G^{1/2}(H_T/Y_c)^{1/2}
 \ll Q^{(\sigma-\eta)/2}Q^{-\sigma/2}=Q^{-\eta/2}.             \tag{17}
\]
The terms (8), (9), (10) save respectively
\(3\sigma/2\), \(1/20+12\sigma/5\), and \(\sigma\).
Fixed-order decay sums the analytic blocks.

For \(v>Q^{\eta/2}\), direct counting gives
\[
 |T_{c,F}|\ll
 Q^\epsilon c^{-1}QBv|\omega_{c,F}|.                             \tag{18}
\]
Choose the available fixed decay order sufficiently large in terms of
\(\eta\) and \(\beta_m<6/5\).  Its dyadic sum is
\(O(c^{-1}Q^{2-\delta_N})\), and the divisor sum completes (3).

If \(H_P<1\), every integer \(F\ge1\) has \(v>1\), but it still
lies in exactly one of the analytic and decaying ranges above.  The
projective Fourier modes and every explicitly legal inherited label have
uniform \(\ell^1\)-cost and are absorbed by decreasing the fixed
savings.  This proves the theorem.

glossary.delta_F: The fixed full-G saving exponent in the abstract closed-endpoint interval-prime trace.
glossary.delta_N: The fixed near-balanced saving exponent in the abstract closed-endpoint interval-prime trace.

ca4977b431a3c229.title: ONE-SHOT VECTOR-VALUED NO-FIT ON A GENUINELY VARYING LARGE-PRIME TMC BLOCK. Adopt the notation of fact e240fbd021e8cb63. Let cal P contain at least two distinct active primes p>2D. Let cal K be a fixed nonempty finite set of nonzero integers with |k|<min_{p in cal P}p, viewed as residues modulo every p. Let b be either one of the literal common sequences a_{t_1}(n)R_{t_2}(n) or a_{t_2}(n)R_{t_1}(n), and define
ca4977b431a3c229.author: slava chan
ca4977b431a3c229.statement:
ONE-SHOT VECTOR-VALUED NO-FIT ON A GENUINELY VARYING LARGE-PRIME TMC BLOCK. Adopt the notation of fact e240fbd021e8cb63. Let cal P contain at least two distinct active primes p>2D. Let cal K be a fixed nonempty finite set of nonzero integers with |k|<min_{p in cal P}p, viewed as residues modulo every p. Let b be either one of the literal common sequences a_{t_1}(n)R_{t_2}(n) or a_{t_2}(n)R_{t_1}(n), and define
(T_pb)(k)=sum_{n in cal I_D}b(n)e_p(-kNn^{-1}),qquad p in cal P, k in cal K.       (1)
All inverses in (1) exist. The varying-prime quadratic norm has the exact dual form
(sum_{p in cal P}sum_{k in cal K}|(T_pb)(k)|^2)^{1/2}
=sup_{sum_{p,k}|nu_{p,k}|^2=1}|sum_{p in cal P}sum_{k in cal K}nu_{p,k}(T_pb)(k)|.     (2)
A single substitution q=p and h=k into fact 73fb9efe1286f7e9 does not represent the full supremum in (2), because that fact requires one numerator-frequency sequence nu_k fixed independently of q, whereas (2) permits an arbitrary array nu_{p,k}. Any use of that fact on (2) must first decompose the array into modulus-independent frequency sequences and pay the resulting projective norm; fact 73fb9efe1286f7e9 supplies no bound for that projective norm.

The exact alternative square expansion is
sum_{k in cal K}|(T_pb)(k)|^2
=sum_{n,m in cal I_D}b(n)conjugate(b(m))cal D_{cal K,p}(N(n-m)(nm)^{-1}),             (3)
where cal D_{cal K,p}(a)=sum_{k in cal K}e_p(ka). For the literal b, equation (3) contains the constraint h=n-m and the two nested reflected Mobius windows R_t. Hence a one-shot substitution of (h,s,t)=(n-m,n,m) into fact 73fb9efe1286f7e9 also fails its independent coefficient-slot hypothesis. This is only a precise no-one-shot-substitution statement. It does not assert that fact 73fb cannot be used after a quantitatively controlled decomposition, and it does not prove or disprove the large-prime portion of QUAD-SUPPLIER_A.
ca4977b431a3c229.proof:
Every n in cal I_D is positive and at most 2D, while every p in cal P is greater than 2D. Hence p does not divide n, proving that (1) is defined.

The direct sum over the nonempty finite set cal P times cal K is a finite-dimensional Hilbert space. Its norm equals the supremum of the absolute inner product against its unit sphere. Applying this to the vector ((T_pb)(k))_{p,k} proves (2).

In fact 73fb9efe1286f7e9 the scalar form W_q uses coefficient sequences nu_h,a_s,b_t that are selected independently of q. Under the literal identification q=p and h=k, one call to that fact therefore produces a pairing whose k-coefficient is the same for every p. The unit sphere in (2), by contrast, contains all arrays nu_{p,k}, with no equality constraint between two different primes. Thus a single call cannot equal the supremum in (2). Representing a general array as a sum or integral of p-independent k-sequences is an additional decomposition, and its coefficient norm is not among the conclusions of fact 73fb9efe1286f7e9. This proves precisely the stated one-shot mismatch, without making a quantitative claim about all possible decompositions.

For (3), expand (1) and its complex conjugate. The phase attached to n,m is
e_p(-kNn^{-1})e_p(kNm^{-1})=e_p(kN(m^{-1}-n^{-1}))
=e_p(kN(n-m)(nm)^{-1}).
Summing over k gives (3). By fact e240fbd021e8cb63,
R_t(n)=sum_v a_t(v)1_{n-v in cal H_mid}.
Thus the coefficient in (3) contains b(n)conjugate(b(m)), while the numerator difference h is forced to equal n-m. Fact 73fb9efe1286f7e9 instead starts with a product of independent one-variable coefficient sequences in h,s,t. Therefore the literal assignment (h,s,t)=(n-m,n,m) is not a one-shot specialization. The final scope sentences explicitly leave open decompositions and all quantitative estimates.

glossary.T_p: the short-frequency reciprocal transform at prime modulus p
glossary.cal D_{cal K,p}: the incomplete additive Dirichlet kernel modulo p over cal K
glossary.cal K: one common nonempty integer frequency set embedded modulo every p in cal P
glossary.cal P: a finite set containing at least two distinct active primes larger than 2D
glossary.nu_{p,k}: the arbitrary modulus-dependent dual test array in equation (2)

ca9ce191fbd75de1.title: Assume the hypotheses and notation of fact 006c61051140749b. Thus
ca9ce191fbd75de1.author: slava chan
ca9ce191fbd75de1.statement:
Assume the hypotheses and notation of fact 006c61051140749b. Thus
\[
 T_x=(\log x)^{6+\eta+\rho},\qquad
 {1\over2}x^{1/2}(\log x)^{-B_{\rm src}}\le D\le2x^{1/2},
 \qquad D>2T_x,
\]
and
\[
 {\cal R}_{<}^{F}
 =
 \sum_{s<T_x^2}c_{T_x}(s)
 \sum_{h\ne0}\omega_s(h){\cal B}_s(h),\qquad
 \omega_s(h)=\min\left(1,{sT_x|h|\over D}\right).       \tag{1}
\]
For \(s\ge1\), put
\[
 {\cal R}_s=\sum_{h\ne0}\omega_s(h){\cal B}_s(h).       \tag{2}
\]
Let
\[
 {\mathfrak D}_N^\Lambda
 =\sum_{m\ge1}\left|
 \sum_{d\in{\cal I}_D}\mu(d)\Phi(d/D)W(dm/x)
 \Phi((N-dm)/U)\Lambda(N-dm)\right|^2                 \tag{3}
\]
be the full-von-Mangoldt top-band dispersion, and define the real number
\[
 H_0=D(\log x)^{-6-\eta-\rho/2}.                        \tag{4}
\]
Then, as \(x\) tends to infinity,
\[
 \sum_{\substack{s<T_x^2\\s\ge T_x}}
 c_{T_x}(s){\cal R}_s
 \ll_{W,\Phi,\alpha,\beta}
 {xD(\log x)^2\log(2T_x)\over T_x},                    \tag{5}
\]
and
\[
 {\cal R}_1
 =
 {\mathfrak D}_N^\Lambda
 +O_{W,\Phi,\alpha,\beta}\left({xD(\log x)^2\over T_x}\right).
                                                               \tag{6}
\]
Consequently
\[
 {\cal R}_{<}^{F}
 =
 {\mathfrak D}_N^\Lambda
 +O_{W,\Phi,\alpha,\beta}\left(
 {xD(\log x)^2\log(2T_x)\over T_x}\right)
 =
 {\mathfrak D}_N^\Lambda
 +o\left(xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta}\right).                  \tag{7}
\]
Thus the Fejer residual is a cleaner diagonal-free analytic expression but
is target-close to the original dispersion; it is not a logically weaker
proposition at the target scale.

The \(s=1\) correlation satisfies the support-counting estimates
\[
 \sum_{0<|h|\le H_0}|{\cal B}_1(h)|
 \ll_{W,\Phi,\alpha,\beta}
 xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta-\rho/2},                          \tag{8}
\]
and
\[
 \sum_{3D/2-H_0<|h|\le3D/2}|{\cal B}_1(h)|
 \ll_{W,\Phi,\alpha,\beta}
 xD(\log x)^{-10-2\eta-\rho}.                          \tag{9}
\]
For all sufficiently large \(x\),
\[
 {D\over T_x}<H_0,\qquad
 \omega_1(h)=1\quad(|h|>H_0),\qquad
 {\cal B}_1(h)=0\quad(|h|>3D/2).                       \tag{10}
\]

Define
\[
 H_j=2^jH_0\quad(j\ge0),
\]
and let \(J\) be the least nonnegative integer such that
\[
 2^{J+1}H_0\ge3D/2.                                    \tag{11}
\]
Then \(H_j\le2D\) for \(0\le j\le J\), and
\[
 J+1\ll_{\eta,\rho}\log(2T_x).                         \tag{12}
\]
For \(0\le j\le J\), define the trimmed middle-shift block
\[
 {\cal S}_j=
 \sum_{\substack{H_j<|h|\le2H_j\\
                  |h|\le3D/2-H_0}}
 {\cal B}_1(h).                                         \tag{13}
\]
The following exact one-sided dyadic theorem is sufficient for
TB-FEJ-RES:
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 {\cal S}_j
 \ll_{W,\Phi,\alpha,\beta,\eta,\rho}
 {xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta}\over\log(2T_x)}
 \quad(0\le j\le J).
 \quad}                                                 \tag{TB-SHIFT-BLOCK}
\]
Indeed, TB-SHIFT-BLOCK implies
\[
 {\cal R}_{<}^{F}\ll xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta}.              \tag{14}
\]
The theorem is one-sided and retains the signs
\(\mu(w)\mu(w-h)\); no absolute value is placed around \({\cal S}_j\).
No estimate asserted in TB-SHIFT-BLOCK is proved here.
ca9ce191fbd75de1.proof:
We first prove a uniform bound for one residual row. Let
\[
 F_s(\theta)=
 \left(\sum_w f_{s,m}(w)e(\theta w)\right)_{m\ge1}.
\]
For fixed \(s\), the support of \(\Phi(sw/D)\) permits \(O(D/s)\)
integers \(w\), and the support of \(W(smw/x)\) permits \(O(x/D)\)
integers \(m\). Also \(|f_{s,m}(w)|\ll_{W,\Phi}\log x\). Cauchy's
inequality in \(w\) gives
\[
 \|F_s(0)\|_2^2
 \le {O(D)\over s}\sum_{m,w}|f_{s,m}(w)|^2
 \ll_{W,\Phi}{xD(\log x)^2\over s^2}.                  \tag{15}
\]
Fact 1024f6bb05c0bb49 proves that the Fejer kernel is nonnegative and
has integral one. Hence
\[
 \int P_{D/(sT_x)}(\theta)\|F_s(\theta)\|_2^2d\theta
 \le\sup_\theta\|F_s(\theta)\|_2^2
 \ll_{W,\Phi}{xD(\log x)^2\over s^2},                  \tag{16}
\]
where the last estimate is the same Cauchy argument as (15), uniformly
in \(\theta\). By the definition of the residual,
\[
 |{\cal R}_s|
 \ll_{W,\Phi}{xD(\log x)^2\over s^2}.                  \tag{17}
\]

Fact 006c61051140749b gives
\[
 c_{T_x}(s)=
 \sum_{\substack{gr=s\\g,r<T_x}}\mu(r).
\]
Therefore, without discarding the signs in the identity (1), the triangle
inequality applied only to the boundary gives
\[
\begin{split}
 \left|\sum_{\substack{s<T_x^2\\s\ge T_x}}
 c_{T_x}(s){\cal R}_s\right|
 &\le
 \sum_{\substack{g,r<T_x\\gr\ge T_x}}|{\cal R}_{gr}|\\
 &\ll xD(\log x)^2
 \sum_{g<T_x}{1\over g^2}
 \sum_{T_x/g\le r<T_x}{1\over r^2}.                    \tag{18}
\end{split}
\]
For \(1\le g<T_x\),
\[
 \sum_{r\ge T_x/g}r^{-2}\ll {g\over T_x}.
\]
Thus the last double sum in (18) is
\[
 \ll {1\over T_x}\sum_{g<T_x}{1\over g}
 \ll{\log(2T_x)\over T_x},
\]
which proves (5).

By (4) of fact 006c61051140749b, all grouped coefficients with
\(1<s<T_x\) vanish and \(c_{T_x}(1)=1\). It remains to compare
\({\cal R}_1\) with (3). Fact 1024f6bb05c0bb49 gives exactly
\[
 {\cal R}_1
 =
 \|F_1(0)\|_2^2-
 \int P_{D/T_x}(\theta)\|F_1(\theta)\|_2^2d\theta,       \tag{19}
\]
and the definition of \(F_1\) gives
\[
 \|F_1(0)\|_2^2={\mathfrak D}_N^\Lambda.                \tag{20}
\]
Expanding the Fejer integral, its Fourier coefficient vanishes unless
\(|h|<D/T_x\) and has absolute value at most one. Its absolute value is
therefore at most
\[
 \sum_{\substack{w,w'\in{\cal I}_D\\|w-w'|<D/T_x}}
 \sum_m
 O_{W,\Phi}\big((\log x)^2\big).                        \tag{21}
\]
There are \(O(D)\) choices for \(w\), \(O(D/T_x)\) choices for \(w'\)
after \(w\) is fixed, because \(D/T_x>2\), and \(O(x/D)\) choices for
\(m\). Thus (21) is
\[
 O_{W,\Phi}\left({xD(\log x)^2\over T_x}\right).
\]
Equations (19)--(21) prove (6). Combining (5), (6), and the exact
cancellation for \(1<s<T_x\) proves the first equality in (7). Since
\[
 {(\log x)^2\log(2T_x)\over T_x}
 =(\log x)^{-4-\eta-\rho}\log(2T_x)
 =o((\log x)^{-4-\eta}),
\]
the second equality in (7) follows.

We prove (8). For each integer \(h\), the conditions
\(w,w-h\in{\cal I}_D\) allow \(O(D)\) integers \(w\). For each such
pair, the two \(W\)-supports allow \(O(x/D)\) integers \(m\). Every
summand in \({\cal B}_1(h)\) has absolute value
\(O_{W,\Phi}((\log x)^2)\). There are \(O(H_0)\) nonzero integers
\(h\) with \(|h|\le H_0\), for all sufficiently large \(x\). Hence
\[
 \sum_{0<|h|\le H_0}|{\cal B}_1(h)|
 \ll xH_0(\log x)^2
 =xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta-\rho/2},
\]
which is (8).

For (9), first take \(h>0\). Membership of \(w\) and \(w-h\) in
\({\cal I}_D\) implies
\[
 D/2\le w,w-h\le2D.
\]
If \(3D/2-H_0<h\le3D/2\), the possible \(w\)'s lie in an interval of
length at most \(3D/2-h\le H_0\). The same bound holds for negative
\(h\) after interchanging \(w\) and \(w-h\). There are \(O(H_0)\)
integers \(h\) in the edge. Hence there are \(O(H_0^2)\) ordered
pairs \((h,w)\), and for each pair there are \(O(x/D)\) integers
\(m\). Therefore
\[
 \sum_{3D/2-H_0<|h|\le3D/2}|{\cal B}_1(h)|
 \ll {x\over D}H_0^2(\log x)^2
 =xD(\log x)^{-10-2\eta-\rho},
\]
proving (9). The additional restriction \(w,w-h\le x^{1/2}\) can only
decrease the count.

From (4),
\[
 {T_xH_0\over D}=(\log x)^{\rho/2}\longrightarrow\infty,
\]
so \(D/T_x<H_0\) and \(\omega_1(h)=1\) for \(|h|>H_0\), for all
sufficiently large \(x\). The support interval
\(D/2\le w,w-h\le2D\) gives
\(|h|\le3D/2\). This proves (10).

The least-integer definition (11) and \(H_0<3D/2\) for sufficiently
large \(x\) imply
\[
 H_J=2^JH_0<3D/2<2D.
\]
Also
\[
 J+1\le 2+\log_2\left({3D\over2H_0}\right)
 =2+\left(6+\eta+\rho/2\right)\log_2\log x
 \ll_{\eta,\rho}\log(2T_x),
\]
which proves (12), including the endpoint assertion.

The intervals
\[
 H_j<|h|\le2H_j\qquad(0\le j\le J)
\]
partition the integer shifts with
\(H_0<|h|\le2^{J+1}H_0\). By (10), every nonzero correlation outside
the small range \(|h|\le H_0\) lies in this union. Splitting off the
edge in (9), we obtain
\[
 {\cal R}_1
 =
 \sum_{j=0}^J{\cal S}_j
 +O_{W,\Phi,\alpha,\beta}\left(
 xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta-\rho/2}
 +xD(\log x)^{-10-2\eta-\rho}\right).                  \tag{22}
\]
Here no absolute value was introduced on any middle block; (8)--(9)
were used only for the two discarded sectors. Under TB-SHIFT-BLOCK,
(12) and (22) give
\[
 {\cal R}_1\ll xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta}.
\]
Adding the boundary estimate (5), whose right side is little-oh of the
same target, proves (14). This proves the sufficiency assertion without
claiming TB-SHIFT-BLOCK itself.

glossary.TB-SHIFT-BLOCK: the one-sided uniform dyadic middle-shift estimate sufficient for TB-FEJ-RES
glossary.cal R_s: the centered Fejer residual row at grouped common divisor parameter s
glossary.cal S_j: the signed s=1 dyadic middle-shift block after deleting the paid outer overlap edge

cbbc7f1404df765c.title: LITERAL FACTORABLE-MODULUS GEOMETRY, EXPLICIT CORRECTION PAYMENTS, AND DISJOINT COVERAGE LEDGER FOR THE SYMMETRIC LARGE-FACTOR HC-MED ROW. Fix A>0 and set K=2. Let C=C(A,2)>0 be sufficiently large for fact e3c0786d33d7e576. Fix one orientation, exact active g,c, one complete frozen source block, kappa, and h|rad(kappa) in fact edabb9a0d2959b41. Put X=B/h and assume X is sufficiently large,
cbbc7f1404df765c.author: slava chan
cbbc7f1404df765c.statement:
LITERAL FACTORABLE-MODULUS GEOMETRY, EXPLICIT CORRECTION PAYMENTS, AND DISJOINT COVERAGE LEDGER FOR THE SYMMETRIC LARGE-FACTOR HC-MED ROW. Fix A>0 and set K=2. Let C=C(A,2)>0 be sufficiently large for fact e3c0786d33d7e576. Fix one orientation, exact active g,c, one complete frozen source block, kappa, and h|rad(kappa) in fact edabb9a0d2959b41. Put X=B/h and assume X is sufficiently large,
Q_c=X^(1/2+delta_h),  delta_h>=0,
0<eta<=1/4,  eta<=3/20+6delta_h.                                (1)
Rename the literal descended outer modulus q of that fact as s, so its active dyadic support is Q_c<=s<2Q_c. Restrict to
d<=m, X^eta<=d<=X^(1/4+eta), X<=dm<2X.                           (2)
Fix a selected prime scale P satisfying
X^(2/5+6delta_h)(log X)^(2C)<=P
 <=X^(1/2-3delta_h)(log X)^(-C),                                 (3)
and put c_*=c rad(kappa), cal P={p prime:P<=p<2P}.

A dyadic factor box alpha=(Q_alpha,R_alpha) means that Q_alpha,R_alpha are powers of two at least 2. Define delta_alpha by
Q_alpha R_alpha=X^(1/2+delta_alpha).                              (4)
Call alpha P-admissible if
X^(6delta_alpha)(log X)^C<=R_alpha
 <=X^(1/10-3delta_alpha)(log X)^(-C),                             (5)
Q_alpha X^(2delta_alpha)(log X)^C<=P
 <=X^(1/2-3delta_alpha)(log X)^(-C).                              (6)
Call an active literal modulus s eligible if it has an ordered factorization
s=q_1 r, Q_alpha<=q_1<2Q_alpha, R_alpha<=r<2R_alpha               (7)
in at least one P-admissible box. Fix a total order on all such triples (alpha,q_1,r), choose the first one for each eligible s, and let cal S_alpha be the chosen pairs in box alpha. Put cal S_elig={s:s is eligible} and let N_box be the number of nonempty cal S_alpha.

Then every s in cal S_elig is squarefree,
(s,c_*)=1,                                                       (8)
and
a_s=ell*(kappa h)^(-1) modulo s                                  (9)
is a reduced residue. For every alpha, (q_1,r)->s=q_1 r is injective on cal S_alpha. Moreover
N_box<=(1+log(2Q_c)/log 2)^2.                                    (10)

Apply the symmetric large-factor marking of fact 2ccb8f56e6084b34, writing m=pm' and v=dm'. Partition v into the half-open power-of-two intervals [M_nu,2M_nu) which meet its support. There are at most three such intervals,
M_nu<=2X/P, and P M_nu is comparable to X.                       (11)
Let Vtilde_s^{large}(p,v) be the coefficient in equation (4) of fact 2ccb8f56e6084b34, let
Delta_s(n)=1_{n congruent a_s (mod s)}
 -phi(s)^(-1)1_{(n,s)=1},                                       (12)
and define the actual prime-unit main row
U_s^{main}=sum_{p in cal P,(p,c_*)=1}sum_v
 Vtilde_s^{large}(p,v)Delta_s(pv),                               (13)
where all literal supports in (2) are retained. Let L_proj be the projective norm in (9) of fact 2ccb8f56e6084b34 and put L_W=L_lit C_D C_M as in its pointwise bound. With
L_log=1+log(2XQ_c),                                              (14)
one has
sum_{s in cal S_elig}|U_s^{main}|
 << N_box L_proj X(log X)^(-A)
 +N_box L_W omega_P(c_*)
  [X P^(-1)L_log^3+Q_c sqrt(X/P)L_log^2],                        (15)
where the implied constant depends only on A. The second line is the explicit p|c_* deletion payment. In particular, (3) gives
X/P<=X^(3/5-6delta_h)(log X)^(-2C),                              (16)
Q_c sqrt(X/P)
 <=X^(4/5-2delta_h)(log X)^(-C).                                (17)

Let E_s^{large} be the exact p|m' fractional-Ramare correction in fact 6951622549da0aa4, with the complete literal amplitude and with an additional zero-one restriction to s in cal S_elig. If its retained smooth/literal factor is bounded by L_0, then
sum_{s in cal S_elig}|E_s^{large}|
 <<L_0 L_log^4[Q_c X/P^2+X/P]                                  (18)
 <<L_0 L_log^4[
 X^(7/10-11delta_h)(log X)^(-4C)
 +X^(3/5-6delta_h)(log X)^(-2C)],                               (19)
with absolute implied constants.

For the fixed scale P, the complete literal HC-MED row in (2) is the exact disjoint sum of
LF-ELIG-MARK: s in cal S_elig and omega_P(m)>0;
LF-ELIG-UNMARK: s in cal S_elig and omega_P(m)=0;
LF-NOSCALE: s notin cal S_elig.                                 (20)
On LF-ELIG-MARK, the exact fractional-Ramare identity and the automatic factor 2 of fact 2ccb8f56e6084b34 identify the row with U_s^{main}+E_s^{large}; hence (15) and (18) pay this entire sector. The v-intervals in (11) and the canonical modulus factor boxes are disjoint, so their aggregation introduces no duplicate source term and only the explicit N_box factor in (15). LF-ELIG-UNMARK and LF-NOSCALE are not estimated. HC-SMALL, HC-HIGH, every no-medium-divisor ROUGH sector, other critical complements, the complete HC-MED block, the complete critical tail, and Goldbach are not asserted.
cbbc7f1404df765c.proof:
Fact 8d9feea8c44da2c8 gives the literal descent q t+kappa n=ell, the coefficient mu(q), and pairwise coprimality of c,q,n. Thus a nonzero q-row has squarefree q and (q,c)=(q,ell)=1. Fact edabb9a0d2959b41 proves that a row with (kappa,q)>1 vanishes. On every nonzero retained row, (kappa,q)=1; since h|rad(kappa), also (h,q)=1. After renaming q as s, this proves
(s,c rad(kappa))=1
and shows that ell*(kappa h)^(-1) is a unit modulo s. The same fact gives exactly its centered bracket
1_{dm congruent ell*(kappa h)^(-1) (mod s)}
 -phi(s)^(-1)1_{(dm,s)=1},
which is (12) evaluated at n=dm=pv. This proves (8)-(9) and the literal reduced-residue match.

Every chosen q_1 and r divides the squarefree integer s, so q_1,r are squarefree and coprime. If two chosen pairs in one cal S_alpha have the same product s, the fixed total-order rule says both must be the unique first triple attached to s, hence they are equal. Therefore the product map is injective. A nonempty box has Q_alpha<=q_1<s<2Q_c and R_alpha<=r<s<2Q_c. There are at most 1+log(2Q_c)/log 2 possible power-of-two values for each of Q_alpha,R_alpha, proving (10).

On the support (2), p in [P,2P), and v=dm/p. Hence
X/(2P)<v<2X/P.                                                   (21)
A positive interval whose endpoint ratio is four meets at most three consecutive half-open intervals [2^j,2^(j+1)); this proves the first assertion of (11), and every active left endpoint satisfies M_nu<=2X/P. Equation (21) also proves P M_nu is bounded above and below by fixed positive multiples of X.

Fix alpha and nu. By (4)-(7), the parameters X,Q_alpha,R_alpha,P,M_nu satisfy every scale hypothesis of fact e3c0786d33d7e576, with K=2 and with C=C(A,2) chosen sufficiently large before (3)-(6). Equations (8)-(9) give its squarefree, modulus-coprimality and unit-residue hypotheses, and the canonical choice gives injectivity. Multiplying the cofactor modes of fact 2ccb8f56e6084b34 by 1_{M_nu<=v<2M_nu} preserves their divisor bounds, absolute convergence, prime-side Siegel-Walfisz property, projective norm L_proj, and reconstructed pointwise bound L_W tau(v). Therefore fact e3c0786d33d7e576 applies to this alpha,nu block.

Its Type-II contribution is bounded by a constant depending on A times L_proj X(log X)^(-A). Its prime-unit comparison costs
L_W omega_P(c_*)[
 M_nu(1+log(2M_nu Q_alpha R_alpha))^3
 +Q_alpha R_alpha sqrt(M_nu)
  (1+log(2M_nu Q_alpha R_alpha))^2]                              (22)
up to a constant depending only on A. If cal S_alpha is nonempty, a chosen product s lies in both [Q_c,2Q_c) and
[Q_alpha R_alpha,4Q_alpha R_alpha). Hence
Q_alpha R_alpha<=2Q_c.                                          (23)
Using (11), (14), and (23) in (22), summing the at most three nu and at most N_box boxes, and enlarging the constant gives (15). Taking reciprocals and square roots in the lower bound in (3), and using Q_c=X^(1/2+delta_h), proves (16)-(17).

Fact 6951622549da0aa4 assumes exactly delta_h>=0, 0<eta<=1/4, the two bounds (3), and a set of distinct squarefree moduli in [Q_c,4Q_c), coprime to c_*, with unit residues. The present eligible set lies in [Q_c,2Q_c) and has all those properties by (8)-(9). Its coefficient may be multiplied by the indicator s in cal S_elig; this only deletes terms and preserves the bound L_0. That fact gives (18), and its displayed exponent calculation is exactly (19).

For every original pair (s,m), exactly one of s in cal S_elig or s notin cal S_elig holds. In the first case exactly one of omega_P(m)>0 or omega_P(m)=0 holds. Thus (20) is disjoint and exhaustive. On its marked member, fact e59f666ecac4d4cb gives the exact fractional-Ramare main-plus-correction identity. Fact 2ccb8f56e6084b34 proves that on (2) every selected p exceeds d, so d<m and the fundamental-domain multiplicity is exactly 2; this cancels the main coefficient -1/2 and identifies the already-folded main term with (13). The same predecessor and fact 6951622549da0aa4 identify the remaining p|m' term with E_s^{large}. Consequently (15) plus (18) pays all of LF-ELIG-MARK. The half-open v partition is unique for each v, and the canonical factor rule selects one pair for each eligible s, proving the boundary and no-duplication assertion. None of the cited estimates treats either complementary member of (20) or a different HC region, so the final exclusions follow.

glossary.E_s^{large}: The exact p-dividing-m-prime-cofactor correction on the literal large-factor row.
glossary.LF-ELIG-MARK: The literal symmetric large-factor HC-MED sector with eligible outer modulus and omega_P(m)>0.
glossary.LF-ELIG-UNMARK: The eligible-modulus HC-MED complement with omega_P(m)=0.
glossary.LF-NOSCALE: The HC-MED complement whose outer modulus has no P-admissible canonical factorization.
glossary.M_nu: The left endpoint of one half-open dyadic cofactor interval for v.
glossary.N_box: The number of nonempty P-admissible canonical dyadic factor boxes.
glossary.Q_alpha: The first dyadic factor scale in the box alpha.
glossary.R_alpha: The convenient-divisor dyadic scale in the box alpha.
glossary.U_s^{main}: The actual prime-unit already-folded large-factor main row at literal modulus s.
glossary.cal S_alpha: The injective family of canonically selected factor pairs in the dyadic box alpha.
glossary.cal S_elig: The set of literal descended moduli having a canonically selected P-admissible convenient-divisor factorization.
glossary.delta_alpha: The exact exponent defined by Q_alpha R_alpha=X^(1/2+delta_alpha).

cbfebc160d4bc310.title: POST-B BUFFER RESIDUAL LEDGER AND THE NEW FIRST OPEN C1 CELL. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, fix 0<eta<sigma and omega>0, and define
cbfebc160d4bc310.author: slava chan
cbfebc160d4bc310.statement:
POST-B BUFFER RESIDUAL LEDGER AND THE NEW FIRST OPEN C1 CELL. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, fix 0<eta<sigma and omega>0, and define
beta_0=6/5-2kappa, beta_1=6/5-3sigma, beta_m=6/5-12sigma/5,
Gamma_BC(beta)=max(0,(19beta-20)/17).
Use exactly the literal paired nonzero-Poisson forced-high source, physical balance hypotheses, exact outer-gcd normalization, forward/reverse conventions, original parent labels, normalized anatomy partition, and provenance coordinates of facts aeffec374578707c and 771d292cffc890c1. Thus Q>1, beta is the normalized exponent, G is the actual normalized imbalance, and beta_orig is retained separately from beta.

Within the standard-marker post-low range beta_0<beta<beta_m, after removing the power-small families proved in facts 15425579cb248eff, 24e911b7685090c1 and 771d292cffc890c1, the complete still-unestimated ledger is the following disjoint union:
(I) beta_0<beta<=beta_1, orientation in {forward,reverse}, parent in {C91,U_sh,U_low}, anatomy in {C1,C2,C3}, and
Q^(-sigma+eta)<=G<Q^(Gamma_BC(beta)+omega);
(II) beta_1<beta<beta_m, the same orientation, parent and G ranges, and anatomy in {A,B,C1,C2,C3}.
All source, high, fixed-U, smooth/projective, Fourier, target-gcd, prime-order, collision, deletion, parent, orientation and exact outer-gcd coordinates remain in this Cartesian refinement. The later sliver beta_m<=beta<6/5 retains the separate general normalized anatomy ledger of fact 15425579cb248eff and is not altered here.

The infimum of normalized-beta values in this ledger is beta_0, and a structurally nonempty cell occurs in every sufficiently short right-neighborhood of beta_0 with forward orientation, parent U_low, anatomy C1 and G=1. Consequently, after anatomies A and B are paid through beta_1, one new first open standard-marker cell is
(parent,anatomy,beta,G)=(U_low,C1,beta_0+,1).
This is an exact coverage/no-fit ledger. It gives no estimate for C1,C2,C3, for A or B above beta_1, for the later general-anatomy sliver, endpoints, PMD, logical bad-N capture or Goldbach.
cbfebc160d4bc310.proof:
Fact aeffec374578707c gives, in beta_0<beta<=beta_1, the exact disjoint residual anatomy list {B,C1,C2,C3} with every other displayed coordinate unchanged. Fact 771d292cffc890c1 proves that the complete B coordinate in this slab is power-small for both orientations, every actual G and every exact outer gcd, without deleting any B atom. Removing that coordinate therefore leaves exactly {C1,C2,C3}, proving family (I). Neither 24e911b7685090c1 nor 771d292cffc890c1 estimates beta>beta_1, so family (II) remains the {A,B,C1,C2,C3} family of aeffec374578707c. The G, parent, orientation and provenance coordinates do not change because both removals are by anatomy and beta selectors. The separate later sliver is exactly the one in fact 15425579cb248eff.

We prove structural nonemptiness of the C1 cell. Fix beta_* with
beta_0<beta_*<beta_1.
For sufficiently large T put Q=T and use the prime-in-(y,2y) theorem recorded in fact b7fcb27a091203e5 to choose three distinct odd primes d,s,p on respective scales
T, T^(beta_*-1), T.
Put
r=sp.                                                               (1)
The standard cutoffs are
L=T^(beta_*-1+sigma),
S_0=T^(2beta_*-2+3sigma),
Z=T^(3/2-beta_*-3sigma).                                            (2)
Because sigma>0, the scale of s is smaller than L by the fixed factor T^sigma. Also
1-(3/2-beta_*-3sigma)=beta_*-1/2+3sigma>0,
so the scale of p is larger than Z by a fixed power. Finally
(2beta_*-2+3sigma)-(beta_*-1)=beta_*-1+3sigma>0,
so s<S_0 for large T. Therefore r has no prime divisor in (L,Z),
v_L(r)=s<=S_0,
and its remaining factor is the single prime p>=Z. By the mutually exclusive alternative C1 of fact 6414b11506a84ff0, r has anatomy C1. Equation (1) gives r=T^(beta_*+o(1)).

Insert this r into the accepted square-root-balanced structural source construction in Part (E) of fact 15425579cb248eff. Namely put m=d, choose a fixed constant c>1 in the positive source-weight region used there, choose an odd positive integer
k=c d^2/r+O(1),
put N=dm+rk and x=N/2, and use the active dyadic labels around d,m,r,k. Then N is even after choosing the odd representative k, DM and RK are comparable to x, g=gcd(d,r)=1, Q=T^(1+o(1)), normalized beta is beta_*+o(1), and the equal D,M normalization gives G=1.

The proof of Part (E) of fact 15425579cb248eff depends on the scale exponents of d,m,r,k and on the distinctness and squarefreeness of d and r, not on whether the factor of r at exponent beta_*-1 lies just below or just above L. Those scale exponents are unchanged here. Hence the forced-high, 60-residual, outside-C91 and deep-scale predicates proved there remain valid, and the frozen parent is U_low. The only altered coordinate is the normalized anatomy, which the preceding paragraph proved is C1.

The exponent beta_* may be chosen in every sufficiently short right-neighborhood of beta_0 contained in (beta_0,beta_1). All beta<=beta_0 cells are power-small by fact 15425579cb248eff. Existing buffer facts 24e911b7685090c1 and 771d292cffc890c1 pay only A and B. The fixed-g estimate does not pay the constructed cell because beta_*>20/19 gives Gamma_BC(beta_*)>0 while G=1. Thus the infimum of the remaining ledger is beta_0 and (U_low,C1,beta_0+,1) is structurally first. No signed lower bound or C1 estimate is asserted.

glossary.C1: The standard one-rough-prime anatomy with v_L(r)<=S_0 and exactly one prime factor at least Z.
glossary.beta_*: A fixed normalized exponent strictly between beta_0 and beta_1 used in the structural C1 construction.

cd13b5e0a78656f1.title: P-qSRC-LOWF: COMPLETE PRINCIPAL-SOURCE PAYMENT BY THE FIRST MARKED-DILATOR MOMENT TERM
cd13b5e0a78656f1.author: slava chan
cd13b5e0a78656f1.statement:
P-qSRC-LOWF: COMPLETE PRINCIPAL-SOURCE PAYMENT BY THE FIRST MARKED-DILATOR MOMENT TERM.

Adopt the Dcal>Q^2 hard good-W block and exact split
H_C=P-qSRC+C-qSRC>=2
from fact e9e9563501147a1a. Assume in addition
1<=F<=Q.                                                        (1)
Then the complete principal source satisfies
|P-qSRC|
 <=x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 BQF.                                    (P-qSRC-LOWF)
Consequently, on (1), the single centered estimate
|C-qSRC>=2|
 <=x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 BQ^2F^2/Dcal                            (2)
would imply
|H_C|
 <=x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2
   (BQF+BQ^2F^2/Dcal).                                         (3)
Thus in the low-frequency large-dilator chamber the principal source is already paid at the complete two-term marked-dilator moment scale; it need not satisfy the stronger isolated second-term estimate P-qSRC-SUP.

This theorem proves no estimate for C-qSRC>=2, no bound for P-qSRC when F>Q, no full GA-RAY-SPEC, no tail payment, and no Goldbach conclusion.
cd13b5e0a78656f1.proof:
Fact 764588e99974a6d9 proves, for every exact selector on the good-W principal source,
|P-qSRC|<=x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2BF^2.                              (4)
This applies to the complete Dcal>Q^2 principal source in fact e9e9563501147a1a because its hard conditions are retained selectors. Under F<=Q,
BF^2<=BQF.                                                       (5)
Equations (4)-(5) prove P-qSRC-LOWF.

The exact decomposition in fact e9e9563501147a1a gives
|H_C|<=|P-qSRC|+|C-qSRC>=2|.
Insert P-qSRC-LOWF and the conditional estimate (2) to obtain (3). The two terms in (3) are exactly the two numerical terms in the marked-dilator moment target of fact e55b27d39c593164. This argument charges the principal source to the first term; it does not assert the isolated second-term estimate P-qSRC-SUP. All limitations follow.

glossary.P-qSRC-LOWF: The payment of the complete large-dilator principal source by the BQF term when F<=Q.

cd8d7d0fe163be6e.title: Fix real constants \(C>0\) and \(\delta>0\). Let \(x\ge3\), let \(N\) be a positive even integer, and let \(d_1\ne d_2\) be positive integers satisfying
cd8d7d0fe163be6e.author: slava chan
cd8d7d0fe163be6e.statement:
Fix real constants \(C>0\) and \(\delta>0\). Let \(x\ge3\), let \(N\) be a positive even integer, and let \(d_1\ne d_2\) be positive integers satisfying
\[
 N,d_1,d_2,|d_1-d_2|\le x^C,\qquad
 \mu(d_1)\mu(d_2)\ne0,\qquad (d_1d_2,N)=1.
\]
Let \(P_1,P_2\) be real numbers with
\[
 x^\delta\le P_1,P_2\le x^C.
\]
Put
\[
 R_N=\prod_{p\mid N}\left(1-\frac1p\right)^{-1}.
\]
For positive integers \(q_1,q_2\), put \(c=[q_1,q_2]\), and define
\[
\begin{split}
 {\cal K}_N(d_1,d_2;P_1,P_2)
 =\sum_{q_1,q_2\ge1}&
 \frac{\mu(q_1)\mu(q_2)}{[q_1,q_2]}
 \log(P_1/q_1)_+\log(P_2/q_2)_+\\
 &\times{\bf1}_{(N,[q_1,q_2])=1}
 {\bf1}_{(q_1,d_1)=1}{\bf1}_{(q_2,d_2)=1}
 {\bf1}_{(q_1,q_2)\mid(d_1-d_2)} .
\end{split}                                                   \tag{1}
\]
Here \(y_+=\max(y,0)\). Let \(\mathfrak S_N(d_1,d_2)\) be the two-affine-form singular series of fact \(b164cd7d1e02e173\). Then, for every \(A>0\),
\[
 \boxed{
 {\cal K}_N(d_1,d_2;P_1,P_2)
 =R_N\mathfrak S_N(d_1,d_2)+O_{A,C,\delta}((\log x)^{-A}).
 }                                                               \tag{2}
\]
The error is uniform in every displayed parameter. Moreover
\[
 R_N\ll_C(\log x)^{C_0}                                         \tag{3}
\]
for an absolute constant \(C_0\). Thus multiplication by \(R_N\) preserves every arbitrary-logarithmic saving in a signed \(d_1,d_2\) aggregate.
cd8d7d0fe163be6e.proof:
For \(\Re s,\Re t>0\), define
\[
 {\cal F}(s,t)=
 \sum_{q_1,q_2\ge1}
 \frac{\mu(q_1)\mu(q_2)}{[q_1,q_2]q_1^sq_2^t}
 {\bf1}_{(N,[q_1,q_2])=1}
 {\bf1}_{(q_1,d_1)=1}{\bf1}_{(q_2,d_2)=1}
 {\bf1}_{(q_1,q_2)\mid(d_1-d_2)} .                       \tag{4}
\]
Absolute convergence follows in this half-plane from the Euler factors below. Put
\[
 u=p^{-1-s},\qquad v=p^{-1-t}.
\]
Because the Möbius factors restrict both local exponents to zero or one, the local factor \({\cal F}_p\) is
\[
\begin{split}
 1&-{\bf1}_{p\nmid Nd_1}u-{\bf1}_{p\nmid Nd_2}v\\
 &+{\bf1}_{p\nmid Nd_1d_2}{\bf1}_{p\mid(d_1-d_2)}\,p\,uv. \tag{5}
\end{split}
\]
Indeed a prime present in both \(q_1,q_2\) occurs only once in their least common multiple, which explains the factor \(p\,uv\).

Extract two inverse-zeta factors:
\[
 {\cal F}(s,t)=\zeta(1+s)^{-1}\zeta(1+t)^{-1}
 {\cal H}_{N,d_1,d_2}(s,t),                              \tag{6}
\]
where
\[
 {\cal H}_{N,d_1,d_2,p}(s,t)
 =\frac{{\cal F}_p(s,t)}{(1-u)(1-v)}.                    \tag{7}
\]
We first evaluate (7) at the origin. Let
\(\nu_p=\nu_p(N;d_1,d_2)\) be the number of roots modulo \(p\) of
\((N-d_1m)(N-d_2m)\), as in fact \(b164cd7d1e02e173\).
If \(p\nmid N\), the four cases in the proof of that fact and (5) give
\[
 {\cal F}_p(0,0)=1-\frac{\nu_p}{p}.                      \tag{8}
\]
For example, two distinct roots give \(1-2/p\); a common root gives
\(1-2/p+1/p=1-1/p\); one available root gives \(1-1/p\);
and no root gives one. If \(p\mid N\), the coprimality condition in
(4) gives \({\cal F}_p=1\). Since \((d_1d_2,N)=1\), the two roots then
coincide at \(m=0\), so \(\nu_p=1\). Therefore (7), (8), and the
definition of the singular series give
\[
 {\cal H}_{N,d_1,d_2}(0,0)
 =\prod_{p\mid N}(1-1/p)^{-1}\mathfrak S_N(d_1,d_2)
 =R_N\mathfrak S_N(d_1,d_2).                            \tag{9}
\]

We now justify the uniform logarithmic truncation in (2). Write
\[
 {\cal H}_{N,d_1,d_2}(s,t)
 =\sum_{r_1,r_2\ge1}\frac{h(r_1,r_2)}{r_1^sr_2^t}.       \tag{10}
\]
The local coefficients are explicit. Away from primes dividing
\(N d_1d_2(d_1-d_2)\), one has
\[
 {\cal H}_p=1-\frac{uv}{(1-u)(1-v)},                    \tag{11}
\]
so \(h(p^a,p^b)=-p^{-a-b}\) for \(a,b\ge1\), and the other nonconstant
local coefficients vanish. At an exceptional prime, (5) shows that the
local factor is one of
\[
 \frac1{(1-u)(1-v)},\qquad \frac1{1-u},\qquad
 \frac1{1-v},\qquad
 1+\frac{(p-1)uv}{(1-u)(1-v)}.                          \tag{12}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \sum_{r_1,r_2}|h(r_1,r_2)|
 \ll \prod_{p\mid Nd_1d_2(d_1-d_2)}(1-1/p)^{-2}
 \ll_C(\log x)^{C_1}.                                   \tag{13}
\]
For the last bound, list the exceptional primes increasingly. The
\(j\)-th is at least \(j+1\), while their product is at most
\(x^{4C}\); summing the logarithms of the local factors gives
\(O_C(\log\log x)\). The generic-prime product converges because its
local excess is \(O(p^{-2})\).

We also need tails. For each fixed \(L>0\), put
\[
 \theta=\frac{L\log\log x}{\log x}.
\]
For sufficiently large \(x\), the same local calculation, with
\(p^{-1}\) replaced by \(p^{-1+\theta}\), gives
\[
 \sum_{r_1,r_2}|h(r_1,r_2)|(r_1r_2)^\theta
 \ll_{C,L}(\log x)^{C_2}.                               \tag{14}
\]
Here \(C_2\) is absolute: among sets of primes having product at most a
fixed power of \(x\), the sum of \(p^{-1+\theta}\) is maximized, up to a
bounded factor, by the smallest primes; on those primes
\(p^\theta=1+o_L(1)\). Primes larger than a fixed power of \(\log x\)
contribute a bounded amount because their number is at most
\(O_C(\log x/\log\log x)\). The generic local excess remains
\(O(p^{-2+2\theta})\), whose sum converges. Rankin's inequality applied
to (14) shows that for every \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(B>0\),
\[
 \sum_{\max(r_1,r_2)>x^\varepsilon}|h(r_1,r_2)|
 \ll_{B,C,\varepsilon}(\log x)^{-B},                    \tag{15}
\]
after choosing \(L\) sufficiently large.

Define
\[
 V(X)=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\mu(n)}n\log(X/n)_+.
\]
The classical summatory-Möbius estimate reproduced in fact
\(71389b22e6f49e13\), followed by partial summation, gives uniformly for
\(X\ge x^\varepsilon\)
\[
 V(X)=1+O_{J,\varepsilon}((\log x)^{-J})                 \tag{16}
\]
for every \(J>0\), and trivially \(|V(X)|\ll\log^2(2X)\) for \(X\ge1\).
For completeness, the constant in (16) is one because
\[
 \sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\mu(n)}n=0,\qquad
 \sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\mu(n)\log n}{n}=-1.
\]
These identities follow by letting \(s\downarrow1\) in
\(\sum\mu(n)n^{-s}=1/\zeta(s)\), using the simple pole of \(\zeta(s)\)
with residue one; the strong summatory-Möbius bound just cited justifies
partial summation and passage to the limit. Its exponential
\(\exp(-c\sqrt{\log X})\) remainder is stronger than (16).

Coefficient convolution in (6) and the definition of the positive-part
logarithms give the exact identity
\[
 {\cal K}_N(d_1,d_2;P_1,P_2)
 =\sum_{r_1,r_2\ge1}h(r_1,r_2)
 V(P_1/r_1)V(P_2/r_2).                                  \tag{17}
\]
Take \(\varepsilon=\delta/2\). On
\(r_i\le x^\varepsilon\), both arguments in (17) are at least
\(x^{\delta/2}\), so (16) and (13), with \(J\) chosen after \(A\),
replace both factors by one with error \(O((\log x)^{-A})\).
The complementary range is \(O((\log x)^{-A})\) by (15) and the trivial
bound for \(V\), again choosing the tail exponent after \(A\).
Thus (17) equals
\[
 \sum_{r_1,r_2}h(r_1,r_2)+O((\log x)^{-A})
 ={\cal H}_{N,d_1,d_2}(0,0)+O((\log x)^{-A}).
\]
Equation (9) proves (2).

Finally, the same increasing-prime argument used in (13) gives
\[
 R_N=\prod_{p\mid N}(1-1/p)^{-1}\ll_C(\log x)^{C_0},
\]
proving (3).

glossary.R_N: the fixed-center Euler multiplier product over primes dividing N of (1-1/p)^(-1)
glossary.V(X): the one-variable inverse-zeta logarithmic kernel sum over n of mu(n)n^(-1)log(X/n)_+
glossary.cal H_{N,d_1,d_2}(s,t): the bivariate Euler product remaining after extracting the two inverse-zeta factors
glossary.cal K_N(d_1,d_2;P_1,P_2): the complete two-variable logarithmic sieve convolution with lcm density

cdb5cefbc7333591.title: Let x≥2 be real with N=2x an integer. Fix real numbers 1/2<a<b<1, a real function W supported in [a,b], a real function ψ on the positive reals satisfying ψ(u)=0 for 0<u≤1, a real number D_* with 1≤D_*≤x, and a real function Φ supported in [1/2,2] such that Σ_{j∈Z}Φ(t/2^j)=1 for every t>0. Define
cdb5cefbc7333591.author: slava chan
cdb5cefbc7333591.statement:
Let x≥2 be real with N=2x an integer. Fix real numbers 1/2<a<b<1, a real function W supported in [a,b], a real function ψ on the positive reals satisfying ψ(u)=0 for 0<u≤1, a real number D_* with 1≤D_*≤x, and a real function Φ supported in [1/2,2] such that Σ_{j∈Z}Φ(t/2^j)=1 for every t>0. Define
H_{N,W,ψ}=Σ_{d,m≥1} μ(d)log(m) W(dm/x)ψ(d/D_*)Λ(N-dm).
For positive dyadic numbers D,M,R,K, define
Q_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;R,K)=Σ_{d,m,r,k≥1; dm+rk=N} μ(d)μ(r)log(m)log(k)W(dm/x)ψ(d/D_*)Φ(d/D)Φ(m/M)Φ(r/R)Φ(k/K).
Then
H_{N,W,ψ}=Σ_{D,M,R,K}Q_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;R,K),
where all four outer sums run over positive dyadic numbers. This identity is exact. Every block is real and retains both Möbius signs. A nonzero block satisfies D>D_*/2, ax/4≤DM≤4bx, and (2-b)x/4≤RK≤4(2-a)x. Moreover at most L_x=(ceil(log_2 x)+4)^4 dyadic quadruples have nonzero blocks.
cdb5cefbc7333591.proof:
First prove the divisor identity Λ(n)=Σ_{rk=n}μ(r)log k for every positive integer n. For n=1 both sides are zero. Let n>1 and let P be the set of distinct prime divisors of n. A divisor r with μ(r)≠0 corresponds to a subset S of P and has μ(r)=(-1)^{|S|}. Thus
Σ_{r|n}μ(r)log(n/r)=Σ_{S⊆P}(-1)^{|S|}(log n-Σ_{p∈S}log p).
The coefficient of log n is (1-1)^{|P|}=0. For a fixed p∈P, the coefficient of log p is -Σ_{S⊆P,p∈S}(-1)^{|S|}=Σ_{T⊆P\{p}}(-1)^{|T|}, which equals 1 if |P|=1 and 0 if |P|≥2. Therefore the divisor sum is log p when n is a positive power of one prime p, and is zero when n has at least two distinct prime divisors. This is exactly Λ(n).

The support condition on W implies ax≤dm≤bx. Since N=2x, q=N-dm satisfies (2-b)x≤q≤(2-a)x and is positive. Apply the proved divisor identity to q to obtain
H_{N,W,ψ}=Σ_{d,m,r,k≥1;dm+rk=N}μ(d)μ(r)log(m)log(k)W(dm/x)ψ(d/D_*).
For every positive integer t, the assumed partition identity gives Σ_{U dyadic}Φ(t/U)=1. Insert this identity separately for t=d,m,r,k. All sums are finite on the support, so their order may be interchanged. The resulting inner sum is precisely Q_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;R,K), proving the exact decomposition. Every factor in a block is real, so every block is real, and the displayed definition shows that μ(d) and μ(r) are unchanged.

If ψ(d/D_*) is nonzero, then d/D_*>1, so d>D_*. If Φ(d/D) is nonzero, then 1/2≤d/D≤2, hence D≥d/2>D_*/2. Similarly, nonzero Φ(d/D)Φ(m/M) implies dm/4≤DM≤4dm. Combining this with ax≤dm≤bx gives ax/4≤DM≤4bx. The identical argument applied to r,k and (2-b)x≤rk≤(2-a)x gives (2-b)x/4≤RK≤4(2-a)x.

It remains to count labels. The inequalities ax≤dm≤bx<x imply d,m≤x. Also rk=N-dm<2x, so r,k<2x. If 1≤t<2x and Φ(t/U) is nonzero, then t/2≤U≤2t, hence 1/2≤U<4x. A dyadic U=2^j in [1/2,4x] has -1≤j≤ceil(log_2(4x)), giving at most ceil(log_2(4x))+2=ceil(log_2 x)+4 possibilities. Applying this upper bound independently to D,M,R,K gives at most L_x=(ceil(log_2 x)+4)^4 quadruples.

glossary.H_{N,W,ψ}: the smooth reflected Möbius source defined in the statement
glossary.L_x: the explicit upper bound (ceil(log_2 x)+4)^4 for the number of nonzero dyadic quadruples
glossary.Q_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;R,K): the four-parameter dyadic block defined in the statement
glossary.Φ: a real dyadic partition function supported in [1/2,2]

ce5de84556b212d9.title: SIMULTANEOUS TWO-ROW COMPLETE GRAM SPECTRUM. Let p>2 be prime and let c be a nonzero residue modulo p. For t modulo p write
ce5de84556b212d9.author: slava chan
ce5de84556b212d9.statement:
SIMULTANEOUS TWO-ROW COMPLETE GRAM SPECTRUM. Let p>2 be prime and let c be a nonzero residue modulo p. For t modulo p write
\[
c_p(t)=\sum_{x\in\mathbb F_p^\times}e_p(tx),
\]
and, on \((\mathbb F_p^\times)^2\), put
\[
G_c(x,y)={p\over p-1}\left({\bf1}_{y=cx}-{1\over p-1}\right).
\]
Define its unnormalised additive Fourier transform by
\[
\widehat G_c(r,s)=\sum_{x,y\in\mathbb F_p^\times}G_c(x,y)e_p(rx+sy).
\]
Then
\[
\widehat G_c(r,s)={p\over p-1}\left(c_p(r+cs)-{c_p(r)c_p(s)\over p-1}\right). \tag{1}
\]
It vanishes whenever r=0 or s=0. If r,s are nonzero, then
\[
\widehat G_c(r,s)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle {p^2(p-2)\over (p-1)^2},&r+cs=0,\\[3pt]
\displaystyle -{p^2\over (p-1)^2},&r+cs\ne0.
\end{cases} \tag{2}
\]
Now let d_1,d_2 be squarefree positive integers, both coprime to p. Let C_1,C_2 be integers with \((C_i,d_i)=1\), and let t_1,t_2 be integers. Define
\[
\begin{split}
\mathcal T(t_1,t_2)=
\sum_{\substack{x\ ({\rm mod}\ pd_1)\\(x,pd_1)=1}}
\sum_{\substack{y\ ({\rm mod}\ pd_2)\\(y,pd_2)=1}}
&G_c(x\bmod p,y\bmod p)e_{d_1}(C_1x^{-1})e_{d_2}(C_2y^{-1})\\
&\times e_{pd_1}(t_1x)e_{pd_2}(t_2y).
\end{split} \tag{3}
\]
If \(r_i\equiv t_i d_i^{-1}\pmod p\), and \(\bar p_i\) denotes the inverse of p modulo d_i, then
\[
\mathcal T(t_1,t_2)=
\widehat G_c(r_1,r_2)
S(t_1\bar p_1,C_1;d_1)S(t_2\bar p_2,C_2;d_2). \tag{4}
\]
Consequently \(\mathcal T=0\) if either \(r_i=0\). For every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
|\mathcal T(t_1,t_2)|\ll_\varepsilon
(d_1d_2)^{1/2+\varepsilon}
\begin{cases}
p,&r_1+cr_2=0,\\
1,&r_1+cr_2\ne0.
\end{cases} \tag{5}
\]
In the literal J_2 Gram kernel of fact b9560e346963b9e0, after all variables other than the two unit residues u_1,u_2 are fixed, \(G_p(A,D)\) is exactly \(G_c(u_1,u_2)\) with \(c\equiv s_1q_2^{-1}\pmod p\). For a fixed pair of additive divisors d_i with q_2=d_2k_2 and s_1=d_1k_1, the signed inverse phases are
\[
e_{d_1}(N[pau_1k_1]^{-1}),\qquad
e_{d_2}(-N[pau_2k_2]^{-1}).
\]
Thus (3)--(5) apply with
\[
C_1\equiv N[pa k_1]^{-1}\pmod {d_1},\qquad
C_2\equiv-N[pa k_2]^{-1}\pmod {d_2}.
\]
The support conditions make these coefficients units modulo d_i and make \((p,d_i)=1\). This statement is a complete-sum identity and bound only; it asserts no incomplete/source-weighted aggregate estimate.
ce5de84556b212d9.proof:
For (1), sum first on the diagonal y=cx and then on the constant subtraction:
\[
\widehat G_c(r,s)={p\over p-1}\left(\sum_{x\ne0}e_p((r+cs)x)
-{1\over p-1}\sum_{x\ne0}e_p(rx)\sum_{y\ne0}e_p(sy)\right).
\]
This is (1). The elementary Ramanujan-sum values are \(c_p(0)=p-1\) and \(c_p(t)=-1\) for \(t\ne0\). If r=0 and s is nonzero, then r+cs is nonzero, so the expression in parentheses is zero. The case s=0 is identical, including r=s=0. If r,s are nonzero and r+cs=0, the expression in parentheses is
\[
(p-1)-{1\over p-1}={p(p-2)\over p-1};
\]
multiplication by p/(p-1) gives the first value in (2). If r,s,r+cs are all nonzero, the expression is
\[
-1-{1\over p-1}=-{p\over p-1},
\]
which gives the second value.

For (4), use the Chinese remainder theorem separately in each variable. The additive character modulo \(pd_i\) factors as
\[
e_{pd_i}(t_ix)=e_p(t_id_i^{-1}x)e_{d_i}(t_i\bar p_i x).
\]
The Gram factor depends only on the two p-components, while the inverse phases depend only on the corresponding d_i-components. Therefore the p-component sum is exactly \(\widehat G_c(r_1,r_2)\), and the d_i-component sum is
\[
\sum_{z\ ({\rm mod}\ d_i)}^{*}e_{d_i}(t_i\bar p_i z+C_i z^{-1})
=S(t_i\bar p_i,C_i;d_i).
\]
This proves (4). The signed squarefree-modulus completion and estimate in fact d9c3f37492846fce, applied with coefficient C_i, gives explicitly
\[
|S(t_i\bar p_i,C_i;d_i)|\le 2^{\omega(d_i)}\sqrt {d_i}
\ll_\varepsilon d_i^{1/2+\varepsilon},
\]
because d_i is squarefree and C_i is a unit modulo d_i. The two nonzero values in (2) have absolute value respectively less than p and at most 9/4 for p>2. This proves (5).

For the literal application, fact b9560e346963b9e0 defines the centered kernel
\[
G_p(A,D)={p\over p-1}\left({\bf1}_{A=D}-{1\over p-1}\right).
\]
On its support, A=D is equivalent to \(u_2=(s_1q_2^{-1})u_1\pmod p\), hence this is G_c with the displayed c. Fact 75432ab3881c2178 proves the exact row-one expansion and the analogous row-two expansion with conjugation: for q_2=d_2k_2 and s_1=d_1k_1 their phases are precisely
\[
e_{d_1}(N[pau_1k_1]^{-1}),\qquad
e_{d_2}(-N[pau_2k_2]^{-1}).
\]
That fact also records the squarefreeness and support coprimalities ensuring \((p,d_i)=1\) and that \(N[pa k_i]^{-1}\) is a unit modulo d_i. Factoring the fixed constants from the inverses gives the stated C_1,C_2 and identifies the fixed literal subface with (3), including the minus sign caused by row-two conjugation.

glossary.C_i: The fixed unit coefficient of the inverse phase modulo d_i.
glossary.G_c: The centered incidence kernel of the line y=cx in the unit square modulo p.
glossary.\\bar p_i: The inverse of p modulo d_i.
glossary.\\mathcal T: The simultaneous two-row complete sum in equation (3).
glossary.\\omega: The number of distinct prime divisors.
glossary.\\widehat G_c: The unnormalised two-dimensional additive Fourier transform of G_c.
glossary.c_p: The prime Ramanujan sum over nonzero residues.
glossary.r_i: The residue t_i d_i^{-1} modulo p.
glossary.t_i: The additive Fourier frequency for the i-th completed row.

cf6e2f624d3b1a82.title: ENVELOPE-WEIGHTED COMMON-HILBERT RECONSTRUCTION. Let \(\mathscr A\) be a finite nonempty set, let \(E_\alpha>0\) for every \(\alpha\in\mathscr A\), and put
cf6e2f624d3b1a82.author: slava chan
cf6e2f624d3b1a82.statement:
ENVELOPE-WEIGHTED COMMON-HILBERT RECONSTRUCTION. Let \(\mathscr A\) be a finite nonempty set, let \(E_\alpha>0\) for every \(\alpha\in\mathscr A\), and put
\[
 \mathcal E=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathscr A}E_\alpha.
\]
Let \(X\) be a positive integer and, for \(1\le n\le X\), let \(V_n=(V_n(\alpha))_{\alpha\in\mathscr A}\) be a complex vector satisfying
\[
 |V_n(\alpha)|\le Z E_\alpha \tag{1}
\]
for a fixed real \(Z\ge0\). In \(\ell^2(\mathscr A)\), with inner product linear in the first variable, define
\[
 U_n(\alpha)=\frac{V_n(\alpha)}{\sqrt{E_\alpha}},
 \qquad r(\alpha)=\sqrt{E_\alpha}. \tag{2}
\]
Then
\[
 \sum_{\alpha\in\mathscr A}V_n(\alpha)=\langle U_n,r\rangle, \tag{3}
\]
\[
 \|r\|_2=\mathcal E^{1/2},\qquad
