 \sup_{1\le n\le X}\|U_n\|_2\le Z\mathcal E^{1/2}, \tag{4}
\]
and therefore, for arbitrary complex scalars \(a_1,\ldots,a_X\),
\[
 \left|\sum_{n\le X}a_n\sum_{\alpha\in\mathscr A}V_n(\alpha)\right|
 \le \mathcal E^{1/2}
 \left\|\sum_{n\le X}a_nU_n\right\|_2. \tag{5}
\]
For every \(m\) and every positive integers \(a,b\) for which \(am,bm\le X\), the exact same-coordinate correlation in the weighted coordinates is
\[
 \langle U_{am},U_{bm}\rangle
 =\sum_{\alpha\in\mathscr A}
 \frac{V_{am}(\alpha)\overline{V_{bm}(\alpha)}}{E_\alpha}. \tag{6}
\]
Thus envelope weighting balances the a priori vector norm and reconstruction norm at the common scale \(\mathcal E^{1/2}\), while inserting the reciprocal envelope \(E_\alpha^{-1}\) into every two-dilate correlation.
cf6e2f624d3b1a82.proof:
For each \(\alpha\), equation (2) gives
\[
 U_n(\alpha)\overline{r(\alpha)}
 =\frac{V_n(\alpha)}{\sqrt{E_\alpha}}\sqrt{E_\alpha}
 =V_n(\alpha),
\]
because \(E_\alpha\) is positive real. Summation proves (3). Also
\[
 \|r\|_2^2=\sum_\alpha E_\alpha=\mathcal E.
\]
By (1),
\[
 \|U_n\|_2^2
 =\sum_\alpha\frac{|V_n(\alpha)|^2}{E_\alpha}
 \le Z^2\sum_\alpha E_\alpha
 =Z^2\mathcal E,
\]
which proves (4). Linearity of the inner product in the first variable, (3), and Cauchy--Schwarz give
\[
 \left|\sum_{n\le X}a_n\sum_\alpha V_n(\alpha)\right|
 =\left|\left\langle\sum_{n\le X}a_nU_n,r\right\rangle\right|
 \le\left\|\sum_{n\le X}a_nU_n\right\|_2\|r\|_2,
\]
which is (5). Finally, expanding the inner product and using (2) gives
\[
 \langle U_{am},U_{bm}\rangle
 =\sum_\alpha
 \frac{V_{am}(\alpha)}{\sqrt{E_\alpha}}
 \frac{\overline{V_{bm}(\alpha)}}{\sqrt{E_\alpha}}
 =\sum_\alpha
 \frac{V_{am}(\alpha)\overline{V_{bm}(\alpha)}}{E_\alpha},
\]
proving (6).

glossary.Z: the uniform multiplicative loss in the coordinatewise envelope
glossary.mathcal E: the total envelope mass sum_alpha E_alpha

cff9d29efb555b8e.title: EXACT HARD GOOD-\(\mathscr W\) DOUBLE-CONDUCTOR SPLIT, THE DELETION-PRESERVING VECTOR TRACE, AND THE SIGNED RAY-MÖBIUS SOURCE CORE
cff9d29efb555b8e.author: slava chan
cff9d29efb555b8e.statement:
EXACT HARD GOOD-\(\mathscr W\) DOUBLE-CONDUCTOR SPLIT, THE DELETION-PRESERVING VECTOR TRACE, AND THE SIGNED RAY-MÖBIUS SOURCE CORE.

Adopt one fixed exact good-\(\mathscr W\) orientation, anatomy, frozen source/projective fibre, frequency block and dilator block
\[
1\le F\le x^3,\quad F\le|h|<2F,\qquad
\mathcal D\le d_\lambda<2\mathcal D
\]
from facts e55b27d39c593164 and 55dee3162ad8a011. Fix a real constant \(C>0\) and put
\[
L=(\log(2x))^C.
\]
For two distinct primitive signed rays
\[
R=(\epsilon,a,b),\qquad R'=(\epsilon',a',b'),
\]
put
\[
\Delta_0=\epsilon ba'-\epsilon'b'a,\qquad m=aa'.                 \tag{1}
\]
For a copy \(\lambda\), put
\[
n=d_\lambda v_\lambda,\qquad
m_d={d_\lambda/(d_\lambda,\mathscr A)\over
\bigl(d_\lambda/(d_\lambda,\mathscr A),\Delta_0\bigr)}.           \tag{2}
\]
Define
\[
g_q=(m,\mathscr A\Delta_0),\qquad
m_q={m\over g_q},\qquad
C_q={\mathscr A\Delta_0\over g_q}.                               \tag{3}
\]
Then
\[
(C_q,m_q)=1,\qquad (m_q,d_\lambda v_\lambda)=1,                  \tag{4}
\]
and the complete physical ray-pair phase in fact 7e9251670db3e1c9 has the exact conductor reduction
\[
\boxed{
e_{aa'}\!\left(
-\mathscr A\Delta_0(d_\lambda v_\lambda)^{-1}\right)
=
e_{m_q}\!\left(
-C_q(d_\lambda v_\lambda)^{-1}\right).
}                                                                 \tag{5}
\]

Let \(\mathfrak H_C\) be the restriction of the exact nonresonant ray-pair form to
\[
aa'>{Q^2\over\mathcal D},\qquad m_d>L.                            \tag{6}
\]
By fact 55dee3162ad8a011, the complement of (6) inside the nonresonant moment is absolutely bounded by
\[
x^{o(1)}|\omega_F|^2{BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}.                    \tag{7}
\]
The hard form has the exact disjoint split
\[
\mathfrak H_C=\mathfrak H_C^{>}+\mathfrak H_C^{\le},              \tag{8}
\]
where the first term has \(m_q>L\) and the second has \(m_q\le L\).

For each supported pair \((d,v)\), let \(\Lambda(d,v)\) be the finite set of exact copies \(\lambda\) with
\[
d_\lambda=d,\qquad v_\lambda=v.
\]
Let
\[
\mathcal H_{d,v}=\ell^2(\Lambda(d,v)),
\]
and, for every primitive signed ray \(R\), define
\[
\mathbf B_{d,v}(R)
=\bigl(B_\lambda(R)\bigr)_{\lambda\in\Lambda(d,v)}
\in\mathcal H_{d,v},
\]
where an unsupported component is zero and \(B_\lambda(R)\) is the complete literal pre-reciprocity coefficient from fact 7e9251670db3e1c9. Then
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\mathfrak H_C^{>}
=\sum_{d,v}\ 
\sum_{\substack{R\ne R'\\
aa'>Q^2/\mathcal D,\ m_d>L,\ m_q>L\\
d\nmid\mathscr A\Delta_0}}
&\left\langle\mathbf B_{d,v}(R),
\mathbf B_{d,v}(R')\right\rangle_{\mathcal H_{d,v}}\\
&\times
e_{m_q}\!\left(-C_q(dv)^{-1}\right).
\end{aligned}
}                                                                 \tag{GA-VBC-DEL}
\]
Every literal joint source coefficient and the pair-dependent nonresonance deletion remains inside GA-VBC-DEL. Thus the estimate
\[
\boxed{
|\mathfrak H_C^{>}|
\le x^{o(1)}|\omega_F|^2{BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}
}                                                                 \tag{9}
\]
is the exact deletion-preserving Hilbert-valued large-\(m_q\) supplier required on this branch. It is not asserted here.

For the small-\(m_q\) branch, fact a36284a9dbec7837 gives, for every ray,
\[
B_\lambda(R)
=\mathcal A_\lambda(R)\mathcal U_\lambda(R),\qquad
\mathcal U_\lambda(R)
=\sum_{k\in\mathscr I_\lambda(R)}
\mu(k)\mathcal W_{\lambda,R}(k),                                 \tag{10}
\]
with the complete literal Fourier-and-mask weight retained. Consequently
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\mathfrak H_C^{\le}
=\sum_\lambda
\sum_{\substack{R\ne R'\\
aa'>Q^2/\mathcal D,\ m_d>L,\ m_q\le L\\
d_\lambda\nmid\mathscr A\Delta_0}}
&\mathcal A_\lambda(R)
\overline{\mathcal A_\lambda(R')}
\mathcal U_\lambda(R)
\overline{\mathcal U_\lambda(R')}\\
&\times
e_{m_q}\!\left(
-C_q(d_\lambda v_\lambda)^{-1}\right).
\end{aligned}
}                                                                 \tag{GA-SIGNED-RAY-MU}
\]
The estimate
\[
\boxed{
|\mathfrak H_C^{\le}|
\le x^{o(1)}|\omega_F|^2{BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}
}                                                                 \tag{11}
\]
is the exact small-\(m_q\) signed source supplier required on this branch. It also is not asserted here.

On the subfamily \(a=a'=1\), one has \(m=m_q=1\). This subfamily occurs in (6) only when
\[
\mathcal D>Q^2.
\]
Its phase in GA-SIGNED-RAY-MU is one, and its restriction is exactly UNIT-RAY-SRC from fact a36284a9dbec7837, further restricted by \(m_d>L\). Thus no inverse-variable phase can cancel this unit-denominator hard slice.

Facts e55b27d39c593164 and a36284a9dbec7837 assume no fixed-polylogarithmic bounded-variation decomposition of the combined weight \(\mathcal W_{\lambda,R}(k)\). Fact a924b399d9dcbd8a proves that squarefree dyadic support, a zero-one hard mask and a pointwise envelope alone cannot imply such a decomposition. Hence weighted Davenport fact 71389b22e6f49e13 cannot be inserted into GA-SIGNED-RAY-MU from the presently verified regularity statements alone. A valid continuation must either verifier-gate a source-genealogy recombination of the actual masks with controlled projective cost and then estimate the complete signed form (not raywise absolute values), or prove (11) by another source-specific mechanism.

Equations (9) and (11), together with fact 55dee3162ad8a011, would prove the fixed-block GA-RAY-SPEC estimate of fact 31ebcf364862d83a. This fact proves the exact split and interfaces only. It proves neither (9), nor (11), nor GA-RAY-SPEC, nor GA-NR-DIL, nor a good-\(\mathscr W\) tail payment, nor Goldbach.
cff9d29efb555b8e.proof:
For every supported ray pair, \(a\mid q_1\) and \(a'\mid q_2\). Fact e55b27d39c593164 gives
\[
(q_1,d_\lambda v_\lambda)=(q_2,d_\lambda v_\lambda)=1.
\]
Therefore
\[
(aa',d_\lambda v_\lambda)=1.                                    \tag{12}
\]
Definition (3) gives \(m=g_qm_q\) and
\(\mathscr A\Delta_0=g_qC_q\). Dividing both integers by their greatest common divisor proves
\[
(C_q,m_q)=1.
\]
Equation (12) implies \((g_qm_q,d_\lambda v_\lambda)=1\), hence the second coprimality in (4).

Let \(u\) be the inverse of \(d_\lambda v_\lambda\) modulo \(m\). Its reduction modulo \(m_q\) is the inverse of the same integer modulo \(m_q\). Thus
\[
\begin{aligned}
e_m(-\mathscr A\Delta_0u)
&=e_{g_qm_q}(-g_qC_qu)\\
&=e_{m_q}(-C_qu),
\end{aligned}
\]
which is (5).

Fact 55dee3162ad8a011 bounds absolutely the nonresonant subfamily
\[
aa'\le Q^2/\mathcal D
\]
and also bounds absolutely the subfamily
\[
m_d\le L.
\]
Their union is therefore bounded by the sum of those two estimates, which is still (7). The complement of that union is exactly (6). Since every positive integer \(m_q\) satisfies exactly one of
\[
m_q>L,\qquad m_q\le L,
\]
equation (8) is an exact disjoint split.

Fact 7e9251670db3e1c9 gives the exact pre-reciprocity nonresonant ray-pair form
\[
\sum_\lambda\sum_{\substack{R\ne R'\\
d_\lambda\nmid\mathscr A\Delta_0}}
B_\lambda(R)\overline{B_\lambda(R')}
e_{aa'}\!\left(
-\mathscr A\Delta_0(d_\lambda v_\lambda)^{-1}\right).            \tag{13}
\]
Restrict (13) by (6) and \(m_q>L\), and replace its phase using (5). Now group copies having the same ordered pair \((d_\lambda,v_\lambda)=(d,v)\). By the definition of the Hilbert inner product,
\[
\left\langle\mathbf B_{d,v}(R),
\mathbf B_{d,v}(R')\right\rangle_{\mathcal H_{d,v}}
=
\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda(d,v)}
B_\lambda(R)\overline{B_\lambda(R')}.
\]
Substitution into the restricted form proves GA-VBC-DEL. This is a finite regrouping only; therefore every coefficient and mask remains literal, and the deletion remains a condition on the complete ordered ray pair.

For the complementary restriction \(m_q\le L\), substitute RAY-MU, equation (10), from fact a36284a9dbec7837 into both coefficient slots of (13), after using (5). This gives GA-SIGNED-RAY-MU exactly. No absolute value is taken during the substitution.

If \(a=a'=1\), then \(m=1\), so definitions (3) give
\[
g_q=1,\qquad m_q=1.
\]
The first condition in (6) becomes
\[
1>Q^2/\mathcal D,
\]
which is equivalent to \(\mathcal D>Q^2\). Fact a36284a9dbec7837 proves that the phase is identically one and that the resulting complete signed cross-ray/copy expression is UNIT-RAY-SRC. The only additional restriction here is \(m_d>L\), proving the unit-denominator assertion.

Fact a36284a9dbec7837 explicitly records the absence of an assumed bounded-variation representation for the actual combined ray weight and the resulting no-direct-Davenport interface. Fact a924b399d9dcbd8a shows that the numerical support and envelope properties alone do not repair this omission. Therefore the stated logical limitation follows without claiming that its abstract alternating mask is the actual source mask.

Finally, the nonresonant moment is the union of the paid complement (7), the large-\(m_q\) hard form, and the small-\(m_q\) hard form. Applying (9), (11), and (7), then using the exact consumer equivalence in fact 31ebcf364862d83a, would prove fixed-block GA-RAY-SPEC. Since (9) and (11) are displayed only as unproved suppliers, every final exclusion follows.

glossary.GA-SIGNED-RAY-MU: The exact small-m_q hard residual after retaining the signed Möbius scaling transform on both primitive rays.
glossary.GA-VBC-DEL: The exact deletion-preserving Hilbert-valued large-m_q inverse-phase form for the hard good-W residual.
glossary.hard good-W double-conductor split: The partition of the residual left by GA-LOW-PRIM-PROD and GA-LOW-dCOND according to whether the physical additive conductor m_q is larger than a fixed power of log(2x).
glossary.m_q: The exact additive conductor aa'/gcd(aa',mathscr A Delta_0) of the physical primitive-ray pair phase.

d016de3f6c03e65c.title: LABELLED DECODER-COPY ENERGY OF THE FIXED-SEMIPRIME COMMON-CELL SOURCE
d016de3f6c03e65c.author: slava chan
d016de3f6c03e65c.statement:
LABELLED DECODER-COPY ENERGY OF THE FIXED-SEMIPRIME COMMON-CELL SOURCE.

Assume the hypotheses and definitions of fact 0abb9119d9247de6, including the fixed common prime cell [H^2,2H^2), the short full-conductor source fibres, and their grouped coefficients gamma_G. Assume H is sufficiently large for fact dcabcf2f566b5721.

For every ordered pair (G,G') of coprime active semiprimes, orient the two primes of G as r_1<r_2 and the two primes of G' as r_3<r_4, put P=GG', and let mathcal E_{G,G'} and N_E(G,G') be the eligible auxiliary residue set and its cardinality from dcabcf2f566b5721 for that ordered prime quadruple. Put
alpha_{G,G'}=phi(P)/P=kappa_Gkappa_{G'}.
For each c in mathcal E_{G,G'}, define the fully labelled decoder-copy coefficient
d_{G,G',c}
 =alpha_{G,G'} gamma_Ggamma_{G'}/N_E(G,G').                  (1)
The label retains (G,G',c), even if a later operation would identify or aggregate decoder parameters.

(A) The exact importance-sampled reopening of the fixed-(G,G') source full face in fact 0abb9119d9247de6 is
alpha_{G,G'}gamma_Ggamma_{G'}
 =sum_{c in mathcal E_{G,G'}}d_{G,G',c}.                      (2)
For each fixed ordered pair,
sum_{c in mathcal E_{G,G'}}|d_{G,G',c}|
 =alpha_{G,G'}|gamma_Ggamma_{G'}|,                            (3)
sum_{c in mathcal E_{G,G'}}|d_{G,G',c}|^2
 =alpha_{G,G'}^2|gamma_Ggamma_{G'}|^2/N_E(G,G').              (4)

(B) With counting measure on the fully labelled disjoint union of all triples (G,G',c),
sum_{\substack{G,G' in mathcal G_H\\gcd(G,G')=1}}
 sum_{c in mathcal E_{G,G'}}|d_{G,G',c}|^2
 <<D^4R^4H^{-12}(log x)^8(log(2H))^2.                         (5)
In the literal nonempty dyadic source range H<=x^{O(1)}, this is
<<D^4R^4H^{-12}(log x)^10.                                   (6)

The carrier inside gamma_Ggamma_{G'} is the actual source carrier C_src of fact 0abb9119d9247de6. Each c separately generates the auxiliary decoder carrier C_dec and the parameters (m,C_dec,K) of dcabcf2f566b5721. Equations (1)-(6) are only coefficient identities on the fully labelled decoder copies. They assert no orthogonality after labels are forgotten, no cancellation or norm bound after equal decoder fibres are aggregated, no varying-(m,C_dec,K) analytic estimate, no common-cell capture, no cross-cell control, and no Goldbach implication.
d016de3f6c03e65c.proof:
Fix an ordered coprime pair (G,G'). Fact 0abb9119d9247de6 proves that its actual source full-face contribution is
alpha_{G,G'}gamma_Ggamma_{G'}.
This complete coefficient includes all retained actual source phases and labels but is independent of the auxiliary primitive-residue coordinate used by dcabcf2f566b5721.

For P=GG', fact dcabcf2f566b5721 defines
omega=phi(P)/(H^4N_E(G,G'))
and proves the exact reopening
alpha_{G,G'}A_prov
 =(H^4/P)omega sum_{c in mathcal E_{G,G'}}A_prov.             (7)
Taking A_prov=gamma_Ggamma_{G'} is legal by the preceding residue-independence. The coefficient of every summand on the right of (7) is
(H^4/P)omega
 =(H^4/P)phi(P)/(H^4N_E(G,G'))
 =alpha_{G,G'}/N_E(G,G'),
which is exactly (1). Summing N_E identical coefficients proves (2). Taking absolute values and squared absolute values proves (3) and (4).

The same fact gives
N_E(G,G')>>H^4/(log(2H))^2                                  (8)
uniformly in the ordered common-cell prime tuple, while 0<alpha_{G,G'}<=1. Therefore (4) and (8) give
sum_{\substack{G,G'\\gcd(G,G')=1}}\sum_c|d_{G,G',c}|^2
 <<H^{-4}(log(2H))^2
   sum_{\substack{G,G'\\gcd(G,G')=1}}|gamma_G|^2|gamma_{G'}|^2
 <=H^{-4}(log(2H))^2 (sum_G|gamma_G|^2)^2.                   (9)
Fact 0abb9119d9247de6 supplies
sum_G|gamma_G|^2<<D^2R^2H^{-4}(log x)^4.
Substitution into (9) proves (5).

On a nonempty literal dyadic source label, G<=b and compact support gives gb<<R. The companion positive-integer source scale K is bounded below by a fixed positive constant, while RK is comparable to x, so R<<x. Hence H^4<=G<<x and log(2H)<<log x, proving (6).

All norms above are on the disjoint label set (G,G',c). The proof never combines two labels having equal later decoder parameters and never invokes an analytic operator across different m, C_dec, or K. This proves the final scope paragraph.

glossary.alpha_{G,G'}: The full four-prime totient fraction phi(GG')/(GG').
glossary.d_{G,G',c}: The coefficient assigned to one fully labelled eligible decoder copy.
glossary.mathcal E_{G,G'}: The eligible auxiliary residue set for the ordered four primes in the disjoint semiprime supports G and G'.

d061fc4dc153e309.title: NORM-ONE FOURIER SEPARATION OF THE LITERAL SMALL-v PMD MASK
d061fc4dc153e309.author: slava chan
d061fc4dc153e309.statement:
NORM-ONE FOURIER SEPARATION OF THE LITERAL SMALL-v PMD MASK.

Let N,r be integers and let v,d_1,d_2 be positive integers with gcd(v,d_1d_2)=1. Put e_v(t)=exp(2 pi i t/v), with e_1(t)=1, and let bars denote inverses modulo v. Then

1_{v|N(d_2-d_1)-rd_1d_2}
 =1/v sum_{s modulo v}
    e_v(sN d_1bar)e_v(-sN d_2bar)e_v(-sr).                 (1)

Thus for each fixed v the exact coupled mask has a finite projective separation into one factor of d_1, one factor of d_2, and one factor of r whose coefficient l1 norm is exactly
  sum_{s modulo v}1/v=1.                                   (2)
The s=0 term is the constant density 1/v; every s nonzero is a genuinely oscillatory separated character atom.

The separation is invariant under the outer-gcd normalization. More precisely, if g divides N, d_i=gq_i, gcd(g,v)=1, and A=N/g, then
  A q_1bar congruent N d_1bar modulo v,
  A q_2bar congruent N d_2bar modulo v,                     (3)
where the first bars are inverses of q_i modulo v and the second are inverses of d_i modulo v. Hence the Fourier atoms obtained from
  1_{v|A(q_2-q_1)-rq_1q_2}
are exactly those in (1), with no g-dependent character left over.

For an integer J>=1, let tau_J(n) be the number of ordered J-tuples of positive integers whose product is n. Fix a dyadic V>=2. Let xi_v be supported on V<=v<2V with |xi_v|<=tau_J(v), and attach coefficient xi_v/v to every pair (v,s), s modulo v. For every epsilon>0,

sum_{V<=v<2V}sum_{s modulo v}|xi_v/v|^2
 =sum_{V<=v<2V}|xi_v|^2/v
 <<_{J,epsilon}V^epsilon.                                  (4)

By contrast, the direct triangle cost of this displayed decomposition is
  sum_{V<=v<2V}sum_{s modulo v}|xi_v/v|
  =sum_{V<=v<2V}|xi_v|,                                    (5)
which can be comparable to V, for example when xi_v=1 throughout the interval. Thus the complete (v,s)-coefficient family has subpolynomial l2 norm but can have linear-size l1 norm. Any later estimate which keeps this family inside one l2 coefficient slot avoids a loss which an atomwise triangle assembly need not avoid. This is a coefficient-norm statement, not a cancellation estimate for the centered prime incidence.
d061fc4dc153e309.proof:
Because d_1d_2 is a unit modulo v, the divisibility condition on the left of (1) is equivalent to
  r congruent N(d_2-d_1)(d_1d_2)bar
    congruent N(d_1bar-d_2bar) modulo v.                    (6)
Additive-character orthogonality gives
  1_{r congruent N(d_1bar-d_2bar) mod v}
  =1/v sum_{s mod v}e_v(s[N(d_1bar-d_2bar)-r]),             (7)
and splitting the exponential in (7) proves (1). All coefficients in (1) have magnitude 1/v and there are v of them, proving (2).

For (3), d_i=gq_i and gcd(g,v)=1 imply
  d_ibar congruent gbar q_ibar modulo v,
so
  N d_ibar congruent N gbar q_ibar
    congruent (N/g)q_ibar=Aq_ibar modulo v.                 (8)
This proves outer-gcd invariance.

It remains to prove (4) with an allowed divisor estimate. On a prime power p^a,
  tau_J(p^a)=binomial(a+J-1,J-1)<=(a+1)^(J-1)=tau(p^a)^(J-1).
Multiplicativity therefore gives
  tau_J(n)<=tau(n)^(J-1).                                  (9)
Fact e705401df9f0709e states the fixed-power divisor estimate tau(n)<<_{L,eta}P^eta uniformly for 2<=n<=P^L. Apply it with P=2V, L=1 and eta=epsilon/[4 max(1,J-1)]. Equations (9) and the hypothesis on xi_v give |xi_v|^2<<_{J,epsilon}V^(epsilon/2). Hence
  sum_{V<=v<2V}|xi_v|^2/v
  <<_{J,epsilon}V^(epsilon/2)sum_{V<=v<2V}1/v
  <<_{J,epsilon}V^epsilon,
proving (4). Equation (5) is immediate from summing v identical magnitudes |xi_v|/v. With xi_v=1 its right side is the number of integers in [V,2V), which is comparable to V. The final norm comparison follows.

glossary.small-v Fourier label s: The additive character frequency modulo v which separates the literal v-divisibility mask.
glossary.tau_J: The J-fold divisor function, counting ordered J-tuples of positive integers with prescribed product.

d1e52dc3184d073d.title: Let p be a prime, let R_count be a positive integer, and let L_0,L_1,L_1^{(prof)},...,L_{R_count}^{(prof)} be integers such that
d1e52dc3184d073d.author: slava chan
d1e52dc3184d073d.statement:
Let p be a prime, let R_count be a positive integer, and let L_0,L_1,L_1^{(prof)},...,L_{R_count}^{(prof)} be integers such that
1 <= L_0 <= L_r^{(prof)} <= L_1 for every 1 <= r <= R_count,
and p L_0 >= 2 L_1^2.
Write F_p^* for the nonzero residue classes modulo p and H_p = l^2(F_p^*) with counting measure. Put e_p(x)=exp(2 pi i x/p) and, for a in F_p^*,
D_r(a)=sum_{0 <= j < L_r^{(prof)}} e_p(-a j),
E_r=p L_r^{(prof)}-(L_r^{(prof)})^2,
phi_r=D_r/sqrt(E_r).
Let S:C^{R_count}->H_p be the linear map satisfying S bold_e_r=phi_r for the standard orthonormal basis (bold_e_r).

Then:

(i) The exact deleted-zero Parseval identities are
< D_r,D_s >_{H_p}
 = p min(L_r^{(prof)},L_s^{(prof)})-L_r^{(prof)}L_s^{(prof)}
and ||D_r||_{H_p}^2=E_r.

(ii) For every c=(c_r) in C^{R_count}, on writing x_r=c_r/sqrt(E_r), one has the exact Abel tail-sum identity
||S c||_{H_p}^2
 = p sum_{j=0}^{L_1-1} | sum_{r: L_r^{(prof)}>j} x_r |^2
   - | sum_{r=1}^{R_count} L_r^{(prof)} x_r |^2.
Equivalently, if 0=ell_0<ell_1<...<ell_m are zero followed by the distinct values among the L_r^{(prof)}, and
T_k=sum_{r: L_r^{(prof)}>=ell_k}x_r,
then
||S c||_{H_p}^2
 = p sum_{k=1}^m (ell_k-ell_{k-1})|T_k|^2
   - |sum_r L_r^{(prof)}x_r|^2.

(iii) With
c_0=(pL_0-L_1^2)/(pL_1),
one has
||S||^2 >= c_0 R_count >= (L_0/(2L_1))R_count.

(iv) If K is any complex Hilbert space and S=VU exactly for bounded linear maps U:C^{R_count}->K and V:K->H_p, then
||U||^2 ||V||^2 >= c_0 R_count.
Consequently, in the copy convention ||U||<=1 forces the coordinate-folding map to satisfy ||V||^2>=c_0R_count, whereas in the merged convention ||V||<=1 forces the coefficient map to satisfy ||U||^2>=c_0R_count.

This is only a finite-dimensional prefix-profile factorization obstruction. It does not assert a counterexample to PAVG27, and the product lower bound in (iv) cannot by itself be assigned to one named coefficient constant in an arithmetic Hilbert-space realization.
d1e52dc3184d073d.proof:
First note that pL_0>=2L_1^2 and L_0<=L_1 imply p>=2L_1, so every L_r^{(prof)} is strictly smaller than p and E_r=L_r^{(prof)}(p-L_r^{(prof)}) is positive.

For any r,s, expand the complete Fourier inner product over all residue classes a modulo p:
sum_{a mod p} D_r(a) overline(D_s(a))
 = sum_{0<=j<L_r^{(prof)}} sum_{0<=k<L_s^{(prof)}} sum_{a mod p} e_p(a(k-j)).
Because both j and k belong to {0,...,p-1}, additive-character orthogonality makes the innermost sum equal to p exactly when j=k and zero otherwise. Hence the complete sum is p min(L_r^{(prof)},L_s^{(prof)}). At a=0 the summand is L_r^{(prof)}L_s^{(prof)}. Removing that one frequency proves
< D_r,D_s >_{H_p}
 =p min(L_r^{(prof)},L_s^{(prof)})-L_r^{(prof)}L_s^{(prof)}.
Putting r=s gives ||D_r||^2=E_r, proving (i).

For (ii), by linearity,
Sc=sum_r x_r D_r.
Apply the already proved deleted-zero Parseval calculation to this linear combination. Its complete Fourier energy is
p sum_{j=0}^{L_1-1}|sum_{r:L_r^{(prof)}>j}x_r|^2:
indeed, the coefficient at the time index j is precisely the displayed tail sum. Its zero-frequency value is sum_r L_r^{(prof)}x_r. Subtracting the squared zero-frequency value gives the first identity in (ii). On every integer interval ell_{k-1}<=j<ell_k, the active set {r:L_r^{(prof)}>j} is exactly {r:L_r^{(prof)}>=ell_k}; grouping these equal terms proves the equivalent Abel form.

For (iii), let G=S^*S. By (i),
G_{rs}=
[p min(L_r^{(prof)},L_s^{(prof)})-L_r^{(prof)}L_s^{(prof)}]/sqrt(E_rE_s).
The numerator is at least pL_0-L_1^2. Also E_r<=pL_r^{(prof)}<=pL_1, so sqrt(E_rE_s)<=pL_1. The lower numerator is positive by the assumed inequality. Therefore every entry G_{rs} is at least c_0. If bold_one is the vector all of whose R_count coordinates are one, the Rayleigh quotient gives
||S||^2=||G|| >= <G bold_one,bold_one>/||bold_one||^2
 >= c_0 R_count^2/R_count=c_0R_count.
Moreover L_1^2<=pL_0/2, hence c_0>=(pL_0/2)/(pL_1)=L_0/(2L_1).

Finally, if S=VU, operator-norm submultiplicativity yields
||S||<=||V||||U||.
Squaring and using (iii) proves (iv). The two convention-specific conclusions follow by inserting respectively ||U||<=1 and ||V||<=1. The argument determines only the product tax unless a separate realization controls one factor, which also proves the stated limitation.

d26acaefc372b4d0.title: BUFFERED LONG NATURAL-FREQUENCY TRANSFER OF THE FIVE ABSTRACT LOW-BETA TRACES. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, fix 0<eta<sigma, and suppose 1<=beta<=6/5-2kappa. For sufficiently large Q put B=Q^beta and H_T=B/Q. Let G>0 and H_P=H_T/G, and assume H_P>=1 and Q^{-sigma+eta}<=G<=Q^{sigma-eta}. Compute the marker cutoffs L=H_TQ^sigma, S_0=H_T^2Q^{3sigma}, and Z=Q^{3/2-beta-3sigma} from H_T
d26acaefc372b4d0.author: slava chan
d26acaefc372b4d0.statement:
BUFFERED LONG NATURAL-FREQUENCY TRANSFER OF THE FIVE ABSTRACT LOW-BETA TRACES. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, fix 0<eta<sigma, and suppose 1<=beta<=6/5-2kappa. For sufficiently large Q put B=Q^beta and H_T=B/Q. Let G>0 and H_P=H_T/G, and assume H_P>=1 and Q^{-sigma+eta}<=G<=Q^{sigma-eta}. Compute the marker cutoffs L=H_TQ^sigma, S_0=H_T^2Q^{3sigma}, and Z=Q^{3/2-beta-3sigma} from H_T.
For each trace statement 664a92777dc5f5db (interval prime A), 533acf4056cf5bee (stopping B), 2ff1c15aef183bac (one rough prime C1), 3b1bda56ad927c5e (two rough primes C2), and 0576f567200d41f1 (three rough primes C3), define its long natural-frequency deformation by retaining exactly its hypotheses, coefficients, factor scales, prime ordering, cutoffs L,S_0,Z, and product scale B, but replacing the frequency support H_T<=|h|<2H_T by H_P<=|h|<2H_P, replacing the Poisson prefactor H_T^{-1} by H_P^{-1}, and replacing |h|/H_T in the smooth amplitude by |h|/H_P. In A retain the original arbitrary unit phase numerator A_q modulo q. In B,C1,C2,C3 retain the original fixed nonzero target A with |A|<=Q^{C_A} and numerator Ah.
Then there is delta=delta(kappa,eta,C_A)>0 such that every nonempty long natural-frequency deformation is O(Q^{2-delta}), uniformly in all factor scales and fixed bounded scaled-smooth amplitude families. The conclusion remains valid after the same polylogarithmic dyadic, sign, Vaughan, stopping, smooth-separation, and prime-cell labels allowed by the five predecessor facts.
The A deformation still requires a unit numerator A_q. The other four permit gcd(A,q)>1 and gcd(h,q)>1. An arbitrary q-dependent unit multiplier is accepted in every correlated-energy use, but this theorem does not add one to the Type-I branches using bbcb9f66597c667c.
For a literal normalized source write d=ga,r=gb, let Q and B be the dyadic scales of a and b, let M be the m-scale, put L_src=N/g, and assume DM and N are comparable to x, with D=gQ and M=GQ. Additive reciprocity gives e_b(L_src h a^{-1})=e_a(-L_src h b^{-1})e(L_src h/(ab)). On h of length H_P=B/M, the final factor is uniformly scaled-smooth because L_src/(QM)=N/(DM) is bounded, and |L_src| is O(GQ^2), hence O(Q^3) on the strip. Thus every H_P>=1 literal source leaf whose remaining coefficients and masks match a displayed deformation is controlled. This corollary excludes A incidences with gcd(L_src,a)>1, outer-g layers outside the G-strip, H_P<1, and Type-I branches with an extra a-dependent unit multiplier.
d26acaefc372b4d0.proof:
Reserve H_T for the cutoff geometry and H_P for the actual frequency.
A. Apply fact 4a101b703d4499f6 with H'=2H_P. The marker scale satisfies Y>=H_TQ^sigma/2 and Y<=Z. Since G>=Q^{-sigma+eta}, H_P<=H_TQ^{sigma-eta}, so H'<=Y for large Q. From UY comparable to B=QH_T, one has U<<Q^{1-sigma}<q. Also 8H_PY<=8H_PZ=8Q^{1/2-3sigma}/G<=8Q^{1/2-2sigma-eta}<q. After summing q and multiplying by H_P^{-1}, the two terms of 4a101b703d4499f6 are G^{1/2}Q^2(H_T/Y)^{1/2} and Q^{7/4}(H_TY)^{1/2}. They are at most Q^{2-eta/2} and Q^{2-3sigma/2}. The p|u diagonal is at most QU<<Q^{2-sigma}. This proves A and shows exactly where its unit-numerator hypothesis enters.
B. Fact e18b670f5d48f500 gives H_T^2Q^{2sigma}<=Y<=Q^{1-2sigma}/H_T^2 and UY comparable to QH_T. Apply the joint-coprimality natural-frequency ledger 95626318cdcc099f with S=Y,T=U. Its first two terms are at most G^{1/4}Q^{2-sigma/2}<=Q^{2-sigma/4-eta/4}; its third is at most Q^{2-sigma}; its fourth is at most Q^{2-sigma}, because the Y-window implies H_T<=Q^{1/4-sigma}. The exact gcd(u,y)=1 selector is therefore paid, and the stopping coefficients separate as in 533acf4056cf5bee.
C1. The proper-prime-power bound in 2ff1c15aef183bac is unchanged because the h-count cancels H_P^{-1}. Every Type-II or medium/large Type-I selected scale obeys H_T^2Q^{3sigma}<=S<=Q^{1-3sigma}/H_T^2 and ST comparable to B. Fact 42720f6d803c4640 gives first two terms at most G^{1/4}Q^{2-3sigma/4}, third term at most Q^{2-3sigma/2}, and fourth term Q^{7/4}H_T, all power-saving under G<=Q^{sigma-eta} and beta<=6/5-2kappa. Low Type-I boxes use bbcb9f66597c667c. Their product and short-factor conditions are unchanged; H_P>=1 and H_P<=H_TQ^{sigma-eta}<=Q verify its frequency range. Prime ordering, automatic coprimality and prime-power counting do not use H_T=H_P.
C2. In Case 1 of 3b1bda56ad927c5e rerun C1 for the separated outer factor; its prime separation remains unchanged. In Cases 2 and 3 the selected scale obeys H_T^2Q^{2sigma}<=S<=Q^{1-3sigma}/H_T^2. Fact 42720f6d803c4640 gives first term at most G^{1/4}Q^{2-sigma/2}, second at most G^{1/4}Q^{2-3sigma/4}, third at most Q^{2-sigma}, and a power-saving fourth term. Equal-cell symmetrization and the repeated-prime diagonal QR/Z are independent of H_P.
C3. The selected scale in 0576f567200d41f1 lies between H_T^2Q^{3sigma} and Q^{1-3sigma}/H_T^2, so the C1 correlated calculation applies. Prime-cell symmetrization and every collision stratum QR/Z are unchanged.
All fixed-target, unit-twist and h-gcd assertions follow from facts 42720f6d803c4640, 95626318cdcc099f and bbcb9f66597c667c with exactly the qualifications stated. Polylogarithmic label counts and epsilon factors are absorbed into the fixed power margins.
For the source, additive reciprocity is a^{-1}/b+b^{-1}/a=1/(ab) modulo one. On scaled supports, L_src h/(ab) has size L_srcH_P/(QB)=L_src/(QM)=N/(DM), and all logarithmic derivatives are uniformly bounded, as in df9748efe29ab475. Finally N comparable to DM=(gQ)(GQ) gives L_src=N/g comparable to GQ^2. This proves the source assertions and exclusions.

glossary.H_P: The literal natural Poisson frequency B/M.
glossary.H_T: The abstract trace frequency B/Q used in the cutoff geometry.
glossary.long natural-frequency deformation: A predecessor trace with H_P>=1, cutoff geometry kept at H_T, and h-support, prefactor and scaled h-coordinate changed to H_P.

d28e8bb75d80eb0d.title: EXACT BETTIN-CHANDEE PHASE MATCH FOR EACH SUPPORTED C4 RECIPROCAL-SLOPE MODE, AND NO DIRECT BLACK-BOX TRANSFER TO THE ELEVEN-MODE COMMON-ROW ENERGY. Use the eleven-mode setting of fact a3132ecd1bd44382. For fixed lambda and r|D_lambda with omega(r)<=2, put
d28e8bb75d80eb0d.author: slava chan
d28e8bb75d80eb0d.statement:
EXACT BETTIN-CHANDEE PHASE MATCH FOR EACH SUPPORTED C4 RECIPROCAL-SLOPE MODE, AND NO DIRECT BLACK-BOX TRANSFER TO THE ELEVEN-MODE COMMON-ROW ENERGY. Use the eleven-mode setting of fact a3132ecd1bd44382. For fixed lambda and r|D_lambda with omega(r)<=2, put
m_lambda,r=v_lambda r,
and choose a nonzero integer theta_lambda,r satisfying
theta_lambda,r congruent to A(D_lambda/r)^{-1} modulo m_lambda,r.    (1)
Such a nonzero representative is chosen even if the residue class is zero. For every primitive ray rho=(epsilon,a,b) carrying at least one supported physical term in B_lambda(rho;z), one has
Psi_lambda,r(rho)
=e_{m_lambda,r}(theta_lambda,r epsilon b a^{-1}).                  (2)
Thus a fixed supported C4 mode has exactly the Kloosterman-fraction phase shape in Bettin and Chandee, arXiv:1502.00769, Theorem 1.

That external theorem states: for a fixed nonzero integer theta and arbitrary one-variable complex sequences alpha_m, beta_n, nu_u supported respectively on dyadic intervals m comparable to M, n comparable to N, u comparable to U, with gcd(m,n)=1,
|sum_u sum_m sum_n alpha_m beta_n nu_u e_n(theta u m^{-1})|
is
<<_epsilon ||alpha||_2||beta||_2||nu||_2
(1+|theta|U/(MN))^(1/2)
[(UMN)^(7/20+epsilon)(M+N)^(1/4)
 +(UMN)^(3/8+epsilon)(UN+UM)^(1/8)].                              (BC)
Here theta is fixed throughout the trilinear sum and the coefficient is the tensor product of three one-variable sequences.

Theorem (BC), as stated, is not a direct black-box proof of the source-specific eleven-mode supplier (9) in fact a3132ecd1bd44382. The exact unproved transfer has at least the following three interfaces.
(i) Across varying lambda and r, the modulus m_lambda,r and the numerator theta_lambda,r both depend on D_lambda,v_lambda,r; (BC) has one fixed integer theta.
(ii) The literal ray coefficient
B_lambda(rho;z)=sum_kappa c_lambda(kappa a,epsilon kappa b;z)mu(kappa a)^2 1_{gcd(kappa a,D_lambda v_lambda)=1}
is a joint function of lambda,a,b and the common row z. Facts fafe50a7d45923d2 and 10fd259d904acea7 separate the smooth pre-ray amplitude and bound one rough coprimality Schur gate, respectively, but they do not factor this ray-scale sum as alpha_a nu_b beta_{m_lambda,r} with controlled projective l1 cost while retaining every mask and the same z.
(iii) The needed quantity is the common-row quadratic energy
sum_lambda theta_lambda^{row} sum_r c_lambda(r)|S_lambda,r(z)|^2,
uniformly in z, whereas (BC) bounds one scalar trilinear form after its tensor coefficients have already been supplied. Applying (BC) separately after fixing lambda,r collapses its varying-modulus sequence to a singleton and supplies no cancellation across the lambda,r family.

Therefore a valid Bettin-Chandee route requires an additional source-preserving tensorization or a vector-valued extension that simultaneously retains the kappa-ray sum, the varying numerator/modulus pair, the anatomy masks, and the common physical row before Cauchy-Schwarz. No such transfer, eleven-mode energy bound, C4 estimate, or Goldbach conclusion is proved here. This is a scoped no-direct-import audit, not an impossibility result for an adapted amplification argument.
d28e8bb75d80eb0d.proof:
Because gcd(D_lambda,v_lambda)=1 and r divides D_lambda, one has
gcd(D_lambda/r,v_lambda r)=1. Hence the inverse of D_lambda/r modulo m_lambda,r exists, so the congruence class in (1) exists. Every residue class modulo the positive integer m_lambda,r has a nonzero integer representative: if its least nonnegative representative is zero, choose m_lambda,r itself. This makes theta_lambda,r an actual nonzero integer as required by (BC), without changing its residue-class phase.

Now let rho carry a supported physical term in B_lambda. Then for some positive kappa, the pair q=kappa a, h=epsilon kappa b lies in the support of fact 134b03fc362a7cf1. Its gate gives gcd(kappa a,D_lambda v_lambda)=1, hence gcd(a,v_lambda r)=1. Thus a^{-1} modulo m_lambda,r is defined. The phase from fact a3132ecd1bd44382 is
Psi_lambda,r(rho)
=e_{v_lambda r}(A epsilon b[a(D_lambda/r)]^{-1}).
Modulo m_lambda,r=v_lambda r, inversion is multiplicative, so
[a(D_lambda/r)]^{-1}
=(D_lambda/r)^{-1}a^{-1}.
Substitution of (1) proves (2). With Bettin-Chandee variables
u=epsilon b, m=a, n=m_lambda,r,
equation (2) is exactly their phase e_n(theta u m^{-1}); the sign epsilon is handled by separating the two signed b-blocks. The support gate gives gcd(a,m_lambda,r)=1, matching the inverse condition.

We now compare quantifiers rather than assume missing coefficient identities. The complete statement (BC), including its epsilon-dependent implied constant, has one nonzero integer theta outside all three sums and three independent coefficient sequences alpha_m, beta_n, nu_u. In (1), theta_lambda,r is determined by D_lambda/r modulo v_lambda r. Since lambda and r vary in the energy of fact a3132ecd1bd44382, neither the modulus nor the numerator is fixed by the currently verified identities. Thus one substitution into (BC) cannot include the whole lambda,r family.

Next, fact 134b03fc362a7cf1 defines B_lambda by the displayed kappa-sum in the statement. Its physical coefficient c_lambda(kappa a,epsilon kappa b;z) is linear in the same common row z and may retain all literal amplitudes and masks. The squarefree gate mu(kappa a)^2, the support q=kappa a and h=epsilon kappa b, and the row masks remain inside that sum. Fact fafe50a7d45923d2 gives a polylogarithmic projective separation of the smooth amplitude in the pre-ray variables q,n,h, but explicitly does not separate arithmetic masks or unit gates. Fact 10fd259d904acea7 bounds a coprimality mask as a Schur multiplier but gives no lower bound and no tensor factorization of the complete ray-scale coefficient. Therefore the hypotheses of the cited facts do not provide the three one-variable tensor coefficient required by (BC).

Finally, equation (9) of fact a3132ecd1bd44382 is a sum of squared transforms with a single common vector z and varying lambda,r. The scalar theorem (BC) has no outer common-row operator quantifier. If lambda,r are fixed first, the n-sequence in the mapping above is supported at the single modulus n=v_lambda r. Such a separate use cannot by itself estimate cross-copy/common-row accumulation in the sum over lambda,r. This proves each stated interface failure. It does not rule out deriving a new tensorization or vector amplification theorem, which is exactly the final scope sentence.

glossary.m_lambda,r: The positive modulus v_lambda r of one reciprocal-slope mode.
glossary.theta_lambda,r: A chosen nonzero integer representative of A(D_lambda/r)^{-1} modulo v_lambda r.
glossary.theta_lambda^{row}: A nonnegative outer row weight, distinguished from the Bettin-Chandee numerator theta.

d2c6c6e9be57e257.title: SELF-CONTAINED STRICT ROW/HILBERT--SCHMIDT TRANSFER FOR PHYSICAL SEMIPRIME MATRICES, AND POSITIVE-GRAM NO-FIT. Let \(x\ge3\), \(D\ge2\), \(R>0\), \(P\ge1\), \(\sigma>0\), and let \(N\) be a positive integer. Put \(H_0=R/D\). Let \(\mathcal P\) be a finite set of integers contained in \([P,2P]\). Let \(\mathscr A\) be a finite set of tuples \(\alpha=(\iota,h,p,\ell)\), where \(h\ne0\) and \(p,\ell\) are distinct primes, and put \(u_\alpha=p\ell\). For each \(\alpha\in\mathscr A\), let \(E_\alpha>0\). For every \(a\in\mathcal P\), positive integer \(m\), and \(\alpha\in\mathscr A\), let \(C_a(m;\alpha)\) be a complex number which is zero unless
d2c6c6e9be57e257.author: slava chan
d2c6c6e9be57e257.statement:
SELF-CONTAINED STRICT ROW/HILBERT--SCHMIDT TRANSFER FOR PHYSICAL SEMIPRIME MATRICES, AND POSITIVE-GRAM NO-FIT. Let \(x\ge3\), \(D\ge2\), \(R>0\), \(P\ge1\), \(\sigma>0\), and let \(N\) be a positive integer. Put \(H_0=R/D\). Let \(\mathcal P\) be a finite set of integers contained in \([P,2P]\). Let \(\mathscr A\) be a finite set of tuples \(\alpha=(\iota,h,p,\ell)\), where \(h\ne0\) and \(p,\ell\) are distinct primes, and put \(u_\alpha=p\ell\). For each \(\alpha\in\mathscr A\), let \(E_\alpha>0\). For every \(a\in\mathcal P\), positive integer \(m\), and \(\alpha\in\mathscr A\), let \(C_a(m;\alpha)\) be a complex number which is zero unless
\[
 am\le D,\qquad m\text{ is squarefree},qquad
 (a,mh u_\alpha N)=1,qquad (m,u_\alpha)=1.               \tag{1}
\]
Let \(\lambda_{a,m}\) be complex numbers, zero unless \(am\le D\), such that
\[
 \sum_{a\in\mathcal P}\sum_{m\ge1}|\lambda_{a,m}|^2\le D.          \tag{2}
\]
For distinct \(a,b\in\mathcal P\), define
\[
 K_m(a,b)=\mu(m)^2{\bf1}_{(ab,m)=1}
 \sum_{\alpha=(\iota,h,p,\ell)\in\mathscr A}
 \frac{C_a(m;\alpha)\overline{C_b(m;\alpha)}}{E_\alpha}
 e_{p\ell}\!\left(Nh\,m^{-1}(a^{-1}-b^{-1})\right),                 \tag{3}
\]
where an inverse is taken modulo \(p\ell\), and every summand outside (1) is zero. Put \(K_m(a,a)=0\), define
\[
 \|K_m\|_{HS}=\left(\sum_{a,b\in\mathcal P}|K_m(a,b)|^2\right)^{1/2},
\]
and put
\[
 \mathcal C_{\rm phys}
 =\sum_{\substack{a,b\in\mathcal P\\a\ne b}}
 \left|\sum_{m\ge1}\lambda_{a,m}\overline{\lambda_{b,m}}K_m(a,b)\right|.
                                                                         \tag{4}
\]
Finally put
\[
 L_*=\frac{D^{2-2\sigma}}R=\frac{D^{1-2\sigma}}{H_0},
 \qquad
 H_*=P L_*=\frac{P D^{2-2\sigma}}R.                                   \tag{5}
\]
Each of the following estimates is sufficient for
\[
 \mathcal C_{\rm phys}\ll_\varepsilon
 x^\varepsilon\frac{P D^{3-2\sigma}}R:                               \tag{6}
\]
\[
 \sup_m\sup_{a\ne b}|K_m(a,b)|
 \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon L_*,                                  \tag{ROW}
\]
or
\[
 \sup_m\|K_m\|_{HS}
 \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon H_*.                                  \tag{HS}
\]
More generally, let \(M_m\) be explicitly specified zero-diagonal matrices on \(\mathcal P\), put \(\Delta_m=K_m-M_m\), and let \(\mathcal C_M\) be the expression (4) with \(M_m\) in place of \(K_m\). If
\[
 \mathcal C_M\ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon\frac{P D^{3-2\sigma}}R
\]
and either (ROW) or (HS) holds with \(\Delta_m\) in place of \(K_m\), then (6) holds. This is the centered physical semiprime discrepancy interface.

The fixed factor \(D^{-2\sigma}\) in (5) cannot be obtained from a positive \(TT^*\) diagonal alone. More precisely, if \(G=(\langle v_a,v_b\rangle)_{1\le a,b\le n}\) is a positive semidefinite Gram matrix satisfying
\[
 G_{a,a}\le L_0=\frac{D^2}R=\frac D{H_0},
\]
then positivity gives only \(|G_{a,b}|\le L_0\), and this is sharp. For every integer \(n\ge2\), taking \(v_1=\cdots=v_n=\sqrt{L_0}\) in the one-dimensional Hilbert space gives
\[
 G_{a,b}=L_0\quad(1\le a,b\le n),qquad
 \|G-L_0I_n\|_{HS}=L_0\sqrt{n(n-1)}.                                  \tag{7}
\]
Since \(L_0/L_*=D^{2\sigma}\), positivity and the diagonal estimate alone imply neither the strict row scale nor a dimension-normalized Hilbert--Schmidt saving by \(D^{-2\sigma}\).

For the corrected forward-E11 data of fact bc1b67324480d454, take
\[
 C_a(m;\alpha)=C_\iota(am;h,p,\ell)
\]
on every literal mask of that fact and zero elsewhere. Its corrected \(q=1\) physical-phase identity identifies \(\mathcal C_{\rm phys}=C_{LL}\). Hence (ROW), (HS), or the centered comparison criterion above supplies exactly the open \(C_{LL}\) aggregate estimate of that fact. No such arithmetic estimate, no E11 closure, and no Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
d2c6c6e9be57e257.proof:
The interval \([P,2P]\) contains at most \(P+1\le2P\) integers. For \(\lambda_m=(\lambda_{a,m})_{a\in\mathcal P}\), Cauchy--Schwarz and (2) give
\[
 \sum_m\|\lambda_m\|_1^2
 \le |\mathcal P|\sum_m\|\lambda_m\|_2^2
 \le2PD.                                                                  \tag{8}
\]
Assume (ROW). Apply the triangle inequality inside (4), interchange the finite sums, and use (8):
\[
\begin{split}
 \mathcal C_{\rm phys}
 &\le\sum_m\sum_{a\ne b}
 |\lambda_{a,m}||\lambda_{b,m}||K_m(a,b)|\\
 &\ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon L_*\sum_m\|\lambda_m\|_1^2
 \le2x^\varepsilon PDL_*.
\end{split}
\]
Equation (5) gives \(PDL_*=P D^{3-2\sigma}/R\), proving (6).

Assume (HS). For each ordered pair define
\[
 S_{a,b}=\sum_m\lambda_{a,m}\overline{\lambda_{b,m}}K_m(a,b).
\]
Put \(\zeta_{a,b}=\overline{S_{a,b}}/|S_{a,b}|\) when \(S_{a,b}\ne0\), and \(\zeta_{a,b}=0\) otherwise. Then
\[
 \mathcal C_{\rm phys}
 =\sum_m\sum_{a\ne b}
 \zeta_{a,b}\lambda_{a,m}\overline{\lambda_{b,m}}K_m(a,b).
\]
For each fixed \(m\), Cauchy--Schwarz on the ordered pairs gives
\[
\begin{split}
 \left|\sum_{a\ne b}\zeta_{a,b}\lambda_{a,m}
 \overline{\lambda_{b,m}}K_m(a,b)\right|
 &\le\|K_m\|_{HS}
 \left(\sum_{a\ne b}|\lambda_{a,m}|^2|\lambda_{b,m}|^2\right)^{1/2}\\
 &\le\|K_m\|_{HS}\|\lambda_m\|_2^2.                                \tag{9}
\end{split}
\]
Summing (9), using (HS) and (2), gives
\[
 \mathcal C_{\rm phys}\ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon H_*D
 =x^\varepsilon\frac{P D^{3-2\sigma}}R.
\]
This proves the Hilbert--Schmidt transfer.

For the centered criterion, substitute \(K_m=M_m+\Delta_m\) into (4). The triangle inequality between the two resulting ordered-pair aggregates gives
\[
 \mathcal C_{\rm phys}\le\mathcal C_M+\mathcal C_\Delta.
\]
The hypothesis pays \(\mathcal C_M\), and the already proved row or Hilbert--Schmidt transfer pays \(\mathcal C_\Delta\). This proves the centered assertion.

For the no-fit, Hilbert-space Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 |G_{a,b}|=|\langle v_a,v_b\rangle|
 \le\|v_a\|\|v_b\|=(G_{a,a}G_{b,b})^{1/2}\le L_0.
\]
Also
\[
 \frac{L_0}{L_*}
 =\frac{D^2/R}{D^{2-2\sigma}/R}=D^{2\sigma}.              \tag{10}
\]
For sharpness, take every \(v_a=\sqrt{L_0}\) in the one-dimensional Hilbert space. Then \(G=L_0J_n\), where \(J_n\) is the all-ones matrix, so \(G\) is positive semidefinite and every entry equals \(L_0\). The zero-diagonal matrix \(G-L_0I_n\) has exactly \(n(n-1)\) entries of modulus \(L_0\), proving (7). Equation (10) proves that positivity and the diagonal bound alone cannot create the fixed saving.

Finally, the support conditions of fact bc1b67324480d454 imply (1) after its literal masks are encoded by zero extension. Equations (11)--(15) of that fact prove that its corrected leading-leading product, including \(q=1\), is exactly the phase in (3), with the same reciprocal envelope and coefficient pair. Therefore its definition of \(C_{LL}\) is exactly (4) under the stated substitution. The preceding transfer applies, while no arithmetic instance of (ROW) or (HS) was proved here.

glossary.C_a(m;alpha): The zero-extended literal source coefficient at dilator a, cofactor m, and physical coordinate alpha.
glossary.H_*: The strict sufficient Hilbert--Schmidt scale P D^(2-2sigma)/R.
glossary.J_n: The n by n all-ones matrix.
glossary.K_m: The zero-diagonal physical semiprime matrix at cofactor m.

d3278c2897e20003.title: GA-qCENT-ADD-LOW: ABSOLUTE PAYMENT OF ALL SMALL ADDITIVE CONDUCTORS, EXACT LARGE-CONDUCTOR HILBERT RESIDUAL, PROJECTIVE-RANK LEDGER, AND SCOPED NO-FIT
d3278c2897e20003.author: slava chan
d3278c2897e20003.statement:
GA-qCENT-ADD-LOW: ABSOLUTE PAYMENT OF ALL SMALL ADDITIVE CONDUCTORS, EXACT LARGE-CONDUCTOR HILBERT RESIDUAL, PROJECTIVE-RANK LEDGER, AND SCOPED NO-FIT.

Adopt the setting and notation of GA-qCENT in fact 764588e99974a6d9. Thus
Dcal<=Q^2,  Y=Q^2/Dcal>=1,                                           (1)
and each exact retained hard ray pair has a squarefree physical conductor
m=m_q>Y, units c=C_q and n=d_lambda v_lambda modulo m, exact ray coefficient B_lambda(R), and every literal pair-dependent condition of that fact. Use the Kloosterman sums S_t and primitive additive-conductor projections P_{t;c,s} of fact a08224dfb222c580.

Uniformly for every factorization st=m with t>1,
|P_{t;c,s}(n)|
 <= product_{p|t}(2-3/p)
 <=2^{omega(t)}
 <=x^{o(1)}.                                                          (2)
Define the complete small-additive-conductor part
H_C^{q-add-low}
 =sum_lambda sum_{exact retained R != R'}
 B_lambda(R) conjugate(B_lambda(R'))
 sum_{st=m_q, 1<t<=Y} mu(s)P_{t;C_q,s}(d_lambda v_lambda)/s.           (3)
Then
|H_C^{q-add-low}|
 <=x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 B Y F^2
 =x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 B Q^2 F^2/Dcal.                                (4)
The multiplicative-centering constant correction H_Theta^corr is already paid at the same target by fact a08224dfb222c580.

Let H_C^{q-add-large} be defined by replacing 1<t<=Y in (3) with t>Y. Then exactly
H_C^{q-cent}
 =H_Theta^corr+H_C^{q-add-low}+H_C^{q-add-large}.                     (5)
For fixed (d,v), let
B_bold_{d,v}(R)=(B_lambda(R))_{lambda in Lambda(d,v)}
be the exact Hilbert ray coefficient of fact 8b46abe31a5ae8d7. On the Hilbert space l2((Z/tZ)^*) with inner product
<u,w>=sum_{a (mod t)}^*u(a)conjugate(w(a)), define
V_{t;c,s}(a)=t^{-1/2}S_t(a,-c s^{-1}),
E_{t;n}(a)=t^{-1/2}e_t(an).                                          (6)
Then
P_{t;c,s}(n)=<V_{t;c,s},E_{t;n}>.                                    (7)
Consequently the exact large residual is
H_C^{q-add-large}
 =sum_{d,v} sum_{exact retained R != R'}
 <B_bold_{d,v}(R),B_bold_{d,v}(R')>
 sum_{st=m_q,t>Y} mu(s)<V_{t;C_q,s},E_{t;dv}>/s.                      (GA-CqADD-VEC)
This formula retains the varying squarefree m_q, the moving c=C_q, n=dv, the full Hilbert ray coefficients, and every marker, source, target-gcd, fixed-U, ordering, collision, deletion, provenance, coprimality and projective selector.

The primitive additive-frequency rank in (6) is exact:
||E_{t;n}||_2^2=phi(t)/t,                                             (8)
||V_{t;c,s}||_2^2
 =(1/t) product_{p|t}(p^2-p-1)
 =product_{p|t}(p-1-1/p).                                            (9)
In particular a bare Cauchy estimate for (7) has the norm scale
||V_{t;c,s}||_2||E_{t;n}||_2=t^{1/2+o(1)}.                           (9a)
This is a fixed-power projective-rank cost on any subrange t>=x^delta with fixed delta>0, but it can be absorbed into x^{o(1)} when t=x^{o(1)}. No unconditional rank no-fit is asserted for subpolynomial t.

For any T>=1, define H_C^{q-add}(T) to be the expression in (3) with its inner divisor range 1<t<=Y replaced by
1<t,  T<=t<2T,                                                       (10)
and with every outer coefficient and exact retained selector unchanged. If T>Y, then H_C^{q-add}(T) is exactly the corresponding dyadic block H_C^{q-add-large}(T) of GA-CqADD-VEC. The minimal deletion-preserving remaining supplier on each T>Y is
|H_C^{q-add-large}(T)|
 <=x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 B Y F^2.                                     (11)
The O(log x) dyadic blocks are absorbed into x^{o(1)}. Estimate (11) is not asserted.

The absolute conductor-cofactor method proves, for every T>=1,
|H_C^{q-add}(T)|
 <=x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 B T F^2.                                     (12)
It therefore pays blocks wholly contained in the already treated range t<=Y and loses T/Y for a block T>Y. This method failure is sharp: if m=p is prime, t=p and s=1, then
P_{p;c,1}(n)=e_p(-c n^{-1})+1/p,
|P_{p;c,1}(n)|>=1-1/p,                                               (13)
so the full additive conductor has coefficient one and an order-one projection. Equation (13) is a no-fit for cofactor-only decay, not a lower bound for the literal signed GA aggregate.

This theorem proves (2)-(10), (12), (13), the exact residual, and the stated qualified rank ledger and scoped method no-fit. It does not prove (11), all of GA-qCENT, GA-CqKLOO-VEC, GA-RAY-SPEC, GA-NR-DIL, a good-W tail payment, or Goldbach.
d3278c2897e20003.proof:
We first prove (2). From the definition in fact a08224dfb222c580, interchange the sums over the primitive additive frequency a and the unit Kloosterman variable x:
P_{t;c,s}(n)
 =(1/t) sum_{x (mod t)}^* e_t(-c s^{-1}x^{-1})
          sum_{a (mod t)}^*e_t(a(x-n))
 =(1/t) sum_{x (mod t)}^* e_t(-c s^{-1}x^{-1})c_t(x-n),              (14)
where c_t is the Ramanujan sum. Hence
|P_{t;c,s}(n)|
 <=(1/t)sum_{x (mod t)}^*|c_t(x-n)|.                                 (15)
Because t is squarefree and n is a unit modulo t, CRT and multiplicativity of Ramanujan sums factor the last sum. For a prime p|t, the unit x=n gives |c_p(0)|=p-1, while each of the other p-2 unit residues gives |c_p(x-n)|=1. Therefore the local L1 sum is 2p-3, and
(1/t)sum_x^*|c_t(x-n)|
 =product_{p|t}(2-3/p)
 <=2^{omega(t)}.                                                      (16)
All parameters are polynomially bounded in x, so the last quantity is x^{o(1)}. This proves (2).

For a fixed squarefree m, use s=m/t in (2):
sum_{st=m,1<t<=Y}|mu(s)P_{t;c,s}(n)|/s
 <=x^{o(1)}sum_{t|m,t<=Y}t/m
 <=x^{o(1)}Y tau(m)/m
 <=x^{o(1)}Y/m.                                                       (17)
The proof of GA-qPRINC in fact 764588e99974a6d9 establishes, over the complete literal scaling-coordinate universe,
sum_coordinates 1/m_q<=x^{o(1)}F^2,                                 (18)
together with pointwise coefficient-product envelope x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 and Bx^{o(1)} exact marked copies. Insert (17), then (18), and take absolute values. Every exact selector only deletes terms. This proves (4), with the complete literal inventory retained.

Fact a08224dfb222c580 gives for every exact pair
K^circ_{m,c}(n)
 =sum_{st=m,t>1}mu(s)P_{t;c,s}(n)/s
   +mu(m)(1/m-1/phi(m)).                                              (19)
Its literal correction theorem pays the last term in (19). Splitting the finite divisor sum at t=Y and substituting into GA-qCENT proves (5).

For the large part, group all exact copies with common
(d_lambda,v_lambda)=(d,v), exactly as in fact 8b46abe31a5ae8d7. Every kernel parameter and displayed pair condition is common to the grouped coordinates, while
sum_{lambda in Lambda(d,v)}
B_lambda(R)conjugate(B_lambda(R'))
 =<B_bold_{d,v}(R),B_bold_{d,v}(R')>.                                (20)
The definitions (6) give (7) immediately. Combining (19)-(20) proves GA-CqADD-VEC without altering any coefficient or selector.

We prove the exact norm ledger. Equation (8) follows because E has phi(t) coordinates, each of squared modulus 1/t. For (9), squarefree CRT factors the primitive-frequency Kloosterman energy. At a prime p and a nonzero inverse argument b,
sum_{a (mod p)}|S_p(a,b)|^2=p(p-1)                                  (21)
by additive Plancherel applied to the function
x mapsto 1_{x !=0}e_p(bx^{-1}).
The a=0 term is |S_p(0,b)|^2=1. Hence
sum_{a (mod p)}^*|S_p(a,b)|^2=p(p-1)-1=p^2-p-1.                      (22)
CRT makes the direct arguments at different primes range independently through the nonzero residues and leaves every inverse argument nonzero. Thus
sum_{a (mod t)}^*|S_t(a,-c s^{-1})|^2
 =product_{p|t}(p^2-p-1).                                            (23)
Dividing by t proves (9). Moreover
(1-1/p-1/p^2)>=(1-1/p)^2
for every prime p. Hence
||V||_2^2>=t(phi(t)/t)^2=phi(t)^2/t,
while ||V||_2^2<=t and ||E||_2^2=phi(t)/t. The standard elementary bound phi(t)=t^{1+o(1)} therefore gives (9a), with the stated fixed-power consequence only when t has a fixed-power lower bound.

Finally, for any T>=1, the literal definition (10) retains 1<t and restricts the same exact additive divisor sum, changing no outer coefficient or selector. Restricting the argument of (17) to 1<t and T<=t<2T gives
sum_{st=m,1<t,T<=t<2T}|mu(s)P_{t;c,s}(n)|/s
 <=x^{o(1)}T/m.                                                       (24)
Using (18) and the same copy/coefficient taxes proves (12) for the explicitly defined H_C^{q-add}(T). When T>Y, definition (10) makes this precisely the corresponding block of H_C^{q-add-large}; the right side of (12) then exceeds the target (11) by T/Y. Thus this absolute method supplies no such large block. For the exact full-conductor obstruction, take m=p prime. Equation (3) of fact a08224dfb222c580 has only s=1,t=p and gives
e_p(-c n^{-1})-mu(p)/p=P_{p;c,1}(n).
Since mu(p)=-1, this is (13), and the reverse triangle inequality gives the stated lower bound. This proves the scoped no-fit and all claimed exclusions.

glossary.E_{t;n}: The normalized primitive-frequency additive phase vector with coordinates t^{-1/2}e_t(an).
glossary.GA-CqADD-VEC: The exact deletion-preserving large additive-conductor Hilbert ray/Kloosterman residual after the additive t<=Y faces and centering correction are paid.
glossary.V_{t;c,s}: The normalized primitive-frequency Kloosterman vector with coordinates t^{-1/2}S_t(a,-c s^{-1}).

d34da66ba1ec4930.title: POLYLOGARITHMICALLY NEAR-MINIMAL FULL SIX-FACE C4 SUBRANGE AT THE CANONICAL MOMENT SCALE. Adopt the literal scalar scoped six-face canonical-dilator block of fact 66185bf160c191f4. Fix a real constant C>=0 and assume
d34da66ba1ec4930.author: slava chan
d34da66ba1ec4930.statement:
POLYLOGARITHMICALLY NEAR-MINIMAL FULL SIX-FACE C4 SUBRANGE AT THE CANONICAL MOMENT SCALE. Adopt the literal scalar scoped six-face canonical-dilator block of fact 66185bf160c191f4. Fix a real constant C>=0 and assume
min{B,Dcal}<=Z^4(log(2Q))^C.                                      (1)
Then, for every epsilon>0,
sum_lambda|T_lambda(1)|^2
<<_{epsilon,C}Q^epsilon BQ^2F^2/Dcal.                              (2)
Thus the complete scoped six-face scalar moment on this subrange is already bounded by the second term of the canonical marked-dilator target
Q^epsilon[BQF+BQ^2F^2/Dcal].                                      (3)
Every literal amplitude, source weight, coprimality, order, collision, deletion and provenance mask, every ray-scale sum, all exact copies, and the varying v_lambda remain included through fact 66185bf160c191f4.

For a fixed C, the complementary blocks satisfy
B>Z^4(log(2Q))^C and Dcal>Z^4(log(2Q))^C.                          (4)
No estimate for (4), vector-valued transfer, other centered-face families, complete C4 anatomy, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
d34da66ba1ec4930.proof:
Fact 66185bf160c191f4 gives
sum_lambda|T_lambda(1)|^2
<<_eta Q^eta
 min{Dcal/Z^4,B/Z^4}
 [BQ^2F^2/Dcal]                                                    (5)
for every eta>0. Assumption (1) implies
min{Dcal/Z^4,B/Z^4}<=(log(2Q))^C.                                 (6)
Given epsilon>0, apply (5) with eta=epsilon/2. For sufficiently large Q,
(log(2Q))^C<=Q^(epsilon/2).
Insert this into (5) to prove (2); the bounded remaining range of Q is absorbed into the implied constant. Since the second term in (3) equals the right side of (2), equation (3) follows. The negation of (1) is exactly (4). All literal-retention assertions are inherited from the predecessor fact.

d399d1df6821854c.title: BUFFER-EXTENDED COMPLETE-FREQUENCY SEPARATED-OUTER ONE-PRIME TRACE
d399d1df6821854c.author: slava chan
d399d1df6821854c.statement:
BUFFER-EXTENDED COMPLETE-FREQUENCY SEPARATED-OUTER ONE-PRIME TRACE.

Fix integers J,C_A>=1, a constant C>=1, and 0<kappa<=1/100. Put sigma=kappa/100 and beta_1=6/5-3sigma. Let Q be sufficiently large, let 1<=beta<=beta_1, and put B=Q^beta, H_T=B/Q and S_0=H_T^2Q^(3sigma).

Let V,P>=1 be dyadic scales with C^(-1)B<=VP<=CB and V<=S_0. Let xi_v be supported on squarefree V<=v<2V and satisfy |xi_v|<=tau_J(v). Assume that every supported v is coprime to every prime p with P<=p<2P that occurs in the sum. No restriction is imposed on the sizes of the prime divisors of v.

Let A be a fixed nonzero integer with |A|<=Q^(C_A), let |c_q|<=1 for Q<=q<2Q, let G>0 and put H_P=H_T/G. For every dyadic integer F>=1, let nu_F(h) be supported on F<=|h|<2F with |nu_F(h)|<=tau_J(|h|), let omega_F satisfy for every fixed J_0>=1
|omega_F|<=C(J_0)min(1,(F/H_P)^(-J_0)),
and let Psi_F be a fixed-complexity uniformly scaled-smooth projective amplitude in q/Q, |h|/F, v/V and p/P. Define
T_sep=H_P^(-1) sum_F omega_F sum_{Q<=q<2Q}c_q
 sum_{F<=|h|<2F}nu_F(h)
 sum_{v,p; p prime; gcd(vp,q)=1}
 xi_v Psi_F(q/Q,|h|/F,v/V,p/P)e_q(Ah(vp)^(-1)).

(i) If G>=1, then T_sep=O(GQ^(2-delta_1)) for some fixed delta_1>0.
(ii) If 0<eta<sigma and Q^(-sigma+eta)<=G<=Q^(sigma-eta), then T_sep=O(Q^(2-delta_2)) for some fixed delta_2>0.

The estimate includes H_P<1, all actual dyadic integer-frequency blocks, a fixed possibly nonunit target A, unrestricted gcd(h,q), proper prime powers and the multiplier-one short Type-I branch. It is uniform under polylogarithmically many one-variable and uniformly projective smooth labels. No arbitrary joint deletion and no modulus-dependent Type-I unit are allowed.

glossary.T_sep: The buffer-extended complete-frequency separated-outer one-prime reciprocal trace.

d3fde76ac4c8c20d.title: Let b>1 be an integer, let L_0 and h be integers, and let f be a finite complex-valued function on the integers. For a residue u modulo b define
d3fde76ac4c8c20d.author: slava chan
d3fde76ac4c8c20d.statement:
Let b>1 be an integer, let L_0 and h be integers, and let f be a finite complex-valued function on the integers. For a residue u modulo b define
F_b(u)=sum_{a congruent to u modulo b}f(a)
and
widehat F_b(n)=sum_{u modulo b}F_b(u)e_b(-nu),
where e_b(t)=exp(2 pi i t/b). Then the exact completion identity is
sum_{a in Z, gcd(a,b)=1} f(a)e_b(L_0h a^(-1))
 =b^(-1)sum_{n modulo b}widehat F_b(n)S(n,L_0h;b),                         (1)
where S is the classical Kloosterman sum of fact b302e2cd6d611a35. Parseval gives
sum_{n modulo b}|widehat F_b(n)|^2
 =b sum_{u modulo b}|F_b(u)|^2.                                          (2)
If f is supported on an integer interval of length A_len<b, then every residue has at most one representative in that interval and the right side of (2) is
b sum_a|f(a)|^2. Thus completion creates a full dual n-axis modulo b; it does not shorten that axis.

Apply this to a separated smooth mode of the nonzero Poisson formula in fact df9748efe29ab475. On its g=1 layer, write D=x^(1/2+o(1)), M=x^(1/2+o(1)), R=x^(rho+o(1)), and suppose
1/2<rho<2/3.
Then b is comparable to R, the incomplete a-length is A_len comparable to D<b, and the natural h-length is
H_len=R/M=x^(rho-1/2+o(1))
 =b^(1-1/(2rho)+o(1))
 <=b^(1/4+o(1)).                                                         (3)
Consequently the direct completion (1) presents the live near-diagonal residual as a fixed-b classical Kloosterman bilinear form only with one full coefficient axis of length b and one axis of length at most b^(1/4+o(1)). Before smooth separation its completed coefficient widehat F_b(n) may also depend jointly on h; separation is an additional projective step.

This completed shape is not a direct specialization of either of the following recent square-root Kloosterman results.

First, Pascadi, arXiv:2511.08445, Theorem 1.1, assumes both arbitrary coefficient lengths are at most b^(1/2+o(1)) and gives a b^(-1/700+o(1)) saving for that two-short-axis fixed-modulus form. The full n-axis in (1) has length b, so this length hypothesis fails.

Second, Blomer and Pascadi, arXiv:2607.24311, Theorem 5.5, does accept arbitrary interval lengths 1<=M_1,N_1<=b, but its bound is
|sum_{m,n; gcd(m,n,b)=1}alpha_m beta_n S(a_0m,n;b)|
 <=||alpha||_2||beta||_2 b^(1+o(1))H_BP(M_1,N_1,b),
for a_0 coprime to b, where
H_BP(M_1,N_1,b)
= M_1^(1/8)((b+M_1N_1)(b+N_1^2))^(1/16)b^(-1/4)
  min(b/M_1,b^(1/2))^(1/16)
 +(N_1^2/b^2+N_1^(1/2)M_1(b+N_1^2)/b^(5/2))^(1/16)
 +(M_1^(1/3)+N_1^(1/3))/b^(1/5)
 +(M_1^(1/2)N_1^(1/6)+M_1^(1/6)N_1^(1/2))/b^(7/18)
 +(M_1^(1/15)+N_1^(1/15))/b^(1/15).
For the completion (1), taking the full-dual length M_1=b makes
H_BP(b,N_1,b)>=1. Therefore this direct theorem application supplies no fixed-power saving over the Fourier-trivial scale ||alpha||_2||beta||_2b^(1+o(1)), even before paying the sum over the varying modulus b, its Möbius coefficient, gcd sectors, and smooth-separation cost.

This is a scoped no-direct-completion theorem for the residual wedge in fact 1e2d635f6691e832. It does not rule out a different transform preserving two short axes, cancellation in the full dual coefficients, a theorem averaging the varying moduli b with their Möbius signs, or any new estimate acting directly on the original Kloosterman-fraction form.
d3fde76ac4c8c20d.proof:
Finite Fourier inversion on Z/bZ gives
F_b(u)=b^(-1)sum_{n modulo b}widehat F_b(n)e_b(nu).
Insert this expression into the left side of (1), grouped by u=a modulo b. Only unit residues u occur. Interchanging the finite sums gives
b^(-1)sum_n widehat F_b(n)
 sum_{u modulo b,gcd(u,b)=1}e_b(nu+L_0h u^(-1)).
The inner sum is S(n,L_0h;b) by the definition in fact b302e2cd6d611a35. This proves (1). Additive character orthogonality gives (2). If the support interval has length less than b, two distinct supported integers cannot be congruent modulo b, so sum_u|F_b(u)|^2=sum_a|f(a)|^2.

We now check the scale claim from the verified Poisson formula. In fact df9748efe29ab475 one writes d=ga, r=gb and has a comparable to D/g, b comparable to R/g, while the nonzero frequency length is R/(gM). On g=1 this gives A_len comparable to D, modulus b comparable to R, and H_len comparable to R/M. In the top logarithmic situation of fact 1e2d635f6691e832, D=x^(1/2+o(1)) and DM is comparable to x, so M=x^(1/2+o(1)). If R=x^(rho+o(1)), then b=x^(rho+o(1)) and
H_len=x^(rho-1/2+o(1)).
Since log b=(rho+o(1))log x, division gives
log(H_len)/log b=1-1/(2rho)+o(1).
For rho<2/3, this exponent is at most 1/4+o(1), proving (3). Since rho>1/2, A_len/b=x^(1/2-rho+o(1)) tends to zero, so A_len<b for sufficiently large x and the injective-residue Parseval identity applies.

The exact formula (1) has n running over every residue modulo b. No support restriction on widehat F_b follows from finite Fourier inversion; Parseval instead records its full-axis norm. If the original smooth amplitude is first separated into products of functions of h,a,b, formula (1) yields a classical Kloosterman bilinear form in n and h for each separated term. Without that separation, the transform of the a-weight depends on h, so the n,h coefficient is joint rather than the product of two arbitrary one-variable sequences. Either way, a direct use of a fixed-modulus two-axis theorem must confront the full n-axis.

We reproduce the external theorem slots used in the audit. Pascadi, arXiv:2511.08445, Theorem 1.1 states, in the notation needed here, that when two arbitrary coefficient lengths M_1,N_1 satisfy M_1,N_1<<b^(1/2+o(1)), the corresponding coprime classical Kloosterman bilinear form at fixed modulus b is at most the product of the two l2 norms times b^(1-1/700+o(1)). In (1) the n-axis has M_1=b, which is larger than b^(1/2+o(1)), so the theorem cannot be specialized with that axis.

Blomer--Pascadi, arXiv:2607.24311, Theorem 5.5 states the full unequal-length bound and the explicit positive sum H_BP displayed in the statement. On setting M_1=b, its last summand is
(b^(1/15)+N_1^(1/15))/b^(1/15)
=1+(N_1/b)^(1/15)>=1.
All other summands are nonnegative. Hence H_BP(b,N_1,b)>=1, and the furnished upper bound is at least the baseline expression ||alpha||_2||beta||_2b^(1+o(1).) In particular, the theorem's displayed bound does not yield b^(-eta) relative saving for any fixed eta>0 on this specialization. Its balanced Theorem 1.1 cannot be substituted instead, because it also requires two axes near b^(1/2), whereas (1) has lengths b and at most b^(1/4+o(1)) in the wedge.

Both cited theorems are fixed-modulus results. Applying either separately for each b and summing absolute values does not preserve possible cancellation from the outer factor mu(b). The possible nonunit value of L_0 modulo b and the exact gcd restriction in the external theorems are additional obligations, but the length calculation already blocks a direct power-saving import even in the favorable unit and coprime subcase. This proves the scoped conclusion. No assertion is made about transformations or theorems outside the stated completion route.

glossary.A_len: the length of the incomplete unit variable a
glossary.F_b: the periodization modulo b of a finite a-weight f
glossary.H_BP(M_1,N_1,b): the explicit unequal-length factor from Blomer--Pascadi Theorem 5.5
glossary.H_len: the nonzero Poisson-frequency length R/M in the g=1 layer
glossary.widehat F_b: the additive Fourier transform of F_b modulo b

d43944f35c05a407.title: COMPOSITE-MODULUS MODULAR-HYPERBOLA COUNT IN TWO ARBITRARY INTERVALS
d43944f35c05a407.author: slava chan
d43944f35c05a407.statement:
COMPOSITE-MODULUS MODULAR-HYPERBOLA COUNT IN TWO ARBITRARY INTERVALS.

Let n>=2 and A be integers with gcd(A,n)=1. Let I and J be cyclic intervals in Z/nZ of cardinalities U and W, respectively, where 1<=U,W<=n. Define
  N_A(I,J)
  =#{(q,m) in I times J:gcd(q,n)=1, qm congruent A modulo n}. (1)
Then
  N_A(I,J)
  =phi(n)UW/n^2
   +O(tau(n)^2[(U+W)n^(-1/2)log(2n)
                +n^(1/2)log(2n)^2]).                        (2)
In particular, for every epsilon>0,
  N_A(I,J)
  <<_epsilon n^epsilon[UW/n+n^(1/2)].                        (3)
The bounds are uniform in the locations of I and J, including intervals which wrap around zero.

The same conclusion, with a change of the absolute implied constant, holds when I and J are ordinary integer intervals of lengths at most n and are reduced modulo n.
d43944f35c05a407.proof:
Write e_n(x)=exp(2 pi i x/n). For a cyclic interval K in Z/nZ define its unnormalized Fourier transform
  Khat(r)=sum_{x in K}e_n(-rx),  r modulo n.                 (4)
Fourier inversion and the condition gcd(A,n)=1 give
  N_A(I,J)
  =n^(-2)sum_{r,s modulo n}Ihat(r)Jhat(s)S(r,sA;n),          (5)
where
  S(r,sA;n)=sum_{x modulo n, gcd(x,n)=1}
              e_n(rx+sA xbar)                               (6)
is the classical Kloosterman sum and xbar is the inverse of x modulo n. Indeed, expand the two interval indicators at x and A xbar, then sum over all units x.

Raphael S. Steiner, arXiv:2302.06409, Lemma 8, defines
  T_f(r,s;q|c)
  =sum_{x modulo c, gcd(x,c)=1, x congruent f modulo q}
       exp(2 pi i (rx+s xbar)/c)
and proves
  |T_f(r,s;q|c)|
  <=2^(3/2)tau(c)min(c/q,gcd(c/q,r,s)^(1/2)c^(1/2)).         (7)
The proof first treats q=1,2 by the classical Weil bound and then proves the general progression statement by twisted multiplicativity and prime-power analysis. Apply (7) with q=1, c=n, and replace s by sA. Since A is a unit modulo n,
  gcd(n,r,sA)=gcd(n,r,s).
Thus
  |S(r,sA;n)|
  <=2^(3/2)tau(n)gcd(n,r,s)^(1/2)n^(1/2).                   (8)
For r=s=0, equation (6) gives S(0,0;n)=phi(n).

We now estimate the nonzero Fourier pairs. For a divisor d of n put
  L_d(K)=sum_{r modulo n, d divides r}|Khat(r)|.             (9)
If K has cardinality T, the geometric-series formula gives
  |Khat(r)|<=min(T,n/(2|r|_n))                               (10)
for r nonzero, where |r|_n is the least positive distance of r from zero modulo n. Writing r=da with a modulo n/d and summing the harmonic series gives
  L_d(K)<=T+2(n/d)(1+log n).                                 (11)
The constant 2 is sufficient after pairing a and n/d-a; changing it only changes the absolute constants below.

For every positive integer g,
  g^(1/2)<=sum_{d|g}d^(1/2).                                (12)
Use (12) with g=gcd(n,r,s), then (9), to obtain
  sum_{r,s modulo n,(r,s)!=(0,0)}
    |Ihat(r)Jhat(s)|gcd(n,r,s)^(1/2)
  <=sum_{d|n}d^(1/2)[L_d(I)L_d(J)-UW].                      (13)
The subtraction is valid because the omitted pair r=s=0 contributes
  |Ihat(0)Jhat(0)|=UW
inside every divisor-d summand.

Insert (11) into (13). With C=2(1+log n),
  L_d(I)L_d(J)-UW
  <=C(U+W)n/d+C^2n^2/d^2.                                  (14)
Therefore the right side of (13) is at most
  C(U+W)n sum_{d|n}d^(-1/2)
  +C^2n^2sum_{d|n}d^(-3/2)
  <=C(U+W)n tau(n)+C^2n^2tau(n).                            (15)
Separate r=s=0 in (5), apply (8) and (15) to the rest, and divide by n^2. This gives
  N_A(I,J)
  =phi(n)UW/n^2
   +O(tau(n)^2[(U+W)n^(-1/2)(1+log n)
               +n^(1/2)(1+log n)^2]),
which is (2) after replacing 1+log n by a constant multiple of log(2n).

The inequalities phi(n)<=n, tau(n)<<_epsilon n^(epsilon/3), and log(2n)<<_epsilon n^(epsilon/3), with epsilon divided among the factors, give (3).

An ordinary integer interval of length at most n reduces modulo n to either one cyclic interval or a disjoint union of two cyclic intervals. Apply (2) to at most four pairs of cyclic pieces and add them. This proves the final assertion.

glossary.L_d(K): The l1 mass of the interval Fourier transform restricted to frequencies divisible by d.
glossary.N_A(I,J): The number of modular-hyperbola pairs in the two intervals I and J.

d4402b645abcaf56.title: SUP-NORM CARRIER-CORRELATED DIGIT REFINEMENT FOR THE COMPLETE GENERIC FIXED FIBRE
d4402b645abcaf56.author: slava chan
d4402b645abcaf56.statement:
SUP-NORM CARRIER-CORRELATED DIGIT REFINEMENT FOR THE COMPLETE GENERIC FIXED FIBRE.

Fix real constants L_0>=1, L_1>=1, A>=1 and D>=0. Let m>=9 be odd with m>4L_1+1, put q=m^2, and let 2<=H<=m^A. Let C be a nonzero integer with |C|<=H^(L_0), let K be an integer with gcd(m,2K)=1, and fix s in {1,-1}. Let I_a,I_c,I_1,I_2 be integer intervals of cardinality at most L_1m, with I_1,I_2 positive, and assume that every integer in their union has absolute value at most L_0H^3.

For a in I_a, c in I_c, n_1 in I_1, n_2 in I_2 put b=n_2 and d=-n_1. Let E_outer_gen consist of tuples
 (a,c,n_1,n_2,u,k,r_2,r_3)
in I_a times I_c times I_1 times I_2 times {0,...,m-1} times Z times Z times Z
such that:
(i) a,c,n_1,n_2 are even;
(ii) r_2,r_3 are distinct primes in [H^2,2H^2), and gcd(m,r_2r_3)=1;
(iii)
 a n_2=K+2smu+km^2,qquad c n_1=a n_2-2K;                         (1)
(iv) the integers
 lambda_A=(b r_3-d r_2)/(2m),quad
 lambda_B=(a r_2-c r_3)/(2m),quad
 lambda_J=(ab-cd)/(4m)                                            (2)
exist, lambda_A and lambda_B have common sign s, and
 gcd(|lambda_A|,|lambda_B|)=1;
(v) r_1=|lambda_A| and r_4=|lambda_B| are primes in [H^2,2H^2), and r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4 are pairwise distinct;
(vi)
 gcd(C,r_1r_2r_3r_4)=1,quad lambda_J is nonzero,quad
 d r_2lambda_B-c r_3lambda_A=2sC;                                (3)
(vii)
 lambda_J is congruent to su modulo m,qquad
 k=2(lambda_J-su)/m.                                              (4)

Let F be supported on I_a, let W be any complex function modulo m, and let alpha,beta be supported on I_1,I_2. Let Omega_outer be any complex function on E_outer_gen, independent of Fourier characters, with
 |Omega_outer|<=(log(2H))^D.                                      (5)
Define
 T_outer_gen=sum_{E_outer_gen}
 F(a)W(u)alpha(n_1)beta(n_2)Omega_outer                            (6)
and
 V_F=||F||_infinity+sum_{z in Z}|F(z+1)-F(z)|.                     (7)
Then, for every epsilon>0,
 |T_outer_gen|
 <=C_{L_0,L_1,A,D,epsilon}m^(15/16+epsilon)
 V_F||W||_infinity||alpha||_2||beta||_2.                           (8)

More precisely, define
 C_outer(x)=sum_{E_outer_gen;ax congruent 1 modulo q}
 W(u)alpha(n_1)beta(n_2)Omega_outer                               (9)
for unit x modulo q, put C_outer(x)=0 on nonunits, and set
 C_outer_hat(p)=sum_{x modulo q}C_outer(x)e_q(-px).                (10)
Then
 ||C_outer_hat||_2
 <=C_{L_0,L_1,A,D,epsilon}q^(1/2+epsilon)
 ||W||_infinity||alpha||_2||beta||_2.                             (11)

For the literal centered quarter-range digit W_star of fact 076bc0ba8fc2536a one has ||W_star||_infinity<=1. Hence
 |T_outer_gen|
 <=C m^(15/16+epsilon)V_F||alpha||_2||beta||_2.                    (12)
For every fixed delta with 0<=delta<=1/80, this is at least as strong in its m-exponent as the m^(19/20-delta+epsilon) fixed-fibre target.

The refinement is carrier-correlated because both x-fibre multiplicity and fixed-column-pair multiplicity are counted only after the determinant, shared digit, complete coefficient matrix, and both recovered-prime/carrier gates are retained. It remains fixed in m,s,C,K and covers only the generic odd unit sector; it supplies no varying-parameter aggregation or K-nonunit estimate.
d4402b645abcaf56.proof:
The pointwise normalization and unitness are proved in fact f23bad095a2e6a52 from the displayed literal conditions. We prove a sharper coefficient norm by using two finite-degree projections.

Fix a unit x modulo q. Since |I_a|<q, at most one a in I_a has ax congruent to one modulo q. Equation (1) modulo m puts n_2 in the single residue class Kx modulo m, so I_2 contains at most L_1+1 choices. For fixed x,a,n_2, the residue u is unique because 2s is a unit modulo m. The positive n_1 divides the nonzero integer
 N_0=a n_2-2K=c n_1,
whose absolute value is at most L_0^2H^6<=L_0^2m^(6A). Fact 212d1415bf03c2a7 proves self-containedly that, for every eta>0, tau(|N_0|)<=C_eta|N_0|^eta. Apply it with eta chosen as epsilon/(12A), decreasing it further to absorb the fixed constant L_0; after the usual epsilon renaming, n_1 and hence c have O_{L_0,A,epsilon}(m^epsilon) possibilities. For each fixed coefficient matrix Q=((a,c),(n_1,n_2)), fact 1218e64e51ba3131 gives H^epsilon possible ordered prime pairs satisfying all normalized carrier conditions. Since H<=m^A, every x-fibre has
 O_{L_0,L_1,A,epsilon}(m^epsilon).                                (13)

Cauchy-Schwarz in each x-fibre and (5) give
 sum_x|C_outer(x)|^2
 <=C m^epsilon(log(2H))^(2D)
 sum_{E_outer_gen}|W(u)|^2|alpha(n_1)|^2|beta(n_2)|^2.             (14)
Fix an ordered pair (n_1,n_2). Reducing the first equation of (1) modulo m gives
 a congruent to K n_2^(-1) modulo m.                               (15)
An interval of cardinality at most L_1m contains at most L_1+1 integers in one residue class modulo m. Thus there are O_{L_1}(1) possible a. For each a, equation (1) uniquely determines c if it is integral, uniquely determines u in {0,...,m-1}, and then uniquely determines k. Hence Q is fixed. Fact 1218e64e51ba3131 again gives O(H^epsilon) ordered prime pairs for this fixed Q,C,K. Therefore
 M_{12}=max_{n_1,n_2}#{E_outer_gen tuples above (n_1,n_2)}
 =O_{L_0,L_1,A,epsilon}(m^epsilon).                               (16)

Use |W(u)|<=||W||_infinity in (14), group by (n_1,n_2), and apply (16):
 sum_{E_outer_gen}|W(u)|^2|alpha(n_1)|^2|beta(n_2)|^2
 <=C m^epsilon||W||_infinity^2
 ||alpha||_2^2||beta||_2^2.                                       (17)
Fixed powers of log(2H) are absorbed because H<=m^A. Equations (14)-(17) give
 ||C_outer||_2
 <=C m^epsilon||W||_infinity||alpha||_2||beta||_2.                 (18)
Additive Parseval modulo q yields (11).

Grouping (6) by x congruent to a^(-1) gives
 T_outer_gen=sum_{x modulo q;gcd(x,q)=1}C_outer(x)F_per(x^(-1)).
Fact 5b9e0311f7e49ea2 gives
 |T_outer_gen|<=Cq^(-1/32+epsilon)V_F||C_outer_hat||_2.
Insert (11) and q=m^2 to obtain (8).

Because m>=9, fact 076bc0ba8fc2536a applies. Its W_star takes the values 1-N/m on its literal residue interval and -N/m off it, with 0<=N/m<=1/2, so its supremum norm is at most one. This proves (12). Finally
 15/16=75/80<=76/80-delta=19/20-delta
for 0<=delta<=1/80. No varying outer parameter was summed, proving the scope.

glossary.M_{12}: the maximum number of admitted complete literal states over one fixed ordered column pair

d472dd752c1eb6a8.title: Let m>1 be an odd integer, and let K,r_2,r_3 be integers such that gcd(m,2 K r_2 r_3)=1. Define T_m to be the set of quadruples (a,b,c,d) modulo m satisfying
d472dd752c1eb6a8.author: slava chan
d472dd752c1eb6a8.statement:
Let m>1 be an odd integer, and let K,r_2,r_3 be integers such that gcd(m,2 K r_2 r_3)=1. Define T_m to be the set of quadruples (a,b,c,d) modulo m satisfying
b r_3-d r_2=0,  a r_2-c r_3=0,  ab-cd=0,  ab+cd=2 K  (mod m).
Then the map from the unit group modulo m to T_m given by
t -> (t r_2^{-1}, K r_2 t^{-1}, t r_3^{-1}, K r_3 t^{-1})  (mod m)
is a bijection. In fact the congruence ab-cd=0 is redundant: the other two linear congruences already imply it, and together with ab+cd=2 K they imply ab=cd=K modulo m.

Now let a,b,c,d be even integers, put Q=((a,c),(-d,b)), assume the exact identity ab+cd=2 K, and define
A=b r_3-d r_2, B=a r_2-c r_3, J=ab-cd, D=ad r_2^2-bc r_3^2.
If m divides A and B, then m divides J automatically, and the three integers
lambda_A=A/(2m), lambda_B=B/(2m), lambda_J=J/(4m)
are well defined. They satisfy
ab=K+2m lambda_J,  cd=K-2m lambda_J,
b lambda_B+c lambda_A=2 lambda_J r_2,
d lambda_B+a lambda_A=2 lambda_J r_3,
D=2m(d r_2 lambda_B-c r_3 lambda_A).
If moreover q=gcd(|A|,|B|)=2m, then gcd(|lambda_A|,|lambda_B|)=1.

If this lift is a normalized unit state of fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb, q=2m, and s is the common sign of A and B, then
lambda_A=s r_1, lambda_B=s r_4, lambda_J=s u,
and
d r_2 lambda_B-c r_3 lambda_A=2sC.

For every integer n, right multiplication by
U_n=((1,2nm),(0,1))
