takes Q to an even integral matrix Q_n with the same determinant and the same reduction modulo m, but changes the carries to
lambda_A(Q_n)=lambda_A-n d r_3,
lambda_B(Q_n)=lambda_B-n a r_3,
lambda_J(Q_n)=lambda_J-nad.
If Q is normalized, the sheared matrices Q_n are only generic integer lifts and need not remain normalized. Nevertheless, because normalized Q has nonzero a,d, the same torus point and determinant have lifts with unbounded coefficients and unbounded carries of either individual sign. Moreover, taking n=lambda_A gives
|lambda_A(Q_n)|=r_1 |1-d r_3|,
which is composite because r_1>=2 and |1-d r_3|>1. Thus the torus parameter t does not determine the exact normal carries, their signs or sizes, a dyadic prime window for the quotient |A|/(2m), or an integer coefficient box. The exact gcd, the second prime quotient, all pairwise-distinctness conditions, and all other literal packet selectors remain separate conditions to check on a chosen lift; no claim is made that each of those predicates changes in the displayed shear family. Hence this is an exact generic congruence parameterization, not a cancellation theorem and not a parameterization of the literal WF-RPS packets.
d472dd752c1eb6a8.proof:
All inverses in the first paragraph are modulo m. The coprimality hypothesis makes r_2 and r_3 units. The first two linear congruences give
b r_3=d r_2 and a r_2=c r_3.
Multiplication followed by cancellation of the unit r_2 r_3 yields ab=cd, proving that the J-congruence is redundant. The determinant congruence then gives 2ab=2 K and 2cd=2 K. Since m is odd, 2 is a unit, so ab=cd=K. The residue of K is a unit. A product is a unit in Z/mZ only if both factors are units: if xy has inverse z, then x(yz)=1 and (zx)y=1. Hence all four coefficient residues are units.

Set t=a r_2. Then t is a unit and the second linear congruence also gives t=c r_3. Consequently
a=t r_2^{-1}, c=t r_3^{-1}.
The product identities give
b=K a^{-1}=K r_2 t^{-1},
d=K c^{-1}=K r_3 t^{-1}.
Thus every element of T_m has the displayed form, and t=a r_2 proves uniqueness. Conversely, direct substitution for an arbitrary unit t gives
a r_2=c r_3=t,
b r_3=d r_2=K r_2 r_3 t^{-1},
ab=cd=K.
This proves the bijection. It also records every invertibility input: r_2 r_3 is cancelled to obtain J=0, 2 is cancelled to obtain ab=K, and K being a unit makes every coordinate and t a unit. No sign hypothesis is used. The excluded m=1 case is the vacuous one-element residue ring and carries no nontrivial conductor information.

For an even integer lift, A and B are even. Since m is odd and divides them, 2m divides each. The modular argument gives m|J. Since ab and cd are divisible by 4, also 4|J; coprimality of 4 and m gives 4m|J. Thus all three carries are integral.

Adding and subtracting ab+cd=2 K and ab-cd=J=4m lambda_J gives the two product identities. Expansion gives
bB+cA=J r_2 and dB+aA=J r_3.
Substitution of A=2m lambda_A, B=2m lambda_B, J=4m lambda_J and division by 2m gives the two linear carry identities. A further expansion gives
d r_2 B-c r_3 A=D,
and division by 2m proves the D-identity. If q=2m, scaling the gcd identity by 2m gives
gcd(|lambda_A|,|lambda_B|)=1.

For a normalized unit state, fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb gives
A=2v r_1, B=2v r_4, J=4uv, D=4vC, q=2|v|, v=sq/2.
When q=2m, one has v=sm. Division gives
lambda_A=s r_1, lambda_B=s r_4, lambda_J=su.
Comparing the two formulas for D gives
d r_2 lambda_B-c r_3 lambda_A=2sC.

Finally U_n is integral, has determinant one, and is the identity modulo m. Direct multiplication gives
Q_n=Q U_n=((a,c+2nma),(-d,b-2nmd)).
Thus Q_n is even, has determinant 2 K, and reduces to Q modulo m. Direct expansion gives
A(Q_n)=A-2nmd r_3,
B(Q_n)=B-2nma r_3,
J(Q_n)=J-4nmad,
which proves the carry transformation. On the normalized layer fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb gives a,d nonzero. Therefore the two varying coefficients and the first two carries are unbounded as n ranges over the integers, and changing the direction of n gives either individual sign for each nonconstant carry.

For the explicit failure of the prime quotient condition, start with normalized Q and choose the integer n=lambda_A=s r_1. Then
lambda_A(Q_n)=lambda_A(1-d r_3),
so its absolute value is r_1 |1-d r_3|. Here d is a nonzero even integer and r_3 is a positive prime, hence |d r_3|>=4 and |1-d r_3|>=3. The displayed absolute value is therefore composite. This sheared Q_n is not asserted to be normalized; it is an even, exact-determinant lift with the same torus residue and demonstrates precisely which information the modular parameterization has discarded. The remaining literal predicates are extra lift tests, not conclusions of the congruence theorem.

glossary.Q_n: the determinant-preserving integer shear lift Q U_n
glossary.T_m: the residue locus modulo m cut out by the two transport congruences, signed-determinant congruence, and fixed-determinant congruence
glossary.m: the odd generic full-conductor modulus q/2
glossary.t: the unique unit-torus parameter a r_2=c r_3 modulo m

d481cd487c91eb70.title: EXACT MEAN-ZERO REDUCTION OF THE SHORT-WINDOW PMD FOURTH MOMENT
d481cd487c91eb70.author: slava chan
d481cd487c91eb70.statement:
EXACT MEAN-ZERO REDUCTION OF THE SHORT-WINDOW PMD FOURTH MOMENT.

Adopt the hypotheses and notation of fact 3704d40c75e8269c. Thus P>2Q, cal P is a set of primes p in [P,2P), J>=1, V>=2, the coefficients b_{v,s}(q) are bounded by one and independent of p, and the squared literal weights are |xi_v/v|^2. For each v,s,p let I_{v,s,p} be a residue interval modulo p of cardinality L_{v,s,p}, where
  1<=L_{v,s,p}<=L<=P,
and put
  W_{v,s,p}=1_{I_{v,s,p}},
  alpha_{v,s,p}=L_{v,s,p}/p,
  W^circ_{v,s,p}=W_{v,s,p}-alpha_{v,s,p}.                 (1)
Then
  sum_{r modulo p}W^circ_{v,s,p}(r)=0.                     (2)

For fixed v,s,p, define S_p(h), T(k), T_0(k), and T_neq(k)=T(k)-T_0(k) from b=b_{v,s} exactly as in fact 27540b4094f677f4, and define
  What(k)=sum_{r modulo p}W(r)e_p(-kr).                     (3)
Let E_p(W;b) be the signed nonzero-integer-determinant centered energy in fact 3704d40c75e8269c. Then exactly
 E_p(W_{v,s,p};b_{v,s})
  =alpha_{v,s,p}E_p(1;b_{v,s})
      +E_p(W^circ_{v,s,p};b_{v,s})                         (4)
  =L_{v,s,p}p^(-2)T_neq(0)
      +p^(-2)sum_{k modulo p; k nonzero}
          What_{v,s,p}(k)T_neq(k).                         (5)
Thus the zero Fourier shift has not been discarded: it is exactly the density multiple of the complete D=0-subtracted energy. The remaining discrepancy has zero mean in the physical residue and contains exactly all nonzero Fourier shifts, still with the all-shift rational-slope subtraction inside T_neq.

The complete-density part of the full literal family already satisfies, for every epsilon>0,
 sum_{V<=v<2V}sum_{s modulo v}|xi_v/v|^2
   sum_{p in cal P}
    |alpha_{v,s,p}E_p(1;b_{v,s})|
 <<_{J,epsilon}(QV)^epsilon
    [L Q^(8/3)+(L/P)Q^4].                                 (6)
Consequently, the localized comparison estimate
 |sum_{V<=v<2V}sum_{s modulo v}|xi_v/v|^2
   sum_{p in cal P}E_p(W_{v,s,p};b_{v,s})|
 <<_{J,epsilon}(QV)^epsilon
    [P Q^(8/3)+(L/P)Q^4]                                  (7)
would follow from the single mean-zero discrepancy estimate
 |sum_{V<=v<2V}sum_{s modulo v}|xi_v/v|^2
   sum_{p in cal P}E_p(W^circ_{v,s,p};b_{v,s})|
 <<_{J,epsilon}(QV)^epsilon P Q^(8/3).                     (8)
Equations (4)-(8) are an exact reduction, not a proof of (8).
d481cd487c91eb70.proof:
The map W -> Gamma_W is complex-linear by its definition in fact 3704d40c75e8269c. Hence E_p(W;b), which is the quadruple sum against Gamma_W, is also complex-linear in W. Equation (1) therefore gives (4). Equation (2) follows because the interval has L_{v,s,p} residues and the constant alpha_{v,s,p} has total mass p alpha_{v,s,p}=L_{v,s,p}.

Fact 27540b4094f677f4 gives, with exact rational-slope subtraction at every shift,
 E_p(W;b)=p^(-2)sum_{k modulo p}What(k)T_neq(k).            (9)
The Fourier transform of the constant function alpha is zero at every nonzero k and equals p alpha=L_{v,s,p} at k=0. Therefore
  (W^circ)hat(0)=0,
  (W^circ)hat(k)=What(k) for k nonzero.                    (10)
For the complete function 1, its transform equals p at k=0 and zero otherwise, so
 E_p(1;b)=p^(-1)T_neq(0).                                  (11)
Substitute (10)-(11) into (4). This proves (5) and the assertion that the zero shift is exactly accounted for rather than deleted.

It remains to prove (6). Fact 3704d40c75e8269c gives uniformly in v,s,p
 |E_p(1;b_{v,s})|
 <<_epsilon Q^epsilon[Q^(8/3)+Q^4/p].                     (12)
Since alpha_{v,s,p}<=L/p, p>=P, and cal P contains at most 2P primes,
 sum_{p in cal P}alpha_{v,s,p}|E_p(1;b_{v,s})|
 <<_epsilon Q^epsilon[
   (2P)(L/P)Q^(8/3)+(2P)(L/P)(Q^4/P)]
 << Q^epsilon[LQ^(8/3)+(L/P)Q^4].                         (13)
The squared (v,s)-coefficient mass is at most V^epsilon by fact d061fc4dc153e309. Multiplying (13) by that mass and adjusting epsilon proves (6).

Finally, insert (4) into the left side of (7) and use the triangle inequality only between its two exact global pieces: the complete-density piece and the mean-zero discrepancy piece. Bound the first by (6) and assume (8) for the second. Because L<=P, one has LQ^(8/3)<=PQ^(8/3). The resulting bound is (7). No triangle over individual Fourier shifts or over the linear coefficients xi_v/v occurs. This proves every asserted implication.

glossary.W^circ_{v,s,p}: The mean-zero part of the interval indicator W_{v,s,p}.
glossary.alpha_{v,s,p}: The residue density L_{v,s,p}/p of the interval.
glossary.localized comparison estimate: The target inequality (7) for the D=0-subtracted centered energy.

d49a344e18754be9.title: U/Z ADMISSIBILITY OF A FULL SMOOTH POISSON ROW
d49a344e18754be9.author: slava chan
d49a344e18754be9.statement:
U/Z ADMISSIBILITY OF A FULL SMOOTH POISSON ROW.

Fix a constant C_1>=1. Let Q>=2 and 1<=H<=Q. Let v be a positive integer, let p>2Q be prime, put n=vp, and assume
  n>=QH.                                                     (1)
Let A be an integer and let cal Q be a subset of the integers in [Q,2Q) such that gcd(q,n)=1 for every q in cal Q. For each q in cal Q let F_q be a smooth complex function supported in [Q,2Q) and satisfying
  |F_q(t)|<=C_1 for every real t.                            (2)
Define the full nonzero-Poisson row a_q and its exact source--density decomposition
  a_q=u_q-z_q
as in fact ace362082848a702:
  u_q=sum_{m in Z; qm congruent A modulo n}F_q(m),
  z_q=n^(-1)Fhat_q(0).                                      (3)

Then each u_q is either zero or consists of one source value F_q(m), so
  |u_q|<=C_1.                                               (4)
The support of u is contained in an actual-source graph
  qm+nk=A,qquad q,m in [Q,2Q),
and for every epsilon>0,
  #{q:u_q nonzero}<<_{C_1,epsilon}Q^epsilon Q/H.             (5)
Moreover,
  |z_q|<=C_1/H                                              (6)
for every q. Thus, up to the harmless divisor factor Q^epsilon in the sparse support, u is a type-(U) row and z is a type-(Z) row in fact 0e8ef74ba484418d.

This statement requires the complete sum over all nonzero Poisson frequencies in fact ace362082848a702. It does not apply to one frequency, one dyadic frequency block, or a frequency-dependent deletion unless the omitted frequency siblings are first restored exactly.
d49a344e18754be9.proof:
Because p>2Q and v>=1, one has n=vp>2Q. The support interval [Q,2Q) has length Q<n. Therefore it contains at most one integer in any fixed residue class modulo n. Since gcd(q,n)=1, the congruence qm congruent A modulo n selects one residue class for m. Hence the sum defining u_q has at most one term, and (2) proves (4). Every nonzero term has k=(A-qm)/n in Z and therefore lies on qm+nk=A.

It remains to count these terms without imposing any coprimality condition on m. As q and m range in [Q,2Q), the product qm ranges in an interval of length less than 4Q^2. The identity qm=A-nk therefore permits at most
  1+4Q^2/n                                                   (7)
integer values of k. For each fixed k, the positive integer A-nk=qm is less than 4Q^2. By the fixed-power divisor estimate in fact e705401df9f0709e, it has O_epsilon(Q^epsilon) ordered positive factorizations. Restricting q,m to their intervals and q to cal Q only deletes factorizations. Hence
  #{q:u_q nonzero}
  <<_epsilon Q^epsilon(1+Q^2/n).                            (8)
By (1), Q^2/n<=Q/H. Since H<=Q, one has 1<=Q/H, and (8) proves (5).

By the Fourier definition,
  |Fhat_q(0)|=|integral_R F_q(t)dt|
   <=C_1Q,                                                   (9)
because F_q is supported in an interval of length Q. Equations (1), (3), and (9) give
  |z_q|<=C_1Q/n<=C_1/H,
which is (6).

Finally, the identity a=u-z in fact ace362082848a702 is obtained by restoring every h in Z and then deleting only h=0. A proper subset of the nonzero h-axis has no such progression-Poisson identity without adding its omitted complement. This proves the scope statement.

glossary.U/Z admissibility: The sparse-source and dense-small coefficient bounds required by fact 0e8ef74ba484418d.
glossary.full smooth Poisson row: The coefficient formed by summing every nonzero Fourier frequency of one compactly supported progression weight.

d4bea99f55cf1827.title: Let \(K:\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\to[0,\infty)\) be a nonnegative real trigonometric polynomial of degree at most the positive integer \(R\). Let \(L\ge1\) be an integer, let \(\|t\|\) denote circular distance from \(t\) to the nearest integer, and define
d4bea99f55cf1827.author: slava chan
d4bea99f55cf1827.statement:
Let \(K:\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\to[0,\infty)\) be a nonnegative real trigonometric polynomial of degree at most the positive integer \(R\). Let \(L\ge1\) be an integer, let \(\|t\|\) denote circular distance from \(t\) to the nearest integer, and define
\[
 Q_L(K)=
 \int_{\mathbb R/\mathbb Z}\int_{\mathbb R/\mathbb Z}
 K(\alpha)K(\beta)
 \left(1-2L\|\alpha-\beta\|\right)_+
 d\alpha d\beta.                                       \tag{1}
\]
Then \(Q_L(K)\ge0\) and
\[
 K(0)\ll (R+L)\sqrt{Q_L(K)},                            \tag{2}
\]
with an absolute implied constant.

For the exact top-band application, fix
\[
 1/2<\alpha_0<\beta_0<1,\quad \eta>0,\quad\rho>0,
 \quad B_{\rm src}>0.
\]
Let \(W\) and \(\Phi\) be bounded real functions supported in
\([\alpha_0,\beta_0]\) and \([1/2,2]\). Let \(N=2x\) be an integer, put
\[
 T_x=(\log x)^{6+\eta+\rho},
\]
and assume
\[
 {1\over2}x^{1/2}(\log x)^{-B_{\rm src}}\le D\le2x^{1/2},
 \qquad D>2T_x,\qquad U>0.
\]
Let \(\mu\) be the Möbius function, extend \(\Lambda\) by zero on nonpositive integers, and put
\[
 {\cal I}_D=\{d\ge2:(d,N)=1,\ \mu(d)\ne0, d\le x^{1/2},\ \Phi(d/D)\ne0\}.
\]
For positive integers \(s,m,w\), define
\[
 f_{s,m}(w)=
 {\bf1}_{sw\in{\cal I}_D}\mu(w)\Phi(sw/D)W(smw/x)
 \Phi((N-smw)/U)\Lambda(N-smw),
\]
\[
 F_s(\theta)=
 \left(\sum_wf_{s,m}(w)e(\theta w)\right)_{m\ge1},
 \qquad
 K_s(\theta)=\|F_s(\theta)\|_{\ell^2_m}^{,2},
 \qquad e(t)=\exp(2\pi it).
\]
For \(1\le s<T_x^2\), define
\[
 R_s=\left\lceil{3D\over2s}\right\rceil,
 \qquad
 L_s^{\rm ceil}=\left\lceil{D\over sT_x}\right\rceil.             \tag{3}
\]
Then \(K_s\) is a nonnegative real trigonometric polynomial of degree at most \(R_s\), and
\[
 K_s(0)\ll
 (R_s+L_s^{\rm ceil})
 \sqrt{Q_{L_s^{\rm ceil}}(K_s)}.                      \tag{4}
\]

Define the signed small-projector energy
\[
 {\cal E}_{<}=
 \sum_{g<T_x}\sum_{r<T_x}\mu(r)K_{gr}(0).              \tag{5}
\]
Then
\[
 |{\cal E}_{<}|
 \ll
 \sum_{g,r<T_x}
 (R_{gr}+L_{gr}^{\rm ceil})
 \sqrt{Q_{L_{gr}^{\rm ceil}}(K_{gr})}.                 \tag{6}
\]
Consequently the positive harmonic estimate
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \sum_{g,r<T_x}
 (R_{gr}+L_{gr}^{\rm ceil})
 \sqrt{Q_{L_{gr}^{\rm ceil}}(K_{gr})}
 \ll xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta}
 \quad}                                                  \tag{TB-QTRI}
\]
implies the signed coprimality-projector bound
\[
 |{\cal E}_{<}|\ll xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta},
\]
hence the hard covariance estimate of fact 1f5316e61daf156d.

This triangular positive condition is implied by TB-VL2 of fact 6a2652fb92d86417. More precisely, let
\[
 J_s=\sup_{\theta_0}
 \int_{\theta_0-D^{-1}sT_x/2}^{\theta_0+D^{-1}sT_x/2}
 K_s(\theta)d\theta.
\]
Then
\[
 Q_{L_s^{\rm ceil}}(K_s)\le J_s\Delta_s,
 \qquad
 \Delta_s=\int_{\mathbb R/\mathbb Z}K_s(\theta)d\theta
 \ll {x(\log x)^2\over s}.                            \tag{7}
\]
If
\[
 \sum_{g,r<T_x}{J_{gr}\over g^2r^2}
 \ll {xT_x\over D}(\log x)^{-4-\eta},                 \tag{8}
\]
then the left side of TB-QTRI is
\[
 \ll x\sqrt{DT_x}(\log x)^{-1-\eta/2}\log(2T_x)
 =o\left(xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta}\right).                \tag{9}
\]
Thus TB-QTRI is a different, positive fourth-order local-circle interface; unlike uncentered TB-VL2, it is not shown here to force logarithmic cancellation of \(\Delta_1\). No estimate for \(Q_L(K_s)\) is asserted.
d4bea99f55cf1827.proof:
Let
\[
 M=\max_{\theta\in\mathbb R/\mathbb Z}K(\theta),
\]
and choose \(\theta_*\) with \(K(\theta_*)=M\). Bernstein's inequality for a trigonometric polynomial of degree at most \(R\) gives
\[
 \|K'\|_\infty\le2\pi RM.                            \tag{10}
\]
Put
\[
 \delta={1\over16\pi(R+L)}
\]
and let \(I\) be the circular interval
\(\|\theta-\theta_*\|\le\delta\). For \(\theta\in I\), (10) gives
\[
 K(\theta)\ge M-2\pi RM\delta\ge {7M\over8}.        \tag{11}
\]
For \(\alpha,\beta\in I\),
\[
 2L\|\alpha-\beta\|
 \le4L\delta\le {1\over4\pi},
\]
so
\[
 \left(1-2L\|\alpha-\beta\|\right)_+\ge {1\over2}.              \tag{12}
\]
Equations (11)--(12) give
\[
 Q_L(K)\ge {1\over2}
 \left(\int_IK(\theta)d\theta\right)^2
 \gg M^2\delta^2.
\]
Thus
\[
 K(0)\le M\ll\delta^{-1}\sqrt{Q_L(K)}
 \ll(R+L)\sqrt{Q_L(K)},
\]
proving (2). Nonnegativity of the integrand in (1) proves \(Q_L(K)\ge0\).

If \(f_{s,m}(w)\ne0\), then
\[
 D/(2s)\le w\le2D/s.
\]
Hence every frequency difference \(w-w'\) in
\[
 K_s(\theta)=
 \sum_m\sum_{w,w'}f_{s,m}(w)\overline{f_{s,m}(w')}
 e(\theta(w-w'))
\]
has absolute value at most \(3D/(2s)\). This proves the degree bound in (3). The complex-inner-product orientation is exactly
\[
 \langle F_s(\theta),F_s(\theta)\rangle
 =\sum_mF_{s,m}(\theta)\overline{F_{s,m}(\theta)},
\]
so \(K_s\) is real and nonnegative. Applying (2) proves (4).

Equation (5) is the exact pre-recombination identity verified in facts 1f5316e61daf156d and 83c98e3d3a11382b. Since \(|\mu(r)|\le1\), the triangle inequality and (4) prove (6). TB-QTRI therefore implies the asserted bound for \({\cal E}_{<}\), and fact 1f5316e61daf156d gives the hard covariance consequence.

We prove the comparison with TB-VL2. The kernel in (1) is at most one and vanishes unless
\[
 \|\alpha-\beta\|\le {1\over2L_s^{\rm ceil}}
 \le {sT_x\over2D}.
\]
For fixed \(\alpha\), the inner \(\beta\)-integral is therefore at most \(J_s\). Integrating against \(K_s(\alpha)\) proves
\[
 Q_{L_s^{\rm ceil}}(K_s)\le J_s\Delta_s.              \tag{13}
\]
The support conditions give \(O(D/s)\) choices for \(w\), \(O(x/D)\) choices for \(m\), and \(|\Lambda|\ll\log x\). Thus
\[
 \Delta_s=\sum_{m,w}|f_{s,m}(w)|^2
 \ll x(\log x)^2/s,
\]
which proves (7). Also, for sufficiently large \(x\),
\[
 R_s+L_s^{\rm ceil}\ll D/s.                            \tag{14}
\]
Equations (7) and (14) give
\[
\begin{split}
 &\sum_{g,r<T_x}(R_{gr}+L_{gr}^{\rm ceil})
 \sqrt{Q_{L_{gr}^{\rm ceil}}(K_{gr})}\\
 &\qquad\ll
 D\sqrt{x}\log x
 \sum_{g,r<T_x}{\sqrt{J_{gr}}\over(gr)^{3/2}}.
                                                                    \tag{15}
\end{split}
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \sum_{g,r<T_x}{\sqrt{J_{gr}}\over(gr)^{3/2}}
 \le
 \left(\sum_{g,r<T_x}{J_{gr}\over g^2r^2}\right)^{1/2}
 \left(\sum_{g,r<T_x}{1\over gr}\right)^{1/2}.
\]
The second factor is \(O(\log(2T_x))\). Insert (8) into (15) to obtain the first expression in (9).

Finally,
\[
 {x\sqrt{DT_x}(\log x)^{-1-\eta/2}\log(2T_x)
  \over xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta}}
 =
 \sqrt{T_x/D}(\log x)^{3+\eta/2}\log(2T_x)\longrightarrow0
\]
because \(D\) is a fixed power of \(x\) divided by a fixed logarithmic power, whereas \(T_x\) is a fixed logarithmic power. This proves (9).

glossary.Q_L(K): the triangular local-circle quadratic energy of a nonnegative trigonometric polynomial K
glossary.R_s: the ceiling degree bound ceil(3D/(2s)) for K_s
glossary.TB-QTRI: the positive triangular-local-circle norm bound sufficient for the signed projector energy

d53bd13f391dd6e4.title: EXACT POST-PAYMENT RESIDUAL LEDGER FOR ACTUAL-Z_MID: VERY-LARGE-CONDUCTOR CORE PLUS THE COMPLEMENTARY SMALL-g PACKET
d53bd13f391dd6e4.author: slava chan
d53bd13f391dd6e4.statement:
EXACT POST-PAYMENT RESIDUAL LEDGER FOR ACTUAL-Z_MID: VERY-LARGE-CONDUCTOR CORE PLUS THE COMPLEMENTARY SMALL-g PACKET.

Assume the selected forced-high forward literal actual-Z_mid source setting of facts 152484e836f90c47 and a24910f2fc49b330. Fix eta with
0<eta<1/12,
and put
G_0=x^(1/12+eta),  F_0=x^(1/2-eta).                         (1)
Let R_mid^{ne0} be the complete literal conjugate-paired nonzero-Poisson actual-Z_mid contribution before any proper frequency-dependent deletion.

Partition it first by exact outer gcd:
R_mid^{ne0}=R_{g>=G_0}^{ne0}+R_{g<G_0}^{ne0}.                (2)
Inside R_{g<G_0}^{ne0}, use the integration-by-parts representation in fact 152484e836f90c47 and let U_{1,1} be exactly the paired potentially nonzero upper-face contribution with g=1 and |h|=1. Define
C_small=R_{g<G_0}^{ne0}-U_{1,1}.                              (3)
Thus C_small includes the paired g=1, |h|=1 derivative-integral term, every paired |h|>1 upper and derivative term at g=1, and every paired upper and derivative term for
1<g<G_0. The lower face is zero. If the alternative smooth-interior plus hard-boundary-strip representation is used, its two pieces are recombined before assigning the same cells in (2)-(3).

Multiplicative character reconstruction partitions U_{1,1} exactly as
U_{1,1}=U_prin+U_np,<=F_0+U_>F_0,                            (4)
where U_prin is the principal-character component,
U_np,<=F_0 is the complete nonprincipal component of primitive conductor f<=F_0, and U_>F_0 is the complete component with nonprincipal primitive conductor
f>F_0, (f,N)=1. Character blocks with (f,N)>1 are identically zero. Every term in (4) retains both conjugate frequencies and every literal natural endpoint mask.

The five cells
R_{g>=G_0}^{ne0}, C_small, U_prin, U_np,<=F_0, U_>F_0        (5)
are pairwise disjoint and have union R_mid^{ne0}. Moreover, for some fixed delta_eta>0,
R_{g>=G_0}^{ne0}+U_prin+U_np,<=F_0
 =O_eta(x^(1-delta_eta)).                                    (6)
Consequently the exact post-payment residual is
R_mid^{ne0}
 =C_small+U_>F_0+O_eta(x^(1-delta_eta)).                     (7)

The very-large-conductor core U_>F_0 has the exact joint f,s vector and Q^(8/3) sufficient energy interface of fact 050efa07f87f374a; in particular its support has
b=fs asymp x^(2/3), f>x^(1/2-eta), (f,N)=1,
s<x^(1/6+eta+o(1)).                                         (8)

Equation (7) does not say that all of C_small is paid. The accepted conductor deletions c9accda871a70b43 and 3afa321a72a3612b apply only to U_{1,1}; they do not estimate |h|>1, g>1, the derivative-integral term, or a proper smooth-interior/boundary-strip frequency cell. Likewise a24910f2fc49b330 applies to the complete g>=G_0 symmetric Fejer packet and is not reused after a proper h- or conductor-dependent deletion. Thus isolating only U_>F_0 is valid inside the distinguished g=1, |h|=1 upper face, while the complete literal small-g residual is the two-term right side of (7). No endpoint capture, C3 conclusion, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
d53bd13f391dd6e4.proof:
For each fixed x, the selected source has finitely many exact outer-gcd layers and frequency Cesaro sums. The predicates g>=G_0 and g<G_0 are disjoint and exhaustive, proving (2). Since G_0>1 for sufficiently large x, the exact layer g=1 belongs only to the second cell.

Fact 152484e836f90c47 proves on every exact g,a,b layer that the lower integration-by-parts face vanishes and that the nonzero hard coefficient is exactly the sum of the upper face and derivative integral. Pairing h and -h is legal before every retained mask. Therefore deleting from R_{g<G_0}^{ne0} exactly the paired upper face at g=1, |h|=1 gives (3) and the explicit inventory following it. No other atom is deleted. The smooth-interior/boundary-strip formula in that fact is an alternative exact decomposition of the same coefficient, so recombining its two terms before applying (2)-(3) preserves this set identity.

Fact c9accda871a70b43 gives exact multiplicative-character reconstruction of U_{1,1} and defines its complete principal component, retaining both conjugate frequencies. Every nonprincipal character has one primitive conductor f. Splitting those conductors at F_0 is disjoint and exhaustive. Fact 5a651793cab6648b proves that the Gauss coefficient vanishes when (f,N)>1, so these zero terms may be omitted without a remainder. This proves (4). Combining (2)-(4) proves the disjoint exhaustive ledger (5).

Fact a24910f2fc49b330, with its threshold G_0, gives
R_{g>=G_0}^{ne0}=O_eta(x^(1-eta)).
Fact c9accda871a70b43 gives
U_prin=x^(1/2+o(1)).
Because 0<eta<1/12<1/2, fact 3afa321a72a3612b applies with F_0=x^(1/2-eta) and gives
U_np,<=F_0=O_eta(x^(1-delta'_eta))
for some fixed delta'_eta>0. Choose a fixed positive delta_eta smaller than eta, delta'_eta and 1/3, and absorb the o(1) and finite sum. This proves (6). Substitution of (6) into the exact ledger proves (7).

Finally fact 3afa321a72a3612b derives exactly the range (8), and fact 050efa07f87f374a gives its joint projector and energy interface. The scope statements follow from the explicit scopes of the three paid facts: the g-threshold payment is complete-frequency, whereas the two character payments concern only the g=1, |h|=1 upper face. No extension of any estimate beyond that signed scope was made.

glossary.C_small: the complete g<G_0 packet after deleting only U_{1,1}
glossary.R_mid^{ne0}: the complete selected conjugate-paired nonzero-Poisson actual-Z_mid contribution
glossary.R_{g>=G_0}^{ne0}: the complete part of R_mid^{ne0} on exact outer gcd g at least G_0
glossary.U_>F_0: the nonprincipal component of U_{1,1} with primitive conductor greater than F_0 and coprime to N
glossary.U_np,<=F_0: the nonprincipal component of U_{1,1} with primitive conductor at most F_0
glossary.U_prin: the principal multiplicative-character component of U_{1,1}
glossary.U_{1,1}: the paired g=1, |h|=1 upper integration-by-parts face

d5cfc4a905989cc8.title: C-qSRC-RES: EXACT COPY/RAY RESIDUE REASSEMBLY, MULTIPLICATIVE SPECTRUM, AND THE RESIDUE-DISCREPANCY FRONTIER
d5cfc4a905989cc8.author: slava chan
d5cfc4a905989cc8.statement:
C-qSRC-RES: EXACT COPY/RAY RESIDUE REASSEMBLY, MULTIPLICATIVE SPECTRUM, AND THE RESIDUE-DISCREPANCY FRONTIER.

Adopt the Dcal>Q^2 centered source C-qSRC>=2 from fact e9e9563501147a1a. For every squarefree integer m>=2, every unit residue c modulo m, and every unit residue z modulo m, define the complete literal aggregate
Z_{m,c}(z)
 =sum B_lambda(R)conjugate(B_lambda(R')),                       (1)
where the sum is over all exact retained lambda,R,R' occurring in C-qSRC>=2 such that
m_q=m,
C_q congruent c modulo m,
d_lambda v_lambda congruent z modulo m.
Every hard, nonresonant, source, copy, and pair-dependent selector remains inside (1). Put
Zbar_{m,c}=phi(m)^{-1}sum_{z modulo m}^* Z_{m,c}(z).             (2)
For a character chi modulo m define
Zhat_{m,c}(chi)=sum_{z modulo m}^*Z_{m,c}(z)chi(z),              (3)
and retain G_{m,c}(chi) and K^circ_{m,c} from fact 764588e99974a6d9. Then
C-qSRC>=2
 =sum_{m>=2}sum_{c modulo m}^*
   sum_{z modulo m}^*
   K^circ_{m,c}(z)[Z_{m,c}(z)-Zbar_{m,c}]                       (C-qSRC-RES)
 =sum_{m>=2}sum_{c modulo m}^*
   1/phi(m) sum_{chi modulo m, chi!=chi_0}
   G_{m,c}(chi)Zhat_{m,c}(chi).                                 (4)

For every such m,c,
sum_{chi modulo m}|G_{m,c}(chi)|^2=phi(m)^2,
G_{m,c}(chi_0)=mu(m),                                           (5)
and hence
sum_{chi!=chi_0}|G_{m,c}(chi)|^2=phi(m)^2-1.                    (6)
Moreover
sum_{chi!=chi_0}|Zhat_{m,c}(chi)|^2
 =phi(m)sum_{z modulo m}^*|Z_{m,c}(z)-Zbar_{m,c}|^2.            (7)
Thus the centered kernel annihilates exactly the constant copy/ray residue profile, but its nonprincipal Gauss spectrum has no generic small operator norm. More precisely, blockwise Cauchy gives only
|sum_z^*K^circ_{m,c}(z)Z_{m,c}(z)|
 <=sqrt(phi(m)-1/phi(m))
   [sum_z^*|Z_{m,c}(z)-Zbar_{m,c}|^2]^{1/2}.                    (8)

The absence of a generic gain is sharp for abstract residue profiles: taking
Z_{m,c}(z)=conjugate(K^circ_{m,c}(z))
gives
sum_z^*K^circ_{m,c}(z)Z_{m,c}(z)
 =sum_z^*|K^circ_{m,c}(z)|^2
 =phi(m)-1/phi(m).                                              (9)
This abstract profile is not asserted to arise from the literal source.

Consequently C-qSRC-SUP cannot follow from centering plus a generic residue L2 bound alone. A valid continuation must prove source-specific smallness or cross-(m,c) cancellation of the exact discrepancy profiles in (1)-(4), before replacing them by arbitrary arrays. This theorem proves the exact residue handoff and spectrum only; it proves no C-qSRC-SUP, no P-qSRC-SUP, no full GA-RAY-SPEC, no tail payment, and no Goldbach conclusion.
d5cfc4a905989cc8.proof:
Fact e9e9563501147a1a writes
C-qSRC>=2
 =sum_lambda sum_{retained R!=R', m_q>=2}
 B_lambda(R)conjugate(B_lambda(R'))
 K^circ_{m_q,C_q}(d_lambda v_lambda).                           (10)
Every supported term has squarefree m_q and both C_q and d_lambda v_lambda are units modulo m_q by fact 764588e99974a6d9. Partition the finite sum (10) by the three residue labels in (1). This gives
C-qSRC>=2
 =sum_{m,c,z}K^circ_{m,c}(z)Z_{m,c}(z).                         (11)
The same fact proves
sum_z^*K^circ_{m,c}(z)=0.                                      (12)
Subtracting Zbar_{m,c} from the profile in (11) therefore changes nothing and proves the first equality C-qSRC-RES.

The multiplicative character formula in fact 764588e99974a6d9 is
K^circ_{m,c}(z)
 =1/phi(m) sum_{chi!=chi_0}G_{m,c}(chi)chi(z).                  (13)
Insert (13) in (11), interchange finite sums, and use definition (3). This proves (4).

For (5), expand the Gauss sums and use character orthogonality on the unit group:
sum_chi|G_{m,c}(chi)|^2
 =sum_{u,v modulo m}^*e_m(-cu+cv)
   sum_chi chi(u)conjugate(chi(v))
 =phi(m)sum_{u modulo m}^*1
 =phi(m)^2.                                                     (14)
For the principal character,
G_{m,c}(chi_0)=sum_{u modulo m}^*e_m(-cu)=c_m(-c).              (15)
Because m is squarefree and c is a unit modulo m, the Ramanujan sum in (15) is mu(m). This proves (5), and its squared modulus is one, so (6) follows.

Apply the same character orthogonality to (3):
sum_chi|Zhat_{m,c}(chi)|^2
 =phi(m)sum_z^*|Z_{m,c}(z)|^2.                                 (16)
The principal transform is
Zhat_{m,c}(chi_0)=sum_z^*Z_{m,c}(z)=phi(m)Zbar_{m,c}.           (17)
Subtracting its squared modulus from (16), and expanding the elementary variance identity, proves (7).

Cauchy--Schwarz in (4), followed by (6)-(7), gives
1/phi(m) sqrt(phi(m)^2-1)
 sqrt(phi(m)sum_z^*|Z-Zbar|^2),
which is exactly (8).

Finally set Z(z)=conjugate(K^circ_{m,c}(z)). The left side becomes the squared L2 norm of K^circ. Parseval applied to (13), together with (6), gives
sum_z^*|K^circ_{m,c}(z)|^2
 =1/phi(m)sum_{chi!=chi_0}|G_{m,c}(chi)|^2
 =phi(m)-1/phi(m),
proving (9). The example is purely formal, so it supplies only the stated generic-method no-fit. All limitations follow.

glossary.C-qSRC-RES: The exact centered-source reassembly by physical conductor, unit phase numerator, and marked-modulus residue.
glossary.Z_{m,c}(z): The complete literal copy/ray coefficient aggregate at fixed m_q=m, C_q=c, and d_lambda v_lambda=z modulo m.
glossary.Zbar_{m,c}: The mean of Z_{m,c} over unit residues.
glossary.Zhat_{m,c}(chi): The multiplicative character transform of the literal residue profile Z_{m,c}.

d5ebef8af499c18f.title: CHARACTER-TWISTED DETERMINANT CONTRACT AND NO DIRECT GAUSS-EXPANSION SUPPLY
d5ebef8af499c18f.author: slava chan
d5ebef8af499c18f.statement:
CHARACTER-TWISTED DETERMINANT CONTRACT AND NO DIRECT GAUSS-EXPANSION SUPPLY.

(A) The sufficient twisted contract. Let X>=2 and let q be an odd integer satisfying 1<q<=X^2. Let Delta be a nonzero integer satisfying gcd(Delta,q)=1 and |Delta|<=X^2. Let M_1,M_2,N_1,N_2 lie in [X,2X]. Let chi and psi be multiplicative characters of the unit group modulo q, extended by zero to nonunits, and let c_chi,c_psi be their primitive conductors. Let f,g be smooth functions supported respectively on [M_1/2,M_1] and [M_2/2,M_2]. Assume eta>=1 and, for every integer j>=0, fix a positive constant C_j independent of q,X,chi,psi such that
 |f^(j)(x)|<=C_j eta^j M_1^(-j),  |g^(j)(x)|<=C_j eta^j M_2^(-j).     (1)
Let alpha,beta be arbitrary complex sequences supported respectively on [N_1/2,N_1] and [N_2/2,N_2], and assume they vanish unless their arguments are coprime to q. Define
 T_{chi,psi}
 =sum_{m_1 n_2-m_2 n_1=Delta}
   f(m_1)chi(m_1)g(m_2)psi(m_2)alpha(n_1)beta(n_2),                  (2)
where all four variables are positive integers. For unit n_1,n_2 modulo q put
 A_{chi,psi}(n_1,n_2;Delta,q)
 =q^(-1) sum_{r modulo q}
   chi((Delta+r n_1)n_2^(-1))psi(r),                                 (3)
and define the explicit complete-residue main term
 Z_{chi,psi}^{tw}
 =sum_{n_1,n_2; gcd(n_1,n_2) divides Delta}
   [gcd(n_1,n_2)/(n_1n_2)] alpha(n_1)beta(n_2)
   A_{chi,psi}(n_1,n_2;Delta,q)
   integral_R f((x+Delta)/n_2)g(x/n_1) dx.                           (4)
The column variables in (4) remain on the supports of alpha,beta.

For a nonnegative function L(c_1,c_2), call CTBC(L) the assertion that, uniformly in all the preceding data and in Delta in the displayed range, for every epsilon>0,
 |T_{chi,psi}-Z_{chi,psi}^{tw}|
 <=C_epsilon [qX(1+|Delta|)]^epsilon
   (eta R_bal)^(3/2)L(c_chi,c_psi)
   X^(19/20)||alpha||_2||beta||_2,                                  (5)
where
 R_bal=M_1N_2/(M_2N_1)+M_2N_1/(M_1N_2),                              (6)
and C_epsilon is allowed to depend on epsilon and on the constants C_j but not on q,X,Delta,chi,psi,alpha,beta. Thus CTBC(L) explicitly records conductor loss, Sobolev loss, arbitrary-column norms, Delta-uniformity, discrepancy, and the main term.

For any finite linear assembly T_ass of instances of (2), let Z_ass be the corresponding assembly of (4). CTBC(L) and the triangle inequality give
 |T_ass-Z_ass|
 <=C_epsilon[qX(1+|Delta|)]^epsilon X^(19/20)P_tw,                   (7)
where
 P_tw=sum_j |lambda_j|(eta_jR_{bal,j})^(3/2)
       L(c_{chi_j},c_{psi_j})||alpha_j||_2||beta_j||_2.               (8)
Writing Pi_tw=P_tw/X and X=H^3, for every fixed delta>0 the two separate bounds
 Pi_tw<=H^(3/20-delta),  |Z_ass|<=H^(6-delta)                         (9)
imply, after renaming epsilon,
 |T_ass|<=C_epsilon H^(6-delta+epsilon).                             (10)

(B) Exact centered shared-digit main-term assembly. Let m>1 be odd, fix s in {1,-1}, put q=m^2, assume gcd(K,m)=1, put Delta=2K and n=phi(q), and let W be a complex function modulo m. Define
 W_hat(ell)=sum_{u modulo m}W(u)e_m(-ell u)                           (11)
and
 S(chi,psi)=sum_{u modulo m}W(u)
   conjugate(chi(K+2smu)psi(K-2smu)).                                (12)
Fix common f,g and common unit-supported column sequences alpha_0,beta_0. In the legal sign orientation
 (m_1,m_2,n_1,n_2)=(a,c,-d,b),
put
 lambda_{chi,psi}=n^(-2)S(chi,psi)psi(-1),
 alpha_{chi,psi}(n_1)=psi(n_1)alpha_0(n_1),
 beta_{chi,psi}(n_2)=chi(n_2)beta_0(n_2).                             (13)
Then the assembly of the main terms (4) is exactly
 Z_W^{tw,ass}
 =[q^(-1)sum_{u modulo m}W(u)]
  sum_{n_1,n_2;gcd(n_1,n_2) divides 2K}
   [gcd(n_1,n_2)/(n_1n_2)]alpha_0(n_1)beta_0(n_2)
   integral_R f((x+2K)/n_2)g(x/n_1)dx,                              (14)
with the columns restricted to units modulo q. Hence Z_W^{tw,ass}=0 whenever W is centered.

If CTBC(L) holds with the common fixed Sobolev data in (13), its assembled discrepancy has the exact conductor-weighted coefficient
 C_W(L)=n^(-2)sum_{chi,psi}|S(chi,psi)|L(c_chi,c_psi).                (15)
For L identically one,
 C_W(1)=m^(-1)sum_{ell modulo m}|W_hat(ell)|.                         (16)
If kappa>=0 and L(c_1,c_2)<=(c_1c_2)^kappa, then
 C_W(L)<=q^(2kappa)m^(-1)sum_ell|W_hat(ell)|.                         (17)
In particular, when m is comparable to X and W(u)=e_m(ell u) is a pure digit mode, (17) is at most a constant times X^(4kappa). Thus a worst-case conductor loss of this form retains some part of the balanced X^(1/20) margin only when kappa<1/80; a subpolynomial conductor loss is admissible up to epsilon-powers. This is only a sufficient worst-case ledger, not a claim that CTBC(L) is true.

(C) Exact tax of the direct Gauss/Fourier use of the existing untwisted corollary. Let p>=5 be prime, q=p^2, X=p, and M_1,M_2 in [p,2p]. Let chi,psi be primitive characters modulo q. For a residue h modulo q let h_cen be its unique integer representative in (-q/2,q/2]. Define e_q(t)=exp(2 pi i t/q) and
 tau(conjugate(chi))=sum_{h modulo q}conjugate(chi(h))e_q(h),
with the analogous definition for psi. The primitive Gauss expansions are
 chi(t)=tau(conjugate(chi))^(-1)
        sum_{h modulo q}conjugate(chi(h))e_q(h_cen t),
 psi(t)=tau(conjugate(psi))^(-1)
        sum_{k modulo q}conjugate(psi(k))e_q(k_cen t)                 (18)
for integer t, and both Gauss sums have absolute value p. Applying Bettin--Chandee Corollary 1 separately to every pair of additive modes in (18) and then using the triangle inequality produces the derivative ledger
 G_{chi,psi}
 =p^(-2)sum_{h,k modulo q; p does not divide hk}
  [eta+M_1|h_cen|/q+M_2|k_cen|/q]^(3/2),                            (19)
and
 G_{chi,psi} is comparable to p^(7/2),                               (20)
with absolute comparison constants when eta is bounded above and below by positive constants.

The main term produced by that termwise application is the explicit Gauss-interpolated expression
 Z_{chi,psi}^{G}
 =[tau(conjugate(chi))tau(conjugate(psi))]^(-1)
  sum_{h,k modulo q}
   conjugate(chi(h)psi(k))
  sum_{n_1,n_2;gcd(n_1,n_2) divides Delta}
   [gcd(n_1,n_2)/(n_1n_2)]alpha(n_1)beta(n_2)
  integral_R f((x+Delta)/n_2)g(x/n_1)
   e_q(h_cen(x+Delta)/n_2+k_cen x/n_1)dx.                            (21)
Thus the untwisted corollary yields a bound for T_{chi,psi}-Z_{chi,psi}^{G} with coefficient G_{chi,psi}, not (5) relative to the complete-residue main term (4). Passing from (21) to (4) is an additional analytic obligation.

For the pure nonzero digit mode W(u)=e_p(ell u), ell nonzero modulo p, the exact character assembly of fact 8230d44e6677f45b has total absolute coefficient mass (p-2)/p on pairs chi,psi that are both primitive modulo p^2. Consequently, applying (18) and the untwisted corollary character-pair by character-pair gives an assembled absolute Gauss ledger at least a positive constant times p^(7/2). This cannot fit the p^(1/20) coefficient margin in the balanced untwisted discrepancy contract.

There are two independent scoped decomposition floors. On the full unit group modulo p^2, fact f225c6e0aab449f4 gives, for the same pure digit mode, Q_col>=phi(p^2), so Q_col/X>=p-1. On the complete prime product graph modulo p, fact 24e13ac742ddd3c1 gives
 sum_j eta_j^(3/2)||beta_j||_2>=sqrt(p-1)                             (22)
for every exact smooth-row decomposition with eta_j>=1. Both exceed p^(1/20) for all sufficiently large p. The first floor concerns full modulo-p^2 row supports and the second concerns the collapsed complete modulo-p product graph; neither is asserted for a literal short coefficient box with every remaining selector.

Therefore Gauss/Fourier expansion followed termwise by the existing untwisted Bettin--Chandee corollary does not directly supply CTBC(L) on the prime near-maximal slice. The conclusion is a theorem-interface and tax audit only. It does not rule out a direct two-row-character proof, cancellation before absolute values in the full character assembly, special short or imprimitive subranges, or a fresh smooth decomposition after all literal selectors are assembled. By fact a695dcaf05aaa83d, every legal determinant sign sector places one chi-factor and one psi-factor in the two row slots; changes of legal orientation and coefficient signs only permute these factors and multiply them by constants of absolute value one, so the same no-direct-application audit preserves every legal sign sector.
d5ebef8af499c18f.proof:
For (A), formulas (2)-(6) define the precise additional theorem rather than asserting its existence. Sum (5) over a finite family after multiplication by lambda_j. The triangle inequality gives (7) with exactly (8). Since P_tw=X Pi_tw and X=H^3, the right side of (7), apart from the explicit epsilon-power, is
 X^(19/20)X H^(3/20-delta)
 =H^(57/20)H^3H^(3/20-delta)
 =H^(6-delta).
Moreover q<=X^2, |Delta|<=X^2, and X>=2 give
 qX(1+|Delta|)<=2X^5=2H^15.
Apply (7) initially with epsilon replaced by epsilon/16. The displayed factor is then at most a constant times H^epsilon. Adding the second bound in (9) proves (10).

For (B), the sum in (3) is q^(-1) times the complete row-character determinant sum
 R_{chi,psi}(n_1,n_2)
 =sum_{a,c modulo q; a n_2-c n_1=2K modulo q}chi(a)psi(c).
Indeed, taking r=c in (3) forces a=(2K+c n_1)n_2^(-1). Insert (13) and (3) into the assembly of (4). All geometric factors are independent of chi,psi, and the character-dependent factor at fixed columns is
 q^(-1)n^(-2)sum_{chi,psi}
 S(chi,psi)chi(n_2)psi(-n_1)R_{chi,psi}(n_1,n_2).
By formula (5)-(6) of fact 382dadf452a0f461, the expression without q^(-1) is sum_u W(u). This proves (14), including the centered cancellation.

The discrepancy coefficient after applying (5) and the triangle inequality is exactly (15), because multiplication of a column sequence by a unit-modulus character does not change its ell^2 norm and the zero values merely impose the already assumed unit support. Fact 8230d44e6677f45b proves
 sum_{chi,psi}|S(chi,psi)|
 =[n^2/m]sum_ell|W_hat(ell)|.
Division by n^2 gives (16). Since each primitive conductor divides q and kappa>=0, the hypothesis on L gives
 L(c_chi,c_psi)<=(c_chic_psi)^kappa<=q^(2kappa).
Combining this with (16) proves (17). For W(u)=e_m(ell u), its Fourier transform has one nonzero value of absolute value m, so the normalized Fourier l1 factor in (17) is one. If m is comparable to X, q^(2kappa)=m^(4kappa) is comparable to X^(4kappa). A factor X^(4kappa) is smaller than X^(1/20) by a fixed power exactly when 4kappa<1/20, equivalently kappa<1/80.

For (C), first prove (18) and the Gauss-sum magnitude. For any character theta primitive modulo q=p^2, extended by zero to nonunits, define
 G_theta(t)=sum_{a modulo q}conjugate(theta(a))e_q(at)
and tau(conjugate(theta))=G_theta(1).
If t is a unit modulo q, the change of variables b=at gives
 G_theta(t)
 =sum_b conjugate(theta(bt^(-1)))e_q(b)
 =theta(t)tau(conjugate(theta)).                                     (23)
If p divides t, primitivity of theta modulo p^2 implies that theta is nontrivial on the subgroup 1+pZ modulo p^2; otherwise theta would factor through reduction modulo p. Choose z in that subgroup with theta(z) not equal to one. Multiplication by z permutes the residues, and zt is congruent to t modulo p^2. Therefore
 G_theta(t)
 =sum_a conjugate(theta(az))e_q(azt)
 =conjugate(theta(z))G_theta(t).
Since conjugate(theta(z)) is not one, G_theta(t)=0. Thus (23) holds for all integers t, because both sides vanish on nonunits.

To calculate the magnitude, expand the finite Fourier energy:
 sum_{t modulo q}|G_theta(t)|^2
 =sum_{a,b modulo q}conjugate(theta(a))theta(b)
   sum_{t modulo q}e_q(t(a-b))
 =q sum_{a modulo q}|theta(a)|^2
 =q phi(q).                                                          (24)
On the other hand, (23) and the nonunit vanishing show that the left side of (24) is
 phi(q)|tau(conjugate(theta))|^2.
Hence |tau(conjugate(theta))|^2=q and its absolute value is p. Apply this proof to theta=chi and theta=psi. Replacing a frequency by its centered representative changes its exponential at integer t by exp(2 pi i times an integer), so (18) follows.

For each h, repeated differentiation of f(x)e_q(h_cen x) and the product rule show, for every derivative order j,
 |[f(x)e_q(h_cen x)]^(j)|
 <=C'_j[eta+M_1|h_cen|/q]^j M_1^(-j),
where C'_j depends only on C_0,...,C_j. The analogous bound holds for g and k. Therefore a common admissible smoothness parameter for a pair (h,k) is a constant multiple of
 eta+M_1|h_cen|/q+M_2|k_cen|/q.
Bettin--Chandee, arXiv:1502.00769, Corollary 1, bounds the determinant discrepancy for that pair by the 3/2 power of this parameter times
 X^(19/20+epsilon)||alpha||_2||beta||_2
in the balanced range. Multiplying by the two Gauss coefficients, whose absolute product is p^(-2), and summing absolute values gives exactly (19), up to constants depending only on the fixed derivative envelopes. Summing the explicit main terms of the corollary before taking absolute values gives (21). Hence this derivation controls T-Z^G and does not by itself control T-Z^tw.

There are fewer than q choices for each of h and k, and
 eta+M_1|h_cen|/q+M_2|k_cen|/q
 <=eta+M_1/2+M_2/2
is at most a constant times p. Thus (19) is at most a constant times
 p^(-2)q^2p^(3/2)=p^(7/2).
For the reverse bound, restrict h_cen and k_cen to the two centered intervals on which
 q/4<=|h_cen|<=q/2,  q/4<=|k_cen|<=q/2,
and exclude multiples of p. Each restriction contains at least a fixed positive multiple of q residues when p>=5. On this set the bracket in (19) is at least a fixed positive multiple of p, because M_1,M_2>=p. Hence the restricted contribution is at least a positive constant times
 p^(-2)q^2p^(3/2)=p^(7/2).
This proves (20).

Now take W(u)=e_p(ell u) with ell nonzero. Fact 8230d44e6677f45b proves that S(chi,psi) has absolute value p precisely when the restriction frequencies satisfy
 gamma(r_chi-r_psi)=ell,
and that every restriction frequency modulo p has exactly n/p=p-1 character lifts. A character lift with nonzero restriction frequency cannot factor modulo p, so its primitive conductor is p^2. Choose r_chi freely. The determined r_psi is nonzero and r_chi is nonzero except for two distinct excluded values of r_chi, because ell is nonzero. Thus there are
 (p-2)(p-1)^2
ordered pairs for which both characters are primitive and |S|=p. Their total absolute coefficient mass in the tensor expansion is
 n^(-2)p(p-2)(p-1)^2
 =[p^2(p-1)^2]^(-1)p(p-2)(p-1)^2
 =(p-2)/p.
Every such pair has the lower bound in (20), so the triangle ledger after the full character assembly is at least a constant times [(p-2)/p]p^(7/2).

For the two decomposition floors, apply fact f225c6e0aab449f4 with m=p and the pure mode. Its Fourier l1 norm is p, hence
 Q_col>=phi(p)p=p(p-1)=phi(p^2).
Division by X=p gives p-1. Apply fact 24e13ac742ddd3c1 to the complete product graph; its formula (6) is exactly (22). Since p-1 and sqrt(p-1) both exceed p^(1/20) for all sufficiently large p, neither scoped decomposition cost fits the full balanced discrepancy margin.

Finally, fact a695dcaf05aaa83d proves that every legal positive determinant orientation places one character from the first determinant product and one character from the second determinant product in the two row slots. Sign changes contribute only chi(-1) or psi(-1), of absolute value one, and orientations merely exchange the row and column names. The Gauss derivative calculation and both norm floors are unchanged by these operations. This proves the all-legal-sector scope and the final no-direct-application conclusion.

glossary.A_{chi,psi}: the normalized complete row-character average on a determinant congruence at fixed unit columns
glossary.CTBC(L): the character-twisted balanced determinant discrepancy contract with conductor-loss function L
glossary.C_W(L): the conductor-weighted absolute character coefficient of a shared digit weight W
glossary.G_theta(t): the finite additive Fourier transform at t of the conjugate primitive character theta modulo p^2
glossary.G_{chi,psi}: the exact derivative-weighted absolute Gauss-mode ledger for two primitive row characters
glossary.P_tw: the assembled conductor-, Sobolev-, and column-norm ledger for CTBC(L)
glossary.T_ass: a finite linear assembly of character-twisted determinant sums
glossary.Z_W^{tw,ass}: the complete shared-digit character assembly of the twisted main terms
glossary.Z_ass: the corresponding finite linear assembly of their explicit main terms
glossary.Z_{chi,psi}^{G}: the continuous Gauss-interpolated main term produced by termwise use of the untwisted corollary
glossary.Z_{chi,psi}^{tw}: the explicit complete-residue main term in CTBC(L)
glossary.c_chi: the primitive conductor of the character chi
glossary.c_psi: the primitive conductor of the character psi
glossary.h_cen: the centered integer representative in (-q/2,q/2] of a residue h modulo q

d61bd0787abcc5ec.title: CLEAN-DILATOR COMMON-CORE FACTORIZATION OF A LARGE-CONDUCTOR CHARACTER PROJECTOR. Let \(N\) be a positive integer, let \(F\ge 1\) be real, let \(a\) be a prime, and let \(q,t,u\) be integers with
d61bd0787abcc5ec.author: slava chan
d61bd0787abcc5ec.statement:
CLEAN-DILATOR COMMON-CORE FACTORIZATION OF A LARGE-CONDUCTOR CHARACTER PROJECTOR. Let \(N\) be a positive integer, let \(F\ge 1\) be real, let \(a\) be a prime, and let \(q,t,u\) be integers with
\[
 q\ge2,\qquad (a,qNtu)=1,\qquad (q,tu)=1.
\]
For a positive integer \(v\) and a Dirichlet character \(\chi\) modulo \(v\), put
\[
 G_{N,v}(\chi)=\sum_{\substack{z\ ({\rm mod}\ v)\\(z,v)=1}}
 e_v(-Nz)\overline{\chi(z)},\qquad e_v(y)=\exp(2\pi i y/v),
\]
and let \({\rm cond}(\chi)\) be the primitive conductor of \(\chi\). Define
\[
 \Pi_{>F}^{a,q}(t,u)=\frac1{\phi(aq)}
 \sum_{\substack{\chi\ ({\rm mod}\ aq)\\
 {\rm cond}(\chi)>F\\({\rm cond}(\chi),N)=1}}
 G_{N,aq}(\chi)\chi(t)\overline{\chi(u)}. \tag{1}
\]
For a character \(\psi\) modulo \(q\), put \(f_\psi={\rm cond}(\psi)\) and
\[
 \mathcal H_{q,a}(\psi;t,u)
 =\frac{G_{N,q}(\psi)}{\phi(q)}
   \psi(t)\overline{\psi(au)}, \tag{2}
\]
\[
 \mathcal E_a(q;t,u)
 =e_a\!\left(-Nt\,(qu)^{-1}\right), \tag{3}
\]
where the inverse in (3) is taken modulo \(a\), and
\[
 \mathcal R_{a,F}(f;q,t,u)=
 \begin{cases}
 \mathcal E_a(q;t,u),&f>F,\\
 \mathcal E_a(q;t,u)+\dfrac1{a-1},&F/a<f\le F,\\
 0,&f\le F/a.
 \end{cases} \tag{4}
\]
Then the exact common-core identity
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \Pi_{>F}^{a,q}(t,u)=
 \sum_{\substack{\psi\ ({\rm mod}\ q)\\(f_\psi,N)=1}}
 \mathcal H_{q,a}(\psi;t,u)
 \mathcal R_{a,F}(f_\psi;q,t,u)
 \quad} \tag{5}
\]
holds.

More generally, let \(b\ne a\) be a second prime with
\[
 (ab,qNtu)=1.
\]
Define \(\Pi_{>F}^{b,q}\), \(\mathcal H_{q,b}\), \(\mathcal E_b\), and
\(\mathcal R_{b,F}\) by replacing \(a\) with \(b\). Then
\[
\begin{split}
 \Pi_{>F}^{a,q}(t,u)\,
 \overline{\Pi_{>F}^{b,q}(t,u)}
 =\frac1{\phi(q)^2}
 \sum_{\substack{\psi,\rho\ ({\rm mod}\ q)\\
 (f_\psi f_\rho,N)=1}}
 &G_{N,q}(\psi)\overline{G_{N,q}(\rho)}
 \psi(t)\overline{\psi(au)}
 \overline{\rho(t)}\rho(bu)\\
 {}\times&
 \mathcal R_{a,F}(f_\psi;q,t,u)
 \overline{\mathcal R_{b,F}(f_\rho;q,t,u)}.
 \tag{6}
\end{split}
\]
In particular the right side of (6) is supported on
\[
 f_\psi>F/a,\qquad f_\rho>F/b. \tag{7}
\]

For the two-dilate variables, let \(m\) be positive, \(h\ne0\), put
\[
 c=(m,h),\qquad q=m/c,\qquad t=h/c,
\]
and suppose \(q\ge2\) and
\[
 (ab,mhuN)=1,\qquad (q,tu)=1.
\]
Then
\[
 \frac{am}{(am,h)}=aq,\qquad
 \frac{bm}{(bm,h)}=bq,\qquad
 \frac h{(am,h)}=\frac h{(bm,h)}=t. \tag{8}
\]
Consequently (6) is the exact projector product for these two descended dilates. Any outer coefficient or zero-one source mask multiplying that product is unchanged. The result gives no estimate for (6), does not treat the complementary nonclean sector, and asserts no multiplicativity in \(m\).
d61bd0787abcc5ec.proof:
Every character \(\chi\) modulo \(aq\) has a unique factorization
\[
 \chi(z)=\xi(z)\psi(z),
\]
where \(\xi\) is a character modulo \(a\) and \(\psi\) is a character modulo \(q\). This follows from the Chinese remainder theorem because \((a,q)=1\). If \(f_\xi={\rm cond}(\xi)\) and \(f_\psi={\rm cond}(\psi)\), then
\[
 {\rm cond}(\chi)=f_\xi f_\psi, \tag{9}
\]
because the two primitive local conductors are coprime. Since \(a\) is prime, \(f_\xi=1\) for the principal character \(\xi_0\), and \(f_\xi=a\) for every nonprincipal \(\xi\).

We next factor the Gauss coefficient with all CRT twists explicit. Parametrize a unit \(z\) modulo \(aq\) by its residues modulo \(a\) and \(q\). Additive CRT gives
\[
 e_{aq}(-Nz)
 =e_a(-Nq^{-1}z)e_q(-Na^{-1}z).
\]
In the first local sum change variables from \(z\) to \(q^{-1}z\) modulo \(a\); in the second change variables from \(z\) to \(a^{-1}z\) modulo \(q\). Multiplicativity of the character values gives
\[
 G_{N,aq}(\xi\psi)
 =\overline{\xi(q)}\,\overline{\psi(a)}
   G_{N,a}(\xi)G_{N,q}(\psi). \tag{10}
\]
Also
\[
 (\xi\psi)(t)\overline{(\xi\psi)(u)}
 =\xi(t)\overline{\xi(u)}
  \psi(t)\overline{\psi(u)}. \tag{11}
\]
The hypothesis \((a,N)=1\) and (9) show that
\[
 ({\rm cond}(\xi\psi),N)=1
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (f_\psi,N)=1. \tag{12}
\]

Fix \(\psi\) modulo \(q\), and abbreviate \(f=f_\psi\). Inserting (10)--(12) into (1), the complete factor depending on \(\psi\) is exactly
\[
 \frac{G_{N,q}(\psi)}{\phi(q)}
 \psi(t)\overline{\psi(au)}
 =\mathcal H_{q,a}(\psi;t,u). \tag{13}
\]
The remaining local factor is
\[
 \frac1{\phi(a)}
 \sum_{\substack{\xi\ ({\rm mod}\ a)\\ f_\xi f>F}}
 G_{N,a}(\xi)\xi(t)\overline{\xi(qu)}. \tag{14}
\]

We evaluate (14). Finite Fourier inversion on the unit group modulo \(a\) gives
\[
 \frac1{\phi(a)}\sum_{\xi\ ({\rm mod}\ a)}
 G_{N,a}(\xi)\xi\!\left(t(qu)^{-1}\right)
 =e_a\!\left(-Nt(qu)^{-1}\right)
 =\mathcal E_a(q;t,u). \tag{15}
\]
Because \(a\nmid N\), the principal local Gauss coefficient is the Ramanujan sum
\[
 G_{N,a}(\xi_0)=\sum_{z=1}^{a-1}e_a(-Nz)=-1. \tag{16}
\]
Thus the principal contribution to (14) is \(-1/(a-1)\), and the sum of all nonprincipal contributions is
\[
 \mathcal E_a(q;t,u)+\frac1{a-1}. \tag{17}
\]

There are now exactly three cases. If \(f>F\), both the principal and every nonprincipal \(\xi\) satisfy \(f_\xi f>F\), so (14) equals the complete response (15). If \(f\le F<af\), the principal character fails the cutoff while every nonprincipal character passes it, so (14) equals (17). If \(af\le F\), no local character passes. These are precisely the three lines of (4). Summing (13) times (4) over the characters \(\psi\) satisfying (12) proves (5).

Apply (5) once with \(a\) and once with \(b\). Taking the complex conjugate of the second identity and multiplying the two finite sums gives (6) term by term. Formula (4) vanishes unless \(f>F/a\), which proves (7).

Finally assume the hypotheses involving \(m,h\). Since neither \(a\) nor \(b\) divides \(m h\),
\[
 (am,h)=(m,h)=c,\qquad (bm,h)=c.
\]
Dividing \(am,bm,h\) by \(c\) proves (8). The unit hypotheses put these variables in the scope of (1)--(6). The substitution changes only the projector product, so multiplying it by any pre-existing outer coefficient or mask preserves that coefficient or mask exactly. No estimate, complementary-sector deletion, or multiplicative relation was used.

glossary.Pi_{>F}^{a,q}(t,u): The primitive-conductor-greater-than-F character projector on the product modulus aq, evaluated at the unit ratio t/u.
glossary.f_psi: The primitive conductor of a Dirichlet character psi modulo q.
glossary.mathcal E_a(q;t,u): The complete local additive response e_a(-Nt(qu)^(-1)) at the prime dilator a.
glossary.mathcal H_{q,a}(psi;t,u): The common-core q-character coefficient including its CRT twist by the prime dilator a.
glossary.mathcal R_{a,F}(f;q,t,u): The exact local a-response after imposing that the product primitive conductor exceed F.

d63101722d12c88c.title: TOP-B-RECOMBINED-COEFF-ENV/CROSSU-DFR-COR. Fix constants \(0<\kappa\le 1/100\), \(C_0,C_B,C_F\ge1\), put
d63101722d12c88c.author: slava chan
d63101722d12c88c.statement:
TOP-B-RECOMBINED-COEFF-ENV/CROSSU-DFR-COR. Fix constants \(0<\kappa\le 1/100\), \(C_0,C_B,C_F\ge1\), put
\[
 \sigma=\kappa/100,\qquad \beta_m=6/5-12\sigma/5,
\]
and let \(Q\) be sufficiently large. Fix
\[
 \beta_m\le\beta<6/5,\qquad B=Q^\beta,
\]
one exact orientation, outer-gcd layer, selected source, parent, fixed-\(U\), high and smooth/projective fibre, one top-\(B\) stopping length \(k\ge2\), dyadic blocks
\[
 U\le u<2U,\qquad Y\le y<2Y,\qquad
 C_B^{-1}B\le UY\le C_BB,
\]
and one nonzero frequency block
\[
 F\le |h|<2F,\qquad 1\le F\le C_FH_P.
\]
Assume \(B,U,Y,F\) and the nonzero integer source target \(\mathscr A\) are at most \(Q^{C_0}\). Put
\[
 L=Q^{\beta-1+\sigma},\quad
 S_0=Q^{2\beta-2+3\sigma},\quad
 Z=Q^{3/2-\beta-3\sigma},
\]
\[
 \alpha_k(u)=
 {(-1)^k\mu(u)1_{j_{(L,Z)}(u)=0}
  \over {k+\omega_L(u)\choose k}},
 \qquad
 \gamma_k(y)=\Gamma_{k;L,S_0}(y).
\]

For each \((u,y)\), let \(\Lambda_k(u,y)\) be the complete family of old exact top-\(B\) stopping-copy siblings in this fixed fibre, with every target-gcd, prime-order/equal-cell, collision, deletion and provenance descendant retained, and let \(c_\lambda(q,h)\) be their zero-extended coefficients. Thus every supported coordinate satisfies
\[
 Q\le q<2Q,\qquad F\le |h|<2F,\qquad
 (q,uy)=(u,y)=1,
\]
both signs of \(h\) occur, and the old contribution is
\[
 {1\over H_P}\sum_{u,y,q,h}
 \left(\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda_k(u,y)}c_\lambda(q,h)\right)
 e_q\!\left(-\mathscr A h(uy)^{-1}\right).                 \tag{1}
\]
Use the source-projective output of fact \(b69e09aaac3766d9\): divisor-bounded \(a_q,b_h\), a Poisson scalar \(\omega_F\), and a fixed-complexity amplitude \(\Psi_F\) of uniformly bounded projective Fourier \(\ell^1\)-norm. Define, on the same literal support and as zero outside it,
\[
 c_k^{\rm rec}(u,y;q,h)
 =\omega_Fa_qb_h\alpha_k(u)\gamma_k(y)
 \Psi_F(q/Q,|h|/F,u/U,y/Y).                                  \tag{2}
\]

Then the following assertions hold.

1. For every integer coordinate \((u,y,q,h)\),
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 c_k^{\rm rec}(u,y;q,h)
 =\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda_k(u,y)}c_\lambda(q,h).\quad}       \tag{3}
\]
Consequently (1) is exactly
\[
 {1\over H_P}\sum_{u,y,q,h}
 c_k^{\rm rec}(u,y;q,h)
 e_q\!\left(-\mathscr A h(uy)^{-1}\right).                   \tag{4}
\]
The outside factor \(H_P^{-1}\), both signs of \(h\), the target \(\mathscr A\), the reciprocal phase, and every listed descendant have only been recombined, not deleted.

2. There are fixed integers \(J\ge1\) and \(C\ge0\), depending only on the fixed source/projective family, such that
\[
 |c_k^{\rm rec}(u,y;q,h)|
 \ll \tau_J(uyq|h|)(\log(2Q))^C.                             \tag{5}
\]
No bound for an individual old \(c_\lambda(q,h)\) is asserted.

3. Put \(\Lambda_k^{\rm rec}(u,y)=\{*\}\) and
\(c_*(q,h)=c_k^{\rm rec}(u,y;q,h)\). Define
\[
 K^{\rm rec}_{u,y}=\sum_{q,h}c_k^{\rm rec}(u,y;q,h)
 e_q\!\left(-\mathscr A h(uy)^{-1}\right),\qquad
 G_y^{\rm rec}=\sum_uK^{\rm rec}_{u,y},
\]
\[
 V_{\rm rec}=\sum_y|G_y^{\rm rec}|^2.
\]
For
\[
 \Omega=h_1q_2u_2-h_2q_1u_1,                                \tag{6}
\]
partition the exact expansion of \(V_{\rm rec}\) into
\(V_{\rm rec}^{(0)},V_{\rm rec}^{(\mathrm{FR})},
V_{\rm rec}^{(\mathrm{NR})}\) according as
\[
 \Omega=0;\qquad
 \Omega\ne0\ \hbox{and}\ y\mid\mathscr A\Omega;\qquad
 y\nmid\mathscr A\Omega.
\]
Then, for every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 |V_{\rm rec}^{(0)}|
 \ll_{\varepsilon,C_0,C_B,C_F}Q^\varepsilon BQF,             \tag{7}
\]
\[
 |V_{\rm rec}^{(\mathrm{FR})}|
 \ll_{\varepsilon,C_0,C_F}Q^\varepsilon U^2Q^2F^2.           \tag{8}
\]
Thus fact \(61cf02eb05b38a54\)'s original individual-copy-envelope
hypothesis is not claimed to be discharged. Equations (7)-(8) are a
separate aggregate singleton corollary. The only remaining sector is the
literal recombined \(V_{\rm rec}^{(\mathrm{NR})}\), with both reciprocity
phases retained.

4. The support of \(\gamma_k(y)\) has \(y\) squarefree and
\(\omega(y)=k\). Hence a fixed \(y\) occurs for at most one \(k\), and
every supported \(k\) satisfies
\[
 k\le {\log(2Y)\over\log2}=O(\log Q).                         \tag{9}
\]
Therefore summing the fixed-\(k\) conclusions introduces at most
polylogarithmic multiplicity and never a power of \(Q\).
d63101722d12c88c.proof:
Fact b69e09aaac3766d9 was proved after fixing exactly the orientation, outer-gcd layer, source, parent, fixed-\(U\), high, projective fibre, stopping length, dyadic \(u,y\) blocks and frequency block displayed here. Its proof first recombines the marker genealogy and every target-gcd, order/equal-cell, collision, deletion and provenance descendant at each fixed source coordinate. It then performs coefficient matching, before any absolute value or Cauchy inequality, with the stopping factors \(\alpha_k(u)\), \(\gamma_k(y)\), the divisor-bounded one-variable factors \(a_q,b_h\), the Poisson scalar \(\omega_F\), and the projective amplitude \(\Psi_F\). This is a coordinatewise coefficient identity, not merely an equality obtained after summing phases. The matched coefficient is exactly the right side of (2). It follows that the coefficient at each \((u,y,q,h)\) is the sum of all old siblings at that coordinate, proving (3). Substitution proves (4), while the construction in b69 retains the outside Poisson factor, both frequency signs, target, phase and every frozen or recombined label listed in the statement.

We prove (5) only for the aggregate. By the fixed-order Poisson decay in b69 and \(F\le C_FH_P\),
\[
 |\omega_F|\ll_{C_F}1.
\]
Write the projective representation supplied there as
\[
 \Psi_F=\sum_\rho\eta_\rho
 A_\rho(q)B_\rho(h)C_\rho(u)D_\rho(y),
 \qquad \sum_\rho|\eta_\rho|\ll1,
\]
with every one-variable factor uniformly bounded. Hence
\[
 \|\Psi_F\|_\infty\ll1.
\]
The definition of \(\alpha_k\) gives \(|\alpha_k(u)|\le1\). By fact
6414b11506a84ff0,
\[
 \gamma_k(y)=
 1_{\substack{y\ {\rm squarefree}\\ \omega(y)=k\\
 P^+(y)\le L\\S_0<y}}
 {1\over k}\#\{p:p\mid y,\ p\ {\rm prime},\ y/p\le S_0\},
\]
so \(0\le\gamma_k(y)\le1\). If
\(|a_q|\le\tau_{J_0}(q)(\log(2Q))^{C_1}\) and
\(|b_h|\le\tau_{J_0}(|h|)(\log(2Q))^{C_2}\), enlarge the fixed divisor
order and use
\[
 \tau_{J_0}(q)\tau_{J_0}(|h|)
 \le \tau_{2J_0}(q|h|)
 \le \tau_{2J_0}(uyq|h|).
\]
Together with (2), this proves (5). This argument applies after summing
the old siblings and says nothing about the size of any summand before
that cancellation.

We next reproduce the algebra and counting for the singleton family.
For every supported coordinate, \((q,uy)=(u,y)=1\). Additive
reciprocity followed by the Chinese remainder theorem gives
\[
 e_q\!\left(-\mathscr A h(uy)^{-1}\right)
 =
 e\!\left(-{\mathscr A h\over quy}\right)
 e_u\!\left(\mathscr A h(qy)^{-1}\right)
 e_y\!\left(\mathscr A h(qu)^{-1}\right).                    \tag{10}
\]
Put
\[
 \widehat c_y^{\rm rec}(u,q,h)
 =c_k^{\rm rec}(u,y;q,h)
 e\!\left(-{\mathscr A h\over quy}\right)
 e_u\!\left(\mathscr A h(qy)^{-1}\right).
\]
Expanding the square of \(G_y^{\rm rec}\), the difference of the two
last phases in (10) is
\[
 e_y\!\left(
 \mathscr A\Omega(q_1q_2u_1u_2)^{-1}\right),
\]
with \(\Omega\) as in (6). This proves the exact three-sector
partition in the statement and retains both the inverse-\(y\) phase
modulo \(u_i\) and the inverse-\(u_i\) phase modulo \(y\).

For the zero sector put \(x_i=q_iu_i\). Then
\[
 UQ\le x_i<4UQ.
\]
Each fixed \(x_i\) has at most \(\tau(x_i)\) supported
factorizations \(x_i=q_iu_i\). If \(\Omega=0\), then
\[
 h_1x_2=h_2x_1.
\]
The nonzero \(h_i\) have the same sign, with two choices. Write uniquely
\[
 (x_i,|h_i|)=k_i(a,b),\qquad (a,b)=1.
\]
The two dyadic rectangles make \(k_1,k_2\) comparable. For a fixed
ordered pair \((k_1,k_2)\), with \(k=\max(k_1,k_2)\), there are
\(O(UQ/k)\) choices for \(a\) and \(O(F/k)\) choices for \(b\).
There are \(O(k)\) comparable ordered pairs with maximum \(k\).
Consequently the number of ordered
\((x_1,h_1,x_2,h_2)\) is
\[
 \ll UQF\sum_{k\le4UQ+2F}{1\over k}
 \ll UQF\log(2UQF).                                         \tag{11}
\]
The two factorizations \(x_i=q_iu_i\) and the two aggregate
coefficient bounds (5) cost \(Q^\varepsilon\), because all variables
have polynomial size. There are fewer than \(2Y\) supported integers
\(y\). Absolute summation and \(UY\le C_BB\) give
\[
 |V_{\rm rec}^{(0)}|
 \ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon YUQF
 \ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon BQF,
\]
which is (7).

For the fully resonant sector, fix
\((u_1,q_1,h_1,u_2,q_2,h_2)\) with \(\Omega\ne0\). Since
\(\mathscr A\ne0\), the integer \(\mathscr A\Omega\) is nonzero and
has polynomial size in \(Q\). The number of positive integers
\(y\in[Y,2Y)\) satisfying \(y\mid\mathscr A\Omega\) is therefore at
most
\[
 \tau(|\mathscr A\Omega|)\ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon.
\]
All literal support conditions only reduce this count. There are
\(O(U^2Q^2F^2)\) ordered row sextuples, and (5) absorbs their two
weights into \(Q^\varepsilon\). Absolute summation proves (8).

Finally the displayed formula for \(\gamma_k\) shows simultaneously
that its support has \(y\) squarefree and \(\omega(y)=k\). Thus \(k\)
is determined by \(y\), while \(2^k\le y<2Y\). This proves (9) and the
polylogarithmic multiplicity assertion. No step invokes or proves the
old individual coefficient envelope from fact 61cf02eb05b38a54.

glossary.Lambda_k^rec(u,y): The singleton family containing the aggregate coefficient c_k^rec at fixed u,y.
glossary.V_rec^(0): The exact-slope Omega=0 sector of the recombined singleton pre-Cauchy energy.
glossary.V_rec^(FR): The nonzero-Omega fully resonant sector y dividing the target times Omega of the recombined singleton pre-Cauchy energy.
glossary.V_rec^(NR): The complementary nonresonant sector of the recombined singleton pre-Cauchy energy.
glossary.c_k^rec: The singleton aggregate coefficient obtained by summing every old exact-copy coefficient at fixed k,u,y,q,h before any absolute value.

d659d90d40151040.title: Fix a real number H>=2, an integer q>=1, and finite sets Sigma and Tau. For sigma in Sigma and tau in Tau let a_sigma>=0 and b_tau>=0 be real weights, let C_sigma and C_tau be integer carriers divisible by q, and let S_sigma and S_tau be finite supports. Put k_sigma=C_sigma/q and k_tau=C_tau/q. Define
d659d90d40151040.author: slava chan
d659d90d40151040.statement:
Fix a real number H>=2, an integer q>=1, and finite sets Sigma and Tau. For sigma in Sigma and tau in Tau let a_sigma>=0 and b_tau>=0 be real weights, let C_sigma and C_tau be integer carriers divisible by q, and let S_sigma and S_tau be finite supports. Put k_sigma=C_sigma/q and k_tau=C_tau/q. Define
E_{0,q}=sum_{tau in Tau} b_tau sum_{sigma in Sigma: S_sigma intersect S_tau is empty, C_sigma=C_tau} a_sigma.
Let ell be an integer satisfying ell>2 max({|k_sigma|:sigma in Sigma} union {|k_tau|:tau in Tau}), with the maximum of the empty set interpreted as 0. Write e_ell(x)=exp(2 pi i x/ell), and define
L_{q,S}(t)=sum_{sigma in Sigma:S_sigma intersect S is empty}a_sigma e_ell(t k_sigma),
X_q(t)=sum_{tau in Tau}b_tau e_ell(-t k_tau)L_{q,S_tau}(t)
for t modulo ell. Then the exact support-dependent transpose identity
E_{0,q}=ell^{-1}sum_{t modulo ell}X_q(t)
holds.

Define the deleted and common carrier weights
L_{q,S}(C)=sum_{sigma in Sigma:S_sigma intersect S is empty,C_sigma=C}a_sigma,
L_q(C)=sum_{sigma in Sigma:C_sigma=C}a_sigma.
Thus L_{q,S}(C)<=L_q(C) pointwise.

For the following conditional transfer, suppose every tau in Tau is equipped with four pairwise distinct odd primes r_1(tau),...,r_4(tau) and four integers b_1(tau),...,b_4(tau). For i<j and a sign s in {+1,-1}, put
S_{ij}^s(tau)=b_i(tau)r_j(tau)+s b_j(tau)r_i(tau).
Partition Tau, in the displayed order, into the b_4-zero stratum Tau_0={tau:b_4(tau)=0}, the small-strip stratum Tau_s consisting of the remaining tau for which either min_{i<j}|b_i(tau)b_j(tau)|<=H or for some i<j and s one has
|S_{ij}^s(tau)| min(|b_i(tau)|,|b_j(tau)|)<=H^3,
the large-gcd stratum Tau_g consisting of the remaining tau for which for some i<j and s one has
H gcd(|C_tau|,|S_{ij}^s(tau)|)>=|b_i(tau)b_j(tau)|,
and the generic stratum Tau_* consisting of all remaining tau.

For every ordered quadruple of pairwise distinct odd primes (r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4), put G=r_1r_2 and T=r_3r_4. Let zeta_G be the residue class modulo G which is 1 modulo r_1 and -1 modulo r_2, and let eta_T be the residue class modulo T which is 1 modulo r_3 and -1 modulo r_4. Let <x>_m be the unique integer in (-m/2,m/2] congruent to x modulo m. Fix literal integer frequency windows I_i(r_i) for i=1,2,3,4. For an integer C define Omega_C to be the set of these ordered prime quadruples for which, with
B=<C T^{-1}>_G, z=<B zeta_G>_G, D=(C-BT)/G, w=<C G^{-1}eta_T>_T,
one has B congruent to z modulo 2, D congruent to w modulo 2, and the four recovered integers
(B+z)/(2r_2), (B-z)/(2r_1), (D+w)/(2r_4), (D-w)/(2r_3)
belong respectively to I_1(r_1),I_2(r_2),I_3(r_3),I_4(r_4). Put I_C=|Omega_C|.

Assume the following explicitly named paid-stratum and comparison hypotheses for some real numbers A>=1, eta>=0, and kappa>=1:
(1) the b_4-zero, small-strip, and large-gcd contributions E_j=sum_{tau in Tau_j}b_tau L_{q,S_tau}(C_tau), for j in {0,s,g}, are each at most A H^{14+eta};
(2) parity and literal-window recovery are exact on Tau_*: there is a map phi:Tau_* to the disjoint union of the Omega_C such that phi(tau) lies in Omega_{C_tau}, has the ordered orientation (r_1(tau),r_2(tau),r_3(tau),r_4(tau)), and its four recovered integers equal b_1(tau),...,b_4(tau);
(3) the orientation and right-weight multiplicity is bounded by kappa: for every omega in the disjoint union of the Omega_C,
sum_{tau in Tau_*:phi(tau)=omega}b_tau<=kappa;
(4) the support-weight comparison is the pointwise deletion inequality L_{q,S_tau}(C_tau)<=L_q(C_tau);
(5) kappa<=H^eta and the literal DCE34cu majorant satisfies
sum_C L_q(C)I_C<=A H^{14+eta}.
Then
E_{0,q}<=4A H^{14+2eta}.
Consequently, for an asymptotic family in which A is bounded and eta=eta(H) tends to 0, the literal frozen same-cell disjoint consumer satisfies E_{0,q}<=H^{14+o(1)}.

The implication in the preceding paragraph is one-way: deleting the support condition enlarges a nonnegative source, and no reverse comparison follows. More generally, if N_C is any other nonnegative sharp three-hit count, then bounds for sum_C L_q(C)N_C and sum_C L_q(C)I_C are power-equivalent only after explicit paid-strata comparisons in both directions. Precisely, if 0<=rho<=H^eta and nonnegative R_1,R_2<=A H^{14+eta} satisfy
sum_C L_q(C)N_C<=rho sum_C L_q(C)I_C+R_1,
sum_C L_q(C)I_C<=rho sum_C L_q(C)N_C+R_2,
then an A H^{14+eta} bound for either weighted sum gives a 2A H^{14+2eta} bound for the other. Thus a DCE34ch-to-DCE34cu comparison is not an identity from the gate definitions; it is power-equivalence only after its boundary, parity, window, and orientation comparisons are paid.
d659d90d40151040.proof:
Expand the definition of X_q(t), interchange the two finite sums, and use additive-character orthogonality:
ell^{-1}sum_{t modulo ell} e_ell(t(k_sigma-k_tau))
is 1 if k_sigma is congruent to k_tau modulo ell and is 0 otherwise. The size condition on ell gives |k_sigma-k_tau|<ell. Therefore congruence modulo ell is equivalent to equality as integers. Since C_sigma=qk_sigma and C_tau=qk_tau, this equality is equivalent to C_sigma=C_tau. The remaining support condition is exactly S_sigma intersect S_tau empty, so the expanded Fourier sum equals E_{0,q}. This proves the exact support-dependent transpose identity.

For every S and C, the summands defining L_{q,S}(C) form a subset of those defining L_q(C), and every a_sigma is nonnegative. Hence L_{q,S}(C)<=L_q(C). This proves the support deletion comparison, rather than inferring it from a total-mass estimate.

The four sets Tau_0,Tau_s,Tau_g,Tau_* are disjoint by their sequential definition and have union Tau. Hence
E_{0,q}=E_0+E_s+E_g+E_*,
where E_*=sum_{tau in Tau_*}b_tau L_{q,S_tau}(C_tau).
Apply pointwise support deletion to E_* and group by phi:
E_*<=sum_{tau in Tau_*}b_tau L_q(C_tau)
=sum_C L_q(C) sum_{omega in Omega_C} sum_{tau in Tau_*:phi(tau)=omega}b_tau.
The exact parity/window/orientation hypothesis ensures that every generic tau is grouped into Omega_{C_tau}; no generic term is discarded or placed at a different carrier. The multiplicity hypothesis makes the innermost sum at most kappa. Therefore
E_*<=kappa sum_C L_q(C)I_C
<=H^eta A H^{14+eta}=A H^{14+2eta}.
Each of E_0,E_s,E_g is at most A H^{14+eta}, and H^eta>=1 because H>=2 and eta>=0. It follows that
E_{0,q}<=3A H^{14+eta}+A H^{14+2eta}<=4A H^{14+2eta}.
If A is bounded and eta(H) tends to zero, the exponent 2eta(H) tends to zero and the constant 4A is H^{o(1)}, proving E_{0,q}<=H^{14+o(1)}.

To see why the arrow cannot be reversed from the definitions, take one carrier C, one right packet tau, and one left packet sigma with C_sigma=C_tau=C, positive weights, and intersecting supports. Then E_{0,q}=0, while L_q(C)>0; if Omega_C contains the image of tau, then L_q(C)I_C>0. Thus the deleted literal energy can be smaller than the common majorant.

For the final power-equivalence assertion, suppose first that sum_C L_q(C)I_C<=A H^{14+eta}. Since rho is nonnegative, the first paid comparison gives
sum_C L_q(C)N_C<=rho A H^{14+eta}+R_1
<=A H^{14+2eta}+A H^{14+eta}
<=2A H^{14+2eta}.
The reverse implication follows from the second paid comparison by the identical calculation with N_C and I_C interchanged. Therefore the two weighted estimates are power-equivalent only under both comparison inequalities. The gate definitions alone provide neither inequality, which proves the stated scope limitation.

d67c1ddb0bdcd135.title: PRIME-RAY RESIDUE ALIGNMENT NO-FIT FOR A GENERIC PROOF OF C-HILBERT-OP-SUP. Let p>=5 be an odd prime, let T be an integer with gcd(T,p)=1, and let r be a unit residue modulo p. Let d_1,...,d_H be distinct positive integers, each congruent to r modulo p. They may in addition be chosen squarefree and with all prime factors above any prescribed roughness threshold; the theorem assumes such a list when those extra properties are desired and does not assert its existence in a specified dyadic interval
d67c1ddb0bdcd135.author: slava chan
d67c1ddb0bdcd135.statement:
PRIME-RAY RESIDUE ALIGNMENT NO-FIT FOR A GENERIC PROOF OF C-HILBERT-OP-SUP. Let p>=5 be an odd prime, let T be an integer with gcd(T,p)=1, and let r be a unit residue modulo p. Let d_1,...,d_H be distinct positive integers, each congruent to r modulo p. They may in addition be chosen squarefree and with all prime factors above any prescribed roughness threshold; the theorem assumes such a list when those extra properties are desired and does not assert its existence in a specified dyadic interval.

For 1<=s<=p-1 define the primitive signed ray
R_s=(+1,p,p+s).                                                   (1)
For s!=t put
Delta_0(R_s,R_t)=p(s-t).                                         (2)
Then the physical conductor and reduced numerator associated with target T are
m_q(R_s,R_t)=p,
C_q(R_s,R_t)=T(s-t).                                             (3)
For each d_j define the (p-1)-by-(p-1) matrix K_{d_j}, indexed by the rays, by zero diagonal and reversed-slot off-diagonal entries
(K_{d_j})_{R_t,R_s}
 =K^circ_{p,T(s-t)}(d_j)
 =e_p(-T(s-t)d_j^{-1})+1/(p-1).                                 (4)
All the matrices K_{d_j} are identical. Moreover,
||K_{d_j}||_{op}>=p-3,                                          (5)
and hence
||sum_{j=1}^H K_{d_j}||_{op}>=H(p-3).                            (6)

Consequently, even for an exact prime physical conductor and a family of genuine centered inverse kernels arising from a complete set of primitive rays, pointwise centering, squarefreeness, roughness, and the d-coprimality gate do not by themselves imply an operator partial-sum bound of order p^2 when H is larger than a constant multiple of p. A proof of C-HILBERT-OP-SUP in fact d92616c2bca6126f must use a property that prevents or cancels this common-residue alignment in the literal Good-W support, coefficients, or pair selectors. This is an abstract arithmetic-kernel no-fit. It does not assert that the list d_j or the complete ray family occurs in one literal Good-W outer row, does not refute C-HILBERT-OP-SUP for the literal source, and proves no lower bound for C-qSRC_C, the tail, or Goldbach.
d67c1ddb0bdcd135.proof:
The rays in (1) are primitive because gcd(p,p+s)=gcd(p,s)=1 for 1<=s<=p-1. With epsilon=epsilon'=+1, a=a'=p, b=p+s, and b'=p+t, the primitive determinant is
Delta_0=(p+s)p-(p+t)p=p(s-t),
which proves (2).

By the conductor formula in fact 764588e99974a6d9,
m_q=p^2/gcd(p^2,Tp(s-t)).
Since gcd(T,p)=1 and 0<|s-t|<p, the greatest common divisor is p. This proves the first part of (3), and division by that greatest common divisor gives C_q=T(s-t), proving the second part.

For prime p, fact 764588e99974a6d9 gives
K^circ_{p,c}(z)=e_p(-c z^{-1})+1/(p-1)
for units c,z modulo p. Here s-t and d_j are units modulo p, so (4) follows. Since every d_j is congruent to the same unit r modulo p, every inverse d_j^{-1} is congruent to r^{-1} modulo p. Thus every matrix in (4) is the same matrix K.

Put u_s=e_p(Ts r^{-1}) for 1<=s<=p-1, let J be the all-ones matrix, and let I be the identity matrix. For all s,t, the matrix u tensor u^* has entry
u_t conjugate(u_s)=e_p(-T(s-t)r^{-1}).
The matrix in (4) has zero diagonal. Therefore
K=u tensor u^* +(1/(p-1))J-(p/(p-1))I.                          (7)
The vector u has squared norm p-1. Because Tr^{-1} is nonzero modulo p,
sum_{s=1}^{p-1}u_s=-1.                                         (8)
Taking the Rayleigh quotient of (7) at u gives
<u,Ku>/||u||_2^2
 =(p-1)-p/(p-1)+1/(p-1)^2.                                    (9)
For p>=5, the right side of (9) is at least p-3. Since K is Hermitian, its operator norm is at least the absolute value of every Rayleigh quotient, proving (5).

All H matrices are K, so their sum is HK. Homogeneity of the operator norm and (5) prove (6). If the d_j are also squarefree with every prime factor above a threshold Z and p<Z, then they satisfy the abstract high-rough and coprimality properties, but those properties do not change their common residue modulo p or any calculation above. The final scope statements follow.

glossary.K_{d_j}: The abstract prime-conductor centered ray matrix associated with the common-residue dilator d_j.
glossary.prime-ray residue alignment: A family of dilators occupying one unit residue modulo p, so their complete centered ray matrices are identical.

d6a6c34620bdfe9d.title: ONE-COMMON-ROW ADJOINT CRITERION FOR A REPEATED RATIONAL OUTPUT RAY. Let Rcal be a finite nonempty family of odd squarefree integers greater than one. Let h and b be nonzero integers such that gcd(bh,r)=1 for every r in Rcal. Let Zcal be a finite nonempty row set. For every r in Rcal choose a unit c_r modulo r, a subset Zcal_r of Zcal, coordinates x_{r,rho} in G_r and complex coefficients alpha_{r,rho} for rho in Zcal_r, and define
d6a6c34620bdfe9d.author: slava chan
d6a6c34620bdfe9d.statement:
ONE-COMMON-ROW ADJOINT CRITERION FOR A REPEATED RATIONAL OUTPUT RAY. Let Rcal be a finite nonempty family of odd squarefree integers greater than one. Let h and b be nonzero integers such that gcd(bh,r)=1 for every r in Rcal. Let Zcal be a finite nonempty row set. For every r in Rcal choose a unit c_r modulo r, a subset Zcal_r of Zcal, coordinates x_{r,rho} in G_r and complex coefficients alpha_{r,rho} for rho in Zcal_r, and define
(I_rz)(x)=sum_{rho in Zcal_r:x_{r,rho}=x}alpha_{r,rho}z_rho.         (1)
Let P_{r,r} be the primitive-conductor projector from fact b4934b4981fc5817. Define
Jz=(P_{r,r}I_rz)_{r in Rcal}
