in Hcal=direct_sum_{r in Rcal}l2(G_r).                              (2)
For complex weights omega_r put
u_{r,b}(x)=e_r(-c_rb^{-1}x),                                       (3)
U_b=(overline{omega_r}u_{r,b})_{r in Rcal} in Hcal,                 (4)
and
S_b(z)=sum_{r in Rcal}omega_r A_{r,c_r}(I_rz;bh,h),                 (5)
where A_{r,c_r} is defined in fact 9d1a11eb8a597a64. Then
S_b(z)=<Jz,U_b>_{Hcal}=<z,J^*U_b>,                                 (6)
J^*U_b=sum_{r in Rcal}I_r^*P_{r,r}(overline{omega_r}u_{r,b}),       (7)
and
sup_{||z||_2=1}|S_b(z)|^2=||J^*U_b||_2^2.                           (8)
For every real Delta>=0, the largest possible contribution of the single ray Delta|S_b(z)|^2 over one common unit row vector z is
Delta||J^*U_b||_2^2.                                                (9)

Thus simultaneous realization of a large primitive single-output scale across many active products is exactly the condition that ||J^*U_b|| be large. Separate realization of the fact 731aecc74ff42615 saturator in each l2(G_r) does not by itself imply such a lower bound for ||J^*U_b||, because the same z must generate every P_{r,r}I_rz and the signed vectors in (7) may cancel. Conversely, any cancellation produced by literal sibling, face, mask or projective coefficients included in alpha_{r,rho} or omega_r occurs inside (7), before its norm is taken. This theorem asserts no upper or lower bound for the literal J^*U_b, no multi-ray estimate, no shared-prime aggregate, no C4 estimate, and no Goldbach conclusion.
d6a6c34620bdfe9d.proof:
From the definition in fact 9d1a11eb8a597a64,
A_{r,c_r}(f;j,h)
=sum_{chi primitive modulo r}fhat(overline chi)chi(-c_r)
 tau_r(overline chi)chi(-hj^{-1}).                                 (10)
Put j=bh. Since b and h are units modulo r,
h(bh)^{-1}=b^{-1} modulo r.
Consequently (10) gives the exact identity
A_{r,c_r}(f;bh,h)=A_{r,c_r}(f;b,1).                                (11)
Apply equation (4) of fact ef131ab87c99303c to the right side of (11), with j_0=b and with the incidence (1). Its phase vector is exactly u_{r,b} from (3), so
A_{r,c_r}(I_rz;bh,h)
=<P_{r,r}I_rz,u_{r,b}>_{l2(G_r)}.                                  (12)

Multiply (12) by omega_r and sum over r. Using inner products linear in their first variable,
S_b(z)
=sum_r<P_{r,r}I_rz,overline{omega_r}u_{r,b}>
=<Jz,U_b>_{Hcal}.                                                   (13)
The definition of the Hilbert-space adjoint proves the second equality in (6).

The direct sum and Rcal are finite, so the adjoint of J is the sum of its component adjoints. Each P_{r,r} is self-adjoint. Apply these observations to (4) to prove (7).

Zcal is nonempty, so its l2 unit sphere is nonempty. Equation (6) makes S_b the linear functional represented by J^*U_b. Its norm is ||J^*U_b||_2, proving (8). Multiplication by Delta>=0 proves (9).

Fact 731aecc74ff42615 identifies the maximum of one unrestricted primitive-modulus functional. Equations (7)-(8) show that the simultaneous functional instead depends on the norm of one signed sum in the common row space. Individual component norms do not supply a lower bound for the norm of their signed sum. Literal scalar signs and masks placed in alpha_{r,rho} or omega_r remain inside that sum by linearity. This proves the criterion and every scope assertion.

glossary.J: the joint primitive incidence from one common row space into the direct sum of primitive modulus spaces
glossary.S_b: the signed primitive synthesis on the repeated rational output ray j=bh
glossary.U_b: the direct-sum primitive additive-phase vector weighted by the signed active-product coefficients

d6fd2c2cf8b5d0f0.title: Fix real numbers 1/2<a<b<1. Let W be a nonzero nonnegative continuously differentiable real function supported in [a,b]. Let ψ be a continuously differentiable real function on the positive reals such that 0≤ψ≤1, ψ(u)=0 for 0<u≤1, and ψ(u)=1 for u≥2. Let B=B(W,ψ)>0 be the exponent supplied by fact 2827630745a3225b. Let x tend to infinity through values for which N=2x is an even integer not representable as a sum of two primes, and put
d6fd2c2cf8b5d0f0.author: slava chan
d6fd2c2cf8b5d0f0.statement:
Fix real numbers 1/2<a<b<1. Let W be a nonzero nonnegative continuously differentiable real function supported in [a,b]. Let ψ be a continuously differentiable real function on the positive reals such that 0≤ψ≤1, ψ(u)=0 for 0<u≤1, and ψ(u)=1 for u≥2. Let B=B(W,ψ)>0 be the exponent supplied by fact 2827630745a3225b. Let x tend to infinity through values for which N=2x is an even integer not representable as a sum of two primes, and put
D_*=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B),
C_2=∏_{p>2}p(p-2)/(p-1)^2,
𝔠(N)=C_2∏_{p|N,p>2}(p-1)/(p-2),
and c_W=2∫_0^∞W(u)du.
Let Φ be a real function supported in [1/2,2] such that
Σ_{j∈Z}Φ(t/2^j)=1
for every real t>0. Define
H_{N,W,ψ}=Σ_{d,m,q≥1; dm+q=N}
 μ(d)log(m)W(dm/x)ψ(d/D_*)Λ(q).
By fact 2827630745a3225b,
H_{N,W,ψ}=-c_W𝔠(N)x+o_{W,ψ}(𝔠(N)x)
uniformly over these bad even integers.

Split H_{N,W,ψ}=H_{N,W,ψ}^{prime}+H_{N,W,ψ}^{pp}, where the first sum is restricted to q=p prime and the second to q=p^j with p prime and j≥2. For every ε>0,
|H_{N,W,ψ}^{pp}|≪_{ε,W,ψ}x^(1/2+ε).
Consequently, uniformly over the same bad even integers,
H_{N,W,ψ}^{prime}=-c_W𝔠(N)x+o_{W,ψ}(𝔠(N)x).

For positive dyadic D,M,U define
P_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;U)
=Σ_{d,m≥1, p prime; dm+p=N}
 μ(d)log(m)log(p)W(dm/x)ψ(d/D_*)
 Φ(d/D)Φ(m/M)Φ(p/U).
Then
H_{N,W,ψ}^{prime}=Σ_{D,M,U}P_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;U)
exactly. Put
J_x=ceil(log_2 x)+4,
L_DM=ceil(log_2(16b/a))+1,
L_U=ceil(log_2(4(2-a)/(2-b)))+1.
At most J_x L_DM L_U of these prime blocks are nonzero. Hence, for every sufficiently large bad N, some positive dyadic triple (D,M,U) satisfies
P_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;U)
≤-c_W𝔠(N)x/(2 J_x L_DM L_U).

Every nonzero such block satisfies
D>D_*/2, ax/4≤DM≤4bx,
and
(2-b)x/2≤U≤2(2-a)x.
Moreover every nonzero incidence in it has d≥2, p>x>d, gcd(d,N)=1, and the block has the exact prime-progression normal form
P_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;U)
=Σ_{d≥2, gcd(d,N)=1} μ(d)ψ(d/D_*)Φ(d/D)
 Σ_{p prime, p<N, p≡N (mod d)}
 log(p) log((N-p)/d) W((N-p)/x)
 Φ(((N-p)/d)/M)Φ(p/U).
This is a pointwise statement for the same fixed N. It asserts neither an average over N nor any distribution estimate for primes in the displayed growing residue class.
d6fd2c2cf8b5d0f0.proof:
On the support of W, ax≤dm≤bx. Since N=2x and q=N-dm, every reflected integer in H lies in
(2-b)x≤q≤(2-a)x.
By the defining support of the von Mangoldt function, q is either a genuine prime or a prime power p^j with j≥2, so the displayed splitting of H is exact.

We first record a self-contained divisor estimate. For every δ>0 there is C_δ such that τ(n)≤C_δ n^δ for all positive integers n. Indeed, write n=∏p^v. For every p≥2^(1/δ), one has v+1≤2^v≤p^(δv). There are only finitely many primes below 2^(1/δ), and for each such p the supremum over v≥0 of (v+1)p^(-δv) is finite. Multiplying those finitely many suprema proves the claim. Also log n≪_δ n^δ for n≥2, since the function (log t)t^(-δ) is bounded on [2,∞).

We now bound the higher-prime-power part absolutely. For a fixed q=p^j in the support interval, put n=N-q. Then ax≤n≤bx, and
Σ_{dm=n}|μ(d)|log(m)|W(n/x)| |ψ(d/D_*)|
≤||W||_∞ τ(n)log n.
Given ε>0, apply the preceding two estimates with δ=ε/4; this is O_{ε,W}(x^(ε/2)). Also Λ(q)≤log(2x)≪_ε x^(ε/2). The number of prime powers p^j≤2x with j≥2 is at most
Σ_{2≤j≤log_2(2x)}(2x)^(1/j)
≤(2x)^(1/2)+log_2(2x)(2x)^(1/3)
≪_ε x^(1/2+ε/4).
Replacing ε by a fixed smaller fraction at the start, these estimates give
|H_{N,W,ψ}^{pp}|≪_{ε,W,ψ}x^(1/2+ε).
Fact f41f5f91b52e0d13 gives 𝔠(N)≥C_2>0. Choosing ε<1/2 therefore makes the prime-power bound o(𝔠(N)x). Subtracting it from the verified source asymptotic in fact 2827630745a3225b proves the asserted asymptotic for H^{prime}. Fact b7fcb27a091203e5 gives the compatible exact sibling interpretation: genuine von Mangoldt mass is supported only on prime powers, and the present split discards precisely the exponents j≥2 rather than selecting an individual divisor sibling.

Insert the dyadic partition identity in d,m,p. All sums are finite, and this gives the exact decomposition of H^{prime} into P(D,M;U).

We count its nonzero labels more sharply than the generic three-variable count. If a summand is nonzero, support of Φ and W gives
ax/4≤DM≤4bx.
For each fixed dyadic D, the possible dyadic M therefore lie in an interval whose endpoint ratio is 16b/a. Hence there are at most L_DM such M. Also p lies in [(2-b)x,(2-a)x], while Φ(p/U)≠0 implies p/2≤U≤2p. Thus
(2-b)x/2≤U≤2(2-a)x,
an interval of endpoint ratio 4(2-a)/(2-b), and at most L_U dyadic U occur. Finally the same elementary label count used in fact 0880dc648c429047 gives at most J_x possible D labels. Therefore at most J_x L_DM L_U prime triples are nonzero.

For sufficiently large bad N, the prime asymptotic gives
H^{prime}≤-c_W𝔠(N)x/2.
If every nonzero P block were greater than
-c_W𝔠(N)x/(2 J_x L_DM L_U),
their sum would be greater than -c_W𝔠(N)x/2. Thus at least one block satisfies the claimed inequality.

It remains to record the structural properties of every nonzero prime incidence. Since ψ(u)=0 for u≤1, nonzero ψ(d/D_*) implies d>D_*. With Φ(d/D)≠0, one has d≤2D, hence D>D_*/2. The d=1 term vanishes because D_*≥1 and ψ(1/D_*)=0. Furthermore
p=N-dm≥(2-b)x>x,
whereas d≤dm≤bx<x. Thus p>d. From dm+p=N one has gcd(d,N)=gcd(d,p); since p is prime and p>d, this gcd is one. Conversely the equation is equivalent to p≡N modulo d and m=(N-p)/d. Substitution gives exactly the displayed prime-progression normal form, with all original weights retained. No distributional assertion is used in this algebraic rewriting.

glossary.H_{N,W,ψ}^{pp}: the part of the smooth reflected source for which the reflected integer is a prime power of exponent at least two
glossary.H_{N,W,ψ}^{prime}: the part of the smooth reflected source for which the reflected integer is a genuine prime
glossary.L_DM: the constant ceil(log_2(16b/a))+1 bounding the number of M labels for a fixed D
glossary.L_U: the constant ceil(log_2(4(2-a)/(2-b)))+1 bounding the number of U labels
glossary.P_{N,W,ψ}(D,M;U): the genuine-prime dyadic block at divisor, complementary-factor, and prime scales

d7186c34eddceffa.title: Let m be a positive odd integer, let s belong to {1,-1}, let K be an integer with gcd(K,m)=1, and let W be a complex-valued function on the residues modulo m. Put e_q(z)=exp(2 pi i z/q), define
d7186c34eddceffa.author: slava chan
d7186c34eddceffa.statement:
Let m be a positive odd integer, let s belong to {1,-1}, let K be an integer with gcd(K,m)=1, and let W be a complex-valued function on the residues modulo m. Put e_q(z)=exp(2 pi i z/q), define
W_hat(ell)=sum_{u modulo m}W(u)e_m(-ell u),
W_mean=m^(-1)sum_{u modulo m}W(u), and W_cent(u)=W(u)-W_mean.
Choose an integer rho satisfying 2s rho=1 modulo m. For residues a,b modulo m^2 define
S_W(a,b)=sum_{u modulo m}W(u) Delta_{m^2}(ab-K-2smu),
where Delta_q is the divisibility indicator from fact 4f2052945785b331. Then
S_W(a,b)=Delta_m(ab-K) m^(-1)sum_{ell modulo m}
 W_hat(ell)e_{m^2}(ell rho(ab-K)).                                      (1)
The right side is independent of the chosen integer representative rho.

The ell=0 term in (1) is exactly
S_mean(a,b)=W_mean Delta_m(ab-K),                                      (2)
and the sum over ell nonzero is exactly S_{W_cent}(a,b). Hence only the zero digit Fourier mode collapses to the unweighted modulus-m product selector; every nonzero digit mode retains the displayed modulus-m^2 additive phase on that product graph.

With the ell^2 norm and inner product taken over all ordered pairs (a,b) modulo m^2, one has the exact identities
||S_W||_2^2=phi(m^2)sum_{u modulo m}|W(u)|^2,                           (3)
<S_mean,S_{W_cent}>=0,                                                  (4)
||S_mean||_2^2=m phi(m^2)|W_mean|^2,                                   (5)
||S_{W_cent}||_2^2
 =phi(m^2)sum_u|W_cent(u)|^2
 =[phi(m^2)/m]sum_{ell nonzero modulo m}|W_hat(ell)|^2.                 (6)
In particular, the m fixed-digit product graphs are pairwise disjoint orthogonal indicator vectors, each of squared norm phi(m^2). For W identically one, every nonzero Fourier coefficient vanishes and S_W=Delta_m(ab-K); a modulus-m^2 analytic argument on a nonconstant literal digit weight must retain and estimate the nonzero ell axis rather than replacing it by its full unweighted average.
d7186c34eddceffa.proof:
Fact 4f2052945785b331 gives
S_W(a,b)=Delta_m(ab-K)W(nu_m(a,b;K,s)),
where on the support of Delta_m one has
nu_m=(2s)^(-1)(ab-K)/m modulo m.
Fourier inversion on the additive group modulo m gives
W(nu_m)=m^(-1)sum_{ell modulo m}W_hat(ell)e_m(ell nu_m).
On the support of Delta_m, write ab-K=mn. Since rho is an inverse of 2s modulo m, nu_m=rho n modulo m, and
e_m(ell nu_m)=e_m(ell rho n)=e_{m^2}(ell rho(ab-K)).
This proves (1). Replacing rho by rho+tm changes the last phase by
e_{m^2}(ell tm(ab-K))=e_m(ell t(ab-K))=1
on the support of Delta_m, proving independence. Since W_hat(0)=mW_mean, the ell=0 term is (2). Fourier inversion applied to W_cent, whose zero Fourier coefficient vanishes, identifies the nonzero-frequency part with S_{W_cent}.

For each u modulo m, let G_u be the indicator of the congruence
ab=K+2smu modulo m^2.
Fact 4f2052945785b331 proves that the supports of the G_u are pairwise disjoint and, because gcd(K,m)=1, that each support has phi(m^2) ordered unit pairs. Since S_W=sum_u W(u)G_u, orthogonality of disjoint supports gives
||S_W||_2^2=sum_u|W(u)|^2||G_u||_2^2
 =phi(m^2)sum_u|W(u)|^2,
which is (3).

Also Delta_m(ab-K)=sum_uG_u by the same fact. Therefore
<S_mean,S_{W_cent}>
 =phi(m^2) conjugate(W_mean) sum_u W_cent(u)=0,
up to the harmless choice of which inner-product slot is conjugate; this proves (4). The modulus-m graph is the disjoint union of the m digit graphs, so its squared norm is m phi(m^2), proving (5). Applying (3) to W_cent gives the first equality in (6). Additive Parseval modulo m gives
sum_u|W_cent(u)|^2=m^(-1)sum_ell|W_cent_hat(ell)|^2
 =m^(-1)sum_{ell nonzero}|W_hat(ell)|^2,
which proves the second equality. The final assertions follow directly from (1)-(6).

glossary.S_W: the weighted normal-digit selector on ordered residue pairs modulo m^2
glossary.W_hat: the additive Fourier transform of W
glossary.W_mean: the average of the digit weight W
glossary.rho: an integer inverse of 2s modulo m

d8ba46800ba433c2.title: Fix positive constants c_0,C_0,c_1,C_1 and a fixed scaled-smooth compactly supported weight mathcal W as in fact df9748efe29ab475. Let x>=3, let c_0x<=N<=C_0x be an integer, and let D,M,R,K satisfy c_1x<=DM,RK<=C_1x. After writing g=gcd(d,r), d=ga, r=gb, and L=N/g as in that fact, define for every admissible g,a,b the smooth function
d8ba46800ba433c2.author: slava chan
d8ba46800ba433c2.statement:
Fix positive constants c_0,C_0,c_1,C_1 and a fixed scaled-smooth compactly supported weight mathcal W as in fact df9748efe29ab475. Let x>=3, let c_0x<=N<=C_0x be an integer, and let D,M,R,K satisfy c_1x<=DM,RK<=C_1x. After writing g=gcd(d,r), d=ga, r=gb, and L=N/g as in that fact, define for every admissible g,a,b the smooth function
F_{g,a,b}(t)=log(t)log((L-at)/b)
 mathcal W(ga/D,t/M,gb/R,(L-at)/(bK)),
extended by zero outside its compact positive support. Use the Fourier transform
Fhat_{g,a,b}(xi)=integral_R F_{g,a,b}(t)exp(-2pi i xi t)dt.
For h nonzero define the nonzero-Poisson coefficient
lambda_{g,a,b,h}=mu(ga)mu(gb)b^{-1}Fhat_{g,a,b}(h/b).
Let Lambda_C2 be any restriction of this coefficient array to the C2 class of fact 85e63a9328d91711, so b=vpq with p,q distinct rough primes, retaining each original coefficient and every additional zero-one source mask.

(A) The total l1 mass satisfies
sum_{(g,a,b,h) in Lambda_C2}|lambda_{g,a,b,h}|
 <<_{mathcal W,c_i,C_i}DR(log x)^2.                                  (L1)
This estimate is uniform in the fixed target N and in every restriction by deletion of indices.

(B) Fix kappa with 0<kappa<1/100 and eta with 0<eta<=kappa/6. Assume
D<=x^(1/2+eta), R<=x^(9/16-kappa),
and put
Z_0=x^(3/4-4eta)/R.
Restrict further to C2 incidences whose two rough primes are at least Z_0, and to the support-disjoint, full-rough-conductor ordered pair block of fact 7cc27e1367d85c60. Apply the full-conductor face coefficient
alpha=product_{i=1}^4(1-1/r_i)
to every such pair. Then the absolute difference between the original paired block and its unique full-four-prime conductor face is
<<_{mathcal W,c_i,C_i,kappa} D^2R^2Z_0^{-1}(log x)^4
 =D^2R^3x^(-3/4+4eta)(log x)^4
 <<x^(31/16-kappa)                                                   (AFF)
for all sufficiently large x. In particular it is o_A(x^2(log x)^(-A)) for every fixed A>0.

Moreover Z_0^3>2R for all sufficiently large x, so the rough cutoff is compatible with the C2 alternative of fact 85e63a9328d91711 on every normalized modulus b<=2R.

(C) Thus, on the buffered balanced range R<=x^(9/16-kappa), the proper-conductor deletion tax is affordable relative to the squared x-scale before any absolute-value loss, using only the literal Poisson coefficient l1 mass. This does not control Q_1,Q_2, non-full frequency-conductor layers, or the modular-window obstruction: those remain the separate blocks and obstruction of facts 7cc27e1367d85c60 and 0aa454c6baf243c0. No estimate for the complete C2xC2 square and no Goldbach implication is asserted.
d8ba46800ba433c2.proof:
The exact Poisson step in fact df9748efe29ab475 writes the progression m congruent to La^{-1} modulo b as
b^{-1}sum_h Fhat_{g,a,b}(h/b)e_b(hLa^{-1}),
up to the harmless choice of Fourier sign. Thus lambda is the literal coefficient before the phase.

Scaled smoothness and compact support imply, for every fixed J>=2,
|Fhat_{g,a,b}(h/b)|
 <<_{J,mathcal W}M(log x)^2(1+|h|M/b)^(-J).                     (1)
Indeed F is supported on an interval of length O(M); every derivative after rescaling t by M is bounded by a fixed constant times (log x)^2, because the four scaled arguments in mathcal W remain in one fixed compact set and DM,RK are comparable to x. Repeated integration by parts proves (1).

For every delta>0 and J>1,
sum_{h nonzero}(1+|h|delta)^(-J)<<_J delta^(-1).
Take delta=M/b in (1). Multiplying by b^{-1} gives
sum_{h nonzero}b^{-1}|Fhat_{g,a,b}(h/b)|<<_{mathcal W} (log x)^2.  (2)

At fixed g, the scaled support permits O(D/g) integers a and O(R/g) integers b. Therefore (2), summed over a,b, is
<<DR g^(-2)(log x)^2.
The C2 condition and any extra zero-one masks only delete indices. Finally
sum_{g|N}g^(-2)<=sum_{g>=1}g^(-2)<infinity.
This proves (L1).

For (B), fact 7bcf6f85c0df5948, equivalently Part (B) of fact 7cc27e1367d85c60, gives on the supported four-distinct-prime full-conductor pair block
error <=4Z_0^(-1)(sum|lambda|)^2.
Insert (L1) to obtain
error<<D^2R^2Z_0^(-1)(log x)^4.
The definition of Z_0 gives the middle expression in (AFF).

The scale hypotheses give
D^2R^3x^(-3/4+4eta)
<=x^(1+2eta)x^(27/16-3kappa)x^(-12/16+4eta)
=x^(31/16+6eta-3kappa).
Since eta<=kappa/6, this is at most x^(31/16-2kappa). The factor (log x)^4 is at most x^kappa for sufficiently large x, proving the final bound x^(31/16-kappa). Its exponent is below two by 1/16+kappa, so it is smaller than x^2 times every fixed negative power of log x.

It remains to check compatibility with the rough classification. Since
Z_0^3/(2R)=x^(9/4-12eta)/(2R^4)
and R^4<=x^(9/4-4kappa), one has
Z_0^3/(2R)>=x^(4kappa-12eta)/2>=x^(2kappa)/2,
which tends to infinity. Hence Z_0^3>2R. On the dyadic support b=r/g<=2R/g<=2R, so Z_0^3>b as required in the rough C2 alternative.

Part (C) is a scope statement. The proof applied the conductor extraction only after restricting to the good disjoint pair block. Facts 7cc27e1367d85c60 and 0aa454c6baf243c0 explicitly leave the collision, conductor-loss, small-v, and literal-window terms outside that block, so none has been estimated here.

glossary.AFF: the buffered balanced full-conductor affordability estimate
glossary.F_{g,a,b}: the one-variable smooth source amplitude after the outer gcd split and substitution k=(L-at)/b
glossary.Lambda_C2: any exact restriction of the Poisson coefficient array to the two-rough-prime C2 class
glossary.kappa: the fixed buffer below the exponent 9/16
glossary.lambda_{g,a,b,h}: the literal nonzero-Poisson coefficient before its reciprocal phase

d90ec957015b32b5.title: Fix L>=1 and epsilon>0. Let H>=2, let C be a nonzero integer with |C|<=H^L, and let K be an integer. Put I_H=[H^2,2H^2) intersect Z and X=ceil(LH^3). For each positive integer m, let U_m be the set of tuples (a,b,c,d,r_2,r_3) such that:
d90ec957015b32b5.author: slava chan
d90ec957015b32b5.statement:
Fix L>=1 and epsilon>0. Let H>=2, let C be a nonzero integer with |C|<=H^L, and let K be an integer. Put I_H=[H^2,2H^2) intersect Z and X=ceil(LH^3). For each positive integer m, let U_m be the set of tuples (a,b,c,d,r_2,r_3) such that:
(1) a,b,c,d are even integers of absolute value at most X and ab+cd=2 K;
(2) r_2,r_3 are distinct primes in I_H;
(3) with
A=b r_3-d r_2, B=a r_2-c r_3,
q=gcd(|A|,|B|), D=ad r_2^2-bc r_3^2, J=ab-cd,
one has q=2m, AB>0, and, writing s for the common sign, the quotients
r_1=|A|/q, r_4=|B|/q
are primes in I_H such that r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4 are pairwise distinct;
(4) gcd(C,r_1r_2r_3r_4)=1, D=2sqC, and J is a nonzero multiple of 2q.

Then U_m is empty for m>2X, and, uniformly for every positive integer m,
|U_m| <<_{L,epsilon} H^epsilon X <<_{L,epsilon} H^{3+epsilon}.       (1)
The same estimate holds after weighting each tuple by the product of the four von Mangoldt prime weights, or by any fixed polylogarithmically bounded weight.

For a real number M_cond>=1, let U_{<=M_cond} be the disjoint union of U_m over positive integers m<=M_cond. Then
|U_{<=M_cond}| <<_{L,epsilon} M_cond H^{3+epsilon}.                  (2)
Consequently, for every fixed delta in (0,3), the complete submaximal-conductor range m<=H^{3-delta} satisfies
|U_{<=H^{3-delta}}| <<_{L,epsilon} H^{6-delta+epsilon}.
Thus any remaining H^{6+o(1)} endpoint obstruction in this normalized coefficient box is confined to the near-maximal range
H^{3-delta}<m<=2ceil(LH^3).
The statement gives no saving for that remaining range after summing its individual m-strata.
d90ec957015b32b5.proof:
The defining clauses are exactly the normalized-unit conditions of fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb with q=2m and the coefficient box added. That fact recovers nonzero integers u,v and the dyadic primes r_1,r_4, with
A=2v r_1, q=2|v|,
b r_4+c r_1=2u r_2,
J=4uv.
Since q=2m, |v|=m. The coefficient and prime windows give
2m H^2<=2m r_1=|A|
 <=|b|r_3+|d|r_2
 <4XH^2.
Hence m<2X, proving emptiness for m>2X.

The second normalized identity gives
2|u|H^2<=2|u|r_2
 <=|b|r_4+|c|r_1
 <4XH^2,
so |u|<2X. For fixed m, the signed-determinant slice coordinate
w=uv=J/4
therefore has at most 4X possible nonzero integer values, because v has one of the two signs and u ranges over the nonzero integers of absolute value below 2X. More directly, regardless of the sign representation, the set of possible products w has cardinality at most 4X.

For each fixed w, fact ab9163da69da1ad4 bounds the number of nonzero coefficient quadruples in the X-box with
ab+cd=2 K, ab-cd=4w
by
4 tau(|K+2w|)tau(|K-2w|).
Every coefficient is nonzero in a normalized unit state by fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb. Also
K+2w=ab and K-2w=cd,
so the two nonzero divisor-function arguments have absolute value at most X^2. The elementary divisor bound, with a portion of epsilon allocated to it, makes the number of coefficient matrices for each w at most H^epsilon. Summing over the at most 4X possible w gives
<<_{L,epsilon}H^epsilon X
coefficient matrices.

For each fixed coefficient matrix, fact 1218e64e51ba3131 bounds the number of ordered prime pairs (r_2,r_3) satisfying all normalized clauses by H^epsilon, uniformly in C,K and Q. Restriction to q=2m only removes pairs. Dividing epsilon between the divisor and fixed-Q estimates proves (1). The weighted version is included in fact 1218e64e51ba3131; fixed polylogarithmic factors may also be absorbed into H^epsilon.

The sets U_m are disjoint because q uniquely determines m=q/2. Summing (1) over at most M_cond positive integers proves (2). Taking M_cond=H^{3-delta} gives the displayed fixed-power estimate. Since all nonempty strata have m<=2X, the complementary range is exactly the stated near-maximal range. The final limitation is a scope statement: summing the pointwise H^{3+epsilon} bound over O(H^3) possible near-maximal m values is compatible with H^{6+epsilon} and supplies no further power saving.

glossary.M_cond: a real upper cutoff for the exact half-conductor m
glossary.U_m: the bounded normalized unit-state family with exact half-conductor m=q/2
glossary.U_{<=M_cond}: the disjoint union of U_m over positive integers m<=M_cond

d92616c2bca6126f.title: GA-GOODW-C-HILBERT-BV: RAY-ENERGY GAIN AND THE EXACT HIGH-ROUGH C-OPERATOR HANDOFF. Adopt one complete Good-W outer row after the genealogy recombination of fact 18c3a93006507edb, a frequency block 1<=F<=x^3, the coordinate functions C_{q,h}(y) of fact 1e357f0a9f079ca2, and the primitive signed rays R=(epsilon,a,b), scaling sets I(R), and multiplicities M(R) of fact 31c1bb8e5ea4b34b. For each fixed A>0 put
d92616c2bca6126f.author: slava chan
d92616c2bca6126f.statement:
GA-GOODW-C-HILBERT-BV: RAY-ENERGY GAIN AND THE EXACT HIGH-ROUGH C-OPERATOR HANDOFF. Adopt one complete Good-W outer row after the genealogy recombination of fact 18c3a93006507edb, a frequency block 1<=F<=x^3, the coordinate functions C_{q,h}(y) of fact 1e357f0a9f079ca2, and the primitive signed rays R=(epsilon,a,b), scaling sets I(R), and multiplicities M(R) of fact 31c1bb8e5ea4b34b. For each fixed A>0 put
Omega_{F,A}=(log x)^{C_1}(1+F/H_P)^{-A},                         (1)
where C_1 is a fixed exponent large enough to absorb the fixed scaled-source derivative costs. Then
sup_y (|C_{q,h}(y)|+|partial_y C_{q,h}(y)|) <<_A Omega_{F,A}    (2)
uniformly on the fixed compact y-support, and
sum_R M(R)^2 << QF log(2QF).                                    (3)

For v in {1,2}, define
I_v(R)={k in I(R):gcd(ak,v)=1}                                  (4)
and
b_{v,R}(y)=mu(a) sum_{k in I_v(R)}mu(k)C_{ak,epsilon kb}(y).     (5)
Let H_ray be the finite Hilbert space l2 of the supported rays and put
b_v(y)=(b_{v,R}(y))_R in H_ray. Then
sup_y (||b_v(y)||_2+||partial_y b_v(y)||_2)
 <<_A Omega_{F,A}(QF log(2QF))^{1/2}.                            (6)
If
T_v(y)=b_v(y) tensor b_v(y)^*                                   (7)
is the rank-one operator on H_ray, then, with ||.||_1 denoting trace norm,
sup_y||T_v(y)||_1+integral_R||partial_y T_v(y)||_1 dy
 <<_A Omega_{F,A}^2 QF log(2QF).                                (8)

Now adopt the exact supported C terminal profile of fact 875cb4f04516b35e in a block D<=d<2D, so n=dv with v in {1,2}, d>1 squarefree, P^-(d)>=Z, dv in the inherited supported set, and D>Q^2. Assume
Z>=2Q.                                                           (9)
For every supported q=ak with Q<=q<2Q,
gcd(q,d)=1, and hence
gcd(q,dv)=1 if and only if gcd(q,v)=1.                            (10)
Consequently the arithmetic-gated flat ray coefficient from fact bab94ab4a0e20bc0 is exactly
B_{dv}^{base}(R)=b_{v,R}(dv/B).                                  (11)

For each v in {1,2} and integer d, define the finite ray operator K_{d,v} as follows. It is zero unless D<=d<2D and the exact C edge n=dv is retained. For every exact retained ordered off-diagonal ray pair (R,R'), put in the reversed matrix slot
(K_{d,v})_{R',R}
 =theta_{d,v}(R,R')K^circ_{m_q(R,R'),C_q(R,R')}(dv),             (12)
where theta_{d,v}(R,R') is the complete inherited hard selector for that ordered pair, and m_q,C_q,K^circ are from facts e9e9563501147a1a and 764588e99974a6d9. All other entries, including diagonal entries, are zero. Thus every squarefreeness, roughness, finite-support, nonresonance, low-d-conductor-complement, conductor-class, numerator-class and terminal condition is retained inside K_{d,v}. Define
L_v=max_{D<=t<2D} ||sum_{D<=d<=t}K_{d,v}||_{op}.                (13)
The complete C-anatomy restriction C-qSRC_C of the centered source in fact e9e9563501147a1a has the exact trace form
C-qSRC_C=sum_{v in {1,2}}sum_{D<=d<2D}
 trace(K_{d,v}T_v(dv/B)),                                      (14)
and satisfies
|C-qSRC_C|
 <<_A Omega_{F,A}^2 QF log(2QF)(L_1+L_2).                       (15)
Therefore the operator estimate
L_v<=x^{o(1)} BQF/D for v in {1,2}                              (C-HILBERT-OP-SUP)
would imply
|C-qSRC_C|<=x^{o(1)}Omega_{F,A}^2 BQ^2F^2/D.                    (16)

This theorem proves (2)-(15) and the exact sufficient operator handoff only. It does not compare Omega_{F,A} with any separately chosen literal Fourier scalar omega_F, prove C-HILBERT-OP-SUP, or treat the complementary chamber Z<2Q, the A terminal anatomy, the beta>2+tau principal complement, the D<=Q^2 projected-incidence branch, the complete centered source, a tail payment, or Goldbach.
d92616c2bca6126f.proof:
The proof of fact 1e357f0a9f079ca2 differentiates the literal scaled source once in y and then integrates by parts in the physical variable. Before its final integration in y, the argument gives, uniformly on the fixed compact y-support,
|C_{q,h}(y)| <<_J (log x)^{C_1}(1+F/H_P)^{-J}
and
|partial_y C_{q,h}(y)| <<_J (log x)^{C_1}(1+F/H_P)(1+F/H_P)^{-J}.
Choose J>A+2. This proves (2), after increasing the fixed exponent C_1 if necessary.

We prove (3) by counting proportional physical coordinates. Ignoring the squarefree restriction enlarges the count. Every supported nonzero integer pair (q,h) in
Q<=q<2Q, F<=|h|<2F
has a unique primitive signed ray and a positive scale. Hence sum_R M(R)^2 counts ordered proportional pairs in this rectangle. Fix (q,h), put k=gcd(q,|h|), and write q=ka, |h|=kb. The other positive scale lies in the intersection of two intervals, each of length at most k, so there are at most k+1<=2k choices. Therefore
sum_R M(R)^2
 <=2 sum_{Q<=q<2Q,F<=|h|<2F}gcd(q,|h|).                        (17)
For positive q,h use gcd(q,h)=sum_{r|q,r|h}phi(r). If U=min(2Q,2F), counting multiples of r in both dyadic intervals bounds the positive-h sum by a constant times
QF sum_{r<=U}phi(r)/r^2
 +Q sum_{r<=U}phi(r)/r
 +F sum_{r<=U}phi(r)/r
 +sum_{r<=U}phi(r).                                             (18)
Since phi(r)<=r and U is at most a constant times min(Q,F), these four terms are respectively O(QF log(2QF)), O(QF), O(QF), and O(QF). Include both signs of h. This proves (3).

Equation (2), the triangle inequality in (5), and |I_v(R)|<=M(R) give
|b_{v,R}(y)|+|partial_y b_{v,R}(y)|
 <<_A M(R)Omega_{F,A}.                                         (19)
Square, sum over R, and use (3), proving (6). The trace norm of b tensor b^* is ||b||_2^2. Also
partial_y T_v=(partial_y b_v) tensor b_v^*
              +b_v tensor (partial_y b_v)^*,
and hence
||partial_y T_v||_1
 <=2||b_v||_2||partial_y b_v||_2.                               (20)
The y-support has bounded length. Equations (6) and (20) prove (8).

In the C profile every prime divisor of d is at least Z. Under (9), every such prime exceeds q because q<2Q<=Z. Hence gcd(q,d)=1. Since n=dv, this proves (10). Substitute q=ak in equation (2) of fact 31c1bb8e5ea4b34b. Its gate gcd(ak,dv)=1 becomes the d-independent gate gcd(ak,v)=1, whose scaling set is I_v(R). This proves (11).

Fact e9e9563501147a1a defines the centered source by multiplying the exact retained ordered ray product
B_{dv}^{base}(R)conjugate(B_{dv}^{base}(R'))
by the corresponding centered kernel and selector. The matrix of T_v has entry
(T_v)_{R,R'}=b_{v,R}conjugate(b_{v,R'}).
By (12),
trace(K_{d,v}T_v)
 =sum_{R,R'}(K_{d,v})_{R',R}
  b_{v,R}conjugate(b_{v,R'}),
which is exactly the ordered centered ray-pair sum at n=dv. Fact 875cb4f04516b35e gives squared marker weight one and the exact squarefree rough support on the C edge. Summing d and v proves (14).

For fixed v put A_v(t)=sum_{D<=d<=t}K_{d,v}. Discrete summation by parts in (14), followed by trace duality
|trace(A_v(t)X)|<=||A_v(t)||_{op}||X||_1,                       (21)
bounds the v-part by
L_v( sup_y||T_v(y)||_1
    +sum_{D<=d<2D}||T_v((d+1)v/B)-T_v(dv/B)||_1 ).              (22)
The fundamental theorem of calculus bounds the discrete variation in (22) by
integral_R||partial_y T_v(y)||_1 dy.                            (23)
Insert (8) and sum v=1,2. This proves (15).

Finally, insert C-HILBERT-OP-SUP into (15):
|C-qSRC_C|
 <<_A x^{o(1)}Omega_{F,A}^2 QF log(2QF) BQF/D.
The fixed logarithm is absorbed into x^{o(1)}, giving (16). No comparison with omega_F is used.

glossary.A_v(t): The partial operator sum of K_{d,v} over D<=d<=t.
glossary.C-HILBERT-OP-SUP: The operator partial-sum estimate L_v<=x^{o(1)}BQF/D sufficient for the high-rough C centered payment with envelope Omega_{F,A}.
glossary.C-qSRC_C: The exact C-terminal-anatomy restriction of the large-dilator centered source.
glossary.C_1: A fixed exponent absorbing logarithmic costs of the scaled Good-W source and its first y-derivative.
glossary.H_ray: The finite l2 Hilbert space indexed by supported primitive signed rays in one Good-W outer row.
glossary.I_v(R): The subset of the primitive-ray scaling set satisfying the fixed high-rough C coprimality gate gcd(ak,v)=1.
glossary.K_{d,v}: The complete literal centered C-anatomy ray operator at terminal integer n=dv, with reversed matrix slots for the trace pairing.
glossary.L_v: The maximal operator norm of the partial sums A_v(t).
glossary.Omega_{F,A}: The explicit order-A Good-W Fourier-decay envelope including fixed logarithmic derivative costs.
glossary.T_v(y): The rank-one ray operator b_v(y) tensor b_v(y)^*.
glossary.b_v(y): The H_ray-valued vector of the coefficients b_{v,R}(y).
glossary.b_{v,R}(y): The gate-stable signed scaling coefficient on ray R in the high-rough C chamber.
glossary.theta_{d,v}(R,R'): The complete inherited zero-one hard selector for the exact ordered ray pair (R,R') at n=dv.

d94629b071c82c5f.title: MIXED-VARIATION LOWER BOUND FOR LONG SMOOTH PRODUCT DECOMPOSITIONS. Let H>=2 be an integer and put I_H={1,...,H}. For a complex sequence v on I_H define TV(v)=sum_{n=1}^{H-1}|v(n+1)-v(n)|. For a complex matrix A on I_H times I_H define MV(A)=sum_{m,n=1}^{H-1}|A(m+1,n+1)-A(m+1,n)-A(m,n+1)+A(m,n)|. Put z(n)=(-1)^n and K(m,n)=z(m)z(n). Suppose a finite exact decomposition K(m,n)=sum_{nu in F}rho_nu v_nu(m)w_nu(n) is given. Then
d94629b071c82c5f.author: slava chan
d94629b071c82c5f.statement:
MIXED-VARIATION LOWER BOUND FOR LONG SMOOTH PRODUCT DECOMPOSITIONS. Let H>=2 be an integer and put I_H={1,...,H}. For a complex sequence v on I_H define TV(v)=sum_{n=1}^{H-1}|v(n+1)-v(n)|. For a complex matrix A on I_H times I_H define MV(A)=sum_{m,n=1}^{H-1}|A(m+1,n+1)-A(m+1,n)-A(m,n+1)+A(m,n)|. Put z(n)=(-1)^n and K(m,n)=z(m)z(n). Suppose a finite exact decomposition K(m,n)=sum_{nu in F}rho_nu v_nu(m)w_nu(n) is given. Then
sum_{nu in F}|rho_nu|TV(v_nu)TV(w_nu)>=4(H-1)^2. (1)
In particular, if TV(v_nu),TV(w_nu)<=M for every nu, then
sum_nu|rho_nu|>=4(H-1)^2/M^2. (2)
More specifically, let S,M_0>=1. If v_nu(n)=W_{nu,1}((n-X_{nu,1})/L_{nu,1}) and w_nu(n)=W_{nu,2}((n-X_{nu,2})/L_{nu,2}), where every W_{nu,i} is continuously differentiable, compactly supported in a real interval of length at most S, and satisfies sup_t|W'_{nu,i}(t)|<=M_0, then TV(v_nu),TV(w_nu)<=SM_0. Consequently, if also L_{nu,i}>=p for a real p>=1, then
sum_nu |rho_nu|L_{nu,1}L_{nu,2}>=4p^2(H-1)^2/(S^2M_0^2). (3)
Thus, in a polynomial asymptotic setup with H>=cQ/a for a fixed c>0, p/a>=Q^xi for a fixed xi>0, and SM_0=Q^o(1), the left side of (3) is at least Q^(2+2xi-o(1)). It cannot satisfy a Q^(2+o(1)) coefficient-length ledger. Applied to the proposed use of fact 2775909b4db4ae24, this proves that its long scaled-smooth atomic hypothesis cannot be deduced solely from a pointwise bound on an arbitrary source row: additional source-specific regularity or cancellation is necessary. This is a method no-go only. It does not assert that the literal Vaughan rows of fact 8d3b2d43277f6d33 realize the alternating matrix, and it does not bound their complementary short-row part.
d94629b071c82c5f.proof:
For a matrix A write Delta_1Delta_2 A(m,n)=A(m+1,n+1)-A(m+1,n)-A(m,n+1)+A(m,n). If A(m,n)=v(m)w(n), then Delta_1Delta_2 A(m,n)=(v(m+1)-v(m))(w(n+1)-w(n)). Therefore MV(v tensor w)=TV(v)TV(w). By the exact decomposition and the triangle inequality,
MV(K)<=sum_nu |rho_nu|TV(v_nu)TV(w_nu). (4)
On the other hand z(n+1)-z(n)=-2z(n), so every one-dimensional difference has absolute value 2. Hence TV(z)=2(H-1). Since K=z tensor z, the rank-one identity just proved gives MV(K)=TV(z)^2=4(H-1)^2. Combining this equality with (4) proves (1). If both total variations are at most M, the right side of (1) is at most M^2 sum_nu|rho_nu|, proving (2).
For the scaled-smooth specialization, extend v_nu to the continuously differentiable real function V_nu(x)=W_{nu,1}((x-X_{nu,1})/L_{nu,1}). The fundamental theorem of calculus and disjointness of the intervals [n,n+1] give
TV(v_nu)<=integral_R |V_nu'(x)|dx=integral_R |W'_{nu,1}(t)|dt<=SM_0.
The same proof applies to w_nu. Substitution into (2), followed by L_{nu,1}L_{nu,2}>=p^2 termwise, proves (3). Finally H-1>=cQ/(2a) for all sufficiently large Q, while p>=aQ^xi and SM_0=Q^o(1). Equation (3) is then at least a fixed positive constant times Q^(2+2xi-o(1)), which is incompatible with Q^(2+o(1)). The final scope statements distinguish this abstract obstruction from an assertion about the actual arithmetic rows.

glossary.F: The finite index set of product atoms.
glossary.K: The alternating checkerboard matrix z tensor z.
glossary.L_{nu,i}: The dilation length of the i-th smooth factor in atom nu.
glossary.MV(A): The discrete mixed total variation of the matrix A on I_H times I_H.
glossary.M_0: A common upper bound for the first derivative of every smooth profile.
glossary.S: A common upper bound for the support length of every smooth profile.
glossary.TV(v): The discrete total variation of the sequence v on I_H.
glossary.p: A common lower bound for both dilation lengths.
glossary.rho_nu: The scalar coefficient of the product atom indexed by nu.
glossary.v_nu: The first one-dimensional factor of atom nu.
glossary.w_nu: The second one-dimensional factor of atom nu.
glossary.xi: A fixed positive exponent measuring the ratio p/a.

d97b0142b0d0a486.title: Fix real numbers
d97b0142b0d0a486.author: slava chan
d97b0142b0d0a486.statement:
Fix real numbers
\[
 1/2<\alpha<\beta<1,\qquad \eta>0,\qquad \rho>0,\qquad B_{\rm src}>0.
\]
Let \(W\) and \(\Phi\) be bounded real functions supported respectively in
\([\alpha,\beta]\) and \([1/2,2]\). Let \(N=2x\) be an integer with \(x\ge3\),
put
\[
 T_x=(\log x)^{6+\eta+\rho},
\]
and assume
\[
 {1\over2}x^{1/2}(\log x)^{-B_{\rm src}}\le D\le2x^{1/2},
 \qquad D>2T_x,\qquad U>0.
\]
Let \(\mu\) be the Möbius function, extend \(\Lambda\) by zero on nonpositive
integers, and put
\[
 {\cal I}_D=\{d\ge2:(d,N)=1,\ \mu(d)\ne0,\ d\le x^{1/2},\
 \Phi(d/D)\ne0\}.
\]
For positive integers \(s,m,w\), define
\[
 f_{s,m}(w)=
 {\bf1}_{sw\in{\cal I}_D}\mu(w)\Phi(sw/D)W(smw/x)
 \Phi((N-smw)/U)\Lambda(N-smw),
\]
\[
 F_s(\theta)=\left(\sum_wf_{s,m}(w)e(\theta w)\right)_{m\ge1},
 \qquad e(t)=\exp(2\pi it).
\]
For \(L>0\), put
\[
 P_L(\theta)=\sum_{h\in\mathbb Z}(1-|h|/L)_+e(h\theta).
\]
Define the Fejer residual
\[
 {\cal R}_{<}^{F}=
 \sum_{g<T_x}\sum_{r<T_x}\mu(r)
 \left(\|F_{gr}(0)\|_2^2-
 \int_{\mathbb R/\mathbb Z}P_{D/(grT_x)}(\theta)
 \|F_{gr}(\theta)\|_2^2d\theta\right).                 \tag{1}
\]
The label TB-FEJ-RES means
\[
 {\cal R}_{<}^{F}\ll_{W,\Phi,\alpha,\beta,\eta,\rho}
 xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta}.                                 \tag{2}
\]

For the \(s=1\) row and integers \(m,w,h\), put
\[
 p=N-mw,\qquad p'=N-m(w-h),
\]
and define
\[
\begin{split}
 {\cal W}(m,w,h)=&
 {\bf1}_{w\in{\cal I}_D}{\bf1}_{w-h\in{\cal I}_D}
 \Phi(w/D)\Phi((w-h)/D)W(mw/x)W(m(w-h)/x)\\
 &\times\Phi(p/U)\Phi(p'/U),                            \tag{3}
\end{split}
\]
\[
 {\cal B}_1(h)=
 \sum_{\substack{m,w\ge1\\w-h\ge1}}
 \mu(w)\mu(w-h){\cal W}(m,w,h)\Lambda(p)\Lambda(p').    \tag{4}
\]
Let
\[
 H_0=D(\log x)^{-6-\eta-\rho/2},\qquad H_j=2^jH_0.
\]
Let \(J\) be the least nonnegative integer satisfying
\[
 2^{J+1}H_0\ge3D/2,
\]
and for \(0\le j\le J\) define
\[
 {\cal S}_j=
 \sum_{\substack{H_j<|h|\le2H_j\\|h|\le3D/2-H_0}}
 {\cal B}_1(h).                                         \tag{5}
\]
The label TB-SHIFT-BLOCK means the simultaneous one-sided estimates
\[
 {\cal S}_j\ll_{W,\Phi,\alpha,\beta,\eta,\rho}
 {xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta}\over\log(2T_x)}
 \qquad(0\le j\le J).                                  \tag{6}
\]
Fact ca9ce191fbd75de1 proves that (6) implies (2).

For every positive integer \(n\),
\[
 \Lambda(n)=\sum_{q\mid n}\mu(q)\log(n/q).              \tag{7}
\]
Consequently one expansion gives
\[
\begin{split}
 {\cal B}_1(h)=
 \sum_{\substack{m,w\ge1\\w-h\ge1}}\mu(w)\mu(w-h){\cal W}(m,w,h)
 \sum_{q_1\mid p}\mu(q_1)\log(p/q_1)\Lambda(p'),        \tag{8}
\end{split}
\]
and two expansions give
\[
\begin{split}
 {\cal B}_1(h)=
 \sum_{\substack{m,w\ge1\\w-h\ge1}}\mu(w)\mu(w-h){\cal W}(m,w,h)
 \sum_{\substack{q_1\mid p\\q_2\mid p'}}
 \mu(q_1)\mu(q_2)\log(p/q_1)\log(p'/q_2).               \tag{9}
\end{split}
\]
Every divisor sum in (8)--(9) is restricted implicitly to \(p,p'\ge1\).

On a nonzero term of (8),
\[
 (q_1,w)=1,\qquad m\equiv Nw^{-1}\pmod {q_1}.           \tag{10}
\]
Thus one-modulus completion creates a reciprocal phase modulo \(q_1\), but
the coefficient retains
\[
 \Lambda(N-m(w-h)),\quad\log((N-mw)/q_1),\quad
 {\cal W}(m,w,h).                                       \tag{11}
\]

For a nonzero term of (9), put
\[
 \delta=(q_1,q_2),\qquad q_1=\delta u,\qquad q_2=\delta v.
\]
Then the active integers are squarefree,
\[
 (\delta,u)=(\delta,v)=(u,v)=1,\qquad
 \mu(q_1)\mu(q_2)=\mu(u)\mu(v),                         \tag{12}
\]
and
\[
 (q_1,w)=1,\qquad(q_2,w-h)=1.                          \tag{13}
\]
Put
\[
 e_N=(\delta,N),\qquad\delta_0=\delta/e_N.              \tag{14}
\]
The congruences
\[
 m\equiv Nw^{-1}\pmod {q_1},\qquad
 m\equiv N(w-h)^{-1}\pmod {q_2}                        \tag{15}
\]
are compatible if and only if
\[
 \boxed{\delta_0\mid h}.                                \tag{16}
\]
When compatible, they define one residue \(m_0\) modulo
\[
 L=[q_1,q_2]=\delta uv.                                 \tag{17}
\]
Write \(\overline a^{(q)}\) for the inverse of \(a\) modulo \(q>1\).
Then
\[
\begin{split}
 m_0\equiv&
 N\overline w^{(\delta)}uv\,\overline{uv}^{(\delta)}
 +N\overline w^{(u)}\delta v\,\overline{\delta v}^{(u)}\\
 &+N\overline{w-h}^{(v)}\delta u\,\overline{\delta u}^{(v)}
 \pmod L,                                               \tag{18}
\end{split}
\]
where a summand whose indicated modulus is one is omitted.
For every finitely supported complex sequence \((A_m)\),
\[
 \sum_{m\equiv m_0\ ({\rm mod}\ L)}A_m
 ={1\over L}\sum_{k\ ({\rm mod}\ L)}
 e_L(-km_0)\sum_mA_me_L(km),                            \tag{19}
\]
where \(e_q(t)=\exp(2\pi it/q)\). The CRT phase is
\[
\begin{split}
 e_L(-km_0)=&
 e_\delta\!\left(-kN\overline w^{(\delta)}
                    \overline{uv}^{(\delta)}\right)
 e_u\!\left(-kN\overline w^{(u)}
                    \overline{\delta v}^{(u)}\right)\\
 &\times e_v\!\left(-kN\overline{w-h}^{(v)}
                    \overline{\delta u}^{(v)}\right),   \tag{20}
\end{split}
\]
with modulus-one factors omitted. Hence the completed two-expansion has
the gcd condition \(\delta/(\delta,N)\mid h\), the sign
\[
 \mu(w)\mu(w-h)\mu(u)\mu(v),                            \tag{21}
\]
and correlated inverse variables \(w\) and \(w-h\).

Let
\[
 K_x=\lceil\log_2(2x)\rceil.
\]
For \(0\le j\le J\), \(0\le k_1,k_2\le K_x\), and \(Q_i=2^{k_i}\), define
\[
\begin{split}
 {\cal V}_{j}(Q_1,Q_2)=
 \sum_{\substack{H_j<|h|\le2H_j\\|h|\le3D/2-H_0}}
 \sum_{\substack{m,w\ge1\\w-h\ge1}}
 &\mu(w)\mu(w-h){\cal W}(m,w,h)\\
 {}\times
 \sum_{\substack{q_1\mid p,\ Q_1\le q_1<2Q_1\\
                  q_2\mid p',\ Q_2\le q_2<2Q_2}}
 &\mu(q_1)\mu(q_2)
 \log(p/q_1)\log(p'/q_2).                              \tag{22}
\end{split}
\]
The one-sided estimate
\[
 \boxed{
 {\cal V}_{j}(Q_1,Q_2)
 \ll_{W,\Phi,\alpha,\beta,\eta,\rho}
 {xD(\log x)^{-6-\eta}\over\log(2T_x)}
 }                                                       \tag{TWO-MOD-REFLECTED}
\]
uniformly in all indices of (22), implies TB-SHIFT-BLOCK and therefore
TB-FEJ-RES.

The phase (20) is not a direct specialization of fact
73fb9efe1286f7e9: that fact has one varying modulus and one reciprocal-product
phase with coefficient sequences independent of the modulus. Formula (20)
has the linked strata \(\delta,u,v\), condition \(\delta/(\delta,N)\mid h\),
inverse variables \(w,w-h\), and the joint amplitude (3) with both
logarithms in (22). This is a scoped coefficient-and-range no-direct-fit.
It does not exclude a new theorem for (20), an iterative reciprocal estimate
after a projective coefficient bound, or cancellation before completion.
No estimate in TWO-MOD-REFLECTED is proved here.
d97b0142b0d0a486.proof:
The identity \(\log n=\sum_{d\mid n}\Lambda(d)\) and Möbius inversion give
(7). Substituting (7) into the first von Mangoldt factor of (4) gives (8);
substituting it into both gives (9). The support of \(W\) gives
\[
 (2-\beta)x\le p,p'\le(2-\alpha)x<2x,                  \tag{23}
\]
whenever a term is nonzero.

If a prime \(\ell\) divided both \(q_1\) and \(w\) in (8), then
\(q_1\mid p=N-mw\) would imply \(\ell\mid N\). This contradicts
\(w\in{\cal I}_D\), which gives \((w,N)=1\). Hence \((q_1,w)=1\), and
reducing \(q_1\mid N-mw\) proves (10). The three expressions in (11) are
literal factors in (8), so solving (10) does not separate them.

On a nonzero term of (9), \(\mu(q_1)\mu(q_2)\ne0\), hence \(q_1,q_2\)
are squarefree. Therefore \(\delta,u,v\) are squarefree and pairwise
coprime. Multiplicativity gives
\[
 \mu(q_1)\mu(q_2)=\mu(\delta)^2\mu(u)\mu(v)=\mu(u)\mu(v),
\]
which proves (12). The preceding argument proves \((q_1,w)=1\).
If a prime \(\ell\) divided both \(q_2\) and \(w-h\), then
\(q_2\mid p'=N-m(w-h)\) would imply \(\ell\mid N\), contradicting
\(w-h\in{\cal I}_D\). This proves (13).

The generalized Chinese remainder theorem says that (15) is compatible
exactly when its residues agree modulo \(\delta\). By (13), both \(w\) and
\(w-h\) are units modulo \(\delta\), and
\[
 N\left(w^{-1}-(w-h)^{-1}\right)
 \equiv-Nh\{w(w-h)\}^{-1}\pmod\delta.                  \tag{24}
\]
Thus compatibility is equivalent to \(\delta\mid Nh\). Since \(\delta\)
is squarefree, \(\delta_0=\delta/(\delta,N)\) is coprime to
\(N/(\delta,N)\). Hence \(\delta\mid Nh\) is equivalent to
\(\delta_0\mid h\), proving (16).

Under (16), (15) is equivalent to
\[
 m\equiv Nw^{-1}\pmod\delta,\qquad
 m\equiv Nw^{-1}\pmod u,\qquad
 m\equiv N(w-h)^{-1}\pmod v.                           \tag{25}
\]
The moduli are pairwise coprime, so ordinary CRT gives (17)--(18).
Additive orthogonality modulo \(L\) gives
\[
 {\bf1}_{m\equiv m_0\ ({\rm mod}\ L)}
 ={1\over L}\sum_{k\ ({\rm mod}\ L)}e_L(k(m-m_0)),
\]
which proves (19). Each CRT idempotent in (18) is one in its own modulus
and zero in the other two. Splitting \(e_L(-km_0)\) across these three
idempotents proves (20). Combining the original \(\mu(w)\mu(w-h)\) with
(12) proves (21).

It remains to prove the sufficiency assertion. By (23), each \(q_i\)
satisfies \(1\le q_i<2x\). The half-open intervals
\[
 [2^k,2^{k+1})\qquad(0\le k\le K_x)
\]
partition all possible divisors, with a possible final excess interval
empty. Equations (5), (9), and (22) give
\[
 {\cal S}_j=
 \sum_{k_1=0}^{K_x}\sum_{k_2=0}^{K_x}
 {\cal V}_{j}(2^{k_1},2^{k_2}).                        \tag{26}
\]
There are \((K_x+1)^2\ll(\log x)^2\) summands. Therefore
TWO-MOD-REFLECTED implies
\[
 {\cal S}_j\ll
 {xD(\log x)^{-4-\eta}\over\log(2T_x)}
 \qquad(0\le j\le J),
\]
which is exactly (6). Fact ca9ce191fbd75de1 then implies (2).

Finally, fact 73fb9efe1286f7e9 assumes one varying modulus \(q\), one phase
\(e_q(A_qh(st)^{-1})\), and three coefficient sequences independent of
\(q\). The exact completed phase (20), compatibility condition (16), and
amplitude (22) have the different literal slots stated in the conclusion.
This proves only the scoped no-direct-fit, not the exclusion of any further
decomposition or new estimate.

glossary.TWO-MOD-REFLECTED: the one-sided dyadic estimate for the doubly expanded correlated-modulus middle-shift sum
glossary.cal V_j(Q_1,Q_2): the dyadic two-divisor-modulus component of the s=1 middle-shift block
glossary.cal W(m,w,h): the literal s=1 middle-shift coefficient after removing the two von Mangoldt factors
glossary.delta_0: the quotient delta/(delta,N) governing compatibility with the shift h
glossary.e_N: the common divisor (delta,N) of the two expansion moduli with the fixed center

d9a096ed4e597b2b.title: WEIGHTED FIXED-ACTIVE-PRODUCT BESSEL BOUND FOR THE C4 EXCEPTIONAL TENSOR KERNEL
d9a096ed4e597b2b.author: slava chan
d9a096ed4e597b2b.statement:
WEIGHTED FIXED-ACTIVE-PRODUCT BESSEL BOUND FOR THE C4 EXCEPTIONAL TENSOR KERNEL.

Let r be a squarefree positive integer. Let I and J be finite integer intervals of cardinalities U and V, and assume
gcd(uh,r)=1
for every (u,h) in I times J. For an integer T put
s(r,T)=product over primes p dividing r with p^2 dividing T of p.
On I times J define the nonnegative symmetric kernel
K_r((u,h),(u',h'))=s(r,r(hu'-h'u))/r.

Then every finitely supported complex coefficient array (a_{u,h}) satisfies
|sum_{u,h,u',h'} a_{u,h} conjugate(a_{u',h'}) K_r((u,h),(u',h'))|
 <=(tau(r)UV/r+min(U,V)) sum_{u,h}|a_{u,h}|^2.                 (1)

Suppose additionally that r,B and the interval endpoints are bounded by a fixed power of Q,
U<=C B/r,   V<=r                                                   (2)
for a fixed C. Then, for every epsilon>0,
|sum_{u,h,u',h'} a_{u,h} conjugate(a_{u',h'}) K_r((u,h),(u',h'))|
 <<_{C,epsilon} Q^epsilon (B/r) sum_{u,h}|a_{u,h}|^2.          (3)

In the same-target C4 tensor setting of fact df97bf1eba0495be, write n=ru and n'=ru'. On one signed natural frequency interval, every nonempty active product r has all of its prime factors at least Z, while the frequency length is O(F) with F<Z for sufficiently large Q. Thus (3) applies to the positive majorant s(r,hn'-h'n)/r for every fixed active r, including arbitrary complex row weights and every zero-one restriction of the literal C4 row set. A two-sign dyadic block costs only an absolute constant.

This is a fixed-r operator bound. It does not sum varying active products or centered faces, restore inactive-prime coefficients, compare different target coordinates, assemble deletion siblings, prove the full C4 moment, or imply Goldbach.
d9a096ed4e597b2b.proof: Because r is squarefree, s(r,r(hu'-h'u))=gcd(r,hu'-h'u). (4) Indeed, for p dividing r, the condition p^2|r(hu'-h'u) is equivalent to p|hu'-h'u. Fix one row (u,h) in I times J. The elementary gcd identity gives gcd(r,hu'-h'u)=sum_{t|r, t|hu'-h'u} phi(t). (5) For a fixed divisor t of r, let N_t(u,h) be the number of pairs (u',h') in I times J satisfying hu'=h'u modulo t. (6) The hypotheses make both h and u units modulo t. For each fixed h', equation (6) specifies one residue class for u' modulo t, so N_t(u,h)<=V(U/t+1). For each fixed u', it specifies one residue class for h' modulo t, so N_t(u,h)<=U(V/t+1). Taking the smaller of these two bounds yields N_t(u,h)<=UV/t+min(U,V). (7) Insert (5)-(7) and divide by r. Using sum_{t|r}phi(t)=r, sum_{t|r}phi(t)/t<=tau(r), we obtain the uniform row-sum estimate sum_{u',h'}K_r((u,h),(u',h')) <=tau(r)UV/r+min(U,V). (8) The kernel is symmetric, so the identical estimate holds for every column sum. Applying Schur's test to the matrix with entries K_r, and first replacing the coefficient product by its absolute value, proves (1). Under (2), fact e705401df9f0709e supplies tau(r)<=Z with Z/F tending to infinity; hence V

glossary.I: The integer interval containing the marked cofactors u.
glossary.J: The integer interval containing one signed natural frequency block h.
glossary.K_r: The nonnegative fixed-active-product majorant kernel s(r,r(hu'-h'u))/r on cofactor-frequency rows.

d9c3f37492846fce.title: EXACT COPRIME-INCIDENCE GRAM-FIBRE COMPLETION TO A SQUARE-ROOT KLOOSTERMAN SUM
d9c3f37492846fce.author: slava chan
d9c3f37492846fce.statement:
EXACT COPRIME-INCIDENCE GRAM-FIBRE COMPLETION TO A SQUARE-ROOT KLOOSTERMAN SUM.

Let p be a prime, let d be a positive squarefree integer with (p,d)=1, let f be an integer with (f,p)=1, and let C be an integer with (C,d)=1. Put
 e_q(y)=exp(2pi i y/q)
and define
 S(m,n;d)=sum_{z modulo d;(z,d)=1}e_d(mz+nz^(-1)),          (1)
with S(m,n;1)=1. For every integer t define
 T_{p,d;f,C}(t)
 =sum_{substack{x modulo pd;(x,pd)=1\x congruent f modulo p}}
   e_d(Cx^(-1))e_{pd}(tx).                                  (2)
Let d_bar be the inverse of d modulo p and p_bar the inverse of p modulo d, with the evident convention when d=1. Then exactly
 T_{p,d;f,C}(t)
 =e_p(t f d_bar)S(t p_bar,C;d).                             (3)
Uniformly in every displayed parameter and every epsilon>0,
 |T_{p,d;f,C}(t)|<<_epsilon d^(1/2+epsilon).                 (4)

Let W be a fixed compactly supported infinitely differentiable complex function on the real line. For X real and L>0 put
 W_{X,L}(x)=W((x-X)/L).
Then
 sum_{substack{x in Z;(x,pd)=1\x congruent f modulo p}}
 W_{X,L}(x)e_d(Cx^(-1))
 <<_{W,epsilon}d^(1/2+epsilon){1+L/(pd)}.                   (5)
The estimate is uniform in X and L.

For a surviving additive denominator d in fact 55c6f91ec7fd414f, put k=s_1/d and n=au_1. Since pM_1 is congruent to N modulo s_1, its row-one phase satisfies exactly
 e_d(M_1[n(s_1/d)]^(-1))
 =e_d(N[pkn]^(-1)).                                        (6)
On the Gram face A=D, fixing every variable except u_1 gives
 u_1 congruent u_2q_2s_1^(-1) modulo p.                     (7)
Thus after fixing a and extracting any separated smooth factor in the remaining u_1-slot, equations (5)--(7) give a square-root-d completion which retains the congruence A=D exactly. This is a complete one-slot interface only: it does not estimate the unsplit Vaughan divisor coefficient or its aggregation over the other variables.

No estimate for the full residual array of fact 55c6f91ec7fd414f, K_inc^rem, K_inc^main, another incidence cell, C_small or Goldbach is asserted.
d9c3f37492846fce.proof:
We first prove (3). CRT gives, for every integer y,
 e_{pd}(y)=e_p(y d_bar)e_d(y p_bar).                        (8)
In (2), write
 e_d(Cx^(-1))=e_{pd}(pCx^(-1)).
Apply (8) to y=tx+pCx^(-1). On the fixed p-coordinate x=f, the p-factor is
 e_p(t f d_bar).
On the d-coordinate, x ranges bijectively over all units modulo d and the factor is
 e_d(t p_bar x+Cx^(-1)).
The latter complete sum is S(t p_bar,C;d), proving (3).

For a prime r|d, CRT factorization of (1) expresses S(t p_bar,C;d) as a product of local sums of the form
 sum_{z modulo r;z nonzero}e_r(A_r z+B_r z^(-1)),
where B_r is nonzero because (C,d)=1. If A_r is nonzero, fact 4f9aec67f5be35db bounds this local sum by 2sqrt(r). If A_r=0, inversion permutes the nonzero residues and the local sum is -1, also bounded by 2sqrt(r). Hence
 |S(t p_bar,C;d)|<=2^omega(d)sqrt(d)<<_epsilon d^(1/2+epsilon).
This proves (4), including d=1.

We prove (5) by finite Fourier completion. Put c=pd and periodize
 F(y)=sum_{x congruent y modulo c}W_{X,L}(x).
With
 F_hat(t)=sum_{y modulo c}F(y)e_c(-ty)
         =sum_{x in Z}W_{X,L}(x)e_c(-tx),
finite Fourier inversion and (2) give
 sum_{substack{x in Z;(x,c)=1\x congruent f modulo p}}
 W_{X,L}(x)e_d(Cx^(-1))
 =c^(-1)sum_{t modulo c}F_hat(t)T_{p,d;f,C}(t).             (9)
Let
 W_hat(xi)=integral_R W(v)e(-xi v)dv.
Poisson summation gives
 F_hat(t)
 =L sum_{j in Z}e(-X(j+t/c))W_hat(L(j+t/c))
up to a unit complex phase depending only on the chosen representatives; only its modulus is used. As t runs over a complete residue system modulo c and j runs over Z, the numbers cj+t run over all integers. Rapid decay of W_hat therefore gives
 sum_{t modulo c}|F_hat(t)|
 <=L sum_{r in Z}|W_hat(Lr/c)|
 <<_W L+c.                                                  (10)
Insert (4) and (10) in (9) to obtain (5).

For (6), reduce the congruence pM_1=N modulo s_1 first modulo d. Since d|s_1 and p is coprime to s_1,
 M_1=Np^(-1) modulo d.
Also s_1=dk. Therefore
 M_1[n(s_1/d)]^(-1)
 =N[pnk]^(-1) modulo d,
which proves (6). In the literal notation of fact 55c6f91ec7fd414f, the Gram condition is
 u_1s_1 congruent u_2q_2 modulo p.
All displayed factors are units modulo p, so solving for u_1 gives (7). The phase (6) is of the form in (5), after absorbing the fixed unit factors pka into C. This proves the stated one-slot application and all scope restrictions.

glossary.S(m,n;d): the classical Kloosterman sum over units modulo d
glossary.T_{p,d;f,C}(t): the complete inverse trace modulo pd restricted to one unit residue f modulo p
glossary.W_{X,L}: the translated and rescaled smooth weight W((x-X)/L)

d9eb8f470bce53ac.title: Let p and ℓ be distinct primes, let q=pℓ, and define S(q)=Σ_{r k=q} μ(r) log k, where the sum is over positive integers r,k. Then S(q)=0, while the four summands indexed by r=1,p,ℓ,pℓ are respectively log(pℓ), -log ℓ, -log p, 0. Consequently, a summand or a proper subset of the divisor siblings in the expansion Σ_{r k=q} μ(r)log k cannot, by divisor support alone, be identified with nonzero von-Mangoldt mass at q. Moreover, if p>ℓ^3 and Q=(pℓ)^(1/2), then every divisor r of q lies outside the interval [Q^(1/2),Q^(3/2)]: r=1 and r=ℓ are below Q^(1/2), whereas r=p and r=q are above Q^(3/2). Thus a purely combinatorial assertion that every divisor path for such a q must meet any subinterval of [Q^(1/2),Q^(3/2)], in particular [Q^(4/3),Q^(3/2)], is false. These conclusions do not rule out endpoint localization proved by analytic cancellation after sibling recombination, or by a separate sign-preserving source-to-packet theorem
d9eb8f470bce53ac.author: slava chan
d9eb8f470bce53ac.statement: Let p and ℓ be distinct primes, let q=pℓ, and define S(q)=Σ_{r k=q} μ(r) log k, where the sum is over positive integers r,k. Then S(q)=0, while the four summands indexed by r=1,p,ℓ,pℓ are respectively log(pℓ), -log ℓ, -log p, 0. Consequently, a summand or a proper subset of the divisor siblings in the expansion Σ_{r k=q} μ(r)log k cannot, by divisor support alone, be identified with nonzero von-Mangoldt mass at q. Moreover, if p>ℓ^3 and Q=(pℓ)^(1/2), then every divisor r of q lies outside the interval [Q^(1/2),Q^(3/2)]: r=1 and r=ℓ are below Q^(1/2), whereas r=p and r=q are above Q^(3/2). Thus a purely combinatorial assertion that every divisor path for such a q must meet any subinterval of [Q^(1/2),Q^(3/2)], in particular [Q^(4/3),Q^(3/2)], is false. These conclusions do not rule out endpoint localization proved by analytic cancellation after sibling recombination, or by a separate sign-preserving source-to-packet theorem.
d9eb8f470bce53ac.proof:
Because p and ℓ are distinct primes, the positive divisors of q=pℓ are 1,p,ℓ,pℓ. For a factorization rk=q, k is determined by r. The Möbius values are μ(1)=1, μ(p)=μ(ℓ)=-1, and μ(pℓ)=1. Therefore the four values μ(r)log(q/r) are log(pℓ), -log ℓ, -log p, and log 1=0. Their sum is log(pℓ)-log ℓ-log p=0. Since log(pℓ), log ℓ, and log p are positive, three isolated siblings are nonzero even though the complete sum is zero. Hence nonzero size of an isolated sibling is not, without recombination or another theorem, nonzero size of the complete reflected coefficient.

Assume additionally p>ℓ^3 and set Q=(pℓ)^(1/2). Since Q^(1/2)=(pℓ)^(1/4), the inequality ℓ<Q^(1/2) is equivalent after taking fourth powers to ℓ^4<pℓ, which is equivalent to ℓ^3<p. Thus 1<ℓ<Q^(1/2). Since Q^(3/2)=(pℓ)^(3/4), the inequality p>Q^(3/2) is equivalent after taking fourth powers to p^4>p^3ℓ^3, which is again equivalent to p>ℓ^3. Finally q=pℓ=Q^2>Q^(3/2) because Q>1. Hence all four possible r-values lie outside [Q^(1/2),Q^(3/2)]. The last sentence of the statement only records the logical scope: the example contradicts an inference based solely on divisor support or on an unrecombined proper subset, but it makes no assertion about conclusions that use additional analytic estimates or a separately proved transfer.

glossary.S(q): the complete divisor convolution Σ_{rk=q} μ(r)log k

da22464a2f614042.title: FORWARD LITERAL-C3 SOURCE-TO-TRACE THEOREM WITH EXACT OUTER-g COLLISION PAYMENT
da22464a2f614042.author: slava chan
da22464a2f614042.statement:
FORWARD LITERAL-C3 SOURCE-TO-TRACE THEOREM WITH EXACT OUTER-g COLLISION PAYMENT.

Fix constants C,c_0,C_0,c_1,C_1>=1 and 0<kappa<=1/100. Put sigma=kappa/100 and beta_1=6/5-3sigma. Let x>=3, c_0x<=N<=C_0x, and let D,M,R,K satisfy R>D, c_1^(-1)x<=DM,RK<=C_1x, D<=Cx^(1/2), R<=Cx, and R/D>x^(23/400). Fix g|N and put Q=D/g>1, B=R/g=Q^beta, G=M/Q, H_T=B/Q, H_P=B/M, L_src=N/g, L=H_TQ^sigma, S_0=H_T^2Q^(3sigma), Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma), with 1<=beta<=beta_1.

Let W be fixed scaled-smooth on a compact four-variable box. Define
F_{g,a,b}(t)=log(t)log((L_src-at)/b)W(ga/D,t/M,gb/R,(L_src-at)/(bK))
and its Fourier transform Fhat. Let T_fwd,C3(g) be the sum over h>0, a comparable to Q, squarefree v<=S_0 with all prime factors at most L, and distinct ordered primes Z<=p_1<p_2<p_3, where b=vp_1p_2p_3 is comparable to B, gcd(a,b)=1, ga and gb are squarefree, of
2mu(a)(-mu(v))Re[b^(-1)Fhat_{g,a,b}(h/b)e_b(L_src h a^(-1))].
Use complete dyadic prime cells and their exact equal-cell pair/triple inclusion-exclusion; impose no further joint deletion.

Then T_fwd,C3(g) equals a polylogarithmic-norm combination of complete traces from fact 73b711f7dea1a0ee with target -L_src, plus outer-g/rough-prime collision correction strata of total size
O(Q^(19/10-2sigma)).
Consequently there are fixed delta_1,delta_2>0 such that
|T_fwd,C3(g)|<<GQ^(2-delta_1) for G>=1,
and
|T_fwd,C3(g)|<<Q^(2-delta_2)
for Q^(-sigma+eta)<=G<=Q^(sigma-eta), 0<eta<sigma.
The result includes H_P<1, all frequencies, nonunit target, all prime order/equal cells, repeated-prime bookkeeping, and the exact p_i|g collision coordinate. It asserts no hard deletion, reverse, later beta, actual-Z, endpoint, PMD, DCE, bad-N, or Goldbach conclusion.
da22464a2f614042.proof:
A nonempty source has squarefree g. The conditions ga and gb squarefree are equivalent to (g,a)=1, (g,v)=1, and p_i not dividing g for all i, in addition to squarefreeness of a,v and distinctness. The first condition is absorbed into the arbitrary bounded modulus coefficient of fact 73b711f7dea1a0ee, and the second into its divisor-bounded xi_v. We will complete the three prime-slot exclusions and pay their corrections.

The C3 marker coefficient is -mu(v) by facts 6414b11506a84ff0 and 73b711f7dea1a0ee: the latter verifies through beta_1 all cutoff hypotheses of the former. Reciprocity gives
e_b(L_src h a^(-1))=e_a(-L_src h b^(-1))e(L_src h/(ab)).             (1)
On F<=h<2F put u_F=F/H_P and rescale t=Ms. Then
b^(-1)Fhat(h/b)
=H_P^(-1)(B/b)integral log(Ms)log((L_src-aMs)/b)
 W(ga/D,s,gb/R,(L_src-aMs)/(bK))e(-hMs/b)ds.                         (2)
The retained archimedean phase from (1), and the Fourier phase in (2), have logarithmic derivative size O(u_F), since |L_src|/(QM)=N/(DM)=O(1). Repeated integration by parts in s and in a torus extension of the logarithmic variables gives projective Fourier l1 norm
O((log x)^2(1+u_F)^(-J_0))                                          (3)
for arbitrary fixed J_0. Equal prime cells satisfy the exact symmetric identities one half times full-minus-pair-diagonal, and one sixth times full-minus-three-pairs-plus-twice-triple. Thus, after prime-slot completion, every mode and repeated-prime bookkeeping term is covered by fact 73b711f7dea1a0ee.

We now restore p_i not dividing g. On each completed ordered cell insert
product_{i=1}^3(1-1_{p_i|g})
and expand it. The term 1 is the complete trace. There are seven nonempty correction types. In each, at least one prime p>=Z is fixed to a prime divisor of g. For each fixed such p, the number of remaining multiplicative tuples (v and the other prime slots), with their product on scale B/p, is O(Q^epsilon B/p) by divisor counting. For every fixed a,b, repeated integration by parts in the defining Fourier integral gives
sum_{h>0}b^(-1)|Fhat_{g,a,b}(h/b)|<< (log x)^2.                       (4)
There are O(Q) choices of a. Hence all corrections containing the fixed p have absolute total
O(Q^(1+epsilon)B/p).
Summing p|g with p>=Z costs at most O(x^epsilon/Z). Corrections with two or three fixed g-primes, overlaps with pair/triple equalities, and ordered-cell restrictions are no larger because absolute deletion only reduces the tuple count. Therefore every outer-g collision correction together is
O(Q^(1+epsilon)B/Z)
=O(Q^(2beta-1/2+3sigma+epsilon))
=O(Q^(19/10-3sigma+epsilon)),                                      (5)
which is O(Q^(19/10-2sigma)) after choosing epsilon<sigma and using Q>=x^(23/80) to absorb divisor and polylogarithmic factors.

The completed terms satisfy fact 73b711f7dea1a0ee. Its target condition holds because Q>x^(23/80) and |L_src|<=C_0x<=Q^4 for large x. Apply its two estimates and add (5). Since (5) has a fixed saving from Q^2 and G>=1 in the first regime, both asserted bounds follow. Equations (3)-(5) also cover H_P<1 and every exact equality/collision stratum.

glossary.T_fwd,C3(g): The complete forward exact-g C3 paired-Poisson sum with source squarefreeness retained.

da23b28ec48ad852.title: Let p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4 be distinct primes greater than 3, put P=p_1p_2p_3p_4, and use the centered interval-weighted companion definitions C_q, E_q and Gamma from fact be4e5ad5378f0122. For every finite companion index set Q and every family of cyclic intervals I_{i,q} in Z/p_iZ, choose epsilon_{i,q} in {0,1}, and define J_{i,q}=I_{i,q} if epsilon_{i,q}=0 and J_{i,q}=(Z/p_iZ)\I_{i,q} if epsilon_{i,q}=1. Put s_q=(-1)^{sum_{i=1}^4 epsilon_{i,q}} and let D be the diagonal matrix on C^Q with diagonal entries s_q. If C_q^I,E_q^I,Gamma^I and C_q^J,E_q^J,Gamma^J denote the companion data for the I-family and J-family respectively, then C_q^J=s_q C_q^I, E_q^J=E_q^I, and Gamma^J=D Gamma^I D on the positive-energy indices. Consequently ||Gamma^J-I||_op=||Gamma^I-I||_op
da23b28ec48ad852.author: slava chan
da23b28ec48ad852.statement:
Let p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4 be distinct primes greater than 3, put P=p_1p_2p_3p_4, and use the centered interval-weighted companion definitions C_q, E_q and Gamma from fact be4e5ad5378f0122. For every finite companion index set Q and every family of cyclic intervals I_{i,q} in Z/p_iZ, choose epsilon_{i,q} in {0,1}, and define J_{i,q}=I_{i,q} if epsilon_{i,q}=0 and J_{i,q}=(Z/p_iZ)\I_{i,q} if epsilon_{i,q}=1. Put s_q=(-1)^{sum_{i=1}^4 epsilon_{i,q}} and let D be the diagonal matrix on C^Q with diagonal entries s_q. If C_q^I,E_q^I,Gamma^I and C_q^J,E_q^J,Gamma^J denote the companion data for the I-family and J-family respectively, then C_q^J=s_q C_q^I, E_q^J=E_q^I, and Gamma^J=D Gamma^I D on the positive-energy indices. Consequently ||Gamma^J-I||_op=||Gamma^I-I||_op.

In particular, for every such P there are explicit cyclic intervals J_{i,2},J_{i,3}, all of cardinality p_i-1, for which the normalized two-column Gram satisfies
||Gamma^J-I||_op=sqrt((phi(P)+1)/(2phi(P)))>1/sqrt(2).
Thus lower bounds on the local interval lengths or densities alone, even local densities 1-1/p_i tending to one as the primes tend to infinity, do not imply an o(1) companion-flatness estimate. A valid literal theorem must use further restrictions, such as upper density bounds, location relations, or arithmetic dependence on q. This is a dense-window companion countermodel, not an arithmetic PAVG27 counterexample and not a counterexample to a fully specified WF-RPS window family.
da23b28ec48ad852.proof:
For a subset I of Z/pZ, its centered indicator is f_I=1_I-|I|/p. Since 1_{I^c}=1-1_I and |I^c|=p-|I|, one has
f_{I^c}=1-1_I-(p-|I|)/p=-1_I+|I|/p=-f_I.                    (1)
Therefore replacing I_{i,q} by its complement multiplies its centered local Fourier transform by -1, while leaving it unchanged if no complement is taken. In the product of the four local Fourier multipliers from fact be4e5ad5378f0122, the total multiplier for the q-th column is consequently multiplied by
s_q=product_{i=1}^4(-1)^{epsilon_{i,q}}=(-1)^{sum_i epsilon_{i,q}}.
The flat companion factor V_{P,q} is not changed. Hence C_q^J=s_q C_q^I. Since |s_q|=1, the energy E_q=sum_h|C_q(h)|^2 is unchanged. In the standard Gram convention of fact be4e5ad5378f0122,
Gamma^J_{q,q'}=sum_h overline(C_q^J(h))C_{q'}^J(h)/sqrt(E_q^JE_{q'}^J)=s_qs_{q'}Gamma^I_{q,q'}.
This is the matrix identity Gamma^J=D Gamma^I D. Because D is unitary, self-adjoint, and D^2=I, one has
Gamma^J-I=D(Gamma^I-I)D,
which proves equality of the operator norms.

Now take the explicit singleton cyclic intervals I_{i,2},I_{i,3} constructed in fact edb218d77d83d52a. Complement every one of the four local intervals for q=2 and q=3. The complement of a singleton in the cyclic order on Z/p_iZ is a cyclic interval of cardinality p_i-1. For each q all four coordinates were complemented, so s_q=(-1)^4=1. Thus C_q^J=C_q^I for q=2,3, and the verified norm formula from fact edb218d77d83d52a gives
||Gamma^J-I||_op=sqrt((phi(P)+1)/(2phi(P)))>1/sqrt(2).
The local densities are (p_i-1)/p_i=1-1/p_i, which tend to one along any choice of four distinct primes tending to infinity. This proves the stated limitation and all scope qualifications.

glossary.D: the diagonal sign matrix with diagonal entries s_q
glossary.Gamma^I: the normalized companion Gram for the original interval family
glossary.Gamma^J: the normalized companion Gram for the complemented interval family
glossary.I_{i,q}: an original local cyclic interval at prime coordinate i and companion index q
glossary.J_{i,q}: either I_{i,q} or its cyclic complement, according to epsilon_{i,q}
glossary.dense-window companion countermodel: the complemented-singleton companion family with every local interval of length p_i-1
glossary.epsilon_{i,q}: the zero-one choice indicating whether I_{i,q} is complemented
glossary.s_q: the sign accumulated in the q-th fourfold multiplier under local complementation

da9b97f255e8bc97.title: FULL LARGE-EFFECTIVE-MODULUS DIVISOR-WINDOW DICHOTOMY IN THE LITERAL STRICT-TOP C1 GEOMETRY. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100 and put sigma=kappa/100. Let beta satisfy beta_m<=beta<6/5 in the strict-top C1 setting of facts f0f6807663d3ef3c and 79ffbcb2ffe4049f. Thus n=pv is squarefree, p is the unique rough prime of the C1 copy, gcd(p,v)=1, and every prime divisor of v is at most
da9b97f255e8bc97.author: slava chan
da9b97f255e8bc97.statement:
FULL LARGE-EFFECTIVE-MODULUS DIVISOR-WINDOW DICHOTOMY IN THE LITERAL STRICT-TOP C1 GEOMETRY. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100 and put sigma=kappa/100. Let beta satisfy beta_m<=beta<6/5 in the strict-top C1 setting of facts f0f6807663d3ef3c and 79ffbcb2ffe4049f. Thus n=pv is squarefree, p is the unique rough prime of the C1 copy, gcd(p,v)=1, and every prime divisor of v is at most
L=Q^(beta-1+sigma).
Let C=mathscr A h and
m_eff=n/gcd(C,n).
Assume
Q^(1/2+kappa)<=m_eff<=Q^(6/5).
Put lambda=1/40.

Then the following classification is exact.

(i) If p divides C, then m_eff has a divisor m_1 satisfying
m_eff^lambda<=m_1<=m_eff^(1/2-lambda).

(ii) If p does not divide C, then p divides m_eff. Put r_eff=m_eff/p. Then r_eff is a squarefree divisor of v. The modulus m_eff has a divisor m_1 in the same window if and only if
r_eff>=m_eff^lambda.

Consequently, among the literal C1 effective moduli in the displayed range, the moduli having no divisor in the factorable effective-modulus window with lambda=1/40 are exactly
m_eff=p r_eff,  p does not divide C,  r_eff<m_eff^(1/40).
They are ultra-near-prime effective moduli and include the prime case r_eff=1. There is no additional factor-gap class made solely from the smooth cofactor v. This is a structural classification only; it does not estimate the reciprocal sum on the ultra-near-prime class.
da9b97f255e8bc97.proof:
Fact 7c1f38cfbb8d0569 gives the literal squarefree factorization n=pv, and fact f0f6807663d3ef3c gives
L=Q^(beta-1+sigma)
with beta<6/5 and sigma<=1/10000. Hence, for sufficiently large Q,
L<Q^(2001/10000).                                               (1)
The lower bound on m_eff gives
m_eff^(1/2-2lambda)=m_eff^(9/20)
 >=Q^((1/2+kappa)9/20)>Q^(9/40).                               (2)
Since 2001/10000<9/40, equations (1)-(2) imply
L<m_eff^(1/2-2lambda).                                          (3)

We first prove a deterministic smooth-divisor statement. Let s be a squarefree divisor of v satisfying s>=m_eff^lambda. Order the prime divisors of s in any fixed way and multiply them successively until their product first becomes at least m_eff^lambda. Let d be the product at that stopping time. The product before the last prime is smaller than m_eff^lambda, and the last prime is at most L. Therefore
m_eff^lambda<=d<m_eff^lambda L
 <m_eff^(lambda+1/2-2lambda)
 =m_eff^(1/2-lambda),                                          (4)
where (3) was used. Thus every such s supplies a divisor d in the required window.

Because n is squarefree, m_eff=n/gcd(C,n) is the product of exactly those prime divisors of n which do not divide C. If p divides C, then p is absent from m_eff, so m_eff divides v. Also m_eff>=Q^(1/2+kappa)>m_eff^lambda. Apply (4) with s=m_eff. This proves (i).

Suppose p does not divide C. Then p divides m_eff, and squarefreeness together with gcd(p,v)=1 gives
r_eff=m_eff/p divides v.
If r_eff>=m_eff^lambda, apply (4) with s=r_eff; the resulting d divides r_eff and hence m_eff, proving the forward implication in (ii).

It remains to prove the converse. Assume r_eff<m_eff^lambda, and let d be any divisor of m_eff. If p does not divide d, then d divides r_eff, so
d<=r_eff<m_eff^lambda.                                         (5)
If p divides d, then
d>=p=m_eff/r_eff>m_eff^(1-lambda)>m_eff^(1/2-lambda).           (6)
Thus no divisor d lies in the required window. Equations (5)-(6) also show that this obstruction is exact, including r_eff=1. Combined with (i) and the forward implication of (ii), this exhausts the literal C1 cases and proves every conclusion.

glossary.ultra-near-prime effective modulus: An effective modulus m_eff=p r_eff whose complementary factor satisfies r_eff<m_eff^(1/40).

db067f4633c13fed.title: ACTUAL-SOURCE PHASE COLLAPSE, DIVISOR-SELECTED PRIME ROW, AND NORMAL-CARRY REFINEMENT OF THE FINITE-BAND MODULAR ALIAS
db067f4633c13fed.author: slava chan
db067f4633c13fed.statement:
ACTUAL-SOURCE PHASE COLLAPSE, DIVISOR-SELECTED PRIME ROW, AND NORMAL-CARRY REFINEMENT OF THE FINITE-BAND MODULAR ALIAS.

Fix Q>=2 and real numbers H,V,P satisfying
  2<=H<=Q^(1/3),  2<=V<H,  P=QH/V.
Let p be a prime in [P,2P), let v be an integer in [V,2V), and assume gcd(v,p)=1. Let A be an integer. For i=1,2,3,4 choose integers q_i,m_i in [Q,2Q) and k_i in Z such that
  q_i m_i+vp k_i=A,  gcd(q_i m_i,vp)=1.                    (1)
Choose h_i in one common interval contained either in [H,2H) or in (-2H,-H], and assume
  h_1+h_2=h_3+h_4.                                         (2)
Put epsilon_1=epsilon_2=1 and epsilon_3=epsilon_4=-1, and define
  R_h=sum_{i=1}^4 epsilon_i h_i m_i,                        (3)
  Delta_h=h_1q_2q_3q_4+h_2q_1q_3q_4
          -h_3q_1q_2q_4-h_4q_1q_2q_3.                     (4)
For every modulus r write e_r(t)=exp(2 pi i t/r), and let bars denote inverses in the displayed modulus. For each i let s_i be the unique integer in [0,v) satisfying
  h_i+p s_i congruent 0 modulo v.                           (5)

Then the following statements hold.

(i) One has gcd(A,vp)=1 and, for every integer h,
  e_{q_i}(Ah(vp)bar)=e_{q_i}(hk_i).                         (6)
Thus the complete quartic reciprocal phase on four actual-source atoms is
  product_{i=1}^4 e_{q_i}(epsilon_i Ah_i(vp)bar)
  =product_{i=1}^4 e_{q_i}(epsilon_i h_i k_i).              (7)

(ii) The exact congruence
  A Delta_h congruent (q_1q_2q_3q_4)R_h modulo p            (8)
holds. Consequently
  p divides A Delta_h  if and only if  p divides R_h.       (9)
In particular, on the MOD sector of fact ddcb0baef17b6ab0, defined by Delta_h nonzero and p dividing A Delta_h, the integer
  j=R_h/p                                                    (10)
is well defined and satisfies
  |j|<6V,                                                    (11)
  j congruent -sum_{i=1}^4 epsilon_i s_i m_i modulo v.      (12)
For fixed v,s_i,m_i the congruence (12) and the bound (11) leave at most thirteen possible integers j.

(iii) The source restoration makes the common prime a divisor-selected coefficient exactly. More precisely, fix v,q_i,m_i with v dividing A-q_i m_i for every i, put
  D_i=(A-q_i m_i)/v,                                       (13)
let cal P be any finite set of primes not dividing v, let K_i be arbitrary subsets of Z, let chi(p) be any complex prime mask, and let F be any complex function of (p,k_1,k_2,k_3,k_4). Then
  sum_{p in cal P} chi(p)
    sum_{k_i in K_i for all i}
      F(p,k_1,k_2,k_3,k_4) product_i 1_{D_i=pk_i}
  =
  sum_{p in cal P} chi(p) product_i[1_{p divides D_i}1_{D_i/p in K_i}]
      F(p,D_1/p,D_2/p,D_3/p,D_4/p).                        (14)
Here p divides 0 for every prime p, as usual. Therefore all literal p-dependent masks may be retained in chi and F, but after source restoration p is constrained jointly by the four divisor equations D_i=pk_i, while the modular-alias condition adds the bounded carry (10)-(12).

This is an exact source-interface refinement of fact ddcb0baef17b6ab0. It proves no cancellation in the divisor-selected prime row, does not replace finite-band coefficients by arbitrary scalar rows, and makes no PMD or Goldbach conclusion.
db067f4633c13fed.proof:
From (1), A is congruent to q_i m_i modulo vp. Since gcd(q_i m_i,vp)=1, this residue is a unit modulo vp, so gcd(A,vp)=1. Also A is congruent to vpk_i modulo q_i. Because gcd(q_i,vp)=1, multiplication by the inverse of vp modulo q_i gives
  A(vp)bar congruent k_i modulo q_i.
Multiplication by h and application of e_{q_i} prove (6); multiplying with signs epsilon_i proves (7).

Let Q_4=q_1q_2q_3q_4. Definition (4) says exactly
  Delta_h=Q_4 sum_i epsilon_i h_i/q_i
as a rational identity whose right side is integral. Reducing modulo p and using A congruent to q_i m_i modulo p gives
  A Delta_h
  congruent sum_i epsilon_i h_i A(Q_4/q_i)
  congruent sum_i epsilon_i h_i q_i m_i(Q_4/q_i)
  =Q_4 R_h modulo p.
Every q_i is a unit modulo p by (1), and A is a unit modulo p by the first paragraph. Hence (8) implies the equivalence (9).

On the MOD sector, (9) makes j in (10) an integer. Equation (2) gives h_4=h_1+h_2-h_3, so
  R_h=h_1(m_1-m_4)+h_2(m_2-m_4)-h_3(m_3-m_4).
Each |h_i| is less than 2H and each |m_i-m_4| is less than Q. Therefore |R_h|<6HQ. Since p>=P=QH/V, division by p proves (11).

By (5), h_i is congruent to -ps_i modulo v. Thus
  R_h congruent -p sum_i epsilon_i s_i m_i modulo v.
On the MOD sector R_h=pj. Since p is a unit modulo v, cancellation of p proves (12). An interval of length less than 12V contains at most
  floor(12V/v)+1<=13
integers in one residue class modulo v, proving the stated multiplicity.

Finally, for fixed p and i, the equation D_i=pk_i has exactly one integer solution k_i=D_i/p if p divides D_i, and no integer solution otherwise. This remains true for D_i=0, when the unique solution is k_i=0. Requiring k_i in K_i gives the two indicators on the right side of (14). Taking the product over i and then summing p proves (14). The scope statement follows because no absolute or oscillatory estimate has been applied.

glossary.D_i: The source difference (A-q_i m_i)/v attached to atom i.
glossary.F: An arbitrary complex function of the common prime and four source frequencies in the exact reindexing.
