glossary.K_i: An arbitrary allowed set of source-frequency values k_i.
glossary.R_h: The signed source-weighted height sum sum_i epsilon_i h_i m_i.
glossary.cal P: An arbitrary finite set of primes in the exact divisor-selected reindexing.
glossary.chi: An arbitrary complex mask on primes in the exact reindexing.
glossary.epsilon_i: The quartic sign: epsilon_1=epsilon_2=1 and epsilon_3=epsilon_4=-1.
glossary.j: The bounded integer normal carry R_h/p on the modular-alias sector.

db2c993b4e4fe611.title: COLLAPSE OF EVEN-AND-CORNER EXCEPTIONS INTO THE K-NONUNIT LAYER
db2c993b4e4fe611.author: slava chan
db2c993b4e4fe611.statement:
COLLAPSE OF EVEN-AND-CORNER EXCEPTIONS INTO THE K-NONUNIT LAYER.

Let H>=2 and let
 (a,b,c,d,r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4,u,v)
be a normalized unit state of type (I) in fact 6e7f7bb2682c39eb, with associated integer K and
 A=b r_3-d r_2,quad B=a r_2-c r_3,quad
 q=gcd(|A|,|B|),quad m=q/2=|v|.                                  (1)
Then:

(a) If m is even, K is even. In particular gcd(m,K)>=2.

(b) If gcd(m,r_2r_3)>1, then gcd(m,K)>1. More precisely, if r_2 divides m, then r_2 divides b,c,K; if r_3 divides m, then r_3 divides a,d,K.

Consequently
 gcd(m,K)=1                                                       (2)
implies simultaneously that m is odd and gcd(m,r_2r_3)=1. For m>1, condition (2) is therefore equivalent, within normalized unit states, to the complete arithmetic unit-conductor hypothesis
 m is odd and gcd(m,K r_2r_3)=1                                   (3)
used by the generic torus and shared-lift core.

In the five-sector partition of fact 9dc06d0e888914a5, E_corner is empty, and E_even is contained arithmetically in the K-nonunit locus. Thus, apart from m=1 and scale/interval restrictions, every normalized state outside the generic odd-unit core has gcd(m,K)>1. This is a coverage simplification only; it supplies no estimate for that K-nonunit layer.
db2c993b4e4fe611.proof:
All four coefficients a,b,c,d are even by the definition of a normalized unit state. Hence ab and cd are divisible by four. Since
 ab+cd=2K,
the integer 2K is divisible by four, so K is even. If m is even, both m and K are divisible by two, proving (a).

Suppose r_2 divides m. Since q=2m, r_2 divides q. The definition of q implies q divides both A and B, hence r_2 divides both A and B. Reducing
 A=b r_3-d r_2
modulo r_2 gives b r_3 congruent to zero. The primes r_2 and r_3 are distinct, so r_3 is a unit modulo r_2 and r_2 divides b. Reducing
 B=a r_2-c r_3
modulo r_2 similarly gives r_2 divides c. Therefore r_2 divides
 ab+cd=2K.
The prime r_2 is odd, so r_2 divides K.

If r_3 divides m, the same argument with reduction modulo r_3 gives r_3 divides d from A and r_3 divides a from B. Hence r_3 divides ab+cd=2K and, being odd, divides K. This proves every assertion in (b).

If gcd(m,K)=1, part (a) forbids even m, and part (b) forbids a common factor of m with r_2r_3. This proves (2) implies (3); the reverse implication is immediate. Fact 9dc06d0e888914a5 defines E_corner by gcd(m,K)=1 together with gcd(m,r_2r_3)>1, which is impossible by (b). Its E_even states all have gcd(m,K)>1 by (a). The final scope statement follows.

db54beb65db1bb72.title: Assume the finite labelled-incidence set, its six parent cells, and the nonzero original real incidence weights w(z) from fact 91db48815d136d4c. Let Y be a set of parent-cell labels such that I_Y, the union of the corresponding incidence cells, is nonempty. Assign to every incidence z an arbitrary integer q_z>1, and write varphi(q_z) for the number of unit residue classes modulo q_z. For every real R_amp>0 there are auxiliary primitive-moment data satisfying fact 676c6a2cb3ebf7cc for which, simultaneously in every parent cell X,
db54beb65db1bb72.author: slava chan
db54beb65db1bb72.statement:
Assume the finite labelled-incidence set, its six parent cells, and the nonzero original real incidence weights w(z) from fact 91db48815d136d4c. Let Y be a set of parent-cell labels such that I_Y, the union of the corresponding incidence cells, is nonempty. Assign to every incidence z an arbitrary integer q_z>1, and write varphi(q_z) for the number of unit residue classes modulo q_z. For every real R_amp>0 there are auxiliary primitive-moment data satisfying fact 676c6a2cb3ebf7cc for which, simultaneously in every parent cell X,
T_X=sum_{z in Z_X}w(z),
although the assigned conductors q_z are arbitrary. Explicitly, take J_z={0}, z_{z,0}=R_amp, x_{z,0}=0, and a_z=w(z)/(varphi(q_z)R_amp^4). Then for every divisor e of q_z and every residue v modulo e,
F_{z,e}(v)=R_amp,
C_z(e)=eR_amp^4,
S_z=R_amp,
widetilde C_z(e)=(e-1)R_amp^4,
and
P_z(q_z)=varphi(q_z)R_amp^4.
Consequently a_zP_z(q_z)=w(z) incidence by incidence, and the centered quotient-conductor identity remains exact.

These same data give an exact leaf reconstruction of T_Y in the sense of fact 4a9a213a428b7e8c by taking one leaf lambda_z for each z in I_Y, singleton modulus and sample sets, H_{lambda_z}=1, c_{lambda_z}=a_z, gamma=b=1, and X_{lambda_z}=P_z(q_z). For this reconstruction the first-stage coefficient norm A_R and coordinate norm M_R are
A_R^2=R_amp^(-8) sum_{z in I_Y}|w(z)|^2/varphi(q_z)^2,
M_R=R_amp^8 sum_{z in I_Y}varphi(q_z)^2.
Both sums on the right are positive. Hence A_R tends to zero and M_R tends to infinity as R_amp tends to infinity, while the opposite occurs as R_amp tends to zero. Their product
A_R M_R^(1/2)=((sum_{z in I_Y}|w(z)|^2/varphi(q_z)^2)(sum_{z in I_Y}varphi(q_z)^2))^(1/2)
is independent of R_amp.

Thus, under the current abstract moment and leaf hypotheses, exact equality with the original source sum and retention of arbitrary declared conductor labels do not normalize the separate Hilbert factors A_R and M_R. In particular, an arbitrarily small standalone first-stage coefficient norm can be manufactured by gauge rescaling without supplying arithmetic cancellation or a physical WF-RPS packet map. This is a formal interface countermodel, not an arithmetic counterexample to a future transform whose Fourier coefficients, phases, conductors, and provenance coefficients are fixed explicitly by the original incidence.
db54beb65db1bb72.proof:
Fix z. Since J_z has one element, its Fourier coefficient is R_amp and its phase label is zero, the exponential factor is one for every modulus and residue. Thus F_{z,e}(v)=R_amp. There are e residues modulo e, so C_z(e)=eR_amp^4. Also S_z=R_amp, giving widetilde C_z(e)=(e-1)R_amp^4. There are exactly varphi(q_z) unit residues modulo q_z, so P_z(q_z)=varphi(q_z)R_amp^4. The chosen provenance coefficient therefore satisfies a_zP_z(q_z)=w(z). Summing this incidencewise equality over any parent cell proves T_X=sum_{z in Z_X}w(z).

For completeness, the centered conductor recombination can also be checked directly. Since q_z>1, sum_{e|q_z}mu(q_z/e)=0, while the standard divisor identity sum_{e|q_z}mu(q_z/e)e=varphi(q_z) holds. Therefore
sum_{e|q_z}mu(q_z/e)widetilde C_z(e)
=R_amp^4 sum_{e|q_z}mu(q_z/e)(e-1)
=varphi(q_z)R_amp^4
=P_z(q_z),
which is also the instance of fact 676c6a2cb3ebf7cc.

Now use the stated one-leaf-per-incidence specialization of fact 4a9a213a428b7e8c. Every inner singleton sum is X_{lambda_z}=P_z(q_z), and its outer coefficient is c_{lambda_z}=a_z, so the leaf sum is sum_{z in I_Y}a_zP_z(q_z)=sum_{z in I_Y}w(z)=T_Y. The coefficient-norm definition in that fact gives A_R^2=sum_{z in I_Y}|a_z|^2, which is the displayed R_amp^(-8) formula. Its coordinate-norm definition gives M_R=sum_{z in I_Y}|P_z(q_z)|^2, which is the displayed R_amp^8 formula. Every w(z) is nonzero by the definition of the incidence set, q_z>1 gives varphi(q_z)>0, and I_Y is nonempty, so both unscaled sums are positive. The limiting statements and the R_amp-independent product follow by taking square roots and multiplying. This proves all claims and the stated formal scope.

glossary.A_R: the first-stage coefficient norm of the gauge-rescaled leaf reconstruction
glossary.I_Y: the nonempty union of the labelled-incidence parent cells selected by Y
glossary.M_R: the coordinate norm of the gauge-rescaled leaf reconstruction
glossary.R_amp: a positive real gauge amplitude used in the singleton Fourier construction
glossary.varphi(q_z): the number of unit residue classes modulo the integer q_z

dbe03cbcb7136c4c.title: ACTUAL CRT-PRESERVING CENTERED PMD TRANSFORM AND OUTER-GCD-INVARIANT INCIDENCE
dbe03cbcb7136c4c.author: slava chan
dbe03cbcb7136c4c.statement:
ACTUAL CRT-PRESERVING CENTERED PMD TRANSFORM AND OUTER-GCD-INVARIANT INCIDENCE.

Let p be a prime, let v,q_1,q_2 be positive integers with gcd(p,v)=1 and gcd(vp,q_1q_2)=1, let A be an integer, and let H>0. Put n=vp. Write e_n(t)=exp(2 pi i t/n), and let bars denote inverses modulo n. Let Phi be smooth with support contained in [-2,-1] union [1,2], and define Phihat(y)=integral_R Phi(t)exp(-2 pi iyt)dt. For
  F(r)=A(q_2-q_1)-r q_1q_2,                                  (1)
one has the exact full-CRT Poisson identity

sum_{h in Z}Phi(h/H)e_n(Ah(q_1bar-q_2bar))
 =H sum_{r in Z}Phihat(-Hr/(vp))
       1_{v|F(r)}1_{p|F(r)}.                                 (2)

If p>2H, then the kernel has exact zero mass on the v-congruence selected by the source:

sum_{r in Z}Phihat(-Hr/(vp))1_{v|F(r)}=0.                    (3)

Consequently the actual source has the exactly p-centered form

sum_{h in Z}Phi(h/H)e_{vp}(Ah(q_1bar-q_2bar))
 =H sum_{r in Z}Phihat(-Hr/(vp))1_{v|F(r)}
       [1_{p|F(r)}-1/p].                                     (4)

Thus retaining the small-v CRT phase changes the literal coefficient from the model mask v|r to the coupled mask v|F(r), but it creates no v-centered remainder. The subtraction 1/p is exact conditionally on v|F(r), because the original h=0 mode is excluded by Phi(0)=0.

There is also an exact outer-gcd-invariant form. Let g,N,d_1,d_2 be positive integers, assume g divides N and d_i=gq_i, put A=N/g, and assume gcd(g,vp)=1. Then

vp|A(q_2-q_1)-r q_1q_2
if and only if
vp|N(d_2-d_1)-r d_1d_2.                                    (5)

In particular both the v-mask and the centered p-incidence in (4) may be written using the physical divisors d_1,d_2 and target N, with no g in the polynomial. If H=vp/M for a positive real M, then the Fourier kernel in (4) is Phihat(-r/M), so its natural r-length is M, independently of g,v,p. No estimate for the centered sum in (4) and no separation theorem for its coupled v-mask are asserted.
dbe03cbcb7136c4c.proof:
Put B=A(q_1bar-q_2bar) modulo n=vp. Poisson summation, with the Fourier convention in the statement, gives

sum_hPhi(h/H)e_n(Bh)
 =H sum_{ell in Z, ell congruent -B mod n}Phihat(Hell/n).     (6)

Set r=-ell. Since
  B congruent A(q_2-q_1)(q_1q_2)bar modulo n,
the condition ell congruent -B modulo n is equivalent to
  n|A(q_2-q_1)-rq_1q_2.
Because gcd(v,p)=1, this is exactly the conjunction v|F(r) and p|F(r). The Fourier weight becomes Phihat(-Hr/(vp)), proving (2).

Because q_1q_2 is a unit modulo v, the condition v|F(r) selects one residue class
  r congruent c=A(q_2-q_1)(q_1q_2)bar modulo v.              (7)
Write r=c+vk. Poisson summation on this progression gives

sum_{r:v|F(r)}Phihat(-Hr/(vp))
 =sum_{k in Z}Phihat(-H(c+vk)/(vp))
 =(p/H)sum_{m in Z}Phi(mp/H)e_v(-mc),                        (8)
up to the immaterial sign convention in the final unit phase. If m=0, the summand is Phi(0)=0. If m is nonzero, then |mp/H|>=p/H>2, outside the support of Phi. Hence every term on the right of (8) vanishes, proving (3). Multiplying (3) by 1/p and subtracting it from (2) proves (4). This is conditional centering on the exact small-v residue class, so no separate term involving 1_{v|F}-1/v appears.

For (5), direct substitution gives

g^2[A(q_2-q_1)-rq_1q_2]
 =N(d_2-d_1)-rd_1d_2.                                      (9)
Since gcd(g,vp)=1, multiplication by g^2 is invertible modulo vp. Divisibility by vp, and therefore divisibility separately by v and p, is equivalent on the two sides of (9). Finally H=vp/M changes -Hr/(vp) to -r/M exactly. This proves every assertion.

glossary.coupled small-v mask: The literal condition v divides A(q_2-q_1)-r q_1q_2 which remains as a coefficient of the centered prime incidence.
glossary.full-CRT PMD transform: Poisson summation with the complete one-rough modulus vp retained, before discarding the small-v phase.
glossary.outer-gcd-invariant incidence: The physical polynomial N(d_2-d_1)-r d_1d_2 obtained after multiplying the normalized incidence by g^2.

dbfaad4be3d523a8.title: ACTUAL C1,C2,C3,C4 SAME-RESIDUE ALL-FOUR JOINT-(h,n/p) ENERGY WITH NO HEIGHT-l1 TAX
dbfaad4be3d523a8.author: slava chan
dbfaad4be3d523a8.statement:
ACTUAL C1,C2,C3,C4 SAME-RESIDUE ALL-FOUR JOINT-(h,n/p) ENERGY WITH NO HEIGHT-l1 TAX.

Adopt the top-sliver first-nonresonant-prime setting of fact ec8a0fbdab03cda6, restricted to a C1,C2,C3, or C4 marker row. Fix a selected prime p, one signed dyadic height interval I_H, and one natural dyadic cofactor interval
T<=t<2T,qquad t=n/p,                                           (1)
contained in the exact integer cofactor range J_p. Assume
2H<p,qquad 2T<p,qquad H,T>=p^delta                            (2)
for a fixed 0<delta<1. If I_H is positive, write h^*=h; if I_H is negative, write h^*=-h, so H<=h^*<2H.

For each nonzero residue x modulo p and every supported pair (h^*,t), let
A_{p,x}(h^*,t)
be the sum of the absolute values of all scalar literal C1,C2,C3,C4 marker-copy coefficients having n=pt and physical q in [Q,2Q) with q congruent to x modulo p. Every literal source mask and every tuple deletion may be retained before this absolute domination.

For every fixed A>=2 and epsilon_0>0,
A_{p,x}(h^*,t)
 <<_{A,epsilon_0} Q^epsilon_0(1+Q/p)
 (1+h^*/H_P)^(-A).                                             (3)
The bound is uniform in p,x,t and in the anatomy.

Fix x. Let O_{p,x} be any scalar source-weighted suboccupancy of the actual all-four same-residue balance
h_1^*/t_1+h_2^*/t_2=h_3^*/t_3+h_4^*/t_4 mod p,                (4)
where all four physical q_i are congruent to x modulo p, all four physical heights lie in the same signed interval I_H, and the quadruple weight is at most
product_{i=1}^4 A_{p,x}(h_i^*,t_i).
Then, for every
0<eta<min(1,4delta),
O_{p,x}
 <<_{A,delta,eta,epsilon_0}
 Q^(4epsilon_0)(1+Q/p)^4
 (1+H/H_P)^(-4A)
 (HT)^4p^(-eta).                                               (5)

Let X_p be the set of nonzero residues modulo p represented by an integer q in [Q,2Q). Then
#X_p<=min(p-1,Q+1),                                             (6)
and therefore
sum_{x in X_p}O_{p,x}
 <<_{A,delta,eta,epsilon_0}
 Q^(4epsilon_0)min(p,Q+1)(1+Q/p)^4
 (1+H/H_P)^(-4A)
 (HT)^4p^(-eta).                                               (7)
Thus the actual scalar source-copy and physical-q multiplicities fit the separated nonnegative coefficient slot of fact 9ea2dddfbbbd191a on the C1-C4 all-four same-residue stratum, with no sum over the H heights.

This theorem does not cover mixed physical-height-sign sectors, zero local heights when p<=2H, the three two-block repeated-pole partitions, Top B, any common-X completion of unequal q-residues, any remaining-face vector norm, or comparison with the complete literal joint-completion Hilbert norm. It proves no complete first-prime occupancy, top trace estimate, or Goldbach conclusion.
dbfaad4be3d523a8.proof:
Fact 3286b0e75a3ea94a proves that every one exact C1,C2,C3,C4 marker-copy coefficient at height h has modulus at most C_{A,epsilon_0}Q^epsilon_0(1+|h|/H_P)^(-A). (8) Fact 41b56ed8e64bdba6 proves that the number of exact marker and convolution copies over one fixed marked integer n is bounded by one fixed divisor function. After decreasing epsilon_0 inside (8) if necessary, summing all copies with n=pt costs at most another factor Q^epsilon_0. For fixed p and x, the congruence q=x mod p and the interval Q<=q<2Q contain at most 1+Q/p integers, up to an absolute enlargement accounting for endpoints. Summing (8) over those physical q and the divisor-bounded marker copies proves (3). Literal source and tuple masks only delete summands before absolute values and cannot enlarge the bound. On either signed interval, h^*=|h| lies in [H,2H). Fact 3286b0e75a3ea94a proves that w_h=(1+h/H_P)^(-A),qquad H<=h<2H, is nonnegative and satisfies sup_h w_h+Var(w)<=2sup_h w_h <=2(1+H/H_P)^(-A). (9) Put b_t=C_{A,epsilon_0}Q^epsilon_0(1+Q/p). Then (3) gives A_{p,x}(h,t)<=w_hb_t after enlarging the constant. The same-sign restriction preserves the (+,+,-,-) balance. For positive physical heights, (4) is unchanged. For negative physical heights, replacing h_i by h_i^*=-h_i multiplies both sides of the original balance by -1 and again gives (4). All hypotheses of fact 9ea2dddfbbbd191a now hold for the fixed residue x: equation (2) supplies 2H,2T

=p^delta; equation (9) supplies the nonnegative bounded-variation numerator weight; and b_t is a nonnegative bounded denominator weight. Equation (6) of that fact gives O_{p,x}<

glossary.A_{p,x}(h,t): The scalar l1 mass of all literal C1-C4 marker-copy coefficients at a fixed selected prime, physical q-residue, height, and natural cofactor.
glossary.O_{p,x}: A masked actual scalar all-four same-q-residue occupancy at fixed selected prime.
glossary.X_p: The nonzero residue classes modulo p represented by the physical q interval.

dbfdaaf10709eca0.title: AUX-COPRIME-MU-BV: CONVOLUTION REMOVAL OF A SQUAREFREE AUXILIARY COPRIMALITY CONDITION IN THE DEEP-SUBHALF RANGE. Let x be sufficiently large, let B>=x^eta for a fixed eta>0, and let c be a squarefree positive integer with c<=x^C0 for a fixed C0. Define
dbfdaaf10709eca0.author: slava chan
dbfdaaf10709eca0.statement:
AUX-COPRIME-MU-BV: CONVOLUTION REMOVAL OF A SQUAREFREE AUXILIARY COPRIMALITY CONDITION IN THE DEEP-SUBHALF RANGE. Let x be sufficiently large, let B>=x^eta for a fixed eta>0, and let c be a squarefree positive integer with c<=x^C0 for a fixed C0. Define
f_c(n)=mu(n)1_{(n,c)=1}.                                       (1)
Let Q>=1, and let cal Q be a set of squarefree q in a fixed-ratio interval q asymptotic to Q with (q,c)=1. For every q in cal Q let V_q be a continuously differentiable complex weight supported on a fixed-ratio interval n asymptotic to B and satisfying, for one fixed C_V,
sup_y|V_q(By)|+integral_R|d/dy V_q(By)|dy
 +sup_y|d/dy V_q(By)| <=(log x)^(C_V).                          (2)
The weights may depend arbitrarily on q subject to (2).

For every prescribed A_0>0 there is C_aux=C_aux(A_0,eta,C0,C_V)>0 such that, if
Q<=sqrt(B)/(log B)^(C_aux),                                     (3)
then
sum_{q in cal Q} max_{(a,q)=1}
 |sum_{n congruent a (mod q)}f_c(n)V_q(n)
  -phi(q)^(-1)sum_{(n,q)=1}f_c(n)V_q(n)|
 <<_{A_0} tau(c)^2 B(log x)^(-A_0).                            (4)
All sums are over positive integers in the support of V_q. The bound has no c^epsilon, Q^epsilon or x^epsilon factor.

More precisely, define
a_c(h)=1 if every prime divisor of h divides c, and a_c(h)=0 otherwise. Then
f_c=mu*a_c                                                       (5)
exactly, and, because (q,c)=1, the discrepancy in (4) is exactly
sum_{h>=1}a_c(h)
 [sum_{m congruent ah^(-1) (mod q)}mu(m)V_q(hm)
  -phi(q)^(-1)sum_{(m,q)=1}mu(m)V_q(hm)].                       (6)
For H=(log B)^D with D sufficiently large in terms of A_0 and C_V, the part h<=H is paid by ordinary Mobius Bombieri-Vinogradov at lengths B/h, and the part h>H is paid elementarily. The exact coefficient bounds are
sum_h a_c(h)/h=product_{p|c}(1-1/p)^(-1)<=(1+log c)^2,          (7)
A_c(1/2):=sum_h a_c(h)h^(-1/2)
 =product_{p|c}(1-p^(-1/2))^(-1)<=tau(c)^2.                    (8)

There is also a no-epsilon outer aggregation rule. If N is a positive integer and active pairs g,c satisfy gc|N, (g,c)=1 and mu^2(gc)=1, then
sum_{g,c active}{tau(c)^2over gc}
 <=product_{p|N}(1+5/p)
 <=(1+log N)^5.                                                 (9)
Thus the tau(c)^2 loss in (4) becomes only a fixed logarithmic tax in the exact g,c aggregation. No assertion outside (3), no Poisson-zero estimate, no critical-tail payment and no Goldbach conclusion is made.
dbfdaaf10709eca0.proof:
For Re(s)>1, the Dirichlet series of f_c has Euler factors
1-p^(-s) for p not dividing c and 1 for p dividing c. Hence
sum_n f_c(n)n^(-s)
 ={1over zeta(s)}product_{p|c}(1-p^(-s))^(-1).                  (10)
The second factor is the Dirichlet series of a_c, because each p|c may occur to any nonnegative exponent and no other prime may occur. Comparing absolutely convergent Dirichlet coefficients proves (5).

Since every prime divisor of h in the support of a_c divides c, (q,c)=1 implies (h,q)=1. Substitute n=hm in both terms of the left side of (4), use (5), and invert h modulo q. The principal condition (hm,q)=1 is equivalent to (m,q)=1. This proves the exact identity (6), including all coefficients and signs.

We establish the coefficient bounds. At s=1,
sum_h a_c(h)/h=product_{p|c}(1-1/p)^(-1).
For squarefree c, the elementary harmonic-product argument used in fact efcd2b6b9fb60a05 gives this at most (1+log c)^2, proving (7). At s=1/2,
A_c(1/2)=product_{p|c}(1-p^(-1/2))^(-1).
For every p>=2, (1-p^(-1/2))^(-1)<4. Since tau(c)=2^(omega(c)) for squarefree c, the product is at most 4^(omega(c))=tau(c)^2, proving (8). Consequently,
sum_{h>H}a_c(h)/h<=H^(-1/2)tau(c)^2,                            (11)
and for every fixed support constant C_1,
sum_{h<=C_1B}a_c(h)
 <=(C_1B)^(1/2)A_c(1/2)
 <<sqrt(B)tau(c)^2.                                             (12)

We now estimate (6). Choose D first, sufficiently large in terms of A_0,C_V and all fixed logarithmic taxes, and put H=(log B)^D. For h<=H, the m-weight
V_{q,h}(m)=V_q(hm)
is supported at length X_h asymptotic to B/h. Under the scaling m=(B/h)y,
V_{q,h}((B/h)y)=V_q(By),                                       (13)
so (2) gives exactly the same supremum, variation and scaled-Lipschitz bounds, uniformly in h.

Use the classical Mobius Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem in Xuancheng Shao, arXiv:1607.01814v2, Introduction, unnumbered Theorem (Bombieri-Vinogradov), specifically the immediately following sentence saying the displayed exceptional-modulus theorem also holds for mu. For every A_1, it supplies a logarithmic exponent B_S(A_1). Choose A_1 after D large enough to absorb A_0,C_V,D and every fixed tax. Then choose C_aux>B_S(A_1)+D/2 plus a fixed support margin. For h<=H, (3) implies
Q<=sqrt(B/h)/(log(B/h))^(B_S(A_1))                              (14)
uniformly. The good/exceptional modulus argument and direct Abel summation in fact c1c141e3d7fb562f apply verbatim at length B/h and to the q-dependent weights (13). They give
sum_{q in cal Q}max_{(a,q)=1}
 |sum_{m congruent a (mod q)}mu(m)V_q(hm)
  -phi(q)^(-1)sum_{(m,q)=1}mu(m)V_q(hm)|
 <<_{A_1}{Bover h}(log x)^(-A_1+C_V+4).                       (15)
The centering difference between Shao's unrestricted mean and the reduced mean displayed here is paid by fact 71389b22e6f49e13, exactly as in fact c1c141e3d7fb562f. Summing (15) over h<=H and using (7) proves that the short-h part is
<<B(log x)^(-A_0-10),                                           (16)
after the chosen exponent hierarchy.

For h>H, no cancellation is used. The support of V_q(hm) forces h<=C_1B. For one h and q, the progression in m contains
O(B/(hq)+1)
integers, while the reduced principal sum contains O(B/h+1) integers. Using (2), summing q asymptotic to Q, and using the squarefree bound
sum_{q in cal Q}1/phi(q)<< (1+log(2Q))^3,                       (17)
the absolute contribution for fixed h is
<<(log x)^(C_V+3){B/h+Q+1}.                                    (18)
Sum (18) over h>H. Equations (11)-(12) give
<<tau(c)^2(log x)^(C_V+3)
 {B H^(-1/2)+Q sqrt(B)+sqrt(B)}.                                (19)
Choose D so the first term is at most tau(c)^2B(log x)^(-A_0-2). Choose C_aux still larger if needed; (3) makes the second term at most the same size. Finally B>=x^eta makes the third term smaller than tau(c)^2B times every fixed negative log power. Thus (19) is
<<tau(c)^2B(log x)^(-A_0),                                      (20)
which, together with (16), proves (4).

For (9), squarefreeness and (g,c)=1 let each p|N occur in neither variable, in g with weight 1/p, or in c with weight tau(p)^2/p=4/p. Therefore the full active-pair sum is bounded by product_{p|N}(1+5/p). Expanding the product gives
product_{p|N}(1+5/p)
 <=sum_{d<=N}tau_5(d)/d
 <=(1+log N)^5,                                                 (21)
where tau_5(d)=sum_{d_1d_2d_3d_4d_5=d}1 and the last inequality follows by bounding each of the five harmonic sums. This proves (9) and completes the proof.

glossary.A_c(1/2): The half-power Dirichlet mass sum_h a_c(h)h^{-1/2}.
glossary.C_aux: A sufficiently large logarithmic depth exponent for the auxiliary-coprime Möbius BV transfer.
glossary.a_c: The multiplicative indicator of positive integers all of whose prime divisors divide c.

dcabcf2f566b5721.title: COMMON-CELL-IMPORTANCE-SAMPLED-IJOP-PUSHFORWARD
dcabcf2f566b5721.author: slava chan
dcabcf2f566b5721.statement:
COMMON-CELL-IMPORTANCE-SAMPLED-IJOP-PUSHFORWARD.

There are absolute constants c_0,C_0>0 with the following property. Let H be a sufficiently large integer, let r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4 be ordered pairwise distinct primes in [H^2,2H^2), and put P=r_1r_2r_3r_4. Consider integer quadruples (c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4) satisfying
7H/8<=c_2<=H,  -H<=c_3<=-7H/8,  c_2 not congruent to c_3 modulo 2,
0<|c_1|<=H/16,  0<|c_4|<=H.
Define
B=c_1r_2+c_2r_1,  D=c_3r_4+c_4r_3,
C=Br_3r_4+r_1r_2D,  v=c_2r_3-c_3r_2.
Let mathcal E be the set of these quadruples for which
gcd(v,BD)=1 and |C|>=H^7/4,
and put N_E=|mathcal E|. Then
N_E>=c_0 H^4/(log(2H))^2.                                      (1)
Consequently
omega=phi(P)/(H^4N_E)
satisfies
0<omega<=C_0(log(2H))^2.                                      (2)

Fix one paired-selector-supported full four-prime Ramanujan face occurring in the carrier routing of fact 707345f56faff29e, and denote by A_prov its complete labelled provenance coefficient, including every already-retained source label and phase but excluding the auxiliary primitive-residue variable. Assume only, as is true for the reopened full-face coefficient, that A_prov is independent of that auxiliary residue. If U_P is the unit group modulo P and alpha=phi(P)/P is the full-face fraction of fact 7bcf6f85c0df5948, then
H^(-4) sum_{rho in U_P} A_prov
 =omega sum_{mathbf c in mathcal E} A_prov,                     (3)
alpha A_prov
 =(H^4/P)omega sum_{mathbf c in mathcal E} A_prov.              (4)
Thus (4) is an exact importance-sampled reopening of one actual full face, not an estimate.

Every sampled quadruple has the following explicit pushforward to the positive generic fixed-fibre chart of fact d4402b645abcaf56. Define
E=c_2r_4+c_4r_2,  F=c_1r_3+c_3r_1,
m=v,  u=c_1r_4-c_4r_1,
a=-2D,  b=2B,  c=-2E,  d=2F,
n_1=-d,  n_2=b,  K=(ab+cd)/2,  s=1.                            (5)
Let u_0 be the representative of u modulo m in {0,...,m-1} and put
k=2(u-u_0)/m. Then
a n_2=K+2mu_0+km^2,  c n_1=a n_2-2K,                           (6)
lambda_A=(br_3-dr_2)/(2m)=r_1,
lambda_B=(ar_2-cr_3)/(2m)=r_4,
lambda_J=(ab-cd)/(4m)=u,                                      (7)
lambda_J congruent to u_0 modulo m,  k=2(lambda_J-u_0)/m,       (8)
d r_2lambda_B-c r_3lambda_A=2C.                               (9)
Moreover
B>=3H^3/4,  F<=-3H^3/4,  7H^3/4<=m<=4H^3,                     (10)
m is odd, n_1,n_2 are positive even integers, a,c are even,
max(|a|,|c|,n_1,n_2)<=8H^3,
H^7/4<=|C|<=32H^7,  |K|<=64H^6,                               (11)
gcd(m,r_2r_3)=1,  gcd(C,P)=1,  u is nonzero, and
gcd(m,2K)=1.                                                    (12)
The recovered corners in (7) are precisely the fixed distinct primes r_1,r_4.

For fixed absolute choices L_0=64, L_1=12 and A=1, all pushed-forward tuples lie in common coefficient intervals of cardinality at most L_1m and satisfy the geometric hypotheses of d4402b645abcaf56 for sufficiently large H. The importance weight times any displayed zero-one sampling, parity, coprimality, carrier-scale, fixed-prime-cell, and labelled-provenance selectors is independent of the Fourier characters and is O((log(2H))^2), hence lies in the Omega_outer range of that fact, for example with exponent D=3 after increasing the lower threshold for H. Fact 212d1415bf03c2a7 likewise permits these character-independent selectors in the shared-lift gate.

This is only a pointwise common-cell localization and density identity. It asserts no source coefficient projective norm, no estimate after summing varying (m,C,K), no cross-cell or rectangular consumer, no total-deficit capture, and no Goldbach implication.
dcabcf2f566b5721.proof:
The c_2 and c_3 intervals each contain a positive constant times H integers, and a positive constant proportion of their ordered pairs have opposite parity. Fix one of the resulting at least cH^2 pairs. Then
v=c_2r_3+|c_3|r_2
satisfies 7H^3/4<=v<=4H^3. It is odd by the opposite-parity condition. Reduction modulo r_2 and r_3, using 0<c_2,|c_3|<r_2,r_3 and distinctness of the corner primes, gives gcd(v,r_2r_3)=1.

We use an elementary interval sieve. If n>=3, I is an interval of L consecutive integers, and gcd(A,n)=1, inclusion-exclusion gives
#{t in I:gcd(At+B,n)=1}
 =L phi(n)/n+O(2^{omega(n)}).                                  (13)
Indeed, each squarefree divisor e of n contributes L/e+O(1) solutions. If p_1<...<p_j are the distinct prime divisors of n, then p_i>=i+1, whence
n/phi(n)=product_i p_i/(p_i-1)<=product_i(i+1)/i=j+1
 <=1+log_2 n.                                                    (14)
Also n>=product_i(i+1)=(j+1)!, and (j+1)!>=(j/2)^{j/2}; hence j=O(log n/log log(3n)) and 2^j=n^{o(1)}. Uniformly for n<=4H^3, (13)-(14) imply
#{t in I:gcd(At+B,n)=1}>>L/log(2H)                              (15)
for L>=cH and sufficiently large H.

Apply (15) with n=v, A=r_2 and 1<=c_1<=H/16. At least cH/log(2H) choices satisfy gcd(v,B)=1. Fix one. As a function of c_4,
C=C_*+r_1r_2r_3c_4.
Let t_*=-C_*/(r_1r_2r_3). The closed H/4-neighborhoods of the endpoint intervals [-H,-3H/4] and [3H/4,H] are disjoint. At least one endpoint interval therefore stays at distance at least H/4 from t_*. On its integer points,
|C|=r_1r_2r_3|c_4-t_*|>=H^7/4.                                (16)
Since D=c_3r_4+c_4r_3 and gcd(r_3,v)=1, another application of (15) on that interval supplies at least cH/log(2H) choices with gcd(v,D)=1. Thus each fixed pair (c_2,c_3) contributes at least cH^2/(log(2H))^2 eligible tuples, proving (1). Since phi(P)<=P<16H^8, (2) follows.

Fact 7bcf6f85c0df5948 gives on paired-selector support
alpha=phi(P)/P=P^(-1)sum_{rho in U_P}1.
Residue-independence of A_prov and the definition omega N_E=phi(P)/H^4 give (3), and multiplication by H^4/P gives (4). Each sampled tuple labels a primitive residue because
C congruent to c_i(P/r_i) modulo r_i,
which is nonzero. Reduction modulo the four primes recovers every c_i modulo r_i; the allowed intervals have width less than r_i, so the sampled map is injective.

We verify the chart identities by expansion. From (5),
br_3-dr_2=2r_1(c_2r_3-c_3r_2)=2mr_1,
ar_2-cr_3=2r_4(c_2r_3-c_3r_2)=2mr_4.                         (17)
Further expansion gives
br_3r_4-ar_1r_2=dr_2r_4-cr_1r_3=2C,                           (18)
br_4+cr_1=2ur_2,  dr_4+ar_1=2ur_3,                            (19)
and
ab=K+2mu,  cd=K-2mu,  ab-cd=4mu.                              (20)
Equations (17)-(20), followed by writing u=u_0+(u-u_0), prove (6)-(9), including integrality and evenness of k=2(u-u_0)/m.

The box extremes give
B>=-(H/16)(2H^2)+(7H/8)H^2=3H^3/4,
F<=(H/16)(2H^2)-(7H/8)H^2=-3H^3/4.
Thus n_1,n_2 are positive. The definitions bound every one of B,D,E,F by 4H^3, proving the coefficient bounds. Expanding
C=sum_{i=1}^4 c_iP/r_i
gives |C|<=32H^7. The coefficient bounds give |K|<=64H^6.

Modulo r_i only the term c_iP/r_i in C survives, so gcd(C,P)=1. If u=0, then c_1r_4=c_4r_1; distinct primality would force r_1 to divide the nonzero c_1 with |c_1|<r_1, impossible. Hence lambda_J=u is nonzero. The two positive coprime quantities lambda_A=r_1 and lambda_B=r_4 recover the missing corners.

Finally m is odd. If an odd prime p divided m and K, (20) would imply p divides ab=-4BD, contradicting gcd(m,BD)=1. Thus gcd(m,2K)=1. All arithmetic d440 gates now hold.

The common intervals I_a,I_c contained in [-8H^3,8H^3] and positive I_1,I_2 contained in [1,8H^3] have cardinality at most 12m by m>=7H^3/4. Taking L_0=64 gives the coefficient and carrier polynomial bounds, H<=m, and eventually m>4L_1+1. Equation (2) and the zero-one selectors give the claimed character-independent Omega range. This is precisely the selector flexibility allowed by d4402b645abcaf56 and 212d1415bf03c2a7, without any varying-fibre summation.

glossary.A_prov: the complete labelled provenance coefficient of one fixed full Ramanujan face, independent of its auxiliary primitive residue
glossary.B: the sampled first pair coordinate c_1 r_2+c_2 r_1
glossary.C: the sampled integer CRT carrier B r_3 r_4+r_1 r_2 D
glossary.D: the sampled second pair coordinate c_3 r_4+c_4 r_3
glossary.E: the auxiliary linear form c_2 r_4+c_4 r_2
glossary.F: the auxiliary linear form c_1 r_3+c_3 r_1
glossary.N_E: the cardinality of the eligible sampled set mathcal E
glossary.U_P: the multiplicative unit group modulo P
glossary.alpha: the full four-prime Ramanujan-face fraction phi(P)/P
glossary.c_i: the i-th small integer local primitive-residue coordinate
glossary.m: the positive odd sampled IJOP modulus parameter c_2 r_3-c_3 r_2
glossary.omega(n): the number of distinct prime divisors of n
glossary.u_0: the canonical representative of u modulo m in {0,...,m-1}

dd7f18552d39e5d4.title: Fix an integer J≥1. Let Q,L_1,M_1,Z≥1, put B=L_1M_1, and assume
dd7f18552d39e5d4.author: slava chan
dd7f18552d39e5d4.statement:
Fix an integer J≥1. Let Q,L_1,M_1,Z≥1, put B=L_1M_1, and assume
Z≤min(L_1,M_1),   max(L_1,M_1)≤Q.                                (1)
Let α_l and β_m be complex coefficients supported respectively on
L_1≤l<2L_1 and M_1≤m<2M_1, with
|α_l|≤τ_J(l),  |β_m|≤τ_J(m).
Then for every ε>0,
Σ_{Q≤q<2Q} max_{gcd(a,q)=1}
 |Σ_{l,m,gcd(lm,q)=1} α_lβ_m e_q(a(lm)^(-1))|
≪_{J,ε}(QL_1M_1)^ε
 [Q^(5/4)B^(3/4)Z^(-1/4)+QB^(7/8)].                         (2)
Here q ranges over arbitrary integers, and the maximum is taken separately for each q.
dd7f18552d39e5d4.proof:
Irving's Lemma 3.1 in arXiv:1301.6372 states that for arbitrary integer moduli q∼Q, lengths A,C≤Q, and coefficients bounded by 1,
Σ_{Q≤q<2Q} max_{gcd(a,q)=1}
 |Σ_{l∼A,m∼C,gcd(lm,q)=1} α_lβ_m e_q(a(lm)^(-1))|
≪_{k,ε}Q^(1+ε)
 [Q^(1/(2k))A^((2k-1)/(2k))C^(1/2)
  +A^((2k-1)/(2k))C]                                      (3)
for every fixed integer k≥1. A fixed divisor-function bound is at most a harmless power on the present polynomial scales, so normalizing the coefficients and adjusting ε allows (3) to be used under the hypotheses of the statement.

Interchange the two coefficient axes if necessary so that L_1≥M_1. Apply (3) with k=2, A=L_1 and C=M_1; condition (1) makes both lengths legal. The resulting two terms, apart from the common epsilon factor, are
Q^(5/4)L_1^(3/4)M_1^(1/2),   QL_1^(3/4)M_1.                 (4)
Since L_1M_1=B, the first equals
Q^(5/4)B^(1/2)L_1^(1/4).
The lower bound M_1≥Z gives L_1=B/M_1≤B/Z, so this is at most
Q^(5/4)B^(3/4)Z^(-1/4).                                    (5)
The second term in (4) equals QB L_1^(-1/4). Since L_1 is the longer of two factors with product B, L_1≥B^(1/2), and hence this is at most
QB^(7/8).                                                    (6)
Equations (5)-(6) prove (2).

glossary.J: The fixed order of the divisor-function bounds.
glossary.L_1: The first coefficient length, oriented as the longer length in the proof.
glossary.M_1: The second coefficient length, oriented as the shorter length in the proof.
glossary.Z: A common lower bound for both coefficient lengths.
glossary.α_l: The divisor-bounded coefficient on the first axis.
glossary.β_m: The divisor-bounded coefficient on the second axis.

ddcb0baef17b6ab0.title: LITERAL FINITE-BAND JOINT (p,h)-GRAPH QUARTIC EXPANSION, PAID EXACT-SLOPE SECTOR, AND FIRST UNSUPPLIED VECTOR TERM
ddcb0baef17b6ab0.author: slava chan
ddcb0baef17b6ab0.statement: LITERAL FINITE-BAND JOINT (p,h)-GRAPH QUARTIC EXPANSION, PAID EXACT-SLOPE SECTOR, AND FIRST UNSUPPLIED VECTOR TERM. Fix Q>=2 and real numbers H,V,P satisfying 2<=H<=Q^(1/3), 2<=V=1, |cal M_COIN|<Q. There is also an elementary absolute modular-alias ledger: |cal M_MOD|<<_{C,epsilon} B^4 #cal L V H^3Q^(4+epsilon). (26) Relative to the target (13), estimate (26) still needs a gain by the factor G_MOD=V^3H/Q^(1/3) (27) whenever G_MOD>1, because [VH^3Q^4]/[P^2Q^(7/3)]=V^3H/Q^(1/3). (28) No accepted post-Cauchy supplier pays the remaining joint sector (MOD) union (OSC). Fact 914048233fada05f applies to one fixed hard actual-source q-row after h has been reassembled and to an independent (v,s,p) family; it does not retain (17)-(20). Fact ace362082848a702 is a complete-row source-minus-density identity. Facts 0e8ef74ba484418d and 11ec605c5135a640 require pointwise type-(U)/(Z) scalar q-rows and a mean-zero physical kernel. Facts 35ff1e5855450319 and 4792a797443e9961 act on the post-Cauchy output profile of a fixed q-row. Fact 84bf915e8a88d8d3 compares the same finite band with a soft translated source, but supplies only twist-average mass and loses H^2 cubically and H^3 quartically relative to pointwise Q/H occupancy. Facts 16eaa93099f0bcdc and 2dd1ed95db5b458c pay the soft-source exact-slope term and show that the soft modular mean recycles the desired fourth moment at additive frequency zero; they do not estimate (16). Therefore a sufficient first new vector theorem is the literal joint estimate |cal M_MOD+cal M_OSC| <
ddcb0baef17b6ab0.proof:
The reciprocity identity (8) follows from
 e_q(a(vp)^(-1))e_{vp}(a qbar)=e_{qvp}(a)
with a=Ah. Thus (2) absorbs only the exact Archimedean reciprocity factor and (4) retains the complete finite-modulus phase.

Apply fact 44e700816602dd36 with outer index (ell,v,p), outer coefficient eta_ell xi_v, and h-row sum y_{ell,v,p,h}=sum_qx_{ell,v,p,h}(q). This proves (10). Also
 sum_ell|eta_ell|^(4/3)<=(sum_ell|eta_ell|)^(4/3).
The divisor estimate used in fact d061fc4dc153e309 gives
 sum_{V<=v<2V}|xi_v|^(4/3)<<_{J,epsilon}VQ^epsilon.
There are O(P) possible primes. Substitution into (9) proves (11). Since each I_ell lies in an interval of O(H) integers, (10)-(11) give (12). Substituting (13) into (12) proves (14).

Expand the fourth power in (7). Fourier orthogonality in theta gives h_1+h_2=h_3+h_4. Multiplying the four phases in (4) gives
 e_{vp}(-A[h_1q_1bar+h_2q_2bar-h_3q_3bar-h_4q_4bar]).
Putting this expression over the common unit denominator q_1q_2q_3q_4 gives (15)-(16).

The CRT identity e_{vp}(z)=e_v(zpbar)e_p(zvbar) gives (18) after defining s_i by (17). Equation (19) is its definition rewritten. Multiply h_1+h_2-h_3-h_4=0 by -pbar modulo v to prove (20). Since p is a unit modulo v, (19) determines one and only one s_i. This proves the graph claims and shows why no independent average over s is available.

Because all q_i are units modulo p, the p-phase in (16) is one exactly when p divides A Delta_h. Rational equality in (22) is equivalent, after cross multiplication, to Delta_h=0. This proves the disjoint partition and its interpretations.

For (23), a coincidence has either
 (h_1,q_1)=(h_3,q_3), (h_2,q_2)=(h_4,q_4)
or the same two equalities after interchanging the right pair. Hence its absolute contribution for fixed ell,v,p is at most
 2(sum_{h,q}|w_{ell,v,p,h}(q)|^2)^2
 <<B^4H^2Q^2.
Sum over ell,v,p.

For (24), fix ell,v,p and regard z=(h,q) as an atom. Group ordered atom pairs by the two rational invariants
 S=h_1+h_2, R=h_1/q_1+h_2/q_2.                             (30)
The Delta_h=0 contribution is exactly
 sum_{S,R}|sum_{(h_1,q_1),(h_2,q_2):(30)}
       w_{ell,v,p,h_1}(q_1)w_{ell,v,p,h_2}(q_2)|^2,         (31)
so it is nonnegative.

We bound a fibre in (30). Write R=u/w in lowest terms with w>0. Because I_ell has one sign, h_1 and h_2 are nonzero and have the same sign, so R is nonzero and u is nonzero. Fix h=h_1; then h_2=S-h. The equation for R is
 u q_1q_2=w[hq_2+(S-h)q_1],
which factors exactly as
 (u q_1-wh)(u q_2-w(S-h))=w^2h(S-h).                       (32)
A represented R has w<=q_1q_2<=4Q^2, while |h(S-h)|<<H^2. The fixed-power divisor bound therefore gives O_epsilon((QH)^epsilon) possible factor pairs in (32), and each factor pair determines q_1,q_2 because u is nonzero. There are O(H) choices of h. Thus every fibre in (30) has size O_epsilon(H(QH)^epsilon). Cauchy's inequality in each fibre and disjointness of the fibres give
 (31)<<H(QH)^epsilon(sum_{h,q}|w_{ell,v,p,h}(q)|^2)^2
 <<B^4H^3Q^2(QH)^epsilon.
Summing proves (24). Since the noncoincidence exact-slope piece is the difference between the full nonnegative quantity (31) and the coincidence subpiece, (23)-(24) give (25). The scale comparison in (25) was checked in the statement.

For (26), fix ell,v and a tuple h_i,q_i with the additive h relation and Delta_h nonzero. The number of primes p in [P,2P) which divide the nonzero integer A Delta_h is bounded by its divisor function. One has |Delta_h|<<HQ^3 and |A|<=Q^C, so the accepted fixed-power divisor estimate gives O_{C,epsilon}(QH)^epsilon such primes. There are O(H^3) h-quadruples after h_4 is determined, O(Q^4) q-quadruples, O(V) values of v, and #cal L labels. Taking absolute values and using (3) proves (26). Substitute P=QH/V to obtain (28).

The final supplier audit is a direct comparison of the exact hypotheses just derived with the accepted statements cited there. None contains the four forced relations (19) together with the h-sum relation and the literal p-average. Thus (29) is sufficient after (25), while (26)-(28) state the first unpaid scale. No estimate for (29) is used.

glossary.Delta_h: The cross-multiplied difference of two weighted reciprocal sums h_1/q_1+h_2/q_2 and h_3/q_3+h_4/q_4.
glossary.G_MOD: The factor by which the elementary absolute modular-alias ledger exceeds the required vector target.
glossary.MOD: The modular alias sector Delta_h nonzero and p dividing A Delta_h.
glossary.OSC: The genuinely nonzero p-phase sector Delta_h nonzero and p not dividing A Delta_h.
glossary.SLOPE: The noncoincident exact weighted-reciprocal-slope sector Delta_h=0.
glossary.cal L: The finite set of literal sign and projective-separation labels.
glossary.cal M_4^lit: The integrated literal outer-vector fourth moment.
glossary.eta_ell: The projective coefficient of label ell.
glossary.s_i: The forced small-v residue -h_i p^{-1} modulo v.
glossary.w_{ell,v,p,h}: The exact literal q-row amplitude after absorbing only the Archimedean reciprocity factor.
glossary.x_{ell,v,p,h}: The literal finite-band q-row including the complete reciprocal phase modulo vp.

ddd3eb74fcd1957d.title: LITERAL NATURAL-COFACTOR SOURCE ENVELOPE FOR THE ALL-ACTIVE FIRST-PRIME TOP-\(B\) BLOCK
ddd3eb74fcd1957d.author: slava chan
ddd3eb74fcd1957d.proof:
Fact \(97b9d86408362df2\) gives the \(p\)-local factor
\[
 e_p\!\left(\mathscr A(hu^{-1})(y/p)^{-1}q^{-1}\right).
\]
Because \(T=u(y/p)\), its coefficient is
\[
 (hu^{-1})(y/p)^{-1}=hT^{-1}\pmod p,
\]
which proves (2). Since \(p\mid y\), literal support gives \(p\nmid u\). Squarefreeness of \(y\) gives \(p\nmid y/p\), hence \(p\nmid T\). Condition (4) and \(0<|h|<2F\) give \(p\nmid h\). Thus all height and cofactor residues in (5) are nonzero.

By fact \(ec8a0fbdab03cda6\), reduction modulo \(p\) is injective on \(J_{p,k}\). Therefore fixed \(\tau\) in (5) determines at most one physical integer \(T\). For such a \(T\), the equation \(uy=pT\) has at most
\[
 \tau(pT)\ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon
\]
positive factorizations, and the dyadic, stopping, squarefree, coprimality, and literal source conditions only delete factorizations.

The interval \(Q\le q<2Q\) contains at most
\[
 1+{Q\over p}
\]
integers in one residue class modulo \(p\). Each of the two signed height intervals
\[
 F\le h<2F,\qquad -2F<h\le-F
\]
has length at most \(F+1\) and, by \(p>2F\), contains at most one integer in a fixed residue class modulo \(p\). Hence there are at most two physical heights for fixed \(H\).

Fact \(d63101722d12c88c\) gives
\[
 |c_k^{\rm rec}(u,y;q,h)|\ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon.
\]
Fact \(97b9d86408362df2\) gives
\[
 |a_{p,\lambda}|=|d_{p,t_y}(u,q,h)|
 =|c_k^{\rm rec}(u,y;q,h)|.
\]
Multiplying the divisor-many factorization count, the at-most-two height lifts, and the \(1+Q/p\) modulus lifts proves (10), after renaming \(\varepsilon\).

Only residues of supported physical heights contribute to (8). There are fewer than \(2F+2\), hence \(O(F)\), such residues. Summing (10) over them proves (11).

For fixed \(X\), supported shifts \(r\) arise from the residues of the physical integers \(q\in[Q,2Q)\). Translation by \(-X\) is a bijection modulo \(p\), so the number of supported shifts is at most
\[
 \min(p,Q+1)\le\min(p,2Q).
\]
Substitution of (11) into (9), followed by summation over these shifts, proves (12).

The blocks \(J_{p,k}\) are disjoint and cover the interval \(J_p\) of fact \(ec8a0fbdab03cda6\). Their lengths satisfy
\[
 L_{p,k}\le {p\over2},\qquad
 \sum_kL_{p,k}=\#J_p\le {3B\over2p}+1.
\]
Hence
\[
 \sum_kL_{p,k}^2
 \le {p\over2}\sum_kL_{p,k}
 \le {3B\over4}+{p\over2}.
\]
The selected prime divides the marked dilator \(y\), and \(y<2B\), so \(p<2B\). Therefore
\[
 \sum_kL_{p,k}^2\ll B.
\]
Summing (12) over \(k\) proves (13).

Finally, the vector and contraction assertion is exactly the accepted construction in fact \(97b9d86408362df2\), now with the same coefficient relabelled by \(T=u(y/p)\). Facts \(a84f95a82329a894\), \(bbd687d016ee3ff6\), and \(ec8a0fbdab03cda6\) define their envelopes by source-copy vector norms, so (7)-(9) match those formal slots. None of those facts constructs the common-\(X\) completion or the upstream baseline comparison. Fact \(9ea2dddfbbbd191a\) requires a separated bounded-variation coefficient in the integer height and cofactor variables, which is not asserted by the divisor bound used in (10). This proves all scope statements.

glossary.A_{p,k,X}: The literal source-copy l1 mass at fixed selected prime, injective cofactor block, translated coordinate, shift, height residue, and natural-cofactor residue.
glossary.T: The natural selected-prime integer cofactor n/p=uy/p.
glossary.U_{p,k,X}: The height-l1 and natural-cofactor-l-infinity envelope formed from A_{p,k,X}.
glossary.Y_{p,k,X}: The block baseline L_{p,k}^2 times the shift-l2 mass of U_{p,k,X}.

dde1e246a629bcc4.title: COMPLETE SAME-SELECTED-N FIRST-BUFFER C3 PAYMENT AND EXACT NEGATIVE LATE-BETA HANDOFF
dde1e246a629bcc4.author: slava chan
dde1e246a629bcc4.statement:
COMPLETE SAME-SELECTED-N FIRST-BUFFER C3 PAYMENT AND EXACT NEGATIVE LATE-BETA HANDOFF.

Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, beta_0=6/5-2kappa and beta_1=6/5-3sigma, and fix 0<eta<sigma. Use the selected fixed-N source of fact 60b26a9b6f79467a: N=2x, fixed dyadic D,M,U, smooth weights W,psi,Phi, and active dyadic R,K in
Q_N(R,K)=sum_{dm+rk=N}mu(d)mu(r)log(m)log(k)W(dm/x)psi(d/D_*)
 Phi(d/D)Phi(m/M)Phi(rk/U)Phi(r/R)Phi(k/K).
Here W is supported in [a,b] with 1/2<a<b<1, Phi is supported in [1/2,2], D<=2x^(1/2), DM is comparable to x, and U is comparable to x. Hence every active label has both DM and RK comparable to x.

Let R_postABC2,sel be the finite real same-selected-N remainder of fact 32f645844f1ca9a1. It satisfies
R_postABC2,sel<=-c_dir c(N)x/log x+o(c(N)x/log x),
with c(N)>=C_2>0. Every atom has normalized beta>beta_0. Inside beta_0<beta<=beta_1 every atom has frozen parent U_low and sole anatomy C3 with all literal coordinates retained.

Let R_C3,buf,sel be the complete projection of R_postABC2,sel onto beta_0<beta<=beta_1, after every auxiliary refinement is recombined. Then for some fixed delta_C3>0,
|R_C3,buf,sel|<<x^(1-delta_C3).                                    (1)
Define
T_late,sel=R_postABC2,sel-R_C3,buf,sel.                              (2)
Then
T_late,sel<=-c_dir c(N)x/log x+o(c(N)x/log x),                       (3)
and every atom of T_late,sel has beta>beta_1.                        (4)
No individual negative atom, moving actual-Z, endpoint, PMD, DCE, four-prime, Goldbach implication, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
dde1e246a629bcc4.proof:
The source formula supplies both product scales. The support of W(dm/x) and the d,m dyadic cutoffs give DM comparable to x. Fact 60b26a9b6f79467a gives U comparable to x, and Phi(rk/U),Phi(r/R),Phi(k/K) give RK comparable to x.

The selected D,M,U are fixed. There are O((log x)^2) active R,K labels, polylogarithmically many v and three-prime cells, finitely many equality partitions, and tau(N)=x^o(1) exact g layers. The fixed smooth functions have uniform scaled derivatives. Selected-source, fixed-U, high and U_low coordinates are frozen scalars; all auxiliary refinements are recombined. Hence the total literal-layer and projective norm is x^o(1). Facts da22464a2f614042 and 2e0b40b1ba77fb6f already include pair/triple equality and p_i dividing g corrections.

We remove the constant-factor ratio issue explicitly. From D<=2x^(1/2) and the forward high condition R>x^(9/16-1/200),
R/D>(1/2)x^(23/400).                                               (5)
In reverse D>R and R<=D_source<=2x^(1/2), while D is the high larger scale, so
D/R>(1/2)x^(23/400).                                               (6)
Choose once and for all lambda=2^(-800/23) and put X=lambda x. Then
X^(23/400)=x^(23/400)/4,
so (5)-(6) are both strictly larger than X^(23/400). Also N=(2/lambda)X, DM and RK are comparable to X, and D<=2lambda^(-1/2)X^(1/2), with the analogous reverse smaller-scale bound. All remaining physical upper bounds change only by fixed constants. Thus the hypotheses of da22464a2f614042 and 2e0b40b1ba77fb6f hold with ambient scale X on every selected layer.

Fix g. Forward put Q=D/g, B=R/g and G=M/Q. From D<=2x^(1/2) and DM>=cx,
G=g(DM)/D^2>=cg/4>=c/4.                                            (7)
For G>=1, da22464a2f614042 gives
GQ^(2-delta)=(DM/g)Q^(-delta)<< (x/g)Q^(-delta).                    (8)
For G<1, fact 15425579cb248eff places the layer in the accepted near-balanced strip. Its Q^(2-delta) bound and (7), using DM=gGQ^2, again give
Q^(2-delta)<< (x/g)Q^(-delta).                                      (9)

Reverse put Q=R/g, B=D/g and G=K/Q. Since R<=2x^(1/2) and RK>=cx,
G=g(RK)/R^2>=cg/4>=c/4.                                            (10)
Fact 2e0b40b1ba77fb6f, with the same G split, gives
O((x/g)Q^(-delta))                                                   (11)
for every reverse layer.

In either orientation Q^(beta-1) is the ratio in (5) or (6), and beta-1<=1/5. Hence Q>=X^(23/80)>=x^(1/4) for large x. Sum (8)-(11) over g|N and the x^o(1) complete labels:
sum_{g|N}(x/g)Q^(-delta)x^o(1)<<x^(1-delta/5),                      (12)
proving (1).

Fact 7ffe3d237362a451 gives beta>beta_0 on the full selected post-low remainder. Fact 32f645844f1ca9a1 gives C3 as the sole coordinate in beta_0<beta<=beta_1. Therefore subtracting the complete projection leaves exactly support beta>beta_1, proving (4). Finally (1) is o(c(N)x/log x) since c(N)>=C_2. Insert (1) into the exact identity (2) and the accepted negative bound for R_postABC2,sel to prove (3).

glossary.R_C3,buf,sel: The complete same-selected-N C3 projection on beta_0<beta<=beta_1.
glossary.T_late,sel: The selected post-C2 remainder after subtracting the complete first-buffer C3 projection.
glossary.delta_C3: The global power-saving exponent for the selected C3 buffer.

de1c0ccbef73029b.title: There are absolute constants c_0>0 and H_0>=2 with the following property. Let H>=H_0 and let r_1,r_2,r_3 be pairwise distinct odd primes in [H^2,2H^2). Let E_H be the positive even integers at most H^3, and form the matrix W=(W_{b,d}) indexed by b,d in E_H, where W_{b,d}=1 if b r_3-d r_2=2r_1 and W_{b,d}=0 otherwise. Let L be the number of nonzero entries of W. Then L>=c_0H. Moreover, among all finite exact decompositions W_{b,d}=sum_j beta_j(b)alpha_j(d) into complex one-variable sequences, the infimum of sum_j ||beta_j||_2||alpha_j||_2 equals L. In particular this separated ell^2 tensor cost is at least c_0H
de1c0ccbef73029b.author: slava chan
de1c0ccbef73029b.statement: There are absolute constants c_0>0 and H_0>=2 with the following property. Let H>=H_0 and let r_1,r_2,r_3 be pairwise distinct odd primes in [H^2,2H^2). Let E_H be the positive even integers at most H^3, and form the matrix W=(W_{b,d}) indexed by b,d in E_H, where W_{b,d}=1 if b r_3-d r_2=2r_1 and W_{b,d}=0 otherwise. Let L be the number of nonzero entries of W. Then L>=c_0H. Moreover, among all finite exact decompositions W_{b,d}=sum_j beta_j(b)alpha_j(d) into complex one-variable sequences, the infimum of sum_j ||beta_j||_2||alpha_j||_2 equals L. In particular this separated ell^2 tensor cost is at least c_0H.
de1c0ccbef73029b.proof:
Because r_2 and r_3 are distinct primes, they are coprime. Choose B_0 to be the integer in [0,r_2) satisfying B_0 r_3 congruent to r_1 modulo r_2, and put D_0=(B_0r_3-r_1)/r_2. Then B_0r_3-D_0r_2=r_1, with 0<=B_0<r_2<=2H^2 and |D_0|<r_3+r_1/r_2<2H^2+2.

Every integer j gives a solution B=B_0+r_2j, D=D_0+r_3j of Br_3-Dr_2=r_1. Take all integers j in [H/16,H/8]. For sufficiently large H, the preceding bounds and H^2<=r_2,r_3<2H^2 imply B>0,D>0 and 2B<=H^3,2D<=H^3. Thus b=2B and d=2D belong to E_H and satisfy b r_3-d r_2=2r_1. The interval [H/16,H/8] contains at least c_0H integers for an absolute c_0>0, proving L>=c_0H. Different j give different b and different d.

For any fixed b the equation b r_3-d r_2=2r_1 determines at most one d, and for any fixed d it determines at most one b. Hence W is a partial permutation matrix with L entries equal to one. Its operator norm on ell^2 is one. Its squared Frobenius norm, which is the matrix inner product <W,W>, is L.

Consider any exact decomposition W=sum_j beta_j tensor alpha_j. By the operator-norm inequality for a rank-one matrix,
|<W,beta_j tensor alpha_j>|<=||W||_op||beta_j||_2||alpha_j||_2=||beta_j||_2||alpha_j||_2.
Summing and using <W,W>=L yields L<=sum_j||beta_j||_2||alpha_j||_2. Conversely, writing W as the sum of its L nonzero matrix units gives a decomposition for which every factor norm is one and the sum is L. Therefore the infimum is exactly L.

glossary.E_H: the set of positive even integers not exceeding H^3
glossary.L: the number of nonzero entries of W
glossary.W: the incidence matrix of the equation b r_3-d r_2=2r_1 on E_H times E_H
glossary.alpha_j: a complex sequence in the d coordinate
glossary.beta_j: a complex sequence in the b coordinate

de324f84f27469cf.title: LARGE-COMMON-GCD PAYMENT IN SIGNED-QPAIR-DISP. Retain fact 0895975a7f3918e9 and fix
de324f84f27469cf.author: slava chan
de324f84f27469cf.statement:
LARGE-COMMON-GCD PAYMENT IN SIGNED-QPAIR-DISP. Retain fact 0895975a7f3918e9 and fix
\[
 0<\delta<1/4,\qquad 0<\eta<1/20.
\]
Let \({\cal O}_h(C)\) be the part of its exact off-diagonal \({\cal O}_h\) restricted by
\[
 C\le(q_1,q_2)<2C.                                         \tag{1}
\]
Then, uniformly for \(1\le C\le2Q\),
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 |{\cal O}_h(C)|
 \ll_A(\log x)^{2C_0}(1+F/H_P)^{-2A}Q^{o(1)}
 \left(Q^3C^{-3/2}+Q^2+BC\right).
 \quad}                                                     \tag{2}
\]
Here \(C_0\) is a fixed source-smoothness exponent, unrelated to the dyadic common-gcd scale \(C\).

Consequently every dyadic common-gcd stratum satisfying
\[
 C\ge Q^{\,{2\over3}(\beta-1+2\delta)+\eta}                \tag{3}
\]
obeys
\[
 |{\cal O}_h(C)|
 \ll_A(\log x)^{2C_0}(1+F/H_P)^{-2A}
 Q^{\,4-\beta-2\delta-\eta}.                               \tag{4}
\]
After all such dyadic \(C\)-blocks are summed, their contribution pays the corresponding part of \(J_qJ_n\) with \(Q^{2-\delta+o(1)}\) through fact 0895975a7f3918e9. Thus the exact unresolved signed residual may be restricted to
\[
 (q_1,q_2)
 <Q^{\,{2\over3}(\beta-1+2\delta)+\eta}.                   \tag{5}
\]
The payment uses no sign cancellation in \(\alpha_J(q_1)\overline{\alpha_J(q_2)}\); those signs remain available in the low-common-gcd residual. No estimate for (5), no complete SIGNED-QPAIR-DISP theorem, and no post-A or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
de324f84f27469cf.proof:
Fix an off-diagonal pair and put
\[
 c=(q_1,q_2),\qquad q_1=cr_1,\qquad q_2=cr_2.
\]
Then \((r_1,r_2)=1\) and \(r_1,r_2\asymp Q/c\). Since every active n is coprime to \(q_1q_2\),
\[
 \overline{q_1}-\overline{q_2}
 \equiv(r_2-r_1)\overline{cr_1r_2}\pmod n.                 \tag{6}
\]
Thus the exposed reciprocal modulus is
\[
 R=cr_1r_2\asymp Q^2/c,                                   \tag{7}
\]
and additive reciprocity gives
\[
 e_n\!\left(a_h(\overline{q_1}-\overline{q_2})\right)
 =
 e\!\left({a_h(r_2-r_1)\over nR}\right)
 e_R\!\left(-a_h(r_2-r_1)\overline n\right).               \tag{8}
\]
The ordinary factor in (8), combined with the two literal coefficients, has the same n-variation bound proved in fact 0895975a7f3918e9.

Put
\[
 G=(a_h(r_2-r_1),R).
\]
Because \((r_1,r_2)=1\),
\[
 (r_2-r_1,r_1r_2)=1.
\]
Therefore
\[
 G\le c\,(a_h,r_1r_2).                                     \tag{9}
\]
The incomplete reciprocal estimate reproduced in fact 8138369f26f88aad, applied after bounded-variation partial summation and the exact auxiliary-g divisor expansion of fact 0895975a7f3918e9, bounds this n-kernel by
\[
 \ll_A(\log x)^{2C_0}(1+F/H_P)^{-2A}Q^{o(1)}
 \left(G\left({B\over R}+1\right)+R^{1/2}\right).           \tag{10}
\]

For every nonzero integer a and \(Y\ge1\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_{Y<r\le2Y}(a,r)
 &=\sum_{s\mid a}\varphi(s)
   \#\{Y<r\le2Y:s\mid r\}\\
 &\le3Y\sum_{\substack{s\mid a\\s\le2Y}}{\varphi(s)\over s}
 \le3Y\tau(|a|).                                           \tag{11}
 \end{aligned}
\]
Also
\[
 (a,r_1r_2)\le(a,r_1)(a,r_2).
\]
Hence, even after dropping \((r_1,r_2)=1\),
\[
 \sum_{r_1,r_2\asymp Q/c}(a_h,r_1r_2)
 \ll (Q/c)^2\tau(|a_h|)^2.                                 \tag{12}
\]
All \(\alpha_J\)-weights cost only \(Q^{o(1)}\) pointwise. Indeed fact 0895975a7f3918e9 gives
\[
 |\alpha_J(q)|\le2\tau_3(q),
\]
and, for every fixed \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 \tau_3(q)\ll_\varepsilon q^\varepsilon.                   \tag{13}
\]
To prove (13), note \(\tau_3(p^k)\le(k+1)^2\). For the finitely many primes \(p\le2^{4/\varepsilon}\), choose a fixed constant making \((k+1)^2\le C_{p,\varepsilon}p^{\varepsilon k}\) for every k; for larger p, \((k+1)^2\le4^k\le p^{\varepsilon k}\). Multiplication over prime powers proves (13). The same argument applies to \(\tau(|a_h|)\), and its \(F^\varepsilon\) cost is absorbed by arbitrary-order frequency decay.

For fixed c, equations (7), (9), and (12) show that the sum over \(r_1,r_2\) of the two G-terms in (10) is at most
\[
 Q^{o(1)}
 \left[
 c\left({Q\over c}\right)^2
 +c\left({Q\over c}\right)^2{B\over Q^2/c}
 \right]
 =
 Q^{o(1)}\left({Q^2\over c}+B\right).                      \tag{14}
\]
The square-root term contributes, for fixed c,
\[
 \left({Q\over c}\right)^2
 \left({Q^2\over c}\right)^{1/2}
 ={Q^3\over c^{5/2}}.                                      \tag{15}
\]
There are \(O(C)\) integers c in (1). Summing (14)-(15) over \(c\asymp C\) proves (2).

Assume (3). The first term in (2) satisfies
\[
 Q^3C^{-3/2}
 \le Q^{\,4-\beta-2\delta-3\eta/2}.                        \tag{16}
\]
This leaves the fixed margin \(\eta/2\) beyond (4). For the second term,
\[
 (4-\beta-2\delta-\eta)-2
 =2-\beta-2\delta-\eta>1/4,                                \tag{17}
\]
using \(\beta<6/5,\delta<1/4,\eta<1/20\). For the third term, \(C\le2Q\) and
\[
 (4-\beta-2\delta-\eta)-(\beta+1)
 =3-2\beta-2\delta-\eta>1/20.                              \tag{18}
\]
Thus the uniform \(Q^{o(1)}\) factor is absorbed by the positive margins in (16)-(18), proving (4). There are \(O(\log Q)\) dyadic common-gcd blocks, also absorbed into those margins. Fact 0895975a7f3918e9 then pays their \(J_qJ_n\) contribution and leaves exactly (5).

glossary.large-common-gcd payment: The absolute payment of SIGNED-QPAIR-DISP strata satisfying (3).
glossary.low-common-gcd residual: The exact remaining q-pair sector in (5).
glossary.mathcal O_h(C): The dyadic common-gcd C stratum of the signed off-diagonal q-pair kernel.

de77752fa0dd5cf7.title: SHIFTED NONZERO-DUAL GRAM FOR CENTERED INVERSE-PHASE ROWS
de77752fa0dd5cf7.author: slava chan
de77752fa0dd5cf7.statement:
SHIFTED NONZERO-DUAL GRAM FOR CENTERED INVERSE-PHASE ROWS.

Let \(p\ge5\) be prime. For \(C\in\mathbb F_p^\times\), define
\[
 f_C(x)={\bf1}_{x\ne0}e_p(Cx^{-1}),\qquad
 \widehat f_C(\rho)={1\over p}\sum_{x\in\mathbb F_p}
 f_C(x)e_p(-\rho x).                                               \tag{1}
\]
For \(C,C'\in\mathbb F_p^\times\) and \(t\in\mathbb F_p\), put
\[
 H_p(C,C';t)=
 \sum_{\substack{\rho\in\mathbb F_p\\
                  \rho\ne0,\ \rho-t\ne0}}
 \widehat f_C(\rho)\overline{\widehat f_{C'}(\rho-t)}.             \tag{2}
\]
Then
\[
 H_p(C,C;0)={p-1\over p}-{1\over p^2},\qquad
 H_p(C,C';0)=-{1\over p}-{1\over p^2}\quad(C\ne C'),               \tag{3}
\]
while for \(t\ne0\),
\[
 |H_p(C,C;t)|\le {3\over p},                                      \tag{4}
\]
and
\[
 |H_p(C,C';t)|\le {4\over\sqrt p}\quad(C\ne C').                  \tag{5}
\]

More generally, let \(r\) be squarefree with every prime divisor at least \(5\). For every \(p\mid r\), choose \(C_p,C'_p\in\mathbb F_p^\times\). Put
\[
 V_C(\boldsymbol\rho)=\prod_{p\mid r}\widehat f_{C_p}(\rho_p),
 \qquad
 V_{C'}(\boldsymbol\rho)=\prod_{p\mid r}\widehat f_{C'_p}(\rho_p),
 \qquad
 \Omega_r=\prod_{p\mid r}\mathbb F_p^\times.                      \tag{6}
\]
For \(\boldsymbol t=(t_p)_{p\mid r}\in\prod_{p\mid r}\mathbb F_p\), define
\[
 H_r(C,C';\boldsymbol t)=
 \sum_{\substack{\boldsymbol\rho\\
                  \boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r,\ 
                  \boldsymbol\rho-\boldsymbol t\in\Omega_r}}
 V_C(\boldsymbol\rho)
 \overline{V_{C'}(\boldsymbol\rho-\boldsymbol t)}.                 \tag{7}
\]
Then
\[
 H_r(C,C';\boldsymbol t)=\prod_{p\mid r}H_p(C_p,C'_p;t_p).         \tag{8}
\]
Every local factor has absolute value at most \(1\). If
\(\boldsymbol t\ne\boldsymbol0\), then for every prime \(p\mid r\) with
\(t_p\ne0\), the \(p\)-factor has size at most \(3/p\) when
\(C_p=C'_p\), and at most \(4/\sqrt p\) when \(C_p\ne C'_p\). Hence an order-one local factor can occur only on the simultaneous stratum
\[
 t_p=0,\qquad C_p=C'_p.                                           \tag{9}
\]

In the same-target GA tensor of fact df97bf1eba0495be,
\(C_p=C'_p\) is equivalent to
\[
 p^2\mid hn'-h'n.                                                  \tag{10}
\]
Thus every nonzero dual shift has a power-saving local factor at at least one shifted prime; on a shifted square-divisor collision it is \(O(1/p)\), and off collision it is \(O(p^{-1/2})\). This is a local/tensor shift table only. It does not sum the shifted modes with literal \(W\)-coefficients, estimate the off-dual discrepancy of fact 9128d43a5ac4e1bb, control distinct active products or the pair-dependent NR deletion, prove GA-NR-DIL, or imply Goldbach.
de77752fa0dd5cf7.proof:
First note from (1), or from fact 4f9aec67f5be35db, that
\[
 \widehat f_C(0)=-{1\over p},\qquad
 |\widehat f_C(\rho)|\le {2\over\sqrt p}\quad(\rho\ne0).           \tag{11}
\]
Complete the sum in (2) over every \(\rho\in\mathbb F_p\). Fourier orthogonality gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 F_p(C,C';t)
 &:=\sum_{\rho\in\mathbb F_p}
 \widehat f_C(\rho)\overline{\widehat f_{C'}(\rho-t)}\\
 &={1\over p}\sum_{x\in\mathbb F_p^\times}
 e_p\!\left((C-C')x^{-1}-tx\right).                               \tag{12}
 \end{aligned}
\]
Indeed, after expanding both normalized transforms, the \(\rho\)-sum forces the two physical variables to be equal.

If \(t=0\), condition (2) deletes only \(\rho=0\), whose contribution is \(p^{-2}\). If \(C=C'\), (12) equals \((p-1)/p\). If \(C\ne C'\), inversion permutes \(\mathbb F_p^\times\), so (12) equals \(-1/p\). Subtracting \(p^{-2}\) proves (3).

Now let \(t\ne0\). The two deleted coordinates are the distinct residues \(0\) and \(t\). By (11)--(12),
\[
 H_p(C,C';t)=F_p(C,C';t)
 +{1\over p}\overline{\widehat f_{C'}(-t)}
 +{1\over p}\widehat f_C(t).                                     \tag{13}
\]
If \(C=C'\), the sum in (12) is
\[
 {1\over p}\sum_{x\ne0}e_p(-tx)=-{1\over p}.
\]
Equation (11) therefore gives
\[
 |H_p(C,C;t)|\le {1\over p}+{4\over p^{3/2}}\le {3\over p}
\]
for \(p\ge5\), proving (4).

If \(C\ne C'\), both coefficients in the Kloosterman sum (12) are nonzero. The Weil bound recorded in fact 4f9aec67f5be35db gives
\[
 |F_p(C,C';t)|\le {2\over\sqrt p}.
\]
Together with (11) and (13),
\[
 |H_p(C,C';t)|
 \le {2\over\sqrt p}+{4\over p^{3/2}}
 \le {4\over\sqrt p},
\]
proving (5).

For the squarefree product, the summation conditions and the summand in (7) factor coordinatewise. The Chinese remainder theorem therefore gives (8). Parseval and restriction show every local factor has absolute value at most
\[
 \left(\sum_{\rho\ne0}|\widehat f_C(\rho)|^2\right)^{1/2}
 \left(\sum_{\rho\ne0}|\widehat f_{C'}(\rho)|^2\right)^{1/2}<1.
\]
Equations (4)--(5) give the asserted saving at every shifted coordinate and prove (9).

Finally, fact df97bf1eba0495be identifies equality of the two same-target local parameters with the square-divisor collision (10). Substitution into (4)--(5) gives the GA interpretation. No summation over \(\boldsymbol t\) or literal multiplier has been performed, so all scope limitations follow.

glossary.dual shift: The coordinatewise difference t between the two active dual-frequency tuples.
glossary.shifted nonzero-dual Gram: The correlation of two centered inverse-phase Fourier vectors after translating one nonzero dual coordinate set.

df2841924153b718.title: LITERAL TYPE-I PHASE AUDIT FOR THE NORMALIZED FIVE-LEAF SOURCE. Let a,b,m,k,L be positive integers with am+bk=L, gcd(a,b)=1, and a,b squarefree. In the forward or equal-scale orientation, the nonzero Poisson character e_b(Lh a^{-1}) has the reciprocity form e(Lh/(ab))e_a(-Lh b^{-1}); the reciprocal modulus is a, the factorized inverse argument is b, and the fixed target is -L. In the reverse orientation, retain the original character e_b(Lh a^{-1}); the reciprocal modulus is b, the factorized inverse argument is a, and the fixed target is +L
df2841924153b718.author: slava chan
df2841924153b718.statement:
LITERAL TYPE-I PHASE AUDIT FOR THE NORMALIZED FIVE-LEAF SOURCE. Let a,b,m,k,L be positive integers with am+bk=L, gcd(a,b)=1, and a,b squarefree. In the forward or equal-scale orientation, the nonzero Poisson character e_b(Lh a^{-1}) has the reciprocity form e(Lh/(ab))e_a(-Lh b^{-1}); the reciprocal modulus is a, the factorized inverse argument is b, and the fixed target is -L. In the reverse orientation, retain the original character e_b(Lh a^{-1}); the reciprocal modulus is b, the factorized inverse argument is a, and the fixed target is +L.
Fix either orientation and write s for the reciprocal modulus, n for the factorized inverse argument, and A for the signed target, so the character is e_s(Ah n^{-1}) times at most the forward archimedean factor. On an exact target-gcd layer c=gcd(s,L), fact 1c64020b89f097c4, applied directly in the forward orientation or after interchanging (a,m) with (b,k) in the reverse orientation, gives s=cq and L=cL_1 with gcd(q,L_1)=1. The descended reciprocal character has modulus q and fixed target -L_1 forward or +L_1 reverse; its unit multiplier is one.
In the C1 proof of fact 2ff1c15aef183bac and the separated-outer C2 Case 1 proof of fact 3b1bda56ad927c5e, the exact Vaughan decomposition is fact 29c43cef40f2e79b. Every Type-I box factorizes the same integer n, or its final prime factor, into convolution variables without changing their product in the reciprocal inverse. Hence every literal Type-I character on a fixed orientation and fixed target-gcd layer is exactly e_q(plus-or-minus L_1 h times the inverse of the displayed convolution product), with no additional q-dependent unit. Therefore the fixed-target Type-I consumer bbcb9f66597c667c matches the literal phase. This result is confined to the Type-I branches explicitly occurring in facts 2ff1c15aef183bac and 3b1bda56ad927c5e; it does not assert a theorem for arbitrary q-dependent unit twists or for branches outside this audited five-leaf proof inventory.
df2841924153b718.proof:
Forward additive reciprocity is the elementary identity a^{-1}/b+b^{-1}/a=1/(ab) modulo one. Multiplication by Lh and exponentiation gives e_b(Lh a^{-1})=e(Lh/(ab))e_a(-Lh b^{-1}). In reverse orientation the marked factor is a and its complementary reciprocal modulus is b, so the original Poisson character already has the required form e_b(+Lh a^{-1}). This proves the orientation table.
For forward target-gcd descent, apply fact 1c64020b89f097c4 to am+bk=L with c=gcd(a,L). It gives a=cq,L=cL_1 and gcd(q,L_1)=1. Repeating the same elementary reciprocity calculation after division gives the modulus-q character e_q(-L_1h b^{-1}). For reverse descent, rewrite the incidence as bk+am=L and apply the same fact with b as its first modulus, k as its first complementary variable, a as its second coefficient, and m as its second variable. With c=gcd(b,L), it gives b=cq,L=cL_1,gcd(q,L_1)=1, and the character is e_q(+L_1h a^{-1}). Fixing c before the modulus average makes L_1 a fixed integer in each layer.
We now audit the actual Type-I inventory. In fact 2ff1c15aef183bac, the C1 integer is n=vp. The proof first replaces the prime indicator by Lambda(n')/log(n') minus proper prime powers, with p replaced by the integer n'. It then invokes the exact Vaughan identity and box ranges of fact 29c43cef40f2e79b, writing n'=ell m' in every convolution box. Pointwise, the inverse argument vp is replaced by the equal product v ell m'. Grouping v with ell changes only which coefficient sequence carries the product v ell; the reciprocal argument remains v ell m'. Thus both its Type-I and Type-II characters keep the fixed numerator plus-or-minus L_1h.
In fact 3b1bda56ad927c5e, only Case 1 invokes a Type-I endpoint theorem: it groups vp_1 into a separated outer integer and treats p_2 as the final prime through the separated-outer C1 theorem af579dffb21039b1, whose proof explicitly reruns 2ff1c15aef183bac after assuming the separated-outer coprimality. Therefore the preceding C1 audit applies with v replaced by vp_1. Cases 2 and 3 use the correlated-energy theorem directly and create no Type-I box. Fact 0576f567200d41f1 treats C3 only by correlated energy; fact 533acf4056cf5bee treats B by correlated energy after its own joint-gcd removal; and fact 664a92777dc5f5db treats A by the interval-prime estimate. Hence there are no other Type-I occurrences within the five cited leaf proofs. The archimedean reciprocity factor and every smooth mask are coefficient amplitudes, not changes to the additive-character numerator. This completes the finite branch audit and the stated scope.

glossary.A: The signed fixed target, equal to -L forward and +L reverse.
glossary.literal Type-I phase audit: The finite orientation and branch check that the actual Type-I characters have a fixed target and unit multiplier one.
glossary.n: The marked inverse argument in the chosen normalized orientation.
glossary.s: The reciprocal modulus in the chosen normalized orientation.

df45be7aead3cec9.title: EXACT FINITE MÖBIUS ROUTING TO MEDIUM-FACTOR, FREE-FACTOR TYPE-I, AND A MULTI-FREE RESIDUAL FOR THE COMPOSITE C1 PHASE. Fix kappa>0 and a fixed K_0>=2. Let Q be sufficiently large. Let n be squarefree, C an integer, m_eff=n/gcd(C,n), and c squarefree, with
df45be7aead3cec9.author: slava chan
df45be7aead3cec9.statement:
EXACT FINITE MÖBIUS ROUTING TO MEDIUM-FACTOR, FREE-FACTOR TYPE-I, AND A MULTI-FREE RESIDUAL FOR THE COMPOSITE C1 PHASE. Fix kappa>0 and a fixed K_0>=2. Let Q be sufficiently large. Let n be squarefree, C an integer, m_eff=n/gcd(C,n), and c squarefree, with
Q^(1/2+kappa)<=m_eff<=Q^(6/5),  nc<=Q^K_0.                       (1)
Write theta_eff=log(m_eff)/log(Q), put eta=kappa/20, and define
a=max{2eta,1-theta_eff+4eta},
b=min{theta_eff-4eta,1-theta_eff/2-4eta}.                        (2)
Then 0<a<b<1.

Let W be extended by zero, supported on Q<=q<2Q, and satisfy V_Q(W)<=Q^epsilon for every fixed epsilon>0. There is an exact finite truncated-inverse expansion of
S=sum_q mu(q)1_{(q,nc)=1}W(q)e_n(Cq^(-1))                      (3)
into fixed-order signed convolution boxes with the following exhaustive routing after dyadic subdivision.

(i) MEDIUM: if one fixed subcollection of the factors in a box has product y of dyadic scale Y with Q^a<=Y<=Q^b, group it as y and group the complementary factors as u. Fact b390149c13836271 gives that complete box the bound Q^(1-eta+o(1)).

(ii) TYPE I: suppose no subcollection has dyadic product scale in [Q^a,Q^b]. Choose, with a fixed deterministic tie-break on the finite factor positions, a maximal subcollection whose dyadic product P is at most Q^b. Then P<Q^a and it contains every Möbius-bearing short factor. If exactly one nonunit factor is omitted, that omitted factor is unweighted, has scale B>Q^(1-a-o(1)), and fact 9be4b1c96a2620dc bounds the box by Q^(1-eta+o(1)).

(iii) MULTI-FREE RESIDUAL: in every remaining box, the same carrier P<Q^a contains every Möbius-bearing factor, and at least two omitted nonunit factors are unweighted. Each omitted factor has scale
>Q^(b-a-o(1)).                                                   (4)

The number of convolution and dyadic boxes is Q^o(1), so the total of (i),(ii) is Q^(1-eta+o(1)). Hence the full composite-Möbius supplier of fact 79ffbcb2ffe4049f in the effective-modulus range (1) reduces exactly to estimating the multi-free residual (iii). The range m_eff<Q^(1/2+kappa), the possibility p|C in the literal C1 row, and the residual (iii) are not estimated here.
df45be7aead3cec9.proof:
First verify the window. If theta_eff<=2/3, then the upper minimum in (2) is theta_eff-4eta. Since theta_eff>=1/2+kappa,
(theta_eff-4eta)-(1-theta_eff+4eta)
=2theta_eff-1-8eta>=2kappa-8kappa/20>0.
It also exceeds 2eta because theta_eff>=1/2+kappa. If theta_eff>=2/3, the upper minimum is 1-theta_eff/2-4eta. Its difference from 1-theta_eff+4eta is theta_eff/2-8eta>0, and its difference from 2eta is
1-theta_eff/2-6eta>=2/5-6eta>0
because theta_eff<=6/5. Thus 0<a<b. The same calculations give the buffered inequalities
a>=2eta,
a>=1-theta_eff+4eta,
b<=theta_eff-4eta,
b<=1-theta_eff/2-4eta.                                         (5)

Apply the finite truncated Dirichlet-inverse construction in the proof of fact 512b50816bb8e5ef with beta=1, the present a,b, c_0=min(a/2,(b-a)/2), z=Q^c_0/16, and a fixed integer K satisfying Kc_0>1. Since kappa is fixed, K is fixed. For every q in [Q,2Q) it gives
mu(q)=sum_{j=1}^K(-1)^(j-1)binom(K,j)
 sum_{d_1...d_j u_1...u_{j-1}=q; d_i<=z}
 mu(d_1)...mu(d_j).                                             (6)
The j=1 term is empty for large Q because then q=d_1<=z<Q. Subdivide every factor into dyadic intervals. There are only log(Q)^{O_K(1)}=Q^o(1) boxes, and every coefficient produced by grouping a fixed subset of factor positions is bounded by a fixed divisor function.

Consider a box in class (i). Dyadic constants change exponents by o(1). Put Y equal to the chosen subset scale and U equal to its complement, so UY is comparable to Q. From (5),
Y>=Q^(2eta-o(1)),
Y m_eff^(1/2)<=Q^(b+theta_eff/2+o(1))<=Q^(1-4eta+o(1)),
U<=Q^(1-a+o(1))<=Q^(theta_eff-4eta+o(1))<m_eff,
and
Y<=Q^(theta_eff-4eta+o(1))<m_eff/4
for sufficiently large Q. Thus fact b390149c13836271 applies, with delta=eta after absorbing the o(1) endpoint losses, and gives Q^(1-eta+o(1)). The original W is exactly its BV product weight, and the gate (q,nc)=1 factors between the two grouped variables.

Now suppose the box has no subset scale in [Q^a,Q^b]. Choose P as in the statement. Then P<Q^a. Every Möbius-bearing factor d_i lies in the carrier. Indeed, if one were omitted, adjoining it would produce a larger subset scale still at most
Q^(a+c_0+o(1))/16<=Q^(b+o(1))/16;
for large Q this contradicts maximality. Unit factors are included by the deterministic inclusion-maximal tie-break. If y>1 is any omitted factor, maximality gives Py>Q^(b-o(1)); since P<Q^(a+o(1)),
y>Q^(b-a-o(1)).                                                 (7)
Only the u_r factors in (6) are unweighted, proving the coefficient assertions.

If exactly one nonunit free factor B is omitted, the carrier has scale A with AB comparable to Q and A<Q^(a+o(1)); hence
B>Q^(1-a-o(1)).                                                 (8)
We check the Type-I tail condition. If a=1-theta_eff+4eta, then
1-a-theta_eff/2=theta_eff/2-4eta>eta.
If a=2eta, then
1-a-theta_eff/2>=2/5-2eta>eta.
Thus (8) implies
B>=m_eff^(1/2)Q^(eta+o(1)).                                     (9)
Also m_eff>=Q^(1/2+kappa). Apply fact 9be4b1c96a2620dc with X=Q. Its complete-period and incomplete-tail terms both save at least Q^(-eta+o(1)), proving the bound in (ii).

If the box is neither (i) nor (ii), at least two nonunit factors are omitted. Equations (7) and the preceding carrier argument prove exactly (iii). Summing the Q^o(1) paid boxes preserves Q^(1-eta+o(1)). Fact 79ffbcb2ffe4049f identifies (3) as the required one-row shape but does not pay the remaining classes, proving every final scope statement.

glossary.composite-Möbius multi-free residual: A finite truncated-inverse factor box in which every Möbius-bearing factor lies in one short carrier and at least two fixed-power unweighted factors remain outside it.
glossary.theta_eff: The exponent log(m_eff)/log(Q) of the effective reciprocal modulus.

df4b02d6fa1181f0.title: BUFFER-EXTENDED COMPLETE-FREQUENCY RAISED-STOPPING B TRACE. Fix integers J,C_A>=1 and 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100 and beta_1=6/5-3sigma, and let 1<=beta<=beta_1. For Q sufficiently large put B=Q^beta, H_T=B/Q, L=H_T Q^sigma, S_0=H_T^2 Q^(3sigma), and Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma). Use the exact raised-stopping coefficient Gamma_{k;L,S_0} of fact 6414b11506a84ff0
df4b02d6fa1181f0.author: slava chan
df4b02d6fa1181f0.statement:
BUFFER-EXTENDED COMPLETE-FREQUENCY RAISED-STOPPING B TRACE. Fix integers J,C_A>=1 and 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100 and beta_1=6/5-3sigma, and let 1<=beta<=beta_1. For Q sufficiently large put B=Q^beta, H_T=B/Q, L=H_T Q^sigma, S_0=H_T^2 Q^(3sigma), and Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma). Use the exact raised-stopping coefficient Gamma_{k;L,S_0} of fact 6414b11506a84ff0.

For each integer k>=2 and each pair of dyadic scales U,Y for which there are integers u,y with U<=u<2U, Y<=y<2Y, B<=uy<2B, and Gamma_{k;L,S_0}(y) nonzero, let c_q be coefficients of absolute value at most one on Q<=q<2Q, let V_q be an arbitrary unit modulo q, and let A be a fixed nonzero integer with |A|<=Q^(C_A). On every dyadic integer frequency block F<=|h|<2F with F>=1, use divisor-bounded coefficients in h and the exact separated stopping coefficients
(-1)^k mu(u) 1_{j_I(u)=0}/binom(k+omega_L(u),k)
and Gamma_{k;L,S_0}(y), subject to gcd(uy,q)=gcd(u,y)=1. Allow a fixed-complexity uniformly scaled-smooth amplitude in q/Q, |h|/F, u/U, y/Y and a scalar omega_F such that, for every fixed integer J_0>=1, there is a constant C(J_0) with
|omega_F|<=C(J_0) min(1,(F/H_P)^(-J_0)).
Use the literal prefactor H_P^(-1) and phase e_q(A V_q h (uy)^(-1)). Sum over both signs of h and all nonempty k,U,Y,F blocks.

(i) If G>=1 and H_P=H_T/G, the complete sum is O(G Q^(2-delta_1)) for some fixed delta_1>0.

(ii) Fix 0<eta<sigma. If Q^(-sigma+eta)<=G<=Q^(sigma-eta) and H_P=H_T/G, the complete sum is O(Q^(2-delta_2)) for some fixed delta_2>0.

Both estimates are uniform in the displayed one-variable coefficients, the choice of V_q, nonunit A, whether H_P is below one, and polylogarithmically many inherited source, fixed-U, high, parent, sign and dyadic labels that act as label scalars.
