They are also uniform under restrictions absorbable into the displayed one-variable coefficient families or into a fixed-complexity amplitude having uniformly bounded projective Fourier norm. No arbitrary joint deletion mask is allowed. The theorem estimates only the raised-stopping B anatomy and asserts no interval-prime A, C1, C2, C3, later-beta, endpoint, PMD, logical bad-N, or Goldbach conclusion.
df4b02d6fa1181f0.proof:
We first verify the marker geometry in the enlarged range without invoking the old beta_0 cutoff. Since H_T=Q^(beta-1)>=1,
S_0/L=H_T Q^(2sigma)>=1,
so 2<=L<=S_0 for large Q. Also
log_Q(Z/L)=5/2-2beta-4sigma
 >=5/2-2(6/5-3sigma)-4sigma
 =1/10+2sigma>0.
Moreover
log_Q(B/S_0)=2-beta-3sigma
 >=2-(6/5-3sigma)-3sigma=4/5>0,
and
log_Q(Z^4/B)=6-5beta-12sigma
 >=6-5(6/5-3sigma)-12sigma=3sigma>0.
Thus every squarefree marked integer in [B,2B) satisfies the hypotheses of fact 6414b11506a84ff0 for sufficiently large Q, and its stopping factor y satisfies
S_0<y<=S_0 L.                                                     (1)

If Y<=y<2Y, then y>S_0 and Q^sigma>=2 give
Y>y/2>S_0/2>=H_T^2 Q^(2sigma).                                  (2)
Also Y<=y<=S_0 L. The logarithmic gap between Q^(1-2sigma)/H_T^2 and S_0 L equals
6-5beta-6sigma
 >=6-5(6/5-3sigma)-6sigma=9sigma>0.                              (3)
Therefore
H_T^2 Q^(2sigma)<=Y<=Q^(1-2sigma)/H_T^2.                         (4)
Because B<=uy<2B and u<2U,y<2Y,
B/4<UY<2B=2QH_T.                                                 (5)

We next separate the exact stopping coefficient and smooth amplitude. The factor
alpha_u=(-1)^k mu(u)1_{j_I(u)=0}/binom(k+omega_L(u),k)
has absolute value at most one, and
beta_y=Gamma_{k;L,S_0}(y)
lies in [0,1]. Expand the uniformly scaled-smooth four-variable amplitude on a fixed logarithmic torus. Repeated integration by parts gives a Fourier series whose one-variable factors have absolute value at most one and whose coefficient l1 norm is bounded uniformly. Absorb the one-variable factors into c_q, the h coefficient, alpha_u and beta_y. A restriction allowed in the statement is, by definition, already absorbed into these same one-variable factors or has a uniformly bounded projective Fourier decomposition and is treated by the identical expansion. Thus it suffices to estimate separated blocks with the exact additional condition gcd(u,y)=1.

Define the following four algebraic baseline expressions:
E_1=G^(1/4)Q^2 H_T^(1/2)Y^(-1/4),
E_2=G^(1/4)Q^(7/4)H_T^(1/2)Y^(1/4),
E_3=Q^2 H_T Y^(-1/2),
E_4=Q^(7/4)H_T.                                                   (6)
No analytic theorem is applied at frequency H_P in this definition.

We now estimate each actual integer frequency block. Put
u_F=F/H_P and G_F=H_T/F=G/u_F.
Apply fact 95626318cdcc099f with its frequency parameter equal to F, factor scales S=Y,T=U, product relation (5), model frequency H_T and imbalance G_F. This is a valid application because F>=1, H_T>=1, U>=1 and Y>=1. It permits the arbitrary unit V_q, fixed nonzero possibly nonunit A, unrestricted gcd(h,q), and the exact joint coprimality condition. Its normalized prefactor is F^(-1), so replacing it by the literal H_P^(-1) multiplies the bound by u_F. Since G_F^(1/4)=G^(1/4)u_F^(-1/4), the first two terms are bounded by
Q^epsilon |omega_F|u_F^(3/4)E_1
and
Q^epsilon |omega_F|u_F^(3/4)E_2,                                (7)
while the last two are bounded by
Q^epsilon |omega_F|u_F E_3
and
Q^epsilon |omega_F|u_F E_4.                                     (8)
Here the factor Q^epsilon may be enlarged uniformly: H_P,U,Y and |A| are bounded by fixed powers of Q, and the F^epsilon part of the cited estimate is u_F^epsilon times another fixed Q-power epsilon loss.

Sum (7)-(8) over dyadic F. If F<=H_P, then u_F<=1, |omega_F| is bounded, and both u_F^(3/4) and u_F are at most one; there are O(log Q) such blocks because H_P is polynomially bounded. If F>H_P, choose J_0>4 in the available decay estimate. Then, even after the additional u_F^epsilon factor, the dyadic sums of
|omega_F|u_F^(3/4+epsilon)
and
|omega_F|u_F^(1+epsilon)
converge. If H_P<1 there are no blocks with F<=H_P, so the same second sum covers every actual integer frequency without applying any theorem below frequency one. Consequently the complete frequency sum is
O(Q^epsilon(E_1+E_2+E_3+E_4)).                                  (9)

For (i), divide (6) by GQ^2. By the lower and upper bounds in (4), the four ratios are at most
G^(-3/4)Q^(-sigma/2),
G^(-3/4)Q^(-sigma/2),
G^(-1)Q^(-sigma),
G^(-1)Q^(beta-5/4).                                               (10)
Since G>=1 and beta<=6/5-3sigma, every ratio in (10) saves a fixed power; the fourth is at most Q^(-1/20-3sigma).

For (ii), divide (6) by Q^2. The four ratios are at most
G^(1/4)Q^(-sigma/2),
G^(1/4)Q^(-sigma/2),
Q^(-sigma),
Q^(beta-5/4).                                                      (11)
The upper bound G<=Q^(sigma-eta) makes the first two at most Q^(-sigma/4-eta/4), while the fourth is at most Q^(-1/20-3sigma). Hence (11) also has a fixed power saving.

Finally, Gamma_{k;L,S_0}(y) nonzero implies 2^k<=y<2B, so k=O(log Q). The k,U,Y, sign, torus-Fourier and explicitly allowed inherited label families are polylogarithmically numerous. Choose epsilon sufficiently small and absorb these counts into half of the fixed margins in (10)-(11). This gives fixed delta_1,delta_2>0 and proves both assertions with exactly the stated restriction class.

glossary.C(J_0): The fixed Fourier-decay constant at order J_0.
glossary.E_1: The first algebraic baseline expression in the complete-frequency estimate.
glossary.E_2: The second algebraic baseline expression in the complete-frequency estimate.
glossary.E_3: The third algebraic baseline expression in the complete-frequency estimate.
glossary.E_4: The fourth algebraic baseline expression in the complete-frequency estimate.
glossary.G_F: The effective imbalance H_T/F on a dyadic frequency block.
glossary.c_q: The bounded coefficient on the reciprocal modulus q.

df9748efe29ab475.title: Fix constants c_0,C_0,c_1,C_1>0 and η_0>0. Let x≥2, let N be an integer with c_0x≤N≤C_0x, and let D,M,R,K be positive real numbers satisfying c_1x≤DM,RK≤C_1x. Let 𝒲 be a fixed C^∞ function supported where each of its four positive coordinates lies in [1/2,2], with all scaled derivatives bounded. Define
df9748efe29ab475.author: slava chan
df9748efe29ab475.statement:
Fix constants c_0,C_0,c_1,C_1>0 and η_0>0. Let x≥2, let N be an integer with c_0x≤N≤C_0x, and let D,M,R,K be positive real numbers satisfying c_1x≤DM,RK≤C_1x. Let 𝒲 be a fixed C^∞ function supported where each of its four positive coordinates lies in [1/2,2], with all scaled derivatives bounded. Define
𝒬_N(D,M;R,K)
=Σ_{dm+rk=N} μ(d)μ(r)log(m)log(k)
 𝒲(d/D,m/M,r/R,k/K).

There is a Poisson decomposition 𝒬_N=𝒬_N^(0)+𝒬_N^(≠0) such that, uniformly in N and the scales, for every ε>0:
if R≥D, then
|𝒬_N^(≠0)|≪_ε x^ε[M^(3/20)D^(17/20)R^(19/20)+D^(7/8)R];
if R≤D, then
|𝒬_N^(≠0)|≪_ε x^ε[M^(3/20)D^(11/10)R^(7/10)+DR^(7/8)].
If max(D,R)≥x^(η_0), then for every A>0,
|𝒬_N^(0)|≪_{A,η_0}x(log x)^(-A).

Consequently:

(1) Fix σ>0. If max(D,R)≥x^(η_0) and either
R≤D, D^19R^14≤x^(17-σ), D^8R^7≤x^(8-σ),
or
R>D, D^14R^19≤x^(17-σ), D^7R^8≤x^(8-σ),
then
|𝒬_N(D,M;R,K)|≪_{A,σ}x^(1-3σ/80)+x(log x)^(-A).

(2) Fix σ>0. If max(D,R)≥x^(η_0) and R/M≤x^(-σ), then for every A>0,
|𝒬_N(D,M;R,K)|≪_{A,σ}x(log x)^(-A).

Now specialize the exact fixed-N source setup of facts 0880dc648c429047 and 91db48815d136d4c by choosing W, ψ, and Φ to be C^∞ functions satisfying their stated hypotheses, and impose X_bal≥4D_*. On every label in the base sets 𝒜_FT or 𝒜_UBC, D>X_bal and hence every d in the dyadic support satisfies d≥D/2>2D_*, so ψ(d/D_*)=1. The resulting joint weight is of the preceding C^∞ type. Set σ equal to the parameter η in fact 91db48815d136d4c. Then, for every A>0, the total contribution C_N^DIR of all base 𝒜_FT and 𝒜_UBC labels satisfies
|C_N^DIR|≪_{A,η}x^(1-η/40)+x(log x)^(-A).
This is uniform in the fixed even integer N. It controls the direct FT/UBC part of C_N; no balanced 𝒜_bal or swap-mirror estimate is asserted.
df9748efe29ab475.proof:
Put g=gcd(d,r). A nonzero summand has g|N. Write d=ga, r=gb, and L=N/g. The Möbius factors imply gcd(a,b)=1 whenever they are nonzero. The equation is
am+bk=L.
For fixed g,a,b, Poisson summation in the progression m≡La^(-1) modulo b gives a zero frequency and nonzero frequencies. This defines 𝒬_N^(0) and 𝒬_N^(≠0).

The natural nonzero frequency length is H=R/(gM). On a positive dyadic h-block the three Bettin--Chandee lengths are H,D/g,R/g and the phase parameter is the nonzero integer L. On a negative block use |h| and phase parameter -L. Smooth Fourier expansion on the fixed compact scaled support separates the joint amplitude with bounded projective norm; the logarithms cost only powers of log x, absorbed by x^ε. The Poisson prefactor and the three coefficient ℓ2 norms combine to
[M/(R/g)]·[(D/g)(R/g)H]^(1/2)=(DM/g)^(1/2).
The phase amplifier is bounded because
1+|L|H/[(D/g)(R/g)]=1+N/(DM)≪1.

Bettin and Chandee, arXiv:1502.00769, Theorem 1, states the following for a nonzero integer θ. For arbitrary coefficients on dyadic intervals of lengths A_1,M_1,N_1,
|Σ_{a,m,n;(m,n)=1}ν_aα_mβ_n exp(2πiθa m^(-1)/n)|
≪||ν||_2||α||_2||β||_2
(1+|θ|A_1/(M_1N_1))^(1/2)
[(A_1M_1N_1)^(7/20+ε)(M_1+N_1)^(1/4)
 +(A_1M_1N_1)^(3/8+ε)(A_1N_1+A_1M_1)^(1/8)].
Apply it separately to positive and negative frequency blocks with
(A_1,M_1,N_1,θ)=(H,D/g,R/g,L)
and
(H,D/g,R/g,-L).
If R≥D, simplifying the two terms gives
g^(-9/5)M^(3/20)D^(17/20)R^(19/20)
and
g^(-15/8)D^(7/8)R.
If R≤D, it gives
g^(-9/5)M^(3/20)D^(11/10)R^(7/10)
and
g^(-15/8)DR^(7/8).
Both g-exponents are below -1, so summing over g|N proves the nonzero-frequency bounds.

If H<1, use actual frequency blocks |h| comparable to T≥1. Repeated integration by parts in the C^∞ m-weight gives (1+T/H)^(-J) for arbitrary fixed J. Replacing H by T in the coefficient norms, Bettin--Chandee factors, and phase amplifier costs at most (T/H)^(3/2+ε). Choose J>3 and sum T dyadically. This proves the same formal-H bounds without applying the external theorem to an interval of length below one.

For zero frequency, fix g and perform the same bounded-projective smooth separation. If g≤x^(η_0/2), at least one of D/g,R/g is at least x^(η_0/2). If D/g is long, fix b and sum a. Since μ(ga) is nonzero only when gcd(a,g)=1 and then equals μ(g)μ(a), while gcd(a,b)=1, the running coefficient is μ(a)1_{(a,bg)=1}. Fact 71389b22e6f49e13, with coprimality integer bg of polynomial size, gives arbitrary logarithmic saving for this smooth a-sum. If R/g is long, fix a and apply the same fact to μ(b)1_{(b,ag)=1}. All separated modes have uniformly bounded total variation, so summing them preserves the saving.

If g>x^(η_0/2), bound the zero-frequency term trivially. The Poisson factor 1/b, the m-integral of length M, and the numbers of a,b give O(x(log x)^C/g) at fixed g. Since g|N,
Σ_{g|N,g>x^(η_0/2)}1/g≤x^(-η_0/2)τ(N)≤x^(-η_0/3)
for sufficiently large x. This is smaller than every x(log x)^(-A). The zero-frequency estimate follows.

For consequence (1), use M comparable to x/D. In the case R≤D, the first polytope inequality makes the first nonzero term at most x^(1-σ/20+ε), and the second makes the second term at most x^(1-σ/8+ε). The R>D case is the same calculation with the displayed exchanged powers. Choose ε=σ/80. Both terms are then O(x^(1-3σ/80)); adding zero frequency proves (1).

For consequence (2), return to the Poisson formula. At fixed g, arbitrary J integrations by parts and absolute summation over h≠0 give
O_J(x(log x)^C g^(-J-1)(R/M)^J).
Since R/M≤x^(-σ), choose J so large that this is O(x(log x)^(-A)) after summing g|N. Add the zero-frequency bound.

In the source specialization, X_bal≥4D_* and D>X_bal imply d≥D/2>2D_*, hence ψ=1. Because DM and RK are comparable to x on every nonzero label by fact cdb5cefbc7333591, W(dm/x) and the dyadic cutoffs give an admissible fixed scaled-smooth joint weight. The same fact gives at most
(ceil(log_2x)+4)^4
active four-variable labels. Apply consequence (2) to 𝒜_FT and consequence (1), with σ=η, to 𝒜_UBC. For the latter, the per-label power is x^(1-3η/80); for sufficiently large x the fourth logarithmic power is at most x^(η/80), leaving x^(1-η/40). For zero-frequency and FT terms, invoke the per-label bound with A replaced by A+5 before summing. This proves the stated C_N^DIR estimate.

glossary.C_N^DIR: the aggregate contribution of the base Fourier-tail and UBC labels
glossary.H: the natural Poisson dual length R/(gM)
glossary.L: the integer N/g after the gcd split
glossary.η_0: a fixed lower exponent for at least one long divisor interval
glossary.σ: the fixed FT or UBC power-saving buffer
glossary.𝒬_N(D,M;R,K): the general fixed-N smooth double-Möbius block
glossary.𝒲: a fixed scaled-smooth compactly supported joint weight

df97bf1eba0495be.title: SIMULTANEOUS C4 ACTIVE-PRIME TENSOR GRAM AND SQUARE-DIVISOR EXCEPTIONAL PRODUCT
df97bf1eba0495be.author: slava chan
df97bf1eba0495be.statement:
SIMULTANEOUS C4 ACTIVE-PRIME TENSOR GRAM AND SQUARE-DIVISOR EXCEPTIONAL PRODUCT.

Let r be a squarefree positive integer. Let n,n' be squarefree positive integers such that
r divides gcd(n,n'),   gcd(r,n/r)=gcd(r,n'/r)=1.                      (1)
Let A,h,h' be integers such that
gcd(Ahh',r)=1.                                                        (2)
For every prime p|r define functions on F_p by
g_{p;n,h}(x)=0 if x=0, and
g_{p;n,h}(x)=e_p(Ah(n/p)^(-1)x^(-1)) if x!=0,                         (3)
and define g_{p;n',h'} by replacing n,h with n',h'. Let their normalized additive Fourier transforms be
ghat_{p;n,h}(rho)=p^(-1)sum_{x in F_p}g_{p;n,h}(x)e_p(-rho x),         (4)
and similarly for n',h'.

Define the simultaneous all-active mixed-dual Gram
G_r(n,h;n',h')
 =sum_{(rho_p): rho_p in F_p^* for every p|r}
   product_{p|r} ghat_{p;n,h}(rho_p)
   overline{ghat_{p;n',h'}(rho_p)}.                                  (5)
Put
E=hn'-h'n,
s=s(r,E)=product_{p|r, p^2|E}p.                                      (6)
Then
G_r(n,h;n',h')=product_{p|r} gamma_p,                                 (7)
where
gamma_p=(p-1)/p-p^(-2) if p^2|E,
gamma_p=-p^(-1)-p^(-2) if p^2 does not divide E.                      (8)
Consequently
|G_r(n,h;n',h')| <=2^{omega(r)} s/r.                                 (9)
If E!=0, then s^2|E. If r and |E| are bounded by a fixed power of Q, fact e705401df9f0709e gives
|G_r(n,h;n',h')| <<_epsilon Q^epsilon s/r.                           (10)
If E=0, then s=r and
G_r(n,h;n',h')=product_{p|r}((p-1)/p-p^(-2)).                         (11)

In a literal same-target C4 centered CRT face, r may be taken as the product of its active primes common to the two compared rows. Equations (7)-(10) show that every nonexceptional active prime contributes its reciprocal factor simultaneously, while the complete loss is confined to the square-divisor product s. This is a local tensor Gram identity and bound only. It does not assemble varying active products, bound the literal weighted E=0 or E!=0 row sums, estimate a proper centered face, prove NR-DIL, or imply Goldbach.
df97bf1eba0495be.proof:
The sum in (5) is over the Cartesian product of the nonzero dual groups. Therefore finite distributivity factors it exactly:
G_r(n,h;n',h')
 =product_{p|r}
   sum_{rho in F_p^*}ghat_{p;n,h}(rho)
   overline{ghat_{p;n',h'}(rho)}.                                   (12)

Fix p|r. The two local rows in (3) have the same target multiplier A, which is a common unit modulo p by (2). Fact 3d10fd30e2a42246 gives their mixed-dual Gram as
(p-1)/p-p^(-2)
when their local slopes agree and as
-p^(-1)-p^(-2)
otherwise. The slope agreement is
Ah(n/p)^(-1)=Ah'(n'/p)^(-1) modulo p.                                (13)
Cancel A and multiply by the two unit cofactors. This is
h(n'/p)=h'(n/p) modulo p.                                           (14)

Write n=pu and n'=pu', where u=n/p and u'=n'/p are integers and units modulo p by (1) and squarefreeness. Then
E=hn'-h'n=p(hu'-h'u).                                                (15)
Equation (14) is precisely p|(hu'-h'u). By (15), this is equivalent to p^2|E. Thus the local factors in (12) are exactly (8), proving (7). Fact 67d49768ecdc058e is the narrower literal C4 specialization of this same equivalence.

For a collision prime, the first quantity in (8) has absolute value at most one. For a noncollision prime,
|p^(-1)+p^(-2)|<=2/p.
The product of all noncollision primes is r/s. Hence (7) gives
|G_r|<=product_{p|r,p^2 not dividing E}(2/p)
 <=2^{omega(r)}s/r,
which is (9).

The primes in s are distinct because r is squarefree, and every one has square dividing E. Therefore s^2|E when E!=0. Also 2^{omega(r)}<=tau(r). Under the fixed-power envelope, fact e705401df9f0709e supplies tau(r)<<Q^epsilon, yielding (10). If E=0, every p^2 divides E, so s=r and every local factor is the collision value, proving (11). The final specialization and scope statements are direct readings of (5) and do not add an estimate.

glossary.C4 active-prime tensor Gram: The product of the prime-local mixed-mode Grams over one common active CRT face.
glossary.G_r(n,h;n',h'): The simultaneous all-active mixed-dual tensor Gram over the squarefree active prime product r.
glossary.s(r,E): The product of active primes p for which p^2 divides the cross determinant E.

dffb2ec702b7e395.title: CENTERED HC3 IDENTITY FOR THE COMPLETE CRITICAL PROGRESSION DISCREPANCY. Fix one orientation, exact active g,c, and one complete frozen critical source block as in fact c1c141e3d7fb562f. Thus q,kappa range over finite fixed supports, (c,q)=1, (kappa,q)=1, ell is fixed, a_{q,kappa} is the reduced residue ell*kappa^(-1) modulo q, and w_{q,kappa}(n) is the complete literal physical amplitude excluding mu(n) and exact unit conditions. Define
dffb2ec702b7e395.author: slava chan
dffb2ec702b7e395.statement:
CENTERED HC3 IDENTITY FOR THE COMPLETE CRITICAL PROGRESSION DISCREPANCY. Fix one orientation, exact active g,c, and one complete frozen critical source block as in fact c1c141e3d7fb562f. Thus q,kappa range over finite fixed supports, (c,q)=1, (kappa,q)=1, ell is fixed, a_{q,kappa} is the reduced residue ell*kappa^(-1) modulo q, and w_{q,kappa}(n) is the complete literal physical amplitude excluding mu(n) and exact unit conditions. Define
D_{q,kappa}^{(c)}=sum_{n congruent to a_{q,kappa} mod q,(n,c)=1}mu(n)w_{q,kappa}(n)
 -phi(q)^(-1)sum_{(n,qc)=1}mu(n)w_{q,kappa}(n).

Let 1<Y<Z. For positive d<=m put omega_diag(d,m)=2 if d<m and omega_diag(d,d)=1. Define
H_{q,kappa}^{small}=sum_{d<=m,d<Y} omega_diag(d,m)rho_{1/2}(d)rho_{1/2}(m)1_{(dm,c)=1}w_{q,kappa}(dm)
 times [1_{dm congruent to a_{q,kappa} mod q}-phi(q)^(-1)1_{(dm,q)=1}],
H_{q,kappa}^{med} by the same formula with Y<=d<=Z, and H_{q,kappa}^{LL} by the same formula with d>Z. Then exactly
D_{q,kappa}^{(c)}=H_{q,kappa}^{small}+H_{q,kappa}^{med}+H_{q,kappa}^{LL}.
In H_{q,kappa}^{LL}, both d and m exceed Z. Every q,kappa-dependent physical weight remains evaluated at n=dm and t=(ell-kappa dm)/q on the physical congruence; no condition (d,m)=1 and no squarefree condition on d,m is inserted.

Consequently the complete fixed-g,c centered AP block
mu(c)sum_{q,kappa}mu(q)D_{q,kappa}^{(c)}
is exactly the sum of the corresponding three HC3 blocks. If, uniformly in every fixed literal label, each of those three summed blocks is O_A(BK_c(log B)^(-A)) for every A>0, then their complete fixed-g,c AP block has the same bound after decreasing A by a fixed amount. This is only an exact reduction and conditional consumer statement; no estimate for any H block is asserted.
dffb2ec702b7e395.proof:
By fact 5999a1878276ac78, for every positive integer n,
mu(n)=sum_{dm=n}rho_{1/2}(d)rho_{1/2}(m),
with no coprimality condition on d,m. Insert this identity into both finite n-sums defining D_{q,kappa}^{(c)} and interchange finite sums.

In the physical sum, n congruent to the reduced residue a_{q,kappa} modulo q implies gcd(n,q)=1. Hence its exact unit conditions can be written as
1_{(dm,c)=1}1_{dm congruent to a_{q,kappa} mod q}.
In the principal sum, the condition gcd(n,qc)=1 becomes
1_{(dm,c)=1}1_{(dm,q)=1}.
Thus their difference is the unrestricted ordered sum over d,m of rho_{1/2}(d)rho_{1/2}(m) times the common literal amplitude and the bracket displayed in the statement.

For fixed product dm, the complete summand is invariant under interchanging d and m: the rho product is symmetric, the unit indicators and congruence depend only on dm, and w_{q,kappa} is evaluated only at dm. Therefore the ordered sum over all d,m equals the sum over d<=m with multiplicity two off the diagonal and multiplicity one on the diagonal, which is omega_diag(d,m).

The conditions d<Y, Y<=d<=Z, and d>Z are disjoint and exhaustive, including both endpoints in the middle range. Splitting the fundamental-domain sum by these conditions gives the asserted identity. On d<=m, the final condition d>Z implies m>=d>Z, so H^{LL} is genuinely both-large.

On the physical congruence q divides ell-kappa dm, so t=(ell-kappa dm)/q is the same integer physical complement as in facts c1c141e3d7fb562f and 876e206eb9190ca9. The latter fact proves that every physical factor and mask is retained at n=dm,t and that neither gcd(d,m)=1 nor squarefreeness may be added. This proves the literal-scope assertions.

Multiplying the identity by mu(c)mu(q), summing the finite q,kappa supports, and using the triangle inequality proves the conditional final statement. Three fixed contributions and the fixed number of literal label families cost only a fixed logarithmic exponent, absorbed by requesting the input bounds with a correspondingly larger A. No analytic estimate was used.

glossary.H_{q,kappa}^{LL}: The centered fundamental-domain HALF-CONV block with both factors above Z.
glossary.H_{q,kappa}^{med}: The centered fundamental-domain HALF-CONV block with smaller factor in the closed interval [Y,Z].
glossary.H_{q,kappa}^{small}: The centered fundamental-domain HALF-CONV block with smaller factor below Y.

e035633108f2b250.title: EXACT FULL-pd CRT FUSION OF THE ROW-ONE ADDITIVE SUBFACES IN BOTH LITERAL CROSS-INCIDENCE MAIN FACES
e035633108f2b250.author: slava chan
e035633108f2b250.statement:
EXACT FULL-pd CRT FUSION OF THE ROW-ONE ADDITIVE SUBFACES IN BOTH LITERAL CROSS-INCIDENCE MAIN FACES.

Let p be a prime, let s_1 be squarefree with (p,s_1)=1, and write
 s_1=dk
for a divisor d|s_1. Let N,n_1,n_2,q_2 be integers satisfying
 (Nn_1,s_1)=(Nn_1n_2q_2,p)=1.
Put n_i=au_i with (a,p)=1, and define nonzero residues modulo p by
 A=N(u_1s_1)^(-1), D=N(u_2q_2)^(-1).                       (1)
Then
 A a^(-1)=N(n_1dk)^(-1),
 D a^(-1)=N(n_2q_2)^(-1) modulo p.                          (2)

Define the row-one additive d-phase
 E_d=e_d(N[pkn_1]^(-1)).                                    (3)
Then exactly
 E_d e_p((A-D)a^(-1))
 =e_{pd}(N[n_1k]^(-1))e_p(-N[n_2q_2]^(-1)).                 (4)
Denote the right side of (4) by cal E_{pd}. Thus the A-half of the coefficient-one p-difference phase fuses with every selected row-one additive denominator d into one full modulus pd; the D-half remains the displayed row-two p-phase.

For
 rho_p(H;a)=e_p(Ha^(-1))+1/(p-1) when H is nonzero and
 rho_p(0;a)=0,
one also has exactly
 1_{A!=D} E_d rho_p(A-D;a)
 =1_{A!=D}{cal E_{pd}+E_d/(p-1)}.                           (5)

Now use the literal notation of fact b9560e346963b9e0. Expand its row-one tensor C_1 by equation (13) of fact 55c6f91ec7fd414f. For every parent h and selected d|h, put k=s_1/d. The selected additive phase is (3). Consequently, after this exact expansion, the exponential term in the H_2 face and the exponential part of the off-diagonal J_2 face both have the common carrier cal E_{pd}, with the same literal beta coefficient, both gamma coefficients, the same parent/subface coefficient, and respectively the unchanged conjugate H_2 or J_2 tensor. The only additional term arising from rho_p in the J_2 face is the explicit 1/(p-1) correction in (5).

No estimate for the fused carrier aggregate, the 1/(p-1) correction, LIT-INC-VLS, K_inc^rem, another incidence cell, C_small or Goldbach is asserted.
e035633108f2b250.proof:
Equation (2) follows immediately from n_i=au_i and s_1=dk. Indeed, modulo p,
 A a^(-1)
 =N(u_1s_1)^(-1)a^(-1)
 =N(au_1s_1)^(-1)
 =N(n_1dk)^(-1),
and the same calculation gives the formula for D.

We prove (4) prime by prime. The p-local component of
 e_{pd}(N[n_1k]^(-1))
is
 e_p(N[n_1k]^(-1)d^(-1))
 =e_p(N[n_1dk]^(-1)).                                      (6)
Its d-local component is
 e_d(N[n_1k]^(-1)p^(-1))
 =e_d(N[pkn_1]^(-1))=E_d.                                  (7)
Because p and d are coprime, CRT says that the product of (6) and (7) is the full phase e_{pd}(N[n_1k]^(-1)). By (2),
 e_p((A-D)a^(-1))
 =e_p(N[n_1dk]^(-1))e_p(-N[n_2q_2]^(-1)).
Multiplication with (7) and the CRT identity prove (4).

If A!=D, expand rho_p by its definition:
 E_d rho_p(A-D;a)
 =E_d e_p((A-D)a^(-1))+E_d/(p-1).
Insert (4). If A=D, both sides of (5) vanish because of the common indicator. This proves (5).

It remains to identify the literal application. Equation (13) of fact 55c6f91ec7fd414f expands every centered parent face in C_1 into additive phases
 e_d(M_1[n_1(s_1/d)]^(-1)).
Equation (6) of fact d9c3f37492846fce, applied with k=s_1/d, identifies this phase with E_d in (3). Fact b9560e346963b9e0 defines its two main local factors as
 e_p((A-D)a^(-1)) overline(H_2)
and
 1_{A!=D}rho_p(A-D;a)overline(J_2).
Apply (4) to the first and (5) to the second. No coefficient or tensor outside the displayed local factors is changed, proving the common-carrier assertion and every scope restriction.

glossary.cal E_{pd}: the fused coefficient-one inverse carrier of modulus pd
glossary.k: the full row-one cofactor s_1/d of a selected additive denominator d

e039a05efe9baf29.title: UNIT-RAY-HARD-ABS: ABSOLUTE PHYSICAL-OCCUPANCY PAYMENT FOR THE COMPLETE HARD UNIT-DENOMINATOR FORM
e039a05efe9baf29.author: slava chan
e039a05efe9baf29.statement:
UNIT-RAY-HARD-ABS: ABSOLUTE PHYSICAL-OCCUPANCY PAYMENT FOR THE COMPLETE HARD UNIT-DENOMINATOR FORM.

Adopt the exact hard good-W ray-pair form of fact cff9d29efb555b8e in one fixed orientation, anatomy, source/projective fibre, frequency block
1<=F<=x^3
and dilator block
Dcal<=d_lambda<2Dcal.
Put T=mathscr A, where mathscr A is the fixed nonzero target in that fact. Restrict the hard form to the unit-denominator rays
R=(epsilon,1,b), R'=(epsilon',1,b').
Retain every exact condition, in particular R!=R', m_d>L, d_lambda not dividing T Delta_0, and every inherited pair-dependent selector. Denote this complete restriction by H_C^unit. Then
|H_C^unit|
 <=x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 B F^2.                                  (UNIT-RAY-HARD-ABS)
If 2F<=Q, then H_C^unit=0.

Consequently, for every fixed A>0, the complete hard unit-ray restriction is at the canonical scale
x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 BQ^2F^2/Dcal
throughout
Dcal<=Q^2(log(2x))^A.                                           (1)
This conclusion has no primality assumption on
rho_lambda=d_lambda/gcd(d_lambda,T)
and no additional chamber condition. Beyond (1), the exact loss of this absolute physical-occupancy argument relative to the canonical scale is Dcal/Q^2.

This proves only the complete hard unit-denominator subfamily. It proves no estimate for pairs with aa'>1, no P-qSRC-SUP, no C-qSRC-SUP, no full GA-RAY-SPEC, no tail payment, and no Goldbach conclusion.
e039a05efe9baf29.proof:
Fact cff9d29efb555b8e identifies the unit-denominator restriction of the hard form with UNIT-RAY-SRC from fact a36284a9dbec7837, with the additional hard selectors retained. For a unit ray, fact a36284a9dbec7837 gives
B_lambda(epsilon,1,b)
 =sum_{k: c_lambda(k,epsilon k b) nonzero}
   c_lambda(k,epsilon k b).                                    (2)
Thus expanding the two ray coefficients in H_C^unit replaces one retained ordered ray pair by retained ordered physical-coordinate pairs
(q,h)=(k,epsilon k b),
(q',h')=(k',epsilon'k'b').                                    (3)
Every expanded coordinate satisfies q|h and q'|h'. The hard conductor m_d, nonresonance, distinct-ray, and inherited selectors are zero-one functions of the two rays, the copy, and the retained labels. Therefore they select a subset of the expanded ordered coordinate pairs; taking absolute values makes each such selector only delete terms.

By UNIT-RAY-PHYS in fact 10b0cd08eacc17fa, the number N_lambda^unit of supported physical coordinates satisfying q|h in one copy is at most x^{o(1)}F. Hence the number of ordered coordinate pairs that can occur after (3) is at most
(N_lambda^unit)^2<=x^{o(1)}F^2.                                (4)
The proof of fact e55b27d39c593164 shows that, after extracting omega_F, each dimensionless coefficient c_lambda(q,h) on the fixed projective fibre is x^{o(1)}, and that the number of exact copies over n asymptotic to B is Bx^{o(1)}. Absolute summation of the products
|c_lambda(q,h)c_lambda(q',h')|
over the subset selected by the hard form, using (4), therefore gives
|H_C^unit|<=x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2BF^2.
This proves UNIT-RAY-HARD-ABS.

Fact 10b0cd08eacc17fa proves that no supported unit coordinate exists when 2F<=Q, so the hard restriction is then empty.

Finally,
BF^2
 =(Dcal/Q^2)(BQ^2F^2/Dcal).
If Dcal/Q^2 is at most a fixed power of log(2x), this quotient is absorbed by x^{o(1)}, proving (1). No condition on rho_lambda was used, and all stated exclusions follow.

glossary.H_C^unit: The complete hard good-W ray-pair form restricted to unit primitive denominators a=a'=1.
glossary.UNIT-RAY-HARD-ABS: The absolute BF^2 bound for the complete hard unit-denominator form obtained by physical q|h occupancy.

e08b28d0e17e861c.title: LITERAL PHYSICAL-DISPLACEMENT/DUAL-SHIFT DECOMPOSITION OF THE GOOD-\(\mathscr W\) FIXED-\(r\) OFF-DUAL DISCREPANCY
e08b28d0e17e861c.author: slava chan
e08b28d0e17e861c.statement:
LITERAL PHYSICAL-DISPLACEMENT/DUAL-SHIFT DECOMPOSITION OF THE GOOD-\(\mathscr W\) FIXED-\(r\) OFF-DUAL DISCREPANCY.

Let \(r\) be a nonempty squarefree integer. Let \(\mathcal R_r\) be a finite family of forward GA-tail rows with common active product \(r\), contained either in one \(C_\ell\)-anatomy as in fact e2e971fd4983bd94 or in one \(A\)-anatomy and dilator block \([\mathcal D,2\mathcal D)\) as in fact 35e599ec4bc284fe. For every row \(j\in\mathcal R_r\), every \(p\mid r\), and every \(q\) in the literal row support, put
\[
 C_{p,j}\equiv\mathscr A h_j(n_j/p)^{-1}\pmod p,
 \qquad
 f_{p,j}(x)={\bf1}_{x\ne0}e_p(C_{p,j}x^{-1}),
\]
and let
\[
 \widehat f_{p,j}(\rho)
 ={1\over p}\sum_{x\in\mathbb F_p}f_{p,j}(x)e_p(-\rho x).
\]
Thus
\[
 V_{j,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)
 =\prod_{p\mid r}\widehat f_{p,j}(\rho_p),\qquad
 W_{j,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)
 =\sum_qB_{j,r}(q)\chi_{\boldsymbol\rho}(q)
\]
are the exact quantities of fact 0aa821ade9a14b45, with every literal support condition included in \(B_{j,r}\). Extend \(B_{j,r}(q)\) by zero to every integer outside that support. For a complex row array \((c_j)\), let \(\mathcal O_r(c)\) be the exact off-dual discrepancy in equation (6) of fact 9128d43a5ac4e1bb.

For \(p\mid r\), \(C,C'\in\mathbb F_p^\times\), \(t,s\in\mathbb F_p\), define
\[
 \mathcal H_p(C,C';t,s)
 =
 \sum_{\substack{\sigma\in\mathbb F_p\\
                  \sigma\ne0,\ \sigma+t\ne0}}
 \widehat f_C(\sigma+t)
 \overline{\widehat f_{C'}(\sigma)}e_p(\sigma s),                \tag{1}
\]
where \(\widehat f_C\) is the normalized transform above. For
\(\boldsymbol t=(t_p)_{p\mid r}\) and an integer \(s\), put
\[
 \mathcal H_r(j,k;\boldsymbol t,s)
 =\prod_{p\mid r}
 \mathcal H_p(C_{p,j},C_{p,k};t_p,s\bmod p),                     \tag{2}
\]
and
\[
 \chi_{\boldsymbol t}(q)=\prod_{p\mid r}e_p(t_pq).
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal O_r(c)
 ={}&
 \sum_{\substack{\boldsymbol t\in\prod_{p\mid r}\mathbb F_p\\
                  \boldsymbol t\ne\boldsymbol0}}
 \sum_{j,k\in\mathcal R_r}c_j\overline{c_k}
 \sum_{s\in\mathbb Z}\sum_{q\in\mathbb Z}
 B_{j,r}(q+s)\overline{B_{k,r}(q)}
 \chi_{\boldsymbol t}(q+s)
 \mathcal H_r(j,k;\boldsymbol t,s).
                                                                    \tag{3}
 \end{aligned}}
\]
Because the \(B\)'s are zero-extended, (3) is finite and retains exactly the two original intervals, coprimality conditions, marker weights, Möbius factors, physical Fourier amplitudes, target-gcd, fixed-\(U\), high, parent, ordering, equality, collision, deletion and provenance masks. No absolute value has been taken in any variable in (3).

The local kernel has
\[
 \mathcal F_p(C,C';t,s)
 ={1\over p}
 \sum_{\substack{y\in\mathbb F_p\\y\ne0,\ y+s\ne0}}
 e_p\!\left(C(y+s)^{-1}-C'y^{-1}-t(y+s)\right),                 \tag{4}
\]
and
\[
 \mathcal H_p(C,C';0,s)
 =\mathcal F_p(C,C';0,s)-p^{-2},                                \tag{5}
\]
while, for \(t\ne0\),
\[
 \mathcal H_p(C,C';t,s)
 =\mathcal F_p(C,C';t,s)
 +p^{-1}\widehat f_C(t)
 +p^{-1}\overline{\widehat f_{C'}(-t)}e_p(-ts).                  \tag{6}
\]
For \(p\ge5\),
\[
 \begin{array}{c|c|c}
 (t,s)&C=C'&C\ne C'\\ \hline
 (0,0)&(p-1)/p-p^{-2}&-p^{-1}-p^{-2}\\
 t\ne0,\ s=0&|\mathcal H_p|\le3/p&|\mathcal H_p|\le4p^{-1/2}\\
 t=0,\ s\ne0&|\mathcal H_p|\le3p^{-1/2}&|\mathcal H_p|\le3p^{-1/2}\\
 t\ne0,\ s\ne0&|\mathcal H_p|\le6p^{-1/2}&|\mathcal H_p|\le6p^{-1/2}.
 \end{array}                                                     \tag{7}
\]
The first two rows are fact de77752fa0dd5cf7. In the GA specialization,
\[
 C_{p,j}=C_{p,k}
 \Longleftrightarrow p^2\mid h_jn_k-h_kn_j.                      \tag{8}
\]
Thus a nonzero shift has the stronger \(p^{-1}\) factor precisely on
\[
 t_p\ne0,\qquad s\equiv0\pmod p,\qquad
 p^2\mid h_jn_k-h_kn_j;                                         \tag{9}
\]
every other nonzero joint shift/displacement stratum has at least a square-root local factor. The primes \(2,3\), when present, cost an absolute constant.

Put
\[
 \kappa_{\mathfrak a}(\mathcal D)
 =
 \begin{cases}
  1,&\mathfrak a=C_\ell,\\
  B/\mathcal D,&\mathfrak a=A.
 \end{cases}
\]
The exact needed fixed-\(r\) supplier is
\[
 \boxed{
 |\mathcal O_r(c)|
 \ll_\varepsilon
 x^\varepsilon|\omega_F|^2Q^2F\,
 \kappa_{\mathfrak a}(\mathcal D)
 \sum_{j\in\mathcal R_r}|c_j|^2.
 }                                                               \tag{GA-SHIFT-SRC(r)}
\]
Together with facts e2e971fd4983bd94 and 35e599ec4bc284fe, this gives
\[
 \left|\sum_{j\in\mathcal R_r}c_jK_{j,r}\right|^2
 \ll_\varepsilon
 x^\varepsilon|\omega_F|^2Q^2F\,
 \kappa_{\mathfrak a}(\mathcal D)
 \sum_j|c_j|^2,                                                   \tag{10}
\]
the scalar fixed-\(r\) face scale required by fact c7970d9d1337bd09 after the common physical choice \(c_{(u,h)}=z_u^{\rm phys}\).

Pointwise local bounds do not prove GA-SHIFT-SRC(r). Already at one prime,
\[
 \sum_{t\in\mathbb F_p}
 |\mathcal H_p(C,C';t,s)|
 \ll
 \begin{cases}
 1,&s=0,\ C=C',\\
 \sqrt p,&\text{otherwise},
 \end{cases}                                                     \tag{11}
\]
and tensorwise absolute summation gives at best an \(r^{1/2+o(1)}\) shift tax in unrestricted strata. Therefore the first remaining fixed-\(r\) theorem is the signed operator (3) at the displayed scale. No estimate for GA-SHIFT-SRC(r), no distinct-\(r\) recombination, no GA-OFF-SYN, no GA-NR-DIL, no good-\(\mathscr W\) payment, and no Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
e08b28d0e17e861c.proof:
Equation (6) of fact 9128d43a5ac4e1bb is
\[
 \mathcal O_r(c)
 =\sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\ne\boldsymbol\sigma}
 \sum_{j,k}\sum_{q_1,q_2}
 c_j\overline{c_k}B_{j,r}(q_1)\overline{B_{k,r}(q_2)}
 V_{j,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)\overline{V_{k,r}(\boldsymbol\sigma)}
 \chi_{\boldsymbol\rho}(q_1)
 \overline{\chi_{\boldsymbol\sigma}(q_2)}.                        \tag{12}
\]
Set
\[
 \boldsymbol t=\boldsymbol\rho-\boldsymbol\sigma,\quad
 s=q_1-q_2,\quad q=q_2.
\]
Then \(\boldsymbol\rho\ne\boldsymbol\sigma\) is
\(\boldsymbol t\ne\boldsymbol0\), and
\[
 e_p(\rho_pq_1-\sigma_pq_2)
 =e_p(t_p(q+s))e_p(\sigma_ps).
\]
The tensor and its support factor over \(p\mid r\), so the inner dual sum is
\[
 \chi_{\boldsymbol t}(q+s)
 \prod_{p\mid r}\mathcal H_p(C_{p,j},C_{p,k};t_p,s).
\]
The integer change \((q_1,q_2)\leftrightarrow(s,q)\) is bijective, and zero extension retains every original restriction. This proves (3).

Complete (1) over all \(\sigma\). Expanding the normalized transforms gives
\[
 {1\over p^2}\sum_{x,y\ne0}e_p(Cx^{-1}-C'y^{-1}-tx)
 \sum_{\sigma\in\mathbb F_p}e_p(\sigma(-x+y+s)).
\]
The last sum forces \(x=y+s\), proving (4). If \(t=0\), only \(\sigma=0\) is deleted, with contribution \(p^{-2}\), proving (5). If \(t\ne0\), the deleted coordinates are \(0,-t\). Since every zero transform is \(-1/p\), subtracting their contributions proves (6).

For \(s=0\), (4)--(6) are exactly the formulas in fact de77752fa0dd5cf7, which proves the first two rows of (7).

Assume \(s\ne0\). If \(t=0\), the substitution
\(z=y/(y+s)\) changes the phase in (4) into a constant plus a Kloosterman phase with both direct and inverse coefficients nonzero; at most one term is deleted. Fact 4f9aec67f5be35db gives
\[
 |\mathcal F_p(C,C';0,s)|\le2p^{-1/2}+p^{-1}.
\]
Equation (5) yields
\[
 |\mathcal H_p(C,C';0,s)|\le3p^{-1/2}
\]
for \(p\ge5\).

Let \(t\ne0\). The phase
\[
 R(y)=C(y+s)^{-1}-C'y^{-1}-t(y+s)                               \tag{13}
\]
has three distinct simple projective poles: \(0,-s,\infty\). It is not of the form \(H^p-H\), because every pole of \(H^p-H\) has order divisible by \(p\). Choose a regular point \(a\in\mathbb F_p\); one exists since \(p\ge5\). Apply a fractional linear change sending \(a\) to infinity. The transformed rational function has denominator degree three with three distinct roots and numerator degree at most three. Lemma 2 of Makhul--Winterhof, arXiv:2106.12218, bounds the transformed affine sum by \(4\sqrt p+1\). This transformed affine sum contains every original term except \(e_p(R(a))\), because the original point \(a\) was sent to infinity. Restoring that unit-modulus term gives
\[
 \left|
 \sum_{\substack{y\in\mathbb F_p\\y\ne0,\ y+s\ne0}}e_p(R(y))
 \right|\le4\sqrt p+2.
\]
Consequently
\[
 |\mathcal F_p(C,C';t,s)|
 \le4p^{-1/2}+2p^{-1}.                                          \tag{14}
\]
Fact 4f9aec67f5be35db gives
\[
 |\widehat f_C(t)|+|\widehat f_{C'}(-t)|\le4p^{-1/2}.
\]
Equations (6) and (14) give
\[
 |\mathcal H_p(C,C';t,s)|
 \le4p^{-1/2}+2p^{-1}+4p^{-3/2}
 \le6p^{-1/2}
\]
for \(p\ge5\), proving the remaining rows of (7). For \(p=2,3\), Cauchy--Schwarz and Parseval bound each local kernel by one, and there are only finitely many local shift coordinates.

Equation (8) is equation (10) of fact de77752fa0dd5cf7. Combining it with the \(t\ne0,s=0\) row of (7) proves (9).

Fact 9128d43a5ac4e1bb gives
\[
 \left|\sum_jc_jK_{j,r}\right|^2
 =\mathcal D_r(c)+\mathcal O_r(c).
\]
Fact e2e971fd4983bd94 bounds \(\mathcal D_r(c)\) by the right side of (10) for \(C_\ell\), and fact 35e599ec4bc284fe gives the same bound with \(B/\mathcal D\) for \(A\). Hence GA-SHIFT-SRC(r) implies (10).

Finally, if \(s=0,C=C'\), fact de77752fa0dd5cf7 gives one order-one \(t=0\) term and \(p-1\) terms bounded by \(3/p\), totaling \(O(1)\). In every other case (7) gives \(p\) terms of size \(O(p^{-1/2})\), totaling \(O(\sqrt p)\). Tensorwise absolute summation factorizes over primes; \(2,3\) cost an absolute constant and fixed constants per prime are \(x^{o(1)}\). This gives \(r^{1/2+o(1)}\) and proves (11). Since (3) was not estimated as a signed operator, all final limitations follow.

glossary.GA-SHIFT-SRC(r): The literal signed physical-displacement/dual-shift operator estimate at the scalar fixed-active-product face scale.
glossary.joint local kernel: The kernel H_p(C,C';t,s) coupling a dual-frequency shift t to the physical modulus displacement s.
glossary.physical displacement: The integer s=q_1-q_2 in the exact two-modulus expansion of the off-dual discrepancy.

e15d7c3384a96dfa.title: DISTINCT-SELECTED-PRIME FIRST-NONRESONANCE MASKS CREATE NO ADDITIONAL FOUR-ROW q-COUPLING. Let d and d' be squarefree positive integers. Let p be a prime divisor of d and p' a prime divisor of d', with p not equal to p'. Order the prime divisors of each integer increasingly. For four row variables (q_i,h_i), assume q_1q_2 is coprime to d and q_3q_4 is coprime to d'. Put Delta_12=h_1q_2-h_2q_1 and Delta_34=h_3q_4-h_4q_3. For a fixed integer A define the exact first-nonresonance predicates
e15d7c3384a96dfa.author: slava chan
e15d7c3384a96dfa.statement:
DISTINCT-SELECTED-PRIME FIRST-NONRESONANCE MASKS CREATE NO ADDITIONAL FOUR-ROW q-COUPLING. Let d and d' be squarefree positive integers. Let p be a prime divisor of d and p' a prime divisor of d', with p not equal to p'. Order the prime divisors of each integer increasingly. For four row variables (q_i,h_i), assume q_1q_2 is coprime to d and q_3q_4 is coprime to d'. Put Delta_12=h_1q_2-h_2q_1 and Delta_34=h_3q_4-h_4q_3. For a fixed integer A define the exact first-nonresonance predicates
D_p^(12)=1_{p does not divide A Delta_12} product_{ell|d, ell<p}1_{ell divides A Delta_12},
D_p'^(34)=1_{p' does not divide A Delta_34} product_{ell|d', ell<p'}1_{ell divides A Delta_34}.
Use the normalized row-projective norms of fact e2dfe323dd49c74d, allowing the first two and last two rows to have different prime lists. Then
||D_p^(12)||_{pi,2}<=2,  ||D_p'^(34)||_{pi,2}<=2,
and
||D_p^(12)D_p'^(34)||_{pi,4}<=4.
Moreover the exact predicate that the first pair selects p and the second pair selects p' is precisely the displayed product. Hence distinctness p!=p' introduces no additional q-dependent condition and no prime-cardinality factor into this selector decomposition. Multiplication by any outer-label mask M with |M|<=1 preserves the bound 4 after its fixed non-q labels are held fixed.

Consequently, in the C1 varying-prime scalar assembly of fact b93c84ae1cba3363, the two first-prime selectors themselves are not the possible “additional non-row-factorable mask” excluded by that fact. Any remaining such obstruction must be a separately identified later q-dependent tuple mask or a source/completion Hilbert coupling. This theorem does not assert that no such later mask exists, does not compare the scalar tensor with an upstream Hilbert norm, and does not estimate the residual composite reciprocal phases of fact 79ffbcb2ffe4049f.
e15d7c3384a96dfa.proof:
The two-row proof is the argument of fact e2dfe323dd49c74d, and we repeat the point needed for the differing prime lists. Fix a lower prime ell dividing d with ell<p. If ell divides A, its divisibility gate is identically one. Suppose ell does not divide A. Since q_1q_2 is a unit modulo ell,
ell divides Delta_12 if and only if h_1q_1^{-1}=h_2q_2^{-1} modulo ell.
If both local heights vanish, the gate is one; if exactly one vanishes, it is zero; if both are units, additive orthogonality gives
1_{ell|Delta_12}=ell^{-1} sum_{u mod ell} e_ell(u h_1q_1^{-1})e_ell(-u h_2q_2^{-1}).
The normalized two-row projective coefficient mass is at most one. At the selected prime p the same case split applies to the complementary gate. In its only nonconstant case,
1_{p does not divide Delta_12}=1-p^{-1}sum_{u mod p}e_p(u h_1q_1^{-1})e_p(-u h_2q_2^{-1}),
whose projective mass is at most two. Multiplying all lower gates and the selected gate proves ||D_p^(12)||_{pi,2}<=2. Notice that this proof uses only the prime list of d.

Apply the identical argument to rows three and four using the prime list of d'. It proves ||D_p'^(34)||_{pi,2}<=2, independently of whether d and d' share any primes and, in particular, for p!=p'. If
D_p^(12)=sum_alpha c_alpha F_{1,alpha}F_{2,alpha}
and
D_p'^(34)=sum_gamma c'_gamma F_{3,gamma}F_{4,gamma},
multiplication gives a four-row projective expansion with coefficient mass at most
(sum_alpha |c_alpha| ||F_{1,alpha}||_infinity||F_{2,alpha}||_infinity)
(sum_gamma |c'_gamma| ||F_{3,gamma}||_infinity||F_{4,gamma}||_infinity)<=4.
This proves the four-row norm bound.

By definition, “the first pair selects p and the second selects p'” is the conjunction of the two independent pair events, so its indicator is exactly their product. The inequality p!=p' is already fixed in the outer selected-prime labels and imposes no condition on q_1,...,q_4. Likewise a fixed outer-label mask M is a scalar multiplier of modulus at most one, so it cannot increase the row-projective coefficient mass. Fact ff228b0e569531f8 identifies these two predicates as the actual first-prime masks in a four-row C1-C4 occupancy. Fact b93c84ae1cba3363 already pays their scalar varying-prime aggregation under the explicit exclusion of any further q-dependent cross-pair mask. The proved factorization shows that such a further mask cannot be generated merely by taking the two distinct first-prime predicates together. The final limitations follow because no later tuple operator or Hilbert comparison was analyzed.

glossary.cross-prime selector mask: The product of the two exact first-nonresonant-prime predicates when two TT-star pairs select distinct primes.
glossary.outer-label mask: A scalar predicate depending on fixed source, anatomy, dyadic, cofactor, height, or provenance labels but not on the four physical q variables.

e18b670f5d48f500.title: RAISED-STOPPING (6/5) EXPONENT GEOMETRY
e18b670f5d48f500.author: slava chan

glossary.S_0: The raised stopping height H^2 Q^(3 sigma).

e240fbd021e8cb63.title: EXACT LARGE-PRIME TOTAL-MODULUS REDUCTION TO TWO REFLECTED MOBIUS WINDOWS. Assume the hypotheses and notation of facts 3db20da48fdfac31 and 16c145000d211540. For real t and an integer n define
e240fbd021e8cb63.author: slava chan
e240fbd021e8cb63.statement:
EXACT LARGE-PRIME TOTAL-MODULUS REDUCTION TO TWO REFLECTED MOBIUS WINDOWS. Assume the hypotheses and notation of facts 3db20da48fdfac31 and 16c145000d211540. For real t and an integer n define
a_t(n)=1_{n in cal I_D}mu(n)Phi(n/D)(n/D)^{it},
R_t(n)=sum_{v in Z}a_t(v)1_{n-v in cal H_mid}.                         (1)
Let p>2D be a prime with p not dividing N. For bold t=(t_1,t_2), define
h_{p,bold t}(n)=-widetilde F_p(t_1)widetilde F_1(t_2)a_{t_1}(n)R_{t_2}(n)
                 -widetilde F_1(t_1)widetilde F_p(t_2)a_{t_2}(n)R_{t_1}(n).     (2)
Then the literal physical row at S=p is
H_{p,bold t}(z)=sum_{n in cal I_D, n congruent -z mod p}h_{p,bold t}(n).         (3)
Every residue class in (3) contains at most one supported n, and every such residue is a unit. Consequently, for every nonzero k modulo p,
Y_{p,bold t}(k)=sum_{n in cal I_D}h_{p,bold t}(n)[p e_p(-kNn^{-1})+1].          (4)
Thus the contribution of primes p>2D to the literal incomplete critical Gram is exactly the short-frequency second moment of two p-independent reflected Mobius-window coefficient sequences a_{t_1}R_{t_2} and a_{t_2}R_{t_1}, multiplied only by the displayed archimedean scalars widetilde F_p(t_j), together with the exact mean term in (4). No estimate for this varying-prime reciprocal large-sieve problem or for QUAD-SUPPLIER_A is asserted.
e240fbd021e8cb63.proof:
For S=p prime, the squarefree pairs with [q_1,q_2]=p are exactly (q_1,q_2)=(p,1),(1,p),(p,p). (5) In the third pair, (q_1,q_2)=p must divide h. But every h in cal H_mid satisfies |h|<3D/2

2D. Hence the (p,p) state is empty. For (p,1), the CRT translation gamma is zero, and equation (3) of fact 7264046d8776d59f requires w congruent -z modulo p. Put v=w-h. The physical coefficient g_{h,bold t}(w) is a_{t_1}(w)a_{t_2}(v), and summing h is the same as summing v subject to w-v in cal H_mid. The Mobius factor from q_1=p is mu(p)=-1. Therefore this state contributes -widetilde F_p(t_1)widetilde F_1(t_2)sum_{w congruent -z mod p}a_{t_1}(w)R_{t_2}(w). (6) For (1,p), gamma is congruent to h modulo p. The row congruence w congruent h-z is equivalent to v=w-h congruent -z modulo p. The same argument gives -widetilde F_1(t_1)widetilde F_p(t_2)sum_{v congruent -z mod p}a_{t_2}(v)R_{t_1}(v). (7) Equations (6) and (7) prove (3) with (2). The support of Phi(n/D) is contained in [D/2,2D], so two supported integers differ by at most 3D/2

glossary.R_t: the signed middle-shift Mobius window in equation (1)
glossary.a_t: the signed one-variable reflected Mobius weight in equation (1)
glossary.h_{p,bold t}: the combined physical coefficient at residue -n for the prime total modulus p

e274e013c7d62c25.title: Let \(N,m,w,h,q_1,q_2\) be positive integers with \(w-h\ge1\). Put
e274e013c7d62c25.author: slava chan
e274e013c7d62c25.statement:
Let \(N,m,w,h,q_1,q_2\) be positive integers with \(w-h\ge1\). Put
\[
 p=N-mw,\qquad p'=N-m(w-h),
\]
and assume
\[
 p,p'\ge1,\qquad q_1\mid p,\qquad q_2\mid p',
 \qquad (w,N)=(w-h,N)=1,
\]
with \(q_1,q_2\) squarefree. Define
\[
 \delta=(q_1,q_2),\qquad q_1=\delta u,\qquad q_2=\delta v,
 \qquad e=(\delta,N),\qquad\delta_0=\delta/e.            \tag{1}
\]
Then
\[
 (q_1,w)=(q_2,w-h)=1,                                  \tag{2}
\]
\[
 \boxed{(\delta,m)=(\delta,N)=e,}                       \tag{3}
\]
and
\[
 \boxed{\delta_0\mid h.}                                \tag{4}
\]
In particular,
\[
 (e,\delta_0)=1,\qquad e\mid m,\qquad
 (\delta_0,mN)=1.                                       \tag{5}
\]

Moreover, \(\delta,u,v\) are pairwise coprime. Let \(k\) be any integer.
Write \(\overline a^{(q)}\) for the inverse of \(a\) modulo \(q>1\).
The common-modulus factor in the CRT phase of fact d97b0142b0d0a486
reduces exactly as
\[
 e_\delta\!\left(
 -kN\overline w^{(\delta)}\overline{uv}^{(\delta)}
 \right)
 =
 e_{\delta_0}\!\left(
 -k{N\over e}\,
 \overline w^{(\delta_0)}
 \overline{uv}^{(\delta_0)}
 \right),                                               \tag{6}
\]
with both sides interpreted as one when \(\delta=1\), and the right side
interpreted as one when \(\delta_0=1\). Thus the fixed-center part
\(e=(\delta,N)\) contributes no oscillatory phase; it divides the quotient
\(m\), while the complementary common modulus \(\delta_0\) divides the
shift \(h\).
e274e013c7d62c25.proof:
Suppose a prime \(\ell\) divides both \(q_1\) and \(w\). Since
\(q_1\mid p=N-mw\), it follows that \(\ell\mid N\), contrary to
\((w,N)=1\). Hence \((q_1,w)=1\). The same argument with \(q_2,p'\), and
\(w-h\) proves \((q_2,w-h)=1\), establishing (2).

Let \(\ell\) be a prime divisor of \(\delta\). If \(\ell\mid m\), then
\(\ell\mid q_1\mid N-mw\) implies \(\ell\mid N\). Conversely, if
\(\ell\mid N\), the same divisibility gives \(\ell\mid mw\). By (2),
\(\ell\nmid w\), so \(\ell\mid m\). Thus, prime by prime inside the
squarefree integer \(\delta\),
\[
 \ell\mid m\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\ell\mid N.
\]
This proves (3).

Because \(\delta\mid q_1,q_2\), it divides both \(p\) and \(p'\). Hence
\[
 \delta\mid p'-p=mh.                                    \tag{7}
\]
Equation (3) and squarefreeness give
\[
 (e,\delta_0)=1,\qquad(e,m)=e,\qquad(\delta_0,m)=1.
\]
Every prime of \(\delta_0\) is absent from \(N\) by the definition
\(e=(\delta,N)\), so \((\delta_0,N)=1\). From (7) and
\((\delta_0,m)=1\), one obtains \(\delta_0\mid h\). This proves (4)--(5).

Since \(q_1,q_2\) are squarefree, writing them as \(\delta u,\delta v\)
implies
\[
 (\delta,u)=(\delta,v)=(u,v)=1.
\]
Put \(N=eN_0\) and \(\delta=e\delta_0\). If \(\delta_0>1\), reduction of
the inverses modulo \(\delta\) to the divisor \(\delta_0\) gives
\[
 \overline w^{(\delta)}\equiv\overline w^{(\delta_0)}
 \pmod{\delta_0},\qquad
 \overline{uv}^{(\delta)}\equiv\overline{uv}^{(\delta_0)}
 \pmod{\delta_0}.
\]
Therefore, for any integer representative \(A\) of the product of the two
inverses modulo \(\delta\),
\[
 \exp\left({2\pi i(-k)eN_0A\over e\delta_0}\right)
 =
 \exp\left({2\pi i(-k)N_0A\over\delta_0}\right),
\]
which is exactly (6). If \(\delta_0=1\), the exponent on the left is an
integer because \(\delta=e\mid N\), so the left side is one. The
modulus-one conventions cover the remaining cases.

glossary.fixed-center common part: e=(delta,N), the part of the common expansion modulus which divides m
glossary.shift common part: delta_0=delta/e, the part of the common expansion modulus which divides h

e2dfe323dd49c74d.title: NORM-AT-MOST-TWO ROW-PROJECTIVE DECOMPOSITION OF THE LITERAL FIRST-NONRESONANT-PRIME PAIR MASK. Let A,h_1,h_2 be integers, let p_1<...<p_j be distinct primes, let q_1,q_2 be integers coprime to P=p_1...p_j, and put Delta=h_1 q_2-h_2 q_1. For 1<=k<=j define
e2dfe323dd49c74d.author: slava chan
e2dfe323dd49c74d.statement: NORM-AT-MOST-TWO ROW-PROJECTIVE DECOMPOSITION OF THE LITERAL FIRST-NONRESONANT-PRIME PAIR MASK. Let A,h_1,h_2 be integers, let p_1<...
e2dfe323dd49c74d.proof:
The definition of first nonresonance gives the displayed product exactly: every smaller prime must divide A Delta and the selected prime must not divide A Delta. Fix a lower prime ell. If ell divides A, the lower gate is automatic. Suppose ell does not divide A. The gate is 1_{ell divides Delta}. Since q_1q_2 is a unit modulo ell, multiplying Delta by q_1^{-1}q_2^{-1} shows
ell divides Delta if and only if h_1 q_1^{-1}=h_2 q_2^{-1} modulo ell.
If both heights vanish modulo ell this is automatic; if exactly one vanishes it is impossible. If both are units, additive orthogonality gives
1_{ell divides Delta}=ell^{-1} sum_{u mod ell} e_ell(u(h_1q_1^{-1}-h_2q_2^{-1})).
Each summand is the product of the row-local unit-modulus functions e_ell(u h_1q_1^{-1}) and e_ell(-u h_2q_2^{-1}). Hence its contribution to the normalized projective coefficient mass is ell^{-1}; summing over ell choices of u gives 1.

For p=p_k, if p divides A the selected event is empty. Otherwise the selected gate is 1_{p does not divide Delta}. The same slope calculation makes it zero when both heights vanish modulo p and one when exactly one vanishes. When both are units, subtracting the slope-congruence projector from 1 gives
1_{p does not divide Delta}=1-p^{-1} sum_{u mod p} e_p(u h_1q_1^{-1})e_p(-u h_2q_2^{-1}).
All factors have sup norm one, so the normalized projective mass is at most 1+p p^{-1}=2. Multiplication of projective decompositions is submultiplicative for the displayed norm: coefficient masses multiply and sup norms of rowwise products are at most the products of their sup norms. Thus the lower gates cost at most 1 each and the selected gate at most 2, proving ||D_{p_k}^{(12)}||_{pi,2}<=2.

Apply the same decomposition to D_{p_k}^{(34)}. If
D_{p_k}^{(12)}=sum_alpha c_alpha F_{1,alpha}F_{2,alpha}
and
D_{p_k}^{(34)}=sum_gamma c'_gamma F_{3,gamma}F_{4,gamma},
then their product is sum_{alpha,gamma}c_alpha c'_gamma product_{i=1}^4 G_{i,alpha,gamma}, with the first two G-factors equal to the corresponding F_{1,alpha},F_{2,alpha} and the last two equal to F_{3,gamma},F_{4,gamma}. Its normalized four-row coefficient mass is at most the product of the two normalized two-row masses, hence at most 4.

Finally, every nonconstant lower-prime row factor is e_ell(C_ell q^{-1}). For distinct primes, the Chinese remainder theorem identifies the product of these characters, and any selected-prime factor of the same form, with e_M(C q^{-1}) for a suitable residue C modulo their squarefree product M. This is an exact identity on q coprime to M. It identifies, but does not estimate, the remaining composite-modulus Mobius reciprocal sum.

glossary.A: The fixed integer factor multiplying each determinant in the resonance test.
glossary.D_{p_k}^{(12)}: The literal first-pair mask selecting p_k as first nonresonant prime.
glossary.D_{p_k}^{(34)}: The literal second-pair mask selecting p_k as first nonresonant prime.
glossary.Delta: The first-pair determinant h_1 q_2-h_2 q_1.
glossary.Delta_{34}: The second-pair determinant h_3 q_4-h_4 q_3.
glossary.P: The squarefree product p_1...p_j of the ordered rough primes.
glossary.e_ell(t): The additive character exp(2 pi i t/ell) modulo the prime ell.
glossary.p_a: The a-th ordered distinct prime in the rough prime product.
