e2e971fd4983bd94.title: LITERAL COMMON-ACTIVE-PRODUCT \(C_\ell\) WEIGHTED TENSOR BOUND IN THE POLYNOMIAL FREQUENCY RANGE
e2e971fd4983bd94.author: slava chan
e2e971fd4983bd94.statement:
LITERAL COMMON-ACTIVE-PRODUCT \(C_\ell\) WEIGHTED TENSOR BOUND IN THE POLYNOMIAL FREQUENCY RANGE.

Work in the forward GA-tail setting of fact e55b27d39c593164 and its exact centered completion in fact 0aa821ade9a14b45. Fix one orientation, exact outer gcd, frozen layer, parent, source/projective fiber, one \(C_\ell\)-anatomy, one dilator block, and one signed frequency block
\[
 1\le F\le x^3,\qquad F\le |h|<2F.                                \tag{1}
\]
Let \(\omega_F\) be the literal Fourier-decay scalar of fact e55b27d39c593164. Fix a nonempty squarefree active product \(r\), and let \(\mathcal R_r\) be any set of actual \(C_\ell\)-rows
\[
 j=(\lambda,h),\qquad n_j=d_jv_j,\qquad v_j\in\{1,2\},
\]
for which \(r\mid d^{\rm u}_{\lambda,h}\), with no repeated triple \((d_j,v_j,h)\). Let \(V_{j,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)\), \(W_{j,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)\), and \(\Omega_r\) be the exact quantities in equations (7)--(8) of fact 0aa821ade9a14b45.

Then for every complex coefficient array \((c_j)_{j\in\mathcal R_r}\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 \sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r}
 \left|\sum_{j\in\mathcal R_r}
 c_jW_{j,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)V_{j,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)\right|^2
 \ll_\varepsilon
 x^\varepsilon |\omega_F|^2Q^2F
 \sum_{j\in\mathcal R_r}|c_j|^2.                                 \tag{2}
\]
The estimate retains the exact marker weight, \(\mu(q)\), dimensionless physical Fourier amplitude, target-gcd, fixed-\(U\), high, source, parent, ordering, equality, collision, deletion, provenance, coprimality, inactive-prime, and small-\(v_j\) factors contained in the literal coefficient of fact 0aa821ade9a14b45.

This is the literal common-\(r\), coordinatewise weighted tensor estimate for one \(C_\ell\)-anatomy in the range (1). Fact e55b27d39c593164 separately disposes of the aggregate \(F>x^3\) Fourier tail; no arbitrary-coefficient operator statement for that tail is asserted here. The result proves no pair-dependent nonresonance deletion, no distinct-\(r\) discrepancy, no recombination of centered faces, no \(A\)-anatomy estimate, no GA-NR-DIL estimate, no payment of the good-\(\mathscr W\) tail, and no Goldbach conclusion.
e2e971fd4983bd94.proof:
For a \(C_\ell\)-row, fact 0aa821ade9a14b45 gives
\[
 B_{\lambda,h,r}(q)
 =b_{\lambda,h}(q)
 e_{v_j}\!\left(\mathscr Ah(qd_j)^{-1}\right)
 {\mu(a_j)\over a_j},\qquad
 a_j={d^{\rm u}_{\lambda,h}\over r}.                              \tag{3}
\]
Fact 19544eedf19b375b applies with its ambient polynomial parameter \(X=x\): condition (1), together with the polynomial bounds in fact e55b27d39c593164, places the frequency interval and all remaining parameters inside a fixed polynomial envelope in \(x\). Since \(v_j\in\{1,2\}\) and \((qd_j,v_j)=1\),
\[
 e_{v_j}\!\left(\mathscr Ah(qd_j)^{-1}\right)
 =e_{v_j}(\mathscr Ah)                                            \tag{4}
\]
is independent of \(q\). Define the stripped transform
\[
 Y_j(\boldsymbol\rho)
 =\sum_{\substack{Q\le q<2Q\\(q,n_j)=1}}
 b_{\lambda,h}(q)\chi_{\boldsymbol\rho}(q).                        \tag{5}
\]
Equations (3)--(5) give
\[
 W_{j,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)
 ={\mu(a_j)\over a_j}e_{v_j}(\mathscr Ah)Y_j(\boldsymbol\rho).      \tag{6}
\]

We give an exact common-spectrum decomposition of (5). Let \(\mathcal T\) be the integers \(q_0\) in \([Q,2Q)\). On the common integer support define
\[
 z_{q_0}(q)={\bf1}_{q=q_0},\qquad
 \beta_{j,q_0}
 ={\bf1}_{(q_0,n_j)=1}b_{\lambda,h}(q_0),                          \tag{7}
\]
and
\[
 Z_{q_0}(\boldsymbol\rho)
 =\sum_qz_{q_0}(q)\chi_{\boldsymbol\rho}(q)
 =\chi_{\boldsymbol\rho}(q_0).                                    \tag{8}
\]
Thus \(\sup_{\boldsymbol\rho}|Z_{q_0}(\boldsymbol\rho)|=1\), and
\[
 Y_j(\boldsymbol\rho)
 =\sum_{q_0\in\mathcal T}\beta_{j,q_0}Z_{q_0}(\boldsymbol\rho).     \tag{9}
\]

In the explicit range \(1\le F\le x^3\), equation (9) and the coefficient discussion in the proof of fact e55b27d39c593164 state that, after extracting \(\omega_F\), the exact dimensionless post-reciprocity coefficient is \(x^{o(1)}\), uniformly on the fixed source/projective fiber. Removing or inserting the unit-modulus factors used in passing between \(c_\lambda\), \(\widetilde c_\lambda\), and \(b_{\lambda,h}\) does not change its magnitude. Hence, for every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 \sup_{j,q_0}|\beta_{j,q_0}|
 \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon|\omega_F|.                         \tag{10}
\]
There are at most \(Q+1\ll Q\) integers in \(\mathcal T\). Therefore the projective cost in fact 19544eedf19b375b satisfies
\[
 \mathfrak P_C(Y)
 \le\sum_{q_0\in\mathcal T}\sup_j|\beta_{j,q_0}|
 \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon Q|\omega_F|.                       \tag{11}
\]
The signed dyadic block contains \(O(F)\) integer frequencies. Apply equation (6) of fact 19544eedf19b375b with \(X=x\), frequency cardinality \(V\ll F\), (6), and (11). Replacing \(\varepsilon\) by a sufficiently small multiple of itself yields
\[
 \sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r}
 \left|\sum_jc_jW_{j,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)V_{j,r}(\boldsymbol\rho)\right|^2
 \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon|\omega_F|^2Q^2F
 \sum_j|c_j|^2,
\]
which is (2). Because the coefficients \(\beta_{j,q_0}\) in (7) are the literal \(b_{\lambda,h}(q_0)\) with only their existing coprimality support imposed, no inherited source or mask factor has been removed. The restriction (1) is exactly the range in which the cited pointwise coefficient bound and the polynomial-envelope hypothesis are available. All limitations are therefore explicit.

glossary.literal common-active-product C_l weight: The exact common-r coordinatewise tensor estimate for one GA C_l anatomy with all source and mask coefficients retained in the polynomial frequency range.

e3c0786d33d7e576.title: COUNTABLE MAYNARD TYPE-II ESTIMATE FOR AN ALREADY-FOLDED PRIME/COFACTOR ROW WITH PRIME-UNIT DELETION. Fix real A>0 and an integer K>=2. Let B be sufficiently large and let delta be real. Let Q_1,R_1,P,M>=2 satisfy
e3c0786d33d7e576.author: slava chan
e3c0786d33d7e576.statement:
COUNTABLE MAYNARD TYPE-II ESTIMATE FOR AN ALREADY-FOLDED PRIME/COFACTOR ROW WITH PRIME-UNIT DELETION. Fix real A>0 and an integer K>=2. Let B be sufficiently large and let delta be real. Let Q_1,R_1,P,M>=2 satisfy
Q_1R_1=B^(1/2+delta), PM asymptotic to B,
B^(6delta)(log B)^C<=R_1<=B^(1/10-3delta)(log B)^(-C),
Q_1B^(2delta)(log B)^C<=P<=B^(1/2-3delta)(log B)^(-C),           (1)
where C=C(A,K)>0 is sufficiently large. Put Q_0=Q_1R_1. Let c be a positive integer, and let cal S be a set of ordered pairs (q,r), q in [Q_1,2Q_1), r in [R_1,2R_1), for which (q,r) maps injectively to the squarefree integer s=qr and (s,c)=1. Choose a unit residue a_s modulo each s.

For each s let W_s(p,v) be supported on primes P<=p<2P and integers M<=v<2M. Assume that a finite or countable set J, coefficients lambda_{j,s}, and sequences A_j,B_j give the absolutely convergent expansion
W_s(p,v)=sum_{j in J}lambda_{j,s}A_j(p)B_j(v),                   (2)
with
sum_j sup_s|lambda_{j,s}|<=L_proj,
|A_j(n)|<=tau_K(n), |B_j(n)|<=tau_K(n),                          (3)
and with every prime-side sequence A_j satisfying Maynard's Siegel-Walfisz condition uniformly in j and all displayed parameters. Assume also the reconstructed pointwise bound
|W_s(p,v)|<=L_W tau(v).                                         (4)
Put
U_s=sum_{p,(p,c)=1}sum_v W_s(p,v)
 [1_{pv congruent a_s (mod s)}
  -phi(s)^(-1)1_{(pv,s)=1}].                                    (5)
Then
sum_{(q,r) in cal S}|U_{qr}|
 <<_{A,K}L_proj B(log B)^(-A)
 +L_W omega_P(c)
  [M(1+log(2MQ_0))^3+Q_0 sqrt(M)(1+log(2MQ_0))^2],              (6)
where omega_P(c)=#{p prime:P<=p<2P,p|c}. In particular this theorem applies directly after several original cofactor variables have been folded into v; it inserts no additional arithmetic coefficient in the v-slot.
e3c0786d33d7e576.proof:
First allow every selected prime and define
U'_s=sum_p sum_v W_s(p,v)
 [1_{pv congruent a_s (mod s)}
  -phi(s)^(-1)1_{(pv,s)=1}].                                    (7)
The p,v support is finite. Absolute convergence in (2) permits termwise insertion, and Tonelli gives
sum_s|U'_s|
 <=sum_j sup_s|lambda_{j,s}| sum_s|U'_{s,j}|,                   (8)
where U'_{s,j} is the centered bilinear row with coefficients A_j(p),B_j(v). Maynard, arXiv:2006.08250, Proposition 5.1, applies to every mode under (1) and (3), uniformly in j and in the varying primitive residue a_s. It gives
sum_s|U'_{s,j}|<<_{A,K}B(log B)^(-A).                            (9)
Thus
sum_s|U'_s|<<_{A,K}L_proj B(log B)^(-A).                         (10)

It remains to compare U_s and U'_s. Their difference contains only the omega_P(c) selected primes p dividing c. Since (s,c)=1, each such p is invertible modulo s. Fix one of them. By (4), the physical part is bounded by L_W times
sum_s sum_{M<=v<2M,v congruent p^(-1)a_s (mod s)}tau(v).         (11)
For every positive integer v,
tau(v)<=2 sum_{e|v,e<=sqrt(v)}1.                                (12)
If the unit residue condition in (11) and e|v hold, then (e,s)=1; writing v=ef leaves one residue class for f modulo s. Hence, for fixed s,
sum_{M<=v<2M,v congruent p^(-1)a_s (mod s)}tau(v)
 <=2 sum_{e<=sqrt(2M)}(M/(es)+1)
 <<M(1+log(2M))/s+sqrt(M).                                      (13)
Injectivity and s in [Q_0,4Q_0) imply that there are O(Q_0) moduli and sum_s1/s<<1. Summing (13) gives
<<M(1+log(2M))+Q_0sqrt(M).                                      (14)

For the principal part, (12) without a congruence gives
sum_{M<=v<2M}tau(v)<<M(1+log(2M)).                               (15)
For squarefree s,
s/phi(s)=product_{l|s}(1-1/l)^(-1)
 <=product_{l|s}(1+1/l)^2
 =(sum_{e|s}1/e)^2<=(1+log s)^2.                                (16)
Therefore
sum_s1/phi(s)<< (1+log(4Q_0))^2,                                (17)
and the principal contribution for the fixed exceptional p is
<<L_W M(1+log(2M))(1+log(4Q_0))^2.                              (18)
Equations (14) and (18), summed over the omega_P(c) exceptional primes, give the second term in (6). Combining this with (10) proves (6). No Ramaré coefficient is introduced because the theorem begins with the already-folded row W_s.

glossary.L_W: The constant in the reconstructed pointwise divisor bound for W_s.
glossary.L_proj: The l1 outer norm of the finite or countable projective expansion.
glossary.U'_s: The auxiliary centered folded row containing every selected prime.
glossary.U_s: The centered folded row with selected primes dividing c deleted.
glossary.W_s(p,v): An already-folded prime/cofactor coefficient to which no further Ramaré factor is applied.

e3ea57dd0f69c38d.title: ABSOLUTE PAYMENT OF THE ALL-ZERO NONRESONANT CRT FACE IN THE LITERAL C4 MOMENT
e3ea57dd0f69c38d.author: slava chan
e3ea57dd0f69c38d.statement:
ABSOLUTE PAYMENT OF THE ALL-ZERO NONRESONANT CRT FACE IN THE LITERAL C4 MOMENT.

Use the exact literal C4 full-n coefficient normal form of fact 9bee61f3627bd506 and the marked-dilator TT-star notation of fact 41b56ed8e64bdba6 on one natural dyadic frequency block F<=C_F H_P, where C_F is fixed. Thus B/2<=n<=2B, each exact C4 copy lambda has
n=d_lambda v_lambda,   D<=d_lambda<2D,   gcd(d_lambda,v_lambda)=1,                 (1)
and d_lambda is the product of its four rough primes. Let A be the signed reduced target from fact 9bee61f3627bd506 and put
Delta=h_1q_2-h_2q_1.                                                               (2)
Assume the physical scales, |A|, and all supported q,h,n are bounded by a fixed power of Q.

For Delta!=0 define
d_0=d_lambda/gcd(d_lambda,A Delta).                                                (3)
In the centered CRT expansion of fact 60ec98d195b61bc1, interpret the all-zero face as mu(d_0)/d_0 when d_0>1 and as 1 when d_0=1. Let M_F^{zero CRT}(D) be the sum of exactly these all-zero-face terms over every Delta!=0 term in the expanded literal C4 moment, with every source coefficient and retained mask unchanged. Then, for every epsilon>0,
|M_F^{zero CRT}(D)| <<_{epsilon,C_F} Q^epsilon BQ^2F^2/D.                         (4)

Thus the all-zero face is already at the second candidate CMD scale, uniformly across fully resonant, partially resonant, and fully nonresonant values of gcd(d_lambda,A Delta). After combining (4) with the Delta=0 payment of fact 54029717e980dcb7, the only unestimated terms in the literal C4 marked-dilator moment are the nonempty centered CRT faces. No estimate for those faces, no full C4 estimate, no other-anatomy estimate, no NR-DIL conclusion, and no Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
e3ea57dd0f69c38d.proof:
Fact 9bee61f3627bd506 writes the literal coefficient after extracting H_P^(-1) as a product of Möbius and retained bookkeeping factors with the dimensionless Fourier amplitude
(H_P/n) Fhat(h/n)
in the forward orientation and
(H_P/n) Fhat(-h/n)
in the reverse orientation, times unit-modulus phases. The Fourier estimate in fact d8ba46800ba433c2 gives
|Fhat(h/n)| << M(log Q)^C
on a natural block in the forward orientation. Since H_P=B/M and n is comparable to B,
(H_P/n)|Fhat(h/n)| <<(log Q)^C.                                  (5)
The swapped reverse estimate in fact 2e0b40b1ba77fb6f is identical with K in place of M and H_P=B/K. All exact marker-copy and retained coefficient multiplicities obey a fixed divisor-function envelope by fact 41b56ed8e64bdba6. Unit-modulus phases do not change absolute values. Consequently all coefficient products below cost at most Q^epsilon after the usual adjustment of epsilon.

Fix q_1,h_1,q_2,h_2 with Delta!=0 and put X=A Delta. Fact 60ec98d195b61bc1 gives the empty centered-CRT face as mu(d_0)/d_0 for d_0>1. For d_0=1 the CRT product is empty and its empty face is 1. In both cases its absolute value is
1/d_0=gcd(d_lambda,X)/d_lambda
 <=gcd(d_lambda,X)/D.                                             (6)

For positive integers d and |X|, the elementary identity
gcd(d,X)=sum_{r|d, r|X} phi(r)                                    (7)
follows by applying sum_{r|m}phi(r)=m to m=gcd(d,X). Insert (7) into (6) and sum over n and its exact C4 copies. If r|d_lambda, then r|n by (1). The number of copies over one n is bounded by a fixed divisor function. Since n lies in [B/2,2B], standard divisor bounds give
#{(n,lambda): B/2<=n<=2B, r|d_lambda} << Q^epsilon B/r.            (8)
There is no endpoint error in (8): every counted r divides n<=2B, so the elementary count of multiples of r is O(B/r).

Equations (6)-(8) imply
sum_{n,lambda}1/d_0
 << Q^epsilon (B/D) sum_{r|X}phi(r)/r
 <= Q^epsilon (B/D) tau(|X|)
 << Q^epsilon B/D.                                               (9)
The last bound uses the displayed fixed-power envelope for A,q,h, which makes 0<|X|<=Q^C for a fixed C, followed by the standard divisor bound.

There are O(QF) supported pairs (q,h), hence O(Q^2F^2) ordered TT-star pairs. Apply (9) separately to each pair and use the coefficient envelope (5). This proves (4).

Fact 60ec98d195b61bc1 partitions the complete d_0-kernel into the all-zero face and faces indexed by nonempty subsets of the primes dividing d_0. Hence, once (4) is removed and fact 54029717e980dcb7 supplies the Delta=0 term, only the stated nonempty centered faces remain unestimated. This proves every scope assertion.

glossary.M_F^{zero CRT}(D): The Delta-nonzero contribution to the literal C4 TT-star moment obtained by taking the subset-empty term in the centered CRT expansion of d_0.
glossary.zero CRT face: The subset-empty centered-CRT face, equal to mu(d_0)/d_0 with the empty-product value one at d_0=1.

e446377f3ab5a559.title: DISCRETE PRODUCT-BOUNDED-VARIATION PERRON TENSORIZATION. Let Q>=4, let W be a complex function on the integers, extended by zero and supported on Q<=k<2Q, and put V_Q(W)=sup_k|W(k)|+sum_k|W(k+1)-W(k)|. Fix A>0. There exist T=Q^(A+3), c=1/log Q, and a complex integrable coefficient C_A(tau), supported on |tau|<=T, such that for all positive integers u,v satisfying Q/4<=uv<=4Q,
e446377f3ab5a559.author: slava chan
e446377f3ab5a559.statement:
DISCRETE PRODUCT-BOUNDED-VARIATION PERRON TENSORIZATION. Let Q>=4, let W be a complex function on the integers, extended by zero and supported on Q<=k<2Q, and put V_Q(W)=sup_k|W(k)|+sum_k|W(k+1)-W(k)|. Fix A>0. There exist T=Q^(A+3), c=1/log Q, and a complex integrable coefficient C_A(tau), supported on |tau|<=T, such that for all positive integers u,v satisfying Q/4<=uv<=4Q,
W(uv)=integral_{-T}^T C_A(tau)u^(-c-i tau)v^(-c-i tau)d tau+E_A(u,v),
where
integral_{-T}^T|C_A(tau)|d tau <<_A V_Q(W)log Q,
|E_A(u,v)|<<_A V_Q(W)Q^(-A-2).
In particular the two one-variable factors have absolute value at most one. Multiplication by arbitrary additional bounded one-variable factors in u and v, including separate coprimality gates or residue-class indicators, preserves the same projective-mass bound. If V_Q(W)<=Q^epsilon for every fixed epsilon>0, this projective mass is Q^o(1), while summing the pointwise remainder over O(Q) pairs (u,v) costs O_A(V_Q(W)Q^(-A-1)). This theorem is a coefficient separation only; it gives no exponential-sum estimate.
e446377f3ab5a559.proof:
For every integer l put d_l=W(l)-W(l+1). Because W has finite support, telescoping gives
W(k)=sum_l d_l 1_{k<=l},
and sum_l|d_l|<=V_Q(W). Only integers l with Q-1<=l<2Q can have d_l nonzero.

We use the following elementary truncated Perron formula. If y>0, y!=1, c>0, and T>=1, then
1_{y>1}=(1/(2 pi)) integral_{-T}^T y^(c+i tau)/(c+i tau)d tau+O(y^c/(T|log y|)).
Indeed the corresponding integral over the entire vertical line equals 1_{y>1}: close the contour to the left when y>1 and to the right when 0<y<1; only the first contour encloses the simple pole at s=0, of residue one. On each omitted tail write y^(c+i tau)=y^c exp(i tau log y) and integrate by parts. The endpoint term is at most y^c/(T|log y|), and the integral of |c+i tau|^(-2) over |tau|>=T is at most a constant times T^(-1), giving the displayed error on both tails.

Apply this formula with k=uv and y=(l+1/2)/k. Since k and l are integers, y is never one and 1_{y>1}=1_{k<=l}. On the stated ranges one has y bounded above and below by positive absolute constants. Moreover |l+1/2-k|>=1/2 and k<=4Q, so the mean value theorem for log, separately on y>=1 and y<1, gives |log y|>=1/(16Q). With c=1/log Q and T=Q^(A+3), the Perron error is therefore O_A(Q^(-A-2)), uniformly in k,l. Multiplying by d_l and summing gives a total error O_A(V_Q(W)Q^(-A-2)).

Interchange the finite l-sum and the truncated integral. The main term becomes
integral_{-T}^T C_A(tau)u^(-c-i tau)v^(-c-i tau)d tau,
where
C_A(tau)=[1/(2 pi(c+i tau))] sum_l d_l(l+1/2)^(c+i tau).
Because Q-1<=l<2Q and c=1/log Q, one has (l+1/2)^c<<1. Hence
|C_A(tau)|<<V_Q(W)/|c+i tau|.
Consequently
integral_{-T}^T|C_A(tau)|d tau
<<V_Q(W)[1+log(T/c)]
<<_A V_Q(W)log Q.
Also |u^(-c-i tau)|=u^(-c)<=1 and similarly for v. Additional bounded one-variable factors merely multiply these two factors and do not alter the coefficient integral. Finally there are O(Q) pairs in any fixed dyadic product box with uv comparable to Q at the crude level needed here, so summing the pointwise error gives the asserted aggregate bound. Every conclusion follows.

glossary.product-BV projective separation: A representation of a bounded-variation weight of a product as a superposition of products of bounded one-variable factors, measured by the total absolute coefficient mass.

e4b8a9247511a282.title: ABSOLUTE PAYMENT OF THE NEAR-CUTOFF ACTIVE-SEMIPRIME SUBFAMILY OF C4-PAIR-LS. Adopt the literal scalar setting and notation of fact 9b40bc10b4d5e5fb. Fix a real constant C>=0 and restrict E_2 to the modes r with
e4b8a9247511a282.author: slava chan
e4b8a9247511a282.statement:
ABSOLUTE PAYMENT OF THE NEAR-CUTOFF ACTIVE-SEMIPRIME SUBFAMILY OF C4-PAIR-LS. Adopt the literal scalar setting and notation of fact 9b40bc10b4d5e5fb. Fix a real constant C>=0 and restrict E_2 to the modes r with
omega(r)=2,  r<=Z^2(log(2Q))^C.                                   (1)
Call the restricted energy E_2^bal(C). Then, for every epsilon>0,
E_2^bal(C)
<<_{epsilon,C}Q^epsilon Z^2 BQ^2F^2/Dcal.                          (2)
Thus this near-cutoff active-semiprime subfamily is absolutely paid at the second term of C4-PAIR-LS. The only remaining pair modes satisfy
r>Z^2(log(2Q))^C.                                                  (3)
No estimate for (3), complete C4-PAIR-LS, C4, or Goldbach is asserted.
e4b8a9247511a282.proof:
For omega(r)=2, fact a3132ecd1bd44382, as used in fact 9b40bc10b4d5e5fb, gives
c_lambda(r)=r/D_lambda.
Since D_lambda>=Dcal, restriction (1) gives
c_lambda(r)<=Z^2(log(2Q))^C/Dcal.                                 (4)
There are six two-prime divisors r for each C4 row.

The scalar literal coefficient envelope gives
|S_lambda,r(1)|<<_epsilon Q^epsilon QF,                            (5)
and the number of exact copies in the canonical-dilator block obeys
sum_n#Lambda_D(n)<<_epsilon Q^epsilon B.                           (6)
These are the same two inputs used in the proof of fact 9b40bc10b4d5e5fb. Multiply (4) by the square of (5), sum over the at most six modes and over the copies in (6), and absorb the fixed power of log(2Q) into Q^epsilon after reducing epsilon at the start. This proves (2). The complement of (1) inside omega(r)=2 is exactly (3).

glossary.E_2^bal(C): The scalar two-prime mode energy restricted to active product r at most Z^2(log(2Q))^C.

e55b27d39c593164.title: GA-TAIL-MARK(\(\tau\)): EXACT GOOD-\(\mathscr W\) RE-MARKER, PARENT LEDGER, LARGE TAIL DILATOR, AND EXPLICIT NONRESONANT MOMENT INTERFACE
e55b27d39c593164.author: slava chan
e55b27d39c593164.statement:
GA-TAIL-MARK(\(\tau\)): EXACT GOOD-\(\mathscr W\) RE-MARKER, PARENT LEDGER, LARGE TAIL DILATOR, AND EXPLICIT NONRESONANT MOMENT INTERFACE.

Fix \(\tau>0\) and put
\[
 Q_\tau=\max\{4,2^{6/\tau}\}.
\]
In the selected post-low construction of fact \(7ffe3d237362a451\), choose its fixed sufficiently-large normalized-base cutoff \(Q_0\) so that \(Q_0\ge Q_\tau\). Use the same selected bad even integer \(N=2x\), source, labels, and post-\(A\) aggregate \(\mathcal T_{\rm postA,sel}\) of fact \(3f2f255ea6845a50\). Consider its inherited sector with normalized exponent \(\beta\ge6/5\). Every atom in this post-low sector has normalized base \(Q>Q_0\).

For exact \(g=(d,r)\), define in the forward orientation
\[
 Q=D/g,\quad B=R/g=Q^\beta,\quad G=M/Q,\quad H_P=B/M,
\]
and in the reverse orientation
\[
 Q=R/g,\quad B=D/g=Q^\beta,\quad G=K/Q,\quad H_P=B/K.
\]
In both orientations,
\[
 H_P={B\over GQ},\qquad
 K_{\rm sh}={Q\over H_P}=GQ^{2-\beta},\qquad
 \mathscr W={B\over H_P^2}=G^2Q^{2-\beta}=GK_{\rm sh}.          \tag{1}
\]
Let \(\mathcal T_{\rm good,sel}(\tau)\) be the complete projection of this inherited tail onto
\[
 \mathscr W\ge Q^\tau.                                          \tag{2}
\]
At a fixed pre-marker atom first recombine every old marker leaf and marker-dependent descendant to the literal normalized factor \(\mu(n_z)\).

On a frozen normalized layer \(\theta\), one has
\[
 B/2\le n_z\le2B,\qquad \mu(n_z)\ne0.
\]
Set
\[
 L_\theta=S_\theta=2,\qquad Z_\theta=\mathscr W^{1/2},\qquad
 J_\theta=\left\lceil{\log(2B)\over\log Z_\theta}\right\rceil.  \tag{3}
\]
Then the exact terminal marker has precisely
\[
 A,\ C_1,\ldots,C_{J_\theta};                                  \tag{4}
\]
\(C_0\) and \(B\) are empty. An \(A\)-copy is \(n_z=up\), with \(p\) prime and \(2<p<Z_\theta\), and has the literal interval-prime marker weight. On \(C_j\),
\[
 n_z=vp_1\cdots p_j,\quad v\in\{1,2\},\quad
 Z_\theta\le p_1<\cdots<p_j,
\]
with weight \((-1)^j\mu(v)\).

Define on each copy
\[
 d_\star^{\rm tail}=
 \begin{cases}
 u=n_z/p,&A,\\
 p_1\cdots p_j=n_z/v,&C_j.
 \end{cases}                                                    \tag{5}
\]
Then \(n_z=d_\star^{\rm tail}v_\star\), \((d_\star^{\rm tail},v_\star)=1\), and
\[
 d_\star^{\rm tail}\ge H_P^2Q^{\tau/3}.                         \tag{6}
\]
The re-marker changes none of the selected source, orientation, actual \(G\), exact \(g\), original label, paired frequency, target \(N/g\), target-gcd, fixed-\(U\), high, source mask, smooth/projective amplitude, ordering/equal-cell, collision, deletion, provenance, or frozen-parent coordinates.

The exact parent inventory is
\[
 6/5\le\beta<4/3:\quad U_{\rm low}\ \text{only},                \tag{7}
\]
and
\[
 \beta\ge4/3:\quad
 E_{11},E_{21},E_{22},E_{\rm asym},
 U_{\rm low},U_{\rm gap},U_{\rm sup}.                           \tag{8}
\]
The complete \(C91\) family has already been subtracted and \(U_{\rm sh}\) is empty. Equation (8) is only an allowed list.

The literal nonresonant analytic supplier is now defined exactly. Fix an orientation, exact \(g\), frozen layer, parent, source/projective fiber, integer-frequency block \(F\le|h|<2F\), and dilator block
\[
 \mathcal D\le d_\star^{\rm tail}<2\mathcal D.
\]
For \(B/2\le n\le2B\), let \(\Lambda_{\mathcal D}(n)\) be the set of exact copies \(\lambda\) over \(n\) in this block, and let \(a_\lambda(n)\) be the literal marker weight. Put \(\mathscr A=N/g\ne0\). Let \(\widehat{\mathcal F}_{q,n}\) be the literal one-variable source Fourier transform in the chosen orientation. Define
\[
 c_\lambda(q,h)=a_\lambda(n)\mu(q){H_P\over n}
 \widehat{\mathcal F}_{q,n}(\varepsilon_{\rm or}h/n)
 e\!\left({\varepsilon_{\rm or}\mathscr A h\over qn}\right)
 \Xi_\lambda(q,h,n),                                           \tag{9}
\]
where \(\varepsilon_{\rm or}\in\{1,-1\}\) is the orientation sign and \(\Xi_\lambda\) is the product of every retained target-gcd, fixed-\(U\), high, source, parent, ordering, equality, collision, deletion and provenance factor. The exact local source is
\[
 \mathcal T_{F,\mathcal D}
 ={1\over H_P}\sum_{B/2\le n\le2B}
 \sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda_{\mathcal D}(n)}
 K_F(n,\lambda),                                               \tag{10}
\]
where
\[
 K_F(n,\lambda)=
 \sum_{\substack{Q\le q<2Q\\F\le|h|<2F\\(q,n)=1}}
 c_\lambda(q,h)e_q(-\mathscr A h n^{-1}).                      \tag{11}
\]
Write \(n=d_\lambda v_\lambda\), with \(d_\lambda=d_\star^{\rm tail}\). Define the exact post-reciprocity coefficient
\[
 \widetilde c_\lambda(q,h)=c_\lambda(q,h)
 e\!\left(-{\mathscr A h\over qd_\lambda v_\lambda}\right)
 e_{v_\lambda}\!\left(\mathscr A h(qd_\lambda)^{-1}\right).     \tag{12}
\]
Then
\[
 K_F(n,\lambda)=
 \sum_{q,h}\widetilde c_\lambda(q,h)
 e_{d_\lambda}\!\left(\mathscr A h(qv_\lambda)^{-1}\right).     \tag{13}
\]

Define the full row moment
\[
 \mathcal M_F(\mathcal D)=
 \sum_{B/2\le n\le2B}\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda_{\mathcal D}(n)}
 |K_F(n,\lambda)|^2.                                           \tag{14}
\]
For \(i=1,2\), let \((q_i,h_i)\) independently run over the support in (11), and put
\[
 \Delta=h_1q_2-h_2q_1.
\]
For \(S\in\{0,{\rm FR},{\rm NR}\}\), define
\[
 \mathcal M_F^{(S)}(\mathcal D)=
 \sum_{n,\lambda}\sum_{q_1,h_1,q_2,h_2}
 {\bf1}_S(\Delta,d_\lambda)\,
 \widetilde c_\lambda(q_1,h_1)
 \overline{\widetilde c_\lambda(q_2,h_2)}
 e_{d_\lambda}\!\left(
 \mathscr A\Delta(q_1q_2v_\lambda)^{-1}\right),                \tag{15}
\]
where all sums have exactly the support just specified and
\[
 {\bf1}_0={\bf1}_{\Delta=0},\quad
 {\bf1}_{\rm FR}={\bf1}_{\Delta\ne0,\ d_\lambda\mid\mathscr A\Delta},\quad
 {\bf1}_{\rm NR}={\bf1}_{\Delta\ne0,\ d_\lambda\nmid\mathscr A\Delta}.
\]
Thus
\[
 \mathcal M_F=\mathcal M_F^{(0)}
 +\mathcal M_F^{(\rm FR)}+\mathcal M_F^{(\rm NR)}.             \tag{16}
\]

Let \(\omega_F\) be the literal Fourier-decay scalar on this projective fiber, satisfying arbitrary fixed-order decay in \(F/H_P\). The range \(F>x^3\) is absolutely \(O_A(x^{-A})\) for every fixed \(A>0\). Uniformly for \(1\le F\le x^3\),
\[
 |\mathcal M_F^{(0)}(\mathcal D)|
 \le x^{o(1)}|\omega_F|^2BQF,                                  \tag{17}
\]
\[
 |\mathcal M_F^{(\rm FR)}(\mathcal D)|
 \le x^{o(1)}|\omega_F|^2{BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}.             \tag{18}
\]
Therefore the sole unproved sector estimate in the explicit moment (14)--(16) is
\[
 \boxed{\ 
 |\mathcal M_F^{(\rm NR)}(\mathcal D)|
 \le x^{o(1)}|\omega_F|^2{BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}
 \ }                                                           \tag{GA-NR-DIL}
\]
for the exact coefficient (12). No estimate for GA-NR-DIL, no claim on \(\mathscr W<Q^\tau\), no anatomy or parent sign, no unconditional good-\(\mathscr W\) payment, and no Goldbach conclusion are asserted.
e55b27d39c593164.proof:
The cutoff \(Q_0\) in fact \(7ffe3d237362a451\) is any fixed sufficiently-large constant for which the cited bounded-base theorem applies. Since \(\tau\) is fixed first, it may be chosen at least \(Q_\tau\). That fact then removes every selected post-low atom with \(Q\le Q_0\). Facts \(01b550792363535d\) and \(3f2f255ea6845a50\) make no subtraction on \(\beta\ge6/5\), so the present inherited tail has \(Q>Q_0\ge Q_\tau\) and retains every old marker sibling. Fact \(a71f777ad842c886\) recombines those siblings exactly to \(\mu(n_z)\).

The identities (1) follow from \(H_P=B/(GQ)\). On (2),
\[
 Z_\theta=\mathscr W^{1/2}\ge Q^{\tau/2}>2.
\]
Definition (3) gives \(Z_\theta^{J_\theta}\ge2B\), so \(Z_\theta^{J_\theta+1}>n_z\). Since \(\mu(n_z)\ne0\), \(n_z\) is squarefree. Also \(n_z\ge Q^{6/5}/2>2\), so \(C_0\) is empty. The product of prime divisors of \(n_z\) at most \(2\) is \(1\) or \(2\), never greater than \(S_\theta=2\), so \(B\) is empty. Fact \(7c1f38cfbb8d0569\) gives exactly (4) and the displayed weights.

On \(A\),
\[
 d_\star^{\rm tail}=n_z/p>{B\over2\mathscr W^{1/2}},
\]
and
\[
 {B/(2\mathscr W^{1/2})\over H_P^2Q^{\tau/3}}
 ={\mathscr W^{1/2}\over2Q^{\tau/3}}
 \ge Q^{\tau/6}/2\ge1,
\]
because \(Q\ge Q_\tau\). On \(C_j\),
\[
 d_\star^{\rm tail}=n_z/v\ge B/4
 \ge (B/\mathscr W)Q^{\tau/3}=H_P^2Q^{\tau/3},
\]
since \(Q^{2\tau/3}\ge4\), also implied by \(Q\ge Q_\tau\). Squarefreeness gives the coprimalities in (5). The re-marker changes only \(\mu(n_z)\), proving all provenance assertions.

Fact \(7ffe3d237362a451\) subtracts the complete \(C91\) family and proves \(U_{\rm sh}\) empty. Fact \(b01d255ce4c5ff24\) gives \(\beta_{\rm orig}\le\beta\). If \(\beta<4/3\), fact \(77d7a3419a07305c\) excludes the four endpoint parents, \(U_{\rm gap}\), and \(U_{\rm sup}\); hence only \(U_{\rm low}\) remains. If \(\beta\ge4/3\), removing only \(C91,U_{\rm sh}\) from the exhaustive nine-parent partition leaves (8). This proves the parent ledger.

We derive (10)--(13). Outer-gcd normalization gives, in the forward orientation, \(qm+nk=N/g\), with \(q\) complementary to marked \(n\). Poisson summation in \(m\), as in facts \(df9748efe29ab475\) and \(d8ba46800ba433c2\), gives the literal nonzero-frequency coefficient
\[
 n^{-1}\widehat{\mathcal F}_{q,n}(h/n)
\]
and the reciprocal phase modulo \(n\). Additive reciprocity moves the phase to modulus \(q\) and produces the Archimedean factor in (9). The identity
\[
 n^{-1}\widehat{\mathcal F}_{q,n}(\varepsilon_{\rm or}h/n)
 =H_P^{-1}(H_P/n)
 \widehat{\mathcal F}_{q,n}(\varepsilon_{\rm or}h/n)
\]
gives the exact prefactor in (10). Multiplication by the marker weight, complementary Möbius factor and the explicitly collected mask \(\Xi_\lambda\) gives (9)--(11). Reverse orientation is the exact interchange of divisor-complement pairs followed by \(h\mapsto-h\), which changes only \(\varepsilon_{\rm or}\).

Now \(n=d_\lambda v_\lambda\) and \((d_\lambda,v_\lambda)=1\). Since \((q,n)=1\),
\[
 e_q(-\mathscr A h(d_\lambda v_\lambda)^{-1})
 =
 e(-\mathscr A h/(qd_\lambda v_\lambda))
 e_{d_\lambda v_\lambda}(\mathscr A hq^{-1}).
\]
The Chinese remainder theorem gives
\[
 e_{d_\lambda v_\lambda}(\mathscr A hq^{-1})
 =
 e_{d_\lambda}(\mathscr A h(qv_\lambda)^{-1})
 e_{v_\lambda}(\mathscr A h(qd_\lambda)^{-1}).
\]
The two factors not having modulus \(d_\lambda\) are exactly those multiplying \(c_\lambda\) in (12). This proves (13) without changing the coefficient named in GA-NR-DIL.

Expanding (14) with (13) gives (15), because
\[
 h_1(q_1v_\lambda)^{-1}-h_2(q_2v_\lambda)^{-1}
 \equiv\Delta(q_1q_2v_\lambda)^{-1}\pmod {d_\lambda}.
\]
The three indicators are disjoint and sum to one, proving (16).

It remains to prove (17)--(18). Fact \(d8ba46800ba433c2\) gives arbitrary fixed-order Fourier decay. All physical scales and \(H_P\) are \(O(x)\). Repeated integration by parts with order chosen after \(A\) makes the total \(F>x^3\) contribution \(O_A(x^{-A})\), even after absolute summation over the polynomially many source variables. On \(F\le x^3\), all of
\[
 n,q,F,|\mathscr A|,|\Delta|
\]
are bounded by a fixed power of \(x\). Every fixed divisor-function loss is therefore \(x^{o(1)}\). After extracting \(\omega_F\), the dimensionless coefficient (12) on one fixed projective fiber is \(x^{o(1)}\).

For \(\Delta=0\), the two \(h_i\) have the same sign and uniquely
\[
 q_i=k_iq_0,\qquad |h_i|=k_ih_0,\qquad (q_0,h_0)=1.
\]
Dyadic decomposition of \(k_1,k_2\) gives \(O(QF\log(2QF))\) ordered proportional pairs. The total number of exact copies over \(n\asymp B\) is \(Bx^{o(1)}\): an \(A\)-integer has at most a divisor-bounded number of interval-prime copies, and a non-\(A\) integer has one unique \(C_j\)-copy. Absolute summation proves (17).

For \(\Delta\ne0\) and \(d_\lambda\mid\mathscr A\Delta\), a fixed coordinate quadruple permits at most
\[
 \tau(|\mathscr A\Delta|)=x^{o(1)}
\]
values of \(d_\lambda\). At fixed \(d_\lambda\asymp\mathcal D\), there are \(O(B/\mathcal D)\) complementary integers \(v_\lambda\), with \(x^{o(1)}\) copy multiplicity. There are \(O(Q^2F^2)\) coordinate quadruples. Absolute summation proves (18). The exact trichotomy (16) then shows that GA-NR-DIL is the only sector estimate not proved here.

The definition (2) was applied to a complete inherited source. Its complement \(\mathscr W<Q^\tau\) was neither re-marked nor estimated, and GA-NR-DIL remains an explicit unproved interface.

e58fc7c00f1683e6.title: EXACT SOURCE-PRESERVING SIX-ANATOMY GENERAL-MARKER LEDGER ON THE PRE-6/5 TOP SLIVER
e58fc7c00f1683e6.author: slava chan
e58fc7c00f1683e6.statement:
EXACT SOURCE-PRESERVING SIX-ANATOMY GENERAL-MARKER LEDGER ON THE PRE-6/5 TOP SLIVER.

Fix (0<kappale 1/100), put
[
 sigma=kappa/100,qquad
  eta_m=6/5-12sigma/5,qquad
  eta_2=6/5-13sigma/5,
]
and fix (0<eta<sigma) and (omega>0). Let
(T_{> eta_2,m sel}) be the same-selected-(N) residual of fact
(be94f5e014ad4d3d), and let (mathcal T_{m top,sel}) be its complete
projection onto
[
  eta_mle eta<6/5.                                           	ag{1}
]
For an exact outer gcd (g=(d,r)), write (d=ga,r=gb). In a forward
layer put
[
 Q=D/g,quad B=R/g=Q^ eta,quad n_z=b,quad s_z=a,quad G=M/Q,
]
and in a reverse layer put
[
 Q=R/g,quad B=D/g=Q^ eta,quad n_z=a,quad s_z=b,quad G=K/Q.
]
On the inherited dyadic support,
[
 B/2le n_zle2B.                                               	ag{2}
]

Freeze on every complete normalized layer the selected (N), original
source atom, active dyadic label, fixed (U), high and smooth/projective
labels, orientation, parent, actual (G), exact (g), target, paired
Fourier frequency and phase, target-gcd, prime-order/equal-cell, collision,
deletion and provenance coordinates. Before selecting any inherited marker
leaf, recombine every inherited general-marker anatomy and all of its
marker-dependent descendants at each fixed pre-marker atom. This restores
pointwise the literal factor (mu(n_z)).

Put
[
 L=Q^{ eta-1+sigma},qquad
 S_0=Q^{2 eta-2+3sigma},qquad
 Z=Q^{3/2- eta-3sigma}.                                      	ag{3}
]
Apply the general terminal anatomy identity of fact
(7c1f38cfbb8d0569) to the restored (mu(n_z)), with (J=4).
Then, for all sufficiently large normalized bases (Q), the exact
pointwise anatomy list is
[
 A,quad B,quad C1,quad C2,quad C3,quad C4.                	ag{4}
]
The small class (C0) is empty, and there is no (C5) or higher rough
class. The coefficients in (4) have exactly the interval-prime,
first-crossing stopping and ordered rough-prime formulas and Möbius signs
of fact (7c1f38cfbb8d0569).

Consequently (mathcal T_{m top,sel}) is the exact disjoint Cartesian
ledger with sole inherited parent (U_{m low}), both orientations,
[
 Q^{-sigma+eta}le G<
 Q^{Gamma_{BC}( eta)+omega},qquad
 Gamma_{BC}( eta)=max{0,(19 eta-20)/17},                 	ag{5}
]
all six anatomies in (4), and every frozen coordinate listed above retained.
Canonical target-gcd, order/equal-cell, collision, deletion and provenance
coordinates introduced inside a new anatomy are exact finite partitions;
recombining them returns that anatomy coefficient.

This is an exact source-preserving structural identity only. It makes no
estimate, assigns no sign to a proper projection or anatomy, and gives no
endpoint-parent, PMD, DCE, four-prime, Goldbach implication or Goldbach
conclusion.
e58fc7c00f1683e6.proof:
Fact (01b550792363535d) gives on the whole range
( eta_mle eta<6/5) the selected general-marker sliver with sole parent
(U_{m low}), both orientations, the (G)-range (5), and every literal
coordinate in the statement retained. Fact (be94f5e014ad4d3d) subtracts
only the complete projection ( eta_1< etale eta_2), where
( eta_2< eta_m). Hence its subtraction changes no atom in (1), so the
same top-sliver ledger and coordinates are inherited by
(T_{> eta_2,m sel}).

We first justify the layerwise restoration. Fact
(a71f777ad842c886) proves that on every nonzero Möbius atom the integers
(g,a,b) are pairwise coprime and
[
 mu(d)mu(r)=mu(s_z)mu(n_z).                                	ag{6}
]
It also proves that the complete inherited normalized marker, including
the small, interval-prime, stopping and every rough-prime leaf, is a
pointwise sign-preserving expansion of (mu(n_z)), while the other source
coordinates are unchanged. Thus summing all inherited marker leaves and
all marker-dependent descendants at a fixed pre-marker atom restores
exactly (mu(n_z)). No estimate or sign inequality is used. The
dyadic convention for the normalized larger-factor label gives (2).

We check the (J=4) hypotheses uniformly on (1). Since
(sigmale10^{-4}) and ( etage eta_m),
[
 {S_0over L}=Q^{ eta-1+2sigma}
 ge Q^{1/5-2sigma/5},
]
so (2le Lle S_0) for sufficiently large (Q). Since
( eta<6/5),
[
 {Zover L}=Q^{5/2-2 eta-4sigma}
 >Q^{1/10-4sigma}>1,                                        	ag{7}
]
so (L<Z). Also
[
 {Bover S_0}=Q^{2- eta-3sigma}
 >Q^{4/5-3sigma}.
]
Together with (2), this gives (n_z>S_0) for sufficiently large (Q);
therefore (C0) is empty.

Finally,
[
 {Z^5over 2B}
 ={1over2}Q^{15/2-6 eta-15sigma}
 >{1over2}Q^{3/10-15sigma}>1.                              	ag{8}
]
By (2), equation (8) gives (Z^5>n_z). The nonzero Möbius support makes
(n_z) squarefree. Equations (7)-(8) and the preceding inequalities are
exactly the hypotheses of fact (7c1f38cfbb8d0569) with (J=4), its
integer (r) replaced by (n_z), and its stopping height (S) replaced
by (S_0). That fact gives the mutually exclusive and exhaustive
alternatives (A,B,C1,C2,C3,C4), with their exact Möbius coefficients.
Since the partition is exhaustive at (J=4), no (C5) or higher class
occurs.

Multiply this pointwise identity by the unchanged factor
(mu(s_z)q_z), where (q_z) is the full transformed source amplitude
and its frozen coordinates, and sum within each fixed layer. Equation (6)
shows that the left side is the original source coefficient. Thus the new
marker neither creates nor removes an atom and preserves every frozen
coordinate. Any canonical refinements added after the anatomy is formed
are exact finite partitions and recombine to their parent anatomy. This
proves the ledger (4)-(5) and all scope assertions.

glossary.T_top,sel: The complete same-selected-N projection of T_>beta2,sel onto beta_m<=beta<6/5 after layerwise recombination of the inherited marker.
glossary.top-sliver six-anatomy ledger: The exact original-cutoff marker partition A,B,C1,C2,C3,C4 on beta_m<=beta<6/5 after restoring the literal normalized Möbius factor.

e59f666ecac4d4cb.title: FRACTIONAL-RAMARE DECOMPOSITION FOR rho_{1/2} WITH AN EXACT PRIME-POWER CORRECTION. Let B>=4, P>=2, Q_0>=1 and L>=0 be real numbers, let c be a positive integer, and put
e59f666ecac4d4cb.author: slava chan
e59f666ecac4d4cb.statement:
FRACTIONAL-RAMARE DECOMPOSITION FOR rho_{1/2} WITH AN EXACT PRIME-POWER CORRECTION. Let B>=4, P>=2, Q_0>=1 and L>=0 be real numbers, let c be a positive integer, and put
cal P={p prime:P<=p<2P},
omega_P(n)=#{p in cal P:p divides n},
b_{P,c}^{rho}(m)
 =rho_{1/2}(m)1_{(m,c)=1}/(1+omega_P(m)).                        (1)
For p in cal P with p|m put r=omega_P(m), a=v_p(m)+1, and define
e_P^{rho}(p,m)
 =rho_{1/2}(m)
  [(a-3/2)/(a r)+1/(2(1+r))].                                   (2)
The condition p|m implies r>=1 and a>=2, so (2) is defined.

Let cal D be any finite set of squarefree positive integers d in [Q_0,2Q_0). For each d in cal D choose an integer a_d with (a_d,d)=1 and a complex function V_d on the positive integers which vanishes outside [B,2B) and satisfies |V_d(n)|<=L. Define
D_d^{rho,med}
 =sum_{n>=1}rho_{1/2}(n)1_{(n,c)=1}1_{omega_P(n)>0}V_d(n)
  [1_{n congruent a_d (mod d)}
   -phi(d)^(-1)1_{(n,d)=1}],                                    (3)
T_d^{rho}
 =-1/2 sum_{p in cal P,(p,c)=1}sum_{m>=1}
 b_{P,c}^{rho}(m)V_d(pm)
  [1_{pm congruent a_d (mod d)}
   -phi(d)^(-1)1_{(pm,d)=1}],                                   (4)
and
E_d^{rho}
 =sum_{p in cal P,(p,c)=1}sum_{m>=1,p|m}
 e_P^{rho}(p,m)1_{(m,c)=1}V_d(pm)
  [1_{pm congruent a_d (mod d)}
   -phi(d)^(-1)1_{(pm,d)=1}].                                   (5)
Then exactly
D_d^{rho,med}=T_d^{rho}+E_d^{rho}                               (6)
for every d in cal D. Moreover
sum_{d in cal D}|E_d^{rho}|
 <<L(1+log(2BQ_0))^2(B/P+Q_0P),                                 (7)
with an absolute implied constant.

Thus a marked-prime sector of one rho_{1/2}-factor has an exact unrestricted prime-by-rho_{1/2} bilinear form plus a squareful selected-prime correction of the standard elementary size. The complementary sector omega_P(n)=0 is not included. No Type-II estimate for T_d^{rho}, projective literal-source match, complete HC-MED payment, or critical-tail conclusion is asserted.
e59f666ecac4d4cb.proof:
Write rho=rho_{1/2}. We first prove the coefficient identity underlying (6). Fix n with omega_P(n)=r>=1. Partition the selected primes p|n into those with v_p(n)=1 and those with v_p(n)>=2.

If v_p(n)=1 and m=n/p, then p does not divide m, omega_P(m)=r-1, and multiplicativity together with rho(p)=-1/2 gives
-1/2*rho(m)/(1+omega_P(m))
 =-1/2*[rho(n)/rho(p)]/r
 =rho(n)/r.                                                      (8)
Thus every selected prime occurring to the first power contributes rho(n)/r to the coprime part of (4).

Now suppose v_p(n)=a>=2 and put m=n/p. Then p|m, omega_P(m)=r, and fact 5999a1878276ac78 gives
rho(n)/rho(m)=rho(p^a)/rho(p^(a-1))=(a-3/2)/a.                   (9)
The contribution of this p to the unrestricted row (4) at n is
-1/2*rho(m)/(1+r).                                               (10)
Its contribution from (5) is, by (2),
rho(m)[(a-3/2)/(ar)+1/(2(1+r))].                                (11)
Adding (10) and (11), the terms with denominator 2(1+r) cancel, and (9) shows that the remainder is
rho(m)(a-3/2)/(ar)=rho(n)/r.                                    (12)
Therefore every one of the r distinct selected primes dividing n contributes exactly rho(n)/r after (4) and (5) are combined, regardless of its exponent. Summing the r contributions gives rho(n). If omega_P(n)=0, neither (4) nor (5) has a factorization n=pm with p in cal P, so both sides of the coefficient identity vanish. The c-coprimality is exact: if (n,c)=1, then every p,m in n=pm are coprime to c; conversely the displayed conditions (p,c)=(m,c)=1 imply (pm,c)=1.

Multiplying this termwise coefficient identity by V_d(n) and the centered progression bracket in (3), then summing over the finite support, proves (6).

It remains to bound the correction. On p|m one has r>=1 and a>=2. Hence
0<=(a-3/2)/a<1,
so, using |rho(m)|<=1 from fact 5999a1878276ac78,
|e_P^{rho}(p,m)|
 <=1/r+1/[2(1+r)]<=5/4.                                        (13)
Thus the absolute value of (5) is at most 5L/4 times the corresponding physical and principal counts of triples d,p,m with p|m and B<=pm<2B.

Write m=pu. If p|d, the physical congruence p^2u congruent a_d modulo d has no solution because (a_d,d)=1. If (p,d)=1, it fixes one residue class of u modulo d. Since B<=p^2u<2B, the number of u for fixed d,p is at most 2B/(p^2d)+1. Summing over p in [P,2P), using at most 2P possible integers p, gives at most 4B/(Pd)+2P for fixed d. Since #cal D<=2Q_0 and sum_{d in cal D}1/d<=2, the total physical count is O(B/P+Q_0P).

For the principal part, before the coprimality deletion there are at most 2B/p^2+1 values of u. Summing p gives O(B/P+P) for each d, multiplied by 1/phi(d). For squarefree d, the elementary estimate proved in fact 512ccc143b3d5fd9 gives
1/phi(d)<=(1+log d)^2/d.
Since d is in [Q_0,2Q_0) and #cal D<=2Q_0, summing over d gives
O((1+log(2Q_0))^2(B/P+P)).
Combining the physical and principal counts, using P<=Q_0P, and multiplying by 5L/4 proves (7).

glossary.D_d^{rho,med}: The centered d-progression discrepancy of rho_{1/2}, restricted to integers with a selected prime factor.
glossary.E_d^{rho}: The exact selected-prime-power correction in the fractional-Ramaré decomposition.
glossary.T_d^{rho}: The unrestricted prime-by-rho_{1/2} bilinear row in the fractional-Ramaré decomposition.
glossary.e_P^{rho}(p,m): The exact correction coefficient on p|m in the fractional-Ramaré identity.

e68c309611367942.title: POWER-SMALL EXCEPTIONAL LEDGER FOR THE SEPARATED ONE-ROUGH PMD SQUARE
e68c309611367942.author: slava chan
e68c309611367942.statement:
POWER-SMALL EXCEPTIONAL LEDGER FOR THE SEPARATED ONE-ROUGH PMD SQUARE.

Fix C_A>=1, 0<kappa<1/10, 0<=sigma<3kappa, and 0<delta<1/10. Let Q be sufficiently large and let
  1<=H<=Q^(1/3-kappa),
  1<=V<=H^2 Q^sigma,
  P=QH/V>=2.                                                (1)
Let A be a nonzero integer with |A|<=Q^C_A. Let Phi be a fixed smooth function supported in [-2,-1] union [1,2], and put
  K_{v,p}(r)=|Phihat(-Hr/(vp))|,
where Phihat is as in fact 1a4654c1b828f1f6. Restrict v,p,q_1,q_2 to
  V<=v<2V,
  P<=p<2P with p prime,
  Q<=q_i<2Q,
and require p not dividing vq_1q_2. For integers r divisible by v put
  F=A(q_2-q_1)-r q_1q_2,
  I_p(F)=1_{p|F}-1/p.                                      (2)
For a set S of such tuples define its PMD square ledger by
  E(S)=QH sum_S K_{v,p}(r)|I_p(F)|.                         (3)

Put
  R_small=Q^(1-delta)/H,
  G_large=H Q^delta.                                       (4)
Then, for every epsilon>0,

(a) E(0<|r|<=R_small, F nonzero) <<Q^(4-delta+epsilon).

(b) E(gcd(q_1,q_2)>=G_large, r nonzero, F nonzero)
    <<Q^(4-delta+epsilon).

(c) E(r nonzero, F=0)<<Q^(2+epsilon)H^2/V.

(d) E(r=0)<<Q^(3+epsilon)H(V+H).

There is also a self-contained pre-Poisson diagonal ledger. Let u_{h,v,p} and c_q be arbitrary complex numbers of magnitude at most Q^epsilon, supported on integers H<=|h|<2H, V<=v<2V, primes P<=p<2P, and Q<=q<2Q, respectively. Let z_{h,v,p,q} be arbitrary complex numbers of modulus one. Define
  S_sep=H^(-1)sum_{h,v,p}u_{h,v,p}
                    sum_q c_q z_{h,v,p,q}.                 (5)
Cauchy in (h,v,p), followed by expansion of the q-square, gives a q_1=q_2 diagonal contribution to |S_sep|^2 of size
  <<Q^(3+epsilon)H^2.                                      (6)

Consequently (a)-(d) and (6) together are <<Q^(4-eta) for some eta=eta(kappa,sigma,delta)>0 after the harmless epsilon losses are chosen sufficiently small. Thus on this separated outer-gcd-one model the only unremoved PMD sector has
  q_1 not equal q_2,
  |r|>Q^(1-delta)/H,
  gcd(q_1,q_2)<H Q^delta,
  A(q_2-q_1)-r q_1q_2 nonzero.                              (7)
No estimate for (7), no separation of the literal frozen-parent source amplitude, and no outer common-gcd assembly is asserted.
e68c309611367942.proof:
First, the hypotheses imply
  P/H=Q/V>=Q^(1/3+2kappa-sigma),                            (8)
which tends to infinity because sigma<3kappa. Hence p>2H for sufficiently large Q, as required by the exact centered transform in fact 1a4654c1b828f1f6.

We use throughout the rapid decay
  K_{v,p}(r)<<_{Phi,J}(1+|r|H/(vP))^(-J),                  (9)
uniformly because p is comparable to P. Since v is comparable to V and VP=QH, the natural r-length vP/H is comparable to Q. Tails beyond any fixed polynomial power of Q are smaller than every prescribed negative power after choosing J large. On the remaining polynomial range, |F| is polynomially bounded in Q, and the elementary divisor bound gives tau(|F|)<<Q^epsilon for F nonzero.

For (a), fix v,r,q_1,q_2 with F nonzero. The primes p for which the indicator in I_p(F) is one are divisors of F, so their number is O(Q^epsilon). The centered 1/p part also has total size O(1), since p is comparable to P. As K is bounded, the p-sum is O(Q^epsilon). Moreover
  sum_{V<=v<2V} #{r: v|r, 0<|r|<=R_small}
  <<sum_{v comparable to V}R_small/v<<R_small.             (10)
There are O(Q^2) ordered q-pairs. Multiplying (10) by QH and using (4) proves (a).

For (b), the number of ordered q-pairs with gcd(q_1,q_2)>=G_large is
  <<sum_{g>=G_large}(Q/g)^2<<Q^2/G_large.                  (11)
For each v the total r-kernel mass is O(P/H)=O(Q/V), by (9), and summing v comparable to V gives O(Q). For the indicator part, divisor switching in p costs Q^epsilon for every nonzero F; the centered part costs O(1). Thus (11) gives
  E<<QH Q^(1+epsilon)Q^2/G_large
    =Q^(4+epsilon)H/G_large
    =Q^(4-delta+epsilon).

For (c), assume r is nonzero and F=0. Define
  X=A-rq_1,  Y=A+rq_2.
Then
  XY=A^2+r[A(q_2-q_1)-rq_1q_2]=A^2.                       (12)
If X=A, then Y=A and the equations rq_1=A-X and rq_2=Y-A force rq_1=rq_2=0, contradicting r nonzero and q_i>0. Thus X is not A. After choosing a signed divisor X of A^2 and putting Y=A^2/X, every solution satisfies
  rq_1=A-X,  rq_2=Y-A.                                    (13)
The nonzero integer r is therefore a signed divisor of the nonzero integer A-X. There are O(Q^epsilon) choices for X and O(Q^epsilon) choices for r; q_1,q_2 are then fixed by (13). Thus there are O(Q^epsilon) triples (q_1,q_2,r). For each r there are O(Q^epsilon) possible v dividing r, and the p-sum is O(P). Therefore
  E<<QH P Q^epsilon=Q^(2+epsilon)H^2/V,
proving (c).

For (d), K_{v,p}(0)=|Phihat(0)|. If p does not divide A, the congruence p|A(q_2-q_1) is q_1 congruent q_2 modulo p. The number of such q-pairs is O(Q+Q^2/p), while the centered term contributes O(Q^2/p). Summing p comparable to P gives O(PQ+Q^2). If p divides A, all q-pairs satisfy the congruence; the number of such p is O(Q^epsilon), because p divides the fixed nonzero polynomially bounded integer A. Thus at each v the r=0 p,q-pair sum is <<Q^epsilon(PQ+Q^2). After summing O(V) values of v and multiplying by QH,
  E(r=0)<<Q^(1+epsilon)H V(PQ+Q^2)
          <<Q^(3+epsilon)(H^2+HV),                          (14)
because VP=QH. This is (d).

For the diagonal assertion, Cauchy applied to (5) gives
  |S_sep|^2<=H^(-2)(HVP)
    sum_{h,v,p}|u_{h,v,p}|^2
       |sum_q c_qz_{h,v,p,q}|^2.                           (15)
After expanding the last square, its q_1=q_2 diagonal is at most Q^(1+epsilon) for every h,v,p. The remaining h,v,p sum has O(HVP) terms and the first Cauchy multiplier is H^(-2)(HVP)=VP/H=Q. Hence the diagonal in (15) is
  <<Q * HVP * Q^(1+epsilon)=Q^(3+epsilon)H^2,
because VP=QH. This proves (6).

Finally,
  Q^3HV<=Q^3H^3Q^sigma<=Q^(4-3kappa+sigma),
  Q^3H^2<=Q^(4-(1/3+2kappa)),
and the bound in (c) is smaller still. Because sigma<3kappa, these exponents and the two Q^(4-delta+epsilon) bounds are all below four by a fixed amount after epsilon is chosen small. This proves the final assertion. Fact 1a4654c1b828f1f6 supplies the exact centered incidence represented by this ledger; the present proof only counts its declared exceptional sectors.

glossary.G_large: The cutoff H Q^delta above which common gcd(q_1,q_2) is paid by pair counting.
glossary.PMD square ledger: The centered prime-modulus divisibility contribution after the separated h,v,p Cauchy step and exact h-Poisson transform.
glossary.R_small: The cutoff Q^(1-delta)/H below which nonzero dual frequencies are paid by divisor switching.
glossary.S_sep: A fully defined bounded separated pre-Poisson atom used only to audit the q-diagonal Cauchy cost.

e6c2db667302ed26.title: C-qSRC-PV-BV: POLYA--VINOGRADOV SHARPENING OF THE DILATOR-VARIATION HANDOFF
e6c2db667302ed26.author: slava chan
e6c2db667302ed26.statement:
C-qSRC-PV-BV: POLYA--VINOGRADOV SHARPENING OF THE DILATOR-VARIATION HANDOFF.

Let m>=2 be squarefree and let chi be a nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo m. For every finite integer interval I,
max_{J subset I, J an interval}|sum_{d in J}chi(d)|
 <=tau(m)sqrt(m)(1+log m).                                      (1)
Consequently, if A(d) is a complex sequence supported on
D<=d<2D
and extended by zero outside this interval, then
|sum_{D<=d<2D}chi(d)A(d)|
 <=tau(m)sqrt(m)(1+log m)
   sum_{d in Z}|A(d+1)-A(d)|.                                   (2)

Apply (2) to the exact profile A_{m,c,chi}(d) and variation V_{m,c,chi} of fact eb01e7b374521a0c. Every supported physical conductor is squarefree and satisfies m<4Q^2. Therefore
|Zhat_{m,c}(chi)|
 <=x^{o(1)}Q V_{m,c,chi}.                                       (3)
Hence the relaxed variation supplier
sum_{m>=2}sum_{c (mod m)}^*1/phi(m)
 sum_{chi!=chi_0}|G_{m,c}(chi)|V_{m,c,chi}
 <=x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 BQF^2/D                                (C-qSRC-PV-BV-SUP)
implies
|C-qSRC>=2|
 <=x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 BQ^2F^2/D.                              (4)

Compared with C-qSRC-BV-SUP in fact eb01e7b374521a0c, the permitted aggregate variation mass is larger by one factor Q. This is a strict theorem-interface improvement in the range D>Q^2. It does not prove C-qSRC-PV-BV-SUP: the inherited provenance/source profile may still have large variation. It also does not estimate N-qSRC-SUP of fact bab94ab4a0e20bc0, the F>Q principal source, the small-D projected-incidence branch, the tail, or Goldbach.
e6c2db667302ed26.proof:
Every Dirichlet character chi modulo squarefree m is induced by a unique primitive character chi_star of conductor r dividing m. Since chi is nonprincipal, r>1. Put s=m/r. Squarefreeness gives gcd(r,s)=1, and
chi(d)=chi_star(d)1_{gcd(d,s)=1}.                                (5)
Use Mobius inversion:
1_{gcd(d,s)=1}=sum_{e|gcd(d,s)}mu(e).
For any integer interval J,
sum_{d in J}chi(d)
 =sum_{e|s}mu(e)chi_star(e)
   sum_{k:ek in J}chi_star(k),                                   (6)
because gcd(e,r)=1.

We prove the primitive Polya--Vinogradov bound directly. Let tau(chi_star)=sum_{a mod r}chi_star(a)e_r(a). Primitivity gives
|tau(chi_star)|=sqrt(r)
and finite Fourier inversion gives, for every integer k,
chi_star(k)
 =1/tau(conjugate(chi_star))
   sum_{a mod r}conjugate(chi_star(a))e_r(ak).                   (7)
For an interval of consecutive k, the geometric progression at frequency a has magnitude at most
min(H,1/(2||a/r||)),
where H is the interval length and || || is distance to the nearest integer. Summing this bound for 1<=a<r and using
sum_{1<=a<=r/2}1/a<=1+log r
gives
|max_J sum_{k in J}chi_star(k)|
 <=sqrt(r)(1+log r)                                              (8)
after changing an absolute constant, which is absorbed by the displayed right side of (1).

There are tau(s)<=tau(m) divisors e in (6), and sqrt(r)(1+log r)<=sqrt(m)(1+log m). Equations (6)-(8) prove (1).

Let S(t)=sum_{d in I,d<=t}chi(d). Endpoint-inclusive discrete summation by parts, with A zero-extended, gives
sum_{d in I}chi(d)A(d)
 =-sum_{d in Z}S(d)[A(d+1)-A(d)].
Use (1) and take absolute values to prove (2).

Fact eb01e7b374521a0c proves
Zhat_{m,c}(chi)=sum_d chi(d)A_{m,c,chi}(d)
and defines V_{m,c,chi} as the variation on the right of (2). Fact d5cfc4a905989cc8 and fact eb01e7b374521a0c give squarefree m and m<4Q^2. Since tau(m)(1+log m)=x^{o(1)}, (2) gives (3).

Finally, the exact character expansion is
C-qSRC>=2
 =sum_{m,c}1/phi(m)sum_{chi!=chi_0}
  G_{m,c}(chi)Zhat_{m,c}(chi).
Apply the triangle inequality and (3), then insert C-qSRC-PV-BV-SUP. This proves (4). No estimate of the relaxed ledger was assumed beyond its displayed conditional statement, so all exclusions follow.

glossary.C-qSRC-PV-BV-SUP: The relaxed aggregate dilator-variation supplier obtained from Polya--Vinogradov.
glossary.chi_star: The primitive Dirichlet character inducing chi.

e705401df9f0709e.title: Fix real numbers L>=1 and epsilon>0. Let P>=2, let I be a nonempty finite set, and for every u in I let q_u be an integer with 2<=q_u<=P^L, let O_u be a subset of {1,2,3,4}, let H_u be a complex Hilbert space, and let v_u belong to H_u. Form the expanded Hilbert direct sum with one copy of H_u for every triple (u,e,F) such that e divides q_u and F is a subset of O_u, and give that copy the coefficient vector
e705401df9f0709e.author: slava chan
e705401df9f0709e.statement:
Fix real numbers L>=1 and epsilon>0. Let P>=2, let I be a nonempty finite set, and for every u in I let q_u be an integer with 2<=q_u<=P^L, let O_u be a subset of {1,2,3,4}, let H_u be a complex Hilbert space, and let v_u belong to H_u. Form the expanded Hilbert direct sum with one copy of H_u for every triple (u,e,F) such that e divides q_u and F is a subset of O_u, and give that copy the coefficient vector
v_{u,e,F}=mu(q_u/e)(-1)^{|F|}v_u.
Then
sum_{u in I}sum_{e dividing q_u}sum_{F subset O_u}||v_{u,e,F}||^2
=sum_{u in I}(sum_{e dividing q_u}mu(q_u/e)^2)2^{|O_u|}||v_u||^2
<=16 max_{u in I}tau(q_u) sum_{u in I}||v_u||^2
<<_{L,epsilon}P^epsilon sum_{u in I}||v_u||^2.
Consequently the expanded coefficient norm is at most C_{L,epsilon}P^{epsilon/2} times the base coefficient norm for a constant C_{L,epsilon}. The constant power P^{epsilon/2} can be replaced by P^eta for every fixed eta>0 after changing the implied constant.

In the centered conductor identity of fact 676c6a2cb3ebf7cc and the four-prime face ledger of fact 697d75223ebc7a8a, this shows that orthogonally recording every signed quotient-conductor term and every nonzero overlap face creates only a subpolynomial coefficient multiplicity when all conductors are polynomially bounded in P. This is solely a coefficient-side duplication statement. It does not allow raw uncentered quotient moments, because their common zero mode overlaps as described in fact 676c6a2cb3ebf7cc; it does not estimate the expanded coordinate energy, the number or weights of distinct physical incidences, external window-cell multiplicity, or the cross-cell operator.
e705401df9f0709e.proof:
For each fixed triple (u,e,F), the scalar mu(q_u/e)(-1)^{|F|} has squared absolute value mu(q_u/e)^2. Hence
||v_{u,e,F}||^2=mu(q_u/e)^2||v_u||^2.
There are exactly 2^{|O_u|} subsets F of O_u. Summing first over F and then over e gives the displayed equality. Since |O_u|<=4, one has 2^{|O_u|}<=16. Also mu(n)^2<=1, so
sum_{e dividing q_u}mu(q_u/e)^2<=sum_{e dividing q_u}1=tau(q_u).
Because I is nonempty, max_{u in I}tau(q_u) is defined. This proves the first inequality.

For completeness, we prove the needed divisor bound. Let alpha=epsilon/L>0. Choose a real number Y>=2 so large that 2<=p^alpha for every prime p>=Y. If a>=1, then a+1<=2^a, hence for p>=Y,
a+1<=2^a<=p^{alpha a}.
For each of the finitely many primes p<Y, the sequence (a+1)p^{-alpha a} for integers a>=0 is bounded; let C_{p,alpha} be its supremum. Put C_alpha=product_{p<Y}C_{p,alpha}, a finite constant. If n=product_p p^{a_p}, then
tau(n)=product_p(a_p+1)<=C_alpha product_p p^{alpha a_p}=C_alpha n^alpha.
Apply this to n=q_u. Since q_u<=P^L,
tau(q_u)<=C_alpha q_u^{epsilon/L}<=C_alpha P^epsilon.
Substitution into the first inequality proves the asserted estimate, and taking nonnegative square roots proves the norm bound. Given any eta>0, repeat the argument with epsilon=2eta to obtain P^eta on the norm side.

Fact 676c6a2cb3ebf7cc supplies the signed coefficients mu(q_u/e) only after the complete moments have been centered, and fact 697d75223ebc7a8a supplies the overlap signs (-1)^{|F|}. Therefore the abstract coefficient array is exactly the categorical duplication produced by those two ledgers. The proof never compares or sums the underlying coordinate vectors and never introduces external-cell labels, which proves the final scope statement.

glossary.C_{L,epsilon}: A positive constant depending only on L and epsilon.
glossary.base coefficient norm: The square root of the sum over u of ||v_u||^2.
glossary.e: A positive divisor of q_u indexing a quotient-conductor term.
glossary.expanded coefficient norm: The square root of the sum over u,e,F of ||v_{u,e,F}||^2.
glossary.q_u: The integer primitive conductor attached to base leaf u.
glossary.tau(q_u): The number of positive divisors of q_u.
glossary.v_{u,e,F}: The signed coefficient-vector copy indexed by base leaf u, quotient conductor e and overlap face F.

e7458a42217c2756.title: RECIPROCAL-DIFFERENCE SLOPE COMPRESSION AND NATURAL DIAGONAL LOCAL ENERGY
e7458a42217c2756.author: slava chan
e7458a42217c2756.statement:
RECIPROCAL-DIFFERENCE SLOPE COMPRESSION AND NATURAL DIAGONAL LOCAL ENERGY.

Let Q>=2 and let cal Q be any finite set of positive integers in [Q,2Q). For an ordered pair (q_1,q_2) in cal Q^2 define its rational reciprocal-difference slope
  lambda(q_1,q_2)=(q_2-q_1)/(q_1q_2)=1/q_1-1/q_2.          (1)
For two ordered pairs put
  Delta=(q_2-q_1)q_3q_4-(q_4-q_3)q_1q_2.                   (2)
Then Delta=0 if and only if
  lambda(q_1,q_2)=lambda(q_3,q_4).                          (3)

Every nonzero slope has at most Q^epsilon representations by pairs in cal Q, for every epsilon>0 and sufficiently large Q. More explicitly, write a nonzero slope in lowest terms as u/w, where u is a nonzero integer, w is a positive integer, and gcd(|u|,w)=1. Every representation lambda(q_1,q_2)=u/w satisfies
  (w-uq_1)(w+uq_2)=w^2,                                    (4)
and is uniquely determined by the signed divisor X=w-uq_1 of w^2 through
  q_1=(w-X)/u,
  q_2=(w^2/X-w)/u.                                         (5)
The zero-slope fibre consists exactly of the pairs (q,q), q in cal Q.

Let a_q be arbitrary complex coefficients supported on cal Q and define the full reciprocal-slope energy

E_slope=sum_{lambda in Q}
  |sum_{(q_1,q_2) in cal Q^2, lambda(q_1,q_2)=lambda}
       a_{q_1} conjugate(a_{q_2})|^2.                       (6)

Then for every epsilon>0,
  E_slope<<_epsilon Q^epsilon (sum_{q in cal Q}|a_q|^2)^2. (7)
In particular, if |a_q|<=Q^epsilon, then E_slope<<Q^(2+epsilon), after adjusting epsilon.

This is also the exact integer-diagonal contribution to every short-window modular local energy. Precisely, let p be a prime not dividing any q in cal Q, let A be an integer, and define
  rho_p(q_1,q_2)=A(q_2-q_1)(q_1q_2)^(-1) modulo p.          (8)
Let W_p be any complex function on Z/pZ with |W_p|<=1. Define the Delta=0 part of the W_p-local modular slope energy by

L_{p,0}(W_p)=sum_{lambda in Q}
 |W_p(rho_p(q_1,q_2))|^2
 |sum_{(q_1,q_2) in cal Q^2, lambda(q_1,q_2)=lambda}
       a_{q_1}conjugate(a_{q_2})|^2,                        (9)
where rho_p(q_1,q_2) is independent of the chosen pair inside a fixed lambda-fibre. Then
  L_{p,0}(W_p)<=E_slope
  <<_epsilon Q^epsilon(sum_q|a_q|^2)^2.                    (10)
Thus for coefficients of bounded size, the Delta=0 contribution is at most Q^(2+epsilon), uniformly for an indicator of an arbitrary short residue interval, a smooth short-window weight, or any other bounded local weight. This is the natural diagonal scale. No estimate for the complementary Delta nonzero modular coincidences is asserted.
e7458a42217c2756.proof:
Equation (3) follows by cross multiplication of (1), and gives exactly (2).

Fix a nonzero reduced slope u/w. The equation lambda(q_1,q_2)=u/w is
  u q_1q_2=w(q_2-q_1).                                     (11)
Expanding gives
  (w-uq_1)(w+uq_2)
  =w^2+uw(q_2-q_1)-u^2q_1q_2=w^2,                          (12)
which is (4). Conversely, any signed divisor X of w^2 for which the two expressions in (5) are positive integers satisfies (12), hence (11). Thus (5) is an injective parametrization of the fibre by signed divisors of w^2.

If the slope has a representation with q_i in [Q,2Q), its reduced denominator satisfies w<=q_1q_2<=4Q^2. Fact e705401df9f0709e supplies the fixed-power divisor estimate tau(n)<<Q^epsilon for integers n of polynomial size in Q. Applying it to w^2<=16Q^4 shows that the number of signed divisors of w^2, and therefore every nonzero fibre size, is O(Q^epsilon). If lambda=0, equation (1) gives q_1=q_2, proving the zero-fibre assertion.

For each slope lambda let cal F_lambda be its pair fibre. Cauchy's inequality gives, for lambda nonzero,
  |sum_{(q_1,q_2) in cal F_lambda}a_{q_1}conjugate(a_{q_2})|^2
  <=|cal F_lambda|
    sum_{(q_1,q_2) in cal F_lambda}|a_{q_1}|^2|a_{q_2}|^2.
Summing over the disjoint nonzero fibres and using their O(Q^epsilon) size gives at most
  Q^epsilon sum_{q_1,q_2}|a_{q_1}|^2|a_{q_2}|^2
  =Q^epsilon(sum_q|a_q|^2)^2.                              (13)
For lambda=0, the inner sum is sum_q|a_q|^2, whose square is already the right side of (13) without Q^epsilon. This proves (7).

If two pairs lie in the same rational slope fibre, cross multiplication gives Delta=0. Since p does not divide any q, reduction modulo p gives
  (q_2-q_1)(q_1q_2)^(-1)
  congruent (q_4-q_3)(q_3q_4)^(-1) modulo p.
Multiplication by A shows that rho_p is constant on the fibre, so (9) is well defined. Since |W_p|<=1, deleting its squared factor from each nonnegative term in (9) only enlarges the sum, giving L_{p,0}(W_p)<=E_slope. Equation (10) follows from (7), and the final bounded-coefficient specialization follows from #cal Q<=Q.

glossary.Delta: The cross-multiplied determinant whose vanishing is equality of two reciprocal-difference slopes.
glossary.L_{p,0}: The Delta=0 part of a bounded-window modular slope local energy.
glossary.reciprocal-difference slope: The rational number 1/q_1-1/q_2 attached to an ordered modulus pair.

e77206678441fe0d.title: EXACT EXPONENT CONSEQUENCES AND VERY-GIANT NO-FIT FOR THE ZHANG-ELIGIBLE GIANT1 CONSUMER. Let X>1, epsilon>0, delta>=0, and Q_1,Q_2,P>=2 satisfy the scale hypotheses of fact 868d2c2698f73b86:
e77206678441fe0d.author: slava chan
e77206678441fe0d.statement:
EXACT EXPONENT CONSEQUENCES AND VERY-GIANT NO-FIT FOR THE ZHANG-ELIGIBLE GIANT1 CONSUMER. Let X>1, epsilon>0, delta>=0, and Q_1,Q_2,P>=2 satisfy the scale hypotheses of fact 868d2c2698f73b86:
Q_1Q_2=X^(1/2+delta),                                           (1)
Q_1^7Q_2^12<X^(4-10epsilon),                                    (2)
Q_1X^(2delta+epsilon)<P<X^(1-epsilon)/Q_1.                      (3)
Put
u=log(Q_1)/log X,qquad v=log(Q_2)/log X,qquad
pi_P=log(P)/log X.                                               (4)
Then
u>2/5+(12/5)delta+2epsilon,                                     (5)
v<1/10-(7/5)delta-2epsilon,                                     (6)
2/5+(22/5)delta+3epsilon<pi_P
 <3/5-(12/5)delta-3epsilon.                                     (7)
In particular, no Zhang factor box of fact 487a65cdbb7ab2fc exists at a prime scale
P>=X^(3/5-3epsilon).                                             (8)
Also, existence of such a box forces
delta<1/14-(10/7)epsilon.                                       (9)
These are necessary conditions only. They do not prove that any box in the remaining range exists or estimate a GIANT1 row.
e77206678441fe0d.proof:
Taking logarithms base X in (1) gives
u+v=1/2+delta.                                                   (10)
Taking logarithms in (2) gives
7u+12v<4-10epsilon.                                              (11)
Substitute v=1/2+delta-u from (10) into (11):
7u+12(1/2+delta-u)<4-10epsilon.
Thus
6+12delta-5u<4-10epsilon,
which is equivalent to (5). Equation (6) follows by subtracting (5) from (10):
v=1/2+delta-u
 <1/2+delta-[2/5+(12/5)delta+2epsilon]
 =1/10-(7/5)delta-2epsilon.

The lower inequality in (3) gives
pi_P>u+2delta+epsilon.
Insert (5) to obtain the lower inequality in (7). The upper inequality in (3) gives
pi_P<1-epsilon-u.
Insert (5) to obtain the upper inequality in (7).

Since delta>=0, the upper inequality in (7) implies
pi_P<3/5-3epsilon.
This contradicts pi_P>=3/5-3epsilon, proving (8).

Finally Q_2>=2 gives v>0. Combining this with (6) forces
1/10-(7/5)delta-2epsilon>0.
Rearranging gives (9). No sufficiency assertion follows from these one-way algebraic consequences.

glossary.pi_P: The base-X logarithmic exponent of the giant-prime scale P.
glossary.u: The base-X logarithmic exponent of the first Zhang modulus factor Q_1.
glossary.v: The base-X logarithmic exponent of the second Zhang modulus factor Q_2.

e7e8025bde57f04f.title: EXACT ALL-BAND SOURCE--DENSITY--LEAKAGE RECOMBINATION AND ITS PRE-CAUCHY PERPENDICULAR SUPPLIER. Let cal I be a finite index set. For i in cal I let b_i be complex, put
e7e8025bde57f04f.author: slava chan
e7e8025bde57f04f.statement:
EXACT ALL-BAND SOURCE--DENSITY--LEAKAGE RECOMBINATION AND ITS PRE-CAUCHY PERPENDICULAR SUPPLIER. Let cal I be a finite index set. For i in cal I let b_i be complex, put
C_src=sum_i |b_i|^2>0,                                     (1)
and let n_i be a positive integer, A_i an integer, H_i>0, and cal Q_i a finite set of positive integers q with gcd(q,n_i)=1. For every i,q let F_{i,q} be smooth and compactly supported on R, with Fourier transform
Fhat_{i,q}(xi)=integral_R F_{i,q}(t)e(-xi t)dt.             (2)
Let kappa_i(q,t) be a specified literal complex multiplier for q in cal Q_i and nonzero t in Z, and assume
sup_{t nonzero}|kappa_i(q,t)|<infinity                     (3)
for every i,q. It may encode an exact height block, projective copy, conductor face, collision condition, deletion, or provenance condition; no independence is assumed. Define the selected signed q-row
z_i=H_i sum_{q in cal Q_i}mu(q)n_i^(-1)
       sum_{t in Z,t nonzero} kappa_i(q,t)
       Fhat_{i,q}(t/n_i)e_{n_i}(A_i t qbar),                (4)
where qbar is the inverse of q modulo n_i. Define its complete physical-source, zero-density, and omitted-family vectors by
u_i=H_i sum_{q in cal Q_i}mu(q)
       sum_{m in Z; qm congruent A_i modulo n_i}F_{i,q}(m), (5)
d_i=H_i sum_{q in cal Q_i}mu(q)n_i^(-1)Fhat_{i,q}(0),       (6)
r_i=H_i sum_{q in cal Q_i}mu(q)n_i^(-1)
       sum_{t in Z,t nonzero}(1-kappa_i(q,t))
       Fhat_{i,q}(t/n_i)e_{n_i}(A_i t qbar).                (7)
All series in (4) and (7) converge absolutely. Coordinatewise and in the earlier signed assembly,
z_i=u_i-d_i-r_i,                                            (8)
sum_i b_i z_i
 =sum_i b_i u_i-sum_i b_i d_i-sum_i b_i r_i.               (9)
Thus every actual source summand in u_i lies on an integer triple
q m+n_i k=A_i.                                              (10)
No source support is assigned to the selected row z_i itself; every failure of the literal multiplier to retain the complete nonzero family is carried exactly by r_i.

For a vector w=(w_i), define its perpendicular projection away from the source-coefficient line by
(P_b^perp w)_i
 =w_i-[sum_j b_j w_j/C_src]conjugate(b_i).                  (11)
Let D_pre(z) be the Lagrange defect
D_pre(z)=(1/2)sum_{i,j}
 |conjugate(b_i)z_j-conjugate(b_j)z_i|^2.                  (12)
Put w=u-d. Then exactly
D_pre(z)=C_src ||P_b^perp(w-r)||_2^2                       (13)
 =C_src{||P_b^perp w||_2^2+||P_b^perp r||_2^2
       -2 Re <P_b^perp w,P_b^perp r>},                     (14)
and consequently
D_pre(z)>=C_src
 [max(0,||P_b^perp w||_2-||P_b^perp r||_2)]^2.             (15)
Also
|sum_i b_i r_i|<=C_src^(1/2)||r||_2,
||P_b^perp r||_2<=||r||_2.                                 (16)
Equations (13)-(16) are a quantitative all-band supplier for the earlier signed PMD slot: one may prove non-collinearity for the complete source-minus-density vector w and pay the literal finite-band leakage r, without asserting false pointwise hard support for a proper band.

There is an absolute high-tail specialization. Suppose for each i,q there are M_{i,q}>0, L_{i,q}>=0, H_{0,i,q}=n_i/M_{i,q}>=1, and for every integer J>=2 a constant C_{J,i,q} such that
|Fhat_{i,q}(xi)|
 <=C_{J,i,q}M_{i,q}L_{i,q}
   (1+M_{i,q}|xi|)^(-J).                                   (17)
If kappa_i(q,t)=1 whenever 0<|t|<Y H_{0,i,q}, for some Y>=1, and |kappa_i(q,t)|<=1 otherwise, then
|r_i|<=2H_i sum_{q in cal Q_i}
 C'_{J}C_{J,i,q}L_{i,q}Y^(1-J),                            (18)
where C'_J depends only on J. Thus restoration of every low band up to YH_0 leaves a power-decaying high-frequency correction. Formula (18) does not apply to a lone dyadic band, because its omitted low frequencies are then part of r_i.

For the natural forward C1 negative-frequency coordinate of fact ee6886ba9ed393f1, take n_i=vp, H_i=H_P, t=-h,
F_{i,q}=F_{g,cq,n_i},
and
kappa_i(q,t)=1_{t=-h_i} chi_nat(v,p,h_i,q)                 (19)
for a literal fixed-height coordinate i=(c,v,p,h_i), with every h-independent outer predicate absorbed into cal Q_i. The literal multiplier in (19) is bounded. Then (4) is exactly the natural q-row inside fact 87fee9c7e02513f9 after the compensating Archimedean phases cancel. The vector u in (5) retains the genuine hard-source condition; after target-gcd descent every nonzero summand satisfies
qm+n_i k_red=A_i, k_red>0.                                 (20)
More precisely, if the short full-conductor refinement uses a nonempty prime set S_i dividing n_i and 0<|h_i|<min_{s in S_i}s, fact 20609f1342ff4558 gives its exact value on the nonzero coordinate as
1_{gcd(A_i,product_{s in S_i}s)=1}.                         (21)
This factor must be retained in chi_nat and hence in kappa_i. Under the additional unit-target condition gcd(A_i,product_{s in S_i}s)=1, it equals one throughout the stated short nonzero range; without that condition it is not discarded. Any other unrecombined joint height/source/deletion mask likewise remains in (19) and is paid by (7). The same abstract identities apply separately to a reverse coordinate after inserting that coordinate's own n_i,A_i,F_{i,q}; no equality between forward and reverse profiles is asserted.

If kappa_i is identically one on the complete nonzero family, then r_i=0 and (8) reduces exactly to the complete hard source minus its zero-density term. For a proper finite band, r_i generally contains low as well as high frequencies, so (15) alone proves no positive defect lower bound. No estimate of ||P_b^perp w||_2 or ||P_b^perp r||_2, no bound for S_lit, no PMD closure, and no Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
e7e8025bde57f04f.proof:
A smooth compactly supported function has a Fourier transform which decays faster than every negative power on the real line. For fixed i,q, boundedness (3) therefore makes both the kappa_i-weighted and the (1-kappa_i)-weighted sampled series absolutely convergent.

Fact ace362082848a702 gives the complete nonzero-Poisson identity
n_i^(-1)sum_{t nonzero}
 Fhat_{i,q}(t/n_i)e_{n_i}(A_i t qbar)
 =sum_{m;qm congruent A_i mod n_i}F_{i,q}(m)
  -n_i^(-1)Fhat_{i,q}(0).                                  (22)
Split the complete multiplier 1 as kappa_i(q,t)+(1-kappa_i(q,t)) in the absolutely convergent left side of (22), multiply by H_i mu(q), and sum q. The kappa part is (4), the physical and zero parts are (5)-(6), and the complementary part is (7). Rearranging proves (8). Multiplication by b_i and summation proves (9). The congruence in (5) is equivalent to qm+n_i k=A_i for an integer k, proving (10).

Fact fa68efb06f0ec564 proves for every vector z that
D_pre(z)=C_src||P_b^perp z||_2^2
with the projection (11). Equation (8) says z=w-r. Linearity of P_b^perp proves (13). Expanding the squared norm proves (14). The reverse triangle inequality gives
||P_b^perp(w-r)||_2
 >=max(0,||P_b^perp w||_2-||P_b^perp r||_2),
which proves (15). Cauchy--Schwarz gives the first inequality in (16), and an orthogonal projection has norm at most one, giving the second.

For (18), the hypothesis on kappa makes every nonzero contribution to (7) have |t|>=YH_{0,i,q}; also |1-kappa_i(q,t)|<=2. From (17), with H_0=n_i/M_{i,q},
n_i^(-1)sum_{|t|>=YH_0}|Fhat_{i,q}(t/n_i)|
 <=C'_J C_{J,i,q}L_{i,q}Y^(1-J).
Multiplying by the additional factor at most two from |1-kappa|, by H_i, and summing q proves (18), after enlarging C'_J.

For the natural specialization, equation (5) of fact ee6886ba9ed393f1 and its proof show that after multiplying by the explicit PMD phase, the fixed reindexed height h_i contributes
-mu(c)mu(v) H_P
 sum_q mu(q)n_i^(-1)Fhat_{g,cq,n_i}(-h_i/n_i)
 e_{n_i}(-A_i h_i qbar)chi_nat.
Thus the expression without the outer coefficient b_i=-mu(c)mu(v) is exactly (4) with t=-h_i and (19). The inherited literal masks in chi_nat are zero-one or signed finite projective/bookkeeping coefficients and hence give a bounded multiplier. Fact 6eacfadbc9a83247 proves the reduced hard-source condition (20). Under the explicitly stated hypotheses on S_i and h_i, fact 20609f1342ff4558 gives exactly (21). Therefore the conductor factor is one only when the displayed unit-target condition holds; in all cases it remains in chi_nat and kappa_i. The remaining scope statements follow directly from retaining every nonconstant multiplier in kappa and hence in the exact complement (7).

glossary.P_b^perp: Orthogonal projection away from the line spanned by the conjugate source-coefficient vector.
glossary.d_i: The zero-frequency density component of coordinate i.
glossary.kappa_i: The bounded exact literal multiplier selecting frequencies, q-values, and bookkeeping copies in coordinate i.
glossary.r_i: The exact omitted-frequency leakage complementing kappa_i to the complete nonzero Poisson family.
glossary.u_i: The complete physical-source component of coordinate i.

e80321eac8f26079.title: COMPLETE \(m_q=1\) COMMON-CORE CLASSIFICATION, PHYSICAL FIXED-\(U\) DIVISIBILITY, AND THE EXACT SIGNED MÖBIUS SUPPLIERS
e80321eac8f26079.author: slava chan
e80321eac8f26079.statement:
COMPLETE \(m_q=1\) COMMON-CORE CLASSIFICATION, PHYSICAL FIXED-\(U\) DIVISIBILITY, AND THE EXACT SIGNED MÖBIUS SUPPLIERS.

Adopt one fixed good-\(\mathscr W\) orientation, anatomy, frozen source/projective fibre, frequency block and dilator block
\[
1\le F\le x^3,\qquad
\mathcal D\le d_\lambda<2\mathcal D
\]
from facts e55b27d39c593164 and cff9d29efb555b8e. Put
\[
T=\mathscr A=N/g_{\rm out}>0,\qquad
L=(\log(2x))^C
\]
with fixed \(C>0\). Let
\[
R=(\epsilon,a,b),\qquad R'=(\epsilon',a',b')
\]
be distinct supported primitive signed rays. Nonzero Möbius support makes \(a,a'\) squarefree. Write
\[
g=(a,a'),\qquad a=g\alpha,\qquad a'=g\beta,
\]
and
\[
L_0=\epsilon b\beta-\epsilon'b'\alpha,\qquad
\Delta_0=gL_0.
\tag{1}
\]
Then \(g,\alpha,\beta\) are pairwise coprime and squarefree and
\((\alpha\beta,L_0)=1\).

Define
\[
r=(g,\operatorname {rad}(T)),\qquad s=g/r.
\tag{2}
\]
The following classification is exact:
\[
\boxed{
m_q=1
\Longleftrightarrow
\left\{
\begin{array}{l}
a=rs\alpha,\quad a'=rs\beta,\\
r\alpha\beta\mid\operatorname {rad}(T),\\
(s,T\alpha\beta)=1,\\
s\mid L_0.
\end{array}
\right.
}
\tag{MQ1-CLASS}
\]
The representation in (2) is unique. If \(m_q=1\), write
\[
T=r\alpha\beta T_0,\qquad L_0=s\ell.
\tag{3}
\]
Then
\[
T\Delta_0=aa'T_0\ell.
\tag{4}
\]
Consequently the CRT-combined ray-pair phase from fact
7e9251670db3e1c9 becomes the ordinary marked-modulus phase
\[
e_{d_\lambda v_\lambda}(T_0\ell),
\tag{5}
\]
its Archimedean reciprocity companion is
\[
e\!\left(-{T_0\ell\over d_\lambda v_\lambda}\right),
\tag{6}
\]
and their product, equivalently the full physical phase modulo \(aa'\), is exactly one.

There is also an exact physical fixed-\(U\) gate. For any literal physical source incidences underlying supported scalings
\[
q=k a,\qquad q'=k'a'
\]
