on the two rays, write the two orientation-neutral source equations as
\[
qt+n u=T,\qquad q't'+n u'=T,\qquad n=d_\lambda v_\lambda.
\tag{7}
\]
Then
\[
\boxed{r\alpha\mid u,\qquad r\beta\mid u'.}
\tag{8}
\]
Thus, writing
\[
u=r\alpha w,\qquad u'=r\beta w',
\tag{9}
\]
the inherited fixed-\(U\) support gives
\[
w\asymp {K_{\rm sh}\over r\alpha},\qquad
w'\asymp {K_{\rm sh}\over r\beta}.
\tag{10}
\]
The constants implicit in (10) are exactly the fixed compact-support constants of the frozen physical source. Statements (7)--(10) hold in both forward and reverse orientations and for every allowed endpoint or \(U\)-parent: those labels only restrict the same physical support and do not change the orientation-neutral equation.

Define
\[
\mathcal A^0_\lambda(R)
={\mathcal A_\lambda(R)\over\mu(a)},\qquad
\mathcal U_\lambda(R)
=\sum_{k\in\mathscr I_\lambda(R)}
\mu(k)\mathcal W_{\lambda,R}(k),
\tag{11}
\]
using RAY-MU from fact a36284a9dbec7837. On \(m_q=1\),
\[
\mu(a)\mu(a')=\mu(\alpha)\mu(\beta);
\tag{12}
\]
the common \(r\)- and \(s\)-Möbius signs square away.

Suppose now
\[
\mathcal D>Q^2.
\tag{13}
\]
Then \(aa'>Q^2/\mathcal D\) is automatic. The complete conductor-one restriction of the exact hard form in fact cff9d29efb555b8e is
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\mathfrak H_C^{m_q=1}
=
\sum_\lambda
\sum_{\substack{r,s,\alpha,\beta,\epsilon,\epsilon',b,b'\\
R\ne R',\ r\alpha\beta\mid\operatorname {rad}(T)\\
(s,T\alpha\beta)=1,\ s\mid L_0\\
m_d>L,\ d_\lambda\nmid T\Delta_0}}
&
\mu(\alpha)\mu(\beta)
\mathcal A^0_\lambda(R)
\overline{\mathcal A^0_\lambda(R')}\\
&\times
\mathcal U_\lambda(R)
\overline{\mathcal U_\lambda(R')},
\end{aligned}
}
\tag{MQ1-MU-N}
\]
where
\[
R=(\epsilon,rs\alpha,b),\qquad
R'=(\epsilon',rs\beta,b'),
\tag{14}
\]
and the sum is restricted to the exact supported rays and retains every literal target-gcd, fixed-\(U\), high, source, parent, ordering, equality, collision, deletion, provenance, coprimality and projective selector. In particular, the fixed-\(U\) part retains (8)--(10). The source-specific estimate
\[
|\mathfrak H_C^{m_q=1}|
\le x^{o(1)}|\omega_F|^2{BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}
\tag{15}
\]
is the smallest full coherent-core supplier after MQ1-CLASS; it is not proved here.

There is a precise opposite-ray restriction. Let
\[
R_+=(+1,a,b),\qquad R_-=(-1,a,b).
\tag{16}
\]
On supported opposite rays, \(m_q=1\) if and only if
\[
a\mid2T.
\tag{17}
\]
In the unique decomposition \(a=rs\) supplied by (2),
\[
s\in\{1,2\}.
\tag{18}
\]
If \(s=1\), then \(a=r\mid\operatorname {rad}(T)\) and
\[
a\mid u,\qquad a\mid u'.
\tag{19}
\]
If \(s=2\), then \(T\) and \(b\) are odd,
\[
a=2r,\qquad r\mid\operatorname {rad}(T),
\]
and
\[
r\mid u,\qquad r\mid u'.
\tag{20}
\]
For this pair put
\[
\rho_\lambda={d_\lambda\over(d_\lambda,T)}.
\]
Since \((d_\lambda,a)=1\),
\[
m_d={\rho_\lambda\over(\rho_\lambda,2b)}.
\tag{21}
\]

The exact opposite-ray part of MQ1-MU-N is
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\mathfrak O_{\rm opp}
=
\sum_{n,\lambda}
\sum_{\substack{a,b\ge1,\ (a,b)=1,\ \mu(a)\ne0\\
a\mid2T,\ m_d>L,\ d_\lambda\nmid2Tab}}
2\operatorname {Re}\!\bigl(
\mathcal A^0_{\lambda,+}(a,b)
\overline{\mathcal A^0_{\lambda,-}(a,b)}
\mathcal U_{\lambda,+}(a,b)
\overline{\mathcal U_{\lambda,-}(a,b)}
\bigr),
\end{aligned}
}
\tag{OPP-MU-N}
\]
with both ray-support conditions and the complete literal fixed-\(U\) and other selectors retained. Here \(\mathcal U_{\lambda,\pm}\) are exactly the two signed scaling Möbius transforms of fact 54e9fd98e7191261. Thus the estimate
\[
|\mathfrak O_{\rm opp}|
\le x^{o(1)}|\omega_F|^2{BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}
\tag{22}
\]
is an explicit signed opposite-ray supplier, not a conclusion.

Neither phase-freeness nor the opposite-ray pairing gives cancellation or positivity. Fact 54e9fd98e7191261 proves that the two sign supports need not agree, the complete transforms may vanish, and even conditional conjugate twins produce a real square with no fixed sign. This theorem proves only the exact classification, divisibility gates and signed reductions. It proves neither (15), nor (22), nor the rest of the \(m_q=1\) core from OPP-MU-N alone, nor GA-SIGNED-RAY-MU, GA-RAY-SPEC, GA-NR-DIL, a tail payment or Goldbach.
e80321eac8f26079.proof:
Fact 3089501f7fb49c18 proves that \(g,\alpha,\beta\) are pairwise coprime and squarefree, that
\[
(\alpha\beta,L_0)=1,
\]
and that
\[
m_q=
{g\over(g,TL_0)}
{\alpha\beta\over(\alpha\beta,T)}.
\tag{23}
\]
Because both factors in (23) are positive integers, \(m_q=1\) is equivalent to
\[
g\mid TL_0,\qquad \alpha\beta\mid T.
\tag{24}
\]

Since \(g\) is squarefree, (2) gives \(g=rs\), where \(r,s\) are coprime and squarefree,
\[
r\mid\operatorname {rad}(T),\qquad (s,T)=1.
\tag{25}
\]
Also \(g\) is coprime to \(\alpha\beta\). Therefore the second condition in (24) is equivalent, together with (25), to
\[
r\alpha\beta\mid\operatorname {rad}(T).
\tag{26}
\]
The first condition in (24) is equivalent to \(s\mid L_0\): the factor \(r\) already divides \(T\), while every prime of \(s\) is coprime to \(T\). Moreover
\[
(s,\alpha\beta)=1
\]
because \(s\mid g\), so (25) gives
\[
(s,T\alpha\beta)=1.
\]
This proves the forward implication in MQ1-CLASS. Conversely, the four displayed conditions in MQ1-CLASS imply \(\alpha\beta\mid T\), \(r\mid T\), and \(s\mid L_0\), hence \(g=rs\mid TL_0\). Equation (23) then gives \(m_q=1\). Uniqueness follows from the definition \(r=(g,\operatorname {rad}(T))\).

Under \(m_q=1\), equations (3) are integral by MQ1-CLASS. Since
\[
\Delta_0=gL_0=(rs)(s\ell)=rs^2\ell
\]
and
\[
aa'=(rs\alpha)(rs\beta)=r^2s^2\alpha\beta,
\]
we obtain
\[
T\Delta_0
=(r\alpha\beta T_0)(rs^2\ell)
=r^2s^2\alpha\beta T_0\ell
=aa'T_0\ell.
\]
This proves (4).

Fact 7e9251670db3e1c9 gives the CRT-combined phase
\[
e_{d_\lambda v_\lambda}
\!\left(T\Delta_0(aa')^{-1}\right).
\]
The inverse exists because \((aa',d_\lambda v_\lambda)=1\). Substitution of (4) reduces its argument modulo \(d_\lambda v_\lambda\) to \(T_0\ell\), proving (5). The Archimedean factor in that fact is
\[
e\!\left(-{T\Delta_0\over aa'd_\lambda v_\lambda}\right),
\]
which becomes (6). Since
\[
e_{d_\lambda v_\lambda}(T_0\ell)
=e\!\left({T_0\ell\over d_\lambda v_\lambda}\right),
\]
the two factors cancel. Equivalently, (4) makes the physical additive character modulo \(aa'\) equal one.

We prove the fixed-\(U\) gate. For a supported scaling \(q=ka\), one has
\[
r\alpha\mid a\mid q.
\]
MQ1-CLASS also gives \(r\alpha\mid T\). Subtracting the two terms in the first equation of (7) gives
\[
nu=T-qt,
\]
so \(r\alpha\mid nu\). The literal coprimality support gives
\[
(q,n)=1.
\]
Because \(r\alpha\mid q\), it follows that \((r\alpha,n)=1\), and hence
\[
r\alpha\mid u.
\]
The same argument in the primed equation proves \(r\beta\mid u'\). This proves (8)--(9).

Fact 8d9feea8c44da2c8 proves in one orientation-neutral statement that the forward source has
\[
(q,n,t,u)=(a,b,m,k)
\]
before ray scaling and that the reverse source interchanges the two divisor-complement pairs; in both cases the short physical complement satisfies
\[
u\asymp K_{\rm sh}.
\]
Applying this support statement separately to the two supported source incidences and dividing by (8) gives (10). That fact also proves that all endpoint, \(U\)-parent, source and deletion labels are transported literally by the orientation-neutral equation, so no endpoint case changes this argument.

By pairwise coprimality,
\[
\mu(a)=\mu(r)\mu(s)\mu(\alpha),\qquad
\mu(a')=\mu(r)\mu(s)\mu(\beta).
\]
All factors are nonzero and squarefree, hence
\[
\mu(a)\mu(a')
=\mu(r)^2\mu(s)^2\mu(\alpha)\mu(\beta)
=\mu(\alpha)\mu(\beta).
\]
This proves (12).

Fact a36284a9dbec7837 gives exactly
\[
B_\lambda(R)
=\mathcal A_\lambda(R)\mathcal U_\lambda(R)
=\mu(a)\mathcal A^0_\lambda(R)\mathcal U_\lambda(R).
\tag{27}
\]
Restrict the hard form of fact cff9d29efb555b8e to \(m_q=1\). Its physical phase is one by (4)--(6). If \(\mathcal D>Q^2\), then
\[
{Q^2\over\mathcal D}<1\le aa',
\]
so the primitive-product hard condition is automatic. Substitute MQ1-CLASS and (27) in both ray slots, then use (12). The remaining hard selectors are exactly \(m_d>L\) and nonresonance, with every inherited selector still inside the literal source coefficients. This gives MQ1-MU-N. Since no absolute value or coefficient replacement occurred, it is the exact full conductor-one hard form. The displayed estimate (15) is precisely the target required for this restriction and remains unproved.

For opposite rays, \(g=a\), \(\alpha=\beta=1\), and
\[
L_0=(+1)b-(-1)b=2b.
\]
MQ1-CLASS says
\[
r\mid\operatorname {rad}(T),\qquad
(s,T)=1,\qquad s\mid2b.
\tag{28}
\]
Because \((a,b)=1\) and \(s\mid a\), one has \((s,b)=1\). Therefore \(s\mid2\), proving (18). Conditions (28) are equivalent to \(a=rs\mid2T\), which also reproves (17) and agrees with fact 54e9fd98e7191261.

If \(s=1\), then \(a=r\), and (8) gives (19). If \(s=2\), condition \((s,T)=1\) makes \(T\) odd, while \((a,b)=1\) makes \(b\) odd. Now \(a=2r\), and (8) gives (20).

The support relation \((q,n)=1\), with \(a\mid q\) and \(d_\lambda\mid n\), gives
\[
(d_\lambda,a)=1.
\tag{29}
\]
Put \(\rho_\lambda=d_\lambda/(d_\lambda,T)\). The definition of \(m_d\) in fact cff9d29efb555b8e and \(\Delta_0=2ab\) gives
\[
m_d={\rho_\lambda\over(\rho_\lambda,2ab)}.
\]
Equation (29) implies \((\rho_\lambda,a)=1\), so the denominator is
\((\rho_\lambda,2b)\). This proves (21).

Finally specialize (27) to the two opposite rays. Their common primitive Möbius factor appears twice and squares to one. The two ordered terms are complex conjugates of one another purely by reversing the two slots:
\[
X+\overline X=2\operatorname {Re}X,
\]
with
\[
X=
\mathcal A^0_{\lambda,+}\overline{\mathcal A^0_{\lambda,-}}
\mathcal U_{\lambda,+}\overline{\mathcal U_{\lambda,-}}.
\]
Insert (17), (21), nonresonance and every literal support selector. This proves OPP-MU-N without assuming equality, conjugacy or nonvanishing of the two scaling supports. Fact 54e9fd98e7191261 supplies exactly the final no-positivity and no-cancellation warning, so all scope exclusions follow.

glossary.MQ1-CLASS: The unique r,s,alpha,beta classification of supported primitive ray pairs whose reduced physical q-conductor equals one.
glossary.MQ1-MU-N: The exact full conductor-one hard good-W signed Möbius source after physical phase collapse.
glossary.OPP-MU-N: The exact opposite-ray restriction of MQ1-MU-N, retaining the two scaling Möbius transforms and every literal selector.
glossary.physical fixed-U divisor gate: The divisibilities r alpha divides u and r beta divides u' forced by the two literal source equations on m_q=1.

e9ba03365d02ff89.title: FIXED-POWER PAYMENT OF THE COMPLETE LITERAL NONRESONANT FULL-DENOMINATOR TERM. Fix 0<eta<1/12, 0<delta<4eta and 0<theta<1/2. Let Q tend to infinity and put U=Q^(1/3), B=Q^(4/3+o(1)), F_0=Q^(1-2eta+o(1)), and A_P=Q^(1+delta)/P^2. Let P be a dyadic shared-prime scale occurring in the literal medium range of fact 55c6f91ec7fd414f; in particular Q^(1/3+2eta+o(1))<=P<=Q^(1/2+theta), and assume A_P>1. Let N be a fixed positive integer. Let cal B be the squarefree integers b in [B,2B), put L_b=product_{r|b,b/r<F_0}r, let cal R={b in cal B:L_b>1,(L_b,N)=1}, define pi(b) as the largest prime divisor of L_b, and put s(b)=b/pi(b). Let gamma_b be complex numbers satisfying sum_{b in cal R}|gamma_b|^2<=1. For primes p in [P,2P) put S_p={s:ps in cal R,pi(ps)=p} and Q_p={q:pq in cal R,p|s(pq)}
e9ba03365d02ff89.author: slava chan
e9ba03365d02ff89.statement:
FIXED-POWER PAYMENT OF THE COMPLETE LITERAL NONRESONANT FULL-DENOMINATOR TERM. Fix 0<eta<1/12, 0<delta<4eta and 0<theta<1/2. Let Q tend to infinity and put U=Q^(1/3), B=Q^(4/3+o(1)), F_0=Q^(1-2eta+o(1)), and A_P=Q^(1+delta)/P^2. Let P be a dyadic shared-prime scale occurring in the literal medium range of fact 55c6f91ec7fd414f; in particular Q^(1/3+2eta+o(1))<=P<=Q^(1/2+theta), and assume A_P>1. Let N be a fixed positive integer. Let cal B be the squarefree integers b in [B,2B), put L_b=product_{r|b,b/r<F_0}r, let cal R={b in cal B:L_b>1,(L_b,N)=1}, define pi(b) as the largest prime divisor of L_b, and put s(b)=b/pi(b). Let gamma_b be complex numbers satisfying sum_{b in cal R}|gamma_b|^2<=1. For primes p in [P,2P) put S_p={s:ps in cal R,pi(ps)=p} and Q_p={q:pq in cal R,p|s(pq)}.
Let w_n be supported on Q<=n<2Q and satisfy |w_n|<=Q^epsilon for every epsilon>0. Extend the literal Vaughan coefficients by zero off Q<=au<2Q and define
beta_{ss,a}(u)=mu(a)w_{au}sum_{m|u,m<=U}mu(m), 1<=a<=U,
beta_{ll,a}(u)=w_{au}sum_{dm=u,U<d<=m}varkappa(d,m)mu(d)mu(m), 1<=a<2U, (1)
where varkappa(d,m)=1 for d=m and 2 for d<m. Put U_a={u in Z:Q<=au<2Q}. For s in S_p with (s,N)=1 define M_1 modulo s by pM_1 congruent to N modulo s. For q in Q_p with q<=F_0 and (q,N)=1 define M_12 modulo q by pM_12 congruent to N modulo q. Define
R_{p,tau,a,s}^{(1)}=sum_{u in U_a,(au,ps)=1}beta_{tau,a}(u)e_s(M_1(au)^(-1)),
R_{p,tau,a,q}^{(2)}=sum_{u in U_a,(au,pq)=1}conjugate(beta_{tau,a}(u))e_q(-M_12(au)^(-1)). (2)
Define the literal nonresonant full-denominator aggregate
E_full^nr(P)=-sum_{p,tau,a}sum_{s in S_p,q in Q_p;(s,N)=(q,N)=1,q<=F_0,(s,q)<A_P} conjugate(gamma_{ps})gamma_{pq} R_{p,tau,a,s}^{(1)}R_{p,tau,a,q}^{(2)}/(p-1)^2, (3)
where tau has the corresponding a-range in (1). Then (3) is exactly the complete nonresonant minus-one contribution obtained by applying the double-nonzero completion formula of fact 5a7bf376fe94485e to every fixed edge of the literal full-denominator face in fact f439118e1e8818a1. Moreover
|E_full^nr(P)|<<Q^(epsilon+o(1))BQ^2/P^3. (4)
Consequently, for every fixed omega_nr<6eta and all sufficiently large Q,
|E_full^nr(P)|<<Q^(7/3-omega_nr). (5)
Thus only the resonant (p-1)-indicator term of fact 5a7bf376fe94485e remains in this full-denominator completion supplier. No estimate for that resonant term, complete E_full(P), another additive subface, or Goldbach is asserted.
e9ba03365d02ff89.proof:
For each fixed literal edge, apply fact 1c0f8ee6ed71cd50 with d_1=s,d_2=q, C_1=M_1a^(-1) modulo s, C_2=-M_12a^(-1) modulo q, a_1(u)=beta_{tau,a}(u)1_{(au,ps)=1}, and a_2(u)=conjugate(beta_{tau,a}(u))1_{(au,pq)=1}. The unit conditions make all phases well defined. Its exact equation (6) says that the nonresonant minus-one completion scalar is precisely -R^{(1)}R^{(2)}/(p-1)^2. Because P is explicitly assumed to be a literal medium dyadic block, fact f439118e1e8818a1 identifies these fixed edges with its exact full-denominator face. Summing with the unchanged gamma coefficients and all displayed restrictions gives exactly (3).
Let V_a=#U_a<=2Q/a+1. The divisor bound in (1) and the hypothesis on w give |beta_{tau,a}(u)|<=Q^(epsilon+o(1)); hence
|R_{p,tau,a,s}^{(1)}|+|R_{p,tau,a,q}^{(2)}|<=Q^(epsilon+o(1))V_a. (6)
For each p define g_1(p)^2=sum_{s in S_p}|gamma_{ps}|^2 and g_2(p)^2=sum_{q in Q_p}|gamma_{pq}|^2. Both ps and pq are multiples of p in [B,2B), so each p-block has at most 3B/p members. Cauchy's inequality gives
sum_{s in S_p,q in Q_p}|gamma_{ps}gamma_{pq}|<=3B g_1(p)g_2(p)/p. (7)
The first-row blocks are disjoint because pi(b) is unique, so sum_p g_1(p)^2<=1. A fixed squarefree b belongs to Q_p only when p divides s(b), hence to at most tau(b)=Q^o(1) such blocks. Therefore sum_p g_2(p)^2<=Q^o(1). Cauchy's inequality in p and p>=P now gives
sum_{p,s,q}|gamma_{ps}gamma_{pq}|<<Q^o(1)B/P. (8)
All restrictions in (3) only decrease this absolute mass. Equations (3),(6),(8), (p-1)^(-2)<<P^(-2), and
sum_{a<=2U}V_a^2<<sum_{a<=2U}(Q/a+1)^2<<Q^2 (9)
give (4), including the at most two tau labels.
Finally P>=Q^(1/3+2eta+o(1)) implies P^3>=Q^(1+6eta+o(1)). Since B=Q^(4/3+o(1)), equation (4) is Q^(7/3-6eta+epsilon+o(1)). Given omega_nr<6eta, choose epsilon sufficiently small and then Q sufficiently large to prove (5). The scope statement follows from the exact decomposition in fact 5a7bf376fe94485e.

glossary.E_full^nr(P): The complete literal nonresonant minus-one full-denominator aggregate.
glossary.R_{p,tau,a,q}^{(2)}: The conjugated second literal incomplete full-denominator phase row.
glossary.R_{p,tau,a,s}^{(1)}: The first literal incomplete full-denominator phase row.
glossary.omega_nr: Any fixed saving exponent less than 6eta.

e9c446110faebff9.title: COMMON-SPECTRUM PROJECTIVE LIFT OF THE FIXED-ACTIVE-PRODUCT TENSOR BESSEL BOUND
e9c446110faebff9.author: slava chan
e9c446110faebff9.statement:
COMMON-SPECTRUM PROJECTIVE LIFT OF THE FIXED-ACTIVE-PRODUCT TENSOR BESSEL BOUND.

Fix a squarefree positive integer \(r\), real numbers \(B,Q\ge2\), a constant \(C\ge1\), and finite integer intervals \(I,J\) of cardinalities \(U,V\). Assume
\[
 U\le {CB\over r},\qquad V\le r,                               \tag{1}
\]
and assume \(r,B\) and the endpoints of \(I,J\) are bounded by a fixed power of \(Q\). Let \(\mathcal R\subseteq I\times J\) be any finite row set. Fix a nonzero integer \(A\). For every row \(j=(u_j,h_j)\in\mathcal R\), assume
\[
 u_j>0,qquad n_j=ru_j\ \hbox{is squarefree},qquad
 (Au_jh_j,r)=1.                                                    \tag{2}
\]
For every prime \(p\mid r\), define \(g_{p;j}\) and its normalized Fourier transform \(\widehat g_{p;j}\) exactly as in fact df97bf1eba0495be, with \((n,h)=(n_j,h_j)\). Put
\[
 \Omega_r=\prod_{p\mid r}\mathbb F_p^\times,qquad
 V_j(\boldsymbol\rho)=\prod_{p\mid r}\widehat g_{p;j}(\rho_p).
                                                                         \tag{3}
\]

Let \(W_j:\Omega_r\to\mathbb C\) be functions. Suppose there is a finite set \(\mathcal T\), complex scalars \(\alpha_{j,t}\), and functions \(Z_t:\Omega_r\to\mathbb C\) such that
\[
 W_j(\boldsymbol\rho)=\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}
 \alpha_{j,t}Z_t(\boldsymbol\rho)                                \tag{4}
\]
for every \(j,\boldsymbol\rho\). Define
\[
 \mathfrak P(W)
 =\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}
   \left(\sup_{j\in\mathcal R}|\alpha_{j,t}|\right)
   \left(\sup_{\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r}|Z_t(\boldsymbol\rho)|\right).
                                                                         \tag{5}
\]
Then for every complex coefficient array \((a_j)_{j\in\mathcal R}\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 \sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r}
 \left|\sum_{j\in\mathcal R}
 a_jW_j(\boldsymbol\rho)V_j(\boldsymbol\rho)\right|^2
 \ll_{C,\varepsilon}
 Q^\varepsilon {B\over r}\,\mathfrak P(W)^2
 \sum_{j\in\mathcal R}|a_j|^2.                                  \tag{6}
\]
The implied constant also depends on the fixed polynomial envelope in \(Q\).

If, on a common finite integer \(q\)-support,
\[
 B_j(q)=\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}\alpha_{j,t}z_t(q),                 \tag{7}
\]
and
\[
 \chi_{\boldsymbol\rho}(q)=\prod_{p\mid r}e_p(\rho_pq),qquad
 W_j(\boldsymbol\rho)=\sum_qB_j(q)\chi_{\boldsymbol\rho}(q),   \tag{8}
\]
then (4) holds with
\[
 Z_t(\boldsymbol\rho)=\sum_qz_t(q)\chi_{\boldsymbol\rho}(q).   \tag{9}
\]

For the forward GA-tail faces of fact 0aa821ade9a14b45, restrict to actual rows with one common nonempty active product \(r\), one signed frequency interval of cardinality at most \(r\), and marked integers \(n=ru\) in \([B/2,2B]\). Every retained row satisfies (2), and the retained cofactors \(u\) lie in an interval of cardinality at most \(2B/r+1\). Consequently, any exact decomposition (7) of the literal face coefficients \(B_{\lambda,h,r}(q)\) gives (6) for their exact weighted tensor Gram with the cost (5). No coprimality is required of points of the enclosing intervals that are not retained rows. This specialization does not remove the pair-dependent NR selector of fact 0aa821ade9a14b45.

The result is only a sufficient projective lift. It proves no bound for the literal cost \(\mathfrak P(W)\), no distinct-active-product estimate, no pair-dependent NR deletion estimate, no GA-NR-DIL or C4-WTG estimate, and no Goldbach conclusion.
e9c446110faebff9.proof:
For \(j,k\in\mathcal R\), all hypotheses of fact df97bf1eba0495be hold. Indeed, (2) states that \(n_j,n_k\) are positive and squarefree, \(r\mid(n_j,n_k)\), and
\[
 (r,n_j/r)=(r,u_j)=1,qquad (r,n_k/r)=1,qquad
 (Ah_jh_k,r)=1.
\]
Hence
\[
 \sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r}
 V_j(\boldsymbol\rho)\overline{V_k(\boldsymbol\rho)}
 =G_r(n_j,h_j;n_k,h_k).                                            \tag{10}
\]
Put
\[
 E_{jk}=h_jn_k-h_kn_j=r(h_ju_k-h_ku_j),
\]
and
\[
 K_r(j,k)={\gcd(r,h_ju_k-h_ku_j)\over r}.                         \tag{11}
\]
Because \(r\) is squarefree, the exceptional product \(s(r,E_{jk})\) of fact df97bf1eba0495be equals \(\gcd(r,h_ju_k-h_ku_j)\). That fact and fact e705401df9f0709e therefore give
\[
 |G_r(n_j,h_j;n_k,h_k)|\ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon K_r(j,k).
                                                                         \tag{12}
\]

We prove the required Schur bound directly on the retained row set. Fix \(j=(u,h)\in\mathcal R\). The identity
\[
 \gcd(r,hu'-h'u)=\sum_{\substack{t\mid r\\t\mid hu'-h'u}}\phi(t)
                                                                         \tag{13}
\]
holds for every retained \(k=(u',h')\). For fixed \(t\mid r\), (2) makes \(u,h\) units modulo \(t\). Among all points \((u',h')\in I\times J\), and hence among the retained subset, the congruence
\[
 hu'\equiv h'u\pmod t
\]
has at most
\[
 {UV\over t}+\min(U,V)                                           \tag{14}
\]
solutions: fixing \(h'\) determines one residue class of \(u'\) modulo \(t\), while fixing \(u'\) determines one residue class of \(h'\); take the smaller of the resulting two rectangle bounds. Insert (14) into (13), divide by \(r\), and use
\[
 \sum_{t\mid r}\phi(t)=r,qquad
 \sum_{t\mid r}{\phi(t)\over t}\le\tau(r).
\]
This gives the row-sum bound
\[
 \sum_{k\in\mathcal R}K_r(j,k)
 \le {\tau(r)UV\over r}+\min(U,V).                              \tag{15}
\]
The same bound holds for columns because the kernel is symmetric. By (1) and fact e705401df9f0709e,
\[
 {\tau(r)UV\over r}+\min(U,V)
 \ll_{C,\varepsilon}Q^\varepsilon{B\over r}.                    \tag{16}
\]
Schur's test, (10), and the entrywise majorant (12) now give, for every complex array \((c_j)\),
\[
 \sum_{\boldsymbol\rho\in\Omega_r}
 \left|\sum_jc_jV_j(\boldsymbol\rho)\right|^2
 \ll_{C,\varepsilon}Q^\varepsilon{B\over r}\sum_j|c_j|^2.       \tag{17}
\]

Insert (4). Minkowski's inequality in \(\ell^2(\Omega_r)\) gives
\[
 \left\|\sum_j a_jW_jV_j\right\|_2
 \le
 \sum_{t\in\mathcal T}
 \left\|Z_t\sum_j a_j\alpha_{j,t}V_j\right\|_2.               \tag{18}
\]
For each \(t\), apply (17) to \(c_j=a_j\alpha_{j,t}\) and bound multiplication by \(Z_t\) by its supremum norm. The right side of (18) is at most
\[
 \ll_{C,\varepsilon}
 Q^{\varepsilon/2}\left({B\over r}\right)^{1/2}
 \mathfrak P(W)
 \left(\sum_j|a_j|^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
Squaring and renaming \(\varepsilon\) proves (6).

Equations (7)--(9) imply (4) by substituting (7) into (8) and interchanging finite sums.

For the GA specialization, fact 0aa821ade9a14b45 gives, on every actual retained row, positivity and squarefreeness of \(n=ru\), \((r,u)=1\), and \((\mathscr Ah,r)=1\), which is (2) with \(A=\mathscr A\). The marked interval gives
\[
 {B\over2r}\le u\le {2B\over r},
\]
so the retained cofactors lie in an enclosing interval of cardinality at most \(2B/r+1\); increasing \(C\) absorbs the endpoint constant. The assumed signed frequency interval has cardinality at most \(r\). The rowwise proof of (15) counts retained rows by the enclosing rectangle and does not require non-retained interval points to be units. Thus the GA rows satisfy the hypotheses just proved. Equations (8)--(10) of fact 0aa821ade9a14b45 identify their exact literal weighted tensor with the left side of (6). That fact separately proves that the NR selector remains pair-dependent, establishing the stated scope.

glossary.common-spectrum projective cost: The quantity mathfrak P(W) measuring a decomposition of all row multipliers W_j into row scalars times dual-coordinate functions common to the family.
glossary.common-spectrum projective lift: The Bessel estimate obtained by applying the unweighted tensor frame separately to each common dual spectrum and summing its projective costs.

e9e9563501147a1a.title: EXACT LARGE-Dcal PRINCIPAL/CENTERED SOURCE SPLIT, MQ1-MU-N IDENTIFICATION, AND THE TWO MINIMAL SIGNED SUPPLIERS
e9e9563501147a1a.author: slava chan
e9e9563501147a1a.statement:
EXACT LARGE-Dcal PRINCIPAL/CENTERED SOURCE SPLIT, MQ1-MU-N IDENTIFICATION, AND THE TWO MINIMAL SIGNED SUPPLIERS.

Adopt one fixed exact good-W orientation, anatomy, frozen source/projective fibre, frequency block and dilator block from fact cff9d29efb555b8e, and assume
Dcal>Q^2.                                                            (1)
Let H_C be its exact hard form. Thus every retained ordered ray pair R != R' satisfies
m_d>L,  d_lambda does not divide A_script Delta_0,                    (2)
and the condition aa'>Q^2/Dcal is automatic. Use the squarefree physical conductor m_q, unit C_q, marked modulus n=d_lambda v_lambda, and complete literal coefficient B_lambda(R) from the same fact.

Define the principal signed source
P-qSRC
 =sum_lambda sum_{exact retained R != R'}
 B_lambda(R)conjugate(B_lambda(R'))
 mu(m_q)/phi(m_q),                                                    (3)
and define the centered source
C-qSRC>=2
 =sum_lambda sum_{exact retained R != R', m_q>=2}
 B_lambda(R)conjugate(B_lambda(R'))
 K^circ_{m_q,C_q}(d_lambda v_lambda).                                (4)
Then the hard form has the exact disjoint decomposition
H_C=P-qSRC+C-qSRC>=2.                                                 (5)
Every literal marker, Möbius, Fourier, target-gcd, fixed-U, high, source, parent, ordering, equality, collision, deletion, provenance, coprimality and projective selector is retained in (3)-(5).

Split (3) according to m_q=1 and m_q>=2:
P-qSRC=P-qSRC_{1}+P-qSRC_{>=2}.                                      (6)
The conductor-one part is exactly
P-qSRC_{1}=H_C^{m_q=1}=MQ1-MU-N                                     (7)
from fact e80321eac8f26079. Hence (7) retains the unique MQ1-CLASS decomposition
a=rs alpha,  a'=rs beta,
r alpha beta divides rad(A_script),
(s,A_script alpha beta)=1,  s divides L_0,                            (8)
the exact physical phase collapse, and the fixed-U divisor gates
r alpha divides u,  r beta divides u'.                               (9)
No m_q=1 source atom is discarded or moved into the centered trace.

For fixed (d,v), use the exact Hilbert ray vector B_bold_{d,v}(R) from fact 8b46abe31a5ae8d7. The centered source has the equivalent exact primewise form
C-qSRC>=2
 =sum_{d,v} sum_{exact retained R != R', m_q>=2}
 <B_bold_{d,v}(R),B_bold_{d,v}(R')>
 sum_{r|m_q,r>1}
 mu(m_q/r) Kcal_{r;m_q,C_q}(dv)/phi(m_q/r).                          (10)
Here Kcal is the centered active-prime tensor of fact 8b46abe31a5ae8d7. Because Q^2/Dcal<1, every positive active product r>1 lies above Q^2/Dcal. Thus there is no low-active-product subfamily in (10), while the full face r=m_q always has coefficient one.

The two exact remaining canonical-scale suppliers are
|P-qSRC|
 <=x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 B Q^2F^2/Dcal,                               (P-qSRC-SUP)
|C-qSRC>=2|
 <=x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 B Q^2F^2/Dcal.                               (C-qSRC-SUP)
Neither estimate is asserted. The absolute GA-qPRINC bound of fact 764588e99974a6d9 gives only x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2BF^2 for (3), which is larger than P-qSRC-SUP by Dcal/Q^2. Likewise, inactive-face decay cannot pay all of (10), because its full active face has coefficient one.

This theorem proves the exact split (5), the complete conductor-one identification (7)-(9), the centered tensor identity (10), and the stated theorem-interface no-fits. It proves neither supplier, no cancellation or positivity for MQ1-MU-N or OPP-MU-N, no GA-RAY-SPEC or GA-NR-DIL estimate, no good-W tail payment, and no Goldbach conclusion.
e9e9563501147a1a.proof:
Fact cff9d29efb555b8e defines H_C by the hard conditions
aa'>Q^2/Dcal and m_d>L together with the exact nonresonance deletion. Under (1),
Q^2/Dcal<1<=aa',
so the primitive-product condition is automatic and the remaining conditions are exactly (2).

Fact 764588e99974a6d9 proves for every supported pair that m_q is squarefree, that C_q and d_lambda v_lambda are units modulo m_q, and that
e_{m_q}(-C_q(d_lambda v_lambda)^{-1})
 =mu(m_q)/phi(m_q)
  +K^circ_{m_q,C_q}(d_lambda v_lambda).                              (11)
Substitute (11) into every term of the exact hard form. The first term is precisely (3). The second term vanishes at m_q=1 because that fact defines
K^circ_{1,C_q}=0,
and its restriction to m_q>=2 is precisely (4). This proves the exact disjoint decomposition (5) without changing any coefficient or selector.

Splitting the finite sum (3) by m_q=1 and m_q>=2 gives (6). On m_q=1,
mu(m_q)/phi(m_q)=1.                                                   (12)
Fact e80321eac8f26079 proves that the complete m_q=1 restriction of the same hard form is exactly MQ1-MU-N, including the classification (8), phase collapse, fixed-U gates (9), and every inherited selector. Equations (12) and that exact identification prove (7). Since the centered term in (11) is zero at m_q=1, no conductor-one atom occurs in (4).

For m_q>=2, the algebraic centered CRT identity in fact 8b46abe31a5ae8d7 is
K^circ_{m_q,C_q}(dv)
 =sum_{r|m_q,r>1}
 mu(m_q/r)Kcal_{r;m_q,C_q}(dv)/phi(m_q/r).                           (13)
Group copies with common (d_lambda,v_lambda)=(d,v), exactly as in that fact:
sum_{lambda in Lambda(d,v)}
B_lambda(R)conjugate(B_lambda(R'))
 =<B_bold_{d,v}(R),B_bold_{d,v}(R')>.                                (14)
Substitution of (13)-(14) into (4) proves (10), retaining every pair condition. Under (1), Y=Q^2/Dcal<1, whereas every r in (13) is an integer greater than one, so no r<=Y occurs. The term r=m_q occurs and its coefficient is
mu(1)/phi(1)=1.                                                       (15)
This proves the exact active-face scope and the inactive-coefficient no-fit.

Finally, fact 764588e99974a6d9 proves the absolute bound
|P-qSRC|<=x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2BF^2.                                  (16)
The target P-qSRC-SUP equals the right side of (16) multiplied by Q^2/Dcal<1, so (16) is too large by Dcal/Q^2. This is a comparison of proved upper bounds, not a lower bound for P-qSRC. Equation (15) proves that inactive-face coefficient decay alone cannot pay every centered face. Therefore the two displayed supplier estimates remain separate source-specific requirements, and all exclusions follow.

glossary.C-qSRC>=2: The exact centered m_q>=2 deletion-preserving source trace on the hard good-W branch with Dcal>Q^2.
glossary.P-qSRC: The exact principal multiplicative-character signed source trace on the hard good-W branch with Dcal>Q^2.

ea57fb03b2cf5c31.title: ACTUAL C1 LARGE-EFFECTIVE-MODULUS SMOOTH-DIVISOR DICHOTOMY AND COMPLETE p-DIVIDES-C PAYMENT OF THE BALANCED TWO-FREE CELL. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, and let beta satisfy beta_m<=beta<6/5 in the strict-top C1 setting of facts f0f6807663d3ef3c and 79ffbcb2ffe4049f. Thus n=pv is squarefree, p is the unique rough prime of the C1 copy, v is the product of the prime divisors of n that are at most L=Q^(beta-1+sigma), and gcd(p,v)=1. Put C=mathscr A h and m_eff=n/gcd(C,n). Assume
ea57fb03b2cf5c31.author: slava chan
ea57fb03b2cf5c31.statement:
ACTUAL C1 LARGE-EFFECTIVE-MODULUS SMOOTH-DIVISOR DICHOTOMY AND COMPLETE p-DIVIDES-C PAYMENT OF THE BALANCED TWO-FREE CELL. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, and let beta satisfy beta_m<=beta<6/5 in the strict-top C1 setting of facts f0f6807663d3ef3c and 79ffbcb2ffe4049f. Thus n=pv is squarefree, p is the unique rough prime of the C1 copy, v is the product of the prime divisors of n that are at most L=Q^(beta-1+sigma), and gcd(p,v)=1. Put C=mathscr A h and m_eff=n/gcd(C,n). Assume
Q^(99/100)<=m_eff<=Q^(101/100).                                 (1)
Then exactly the following structural conclusions hold.

(i) If p divides C, then m_eff divides v and m_eff has a divisor m_1 satisfying
m_eff^(1/40)<=m_1<=m_eff^(1/2-1/40).                            (2)

(ii) If p does not divide C, then p divides m_eff. Put r_eff=m_eff/p. One has r_eff|v. If r_eff>=Q^(1/20), then m_eff again has a divisor m_1 satisfying (2). If r_eff<Q^(1/20), then m_eff=pr_eff is a near-prime effective modulus with a Q^(1/20)-small complementary factor.

Consequently fact 629ed652df233d7b pays the balanced two-free cell of fact 3dabf494e3ed99fd throughout the chamber (1) when p divides C, and when p does not divide C except possibly on the near-prime subchamber r_eff<Q^(1/20), subject only to the coefficient and polynomial-size hypotheses already displayed in fact 629ed652df233d7b. Thus p divides C is not an independent large-effective-modulus obstruction on this cell.
ea57fb03b2cf5c31.proof:
Fact 7c1f38cfbb8d0569 gives the exact C1 factorization n=pv in which v is the product of the prime divisors of n at most L. Fact f0f6807663d3ef3c gives the strict-top scales, and fact 79ffbcb2ffe4049f identifies the same squarefree n=pv in the composite reciprocal phase. Since beta<6/5 and sigma<=1/10000,
L=Q^(beta-1+sigma)<Q^(2001/10000)<Q^(21/100).                  (3)
Every prime divisor of v therefore is at most Q^(21/100).

We use the following deterministic divisor construction. Let s be any squarefree divisor of v with s>=Q^(1/20). Order its prime divisors in any fixed way and multiply them successively until the product first becomes at least Q^(1/20). Call the resulting product d. The product before the last prime is smaller than Q^(1/20), while the last prime is at most Q^(21/100) by (3). Hence
a divisor d of s satisfies
Q^(1/20)<=d<Q^(1/20+21/100)=Q^(13/50).                          (4)
Under (1),
m_eff^(1/40)<=Q^(101/4000)<Q^(1/20),                           (5)
and
Q^(13/50)<Q^(1881/4000)<=m_eff^(19/40)=m_eff^(1/2-1/40),       (6)
because 13/50=1040/4000<1881/4000 and m_eff>=Q^(99/100). Equations (4)-(6) show that d satisfies (2).

Because n is squarefree, m_eff=n/gcd(C,n) is the product of exactly those prime divisors of n that do not divide C. If p divides C, the prime p is absent from m_eff, so m_eff divides v. Assumption (1) implies m_eff>=Q^(99/100)>Q^(1/20). Apply the construction with s=m_eff to prove (i).

If p does not divide C, then p divides m_eff. Since gcd(p,v)=1 and m_eff divides pv, the quotient r_eff=m_eff/p is an integer divisor of v. If r_eff>=Q^(1/20), apply the construction with s=r_eff; the resulting d divides r_eff and hence m_eff, and satisfies (2). If r_eff<Q^(1/20), the displayed near-prime alternative is its definition. This proves (ii) and exhausts the two cases p|C and p not dividing C.

Fact 629ed652df233d7b applies to a factorization m_eff=m_0m_1 whenever m_1 satisfies m_eff^lambda<=m_1<=m_eff^(1/2-lambda), with lambda>0 fixed. Take lambda=1/40 and m_0=m_eff/m_1. The balanced two-free cell has both factor scales comparable to Q^(1/2), while (1) makes m_eff comparable to Q. Therefore every scale hypothesis of its balanced corollary is fulfilled; its remaining coefficient, bounded-variation, coprimality, and polynomial-size hypotheses are exactly those already stipulated in the final sentence of the present statement. This proves the payment claim without invoking any p-local four-row fact.

glossary.near-prime effective modulus: An effective modulus m_eff=pr_eff whose complementary factor r_eff is smaller than Q^(1/20).
glossary.r_eff: The complementary effective-modulus factor m_eff/p when the selected rough prime p survives in m_eff.

ea623cefa72d3a76.title: OFF-SCALE UNIT-TARGET INTERVAL-PRIME TRACE AT THE LITERAL POISSON FREQUENCY
ea623cefa72d3a76.author: slava chan
ea623cefa72d3a76.statement:
OFF-SCALE UNIT-TARGET INTERVAL-PRIME TRACE AT THE LITERAL POISSON FREQUENCY.

Fix \(0<\kappa\le1/100\), put \(\sigma=\kappa/100\), and let
\[
 1\le\beta\le6/5-2\kappa,\qquad
 H_T=Q^{\beta-1},\qquad B=QH_T.
\]
Let \(G\ge1\), put \(H_P=H_T/G\), and assume \(H_P\ge1\). For every squarefree integer \(q\) with \(Q\le q<2Q\), choose a unit \(A_q\) modulo \(q\) and its integer representative with \(|A_q|\le q\). Let
\[
 \frac12H_TQ^\sigma\le Y\le Q^{3/2-\beta-3\sigma},
 \qquad UY\asymp B.                                          \tag{1}
\]
Let \(\alpha_u,\gamma_p,\nu_h\) be divisor-bounded coefficients supported on \(u\asymp U\), primes \(p\asymp Y\), and
\[
 H_P\le |h|<2H_P,
\]
respectively. Let \(\Psi\) belong to a fixed uniformly scaled-smooth family in the normalized variables. Define
\[
 \mathcal A_{U,Y}
 =H_P^{-1}\sum_{\substack{Q\le q<2Q\\q\ {\rm squarefree}}}c_q
 \sum_{\substack{u\asymp U,\ p\asymp Y\\p\ {\rm prime}\\
                  (up,q)=1,\ (u,p)=1}}
 \alpha_u\gamma_p
 \sum_{H_P\le|h|<2H_P}\nu_h\Psi
 e_q(A_qh(up)^{-1}),
\]
where \(|c_q|\le1\). Then, for every \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
 |\mathcal A_{U,Y}|
 \ll_\epsilon Q^\epsilon
 \left[
 G^{1/2}Q^2(H_T/Y)^{1/2}
 +Q^{7/4}(H_TY)^{1/2}
 +QU
 \right].                                                     \tag{2}
\]
Consequently, if a global scale satisfies
\[
 x\asymp gGQ^2
\]
with \(g\ge1\), then
\[
 |\mathcal A_{U,Y}|\ll xQ^{-\delta}/g                         \tag{3}
\]
for some \(\delta=\delta(\kappa)>0\), after choosing \(\epsilon\) sufficiently small. This is uniform for every \(G\ge1\) with \(H_P\ge1\).

The theorem applies to every unit-target normalized interval-prime \(A\) block in fact \(664a92777dc5f5db\) after replacing its model frequency \(H_T\) by the literal frequency \(H_P\). It does not apply when the literal target is a nonunit modulo some supported reciprocal modulus.
ea623cefa72d3a76.proof:
Separate the uniformly scaled-smooth function \(\Psi\) by a logarithmic Fourier expansion exactly as in fact \(664a92777dc5f5db\). The total projective norm is bounded, and the separated one-variable factors preserve the fixed divisor bounds. It is enough to prove (2) for one separated mode.

First remove the coupled selector by the exact identity
\[
 {\bf1}_{(u,p)=1}=1-{\bf1}_{p\mid u}.                         \tag{4}
\]
For the unrestricted term, apply fact \(4a101b703d4499f6\) pointwise for each \(q\), with its numerator equal to the chosen unit \(A_q\) and its support parameter
\[
 H'=2H_P.
\]
We verify its scale hypotheses. From \(UY\asymp QH_T\) and \(Y\ge H_TQ^\sigma/2\),
\[
 U\ll Q^{1-\sigma}.
\]
Hence \(U\le q\) for sufficiently large \(Q\), after absorbing the fixed comparability constant. Also, for sufficiently large \(Q\),
\[
 H'=2H_P\le2H_T\le \frac12H_TQ^\sigma\le Y.
\]
The upper bound for \(Y\) gives
\[
 H_TY\le Q^{\beta-1}Q^{3/2-\beta-3\sigma}
 =Q^{1/2-3\sigma}.
\]
Since \(H_P\le H_T\),
\[
 4H'Y=8H_PY\le8H_TY< Q\le q
\]
for sufficiently large \(Q\). Finally \((A_q,q)=1\) by construction. Every hypothesis of fact \(4a101b703d4499f6\) is now satisfied.

That fact gives, pointwise in \(q\), with \(R=UY\asymp B\),
\[
 \ll_\epsilon(qUYH')^\epsilon
 \left[B(H'/Y)^{1/2}
       +H'(BY)^{1/2}q^{1/4}\right].
\]
Since \(q,|A_q|\ll Q\), all fixed divisor bounds and numerator sizes are absorbed into \(Q^\epsilon\). Replacing \(H'\) by \(H_P\) changes only absolute constants. Sum over \(q\asymp Q\) and multiply by \(H_P^{-1}\). The first term becomes
\[
 QB(H_PY)^{-1/2}
 =Q(QH_T)(H_PY)^{-1/2}
 =G^{1/2}Q^2(H_T/Y)^{1/2}.
\]
The second becomes
\[
 Q^{5/4}(BY)^{1/2}
 =Q^{5/4}(QH_TY)^{1/2}
 =Q^{7/4}(H_TY)^{1/2}.
\]

We now bound the diagonal in (4). The number of supported pairs \((p,u)\) with \(p\mid u\) is \(O(Q^\epsilon U)\): if \(U/Y\ge1\), there are \(O(Y)\) primes and \(O(U/Y)\) possible quotients; if \(U/Y<1\), nonemptiness forces \(U\asymp Y\) and the quotient is bounded. Summing \(q\), summing \(h\), and multiplying by \(H_P^{-1}\) therefore gives
\[
 \ll Q^\epsilon QU.
\]
This proves (2).

Divide by \(x\asymp gGQ^2\). The first ratio is
\[
 \ll g^{-1}G^{-1/2}(H_T/Y)^{1/2}
 \ll g^{-1}G^{-1/2}Q^{-\sigma/2},
\]
where the harmless factor \(2^{1/2}\) from (1) is absorbed. The second ratio is
\[
 \ll g^{-1}G^{-1}Q^{-1/4}(H_TY)^{1/2}
 \le g^{-1}G^{-1}Q^{-3\sigma/2}.
\]
For the diagonal, \(U\ll Q^{1-\sigma}\), so
\[
 \frac{QU}{gGQ^2}\ll g^{-1}G^{-1}Q^{-\sigma}.
\]
All three terms save a fixed power of \(Q\). Choosing \(\epsilon\) sufficiently small proves (3).

Fact \(664a92777dc5f5db\) has exactly a family of unit numerators \(A_q\), the selector \((u,p)=1\), product \(UY\asymp QH_T\), and prime cells with \(H_TQ^\sigma/2\le Y\le Q^{3/2-\beta-3\sigma}\). The proof above retained each of these slots and replaced only its frequency and prefactor by \(H_P\) and \(H_P^{-1}\). Therefore the final applicability statement follows.

glossary.H_P: The literal Poisson frequency scale H_T/G in the off-scale unit-target interval-prime trace.
glossary.cal A_{U,Y}: The literal-frequency unit-target interval-prime reciprocal trace.

eb01e7b374521a0c.title: C-qSRC-DIL-BV: EXACT DILATOR-CHARACTER TRANSPOSE AND THE SCALE-PERFECT DISCRETE-VARIATION SUPPLIER
eb01e7b374521a0c.author: slava chan
eb01e7b374521a0c.statement:
C-qSRC-DIL-BV: EXACT DILATOR-CHARACTER TRANSPOSE AND THE SCALE-PERFECT DISCRETE-VARIATION SUPPLIER.

Adopt C-qSRC-RES from fact d5cfc4a905989cc8 on one block
Dcal<=d_lambda<2Dcal,
with Dcal>Q^2. For every squarefree m>=2, unit c modulo m, and nonprincipal character chi modulo m, define for each integer d
A_{m,c,chi}(d)
 =sum chi(v_lambda)B_lambda(R)conjugate(B_lambda(R')),           (1)
where the sum is over all exact retained lambda,R,R' entering C-qSRC>=2 with
d_lambda=d, m_q=m, C_q congruent c modulo m.
Every literal hard and pair-dependent selector remains inside (1). Set A_{m,c,chi}(d)=0 outside
Dcal<=d<2Dcal,
and define its complete discrete variation
V_{m,c,chi}
 =sum_{d in Z}|A_{m,c,chi}(d+1)-A_{m,c,chi}(d)|.                (2)
Then the literal multiplicative transform in fact d5cfc4a905989cc8 has the exact dilator transpose
Zhat_{m,c}(chi)
 =sum_{Dcal<=d<2Dcal}chi(d)A_{m,c,chi}(d),                      (C-qSRC-DIL)
and
|Zhat_{m,c}(chi)|<=m V_{m,c,chi}.                               (3)

Every supported physical conductor satisfies
m=m_q<4Q^2.                                                      (4)
Consequently the single source-specific variation estimate
sum_{m>=2}sum_{c modulo m}^*
  1/phi(m)sum_{chi!=chi_0}
  |G_{m,c}(chi)|V_{m,c,chi}
 <=x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 B F^2/Dcal                              (C-qSRC-BV-SUP)
implies
|C-qSRC>=2|
 <=x^{o(1)}|omega_F|^2 BQ^2F^2/Dcal.                            (5)

Estimate C-qSRC-BV-SUP is not asserted. It requires the variation of the complete literal dilator profile after all v, copy, ray, source and deletion aggregation; no bounded variation of an individual mask is assumed. This theorem proves the exact transpose, the elementary complete-period bound, and the scale-perfect conditional handoff only. It proves no C-qSRC-SUP, no P-qSRC-SUP, no full GA-RAY-SPEC, no tail payment, and no Goldbach conclusion.
eb01e7b374521a0c.proof:
By definition (3) in fact d5cfc4a905989cc8,
Zhat_{m,c}(chi)
 =sum_z^* Z_{m,c}(z)chi(z).                                    (6)
Expand Z_{m,c}(z) using its complete literal definition in that fact. On every supported term n=d_lambda v_lambda is a unit modulo m, so
chi(n)=chi(d_lambda)chi(v_lambda).                              (7)
Group the resulting finite sum by d=d_lambda. The factors other than chi(d) are exactly those collected in (1), including chi(v_lambda). This proves C-qSRC-DIL without changing any selector.

Let I be the finite integer interval Dcal<=d<2Dcal, and write
S(t)=sum_{d in I,d<=t}chi(d).
Because chi is nonprincipal, its sum over a complete residue system modulo m is zero. Partition any initial segment of I into complete blocks of length m and one remaining block. The remaining block has fewer than m terms, each of modulus at most one, so
|S(t)|<=m.                                                        (8)
Discrete summation by parts, with A(d) extended by zero off I, gives
sum_{d in I}chi(d)A(d)
 =-sum_{d in Z}S(d)[A(d+1)-A(d)],                               (9)
where S(d) is interpreted as zero before I and as the complete sum after I; the latter is also covered by (8). Taking absolute values in (9) and using (8) proves (3).

For a supported primitive ray R=(epsilon,a,b), the physical support has q=ka with k>=1 and q<2Q, hence a<2Q. The same holds for a'. Fact cff9d29efb555b8e gives
m_q=aa'/gcd(aa',mathscr A Delta_0),
so
m_q<=aa'<4Q^2,
proving (4).

Finally use the exact character expansion (4) in fact d5cfc4a905989cc8:
C-qSRC>=2
 =sum_{m,c}1/phi(m)sum_{chi!=chi_0}
   G_{m,c}(chi)Zhat_{m,c}(chi).                                (10)
Apply the triangle inequality, (3), and (4):
|C-qSRC>=2|
 <=4Q^2
   sum_{m,c}1/phi(m)sum_{chi!=chi_0}
   |G_{m,c}(chi)|V_{m,c,chi}.                                  (11)
Insert C-qSRC-BV-SUP into (11). The absolute constant four is absorbed in x^{o(1)}, proving (5). No claim about the unproved variation ledger was used, and all limitations follow.

glossary.A_{m,c,chi}(d): The complete literal v/copy/ray aggregate at fixed marked dilator d after extracting the character factor chi(d).
glossary.C-qSRC-BV-SUP: The weighted total-variation estimate sufficient for the centered-source target.
glossary.C-qSRC-DIL: The exact character transpose of the centered source into the marked dilator variable.
glossary.V_{m,c,chi}: The endpoint-inclusive discrete total variation of the exact dilator profile A_{m,c,chi}.

eb589e60e7e30a33.title: UNIT-RAY HARD-CONDUCTOR RAMANUJAN SPECTRUM AND THE EXACT CONSTANT-RESIDUE CORE
eb589e60e7e30a33.author: slava chan
eb589e60e7e30a33.statement:
UNIT-RAY HARD-CONDUCTOR RAMANUJAN SPECTRUM AND THE EXACT CONSTANT-RESIDUE CORE.

Adopt the Dcal>Q^2 principal source P-qSRC and its exact unit-denominator restriction a=a'=1 from facts e9e9563501147a1a, cff9d29efb555b8e, and a36284a9dbec7837. Fix one exact marked copy lambda over n=d_lambda v_lambda. Put
T=mathscr A,
rho_lambda=d_lambda/gcd(d_lambda,T).                               (1)
The integer d_lambda and hence rho_lambda are squarefree.

For a unit ray R=(epsilon,1,b), retain the complete coefficient
C_lambda(R)=A_lambda(epsilon,b)U_lambda(epsilon,b),                 (2)
with the exact signed U_lambda transform and every literal mask of fact a36284a9dbec7837. Aggregate these coefficients by the signed-numerator residue
C_lambda(z)
 =sum_{supported (epsilon,b): epsilon b congruent z (mod rho_lambda)}
   C_lambda(epsilon,1,b),
z in Z/rho_lambda Z.                                               (3)
Define the hard conductor kernel
K_{rho,L}(delta)
 =1_{rho/gcd(rho,delta)>L},
delta in Z/rho Z,                                                  (4)
where gcd(rho,0)=rho. Then the complete hard unit-ray contribution of this copy is exactly
Q_lambda^{unit}
 =sum_{z,z' (mod rho_lambda)}
  K_{rho_lambda,L}(z-z')
  C_lambda(z)conjugate(C_lambda(z')).                              (5)
No ray coefficient or selector is changed in (3)-(5).

For a modulo rho define
C_hat_lambda(a)=sum_{z (mod rho)}C_lambda(z)e_rho(-az),             (6)
and define
kappa_{rho,L}(a)
 =sum_{e|rho,e>L}c_e(a),                                          (7)
where c_e is the Ramanujan sum. The exact additive spectral decomposition is
Q_lambda^{unit}
 =1/rho_lambda sum_{a (mod rho_lambda)}
  kappa_{rho_lambda,L}(a)|C_hat_lambda(a)|^2.                      (UNIT-RAY-RAM-SPEC)
Consequently the full hard unit-ray restriction of P-qSRC is the sum of UNIT-RAY-RAM-SPEC over its exact n,lambda copies.

There are three exact consequences.

First, if rho_lambda<=L, then Q_lambda^{unit}=0.                     (8)

Second, the constant-residue eigenvalue is
kappa_{rho,L}(0)=sum_{e|rho,e>L}phi(e).                            (9)
Thus the dangerous constant Fourier mode is the complete signed unit-ray aggregate
C_hat_lambda(0)
 =sum_{supported (epsilon,b)}
   A_lambda(epsilon,b)U_lambda(epsilon,b).                         (10)
No cancellation of (10) is supplied by the hard-conductor projector.

Third, if rho_lambda=p is prime and p>L, then
kappa_{p,L}(0)=p-1,
kappa_{p,L}(a)=-1 for a not congruent 0 modulo p,                  (11)
and therefore
Q_lambda^{unit}
 =|C_hat_lambda(0)|^2
  -sum_{z (mod p)}|C_lambda(z)|^2.                                (12)
Hence on the prime-rho chamber every nonconstant residue mode has operator size one, while the sole constant residue mode has size p-1. The remaining prime-rho supplier is therefore source cancellation in the complete signed aggregate (10), or cancellation after aggregation over exact copies; generic positive row norms do not pay it.

This theorem proves the exact hard-deletion spectrum only. It proves no bound for the constant mode (10), no complete unit-ray estimate, no P-qSRC-SUP, no C-qSRC-SUP, no tail payment, and no Goldbach conclusion.
eb589e60e7e30a33.proof:
Fact e55b27d39c593164 proves that d_lambda is the squarefree marked divisor of a squarefree n. Therefore its divisor rho_lambda in (1) is squarefree.

For unit rays R=(epsilon,1,b), R'=(epsilon',1,b'), the primitive determinant is
Delta_0=epsilon b-epsilon'b'.                                      (13)
Fact cff9d29efb555b8e gives
m_d=
 rho_lambda/gcd(rho_lambda,Delta_0).                               (14)
The Dcal>Q^2 principal coefficient on m_q=1 is one by fact e9e9563501147a1a, and fact a36284a9dbec7837 gives the complete coefficient product
C_lambda(R)conjugate(C_lambda(R')).
Because L>1, the condition m_d>L automatically excludes Delta_0=0 and the fully resonant pairs. Thus the hard unit-ray form has exactly the pair kernel in (14).

The value of gcd(rho_lambda,Delta_0) depends only on the two residues
z=epsilon b and z'=epsilon'b' modulo rho_lambda. Grouping all exact supported rays by these residues gives (5). This finite regrouping occurs after every complete U_lambda transform is formed, so no coefficient or selector is changed.

We diagonalize the translation-invariant kernel (4). For fixed a modulo rho,
sum_{delta (mod rho)}K_{rho,L}(delta)e_rho(a delta)
 =sum_{e|rho,e>L}
   sum_{delta (mod rho): rho/gcd(rho,delta)=e}
    e_rho(a delta).                                                (15)
For one divisor e|rho, the residues in the inner sum are uniquely
delta=(rho/e)u (mod rho),
u in (Z/eZ)^*.
Therefore that inner sum is
sum_{u (mod e)}^*e_e(au)=c_e(a).                                  (16)
Equations (15)-(16) prove that the additive Fourier eigenvalue is kappa_{rho,L}(a) from (7). Fourier inversion and Parseval for the circulant quadratic form prove UNIT-RAY-RAM-SPEC.

If rho<=L, no divisor e|rho exceeds L, so (7) is empty and (8) follows. At a=0, c_e(0)=phi(e), proving (9). Equation (10) is immediate from (3) and (6).

If rho=p is prime with p>L, the only divisor e>L is p. The prime Ramanujan sum is
c_p(0)=p-1,
c_p(a)=-1 for a not congruent 0 modulo p.
This proves (11). Insert (11) in UNIT-RAY-RAM-SPEC and use Parseval
sum_{a (mod p)}|C_hat_lambda(a)|^2
 =p sum_{z (mod p)}|C_lambda(z)|^2.
The result simplifies to (12). Every scope exclusion follows because no estimate for the literal coefficient aggregate has been assumed.

glossary.C_lambda(z): The complete signed unit-ray coefficient aggregated by epsilon b modulo rho_lambda.
glossary.UNIT-RAY-RAM-SPEC: The exact Ramanujan spectral decomposition of one hard unit-ray copy.
glossary.kappa_{rho,L}(a): The additive Fourier eigenvalue sum_{e|rho,e>L}c_e(a) of the hard conductor kernel.

ebef127160e08c0f.title: LABEL-AND-AMPLITUDE PROVENANCE BRIDGE FOR THE SELECTED FIRST-BUFFER C3 PROJECTION
ebef127160e08c0f.author: slava chan
ebef127160e08c0f.statement:
LABEL-AND-AMPLITUDE PROVENANCE BRIDGE FOR THE SELECTED FIRST-BUFFER C3 PROJECTION.

Use the fixed bad-N active sibling labels (D,M,U;R,K) of facts 1e2d635f6691e832 and 60b26a9b6f79467a. Their original source blocks contain the smooth factors
W(dm/x)psi(d/D_*)Phi(d/D)Phi(m/M)Phi(rk/U)Phi(r/R)Phi(k/K),
with W supported in [a,b], 1/2<a<b<1, Phi supported in [1/2,2], and U comparable to x. Consequently every active label satisfies
DM comparable to x and RK comparable to x.                                (1)

Perform the Poisson decomposition separately inside each fixed active label and exact outer gcd, and consider its paired nonzero-frequency terms. Let R_C3,buf,sel be the complete selected first-buffer C3 projection of facts 32f645844f1ca9a1 and dde1e246a629bcc4. Then every paired-frequency term of R_C3,buf,sel retains:
(a) one original active label (D,M,U;R,K), hence both comparisons in (1);
(b) the Fourier-transformed smooth amplitude arising from that label's original W,psi,Phi factors;
(c) the same selected N, fixed-U, high, frozen U_low parent, orientation, provenance and exact outer-gcd coordinates.

The intervening selected-high, parent, normalized-beta and A/B/C1/C2/C3 operations only restrict or finitely partition these transformed paired-frequency terms. They do not mix active scale labels, change D,M,U,R,K, or create a term with no original active-label provenance. Auxiliary target-gcd, prime-order, equal-cell, collision and deletion refinements retain the same label and amplitude provenance, and recombination returns the complete transformed coefficient on that label.

Therefore every fixed selected C3 layer satisfies the two product-scale hypotheses required by facts da22464a2f614042 and 2e0b40b1ba77fb6f. This theorem asserts label and transformed-amplitude provenance only; it does not claim that a Poisson dual-frequency term is an unchanged original dm+rk=N summand. It asserts no C3 estimate, negative atom, late-beta estimate, moving actual-Z, endpoint, PMD, DCE, or Goldbach conclusion.
ebef127160e08c0f.proof:
The product comparisons are label-level facts. On W(dm/x) support, dm is comparable to x, and the d,m dyadic cutoffs make dm comparable to DM. Thus DM is comparable to x. Fact 60b26a9b6f79467a gives U comparable to x. The factors Phi(rk/U), Phi(r/R), and Phi(k/K) make rk comparable both to U and to RK, so RK is comparable to x. This proves (1) for every original active label before Poisson summation.

Fact df9748efe29ab475 performs the Poisson decomposition after fixing the physical scales and exact g. Its proof writes the progression sum on that fixed label as a zero frequency plus dual frequencies h, with a Fourier transform of the fixed label's smooth one-variable amplitude. It does not sum together or replace D,M,U,R,K by new scales. Fact d8ba46800ba433c2 gives the explicit transformed amplitude F_{g,a,b} and its Fourier transform; every smooth source factor is retained inside that amplitude. Hence each paired nonzero-frequency term is new as a Fourier term, but carries the same active scale label and transformed-amplitude provenance. We make no termwise claim about the original arithmetic summands.

Fact 60b26a9b6f79467a selects residual/high families after this labelwise Poisson decomposition. Fact 7ffe3d237362a451 then subtracts complete C91 and low-beta transformed families without changing the labels of the remaining Fourier terms. Facts c155c30b0450a4f9, 323499eb9e75ce72, 3edf35eeb12b56e8 and 32f645844f1ca9a1 successively subtract complete A, B, C1 and C2 coordinates and identify C3 in the first buffer. Each statement explicitly retains the selected source, fixed-U, high, smooth/Fourier, parent, orientation, provenance and exact-g coordinates. Anatomy expansion partitions the normalized Mobius coefficient but leaves the paired phase and smooth Fourier amplitude unchanged. Fact dde1e246a629bcc4 finally projects to the first buffer and recombines auxiliary refinements.

Restrictions and finite partitions of an indexed transformed family preserve the index label and amplitude provenance. Recombination sums the partition pieces back to the complete transformed coefficient on the same label. Therefore every term in R_C3,buf,sel carries an active label satisfying (1) and the claimed coordinates. This is exactly the product-scale information required by the two orientation facts and proves all assertions, while avoiding any inverse-Poisson or unchanged-original-summand claim.

glossary.label-and-amplitude provenance: Inheritance by a Poisson dual-frequency term of its fixed active scale label and the Fourier-transformed smooth source amplitude, without claiming identity with an original arithmetic summand.

ec8a0fbdab03cda6.title: ACTUAL FIRST-NONRESONANT-PRIME COFACTOR BLOCK CHAMBER FOR THE TOP B,C1,C2,C3,C4 ROWS, WITH NO FORMAL REPEATED-BLOCK CARDINALITY TAX
ec8a0fbdab03cda6.author: slava chan
ec8a0fbdab03cda6.statement:
ACTUAL FIRST-NONRESONANT-PRIME COFACTOR BLOCK CHAMBER FOR THE TOP B,C1,C2,C3,C4 ROWS, WITH NO FORMAL REPEATED-BLOCK CARDINALITY TAX. Fix 0=Z>=Q^zeta (3) for all sufficiently large Q. On a B row, (3) is not automatic; define the exact B small-selected-prime complement by p=Q^zeta for which J_p is nonempty, put M_p=floor((p-1)/2). Starting at the least element of J_p, partition J_p deterministically into consecutive disjoint integer blocks J_{p,k}, every block except possibly the last having cardinality M_p and the last having cardinality at most M_p. Put L_{p,k}=#J_{p,k}. Call a block long when p^delta<=L_{p,k}

=Q^zeta} sum_{k: J_{p,k} long} V_{p,k} <<_{delta,eta,zeta} Q^(-zeta eta) (sum_{p>=Q^zeta} sum_{k: J_{p,k} long} Y_{p,k})^2. (8) In particular, repeated disjoint cofactor blocks at the same selected prime cause no formal factor equal to their number in (8). The exact unestimated complement of this block payment is the union of: (i) the B rows in (4); (ii) all short blocks L_{p,k}3B then all of J_p is one short block. (9) Thus p^(1+delta)>3B is an explicit large-selected-prime/short-cofactor subcomplement. This theorem is a literal chamber and tax ledger only; it proves no estimate for the complements (i)-(iii), no complete B,C1,C2,C3,C4 trace estimate, and no Goldbach conclusion.
ec8a0fbdab03cda6.proof:
Facts e58fc7c00f1683e6 and f0f6807663d3ef3c give B/2<=n<=2B, d_star|n, squarefreeness of d_star, and (d_star,n/d_star)=1. Fact 4f9aec67f5be35db selects a prime p|d_star and writes d_star=pm with (p,m)=1. Write n=d_star v_star, where (d_star,v_star)=1 by fact f0f6807663d3ef3c. Then
t=n/p=m v_star.
Neither m nor v_star is divisible by p, so p does not divide t. Dividing B/2<=n=pt<=2B by p and using integrality of t gives (1).

On every Cj copy, fact f0f6807663d3ef3c defines d_star as the product of the exact rough primes in that Cj copy. Fact e58fc7c00f1683e6 states that each such prime is at least
Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma).
Because beta<6/5,
3/2-beta-3sigma>3/10-3sigma>zeta.
Therefore Z>=Q^zeta for all sufficiently large Q, and p|d_star implies (3).

On a B copy, fact f0f6807663d3ef3c defines d_star=y, the first-crossing stopping product. The stopping identity in its predecessor states that every prime divisor of y is at most L=Q^(beta-1+sigma); it gives no fixed positive-power lower bound for each prime divisor. Therefore one may restrict to p>=Q^zeta and must leave (4) as a separate literal complement. No stronger B lower bound is claimed.

Assume p>=Q^zeta. For sufficiently large Q, p>=3, so M_p=floor((p-1)/2) is a positive integer and M_p<p. The stated left-to-right partition is finite, disjoint, exhaustive, and each block has cardinality at most M_p<p. If two integers in one block have the same residue modulo p, their difference is divisible by p and has absolute value strictly below p, hence is zero. Reduction is injective. Deleting the possible integer divisible by p splits the cyclic residue interval into at most two nonzero additive intervals. These are exactly the integer-block hypotheses of fact bbd687d016ee3ff6.

Fix a long block. By (5), its length is below p and at least p^delta. Apply equation (2) of fact bbd687d016ee3ff6 with this block, its literal source data, its tuple mask, and its assumed contractive four-linear functional. With the notation (6), that fact gives
V_{p,k} <<_{delta,eta} p^(-eta) Y_{p,k}^2.                       (10)
The constant is uniform in p and k because the residue image has at most two interval components.

For every term in the double sum, p>=Q^zeta, so p^(-eta)<=Q^(-zeta eta). Summing (10) gives
sum_{p,k}V_{p,k}
 << Q^(-zeta eta) sum_{p,k}Y_{p,k}^2.
All Y_{p,k} are nonnegative. Therefore
sum_{p,k}Y_{p,k}^2 <=(sum_{p,k}Y_{p,k})^2.
This proves (8). The argument contains no application of Cauchy or the triangle inequality that inserts the number of blocks; this proves the stated no-formal-cardinality conclusion. It does not compare the final sum of Y_{p,k} with an upstream norm, which is why complement (iii) is retained.

It remains to prove (9). From (1),
#J_p=floor(2B/p)-ceil(B/(2p))+1.
The elementary floor and ceiling inequalities give
3B/(2p)-1 <=#J_p<=3B/(2p)+1.                                  (11)
If p^(1+delta)<=B, then the lower bound in (11) is at least
(3/2)p^delta-1>=p^delta
for sufficiently large p. Also M_p>=p^delta for sufficiently large p because delta<1. Hence the first block, whose cardinality is min(M_p,#J_p), is long.

If p^(1+delta)>3B, the upper bound in (11) is strictly less than
p^delta/2+1<p^delta
for sufficiently large p. Hence #J_p<p^delta. The deterministic partition then consists of the single block J_p, and it is short. This proves (9). The three listed complements and the final scope statements merely record hypotheses or sectors not estimated by (8).

glossary.J_p: The exact integer interval containing every cofactor t=n/p at a fixed first nonresonant selected prime p.
glossary.J_{p,k}: A deterministic consecutive sub-p block in the partition of J_p.
glossary.V_{p,k}: The exceptional repeated-pole occupancy on one selected-prime cofactor block.
glossary.Y_{p,k}: The trivial fourth-moment source-envelope scale for one selected-prime cofactor block.

ec9d666ae1756a03.title: EXPLICIT SMALL-TARGET-GCD INTERVAL-PRIME TRACE BOUND. Fix integers J,C_A>=1, constants C>=1, 0<kappa<=1/100, sigma=kappa/100, 0<eta<sigma, and 1<=beta<=6/5-2kappa. Let Q be sufficiently large, put B=Q^beta, H_T=B/Q, choose G>0 with Q^{-sigma+eta}<=G<=Q^{sigma-eta}, put H_P=H_T/G, L_0=H_TQ^sigma, and Z=Q^{3/2-beta-3sigma}. Fix a nonzero integer L_src with |L_src|<=Q^{C_A}, and let C_small be the squarefree divisors c of L_src with c<=Q^{sigma/2}
ec9d666ae1756a03.author: slava chan
ec9d666ae1756a03.statement:
EXPLICIT SMALL-TARGET-GCD INTERVAL-PRIME TRACE BOUND. Fix integers J,C_A>=1, constants C>=1, 0<kappa<=1/100, sigma=kappa/100, 0<eta<sigma, and 1<=beta<=6/5-2kappa. Let Q be sufficiently large, put B=Q^beta, H_T=B/Q, choose G>0 with Q^{-sigma+eta}<=G<=Q^{sigma-eta}, put H_P=H_T/G, L_0=H_TQ^sigma, and Z=Q^{3/2-beta-3sigma}. Fix a nonzero integer L_src with |L_src|<=Q^{C_A}, and let C_small be the squarefree divisors c of L_src with c<=Q^{sigma/2}.
For each c in C_small put Q_c=Q/c and choose real U_c,Y_c>=1 satisfying C^{-1}B<=U_cY_c<=CB and L_0/2<=Y_c<=Z. For q with Q_c<=q<2Q_c let |d_{c,q}|<=1, supported only when q is squarefree, gcd(c,q)=1, and gcd(L_src/c,q)=1. For every dyadic F>=1 choose coefficients nu_{c,F}(h), alpha_{c,F}(u), gamma_{c,F}(p) with |nu_{c,F}(h)|<=tau_J(|h|), |alpha_{c,F}(u)|<=tau_J(u), and |gamma_{c,F}(p)|<=1. Their supports are F<=|h|<2F, U_c<=u<2U_c, and primes p with Y_c<=p<2Y_c and L_0<p<Z. Let omega_{c,F} be scalars such that for every integer J_0>=1, |omega_{c,F}|<=C_{J_0}min(1,(F/H_P)^{-J_0}), uniformly in c,F.
Let mathfrak F be a fixed family of smooth functions Psi on (0,infinity)^4, supported in [1,2]^4, such that for every multi-index all derivatives with respect to the four logarithmic coordinates are uniformly bounded. Choose Psi_{c,F} in mathfrak F and define
T_c=H_P^{-1} sum_{F dyadic,F>=1} omega_{c,F} sum_{Q_c<=q<2Q_c} d_{c,q} sum_{F<=|h|<2F} nu_{c,F}(h) sum_{U_c<=u<2U_c} alpha_{c,F}(u) sum_{Y_c<=p<2Y_c, p prime, L_0<p<Z, gcd(up,cq)=1} gamma_{c,F}(p) Psi_{c,F}(q/Q_c,|h|/F,u/U_c,p/Y_c) e_q(-(L_src/c)h(up)^{-1}).
Then there exists delta=delta(kappa,eta,C_A,J,C,mathfrak F)>0 such that sum_{c in C_small}|T_c|<<Q^{2-delta}.
ec9d666ae1756a03.proof:
We first separate the smooth amplitude rigorously. In the logarithmic coordinates log(q/Q_c), log(|h|/F), log(u/U_c), log(p/Y_c), extend each Psi_{c,F} from its fixed compact box to a smooth function on a fixed four-dimensional torus. Its Fourier series is an absolutely summable combination of products f_n(q)g_n(h)a_n(u)b_n(p), with every one-variable factor bounded by one and sum_n|lambda_n| bounded uniformly over mathfrak F. This follows by repeated integration by parts, choosing derivative order greater than five. Thus it suffices to estimate one product mode; absorb its factors into d,nu,alpha,gamma. The condition gcd(up,c)=1 is the product of gcd(u,c)=1 and gcd(p,c)=1 and is likewise absorbed into the separate u and p coefficients.
Fix c,F and put u_F=F/H_P. Suppose 2F<=Y_c and 16FY_c<=Q_c. Then q>=Q_c gives 8FY_c<q. Apply fact 4a101b703d4499f6 with modulus q, target -(L_src/c), frequency parameter 2F, u-scale U_c and prime scale Y_c. Its target is a unit because gcd(L_src/c,q)=1. Also U_c<=q: from U_cY_c<<B and Y_c>=H_TQ^sigma/2, U_c<<Q^{1-sigma}, while q>=Q/(2c)>=Q^{1-sigma/2}/2.
After summing q, fact 4a101b703d4499f6 has prefactor F^{-1}. Multiplying by F/H_P=u_F and by omega_{c,F}, its first term, second term, and p|u diagonal are bounded, up to Q^epsilon, by
c^{-1}G^{1/2}Q^2(H_T/Y_c)^{1/2}|omega_{c,F}|u_F^{1/2},
c^{-5/4}Q^{7/4}(H_TY_c)^{1/2}|omega_{c,F}|u_F,
and c^{-1}QU_c|omega_{c,F}|u_F.
Here the powers c^{-1},c^{-5/4},c^{-1} arise by replacing the modulus scale Q by Q_c=Q/c in the two terms and the q-count. Since Y_c>=H_TQ^sigma/2, Y_c<=Z, G<=Q^{sigma-eta}, and U_c<<Q^{1-sigma}, the scale parts are respectively O(c^{-1}Q^{2-eta/2}), O(c^{-5/4}Q^{2-3sigma/2}), and O(c^{-1}Q^{2-sigma}). The dyadic u_F factors are at most one when u_F<=1 and are summable for u_F>1 after using the omega bound with J_0>3.
It remains to show that this analytic range extends far enough. One has Y_c/H_P>=GQ^sigma/2>=Q^eta/2. Also, using Y_c<=Z and H_TZ=Q^{1/2-3sigma},
Q_c/(H_PY_c)>=c^{-1}GQ^{1/2+3sigma}>=Q^{1/2+(3/2)sigma+eta}.
Thus both 2F<=Y_c and 16FY_c<=Q_c hold whenever u_F<=c_0Q^eta for a fixed sufficiently small c_0.
For u_F>c_0Q^eta use the literal formula and bound absolutely. The q,h,u,p counts and H_P^{-1} give, up to Q^epsilon and the uniformly bounded amplitude, Q_cU_cY_cu_F|omega_{c,F}|<<c^{-1}Q^{1+beta+epsilon}u_F|omega_{c,F}|. Since beta<=6/5, choose J_0 sufficiently large in terms of eta; the dyadic tail is O(c^{-1}Q^{2-delta_0}) for some delta_0>0.
Finally sum c. Both sum_{c|L_src}c^{-1} and sum_{c|L_src}c^{-5/4} are at most tau(|L_src|)<<Q^epsilon. The uniform Fourier projective norm and all dyadic sums are absorbed by reducing the fixed power saving. This proves the theorem.

glossary.C_small: The small exact target-gcd divisor set.
glossary.T_c: The explicit complete-frequency interval-prime trace on gcd layer c.
glossary.mathfrak F: The uniformly bounded four-variable scaled-smooth amplitude family.

ecd6325d7ef2bc37.title: ADDITIVE-RECIPROCITY EXCHANGE, EXACT ARCHIMEDEAN-PHASE CANCELLATION, AND THE DOUBLE-MU-RECIP-N SUPPLIER. Fix one strict-top complete unmarked pre-marker source row of facts \(b0a38f5e9ae7feb6\) and \(544c7ba4db45c06f\). Thus
ecd6325d7ef2bc37.author: slava chan
ecd6325d7ef2bc37.statement:
ADDITIVE-RECIPROCITY EXCHANGE, EXACT ARCHIMEDEAN-PHASE CANCELLATION, AND THE DOUBLE-MU-RECIP-N SUPPLIER. Fix one strict-top complete unmarked pre-marker source row of facts \(b0a38f5e9ae7feb6\) and \(544c7ba4db45c06f\). Thus
\[
 \beta_m<\beta<6/5,\qquad q\asymp Q,\qquad n\asymp B=Q^\beta,
\]
the orientation is \(\epsilon\in\{-1,1\}\), the exact outer gcd is \(g\), the fixed target is \(L_{\rm src}=N/g\), and
\[
 (g,qn)=(q,n)=1.
\]
Let \(H_P\) be the literal Poisson frequency scale. Fix a signed dyadic block
\[
 F\leq |h|<2F.
\]
After all complete provenance siblings are recombined, define the literal coefficient without the Archimedean reciprocity phase by
\[
 {\cal C}^{\flat}_{g,q,n}(h)
 =\mathbf 1_{F\leq |h|<2F}{H_P\over n}
  \widehat F^\epsilon_{g,q,n}(\epsilon h/n).                \tag{1}
\]
It has a separated projective expansion
\[
 {\cal C}^{\flat}_{g,q,n}(h)
 =\sum_\rho\eta_\rho A_\rho(q)C_\rho(n)E_\rho(h),        \tag{2}
\]
where the one-variable factors in \(q,n\) have supremum at most one after normalization, and, for every fixed \(A>0\),
\[
 \sum_\rho|\eta_\rho|\,{\cal V}_F(E_\rho)
 \ll_A(\log x)^{O(1)}(1+F/H_P)^{-A}.                         \tag{3}
\]
Here \({\cal V}_F\) is supremum plus discrete total variation on the fixed signed block. The complete dyadic \(F\)-sum and all standard dyadic source boxes have total coefficient cost \(x^{o(1)}\).

For every supported \((q,n)\), one has the exact phase identity
\[
 \boxed{
 e\!\left({\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\over qn}\right)
 e_q\!\left(-\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\overline n\right)
 =
 e_n\!\left(\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\overline q\right).
 }                                                             \tag{4}
\]
Consequently the exact contribution of this projective box to the complete unmarked row is
\[
 \boxed{
 {\cal U}^{\epsilon}_{g;B,F}
 ={1\over H_P}\sum_\rho\eta_\rho
 \sum_{\substack{q\asymp Q,\ n\asymp B\\(g,qn)=(q,n)=1}}
 \mu(q)\mu(n)A_\rho(q)C_\rho(n)
 \sum_{F\leq |h|<2F}E_\rho(h)
 e_n\!\left(\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\overline q\right).
 }                                                             \tag{5}
\]
Thus additive reciprocity changes the reciprocal modulus from \(q\) to \(n\) while retaining both literal signs \(\mu(q)\) and \(\mu(n)\), both frequency signs, the fixed possibly nonunit target, every exact \(g\)- and cross-coprimality gate, and the complete source coefficient. No one-sided identity, HB routing, q-wise Cauchy inequality, or absolute value has been used.

The corresponding source-specific analytic supplier is
\[
 \boxed{
 {1\over H_P}\left|
 \sum_\rho\eta_\rho
 \sum_{\substack{q\asymp Q,\ n\asymp B\\(g,qn)=(q,n)=1}}
 \mu(q)\mu(n)A_\rho(q)C_\rho(n)
 \sum_{F\leq |h|<2F}E_\rho(h)
 e_n\!left(\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\overline q\right)
 \right|
 \ll Q^{2-\delta_D}.
 }                                                     \tag{DOUBLE-MU-RECIP-N}
\]
If this holds uniformly over the displayed projective boxes for some fixed \(\delta_D>0\), their \(x^{o(1)}\) mass pays the complete strict-top unmarked source at each fixed outer row. In particular it would bypass, rather than estimate separately, ULTRA-LONG-MU-N and ENDPOINT-DIAGONAL-N. Fact \(b67d5504c8454100\) proves that the direct arbitrary-coefficient Bettin--Chandee right-hand side does not furnish this saving on the source band \(\beta>7/6\).

Neither DOUBLE-MU-RECIP-N nor any cancellation estimate is asserted here. The statement is an exact source handoff and legal coefficient audit only. It proves no post-A or Goldbach conclusion.
ecd6325d7ef2bc37.proof:
For coprime positive integers \(q,n\), choose inverses \(\overline n\pmod q\) and \(\overline q\pmod n\). The integer
\[
 n\overline n+q\overline q-1
\]
is divisible by both \(q\) and \(n\), hence by \(qn\). Therefore
\[
 {\overline n\over q}+{\overline q\over n}
 \equiv {1\over qn}\pmod 1.                                \tag{6}
\]
Multiplying (6) by \(-\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\) gives
\[
 -{\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\over q}\overline n
 \equiv
 -{\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\over qn}
 +{\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\over n}\overline q
 \pmod1,
\]
which proves (4).

We next justify (2)--(3), including the removal of the ordinary exponential. Fact \(544c7ba4db45c06f\), applied with the factorization \(n=n\cdot1\), gives a separated expansion with (3) for
\[
 {\cal C}^{\flat}_{g,q,n}(h)
 e\!\left({\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\over qn}\right).        \tag{7}
\]
It remains to multiply (7) by
\[
 R(q,n,h)=e\!\left(-{\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\over qn}\right).             \tag{8}
\]
On the normalized dyadic box, the scaled phase size of (8) is
\[
 {|L_{\rm src}|F\over QB}
 ={ |L_{\rm src}|\over QM}{F\over H_P}                     \tag{9}
\]
in the forward orientation, because \(H_P=B/M\); in the reverse orientation the same identity holds with the corresponding physical scale \(K\). The strict-top source relations in facts \(b0a38f5e9ae7feb6\) and \(3f2f255ea6845a50\) give \(N\asymp DM\) in the forward orientation and \(N\asymp RK\) in the reverse orientation. Since \(L_{\rm src}=N/g\), \(D/g\asymp Q\) forward and \(R/g\asymp Q\) reverse, the first factor on the right of (9) is bounded. Thus every scaled derivative of (8) is bounded by a fixed power of \(1+F/H_P\).

Extend the normalized-box version of (8) smoothly to a fixed compact cube and expand it in a Fourier series. Repeated integration by parts gives a separated expansion whose coefficient mass, with one frequency derivative included for the discrete \(h\)-variation, is at most
\[
 (1+F/H_P)^{O(1)}.                                            \tag{10}
\]
Multiplying this expansion with (7) proves (2). Since the decay in fact \(544c7ba4db45c06f\) is available to arbitrary order, choose its order larger than the fixed power in (10). This proves (3), and its complete dyadic summability follows exactly as in that predecessor.

Finally insert (4) into equation (4) of fact \(b0a38f5e9ae7feb6\), restrict to the signed dyadic block, and use (2). The arithmetic coefficient in that fact is exactly \(\mu(q)\mu(n)\), and its source support is exactly \((g,qn)=(q,n)=1\). This gives (5) without an absolute value and proves every retention assertion. Summing (5) over the projective boxes reconstructs the complete row. The conditional supplier implication follows from (3), the standard outer-row summation in the cited strict-top facts, and the triangle inequality only after each complete source box has been estimated. The final no-direct-Bettin--Chandee sentence is fact \(b67d5504c8454100\).

glossary.DOUBLE-MU-RECIP-N: The source-specific trilinear estimate after additive reciprocity, retaining both Mobius coefficients and using n as the reciprocal modulus.
glossary.delta_D: A proposed fixed positive saving exponent in DOUBLE-MU-RECIP-N.
glossary.mathcal C_flat: The literal Fourier coefficient after removal of the Archimedean reciprocity phase.

ed8954118b71276a.title: ACTUAL STRICT-TOP SOURCE GEOMETRY MAKES EVERY TINY SELECTED-p C1 ROW FOURIER-POWER-SMALL. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, and fix 0<eta_G<sigma. Work in either orientation of an actual strict-top source atom of fact 3f2f255ea6845a50, so beta_m<beta<6/5, B=Q^beta, G>=Q^(-sigma+eta_G), and H_P=Q^(beta-1)/G. In a literal C1 copy let p be its unique rough prime, so p>=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma). Assume that this same p is the prescribed first-nonresonant prime in the active exact pair mask and that the row lies in the tiny effective chamber 1<=m_eff<Q^(kappa/20). Then p/H_P>Q^(9/100) for all sufficiently large Q. Consequently, for every target E>0, the literal scalar marker-copy coefficient in this row is O_E(Q^(-E)). This includes m_eff=1. The result is scalar: it makes no rowwise-nonresonance assertion and does not by itself identify or estimate a larger upstream Hilbert/completion object
ed8954118b71276a.author: slava chan
ed8954118b71276a.statement: ACTUAL STRICT-TOP SOURCE GEOMETRY MAKES EVERY TINY SELECTED-p C1 ROW FOURIER-POWER-SMALL. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, and fix 0<eta_G<sigma. Work in either orientation of an actual strict-top source atom of fact 3f2f255ea6845a50, so beta_m<beta<6/5, B=Q^beta, G>=Q^(-sigma+eta_G), and H_P=Q^(beta-1)/G. In a literal C1 copy let p be its unique rough prime, so p>=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma). Assume that this same p is the prescribed first-nonresonant prime in the active exact pair mask and that the row lies in the tiny effective chamber 1<=m_eff<Q^(kappa/20). Then p/H_P>Q^(9/100) for all sufficiently large Q. Consequently, for every target E>0, the literal scalar marker-copy coefficient in this row is O_E(Q^(-E)). This includes m_eff=1. The result is scalar: it makes no rowwise-nonresonance assertion and does not by itself identify or estimate a larger upstream Hilbert/completion object.
ed8954118b71276a.proof:
In both orientations fact 3f2f255ea6845a50 defines H_P=H_T/G with H_T=B/Q=Q^(beta-1). Hence
H_P=Q^(beta-1)/G <= Q^(beta-1+sigma-eta_G).                    (1)
The literal C1 rough-prime cutoff from the same fact and fact f0f6807663d3ef3c is
p>=Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma).                                     (2)
Dividing (2) by (1) gives
p/H_P >= Q^(5/2-2beta-4sigma+eta_G).                          (3)
Since beta<6/5, the exponent on the right is strictly larger than
1/10-4sigma+eta_G.
The hypotheses kappa<=1/100 and sigma=kappa/100 give 4sigma<=1/2500. Therefore
1/10-4sigma+eta_G >= 1/10-1/2500=249/2500>9/100.              (4)
Equations (3)-(4) prove p/H_P>Q^(9/100).

All hypotheses of fact 555ec032e5c78720 now hold for the displayed tiny selected-p row. Apply its consequence with zeta=9/100 and with its target power B chosen equal to the present arbitrary E. It yields the scalar coefficient bound O_E(Q^(-E)). That fact explicitly retains the m_eff=1 case and uses the pair mask only to derive p not dividing mathscr A, not the false assertion p not dividing mathscr A h. The final scope statements follow.

glossary.eta_G: The fixed positive slack in the actual imbalance lower bound Q^(-sigma+eta_G)<=G.

edabb9a0d2959b41.title: CRIT-HALF-DYADIC-PROJECTIVE-LEDGER. Fix one orientation, exact active g,c, and one complete frozen selected critical source block of facts 328503a935cabe60 and 8d9feea8c44da2c8. Thus (ell,q)=1 on every active physical row, q is on the Q_c-scale, kappa is on the K_c-scale, n is on the B-scale, and
edabb9a0d2959b41.author: slava chan
edabb9a0d2959b41.statement:
CRIT-HALF-DYADIC-PROJECTIVE-LEDGER. Fix one orientation, exact active g,c, and one complete frozen selected critical source block of facts 328503a935cabe60 and 8d9feea8c44da2c8. Thus (ell,q)=1 on every active physical row, q is on the Q_c-scale, kappa is on the K_c-scale, n is on the B-scale, and
t=(ell-kappa n)/q.                                                (1)
Let A_lit(q,kappa,n;t) denote the complete literal smooth amplitude excluding mu(c)mu(q)mu(n) and exact arithmetic unit conditions. It retains every source, dyadic, fixed-U, high, parent, target-gcd, factorization, provenance and projective weight or mask of the complete sibling-recombined source, with its orientation-specific core from fact 8d9feea8c44da2c8. For every positive q,kappa define
E_{q,kappa}(n)
 =1_{q divides ell-kappa n}
  -phi(q)^(-1)1_{(kappa n,q)=1}.                                 (2)
The complete centered fixed-g,c block is
C_cent=mu(c)sum_{q,kappa}mu(q)sum_{n>=1,(n,c)=1}
 mu(n)A_lit(q,kappa,n;(ell-kappa n)/q)E_{q,kappa}(n),             (3)
with the original finite supports and all frozen labels retained.

Put R_kappa=rad(kappa), and let rho_{1/2} be as in fact bab73c9febc955ed. Then exactly
C_cent=mu(c)sum_{q,kappa}mu(q)
 sum_{h|R_kappa,(h,c)=1}mu(h)
 sum_{d,m>=1,(dm,cR_kappa)=1}rho_{1/2}(d)rho_{1/2}(m)
 A_lit(q,kappa,hdm;(ell-kappa hdm)/q)E_{q,kappa}(hdm).            (4)
There is no condition (d,m)=1 and no squarefree condition on d or m. In particular, the outer mu(q), the quotient t=(ell-kappa hdm)/q, the c-coprimality, every q-dependent weight, and every literal mask and frozen label remain present.

If (kappa,q)>1, the entire q,kappa row in (4) is zero. If (kappa,q)=1, then every h|R_kappa is coprime to q and (2) becomes
E_{q,kappa}(hdm)
 =1_{dm congruent ell*(kappa h)^(-1) (mod q)}
  -phi(q)^(-1)1_{(dm,q)=1}.                                     (5)
Thus (5), not a fixed residue independent of kappa and h, is the exact moving reduced progression.

Here is an exact smooth dyadic ledger. Choose a smooth function theta on the positive reals which equals 1 on (0,1] and 0 on [2,infinity), and put Psi(u)=theta(u)-theta(2u). For powers of two D and M put Psi_D(d)=Psi(d/D) and Psi_M(m)=Psi(m/M). Then
sum_D Psi_D(d)=sum_M Psi_M(m)=1                                 (6)
for every positive d,m. Inserting the product of these two partitions in (4) is exact and creates finitely many active cells.
