Before choosing a fundamental domain, interchange of d and m carries the (D,M)-cell exactly to the (M,D)-cell: all arithmetic conditions, E_{q,kappa}(hdm), the quotient (1), A_lit, and rho_{1/2}(d)rho_{1/2}(m) are invariant under this interchange. Consequently (4) also has the exact fundamental-domain form obtained by restricting to d<=m and multiplying by
omega_diag(d,m)=2 if d<m and omega_diag(d,d)=1.                  (7)

Assume a particular n-support block is contained in B<=n<2B, put X_h=B/h, and suppose X_h>1. On its h-row,
X_h<=dm<2X_h.                                                    (8)
After (7), the actual smaller factor d satisfies
d<sqrt(2X_h).                                                    (9)
For 0<eta<=1/4 the row is therefore the exact disjoint sum of the three regions
HC-SMALL: d<X_h^eta;
HC-MED: X_h^eta<=d<=X_h^(1/4+eta);
HC-HIGH: X_h^(1/4+eta)<d<sqrt(2X_h).                             (10)
The last endpoint is the genuine support endpoint. It must not be replaced by infinity or by an asserted both-large estimate. Each region may simultaneously retain the exact smooth cells (6).

A one-dimensional Mellin cost can be registered, but it is not a two-dimensional projective theorem. For fixed q,kappa,h and frozen labels, normalize the smooth product profile by
V_{q,kappa,h}(u)
 =A_lit(q,kappa,hX_h u;(ell-kappa hX_h u)/q)                     (11)
on its compact positive u-support, and define
Vhat_{q,kappa,h}(tau)=integral_0^infinity
 V_{q,kappa,h}(u)u^(i tau)du/u,
M_1(q,kappa,h)=integral_R |Vhat_{q,kappa,h}(tau)|d tau.           (12)
Whenever Mellin inversion is used, the actual quantity M_1(q,kappa,h), or a proved uniform aggregate of it, must be carried in the estimate. Fact 5772f2de626492b3 supplies one-variable supremum, variation and scaled-Lipschitz control; no two-dimensional q-versus-product projective norm follows from that fact or from (11)-(12). In particular, the q-dependence of Vhat, the moving quotient, and all q-dependent masks remain joint data.

Finally, a row at scale X_h is eligible for any proposed high-level shifted-convolution theorem requiring the three size conditions only if, for its theorem parameter delta>0,
Q_c<=X_h^(1/2+delta),  kappa h<=X_h^delta,
ell<=X_h^(1+delta).                                               (13)
These conditions must be checked for every retained h-row; the harmonic h-sum alone does not imply them. Equations (3)-(13) are an algebraic and norm ledger only. They assert no Siegel-Walfisz property for rho_{1/2}, no arithmetic-progression estimate, no projective norm bound, no payment of any region in (10), and no Goldbach conclusion.
edabb9a0d2959b41.proof:
Apply the c-coprime identity (2) of fact bab73c9febc955ed separately for each fixed q,kappa to the finitely supported function
F(n)=A_lit(q,kappa,n;(ell-kappa n)/q)E_{q,kappa}(n).
This gives exactly the h,d,m sums in (4). Multiplication by the unchanged outer factors mu(c)mu(q), followed by the original finite q,kappa and label sums, proves (4). The cited gcd-strip fact also proves that d,m need not be coprime or squarefree and that the exact c- and R_kappa-coprimality restrictions are those displayed.

Suppose a prime p divides (kappa,q). Since (ell,q)=1, p does not divide ell. For every n one has p|kappa n, so q cannot divide ell-kappa n; hence the first term of E_{q,kappa}(n) is zero. Also (kappa n,q)>1, so the second indicator is zero. Thus E_{q,kappa}(n)=0 identically, proving the zero-row assertion.

Now suppose (kappa,q)=1. Every prime divisor of h divides kappa, because h|R_kappa, so (h,q)=1. Therefore kappa h is invertible modulo q. The divisibility q|ell-kappa hdm is equivalent to
dm congruent ell*(kappa h)^(-1) modulo q.
Moreover (kappa hdm,q)=1 is equivalent to (dm,q)=1. This proves (5).

For the dyadic identity, theta(u)-theta(2u) vanishes unless 1/2<u<2, up to harmless boundary values. For fixed x>0 and integers J_1<J_2,
sum_{j=J_1}^{J_2}Psi(x/2^j)
 =theta(x/2^(J_2))-theta(x/2^(J_1-1)).
As J_2 tends to infinity the first term tends to 1, and as J_1 tends to minus infinity the second tends to 0. Only finitely many terms are nonzero, proving (6). Insertion in a finite source sum is therefore exact.

Every factor in the summand of (4), except the two separately displayed rho factors and dyadic cutoffs, depends on d,m only through their product dm. The product rho_{1/2}(d)rho_{1/2}(m) and the unit conditions are symmetric as well. Swapping d,m thus swaps D,M and changes nothing else. Pairing off-diagonal ordered pairs and retaining one diagonal copy proves (7).

On the stated support, B<=hdm<2B. Dividing by h proves (8). Under d<=m one has d^2<=dm<2X_h, which proves (9). The three inequalities in (10) partition the full interval 1<=d<sqrt(2X_h): the first two share no point because of their chosen strict and weak endpoints, and the second and third share none for the same reason. Hence (10) is exact.

The definitions (11)-(12) merely record the Mellin transform and its L1 cost for the one real product variable u. The complete amplitude is smooth and compactly supported in that variable by facts 328503a935cabe60 and 5772f2de626492b3, so each fixed-row transform is defined and Mellin inversion may be invoked only with its actual convergence cost. Nothing in this one-variable definition writes the family Vhat_{q,kappa,h}(tau) as a bounded projective sum of a q-function and a tau- or product-function. Therefore no two-dimensional norm follows. Conditions (13) are simply the explicit hypotheses that a prospective supplier must satisfy after the h-row length has become X_h; no identity above implies them.

glossary.A_lit: The complete frozen literal smooth critical amplitude after sibling recombination, excluding the displayed Mobius coefficients and exact arithmetic unit conditions.
glossary.C_cent: The complete centered fixed-g,c critical block.
glossary.E_{q,kappa}: The unit-compatible centered congruence bracket defined in equation (2).
glossary.M_1: The L1 norm of the one-dimensional Mellin transform of the fixed-row product profile.
glossary.Psi: The smooth dyadic partition function theta(u)-theta(2u).
glossary.omega_diag: The multiplicity two off the d=m diagonal and one on the diagonal in the d<=m fundamental domain.

edb218d77d83d52a.title: Let p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4 be distinct primes greater than 3, put P=p_1p_2p_3p_4, and use the centered interval-weighted companion definitions of fact be4e5ad5378f0122. There are explicit singleton intervals for the two distinct external units q=2 and q=3 such that the normalized two-column companion Gram Gamma satisfies
edb218d77d83d52a.author: slava chan
edb218d77d83d52a.statement:
Let p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4 be distinct primes greater than 3, put P=p_1p_2p_3p_4, and use the centered interval-weighted companion definitions of fact be4e5ad5378f0122. There are explicit singleton intervals for the two distinct external units q=2 and q=3 such that the normalized two-column companion Gram Gamma satisfies
||Gamma-I||_op=sqrt((phi(P)+1)/(2phi(P)))>1/sqrt(2).
Thus centered interval form by itself, without the literal arithmetic lower bounds and relations governing interval lengths and locations, does not imply an o(1) companion-flatness estimate. This is an exact singleton-window countermodel inside the unrestricted interval family of fact be4e5ad5378f0122; it is not a counterexample to an actual WF-RPS window family whose lengths and shifts obey additional scale-dependent constraints, and it is not an arithmetic PAVG27 counterexample.
edb218d77d83d52a.proof:
For a global residue X modulo P, let its i-th local residue be x_i=X modulo p_i and take the singleton local interval I_{i,q}={x_i}. Its centered indicator is
f_{i,q}(x)=1_{x=x_i}-1/p_i.
For a nonzero local frequency a its Fourier transform is e_{p_i}(-ax_i), while at a=0 it is zero. The CRT decomposition from fact be4e5ad5378f0122 therefore gives
M_q(h)=1_{gcd(h,P)=1}e_P(-hX).                                             (1)

Choose X_2=0 and X_3=2^{-1}-3^{-1} modulo P. Combining (1) with the definition of V_{P,q}, the q=2 column is
C_2(h)=1_{gcd(h,P)=1}e_P(-h 2^{-1}).
The q=3 column is
C_3(h)=1_{gcd(h,P)=1}
 [e_P(-h(X_3+3^{-1}))+e_P(-h(X_3+2 times 3^{-1}))]
=1_{gcd(h,P)=1}
 [e_P(-h2^{-1})+e_P(-h(2^{-1}+3^{-1}))].
Thus the first q=3 atom coincides exactly with the unique q=2 atom.

For squarefree P with four prime factors, the Ramanujan values satisfy
c_P(0)=phi(P)
and
c_P(y)=mu(P)=1 whenever y is a unit modulo P.
The difference 3^{-1} is a unit modulo P. Hence
E_2=sum_h|C_2(h)|^2=phi(P),
E_3=sum_h|C_3(h)|^2=2phi(P)+2,
and, in the standard Gram order,
sum_h overline(C_2(h))C_3(h)=phi(P)+1.
Indeed, the diagonal atom collision contributes c_P(0)=phi(P), and the remaining cross atom contributes c_P(-3^{-1})=1; the two off-diagonal terms in E_3 each contribute 1.

It follows that the modulus of the normalized off-diagonal Gram entry is
(phi(P)+1)/sqrt(phi(P)(2phi(P)+2))
=sqrt((phi(P)+1)/(2phi(P))).
For a two-by-two normalized Hermitian Gram with diagonal entries one, the operator norm of Gamma-I is the modulus of its off-diagonal entry. This proves the equality and the strict lower bound. The intervals used here have length one, so the conclusion is scoped exactly as stated.

glossary.X_2: global CRT shift chosen as zero for the q=2 singleton windows
glossary.X_3: global CRT shift 2^{-1}-3^{-1} chosen so one q=3 companion atom matches the q=2 atom
glossary.singleton-window countermodel: a companion family whose four local interval weights are centered indicators of one residue each

ee6886ba9ed393f1.title: EXACT NEGATIVE-FREQUENCY BRIDGE FROM THE NATURAL FORWARD C1 SOURCE TO THE PMD SLOPE GAUGE. Use the complete forward C1 coordinate and notation of fact 6eacfadbc9a83247. Thus n=vp, s=cq, L_0=cA, and the reduced positive source equation is
ee6886ba9ed393f1.author: slava chan
ee6886ba9ed393f1.statement:
EXACT NEGATIVE-FREQUENCY BRIDGE FROM THE NATURAL FORWARD C1 SOURCE TO THE PMD SLOPE GAUGE. Use the complete forward C1 coordinate and notation of fact 6eacfadbc9a83247. Thus n=vp, s=cq, L_0=cA, and the reduced positive source equation is
q m+n k_red=A.                                              (1)
For an original nonzero Poisson frequency h_prime, the normalized natural summand is
H_P^(-1)[-mu(c)mu(q)mu(v)(H_P/n)
 Fhat_{g,cq,n}(h_prime/n)]e_n(Ah_prime qbar),               (2)
times every inherited literal bookkeeping factor.

Reindex the complete negative-frequency half by
h_prime=-h.                                                 (3)
Then the same summand is exactly
H_P^(-1) a_h^PMD(q)
 e(Ah/(qn))e_n(-Ah qbar),                                  (4)
where
a_h^PMD(q)
 =-mu(c)mu(q)mu(v)(H_P/n)
   Fhat_{g,cq,n}(-h/n)e(-Ah/(qn))
   chi_nat(v,p,h,q),                                       (5)
and chi_nat is the correspondingly reindexed product of all inherited bookkeeping factors. Moreover
e(Ah/(qn))e_n(-Ah qbar)
 =e_q(Ah nbar)
 =e_q(h k_red).                                             (6)
Thus (4) is exactly the PMD restored-slope phase e(h k_red/q).

In the factor notation of fact 294ac3b02b065aec, the exact natural PMD-gauge identification on this reindexed half is therefore
eta_c=-mu(c), xi_v=mu(v), c_q=mu(q),                        (7)
U_PMD(q,h,v,p)
 =(H_P/(vp))Fhat_{g,cq,vp}(-h/(vp))
   e(-Ah/(qvp)),                                            (8)
with chi_ell=chi_nat and with the explicit factor
e(Ah/(qvp))e_{vp}(-Ah qbar)
left exactly as in that fact. The two Archimedean factors in (8) and in the explicit PMD phase cancel; neither may be discarded before the identity is formed.

This bridge corrects the positive-frequency orientation mismatch: the positive natural phase e_n(Ah qbar) is not the PMD slope phase, while the reindexed negative-frequency term (4) is. It is an exact coefficient identity only. Fact 7596cf19a80bf8f3 still prevents the complete hard-source positivity support from being inserted as a pointwise mask into a proper finite band merely from Fourier truncation. No window-energy estimate, Gadd^(-1) saving, PMD closure, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
ee6886ba9ed393f1.proof:
Substitute h_prime=-h into (2). This gives
H_P^(-1)[-mu(c)mu(q)mu(v)(H_P/n)
 Fhat_{g,cq,n}(-h/n)]e_n(-Ah qbar)chi_nat.
Multiply the bracketed coefficient by
1=e(-Ah/(qn))e(Ah/(qn))
and group e(-Ah/(qn)) with the coefficient. The coefficient becomes exactly (5), and the remaining phase becomes the first expression in (6). This proves (4)-(5).

For coprime q,n, additive reciprocity gives
nbar/q is congruent modulo one to 1/(qn)-qbar/n.
Multiplying by Ah and exponentiating yields
e_q(Ah nbar)=e(Ah/(qn))e_n(-Ah qbar),
which is the first equality in (6). Reducing (1) modulo q gives
n k_red congruent A modulo q.
Since gcd(n,q)=1, k_red is congruent to A nbar modulo q, so
e_q(Ah nbar)=e_q(hk_red),
proving the second equality.

Now set n=vp. Equations (5) and (7)-(8) show
eta_c xi_v c_q U_PMD chi_nat
=-mu(c)mu(v)mu(q)(H_P/n)
 Fhat_{g,cq,n}(-h/n)e(-Ah/(qn))chi_nat.
Multiplying this by the explicit factor
e(Ah/(qn))e_n(-Ah qbar)
in fact 294ac3b02b065aec cancels the two ordinary exponential factors and reproduces the reindexed natural term from (2). This proves the exact factor identification. The final support warning is precisely fact 7596cf19a80bf8f3.

glossary.U_PMD: The exact natural Fourier amplitude in the PMD gauge, including the compensating Archimedean phase.
glossary.a_h^PMD: The exact q-coefficient in the restored PMD slope gauge.
glossary.h_prime: The original natural Poisson frequency before the reindex h_prime=-h.

eeb2a1f90b2a4cb2.title: SQUAREFREE-ZERO HILBERT--KATAI ALTERNATIVE AND THE EXACT SELECTOR TRADEOFF. Let \(\mathcal H\) be a complex Hilbert space whose inner product is linear in the first variable. Let \(X\) be a positive integer and let \(V_n\in\mathcal H\) for \(1\le n\le X\), with
eeb2a1f90b2a4cb2.author: slava chan
eeb2a1f90b2a4cb2.proof:
The defining identity of the Möbius function gives
\[
 \mu(n)\mu(n)^2=\mu(n)
\]
for every positive integer \(n\). Multiplication by \(V_n\) and summation prove (4).

Write
\[
 S=\sum_{n\le X}\mu(n)W_n,\qquad
 A=\sum_{n\le X}\mu(n)W_n\Omega_{\mathcal P}(n).
\]
The triangle inequality and scalar Cauchy--Schwarz give
\[
 \|S-L_{\mathcal P}^{-1}A\|
 \le
 \frac{BX^{1/2}}{L_{\mathcal P}}
 \left(\sum_{n\le X}
  (\Omega_{\mathcal P}(n)-L_{\mathcal P})^2\right)^{1/2}, \tag{7}
\]
because \(\|W_n\|\le\|V_n\|\le B\).

Open the prime-divisor count:
\[
 A=\sum_{a\in\mathcal P}\sum_{m\le X/a}
   \mu(am)W_{am}. \tag{8}
\]
If \(a\nmid m\), then \(\mu(am)=-\mu(m)\). If \(a\mid m\), then \(am\) is not squarefree and (1) gives \(W_{am}=0\). Therefore the following identity holds for every \(m\), with no exceptional terms:
\[
 A=-\sum_{a\in\mathcal P}\sum_{m\le X/a}
   \mu(m)W_{am}. \tag{9}
\]
For \(m\le X/P_-\), put
\[
 Z_m=\sum_{\substack{a\in\mathcal P\\am\le X}}W_{am}.
\]
Then \(A=-\sum_{m\le X/P_-}\mu(m)Z_m\). Since
\(|\mu(m)|\le1\), Hilbert-space Cauchy--Schwarz yields
\[
 \|A\|^2\le
 \lfloor X/P_-\rfloor
 \sum_{m\le X/P_-}\|Z_m\|^2. \tag{10}
\]
Expanding the Gram matrix gives
\[
 \sum_m\|Z_m\|^2
 =\sum_{a,b\in\mathcal P}
  \sum_{m\le X/\max(a,b)}
  \langle W_{am},W_{bm}\rangle. \tag{11}
\]

For the diagonal \(a=b\), boundedness and
\(\mu(am)^2\le1\) give
\[
 \sum_{a\in\mathcal P}\sum_{m\le X/a}
 \|W_{am}\|^2
 \le B^2\sum_{a\in\mathcal P}\left\lfloor\frac Xa\right\rfloor
 \le B^2XL_{\mathcal P}. \tag{12}
\]
For distinct primes \(a,b\), the elementary squarefree identity
\[
 \mu(am)^2\mu(bm)^2
 =\mu(m)^2{\bf1}_{(ab,m)=1} \tag{13}
\]
holds: both sides are one exactly when \(m\) is squarefree and neither \(a\) nor \(b\) divides \(m\), and both sides vanish otherwise. By (1) and (13), the \((a,b)\) term of (11) is exactly \(\mathfrak C^{\rm sq}_{a,b}\). Pairing conjugate off-diagonal terms and applying the triangle inequality bounds their total by
\[
 \sum_{\substack{a,b\in\mathcal P\\a\ne b}}
 |\mathfrak C^{\rm sq}_{a,b}|. \tag{14}
\]
Combining (7), (10)--(14), and
\(\|S\|\le\|S-L_{\mathcal P}^{-1}A\|+
L_{\mathcal P}^{-1}\|A\|\) proves (5).

Finally,
\[
 \sum_{n\le X}\Omega_{\mathcal P}(n)
 =XL_{\mathcal P}+O(|\mathcal P|)
\]
and
\[
 \sum_{n\le X}\Omega_{\mathcal P}(n)^2
 =X\left(
 L_{\mathcal P}^2+
 \sum_{a\in\mathcal P}(1/a-1/a^2)\right)
 +O(|\mathcal P|^2).
\]
Substitution into the expansion of
\(\sum(\Omega_{\mathcal P}-L_{\mathcal P})^2\) proves (6). Equation (9) proves the claimed disappearance of the squareful-dilation error, while (13) proves the exact selector price.

glossary.W_n: The squarefree-zero auxiliary Hilbert vector mu(n)^2 V_n.
glossary.mathfrak C^{sq}_{a,b}: The selector-bearing two-dilate correlation produced by the squarefree-zero extension.

eed7c65b2f8b19a3.title: Under the hypotheses and notation of fact 3bb378b0a49679f9, the four possible exact gcd layers and their quotient-modulus primitive additive conductors are:
eed7c65b2f8b19a3.author: slava chan
eed7c65b2f8b19a3.proof:
Fact 3bb378b0a49679f9 proves b_z=p ell_p/g_z and proves that the possible primitive additive conductors are exactly the divisors e of b_z. Substitute the four possible values of g_z. For g_z=1, b_z=p ell_p, whose divisors are 1,p,ell_p,p ell_p because p and ell_p are distinct primes. For g_z=p, b_z=ell_p, whose divisors are 1,ell_p. For g_z=ell_p, b_z=p, whose divisors are 1,p. For g_z=p ell_p, b_z=1, whose sole divisor is 1. This proves the table.

On the last layer the normalized equation a_zm+b_zk=n_z becomes a_zm+k=n_z. Reduction modulo b_z=1 imposes no condition, and the exact additive detector in fact 3bb378b0a49679f9 is c_1=1. Hence that detector has no term of conductor greater than one.

Fact 4a9a213a428b7e8c assumes q_z>1 for every primitive-moment leaf, and fact f5b31dd3643732ac invokes that architecture conditionally for the forward component. Under the additional identification q_z=e stated explicitly in the present theorem, the maximal-gcd layer yields only e=1 and therefore cannot supply such a leaf. The three listed alternatives are exhaustive logical ways for a complete formula of this specified type to handle that layer: assign its contribution to the permitted real remainder, show the layer contributes nothing, or introduce and justify a different nontrivial modulus. The final scope sentence prevents this architecture-specific conclusion from being read as a universal no-go.

eeee52899369d087.title: Fix B>0 and a real number vartheta_AP with 1/2<vartheta_AP<1. As x tends to infinity put D_*=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B) and Q_lvl=x^(vartheta_AP). Let psi be a real cutoff with psi(u)=1 for u>=2, and let Phi be the nonnegative smooth dyadic partition constructed in fact 3ef233e014331fc3. Let D be the least positive power of two with D>=2D_*, and define lambda_D(d)=mu(d)psi(d/D_*)Phi(d/D) for positive integers d. Fix real numbers 1<alpha<beta<2, put c_Phi=min_{alpha<=t<=beta}Phi(t)>0, and fix real exponents gamma_1,gamma_2 satisfying
eeee52899369d087.author: slava chan
eeee52899369d087.statement:
Fix B>0 and a real number vartheta_AP with 1/2<vartheta_AP<1. As x tends to infinity put D_*=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B) and Q_lvl=x^(vartheta_AP). Let psi be a real cutoff with psi(u)=1 for u>=2, and let Phi be the nonnegative smooth dyadic partition constructed in fact 3ef233e014331fc3. Let D be the least positive power of two with D>=2D_*, and define lambda_D(d)=mu(d)psi(d/D_*)Phi(d/D) for positive integers d. Fix real numbers 1<alpha<beta<2, put c_Phi=min_{alpha<=t<=beta}Phi(t)>0, and fix real exponents gamma_1,gamma_2 satisfying
max(1/2,2 vartheta_AP/3)<gamma_1<gamma_2<1.
For each x let V_x be an arbitrary finite complex linear combination of sequences which are triply well-factorable of level Q_lvl in the sense reproduced in fact 3bcd070f8558ce6f. Put
c_1=c_Phi(beta-alpha)log(gamma_2/gamma_1)/10,
c_2=c_Phi^2(beta-alpha)log(gamma_2/gamma_1)/10.
Then c_1,c_2 are positive and, uniformly over V_x, for every sufficiently large x,

sum_{D<d<2D}|lambda_D(d)-V_x(d)| >= c_1 D,

sum_{D<d<2D}|lambda_D(d)-V_x(d)|^2 >= c_2 D.

Consequently the raw high-divisor weight cannot be approximated by finite same-level triply well-factorable combinations with l1 error o(D), nor with l2 error o(D^(1/2)), on its own dyadic support. This is a coefficient-norm obstruction only: it does not rule out cancellation-based transforms, changed moduli or levels, a different coefficient class, or approximation in a weaker problem-specific seminorm.
eeee52899369d087.proof:
Let
P_sq=sum_{q prime}1/q^2.
This convergent sum is strictly less than 1/2. Indeed,
P_sq<=1/4+sum_{k>=1}1/(2k+1)^2,
and (2k+1)^2>4k(k+1), so
sum_{k>=1}1/(2k+1)^2<1/4 sum_{k>=1}(1/k-1/(k+1))=1/4.

For every prime p satisfying D^(gamma_1)<p<=D^(gamma_2), consider the real interval
I_p=[alpha D/p,beta D/p].
Its length is L_p=(beta-alpha)D/p, and its upper endpoint is U_p=beta D/p. The number of non-squarefree positive integers in I_p is at most
sum_{q prime, q<=sqrt(U_p)}(L_p/q^2+1)
<=P_sq L_p+sqrt(U_p).
The harmless endpoint rounding changes this by O(1). Uniformly over the displayed p-range, L_p is bounded below by (beta-alpha)D^(1-gamma_2), which tends to infinity, and sqrt(U_p)/L_p is O(D^(-(1-gamma_2)/2)). Since P_sq<1/2, it follows that, for every sufficiently large x and every such p, I_p contains at least L_p/3 squarefree integers s.

Because gamma_1>1/2, for sufficiently large D every such pair satisfies
p>D^(gamma_1)>beta D^(1-gamma_1)>=s.
Thus p does not divide the squarefree integer s, the product n=ps is squarefree, and p>sqrt(n). In particular the map (p,s) to n is injective: an integer cannot have two distinct prime factors both greater than its square root.

Also gamma_1>2 vartheta_AP/3. Since log D=(1/2)log x-B log log x+O(1), one has
log(D^(gamma_1)/Q_lvl^(1/3))=(gamma_1/2-vartheta_AP/3)log x-gamma_1 B log log x+O(1),
which tends to infinity. Hence p>Q_lvl^(1/3) for all sufficiently large x.

We claim that every triply well-factorable sequence nu of level Q_lvl vanishes at each constructed n=ps. Use the balanced factorization in the definition reproduced in fact 3bcd070f8558ce6f. Every term representing n has n=q_1q_2q_3 with q_i<=Q_lvl^(1/3). Since the prime p divides q_1q_2q_3, it divides at least one q_i. That factor then satisfies q_i>=p>Q_lvl^(1/3), a contradiction. Thus nu(n)=0. It follows that V_x(n)=0 for every constructed n, uniformly in the number and coefficients of the finite combination.

It remains to count the constructed integers. The Prime Number Theorem in Subham De, arXiv:2308.16303, Theorem 2.2.1, states pi(y)~y/log y. Partial summation therefore gives
sum_{D^(gamma_1)<p<=D^(gamma_2)}1/p -> log(gamma_2/gamma_1).
For completeness, with Y=D^(gamma_1) and Z=D^(gamma_2), partial summation writes the prime reciprocal sum as
pi(Z)/Z-pi(Y)/Y+integral_Y^Z pi(t)/t^2 dt.
The two boundary terms tend to zero. The PNT is uniform on t>=Y once Y tends to infinity, so the integral equals
[1+o(1)] integral_Y^Z dt/(t log t)=[1+o(1)]log(gamma_2/gamma_1).
Consequently, for all sufficiently large x, the number of distinct constructed squarefree n is at least
sum_{D^(gamma_1)<p<=D^(gamma_2)}L_p/3
=(beta-alpha)D/3 sum_{D^(gamma_1)<p<=D^(gamma_2)}1/p
>=(beta-alpha)log(gamma_2/gamma_1)D/4.

Every constructed n lies in [alpha D,beta D], hence strictly between D and 2D. Also n>=alpha D>=2D_*, so psi(n/D_*)=1. Since n is squarefree, |mu(n)|=1, and since n/D lies in [alpha,beta],
|lambda_D(n)|=Phi(n/D)>=c_Phi.
Because V_x(n)=0, restricting the two sums in the statement to the constructed n gives lower bounds
c_Phi(beta-alpha)log(gamma_2/gamma_1)D/4
and
c_Phi^2(beta-alpha)log(gamma_2/gamma_1)D/4,
respectively. These are stronger than the asserted constants c_1 and c_2. The two non-approximation consequences and the final scope sentence follow.

glossary.P_sq: the convergent sum of reciprocal squares of primes
glossary.c_1: the explicit positive l1 separation constant in the statement
glossary.c_2: the explicit positive squared-l2 separation constant in the statement
glossary.gamma_1: the lower fixed exponent for the distinguished large prime p
glossary.gamma_2: the upper fixed exponent for the distinguished large prime p

ef06a895e7e793a6.title: ABSOLUTE SCHUR COST FOR EVERY LITERAL PRE-6/5 C4 ROUGH COPRIMALITY GATE. Assume the literal top-sliver parameters of fact e58fc7c00f1683e6:
ef06a895e7e793a6.author: slava chan
ef06a895e7e793a6.statement:
ABSOLUTE SCHUR COST FOR EVERY LITERAL PRE-6/5 C4 ROUGH COPRIMALITY GATE. Assume the literal top-sliver parameters of fact e58fc7c00f1683e6:
beta_m<=beta<6/5,  sigma<=10^{-4},  Z=Q^{3/2-beta-3sigma}.             (1)
Let q be a positive integer with Q<=q<2Q. Then q is divisible by at most three distinct primes p>=Z.                                           (2)
Consequently, let Lambdacal be any finite family of literal C4 rows, and for each lambda let m_lambda be any squarefree divisor of the four-rough-prime product in that row. For every complex row-output matrix A=(A(lambda,q)) supported on Q<=q<2Q,
|| (1_{gcd(q,m_lambda)=1} A(lambda,q)) ||_{op}
<=2^{7/2}||A||_{op}.                                                (3)
The operator norm is from l2 of the supported q-values to l2(Lambdacal). The bound is uniform in the number of rows and the union of their rough primes. It applies separately after any fixed projective, face, orientation, target and provenance restriction. It does not prove that the full literal PFACE-VEC/XR synthesis is one such matrix before sibling recombination, does not handle the varying small-v gate, the shared-prime exceptional aggregate, the primitive common-z estimate, another anatomy, C4, or Goldbach.
ef06a895e7e793a6.proof:
Suppose that four distinct primes p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4 at least Z divide q. Their product divides q, so
q>=p_1p_2p_3p_4>=Z^4
=Q^{6-4beta-12sigma}.                                              (4)
Since beta<6/5 and sigma<=10^{-4},
6-4beta-12sigma>6-24/5-12/10000
=6/5-12/10000>1.                                                   (5)
Thus Z^4/(2Q) tends to infinity with Q. For all sufficiently large Q, (4) contradicts q<2Q. This proves (2).

Fact 9bee61f3627bd506 states that every literal C4 row has exactly four distinct rough primes in its marked rough product. Hence each m_lambda has at most four prime divisors. Take Pcal in fact 10fd259d904acea7 to be the finite union of all rough primes occurring in the chosen rows. For each q, its subset T_q of primes from Pcal has cardinality at most three by (2). The Schur-multiplier theorem 10fd259d904acea7 therefore applies with J=4 and K=3, giving the factor
2^{(J+K)/2}=2^{7/2}.                                                (6)
This proves (3). Fixed row or output restrictions only delete rows or columns before the same Schur multiplication and do not alter J or K. The excluded structures are not used in this argument, proving the scope assertions.

ef131ab87c99303c.title: VARYING-HEIGHT TRUE-INCIDENCE PULLBACK AND THE SINGLE-OUTPUT PRIMITIVE C4 SATURATION CRITERION. Let r>1 be odd and squarefree. Let c and j_0 be units modulo r. Let Zcal be a finite nonempty set. For every rho in Zcal let h_rho and n_rho be integers such that r divides n_rho and gcd(h_rho(n_rho/r),r)=1, and let alpha_rho be a complex number. Put
ef131ab87c99303c.author: slava chan
ef131ab87c99303c.statement:
VARYING-HEIGHT TRUE-INCIDENCE PULLBACK AND THE SINGLE-OUTPUT PRIMITIVE C4 SATURATION CRITERION. Let r>1 be odd and squarefree. Let c and j_0 be units modulo r. Let Zcal be a finite nonempty set. For every rho in Zcal let h_rho and n_rho be integers such that r divides n_rho and gcd(h_rho(n_rho/r),r)=1, and let alpha_rho be a complex number. Put
x_{r,rho}=h_rho(n_rho/r)^{-1} modulo r,                             (1)
(I_r^{var}z)(x)=sum_{rho in Zcal:x_{r,rho}=x}alpha_rho z_rho.       (2)
Let P_{r,r} be the primitive-conductor projector of fact b4934b4981fc5817, put
C=cj_0^{-1} modulo r,  u_C(x)=e_r(-Cx),                             (3)
and let A_{r,c} be the primitive common-output synthesis of fact 9d1a11eb8a597a64. Then
A_{r,c}(I_r^{var}z;j_0,1)
=sum_{x in G_r}(P_{r,r}I_r^{var}z)(x)e_r(Cx)
=<z,(I_r^{var})^*P_{r,r}u_C>.                                      (4)
Consequently
sup_{||z||_2=1}|A_{r,c}(I_r^{var}z;j_0,1)|^2
=||(I_r^{var})^*P_{r,r}u_C||_2^2
=sum_{rho in Zcal}|alpha_rho|^2|(P_{r,r}u_C)(x_{r,rho})|^2
=sum_{x in G_r}M_r(x)|(P_{r,r}u_C)(x)|^2,                           (5)
where
M_r(x)=sum_{rho in Zcal:x_{r,rho}=x}|alpha_rho|^2.                  (6)
In particular,
sup_{||z||_2=1}|A_{r,c}(I_r^{var}z;j_0,1)|^2
<=||M_r||_infinity phi^*(r)r/phi(r).                               (7)
Thus repeated rational rays affect the single-output primitive norm only through M_r: rows on an already present ray repeat one sampled value of the primitive additive phase and do not create a new residue coordinate. The abstract scale of fact 731aecc74ff42615 is realized by this incidence if and only if the weighted sampling expression in (5) has that scale; multiplicity alone does not establish this.

The literal small-v coefficient is a contractive Hilbert slot before recombination. Namely, for each rho let v_rho be a positive integer coprime to r and let C_rho be an integer. Let kappa_{v_rho,C_rho}(s) be defined by fact 4d4bc6711163794c. If rho is expanded into labels (rho,s), with the same incidence coordinate x_{r,rho} and coefficient alpha_rho kappa_{v_rho,C_rho}(s), its expanded fibre mass is
M_r^{small-v}(x)
=sum_{rho:x_{r,rho}=x}|alpha_rho|^2
 sum_{s modulo v_rho}|kappa_{v_rho,C_rho}(s)|^2
=sum_{rho:x_{r,rho}=x}|alpha_rho|^2 phi(v_rho)/v_rho
<=M_r(x).                                                          (8)
The phases e_{v_rho}(sj_0) are retained in the signed synthesis, not summed in absolute value.

Under the literal nonresonant C4 hypotheses of fact 3330e83b6d253b69, equation (1) is the correct varying-height rough-face incidence because
product_{p|r}e_p(Ah_rho(n_rho/p)^{-1}q^{-1})
=e_r(Ax_{r,rho}q^{-1})                                             (9)
for every unit q, where A is the common signed reduced target. At a fixed source-balanced projective atom and common output, alpha_rho in (2) may therefore retain the atom's scalar n_rho,h_rho factors, every row-dependent literal mask at that output, the inactive coefficient mu(a_{rho,r})/a_{rho,r}, and one small-v Hilbert coefficient from (8). The h_rho inside (9) is retained in x_{r,rho}, not absorbed into alpha_rho. Proper-conductor, nonunit-completion and shared-prime sectors remain governed respectively by facts b4934b4981fc5817, 67ebf7acc95b59b6 and 31b158a7a3ce80d3. No multi-output, varying-r, complete-face-sibling, shared-prime aggregate, C4, or Goldbach estimate is asserted.
ef131ab87c99303c.proof:
Since r is squarefree, CRT gives
e_r(Y)=product_{p|r}e_p(Y(r/p)^{-1}).                               (10)
For p dividing r, definition (1) gives
x_{r,rho}(r/p)^{-1}
=h_rho(n_rho/r)^{-1}(r/p)^{-1}
=h_rho(n_rho/p)^{-1} modulo p.                                     (11)
Apply (10) with Y=Ax_{r,rho}q^{-1}. This proves (9), including the row-dependent height in the residue coordinate.

With the normalized multiplicative transform of fact 18a0de57eaf35171, Fourier inversion on G_r gives
P_{r,r}f(x)=sum_{eta primitive modulo r} fhat(eta)eta(x).           (12)
Therefore
sum_x(P_{r,r}f)(x)e_r(Cx)
=sum_{eta primitive}fhat(eta)overline{eta(C)}tau_r(eta).            (13)
In A_{r,c}(f;j_0,1), as defined in fact 9d1a11eb8a597a64, reindex chi=overline eta. The character evaluations satisfy
chi(-c)chi(-j_0^{-1})=chi(cj_0^{-1})=overline{eta(C)}.              (14)
Thus its defining sum is the right side of (13). Taking f=I_r^{var}z proves the first equality of (4).

Use the finite l2 inner product linear in the first variable. By (3), the first sum in (4) is <P_{r,r}I_r^{var}z,u_C>. The orthogonal projector P_{r,r} is self-adjoint. Moving P_{r,r} and I_r^{var} to the second slot proves the second equality in (4).

From (2),
((I_r^{var})^*y)_rho=overline{alpha_rho}y(x_{r,rho}).               (15)
Apply (15) to y=P_{r,r}u_C and square its l2 norm. This gives the first two sums in (5), and grouping equal x_{r,rho} gives the last sum and (6). Since Zcal is nonempty, its l2 unit sphere is nonempty. The norm of z mapsto <z,w> is ||w||_2, proving the supremum identity. Since M_r(x)<=||M_r||_infinity, (5) is at most ||M_r||_infinity||P_{r,r}u_C||_2^2. Fact 731aecc74ff42615 gives
||P_{r,r}u_C||_2^2=phi^*(r)r/phi(r),                               (16)
because C is a unit. This proves (7). Equations (5)-(6) prove the statement about repeated rays and the exact if-and-only-if sampling criterion.

Fact 4d4bc6711163794c proves, without requiring C_rho to be a unit modulo v_rho,
sum_{s modulo v_rho}|kappa_{v_rho,C_rho}(s)|^2
=phi(v_rho)/v_rho<=1.                                              (17)
The expanded labels are orthogonal coefficient coordinates, so their fibre mass is the sum of |alpha_rho kappa(s)|^2. Sum (17) over rho with x_{r,rho}=x to obtain (8). Multiplication by e_{v_rho}(sj_0) preserves every squared coefficient norm. Fourier inversion in the same predecessor proves that the signed s-sum reconstructs the exact zero-extended small-v inverse phase.

Finally, fact 3330e83b6d253b69 supplies the literal hypotheses r|n_rho, gcd(h_rho(n_rho/r),r)=1, the inactive coefficient, and the retained masks; fact fafe50a7d45923d2 supplies scalar row factors for each fixed projective atom. Identity (9) proves that the non-scalar h_rho dependence is exactly the coordinate (1). Hence the remaining displayed literal quantities are scalar row coefficients and can be retained in alpha_rho. The final sector references only retain their already verified exact ledgers and are excluded from the asserted estimate. This proves every identity and scope assertion.

glossary.I_r^{var}: the varying-height true rough-face incidence map
glossary.M_r: the weighted multiplicity of literal rows on one varying-height incidence coordinate modulo r
glossary.M_r^{small-v}: the expanded fibre mass after retaining the small-v Fourier coefficient as a Hilbert slot
glossary.u_C: the additive phase vector x mapsto e_r(-Cx) on G_r
glossary.x_{r,rho}: the varying-height literal incidence coordinate h_rho(n_rho/r)^{-1} modulo r

ef32ac12080ad96a.title: Let N>=3 and m>=2 be integers, let x>0 be real, and let W be a bounded complex function on the positive reals. Define the fixed-m reflected prime core
ef32ac12080ad96a.author: slava chan
ef32ac12080ad96a.statement:
Let N>=3 and m>=2 be integers, let x>0 be real, and let W be a bounded complex function on the positive reals. Define the fixed-m reflected prime core
R_{m,N}(W)=sum_{p prime, p<N, p congruent N modulo m}log(p)mu((N-p)/m)W(p/x).
Then the change of variables d=(N-p)/m is a bijection and gives the exact d-form
R_{m,N}(W)=sum_{1<=d< N/m, N-md prime}mu(d)log(N-md)W((N-md)/x).

Define the reflected von-Mangoldt core by either of the equal expressions
R_Lambda_{m,N}(W)=sum_{1<=d<N/m}mu(d)Lambda(N-md)W((N-md)/x)
=sum_{1<=q<N, q congruent N modulo m}Lambda(q)mu((N-q)/m)W(q/x).
Then
R_Lambda_{m,N}(W)=R_{m,N}(W)+E_pp,
where E_pp is exactly the same q-sum restricted to higher prime powers q=r^j with r prime and j>=2. For every epsilon>0,
|E_pp|<<_epsilon ||W||_infinity N^(1/2+epsilon),
uniformly in m,N,x and W.

Finally, if gcd(m,N)>1, every prime p occurring in R_{m,N}(W) satisfies p|m and p<=m. Consequently the large-prime slice obtained by additionally imposing p>m is empty. In particular, if W is supported on arguments t for which tx>m, then R_{m,N}(W)=0 whenever gcd(m,N)>1.
ef32ac12080ad96a.proof:
If p<N is prime and p is congruent to N modulo m, then N-p is a positive multiple of m, so d=(N-p)/m is a positive integer with d<N/m and p=N-md. Conversely, if 1<=d<N/m and N-md is prime, then p=N-md is positive, is less than N, and is congruent to N modulo m. These maps are inverse, and substitution gives the displayed exact d-form.

The substitution q=N-md is the same bijection between positive integers d<N/m and positive integers q<N satisfying q congruent to N modulo m. Applying it to the von-Mangoldt-weighted d-sum proves the two exact formulas for R_Lambda_{m,N}(W).

By the definition of the von Mangoldt function, Lambda(q) is zero unless q=r^j is a prime power, and Lambda(r^j)=log r. Its j=1 terms are exactly the prime terms of R_{m,N}(W). Therefore the difference E_pp is exactly the restriction to j>=2.

For each j>=2 there are at most N^(1/j) possible prime bases r with r^j<N. Also j<=log_2 N. Hence the number of possible higher prime powers is at most
sum_{2<=j<=log_2 N}N^(1/j)
<=N^(1/2)+(log_2 N)N^(1/3)
<<_epsilon N^(1/2+epsilon).
Every summand has |mu((N-q)/m)|<=1, |W(q/x)|<=||W||_infinity, and Lambda(q)<=log N. Absorbing this logarithm into N^epsilon after replacing epsilon by epsilon/2 proves the asserted error bound, uniformly in m and x.

Let g=gcd(m,N)>1 and suppose p is a prime with p congruent to N modulo m. Since g divides m and N, the divisibility m|(p-N) implies g|p. A divisor greater than one of the prime p must equal p, so g=p. In particular p divides m and p<=m. Thus no such prime satisfies p>m, proving the local gate. If W is supported where p/x>m/x, equivalently p>m, every potential summand is zero, which proves the final consequence.

glossary.R_{m,N}(W): the fixed-m prime core defined in the statement

ef53db9a50c698b0.title: Assume the hypotheses and notation of fact aa34b1862b993377, including the real dyadic partition function Phi, the controlled set of dyadic labels 𝒞, the complete source H_N, the controlled aggregate C_N, the nonterminal aggregate U_{T,N}, and the terminal aggregate T_N. For positive integers d,m,r,k define the controlled dyadic mask
ef53db9a50c698b0.author: slava chan
ef53db9a50c698b0.statement:
Assume the hypotheses and notation of fact aa34b1862b993377, including the real dyadic partition function Phi, the controlled set of dyadic labels 𝒞, the complete source H_N, the controlled aggregate C_N, the nonterminal aggregate U_{T,N}, and the terminal aggregate T_N. For positive integers d,m,r,k define the controlled dyadic mask
Xi_C(d,m,r,k)=sum_{(D,M,R,K) in 𝒞} Phi(d/D)Phi(m/M)Phi(r/R)Phi(k/K).
Then the original unmasked aggregates admit the exact integer-tuple formulas
C_N+U_{T,N}
=sum_{d,m,r,k>=1; dm+rk=N} mu(d)mu(r)log(m)log(k)W(dm/x)psi(d/D_*)
 times [1_{r<k^2}+1_{r>=k^2}Xi_C(d,m,r,k)],
and
T_N
=sum_{d,m,r,k>=1; dm+rk=N} mu(d)mu(r)log(m)log(k)W(dm/x)psi(d/D_*)
 times 1_{r>=k^2}[1-Xi_C(d,m,r,k)].
Also
C_N
=sum_{d,m,r,k>=1; dm+rk=N} mu(d)mu(r)log(m)log(k)W(dm/x)psi(d/D_*)Xi_C(d,m,r,k),
while H_N is the same sum with mask 1.

Thus the complement C_N+U_{T,N} consists of the completely label-free actual-integer truncation r<k^2, plus controlled-label leakage only on r>=k^2. The identities remain valid after multiplying the integer-tuple weight by any auxiliary coefficient depending on N,d,m,r,k but independent of the dyadic labels. They need not remain compressed in this form for a label-dependent auxiliary coefficient. Moreover Phi is only assumed real, so Xi_C need not lie between zero and one; the formulas are signed partition identities and do not furnish a pointwise majorant or positivity statement.
ef53db9a50c698b0.proof:
For a positive integer tuple (d,m,r,k), write
P_{D,M,R,K}=Phi(d/D)Phi(m/M)Phi(r/R)Phi(k/K).
The one-variable dyadic partition identity for Phi gives
sum_{D,M,R,K}P_{D,M,R,K}=1,
where all four sums range over positive dyadic labels. The sums are finite because Phi is supported in [1/2,2]. By definition, the sum of P_{D,M,R,K} over labels in 𝒞 is Xi_C(d,m,r,k), and therefore its sum over labels outside 𝒞 is 1-Xi_C(d,m,r,k).

Now fix an integer tuple satisfying dm+rk=N and factor from every labelled incidence its label-independent base weight
mu(d)mu(r)log(m)log(k)W(dm/x)psi(d/D_*).
The controlled aggregate C_N takes all labels in 𝒞, so its total dyadic coefficient at this tuple is Xi_C. This proves the displayed formula for C_N. Summing all dyadic labels gives coefficient one and proves the displayed formula for H_N.

By fact aa34b1862b993377, after C-precedence the union of the low, diagonal, and middle cells is exactly the actual-integer condition r<k^2, and the endpoint plus supercritical terminal union is exactly r>=k^2. Hence U_{T,N} has tuple coefficient
1_{r<k^2}[1-Xi_C],
whereas T_N has tuple coefficient
1_{r>=k^2}[1-Xi_C].
Adding the controlled coefficient Xi_C to the first of these gives
Xi_C+1_{r<k^2}(1-Xi_C)
=1_{r<k^2}+1_{r>=k^2}Xi_C,
because exactly one of r<k^2 and r>=k^2 holds. This proves both principal formulas.

If an auxiliary coefficient depends only on N,d,m,r,k, it factors out before the dyadic-label summation, so the proof is unchanged. A label-dependent coefficient cannot in general be factored out, which proves the stated scope limitation. Finally, neither the assumptions on Phi nor partition of unity assert Phi>=0. Therefore the partial sum Xi_C is not necessarily in [0,1], and no positivity or majorization follows from the identities.

glossary.Xi_C: the real-valued controlled dyadic mask obtained by summing the fourfold Phi partition weight over labels in 𝒞

efb6934a518932be.title: Fix positive constants c_0,C_0,c_1,C_1, a real number κ with 0<κ<1/100, and a bounded scaled-smooth family 𝔉 of functions of four positive variables: every member is supported where all four variables lie in [1/2,2], and for every derivative order the corresponding scaled derivatives are uniformly bounded over 𝔉. There exist positive constants η=η(κ,𝔉) and δ=δ(κ,𝔉) such that the following holds. Let x be sufficiently large, let c_0x≤N≤C_0x be an integer, let 𝒲∈𝔉, and let D,M,R,K satisfy
efb6934a518932be.author: slava chan
efb6934a518932be.statement:
Fix positive constants c_0,C_0,c_1,C_1, a real number κ with 0<κ<1/100, and a bounded scaled-smooth family 𝔉 of functions of four positive variables: every member is supported where all four variables lie in [1/2,2], and for every derivative order the corresponding scaled derivatives are uniformly bounded over 𝔉. There exist positive constants η=η(κ,𝔉) and δ=δ(κ,𝔉) such that the following holds. Let x be sufficiently large, let c_0x≤N≤C_0x be an integer, let 𝒲∈𝔉, and let D,M,R,K satisfy
c_1x≤DM,RK≤C_1x,                                             (1)
x^(1/2-η)≤D,M≤x^(1/2+η),                                    (2)
x^(1/2+κ)≤R≤x^(9/16-κ).                                     (3)
Define
𝒬_N(D,M;R,K)
=Σ_{dm+rk=N}μ(d)μ(r)log(m)log(k)
 𝒲(d/D,m/M,r/R,k/K),                                        (4)
and use the Poisson decomposition
𝒬_N=𝒬_N^(0)+𝒬_N^(≠0)
of fact df9748efe29ab475. Then
|𝒬_N^(≠0)(D,M;R,K)|≪_{κ,𝔉,c_i,C_i}x^(1-δ).                 (5)

Consequently, in the hybrid decomposition of fact 1e2d635f6691e832, the total nonzero-frequency contribution of all residual labels satisfying (2)-(3) is O(x^(1-δ/2)) and hence o(x/log x). This removes the buffered balanced band through R=x^(9/16-κ). It asserts no estimate for residual labels with R>x^(9/16-κ), for unbalanced D or M, or for terminal-anatomy masks not present in (4).
efb6934a518932be.proof:
Choose η>0 sufficiently small in terms of κ and the fixed uniform derivative bounds defining 𝔉, and put ζ=η/100. Define
H=R/M,   L_s=Hx^(4η),   Z_s=x^(3/4-4η)/R.                   (6)
Then H≥x^(κ-η), and, after taking η<κ/10,
L_s²<Z_s,   Z_s³>2R.                                        (7)
The second inequality follows from ρ<9/16-3η, where ρ=log R/log x; the first has a fixed additional margin.

We first make the smooth-separation cost explicit. In the Poisson formula of fact df9748efe29ab475, scale every positive variable by its dyadic length and then use logarithmic coordinates on a fixed compact box. The joint amplitude, after multiplying by the ordinary reciprocity phase introduced below, belongs to a bounded smooth family: the only phase parameter is N/(DM), which lies in a fixed compact interval by (1). Extend each such compactly supported log-coordinate function smoothly to a fixed torus. Repeated integration by parts shows that its Fourier coefficients c_n satisfy
|c_n|≤C_J(1+|n|)^(-J)
uniformly over 𝔉, for every fixed J. Taking J larger than the number of variables plus two gives
Σ_n|c_n|≪_𝔉1.                                                (8)
Each Fourier mode is a product of one-variable coefficients. The factors log m and log k add only O((log x)²). After a factorization r=uy or r=vp, the product cutoffs are still smooth functions of the logarithms of the scaled factors and have the same uniformly summable expansion. Thus all smooth separation below costs O_𝔉((log x)^C), not x^(Cη). Repeated integration by parts in the Poisson transform, exactly as in df9748efe29ab475, restricts the relevant frequencies to
0<|h|≤H_gx^ζ                                                  (9)
with an error O_A(x^(-A)) after summing all variables.

Put g=gcd(d,r), d=ga, r=gb, and N=gN_g. On nonzero Möbius support, g,a,b are pairwise coprime and squarefree,
μ(d)μ(r)=μ(a)μ(b),                                           (10)
and
am+bk=N_g.                                                    (11)
The natural frequency length is H_g=R/(gM)=H/g and the Poisson prefactor is H_g^(-1). For fixed g, fixing (b,k) leaves at most x^ε factorizations of am=N_g-bk, so the original fixed-g block is O(x^(1+ε)/g). The zero-frequency integral has the same support-volume bound. Therefore
Σ_{g|N,g≥x^η}|𝒬_g^(≠0)|≪x^(1-η+2ε).                         (12)
Likewise the layers g>H contribute O(x^(1+ε)/H)=O(x^(1-κ+2η+ε)). We may hence assume
g<x^η,  g≤H,  H_g≥1.                                        (13)

Now b is squarefree, has scale B_0=R/g, and satisfies b>L_s. Fact 85e63a9328d91711, using (7), partitions every b exactly into four classes: an (L_s,Z_s)-prime marker; a stopping-composite marker L_s<y≤L_s²; b=vp with v≤L_s and p≥Z_s prime; or b=vpq with v≤L_s and distinct primes Z_s≤p<q. The interval-prime and stopping coefficients are separated by facts 85e63a9328d91711 and 9ba4d2d84f0b37d6. In the endpoint classes the prime factors of v are at most L_s, while the rough primes are at least Z_s. Dyadic subdivision and the stopping index cost x^ε.

Additive reciprocity gives
e_b(N_gh a^(-1))
=e_a(-N_gh b^(-1))e(N_gh/(ab)).                             (14)
The last phase is included in (8), since
N_gH_g/[(D/g)(R/g)]≍N/(DM)≍1.                              (15)

For a marker class put s=gcd(N_g,a), a=sq. If s>x^η, equation (11) forces s|k; writing k=sℓ and counting (b,ℓ) gives O(x^(1+ε)/(gs)), so these layers total O(x^(1-η+2ε)). If s≤x^η, reduce (14) to modulus q and apply fact 4a101b703d4499f6 with
U=B_0/Y, marker length Y, and frequency length H_gx^ζ.
The inequalities
U≤q,  H_gx^ζ≤Y,  4H_gx^ζY<q                               (16)
follow from Y≥L_s, Y≤Z_s, ζ<η, and (1)-(3). Summing the fixed-q bound over q of length D/(gs), multiplying by H_g^(-1), and using (8) gives
≪x^ε[
 DM(H/Y)^(1/2)x^(ζ/2)g^(-3/2)s^(-1)
 +D^(5/4)(RY)^(1/2)x^ζg^(-7/4)s^(-5/4)].                    (17)
The gcd powers are summable. Since Y≥L_s, the first term is
≪x^(1-2η+ζ/2+ε).
Since Y≤Z_s and D≤x^(1/2+η), the second is
≪x^(1-3η/4+ζ+ε).
With ζ=η/100 and ε<η/100, both retain a fixed positive multiple of η as a saving. This repairs the marker margin without any x^(Cη) separation loss.

For b=vp, freeze h, put c=gcd(N_gh,a), and write a=cq. Let V and P be the dyadic v- and p-lengths, so V≤L_s and VP≍B_0. Choose
C_p=(D/g)B_0^(-3/4)x^(-20η).                                (18)
For c≤C_p, Q'=(D/g)/c satisfies
B_0≤(Q')^(4/3),   B_0^(2/3)V^(1/3)≤Q'.                      (19)
If V≥2, apply fact a0cf2b6037398f9f to the q-average; if V=1, apply the separately verified pure-prime fact 8f111039bd9bc8ac. Sum over c|N_gh, then over h, and multiply by H_g^(-1); the h-length cancels. Up to x^ε and summable negative powers of g, the resulting terms are
D^(11/10)R^(4/5),
D^(7/6)R^(13/18)L_s^(1/9),
DR^(7/8),
D^(3/2)R^(1/3)L_s^(2/3),
R,
DR^(1/2)L_s^(1/2).                                           (20)
For c>C_p, trivial summation gives
≪x^(20η+ε)B_0^(7/4).                                        (21)

For b=vpq, combine v with the smaller rough prime p. The two coefficient lengths have product B_0, are at least Z_s, and are at most B_0/Z_s. Put
C_{pq}=(D/g)Z_sB_0^(-1)x^(-20η).                            (22)
For c≤C_{pq}, apply fact dd7f18552d39e5d4; after the same h-cancellation this gives
x^ε[D^(5/4)R^(3/4)Z_s^(-1/4)+DR^(7/8)]                     (23)
with summable negative g-powers. The range c>C_{pq} contributes
≪x^(20η+ε)B_0²/Z_s.                                        (24)
When the two prime dyadic blocks coincide, impose p<q by one half of the unrestricted ordered product minus its diagonal. The diagonal has at most O(VP)=O((B_0V)^(1/2)) pairs at fixed modulus, so after modulus averaging and h-cancellation it is
≪x^ε D(RL_s)^(1/2),                                        (25)
which is the sixth scale already present in (20).

It remains to choose η. With R=x^ρ and D,M=x^(1/2+O(η)), the six terms (20) have exponents
11/20+4ρ/5,
19/36+5ρ/6,
1/2+7ρ/8,
5/12+ρ,
ρ,
1/4+ρ,                                                       (26)
plus fixed multiples of η and ε. At ρ=9/16 they equal
1, 287/288, 127/128, 47/48, 9/16, 13/16.                    (27)
The terms (23)-(24) have exponents
7/16+ρ,  1/2+7ρ/8,  3ρ-3/4,                                (28)
plus fixed multiples of η and ε; only the first reaches 1 at ρ=9/16. The large-c term (21) has exponent at most 63/64+20η+ε. Because ρ≤9/16-κ, first choose η>0 small enough in terms of κ and the fixed family 𝔉 that every endpoint term in (20)-(28) is at most x^(1-c_κ), while the marker estimate (17) retains its cη saving. Then choose ε still smaller. Together with (12)-(13), this gives some δ=δ(κ,𝔉)>0 and proves (5).

Finally, the source-specialized weights of fact 1e2d635f6691e832 form a bounded scaled-smooth family by the uniform derivative argument already verified there. There are O((log x)²) residual labels. Summing (5) over those satisfying (2)-(3) gives O(x^(1-δ/2)). The last sentence of the statement excludes only R>x^(9/16-κ), so there is no endpoint overlap.

glossary.C_p: The target-gcd cutoff for b=v p.
glossary.C_{pq}: The target-gcd cutoff for b=v p q.
glossary.s: The gcd gcd(N_g,a) in a marker class.
glossary.v: The small-prime product in a rough endpoint class.
glossary.ζ: The independent Poisson-frequency truncation exponent η/100.
glossary.η: A sufficiently small balance and marker buffer depending on κ and 𝔉.
glossary.κ: The fixed positive distance from the endpoint exponents 1/2 and 9/16.
glossary.𝒬_N^(≠0): The nonzero Poisson-frequency piece of the smooth double-Möbius block.
glossary.𝔉: A prescribed family of scaled-smooth four-variable weights with uniform support and derivative bounds.

efcd2b6b9fb60a05.title: CRIT-LARGE-e-AUDIT: REDUCED-MEAN AND BARE-MOBIUS LARGE-e PAYMENT, WITH THE EXACT COPRIMALITY RESIDUAL. Work on the actual complete selected critical physical block of fact 5772f2de626492b3 and its primitive cofactor kernel of fact 703f9c67394fc2fc. Fix one orientation, exact g,c, and one frozen outer block. Thus q=de is squarefree with (d,e)=1,
efcd2b6b9fb60a05.author: slava chan
efcd2b6b9fb60a05.statement:
CRIT-LARGE-e-AUDIT: REDUCED-MEAN AND BARE-MOBIUS LARGE-e PAYMENT, WITH THE EXACT COPRIMALITY RESIDUAL. Work on the actual complete selected critical physical block of fact 5772f2de626492b3 and its primitive cofactor kernel of fact 703f9c67394fc2fc. Fix one orientation, exact g,c, and one frozen outer block. Thus q=de is squarefree with (d,e)=1,
t=(ell-kappa n)/(de) is asymptotic to T,
n is asymptotic to B, kappa is asymptotic to K_c,
q is asymptotic to Q_c, and BK_c is asymptotic to ell.           (1)
Let w_{d,e,kappa}(n) be the source-specific complete literal smooth amplitude of fact 5772f2de626492b3.

For fixed d,e,kappa with (kappa ell,de)=1, define
a_d=ell kappa^(-1) modulo d                                      (2)
and
Delta_{d,e,kappa}
 =sum_{n congruent a_d (mod d),(n,e)=1}mu(n)w_{d,e,kappa}(n)
  -phi(d)^(-1)sum_{(n,de)=1}mu(n)w_{d,e,kappa}(n).             (3)
The second term is the true reduced-residue mean introduced by centering the d-progression; it is distinct from the original t-progression Poisson zero mode.

For every prescribed A>0, the aggregate reduced-residue mean in the primitive cofactor kernel, after summing all active d,e and the O(K_c) values of kappa, is
<<_A BK_c(log x)^(-A)                                          (4)
after increasing the input saving exponent by a fixed amount. Hence it is smaller than ell times every prescribed negative logarithmic power.

There is an exact inclusion-exclusion identity
Delta_{d,e,kappa}=sum_{r divides e}mu(r)Delta_{d;r,kappa},       (5)
where
Delta_{d;r,kappa}
 =sum_{n congruent a_d (mod d),r divides n}mu(n)w_{d,e,kappa}(n)
  -phi(d)^(-1)sum_{(n,d)=1,r divides n}mu(n)w_{d,e,kappa}(n).   (6)
The r=1 term is the bare centered Mobius progression. For r>1, the first sum in (6) is supported on the simultaneous conditions
n congruent a_d (mod d), n congruent 0 (mod r),                  (7)
a nonreduced residue modulo dr; after n=rm its coefficient is mu(rm), not mu(m).

Use the classical Mobius Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem recorded by Granville and Shao, arXiv:1703.06865, introduction equation (1.1) and the immediately following sentence: for every A_1>0 there is C_BV=C_BV(A_1)>0 such that, for
D_0<=X^(1/2)/(log X)^(C_BV),
sum_{d asymptotic to D_0} max_{(a,d)=1}
 |sum_{n<=X,n congruent a (mod d)}mu(n)
  -phi(d)^(-1)sum_{n<=X,(n,d)=1}mu(n)|
 <<_{A_1}X(log X)^(-A_1).                                      (8)

Fix a desired A_0>0. First take A_1>A_0+C_reg+C_tax+20, where C_reg is the regularity exponent in fact 5772f2de626492b3 and C_tax is a fixed exponent large enough for all displayed divisor and label sums below; then take C_BV=C_BV(A_1), enlarged by a fixed constant. If B>1 and
E_0>=max{2,4Q_c(log B)^(C_BV)/sqrt(B)},                          (9)
then the total r=1 contribution from e>=E_0 is
<<_{A_0}BK_c(log x)^(-A_0).                                    (10)

After the payments (4) and (10), the exact residual primitive-sector interface is:

(i) every small-e term e<E_0 in the cofactor kernel of fact 703f9c67394fc2fc; and

(ii) for e>=E_0, every term (6) with r|e and r>1, retaining the coefficient mu(d)mu(r)mu(n)/phi(e), the complete w_{d,e,kappa}(n), all unit conditions, and the q=de source support.

Because E_0>=2, the endpoint e=1 lies in (i) and remains the top-modulus truncated Mobius divisor/parity kernel isolated by fact 703f9c67394fc2fc. The quoted bare-Mobius theorem does not pay (ii): dr can be as large as de asymptotic to Q_c, and n=rm leaves mu(rm). A sufficient new large-e input would be a weighted maximal BV estimate for mu(n)1_{(n,e)=1}, uniform in e and the actual literal weights. No such extension, small-e payment, full primitive payment, critical-tail estimate, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
efcd2b6b9fb60a05.proof:
Fact 5772f2de626492b3 proves uniformly that w_{d,e,kappa}(By) is supported on a fixed compact y-interval and satisfies
sup_y |w(By)| + integral |d/dy w(By)|dy + sup_y |d/dy w(By)|
 <<(log x)^(C_reg),                                             (11)
and also that B>=x^(1/20). Thus every use below satisfies the fixed-power length condition.

The condition d|kappa n-ell is equivalent to n congruent a_d modulo d because (kappa,d)=1. Centering that progression gives (3). Fact 71389b22e6f49e13, applied with coprimality integer de, length B>=x^(1/20), and the smooth norm (11), gives uniformly
sum_{(n,de)=1}mu(n)w_{d,e,kappa}(n)
 <<_A B(log x)^(-A).                                           (12)

We record the divisor accounting. For every squarefree h<=2Q_c,
h/phi(h)=product_{p|h}(1-1/p)^(-1)
 <=product_{p|h}(1+2/p)
 <=sum_{a|h}2^(omega(a))/a
 <=sum_{a<=2Q_c}tau(a)/a
 <=(1+log(2Q_c))^2.                                            (13)
The last inequality follows by writing tau(a)=sum_{uv=a}1 and bounding the two harmonic sums. Hence
sum_{h<=2Q_c,h squarefree}1/phi(h)
 <=(1+log(2Q_c))^3.                                            (14)
The mean in (3) has primitive-kernel coefficient 1/[phi(d)phi(e)]. Applying (12), then (14) twice to d and e, and finally summing the O(K_c) kappa-values proves (4), with the resulting fixed logarithmic exponent absorbed by choosing A larger. Relation (1) converts BK_c to ell.

Insert
1_{(n,e)=1}=sum_{r|e,r|n}mu(r)
in both sums of (3). This proves (5)-(6). Squarefreeness of de gives (d,r)=1. The Chinese remainder theorem gives the unique simultaneous class (7) modulo dr. It is nonreduced for r>1, and n=rm leaves mu(rm), proving the arithmetic claims.

It remains to prove the weighted r=1 estimate without an endpoint-grid gap. For fixed e,kappa and d, let
A_d(u)=sum_{n<=u,n congruent a_d (mod d)}mu(n)
       -phi(d)^(-1)sum_{n<=u,(n,d)=1}mu(n).                    (15)
The r=1 weighted discrepancy is the Stieltjes integral of w_{d,e,kappa}(u) against dA_d(u). Abel summation and the smooth compact support give
|Delta_{d;1,kappa}|
 <= boundary_d
   +integral |A_d(u)| |w'_{d,e,kappa}(u)|du,                   (16)
where the boundary term is bounded by sup|w| times endpoint values of |A_d|.

For fixed e, the source restriction de asymptotic to Q_c confines d to one fixed-ratio interval with d<=2Q_c/e. Under (9),
d<=sqrt(B)/(2(log B)^(C_BV)).                                  (17)
Every u in the support is comparable to B. After the fixed enlargement of C_BV, (17) lies inside
d<=sqrt(u)/(log u)^(C_BV)
uniformly throughout the support. Apply (8) at each real endpoint u and to the fixed-ratio d-interval, splitting that interval into O(1) dyadic intervals if necessary. Since (2) is a reduced residue, this gives
sum_d |A_d(u)| <<_{A_1} B(log x)^(-A_1)                        (18)
uniformly for u on the support.

From (11),
sup_{d,u}|w'_{d,e,kappa}(u)|
 <=B^(-1)(log x)^(C_reg),                                      (19)
while the u-support has length O(B), and sup|w| has the same logarithmic bound. Sum (16) over d, use (18) for the boundary and at every u, and then integrate:
sum_d |Delta_{d;1,kappa}|
 << B(log x)^(-A_1+C_reg).                                    (20)
This is a direct Abel transfer; there is no endpoint grid and no unabsorbed grid factor.

Multiply (20) by 1/phi(e), sum e using (14), and sum the O(K_c) kappa-values. The chosen order A_1>A_0+C_reg+C_tax+20 absorbs all fixed divisor, dyadic and frozen-label taxes, proving (10). The threshold (9) also forces E_0>=2, so the endpoint classification is exact.

For r>1, neither (8) nor fact 71389b22e6f49e13 estimates (6): the modulus dr may recover the full q-scale, the residue is nonreduced, and substitution changes the coefficient to mu(rm). Retaining these terms and all small-e terms gives exactly (i)-(ii), completing the proof.

glossary.A_d: The unweighted centered partial-sum discrepancy for the Mobius function in residue a_d modulo d.
glossary.C_BV: The logarithmic modulus-range exponent supplied by the cited Mobius Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem.
glossary.C_tax: A fixed exponent chosen to dominate all divisor, dyadic, and frozen-label logarithmic taxes in the aggregate.
glossary.Delta_{d,e,kappa}: The centered literal Mobius discrepancy modulo d with the extra condition (n,e)=1.
glossary.Delta_{d;r,kappa}: The r-divisibility row in the exact inclusion-exclusion of Delta_{d,e,kappa}.
glossary.E_0: The cofactor threshold separating small e from large e.
glossary.a_d: The reduced residue ell times the inverse of kappa modulo d.

efd5ace01f0a6c11.title: LITERAL FORWARD-REVERSE ONE-ROUGH-PRIME C1 CLOSURE IN THE FIRST POST-LOW-BETA BUFFER
efd5ace01f0a6c11.author: slava chan
efd5ace01f0a6c11.statement:
LITERAL FORWARD-REVERSE ONE-ROUGH-PRIME C1 CLOSURE IN THE FIRST POST-LOW-BETA BUFFER.

Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, put sigma=kappa/100, beta_0=6/5-2kappa, beta_1=6/5-3sigma, kappa_0=1/200, and fix 0<eta<sigma. Let x>=3 and let N be a positive integer comparable to x. Work with the literal paired nonzero-Poisson source atoms, exact outer-gcd normalization d=ga, r=gb with g=gcd(d,r) dividing N, normalized marker partition, and post-B residual ledger of facts 323499eb9e75ce72 and cbfebc160d4bc310.

In the forward orientation assume
R>D, c_1 x<=DM<=C_1 x,
c_D x^(1/2)(log x)^(-A_D)<=D<=C_D x^(1/2),
and R>x^(9/16-kappa_0).
In the reverse orientation assume
D>R, c_1 x<=RK<=C_1 x,
c_R x^(1/2)(log x)^(-A_R)<=R<=C_R x^(1/2),
and D>x^(9/16-kappa_0).
All displayed c_i,C_i are fixed positive constants, A_D,A_R are fixed nonnegative constants, and every physical scale D,M,R,K is at most Cx for a fixed C.

Forward put Q=D/g, B=R/g=Q^beta, G=M/Q, H_T=B/Q, H_P=B/M and L_src=N/g. Reverse put Q=R/g, B=D/g=Q^beta, G=K/Q, H_T=B/Q, H_P=B/K and L_src=N/g. On a normalized C1 atom write the normalized marked factor b=vp in the forward orientation and a=vp in the reverse orientation, where v<=S_0=H_T^2Q^(3sigma), every prime divisor of v is at most L=H_TQ^sigma, p is the unique prime at least Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma), and the exact marker coefficient is -mu(v).

Let R_C1,buf be the sum of every normalized one-rough-prime C1 atom in either strict orientation for which beta_0<beta<=beta_1, over every actual G>0 and every exact outer gcd g dividing N. Include every frozen source phase, parent, fixed-U, high, smooth/projective, Fourier and provenance coordinate. Include all atoms in every inherited target-gcd, prime-order, outer-gcd/rough-prime collision, and deletion refinement; these auxiliary refinements are summed to completion within R_C1,buf rather than imposed as arbitrary joint masks on the separated trace.

Then there is a fixed delta_C1,buf>0 such that
|R_C1,buf| << x^(1-delta_C1,buf).
No C1 atom, G-range, frequency block, parent, orientation, outer-g layer, prime ordering, collision stratum, or provenance coordinate in the displayed complete buffer is deleted. The theorem estimates only the complete C1 anatomy in the displayed normalized-beta buffer. It does not estimate C2, C3, A or B above beta_1, the later beta_1<beta<6/5 range, higher anatomies, moving actual-Z deletions, endpoints, PMD, logical bad-N capture, or Goldbach.
efd5ace01f0a6c11.proof:
The standard five-way marker is valid throughout the displayed buffer by fact 15425579cb248eff. Facts 323499eb9e75ce72 and cbfebc160d4bc310 give the exact post-B disjoint anatomy list C1,C2,C3 in this slab, with every orientation, parent, actual-G, outer-g and provenance coordinate retained. Therefore we may select the complete C1 anatomy coordinate and sum all its auxiliary refinements back to the exact C1 coefficient before applying a separated reciprocal estimate. This is not an arbitrary joint deletion.

Fix a forward exact-g layer. Since d and r are squarefree on every nonzero Mobius source atom, writing d=ga and r=gb gives gcd(a,b)=1 and separates the outer Mobius factor as a label scalar. The normalized C1 alternative of fact 6414b11506a84ff0 gives uniquely
b=vp, mu(b)=-mu(v),                                                   (1)
where v<=S_0, all prime divisors of v are at most L, and p is the unique prime at least Z. The proof of fact 76040270e1ddf949 shows more strongly that on every dyadic C1 block p is larger than every prime divisor of v, so gcd(v,p)=1 and all prime-order and internal collision conditions are exact.

The normalized source equation is
am+bk=L_src.                                                          (2)
Solving (2) for m modulo b gives
m congruent to L_src a^(-1) modulo b,                                (3)
because gcd(a,b)=1. Poisson summation in m, with the literal forward Fourier-sign convention, therefore produces the reciprocal phase
e_b(L_src h a^(-1)).                                                 (4)
Additive reciprocity gives
e_b(L_src h a^(-1))
=e_a(-L_src h b^(-1)) e(L_src h/(ab)).                               (5)
Using b=vp, the reciprocal trace in (5) has modulus a comparable to Q, factor product vp comparable to B, fixed target A=-L_src, and no modulus-dependent unit multiplier. In particular, the short Vaughan Type-I branch has exactly the multiplier-one phase required by fact 76040270e1ddf949. The target may be nonunit modulo a, which that fact permits.

On every actual dyadic integer-frequency block F<=|h|<2F, fact df9748efe29ab475 and the literal projective audit in fact 0d53c27d174b26ed give the prefactor H_P^(-1) and a scalar omega_F satisfying, for every fixed J_0>=1,
|omega_F|<<min(1,(F/H_P)^(-J_0)).                                    (6)
After extracting omega_F, the remaining amplitude in a/Q, |h|/F, v/V and p/P has uniformly bounded projective Fourier norm. This includes the archimedean factor in (5), because its logarithmic phase size after the frequency scaling is controlled by
L_src/(QM)=N/(DM)=O(1).                                              (7)
The literal source, fixed-U and dyadic masks are fixed-complexity smooth restrictions; high and parent are frozen label scalars by facts 77d7a3419a07305c and a71f777ad842c886. Every target-gcd, prime-order, collision and deletion refinement was recombined before this step. Thus each complete forward C1 block matches fact 76040270e1ddf949 exactly, with xi_v=-mu(v). Proper prime powers, every Vaughan Type-I and Type-II slot, H_P<1, both signs and all Fourier tails are already included in that fact.

We check the fixed-target size without suppressing a physical hypothesis. Forced high gives
Q^(beta-1)=R/D>x^(1/16-kappa_0+o(1)).                                (8)
Since beta-1<=1/5, (8) implies Q>=x^c for a fixed c=c(kappa)>0. Also
|L_src|=(N/D)Q<=x^(1/2+o(1))Q,
so |L_src|<=Q^(C_src) for a fixed C_src depending only on kappa. Hence the target hypothesis of fact 76040270e1ddf949 holds.

Fact 15425579cb248eff proves that every actual forward G<1 is in
Q^(-sigma+eta)<=G<=Q^(sigma-eta),
whereas every actual G>=1 is in the full-G regime. If G>=1, fact 76040270e1ddf949 gives the fixed-g complete C1 contribution
O(GQ^(2-delta_1)).
Since DM=gGQ^2 is comparable to x, this is
O((x/g)Q^(-delta_1)).                                                (9)
If G<1, the same fact gives
O(Q^(2-delta_2)).                                                     (10)

For the reverse orientation interchange (d,m,D,M) with (r,k,R,K) and reindex the complete signed frequency family by h to -h, as in fact 65b10e9a052e9479. Now Q=R/g, B=D/g, G=K/Q, the normalized C1 marked factor is a=vp, and the reciprocal modulus is b. The verified reverse chart in fact 65b10e9a052e9479 gives, after that sign reindexing, the phase
e_b(+L_src h a^(-1)),                                                (11)
so fact 76040270e1ddf949 applies with target A=+L_src and again with multiplier one in Type I. The retained archimedean factor is uniformly projective because
L_src/(QK)=N/(RK)=O(1).                                              (12)
The C1 coefficient (1), frequency decay (6), target bound, and estimates (9)-(10) are otherwise unchanged. The physical reverse forced-high hypothesis gives the same fixed power lower bound Q>=x^c.

It remains to sum exact outer gcds and fixed labels. In the G>=1 case, (9) and Q>=x^c give
sum_{g|N}(x/g)Q^(-delta_1)<<x^(1-c delta_1+o(1)).                    (13)
In the G<1 case, Q=D/g forward and Q=R/g reverse. After decreasing delta_2 below one,
sum_{g|N}(D/g)^(2-delta_2)
<=D^(2-delta_2) sum_{g>=1}g^(-2+delta_2),
and the same bound holds with R in reverse. The displayed physical upper bounds D,R<<x^(1/2) make these sums
O(x^(1-delta_2/3))                                                   (14)
after shrinking the exponent to absorb logarithmic factors. All inherited fixed source, parent, fixed-U, high, provenance and smooth labels are polylogarithmically numerous. Combining (13)-(14) proves the asserted fixed power saving without estimating any other anatomy or beta range.

f077de751a5189b6.title: Let L_set and R_set be finite sets of labelled left and right packets. Each P_L in L_set has a finite prime support S_L(P_L) and an integer carrier c_L(P_L). Each P_R in R_set has an ordered support S_R(P_R)={r_1(P_R),r_2(P_R),r_3(P_R),r_4(P_R)} of four distinct primes and an integer carrier c_R(P_R). Define the provenance-preserving pair-coordinate set
f077de751a5189b6.author: slava chan
f077de751a5189b6.statement:
Let L_set and R_set be finite sets of labelled left and right packets. Each P_L in L_set has a finite prime support S_L(P_L) and an integer carrier c_L(P_L). Each P_R in R_set has an ordered support S_R(P_R)={r_1(P_R),r_2(P_R),r_3(P_R),r_4(P_R)} of four distinct primes and an integer carrier c_R(P_R). Define the provenance-preserving pair-coordinate set
A_pair={(P_L,P_R,C):c_L(P_L)=c_R(P_R)=C}
and, for alpha=(P_L,P_R,C), define
m(alpha)=1_{S_L(P_L) intersect S_R(P_R) is empty}.

(A) On l^2(A_pair), multiplication by m is an orthogonal projection Pi_dis with ||Pi_dis||_op<=1. It has the exact sixteen-face expansion
m(P_L,P_R,C)=sum_{F subset {1,2,3,4}}(-1)^{|F|} product_{i in F}1_{r_i(P_R) in S_L(P_L)}.                 (SF)
For any finite external index set Q_set and arbitrary vectors b_q in l^2(A_pair), define
G_dis(q,q')=sum_{alpha in A_pair}m(alpha)overline(b_q(alpha))b_{q'}(alpha),
G_all(q,q')=sum_{alpha in A_pair}overline(b_q(alpha))b_{q'}(alpha).
Then for every z in C^{Q_set},
sum_{q,q'}overline(z_q)G_dis(q,q')z_{q'}
=sum_{alpha}m(alpha)|sum_q z_q b_q(alpha)|^2>=0.                    (PSD)
Thus G_dis is positive semidefinite. If G_all(q,q)>0, then
0<=G_dis(q,q)/G_all(q,q)<=1.                                      (DR)
Both endpoints in (DR) are sharp uniformly over packet systems and amplitudes. This does not contradict fact 9fa397ffcac491a6: Pi_dis is diagonal on ordered pair provenance (P_L,P_R,C), whereas the indefinite matrix in that fact is obtained by collapsing the two provenance roles and using disjointness as a matrix indexed by single support states.

(B) Fixed diagonal masses and all pairwise Cauchy bounds do not imply a simultaneous cross-q Gram representation. Indeed, on three external labels define
H=[[1,1,-1],[1,1,1],[-1,1,1]].
Every two-by-two principal submatrix is positive semidefinite and saturates |H(q,q')|<=sqrt(H(q,q)H(q',q')), but det(H)=-4. Hence H is not positive semidefinite and is not the Gram matrix of one common family of three vectors. It is the three-q one-edge phase-flip countermodel: two edges have phase +1 and one edge has phase -1.

(C) The provenance-correct primitive-window coherence contract COH is the following additional input, not a consequence of (A). For alpha=(P_L,P_R,C), put
n_L(alpha)=product_{p in S_L(P_L)}p,
n_R(alpha)=product_{r in S_R(P_R)}r,
and define the pair primitive-frequency set
Xi_alpha={(h_L modulo n_L(alpha),h_R modulo n_R(alpha)):gcd(h_L,n_L(alpha))=gcd(h_R,n_R(alpha))=1},
with the evident singleton convention when a support is empty. A literal COH representation must supply, simultaneously for every q in Q_set, one vector Phi_q(alpha) in l^2(Xi_alpha) whose coordinates contain the actual q-dependent centered window Fourier multipliers, companion phases, and packet weights, and must prove for all q,q' the exact literal kernel identity
K_lit(q,q')=sum_{alpha in A_pair}m(alpha)<Phi_q(alpha),Phi_{q'}(alpha)>_{l^2(Xi_alpha)}.       (COH-REP)
The separate primitive conditions on n_L(alpha) and n_R(alpha), and the ordered pair label (P_L,P_R), may not be replaced silently by a single collapsed packet product. If D_q=K_lit(q,q)>0 and Gamma_COH(q,q')=K_lit(q,q')/sqrt(D_qD_{q'}), the normalized analytic target is, for every z,
|sum_{q,q'}overline(z_q)(Gamma_COH(q,q')-1_{q=q'})z_{q'}|
<=delta sum_q|z_q|^2,                                               (COH-delta)
equivalently ||Gamma_COH-I||_op<=delta. Neither (COH-REP), a value delta<1, nor any fixed-power saving is asserted. Facts da23b28ec48ad852, 925b3fb5df2c17cc, and 225b1500e4d495e6 show that interval density, interval length, and common local shape do not supply (COH-delta) when q-dependent translations are free; the literal arithmetic location law must be retained.

(D) The connected partition index and the support-face index remain separate. For the fifteen set partitions pi of {1,2,3,4}, the connected coefficient c_pi=(-1)^{|pi|-1}(|pi|-1)! equals +1 on the one one-block partition, -1 on the seven two-block partitions, +2 on the six three-block partitions, and -6 on the one four-block partition. Therefore a full expansion with support faces is indexed by (pi,F), not by one common index. Positivity of Pi_dis and (PSD) does not turn a signed connected-partition kernel sum_pi c_pi U_pi into a Gram matrix. To include connected/Ursell bundling in COH, one must additionally prove that the actual full signed partition kernel is positive semidefinite and give a common Hilbert factorization, or prove an exact prior bundling that incorporates the signed sum into the vectors Phi_q. No such partition factorization and no arithmetic saving is asserted.
f077de751a5189b6.proof:
For (A), m takes only the values zero and one. Thus multiplication by m is self-adjoint and its square equals itself, so it is an orthogonal projection. Every orthogonal projection has operator norm at most one. Pointwise,
1_{S_L intersect S_R is empty}=product_{i=1}^4(1-1_{r_i in S_L}),
and expanding this product proves (SF), with one empty face and fifteen nonempty faces.

Expand the left side of (PSD), interchange the finite sums, and use the definition of G_dis:
sum_alpha m(alpha) sum_{q,q'}overline(z_q b_q(alpha))z_{q'}b_{q'}(alpha)
=sum_alpha m(alpha)|sum_q z_qb_q(alpha)|^2.
Every summand is nonnegative. On the diagonal,
G_dis(q,q)=sum_alpha m(alpha)|b_q(alpha)|^2
and
G_all(q,q)=sum_alpha|b_q(alpha)|^2.
The first is a sub-sum of the second, proving (DR). The lower endpoint is realized by a packet system with one intersecting pair and an amplitude supported on it; the upper endpoint is realized by one disjoint pair and an amplitude supported on it. Hence the bounds are sharp. The distinction from the collapsed support-state adjacency of fact 9fa397ffcac491a6 is exactly the distinction between a diagonal multiplication operator on ordered pairs and a matrix whose two indices are separate single-support states.

For (B), every diagonal entry of H is one and every off-diagonal entry has modulus one. Each two-by-two principal submatrix is therefore [[1,u],[conjugate(u),1]] with |u|=1, so it is positive semidefinite of rank one and saturates Cauchy. Direct expansion gives det(H)=-4, so H has a negative eigenvalue and cannot be a Gram matrix. Equivalently, if unit vectors v_1,v_2,v_3 had this Gram, equality with inner product +1 on edges (1,2) and (2,3) would give v_1=v_2=v_3, while inner product -1 on edge (1,3) would give v_3=-v_1, a contradiction.

For (C), centered local window multipliers vanish when a local frequency is zero, as proved for the four-prime companion in fact be4e5ad5378f0122. Thus the correct common pair fibre records primitive frequencies separately on the left and right packet moduli. If (COH-REP) is proved, the direct sum over alpha of the vectors m(alpha)^{1/2}Phi_q(alpha) has Gram K_lit, so K_lit is positive semidefinite. After diagonal normalization, the standard Hermitian Rayleigh-quotient identity makes (COH-delta) equivalent to the stated operator norm. Part (B) proves why separately constructed q,q' factorizations and pairwise Cauchy bounds cannot replace one simultaneous family Phi_q. The counterexamples in facts da23b28ec48ad852, 925b3fb5df2c17cc, and 225b1500e4d495e6 prove the stated necessity of literal q-dependent placement information. These are contract and non-implication statements, not a proof that the actual arithmetic family satisfies COH.

For (D), the numbers of partitions of a four-element set into one, two, three, and four blocks are respectively 1,7,6,1. Substituting the block number into (-1)^{|pi|-1}(|pi|-1)! gives +1,-1,+2,-6. The support face F is instead a subset of four coordinates with coefficient (-1)^{|F|}, as in (SF), so applying both expansions produces the Cartesian index (pi,F).

To see that support positivity cannot by itself repair the partition signs, take an abstract family in which U_pi is the scalar positive semidefinite matrix [1] for one two-block partition and is zero for every other partition. The signed partition sum is then [-1], which is not positive semidefinite, although its support multiplier may be the identity projection. The same example works with the four-block coefficient -6. Therefore a positive factorization of the actual fully bundled signed partition kernel is an additional theorem, unless an exact prior identity has already incorporated it into common vectors. This proves every asserted algebraic clause and the stated missing-seam qualifications.

glossary.COH-REP: the missing simultaneous literal common-pair-amplitude identity across every q,q'
glossary.COH-delta: the normalized arbitrary-coefficient cross-q near-isometry target after COH-REP
glossary.DR: the sharp masked-to-unmasked diagonal ratio bound
glossary.G_dis: the support-masked Gram formed from common pair amplitudes
glossary.Xi_alpha: the separate left-right primitive-frequency fibre at pair coordinate alpha
glossary.c_pi: the connected partition-lattice coefficient indexed by pi
glossary.m: the zero-one support-disjoint membership function on A_pair
glossary.n_L: the prime-support product of the left packet in an ordered pair coordinate
glossary.n_R: the prime-support product of the right packet in an ordered pair coordinate
glossary.three-q one-edge phase-flip countermodel: the three-by-three pairwise-valid but globally indefinite matrix H

f0f6807663d3ef3c.title: CANONICAL MASK-SAFE MARKED DILATOR AND UNIFORM TERMINAL-SQUARE LOWER BOUND
f0f6807663d3ef3c.author: slava chan
f0f6807663d3ef3c.statement:
CANONICAL MASK-SAFE MARKED DILATOR AND UNIFORM TERMINAL-SQUARE LOWER BOUND.

Fix (0<kappale 1/100), put
[
 sigma=kappa/100,qquad  eta_m=6/5-12sigma/5,
]
and let (Q) be sufficiently large. Let
[
  eta_mle eta<6/5,qquad B=Q^ eta,qquad
 H_T=B/Q,
]
[
 L=Q^{ eta-1+sigma},qquad
 S_0=Q^{2 eta-2+3sigma}=H_T^2Q^{3sigma}.
]
Consider one exact non-(A) marker copy in the source-preserving top-sliver ledger of fact (e58fc7c00f1683e6), so its normalized marked squarefree integer (n_z) satisfies (B/2le n_zle2B).

Define its canonical marked dilator (d_star) as follows.

* On a (B) copy, write the exact first-crossing representation as (n_z=uy) appearing in the stopping coefficient and set (d_star=y).
* On a (Cj) copy, (1le jle4), write the exact rough representation as
[
 n_z=v p_1cdots p_j,qquad vle S_0,qquad
 Zle p_1<cdots<p_j,
]
and set
[
 d_star=p_1cdots p_j=n_z/v.
]

Then (d_starmid n_z), (d_star) is squarefree, and, on writing
(n_z=d_star v_star), one has ((d_star,v_star)=1). Moreover
[
 d_star>S_0=H_T^2Q^{3sigma}quadhbox{on (B)},             	ag{1}
]
and
[
 d_starge {Bover2S_0}
 ={1over2}H_T^2Q^{,4-3 eta-3sigma}
 gg H_T^2Q^{3sigma}quadhbox{on every (Cj)}.             	ag{2}
]
The implied constant in (2) is absolute and the final comparison is uniform for ( eta_mle eta<6/5).

The definition is deterministic on each already existing exact marker copy. It does not inspect, delete, or alter the selected (N), literal source coefficient, fixed (U), parent, orientation, exact outer gcd, actual imbalance, target, paired frequency and phase, target-gcd, prime-order/equal-cell, collision, deletion, or provenance coordinate. Therefore insertion of any exact smooth dyadic partition of unity in (d_star), followed by summation of all (d_star)-blocks, restores the original (B) or (Cj) coefficient identically. No estimate for a Poisson trace or for the complete non-(A) aggregate is asserted.
f0f6807663d3ef3c.proof:
Fact (7c1f38cfbb8d0569) gives the exact stopping and rough-prime formulas used by fact (e58fc7c00f1683e6).

On a nonzero (B) copy, the stopping formula has (n_z=uy), ((u,y)=1), and
[
 S_0<yle S_0L.
]
