Both (u) and (y) divide the squarefree integer (n_z). Hence (d_star=y) is squarefree, divides (n_z), is coprime to (v_star=u), and satisfies (1).

On a (Cj) copy, the same exact formula has
[
 n_z=v p_1cdots p_j,
]
where (vle S_0), the displayed primes are distinct, and no displayed prime divides (v). Consequently (d_star=p_1cdots p_j=n_z/v) is a squarefree divisor of (n_z), coprime to (v_star=v). The inherited dyadic support in fact (e58fc7c00f1683e6) gives (n_zge B/2), hence
[
 d_star={n_zover v}ge {Bover2S_0}.
]
Since (B=Q^ eta), (S_0=Q^{2 eta-2+3sigma}), and (H_T^2=Q^{2 eta-2}),
[
 {Bover2S_0}
 ={1over2}Q^{2- eta-3sigma}
 ={1over2}H_T^2Q^{4-3 eta-3sigma}.
]
Now ( eta<6/5), so
[
 4-3 eta-3sigma>2/5-3sigma.
]
Because (sigma=kappa/100le10^{-4}), one has
(2/5-3sigma>3sigma). Thus for sufficiently large (Q),
[
 {1over2}Q^{4-3 eta-3sigma}gg Q^{3sigma},
]
uniformly in the displayed beta range. This proves (2).

The stopping formula is a sum over exact copies ((u,y)), so selecting (y) is deterministic after that copy has been fixed; uniqueness for the underlying unexpanded integer is neither needed nor claimed. The rough representation in a (Cj) copy is part of its exact ordered coefficient. Hence (d_star) is defined without reference to any inherited auxiliary coordinate. Multiplying each copy by a dyadic partition identity (sum_DXi(d_star/D)=1) and summing over (D) leaves that copy unchanged. Summing all copies therefore restores the original anatomy coefficient, with every inherited coordinate untouched.

glossary.d_star: The canonical marked dilator: the first-crossing factor on B and the complete rough-prime product on Cj.
glossary.v_star: The cofactor n_z/d_star attached to one exact marker copy.

f0fa4ee49bb23934.title: GA-CqADD CROSS-gamma INVERSE-ARGUMENT AGGREGATION AND THE EXACT KLOOSTERMAN-COLUMN SPECTRUM
f0fa4ee49bb23934.author: slava chan
f0fa4ee49bb23934.statement:
GA-CqADD CROSS-gamma INVERSE-ARGUMENT AGGREGATION AND THE EXACT KLOOSTERMAN-COLUMN SPECTRUM.

Adopt one genuinely large dyadic additive-conductor block of fact 7ee795d9bff04bb2. Thus gamma=(t,s,c), the conductor t is positive and squarefree, c and s are units modulo t, and
H_C^{q-add-large}(T)=sum_gamma <V_gamma,G_gamma>.                    (1)
For every gamma define its inverse-argument class
eta_gamma=-c s^{-1} (mod t).                                        (2)
For a unit eta modulo t put
V_{t;eta}(a)=t^{-1/2}S_t(a,eta),  a in (Z/tZ)^*,                    (3)
and define the exact cross-gamma aggregates
Z_{t,eta}^{agg}(n)
 =sum_{gamma: t_gamma=t, eta_gamma=eta} Z_gamma(n),
G_{t,eta}^{agg}
 =sum_n conjugate(Z_{t,eta}^{agg}(n))E_{t;n}.                       (4)
Empty classes are zero. Then the literal block has the exact pre-Cauchy compression
H_C^{q-add-large}(T)
 =sum_{T<=t<2T}sum_{eta (mod t)}^*
  <V_{t;eta},G_{t,eta}^{agg}>.                                      (GA-CqADD-ETA)
Every literal source coefficient and pair-dependent deletion remains inside the sums Z_gamma in (4).

For arbitrary positive weights rho_{t,eta},
|H_C^{q-add-large}(T)|^2
 <=[
 sum_{t,eta}rho_{t,eta}||V_{t;eta}||_2^2]
 [
 sum_{t,eta}rho_{t,eta}^{-1}||G_{t,eta}^{agg}||_2^2].               (5)
Unlike the direct-sum inequality in fact 7ee795d9bff04bb2, equation (5) retains all cancellation among distinct gamma having the same pair (t,eta).

The complete column Gram is exact. For units eta,eta' modulo squarefree t,
<V_{t;eta},V_{t;eta'}>
 =product_{p|gcd(t,eta-eta')}(p-1-1/p)
  product_{p|t/gcd(t,eta-eta')}(-1-1/p).                            (6)
Let M_t be this Gram matrix indexed by all units eta modulo t. Under the squarefree Chinese remainder identification, up to permutations and unit rescalings of the local eta coordinates,
M_t is the Kronecker product
M_t similar to tensor_{p|t} M_p,
M_p=p I_{p-1}-(1+1/p)J_{p-1}.                                      (7)
For every odd p, M_p has eigenvalue p with multiplicity p-2 and eigenvalue p^{-1} with multiplicity one. For p=2 it is the one-by-one matrix (1/2), so only the eigenvalue p^{-1} occurs. Consequently every eigenvalue of M_t is a product of allowed local choices p or p^{-1}; in particular
lambda_min(M_t)=1/t,  lambda_max(M_t)<=t,                            (8)
with lambda_max(M_t)=t when t is odd. Equivalently, the synthesis map
A_t: l2((Z/tZ)^*) -> l2((Z/tZ)^*),
A_t x=sum_eta x_eta V_{t;eta},
satisfies
t^{-1/2}||x||_2<=||A_t x||_2<=t^{1/2}||x||_2,                       (9)
and the upper constant is exact for odd t. The lower eigenspace in (8) is the tensor of the local constant eta-vectors.

Thus GA-CqADD-ETA is a genuine cross-gamma-before-Cauchy reduction, but the bare eta-column operator has the natural t^{1/2} top singular scale. A fixed-power gain must prove cancellation inside the literal aggregates Z_{t,eta}^{agg}, show that their eta-profile couples preferentially to low-eigenvalue modes of (7), estimate the direct pairings in (GA-CqADD-ETA) by additional source structure, or correlate distinct t. Generic eta-column Cauchy or the operator norm (9) alone does not supply the large-conductor estimate.

On a prime t=p for which an aggregate Z_{p,eta}^{agg} has at most p/2 distinct supported source residues, fact 538182294674b266 still applies to that aggregate. Hence cross-gamma aggregation can help there only through cancellation in the actual coefficient sum Z_{p,eta}^{agg}; it cannot create a per-aggregate Ramanujan-norm power saving from support geometry alone.

The aggregation (2)-(5), the column Gram (6), and its spectrum (7)-(9) are anatomy-independent for every row family using the normalized Kloosterman columns (3). The literal definition of Z_gamma, its Good-W source support and deletion, and the canonical target scale are Good-W-specific. This theorem proves no bound for the aggregated coefficient mass, no alignment with the low eta-modes, no correlation across distinct t, no GA-qCENT estimate, no tail payment, and no Goldbach conclusion.
f0fa4ee49bb23934.proof:
By fact d3278c2897e20003,
V_gamma(a)=t^{-1/2}S_t(a,-c s^{-1}).
Thus (2)-(3) give V_gamma=V_{t;eta_gamma}. Summing the finitely many G_gamma with fixed (t,eta) gives
sum_{gamma: fixed (t,eta)}G_gamma
 =sum_n conjugate(sum_gamma Z_gamma(n))E_{t;n}
 =G_{t,eta}^{agg}.
Regroup equation (1) by (t,eta). This proves GA-CqADD-ETA without changing any Z_gamma or any selector. Weighted Cauchy in the direct sum over (t,eta) proves (5).

We compute the column Gram first at a prime p. For nonzero eta,eta' modulo p, expand the Kloosterman sums:
p<V_{p;eta},V_{p;eta'}>
 =sum_{a !=0}S_p(a,eta)conjugate(S_p(a,eta'))
 =sum_{a,x,y !=0}e_p(a(x-y)+eta x^{-1}-eta' y^{-1}).               (10)
For fixed x,y,
sum_{a !=0}e_p(a(x-y))=p 1_{x=y}-1.                                (11)
Insert (11) in (10). The first part is
p sum_{x !=0}e_p((eta-eta')x^{-1})=p c_p(eta-eta'),                 (12)
because inversion permutes the nonzero residues. The subtracted part factors as
[sum_{x !=0}e_p(eta x^{-1})]
[sum_{y !=0}e_p(-eta' y^{-1})]
=(-1)(-1)=1.                                                        (13)
Divide (10) by p. This gives
<V_{p;eta},V_{p;eta'}>=c_p(eta-eta')-1/p.                           (14)
If eta=eta', this is p-1-1/p; otherwise it is -1-1/p.

For squarefree t, the Chinese remainder theorem factors every Kloosterman sum into prime-modulus Kloosterman sums. In the p-component both Kloosterman arguments are multiplied by units depending only on p and t. After a change of the local direct-argument variable, the inverse arguments eta and eta' are multiplied by the same nonzero local unit. Therefore their transformed local arguments agree exactly when eta is congruent to eta' modulo p. The normalized sum over primitive a modulo t factors into the product of the normalized prime sums (14). At primes dividing eta-eta' the diagonal value is p-1-1/p; at the other primes the off-diagonal value is -1-1/p. This proves (6).

Under the CRT identification of the eta index set with the product of the nonzero local residue sets, the preceding factorization says that M_t is a Kronecker product of the local matrices whose diagonal is p-1-1/p and whose off-diagonal is -1-1/p. Such a matrix is
pI_{p-1}-(1+1/p)J_{p-1},
which proves (7).

The all-ones local vector is an eigenvector of J_{p-1} with eigenvalue p-1. Its M_p eigenvalue is
p-(1+1/p)(p-1)=1/p.                                                 (15)
Every vector perpendicular to the all-ones vector is killed by J_{p-1} and has M_p eigenvalue p. This subspace has dimension p-2. At p=2 the perpendicular subspace has dimension zero and (15) is the sole eigenvalue. Eigenvalues of a Kronecker product are products of local eigenvalues, with multiplicities multiplied. Choosing p^{-1} at every prime gives 1/t. Every allowed local eigenvalue is at most p, giving lambda_max<=t; when t is odd every local p-eigenspace is nonzero, so choosing p everywhere gives t. This proves (8). Since M_t=A_t^*A_t, taking square roots gives (9), and the local all-ones tensor gives the described lower eigenspace.

The upper singular scale in (9) is t^{1/2} for odd t, so the column operator norm itself supplies no fixed-power improvement over the natural Kloosterman column scale. Equations (4)-(5) show exactly where actual cross-gamma cancellation can still occur: in Z_{t,eta}^{agg} before its norm is taken. The prime-aggregate consequence follows by applying fact 538182294674b266 to the finitely supported sequence Z_{p,eta}^{agg}. Every method-interface and scope statement follows from these exact formulas.

glossary.A_t: The synthesis map whose columns are the vectors V_{t;eta}.
glossary.GA-CqADD-ETA: The exact large-additive-conductor block after aggregating distinct gamma with identical Kloosterman column.
glossary.G_{t,eta}^{agg}: The primitive additive-frequency source vector formed from Z_{t,eta}^{agg}.
glossary.M_t: The complete Gram matrix of normalized Kloosterman columns V_{t;eta} over all unit inverse arguments eta modulo t.
glossary.Z_{t,eta}^{agg}(n): The sum of all literal Z_gamma(n) with common additive conductor t and inverse-argument class eta.
glossary.eta_gamma: The unit inverse-argument class -c s^{-1} modulo the additive conductor t attached to gamma=(t,s,c).

f144376ade9a27f0.title: Fix real numbers 1/2<a<b<1, a nonzero nonnegative continuously differentiable real function W supported in [a,b], a continuously differentiable real function psi with 0<=psi<=1, psi(u)=0 for 0<u<=1 and psi(u)=1 for u>=2, a fixed exponent B_src>0, and the nonnegative smooth dyadic partition Phi from fact 3ef233e014331fc3. For t sufficiently large put D_*(t)=(t/2)^(1/2)(log(t/2))^(-B_src). Let Y be sufficiently large, let K>=1 be an integer, and let D,M,U>=1 be positive dyadic numbers. For every integer N in [Y,2Y] define P_N^{mov}(D,M;U)=sum_{d,m>=1, p prime, dm+p=N}mu(d)log(m)log(p)Phi(d/D)Phi(m/M)Phi(p/U)W(2dm/N)psi(d/D_*(N)). Put y_j=Y(1+j/K) for 0<=j<=K. There exist nonnegative piecewise-linear functions h_0,...,h_K on [Y,2Y] such that sum_j h_j(t)=1 and at most two h_j(t) are nonzero at each t, and for every j,m define the nonnegative N-independent d-weight u_{j,m}(d)=Phi(d/D)W(2dm/y_j)psi(d/D_*(y_j)). Each u_{j,m}, viewed as a function of the positive real variable d, is supported in [D/2,2D] and has uniformly bounded supremum and total variation, with a bound depending only on W,psi,Phi. If T_{j,N}(D,M;U)=sum_{d,m>=1,p prime,dm+p=N}mu(d)log(m)log(p)Phi(m/M)Phi(p/U)u_{j,m}(d), then P_N^{mov}(D,M;U)=sum_{j=0}^K h_j(N)T_{j,N}(D,M;U)+E_N and |E_N|<<_{a,b,B_src,W,psi,Phi} DM log(2M)log(2Y)/K, uniformly in the integer N in [Y,2Y] and in D,M,U,K. In every T_{j,N}, the equation p=N-dm and the prime window Phi(p/U) are unchanged; no prime-variable window is frozen, shifted, or interpolated
f144376ade9a27f0.author: slava chan
f144376ade9a27f0.statement: Fix real numbers 1/2<a<b<1, a nonzero nonnegative continuously differentiable real function W supported in [a,b], a continuously differentiable real function psi with 0<=psi<=1, psi(u)=0 for 0<u<=1 and psi(u)=1 for u>=2, a fixed exponent B_src>0, and the nonnegative smooth dyadic partition Phi from fact 3ef233e014331fc3. For t sufficiently large put D_*(t)=(t/2)^(1/2)(log(t/2))^(-B_src). Let Y be sufficiently large, let K>=1 be an integer, and let D,M,U>=1 be positive dyadic numbers. For every integer N in [Y,2Y] define P_N^{mov}(D,M;U)=sum_{d,m>=1, p prime, dm+p=N}mu(d)log(m)log(p)Phi(d/D)Phi(m/M)Phi(p/U)W(2dm/N)psi(d/D_*(N)). Put y_j=Y(1+j/K) for 0<=j<=K. There exist nonnegative piecewise-linear functions h_0,...,h_K on [Y,2Y] such that sum_j h_j(t)=1 and at most two h_j(t) are nonzero at each t, and for every j,m define the nonnegative N-independent d-weight u_{j,m}(d)=Phi(d/D)W(2dm/y_j)psi(d/D_*(y_j)). Each u_{j,m}, viewed as a function of the positive real variable d, is supported in [D/2,2D] and has uniformly bounded supremum and total variation, with a bound depending only on W,psi,Phi. If T_{j,N}(D,M;U)=sum_{d,m>=1,p prime,dm+p=N}mu(d)log(m)log(p)Phi(m/M)Phi(p/U)u_{j,m}(d), then P_N^{mov}(D,M;U)=sum_{j=0}^K h_j(N)T_{j,N}(D,M;U)+E_N and |E_N|<<_{a,b,B_src,W,psi,Phi} DM log(2M)log(2Y)/K, uniformly in the integer N in [Y,2Y] and in D,M,U,K. In every T_{j,N}, the equation p=N-dm and the prime window Phi(p/U) are unchanged; no prime-variable window is frozen, shifted, or interpolated.
f144376ade9a27f0.proof:
Let Delta=Y/K. Define the standard nodal hats as follows. If t belongs to [y_i,y_{i+1}], put
h_i(t)=(y_{i+1}-t)/Delta,  h_{i+1}(t)=(t-y_i)/Delta,
and put h_j(t)=0 for every other j. The definitions agree at the nodes. They give nonnegative piecewise-linear functions, their sum is one, and only the two adjacent hats can be nonzero.

For fixed positive integers d,m define
f_{d,m}(t)=W(2dm/t)psi(d/D_*(t)),   Y<=t<=2Y.
We prove a uniform Lipschitz bound. Logarithmic differentiation gives
D_*'(t)/D_*(t)=1/(2t)-B_src/[t log(t/2)].
For sufficiently large Y its absolute value is O_{B_src}(1/t). If z=d/D_*(t), then |z'(t)|<<_{B_src}z/t. Since psi is constant on (0,1] and on [2,infinity), its derivative vanishes unless 1<z<2. Hence
|d[psi(d/D_*(t))]/dt|<<_{B_src,psi}1/t.
Put q=2dm/t. Then q'=-q/t. The derivative W'(q) vanishes off [a,b], and on [a,b] one has q<=b. Therefore
|d[W(2dm/t)]/dt|<=b||W'||_infinity/t.
The product rule now gives
sup_{Y<=t<=2Y}|f_{d,m}'(t)|<<_{a,b,B_src,W,psi}1/Y,                       (1)
uniformly in d,m.

For t in [y_i,y_{i+1}], linear interpolation is exactly
I_{d,m}(t)=h_i(t)f_{d,m}(y_i)+h_{i+1}(t)f_{d,m}(y_{i+1})
=sum_{j=0}^K h_j(t)f_{d,m}(y_j).
By (1) and the mean-value theorem,
|f_{d,m}(t)-I_{d,m}(t)|<<1/K.                                            (2)
Multiplying (2) by Phi(d/D) and inserting it term by term into the definition of P_N^{mov} gives the asserted identity with an error E_N. The support of Phi(d/D) restricts d to [D/2,2D], and Phi(m/M) restricts m to [M/2,2M]. There are O(DM) integer pairs (d,m) in these ranges, and for each pair the equation dm+p=N determines at most one p. On a nonzero term, log(m)<=log(2M) and log(p)<=log(2Y). The functions mu and Phi are uniformly bounded. Taking absolute values and using (2) proves
|E_N|<<DM log(2M)log(2Y)/K.

It remains to prove the bounded-variation assertion. For fixed j,m, u_{j,m} is a product of three nonnegative functions. Its support is contained in the support [D/2,2D] of Phi(d/D). Its supremum is bounded by the product of the three fixed supremum norms. By the product rule and a change of variables,
integral_0^infinity |D^(-1)Phi'(d/D)|dd<=integral_0^infinity|Phi'(s)|ds,
integral_0^infinity |(2m/y_j)W'(2dm/y_j)|dd<=integral_0^infinity|W'(s)|ds,
and
integral_0^infinity |D_*(y_j)^(-1)psi'(d/D_*(y_j))|dd<=integral_0^infinity|psi'(s)|ds.
Multiplying each derivative term by the fixed supremum norms of the other two factors shows that the total variation of u_{j,m} is bounded solely in terms of W,psi,Phi, independently of j,m,Y,D,M,U,K.

Finally, the interpolation was applied only to W(2dm/N)psi(d/D_*(N)). In T_{j,N}, the prime p is still determined by the original equation p=N-dm and carries the original factor log(p)Phi(p/U). Thus there is no hidden movement or interpolation of the prime window.

glossary.D_*(t): the moving deep-divisor cutoff at center t
glossary.P_N^{mov}: the actual center-dependent genuine-prime dyadic block
glossary.T_{j,N}: the node-frozen block at center N
glossary.h_j: the nonnegative piecewise-linear hat centered at y_j
glossary.u_{j,m}: the frozen N-independent d-weight at node j and cofactor m
glossary.y_j: the j-th equally spaced freezing node

f1cd394ea025163e.title: GA-COMMON-CORE-DESCENT-MODE: THE UNIQUE LARGE PRIME-SLOPE FREQUENCY IS AN EXACT PHYSICAL PRIME-DESCENT ALIAS. Adopt the forward orientation epsilon_or=+1 in the high-rough C chamber. Fix a common-core survivor class from fact fd22069145f59332:
f1cd394ea025163e.author: slava chan
f1cd394ea025163e.statement:
GA-COMMON-CORE-DESCENT-MODE: THE UNIQUE LARGE PRIME-SLOPE FREQUENCY IS AN EXACT PHYSICAL PRIME-DESCENT ALIAS. Adopt the forward orientation epsilon_or=+1 in the high-rough C chamber. Fix a common-core survivor class from fact fd22069145f59332:
g=pg_0, alpha beta divides T, T_0=T/(alpha beta),
gamma congruent T_0g_0^{-1} (mod p),                              (1)
where p is the odd prime physical conductor. Fix n=dv and the distinguished local frequency
a_n=gamma n^{-1} (mod p)                                        (2)
from fact 122bdf7f46de05e6.

Let R=(epsilon,pg_0alpha,b) be a supported left ray and let k be any supported scaling in I_v(R). Put
q=kpg_0alpha, h=epsilon kb.                                      (3)
Then p divides q exactly once, gcd(p,(q/p)n)=1, and
a_n epsilon b beta
 congruent T h (q/p)^{-1}n^{-1} (mod p).                         (4)
Equivalently, if the physical source equation on this coordinate is
qt+nu=T,                                                         (5)
then
a_n epsilon b beta
 congruent u h(q/p)^{-1} (mod p).                                (6)

The forward literal coordinate function of fact 1e357f0a9f079ca2 is
C_{q,h}(n/B)
 ={H_P/n}widehat{mathcal F}_{q,n}(h/n)
  e(Th/(qn)).                                                     (7)
Its distinguished common-core twist has the exact prime-descent identity
C_{q,h}(n/B)e_p(-a_n epsilon b beta)
 ={H_P/n}widehat{mathcal F}_{q,n}(h/n)
  e_{(q/p)n}(Th p^{-1}),                                         (8)
where p^{-1} in the last phase denotes the inverse of p modulo (q/p)n.

Consequently the p-frequency projection of the actual incomplete left-ray aggregate in equations (7) and (12) of fact 53737f4b1646ac1c is exactly
sum_{supported R=(epsilon,pg_0alpha,b)}
 b_{v,R}(n/B)e_p(-a_n epsilon b beta)
 =mu(pg_0alpha)
  sum_{supported R} 
  sum_{k in I_v(R)}
   mu(k){H_P/n}widehat{mathcal F}_{q,n}(h/n)
   e_{(q/p)n}(Th p^{-1}),                                       (9)
with q,h as in (3). Every scaling support, squarefree Mobius sign, source Fourier amplitude, fixed-U gate, and incomplete ray restriction in b_{v,R} is retained. Equation (9) does not replace the q-indexed Fourier amplitude by one at q/p.

Thus the unique order-p local eigenmode in fact 122bdf7f46de05e6 is not an unspecified Fourier coefficient: in the forward literal source it is the exact row obtained by descending the Archimedean/reciprocity phase from qn to (q/p)n while leaving the physical q-indexed amplitude and all source masks unchanged. No estimate or recursive identification with an existing q/p source row is asserted. In particular, the unchanged q-index of widehat{mathcal F}_{q,n} is an exact obstruction to treating (9) as automatic modulus descent.

This theorem proves only (4)-(9). It does not treat the reverse orientation, the g_0 or rho_d Fourier coordinates, the right-ray factor, one-end chambers, additional pair selectors, the distinguished-mode estimate, the prime trace, C-HILBERT-OP-SUP, tail payment, or Goldbach.
f1cd394ea025163e.proof:
Because q is supported by a squarefree Mobius coefficient and p divides the primitive denominator pg_0alpha, p divides q exactly once and is coprime to k,g_0,alpha. The high-rough C gate gives gcd(q,n)=1, so gcd(p,(q/p)n)=1.

Using T=alpha beta T_0, h=epsilon kb, and q/p=kg_0alpha, one has modulo p
T h(q/p)^{-1}n^{-1}
 congruent alpha beta T_0 epsilon kb
          (kg_0alpha)^{-1}n^{-1}
 congruent T_0g_0^{-1}n^{-1}epsilon b beta
 congruent a_n epsilon b beta.
This proves (4).

Reduce the source equation (5) modulo p. Since p divides q and p is coprime to n,
u congruent Tn^{-1} (mod p).
Also h(q/p)^{-1} is congruent epsilon b(g_0alpha)^{-1}. Substitution gives (6).

We prove the phase identity. Put m=(q/p)n. Then gcd(p,m)=1 and qn=pm. Additive reciprocity for the inverses of p and m gives
1/(pm)-m^{-1}/p congruent p^{-1}/m (mod 1).                      (10)
Multiply (10) by Th and exponentiate:
e(Th/(qn))e_p(-Th m^{-1})
 =e_m(Th p^{-1}).                                                (11)
By (4), the second factor on the left of (11) is
e_p(-a_n epsilon b beta).
Insert the coordinate formula (7) to obtain (8).

Finally fact d92616c2bca6126f defines
b_{v,R}(n/B)
 =mu(pg_0alpha)sum_{k in I_v(R)}mu(k)C_{q,h}(n/B).
Multiply by the ray twist, sum over the exact supported rays, and use (8) term by term. This proves (9) without changing any scaling or coefficient. The Fourier amplitude remains indexed by the original q in (7), so no q/p source-row identity follows. All exclusions are immediate.

glossary.a_n: The distinguished common-core p-frequency gamma n^{-1}.
glossary.prime-descent alias: The source row obtained when the distinguished p-twist descends the phase modulus qn to (q/p)n while retaining the original q-indexed amplitude.

f21be13a19bbb435.title: Let Q be real, let M,E,a,b,c,R_1,R_2 be nonnegative real numbers with c>0, and suppose
f21be13a19bbb435.author: slava chan
f21be13a19bbb435.statement:
Let Q be real, let M,E,a,b,c,R_1,R_2 be nonnegative real numbers with c>0, and suppose
(-Q)_+≤aM^{1/2}+R_1,
M≤bE^{1/2}+R_2.
Then
(-Q)_+≤cE^{1/2}+a^2b/(4c)+aR_2^{1/2}+R_1.
In particular, let P>1, let ε>0, and suppose a≤P^{3/2+ε/6}, b≤P^{6+ε/6}, R_1+aR_2^{1/2}≤P^6(log P)^{-B} for some B>0. Taking c=P^{3+ε} gives
(-Q)_+≤P^{3+ε}E^{1/2}+P^{6-ε/2}/4+P^6(log P)^{-B}.
Consequently, for every fixed A_0>0, once P is sufficiently large in terms of ε,A_0,B and B≥A_0, the last two terms are at most 2P^6(log P)^{-A_0}.
f21be13a19bbb435.proof:
From M≤bE^{1/2}+R_2 and the subadditivity of the nonnegative square root,
M^{1/2}≤b^{1/2}E^{1/4}+R_2^{1/2}.
Therefore
(-Q)_+≤ab^{1/2}E^{1/4}+aR_2^{1/2}+R_1.
For nonnegative x and any c>0, the square (c^{1/2}x^{1/2}-ab^{1/2}/(2c^{1/2}))^2 is nonnegative. Expanding it gives
ab^{1/2}x^{1/2}≤cx+a^2b/(4c).
Apply this with x=E^{1/2}. This proves the first displayed conclusion.

Under the power hypotheses and c=P^{3+ε},
a^2b/(4c)≤P^{3+ε/3}P^{6+ε/6}/(4P^{3+ε})
=P^{6-ε/2}/4.
Substitution gives the second conclusion. Finally, for fixed ε>0 and A_0>0, P^{-ε/2}(log P)^{A_0} tends to zero as P tends to infinity, so P^{6-ε/2}/4≤P^6(log P)^{-A_0} for all sufficiently large P. If B≥A_0 and P≥e, then (log P)^{-B}≤(log P)^{-A_0}. Adding the two remainder estimates proves the final claim.

glossary.(-Q)_+: The positive part max(-Q,0) of the negative of Q.
glossary.A_0: The desired positive logarithmic-saving exponent in the final remainder.
glossary.B: A positive logarithmic-saving exponent already available in the input remainders.
glossary.P: A real scale parameter satisfying P>1.
glossary.R_1: The nonnegative remainder in the first-stage estimate.
glossary.R_1+aR_2^{1/2}: The combined nonnegative input remainder after the two stages.
glossary.R_2: The nonnegative remainder in the intermediate-moment estimate.
glossary.c: A positive coefficient chosen for linearization in E^{1/2}.

f225c6e0aab449f4.title: Let m>1 be odd, let s belong to {1,-1}, let K be an integer with gcd(K,m)=1, and let W be a complex-valued function modulo m. Let G be the unit group modulo m^2 and let T_W be the shared normal-digit tensor of fact 8230d44e6677f45b. Suppose that I is a finite set and that T_W has an exact decomposition
f225c6e0aab449f4.author: slava chan
f225c6e0aab449f4.statement:
Let m>1 be odd, let s belong to {1,-1}, let K be an integer with gcd(K,m)=1, and let W be a complex-valued function modulo m. Let G be the unit group modulo m^2 and let T_W be the shared normal-digit tensor of fact 8230d44e6677f45b. Suppose that I is a finite set and that T_W has an exact decomposition
T_W(a,b,c,d)=sum_{j in I} f_j(a)g_j(c)beta_j(b)alpha_j(d),             (1)
where f_j,g_j,alpha_j,beta_j are complex-valued functions on G and
||f_j||_infinity<=1,  ||g_j||_infinity<=1                            (2)
for every j. Define the total separated column cost
Q_col=sum_{j in I}||alpha_j||_2||beta_j||_2.                          (3)
Then
Q_col>=phi(m)sum_{ell modulo m}|W_hat(ell)|,                           (4)
where W_hat(ell)=sum_{u modulo m}W(u)e_m(-ell u).

In particular, if W is the indicator of one fixed digit, or if W is identically one and hence represents the full unweighted digit union, then
Q_col>=phi(m^2).                                                       (5)
This is a quantitative dense-modular smooth-row-slot obstruction: allowing many row-profile pairs of supremum norm at most one does not make the full unit-group tensor cheap in the arbitrary-sequence slots. It is not the literal normalized Pi_BC of fact b1398db2962d7491. Restricting all four variables to coefficient intervals, imposing the exact determinant equation and the prime, gcd, C-coupling, mask, and source selectors, or permitting row profiles with a separately paid amplitude normalization can change the relevant lower bound.
f225c6e0aab449f4.proof:
Put n=|G|=phi(m^2). Every function f_j on G satisfying ||f_j||_infinity<=1 has ||f_j||_2<=n^(1/2), and the same bound holds for g_j. Hence every term in (1) has four-fold projective cost
||f_j||_2||g_j||_2||beta_j||_2||alpha_j||_2
 <=n||beta_j||_2||alpha_j||_2.                                       (6)
By the definition of the four-fold projective norm P_4 in fact 8230d44e6677f45b, summing (6) over j gives
P_4(T_W)<=n Q_col.                                                     (7)
The exact formula in that fact is
P_4(T_W)=[n^2/m]sum_{ell modulo m}|W_hat(ell)|.                        (8)
Combining (7) and (8), then dividing by n, yields
Q_col>=[n/m]sum_ell|W_hat(ell)|.                                      (9)
Since n=phi(m^2)=m phi(m), equation (9) is exactly (4).

For a fixed digit, every Fourier coefficient has absolute value one, so its Fourier l1 norm is m. For W identically one, W_hat(0)=m and all nonzero frequencies vanish, so its Fourier l1 norm is again m. Substituting either value into (4) gives m phi(m)=phi(m^2), proving (5). The final scope statement follows because (6) used the full unit group G and the explicit supremum normalization (2); neither these supports nor this normalization is the literal coefficient setup in fact b1398db2962d7491.

glossary.Q_col: the total separated ell^2 cost of the b- and d-factors in a bounded-row-profile decomposition of T_W

f234dbd4fdda994e.title: GA-PRECOPY-ALIGN: EXACT FIXED-n TERMINAL-COPY CLASSIFICATION AND SELECTOR-MISALIGNMENT VARIANCE IDENTITY
f234dbd4fdda994e.author: slava chan
f234dbd4fdda994e.statement:
GA-PRECOPY-ALIGN: EXACT FIXED-n TERMINAL-COPY CLASSIFICATION AND SELECTOR-MISALIGNMENT VARIANCE IDENTITY.

Adopt the exact Good-W terminal-copy family, notation, and pre-copy moment of fact 5ce54dcef3d61da1. In particular the terminal marker has L=S=2 and cutoff Z>2, the marked integer n is squarefree, and K_F(n,lambda)=a_lambda(n)K_F^flat(n,lambda). Put
P_I(n)={p:p is prime, p divides n, and 2<p<Z},
r(n)=|P_I(n)|.

For every fixed supported n exactly one of the following alternatives holds.

(A) If r(n)>0, the terminal copies are the interval-prime A-copies. Their terminal factorizations are indexed by p in P_I(n), with d_lambda=n/p and v_lambda=p, and every such terminal marker coefficient is
a_lambda(n)=mu(n)/r(n).                                           (1)
In particular, for any two A-copies over n,
a_lambda(n)conjugate(a_lambda'(n))=1/r(n)^2.                      (2)

(C) If r(n)=0, then the stopping B alternative is empty and there is one unique integer j>=1 and one unique rough factorization
n=v p_1...p_j,  v in {1,2},  Z<=p_1<...<p_j,                    (3)
so the only terminal anatomy is C_j and
a_lambda(n)=(-1)^j mu(v)=mu(n).                                  (4)
Thus there are no A--C or C_j--C_k terminal cross-copy pairs over the same n.

In case (A), group every exact zero-extended flat descendant row having marked interval prime p into
X_p(n)=sum_{lambda over n marked by p}K_F^flat(n,lambda).        (5)
Every hard, source, provenance, equality, collision, deletion, dilator, coprimality, and projective selector present in the exact pre-copy family remains inside the zero-extended summands in (5). Then
K_F^agg(n)=mu(n)/r(n) sum_{p in P_I(n)}X_p(n),                   (6)
and the exact alignment identity is
|K_F^agg(n)|^2
 =1/r(n) sum_{p in P_I(n)}|X_p(n)|^2
  -1/(2r(n)^2) sum_{p,p' in P_I(n)}|X_p(n)-X_p'(n)|^2.          (7)
Consequently
|K_F^agg(n)|^2<=1/r(n)sum_p|X_p(n)|^2,                          (8)
with equality if and only if all X_p(n) are equal. In case (C), if X_C(n) denotes the sum of the zero-extended flat descendants of the unique C_j factorization, then
K_F^agg(n)=mu(n)X_C(n),  |K_F^agg(n)|^2=|X_C(n)|^2.             (9)

Hence every relative terminal-marker product that can occur over a fixed n is nonnegative. Perfectly aligned flat rows maximize the pre-copy moment and have no terminal-marker cancellation; any mismatch caused by the retained selectors or by the marked-dilator factorization contributes through the nonnegative defect subtracted in (7). This theorem concerns the complete physical pre-copy square of fact 5ce54dcef3d61da1. It does not commute the terminal aggregation through a post-copy hard/principal/centered ray-pair projection, does not estimate the F>Q principal source, does not estimate the small-dilator projected-incidence branch, and proves no C-qSRC-BV-SUP, GA-NR-DIL, tail payment, or Goldbach conclusion.
f234dbd4fdda994e.proof:
Fact e55b27d39c593164 applies the terminal identity of fact 7c1f38cfbb8d0569 with L=S=2 to a squarefree integer n. Let I=(2,Z). If r(n)=j_I(n)>0, alternative (A) of fact 7c1f38cfbb8d0569 is the only alternative. Its factorizations are n=up with p in P_I(n), so u=n/p. Since n is squarefree,
mu(u)=-mu(n),
and j_I(u)=r(n)-1. Therefore the coefficient of the p-factorization in the exact interval-prime identity is
-mu(u)/(1+j_I(u))=mu(n)/r(n).
This proves (1), and since mu(n) is real with square one, (2) follows.

Suppose r(n)=0. Because n is squarefree, the product v_2(n) of its prime divisors at most 2 belongs to {1,2}. Hence v_2(n)<=S=2, so the stopping condition v_2(n)>S defining alternative (B) is impossible. Alternative (C_j) of fact 7c1f38cfbb8d0569 therefore applies. That fact proves that j and the ordered rough factorization (3) are unique and that its coefficient is (-1)^j mu(v)=mu(n), giving (4). The alternatives in that fact are disjoint, so there are no cross-anatomy pairs over n.

In case (A), every exact descendant of the p-factorization has the same scalar marker coefficient mu(n)/r(n); all other coefficients and selectors belong to the flat row. Summing first over descendants with common p and then over p proves (6) from the definition of K_F^agg in fact 5ce54dcef3d61da1. Zero-extension preserves every selector literally.

For arbitrary complex numbers X_p, expansion gives
sum_{p,p'}|X_p-X_p'|^2
 =2r(n)sum_p|X_p|^2-2|sum_pX_p|^2.                              (10)
Rearrange (10), divide by r(n)^2, and use |mu(n)|=1 in (6). This proves (7), and nonnegativity of the double sum proves (8). Equality in (8) holds exactly when every difference X_p-X_p' vanishes. In case (C), the unique terminal factorization has coefficient mu(n), so grouping its flat descendants proves (9). All scope exclusions follow because no post-copy ray-pair projection or analytic estimate was used.

glossary.GA-PRECOPY-ALIGN: The fixed-n terminal-copy classification and exact selector-misalignment variance identity.
glossary.P_I(n): The set of prime divisors p of n lying in the terminal interval (2,Z).
glossary.X_C(n): The complete zero-extended flat pre-copy row grouped over the unique rough C_j factorization.
glossary.X_p(n): The complete zero-extended flat pre-copy row grouped by the marked interval prime p.

f23bad095a2e6a52.title: CARRIER-FIRST AGGREGATION OF THE COMPLETE GENERIC FIXED-FIBRE IJOP FAMILY
f23bad095a2e6a52.author: slava chan
f23bad095a2e6a52.statement:
CARRIER-FIRST AGGREGATION OF THE COMPLETE GENERIC FIXED-FIBRE IJOP FAMILY.

Fix real constants L_0>=1, L_1>=1, A>=1 and D>=0. Let m>4L_1+1 be odd, put q=m^2, and let 2<=H<=m^A. Let C be a nonzero integer with |C|<=H^(L_0), let K be an integer with gcd(m,2K)=1, and fix s in {1,-1}. Let I_a,I_c,I_1,I_2 be integer intervals of cardinality at most L_1m, with I_1,I_2 positive, and assume that every integer in their union has absolute value at most L_0H^3.

For a in I_a, c in I_c, n_1 in I_1, n_2 in I_2 put b=n_2 and d=-n_1. Let E_outer_gen be the tuples
 (a,c,n_1,n_2,u,k,r_2,r_3)
in I_a times I_c times I_1 times I_2 times {0,...,m-1} times Z times Z times Z
with the following properties:
(i) a,c,n_1,n_2 are even;
(ii) r_2,r_3 are distinct primes in [H^2,2H^2), and gcd(m,r_2r_3)=1;
(iii)
 a n_2=K+2smu+km^2,  c n_1=a n_2-2K;                              (1)
(iv) the integers
 lambda_A=(b r_3-d r_2)/(2m),
 lambda_B=(a r_2-c r_3)/(2m),
 lambda_J=(ab-cd)/(4m)                                             (2)
exist, lambda_A and lambda_B have common sign s, and
 gcd(|lambda_A|,|lambda_B|)=1;
(v) r_1=|lambda_A| and r_4=|lambda_B| are primes in [H^2,2H^2), and r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4 are pairwise distinct;
(vi)
 gcd(C,r_1r_2r_3r_4)=1, lambda_J is nonzero,
 d r_2lambda_B-c r_3lambda_A=2sC;                                 (3)
(vii) lambda_J is congruent to su modulo m and
 k=2(lambda_J-su)/m.                                               (4)

Let F be supported on I_a, let W be any complex function modulo m, and let alpha,beta be supported on I_1,I_2. Let Omega_outer be any complex function on E_outer_gen that is independent of Fourier characters and satisfies
 |Omega_outer|<=(log(2H))^D.                                       (5)
Define
 T_outer_gen=sum_{E_outer_gen}
 F(a)W(u)alpha(n_1)beta(n_2)Omega_outer.                            (6)
Put
 V_F=||F||_infinity+sum_{z in Z}|F(z+1)-F(z)|.                      (7)
Then, for every epsilon>0,
 |T_outer_gen|
 <=C_{L_0,L_1,A,D,epsilon}m^(15/16+epsilon)
 V_F||W||_2||alpha||_2||beta||_2.                                 (8)

More precisely, for a unit residue x modulo q define
 C_outer(x)=sum_{E_outer_gen; ax congruent 1 modulo q}
 W(u)alpha(n_1)beta(n_2)Omega_outer,                               (9)
and put C_outer(x)=0 on nonunits. If
 C_outer_hat(p)=sum_{x modulo q}C_outer(x)e_q(-px),                 (10)
then
 ||C_outer_hat||_2
 <=C_{L_0,L_1,A,D,epsilon}q^(1/2+epsilon)
 ||W||_2||alpha||_2||beta||_2.                                   (11)

Thus, at fixed m,s,C,K, the complete coefficient shell, every ordered pair r_2,r_3, both recovered primes r_1,r_4, both correlated carrier gates, the common shared lift, moving coefficient intervals, parity, distinctness, coprimality, and every source mask satisfying (5) are retained inside one coefficient before Fourier completion. Their carrier-first aggregation costs m^epsilon, not the H cost of prime-line-first atomization and not the raw number of prime tuples.

The theorem does not sum varying C or K, does not improve the explicit digit factor ||W||_2, and does not cover even m, gcd(m,2K)>1, or normalized states whose conductor q_state=gcd(|b r_3-d r_2|,|a r_2-c r_3|) is not 2m.
f23bad095a2e6a52.proof:
We first check the normalization pointwise without imposing a common positive row box. Equations (1) and b=n_2,d=-n_1 give
 ab+cd=a n_2-c n_1=2K,                                             (12)
and, modulo m,
 ab is congruent to K,   cd is congruent to K.                      (13)
Since gcd(K,m)=1, all four integers a,b,c,d are units modulo m and hence modulo q.

The integrality of lambda_A and lambda_B gives
 b r_3 congruent to d r_2,  a r_2 congruent to c r_3                (14)
modulo m. Put t congruent to a r_2 modulo m. It is a unit by (13) and hypothesis (ii). Equations (13)-(14) give
 a congruent to t r_2^(-1),
 c congruent to t r_3^(-1),
 b congruent to K r_2 t^(-1),
 d congruent to K r_3 t^(-1)                                      (15)
modulo m. These are exactly the generic torus residues in fact 17557ebe80636618. All four coefficients are even by (i), (12) is its determinant lift equation, and (2) are its three literal carries. Conditions (iv)-(vi) are precisely the sign, gcd, recovered-prime, distinctness, C-unit, nonzero-carry, and carrier conditions in that fact. Hence, for each fixed (r_2,r_3), fact 17557ebe80636618 proves that the tuple is exactly a normalized generic unit state with
 gcd(|b r_3-d r_2|,|a r_2-c r_3|)=2m.                              (16)
The present moving intervals are merely additional selectors inside the absolute coefficient box |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|<=L_0H^3 allowed by that fact; no common positive interval is used.

That fact recovers the signed short coordinate as s lambda_J. Condition (vii) chooses its unique residue u in {0,...,m-1}; then (4) uniquely defines k. Conversely, from (12),
 4m lambda_J=ab-cd=2ab-2K,
and (1) gives lambda_J=su+km/2, so the k in (4) is exactly the k in (1). Thus every state in this fixed sign and conductor sector satisfying the moving interval selectors occurs exactly once in E_outer_gen.

Fix a unit x modulo q. Since |I_a|<q, at most one a in I_a satisfies ax congruent to 1 modulo q. Reducing the first equation in (1) modulo m gives
 n_2 congruent to Kx modulo m.                                     (17)
An interval of cardinality at most L_1m contains at most L_1+1 representatives of one residue modulo m. Once x,a,n_2 are fixed, division of
 (a n_2-K)/m congruent to 2su modulo m
determines the representative 0<=u<m uniquely. The nonzero integer
 c n_1=a n_2-2K                                                    (18)
has absolute value at most L_0^2H^6. Therefore its positive divisors n_1, and hence c, have O_{L_0,A,epsilon}(m^epsilon) possibilities. Here H<=m^A and the elementary divisor estimate tau(N)<<_epsilon N^epsilon proved in fact 212d1415bf03c2a7 are used.

For each resulting even coefficient matrix
 Q=((a,c),(-d,b))=((a,c),(n_1,n_2)),                               (19)
all four entries have absolute value at most L_0H^3 and its determinant is 2K. Fact 1218e64e51ba3131 applies with fixed C,K,Q and shows that the number of all ordered prime pairs (r_2,r_3) satisfying the complete intrinsic normalized-unit conditions is O_{L_0,epsilon}(H^epsilon). Our set is a restriction of that set. Combining this with the preceding paragraph, every x-fibre in (9) has
 O_{L_0,L_1,A,epsilon}(m^epsilon)                                  (20)
tuples, after changing epsilon. This is the first use of the joint carrier-first multiplicity.

Cauchy-Schwarz inside every x-fibre, (5), and (20) give
 sum_x|C_outer(x)|^2
 <=C m^epsilon(log(2H))^(2D)
 sum_{E_outer_gen}|W(u)|^2|alpha(n_1)|^2|beta(n_2)|^2.              (21)
Fix (u,n_1,n_2). The first equation in (1) determines a modulo q. Since |I_a|<q, it gives at most one a in I_a, after which k and c are uniquely determined by (1). Thus Q is fixed. Fact 1218e64e51ba3131 again gives O(H^epsilon) possibilities for the ordered prime pair. Consequently
 sum_{E_outer_gen}|W(u)|^2|alpha(n_1)|^2|beta(n_2)|^2
 <=C H^epsilon||W||_2^2||alpha||_2^2||beta||_2^2.                  (22)
Because H<=m^A, the powers H^epsilon and every fixed power of log(2H) are absorbed into m^epsilon. Equations (21)-(22) prove
 ||C_outer||_2
 <=C m^epsilon||W||_2||alpha||_2||beta||_2.                        (23)
Additive Parseval modulo q proves (11).

Group (6) by the unique x congruent to a^(-1) and periodize F modulo q. This gives exactly
 T_outer_gen=sum_{x modulo q;gcd(x,q)=1}C_outer(x)F_per(x^(-1)).    (24)
Fact 5b9e0311f7e49ea2 applies because F is supported on one interval of cardinality at most L_1m. It yields
 |T_outer_gen|<=C q^(-1/32+epsilon)V_F||C_outer_hat||_2.            (25)
Insert (11) and q=m^2. Since q^(-1/32)q^(1/2)=m^(15/16), this proves (8).

No prime tuple, coefficient matrix, or carrier gate was separated before (25): all were counted only through the two divisor-scale fibre bounds. This proves the asserted carrier-first cost. The final exclusions are literal hypotheses or parameters held fixed throughout the proof, so no estimate for them is implied.

glossary.C_outer: the one-column coefficient formed from E_outer_gen before any tuplewise absolute value
glossary.E_outer_gen: the complete fixed-(m,s,C,K) generic incidence set, with coefficient matrices and every ordered prime pair summed jointly
glossary.Omega_outer: a bounded or fixed-polylogarithmic literal source weight on an admitted outer tuple
glossary.T_outer_gen: the weighted complete generic fixed-fibre sum over E_outer_gen

f26c5b12eea4a623.title: COMPLETE LITERAL STRICT-TOP \(A_X/B_X\) CLEAN-WINDOW PAYMENT WITH ALL OUTER-\(g\) LAYERS. Fix the strict-top selected unmarked source of facts \(b0a38f5e9ae7feb6\) and \(544c7ba4db45c06f\). Thus
f26c5b12eea4a623.author: slava chan
f26c5b12eea4a623.statement:
COMPLETE LITERAL STRICT-TOP \(A_X/B_X\) CLEAN-WINDOW PAYMENT WITH ALL OUTER-\(g\) LAYERS. Fix the strict-top selected unmarked source of facts \(b0a38f5e9ae7feb6\) and \(544c7ba4db45c06f\). Thus
\[
 \beta_m<\beta<6/5,\qquad B=Q^\beta,\qquad
 H_T=B/Q,\qquad H_P=H_T/G,
\]
in either orientation, with exact outer gcd \(g\), actual imbalance \(G>0\), and normalized target
\[
 L_{\rm src}=N/g.
\]
Fix \(0<\tau<1/100\) sufficiently small and put
\[
 a=2\beta-2+\tau,\qquad
 b=3-2\beta-\tau,\qquad
 X=Q^{b-\tau}.                                                   \tag{1}
\]
Apply the exact one-sided identity of fact \(391896a807980083\) only to the restored factor \(\mu(n){\bf1}_{(n,g)=1}\):
\[
 \mu(n)
 =-\sum_{\substack{rw=n\\r\le X}}\mu(r)
  -\sum_{\substack{mt=n\\m>X,\ t>1}}\mu(m).                     \tag{2}
\]

Define the clean \(A_X\) part by
\[
 Q^a\le r\le X,                                                 \tag{3}
\]
and define the clean \(B_X\) part by the following exact disjoint routing:
\[
 \begin{cases}
 Q^a\le m\le Q^b, &\text{with every }t>1,\\
 m>Q^b,\quad Q^a\le t\le Q^b. &
 \end{cases}                                                    \tag{4}
\]
The first line receives a tuple whenever \(m\) lies in the clean window, including when \(t\) does also; the second line receives the remaining clean tuples. Thus there is no joint deletion mask in (4).

Let \({\cal T}_{A_X/B_X,\rm clean}\) be the complete contribution of (3)--(4) to the strict-top unmarked source: include both orientations, every active source/dyadic/fixed-\(U\)/high/smooth-projective row, every actual nonzero frequency and both signs, and every exact \(g\mid N\); at each row recombine all provenance siblings before taking an absolute value. Then there exists a fixed
\[
 \delta_{\rm clean}>0
\]
depending only on the fixed parameter hierarchy such that
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 |{\cal T}_{A_X/B_X,\rm clean}|
 \ll x^{1-\delta_{\rm clean}}.
 \qquad}                                                        \tag{5}
\]

More precisely, on every fixed outer row and every dyadic factor box in (3) or (4), facts \(f7b5ba9fa0d6cfc8\) and \(07bfa46055824600\) give
\[
 H_P^{-1}\sum_{s\asymp Q}|W_s|
 \ll x^{o(1)}\max(1,G)Q^{2-\delta_0}                            \tag{6}
\]
for a fixed \(\delta_0>0\). The match uses the original reciprocal modulus \(s\), the unit \(V_s=1\), the fixed possibly nonunit target
\[
 A=-\epsilon L_{\rm src},
\]
the no-condition-between-factors version of the theorem, and
\[
 ST\asymp B=QH_T,\qquad
 H_T^2Q^\tau=Q^a,\qquad
 Q^{1-\tau}/H_T^2=Q^b.                                        \tag{7}
\]
The full-frequency projective coefficient mass, including the dyadic factor boxes, is \(x^{o(1)}\) by fact \(544c7ba4db45c06f\).

The exact complement of (3)--(4) inside (2) is
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 A_X{\rm\ Type\!-\!I}:&\quad r<Q^a,\\
 {\rm ULTRA\hbox{-}LONG\hbox{-}MU\hbox{-}N}:&
 \quad m>Q^b,\quad1<t<Q^a,\\
 {\rm ENDPOINT\hbox{-}DIAGONAL\hbox{-}N}:&
 \quad m>Q^b,\quad t>Q^b .
 \end{aligned}}                                                \tag{8}
\]
There is no further class.

Fact \(9ea2dddfbbbd191a\) is not invoked in this payment. Its joint fourth-energy conclusion is compatible with the bounded-variation \(h\)-slot of fact \(544c7ba4db45c06f\), but the full-frequency reciprocal-energy theorem \(f7b5ba9fa0d6cfc8\) already supplies (6) directly and requires only the separated divisor-bounded arrays.

This theorem pays no class in (8), no critical \(\beta\ge6/5\) source, and no Goldbach conclusion.
f26c5b12eea4a623.proof:
We first prove the fixed-row analytic match. The exact normal form in fact \(b0a38f5e9ae7feb6\) has reciprocal modulus \(s\asymp Q\), coefficient \(\mu(s){\bf1}_{(s,g)=1}\), fixed target \(-\epsilon L_{\rm src}\), and reciprocal phase
\[
 e_s\!\left(-\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\,\overline n\right).
                                                                    \tag{9}
\]
Fact \(391896a807980083\) applies (2) without changing this modulus coefficient or target. In an \(A_X\) row put \(n=rw\); in a \(B_X\) row put \(n=mt\). The gates
\[
 (g,sn)=(s,n)=1
\]
become one-variable auxiliary gates with \(g\), together with
\[
 (rw,s)=1\quad\text{or}\quad(mt,s)=1.                              \tag{10}
\]
There is no condition between \(r,w\), and none between \(m,t\). This is the no-cross-condition coefficient class allowed by fact \(f7b5ba9fa0d6cfc8\).

Fix a signed dyadic frequency block and dyadic boxes for the two factors. Fact \(544c7ba4db45c06f\), using the expansion of fact \(062a7f6f0c58b1f2\), gives the exact separated expansion of
\[
 {H_P\over n}\widehat F^\epsilon_{g,s,n}(\epsilon h/n)
 e\!\left({\epsilon L_{\rm src}h\over sn}\right)                   \tag{11}
\]
into bounded one-variable functions of \(s\), the two factors of \(n\), and \(h\). All provenance siblings have already summed to one. Multiply these functions by \(\mu(s){\bf1}_{(s,g)=1}\), by \(-\mu(r){\bf1}_{(r,g)=1}\) and \({\bf1}_{(w,g)=1}\) in an \(A_X\) row, or by \(-\mu(m){\bf1}_{(m,g)=1}\) and \({\bf1}_{(t,g)=1}\) in a \(B_X\) row. Every resulting one-variable array is bounded by a divisor function. Equation (10) is exactly the theorem's condition \((ST,s)=1\). The remaining phase from (9) is
\[
 e_s(Ah(ST)^{-1}),\qquad A=-\epsilon L_{\rm src},
\]
with \(V_s=1\). No coprimality of \(A\) with \(s\) is required.

For a dyadic block in (3), choose \(S\) to be the \(r\)-scale and \(T\) the \(w\)-scale. Since \(X<Q^b\), (3) gives
\[
 Q^a\le S\le Q^b.
\]
For the first line of (4), choose \(S\) to be the \(m\)-scale; for the second line choose \(S\) to be the \(t\)-scale. Again \(Q^a\le S\le Q^b\). In every case the source support \(B/2\le n\le2B\) gives
\[
 ST\asymp B=QH_T.
\]
The definitions in (1) give the two equalities in (7), so this is exactly the clean window of fact \(f7b5ba9fa0d6cfc8\).

If \(H_P\ge1\), that fact bounds the four terms, after the clean-window inequalities, by
\[
 G^{1/4}Q^{2-\tau/4},\qquad
 G^{1/4}Q^{2-\tau/4},\qquad
 Q^{2-\tau/2},\qquad
 Q^{7/4}H_T.                                                     \tag{12}
\]
Since \(\beta<6/5\),
\[
 Q^{7/4}H_T=Q^{\beta+3/4}<Q^{2-1/20}.                            \tag{13}
\]
Also \(G^{1/4}\le\max(1,G)\). After choosing the internal epsilon sufficiently small, (12)--(13) give (6). If \(0<H_P<1\), then \(H_T>1\) and \(G>1\); the exact reset fact \(07bfa46055824600\) gives
\[
 GQ^{2-\delta_1}=\max(1,G)Q^{2-\delta_1},
\]
again proving (6).

We account for the coefficient family. On one signed frequency block, fact \(544c7ba4db45c06f\) gives projective coefficient mass
\[
 O_A((\log x)^2(1+F/H_P)^{-A})
\]
for every fixed \(A\). To put a separated mode into the full-frequency hypothesis, choose its frequency array with the required fixed decay exponent and transfer the compensating factor \((1+F/H_P)^{A_0}\) to its projective scalar. Taking \(A>A_0+2\) makes the dyadic \(F\)-sum convergent above \(H_P\), while the blocks below \(H_P\) cost only \(O(\log(2+H_P))\). The two signs and the dyadic factor boxes cost only further powers of \(\log x\). Hence the total projective mass multiplying (6) is \(x^{o(1)}\).

It remains to sum outer rows. The two orientations and the active physical labels have polylogarithmic multiplicity. The target and every source scale are bounded by a fixed power of \(Q\) on the strict top sliver, as verified in the outer-scale audit of fact \(be94f5e014ad4d3d\). The same audit gives a fixed \(c_0>0\) such that
\[
 Q\ge x^{c_0}.                                                     \tag{14}
\]
In the forward orientation \(gGQ^2=DM\asymp x\), and in the reverse orientation \(gGQ^2=RK\asymp x\).

For \(G\ge1\), the right side of (6) is
\[
 GQ^{2-\delta_0}\asymp {x\over g}Q^{-\delta_0}
 \ll {x^{1-c_0\delta_0}\over g}.                                \tag{15}
\]
Summing (15) over \(g\mid N\) costs \(x^{o(1)}\). For \(G<1\), let \(D_{\rm sm}\) be the smaller physical divisor scale, so \(Q=D_{\rm sm}/g\) and \(D_{\rm sm}\ll x^{1/2}\). Then
\[
 \sum_{g\mid N}Q^{2-\delta_0}
 \le D_{\rm sm}^{\,2-\delta_0}
 \sum_{g\mid N}g^{-2+\delta_0}
 \ll x^{1-\delta_0/2+o(1)}.                                    \tag{16}
\]
Equations (15)--(16), after the \(x^{o(1)}\) source/projective taxes, prove (5).

Finally, (3) and \(r<Q^a\) partition the \(A_X\) range because \(r\le X\). Fact \(391896a807980083\) proves that the complement of the clean \(B_X\) tuples is exactly the last two rows of (8). The disjoint routing (4) includes every clean tuple once. This proves the exact complement and all scope statements.

glossary.D_sm: The smaller physical divisor scale: D forward and R reverse.
glossary.cal T_{A_X/B_X,clean}: The complete strict-top unmarked contribution of the clean A_X rows and the disjointly routed clean B_X rows, over both orientations and all exact outer-gcd layers.
glossary.delta_clean: A fixed positive saving exponent for the complete literal clean contribution.

f271bfac142ef5e0.title: SINGLETON NO-FIT FOR FIXED-SUBFACE DENOMINATOR SAVING WITH ARBITRARY COMMON COEFFICIENTS. Let p>2 be prime. Let d_1,d_2 be arbitrary positive squarefree integers coprime to p, and let \((C_i,d_i)=1\). Put
f271bfac142ef5e0.author: slava chan
f271bfac142ef5e0.statement:
SINGLETON NO-FIT FOR FIXED-SUBFACE DENOMINATOR SAVING WITH ARBITRARY COMMON COEFFICIENTS. Let p>2 be prime. Let d_1,d_2 be arbitrary positive squarefree integers coprime to p, and let \((C_i,d_i)=1\). Put
\[
G_1(f,g)={p\over p-1}\left({\bf1}_{f=g}-{1\over p-1}\right)
\qquad(f,g\in\mathbb F_p^\times).
\]
For a finitely supported complex sequence w on the integers define
\[
A_f(w)=\sum_{\substack{x\in\mathbb Z\\(x,pd_1)=1\\x\equiv f\ ({\rm mod}\ p)}}
w_x e_{d_1}(C_1x^{-1}),
\]
\[
B_g(w)=\sum_{\substack{y\in\mathbb Z\\(y,pd_2)=1\\y\equiv g\ ({\rm mod}\ p)}}
\overline{w_y}e_{d_2}(C_2y^{-1}),
\]
and
\[
\mathcal Q(w)=\sum_{f,g\in\mathbb F_p^\times}G_1(f,g)A_f(w)B_g(w). \tag{1}
\]
There exists w with \(\|w\|_2=1\) such that
\[
|\mathcal Q(w)|={p(p-2)\over (p-1)^2}\ge {3\over4}, \tag{2}
\]
independently of d_1,d_2. Consequently there is no uniform estimate
\[
|\mathcal Q(w)|\le \Psi(d_1,d_2)\|w\|_2^2 \tag{3}
\]
for all such data and all finitely supported w if \(\Psi(d_1,d_2)\) tends to zero as either squarefree denominator tends to infinity. In particular, the square-root denominator gain for smooth fibres in fact 6ab529accdede090 cannot be extended to arbitrary common coefficients by a fixed-subface argument alone. This is an abstract theorem-interface no-fit. It is not a lower bound for the varying-(b_1,b_2) literal aggregate of fact b9560e346963b9e0.
f271bfac142ef5e0.proof:
Choose an integer x_0 coprime to pd_1d_2 and let w be the singleton sequence w_{x_0}=1 and w_x=0 for x different from x_0. Put f_0=x_0 modulo p. Then A_f(w) vanishes unless f=f_0, and B_g(w) vanishes unless g=f_0. Their two nonzero values are unit complex numbers:
\[
A_{f_0}(w)=e_{d_1}(C_1x_0^{-1}),\qquad
B_{f_0}(w)=e_{d_2}(C_2x_0^{-1}).
\]
Therefore (1) has exactly one term and
\[
|\mathcal Q(w)|=|G_1(f_0,f_0)|
={p\over p-1}\left(1-{1\over p-1}\right)
={p(p-2)\over(p-1)^2}.
\]
For p at least 3 this quantity is at least 3/4. Also \(\|w\|_2=1\). This proves (2). Since the construction works for every displayed d_1,d_2,C_1,C_2, any function \(\Psi\) satisfying (3) must be at least 3/4 on all such pairs and therefore cannot tend to zero. The scope conclusion follows: the smoothness in fact 6ab529accdede090, or a correlation among varying outer arithmetic data unavailable after freezing one subface, is indispensable.

glossary.A_f(w): The first-row inverse-phase fibre formed from the common sequence w.
glossary.B_g(w): The second-row inverse-phase fibre formed from the conjugate common sequence.
glossary.\\mathcal Q(w): The fixed-subface centered quadratic incidence form.

f3f424d2419a854f.title: Fix an integer m>=2, a real number rho with 0<rho<=1, and continuously differentiable complex functions F and V supported in [1/2,2]. For real X>=3 and D satisfying X^rho<=D<=X, define the center-independent finite sequences a_D(d)=mu(d)F(d/D) for positive integers d and b_X(n)=(1_{n is prime}log(n)-1)V(n/X) for positive integers n, with b_X(n)=0 for n<=0. For every integer center N put C_N(X,D)=sum_{d>=1}a_D(d)b_X(N-md). Then, for every K>0, sum_{N in Z}|C_N(X,D)|^2 <<_{K,rho,m,F,V} X D^2(log X)^(-K). Consequently, for every B>0 and L>0, the number of integer centers N for which |C_N(X,D)|>D(log X)^(-B) is O_{B,L,rho,m,F,V}(X(log X)^(-L)). In particular, if D is bounded below by a fixed positive multiple of X, then outside O_L(X(log X)^(-L)) centers one has C_N(X,D)=O(X(log X)^(-2))=o(X/log X). These conclusions require the same weights a_D and b_X for every center N. They give no estimate for a specified center and no every-bad-N conclusion: without an independent result forcing a hypothetical set of bad centers to be too large for the exceptional set, all bad centers may lie inside it
f3f424d2419a854f.author: slava chan
f3f424d2419a854f.statement: Fix an integer m>=2, a real number rho with 0<rho<=1, and continuously differentiable complex functions F and V supported in [1/2,2]. For real X>=3 and D satisfying X^rho<=D<=X, define the center-independent finite sequences a_D(d)=mu(d)F(d/D) for positive integers d and b_X(n)=(1_{n is prime}log(n)-1)V(n/X) for positive integers n, with b_X(n)=0 for n<=0. For every integer center N put C_N(X,D)=sum_{d>=1}a_D(d)b_X(N-md). Then, for every K>0, sum_{N in Z}|C_N(X,D)|^2 <<_{K,rho,m,F,V} X D^2(log X)^(-K). Consequently, for every B>0 and L>0, the number of integer centers N for which |C_N(X,D)|>D(log X)^(-B) is O_{B,L,rho,m,F,V}(X(log X)^(-L)). In particular, if D is bounded below by a fixed positive multiple of X, then outside O_L(X(log X)^(-L)) centers one has C_N(X,D)=O(X(log X)^(-2))=o(X/log X). These conclusions require the same weights a_D and b_X for every center N. They give no estimate for a specified center and no every-bad-N conclusion: without an independent result forcing a hypothetical set of bad centers to be too large for the exceptional set, all bad centers may lie inside it.
f3f424d2419a854f.proof:
Write e(t)=exp(2 pi i t) and define the finite Fourier sums
A(alpha)=sum_{d>=1}a_D(d)e(md alpha),   B(alpha)=sum_{n in Z}b_X(n)e(n alpha).
The coefficient of e(N alpha) in A(alpha)B(alpha) is exactly
sum_{d>=1}a_D(d)b_X(N-md)=C_N(X,D).
Orthogonality of the functions e(N alpha), N in Z, and Parseval's identity therefore give the exact equality
sum_{N in Z}|C_N(X,D)|^2=int_0^1 |A(alpha)B(alpha)|^2 d alpha.
It follows that
sum_N|C_N(X,D)|^2 <= (sup_{alpha in R}|A(alpha)|)^2 int_0^1|B(alpha)|^2d alpha
=(sup_alpha|A(alpha)|)^2 sum_{n in Z}|b_X(n)|^2.                                             (1)
The center-independence of a_D and b_X is what makes one common product A(alpha)B(alpha) occur in this identity.

We record the external input with its exact relevant slots. Liu and Sarnak [LS13, Lemma 2.1] state that if nu is a positive integer, 0<=l<nu, and phi(u) is a real polynomial of positive degree, then for arbitrary J>0,
sum_{n<=Y, n congruent l modulo nu}mu(n)e(phi(n)) <<_{J,nu} Y(log Y)^(-J),
where the implied constant is independent of every coefficient of phi. Take nu=1 and the linear polynomial phi(n)=beta n. Thus, uniformly for every real beta,
S_beta(Y):=sum_{n<=Y}mu(n)e(beta n) <<_J Y(log Y)^(-J).                                      (2)
The source explicitly attributes the linear case to Davenport. Applying Stieltjes partial summation to (2) on the support D/2<=d<=2D of F(d/D) gives
|sum_d mu(d)F(d/D)e(beta d)|
<<_{J,F} D(log D)^(-J).                                                                      (3)
Indeed the boundary terms are bounded by the supremum norm of F times the maximum of |S_beta(t)| on [D/2,2D], and the integral term is bounded by D^(-1) times the integral over that interval of |S_beta(t)F'(t/D)|dt. Both have the size in (3), uniformly in beta. Taking beta=m alpha proves
sup_alpha|A(alpha)|<<_{J,F}D(log D)^(-J).                                                     (4)
The fact that m is fixed is harmless because (2) is uniform in the linear coefficient.

The sequence b_X is supported on positive integers n with X/2<=n<=2X. On this support,
|1_{n is prime}log(n)-1|<=log(2X)+1.
There are at most 2X such integers, and hence
sum_n|b_X(n)|^2<<_V X(log X)^2.                                                              (5)
Combining (1), (4), and (5) yields
sum_N|C_N(X,D)|^2<<_{J,F,V} XD^2(log D)^(-2J)(log X)^2.
Because D>=X^rho, one has log D>=rho log X. Given K>0, choose J=(K+2)/2. Absorbing the resulting fixed power of rho proves
sum_N|C_N(X,D)|^2<<_{K,rho,m,F,V}XD^2(log X)^(-K).

For the exceptional-set assertion, use the last energy estimate with exponent K=L+2B. If E is the set of centers satisfying |C_N(X,D)|>D(log X)^(-B), then
|E|D^2(log X)^(-2B) < sum_N|C_N(X,D)|^2 << XD^2(log X)^(-L-2B),
so |E|<<X(log X)^(-L). If D>=cX for a fixed c>0, choosing B=2 gives the stated O(X(log X)^(-2)) bound at every nonexceptional center.

Finally, the estimate bounds only the cardinality of E; it does not identify any member or exclude a prescribed integer N from E. It is logically compatible with a hypothetical set of bad Goldbach centers in a dyadic range being a subset of E, even if E has arbitrarily strong logarithmic density zero. Moreover, if a separate weight a_D^{(N)} were selected for each N, the diagonal values would be Fourier coefficients of different products A_N B rather than of one common product, so the displayed Parseval sum would not apply. An independent lower bound for the number of bad centers, or a pointwise theorem uniform in N, is therefore required before this almost-all statement can imply an every-bad-N conclusion.

glossary.A(alpha): the additive Fourier transform of a_D after dilation by m
glossary.B(alpha): the additive Fourier transform of b_X
glossary.C_N(X,D): the affine convolution of a_D and b_X at center N
glossary.E: the exceptional set of centers exceeding the chosen threshold
glossary.a_D: the center-independent dyadic Möbius weight d maps to mu(d)F(d/D)
glossary.rho: the fixed exponent in the lower scale condition D>=X^rho

f41f5f91b52e0d13.title: Let C_2=∏_{p>2}p(p-2)/(p-1)^2, where the product is over primes. For every even integer N=2x define
f41f5f91b52e0d13.author: slava chan
f41f5f91b52e0d13.statement:
Let C_2=∏_{p>2}p(p-2)/(p-1)^2, where the product is over primes. For every even integer N=2x define
𝔠(N)=C_2∏_{p|N,p>2}(p-1)/(p-2),
Q_N=rad(2N),
r_N(n)=1_{gcd(n,Q_N)=1}∏_{p|n,p∤Q_N}(p-1)/(p-2),
and b_N(n)=2𝔠(N)r_N(n).
Fix real numbers 1/2<a<b<1 and a continuously differentiable real function W supported in [a,b]. Define
E_{0,N}=Σ_{n≥1}W(n/x)log(n)(Λ(N-n)-b_N(n)).
Then C_2 is positive, 𝔠(N)≥C_2, and
E_{0,N}=o_W(𝔠(N)x)
as x tends to infinity through values for which N=2x is an even integer. The relative error is uniform in N.
f41f5f91b52e0d13.proof:
The factor p(p-2)/(p-1)^2 equals 1-1/(p-1)^2. Since Σ_{p>2}1/(p-1)^2 converges and every factor is positive, the infinite product C_2 converges to a positive number. Every factor (p-1)/(p-2) in the definition of 𝔠(N) is greater than 1, so 𝔠(N)≥C_2.

We use the following external theorem, stated in the introduction of Shao and Teräväinen, arXiv:2006.05954: for every fixed A>0 and ε>0,
Σ_{q≤y^(1/2-ε)} max_{gcd(c,q)=1}|Σ_{n≤y,n≡c (mod q)}Λ(n)-y/φ(q)| ≪_{A,ε} y/(log y)^A.
Taking the q=1 term gives Σ_{n≤y}Λ(n)=y+O_{A,ε}(y/(log y)^A). Partial summation therefore shows that, for the x-dependent continuously differentiable function F_x(u)=W(u)log(xu),
Σ_{n≥1}W(n/x)log(n)Λ(N-n)=x∫_0^∞F_x(u)du+o_W(x).                    (1)
Indeed, after q=N-n and u=n/x, the prime-number-theorem main integral is x∫W(u)log(xu)du; the derivative of the smooth weight is O_W(log x/x), and choosing A sufficiently large makes the integrated error o_W(x).

We next evaluate the mean of r_N. Define a multiplicative function h_N supported on squarefree integers by
h_N(p)=-1 if p|Q_N, and h_N(p)=1/(p-2) if p∤Q_N.
For every prime power p^j with j≥1, one has 1+h_N(p)=0 when p|Q_N and 1+h_N(p)=(p-1)/(p-2) when p∤Q_N. Hence
r_N(n)=Σ_{d|n}h_N(d).                                                   (2)
The absolutely convergent Euler product of the mean in (2) is
κ_N=Σ_{d≥1}h_N(d)/d
=∏_{p|Q_N}(1-1/p)∏_{p∤Q_N}(1+1/[p(p-2)]).
For p>2, 1+1/[p(p-2)]=(p-1)^2/[p(p-2)]. Since 2|Q_N, separating p=2 and multiplying the local factors gives
κ_N=(1/2)C_2^(-1)∏_{p|N,p>2}[(p-1)/p][p(p-2)/(p-1)^2]
=1/[2C_2]∏_{p|N,p>2}(p-2)/(p-1)=1/[2𝔠(N)].                    (3)

We justify uniformly replacing the finite divisor sum in (2) by the Euler product (3). For σ=3/4,
Σ_{d≥1}|h_N(d)|/d^σ
=∏_{p|Q_N}(1+p^(-σ))∏_{p∤Q_N}(1+1/[(p-2)p^σ]).
The second product is bounded by an absolute constant because 1/(p-2)≤3/p for p≥3 and Σ_p p^(-7/4) converges. If p_1<...<p_k are the distinct prime divisors of Q_N, then p_j≥j+1, so Σ_{p|Q_N}p^(-3/4)≤Σ_{j≤k}j^(-3/4)=O(k^(1/4)). Also 2^k≤Q_N≤2N, hence k=O(log N). Therefore the first product is exp(O((log N)^(1/4)))=N^{o(1)}, uniformly in N. It follows that
Σ_{d>x}|h_N(d)|/d≤x^(-1/4)N^{o(1)}=x^(-1/4+o(1)).              (4)
Furthermore,
Σ_{d≤x}|h_N(d)|≤2^{ω(Q_N)}∏_{3≤p≤x}(1+1/(p-2))=x^{o(1)}(log x)^{O(1)}=x^{o(1)}.       (5)
Here 2^{ω(Q_N)}=N^{o(1)}, and the last Euler product is polylogarithmic because 1/(p-2)≤3/p and Σ_{p≤x}1/p=O(log log x).

Insert (2) into the weighted sum and interchange the finite sums:
Σ_{n≥1}r_N(n)F_x(n/x)=Σ_d h_N(d)Σ_m F_x(dm/x).
A Riemann-sum estimate for the fixed compact support and continuously differentiable W gives
Σ_m F_x(dm/x)=(x/d)∫_0^∞F_x(u)du+O_W(log x).
Using (4) to replace the truncated main coefficient by κ_N, and (5) for the total Riemann-sum error, yields
Σ_{n≥1}r_N(n)W(n/x)log n=κ_N x∫_0^∞F_x(u)du+o_W(x).             (6)
All estimates in (4)-(6) are uniform in N. Multiplying (6) by 2𝔠(N) and using (3) gives
Σ_{n≥1}b_N(n)W(n/x)log n=x∫_0^∞F_x(u)du+o_W(𝔠(N)x).             (7)
Subtracting (7) from (1), and using 𝔠(N)≥C_2>0 to absorb o_W(x) into o_W(𝔠(N)x), proves the result.

glossary.E_{0,N}: the logarithmic shallow discrepancy defined in the statement
glossary.W: a continuously differentiable real weight supported in [a,b]
glossary.h_N: the squarefree-supported convolution coefficient introduced in the proof
glossary.r_N(n): the local-density multiplicative weight defined in the statement
glossary.κ_N: the mean Euler product Σ h_N(d)/d
glossary.𝔠(N): the Goldbach singular factor defined in the statement

f439118e1e8818a1.title: EXACT LITERAL COEFFICIENT-ONE FULL-DENOMINATOR SHORT-ROW SUPPLIER AND ITS DIRECT FIXED-BLOCK EXCESS. Fix 0<eta<1/12, 0<delta<4eta, and 0<theta<1/2. Let Q tend to infinity and put U=Q^(1/3), B=Q^(4/3+o(1)), F_0=Q^(1-2eta+o(1)), and A_P=Q^(1+delta)/P^2. Let P be a dyadic shared-prime scale occurring in the literal medium range of fact 55c6f91ec7fd414f, so Q^(1/3+2eta+o(1))<=P<=Q^(1/2+theta), and assume A_P>1. Let N be a fixed positive integer. Let cal B be the squarefree integers b in [B,2B), put L_b=product_{r|b,b/r<F_0}r, let cal R={b in cal B:L_b>1,(L_b,N)=1}, define pi(b) as the largest prime divisor of L_b, and put s(b)=b/pi(b). Let gamma_b be complex numbers with sum_{b in cal R}|gamma_b|^2<=1. For primes p in [P,2P) define S_p={s:ps in cal R,pi(ps)=p} and Q_p={q:pq in cal R,p|s(pq)}
f439118e1e8818a1.author: slava chan
f439118e1e8818a1.statement:
EXACT LITERAL COEFFICIENT-ONE FULL-DENOMINATOR SHORT-ROW SUPPLIER AND ITS DIRECT FIXED-BLOCK EXCESS. Fix 0<eta<1/12, 0<delta<4eta, and 0<theta<1/2. Let Q tend to infinity and put U=Q^(1/3), B=Q^(4/3+o(1)), F_0=Q^(1-2eta+o(1)), and A_P=Q^(1+delta)/P^2. Let P be a dyadic shared-prime scale occurring in the literal medium range of fact 55c6f91ec7fd414f, so Q^(1/3+2eta+o(1))<=P<=Q^(1/2+theta), and assume A_P>1. Let N be a fixed positive integer. Let cal B be the squarefree integers b in [B,2B), put L_b=product_{r|b,b/r<F_0}r, let cal R={b in cal B:L_b>1,(L_b,N)=1}, define pi(b) as the largest prime divisor of L_b, and put s(b)=b/pi(b). Let gamma_b be complex numbers with sum_{b in cal R}|gamma_b|^2<=1. For primes p in [P,2P) define S_p={s:ps in cal R,pi(ps)=p} and Q_p={q:pq in cal R,p|s(pq)}.
Let w_n be supported on Q<=n<2Q and satisfy |w_n|<=Q^epsilon for every epsilon>0. Define the literal Vaughan rows, by zero extension off Q<=au<2Q, by beta_{ss,a}(u)=mu(a)w_{au}sum_{m|u,m<=U}mu(m) for 1<=a<=U and beta_{ll,a}(u)=w_{au}sum_{dm=u,U<d<=m}varkappa(d,m)mu(d)mu(m) for 1<=a<2U, where varkappa(d,m)=1 if d=m and 2 if d<m. Put U_a={u in Z:Q<=au<2Q}.
For s in S_p with (s,N)=1 define M_1 modulo s by pM_1 congruent to N modulo s. For q in Q_p with q<=F_0 and (q,N)=1 define M_12 modulo q by pM_12 congruent to N modulo q. Define E_full(P) to be the sum over p,tau,a,s,q,u_1,u_2 subject to p in [P,2P), tau in {ss,ll} with its displayed a-range, s in S_p, q in Q_p, (s,N)=(q,N)=1, q<=F_0, (s,q)<A_P, u_i in U_a, and (au_1,ps)=(au_2,pq)=1, of
conjugate(gamma_{ps})gamma_{pq} beta_{tau,a}(u_1)conjugate(beta_{tau,a}(u_2)) e_s(M_1(au_1)^(-1)) e_q(-M_12(au_2)^(-1))
 times p/(p-1){1_{u_1s congruent to u_2q (mod p)}-1/(p-1)}. (1)
All inverses are taken in the displayed coprime modulus. Define X^full_{p,tau,a,s}(f) and Y^full_{p,tau,a,q}(g) by the two corresponding u-sums in (1), including respectively conjugate(gamma_{ps}) and gamma_{pq}, over u congruent to f and g modulo p. With the Fourier convention of fact 674a62f128f05a44, form lambda^full_{p,tau,a,c}(chi) from these rows by restricting (s,q)<A_P and sq^(-1)=c modulo p, and put Lambda^full_{p,tau,a}(chi)=sum_c chi(c)lambda^full_{p,tau,a,c}(chi). Then exactly
E_full(P)=sum_{p,tau,a} p/(p-1)^2 sum_{chi nonprincipal mod p}Lambda^full_{p,tau,a}(chi). (2)
Moreover, direct fixed-block completion and Cauchy give
|E_full(P)|<<Q^(epsilon+o(1))B^2Q/P^2=Q^(11/3+epsilon+o(1))/P^2. (3)
In the tensors of fact 8d3b2d43277f6d33, (1) is exactly the additive subface h_1=d_1=s of C_{p,s} and h_2=d_2=q of J_{p,q}, on the displayed unit and q<=F_0 range. Both subface coefficients are one. Since pd_1=ps and pd_2=pq belong to [B,2B) while #U_a<=Q/a+1, both rows are short by the fixed power Q/B=Q^(-1/3+o(1)); fact 2775909b4db4ae24 applies to none of these terms. In the exact residual ledger of fact 55c6f91ec7fd414f, the row-one complementary divisor is e=h_1/d_1=1<A_P, so the portion of (1) with a<A_P is contained in that fact's unpaid region a<A_P,e<A_P.
Relative to the desired Q^(7/3-omega) scale, (3) has excess factor Q^(4/3+omega+o(1))/P^2. Since A_P>1 gives P^2<Q^(1+delta), and delta<4eta<1/3, this direct bound misses by a fixed positive power. The exact fixed-block norm in fact 1a9ce3acae020cb8 shows that the two primitive inverse phases do not improve a frozen edge operator norm. These are an exact possibly-empty supplier identification and a no-fit for direct fixed-block completion. They are not a lower bound for the assembled literal sum and do not rule out cancellation across p,s,q,characters,or the signed Vaughan labels.
f439118e1e8818a1.proof:
For each displayed s, (p,s)=1 and pM_1 congruent to N modulo s, so (M_1,s)=1 exactly when (N,s)=1. The analogous assertion holds for M_12 and q. Thus every inverse in (1) is defined.
Fix p,tau,a,s,q. On the unit support, a is a unit modulo ps and pq, and therefore e_s(M_1(au_1)^(-1))=e_s((M_1a^(-1))u_1^(-1)) and e_q(-M_12(au_2)^(-1))=e_q((-M_12a^(-1))u_2^(-1)). (4) The two coefficients in parentheses are units in their displayed squarefree moduli. The final factor of (1) is the centered slope kernel G_{sq^(-1)}(u_1 mod p,u_2 mod p) of fact 674a62f128f05a44. Since A_P>1, that fact applies with G=A_P to the rows X^full,Y^full and proves (2), retaining the character-dependent slope weights and the strict gcd cutoff.
For the bound, fact 1a9ce3acae020cb8 applies to the fixed block (4), with d_1=s,d_2=q,c=sq^(-1) modulo p and interval cardinalities at most Q/a+1. Its equation (7), after absorbing the pointwise beta bound and the unit deletions, gives
|B_{p,a,s,q}|<<Q^(epsilon+o(1))(Q/a+1)sqrt(sq) product_{i=1}^2(1+(Q/a+1)/(pd_i))^(1/2). (5)
Here ps,pq are in [B,2B), so sqrt(sq)<=2B/P and each ratio in the product is O(Q/B)=Q^(-1/3+o(1)). Hence |B_{p,a,s,q}|<<Q^(epsilon+o(1))(Q/a+1)B/P. (6)
For i=1,2 let g_i(p)^2 be the gamma square mass on the corresponding p-block. Counting multiples of p gives at most 3B/p members of each block, so Cauchy's inequality gives sum_{s in S_p,q in Q_p}|gamma_{ps}gamma_{pq}|<=3B g_1(p)g_2(p)/p. (7) The first-row blocks are disjoint. In the literal incidence range every row-two b belongs to Q^o(1) relevant p-blocks, as established in facts a4c3df18327fbfb1 and 39071136bb037885. Thus sum_p g_1(p)^2<=1, sum_p g_2(p)^2<=Q^o(1), and summing (7) over p gives total outer absolute mass at most Q^o(1)B/P. The restrictions q<=F_0 and (s,q)<A_P only decrease it. Finally sum_{a<=2U}(Q/a+1)<<Qlog Q+U=Q^(1+o(1)). Multiplying this with (6)--(7) and the two tau labels proves (3).
For the exact literal face, equation (12) of fact 8d3b2d43277f6d33 permits h_1=s because ps>=B>F_0, so s>F_0/p; under (s,N)=1 its parent unit condition holds. Choosing d_1=h_1=s makes both totient denominators one and c_{s/h_1}=c_1=1, leaving the first phase in (1). Equation (13) of that fact permits h_2=q because pq>=B>F_0 gives q>F_0/p, while q<=F_0 is imposed; under (q,N)=1 its parent unit condition holds. Choosing d_2=h_2=q again has coefficient one, and conjugating row two gives the negative phase in (1). This proves the exact subface identification. The inequalities pd_i>=B prove the shortness claim. Finally, all eta,delta,theta,P and literal-array hypotheses of fact 55c6f91ec7fd414f are now in force; its residual coordinates are a<A_P and e<A_P, while this face has e=1. The exponent comparison follows from B=Q^(4/3+o(1)), A_P>1, and delta<4eta<1/3. The exact fixed-edge norm and the scope restrictions are those of fact 1a9ce3acae020cb8.

glossary.A_P: The literal medium-P residual cutoff Q^(1+delta)/P^2.
glossary.B_{p,a,s,q}: One frozen full-denominator centered bilinear block.
glossary.E_full(P): The literal coefficient-one full-parent/full-denominator subface aggregate.
glossary.Lambda^full: The nonprincipal character-dependent slope transform of the full-denominator face.
glossary.X^full_{p,tau,a,s}: The first literal row restricted to h_1=d_1=s.
glossary.Y^full_{p,tau,a,q}: The second literal row restricted to h_2=d_2=q.
glossary.g_i(p): The restricted gamma l2 mass in row i at shared prime p.
glossary.lambda^full: The slope weight formed from the two full-denominator row Fourier transforms.

f5b31dd3643732ac.title: Assume the hypotheses and notation of fact aa34b1862b993377. Let J_term consist of the ten labels
f5b31dd3643732ac.author: slava chan
f5b31dd3643732ac.statement:
Assume the hypotheses and notation of fact aa34b1862b993377. Let J_term consist of the ten labels
(F,1x1),(F,2x1),(F,2x2),(F,asymmetric),(R,1x1),(R,2x1),(R,2x2),(R,asymmetric),gap,sup.
For j in J_term let T_{N,j} be the real signed sum of the original incidence weight w(z) over the corresponding terminal piece: the first eight labels mean the forward or reverse endpoint-anatomy pieces of that fact, gap means its endpoint gap piece, and sup means its supercritical cell Z_sup. Then
T_N=sum_{j in J_term}T_{N,j}.
If H_N<0, A_N^*=-H_N>0, 0<theta_N<=1, and rho_N is real, then the deficit hypothesis
C_N+U_{T,N}>=-(1-theta_N)A_N^*-rho_N
implies
min_{j in J_term}T_{N,j}<=-theta_N A_N^*/10+rho_N/10.
In particular, along a sequence for which rho_N=o(theta_N A_N^*), at least one terminal component j_N satisfies
T_{N,j_N}<=-theta_N A_N^*/10+o(theta_N A_N^*).

Every T_{N,j} retains the full fixed-N incidence weight, both Möbius signs, smooth labels, and every incidence-dependent auxiliary coefficient permitted in fact aa34b1862b993377. In particular, its incidences retain their unique parent-cell label from fact 91db48815d136d4c and may carry the centered primitive-conductor provenance of fact 676c6a2cb3ebf7cc. Consequently, suppose for one selected component j an exact literal transform has additionally been proved which writes
T_{N,j}=R_j+Re(V_j),
where R_j is real and V_j has a literal primitive-conductor leaf reconstruction satisfying the hypotheses and notation of fact 4a9a213a428b7e8c, with first-stage coefficient norm A_j and coordinate moment M_j. Then
(-T_{N,j})_+<=A_j M_j^{1/2}+|R_j|.
If M_j<=b_j E_j^{1/2}+R_{2,j} with nonnegative b_j,E_j,R_{2,j}, then for every c_j>0,
(-T_{N,j})_+<=c_jE_j^{1/2}+A_j^2b_j/(4c_j)+A_jR_{2,j}^{1/2}+|R_j|.
If the four-prime support-disjoint part of that leaf reconstruction is stored through the full sixteen-face orthogonal direct sum, fact 697d75223ebc7a8a shows that face duplication multiplies its coefficient norm by at most four.

Thus the passage from the exact terminal deficit to one terminal anatomy/supercritical component and then through all four-prime Ursell faces has only the absolute selection factor ten and coefficient factor four. It creates no power of the scale parameter. This is a conditional source-to-Hilbert interface: it does not prove the deficit hypothesis, the component-specific literal primitive-conductor transform, the moment-to-energy estimate, the cross-cell PAVG26/PAVG27 input, or Goldbach.
f5b31dd3643732ac.proof:
Fact aa34b1862b993377 proves that its nine endpoint pieces are pairwise disjoint and sum to E0_N, and that T_N=E0_N+S_N. The set J_term lists those nine pieces and the supercritical piece S_N, so it has ten elements and its component sums add exactly to T_N.

The same fact proves that the displayed deficit hypothesis is equivalent to
T_N<=-theta_N A_N^*+rho_N.
For ten real numbers, the minimum is at most their arithmetic mean. Therefore
min_{j in J_term}T_{N,j}<=T_N/10<=-theta_N A_N^*/10+rho_N/10.
If rho_N=o(theta_N A_N^*), division by the fixed number ten preserves the little-o relation and gives the asymptotic conclusion.

Fact aa34b1862b993377 also proves that each refined component is formed by multiplying the original labelled-incidence weight by a zero-one selector and that arbitrary incidence-dependent auxiliary coefficients remain attached. Its proof explicitly invokes the parent-cell provenance of fact 91db48815d136d4c and the centered-conductor provenance of fact 676c6a2cb3ebf7cc. Hence those labels can be retained inside every one of the ten terminal components.

Now assume the additional component-specific literal transform in the statement. This is exactly the first-stage situation of fact 4a9a213a428b7e8c with Q specialized to T_{N,j}, R specialized to R_j, and its primitive-conductor leaf sum specialized to V_j. That fact gives
(-T_{N,j})_+<=A_jM_j^{1/2}+|R_j|.
Under the displayed second-stage moment hypothesis, its nested Cauchy-Young conclusion gives the inequality with arbitrary c_j. Finally fact 697d75223ebc7a8a proves that duplicating a four-prime base coefficient over the unrestricted and fifteen overlap faces changes its Hilbert norm by at most four. Combining these exact statements proves the coefficient-tax assertion.

The first paragraph used only an exact partition and the arithmetic-mean inequality. The later Hilbert conclusions were explicitly conditional on a transform and moment bound not supplied by the predecessor facts. Therefore none of the missing analytic inputs in the final scope sentence has been inferred.

glossary.A_j: The first-stage Hilbert coefficient norm for component j.
glossary.E_j: The nonnegative terminal energy for component j.
glossary.J_term: The ten terminal-component labels consisting of eight oriented endpoint anatomies, the endpoint gap, and the supercritical component.
glossary.M_j: The first-stage coordinate moment for component j.
glossary.R_j: The real remainder in a component-specific literal transform.
glossary.R_{2,j}: The nonnegative remainder in the component's second-stage moment bound.
glossary.T_{N,j}: The signed fixed-N incidence sum over terminal component j.
glossary.V_j: The primitive-conductor leaf sum in a component-specific literal transform.
glossary.b_j: The nonnegative coefficient in the component's second-stage moment bound.
glossary.c_j: A positive Young-inequality coefficient chosen for component j.
glossary.j_N: A terminal component selected along an asymptotic sequence.

f6871c593f8f6f35.title: Fix real numbers A>0 and C>=0. There exists B_init=B_init(A,C)>0 such that the following holds as x tends to infinity through values for which N=2x is an integer. Put Q_init=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B_init). For every positive integer q<=Q_init let F_q be a continuously differentiable complex function on [2,x] satisfying
f6871c593f8f6f35.author: slava chan
f6871c593f8f6f35.statement:
Fix real numbers A>0 and C>=0. There exists B_init=B_init(A,C)>0 such that the following holds as x tends to infinity through values for which N=2x is an integer. Put Q_init=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B_init). For every positive integer q<=Q_init let F_q be a continuously differentiable complex function on [2,x] satisfying
2 sup_{2<=t<=x}|F_q(t)|+integral_2^x|F_q'(t)|dt <=(log x)^C.
Let D_*>0, let psi_cut be real with 0<=psi_cut<=1, let Phi be the nonnegative dyadic partition from fact 3ef233e014331fc3, and for a positive dyadic D define
lambda_D(q)=mu(q)psi_cut(q/D_*)Phi(q/D).
Assume 2D<=Q_init and define
P_raw=sum_{q<=Q_init}lambda_D(q) sum_{2<=n<=x, n congruent N modulo q}Lambda(n)F_q(n).
Then
P_raw=sum_{q<=Q_init, gcd(q,N)=1}[lambda_D(q)/phi(q)]integral_2^xF_q(t)dt +O_{A,C}(x(log x)^(-A)),
uniformly in the integer N=2x, the positive number D_*, the cutoff psi_cut, the dyadic D, and the allowed family F_q. Thus below the classical modulus level the complete raw weighted prime-progression sum has only the coprime density main term; the remaining unresolved raw range consists of dyadic supports with 2D>Q_init.
f6871c593f8f6f35.proof:
Apply fact 052064336e86e65c with target exponent A+2 and the same C, and let B_init be the exponent B_BV furnished there. Since 0<=Phi<=1 by fact 3ef233e014331fc3, one has |lambda_D(q)|<=1. The support condition 2D<=Q_init places the complete support of Phi(q/D) below Q_init. Fact 052064336e86e65c therefore gives
sum_{q<=Q_init, gcd(q,N)=1}lambda_D(q) sum_{2<=n<=x, n congruent N modulo q}Lambda(n)F_q(n)
=sum_{q<=Q_init, gcd(q,N)=1}[lambda_D(q)/phi(q)]integral_2^xF_q(t)dt
+O_{A,C}(x(log x)^(-A-2)).
