It remains to bound the noncoprime part
S_nc=sum_{q<=Q_init, gcd(q,N)>1}lambda_D(q) sum_{2<=n<=x, n congruent N modulo q}Lambda(n)F_q(n).

A nonzero lambda_D(q) has mu(q) nonzero, so q is squarefree. If a summand in S_nc has Lambda(n) nonzero, write n=p^j for a prime p and an integer j>=1. Choose a prime r dividing gcd(q,N). The congruence n congruent N modulo q gives r|(N-n), while r|N, so r|n=p^j. Hence r=p and in particular p|N.

For each prime p|N there are at most log_2 x exponents j with p^j<=x. Since N=2x and p^j<=x, the integer N-p^j is nonzero. Every modulus q occurring with this p^j divides N-p^j, so there are at most tau(|N-p^j|) choices for q.

We use the standard elementary divisor bound tau(m)<<_epsilon m^epsilon for every fixed epsilon>0. To recall a proof, write m=product_l l^(a_l). For all sufficiently large primes l, the inequality a+1<=l^(epsilon a) holds for every a>=1. For each of the finitely many remaining primes, (a+1)l^(-epsilon a) is bounded uniformly in a. Multiplication over the prime factors gives tau(m)<=C_epsilon m^epsilon.

There are at most log_2 N distinct prime divisors p of N. Also |F_q(n)|<=(log x)^C and Lambda(p^j)=log p<=log x. Since |N-p^j|<=N<=2x, the preceding count gives, for every fixed epsilon>0,
|S_nc|<<_{C,epsilon}x^epsilon(log x)^(C+3).
Taking epsilon=1/4, this is O_{A,C}(x(log x)^(-A)) for all sufficiently large x. Combining it with the coprime formula proves the displayed asymptotic. The final range description is exactly the support condition used in the proof.

glossary.B_init: the classical logarithmic level exponent chosen for the complete initial-slice formula
glossary.P_raw: the complete raw-weighted prime progression sum defined in the statement
glossary.Q_init: the classical modulus level x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B_init)
glossary.S_nc: the portion of P_raw on moduli q with gcd(q,N)>1

f6f2a56af7b391c8.title: ACTUAL C1,C2,C3,C4 FULL SCALAR REPEATED-POLE OCCUPANCY IN ONE LONG NATURAL COFACTOR CHAMBER
f6f2a56af7b391c8.author: slava chan
f6f2a56af7b391c8.statement:
ACTUAL C1,C2,C3,C4 FULL SCALAR REPEATED-POLE OCCUPANCY IN ONE LONG NATURAL COFACTOR CHAMBER.

Adopt the selected first-nonresonant-prime setting of fact 9a34f6ae3a1ceca8 for one actual top C1, C2, C3, or C4 row. Fix a selected prime p and positive integers H,T such that the natural dyadic cofactor interval
  T <= t=n/p < 2T
is contained in the exact range J_p of fact ec8a0fbdab03cda6, and assume, for a fixed 0<delta<1,
  2H<p,  2T<p,  H,T>=p^delta.                                    (1)
Each physical nonzero height h may lie in either signed interval
  H<=h<2H  or  -2H<h<=-H.                                       (2)
Let X_p be the set of nonzero residues modulo p represented by a physical q in [Q,2Q), and put
  R_{p,Q}=#X_p<=min(p-1,Q+1).                                   (3)

Give the four TT-star positions signs sigma_1=sigma_2=+1 and sigma_3=sigma_4=-1. Let O_{p,C_j}^{rep} be any scalar absolute source-weighted suboccupancy of ordered four-row tuples satisfying the following conditions:
(i) the equality partition of the four physical q-residues modulo p has no singleton;
(ii) on every equal-residue block B,
  sum_{i in B} sigma_i h_i/t_i=0 mod p;                          (4)
(iii) each scalar coefficient is a literal Cj marker-copy coefficient, and every literal source, selected-first-prime, pair-deletion, and tuple mask is retained before absolute domination.
Thus O_{p,C_j}^{rep} is the union of the all-four-equal residue stratum and the three two-pair residue partitions.

Fix A>=2 and epsilon_0>0. For every
  0<eta<min(1,4delta)
and
  0<rho<min(eta,2delta),                                        (5)
one has, for all sufficiently large p,
  O_{p,C_j}^{rep}
  <<_{A,delta,eta,rho,epsilon_0}
  Q^(4epsilon_0)(1+Q/p)^4(1+H/H_P)^(-4A)
  R_{p,Q}^2(HT)^4 p^(-rho).                                    (6)
More precisely, before using T>=p^delta, the all-four block and all three two-pair blocks together are bounded by
  Q^(4epsilon_0)(1+Q/p)^4(1+H/H_P)^(-4A)
  {R_{p,Q}(HT)^4p^(-eta)+3R_{p,Q}^2H^4T^2}.                    (7)
Every physical-height sign sector is included, and no height-l1 tax occurs on the all-four block.

This theorem pays all four rank-one repeated-pole equality partitions at the scalar absolute-source level for actual C1-C4 coefficients in the long natural chamber (1). It does not construct a common-X completion for unequal q-residues on the nonexceptional locus, dominate a remaining-face vector or Hilbert norm by the scalar coefficient majorant, sum varying selected primes or composite remaining faces, pay short blocks or zero local heights outside (1), cover Top B, or prove a complete trace or Goldbach estimate.
f6f2a56af7b391c8.proof:
For a physical residue x in X_p and a supported signed height h and cofactor t, aggregate the absolute values of all literal source-copy coefficients into A_{p,x}(h,t). The coefficient argument in facts 9a34f6ae3a1ceca8 and 3286b0e75a3ea94a gives uniformly
  A_{p,x}(h,t)
  <<_{A,epsilon_0}
  Q^epsilon_0(1+Q/p)(1+|h|/H_P)^(-A)
  <<Q^epsilon_0(1+Q/p)(1+H/H_P)^(-A).                          (8)
The factor 1+Q/p includes all physical integers q in [Q,2Q) in the residue x and their literal scalar source copies. All tuple masks lie between zero and one, so after taking the nonnegative absolute coefficient product they may be dropped for an upper bound, without losing their validity before domination.

By fact 549328a9f587f158, there are exactly four equality partitions with no singleton: one four-element block and three partitions into two two-element blocks. We estimate them separately.

For the one-block partition all four q-residues equal one x. Its block equation (4) is
  h_1/t_1+h_2/t_2=h_3/t_3+h_4/t_4 mod p.                       (9)
Fact 9a34f6ae3a1ceca8 applies to every independent choice of the four physical-height signs, with the literal coefficient domination (8), and already sums the sixteen choices into its all-sign occupancy. Summing its estimate over x in X_p gives
  O_p^{one}
  <<Q^(4epsilon_0)(1+Q/p)^4(1+H/H_P)^(-4A)
    R_{p,Q}(HT)^4p^(-eta).                                     (10)

Now fix one of the three two-block partitions and one of its two-element blocks {i,j}, whose common physical q-residue is x. Its equation (4) is
  sigma_i h_i/t_i+sigma_j h_j/t_j=0 mod p.                     (11)
All h_i,h_j,t_i,t_j are nonzero modulo p by (1)-(2). Once h_i,h_j and t_i are fixed, multiplying (11) by t_it_j shows that t_j is uniquely determined as a residue modulo p. Because the integer interval [T,2T) has cardinality T and length T<p, reduction modulo p is injective, so at most one supported integer t_j realizes that residue. There are fewer than 2H choices for each signed-height union and T choices for t_i. Using (8), the total scalar absolute occupancy of this two-row block at x is therefore
  <<Q^(2epsilon_0)(1+Q/p)^2(1+H/H_P)^(-2A)H^2T.                (12)
The two blocks of an exact two-pair partition have distinct residues. Dropping distinctness and all masks only enlarges the nonnegative sum, so multiplying two copies of (12) and summing their residue labels gives at most
  <<Q^(4epsilon_0)(1+Q/p)^4(1+H/H_P)^(-4A)
    R_{p,Q}^2H^4T^2.                                           (13)
There are three two-pair partitions. Adding (10) and three copies of (13) proves (7).

If R_{p,Q}=0, both sides of (6) vanish. Otherwise R_{p,Q}<=R_{p,Q}^2. Relative to the baseline
  R_{p,Q}^2(HT)^4,
the two terms in braces in (7) are at most p^(-eta) and 3T^(-2), respectively. By T>=p^delta, the latter is at most 3p^(-2delta). For any rho satisfying (5), their sum is O_{delta,eta,rho}(p^(-rho)) for sufficiently large p. This proves (6). The argument uses only scalar absolute source masses and therefore proves exactly the stated exclusions.

glossary.O_{p,C_j}^{rep}: The scalar absolute-source occupancy of all no-singleton repeated-pole residue partitions for one actual Cj row at selected prime p.
glossary.R_{p,Q}: The number of nonzero physical q-residues modulo p represented by integers q in [Q,2Q).

f702d90f3491c7c0.title: DISJOINT MULTISCALE EXTENSION OF THE SYMMETRIC LARGE-FACTOR HC-MED PAYMENT. Fix A>0, set K=2, and choose C=C(A,2)>0 sufficiently large for fact e3c0786d33d7e576. Adopt one literal row and all notation and hypotheses (1)-(2) of fact cbbc7f1404df765c. Thus
f702d90f3491c7c0.author: slava chan
f702d90f3491c7c0.statement:
DISJOINT MULTISCALE EXTENSION OF THE SYMMETRIC LARGE-FACTOR HC-MED PAYMENT. Fix A>0, set K=2, and choose C=C(A,2)>0 sufficiently large for fact e3c0786d33d7e576. Adopt one literal row and all notation and hypotheses (1)-(2) of fact cbbc7f1404df765c. Thus
Q_c=X^(1/2+delta_h), delta_h>=0,
0<eta<=1/4, eta<=3/20+6delta_h,                                 (1)
and the HC-MED support is
d<=m, X^eta<=d<=X^(1/4+eta), X<=dm<2X.                           (2)
Let J>=1. For 1<=j<=J let
cal P_j={p prime:P_j<=p<2P_j}                                   (3)
be pairwise disjoint, and assume every P_j satisfies
X^(2/5+6delta_h)(log X)^(2C)<=P_j
 <=X^(1/2-3delta_h)(log X)^(-C).                                (4)
For a positive integer n define
omega_j(n)=#{p in cal P_j:p|n},
R_1(n)=1,qquad
R_j(n)=1_{omega_i(n)=0 for every 1<=i<j} quad (j>=2).           (5)

For each j, let cal S_elig,j and N_box,j be the eligible literal modulus set and number of canonical P_j-admissible factor boxes defined in fact cbbc7f1404df765c, using the same X,Q_c,A,C. Define three support sectors:
MS-ELIG consists of the pairs (s,m) for which j is the least index with omega_j(m)>0 and s belongs to cal S_elig,j;
MS-FIRST-NOSCALE consists of the pairs (s,m) for which j is the least index with omega_j(m)>0 and s does not belong to cal S_elig,j;
MS-UNMARK consists of the pairs (s,m) for which omega_j(m)=0 for every 1<=j<=J.              (6)
Then (6) is a disjoint exhaustive partition of the complete literal HC-MED row (2).

For each j, restrict the symmetric large-factor fractional-Ramare marking to
R_j(m)1_{omega_j(m)>0}1_{s in cal S_elig,j}.                    (7)
Writing m=p m' and v=dm', its all-selected-primes main coefficient is
Vtilde_{s,j}^{large}(p,v)
 =-1_{(v,c_*)=1}
  sum_{dm'=v,X^eta<=d<=X^(1/4+eta)}
  rho_{1/2}(d)b_{P_j,c_*}^{rho}(m')R_j(m')
  Psi_D(d)Psi_M(pm')
  A_lit(s,kappa,hpv;(ell-kappa hpv)/s),                          (8)
where c_*=c rad(kappa) and every original sampled support is retained. Let
U_{s,j}^{main}
 =sum_{p in cal P_j,(p,c_*)=1}sum_v
  Vtilde_{s,j}^{large}(p,v)
  [1_{pv congruent ell*(kappa h)^(-1) (mod s)}
   -phi(s)^(-1)1_{(pv,s)=1}].                                   (9)
Let L_proj,j, L_W,j, and L_0,j be, respectively, the projective norm, reconstructed pointwise constant, and correction-amplitude bound for the j-th row, in the senses of facts 2ccb8f56e6084b34 and 6951622549da0aa4. Put
L_log=1+log(2XQ_c).                                              (10)
Let E_{s,j}^{large} be the exact p|m' correction in the j-th restricted row. Then
sum_{j=1}^J sum_{s in cal S_elig,j}|U_{s,j}^{main}|
 << sum_{j=1}^J [
 N_box,j L_proj,j X(log X)^(-A)
 +N_box,j L_W,j omega_{P_j}(c_*)
  {X P_j^(-1)L_log^3+Q_c sqrt(X/P_j)L_log^2}],                   (11)
where the implied constant depends only on A, and
sum_{j=1}^J sum_{s in cal S_elig,j}|E_{s,j}^{large}|
 <<sum_{j=1}^J L_0,j L_log^4[Q_cX/P_j^2+X/P_j]                  (12)
with an absolute implied constant. The right side of (12) is at most
sum_{j=1}^J L_0,j L_log^4[
 X^(7/10-11delta_h)(log X)^(-4C)
 +X^(3/5-6delta_h)(log X)^(-2C)].                               (13)
The prime-unit deletion part of (11) is at most
sum_{j=1}^J N_box,j L_W,j omega_{P_j}(c_*)[
 X^(3/5-6delta_h)(log X)^(-2C)L_log^3
 +X^(4/5-2delta_h)(log X)^(-C)L_log^2].                         (14)

The exact row on MS-ELIG is the sum over j of U_{s,j}^{main}+E_{s,j}^{large}; hence (11)-(12) pay all of MS-ELIG without duplicating any original pair (s,m). MS-FIRST-NOSCALE and MS-UNMARK are not estimated. In particular, multiscale marking replaces the single-scale omega_P(m)=0 complement by the smaller exact residual MS-UNMARK, in which m has no prime divisor in the union of the cal P_j, together with the separate first-occupied-scale modulus failure MS-FIRST-NOSCALE. No HC-SMALL, HC-HIGH, ROUGH, complete HC-MED, critical-tail, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
f702d90f3491c7c0.proof:
For every positive integer m, either all omega_j(m) vanish or the finite nonempty set {j:omega_j(m)>0} has a unique least member. In the second case, s either belongs or does not belong to the corresponding cal S_elig,j. This proves that (6) is disjoint and exhaustive.

Fix j and p in cal P_j. The intervals cal P_i are pairwise disjoint, so p does not belong to cal P_i for i<j. Therefore, for every positive integer m',
omega_i(pm')=omega_i(m') quad (i<j),
and hence
R_j(pm')=R_j(m').                                                (15)
The coefficient identity of fact e59f666ecac4d4cb may be multiplied termwise by the zero-one factor R_j(m). On the main factorization m=pm', equation (15) makes this factor depend only on m'. Fact 2ccb8f56e6084b34 proves from (1),(2),(4) that every selected p exceeds d, so the fundamental-domain multiplicity is exactly 2 and cancels the fractional-Ramare main factor -1/2. Folding v=dm' gives exactly (8).

The logarithmic Fourier proof of fact 2ccb8f56e6084b34 is unchanged. The only modification is that its cofactor mode becomes
H_D^(-1)v^(i tau)
 1_{(v,c_*)=1}
 sum_{d|v,X^eta<=d<=X^(1/4+eta)}
 rho_{1/2}(d)b_{P_j,c_*}^{rho}(v/d)R_j(v/d)
 (v/d)^(i sigma)Psi_D(d).                                       (16)
Since |R_j|<=1, the divisor sum in (16) is bounded by C_D tau(v), exactly as in the cited proof. The prime mode, its normalized logarithmic twist, its uniform Siegel-Walfisz property, the outer projective coefficients, and their l1 norm are unchanged. Crucially, R_j is independent of the modulus s, because first occupied scale was chosen before testing s for eligibility. Thus (16) is a common cofactor sequence over every s in cal S_elig,j, as required by fact e3c0786d33d7e576.

Fact cbbc7f1404df765c verifies for cal S_elig,j the exact factorable scales, squarefreeness, canonical injectivity, reduced residue ell*(kappa h)^(-1), and coprimality (s,c_*)=1. Its at-most-three v-block aggregation and at-most-N_box,j factor-box aggregation apply to (16) with unchanged bounds. Applying fact e3c0786d33d7e576 therefore gives the j-th summand in (11), including the displayed p|c_* deletion cost. Summing j proves (11). The exponent bounds in (14) follow from (4) exactly as equations (16)-(17) of fact cbbc7f1404df765c.

For the correction, p|m' means m'=pu and the original large factor is m=p^2u. Pairwise disjointness again gives
R_j(p^2u)=R_j(u).                                                (17)
This zero-one factor may be included in the arbitrary coefficient F_s of fact 6951622549da0aa4 and does not increase its bound L_0,j. All other hypotheses of that fact are (1),(4) and the literal geometry already verified by fact cbbc7f1404df765c. It yields the j-th summand of (12); summing j proves (12). Substitution of the lower bound in (4) gives (13), as in the cited fact.

Finally, the exact fractional-Ramare identity applies on every first-occupied-scale sector (7), and these sectors are disjoint in the original variable m. Equations (15)-(17) show that neither the main folding nor the correction changes the prefix allocation. Hence the exact MS-ELIG row is the asserted sum of main and correction rows, with no duplicate (s,m). The two other members of (6) were never included in a cited estimate, which proves the final scope statements.

glossary.E_{s,j}^{large}: The prefix-restricted p-dividing-m-prime-cofactor correction at scale j.
glossary.MS-ELIG: The sector whose first occupied selected-prime scale has an eligible literal modulus.
glossary.MS-FIRST-NOSCALE: The sector whose first occupied selected-prime scale has no eligible literal modulus factorization.
glossary.MS-UNMARK: The sector with no prime divisor in any selected-prime interval of the multiscale family.
glossary.N_box,j: The number of nonempty canonical P_j-admissible factor boxes.
glossary.R_j(n): The first-occupied-scale prefix selector excluding all earlier selected-prime intervals.
glossary.U_{s,j}^{main}: The prefix-restricted actual prime-unit main row at scale j.
glossary.Vtilde_{s,j}^{large}(p,v): The prefix-restricted all-selected-primes folded main coefficient at scale j.
glossary.cal P_j: The j-th half-open selected-prime interval in the ordered multiscale family.
glossary.cal S_elig,j: The P_j-eligible canonical factorable literal modulus set from fact cbbc7f1404df765c.
glossary.omega_j(n): The number of distinct prime divisors of n in cal P_j.

f71c0564150cb532.title: EXACT FOUR-FACE COMMON-CORE PARTITION, CRT COLLAPSE OF THE FULL-DOUBLE FACE, AND ITS RESIDUE DIAGONAL
f71c0564150cb532.author: slava chan
f71c0564150cb532.statement:
EXACT FOUR-FACE COMMON-CORE PARTITION, CRT COLLAPSE OF THE FULL-DOUBLE FACE, AND ITS RESIDUE DIAGONAL.

Assume the notation, hypotheses, and exact unequal-a crossed kernel of fact 2e80012db28da736. Thus
f_1=dr_1, f_2=dr_2, b=dr_1r_2t,
where d,r_1,r_2,t are pairwise coprime and squarefree, and put
v=r_1r_2t=b/d.
In particular (d,Nv)=1 and (a_1a_2,dv)=1.

For each prime p|d, expand the four terms in the common-core local factor (9) of that fact. There is a unique partition
d=d_0d_1d_2d_{12},                                         (1)
into pairwise coprime squarefree factors, where d_0 records the primes at which the constant term is selected, d_1 the conjugated a_1-only response, d_2 the a_2-only response, and d_{12} the double response. Define
Phi_{d_0,d_1,d_2,d_{12}}(a_1,a_2;d,v)
 =product_{p|d_1} e_p(N[a_1(dv/p)]^(-1))
  product_{p|d_2} e_p(-N[a_2(dv/p)]^(-1))
  product_{p|d_{12}}
   e_p(N(a_1^(-1)-a_2^(-1))(dv/p)^(-1)),                    (2)
where every inverse in a p-factor is modulo p. Then the exact normalized common-core expansion is
1/phi(dv)^2 product_{p|d}
 [1+(p-1)e_p(N[a_1(dv/p)]^(-1))
   +(p-1)e_p(-N[a_2(dv/p)]^(-1))
   +(p-1)^2e_p(N(a_1^(-1)-a_2^(-1))(dv/p)^(-1))]
 =
sum_{d_0d_1d_2d_{12}=d; pairwise coprime}
 Phi_{d_0,d_1,d_2,d_{12}}(a_1,a_2;d,v)
 /[phi(v)^2 phi(d_0)^2 phi(d_1)phi(d_2)].                   (3)

On the full-double face d_{12}=d and d_0=d_1=d_2=1, Chinese remaindering gives
product_{p|d}e_p(N(a_1^(-1)-a_2^(-1))(dv/p)^(-1))
 =e_d(N(\bar a_1-\bar a_2)\bar v),                         (4)
where bars denote inverses modulo d. Consequently the exact full-double part of C_{F_0}(a_1,a_2) is
C_{F_0}^{dbl}(a_1,a_2)
 =sum_{d,r_1,r_2,t}^{*}
  c_{r_2t}(N)c_{r_1t}(N)/phi(r_1r_2t)^2
  overline(K_{r_1}(dr_1r_2t;a_1))
  K_{r_2}(dr_1r_2t;a_2)
  e_d(N(\bar a_1-\bar a_2)\overline{r_1r_2t}),             (5)
and its contribution to the energy is
E_cross^{dbl}
 =sum_{a_1!=a_2}alpha_{a_1}overline(alpha_{a_2})
   C_{F_0}^{dbl}(a_1,a_2).                                  (6)
The star in (5) retains exactly all conditions inherited from (4)-(8) of fact 2e80012db28da736: d,r_1,r_2,t are pairwise coprime squarefree, dr_i>F_0, dr_1r_2t asymp B, (dr_1r_2,N)=1, and (a_1a_2,dr_1r_2t)=1. Thus (5)-(6) retain the literal alpha coefficients, both Ramanujan weights, both one-sided r_i Euler responses, the varying squarefree modulus d, and the dyadic b condition.

For fixed d and v, the sum of the absolute values of all normalized local coefficients in (3) is exactly
1/phi(v)^2 product_{p|d}(1+2/(p-1)+1/(p-1)^2)
 =1/phi(v)^2(d/phi(d))^2.                                  (7)
Thus proper common-core faces are explicit, but absolute summation of their local coefficients provides only a subpolynomial ledger and no displayed fixed negative power of d.

The full-double composite phase in (4) equals one precisely when
a_1 congruent a_2 (mod d).                                  (8)
This residue diagonal is compatible with a_1!=a_2. If d asymp D and a_1,a_2 range in an interval of length O(Q), a direct support count gives
number of ordered unequal pairs with a_1 congruent a_2 (mod d)
 << Q^2/D+Q.                                                 (9)
After also counting unrestricted v with dv asymp B and its ordered squarefree factorizations v=r_1r_2t, the corresponding unweighted support ledger is
<<Q^o B(Q^2/D+Q).                                            (10)
At the actual forced lower edge from fact 2e80012db28da736,
D=Q^(2/3-4eta+o(1)),
formula (10) is
Q^(8/3+4eta+o(1)),                                           (11)
which is larger than the nonsaving Q^(8/3+o(1)) MZB-ENERGY scale by Q^(4eta+o(1)).

Equations (1)-(11) are identities, support counts, and a direct absolute-ledger no-fit only. They do not estimate E_cross^{dbl}, the proper faces, or C_small, and they assert no actual-Z_mid or Goldbach closure.
f71c0564150cb532.proof:
For each p|d, fact 2e80012db28da736 gives four summands with scalar amplitudes 1, p-1, p-1, and (p-1)^2. Choosing one summand independently at every prime partitions the prime divisors of squarefree d uniquely into d_0,d_1,d_2,d_{12}. The product amplitude is
phi(d_1)phi(d_2)phi(d_{12})^2.
Since d and v are coprime,
phi(dv)^2=phi(v)^2phi(d_0)^2phi(d_1)^2phi(d_2)^2phi(d_{12})^2.
Dividing the response amplitude by this identity gives exactly the denominator in (3), while the selected phases give (2). This proves (1)-(3).

On the full-double face, b=dv and for every p|d,
(dv/p)^(-1)=(d/p)^(-1)v^(-1) modulo p.                       (12)
For any integer y and squarefree d, the elementary CRT identity is
e_d(y)=product_{p|d}e_p(y(d/p)^(-1)).                         (13)
Indeed the CRT idempotent attached to p is
(d/p)[(d/p)^(-1) modulo p], and multiplying its contribution by 1/d gives the p-character in (13). Apply (13) with
y=N(\bar a_1-\bar a_2)\bar v.
Together with (12), this proves (4).

Because f_1=dr_1 and f_2=dr_2 with disjoint prime supports,
K_{f_1}(b;a_1)=K_d(b;a_1)K_{r_1}(b;a_1),
and similarly for f_2. Select the full-double term in
overline(K_d(b;a_1))K_d(b;a_2), use (4), and insert it into formula (4) of fact 2e80012db28da736. Its factor phi(d)^2 cancels the d-part of phi(b)^2, leaving phi(v)^(-2). The complementary factors b/f_1=r_2t and b/f_2=r_1t give the two Ramanujan weights displayed in (5). All other factors and support conditions are unchanged. This proves (5), and summing it against the original unequal-a tensor coefficients proves (6).

For (7), divide the four scalar amplitudes at p by (p-1)^2. Their absolute values are
1/(p-1)^2, 1/(p-1), 1/(p-1), 1,
whose sum is (p/(p-1))^2. Multiplication over p|d proves (7). Since d/phi(d)<=tau(d) for squarefree d and tau(d)=d^o(1), this absolute ledger is subpolynomial; it exhibits no factor d^(-delta).

Because (d,Nv)=1, the character in (4) equals one if and only if
\bar a_1 congruent \bar a_2 (mod d), equivalently a_1 congruent a_2 (mod d). This proves (8). In an interval of length at most C Q, each fixed a_1 has O(Q/D+1) possible a_2 in the same residue class modulo d, proving (9).

Finally, for d asymp D there are O(D) choices of d and, for each d, O(B/D+1) possible v with dv asymp B. In the actual nonempty range d<=O(B), this totals O(B+D)=O(B) pairs (d,v). A squarefree v has at most 3^{omega(v)}=v^o(1)=Q^o(1) ordered factorizations v=r_1r_2t; imposing pairwise coprimality and the conductor thresholds only deletes choices. Multiplying this count by (9) proves (10). Substituting B=Q^(4/3+o(1)) and the inherited forced lower edge D=Q^(2/3-4eta+o(1)) gives (11).

glossary.d_0: The factor of the common conductor core carrying no selected Euler response.

glossary.d_2: The factor of the common conductor core carrying only the a_2 response.

f7b5ba9fa0d6cfc8.title: FULL-FREQUENCY COMPLETION OF THE NATURAL CELL-\(G\) RECIPROCAL-ENERGY LEDGER
f7b5ba9fa0d6cfc8.author: slava chan
f7b5ba9fa0d6cfc8.statement:
FULL-FREQUENCY COMPLETION OF THE NATURAL CELL-\(G\) RECIPROCAL-ENERGY LEDGER.

Fix integers \(J,C\ge1\) and \(A_0\ge3\). Let
\[
 Q,H_P,H_T,S,T\ge1,\qquad G=H_T/H_P>0,
\]
and assume
\[
 C^{-1}QH_T\le ST\le CQH_T.                                  \tag{1}
\]
For each \(q\asymp Q\), choose a unit \(V_q\) modulo \(q\), and fix a nonzero integer \(A\). Let \(a_s,b_t\) be divisor-bounded coefficients supported on \(s\asymp S,t\asymp T\). Let
\[
 |\nu_h|\le\tau_J(|h|)
 \left(1+\frac{|h|}{H_P}\right)^{-A_0}\quad(h\ne0).           \tag{2}
\]
Define
\[
 W_q=\sum_{\substack{h\ne0,\ s\asymp S,\ t\asymp T\\(st,q)=1}}
 \nu_ha_sb_t e_q(AV_qh(st)^{-1}).                            \tag{3}
\]
Either impose no condition between \(s,t\), or additionally impose \((s,t)=1\). Then
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 H_P^{-1}\sum_{q\asymp Q}|W_q|
 \ll (|A|QH_PST)^\epsilon\big[
 &G^{1/4}Q^2H_T^{1/2}S^{-1/4}\\
 &+G^{1/4}Q^{7/4}H_T^{1/2}S^{1/4}\\
 &+Q^2H_TS^{-1/2}+Q^{7/4}H_T\big].                           \tag{4}
 \end{aligned}
\]

More generally, let \(i\) range over a finite set, let \(d_i\in\mathbb C\), and for each \(i\) let the three coefficient arrays in (3) satisfy the same supports and bounds. If
\[
 \mathfrak P=\sum_i|d_i|,                                    \tag{5}
\]
then the absolute aggregate of \(\sum_i d_iW_{q,i}\) is bounded by the right side of (4) multiplied by \(\mathfrak P\).
f7b5ba9fa0d6cfc8.proof:
Split \(h\ne0\) into signed dyadic blocks \(H\le|h|<2H\), \(H\ge1\). Put
\[
 V=H/H_P,\qquad G_H=H_T/H=G/V.
\]
On this block, remove the factor \((1+V)^{-A_0}\); the remaining frequency coefficient is divisor-bounded and
\[
 ST\asymp QH_T=G_HQH.
\]

Without \((s,t)=1\), apply fact \(42720f6d803c4640\) at frequency \(H\) and imbalance \(G_H\). Its normalization is \(H^{-1}\), so restoring \(H_P^{-1}\) multiplies the bound by \(V\). The first two terms of that fact become the first two terms of (4) multiplied by
\[
 V(G_H/G)^{1/4}(1+V)^{-A_0}
 =V^{3/4}(1+V)^{-A_0},                                      \tag{6}
\]
and its last two terms become the last two terms of (4) multiplied by
\[
 V(1+V)^{-A_0}.                                               \tag{7}
\]
For dyadic \(0<V\le1\), the sums of (6)-(7) are bounded by geometric series in \(V^{3/4}\) and \(V\). For \(V\ge1\), they are bounded by geometric series in \(V^{3/4-A_0}\) and \(V^{1-A_0}\), which converge because \(A_0\ge3\). The blockwise epsilon factor contains \(V^\epsilon\); choose the internal epsilon smaller than the displayed epsilon and smaller than \(1/4\), preserving convergence. This proves (4).

With \((s,t)=1\), insert
\[
 {\bf1}_{(s,t)=1}=\sum_{e\mid s,\ e\mid t}\mu(e).
\]
The proof of fact \(2b4989d9d25f33cc\), before its balanced-window simplification, gives the same four blockwise terms with additional factors
\[
 e^{-5/4},\quad e^{-7/4},\quad e^{-3/2},\quad e^{-2}.
\]
Their divisor-weighted sums converge independently of \(V\), so the same proof applies.

For the finite projective family, apply (4) to each \(i\), multiply by \(|d_i|\), and use the triangle inequality. Summing gives precisely the factor \(\mathfrak P\) in (5).

glossary.G_H: The blockwise imbalance H_T/H on a dyadic frequency block.
glossary.mathfrak P: The l1 projective coefficient norm sum_i |d_i| in the full-frequency CELL-G expansion.

f7bbe736fbfa275b.title: NONZERO SQUARE-SLOPE DIVISOR INCIDENCE FOR EVERY RESONANT FULL-DENOMINATOR COMPLETION MODE. Fix 0<eta<1/12 and 0<delta<2eta. Let Q tend to infinity, put B=Q^(4/3+o(1)), and let P satisfy P>=Q^(1/3+2eta+o(1)). Put A_P=Q^(1+delta)/P^2 and assume A_P>1. Let p be a prime in [P,2P), and let s,q be positive integers with ps,pq in [B,2B), (p,sq)=1, and g=(s,q)<A_P. Write s=gs' and q=gq', so (s',q')=1. Let k_1,k_2 be centered integer representatives of nonzero residue classes modulo ps and pq respectively, so 0<|k_1|<=ps/2 and 0<|k_2|<=pq/2. Assume the shared-prime frequency resonance from fact 5a7bf376fe94485e,
f7bbe736fbfa275b.author: slava chan
f7bbe736fbfa275b.statement:
NONZERO SQUARE-SLOPE DIVISOR INCIDENCE FOR EVERY RESONANT FULL-DENOMINATOR COMPLETION MODE. Fix 0<eta<1/12 and 0<delta<2eta. Let Q tend to infinity, put B=Q^(4/3+o(1)), and let P satisfy P>=Q^(1/3+2eta+o(1)). Put A_P=Q^(1+delta)/P^2 and assume A_P>1. Let p be a prime in [P,2P), and let s,q be positive integers with ps,pq in [B,2B), (p,sq)=1, and g=(s,q)<A_P. Write s=gs' and q=gq', so (s',q')=1. Let k_1,k_2 be centered integer representatives of nonzero residue classes modulo ps and pq respectively, so 0<|k_1|<=ps/2 and 0<|k_2|<=pq/2. Assume the shared-prime frequency resonance from fact 5a7bf376fe94485e,
k_1 s^(-1)+s q^(-1) k_2 q^(-1) congruent to 0 modulo p. (1)
Then the integer
R=k_1 q'^2+k_2 s'^2 (2)
is nonzero and p divides R. Moreover |R|<8B^3/P^2. Consequently, for fixed s',q',k_1,k_2, the number of primes p in [P,2P) that can satisfy (1) is O_{eta,delta}(1).
Thus, after any legal reindexing that fixes the primitive cofactors and completion frequencies before the p-sum, the resonant part of the exact tensor in fact 5a7bf376fe94485e has divisor-sparse shared-prime multiplicity. This statement does not perform that reindexing in the literal gamma/Vaughan array, does not estimate the nonresonant minus-one term in the completion formula, and does not bound E_full(P) or Goldbach.
f7bbe736fbfa275b.proof:
Because ps>=B and p<2P, one has s>B/(2P), and similarly q>B/(2P). Since g<A_P=Q^(1+delta)/P^2,
s',q'>B/(2PA_P)=BP/(2Q^(1+delta)). (3)
For every sufficiently small fixed epsilon>0, the hypotheses B=Q^(4/3+o(1)) and P>=Q^(1/3+2eta+o(1)) imply, for all sufficiently large Q,
BP/(2Q^(1+delta))>=Q^(2/3+2eta-delta-epsilon). (4)
Choose epsilon so small that 2epsilon<4eta-2delta. Squaring (3)--(4) and comparing with B=Q^(4/3+o(1)) gives s'^2,q'^2>B for all sufficiently large Q. (5)
Multiply resonance (1) by s q^2, which is a unit modulo p. This gives
k_1q^2+k_2s^2 congruent to 0 modulo p. (6)
Since s=gs', q=gq' and p does not divide g, division by g^2 modulo p turns (6) into p|R.
Suppose R=0 as an integer. Then k_1q'^2=-k_2s'^2. Because (s',q')=1, one has (s'^2,q'^2)=1. Hence s'^2 divides k_1 and q'^2 divides k_2. But the centered bounds and ps<2B,pq<2B give 0<|k_i|<B, contradicting (5). Therefore R is nonzero.
Also s,q<2B/P and g>=1, so s',q'<2B/P. Together with |k_i|<B this yields
|R|<=|k_1|q'^2+|k_2|s'^2<2B(2B/P)^2=8B^3/P^2. (7)
If r distinct primes in [P,2P) divide the nonzero integer R, then P^r<=|R|. Thus r<=log|R|/log P. Equation (7), B=Q^(4/3+o(1)), and P>=Q^(1/3+2eta+o(1)) make this ratio bounded by a constant depending at most on eta and delta. This proves the claimed multiplicity and all scope statements.

f8785a5bccd97804.title: There are absolute constants c_0>0 and H_0>=2 such that for every real H>=H_0, the fixed-determinant shell S_2(H,1) from fact 1218e64e51ba3131 contains at least c_0 H^6 matrices Q=((a,c),(-d,b)) whose four entries a,b,c,d are all nonzero and even. Equivalently, the exponent 6 in the complete shell tax is sharp: already for the fixed value K=2 (so det Q=4),
f8785a5bccd97804.author: slava chan
f8785a5bccd97804.statement:
There are absolute constants c_0>0 and H_0>=2 such that for every real H>=H_0, the fixed-determinant shell S_2(H,1) from fact 1218e64e51ba3131 contains at least c_0 H^6 matrices Q=((a,c),(-d,b)) whose four entries a,b,c,d are all nonzero and even. Equivalently, the exponent 6 in the complete shell tax is sharp: already for the fixed value K=2 (so det Q=4),
c_0 H^6 <= |S_2(H,1)| << H^6 log(2H).
Consequently the bare conditions det Q=2K, even nonzero coefficients, and coefficient height H^3 cannot yield any H^{-delta} shell sparsity for delta>0.
f8785a5bccd97804.proof:
Let N=floor(H^3/8). We first show that, for all sufficiently large N, at least c_1N^2 ordered pairs (a_0,c_0) in the integer square [N,2N]^2 are coprime, for an absolute c_1>0. A noncoprime pair has a common prime divisor p<=2N. The number of multiples of p in [N,2N] is at most N/p+1, so the number of noncoprime pairs is at most
sum_{p<=2N}(N/p+1)^2
 <=N^2 sum_{p}p^{-2}+2N sum_{n<=2N}n^{-1}+2N.
The prime sum is at most sum_{n=2}^infinity n^{-2}, and
sum_{n=2}^infinity n^{-2} <=1/4+integral_2^infinity t^{-2}dt=3/4.
The other two terms are O(N log(2N)). Since the square contains at least N^2 pairs, at least N^2/8 pairs are coprime once N is large. Thus one may take c_1=1/8.

Fix such a coprime pair. Since a_0 is invertible modulo c_0, choose the least-absolute residue b_0 satisfying
a_0b_0 congruent to 1 modulo c_0,
so |b_0|<=c_0/2. Put
d_0=(1-a_0b_0)/c_0.
Then d_0 is an integer and
a_0b_0+c_0d_0=1.                                                     (1)
Neither b_0 nor d_0 is zero: b_0=0 would make 0 congruent to 1 modulo c_0>1, while d_0=0 would give a_0b_0=1 with a_0>1. The size bounds are
|b_0|<=c_0/2<=N,
|d_0|<1+a_0|b_0|/c_0<=1+a_0/2<=N+1.

Now define
(a,b,c,d)=2(a_0,b_0,c_0,d_0).
All four integers are nonzero and even. By (1),
ab+cd=4(a_0b_0+c_0d_0)=4=2K
with K=2. Also
|a|,|c|<=4N<=H^3/2,
|b|<=2N<=H^3/4,
|d|<=2N+2<=H^3
for sufficiently large H. Hence Q belongs to S_2(H,1). Distinct pairs (a_0,c_0) give distinct matrices because they give distinct first and third coefficients. We have therefore constructed at least N^2/8>=c_0H^6 matrices for a suitable absolute c_0>0 and all large H.

The upper bound |S_2(H,1)|<<H^6log(2H) is the shell estimate in fact 1218e64e51ba3131. Combining it with the constructed lower bound proves sharpness of the exponent. In particular an estimate |S_2(H,1)|<<H^{6-delta} for any fixed delta>0 would contradict the lower bound for large H.

glossary.a_0: first coordinate of an auxiliary coprime pair
glossary.b_0: least-absolute modular inverse coordinate satisfying a_0 b_0 congruent to 1 modulo c_0
glossary.c_0: absolute positive constant in the shell lower bound
glossary.c_0_aux: second coordinate of an auxiliary coprime pair; written c_0 in the proof
glossary.c_1: absolute positive proportion of coprime pairs in the auxiliary square

f976f03f881550b2.title: Assume the hypotheses and notation of fact ae1febd328547ccc, and additionally assume that the dyadic partition function Phi is bounded on the positive reals. Split the forward 1x1 source exactly as
f976f03f881550b2.author: slava chan
f976f03f881550b2.statement:
Assume the hypotheses and notation of fact ae1febd328547ccc, and additionally assume that the dyadic partition function Phi is bounded on the positive reals. Split the forward 1x1 source exactly as
T_{F,11}=T_{F,11}^{small}+T_{F,11}^{large},
where the first sum is over incidences with D<=64 and the second is over incidences with D>64. Then
|T_{F,11}^{small}|<<_{W,Phi} log(2N).
Consequently T_{F,11}^{small} may be used as the real remainder R_{F,11} in the component architecture of fact f5b31dd3643732ac with only logarithmic size, while every incidence in T_{F,11}^{large} has nontrivial physical quotient modulus b_z>1 by fact a94835cfd97853a0. This statement supplies no primitive fourth-moment, carrier, external-window, or cross-cell formula for the large component.
f976f03f881550b2.proof:
The split is the disjoint partition of the finite source component by D<=64 and D>64. Consider an incidence in the small part. Nonzero Phi(d/D) and support of Phi in [1/2,2] give d<=2D<=128. Forward boundary-admissibility has beta=log R/log D with beta<=3/2-kappa<3/2 and D>1, so R=D^beta<D^(3/2)<=64^(3/2)=512. Nonzero Phi(r/R) gives r<=2R<1024. Membership in the actual endpoint cell gives k^2<=r, hence k<32; replacing strict inequalities by d<=128,r<=1024,k<=32 only enlarges the finite set.

For each positive integer triple d,r,k, the fixed equation dm+rk=N determines at most one positive integer m. For any fixed positive integer u, there are at most three positive dyadic labels U for which u/U lies in [1/2,2], because such U lie in [u/2,2u], an interval of multiplicative length four. Therefore each fixed integer quadruple d,m,r,k occurs under at most 3^4 labelled quadruples D,M,R,K. The controlled-set complement, forward selector, 1x1 tag, and canonical factor conditions only remove occurrences. Hence the number of small-D labelled incidences is bounded by an absolute constant, for example 128 times 1024 times 32 times 3^4.

On every such incidence, |mu(d)mu(r)|<=1, m<N and k<=32, so |log m log k| is at most log(2N)log(32). The function W is continuously differentiable with compact support by the inherited source hypotheses and is therefore bounded. The inherited cutoff satisfies 0<=psi<=1. By the additional hypothesis, each of the four Phi factors is bounded by ||Phi||_infinity. Multiplying the uniform bound per incidence by the absolute incidence-count bound proves |T_{F,11}^{small}|<<_{W,Phi}log(2N).

The exact identity permits the first term to be designated as a real remainder. Fact a94835cfd97853a0 applies to every incidence in the large term and proves b_z>1 there. The final scope sentence makes no additional transform claim.

glossary.T_{F,11}^{large}: the forward 1x1 source contribution with D greater than 64
glossary.T_{F,11}^{small}: the forward 1x1 source contribution with D at most 64

fa4091851a622bcb.title: TOP-B-SINGLETON-SQFREE-q AND LOW PHYSICAL RAY-CONDUCTOR PAYMENT. Fix the complete data and singleton aggregate coefficient
fa4091851a622bcb.author: slava chan
fa4091851a622bcb.statement:
TOP-B-SINGLETON-SQFREE-q AND LOW PHYSICAL RAY-CONDUCTOR PAYMENT. Fix the complete data and singleton aggregate coefficient
\[
 c_k^{\rm rec}(u,y;q,h)
\]
of fact \(d63101722d12c88c\), including one orientation, outer-gcd layer, selected source, parent, fixed-\(U\), high and smooth/projective fibre, one stopping length \(k\ge2\), blocks
\[
 U\le u<2U,\qquad \mathcal D\le y<2\mathcal D,\qquad
 B/2\le uy<2B,
\]
\[
 Q\le q<2Q,\qquad F\le |h|<2F,\qquad F\ge1,
\]
the conditions
\[
 (q,uy)=(u,y)=1,
\]
and a nonzero integer target \(\mathscr A\), with all displayed quantities bounded by fixed powers of \(Q\). The canonical marked dilator is \(y\), and all target-gcd, order/equal-cell, collision, deletion and provenance descendants have already been recombined inside \(c_k^{\rm rec}\).

Then
\[
 \boxed{\quad c_k^{\rm rec}(u,y;q,h)\ne0
 \ \Longrightarrow\ q\ {\rm is\ squarefree}.\quad}             \tag{1}
\]
Moreover, for a primitive signed ray
\[
 R=(\epsilon,a,b),\qquad
 \epsilon\in\{-1,1\},\quad a,b>0,\quad (a,b)=1,
\]
define
\[
 B_{u,y}(R)
 =\sum_{\ell\ge1}
 c_k^{\rm rec}(u,y;\ell a,\epsilon\ell b),                     \tag{2}
\]
where the sum is restricted automatically to the literal support. For a second ray
\[
 R'=(\epsilon',a',b')
\]
put
\[
 \Delta_0(R,R')=\epsilon ba'-\epsilon'b'a,                     \tag{3}
\]
and, when \(R\ne R'\), define the positive integer
\[
 m_q={aa'\over(aa',\mathscr A\Delta_0)}.                       \tag{4}
\]
Let \(1\le\mathcal Y\le Q^{C_1}\), where \(C_1\) is fixed, and let
\(\Theta(u,y,R,R')\in\{0,1\}\) be any existing literal selector on the exact row-pair sum. Then, for every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 \left|
 \sum_{u,y}\sum_{\substack{R\ne R'\\m_q\le\mathcal Y}}
 &\Theta(u,y,R,R')\,
 B_{u,y}(R)\overline{B_{u,y}(R')}\\
 &\times
 e_{aa'}\!\left(
 -\mathscr A\Delta_0(uy)^{-1}\right)
 \right|
 \ll_{\varepsilon,C_1}Q^\varepsilon B\mathcal YF^2 .
 \end{aligned}}                                                \tag{TOP-B-SINGLETON-LOW-qCOND}
\]
Every inverse in this formula is defined on the literal support. The estimate is absolute, so \(\Theta\) may include the exact nonresonant selector
\[
 y\nmid\mathscr A\Delta_0
\]
and any inherited selector already present after recombination.

In particular, if
\[
 \mathcal D\le Q^2,
\]
then taking
\[
 \mathcal Y={Q^2\over\mathcal D}
\]
pays the subform \(m_q\le Q^2/\mathcal D\) at
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 Q^\varepsilon{BQ^2F^2\over\mathcal D}.
 \quad}                                                         \tag{5}
\]
The complementary \(m_q>Q^2/\mathcal D\) form is not estimated. This theorem applies only to the singleton aggregate coefficient; it makes no pointwise claim about, and does not apply the count to, the old unrecombined siblings. It estimates the sum of the individual canonical rows indexed by \((u,y)\); it is separate from the cross-\(u\) pre-Cauchy energy in which two different \(u\)-rows are paired.
fa4091851a622bcb.proof:
We first prove the squarefree support. In the exact outer-gcd normalization of fact a71f777ad842c886, write the two original Möbius variables as
\[
 d=ga,\qquad r=gb,\qquad g=(d,r).
\]
Every nonzero source atom has \(\mu(d)\mu(r)\ne0\). Hence \(g,a,b\) are pairwise coprime and squarefree, and
\[
 \mu(d)\mu(r)=\mu(a)\mu(b).
\]
In the forward orientation the normalized marked factor is \(n_z=b\) and its complementary source factor is \(s_z=a\); in the reverse orientation \(n_z=a\) and \(s_z=b\). Fact e58fc7c00f1683e6 applies the stopping anatomy to \(n_z\), while the reciprocal-modulus variable \(q\asymp Q\) is exactly the complementary factor \(s_z\). Thus every old exact top-\(B\) coefficient is zero unless
\[
 \mu(q)=\mu(s_z)\ne0.
\]
All later descendant coordinates partition the same source atom and do not change \(q\). Fact d63101722d12c88c proves coordinatewise that \(c_k^{\rm rec}\) is the sum of those old coefficients after every descendant is recombined. Therefore this sum also vanishes unless \(q\) is squarefree, proving (1).

For a supported term on \(R\), write
\[
 q=\ell a,\qquad h=\epsilon\ell b.
\]
Because \(q\) is squarefree, \(\ell\) and \(a\) are squarefree and coprime. In particular \(a\) is squarefree. Since \((q,uy)=1\), every factor of \(a\) is a unit modulo \(uy\), and cancellation of the common scaling in the additive character gives
\[
 e_q\!\left(-\mathscr A h(uy)^{-1}\right)
 =
 e_a\!\left(-\mathscr A\epsilon b(uy)^{-1}\right).            \tag{6}
\]
Multiplying (6) by the conjugate expression for \(R'\) gives exactly
\[
 e_{aa'}\!\left(-\mathscr A\Delta_0(uy)^{-1}\right),           \tag{7}
\]
as in the physical ray-pair identity of fact 7e9251670db3e1c9. Distinct primitive signed rays have distinct reduced signed slopes, so \(R\ne R'\) implies \(\Delta_0\ne0\).

We repeat the low-conductor arithmetic count, now on the singleton rows. Since \(a,a'\) are squarefree, write
\[
 g=(a,a'),\qquad a=g\alpha,\qquad a'=g\beta.
\]
Then \(g,\alpha,\beta\) are pairwise coprime and squarefree. Put
\[
 L_0=\epsilon b\beta-\epsilon'b'\alpha.
\]
One has
\[
 \Delta_0=gL_0,\qquad(\alpha\beta,L_0)=1.                      \tag{8}
\]
Indeed, if a prime divides \(\alpha\), then it divides neither \(b\) nor
\(\beta\), so the first term defining \(L_0\) is nonzero modulo that
prime; the argument for a prime dividing \(\beta\) is symmetric.

From
\[
 aa'=g^2\alpha\beta,\qquad
 \mathscr A\Delta_0=\mathscr A gL_0
\]
and (8),
\[
 m_q=
 {g\over(g,\mathscr A L_0)}
 {\alpha\beta\over(\alpha\beta,\mathscr A)}.                   \tag{9}
\]
Fix \(b,b'\), the two signs, and dyadic blocks
\[
 A\le a<2A,\qquad A'\le a'<2A'.
\]
Set
\[
 t=(\alpha\beta,\mathscr A),\quad
 v={\alpha\beta\over t},\quad
 r=(g,\mathscr A).
\]
Then \(t,r\mid|\mathscr A|\). Write \(g=rs\), put
\[
 s_0=(s,L_0),\qquad s_1=s/s_0.
\]
The integer data
\[
 t,v,\alpha,\beta,r,s_0,s_1
\]
determine \(g=rs_0s_1\), hence \(a,a'\). There are divisor-many choices for
\(t,r\), for the ordered factorization \(tv=\alpha\beta\), and for
\(s_0\mid|L_0|\). Formula (9) becomes
\[
 m_q=vs_1.
\]
Thus \(m_q\le\mathcal Y\) leaves at most
\[
 \sum_{v\le\mathcal Y}
 \left\lfloor{\mathcal Y\over v}\right\rfloor
 \ll\mathcal Y\log(2\mathcal Y)
\]
choices for \((v,s_1)\). The target, all ray coordinates and
\(0<|\Delta_0|<8QF\) have polynomial size, so every divisor factor is
\(O_\varepsilon(Q^\varepsilon)\). Therefore, for fixed \(b,b'\), signs
and dyadic denominator blocks,
\[
 \#\{(a,a'):m_q\le\mathcal Y\}
 \ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon\mathcal Y.                     \tag{10}
\]

It remains to include the positive scaling variables. A supported
\(q=\ell a\) with \(A\le a<2A\) has
\[
 {Q\over2A}<\ell<{2Q\over A},
\]
so there are at most
\[
 K_A=1+{2Q\over A}
\]
possible \(\ell\). Since \(|h|=\ell b<2F\),
\[
 b<{4FA\over Q}.
\]
For a nonempty block \(A<2Q\), and the product of the number of possible
positive \(b\) and the number of possible \(\ell\) is at most \(16F\).
The same bound holds for the primed ray. Summing (10) over \(b,b'\) and
the scaling variables therefore gives
\[
 \#\{(q_1,h_1,q_2,h_2):m_q\le\mathcal Y\}
 \ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon\mathcal YF^2.                  \tag{11}
\]
The logarithmically many denominator blocks and four sign choices are
absorbed into \(Q^\varepsilon\).

By fact d63101722d12c88c,
\[
 |c_k^{\rm rec}(u,y;q,h)|
 \ll \tau_J(uyq|h|)(\log(2Q))^C
 \ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon.                               \tag{12}
\]
The supported pairs \((u,y)\) satisfy \(B/2\le uy<2B\). For every integer
\(n\) in that interval the number of factorizations \(n=uy\) is at most
\(\tau(n)\); hence the number of supported singleton rows is
\(O_\varepsilon(Q^\varepsilon B)\). Expand both ray coefficients in
(2), apply (11)-(12), take absolute values, and observe that the phase
in (7) has modulus one and every value of \(\Theta\) only deletes a
term. This proves TOP-B-SINGLETON-LOW-qCOND. Fact
d63101722d12c88c also shows that summing over all supported stopping
lengths \(k\) costs only another logarithmic factor, absorbed into
\(Q^\varepsilon\).

Finally, when \(\mathcal D\le Q^2\), the choice
\(\mathcal Y=Q^2/\mathcal D\) is at least one and has polynomial size.
Substitution gives (5). The proof operated on one aggregate coefficient
per \((u,y)\), never on an old sibling, and paired rays only inside the
same row; this proves the final scope distinctions.

glossary.B_{u,y}(R): The recombined singleton coefficient summed over positive scalings on one primitive signed ray in the fixed row u,y.
glossary.TOP-B-SINGLETON-LOW-qCOND: The absolute low physical ray-conductor payment for the recombined singleton top-B rows.
glossary.m_q: The effective physical ray conductor aa' divided by its gcd with the target times the primitive ray determinant.

fa68efb06f0ec564.title: ORTHOGONAL-PROJECTION FORM OF THE PRE-CAUCHY PMD DEFECT. Use the finite index set cal I and complex numbers b_i,z_i of fact 87fee9c7e02513f9. Put
fa68efb06f0ec564.author: slava chan
fa68efb06f0ec564.statement:
ORTHOGONAL-PROJECTION FORM OF THE PRE-CAUCHY PMD DEFECT. Use the finite index set cal I and complex numbers b_i,z_i of fact 87fee9c7e02513f9. Put
C_src=sum_{i in cal I}|b_i|^2,
M_src=sum_{i in cal I}|z_i|^2,
T_src=sum_{i in cal I}b_i z_i,
D_pre=(1/2)sum_{i,j in cal I}
 |conjugate(b_i)z_j-conjugate(b_j)z_i|^2.                  (1)
Assume C_src>0 and define
z_i^perp=z_i-(T_src/C_src)conjugate(b_i).                  (2)
Then exactly
sum_i z_i^perp b_i=0,                                      (3)
D_pre=C_src sum_i|z_i^perp|^2,                             (4)
and
sum_i|z_i^perp|^2
 =inf_{alpha in C}sum_i|z_i-alpha conjugate(b_i)|^2
 =M_src-|T_src|^2/C_src.                                   (5)
In particular D_pre=0 if and only if there is alpha in C such that
z_i=alpha conjugate(b_i)
for every i in cal I.                                      (6)

For the complete literal finite-band PMD row of fact 87fee9c7e02513f9, take
i=(ell,v,p,h), b_i=eta_ell xi_v,
z_i=sum_q x_{ell,v,p,h}(q), and T_src=H S_lit.             (7)
Then, for every epsilon>0, the desired signed estimate
|S_lit|^2<=P Q^(8/3+epsilon)                               (8)
is equivalent to the exact quantitative non-collinearity condition
sum_i|z_i^perp|^2
 >=M_2^lit-[H^2 P Q^(8/3+epsilon)]/C_src.                  (9)
Thus the earlier signed theorem slot is precisely a lower bound for the squared distance of the literal q-row vector z from the one-dimensional source-coefficient line spanned by the conjugate vector (conjugate(b_i))_i. It must retain the cross-height, cross-v, cross-p, and cross-projective-label structure inside this projection. This is an exact reformulation only; it proves no positive lower bound in (9), no PMD closure, and no Goldbach conclusion.
fa68efb06f0ec564.proof:
By fact 87fee9c7e02513f9,
D_pre=C_src M_src-|T_src|^2.                               (10)
Using definition (2),
sum_i z_i^perp b_i
=sum_i z_i b_i-(T_src/C_src)sum_i conjugate(b_i)b_i
=T_src-(T_src/C_src)C_src=0,
which proves (3).

For any alpha in C, expand
sum_i|z_i-alpha conjugate(b_i)|^2
=M_src-2 Re(conjugate(alpha)T_src)+|alpha|^2 C_src.
Completing the square gives
sum_i|z_i-alpha conjugate(b_i)|^2
=M_src-|T_src|^2/C_src
 +C_src|alpha-T_src/C_src|^2.                              (11)
Because C_src>0, the last term is nonnegative and vanishes exactly at alpha=T_src/C_src. This proves both equalities in (5). Taking alpha=T_src/C_src and multiplying (5) by C_src gives
C_src sum_i|z_i^perp|^2=C_src M_src-|T_src|^2=D_pre,
which is (4). Equation (11) also proves (6).

In the literal specialization, fact 87fee9c7e02513f9 gives M_src=M_2^lit and T_src=H S_lit. Substitution into (5) yields
sum_i|z_i^perp|^2
=M_2^lit-H^2|S_lit|^2/C_src.                              (12)
Since C_src>0, inequality (8) is equivalent, by rearranging (12), to (9). The stated scope follows because all components of z_i and all outer indices are exactly those retained in the cited literal specialization.

glossary.alpha: A complex scalar parameter in the best one-dimensional approximation.
glossary.z_i^perp: The component of z_i after subtracting its orthogonal projection onto the line spanned by conjugate(b_i).

faf90ac2f8827442.title: SELECTED-FIRST-PRIME ROW-GRAM AND BARE POINT-EVALUATION NO-FIT FOR THE \(V_{\rm deep}\) RANK-ONE CONSUMER
faf90ac2f8827442.author: slava chan
faf90ac2f8827442.statement:
SELECTED-FIRST-PRIME ROW-GRAM AND BARE POINT-EVALUATION NO-FIT FOR THE \(V_{\rm deep}\) RANK-ONE CONSUMER.

Let \(p\) be a prime with \(p\nmid\mathscr A\), and assume \(p\) is a common eligible marked-dilator prime for \(m\ge2\) local rows. Assume the local data of all rows are identical at every eligible prime smaller than \(p\), while their \(p\)-local slopes
\[
 a_i=h_i(q_iT_i)^{-1}\in\mathbb F_p,\qquad 1\le i\le m,        \tag{1}
\]
are pairwise distinct. Here \(T_i=n_i/p\) is the natural cofactor of fact \(ddd3eb74fcd1957d\). Then the condition that \(p\) is the first active prime for the ordered pair \((i,j)\) is
\[
 D_p(i,j)=1_{a_i\ne a_j}.                                     \tag{2}
\]
Consequently
\[
 D_p=J_m-I_m,                                                  \tag{3}
\]
its eigenvalues are \(m-1\) and \(-1\), and
\[
 \|D_p\|_{\rm op}=m-1.                                        \tag{4}
\]
It is indefinite and cannot be represented as a positive row Gram
\[
 D_p(i,j)=\langle v_i,v_j\rangle                              \tag{5}
\]
in a complex Hilbert space. Thus the selected-first-prime pair deletion is neither a positive row Gram nor a uniformly contractive literal row operator as the number of distinct local slopes grows.

This does not contradict facts \(549328a9f587f158\),
\(a84f95a82329a894\), and \(bbd687d016ee3ff6\). They permit the selected-prime condition as a tuple-dependent scalar mask after the relevant four-row occupancy is formed and absolute coefficient norms dominate its tuples; they do not assert the preceding rowwise factorization (5).

For every function \(F:\mathbb F_p\to\mathbb C\),
\[
 |F(0)|
 \le p^{1/4}
 \left({1\over p}\sum_{X\in\mathbb F_p}|F(X)|^4\right)^{1/4}. \tag{6}
\]
The factor \(p^{1/4}\) is sharp. Hence a completion supplying only
\[
 {1\over p}\sum_X|F(X)|^4\le p^{-\eta}M^4,\qquad 0<\eta<1,    \tag{7}
\]
gives
\[
 |F(0)|\le p^{(1-\eta)/4}M,                                  \tag{8}
\]
which is not a saving over \(M\). The occupancy facts
\(549328a9f587f158\) and \(bbd687d016ee3ff6\) allow only
\[
 0<\eta<\min(4\delta/3,1),
\]
so their fourth-root gain alone cannot pay the sharp bare point-evaluation cost (6).

Therefore a common-\(X\) consumer for fact \(97b9d86408362df2\) must retain ordered-pair provenance through a deletion-aware fourth-moment formation, prove source-driven translation averaging or a stronger literal point-evaluation theorem, or obtain additional saving beyond the fixed-prime occupancy factor. This is a scoped method no-fit. The matrices and delta functions used here need not be realizable by the complete literal source. It proves no lower bound for \(V_{\rm deep}\), no failure of TOP-B-FIRSTP-JCOMP-ENV or TOP-B-BALG-DEEP-NR-SPEC, no POST-A-TAIL statement, and no Goldbach conclusion.
faf90ac2f8827442.proof:
For rows \(i,j\), the \(p\)-local phase difference from facts
\(97b9d86408362df2\) and \(ddd3eb74fcd1957d\) is
\[
 \mathscr A(a_i-a_j)\pmod p.
\]
Because \(p\nmid\mathscr A\), this is nonzero exactly when \(a_i\ne a_j\). All smaller eligible primes are resonant by the identical-data hypothesis. Therefore \(p\) is first active exactly under (2). Pairwise distinctness gives zero diagonal and one off the diagonal, proving (3).

The constant vector is an eigenvector of \(J_m-I_m\) with eigenvalue \(m-1\). Every vector with coordinate sum zero is an eigenvector with eigenvalue \(-1\). This proves (4) and indefiniteness. A matrix of the form (5) is positive semidefinite because
\[
 \sum_{i,j}\overline{z_i}\langle v_i,v_j\rangle z_j
 =\left\|\sum_i z_iv_i\right\|^2\ge0.
\]
Therefore (5) is impossible. Equivalently, its zero diagonal would force every \(v_i=0\), contradicting its off-diagonal entries.

The cited occupancy facts state their selected-prime allowance only for a tuple mask after vector norms dominate the four-row terms. Hence their assertions do not imply (5) and are consistent with this matrix calculation.

For (6), the nonnegative complete sum contains its \(X=0\) summand:
\[
 |F(0)|^4\le\sum_X|F(X)|^4
 =p\left({1\over p}\sum_X|F(X)|^4\right).
\]
Take fourth roots. Equality holds for the delta function that is one at zero and zero elsewhere, proving sharpness for arbitrary functions. Substitution of (7) proves (8). Since every allowed fixed-prime occupancy exponent is strictly below one, \(p^{(1-\eta)/4}>1\), proving the scale no-fit and all scope statements.

glossary.bare common-X point evaluation: A completion controlling only the normalized full X-fourth moment and recovering one physical point by the general point-evaluation inequality.
glossary.p-local slope: The residue h(qT)^{-1} modulo p, with natural cofactor T=n/p.
glossary.selected-first-prime row mask: The pair matrix recording resonance at every smaller eligible prime and nonresonance at p.

fafe50a7d45923d2.title: SOURCE-BALANCED NATURAL-BLOCK PROJECTIVE SEPARATION OF THE LITERAL C4 SMOOTH FOURIER AMPLITUDE. Assume the exact C4 coefficient normal forms of fact 9bee61f3627bd506 and the literal physical balances
fafe50a7d45923d2.author: slava chan
fafe50a7d45923d2.statement:
SOURCE-BALANCED NATURAL-BLOCK PROJECTIVE SEPARATION OF THE LITERAL C4 SMOOTH FOURIER AMPLITUDE. Assume the exact C4 coefficient normal forms of fact 9bee61f3627bd506 and the literal physical balances
C_0^{-1}X<=DM<=C_0X,  C_0^{-1}X<=RK<=C_0X                         (1)
for fixed C_0 and X>0. Fix g,c and one orientation. In the forward orientation suppose
q is comparable to D/(gc), n is comparable to R/g, T_eps=M, and K_eps=K;
in the reverse orientation suppose
q is comparable to R/(gc), n is comparable to D/g, T_eps=K, and K_eps=M. (2)
Here every comparison constant is fixed. Put H_P=B/T_eps, where B is the dyadic scale of n. Fix a signed block F<=|h|<2F with F<=C_FH_P. Let the literal smooth support in fact 9bee61f3627bd506 retain t comparable to T_eps and (L_src-cqt)/n comparable to K_eps, with fixed positive comparison constants. Define
A_eps(q,n,h)=(H_P/n)widehat F^eps_{g,cq,n}(eps h/n).                 (3)
Assume the nonzero physical scales are bounded by fixed powers of a parameter Q_0>=2.

There are coefficients gamma_l, l in Z^3, and separated functions a_l(q),b_l(n),c_l(h), each bounded in absolute value by one, such that exactly on this block and smooth support,
A_eps(q,n,h)=sum_l gamma_l a_l(q)b_l(n)c_l(h),                       (4)
the series converges absolutely and uniformly, and
sum_l|gamma_l|<< (log Q_0)^2.                                       (5)
After consuming the Archimedean phase as in fact 3330e83b6d253b69, the coefficient without its retained arithmetic masks is
D^0(q,n,h)=mu(c)mu(q)mu(v)sum_lgamma_l a_l(q)b_l(n)c_l(h).           (6)
Thus the literal smooth amplitude legally separates the common q multiplier at polylogarithmic cost under the actual source balance. This theorem does not separate arithmetic masks or unit gates, absorb the small-v phase, define the final PMLS incidence, prove C4, or imply Goldbach.
fafe50a7d45923d2.proof:
Rescale the physical integration variable by t=T_eps u. On the fixed smooth support, u and the complementary quotient (L_src-cqt)/(nK_eps) lie in fixed compact subsets of the positive reals. The prefactor H_PT_eps/n=B/n is bounded.

The load-bearing balance for normalized q derivatives follows from (1)--(2). In the forward chart,
cqT_eps/(nK_eps)=cqM/(nK) is comparable to DM/(RK),                  (7)
and in the reverse chart,
cqT_eps/(nK_eps)=cqK/(nM) is comparable to RK/(DM).                  (8)
Both are bounded above and below by fixed constants. Since the complementary quotient is bounded away from zero, the logarithmic derivative ratio
cqT_eps u/(L_src-cqT_eps u)                                         (9)
is also uniformly bounded. Finally,
|h|T_eps/n<<F/H_P<<1.                                                (10)

Normalize q,n,h by their dyadic scales. Equations (7)--(10), scaled smoothness of W, and compact support show that every fixed mixed logarithmic derivative of A_eps is O((log Q_0)^2). The only logarithmic growth comes from the two literal logarithmic weights; all of their differentiated versions obey the same bound because both physical variables stay in fixed positive dyadic ranges.

Multiply by fixed smooth cutoffs equal to one on the normalized dyadic support, extend to a fixed three-torus, and take its Fourier series. Repeated integration by parts twice in each coordinate gives coefficients
|gamma_l|<< (log Q_0)^2 product_{i=1}^3(1+|l_i|)^{-2}.               (11)
The corresponding one-variable Fourier exponentials are the functions a_l,b_l,c_l and have modulus one. Summing (11) proves (4)--(5), including absolute uniform convergence.

Fact 9bee61f3627bd506 shows that its Archimedean factor is removed exactly in D^0, leaving mu(c)mu(q)mu(v)A_eps times the retained masks. Substitute (4) to obtain (6).

glossary.A_eps: the source-balanced dimensionless literal C4 Fourier amplitude
glossary.K_eps: the complementary physical scale K forward and M reverse
glossary.T_eps: the physical integration scale M forward and K reverse

fc328dd4cfe6679c.title: FORWARD NEAR-BALANCED ALL-PARENT ASSEMBLY THROUGH THE FULL LOW-BETA RANGE, WITH NO TARGET-GCD DELETION. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, sigma=kappa/100, and 0<eta<sigma. Use the literal forward high-source atom family, exact outer-gcd normalization d=ga,r=gb, paired nonzero-Poisson coefficients, frozen parents, and normalized marker coefficients of facts 7131a06664967733 and a71f777ad842c886. Thus R>D, Q=D/g, B=R/g, H_T=B/Q, G=M/Q, H_P=B/M, L_src=N/g, and each exact g-layer is the unchanged sum over parents and marker leaves C0,A,B,C1,C2,C3 with cutoffs L=H_TQ^sigma, S_0=H_T^2Q^(3sigma), and Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma), where beta=log B/log Q
fc328dd4cfe6679c.author: slava chan
fc328dd4cfe6679c.statement:
FORWARD NEAR-BALANCED ALL-PARENT ASSEMBLY THROUGH THE FULL LOW-BETA RANGE, WITH NO TARGET-GCD DELETION. Fix 0<kappa<=1/100, sigma=kappa/100, and 0<eta<sigma. Use the literal forward high-source atom family, exact outer-gcd normalization d=ga,r=gb, paired nonzero-Poisson coefficients, frozen parents, and normalized marker coefficients of facts 7131a06664967733 and a71f777ad842c886. Thus R>D, Q=D/g, B=R/g, H_T=B/Q, G=M/Q, H_P=B/M, L_src=N/g, and each exact g-layer is the unchanged sum over parents and marker leaves C0,A,B,C1,C2,C3 with cutoffs L=H_TQ^sigma, S_0=H_T^2Q^(3sigma), and Z=Q^(3/2-beta-3sigma), where beta=log B/log Q.
Assume c_1x<=DM,RK<=C_1x, c_Dx^(1/2)(log x)^(-A_D)<=D<=C_Dx^(1/2), and all physical scales are at most Cx. Let mathcal G_full be the exact g|N layers for which Q is sufficiently large,
1<=beta<=6/5-2kappa,
and Q^(-sigma+eta)<=G<=Q^(sigma-eta).
Let R_near_full be the sum of every parent and every normalized marker leaf on all g in mathcal G_full, retaining every literal source coefficient, phase, fixed-U mask, high-label mask, parent mask, Fourier-frequency block, target-gcd layer, prime-order label, and collision stratum. Add every bounded-normalized-base C0 layer from the same forward source.
Then there exists delta=delta(kappa,eta)>0 such that
|R_near_full|<<x^(1-delta).
No A target-gcd incidence is deleted. No B,C1,C2,C3,C0, Fourier-frequency, parent, collision, prime-order, source-amplitude, target-size, or Type-I sector is deleted. The theorem does not estimate outer-g layers outside the displayed G strip.
fc328dd4cfe6679c.proof:
Fact af2d16567b876aaf proves the assertion directly when beta<=1+sigma/4. For 1+sigma/4<beta<=6/5-2kappa it proves the identical literal all-parent assertion after deleting only A incidences with
Q^(sigma/2)<c=gcd(a,L_src)<H_TQ^(sigma/4).                   (1)
It therefore remains only to estimate (1), with every inherited label retained.

Fix one exact g-layer and one incidence in (1). The source variables are positive, a and b are squarefree, gcd(a,b)=1, and am+bk=L_src. Fact 1c64020b89f097c4 applies with all of its hypotheses: write
a=cq, k=ck_1, L_src=cL_1.
It gives gcd(c,q)=gcd(c,b)=gcd(q,b)=1 and gcd(q,L_1)=1. The exact forward reciprocity character before descent is
e_a(-L_src h b^(-1)).
Consequently
e_{cq}(-cL_1 h b^(-1))=e_q(-L_1 h b^(-1)),                 (2)
where b is a unit in both displayed moduli. Thus the descended target is exactly the unit target required in fact 97e9b97caca25b8d, with no change of h or of the inverse-product variable.

The exact interval-prime marker writes b=up with UY comparable to B and
H_TQ^sigma/2<=Y<=Z.
Squarefreeness of b gives gcd(u,p)=1, while gcd(a,b)=1 gives gcd(up,cq)=1. Also a comparable to Q implies q comparable to Q/c. The target bound |L_src|<=Q^C_A on this strip and the uniform scaled-smoothness of the archimedean reciprocity factor are established in facts d26acaefc372b4d0 and 3e326f797b2e04e4. Their complete Fourier decomposition supplies the scalars omega_F with arbitrary decay in F/H_P. Every fixed-U, high-label, parent, sign, prime-cell, and source mask is either a one-variable coefficient or a deletion mask; fact 97e9b97caca25b8d is uniform in all of them. The exact A coefficient has the required divisor bounds and interval-prime selector by the marker identity used in af2d16567b876aaf.

Choose C_med in fact 97e9b97caca25b8d to be exactly the divisors c in (1). All its hypotheses now hold, and it gives
sum_{c in (1)}|T_c|<<Q^(2-delta_1)                           (3)
on this fixed g-layer, uniformly after the polylogarithmically many inherited labels. Thus the only deletion in the second assertion of af2d16567b876aaf is power-saving and can be restored.

All other leaves and all complementary target-gcd layers are already paid by af2d16567b876aaf. Sum (3) over exact outer gcds. Since Q=D/g,
sum_{g|N,Q large}Q^(2-delta_1)
<=D^(2-delta_1)sum_{g>=1}g^(-2+delta_1)
<<D^(2-delta_1)
<<x^(1-delta_1/2).
The divisor, parent, cell, sign, and smooth labels are polylogarithmic and are absorbed by reducing the exponent. Bounded-Q C0 contributes O(x^(1/2+epsilon)) by fact 8bf5ca45f71b8c2c, exactly as in af2d16567b876aaf. Combining the two beta ranges proves the theorem with no target-gcd deletion.

glossary.L_1: The descended positive target L_src/c on one exact target-gcd layer.
glossary.R_near_full: The complete literal forward all-parent sum with every target-gcd layer restored.
glossary.mathcal G_full: The exact forward outer-gcd layers in the near-balanced full low-beta strip.

fc442085ff47a053.title: FORWARD \(E_{11}\) FULL-CONDUCTOR REDUCTION ON THE CENTRAL STRIP. Fix the literal high nonzero-Poisson source of facts 60b26a9b6f79467a and 77d7a3419a07305c. Thus \(N=2x\), \(D_*/2<D\le2x^{1/2}\), \(D_*=x^{1/2}(\log x)^{-B_{\rm src}}\), \(DM\asymp x\), and every retained atom has its original fixed-\(U\), high-label, dyadic, smooth, logarithmic, and conjugate-frequency masks. Restrict to the forward parent \(E_{11}\). Hence
fc442085ff47a053.author: slava chan
fc442085ff47a053.statement:
FORWARD \(E_{11}\) FULL-CONDUCTOR REDUCTION ON THE CENTRAL STRIP. Fix the literal high nonzero-Poisson source of facts 60b26a9b6f79467a and 77d7a3419a07305c. Thus \(N=2x\), \(D_*/2<D\le2x^{1/2}\), \(D_*=x^{1/2}(\log x)^{-B_{\rm src}}\), \(DM\asymp x\), and every retained atom has its original fixed-\(U\), high-label, dyadic, smooth, logarithmic, and conjugate-frequency masks. Restrict to the forward parent \(E_{11}\). Hence
\[
 R>D,\qquad 4/3\le\beta_E=\frac{\log R}{\log D}\le4/3+6\eta_t,
\]
and the least eligible factor and its complement are distinct primes \(p,\ell\) with
\[
 r=p\ell,\qquad
 D^{,2-\beta_E-3\eta_t}\le p,\ell\le
 D^{,2(\beta_E-1)+3\eta_t}.
\]
Put
\[
 a_E=1/3-15\eta_t>0,qquad H_0=R/D,qquad
 Y_E=\tfrac12H_0D^{a_E}.
\]
For every atom put \(g=(d,r)\). Let \(T_{E11}\) be the complete real paired nonzero-Poisson sum of these literal forward \(E_{11}\) atoms. The same notation may include the actual outer-gcd-normalized marker refinement of fact a71f777ad842c886 and its internal interval-prime or stopping copies; no coefficient other than this exact marker/least-tag inventory is allowed.

There is a fixed \(\delta_E>0\), depending only on the fixed source parameters, such that the following three deletion sectors have total absolute mass \(O(x^{1-\delta_E})\):

(i) every atom with \(g>1\);

(ii) among the \(g=1\) atoms, every atom with \((r,N)>1\);

(iii) among the remaining atoms, every frequency with \(|h|\ge Y_E\).

Consequently
\[
 T_{E11}=T_{E11}^{\rm crit}+O(x^{1-\delta_E}),             \tag{1}
\]
where \(T_{E11}^{\rm crit}\) is the unchanged signed literal sum restricted exactly by
\[
 g=1,qquad (r,N)=1,qquad 0<|h|<Y_E.                       \tag{2}
\]
On every atom in (2),
\[
 (d,r)=1,qquad (Nh,r)=1,
\]
so the complete additive phase
\[
 e_r(Nh\,d^{-1})
\]
has primitive denominator \(r=p\ell\), with both canonical primes retained. Equation (1) preserves the full phase, all original source masks, the forward \(E_{11}\) least-tag predicate, and every actual normalized-marker copy. It is only a full-conductor reduction: no cancellation estimate for \(T_{E11}^{\rm crit}\), no assertion for \(E_{21}\) or \(E_{22}\), and no theorem for arbitrary weighted subleaves is claimed.
fc442085ff47a053.proof:
First compare the canonical prime scales with the deletion threshold. Since \(R=D^{\beta_E}\),
\[
 H_0D^{a_E}=D^{\beta_E-2/3-15\eta_t}.
\]
The upper central-strip inequality \(\beta_E\le4/3+6\eta_t\) is equivalent to
\[
 2-\beta_E-3\eta_t\ge\beta_E-2/3-15\eta_t.
\]
Therefore the lower boundary-admissibility inequality gives
\[
 p,\ell\ge H_0D^{a_E}=2Y_E.                               \tag{3}
\]

We pay \(g>1\) first. Facts 3bb378b0a49679f9 and a94835cfd97853a0 show, for sufficiently large \(x\), that on the forward \(E_{11}\) component
\[
 g\in\{1,p,\ell\};
\]
the fourth formal possibility \(g=p\ell=r\) is empty because \(D>64\) and \(r>d\). Thus (3) implies
\[
 g>1\quad\Longrightarrow\quad g>Y_E.                    \tag{4}
\]
Apply the raw large-outer-gcd estimate (1) of fact 0a39d6be778e7dc9 with cutoff \(G=Y_E\). The forward \(E_{11}\) predicate and every original source mask are deletions of indices, so that fact applies directly. The exact normalized factor \(b=r/g\) has at most two prime factors. In the actual normalized marker identity of fact a71f777ad842c886, each applicable \(A\), \(B\), \(C_0\), \(C_1\), or \(C_2\) coefficient has only the divisor copies of this one- or two-prime integer. The explicit formulas in fact 3d343e417a673e84 therefore give total absolute copy variation bounded by an absolute constant. Hence the same estimate applies after this actual finite refinement, but not to arbitrary new weights. We obtain
\[
 \sum_{E_{11},,g>1}|\lambda_{g,a,b,h}|
 \ll \frac{DR}{Y_E}(\log x)^2
 =2D^{,2-a_E}(\log x)^2.                                 \tag{5}
\]
Since \(D\le2x^{1/2}\) and \(a_E>0\), (5) is \(O(x^{1-\delta_1})\) for some fixed \(\delta_1>0\).

Now take \(g=1\). Then \(d=a\), \(r=b=p\ell\), and \((d,r)=1\). By (3), if \((r,N)>1\), at least one of the two primes \(t\in\{p,\ell\}\) divides \(N\) and satisfies \(t\ge2Y_E\). For each such divisor \(t\mid N\), the complementary integer \(s\) in \(r=ts\asymp R\) has at most \(O(R/t)\) possible values; the additive \(O(1)\) in the interval count is absorbed because \(s\ge2Y_E\), hence \(R/t\gg Y_E\). Overcounting primes by all positive divisors gives
\[
 \#\{r\asymp R:r=p\ell,\ (r,N)>1\}
 \ll R\sum_{\substack{t\mid N\\t\ge2Y_E}}\frac1t
 \le \frac{R\tau(N)}{2Y_E}.                              \tag{6}
\]
The Fourier integration-by-parts estimate used in the proof of fact 0a39d6be778e7dc9 gives, for each fixed pair \((d,r)\),
\[
 \sum_{h\ne0}\left|r^{-1}\widehat F_{1,d,r}(h/r)\right|
 \ll(\log x)^2.                                           \tag{7}
\]
There are \(O(D)\) possible \(d\)'s. Combining (6) and (7), and again using the constant variation of the actual normalized marker copies, gives
\[
 \sum_{E_{11},,g=1,,(r,N)>1}|\lambda_{1,d,r,h}|
 \ll \frac{DR}{Y_E}\tau(N)(\log x)^2
 \ll D^{,2-a_E}x^{o(1)}.                                 \tag{8}
\]
This is \(O(x^{1-\delta_2})\).

It remains to make the surviving denominator primitive also with respect to the Poisson frequency. Repeated integration by parts, exactly as in fact 0a39d6be778e7dc9, gives for every fixed integer \(J\ge2\)
\[
 \sum_{|h|\ge Y_E}
 \left|r^{-1}\widehat F_{1,d,r}(h/r)\right|
 \ll_J(\log x)^2
 \left(1+\frac{Y_EM}{R}\right)^{1-J}.                    \tag{9}
\]
Here
\[
 \frac{Y_EM}{R}=\frac12M D^{a_E-1}.
\]
The source hypotheses \(DM\asymp x\) and \(D\le2x^{1/2}\) imply \(M\gg x^{1/2}\), and hence
\[
 Y_EM/R\gg x^{a_E/2}.
\]
There are at most \(O(DR)\ll O(x^{3/2})\) pairs \((d,r)\). Choose the fixed \(J\) sufficiently large in terms of \(a_E\). Summing (9) then gives \(O(x^{1-\delta_3})\). The same constant marker-variation argument applies.

Take \(\delta_E=\min(\delta_1,\delta_2,\delta_3)>0\). Removing the three sectors proves (1). On (2), \((d,r)=1\) by \(g=1\), \((N,r)=1\) by construction, and \((h,r)=1\) because \(|h|<Y_E\) while both prime divisors of \(r\) are at least \(2Y_E\). Thus \((Nh,r)=1\), and multiplication by the unit \(d^{-1}\) preserves this. The numerator of the displayed additive phase is therefore a unit modulo the squarefree modulus \(r=p\ell\), so its primitive denominator is the full product. No coefficient or phase was changed; only the three stated index sectors were deleted. This proves every scope assertion.

glossary.T_E11: The complete literal paired nonzero-Poisson sum in the forward E11 central strip.
glossary.T_E11^crit: The surviving signed E11 trace with g=1, target coprime to r, and frequency shorter than Y_E.
glossary.Y_E: One half of H_0 D^{a_E}, used as the outer-gcd and frequency cutoff.
glossary.beta_E: The original forward endpoint exponent log R/log D on the E11 central strip.
glossary.delta_E: A fixed positive exponent saving for the three deleted E11 sectors.

fcba64a06e489c96.title: EXACT COUNTABLE PRIME/COFACTOR PROJECTIVE FOLDING OF THE UNRESTRICTED MARKED HC FACTOR ROW. Fix the hypotheses and notation of fact edabb9a0d2959b41, one kappa,h row, one HC smooth cell Psi_D(d)Psi_M(m), and one selected prime scale cal P={p prime:P<=p<2P}. Put c_*=cR_kappa. Consider the unrestricted main row obtained by applying the fractional-Ramare identity of fact e59f666ecac4d4cb to rho_{1/2}(d)1_{omega_P(d)>0}, before its p|d' correction. Thus d=pd', and after putting v=d'm define the actual unrestricted marked-row coefficient
fcba64a06e489c96.author: slava chan
fcba64a06e489c96.statement:
EXACT COUNTABLE PRIME/COFACTOR PROJECTIVE FOLDING OF THE UNRESTRICTED MARKED HC FACTOR ROW. Fix the hypotheses and notation of fact edabb9a0d2959b41, one kappa,h row, one HC smooth cell Psi_D(d)Psi_M(m), and one selected prime scale cal P={p prime:P<=p<2P}. Put c_*=cR_kappa. Consider the unrestricted main row obtained by applying the fractional-Ramare identity of fact e59f666ecac4d4cb to rho_{1/2}(d)1_{omega_P(d)>0}, before its p|d' correction. Thus d=pd', and after putting v=d'm define the actual unrestricted marked-row coefficient
C_{q,kappa,h}^{mark}(p,v)
 =-1/2 sum_{d'm=v}
 b_{P,c_*}^{rho}(d')rho_{1/2}(m)
 Psi_D(pd')Psi_M(m)
 A_lit(q,kappa,hpv;(ell-kappa hpv)/q).                            (1)
The sum is over positive d',m and is extended by zero unless all original unit and sampled dyadic support conditions hold.

On every fixed sampled dyadic rectangle for p,d',m there are real frequencies sigma_k and coefficients a_k, independent of q,kappa,h, such that
Psi_D(pd')=sum_{k in Z}a_k p^(i sigma_k)d'^(i sigma_k),           (2)
with absolute uniform convergence on the rectangle and
sum_k|a_k|<<1.                                                    (3)
Let tau_j and lambda_{j,q,kappa,h} be the exact literal-amplitude coefficients of fact 97cfedc76bcae0ad on the corresponding p,v rectangle. Put C_Psi=||Psi_M||_infinity and define
A_{j,k}(p)=1_{(p,c_*)=1}p^(i(tau_j+sigma_k)),                    (4)
B_{j,k}(v)
 =v^(i tau_j)1_{(v,c_*)=1}
  sum_{d'|v}b_{P,c_*}^{rho}(d')rho_{1/2}(v/d')
  d'^(i sigma_k)Psi_M(v/d').                                    (5)
Then exactly on the complete zero-extended sampled rectangle
C_{q,kappa,h}^{mark}(p,v)
 =sum_{j,k in Z}[-lambda_{j,q,kappa,h}a_k/2]A_{j,k}(p)B_{j,k}(v). (6)
The double series is absolutely convergent, its outer projective norm satisfies
sum_{j,k}sup_{q,kappa,h}|lambda_{j,q,kappa,h}a_k|/2
 <<(log x)^(C_proj),                                             (7)
and, uniformly in j,k,p,v,
|A_{j,k}(p)|<=1,  |B_{j,k}(v)|<=C_Psi tau(v).                    (8)

Thus the complete unrestricted marked-factor main coefficient has an exact countable l1-summable prime/cofactor projective decomposition with uniform divisor bounds. This conclusion alone does not satisfy the finite-index hypothesis of fact be6fb90ce3095e82: a finite-truncation and limit extension, as well as the uniform Siegel-Walfisz condition for the prime modes and the explicit scale/collision hypotheses, remains to be checked before that fact can be applied. No estimate is asserted for the p|d' correction, the omega_P(d)=0 sector, nonfactorable moduli, HC-HIGH, or the complete critical tail.
fcba64a06e489c96.proof:
By the exact fractional-Ramare identity in fact e59f666ecac4d4cb, the unrestricted part of the marked d-factor is -1/2 times a selected prime p times a cofactor d', with coefficient b_{P,c_*}^{rho}(d'). Folding m into v=d'm therefore gives exactly (1), including the outer factor -1/2 and with no rearrangement issue because each sampled dyadic cell is finite. The original unit condition (p d'm,c_*)=1 is exactly the conjunction (p,c_*)=1 and (v,c_*)=1.

Write y=log(pd'). On the compact logarithmic interval containing the complete sampled p,d' rectangle, the fixed smooth function Psi_D(e^y) has bounded derivatives of every fixed order. Choose a larger interval on which it vanishes near the endpoints, periodize there, and take its Fourier series. Repeated integration by parts makes the Fourier coefficients absolutely summable; on the original interval the periodization equals the original cutoff. Writing each Fourier character of y=log p+log d' as p^(i sigma_k)d'^(i sigma_k) proves (2) and (3). This is the same compact-interval, no-alias construction used for the literal amplitude in fact 97cfedc76bcae0ad.

Fact 97cfedc76bcae0ad gives, on the complete sampled p,v rectangle,
A_lit(q,kappa,hpv;(ell-kappa hpv)/q)
 =sum_{j in Z}lambda_{j,q,kappa,h}p^(i tau_j)v^(i tau_j),
with absolute uniform convergence and
sum_j sup_{q,kappa,h}|lambda_{j,q,kappa,h}|<<(log x)^(C_proj).
Insert this identity and (2) into (1), retain the factor -1/2, and substitute m=v/d'. The unit condition supplies the two indicators in (4) and (5). The resulting expression is precisely (6). Absolute uniform convergence of both Fourier series and finiteness of the divisor sum justify rearrangement.

For (7), factor the nonnegative majorant:
sum_{j,k}sup_{q,kappa,h}|lambda_{j,q,kappa,h}a_k|/2
 <=(1/2)(sum_j sup_{q,kappa,h}|lambda_{j,q,kappa,h}|)(sum_k|a_k|)
 <<(log x)^(C_proj).
The bound |A_{j,k}(p)|<=1 is immediate. By fact 5999a1878276ac78, |rho_{1/2}(n)|<=1. Definition (1) of fact e59f666ecac4d4cb gives |b_{P,c_*}^{rho}(d')|<=1. Hence every summand in (5) has modulus at most C_Psi, and there are at most tau(v) divisors d' of v; this proves (8).

The expansion has indices (j,k) in Z^2. Absolute summability proves the stated countable projective shape but does not turn the index set into the finite set assumed in fact be6fb90ce3095e82. The final scope sentence therefore records that interface, rather than invoking the Maynard payment.

glossary.A_{j,k}(p): The prime-side projective mode, including the exact coprimality indicator for p.
glossary.B_{j,k}(v): The cofactor-side projective mode after summing over decompositions v=d'm.
glossary.C_Psi: The supremum norm of the fixed smooth cutoff Psi_M.
glossary.C_proj: A fixed exponent controlling the polylogarithmic l1 norm of the literal-amplitude Fourier coefficients.
glossary.C_{q,kappa,h}^{mark}(p,v): The actual unrestricted marked-factor main coefficient, including the outer fractional-Ramare factor -1/2, after writing d=pd' and folding v=d'm.
glossary.a_k: The kth absolutely summable logarithmic Fourier coefficient for the fixed smooth d-cell cutoff.
glossary.c_*: The combined fixed unit modulus cR_kappa.
glossary.sigma_k: The kth real logarithmic Fourier frequency for the fixed smooth d-cell cutoff.

fd22069145f59332.title: GA-PRIME-qCLASS: EXACT TWO-CHAMBER PRIME PHYSICAL-CONDUCTOR CLASSIFICATION AND NUMERATOR FACTORIZATION. Adopt two distinct supported primitive signed rays
fd22069145f59332.author: slava chan
fd22069145f59332.statement:
GA-PRIME-qCLASS: EXACT TWO-CHAMBER PRIME PHYSICAL-CONDUCTOR CLASSIFICATION AND NUMERATOR FACTORIZATION. Adopt two distinct supported primitive signed rays
R=(epsilon,a,b),  R'=(epsilon',a',b')
in one fixed Good-W outer row, with nonzero target T. Put
g=gcd(a,a'),  a=g alpha,  a'=g beta,
L_0=epsilon b beta-epsilon'b'alpha,  Delta_0=gL_0.                (1)
As in fact 3089501f7fb49c18, g,alpha,beta are pairwise coprime and squarefree, gcd(alpha beta,L_0)=1, and
m_q=s u,                                                         (2)
where
s=g/gcd(g,TL_0),  u=alpha beta/gcd(alpha beta,T).                 (3)
The integers s,u are coprime.

Assume m_q=p is an odd prime, and let c=C_q modulo p be the reduced numerator from fact cff9d29efb555b8e. Then exactly one of the following two disjoint chambers occurs.

(I) COMMON-CORE SURVIVOR. One has s=p and u=1. Equivalently,
alpha beta divides T,
g=p g_0,
gcd(g,TL_0)=g_0,
and p does not divide TL_0.                                      (4)
Put T_0=T/(alpha beta). Then
C_q=T_0L_0/g_0                                                   (5)
as an integer, and modulo p
c congruent gamma L_0
  =gamma(epsilon b beta-epsilon'b'alpha),                        (6)
where gamma congruent T_0 g_0^{-1} (mod p) is a unit. Hence for every unit z modulo p,
e_p(-c z^{-1})
 =e_p(-gamma epsilon b beta z^{-1})
  e_p(+gamma epsilon'b'alpha z^{-1}).                            (7)
Thus after g_0,alpha,beta are frozen, the raw prime-conductor phase is a genuine left-endpoint/right-endpoint rank-one product on every incomplete ray block.

(II) ONE-END SURVIVOR. One has s=1 and u=p. Equivalently,
g divides TL_0,
alpha beta=p tau,
tau=gcd(alpha beta,T) divides T,
and p does not divide T.                                        (8)
