Put T_1=T/tau. Then
C_q=T_1L_0/g                                                     (9)
as an integer, and gamma congruent T_1g^{-1} (mod p) is a unit. The prime p divides exactly one of alpha,beta. If p divides alpha, then
c congruent gamma epsilon b beta (mod p),                         (10)
so the raw phase e_p(-c z^{-1}) depends only on the left endpoint after g,alpha,beta are frozen. If p divides beta, then
c congruent -gamma epsilon'b'alpha (mod p),                       (11)
so the raw phase depends only on the right endpoint.

For both chambers the literal centered kernel is
K^circ_{p,c}(z)=e_p(-c z^{-1})+1/(p-1).                          (12)
Thus equations (7), (10), and (11) factor only its exponential part; the constant term remains on the exact incomplete ordered-pair incidence block. Every hard selector theta_{d,v}(R,R'), terminal support condition, scaling sum, source weight, and pair deletion remains outside this arithmetic factorization. In particular, a pair-dependent deletion can destroy the rank-one product after entrywise masking.

Applied to fact 5c2e3d6320031fbf, this splits every literal odd-prime discrepancy coefficient into a common-core difference-phase chamber and two one-end chambers. The classification and factorization prove no cancellation in any chamber, no PRIME-PAIR-DISC, no prime trace estimate, no composite-conductor estimate, C-HILBERT-OP-SUP, tail payment, or Goldbach.
fd22069145f59332.proof:
Fact 3089501f7fb49c18 proves the pairwise coprimalities, equation (1), and
m_q=[g/gcd(g,TL_0)][alpha beta/gcd(alpha beta,T)]=su.             (13)
Because g is coprime to alpha beta, every divisor of g is coprime to every divisor of alpha beta; hence gcd(s,u)=1. If su is prime, the ordered pair (s,u) is either (p,1) or (1,p), and the two alternatives are disjoint.

The reduced-conductor definition in fact cff9d29efb555b8e gives
C_q=T Delta_0/[aa'/p].
Using Delta_0=gL_0 and aa'=g^2 alpha beta yields
C_q=TpL_0/(g alpha beta).                                       (14)

Suppose first s=p,u=1. The equality u=1 is equivalent to alpha beta dividing T. The equality
g/gcd(g,TL_0)=p
and squarefreeness of g imply p divides g, p does not divide TL_0, and, on writing g=pg_0,
gcd(g,TL_0)=g_0. This proves (4). Substitute T=(alpha beta)T_0 and g=pg_0 into (14) to obtain (5). Since gcd(g_0,alpha beta)=1 and g_0 divides TL_0=(alpha beta)T_0L_0, one has g_0 divides T_0L_0, so (5) is indeed an integer. Moreover p divides neither T_0 nor g_0, because p does not divide T and g is squarefree. Thus gamma is a unit modulo p. Reducing (5) modulo p proves (6), and additivity of the exponent proves (7).

Now suppose s=1,u=p. Since alpha beta is squarefree,
alpha beta/gcd(alpha beta,T)=p
means alpha beta=p tau with tau=gcd(alpha beta,T). Thus tau divides T and p does not divide T. Since alpha and beta are coprime, p divides exactly one of them. The equality s=1 is g divides TL_0, proving (8). Write T=tau T_1 and substitute alpha beta=p tau into (14); this gives (9). Because gcd(g,tau)=1 and g divides tau T_1L_0, one has g divides T_1L_0, so (9) is an integer. Also p divides neither g nor T_1: it does not divide g because g is coprime to alpha beta, and it does not divide T_1 because p does not divide T. Hence gamma is a unit.

If p divides alpha, reduction of L_0=epsilon b beta-epsilon'b'alpha modulo p gives L_0 congruent epsilon b beta. Reducing (9) modulo p proves (10). If p divides beta, the analogous reduction gives L_0 congruent -epsilon'b'alpha, proving (11).

Finally fact 764588e99974a6d9 gives (12). Multiplying an exact factorized array entrywise by an arbitrary pair-dependent selector need not preserve its rank-one form, so the stated scope restriction is necessary. All exclusions follow.

glossary.g_0: The quotient g/p in the common-core survivor chamber.
glossary.gamma: The unit scalar modulo p multiplying the reduced numerator in a frozen prime-conductor arithmetic class.
glossary.s: The part of the common primitive-denominator core g surviving reduction by the target and ray determinant.
glossary.tau: The quotient alpha beta/p in the one-end survivor chamber.
glossary.u: The part of alpha beta surviving reduction by the target.

fddede33d4205fe2.title: MODULAR-HYPERBOLA WINDOW NORMAL FORM FOR EACH LITERAL CRITICAL SOURCE CLUSTER
fddede33d4205fe2.author: slava chan
fddede33d4205fe2.statement:
MODULAR-HYPERBOLA WINDOW NORMAL FORM FOR EACH LITERAL CRITICAL SOURCE CLUSTER.

Fix Q>=8, H>=2, and a positive integer n>=QH. Let A be an integer. Let cal X be a finite set of integer triples x=(q,m,k) satisfying
  Q<=q,m<2Q,  qm+nk=A,  gcd(qm,n)=1.                       (1)
If cal X is nonempty, then gcd(A,n)=1. For every integer q in [Q,2Q) with gcd(q,n)=1, let m_n(q) denote the unique integer m in [Q,2Q), if one exists, satisfying
  qm congruent A modulo n.                                 (2)
Then the map
  x=(q,m,k) maps to q                                      (3)
is injective on cal X, and every x in cal X is recovered by
  m=m_n(q),  k=[A-qm_n(q)]/n.                              (4)

Put
  Y_n(q)=m_n(q)-A/q                                       (5)
whenever m_n(q) exists. For the exact source slope lambda_x=k/q,
  lambda_x=-Y_n(q)/n.                                      (6)
Consequently, for every real interval J,
  lambda_x in J
if and only if
  Y_n(q) in -nJ.                                           (7)
If J has length at most 1/(12H), then -nJ has length at most
  n/(12H).                                                 (8)
In a dyadic outer row n=vp with
  V<=v<2V,  P<=p<2P,  VP=QH,                              (9)
one has
  Q/12<=n/(12H)<Q/3.                                      (10)
Thus every critical source-slope cluster is exactly the inverse image of a real interval of length at most n/(12H)<Q/3 under the corrected modular-inverse map q maps to m_n(q)-A/q.

More precisely, let cal X_J={x in cal X:lambda_x in J}, let I be any finite height set, and let
  a_h(x)=nu_h b_h(x),                                      (11)
where nu_h is independent of x. Then exactly
  sum_{h in I}|sum_{x in cal X_J}a_h(x)e(h lambda_x)|^2
   =
  sum_{h in I}|nu_h|^2
   |sum_{q in cal Q_J}
      b_h(q,m_n(q),[A-qm_n(q)]/n)
      e(h[A/(nq)-m_n(q)/n])|^2,                            (12)
where
  cal Q_J={q in [Q,2Q) intersect Z:
            gcd(q,n)=1, m_n(q) exists, Y_n(q) in -nJ,
            (q,m_n(q),[A-qm_n(q)]/n) in cal X}.            (13)

For the literal coefficient of fact 3b2d15db39ad0217 one has
  b_h(x)=c_q U_ell(q,h,v,p)chi_ell(v,p,h,q).               (14)
Hence, after the exact height-factor removal of fact a1b0c0ad5a923524, the local fixed-power target is a weighted modular-hyperbola-window energy estimate for the one-dimensional q-sums in (12), with every source mask retained in (13)-(14). The exact upstream factor mu(q) identified in fact 38bc0e88e17aef0e may be retained inside c_q, but that fact shows that this factor alone does not yield the required Gadd^(-1) saving.

This is an exact normal form and theorem interface only. It supplies no estimate for (12), does not assert that the remaining literal mask or smooth amplitude cancels, gives no global Aadd lower bound, no PMD closure, and no Goldbach conclusion.
fddede33d4205fe2.proof:
Take any x=(q,m,k) in cal X. Reducing (1) modulo n gives
  qm congruent A modulo n.
Since gcd(qm,n)=1, both qm and A are units modulo n. Thus gcd(A,n)=1 when cal X is nonempty.

The interval [Q,2Q) has length Q, while n>=QH>=2Q>Q. For a fixed unit q modulo n, equation (2) selects one residue class of m modulo n, and an interval of length less than n contains at most one representative. Hence m_n(q), when it exists, is unique. Once q and m are fixed, equation (1) uniquely determines k=(A-qm)/n. This proves injectivity and (4). Conversely, every q satisfying the membership conditions in (13) produces by (4) exactly one atom of cal X.

Divide qm+nk=A by nq:
  m/n+k/q=A/(nq).
Rearranging gives
  lambda_x=k/q=A/(nq)-m/n
                 =-[m-A/q]/n
                 =-Y_n(q)/n,
which is (6). Multiplication by the negative number -n maps J bijectively to -nJ, proving (7). A dilation by n multiplies interval length by n, proving (8).

Under (9),
  n=vp>=VP=QH
and
  n=vp<(2V)(2P)=4QH.
Divide by 12H to prove (10). The phrase 'length at most' in the preceding sentence uses only the upper bound in (10); the lower bound records the natural full critical-window scale.

For (12), use the bijection (3)-(4) between cal X_J and cal Q_J. Equation (6) gives
  e(h lambda_x)=e(h[A/(nq)-m_n(q)/n]).
Equation (11) factors nu_h outside the inner q-sum. Taking squared absolute values and summing h proves (12) exactly, with every membership condition retained in (13).

Fact 3b2d15db39ad0217 identifies the literal coefficient after source restoration as
  a_h(x)=c_q nu_h U_ell(q,h,v,p)chi_ell(v,p,h,q).
Thus (11) holds with (14), and no factor or mask is removed. Fact a1b0c0ad5a923524 proves that nu_h only nonnegatively reweights the fixed-height base energies. Fact 38bc0e88e17aef0e proves both the exact upstream mu(q) provenance and a prime-q source cluster on which that sign is constant, so the final warning about mu(q) is exactly within its accepted scope. No inequality beyond the interval-length calculation has been asserted, proving all scope qualifications.

glossary.Y_n(q): The real corrected inverse image m_n(q)-A/q.
glossary.m_n(q): The unique integer m in [Q,2Q), when it exists, satisfying qm congruent A modulo n.
glossary.modular-hyperbola window: A restriction Y_n(q) in a fixed real interval, together with existence of m_n(q).

fea13f398a742864.title: PHASE-ALIGNMENT SATURATION OF AN ALL-NONZERO OSC ROW
fea13f398a742864.author: slava chan
fea13f398a742864.statement:
PHASE-ALIGNMENT SATURATION OF AN ALL-NONZERO OSC ROW.

Fix constants C>=1 and Q>=2. Let real numbers H,V,P satisfy
  2<=H<=Q^(1/3),  2<=V<H,  P=QH/V.                          (1)
Let v be an integer in [V,2V), let p be a prime in [P,2P), and assume gcd(v,p)=1. Let A be a nonzero integer with |A|<=Q^C. Let cal X be a finite set of integer triples x=(q,m,k) satisfying
  Q<=q,m<2Q,
  qm+vpk=A,
  gcd(qm,vp)=1,
  vk nonzero.                                                (2)
Put X_src=#cal X. Let I be a consecutive interval of L positive number of integers, contained either in [H,2H) or in (-2H,-H], and assume
  p>2H.                                                       (3)
For every positive integer r define
  e_r(t)=exp(2 pi i t/r).
For every h in I and x=(q,m,k) in cal X define
  c_h(x)=e_q(-hk).                                           (4)
Thus |c_h(x)|=1.

Put epsilon_1=epsilon_2=1 and epsilon_3=epsilon_4=-1. For a complex number z define z^{[1]}=z and z^{[-1]}=conjugate(z). For heights h_i and source atoms x_i=(q_i,m_i,k_i), define
  Delta_h=h_1q_2q_3q_4+h_2q_1q_3q_4
          -h_3q_1q_2q_4-h_4q_1q_2q_3.                      (5)
Define
  T_align
  =sum_{h_1,h_2,h_3,h_4 in I,
         h_1+h_2=h_3+h_4}
    sum_{x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4 in cal X,
         Delta_h nonzero,
         p does not divide A Delta_h}
      product_{i=1}^4 c_{h_i}(x_i)^{[epsilon_i]}
      product_{i=1}^4 e_{q_i}(epsilon_i h_i k_i).            (6)
Then every summand in (6) equals one, T_align is a nonnegative integer, and
  T_align
  >=[(2L^3+L)/3] X_src^3(X_src-1).                           (7)
In particular, when X_src>=2,
  T_align/([(2L^3+L)/3]X_src^4)>=1-1/X_src.                 (8)

Consequently no estimate which is uniform over all coefficient arrays satisfying only |c_h(x)|<=1 can give a fixed-power saving, or even an o(1) relative saving as X_src tends to infinity, from the full fixed-row fourth-power scale. Any successful bound for the literal all-nonzero OSC term of fact 670a97b5f2366250 must use structure not implied by coefficient boundedness and source occupancy alone, or cancellation across outer rows. This is a coefficient-class no-go. It is not a counterexample for the literal Poisson coefficients, not a lower bound for the global OSC sum, and not a PMD or Goldbach conclusion.
fea13f398a742864.proof:
For epsilon_i=1, equations (4) and (6) give
  c_{h_i}(x_i)e_{q_i}(h_i k_i)
  =e_{q_i}(-h_i k_i)e_{q_i}(h_i k_i)=1.                    (9)
For epsilon_i=-1, the definition of the bracket operation gives
  c_{h_i}(x_i)^{[-1]}e_{q_i}(-h_i k_i)
  =conjugate(e_{q_i}(-h_i k_i))e_{q_i}(-h_i k_i)=1.         (10)
Thus every retained summand equals one.

We count the support. For an integer S define
  r_I(S)=#{(h_1,h_2) in I^2:h_1+h_2=S}.
As S runs across the pair-sum interval, the nonzero values of r_I(S) are
  1,2,...,L-1,L,L-1,...,2,1.
Therefore the number E_I of ordered quadruples (h_1,h_2,h_3,h_4) in I^4 satisfying h_1+h_2=h_3+h_4 is
  E_I=sum_S r_I(S)^2
     =L^2+2sum_{j=1}^{L-1}j^2
     =(2L^3+L)/3.                                           (11)

Fix one of the E_I height quadruples and choose x_1=(q_1,m_1,k_1), x_2=(q_2,m_2,k_2), and x_3=(q_3,m_3,k_3) arbitrarily from cal X. Condition (3) and the same-sign support imply h_4 is nonzero modulo p. Fact db067f4633c13fed proves on the source tuples (2) that
  p divides A Delta_h
if and only if
  p divides h_1m_1+h_2m_2-h_3m_3-h_4m_4.                  (12)
For the fixed heights and first three atoms, equation (12) determines m_4 modulo p because h_4 is invertible modulo p. Fact 914048233fada05f proves under the scale and source hypotheses (1)-(3) that the projection x=(q,m,k) to m modulo p is injective on cal X. Hence at most one x_4=(q_4,m_4,k_4) in cal X lies on the p-modular diagonal.

It follows that, for each height quadruple, at most X_src^3 of the X_src^4 ordered atom quadruples satisfy p|A Delta_h. Every tuple with Delta_h=0 is included among those diagonal tuples. Therefore at least
  X_src^4-X_src^3=X_src^3(X_src-1)                           (13)
atom quadruples satisfy both Delta_h nonzero and p not dividing A Delta_h, which is exactly the support in (6). Multiply (13) by (11). Since each retained term equals one by (9)-(10), this proves (7). Division by E_I X_src^4 proves (8).

If a bound uniform over all arrays with modulus at most one supplied a relative factor tending to zero, applying it to (4) along any family for which X_src tends to infinity would contradict (8). A fixed negative power is a special case. The final scope statement follows because (4) is an adversarial admissible bounded coefficient chosen to cancel the source phase; no assertion identifies it with the literal coefficient of the project.

glossary.E_I: The additive energy (2L^3+L)/3 of the consecutive height interval I.
glossary.T_align: The fixed-row all-nonzero OSC sum with phase-aligned coefficient c_h(x)=e_q(-hk).
glossary.r_I(S): The number of ordered pairs of heights in I with sum S.

ff228b0e569531f8.title: ACTUAL STRICT-TOP C1,C2,C3,C4 q-PROFILE BEFORE, AND INSIDE, THE PAIR-DEPENDENT SELECTED-PRIME MASK
ff228b0e569531f8.author: slava chan
ff228b0e569531f8.statement:
ACTUAL STRICT-TOP C1,C2,C3,C4 q-PROFILE BEFORE, AND INSIDE, THE PAIR-DEPENDENT SELECTED-PRIME MASK.

Work in the strict top sliver beta_m<beta<6/5. Fix the selected N, one active dyadic label, exact outer gcd g, orientation epsilon, fixed-U, high, U_low-parent, actual-G, smooth/projective source fibre, and one signed dyadic nonzero-frequency block F<=|h|<2F. Use the complete-provenance unmarked source of fact 544c7ba4db45c06f, with the orientation-independent notation
  s asymp Q, n asymp B, st+nu=L_src=N/g,
  (g,sn)=(s,n)=1.                                             (1)
Fix dyadic factors
  n=mv, M_1<=m<2M_1, V_1<=v<2V_1, M_1V_1 asymp B.             (2)

Legally reapply the exact six-anatomy marker of fact e58fc7c00f1683e6 to the n-variable, fix one anatomy Cj with 1<=j<=4 and one exact marker/convolution copy lambda, and let d_lambda be its canonical marked dilator from fact f0f6807663d3ef3c. Recombine every auxiliary marker-dependent provenance, target-gcd, prime-order/equal-cell and collision sibling back to the fixed Cj copy before forming its one-row q-profile.

For every fixed A>0, the dimensionless literal one-row coefficient before the reciprocal phase and before imposing a first-nonresonant-prime selector has an exact absolutely convergent representation
  c_lambda(s,n,h)
  =sum_rho kappa_{lambda,rho}(n,h)
    mu(s)1_{s asymp Q}1_{(s,gn)=1}A_rho(s),                   (3)
where
  ||A_rho||_infinity<=1,                                      (4)
and, uniformly in the fixed Cj copy and the displayed dyadic boxes,
  sum_rho|kappa_{lambda,rho}(n,h)|
  <<_A (log x)^2(1+F/H_P)^(-A).                              (5)
The same representation holds in the reverse orientation after the verified h-to--h reindexing. Summing all dyadic F,M_1,V_1 boxes gives total coefficient mass x^{o(1)}.

More explicitly, the coefficient in one separated mode is
  kappa_{lambda,rho}(n,h)
  =eta_rho mu(n)a_lambda(n)C_rho(m)D_rho(v)E_rho(h)           (6)
times fixed unit or outer-label scalars, where a_lambda(n) is the exact Cj marker coefficient, and
  |a_lambda(n)|,|C_rho(m)|,|D_rho(v)|,|E_rho(h)|<=1.          (7)
Thus the physical reciprocal-modulus profile q=s is not an arbitrary array: mode by mode it is a Möbius sequence, with the exact coprimality gate against gn, multiplied by one bounded one-variable profile A_rho(q). The Cj marker and canonical marked dilator do not change this q-profile because they are constructed from n and its fixed factorization.

The selected prime is different and remains entirely pair-dependent. For a nonresonant TT-star pair of rows of the fixed copy lambda, put
  Delta=h_1q_2-h_2q_1,
assume
  Delta!=0,  d_lambda does not divide mathscr A Delta,          (8)
and define
  p=min{ell: ell divides d_lambda and ell does not divide mathscr A Delta}.  (9)
For a prescribed prime p dividing d_lambda, the exact pair mask is
  D_{p,lambda}(q_1,h_1,q_2,h_2)
  =1_{p does not divide mathscr A Delta}
   product_{ell divides d_lambda, ell<p}1_{ell divides mathscr A Delta}.     (10)
Within a fixed-p pair sum, equations (3) for the two rows are multiplied first and then by (10). In a four-row occupancy formed from two TT-star pairs, the two exact masks (10), together with every later pair deletion and tuple mask, remain outside the four one-row profiles. No claim that p depends only on n is made.

This theorem removes the arbitrary-row-profile ambiguity exposed by fact 7fb1e62c5a0e5efa, but proves no cancellation for (3) under (10). The remaining unequal-residue supplier is a source-specific deletion-aware four-linear translation estimate for the profiles
  mu(q_i)1_{(q_i,gn_i)=1}A_{rho_i}(q_i),                       (11)
with both actual masks (10) and the complete physical interval lifts retained. Generic Fourier l2 and pointwise rational Weil bounds do not supply that estimate by fact 7fb1e62c5a0e5efa. No such four-linear estimate, cross-modulus assembly, short-block payment, complete C1-C4 trace estimate, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
ff228b0e569531f8.proof: Fact b0a38f5e9ae7feb6 gives the complete unmarked row, in both orientations, with coefficient mu(s)mu(n)Theta_lambda^epsilon(s,n,h) 1_{F<=|h|<2F} (H_P/n)Fhat_{g,s,n}^epsilon(epsilon h/n) e(epsilon L_src h/(sn)), (12) and reciprocal phase e_s(-epsilon L_src h n^(-1)). Its support has exactly the gates in (1). Fact 544c7ba4db45c06f proves that, after summing every inherited provenance sibling, Theta contains no remaining physical or provenance hard selector. On the factor box (2), its equations (3)-(4), inherited from fact 062a7f6f0c58b1f2, give the exact expansion 1_{F<=|h|<2F}(H_P/(mv)) Fhat_{g,s,mv}^epsilon(epsilon h/(mv)) e(epsilon L_src h/(smv)) =sum_rho eta_rho A_rho(s)C_rho(m)D_rho(v)E_rho(h), (13) with every one-variable factor bounded by one and sum_rho|eta_rho| <<_A(log x)^2(1+F/H_P)^(-A). (14) Multiply (13) by the two literal Möbius factors and the support gates in (12). Since n=mv is now fixed, the s-dependent part is exactly mu(s)1_{s asymp Q}1_{(s,gn)=1}A_rho(s), (15) while every other factor is the n,h-scalar displayed in (6), before re-marking. Fact e58fc7c00f1683e6 states that the six-anatomy marker is a pointwise identity applied to the n-variable after the complete inherited genealogy is recombined. Its Cj coefficients are the stopping, interval-prime, and ordered rough-prime functions of n specified there. Fixing one Cj marker/convolution copy therefore multiplies (12)-(15) by a scalar a_lambda(n) independent of s. Fact 3286b0e75a3ea94a records |a_lambda(n)|<=1. Fact f0f6807663d3ef3c constructs the canonical marked dilator d_lambda from that same n-factorization, so fixing the copy and d_lambda introduces no new s-dependence. The auxiliary marker-dependent provenance, target-gcd, order/equal-cell and collision refinements are finite sibling partitions whose recombination returns the fixed anatomy coefficient, by fact e58fc7c00f1683e6. Recombining them before the one-row profile therefore preserves (15). Equations (13)-(15) give (3) and (6); (4)-(5) follow from (7), (14), and |mu(n)|<=1. Fact 544c7ba4db45c06f proves the reverse sign reindexing and the complete dyadic summability. We now separate the pair-dependent selection. Fact 41b56ed8e64bdba6 gives the TT-star determinant Delta in (8), and fact 4f9aec67f5be35db defines the first nonresonant prime only under (8), exactly by (9). For a prescribed divisor p of d_lambda, equation (9) is equivalent to the conjunction that p does not divide mathscr A Delta and every divisor prime ell

glossary.A_rho(s): The bounded one-variable reciprocal-modulus profile in one separated smooth/projective mode.
glossary.D_{p,lambda}: The exact pair-dependent mask selecting p as the first nonresonant prime for one TT-star pair.
glossary.c_lambda(s,n,h): The literal dimensionless one-row Cj coefficient before its reciprocal phase and before the pair-dependent first-prime selector.
glossary.kappa_{lambda,rho}(n,h): The n,h scalar coefficient of one separated physical-q profile mode.

ffa8f6d3f766b9f5.title: TOTAL-MODULUS LOW-\(k\) PROJECTION AND PRECISE PASCADI NO-FIT
ffa8f6d3f766b9f5.author: slava chan
ffa8f6d3f766b9f5.statement:
TOTAL-MODULUS LOW-\(k\) PROJECTION AND PRECISE PASCADI NO-FIT.

Fix
\[
 \frac12<\alpha<\beta<1,\qquad \eta,\rho,B_{\rm src}>0.
\]
Let \(W,\Phi\) be continuously differentiable real functions with bounded
first derivatives, supported respectively in \([\alpha,\beta]\) and
\([1/2,2]\). Let \(N=2x\) be an integer with \(x\ge3\), let \(U>0\), and
assume
\[
 \frac12x^{1/2}(\log x)^{-B_{\rm src}}\le D\le2x^{1/2},
 \qquad D>2(\log x)^{6+\eta+\rho}.
\]
Put
\[
 M_0=x/D,\qquad H_0=D(\log x)^{-6-\eta-\rho/2},
\]
\[
 {\cal H}_{\rm mid}=\{h\in\mathbb Z:H_0<|h|\le3D/2-H_0\},
\]
and
\[
 {\cal I}_D=\{w\ge2:(w,N)=1,\ \mu(w)\ne0,\ w\le x^{1/2},
                         \ \Phi(w/D)\ne0\}.
\]
Choose a fixed infinitely differentiable function \(\chi\) with
\(0\le\chi\le1\), equal to one on \([\alpha/2,2\beta]\), and supported in
\([\alpha/4,4\beta]\).

For \(q\ge1\) and \(u>0\), extended by zero outside the support of \(W\),
define
\[
 F_q(u)=W(u)\Phi(x(2-u)/U)\log(x(2-u)/q)_+,
\]
\[
 \widetilde F_q(t)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^\infty
 F_q(u)u^{-it}\frac{du}{u}.
\]
For \({\bf t}=(t_1,t_2)\in\mathbb R^2\), define
\[
 f_{\bf t}(m)={\bf1}_{(m,N)=1}\chi(mD/x)(mD/x)^{i(t_1+t_2)}
\]
and, for \(h\in{\cal H}_{\rm mid}\),
\[
\begin{split}
 g_{h,{\bf t}}(w)={}&{\bf1}_{w,w-h\in{\cal I}_D}\mu(w)\mu(w-h)
 \Phi(w/D)\Phi((w-h)/D)\\
 &\times(w/D)^{it_1}((w-h)/D)^{it_2}.
\end{split}
\]
For an integer \(S>1\), put
\[
 B_{S,{\bf t}}(k)=\sum_m f_{\bf t}(m)e_S(km),\qquad
 G_{S,h,{\bf t}}(r)=\sum_wg_{h,{\bf t}}(w)e_S(rw).
\]
All sums here and below are finite. For \(r\pmod S\), define
\[
\begin{split}
 A_{S,{\bf t}}(r)=
 \sum_{\substack{q_1,q_2\ge1\\
                 \mu(q_1)\mu(q_2)\ne0\\
                 [q_1,q_2]=S\\(N,S)=1}}
 &\mu(q_1)\mu(q_2)\widetilde F_{q_1}(t_1)
                         \widetilde F_{q_2}(t_2)\\
 {}\times\sum_{\substack{h\in{\cal H}_{\rm mid}\\
                         (q_1,q_2)\mid h}}
 &G_{S,h,{\bf t}}(r)
 e_{q_2/(q_1,q_2)}
 \left(-rhq_1^{-1}\right).                              \tag{1}
\end{split}
\]
The inverse in (1) is taken modulo \(q_2/(q_1,q_2)\), and the twist is one
when that modulus is one. Define
\[
 Y_{S,{\bf t}}(k)=
 \sum_{\substack{r\ ({\rm mod}\ S)\\r\ne0}}
 A_{S,{\bf t}}(r)S(r,kN;S),                             \tag{2}
\]
where
\[
 S(a,b;S)=\sum_{\substack{z\ ({\rm mod}\ S)\\(z,S)=1}}
 e_S(az+bz^{-1}).
\]
For a residue \(k\pmod S\), let
\(\|k\|_S=\min_{n\equiv k\ ({\rm mod}\ S)}|n|\).
For \(1\le K_0\le S/2\), put
\[
 {\cal T}_{S,K_0}^{\times}
 =\frac1{S^2}\int_{\mathbb R^2}
 \sum_{\substack{k\ ({\rm mod}\ S)\\
                 0<\|k\|_S\le K_0}}
 B_{S,{\bf t}}(k)Y_{S,{\bf t}}(k)\,d{\bf t},             \tag{3}
\]
and
\[
 {\cal E}_S=
 \frac{M_0}{S^3}
 \left\{\int_{\mathbb R^2}
 \left(\sum_{\substack{k\ ({\rm mod}\ S)\\k\ne0}}
 |Y_{S,{\bf t}}(k)|^2\right)^{1/2}d{\bf t}\right\}^2.   \tag{4}
\]
Thus (1) aggregates every \(q_1,q_2,h\) coefficient, Möbius sign,
translation twist, moving positive logarithm and source selector with total
modulus \(S\) before the norm in (4). One has
\[
 \boxed{
 |{\cal T}_{S,K_0}^{\times}|
 \ll_{\chi}
 \left(\frac{K_0M_0}{S}\right)^{1/2}{\cal E}_S^{1/2}.
 }                                                       \tag{LOW-k}
\]
In particular, for fixed \(B>0\),
\[
 K_0\le \frac{S}{M_0}(\log x)^{-B}
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 |{\cal T}_{S,K_0}^{\times}|
 \ll(\log x)^{-B/2}{\cal E}_S^{1/2}.                    \tag{5}
\]
This is stronger than the same assertion with a factor \(x^{o(1)}\).

The exact Mellin inversion in (1)--(3) gives
\[
 {\cal N}_{\rm mid}^{\times}
 =\sum_{\substack{S>1\\(N,S)=1}}
 {\cal T}_{S,\lfloor S/2\rfloor}^{\times},              \tag{6}
\]
where \({\cal N}_{\rm mid}^{\times}\) is the accepted literal nonzero
family in fact \(2d839168a73eedfa\).

The nonprimitive-frequency conductor sectors are exact. For a term with
\(k,r\ne0\), put
\[
 g=(k,r,S),\qquad C=S/g,\qquad k=g\kappa,\qquad r=g\varrho.
\]
Then
\[
 (\kappa,\varrho,C)=1,\qquad
 S(g\varrho,g\kappa N;S)
 =\frac{\phi(S)}{\phi(C)}S(\varrho,\kappa N;C),          \tag{7}
\]
and
\[
 \frac{(K_0/g)M_0}{C}=\frac{K_0M_0}{S}.                 \tag{8}
\]
Thus (LOW-\(k\)) includes every common nonprimitive-frequency sector.
There is no additional nonunit-center sector in (6): fact
\(2d839168a73eedfa\) proves \((N,S)=1\) on every active unit-\(m\) tuple
and pays the complementary \((m,N)>1\) sector by proper-prime-power
support before divisor expansion.

Theorem 1.1 of Pascadi, arXiv:2511.08445, has the following precise
relevant slot: for a fixed modulus \(C\), a unit multiplier, two arbitrary
coefficient sequences supported on intervals of lengths
\(\ll C^{1/2+o(1)}\), and the joint condition
\((\kappa,\varrho,C)=1\), it gives a
\(C^{1-1/700+o(1)}\) operator bound. After (7), its unit and joint
coprimality slots are satisfied, but its two-short-interval hypothesis is
not supplied by (1): even when the \(\kappa\)-axis is restricted by
\(K_0/g\), the Möbius-weighted transform \(A_{S,{\bf t}}(g\varrho)\) is a
vector on the full residue system modulo \(C\). Therefore that theorem
does not, by itself, estimate \({\cal E}_S\) or improve (LOW-\(k\)).
Splitting the full \(\varrho\)-axis into short intervals and summing their
bounds absolutely would be an additional triangle-factorization tax, not
a consequence of the published theorem.

At each fixed \({\bf t}\), the Cauchy--Schwarz step in (LOW-\(k\)) is
exactly sharp for arbitrary response vectors relative to the actual
projected norm of \(B_{S,{\bf t}}\): equality is attained by taking the
projected \(Y_{S,{\bf t}}\) proportional to
\(\overline{B_{S,{\bf t}}}\). When \(K_0\asymp S/M_0\), the proved
projection multiplier is only of constant size. Hence this method gives
no critical-band logarithmic gain for an arbitrary response matrix. This
does not assert that the majorant
\(\|B\|_2\ll K_0^{1/2}M_0\) is attained, nor that the literal row (1)
saturates; a source-specific reflected/Bombieri--Vinogradov estimate at
the critical band remains open.
ffa8f6d3f766b9f5.proof:
For \(u\) in the support of \(W\), fact \(88d5e14f4865c93b\) proves the
absolutely convergent exact Mellin inversion
\[
 F_q(u)=\int_{\mathbb R}\widetilde F_q(t)u^{it}\,dt,
 \qquad
 \int_{\mathbb R}|\widetilde F_q(t)|\,dt\ll\log(2x).     \tag{9}
\]
On the support of the literal coefficient one has
\(\chi(mD/x)=1\). Insert (9) for the two moving logarithmic factors and
put the unit mask \({\bf1}_{(m,N)=1}\) into the common \(m\)-factor.
Finite Fourier transformation modulo \(S=[q_1,q_2]\) gives
\[
 \widehat A^\times_{h,q_1,q_2}(k,r)
 =\mu(q_1)\mu(q_2)\int_{\mathbb R^2}
 \widetilde F_{q_1}(t_1)\widetilde F_{q_2}(t_2)
 B_{S,{\bf t}}(k)G_{S,h,{\bf t}}(r)\,d{\bf t}.          \tag{10}
\]
All sums are finite and (9) permits the changes of order. TMC-EXACT in
fact \(967520f427b111c5\), followed by grouping all tuples with the same
\(S\), turns (10) exactly into (1)--(3). The hypotheses on \(W,\Phi\)
are the real-valued hypotheses of fact \(2d839168a73eedfa\), so summing
the nonzero \(k\)-bands through their full centered residue system proves
(6). No absolute value has been put around the \(q_1,q_2,h\) sum in (1).

The support of \(\chi(mD/x)\) contains \(O_\chi(M_0)\) integers and
\(|f_{\bf t}(m)|\le1\). Hence, uniformly in \({\bf t},S,k\),
\[
 |B_{S,{\bf t}}(k)|\ll_\chi M_0.
\]
There are at most \(2K_0+1\) residues in the band in (3), so
\[
 \left(\sum_{0<\|k\|_S\le K_0}
 |B_{S,{\bf t}}(k)|^2\right)^{1/2}
 \ll_\chi K_0^{1/2}M_0.                                \tag{11}
\]
Cauchy's inequality in \(k\), followed by integration in \({\bf t}\),
gives
\[
\begin{split}
 |{\cal T}_{S,K_0}^{\times}|
 &\ll \frac{K_0^{1/2}M_0}{S^2}
 \int_{\mathbb R^2}\|Y_{S,{\bf t}}\|_2\,d{\bf t}\\
 &=\left(\frac{K_0M_0}{S}\right)^{1/2}{\cal E}_S^{1/2}.
\end{split}
\]
This proves (LOW-\(k\)) and (5).

Since \((N,S)=1\), one has \(g=(r,kN,S)\). The definition of \(g\)
gives \((\kappa,\varrho,C)=1\). Directly partitioning the units modulo
\(gC=S\) above their reductions modulo \(C\) gives
\[
 S(ga,gb;gC)=\frac{\phi(gC)}{\phi(C)}S(a,b;C):
\]
each unit modulo \(C\) has \(\phi(gC)/\phi(C)\) unit lifts and the phase
is constant on those lifts. This proves (7), and (8) is immediate.

The quoted support, coefficient and coprimality hypotheses of Pascadi's
Theorem 1.1 are its printed hypotheses. Formula (1) contains no
restriction of \(\varrho\) to a short interval: the finite Fourier
transform of the literal shifted Möbius row is a vector on all residues.
Thus its second short-support hypothesis cannot be inferred. The final
statement about arbitrary responses is precisely the equality condition
in the pointwise Cauchy--Schwarz step and makes no claim that (11) is a
matching lower bound or that phases align through the \({\bf t}\)-integral.

669f51715cd33aa0.title: SELF-CONTAINED PAIRWISE KLOOSTERMAN-FRACTION PUSHFORWARD AND PRODUCT-COEFFICIENT NO-DIRECT-FIT. Let N be a nonzero integer, let P>=2, and let cal P be a finite set of primes in [P,2P]. Put e(z)=exp(2 pi i z) and e_c(z)=e(z/c). For every ordered pair of distinct a,b in cal P, let I_{a,b} be a finite set of triples (m,h,u) with m,u positive integers, h a nonzero integer, and gcd(abm,u)=1. Let w_{a,b}(m,h,u) be arbitrary complex weights on I_{a,b}. Define
669f51715cd33aa0.author: slava chan
669f51715cd33aa0.statement:
SELF-CONTAINED PAIRWISE KLOOSTERMAN-FRACTION PUSHFORWARD AND PRODUCT-COEFFICIENT NO-DIRECT-FIT. Let N be a nonzero integer, let P>=2, and let cal P be a finite set of primes in [P,2P]. Put e(z)=exp(2 pi i z) and e_c(z)=e(z/c). For every ordered pair of distinct a,b in cal P, let I_{a,b} be a finite set of triples (m,h,u) with m,u positive integers, h a nonzero integer, and gcd(abm,u)=1. Let w_{a,b}(m,h,u) be arbitrary complex weights on I_{a,b}. Define
 T_{a,b}=sum_{(m,h,u) in I_{a,b}} w_{a,b}(m,h,u)e_u(Nh m^{-1}(a^{-1}-b^{-1}))
and C(P)=sum_{a,b in cal P, a!=b}|T_{a,b}|, where inverses inside e_u are modulo u.
For fixed a,b define s=h(b-a), K=abm, and define Gamma_{a,b}(s,u,K) to equal w_{a,b}(K/(ab),s/(b-a),u) when ab divides K, b-a divides s, and (K/(ab),s/(b-a),u) belongs to I_{a,b}; define it to be zero otherwise. Then
 T_{a,b}=sum_{s,u,K} Gamma_{a,b}(s,u,K)e_K(-Ns u^{-1})e(Ns/(Ku)),
and consequently C(P) is the sum over a!=b of the absolute values of these pushed-forward traces.
Bettin and Chandee, arXiv:1502.00769, Theorem 1, bound a trilinear sum with phase e_n(theta a m^{-1}) only for a product coefficient nu_a alpha_m beta_n. Their immediately following smooth-perturbation remark accepts a reciprocal correction of the form e(theta a/(mn)), but does not replace the product coefficient by an arbitrary joint tensor. Wright, arXiv:2604.25177v2, Theorem 2.1, likewise treats product coefficients with one fixed denominator factor R. Hence neither cited theorem directly bounds the displayed trace for arbitrary Gamma_{a,b}.
Moreover, no Bettin--Chandee-strength extension to arbitrary bounded joint Gamma with only its l2 norm can hold. On balanced dyadic ranges A=M=N_0=X, choose Gamma(a,m,n)=conjugate(e_n(theta a m^{-1})) on triples with gcd(m,n)=1. The sum is comparable to X^3 and ||Gamma||_2 is comparable to X^(3/2), whereas replacing ||alpha||_2||beta||_2||nu||_2 by ||Gamma||_2 in the Bettin--Chandee right side would give O(X^(23/8+epsilon)). Thus use of the pushforward requires a source-specific separated or bounded-projective decomposition of Gamma_{a,b}, or a theorem retaining its joint structure. This is a theorem-interface no-direct-fit statement, not a bound for C(P).
669f51715cd33aa0.proof:
Fix distinct a,b and a triple in I_{a,b}. Put s=h(b-a) and K=abm. Since gcd(K,u)=1 and a^{-1}-b^{-1}=(b-a)(ab)^{-1} modulo u, the phase in T_{a,b} is e_u(NsK^{-1}). Additive reciprocity for coprime K,u states that K^{-1}/u+u^{-1}/K is congruent to 1/(Ku) modulo 1. Therefore
 e_u(NsK^{-1})=e_K(-Ns u^{-1})e(Ns/(Ku)).
For fixed a,b, multiplication by the nonzero integers ab and b-a makes the maps m to K and h to s injective. The definition of Gamma_{a,b} is thus unambiguous, and termwise substitution proves the pushed-forward formula. Taking the already defined outer absolute values proves the formula for C(P).
Bettin--Chandee Theorem 1 states, for nonzero theta and product coefficients alpha_m beta_n nu_a on dyadic ranges, the upper bound
 ||alpha||_2||beta||_2||nu||_2(1+|theta|A/(MN_0))^(1/2){(AMN_0)^(7/20+epsilon)(M+N_0)^(1/4)+(AMN_0)^(3/8+epsilon)(AN_0+AM)^(1/8)}
for sum alpha_m beta_n nu_a e_n(theta a m^{-1}). The following perturbation remark permits a C^1 reciprocal correction. The product-coefficient hypothesis remains unchanged, so it does not apply to arbitrary Gamma_{a,b}.
Wright Theorem 2.1 bounds a corresponding product-coefficient sum whose denominator has one fixed factor R. Its proof keeps R fixed, sums a squarefree auxiliary divisor r of R, separately introduces a square-full auxiliary variable, and invokes separated Bettin--Chandee estimates. It likewise contains no arbitrary joint-tensor conclusion.
Finally, on A=M=N_0=X let Gamma be the conjugate Kloosterman phase on coprime triples. A positive constant proportion of the X^3 dyadic triples has gcd(m,n)=1, and every retained summand is one, so the sum is comparable to X^3. Its l2 norm is comparable to X^(3/2). In the balanced regime the larger geometric term in the cited theorem is O(X^(11/8+epsilon)), giving the hypothetical joint-l2 bound O(X^(23/8+epsilon))=o(X^3). This refutes an abstract joint-tensor extension and proves all scope assertions.

70f0948e686a21c8.title: EXACT FOUR-MODE TRUNCATED-PROJECTOR DECOMPOSITION, PAID CORRECTION MODES, AND LITERAL PRINCIPAL RESIDUE-ENERGY SUPPLIER FOR FORWARD E11
70f0948e686a21c8.author: slava chan
70f0948e686a21c8.proof:
If (2) is zero, every term in the exact kernel (5) of fact a5f73e19fca8e2d5 is multiplied by zero. Thus all four mode kernels, W, every S-row, and both sides of (23) vanish. No projector estimate is used in that case.

Assume henceforth that (2) equals one. Then (mu(m_sharp)^2=1), so (m_sharp) is squarefree. Since (qmid m_sharp), q is squarefree. This verifies the squarefree hypothesis every time facts adb3b38d14670d3c and 9ef7fac8978ac244 are used below.

For q at least two, equation (11) of fact a5f73e19fca8e2d5, from fact d61bd0787abcc5ec, gives (8). Multiplication proves (9)-(10). For (11), reduce (A=Nt(a-b)) modulo a and b. Its a-residue is (-Ntb), and its b-residue is Nta. Additive CRT therefore identifies the product (E_aoverline{E_b}) with the right side of (11).

If F/a is at least one, both F/a and F satisfy the threshold hypothesis of fact 9ef7fac8978ac244, and q has just been proved squarefree. Hence both projectors are (O_arepsilon(q^arepsilon)), and so is their difference. This proves (12). If (0<F/a<1), conductor integrality shows that the only character added below threshold one is the principal character. Its conductor is one, its unit values are one, and its Gauss coefficient is (c_q(N)). This proves (13). Fact 9ef7fac8978ac244 bounds P_a(1), and (|c_q(N)|lephi(q)), proving (12) in this case. When (q,N)=1, every character conductor divides q and is coprime to N, so (13) is the complete character Fourier inversion, which is (14). Without that extra hypothesis omitted characters prevent completion.

For q=1, if F/a<1<=F, formula (8) becomes (Pi_a=E_a+1/(a-1)), the exact nonprincipal local-character response computed in fact d61bd0787abcc5ec. If F/a>=1, then a<=F and both sides vanish. This proves the q=1 case.

From (1), beta at least 4/3, and the balanced source lower bound (Dgg x^{1/2}(log x)^{-B}) for a fixed B, one has
[
 a,bge Z_dge D^{2/3+2sigma}ge x^{1/3+sigma-o(1)}>x^{2/9}ge F
]
for large x. Thus the actual range is subunit.

For the correction modes, use the bare Fourier envelope underlying fact a5f73e19fca8e2d5:
[
 |C_iota(n;h,p,ell)|le x^arepsilon E_{iota,h,p,ell},
 qquadsum_alpha E_alphall Rx^arepsilon.              	ag{28}
]
Partition coordinates by u modulo q. Apply weighted Cauchy within each residue class and then across the residue classes. This gives
[
 sum_alpha rac{|C_iota(am_sharp;h,p,ell)
 C_iota(bm_sharp;h,p,ell)|}{E_alpha}ll Rx^arepsilon. 	ag{29}
]
The literal masks only delete terms. Now (12), used only in the squarefree nonzero-selector case, and the denominators in (10) yield at each fixed a,b,m_sharp
[
 |K_{10}|+|K_{01}|ll RZ_d^{-1}x^arepsilon,qquad
 |K_{11}|ll RZ_d^{-2}x^arepsilon.                         	ag{30}
]
The zero-selector rows contribute zero. There are (O(Z_d^2)) ordered dilator pairs and (O(D/Z_d)) cofactors. Summing proves (15). Condition (1) rearranges to (RDle Z_dD^{3-2sigma}/R), proving (16).

For the principal mode, (h/m_sharp=t/q), so the continuous phase in the kernel is
[
 eleft( rac{Nh}{m_sharp u}(1/a-1/b)ight)
 =e(-A/(abqu)).
]
Together with (11) this is Phi. Everything else is precisely W. Since the common-core projectors depend on u only modulo q, exact grouping by residues proves (19)-(21) with no change to any mask.

On nonzero support, (12) gives (|Q(v)|ll q^arepsilon). Cauchy over at most q residues proves (23). On zero support it is the identity 0<=0.

Expanding (22) pairs exactly two u-rows in the same residue class, hence gives the unique integer tau in (24), including tau=0. Since q,u_1,u_2 are units modulo ab,
[
 u_1^{-1}-u_2^{-1}equiv(u_2-u_1)(u_1u_2)^{-1}
 equiv q	au(u_1u_2)^{-1}pmod {ab}.
]
This proves the finite factor in (25). Also
[
 1/u_1-1/u_2=q	au/(u_1u_2),
]
which proves its Archimedean factor. The source rows were independently retained before the residue condition was imposed, so no other tau restriction appears.

The exact off-diagonal aggregate is partitioned by (9). Equation (16) pays three parts, leaving exactly (26). Equation (23), square roots, and the triangle inequality show that (27) implies (26). Finally, the estimates in fact a5f73e19fca8e2d5 sum an interval inverse trace after suppressing the literal projector and source structure; they do not have the sparse paired summation set or q-dependent coefficients of (22). This proves only the stated no-direct-fit. All scope restrictions follow.

866cdb3eb8c3bf0d.title: UNIVERSAL SUBUNIT COMPLETION, INDEPENDENT FOUR-MODE FORWARD-E11 DECOMPOSITION, CORRECTION PAYMENTS, AND EXACT PHYSICAL LEADING PHASE. Let x be sufficiently large. Fix real eta,omega,sigma with 0<eta<1/120, 0<omega<2/9-3eta, sigma>0. Let D satisfy x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B)<=D<=2x^(1/2) for a fixed B, put R=D^beta with 4/3<=beta<=4/3+6eta, and F=x^(2/9-3eta-omega). Let P satisfy P>=(R/D)^2D^(2sigma), and let cal P be primes in [P,2P]. Then every a,b in cal P satisfies a>F,b>F for sufficiently large x
866cdb3eb8c3bf0d.author: slava chan
866cdb3eb8c3bf0d.statement:
UNIVERSAL SUBUNIT COMPLETION, INDEPENDENT FOUR-MODE FORWARD-E11 DECOMPOSITION, CORRECTION PAYMENTS, AND EXACT PHYSICAL LEADING PHASE. Let x be sufficiently large. Fix real eta,omega,sigma with 0<eta<1/120, 0<omega<2/9-3eta, sigma>0. Let D satisfy x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B)<=D<=2x^(1/2) for a fixed B, put R=D^beta with 4/3<=beta<=4/3+6eta, and F=x^(2/9-3eta-omega). Let P satisfy P>=(R/D)^2D^(2sigma), and let cal P be primes in [P,2P]. Then every a,b in cal P satisfies a>F,b>F for sufficiently large x.
Let N be a positive integer. Let m,u be coprime positive integers, h nonzero, c=gcd(m,h), q=m/c, t=h/c, and assume m is squarefree, (ab,mhuN)=1, and (q,tu)=1. For q>=2 and T>0 define
 P_a(T;t,u)=phi(q)^(-1) sum_{psi mod q, cond(psi)>T, gcd(cond(psi),N)=1} G_{N,q}(psi)psi(t)conjugate(psi(au)),
where G_{N,q}(psi)=sum_{z mod q,gcd(z,q)=1}e_q(-Nz)conjugate(psi(z)) and e_v(y)=exp(2 pi i y/v). Define P_b similarly. For q=1 put P_a(T;t,u)=P_b(T;t,u)=1_{T<1}.
For every squarefree q>=2 and every N, if 0<T<1 then
 P_a(T;t,u)=e_q(-Nt(au)^(-1)).
No hypothesis gcd(q,N)=1 is needed. For q=1 the displayed convention is the complete response.
Put E_a=e_a(-Nt(qu)^(-1)) and E_b=e_b(-Nt(qu)^(-1)), with E_a=E_b=1 when q=1, and define A_a=P_a(F/a;t,u), B_a=P_a(F/a;t,u)-P_a(F;t,u), and analogously A_b,B_b. Let Pi_a and Pi_b be the primitive-conductor-greater-than-F descended projectors modulo aq and bq. Then, without using facts 70f0948e686a21c8, d716d761596faa18, or f387dfb8f31400c6,
 Pi_a=L_a+D_a, L_a=E_aA_a, D_a=B_a/(a-1),
 Pi_b=L_b+D_b, L_b=E_bA_b, D_b=B_b/(b-1).
Thus Pi_a conjugate(Pi_b) is the sum of the four products LL,LD,DL,DD.
Let Alpha be a finite coordinate set alpha=(iota,h,p,ell) with u=p ell, let E_alpha>0, and let C_iota(n;h,p,ell) be complex coefficients, extended by zero off all desired literal masks and in particular off gcd(m,u)=1, such that |C_iota(n;h,p,ell)|<=x^epsilon E_alpha for squarefree n and sum_alpha E_alpha<=R x^epsilon. Let lambda_{a,m} be supported on a in cal P, am<=D, satisfy sum_{a,m}|lambda_{a,m}|^2<=D, and vanish unless m is squarefree and all displayed clean conditions hold. Form the exact two-dilate correlation with weight
 mu(m)^2 lambda_{a,m}conjugate(lambda_{b,m}) C_iota(am;h,p,ell)conjugate(C_iota(bm;h,p,ell))/E_alpha,
continuous phase e(Nh/(mp ell)(1/a-1/b)), and projector product Pi_a conjugate(Pi_b). Let C_LL,C_LD,C_DL,C_DD be the sums over ordered a!=b of the absolute values of the corresponding inner mode sums. Then
 C_LD+C_DL <<_epsilon x^epsilon RD,
 C_DD <<_epsilon x^epsilon RD/P,
and all three correction aggregates are <<_epsilon x^epsilon P D^(3-2sigma)/R.
The LL product, together with the continuous phase, is exactly
 e_{p ell}(Nh m^(-1)(a^(-1)-b^(-1))).
Consequently C_LL is exactly the complete physical-phase trace obtained by replacing the LL projector product with this phase and leaving every coefficient and mask unchanged. To close this off-diagonal stratum it would suffice to prove the open estimate
 C_LL <<_epsilon x^epsilon P D^(3-2sigma)/R.
This estimate is not asserted or proved here, and no accepted predecessor cited here supplies it. Applying residue Cauchy after artificially retaining a q-residue projector would introduce an unnecessary q^(1/2) norm: universal subunit completion has already recombined that projector into the complete physical phase. No E11 closure, C3, PMD, DCE, or Goldbach conclusion is asserted.
866cdb3eb8c3bf0d.proof: 1. Dilator size. The assumptions give P>=D^(2beta-2+2sigma)>=D^(2/3+2sigma). Since D>=x^(1/2)(log x)^(-B), this exceeds x^(1/3+sigma)(log x)^(-O(1)), whereas F=P>F for large x. 2. Universal conductor-sharing vanishing and completion. Let q>=2 be squarefree and let psi be a nonprincipal character modulo q with primitive conductor f. Squarefreeness gives q=fs with gcd(f,s)=1, and psi is induced by a primitive character psi_star modulo f, principal on the s-coordinate. Additive Chinese remaindering factors G_{N,q}(psi) into a Ramanujan sum on s times sum_{v mod f,gcd(v,f)=1} e_f(-N s^(-1)v)conjugate(psi_star(v)). If a prime r divides gcd(f,N), then the r-local additive character is constant one, while the r-local component of the primitive character psi_star is nonprincipal. Its sum over the units modulo r is zero. Hence G_{N,q}(psi)=0 whenever gcd(f,N)>1, for arbitrary squarefree q and arbitrary N. Now let 01 has just been proved to have zero Gauss coefficient. Therefore the restricted sum equals the complete character Fourier sum. Finite Fourier inversion on the unit group gives phi(q)^(-1)sum_{psi mod q}G_{N,q}(psi)psi(t)conjugate(psi(au))=e_q(-Nt(au)^(-1)). For q=1 the unit group has one element and the convention is immediate. 3. Independent local decomposition. For q>=2, fact d61bd0787abcc5ec gives exactly Pi_a=E_aP_a(F/a)+(P_a(F/a)-P_a(F))/(a-1), and likewise for b. Its hypotheses do not require gcd(q,N)=1. For q=1, a>F>=1. Modulo the prime a the cutoff cond>F retains exactly the nonprincipal characters. Complete Fourier inversion gives E_a, while the principal local contribution is -1/(a-1) because gcd(a,N)=1. Thus the retained response is E_a+1/(a-1), equal to the displayed formula under the q=1 convention. This proves the decompositions and four products. 4. Correction rows. For q>=2, fact 9ef7fac8978ac244 gives |P_a(F)|<<_epsilon q^epsilon. Universal completion gives |P_a(F/a)|=1, and similarly for b. The q=1 bounds are immediate. At fixed a,b,m, the coefficient assumptions give sum_alpha |C_iota(am;h,p,ell)C_iota(bm;h,p,ell)|/E_alpha <=x^(2epsilon)sum_alpha E_alpha<=(R/D)^2D^(2sigma), one has RD<=P D^(3-2sigma)/R, proving their common budget. 5. Physical leading phase. Universal completion and additive CRT give L_a=e_{aq}(-Nt u^(-1)) and L_b=e_{bq}(-Nt u^(-1)), including q=1. Since h/m=t/q and gcd(m,u)=1, additive reciprocity gives e(Nh/(amu))L_a=e(Nt/(aqu))e_{aq}(-Nt u^(-1))=e_u(Nh(am)^(-1)), and similarly for b. Their product is the stated physical phase. Coefficients and masks are unchanged. Therefore the LL aggregate equals the complete physical-phase trace. The correction modes are proved small, but no argument here estimates LL; the displayed LL inequality is explicitly an open sufficient supplier. Completion occurs before residue grouping, so no q-residue vector or q^(1/2) Cauchy norm is intrinsic. All scope restrictions follow.

d716d761596faa18.title: ACTUAL UNIQUE-DILATOR COEFFICIENT-ENERGY PAYMENT, MODE-NAMING RECONCILIATION, AND COMPLETE TAU-STRATUM LEDGER FOR THE FORWARD E11 PRINCIPAL FRONTIER
d716d761596faa18.author: slava chan
d716d761596faa18.proof:
Equations (1)-(3) follow by substituting (L_a=E_aP_a(F/a)) and (D_a=(P_a(F/a)-P_a(F))/(a-1)) into the four modes of fact 70f0948e686a21c8. No term changes; only the meaning of the binary labels changes.

At fixed m, finite-dimensional Cauchy--Schwarz gives
[
 |lambda_m|_1^2le|mathcal P||lambda_m|_2^2.
]
Summing and applying the coefficient hypothesis (2) of fact 0fd3b33d63081ee3 proves (5)-(6), since the number of integers, and hence primes, in ([P,2P]) is (O(P)).

Fact 70f0948e686a21c8 proves the fixed-row bounds (7) from the bare pre-projector envelope, after first splitting off the zero squarefree selector. Use the triangle inequality in the exact off-diagonal aggregate:
[
 sum_{a
e b}left|sum_mlambda_{a,m}overline{lambda_{b,m}}
 mathcal K_{10}(a,b;m)ight|
 le rac{x^arepsilon R}{P}
 sum_msum_{a,b}|lambda_{a,m}lambda_{b,m}|
 = rac{x^arepsilon R}{P}sum_m|lambda_m|_1^2.
]
Equation (6) gives (O(x^arepsilon RD)). The same proof applies to mode 01. With (R/P^2) instead, it gives (O(x^arepsilon RD/P)) for mode 00. This proves (8).

Condition (9) is equivalent to
[
 Pge(R/D)^2D^{2sigma}.
]
After rearrangement this gives
[
 RDle P D^{3-2sigma}/R.
]
It also bounds (RD/P) by the same quantity. Thus (10) follows.

On the clean sector of fact 70f0948e686a21c8, a and b divide none of (N,t,u_1,u_2,q). Since a and b are distinct primes, neither divides a-b. Hence ((A,ab)=1). Also each (u_j) is a unit modulo ab. Therefore the numerator of the additive phase (12) has greatest common divisor ((ab,	au)) with ab. Reducing an additive character by that greatest common divisor proves (13), and squarefreeness (ab) gives exactly the four rows of (14). Formula (15) is equation (25) of fact 70f0948e686a21c8 and was not changed in reducing only the finite additive conductor. If tau is zero, (11) gives (u_1=u_2), proving the diagonal assertion.

Each (u_j) has exactly two distinct prime factors. If (u_1
e u_2), their gcd can therefore contain zero or one common prime; if it contained both, the products would be equal. This proves (16). Equations (11), (14), and (16) are classifications of the already existing pair set, so they impose no deletion and preserve every literal mask.

By (3), the old leading (M_{00}) is the new principal (widetilde M_{11}), so equation (26) of fact 70f0948e686a21c8 is exactly (17).

Finally, the residue energy is (|S|_2^2), whereas (18) is the scalar inner product of S with the conjugate of Q. Cauchy--Schwarz supplies an upper bound for the latter from the former. If the unit-residue space has dimension greater than one and Q is nonzero, the kernel of this scalar functional has positive dimension, so no identity or two-sided comparison follows from finite-dimensional linear algebra alone. If Q is zero, the linear row vanishes for every S while the energy need not. This is only an algebraic non-equivalence statement and makes no claim about realizability by the literal source. Every scope restriction follows.

f387dfb8f31400c6.author: slava chan
f387dfb8f31400c6.statement:
ACTUAL-SOURCE RECOMBINATION OF THE FORWARD E11 PRINCIPAL LEADING MODE. Assume the hypotheses and notation of facts 70f0948e686a21c8 and d716d761596faa18, with dilator scale P, and let C_prin,11(P) be the exact principal-leading aggregate of fact d716d761596faa18. For every clean nonzero-selector row, put c=(m,h), q=m/c, t=h/c, u=p ell, and A=Nt(a-b), as in fact 70f0948e686a21c8. On the actual subunit range F/a,F/b<1, including q=1, one has the exact pointwise phase identity
Q_{a,b,m,h}(u mod q) Phi_{a,b,q,t}(u)=e_u(Nh m^{-1}(a^{-1}-b^{-1})),
where the inverses on the right are modulo u. Consequently
C_prin,11(P)=sum_{a,b in Pset, a!=b} | sum_{m,h} sum_{u=p ell} W_{a,b,m,h}(u)e_u(Nh m^{-1}(a^{-1}-b^{-1})) |,
with exactly the W-row, reciprocal envelope, source/least/marker/fixed-U/frequency/collision masks, canonical distinct-prime semiprime support, q=1 block, and zero-selector convention of fact 70f0948e686a21c8. Thus the residue condition u_2-u_1=q tau, its four conductor-drop strata, and its diagonal/shared-star/four-distinct collision partition belong to the stronger residue-energy expansion after residue Cauchy; they are not extra masks on this exact linear trace. This identity supplies no bound for C_prin,11(P), no E11 closure, and no PMD, DCE, or Goldbach conclusion.
f387dfb8f31400c6.proof:
Fix a clean nonzero-selector row. Clean support in fact 70f0948e686a21c8 gives (ab,mhuN)=1, so q divides m and hence (q,Nabu)=1. The actual range has F/a,F/b<1. Equation (14) of that fact therefore applies to both leading projectors. With A=Nt(a-b), their product is
Q(u mod q)=e_q(-Nt(au)^{-1}) e_q(Nt(bu)^{-1})=e_q(A(ab u)^{-1}).
For q=1 this reads Q=1 by the explicit q=1 convention. Equation (17) of fact 70f0948e686a21c8 gives
Phi(u)=e_ab(A(q u)^{-1}) e(-A/(abqu)).
Put k=abq. Since a,b,q are pairwise coprime on clean support, additive Chinese remaindering gives
e_q(A(ab u)^{-1})e_ab(A(q u)^{-1})=e_k(Au^{-1}).
For coprime positive integers k,u, choose inverses so that
u^{-1}/k+k^{-1}/u is congruent to 1/(ku) modulo 1. Hence
 e_k(Au^{-1})e(-A/(ku))=e_u(-Ak^{-1}).
This also proves the q=1 case, where the q-factor is absent. Finally m=cq and h=ct, while c is a unit modulo u on clean support. Therefore, modulo u,
-A(abq)^{-1}=-Nt(a-b)(abq)^{-1}=Nh m^{-1}(a^{-1}-b^{-1}).
This proves the pointwise identity. Substitute it into equation (21) of fact 70f0948e686a21c8, then use the mode relabelling in fact d716d761596faa18. No coefficient is altered: W already contains the unique-dilator coefficients, the reciprocal envelope, both literal source rows and all masks, while zero-selector rows have W=0. The residue-pair relation u_2-u_1=q tau is introduced only when equation (22) of fact 70f0948e686a21c8 expands the squared residue norm. Therefore all its conductor and collision strata remain valid for that stronger energy, but none is an additional condition on the displayed exact linear trace. The scope restrictions follow.
